However, findings from related research show that disabled people in rural areas are economically active, able to generate income, and have the possibility of a productive path out of poverty. By enhancing the professional knowledge and business skills of disabled persons with disabilities, they are supported to implement their own businesses and to be part of the labor market under equal conditions.
The 24month ARABLE project involves 10 experienced partner organizations in 3 EU Member states (Greece(2) and Croatia), 2 third counties associated with the Programme (Liechtenstein and North Macedonia) as well as 5 third countries not associated with the Programme – Southern Mediterranean / Region 3 (Tunisia, Morocco, Egypt, and Israel, Jordan) to support inclusive and sustainable future societies, by empowering youths that face disabilities, to gain entrepreneurship skills, to engage in sustainable agricultural entrepreneurship through an encompassing curriculum that suits to their needs and interests. 
To reach the above goal, ARABLE suggests the implementation of youth workers' learning experiences, research activities on best practices among 10 countries, and transnational organizational meetings, resulting in the development of the ARABLE transitional DataBase & e-Guide on best practices, training techniques, rates & guidelines and the Open online Learning Environment for agricultural entrepreneurship for disabled young people.
ARABLE “talks” about the arable lands that will be cultivated, the opportunities that are ready to be seized, and the ABILITIES that will shine.

101130023.action_type: Capacity Building in the field of Youth
101130023.title: MEDIActive Youth: Informing the Balkans
101130023.summary:
Our two previous and one ongoing E+ projects successfully launched a global initiative in improving media literacy. By now, capacities of 28 youth NGO’s from Europe, Latin America and Africa have been raised, a Transnational Youth Magazine (TYM) - e-magazine for youth policy has been launched, and online courses in media literacy and activism have been created. 

The overall objective of this two-years Project is to continue with building capacities of youth NGOs globally and with developing new high-quality open education resources (OER) in the field of media/news literacy. Particular attention is given here to the Balkans within the broader European context, and this project will enable it to join the MEDIActive youth initiative, but also to strengthen the dialogue and post-conflict reconciliation in this region. 

SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES
1. Increasing the capacity of youth NGOs/workers/activists from 6 Balkan countries in the field of news literacy, critical thinking and media activism, and fostering their active participation in society.
2. Creating high-quality multilingual OER for an innovative learning on news literacy and critical thinking.
3. Further improving the TYM by engaging youth activists from Balkans to start write for it, which will: a) empower an informational/media hub between Europe, Africa and Latin America in the field of youth policy; b) foster post-conflict reconciliation, and promoting the EU and the EU values in the Balkans.

MAIN ACTIVITIES
1. News Literacy, Critical Thinking and Media Activism Training Course
2. Design and development of teaching material pack (TMP) in the field of news literacy and critical thinking
3. Creating MOOC: “Sorting Facts from Fiction: Critical thinking vs Information disorder and Propaganda”
4. Improving the TYM 

DIRECT BENEFICIARIES
24 youth trainers and 60 young activists from partner countries

OUTPUTS
Training course realised
TMP created
MOOC designed
At least 60 articles written for the TYM

hr.name: Hrvatska edukacijska i razvojna mreza za evoluciju sporazumijevanja (HERMES)

101130196.action_type: Capacity Building in the field of Youth
101130196.title: NURTURE - NURTURING THE WORLD CAN BE A JOB
101130196.summary:
The project Nurturing the world can be a job is designed to raise the capacity of non-governmental organisations from Western Balkans countries, to empower young people in finding their career path, especially those with fewer opportunities, and to promote the NGO sector as employer.  In order to achieve these aims, the project foresees the following work packages: 1) management and coordination (WP1), 2) building capacities of youth organisations (WP2), 3) empowering young people (WP3), and 4) promoting NGO sector as employer (WP4). In the work packages the project partners will target the next groups: 1) representatives of the project partners that will be involved in the National support points, 2) NGOs working with young people and their representatives, and 3) young people aged between 18 and 30, with a special focus on young people with fewer opportunities.

One of the major results of the project will be the establishment of National support points in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Albania, and Montenegro which will be the main actors to build the capacity of NGOs and contribute to the career development of young people. National support points will organise seminars and workshops for young people and representatives of NGOs, provide career counselling, and support the implementation of apprenticeships in which 90 young people (54 of which will be young people with fewer opportunities) will have their first working experience in the NGO sector and so gain the skills and competencies necessary to participate in the labour market.  

The main activities for the promotion of the project and for the dissemination of the results will be the Campaign Nurturing the world can be a job. Through the campaign the general public will be informed about the work of the NSPs and young people will be invited and encouraged to apply for the apprenticeships. The aim of the campaign will be to raise awareness about NGOs being important potential employers for young people.

101130622.action_type: Capacity Building in the field of Youth
101130622.title: DPYU4P - DigiPath - Youth Up 4 Possibilities
101130622.summary:
‘DigiPath - Youth Up 4 Possibilities’ addresses youth unemployment by enabling shared digital youth work in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Kosovo, Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia. Unsustainable youth brain drain is a big risk. Trends show young people migrating from WB6 economies, to Croatia and Slovenia, there is a lack of shared data on flows and quality opportunities. Four urgent concerns contribute to young people living in precarious conditions: unemployment, repercussions of the COVID-19 pandemic, sluggish transition to digital youth work, and absence of inter-sectoral collaboration. In the 24 month project, partners will collaborate to develop a digital tool that connects education, labour market and the youth sector to each other and young people. Enabling visibility about decent personal and professional development opportunities in home and destination countries. Objectives: (i) enhance capacities of 8 youth organizations in inter-sectorial cooperation with education and the labour market; (ii) support the digital transition and increase competences in digital youth work; (iii) enable participating organizations to co-deliver sustainable projects supporting youth future prospects; (iv) create a digital tool, DIGITAL PLATFORM, enabling cooperation between sectors, youth participation and strengthening cooperation in WB6 economies, Croatia and Slovenia; (v) and setting a circular framework of youth empowerment.   
Project logic: IF we digitize inter-sectoral and cross-border youth work in WB6 economies, Croatia and Slovenia, AND create linkages to education and the labour market AND develop a DIGITAL PLATFORM to connect young people far from the labour market, or in long-term unemployment to information, resources, personal and professional opportunities THEN the DIGITAL PLATFORM will be a tool to create shorter and sustainable pathways for young people and co-creation of responsive projects for youth empowerment and employment.

101183591.action_type: Capacity Building in the field of Youth
101183591.title: UPSHIFT Impact: Amplifying Social Change through Youth Initiatives
101183591.summary:
The UPSHIFT project is an innovative initiative designed to empower youth aged 16 to 25 across Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, North Macedonia, and Albania. Through a comprehensive approach that combines capacity building, civic engagement, social innovation, peacebuilding, and strategic communication, the project aims to equip young individuals with critical thinking, leadership, and digital literacy skills. These skills will enable them to address community challenges, foster social cohesion, and contribute to democratic processes and the evolving global job market.

The UPSHIFT project's impact extends beyond individual participants, influencing communities and policies by instilling a culture of proactive civic engagement and innovation among youth. It aims to build a network of empowered young leaders capable of initiating change, fostering peace, and contributing to societal development, setting a precedent for future youth-oriented programs across the region.

Led by Genesis Project, with partners including LEAD MK, HERMES, and Nisma ARSIS, the project is structured around five work packages (WPs). WP1 focuses on project management, ensuring coordinated efforts and alignment with goals. WP2 is dedicated to capacity building, enhancing participants' skills in project management and civic engagement. WP3 drives civic engagement and social innovation, offering youth the platform to ideate and implement community-based projects. WP4 emphasizes peacebuilding and inclusivity, fostering an environment of tolerance and collaboration. Lastly, WP5 focuses on communication and dissemination, spreading the project's message and achievements to a broader audience.

Each partner brings unique expertise to the project, ensuring a holistic approach to youth empowerment. Genesis excels in project management and capacity building, LEAD MK leads in fostering civic engagement and innovation, HERMES champions peacebuilding initiatives, and Nisma ARSIS spearheads communication.

hr.name: Hrvatska edukacijska i razvojna mreza za evoluciju sporazumijevanja (HERMES)

101183596.action_type: Capacity Building in the field of Youth
101183596.title: Halan We Grow
101183596.summary:
CSOs working with youth in the Southern Mediterranean region (Morocco, Lebanon and Tunisia) are facing major multiple crises;
We, with the support of the main application LUMEN (Croatia) and MasterPeace (MP) (NL), will develop new ways to engage, connect and empower youngsters.
The overall needs overview matches with our main objective ‘to boost the quality, capacity and recognition of youth work in the Southern Mediterranean in an international cooperation of CSOs by jointly learning, developing and implementing innovative Non Formal Education methodologies and materials to engage, connect and empower youngsters (especially young women and minority groups in remote areas) outside formal learning”.’

Main outputs/ products/ events: 
- 6 online trainings raising capacity; 12 Youth Workers’ Passion Grow Plans; 4 CSO strategies; 
- 5 online trainings on 21st century skills related to EU values; 1 NFE material as output 
- 3 Thematic upgraded NFE Methodologies with e-learning (Artivism, Doughnut Economy and Social Entrepreneurship in 5 languages); 16 Youth workers from associated CSOs trained
- Halan We Grow e-learning platform
- 28 trained Youth Workers guide 20 projects resulting in 20 theatre plays and 4 educational board games run by 140 youngsters (80% female; 40% from minority background); 
- 1 transnational online Social Entrepreneurship challenge with 30 participants from the Southern Mediterranean region
- 4 local Growth Mindset summits each with 30 stakeholders; 4 MoUs signed
- 1 MP global Innovation Factory; 15 global CSOs attend;
- 2 MP EU/MENA capacity building bootcamps with 40 representatives from 15 EU and MENA countries; 2 reports mentioning the upgrading of the CSOs strategy
- 7 webinars “Taking The Stage” meeting hundreds of youth workers during prestigious global online meetings; 7 reports on upgrading the CSOs strategy
- 3 global surveys on needs of CSOs and Youth Workers
- 22 stories will be published and reach youth workers

101184372.action_type: Capacity Building in the field of Youth
101184372.title: THE STORY OF THE 1.5°C LIMIT - Solutions and storytelling of youth from Western Balkan
101184372.summary:
The main objective of  “THE STORY" project is to raise the capacity of youth and organizations that work with youth from the Western Balkan region, to understand and advocate for solutions to the environmental crisis, using civic education and arts, especially literature.
Our primary target group are youth and youth with fewer opportunities of Western Balkan, our secondary target group are youth workers and organizations working with youth in the region.

The specific objectives of the project are to prepare the two target groups for:
1) in-depth understanding of the climate crises through non-formal education 
2) finding specific local solutions (with focus on local community solutions, zero waste systems, public advocacy methods, civic participation and art.)
3) communicating the findings from the activities to wider public through an artistic perspective - creative writing and climate fiction.

The chosen activities support the main objective and present the best examples of engaging youth through art and focus on solutions. The activities, through 5 work packages, include: a youth exchange, several workshops on art and creative writing for youth, different youth led ideas in Western Balkans, a training course and two study visits for staff and youth workers, among others. Two major outputs of the project are a Collection of climate fiction stories and poems (“Booklet”) written by youth, and an educational Manual "Stories for change", on how to use art and storytelling for social change for youth workers and youth organizations.

We aim to establish a cross-border collaboration on a topic of European interest, by giving space, mentorship and tools to youth to express themselves and find creative solutions to climate change on the local, national and regional levels. This will aslo offer a blueprint for similar art and activist based activities, improving overall quality and recognition of youth work in Europe.

101185222.action_type: Capacity Building in the field of Youth
101185222.title: Youth IMPACT - Youth Integration and Motivation for Positive Achievement and Capacity Transformation
101185222.summary:
The partnership implementing Youth IMPACT project includes the Croatian Blind Union, The Association of the Blind and
Visually Impaired of Slovenia, the Union of the Blind of Montenegro, the Herceg-Bosna Union of the Blind and the Emphasys Center from Cyprus. Joint efforts and expertise in the area of working with visually impaired youth (VI youth) will result in achieving general objective - building capacities of organizations active in the field of youth, and VI youth themselves.
Youth IMPACT includes four main capacity-building activities. Building capacities of organizations working in the field of youth occurs at 2 levels. The micro level refers to strengthening capacities of PPs through an training and creation of “Bridging Differences
Programme” Toolkit. The macro level entails strengthening capacities of local VI organizations to include young people in their
management and operational structures (knowledge transmission), as well as organizations working in the field of youth regarding correct approach and communication with VI people, so that they are better skilled to include VI youth in their programs (Awareness and Capacity Raising Campaign) (104 organizations in total for both levels).
The fourth building-capacity activity refers to VI youth and the implementation of two mobility program cycles. On the one hand,
encouraging PPs with less experience (2 third not associated countries) to develop and implement youth mobility programs through testing
BDP Toolkit, and on the other hand, raising capacities of 24 young VI people in all areas necessary to increase their employability, active
participation and inclusion in the society. Visibility activities, including 5 initial and 1 final conference, as well as multiplier event and BDP
EU-dimension event will contribute to the dissemination of the BDP Toolkit, as well as to a broader integration of the aforementioned in
the future programmes and activities aimed at youth.

101243616.action_type: Capacity Building in the field of Youth
101243616.title: Joyful Minds: Humor-based program for enhancing adolescent psychological resilience
101243616.summary:
"Joyful Minds" is an Erasmus+ initiative addressing European adolescents' growing mental health crisis by integrating humor-based resilience training into youth work. With increasing social pressures, digital overload, and the lasting effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, traditional mental health education often struggles to engage young people. This project fills a critical gap by offering an innovative, culturally adaptable, evidence-based approach to emotional well-being.  

Project objectives & target groups  
"Joyful Minds" equips youth workers with practical, research-backed humor techniques to enhance emotional regulation, cognitive flexibility, and stress management in vulnerable youth populations. The project aims to:  
- Train over 50 youth workers and educators in humor-based mental health strategies.  
- Develop a blended learning curriculum combining digital tools and in-person training.  
- Engage more than 1,000 adolescents in humor-based resilience workshops.  
- Strengthen transnational collaboration among youth organizations.  

The project primarily targets:  
- Youth workers and educators are direct beneficiaries.  
- Adolescents (aged 12–18), including neurodivergent individuals, rural youth, and gender-diverse populations.  
  
Impact & sustainability  
- Short-term: Enhanced resilience skills in youth workers and adolescents.  
- Mid-term: Scalable humor-based training models for European youth organizations.  
- Long-term: Integration of humor-based resilience strategies into national youth work policies.  

Led by the Genesis Project (Bosnia & Herzegovina), the consortium includes expert organizations from Croatia, Albania, and North Macedonia with backgrounds in youth work, mental health, and digital education. By combining experienced Erasmus+ partners with emerging organizations, the project fosters knowledge transfer, innovation, and cross-cultural adaptation of humor-based resilience strategies.

101246605.action_type: Capacity Building in the field of Youth
101246605.title: STAR Youth - Social Transformation and Reconciliation Youth
101246605.summary: The STAR Youth project is developed in response to the need for an approach to peacebuilding and peace education that built on practices proven to resonate within the current European context. Given the history of lecture-based learning, geographic and spatial divides that have kept interethnic interactions limited, and a slow acceptance of participant-led dialogue, this project sought to build on the newer peace education practices consistent with European traditions. STaR Youth project also supported integration in an indirect, non-confrontational way among those not yet ready to face the past head-on. Social Transformation and Reconciliation and role that Youth Work is playing and can play is the core to the goals and methodology of this project. How the youth work can create safe spaces for authentic dialogue, in which the wounds of conflict could be jointly acknowledged and biased narratives jointly dismantled, both critical steps in the path towards genuine social healing, reconciliation and conflict prevention. The project goals are: (a) Humanize and increase empathy for members of other ethnoreligious groups; and (b) Catalyse youth to take action to promote interethnic respect. In service of these goals, the project objectives are: 1. To develop improved interethnic attitudes and behavioural tendencies among targeted youth organizations and organization working with youth and 2. To share insights about interethnic respect with youth and youth work organizations.

101246818.action_type: Capacity Building in the field of Youth
101246818.title: SocEntYwD - Capacity building in youth work for social entrepreneurship of youngsters with disabilities
101246818.summary:
Young people with disabilities (YWDs) face significant barriers to employment and economic independence. Many are excluded from traditional job markets due to misconceptions about productivity, limited accessibility, and a lack of inclusive policies. In non-EU countries, structured support for the employment and entrepreneurship of YWDs is even more scarce

The SocEntYwD project directly tackles these challenges by equipping youth workers and organizations with the skills and tools to support disability-inclusive social entrepreneurship. Through targeted training, digital learning resources, and advocacy efforts, the project aims to:

-Train youth workers to effectively mentor and support young social entrepreneurs with disabilities.
-Develop inclusive learning materials, including a curriculum, an online course, and a toolkit tailored to the needs of YWDs.
-Provide digital tools to enhance financial literacy, business development, and digital accessibility.
-Launch six online campaigns to raise awareness and engage stakeholders in promoting disability- inclusive entrepreneurship.
-Organize advocacy workshops and policy dialogues to influence national policies in at least three countries.

With a strong focus on sustainability, all project materials will be made available online and promoted beyond the consortium’s networks. By combining education, advocacy, and digital tools, the project empowers young people with disabilities to thrive as social entrepreneurs, shaping a more inclusive and innovative future.

hr.name: Savez gluhih i nagluhih grada Zagreba

101246981.action_type: Capacity Building in the field of Youth
101246981.title: SGS - Sustainable Goals through Sport
101246981.summary:
The Sustainable Goals through Sport (SGS) project is a transnational capacity-building initiative that leverages sport-based education to promote sustainability, youth empowerment, and cross-sector collaboration. It aims to bridge the gap between mega-sport events, sustainability education, and youth inclusion, ensuring that events like the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games leave a lasting educational legacy.

SGS will develop a Sport & Sustainability toolkit, an e-learning course and a Digital Knowledge Hub, equipping youth workers, educators, and sports organizations with accessible educational tools. It will train 100+ Youth Sustainability Ambassadors, empowering young people, particularly from disadvantaged backgrounds, to lead sustainability-focused sports initiatives. As part of its outreach, the project will host a Youth Engagement Festival at Dakar 2026, featuring interactive workshops, peer-led activities, and sustainability challenges. Additionally, a Final Policy Conference within the European Youth and Sport Platform 2027 will ensure that project outcomes influence EU and international policy on sport, sustainability, and youth development.

By integrating sport, education, and sustainability, SGS will create lasting change, strengthening cooperation between youth organizations, sports federations, and policymakers across Europe and Africa

101056023.title: AgriNext - Agricultural and rural excellence Incubator and Platform for the Exchange of competencies
101056023.summary:
General aim of the AgriNext project is to create learning environment that responds to the skill demand on the job market in the field of Multifunctional Agriculture. In order to achieve this aim, the specific project objectives include: 
1.Flexibilization of learning environments and curriculums in I-VET and C-VET, on EQF levels 3-6, in order to facilitate fast responses to job market demands 
2.Teacher empowerment (continuous professional and pedagogical) for a fast response to the job market demands, 
3.Established system of continuous exchange between employers, teacher/trainers/guidance service providers, in order to respond to the skills needed 
4.To develop students/learners who are highly skilled, motivated, entrepreneurial and aware of the importance of C-VET and lifelong learning 
5.Creating physical and virtual environment that enables:  
-Interaction between teachers, trainers, mentors from companies, students, and researchers; 
-Individualisation of the learning process;  
-Demonstration & try-outs of new technologies 
-Development of entrepreneurial activities  
6.Promoting rural development & vitality by demonstrating and highlighting opportunities of Multifunctional Agriculture.
7.Increasing digital competencies among students and teachers

The main expected results are: 
-Online training for guidance service providers for the use of new guidance service model
-Online training for VET teachers for flexible learning processes
-Proposals of flexibilization of VET 
-Green job = dream job video trailers
-Established Incubators (business – education partnership) 
-AgriNext IT Platform for Rural Excellence 

Activities has been divided in to 5 implementation Work Packages:
WP1–Guidance services to foster lifelong learning and development of VET skills in multifunctional agricultural
WP2–Flexibilization of school systems
WP3–Green job=dream job
WP4–Business incubator for rural excellence
WP5- AgriNext IT platform

101104579.title: AI4VET4AI - AI-powered Next Generation of VET
101104579.summary: Science is clear: Artificial Intelligence will be the defining development of the 21st century. Experts estimate that due to the rise of AI within only 2 decades aspects of daily human life will be unrecognisable. The influence of AI is about to challenge the very organising principles of our economic and social order. It can generate unprecedented wealth, revolutionise medicine and education, but it can bring existential perils for life as we know it. This makes the EC2020 report that the EU is lagging behind USA and Asia in AI adoption and development all the more worrying. Among many reasons behind that, the lack of skilled workforce is definitively one of the more prominent ones. The objective of AI4VET4AI is to contribute to the digital transformation of the EU labour market by adding new innovative teaching content and methods to VET curricula across 11 European countries and 18 EU NUTS2 regions, in order to support the growth of AI-skilled workers. We start from the ground up: we investigate the most potent sectors for AI deployment in our 17 regions, and for those sectors, in close cooperation with enterprises and their cluster organisations we create 14 MOOCs and TT materials that can easily be implemented in VET programmes (IVET and CVET). We organise 11 innovative AI VET campuses and 7 VET innovation AI incubators, in which VET learners hone their creative and entrepreneurial skills. We use project activities to connect partners closely and to raise awareness of the AI potential in our regions among representatives of public and private sector, as well as civil society. In turn, this helps us to create a joint and active platform of concerned EU citizens and institutions, interested, informed and motivated in supporting AI development further -- this being the basis of our ambitious CoVE, which aims to attract many more institutions (HEIs, VETs, companies, agencies, individuals) in its pursuit of sustainable, inclusive and just AI-powered future for all.

101194014.title: EXCEL4HOUSING4.0 - Centers of Vocational Excellence for Energy Efficiency and Sustainable Housing
101194014.summary:
EXCEL4HOUSING4.0 is a world-class Erasmus+ Partnership for Excellence aimed at building a transnational network of Centres of 
Vocational Education bringing together VET providers, academic and research entities, innovation and industry clusters as well as public 
entities coordinating energy efficiency and sustainable programs at national and regional level. This initiative will seek to address emerging 
needs and the “jobs of the future” for energy efficient and sustainable housing – Housing 4.0. To that end, we will: (i) Cluster 1 – Teaching 
and Learning: Design and develop innovative cross-border training and capacity building programmes and exchange practices aimed at 
fostering the transfer of smart and green skills, as well as circular economy methodologies, principles and tools for the improvement of the 
environmental sustainability of the housing sector; (ii) Cluster 2 - Business-education partnerships - Develop VET-academia-business 
strategic partnerships oriented to co-develop and implement industry-relevant curricula, work-based learning opportunities, and upskilling 
and re-skilling programmes for VET learners, teachers, SMEs, and workers in the energy efficiency and housing sectors; (iii) Cluster 3 – 
Governance and funding: Develop a collaborative and long-term sustainability framework, supported by a sustainable funding model for 
training and education in Energy Efficiency Finance. EXCEL4HOUSING4.0 will contribute to the twin digital and green transition in the 
construction sector, while ensuring the delivery of the Green Deal targets and effective transition pathways for environmentally, socially, 
and economically sustainable housing.

101260541.title: VET5.0 - Transforming Vocational Education Through Advancing Learner-Centricity, Education 5.0, and Lifelong Learning for Industry 4.0/5.0 in Rural Regions
101260541.summary: In the VET5.0 project, we promote learner-centricity, Education 5.0, and lifelong learning for Industry 4.0/5.0 in rural areas. We work with learners of all ages and backgrounds, including young people, professionals and vulnerable groups. We develop and implement high-quality, learner-centric services and training programmes. Thanks to adaptive learning, micro-credentials, and flexible programme design with accessible entry points, all learners — including those from disadvantaged backgrounds — will be able to customise their education. We will collaborate with alumni to provide lifelong learning opportunities. Our approach is based on novel pedagogical methods that utilise advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence, immersive learning, and gamification. We will work with educators to make them experts in Education 5.0, teaching them to use new digital tools effectively and adopt suitable pedagogy in the new learner-centred paradigm. Our educators and researchers will develop training programmes that incorporate adaptive learning and micro-credentials. They will also develop distance learning laboratories and receive inclusive education training. We engage with stakeholders, including VET providers, industry, SMEs, public authorities and policymakers, to develop a VET skills ecosystem centred on Industry 4.0 and 5.0. The technological backbone of this ecosystem centres on artificial intelligence, robotics and additive manufacturing. The project will prepare us for future mass customisation and human–machine interaction markets, with a focus on digital and green manufacturing. The VET5.0 project is accompanied by a robust EQAVET quality assurance system, as well as professional dissemination and exploitation activities. With VET5.0, we will establish an Excellence Academy comprising six CoVEs. This will involve developing sustainability concepts to facilitate the Academy's future expansion, as well as testing the onboarding process for new regions.

hr.name: AGENCIJA ZA STRUKOVNO OBRAZOVANJE I OBRAZOVANJE ODRASLIH

101260687.title: ELIA - Excellence in Learning, Innovation, and Agriculture: A Centre of Vocational Excellence for the Olive Sector
101260687.summary:
The ELIA (Excellence and Learning for the Innovation of Agriculture) project proposes the establishment of a transnational Centre of Vocational Excellence (CoVE) for the olive production sector—one of Europe's most traditional yet increasingly vulnerable agri-food domains. Operating across seven countries (Greece, Italy, Cyprus, Spain, Portugal, Croatia, and Turkey), ELIA addresses urgent challenges posed by climate change, digital transition, skills mismatches, and rural exclusion.

Grounded in extensive partner-led needs analyses and aligned with the European Green Deal, the Digital Education Action Plan, and the Council Recommendations on VET and micro-credentials, ELIA aims to transform vocational training into a flexible, inclusive, and innovation-driven system. The project will co-create modular curricula and EU-aligned micro-credentials, develop digital and sustainability-focused training for both learners and educators, and pilot structured mobility and work-based learning schemes in collaboration with SMEs, cooperatives, and policy makers.

Through deep, sustained cooperation between VET providers, industry actors, and public authorities, ELIA will enhance regional innovation capacity, strengthen policy frameworks for skills recognition, and offer scalable models of excellence that directly contribute to green growth and social resilience. It will deliver high-quality, labour market-relevant education that empowers individuals, revitalises rural economies, and advances systemic reform in the vocational landscape across Europe.

101090539.action_type: Cooperation Partnerships in the field of Education and Training – European NGOs
101090539.title: V-CALC - Volunteering Impact Measurement Training in Europe
101090539.summary: Evidence shows that volunteering is beneficial in many fields, unfortunately the methods used to measure the impact of volunteering are lacking.  The V-Calc project will enable 800 volunteer managers and coordinators of all ages & diversity to measure and understand the impact of their volunteers. The objectives are to: develop a suitable methodology for gathering data about the numbers and profiles of volunteers, their motivation and impact on society and individual volunteer learning; Create and put in place the user-friendly online platform to gather the information from primary and secondary sources; Train and develop the capacity of volunteer managers and coordinators to gather and provide information about the impact of the volunteers that they engage with and in their countries more widely; Ensure the sustainability of project results by developing the community of practitioners from across Europe in order to promote the use of the V-Calculator and the importance of measuring volunteering for the development of better evidence based policies. The training programme in the use of the volunteer impact measurement methodology will lead to increased quality in the work, activities and practices of the volunteering organisations and institutions involved. It will introduce new actors to the importance of volunteer impact measurement across all sectors and fields that engage volunteers. Through the V-CALC project we will build the capacity of organisations to work transnationally and across sectors and at the same time address common needs and priorities for the volunteer-involving stakeholders in the fields of education, training, youth and sport, amongst others.  The online platform, impact measurement methodology and training activities, together with the policy development work, will enable transformation and change at individual, organisational and sectoral level, leading to improvements and new approaches, in a wide variety of different volunteering contexts.

101090971.action_type: Cooperation Partnerships in the field of Education and Training – European NGOs
101090971.title: ECEM - Enriching Communities through Engaged Mobilities
101090971.summary:
Inclusion and civic engagement are two horizontal priorities of the Erasmus+ programme 2021-2027, but approached as individual elements.  Based on this observation, the Enriching Communities through Engaged Mobilities (ECEM) project wants to further develop the connections between civic engagement, internationalisation and inclusion. Ensuring active citizenship and participation in society is understood as a key element in the process of making mobilities more inclusive and societies more integrated. Ensuring a sense of belonging through actively participating in society, enforces inclusive and integrated societies at European level.
The ECEM project seeks to: (a) Increase the civic engagement component of mobilities in the field of internationalisation of Higher Education, contributing to making interaction with local communities the norm in mobilities (b) Ensuring recognition of learning outcomes for participants that take part in civic engagement initiatives. (c)  Improve the collaboration frameworks between Higher Education Institutions and other societal actors to make mobilities contribute to societal change and common European values.
The project brings together organisations representing students, Higher Education Institutions, national funding agencies and civil society parties and community organisers to create a cross-sectoral approach that improves policies and practices by creating tools to foster collaboration and improve implementation.  It builds on the experiences of the project partners in the fields of inclusion and engagement, trying to consolidate advances that have been made in the last programme cycle.
The project consortium will aim to influence the implementation of the current Erasmus+ programme at the different levels while paving the way for changes in the future Erasmus+ programme. It will do so through a combination of training events, research, policy materials and testing of activities on the ground.

101134702.action_type: Cooperation Partnerships in the field of Education and Training – European NGOs
101134702.title: SLIPS - “Service Learning in Primary Schools”
101134702.summary: Evidence shows that SL is beneficial but access to service learning in primary schools in Europe remains limited despite some growth in FE and in Secondary Education, notably through the Erasmus Plus SLUSIK project. SLIPS will upscale an existing Service Learning programme for secondary level for primary school pupils. Through its training programme it will enable 600 primary school teachers, 150 schools’ principals & governors, 75 schools and 90 policy makers to build capacity in SL. The objectives are: develop a suitable upscaled methodology for delivering service learning programmes in primary schools; Create and put in place the user-friendly online platform to train the primary school teachers; Train and develop the capacity of primary school teachers to deliver quality service learning in primary schools; Develop links between schools and civil society in order to better meet community needs; Ensure the sustainability of project results by developing the community of practitioners in order to promote the use of the the methodology and the importance of service learning for social inclusion, civic engagement, resilience, prosperity and sustainability. The training programme in Service Learning will lead to increased skills for primary school teachers leading to increased quality in the work, activities and practices of the schools, volunteering organisations and institutions involved. It will introduce new actors to volunteering, civil society and civic engagement. We will build the capacity of primary schools and primary school teachers to work transnationally and address common needs and priorities for children in the EEA.  The online platform, service learning methodology and training activities, as well as policy development work, will enable transformation and change at individual, organisational and sectoral level, leading to improvements, new approaches and upgraded skills in a variety of different formal and nonformal education context.

101184061.action_type: Cooperation Partnerships in the field of Education and Training – European NGOs
101184061.title: ETHLAE - Emerging Technologies for Holistic Literacy in Adult Education
101184061.summary:
The "Emerging Technologies for Holistic Literacy in Adult Education (ETHLAE)" project aims to address the challenge of effectively integrating emerging technologies into adult learning and education contexts. Despite extensive exploration of these technologies, there remains a gap in pedagogical approaches to ensure their meaningful incorporation, particularly in inclusive literacy and life skills programs for adults. Building on the findings from extensive research at a European level, ETHLAE aligns with EU policies like the Digital Education Action Plan to foster digital proficiency and understanding among learners.
 
Key Objectives:
1. Analyzing, Adapting, and Testing Methods to embed emerging technologies in the Adult Learning and Education (ALE) sector and in holistic literacy programs.
2. Supporting ALE Educators in designing and delivering holistic literacy education programs for adults in vulnerable situations, embedding emerging technologies when beneficial, and considering social, contextual, economical, and personal needs of educators and learners.
3. Addressing Inclusion and Diversity in ALE by improving the delivery of holistic literacy programs for adults in diverse states of exclusion.
4. Building Capacity of ALE educators in integrating emerging technologies into adult education, addressing digital transformation by providing resources, training, and support.
5. Enhancing Educator Competences, particularly in teaching methods, digital skills development, and teaching for sustainability, by  employing peer learning methods and fruitful exchange between adult educators and ALE staff. 
6. Promoting Local Learning Centers and Innovative Learning Spaces by piloting holistic literacy programs embedding emerging technologies in local ALE organizations.

Main Audiences:
Adult Learning and Education (ALE) educators
Adult learners 
Local authorities
Civil society organizations
Stakeholders in technology-driven education initiatives

101184321.action_type: Cooperation Partnerships in the field of Education and Training – European NGOs
101184321.title: ETI Labs - Erasmus Talent & Innovation Labs
101184321.summary:
The Erasmus Talent & Innovation Labs (ETI Labs) project is an ambitious and comprehensive initiative designed to bridge the gap between higher education and the labor market, enhancing the employability of students and recent graduates through innovative learning methodologies and strategic partnerships. 

The project aligns closely with the Erasmus+ Work Programme's focus on fostering quality, innovation, and internationalisation education. addressing key areas such as skill mismatch, employability, and the integration of learning with real-world business challenges while fostering a more dynamic, responsive, and interconnected European Education Area.

ETI Labs aims to create an integrated framework that connects academia with industry, focusing on developing skills that are in high demand in the contemporary job market. It involves the development of Talent & Innovation Labs, a recent-graduate traineeship track, and advocacy for improved University-Business Cooperation (UBC).

The primary objective is to enhance student employability and skill development, facilitate strategic alignment between education and market needs, and promote the integration of innovative educational practices within the higher education sector. This will be achieved by developing a new methodology inspired by the ‘Science Shop’ model to foster symbiotic relationships between academia and industry, including desk research on UBC and organising focus groups.

Morever the project will establish innovative Labs in Entrepreneurship, Sustainable Economy, and Digital Transformation to directly enhance student competencies, supported by European Digital Credentials for Learning (EDCs). ETI Labs will align recent graduate mobility with entry-level professional opportunities through comprehensive research and pilot traineeship programs.

The project will advocates for policies supporting enhanced UBC, leveraging strategic documents, and raising the stakeholders' and public's awareness on UBC.

101243952.action_type: Cooperation Partnerships in the field of Education and Training – European NGOs
101243952.title: ImpactBOX - Inclusion Impact Box: Unlocking the Power of Diversity in Education
101243952.summary: The ImpactBOX project aims at addressing the EU political commitment to a cross cutting priority for all education and trainingsectors and levels, focusing on capacity-building with a multi-level approach - starting from EU to local level. Its goal: to improve inclusive, digital, and sustainable strategies and practices in education and training organisations - considered as multipliers - to create transformative change by challenging current inequalities and environmental challenges. The consortium involves 5 full partners and 6 Affiliated Entities, ensuring impact from international to the local level through their extensive network of members and partners in several EU and non-EU countries. The primary target group of the project are the adult educators and staff working in the education and training sector. ImpactBOX is structured in 5 work packages.WP1 ensures the basic project management needs: project and financial management, dissemination and communication and quality assurance, monitoring quality and project progress.WP2 will gather resources and materials from the four core areas of the project: access and participation, inclusion and diversity, digital skills for inclusion and environmental sustainability. All resources and materials will be included in an free-of-charge e-learning platform. The WP3 includes a transnational in-person training on the project 4 core themes, as well as adapted local trainings based on the needs of the local organisation involved. WP4 will provide an impact assessment tool, validated by stakeholders and peer reviewing to education and training providers, CSOs and NGOs, to support them on their own assessment and impact measurement. WP5 focuses on policy and decision-makers including the development of policy recommendations using a bottom-up approach. The pedagogical approaches implemented will all make educational staff and managers of CSOs more aware and willing to practise inclusive approaches also at internal level.

101245382.action_type: Cooperation Partnerships in the field of Education and Training – European NGOs
101245382.title: DeStalk EU - Developing capacities to address stalkerware and digital violence against women across Europe
101245382.summary:
One in three women in Europe has experienced physical or sexual violence, one in five by an intimate partner. One in ten women has faced cyber violence, such as online stalking and non-consensual sharing of intimate images. The rise of digital technologies has amplified gender-based violence (GBV) creating a harmful continuum. 
DeStalk EU aims to address the digital dimension of GBV and achieve upgraded know-how through: • Transferring knowledge to victim support services (VSS) and perpetrator programmes (PP) to identify and respond to digital abuse. • Engaging public institutions and decision-makers to support the creation and promotion of territorial responses. • Raising awareness among communities about cyber violence against women and girls (CVAWG) to prevent all forms of abuse. • Empowering victims and offering solutions for both victims and perpetrators to break the cycle of violence. 
The project will strengthen professional capacities and community empowerment through delivering: • Mutual learning among 10 expert organizations across Europe. • A capacity-building program including e-learning in 8 languages. • Training sessions in 8 countries involving 420+ practitioners. • Adapted toolkits to ensure sustainable work of VSS and PP, and materials for public awareness and prevention, available in 8 languages. • Advocacy actions with the mobilisation of public entities and media in the relevant regions. • Public campaigns reaching 1k people in each country. • National events in 8 countries engaging 240 key actors, and a European event with 60 multipliers. • European guidelines for practitioners to address the digital dimension of violence against women. 
Thanks to the Erasmus+ framework, DeStalk EU will provide enhanced capacities and tools among over 740 experts in Europe to make a sustainable change in how GBV is addressed and will raise the awareness of 10k people among our communities across Europe to keep relationships safe for everyone offline and online.

101246086.action_type: Cooperation Partnerships in the field of Education and Training – European NGOs
101246086.title: SHIFT - Student-centred Higher Education Innovation for the Future of Teaching
101246086.summary:
The SHIFT project aims to transform higher education by embedding student-centred learning methodologies and developing flexible academic pathways that respond to students' needs and labour market demands. Higher education institutions (HEIs) must evolve to provide inclusive, adaptable, and internationally connected learning environments, ensuring that students actively shape their own educational experiences. SHIFT responds to the challenges of academic rigidity, skills mismatches, and the limited recognition of learning outcomes from mobility experiences, directly contributing to the priorities of the European Education Area and the Erasmus+ Programme.
The SHIFT project seeks to:
Empower students as co-creators of their learning experiences, promoting student-centred approaches across European HEIs.
Improve the recognition of skills and learning outcomes gained through international education, supporting both academic and professional progression.
Strengthen the capacity of academic staff to implement, assess, and refine student-centred teaching methods, ensuring inclusive and adaptable pedagogical practices.
Bridge the gap between higher education and the labour market, fostering structured cooperation between HEIs, students, and employers to align educational outcomes with workforce demands.
The project brings together European University Alliances, student organisations, policymakers, and research institutions to co-create methodologies and policy recommendations that support International education activities. It builds upon the experiences of the project partners in education policy, flexible learning, and skills recognition, contributing to the broader goal of implementing the European Degree and strengthening student-centred teaching.
The SHIFT consortium will influence policy development, institutional strategies, and teaching methodologies, ensuring that student-centred education becomes an embedded and sustainable practice in European Education.

101049682.action_type: Cooperation Partnerships in the field of Youth – European NGOs
101049682.title: WISEs4Youth - WISEs for Youth in Western Balkans
101049682.summary: WISEs4Youth general objective of this project is to develop training activities for social entrepreneurial skills development targeting potential young social entrepreneurs in Western Balkans. Below project specific objectives and number of targeted beneficiaries. 1. Promote youth social entrepreneurship in the Western Balkans region through training and mobility activities (such as study visits).2. Create replicable and sustainable training methodology and modules that will orient and guarantee and effective and targeted training implementation. 3. Promote mobility and exchanges between the different project partners countries through study visits organised in successful WISEs or social enterprises. 4. Implement structured training activities involving partners and young potential entrepreneurs, through the empirical application of training modules. 5. Strengthen the creation of regional WISEs and social enterprises networks in the region, promote the social impact of these business and achieving among others common growth and inclusion of young people. 6. Impact measurement from project results (Toolkit). The project main activities are: study visits, peer-to-peer events, trainings and final toolkit for beneficiaries. Number of beneficiaries: at least number 5 trained new young social entrepreneurs in each partnership countries. Through the dissemination of toolkit to at least number 10 young potential social entrepreneurs and 5 WISEs /social enterprises per partners’ country. Involvement of number 2 local or national authorities for each project partner country through the peer learning activities.

101134732.action_type: Cooperation Partnerships in the field of Youth – European NGOs
101134732.title: WHGD - Women's Health Goes Digital
101134732.summary:
Main objectives are: 
1. To develop capacities of 12 partner organizations and WYAE member branches, and skills and competences of 50 youth workers to design and deliver innovative training programs in the field of women’s mental and reproductive health and rights

2. To develop an innovative training program and methodology for informing and educating girls and young women on women’s mental and reproductive health and rights

3. To develop innovative digital platform which will provide information and education for girls and young women on mental and reproductive health and rights 

4. To inform and educate 480 girls and young women, including those with fewer opportunities, on women’s mental and reproductive health and rights 

5. To design policy recommendations and raise awareness on women’s mental and reproductive health and rights among 100.000 girls and young women, decision-makers, experts, the media and the general public

Several tangible outcomes will be produced as a result of the activities, such as: handbook with best practices, approaches and methodologies, a training program containing step-by-step activities, digital platform, and 2 policy recommendations.

Project will involve 701 direct participants - mainly young women and girls, including 200 of those with fewer opportunities, and trainers/youth workers from partner organizations.

The project will involve various activities, including coordination meetings of the project team, meetings for the exchange of best practices, 2 trainings of trainers, conference with decision-makers, online awareness raising campaign, MOOC, etc.

101245828.action_type: Cooperation Partnerships in the field of Youth – European NGOs
101245828.title: youthinfo.ai - Youthinfo.ai: AI-Driven Innovation in Youth Information
101245828.summary:
Youthinfo.ai is an initiative empowering youth information workers and indirectly impacting the young individuals they engage with daily. The project aims to help youth information workers deliver their work better through the safe and effective application of AI.
The strategy focuses on equipping youth information coordinating structures and organisations with tools to respond to dynamic changes introduced by AI and augmenting the capacity of youth information workers (YIW) to comprehend AI features, nuances, including biases in algorithms. The implications for ethics, fairness, and information accuracy will be tackled through a participative approach, unlocking AI's full potential to meet evolving needs. Concrete examples through chatbots as information and conversation tools between YIW and young people will give a practical perspective of AI. 
Extensive research on AI in youth information will be conducted, and youth information workers can deliver personalised, accessible, and innovative support services to young people.The work comprises essential components: desk research and user research on how knowledgeable youth info workers are on AI, on ethics and the use of chatbots as an AI tool for more inclusivity. The project will enhance YIW knowledge and skills by providing a series of webinars on AI, ethics and chatbots and a training on AI and automation. The guidelines on ethics and the use of chatbots based on a testing phase will provide concrete recommendations for a safe and helpful use of AI in youth info work. The national dissemination event and final seminars will create synergies with policymakers, other youth organisations and other relevant stakeholders. 
In summary, youthinfo.ai aims to understand how European YIW can benefit from AI in their work as a helpful assistant and not a competitor. It will empower youth information workers to use AI tools in promoting democratic values, civic engagement, and informed decision-making among young people.

2021-1-BE02-KA220-ADU-000033662.title: De-escalating Polarization in Europe
2021-1-BE02-KA220-ADU-000033662.summary:
<< Background >>

The CQ+ Project Consortium embarked on a mission to enhance cultural intelligence (CQ) across Europe, recognizing culture as a defining aspect that shapes behavior, belonging, motivation, and efficacy. CQ surpasses cultural sensitivity, emphasizing the skills essential for successful navigation of diverse cultural contexts. With European identity grounded in cultural diversity, the project aimed to cultivate tolerance and CQ skills among citizens amidst rising racism, xenophobia, and hate crimes. The imperative to counteract division and protect values of peace and acceptance fueled the consortium's determination. Identifying an unmet need, the project focused on creating targeted educational materials for citizens and adult learners to develop CQ, countering racism and prejudice. To facilitate this, a CQ+ in-service training program for adult educators was devised, integrating CQ as a continuous skill requiring improvement. The program addressed pedagogic practices and didactic skills for online learning environments, aligning with the central needs of enhancing cultural understanding and combating intolerance.

<< Objectives >>

The overall objective of the CQ+ project is to address polarization in Europe by supporting adult learners of all ages,
abilities, professions and background to develop their cultural intelligence and appreciation and tolerance of diversity. We achieve this through the development of a comprehensive package of training supports that address adult educators as the facilitators of community-based, informal and non-learning and learning resources that directly engage adult learners interested in developing their cultural intelligence. The business case for promoting diversity and inclusion has never been more compelling as we emerge from a post-COVID era, as ultimately having more diverse communities and organisations and building inclusive cultures through the development of citizen-level cultural intelligence is in the end about addressing inequality, which is a central tenet of the new Erasmus+ Programme and EU social policy. We live in a world with exponentially increasing connectivity across all sectors, communities, businesses, classrooms and individuals alike. With global collaboration becoming progressively instrumental for social and economic success, cultural intelligence is now more important than ever in our daily lives.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were actioned by the project consortium during the 24-months of the project:
Action 1 – establish local advisory committees to ensure that the input and perspectives of key local stakeholders & associate partners are integral to the project work plan and development approach.  Each partner decided if they did this in a formal setting or through informal interactions.
Action 2 - design, develop, test, revise, translate and produce a toolkit of 20 Interactive Infographic resources to build Cultural Intelligence amongst a diverse range of adult learner groups based on the proposed Cultural Intelligence  model
Action 3 - design, develop, test, revise, translate and produce a needs-led tailored in-service training programme for frontline  educators to support them to work in culturally diverse and online learning environments
Action 4 - create the CQ+ MOOC & Community of Practice using appropriate and accessible web-based environments and media platforms 
Action 5 - implement in-service training with front-line educators through a cascading model of training
Action 6 - pilot and implement the Toolkit of Interactive Infographics and the MOOC & Community of Practice with the project target groups
Action 7 - animate, share and promote the project results extensively at local, regional, national and EU level through our extensive network of contacts, associate partners and adult education stakeholders
Action 8 - measure the impact of the project on our target groups and inform policy debates based on our practical
implementation experience
Action 9 – host multiplier events to engage key target groups and stakeholders locally in order to share the project results and promote the transfer and use of them in diverse learning settings and online learning environments
Action 10 - network adult learners, adult educators and service providers transnationally via the proposed Community of Practice incorporating a European dimension into our project results and sustain this platform for a further 5 years after the active funding period of the project.

<< Results >>

The CQ+ Project delivered the following 3 project results:
1.) CQ+ Toolkit of Interactive Infographics for build cultural intelligence
2.) In-service Training Programme for Front-line Adult Educators that develops their pedagogic practice and didactic skills to facilitate learning in multi-cultural and digitised learning environments
3.) CQ+ MOOC and Community of Practice that ensures the project results of CQ+ are widely available to significant sectors of adult education and opportunities for Pan-European collaboration are fostered and achieved.
In addition, we delivered the following KPIs over the lifetime of the project:
- 77 adult educators completed the in-service training and start to integrate the new resources into their day-to-day teaching practice (target 54) (note this includes some learners as well as Blenders, Squaredot and KMOP combined their PR1 and PR2 piloting; 
- 52 adult learners joined the PR1 Interactive infographic country pilots;
- 20 Interactive Infographics were developed to support the development of cultural intelligence amongst adult learners, young people and EU citizens to build their knowledge and competences in this critical skill
- 164 adult learners, adult educators and front-line professionals, etc., attending the
multiplier events in BE, IE, DE, PT, ES, CY, AT and CZ (Target was 160)
- 26 adult education managers and trainers, community leaders, integration workers and trainers, adult learners,
academics, policy makers, etc., attended the Final Conference in Belgium on October 24 when the CQ+ project and all its results were presented and when all partners presented their experiences in their local setting.  An additional 70 participants were present at the keynote of Blenders on the “Impact Into Play” event earlier in October.  Target reach was 70.
-  There was a target of 200 registered members of the Community of Practice.  This we could not exactly track as we removed the requirement to register in order to make the Community of Practice more accessible.  We know however that the CQ+ MOOC was visited by 321 users.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2021-1-CZ01-KA220-ADU-000033499.title: Integrating the European Knowledge in employment and entrepreneurship for Disadvantaged Groups
2021-1-CZ01-KA220-ADU-000033499.summary:
<< Background >>

Disadvantaged, vulnerable groups are deeply affected by unemployment and social exclusion, as low-income families with children face difficulties in finding affordable childcare and migrants encounter unprecedented barriers in the job market.
The project partners applied for this project because they wanted to create innovative learning opportunities for social inclusion groups, such as women, seniors, unemployed, migrants and Romani, using interactive techniques, topics, and digital tools. The main needs that they addressed were:
•	The need to boost the social integration of the target groups through employment or entrepreneurship, by enhancing their employability, upskilling, innovation, social mobility, and equality.
•	The need to develop a comprehensive approach and endorse a number of goals in entrepreneurial training and employment, in order to support the implementation of national inclusion strategies and the Council Recommendation of their Integration.
•	The need to improve the digital competence, connectivity, innovation, and business environment of the target groups, by providing them with access to online platforms, virtual learning environments, digital tools and resources.

<< Objectives >>

The project PAL PUSH II offered innovative learning opportunities for social inclusion groups, such as women, seniors, unemployed, migrants and Romani, using interactive techniques, topics, and digital tools. The main aim was to improve their social integration through employment or entrepreneurship. The project tackled several priorities, such as improving employability, upskilling, innovation, social mobility, and equality for the target groups. The project used advanced integrated approaches, such as blended learning, coaching, apprenticeships, and digital literacy. The specific objectives of the project were to enhance the entrepreneurial and employability competences, increase the knowledge and skills, deliver the tools to develop the digital competence, support the start-up of new enterprises, reduce the unemployment in post-COVID era, foster the cooperation and networking, boost the digital connectivity and innovation, and raise the growth potential of the entrepreneurs from underrepresented groups.

<< Implementation >>

•	Mapping the target groups’ needs in the post-COVID era and adapting existing training materials, based on online discussions, research, stakeholder engagement, and roundtables to develop two curriculum plans.
•	Enhancing inclusive entrepreneurship education and coaching services, by developing, translating, and piloting an entrepreneurial curriculum and materials (10 modules), and providing personalized coaching services to new entrepreneurs.
•	Supporting inclusive employment through upskilling, by developing, translating, and piloting an inclusive employment curriculum and materials (10 modules).
•	Speed-up Dating and Apprenticeship activities at local and international level, by developing and piloting these innovative support actions at local level through multiplier events and apprenticeship procedures.
•	Developing and maintaining an online platform and a virtual learning environment, which provide access to the training materials, modules, tools, and resources developed by the project.
•	Creating and expanding a network of stakeholders, partners, and beneficiaries, which facilitate the exchange of good practices, experiences and opportunities among the target groups and the relevant actors in the field of social inclusion, entrepreneurship and employment.
•	Conducting impact assessment and evaluation reports, which document the achievements, challenges and lessons learned from the project implementation and provide recommendations for future actions and improvements.

<< Results >>

•	Two curricula and materials for inclusive entrepreneurship and employment, covering 10 modules each, such as business planning, marketing, financial management, communication skills, etc.
•	Personalized coaching services to new entrepreneurs, helping them to identify their strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats, and to develop their business ideas and plans.
•	Speed-up dating and apprenticeship activities at local and international level, enabling the target groups to network with potential employers, mentors, investors, partners, and customers.
•	An online website and library of the project results, which provide access to the training materials, modules, tools and resources developed by the project.
•	A network of stakeholders, partners and beneficiaries, which facilitate the exchange of good practices, experiences and opportunities among the target groups and the relevant actors in the field of social inclusion, entrepreneurship and employment.
•	Impact assessment and evaluation reports, which document the achievements, challenges and lessons learned from the project implementation and provide recommendations for future actions and improvements.

2021-1-CZ01-KA220-ADU-000035354.title: Quality rating system for Adult Learning Providers
2021-1-CZ01-KA220-ADU-000035354.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated in response to the need for a comprehensive quality assurance system in adult education, a key priority in all partner countries. Adult learning institutions (ALI) operate in a largely unregulated market, where quality standards are inconsistent. This lack of standardization impacts the reliability of educational services and the ability of institutions to meet the requirements of learners, employers, and public authorities. The project addresses the absence of a quality rating system, which is crucial for informing adult learners about available education options and ensuring high standards of education delivery. It also supports the development of new tools and methodologies to enhance the quality and transparency of adult education services, ensuring that educational institutions can better respond to social and economic demands.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objective of this project was to create a structured and transparent quality rating system for adult learning institutions (ALI) across participating countries. This system aims to improve the quality of adult education by providing a clear mechanism for evaluating and ranking institutions based on defined quality criteria. By implementing this model, the project sought to: (a) enhance the quality standards of educational institutions, (b) offer a reliable framework for learners to make informed choices regarding education providers, and (c) promote competition and improvement within the sector. The project also aimed to equip educational institutions with the tools to self-assess and improve, while providing external evaluators with methodologies to ensure objective, standardized assessments. Ultimately, this initiative supports lifelong learning by fostering an environment of quality and accountability, benefiting learners, institutions, and stakeholders alike.

<< Implementation >>

In the project, we successfully implemented all activities as outlined in the original application. These included:
1. Common quality rating model setup: We developed a unified quality rating model for adult learning institutions (ALI). This involved expert consultations with stakeholders across partner countries to define quality levels, criteria, and evaluation procedures for educational institutions.
2. Development of methodologies and related documents: We created a set of methodologies as planned, including a self-evaluation methodology for ALI, an external assessor evaluation methodology and a preparation methodology for educational institutions. These documents provided standardized approaches to ensure consistency in the rating process.  All methodologies are covered by a general document.
3. Pilot preparation: We selected assessors and a sample of adult learning institutions in each partner country. Both groups received training on the evaluation procedures, with pilot institutions testing the rating model.
4. Pilot rollout: The rating model was piloted across selected institutions, which completed self-evaluations. External assessors then verified these assessments and feedback was gathered from both assessors and institutions to refine the model.
5. Creation of online tools: We developed an online platform to support the rating process, including e-learning modules for assessors and institutions.

<< Results >>

The project produced several key outputs and results:

1. General document:
- A comprehensive document detailing the QUALTRACK model, its justification, and development.
- A description of the assessment process.
- An explanation of each assessment area, based on evaluation criteria. Each criterion is thoroughly described, including sub-criteria and methods of evaluation, evidence sources (documentation) and a guide for external assessors.
- An additional section for each area, known as the “badge,” which allows institutions to earn extra recognition.
- Suggestions for further organizational development, including additional rating scales and sources of inspiration.

2. Self-evaluation tools: This includes a self-evaluation questionnaire for institutions, a checklist for external assessors, a set of guiding questions for on-site evaluation visits and feedback questionnaires for all stakeholders involved in the assessment process.

3. International comparison: A report comparing approaches to quality assessment of educational institutions in the partner countries.

4. Recommendations for public authorities: Based on the experience gained during project implementation, recommendations were developed to guide public authorities in enhancing quality assurance systems.

5. E-learning courses: Courses were developed for both educational institutions and external assessors, available on an online platform (Moodle).

6. Online platform and website: A dedicated online tool was created, along with the project’s website, which serves as a resource hub for institutions and assessors. This platform includes e-learning modules and other digital resources.

7. Multiplier event: Presentations and outcomes from an international conference organized as part of the project.

8. Webinar and dissemination: A recorded webinar to share the project results, along with newsletters, a Facebook profile and other dissemination materials to promote the project outcomes.

9. Operational results: These include the actual assessment results of the participating institutions, recommendations for refining the assessment model and methodologies.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business
Reaching the policy level/dialogue with decision makers

2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000026992.title: MIGRACTION: Migrants inclusion through entrepreneruship supported by business sector
2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000026992.summary:
<< Background >>

Since 2015, migration has risen high on the agendas of governments and development partners, following its historic inclusion in the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and as a response to large flows of migrants and refugees that have occurred in different parts of the world. In September 2016, governments adopted the New York Declaration, which calls for strengthening international cooperation on migration and forced displacement and for the development and adoption of two collaborative instruments – a global compact for safe, orderly and regular migration, and a global compact on refugees. Both compacts emphasize the issue of socioeconomic integration of both migrants and refugees, including through support to self-employment and entrepreneurship. They are based on the premise that migrants and refugees can contribute positively to the development of communities back at home or in their new places of residence, provided that their skills, capabilities and entrepreneurial spirit – often acquired in migration – are given sufficient support and recognition.

<< Objectives >>

●	to support the entrepreneurship of migrants, asylum seekers and refugees
●	to involve professionals from business and social areas in educational communities for inclusive entrepreneurship
●	to identify business opportunities for migrants, asylum seekers and refugees
●	to design and implement a digital environment for business incubation and mentoring
●	to develop an application for financial and legal assessment of new entrepreneurs with migrant or refugee background
●	to create and foster local stakeholder groups in order to strengthen the topic 

<< Implementation >>

PR1 included two activities in particular: Identification of the start-up ecosystem and relevant stakeholders in the respective countries, Development of materials to facilitate the recruitment and involvement of trainers and mentors in incubation programs.
PR2 consisted in an online tool to collect and disseminate business: Definition of selection criterias, Elaboration of  a methodological framework, local workshops with relevant stakeholders, Description of 8 business opportunities, elaboration of mentoring plans.
PR3: Digital platform for financial and legal assessment: Creation of an E-Learning platform on financial and legal mechanisms regarding entrepreneurship in 5 countries, study and identifying  needs in each country, elaboration of contents, design of the e-learning application, testing with the target group.
In PR4, 6 E-learning modules in 6 languages where developed, which support Incubation programmes and can also be used for self-studying: Training/incubation experiences for migrant people at risk of exclusion were analysed, we defined the incubation curricula, designed contents and resources and tested and validated the tool. 

<< Results >>

WP2: Communication and Dissemination: Project website in 6 languages, 9 newsletters, 9 videoclips, Social Media profils and regular posts 
WP3 (PR1): Recruiting professionals: Creation of local stakeholder groups, Definition of selection process and set of selection criteria for mentors recruitment, Call for professionals (Video & Poster), Definition of new models for volunteering plans in 4 languages 
WP4 (PR2) Business Ideas: Methodological framework to identify and analyse business opportunities, description of 8 (new) business ideas from and for migrant persons; Interviews with these persons and video clips, User-friendly and appealing digital platform in order to explain and business ideas, 8 mentoring plans drafted 
WP5 (PR3) Digital assessment tool: Realization of focus groups on national and transnational level,  E-Learning Modules on the financial and legal mechanisms existing in the different partner countries, Testing, evaluation of the BETA version, launch of the final version
WP6 (PR4) Developing a digital environment for business incubation:12 incubation models analysed, 6 modules on entrepreneurship designed in 6 languages, testing, evaluation of the BETA version, launch of the final version
topics: Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000030466.title: UNITED GENERATIONS
2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000030466.summary:
<< Background >>

Ageing is a global phenomenon. The world population is ageing causing changes in the society as whole. Senior citizens represent an important and ever growing part of our European population, economy and society: Nowadays 20% of the Berlin population (700.000 people) and 22% of the Erfurt population (50.000 people) is over 65 years old.
