This poses manifold questions as to how member states can best ensure social inclusion, active citizenship and participation in life, economy and the society, access to services, goods and opportunities in order to enable healthy well-being and independent living thus minimizing the cost on their families, the society and the economy in general. Therefore, the project will address the above mentioned challenges and collaborate with partners on building interactive tools to address them.


<< Objectives >>

The Europe 2020 Strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth acknowledges LifeLong Learning and digital skill development as key elements in response to the current economic crisis and demographic aging. By improving adults' ability to adapt to changes in the labor market, the family and the society, a contribution to the overcoming of the economic crisis, as well as the achievement of the Europe 2020 targets can be made. New adult learning possibilities provide upgrade- as well as re-skilling opportunities for those affected by unemployment and aging, while at the same time important contributions to social inclusion, active citizenship and personal development are being made.
Yet, there is a growing consensus that adult learning is currently the weakest unit in developing national lifelong-learning systems. Participation in adult learning has continued to grow slowly, from 9,8 % of the 25-64 year-old population in 2005 to only 10,7 % in 2014, thus making the increased ‘ET2020’ target of 15 % by 2020 an even greater challenge.


<< Implementation >>

The consortium consists of 7 partners, from 6 EU countries which cover a wide range of expertise. The United Generations project is complementary to previous projects, as apart from the development of a powerful and dynamic platform specially designed to unite and link seniors across Europe, the project proposes to deliver a targeted and high quality series of digital learning opportunities, which are expected to bring systemic changes on senior citizens’ health and wellbeing, social inclusion, active participation and personal development, thus meetings the targets of the EU 2020 for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth and the ET 2020 Strategies for Adult learning, as well as on improving the PIAAC results in the acquisition of adults’ digital and language competences.

We implemented the following activities: 

Research and data collection that was presented in a structured, visual format to emphasize the importance of lifelong learning and intergenerational engagement, promoting active aging and digital inclusion. The consortium created seven Mapping Intergenerational Learning focused on Basic Skills reports. 

Development of Learning Pathways: The consortium worked on creating an innovative learning pathway program, both online and in-house, aimed at helping senior citizens acquire digital and literacy skills. This program was complemented by a learning pack supported by data from the research. We created and disseminate a Generations United Online: Toolkit for digitally oriented learning pathways strategies- upskilling programmes. We also created and disseminate the Guidebook on Development and Implementation of Strategies for Up-skilling Adults with various tips for adult educators to implement the Program of United Generations. 

Creation of a Digital and English Literacy Backpack: This “backpack” was designed to address the educational needs of senior citizens. It included a Digital and Literacy Competence Framework, online and paper manuals, and a strategic campaign promoting digital active aging, in alignment with the EU Adult Learning Agenda. It included the Digital and Literacy Competence Framework, which is a structured framework outlining the necessary competencies for digital literacy, tailored specifically for seniors. The Open Badges were used in the project as a multi-level assessment system designed to validate and recognize the digital and literacy skills acquired by the senior citizens.

Development of an Interactive Online Tool: A dynamic online tool was developed to support the digital up-skilling of adults, helping them live self-determined lives. This tool used data from self-assessments and benchmarks to evaluate users’ skills.

Launch of the United Generations Platform: The project developed and launched an interactive online platform using cutting-edge technology to connect seniors with younger generations across Europe.

Pilot Testing and Training Modules: The project included pilot testing of digital and English literacy modules in the 7 partner regions. These pilots help assess and refine the materials and strategies before full implementation across all partner countries.

Blended Mobility and Learning Events: Specific events were organized where participants engaged in both in-person and online training to test and analyze project outputs. There was a Joint Staff Training (C1) in Cyprus which focused on training the project staff, which includes teachers, trainers, and researchers. The goal was to prepare them to better support the senior citizens in acquiring digital and literacy skills. 
We implemented a Blended Mobility of Adult Learners (C2) that targeted the adult learners themselves, particularly seniors, and used a blended approach combining online and physical mobility learning methods. Seniors participated face-to-face learning sessions in Croatia to improve their digital and English literacy skills.

Various transnational project meetings

<< Results >>

The most important results to be expected during the project and on its completion are the following:
1. An innovative learning pathway program (offered on-line and in-house) to acquire digital and literacy skills to be accompanied with a learning pack supported by the targeted framework and data from the survey.
2. The complete “Digital and English Literacy backpack” designed to meet the physical, mental and scientific needs of senior citizens that will include the: Digital and Literacy Competence Framework, on-line/on-paper manuals, strategic campaign etc. for Digital Active Aging in support of the value of EU Agenda for Adult Learning.
3. The dynamic and interactive online tool, based on data to support the digital up-skilling of adults to contribute to a self- determined life as long as possible. The online tool will record adults' data taken from the self- assessment (i.e. stocktaking-audit) and at the same time generate relevant data based on a profiling system that will evaluate their skills against benchmarks and indicators as set in the framework developed. Through a multi-level assessment system  from self-assessment to peer-review-mentoring and external assessment for validation purposes following a mechanism widely used the Open Badges, complying with the 2016 EC Recommendation for the skills guarantee.
4. The upload of a dynamic and interactive online platform based on cutting edge technology named United Generations, which will link adults and young people.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000033524.title: Becoming a global witness via digital toolkit
2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000033524.summary:
<< Background >>

The reason of application for this project was to realise and implement the idea of the DIG-GSW project which was created based on the common need of the partner's organizations for the development of qualifications for adult trainers on the national and European level in terms of promoting global citizenship through "Global Social Witnessing". This project is complementary to other projects already carried out by the participating organizations. The DIG-GSW project thus needed to be carried out transnationally as this made it possible for partners from different EU Member States with complementary expertise and interests in the topic adult training and technology, to exchange and pool their knowledge/resources to contribute to developing a novel adult training toolkit. Moreover, the synergy between international organizations and adults, guaranteed the knowledge and comprehension of different cultural realities and stimulated intercultural dialogue.

<< Objectives >>

The DIG-GSW project implemented the following objectives: 
OB1: To develop new methods and tools of GSW for education 
OB2: To establish 'cosmopolitan education' for adults 
OB3: To develop skills for critical humility in the global political processes 
OB4: To strengthen the professional profile of trainers, by using this innovative material of GSW 
OB5: To disseminate and exploit the outputs of the DIG-GSW project and in particular ensure that the innovative toolkit is openly available to all stakeholders across Europe. 

TARGET GROUPS (TGs) 
TG1: the primary TG are EU trainers as these will be able to exploit the training toolkit to help adults to become mature global citizens; 
TG2: the secondary TG is adults as they will become aware of and understands the wider world - and their place in it; 
TG3: the third TG consists of stakeholders related to the adult sector and other members of local communities including policy makers

<< Implementation >>

Activities implemented:

1. agreeing on the logo of the project in its beginning, so as to be easily recognised 
2. creating a DIG-GSW website and a Curriculum on GSW with data on the project, its IOs, events, articles, material, pictures etc., which was the first place to turn to for information 
3. producing a learning platform (www.lms.dig-gsw.eu) by selecting refugee camps, inviting refugees to interviews, interviewing and recoding, editing recordings, transcribing all interview texts, translating them, etc.
4. using social media(like Facebook) and multimedia channels to disseminate the outcome, updating them regularly, posting news, outcome, activities 
5. carefully organising multiplier events 
6. carefully organising the LTTA 
7. carefully organising the TPMs 
8. planing press releases and newsletters 
9. releasing articles on specialized magazines, papers and scientific journals nationally and internationally, informing about the outcome of the project 
10. pursuing interaction with other current projects 
11. pursuing contacts with shareholders, with local and regional administration, organisations and policy makers.

<< Results >>

To foster the emergent human capacity to mindfully attend to global events with an embodied awareness was the main outcome of the DIG-GSW project. More specifically, the project produced the following results: 

- The creation new ideas, strategies, and tools to help adults become mature global citizens in our times of disruption and transformation 
- Increasing the awareness and motivation of adults about global social realities 
- Generating compassionate awareness and interconnectedness while deepening the felt sense as a global human 
- Leaning into an embodied practice of compassionate global citizenship 
- Enhancing the skills of trainers, by using an innovative material to help adults become mature global citizens 
- Empowering bonds among people 

The main outputs of the project are: 
- A Curriculum on GSW
- An e-Learning Platform on GSW. The e-learning course is open for use from any stakeholder who has interest in the learning material it includes. Moreover,
- four TPMs took place to ensure the smooth implementation of the project 
- one LTTA took place in Germany to train adult learners in developing inter-bodily resonance competence and emotional intelligence 
- five multiplier events took place, one in each partner country aimed at raising awareness of the DIG-GSW project. 
Additionally, to the above mentioned: 
- Partner organizations became more known and reputable among other associates, especially in other countries of Europe, so that they could acquire more contacts within them.
- Participants became more skilled regarding the project’s fields. Also, they could profit through their communication with their European colleagues by broadening their horizons. 
- Partners benefited from the DIG-GSW project by enhancing their management skills, assessment competency, their abilities and ways to disseminate the results, how to make good use of the knowledge acquired, and achieve feasibility of goals.

2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000033541.title: European Certificates and Accreditation for European Projects
2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000033541.summary:
<< Background >>

The results of our needs analysis from 2020 among adult education providers, focusing on trainers, course designers, advisers, and administrative staff, highlighted several key organizational issues and the need for digital solutions to address certification challenges in adult education. More than 85% of participants (86.5%) expressed a strong need for evidence-based approaches to certification, emphasizing the importance of accredited certificates. Such certification is crucial for facilitating entry into labor markets and enhancing the importance and credibility of adult education initiatives. Concerning remote work and elearnings possibilities in adult education the resondants of the stufy stated that these issues have to be a crucial aspect in the certification criteria, which are needed in adult education. There is a need to improve quality and more than 70 % of the participants emphasized this need to improve the quality of adult education via a certification system. In addtion to that they pointed on the need that policy makers should be provided with recommendations and innovative ideas in this field and that accreditation is an important issue.

<< Objectives >>

The EU-CERT project is dedicated to improving adult education by promoting the results of ERASMUS+ projects. Currently, these projects often lack certification or accreditation. In a needs analysis conducted in winter 2020 with 200 trainers and 50 adult education providers, 87% of participants reported concerns about the transparency and quality of European adult education project outcomes, which are often difficult to integrate into daily practice. The EU-CERT project aims to address these issues by enhancing the quality of adult education and ensuring that providers can access high-quality, practical education results derived from excellent projects. We will develop a mechanism to monitor the effectiveness of adult education projects through an accreditation system based on clear criteria and a robust accreditation procedure. This system will support shared values in adult education and serve as a foundation for civic engagement, driven by excellent educational approaches. Furthermore, the project will foster participation among European adult educators in a high-quality network with standardized practices. By promoting the ERASMUS+ initiative, the accreditation system will enhance transparency and visibility across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

In the project EU-CERT a core activity was to have a closer look at adult education in the different partner countries. This was basis to find adequate quality criteria for accreditation which fit to the situation in the countries and to adult education. We had a closer look at other accreditation system in other parts of education to make sure that the accreditation processes are relevant and adequate as well as user-friendly. We created the accreditation concept with the accreditation pocesses and discussed it on a European basis. After and Agreement on the criteria and the processes we designed the tool structure of the online platform and programmed the acceditation tooland the data-base behind it. We did design work to the user-friendly and created an accredition handbook which we also used to train the persons who used the accredition tool to accredite adult education organisations and materials during the piloting and the roll-out to adult education providers. In the end we provides feedback and certificates via the platform to the adult education providers and ensured smooth processes. To finalise the work we created a policy paper and a layman´s report on the accredition tool, the criteria and the processes as well as our experiences.

<< Results >>

The core results of the project are an online platform for accreditation and certification in adult education. The basis for this are the developed European Accreditation Quality criteria for adult eduction and European adult education projects.The process of accredition was specified and there is an option for (a) System / Institutional Accreditation as well as for (b) Product material, OER and Course Accreditation. Another result are also accreditations of organisations / institutions and materials in these fields in all partner countries. Moreover, an accreditation handbook was designed, which offers in insight into the platform, the criteria, the accreditation processes and offers a basis for the use of the platform in the future and supports future users. In addition to that a policy paper and a layman´s report were created to bring the results into public and towards policy makers.

2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000035090.title: Quid-Pro-Quo – Inter-generational Education to Ease Global Warming
2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000035090.summary:
<< Background >>

Climate change is one of the greatest social challenges of the 21st century. Due to its complexity and the need to develop solutions, contemporary education faces high demands on contemporary education. Climate education must be more strongly integrated into educational programs to sensitize people to the major challenges of climate change and a sustainable society. There is a call for learning models that promote intergenerational senior citizens and digital natives in dealing with climate change and demonstrate how important it is for all generations to play an active role in tackling climate change. These offerings must take a concrete approach to the people's living environments, show how everyday behavior can be changed to a sustainable lifestyle, and suggest alternative behaviors.

<< Objectives >>

Young people alone cannot change the world – it takes a collective effort to achieve an impact on reducing our carbon emissions and changing our consumption and waste production habits. Senior citizens have considerable tacit knowledge garnered during less affluent eras, when resourcefulness and imagination were needed to find quick fixes to problems. Many of these solutions, which are still relevant today and could be implemented across the whole of society, emerged due to shortages of raw materials, lower income thresholds than we see today, and a less wasteful consumer ethos throughout the community than one experiences today. The focus of the project is to demonstrate the considerable value that the tacit knowledge of older generations has in a climate change crisis, while at the same time introducing the latest high-tech applications that help reduce the carbon footprint of every individual. Calendar for Climate Change is a knowledge exchange project between young digital natives and older generations.

<< Implementation >>

The C4CC-Consortium developed, tested and implemented climate change resources as a part of an inter-generational model. In the first phase of the project, each partner established a support group of at least five experts. This group was set up to match resources to realistic needs in different national contexts. Once the development process began, the project partners extended their dissemination activities to the regional, national and international levels, reaching out to organizations and institutions working in the field of youth and senior citizens in different fields. During the project period, the consortium directly or indirectly reached over 15,000 people with the topic of climate change in Europe. These include pupils, students, senior citizens, teachers, youth workers, social educators and youth social workers, political decision-makers, school administrators and parents. They participated online or in person in multiplier events, piloting sessions, workshops and conferences.

<< Results >>

The main result is an interactive calendar, with training resources that support the implementation of 12 high-tech climate change solutions and 12 low-tech climate change solutions. Each resource comprises three elements: (1) an introductory/explainer video to present the concept/issue being addressed; (2) a step-by-step guide that demonstrates how to implement the low-tech or high-tech solution; (3) an example of the solution in practice. The resources are present in two formats: (1) a mobile calendar app where the explainer video and learning content can be downloaded for use on a smartphone - this is specifically designed for young digital natives; (2) an interactive printed calendar where seniors can access the learning content through the QR code reader on a smartphone. Partners also developed an in-service training programme for adult educators to ensure that they can successfully manage the inter-generational model being proposed; build their understanding of climate change mitigating actions; and also build their skills to enable them to develop media-rich learning content using different software programmes. The final project result comprises the Calendar for Climate Change Calendar App – allowing for the online sharing.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000035124.title: Guide Me Green
2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000035124.summary:
<< Background >>

Despite growing awareness of sustainable practices in tourism, there remains a significant gap in accessibility for individuals with lower education levels, limited budgets, or disabilities. These groups are often excluded from participating in sustainable tourism due to several factors:

PERCEIVED COST BARRIER: There is a widespread misconception that sustainable tourism is inherently more expensive than conventional tourism. 
LACK OF ACCESSIBLE INFORMATION: Sustainable and low-budget tourism offerings are frequently underrepresented in marketing efforts targeting disadvantaged adults. 
INCLUSIVE DESIGN AND ACCESSIBILITY: Existing sustainable tourism initiatives often overlook the specific needs of disadvantaged adults, such as accessibility considerations for individuals with disabilities or tailored educational materials for those with lower literacy levels.

The Guide Me Green project addressed these challenges by fostering a more inclusive and accessible approach to sustainable tourism. By targeting not only adult learners but also adult educators, policymakers, DMOs, and tourism professionals, we aimed to promote sustainable tourism practices that cater directly to the needs of disadvantaged adults. 

<< Objectives >>

1) Making sustainable tourism accessible to diverse, disadvantaged, and low-income groups by debunking misconceptions about its exclusivity.
2) Developing project materials specifically tailored to engage and involve diverse groups, promoting sustainable tourism as a tool for social inclusion.
3) Advocating for inclusive sustainable tourism with public authorities to drive adoption and foster the development of sustainable experiences. Partnering with educational, civil, and tourism organisations to enhance their inclusive offerings.
4) Educating adult learners and educators about sustainable tourism's benefits to local ecosystems, well-being, cultural heritage, and sustainable business development. This knowledge empowers individuals to make sustainable choices in travel and daily life.
5) Inspiring community action through collaborative projects and engaging stakeholders across sectors to create lifelong learning opportunities for adults.
6) Empowering adults with sustainability knowledge to enhance their lives and contribute positively to their communities


<< Implementation >>

1) MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES : We adhered to a structured Project Management Plan, facilitating regular partner meetings for effective communication and synergy. These efforts were pivotal in maintaining project alignment and progress.
2) QUALITY ASSURANCE ACTIVITIES: We implemented a rigorous quality assessment framework across all project phases, ensuring thorough research, meticulous design, effective implementation, comprehensive evaluation, and ongoing revision. This approach aimed to uphold the quality and relevance of project outcomes.
3) DISSEMINATION ACTIVITIES: Extensive dissemination activities were conducted to increase awareness of project activities and outcomes, particularly highlighting sustainable tourism's role in social inclusion. 
4) DEVELOPMENT OF CONCEPTUAL BACKGROUND/COLLECTION OF PRACTICES: We curated best practices in sustainable travel, focusing on inclusivity for socially disadvantaged and low-income groups. These practices informed the development of our Training Programme (PR 2) and Toolbox (PR 3), providing valuable resources for educators and stakeholders.
5) DEVELOPMENT OF TRAINING PROGRAMME, WEBSITE/OER: We created an interactive Training Programme and user-friendly Open Educational Resources (OER) accessible in multiple languages. These digital tools aimed to support lifelong learning in sustainable tourism, catering to diverse learner needs.
6) DEVELOPMENT OF TOOLBOX: Activities centered on promoting sustainable practices through the development of a Manifesto and Policy Recommendations, engaging training providers, civil organisations and community agents. 
7) LOCAL ACTIONS AND ENGAGEMENT: Targeted local actions and a comprehensive campaign were implemented to engage various stakeholders, including learners, educational providers, NGOs, and policymakers. These initiatives sought to raise awareness and advocate for inclusive tourism policies at different governance levels.

<< Results >>

1) MANUAL ON GOOD PRACTICES  AND FRAMEWORK: This manual compiles 99 exemplary practices in sustainable and inclusive tourism worldwide. Organised into four chapters tailored for distinct audiences—adult educators and trainers, public authorities and policymakers, tourism professionals, and the general public—the manual showcases diverse examples of learning activities, sustainable destinations, initiatives, and budget-friendly tourism offers. 
2) CREATION AND PILOT TESTING OF ONLINE TRAINING COURSE: We developed a comprehensive online training course comprising six modules focused on sustainable tourism strategies within budget constraints. Designed for accessibility and user-friendliness, the course accommodates diverse learners, including those new to sustainable tourism. Interactive audiovisual materials enhance engagement, and an e-learning environment facilitates asynchronous learning.
3) HANDBOOK FOR EDUCATORS AND TRAINERS: This additional tool assists adult educators and trainers in effectively integrating the Online Training Course content into their teaching methodologies, fostering knowledge transfer and application.
4) AWARENESS-RAISING CAMPAIGN: This initiative includes:
a) Production of 13 short videos (reels) targeting the general public
b) Hosting of 9 webinars tailored for adult educators, policymakers, and tourism professionals
c) Publication of 120 posts across three social media platforms
5) DEVELOPMENT OF GUIDE ME GREEN TOOLBOX: This toolbox facilitates the implementation of sustainable tourism practices and policies. It includes a Manifesto and Policy Recommendations aimed at promoting sustainable tourism principles.
6) ORGANISATION OF MULTIPLIER EVENTS: Five events were organised to disseminate project outcomes, promote collaboration among stakeholders, and encourage the adoption of sustainable and inclusive tourism practices.

2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000035188.title: GOLDEN SKILLS  - Parents as Teachers of Financial Literacy
2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000035188.summary:
<< Background >>

As a new era of growth and prosperity gathers pace, there are many families for whom the debt legacy of recent years remains a profound and ongoing problem. Debt consolidation and restructuring, negative equity mortgages, personal insolvency and vulture funds are terms that many adults across Europe are all too familiar with, along with repossessions of goods and property and evictions. These are the visible signs of the stress that many families are under. For many adults, a lack of financial knowledge is at the root of these ongoing problems.

<< Objectives >>

If we can learn anything from recent events in Europe, it is to recognise that financial literacy is a key skill for all Europeans if we are to achieve the inclusive and equitable society that is one of the EU's core objectives. Financial education is essential for life in the 21st century. Yet very little attention is paid to financial literacy in schools. Schools are not teaching children financial skills for real life. The big responsibility lies with parents, who are the most important role models for their children and from whom children learn how to manage their money. But how can parents be good teachers of financial literacy if no one supports them?

<< Implementation >>

During the development and pilot phase of the GOLDEN SKILLS project, the results achieved were considered in terms of resources, measures and people. 
1. this includes a range of appropriate learning resources for families that promote financial literacy. The partners have deliberately selected the different types of learning resources for their flexibility, adaptability and accessibility. All resources for family members are available via a smartphone and on mobile devices. 
2. an educational programme for parents to support their engagement with the newly developed learning resources for families 
3. a customised online learning portal has been developed and populated with innovative learning resources for families.
All resources developed are available in traditional and online formats in five partner languages and are available to all interested parties without restriction to meet the open access requirements of the ERASMUS+ programme.

<< Results >>

The project supports parents in teaching their children about financial literacy. The project provides parents with attractive and entertaining teaching tools that children can use on their mobile phones. Teenagers like to spend time on their mobile phones, and successful teaching materials need to adapt to this. The project team has developed 32 educational tools for teenagers aged 13 to 19. These 32 learning tools consist of 8 videos, 8 WebQuests, 
8 breakout rooms and 8 quizzes.
The teaching tools cover the following 8 financial education topics:
1. money and its importance in daily life 
2. budgeting and personal financial management 
3. financial maths 
4. income and earning money 
5. spending money 
6. saving money 
7. borrowing money 
8. the importance of financial knowledge for independent living 
All of the engaging resources created are accessible via mobile phone, tablet and computer. 
To further increase the appeal to young people, the project team has created a dedicated infographic for each topic. Each infographic contains a QR code.
Each QR code is assigned to exactly one of the 8 financial education topics.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000035207.title: Digital Social Entrepreneurship of seniors and adults with different abilities
2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000035207.summary:
<< Background >>

There is an alarmingly big number of seniors and adults with disabilities who lack the employment and regular salary/income. 
Quite often, both salaries of the employed citizens, as well as the pensions for the retired seniors, where exist - are not fully sufficient for the high costs of life in those “older” ages. More and more seniors and adults (with disabilities), thus, are looking forward to another way of regular money incoming into their households.

In addition, persons with disabilities often face societal barriers and disability evokes negative perceptions and discrimination in many societies. 

For this target group, formal education takes too much time and is not a preferred option to take. The adult education is a very appreciated option both for seniors and adults with disabilities and is perceived as a better option, as it is easier to enrol in an adult education programme, as well as the courses last shorter and are following the latest trends and needs of society and opportunities existing. 

The project responded to the outcomes of the survey implemented and regular work with our beneficiaries and educators of our organisations; by empowering for and promoting the digital social entrepreneurship among them.

<< Objectives >>

Motivation of partners in this project was to “equip” seniors and adults with disabilities with set of skills needed to work on personal development in fields of digital-social-entrepreneurial intelligence and creating (self-)employment opportunities proactively in today’s reality of employment uncertainty and the world of extinction of many known jobs and occupation now and even more in the future. 

With this project, we want our beneficiaries, seniors and adults with disabilities, to improve their digital social entrepreneurial skills, and we also aim to empower more adult educators for organising digital social entrepreneurial learning activities, in line with the newest updates.

Project objectives were:
-	Empower seniors and unemployed adults with disabilities for digital social entrepreneurship start-up.
-	Empower our adult educators and improve knowledge management of our organisations in theory and practice for building competences of educators in digital social entrepreneurship for seniors and adults with disabilities.
-	Exchange good practices and further develop quality strategic partnership among partners from 4 European countries with different realities in regards to employment and digital/social entrepreneurship.


<< Implementation >>

Project activities were:
-	A1 – Project Management activities throughout the duration of the whole project.
-	M1 – Kick-off meeting in Modena (IT) hosted by LINK DMT.
-	O1 – Handbook “Exploring Digital Social Entrepreneurship for seniors and adults with different abilities”; led by LINK DMT and co-lead by Zanandrea (IT); Produced in 5 languages.
-	M2 – Second meeting in Zadar (HR) hosted by Realization.
-	O2 – Curriculum “Empowering adult educators to encourage Digital Social Entrepreneurship start-ups among seniors and adults with different abilities”; led by CNELL and co-lead by Iteccion (RS); Produced in 5 languages.
-	O3 – Toolkit “Mentoring and supporting seniors and adults with different abilities for Digital Social Entrepreneurship start-up”; led by OH (DE) and co-lead by Iteccion (RS); Produced in 5 languages.
-	M3 – Third meeting in Pancevo (RS) hosted by Iteccion.
-	O4 – E-learning course “Digital Social Entrepreneurship start-up course for seniors and adults with different abilities”; led by Realization and co-lead by Wizard (HR); Produced in 5 languages.
-	C1 - LTTA Training of trainers; in Pancevo (RS) hosted by Iteccion.
-	E1, E2, E3, E4 – Open conferences in Zagreb (HR), Novi Sad (RS), Cento (IT), Hannover (DE)
-	M4 – Evaluation meeting in Munich (DE) hosted by OH.


<< Results >>

Intellectual Outputs:

O1 – Handbook “Exploring Digital Social Entrepreneurship for seniors and adults with different abilities”
Purpose: It is a step-by-step guide for successfully preparing seniors and adults with disabilities to start-up digital social business with simplified instructions on needed steps. The Handbook also serves as theoretical and conceptual resource for adult educators when organising further empowerment of beneficiaries in Digital Social Entrepreneurship (DSE), in line with the latest developments.

O2 – Curriculum “Empowering adult educators to encourage Digital Social Entrepreneurship start-ups among seniors and adults with different abilities”
Purpose: It is a resource material for educators to organise a 7-day long training course on empowering adult educators to further develop (online and offline) organisational culture, mentoring and education/workshops/courses for seniors and adults with disabilities and other beneficiaries in our communities on the topic of digital social entrepreneurship start-ups.

O3 – Toolkit “Mentoring and supporting seniors and adults with different abilities for Digital Social Entrepreneurship start-up”
Purpose: It is a resource material that serves as a theoretical and conceptual resource for andragogic workers in adult education institutions, educators and professors who work closely with seniors and adults in organisations, schools and institutions. The toolkit gives recommendations to educators when organising workshops and activities with seniors and adults with disabilities in DSE, as well as it consists of 12 different tools explored and adapted for using in NFE when directly educating and mentoring seniors and adults with disabilities for digital social entrepreneurship (DSE) start-up.

O4 – E-learning course “Digital Social Entrepreneurship start-up course for seniors and adults with different abilities”
Purpose: It is an innovative and up-to-date digital tool / online course for relevant topics and with tools for start-up of digital social enterprises for interested individuals, beneficiaries. It allows for bigger impact of our project, as it is free and easily accessible from any community, country. This is an internet-based course on DIGITAL SOCIAL Entrepreneurship for seniors and adults with different abilities who are hard to reach and who otherwise don’t participate in many education activities. The tool is an interactive platform where the participants are able to read, watch videos, take quizzes, communicate with each other and do a lot more. 

All the above intellectual outputs are available in English, German, Croatian, Italian and Serbian, catering to multiple countries where these languages are official.

Direct Results:

Utilisation of Outputs:
*- 24 multipliers adult educators across partner organisations utilised the intellectual outputs and tested them with beneficiaries on local level; In this way also testing for its efficacy both at a personal and organisational level, aiming to refine processes and practices in adult education activities.
*- at least 80 beneficiaries, seniors and adults with disabilities (20 per country) benefited directly from these outputs through the actions of these multipliers.

Training the Trainers and further Empowerment:
*- 14 adult educators participated in the Learning Teaching Activities (LTTA) and are subsequently empowered to educate other adult educators. Post-project, these trainers will organise smaller training sessions in their native organisations, thereby indirectly benefitting another 20-30 adult educators who will be equipped to use the project’s outputs in their daily activities.

Local Impact:
*- 113 local multipliers/adult educators across four countries empowered during the multiplier events. The focus was on accentuating the significance adult education for digital social entrepreneurship education, and ensuring the necessary support structures are in place for entrepreneurship education work for digital social entrepreneurship start-up among seniors and adults with disabilities.

Expected project results were two-fold: (1) the organisations developed publications to be used to provide quality NFE about Digital Social Entrepreneurship (DSE); (2) we also developed online course that can be used by target groups who are not able to physically attend educational activities and/or who we had no chance to work with before. 
In sum, the project not only produced valuable, multilingual resources, but also ensured the empowerment of a significant number of adult educators, trainers, and multipliers, amplifying its impact across multiple countries.

2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000035248.title: A sustainable framework for improving the digital upskilling of adult cultural professionals
2021-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000035248.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project due to its direct relevance to the cultural and creative sectors, heavily affected by COVID-19. Initially, the pandemic caused disruptions in visitation and operations, especially for smaller institutions, leading to financial strain. Many in Europe shifted to digitalization, yet comprehensive approaches for adult cultural workers and small to medium-sized organizations are lacking. The BoostDigiCulture project aimed to bridge this gap by supporting digital transition, offering upskilling pathways, and enhancing accessibility to digital learning. It addressed the needs highlighted in the NEMO Final Report (2021), particularly focusing on smaller organizations' urgent demand for digital transition support. Recognizing the unique challenges faced by these organizations, such as limited resources and skills, BoostDigiCulture provided tailored assistance. Ultimately, the project aimed to ensure the sustainable digital transformation of the cultural and creative sectors, strengthening their resilience in the face of future challenges.

<< Objectives >>

BoostDigiCulture aimed to strengthen the digital upskilling of adult cultural professionals within medium-sized cultural institutions across partner countries. Its core mission was to establish a sustainable and inclusive professional development framework leveraging open educational resources and practices. This framework was tailored to elevate the digital competencies of cultural professionals with limited digital skills.
The project had several key objectives. Firstly, an important objective was to empower adult cultural professionals to integrate digital culture effectively into their institutional agendas. Additionally, it aimed to raise awareness about the significance of digital readiness and training for these professionals, emphasizing their role in fostering institutional resilience and sustainability.
Another goal was the creation, implementation, and validation of a durable professional development framework for digital upskilling. This framework was designed to support adult learners in the cultural sector, ensuring they could navigate digital platforms while preserving the inclusive nature of digital culture in their online institutional offerings.

<< Implementation >>

In the BoostDigiCulture project, various activities took place in the pilot and implementation phases of the systemic design framework that was pursued. 
The activities included:
-	A total of four transnational project meetings – two of which took place face-to-face in Potenza, Italy in July 2022 and one year later in Berlin, Germany in July 2023. Two additional project meetings were held online to kick-off the project in February 2022 and in between the face-to-face meetings in January 2023. Additionally, regular check-in meetings were conducted to ensure a good level of team communication and collaboration
-	Project result piloting activities for all of the project results, in the form of focus groups, feedback forms and questionnaires and workshops
-	A virtual workshop between experts and novices in digital cultural heritage, with interaction between large scale and small and medium sized cultural institutions at a transnational level. The workshop was designed as part of PR1 and was thus announced for its users through the forum
-	Regarding PR4, the BoostDigiCulture online self-assessment tool was designed to evaluate adult cultural professionals’ readiness in integration of digital cultural in their institutional agenda. This was tested and successfully implemented in the elearning platform. All registered users had to first pass the self-assessment in order to complete the upskilling programme and again take the assessment in order to receive their digital badges
-	Concerning PR3, 50 cultural professionals completed the microlearning upskilling programme; a tailored course for the targeted adult cultural professionals, to enhance their competences in inclusive digital content creation and curation and institutional digital strategy. Additional viewers were gathered through the project’s YouTube channel
-	Moreover, through local events and seminars policy makers, cultural professionals and stakeholders were informed about the project’s scope, methodology, and products. 
-	A learning, teaching and training activitiy (LTTA), which took place in Portugal in June 2023. The LTTA was organized as a “Hands-on BoostDigiCulture Workshop” which was meant to facilitate the implementation of the project results. The participants were adult cultural professionals from the partner countries
-	Further activities took place in the form of dissemination efforts and social media postings

<< Results >>

The project produced four main project results, namely:
-	PR1: BoostDigiCulture e-learning mentoring platform: Digital cultural affinity spaces Establish digital cultural affinity spaces with: an interactive map feature to display profiles for peer-to-peer mentoring among cultural professionals - and their institutions virtual workshops between experts and novices in digital culture, with interaction between large scale and small and medium sized cultural institutions at a transnational level
-	PR2: BoostDigiCulture Professional Digital competence Profile (PDP):defining the digital competences needed for adult cultural professionals in small and medium sized cultural institutions.
-	PR3: BoostDigiCulture Microlearning upskilling programme: A sustainable professional development framework with a tailored course for the targeted adult cultural professionals, to enhance their competences in inclusive digital content creation and curation and institutional digital strategy. Includes provision for open digital badges and accreditation in digital cultural heritage. 
-	PR4: BoostDigiCulture Self-assessment tool: an online evaluation rubric, designed to assess adult cultural professionals’ readiness in integration of digital cultural in their institutional agenda. Point of reference: DigComp Framework indicators and levels of competence.

2021-1-DK01-KA220-ADU-000033790.title: Building Capacity for Informal Adult Education and Debate on the EU
2021-1-DK01-KA220-ADU-000033790.summary:
<< Background >>

Before the project, all partner organisations experienced similar challenges with regards to activating and engaging adults and we identified a need for a transnational European public in which EU topics and national perspectives could be discussed with. The project aimed to establish a transnational adult education sphere where all adults of diverse backgrounds have the possibility to participate. Our ambition to improve adult education on the EU included both physical and digital engagement of a broader range of participants in terms of social backgrounds, ethnicity, gender, age. During the Covid-19 pandemic, we discovered that virtual formats could be more inclusive and diverse and had a huge potential for education on the EU. Therefore, we aimed to incorporate and implement our organisations’ experiences to develop new designs suited for online informal adult education. We also aimed to inspire each other to create better face-to-face debates, and the online events could help build capacity for future physical meetings as more people would become familiar with the formats online. All in all, we wanted to re-think and improve our capacity for physical events and courses which would be of mutual benefit of all organisations.

<< Objectives >>

We had four objectives. Objective 1: A crucial and our primary objective was to increase our numbers of participating adult learners as well as including adult learners with more diverse range of backgrounds. Objective 2: It was important for us to establish a pan-European public with pan-European content available for debate (this would contribute to widening our project and strengthening our networks). Objective 3: It was important for us to assist each other’s organisational development. We saw a huge potential in each other for bettering our adult education as well as enhancing and building capacity for cooperation and network-building. Objective 4: It was of importance for us to develop products, tools, methodology, results etc. that would be beneficial to external adult education organisations that seek to obtain similar results as us. 

<< Implementation >>

7 online debates (two in each country + a final debate hosted by DEO) with lectures from EU experts, group discussions, and participant question rounds. The purpose was to inform participants about EU politics, create an engaging discussion, and they functioned as a learning device for the organisations. The debates were followed up with a survey to improve future debates. 3 workshops (one in each partner country) with two functions: 1) to educate adult learners and teachers about the two project topics and other EU relations and politics in the three countries and other EU countries – and strengthen the abilities of the partner organisations to engage new target groups with innovative approaches to improve teaching abilities and methodology in the future, and 2) to debate on the EU on a pan-European level. These events had a high degree of transferability to other organisations in adult education across Europe. 3 multiplier events (one in each partner country): The objective of the multiplier events was to introduce the project products to stakeholders to ensure the continued sustainability of the project and its innovative content.

<< Results >>

1) We wanted to engage more adult learners with a focus on diversity: Based on surveys from online debates and workshop participants, we have seen an increase in the number of participants as well as participants with diverse backgrounds. 2) We wanted to establish and develop pan-European content, debates, and a pan-European public: a) We have produced content (online debates, e-books, workshops, handbooks, engagement guides, webpage, and multiplier events) with a clear pan-European perspective, b) we have identified national perspectives and brought them into a pan-European context in all materials in the project, and c) surveys after activities have indicated that participants have felt included in a pan-European debate. 3) We wanted to develop the partner organisations' competencies towards adult education on EU at a transnational level: a) Internal evaluation indicates that the staff have increased their abilities to operate at a transnational level, b) internal evaluation indicates that the staff have increased their abilities to implement adult education on the EU at a national level, and c) each organisation has evaluated their progress on the area they wanted to develop in the project. 4) We wanted to benefit other adult education organisations with new products, results, and methodologies from our project: We have developed: a) Engagement guides, b) website, c) multiplier events, d) workshops, and e) outreach through other organisations.

2021-1-EL01-KA220-ADU-000035230.title: Burnout of Professionals and Parents with Children with Disabilities: Prevention, common challenges and mutually empowering methodologies and practices in Early Child Intervention Services
2021-1-EL01-KA220-ADU-000035230.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the Project to address the challenges faced by parents, professionals and organizations in the disability sector, particularly the serious issue of burnout. The project highlighted the need to enhance protective factors for families and Early Childhood Intervention (ECI) professionals while reducing burnout risks, which can lead to isolation and social exclusion. By empowering those responsible for the care and education of children with disabilities (CwD), we aimed to empower the children themselves.
We focused on addressing the following needs:
For Parents & Professionals:
•Strengthen their emotional, social, parenting and professional skills 
•Identify, prevent burnout & enhance resilience
•Improve cooperation & teamwork
•Have access to high-quality learning opportunities 
For Organizations:
•Adapt organizational structures and tools 
•Build connected and dedicated teams
•Create a culture of resilience 
•Improve the quality of services offered
Through Innovative Digital Tools:
•Enhance digital skills & readiness
•Ensure access to up-to-date knowledge and resources
The ultimate goal was to provide CwD with better care and support, helping them reach their full potential and promoting their social inclusion. 

<< Objectives >>

The Project involved 10 partners and 1 associated partner from 8 countries. Its goal was to ensure CwDs’ healthy development and social inclusion. It aimed to help parents & professionals overcome vulnerability, empower each other, cultivate relationships based on empathy and improve participation in all aspects of life. It  aimed to promote digital transformation, provide tailored quality learning opportunities, improve organizational quality, build capacity and enable transformation. Its objectives included:
•	Develop a burnout screening inventory
•	Gain in-depth knowledge of professionals’ and parents’ with CwD needs and identify burnout risk factors
•	Develop Burnout FREE ECI Methodology to improve well-being, resilience and adult-child relationships
•	Create an Innovative Train the Trainers Burnout FREE ECI Program
•	Develop a digital ecosystem for the ECI field
•	Validate and certify the Burnout FREE ECI Program
•	Ensure sustainability of best practices, raise awareness, foster social inclusion and extend the project impact
•	Establish collaboration to promote synergy, networking, and capacity building, tackling joint challenges and promoting social inclusion and skill development for families with CwD & ECI professionals. 

<< Implementation >>

The overall strategy of Burnout FREE ECI Project was based on a synthetic plan of activities to achieve its aims. To ensure high quality objectives a PDCA (Plan, Do, Check, Act) cycle process was applied and all activities correlated directly with the objectives and the results. The project activities were: 
•European & International Literature Review on Burnout affecting Professionals and Parents with CwD within the context of ECI Services.
 •A Needs Assessment survey related to burnout per Partner Organization & respective assessment tools regarding the identification of ECI professionals’ and parents’ with CwD needs. Data was collected from a sample of 227 professionals and 284 parents. These numbers have far exceeded the requirements of the proposal (110 professionals and 220 parents). 
 •Workshop for professionals to work together, structure the Training Material content and the work division among partners, according to their expertise during TM2. 
•Development of Burnout Free ECI Training Material & Content for Professionals & Parents, covering the need for enriched knowledge on burnout prevention and treatment techniques and addressing the specific needs of professionals and parents.
•3 Webinars (1 Webinar was planned according to the proposal) to structure the guidelines on how to test and try Burnout FREE ECI techniques during the Pilot phase in ECI settings.
 •Pilot Implementation in a minimum of 15 families from each ECI Organization Partner, for a seven-month period during ECI Sessions. 
•Design and development of E-Learning Game and authoring tool, giving Professionals and Parents an extra tool to deal with burnout and cope better with their personal and professional challenges. 
•Development of Certification Scheme for the certification of Curriculum & Training Material and Certification Scheme for Persons to enhance quality assurance in adult education, in correlation to EQF Level 5, ECVET and Standard ISO 17024. 
•4 Days training Activity (C1) of 37 professionals, leading to their certification (the estimated number in the proposal was 22 certified professionals). The professionals mastered the innovative Burnout FREE ECI methodology,  acted as Train the Trainers of the Methodology and replicated the knowledge in an organizational, national and European level. 
•Development of Digital Toolkit with Library of re-usable OER and newly developed e-learning courses (webinars), enhancing digital readiness of participants, ensuring full access to open and flexible learning and inclusion for all, even in challenging circumstances.
 •Development of Replication Burnout Free ECI Methodology Guide, enabling the successful replication of the project results to organizations beyond the consortium.
• 12 Workshops (10 workshops were planned according to the proposal) on Burnout FREE ECI methodology were organized in partners’ organizations, other organizations and members of EASPD to familiarize 225 parents and professionals (exceeded the requirements of the proposal, which were 10 workshops and approx. 200 persons) with the mutually empowering practices to prevent burnout.
 •Performance of Train the trainers’ activity "Summer School: BURNOUT FREE ECI", a 4-day training program designed to equip 33 professionals with the knowledge, skills and competences required to be “facilitators of change” in organizations beyond the consortium, according to demand. 
•Adaptation of 3 universities courses curriculum to incorporate the Burnout FREE ECI Methodology, adding value to the ECI field knowledge and enhancing the responsiveness of the research community to the societal needs.
•Development of the Burnout FREE ECI Hub, as vibrant Burnout FREE ECI community, extending the project impact beyond its lifetime. 
•Realization of 4 Multiplier Events giving the opportunity to 340 persons (the estimated number in the proposal was 255 persons) to attend live and virtually, through the e-conference tools. 
•Application of internal evaluation tools and performance of external evaluation to assess the project outcomes & results. 
•Organization of TMs as participatory project management activities and cooperation processes to minimize risk factors and enhance the quality of the Project Results. 
•Incorporation of green practices when designing all project activities and adoption of alternative greener ways of implementation (Webinars, E-Multiplier Events, E-Conferences, Adaptation of the Universities’ curricula in hybrid format, e-leaflets, etc).  

<< Results >>

Overall the project led to an increased capacity of partner organizations to anticipate and welcome change, to synchronize with the opportunities and constraints of the digital transformation, proactively support professionals and build connected and united teams. The concrete outputs and results of our project were the following: 
• The website of the project, evolved into an empowering network and active community, incorporating the ‘ Burnout Free ECI Hub’.
• The Report on Burnout (PrR1) including Literature Review and Needs Assessment Survey.
• The Workshop ‘Burnout Free ECI Training Material & Content for Professionals and Parents’, held in TM2 in Croatia, focused on structuring the Burnout Free ECI Training Material.
 • The Burnout Free ECI Training Material & Content for Professionals & Parents (PrR2) covering the need for enriched knowledge on burnout prevention and treatment techniques.
• The Methodology (PrR3) with Guidelines which were applied to ECI services during the pilot phase in each ECI Organization and Assessment tools. 
• Three Webinars on Pilot guidelines, which guided the Professionals through the Pilot Phase and the content of the Methodology Guide. The Webinars were performed by UTH, UNIZG, UBB, Omegatech and Amimoni.
• The Report on the Burnout Free ECI Pilot (PrR3), including the results derived from piloting Burnout FREE ECI techniques in partner organizations.
• E-learning Game (PrR4) consisting of free applications (for PC, iOS and android devices) including a mood quiz and multiple scenarios. It is accompanied by an authoring tool that allows development of new scenarios in various languages. 
• The Certification Scheme (PrR5), which led to Certification of Curriculum &Training Material and Certification of Persons, according to EQF Level 5, ECVET and Standard ISO 17024.
• 4 Days training Activity (C1), which led to 37 Certified Burnout FREE ECI Professionals who acquired the required knowledge, skills and competences to perform Trainings/ Workshops/Webinars on Burnout FREE ECI Methodology and were equipped with the necessary knowledge, skills and key competences to apply Burnout FREE ECI practices and help other professionals in ECI or related services and parents with children with disabilities overcome challenges, improve their quality of life and consequently improve the quality of support, care and education offered to the child with disabilities.
 • The Digital Toolkit and the Replication Methodology (PrR6); The Digital toolkit  includes an online training platform, e-learning courses (MOOC) and webinars and the  Digital Educational material in OER format available in the E-learning Platform (E-library). The Replication Methodology  enables the development of digital tools, of the methodology replication guide,  hybrid learning opportunities from Universities, innovative approaches for addressing target groups, increasing the reach and impact of the project beyond ECI Organizations. 
• 12 Workshops on Burnout FREE ECI methodology, which were organized in partners’ organizations, other organizations and members of EASPD and familiarized more parents and professionals (225 persons) with the mutually empowering practices to prevent burnout. 
• Adaptation of scientific curricula from 3 Universities, in hybrid format, providing future professionals with knowledge, skills and key competences on the issue. These courses, offered by UTH, UBB, and UoZ, are expected to reach approximately 430 students annually (significantly more than the originally foreseen 50 students per university).
The results and outcomes of the project benefited the broad community of ECI service providers as well as other Associations in the disability field. The quality assurance framework and impact measurement methodology used in the project were based on the Theory of change assessing the intermediate goals and the progress towards the desired impact and ultimate objectives and it was guaranteed through a sound management system. The project helped people live a better life and create a “muscle of resilience” during times of crisis. The partnership between parents and professionals had a positive impact on altering the society’s stereotypes on disability and encouraging child inclusion in society. As for the longer-term benefits, the project paved the way for the development of new areas of complementarity in the disability field aiming at longer term perspectives and upscaling collaborations for long lasting sustainable impact.

2021-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000027035.title: MigrArts, arts et culture pour l'intégration des migrants
2021-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000027035.summary:
<< Background >>

Le contexte européen actuel marqué par la montée des nationalismes et discours identitaires montre la nécessité de notre projet qui vise à promouvoir une Europe inclusive et gardienne des droits des personnes migrantes et notamment de leurs droits culturels. Ces droits sont fondamentaux au bien-être des migrants et de puissants canaux de partage et de transmission de valeurs que l'Europe se doit de sauvegarder. 
Ce projet s'inscrit tant dans une perspective de reconnaissance des droits culturels des personnes migrantes que dans une perspective d'épanouissement individuel permis par le développement de compétences créatives et le renforcement d'un sentiment d'appartenance à différents échelons. Aussi, le projet MigrArts a pour vocation l'accompagnement des acteurs culturels, socioculturels ainsi que ceux en charge de l'accompagnement des migrants afin de les encourager à travailler ensemble, dans une approche innovante, intersectorielle et interculturelle. 

<< Objectives >>

A travers le projet MigrArts, nous souhaitions promouvoir les droits culturels et mettre en œuvre une meilleure intégration des personnes migrantes par les arts et la culture à l'échelle locale, nationale et européenne. C'est en employant une démarche inclusive, participative et émancipatrice qui a mêlé activités culturelles et artistiques que nous voulions atteindre cet objectif global et les objectifs spécifiques suivants : l'inclusion des droits culturels dans les projets à destination des personnes migrantes; inciter les acteurs des milieux culturels et artistiques à travailler avec des personnes migrantes; la co-construction de parcours culturels et artistiques avec des personnes migrantes favorisant leur inclusion ainsi que l'émergence d'une conscience européenne; le développement et la valorisation des compétences psychosociales des personnes migrantes dans une perspective d'insertion sociale, professionnelle et citoyenne; l'incitation auprès des décideurs politiques pour une intégration de l'art et de la culture dans un plan d'action.  

<< Implementation >>

La mise en œuvre du projet MigrArts a été permise à travers les activités suivantes : 
- Mise en commun des recherches, des ressources et des expériences de chaque partenaire du projet afin d'établir un état des lieux des politiques promouvant les droits culturels des personnes migrantes en Europe (R1) et de créer différents outils permettant la construction d'une démarche inclusive et émancipatrice des personnes migrantes à travers des activités culturelles et artistiques. De cette mise en commun et réflexions collectives découlent l'émergence d'un premier réseau associatif européen dédié aux droits culturels des personnes migrantes qui s'est rassemblé à maintes reprises en ligne et en présentiel lors des réunions transnationales.
- Collaboration de participants volontaires issus des associations et des institutions dans les secteurs de la culture, de la médiation culturelle et de l'accompagnement des personnes exilées ainsi que des personnes migrantes afin d'expérimenter et d'analyser un cadre méthodologique commun pour la mise en place de pratiques innovantes (R2).
- Participation des représentants du consortium et de partenaires à des activités transnationales d'apprentissage pour approfondir des thématiques clés du projet (droits culturels, valorisation des acquis d'apprentissage dans un cadre non formel) et de développer une certaine expertise autour de ces questions avant la rédaction du guide (R3) et des scénarios de formation (R4).
- Production d'outils (R3 et R4) issus de la démarche expérimentale (R2) destinés à une large diffusion afin d'encourager et de faciliter d'autres initiatives s'inscrivant dans une démarche similaire.
- Communication autour du projet et dissémination du guide pédagogique (R3) et des scénarios de formation (R4) à travers des communications en ligne (mailings, lettres d'information, site web des organisations, posts sur les réseaux sociaux, ...) et en présentiel, notamment grâce aux événements de dissémination prévus dans chaque pays. Cette dissémination était destinée d'abord et avant tout aux bénévoles, salariés et élus actifs dans les champs éducatif, culturel, artistique, social et solidaire même si elle touche, de par sa diffusion, un public plus large.

<< Results >>

Les réalisations concrètes issues du projet MigrArt sont notamment : 
- l'établissement d'un état des lieux des politiques et droits culturels au sein des pays des organisations participantes dans le cadre de l'intégration des personnes migrantes (R1) 
- la création (R1) et l'expérimentation (R2) d'une méthodologie commune aux partenaires visant à intégrer une approche inclusive et émancipatrice des personnes migrantes à travers des activités culturelles et artistiques 
- la création d'un guide pratique (R3) et de scénarios de formation (R4) avec et destiné aux personnes et organisations actives dans les champs éducatif, culturel, artistique, social et solidaire
- et plus globalement, la création d'un réseau européen d'acteurs associatifs de Macédoine, de Croatie, d'Italie et de France autour des droits culturels des personnes migrantes. Réseau que nous souhaitons continuer d'élargir à d'autres structures et pays

Nous pouvons noter d'autres résultats qui découlent de ce projet dont : 
- le renforcement des liens militants entre les organisations participantes et au sein même de ces dernières qui, au vu du contexte politique européen marqué par la monté des nationalismes et des extrêmes, est une plus-value remarquable. 
- ce renforcement de réseaux associatifs permet alors de remettre à l'agenda la question de l'accueil des personnes migrantes et de l'aborder sous un angle inédit qui dépasse le paradigme habituel se limitant aux aspects matériels de leur inclusion - loger, nourrir et maintenir en bonne santé-. 
- ce travail autour du projet MigrArts a aussi été marqué par une redynamisation des échanges et de la collaboration entre les différentes fédérations qui composent certaines organisations participantes, qui a notamment permis la diffusion et le partage de connaissances et de compétences au sujet des thématiques abordées.

2021-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000028212.title: AGRI Smart
2021-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000028212.summary:
<< Background >>

With the global population surpassing 9 billion by 2050 and food demand increasing by 70%, traditional farming fell short in addressing future needs. Recognizing the importance of sustainable production, digital farming emerged, leveraging precision technology.

Precision agriculture, defined as applying the right treatment at the right time and place, gained traction, particularly in irrigation methods aimed at water conservation and improved yields (2019). In 2019, 24 EU Member States acknowledged the potential of digital technologies in addressing economic, social, climate, and environmental challenges in agriculture.

Roberto Viola from the European Commission highlighted consumer expectations for high-quality, safe, and environmentally conscious food (08/03/2020). Digital farming, integrating AI, robotics, and data analysis, arose as a solution to enhance farm efficiency and environmental sustainability.

Digital technologies were expected to enhance rural life quality and attract younger individuals to farming. With only 5.6% of European farms run by those under 35 in 2017, the "AGRI's" project aimed to equip adult educators with tools to promote awareness and provide skills for entrepreneurship in the agro-food industry.

<< Objectives >>

With these premises, the "AGRI Smart" (AGRI’s) Cooperation Partnership project aimed at:

Objective 1: Promoted agriculture entrepreneurship as a sustainable farming model.

Objective 2: Developed precision agriculture in Europe to answer the growing need for food and promoted a new model of farming towards a more sustainable one.

Objective 3: Empowered adults with digital and entrepreneurial skills in the agro-food industry to become actors of a sustainable future and become more competitive actors at the same time.

<< Implementation >>

The activities that were implemented during the project lifetime were the following:

Production of a Guide addressed to all adults interested in the topic. For this purpose, partners used surveys for needs analysis, conducted research, interviews with professionals, and employed peer-review methodologies.

Production of a Training Format addressed to adults' trainers/educators. Partners implemented the output through research, peer-review methodology, piloting of the Training Format, local workshop implementation, and collection of feedback.

Creation of a social community to be used by farmers interested in/using precision agriculture and willing to share and/or discuss their experience regarding precision agriculture practices.

<< Results >>


In order to reach the objectives, the project's partners produced the following results:

1 guide that explained the concept of precision agriculture and how it could help achieve a more sustainable model of production. The guide contained a state-of-the-art overview in the involved countries regarding precision technologies applied to the agricultural industry. It included examples of best precision agriculture practices to showcase the benefits and encourage future entrepreneurs to consider them. The guide was addressed to adults interested in the topic.

1 Training Format for adults' educators interested in promoting agricultural entrepreneurship in a sustainable way. The Training Format provided the target group with tools and methodologies to be used and reproduced at the local level. It aimed to give new skills and knowledge to young adults interested in agricultural entrepreneurship, guiding them on how to start a business in agriculture. The Training Format included modules covering entrepreneurial skills applied to agriculture, incorporating digital skills for young adults to be prepared for a new farming model, such as data analysis, Artificial Intelligence, social media communication, etc.

1 social community on a web platform where farmers could share their experience with precision technologies used in their agricultural business. It served as a space for discussion among farmers regarding these technologies and the data they collected to improve farming methods, ultimately leading to better quality and more sustainable products.

2021-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000033655.title: Aller-vers : transformer les cadres pour l’inclusion de tous
2021-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000033655.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was inspired by the observation that, although outreach practices are covered in training courses, they often present challenges when implemented by social workers and volunteers working with (young) people experiencing social exclusion. What's more, these practices are not systematically recognised and supported within the wider public policy framework. The complexity arises from the need to bridge the three interconnected dimensions: policy planning, institutional organisation and professional intervention on the ground, which makes effective implementation difficult. This leads to a number of unmet needs in most countries, particularly in terms of reducing the gaps mentioned above. The project has enabled us to identify and assess the gaps in current training, the gaps between training and practice and the gaps between the needs of individuals and the recognition of these needs by public policy, to improve the quality of training and methodologies in the field and to create a social dialogue between all stakeholders. 

<< Objectives >>

Our general objectives were to : 
-Reduce the gap between training and practice through adult education (whether they are volunteers, people undergoing retraining, continuing education, etc.) 
-Reduce the gap between social policies and professional practices 
-Implementing adult education and intervention strategies that strengthen coordination between institutions, national, regional and local authorities, social partners and civil society.
-Combating isolation, withdrawal and the denial of rights to those most in difficulty 
-Create a network of researchers involved in the issue to develop the capacity to act.
Operational objectives: 
-Make an inventory of existing studies and practices 
-Design a training module and integrate it into existing training courses 
-Train the trainers who will implement the module 
Create and test a support methodology and experiment with low-threshold services 
-Train adults who will implement the experiment (educators, volunteers, social workers, etc.) 
-Creation of a pedagogical toolkit and a common reference framework 

<< Implementation >>

As part of our project, we have implemented 4 main activities: 
-Capitalising on training content and outreach practices in partner countries 
-Designing and implementing a training module on outreach in social work training courses 
-The design and testing of an outreach methodology by professionals 
-The design of a pedagogical toolkit based on these elements.
To accompany these activities, 2 learning mobilities were carried out: one to train the trainers who took part in the training modules on outreach, the other to train in the practical methodology of outreach in the field.

<< Results >>

The results of our project :
