2021-1-IE01-KA220-ADU-000035273.title: Supporting Families through the Dual Transition: Family Learning Model to Manage Carbon and Digital Footprints
2021-1-IE01-KA220-ADU-000035273.summary:
<< Background >>

The Family Footprints project partners came together to apply for this project as a response to pressing local needs and educational gaps identified within partner communities. The decision to apply for the project stemmed from partners identifying a need to support local communities to come to terms with European policies and strategies, which have been put in place to support the dual or twin transition of Europe to a more sustainable and digital society. Specifically, through the materials we developed in this project, we have linked to the European policies - European Green Deal, Europe Fit for a Digital Age and the DigComp Framework, to build the climate and digital literacies of whole families. We took a family learning approach because we saw the family unit as an ideal microcosm of our local communities, with so many different age groups in one family. As such, that through one high-quality, targeted family learning intervention, we have been able to reach parents (adult learners), grandparents (senior adult learners), and children, teenagers and young adults; and to support each of these European citizens to develop their digital and climate literacies, through high-quality curricula and age-appropriate digital resources.

<< Objectives >>

Through the Family Footprints project, partners aimed to address the dual transition towards digitalisation and sustainability that were sweeping across Europe, by developing comprehensive educational resources tailored to the needs of families and adult learners. The implementation of the Family Footprints project was driven by a clear set of objectives aimed at achieving meaningful and sustainable outcomes for adult learners, families, and adult educators. At the commencement of the project, partners identified a pressing need to ensure that all members of society could upskill to avoid being left behind by the digital and sustainable transitions. Specifically, the project aimed to bridge the Family Digital Divide by ensuring that all family members, regardless of age, had basic digital competence to manage their digital footprint, and to support families and communities in embracing a more sustainable way of living to address the climate crisis. As such, what we aimed to achieve through this project was to empower families in our communities and across Europe to develop their digital and climate literacies, manage their digital and carbon footprints, and support the dual transition of Europe.

<< Implementation >>

Over the 24-month project lifecycle, the Family Footprints partners engaged in research and consultation activities, curriculum development and translation, piloting, and promotional activities to ensure that our project results were developed to a high standard, and that they reached our intended audiences. At the commence of the project, all partners established Local Advisory Groups (LAGs), comprised of local parents, adult educators and advisors who would support our project work. By the end of the project, we engaged 46 individuals in these LAGs, surpassing the target of 28 foreseen at application stage. Through our curriculum development activities, partners collaborated to produce the Induction to Pedagogy Programme for Parents and the Dual Transition: Digital and Climate Literacy Programme for Parents. These programmes provide parents with essential skills to deliver family learning in their homes; and knowledge in digital literacy and sustainability, empowering them to make informed decisions and adopt sustainable behaviours within their families. Through our piloting activities, we reached 131 parents across the consortium. Partners also developed the Family Learning Toolkit, comprising age-appropriate resources for all family members - Comic Strips, Interactive Magazines, and Audio Books, to engage families in interactive and accessible learning. Through these activities we reached 107 families. Partners also developed and delivered in-service training for community and adult educators, supporting them with new skills to deliver family learning in their communities. Through national piloting, we reached 53 adult educators across our 7 countries, and a further 12 who participated in our transnational training event in Portugal in May 2023. Through our promotional activities, we reached 248 participants through our virtual multiplier event (31 participants) and our face-to-face events in each participating country; and a further 881 followers on our project Facebook page.

<< Results >>

The Family Footprints project partners produced the following concrete project results:

PR1 – Induction to Pedagogy Programme for Parents - This training for parents supports their role as facilitators of learning in a family learning model. The induction programme provides a series of practical workshops that support parents in their new role as facilitators of family learning on the topic of digital and climate literacy and supports parents to apply the Family Learning Toolkit by introducing them to the comic strips, magazine and audio books developed to address young children, teenagers and young adults and senior adult, respectively. These workshops also present approaches and guidance for applying these digital tools in a family learning environment. These workshops were delivered to 72 parents across the 7 partner countries.

PR2 – The Dual Transition: Digital and Climate Literacy Programme for Parents - The content of the programme comprises 12 short modules and addresses two core subject areas: digital literacy, and climate literacy. Six modules support parents to develop their digital literacy and competence. These modules develop the skills and aptitudes of parents and will be benchmarked to the DIGCOMP 2.1 Framework for Citizens. A further six additional modules support parents to develop their climate literacy. These modules are in line with the most appropriate pillars of the European Green Deal. Both the digital and climate components of this curriculum begin with two introductory modules – each introductory module supports parents to learn the key terminology and concepts related to digital literacy and climate change. These modules were delivered to 74 parents across the consortium.

PR3 – Family Learning Toolkit - Comic Strips, Interactive Magazines and Audio Books - This Toolkit provides age-appropriate learning materials for family members of different age groups. For children, there are 12 themed comic strips that introduce digital and climate literacy, for a young target group. The comics are themed, with the first 6 comics addressing issues related to online safety and our digital footprint, and the second 6 comics presenting scenarios related to climate change and our carbon footprint. For teenagers, the toolkit provides a series of short explainer videos, self-help resources, games, and puzzles, all presented through an interactive digital magazine. The set of 12 magazines addresses 6 themes – 3 aimed at developing digital and media literacy – as research shows that young adults require media literacy training to counter the spread of disinformation through social media, and 3 to raise awareness of climate change. For senior adult learners and grandparents in the family unit, there are 8 audiobooks that address 4 topics relating to digital competence and 4 which aim to raise climate and environmental awareness. 86 families were engaged in testing this curriculum across the consortium.

PR4 – In-service Training Programme for Community and Adult Educators - This final project result comprises a bespoke in-service training programme to ensure that adult educators are fully trained to harness the potential of the educational resources developed in the family learning model. The in-service training begins by introducing the basic principles of digital and climate literacy before switching its attention to the family learning model developed and the different age-appropriate resources developed. The in-service training comprises 60 hours of instruction made up of 28-hours of hands-on workshop learning and 32 hours of online self-directed learning.  56 adult educators were reached through our national piloting of this curriculum, and a further 12 educators through the transnational training activity in Portugal.

Partners also reached 248 participants through our multiplier events, and a further 881 followers through our promotion of the project through our Facebook page.

2021-1-LT01-KA220-ADU-000026390.title: E-Commerce Training for Women Entrepreneurs
2021-1-LT01-KA220-ADU-000026390.summary:
<< Background >>

The main goal of this project was addressing the challenges women faced when establishing and running businesses which are the difficulties in accessing finance, information, training, business networks, and balancing business and family responsibilities. The project contributed to the objectives of the EU's Entrepreneurship 2020 Action Plan, which highlighted opportunities for women, recognizing that female creativity and entrepreneurial potential were underutilized.

The project aimed to address the following needs:

The underrepresentation of women in entrepreneurship, where only 34.4% of the EU's self-employed and 30% of start-up entrepreneurs were women.
The high rates of inactivity among women in the labor market, particularly those aged 25-49.
Barriers to digital inclusion that limited women's access to business growth opportunities and formal financial services in the competitive digital economy.

Ecommerce4women project wanted to support women entrepreneurs in adopting and leveraging digital platforms and we wanted to help them overcome these barriers by enhancing their participation in the digital economy and enabling their businesses to thrive.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to achieve several key objectives by implementing this project:
1. We aimed to facilitate women’s access to information through the use of e-commerce tools, helping them navigate the challenges of the business world more easily. 
2. To improve the digital skills of women entrepreneurs, particularly regarding e-commerce, by providing them with a dedicated e-learning platform.
3. To develop a tailored training program to address the specific needs of women entrepreneurs and offer effective training solutions. By doing so, we aimed to contribute to women's employment, giving them a better chance to reveal their entrepreneurial potential. 
4. To certify the e-commerce skills of women entrepreneurs, ensuring they were equipped to increase their entrepreneurship skills to fit in the digital economy.

<< Implementation >>

In PR1;
A curriculum targeting women entrepreneurs was prepared. All partners applied questionnaires, and conducted literature reviews. Each partner country organized workshops with stakeholders to discuss the curriculum of the training and report the workshop results. 
The training modules were developed in line with the curriculum. KSU developed measurement and evaluation tools for each module.
All partners tested e-learning platform by 25 participants by using an online questionnaire.

In PR2;
The e-learning platform was designed and launched after piloting and testing.
The e-commerce tools in line with the curriculum and the modules were developed: these tools include interactive videos, gamification elements and presentations. 
For each module interactive Videos, presentation and related content were produced. 


In PR3
The E-commerce Guidebook in line with the curriculum, modules and e-commerce tools for trainees was prepared.

For a better dissemination of the project results, partners utilized their social media accounts. Also, social media accounts of the project were launched. Seven e-newsletters were produced for dissemination and sent to all stakeholders.
To ensure project progress and monitoring both online and face-to-face meetings were organized. Also, monthly online monitoring meetings were organized for a better communication among the partners.

<< Results >>

The main results of this project are;
1. E-Commerce Curriculum and Modules(PR1)
2. E-Commerce e-learning Platform with E-Commerce tools (Interactive Videos, presentations, etc)(PR2)
3. A Guidebook of E-Commerce (PR3)

The website https://www.ecommerce4women.com/ was created to disseminate the project results and also to set the learning platform. 
To facilitate a better user experience we developed a tutorial video and put it as "How to Use" section in Project eLearning platform.
The eLearning has 6 main modules and 19 subchapters with an additional literature section and assessment part. The modules have gamification elements.

We also prepared an Entrepreneur's experience video.

2021-1-LV01-KA220-ADU-000026049.title: CREative MEdia Lab
2021-1-LV01-KA220-ADU-000026049.summary:
<< Background >>

The crisis due to COVID-19 underlined the importance of access to digital media/tools and to be familiar with them, as well as the role and power of cultural development in society. Cultural and Creative Industries (CCI) were among the hardest affected by the pandemic crisis, Covid-19 pandemic, with jobs at risk ranging from 0.8 to 5.5% of employment across OECD regions. 
The pandemic particularly affected venue-based activities due to social distancing (i.e. museums, performing arts, live music, festivals, cinema, etc.). 
With over 1.1 million cultural enterprises in the EU-27 as of 2017, and a significant presence in Italy, the project targeted CCIs educators, and professionals, especially in rural areas, to bridge the digital divide and empower individuals within the CCIs for resilience and growth.

<< Objectives >>

CREative MEdia Lab aimed to create an international strategic partnership and test innovate e-learning content and methodology addressing Cultural and Creative Industries (CCIs), particularly for those in remote and rural areas. The project had three main objectives:
1. To develop a comprehensive pool of skills blending knowledge and tools in new media, tailored for CCIs.
2. To provide targeted training for CCI operators working with CCIs in rural and remote areas, covering 5 knowledge pillars for the improvement of digital and technological skills: -Digital Publishing; -Communication, Marketing and Content Planning; -New Media, Social Networks and New Technologies Management; -Creative skills: Branding, Visual Design, Audio-Visual; -E-Learning methods.
3. To promote and encourage a bottom-up cultural development strategy for competence circulation and for interactive training activities in the European context, by providing free e-learning tools that contribute to promote sustainable and continuous CCIs innovation processes. 

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the project all 6 partners actively participated.
The project activities have been implemented according to the application:
Development of IO1 Creative Academy Training Programme fully completed (A1 Master Design Team' Selection; A2 Training Team' Selection; A3 Master Training Programme and Calendar).
Development of IO2 CREMEL Online Training Platform fully completed (A1 E-learning Platform Design; A2 Calls for Master Participants' Selection; A3 E-learning Web Masters Implementation).
Development of IO3 Case Studies Handbook / Trainers Guide fully completed (A1 Handbook Design; A2 Countries Innovation Research; A3 Final Document Publication).
Transnational project meetings (TPM):
TPM 1 Kick-Off Meeting in Latvia – meeting took place online due to COVID-19 pandemia 25.-26.01.2022. with 13 participants.
TPM 3 Project Meeting in Poland – meeting took place in Kielce, Poland 01.12.2022. with 13 participants.
TPM 5 Final Project Meeting in Italy - meeting took place in Bari, Italy 5.-6.12.2023. with 12 participants.
To save budget and time, whenever possible, partners’ meetings were coupled with other activities of the project. In addition, two additional one-day project meetings took place in conjunction with other project activities, namely: - the training-for-trainers on 15.07.2022. TPM2 in Lecce, Italy with 14 participants and a transnational workshop with CCIs professionals 18.07.2023. TPM4 in Rijeka, Croatia with 8 staff members.
In addition, at least 10 online project partners meetings were organized.
Learning, Teaching, Training Activities: C1 Training for Trainers (T4T) in Italy – implemented on 11-15 July 2022 in Lecce Italy, with 14 participants and C2 Training for Master / Courses Participants (TCP) in Croatia – implemented 17.-21. July 2023. with 27-29 participants.
6 Multiplier events implemented in 4 partner countries.

<< Results >>

The CREMEL project has produced significant outcomes aimed at enhancing the capabilities and reach of Cultural and Creative Industries (CCIs), particularly focusing on individuals and organizations in remote and rural areas. Results are three main deliverables:
1. Creative Academy Training Programme and teachers implementing the programme can be seen https://www.cremel.eu/ under each partner profile scrolling down. This comprehensive, free learning program is designed for CCI students, professionals, and the wider public. It focuses on the use of new media, digital communication, and publishing within the cultural and creativity sectors. Tailored to meet the specific needs of its users and adaptable to country-specific features, this program seeks to expand participants' knowledge and skills in applying digital tools for culture and creativity promotion and consumption.
2. CREMEL Online Training Platform: An innovative, open-source online platform that aggregates multi-language content for users in project countries and beyond. This interactive tool serves various educational purposes, offering an easily maintainable, transferable, and extensible resource. It aimed to be user-friendly, attractive. See: https://www.cremel.eu/

3. Creative Academy Trainers Guide: A toolkit for trainers and professionals in the cultural and creative sector, incorporating insights from the Creative Academy Training Programme and the Online Training Platform. It includes case studies and examples of projects initiated by CCI professionals as a result of CREMEL training, offering a rich resource for future training endeavours.
The Guide is a digital document in 5 languages - English , Croatian , Italian , Latvian , Polish and available on CREMEL platform under section Resources under Project guides:
https://www.cremel.eu/project-guides/ and under section Partner under each project partner profile.
Outcomes include strengthened networks of CCI professionals, enhanced creative capital, increased awareness of new media's impact on European cultural growth, and improved economic and social sustainability of CCI projects; The project also increased number of trained CCI operators, enhancing the value of cultural and creative enterprises and initiatives, and expanding the availability of training tools on new media and technologies.
topics: Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

2021-1-LV01-KA220-ADU-000026286.title: Intergenerational Learning Communities towards Environmental Sustainability
2021-1-LV01-KA220-ADU-000026286.summary:
<< Background >>

Europe is the first continent to declare climate and environmental emergency. Part of the priorities mentioned in the European Green Deal is activating education and training to engage students, parents and the community in the changes needed. To reach the proposed climate neutrality there is a need for new, innovative learning approaches to educate all community members (not only students at school) on environmental and sustainability issues. Therefore ILCES project aimed to strengthen intergenerational learning within community to promote environmental awareness and change of behavior towards environmental sustainability through 6 R’s of sustainability: rethinking, refusing, reducing, reusing, repairing, recycling. The project objective was achieved through creating a set of activities to challenge local communities to learn, discuss and understand the importance of behavioral change regarding environmental sustainability using ILCES e-learning platform. Besides ILCES project explored existing networks in the framework of local community between organisations and provided new ways, approaches, possibilities and models to ensure sustainable collaboration between involved stakeholders to develop forward-looking learning centres.

<< Objectives >>

The project overall goal was to strengthen intergenerational learning within community to promote environmental awareness and change of behavior towards environmental sustainability through 6 R’s of sustainability. The project had the following objectives: - To increase environmental awareness through an active, critical approach involving people of different age groups. - To increase digital competence of the involved target groups while boosting their awareness on environmental issues. - To support local community intergenerational learning providers with tools and resources on environmental sustainability. - To highlight innovative and effective models and approaches of intergenerational learning in local communities through environmental education activities using 6 R’s of sustainability: rethinking, refusing,
reducing, reusing, repairing, recycling. - To discover and identify core principles, different structures and approaches of sustainable local community involvement in intergenerational learning to raise environmental awareness through experience exchange and best practices. - To present challenges to implementing intergenerational learning in local community and forward recommendations for supporting work in this area.

<< Implementation >>

To reach the goal many activities of the project were carried out simultaneously. The first activity of ILCES was development of recommendations and guidelines for forward-looking community learning centres which had several tasks: exploring the existing situation, networks, activities carried out in local community in the organisation of adult/intergenerational education, developing methodology and structure of recommendations and guidelines, development of recommendations and guidelines for forward-looking community learning centres. The first activity was strengthened by learning activity "Effective networking in adult education". Parallel with the first activity the development of Impulse handbook which included 6 modules following Sustainability Development Goals (SDG) with 6 units of interactive activities following 6 R's of sustainable development was created. This activity was supported by learning activity "Environmental awareness and sustainable development".The Impulse handbook is transferred into interactive e-learning platform. Multiplier events were organised in each partner country.

<< Results >>

There were four tangible results in the ILCES project: 1. Impulse handbook. 2. Recommendation and guidelines for forward-looking community learning centres. 3. E-learning platform. 4. ILCES project website https://ilces.eu/ in five languages containing previously mentioned results. Result 4 is additional to the initial application. It was decided to develop website to make project results more available for broader public not only within partner countries.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2021-1-LV01-KA220-ADU-000028213.title: Inclusive human rights education - a gateway to civic participation and common values of European citizens
2021-1-LV01-KA220-ADU-000028213.summary:
<< Background >>

 It is generally recognized that human rights education is a key to human rights protection. As stated in the UN Declaration on Human Rights Education, knowledge of human rights empowers people and develop their competences to participate in democratic processes. These competences must be taught at early years of age and improved throughout one’s lifetime. Unfortunately, many states currently do not have a structural, thorough, and coordinated human rights education strategy at a governmental level, nor they education materials.

By bringing together competences and resources, the project partnership aimed to provide free and equal access to comprehensive and qualitative human rights education resources to European citizens. The cornerstone of the project is the Human Rights Guide (HRG) – a universal, easy-to-use and open access human rights education platform online which serves as an information resource and self-help tool for society-at-large and professionals in understanding human rights and developing competences in applying human rights in specific situations. As a result of the project, the Guide was implemented in eight EU member states, making it a truly pan-European education platform.

<< Objectives >>

The concrete objectives of the project were:
- To raise and consolidate the understanding of human rights as a common European value among European citizens and professionals by upscaling the HRG to new EU member states.
- To provide qualitative, up-to-date and inclusive human rights education to European citizens on equal basis by expanding and improving the HRG’s content and learning methodologies by using the advantages of the digital domain.
- To strengthen the efforts of the partner-organizations in providing human rights education by sharing good practices and contributing joint effort in further devising innovative approaches to both national and common European human rights challenges.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities of the project were centred around the creation of the project results, namely, the upscaling and the expansion of the Guide and the Online Knowledge Assessment Tool, as well as the creation of the Human Rights Case Box and the Rights Compendium. To create these intellectual outputs, the following core activities were implemented: the selection of the priority themes / cases in each partner country, the preparation of the content (research, drafting, testing, editing, translating), elaboration of the visual solutions based on the principles of visual education and the technical solutions.

The partnership also implemented a series of promotion and exploitation activities: multiplier events in each partner country, public outdoor campaign of the Guide in France and Croatia, information sessions to introduce the Guide with strategic partners, roundtables and discussions with policy and decision makers to discuss strategic implementation of human rights education initiatives at a national level.

<< Results >>

As a result of the project, large number of European citizens have free and equal access to qualitative human rights education online. The Human Rights Guide is available for the first time in France and Croatia, and new expanded versions are available in Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia, Bulgaria, Slovenia and Slovakia. The Guide now features new themes illuminated by the Covid-19 crisis such as restrictions on human rights, health and democratic participation. 

The Guide is also supplemented by new learning functionalities. The Rights Compendium explains the human rights as contained in international conventions but placed in respective national contexts. The Human Rights Case Box allows to explore human rights through human rights case-law, bringing it to the forefront as a pivotal source in human rights development. The new upscaled Human Rights Guide Europe platform technically offers a significant expansion and transferability potential for a new content, languages and EU countries.

The members of the target groups gained awareness of fundamental rights as core social and civic entitlements, acquired courage to participate in democratic processes and civic activities, and embraced human rights as a European value.

The partnership established the participating organizations as innovative human rights education providers in their respective countries and in the wider Europe and provided for a potential to develop further human rights education projects on the basis of the fundaments laid down by this project.
topics: Human rights and rule of law

2021-1-NL01-KA220-ADU-000028257.title: Biodiversity preservation in rural and maritime areas of EU islands
2021-1-NL01-KA220-ADU-000028257.summary:
<< Background >>

The BioIslands project aimed to address the urgent need for biodiversity preservation in rural and maritime areas, particularly in European islands, driven by recognizing the critical interdependence between human health and ecosystem health, especially highlighted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The project focused on three main sectors—agriculture, pastoralism, and fisheries—where biodiversity preservation is essential but faces challenges such as land-use intensity, invasive species, and unsustainable practices. The project targeted farmers, shepherds, and fishermen, acknowledging their role as key actors in implementing biodiversity preservation strategies.

<< Objectives >>

TThrough the project, the consortium sought to achieve several objectives:
1.	Foster biodiversity preservation in rural and maritime areas of European islands.
2.	Provide high-quality learning opportunities for farmers, shepherds, and fishermen in biodiversity preservation.
3.	Develop user-friendly digital tools to support these stakeholders in preserving biodiversity in their daily work.


<< Implementation >>

Partners implemented transnational focus group, pilotings for both results R1 and R2 with the involvement of adults learners, they organized international conference for Biodiversity day, and each partner organized multiplier events in order to promote project and its results to multiple stakeholders.



<< Results >>

PROJECT RESULTS INCLUDE A COMPREHENSIVE RESEARCH REPORT ON BIODIVERSITY STATUS AND UP-SKILL NEEDS, AS WELL AS A WEB PLATFORM WITH E-LEARNING COURSES TAILORED TO AGRICULTURE, PASTORALISM, AND FISHERY BIODIVERSITY. INTANGIBLE OUTCOMES INCLUDE RAISING AWARENESS, ADOPTION OF PROJECT RESULTS BY VARIOUS ENTITIES, AND THE CONSOLIDATION OF A COOPERATION FRAMEWORK FOR ONGOING INITIATIVES AND INFORMATION EXCHANGE AMONG STAKEHOLDERS.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

hr.name: Agencija za ruralni razvoj Zadarske zupanije

2021-1-PL01-KA220-ADU-000026916.title: Training of family members and guardians for inclusion of ageing adults with disabilities
2021-1-PL01-KA220-ADU-000026916.summary:
<< Background >>

The implementation of the project stems from an analysis of the complex situation of ageing adults with intellectual disabilities both globally and in the countries of the project consortium. . as indicated in reports by WHO, IASSID, and Inclusion International, ageing adults are at risk of social marginalisation, neglect, inadequate housing, limited access to health care, and low socio-economic status. Social attitudes towards ageing adults are also unfavourable, and solutions in the context of family and legal carer support are not at a satisfactory level. Barriers also include prejudice, disorganisation in services for ageing people, lack of legal solutions and professionals.  Our project responds to the issues identified above, as well as the demographic trend associated with global ageing. The aim was to better prepare families and legal carers of ageing people with disabilities so that the ageing processes experienced are safe and inclusive. The project produced a range of educational materials for the identified target group, a guidebook, a toolkit on inclusive working methods, instructional videos, an online resource database and a report with recommendations on social policy for older people. 

<< Objectives >>

The aim of "Training of family members and guardians for the inclusion of ageing adults with disabilities" was to develop informal educational materials to support ageing and social inclusion of ageing adults with disabilities. Recognizing the increasing population of elderly in EU and the complex challenges faced by those with intellectual disabilities, the project sought to address the inadequate care and social inclusion policies. 

<< Implementation >>

The main activities implemented in the project include:
Production of the toolkit on how to train parents and legal guardians of ageing adults with disabilities (R1).
Production of the parental education guidebook (R2).
Production of the educational spot videos for families (R3).
Production of the online learning HUB for family members of ageing adults with disabilities (R4).
Production of the policy recommendation report (R5).
Arrangement of pilot training activities with target groups (use produced project results in pilot training).
Arrangement of the multiplier event "Seminar: Active Ageing and Wellbeing for People with Disabilities" in each partner country.
Arrangement of the multiplier event "Final Conference: Inclusion of ageing adults with disabilities".
Creation of the project web platform.
Designing paper brochures of project results and other dissemination materials.
Setting up an advisory board per country with experts.
Monitoring all project activities.
Managing the pre-defined work plan and the deadlines for all tasks.






<< Results >>

The outcomes of the project were: 
A toolkit on how to train parents and legal guardians of ageing adults with disabilities. 
A parental education guidebook. 
Educational spot videos for families. 
An online learning HUB for family members of ageing adults with disabilities. 
A policy recommendation report. 
A project website. 
Paper brochures. 

The consortium reached a total of 963 beneficiaries.

hr.name: CROATIAN ASSOCIATION OF SOCIETIES OF PERSONS WITH INTELLECTUAL DISABILITIES

2021-1-PL01-KA220-ADU-000033582.title: Energy literacy–practical trainings for sustainable energy consumption via personal behavioural changes
2021-1-PL01-KA220-ADU-000033582.summary:
<< Background >>

The implementation of the El-Practice project facilitated the convergence of two important and underutilized potentials – knowledge of sustainable energy use and the education of young adults. It was a response to the needs of this social group, which is at the initial stage of establishing their households and faced with the necessity of making sustainable and conscious decisions that significantly impact their future and the climate. Numerous studies highlight the strategic role of education and digitalization in enhancing energy efficiency and promoting sustainable energy practices. Building knowledge in the field of energy literacy is an important element that enhances competencies in the job market and enables conscious utilization of sustainable solutions in private life. Due to the limited time availability of the project's target group, an online educational platform (e-course) was developed, where knowledge was divided into smaller modules, known as micro-sessions. These short lessons address issues related to efficient energy utilization, enabling flexible and focused learning depending on the participants' time availability.

<< Objectives >>

The objective of the El-Practice project was to support young adults in expanding their knowledge and enhancing their qualifications, abilities, and skills in sustainable energy utilization, as well as increasing their self-confidence, leading to greater involvement in creating a sustainable society and assuming responsibility for their life choices. Within the project, existing competencies and awareness levels regarding energy literacy among young adults were identified (PR1), followed by the development of a publicly accessible and interactive e-course (PR2), tailored to the needs of the young adults (PR3). A key aspect was also to support positive changes related to energy use, promote its sustainable utilization, and increase ecological awareness among citizens, taking into account the climate goals of the EU. Enhancing competencies in energy and climate issues and promoting habit changes at the individual level was achieved not only through course development but also through interactions with stakeholders, addressing the need for comprehensive education and actions in these areas.

<< Implementation >>

The project placed particular emphasis on developing an interactive and publicly accessible e-course on sustainable energy use. The course was designed to effectively engage and educate young adults, the main target group of the El-Practice project. A key result of the project is the online platform, which served as the focal point of all partners' activities. The platform was created to facilitate interactive remotely learning in energy literacy. Educational materials were divided into thematic modules covering key energy-related issues, such as actions under the European Green Deal, financing opportunities for investments in renewable energy, efficient resource management, and practical advice on implementing positive energy habits at home. Each training session includes active start, active learning, summaries, a glossary of key terms, as well as a quiz to test gained knowledge. The course was developed in English and translated into five national languages. Key activities also included organizing two training sessions for project partners and young adults. Project was widely promoted through various communication channels.

<< Results >>

The El-Practice project allowed for the achievement of three main outcomes:
PR1 – COMPETENCES ABOUT ENERGY LITERACY BY YOUNG ADULTS. Analyses were conducted to map existing competencies of young adults in energy-related skills in the project's partner countries. Competency gaps and deficiencies were identified, forming the basis for further development of training content and the e-course.
PR2 – EL-PRACTICE MOBILE-FRIENDLY PLATFORM. A mobile online platform was developed as the basis for training in energy literacy, created within the framework of Project Result 3. The platform aimed to engage young people in interactive distance learning and expand their knowledge in an innovative way, enabling the implementation of small changes related to energy use in everyday life.
PR3 – EL-PRACTICE MODULE BOOSTING ENERGY LITERACY COMPETENCIES IN. Online training content was developed in aim to support the expansion of knowledge in the field of energy, energy literacy, and climate, as well as to contribute to behaviour change among young people. The course was integrated with the mobile platform (developed as part of Project Result 2), ensuring the consistency of actions and access to education at different levels of advancement.

2021-1-PL01-KA220-ADU-000035250.title: Seniors Adaptation to the Virtual Environment
2021-1-PL01-KA220-ADU-000035250.summary:
<< Background >>

W Europie 18% populacji ma więcej niż 65 lat (Population Reference and Bureau, 2020). W wieku 65 lat obywatele europejscy mogą spodziewać się jeszcze około 20 lat życia, a liczba stulatków ma przekroczyć pół miliona do 2050 r. (Eurostat, 2019). W związku ze stereotypem osoby starszej całkowicie zależnej WHO wprowadziła w sferę polityki i gospodarki koncepcję aktywnego starzenia się (active ageing). Stanowi ona próbę nowego ujęcia procesu starzenia się i starości. Kształtuje nowy wizerunek osoby starszej. Projekt miał wspomagać aktywizowanie osób starszych poprzez umożliwienie im poznawania nowoczesnych narzędzi komunikacji przy jednoczesnej realizacji własnych pasji – dzielenie się swoimi pracami, współtworzenie treści cyfrowych, korzystanie z porad online. Założeniem projektu było włączenie osób starszych do aktywności społecznej poprzez umożliwienie im opanowania narzędzi ułatwiających włączenie. Zależy nam również na niwelowaniu negatywnych skutków odosobnienia związanego z lockdownem i umożliwienie osobom starszym nadal rozwijać swoje pasje, zainteresowania a także kontakty społeczne. 

<< Objectives >>

Celem projektu było stworzenie warunków do zwiększenia aktywności seniorów poprzez sztukę, kreatywność, kulturę oraz dostarczenie inspiracji osobom zajmującym się aktywizacją seniorów, poprzez dostarczenie adekwatnych narzędzi. Projekt powstał wraz ze środowiskiem seniorów i wynika z bogatego doświadczenia Wnioskodawcy i Partnerów. Zależało nam na poszerzeniu i rozwoju kompetencji cyfrowych seniorów poprzez korzystanie z narzędzi IT i wykorzystaniu ich do stworzenia konkretnych wytworów pracy takich jak zdjęcia, teksty. Narzędziami, które miały nam pomagać w osiągnięciu założeń były materiały edukacyjne w wersji cyfrowej, zasoby online, materiały tworzone w oparciu o e-learning i mikro-learning, poradniki, dobre praktyki. Udało się zaangażować bezpośrednio ponad 300 osób, które brały udział w wydarzeniach i współtworzyły Europejski Głos Seniora. Projekt dotarł bezpośrednio do ponad 50 edukatorów związanych z uczelniami wyższymi, NGO, ośrodkami społecznymi, ośrodkami sztuki. Działania projektowe dotarły do przedstawicieli kilkudziesięciu instytucji, które wspierają politykę dla osób starszych.

<< Implementation >>

W celu osiągnięcia wyników, partnerzy projektu wykorzystywali metodologię działań stosowaną w innych projektach. Głównym założeniem takiej metodologii jest zaangażowanie wszystkich partnerów w realizację wyników oraz weryfikację i opracowywanie produktów. Na każdym etapie zaplanowano działania weryfikacyjne i monitorowanie jakości (korekty merytoryczne, dyskusje, wymianę informacji). Cele projektu i rezultaty zostały osiągnięte poprzez: 1. Prace intelektualne ekspertów (rezultaty pracy intelektualnej) 2. Spotkania i warsztaty (spotkania projektowe połączone z warsztatami i testami rozwiązań proponowanych w projekcie) 3. Wydarzenie upowszechniające Działania w ramach projektu były bezpośrednio związane z osiąganiem celów projektu i realizacją zaplanowanych wyników. Dla każdego wyniku zaplanowano sekwencję działań z zapewnieniem informacji zwrotnych i mechanizmów kontrolnych. Działania monitorujące miały zapewnić wysoką jakość produktów i ich terminową realizację. Typowa sekwencja prowadząca do powstania rezultatu intelektualnego to: 1. Ustalenie punktu początkowego (na podstawie analizy potrzeb, wcześniejszych prac wykonanych itp.) 2. Ustalenie planu pracy i podział zadań (z uwzględnieniem możliwych zmian występujące po złożeniu projektu) 3. Praca nad rezultatami 4. Ponowne sprawdzenie i kontrola jakości 5. Testowanie 6. Modyfikacja 7. Wdrożenie 8. Rozpowszechnianie, wykorzystywanie i rozwój. Należy zauważyć, że działania w ramach projektu były bezpośrednio związane z regularnymi działaniami partnerów projektu, a wyniki będą miały bezpośrednie zastosowanie w instytucjach partnerskich. Wnioskodawca prowadził działania promocyjne i Public Relations prowadzące do osiągnięcia celów projektu i planowanych rezultatów, udostępniał rezultaty pracy intelektualnej na specjalnej stronie internetowej projektu, stronach internetowych członków konsorcjum, na profilach społecznościowych Prowadzano aktywne kontakty z otoczeniem partnerów np. kluby seniora, uniwersytety trzeciego wieku, galerie sztuki, uczelnie wyższe.  Partnerzy wykorzystali również  potencjał innych projektów (prowadzonych we własnych organizacjach i otoczeniu organizacji) do działań informacyjnych i upowszechniających.

<< Results >>

Rezultaty osiągnięte w trakcie trwania projektu: Rezultaty twarde: ilość uczestników spotkań międzynarodowych – 20, ilość uczestników szkoleń i warsztatów – około 80, ilość organizacji biorących udział w projekcie – 5, ilość rezultatów pracy intelektualnej – 3, ilość osób objętych wydarzeniami upowszechniającymi – ponad 300, udzielone wsparcie i zaktywizowanie co najmniej 300 seniorów (poprzez wspólną pracę przy Europejskim Głosie Seniora, konkursy, udział w wydarzeniach).
W ramach projektu zostały wypracowane następujące rezultaty o charakterze edukacyjnym O1 - MOOC - narzędzia i metody do pracy kreatywnej O2 - Dobre praktyki dla seniorów (w tym dokument Dobre Praktyki, Portfolio, Film z dobrymi praktykami) O3 - Seniorzy dla seniorów – Europejski Głos Seniora. 
Rezultaty związane z dotarciem: newsletter i mailingi wysłane do 15 000 osób, informacja o projekcie wyszła w wersji drukowanej (gazeta) w ilości 10 000 sztuk, 5 wydarzeń upowszechniających, 4 konkursy dla seniorów, ponad 20 informacji, postów, wzmianek o projekcie, ok. 50 instytucji, do których dotarła informacja o projekcie
Rezultaty miękkie: wzrost wiedzy edukatorów osób starszych w zakresie nowatorskich form i dobrych praktyk aktywizacyjnych, wzrost wiedzy na temat wykorzystania sztuki i kreatywności jako podstawy aktywizacji, wzrost wiedzy na temat narzędzi IT wspomagających aktywizację oraz działania artystyczne, wzrost wiedzy na temat zarządzania projektami partnerskimi wśród organizacji uczestniczących. Następujące obszary mogą zostać uznane za ważne dla przyszłego rozwoju instytucji biorących udział w projekcie: - kreatywne i krytyczne myślenie - umiejętności zarządzania projektami (w tym pisanie dotacji / wniosków, budżetowanie itp.) - zarządzanie ryzykiem - zarządzanie jakością - umiejętności pracy w sieci - kreatywne podejście do rozwóju produktów / usług - zarządzanie własnością intelektualną.
Chcieliśmy pokazać że osoby starsze są kreatywne i pełne sił witalnych. Połączyliśmy (pod kątem artystycznym/twórczym) osoby starsze z różnych krajów bowiem starość nie ma granic, jest obecna we wszystkich krajach w tym naszych partnerskich. Pokazaliśmy,  że dzięki sztuce i wspólnym działaniom zatracają się również granice językowe. Jednym z elementów projektu były wspólne warsztaty dla seniorów. Efektem tej współpracy są motywacje, inspiracje i grupa liderów, którzy przeniosą swoją pasję do lokalnych środowisk. Zależy nam na rozwoju wiedzy oraz umiejętności komunikacyjnych u osób 60+ tu przede wszystkim umiejętność pracy w zróżnicowanej (również językowo) grupie.

2021-1-RO01-KA220-ADU-000030224.title: Think differently and act differently
2021-1-RO01-KA220-ADU-000030224.summary:
<< Background >>

We implemented this project because we want to get involved in finding solutions to reduce the negative impact of household activities on the environment. We believe that adopting more environmentally friendly practices in the family is one way to meet this challenge.
The partners identified among local communities the need for awareness, education and motivation of individuals to adopt more environmentally friendly practices in the family. We found that there is a real interest among members of local communities to learn how to protect their environment. Many are aware that their practices are not sustainable, but they do not know what they need to do or how easy it is to get involved. Our answer to these needs was the TD&AD kit, an awareness-learning-motivation tool addressed to parents and children in an intergenerational learning approach. 
Its elaboration was possible through the collaboration of the partners' trainers after participating in 2 learning activities and the exchange of good practices.
For the results of our project to benefit as many organizations as possible, we created the TD&AD network at the European level.

<< Objectives >>

We implemented the TD&AD Project in order to raise awareness, educate and motivate people to adopt more environmentally friendly practices within families within households. To achieve this goal, we created the TD&AD kit as an intergenerational learning tool to put parents and children together.  In order for these results to have as much impact as possible, we disseminated them and transferred them to other organizations. 
The 4 objectives underlying the achievement of the project goal are: 
OB1." Improving competences and training methods in the field of environmental protection for 15 trainers through 2 transnational learning activities and exchange of good practices to create the learning tool for adults TD&AD"
OB2: "Competence development and skills training for a more environmentally friendly lifestyle for 50 families by using TD&AD during 2 non-formal learning activities"
OB3: "Raising awareness and motivating 500 families to adopt a more environmentally friendly attitude by using TD&AD"
OB4: "Creation of a TD&AD network at European level to support the transition to a more environmentally friendly lifestyle"

<< Implementation >>

The main activities implemented in the TD&AD project were:
•	2 learning activities and exchange of good practices with G1 members (partner trainers) in Portugal and Greece;
•	Development of TD&AD kit consisting of: Guide, 2 animated educational videos, e-Learning Platform;
•	2 TD&AD kit learning and testing workshops with 50 parents and their children (G2 members);
•	Awareness and motivation campaigns for more environmentally friendly practices with more than 500 parents;
•	5 multiplier events with a total of 222 participants
•	Promotion and dissemination activities 

<< Results >>

	Guide consisting of 2 chapters;
•	2 animated videos related to the impact of household impact on the environment and circular economy 
•	an e-Learning paltform  
•	2 training workshops
Results of Learning and Exchange of Good Practice Activities
•	Improved skills for 15 trainers in environmental protection and circular economy;
•	Training methods and techniques specific to intergenerational education.
Results of workshops with G2
•	Separate waste collection skills in the family
•	Skills to eliminate food, energy, and water waste
•	Reducing plastic consumption
•	TD&AD kit tested and improved for transferability.
• 30 posts on the project blog after the practical activities carried out in families of the target group
Results of awareness campaigns
•	510 parents aware and motivated to adopt more environmentally friendly practices in face-to-face and online meetings
• more than 20,000 persons  awarded and motivated  to adopt environmentally friendly attitudes on social media 

Multiplier event results
•   222 persons informed about project results
•	TD&AD network consisting of 63  Members
Results of the Dissemination Commission
•	64791 people came into contact with the TD&AD project and its results

2021-1-RO01-KA220-ADU-000035325.title: Hubs for entrepreneurs from rural areas
2021-1-RO01-KA220-ADU-000035325.summary:
<< Background >>

Women in the European space are to be encouraged to become business owners, as in the context of women’s business, we noticed a positive trend in regards to the number of women entrepreneurs, meaning that in Europe the need for teaching women to become entrepreneurs is to be highlighted. Women still face a noticeable gender pay gap and providing entrepreneurial skills to them sustains their development and creates the opportunity for women to become business owners and manage their own payroll. Also, women from rural areas are a vulnerable group and we need to help them find their way and build a career using their skills and competencies to develop a business and support the local economy. Thus, the project helped women from rural areas gain access to educational tools and opportunities for understanding what entrepreneurship means, as adult education trainers were provided a training methodology and a self assessment guide for sustaining courses to women from rural areas. Also, the topics of innovation and entrepreneurship strategy were developed throughout the project, published on the platform including an e-learning section and promoted to the adult education trainers and women from rural areas.

<< Objectives >>

The project aims to address high unemployment rates among rural women by providing support and resources to overcome educational challenges and empower them to become successful entrepreneurs. Our main goal is to develop effective tools and methodologies for entrepreneurship education, benefiting adult education trainers and aspiring female entrepreneurs. We conducted needs assessments, developed a training methodology, an e-learning platform, and a self-assessment guide, all digitally accessible. Throughout the project, we successfully met our objectives, enhancing entrepreneurial skills among adult education trainers and learners through innovative training methods and global best practices. Additionally, we sought to expand digital learning programs for female entrepreneurs, improve entrepreneurship competencies in rural women, and enhance organizational capacity in teaching innovation and business management strategies. Our e-learning platform facilitates the creation of a transnational network of female entrepreneurs and hubs.

<< Implementation >>

As the project aims to provide qualitative educational support for adult education trainers in the field of entrepreneurship, in order to support future female business owners from rural areas, the activities implemented throughout the project focused on developing practical solutions for strategic entrepreneurship teaching, adapted for women from rural areas. All activities were organized in 6 working packages, as follows: (1) Management and coordination - for which the project manager coordinated all activities and ensured the good collaboration of all partners through efficient discussion and problem solving when it was the case; (2) Communication, dissemination and exploitation, which includes - the website and all digital content produced and promoted, 5 multiplier events; (3) Monitoring, evaluation and quality management - including the creation and then the monitoring of the development of the project referring to the initially set indicators; (4) Training Methodology and Self-Assessment Guide - for which the partners collaborated to produce qualitative results, based on best proven global practices; (5) Online platform - which was constantly improved during the project and created to increase accessibility to educational content in the field of entrepreneurship, becoming a sustainable result of the project which will be available to the target group and to anyone interested in improving knowledge; (6) Piloting - through which we were allowed to experiment with the self-assessment, training course and online platform with final users and were able to improve the results, ensuring the quality of the educational materials published. All activities took place exactly as it is written in the project plan. 
All activities were conducted in order to leverage partners’ diversity of profiles, expertise and cultural background in the way of developing solutions that are accessible and relevant to the target group. Partners were selected according to their relevant experience, as they have either been involved in the implementation of other Erasmus projects, meaning that they have the necessary knowledge and they are either teachers, trainers, involved in learning activities for adults and / or social work. Starting with the management and coordination working package, we ensured throughout the project the good collaboration of partners so that the project’s outputs are available in all partners’ languages and communities, thus making sure qualitative dissemination of project’s results is achievable. Recurrent transnational project meetings were necessary and used to discuss the important aspects of the project, outlining key steps to follow and providing strategic solutions. Then, in order to achieve the project’s objective of increasing skills of adult education trainers and teachers regarding entrepreneurial expertise we organized 4 Learning, Teaching, Training (LTT) sessions, one in each of the partners’ countries, providing cultural background in addition to knowledge related to entrepreneurship strategies, including how to obtain funding, according to each country, how to manage a business and seeing examples of businesses in rural areas, in addition to moments of transnational networking helping the overall development and collaboration throughout the project. Moreover, aiming to create results that are digitally available, highly qualitative and relevant for future female business owners from rural areas, we researched proven best practices in entrepreneurship and used all relevant information to create an e-learning platform, a self-assessment guide and a training methodology, thus every teacher or trainer having access to resources to promote entrepreneurship in their local communities. All results were disseminated through 5 multiplier events, one in each country and an additional one in the project manager’s country, where 200 local participants attended and understood how the project’s results can be used in their communities in order to help support women from rural areas learn entrepreneurship and become business owners and community leaders. Letting the educational resources available digitally, online to anyone interested ensures the good sustainability of the project and a continuous dissemination of intellectual materials.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results of the project were the (1) self assessment guide and the training methodology - the entrepreneur handbook, designed to fit the needs of adult education trainers and learners in the field of entrepreneurship, based on learning in a self paced rhythm. These materials are to be used by people all over Europe & the world in general and thus it is important to ensure the quality of learning and accessibility. So, the learning handbook includes instructions for how to use it, how to study by yourself efficiently as it is based on asynchronous learning and all training materials are included in recommended training paths. This handbook is very relevant to the project as it is built in a modular form, allowing anyone interested to have a good learning experience and to use what parts are relevant to them, adjusting the material after it is downloaded and using it as a self assessment tool becoming easier than ever. This material has been realized according to thorough research and based on proven global best practices, as well as using expertise in the field of training innovation, ensuring the elearning solution is engaging for the target group. The methodology supports innovation in training and high effectiveness in what means teaching entrepreneurship, any participants to the training being involved as interactivity is a key point in the published methodology, as well as practical methods of teaching for engaging participants effectively. Materials are made to be easy to understand, written in a simplistic vocabulary so that everything is clear enough in order to create a straightforward training, in a more intuitive way. What is truly special about the handbook is that people from multiple countries worked upon its realization so the information was applied in different cultural contexts, adapted to each country’s necessities and so, having this target group - oriented methodology, we managed to facilitate the transfer of knowledge to local communities and more, and to women of different ages and different professional backgrounds. Easily transferable, the handbook has been created in order to sustain the continuous dissemination of knowledge and to facilitate implementing innovation intro trainings, interactivity, relevant information regarding entrepreneurship, adaptability and adjusting it to the needs of the participants, of female rural entrepreneurs, and to prompt self-development using it the self assessment guide. 
Another output of the project is the (2) online e-learning platform, where the thoroughly developed outcomes are still available and will remain available after the completion of the project, in a digital environment, accessible to anyone interested in entrepreneurship teaching and learning. Participants, trainers and anyone else can see and download the methodology and results developed during the project, thus ensuring the transferability of results, as well as the sustainability of the project. It only takes a few trainers to use the materials, either participants or beneficiaries of the project to disseminate the opportunity of using these materials in order to improve a teaching experience. The e-learning platform includes interactive sections so that learning becomes more efficient and thus it becomes an example of how the methodology can be applied, as teaching an interactive training, engaging participants, ensures highly effective learning. The platform contains pedagogical materials, learning objects, explanations on the way of teaching and the self assessment tool, so that the results become more attractive to the beneficiary. The platform also provides users with the possibility of approaching in more detail issues related to the project or curiosities in the field of entrepreneurship education, so related to the project’s materials and information provided through contacting the project manager. Interaction with other users and in the case of women -entrepreneurs from rural areas that want to discover more and network is possible then through a specific, open group similar to a forum, where different kinds of issues can be discussed. 
Another output of the project is the (3) best practice guide, realized based on our pilot testing outcomes and global best practices in entrepreneurship. This document is helping teaching and trainings with guidelines and advice regarding education in this field, alongside practical, useful recommendations, do’s and don’ts of teaching, especially created and adjusted for the target group and easy to use in their own trainings.
