2021-1-RS01-KA220-ADU-000028364.title: "Art of voices- art as a medium of support for voice hearers and other mental health care users"
2021-1-RS01-KA220-ADU-000028364.summary:
<< Background >>

Since the '90 war and crises and especially after the pandemic, mental health problems are a burning issue in the region of ex- Yugoslavia. According to the WHO regional EU office report (2014), there is a large treatment gap in low- and middle- income countries in South Eastern Europe where up to 50% of affected people do not receive care for their condition, Healthcare systems in high income countries provide a combination of care, medication and psychosocial interventions which successfully helps people affected by MH issues to lead a productive life and be integrated in society. However, LMICs have neither the funding nor enough qualified staff to provide such specialized services and unfortunately MH care is based mostly on using psychiatric drugs. The Balkan Hearing Voices Network, together with the UK partner Mind in Camden- experienced consortium in the field of community MH, recognized an urgent need to implement effective, low-cost and easily deliverable interventions to expand access to MH care and alleviate the suffering of psychiatry survivors and their families. The Art of voices training supports MH care practitioners with new skills through an innovative, integrative, multidisciplinary approach. 

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of this project were to provide EU adult education actors with quality training for the use of art as support for voice hearers and MH care users, promote the training and attract potential participants, pilot the training in order to ensure quality, and raise awareness on the subject of MH, human rights of voice hearers (and MH care users) and the potential of alternative approaches to the treatment of MH issues. During different phases of the project, we achieved the objectives set in the project application, exceeding some as well. The LTT activity in Sarajevo gave us an opportunity to pilot the training with the group of 30 participants- experts by experience and experts by profession (psychologists, psychotherapists, occupational therapists, etc.) and it turned out to be a great success (please see evaluation results in the LTT section). This success led to reaching more objectives- dissemination of the project was carried out more successfully then planned- we carried out the whole training on two more occasions- on Mentalfest in Rijeka, annual festival of MH and on the World Hearing Voices Congress in Paris, reaching a wider audience, potential future participants and rising awareness on the subject of MH.

<< Implementation >>

The Art of voices project activities included: 

1) General project coordination including regular monthly all team supervisions, individual supervisions with the supervisor from Mind in Camden and the representative of affiliated partner Portugal prints and country coordinator meetings, communication tracking, email and Viber group communication; 
2) Preparatory activities- preparation of resources and materials- local, regional and international desk research and mapping of the stakeholders, preparation of LEAP groups in each country- groups of "experts by experience"- psychiatric care users that gathered to provide valuable feedback on training modules; 
3) Development of each training module (results 1- 4) done by every team separately with regular feedback from local LEAP groups as well as by other teams on monthly bases and preparation of written material (guide)- handouts for LTT Sarajevo pilot training participants; 
4) Organization and logistics for the transnational project meeting in London, organized in the middle of the project and prior to LTT pilot training making sure we integrated the training segments in cohesive training module and to prepare for piloting; 
5) Organization, promotion, logistics for the Sarajevo LTT and coordination of the full 4- module training, evaluation and follow-up. This pilot training enabled us to test our module, and get valuable feedback of the participants, making sure the final product is in line with the EU standards in the field of adult education; 
6) Production of the final version (result 5)- the second half of the project, after piloting, was dedicated to the production of the final version of the full training (result 5) and adaptation of this result for the online version, based on thorough research, development of separate segments, piloting and evaluation; 
7) Online training included adaptation of the handouts for online format and recordings of video materials, research and testing of the platform for online courses (https://aov.thinkific.com/pages/art-of-voices) and finally uploading, designing, launching and promoting our online training. 
8) Multiplier events- successful multiplier events were organized in all partner countries, attracting more participants than expected. Multiplier events in Slovenia, UK and Bosnia and Herzegovina were organized prior to the LTT pilot training in Sarajevo aiming to promote the pilot training in the region and raise awareness on the project and the Art of voices training, and in Croatia and Serbia- the events were organized in October 2023, on the occasion of the World Mental Health Day as part of annual mental health festivals taking place in the cities of Rijeka and Belgrade. We used these occasions to further promote the project, and especially to announce the online training that will be available by the end of 2023. We used the multiplier event in Rijeka to carry out the whole full 4- module training once again, although that was not originally planned in the application. We used this opportunity to reach wider audience and promote the training, but also to achieve institutional recognition since Croatian partner Dom Turnic is a state institution, recognized by local and regional decision makers and the annual festival of mental health- Mentalfest is highly visible and recognized by the public.  
9) Dissemination- apart from these events, we also got invited to the World Hearing Voices Congress in Paris where we carried out two out of four training modules and had the chance to promote the Art of voices project and training in front of an international audience (Denmark, Netherlands, UK, USA, France, etc.). This dissemination activity was also not planned but contributed immensely in particular to project dissemination, but the realization of project objectives as well. It also resulted in two invitations for the whole team to provide the full face to face training in France and Croatia.
Other dissemination activities included: preparation and dissemination of promotional, educational material, social networks, media, creating a network of training participants and other potentially interested professionals/ supporters/ users by collecting contact details and maintaining contact, aiming to reach wider audience and raise awareness about mental health and different approaches to mental health care. 
10) Monitoring and evaluation- PTT (Progress Tracking Tool) was created by partner Tavan to facilitate the process of M&E and it has proven to be rather helpful because it enabled the partners to evaluate the project progress in an user friendly and ready to use tool, developed specifically to fulfill the M&E needs of this specific project (please see results in the "Monitoring and Evaluation" section). 

<< Results >>

The most important final result of the Art of voices project is the result 5- the final version of the full 4- module, integrative, multidisciplinary training in the use of different art forms- visual arts, literature, improvisation and theatre, in working with voice hearers and mental health care users. This training was developed both for offline (face to face) and online use and is  available for mental health professionals, community supporters, volunteers and students that provide services to mental health care users, but also to users or "experts by experience", as called in the Hearing Voices movement.
The training is in line with the quality standards and criteria in the EU adult education in the field of mental health. The face to face training includes live workshops coordinated by artists and mental health professionals from four partner countries. For the purpose of a short, 2 or 3-day format, the team agreed that each module should last for 3 hours (with the possibility to develop a longer version depending on the needs and context), and the whole program includes the introductory part coordinated by all teams, as well as final evaluation and feedback, wrap-up session usually led by Tavan. 
As a supervisor, the partner from the UK- Mind in Camden, with the support of the affiliated partner Portugal prints, experienced in developing and providing artistic educational activities, provided valuable feedback throughout the project, both through individual and all teams’ supervisions. 
Result 5 is composed by results 1- 4. 
Result 1 (visual arts/ art therapy)- the team of Prostor (artist, art therapist and community supporter and medical doctor and artist, both with decades long experience in the context of mental visual arts and mental health), developed the training segment that uses visual arts in therapeutic purposes in providing support to voice hearers and mental health service users. Artistic creation and its therapeutic properties are used to help overcome psychological distress, promote self-confidence, sense of achievement, self-worth, socialization, communication and social skills in a protected environment. This training module offers a new type of communication on individual and social level, often less threatening than verbal communication. The aims of the module are: to provide professionals with basic skills for the use of the art in the context of providing support to vulnerable populations, especially in the context of mental health, focusing on the awareness of the necessity to respect all ethical considerations, to practice adequate communication (non-hierarchic, authentic, with empathy, etc.); to have basic knowledge and skills to increase motivation, concentration, imagination, etc.; to introduce art’s transcendent and transformative capacity through particular workshops. Some of the main aims of visual art workshops explained in this module are: to empower participants to start enjoying art and widen their cultural interests, to support participants to reach the state of "flow"- a state that increases focus, energy level and involvement. The staff of psychiatric hospitals often thinks that most users of psychiatric services, especially those diagnosed with some of the diagnoses from the psychotic spectrum, are not able to make any progress. Art therapy has proven to be one of the most efficient methods in providing support to this population, based on recent studies done by NICE, UK (https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg178). Since the Hearing voices movement is entirely based on the “person centered” approach, we focused this training segment, but also the other 3 modules, on breaking these prejudices and supporting future practitioners in delivering quality, human rights based services to their users. We also consulted the local LEAP group throughout the development of the module. This module is based on one decade long practice of Prostor, and the methods used in regular visual arts and art therapy activities were adjusted to the training format, improved and integrated, so that they make a cohesive unit with other 3 training segments developed by partners, applicable in the practice of mental health care providers both in institutional and the community settings. 
Result 2 (literature/ bibliotherapy)- The team of Tavan (2 psychologists and psychotherapists in training, one with the master’s degree in world literature, as well, both with many years of experience in working with mental health care users in the community settings, as well as with organizing training in the Hearing Voices approach), developed this module. Literature and psychology are fields that are intertwined in many ways. Many literary works directly deal with topics from psychology, and we could say that every literary work is a commentary on the human condition and therefore deals with human behavior and psyche. Numerous mental health professionals recognize this fact and use literature in their work in a number of ways that come together under the name of bibliotherapy. This is not a therapeutic direction but emphasizes the fact that literature can have a therapeutic effect. Reading and writing helps us to better understand our own psychological states and processes. This module was based on long practice of Tavan literary support group and it includes a strong "expert by experience" perspective and profound love for literature. The module itself consists out of several separate but interconnected segments or different techniques- from free writing to personal script, group sharing and integration. The great advantage is that each of these techniques has been tried and worked out with the people with the lived experience and the local LEAP group during the preparation of the module allowing for a blend of theory and practice, turning this experience and knowledge into a unique training segment that brought mental health professionals closer to different techniques with which they can us in their everyday work. During the development of the module, the methods used in regular literary activities have been improved and integrated, so that they make a cohesive unit with the training segments developed by other partners, applicable in the practice of mental health care providers both in institutional and the community setting. Main aims achieved in this module are: to empower participants to learn what it means to use a literary perspective as a way of looking at the world and our experiences, to show participants the benefits and power working with literature for mental health and to give participants tools that they can use in group reading and writing workshops to support others (and themselves). Outcomes of the module: participants understand what it means to work from a literary perspective when supporting others (and themselves), participants understand the role of words and language (or terminology) related to the way we connect to each other and ourselves, when we are in different states of mind, participants gained emotional, practical and creative tools that they can adapt in their everyday work supporting others. 
Result 3 (theatre/ drama therapy) - the team of Dom Turnic (occupational therapist trained in sensorimotor reintegration and actor and illusionist, both with many years of experience in creating and implementing this program and providing services for mental health care users in institutional and community settings, as well as with organizing training in the Hearing Voices approach), developed this training module that uses theatre as means of psychological and social support. Drama therapy is the intentional use of drama and/or theater processes to achieve therapeutic goals; it is an embodied practice that is active and experiential. The aim of this module is to provide the context for participants to tell their stories, set goals and solve problems, express feelings, or achieve catharsis, using theatre techniques to facilitate personal growth and promote mental health. Participants in drama therapy follow roles to tell a story or perform a part, thus embracing a new perspective of the character and themselves. Another key element is space, or where the acting takes place. Other components of drama therapy module include ritual, conflict, resistance, spontaneity, distance and catharsis. Drama therapy works to shed light on feelings and behaviors of a person and helps teach ways to manage and overcome obstacles they struggle with. This module is a result of a decade of coordinating drama workshops for the purpose of recovery, and it is a combination of relaxation, dance, movement, fun, and improvisation, voice exercises, creating a script and performing. Training participants went through a series of exercises that include sensorimotor workshops, exploring their senses in relation to their own body, the material environment and the intangible environment, and which encourage sensorimotor reintegration. The module includes role-play in which actors explore the energy of the characters they are in during the exercise. Going through the most diverse states and energy of the characters during the exercises, they get the opportunity to express the deepest emotions, often deeply hidden and repressed. In addition to exploring emotions and states, exercises help to recognize and understand one’s own reactions in certain life situations, thus increasing the possibility of coping with difficult life situations or psychological states. The theatre troupe composed by psychiatric care users (local LEAP group in this project) was created through the process, and was recognized in the local community and contributes immensely to a sense of success and productivity in members. Members of Hearing voices groups, who go through theater workshops, state that the program helps them recognize their own emotions and empowers them in relation to the voices and improves the sense of self-worth. It has been shown to reduce fear of public speaking, express creativity, develop a sense of humor and develop a sense of value, self-confidence, improve intra and inter personal communication, develop group cohesion, enhance a sense of belonging, productivity and easier and better integration into society. We would like to train professionals and volunteers in institutions or CSOs, in order to acquire skills that they could use in their work. Training curriculum: Sensorimotor workshops, Role- playing and emotion recognition workshops, Creating a show, Public performance of the play in the theater in the local community. During the project, the methods used in regular drama therapy activities are going to be improved and integrated, so that they make a cohesive unit with the training segments developed by other partners, applicable in the practice of mental health care providers both in institutional and the community setting.

Result 4 (improvisation/ performance art and voice hearing)- developed by the Hearing Voices Slovenia team (2 professional actors- performers with previous experience in working in the community mental health context and a University professor in the department of social pedagogy with many years of experience in working with mental health care users in community settings, teaching and organizing training in the Hearing Voices approach), developed this module in the field of performing arts. The module covers theatrical approaches, dance, as well as elements of clowning and music, and above all, artistic improvisation and collective stage creation. The key principle is the principle of reprocessing life by performative artistic means, the artistic transformation of the personal. This principle allowed participants to create a playful distance to their topics, stories, thoughts and feelings, which helps with confronting, accepting, processing experiences, hearing them and giving them space, encourages experimentation. This stage refabricating also allows for contact with other participants and joint processing of topics. Artistically transformed themes also address and touch the viewers and vibrate with their own content and lives. During the development of the module, the methods used in regular performance art activities of Hearing Voices Slovenia, were improved and integrated, so that they make a cohesive unit with the training segments developed by other partners, applicable in the practice of mental health care providers both in institutional and the community setting. Some of the achieved aims of this module include: engaging with the proposals on how to use approaches of artistic improvisation in support work, getting to know the tools for creating performative situations built upon the personal stories of participants and consider ways of holding the supportive environment and taking into account the immediate context.
The online training module is composed of the same content but adjusted to online format, so people who decide to take the online course can enjoy similar benefits as participants who were present on the face to face training. Obviously, taking in consideration that artistic creation is very much about live expression and human contact, the online version cannot reach those goals, but through short and interesting videos and the possibility of contacting the trainers, we managed to overcome this obstacle. The online training is available on Thinkific platform on the following link https://aov.thinkific.com/pages/art-of-voices, and the link can also be found on the website and social media of the Balkan Hearing Voices Network. Short online tests and certificates are also available and at disposal for participants who finish the course successfully. The offline/ face to face training will also be offered to different institutions, CSOs or individuals interested in hiring the team of authors/trainers to provide face to face training in their respective communities/ countries, after the end of the Erasmus+ funding, thus providing sustainability. The face to face training is carried out in all partner countries languages- including Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, Slovenian and English languages, while the online version is done in local languages with English subtitles. The main output of this project is an increased number of trained professionals/ community supporters/ experts by experience/ students/ volunteers in the West Balkan region and the European union. The end users of this training gained new knowledge, skills and an opportunity to change their attitude toward mental health service users, improve their practice and start implementing alternative approaches to the treatment of mental health issues, thus improving life quality of their beneficiaries and changing wrong public attitudes on the subject. This project resulted in an increased interest in education in alternative approaches to mental health and the improvement of both institutional and community practice.

TRANSNATIONAL PROJECT MEETING
A three day- transnational project meeting in London was organized before the piloting phase (LTT activity in Sarajevo), toward the middle of the project. In the first half of the Art of voices project, we focused mostly on the development of individual training modules, with regular online support from our UK partner Mind in Camden and consultations with affiliated partner Portugal prints through individual and all team supervisions, so we used the opportunity of this transnational meeting, to get to know the other teams/ trainers in person, try out all 4 modules among ourselves both as trainers and participants and discuss further steps in integrating the 4 modules in final full version of the Art of voices training (result 5). All teams participated (2 persons per country). Country coordinator meeting was also held on this occasion, revising what was done in the project so far and discussing the management and implementation activities carried out, finances and reporting. We also focused on communication and dissemination, as well as next steps and project evaluation planning. The remaining two and a half days will be dedicated to the training module development. Firstly, together with a training expert from Mind in Camden and expressive art therapy consultant from Portugal prints, we revised each segment of the training module thoroughly. This revision was crucial at this point in order to systemize each segment, test the methodology and approach that was used, make sure it can work as a whole with other 3 training modules, both online and offline. And most importantly, to have experts from Mind in Camden with many years of organizing and delivering training in the field of alternative approaches for supporting voice hearers and mental health service users, supervise the integration of the four separate training segments in the final, multidisciplinary training module that responds to the real needs of adult learners in the field and to the criteria and standards in EU adult education. We choose London for this meeting in order to facilitate full participation from the UK partners as well as the use of all available resources they can offer on the spot, including the valuable advice from their staff and London LEAP group.

LTT PILOT TRAINING SARAJEVO
Pilot training took place in Sarajevo. It lasted three days, 19.-21. May 2023. In total 26 participants were present, 8 trainers from all partner countries as well as 2 supervisors from the UK, plus one country coordinator from Slovenia. 
Participants were experts by practice (psychologists, psychotherapists, occupational therapists, artists), including students as future experts by practice and experts by experience (LEAP group and other participants). We’ve had 2 participants from Slovenia (along with trainers) that are experts by experience and have an important role in peer activities in their country, and the rest of the participants were from Sarajevo.
38% of the participants were present at our multiplier event held prior to the pilot training, so they got the necessary information on that event, where we also had time to talk about expectations. Another 30% of the participants contacted us directly and we held short consultations, either online or in person, and they were mostly members of other organizations and institutions that we work closely with. For about 20% of the participants this was the first time they got involved with Tavan.  Additional attention and preparation were given to experts by experience and LEAP group, making sure they have all the necessary information for their informed decision about attending the training.
During the training, at the venue we had a common place dedicated to participants if they needed alone or quiet time to process their experiences that came up during the training. Also, in each workshop, as agreed in previous meetings, we’ve had two people or ‘aunties’ ready to offer additional support if anybody of the participants needed it. All the participants had support and co-created safe space within each workshop. The whole training and its program were planned according to principles of safe space and support, ensuring the maximum of experiential learning.
All the participants started the work in the big group, and we did introductions in that way. After that, the group divided into two smaller groups, so the work would be more effective, and we had time on breaks to share, hang out in the common area. Each participant went through all 4 workshops – artistic improvisation, drama, visual arts and literature, and each module had different expectations and tasks for them. At the end or the third day, we closed the training again in the big group, offering enough time to process the whole training and to share thoughts, feelings, expectations, and achievements.
The pilot training allowed us to test the separate segments of the training as well as to test how it functions. One of the things that it showed us is that it has a great potential, and that different modules lean on each other, that each next one takes into consideration different aspects of our experiences as human beings and it helps us build on them, while making a lasting and positive change. All the participants were unanimous that this training was needed, for them personally but also that more training like this is needed for professionals by practice as it models the cooperation between experts by practice and experts by experience based on respect, safe space, personal responsibility, and agency.
After sharing and feedback, each participant fulfilled an evaluation form for the training, after which we had a short certificate awarding ceremony. Each participant received a certificate of attendance, indicating the number of days and hours spent in learning, and for the trainers – in teaching.
 
MULTIPLIER EVENTS

BELGRADE
The Belgrade multiplier event "Art and Mental health" was organized by the lead applicant Prostor, in cooperation with partner organizations from the Serbian Mental Health Movement, on the occasion of the International Day of Mental Health on October 10th, 2023, within the III Belgrade Festival of Mental Health, in Belgrade Youth Center (Dom Omladine). 
The multiplier event was divided in theoretical and practical part, aiming at reaching a greater number of people by a wider discussion on the power of art in the context of vulnerable populations and at the same time- offering a concrete, tangible experience for practitioners that can benefit directly from the training. It was decided to organize this event in October, prior to finalizing the online training so it can be promoted and offered as a next step after the initial workshop. The event included a presentation of Result 1- the training module Visual arts workshop, a round table on the use of the arts in providing support to vulnerable populations, especially in the mental health context, screening of a short documentary film about the work of Prostor from the users’ perspective, followed by a mini exhibition of art works and products created by psychiatric care users. 
Result 1- Visual arts workshop, as one of the 4 training modules for the use of art in providing support to the users of psychiatric services, was led by Serbian Art of Voices team- Prim dr Bogdanka Cabak – medical doctor and artist and the project coordinator Mina Aleksic - artist and art therapist. Main target group for this workshop were occupational therapists, but also other mental health staff and community supporters of partner institutions and organizations. There were 19 participants.
The round table that gathered 49 people (mental health professionals, students, volunteers, artists, community supporters and psychiatric care users), was aimed at presenting different art forms as tools for providing support to a variety of marginalized and vulnerable populations, providing the participants with an opportunity for a “glimpse” into the whole 4- module Art of Voices training. Apart from Mina Aleksic, as moderator, the speakers were experts- artists/ psychologists/ community supporters with many years of experience in using art as a powerful tool for individual support and social change. Vera Erac- psychologist, artist, body psychotherapist from association Transformator, Irena Ristic from association Hop la!- theatre director, psychologist, professor at the Faculty of Dramatic Arts, Aleksandra Jelic from  association Aps Art – artist and theatre director, and Bosiljka Brdar- user led organization Dusa and art community TribeF20, artist.
The round table aims to promote artistic creativity as an effective form of psychosocial support vulnerable groups.
the opportunity to attend the screening of the short documentary film "(U)druzenje Prostor" by Vanja Matic and Vanja Stulic, created within the School of Visual Anthropology organized by the Center for Visual anthropology and DC Krov in cooperation with the association Prostor. Accompanying program: A mini-exhibition/fair of artworks and products by people with problems mental health. Visitors had  the opportunity to meet the authors as well as volunteers and members associations engaged in providing support to citizens in the field of mental health in the community.

RIJEKA
The multiplier event was organized in the new occupational therapy premises- a newly  constructed building in Dom Turnic compound, and it was incorporated in the program of the annual festival of mental health- Mentalfest, aiming to reach a wider audience, since this Festival already has a tradition of successfully attracting the public with its variety of interesting and important content. Mentalfest traditionally lasts for the whole week around the International mental health day on October the 10th, and includes many different public events such as round tables, conferences and many other manifestations dedicated to different aspects of the subject of mental health (mental health and work, aging, the youth, etc.), taking place in the City hall, different hotels, cafes and public spaces.  
This Art of Voices multiplier event was one of the events that attracted the public attention and it included the presentation of the whole Art of Voices project for general public and the practical part- the whole 4- module training for Dom Turnic staff, the staff of the partner institutions and organ

2021-1-SE01-KA220-ADU-000028217.title: The CREATIVE AGORA: empowerment and education through participatory and community arts
2021-1-SE01-KA220-ADU-000028217.summary:
<< Background >>

CREATIVE AGORA was driven by the desire to promote the European dimension in non-formal participatory arts education for adults, particularly targeting disadvantaged and diverse communities. It aimed to address the unique intrinsic ability of community and participatory arts and creative expression to engage adults alienated or excluded by traditional adult education offers and to promote transnational exchange and transfer of practice. The project specifically focused on developing 'artists as educators' to foster educational and social inclusion for all, addressing challenges faced by these educators, such as precarious employment, lack of professional recognition or validation, barriers to accessing professional development and isolation. It promoted innovations in formal and non-formal adult education in Europe through creative practices in various art forms, breaking down barriers to learning for adults in disadvantaged and migrant communities, thereby contributing to social inclusion, empowerment, and recovery from the Covid pandemic's impacts.

<< Objectives >>

CREATIVE AGORA aimed to enhance the professional development and recognition of artists as educators within non-formal adult education, focusing on participatory and community arts. Its concrete objectives were (a) the creation of innovative, new learning materials supporting educators, particularly sessional and freelance tutors working as 'artists as educators' in formal and non formal adult education settings, (b) developing a European learning 'community of practice' that fostered transfer and exchange of best practice between artist educators at a transnational level, and (c) design and transfer of learning and practice between fields of community education, the arts and technology. The objectives also included promoting social inclusion and empowerment through arts, targeting disadvantaged and diverse communities, thus contributing to a more inclusive and creative Europe.

<< Implementation >>

CREATIVE AGORA implemented a range of activities to achieve its objectives, combining both traditional Erasmus+ activities with innovative concepts. These activities included:

•	Facilitating exchange and learning among artist educators across borders to share and co-create solutions, methodologies, and learning materials.
•	Developing open-access resources for broader dissemination and use in adult education, particularly in participatory and community arts including case studies and learning modules on Internationalisation, Health and Wellbeing and the Social Impact of participatory arts practice.
•	Engaging with ultimate beneficiaries to validate the developed learning materials and methods, ensuring their effectiveness and relevance.
•	Focusing on the professional development of artist educators to enhance their skills and competences in adult education through participatory arts.
•	Conducting extensive outreach programs to share project outcomes and engage wider communities, leveraging festivals and cultural projects for broader impact.
•	Establishing a digital platform for ongoing collaboration, knowledge exchange, and co-creation among artist educators, fostering a sense of community and shared learning.
•	Implementing local groups for peer review and collaborative development, tailored to national and linguistic contexts, to extend participation and ensure the relevance and applicability of methodologies.

These activities were designed to create a flexible engagement process, supporting casual to deep participation levels, and were underpinned by core principles of adult learning through participatory arts. The approach aimed to innovate adult education practices, promote social inclusion, and support the professional development of artists as educators, addressing their unique challenges and leveraging their potential to contribute to educational and social objectives.


<< Results >>

CREATIVE AGORA resulted in significant outputs and achievements, as outlined below:
1. Technical Framework for Participatory Arts Education: Led by Folkuniversitetet, this framework established a technical foundation for the digital environment and communication tools supporting a community of practice for transnational exchange and learning among adult learners in community and cultural settings outside formal education.
2. Open Educational Resource (OER) for Digital Learning Community: Spearheaded by Rinova Málaga from Spain, this OER provided a digital learning platform and resources for the digital learning community, making project outputs and results accessible and available transnationally.
3. Digital Learning Suite for Artist Educators: Managed by DIMITRA Education & Consulting from Greece, this suite comprised three blended learning modules focused on internationalization and intercultural awareness, health and wellbeing, and the social impact of participatory arts education.
These outputs were designed to support artist educators and engage adult learners from marginalized and disadvantaged communities, facilitating the transfer and exchange of best practices among educators at a transnational level. The project fostered the development of professional competences for independent artist educators, enhancing their ability to access professional development and internationalize their practice, significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.

The digital platform and community of practice it created offered unrestricted access to learning resources, peer mentoring, and support, ensuring sustainability beyond the project's life. The outputs validated, tested, and disseminated through various activities, reached an extensive audience and contributed to raising awareness of innovative adult learning practices embedded in participatory arts education methodologies, promoting social inclusion, civic competences, and critical thinking.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-SI01-KA220-ADU-000026810.title: Twisted Tales Educational Toolkit for parent tutoring and inter-generational learning
2021-1-SI01-KA220-ADU-000026810.summary:
<< Background >>

Fairy tales, as originally written, were perfectly suited to the subject of stigmas. It is only in the more recent sanitised re-interpretations that their valuable lessons have become lost. The modern versions of fairy tales like Cinderella, Sleeping Beauty, and Snow White are very different from their originals. Instead of important life lessons, they teach girls to wait for a prince to save them. Stereotypes like passive women with dubious life goals were not always part of the tales, either. TwistedEDU rewrites these tales with an eye to lessons for a world of empathy and understanding and without bias of the stigmas in question.
Re-telling well-known fairy tales provides an important familiarity to effectively emphasize the new digital narrative developments.
Needs covered by the project:
- Lack of quality content for parental education on creativity and family co-creation
- Low level of digital competences among grandparents
- Lack of the awareness on the benefits of new and emerging technologies/digital tools


<< Objectives >>

TwistedEdu is an educational project whose overall goal is to contribute to non-formal and informal adult learning with a creative and cultural component to support children in improving their creativity and empathy for vulnerable groups. 
By developing tools that foster innovative approaches to participation and intercultural dialogue in local languages, this project contributes to the development of digital competencies and skills of adults while also promoting social inclusion of vulnerable groups. More precisely, the project contributes to:
the non-formal and informal learning of adults with a creative and empathy component that supports young generation in improving their creativity and sensibility for vulnerable groups
the non-formal and informal learning of adults in acquiring new skills and competences, forefronting digital competences
social inclusion of vulnerable groups through the arts, by fostering innovative participatory and intercultural dialogue approaches


<< Implementation >>

Implemented activities:
Transnational Meetings (3) delivered in Montenegro, Croatia and Serbia, supporting detailed planning of the project implementation and IO developments.
In-depth Research, conducted to analyze needs and aspirations of the targeted groups.
Creation of Audio-tales, well-known fairy tales reinterpreted and rewritten, localized, and digitized. 
Development of the application, to stimulate creativity, as well as a deeper understanding of a particular theme of stigma. 
Tutorial Package Design, to bring the awareness on HOW to use the application and the method
Development of the Experiential Installation, an innovative form of engagement with the target groups through the performing arts and UGC.
Delivery of Mutual Learning Events (2) merged with Partner Meetings to maximize the impact of the knowledge sharing activity among partners.
Development and implementation of Dissemination Conference (4) in Slovenia, Serbia, Croatia and Montenegro.


<< Results >>

Project Results:
Research - Detailed analysis of the final beneficiaries’ groups’ needs (IO1) in-depth analysis of the beneficiary groups' needs and aspiration was delivered in a white paper form, serving as a ground for IO2, IO3 and IO4 developments.
Audio tales - Tales creation, digitalisation and localization (IO2) one existing Twisted Tales (Cinda Real) and four newly created fairy tales (Allen and the Magic Lamp, Desire and the Snow Queen, New Hansel and Grettel,  Little Red Bianca) reinterpreted, localized, and digitized, serving as a tool to stimulate creativity and provide a deeper understanding of a particular theme of stigma. The stories are available in five different languages: Slovenian, Croatian, Serbian, Montenegrin, and English. While Cinda Real is also available in Spanish language.
App for creativity - Web and mobile application for participatory creation (IO3) accessible via Android Play Store, Apples I-Store, and Twisted Tales website.
Tutorials - Tutorial package Twisted Tales for parents and grandparents (IO4) that equips adults with the knowledge on how to use the new tools for promotion of creativity and empathy among children.
Exhibition / Experimental installation and online archive of user generated stories (UGC) -  Twisted Tales experimental installation and online archive of user generated stories (IO5), to motivate parents, grandparents and children to participate in the experience and to return to the learning programme and to create and share UGC (user generated content).
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2021-1-SI01-KA220-ADU-000033626.title: HELP TO OPPORTUNITIES
2021-1-SI01-KA220-ADU-000033626.summary:
<< Background >>

S projektom smo želeli izboljšati zdravstveno pismenost Romov, spodbujati zdrav življenjski slog, povečati zaupanje v zdravstveni sistem ter zmanjšati diskriminacijo in neenakosti, povezane z zdravjem. Povod za izvedbo projekta H2O je ugotovitev partnerskih organizacij, da je zdravstvena nepismenost Romov eden izmed dejavnikov, ki vodi v socialno izključenost, slabšo zdravstveno oskrbo in nezdrav življenjski slog. Kjub temu, da se o tem veliko pogovarjamo, se soočamo s številnimi omejitvami, kako vplivati na izboljšanje trenutnega stanja ter kakšne pristope pri tem uporabiti. Projekt skozi različne faze zagotavlja konkretne rešitve, ki jih je mogoče nadgraditi in celo prilagoditi drugim skupinam, kjer prihaja do razlik v primerjavi z večinskim narodom. 

Projekt H2O je obravnaval naslednje potrebe:
- Nizko stopnjo zdravstvene pismenosti, ki se kaže v nerazumevanju diagnoz, potekov bolezni in nezaupanju v zdravstvene sisteme.
- Nezdrav življenjski slog.
- Vzpostavitev zaupanja, s ciljem zmanjševanja izključenost Romov iz zdravstvenih sistemov.
- Razvoj mreže in usposabljanje laičnih izobraževalcev, da bi bolje razumeli in naslavljali zdravstvene potrebe romske skupnosti.

<< Objectives >>

Z izvedbo projekta H2O smo želeli:
- Razviti enoten program zdravstvene pismenosti za Rome, ki bo prilagojen specifičnim potrebam romske skupnosti.
- Izboljšati zdravstveno pismenost Romov tako, da izboljšamo znanje in razumevanje Romov o zdravju, boleznih, zdravljenju in preventivi.
- Vplivati na zdrav življenjski slog in spodujati navade, ki vodijo k boljšemu zdravju in manjši obolevnosti.
- Usposobiti romske izobraževalce laike, katerih vloga bo izvedba programa zdravstvene pismenosti in spodbujanje zdravega življenjskega sloga.
- Razvijati digitalne kompetence, ki bodo pripadnikom romske skupnosti omogočile lažji dostop do informacij o zdravju.
- Z vključevanjem Romov kot izobraževalcev laikov zmanjšati diskriminacijo na področju zdravja in povečati vključenost Romov v družbo.
- Posledično smo želeli vplivati tudi na razvoj socialnih, kulturnih in državljanskih kompetenc ter krepiti zaupanje v zdravstveni sistem.

<< Implementation >>

V okviru projekta H2O so bile izvedene naslednje aktivnosti:

- Pet mednarodnih uskladitvenih srečanj, kjer so bili pregledani dosežki in rezultati projekta, načrtovanje dodatne aktivnosti ter analiziran učinek projekta.
- Organiziranih je bilo osem multiplikativnih dogodkov za predstavitev projekta in njegovih rezultatov lokalnim in regionalnim deležnikom v različnih državah.
- Namesto štirih smo ivedli osem pilotnih izobraževanj po nastalem programu za dvig zdravstvene pismenosti Romov, v vseh partnerskih državah. Do tega je prišlo zaradi želje po večjem učinku programa, saj smo na ta način zmanjšali morebitne jezikovne bariere ter smo nekaterim temam tako posvetili več časa.
- Izvedeno je bilo obsežno usposabljanje romskih izobraževalcev laikov za izvajanje programa zdravstvene pismenosti, ki je potekalo v dveh delih - 5 dni na spletu in 5 dni v živo v Solunu.
- Razvili smo pet intelektualnih rezultatov (Primarno in sekundarno raziskavo o zdravju Romov in ravni zdravstvene pismenosti v partnerskih državah, Program usposabljanja romskih izobraževalcev laikov, Program dviga ravni zdravstvene pismenosti in zdravega življenjskega sloga za Rome, Vzpostavitev spletne platforme in razvoj mobilne aplikacije, izdelava družabne igre "Healthivity").
- Vsa pomembna poročila in materiale smo prevedli v nacionalne jezike in angleščino.
- Pripravili smo nastavke kviza za napredno učenje, ki bo dostopen na spletni strani projekta.
- Izvajali smo obsežno diseminacijo projekta in projektnih aktivnosti, vključno z zaključno mednarodno konferenco, katere se jeudeležilo več kot 100 ljudi različnih profilov udeležencev (odločevalci, strokovnjaki, nevladniki, učitelji, izobraževalci, predstavniki centrov za socialno delo, predstavniki občin, zdravstveni delavci itd.).
- Po najboljših močeh smo gradili trajnost projekta in projektnih rezultatov.
- Intenzivno smo delali na ozaveščanju Romov o pomenu zdravja in zdravega življenjskega sloga.

Poleg navedenega je pomemben dosežek projekta tudi priznanje razvitega programa usposabljanja s strani Centra za usposabljanje in vseživljenjsko učenje Univerze v Tesaliji kot programa stalnega usposabljanja z obremenitvijo 4 ECTS. Prav tako so bile pripravljene smernice na ravni EU, ki bodo posredovane nacionalnim in evropskim organom.

<< Results >>

Izvedba projekta je stremila h kakovosti, kjer bodo rezultati projekta raznoliki in segajo od konkretnih izdelkov, kot so programi usposabljanja in digitalna orodja, do širših družbenih učinkov, kot so izboljšanje zdravstvene pismenosti, boljši življenjski slog in večja vključenost Romov v družbo. Tako so v okviru projekta nastali naslednji izdelki:

- Anketni vprašalnik za preverjanje zdravstvene pismenosti in zdravstvenega stanja pripadnikov romske skupnosti.
- Poročilo o analizi zdravstvenega stanja Romov v sodelujočih državah. 
- Podatkovna baza z zbranimi podatki po državah (N=247).
- Poročilo o programu usposabljanja romskih laičnih izobraževalcev za izvajanje programa zdravstvene pismenosti in zdravega življenjskega sloga za Rome.
- Brošura s povzetki programa zdravstvene pismenosti za Rome.
- Program zdravstvene posmenosti za Rome, ki je razdeljen na pet modulov, ki vsebujejo po štiri poglavja.
- Povzetki vseh petih modulov z opredeljenimi cilji in učnimi vsebinami.
- Spletna stran, ki je na voljo na naslednjem naslovu: https://www.h2oerasmus.eu/
- Aplikacija za android pametne telefone, ki je na voljo na naslednjem naslovu: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.app.h2oerasmus
- Priporočila in smernice za odločevalce na EU ravni.
- Namizna igra Healthivity
- Nabor vprašanj za napredno učenje in preverjanje zdravstvene pismenosti v obliki kviza, ki bo dostopen na spletni strani projekta.

Poleg konkretnih izdelkov med projektne rezultate štejejo tudi:
- S programom usposabljanja za romske laične izobraževalce in spremnimi aktivnostmi smo ustvarili usposobljene posameznike, ki lahko suvereno širijo znanje med skupnostjo ter imajo na voljo nova orodja in metode za delo.
- S programom zdravstvene pismenosti smo razširil ponudbo izobraževalnih programov za Rome ter tudi druge posameznike, ki delajo z Romi in se ukvarjajo z romsko in drugimi tematikami.
- Dvig ravni zdravstvene pismenosti Romov v sodelujočih državah.
- Spodbujanje pripadnikov romske skupnosti k prevzemanju odgovornosti za lastno zdravje in zdravje družinskih članov.
- Spodbujanje zdravega življenjskega sloga med Romi.
- Vključevanje Romov v aktivnosti in zmanjševanje njihove marginalizacije.
- Povezovanje različnih skupin Romov na ravni EU.
- Vpliv na razvoj socialnih, kulturnih in državljanskih kompetenc Romov.
- Vpliv in razvoj zaupanja v zdravstveni sistem.
- Izmenjava dragocenih izkušenj med partnerji.
- Širitev mreže organizacij, ki delajo z Romi.

2021-1-SK01-KA220-ADU-000028403.title: Learning Fwd 21
2021-1-SK01-KA220-ADU-000028403.summary:
<< Background >>

Motiváciou pre navrhnutie tohto projektu bolo zistenie, že počty dospelých, ktorí sa vzdelávajú na Slovensku aj v Chorvátsku boli veľmi nízke (údaje Eurostatu pre rok 2019). Úroveň povedomia o prínosoch a potenciáli vzdelávania dospelých bola tiež nízka, vrátane miestnych orgánov, ktoré obvykle nevnímajú agendu celoživotného učenia/vzdelávania dospelých ako súčasť svojich vzdelávacích alebo rozvojových politík. To viedlo aj k takmer neexistujúcej spolupráci vzdelávacích subjektov na miestnych alebo regionálnych úrovniach, či už ide o poskytovateľov alebo zúčastnené strany. Predbežné výskumy potvrdili zjavnú potrebu rozvoja kompetencií v celoživotnom učení všeobecne, a aj pre dospelých. Občianske a zelené kompetencie podľa nás sú veľmi dôležité, a nie sú dostatočné možnosti na ich získanie počas celého (dospelého) života. Rýchly vývoj nových vzdelávacích nástrojov a digitálnych prostriedkov ponúka možnosti vyvíjať vzdelávacie moduly iným spôsobom, ktorý zapája učiacich sa.

<< Objectives >>

Hlavným cieľom projektu bolo vytvoriť perspektívne vzdelávacie centrá, FLLC, v dvoch regiónoch projektového partnerstva, v regióne Rijeka (HR) a v regióne Malé Karpaty (SK). Toto by podporilo inkluzívne miestne/regionálne vzdelávacie prostredie, otvorené a prístupné pre rôznorodú komunitu dospelých učiacich sa. Centrá (alebo siete) by spájali typických aj netypických poskytovateľov vzdelávania dospelých, ako sú školy, knižnice, múzeá, kultúrne centrá, jazykové školy, akadémie tretieho veku, neziskové organizácie. Centrá by ponúkali flexibilné a inovatívne vzdelávacie moduly, ľahko prispôsobiteľné na online aj offline verzie. Moduly by boli navrhnuté na budovanie zelených kompetencií a občianskych kompetencií, spoločne projektovými partnermi a miestnymi inštitúciami. Vytvorením siete takýchto inštitúcií do virtuálneho vzdelávacieho centra a vybavením jeho členov novými zručnosťami v tvorbe vzdelávacích modulov by sa vytvorili podmienky na propagáciu a vytváranie nových a inovatívnych kurzov. Projekt pracoval s konceptom kolektívneho dopadu. V tomto prípade je požadovaný dopad na vzdelávacie prostredie, ktorý by sa dosiahol vďaka aktivitám všetkých členov sietí FLLC.

<< Implementation >>

V našom projekte sme realizovali ucelený súbor aktivít zameraných na efektívne riadenie projektu a úspešnu implementáciu. Riadenie projektu bolo založené na podrobnom Pláne riadenia projektu, ktorý poskytoval štruktúrovaný rámec zahŕňajúci pracovné plány, harmonogramy, úlohy a zodpovednosti, vnútorné termíny, systémy podávania správ, postupy finančného riadenia, opatrenia na zabezpečenie kvality a stratégie komunikácie a šírenia informácií. Skutočné aktivity, ktoré sme implementovali, boli nasledovné: - Sieťové aktivity s cieľom budovania FLLC (plánovanie, tvorba databázy, zbieranie údajov, organizovanie stretnutí, uzatvorenie memoranda, stanovenie programu, zviditeľnenie - organizovanie Learning Festivals) - Školiace aktivity pre projektové partnerstvo (stratégia vytvárania sietí, kolektívny vplyv, Human Centered Design and Design Thinking), ako aj pre siete FLLC (vzdelávanie dospelých a miestna politika, kolektívny dopad, dizajn zameraný na človeka a dizajnové myslenie) - Vývoj nových vzdelávacích modulov o občianstve a zelené kompetencie (rozhodovanie o presných témach, obsahu a nástrojoch, testovanie, prispôsobovanie) - Rozvoj digitálnej Platformy (dohoda o štruktúre a obsahu, zhromažďovanie a vytváranie materiálu, nahrávanie)

<< Results >>

Podľa projektovej žiadosti sme úspešne dosiahli nasledovné výsledky a výstupy: 1: Mobilizované a sieťové vzdel. prostredie v dvoch cieľ. regiónoch: Malokarpatský reg. (SK) a Reg. Rijeka (HR) s uplatnením konceptu kolektívneho dopadu. Výstupy: 1.1 Založenie Forward Looking Learning Centers (FLLCs) – ako sieťovo prepojených skupín inštitúcií a organizácií 1.2 FLLC Digital Platform – ako virtuálna reprezentácia siete poskytujúca e-learningovú platformu prístupnú regionálnym/miestnym komunitám. 1.3 Príručka FLLC – zaznamenávanie aktivít projektu a identifikácia získaných poznatkov, ktorá obsahuje usmernenia o osvedčených postupoch na uľahčenie fungovania a udržateľnosti FLLC. – Výsledok 2. Moduly vzdelávania o kľúčových kompetenciách, ktoré ponúkajú a poskytujú regionálne FLLC regionálnym/miestnym komunitám. Výstupy: 2.1 Vzdelávací modul – Ako žiť ekologickejšie, 2.2 Projektové myslenie, 2.3 Ako byť mediálne zdatný, 2.4. Ako byť aktívnym občanom. Tieto moduly sú prístupné na otvorenej, online a digitálnej vzdelávacej platforme, čo zabezpečuje široký prístup a účasť. Náš projekt účinne podporil mobilizované a prepojené vzdelávacie prostredie v cieľových regiónoch, čo umožňuje posilnenie kľúčových kompetencií obyvateľov.

2021-1-SK01-KA220-ADU-000033397.summary:
<< Background >>

In Slovakia, more than 44% of the total population lives in rural areas. However, women are more and more often just the owners of farms or businesses, so it is absolutely appropriate to address the specificity of women
business, especially in rural areas. Even now, the European Union places great emphasis on emphasizing the role and importance of women in rural areas by introducing activities aimed at bringing them together. Women often do not make full use of the existing possibilities of obtaining EU funds due to socio-cultural and psychological barriers. Therefore against it
It is a phenomenon in Slovakia that women can now join in various women's associations. And that's also why we decided to implement the WOBIS project. Due to urgent needs
target groups in partner countries. That is, due to the high marginalization of rural areas and the low level of entrepreneurial skills of women in rural areas, because often women in rural areas are excluded from business. Even if they would like to learn how to implement some new business, there are many
social and knowledge barriers.

<< Objectives >>

The project has a strategic impact on the future of women-led businesses in rural areas by increasing the knowledge of entrepreneurship among members of women's organizations in rural areas. The main goal of the project is to improve the skills and competences of members of rural women's associations by implementing interactive courses corresponding to the educational needs of the project's target group. Maintaining the achieved results and the training platform is also an important part of the project's sustainability strategy. The interactive model will be implemented not only as useful, but also extensible by adding case studies and best practices. The case studies are not only supplementary material, but also an example of the possibility for new beneficiaries to implement the idea in another region of Europe. In line with this strategy for smart rural planning, existing problems of the digital divide can also be overcome. In addition to the group of promoters and directly involved networks, associations, training centers, universities and lifelong learning providers are also interested in the possibility of using online courses.

2022-1-BG01-KA220-ADU-000085168.title: Developing Responsible Global Citizens
2022-1-BG01-KA220-ADU-000085168.summary:
<< Background >>

The DRGC project transforms adult language courses into holistic development pathways by strengthening language competences. To support this, we developed the Curriculum Builder which helps educators design courses by integrating CEFR and DRGC learning outcomes. Built on the DRGC Framework, the app provides structured course outlines. Training materials (the Digital Handbook and an interactive Moodle course) offer essential guidance and assessments.

The CHEDI topics—Community, Health, Environment, Diversity, Innovation—are key to 21st-century society but often overlooked in education. With 1.5 billion people learning English, language courses serve as a global tool for discussing these issues.

As a collaboration among EU-based institutions, the project integrates geographical, cultural, and demographic content while aligning with the EU 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development SDGs. It provides teachers worldwide with access to materials. Learning outcomes span CEFR levels A1 to C2, benefiting learners and educators.

The project fosters civic engagement through CHEDI-based curricula on social values, well-being, diversity, sustainability, and STEM, promoting student-centered, innovative teaching for a changing world.

<< Objectives >>

The project prioritizes civic engagement, sustainability, innovative curricula, and community development through foreign language learning.

Teachers: The objective is to strengthen the teaching and professional capacities of teachers, providing up-to-date topics, methodologies and effective teaching approaches, while increasing IT competencies. To give access to curriculum development frameworks in order to plan courses around current topics and themes directly related to adult learners' needs, to supplement (or replace) their current learning programs and curricula.

Learners: The objective is to increase the language competencies of students in line with the CEFR A1-C2 while developing globally responsible citizens by increasing their 21st-century skills and providing a safe platform to discuss CHEDI topics. This aims for community development with the ability to address common values, civic engagement and participation effectively and open-mindedly.

Learning Centers: The objective is to develop forward-looking learning centers by providing new concepts of language courses, themes and technology to academic and center managers, using IT tools, frameworks and rationale to quickly and simply adapt or implement new curricula.

<< Implementation >>

The project started on 1.10.2022. as planned, with all activities implemented as proposed.

For output development, WP2 (Building the DRGC framework & interactive tools) and WP3 (Online Teacher Training course) were fully completed.
WP2: The DRGC Framework and Syllabus Builder were developed, including QM procedures and piloting. Development covered activities 1-11.
WP3: The Digital Handbook (10 chapters) and the Moodle course were finalized, with QM procedures and piloting. Development covered activities 1-7.

Five TNPMs were held in Bulgaria, Croatia, Spain, and Italy. 

The Dissemination Plan in KA+ was regularly updated, covering all dissemination activities, including conference presentations and 5 Multiplier Events. Three Dissemination Reports were created.

Quality Management included TNPM and project implementation assessments. Quality standards were defined for all outputs, and corresponding quality control procedures were conducted, resulting in three Quality Management Reports.

All partners completed the Impact+ tool, regularly updating the Impact Plan. Impact assessments were conducted for WP2 and WP3, engaging individuals working on the outputs, as well as piloting participants. Three Impact Reports were prepared.

<< Results >>

The concrete results we produced are:
A) A DRGC Framework that aligns Responsible Global Citizens issues to the CEFR
- Follows and integrates the CEFR (levels A1 to C2)
- CHEDI topics and themes include Community, Health, Environment, Diversity and Innovation
- Interdisciplinary concepts and themes develop skills to evaluate, analyze, describe etc. (taxonomy)

B) The Curriculum Builder is based on the DRGC framework, an IT tool that allows teachers and academic managers to design study programs and syllabi, with sets of learning outcomes.
- Can be shared digitally by academic managers, teachers and students
- Adaptable to the individual center or teacher
- Hosted on the DRGC website

C) A Digital Handbook for academic managers and teachers
- 10 formatted chapters
- Instructions on how to design a curriculum using the framework and curriculum builder
- How to set up and manage projects
- Learning processes and methodologies

D) An interactive online teacher training Moodle course for academic managers and teachers
- Video-based training course with 10 modules
- Transcripts for all 10 videos
- 10 interactive Handbook chapters and related subchapters
- 10 end-of-chapter tests
- 10 feedback forms (for every chapter)

2022-1-BG01-KA220-ADU-000089290.title: Modern Tools for Work-Related Stress Management
2022-1-BG01-KA220-ADU-000089290.summary:
<< Background >>

Work-related stress and burnout have been (and still are) a growing concern for employees and employers in the EU. This was especially true during the COVID-19 pandemic (when we applied for the project), which was a driver for significant changes in the working environments of millions of adults.

At proposal stage, our research showed more than half of all working days lost in the EU are because of stress, and more than half of all workers in the EU report that work-related stress is common in their workplace. 

- A need to raise awareness around the the consequences of work-related stress and burnout;
- A need for a coordinated policy solution, to enable both employers and employees prevent stress and burnout on the workplace;
- A need for a resources and tools to help equip EU's workforce to learn how hope to cope with work-related stress and burnout;
- A need for easily accessible digital tools addressing work-related stress in a modern way;

Via our extensive EU-wide research with 516 adult workers, we've simultaneously both re-confirmed this and discovered troubling trends and uncovered reasons of why this was happening. Our project addressed these issues by creating on point digital tools for stress and burnout management.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives were to provide tools for stress prevention and management on both personal and business level, raise awareness about the importance of mental health and thus contribute to the creation of safer and healthier workplaces across the EU. These objectives remained unchanged for the entire duration of the project.

In the first stage of our project, we wanted to execute an EU-wide research to dig out the specific issues concerning work-related stress factors and needs to be addressed, in order to accurately define the training content, and based on that to elaborate a comprehensive policy recommendations report to provide an impetus for a EU-wide action on work-related stress management.

In the second phase of the project, we wanted to develop an innovative training course for work-related stress management and prevention, aiming to transfer specific skills and competences to the end users. We also wanted to create additional tools to support this objective like a tool to help the end users discover if they are under stress and provide them specific resources to manage it. We also wanted to create a mobile application to facilitate easy access to all these these tools and that's exactly what we did.

<< Implementation >>

In WP2 we did:

- A1.1: An EU-wide Research on Work-related Stress Prevention & Management (survey report);
- A1.2: End Users Focus Groups
- A1.3: Elaboration of the Policy Recommendations Report

- A2.1: Integration of the identified training needs
- A2.2: Development of learning objectives
- A2.3: Development of the methodological framework

- A3.1: Elaboration of common working templates
- A3.2: Development of the training course
- A3.3: Development of a guidebook for employers

In WP3 we did:

- A1.1: Definition of a logical approach
- A1.2: Development of an assessment framework
- A1.3: Elaboration of the assessment tool

- A2.1: Definition of contents

2022-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000088932.title: Inclusive First Aid
2022-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000088932.summary:
<< Background >>

Everyone can learn first aid as, by definition, it means simple measures that, while potentially life-saving, can be done by laypersons. This explicitly also includes persons with disabilities - but mainstream courses often are neither accessible nor inclusive.
While we recognize that teaching persons with disabilities in a practical, physical skill can be a didactic challenge that varies by type of disability, we found that different approaches at the consortium organisations already had shown success and that good learning results can be achieved if measures to provide accessibility and inclusion are observed. In INFA, we collected these practices and discussed them with representatives of disabled people's organisations (DPOs), to ensure that they can be recommendable examples of practice. In our final document, we put these examples into the context of why first aid education, as a form of civic engagement and thus being connected to active citizenship, is important for the target group, recognizing the right of persons with disabilities to all aspects of education including training in first aid, and also formulate a recommendation on remaining practical and regulatory challenges.

<< Objectives >>

Inclusive First Aid (INFA) conducted a best practice exchange on first aid training for people with disabilities. Under inclusion of relevant target group stakeholders, we collected, debated and documented practices that led to succesful learning results.
The successful conduction of the best practice exchange was our one central objective.
We had two intermediate goals in focus:
1)	Valuable lessons learned to improve first aid training for persons with disabilities, as trainers could learn from the presentations of and discussion about the practice examples.

2)	Recommendations on the way forward for first aid for persons with disabilities, based on a wide group of experts exchanging on the topic. The final project publication, in addition to documenting the discussed practices, has general chapters addressing this point.


<< Implementation >>

We implemented a series of five best practice exchange workshops. At the first workshop in Italy, not only did the hosting partner present their practices in first aid for persons with disabilities, but we also worked together with Disabled People's Organisations to define principles for first aid for persons with disabilities and directly apply them in a review of the first presented practices.

We then held four more best practice workshops (Denmark, Germany, North Macedonia, Italy) where practices were presented and discussed in light of the previously defined principles. Where possible, these workshops included discussions with additional local DPOs. A process to document the practices and compile our final publication, our best practice brochure, ran intertwined with the meetings, with each draft practice chapter reviewed again at the following meeting. Each meeting had a hybrid segment for feedback from the associated DPO partners on the agenda.

A final workshop discussed the project with clients of our Croatian partner SRCE, who are a service provider for persons with disabilities, and also saw the associated DPO partners participate again for additional feedback, before finalizing the best practice brochure.

<< Results >>

In addition to the lessons learned from the discussions and the exchange for the immediate participants in the project's workshops, the central, concrete project result is a best practice brochure, a collection of practices for first aid training to persons with disabilities. It is embedded into a context of general principles to observe when designing first aid training for persons with disabilities and additional recommendations for further advancing the availability of accessible and inclusive first aid training. The best practice brochure itself a proof-of-concept that can motivate other first aid trainers to also offer accessible and inclusive courses.

2022-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000089906.title: Adult Education addressing today’s Challenges
2022-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000089906.summary:
<< Background >>

ATTACH tackles the very important issue of low civic engagement among adults and seniors, which is especially alarming in countries like Germany, Greece, Cyprus, and Croatia, where participation rates are among the lowest in Europe. Lower education levels, income disparities, and outdated methods of participation impede active citizenship for adults with fewer opportunities. Adult educators are without tools and competencies that would serve to effectively engage learners, especially on contemporary issues such as Human Rights and Climate Change, Data Protection, Immigration, and Euroscepticism. The project answers these needs by promoting active civic engagement through adult education. It focuses on developing the competences of adult educators and introducing innovative, engaging tools such as Photovoice, Educational Animation, Storytelling, and Kahoot! Quizzes. ATTACH also covers the political dimension of the work of adult educators, which is a gap in research. By empowering educators and learners, the project supports social inclusion, lifelong learning, and the EU's goal of fostering active citizenship.

<< Objectives >>

ATTACH promoted active civic engagement through adult education, empowering educators and engaging adult and senior learners, with a particular focus on those with fewer opportunities. The project has reached its objectives by tackling essential challenges and introducing innovative solutions. This it has done through targeted research in mapping the political dimension of the work of adult educators both nationally and at EU levels. The project has developed better capacity in the skills of adult and senior coordinators, volunteers who manage the initiatives regarding active citizenship. The project developed and implemented innovative educational tools, such as Photovoice, Educational Animation, Storytelling, and Kahoot! Quizzes, to engage learners in an active learning process. These methods focused on contemporary issues, like Human Rights, Data Protection, Immigration, and Euroscepticism, making civic participation more accessible and appealing.
The project finally empowered educators to use social media effectively, training learners in the design of effective online campaigns on real community issues.

<< Implementation >>

ATTACH implemented a set of activities to promote active civic engagement through adult education. First, the work of adult educators was analyzed in detail, considering its political dimension both at EU and national levels, as one of the main ways of enhancing civic participation. The project, secondly, developed educational tools to enhance the civic engagement potential of adult and community educators. Such tools included Photovoice, Educational Animation, Storytelling, and Kahoot! Quizzes on such contemporary issues as Human Rights, Data Protection, Immigration, and Euroscepticism. Third, the project deepened adult learners' understanding in how to leverage social networks and social media to advance social change. Educators and learners were trained in the design and implementation of effective online campaigns on priority community issues. Finally, targeted dissemination actions ensured the exploitation of project results. Four social media campaigns and photo exhibitions were organized in each partner country, showcasing the outcomes produced during Photovoice workshops. These activities empowered educators, engaged adult learners, and fostered active participation in civic and democratic life.

<< Results >>

ATTACH had tangible results and impacts on promoting civic engagement and professional development for adult educators. It produced two toolkits and a promotional video as its major outcomes.The first toolkit, developed under WP3, introduced innovative educational tools such as Photovoice, Educational Animation, Storytelling, and Kahoot! Quizzes. These tools enabled adult and community educators to engage adult and senior learners, particularly those with fewer opportunities, in discussions on contemporary issues like Human Rights, Data Protection, Immigration, and Euroscepticism.Under WP4, the second toolkit focused on how to use social networks and social media for creating social change. It provided educators and learners with practical competencies in the design and implementation of effective online campaigns on issues relevant to their communities.ATTACH's Promotional Video was an effective showcase of the objectives of the project, its activities, and its achievements; it served as a dissemination tool to promote its impact across Europe.These results provided educators with practical tools to inspire civic engagement, supporting adults and seniors to become active citizens and volunteers.

2022-1-ES01-KA220-ADU-000088102.title: DRAMA BASED TRAINING PROGRAM FOR INCREASING THE GENDER EQUALITY IN PERSONS WITH INTELLECTUAL DISABILITIES
2022-1-ES01-KA220-ADU-000088102.summary:
<< Background >>

Persons with Intellectual Disabilities (PID) must be trained in understanding the relevance of gender issues, identifying inequalities affecting their own lives and implementing actions and being active towards a behavior change of themselves and the rest of the society stakeholders.
Main needs addressed were;
PID need to improve their knowledge, skills and attitudes towards gender equality to reduce stereotypes and discrimination based on disability-gender issues.
PID need accessible and action learning methodologies (drama based) to motivate their participation and acquisition of competences about gender issues and achieve their full inclusion in society.
PID’s trainers need specific training to deliver accessible and action-oriented training courses about gender issues
PID need to be skilled in digital tools to be more active in the creation and dissemination of their drama work arts, helping society to overcome stereotypes.
On the other hand;
Supports (relatives, etc.) need to be aware of the discrimination that PID suffer when approaching gender issues and tools for support them.
Society needs to be aware of the challenges that gender issues pose on PID and that their action is needed to achieve a gender-inclusive society

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to increase the competences of PID towards gender equality through a Drama Based Training (DBT) approach. General objectives:
GO1; To develop an inclusive and accessible DBT methodology (DBTM) based in action-oriented learning principles for increasing the knowledge, skills and attitudinal change of PID towards gender equality, considering their learning difficulties and the impact of gender issues in this collective.
GO2; To develop a Trainer ́s Guide for enhancing the implementation of the DBTM.
GO3; To develop a set of Training Materials for PID for enhancing their successful involvement in the training process and acquisition of competences.
GO4; To develop a Digital Training Tool adapted to PID for the implementation of the DBTM, including a module where PID will be able to record, edit and upload their videos including the created and performed drama based training plays, thus increasing their social and digital skills.
GO5; To implement pilot training actions for validating the quality of the training program and its capacity for increasing competences, addressing gender equality issues.
GO6; To increase the awareness of related stakeholders and commitment with the exploitation of the project results.

<< Implementation >>
