2023-1-LT01-KA220-ADU-000153426.title: Critical theory in adult education practice: empowerment for critical actions
2023-1-LT01-KA220-ADU-000153426.summary:
<< Background >>

The professional experience of the partner organizations proved that CT education had already become a part of formal school education and higher education studies. But in non-formal adult education, CT presented in a very fragmented way, either as part of media literacy, or as a tool to fight against propaganda. However, neither the concept of CT itself, nor its attributes as a CT competence, have been widely studied or analyzed in terms of how it is manifested in non-formal adult education, how it is applied. A preliminary analysis of the literature on the subject had revealed an apparent lack of not only the development but also the presentation of this competency in adult education of Lithuania. The situation was very similar in the partner countries - Latvia, Croatia and Romania. Therefore, all partners agreed on the need to increase the awareness and application of CT in non-formal education by bringing together science and best practice to suggest a universal model that can be applied and adapted in different adult education contexts while at the same time providing guidance for adult education policy.


<< Objectives >>

The project MIND aimed to fill in the gap and to foster critical thinking approach in non-formal adult education by strengthening professional capacities of adult educators and empowering diverse groups of learners to apply and cultivate CT in various spheres of personal, community, professional and social life. This was done by consolidating scientific knowledge and good practice, through partner organizations active in the fields of adult education, general education and high education.

<< Implementation >>

While implementing this project we wanted to improve the competences of adult educators by fostering CT among adult learners so that they can apply it in their daily professional and community life and make a meaningful contribution to their own well-being. This ambition was reflected in the following project objectives:
1. Provided evidence of CT presence (and non-presence) and importance for adult education.
2. Provided clear guidance on how CT can be developed and practiced.
3. Provided opportunity to practice CT and improve digital skills in adult education organizations and communities.
4. Fostered CT teaching and learning by developing engaging digital teaching-learning.
5. Shared project results and lessons learned among partnership, local communities, respective audience at national and international contexts.

<< Results >>

Project activities provided evidence-based answers to questions: What is critical thinking in non-formal adult education? What is its value for individual, organization, community and society? How it can be specifically developed and applied in different situations and contexts? Answers will be embedded in following outputs: Compendium of scientific literature; Report of analysis of adult education documents/programs; CT Program and Toolkit; Recommendations for adult education policy makers at different level. During the development of the project Digital  Learning Platform was designed by digitalizing the Program and Toolkit. Project had it's Facebook account, result were disseminated on EPALE platform and informative Newsletters as well as on-line and face-to face conferences.

2023-1-LT01-KA220-ADU-000156443.title: Discover & Empower – an innovative model of career guidance to discover your future path
2023-1-LT01-KA220-ADU-000156443.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the DISCOVER & EMPOWER project in response to the growing need for structured, innovative, and accessible career guidance for young adults, particularly those with fewer opportunities and low or outdated skills. In our daily work with adult learners, we observed that many struggle to identify their strengths, understand labour market changes, and make informed career decisions. Rapid digital transformation, post-pandemic instability, and skills mismatch have further increased uncertainty and reduced confidence among young adults.
The project addressed the need for improved career management skills (CMS), stronger links between lifelong guidance and lifelong learning, and better support from adult educators. We recognized a gap in practical, engaging, and ICT-based resources that would empower learners to take ownership of their career paths. At the same time, educators needed modern tools and methodologies to effectively guide and motivate adults.
By developing a digital portal, self-assessment tools, workshops and a teacher’s manual, we aimed to create sustainable, flexible, and inclusive guidance solutions aligned with labour market realities and European priorities in adult education.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to strengthen career management skills (CMS) among young adults and improve the quality and accessibility of lifelong guidance within adult education. Our main objective was to empower participants to identify their strengths, interests, and values, explore career opportunities, and make informed decisions about their professional pathways in a rapidly changing labor market.
We also sought to enhance career adaptability, digital readiness, and self-directed learning competences, enabling young adults to better respond to technological change and evolving employment demands. At the same time, the project aimed to increase the competencies of adult educators by providing them with innovative tools, digital resources, and a structured methodology for delivering career guidance.
Through the development of an online portal, self-assessment tools, interactive learning materials, and a teacher’s manual, we intended to create sustainable, flexible, and transferable resources that strengthen the link between lifelong learning and lifelong guidance across partner countries.

<< Implementation >>

Partners collaboratively developed and tested a comprehensive set of career guidance resources. We created an online portal containing eight learning modules focused on key career management skills, accompanied by self-assessment tools that guide users toward personalized learning pathways.
In addition, we developed interactive learning materials, including webquests and quizzes, designed to support self-directed and engaging learning. A Teacher’s Manual was produced to help adult educators integrate these resources into their daily practice through structured workshops and blended learning approaches.
We organized a short-term joint staff training event to build educators’ capacities and ensure consistent implementation across partner countries. Piloting activities with young adults were carried out locally to test, evaluate, and improve the materials.
To ensure visibility and sustainability, we implemented promotional activities, including podcasts, short videos, posters, and multiplier events aimed at stakeholders from adult education, VET, and employment sectors.

<< Results >>

The main result was the DISCOVER & EMPOWER online portal, containing 8 structured modules on key career management skills and 1 self-assessment tool guiding users toward personalized learning pathways.
Within the Toolbox, we developed 8 webquests and 8 interactive quizzes to support self-directed learning. A comprehensive Teacher’s Manual was produced, including 20 hours of workshop-based activities and structured guidance for educators. 8 one-day workshops were designed and piloted with young adults.
For dissemination, we created 16 podcasts, 24 short videos, and 32 promotional posters. We also organized multiplier events in all partner countries.
All materials and resources were developed in English, and translated into 6 partner languages (Icelandic, Lithuanian, Croatian, Spanish, Italian, and Bulgarian), ensuring accessibility and transferability across different educational contexts.
Beyond tangible outputs, the project strengthened young adults’ career adaptability and enhanced adult educators’ guidance competencies.

2023-1-PL01-KA220-ADU-000154257.title: Democracy Dialogues
2023-1-PL01-KA220-ADU-000154257.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the Democracy Dialogues (DEMOS) project in response to shared challenges identified in our countries: Croatia, Finland, and Poland, such as the growing lack of dialogue, the deepening crisis of democracy, increasing social polarisation, and the declining capacity for constructive communication and conflict resolution. These issues are exacerbated by a widespread lack of both dialogue-related skills and the motivation to engage in conversations across divides. Many community leaders, activists, and influencers, despite their potential to shape public debate, often lack training in dialogue methods and adopt radical attitudes that can undermine the effectiveness of their efforts. This situation was further intensified by the pandemic, which exposed the vulnerability of our democracies to crises, contributed to the spread of misinformation and conspiracy theories, and deepened social divisions in a time of great uncertainty. Additional burdens on democratic systems and social cohesion include climate change, inflation, and the deteriorating economic situation of many individuals. In this context, we saw the DEMOS project as an opportunity to strengthen democracy through dialogue.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the DEMOS project was to promote dialogue as an effective method for strengthening democracy, social cohesion, and active citizenship in the face of growing polarisation, misinformation, and democratic fatigue. We aimed to:
1. Enhance the knowledge and practical skills of facilitators (and all people interested) in using dialogue as a tool for civic engagement and conflict resolution.  
2. Develop and test an educational program - Democracy Dialogues - based on the experiences and methodologies of three dialogue experts from Croatia, Finland, and Poland. The program was designed to be flexible and applicable in various national contexts, while maintaining shared democratic values.  
3. Create user-friendly tools (DEMOS Facilitator’s Guide, DEMOS Cards and DEMOS Package, e.g. scenario and communication materials) to support the delivery of high-quality, inclusive dialogue sessions.  
4. Build and support a community of practice by establishing local and international groups of trained facilitators who can continue to lead and promote dialogue in their communities, both in-person and online.  
5. Deepen understanding of the challenges facing democracy through research done in the countries involved in the project.


<< Implementation >>

1. At the outset, the partners exchanged existing dialogue methodologies, experiences, and approaches to identify common themes and practices.  
2. We conducted research in each country to gain a deeper understanding of local democratic challenges, dialogue needs, and the experiences of facilitators and community leaders. The results of this research directly informed the content and design of the Democracy Frames / Dialogue Cards.  
3. Based on the gathered insights, we collaborated with three experienced dialogue experts to create a comprehensive training program: the program combined theory and practical tools to help facilitators lead inclusive, structured conversations on democratic topics.  
4. Two key resources were developed:  
 - A Facilitator’s Guide for Democracy Dialogues – a framework for planning and conducting dialogue sessions.  
 - Democracy Frames / Dialogue Cards – a flexible and engaging tool to support meaningful discussions.  
5. We organised a training session for 24 facilitators (12 from Poland, 6 from Croatia and 6 from Finland). Participants were equipped with both theoretical knowledge and practical tools. 
6. The facilitators then organised and led sessions within their communities.


<< Results >>

- An educational program co-created with three experts, designed to build/upgrade dialogue skills.  
- The DEMOS Guide – a practical handbook supporting individuals in planning, organising, and moderating dialogue sessions on democratic topics.  
- The DEMOS Cards – a set of 71 topic cards (e.g. Education) based on research from three countries, designed to stimulate structured conversations around core democratic values, challenges, and perspectives. 
- Additional materials supporting facilitators, like a scenario of a session.
- Training for 24 facilitators – individuals from Poland, Finland, and Croatia received training in dialogue methods and were equipped with tools for use in their communities.  
- Local and international dialogue events – led by the trained participants, these events engaged diverse community members in dialogue sessions both in person and online.  
- International cooperation and learning – partner organisations built long-term relationships and exchanged knowledge on dialogue practices and democratic challenges.  
- Increase in the visibility of dialogue as a democratic tool– through distribution, social media, and presentations, we reached broader audiences and promoted the use of dialogue.

2023-1-RO01-KA220-ADU-000153788.title: New Approaches, Practices, and Mentorship for Foster Parents and Professionals
2023-1-RO01-KA220-ADU-000153788.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address critical gaps in training, mentorship, and support for foster parents and professionals in Romania, Türkiye, and Croatia. Across all three countries, existing structures were insufficient to provide continuous, evidence-based, and culturally adapted guidance. In Türkiye, participants highlighted the need for training on trauma-informed care, communication strategies, and emotional support. Romanian foster parents emphasized educational guidance and practical tools to improve day-to-day care. Croatian respondents noted challenges related to the transition to mandatory education and the lack of standardized frameworks for monitoring children’s well-being. Common issues across all countries included insufficient ongoing training and supervision, limited psychosocial competencies, and a need for transnational knowledge exchange. Operational challenges, bureaucratic hurdles, and financial constraints—particularly regarding access to medical and psychological support—were also reported. These needs were identified through surveys (Turkey 33, Romania 150, Croatia 25), in-depth interviews (5 per country), and group discussions. 

<< Objectives >>

By implementing MAP4FosterCare, we aimed to achieve multiple objectives. 
First, to review and assess the current state of foster family support systems in Romania, Türkiye, and Croatia. 

Second, to identify the specific needs and challenges faced by foster parents, children, and professionals, including gaps in training, knowledge, and support. 

Third, to develop and implement improved, evidence-based training programs and support mechanisms for foster parents, equipping them with skills in psychosocial care, coaching, parenting, and Philosophy for Children (P4C), while providing professionals with tools to better support foster families. 

Fourth, to encourage cross-country collaboration and knowledge exchange, strengthen existing training approaches, and establish a mentor network of experienced foster parents to guide newcomers.

Finally, to increase the overall quality, accessibility, and effectiveness of foster care services, ensuring that trained parents and professionals can sustainably apply best practices in their communities, supporting children’s well-being and fostering inclusive, culturally aware approaches to foster care.

<< Implementation >>

The MAP4FosterCare project (Dec 2023–Dec 2025) was implemented through four interlinked WPs. WP1 covered project management and coordination, including monitoring, reporting, and transnational meetings. WP2 conducted research and needs assessment in Romania, Türkiye, and Croatia using surveys, interviews, and group discussions, producing national and transnational reports to inform training design. WP3 developed and piloted a six-module training program, delivered mentorship and supervision sessions, and produced toolkits and workshops to validate content and incorporate participant feedback. WP4 carried out dissemination activities, including social media campaigns, e-newsletters, publications, and presentations at national and international events. Cross-cutting activities ensured quality assurance, communication, multilingual deliverables, and sustainability planning, making project outputs accessible, evidence-based, and relevant for foster parents, social workers, and wider stakeholders.

<< Results >>

WP1 ensured coordinated management, quality monitoring, and effective transnational collaboration, enabling timely and consistent delivery of all outputs. WP2 produced national and transnational research reports identifying foster care challenges and needs, providing a strong evidence base. Five multilingual, culturally adapted training modules were developed, piloted, and validated. WP3 implemented six interactive training modules, the Train-the-Trainer program, supervision sessions, and a Parental Toolbox, enhancing foster parents’ psychosocial, coaching, reflective, and culturally sensitive skills, while mentors and trainers strengthened their capacity to support peers sustainably. WP4 ensured wide dissemination through a communication kit, stakeholder engagement, promotional materials, social media, websites, newsletters, webinars, seminars, national events, and scientific contributions, fostering dialogue, promoting sustainable uptake, and supporting long-term improvements in foster care practice and professional capacity across all partner countries.

2023-1-RO01-KA220-ADU-000155199.title: The integration of parents in the activity of female athletes practicing football and improvement of school-parents-football club relationship
2023-1-RO01-KA220-ADU-000155199.summary:
<< Background >>

This project was developed in response to the limited level of parental awareness, support, and active involvement in girls’ football, which has a direct impact on participation rates and the long-term engagement of female athletes. In Romania and the partner countries, football is still often perceived as a sport mainly for boys, while many parents who allow their daughters to play are not sufficiently informed about the realities, demands, and opportunities of women’s football. This lack of understanding is frequently reflected in inadequate behaviour during trainings and matches and contributes to early dropout, reduced development opportunities, and the slower growth of women’s football. The project aimed to address these challenges by educating parents about women’s football, promoting positive and supportive parental behaviour, strengthening cooperation between schools, parents, and football clubs, and using football as a tool to promote gender equality and social inclusion, particularly for girls from disadvantaged or vulnerable backgrounds.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we wanted to improve parents’ overall understanding of women’s football and their role in supporting girls who practice this sport. We aimed to increase the visibility of the partner clubs and support the growth of their female player base by attracting new girls to women’s football and encouraging their enrolment in organised and professional clubs. Another key objective was to raise parents’ awareness that their daughters can also pursue a football career, with the same value and opportunities as boys. Through targeted activities and events, we also aimed to increase the visibility of women’s football by involving media representatives and promoting positive public narratives. Finally, the project sought to promote women’s football as an effective tool for social inclusion, gender equality, and the integration of girls from disadvantaged or vulnerable backgrounds.

<< Implementation >>

Within the project, we implemented a wide range of educational, sporting, and awareness-raising activities aimed at parents and the wider community. We organised 3 conferences for parents focusing on key topics such as education, nutrition, psychology, and fair play, as well as meetings with parents in schools to raise awareness of women’s football.
To ensure long-term impact and accessibility, we developed an e-learning platform offering educational resources for parents and other stakeholders, and we produced a learning support booklet to consolidate knowledge and support continued learning beyond the project activities.
We organised three international football tournaments, actively involving parents to encourage positive support and engagement. Three school competitions were held to introduce football to new audiences and to strengthen cooperation between schools, families, and football clubs. We also organised three football festivals for girls and parents, creating inclusive environments that promoted participation, enjoyment, and social interaction.
All these activities were implemented in all three partner countries—Romania, Hungary, and Croatia.

<< Results >>

Within the project, several key activities were implemented in all three partner countries. Three international football tournaments for girls and parents were organised to encourage participation and active parental involvement. In addition, three school competitions for girls and parents were held in Romania, Croatia, and Hungary, with the participation of over 200 parents, helping to strengthen cooperation between schools, families, and football clubs.

Football festivals for girls and parents were also organised in all partner countries and proved to be among the most successful activities. More than 350 parents participated across the three countries, as each girl was accompanied by one or both parents, allowing families to better understand the value of sport and the realities of women’s football.

Conferences for parents and players were organised in Romania, Croatia, and Hungary, with over 300 parents attending sessions focused on education, health, and sport-related topics. 

To ensure long-term impact and sustainability, an e-learning platform was created to provide accessible educational resources for parents and other stakeholders, complemented by a learning support booklet designed to consolidate knowledge.

2023-2-TR01-KA220-ADU-000181891.title: Enhancement of Incubators' International Entrepreneurship and Trade Abilities in Digital Platform
2023-2-TR01-KA220-ADU-000181891.summary:
<< Background >>

The ENTRANT Project was designed to address the common needs of early-stage start-ups operating within technoparks, particularly in the fields of digital entrepreneurship and international trade. The needs analysis identified limited access to structured mentoring services, insufficient knowledge exchange and collaboration among technoparks, and a significant need for practical guidance on international trade processes. Furthermore, the lack of comparative data on incubation practices across different countries and the absence of policy recommendations were identified as important gaps.
To address these needs, ENTRANT developed an integrated support model comprising a Digital Learning Platform delivering digital entrepreneurship training, a Digital Mentoring Platform fostering international collaboration and knowledge exchange, and a policy report informed by comparative international research. By combining the expertise of four technoparks and two universities, the project aimed to strengthen entrepreneurship support mechanisms and establish a sustainable, scalable, and internationally transferable model that can be adopted across diverse innovation ecosystems.

<< Objectives >>

With the ENTRANT project, we aimed to create a sustainable and integrated entrepreneurship support model that strengthens the international entrepreneurial capacity of technoparks and incubators. To this end, we developed a high-quality MOOC-based learning program that will enhance entrepreneurs' competencies in international trade, export, digital entrepreneurship, and business development, and which will continue to be used even after the project ends. We supported this learning structure with a Digital Mentoring Platform that combines international mentoring and knowledge sharing, laying the groundwork for lasting international collaborations between entrepreneurs, mentors, and technoparks. We aimed to create an evidence-based policy development model by comparing incubation ecosystems in different countries, strengthen the entrepreneurship support mechanisms of technoparks, and provide policymakers with actionable recommendations. Thus, we aimed not only to produce outputs that benefit only during the project but also to create a sustainable entrepreneurship support model that integrates education, mentoring, research, and policy development, adaptable to different institutions, and usable in the long term.

<< Implementation >>

During the ENTRANT project, capacity-building, research, mentoring, networking, and dissemination activities were implemented to support incubated startups and strengthen technopark ecosystems.
A MOOC-based E-Learning Platform provided training on entrepreneurship, international trade and business development, complemented by face-to-face workshops. In parallel, the ENTRANT Digital Mentoring Platform integrated eight mentoring training modules, digital mentoring and an interactive forum, connecting experienced mentors with startup founders to support internationalisation, export readiness and business growth while enabling knowledge exchange with project partners and peers.
The consortium conducted comparative research, including ecosystem analyses, PEST assessments, entrepreneur interviews, and cross-country evaluations of incubation systems. These activities contributed to the development of a policy report, incubation development recommendations, and academic publications.
To support cooperation and dissemination, the project organised transnational meetings, learning and training activities, Techno Talks webinars, multiplier events, social media campaigns, newsletters, and  communication activities.



<< Results >>

The ENTRANT project delivered high-quality and sustainable outputs. A MOOC-based digital learning platform comprising 10 entrepreneurship training modules was developed and supported by four face-to-face workshops. The ENTRANT Digital Mentoring Platform, built on the Babele infrastructure, integrated an eight-module training programme, individual and group mentoring, event management and an interactive Forum for knowledge exchange among entrepreneurs, mentors and technoparks. Comparative research conducted across the partner countries resulted in an evidence-based Policy Report providing a development model for incubation centres. The aim was to contribute to the academic literature through the prepared international publications.The 13-episode Techno Talks success stories and webinar series promoted international knowledge exchange by bringing together entrepreneurs, mentors and experts to share success stories and good practices. Four TPMs and one LTT activity further strengthened partner cooperation. Project results were widely disseminated through the project website, social media, newsletters, seminars and multiplier events, increasing their visibility, sustainability and long-term use.

2024-1-MK01-KA220-ADU-000246628.title: VibrantLife Endeavor: Empowering Health through Nutrition Advocacy and Medical Literacy
2024-1-MK01-KA220-ADU-000246628.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we identified a strong need to improve digital and health literacy among different communities in North Macedonia. Many citizens, especially young people and patients, had limited access to reliable, clear and bilingual health information in Macedonian and Albanian. This created barriers to informed decision-making, prevention and healthier everyday choices.
The project addressed the need for an accessible e-platform with trustworthy medical content, practical educational materials and resources adapted to the local context. We also recognized the need to raise awareness about the importance of hospital nutrition standards, as nutrition plays an important role in patient recovery, well-being and quality of care.
In addition, the project responded to the need for greater youth involvement in health-related topics. By engaging young people and healthcare professionals, we aimed to encourage community participation, promote healthier habits and make health information more inclusive, understandable and available to everyone.

<< Objectives >>

The objective of the project was to strengthen adult education in the field of digital and health literacy by creating an accessible bilingual e-platform in Macedonian and Albanian. We aimed to provide adults, patients, caregivers, young adults and community members with reliable, practical and easy-to-understand health information.
Through the project, we wanted to improve people’s ability to find, understand and use digital health resources, make informed decisions, and adopt healthier habits. Another objective was to research hospital nutrition practices and use evidence-based findings to advocate for improved nutritional policies in healthcare institutions.
We also aimed to encourage stronger community participation in health advocacy and policy dialogue. By combining adult learning, digital tools and healthcare expertise, the project sought to create a more informed, proactive and empowered community.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, we implemented several activities focused on adult education, digital health literacy and improved hospital nutrition. We developed a user-friendly bilingual e-platform in Macedonian and Albanian, designed as a central hub for reliable health information, practical educational materials and digital resources for adults, patients, caregivers and the wider community.

Hospital menu proposals were developed with CroAN’s nutrition expertise, contextualised through Croatian practice and the wider European context, and adapted to local healthcare needs.”

We conducted empirical research on health literacy among European medical students and a mixed-method consultation with frontline nurses concerning hospital nutrition. The nursing consultation documented professional observations and did not measure patient satisfaction directly.

As part of the educational component, we organized targeted workshops and training sessions for healthcare professionals, including nurses, with a focus on health communication, patient education, digital literacy and the role of nutrition in patient recovery and well-being.

In addition, we implemented a digital campaign for better hospital food, aimed at raising public awareness.

<< Results >>

The project produced concrete outputs in adult education, digital health literacy and hospital nutrition. A bilingual e-platform in Macedonian and Albanian was developed as a central place for reliable health information, educational articles and practical resources for adults, patients, caregivers and the wider community.

Health literacy materials were prepared and published, focusing on prevention, nutrition, healthy habits and patient empowerment. 

A multinational health-literacy study and a mixed-method consultation with frontline nurses on hospital nutrition were completed. The findings informed professional training, hospital-menu proposals and policy recommendations.
Based on the research findings, hospital menu proposals were created in line with relevant European standards and adapted to the local healthcare context. These proposals were prepared for presentation to local decision-makers and institutions.

Workshops for healthcare professionals, including nurses, and a digital campaign for better hospital food were also implemented. Overall, the project improved access to health knowledge and strengthened advocacy for better hospital nutrition policies.

Caring to Include

<< Objectives >>

With our project “Caring to Include” we aim to develop a sustainable NGO-community of practice (CoP) & toolkits to exchange experiences and to learn from each other and from experts, in order to improve trauma-informed support to refugees and migrants, as well as the mental wellbeing of NGO staff and volunteers working with these groups. Ultimately our objective is to improve the wellbeing of refugees and migrants, so that they can be better included and take part in European societies.

<< Implementation >>

During 3 years, we will organize 17 meetings (online&in-person) for partners (12-14 participants) and 1 events for other stakeholders (30 –40 participants) to learn from each other and to create and disseminate 2 toolkits on (1) methods for mental well-being of staff; (2) methods for trauma-informed support to refugees/migrants. Both toolkits will be piloted in the daily work of the 7 partners, through: training of 50-70 staff; and trauma-informed support to 60-70 refugees/migrants.

<< Results >>

We expect an established CoP among EU-NGOs working with refugees/migrants, with 15 NGOs regularly exchanging learnings on trauma-informed support and on staff mental wellbeing. The 7 partners will execute an implementation plan on the theme, which will benefit hundreds of our staff, and thousands of our beneficiaries annually, so that they will be better included in society. The learnings & toolkits will be disseminated through our networks to thousands of NGO-workers and others stakeholders.

2024-1-SK01-KA220-ADU-000249488.summary:

Training programs for women farmers

2025-1-AT01-KA220-ADU-000354002.title: Seniors’ Media Awareness & Resilience in the Digital Age

2025-1-AT01-KA220-ADU-000357396.title: Balance your Life
2025-1-AT01-KA220-ADU-000357396.summary:

The project aims to equip adults with practical tools and strategies to achieve work-life balance and prevent burnout. It seeks to raise awareness about burnout's impact on mental health and productivity, teach effective time management and self-care techniques, and create a supportive learning environment. Through digital and interactive learning, the project fosters well-being, resilience, and sustainable work habits for a healthier, more productive society.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes developing a Work-Life Balance Curriculum covering burnout prevention, time management, and self-care strategies. A Digital Well-being Platform will provide educational materials, interactive tools, and self-assessments. Webinars will bring experts and participants together for discussions on mental well-being. Expected results include a comprehensive curriculum for work-life balance, a digital well-being platform offering accessible resources, and increased awareness of burnout prevention. Participants will gain practical skills, fostering healthier work habits. Educators will be equipped with improved teaching materials. Long-term outcomes include enhanced productivity, mental well-being, and a stronger culture of self-care and resilience in adult education and workplaces.

2025-1-CZ01-KA220-ADU-000357600.title: Express to Protect
2025-1-CZ01-KA220-ADU-000357600.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project empowers seniors by enhancing their communication, boundary-setting, and self-defense skills while also improving digital literacy. Key actions include training new Empowerment Self Defense trainers, developing an Edu-Toolkit, and creating e-learning for offline, online and hybrid models. The project introduces Empowerment Self Defense to learners and organizations, which will use pilot training and outreach events to apply the Edu-Toolkit and e-learning. Key activities include curriculum development, digital tool creation, hands-on workshops, and stakeholder engagement. The project include also a final dissemination activities to promote and sustain project results.

topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2025-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000356853.title: Learning4Resilience - Aufbau lokaler Lernzentren zur Katastrophenschutzbildung
2025-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000356853.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The aim of Learning4Resilience is to enhance adults' skills in coping with crises and disasters, empowering them to support both themselves and others. The project focuses on population groups with limited access to such learning opportunities due to their living conditions. We demonstrate how effective and sustainable disaster preparedness education can be developed within communities – strengthening societal resilience while fostering social cohesion, participation, and civic engagement.

<< Implementation >>

Together with a network of stakeholders, the partnership develops information and learning materials on disaster prevention, designs and tests high-quality, target group-specific learning opportunities for dealing with major disasters – tailored to older people, women, refugees, and people with disabilities. It qualifies stakeholders as resilience trainers and establishes local learning centres as innovative spaces for sustainable disaster preparedness education within communities.

<< Results >>

The result is a sustainable model for target group-oriented disaster prevention education for adults, combining skills development with participation and civic engagement. It includes a knowledge base, tailored learning opportunities for different population groups, community-based learning centres with innovative spaces, training programmes, capacity-building strategies, and policy recommendations for decision-makers and education providers.

2025-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000357157.title: Empowering Coastal Governance Through Ocean Literacy
2025-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000357157.summary:

BlueGOV was designed to support people to make responsible, ocean-conscious decisions in both their professional and daily lives. It raises an important question: Who are these ‘people’ that affect and are affected by the ocean? The answer is everyone, but some more than others - in particular, those with decision-making power. With this in mind, BlueGOV aims to foster a new generation of ocean-conscious leaders and communities ensuring ocean literacy becomes more than a concept but a mindset.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities we will carry out are:
- Research and analysis of OL challenges;
- Develop targeted training program and a practical OL toolbox for coastal authorities, along with capacity-building workshops in pilot regions;
- Foster meaningful dialogue and collaboration among key actors through stakeholder engagement sessions;
- Inspire communities in ocean-conscious behavior through awareness campaign;
- Engage policy-making to promote OL adoption in governance frameworks.

<< Results >>

The core results of BlueGOV will be:
- Map of critical needs providing a structured analysis of where OL efforts need the most improvement in governance;
- A training program with training contents;
- A digital e-learning platform and open-access repository containing practical toolbox with best practices to support lifelong learning;
- Community awareness campaign;

2025-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000357198.title: Training module Inclusive First Aid
2025-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000357198.summary:
<< Objectives >>

TIFA intends to contribute to wider availability of first aid courses for persons with disabilities by addressing a gap in trainer education. Regular first aid trainer education does not currently include how to teach first aid to persons with disabilities and most educational offers that exist are thus based on experience, flexibility, and goodwill of individual trainers. TIFA will develop and test a train-the-trainer module for further and initial trainer education to address this issue.

<< Implementation >>

The project will conduct a structured process of creating a train-the-trainer module on first aid for persons with disabilities based on the current mainstream first aid guidelines. This module will be tested and evaluated in pilot actions before authoring the final version to be released. The project's work is a collaboration of first aid organisations, social service providers and disabled people's organisations, who each contribute their own specific expertise.

<< Results >>

The concrete result of the project will be a train-the-trainer module that can be used for further education of first aid trainers but potentially also in initial education of trainers and thus make a long-term positive contribution to the availability of accessible and inclusive courses wherever it is implemented - within the circle of the consortium and at other first aid educators, who adapt the module, which will be available as an open educational resource, for their training programs.

2025-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000361155.title: DANUBE PEACE: LEARNING ACTION ON PROMOTING PEACE THROUGH DANUBE CULTURAL EXCHANGE
2025-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000361155.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The Danube region holds unique potential as a hub for inclusive peacebuilding. The region can counter polarisation and become a model for resilience.

The Danube Peace project strengthens adult educators through intergenerational and inclusive peace education rooted in Danube and EU values. It promotes peacebuilding, social cohesion, and post-war recovery while supporting diverse adults and educators by addressing their needs for inclusive education and psychosocial support in togetherness.

<< Implementation >>

- Develop innovative, inclusive, and intergenerational peace education materials tailored to adult learners.
- Equip adult and community educators with a learning pathway for peace through Danube culture and heritage.
- Enhance cooperation among partner organisations in the Danube region.
- Promote EU values, including inclusion, democratic participation, and social cohesion.
- Support adults, including displaced persons impacted by war through targeted training and learning resources.

<< Results >>

- A comprehensive mapping of peace education practices in the region (WP2).
- Ten animated explainer videos on peace education topics, tailored for diverse audiences (WP3).
- Open Educational Resources (OERs) co-created with partners and piloted in real-life learning contexts (WP4).
- A sustainable peacebuilding network that unites stakeholders across the region (WP5) including 150 persons.
- Training mobility in Berlin for 30 participants to strengthen skills and share best practices.

2025-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000364303.title: HomeBoundHorizons: "Empowering homeless individuals to overcome adversity and build brighter futures through comprehensive training and community support."
2025-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000364303.summary:

2025-1-DK01-KA220-ADU-000362386.title: The BEAM - Building Engagement and Access for Many
2025-1-DK01-KA220-ADU-000362386.summary:
<< Objectives >>

BEAM expands the Building Bridges Model to enhance social inclusion, remove participation barriers, build stronger, engaged communities; raises awareness of inclusive communities; empowers individuals (community guides), volunteer centres and CSOs, equipping them with competences to provide tailored support for lonely and at-risk individuals; fosters cross-sector collaboration, advocates for policy recognition of bridge-building as a key strategy for social cohesion at local, national, EU level.

<< Implementation >>

BEAM integrates research (surveys, focus groups, interviews, analysis), training and mentoring sessions, peer exchanges, dissemination events, webinars, storytelling, exhibitions and roundtable discussions. It directly engages min. 400 individuals (volunteer centre representatives, CSOs, policymakers, community guides) to showcase the impact and advocate for the BBModel, enhancing social inclusion, removing participation barriers and fostering stronger, more engaged communities.

<< Results >>

BEAM will produce a Mapping Report on bridge-building practices, the Blueprint to Bridge-Building Guide and the BBModel Training Curriculum for volunteer centres and community leaders. It will develop the Community Guides Training Programme and Charter, a Multimedia Storytelling Platform and policy recommendations. The project will culminate in the Voices of Inclusion Exhibition and an EU Policy Roundtable to promote policy integration.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2025-1-ES01-KA220-ADU-000362856.title: Resilient Citizens: Empowering Communities for Climate Emergency Preparedness
2025-1-ES01-KA220-ADU-000362856.summary:
<< Objectives >>

RESILIENT CITIZENS aims to empower citizens by enhancing their preparedness and resilience to climate-related emergencies through accessible, practical, and regionally adapted training. By developing tailored training content and piloting activities in learning spaces, the project creates an impactful and innovative methodology tested and evaluated in three key pillars: prevention and sustainability; reaction and resilience; and reliable communication.

<< Implementation >>

The RESILIENT CITIZENS project will implement online training content and local experiential learning spaces for training citizens. Key activities are Analysis of specific climate risks in Mediterranean areas and Review of best practices and existing programs in prevention, response, and communication (WP2), Development and testing of training modules integrating local adaptations (WP3), Design and testing of experiential learning spaces (WP3 + WP4) and dissemination events (WP5).

<< Results >>

R2.1 Competence Framework + Learning Methodology.
R3.1 Training modules with local adaptations.
R3.2 Guide for facilitators with resources for leading experiential learning spaces.
R3.3 Transnational training and validation of facilitators.
R4.1 Pilot results report and impact analysis.
R4.2 3 experiential learning spaces ongoing.
R5.1  Dissemination and communication plan.
R5.2 Dissemination events in each country.
R5.3 Accessible digital repository.
R5.4 Sustainability strategy.

2025-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000351314.summary:

HERizon aims to empower women by providing tools and resources to prevent violence and promote self-advocacy. The project will create digital platforms, training modules, and storytelling tools to build resilience and foster solidarity. Through workshops, mentorship programs, and public campaigns, HERizon will raise awareness about women’s rights, encourage creative expression, and support long-term change in communities.

2025-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000360989.title: Accompagner le retour à la terre au service de la renaissance et des transitions territoriales
2025-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000360989.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to increase the skills of territorial actors (associations, elected officials, attractiveness agencies, agricultural actors) in order to welcome and support project holders returning to the land whether they are new farmers, entrepreneurs or families. It aims to create common and specific training modules for Greece, Italy, France, Cyprus and Croatia. It also aims to launch a community of European actors mobilized around the "return to the land" at the level of the union.

<< Implementation >>

We will organize 5 learning expeditions in Greece, Cyprus, Italy, Croatia and France to discover inspiring projects, exchange with local actors and identify the issues, opportunities and levers that are common and specific to each country. We will develop a training methodology and specific modules that will be tested in the 5 countries. We will publish a book incorporating projects from other countries, and we will launch the community of European actors of return to land.

<< Results >>

We aim to produce hospitality methodologies in order to support of project holders,with a European base but applicable in different countries. Through the project, we will mobilize core groups of actors involved in supporting the "return to land" in the countries covered by the project. We will launch a community of European players at the level of the 27 to promote and support the "return to land", as a European response to address the challenges of transitions.

2025-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000362621.title: CLIM·IN
2025-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000362621.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to enhance the preparedness of small local authorities (SLAs) for climate-related risks, with a strong focus on vulnerable populations. It will enable SLAs to assess their climate preparedness, equip them with awareness and training tools, and empower outreach experts to support at-risk citizens. Additionally, it seeks to create an international Community of Practice (CoP) to sustain collaboration and knowledge exchange, promoting inclusive climate resilience strategies.

<< Implementation >>

The project will develop a Status Review Tool to help SLAs assess their preparedness and community engagement plans. Workshops will train officials on integrating climate risk communication. Ready-to-use learning tools will be co-designed and piloted in local events and in learning spaces. Outreach experts will be equipped and trained to engage vulnerable groups. The results will be shared through an online platform, promotional events, and a final Road Map to guide further replication

<< Results >>

The project will produce improved outreach and planning skills for SLA officials, increased resilience among vulnerable citizens, and stronger partnerships between local authorities and community organizations. It will also lead to the development of learning tools, including accessible ones, a Community of Practice with a forum to help SLAs across Europe implement inclusive climate preparedness. The project will facilitate policy improvements and create a sustainable knowledge-sharing network.

2025-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000351486.title: Head-Heart-Hands - 3H for Climate Agents of Change
2025-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000351486.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Main aim of this project is to create as many AGENTS OF CHANGE as possible accros the EU, i.e. people that are informed, engaged and deeply emotionaly connected to the issue of climate changes. For that purpose we will offer an innovative learner-oriented program; build capacities and expertise of adult educators; promote intergeneration and inclusivity; ensure the sustainability of project's results and encourage international collaboration.

<< Implementation >>

Numerous activities will be implemented, including survey on climate communication, communication report, 4 short-term staff trainings, development of training programme and handbook, 4 test trainings of adult educators, 4 pilot workshops for adult learners, collection of 40 climate stories, development of Digital Climate Stories Map platform, 4 national multiplier events-Storytelling festivals, 4 round tables, 1 exhibition, 8 podcasts, Final conference, 4 transnational Partners meetings

2025-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000358109.title: MOMental - Cross-Border Collaboration for Maternal Mental Health in Crisis Settings
2025-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000358109.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project will improve maternal mental health support in crisis settings by equipping caregivers and mothers with new knowledge and practical tools. It will train peer-to-peer educators, healthcare professionals, and NGOs to provide better care while empowering women with accessible, evidence-based resources. Through international collaboration, the project will develop sustainable solutions that help women navigate pregnancy and early motherhood in difficult circumstances.

<< Implementation >>

The project will create a structured learning guide, a comprehensive training program for caregivers, and an interactive Learning Hub for mothers and professionals. The Learning Hub will feature multilingual webinars, e-learning courses, and self-assessment tools, making mental health support accessible anytime, anywhere. These activities will provide practical, research-based guidance, ensuring that both caregivers and mothers can confidently address mental health challenges in crisis settings.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver evidence-based guidelines, a structured training program, and a digital Learning Hub with accessible learning resources. By uniting partners from Croatia, Czechia, Cyprus, and Ukraine, along with UNICEF Croatia as an associated partner, the project aims to create a long-term impact. Women in crisis situations will gain access to sustainable, high-quality mental health support, fostering resilience and well-being across Europe.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2025-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000363333.title: Edukacijom do društvene uključenosti Roma
2025-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000363333.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We aim to enable Roma people to participate in educational programs, providing them with opportunities to acquire key skills necessary for active participation in society and the modern labor market (digital and soft skills, micro-credentials). By empowering Roma and raising awareness of the importance of education, we strive to foster social cohesion. The project also focuses on promoting lifelong learning and strengthening the capacities of adult education institutions.

<< Implementation >>

Main Activities:
WP1: Coordination, budget management, communication
WP2: Research implementation (best practices, attitudes, barriers, and educational needs) and informational workshops
WP3: Development of non-formal educational programs for strengthening digital and soft skills
WP4: Implementation of non-formal educational programs and inclusion of the target group in accredited education programs; program evaluation
WP5: Media campaign, dissemination, digital handbook, final conference

<< Results >>

1. Research conducted on the educational needs of Roma and approaches to their inclusion in lifelong learning
2. Non-formal educational programs for strengthening soft and digital skills have been developed
3. At least 60 individuals have attended the developed non-formal programs
4. At least 15 individuals have completed an accredited education (micro-credentials)
5. A digital handbook has been developed (research results, developed educational programs, and project participants' experiences

2025-1-IT02-KA220-ADU-000360255.title: Theatre x Power x Community
2025-1-IT02-KA220-ADU-000360255.summary:
<< Objectives >>

In this critical moment for democracy in the EU, we aim to create spaces for reflection on the theme of Power. We will strengthen community-based education hubs to foster inclusive, engaging environments for adult learners, empower communities through participatory methods, and pilot innovative learning approaches. Through book clubs and discussion groups, we will encourage deeper engagement with social issues and power dynamics, promoting critical thinking and collective action.

<< Implementation >>

To ensure shared understanding of power analysis, the project includes two in-person training sessions (in Croatia and in Italy) and 20 online book club meetings (The Power Book Club). The in-person sessions will focus on practical learning and relationship building, while the online meetings will enable ongoing reflection and quick communication of ideas and questions.

<< Results >>

The main result will be a digital manual featuring theoretical insights on power analysis in education and organizing, practical methodologies, and a framework integrating Freirean perspectives, deep community organizing, and Legislative Theatre. Developed through pilot programs and training sessions, it will include multimedia case studies (videos, photos, reports). The project will also create tailored teaching materials for adult education, inspired by the online book-club.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2025-1-LV01-KA220-ADU-000363211.title: UnlockEquality: Level up your workplace
2025-1-LV01-KA220-ADU-000363211.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to increase awareness of gender equality among employees, managers, and educators. It will improve companies’ and teachers’ ability to identify and address gender inequality through practical tools and guidelines. The project will promote inclusivity and diversity in workplaces and educational settings, fostering environments where gender equality is a core value. It will also provide adult educators with resources to teach how to recognize and address gender inequality.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement various activities, including developing a repository with tools, games, and resources on gender equality. We will create checklists, workshops, and guidelines tailored to businesses, employees, and educators. Interactive serious games and pilot testing will engage participants, allowing for feedback and refinement. These activities will be tailored to address the specific needs of SMEs, adult learners, and companies to foster gender equality.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver concrete results through innovative tools like interactive serious games, engaging workshops, and practical guides. These resources will provide accessible and impactful ways for participants to learn about and reflect on gender equality, fostering a deeper understanding and encouraging actionable change across target groups.
topics: Human rights and rule of law

2025-1-NL01-KA220-ADU-000351570.title: Empowering Voices for Inclusion – Advocating meaningful participation and leadership to inspire full inclusivity
2025-1-NL01-KA220-ADU-000351570.summary:
<< Objectives >>

VOICES_EU empowers people with disabilities to set up impactful awareness-raising campaigns and successfully advocate for their interests to other stakeholders. People with disabilities self-reported are more often women or older people, more frequently have lower incomes and educational levels, and have had, therefore, fewer opportunities in life to build self-respect and to learn to express their interests effectively. VOICES_EU want to provide inclusive and accessible learning materials.

<< Implementation >>

With people with disabilities, VOICES_EU will collect good practices of awareness-raising and advocacy and build a fully inclusive and accessible learning toolkit. Interactive guidance and training materials will be co-designed and validated by people with disabilities, ensuring that the learning materials are entirely equipped for them. Additionally, we will engage persons with disabilities and stakeholders in education, sports, and employment as ambassadors of VOICES_EU.

<< Results >>

VOICES_EU will deliver an online and printable fully inclusive and accessible toolkit with awareness-raising and advocacy tools that people with disabilities can use to set up effective campaigns to have their voices heard in Europe. With VOICES_EU, we aim to take at least one step further towards a society where people with disabilities can fully participate and are respected.
topics: Human rights and rule of law

2025-1-NL01-KA220-ADU-000354350.title: Empowering adults with Acquired Brain Injury for participation and autonomy by knowledge, AI, training and personalised tools
2025-1-NL01-KA220-ADU-000354350.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Each year, over 3.3 million Europeans experience an Acquired Brain Injury (ABI), fundamentally altering their lives. These people often face persistent challenges in communication, daily interactions, and participating fully in society. ABI_SPARK addresses these barriers by adopting a participatory approach, involving people with ABI and their network to achieve sustainable, inclusive and accessible learning facilities to support the social participation and autonomy of people with ABI.

<< Implementation >>

ABI_SPARK will implement the following activities with people with ABI:
- Co-design learning needs and gaps and collect good practices of supportive AI technology and communication tools.
- Co-create learning materials and knowledge hub.
- Test and validate the learning materials and knowledge hub.
- Effective outreach and visibility to the target groups and broader audience.
- Sustain the future of the learning materials through a European community of ambassadors.

<< Results >>

ABI_SPARK will result in:
- Collection of inclusive and accessible tools for people with ABI to support their participation and autonomy.
- Inclusive and accessible for all abilities and generations, training and learning materials addressing the needs.
- Fully accessible co-created knowledge hub.
- Sustainable future of the materials supported by a community of ambassadors of the target group and the project partners.

2025-1-NL01-KA220-ADU-000358283.title: Opportunities for People through Equity and Networking
2025-1-NL01-KA220-ADU-000358283.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The OPEN project aims to promote equity, equality, diversity, and inclusion (EEDI) in European libraries by developing inclusive collections, enhancing cultural awareness and strengthening community engagement. By fostering collaboration among national libraries, it creates sustainable strategies to ensure marginalized communities have better access to library resources. OPEN will also train library managers, improve metadata inclusivity, and establish long-term EEDI practices in the sector.

<< Implementation >>

OPEN will implement activities across five key areas: project management, inclusive collections, cultural awareness, training, and dissemination. It will organize focus groups with marginalized communities, develop a digital platform for cultural exchange, and run training seminars for library managers. Additionally, it will create an inclusive metadata framework, launch media campaigns, and engage associated partners to ensure long-term adoption of diversity strategies.

<< Results >>

OPEN will deliver several key results to transform library services. It will develop 
- Inclusive Metadata Framework to improve cataloging practices 
- Sustainability Toolkit to ensure long-term impact 
- Digital Platform for Cultural Dialogue will facilitate knowledge exchange, while training programs will equip library managers with inclusive leadership skills 
- Best practice guidelines, community engagement initiatives, implement public awareness campaigns to foster diversity and inclusion.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

hr.name: NACIONALNA I SVEUCILISNA KNJIZNICA U ZAGREBU

2025-1-NO01-KA220-ADU-000351372.title: Dementia Awareness Education
2025-1-NO01-KA220-ADU-000351372.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our general objectives are raising awareness and strengthening strategic cooperation in the field of dementia through continuous learning and innovative activities among organizations in Europe and beyond. Specific objectives achieved by implementing this project will include inclusion and diversity, digital transformation, and capacity building.

<< Implementation >>

Few activities will be conducted:Conducting research on dementia awareness activities (including interviews and literature review); Developing a freely available data base in a data repository with many potential awareness activities and initiatives as well as resources attached to them; Organizing onsite and online training; Disseminating results by publishing scientific articles, webinars, and media events. Cooperation and communication with all Partners is central to project implementation.

<< Results >>

We will strengthen cooperation among EU countries in dementia, avoid stigmatization of dementia persons, and foster understanding and inclusion of affected families. We will improve caregivers’ and volunteers’ skills, who will be the motivators. Project’s accessible database of awareness-raising activities will improve knowledge about existing awareness raising activities; online learning program will increase digital skills of elderly people, caregivers and persons living with Dementia.

2025-1-PT01-KA220-ADU-000361371.title: Adapt & Solve: Practical Skills for Life and Work
2025-1-PT01-KA220-ADU-000361371.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Adapt & Solve aims to equip low-skilled adults with adaptive problem-solving skills for daily life, work, and digital environments. It trains educators in innovative teaching methods, develops interactive Playlists and Digital Badges, and ensures long-term sustainability through the Cities of Learning platform. The project promotes inclusion, digital transformation, and flexible learning, enhancing Europe's employability, independence, and lifelong learning opportunities.

<< Implementation >>

Adapt & Solve will develop the Think, Act, Solve Handbook, an Educator Toolkit, and interactive Playlists with Digital Badges. Activities include educator training (LTTA), hands-on adult learner sessions, and digital adaptation on the Cities of Learning platform. Dissemination efforts include social media, publications, and multiplier events, ensuring wide adoption. A sustainability plan secures long-term impact beyond the project’s duration.

<< Results >>

Adapt & Solve project foresees the following results and outcomes:
-Think, Act, Solve Handbook- Practical guide for problem-solving skills
-Educator Toolkit- Structured resources for teaching problem-solving
-4 Interactive Playlists- Hosted on COL
-16 Digital Badges- Recognising learners' achievements
-8 Video Interviews- Showcasing adult learners’ experiences
-80 Adult Learners- Involved in Pilot Testing
-80+ Publications &1500+ Social Media Followers– Ensuring visibility and long-term impact.

hr.name: Udruga za kreativno-održivi razvoj i konkuretnost

2025-1-SI01-KA220-ADU-000355690.title: NextGen Parenting: Improving Adult Learning and Parenting via the setting up of multi-level e-Academies for the promotion of critical thinking and media literacy to combat gender stereotypes and any form of violence in the digital age
2025-1-SI01-KA220-ADU-000355690.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The NextGen Parenting project’s main aim is to set up the e-PARENTING ACADEMIES in the form of LEARNING HUBS that will upgrade Adult Leaning and offer comprehensive and organised opportunities to empower parents/family members of young children and teenagers and adult educators to become AMBASSADORS against gender-based violence and cyber violence, fostering a community of proactive families committed to promoting gender equality and digital safety.

<< Implementation >>

WP2: CO-DESIGNING THE NextGen E-PARENTING ACADEMIES PROGRAMME
WP3: VALIDATED UPSKILLING PATHWAYS COURSE & ‘POSITIVE PARENTING TOOKLIT’
WP4: SETTING UP THE NextGen E-PARENTING ACADEMY PORTAL AND THE TRANSNATIONAL &NATIONAL BLENDED UPSKILLING
WP5: NextGen Parenting DISSEMINATION, EXPLOITATION & SUSTAINABILITY

<< Results >>

WP2-Consultation meetings, video infographics, podcasts, transnational peer review, Mapping tool, e-parenting methodology for AdED
WP3-Upskilling Pathways Course, E-glossary Resource Hub, Case Study Activity Pack

2026-1-BG01-KA220-ADU-000464726.title: AI Compass - Inclusive AI Skills for Work & Life
2026-1-BG01-KA220-ADU-000464726.summary:
<< Objectives >>

To increase digital readiness and practical AI literacy among adults (18+) with basic skills and fewer opportunities through two accessible learning pathways. To develop a shared AI competence framework, a modular curriculum and open educational resources, and to strengthen trainers’ and adult education organisations’ capacity to integrate safe, ethical and inclusive AI use into institutional practice, training provision and strategic development.

<< Implementation >>

We will conduct a needs analysis and co-design process (surveys, focus groups), develop a curriculum and six modular packages: Starter “Digital Bridge + AI Basics” and Standard “AI for Work & Life”, including safe-use tools. We will create a Trainer Toolkit and deliver a Training of Trainers (20 participants). Piloting will take place in BG/RS/HR, including pre/post assessments and practical tasks. We will analyse data, refine and publish the resources, and organise three multiplier events.

<< Results >>

Expected results include: an AI competence framework and assessment rubrics; six openly licensed, localised and editable resources; a Trainer Toolkit and ToT package; 20 trained trainers; six pilot groups with approx. 90 learners plus one institutional group; an evaluation and refinement report; a short policy briefing (5–6 pages), and a sustainability and mainstreaming plan.

hr.name: KOMPAKT, obrt za savjetovanje i usluge, vl. Krunoslav Đurec, Križevci, Karane 35

2026-1-CY01-KA220-ADU-000457738.title: ExhiBIT_Next. The Museum of the People: Embedding Co-Curated Adult Learning in European Museum Governance
2026-1-CY01-KA220-ADU-000457738.summary:
<< Objectives >>

ExhiBIT_Next aims to institutionalise the Museum of the People as a governance model embedding adult co-curation within museum structures. It seeks to equip professionals with validated competences, enable adults 55+ to generate documented heritage contributions, and integrate micro-credentials into museum practice. The project advances participatory governance, digital inclusion and sustainable adult learning across European heritage institutions.

<< Implementation >>

The project will develop a competence framework and micro-credential model for museum educators, create and test a Virtual Learning Lab and digital simulations, implement community documentation labs with adults 55+, deliver co-curation workshops and exhibitions, and conduct structured dissemination, policy dialogue and replication actions to ensure European uptake and long-term sustainability.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver a validated Museum of the People framework, an operational App for citizen documentation, an Adult Competence Model with EU-aligned micro-credentials, Virtual Learning Labs for educators and adults, co-curated exhibitions, and a replication toolkit. Outcomes include strengthened adult participation (55+), institutional embedding of participatory governance, and sustained digital and policy impact across European museums.

hr.name: Muzej za umjetnost i obrt (Museum of Arts and Crafts)

2026-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000450589.title: Full STEM Ahead: Building scientific literacy of adults through Place-Based Education
2026-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000450589.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The Full STEM Ahead project aims to enhance scientific literacy among adult learners by equipping educators with innovative place-based education (PBE) strategies. It seeks to break down barriers to STEM engagement, making science more accessible, engaging and relevant to daily life. Through a comprehensive CPD programme, a PBE Toolkit, and Science Learning Festivals the project will foster critical thinking, problem-solving and lifelong scientific literacy for diverse groups of adult learners.

<< Implementation >>

The project will develop a 30-hour CPD programme for educators supporting them to integrate PBE and scientific literacy into adult learning. 72 educators will be trained and supported. A PBE Toolkit will be created comprising 24 resources presented as digital escape rooms, citizen science projects, PBL challenges and science roundtables. Science Learning Festivals will be organised across partner countries providing accessible new learning experiences for 300+ adult learners.

<< Results >>

1. Full STEM Ahead 30-hour CPD Training for Adult Educators - opportunities for transnational mobilities and exchange
2. PBE Toolkit with 24 innovative science-based resources
3. Festival Organisers Handbook and the programming and delivery of 6 Science Learning Festivals for 300+ adult learners
4. All project results will be available as OERs accessible through the project's online platform
5. Comprehensive dissemination strategy to guarantee local, regional and EU impact of the project results
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2026-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000459710.title: Green Corner – immersive learning space for adults
2026-1-DE02-KA220-ADU-000459710.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Green Corner introduces environmental learning as a transformative, welcoming methodology for every adult regardless of background, mobility, or prior experience. We aim to create immersive learning which genuinely offers relief: a moment of nature, beauty, and quiet agency inside the buildings people already inhabit. Through three culturally distinct installations, "Green Corners", and a free multilingual platform, we build a replicable model for inclusive, embodied ecological education.

<< Implementation >>

We co-build three indoor nature-based learning installations with vulnerable adult communities in Berlin, Piła, and Lipik; conduct a 10-month longitudinal observation study; train 12 Green Corner Ambassadors at an International Laboratory; develop a WCAG-compliant five-section Learning Platform in four languages; and disseminate the methodology through 18 institutional roadshows, a coordinated media campaign, and a final international online MeetUp.

<< Results >>

Three self-standing public Green Corner installations with 27 validated educational activities aligned with GreenComp. A free multilingual Learning Platform with an interactive Design Matrix, Green Corner Notebook, and optional certificates. Twelve trained Ambassadors will carry the methodology into new institutions. Over 250 adult learners reached directly, 300 institutions by email, and 6,000 indirectly, with 130 Expression of Interest forms evidencing real replication potential across Europe

2026-1-ES01-KA220-ADU-000460363.title: Improving rehabilitation and independent living skills of adults with intellectual disabilities using virtual reality and artificial intelligence
2026-1-ES01-KA220-ADU-000460363.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project is the implementation of virtual reality (VR) scenarios to apply rehabilitation and autonomy therapies
for the independent living of people with Intellectual Disabilities (ID) using the possibilities of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to
personalise and improve the performance of learning in the use of the scenarios designed and developed based on the
needs of the therapists. Immersive environments will be safe and controlled.

<< Implementation >>

The experts have defined 9 scenarios to be developed in VR with AI, 5 for rehabilitation therapies (cognitive, physical
rehabilitation, speech and language, interpersonal in social skills, emotional) and 4 for independent living (autonomy at
home, social relations, citizenship, at work).
Two training courses are planned, the first to learn the technologies and develop the scenarios and the second for therapists
to apply them in local pilots.

<< Results >>

The project will include a VR user manual with specifications for applying the 9 scenarios developed according to the DI
scaling. Appropriate configurations and indications for customisation. The AI are also evaluated and explained for
adaptation and use for people with ID. Ethical and safety considerations will be specified. Good usage practices will be
defined in the planned pilots and usage tutorials will be developed in English and in the consortium languages.
