2026-1-ES01-KA220-ADU-000464307.title: Story Maps: Creative Storytelling for Community Resilience
2026-1-ES01-KA220-ADU-000464307.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We aim to strengthen adult learning and civic participation through arts-based educational practices. Our objectives are:
- To enhance the capacity of artists and cultural operators to deliver non-formal adult education in cultural spaces;
- To improve the social and civic competences of adult learners, particularly those facing disadvantage;
- To establish a sustainable, transnational model for socially engaged arts that can be replicated, fostering a lasting ecosystem for cultural democracy.

<< Implementation >>

Activities include co-designing a 5-module Learning Programme and testing it with 70+ artists and cultural operators. 
We will develop the Story Maps Web App and Digital Hub to support a new Community of Practice. 
We will train 10 lead facilitators at a European Bootcamp, who will then run 4 national Community Laboratories with 100+ adult learners. 
These labs will use participatory arts to explore the local impacts of the climate crisis, generating co-created community stories for the Web App.

<< Results >>

Expected results include: 
1) The Story Maps Learning Programme, an Open Educational Resource to professionalise artists as educators;
2) Story Maps Web App, a living archive showcasing at least 20 co-created community stories;
3) A Best Practice and Policy Recommendations Guide to support replication. 
We will establish a Community of Practice of 70+ practitioners and expect at least 100 adult learners to demonstrate increased civic agency and critical thinking through their participation.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

hr.name: UDRUGA ZA PROMICANJE KVALITETE URBANOG ZIVOTA "URBANI SEPARE"

2026-1-FI01-KA220-ADU-000465129.title: Putting the You into EU
2026-1-FI01-KA220-ADU-000465129.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We want to achieve four general objectives: 
(1) increasing adult learners’ knowledge of the EU, its common values, and opportunities for participation and active citizenship; 
(2) increasing the sense of European identity and identification with common EU values among adult learners; 
(3) increasing adult educators' competences and providing them with accessible resources for teaching EU topics; and 
(4) empowering adult learners to inform others about the EU and give peer-to-peer training.

<< Implementation >>

In addition to project management, we will implement four work packages:
WP2: researching adult learners' and educators' attitudes towards the EU and their needs for a training programme. 
WP3: developing teacher resources for EU topics and learner material for giving peer-to-peer training. 
WP4: creating digital self-learning and self-assessment tools for learners on EU issues, and organising international mobilities for piloting peer-to-peer training.
WP5: regular dissemination activities.

<< Results >>

Concrete results:
PR1: a research report on learners' and educators' views and attitudes towards the EU. 
PR2: teacher resources for teaching EU topics and basic pedagogical skills to learners. 
PR3: learner material for peer-to-peer training
PR4: digital self-learning tool
PR5: recommendation for micro-credential

Further:
-	increased competences, knowledge of the EU, and sense of European identity among target groups
-	local outreach through piloting PR2 and PR3
-	international mobilities

2026-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000468740.title: Human Rights Guide - Building a Future of Equal Human Rights Education Across Europe
2026-1-FR01-KA220-ADU-000468740.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to provide user-friendly and inclusive human rights education to European citizens on equal basis and to raise and consolidate the understanding of human rights as a common European value by implementing the Human Rights Guide - an online free access human rights education platform in ten EU countries. The project will also strengthen the capacity of partner organizations to establish themselves as recognised human rights education providers within their national contexts.

<< Implementation >>

The project will transfer the Human Rights Guide to Malta and Hungary, and it will expand and maintain the content in eight existing partner countries – Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia, Bulgaria, Slovakia, Slovenia, Croatia and France. The project will provide large-scale online human rights training to select professional groups at the EU and national levels. At the end, a conference in France and multiplier events in the new partner countries will be organized to promote the Guide.

<< Results >>

As a result of the project, large number of European citizens will have free and equal access to qualitative human rights education online. Understanding human rights, citizens will gain awareness of their core civic entitlements, gain courage to participate in democratic processes and identify human rights as a European value. Large number of professionals will have an increased knowledge and competences to apply human rights in their daily work.
topics: Human rights and rule of law

2026-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000451434.title: Strengthening Inclusive Lifelong Learning, Valid Engagement and Readiness for Age-Friendly Universities
2026-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000451434.summary:
<< Objectives >>

SILVER-UNI pursues to develop  strategic framework for sustainable third-age education applicable at European universities. During the project a three-strand intergenerational curriculum positioning older adults as knowledge creators will be developed. A comprehensive pre-retirement preparation curriculum for the 60–65 age cohort will be created and piloted for the purpose retirement readiness. Finally, andragogical research unit will be established at UNIZG for longterm research activities.

<< Implementation >>

Six work packages over 36 months bring together four international partners to co-create, pilot, and disseminate concrete adult education solutions. The project develops a Strategic Framework for AFU, an intergenerational curriculum positioning older adults as  educators across three countries, and a practical pre-retirement programme. A permanent research centre generates cross-national evidence, and four international conferences and open-licensed multilingual outputs ensure lasting impact.

<< Results >>

SILVER-UNI will directly engage 300 adults aged 60+ as active learners and 100 adults aged 60–65 through a pre-retirement programme. Students will benefit from intergenerational sessions where older adults serve as educators and mentors. 15 trained facilitators will ensure lasting delivery. Open license tools, a permanent research centre, 3 peer-reviewed publications, a European Research Network, and 4 international conferences will sustain impact across CRO, CZ, PL.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2026-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000460882.title: RiversUP - Integrating Citizen Science and Participatory River Monitoring into Adult Education Pathways
2026-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000460882.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen Adult Education's role in the green transition by bridging the gap between knowledge and civic action. The project aims to: 1) Upskill educators in innovative methodologies; 2) Develop a shared framework for community-based environmental monitoring; 3) Enhance learners' green and digital competences; and 4) Transform learning centers into sustainability hubs that empower citizens to inform local governance and inclusion

<< Implementation >>

RiversUp follows a 4-phase plan:1)Co-designing a Methodological Framework, a 20-hour SPOC training, and a Pedagogical Toolkit.2)Upskilling educators and learners via project tools and activities 3)Conducting 15 monitoring workshops and storytelling labs for 225 learners in IT, HR, and NL, producing 18 "data stories".4)Holding and participating in national and EU events where learners, as “Science Ambassadors,” present evidence-based recommendations to local and European decision-makers.

<< Results >>

RiversUp will deliver: 1)A Methodological Framework; 2) A 20-hour SPOC training for 100 educators; 3) A multilingual Pedagogical Toolkit. Expected outcomes include 15 workshops for 225 learners, producing validated datasets and 18 "data stories". The project will host 9 Policy Labs leading to 4 policy recommendations. Key impacts: improved green, digital, and civic skills and the creation of "Science Embassies" for water governance

2026-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000466454.title: The Green Agora: Community learning centers for environmental literacy and civic engagement
2026-1-HR01-KA220-ADU-000466454.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We aim to professionalize the Green Agora learning model to enhance environmental education across Croatia, Austria and Bulgaria. By integrating citizen science (scientific), film festival (cultural) and community building (personal), we transform adult learners from passive consumers into active knowledge producers. Our objectives are to strengthen consortium capacity for long-term engagement, increase participation among underrepresented groups and deliver a transferable pedagogical toolkit.

<< Implementation >>

Under WP2 staff will gain specialized skills via 3 methodological guidelines, 3 study visits, and peer-mentoring. WP3 features piloted events in each country reaching diverse adult learners, enhancing inclusive pedagogy and civic engagement. Finally, we will publish the digital Green Agora toolkit in four languages,enabling national and European networks to replicate our learning tools and professionalized methodologies. In WP4 we will disseminate the results on the national and European levels.

<< Results >>

We will deliver 23 pilot events reaching 220 diverse adult learners.Key outcome includes the Green Agora toolkit in 4 languages, a transferable resource for European NGOs. Staff and volunteers (TG1) will gain knowledge on inclusive and interactive methods and strengthen strategic partnerships across Croatia, Bulgaria and Austria. Adult learners (TG2) will gain access to inclusive spaces and increase their competencies in active citizenship, critical thinking, technical skills and media literacy.

2026-1-IS01-KA220-ADU-000451593.title: EMPOWER+ Wellbeing pathways for older adults
2026-1-IS01-KA220-ADU-000451593.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen digital autonomy, emotional resilience and civic participation of adults aged 55+ by upgrading an existing European learning platform and developing age-friendly modules co-created directly with seniors. It also seeks to equip adult educators with a structured capacity building programme and practical tools to effectively support active ageing, intergenerational learning, social inclusion and lifelong learning across partner countries and beyond.

<< Implementation >>

We will conduct a transnational needs analysis and co-creation workshops with seniors; adapt existing and develop new learning modules; upgrade the digital platform; pilot activities with 55+ learners; design and deliver a Training of Trainers; create Story Cards for dissemination; organise multiplier events; and implement coordinated communication, evaluation and sustainability actions across partner countries.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver an upgraded multilingual learning platform, adapted and newly developed senior-focused modules, a structured Capacity Building Programme and Trainer’s Manual, and a set of co-created Story Cards. Outcomes include increased digital confidence, wellbeing and civic engagement of seniors, improved competences of adult educators, strengthened organisational capacity, and sustainable use of results beyond the project period.

2026-1-LV01-KA220-ADU-000454986.title: Supporting connection, well-being and active ageing through adult learning
2026-1-LV01-KA220-ADU-000454986.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Connected Lives aims achieve the following:
-To build the capacity of adult educators and community organisations to recognise and address hidden loneliness in later life.
-To develop and pilot an interest-based relational learning pathway to support inclusion and address hidden loneliness in older adults. 
-To support transition-sensitive facilitation in adult education contexts.
-To produce a practical guide to embed connection-oriented approaches in adult education practice across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement coordinated research-to-practice activities across partners to translate evidence on hidden loneliness into tested adult education models.

Partners will:
-Develop an Educator Toolkit and Relational Learning Practice Guide.
-Design interest-based learning pathways.
-Pilot pathways with older adults in each country.
-Train adult educators in transition-sensitive facilitation and hidden loneliness awareness.
-Organise dissemination events and European knowledge sharing.

<< Results >>

We will deliver practical and transferable results to enhance adult education responses to hidden loneliness:

The concrete results from Connected Lives will include:
-An Educator Toolkit with structured facilitation tools.
-A Relational Learning Practice Guide for uptake and sustainability.
-A Micro-learning Reflection Journal for Older Adults to support them through transitions.
-Tested interest-based learning pathways.
-Increased confidence, connection and participation among older adults.

2026-1-NL01-KA220-ADU-000458970.title: Pact for All
2026-1-NL01-KA220-ADU-000458970.summary:
<< Objectives >>

With our project Pact for All (PALL) we aim to strengthen the capacity of Civil Society Organisations (CSOs), including Refugee-Led Organisations (RLOs), through structured learning, to contribute to a human rights-based and inclusive implementation of the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, which will enter into force in June 2026. Ultimately our objective is to improve the position of refugees, asylum seekers and migrants, so that they can be better included and take part in European societies.

<< Implementation >>

Partners develop national shadow reports analysing the impact of the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum on refugees, asylumseekers and other migrants. An innovative advocacy toolkit will be developed to strengthen advocacy and strategic litigation, putting lived experience perspectives in the centre. A transnational Community of Practice will be established to support continuous peer-to-peer learning and cooperation, resulting in training and events on local, national and European level.

<< Results >>

We expect an established CoP, with the broader civil society community benefitting from participants’ increased knowledge and skills on innovative methods to strengthen advocacy and strategic litigation on the Pact. Adults with refugee and migrant backgrounds are involved as partners and participants, thereby contributing to inclusion and diversity. Partners will integrate the learnings in their daily operations, which will benefit the protection of rights of thousands of refugees in Europe.
topics: Reception and integration of refugees and migrants
Human rights and rule of law

2026-1-SE01-KA220-ADU-000464718.title: Creative and Cultural Industries (CCIs) as a key for cohesive development - The Key
2026-1-SE01-KA220-ADU-000464718.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The Key empowers rural CCI professionals to lead sustainable territorial development through a locally anchored micro-learning and incubation program. By upskilling adult learners in entrepreneurial, digital, and green competencies aligned with the New European Bauhaus, the project redefines creatives as agents of structural change. It further promotes cultural heritage as a strategic resource for circular economic models.

<< Implementation >>

The Key implements five interconnected work packages:
WP1: Continuous project management and quality monitoring led by Coompanion.
WP2: Mapping practices, collecting data from 140+ professionals, and defining the NEBComp framework.
WP3: Designing a modular micro-learning program and a residency/incubation model.
WP4: Pilot testing capacity-building in Spain and a residency in Italy.
WP5: Multi-channel dissemination, national events, and a Brussels conference.

<< Results >>

The Key will deliver a documented NEB Comp Framework and a catalogue of 30+ rural incubation practices. Key outputs include a modular curriculum and a digital repository of 30+ OER tools for creative entrepreneurs. Validation results from Spanish and Italian pilots will prove the model's efficacy. Finally, a Policy Toolkit and Replication Guidelines will be disseminated to 20,000+ stakeholders to ensure long-term European impact.
topics: Economic and financial affairs (including funding issues)

2026-1-SI01-KA220-ADU-000460291.title: Budgeting, Awareness, Responsibility for Valuable Opportunities
2026-1-SI01-KA220-ADU-000460291.summary:

With the BARVALO project, we aim to empower Roma communities by improving their financial literacy, reducing economic vulnerability, and promoting long-term financial independence. Through training Roma mentors, developing MOOC and OER materials, and advocating policy change, we ensure sustainable access to financial education. By integrating financial literacy into education and social policies, we foster social inclusion, economic empowerment, and lifelong learning opportunities.

<< Implementation >>

The BARVALO project will implement key activities to improve Roma financial literacy and ensure long-term impact. We will develop MOOC and OER materials, train Roma mentors, and organise multiplier events to promote financial education. A final conference will showcase results and engage policymakers in discussions on sustainability. Through media outreach, policy recommendations, and community-based training, we will ensure the widespread adoption of financial literacy programs.

The BARVALO project will deliver tangible results, including trained Roma mentors, MOOC and OER materials, and policy recommendations to support financial literacy. We expect increased financial awareness among Roma, better access to financial education, and the integration of financial literacy into educational and social policies. Multiplier events and a final conference will ensure broad dissemination, fostering long-term adoption and systemic change across sectors.

2021-1-BE01-KA220-HED-000023346.title: Interdisciplinary Dialogue
2021-1-BE01-KA220-HED-000023346.summary:
<< Background >>

The ID project aimed to shape a new kind of theatre professional, one skilled in blending artistic disciplines—a key aspect of contemporary theatre. By supporting collaboration, it provided participants with tools to navigate the increasingly interdisciplinary art industries. 
 A core goal was to harness theatre’s multidisciplinary nature to introduce new educational methods, strengthening both artistic training and higher education. Using research-based learning in a diverse environment, participants enhanced their adaptability, communication, and critical thinking. 
 The pandemic highlighted the limits of single-discipline education, reinforcing the need for interdisciplinary approaches. ID project pioneered cross-disciplinary courses, merging fields like music, acting, directing, digital technology, movement, antropology, environmmental studies, aboriginal performance. 
This training helped students embrace new skills, forming a university consortium to further these essential skill combinations. The project also emphasized theatre’s role in fostering new professions and international cooperation. By engaging across cultures, participants deepened their artistic abilities and appreciation for ID in both creative and educational

<< Objectives >>

The Interdisciplinary Dialogue project set out to prepare future theatre professionals for the demands of a rapidly evolving creative industry, shaped by technological advancements and shifting global dynamics. The aim was to provide participants with the knowledge and tools needed to rethink their role in modern theatre, fostering innovation through cross-disciplinary collaboration. 
 At its core, the project sought to develop versatile professionals who could adapt to industry shifts, handle challenges, and stay resilient in uncertain career landscapes, encourage the use of digital tools and interactive learning methods in higher education to enhance both technical and artistic capabilities, bridge the gap between academia and the professional world by strengthening partnerships between universities and the theatre industry, introduce a holistic approach to theatre-making by merging different disciplines, including green skills and approiaches in theatre making —to create more dynamic and forward-thinking productions, and create educational resources and teaching materials to ensure that interdisciplinary methods could be shared and adopted beyond the scope of this project. 

<< Implementation >>

The project included four Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities, during which the practical principles of the Interdisciplinary Dialogue methodology were developed and tested. A comprehensive ID Study Guide was created, featuring key methodological principles, exercises, illustrations, expert articles from consortium members, and testimonials from students. To complement this, a Video Tutorial was produced as a dynamic and interactive representation of the Study Guide.
A Youtube chanel was launched to make both the Students Experience videos and Video Tutorial accessible to a wider audience, serving as a space for knowledge exchange, inspiration, and collaboration between project partners and participants. Throughout the project, a strong network of like-minded individuals was formed, committed to continuing interdisciplinary cooperation beyond the project's completion.
A Multiplier Event was held in Brussels, bringing together a large academic audience to present the project’s outcomes and further encourage discussion on interdisciplinarity in education and the arts. Looking ahead, one possible future direction for collaboration discussed between project partners is the creation of an annual Interdisciplinary Dialogue Festival, which would allow universities to showcase their innovations, present educational performances, and explore joint productions. The festival would also aim to expand ID principles, integrate new disciplines, introduce environmentally sustainable technologies in theatre, and promote intercultural collaboration by combining different languages and artistic traditions.
During the three-year exploration of what Interdisciplinary Dialogue could be, students were encouraged to document their thoughts and share video feedback, giving us direct insights into their learning experiences. This resulted in a collection of ID SEV student experience videos, forming a kind of podcast made up of different short clips that capture their reflections on the project. These videos, which were recorded throughout the workshops, will be available on our YouTube channel from the official end of the project on March 31, 2025.
As a final creative and symbolic act, joint performance of all ID participants was help in Brussels in the iconic studio of world known associated partner of the project Ultima Vez company. This performance was bult with the use of organic material for the stage design and not only encouraged students to become versatile artists but also instilled a sense of environmental responsibility, aligning artistic creation with ecological awareness.
The consortium has created the Interdisciplinary Dialogue platform - an evolving and developing art object on the Internet, which will not only be a nest for the results of the project, but also a platform for new contacts, a home for young artists and experienced teachers, a place for publishing new research and experiments after the end of European funding, a place for marketing the Interdisciplinary Dialogue label.

<< Results >>

The Interdisciplinary Dialogue project produced a range of intellectual outputs designed to enhance interdisciplinary education in theatre and related fields, ensuring long-term impact beyond the project’s duration. 
One of the key results was the ID Study Guide, a comprehensive resource aimed at higher education institutions in theatre and technology. Created as a collaborative scientific and creative work, it consolidates knowledge from various theatre and design institutions within the project consortium. The guide expands upon existing theatre and art curricula by providing interactive methodologies for character development, stage design, and physical embodiment techniques for performers. Additionally, it includes online training materials, making it a lasting educational tool for students and professionals. 
Complementing the Study Guide, the ID Video Tutorial was developed as a visual learning resource, documenting the practical implementation of interdisciplinary methodologies throughout the project’s Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities. It highlights the collaborative process between actors and technologists, demonstrating how this approach can be applied across disciplines. Beyond its educational purpose, the tutorial also serves as promotional material for stakeholders, showcasing the project’s innovative methodology to a broader audience. 
A major achievement of the project was the development of Interdisciplinary Dialogue as a structured curriculum, tested by all partner institutions and integrated into their educational programs. This curriculum establishes a sustainable framework for interdisciplinary education, fostering continuous dialogue and development among students, educators, and professionals. Participants from associated partner organizations and non-HEI professionals were also recognized with certificates of mastery in the ID methodology, further solidifying the project’s impact. 
The project directly addressed a wide range of target groups, including BA and MA students, university educators, alumni, freelance artists, and professionals from the cultural sector. On a broader scale, it contributed to the development of new professions and innovative mechanisms for skill exchange between higher education and the professional world. 
The consortium has created the Interdisciplinary Dialogue platform - an evolving and developing art object on the Internet, which will not only be a nest for the results of the project, but also a platform for new contacts, a home for young artists and experienced teachers, a place for publishing new research and experiments after the end of European funding, a place for marketing the Interdisciplinary Dialogue label.
By creating these intellectual outputs, the Interdisciplinary Dialogue project established a lasting foundation for interdisciplinary collaboration, ensuring that its methodologies, educational tools, and professional networks continue to evolve and influence future generations of artists, educators, and researchers
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2021-1-BE02-KA220-HED-000030335.title: GEOinformation educational resources for CLImate Change Management
2021-1-BE02-KA220-HED-000030335.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was created through previous partnerships in various E+ CBHE projects. All partners have background in geoinformatics, remote sensing, GIS, geodesy, agriculture, etc. We would like to create a project to address Sustainable Development Goals, in particular in Climate Change mitigation. We checked online there are no programs addressing directly the topic: geoinformation on climate change management. Due to the complimentary background in agriculture, urban, forestry and experience with applying newly available sensor technologies such as hyperspectral images, lidar, drone-based photogrammetry, we decided to strengthen the partnership in creating MOODLE program on the topics, providing necessary open source elearning materials for potential students and professionals. The courses are designed in a way that anyone can start learning the skills even with no remote sensing and GIS background. As long as they are interested in climate change management, and would like to learn the skills and methods in geoinformation, they can receive professional trainings through output of this project. 

<< Objectives >>

By sharing academic resources, the consortium’s overall aim is to increase analytic and professional skills among students and Lifelong learners to improve their competencies in CCM through use of GIS and RS tools online. Herein, GeoCLIC introduces the Work-based learning approach to develop training projects and internships in areas impacted by Climate Change. A particular priority is to motivate participation of female learners. 5 modules and OERs (Open Educational Resources) related to CCM will be developed and further enhanced by the use of innovative online learning tools and international collaboration. Employability skills will be boosted by hands-on practices and direct contact with employers. To transfer the project benefits to society, multiple interactions between educators, researchers, environment companies/NGOs and decisionmakers are planned.
In summary, we aim to improve employability among enrolled and unemployed graduates as CC analyst in earth observation, GIS/RS sector; strengthen cooperation among GIS/RS enterprises and academia; ensure sustainability with OER and MOODLE program in geoinformation in CCM.

<< Implementation >>

Kick-off meeting was organized in July 2022, some delay due to partnership agreement and schedule clashes are the causes. The kick-off was to overlap with the 1st Joint Staff Training at VUB.
July 2022. Two Joint staff trainings on MOODLE platform in University of Nicosia. Experts from Nicosia gave trainings on Distance Learning and Online Education; E-Learning pedagogical Model, Modes of Delivery and Assessment; Social Learning and Learning in Organization. Best Practices for online courses such as the use of videos, and how to provide quality assurance for online learning. After the 1st training, the consortium has started to investigate how to prepare elearning materials for the project in relation to each specialization.
November 2022. In the 2nd Joint staff training at Cyprus, the consortium review the program objectives, with reference to the findings of a survey to understand existing gap in educational program. Colleagues from HSWT presented the survey and we discussed the appropriate modules and format. UNIC presented a structure of a typical course on its MOODLE platform. More trainings are related to how to choose the right tools, such as open-source tools in online courses. One specific topic is video productions. 

<< Results >>

Based on the materials developed, a Diploma of Advanced studies (Diploma de Experto) (15 ECTS) has been approved and certified by UPV Council in the form of LifeLong Learning and adult education. It contains five modules covering Basics of GIS/RS, urban monitoring, forest conservation, coastal dynamics, and smart agriculture. Each module can be taken separately in the form of micro-credential. UNIC has provided its Moodle platform for the delivery of the modules online and make the modules sustainable in the medium term. Over 60 videos have been edited and integrated into the platform and are part of OERs which can be also found in designated YouTube channel. Practical oriented education and practical assignments are integrated in the modules to enhance employability.   The project organized 2 Winter and 3 Summer Schools, intensive training courses with practical assignments building academic staff capacity across European partners. Likewise, 5 multiplier events have been organized - one of them co-funded by UNIC. Over 50 students have benefitted directly from the activities of the project. The project has paid special attention to female participation in GIS/RS field - targeting 50% female student participation at each event.

2021-1-BE02-KA220-HED-000032235.title: Service-Learning as a pedagogy to promote inclusion, diversity, and digital empowerment
2021-1-BE02-KA220-HED-000032235.summary:
<< Background >>

The education shaped by the COVID-19 pandemic brought into sharp focus three acute needs of contemporary education that shaped the outlines of the SLIDE project: 1) a need to digitally empower university teachers who rapidly needed to transform from teaching professionals into learning experience designers and experts in emerging technologies, 2) a need to close the gap between self-perceived and actual digital competences of university students by equipping them with digital fluency, intelligence, and engagement skills, but also with pedagogical skills to sensitize them towards digital inclusion and to empower them to address sensitive contemporary societal issues while developing their digital competences, and 3) a need to combine the digital empowerment of teachers and students with the pedagogical approach of Service-Learning for the promotion of diversity an inclusion, while establishing connections between higher education institutions and communities at risk, either in direct proximity or rural/remote areas. The project answered to the growing need to promote inter-connected higher education systems, stimulate innovative learning and teaching practices, digital empowerment, inclusion, and diversity, and active citizenship.

<< Objectives >>

The SLIDE project aimed to intertwine the service-learning (SL) pedagogy with digital empowerment (DE) in order to promote inclusion (I) and diversity. The objectives were to: (1) strengthen service-learning (SL) as a pedagogical approach that promotes inclusion and diversity, as well as digital empowerment of the ones lagging behind the most, embedding and developing civic engagement within higher education students, teachers, and communities in Europe; (2) equip students with digital capabilities and skills necessary for the use of technology in creative, critical, competent, and inclusive ways through SL activities that address human, social, and environmental needs from the perspective of social justice; (3) increase the capacity and readiness of teachers to manage an effective shift towards digital education, to encourage their purposeful and inclusive use of digital technologies for teaching, as well as the development of digital pedagogy and expertise in the use of digital tools; (4) facilitate the exchange and co-creation of knowledge on SL and DE in Europe, consolidate institutional and national commitments and enable a culture of promotion and public articulation of university-community partnership through SL.

<< Implementation >>

The project provides a holistic and forward-thinking approach to contemporary education. The initiative not only responds to immediate challenges but also lays a foundation for sustainable, inclusive, and digitally advanced learning environments.
1)	The project partners organized a total of 20 focus groups with 120 service-learning stakeholders to discuss the needs, innovation, impact and conditions for success on service-learning and digital empowerment. These focus groups resulted in the creation of the Service-Learning and Digital Empowerment Manifesto.
2)	The project developed two MOOC’s on digital empowerment, boosting digital literacy in higher education: one for HE teachers, one for HE students. Both MOOC’s consist of 8 modules focusing on topics like digital intelligence, digital wellbeing, use of interactive digital media in teaching and learning, digital engagement, and digital inclusion. Both MOOC’s are self-paced, registration is free. The MOOC’s are available in English and Slovak. Currently, 129 participants are enrolled in the MOOC for teachers, and 462 participants are enrolled in the MOOC for HE students.
3)	In June 2023, the Learning, Teaching and Training Activity ‘Service-Learning and Digital Empowerment, how can we make it work?’ was organized, to train higher education teachers, trainers and educational leaders on digital empowerment. In this LTTA, 43 participants from 9 different countries were involved.
4)	In October 2023, we organized the Online World Café event ‘Digital Empowerment Transformation with You!’ 35 HE teachers from 12 different countries took part in discussions on how to connect the service-learning pedagogy with digital inclusion. The input from participants resulted in a manual for teachers on how to integrate the OWC method in their own teaching practice.
5)	In November 2024, we organized the hybrid Social Hackathon event ‘Digital bridges and gaps in society’. During this activity, 76 students worked together in multidisciplinary teams to solve social challenges focused on the topic of digital inclusion, proposed by 9 community partners from all over Europe. During the event, students connected online with community partners and other student teams, and were coached by international mentors. The input from participants resulted in a manual for teachers on how to integrate the hybrid social hackathon method in their own teaching practices.
6)	During the SLIDE project, two Multiplier Events were organized in which the Project Results of the project were disseminated among external stakeholders. ME1 welcomed 175 participants (of which 35 connected virtually), and ME2 welcomed 216 participants (of which 71 connected virtually).

<< Results >>

1) PR1: Service-Learning Inclusion, Diversity and Digital Empowerment Manifesto - The SL&DE Manifesto emancipates target groups involved in service learning and digital empowerment by formulating a policy and action plan for four stakeholder groups involved in service-learning. 
2) PR2: MOOC Digital Empowerment – Teacher training for teachers, trainers and educational leaders - This e-learning module (accessed for free through the SL&DE European Hub) equips higher education teachers, trainers and educational leaders with skills necessary for the use of technology in creative, critical, competent and inclusive ways, but also to define the purposeful use of emerging technologies in education (such as AI, AR or robotics), to foster digital competence, fluency, intelligence and engagement of students, critical thinking, design thinking and student creativity. 
3) PR3: Online World Café for teachers, trainers and educational leaders - The Online World Café method is developed for teachers, trainers and educational leaders in higher education interested in digital empowerment through community-university partnerships and service-learning that aims to help them to effectively utilize students, assess potential vulnerabilities and negative unforeseen consequences, which might arise from the use of emerging digital technologies. It aims for target groups that strive to become actively involved in shaping and, co-designing education. During the SLIDE project, a pilot event was organized in October with participants from all over Europe. Feedback from participants and lessons learned from the event resulted in a manual for teachers on the use of the Online World Café method in higher education teaching and learning practices.
4) PR4: MOOC Digital Development – Competence, fluency, intelligence and engagement of HEI students - This e-learning module equips students with skills to fully participate in digital education, but also with skills to make connections with local communities and sensibilize them towards digital empowerment of communities at risk.
5) PR5: Social Hackathon - The hybrid social hackathon method aims for students to engage in a peer-learning activity which will not only ensure learning by doing, but will also has a strong transnational, transdisciplinary and inclusive dimension. Students (including students with fewer opportunities) participated in the pilot of the social hackathon event, organized in November 2024. Students were part of teams, with each team selecting a community need (social, economic, migrant, cultural, educational or rural/remote) to address during the event in the form of an e-service-learning project. Representatives of community organizations from each partner’s country participated invited in the event to define the needs that were be addressed during the social hackathon. The insights from the pilot event and the feedback from participants resulted in a guideline for teachers for the use of the hybrid social hackathon method in higher education teaching and learning practices.
6) PR6: Service-Learning and Digital Empowerment Virtual European Hub - The European hub facilitates the exchange and co-creation of knowledge on digital empowerment, inclusion, diversity and service-learning in Europe and acts as a dissemination tool for innovative methods, learning and teaching materials, attracting more stakeholders to contribute to the growth of the content base. It is created for all stakeholders (project partner universities, other higher education (HE) institutions in their countries, community organizations, national service-learning networks) that want to exchange and co-create knowledge in Service-Learning (SL) and Digital Empowerment (DE) across and beyond the EU. The European hub allows users to browse the database of collaborators and the repository of stories with a specific set of keywords. The content of the Hub is dynamically updatable by the partners, also after termination of the SLIDE project.
The project results generated the following strengths in our project consortium:
1. Diverse Stakeholder Engagement – The inclusion of a diverse group of participants in the focus groups in PR1, LTTA, Online World Café (PR3) and the Social Hackathon (PR5) demonstrated a strong variety of methods to engage educators, students, and community partners. This ensures a broad impact and knowledge-sharing across disciplines and countries.
2. Practical & Sustainable Outputs – The MOOCs (PR2&PR4), documentation (PR1, PR3, PR5 & PR7), and  the Virtual European Hub (PR7) provide lasting resources beyond the project’s duration, ensuring long-term accessibility and continued use.
3. Interdisciplinary & Inclusive Approach – The project effectively integrated digital literacy, service-learning, and social inclusion, particularly by involving students with fewer opportunities, thus promoting equity and accessibility.
4. Focus on Digital Empowerment – By addressing not only technological competence but also critical engagement with emerging technologies (AI, AR, robotics), the project helps to ensure future-proof higher education.

2021-1-BG01-KA220-HED-000031185.title: Digital Transformation of Higher Education and Training
2021-1-BG01-KA220-HED-000031185.summary:
<< Background >>

Digital transformation is one of the key dimensions of modern social, economic, and organisational development in adapting to the increased use of digital technologies, and to the features of the rising digital society and economy. Digital transformation also implies making changes in the strategy, operational model, processes as well as in the organisation’s culture. Due to the experience of digitalisation gained before, during, and after the pandemic, the preconditions were ripe to set up more comprehensive approach to digitalisation. In this respect, there was a recognised need for educational institutions to integrate and effectively use digital technologies in order to achieve their core mission: to educate students to be successful in a complex and interconnected world that faces rapid technological, cultural, economic, informational, and demographic change. Moreover, the pandemic accelerated the digital transformation of education that raised the major need to develop digital readiness and resilience of the institutions. The pandemic also revealed needs related to difficulties for the transition in terms of digital strategy, digital pedagogy and digital competence. Generally, these were the needs the project addressed.

<< Objectives >>

The DigiTransformEdu project aimed to foster the digital transformation of HE and tertiary VET institutions as its main objective. The main objective was implemented through a six-step approach (operational objectives):
1.	Mapping the digital readiness and resilience of educational and training institutions in response to the COVID-19 crisis (Results 1 & 2)
2.	Promoting the development of a digital culture by supporting institutional leadership to pursue digital strategy at institutional level (Result 3)
3.	Encouraging the digitalisation of educational processes and promoting effective digital-age learning by integrating the DigCompOrg framework (Results 3 & 4)
4.	Based on the DigCompEdu framework and the concept for the different roles of educators in an online environment, defining the knowledge and skills needed by the digital educator (Result 5)  
5.	Raising the digital competence of educators by organising training activities and preparing training materials (Results 5 & 6) 
6.	Enhancing international networking and cooperation and contributing to the EU Digital Education Action Plan (Result 6 & four MEs).

<< Implementation >>

The project started with research that aimed to identify lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic in terms of governance and enabling/administrative services, teaching, learning and infrastructure. In this respect, literature was reviewed and subsequently in Result 1 the survey targeted respondents who were able to evaluate institutions’ response at the level of governance and enabling services. The findings were collected in country reports that were further analysed to produce a synthesis report compiled together with the findings from Result 2.

Result 2 studied the perceptions of educators and students/learners. At teaching level, the use of digital pedagogy and assessment as well as digital competence were explored. Students were targeted to dip into their perception in terms of effectiveness, adaptation to online provision, digital inclusion, engagement, quality of communication and collaboration. The picture was complemented with mapping digital infrastructure and tools. 

This research and mapping aimed to trigger tangible changes in digital strategy (Result 3), digital pedagogy (Result 4) and digital competence (Results 5 & 6) thanks to the provision of guidance, tools and resources.

Result 3 focused on the strategical aspect of digitalisation. Starting with qualitative research and analyses of the survey results obtained in Results 1 & 2, examples of best practice were selected, described following a common template and included in a collection of case studies. Using the exploratory and analytical work coming from the case studies and complemented with analysing existing digital transformation concepts and exploring institutional approaches to digital strategy, a blueprint to guide HE and VET institutions in the development of a digital strategy was developed.

Simultaneously, Result 4 addressed educators and managers to guide them in the successful operationalisation of effective digital instruction. The project team mapped successful practices, approaches and tools used for the design, delivery and assessment of digital education. The data and insights were used to define a set of guidelines and operational tools in the form of a blueprint to assist in making the transition from a traditional class-based pedagogy to a blended or pure digital one.

Starting from a range of sources that reflect on the different roles of the digital educator and relying on the conducted analyses and identified learning needs, Result 5 explored further to collect inputs about the knowledge and skills needed for each role and ways to assess them. The analysis of the different roles led to a model (the Octopus model as the project team called it) that can be used to design training. Taking into consideration the job market and the main insights coming from the literature review, it was decided to design training for one of the most rising figures of the EdTech job market, the instructional designer. In addition, a learning platform was devised to serve the training and store the open educational resources elaborated in Result 6.

Subsequently, Result 6 implemented the training programme and inspired by it developed self-training materials to assist educators in implementing the different roles of the digital educator. Master trainers were selected from within the partner institutions to participate in a three-day joint staff training event to experience the training programme and its facilitation. Later on, they led other educators through the training programme and used the learning platform during collaboration sessions. In addition to improving their digital competence, they worked together to replicate the training and turn it into a comprehensive range of solutions applicable to different learning and training objectives.

Finally, four multiplier events "Foster DigiTransformEdu" gathered key stakeholders in Bulgaria, Croatia, Germany, and Italy to present the project results and foster their up-taking.

<< Results >>

The DigiTransformEdu project produced the following outputs and results.
1. Survey methodology for conducting the research in R1 & R2.
2. Five country reports on mapping the digital readiness and resilience of educational institutions in response to the COVID-19 crisis in the context of governance and enabling services, teaching and learning practices, and infrastructure (Bulgaria, Croatia, Germany, Italy, EU level).
3. Synthesis report summarising the main findings from the five country reports.
4. Compiled publication containing all deliverables produced in R1 and R2 titled "Lessons Learned From the COVID-19 Crisis: Governance and Enabling Services, Teaching, Students and Infrastructure" and referenced with an ISBN number 978-953-322-492-3.
5. Report "Analysis and presentation of the existing digital transformation concepts".
6. Report "Exploring the institutional approach to digital strategy".
7. Collection of best practices and case studies in the institutional strategic approach to digital transformation.
8. Blueprint for digital transformation strategy in education.
9. Compiled publication containing all deliverables produced in R3 titled "Strategical Approach to Digitalisation in Education: Institutional Concepts, Best Practices, Blueprint, and Case Studies" and referenced with an ISBN number 978-953-322-511-1.
10. Literature review on the pedagogical approach to digitalisation in education.
11. Collection of best practices and case studies in the pedagogical approach to digitalisation.
12. Blueprint for digital transformation of pedagogy in education.
13. Compiled publication containing all deliverables produced in R4 titled "Pedagogical Approach to Digitalisation in Education: Institutional Concepts, Best Practices, Blueprint, and Case Studies".
14. The DigiTransformEdu learning platform: https://www.transformeducation.eu/.
15. The DigiTransformEdu competence framework (the Octopus model).
16. The DigiTransformEdu training programme to develop the skills of the instructional designer.
17. A collection of digital self-training materials including short courses, video tutorials, podcasts, use of artificial intelligence, etc. available on the learning platform.
18. Project website: https://www.digitransformedu.com/.
19. Four multiplier events to expand the DigiTransformEdu network with key stakeholders.

2021-1-CZ01-KA220-HED-000031187.title: Sustainable Development Goals in education and in action!
2021-1-CZ01-KA220-HED-000031187.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated to address the growing need for equipping students and educators with tools to integrate sustainability into entrepreneurial practices. As future innovators, students often lack access to educational frameworks that combine entrepreneurship with the principles of sustainability, leaving them unprepared to tackle pressing global challenges such as climate change and social inequality. Similarly, educators and the general public face a scarcity of accessible resources to understand and apply sustainable business models in their professional and personal contexts.
This project leverages a unique partnership of European universities, pooling diverse expertise and perspectives to develop innovative, high-quality educational materials. By fostering transnational collaboration, the initiative ensures outputs are adaptable to different cultural and institutional contexts while meeting international standards of excellence. The creation of a free, open-access MOOC and supplementary teaching materials supports not only university students but also educators, professionals, and lifelong learners. This broad reach empowers a wide audience to adopt entrepreneurial solutions that align with SDGs.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to integrate sustainability into entrepreneurship education to address global challenges like climate change, inequality, and resource scarcity. It sought to empower students, educators, and professionals to create sustainable business solutions, fostering innovation aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). By inspiring individuals to act as agents of change, the project aimed to contribute to a resilient and equitable economy.
To achieve this, the project delivered two key outputs. R1: Library of Educational Lectures and Practical Tasks provided educators with comprehensive resources, including lectures, assignments, and best practices. These tools bridged theory and practice, enabling students to design sustainable business models. Simultaneously, the MOOC extended access to free, flexible education, ensuring global audiences could overcome barriers to learning about sustainability and entrepreneurship.
Through European university collaboration, the project fostered innovation and adaptability, transforming education to equip the next generation with the skills to address global challenges sustainably.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented in accordance with the planned project schedule with only minor changes without affecting the fulfilment of project results and final deadlines. 

In the planning phase (at the beginning), project plans were clarified and processed in detail. The project team including Project Board was specified and roles and responsibilities were divided. Contracts between the coordinator and each partner were signed. 
In this phase, the relevant documents for project management were also created. These are the following documents:
- Configuration, Change and Quality Management Strategy; 
- Communication and Dissemination Strategy; 
- Risk Management Strategy. 

At the beginning of the project implementation, the Risk Management Strategy was created, within which the project risks were analyzed. This strategy helps the project team respond to risks earlier become problems. For this reason, partial issues have been operatively solved during project implementation.
Planned communication and dissemination activities are also taking place in parallel. The main communication channel is the ESDGs! project website and social media channels of ESDGs! and each partners.  
Activities connected with results (R1 and R2) were following:
R1 - Mapping, providing scientific literature review (studies/analysis) – from March to May 2022 (extended by one month due to partners´ discussion about appropriate studies and analysis for literature review at the beginning); 
R1 - Design and development of course/curriculum – from May 2022 to May 2023 (extended by five months, English version prepared on time but there were higher demands on translation into individual language mutation); 
R1 - Audiovisual material (learning/teaching material) – from September 2022 to May 2023 (extended by three months due to the connection to the content of individual modules and language mutations – previous activity);
R1 – Manual/handbook guidance material (learning/teaching material) – from September 2022 to June 2023 (this activity has started earlier because the content was first discussed on TPM2); 
R1 – Best practice guidelines/report (studies/analysis) – from March 2023 to January 2024 (extended by three months – the most of the case studies were created on time, but subsequently it was necessary to translate them into national languages);
R1 – Pilot of the full-time course at each university – from September 2023 to June 2024 (during the academic year according to the regular teaching schedule at each university); 
R1 – Questionnaires measuring knowledge of students and impact of the course – from September 2023 to June 2024 (corresponding with the previous activity pilot of the full-time course); 
R2 – Design and creation of MOOC course – from January 2023 to March 2024 (extended to the end of MOOC course pilot because the MOOC course could be modified after the feedback from participants); 	
R2 – MOOC course pilot – from September 2023 to March 2024; 
R2 – Questionnaires measuring knowledge of students and impact of the course – from September 2023 to June 2024 (in connection with the MOOC course pilot);
R1 + R2 - Evaluation of questionnaires and feedback - from June to October 2024 (including partial changes of results based on feedback evaluation). 

<< Results >>

Within R1, the following has been created:
- Comprehensive study material focusing on identified areas in sustainable development, entrepreneurship, available for download on ESDGs! website (https://esdgs.erasmus.site/en/modules-pdf/).
- 7 audiovisual materials focusing on the project topics. The audiovisual materials are published on the project website (https://esdgs.erasmus.site/en/video/) and also on the YouTube channel ESDGs! (https://www.youtube.com/@ESDGs-sp9uu).
- 7 best practice guidelines, again published on the ESDGs! website (https://esdgs.erasmus.site/en/video/).
- A study manual for teachers to help them work with the created study materials, available for download on the ESDGs! website (https://esdgs.erasmus.site/en/manual-for-teachers/).
These developed materials were subsequently piloted by all university partners in an off-line teaching session, the number of participants in this pilot, exceeding the expected number of participants from 280 to 677.
Part of the piloting was to get feedback from the piloting participants. On the basis of this evaluation, evaluation reports were compiled for all partners who implemented the pilot - 7. All evaluation reports have been translated into all partner languages and are available on the ESDGs! website (https://esdgs.erasmus.site/en/resources/).
At the same time, the number of associated partners (external persons/institutions actively involved in this activity, whether in mentoring, advising, etc.) was increased from the expected 24 to 38.
Last but not least, the dissemination of the project results through six multiple events significantly exceeded the expected number of participants from 175 to 216. 
Within R2, the following has been created:
The MOOC corresponds to the content of ESDGs! The MOOC contains a total of 18 modules dealing with systematically selected areas. The MOOC is created in all languages, i.e. in 8. The Czech version includes an extra module in cooperation with the Association of Social Responsibility, which focuses on practical examples of SDGs implementation in the Czech Republic. After logging in to the MOOC, the participants are invited to take a self-assessment test to provide feedback on their current knowledge. Individual learning modules are supplemented with additional, recommendable resources and materials and are always concluded with a quiz section. After studying all modules, the participant is invited to take a final evaluation, after which he/she will receive a certificate confirming the completion of the MOOC. 
As of 6 November 2025, a total of 755 participants have participated in the MOOC and a total of 268 have been awarded a certificate. 
After the piloting, the outputs of the evaluation were evaluated (the evaluation report produced is translated into all partners' languages and is available on the project website (https://esdgs.erasmus.site/en/resources/) and selected steps reflecting the feedback were implemented (within the timeframe of the project implementation). A list of key words on MOOC issues was created to facilitate the participant's ease of orientation.

2021-1-CZ01-KA220-HED-000032237.title: Surgery Collaborative and Long-term Practical Experience Learning
2021-1-CZ01-KA220-HED-000032237.summary:
<< Background >>

Surgery is one of the fields of medicine where professionals are heavily relying on dexterity and practical application of specialised skill sets. With each opportunity to practice surgical skills, the students as well as practicing surgeons gain confidence and experience; more so if they have opportunities to practice outside of the operating rooms on simulators and cadaveric material prior to practicing the procedures on their patients. The project provided international opportunities for practical, hands-on training in surgical skills for postgraduate (PG) students (equivalent to early-career surgeons) and senior academics in the field of surgery. Through collaboration between Masaryk University CZ(MU), Universita Cattolica del Sacro Cuore IT(UCSC),The Poznan University of Medical Sciences PL(PUMS), and the University of Zagreb HR(UNIZG), the project enabled access to advanced training in surgical procedures, utilising simulators and cadavers. It fostered the exchange of knowledge on the latest trends in surgical techniques among surgeons of various experience levels. The project was instrumental for UNIZG anatomists who observed the set up and running of cadaveric courses and developed a plan to organise such courses at UNIZG.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, the following objectives were achieved: 
- surgical knowledge, experience, and practical skills at the level of PG students/early-career surgeons and academics specialised in surgery was exchanged, 
- surgical skills of PG students/early-career surgeons from the field of surgery were enhanced via participation in international internships where they were able to observe and assist with specialised surgical procedures under the mentorship of world-renown experienced surgeons, 
- expertise of European surgeons was increased, 
- early international collaborations within the target groups were supported by providing extended networking opportunities and activities to PG students and more senior surgeons (i.e. academics); the target groups had multiple opportunities to share and exchange their knowledge and experience not only within the bounds of their surgical specialisation, 
- inspiration and support for setting up surgical cadaveric courses at other institution’s anatomical department (UNIZG) was provided. This fruitful collaboration now offers further opportunities for training of surgeons in a long run. 

<< Implementation >>

TRANSNATIONAL PROJECT MEETINGS 
All transnational project meetings that took place as a part of this project were organised in an online form. Multiple formats were tried out to suit the availability of the project leadership (separate meetings for each surgical specialisation and also meetings with all partners at once were attempted). The following transnational project meetings took place throughout the course of the project. For more information about the names and numbers of participants and/or focus of each of the meetings, please see the Transnational Project Meetings section of the Beneficiary Module. 

TPM 1 
Plastic surgery kick off meeting, 14th of January 2022 
Spondylosurgery kick off meeting, 18th of January 2022 
Neurosurgery kick off meeting, 25th of January 2022 

TPM 2 
GIT surgery kick off meeting, 15th of June 2023 

TPM 3 
the second TPM common for ALL surgical specialisations, 6th of October 2023 

TPM 4 
The third TPM (originally intended for all surgical specialisations, but present only representatives of GIT, neuro and spondylosurgery), 31st of May 2024 

TPM 4 
The third TPM organised solely for plastic surgeons, 25th of June 2024 

LEARNING/TEACHING/TRAINING ACTIVITIES  
C1 - C3: Blended summer schools of surgery  
All activities from this category planned in the project proposal were implemented and took place. A detailed description of the activities together with dates, number of participants and explanations of any deviations from the proposal are included in the relevant section of the Beneficiary Module dedicated to Learning, Teaching, Training Activities. This training activity was closely associated with online case study meetings that took place throughout each year of the project duration. Each surgical specialisation organised approximately two online case study meetings per year where they discussed the theory behind and real-patient cases relevant to each year’s topic (this was an opportunity to create project results 2 – case files). The second part of this activity took place physically at MU - Department of Anatomy and Simulation centre. Here, the participants had a chance to practically train and enhance their surgical skills using bodies of donors and simulators. There was also a possibility to record the lectures and/or training sessions in dissection room to produce more project results 1 (i.e. videos). The target participants were PG students specialising in surgery (early-career surgeons) and academics (more senior surgeons and anatomists). Each surgical specialisation had their own summer school of surgery running yearly for the duration of the project (total number of summer schools was 3 for each of the surgical specialisations. 

C1 + C2 + C3 Spondylosurgery  
C1 + C2 + C3 Neurosurgery  
C1 + C2+ C3 Plastic surgery  
C1 + C2+ C3 GIT surgery  
C3 anatomists – additional event for anatomists from UNIZG 

C4 - C15: Short surgical courses + internships  
All activities from this category planned in the project proposal were implemented and took place. A detailed description of the activities together with dates, number of participants and explanations of any deviations from the proposal are included in the relevant section of the Beneficiary Module dedicated to Learning, Teaching, Training Activities. This activity gave participants the opportunity to observe, assist and discuss real cases at the foreign surgical departments of their specialisation. Furthermore, they had an opportunity to observe surgical procedures and discuss techniques and approaches practiced by the host department. The PG students were able to enhance their knowledge and practical surgical skills as they were able to observe and assist with specialised surgical procedures that they might not necessarily encounter at their home institution. The students were under the mentorship of world-renown senior surgeons and the academics (surgeons) had a great opportunity to instruct and collaborate with the PG students from a department with perhaps a slightly different focus. Therefore, the participating senior surgeons (academics) could gain a different perspective on given case. This activity also helped with increasing of expertise of European surgeons by enhancing the surgical experience of students as well as academics. Moreover, the weekend between the short course and the internship part of the activity was usually filled with a cultural programme and exploration of the surroundings which helped with networking and socialisation of the two collaborating teams. Based on the proposal, different PG students would participate in this activity each year of the project’s duration. This plan was achieved fully by specialisations SPONDYLO and PLASTIC. Some deviations occurred within specialisations NEURO and GIT, these are explained closer in descriptions of the activities.  

C4 + C5 + C6 Neurosurgery  
C7 + C8 + C9 Plastic surgery 
C9 Plastic surgery (an extra activity) 
C10 + C11 + C12 GIT surgery 
C13 + C14 + C15 Spondylosurgery  
 
C16 - C18: Internships  
All activities from this category planned in the project proposal were implemented and took place. A detailed description of the activities together with dates, number of participants and explanations of any deviations from the proposal are included in the relevant section of the Beneficiary Module dedicated to Learning, Teaching, Training Activities. This activity was closely tied to the Blended Summer schools of surgery (C1-C3), as these were the internships at one of four MU surgical departments (plastic, neuro, spondylo/orthopaedic, gastrointestinal surgery)  for PG students from three partner institutions (each of the fours surgical specialisations). The PG students from their respective field of surgery were able to enhance their practical surgical skill via participation in international internships at the partner institution in their respective field of specialisation. The students were able to observe and assist with specialised surgical procedures they might not necessarily encounter at their home institution. The students were under the mentorship of world-renown experienced surgeons and the academics (surgeons) were in turn able to instruct and collaborate with the PG students from a department with possibly slightly different focus to their own, gaining so a different perspective on a given case. The following internships took place: 

C16 + C17 + C18 Spondylosurgery 
C16 + C17 + C18 Neurosurgery  
C16 + C17 + C18 Plastic surgery  
C16 + C17 + C18 GIT surgery  

 
MULTIPLIER EVENTS  
The following multiplier events were implemented during the course of the project. Their detailed description can be found in the part of the Beneficiary Module dedicated to Multiplier Events. 

E1 SCaLPEL Multiplier Event for Neurosurgery within EANS (European Association of Neurosurgical Societies) Course, Czechia 
This event took place on the 27th of November 2024 as a part of the EANS (European Association of Neurosurgical Societies) 2024 conference in Brno, Czechia. 

E2 SCaLPEL Multiplier Event within 16th Congress of Croatian Society for endoscopic surgery, Croatia  
This event took place on the 18th of October 2024 as a part of the 16th Congress of Croatian Society for Endoscopic Surgery in Dubrovnik, Croatia. 

E3 SCaLPEL Multiplier Event: Growth & Ideas, Italy  
This event took place on the 26th of November 2023 at the Catholic University of the Sacred Hearth in Rome, Italy. 

E4 SCaLPEL Multiplier Event: Presentation Summary of the participation of the Department of Adult Spine Orthopaedics, Poland  
This event titled Podsumowanie udziału Kliniki Ortopedii Kręgosłupa Dorosłych w projekcie unijnym SCaLPEL project ERASMUS+ w latach 2022-2024 took place on the 20th of December 2024 in Gułtowy, Poland. 

E5 SCaLPEL Multiplier Event for Plastic Surgery within Flap Dissection Course, Czechia 
This event took place on the 25th of September 2023 in Valtice, Czechia as a part of the Brno Flap Dissection course 2023 which is an international event organised for plastic surgeons from the whole world. 

E6 SCaLPEL Multiplier Event: Residents’ international experiences - the SCaLPEL project, Italy 
This event took place on the 11th of October 2024 as part of a 72nd national conference SICPRE (Italian Society of Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgery) in Giardini Naxos, Italy. 

<< Results >>

O1: Video recordings of clinical anatomy lectures, live surgical procedures, training of surgical procedures 
As stated in the project proposal, the package contains videos from various topics of clinical anatomy, live surgical procedures, and videos of training surgical procedures relevant to and practiced at each summer school of surgery.  

The topics of these videos are related to the topics for each surgical specialisation at each summer school of surgery and short training courses. The clinical anatomy videos are recorded lectures either presented directly during the activities or deposited on the platform to be watched at a later time. In line with the project proposal, the rest of the videos are mainly live recordings of surgical procedures, segments of these surgical procedures, as well as some theoretical lecture materials explaining the steps of procedures.  

These videos are aimed mainly at the medical PG students attending the teaching and training activities and eventually at any medical healthcare professional interested in enhancing their knowledge and experience in specific surgical method. Wider target group is also undergraduate students studying towards medical degree or specialisation in surgery.  

The final package contains the following numbers of videos: 

- 37 videos from various topics related to plastic surgery (5 on clinical anatomy topics, 32 on surgical topics) 
- 36 videos from various topics related to neurosurgery (32 on clinical anatomy topics, 4 on surgical topics) 
- 27 videos from various topics related to GIT surgery (17 on clinical anatomy topics, 10 on surgical topics) 
- 13 videos from various topics related to spondylosurgery (3 on clinical anatomy topics, 10 on surgical topics) 

All of the recorded videos were uploaded on a secure online platform MEFANET that is run by Masaryk University. The materials are available for students of medical degrees and medical professionals world-wide (institutional log-in is possible via Shibboleth identity provider) which significantly widens the pool of medical students and further healthcare professionals and academics who can benefit from the project results when compared to the original proposal. The videos of project results 1 package can be accessed here: 

https://portal.med.muni.cz/article-776-scalpel-clinical-anatomy-and-surgical-procedures-videos-abdominal-git-surgery.html 
https://portal.med.muni.cz/article-778-scalpel-clinical-anatomy-and-surgical-procedures-videos-neurosurgery.html 
https://portal.med.muni.cz/article-780-scalpel-clinical-anatomy-and-surgical-procedures-videos-plastic-surgery.html 
https://portal.med.muni.cz/article-782-scalpel-clinical-anatomy-and-surgical-procedures-videos-spondylosurgery.html 

O2: Case study materials 
In line with the project proposal, case study materials are collections of case reports and any materials with relevant images from various imaging examinations and/or relevant videos from examinations of patients with different medical problems, including working sheets and materials related to surgical practice in simulation centre of MU (where relevant).  

Over the course of three years, project participants for the specialisation of plastic surgery prepared and discussed 15 cases spread across 17 different presentation files. They have organised and participated in 6 online meetings. 

Over the course of three years, project participants for the specialisation of spondylosurgery prepared and discussed 8 cases included in 7 different presentation files and 1 live stream surgical procedure event. They have organised and participated in 6 online meetings and 1 live stream online surgery. 

Over the course of three years, project participants for the specialisation of neurosurgery prepared and discussed 38 cases included as a part of 12 different presentations. They have organised and participated in 5 online meetings. 

Over the course of two* years, project participants for the specialisation of GIT surgery prepared and discussed 17 cases within 17 different presentations. They have organised and participated in 6 meetings (3 online meetings and 3 in-person meetings). 

*the GIT surgical specialisation had issues with the partnership – originally intended GIT surgical department from UCSC did not form partnership with GIT surgeons from MUand therefore a new partnership was formed with UNIZG GIT surgeons, but it shortened the duration of this particular collaboration from original three to two years. 

These case file materials can be accessed and used by medical students, academics and medical professionals world-wide for future teaching activities in modules dedicated to surgery. The files are available via secure online platform MEFANET that is run by MU to students of medical degrees and medical professionals world-wide (institutional log-in is possible via Shibboleth identity provider) which significantly widens the pool of medical students and further healthcare professionals and academics who can benefit from the project results when compared to the original proposal. Links to the case files based on each surgical specialisation: 

https://portal.med.muni.cz/article-777-scalpel-case-files-neurosurgery.html 
https://portal.med.muni.cz/article-779-scalpel-case-files-plastic-surgery.html
