https://portal.med.muni.cz/article-775-scalpel-case-files-abdominal-git-surgery.html 

Other results 
Participation of surgeons (regardless of their level of experience) in the Learning, Teaching, Training Activities of this project resulted in a standing and strong collaboration of each of the surgical specialisation team with their international partners. The surgeons exchanged their knowledge and experience (same/new surgical procedures done in different ways, inspirations for trying different surgical approaches, trying/buying new equipment, application of new protocols and procedures to run the department/unit more effectively). The surgeons further increased the level of surgical skills by having the option to try new approaches hands-on on bodies of donors as well as patients, they enhanced their foreign language skills and soft skill required for presentation preparation and delivery. More senior surgeons honed their skills in providing feedback to their junior colleagues not only within their team, but also on an international level. Overall, the project helped to enhance practical experience of surgeons on multiple levels giving them an opportunity to increase their general expertise.

2021-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000027652.title: DigiChem: Creating a Digital Study Environment for Sustainable Chemistry
2021-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000027652.summary:
<< Background >>

Sustainability is one of the major challenges facing both the economy and society in the future. International organizations along with national agencies, have identified sustainability as a key challenge of the 21st century. In the European Union, the Green Deal has set a fundamental goal of achieving sustainability across all sectors of life, economy, and society. The European Parliament, in its recent resolution on the Chemical Strategy for Sustainability, has highlighted critical issues such as zero pollution, resource efficiency, circular economy, risk management, and sustainable research as priorities for Europe.
To address these challenges, there is an urgent need for new skills development among academic and industrial researchers, particularly in the field of chemistry, which plays a central role in developing innovative sustainability solutions and is a strategic sector for industry. These experts must be capable of solving complex problems within multidisciplinary, international teams. However, many existing study programs do not yet adequately meet these needs. Through this project, we aim to address these gaps and begin developing a study program that will generate the future experts needed in sustainable chemistry.

<< Objectives >>

The long-term goal of our consortium is to establish a joint, fully digital international study program in sustainable chemistry. The DIGICHEM project was envisioned as the first step toward achieving this goal. During this project, we aimed at developing digital modules that could be integrated into various study programs at the partner institutions. This would allow each university to benefit from the expertise and courses offered by the other partners, leading to a broader range of available modules and additional content in sustainable chemistry for students at each institution.
Our objective was to unite experts from different areas of sustainable chemistry to collaborate in teaching. The project's goal was to develop and deliver four modules through international cooperation, featuring joint teaching and learning. These modules cover key topics such as circular economy, product life cycle, sustainable raw materials, polymers, sustainable chemical synthesis, recycling, sustainable energy materials, waste management, and water management. The modules will be accessible to students through an electronic platform, and the developed module descriptions are intended to serve as a "best practice example" for others.


<< Implementation >>

We agreed on the content and competencies for four joint modules and developed module descriptions, which were integrated into the study programs at each partner institution. The modules were each taught by staff from all four partners. The modules were designed based on mutual recognition of teaching across the partners. To deliver the modules, we organized four learning, teaching, and training activities (LTTAs), one at each partner institution. We actively promoted the program to motivate students from all four institutions and various study programs to participate. During the LTTAs, students from different universities worked together in mixed groups on assigned topics, which we set up. Notably, the group of students was cooperating continuously across the semesters, as a cohort. We evaluated the LTTAs and the modules, and based on the results, the modules were revised. While the LTTAs combined "in-person" teaching with some asynchronous digital elements, in the second round of delivery, the modules were digitaland integrated into the Virtual International Program (VIP) at JLU. As a result, many international students participated in the virtual teaching program.
We promoted the project and its outcomes via various channels.

<< Results >>

As a first step towards a joint study program, we developed module descriptions. These joint module descriptions are the key output of the program. Students from all four partners studied based on these module descriptions and got the courses accepted as part of their local study programs. The module descriptions have been implemented into the study programs of the four partners. These modules are accessible to various international students through JLU’s Virtual International Program (VIP) on the ILIAS platform. We taught these modules to a group of international students from different study programs, assigning them tasks to solve in international teams. The full teaching content for these modules, is available digitally on the learning platform, accessible to international students through the VIP. We have been teaching these modules via VIP, and we plan to continue offering them in the future. We communicated the results of our experiences through several channels, including conferences, presentations, websites and flyers. The close cooperation between the partners resulted in new ERASMUS agreements and reinforced our decision to continue developing the pathway toward a fully joint Master’s program in sustainable chemistry.

2021-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000032038.title:
Technodiversity: Harmonising European education in forest engineering by
implementing an e-learning platform to support adaptation and evaluation of forest
operations
2021-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000032038.summary:
<< Background >>

Modern machines and devices for harvesting and transporting wood are largely similar internationally, and the options are manageable. But the options for which they are used locally, differ greatly depending on the local conditions, social environment and market situation. This is related to the natural site and stand conditions, but also to local traditions, historical roots, and economic circumstances. Technology has to regard this diversity; this should be a yardstick for the competent and responsible use of technology in the sensitive forest areas. 

But educational programs on professional school and university level very often stick on economic maximation and underestimate the relevance of ecological risks and side effects, societal needs, and ergonomics. Under these conditions, it is likely that knowledge about tools and machines as well as harvesting and transport methods and their impact on environment and society is not well developed. The consequence will be that foresters’ technological knowledge will be restricted, in terms of the ability to optimize their actions on local environmental and societal needs.

<< Objectives >>

TECHNODIVERSITY addresses these challenges by building a common basis of technological knowledge and increasing the sensitivity for diversity in this field. The aim was to bring together existing knowledge in forest operations that is scattered across Europe and to develop a common understanding in forest operations to improve the forest actions while reducing environmental impact and diminishing ergonomic harms and risks. 

In detail, the aim of the project was to show and explain the technological diversity in harvesting operations and to promote it through targeted training. For this purpose, four project results were planned:
(i) Facts and methods: Develop a glossary on forest operations and tutorials about research methods on forest engineering 
(ii) Scientific audiovisuals: Provide video strings to illustrate typical harvesting methods under regional forest situations
(iii) Knowledge platform: Develop a platform to allow the access to this complex knowledge base in a didactically easy and barrier-free way
(iv) E-learning course: Implement an e-learning course on forest operations with the task to develop optimal harvesting methods that can be included in existing master programs.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities are implemented by the project:
PR1: Facts and methods: During the first half of the project, the project partners have jointly created a teaching module that explains scientific principles, defines terms, introduces methods and presents optimization tools. Based on an initial draft presented jointly by the CNR and TUD, a common understanding was developed in several iteration steps. This was executed very quickly for most of the teaching content; but the agreement on one sub-module as an extreme example took more than one year. This content-related work on a common product, in which all project partners took part, represents a significant benefit to the entire project.

PR2: All project partners have provided video material demonstrating local practices. With the support of SLU, UNITBV reviewed the material and designed a uniform structure for educational films. Using this structure, 47 educational films were then put together and provided with an explanatory soundtrack in English. In contrast to usual short videos, these films only contain scientific information, so that they can be used directly as teaching material.

PR3: A learning platform was created under the leadership of CNR. The Moodle software was chosen from various options because it is widely used and is therefore already known to users and has already proven itself very well in other projects with its detailed management of roles and rights. After three workshops (LTT1, LTT3 and LTT4), in which the use of the learning platform was tested by students and lecturers, the fourth, continually improved version is finally available.

PR4: In order to ensure barrier-free use of the learning platform and recognition of learning success for the learner's own studies, the module was included in the PULS Erasmus+ learning catalog. Various levels of the university had to be convinced to do this; new agreements had to be made and the teaching module had to be integrated into the university's accreditation procedures. At an online conference (LTT2), the heads of the participating faculties were informed with the aim of recommending the module to their students. To harmonize the contents and the form, PULS was responsible for the teaching contents of LTT3 and LTT4. 

The project was presented publicly at two European conferences: The presentation at the EUROFOREST 2023 forestry trade fair in France was aimed at decision making staff in forestry management in order to build up demand from the professional environment. The presentation at the international forest mechanization conference FORMEC, on the other hand, was aimed at scientists in the field of forest operations in order to make the product known as a platform for further scientific exchange.

<< Results >>

The following concrete outputs are given by the project:
(i) E-learning module: A complete teaching module consisting of 7 chapters, each with 5 to 7 sections, in which the scientific principles are explained, terms are defined, methods are introduced, and optimization tools are presented.
(ii) Online glossary: An extensive glossary was created as an independent product, which is linked to the teaching modules and the audiovisuals.
(iii) Short portraits: Sub-processes that are introduced in practice are described with a uniform pattern and assessed in all three dimensions (economic, ecological, and social).
(iv) Scientific audiovisuals: Short films with a length of 5 to 10 minutes were produced for 47 different sub-processes according to a uniform, scientific scheme, which are suitable for self-study but can also be used in present teaching.
(v) Platform: The various products are arranged on a Moodle platform as a teaching module, where users have different roles and rights.
(vi) E-learning procedures: With the beginning of the 2024 summer semester, the sub-modules will be freely available for everybody and can also be completed with an exam as an Erasmus+ course available in the curriculum of Faculty of Forestry and Wood technology, based in Poznan University of Life Sciences.
(vii) Different publications that point to the project on different levels, starting with students over scientific colleagues for forest operations to practicioneers who as well are interested in the new information als further education.

2021-1-EE01-KA220-HED-000023269.title: Process-based Business Management module
2021-1-EE01-KA220-HED-000023269.summary:
<< Background >>

Efficient management of ever-growing data flow can be a key to successful business, optimising material and cash flows while increasing profitability and environmental friendliness of a company. The huge amounts of data needed fast processing requires business digitalisation. Business digitalisation can increase the competitveness of companies, and whole national economies on a wider scale. This is especially true for the less-digitalised EU member countries.

The prerequisite of successful digitalisation is the understanding of the business processes. This requires a sufficient understanding of Business Process Management (BPM): thus, BPM-related knowledge and its practical application are the basis of successful business digitalisation.

This brings about the need for a concise and practical study module to provide current students and future specialists with BPM knowledge, while simultaneously applicable for training courses for the field practitioners. There must be a good balance between theory and practice in such study materials: new learners must be acquainted with theory and see its applications, while the advanced learners see the underlying theory and use it to better manage the processes that they are applying. 




<< Objectives >>

The goal of this project was the creation of a concise practice-based and practice-oriented Business Process Management (BPM) study module. In order to attract maximal amounts of potential learners, the module was planned to be digitalised, so that web-based or hybrid learning processes could be carried out with the same level of convenience as the on-site learning activities.  Besides being concise and maintaining a good balance between the theory, practical examples and independent work, the study  module in question was from the start meant to meet the needs of learners at different levels, being able to both provide new practical knowledge and fill in the missing information gaps whenever necessary. 

The implementation of the module as a compulsory or optional course in cooperation with partners from other countries certainly represents a deeper approach to its development.


<< Implementation >>

The implementation of the project consisted of the current activities:
- The creation of a questionnaire for partner enterprises in order to map the current level of Business Process Management (BPM) skills and their application in a wide range of economic sectors. Besides providing data on the current BPM levels, it also served as one of the starting points for the creation of the study materials, highlighting the expertise areas where knowledge and skills are currently insufficient.
- The creation of a questionnaire for students, partner companies and members of the economic council with the aim of defining the needs for the module and obtaining opinions on the structure of the module itself
- Obtaining data either through the questionnaire or through formal and informal personal contacts and interviews to collect the data.
- Analysis of the current amount and level of teaching BPM-related aspects in the partner Universities’ curricula
- Joint and comparative analysis of the input data obtained from both the Universities’ curricula and commercial enterprises allowed outlining the data scope which needed inclusion into the study materials to be created.
- The division of the outlined data into logical blocks, resulting in the eventual formation of the six Learning Outcomes (LOs), which were equally distributed for composition among the project Partners.
- Collection of study-related data, including BPM case studies, from partner enterprises; this was necessary in order to supply all the LOs with sufficient amounts of practical examples for case-solving tasks.
- Creation of the materials and adjusting the case study for the learning process (e.g. omitting sensitive data).
- Choice and creation of the electronic platform for the module materials; Moodle-based platform was chosen due to its universal availability, simplicity of use and the familiarity with it of the vast majority of both learners and teachers.
- Digitalisation of the learning materials.
- Comparison and several proof-readings of the study materials in order to ensure the continuity of the presented information, its quality, uniformity, and to detect and address any information gaps found.
- Throughout the project, three Multiplier Events were used to share information on the project, disseminate the obtained results, and collect feedback from the groups of interest (students, representatives of business companies, teachers, public sector, etc.). The obtained feedback was used to further focus the study materials and address additional issues arising from the discussion.


<< Results >>

The project resulted in the creation of a concise and digitalised practice-based and practice-oriented Business Process Management (BPM) study module which is meant to meet the needs of learners at different levels. In its initial shape, the module is meant for on-site or online teaching, either at the partner Universities, or as an international cooperation project with student exchange. Later on, upon accumulation of sufficient amounts of video lectures, webcasts, etc. the materials can be also used for independent learning.  Besides teaching activities connected to the partner Universities, the created module can additionally be used for in-service training of partner company employees.

2021-1-ES01-KA220-HED-000027588.title: Leveraging Individual SDG Contributions by University Staff
2021-1-ES01-KA220-HED-000027588.summary:
<< Background >>

“Leveraging Individual sustainable development goals contributions from university staff” (SDG-iLevel) has been a project directly related to the horizontal priority on the environment and the fight against climate change, that aimed to promote innovation in higher education (HE) in the field of sustainable development (SD), through digital innovation and by providing tools and resources for improving the mental well-being of HE academics. 
In recent years, SD has become a prominent theme in HE. However, the contributions to the Agenda 2030 and the SDGs are predominantly seen and measured at the level of institutions or units, and individual contributions often go unnoticed and unappreciated. The consortium applied for this project to highlight and recognize the contributions made by individual academic staff, considering their different roles and responsibilities within the institution and with the community. Throughout the project, approaches, tools, and resources have been developed to uncover, leverage, and strengthen HE academics' individual contributions to the SDGs, thereby improving their mental well-being, job satisfaction, productivity, and teamwork, and fostering greater contributions to the SDGs.

<< Objectives >>

The project has been ambitious and sought to achieve the following objectives linked to the project results: 
1. Develop a conceptual framework to link university roles and responsibilities with individual contributions to the sustainable development goals (SDGs).
2. Enhance the training of academic staff with a better understanding of their real roles and their potential contributions to the SDGs. 
3. Equip university academic staff with effective online tools to discover, promote and reinforce their individual contributions to the SDGs.
4. Build and reinforce the capacity of the university at the institutional level and at the departmental level to strategically promote individual contributions to the SDGs. 
5. Facilitate the implementation of relevant policies in the departments of the participating universities.

Other objectives linked to project impact are:
6. Improve the mental well-being, job satisfaction and productivity of university academic staff. 
7. Increase awareness and general commitment to sustainable development in higher education institutions. 


<< Implementation >>

A conceptual framework to analyse individual contributions to the SDGs
Development & testing of a training workshop & MOOC
Design of online tool and nudge toolkit
Focus group interviews for the creation of policy guidelines & roadmaps
4 multiplier events

<< Results >>

- PR1. SDG-ilevel Maps
- PR2. Online Visibility Booster 
- PR3. Self-Nudging Online Toolkit
- PR4. Staff Study Workshop (MOOC)
- PR5. Policy Guidelines
- PR6. Departmental Roadmaps
- A 2-day learning activity/ University staff workshop.

2021-1-ES01-KA220-HED-000030125.title: Habilidades transversales en la Inteligencia Artificial Aplicada
2021-1-ES01-KA220-HED-000030125.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was commissioned to address the urgent need to train professionals and teachers in key skills in applied artificial intelligence, one of the most in-demand areas in the labor market and in the digital transformation of education systems. Despite the growing interest in AI, there was a shortage of accessible, multidisciplinary, practice-oriented training options tailored to different profiles. Furthermore, a lack of open, up-to-date, and multilingual resources was identified that would allow for modular and flexible training in this field. Another important motivation was the demand for training from employees who need to adapt to the new AI context in companies, both at the technical and managerial levels. The project addressed these shortcomings by designing an innovative online course, hosted on a proprietary platform, with content in seven languages ​​and a pedagogical approach aligned with European digital competence frameworks, thus ensuring its applicability and transferability in different contexts.

<< Objectives >>

The project's main objective was to design, develop, and pilot an innovative, accessible, multilingual, and modular training course in applied artificial intelligence that would enhance the digital and professional skills of students, university lecturers, and other technical professionals. The project sought to promote active and inclusive teaching and learning methodologies aligned with European frameworks such as DigCompEdu, EQF, and ECTS, and to facilitate the formal recognition of learning through microcredentials. It also aimed to foster collaboration between higher education institutions, research centers, and technology sector stakeholders to jointly address the challenges of digital transformation. The project also aspired to generate open and reusable resources accessible at the European level and to consolidate a sustainable community of practice capable of transferring the approach to other fields or educational contexts. An important aspect was the multilingual nature of the entire project to facilitate access for individuals with limited English proficiency or who felt more comfortable in their native language.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented a set of coordinated activities to achieve its objectives. Initially, the curriculum was developed, which served as the basis for the pedagogical design of the "University Expert in Applied Artificial Intelligence" course. Learning content was then developed in seven languages, structured into thematic modules, combining multimedia resources, practical exercises, and assessment tools. In parallel, the accessible, freely usable FuturIA training platform was designed and launched.
During the pilot course phase, a real-life training experience was organized with more than 30 participants from different countries, validating both the content and the methodological approach. In addition, evaluation reports, a methodological guide, dissemination materials, and a competency framework were developed. The consortium carried out ongoing management activities, quality monitoring, dissemination through events, social media, the press, and European platforms, and transnational meetings to ensure a collaborative, effective, and transfer-oriented implementation.

<< Results >>

The project generated a series of concrete, high-impact results. The main one was the development and launch of the multilingual online course "University Expert in Applied Artificial Intelligence," composed of more than 150 teaching units in seven languages, structured by level and professional profile. This course is certified with 15 ECTS credits with a joint certificate from the six universities, thanks to the joint certification agreement signed by all partners. Each teaching unit is independent and consists of a video, explanatory text, self-assessment, and activities. This course was hosted on the FuturIA platform, also developed by the project, and is freely accessible. A methodological guide for designing microcredentials was designed, along with a competency framework adapted to AI. A pilot course was run with more than 30 international participants, the results of which were systematized in evaluation reports. In addition, more than 250 outreach activities were carried out, with an estimated reach of more than 25 million people. These combined results contributed to strengthening the partner institutions' capacity to offer innovative and open training in applied AI.

2021-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000023509.title: Food PackagIng open courseware for higher Education and Staff of companieS 2.0
2021-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000023509.summary:
<< Background >>

The European Green Deal and the new Circular Economy Action Plan have changed the data in food production and distribution. The food and beverage industry is the largest manufacturing industry in the EU (EU Food Drink Industry Data and Trends 2019) and therefore one of the main contributors to the European economy, but faces many challenges, linked to insufficient preparedness and the lack of harmonised regulations and standards. Education programmes need to be reshaped to accelerate the transition to sustainable production and stimulate innovation. The paradoxical situation of packaging materials, major sources of environmental pollution and food contamination, highlights the need for a holistic pedagogical approach. Polymer chemistry, food technologies and packaging education have remained compartmentalised, privileging particular points of view and moving away from general issues. The FitNESS 2.0 project was launched to address pressing challenges in sustainable food packaging and provide targeted solutions to pressing gaps in industry and education.

<< Objectives >>

Food packaging is at the centre of current and future challenges. For instance, collecting packaging is an issue associated with plastic and chemical pollution. The initial assessment revealed significant gaps in teaching practices, including outdated content and insufficiently targeted audiences. FitNESS 2.0 aimed to radically transform educational approaches by revising how packaging is designed, used, collected, recycled, and reused, while maintaining food safety and minimising waste. This transformation focuses on creating participative, scalable, and certifiable learning opportunities across the EU. Our aim was to reach a broader audience in the food packaging value chain, from the chemical industry to recyclers, and to offer certified courses validated by online tests.
GOALS
1. Development of academic and professional certifications
2. Supporting the development of science-based content in an attractive and innovative format
3. Scaling-up and disseminating FitNESS 2.0 beyond partnering universities and conventional industries and encouraging external contribution

<< Implementation >>

To tackle the core of the problem, we created validated and original content and designed a way to distribute it. The whole is an open-source platform FitNESS 2.0 that can be run remotely as a server or locally as an independent application within a web browser (www.fitness-foodpackaging.com). We allow the content, in particular, the most advanced, to be taught traditionally in classrooms with a beamer and teacher having a presenter view with the same experience as PowerPoint or by following the multiple links that connect the encyclopedic content of the platform. Thousands of learners from over 100 countries have used it. We updated 48 of 57 original topics and created 16 new modules focused on sustainability and recycling, organizing them into modular pathways for various skill levels. We developed quizzes, certification processes, and hosted training events. 

<< Results >>

The FitNESS 2.0 project focused on advancing circular economy goals by updating and expanding the FitNESS v1 content, adding new modules, and creating interactive resources like quizzes and case studies. It developed a flexible, open-source platform supporting both online and offline use, allowing for decentralized access. The project implemented structured certification programs aligned with the European Credit Transfer System (ECTS) and provided training for trainers in web-based content creation. Extensive dissemination reached thousands of learners worldwide, promoting the platform’s use and contributing to its sustainability through collaborations and engagement with industry, academia, and government.

Four project results were delivered:
R1 - Content’s enrichment of FitNESS v1 and curricula development related to responsible food packaging design and use
R2 - Development of the certification instruments to monitor and record learners’ understanding
R3 - Templates and training program for trainers and contributors
R4 - Upscaling and extending the platform's capabilities, referencing and mirroring

2021-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000023532.title: Sports Handicap Inclusive Experience
2021-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000023532.summary:
<< Background >>

The issue of welcoming, supporting, and training “students with special status” arises recurrently in higher education institutions, both in France and in the other countries of this consortium. Among these students, students with disabilities (SWD) constitute the majority, which makes it legitimate within a European university to pay particular attention to their needs within the framework of a cooperation project. Laws, practices, and financial resources vary from one institution to another, influencing the support measures established for these students, especially concerning access to training programs and, even more so, to sports activities. SWD express specific needs that, often linked to their disability, are directly related to the obstacles posed by international mobility, which is frequently seen as challenging to pursue under suitable conditions, despite the many advantages it can offer. Our project aims to enhance the benefits of exchanges and interpersonal relationships to address these needs.

<< Objectives >>

The project aims to achieve several ambitious yet realistic objectives for the benefit of students with disabilities (SWD) and the staff involved. For SWD, the general goal is to facilitate (and increase) mobility opportunities related to their study programs by ensuring that the teams responsible for supporting SWD, both in home and host institutions, work closely together and follow similar or complementary procedures. The project also includes a sports component, enabling SWD to discover and then regularly practice a sport under optimal conditions, with, for example, staff specially trained in adaptive sports or specific equipment. Of course, the goal is not to separate SWD from other students, whether in their studies or sports activities. In an inclusive approach, priority will be given (depending on the possibilities of the sport in question) to creating mixed teams, as with sailing in La Rochelle or calisthenics in Athens

<< Implementation >>

The project enabled the implementation of specific training: improvement of foreign language skills (for both students and staff), as well as the acquisition of techniques and professional procedures related to the support of SWD in the context of their university studies or the practice of adapted sports activities (for professionals). Several mobilities were carried out for both students and professionals; in total, 31 students were able to benefit from mobility thanks to the project. Five mobilities were organized as part of the project, each accompanied by an adapted sports event for disabilities: the first in Zadar, with the Zadar Games; the second in La Rochelle, with the Mille Sabords; the third in Athens, with a wheelchair basketball tournament; the fourth in Bucharest, with a multisport afternoon; and the last in Klaipeda, with an orienteering race.

<< Results >>

As part of this project, several concrete achievements were realized. It enabled the organization of sports events tailored for students with disabilities (SWD), linked to transnational meetings where mobilities were arranged for SWD accompanied by university staff trained in disability support. In total, five sports events and five in-person transnational meetings took place, along with 38 mobilities for students with disabilities.

This collaborative effort and these transnational meetings also made it possible to draft a best practices guide, providing all necessary information to prepare a mobility experience for an SWD. Finally, to showcase these achievements and their outcomes, three short videos were created. They highlight the sports events organized as part of the project, the adapted sports facilities available in each partner region, and testimonials from SWD who benefited from a mobility opportunity through the SHIE project.

2021-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000030081.title: Toxicology Innovative Learning For Europe
2021-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000030081.summary:
<< Background >>

The European Green Deal EU (Action Plan: 'Towards Zero Pollution for Air, Water and Soil', 2021), calls for the EU to better monitor, prevent and remedy air, water, soil and consumer product pollutions. Toxicologists and ecotoxicologists are needed to fulfil the Action Plan objectives as it aims in particular to better evaluate toxicity of pollutants (especially emerging ones such as microplastics) but also complex mixtures, to develop innovative methods to evaluate toxicity, and to biomonitor our environment. Thus, the next decade will see an increasing demand for high-qualified toxicologists and ecotoxicologists, especially in Europe. However, Europe is facing an important shortage of experts in those domains. One of the main reasons to explain this shortage is the insufficient training opportunities in Europe to face the increasing job market demands. The other main reason is a lack of interest of students for those fields due inappropriate education systems in Europe (considered as "old-fashioned"). Thus, there is an urgent need to modernise European curricula and teaching methods in toxicology an ecotoxicology, which is totally in line with the proposals of the renewed EU agenda for higher education (2017).

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to modernize of Toxicology and Ecotoxicology teaching in Europe and had several objectives:
-develop and use innovative and free educational resources (online courses, interactive PBL) in order to develop high quality digital education 
- provide innovative content on current hot topics in the field of Toxicology/Ecotoxicology to fit with recent evolution of European Policy and with job market needs 
– stimulate interest of students for those fields and limit school dropout 

The project meets the needs of: 
- students by stimulating their interest, putting them back at the center of teaching through the use of active pedagogies adapted to digital practice to recreate interactions between students, between students and teachers, and by stimulating their motivation through playful approaches. 
- teachers by proposing stimulating online courses which can be integrated in their own courses, or by motivating them to design and create their own new innovative courses. 
- partners by modernizing part of their curricula. 
- stakeholders by developing student and lifelong learner competencies adapted to job market 
- European Commission by modifying curricula and developing courses adapted to the Green Deal. 

<< Implementation >>

The Erasmus ToxLearn4EU project was built by a consortium of 7 HEIs and 3 research centers and laboratory. The consortium has organized its work into 5 Work Packages: 
- WP1: Coordination and quality management 
- WP2: Communication and dissemination of project results 
- WP3: Priority and emerging pollutants 
- WP4: New approaches, methodologies and models 
- WP5: Risk assessment, policy and risk communication 

The ToxLearn4EU project proposed a series of complementary activities that follow logically on from each other during the three years of the programme in order to achieve the defined objectives: 
- creation of 9 Intellectual Outputs (see expected results below; R1 to R9) with approx. 750h of student workload (30 ECTS)
 - organization of 2 summer schools training 55 students (A1, A2) 
- management of 6 Transnational meetings to organize the project (TPM1 to TPM6) 
- organization of a series of dissemination events: 5 dissemination activities (oral communication, poster, webinar) which  allowed regular communication on the project progress and its results (E1 to E5) and a final conference (E6)

<< Results >>

The direct and tangible outputs are: 
- Creation of online courses. The first objective of WP3, 4 and 5 was to create a catalogue of online interactive courses on priority and emerging pollutants (R1; e.g. microplastics, nmilitary pollutants), new methods and models to evaluate pollutants (R4; e.g. new exposure assessment in air quality) and risk assessment, policy and risk communication (R7; e.g. How to make sense of complex data for human and environmental risk assessment). A total of 250h (equivalent to 10 ECTS) of student workload is available for master level students and/or PhD students in a form of different interactive courses (online lectures, ebook…). These contents are intended to be used directly by teachers from other HEIs or to serve as a model to develop their own online resource. Accessibility by other audiences working in the specific domain (e.g young graduated, advisors, etc.) is possible as lifelong learning course. 

- Creation of interactive PBLs. The second objective of WP3, 4 and 5 was to create a catalogue of online PBL case studies on priority and emerging pollutants (R2; e.g. Assessment on war contaminants: case study of depleted uranium), new methods and models to evaluate of pollutants (R5; e.g. How to evaluate the pollution if Plitvička jezera National Park in Croatia?) and risk assessment, policy and risk communication (R8; e.g. Environmental Risk assessment of Pesticides: role-play with different stakeholders). A total of 410h (equivalent to 16,5 ECTS) of student workload is available for master level students and/or PhD students in a form of short (0,5 ECTS), medium (1 ECTS) and long (up to 3ECTS) case studies. These contents are intended to be used directly by teachers from other HEIs or to serve as a model to develop their own online resource. Tutorials to explain the philosophy of the pedagogical tools and in order to explain teachers from other HEIs to use them properly. This should increase the transferability of these IOs but also encourage teachers to create their own resources. Accessibility by other audiences working in the specific domain (e.g young graduated, advisors, etc.) is also possible as lifelong learning course, even though these PBLs are more designed to be used by teacher in a frame of a specific course. 

- Creation of advanced courses. The third objective of WP3, 4 and 5 was to create a catalogue of advanced courses focused on a specific topic and taught during 2 summer schools: SS2: From simple molecule to complex mixture and matrix evaluation (A1); SS3: Climate change and pollution: impacts on humans and ecosystems (A2). A total of 85h (equivalent to 3.5 ECTS) of student workload is available for master level students and/or PhD students and lifelong distance learners in the same way as interactive courses. 

More indirect results were achieved: 
- Development of teacher skills: All along the project, the teachers will strongly develop their skills in online interactive content creation and PBL case study design (only 2 HEIs were expert at the beginning of the project). All partners participated to the creation of each result/researchers, thus teachers with less experience benefited from the help of experienced ones. 
- Enhancing synergies between the partners: The consortium enhanced its collaboration in the pedagogical aspects that lead to the creation of common Teaching Units instead of each HEI creating its own.

2021-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000032112.title: Erasmus+ 60
2021-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000032112.summary:
<< Background >>

Erasmus+60 is a highly innovative project focusing on a particular age group that has not been sufficiently considered in the development of HEI activities and framework programmes like Erasmus+: European citizens aged 60 and above. With life expectancy increasingly growing and given the fact that one citizen in three is expected to be over 65 by 2060, the need for studying and training opportunities grows correspondingly. Studies are not only of benefit to the mental and physical health of senior citizens, but they are also important in view of late career development and professional activities during semi-retirement and beyond as well as personal development of senior citizens including critical thinking as well as language and IT skills.

<< Objectives >>

Erasmus+60 aimed first of all at taking stock on a large scale of existing Higher Education offers for citizens aged 60 and over in relation to the issues of inclusion and diversity.  The second objective consisted in developing pilot courses contributing to the aim of building inclusive higher education systems that contain adapted offers to citizens over 60, including student life activities to maintain one’s health. The project’s third objective contributed to the aim of promoting inter-connected higher education systems in Europe by providing a pilot platform for an online offer of shared courses as well as intercultural learning activities for citizens over 60. The fourth and final objective was to develop policy recommendations that drawing on the project results in order to highlight the urgent need to open new and more systematic educational perspectives for senior citizens of the EHEA. 

<< Implementation >>

To achieve the project’s objectives, activities were implemented in the following way: 

First objective: Erasmus+60 analyzed best practices on how to overcome important barriers for end-users. 
Project results 2 to 3 were designed to achieve this objective, that-is-to-say, to take stock of existing educational offers for senior citizens and to analyze best practices on how to overcome important barriers. In order to develop proof-of-concept courses and the toolbox we needed to have as diversified and accurate a picture of senior citizens’ attitudes to Third-Age Education and their needs (PR2) as possible, while discussing best practices. The second part of PR2 was then dedicated to the development of a methodology for co-managing online intergenerational learning offers as a particular strategy of peer learning for senior citizens and younger students. Feedback PR2 and the feedback collected during the Hackathon (PR3) as well as the learning activity provide a very robust base to develop the pilots in PR4.

Second objective: Erasmus+60 developed pilot courses to facilitate access to Third-Age Higher Education Programmes drawing partly on existing offers but also developing several new pilot courses to address specific needs. In PR4, we developed online courses dedicated notably to the issues of European identity and diversity, critical thinking, developing digital competences for citizens 60+, intergenerational online learning, as well as promoting healthy and active aging. 

Third objective: It appeared obvious that there is a need for European platforms of Third-Age Education with academically sound and internationally shared content that could eventually reflect or even be a part of European University Alliances. As there was no e-learning platform specifically designed for 60+ project results, PR4 addressed this need by providing a toolbox and guidance on how to create national/local entry points into a safe European learning space for seniors that supports their unique learning interests, motivations and needs.

 Fourth objective: Erasmus+ 60 has provided ground-breaking policy recommendations based on our research results that incorporate end-user feedback from 7 European countries. They contribute to the effort of raising awareness about the challenge that inclusion, diversity and the internationalisation of studies represents in Third-Age Education. PR5 points ways to make Third-Age Education the norm in the European Higher Education Area and formulate concrete recommendations, including both educational offers that HEIs can develop as well as full scale student services, including mobility opportunities.

<< Results >>

The Erasmus+60 project results’ objectives and outcomes are the following: 

PR2 - Enhancing lifelong learning through intergenerational learning - toolkit development for Third-Age educational activities (LEAD: ELTE) PR2 provides desk research on best practices to overcome barriers and to put into place intergenerational offers in the higher educational context. It also developed a toolkit to propose a model for planning, implementing and evaluating intergenerational learning based on the collaboration between senior citizens and universities. 

PR3 – The hackathon with stakeholder organisations regarding the co-design of an Erasmus+60 Third-Age educational offer integrating intergenerational learning perspectives (LEAD: UL) The purpose of this hackathon was to stage a large effort to collect feedback from stakeholders such as HEIs as well as local, regional, national and international educational authorities and other organisations reflecting the partners’ countries. This PR allowed the consortium to collect extensive feedback on the results of the desk research in view of preparing its piloting courses and toolbox for online platforms. The outcome was a general report. 

PR4 – Creation of 7online courses and toolbox development for online platforms to offer, exchange, link, and access community-specific and European across-community distance learning courses designed with and for citizens 60+ (LEAD: UNIST, CO-LEAD: UZURICH). Following the deskresearch and feedback collected from stakeholders in P1-3 and the learning activity, this PR developed 7 online courses (each one in English and the national language of the course leader) as well as a toolbox with guidelines, and cost-effect evaluations for a European network of online platforms offering distance learning courses for citizens 60+. The outcomes of this PR were 7 courses and thetool box. 

PR5 - Policy recommendations (LEAD: EUF) The reports, hackathon and feedback from the platform’s testing phase and final outcome provided a very solid basis in academic terms and as far as end-users' needs are concerned on which the project’s policy recommendations were made. EUF coordinated this final phase of discussions involving all partners leading to the writing of the policy recommendations report.
