2021-1-MK01-KA220-HED-000027547.title: Mainstreaming Environmental Communication through Online Learning and Virtual Mobility
2021-1-MK01-KA220-HED-000027547.summary:
<< Background >>

The Balkan region, including North Macedonia, Croatia, Serbia, Albania, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, is endangered from high and various pollution, and due to the human neglect, a large number of animal and plant species were destroyed. Citizens of the region concerned about their worsening health condition, took to the streets to demand that authorities find long-term solutions. There is insufficient understanding of the problems and roles in responding to environmental challenges by both citizens and other stakeholders. In this regard, environmental communication is a practical and essential tool for action, which enables understanding of complex environmental issues and nature, and strengthens the role of individuals and organizations in environmental governance. However, environmental communication is not included in existing educational programmes in the Western Balkans and Croatia in a way that combines environmentalism, research, journalism, communication, advocacy and awareness promotion.

<< Objectives >>

ICS and its partners propose a project that will introduce an innovative and interdisciplinary approach to education through a six-months non-degree Online Programme in Environmental Communication.

Objectives of the project:
• Develop environmental communication professionals who can promote environment- and climate-conscious choices by individuals and social groups.  
• Create a new flexible and transdisciplinary model in a virtual setting that enables lifelong learning and validation of microcredentials in environment and communication education in the region.

<< Implementation >>

The project will include Training of Trainers and curriculum development on environmental communication, creation of ten online educational tutorials and learning game, development of a Learning Management System and a Mobile App for online collaborative learning of students from five countries, online courses and a hackathon for environmental problem-solving, production of a Guide for Excellence in Environmental Communication, and multiplier events. Students will be able to obtain a certificate and ECTS credits.

<< Results >>

• Strengthened abilities of 100 students and 20 educators in environmental communication and community engagement for environmental-friendly policies and change among people.
• At least 15 student campaign plans for solving environmental problems in the region developed by the end of the program.
• A Guide for Excellence in Environmental Communication published in six languages and promoted in the five project countries, and more widely through European and international networks of partner HEIs and EPALE.
• Civic and social responsibility of students and lecturers reinforced, reflected as changes of their own attitudes and/or behaviour, or encouraging others to do so.

The project will introduce innovations in the educational programming of the partner HEIs, through environmental communication as a new discipline and use of technology for education on environmental sustainability. It will also increase the understanding of environmental communication and its relevance in different sectors and aspects of society.

Additionally, the project will open a new field of research and employment opportunities for educators and students in the region given the necessity of environmental communication in the society. Equally important is the possibility for region-based solutions to feed into European efforts in addressing environmental disruption through joint work of relevant and highly reputable HEIs in the Western Balkans and Croatia.

In the long term, the programme has the potential to develop into a Regional Centre for Environmental Communications that will serve as a hub for training and research, organizing conferences and other public events, production of online resources and implementation of campaigns.

<< Background >>

Thе COVID-19 pandеmic highlightеd that digitalization in schools is still at a vеry low lеvеl.  Whеn schooling movеd onlinе,  it bеcamе еvidеnt that digital lеarning contеnt is crucial for еffеctivе rеmotе lеarning.  In rеcеnt yеars,  еfforts havе bееn madе to intеgratе ICT in еducation,  but progrеss has bееn slow for various rеasons:

2021-1-NL01-KA220-HED-000032004.title: Citizen-enhanced Open Science in Southeastern Europe Higher Education knowledge hubs
2021-1-NL01-KA220-HED-000032004.summary:
<< Background >>

The European Union promotes accountability, transparency, and sustainability in addressing global challenges. Citizen Science (CS) is a vital part of Open Science (OS) and has engaged millions of volunteers. However, a disconnect between CS and OS limits the accessibility and impact of CS data. Bridging this gap could enhance initiatives like the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) to tackle global issues, including the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals.
Research libraries are essential in connecting science and society, supporting CS initiatives, and fostering open knowledge. Unfortunately, South-eastern Europe (SE) lags in OS and CS integration due to limited funding, language barriers, and insufficient professional skills, along with minimal engagement with broader European networks.
To strengthen the OS culture in SE Europe, efforts should focus on:
- Training professionals in OS and CS.
- Encouraging library directors to connect with the European library community.
The proposed project aims to promote Citizen-Enhanced Open Science by using higher education institution (HEI) libraries, in collaboration with public libraries, as hubs for open knowledge and innovation in SE Europe.

<< Objectives >>

The project aims to enhance awareness and integrate OS and CS practices in Southeastern European countries, including Bulgaria, Cyprus, Greece, Croatia, Italy, and Serbia. Currently, OS and CS activities in these regions are limited. The project focused on monitoring OS and CS implementation, sharing best practices that follow FAIR principles, and engaging the public in scientific collaboration. Key goals included:
- Highlighting challenges and cultural diversity in Southeastern Europe.
- Empowering academic libraries as knowledge hubs by upskilling staff in OS and CS.
- Piloting Citizen-enhanced Open Science (CeOS) practices in libraries to foster inclusivity and external collaborations.
The project was coordinated by LIBER, which emphasizes OS in its strategy. A strong focus was placed on connecting with the European Open Science Cloud to promote cultural change, sustainability, and inclusivity. Selected Target Groups:
- Library staff: Professional development in OS and CS skills.
- Academic staff at higher education institutions: increased awareness and support for CS projects.
- Citizens: Engagement in OS and CS to strengthen ties between academia and society.

<< Implementation >>

The CeOS_SE project was structured around six interconnected objectives, each leading to a specific project result (PR) aimed at promoting Citizen-enhanced Open Science (CeOS) in Southeastern (SE) Europe.
1.	Objective 1 – Building Knowledge Base: PR1: Framework for Transfer of Knowledge and Innovation on Citizen-Enhanced Open Science
Established a framework for transferring knowledge and innovation to libraries as hubs of open science in SE Europe.
2.	Objective 2 – Fostering Collaboration Among Libraries:PR2: Report on Implementation of CeOS Activities in Open Knowledge Hubs. Initiated and sustained dialogue among public, university, and research libraries to engage civil society, NGOs, and public/private sectors in CeOS activities.
3.	Objective 3 – Upskilling Academic and Library Staff: PR3: Training Report and Guidelines for CeOS Implementation. Conducted CeOS public activities and staff training in Higher Education Institution (HEI) libraries, focusing on developing transferable and replicable practices.
4.	Objective 4 – Regional Focus on the Balkans: PR4: Roadmap on CeOS in the Balkans. Developed a roadmap addressing regional diversity and opportunities for capacity building in CeOS in the Balkans.
5.	Objective 5 – Integrating CS into Higher Education: PR5: Publication on Uptake of Citizen Science in Higher Education Curricula in SE Europe. Explored how Citizen Science (CS) can influence HEIs, particularly through Library Studies, to integrate CS into curricula and open science practices.
6.	Objective 6 – Driving Policy Change: PR6: Policy Recommendations on CeOS for Sustainability and Impact – Connecting to EOSC. Encouraged policy change based on project findings, aiming to connect CeOS practices with the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) for sustainability and broader impact.
Additional Activities:
•	Eight multiplier events across Europe (Belgrade, Zagreb, Sofia, Patras, Nicosia, Odense, Torino, and The Hague) will promote project outcomes and ensure knowledge transfer.
•	A 4-day training event was held to upskill project members in designing, delivering, and assessing CeOS activities.

<< Results >>

1.	PR1: Framework for Transfer of Knowledge and Innovation on CeOS
o	PR1A1: Collection of best practices in citizen engagement in Open Science (OS) across European university libraries.
o	PR1A2: Audit of skills and practices in SE European university libraries.
o	PR1A3: Guidelines for SE European university libraries on citizen engagement in OS.
2.	PR2: Report on CeOS Implementation in Open Knowledge Hubs in SE Europe
o	PR2A1: Compilation of collaborative practices between academic and public libraries in SE Europe.
o	PR2A2: Report on co-created Citizen Science (CS) activities by academic and public libraries.
o	PR2A3: Study on scaling up academic-public library collaboration for CeOS in SE Europe.
3.	PR3: Report on CeOS Activities and Staff Training for Academic Libraries
o	PR3A1: Framework for designing and implementing CeOS activities in SE Europe libraries.
o	PR3A2: Assessment report of CeOS activities at partner institutions.
o	PR3A3: Training guide and self-assessment tool for library staff.
4.	PR4: Roadmap on CeOS in the Balkans
o	PR4A1: Draft roadmap for CeOS development in the Balkan region.
o	PR4A2: Regional consultation on CeOS practices in the Balkans.
o	PR4A3: Finalized roadmap on CeOS in the Balkans.
5.	PR5: Uptake of Citizen Science in HE Curricula and OS Practices in SE Europe
o	PR5A1: Analysis of current CeOS integration in Library studies curricula in SE Europe.
o	PR5A2: Digital showcase highlighting CeOS integration in higher education (HE) curricula.
o	PR5A3: Audit on how Citizen Science contributes to the Open Science cycle in SE Europe.
6.	PR6: Policy Change for CeOS Sustainability and Impact – Connecting to EOSC
o	PR6A1: Report on vision-building workshops in SE Europe.
o	PR6A2: Analysis of CeOS practices in the Netherlands and their transferability.
o	PR6A3: Report on European-level stakeholder consultations.
o	PR6A4: Policy recommendations for sustaining CeOS and connecting it to the EOSC.

Additional Outcomes:
•	Learning/Teaching/Training Activity: A focused training session to build capacity for CeOS practices.
•	Multiplier Events: Organized to disseminate project results, promote knowledge sharing, and encourage adoption of CeOS practices across SE Europe.

Translation of Results:
To maximize local impact, key project results will be translated into eight languages, covering:
•	SE European languages: Greek (EL), Serbian (SR), Croatian (HR), Bulgarian (BG), Italian (IT).
•	Partner languages: Danish (DK), Dutch (NL), and English.
Specific documents like PR2A3 (collaboration study), PR4A3 (final roadmap), and their related infographics will be translated, ensuring accessibility for local and national stakeholders.

2021-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000022919.title: End of Disaster: Undoing Crisis. Active Tutors Open to Reflective Education (EDUCATORE)
2021-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000022919.summary:
<< Background >>

Past the COVID-19 pandemic and lockdowns, we have identified significant needs of our students and staff and generally of people in the education sector, who were forced to move their activities online for a significantly long period. Morevoer, the recent outbreak of war in Ukraine affected the feeling of safety and well-being in our region. Statistics indicate mental health crises are on the rise, especially among young people and children. Our project is meant to provide strategies and tools for the enhancement of well-being and resilience in the education and care sector, whilst giving opportunities for international, interprofessional collaboration and leading to internationalization of our institutions. 

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to assess the needs, test tools and solutions, and provide pathways for building well-being-conscious, resilient HE. We wanted to increase our internationalization capacity whilst creating ready recipes for fostering the well-being and resilience of teachers, social workers, academic teachers and students to cascade the effects of our project.  

<< Implementation >>

We carried out international survey for mapping the needs of teachers, academic teachers and students in 4 countries: Poland, Romania, Croatia and Belgium. We wanted to see if there are any significant differences between the countries. We organized 2 interprofessional international training events for students and tutors from 4 countries, one in Warsaw and one in Oradea, during which we mapped the needs and tested tools that help to address them. Based on the survey results and research in action that took place during the international events we developed joint curriculum proposal, research report, 2 academic articles and 2 edited volumes gathering knowledge relevant to our project. In the implementation, we organized 4 PMU meetings in Belgium and Croatia and a number of meetings online. We translated the reports and curriculum to 7 languages. We also organized the main international conference (multiplier event) and 4 national dissemination events. As value added we managed to organize 2 more international conferences and participated in 3 conferences to present the results of our project. Participating entities use the curriculum materials for innovating their teaching and learning practices, enriching courses' contents. 

<< Results >>

All planned results R1,R2,R3,R4,R5 were achieved. We published 2 peer-reviewed open-access articles presenting the project results. The project information was included in 6 international conference programmes and related books of abstracts. Additionally, we published 2 peer-reviewed Edited Volumes due to the main international conference we organized at the end of the project. Both books are available in print and as open-access PDFs published in the UNESCO Chair's series. We prepared a research report available on the project website in 7 languages and a proposed course curriculum, also available in 7 languages. The curriculum has been used and implemented in a new facultative subject offered at Maria Grzegorzewska University to Polish and Erasmus exchange students. As value-added we managed to present project results in North Africa, chose a reputable educational Turkish journal to expand our reach Eastwards and translated the second article into Croatian so it is available not only in English but also in Croatian expanding the reach to Croatian teachers. Our project was visible in multipole newsletters of international associations and discussed during network meetings, eg. ISA RC25, ESA RN10, IKA, CREAN, Polish Educational Research Association, and UniTwin UNESCO. Our conference and international events gained the patronage of UNICEF Polska and the Polish Commission for UNESCO.  There is a stable and durable online resource containing project results and information about project activities, with the ability to further update it in the future and guarantee lifetime maintenance.  https://educatore.aps.edu.pl/educatore/
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2021-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000032194.title: e-SL4EU - e-Service Learning for more digital and inclusive EU Higher Education systems
2021-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000032194.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was developed to address the emergence of e-Service-Learning (e-SL) as an innovative pedagogical approach in higher education. e-SL was implemented as a course-based, credit-bearing educational experience where students participated in service activities meeting community needs, and reflected on these experiences to deepen their understanding of course content and enhance civic responsibility. The project aimed to address several key needs: 1) improving the capacity of higher education teachers to transition to socially inclusive digital education; 2) enhancing lecturers’ digital and instructional design skills to utilize new technologies for Service-Learning; 3) shifting from traditional teaching models to more innovative pedagogical approaches; 4) raising student awareness of e-SL opportunities; 5) measuring the impact of e-SL activities on both student learning and community outcomes; 6) developing students’ digital skills and competences; and 7) facilitating the exchange of best practices and guidelines for organizing e-SL projects.

<< Objectives >>

The project successfully aimed to develop the University Third Mission into social engagement. It achieved the following objectives: 1) it built learning systems with an innovative pedagogical approach integrating community services into students’ curricula; 2) it promoted a shift from a traditional assistive model (service for the community) to a horizontal model of solidarity (service with the community); 3) it spread knowledge of e-SL methodologies by developing training materials for academics, guiding them in adopting e-SL and helping students address social needs, especially during emergencies like the pandemic; 4) it developed digital skills of HE lecturers/trainers and students to implement e-SL effectively; 5) it linked e-SL education with research and innovation, addressing community needs; 6) it put students’ hard and soft skills into practice through e-SL projects; 7) it maximized social impact and fostered civic responsibility; 8) it promoted prosocial behavior through engagement with people facing fewer opportunities; 9) it provided educational pathways for students who faced barriers to accessing education due to geographic, social, economic, or cultural challenges; 

<< Implementation >>

The project partners successfully implemented a development path to reach the project objectives. The initial step was the definition of design principles and quality elements for e-SL projects, addressing an urgent need highlighted by the COVID-19 pandemic restrictions, which limited in-person SL. Once these elements were nationally and internationally validated, the partners developed training content for HE teachers to implement e-SL projects with their students during curricular activities. Jointly developed training materials were tested by over 50 HE teachers, who provided feedback that led to revisions and the creation of a Training Manual and e-learning course for self-training. The next phase involved students and community organizations in implementing e-SL projects. Tools were created in PR3, PR4, PR5, and PR6, focusing on guidelines for community partners, facilitating methodologies, assessment of community impact, and students’ learning outcomes. The methodologies followed a development, testing, revision, and release process. After testing and revising the materials, the final versions were released, and partners focused on exploitation activities to engage other stakeholders in replicating e-SL projects.

<< Results >>

The project successfully achieved the following results and outcomes. PR1: Design principles for e-SL projects, defining the foundation for the eSL4EU course for trainers. PR2: Training materials and tools for academics, enabling the adoption of e-SL in inclusive higher education systems. This included blended training materials, a Training Manual for trainers, and an e-learning course for self-training. PR3: e-SL guidelines for community partners, explaining the role and responsibilities of community organizations in e-SL projects. PR4: Facilitating methodologies for trainers, providing guidance to support students in e-SL projects, along with a Facilitator's Video Guide for future self-training. PR5: Evaluation methodology and materials for assessing the social impact of e-SL projects on the community. PR6: Evaluation methodology for assessing students' learning outcomes, including a guide for other HEIs. The project also aimed to increase pedagogical skills of HE trainers, raise awareness of e-SL’s social impact, and promote its use in higher education, providing a full package of materials for HEIs to adopt and implement e-SL.

2021-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000032201.title: Sustainable Design and Process in Textiles for Higher Education
2021-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000032201.summary:
<< Background >>

The aim of the project is to undertake various types of educational activities in the area of Sustainable Design and Process in Textile. It is necessary to change the awareness and approach to this important topic. Future textile designers who will create new products and solutions for the textile and clothing industry, and for others that use textile products (medicine, transport, hygiene industry, or protective equipment) must have full knowledge and awareness of how to create new solutions in line with the goals of sustainable development. The textile and clothing industry is responsible for the emission of around 2 to 3 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide annually. This industry is on the same list of the largest global emitters of greenhouse gases as energy, transport and food manufacturing. At the same time, the production of textiles and footwear consumes a great deal of water, and the cultivation of cotton used in the garment industry requires intensive pesticide use and degrades soil. All those negative aspects should be improved in coming years. Deep knowledge & case studies with real challenges in this area must be provided by the higher education institutions, including those that carry research in the textile field.

<< Objectives >>

The intention of the project implementers is to fill the knowledge gap in the area of Sustainable Design and Process in Textiles for Higher Education. The condition of the textile and clothing industry and related industries does not look optimistic in the context of care for the natural environment. Therefore, it is necessary to raise awareness of the environmental effects of this industry. But most importantly, innovative solutions and directions of action must be developed so that this industry becomes less carcinogenic for the industry and the end user receives a safe product of high quality. Students are guided through the most important issues helpful in understanding the complexity of the textile and clothing industry. The prepared materials show a whole series of possibilities that can be used in the education process and in business by planning and developing sustainable development patterns in textiles. 
The GreenTEX project is about innovative teaching materials in the field of Sustainable Design and Process in Textiles, the materials are available on the multimedia platform Sustainable BOOSTER in Textiles.

<< Implementation >>

(1) Organization of regular meetings of the project team (on-line and face-to-face) to monitor the progress of the project, exchange experiences, discuss project issues and solve current problems and challenges. 

(2) Creating modern research and teaching materials for teachers and students as well as research and teaching reports. 

(3) Preparation of case studies based on real situations / problems in enterprises. 

(4) Based on the prepared materials, a Sustainable Design and Process in Textiles course sheets (2 versions) were created. 

(5) Organization of the International Green Summer School (students from five European countries took up the design challenge & created innovative solutions in the area of Sustainable Design and Process in Textiles). 

(6) Creation of a Green Exhibition, which presents students' projects developed during the Green Summer School and some more "green examples".

(7) Arrangement of several meetings with various project stackholders at all partner universities - Mulitplier Events such as Meetings with project stakeholders, and local Teacher's Trainings organized at the end of the project at all consortium universities. 

(8) Final conference -  a good opportunity to learn about examples of good practices, hear experts, exchange experiences and disseminate the results achieved.

<< Results >>

The main goals of the project were to increase the awareness of target groups, increase the attractiveness of higher education and build better cooperation between research units and industry. 

The concrete outputs that were created as a result of the project implementation are: 
(1) E-book with Green Handouts - materials for teachers and student for Sustianable Design and Process in Textiles;(2) Case studies (created with the cooperation with selected companies);
(3) Multimedia platform Sustainable BOOSTER in Textiles with 15 learning modules; 
(4) Course sheets (basic and extended ones) - Sustianable Design and Process in Textiles;
(5) Scientific and didactic reports - valuable publications that are available for a wide audience; 
(6) Innovative solutions developed at the International Green Summer School presented at the
Green Exhibition. 

Moreover, the project achieved such results as: 
(1) Raising professional qualifications, enabling further education or increasing the chance of finding a work that meets the expectations of students and the demanding labor market (students develop skills, qualifications and competences, learn modern didactic methods); 
(2) Teachers improve their professional competences, learn about and apply modern teaching methods, and introduce innovative solutions;
(3) training (obtaining new/additional qualifications in a specific scope);
(4) establishing cooperation (inter-branch, transnational) with project partners and associated partners. 

Benefits resulting from the cooperation of partner institutions at the international level and soft results: 
-increasing the sense of responsibility for the tasks performed;
-increasing the level of knowledge and competences during the exchange of experiences;
-acquisition of communication skills (interpersonal contacts), improvement of cooperation between universities, business and public institutions;
-development of intercultural competences: openness, acceptance, tolerance, increased independence.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2021-1-RO01-KA220-HED-000027576.title: Digital Platform Enterprise
2021-1-RO01-KA220-HED-000027576.summary:
<< Background >>

This project addresses the significant underrepresentation of European Union companies within the global digital platform economy.  While Europe boasts a skilled workforce and strong technical capabilities, two primary obstacles hinder the growth of European Digital Platform Enterprises (DPEs): insufficient risk capital and a lack of crucial skills for scaling these businesses.  The project directly tackles these challenges.  It aims to develop a comprehensive Digital Platform Enterprise Management module that will provide students with the necessary expertise in areas such as digital product-service systems, network effects, and the optimization of digital enterprise architecture.  The ultimate goal is to equip future graduates with the skills required to successfully establish and scale innovative DPEs within the European context, thereby boosting the EU’s competitiveness in the global digital economy.  The project's activities are tailored to develop educational materials, a training methodology, and a collaborative online learning tool.

<< Objectives >>

This project aims to significantly enhance the topical, methodological, and intercultural competencies of 40 students specializing in Digital Platform Enterprise management.  A core component involves the development of a robust online learning environment, specifically designed to foster collaboration and support effective digital learning practices amongst students pursuing Business Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or Business Informatics degrees.  Furthermore, the project will improve the flexibility of individual learning journeys for 20 students through strategically implemented blended mobility programs.  The ultimate goal is to create a high-quality, adaptable curriculum framework that can serve as a model for modernizing Master's level programs focused on Digital Platform Enterprise management within higher education institutions worldwide.

<< Implementation >>

The DEMO Report PR1 provides a comprehensive study of Digital Platform Enterprise (DPE) education literature, synthesizing key findings from academic sources, HEI programs, industry cases and publications. It establishes a state-of-the-art analysis of the research, education, and applied science in DPE, fostering a shared understanding and common terminology. The Digital Platform Enterprise methodology was developed as part of the DEMO project using the Balanced Design Planning tool. This tool ensures an innovative alignment of course content with learning outcomes (LO) and student workload. The Digital Platform Enterprise methodology was developed as part of the DEMO PR2 using the Balanced Design Planning tool. This tool ensures an innovative alignment of course content with learning outcomes (LO) and student workload. PR3 provides 15 teaching units (90 minutes each) for a Digital Platform Enterprise module, addressing a gap in current educational resources. The innovative element is the comprehensive coverage of key topics across different disciplines. As PR4 we developed practice-based case studies which have proven to be an effective method for enabling students to explore theoretical concepts and apply them to real-world scenarios. Used in both summer schools (2023 and 2024), they required students to address open-ended problems and develop solutions in interdisciplinary teams. PR5 presents a modular, adaptable curriculum framework for a Joint Industry-Academia Master's program focusing on Digital Platform Enterprises.  Designed to address the scarcity of standardized, interdisciplinary higher education programs in this critical emerging field within the European context, this framework facilitates integration into existing university structures while adhering to national regulatory requirements.  PR6 represents the Digital Platform Creator which is an innovative online tool designed for students to collaboratively design and analyze digital platforms. It offers a visual platform canvas, real-time collaboration and a recommender system for guided learning. The goal of PR7 was to support students in developing scientific papers, either individually or in teams, under the guidance of teachers, and concluded with 7 papers. DEMO project held two planned Summer Schools on the topic of Digital Platform Enterprise in 2023 and 2024, in Romania, with 20 participating students and 6 teachers per summer school. 2 Multiplier Events in 2024. ME1: Improving student competences for the Platform Economy, in October 2024 (for local participants) and December 2024 (for international participants) in Croatia. ME2: Results and contribution of the DEMO project to career chances for students, December 2024, in Romania.

<< Results >>

The DEMO project produced several significant outputs.  First, a comprehensive report (PR1) synthesized existing research, educational programs, and industry practices related to Digital Platform Enterprise (DPE) education, establishing a shared understanding and common terminology within the field.  Second, a novel and innovative training methodology (PR2), developed using the Balanced Design Planning tool, ensured effective alignment of course content with learning objectives and student workload.  Third, fifteen 90-minute teaching units (PR3) were created to address a significant gap in available DPE educational resources, offering a multi-disciplinary approach. Fourth, practice-based case studies (PR4), implemented in summer schools, provided students with valuable real-world experience in addressing open-ended problems collaboratively.  Fifth, a flexible and adaptable curriculum framework (PR5) was developed to guide the creation of Joint Industry-Academia Master's programs in DPE, addressing the lack of standardized, interdisciplinary programs in Europe. Sixth, a cutting-edge digital platform design and analysis tool https://digitalplatformcreator.io  (PR6) was created to facilitate collaborative learning and provide students with a guided learning experience.  Finally, the project culminated in the production of seven peer-reviewed scientific papers authored by students under faculty guidance (PR7). In addition to student contributions, the Erasmus+ DEMO consortium – the group of professors and researchers from the partner institutions highlighted in bold font in the listing below – produced ninet research papers on topics related to enterprise modeling, digital platforms, and innovative educational methods: 
-	CM2KGcloud - An open web-based platform to transform conceptual models into knowledge graphs. Science of Computer Programming Journal: 103007 (2024)
Co-authored by: Muhamed Smajevic, Syed Juned Ali, Dominik Bork (TUW)
-	EA ModelSet – A FAIR Dataset for Machine Learning in Enterprise Modeling. 16th IFIP Working Conference on the Practice of Enterprise Modeling.
Co-authored by Philipp-Lorenz Glaser, Emanuel Sallinger, Dominik Bork (TUW)
-	The Extended EA ModelSet–A FAIR Dataset for Researching and Reasoning Enterprise Architecture Modeling Practices
Co-authored by Philipp-Lorenz Glaser, Emanuel Sallinger, Dominik Bork (TUW)
-	Model-Based Construction of Enterprise Architecture Knowledge Graphs. 26th International Conference on Enterprise Design, Operations, and Computing.

Co-authored by: Martin Robl, Dominik Bork (TUW)
-	The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Education, International Conference of Management and Industrial Engineering 2023, vol.11
Co-authored by: Olivia Doina Negoita (UPB), Mirona Ana-Maria Popescu (UPB)

2021-1-RO01-KA220-HED-000031987.title: Civic engagement of cultural and historical heritage in urban and sub-urban environment – EU context, perspectives & good practices
2021-1-RO01-KA220-HED-000031987.summary:
<< Background >>

The importance of preservation & socialization of cultural and historical heritage (CHH) in urban & sub-urban environments had to be explained to university professors & assistants. They needed a little more practically oriented knowledge, skills & competencies to be able to defend more convincingly & qualitatively the need for socialisation, conservation & exposure of this heritage in an adequate & correct way. To ensure the future of the cultural, historical and even social heritage, more awareness is needed among all members of today’s society. Therefore, it is important, on the one hand, to seek and promote good practices for socialization and exposure of CHH. On the other hand, to give a little more "publicity" to those well-developed & existing examples of harmonious socialization, respectful exhibition and conscious preservation and sustainable "use" of the cultural and historical heritage of the communities in a modern urban environment.
The involvement of university professors & assistants can contribute to raising awareness & involvement of students as active social actors in promoting & preserving heritage; the students could become keys agents in promoting cultural heritage through digital technologies.

<< Objectives >>

The emphasis on the heritage value for the society based on the concept of utilization of the full potential of the CHH and transforming it to be part of a working economy is a unique combination. A combination that can have a huge impact not only for the local communities & region but also nationwide. As such initiatives are very new and necessary for fostering learning about and through CHH and its positive utilization of the local & national cultural & historical identity and its part in forming the diverse identity of our common EU family. Only through acknowledging that local heritage is also part of EU heritage, the European idea & unity can survive. 
The general objective of CultHera was to enhance the competencies of university staff to teach and apply models for the socialization of cultural & historical heritage, to support the partners to create new or to develop/improve existing programmes & training courses for specialists in the preservation & socialization of the CHH in urban & sub-urban environment and to facilitate the civic engagement with cultural and historical heritage in these environments to raise awareness and foster better understanding of  common EU values, and concepts of common & shared future. 

<< Implementation >>

To achieve the defined objective CultHera developed the following activities:
•	Transnational meetings.
There were 6 official project meetings. The 1st meeting was in Bulgaria where the partners discussed the report based on content analysis and the survey for the stakeholders. There were discussions about the main characteristics of the Methodological framework, timeline, and tasks. Partners discussed and agreed on the action plan. The 2nd meeting took place in Croatia. The partners discussed in detail the development of the Training pack. (the applied approach, the structure, the exact content incl. all thematic chapters.). They agreed also on the content of the website & and detailed the structure of the E-platform. The 3rd official work meeting took place in Portugal. The partners discussed the developed so far content of the training course & and the Guidebook for mentors – structure, content & partners’ roles. The 4th meeting took place in Poland. The partners provided the structure of R3. CultHera Model and discussed also the frameworks for an internal revision process. They agreed on the exact profile of the university academic staff to take the training course as well as on the profile of the trainer to lead the training. They set the timelines for the piloting. The 5th meeting took place in Italy. Partners presented & discussed the gathered feedback from the piloting. They decided on the relevance of the received suggestions to refine the CultHera outcomes. The partners discussed the structure & content development of the Strategy for civic engagement The last meeting was in Romania, and it was combined with the final conference to present CultHera outcomes to the general audience. Combining the final conference with the final project meeting made it possible for all partners to attend the conference & share their experiences with the interested stakeholders. During the final project meeting partners discussed different approaches & strategies for further development & use of CultHera outcomes.
•	Production of the results
For the production of the results, the partners began with the development of the Methodological framework. For this, a context and a need analysis were conducted. For all results, each lead partner provided a template for collecting texts and had the responsibility to realise the final document. All documents were reviewed internally and then piloted by each partner. In the end, they were evaluated by an external evaluator. The content of these documents was posted on the E-platform (https://moodle.culthera.eu/) and seven participants from each country provided feedback. This feedback was incorporated into the final form of the documents. After a final correction, these documents were translated into the national languages of the partners and are available on the E-platform.
•	Multiplier events
In the last month of the project, all partners organized a conference and the final conference of the project was held in Romania, Brasov. All partners were presented with at least 2 participants. Information about these events was posted on the website, Facebook page and other media locations. During these events, the results of the project were presented, and part of the feedback from participants was incorporated into Strategy for for further exploitation of the results. Discussions with the participant offered ideas for future collaboration in this area. FRAME created a brochure and a movie to promote the project, which was posted on both the website (https://culthera.eu/) and Facebook page (https://www.facebook.com/CultHeraProject). The movie was done during the Final conference from Romania.

<< Results >>

R1.Methodological framework. The main aim of the Methodological Culthera Framework was to provide the structure, roadmap, and key points of the training process to achieve the project’s goals. This document provided the basis for the development of the R2. CultHera training package.
R2.Training pack. The CultHera project offers, through its Training Package components (CultHera Handbook and CultHera Manual), tools to improve understanding and awareness of the common EU values and principles that heritage conveys. These are tools for managing cultural and historical heritage resources in urban and suburban environments. The Training kit also includes the document “Methodology for “inclusion” of cultural & historical heritage (CHH) in the modern urban & sub-urban environment which presents an overview of those two documents. The Handbook offers a short theoretical background regarding cultural heritage to those who are not necessarily specialized in this field. CultHera Manual is a complementary tool to the CultHera Handbook. The Manual contains specific case studies related to the chapters of the Handbook. Therefore, these two documents are complementary. 
R3. CultHera Model for integrated approach for cultural & historical heritage socialization & management in urban and suburban environment. CultHera Model for integrated approach provides opportunities for increasing the investments and professional qualification of specialists working to preserve and socialize cultural-historical heritage (CHH). This integrated approach presupposes participatory governance, an approach for which the EU Council has developed specific conclusions. The integrated approach required the active participation of all relevant stakeholders in public actions, i.e., public authorities, business sector, civil society organizations, nongovernmental organizations, voluntary sector, and stakeholders. This approach presupposed their active involvement in all decision-making processes, planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of CHH-related policies and programs. Such engagement aims to increase the accountability and transparency of invested public resources and build public confidence in policy decisions. 
R4 . Guidebook for mentors. The Guidebook for Mentors is intended to serve users of the educational materials available on the CultHera platform (https://moodle.culthera.eu/). Its main purpose is to explain how to effectively carry out the CultHera training. 
Moreover, based on the results of the survey, the consortium proposed a teaching methodology that includes both theoretical and practical approaches, incorporating case studies, fieldwork, and project work. It adopts a holistic and interdisciplinary approach, linking cultural disciplines to other areas (economics, management, marketing, psychology, sociology) and dimensions (territorial traditions, gastronomic traditions, tourism, social responsibility). The content was created with an explicit tendency to be more operational and practical, with a multidisciplinary approach focused on a better definition of cultural heritage and intangible aspects of cultural heritage. It seeks a balance between the exploitation and protection of cultural heritage, showcasing good practices in valorization. The Guidebook also aims to establish links between traditional aspects (cultural heritage and protection) and other disciplines (valorization, social dimensions, digitalization, management, and planning).
R5. Strategy for civic engagement in the socialization of cultural & historical heritage in urban and suburban environments
The project partners developed this strategic document to present possible solutions for reducing and overcoming the identified deficits in the existing training offered in the socialization and management of cultural and historical heritage (CHH) in urban and suburban environments (USE). The strategy is based on the identified good practices and approaches, as well as the deeper knowledge and understanding of the topic acquired during the development of all previous results and through multiple discussions with the target group members and stakeholders. The partners’ specific expertise in the topic was also an important factor in the distribution of development tasks.
R6. E-platform& E-library. CultHera E-platform is a Moodle platform, as it is very user-friendly, easy to work with, and already familiar to the majority of the stakeholders. The platform hosts all materials developed under the project. The material in each section and respective sub-section is available as a separate .pdf downloadable file so that in case a trainee/user is interested only in a specific part of the module to be able to download it for self-study and offline use. The E-library is the last section of the platform. It is a collection of various digital resources that complement the respective topic and provide additional information that can expand the knowledge & competencies of the trainees in that area. The system allows the list to be displayed according to different criteria – title, type, and language of the resource. The resources are uploaded in their original. The language of each resource is provided in the displayed list. The uploaded resources are categorized as follows: Official document (like strategy, EU council regulation, EU parliament decision, any national state document/report, etc.); Scientific article; General article; Book and/or textbook; Presentation; Video (incl. YouTube); Blog/Vlog; Social media; Other. The use of the materials in the interactive library is not bound with the use of the training course or with any of the other resources on the platform. It is available for use by any student who is registered and enrolled in the course. It could be further amended & expanded by the partners even after the end of the project.
Besides all results described in the respective section, the project developed a website to provide information about the project. There is information about the results of the project and access to the E-platform, about TPM and ME and some dissemination documents (brochure, video). Other outputs are Progress quality reports (interim & final report), Dissemination strategy (marketing channels & the structure of the dissemination activities for all partners), and Exploitation strategy (it outlines concrete steps for outputs’ exploitation beyond the project lifetime. and guidelines for future development of the CultHera outputs),  and IPR Agreement (It clarifies the rights of use for CultHera outputs).

2021-1-RS01-KA220-HED-000032054.title: From digital technology to educational tools: Improving the quality of active learning and teaching in the online and hybrid environment in applied disciplines of agricultural sciences
2021-1-RS01-KA220-HED-000032054.summary:
<< Background >>

The idea for applying to the Erasmus+ HEAL-in-ONE project stemmed from the urgent need to enhance the quality of online and hybrid teaching in applied agricultural sciences. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed significant gaps in digital preparedness, teaching methods, and student engagement across partner institutions. Teachers lacked competencies in using Active Learning and Teaching (ALT) methodologies and digital tools effectively, while students faced difficulties in actively participating and achieving expected learning outcomes in the virtual environment. Traditional methods proved inadequate in fostering practical, hands-on skills essential in applied disciplines. There was a clear need to implement ALT methodologies, improve digital infrastructure, and support both educators and students with resources that ensure inclusive, engaging, and competency-based learning. HEAL-in-ONE was designed to meet these challenges by creating a framework for ALT, offering training programs, developing digital tools, and supporting curriculum improvement to make higher education in agriculture more resilient, innovative, and aligned with societal and labour market needs.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the Erasmus+ project HEAL-in-ONE is to improve the quality of online and hybrid learning and teaching in applied agricultural sciences through the implementation of active learning and teaching (ALT) methodologies. By doing so, the project aims to enhance student engagement, foster the development of subject-specific and 21st-century competencies, and ensure better alignment between learning outcomes, teaching strategies, and assessment methods. HEAL-in-ONE also seeks to strengthen teacher competencies in using digital tools and modern pedagogical approaches, as well as to support institutions in creating sustainable structures, such as the Centers for Quality Improvement. Furthermore, the project aims to modernize study programs by integrating ALT strategies and improving course design, delivery, and evaluation processes. Through international collaboration, training events, digital tool development, and dissemination of results, the project strives to build a vibrant learning community, ensure wider stakeholder engagement, and contribute to a more innovative, inclusive, and future-ready higher education in the field of applied agricultural sciences.

<< Implementation >>

In the Erasmus+ HEAL-in-ONE project, we implemented a range of interconnected activities aimed at improving the quality of teaching and learning in applied agricultural sciences. We organized Transnational Project Meetings (TPMs) to coordinate work and ensure smooth collaboration among partners.  Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities (LTTAs) were held to strengthen teacher competencies in active learning and digital methodologies. We developed and piloted an innovative ALTONE Manual, created new course specifications with integrated active learning strategies, and introduced digital tools to support teaching and student engagement. Multiplier Events (MEs) were conducted to present results and encourage stakeholder participation. Centers for the Improvement of Learning and Teaching Quality were established at partner institutions to support sustainable development. Activities also included course modernization aligned with learning outcomes, assessment methods, and ECTS standards, as well as student work plans that promoted the development of generic and 21st-century competencies. A strong dissemination strategy and stakeholder engagement supported long-term impact and sustainability. 

<< Results >>

The Erasmus+ project HEAL-in-ONE resulted in a series of impactful and sustainable outcomes that support the modernization of higher education in applied agricultural sciences. Key results include: 
•	The development of the ALTONE Manual, which outlines methodologies, strategies, and techniques for active learning and teaching tailored to applied disciplines. 
•	Modernized course specifications (Book of Courses) designed with constructive alignment, clearly defined learning outcomes, and integrated digital tools. 
•	Strengthened teacher competencies through targeted LTTAs, focusing on pedagogy-first approaches and the effective use of digital media in education. 
•	Enhanced student work plans and activity schedules promoting generic and 21st-century competencies through active engagement. 
•	Creation of Centers for Improvement of Learning and Teaching Quality within partner institutions to ensure sustainability and continued support for innovation. 
•	Conducted Multiplier Events and stakeholder presentations to share outcomes and build a wider learning community. 
•	A strong focus on self-assessment and accreditation processes for study programs, ensuring alignment with European standards and relevance to societal and economic needs. 
These results contribute to long-lasting improvements in education quality, institutional capacity, and student readiness for real-world challenges. During the implementation of the project, teachers of pilot subjects were expected to adopt principles of good practice in active learning/teaching (ALT), improve the planning of subject objectives for an online environment, acquire relevant competencies for applying ALT methodology, and contribute to enhancing interactivity between themselves and students, as well as among students. They also aimed to foster creativity and critical thinking in both students and teachers, improve students' self-reflection on learning, and develop self-reflection in their teaching methods. Additionally, they worked on improving shared inquiry between learners and teachers to answer questions and solve problems that facilitated modelling, fostered creativity, and enhanced active and collaborative learning.  Since learners came from various generations, it was important for teachers to address their learning needs and plan effective programs using ALT. 
Formative and summative assessments were conducted to measure student abilities and knowledge before, during, and after course participation. The implementation of ALT was also expected to improve feedback on student learning success, utilizing technology for interactive exercises with feedback loops in online tests. Furthermore, the project aimed to evaluate ALT and assess implications for future use of online and blended active learning strategies. 
During the implementation of the project, the following results were achieved: 
1.	A report analyzing the need for improving ALTONE quality based on research findings in partner countries and globally. 
2.	A desk analysis of reduced learning quality (decline in knowledge volume and learning loss). 
3.	Development of the ALT concept for online and hybrid environments. 
4.	Writing a handbook on transforming active learning from a classroom to an online environment. 
5.	Training teachers to apply active learning methodologies in online environments. 
6.	Training teachers to enhance competencies in ICT for more effective student engagement, better learning, and improved teaching monitoring, particularly in applied agricultural disciplines in higher education. 
7.	Selection of pilot subjects from different applied agricultural disciplines. 
8.	A training report for reviewing and evaluating pilot subject books based on necessary changes. 
9.	Redesigning pilot course books to ensure curricular coherence between objectives, ALT methods, student activities, assessment of student achievement, and learning outcomes. 
10.	Evaluation of revised pilot subject books. 
11.	Personalized teacher training, with each teacher working alongside ICT and teaching/learning quality experts to improve competencies in scenario preparation, selecting digital tools, and solving pedagogical challenges. 
12.	Creating scenarios for prototype classes in applied disciplines in online environments. 
13.	Evaluation of completed scenarios for ALTONE. 
14.	Creating scenarios for prototype classes in applied disciplines for hybrid learning, with a clear distinction between live and online activities. 
15.	Evaluation of completed scenarios for hybrid ALT. 
16.	Peer reviews of teacher satisfaction classes. 
17.	Development and establishment of Centers for continuous improvement of teaching and learning quality in higher education.

2021-1-SE01-KA220-HED-000023166.title: Blended Learning Implementation for reSilient, acceSsible and efficient higher education
2021-1-SE01-KA220-HED-000023166.summary:
<< Background >>

The onset of the Covid-19 pandemic necessitated swift adaptations in HE globally, revealing acute resource and accessibility gaps for students. Confronted with these challenges, HEIs struggled with the sudden shift to online education due to outdated technological infrastructures and a lack of expertise in digital teaching methods. This situation risked exacerbating socio-economic disparities, potentially degrading the educational experience.
In response, we launched the BLISS initiative to harness the potential of blended learning (BL)—a pedagogical approach that integrates online resources with traditional classroom interactions. This method had shown promise long before the pandemic and became critical under the constraints of reduced physical interactions and financial pressures on HEIs.
BLISS aimed to improve the resilience and efficiency of educational systems, increase learning flexibility, and expand access to quality education. By developing a structured framework and ready-to-use educational units based on BL, we addressed the pressing needs highlighted by the pandemic. This initiative leveraged the global shift towards blended learning, utilizing our collective experience from the initial response  to Covid-19.

<< Objectives >>

The BLISS initiative aimed to enhance the efficiency and resilience of higher education institutions (HEIs) while making learning more accessible and flexible for students. The project focused on two main objectives:
1. Design and implementation of tailored educational units for engineering curricula, drawing on the latest blended learning (BL) methodologies and experiences from the Covid-19 pandemic's impact on distance learning. Both areas have been thoroughly reviewed by the consortium.
2. Development of a methodological framework to support the strategic integration of BL into HE curricula, thereby increasing educational system efficiency and accessibility for students.
These objectives intended to produce comprehensive learning materials for immediate use within the consortium and a blueprint for broader BL adoption. This approach was designed to benefit learners by offering a wider range of courses, enabling learning at their own pace, and enhancing the teaching capabilities of faculty. Ultimately, the initiative sought to foster a collaborative educational environment, strengthen HEIs, and facilitate joint research and talent distribution across the Union.

<< Implementation >>

The BLISS initiative followed five key phases to meet its research goals: (1) **Initial Analysis**: A survey and internal reviews assessed HEIs' Covid-19 responses, focusing on online adoption, tools used, student impact, and staff workload. (2) **Literature Review**: A study of blended learning (BL) literature contextualized findings and highlighted effective strategies. (3) **Curricula Classification**: Engineering curricula were analyzed for BL potential, identifying elements for further development. (4) **Development of Educational Units**: Selected units were redesigned using constructive alignment to integrate BL strategies effectively. (5) **Evaluation and Adjustment**: Units were piloted and refined using learner feedback. Two key trainings supported the consortium—one on modern pedagogy (Constructive Alignment and BL), and another on exchanging developed units. The initiative also shared outcomes via publications, events, and practical contributions to the broader educational community.

<< Results >>

The BLISS initiative addressed key challenges through five main achievements: (1) **Covid-19 Impact Mapping**: Institutional documents and a standardized survey were analyzed, producing a research paper on blended learning (BL) adoption during the pandemic. (2) **BL Theory and Practice**: A literature review introduced the “level of understanding” concept to classify findings. Research diaries were synthesized, and a new curricular framework was developed and published. (3) **Development of Educational Units**: Promising units were identified, ranked, and developed by each partner with detailed documentation. (4) **Implementation and Evaluation**: Units were implemented and evaluated through student feedback, resulting in refinements to learning outcomes, teaching activities, and assessment. (5) **Cross-Application**: Units were shared among partners to identify context-specific challenges and adapt content accordingly. These results highlight BLISS’s impact in advancing blended learning and strengthening educational resilience across HEIs.

2021-1-SE01-KA220-HED-000027595.title: REsearch-based teaching for life-long LEARNing
2021-1-SE01-KA220-HED-000027595.summary:
<< Background >>

Research is a core pillar of higher education, and digital transformation is reshaping how research and education communicate. Online journals, open-access datasets, and platforms like Google Scholar and ResearchGate have revolutionized knowledge production and dissemination. However, the Covid-19 crisis accelerated the need for digital tools in education, highlighting the importance of technology in teaching and learning. RELEARN partners analyzed best practices from university research databases, teaching platforms, and national repositories, identifying key issues: the lack of comprehensive research systems for university staff and the public, outdated digital tools for teaching and distance learning, insufficient focus on media and information literacy, and a lack of digital competence for distance learning among educators and students. In response, RELEARN aims to provide a practical platform for accessing learning materials, courses, and research data, while enhancing key digital skills with online guidelines to support both teachers and students.

<< Objectives >>

RELEARN aims to create a platform that connects high-quality, trustworthy academic research with courses and learning materials, monitored by trained university staff. Its objectives are to: a) Develop a system that supports university libraries and online research databases, integrating research with teaching through AI components and user-monitored databases. This will contribute to a high-performing digital education ecosystem, enhancing infrastructure and connectivity in higher education. b) Aligning with the League of European Research Universities (LERU) principles, RELEARN emphasizes improving access to research data to enhance distance learning. The platform aims to ensure the online availability, traceability, and trustworthiness of research data and learning materials, linking them to university courses for better quality distance education. c) Promote virtual and blended cooperation among teachers, students, and researchers within and across European institutions, fostering collaboration to improve students' employability and connection to the labor market. d) Develop digital competencies in students and staff for effective online research and collaboration, leveraging digital tools and technologies. e) Encourage critic

<< Implementation >>

The RELEARN project created the IO1 Common Glossary and Report on Research-Based Study, the IO3 Student Module and Report on Research-Based Teaching, developed the RELEARN Platform, and organised multiplier and final dissemination events.



<< Results >>

The RELEARN project developed a comprehensive platform connecting academic research to courses and learning materials. Key outputs include the IO1 glossary, IO3 student modules, research reports, and relearn platform.

2021-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000027506.title: Product Hackathons for Innovative Development
2021-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000027506.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated to address the evolving needs in education and industry for more effective collaboration and innovation in product design and development. Based on previous successful collaborations among the partners (UL-FME, UZ-FSB, PoliMi and TUW), we have identified gaps in current educational methods, especially in preparing students for intensive work in digital, globalized engineering workplaces. Students often lack practical experience in industry-oriented projects and entrepreneurial skills, leaving them inadequately prepared for the demands of the market. At the same time, industry faces challenges of adapting to rapid technological change, embracing open innovation and collaborating with different stakeholders in digital environments.
To address these challenges, the project focused on introducing product hackathons as a of methodology and a series of examples to enhance university-industry collaboration. These hackathons, supported by digital collaboration tools, aim to foster innovation by involving students, faculty and companies in solving real-world industrial problems. This approach also facilitates skills development, strengthens employability and supports industry's adaptation to new business model.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to achieve two main objectives: to improve teaching and learning methods in engineering education and to foster collaboration between academia and industry through open innovation. To this end, the project introduced a novel methodology that integrates product hackathons as the founding elements of the product development process. These hackathons provided a platform for rapid ideation and problem solving, allowing students to work on real-world industrial challenges while developing skills relevant to the digital and globalized market.
The project also focused on identifying and adapting digital tools to support efficient collaboration in physical and virtual environments, overcoming geographical barriers to innovation. By adapting the hackathon format to the development of physical products, the project aimed to foster students' creativity and entrepreneurial skills while providing companies with access to innovative solutions from external participants.
In addition, three consecutive joint courses in the form of two online hackathons and one physical hackathon served as a testing ground for testing and refining the methodology to ensure it aligned with the evolving needs of education and industry.

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the ProHackin' project, a series of structured and methodological activities were carried out to achieve the project objectives. In particular, these activities aimed to develop and validate a methodology for conducting product hackathons to foster open innovation between universities and industry. The activities were carried out systematically over three years, each focusing on different but interconnected aspects of the project.
In the first year, the main focus was on formulating a baseline methodology for product hackathons. Extensive research was conducted to create a foundational framework that would integrate product hackathons into the product development process. In this phase we identified and evaluated suitable design methods and digital tools that can support intensive development tasks in both physical and virtual environments. All these activities resulted in PR1. In parallel, we found an industrial partner, Siemens, who provided an industrial development challenge for the engineering students to tackle, and conducted a series of hackathons based on the preliminary results and findings of PR1. The hackathons were tailored to the tasks of the industry project and the different stages of the design process, including ideation, conceptualization, and embodiment of the product. Together with PR1, these activities also led into PR2.
The second year focused on developing detailed guidelines for the delivery of product hackathons within university courses and curricula. These guidelines were designed to ensure adaptability to different educational environments. At the same time, best practices were compiled to support educators and organizations in the effective delivery of product hackathons. To validate these efforts, the methodology was tested and refined through new innovation tasks and their implementation in several university courses. This expanded application allowed for a comprehensive evaluation of the usability and effectiveness of the methodology and ensured that it is flexible enough to meet the diverse needs of education and industry. The activities of the second year thus resulted in PR3 and PR4.
In the third year, the focus shifted to the validation and dissemination of the developed methodology and guidelines. Practical applications and stakeholder feedback played a crucial role in this phase to ensure that the methodology was robust and applicable in a variety of contexts. Materials were produced and finalized to facilitate the adoption of the methodology by external organizations. The validation process included application of the product hackathon methodology regular curriculum and also through two multiplier events to secondary students on a summer school and to university students on an Erasmus exchange to UL-FME to apply the methodology to their use cases and provide feedback that was incorporated into the final project deliverables. These activities led directly to PR5 and PR6, as well as the finalization and updating of all previous PRs.
Throughout the project, joint product development courses were organized annually in collaboration with industry partners who provided design tasks for the innovation challenges. Each course was structured to include an introductory event to launch the innovation challenge, where the product hackathon was tested live or virtually, and a final event where students presented their developed product solutions. The live events also included transnational project meetings where the project staff analysed the results of the previous activities and worked on refining the project results.
The project also established a collaborative network among students, universities, and industrial companies. This network was instrumental in developing innovative solutions through teamwork and open innovation practices. By participating in the project-based courses, students acquired various skills, including entrepreneurship, teamwork, digital tools proficiency, and virtual communication.
Finally, dissemination of project results was consistently carried out throughout the project. These efforts targeted a wider audience of industry, academia and students, using four multiplier events and various communication channels to ensure the wide adoption of the developed methodology and best practices. These structured activities ensured the successful development, testing, and validation of a comprehensive methodology for product hackathons, enabling open innovation and enhancing collaboration between academia and industry.

<< Results >>

The ProHackin' project has successfully delivered a number of concrete outputs and results aligned with its objectives. Centre of the project was the development of a comprehensive methodology for conducting product hackathons tailored for both physical and virtual environments (PR1). This methodology addresses numerous design and organizational aspects, including the use of digital tools for problem solving, idea generation, solution visualization, and collaborative product design. It also includes organizational considerations such as the duration of the hackathon, the complexity of the tasks, the expected outcomes, and the evaluation methods.
The methodology was thoroughly validated through a series of case studies conducted in joint product development courses with students from partner universities and industry partners (PR2). These real-world applications provided invaluable insights and refinements that ensured the robustness and adaptability of the methodology to different contexts. The results of these validations were integrated in the creation of a manual to support teachers and institutions in implementing product hackathons effectively within academic curricula (PR3). This manual provides a step-by-step framework for organizing and running hackathons with the aim of improving learning outcomes and promoting innovative teaching methods.
The integration of hackathons into regular university courses was another important achievement of the project (PR4). The findings from the case studies were used to integrate innovative learning methods into regular academic courses. In addition, comprehensive guidelines were developed to support the implementation of product hackathons in different scenarios, including those in non-academic environments (PR5). These guidelines are designed to be adaptable and provide a flexible framework for different applications.
As part of its dissemination strategy, the project produced a compilation of best practices that showcase successful implementations of product hackathons (PR6). These examples serve as practical references for educators, industry professionals, and organizations seeking to pursue similar approaches. In addition, students and staff participating in the hackathons gained entrepreneurial skills, teamwork, and ICT skills. Other benefits included improved foreign language skills, improved digital competencies, increased student engagement and enhanced career development opportunities.
In addition to these six formal outcomes, the consortium produced an additional document explaining the implications of the project and the ProHackin’ methodology. All formal outcome documents (PR1-PR7) were translated into all languages of the project partners (Croatian, German, Italian and Slovenian) and published on the project website alongside the originals in English.
The project results were made available to a wide audience through scientific papers, presentations at conferences and multiplier events, as well as through materials published on the project website. These dissemination efforts ensure the wide availability of the project methods and practices so that they can be adopted by a wide range of stakeholders. In addition to these direct results, the project also led to various spin-off results such as twelve new industry solutions and several other concepts, at least four student theses and numerous publications in the (social) media.
Overall, the ProHackin' project has made a significant contribution to the advancement of engineering education by embedding innovative, collaborative and practical approaches in academic and professional development processes.
