2021-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000027622.title: Simulation of Sustainable International Business
2021-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000027622.summary:
<< Background >>

The Erasmus+ higher education cooperation project Simulation of Sustainable International Business (SOS IB) was implemented by 3 higher education institutions and the institute for corporate sustainability from Western Balcan. The project was the respond to the identified needs of partners’ institutions to enhance access to higher education internationalisation through the integration of digital solutions into teaching practices. 

Concretely, 2 partner HEIs faced challenges in internationalisation through physical mobility due to employed, family-oriented students and business-engaged lecturers. Their focus on accounting and finance further limited curriculum internationalisation due to national regulations. The third, a highly internationalised management-focused HEI, leveraged the project to enhance digital support for internationalization at home.

Based on above needs assesments, SOS IB project aimed to, and successfully established e-learning practices by employing innovative pedagogy and digital simulation in the field of sustainabile international business. The topic of sustainable international business was chosen based on its relevance for partner institutions and broader society.


<< Objectives >>

Pursuing its core aim, the SOS IB project successfully achieved all 10 objectives. The consortium:
(1) Designed, developed, and tested the SOS IB digital platform, enabling sustainable international business simulations and fostering collaboration among lecturers and students.
(2) Trained lecturers in digital simulations and innovative e-learning methods for international business.
(3) Trained teaching staff to integrate sustainability into the international business curriculum.
(4) Developed and tested simulation cases on sustainable international business for HE teaching.
(5) Created a methodological guide for integrating digital simulations, used in student training.
(6) Developed content for a mobile game on sustainable international business for distance learners.
(7) Designed and implemented the technological solution for the mobile game.
(8) Created and delivered daily training modules for lecturers using the digital simulation.
(9) Monitored, analyzed, and interpreted synergies, challenges, and best practices in digitalizing learning for internationalization in smaller HEIs.
(10) Disseminated project information, program details, and results per the dissemination strategy.

<< Implementation >>

SOS IB project’s activites were grouped in 5 working packages (WP): Management, Techological development, Content development, Trainings, and Disemination. 	

Within WP MANAGEMENT, the consortium implemented the preparatory activities (legal, administrative, infrastructural), administrative and financial management and monitoring, managed internal cooperation and communication, ensured quality monitoring of all activities and results development, organised and implemented transnational project meetings, internal evaluations, and took care of logistics and organisational aspects of other activities (trainings, multipliers, team meetings,..) along with the reporting.

Within WP TECHOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT, the consortium designed and technologically developed the digital platform for simulation of sustainable international business (SIB) in higher education and the mobile game for distant adult players, along with several rounds of testing, technological upgrades and improvements. 

Within WP CONTENT DEVELOPMENT, the consortium conducted a needs analysis on the integration of sustainability in teaching and business practices at the involved HEIs, developed 11 digital simulation cases on the topic of sustainable international business for higher education use, and the simulation content for the mobile game. Such content development relied on substantial research in various business areas and related sustainability practices, innovative pedagogy principles with the focus on e-learning, digital simulation, and extensive testing accros various groups that leaded to content improvements. This work package also included an impact case study analyzing the effects of the SOS IB e-learning practice on the internationalisation of the three participating higher education institutions.

Within WP TRAININGS, the consortium implemented a week-long international training for pedagogical staff and experts, produced online tutorials and guidelines for future users of the SOS IB e-learning practice (lecturers and students). These resources covered key areas such as e-learning with a focus on digital simulations in HE, storytelling, intercultural communication, and sustainability. Additionally, the consortium carried out 10 inter-/national training sessions and knowledge transfers to support the broader usage of SOS IB e-learning practice.

Within WP DISEMINATION, the consortium carried out dissemination and promotion activities, showcasing both the project and its results through various channels, events, and occasions, reaching diverse target audiences within and beyond the consortium. This work pachage contributed various promotional materials, project webpage in English and Slovenian, three promotional social media campaigns, and six multiplier events (2/6 were international, 5/6 covered results 1,2,3 (platform, simulation cases & game), and 1/6 covered result 4 (impact case study)). 


<< Results >>

THE SOS IB project produced 4 key RESULTS with the following outputs: 

RESULT 1: DIGITAL PLATFORM FOR SIMULATION OF SUSTAINABLE INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS with Privacy policy, Terms & conditions, Data Protection Impact Assessment, lecturers’ & students’ surveys.
RESULT 2: 11 SIMULATED CASES OF SUSTAINABLE INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS with summaries of all cases, international training programme & materials (PPTs, videos, photos) on e-learning, innovative pedagogy & simulations in HE, storytelling, European Green Deal, needs analysis about state of addressing sustainability in consortium HEIs, 10 inter-/national trainings & knowledge transfers with recordings, PPTs & photos, 2 content variantions for 2 of final simulation cases & 1 preliminary case, assessment rubric, students certificates, list of films on sustainability, guides (videos, PPTs) with navigation maps for lecturers & students (on simulations, sustainability, technical instructions, grading, intercultural communication, storytelling) in English and (partially) Slovenian (see also Annex 1)
RESULT 3: MOBILE GAME ABOUT SUSTAINABLE INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS with 5 content variations & around 300 ballance sheets & income statements, 11 final outcomes table, sustainability & profitability index calculations at each level of the decission tree, survey for players (see also Annex 2)
RESULT 4: CASE STUDY ON E-LEARNING AS A DRIVER OF INTERNATIONALISATION IN HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS with datasets (2 bibliometrical, 1 baseline measurement & 1 student survey dataset), qualitative data from interviews & focus group (18 interviews recordings, transcriptions, translations & 18 anonymised versions for coding, 4 coding tables with instructions & 24 filled in coding tables, focus group recording), to all data connected (partial) analyses with graphs, etc., literature review spreadsheet, leaflet with summary of key findings with dedicated infographics in English, Slovenian, Bolgarian.

The SOS IB project has moreover contributed to other outputs (promotional brouchures & leaflet, images & videos for social media campaigns, project websites in English & Slovenian, photos, video recordings, agendas, PPT presenations, etc.) through its dissemination and monitoring activites, as well as at transnational project meetings.

2021-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000032006.title: ACTIVE AND INCLUSIVE TEACHING OF LITERACY AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS FOR ENHANCED EMPLOYMENT AND SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC GROWTH
2021-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000032006.summary:
<< Background >>

The partnership for this project was formed to create innovative state-of-the-art curricula for teaching communication skills that are significant in all areas of our lives - from personal development to progress in business and economic growth. Such curricula (for BA and MA levels) could contribute to higher quality of HEI (upgrade of teaching), improved inclusion of students with less possibillities and of impaired students, and to more successful students, who will become successful professionals contributing to a better, more understanding and sustainable economy. The innovation of the proposed communication skills curricula is in combining of travel writing, movement, reading, rhetorical skills and intercultural communication and non-verbal communication (signing). Significant emphasis is on digitalisation, inclusion and individual's responsibility for their own health and healthy way of living. The main idea of this Erasmus+ project was to raise awareness about students with lesser opportunities, help them and increase awareness about the challenges they are facing, and develop and offer communication skills curricula for students so that they will become more responsible and more successful in inclusion on the job market.

<< Objectives >>

 Raising awareness about specific needs of students in communication, the importance of knowledge of students’ diversity and the significance of inclusion is one of project’s top goals. One of the objectives was developing literacy and communication skills through combining travel writing and movement, our next goal was to develop communication skills curricula by employing knowledge about sign languages for online/classroom communication skills courses. Due to specific rules in sign communication, we included non-verbal communication in general and raising awareness about specifics of sign languages. Our next goal was enhancing writing skills as the core of successful education and business, and if they are developed and enhanced successfully, this is beneficial for the overall development of the communities, especially underprivileged rural communities. Our goals were also to further develop reading, writing, social, digital and intercultural skills, to create a partnership that will be inclusive and disseminate the results of the project successfully on the local, regional, national and international levels; to support teachers and students of HEI. Focus was on the creation of flexible, creative and active learning paths.

<< Implementation >>

The IN-COMM GUIDE project used a result-oriented methodology to prepare and develop state-of-the-art communications skills curricula and guidelines for higher education institutions and business industry. As the project application reviewers suggested, the project team joined the method guides, proposed in the project application, into two guidelines, one for the BA level and the second one for the MA level. Thus, the practical results are as follows: BA curriculum (6 ECTS); MA curriculum (6 ECTS); METHOD GUIDE AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS CURRICULUM GUIDANCE TOOL_BACHELOR level for BACHELOR study programms and students (may be employed for the industry as well); METHOD GUIDE AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS CURRICULUM GUIDANCE TOOL MASTER level for master study programmes and students; the scientific monograph ACTIVE AND INCLUSIVE TEACHING OF LITERACY AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS FOR ENHANCED EMPLOYMENT AND SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC GROWTH, published with the University of Maribor Publishing House; and Travel Writing teaching pack. Additionally, the project team organized and delivered face-to face, field and online testing teachings, worked with various stakeholders (associations, companies, individuals etc.) and established new partnerships or upgraded the existing ones; organized and successfully completed project meetings (online, face-to-face, hybrid), meetings with associations and stakeholders, presented the project, objectives and results at home, abroad, to students, administrative and teaching staff, intensively promote the project and delivered dissemination activities at different levels, carried out analyses, developed and carried out research, bring results into practice, work with local associations and local communities, participated in conferences and scientific events, read, write, translate, teach, publish research results, evaluate, prepare media newsletters, participate in media interviews, write not only teaching materials and research publications, but also promotional texts, created videos and other teaching, research and dissemination materials. Further on, the project team organized face-to-face and online workshops and a successful multiplier event with participants from partner countries and abroad. Dissemination activities at the local, national and international levels took place from the beginning of the project and they still continue. Project was promoted also in social media. Project Facebook profile (Inclusive Teaching Guide) has had more than 60 posts and the website of the project was established. For promotional purposes also the EPALE platform has been used. The objectives were achieved jointly in several monitored stages/phases of the project as follows: Within the project activities the partners jointly attended meetings, discussed challenges, did research work, developed and prepared BA and MA guidelines focused on communication skills for various educational and business purposes. The first step involved developing a common methodology of research; secondly, the project units analysed existent curricula and developed curricula for communication skills modules (BA and MA levels); thirdly, the developed curricula was uploaded to open-access websites. The development steps of the project included research, analysis, a testing phase, where the target and control groups were involved by employing testing teachings. All stages of the project were monitored, evaluated, partial results were disseminated at conferences, at HEI (students, teachers, administrative staff) and also the overall project results were disseminated. Based on the comments of the project application reviewers, project results PR1, PR2, PR3 and PR 4 and corresponding activities were joined and partners worked together on all project results. According to the proposed project results (PR), the following activities took place: The preparation of a common methodology that was used for developing curricula and innovative methodology based on travel writing and movement employing non-verbal communication. By developing methods and guidelines for inclusion of non-verbal communication and raising awareness about sign languages, we wished to raise awareness about challenges of communication of some specific groups, for example the Deaf,  increase the possibilities for inclusion of students with hearing and other impairments and consequently to enhance performance of students with hearing impairments (the focus is on teaching students and staff with no impairments to acquire knowledge about specifics of sign language and to become more aware of the needs and challenges of students with impairments). Teaching and learning was based on the communicative approach to learning the English language as lingua franca, the focus was on learning rhetoric skills, reading, health, movement and travel writing in connection to innovative methods, inclusion, digitalisation and sustainability. The project team worked and developed the curricula and the guidelines in cooperation with the Association of Disabled Students of Slovenia, with the Association of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing of Ljubljana and Slovenia, and with the Association of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing of Maribor. Further on, the project team worked with a member of the Deaf community in Zwickau, with various business associations, business company representatives, HEI teaching and administrative staff, with students and with esteemed professionals and professors from partner countries and elsewhere.
Because the project team wanted students to increase their intercultural communication skills as well as broaden their understanding of inclusion and social diversity, project researchers  carried out thorough background research (data collection, analysis of curricula and available methodologies, non-verbal communication inclusion and raising awareness about sign languages),  they developed and wrote method guidelines for modules for BA and MA (6 ECTS, 2 semesters, 2 contact hours a week),  essential part of the project activities was quality control,  they employed raising awareness about essential elements of the local sign language to break communication barriers and contribute establishing a basic workplace communication with Deaf and Hard-of-hearing individuals, organized and actively participated in meetings with the Associations of Deaf and hard of hearing; meetings with the Association of students with impairments; actively participated in discussions, evaluation processes,  prepared, designed, translated, proofread various types of texts, organize and deliver dissemination & promotion activities,  actively participated in dissermination activities. All project partners cooperated in the preparation of curricula for targeted groups (preparation of a common methodology employing travel writing, movement, nonverbal communication, choosing topics on inclusion, sustainability, digitalisation etc.); project researchers collected and created teaching materials, focusing on topics for developing communication skills,  they developing curricula contents for BA and MA modules, provided IT support, created contents for the website, social and other media and prepared newsletters,  organized and delivered testing teachings, evaluated testing teachinf, wrote abstracts and papers, published abstracts, papers and other relevant project materials,  wrote and prepare texts for the scientific monograph, disseminated project objectives, activities and results, promoted the project through various channels and media, had meetings with associations, stakeholders and experts;  tested curricula in targeted groups, gathered feedback, organized evaluation meetings, collected and developed teaching materials, focused on topics regarding inclusion, health, diversity, sustainability; organized and delivered teaching & workshops; -upgraded curricula and guidelines, created new networks with universities and businesses/stakeholders, associations, disseminated the results & promoted activities; used the curricula developed, finalised curricul and other materials, organized the reviewing, upgrading  and publishing processes  of curricula, guidelines and  e-monograph (scientific monograph), –organized dissemination activities. BA and MA curricula, BA and MA Guidelines s and the e-monograph were reviewed by at least 2 independent reviewers.


<< Results >>

Starting with the concrete outputs and results of the project, the following needs to be emphasised:  BA curriculum for further developing communication skills (6 ECTS); MA curriculum for further developing communication skills (6 ECTS); METHOD GUIDE AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS CURRICULUM GUIDANCE TOOL_BACHELOR level for BACHELOR study programms and students, METHOD GUIDE AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS CURRICULUM GUIDANCE TOOL _MASTER level for master study programmes and students; the scientific monograph ACTIVE AND INCLUSIVE TEACHING OF LITERACY AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS FOR ENHANCED EMPLOYMENT AND SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC GROWTH, published with the University of Maribor Publishing House; and Travel Writing teaching pack. Further on, the project has significantly contributed to raising awareness about the importance of communication skills and to an understanding that individuals have different needs and that many have various limitations in communication. Therefore, awareness of diversity in communication is crucial. The project team considers it a success that the team not only collaborated with the associated partner, the Association of Students with Disabilities in Slovenia but also managed to connect with the Association of Deaf and Hard of Hearing in Slovenia and the Association of Deaf and Hard of Hearing in Maribor. All mentioned associations informed us about the challenges their members face, provided advice in planning project activities, and evaluated them. They all played a crucial role in developing inclusivity in communication during the process of curricula and modules development.
At the same time, the project team, along with partners from abroad, shared knowledge, experiences, and examples of good practices in inclusion from other countries with the associated partners. A strong collaboration was established between the project team, associated partners, and other participating stakeholders (experts of various fields, Association of Regional Tour Guides of Slovenia - ARGOS, university professors etc.). This collaboration will be maintained in the future. The Association of Disabled Students of Slovenia and the Association of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing Associations of Slovenia and the coordinator will continue cooperation through regular meetings, occurring once or twice a year, and mutual assistance. The Association of Disabled Students of Slovenia will be actively participating in ensuring better inclusion of disabled students enrolled at the University of Maribor.

Further on, the project team believes that the project activities and results significantly contributed to the raised awareness about the significance of teaching communication skills in higher education and through various teaching activities to the enhancement of communication skills at higher education institutions. The project also contributed to understanding the importance of inclusion of students with hearing impairments, to promotion of sign languages, to improved quality of teaching, to improved understanding among different groups of students. Besides that the developed communication skills modules are open to students from all European countries. Project’s results and activities were presented not only within the University of Maribor network, but also new partnerships were created through the project, knowledge and creativity were shared, and new opportunities created across Europe. Therefore sustainability of the project has been achieved through developing further national and international networks with HEI (Manchester University, University of Perugia, University of Algarve etc.), business sector stakeholders (Travel Writers Online, IBE d. o. o., AFP d. o. o., Elektro Ljubljana, Tourist farm Pomona, Rogaška Slatina Glassworks) and local community representatives (Association of Deaf and Hard of Hearing in Slovenia and the Association of Deaf and Hard of Hearing in Maribor) through the preparation of teaching sessions and workshops for targeted groups and through various dissemination activities, meetings, publications and open access materials. With the proposed curricula, which has the potential to become part of study programmes, to Slovenia this project brings much needed good foundations for further development of teaching and learning communication skills through innovative and inclusive methods that will also promote health and healthy lifestyle. Besides improvement of communication skills that will lead to enhanced literacy, personal growth, improved competencies, better employment possibilities, critical thinking and economic growth, the project will contribute to better cooperation with local communities, interested associations, HEI policy-makers and quality-assessment bodies. These positive impacts are expected also in partnership countries as well as beyond our partnership on the European and global levels. The knowledge and results from this project will be shared further not only through developed modules that will be part of study programmes but also through dissemination of results on conferences, symposiums etc. After the end of the project the developed curricula will further be monitored and evaluated, and thus, the curricula will be further tailored and developed according to the needs of specific groups. Namely, the curricula will is designed in such ways that their further tailoring in various directions is  possible. Besides curricula for BA and MA modules, BA Guidelines and MA Guidelines, e- scientific monograph is available. The latter offers deeper insights into teaching communication skills, inclusion, digitalization and some of the project challenges.

2021-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000032218.title: Better Employability for Everyone with APEX
2021-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000032218.summary:
<< Background >>

The IT sector in the EU is one of the fastest growing ones, and more importantly, it is one of the key sectors central to building a green, digital and resilient economy. The demand for developers in the EU has registered a continuous annual increase, a trend explicit across all EU member states. Preliminary research carried out by the project consortium indicated that growing up with ICT is not enough to develop the digital skills necessary for the digital economy, and that ICT curricula (even basic level courses) offered to non-ICT majors should be revised in order to better prepare future graduates for the needs of a digital workplace. Low-code software is software that can be fully customized with a minimal amount of programming. Low-code development still requires some basic programming skills, but it is faster, cheaper, and easier to learn. This project was formed to support the digital transformation of HE, strenghten the resilience and capacity of educators and students, to modernize the IT curricula, to offer non-technical majors with opportunities to advance their IT knowledge and employability and fill in the gap between the demand and supply of IT developers.

<< Objectives >>

The project was aimed to align higher education with market demands by involving employers in course design, enhancing digital skills, and fostering employability. It addressed curriculum gaps by engaging with Oracle and local SMEs to develop IT courses, improving educators' and students' digital competencies. The focus was on expanding IT training to non-technical students and integrating digital readiness across disciplines. By creating new courses through business-academic partnerships and emphasizing low-code programming, the project’s objective was to  accelerate curriculum updates and boost student employability. This collaborative approach would bring benefits to local businesses by providing a skilled workforce, fostering productivity, and driving economic growth. Higher education institutions (academic stuff and students) would get learning materials for courses in 7 languages.

<< Implementation >>

Project teams developed the advanced and the short digital course on low-code programming introducing students to the foundations of APEX and basic application and database design. Endeavor included gathering, organizing, adjusting and integrating business cases into learning material. Advanced and short course was either accredited or integrated into existing courses. Learning materials was prepared in 7 languages – English and in 6 languages of the project consortium. Each e-book has more than 400 pages supported by Q&A, source code of applications, scripts, and video tutorials. The courses were implemented in Moodle LMS, the backups are offered in open access to any interested HE. Two flavors of short course were assembled to meet two common situations. The testing and piloting the courses was conducted in all project partners institutions. To get students better insight into labor market eight webinars are provided on Youtube. LTTA and all ME among target groups were conducted. By the end of the project eighteen articles were written, presented in different international conferences and published in corresponding proceedings.

2021-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000035825.title: DIDAKTIČNO-DIGITALNO ORODJE ZA USPOSABLJANJE IZ PRAKTIČNIH VSEBIN
2021-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000035825.summary:
<< Background >>

The pandemic has posed challenges to practical education, particularly in agriculture and horticulture. This project aimed to develop, implement and evaluate an innovative online training programme, free of charge to users. It aimed to reinforce trainers' professional development, integrate their knowledge, skills and competencies into their teaching and enhance students' and other stakeholders' professional and pedagogical competencies. 
The project aimed to:
- Promote education that is accessible at any time and in any location;
- Provide training for teachers and trainers in the effective online delivery of practical content;
- Increase teaching flexibility;
- Make distance learning accessible to all learners (especially students, but also external users), including those from vulnerable groups;
- Ensure the sustainability and use of the project results for other stakeholders, including adults engaged in lifelong learning and vulnerable groups.

<< Objectives >>

The project's objectives include enabling distance learning for all students, increasing the flexibility of practical training and improving the pedagogical and digital competences of tutors and students. The project aimed to create an effective tool for distance learning of practical content, with a particular focus on different forms of collaborative learning between all participants in the learning process: lecturer, tutor, student, as well as adults involved in lifelong learning and vulnerable groups. As the content is practical, we have used a lot of visual and audio effects to achieve the best possible impact. We have included a variety of digital assessment tools and the telephone as a tool that we all use frequently.

<< Implementation >>

In order to adapt to the changes in the workplace brought about by digitalisation, lifelong learning is a necessity. Furthermore, the DIGIAGRI project has facilitated the digitisation of practice to a certain extent. The project was undertaken in collaboration with four partners from Spain, Croatia and Slovenia. 
The project is structured into two distinct levels: intellectual outputs and transversal activities. The project has yielded five intellectual outputs, which are presented in detail below. The activities were linked to the collaboration with partners, students, teachers and mentors of vulnerable groups. Additionally, a multiplier event was organised, which involved representatives of the local community, school management, political decision-makers, employers, development agencies, pensioners' associations, people's universities, gardeners, teachers and mentors of practical classes in schools with biotechnical content, and mentors of gardening circles. The project also encompassed cross-cutting activities, including project management and implementation, project monitoring and evaluation, and the dissemination of project results. The dissemination of the project's findings included active participation in print media, social networks, professional and scientific conferences, and the production of a promotional video for the VITRAŽ conference.

<< Results >>

The project has developed the following five results.
1: Analysis of the state of the existing tools, environments and applications for distance education with case studies (in English and Slovenian), including an analysis of different distance education resources, a collection of online courses to support distance education lecturers, contemporary pedagogical-didactic approaches, principles and challenges of distance education, case studies of digital tools/applications, a SWOT analysis, an analysis of questionnaires, an analysis of interviews and a selection of tools for working in a digital environment. Case studies of European good practices in digital agricultural education have been added. In order to disseminate and strengthen pedagogical competences, we have also presented several papers with pedagogical/didactic content related to digital environments at different conferences (Quality in Higher Education, When I Teach, I Build, EduIzziv and Creative Learning Environments).

2: Proposing the curriculum of the online training course "e-learning for practical teaching" and preparing the expert guides (in English, Spanish, Croatian and Slovenian). The curriculum has been prepared for tomato, pepper and viticulture) and a document containing the introduction to the curriculum for the training course "Vegetable Growing", the descriptions of the units for the three modules: tomato growing, pepper growing, vine growing. Each module contains the general objectives, the duration, the target groups, who can teach the course, the elements of assessment, a list and description of the teaching units. The unit syllabus contains general information, objectives and learning outcomes and references. Guidelines for mentors/lecturers are added.

3: The e-application for both teaching and self-study is available at https://digiagri.miteam.si, to register you must follow the instructions given. A personalised learning platform has been developed in order to - the entire learning process (planning, implementation, assessment, evaluation) - LMS environment for managing organised forms of education, learning paths, assessments, tests, assignments, certificates. The W-application is partly in Slovenian, partly in English, the instructions are also in Spanish and Croatian. The platform is interactive and allows to reach different taxonomic levels and social learning, with instructions and immediate feedback. 
The tasks are designed on three levels: 1. reproduction of theory in the form of quizzes; 2. calculation tasks; 3. practical work (home experiments, uploading photos and videos, critical evaluation, comments). The DIGIAGRI e-application consists of two workspaces: an internal one (DIGIAGRI Students and DIGIAGRI Community) and a public one (DIGIAGRI Public). The internal workspace contains collaborative and educational working groups and other tools such as a content library, member list, publications and other collaborative tools, but is only accessible to registered users. The public workspace is also accessible to anonymous, non-registered users.
Evaluations of the platform have been carried out and improvements have been made based on feedback.

4: Development of e-materials and production of an online interactive  (in English, Spanish, Croatian and Slovenian). The materials has been produced on the MITEAM platform (https://digiagri.miteam.si/). The materials on tomato, pepper and grapevine production are freely available as an example of a practical training format. Some horticultural articles have been published in the magazine My countryside, and tips for gardeners have been published in Kranjčanka and Slogine novice with the aim of improving self-sufficiency. Some of the material is designed as 'easy reading' for vulnerable groups. This approach is suitable for students with learning difficulties, as well as for students from more remote areas and socially disadvantaged backgrounds, which was also welcomed from an inclusion perspective.

5: Examples of e-learning plans and their implementation (in the field) and evaluation in practice. Online training for mentors was developed with chapters on Who is a Mentor, Mentoring in an Online Environment, Mentoring Vulnerable Groups. Multiplier events took place in all three partner countries.

2021-2-NL01-KA220-HED-000048818.title: Enhancing Volunteer Impact - Developing European Management Standards
2021-2-NL01-KA220-HED-000048818.summary:
<< Background >>

Europe needs well trained volunteer managers to properly harness the vast potential of volunteering impact but lacks quality ‘volunteer management courses’ at the HE level. There are also big gaps and needs in terms of recognition of volunteer managers as a profession and in general. That’s why the common action was needed to gather relevant experiences, expertise and skills to collaborate to produce HE learning opportunities (modules) and associated learning resources that can serve to properly train and accredit voluntary managers with qualifications that are given against European standards and reflect European values. PR1 – the state of the art report, which examined the current state of HE and other educational offerings for volunteer managers laid out how across Europe this offering is nearly completely lacking. Confirming the vision on the matter that existed before starting the project. Additionally, the aim was to develop some needed practical guides for volunteer managers.

<< Objectives >>

For one, to gain a greater understanding of the current situation regarding the training and qualifications currently available to existing and potential volunteer managers. Then, with this increased understanding, the partners aimed to develop a HE master level programme and associated resources that increase the opportunities for the partners and stakeholders to increase the opportunities across Europe for existing and future volunteer managers to be properly trained at HE level and receive a recognised qualification based on common European standards for volunteer management education. This will serve to ensure that volunteers across Europe are managed effectively and in a more ethical way, avoiding exploitation, instrumentalisation and job substitution. It will also increase the capacity of communities in general regarding disaster prevention, preparedness and recovery through having better trained and qualified volunteer managers and increase the diversity and inclusivity in the volunteering sector with better trained and qualified volunteer managers able to assess the inclusiveness of the organisations where they are active and develop, manage and follow up on plans and strategies to mitigate risks of lack of inclusivity.

<< Implementation >>

The Project Handbook was developed in order to provide a shared and clear vision for the project partners and to monitor the implementation of the project against the specified objectives. This has supported the management of contractual obligations related to the project including the management of the finances of the project. Evaluation of the quality management process concerning communication and cooperation, methods applied, progress of the output delivery and the project impact on target groups was conducted, and interim and final reports have been produced. The transnational project meetings have been held to ensure shared understanding concerning the objectives and activities of the project and give the space for any necessary adjustments to be made. Monthly meetings have been held throughout the project, to keep production on track and to address any concerns immediately. Two sessions with a European programme committee (created for this project consisting of experts from each partner country) were held to gain outside feedback on the material created for PR2. A training event was held in Lithuania where invited university lectures, teachers and other experts from practice were invited to provide input, co-create and provide feedback to the PR2 material. Each partner has held a multiplier event in their respective countries.

<< Results >>

PR1: State of the Art report about Volunteer Management in Europe was produced where the current state of affairs around formal and informal educational offerings was examined in various countries including those inside but also outside of the consortium.
PR2: The project has produced a one-year (60 ECTS) pre-experience educational programme at masters level for volunteer managers. It consists of four modules (15 ECTS each) at the 1) individual- 2) organizational- 3) societal- 4) and professional levels. Each module contains 3 courses that can be taken together or individually by interested candidates. Each module has three underlying documents: 1) a Course Manual, including syllabus 2) an assessment plan and 3) a slide deck for lecturers to support lectures. These slide decks were not promised in the original proposal and developed additionally. On top of that, an overview presentation, a literature overview, an introductory document a.o. including programme learning objectives and minor programme suggestions and a learning objective overview were also created on top of what was written in the proposal. PR4 – 6 are guides created to support the master programme courses but are also valuable resources for those in practice already. They provide insight and practical value on their respective topics. These are: PR3: a “European Code of Ethics for Volunteer Managers”, PR4 a “Guide to Volunteering, Solidarity and European Values” PR5: a “Guide on the role of volunteer managers in facilitating inclusive volunteering” and PR6 a “Guide to managing volunteers contributing to disaster prevention, preparedness and recovery”. This common curriculum, available to any interested Higher Education institution in Europe, EVI-DEMS promotes Inter-connected Higher Education Systems. All of this concretely results in 45 highly coherent, cohesive and qualitative documents.
As PR1 showed, the EVI-DEMS Master Programme is the first of its kind, it provides something truly novel and is an important landmark in the development of volunteer management as a profession. Through having a more prepared higher education sector with the tools and materials to better meet the training needs of current and future volunteer managers the volunteer sector in Europe will become stronger and the volunteer-involving organisations will be more enabled to better argue for the professional recognition of volunteer managers in those countries where it is not currently possible in Europe.
Further outcomes to this newly available volunteer manager training and qualification will be seen in increased sustainability of volunteer organisations assisting them to enlarge the outreach and capacity building of their networks staff and expertise in supporting quality training and qualifications for volunteer managers. The project will also support organisations to exchange good practices in the field of education to increase the effectiveness of volunteers through better volunteer management expertise.

2022-1-BE02-KA220-HED-000088974.title: Simulation-based learning in occupational therapy
2022-1-BE02-KA220-HED-000088974.summary:
<< Background >>

The project addresses a critical gap in occupational therapy (OT) education: preparing students to acquire essential professional competencies for complex and diverse healthcare systems despite limited practice placements. These constraints hinder progression from theoretical knowledge (“knows/knows how”) to practical application (“shows how/does”), as described by Miller’s pyramid (1990). OT programs often lack sufficient and varied placements, reducing exposure to diverse populations and rare cases such as spinal cord injuries. This limitation affects students’ readiness for professional practice and, ultimately, the quality and safety of patient care. Traditional approaches cannot fully develop competencies such as critical thinking, decision-making, and cultural awareness. Simulation-based learning (SBL), widely adopted in nursing and medicine, offers authentic, safe environments to bridge this gap. However, OT lacks guidelines and evidence-based practices for SBL, as its focus on daily activities and participation differs from other professions. The SIMBA project was designed to integrate SBL into OT curricula, enhancing preparedness and ensuring novice occupational therapists deliver high-quality care across contexts.

<< Objectives >>

The SIMBA project aimed to integrate simulation-based learning (SBL) into all stages of occupational therapy (OT) education across five partner institutions, supported by evidence-based practice. Its purpose was to introduce SBL as an innovative method for teaching, learning, and assessing OT competences, ensuring that students gain the skills and confidence required for a smooth transition into professional practice and actively engage in their learning. In the long term, the project seeks to enhance the quality, safety, and effectiveness of OT services through authentic, inclusive, and innovative methodologies. To achieve this, SIMBA set three main objectives: first, to develop a competence framework and SBL guidelines; second, to design and integrate a valid and reliable SBL assessment tool; and third, to create practical resources such as a structured scenario template, hands-on and digital case-based scenarios, a teacher instruction manual, and an open-access web platform for learning and dissemination. These objectives align with Erasmus+ priorities by promoting innovative teaching and learning practices, fostering diversity and inclusion, and combining hands-on and digital approaches to strengthen OT education in Europe.

<< Implementation >>

All planned activities were successfully implemented across the four work packages (WP). WP1 focused on project management, including financial and time planning, coordination of tasks, and monitoring through an internal commission for project management and progress evaluation, as well as an external commission for methodology and quality assurance. WP2 delivered the Competency Framework and Implementation Guidelines for integrating simulation-based learning (SBL) into occupational therapy education. WP3 involved creating and applying a valid and reliable SBL assessment tool, supported by a guiding manual and documents for tracking student competency growth. WP4 concentrated on resource development, including a structured scenario template, 15 hands-on and 15 digital occupational therapy scenarios for different stages of education, and a comprehensive teacher manual for scenario design and implementation. Additionally, WP4 produced a validated open-access web platform hosting all resources and linked to a dedicated LinkedIn group to foster ongoing exchange of experiences and good practices among educators and students in occupational therapy and allied health professions.

<< Results >>

Key learning resources were developed to support teachers in designing and implementing simulation-based learning (SBL) in occupational therapy education. These include the Competency Framework and Implementation Guidelines (e-book) supported by a guiding webinar series, a validated SBL assessment tool (SimOT Compass) for formative and summative evaluation, accompanied by a manual and supporting documents to monitor student competency growth. Two structured scenario templates were created, along with 15 hands-on and 15 digital occupational therapy scenarios addressing different professional competencies across various stages of education, and a comprehensive teacher manual for scenario design and implementation. Except for the Competency Framework and Guidelines, all resources are available in English, Croatian, Dutch, Finnish, German, and Turkish. 

For dissemination, an open-access web platform was launched, hosting all resources and complemented by blog posts, activity reports, presentations (inter)national conferences, and peer-reviewed publications. 

For collaboration, a dedicated LinkedIn group was established to foster ongoing exchange of experiences and good practices among educators and students.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-BG01-KA220-HED-000089080.title: Introducing Sustainability and Energy Efficiency Principles in Architectural Education: Towards Designing Climate Neutral and Inclusive Buildings
2022-1-BG01-KA220-HED-000089080.summary:
<< Background >>

In implementing the INCEPT project, the participating universities begin with the understanding that architectural education plays a fundamental role in achieving a sustainable built environment by preparing future professionals who can integrate sustainability into their practice. Moreover, in order to envision a sustainable climate neutral built environment, it covers a fundamental understanding of the link between sustainability, technology and design. The project aims to develop and implement forward-looking upgrade of architectural education curricula within the existing Master of Architecture programmes at the participating universities based on the understanding of the utmost need to establish a balanced integration of creativity and sustainability approaches. The starting point for the initiation of the INCEPT  Project is  the awareness of the critical need to align the Master of Architecture curricula  with the contemporary requirements for sustainability and  radical  energy performance improvements of the built environment. The project is also driven by the understanding of the strong relation between architectural education and the profession itself.


<< Objectives >>

As main objective INCEPT Project was to develop, validate and implement a curricula on sustainable architecture within the Master of Architecture programmes at the participating universities. This curricula was designed to provide knowledge and build digital and green skills of architecture students on the major principles of sustainability and energy efficiency in the design of different building typologies. In addition to its main objective, the project aimed to achieve the following specific goals:

- Enhance the knowledge of architecture students on key energy efficiency principles across the entire building life cycle, addressing both operational and embodied carbon as well as advanced climate smart, energy efficient and inclusive building design.
- Train architecture students in designing more energy efficient, less carbon intensive and more sustainable buildings in the wider multi-faceted urban context allowing room for creativity and aesthetic decisions.
- Validate and implement the newly developed educational curricula and design studio on sustainable architecture for architecture students.
- Establish a digital educational platform to support e-learning and facilitate inter-university knowledge exchange.


<< Implementation >>

The project enhanced the educational curricula within the Master of Architecture programmes at the participating universities by developing and validating the INCEPT Compendium, Design Atelier and Training Course as key intellectual outputs. It was focused on advancing the quality of architectural education in line with the high academic standards also set by the European Association of Architectural education. The implementation of the Design Atelier was developed to test low- and zero-energy design concepts and tools as part of an experience-based training in a "living lab" ecosystem.

INCEPT also created and operated a digital educational platform to support e-learning and inter-university knowledge exchange.

The dissemination and exploitation of the project outputs at inter-university, national and EU level strengthened the impact and transferability of the results. Within INCEPT the dissemination and exploitation of project outputs and results was ensured at inter-university, national and EU level. Communication and dissemination activities were designed to reach a broad spectrum of target groups - from architecture students to energy efficiency and sustainability experts, as well as professional organisations.


<< Results >>

The INCEPT project successfully developed and validated the following key intellectual outputs:

1) a Compendium on the Green Transition to Affordable and Clean Energy in Buildings, Sustainable Cities and Climate Resilience for Architecture Students and compendium-related lecture course,
2) a Climate Neutral Building Design Atelier for Architecture Students, and
3) an Online Training Course on Sustainable Architecture.

The project established and tested a digital educational platform for e-learning, enabling the delivery of online courses on sustainable architecture to the wider professional community.

In addition, the project created the INCEPT Community on Zenodo – EU Open Research Repository – serving as the main digital platform for disseminating and ensuring the transferability of the project’s final intellectual outputs to the broader academic community at the EU level.

The project team participated in more than 20 specialised events at both national and EU levels, further strengthening the project’s impact.

Throughout the project, the initial consortium evolved into a strong team of academic educators and researchers, thereby strengthening inter-university collaboration in the long run.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-CZ01-KA220-HED-000085765.title: Research into representations of intercultural contacts in Czech travelogue texts from the Mediterranean up to 1918, using digital humanities
2022-1-CZ01-KA220-HED-000085765.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to compile an international interdisciplinary team (affiliating experts in literary culture, digital mapping, digitisation of written sources, linguists, geographers and GIS specialists), which will focus on the study of representations of intercultural contacts in Czech travelogues from the Mediterranean from the 15th century to 1918, and create an innovative and prototypical digital humanities tool for obtaining and presenting data on intercultural contact from such texts.

<< Implementation >>

1) heuristic activity leading to creation of a body of travelogue texts, 2) digitisation of texts and creation of a digital library, 3) plotting of routes of journeys on digital maps, 4) determination of key themes for study of representations of intercultural contact in travelogues, 5) creation of an atlas from digital maps with routes, 6) connection of digital atlas with digital library via key themes, 7) provision of online access to tool and its presentation, 8) use of tool for education.

<< Results >>

The main project outcome will be a multi-thematic atlas accessible online, connected via themes focusing on intercultural contact with a digital library consisting of the selected body of travelogues - DIGEOCAT & Lib.
Other outcomes will use the created digital humanities tool, capable of processing a large volume of data: academic studies, specialised maps, reports and other dissemination activities essential for presenting the usability of the tool in education and research.

2022-1-CZ01-KA220-HED-000088039.title: Transdisciplinary Approaches to Archaeological Heritage
2022-1-CZ01-KA220-HED-000088039.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was submitted in response to the growing need for innovative and transdisciplinary approaches in the field of archaeological and cultural heritage management. Higher education curricula in this area remained largely compartmentalised, while professional practice increasingly required the ability to combine humanities-based theoretical knowledge with practical fieldwork, laboratory methods, digital tools and cooperation with a wide range of stakeholders.

The consortium identified a clear gap between existing study programmes and the competences demanded by the labour market, particularly in terms of transdisciplinary collaboration, international experience and an understanding of diverse cultural landscapes and heritage management frameworks across Europe. The project therefore aimed to develop and implement an immersive and participatory curriculum that would bring together expertise from archaeology, history, art history, social sciences, natural sciences, applied IT and management.

Another key need addressed by the project was the lack of training opportunities enabling students, especially in humanities-related disciplines, to prepare for heritage management positions at the international level. 

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to develop and pilot a comprehensive transdisciplinary syllabus responding to the evolving needs of archaeological and cultural heritage management. The syllabus was designed to integrate theoretical knowledge, practical skills and soft competences for professional practice, while overcoming the traditional separation between academic disciplines.

Its development was supported by cooperation among students and teachers from diverse educational backgrounds through participatory and immersive learning methods, including hands-on activities outside the classroom. By confronting different academic traditions and perspectives, the project strengthened transdisciplinary thinking, teamwork and problem-solving skills.

Another objective was to stimulate innovative learning and teaching practices by combining in-person activities with digital content. This approach enhanced student engagement, digital readiness and inclusivity, enabling broader access to learning opportunities regardless of physical or socio-economic barriers.

Finally, the project aimed to reinforce transnational academic cooperation and create conditions for collaboration in heritage education.

<< Implementation >>

Project management was ensured through a series of physical and virtual coordination meetings used to monitor progress, coordinate tasks and continuously refine the syllabus based on feedback from previous activities.

Four international participatory workshops formed the core of the educational activities. Each workshop addressed a specific thematic area, including historical landscape reconstruction, digital and IT tools for research and management, conservation and laboratory analysis of archaeological artefacts, and open-area stratigraphical excavation and experimental archaeology. The workshops combined fieldwork, laboratory practice and collaborative learning outside the traditional classroom environment and brought together students from different educational backgrounds.

In parallel, a digital learning platform was developed and tested during the project activities. The platform enabled the use of interactive visual materials, 3D data and digital resources linked to field and laboratory work.

In addition, an international professional conference was organised to discuss transdisciplinary approaches to heritage management and to collect expert feedback supporting the further development of the educational framework.

<< Results >>

The main result of the project was the production of a comprehensive transdisciplinary syllabus for a Master’s degree in “Project Manager in Archaeological Heritage”, made publicly available for use by other higher education institutions. The syllabus integrates theoretical knowledge, practical skills and soft competences from archaeology, heritage management, IT, hard sciences and business, and was piloted through four participatory workshops with students from the partner institutions.

In parallel, a publicly accessible online platform was developed and tested during the workshops. It provides learning materials and resources essential for both fieldwork and laboratory activities, including photos, videos and 3D visualisations of sites and artefacts, and enhances inclusivity and remote access to the curriculum.

Additionally, a short sociological survey among students and early-career researchers provided indicative data on attitudes towards archaeological heritage and historical landscapes. The project also strengthened transnational collaboration among partner institutions, creating foundations for future cooperation and networking.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000087983.title: Diagnostic Tool in Mathematics
2022-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000087983.summary:
<< Background >>

The DiToM project was initiated in response to a widely recognised need across European education systems for practical and reliable diagnostic tools in mathematics that support teachers in identifying learning difficulties at an early stage. In many countries, existing assessments are predominantly summative, curriculum-bound or designed for research purposes, and therefore offer limited support for everyday classroom practice and timely pedagogical intervention.
Teachers often lack accessible instruments that help them identify critical inner-mathematical prerequisites at key transition points in compulsory education, particularly in arithmetic and algebra. This gap is especially relevant in inclusive classrooms, where learning diversity requires diagnostic approaches that go beyond standardised testing and deficit-oriented classifications.
DiToM addressed this need by developing formative and preventive diagnostic tools focused on essential mathematical competencies rather than national curricula. By involving teachers throughout development and piloting, the project responded to a shared European need for classroom-oriented, evidence-based diagnostic tools.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the DiToM project was to develop, validate and make available a coherent set of formative diagnostic tools in mathematics that support teachers in identifying learning difficulties at critical transition points in compulsory education. The project aimed to provide instruments that focus on essential inner-mathematical competencies in arithmetic and algebra, rather than on national curricula, and that can be applied directly in everyday classroom practice.
A further objective was to ensure that the diagnostic tools are preventive in nature, enabling early identification of potential learning difficulties before they become persistent. To achieve this, DiToM sought to involve teachers throughout the development, testing and refinement phases, ensuring usability, clarity and pedagogical relevance.
The project also aimed to address inclusion and learning diversity by integrating specifications for learners with different educational needs and by providing accompanying teacher manuals and evaluation guides. Finally, DiToM aimed to create open-access, multilingual resources that can be used across European contexts and sustained beyond the project duration through a shared digital platform.

<< Implementation >>

The DiToM project was implemented through a structured sequence of activities covering development, testing, validation, digital deployment and dissemination. The work began with the establishment of a common methodological framework defining the principles and design guidelines for the diagnostic tools. This framework was developed collaboratively and validated through focus groups and external evaluation.
Based on this foundation, diagnostic screening tools for five key transition points from early primary to lower secondary education were developed in arithmetic and algebra. Teachers and schools participated in several piloting phases, allowing systematic testing and refinement under real classroom conditions.
In parallel, teacher manuals, evaluation sheets and support materials were created to ensure consistent implementation and interpretation of results. Guidelines were developed to address functional diversity and inclusive classroom contexts.
All outputs were translated into the partner languages and integrated into an open-access digital platform. Dissemination included national multiplier events, an international final conference and online communication, reaching teachers and stakeholders across Europe.

<< Results >>

The DiToM project produced a set of concrete and publicly accessible outputs supporting the early diagnosis of mathematical learning difficulties. The main results include five formative diagnostic screening tools covering key transition points in compulsory education, from early primary to lower secondary level, with a focus on essential competencies in arithmetic and algebra.
All diagnostic tools are accompanied by teacher manuals, evaluation sheets and implementation guidelines, including adaptations for inclusive classrooms. The complete set of core materials was translated into eight European languages, with additional regional adaptations developed and integrated into the project’s dissemination and sustainability strategy through a dedicated digital platform.
The tools were tested and validated in real school contexts. Across several piloting phases, the diagnostic screenings were applied with a total of 6,863 pupils in participating countries, demonstrating their applicability in classroom practice.
Project results were disseminated through national multiplier events, an international final conference and online communication activities, reaching teachers across Europe and supporting sustained use of the project outputs.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000088645.title: GEM – Green Education in Media
2022-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000088645.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to the project because of the need of the partner organisations to integrate sustainability into media design and production curricula - both because of institutional requirements and rising demand by students. We also wanted to bridge the gap between digitized media worlds and real environmental challenges faced across Europe, aiming to empower media students to create content with sustainability in mind. GEM's interdisciplinary approach and its timely focus on sustainable media practices make it vital for fostering self-reflective professionals.
The project addressed the need for integrating sustainability into education for five key groups: Students seeking climate-conscious curricula, teachers updating project-based learning to reflect contemporary realities, university managers implementing sustainability goals in curricula, scientists wanting to broaden outreach beyond academic jargon, and the overall push for internationally coordinated environmental action.
The project also facilitated exchanges of good practices and collaborative development of teaching resources, enriching educational programs with innovative methods and practical solutions.


<< Objectives >>

By creating environmental awareness in media education GEM seeks to make a lasting contribution to a sustainable future. We seek to empower students with the competencies needed to make an impact in their future jobs and in society. GEM aims to embrace nature as a source of learning, fostering dialogue and creative collaboration between media creators, sustainability experts and climate scientists, empowering students and teachers to become green changemakers in their institutions by devising artistic solutions to a sustainable future and integrating sustainability themes into regular curricula.

<< Implementation >>

The project’s activities comprised good practice research, engagement formats with sustainability experts, creation of tools for students, and design and implementation of blended transnational learning activities. Accompanied by curriculum building and diverse dissemination channels, the activities led to a comprehensive portfolio of concepts, courses and recommendation for integrating sustainability into media design and production curricula.
In exploratory activities the project sought to widen our understanding of how nature can become a place of learning, as well as how nature and virtual learning spaces could be connected. This also incorporated early ideation and co-creation with students. Then the consortium focused on the process of film and media production itself, reflecting on how it can become more sustainable in project-based learning. It also featured an extensive 15-part lecture series with external experts from the industry and other branches of academia. In three large transnational blended workshops the approaches were tested, following an adapted “design sprint” approach. In parallel, good practice research was conducted and the insights were used to create curriculum concepts for project sustainability.


<< Results >>

Students and teachers from 8 universities and one sustainability institute participated in three intensive one-week workshops, with preparatory online courses on sustainable design and interdisciplinary teamwork. Participants experimented with digital storytelling inspired by nature and presented their work in natural settings. Teaching materials, course concepts, and evaluations were published on the GEM website alongside videos and transcripts of the 15-part "green screen international" lecture series. The consortium created a prototypical virtual space in Open Simulator to capture the natural learning environment for reflection and future courses.
To support sustainability in student productions, the project documented best practices and developed tools through student co-creation, ensuring outputs were innovative and practically relevant. Insights from teaching sustainability were formalised into curriculum design recommendations, illustrated with examples already integrated by consortium members. Project results reached broader academic and industry audiences at high-profile events including the Berlinale and Krakow Film Festival.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000089750.title: Open GLASSroom
2022-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000089750.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project against the background of current problems in glass education and the resulting needs for improvement and innovation:

•	Existing teaching materials are fragmented, outdated, and lack an interdisciplinary perspective. → Need: Up-to-date, quality-assured, openly accessible teaching materials (= open educational resources, further OER) in the EU.
•	Little international collaboration; knowledge is limited to a few institutions and not widely shared. → Need: Open, accessible online platform to connect educators, students, and practitioners.
•	The global pandemic highlighted the need for digitalization and quality control of teaching materials. → Need: Reliable digital resources and infrastructure for virtual and blended education.
•	Education on glass as a building material lags behind current industry trends, especially on sustainability. → Need: Promote glass as a sustainable building material and strengthen links between education, research, and practice.
•	Commuting and travel for education have a significant carbon footprint.→ Need: High-quality OER and digital platforms to reduce travel and CO₂ emissions.


<< Objectives >>

To address the identified needs, we set the following objectives for the project:

•	Establish a digital environment for high-quality educational materials on glass design and engineering by creating/launching an open-access OER platform.
•	Develop a comprehensive, multidisciplinary glass curriculum for European higher education by collecting and sharing resources from partner universities and integrating perspectives from architecture, engineering, building physics, and material science.
•	Build an open, cross-institutional education community in higher education glass education by engaging students, lecturers, researchers, and practitioners from various countries and backgrounds in content creation and exchange.
•	Set high standards for teaching and expertise in glass education by implementing peer review and sharing best practice examples across institutions.
•	Position the Open GLASSroom community as a leading authority in EU glass education by joining academic, industry, and research stakeholders and supporting continuous cooperation.
•	Promote glass as a sustainable building material by developing and sharing OER that highlight sustainability.

<< Implementation >>

WP1 – Project Management ensured overall coordination, communication, and quality control.

WP2 – Create OER Platform
•	A2.1: The platform architecture based on open-source software and a central data repository was planned and implemented.
•	A2.2: User roles were defined and upload functions for partners were enabled.
•	A2.3: New content was screened and user support was provided.

WP3 – Design OER Content
•	A3.1: Existing digital teaching materials from all partners were collected and documented.
•	A3.2: Staff and students were trained in OER development, copyright and open licencing.
•	A3.3: The digital learning environment and platform structure were jointly designed.

WP4 – Produce OER Content
•	A4.1: Collected materials were converted into openly licenced OER.
•	A4.2: New OER (videos, interviews, research contributions) were produced to fill gaps.
•	A4.3: A multi-step peer-review and internal feedback cycles ensured quality.

WP5 – Dissemination
•	A5.1: OER were implemented in partner university courses and feedback was gathered.
•	A5.2: Community building took place through conferences, workshops and social media.
•	A5.3: An introductory course was designed (later launched as a ProfEd course in 2026).

<< Results >>

The project outputs are largely in line with the original plan. Minor deviations were well justified and agreed with the National Agency and consortium. Strong partner commitment and highly positive feedback from international experts and the OER community resulted in outputs exceeding expectations.

Core Outputs
WP2 – OER Platform: Launch of the Open GLASSroom platform consisting of a technical OER repository (edusources.nl/en/communities/open-glassroom/) and a community homepage (openglassroom.eu).
WP3 – OER Content Design: Inventory of 177 existing digital teaching materials (metadata set); OER training concept and materials (TU Delft library); jointly designed digital learning environment.
WP4 – OER Content Production: 45 project-produced, peer-reviewed OER across five thematic areas, plus 129 supplementary resources (status 30/11/2025).
WP5 – Dissemination: OER implementation in 20 GLASS courses within the consortium (2025); outreach assets incl. image video and social media accounts (e.g. LinkedIn with 492 followers, status 30/11/2025); draft MOOC concept.

Other Results: TU Delft ProfEd Glass course (from 2026); strengthened open education practices; enhanced staff competences in digital teaching; broader globa
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2022-1-EE01-KA220-HED-000089329.title: COOPERATION FOR DEVELOPING JOINT CURRICULUM ON TACKLING HYBRID THREATS
2022-1-EE01-KA220-HED-000089329.summary:
<< Background >>

During the development of the EEAS Training Requirement Analysis (TRA) on hybrid threats and cyber, it became evident that the knowledge derived from this assessment had broader applications. The ever-evolving security landscape necessitates the wider dissemination of knowledge on hybrid threats. While certain specialties related to handling hybrid threats are taught at universities across EU Member States (MS) and in applied law enforcement and defense training institutions, these studies often have a military orientation or are limited in scope, with only a fraction of the curriculum openly accessible. Hybrid attacks have the potential to paralyze society at various levels, whether national or regional. Within the EU, there is a shared recognition of the challenges posed by hybrid threats. Consequently, the creation of a joint international master’s program in internal security became imperative.

<< Objectives >>

General aims of the Project were: 1. Development of an international, Master level, 60 ECTS Curriculum on Tackling Hybrid Threats; 2. To promote the highest opportunities for co-operation in research, education and interoperability to combat hybrid threats and their consequences through common training standards. 3. To be a pioneer in the development of academic competence in the field of hybrid threats with a view to the European Union. 4. To protect and promote the field of internal security as a whole. 5. To provide officials deployed in the European internal security area with a broad knowledge for professional decision-making in a hybrid context, equipping them with the skills and competencies acquired to analyze and solve problems through up-to-date training. 6. To transfer evidence-based knowledge developed in formal academic and disciplinary structures by providing a stimulating and innovative environment for teaching, learning and research. 7. To enable current and future leaders in the field of EU internal security to use practices and theory in tackling hybrid threats and to encourage further development in this field. 
All objectives have been successfully achieved.


<< Implementation >>

1.	Establishment of a Scientific Research Network: A dedicated network of scientific researchers was established, focusing specifically on the study and analysis of hybrid threats. This network fosters collaboration, knowledge exchange, and the advancement of innovative research in the field. 2. Compilation of a Research Agenda: A structured list of scientific research topics was developed, each aligned with the objective of combating hybrid threats. The list included the names of assigned researchers and realistic submission deadlines, ensuring a focused and time-bound research process. 3. Production of Scientific Publications: A total of 32 scientific articles were researched, written, and successfully published in recognized academic journals. This outcome significantly exceeded the initial target of 9 publications, highlighting the productivity and commitment of the research teams involved. 4. Development of Curriculum: A detailed list of curriculum topics and corresponding module titles and Learning Outcomes was defined, forming the foundation for academic and professional training in the area of hybrid threats. 5. Micro-credential course was developed and launched.https://koolitus.edu.ee/course/6174?_locale=en  



<< Results >>

The project has successfully demonstrated its necessity and effectiveness. It has achieved all objectives: to develop a 60 ECTS, accredited master's curriculum, 6 A4 pages of study materials and methodology (WP3), publish up to 9 research articles (WP2), and create a micro-credential course (WP3). The project has remarkably exceeded expectations, with 32 research articles published. The micro-credential course development progressed from planning to practical implementation by the consortium partners, showcasing excellent execution. The high demand for the program—74 applicants from the European Union, tripling the available vacancies—underscores its relevance. 25 students from 11 EU countries graduated Course corresponding to 21 ECTS and received the Certificate. Moreover, the master's-level micro-credential course on countering hybrid threats represents an outcome that surpasses the current state-of-the-art, marking a significant contribution to the field. 
Curriculum and Methodology have been created. Ca 1000 pages of Study Materials with the lists of mandatory and recommended readings have been developed by Consortium members. This Project has remarkably exceeded its' initial expectations.
