2022-1-FI01-KA220-HED-000086152.title: Experiential Learning tools to obtain SMART supply chain competences
2022-1-FI01-KA220-HED-000086152.summary:
<< Objectives >>

SMARTER develops smart supply chain knowledge competences as well as transversal skills through experiential learning applications. 7 universities from Spain, Austria, Ireland, Finland, Croatia, Romania and Argentina as well as 2 business development organisations (IRE, ESP) deliver digital learning material, innovation created in industry-university collaboration, as well as formative assessment tools for sustainable learning methods realising the 'Internationalisation at home' principle.

<< Implementation >>

University students will conduct a digital maturity gap analysis within the target businesses to create the framework for the core learning activity - the SMARTER Student Challenge, organised in Ireland in April 2024. Work packages 4-6 will prepare the Smart Material, Money, and Info flow to support the student challenge by using simulations, serious gaming, webinars and online workshops. The in-person workshop will be realised as a collaborative industry-university knowledge creation event.

<< Results >>

The final conference in Croatia in June 2025 will present the research publication of the digital maturity gap analysis, smart supply chain learning material, the experiential learning tools, the best practices learned from the student challenge, and feedback and reflection documents from student, educators and target group representatives as well as formal curricula integration opportunities. SMARTER achievements are also published in Social Media throughout the progress of the SMARTER project.

2022-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000086863.title: Strengthening the digital transformation of higher education through low-code
2022-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000086863.summary:
<< Background >>

European universities face increasing pressure to modernise digital education, yet low-code environments remain poorly integrated into teaching practice. Institutions lack structured pedagogical resources, teacher training, and accessible platforms to introduce algorithmic thinking, data structures and automation without requiring advanced programming skills.

We applied for this project to address these needs by developing (1) a research-based framework on low-code education, (2) a complete pedagogical curriculum for students and teachers, and (3) an open online platform enabling practical experimentation. The objective was to strengthen digital transformation capacity in higher education and provide scalable, transferable tools for multidisciplinary programmes.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to strengthen the digital transformation capacity of higher education institutions by introducing a structured approach to low-code education. Its objectives were:
1. Analyse institutional and pedagogical needs related to low-code adoption and define a clear framework for integrating low-code in higher education.
2. Develop a complete and transferable curriculum introducing students to core low-code concepts through structured chapters and practical examples.
3. Create an accessible online platform enabling hands-on experimentation with data models, automation, state machines and interface components.
4. Build staff capacity through targeted teacher training and shared pedagogical resources.
5. Disseminate results through publications, events and communication actions to support reuse and scaling.

Overall, the objective was to provide practical tools and evidence-based guidance to embed low-code approaches in teaching and learning.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented across four work packages using an agile, iterative and collaborative approach. Instead of a rigid waterfall model, partners worked through regular online meetings, asynchronous exchanges and shared digital workspaces. This enabled continuous improvement of outputs, quick feedback loops and efficient coordination without unnecessary administrative procedures.

WP2 carried out surveys, interviews, focus groups and desk research to define needs and produce the LightCode Manifesto and the Teacher Training Programme.
WP3 developed a complete 13-chapter curriculum, refined through iterative testing and feedback from students and staff.
WP4 designed and developed the LightCode online platform, translating pedagogical requirements into functional and technical specifications validated through an independent evaluation.
WP5 delivered dissemination actions in Austria, Serbia, Greece and Croatia, complemented by major activities in France, international conferences, publications, newsletters and the dissemination kit.

This implementation ensured timely delivery, strong partner engagement and high practical impact.

<< Results >>

The project produced a complete set of pedagogical, technical and dissemination outputs.
WP2 delivered the LightCode Manifesto, a research-based framework on low-code education, and a full Teacher Training Programme for faculty.
WP3 produced the complete LightCode Course, consisting of thirteen structured chapters with practical examples accessible through the platform.
WP4 developed the LightCode online platform, along with detailed functional and technical specifications validated by an independent evaluation. The platform enables hands-on experimentation with data models, state machines, interfaces and automation.
WP5 delivered a full dissemination package: project website and platform, dissemination kit, newsletters, media coverage, four multiplier events, scientific publications (including the LightCode Manifesto paper), international conference presentations, and a French national-level dissemination activity.

Together, these outputs form a coherent set of resources supporting the integration of low-code approaches in higher education.

2022-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000085120.title: Girls go STEM
2022-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000085120.summary:
<< Background >>

The vision of the project was a society in which girls confidently lead in STEM entrepreneurship and contribute to their community and the economy.
Identified problem: Underrepresentation of women and girls in STEM is a deeply rooted and complex social problem.
Recent research and real-world initiatives have shown that there are ways to reduce gender bias, increase the perceived and actual social relevance of STEM, and ultimately increase women’s sense of belonging in these fields. In the report on Women and STEM in Europe and Central Asia, released in 2021 by the Word Bank Group, the authors made a systematic review on 21 articles, and concluded that there are several answers to the question: What works? Mostly, it is: the education domain of female teachers; exposing girls to nontraditional or gender-neutral roles in the learning environment; and female peer mentoring.
We were using this and similar research to make a unique approach in our project. Final goal of the project and our motivation was to have more girls and young women in the STEM subject studies, using the activities and results within this project.

<< Objectives >>

The vision of the project was a society in which girls confidently lead in STEM entrepreneurship and contribute to their community and the economy.
The main objectives of this project were:
1. Promote access to and retention of women in STEM higher education at all levels.
2. Promote gender equality in career progression for scientists and engineers.
3. Change perceptions, attitudes, behaviors, social norms and stereotypes towards women in STEM in society.

<< Implementation >>

1. Developing an e-platform for mentoring.
2, Collecting a wide range of information on STEM studies and career choices.
3. Videos involving STEM promotion.
4. STEM cafes stories promotional activities, both in STEM Laboratories and with a role model.
5. Conference in Ankara: Women in STEM.
6. Development of guidelines on integrating gender perspectives in teaching.
7. Training on integrating gender perspectives in teaching in Rijeka.

<< Results >>

1. E-learning platform- a digital tool for mentoring girls and young women.
2. Guidelines on integrating gender perspectives in teaching, intended to increase awareness of gender bias, particularly unconscious and unintentional bias held by individuals in academic sense in STEM fields.
3. Impact on getting girls into STEM subject studies. We expect increased number of females enrolling in STEM subject studies on the partner universities.

2022-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000085818.title: Innovating Learning Design in Higher Education
2022-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000085818.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address gap between the increasing use of digital technologies in higher education (HE) and their effective pedagogical use, focusing on the potentials of learning design (LD) to increase the quality of teaching and learning. Previous research and Erasmus+ projects (RAPIDE, eDesk) showed a clear need for a balanced, student-centred and learning-outcome-based approach to LD, supported by practical tools and professional development.
We also addressed need to further explore connection between LD and learning analytics (LA), as interest in their coordination has been growing. Research demonstrates that LD and LA can mutually reinforce each other, yet holistic frameworks and practical guidance are largely missing. In project, we focused on ensuring the soundness of LD, which is critical if we want to ensure that LA are meaningful and actionable.
The project responded to limited opportunities for structured staff development in innovative pedagogies, LD, AI in education, and to EU priorities on flexible learning pathways, microcredentials and lifelong learning (LLL). 
The project aimed to strengthen LD, integrate LA, build HE staff competences, support curriculum innovation, and use of microcredentials.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to enhance the quality and efficiency of HE by fostering the use of learning design (LD), learning analytics (LA) and innovative pedagogies. Previous projects (Erasmus+ RAPIDE, eDesk) and research indicated a need for a concept of balanced and student-centred LD, enhanced through LA. Considering the needs expressed by HE practitioners, the Balanced Design Planning (BDP) LD concept and tool (learning-design.eu) were piloted. With iLed, we wanted to take this further, by evaluating the BDP concept and tool in different educational contexts internationally and using the feedback as the basis for further development. We aimed to make the BDP tool even more aligned with practitioner needs, user-friendly and accessible, to support them in sound pedagogical planning. We wanted to test the BDP concept and tool in authentic learning environments and use it to innovate curricula at the partner HE institutions (HEIs), emphasizing the use of innovative pedagogies, and enhance the capacities of HEIs by providing new learning opportunities – an e-course and MOOC on LD, innovative pedagogies, LA and AI in education. We wanted to promote LLL and flexible learning pathways by exploring the use of microcredentials and digital credentials.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the design cycle, we evaluated the BDP tool in an international context, gathering feedback from 53 educators and researchers from the 4 partner HEIs in Croatia, Germany, Finland and the UK. Based on the feedback, we developed further functionalities aligned with educator needs, as well as direct transfer of LDs to a learning management system (LMS). We investigated the implementation of innovative pedagogies and identified 11 authentic learning scenarios, used the BDP approach to enhance 37 courses in the four HEIs, out of which 22 were delivered, and collected student feedback. We co-designed and piloted a mentored e-course on LD, LA and AI in education, enrolled by over 260 participants, over 120 having completed the intro survey and participated. We also adapted the e-course to and created a self-paced MOOC for further use by educators internationally. We examined the interoperability requirements for the BDP tool and developed a mechanism for issuing Europass-compliant microcredentials. We held a final conference “Learning Design in the AI Era” in July 2025, in synergy with the TRUELA project financed by the Croatian Science Foundation, gathering around 100 participants.

<< Results >>

The key output of the project is internationally validated and enhanced LD tool, BDP (learning-design.eu), presenting a sustainable effort building on previous Erasmus+ projects (RAPIDE, eDesk). The tool is now available in 4 European languages (Croatian, English, German, Finnish), and used by more than 3000 users worldwide. Besides upgrades in terms of userfriendliness and other minor updates, the 2 major upgrades of the tool refer to: 1. enabling direct scaffolding of LD in an LMS; 2. possibility for issuing Europass-compliant microcredentials based on LD data. Experimenting with AI assistance in LD was done. An analysis of interoperability requirements for BDP tool was also done. Further project outputs include the 11 authentic learning scenarios for the application of the BDP approach, enhanced 37 LDs and implemented 22 enhanced LDs at iLed HEIs, followed by collection of student and teacher feedback. A major output is e-course on “Learning Design in the AI Era” and its self-paced MOOC version available to educators internationally. The project resulted in 6 research papers and 3 posters presented on internationally acclaimed research conferences, and 1 research paper published in an acclaimed international scientific journal.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000088675.title: Play to Green: Serious Gaming for Universal Access to Green Education
2022-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000088675.summary:
<< Background >>

The Play2Green project is carried out by a consortium with a strong background in addressing global societal challenges, building on previous initiatives focused on diversity and inclusion, such as the Erasmus+ INNOSID project (2019-1-HR01-KA203-060959). It draws inspiration from environmental efforts like the "European Green Deal", aiming to raise awareness of pressing environmental issues. The project addresses a key gap in the fight against climate change, the lack of innovative, digital educational materials that promote green education. The goal of the project is to support the EU strategy by encouraging people, communities, and organizations to engage in climate action and help build a greener Europe. The objectives are achieved through innovative learning and teaching activities in green education, with educational materials developed as green-themed serious games based on emerging technologies such as AI, AR, and holography. To further engage students, the main target group, these games are integrated into general HEI courses and designed for universal access through Universal Design for Learning principles, ensuring inclusivity for diverse learners.

<< Objectives >>

The Play2Green project was implemented by a consortium consisting of 5 higher education institutions (HEI) and 1 non-governmental organization (NGO) from the domain of people with hearing impairments, from 4 EU countries (Croatia, Spain, France and Hungary). The general objective of the Play2Green project was to raise awareness of the environmental issues described in the “green agenda” and fight against climate change among all diverse learners. To meet the general objective, the project has developed solutions for the following specific objectives: (i) increasing the number of higher education students and lecturers who covered green topics within their studies through a study reporting the potential and good practices that can be implemented; and (ii) providing innovative, green-themed educational resources to everyone. This was managed through developing three green serious games designed following Universal Design for Learning guidelines and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, augmented reality and holography technology.

<< Implementation >>

To meet the objectives, the project implemented fifteen activities from three work packages (excluding the work package regarding project management). The project implemented a report analyzing and identifying modalities for inclusion of green-themed serious games in non-green-themed Higher Education (HE) courses. Three green-themed serious games based on emerging technologies, including AI, AR and holograms were developed. To ensure the effective dissemination of project results, 4 multiplier events in Debrecen (Hungary), Valencia (Spain), Zagreb (Croatia), and Dubrovnik (Croatia) were organized for more than 400 participants. This was accompanied by extensive web and social media activities geared toward the dissemination of project results to the target groups. Dissemination was also administered through publishing several conference papers. Lastly, a learning/training/teaching (LTT) activity was organized in the form of a blended mobility hackathon with a physical workshop in Dubrovnik. More than 30 participants, including lecturers and students, took part in the hackathon and worked in multicultural teams, during which they prepared visual prototypes of innovative IT solutions based on previously prepared game scenarios.

<< Results >>

The key project results and outputs can be summarized as follows: A study of modalities for inclusion of green-themed serious games (SGs) in non-green-themed HE courses was prepared. Three multilingual green-themed SGs based on emerging technologies, including AI, AR and holograms, were developed, (supporting Croatian, English, Spanish, Hungarian and French, including multilingual user guides and explainer/promo videos). Green Siesta, Green Siesta Quiz and HoloZoo are publicly available SGs based on AI, AR and holograms respectively, developed for raising awareness on proper waste management and animal species endangerment. In addition, a total of 9 green-themed SGs based on emerging technology project assignments were prepared alongside 5 green-themed SG scenarios. Afterwards, a successful blended hackathon on green topics, SGs and UDL was held in Dubrovnik. Finally, for a wide outreach of the project’s goals and achievements, a website and two social media channels were made, with several mass media appearances, on TV programs, radio shows and news portals. Four multiplier events were organized in Debrecen, Valencia, Zagreb and Dubrovnik where developed SGs were disseminated, alongside university courses and other events.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000089657.title: University Green Digital HUB
2022-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000089657.summary:
<< Background >>

The University Green Digital HUB (UGDH) project was conceived to address critical gaps in digital, green, and entrepreneurial (DGE) skills among university students, staff, and startups. The motivation stemmed from a shared understanding among partner institutions that higher education must align with Europe’s twin digital and green transitions to remain competitive and relevant in a rapidly evolving global landscape.
Project responds to the need for equipping students with competencies for emerging green and digital economies, fostering innovative startups, and modernizing education through interdisciplinary approaches and digital platforms.
Surveys conducted by project partners highlighted skill gaps in DGE competencies, underscoring the need for targeted programs to bridge them. The project partners mapped these skill levels and developed targeted programs to bridge these gaps effectively.
They have also created a support network for university startups in the area of digital and green innovation, recognizing their potential as enablers of disruptive changes that drive sustainability and digital progress.

<< Objectives >>

The main aim of the project was to develop DGE upskilling programs for university students and staff and a support program for university startups in the area of green and digital innovation.  Therefore, this project main achievement can be seen in advanced digital, green, and entrepreneurial (DGE) competencies among university students, academic staff, and university startups. 
The project managed to strengthen: DGE skills among university staff, students and university startups, the capacity of the HEIs in the field of teaching for the digital and green transition, cooperation between HEIs and partners from the private sector in developing re- and upskilling programs, entrepreneurial activities in the field of digital and green transition. It also enhanced entrepreneurial ventures in the field of digital and green transition and increased use of digital technologies and tools in education and training of selected target groups and provided modernization and improvement of teaching in the field of entrepreneurship
As a central outcome, the project established an international University Green Digital HUB, a collaborative platform offering continuous support, resources, training, and mentorship to develop DGE competencies.

<< Implementation >>

The UGDH project implemented a series of targeted activities to achieve its objectives of enhancing digital, green, and entrepreneurial (DGE) skills among target groups.
In WP2, we held a kick-off meeting to approve project and financial plans, conducted research to assess DGE skill levels, and defined tools for measuring program impact. We trained university staff and trainers, created a database of DGE courses, developed a program framework, and established a dissemination strategy, project visual identity, and website. In WP3, we developed a DGE learning program and launched the DGE Knowledge Factory e-learning platform with educational materials. We compiled a library of open resources, conducted a hybrid pilot program at partner universities, distributed Europass credentials, and organized a transnational meeting to ensure quality. In WP4, we created an action plan to support green startups, and organized green-oriented competitions. We held intensive training programs for university startups focusing on digital and green innovations, facilitated their participation in international startup competitions, developed a joint startup program, and issued Europass credentials, disseminating outcomes through media campaigns.

<< Results >>

The main outputs of the project:
- developed and implemented DGE upskilling education program with university students and staff.
- developed and implemented DGE Knowledge factory web platform.. 
- developed and implemented Greenpreneur startup factory program, support program for university startups in areas of green and digital innovation.

The concrete results of the project were realized through work packages::
- conducted research on the DGE skills of the target groups; methodology for measuring the impact of planned programs; Train the Trainer program; database with systematic insight into DGE courses; developed program framework.  
- developed DGE upskilling program with educational content; DGE Knowledge Factory e-learning platform with learning materials in all languages of partner organizations; a library of open educational resources related to DGE skills; DGE hybrid pilot program implemented; Europass digital credentials distributed to participants.
- developed action plan for supporting green startups; joint startup program; organized green-oriented competitions; blended intensive program and international startup competition for university startups developing digital and green innovative products or services.

2022-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000090031.title: Upgrading and harmonization of Maritime law STCW based curriculum for Maritime students
2022-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000090031.summary:
<< Background >>

Years of experience in teaching maritime law in the process of educating seafarers and discussions with teachers who teach the same subject at other higher maritime educational institutions, led to identifying key problems in this project: 
-	the lack of adequate teaching literature that fully covers all the required content in accordance with IMO Model Course 7.01;
-	the inconsistency of the content and methods of teaching in the maritime law subject as prescribed by IMO Model Course 7.01.
The key results of this project address both of the above issues, not only at the partner institutions but also at other higher maritime educational institutions that educate seafarers. The teaching materials are now available in digital form, via the project website, and are designed in such a way that they do not represent an obstacle with regard to the country or place of teaching. The guidelines for developing the curriculum of the maritime law subject contains a detailed maritime law syllabus aligned with the STCW Convention, while considering all the particularities of national law. Constructive alignment of all learning outcomes has been carried out, both at the level of individual thematic units and at the level of the subject entirely.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we wanted to modernize the teaching process of maritime law at maritime colleges and raise the professional competences of teachers who teach maritime law and related subjects. A modern teaching process primarily involves digital teaching materials, easily accessible to everyone. Students of maritime colleges should be distinguished from students of law colleges and teaching materials should be designed primarily to cover the entire content, and also to be easy to adopt for all those who do not have a sufficient level of previous legal education. All of the above has been achieved by this project. On the other hand, since maritime is an extremely dynamic branch of the economy, which is continuously experiencing changes in the form of technical progress and more modern regulations regulating maritime activities, the professional knowledge of teachers needs to be continuously upgraded, especially in areas that have undergone significant changes in recent years (safety, security, labor relations of seafarers, port law, etc.). Only a teacher who monitors the development of the profession can adequately prepare a future seafarer for contemporary trends in the maritime industry.

<< Implementation >>

The core project activities implemented, done in cooperation among partners consisted of:
•	creating a questionnaire as an instrument that analysed academic background and competencies maritime law teachers, extended to courses that contain particles under maritime law, such as environmental protection that can be governed by maritime law;
•	focus groups analysing different approaches to teaching, teaching materials, with recommendations for improved learning outcomes for maritime law course according to STCW Convention;
•	various workshops improving teachers’ digital, pedagogical and professional competencies;
•	creating guidelines for the harmonisation of maritime law course;
•	creating web page for publishing results available in open access, set of exam questions and self–assessment forms;
•	dissemination activities at numerous events with the participation of relevant stakeholders (e.g industry, other universities), at the advanced level than planned in the application phase of the project;
•	project management activities that followed smooth implementation, involving communication and cooperation, financial and administrative support, and monitoring of the achievements.


<< Results >>

Our project resulted in:
•	Report 1: Analysis of academic background and teachers’ competencies (WP2)
•	Report 2: Double screening of approaches and teaching materials (WP2)
•	Report on the results of Focus Group 1 (WP2)
•	Report on the results of Focus Group 2 (WP2)
•	Certificate of completed workshop on Improvement of teachers’ digital and pedagogical competencies (WP3)
•	Certificate of completed workshop on Improvement of teachers’ professional competencies (WP3)
•	Report on EMSA online event: Gaining specific practical knowledge and strengthening institutional capacity building (WP3)
•	Guidelines for harmonisation of Maritime law course curriculum (WP4)
•	Teaching materials and set of exam questions available online (WP4)
•	Presentation of the prepared teaching materials and set of exam questions (WP4)
•	Report on the final dissemination event at EMSA (WP4)
Results and reports were produced as results of specific activities, and further inputs for the following ones.

2022-1-IS01-KA220-HED-000089316.title: CUTIE - Competencies for University Teaching & Institutional Empowerment
2022-1-IS01-KA220-HED-000089316.summary:
<< Background >>

HEIs across Europe face pressure to respond to digital transformation, yet the development of teachers’ digital competences often remains fragmented and poorly embedded in institutional strategies. Teachers are still often recruited and rewarded for research activities. Digital competence is frequently treated as a personal skill rather than a shared institutional responsibility. As a result, progress in this area depends largely on individual motivation and available time instead of structured support. 

Previous research and recent crises (the COVID-19 pandemic) have shown that technology-focused investments alone do not ensure sustainable digital transformation. What is needed is a systemic and participatory approach that recognises digital teaching competence as a core institutional condition involving multiple actors, including students, managers and support units. CUTIE was designed to address these gaps by shifting the focus from isolated initiatives to institution-wide strategies, grounded in shared reflection, collaboration and the DigCompEdu framework. It responded to the need for sustainable models, practical tools and transferable examples that can support European HEIs in strengthening digital teaching competence. 

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to develop and test approaches for improving digital competences for HE teaching and learning that could be implemented at various levels, enabling systemic and sustainable impact. The project aimed to position digital teaching competence not as an individual concern, but as a shared institutional responsibility shaped by collaboration between teachers, students, managers and support units. 

The aim was to collect, analyse and make accessible existing European initiatives and practices supporting teachers’ digital competences, creating a shared knowledge base for reflection and transfer. Another key objective was to explore and pilot models for integrating students’ voices into the development of teachers’ digital competences through structured co-creation processes. The project aimed to support and empower those with leadership and management responsibilities for teaching and learning by providing them with practical strategies. CUTIE intended to promote institution-wide strategies, local actions, and an open, flexible online course - all grounded in collaboration, shared reflection and the DigCompEdu framework, offering transferable and practical toolkits for European HEIs.  

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through a coherent set of interlinked WPs combining research, reflection, co-creation, implementation and dissemination. In WP2, partners collected and analysed European initiatives and local practices related to teachers’ digital competences, jointly designing and populating an open catalogue hosted on the COMET platform. Regular collation and analysis sessions supported shared learning, followed by the planning and implementation of institutional actions using the CUTE Canvas tool. 

WP3 focused on embedding student perspectives through desk research, literature reviews, creating principles for co-creation and piloting co-creation models in which students acted as co-creators of digital teaching resources. These activities were supported by workshops, local pilots and cross-partner reflection meetings. 

In WP4, partners conducted needs analyses and collaboratively designed an open online course for HE leaders and managers. It was developed using recognised online learning design principles, piloted internationally and adapted locally. Throughout the project, extensive local actions and dissemination activities ensured visibility and knowledge transfer across European HE networks. 
https://cutie.unak

<< Results >>

The project delivered a coherent set of openly available results supporting the institutional development of digital teaching competences in HE. A key output was the fully operational CUTIE Catalogue, bringing together documented actions and initiatives aligned with the DCE framework. Institutional practices and co-creation activities implemented by partners were transformed into structured use cases, ensuring transparency, comparability and reuse beyond the consortium. 

The project produced evidence-based principles and hands-on models for co-creation, demonstrating the added value of student involvement in strengthening teachers’ digital competences, particularly in learner empowerment and engagement. Another major result was the open online course Digital Leadership in Higher Education, offering interactive content, self-assessment tools and practical guidance for academic leaders and managers. The course attracted strong international interest, high participation rates and very positive feedback, and was adapted locally within partner institutions. 
CUTIE enhanced institutional cooperation and supported a shared European understanding of systemic and participatory approaches to digital transformation in HE. https://cutie.unak
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

I have applied for this project in response to the following: 1) VILNIUS TECH contribution, by addressing the university digital transformation through development of digital readiness of the current and future students by provision and absorption of digital tools in the area of rapid application development (RAD) thereby enhancing the effectiveness and efficiency of the educational experiences of the students with tech and business backgrounds. 2) Personal Motivation and Professional development, which allows to enhance my professional and personal skills in communication and digital transformation. 2022-1-MK01-KA220-HED-000087530.title: Blended Learning and Evaluation Practices for Inclusive Digital Higher Education
2022-1-MK01-KA220-HED-000087530.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied with this project because we wanted through "Blended Learning and Evaluation Practices for Inclusive Digital Higher Education" project to address the need for modernizing and enhancing the quality and efficiency of higher education provided by HEIs, by establishing a foundation for inclusive and dynamic blended learning models tailored to the evolving demands of the modern era.

Our primary objectives include promoting inclusive blended learning practices that will enable better experiences for students with disabilities, enhancing personalization, and increasing the quality of educational practices for inclusive blended learning. 2022-1-MK01-KA220-HED-000089263.title: Leaders of the Green Economy
2022-1-MK01-KA220-HED-000089263.summary:
<< Background >>

The topic of circular economy and the competencies needed has rarely been explored on University level. There is an obvious gap between the knowledge produced on the academic level and knowledge required by the industry, regarding the circular economy requirements. In such circumstances, it looks like the industry requirements are going faster than the readiness of academia to respond to specific needs (Morrison and Pattison, 2020). This is especially prominent in the countries of the Balkans where the linkages between industry and academia are still weak. Therefore this project addresses the gap between the needs of the economy and the preparedness of the students with knowledge, skills and competences for the “green” economy. The preparedness of the students is directly linked to the preparedness of higher education institutions to develop such competencies among students and to the availability of the materials used in teaching and learning. Students learn best when using practical, engaging and locally relevant materials and from professors that are well skilled and motivated. The project trained professors to develop  and use case studies and other OER materials and engaged students in applied activities with industry. 

<< Objectives >>

The project had the following objectives:
- Understanding the current situation regarding teaching and learning about circular economy on University level as well as student experiences and understanding of circular economy concepts; 
- Establishing linkages and enhancing the cooperation between the academia and industry in relation to circular economy by means of creating and further enriching existing networks;
- Creating a digital repository of knowledge, tools and activities that can be utilized by teachers and students in their future activities related to stimulation of circular economy;
- Enrichment of the knowledge and skills of the University staff in teaching about circular economy;
- Empowering students to enrich their knowledge and skills in the area of circular economy and motivating them to implement concepts of circular economy in their future jobs. 
The project focused on enhancing circular economy skills among students which will be needed for the future in fighting climate change, ensuring sustainability and protecting the environment. The project activities will ensure not only that the students develop their skills but that the Schools participating in the action will continue to implement such activities. 

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented the following activities: 
WP1 Project management: signing Cooperation Agreements with partners; holding regular coordination meetings; monitoring of the activities in each institution; 
WP2 White Paper: mapping of the curricula and subjects of each partner; survey with the students of each of the partners; Based on the mapping and the survey, a study and recommendations were published with an ISBN number.
WP3: Digital Repository: selected professors from each partner were trained in the development of digital materials (case studies, quizzes and short videos) and involved in ongoing online coordination; With joint efforts we developed OER materials: 8 case studies, 7 quizzes and 7 videos. 
WP4: Activities with students. We organized two live boot-camp activities and 7 hybrid lectures attended by students from all partner institutions. 
WP5: Dissemination. Each partner undertook internal dissemination on use of OER materials for teachers (train the trainers); we created a web-site for dissemination of the project materials (https://sites.google.com/view/leadersofthegreeneconomy/home-latest-updates) and social media profiles; we published articles in local media and held a closing conference.

<< Results >>

As a results of the project we achieved the following outputs: 
- White Paper publication - summarizing the results of the curriculum mapping at each institution and the surveys at each institution with a total of 427 students. The publication contains recommendations for curricular improvement  and teaching about circular economy. It has an ISBN number and is available on the project website, EPALE and Erasmus+ Project Platform. 
-training session on how to develop and use OER materials in teaching - held on 31 March 2023 at DOBA. 
- Digital Repository - database containing 8 case studies, 7 quizzes and 7 videos. The publication has an ISBN number. All materials are OER and are available on the project web-site, EPALE and Erasmus+ Project Platform. 
- boot-camps: one in Rijeka (28.06.2023 – 01.07.2023) and one in Skopje (14.02.2024 – 16.02.2024) attended by 44 participants in total. 
- hybrid lectures: we held 7 hybrid lectures in fall 2023. The lectures were attended by students from each partner institution. In total 322 students attended the lectures. 
- dissemination activities: project web-site; social media profiles, local media articles, internal dissemination at each institution and closing conference.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2022-1-NL01-KA220-HED-000088069.title: Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics Teach the Teacher program
2022-1-NL01-KA220-HED-000088069.summary:
<< Background >>

For our Erasmus+ application, we aimed to address the critical need for modernized, harmonized education in medication prescribing. This need was highlighted by the WHO, with its goal to reduce avoidable medication-related harm by 50% [Donaldson, 2017], the European Commission, and the European Association for Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics [Brinkman et al. 2018].

The existing 30-years-old ‘WHO Guide to Good Prescribing’ and its related Teacher’s Guide including materials were outdated and no longer met current standards [Tichelaar, 2019]. As a result, prescribers were not fully equipped to address contemporary challenges like polypharmacy, deprescribing, race-based medicine, gender, and electronic prescribing. Our group aimed to bridge this gap by creating the CP4T program to modernize CPT education
.
Through updating the guidelines, offering a multimodal (online) teach the teacher course, and developing supplementary training materials (tutorials, case repositories, videos), we sought to provide future healthcare professionals with the most up-to-date, evidence-based education. This project eventually improves CPT education, and thereby improving medication safety and patient care.

<< Objectives >>

By introducing the CP4T program, including the updated guides and the multimodule course, we aimed to harmonize and modernize the teaching and training of Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics (CPT) across Europe and beyond. The project sought to educate and support CPT teachers through updated teaching materials that reflect the latest educational insights, offer an aligned CPT curriculum that also takes into account the needs of students with disabilities, and provide a comprehensive assessment program covering both traditional and emerging topics.

Furthermore, the program aimed to foster collaboration between European universities through international and interprofessional student-run clinics, facilitating teacher and student exchange opportunities. After the project, the complete “teach-the-teacher” package—including the training activities, aligned CPT curriculum, comprehensive assessment program, and international collaboration framework—will be freely available to all medical universities worldwide.


<< Implementation >>

Within this project we have completed/executed to following activities:
-	Conducting needs analysis and research about the two WHO guides;
-	Conducting research on therapeutics reasoning;
-	Conducting research on differences between prescribers; 
-	Developing and updating the WHO Guide to Good Prescribing;
-	Developing and updating the WHO Teacher’s Guide to Good Prescribing;
-	Designing and piloting various multimodule teach the teacher courses;
-	Conducting research on the bricks and barriers in organizing teach the teacher courses;
-	Organizing new multimodule teach the teacher courses; 
-	Organizing Student-run Medication Review sessions;
-	Conducting research on Student-Run medication Review sessions;
-	Developing new teaching materials; 
-	Coordinating consortium meetings and dissemination events.


<< Results >>

Within this project we have achieved the following outputs/results:
-	Creating and maintaining the project website;
-	Creating and maintaining a SharePoint page;
-	Posting news articles on the project website and social media;
-	11 videoconference calls including minutes/reports;
-	5 transnational project meetings including minutes/reports;
-	Revised version of Guide to Good Prescribing
-	Revised version of Teacher’s Guide to Good Prescribing
-	Teach the Teacher coursers; 5 in-person and 2 online
-	12 International Student-Run Medication Reviews
-	9 published research papers in peer-reviewed journals;
-	5 papers in progress to publish;
-	Teaching materials:
 Guide on how to create a videoclip about ‘the medicine of the week;
 9 Translated and 22 new video clips of Medicine of the week;
 Turtorial about how to use AI in creating diverse and inclusive patient cases;
 An AI metaprompt with a seed to create synthetic clinical cases 
 Turtorial on what and how to teach about prescribing anti-hyperglycaemic drugs;
 Turtorial on Team-Based Learning (TBL);
 Turtorial on high-fidelity simulation education;
 List of the most important drug-drug interactions that should be taugt to students;
 Report on therapeutic reasoning

2022-1-NL01-KA220-HED-000089789.title: Expanding the network of Inclusion, Diversity, Equity and Access (IDEA) practitioners in higher education through institutional capacity building
2022-1-NL01-KA220-HED-000089789.summary:
<< Background >>

The IDEA-net project was born out of a shared recognition of the urgent need to embed inclusion, diversity, equity, and access (IDEA) more systematically within higher education institutions (HEIs) across Europe. Despite isolated efforts, many institutions lacked coordinated, research-informed strategies to support IDEA work. The project addressed the need for structured frameworks, capacity building, and practical tools to promote sustainable change, especially in contexts where IDEA infrastructure is still emerging, such as the Western Balkans (WB) region. It aimed to foster inclusive institutional cultures, support leadership and staff development, and ensure that IDEA initiatives are context-sensitive and aligned with local realities. Partners also identified the need to critically reflect on their own policies, improve support for underrepresented groups, and enable evidence-based decision-making. IDEA-net provided an opportunity to exchange practices, bridge gaps between policy and practice, inspire innovation, strengthen regional collaborations to support long-term transformation and empower staff, students, and faculty to become change agents in building equitable and resilient learning environments. 

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to build institutional capacity for IDEA in HEIs by creating practical, evidence-informed resources.This objective ensured that the outputs were not isolated, but part of a long-term strategic agenda to embed IDEA institutionally.It sought to collect and share context practices in a Compendium, develop a cooperative, accessible and adaptable Toolkit for setting up IDEA offices, and pilot a peer-based Capacity Building Tool (CBT) tailored to local realities (Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia), rather than simply applying existing activities. Through its Community of Practice (CoP), the project supported professional development, critical reflection, and exchange of knowledge among HEIs’ staff. A key objective was to embed IDEA into policies, teaching, governance, and support systems by offering adaptable frameworks rooted in lived experiences. It also aimed to promote structural change by raising awareness of inequalities, strengthening leadership engagement, and empowering institutions to act intentionally. Ultimately, the project sought to create a sustainable, transnational network of IDEA practitioners committed to disseminate innovative and transferable resources, capable of influencing both practices and policies

<< Implementation >>

A data collection tool was created and used to gather best practices from global institutions, resulting in a public and online Compendium with 60 good practices. Guidelines were developed to support the creation of IDEA offices, informed by desk reviews, institutional mapping and peer feedback, and not just the product of one singular experience. Focus groups, interviews, meetings with institutional leadership and cultural analyses shaped the CBT, which was piloted through intensive 12 hours workshops each, in three partner countries. These sessions used theoretical frameworks with interactive peer-learning formats, such as forum theatre and roleplay, to explore IDEA-related challenges and build skills. Training resources, including content information, facilitation guidelines and presentation slides, were made publicly available online for future use (train-the-trainer approach). Partners also organized institutional webinars, local and in-person workshops and participated in international conferences, while contributing to a CoP through a LinkedIn group, a podcast, blogs, webinars, and a newsletter—creating an active network to support IDEA engagement across other geographies.

<< Results >>

A key result is the Compendium of Best Practices with 60 IDEA initiatives from HEIs worldwide. Additionally, a Guideline Toolkit offering a digital, open-access and practical roadmap for establishing IDEA offices, with self-assessment tools and adaptable strategies. Another outcome was the in-person (and then digitally-available) CBT that includes peer-learning methods and facilitation guides, piloted through three intensive training sessions. These sessions generated trained facilitators and were foundational in initiating dedicated networks for further exchange and collaboration. A CoP and all the material produced (six webinars, one podcast-webinar, 27 posts on the LinkedIn group, eight blog posts, six vox pops and one newsletter) which fostered peer learning and international collaboration. While the University of Ljubljana (UL) and University of Belgrade (UB) advanced towards formal establishment of IDEA offices, the University of Zadar (UZ) re-assessed existing inclusive practices and has built capacity to expand them, notably by building on the work of the Student Counselling Centre. This ensures that the original commitment of three WB universities taking first steps toward IDEA institutionalization was fully addressed.

2022-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000086080.title: Electronic Pan-European Learning System for Sustainable Agribusiness MBA Education
2022-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000086080.summary:
<< Background >>

The e-AgriMBA project was initiated to respond to key challenges in agribusiness education identified by the AgriMBA network, which develops and monitors MBA programs in the field of agribusiness and commerce in Europe since 1995. In 2025, 11 local AgriMBA programs were available within the network. The project was an answer to the main challenges of a MBA education, identified by the AgriMBA board, namely that agribusiness professionals face difficulties combining work with MBA studies, while economic and geographical barriers limit access to quality education—especially for students from rural or less affluent regions. On the other hand, the current globalisation of the agribusiness requires cutting edge, innovative knowledge more than ever. The project, therefore, innovated and digitalised existing AgriMBA programs (need N1), improved their quality and attractiveness through shared international resources (N2), fostered the internationalisation of agribusiness teaching and networking (N3), and strengthened cooperation with EU neighbouring countries by integrating Moldova into the AgriMBA network (N4). Together, these needs reflect EU priorities in inclusion, digital transformation, and lifelong learning.

<< Objectives >>

The two main objectives of the e-AgriMBA project were to develop and implement the Electronic Pan-European Learning System for Sustainable Agribusiness MBA Education and to integrate the first Moldovan university into the AgriMBA network. These goals were achieved through three specific objectives. O1 aimed to establish the AgriMBA Learning System — a digital platform based on MOODLE enabling online and blended learning across partner institutions. O2 focused on broadening the course portfolio of local MBA programs by creating and sharing nine high-quality courses developed collaboratively by international experts. O3 targeted the establishment of a new local AgriMBA program and the integration of a new partner university – Technical University of Moldova – into the AgriMBA network, extending both the network’s European neighbourhood dimension and bringing Moldova’s academic system as well as the agribusiness sector closer to the EU to facilitate the EU accession. These objectives directly supported EU priorities of inclusion, digital and green transformation, and lifelong learning by improving access to education, promoting innovation, and strengthening cross-border cooperation and quality in agribusiness higher education.

<< Implementation >>

The e-AgriMBA project was implemented through four Work Packages (WP1–WP4), each addressing a specific objective. WP1 ensured coordination, communication, and quality management across the consortium. WP2 focused on developing the AgriMBA Learning System — an innovative, secure, and user-friendly digital platform. Activities included identifying best practices, assessing user needs, designing the system architecture, training teachers (“train the trainers” workshops in Mád and Chisinau), and preparing user guides and instructional videos. WP3 broadened the AgriMBA course portfolio: all partners jointly designed, developed, and tested nine complete courses integrated into the e-learning system, ensuring high pedagogical and technical quality. WP4 established and piloted the first AgriMBA MBA program in Moldova, implemented new modules, trained teachers, and carried out real-life testing with students. Together, these activities modernised agribusiness education, strengthened digital competencies, and expanded international cooperation within the AgriMBA network.

<< Results >>

The project resulted in the successful implementation of the Electronic Pan-European Learning System  AgriMBA Education. A report on best online e-learning practices (R2.1) and a needs and preferences analysis (R2.2) provided the evidence base for the system’s design. The AgriMBA Learning System (R2.3) was developed using the Moodle framework, integrating video tools. Written and video instructions (R2.4) were produced, and two international training sessions (R2.5) for teachers were organised in Hungary (2023) and Moldova (2024). Partners jointly developed curricula for 9 MBA courses (R3.1). High-quality course materials (R3.2) were prepared and implemented in the AgriMBA Learning System (R3.3). The courses were tested in real teaching within the newly established Moldovan MBA program. 
The Technical University of Moldova joined the AgriMBA network and established the first AgriMBA program (R4.1). The program received national accreditation, developed 6 new modules and 36 courses (R4.2), and trained over 40 local teachers to use the AgriMBA Learning System (R4.4). Necessary equipment and facilities were installed (R4.3). The first graduates successfully defended their theses (R4.5), and TUM achieved international accreditation.

politics with a specific & target focus on the shared European values, principles, identity and awareness. We hope that based on our efforts students in social sciences and humanities are will be able to deconstruct stereotypes or, from time to time, to construct new approaches to understand the each other, our societies, European integration &the world.

EUROPIA main objectives was to develop an innovative, holistic, integral and modular training approach for enhancing the capacities of university academia to conduct education process in the field of European history, law and politics with a specific & target focus on the shared European values, principles, identity and awareness. These experts participated in various configurations, from individual contributions to group work in order to deliver the necessary input for the implementation of the particular results. The national coordinators had to assemble, organize and secure the successful conduct of the On Wheels Summer School in August 2024 and afterwords to secure the update and upgrade of the educational materials. Project website and Training Platform were created and the dissemination and project valorisation were conducted. The partners also followed the necessary Quality Management principles and duly responded the Quality Management activities. In addition a scholar conference was organized and financial discipline was kept.

The creation of three new Training Packages TK5, TK6 and TK7 and the update of TK's1,2,3&4 with the Spanish content. The development of a Manual and a Guidebook accomplished the tasks within WP2. Within WP3 a project website europiaproject.eu was created and an educational training platform, with all the necessary functionalities and open access. The organization and conduct of the piloting On Wheels Summer School in August 2024 in Warsaw was the key result of WP4, followed by piloting at national levels. Within WP5....
In addition, to all the planned outputs, based on the nature of the collaboration between the project partners, we agreed to go beyond the initial strictly educational goals and to add a scholar component based on our fields of interests and contributions. Hence, we organized a scholar conference Current Challenges for the Rule of Law in Europe, which we used for the promotion of Europia and for a publication to be published in Nov.25.

2022-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000087149.title: Integrating Nature-Based Solutions into Higher Education towards exploiting the transformative potential of Social Economy for a green and inclusive future
2022-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000087149.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the critical gap between the environmental potential of Social Economy Entities (SEEs) and the limited role of environmental education in SE- related university curricula. While SEEs are increasingly recognized as key players in the green transition, their capacity remains underutilized—mainly due to a lack of training and practical educational frameworks. Existing programs focus on theoretical aspects of sustainability, offering few opportunities for experiential learning.

Our project responds to this by developing SEgoesGreen—an innovative educational programme that integrates Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) and eco-citizenship into SE studies. The aim is to move from “learning about” sustainability to “learning for” climate action. We seek to empower SE students with green skills, creativity, and initiative, and to support educators with resources and training to deliver transformative, action-oriented environmental education. Through this, we aim to build a new generation of environmentally engaged social entrepreneurs. The project also supports systemic change by aligning higher education with EU climate and sustainability goals.

<< Objectives >>

Through the SEgoesGreen project, we aimed to bridge the gap between Social Economy (SE) education and the urgent need for action-oriented environmental learning. Our main goal was to embed Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) into SE-related higher education programmes, using them as a powerful pedagogical tool to engage both students and educators in addressing climate change and environmental challenges.
We wanted to support university educators by developing a comprehensive blended training programme—including an educator’s manual, a MOOC platform, and a Hackathon Seminar—that would introduce innovative, experiential, and eco-citizenship-based teaching practices. Simultaneously, we aimed to empower students by offering them a future-oriented Green SE curriculum that fosters green skills, creativity, and active citizenship through real-world, challenge-based learning.
Finally, we sought to create a replicable and scalable model for integrating NBS into SE education and promote its uptake EU-wide through policy recommendations and ready-to-use training materials - ensuring long-term impact beyond the project’s lifetime.

2022-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000088856.title: Business Analytics Skills for the Future-proof Supply Chains
2022-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000088856.summary:
<< Background >>

The dynamically changing logistics market, which is increasingly based on digital solutions, means that the requirements for university graduates are also evolving. Consortium partners with many years of experience in educating students in areas such as logistics and supply chain management have recognised the need to adapt and modify educational programmes. This will ensure that future supply chain managers have the knowledge and skills to adapt to the ever-changing requirements of the logistics market. In response to this need, the BAS4SC project developed 3 courses that cover methods and teaching materials to enable students to acquire and effectively apply analytical skills in practice. The results of this work include educational programmes and an increased number of specialists whose knowledge and skills will improve the efficiency of the logistics industry as a whole. This project has enabled the creation of a virtual environment containing developed courses, which are available not only to partner universities, but also to universities and students outside the project consortium. This contributes to the growth of knowledge and skills in business analytics among students, particularly those in Central and Eastern Europe.

<< Objectives >>

The project consortium wanted to use the project's results primarily to expand and improve their universities' educational offerings, adapting them to the requirements of the "new age" of logistics. This would enable their graduates to acquire analytical skills and prepare them for work in a digitally transformed logistics industry. The consortium aimed to accurately identify the profiles of the logistics industries and educational institutions in the partner countries, to ensure that the planned courses met the real needs of companies in terms of their future employees' competencies. This activity contributed to the development of 3 courses on the use of business analytics in logistics, which was the project's main goal, creation of a virtual E-learning environment containing materials in 5 languages. To extend the impact of the results, partners made the virtual environment accessible to universities outside the consortium, enabling them to implement the courses in their modules. The active involvement of stakeholders, including companies, academic teachers and students ensured that the courses met the expectations of all interested parties. These activities enabled the project's main and specific objectives to be achieved.

<< Implementation >>

The activity that prepared the consortium to achieve the project's main objective was to identify the competence gap. This was based on an analysis of the business analytics in logistics curriculum implemented at universities from Europe and USA, as well as a survey of companies in the logistics and manufacturing sector, academic teachers and students. The identified gap was used to develop three courses: C1: Advanced spreadsheet analysis for logistics data; C2: Business Intelligence; and C3: Statistical methods for logistics data analysis. These were implemented in an open-access virtual environment, together with handbooks, lecture materials, workshop materials and additional Open Educational Resources (OER). The developed materials and virtual environment were provided in five languages: English, Polish, Croatian, Slovenian and Serbian. These materials were also verified during a series of training sessions for academic staff and students. Feedback collected after these sessions was used to improve the materials. The project also involved various dissemination activities, such as multiplier events, presentations at international scientific conferences and social media initiatives. Guide in file WP1.1_BAS4SC Project Abstract.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs of the project were the contents of 3 courses: C1: Advanced spreadsheet analysis for logistics data; C2: Business Intelligence; and C3: Statistical methods for logistics data analysis. These courses included course cards, handbooks, lecture materials, pre- and post-tests and workshop materials, including multimedia presentations, tasks with data sets, and case studies. Additional materials were provided in the form of OER. The partners also developed a two-stage case study that summarises all the topics covered in the courses. These materials were then implemented in a virtual environment adapted for the 5 languages, which is also open to universities outside the consortium. Project partners produced also the following results: an analysis of educational programmes used at European and US universities, a needs analysis of existing business analytics competencies among academic teachers and students, a needs analysis of business analytics competencies among logistics and manufacturing company management staff. The consortium also identified a skills gap. Together with the above-mentioned analyses, this was used to develop the project's main results, i.e. course content for three areas: C1, C2 and C3.

2022-1-RO01-KA220-HED-000088958.title: Cooperation to implement innovative methods for the assessment of medicinal plants with central roles in pharmaceutics, agriculture and nutrition
2022-1-RO01-KA220-HED-000088958.summary:
<< Background >>

The application for this project aimed to: update and improve knowledge about medicinal plants; build a transnational partnership; train and develop experts and students; create a specialized curriculum; encourage internationalization and networking.
The project addressed the needs for: (i) teachers/specialists - skill development, career development, modernization and internationalization, active learning methods, alignment with the labor market, language skills, networking; (ii) students - communication and teamwork, language skills, entrepreneurship, mobility and cultural awareness, academic performance and skills, connection to the labor market, access to scientific information; (iii) entrepreneurs and the medicinal plants industry sector - data and best practices; and (iv) the general population - awareness of medicinal plants, lifestyle changes for health and sustainability.
The needs addressed reflect the project’s objectives to: improve the quality of education, support professional development, increase employability, encourage sustainability, and enhance public awareness regarding medicinal plants and health.

<< Objectives >>

As a result of the project implementation, the main objective of the project was intended to be achieved. Thus, the focus was on developing a transnational cooperation partnership, as well as applying joint initiatives for cooperation and exchange of best practices at the European level, with the goal of facilitating the transfer of knowledge in the field of medicinal plants, technologies, and plant extract products with a central role in nutrition, pharmacy, and agriculture. All these were also aimed at increasing interconnectedness, innovation, inclusion, and digitalization in higher education.

<< Implementation >>

The project established three specific objectives: 1) The continuous training of specialists and the instruction of new experts, in line with ERASMUS+ priorities; 2) The transfer of knowledge to the target group and socio-economic environment through a specialized curriculum, a guide, and an interdisciplinary course focused on the cultivation, analysis, evaluation, and valorization of medicinal plants with central roles in nutrition, pharmacy, and agriculture; and 3) Awareness activities through the dissemination of project results via multiple digital learning events (workshops, publications, digital platform).
The implemented activities were aligned with these three objectives and included: management actions and meetings for effective collaboration among partners (based on digital tools), training sessions for experts to exchange practices and for students to gain appropriate specialization to facilitate their integration into the job market, the development of specialized materials, and the dissemination of project results.

<< Results >>

The project outcomes (curriculum, guide, course, website) were designed to serve multiple users as follows: i) academic experts; ii) students, master's and Ph.D. students; iii) specialists in the fields of medicine, pharmacy, food industry, and agriculture; iv) entrepreneurs, and v) the general public through access to the digital educational platform (the project's website).
Concrete outputs refer to: innovative approaches for more attractive education and training programs, aligned with the labor market; increased effectiveness of activities benefiting communities; a modern, dynamic, and professional environment within the organization, capable of integrating best practices and new methods; creating synergies with organizations active in complementary fields; strategic planning of staff professional development in line with individual needs and organizational objectives.

2022-1-RS01-KA220-HED-000089900.title: Agroforestry practices in West Balkan for sustainable development: weaknesses and strengths
2022-1-RS01-KA220-HED-000089900.summary:
<< Background >>

The need to implement innovative approaches in fight against climate change is urgent. It is necessary to identify all the resources and potentials of measures in different sectors that can contribute to this aim. Agroforestry practices stemming from traditional methods, revisited and adapted to local environmental and socioeconomic conditions, could serve as mighty tool for mitigating climate change. Students of agriculture and forestry, should be able to apply such innovative approaches through learning the concepts, design and implementation of agroforestry. To foster the adoption of agroforestry practices within local communities, it is essential to inform, educate, and train farmers and local governments on transitioning from conventional methods to agroforestry practices to help them diversify their production, increase profitability, and ensure long-term resource sustainability.  The education of professionals in this field a lack of modern literature has been noted, as well as the lack in digital skills’ training in current curricula. This project specifically targets solving these shortcomings through the introduction of new literature, spatial databases in a GIS environment that will serve to educate new professionals.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of AGFORWEB project was to improve education in the field of agroforestry which is recognized as sustainable land use solution with potential to combat climate change, enhance biodiversity, and improve local people well-being. Curricula improvement of seven agroforestry or related modules at partner universities included the implementation of digital tools in planning and design of agroforestry practices, and creation of new learning materials such as a textbook - Agroforestry Practices in Southeast Europe and a manual for digital databases - GIS Application in Agroforestry. The joint digital database, enabled raising of digital literacy of students and their learning on real-world data but also it is resource for research. To ensure that knowledge in agroforestry is inclusive and accessible to farmers and policymakers, guides - Agroforestry in Practice were prepared in local languages, and workshops were conducted for them. Finally, sharing best practices among partner countries through study visits and guest lectures has fostered exchange and internationalization. That also strengthen cooperation among partner institutions and enabled networking both teaching stuff and students.

<< Implementation >>

To ensure effective project implementation we conducted various activities. We analyzed existing Agroforestry module curricula and agroforestry related fields at partner universities compare them with Agroforestry module curricula at EU universities to identify gaps and effectively improve existing curricula and to prepare curriculum for new Agroforestry module at UOM. Also, a digital database was created primarily for student training, which aims to support curriculum improvements made in accordance with modern agroforestry modules curricula at EU universities. Provision of learning materials for students was conducted through activities of creating textbooks in English and partner languages, manual for utilizing digital database. To support lifelong learning, we prepared guides - Agroforestry in Practice in partner languages which were presented and distributed to attendees at workshops for local community. Knowledge exchange and networking were enabled through conducted study visits and held guest lectures. Continuous dissemination of results and project was conducted through preparation and distribution of promotion materials, conferences, and other events, magazine articles as well as by project website and social networks.

<< Results >>

AGFORWEB project achieved the results, including seven improved Agroforestry or related modules curricula at partner universities and one new Agroforestry module curriculum ready for accreditation at UoM. A digital database of common agroforestry practices was created to support hands-on learning, accompanied by updated learning materials—textbooks, a manual, and video tutorials. Final and master theses based on the database confirmed value of the digital database for further agroforestry research. Guest lectures provided students with insights into agroforestry practices from different regions, showcasing the unique approaches adopted by each partner country, while teaching staff enhanced their skills and explored collaborations through shared experiences. Study visits facilitated knowledge exchange among partner countries, addressing diverse expertise levels in the West Balkans and beyond. Lifelong learning materials, including a guide for farmers and local governments, were developed and presented at workshops to promote agroforestry practices among stakeholders. Project results were showcased through three poster presentations at EURAF 2024, the leading agroforestry conference.
