2022-1-SE01-KA220-HED-000085564.title: Towards a European Heritage Interpretation Curriculum
2022-1-SE01-KA220-HED-000085564.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We aim to create a standardised training curriculum and related training contents in heritage interpretation (HI) that will contribute to the recognition and professionalization of heritage interpreters and raise their employability.

Specific objectives are: 

-To collect, analyse and share good practices examples in HI.
-To develop a MOOC in HI at higher education level.
-To raise awareness among EU citizenship about the value of cultural and natural heritage and the need for its protection.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities we are going to implement are:

- Analysis of good practices in heritage interpretation and their compilation in a Good practices manual.
- Development of a training curriculum for heritage interpretation at higher education level.
- Development of training modules and learning units on heritage interpretation.
- Development of the TEHIC MOOC on heritage interpretation.

<< Results >>

The main result will be a MOOC that will allow the professionalisation of heritage interpreters and the recognition of their profession at European level. Our course will be designed to meet the criteria of academic training, but its format and flexibility will allow its use in other educational fields such as CVET and adult education.

The other main outcome of the project will be raising awareness and understanding of European natural and cultural heritage.

2022-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000085761.title: Diversity in action: a cross-border online space for training teachers through multilingual and multicultural experiences
2022-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000085761.summary:
<< Background >>

The main idea when applying for the project was to develop future teachers' multicultural and multilingual skills and competences which would enable them to teach in linguistically and culturally diverse classrooms. The partner institutions have recognized the need to enhance pre-service primary school and preschool teachers competences for teaching in linguistically and culturally diverse classrooms. This is especially relevant as all partner institutions are all located in multilingual and multicultural environments. In addition, the need for the project is related to the fact that education study programs face low numbers of student mobility which is partly due to the fact that they are regulated by the government which means there are some extra requirements that students have to fulfill (such as the obligatory teaching practice). This need is addressed by the objective of creating a cross-border online  virtual space for students to learn through multilingual and multicultural experiences.  In line with the EU objectives of promoting multilingual and multicultural practices, the projects also addresses the need to offer a teacher training course in the form of a MOOC aimed at in-service teachers. 

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project we especially wanted to achieve a working and innovative cooperation network between partner institutions in the form of a cross-border online learning platform. The network is the basis for designing and piloting a BA study course aimed at developing future teachers' multilingual and multicultural competences by participating in cross-border border student collaboration and participation, and encouraging students to take part in student exchange programs. In addition, the project was aimed at bringing together experts in multilingual teaching methodology from different countries to work in teams and use their expertise ti develop innovative instructional approaches for promoting multilingual practices.  An important objective was also to develop an open-source multilingual MOOC on teaching in linguistically and culturally diverse classrooms, aimed at in-service teachers as a professional development course. 

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were implemented:

- Project management activities (coordinating and monitoring project activities and communication, evaluating and reporting)
- Drafting, designing, and piloting a BA Study Course (Intellectual output)
- Developing and evaluating a Study Book (Intellectual output)
- Developing, piloting and evaluating an open-source MOOC course (Intellectual output)
- Kick-off and two transnational meetings
- Language teaching and training activities (LTTs)
- Student physical mobility
- Multiplier events in all partner institutions
- Dissemination events

Besides the activities included in the application, we implemented other unplanned activities:
- designing the project web page
- organising a competition among art students of the project partners for the design of the project logo
- receiving funds for the publication of the Study Book in print form

<< Results >>

The most important objective of the DivA project is to create a new cooperation model between partner institutions by developing an innovative cross-border online learning platform. This model enables partner institutions, all located in multilingual environments, to offer a teacher training course aimed at promoting multilingual and multicultural practices. The concrete results are:

1. drafting, designing, and piloting a BA Study Course (3 ECTS), evaluating the results and implementing improvements,
2. developing and evaluating a Study Book as a support for the Study Course which will promote the benefits and integrate the principles of multilingual education,
3. developing, piloting and evaluating an open-source multilingual MOOC on teaching in linguistically and culturally diverse classrooms, aimed at in-service teachers as a professional development course and at the general public.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business
Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2022-1-SK01-KA220-HED-000087306.title: Application of Inclusive Design Thinking in the Technically-Oriented Subjects at HEI
2022-1-SK01-KA220-HED-000087306.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project in response to the growing need for more inclusive and human-centered teaching approaches in higher education, especially in technical fields. As European society becomes more diverse due to demographic shifts, digitalization, migration, and post-pandemic challenges, education must evolve as well. Education should transmit knowledge and prepare students to understand and respond to real societal needs. One key challenge we identified is the lack of practical tools to help lecturers engage students in inclusion-related topics and guide them in designing meaningful, user-focused solutions. Inclusive Design Thinking (IDT) offers such a tool. IDT enables students to work creatively while considering the perspectives of underrepresented groups. Our goal was to equip lecturers with this methodology so they can empower future professionals to create accessible, equitable, and respectful solutions. We believe that a university education should prepare students to become socially responsible innovators, not merely experts. By incorporating inclusive thinking into everyday teaching practices, we aim to impact how graduates approach their future careers and contribute to a more inclusive society in the long term.

<< Objectives >>

The project's primary objective was to promote the implementation of Inclusive Design Thinking (IDT) in technically-oriented subjects at higher education institutions. Our aim was to provide lecturers with the necessary knowledge, materials, and support to integrate IDT into their teaching and foster inclusive, human-centred approaches. By doing so, the project contributes to building a more inclusive academic environment and, in the long term, a more inclusive society. To achieve this goal, we established three specific objectives. First, we aimed to provide access to high-quality IDT learning materials for lecturers and the general public; specifically, a detailed e-book and a series of instructional videos explaining the theory and application of IDT step by step. All materials were made available in eight languages and published freely on the project website. Second, we aimed to prepare lecturers to apply IDT through practical training, expert consultations, and testing of methods with students. Third, we aimed to support the implementation of IDT in real-life courses and collect best practices from teachers' experiences to guide future adopters.

<< Implementation >>

The project began with a collaborative analysis of existing literature on inclusive design, inclusion, and design thinking, followed by a joint concept design meeting during which all partners agreed on the structure, scope, and format of the study materials. This phase laid the foundation for developing the e-book, educational videos, and method templates. Building on this, we organised workshops to prepare lecturers to implement IDT in technically-oriented subjects. During these sessions, lecturers experienced the methodology through hands-on activities, consulted with experts, and subsequently led student teams to test the prepared materials and task sets. In the next phase, lecturers integrated IDT into their courses, applying it across a variety of subject areas. Their experiences were collected through structured reflection reports and presented at the final project conference. These insights were compiled into a Best Practices and Recommendations report to guide future adopters. To ensure broad impact, we also carried out dissemination activities, including three national multiplier events in Slovakia, Spain, and Croatia, aimed at sharing results and strengthening the project’s reach within the academic community.

<< Results >>

The project's primary outcome was an e-book that introduces Inclusive Design Thinking (IDT), explains each phase of the process, and provides lecturers with practical methods, filled-in templates, personas, and tips. Seven educational videos were produced to complement the book, providing both an introduction to the principles of IDT and practical guidance for each phase of the process. All materials were translated into eight languages and are freely accessible online. Another significant outcome was a collection of IDT tasks co-developed and tested by lecturers and students. Each task includes clear guidance on who is responsible, what should be done, and how to achieve the desired outcome. We also produced a Best Practices and Recommendations report based on the hands-on experience of lecturers who implemented IDT in their courses. Beyond these tangible results, the project delivered important intangible outcomes as well. Lecturers strengthened their inclusive pedagogy, communication, creativity, and problem-solving skills. By addressing real challenges faced by underrepresented groups, lecturers developed a deeper awareness of diverse social needs and learned how to incorporate these needs into course design.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-SK01-KA220-HED-000089149.title: Including EVERyone in GREEN Data Analysis
2022-1-SK01-KA220-HED-000089149.summary:
<< Background >>

According to the EC, making Europe greener and more digital are the twin challenges member states need to address and resolve in the coming decades to ensure the quality of life of European citizens. According to IDC, the amount of new data created annually has grown tenfold between 2013 and 2020, from 4.4 trillion gigabytes to 44 trillion gigabytes, and spending on big data and business analytics is predicted to grow by 11% annually in the period 2021-2025. This increase has necessitated a higher dependence on data analytics and machine learning as the need for machines for data processing purposes has grown, and it has become evident that data without analysis has very little value.
Data analytics thus holds the potential to solve issues related to climate change and global warming, but also to other social challenges. Environmental data analysis can be used to collect and analyze data on an array of environmental topics and use it as evidence for making management, financial & community decisions (Data-Driven Decision-Making).
The proposed project addressed the discrepancy between the demand and supply of business analysts, which is estimated to be half a million on the EU level. 

<< Objectives >>

1. To develop the digital and sustainability competencies of educators in higher education and trainers working with NEETs through educator training and expertise exchange
2. To increase IT students' employability and environmental consciousness through the development of a joint course curriculum and learning and teaching materials on data analysis of environmental issues in partnership with the business sector. 
3. To make higher education more inclusive of diverse groups of learners through cross-sectoral partnership, and the offering of more modular and flexible forms of education. All objectives contributed to the better integration of higher education institutions in local communities, and improved their social and environmental footprint on local and EU levels.

<< Implementation >>

- improved digital and sustainability competencies of educators (10 educators)
- improved employability and knowledge of data analysis, in particular of environmental issues, of 60 undergraduate students (real: more than 100)
- created a blended model of learning in higher education through cross-sectoral transnational cooperation among 4 higher education institutions, 2 companies from the IT and green production sectors, and a NEET academy.
The set up objectives and the expected results directly contributed to the selected project priorities. All 3 objectives supported the digital transformation of higher education contributing to the development of its digital and green capabilities and resilience. The educating of educators and students on data analytics advanced the digital skills and competences of these target groups, and the development and piloting of a new, innovative course and digital module on data analytics advanced the adoption of blended learning models in the involved institutions. In particular the inclusion of NEETs who are
not formally enrolled in the higher education institutions in the project built digital readiness and resilience promoting wider use of digital materials and tools. 

<< Results >>

- trained educators through the 2 three-day trainings, 
- skilled students from 4 universities and NEET academy
- developed course for the universities and NEET academies, but also applicable in vocational schools, business environments
- created course, piloted and optimized course
- study materials, digital contents, use cases, 6 books
- conference on environmental data analysis
- conference papers (more than 30, expected 5), workshops on the conference FRUCT (https://www.fruct.org/conferences/37/10th-dataworld-workshop/) and WorldCist (https://worldcist.org/index.php/workshops/eda-2025)
- many additional activities supporting the project dissemination (https://evergreen.fri.uniza.sk/index.php/other-activities/)
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2022-1-TR01-KA220-HED-000085597.title: Bridging the Gap Between Biotechnology and Industry: Integrating Design Thinking and Flipped Learning
2022-1-TR01-KA220-HED-000085597.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the gap between university education and industry expectations in the biotechnology sector. Research highlighted that graduates lacked transversal skills, such as problem-solving, communication, self-directed learning, and work-specific competencies required by employers. The European Commission's Bioeconomy Strategy (2018) emphasized the urgent need for upskilling to support employment growth and sustainability.

A needs analysis with 100 academicians and industry representatives in partner countries and literature reviews confirmed that graduates required further training to transfer academic knowledge into practice. The needs we addressed in the project were enhancing students' practical and transversal skills, modernizing teaching methods through flipped learning and design thinking, developing open-access learning resources, strengthening university-industry collaboration, creating industry-relevant curriculum modules and promoting employability and career readiness. 
We addressed the need to modernize higher education programs to prepare undergraduates for careers in biotechnology better, strengthening collaborations between academia and industry.



<< Objectives >>

We aimed to create a curriculum by using design thinking that enhanced the transition from higher education to the labour market in agricultural biotechnology in connection to recent technological achievements and to
develop teaching materials supporting the course delivery designed with flipped learning.
We also aimed:
1- to support undergraduate students to connect data and information explicitly with the areas of knowledge, skills and approaches needed for professional work
2- to equip undergraduate students for work in a world with continuous technological innovations
3- to foster students' self-awareness to improve their transversal skills
4- to create dynamism and synergies between the university and industry representatives to invest in innovation and innovational thinking
5- to integrate "design thinking" and "flipped learning" as a novel course delivery design

<< Implementation >>

2022-2-HU01-KA220-HED-000099410.title: The development of the innovative educational method of ACCESSIBLE tourism in Central Europe
2022-2-HU01-KA220-HED-000099410.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the growing demand for accessible tourism, i.e. tourism for people with all kinds of disabilities, driven by an ageing population and the increasing number of people with disabilities—estimated at 10–16% globally. Despite its legal, ethical, and economic importance, accessibility remains underrepresented in tourism education. Most service providers are unaware of the real needs of people with disabilities, which go far beyond ramps or reserved parking spaces. (And also, of the significant business potential that accessible tourism means for them.) There is a lack of comprehensive training materials and university-level courses addressing these issues, which is shown e.g. by the fact that there is only one Hungarian higher education institution to offer a course on accessible tourism in its training programme. Our previous experience in the PeerAct project showed the need for a deeper and broader analysis and highlighted the importance of involving people with disabilities more actively. This project filled those gaps by developing innovative educational content and involving PWD in the development process and its dissemination and addressed unmet educational needs with real-world relevance.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to address the lack of focus on accessible tourism in education and training. Although up to 10% of the global population may be affected by accessibility issues (UNWTO), this topic remained underrepresented in both tourism research and curricula. The project aimed to fill this gap by developing a comprehensive course curriculum, an innovative teaching methodology, and a study book to support tourism education in several countries. Through these tools, future tourism professionals could gain a holistic understanding of how to effectively serve people with disabilities, while also raising awareness of the legal, ethical, and economic importance of accessibility in tourism. The project also aimed to integrate the real needs and experiences of people with disabilities into the teaching materials. A further objective was sensitisation, raising awareness of society about the travel needs of people with disabilities.

<< Implementation >>

The project consisted of four main professional work packages (WPs), each contributing to innovative teaching materials tailored to the needs of people with disabilities (PWD). 
WP2 involved a comprehensive literature and legal review, collection of good practices, and analysis of data from a 1000-person survey and situation assessments among PWD in English and partner countries’ languages. This WP also created a literature database and common repository.
WP3 built on WP2 results to develop a study book with a syllabus, brief modules (4-, 8-, and 12-class modules), and an e-learning platform, available in English and translated versions.
WP4 focused on developing an innovative teaching aid and methodology, which were refined through pilot trainings involving PWD and findings of students’ feedback, ensuring practical applicability. All results were provided in English and national languages.
Throughout the project, dissemination activities such as publications, events, conferences, meetings, and workshops ensured not only broad visibility but also the effective sharing of project results, while project management activities supported the smooth implementation of all work packages.


<< Results >>

Results of the WP2 are literature and legal review, collection of good practices, analysis of the results of the situation assessment among PWD and 1000-person survey, collection of good practices on partner and on consortium level. Furthermore, a database of literature and common repository of the above-mentioned materials. Materials in English and national languages of the respective countries.
WP3 main results can be listed as follows: the results of WP2 incorporated into a study book, 4-, 8- and 12 class brief modules and E-learning platform and syllabus, in English version and translated into national languages of partners.
WP4 results are the follows: Innovative teaching aid and teaching methodology which were tested and finetuned along with the Brief modules and E-learning platform based on the findings of Pilot trainings and involvement of people with disabilities. Results are available in English and on national languages of partners.
Projects results were disseminated via national and international publications, dissemination events, conferences, and different communication tools.
In summary the project resulted in innovative novel-teaching practice-oriented gap-filling teaching materials based on real-life needs of PWD.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2023-1-AT01-KA220-HED-000156007.title: Interdisciplinary Puppetry Modules for Art Universities
2023-1-AT01-KA220-HED-000156007.summary:
<< Background >>

The LILARUM Puppet Theatre in Vienna has been committed to the development of contemporary puppetry for many years. A key obstacle to this has been the lack of puppetry training programmes at Austrian art universities, as well as in many other European countries. Art students interested in puppetry as a form of expression have had little opportunity to explore it as part of their studies. At the same time, there is a significant artistic overlap between the visual arts and puppet theatre, which is still largely untapped in higher education. The Interdisciplinary Puppetry Modules for Art Universities (iPmau) project arose from the desire of the two Austrian partners to bridge this gap and meet the existing demand from students, whilst developing interdisciplinary teaching modules that can be integrated into the existing curricula of art universities.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to develop, test and evaluate a modular, transdisciplinary teaching concept for puppetry at art colleges. Specifically, the plan was to develop a core module and two specialised modules and to pilot these at the art colleges in Vienna and Budapest. In addition, the project aimed to establish a network of art colleges, puppet theatres and artists that would provide a lasting boost to European puppetry. Particular emphasis was placed on international collaboration between students from different countries and artistic disciplines.

<< Implementation >>

Numerous activities took place as part of iPmau: three transnational project meetings (Vienna, Budapest, Osijek), a student kick-off event in Osijek (November 2024) with around 40 participants from Vienna, Budapest and Osijek, a core module at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna (December 2024) and at the Budapest University of Fine Arts (January/February 2025), as well as two specialised modules: “Materiality & Movement” (rod puppets) in Vienna (summer semester 2025) and “Expressing Abstract Terms and Sentiments” in Budapest (summer semester 2025). The programme concluded with the Closing Conference at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna (23 January 2026). This was accompanied by a PR campaign featuring video portraits of the students on YouTube, as well as the initiation of networking with art colleges, puppet theatres and research institutions across Europe.

<< Results >>

The project has produced the following results: a comprehensive List of Focuses to serve as a basis for future module development, a piloted and evaluated basic module, and two piloted and evaluated focus modules; video portraits of art students discussing their transdisciplinary connection to puppetry, available on YouTube, evaluation reports (students and teachers), media coverage in Austria, Hungary and Croatia, a growing European network, as well as a detailed proposal for a follow-up project – submitted under the title “PUPPETRY IN CRITICAL PRACTICE – Transnational Teaching, Artistic Networks & Civic Engagement”.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2023-1-AT01-KA220-HED-000162174.title: Everyone can improvise
2023-1-AT01-KA220-HED-000162174.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We are developing university courses that train for a new, socially inclusive approach to music education: Music students and music school teachers learn with and from each other how to improvise musically with socially diverse groups of pupils in an open-ended, low-threshold way. The aim is to develop and train a teaching method that enables pupils from different socio-cultural backgrounds to contribute their musical ideas outside the classical repertoire and use them to create music together.

<< Implementation >>

The partner universities establish courses together with with non-university institutions in order to provide training that is as close to practice as possible and in the same time guided by research: Associated schools and pre-schools enable students and trainees to teach socially disadvantaged children in their pupil population. Music schools provide teachers who can pass on their practical experience to students. Lecturers from the universities teach based on research on the project.

<< Results >>

Our project creates the long-term conditions to train 21 music educators per year in inclusion-oriented music improvisation pedagogy. Through the new cooperations between university and non-university institutions, 84 pupils per year from socially disadvantaged backgrounds are given the opportunity to create music together with music educators across cultural differences. The project-research makes it possible to communicate and establish the new teaching model in other regions as well.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2023-1-BE01-KA220-HED-000155735.title: LEARN4GREEN
2023-1-BE01-KA220-HED-000155735.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our Erasmus+ project aims to create an international, collaborative, and multidisciplinary online course module, focused on environment, sustainability, and health using blended and remote teaching methods. It will be integrated into the curricula of bachelor’s degree studies at the 4 partner higher education institutions, and disseminated to other higher education curricula. It will provide students with a unique opportunity to expand their learning and will be a development tool for teachers.

<< Implementation >>

To achieve our goals, we will develop three parts of the future module. Each year, we will create a third of the program through one week of online activities (lecturers, workshops) and one week of face-to-face activities (lecturers, labs, workshops in international teams, oral communication as a pitch). First-year topic: energy crisis and current environmental situation. Second-year topic: analysis methods in the environmental field. Third-year topic: green smart factories (case studies). 

<< Results >>

R1: Deliver a multidisciplinary, collaborative online module (5ECTS) with pedagogical supports and integrate it in our curricula. R2: Provide students with relevant knowledge on environmental topics to become responsible citizens of tomorrow R3: Enhance innovation within our education institutions by offering innovative learning and teaching methods R4: Develop a framework and methodology guidelines (based on the report conclusions) R5: Disseminate the model to other education institutions.

2023-1-BG01-KA220-HED-000151316.title: Academic partnership for health improvement of youth  with health disorders and special needs
2023-1-BG01-KA220-HED-000151316.summary:
<< Objectives >>

•	Increasing the level of physical culture of young people who require special needs, as well as having health problems, overweight, obesity;  
•	Developing and organizing set of special trainings and special wellness program for young people with special needs;
•	Development of an educational and methodological manual to improve the level of physical health of students with special needs with the help of special physical culture;

2023-1-CY01-KA220-HED-000158284.title: Education in Living Labs: Participatory Skills for sustainable Urban Governance
2023-1-CY01-KA220-HED-000158284.summary:
<< Objectives >>

PS-U-GO will implement Urban Living Labs (ULLs) as educational spaces involving stakeholders from the quadruple helix to experiment and test ideas and solutions to urban challenges. The ambition of the project is to enable place-based civic participation to address issues of public concern in respect to common values. The aim is to equip students with advanced participatory and soft skills for sustainable urban governance through innovative education, set in real-life environments.

<< Implementation >>

The project will review and map existing ULL methodologies and participatory approaches to establish a pedagogic framework of situated learning and a strategy for co-creation.
Online and in-person training will prepare the students to take part in their local ULLs, which will be implemented in four cities: Cottbus, Naples, Nicosia, Petralia Sottana (Palermo). The ULLs will be accompanied by a process of reflection - through qualitative research - and formal validation of educational outcomes.

<< Results >>

The key results of the project will be: a) the co-creation of urban solutions and interventions in four ULLs in European cities and b) the development of advanced participatory and soft skills of students and other stakeholders. The achievement of these results will be supported by a series of outputs, including a framework for situated learning in ULLs, a co-creation handbook, context-sensitive ULL methodologies, an online manual for participatory skills and a booklet for each ULL.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2023-1-CZ01-KA220-HED-000159335.title: Micro-credentials in Soft Skills for Healthcare Professionals and Students
2023-1-CZ01-KA220-HED-000159335.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Currently, proper learning schema based on MOOC and micro-credentials for healthcare professionals and students in soft skills is missing. So the general objective of MISS4Health is to improve competences in soft skills using a modular MOOC based on micro-credentials at EU level that certificates these competences and the pedagogical value of the MOOC. This way, HEIs and VET institutions will have the opportunity to offer shorter, more flexible, accredited programs.

<< Implementation >>

MISS4Health includes four work packages to develop and validate the MOOC based on micro-credentials. These WPs cover curricular design, content creation, micro-credentials establishment and interactive resources, as well as a double loop validation that assures the overall quality of the MOOC. Besides, a joint workshop for staff, 7 multiplier events and a closing workshop are planned. Management, quality, and dissemination and exploitation activities complete the workplan.

<< Results >>

MISS4Health will produce a high quality and validated MOOC based on micro-credentials. Besides, learning materials including guidelines and recommendations will be created. Additionally management, quality, dissemination, and sustainability plans will conduct the project and contribute to its widespread. And finally, several intangible results will be obtained, such as feedback and motivation of end-users and stakeholders.

2023-1-EL01-KA220-HED-000167028.title: Bridging the Gap: Research Ethics Training and Education
2023-1-EL01-KA220-HED-000167028.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Improve availability and accessibility of research ethics training and education
Foster collaboration and knowledge-sharing among researchers, research institutions and Research Ethics Committees (RECs)
Promote responsible and inclusive approach to AI research
Enhance competitiveness of research in Europe.

<< Implementation >>

Develop and deliver research ethics training and education programs
Create and maintain a research ethics training and education network
Develop and provide digital content and tools to support research ethics training and education
Organize a young researcher competition for the creation of social media content on research ethics
Foster collaboration and knowledge-sharing among researchers, research institutions and RECs
Regularly review and update ethical guidelines and best practices

<< Results >>

Improved awareness knowledge and skills of researchers, research institutions and RECs in conducting ethical research

2023-1-ES01-KA220-HED-000155981.title: Developing SustaINable Skills for DesiGners in Additive Manufacturing
2023-1-ES01-KA220-HED-000155981.summary:
<< Background >>

SING for GREEN (SFG) was launched to bridge the gap between European Green Deal goals and manufacturing workforce skills. While Additive Manufacturing (AM) inherently reduces raw material waste, these benefits depend on sustainable design expertise. Our project addressed three critical needs:
1.	Skill Alignment: To meet the industry's demand for "green skills," we developed two EQF Level 7 Competence Units (CUs). Through "AM Life Cycle Assessment," designers learned to analyse carbon footprints and mitigate data-related risks. Through "Sustainability-oriented Design Strategies in AM" we equipped them with technical skills in part consolidation, topology optimization, and lightweighting (lattice structures) to maximize resource efficiency.
2.	Industrial Evolution: SFG supported the green transition of the manufacturing sector by aligning workforce competence development in AM with the EU’s 2050 climate-neutrality targets, contributing to the advancement of greener, more sustainable industrial value chains.
3.	Environmental Impact: SFG empowered AM designers to make informed decisions using the GreenComp framework, directly reducing energy consumption and material waste. 


<< Objectives >>

By implementing the SFG project, we aimed to better align higher education with the evolving needs of the green and digital labour market, with a specific focus on AM and sustainable design. The primary objective was to address the existing skills gap by equipping both higher education students and adult learners with the competences required for emerging green jobs linked to AM technologies. 
More specifically, SFG sought to: (i) develop an innovative curriculum to train AM designers to adopt sustainable design approaches; (ii) create Open Educational Resources (OERs) to support higher education teachers and learners in mastering sustainable AM strategies; and (iii) validate all educational materials through national piloting phases to ensure their practical relevance, accessibility, and long-term usability.
Ultimately, by tailoring course content to real industrial needs and delivering freely accessible training resources, the project contributed to reducing skills mismatches and unemployment, and promoted more resource-efficient and sustainable manufacturing practices across the EU.


<< Implementation >>

The SFG project was executed through a structured, multi-phase methodology based on a rigorous research-to-action path:
•	Research & Analysis: We conducted extensive desk research, followed by interviews with 35 participants and focus groups with 17 industry experts. This ensured the project was grounded in real-market needs and expert insights.
•	Design & Development: Based on these findings, a curriculum design workshop was held with consortium members, leading to the creation of a specialized curriculum. Comprensive training materials were developed, including instructional videos and a digital manual. To ensure high-quality delivery, we also organized "Train the Trainer" sessions with 13 trainers (11 face to face and 2 online) of partner organisations. 
•	Validation: The curriculum and materials were rigorously tested during the national piloting phases with 145 participants, allowing for refinement based on direct learner feedback.
•	Continuous Activities: Throughout the project lifecycle, project management ensured seamless cooperation between partners (for further details see WP1), while dissemination activities (for further details see WP5) maximized the project's visibility and impact.



<< Results >>

The project results include: 
-	Needs analysis report, that reveals several skills and knowledge gaps in AM technologies and processes, materials knowledge, product life cycle and environmental impact, as well as the economic and marketing benefits of sustainability. These gaps guided the developing of the SFG curriculum for AM designers.
-	EQF level 7 curriculum structure and competence unis framework, focused on two new competence units: “Additive Manufacturing Lifecycle Assessment” and “Sustainability-Driven Design Strategies in Additive Manufacturing”. 
-	Open educational resources, including slide decks, tutorial videos, and assessment methods.
-	Training manual, created to help the effective implementation of the training courses. 
-	National pilots results report, including feedback from the trainees and trainers who tested the training materials. 
-	Multiple dissemination materials (webpage, press releases, leaflets, roll-up, posters, articles, newsletters, videos, etc)
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2023-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000164618.title: Boost your international mobility
2023-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000164618.summary:
<< Background >>

The project arose from a shared observation: through their experiences of mobility, volunteering, community involvement or non-formal and informal learning, young people develop numerous transferable skills that remain insufficiently identified, formalised and recognised, particularly during their transition to higher education or the labour market. This situation creates a disconnect between the skills actually acquired and their recognition by higher education institutions, youth professionals and employers, thereby limiting young people’s ability to capitalise on these experiences as they enter the world of work. The project also addressed the need to develop innovative educational tools to support young people in identifying and capitalising on their learning outcomes, whilst strengthening links between international mobility, engagement, training and employability. Through a common European approach, the project aimed to produce transferable resources, foster cooperation between the youth, higher education and employment sectors, and promote mobility and engagement.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to strengthen young people’s ability to identify, recognise, value and transfer the skills acquired through their experiences of mobility, volunteering and civic engagement, in order to promote their employability and their transition into higher education and the labour market. It sought to boost their self-confidence, their sense of legitimacy and their ability to present their achievements in academic and professional contexts. The partnership also sought to develop a common European approach to the recognition of non-formal and informal learning, based on the exchange of best practice, needs analysis and an understanding of national contexts. Finally, the project aimed to produce innovative, accessible and transferable educational resources, including interactive games, enabling young people, youth workers and higher education institutions to better facilitate the recognition of skills and support sustainable pathways to integration.

<< Implementation >>

Firstly, focus groups and interviews were organised with young people, youth workers and employment practitioners in order to gather qualitative data and contribute to the development of the project’s various deliverables. These activities helped to identify the needs and obstacles faced by young people, as well as best practices relating to the recognition of mobility and engagement experiences.
The consortium also organised two training events. These sessions provided an opportunity to present the materials developed, to test them in a collaborative setting and to improve the tools based on participants’ feedback and the exchange of best practices.
At the same time, three conferences were organised to raise awareness amongst a wider audience of the challenges relating to young people’s employability, international mobility and the recognition of skills acquired through non-formal education. Finally, several multiplier events were organised in the partner countries to ensure the dissemination of the project’s results and to raise their profile amongst local, national and European stakeholders.

<< Results >>

The consortium first carried out a comparative analysis of young people’s employability in relation to the international mobility of students and recent graduates. This analysis is based on interviews and case studies conducted by each partner with young people and stakeholders in the employment sector. It helped to identify common trends, barriers and best practices across the various national contexts represented in the project.
A guide was also designed to strengthen organisations’ methodological skills in supporting young people towards the recognition and promotion of their experiences.

The project also produced several fun and accessible tools aimed at raising awareness amongst a wider audience: card games, a TikTok challenge and a personality test. These tools help young people to reflect personally on their skills, their career paths and their ability to present their experiences in a relevant way.
Finally, following the training activities, a self-guidance toolkit was developed to enable young people to work independently on the link between their personal experiences and their career plans.

2023-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000158143.title: Summer schools on environmental protection, sustainability & ecological behavior to support the integration and inclusion of migrants & refugees in the higher education – enhance the university professors competences
2023-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000158143.summary:
<< Background >>

We launched the IntegratEU project to tackle several related challenges in Europe. These include helping migrants and refugees, especially those from Ukraine, to integrate and access higher education, as well as promoting environmental awareness and sustainable behavior. Many universities lacked practical and flexible tools to help staff work with diverse and vulnerable groups. Our project aimed to improve teachers’ skills in inclusive and intercultural education, and to give migrants and refugees better information about higher education and support services. IntegratEU brought these goals together through summer schools, outdoor learning, and digital resources, connecting social inclusion with environmental education, European values, and active participation in local communities.

<< Objectives >>

IntegratEU set out to create a practical and innovative educational approach to help higher education institutions better support the inclusion and integration of migrants, refugees, and other vulnerable groups. The project focused on improving university teachers’ skills in running inclusive summer schools about environmental protection, sustainability, and ecological behavior. It combined theory with hands-on, outdoor, and digital learning, so participants could gain practical skills, connect with local communities, and learn more about European values. Another goal was to give migrants and refugees clear information about higher education systems, how to enroll, available support services, and opportunities in the partner countries. By developing training materials, integration guidelines, outdoor activities, a digital platform, and an interactive library, the project aimed to build a complete educational ecosystem that universities, NGOs, and other groups could use and adapt. In the end, IntegratEU wanted to bring together environmental responsibility, social inclusion, intercultural dialogue, and active citizenship in one unified model for higher education.

<< Implementation >>

The project carried out a series of coordinated activities in five main areas. First, the team created a Conceptual and Methodological Framework to set a common teaching approach and show how environmental education, inclusion, and European values fit together. Next, the partners developed the IntegratEU Training and Integration Pack, which includes the Handbook for Summer Schools, a Collection of Outdoor Activities, the Manual on Integration, the Manual on Organizing IntegratEU Summer Schools, and a Guidebook for Migrants and Refugees about higher education and environmental protection. They also built a multilingual digital platform and interactive library to give open access to these materials, learning resources, and assessment tools. The project held both in-person and online meetings, quality reviews, outreach activities, newsletters, social media updates, and national events to promote the work. All materials and digital tools were tested in each partner country through a structured pilot process with external higher education experts, monitoring meetings, and national reports. The team compared the feedback and used it to revise and improve the project outputs before sharing them more widely.

<< Results >>

The project delivered a well-connected set of educational, methodological, and digital resources. These included the Conceptual and Methodological Framework, the IntegratEU Handbook for Summer Schools, the Collection of Outdoor Activities, the Manual on Integration, the Manual on Organising IntegratEU Summer Schools, and the Guidebook for Migrants and Refugees on higher education and environmental protection in the partner countries. All materials are available on a multilingual digital platform and interactive library, along with learning resources and assessment tools. The project also produced national piloting reports and a comparative report, based on feedback from experts in six countries. This feedback helped improve the usability, accessibility, and teaching value of the materials. Other results included stronger skills among university staff in inclusive and hands-on teaching, better cooperation between universities and civil society, and increased awareness of sustainability, ecological behavior, European values, and migrant inclusion. The project also created a model for running inclusive environmental summer schools and set the stage for ongoing use of its materials in university teaching, lifelong learning
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2023-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000161576.title: Digital literacy enables up-to-date sleep medicine in inclusive healthcare
2023-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000161576.summary:
<< Background >>

The eSleep_dHealth project was initiated to address the growing challenges related to sleep disorders and the rapid digital transformation of healthcare. Although digital tools offer new possibilities for diagnosing and managing conditions such as obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), these advances are not equally accessible to all. Vulnerable groups – particularly the older adults – often lack digital literacy, limiting their access to digital health solutions.
At the same time, partner universities lacked applied sleep medicine and digital health content in their curricula, as well as opportunities for students to develop innovation, entrepreneurship, and social problem-solving skills. Teaching staff had limited experience in applying methodologies, such as open pedagogy and design thinking, for the development of new educational programmes.
To address these gaps, the project partners project jointly developed a new training programme consisting of curriculum, Open Educational Resources (OERs) and a Joint Social Innovation Incubator. This integrated structure enabled students to acquire essential knowledge and apply it in practice by working with real-world data and collaborating directly with vulnerable groups.


<< Objectives >>

The eSleep_dHealth project objectives are:
•	O1 Strengthen collaboration among the project partners – E.C.H.R. d.o.o. (NetHub), University of Split (UNIST), Reykjavik University (RU), University of Crete (UOC), and Mediterranean Economic Foresight Institute (IPEMED) – through the development of joint training programme.
•	O2 Develop teaching staff and student competencies in open pedagogy and design thinking for curriculum and content design.
•	O3 Enhance the capacity of universities to foster social innovation competencies among students and staff.
•	O4 Train students of medical and engineering professions to become drivers of social innovation to reduce prevalent harsh consequences of sleep disorders.
•	O5 Contribute to reducing the digital divide affecting older adults and populations in remote areas.
•	O6 Establish the foundation for a joint master’s programme on sleep medicine, digital health, and entrepreneurship across the partner universities.


<< Implementation >>

The eSleep_dHealth project was structured into five Work Packages (WPs), each with a clear focus and set of activities.
WP1 – Project Management ensured effective coordination, monitoring, and quality management, including regular partner and Steering Committee meetings.
WP2 – Design of eSleep_dHealth Curriculum and OERs included the first short staff training on open pedagogy and design thinking, the development of a three-module curriculum and OERs, and assessment of the curriculum to ensure quality and applicability.
WP3 – Design of Social Innovation Toolkit for Digital Sleep Medicine involved the second short staff training on fostering innovation skills in higher education, the creation of the Social Innovation Toolkit, and internal and external assessment of the Tookit.
WP4 – Implementation and Assessment of eSleep_dHealth OERs and Joint Social Innovation Incubator focused on implementation of the course, launching the Joint Social Innovation Incubator, and organizing two learning expeditions for work with vulnerable groups.
WP5 – Communication, Dissemination, and Exploitation aimed to maximize project visibility and ensure sustainability through the website, social media, promotional materials, and four conferences.


<< Results >>

The eSleep_dHealth project produced following results:

•	WP 1 - 4 Partnership Agreements signed, Project Management Plan developed, 4 transnational partner meetings held, 16 Steering Committee meetings held, 8 internal progress reports prepared
•	WP2 - 15 participants trained in design thinking and open pedagogy, 15 Europass certificates issued, eSleep_dHealth Curriculum and OERs developed, curriculum assessment prepared.
•	WP3 – 17 participants trained in innovation skills, 17 Europass certificates issued, Social Innovation Toolkit for digital literacy and inclusive sleep medicine interventions developed, internal and external assessment conducted.
•	WP4 - eSleep_dHealth course (84 students) and Joint Social Innovation Incubator (35 students) implemented, OERs and incubator assessment developed, 2 Learning Expeditions organized (Crete, Split) and in total 59 Europass certificates issued, 11 student innovation solutions developed during Learning Expeditions.
•	WP5 - Communication, Dissemination, and Exploitation Plan developed, project website, logo, and promo materials created, 4 project conference organized, 2 promotional videos produced, 13 social media posts and 19 web articles published.

2023-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000164970.title: Micro-qualifications in seafarers' education and training
2023-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000164970.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the MICROMET project because there was a clear gap in the recognition of short learning programmes and micro-credentials in maritime education and training. The main need was to define guidelines for recognising learning outcomes acquired through STCW and non-STCW short courses, especially when seafarers continue into undergraduate studies and those previous courses are not recognised, even when the content overlaps with degree programmes.
The project addressed the lack of common rules, data, and procedures for recognising micro-credentials across maritime higher education institutions and training centres. 
The project also aimed to support lifelong learning in maritime education, make certification and recognition of short courses easier, and enhance the attractiveness of maritime study and training programmes. Another important need was to improve the validation of competencies acquired through short learning programmes and to strengthen cooperation between higher education institutions, training centres, and shipping companies.
The project was also needed because maritime education is inherently international, but cooperation between institutions across countries was still limited. 

<< Objectives >>

The main objective was to determine how micro-credentials from short learning programmes could be recognised within maritime higher education. This included identifying overlaps between short courses and study programmes, analysing current practices, and developing a methodology for recognition and validation of competencies.
We also wanted to improve educational and training programmes for seafarers by making them more responsive to labour market needs and individual career paths. Another key objective was to improve processes for recognising and validating competencies gained through STCW and non-STCW short courses, so that learning outcomes could be more easily transferred into formal education and professional development.
A further objective was to strengthen cooperation between the institutions and organisations involved in providing and recognising short learning programmes. 
Through these objectives, we wanted to support lifelong learning in maritime education, make short courses easier to certify and recognise, and increase the attractiveness of maritime education and training programmes. 

<< Implementation >>

Activities implemented in the project:
WP2-A 1. Identification of specific needs and previous research in the field of additional short learning programmes.
WP2-A2. Collecting data about non-STCW short learning programmes. 
WP2-A3. Analysis of non-STCW short learning programmes’ contents and outcomes. 
WP3-A1. Analysis of the current micro-credential status at MHEIs.
WP3-A2. Analysis of key stakeholders’ observation related to micro-credentials.
WP3-A3. Review of current curricula and practices for micro-credentials recognition at MHEIs.
WP3-A4. Determine the level of understanding the micro-credentials at the MHEIs and barriers for their recognition.
WP4-A1. Identification of the current micro-credential status at maritime training centres.
WP4-A2. Identification of changes that should be carried out at maritime training centres.
WP4-A3. Development of staff training on learning outcomes, ECTS points and  micro-credentials at maritime training centres.
WP5-A1. Analysis of the current situation on the internationalisation and recognition related to micro-credentials.
WP5-A2. Evaluation of quality control process related to micro-credentials.
WP5-A3. Analyse understanding of Bologna Tools usage in micro- credentials recognition.

<< Results >>

The MICROMET project produced a set of concrete outputs that directly supported its objectives. Its main results included comparative analyses of micro-credential status and recognition mechanisms, a methodology for recognising and validating competencies from STCW and non-STCW short courses, reports on the current situation and future needs of the maritime sector, surveys, mapping of competencies, best-practice reports, self-assessment tools, quality-control reports, round tables, workshops, pilot staff training, training materials, conference presentations, scientific papers, and a final WP-level reporting framework. Beyond the formal deliverables, the project created a strong transnational cooperation platform linking universities, a private maritime training centre, and a shipping company. This cooperation improved knowledge exchange, enabled comparison of national and institutional practices, and made the results more relevant to real sector needs. The project also achieved significant dissemination through conference participation, scientific publications, workshops, and a final conference, which increased the visibility and potential use of the results.

2023-1-IE02-KA220-HED-000151855.title: INSPIRE: Innovative Support for Promoting Refugee Entrepreneurship in Tourism
2023-1-IE02-KA220-HED-000151855.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the INSPIRE project because we recognised an urgent need to support refugees in establishing their own tourism ventures. Funded under Erasmus+ Key Action 2 and led by the Technological University of the Shannon in Ireland, INSPIRE runs from late 2023 to late 2025. It offers a valuable platform to collaborate with partners across Europe—Belgium, Croatia, Türkiye, and Ukraine—to create practical, high‑impact resources for refugee tourism entrepreneurs. The project enabled us to develop tools that help refugees overcome the economic and social challenges they face. Through training, digital tools, and shared learning, we aimed to empower individuals in refugee‑like situations to build businesses that support their economic resilience and help them integrate into new communities. Refugees often have restricted access to essential supports such as finance, training, and business networks. INSPIRE provided, and continues to provide, a bespoke good‑practice guide, training course, and digital badge to bridge that gap. Generic entrepreneurship programmes rarely address the specific experiences and constraints of refugees. INSPIRE addressed this by producing resources built directly from desk research and interviews.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the INSPIRE project, our aim was to provide meaningful, practical support for refugees who wish to create tourism enterprises. We wanted to ensure that people in refugee-like situations are not only able to access opportunities for self-employment, but also feel equipped and confident to succeed in their host communities. More specifically, we wanted to achieve the following:
Develop tailored resources
Create a good practice guide, training programme, and digital badge designed specifically for refugee tourism entrepreneurs, based on real evidence gathered from research and interviews across several countries.
Increase access to support
Build a comprehensive and easy-to-use database of supports, delivered via a website and mobile app, that includes information on training, funding, mentoring, and networking opportunities.
Promote skills and confidence
Strengthen entrepreneurial and digital skills among refugees, while recognising and validating their achievements through structured training and digital credentials.
Encourage integration and economic resilience
Support refugees in developing sustainable tourism ventures that can improve their livelihoods and increase their independence

<< Implementation >>

In the INSPIRE project, we implemented a set of activities designed to support refugees in establishing tourism enterprises. We began with desk research, interviews and engagement with refugees, practitioners and stakeholders to identify barriers and highlight good practice. Based on this evidence, we produced a Good Practice Guide offering concrete recommendations. A tailored webinar or in person training programme was then developed, combining entrepreneurial and digital skills, supported by the creation of a digital badge to recognise learning achievements. Alongside this, we built a searchable online database of relevant supports, including funding, mentoring, training and networking opportunities, with a mobile app created for greater accessibility. All outputs were piloted with refugee and NGO participants to test usability and effectiveness. Finally, we delivered dissemination activities such as partner meetings, multiplier events and online communication to ensure the results reached a wide audience and could be adapted for use across Europe.

<< Results >>

The INSPIRE project delivered a range of concrete outputs and measurable results. We carried out over 210 interviews with refugees, educators and NGOs, alongside policy reviews from five countries, to build a solid evidence base. 28 workshops were held with refugees, educators and NGOs, engaging over 200 participants who completed the training and received the INSPIRE digital badge. Our tailored online course achieved more than 200 completions, while the Good Practice Guide was downloaded over 500 times. A searchable database of supports was created, and the digital badge system was established to validate learning. Three transnational partner meetings were organised to coordinate progress and ensure consistency across countries. Dissemination reached wider audiences through social media, where we gained over 100 followers, as well as through a published research paper and presentations at academic conferences. Together, these outputs provided practical tools, validated training, and strong evidence to support refugee entrepreneurship in the tourism sector across Europe.
topics: Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

2023-1-IT02-KA220-HED-000154539.title: EDU-Home
2023-1-IT02-KA220-HED-000154539.summary:
<< Background >>

EDU-Home originates from the existing barrier to the mobility represented mainly by the housing. Indeed, accommodation is often perceived as an obstacle, as it is quite common for students to be dealing with fake advertising, solutions that are too expensive and where they would not feel safe.
EDU-Home proposal was aimed at addressing the following needs:
-	increasing the quantity and quality of mobilities and the quality of services offered during these programs; 
-	enhancing the quality of life of students and staff involved in international mobility 
-	reducing obstacles to full equality of opportunity 
-	promoting inclusiveness especially towards mobility participants 
- 	contributing to the concrete realisation of broader European Education Area such as social inclusion, environmental sustainability and a wider use of digital tools.

<< Objectives >>

EDU-Home main goal was to foster inclusiveness in HEI systems by increasing the quality and quantity of transnational mobilities, and concretely supporting mobility participants in the search process of a safe and affordable accommodation. EDU-Home aimed at creating a freely accessible online platform for smooth and effective dialogue and cooperation between the actors and stakeholders involved in the accommodation and mobility sectors, ensuring transparency, reliability and timeliness to address the asymmetries that make housing a barrier to mobility. The platform, thanks to the model it relies on, could be adopted on a larger scale in the future.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were carried out:first,a research was carried out to define the characteristics and needs of the different actors involved in demand,offer and intermediation of the housing sector in each of the partners’ countries.This represented the basis for the development of the platform governance model describing all its features,structure,policies,the partners’ different roles and the countries for which they are supervisor.All partners provided the translation for each platform section.The platform was tested from the different users’ point of views and after its technical and formal finetuning, it was officially validated and populated with real accommodation solutions.Indeed,the platform was made available in 5 languages,and it is fully accessible,operational in real scenarios and ready to be adopted by other HEIs and extended to the participation of other stakeholders.Partners also developed guidelines and training packages for both demand users and providers,as well as guidelines for the implementation,which were presented to the wide audience invited to the final dissemination event that were hosted by each partner to mainstream the project results and give a wider outreach and visibility to the platform.

<< Results >>

The main results of the EDU-Home project are:
-	An open-access OER platform available in five languages, featuring a fully custom-built codebase developed and governed by the consortium, giving it full discretion over whether and how the source code is shared;
-	Guideline-Training package for offer and intermediary users in 5 languages;
-	Guidelines for demand users in 5 languages;
-	Guidelines for implementation and mainstreaming in 5 languages;
-	Data rendering report in 5 languages.

2023-1-IT02-KA220-HED-000158157.title: ACTIONS TO BOOST COMPETENCES ON DIGITALISATION & ENTREPRENEURSHIP IN ARTISTIC PROFESSIONS
2023-1-IT02-KA220-HED-000158157.summary:
<< Background >>

DIG.ENT/ART was conceived in response to a structural gap identified within higher education institutions in the arts: while artistic training remains strong in technical and creative domains, digital transformation and entrepreneurial competences are often insufficiently integrated into curricula. At European level, the cultural and creative sectors are undergoing rapid technological change, requiring artists and artisans to master digital tools, sustainable production approaches and self-positioning strategies in increasingly competitive markets.
Through its experience in vocational and higher training in the CCI sector, partners of the project observed that students and young professionals frequently lack structured pathways to develop transversal skills combining digitalisation, sustainability and entrepreneurship.
The project therefore addressed the need to modernize art education by building a shared European framework, testing innovative training pilots, and creating practical tools (Skills Box) to support institutional change. DIG.ENT/ART aimed to strengthen the employability, adaptability and future-readiness of emerging artistic professionals.

<< Objectives >>

Through DIG.ENT/ART, the partnership aimed to contribute to a structural modernisation of higher education in the artistic field by addressing the gap between traditional art training and the accelerating digital and entrepreneurial transformation of the Cultural and Creative Industries. The core objective was not only to introduce new contents, but to embed digitalisation, sustainability and entrepreneurial competences into artistic education in a coherent, systemic and transferable way.
The project sought to develop a shared European competence framework for emerging artistic professionals, grounded in research and stakeholder dialogue, and to translate it into a modular and adaptable training model supported by concrete pilots, co-design workshops and interdisciplinary experimentation. By testing and refining this model across partner institutions, DIG.ENT/ART aimed to generate evidence-based practices capable of strengthening institutional capacity, fostering transnational cooperation and supporting a long-term transformation of art education ecosystems in Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The implementation of DIG.ENT/ART was organized across interconnected WPs ensuring coordination, research, experimentation and dissemination.
WP1 focused on project management and coordination. The partnership established a shared monitoring framework, regular online meetings, financial tracking tools, reporting templates and risk management procedures to guarantee alignment and compliance throughout the project lifecycle.
WP2 consisted of a comprehensive baseline analysis combining desk research, semi-structured interviews with stakeholders in Italy, France and Croatia, and collection of European good practices. The findings were structured into three Skills Matrices (Digitalization, Sustainable Materials and Entrepreneurship), forming the conceptual backbone of the project.
WP3 translated this framework into concrete training pilots, workshops and interdisciplinary labs addressing AI in artistic production, digital animation, 3D scanning and printing, robotics, audiovisual experimentation and ethical reflection on technology.
WP4 systematized results into a structured curriculum and the DIG.ENT/ART Skills Box, while WP5 ensured communication, stakeholder engagement and dissemination (public events and final conference).

<< Results >>

DIG.ENT/ART produced a structured set of research, training and policy outputs across 3 partner countries. The Baseline Analysis involved stakeholders from Italy, France and Croatia and resulted in 3 Skills Matrices covering Digitalization, Sustainable Materials and Entrepreneurship. WP3 delivered more than 15 training initiatives, including 5 workshops, 1 masterclass, 1 seminar and 1 study day in Marseille, 3 specialized labs in Dubrovnik (3D scanning – 15h; Plastic Transformation – 4h; AI/AR/VR – 20h)cand multiple modules in Ravenna.
Over 150 students and graduates participated in structured training activities, producing prototypes, interactive installations, digitally fabricated objects and AI-based artistic works.
WP4 resulted in the DIG.ENT/ART Skills Box, including an Ethical Charter for Generative AI, a Policy Paper on Digital Transformation, and a Digital Strategy Guide for Emerging Artists. Additional results include a shared evaluation system, documented reports per country, and strengthened institutional capacity for curriculum innovation.

2023-1-LV01-KA220-HED-000157623.title: Building an Eco-Friendly Future with Robots
2023-1-LV01-KA220-HED-000157623.summary:
<< Background >>

It is no secret that there is a lot of discussion around the world about global environmental problems that have accumulated around us and affect the future of the world. Similarly, new, up-to-date, and innovative teaching methods are also a growing issue. 
For the most part, it can be said that the learning process begins in preschool, with both innovative teaching methods and an initial understanding of environmental protection. 

This project was initiated with the aim of combining globally significant environmental awareness issues with the preschool education process and the educational potential of robotics for young learners, all of which could be incorporated into inquiry-based learning, bringing it together in learning model. 
In order to implement changes at the preschool education level, it is necessary to start with the adults who develop, plan, and manage this learning process for young children, which is why the most important target audience is preservice and current preschool teachers. 

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the GREENCODE project was to improve the skills and training opportunities of pre-service preschool teachers in order to equip them with
the necessary skills to stimulate children's interest in the future world and develop their environmental awareness. 
The project focused on strengthening the capacity of the education sector to provide high-quality environmental education and algorithmic thinking training
using educational robotics at the preschool level in partner countries.

<< Implementation >>

Project partners in all member countries met with pre-service and in-service preschool and ICT teachers in various events, such as focus groups and discussions, roundtable meetings and workshops, and collected data, teachers' opinions, insights, and experiences, promoting the exchange of information that was later used in the development of the project results. The literature review also supported the content development process, based on both individual and team contributions. 
The effectiveness of the project results was tested in a pilot process in which 97 preschool teacher students were trained. In countries where no pilot activities were carried out, the materials were distributed to universities and existing preschool teachers, (more than 50 teachers in Germany, Ireland, Turkey, and Italy). Volunteer teachers were encouraged to use the teaching materials in their teaching practice.
The materials were also tested in several events and in several preschool institutions, together with children and with the support of preschool teachers. 

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs and results of the Greencode project that were delivered:

1. Preparing Future Educators: a Digital Handbook on Robotics and Environmental Education

2. Preparing Future Educators: a Higher Education Course Curriculum on Robotics and Environmental Education

3. Preparing Future Educators: Lesson Plans - Supporting the Higher Education Course Curriculum on
Robotics and Environmental Education

4. Activity Book - Educational Robotics and Environmental Education in Early Childhood Education & Activity Book: Printable pages

5. Video Tutorials for Preservice Teachers and Current Teachers: 
1) Inquiry-based Learning Approach 
2) Creating Eco Friendly Habits 
3) Creating Engaging Contexts 
4) Algorithmic Thinking 
5) Learning Robots and Spatial Skills (The project's YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/@GreencodeProject)

6. Dream City: Set of Cards & Manual of the Set of Cards for Storytelling with Educational Robotics

All results have also been published on the project website (https://www.greencodeproject.com/).
