2023-1-RO01-KA220-HED-000164767.title: Partnership for innovation on the exchange of best practices and the design of joint collaborative initiatives at European level related to the awareness of the effects of contamination on human health
2023-1-RO01-KA220-HED-000164767.summary:
<< Background >>

The INNO-SAFE-LIFE project was created to address the shared need among EU partners to modernise education, strengthen interdisciplinary cooperation, and raise awareness of the link between environmental pollution and human health. The consortium applied to develop innovative, inclusive, and sustainable approaches connecting academia, research, industry, and society.
For teachers and specialists, the project responded to the need for updated theoretical and practical knowledge, improved digital and foreign language skills, and stronger international collaboration through modern teaching/learning methods.
For students, it addressed the need to enhance communication, teamwork, mobility, and entrepreneurial skills, while aligning training with the demands of the EU labour market and promoting creativity and innovation in environmental and health-related fields.
For entrepreneurs, the focus was on access to up-to-date, internationally recognised practices and technologies, and for the public, on clear, accessible information about sustainability, responsible resource use, health protection.
The project aimed to build a EU network of cooperation that promotes education, sustainability, health awareness for a cleaner, healthier future.

<< Objectives >>

Through the project, the consortium aimed to build a strong international and interdisciplinary partnership connecting education, research, and industry to address the growing challenges of pollution and its direct effects on human health. The project sought to enhance awareness, promote sustainability, and strengthen the quality of higher education through innovative, collaborative approaches.
The main goal was to develop lasting cooperation across Europe, fostering the exchange of good practices and creating a shared framework for interdisciplinary learning. By uniting experts from biomedical, agricultural, pharmaceutical, and environmental disciplines, the project worked to improve teaching and training, modernise curricula, and stimulate research aligned with EU sustainability goals.
It also aimed to strengthen translational links between science and society, promote internationalisation through mobility and collaboration, and empower students, educators, and professionals to act as agents of change. The project sought to contribute to a healthier, cleaner, and more sustainable Europe by fostering knowledge, innovation, collectively responsability in reducing pollution and protecting human well-being.

<< Implementation >>

The project was built around 4 main work packages (WPs), each contributing to its objectives through coordinated actions by all partners.
WP1 – Project Management, the consortium ensured efficient coordination, planning, monitoring, and financial control. The Management Team, led by CO, oversaw project implementation, maintained communication among partners, organised quarterly meetings, and ensured quality and risk management. Shared digital tools and reporting guaranteed transparency and timely progress.
WP2 – Training, Teaching, and Learning, 8 international training sessions were organised for staff and students, combining theory and practice on topics such as soil-to-food contamination, toxicology, antimicrobial resistance, and sustainable resource use. Over 22 experts and 100 students were trained, gaining strong interdisciplinary skills.
WP3 – Research and Development, partners produced 3 major outputs (Curriculum, Guide, Course) all in 5 languages, integrating environmental sustainability, health, and green innovation into higher education.
WP4 – Communication and Dissemination, 6 international workshops, 12 newspapers, 1 website, to promote open-access results and raise awareness on pollution, health, sustainability.

<< Results >>

The project generated concrete and lasting results that directly supported its goals of promoting inclusion, sustainability, and awareness of the link between environment and human health. The consortium developed 3 major educational outputs: Curriculum, Guide, Course, all produced in 5 languages and integrated into university programs to enhance teaching and research in sustainability and health.
Through eight international training sessions, the project trained more than 22 specialists and over 100 students, equipping them with interdisciplinary skills in environmental protection, food safety, toxicology, and sustainable innovation. In parallel, six international workshops brought together more than 200 participants, fostering collaboration among academia, industry, and public authorities.
The partners produced 12 newspapers and launched the project website (https://inno-safe-life.com/), offering open access to all materials. These outcomes advanced the Erasmus+ priorities of inclusion, digitalisation, and civic engagement, while raising public awareness about pollution and sustainability. Collectively, they built a strong European network committed to environmental health and innovative education.

2023-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000154000.title: INCLUSIVE SOCIAL EDUCATION FIT FOR HEALTHY LIFE-STYLE: PREVENTING OBESITY IN YOUNG ADULTS
2023-1-SI01-KA220-HED-000154000.summary:
<< Background >>

According to the World Health Organization (2022), more than one billion people worldwide are obese, including 650 million adults, 340 million adolescents and 39 million children. Obesity is associated with a serious burden due to high morbidity, mortality and impact on quality of life. Obese people face societal stigmatisation and suffer from insecurity and other psychologically motivated frustrations, which influence the quality of life. Overweight and obesity are linked to more deaths worldwide than underweight, and it is a growing problem, rivalling world hunger in the number of people that suffer from it. Information on the dangers of obesity is available in various forms (primarily online sources), however our needs analysis demonstrated that in the university environment, students are rarely offered an intentional, strategically planned, professional and direct approach (e.g. in a form of a curriculum, handbooks, workshops or other learning material) on how important it is develop healthy life-style habits and prevent obesity. This was the primary need the project addressed - to offer students multilingual tools and methods for preventing obesity and developing healthy lifestyle habits.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objectives of the project were: (1) to create permanent, sustainable, digital and multilingual learning and teaching tools, methods and practices for developing healthy lifestyle habits and preventing obesity in the university environement; (2) to create tools and practises for developing a sensitive communication competences in the field of obesity which is necessary to avoid stigmatization; (3) to prepare guidelines for university canteen staff on including techniques for preparation of healthy meals, and (4) to implement and accreditate the project results at the university level. This corresponds with the chosen priorities of “Stimulating awareness on healthy lifestyle habits” and “Building inclusive higher education systems”. All objectives can be included in the higher education programs at the university level and were developed for the target group of students and young adults, but, considering the importance of preventing obesity and developing healthy lifestyle habits, the project outcomes can also be used by other sectors of society. All project outcomes were translated into 6 partners' languages (Engish, Slovene, Slovak, Portuguese, Norwegian and Croatian).

<< Implementation >>

-WP2: online survey for students in all partner countries on healthy lifestyle habits (1533 students' responses); developing a digital handbook on preventing obesity; project kick-off meeting; a multiplier event (webinar);
-WP3: desktop research on official guidelines for canteen staff; an online workshop for partners and target groups; pre- and post-questionnaires on preparation of healthy meals for canteen staff; implementation of posters for canteen staff; transnational meeting; a multiplier event (a conference).
-WP4: developing guidelines for a a sensitive communication "How to communicate without offending" based on surveys by 1102 students from all partner countries; guidelines of the use of machine translation technology in the health domain and the importance of terminology; partners' meeting; a multiplier event (webinar)
-WP5: designing a curriculum for a course on preventing obesity and developing healthy lifestyle habits; a multiplier event (a webinar); field research and testing procedures for fast implementation of the new curriculum; partners' meeting.
-WP 6: implementation and piloting of the curriculum and all didactic material; a multiplier event and a final conference; accreditation of the new course.

<< Results >>

All outputs and results were digital and multilingual in 6 languages (English, Slovak, Slovene, Portuguese, Croatian and Norwegian): (1) A digital, interactive handbook on preventing obesity and developing healthy lifestyle habits in the university environment based on the results of the survey filled in by 1533 students from all partner countries available at: https://sites.google.com/g.uporto.pt/edu-fit/handbook;  (2) A curriculum for the course on developing healthy lifestyle habits and preventing obesity which consists of 5 modules: https://sites.google.com/g.uporto.pt/edu-fit/curriculum (3) Creation, implementation and evaluation of posters with easily accessible tips/advice for preparation of healthy meals for university canteen staff: https://sites.google.com/g.uporto.pt/edu-fit/outcomes; (4) Developing guidelines for developing sensitive communication skills in the filed of obesity in everyday and in medical environment:  https://sites.google.com/g.uporto.pt/edu-fit/sensitive-communication; (5) Implementation of the curriculum and the handbook with 122 students taking part in the piloting phase and accreditation of the curriculum. Reports on all WPs are attached.

2023-1-SK01-KA220-HED-000161639.title: Ecology Awareness of Sustainable Green Development: Collaboration of Universities and Local Actors
2023-1-SK01-KA220-HED-000161639.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to provide our students to become more aware of strengthening cooperation between universities and NGOs in addressing sustainability and environmental protection. The project focused on increasing the awareness of sustainable green development among university students and preparing them to take an active role in solving environmental problems from the perspective of public management, business, and economics. We focused on contributing to initiatives that encouraged students to take social responsibility and engage with real-world environmental challenges.

Universities play an important role in preparing students to deal with sustainability challenges in both their personal and professional lives. The project also addressed the need to provide students with practical experience through interaction with NGOs. This experience helped them develop key skills such as civic engagement, communication, and teamwork, which are important for their future careers.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the ECOUNITY project, we wanted to increase the awareness of university students and local actors about sustainable green development (SGD) and strengthen the cooperation of universities and NGOs. In line with this purpose, the following aims were adopted:
O1.1 to examine effective approaches regarding economic, social, and environmental issues, and create innovative educational plans to encourage learning and teaching of SGD
O1.2 to add new course modules to increase environmental awareness as a part of SDGs and interactions of local actors
O1.3 to bridge the gap between undergraduate students and NGOs operating in the field of environment and society and establish integrative and constructive collaborations
O1.4 to raise students' awareness of SGD and how to take action by collaborating with local actors
O1.5 to contribute to the digital transformation in HE through eco-friendly digital learning tools
O1.6 to pave the way for future studies in this field
O1.7 to exchange information by observing the practices of partner countries in the field of environment and climate
O1.8 to share and promote the use of project outcomes in other European universities and raise awareness of local actors for better interactions.

<< Implementation >>

During the ECOUNITY project, we carried out a range of key activities across partner countries. Project management included regular coordination, budget follow-up and quality monitoring meetings. 
To identify needs and collect stakeholder input, we conducted 5 surveys and 5 workshops translating to curriculum modules.
Transnational project meetings (TPM) supported the process: the Kick-off TPM in Nitra focused on general planning, data collection and curriculum development, the 2nd TPM in Rijeka on digital learning activities, LMS platform content, mobile application, and video tutorials, and the 3rd TPM in Bucharest on monitoring pilot implementation and multiplier event organisations.
Academic and research activities included 15 focus group interview reports, 5 country-based legal analyses, and one comparative legal analysis. We also designed and piloted a higher education course using flipped and active learning methods, involving 252 students across partner institutions.
As part of dissemination and stakeholder engagement activities, ECOUNITY Days were organised in all partner countries, bringing together 462 participants from academia and local communities to exchange ideas and discuss sustainability and green transformation.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs of the project:
5 Survey reports and 5 workshop reports to translate the training needs to the ECOUNITY HED course curriculum
1 Higher Education Course Curriculum, including 4 modules to increase the quality of environmental education within the scope of SGD
1 Project Website
E-learning platform (LMS) in 6 languages (4 modules and lesson plans, 6 expert videos, 6 animated videos, 15 quizzes, 15 articles, 5 chat rooms for student discussions, and its mobile application)
15 Focus Group Interview Reports
1 Comparative Legal Analysis
1 SGD Guide and Action Plan (6 language versions)
5 Pilot reports testing the effectiveness of project outputs.
5 ECOUNITY-DAY events, which aimed to share and promote the use of project results.

The ECOUNITY project successfully developed a scalable learning model based on Blended Learning and Active Learning Approaches, which can be transferred to other European Universities and Business, Economy and Management Faculties. This replicable approach provided a reliable, inspirational example for other HEIs, offering a valuable foundation for future Erasmus+ projects. The project had a clear impact on students, enhancing their 21st-century skills for sustainable green development.

2024-1-EL01-KA220-HED-000251373.title: Novel Biotechnological Solutions in Climate Change Mitigation
2024-1-EL01-KA220-HED-000251373.summary:
<< Objectives >>

BIOSHIELD aims to develop a tailored curriculum and teaching materials that centres around novel solutions for the mitigation of climate change and resulting disasters. We also aim to cultivate a seamless transition for graduates into the labour market by harnessing the power of design thinking. BIOSHIELD will respond to the rising demand for biotech professionals across sectors: biology, chemistry, energy, biochemistry, genetics, plant science, and microbiology through the project practice.

<< Implementation >>

BIOSHIELD consortium will carry out workshops, teamwork, and interviews with participants for data collection and joint works with partners at the international level, literature reviews for creative content development processes. These activities will yield the project results and their effectiveness will be tested during an online LTTA and 5 piloting processes in the partner universities. In each work package, partners will share and promote the use of project results among stakeholders.

<< Results >>

Project results comprise:
1- 5 workshop reports
2- A higher education curriculum "From Lab to Field: Biotechnology’s Role in Climate Change and Climate Change-Oriented Disaster Mitigation"
3- 10 video tutorials for efficient use of blended learning with 5 partners' language versions
4- 1 LTTA (Training Activity) report
5- A student's Handbook "Biotech Student's Guide to Future Projections"
6- Piloting report and Student's Research Results/Prototypes
7- Biotechnology fairs in 4 partner countries

2024-1-ES01-KA220-HED-000246558.title: Gender Diversity in Information Science: Challenges in Higher Education
2024-1-ES01-KA220-HED-000246558.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to embed gender equality deeply into our workplace, ensuring it shapes how we operate. We plan to educate our team on gender issues, fostering a culture that values everyone's contribution equally. Through ongoing training and awareness efforts, we're committed to maintaining an environment where inclusivity is a constant priority, ensuring these values endure well into the future. This project is to make gender equality a key part of our work culture, train our staff.

<< Implementation >>

Our activities will include curriculum evaluation and expert consensus, analysis of best practices in teaching and learning, training workshops for faculty and librarians, development of gender-sensitive educational materials on gender perspective and inclusive communication, student engagement activities, collaboration and networking events, and engagement with stakeholders and gender equality experts to foster an inclusive workplace. Monitoring progress ensures a lasting impact.

<< Results >>

Our main results will be increased awareness and understanding among students, faculty, and librarians, to enhance gender sensitivity in the curriculum, improved policies and practices, strengthened competencies, active student engagement, and sustainable change. We expect to achieve a more inclusive workplace culture, enhanced gender sensitivity and equality among staff, improved gender balance in decision-making, and stronger policies supporting equality.

hr.name: Sveučilište Josipa Jurja Strossmayera u Osijeku

2024-1-ES01-KA220-HED-000252587.title: EcoHarmony
2024-1-ES01-KA220-HED-000252587.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The "EcoHarmony" project's objectives are:
+ to develop a comprehensive curriculum,
+ to launch a digital collaboration platform,
+ to implement a micro-credential framework, and assessing the impact of sustainable tourism education,
+ to create a more sustainable, inclusive, and competitive tourism industry,
+ to organize a SustainEurope 2027 Summit on the World Environment Day simultaneously in 5 different countries.

The activities of the "EcoHarmony" projects are:

+SustainEurope 2027 Summit on the World Environment Day

+Launch of a digital collaboration platform for sustainable tourism education, facilitating global collaboration and knowledge exchange.

2024-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000244364.title: Fostering fEMale participation and LEADership in open science initiatives
2024-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000244364.summary:
<< Objectives >>

FEMLEAD introduces a new model for HEIs to implement comprehensive measures for reducing the gender gap in STEM, assuming a central role in social change. It implements a multi-stakeholder approach to advance OS practices and STEM initiatives in HEIs, promoting gender diversity, inclusivity, and systematisation. HEI staff, students, researchers and (minority) women communities, research organisations and policymakers are trained and mobilised to enable women’s participation.

<< Implementation >>

WP2:Training sessions via the Virtual Learning Lab to upskill 125 HEIs staff, researchers, students and 75 stakeholders in the research and innovation sector and grassroots communities  
WP3:50 female HEIs researchers/students participate in 15 STEM OS projects; 3 HEIs OS Fairs, and 5 Info Days with 1600+ participants from academic, research and educational communities.  
WP4:5 Policy Labs with 25 HEIs staff, researchers, students, policymakers, grassroots communities and other STI stakeholders.

<< Results >>

FEMLEAD creates a VLL on inclusive gender methodologies in R&I (STEM/OS) to train HEI researchers, students, and other stakeholders; facilitate female researchers and students’ co-participation in STEM Open Science projects, showcasing female achievement and increasing recruitment opportunities in OS Fairs and InfoDays; co-develops Policy Recommendations and Gender Equality Implementation Plans, to ensure the effective mainstreaming of inclusive gender practices within HEIs and beyond.
topics: Reaching the policy level/dialogue with decision makers

2024-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000248429.title: Interculturality Concepts Analysed and Renewed for Education and Training
2024-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000248429.summary:
<< Objectives >>

ICARET's overall objective is to build more inclusive education systems based on intercultural approaches. To achieve this goal, the project has two specific objectives:
- Research on intercultural issues for students’ mobility, to improve the quality of the student experience. This implies analysing the written and oral texts about interculturality.
-design intercultural training and educational tools that can be adapted to different contexts.

<< Implementation >>

There 6 main activities from 3 workpackages 
- Collect the relevant data
- Analyse the collected data
- Collect and analyse personal data 
- Design didactic videos
- Develop and test the videos
- Share and promote the project outcomes in digital (website, social media) and physical forms (conferences, scientific publications).

<< Results >>

The project will produce:
- R2.1: Definition of the corpus criteria
- R2.2: Corpus and verbatim
- R2.3: Mid-report with first analysis
- R3.1:  Creation and development of  the videos
- R3.2 : publication of the  proceedings
- R3.3: Designing of 4 didactic and multilingual videos
- R3.4: test and feed back about the videos

Thus the quality of mobility – in and out – should be improved: more interactions between local and international students should be facilitated.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2024-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000245495.title: Eco Minds - Enhancing Environmental Data COllection through Machine Learning and Database Systems
2024-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000245495.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project's overall purpose is to contribute to the digital & green transformations of higher education through cross-sectoral transnational cooperation & IT curriculum modernization. The specific objectives are: 1.To develop the digital & green competences of educators in higher education, 2. To build undergraduate students' digital & green skills and increase their employability in partnership with the business sector. 3. To make higher education more accessible to diverse groups of learners

<< Implementation >>

The following activities will be implemented, in addition to Project Management:
- training and exchange of expertise for university professors, lecturers, postgraduate teaching assistants and vocational secondary school teachers,
- development and piloting of two elective undergraduate-level courses and a digital seminar on machine learning, database design and environmental data analysis,
- transnational project team meetings,
- multiplier events.

<< Results >>

The expected project results are:
- Improved capacity of partners (5 higher education institutions, 1 secondary vocational school, 1 IT employer, and 1 NGO) to work transnationally and across sectors,
- Improved digital & green competences of 15 educators,
- Improved digital (in machine learning and database design) and green competences of 90 undergraduate students, 10 vocational school pupils and 2 NEETs,
- Increased stakeholder awareness of environmental trends and challenges on local level.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2024-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000252764.title: Advancing Geriatric Education for Nurses and Techs at High University
2024-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000252764.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The general objective of project is to contribute to the improvement of the quality and relevance of activities in higher education institutions in the European Union through transnational and international cooperation with organizations from various sectors.  The specific objective of project is to develop an innovative education program for nurses and technicians in higher education with a focus on geriatrics and gerontology in four EU countries (Croatia, Netherland, Portugal, Greece).

<< Implementation >>

Activities are divided into 5 packages:
WP1 Project Management
-Research on the needs 
WP 2 Creation of recommendations for improvement of nursing studies with an emphasis on geriatrics/gerontology
WP 3 Development of educational materials for the subject of geriatrics/gerontology
WP 4 Development of VR practice software
-Development of the VR platform
-Online education of professors and external lecturers
-Testing of the VR platform (blended mobility)
WP 5 Dissemination events

<< Results >>

Conducted research on the needs and shortcomings of nursing studies in geriatrics and gerontology, Developed policy recommendations for improving nursing studies, Proposed a new nursing study program in geriatrics and gerontology, Created educational materials for students, professors and practice providers, Developed VR platform, Conducted a 3-day online workshop for professors and external lecturers (min. 20) to develop digital skills, Disseminate project results through 4 events.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2024-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000254853.title: Strengthening the ecosystem for sustainable student mobility
2024-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000254853.summary:
<< Objectives >>

SuMoS project is designed with wider objective to strengthen the institutional ecosystem for strategic, structured and sustainable cooperation between HEIs in the field of student mobility through the development and purposeful use of green practices, digital tools and approaches to curriculum comparison. It is a joint initiative around 5 specific objectives of 5 partners from 4 EU countries (Croatia, Slovakia, Slovenia, France) and 1 candidate country (Serbia).

<< Implementation >>

Besides management and dissemination activities partners will perform development and training activities aimed for all target groups (HEI academic and non-academic staff, students, decision-makers) in different EU countries. The project is co-creational exercise of 5 project partners resulting in transferable and sustainable results to be available for partners' daily operations in the field of student mobility as well to all interested target groups world-wide after the project lifetime.

<< Results >>

The project includes both intangible and tangible results. While intangible include the raising of the awareness and inclusion within the questions related to green, sustainable and digitalised student mobility, the tangible results include the workshops for academics, support staff and students, as well as the benchmark for green footprint, course comparability protocol for HEIs and innovative platform to assist students and staff in more individualised support during mobility.

2024-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000257095.title: Heal-4-ALL: Higher Education Alliance for Innovative Healthcare and Education
2024-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000257095.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Existential well-being, encompassing meaning, purpose, and comfort with life's end, is now recognized as vital for healthy aging. Higher Education Alliance for Innovative Healthcare and Education (Heal4ALL) interconnects European higher education systems by co-creating a joint inter-university programme training students to put existential well-being into practice, enhancing innovations in healthcare education, use of innovative pedagogies and digital readiness of higher education.

<< Implementation >>

Project activities include designing and piloting a novel online interdisciplinary training program followed by real-life immersion through service-learning and international learning expeditions. Teaching staff will be trained in Design Thinking, Open pedagogy and Service learning practices, which are the foundation of the Heal4ALL programme. The programme will be evaluated and further improved, thus supporting evidence-based programme development and results will be widely disseminated.

<< Results >>

Heal4ALL will create a new curriculum, a blended interdisciplinary course on existential well-being with a focus on older people based on innovative teaching methods and an exchange of students and academic staff. The project aims to improve the quality of healthcare education and enhance the well-being of older people. The capacity-building activities will increase the use of innovative teaching pedagogies and foster vital collaboration in European healthcare higher education.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-1-IT02-KA220-HED-000244375.title: AI-Infused Language Education: Empowering teachers through Multilingual MOOC Training
2024-1-IT02-KA220-HED-000244375.summary:
<< Objectives >>

LSP courses are essential for enabling professionals to communicate effectively within their respective fields. Language educators play a pivotal role in preparing learners for these specialised contexts. 
AILEM project aims to empower language educators with the essential skills for effectively utilising AI in LSP content development. 
AI-driven tools can support the development of adaptive and tailored LSP materials for numerous languages, catering to the unique needs of different professions.

<< Implementation >>

AI-driven tools can support the development of adaptive and tailored LSP materials for numerous languages, catering to the unique needs of different professions by generating exercises, assessments, and content that are contextually relevant and up-to-date. 
AILEM will work in the selection of Artificial Intelligence (AI) open resources addressed for the application of the development of lessons in the LSP sector by development of a methodological learning framework and teaching by the MOOC.

<< Results >>

AILEM aims to place EU as a reference point about Teacher Training in AI for LSP Content Development:
- A methodological framework for a secure, sustainable and effective use of AI for LSP scopes
- A Multilingual miniMOOC tailored for language educators with expertise in Language for Specific Purposes (LSP).
- A community of practice built in this field involving stakeholders, experts and other HEIs.
- A series of success stories and guidelines for a further reapplication of the AILEM model.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
