2026-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000456132.title: Multidisciplinary Approach to the Conservation and Restoration of Technological Heritage in Universities and Museums
2026-1-DE01-KA220-HED-000456132.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to create a standardized European framework for conserving and restoring technological heritage in universities and museums through interdisciplinary collaboration. It will harmonize methodologies to preserve artifacts as historical evidence and functional educational tools, develop educational resources for future conservators-restorers and engineers, foster a STEAM bridge to attract underrepresented groups to technical disciplines and implement a Green and Digital transition.

<< Implementation >>

Activities will combine theory, virtual innovation and hands-on conservation:
1 Building an international and collaborative network of professionals of conservation and engineering.
2 Creating an online hub for Open Educational Resources. 
3 Workshops for hands-on conservation awarding ECTS and Micro-credentials. 
4 Developing a Best Practices Manual for conservation of technological heritage.
5 Impacting schools and industry via a Project Conference and mass events to promote STEAM vocations.

<< Results >>

1 Best Practices Manual: A multilingual benchmark for the sustainable restoration of technological heritage, validated by networks such as ERIH and Universeum.
2 Certified Competency Framework: Successful technical training of at least 35 students and 20 faculty members, authenticated through Europass and Micro-credentials.
3 European Multiplier Impact: reaching 375 secondary students via 5 multiplier events in 5 countries, assessed by attendance and 100 attenders to the Project Conference.

2026-1-EL01-KA220-HED-000454995.title: CitSci4SSH – Citizen Social Science for Social Sciences and Humanities
2026-1-EL01-KA220-HED-000454995.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to institutionalise Citizen Social Science within accredited Social and Political Science curricula across four European universities. It seeks to strengthen students’ digital, analytical and civic competences by embedding participatory research, discourse analysis and FIMI-informed methodologies into ECTS-based courses addressing migration, asylum and identity.

<< Implementation >>

The partnership will co-design and integrate 4–6 accredited modules (3–5 ECTS) through curriculum mapping, shared codebooks, ethics protocols and CSS Living Lab pilots. Activities include development of national evidence packs, staff training, student pilots with expert citizen validation, QA alignment and deployment of a multilingual open-access platform.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver a validated pedagogical framework, shared analytical tools and accredited modules embedded in at least eight university courses. Expected outcomes include improved student competence in evidence handling and discourse analysis, trained academic staff, sustained university–community partnerships, and a multilingual OER platform supporting European replication.

2026-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000460900.title: Green-TIME: Implementing Green Transition in Management Education
2026-1-FR01-KA220-HED-000460900.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project operationalises the EUA’s Green Deal roadmap within management higher education. It develops and pilots an operational framework covering strategy and governance, education, research, campus operations and external partnerships. Its objective is to translate these areas into concrete assessment criteria for business schools and management faculties, enabling them to determine their stage of green transition and define their priorities for action.

<< Implementation >>

The project first maps regulatory frameworks and institutional practices in 4 countries and at  EU-level, to identify the regulatory context shaping the green transition in management education. On this basis, it develops a beta operational framework translating the EUA’s Green Deal roadmap. This framework is tested in the 4 academic partners for validation. Results are disseminated through a reference book, Green Transition days, a EFMD conference session, video capsules and a project website.

<< Results >>

The project produces 5 reports mapping the regulatory context of the green transition (4 national reports and 1 EU-level report) and 4 institutional mapping reports analysing current practices. It creates an operational framework for management education based on the EUA’s Green Deal roadmap. The pilot phase produces 4 institutional self-assessment reports. Results are shared through a reference book, 15 video capsules, 4 Green Transition Days in partner HEIs and a presentation at an EFMD event.

2026-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000459075.title: Connecting Engaged Academics and Communities to Advance Institutional Change in Higher Education
2026-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000459075.summary:
<< Objectives >>

CONNECT aims to strengthen the role of community-engaged teaching and learning (CETL) in European university curricula, as it remains widely endorsed in principle but inadequately supported in practice.

The project has three objectives:
1. Strengthen university support for CETL through formally recognised Communities of Practice 
2. Integrate CETL into curricula through supported course redesign 
3. Improve institutional recognition of community-engaged academic work

<< Implementation >>

CONNECT brings together academic staff, students and community partners in Belgium, Croatia, Ireland and Spain, as well as four European university alliances.

The core project activities are:
• Establishing Communities of Practice for community-engaged teaching and learning	
• Piloting student-led community-engaged research projects within credit-bearing BA and MA courses	
• Improving recognition and career development for engaged academics	
• European knowledge exchange and community building

<< Results >>

At the four partner universities:
• Formally recognised Communities of Practice for CETL (80+ members)
• 20 courses redesigned to incorporate student-led community-engaged research (12 implemented with 200+ students)
• Stronger university recognition of CETL through four piloted measures

At the European level:
• 3 practical European CETL guides and frameworks
• Open-access repository of case studies 
• 50+ members of European Practice Forum
• 250+ participants reached through European events
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2026-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000467783.title: Systems Learning for Equitable Cancer Care
2026-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000467783.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Cancer care is delivered through complex systems, but higher education still trains professionals mainly within disciplinary boundaries. The ONCOLIGHT project aims to break educational silos by preparing students to communicate across disciplines and understand cancer care as an integrated system. By aligning higher education more closely with real healthcare practice, the project will prepare graduates to become engaged professionals with essential skills to address EU healthcare inequalities.

<< Implementation >>

Partners will jointly design and pilot a four-module interdisciplinary programme covering communication, systems thinking, comparison of EU healthcare systems, and professional and civic responsibility. Activities include staff capacity training, joint curriculum and digital learning development, and definition of micro-credentials. Students will learn core disciplinary basics independently, allowing teaching time to focus on interdisciplinary collaboration and system-level problem solving.

<< Results >>

We will develop an interdisciplinary, systems-oriented curriculum aligned with real healthcare and societal challenges, reusable open learning resources, defined micro-credentials, an ONCOLIGHT Knowledge Hub, and an Interdisciplinary Programme Adoption Guide. At least 160 students will gain competencies to work across disciplines and analyse healthcare inequalities. Results will strengthen institutional capacity of partner universities to adopt interdisciplinary education models.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2026-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000468605.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence for the Digital Transformation of Language Teaching
2026-1-HR01-KA220-HED-000468605.summary:
<< Objectives >>

AI4LANG upgrades an already operational platform into a CEFR-traceable multilingual system (Japanese, Croatian, English) that combines Can-Do descriptors, lexical and grammar resources, guided interaction, and audio-supported practice. The objective is educator-controlled personalization that improves learning progression, inclusion, and instructional reliability in higher-education classrooms.

<< Implementation >>

Implementation is structured in four connected WPs: WP1 governance and quality control, WP2 platform expansion and multilingual module hardening, WP3 multi-site pilots with shared evaluation, and WP4 dissemination, exploitation, and sustainability. Delivery is evidence-gated, with defined ownership, corrective loops, and controlled WP handovers to ensure that each phase starts from validated readiness.

<< Results >>

Results include a pilot-ready multilingual AI language-learning system, validated CEFR-linked learning modules, comparative cross-site pilot evidence, and a prioritized optimization roadmap. The project also delivers educator-ready transfer assets, curated FAIR-compliant resources where permissible, and a partner-approved continuation framework with documented adoption commitments and post-project operating conditions.

Inclusion and Diversity

2026-1-IT02-KA220-HED-000467548.title: BORDERSCAPE. Eastern Perspectives on European Identity: Developing and Validating an Innovative Teaching Model in Higher Education
2026-1-IT02-KA220-HED-000467548.summary:
<< Objectives >>

BORDERSCAPE aims to develop, refine and empirically validate an innovative, transferable teaching model on European identity, citizenship and belonging from Eastern and borderland perspectives. The project strengthens inclusive dialogue, democratic awareness and high-quality learning in Higher Education by integrating diverse regional narratives into Master-level curricula.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement two transnational Winter Schools, an International Methodological Workshop and a Final Policy and Academic Roundtable. Partners will co-design, refine and validate a transferable pedagogical framework, produce a podcast series and create a permanent educational exhibition and digital repository to support innovative teaching and civic engagement.

<< Results >>

BORDERSCAPE will deliver an empirically validated and transferable teaching framework, two tested intensive learning formats, a policy-oriented report, a podcast series and a permanent physical and digital exhibition. The project will strengthen curriculum innovation, intercultural dialogue and inclusive understanding of European identity across partner institutions and beyond.

2026-1-LU01-KA220-HED-000467555.title: Green Startups for Bioeconomy and Higher Education
2026-1-LU01-KA220-HED-000467555.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Develop and validate a transnational HE framework for bioeconomy entrepreneurship equipping students — especially women — to create green startups in bio-energy, bio-materials and circular bioeconomy. Co-create an 8-module GreenComp/EntreComp curriculum and train 40 faculty; deploy a MOOC with 8 ECTS micro-credentials (500+ learners); pilot pre-incubation for 120 students with a Green Startup Challenge; produce a multi-country green startup definition, 6 Policy Labs, and enterprise matching.

<< Implementation >>

WP2: 8-module Curriculum co-creation; 5-day BIP in Rome (40 faculty); piloting in 6 HEI courses (240 students). WP3: MOOC platform — 48 lectures, 16 case studies, 8 ECTS micro-credentials; testing with 160 students. WP4: 4-week blended pre-incubation across 7 countries (120 students); Green Startup Challenge in Tartu (21 finalist teams). WP5: Green Startup Definition Framework; 6 national Policy Labs; 24 student-enterprise matches; 6 National Briefs + 1 European Synthesis Brief.

<< Results >>

8-module Curriculum + Guide (CC BY-SA 4.0). 40 trained faculty. MOOC: 48 lectures, 16 case studies, 8 ECTS micro-credentials, 500+ enrolments. Pre-incubation: 120 students, 21 teams at Challenge, 6 incubator connections. Green Startup Definition Framework validated by 21-member panel. 6 Policy Lab Reports, 24 enterprise matches, 6 National Briefs, 1 European Synthesis Brief (100+ HEI decision-makers). Women in Green STEM Toolkit. All outputs in 7 languages.

2026-1-LV01-KA220-HED-000462189.title: English as the Basis for Experiential Pedagogical Training
2026-1-LV01-KA220-HED-000462189.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen university faculty’s capacity to implement flipped and blended teaching through an experiential professional development model integrating digital pedagogy and responsible use of AI. It will develop, pilot and evaluate an English-based PD course designed to support adoption of digitally enriched teaching practices in higher education.

<< Implementation >>

The project will design a two-level English-based experiential PD course integrating flipped and blended pedagogy and an AI-supported language assistant prototype. The course will be piloted in two transnational iterations with university faculty from partner countries. Data will be collected through surveys, reflections, and analyses of teaching practice. Results will inform course refinement and recommendations for institutional integration.

<< Results >>

The project will produce: (1) a validated experiential PD course model integrating English learning, digital pedagogy, and AI-supported tools; (2) an evaluated AI-based language assistant; and (3) institutional recommendations for integrating the model into faculty development. The project will enhance participants’ digital pedagogical competence and generate a transferable model adaptable across European higher education contexts

2026-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000460921.summary:

The project's goal is to develop a curriculum that will be implemented in the curricula of universities participating in the project consortium at EQF level 6 or 7. The program will focus on developing practical skills of students in using electronic communications compliant with GS1 standards for inter-company communication in the supply chain. The program will be supplemented with teaching materials and a board game with Augmented Reality elements.

The project will include 4 main groups of tasks: (1) research: research on educational programs, research on the needs of students, academic teachers and enterprises; (2) implementation: development of a program, teaching materials for students and academic teachers, board game with AR, (3) testing: pilot sessions, improvement of results; (4) dissemination and use of the developed results in the form of a series of workshops for students using the developed results.

Competency framework and best practices for using electronic communication solutions in supply chain.
Learning materials for students include a textbook, presentations, case studies, assignments and tests. Academic lecturers materials explaining teaching methods using AR solutions supported by board game.
Building awareness of Paperless concept and global communication standards among 500 participants over 5 years, including more than 250 during the project and the remainder after its completion

2026-1-PL01-KA220-HED-000464643.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the DIGESM is to strengthen HE capacity in sustainable mining and resource engineering by integrating circular economy principles and responsible post-mining land management into teaching through innovative digital and game-based learning. The project aims to modernise curricula and empower students and academic staff with green and digital competences for sustainable industrial transformation.

The project activities are based on transnational collaboration and co-design and include: 1) conducting a multi-country needs analysis and stakeholder engagement, 2) developing a pedagogical framework for decision-based learning, 3) designing and developing a modular digital simulation prototype and complementary board-based tool, 4) piloting and validating the tools in five universities, and 5) disseminating results through open-access materials and multiplier events.

<< Results >>

The DIGESM will deliver an innovative digital simulation prototype, a board-based learning toolkit, and an open-access educator package supporting sustainable resource engineering education. The tools will be integrated into existing courses and tested with students to assess learning impact. The project will strengthen institutional capacity, foster digital and green competences, and provide a scalable model for long-term curriculum modernisation.

2026-1-RO01-KA220-HED-000462340.summary:

1. improving support services for non-mobile, exchange and international students; 2. reducing access barriers to mobility opportunities for students with fewer opportunities; 3. boosting DEI competencies, and sustainable thinking by developing and showcasing innovative educational materials that integrate and promote common European values; 4. fostering cultural immersion, civic engagement and sustainable thinking for international and local students within Hands-On Labs.

2026-1-RO01-KA220-HED-000464956.title: Promoting Green Futures in Higher Education
2026-1-RO01-KA220-HED-000464956.summary:
<< Objectives >>

ECO-STEP aims to strengthen sustainability competences in higher education by developing an interdisciplinary curriculum, an interactive Sustainability Impact Simulator and a Digital Hub offering a MOOC and multimedia resources. The project will build institutional capacity, enhance digital readiness, support transparent recognition of learning and promote the adoption of green and digital competences for ≥300 learners across HEIs, VET providers, public bodies and community organisations.

<< Implementation >>

ECO-STEP will design a competence framework, develop and pilot a sustainability curriculum, create data-driven scenarios and build a multilingual Simulator. It will develop a Digital Hub featuring a MOOC, videos, podcasts, quizzes and mini-games. The project will deliver 5 national workshops, a 1 final conference and structured dissemination actions. All outputs will be user-tested, refined and supported by a Sustainability Plan to guide long-term uptake.

<< Results >>

ECO-STEP will produce a validated curriculum, a functional Sustainability Impact Simulator and a Digital Hub hosting open-access materials, including a 1-ECTS MOOC and multimedia tools. It will create a collaboration network, deliver national workshops and a final conference and produce a Sustainability Plan for long-term use. The results will strengthen green and digital competences, support recognition through Europass and enable broad uptake by HEIs, VET providers and community organisations.

2026-1-SE01-KA220-HED-000450753.title: ACTivateWellness: Enhancing Resilience and Well-Being Through Acceptance and Commitment Training for University Students
2026-1-SE01-KA220-HED-000450753.summary:
<< Objectives >>

In response to rising mental health pressures among university students across Europe, the project aims to shift from reactive support to a scalable, preventative ACT-based model within higher education. It seeks to strengthen resilience, reduce escalation of mental health difficulties and dropout risk, and embed sustainable, inclusive, evidence-based wellbeing strategies within institutional systems to ensure long-term impact, equitable student participation and academic success.

<< Implementation >>

With 10 partners across 10 countries representing over 85,000 students, the project will design and deliver the ACT curriculum, preparing 20–30 facilitators across partner institutions, and will pilot a 4-hour ACT intervention with 450–675 students. Implementation will be monitored through pre- and post-intervention surveys and facilitator feedback, supporting quality and sustainable embedding.  A feasibility study will assess scalability, and CPD accreditation ensures professional recognition.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver a validated 27-hour ACT curriculum (1 ECTS), train staff and student facilitators to implement a 4-hour preventive intervention, and produce open-access materials available for at least five years. Expected outcomes include strengthened student resilience, earlier coping, reduced escalation of mental health difficulties, and institutional integration of sustainable, transferable and scalable wellbeing strategies across European higher education systems.

2021-1-BG01-KA220-SCH-000034422.title: INCREASING THE COMMITMENT OF STUDENTS DURING THE SHIFTS BETWEEN ONLINE AND IN-PERSON EDUCATION ON HUMANITARIAN SUBJECTS THROUGH OBSERVATION AND REFLECTION TOOLS
2021-1-BG01-KA220-SCH-000034422.summary:
<< Background >>

School subjects have been influenced by the shifts between online and in-person education within and after COVID-19. Lessons requiring discussion and exchange of oral information have been deeply affected by limitations in the interactions among students and teachers. This concerned formation of vital expression and communication skills of students and resulted in decline in study motivation and commitment in class.
As such, new approaches accustomed both to real and virtual classrooms had to be applied in order to help tutors to monitor the class and to raise motivation of students.
The project has been oriented to address the following: 
- Negative impact of simplified conversation through online platforms which very often led to a monologue lecture 
- Impossibility for asking embarrassing questions when everyone responds in a one-by-one mode and has sufficient time to consider the answer
- Scarcity of suitable digital devices or stable Internet connection faced by disadvantaged students influencing their engagement in class 
- Minimizing cases when students could stay inactive behind their switched off cameras and microphones 
- Keeping continuity of online classes with traditional ones in terms of active participation

<< Objectives >>

The project envisaged two areas of interventions. The first one concerned development of communication and expression skills in class. The project team believed that education is also an important process that allows students to learn through interactions with their teachers and peers. The second area of intervention has been oriented towards improvement of monitoring students’ level of engagement and raising commitment. In traditional classrooms tutors often can closely monitor student’s level of motivation expressed by participation, attention to the subject, and extent of distraction. On contrary, during online teaching this was hampered. 
The general project objective was to address deficiencies during online education in terms of developing communication and expression skills within humanitarian school disciplines focusing on disadvantaged students falling behind and getting them closer to their peers. 
The specific objectives were: 
- Provision of guiding materials for students adapted to those with poor skills
- Equipping teachers with applicable pedagogical approaches and supporting thematic sets
- Raising attractiveness and efficiency of the training on humanitarian subjects by production of interactive elements

<< Implementation >>

Implemented activities within the project were in following groups:
= Development of Project Results
PR1 Student`s Booklet about communication and expression skills on social topics and the linkage with future professional realisation 
PR2 Teacher` Handbook on observation and reflection techniques 
PR3 Toolbox for observation and reflection in online and present education
= Piloting and optimization of training content
The team contacted various schools in order to get feedback about the developed content.
= Project management
- General management of the project carried out with regular contributions, support and input from all partners.
- Organization of transnational partner meetings – 4 TPMs have been held
- Internal information flow regulated by internal data repository and exchange system
= Quality assurance
- Quality of elaborated training materials in methodological and content related aspects
- Internal quality assurance in project administration aspect
= Sharing and promotion activities, external communication and publicity measures – through in-person or online contacts, multiplier events, promotional meetings, participation at networking events among educational organizations, usage of Social Media, web-presense, etc.

<< Results >>

As a result of the development phases, the following outputs have been produced:
- Student`s Booklet about communication and expression skills on social topics and the linkage with future professional realisation 
- Teacher` Handbook on observation and reflection techniques 
- Toolbox for observation and reflection in online and present education
Besides the development of training materials as outputs, the project produced the following results:
 - Outlining areas of intervention in concrete taught subjects and lessons in compliance with the existing formal curricula. 
- Addressing the lack of multi-directional interaction within the class and the teacher in online environment. 
- Introducing and piloting techniques for monitoring engagement and stimulating commitment. 
- Strengthening the aspect of educational inclusion among the targeted students with main focus on the disadvantaged ones in order to prevent those falling behind. 
- Ameliorating the specific preparation of the students in need on humanitarian subjects and making it equal as much as possible of those not facing social or technical challenges compared to their peers. 
- Enhancing the preparation for keeping commitment in switching in-person and online environment by teachers and students through introducing adapted measuring applications. 
- Provision of tailor-made learning materials to improve social interaction aspects and specific skills and knowledge for future society-oriented professionals. 
- Stimulating school teachers and students to enter into contacts with people from abroad. 
- Establishing multilingual online platform for exchange of knowledge, advice and feedback. 
- Strengthening the understanding and skills of students in areas such as multiculturalism, diversity, successful employment, active citizenship, social inclusion, equal opportunities and managing of personal change. 
- Supporting diffusion of offline lessons and self-study approach into mainstream educational programs concerning subjects related to public speaking and audience proficiency. 
- Providing support by business world and experts in social field towards raising motivation and outlining the perspectives for joining such fields by future graduates. 
- Stimulating exchange of views on obstacles in proper qualification on social and humanity subjects.

2021-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000024558.title: INNOVATIVE APPROACH FOR CODING IN DIGITAL ERA
2021-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000024558.summary:
<< Background >>

The current COVID19 pandemic has highlighted the need for Europe to speed up its digital transition process in order to overcome the gap that splits Europe into two areas that are growing at different rates. In addition, given the growing necessity of regulating the amount and the storage of big data through the use of artificial intelligence, European institutions require the development of digital competencies by European citizens. Digital transformation is a requirement for all European citizens, especially for the school system which shapes European citizens. For this purpose, teachers needed to upgrade their digital skills in order to keep up with the demands of a society that is continuously developing. Coding offers the opportunity to orient students towards computer science and new technologies. Besides improving logical abilities and analysis, teaching coding at school was a powerful tool for creative projects such as music and arts, expressing sensibility and each students’ personality. Like all citizens, teachers needed to acquire the necessary digital skills for their personal and professional lives and for participating in the digital society.

<< Objectives >>

The activities implemented within the scope of this project targeted teachers and students wih the aim of;
-Contributing to the readiness of schools and teachers for digital education processes
-Creating open source for Robotics / Coding lessons applied in schools
-Contributing to the development of 21st century skills (creativity, problem solving, analytical thinking ... etc) of students.
-Training teachers in coding teaching and to contribute to the development of their professional profiles.

All participants in our project were recruited from the school environment. Since the topic of the project is universal for all groups of teachers, we involved teachers from primary schools, secondary schools, vocational education and training and teachers from universities.The project consortium had extensive links and cooperation with many different schools in Europe, so we involved participants from these schools. As our project had the ambition to be more international than just for the partner countries, we reached out with our content also to schools with abroad.

<< Implementation >>

ROBYCODE was responsible for preparing project management guidebook (PMG), financial management of the project and subcontracting external evaluator. UNZIG was responsible for monitoring & evaluating of the project. Korfez Mesleki ve Teknik Anadolu Lisesi (Körfez MTAL) was leading the communication
plan. ISTITUTO ISTRUZIONE SUPERIORE "A. LINCOLN" will br responsible for social media management of the project. Paula-Fürst-Schule Berlin was responsible for leading dissemination activities.
Within the scope of project both tangible and intangible results were developed.
A)Intellectual Outputs

2.Experiment sets
3.Experiment Booklet: (Teachers’ Book & Students’ Book) including 17 experiments
4.Interactive Website

In the project, it wasaimed to increase the awareness and dissemination of coding and digital competence, which are increasing in importance every day. In order to achieve these goals, it was planned that the teachers included in the project would be included in the process, undergo training of trainers and indirectly involve the students in the target audience. For this purpose, Arduino sets were prepared that allow teachers to use in their training and later in their classes. The training of the prepared sets were done on Arduino sets with the participation of the relevant teachers. The training received were certified with the certificate to be given to the teachers after the training. With the interactive web page to be prepared, teachers and students are able to access training regardless of time and place. In this way, it is ensured that the training continues continuously with the use of the internet, which is an indispensable tool of digital life.

2021-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000032446.title: SUSTAINABILITY, AUTHENTIC LEARNING AND THINKING FROM EARLY CHILDHOOD: THINKIDS
2021-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000032446.summary:
<< Background >>

Der Rat hat 2017 aufgrund eines Vorschlags der Kommission eine Empfehlung zu Schlüsselkompetenzen für lebenslanges Lernen angenommen. In der Empfehlung werden acht Schlüsselkompetenzen aufgeführt, die für die persönliche Entfaltung, einen gesunden, nachhaltigen Lebensstil, Vermittelbarkeit, aktive Bürgerschaft und soziale Inklusion erforderlich sind. 
• Lese- und Schreibkompetenz 
• Mehrsprachigkeit
• Mathematische, wissenschaftliche und technische Fähigkeiten 
• Digitale und technologiebasierte Kompetenzen
• Soziale Kompetenz und Fähigkeit, neue Kompetenzen zu erwerben 
• Aktive Bürgerschaft 
• Unternehmerische Kompetenz 
• Kulturbewusstsein und kulturelle Ausdrucksfähigkeit 
Die EU Mitgliedsstaaten sind aufgefordert, diese in ihre Bildungslandschaften ab der frühen Kindheit zu implementieren. In einigen Ländern, wie z.B. Spanien ist dies bereits in Gesetzgebung umgesetzt, aber noch nicht überall. Die Vermittlung der Schlüsselkompetenzen für lebenslanges Lernen ab der frühen Kindheit soll dazu beitragen die nachhaltige Entwicklung europäischer Staaten zu gewährleisten. Lehrkräfte sind mit der praktischen Umsetzung, Kinder anhand der Schlüsselkompetenzen zu aktiven Gestaltern ihres Lebens und ihrer Umwelt allein gelassen. 

<< Objectives >>

Da die Menschen im 21. Jahrhundert mit vielen Unwägbarkeiten und Unsicherheiten umgehen müssen, wollte das Thinkids Projekt einen authentischen Lernansatz entwickeln und testen, der Pädagoginnen und Pädagogen und Kindern helfen soll, Kohärenz zwischen dem, was sie denken, was sie wollen und fühlen und ihrem Handeln zu finden. Kurz gesagt geht es darum, Kinder dazu zu befähigen zu aktiven Gestaltern ihres Lebens und damit der Gesellschaft zu werden und ihnen sowohl die Kompetenzen, die es für nachhaltiges Leben braucht als auch altersgerechte Ansätze zur Erreichung der Nachhaltigkeitsziele zu vermitteln. Dabei wollen wir die pädagogischen Fachkräfte durch das zur Verfügung stellen von Materialien und Hintergrundwissen unterstützen, die sie dazu befähigen die gesteckten Ziele (Umsetzung der kompetenzbasierten Bildung basierend auf den 8 Schlüsselkompetenzen für Lebenslanges Lernen (LLL) und Bildung für nachhaltige Entwicklung basierend auf den 17 Nachhaltigkeitszielen der UN - 17 SDGs) zu erreichen. 

<< Implementation >>

In einem stufenweisen Prozess haben wir zunächst in den teilnehmenden Ländern pädagogische Fachkräfte quantitativ als auch qualitativ in Experteninterviews zu ihrer Einschätzung der Situation in ihren Ländern bezüglich des Fortschritts der Bildung für nachhaltige Entwicklung und Implementierung der Schllüsselkompetenzen Lebenslangen Lernens (LLLs) befragt. Ebenso hat uns interessiert, welche Lehrmethoden sie in diesem Zusammenhang für zielführend erachten. Basierend auf den Ergebnissen wurde das Curriculum erstellt, welches Pädagogen einen Überblick über die Thematik und die damit verbundenen Lernbedarfe gibt. Basierend auf dem Curriculum wurden dann die Materialien, die die LLLs mit den Nachhaltigkeitszielen (SDGs) verbinden entwickelt, von Experten evaluiert und in einem Handbuch zusammengefasst. Um jederzeit auf die Materialien zugreifen zu können, wurde die Webplattform THINKIDS eHub programmiert und die Ergebnisse sowie Informationen über das Projekt online in den Partnersprachen zur Verfügung gestellt. Im Anschluss an eine Pilotierungsphase der Materialien durch pädagogische Fachkräfte  in ihrer beruflichen Praxis wurde deren Feedback zur Umsetzung in den Umsetzungsleitfaden aufgenommen, der dabei unterstützen soll, die pädagogischen Thinkids Ansätze in die jeweiligen nationalen Bildungsstrukturen zu implementieren. Alle Entwicklungsstufen wurden von externen Bildungsexperten, wie z.B. Dra Alicia Blanco-Bayo, Dozentin für frühkindliche Bildung und Programmleiterin an der Edge Hill University (UK)  und Alina Boutiuc-Kaiser, Dipl. Phil., Dipl. Paed., Pädagogische Hochschule Freiburg (DE) begleitet und evaluiert. Um das Projekt auf Kurs zu halten fanden zwei Präsenztreffen und monatliche Onlinetreffen statt. Zum Ende der Projektlaufzeit und nach Finalisierung der Ergebnisse wurden in allen Ländern Multiplikatorenveranstaltungen durchgeführt, um die THINKIDS Materialien bekannt zu machen. Darüber hinaus wurden vielfältige digitale Möglichkeiten der Verbreitung genutzt, wie Artikel, Social Media Beiträge, Nutzung von Bildungsplattformen etc.. 

<< Results >>

Das Curriculum THINKIDS für Vor- und Grundschulpädagogen, um Schlüsselkompetenzen für Lebenslanges Lernen (LLL) und  UN-Nachhaltigkeitsziele (SDGs) mit Hilfe eines authentischen Lernansatzes in ihren Unterricht zu integrieren. 
Ein Handbuch für Lehrkräfte mit Erklärungen zum THINKIDS-Ansatz, den 8 Schlüsselkompetenzen für lebenslanges Lernen und den 17 SDGs sowie mit praktischen Ressourcen für die Umsetzung im Unterricht.

2021-1-DK01-KA220-SCH-000034350.title: GAMESS: Games for students with Autism as an effective Methodology in Education for the development of Social Skills
2021-1-DK01-KA220-SCH-000034350.summary:
<< Background >>

Schools in Denmark are obliged to differentiate education on the requirements of the children as a whole rather than sending them to special education. However, development has demonstrated that to effectively differentiate teaching strategies, curriculum, and instructional materials for kids with varying developmental, linguistic, and cultural backgrounds, schools must have access to certain resources. In Finland, inclusion is the official educational policy, and a systematic way of organizing support, a so-called three-tiered support model, has been implemented. Rehabilitation and new technology give more opportunities for early rehabilitation and Finland puts attention to new possibilities. For CZA and Miradas organisations, actively working with children with autism, the need to improve the quality of life of their students with ASD and fulfil one of the rights from Convention on the Rights of the Child which is related to achieving the fullest possible social integration and individual development. STANDO offers teacher training to teachers from all over Europe, therefore, this project will help them to bring together the skills of such a diverse set of partners in creating new curricula and expanding their training offer

<< Objectives >>

One of the characteristics of children with ASD, ADHD, learning disabilities and other neurodevelopmental disorders is social skills deficiency. Given the idiosyncratic difficulties in the social and emotional understanding of pupils with ASD, teachers may face considerable difficulties in managing their needs, thereby affecting the quality of the teachers’ relationship with these pupils (Emam and Farrell, 2009). Within this context, and considering how important learning social skills from an early age is, and the challenges teachers can face, we proposed a project with a target group of general preschool/primary school teachers that have in their mainstream classes children with ASD, with the following objectives:
*To design, test and publish an innovative Educational Package on GBL for mainstream education teachers (primary
school) 
*To design and create a variety of games- a VR game, and a booklet with a number of group classroom games that promote social skills development in children with autism but also in their neurotypical peers
*To deliver a training course to train general primary teachers on GBL and how to use and create a variety of games to teach social skills to children with autism in the mainstream classroom

<< Implementation >>

The mission of the project was to develop a GBL package for Social Skills specially designed for young children with autism. An integrated approach was used to accomplish this task. The consortium started by creating the Social Skills Curriculum (IO1) for primary school teachers complemented by 2 types of games - a VR game (PR2), and group classroom games (PR3), as an educational package, which set up the pathway for teachers to effectively teach important social skills to students with autism. Apart from the aforementioned project results, a 5-day LTTA (C1) was organized for teachers. During the C1 training, the teachers were trained on how to utilize the PRs to teach children with autism social skills they needed to integrate into the community. All PRs were pilot-tested on the teachers during the LTTA. The pilot testing of the developed PRs started after the completion of their drafts to allow improvements and modifications during the C1. The teachers, upon completion of the training event, gave feedback with suggestions for improvements. Besides the PRs and the LTTA, 5 ME were organized towards the end of the project to disseminate the project results.

<< Results >>

1. Project Results: The GBL for Social skills Curriculum, a VR game promoting social skills, and a booklet with group classroom games promoting social skills, all interconnected. 
2. LTTA: 1 training activity for teachers to use GBL (including VR technology) to teach social skills to children with ASD in the mainstream classroom 
3.5 multiplier events to promote the project, its results and outcomes among teachers and other stakeholders (organisations for people with SEN, teacher organisations, SENCOs, policymakers, and reformers) (E1-E5)
Other expected outcomes of the project include:
-Each partner had the opportunity to learn about different aspects of GBL as well as VR technology as an educational tool, as practised in each partner’s country, exchange good practices and experiences, develop common
recommendations and guidelines and improve their competencies in the field of GBL and teaching social skills to children with ASD.
-Formation of friendly relations between teachers from Denmark and the other partner countries, exchange of experiences and challenges they face and mutual support regarding the social inclusion of pupils with autism in the mainstream classroom
-The project facilitated the collaboration between key people (trainers, specialists, experts, representatives of local authorities) and teachers from each partner
-The project facilitated the social integration of children with ASD in the mainstream classroom
-European international mobility of project participants (field professionals, representatives of target groups) 
-Social media campaigns 
-Project participants’ language and social competencies through active transnational communication and participation in project activities
-It could raise autism awareness at local and EU level
It is expected to improve children with ASD’s and their neurotypical peers’ social skills
Additionally, the project also foresees a set of project management, dissemination, monitoring and evaluation, and coordination results. 
Once the project is completed the partnership will disseminate its results and will transfer the developed practices and educational products to other contexts and educational fields. Moreover, the PRs will be used in partners' institutional activities with other teachers working with children with ASD.

2021-1-EL01-KA220-SCH-000034476.title: Teaching STEAM through Urban Garden Based Learning in the kindergarten
2021-1-EL01-KA220-SCH-000034476.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the critical need for age-appropriate outdoor STEAM activities in preschool settings. Recognizing the pivotal role of early childhood experiences in shaping future academic success, particularly in math and STEM subjects, we aimed to bridge the gap by integrating urban gardening into teaching and learning.

Our project targets the need for educators to enhance their skills in teaching STEAM concepts through practical experiences in urban gardens. By leveraging children's innate curiosity about math and STEM, we create a rich learning environment that fosters both academic growth and environmental consciousness.

Furthermore, by incorporating Permaculture values, we addressed the broader goal of promoting ecological and social justice considerations in education. Through collaboration and knowledge exchange among educators, children, and project partners, we aimed to create a cross-generational learning community dedicated to advancing STEAM education and sustainable practices.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, our primary goal was to enhance the teaching of STEAM concepts through hands-on urban gardening experiences in preschool settings. Recognizing the critical role of early childhood education in shaping future academic success, particularly in math and STEM subjects, we aimed to leverage children's innate curiosity about nature and math to create a rich learning environment.

Additionally, our project seeks to address the need for educators to adapt flexible teaching practices that meet the ecological, social, and economic challenges of the 21st century. By integrating Permaculture values and fostering collaboration among educators, children, and project partners, we aimed to create a cross-generational and cross-cultural learning community dedicated to advancing STEAM education and sustainable practices.

Ultimately, through the UrbSTEAM initiative, we aimed to equip educators with the necessary skills to play an active role in children's development and foster a lifelong interest in STEAM subjects and nature, contributing to a sustainable future for all.

<< Implementation >>

The preliminary research carried out prior to the writing of this proposal indicated a strong need for more practical resources that focused on garden-based methods for STEAM learning in young ages, especially for the countries represented in the partnership, who all fell below average when it came to STEAM, outdoor learning, and awareness of sustainable development compared to the rest of Europe. Thus, the objectives were formed based on these needs, and the activities were designed to meet these objectives. As a reminder, the objectives of the UrbSTEAM project were:
a. To enable at least 150 educators (30 participants per partner country) to understand and work with the garden-based methodology for teaching STEAM to kindergarten students and to raise awareness of the principles of permaculture and sustainable development.
b. To equip the educators with the appropriate materials/resources in order to deliver garden-based learning for STEAM education at an early age by using the resources from an innovative digital platform - toolkit.
c. For children, to come in contact with nature, STEAM education, and become the future agents of change towards a more sustainable future.
d. To develop children’s interest in and appreciation of nature and STEAM.
Thus, the following project activities helped us achieve the objectives above:
Results – The project saw the development of three Results, which were the driving forces behind the achievement of our objectives. Each result addressed at least one objective directly (explained in each Result description), and together they worked to improve the overall quality of STEAM teaching resources through garden-based methods for educators working with young children when teaching STEAM.

Management - The success of the project was based on strong management and frequent, effective monitoring of the activities being carried out. The coordinator’s past experience with project management and implementation provided valuable lessons on what (and what not) to do, thus the management plan reflected this. Management was supported by constant and clear communication among the partners through Slack, as well as the clear allocation of tasks and deadlines using a task management system and Gantt chart. Strong management equaled a strong outcome.

Publicity - One of the project’s objectives was to promote and implement an innovative approach to teaching STEAM in a garden-based approach by using research-backed techniques to simultaneously improve emotional intelligence. Through the project’s publicity efforts, we were able to spread the word about this well-researched but little-used approach in order to generate interest (and eventually sustainability) in the UrbSTEAM project. Publicity materials clearly stated the project’s objectives and how stakeholders could get involved. The project also included national Multiplier Events which encouraged the uptake of the Results created throughout the project. This helped to spread the word at local, regional, and national levels among stakeholders.

Evaluation – Regular evaluation reports ensured that the project’s Results were of high quality in the end. The process of evaluation involved following an Evaluation plan in which internal and external evaluators provided insight into how the project’s activities were progressing. This allowed us to see whether any adaptations to the project needed to be made in order to deliver Results in a timely manner which accurately reflected the project’s objectives.

<< Results >>

Our consortium worked together for 2 years to explore the current situation in each country related to outdoor learning, urban gardening, and STEAM. The UrbSTEAM project revolved around the production of 3 innovative results:

Manual of best practices on garden-based learning and development of Educational material
Toolkit for educators and schools
Online learning platform and networking
Aside from the outputs, the UrbSTEAM project also produced the following:

Project Management Plan
Project Evaluation Plan
Project Dissemination Plan
Project Quality Assurance Plan
Project Impact and Sustainability Plan
Project Logo
Project Website
Social Media Channels and Profiles
6 Project Leaflets
6 Project Newsletters
3 Transnational Meeting Agendas and Minutes
1 Piloting Report
5 Multiplier Events
4 Internal Administrative Reports
4 Internal Financial Reports
5 Internal Dissemination Reports
5 Quality Assurance Reports
OUTCOMES:

With these outputs, the target group became aware of the concepts and principles of garden-based learning not just towards STEAM in kindergarten but in general as well as an educational approach. This enabled them to engage immediately with the theory and practice of garden-based learning as it relates to their own projects. They also had access to a forum where the emerging ideas of early childhood education were discussed. Partner organizations increased their capacity to educate others about the methodologies and tools used in educational approaches to STEAM learning in early age and also were able to implement best practices in their operations as a model to other stakeholders. Meanwhile, participants gained experiential knowledge and thus were equipped and motivated to apply this knowledge to their classrooms. The knowledge of all stakeholders in the field was greatly enriched by involvement in the project, and the reasonable expectation was that they would directly and tacitly disseminate that learning in a variety of settings.

The project was expected to produce a number of intangible outcomes as well, including:

Improved quality and availability of STEAM teaching on garden-based resources for kindergartens
Increased capacity to successfully teach STEAM in a creative way
Exchange of knowledge and best practices among partners
IMPACT:

Much was already written about this aspect of results in the Impact section. However, briefly stated, this project raised awareness about the benefits and importance of STEAM learning through a garden-based approach at a young age. This, in turn, had a positive impact on preschool & kindergarten teachers on how they could use this approach in learning important aspects of STEAM, while helping them get in touch with nature themselves and be more aware regarding permaculture.

Aside from the outputs, the project also produced a number of tangible and intangible results. Other tangible results included:

6 partner organizations actively participating/organizing three (3) transnational meetings in Greece, Italy, and Cyprus, four (4) national multiplier events (with at least 40 participants in Croatia, Greece, Turkey, and Italy), and one (1) final international event in Cyprus.
Successful implementation of the project and impact achieved: conditions provided through due professional strategic partnership establishment, careful planning, human and financial resources allocation, Project Management Plan, Quality and Evaluation Plan elaboration, etc.
Successful project dissemination and solid provision of project sustainability: Communication and Dissemination Plan elaboration, Dissemination activities realization, outstanding outreach provided through planned activities and networks available, etc.

2021-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000024455.title: E = MD^2 : Excellence in Math Education through (e-) Debate and Diversity.
2021-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000024455.summary:
<< Background >>

The consortium decided to apply for this project to address the general lack of motivation to study mathematics that the partners have identified in children as early as primary school. As a result, more than 20% of young Europeans do not reach a minimum level of basic maths skills, making it difficult for them to pursue a scientific or technical career that offers more professional opportunities.
The school years are considered the most critical period of education, when students create learning mechanisms, build knowledge and develop basic skills and learning methods. For this reason, the partners decided to tackle this issue at school level and apply for the school education project.
The needs that have been addressed are:
●	Lack of motivation among pupils to learn maths. Children perceive this subject as difficult and detached from everyday life, which causes particular difficulties in understanding. This requires a less passive and more participative learning experience.
●	Gap in the student achievement: Maths is the area with the lowest student achievement and therefore requires special attention and initiatives.
●	Need to modernise the study of mathematics to make it more attractive and purposeful to students through STEAM 

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of this project was raising the profile of mathematics teachers and equip them with the knowledge and skills they need to be able to motivate the students to improve academic performance through targeted initiatives and focused actions to address low student achievement in this subject area.
The specific objectives were: 
●	O1. Transform the learning experience from passive to participative, engaging students actively in the educational process.
●	O2. Democratize the learning process by involving students in choosing their preferred learning methods, influencing teaching activities, and contributing to the revision of the mathematics curriculum.
●	O3. Explore and emphasize the relevance of mathematics in the STEAM context involving other subject teachers. 
●	O4. Ensure inclusive education by developing specific components to support students from vulnerable groups, including those with mild intellectual disabilities like dyscalculia and mathematical anxiety.
●	O5. Implement peer-assisted learning as an innovative approach, fostering teamwork and increasing motivation.
●	O6. Promote the use of ICT in the educational process, offering a virtual learning environment through the e-platform to enhance the effectivene

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation phase of the project we have developed the following activities:
COORDINATION: internal communication between partners and internal communication with the NA, organisation of meetings, administration, conflict and risk management.
DISSEMINATION AND IMPACT: development of the project website, development and distribution of promotional material, organisation of dissemination events, active use of social media, impact assessment, recording of dissemination activities.
QUALITY CONTROL: Conducting regular internal evaluations to review compliance with project objectives, quality of results and overall progress. Implementation of corrective and preventive measures. Preparation of periodic quality reports.
MATERIALS DEVELOPMENT: field research with surveys, collection of good practices, elaboration of the methodology E= MD ^2, development of the materials for the online course, internal and external evaluation of all materials (piloting).
EXPLOITATION AND SUSTAINABILITY: integration of the project results in the schools' curriculum, alliances and collaborations to continue the work started in the project and guarantee its continuity and expansion.


<< Results >>


1.	E-BOOK: ANALYSIS OF TEACHING METHODOLOGIES about the current situation in partner countries
2.	DISCUSSION GROUP in Romania and North Macedonia. & REPORT in EN
3.	A COLLECTION OF 12 GOOD PRACTICES about different math domains as a filtered database to raise motivation in the inclusive classroom
4.	E-MATHDEBATE PLATFORM that gathers all the results developed within the project and has a forum for communication and debate
5.	GUIDEBOOK FOR NEW MATH (E-) DEBATE – Teaching methodology with STEAM approach in inclusive classroom
6.	COLLECTION OF 12 LESSON PLANS ready to be used by teachers about how to deliver inclusive classes with STEAM
7.	GUIDELINES ON HOW TO IMPLEMENT E-DEBATE IN THE CLASSROOM
8.	ONLINE TRAINING COURSE FOR TEACHERS on for using the E=MD^2 method, as a new method for increasing the motivation. 12 modules with a theoretical part, a CANVA presentation and a video (EN)
9.	4-day TRAIN THE TRAINERS in Croatia to present the E=MD^2 method
10.	E-BOOKLET that collects the training structure in all the languages
11.	CURRICULUM to deliver the E=MD^2 method in the future. GDU will grant 4 ECT to the participants that have completed the course
Outcomes are available in EN, SP; GR, ROM, CRO & MAC https://excellenceinmath.eu/

2021-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000027663.title: PlAn for Green OppoRtunities: Be A Digital scIentific chanGeMaker
2021-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000027663.summary:
<< Background >>

The active role of citizens and their involvement is essential to address climate change. Changes in citizens behaviours towards more sustainable patterns can be boosted through STEM, which has attracted a lot of interest lately due to the increased availability of low-cost open-source solutions and the increased interest of young students in being engaged in such activities. Latest technological advances in the fields of wireless sensor networks and the IoT have introduced unprecedented capabilities towards monitoring the environment in aspects of everyday life. Turning these technological tools into powerful educational tools coupled with their proper societal dimension is the opportunity foreseen by PARADIGM: it is a structured pedagogical, scientific and educational project. It contributes to the needs through involving citizens directly and especially the young generation and communities in action plans that leads to a more sustainable lifestyle and relationship to the environment. It contributes to emerging environmental challenges; develops innovative curricula in the green sector, that it is not effectively included in school education; promotes STEM approaches and; upskills teachers through innovative methodologies.

<< Objectives >>

PARADIGM uses the appropriate technological infrastructure (devices, data platforms and tools) to empower the active engagement of citizens in taking action against climate change and for sustainable development through better monitoring and observing the environment and its environmental impacts. PARADIGM promotes innovative practices based on designing and developing the appropriate technological infrastructure coupled with selected learning scenarios that follow challenge-based and project-based learning methodologies, piloted by the network of European Schools in each partner country. In specific, the purpose is to train, lead and motivate learners to gain environmental knowledge and propose solutions via an educational process based on three different learning dimensions-objectives: a)Cognitive: learners gain environmental knowledge through IoT-STEM based activities and platforms b)Scientific: learners acquire knowledge through an empirical process based on the scientific method (e.g. observation, scepticism, cognitive assumptions, hypotheses, inductive thinking, e.t.c.) c)Pedagogical: educators receive the appropriate pedagogical directions to implement a teaching approach based on an e-learning course and repository.

<< Implementation >>

PARADIGM activities evolve around 3 main expected project results which are structured in 4 phases: 1. PREPARATION: project management activities, dissemination plans, exploitation, quality assurance and evaluation, methodology and tools, training curricula and definition of the objectives, target group, learning outcomes and structure of the e-learning, specifications of STEM platform, cataloguing criteria, repository structure, design of CS platform and the evaluation of existing material and the content selection. 2. DEVELOPMENT: training curriculum and modules, setting up of Moodle platform, development of learning scenarios, online events, invitations to participants, setting up and installing the DIY kits in schools, developing the European Community. 3. PILOTING: learning scenarios, e-learning, CS platform, collection of best practices, learning Scenarios, peer review. 4. FOLLOW UP: translations, finalisation of results, European contest, mapping tool of best practices. OTHER ACTIVITIES: validation actions, LTTA, meetings (online and face to face), exploitation, sustainability, multiplier events.

<< Results >>

PARADIGM has three main project results.

PR1. E-learning course for environmental awareness: The online training programme for environmental awareness aims to prepare educators for applying pedagogical structured problem-based learning (PBL) and challenge-based learning (CBL) projects. Furthermore, it seeks to introduce environmental observatories in classrooms to produce inspiring new knowledge based on appropriate technological infrastructure. The training course also guides learners to adopt and implement inclusive education strategies and take actions based on them. The course is accompanied by 15 learning scenarios, self-assessment questions, 7 video tutorials and 1 step-by-step user guide for setting up an ESP32 board with sensors using Arduino. It consists of the following modules and units: PARADIGM strategies to raise environmental awareness, the PARADIGM pedagogical methodology, the PARADIGM environmental challenges, the PARADIGM environmental observatories and turning youth to digital scientific changemakers.

PR2. IoT-STEM Based Environmental Observatories Framework: This includes the design and development of the observatories through the ThingsBoard platform, the DIY kits’ installation and the development of the learning scenarios. In specific, teachers were guided to coordinate students to manage and collect data of natural resources via an environmental data monitoring process (selection, analysis, interpretation of data on the PARADIGM platform ThingsBoard). 1 step-by-step user guide and 7 video tutorials were also created in order to help teachers and students with the installation of the ESP32 board with sensors. Finally, codes for programming the sensors with Arduino were also created for the following sensors: CO2, humidity and temperature, dust, air quality.

PR3. Citizen Science platform: This is the PARADIGM Virtual Maker Space and Repository. It enables teachers and students to participate in fundamental cutting-edge research across environmental issues, increasing its visibility within the European public and discourse. In the citizen science platform, learners can also discuss the results of data (findings) and propose practical solutions. They can engage with other European schools' citizen scientists. Schools have also participated in a European contest among European schools that contributed to delivering the PARADIGM project. The Citizen Science platform also includes a mapping tool of best practices in STEM, green and/or IoT projects, initiatives, organisations, educational programmes, etc. The repository also contains online available resources related to STEM and green education through IoT technologies.

2021-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000027770.title: Open Digital Competences Training for School Educators
2021-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000027770.summary:
<< Background >>

The OpenDigCompEdu project aimed to enhance the digital competences of school educators in Spain, Romania, Croatia, Greece, and Norway to support the sustainable adoption of online and blended education through open educational technologies and principles. Going open is a transformative process for institutions, educators, and learners, fostering collaboration, transparency, and inclusion.

This need remains vital to improving digital readiness, resilience, and capacity to handle crises like COVID-19, as outlined in the European Commission’s Digital Education Action Plan (2021–2027). By accelerating digital transformation, the project equipped educators with blended learning strategies and key competences framed within open education principles.

As a result, OpenDigCompEdu has empowered educators to become enablers of change, integrating innovative digital practices with pedagogical values. These educators are at the forefront of open education in their regions, driving innovation and leveraging digital technologies to create inclusive, future-ready learning environments.

<< Objectives >>

The OpenDigCompEdu project aimed to complement national initiatives by providing a European perspective to develop a European Digital Education Content Framework and contribute to defining the criteria for a European Digital Skills Certificate (EDSC), key priorities of the EU Digital Education Action Plan 2020. The project developed detailed courses and incorporated micro-credentials to improve and validate educators’ digital competences.

The following objectives were successfully achieved: 1) raising awareness of the need for a digital education ecosystem in European schools; 2) devising and validating profiles of digitally competent educators within open education; 3) enhancing the uptake of open education practices, resources, and tools for competence-based teaching; 4) fostering sustainability in education through open education frameworks; 5) improving recognition of digital competences through e-portfolios and MOOCs; 6) introducing micro-credentials and open badges for digital competences; and 7) strengthening collaboration among educators, learners, institutions, universities, and EdTech companies. The project leveraged joint experiences from the diversity of partners, ensuring impactful outcomes.

<< Implementation >>

The OpenDigCompEdu project successfully implemented a wide range of activities to address its objectives, although certain tasks were streamlined or adapted to better align with the evolving project framework and practical considerations.

The Conceptual Framework for the application of open and digital competences for educators was effectively embedded into the project’s broader outputs. As for the Design Guide and guidelines, the principles of open digital competences were incorporated into the curricula, the OpenDigCompEdu program and the training materials.

Insights from tools such as SELFIE, and key frameworks like DigCompEdu, informed the project’s approach, though an iterative feedback and collaborative workshops with educators and stakeholders. Best practices, training resources, and validation criteria were also integrated into the finalized outputs, reflecting the project’s core principles.

The OpenDigCompEdu e-portfolio foundational elements informed other deliverables such as the courses included in the OpenDigCompEdu program which were based on the defined curricula and syllabus of the five courses. Following the approach described on the proposal, the partnership assured the validation and sustainability of the project results through the regional capacity. 

Enriching the experience of educators, OpenDigCompEdu was enhanced and aligned to meet national specifics, integrating online the OpenDigCompEdu for Educators and start the training of the OpenDigCompEdu facilitators.

Finally, the last developed output, the micro-credentials set up the quality validation micro-credentials process and the Open Badges and Certificates. The quality validation process included the designing of the quality assurance standards and the designing of evaluation instruments and periodical progress reports to guide the implementation of the OpenDigCompEdu for educator’s micro-credential. The Open Badges and Certificates included the definition and the design of the open badges, the set-up of the badges and certificates, the user testing and reporting, as well as actions to ensure OpenDigCompEdu sustainability. 

All of these outputs were embedded on a transversal task structure system that ensured an open communication and all the steps possible for the sustainability of the project.

OpenDigCompEdu was able to deliver meaningful, scalable, and sustainable outcomes that aligned with its overarching goal: to enhance digital competences in education through open and innovative approaches.

<< Results >>

As projected on the proposal, the main result of the OpenDigCompEdu project has been an educational program developed for school education. More specifically, the core achievement is the successful implementation of the Open Digital Competences Training Program for Educators, which has significantly advanced the digital competencies of educators across partner countries. This program includes an adaptable training framework and five comprehensive courses tailored to national contexts and specific educator needs.

The project also contributed to capacity building for school educators through a blended approach, combining regional training efforts and a focus on digital transformation. This included the training of facilitators to ensure long-term dissemination and adoption of the program's principles.

Another major accomplishment is the development and implementation of OpenDigCompEdu Micro-Credentials, Open Badges, and Certificates. These tools validate the competencies of educators, offering a scalable, accessible system to support lifelong learning. The program incorporated quality assurance measures, including feedback mechanisms and testing, to ensure credibility and usability.
Certain activities, such as the Conceptual Framework and the e-portfolio, were adapted or integrated into other outputs, the project leveraged iterative development and practical approaches to ensure its goals were met in meaningful ways. This ensured that the program remains aligned with the European framework for digital education while addressing the immediate and long-term needs of educators.

Through targeted dissemination efforts, especially in-person as much as digitally that topped the regional capacity-building activities and the national Greek Multiplier Event and the final multiplier events, the project has empowered educators to become change agents in their schools and communities, fostering open, inclusive, and digitally-enabled learning environments.

2021-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000031544.title: STEM and Gaming Aims for a Meaningful Educational Success
2021-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000031544.summary:
<< Background >>

Technology has been improving so rapidly that it is of great significance for students to adapt to constant changes in technology. Individual competencies in STEM subjects are getting more important for the occupations of the future which are based on high technology. Therefore, innovative approaches are required in education. The era of the fast moving technology needs to be brought in the classroom, and more teachers need to be aware of the patterns that these students need, in order to capture their attention and make them acquire skills and competences. The critical thinking and creativity can be learnt by the studentsin order for them to be ready to cope with the challenges of the society. Within this scenario the project's partners had identify 3 main needs: Support learners at risk dropout with new educational contents; To enhance the participation to educational initiatives of groups at risk of exclusion by developing educational contents and approaches based on the universal language of Multimedia; To find new ways for teachers of motivating students using the tools that students use everyday.

<< Objectives >>

The project's partners had identified three main needs that correspond to the main objectives of STEM&GAMES:
- Support learners at risk dropout with new educational contents;
- To enhance the participation to educational initiatives of groups at risk of exclusion by developing educational contents and approaches based on the universal language of Multimedia, that are often one of the only interest of students;
- To find new ways for teachers of motivating students using the tools that students use everyday.
Through the project, we proposed to:
- improve school success and motivation;
- fight against school failure and absenteeism;
- increase motivation of the students;
- promote the application of innovative strategies and solutions to education;
- empower students to be problem solvers and innovative thinkers through science and technology;
- make an effective use of gaming teaching and learning tools for promoting students interest and active participation;
- bridge the gap between traditional teaching and approaches and new ones;
- enable and motivate students to learn STEM topics;
- promote the application of innovative strategies and solutions to education;
- increase schools’ European dimension.

<< Implementation >>

During the lifetime of the project there were:
1) Three transnational meetings at project partners level (Kick - off meeting – Croatia; Mid-project cycle meeting – Germany; Final meeting – Spain);
2) Two LTTAs about ESL and Game based learning (one in Spain and one in Italy);
3) Analysis of the state of art about gamification in the participating countries;
4) Extracurricular activities about STEM and Gamification;
5) Six (one per country) Multiplier Events;
6) Evaluation and validation of the contents;
7) Dissemination and exploitation activities.
All the above activities contribute to the realization of the IOs of the STEM&GAME project (Guide and APP).

<< Results >>

As mentioned above, two final products were created:
- Intellectual Output 1: a guide of more than 400 pages, designed to help teachers of STEM subjects to combat the phenomenon of school dropout through the integration of the Gamification methodology within the teaching of these disciplines. The guide starts from an analysis of the  health status across the various countries and districts regarding the scientific subjects and proposes a series of educational examples to show how, through the use of educational games, we can help students to practice and improve their performance levels in disciplines they traditionally considered difficult to understand.
- Intellectual Output 2: an educational app that in escape room mode allows students to work in groups to review some fundamental concepts of STEM disciplines. The student has the possibility to choose six different scenarios with different stories that present a difficult situation from which he will be able to escape only by passing a series of tests: within each scenario, in fact, the student will be able to try his hand at four different levels of difficulty, in each of whom, however, in order to escape from the situation identified from time to time, will have to answer a question for each of the selected STEM subjects: Mathematics, Physics, Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Technology or Engineering. In this way the review of the topics will take place in a fun and dynamic way.
Moreover we created the Project website (https://stemandgamesproject.eu/) with description of the project’s activities. It aims to give a reference point for being updated about carrying out of the project activities, for the circulation of the information. It collects and makes available all the contents developed within the project’s activities.
