2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000027781.title: Cell Biology and Art Class Omnibus
2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000027781.summary:
<< Background >>

By encouraging different skills in early childhood, through the family and then the educational environment, a series of skills are developed that remain instilled in children throughout their lives. One example is a way of thinking that involves breaking out of conventional norms and frameworks. Such way of thinking brought the idea of a joint project developed between Juraj Dobrila University of Pula (furthermore UNIPU), fabula movens doo and Petar Pan kindergarten. Creativity, openness, collaboration, resilience, cognitive elasticity as well as social and emotional competencies are becoming an essential toolkit for any child. In addition, STEM education Is becoming vital in helping children better understand the world. Pre-school teachers are the main facilitators of inciting and nurturing diverse sets of skills for pre-school children. Combining biology, music, artists, pre-school teachers, technology driven learning methods brought an idea of Cell Biology and Art Class Omnibus (CACAO) project. Five different countries involved experts in different fields with joint initiative to co-create unique pre-school learning program blending cell biology, music, dance, and visual art.  

<< Objectives >>

Respective project tries to bridge this gap by developing and implementing a highly innovative and inclusive pedagogical concept blending music, visual art, and cell biology.
Research in cognitive psychology and neuroscience implies that engaging in activities that combine multiple sensory skills such as singing, playing, clapping, and dancing makes a significant difference in cognitive development and educational success. On the other hand, the education systems do not offer the possibility of educating educators how to think outside the box and, in a specific project example, use music as an educational tool. An additional problem is the basic IT knowledge of educators. 
Program developed throughout the project is focused on five and six-year-old children and their teachers who can acquire certified professional education on using music as an educational tool to teach children biological concepts. Such interdisciplinary educational approach would not be possible without the support of parents and preschool headmasters who will recognize the value and the need for such a program.



<< Implementation >>

In order to make the project successful the project application envisaged 4 transnational project meetings entitled for administrative discussions.  For the learning, teaching and training 4 different trainings took place. In such an interdisciplinary group, comprised of scientists, academics, and practitioners it was necessary to complement each other’s, knowledge, skills, and experiences. The first training covered design thinking in curriculum design, basic cell biology training, and training on how to use virtual collaborative ILDE 2 platform for co-creation of the project results. The second training covered music as a learning and communication tool and embodied learning. The third training covered engaging communication in front of the camera and the process of creating an online course, as well as the use on online learning tools for continuous professional development. The fourth training was a hands-on training to test newly developed activities in working with children. In order to present and disseminate project results three multiplier events/conferences took place, one in Brussels, second in Zagreb and final conference in Pula. 

<< Results >>

During the two years of the project implementation, five project results was created in a collaborative manner. The first and second project results are curriculum designed for blending biology and art (with emphasis on music) for pre-school children and curriculum designed for blending biology and art (with emphasis on music) for early childhood educators and a definition of CACAO certification. Furthermore, CACAO online platform with the web repository of activities, songs, video, and sound material for the CACAO curriculum is created. The fourth project result is a CACAO online course for early childhood educators following CACAO curriculum design, allowing continuous professional development in STEAM for preschool educators. Fifth project results refers to extensive scientific evaluation of the impact of CACAO program implementation and create Final Project Report. Project activities and results are designed to strengthen STEAM learning in the preschool setting, by developing an innovative educational program and creating complementary professional training for the preschool educators as well as the wealth of material for seamless implementation of the CACAO program. In summary, for the first time to our knowledge, the CACAO project designed and implemented structured multidisciplinary curricula for pre-school educators and pre-school kids, complemented with free and comprehensive training and the omnibus of interdisciplinary activities where multifaceted effects of art are used to immerse both the pre-school teachers and the pre-school children in the world of cell biology to ignite the life-long love for both disciplines.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000031584.title: Law in Everyday Life
2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000031584.summary:
<< Background >>

We initiated this project to empower citizens, especially students, with the basic legal literacy necessary to actively participate in democratic processes, uphold the rule of law, and safeguard fundamental rights. Aligned with the EU's core values of democracy, human rights, and the rule of law (Art. 2; Treaty on EU), the project strengthens the democratic foundations of society. The project tackles key challenges such as the lack of legal literacy by creating a competence framework and educational materials to integrate basic legal education into schools. It focuses on empowering active citizenship, providing individuals with the knowledge needed to advocate for their rights, fulfil civic responsibilities, and engage meaningfully in their communities. Recognising the vital role of teachers, the project supports their professional development, equipping them with tools to teach legal literacy effectively. Additionally, it aligns with EU priorities (Key Competences for Lifelong Learning, European Education Area), fostering resilience, civic engagement, and youth empowerment. The project contributes to preparing students for active citizenship while promoting an informed, participatory society rooted in EU values.

<< Objectives >>

This project aims to achieve several key objectives: Develop a Competence Framework for Legal Literacy: Create a structured framework outlining the essential competences needed for 14- to 18-year-olds to acquire basic legal literacy. This will guide education stakeholders in designing programs and activities that effectively promote legal literacy. Develop Practical Teaching Materials: Develop accessible resources for both teachers and students, using youth-friendly language to explain basic legal concepts and principles. These materials will empower teachers to deliver legal literacy education and help students understand crucial legal structures that impact their personal and civic lives. Raise Awareness About Legal Literacy: Emphasise the importance of legal literacy as a fundamental life skill and a cornerstone of active citizenship. The project will highlight how legal frameworks influence daily life, ensuring legal literacy is recognised as an essential competence. The project aspires to equip young people with the knowledge and skills to engage with legal concepts and rights, enabling them to become informed, active participants in democratic societies.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented the following activities to achieve its objectives:
First, a mapping methodology was developed to collect data from students, teachers, and legal professionals. This involved creating and disseminating a questionnaire to legal experts, scholars, judges, and lawyers specialising in working with young people, aiming to identify key legal structures and concepts for 14- to 18-year-olds. Additionally, interviews with teachers and focus groups with students were conducted in each partner country to gather their perspectives.
Second, the collected data was analysed, and the Competence Framework for basic legal literacy was developed. This framework was subsequently reviewed by elementary and secondary school teachers to ensure its suitability for school settings and its relevance to students’ ages.
Third, based on the Competence Framework, teaching and learning materials were created. These included a teacher professional development program curriculum designed as a model for tailor-made programs, a student textbook, and an accompanying teacher manual, providing a comprehensive educational model for classroom use. Additionally, a massive open online course (MOOC) was developed to offer students accessible and youth-friendly learning materials on basic legal concepts and terms.
Fourth, a limited-scale pilot was conducted with teachers and students. Feedback was collected to assess the clarity and appropriateness of the concepts and structures presented.
Fifth, awareness-raising activities were carried out through online and offline events in each partner country. These efforts culminated in a final international conference, where the project’s results and impact were shared and promoted.
These activities successfully advanced basic legal literacy and provided valuable tools and frameworks to support educators and students in this critical area.

<< Results >>

The project resulted in several concrete outputs and achievements that contributed to promoting and integrating basic legal literacy in education systems.

Concrete outputs:
Competence Framework for basic legal literacy: Developed using a comprehensive mapping methodology and incorporating feedback from teachers of social studies and civic education from four countries. Published in five languages (EN, HR, IT, FR, PT) to ensure accessibility across all participating countries.

Teaching and learning materials available in five languages (EN, FR, IT, PT, HR):
- Teacher Training Program: Designed as a professional development module for teachers to support implementing legal literacy education.
- Students’ Textbook: Introducing key legal terms and concepts in an easy-to-understand format for students.
- Teachers’ Manual: Providing guidance and resources for teachers to implement textbook lessons effectively.
- Massive Open Online Course (MOOC): This MOOC explains and contextualizes key legal principles and structures in everyday life, offering an interactive and accessible platform for students.

Piloting of Materials: Piloted with 80 teachers and 348 students across participating countries, gathering valuable feedback on the materials’ clarity and applicability.

Awareness-Raising and Dissemination Activities: Conducted 11 national sharing and promotion events, reaching 342 participants. Organized a final international conference with 63 live participants and 39 joining online from nine countries to showcase the project’s outcomes and impact.

Other results: - Cross-Country Collaboration: Fostered collaboration between partners from different countries, facilitating the development and dissemination of multilingual resources and strengthening the exchange of best practices. - Scalable and Replicable Model: Developed tools, resources, and examples that can be adapted and integrated into educational systems worldwide, ensuring the project’s sustainability and long-term impact.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000031587.title: Spretne ruke-sretna djeca
2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000031587.summary:
<< Background >>

During the pandemic, the way of schooling and student activities changed: students were significantly more exposed to digital content while studying and during their free time. We noticed changes in their abilities, skills and achievements: poorer graphomotor skills, illegible handwriting, clumsiness in basic motor actions, poor experiential knowledge and knowledge of basic facts.
But even in the education system, there are no opportunities to practice motor skills and practical work since the number of hours dedicated to art and technical culture subjects in which work with hands is applied has been reduced. As a result, students' interest in vocational training has decreased. Research has shown that working with hands develops motor skills, trains multitasking, exercises internal control, calmness, and concentration. In order to motivate students for more active involvement in the learning process, we remembered the thought: "What I hear, I forget. What I see is what I remember. What I do, I understand." This was our motivation for designing a project with which we wanted to include more experiential and practical learning, movement, being in nature in the classes and thus influence the psychological well-being of the students.

<< Objectives >>

We focused on the necessary changes in approaches to teaching in which, in addition to the development of digital skills that are necessary, there should be more practical work and raising awareness of environmental protection. We believed that such approaches to teaching will enable greater motivation, easier learning, acquisition of basic skills and an easier transition to the next level of education. The general goal of our project is to improve the competence of students and teachers in the field of teaching and learning through practical work and activities in the field of environmental protection. Other goals of the project are to increase students' interest in working with their hands, practical, research, student learning in class; strengthen the ecological awareness and responsibility towards all living beings, the environment;through practical learning to increase students' interest in natural subjects and education in trades; to improve the key competences of teachers and school management and to incorporate the exchanged knowledge and skills into the work of schools; improve communication in English and improve the internationalization of schools.

<< Implementation >>

The most important group of activities were activities in TEACHING, i.e. teachers of all partner schools applied practical work in their work in correlation of several subject areas, on the topics: Healthy and balanced diet, Household and sustainable development, Recycling, Green trips, Community and nature.Lessons, workshops, lectures, fairs, exhibitions, contests, marking important dates, and monitoring the work of students and teachers were held. The second group of activities were transnational meetings held in Pakrac with the aim of creating a better relationship with partners, a collaborative climate and successful implementation of the project. The third group of activities are learning and teaching activities, a total of 6 activities. 
 The positive effects of these activities on students are: better understanding of intercultural diversity and increased tolerance, improved interactions with other students, improved English speaking skills, greater motivation for the project and other projects.The intellectual results of the project were created from the overall activities of the partner schools, based on the practices and experiences of classroom teachers. The last group of activities were dissemination activities.

<< Results >>

The project results are an online platform called "Explain to me, show me, involve me" and digital games for students. The online platform is publicly published and contains methodical scenarios intended for teachers and challenging tasks for students. The scenarios are high-quality methodical examples of practical work with different topics with an emphasis on environmental protection. On the online platform there are 25 methodical examples and 50 tasks with the following topics: Environment/nature; Language and communication; Man and nutrition; Household and sustainable development.Another result of this project is 24 educational digital games for students. All games are made in English, and students improve their understanding of the English language as well as their knowledge, skills and attitudes about climate change, sustainable development, the relationship to nature, the environment, consumer lifestyle.Other results emerged from the numerous activities of the project: brochures about the project, a digital cookbook of recipes made from leftover food, didactic materials for classes made by recycling, landscaped school gardens, planted tree rows, ecological cleaning products, a project website that can serve as inspiration.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000032499.title: deutsch.info+
2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000032499.summary:
<< Background >>

Dyslexia affects 9-12% of the population, according to the European Dyslexia Association, and poses significant challenges in reading, spelling, and writing. A major area of difficulty is learning foreign languages through traditional methods, which are integral to European curricula and essential for workplace success.
Deutsch.info+ aimed to address the gap in teaching methods and materials suitable for dyslexic learners in foreign language education, specifically focusing on German. Despite the importance of multilingual skills, there is a notable lack of effective resources for teaching foreign languages to dyslexic students, especially in languages other than English.
By developing innovative teaching methods and resources tailored for dyslexic students, we aimed to equip educators with the tools and knowledge needed to support these learners effectively. The project targeted both the immediate educational needs of dyslexic students and the professional development of German language teachers, providing accessible, practical information and materials to enhance teaching practices and improve learning outcomes for dyslexic students.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objective of the deutsch.info+ project was to enhance the educational experience and outcomes for students with dyslexia learning German as a foreign language. The aim was to provide German language teachers with specialized materials for their professional development through an online course, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to effectively support dyslexic learners. Additionally, we sought to create and disseminate ready-to-use teaching materials tailored to dyslexic students, ensuring these resources are practical and accessible for classroom use.
The project also focused on developing online materials for individual use by dyslexic children, allowing personalized learning experiences. By raising teachers' awareness of the challenges faced by dyslexic students and providing effective strategies and tools, we aimed to foster a more inclusive learning environment.
Ultimately, we sought to boost the confidence and language learning success of dyslexic students, empowering them to overcome difficulties and achieve academic success. Through a cross-professional approach, we aimed to create a lasting impact on educational practices and outcomes for dyslexic learners.

<< Implementation >>

Key activities included:
- Assessment of Status Quo: Initial assessments were conducted through interviews with teachers and students to understand current learning methods and the challenges faced by dyslexic learners.
- Development of Guidelines: Detailed guidelines for teaching German to dyslexic students were created, incorporating background information, practical tips, and effective methods. These guidelines were formatted as an online course available on the widely-used deutsch.info portal.
- Creation of Teaching Materials: Downloadable and online dyslexia-friendly teaching materials were developed. The offline materials encompass 35 ready to use modules on the deutsch.info teachers' platform. The online materials cater to the unique needs of dyslexic learners by offering multisensory input, self-paced learning, and stress-free interaction with digital devices.
- Multiplier Events: Workshops, seminars, and presentations were organized to disseminate project findings and resources.
- Platform Extension: The deutsch.info portal was enhanced to host all project materials, ensuring free and easy access for teachers and students. This extension aimed to make the platform a central hub for German language teachers across the EU, offering unique materials that meet classroom needs.
These activities collectively aimed to improve educational outcomes for dyslexic students, provide teachers with effective tools, and promote inclusive and equitable learning environments.

<< Results >>

Deutsch.info is the most comprehensive free platform for German language learning and teaching in the world. It was enriched with the following materials to support teachers of German working with dyslexic pupils:
1. Online Guidelines for Teachers "German Lessons for Learners with Dyslexia": This course provides comprehensive guidelines and strategies for German language teachers to support dyslexic learners.
2. Teaching Materials for Pupils with Dyslexia: A variety of dyslexia-friendly teaching materials, including interactive exercises, games, and illustrated wordlists, enhance the learning experience for dyslexic students.
3. Learning Tools for Pupils: Online resources facilitate personalized and effective language learning for dyslexic students.

Beyond tangible outputs, the project achieved the following results:
- Broad Dissemination: Multiplier events and workshops directly reached approximately 300 stakeholders, spreading awareness and sharing project outcomes. Several hundred thousand people were reached through other offline and online dissemination activities.
- Enhanced Educators’ Skills and Awareness: Awareness was raised among teachers about the challenges faced by dyslexic learners, equipping them with the necessary tools and knowledge. This led to improved educational practices and better learning outcomes for dyslexic students.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000032658.title: VIRTUALNA ŠETNJA EUROPOM
2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000032658.summary:
<< Background >>

The project is based on the previous project Literary Map of Zagreb, which connected students' experiences of the urban space of Zagreb and the world of literary works during online classes. Due to the positive reactions of students and teachers, the project was expanded to the international level with the aim of exploring cultural connections between different EU countries. The project was designed to respond to the need for digital educational resources and the development of digital competences of students and teachers, which has become especially important during the COVID-19 pandemic and the sudden digitalization of teaching.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project was to create an interactive map of partnership school cities, produce 8 short videos per partner and integrate street view, an interactive virtual walk, which will present the cultural heritage of partnership cities. The map is integrated into the Google Maps platform, where video materials with an innovative approach and purpose for schools are added to the already existing content, as well as street view, which was designed, recorded and edited by students - participants of the project. In addition to the interactive map and video materials, online video lessons for educating students and teachers were developed in the project. The project encourages new ways of creative expression with the help of digital tools and innovative and interdisciplinary approaches to learning. The participants of the project designed content, wrote synopses and recorded videos that present each of the partnership cities. Various recording techniques were applied, such as drone recording, stop motion and street view recording methods, in order to encourage the strengthening of digital competencies of students and teachers as well as creativity and innovation in filming and editing.

<< Implementation >>

The project included three Joint Staff Meetings, four student exchanges, a final meeting in Spain, and final multiplier events in each partner country. It began with an online Kick-Off Meeting in January 2022 to define goals and assign tasks. The First Joint Staff Meeting in Zagreb (February 2022) focused on synopsis writing, filming, and editing workshops, leading to the First Student Mobility in Zagreb (September 2022), where teams filmed and produced a video on the city's cultural heritage.
The Second Joint Staff Meeting in Sofia (June 2022) evaluated progress, showcased initial videos, and improved editing skills. The Second Mobility in Thessaloniki (March 2023) included filming workshops and the production of videos on Thessaloniki’s cultural heritage. The Third Mobility in Sofia (October 2023) and Fourth Mobility in Mieres (February 2024) followed similar formats, focusing on each city’s cultural landmarks.
The final meeting in Mieres (June 2024) reviewed documentation, verified results, and planned dissemination. Throughout the project, results were shared within schools and communities, promoting cultural awareness and educational innovation.

<< Results >>

The project delivered three key outputs: Video Lessons, Video Materials, and the Interactive Map, designed to enhance digital skills, cultural awareness, and education.
Video Lessons provided step-by-step guidance on video production, including scripting, filming, editing, and directing, using DaVinci Resolve software. Developed collaboratively with partner schools, these lessons target students and teachers, enabling them to create videos that showcase cultural landmarks. 
Video Materials consisted of student-produced three to seven minute videos on cultural and historical landmarks, aligned with various curricula. Available on Google Maps, these videos offer an engaging tool for teaching and deepen understanding of European culture, fostering creativity and language skills.
The Interactive Map features videos of heritage sites in partner cities, accessible via Google Maps with clickable locations. Enhanced with street-view content, it serves as an educational and tourism tool, offering a virtual field trip experience. Continuously updatable, it promotes European heritage to a global audience.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000032765.title: ChemDM - Chemical Dancing Models
2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000032765.summary:
<< Background >>

The main goal of the project was to create a new curriculum encompassing latest approaches and methods of learning, as well as systematic use of digital tools in the educational process. After implementation, educational materials and examples of good practices were provided; both the curriculum and an accompanying handbook for teachers were made available, enabling the systematic use of digital technologies in classrooms and contributing to the capacity and readiness of institutions to transition to digital education through innovative learning approaches, while simultaneously providing necessary support to the teaching staff.
In the STEM field, the most common challenge is the visualization of abstract concepts or phenomena in nature at the microscopic level. The introduction of the new curriculum increased the possibility of visualization, both for molecules and more complex structures, as well as for intricate natural phenomena. In this way, students found it easier to understand and explain how more complex processes function in all living organisms, as well as ways in which digital tools can be used. This has greatly facilitated the mastery of educational outcomes in regular teaching, improved results, and promoted the field

<< Objectives >>

During the four TPMs, some of which took place via the Zoom application, teachers exchanged experiences, new ideas, and suggestions, while collaboratively working on curriculum development. Discussions also covered all project management-related issues, ensuring its quality, and activities related to disseminating project results. The achievement of project goals and planned outcomes was facilitated by organizing two LTT activities. These activities provided training to teachers on the usage and possibilities of the program and its potential applications in the classroom. This enabled the development of digital competences among teachers, as well as their key skills. The 2nd LTT activity served as a curriculum pilot, allowing teachers to gain insights into the quality of the developed curriculum and receive feedback from students. Based on this feedback, teachers could improve the curriculum. Students had the opportunity to enhance their knowledge of chemistry, digital skills, collaborative skills, research skills, critical thinking, and language skills using new interactive methods.
Project activities also included the elaboration of the methodology for monitoring project implementation, work on the project's intellectual output,

<< Implementation >>

During the 4 TPMs, teachers exchanged experiences, new ideas, and suggestions, while collaboratively working on curriculum development. Discussions also covered all project management-related issues, ensuring its quality, and activities related to disseminating project results. The achievement of project goals and planned outcomes was facilitated by organizing two LTT activities. These activities provided training to teachers on the usage and possibilities of the program and its potential applications in the classroom. This enabled the development of digital competences among teachers, as well as their key skills. The 2nd LTT activity served as a curriculum pilot, allowing teachers to gain insights into the quality of the developed curriculum and receive feedback from students. Based on this feedback, teachers could improve the curriculum. Students had the opportunity to enhance their knowledge of chemistry, digital skills, collaborative skills, research skills, critical thinking, and language skills using new interactive methods.
Project activities also included work on the project's intellectual output, evaluation, operational project management and logistical tasks, etc. At the end, four final project conferences were organized

<< Results >>

The main outcome achieved is the curriculum for a new chemistry subject, offered to high school students as an elective course "3D World of Chemistry”, with an accompanying handbook, tasks and examples.
The curriculum enables the establishment of interdisciplinary correlations with a wide range of subjects. This subject allows for connections between chemistry and mathematics (solving problems and various calculations, etc.), studying the structures of different biomolecules correlates with biology, and the program offers the calculation of various physical properties of compounds, such as density, polarizability, etc. This represents an excellent correlation between chemistry and physics. Some parts of the curriculum go beyond the framework of the regular chemistry curriculum, providing excellent preparation for the future job market and strengthening digital competencies, thereby increasing the interest in the STEM field. Students can conduct virtual experiments to better understand the covered topics, especially those they find abstract and challenging.
This encourages interactive and collaborative learning, problem-solving, and critical thinking. The use of digital tools has numerous benefits for both students and teachers.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000034415.title: LINGUA MATHEMATICA
2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000034415.summary:
<< Background >>

LINGUA MATHEMATICA is an Erasmus+ project that aims to bring together two disciplines and two generations. English is one of the disciplines, and Math is the other.
Preschoolers make up one generation, while teenagers make up the other.
According to a survey we conducted with our teenagers, English and Math are both regarded as one of the most difficult subjects. This project makes use of emerging digital resources to create motivational activities for Math learning that are integrated with English lessons. We will create some lesson materials to teach English vocabulary associated with Math subjects. It develops and supports learners in comprehending and enjoying these lessons by using shared terminology, shared applications and web tools, and shared lingua franca. Students will learn Math and English together this way. Teenagers will plan a variety of activities for Maths integrated English classes for primary and preschool students. And we will put these activities into practice in the pre-schools.

The project raises awareness of the importance of Math and English across skill sets and countries, as well as provides a shared practice in using digital resources to communicate across cultures. It encourages learners and tutors from different countries and cultures to work together to improve their skills and communication, much like a video game, but with real-life skills.

<< Objectives >>

The project develops key competencies in 21st century skills, providing participants with the necessary digital era abilities, while also developing a concurrent mindset in using cross-curricular skills to embed learning for new careers and work in the twenty-first century.
The project delves into an evolving and emerging digital world to determine the best job to do in the future. The project recognizes the importance of cultivating creativity in all students, particularly in the critical subjects of English and Math, both together and separately.
Virtual lessons will reinforce creativity in education, as will contests to improve quality and innovation with new methodologies to support our students' creative potential in Math and English. The project will supplement efforts to assist the cultural and creative sectors in recovering from a crisis in terms of greener, more digital, and resilient recovery, contributing to the EU's strategic priorities.

<< Implementation >>

To improve their digital skills, key competencies, and 21st century skills, participants create digital games, digital stories, audiobooks, animated presentations, digital flashcards, augmented reality materials, and other digital materials.
They participate in activities such as logo design contests, building designs with geometric shapes, ornament designs, handmade decorations, art designs with digital tools, patchwork, DIY activities, and short film shooting to improve their creativity and art skills.
They have some activities to make them work collaboratively, such as preparing school bulletin boards, project logo, poster, and slogan contests, chess& backgammon competition, orienteering competition, making researches and presenting them as group works, special occasion celebrations, and, most importantly, LTT activities.
They design a variety of activities that are used with kindergarten students both online and in person. This will instill empathy and tolerance in them toward younger people.
The participants will work with SEN students who have some learning disabilities, and this work will improve the empathy feelings of teenagers.
Teenagers will learn how to conduct research, collect data, and report the findings of their studies.
They will participate in some STEM challenges to reinforce their knowledge of STEM fields, which will be useful in their future careers.

<< Results >>

Through the project, the participants will acquire a better understanding of Mathematics and English and help to foster an environment of intercultural communication. The visibility of the ERASMUS+ program in the regions would be further enhanced.
the project's working methodology will be a combination of means of formal and non-formal education. Participation will be actively encouraged by giving the participants the freedom to work on the project and enabling them to become informal and involved as well as directly involve stakeholders.
All results of the project's findings will be made available on the Erasmus+ Project Results Platform as an open learning resource.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000034443.title: CARE2LEARN - Supporting the Transition from Early Childhood Education and Care to Primary School
2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000034443.summary:
<< Background >>

Primary Education programs provide fundamental academic skills, establishing a solid foundation for learning. Successful transition to PE requires child maturity, quality education, and a support system that acknowledges unequal development and opportunities. Ignoring these can exacerbate social inequalities.

Key early skills for school readiness include gross and fine motor skills, social and emotional maturity, independence, language and communication skills, understanding elementary concepts, and the ability to follow rules and focus. These skills are often practiced in ECEC settings, but many children do not attend ECEC, necessitating family-based reinforcement. Engaging parents in home activities with their children can significantly promote intellectual and social development. Effective programs combine early, child-focused education with strong parental involvement and family support.

The CARE2LEARN project aimed to develop an early intervention tool to strengthen key early skills, laying a quality foundation for education and improving life outcomes. 

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the CARE2LEARN project were:

1. Increase Key Early Competencies: Enhance early competencies in children to improve their chances of early academic success and positive life outcomes. This objective focuses on developing fundamental skills in children at local, regional, national, and EU levels, ensuring they have a solid foundation for future learning and development.
2. Increase Parental Capacity: Empower parents of preschool children to better support their children’s development of early key skills and academic achievement. The project aimed to provide parents with the resources and tools needed to actively participate in their children’s education, fostering a supportive home environment.
3. Relieve Educator Pressure: Alleviate the pressure on ECEC and primary school teachers by increasing parental involvement in early education. 

Overall, the CARE2LEARN project aimed to create a comprehensive support system that benefits children, parents, and educators, enhancing early childhood education and ensuring better long-term outcomes for all stakeholders involved.

<< Implementation >>

The CARE2LEARN project implemented several key activities to achieve its objectives:

1. Development of the C2L SCHOOL READINESS DEVELOPMENT TOOL CURRICULUM (PR1):
    - Conducted scientific literature review, expert interviews (5 people x 3 countries), and parent interviews (5 people x 3 countries), to create a document detailing validated key competencies for children transitioning from preschool to school.
    - Defined 4 broad fields and key competencies for parents to support their children in this transition.
    - Developed activities and materials to support children and parents, later digitalized in PR3 in 4 fields: socio-emotional (6), psychomotor (3), language, literacy, cognitive (7), motivation and learning (4).
    - Translated relevant materials to multiple languages for broader accessibility and use across the EU.

2. Creation of the C2L SCHOOL READINESS ASSESSMENT TOOL (PR2):
    - Developed a tool to assess and monitor children's progress in validated competencies troughout 4 broader fields.
 The activity was led by psychologists, ensuring ethical and professional standards. It was based on the results of PR1, aimed at providing parents with a checklist to track their child's development.
    - Translated relevant materials to multiple languages for broader accessibility and use across the EU.

3. Development of the C2L Mobile App (PR3):
    - Digitalized the activities from PR1 and the assessment tool from PR2.
    - Designed with features for assessment and monitoring, skill development, and parental support.
    - Offered multiple activities for promoting skill development, with a balance of online and offline tasks, to develop key competencies while limiting screen time.
    - Included weekly articles to support parents in the transition process (30 in total).
    - Conducted pilot testing of the app by experts in each partner country: Organized focus groups to gather feedback and improve the app based on expert evaluations.
    - Involved parents and children in testing the app for a month: Held focus groups to evaluate the app from the target group's perspective, and made final adjustments to the app before its official launch based on feedback.
    - Translated relevant materials to multiple languages for broader accessibility and use across the EU.

4. Dissemination Activities:
    - Organized 6 multiplier events in 3 countries with 162 participants in total, to present and share project results with stakeholders.
    - Engaged ECEC and primary school educators, parents, and other relevant stakeholders.
    - Promoted the project through various channels, including social media, partner and project webpages, newsletter and social network.
    - Prepared and distributed promotional materials (articles, infographics, newsletter, leaflets) and press releases.
    - Translated relevant materials to multiple languages for broader accessibility and use across the EU.
    - Following progress and creating dissemination reports

5. Quality Assurance and Evaluation:
    - Conducted regular quality assurance checks and final quality reports.
    - Gathered feedback through questionnaires and focus groups to continually improve project outcomes.

<< Results >>

The CARE2LEARN project produced several concrete outputs and achieved significant results, contributing to its overarching goals of enhancing early childhood education and supporting the transition to primary school:

1. C2L SCHOOL READINESS DEVELOPMENT TOOL CURRICULUM (PR1):
The consortium developed a methodological framework and trough validation process, including literature reviews and interviews with experts and parents created a comprehensive document detailing validated key competencies for children transitioning from preschool to school.
In that document key competencies for parents to help them support their children during this transition are defined with activities targeting these competences also defined.

2. C2L SCHOOL READINESS ASSESSMENT TOOL (PR2):
A practical assessment tool for parents to monitor their child's progress in key competencies was developed, targeting competences identified trough PR1. This tool provided a simple checklist to track the development of early skills, ensuring parents could easily assess and support their children's growth.

3. C2L MOBILE APP (PR3):
An innovative mobile application that digitalized the activities from PR1 and the assessment tool from PR2 was created.
Key features included:
- Assessment and Monitoring: Allowing parents to track their child's skill development.
- Skill Development: Offering activities, with a mix of online and offline tasks, to develop key competencies.
- Parental Support: Providing weekly articles related to child development and the transition to primary school.
- The app was made available in multiple languages (English, Croatian, Serbian, Greek), ensuring broad accessibility.
Reports detailing the feedback and evaluations from expert pilot testing and parent beta testing were also created. These reports informed final improvements and adjustments to the mobile app before its official launch.

5. Multiplier Event:
In total 6 events held in 3 countries with 162 people involved, exceeding plans and expectations (90 people planned). The events disseminated the project's results, allowed participants to try out the C2L app, and facilitated networking and feedback collection.

6. Dissemination Materials:
 A common graphic identity and guidelines for these materials were created and ensured consistent and effective communication of the project's goals and results. Project web page, Facebook page and Instagram page were created.
A variety of promotional and informational materials, including infographics, press releases, leaflets, and articles. All these materials were regularly shared trough these channels, web pages and social media of the partners and newsletters of the partners.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000034473.title: Be Well and Green when Digital
2021-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000034473.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we live in a technologically advanced world, where digital devices and smart gadgets are ubiquitous and despite the convenience they bring, the impact of excessive screen time on both well-being and the environment is often overlooked. The youth face issues such as social isolation, psychological distress, and anxiety. The long-term consequences of environmental ignorance, coupled with recently COVID – 19 pandemic crisis, exacerbate these challenges. We applied for this project because, although, basic health and environmental guidelines exist, they fall short in fostering comprehensive competence. Environmental risks, such as the carbon footprint of streaming services, and socioemotional and psychological health risks from excessive screen time are often neglected. It is crucial to develop the skills of high school teachers and students for the safe and responsible use of ICT, which are needs we want to address. Shift to digital classrooms added challenges, leaving the Safety aspects low on the priority list for teachers due to time constraints and lack of knowledge. The hybrid learning model adopted by most countries hinders proper pedagogical design for training within national curricula.

<< Objectives >>

We've established a Partnership for Digital Education Readiness to enhance proficiency levels up to 7, fostering a "healthier and more responsible use of digital technology" among High School Teachers and students. Aligned with the EU Digital Competence Framework (DigComp), our project targeted Competences 4.3 and 4.4 in Area 4 "Safety" - "Protecting health and well-being" and "Protecting the environment." Despite DigComp's widespread use for learning materials, a comprehensive training pack covering all 8 proficiency levels under Area 4 was lacking. Existing materials often focused on selected competences, primarily "4.1 Protecting devices" and "4.2 Protecting personal data and privacy," up to proficiency levels 3-4. 
Our initiative aimed to fill this gap by providing thorough training for all competences in Area 4, with a particular focus on addressing the scarcity of materials for "4.3 Protecting health and well-being" and the almost non-existent resources for "4.4 Protecting the environment."


<< Implementation >>

The BeWEEN project adopted a bottom-up approach, involving high school teachers and students in a comprehensive process of research, analysis, piloting, evaluation, and policy making. Each partner committed a minimum of 15 teachers and 150 students. Over 24 months the project conducted research on competence and mind-set development needs, gathering best practices from Europe. These findings informed the development and piloting of BeWEEN's curriculum for teachers. Piloting activities empowered participating institutions by facilitating practice-related tasks. In the initial phase, the project developed the BeWEEN curriculum, created teaching and course materials, and integrated the training course into the BeWEEN eLearning platform. Tasks included establishing a helpdesk, translating materials, conducting pilot testing with teachers, adapting course content and co-creating teaching resources. In the second phase, the project focused on developing a badge evaluation system for an educational mobile game, collecting and creating game-based learning content, designing the game, and translating it. This phase involved pilot testing, necessary adaptations, and the final release of the educational mobile game.

<< Results >>

Concrete and tangible outputs created through the implementation of the project are BeWEEN curriculum which set the tone for the creation of training materials for module A.  Protecting health and well - being and Module B. Protecting  environment,  teaching resources co-created with teachers ( total 30, 6 per partner country)  and the BeWEEN educational mobile game available on the Google Play application. All outputs available on: https://www.beween.eu/
As it was planned,  BeWEEN project improved the level of key digital competences and skills among high school teachers, intending to transfer this knowledge to students by delivering innovative practices and results related to safe and responsible use of digital tehnology in the digital era.  Also BeWEEN project promoted and strengthend the European lifelong learning area by contributing to the dissemination, multiplication and replication of the use of European transparency and recognition tools and project will have impact on EU policies concerning the safe and responsible use of digital technology.

2021-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000024512.title: GIFTED - Games and Inclusion For Teacher EDucation
2021-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000024512.summary:
<< Background >>

The GIFTED project addressed a critical gap in European education: equipping teachers with the skills to identify and support gifted and talented (G&T) students effectively. In 1994, the Council of Europe recognized the unique needs of G&T students, urging member states to implement measures for their early identification and support. However, many countries, including those in the GIFTED consortium, lack formal teacher training programs addressing these needs, leaving G&T students—especially twice-exceptional learners and those from underserved backgrounds—unrecognized and unsupported. This gap often leads to disengagement, underachievement, and psychological distress. Teachers, feeling unprepared, frequently rely on stereotypes, further marginalizing these students. The GIFTED project bridged this gap by creating an innovative gamified training program and a serious game to enhance teachers’ competencies. These tools help educators identify G&T students, understand their profiles, and implement inclusive strategies in diverse classrooms. GIFTED promotes equitable practices, ensuring all students, also the gifted, can reach their potential and thrive academically and in their overall well-being.

<< Objectives >>

The GIFTED project aimed to address the EU Council’s strategic priorities by enhancing the quality, equity, and inclusivity of education, particularly for gifted and talented (G&T) students, who often remain unrecognized and unsupported in traditional classrooms. The objective was to empower teachers with the skills, knowledge, and tools needed to identify and support G&T students, including those from underserved or twice-exceptional backgrounds. Through a transnational, collaborative approach involving partners from four EU countries and the UAE, the project developed an innovative game-based training program. This program promotes experiential learning, engages teachers in real-world classroom scenarios, and fosters their motivation, commitment, and use of digital tools. By implementing this project, GIFTED sought to bridge gaps in teacher training, provide strategies for inclusive and differentiated instruction, and equip educators to nurture the academic potential and socio-emotional well-being of all students, ensuring fair and equitable access to education.

<< Implementation >>

The GIFTED project implemented a series of collaborative, evidence-based activities to address the critical educational needs of gifted and talented (G&T) students by equipping teachers with innovative tools and training. These activities were designed to develop, test, and refine the project’s core outputs: the Game-Based Assessment Tool (PR1), the gamified online training platform and content (PR2), the comprehensive Training Manual (PR3), and the Open Badge system (PR4), which validates the competencies acquired by participating teachers. The project began with an in-depth review of national and international research on G&T education. Educational experts within the GIFTED consortium analyzed policies, teacher training programs, and best practices, focusing on strategies for identifying and supporting G&T students. This collaborative effort laid the foundation for designing a cohesive training ecosystem, emphasizing inclusivity and responsiveness to the needs of twice-exceptional children and culturally and linguistically diverse learners. Two main pilot phases validated the project’s outputs. The first, a restricted pilot, involved teachers from all consortium countries and external experts from Italy, Croatia, Portugal, and the UAE, who provided initial feedback on the project’s results. The second pilot reached a broader audience of teachers, who completed the training modules and applied the PR1 tool in classroom settings, impacting over 1,000 students. Feedback collected through evaluation questionnaires in both pilots guided refinements, ensuring the outputs’ usability, relevance, and effectiveness.Dissemination and sustainability were integral to the project’s implementation. Throughout its duration, partners disseminated the project through various channels, including university courses, scientific conferences, trsaining events fr parents and professionals, and activities organized by external partners. In Italy, the project was also presented as an example of best practice to the Senate Commission 7 during a hearing on legislative proposals (DDL NN. 180 and 1041) concerning students with high cognitive potential on 9 April 2024. Multiplier events in all consortium countries introduced stakeholders to the tools and methodologies, fostering dialogue between educators, policymakers, and researchers. The PR1, PR2, and PR3 were translated into all consortium languages and are being integrated into teacher training curricula at participating universities, ensuring long-term impact. By combining cutting-edge technology with collaborative educational expertise, the GIFTED project not only addressed a critical gap in G&T education but is also setting a new standard for teacher training in this field, ensuring its innovation and transferability across Europe and beyond.

<< Results >>

The GIFTED project successfully delivered four core project results (PRs), each contributing to the identification and support of gifted and talented (G&T) students and advancing teacher professional development. These outputs were designed for sustainability, inclusivity, and scalability, trying to ensure their long-term impact across consortium countries and beyond. 
PR1: The Serious Game GIFTED is an innovative game-based assessment tool designed to assist teachers in identifying G&T students, particularly in logical-mathematical reasoning. The game promotes inclusivity through cooperative gameplay, where all students collaborate toward a shared class score, shifting the focus from individual competition to collective achievement. Adaptive difficulty mechanisms ensure personalized engagement, while embedded self-perception questions provide insights into socio-emotional skills. Teachers receive detailed reports that guide personalized instructional strategies. Prioritizing data safety, the game operates on a dedicated server, anonymizes student data, and requires parental consent. Piloted with over 1,000 students, the game demonstrated effectiveness and adaptability in diverse educational contexts, making it a valuable resource globally. 
PR2: The Gamified Training Platform and Program is an open-access, asynchronous learning environment tailored to enhance teachers’ competencies in G&T education. Integrating gamification principles, it offers a dynamic learning experience with storytelling, progress tracking, and interactive activities. The platform includes five training modules aligned with the Training Manual (PR3) and supports personalized learning through an initial assessment. Features such as digital portfolios, forums, and a glossary foster collaboration and engagement. Available in six languages, the platform was extensively piloted, with feedback informing refinements. Its seamless integration with PR1 and PR3 ensures a comprehensive ecosystem for teacher training. 
PR3: The Training Manual (TM) provides theoretical and practical guidelines for understanding, identifying, and supporting G&T students. Organized into five chapters, it covers critical aspects such as giftedness traits, socio-emotional needs, inclusive assessment strategies, whole-school approaches, and best practices for instruction. The TM’s hypertextual structure enables interactive, non-linear navigation, supported by links to external resources and materials integrated within PR2. Available in consortium languages, the TM bridges theory and practice, empowering teachers to apply inclusive strategies effectively. Its free e-book version ensures broad dissemination and accessibility. 
PR4: The Open Badge System validates teachers' competencies gained through the GIFTED program. Aligned with the EU’s focus on modular micro-credentials, it offers standardized digital certifications embedded with metadata detailing skills and issuing institutions. Teachers can share badges on professional platforms like LinkedIn, enhancing their visibility and career prospects. Integrated into university programs across consortium countries, the OB system ensures the program’s sustainability and broad adoption in higher education.

2021-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000029847.title:
Litigare a scuola. Metodi ed esperienze per imparare dai litigi tra pari (da 2 a 18
anni)
2021-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000029847.summary:
<< Background >>

The Litigare a scuola project was born after three decades of pedagogical work carried out by the CPP, focused on the recognition of the importance of quarrels among children for learning basic social skills, developing their ability to express themselves, and putting themselves in other people's shoes. It is worth remembering the international recognition of the right to play as part of children's rights (since quarrels are part of games, the right to play implies the right to quarrel). The Litigare bene method by Daniele Novara is taught by the CPP, and well known by two schools of the Erasmus consortium in Italy and Croatia. The work of the LaS project involved two other schools and five partners in Romania, Malta, France and Belgium. The importance of quarrels at schools has been widely confirmed, broadening the scope to two other methods: Peer Mediation at school and the Maltese method using Friendship Cards. The school context in all countries has a strong need to deepen and develop these themes and good practices. A whole school approach is needed on this issue because it is important for health, democratic participation and the inclusion of all citizens. 

<< Objectives >>

Discuss the absence or presence of pedagogical methods to turn quarrels into opportunities to learn basic skills is the first objective. Exploring three main methods for arguing at school helps to understand and define common basic principles. How many teachers know it? We want to make our methods more visible.
We want to work on the transferability of our methods (teacher training and collegial choices), helping teachers to trust more in the potential of children and students. What is common at school is the absence of a pedagogical method for arguing, this generally corresponds to the presence of corrective and stressful interventions by teachers when students quarrel. We have described the effects of methods and lack of methods on relationships in the classes.
Our Project Results are tools for involving the school community in cultural and pedagogical evolution, with the help of communities and Universities.
The link between the early use of methods for quarrelling and the development and maintenance of conflict skills after several years has been explored.
The centrality of learners, children, students or teachers is key to increasing the quality of education to prevent or curb the dynamics of exclusion and violence.

<< Implementation >>

Activities within the partnership. Numerous actions were necessary to make the partnership work and create the attunement to common objectives, built on the specificities and resources of each partner. 
Activities within the schools. The schools worked involving the teaching staff, students, parents and other professional figures useful for producing the results and experimenting with the LaS methods. Some activities were very visible and public, others not. The production of the results and the extraordinary local participation in the LTTA involved non-partner schools.
Outward Activities. The production of Project Results,  information, posts, news published directly or contacts with the press for articles or television reports on the project is very varied. 
Network activities. Surveys were used both internally and to involve other teachers. Workshops and dissemination events were important for networking, too. The activation of Policy Labs in 4 countries involved many people who would not have been involved in the previous actions. 
Training activities prepared for the LTTA and carried out by a team of 6 trainers from 3 different countries.
Research, discussion and production of the planned and unplanned Project Results.

<< Results >>

R1 – coordinated by CPP
A methodological framework about quarrelling children (2 to 18 years old). Texts and original videos:
The three methods are: 
➢ Daniele Novara’s Litigare Bene Method 
➢ Friendship cards by RAFF 
➢ Peer mediation by CPO. 
An Annex to R1 was published in 2024 in EN and IT. 
A one page synthesis of the three methods was made with the “Manifesto for Arguing at School” in 12 languages.
R2 – (CPO)
It is composed of three PDFs, published before and after the LTTA.
The Data Processing Report. It contains data about teachers’ perspectives on “conflicts” and information about courses and activities. 
The Handbook for Nonviolent Conflict Management using the Litigare bene method (In EN and Croatian). It is addressed to Elementary school teachers.
Toolkit for Teachers Training - Know how for let children argue better (made after the LTTA).
R3 – (FREREF)
Guidelines for a Whole School Approach to Pupils Quarrelling
What is WSA; a synthesis of examples; practical guidelines for implementing a successful WSA.
R4 - (IIHL)
Policy Recommendations
They emerged from the cycles of Policy Labs held in the countries involved.
R5 – The Manifesto for Arguing at School. It was unplanned: a small PDF translated in EN, IT, RO and HR.

2021-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000032833.title: BE-IN: Best Innovative Practices for an Inclusive and Emotional Education to face early school leaving in Europe
2021-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000032833.summary:
<< Background >>

Social inequalities developing in the EU school environment is a central issue for our welfare system, present and future.Early school leaving is most often the result of a combination of personal, social, economic, educational and family-related factors, strongly intertwined and leading to cumulative disadvantage. In many cases early school leaving is the result of a process of progressive disengagement from education, linked to underachievement, whose roots may lie in early years. 
The average of Early school leaving  is growing, with the risk of increase the number drop out and of more vulnerability and exclusion of disadvantages students and children. The schools play a key role to prevent and face the effects of early school leaving and the consequences for the youth future. Teachers need to manage the less of cognitive skills and socio emotional competences and the multicultural dimension of the school environment. The BE-IN project played a key role to renew the teaching and learning approaches for secondary school teachers to work in cross-disciplinary areas and to identify the better learning approaches to address personal formative needs of students, tackling educational disadvantage and preventing drop-out. 

<< Objectives >>

The complexity and multi-faceted dimension of early leaving is widely acknowledged and requires an equally multi- dimensional approach to adequately address its diverse causes. The BE-IN project aimed to increase the capacity of the EU education system to face early school leaving by innovative and inclusive educational program and curriculum where learner is at the center of the teaching and learning experiences and teaching is addressed to the personal formative needs. The outputs achieved by the project focused on: 
- creation of an innovative EU training program and pedagogical resources for teacher to promote wellbeing and tackle in effective way early school leaving;
- production of digital pedagogical resources and tools for inclusive and socioemotional education to support vulnerable students with cumulative disadvantage;
- enrichment of the competences and talents of each students valuing cognitive and emotional skills  to prevent exclusion and failure at school;
- development of an EU community of practiones( teachers, educators,  and experts from the field of the SCO)  to exchange inclusive good practices to tackle early school leaving, to elaborate personal learning program for students in vulnerable situation

<< Implementation >>

R1: With the coordination of the Sudwin partner the international report on the state of the art of innovative and inclusive pedagogical methodologies and practices has been realized. The research activities included for each partner country a:desk  research  on European system, policy, connected to early school leaving on diversity of learning   style of students, of the multiple intelligences and on the motivation and recognition of non-formal competences; a focus  group and a online survey  with teachers, educators and students to exchange practices, formative needs,  and to collect feedback on the well-being at school, positive and negative aspect of Dad, needs of vulnerable students; Interviews with selected stakeholders and a shadowing  activity, to observe people in their daily context;  A international  report and Road Map has been realized to summary the evidences of the qualitative and quantitative research activities to develop the curriculum;
R2: With the coordination of Oxfam Italia Intercultural Inclusive and emotional Curriculum e induction training program and testing with teachers has been developed and tested. At the first step a common framework to apply at the educational subject matters the inclusive approach has been designed. Than an intensive training of partner trainers to share methodologies and guidelines to realize pedagogical units in an  inclusive prospective has been done; than Oxfam developed the Curriculum contents on inclusive and emotional dimension, designed the framework of tools for the assessment of the course and the related guidelines. Oxfam worked very closed with the Citizenship in power partner for the digitalization of all material and for the creation of the inclusive Platform for the e-learning course. In each partner country a testing activity of the training program has been done involving successfully teachers.  
R3: With the coordination of Forum for freedom partner, inclusive and emotional curriculum workshop with classrooms has been tested and implemented. Each partner engaged 3 hub classrooms to test the curriculum  program and the inclusive pedagogical material and adopted monitoring tools to investigate the student’s socio emotional skills and problem solving ability. Evidences and suggestions from the students and the teachers to improve the curriculum program have been taken in consideration. 
R4: With the coordination of Citizenship in power partner, the digital European inclusive and emotional platform has been developed and disseminated. From a dedicated section of the platform teachers are provided the training program to acquire the competences and skills to innovate the curriculum with the approach of inclusive and socio emotional education.  The platform provided also, by different section, all tools and resources developed by the project: theorical documents and materials, digital resources, pedagogical kits for teachers and educators  to enrich the teaching methods to tailored formative needs of vulnerable students. 
R5: With the coordination of Antropolis international publication has been realized and disseminated. The publication collects all the main results of the research activities, the results of the testing teachers e- learning course and the testing with the hub schools and the modeling of innovative learning methodology designed by the Be-In project.  
During the project life-cycle cross-activities have been  led by the partners. OII coordinated the project from the management, timing and financial aspects designing a Management Plan, a Quality Assurance, Monitoring and Evaluation Plan and  a Communication and Dissemination plan



<< Results >>

In order to build an education system more equitable and inclusive the BE-IN project developed and tested the innovative Inclusive and Emotional  e-learning program for secondary schools with pedagogical practices and tools specifically tailored on students’ personal learning processes and skills. Thanks to the results achieved with the project, the Consortium developed a specific training course and tools to overcome some barriers (cognitive, social, linguistic and emotional) in learning environment, to promote a more inclusive space for students at school and reduce early school  leaving with an innovative approach. In specific, the concrete output realized are:
 - R1: 5 National and 1 International Report realized with the  action and research approach. The report focused on: state of the art on early school leaving in the EU secondary schools, the effects of Covid19 pandemic and lockdown on wellbeing of students and their motivation to be engaged at the school life, the main formative needs of teachers and students to improve the teaching and learning processes and methods, recommendation to design an inclusive learning course for teachers; 95 teachers  and 120 students involved in the qualitative research, 22 key experts and relevant stakeholders involved; 5 country research report and 1 international report; 1 road maps with the main results of the research activities at EU level; - R2: Inclusive and emotional e-training program created, tested and disseminated in 5 Eu country. The e learning course, based on the inclusive and socio emotional paradigm, provided to teachers and educators theorical framework, digital resources and tools to put in practices into the classroom to innovate the teaching methods to tackle early school leaving and promote wellbeing. The training course provided also multilevel units created by each partner and some teachers to integrate the school curriculum and support better vulnerable students; 281 teachers enrolled at the training and 149  teachers trained (at 31st december 2023); 10 pedagogical materials- multilevel units created;
-R3: Coaching activities at school to test the inclusive and emotional training program and tools designed in the R2 was conducted in 5 countries on groups of 325 students and 27 teachers from 13 schools involved.  The coaching activities investigated the effects and impacts of educational  intervention based on socio-emotional and collaborative learning (applied in the classrooms). The research evaluated the impact on students´ perceptions, such as feelings of safety and inclusion in the classroom, motivation, cooperation and the relationship with the teacher. Also, the research measured teachers' experiences of the  intervention:
 -R4: Digital European inclusive and emotional platform has been designed and disseminated. The platform has been a tool that gathered all the project outputs and documents, digital pedagogical tools and materials, stakeholder’s contribution and hosted  the e-learning course for teachers developed in the R2; 
- R5: International publication that collected all the efforts and results developed during the life of the project has been designed and disseminated. The publication gathered:  an introduction on the weaknesses of the EU educational system, overview of the formative needs of teachers and students with a focus on vulnerable students, the theorical framework of the inclusive and socioemotional education adopted by the project to develop the e- learning course, the main information and results of the testing activities with teachers and students and recommendations for sustainability   of the project. The publication has been translated in 5 language.
