2021-1-LT01-KA220-SCH-000032440.title: Multimodal Mindset
2021-1-LT01-KA220-SCH-000032440.summary:
<< Background >>

The project addressed various needs identified by its consortium members:

1. Alytaus Adolfo Ramanausko-Vanago Gymnasium aimed to enhance teacher competencies in Multimodal Literacy. By improving teachers' skills in this area, they intended to empower students to develop Multimodal Literacy skills, ultimately leading to improved academic performance.

2. Srednja škola Ban Josip Jelačić acknowledged the benefits of Multimodal Literacy for students but identified a need for innovative methodologies and tools to effectively teach these skills. 

3. iTEACH ITL was an institution actively involved in school education that aimed to increase the quality of education by strengthening existing programs with innovative methodologies. 

4. Educademy, a training institution in the field of Media Literacy, joined the project to address the need for materials that could be used in the realm of Multimodal Literacy. 

5. SC Psihoforworld, an institution working with disadvantaged students, recognized the benefits of Multimodal Literacy for their target audience. However, they highlighted problems with the competence of the institution's staff and educators. 

6. Fundacja wanted to increase both the quality and quantity of these studies. 

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of implementing the project were multi-faceted. Firstly, the project aimed to equip teachers and trainers with innovative pedagogical tools, enhancing their capabilities to effectively teach Multimodal Literacy. Secondly, the project sought to raise awareness of Multimodal Literacy, emphasizing its importance in the contemporary educational landscape. Within the classroom environment, the primary goal was to teach students Multimodal Literacy skills using the most innovative tools and methods available, fostering a comprehensive understanding of communication in a multimodal world. Additionally, the project aimed to cultivate critical thinking among students, specifically in their interpretation of messages conveyed through various media forms. It aspired to enable students to analyze complex multimodal texts and provide them with skills and models to approach such texts from a critical perspective. Furthermore, the project had the objective of assisting students in understanding challenging scientific concepts and enhancing their ability to create graphics, leveraging the cognitive benefits associated with Multimodal Literacy. 

<< Implementation >>

1. International Piloting Short-term Joint Staff Training Event:
This activity involved the participation of teachers and trainers from partner organizations, with four representatives per country/partner. The event focused on providing international training to enhance the competencies of educators in Multimodal Literacy.

2. International Piloting Short-term Exchanges of Groups of Pupils:
Students from partner countries, along with accompanying persons, engaged in international exchanges to share experiences and perspectives related to Multimodal Literacy. 

3. Local activities were organized with the involvement of 40 students per country. These activities aimed to directly engage students in learning and practising Multimodal Literacy skills within their local contexts.

4. Each partner country hosted a local seminar with the participation of 20 teachers/trainers from other schools, NGOs, and institutions. These seminars served as forums for sharing knowledge and best practices in Multimodal Literacy education.

5. One multiplier event per partner country was organized, with the participation of 20 individuals from the general public, targeted students, and stakeholders. 

<< Results >>

The project has successfully generated concrete outputs and results, each contributing to the project's overarching goal of promoting Multimodal Literacy in educational settings:

1. Multimodal Mindset in The Classroom: The Education Format:
This comprehensive educational resource provides content to empower teachers in enabling students to acquire Multimodal Literacy skills within the multimodal and digital world. The focus on increasing the competence of teachers and trainers in this field ensures that educators are well-equipped to effectively teach Multimodal Literacy, contributing to a more robust educational environment.

2. Multimodal Literacy Tool Kit:
This tool kit represents a tangible outcome that supports the research-based education format obtained in R1. It serves as a practical guide for teachers and trainers, offering tools, methodologies, and resources to facilitate the integration of Multimodal Literacy into their teaching practices. 

3. Multimodal Mindset Web Portal:
The web portal serves as a centralized and accessible online platform, offering content related to Multimodal Literacy. It encompasses the educational format, the Multimodal Literacy Tool Kit, and additional resources.

2021-1-LV01-KA220-SCH-000027689.title: Innovative digital approaches in learning environment in European schools
2021-1-LV01-KA220-SCH-000027689.summary:
<< Background >>

The project "Innovative Digital Approaches in the Learning Environment in European Schools" was set up to offer the students and teachers involved a new way of understanding technology and how to use it in the classroom. Digital technology is of many children's lives, they are surrounded by technology in the form of smartphones, tablets, internet apps, video games, video entertainment, websites, and even robots. When students learn to use technology in the classroom and outside, they develop cognitive skills and methodological, problem-solving process that resembles a computer. Modern and interactive digital tools and Web, 3D, and media technology help us at this point, the teachers to create a more appropriate education environment for students by providing them with an opportunity to design their learning materials and to enrich their curriculum. The COVID-19 pandemic spread rapidly worldwide, turning our lives upside down, having already claimed thousands of lives, and bearing disastrous consequences at an economic and social level looming on the horizon. This project helped participants by improving their understanding of digital tools, technology, and methodologies that are used in schools all around Europe.

<< Objectives >>

With this project, we aimed to reduce the absences of our students' school by increasing their interest in school subjects connected with IT and STEM disciplines. We provided students with better learning of subjects by using Web, 3D, media, and other digital tools in the project so that we contributed to achieving the EU goals. Integrating digital tools such as Coding, Web, 3D and media technology in the educational environment created a more active and engaging classroom environment where students have a more positive attitude towards each other, collaborative study, effective learning, analytical thinking, individual learning, student responsibility, etc. Students learned literacy in technology and became more motivated for their lessons. The teachers integrated product-focused assessment and not a standardized assessment by gathering more information in a shorter time, making assessments faster and using time more efficiently. 
Project objectives were met: improved 4 schools’ curriculums in the field of teaching digital skills among students and raising teachers’ skills through exchanging methodologies & good practices. Participants developed personally and professionally - they became more self-confident, more intercultural.

<< Implementation >>

We organized 4 learning activities for students, 2 teacher training activities, and 3 TPMs. Every month, virtual project meetings were organized. The LTTAs provided us the opportunity to meet and share our research and work because of the elaboration of intellectual outputs. The virtual transnational project meetings provided the opportunity for management teams to discuss, evaluate, and adjust the management and implementation activities following the needs and problems identified. The project activities bear positive effects on all the involved participants, on all project organizations as a whole, and on other categories of target groups and beneficiaries that we have established as our priority. 
C1 - Teacher training: SCIENTIA NOVA: Innovative teaching/learning approach integrating Block-based coding with Micro: bit, interactive OERs, and e-learning.
This activity accomplished the aims: 
- equipped the teachers with the skills, tools, and methodologies to answer and address the needs of the students in the field of innovation, digital tools creating platforms, etc.
 - improved IT, social software, and the use of multimedia which enhanced existing curriculum delivery and improved the learning experience supporting educators’ practice. 
C2 - LTTA for students : AECCB: Web tools for foreign language learning.
This activity was focused on how to use web tools in foreign language learning. The students and teachers involved learned about web tools for foreign language learning. 
The activity was focused on how to use web tools in foreign language learning. During these days, the students and teachers learned about web tools for foreign language learning. The activity worked with the following web tools:
- instruments for creating presentations: Prezi, Voki;
- an instrument to create animations: Xtranormal, PowToon - tools to collaborate: Blogger, Wikispaces, PadLet;
- audio-video instruments: VoiceThread, YouTube, H5P - Google+ instruments: Google Docs, Google Slides, Google Spreadsheets, Google Maps; 
- planning instruments: Mindomo, Dipity;
- instrument for sharing: Calameo; 
- instruments created for online tests: ProProfs, Classtools, FrancaisFacile. All these web tools familiarized the students with the variety of web tools and learning how to use them in the classroom.
Students were introduced to educational web tools for learning foreign languages but also became able to create their educational content, using their favorite web tool.
C3 - Teacher training: SDZ: Creating digital environments for teaching potentially gifted children and youth.
The aim of this teacher training was to demonstrate/observation of center activities both online and offline, to continue the integration of international teams, deepen knowledge, and improve the digital skills of teachers. This activity helped raise teachers’ skills through exchanging methodologies & good practices and sharing digital and coding info, national strategies, teachers' methods, and best practices currently available in Croatia. It also helped partners in realizing that gifted children also have special educational needs. During all 5 days teachers and educators integrated, worked, and cooperated in international teams, and communicated in English. Apart from improving skills related to the project topics, the guests also learned aspects of the culture of Croatia through cultural activities. Teachers participated in the Enter conference with presentations on the education system for gifted children in the partner countries.
C4 - LTTA for students: ESRG: Real-world applications of sensors, robots, and drones for educational purposes. Interactive approach with AppInventor.
Participants learned about sensors, robots, and drones which was exciting and motivating for them. They saw and used hardware and real-world application approaches where the students constructed an educational robot. The pedagogical approach with AppInventor introduced to the students the making of mobile Apps with AppInventor and examples of applications of robots and drones and game making with the constructed educational robots and drones. The teacher learned about interactive and innovative teaching and learning methods and approaches with which they can motivate the students to become creative, problem-solving, motivated, researching, and engaging persons who can create mobile games and applications for robots, sensors, and drones and build them. They visited Experimental activities in the Expolab Centre (Augmented reality, virtual reality, and a surprise game). Participated in educational game programming with the constructed educational robots and drones. 
C5 - LTTA for students: OGRES TEHNIKUMS: 3D Design and Modelling. 
This LTT aimed to continue the integration of international teams, deepen knowledge of coding, and improve the digital skills of students and teachers. During all 5 days, the students apart from improving skills related to the project topics, learned aspects of the culture of Latvia through cultural activities. Project participants were given insight bout 3D design and modeling as well as 3D printers. 
Project participants participated in several master classes organized by teachers and students of the Ogre Technical School, such as the master class on creating 3D animations organized by Ogre Technical School professional subject teacher Armands Pučs. 
As part of the master class, the project participants had the opportunity to participate in the process of creating 3D animations themselves, using various programs, as well as learn new knowledge about creating 3D animations. The second master class was provided by Dace Runča, teacher of vocational subjects, and Artis Slenģis and Rūta Jaunzema, students of the Department of Design and Art. Within the framework of the master class, the project participants were introduced to the specifics and basic principles of 3D product design, as well as the basic principles of using 3D in graphic design. Project participants had the opportunity to see first-hand the working principles of a 3D printer, as well as to practically create a 3D element themselves. The third master class was provided by the representative of "AlienWorx" company Kristians Timma, who presented the differences between different 3D printers, the latest technologies in 3D printing and modeling. Project participants had the opportunity to view various 3D printers and also the final results of 3D printing - products.
C6 - LTTA for students: Ibrahim Kozacioglu Ortaokulu: Building A Sensor For Distance Learning Through Arduino Set.
This LTTA aimed to develop digital skills through Arduino. At the time of the mobility, students had the chance to create a sensor that helps to keep good posture in front of the computer. Approaches used in the mobility were practical, experimental, and based on analyses of reality and concerns of the group. Participants worked in small groups, encouraging reflection and creativity between groups. All the participants were given an introduction to Arduino coding, and how to use it to become a new creator. Students were also introduced to 3D design possibilities in Turkey. Apart from improving skills related to the project topics, the guests also learned important aspects of the culture of Turkey through cultural activities.




<< Results >>

Three outputs were created during the project: https://www.indigproject.eu/project-results
1. Innovative methodologies:
These methodologies introduced innovative approaches to the teaching and learning process. Teachers will implement these methodologies in the next few years which will be a subject of continuous evaluation and improvement in teaching various teaching subjects. This project's results aim to create a methodology for improving teaching skills and professional development of teachers systematically when it comes to effective teaching and learning. In this context, the use of digital tools should improve the quality of lessons in Europe. Developed more interactive and motivating teaching and learning methods and techniques for better student engagement.
 2. Platform (Toolkit) with a selection of Web, 3D, media and other digital tools and applications to be used by students and teachers to learn, present results of their work, asses etc. - https://www.indigproject.eu/.
This platform supports teachers in Europe to teach effectively and activate their students when it comes to communicative skills, creativity, and critical thinking – basically preconditions for studying and working in Europe. At the same time, students became more competent in the digital field. The scope and complexity of digital learning arrangements differ widely –from simple multiple-choice tests on the one hand to openly designed explorative virtual environments; digital content in addition to their paper textbooks and a large number of learning tools and -games as digital teaching material produced by teachers. The benefit of introducing digital learning material is not only the sheer number of available products but even more the lack of a valuation model that is not so much focused on the aims of the material but on the underlying learning model. Teachers should understand that they have to be concerned about becoming good teachers to consider using digital tools to enhance the learning process and then integrate digital tools. To engage students more thoroughly in the learning process, it is a good idea to use various digital or media tools. Teachers need to transform their lessons so students can learn to cooperate, develop creative and critical thinking, improve problem-solving skills, and have fun using modern technology. In this example, students learned how to use a 3D modeling and 3D printer and how to use its resources carefully as they can only print a limited number of different shapes, so they need to plan. Also, teachers need - an interactive mathematical software program for learning and teaching mathematics and science in school up to university level.
3. Integrating performance and product-focused assessment as part of teaching potentially gifted students in European schools is an attempt to create guidelines and surveys usable at schools to estimate how their projects integrate the two types of assessment. It resulted in a survey translated into all partner languages and a summary of our initial surveys. It is a valuable tool for schools to analyze how their projects approach assessment.
At the end of the project Multiplier event / The Closing Conference “Milsetones of InDig” took place at Ogre Technical School. In this event, 30 local participants and 20 foreign participants participated. 
Project social media and other collaborative digital networks were made:
-Facebook project page https://www.facebook.com/groups/602168614221981; 
- Youtube page https://youtube.com/@InDIG_EU?si=qsfcaRpbsg2ZoRRO
- Facebook, Whatsapp, eTwinning Space, and other virtual media; 
For each mobility digital and face-to-face presentations of the topics defined for each physical or virtual activity of the project were made.
A logo competition took place at the beginning of the project in which participated all partner schools. 
Technology days were taking place in partner schools as "Other activities" implemented within the project. 
Assessment questionaries were made for each LTTA in Google Forms. It helped evaluate each activity and to report data.
Every participant improved social and intercultural competencies that will help them avoid any kind of violence, discrimination, and bullying in their everyday life.
During the time of the project improved the network between schools by cooperating, and sharing pedagogical experiences and good practices.

2021-1-LV01-KA220-SCH-000029630.title: Digitāli klimatam
2021-1-LV01-KA220-SCH-000029630.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was an international collaboration to contribute to two global issues: the fight against climate change and digital transformation. Climate change is one of the biggest threats to our environment, social environment and economy. The impacts of climate change are already visible and are expected to become more pronounced. Through Digi4Clima, we wanted to provide knowledge and raise awareness about environmental sustainability and climate change of project's target audience - teachers working with primary school students, who in turn are a generation with the potential from a young age to acquire the necessary competences to take responsibility for their actions towards a healthy global environment. 
The increasing volume of information and the rapid development of modern technologies make changes in pedagogical work necessary, so the use of digital learning tools in the teaching process is a topical issue in order to help students not only acquire the necessary knowledge, but also be prepared for the life in the digital environment.  Effective digital learning requires the development of digital learning tools that go beyond the mere transfer of content into digital formats - these tools need to be interactive


<< Objectives >>

In an age of technology, it is essential to give students a comprehensive understanding of the challenges facing our planet and to inspire them to become environmentally conscious citizens. 
DIGI4Clima aims to develop and promote a digital learning tool (DLT) on climate change that provides knowledge, raises awareness on environmental sustainability and promotes digital literacy. The DLT supports teachers in educating elementary school students about the dangerous effects of climate change, thus developing a respectful attitude towards nature, making them aware of the consequences of their daily actions and encouraging them to live more environmentally friendly lives. The project results were expected to provide teachers and students with access to high quality and easy to use digital learning resources on environmental sustainability, as well as to support educators in the use of ICT for face-to-face and distance learning.
The implementation of the project results will build an international network of partner organisations and educational institutions using the DLT. The DLT emphasises the idea of unity and togetherness to highlight that we are all united in a global family and dependent on each other


<< Implementation >>

Project management team was formed, which consisted of representatives of each member organization. In the course of the project, three international meetings were organized for the management team, which took place in all three member states - Latvia, Lithuania and Croatia. Remote international meetings were also regularly organized throughout the project. 
During the implementation of the project, the project results development team developed the curriculum and guidelines, and performed the digitization. The results of the project were developed in accordance with the set goals and tasks. Three outputs were developed in the project: 
1) Curriculum "Climate and its changes"
2) Guidelines for teachers 
3) Digital learning tool (DLT) "Climate and its changes"
To ensure quality of results development, three training sessions were organized for the project results development team – one in each partner country. A fourth training session on maintaining, updating and improving the digital learning tool, which was not initially planned, was organized in Croatia. 
With the aim of spreading and popularizing the results of the project, three seminars for educators were organized - in Latvia, Lithuania and Croatia. 

<< Results >>

The curriculum "Climate and its changes"  is the first result of the project that consists of 12 lessons. The curriculum is intended for teachers’ work with primary school students. It defines learning objectives, describes planned activities of teachers and students, necessary materials for practical lessons, used literature and resources. 
Guidelines for teachers on the use of the digital learning tool "Climate and its changes" (DLT) are the second project result. The main aim of the guidelines is to provide a structured framework for effective introduction to complex concepts related to climate change. The guidelines reflect the approbation process of the DLT and include printable worksheets for students. 
The DLT "Climate and its changes" is the third project result. DLT is designed to provide knowledge, build skills and understanding of environmental sustainability and promote digital literacy. The DLT is intended for primary school students to learn about the dangerous effects of climate change on Earth. The tool is designed by adapting the information to the age of the students and ensuring that it is engaging and meaningful, using a combination of visual information, narration, interactive and practical activities.

2021-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000024460.title: The Challenge to a Healthy Life
2021-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000024460.summary:
<< Background >>

We started with the wish to change the mentality ”Food is tasty, time is short and exercise is hard” that exists in more students and adults all over the world. The needs we wanted to address were: low levels of physical activity for students and teachers, the lack of places where to
be active, lack of time to do physical activities, few or no knowledge about healthy eating principles. Another issues we wanted to solve with this project were the low levels of active participation of students in school activities,  and also no preoccupation and time of teachers  to motivate, mentor and help students to learn by reflection, to have agency, to be capable of acting by themselves to make plans, carry out actions, make an informed decision based on their knowledge, and be flexible in changing times.
The third need identified in all schools, from all six countries involved in the project, was the low level of active participation in the life of communities. We wanted to help students discover the ways in which they can take action and improve the community, respecting principles of sustainable development, through service learning campaigns.

<< Objectives >>

Briefly, we wanted to achieve more students, more active and healthy, more often. We decided to start  to build capacity for teachers to become active and to be prepared to motivate, mentor, and help students to adopt a healthy lifestyle. We  wanted  that participants gain awareness and understanding about the importance of a healthy lifestyle by participating in conferences and presentations on the theme, and practice physical activities and healthy eating habits, by participating in the challenges of the project or by setting their own goals. At the end of the project, we wanted for the participants to reach the WHO recommendations regarding physical activity and healthy eating habits. Also, we wanted that participants to experiment with an approach for personal development: set a goal, made a plan, and achieved the goal; to  acquire knowledge for critical thinking and media literacy for the identification of fake news regarding healthy eating and safe physical training.
We wanted to involve the students in community life; regardless the community is the school or the whole city, by organizing public events  and building the safe routes, usable for all members of the community.

<< Implementation >>

The main activity consisted of challenges for PA (physical activity) and EH (eating habits). Every month students and teachers were challenged to reach a goal for PA such: number of steps, minutes of activity, number of activities, distance covered by walking, running, riding. For eating habits, they were challenged to have a number of days without sweets or without fast food, or days when ate much fruits or vegetables, or counted the number of glasses of water, number of days in a month when they were eating the healthy dish (half vegetables, quarter protein, and quarter carbos), etc.  Another activity consisted of courses intended for teachers to develop knowledge, skills, and attitudes for motivating students, time management, and reflection. Also, teachers involved in this project had some individual activity in order to reach a specific health goal. We organized mentoring activities for students with health-related problems, low levels of fitness, in general students who were reluctant to PA or who had unhealthy eating habits. Teachers created content for the lesson to be embedded in PE lessons and Counselling Classes, organized activities for students designed to know and understand the basics for PA (warm-up, intensity and cools down), practical activities with students to experiment new physical activities which could be performed with moderate to vigorous intensity. We organized Sports Events  and made Service-learning projects to design and create safe routes to school, for walking, riding, and running in the surroundings of the cities. 
We organized Special Days at which were invited  the students, teachers, and parents, cooking workshops (and created healthy recipes starting with favorite dishes and replaced some ingredients with healthy ones and also we  recorded the making of cooking healthy dishes.

<< Results >>

431 participants gained the healthy lifestyle status, an indicator (healthy ladder) which was computed based on the daily reports of participants,  which were made on our platform (PDP- https://chl.cnlr.ro/), 36+17 teachers with knowledge about how to coach students (620 students) to achieve  a healthy lifestyle (set a goal, make a plan and perform activities to reach the goal), 6 routes  for doing PA, Several safe routes to each school, Handbook about designing a service-learning campaign for teachers, Handbook for embedding Healthy Habits into school culture= the calendar for schools, 6 guides: Step by step approach to... running, riding/cycling, dancing, outdoor games, hiking, healthy eating, orienteering -designed for students, teachers and parents, 7 Recipe blog - with recipes for students’ favorite dishes modified with healthy ingredients, one in each schools, in their own language, and one in English, one vlog, on the YouTube (video - recording of cooking healthy food), 4 types of lessons:  with the objective:  set a goal, be physically active, deal with fake news for PE classes and Counselling Classes, An online platform for monitoring progress of PA and eating habits developed during the project (PDP).

2021-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000027872.summary:
<< Background >>

The most intense security problem in our educational environments was different forms of bullying (physical, verbal, social or relational, cyberbullying and sexual bullying) experienced in inclusive classes and classes with pupils from different socio-cultural, economic and ethnic groups.
We applied for this project because we all registered various forms of bullying, as consequence of different barriers to access education, such as barriers linked to education and training systems, cultural differences, social barriers and barriers linked to discrimination. We aimed to eliminate the disadvantage of obstacles by changing the mental structure rather than working with each type of obstacle separately.
Our project emerged as the product of our search for solutions to those problem areas. Our needs were related to ways to tackle any form of bullying. We needed to enable our institutions to become safe places for everyone. To increase our capacity to produce sustainable solutions with innovative methods and techniques, and innovations in anti-bullying tool. To develop mutual understanding, tolerance, respect for differences and caring thinking. To install and secure more inclusive, peaceful, more participatory learning environments.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of our project was to enable our institutions to become a safe place for everyone, where any soul can flourish by eliminating the disadvantage of obstacles by changing the mental structure rather than working with each type of obstacle separately.

At the end of the project period, the number of bullying cases decreased by 50% compared to the pre-project situation by increasing anti-bullying skills from 40% to 70%, developed during 3 LTTs for 44 educators on-line and 7 educators on-line, and by increasing the ability to cope and combat bullying and discrimination from 40% to 70% by implementing activities, workshops and campaigns for 1 LTT for 29 student and aprox.4000 students - 200 parents from 7 partner countries, and by raising awareness of bullying and discrimination from 30% to 60% through publications and events
2. Developing critical-creative-collaborative and caring thinking skills of educators and students from 7 partner countries from EU and beyond by using formal and non-formal education.
The intellectual foundation studies carried out on preventing bullying and discrimination, and the international conference became part of our project legacy.

<< Implementation >>

Transnational management meetings:

2.Mid-term Management Meeting in Umag, HR
3.Final Meeting in Sliema, MT

Learning, teaching, training activities:

Other Relevant Activities: Philosophy Workshop For Adults(Teachers)-16 sessions/24 Philosophy workshop for adults

Our project faced a challenge that was successfully tackled under RO NA supervision: the FR partner school dropped out, so it was replaced by a similar school from GR. The budget was re-organized, as the timeline. After announcing the winning of the project, each partner established by internal decision a project team and a coordinator. These were approved within the administrative councils held at the school/organizational level. The project coordinators held an online meeting at the beginning of the project. During this meeting they made the necessary updates and plans regarding the time management of the project activities and the efficient use of the budget. Together we designed a Gantt chart based on the project activities and the DEOR plan (the integrated campaign for communicating the results of our project). These meetings were repeated monthly. In addition, committees of at least 3 people were formed from all partners under the chairmanship of the project coordinators. The task of this commission was to control the time allocated to the activities and to ensure the efficient use of the budget. 
After starting the project, our committees created a plan to implement the activity, which included the following information:
• For each activity, what was the most optimistic, most pessimistic and most likely determined time. The duration and expected time of the activity were determined taking into account these periods and other possible situations.
• The persons responsible for each activity from the activity implementation plan were designated.
• The budget information and possible expenses related to each activity were recorded in the activity program. Budget and activity related packages have been established. With this planning, our project was completed within the project period and with a budget in which we fit optimally. Our committees held monthly monitoring and evaluation meetings. They also provided information on a monthly basis to other people from the institutions involved. Digital technologies were actively used for time management. The Budget and Time Committee planned budgetary resources, estimated and controlled costs. They looked for the best financial options for financing the project activities (equipment, training, seminars, tickets, etc.). They ensured that the host countries found 2-3* hotels at a good price and only the necessary equipment is purchased by them. The committees performed the monthly monitoring of the budget and time management according to the following criteria:
• compliance with the contract/program
• respecting the administration of each partner school
• compliance with the law
• compliance with the activity plan and project objectives
• carrying out activities efficiently, economically and efficiently
• protection of assets and resources
• keeping accurate and complete accounting records

2021-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000027875.title: Inclusion gets viral
2021-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000027875.summary:
<< Background >>

"Inclusion Goes Viral" envisioned the imperative integration of students from diverse social backgrounds into a cultural environment. Its goal was to assimilate them into European heritage by exploring their roots and fostering the creation of their unique identity through innovative tools like videos. The partner countries involved in the project were Romania, Portugal, Italy, Spain, Croatia. The project facilitate idea was to explore our origins through innovative approaches, fostering participants' creativity in the process. The needs of the partners were: promoting the cultural development of students to cultivate a positive attitude toward national and European values; to cultivate a European sense of belonging through culturally and educationally significant initiatives; to identify common tools for exploring shared origins, history and culture; to advocate for the cultural heritage of European values; to foster an anti-discriminatory attitude against race, gender, age, ability, class, sexuality, language, and religion; to nurture a sense of belonging to an open, democratic, and sustainable society; to promote social inclusion for disadvantaged groups and also to strengthen key citizenship competencies.

<< Objectives >>

The project's objective was to cultivate students' awareness of the cultural richness within the European Union, uniting nations through shared values such as respect for human rights, dignity, freedom, equality, democracy, and the rights of minority groups. Additionally, the initiative aimed to seamlessly integrate literature, arts, geography, and history into transdisciplinary activities beyond the conventional classroom setting. The envisioned accomplishments included:
1.	Assisting 25 socially disadvantaged students from four European countries, with limited access to culture, in finding their equilibrium for successful integration into a multicultural society over the two years of implementation.
2.	Integrating literature, arts, geography, and history into transdisciplinary activities outside the classroom for 100 students from each partnering country.
3.	Finding a new hobby by engaging a target group of 100 students in the study of writing effective poems or creating works of art.
4.	Strengthening key competences and citizenship, especially in the areas of learning to learn, design, collaboration, and active participation, for 100 students from each partner country over the two years of the partnership, also in the future

<< Implementation >>

To accomplish the project's objectives, we implemented five distinct types of activities:
- Local Activities: These activities involved both students and teachers, focusing on the preparation of LTTAs (TikTok's for the Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities), linguistic preparation,  as well as dissemination events/ articles.
- Virtual Collaboration Activities: Team meetings were organised virtually every 2 months or more often before a LTTA, in order to discuss details, program, activities, hotels suggestions for accommodate students and accompanying teachers, local transportation and other topics; the results from all activities were shared on Twinspace, in the collaborative digital space created for this purpose.

LTTAs organised, according to the application form:
C1. Sharing Traditions - a Way to Inclusion (October 2022, Craiova, Romania):
Objectives included raising awareness of one's culture, preventing school dropout through creativity, promoting and consolidating cultural parameters, and fostering active citizenship and intercultural dialogue.
C2. Country Map Craft (November 2022, San Antonio de Benagéber, Spain):
Focused on increasing awareness of the environment, exploring natural landscapes, and utilising natural resources to create artworks. Because this partner could not host the groups when we intended to do this initially, due to other postponed projects in the pandemic, and the all the partners agreed, we switched these 2 mobilities: first the students and teachers went to Spain and only next year to Croatia. Despite all these changes, the achievement of the objectives was not prevented., thanks to the good communication and understanding among partners. We decided everything during the TPM.
C3. Let’s make History come alive (March 2023, Città di Castello, Italy):
Aims were to raise awareness of historical backgrounds, understand the past as a means to comprehend the present and future, and use historical names for self-discovery.
C4. Let's becreative! (May 2023, Dugo Selo, Croatia):
Objectives included recognizing creative potential, enhancing social skills like cooperation and communication, developing teamwork, and improving education through creativity.
C5. Let’s bring literature to life (September 2023, Paredes, Portugal):
Aimed to explore national literature for self-discovery, encourage communication and cooperation, build team spirit, and promote independence and self-awareness.
Other activities that we considered very important for our project:
- Dissemination results activities and Follow-up: This involved sharing the outcomes of the project and subsequent actions taken. We were all involved in our own organisation and we did materials together during the LTTAs.
- Management Activities: Included monitoring and evaluation activities to ensure the progress of the project. The methodology employed encouraged students to create authentic materials in a playful and secure environment, combining face-to-face and online interactions. Multicultural teamwork and peer learning were emphasized, enabling students to achieve a profound self-discovery of their identities and engage in activities promoting social inclusion.

<< Results >>

Our students, before the Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities (LTTAs), created five TikToks per country, according to the theme of each LTTA, by a scenario created exclusively by the students, their voices, their acting... These videos served as a dynamic medium for sharing their cultural insights, history, literature, and more, while also facilitating mutual learning. 
Throughout the LTTAs, students were organized into multicultural teams, with each team producing a daily video to exchange their newfound knowledge and experiences. These videos are like a dynamic report of each day in many versions, according to each group experience.
Additionally, a noticeable outcome of the project is the creation of a dedicated project website - created by the Spanish partner, ant this website is promoted on all the partners' websites.

2021-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000029897.title: Let It Grow!
2021-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000029897.summary:
<< Background >>

To achieve sustainable development and greener societies all partner schools understood that sustainability was not an endeavor for one country alone. Each and every one of our schools is near protected natural areas making us more aware of how species interact within their ecosystems and how they are affected by human influences. We truly believed in the need to conserve wildlife, to incorporate more eco-friendly habits in our life. Through common practices we wanted to “grow” a sincere urge to live sustainably. Our project identified the following problems: 1. Teachers were not trained and lacked models of activities on sustainability so it was not a common practice to teach sustainability. 2. Learners lacked knowledge on the process and effects of pollution so they weren’t actively involved in finding solutions to real problems. 3. There was a lack of environmental sustainability (ES) culture in our communities that resulted in harmful behaviors to nature. These became directions for our project since we needed to develop coherent programs to integrate curriculum with ES. Also, we lacked experience in organizing large scale events and campaigns. The project offered plenty of opportunities to exercise this. 

<< Objectives >>

As a result of the above mentioned needs, THE AIM of LET IT GROW! project was: training teachers to integrate environmental sustainability learning activities throughout the curriculum in order to raise awareness from an early age and to engage citizens to be active change-makers. We achieved these, through 3 objectives each targeted mainly towards: teachers, learners and community: 
1. Concerning teachers, we wanted to achieve the following: 
- Grow the number of trained teachers in environmental sustainability to at least 30% of the total number of teachers from partner schools by the end of the project. 
- Give opportunities to participating teachers to naturally include environmental sustainability activities in the regular flow of curricular lessons. 
2. Concerning learners, through the project we wanted to: 
- Grow the number of actively involved learners in implementing environmental sustainability actions to at least 75% of learners from all partner schools by the end of the project. 
3. Concerning the community, the project objective was to: 
- Raise awareness of environmental sustainability in the community through 14 campaigns (reforestation and clean-up) and 14 workshops by the end of the project.


<< Implementation >>

The implementation of the project involved the following types of activities: 
1. activities to produce results which were: 
1.a. project activities at the level of each partner organization: 
-training activities for participating teachers 
-the Awareness Campaign (1st year) during which the learners found out through experiential, hands-on activities about the process and effects of pollution. The best 140 activities from all partners were included in the outcome The Digital Guide of Environment Sustainability Activities, written in English and native languages. One special activity included here was the Young Photographers for the Environment photo exhibition which helped raise awareness in the community about local pollution. 
-the RRR campaign (throughout the project and after) which developed habits of reducing waste, recycling and reusing in each partner school 
-ACT NOW! Campaign (2nd year) where children used what they learnt during the Awareness campaign and acted by finding sustainable solutions to apply at school, at home and in the community. Their ideas were presented in a digital format, uploaded on a common project website and there they were rated by viewers from all partner countries. A system of awards certified the success of their ideas. Preschoolers worked along with parents, other students worked independently. The project website is called LET IT GROW! and it was the 2nd outcome of the project. It was a portal for the ACT NOW! campaign and it is a place to get informed about sustainability and share best practices of teachers, learners and community. 
-Reforestation Campaign was a common effort of school and community to undo the effects of deforestation and grow new forests 
-Clean-Up Campaign raised awareness at the level of the community on local pollution 
-2 workshops with parents and community laid the basis for a more Eco-friendly living and further developing of green skills 
-the partnership with local authorities or NGOs helped establish the school as a hub in networking for sustainability. 
1.b. project activities at the level of the partnership: teacher training activities during the LTTAs 
2. activities to monitor and analyze progress (through 7 plans and a Master Tracker) 
3. activities of evaluation and re-planning (at the level of each Project Management Team and based on the plans and tracker) 
4. progress reporting activities by collecting data from all LTTAs and TPMs and monitoring the updating with all relevant information of the Master Tracker for each partner school.


<< Results >>

The project outcomes are: 
For objective 1: 
-at least 30% of the teachers from all partner schools trained in environmental sustainability through professional development events (courses, webinars, conferences, workshops) by the end of the project. This target was met by all partners and the list of the courses that were attended is available on the project website at  https://sites.google.com/view/let-it-grow-erasmus/reasources/courses 
-at least 2 lessons on environmental sustainability per class per month throughout the project. At the level of the project there were more than 1134 lessons developed by all partners.
-the planning, developing and assessing the activities for the ″Digital Guide of Environmental Sustainability Activities″, resulted in better trained teachers to implement environmental sustainability activities throughout the curriculum. 
-A ″Digital Guide of Environmental Sustainability Activities″ to provide teachers with a resource to help introduce environmental sustainability. The guide contains a call for supporting sustainability through education, the best 140 activities for preschool, primary and secondary levels from all partners and conclusions/impressions of participating teachers and learners. The guide was written in English and native languages. All activities were tested and approved by teachers and children. 
-″Let It Grow″ project website with summary of the project, learners’ ideas on sustainable solutions, presentations of campaign activity, useful links, books and online references, relevant photo and video gallery and other resources. The site is a public open resource. 
For objective 2 
-min 75% of learners from all partner schools who are more aware of environmental sustainability through the Awareness Campaign that took place during the 1st year of the project. 
-min 75% of learners from all partner schools who developed the habit of daily reusing, reducing and recycling in their schools through the RRR Campaign. The campaign lasted all throughout the project and will continue after.

2021-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000032488.title: BEFORE IT IS TOO LATE
2021-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000032488.summary:
<< Background >>

The needs of schools and NGO were identified through a SWOT analysis, analysis of reports, and council meetings. The identified needs include: 
1.	Understanding the causes of climate change and its likely impacts on nature and humans, along with precautionary measures to mitigate climate change
2.	Raising awareness of climate change, reflected in the interest of students and teachers to engage in promoting awareness and addressing it at the national level
3.	Recognizing similar social contexts in each partner region, encompassing students from diverse cultures, ethnicities, backgrounds, education levels, as well as those with disabilities or learning difficulties
4.	Acknowledging the inevitable consequences of climate change without necessary precautions
5.	Informing and raising awareness about climate change to as many people as possible (students, teachers, communty members)

<< Objectives >>

BITL is a project with the following aims:
•	Enable participants and stakeholders to comprehend the severity of climate change;
•	Raise awareness about the dangers of climate change and its potential consequences for future generations;
•	Address environmental issues such as global warming and energy shortages, recognizing them as potential threats to the world if no precautions are taken;
•	Strengthen intercultural dialogue; 
•	Provide opportunities to encounter and learn about new teaching methods and learning approaches, integrating them into the standard school curriculum;
•	Encourage participants to take action on social issues and become active citizens; 
•	Offer the acquisition of innovative and motivating strategies for the social inclusion of students, utilizing national and EU cultural elements as support.
The project aims to decrease the percentage of those who
•	say 'I don't know what causes climate change' from 68% to 42%;
•	say 'I don't know what precautions are taken nationally and internationally to curb climate change' from 72% to 51%; 
•	and increase the percentage of those who say 'I know what precautions may be taken individually to fight climate change' from 23% to 56% within three years

A2. Dissemination

2021-1-RS01-KA220-SCH-000034462.title: Dobre aplikacije za obrazovanje
2021-1-RS01-KA220-SCH-000034462.summary:
<< Background >>

Knowing the way of learning and the specifics of children with different developmental disabilities obliges teachers to adequately choose approaches, methods and tools in their work. In the countries of the region, there are no adapted teaching materials that would bring students closer to the contents of the national curriculum. Teachers, educators, parents as well as all other participants in the educational process rely on their own resources to find adequate methods and means of work. The development of modern technology and digitization of teaching have created favorable conditions for various tools that enable easier learning and functioning of children with disabilities, but not a single available learning application was based on the national curriculum. The challenge was also insufficient competence and training of teachers to independently create learning materials, which caused teachers to spend a lot of time in searching different platforms of suitable materials. All this led us to the idea of creating a database of adapted teaching materials and an application based on the curriculum in 3 subjects of the 1st cycle of education (mother tongue, mathematics,sience) created in Serbian, Croatian and Slovenian.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we wanted to achieve a wide application of adapted teaching material and applications in teaching children with autism spectrum (referred to as ASD) and other forms of intellectual disabilities (referred to as ID).Also, we wanted to create a unique base of materials available to everyone and at any time, which would greatly facilitate the work of teachers in regular schools and special education teachers. We would train teachers for independent materials production, which would constantly increase the database. The existence of such a database can be an idea and a guideline for the teaching for many teachers in regular schools. Based on the material, there is a learning application that monitors all areas and is additionally adapted to the specifics of children, enabling them to develop independence and facilitating the entire learning process.In general, the main goals for the implementation of this project were: improvement of the quality of educational work with children with ID and ASD, support for inclusive practice, free access to the material base and application, teacher training for independent preparation and application of materials in order to improve personal and professional competencies

<< Implementation >>

At the beginning, the project teams analyzed the national curriculum of the subjects they were responsible for developing in order to harmonize the adapted teaching material with the plan and program for students of younger school age (7-12 years). In cooperation with associated partners from the Institute for Quality of Education and Training Evaluation in Serbia (referred as ZVKOV), an analysis of the test results was carried out within all partner countries. The goal of the survey was to collect data related to key topics and areas in which teachers have the greatest need for support for creating learning materials. Also, in the initial phase, Elementary School "Anton Skala" hired an IT specialist who created the project website as a tool where all PDF materials will be stored and which will be used for promotional purposes and the sharing of all news related to project activities. After the analysis of the national curriculum of all three countries, at the first transnational meeting held in Belgrade, an activity plan with deadlines for implementation was defined. During the preparation of the materials, team members continuously communicated and exchanged materials, which were translated into the partners languages. The materials were posted on the project website ahead of the second transnational meeting that was held in Radovljica in August 2022. At the meeting, an analysis of the materials and previous activities was carried out, and certain changes and corrections to both the materials and the appearance of the site were agreed. The materials were promoted at scientific and professional conferences along with announcements of upcoming trainings for teachers as well as the announcement of the creation of a learning application. Along with the creation of the materials, the project coordinator hired a software company that is in charge of creating the application. Meetings were organized with the developers in order to give them the idea of the appearance and possibilities of the application as much as possible. The analysis of the application Beta version was carried out at the 3rd transnational meeting held in May 2023 in Zagreb. Members of the project teams, in cooperation with the developers of the Projectland development company, agreed on certain changes within the application so that it would be maximally adapted to learning specifics of students with ID and ASD. Elementary school "Anton Skala" organized a multiplayer event in Belgrade at the end of May. The event was attended live and online via the Zoom platform by members of associations and organizations of neighboring countries. In this way, the materials and application were presented on a concrete example through video material recorded by the teachers during their use in working with their students, and trainings that will be implemented by partner organizations, each in accordance with the capabilities and needs of professional staff in their countries. The trainings were implemented in different ways, through online platforms, which made it possible to expand the results of the project and improve the competence level of professional staff who deal with the educational work of students with developmental disabilities. During the project, partner organizations were active participants in professional-scientific conferences and gatherings, which enabled the dissemination of project results and the announcement of upcoming activities. In addition to the official website of the project, the results were also shared on the partner’s websites, social networks (Facebook and Instagram), Twinspace and the EU project result platform. Along with all the activities, we prepared and realized the evaluation of both the event and the results of the project. The evaluations results were collected and presented at TM meetings, which served as guidelines for our further work.

<< Results >>

Due to the insufficient supply of adapted teaching materials that would be adequate for the learning of children with ID and ASD,it was the basis for planning project activities and results.Based on research conducted among professionals in all three partner countries,we selected the areas and topics for which we created the primary results of the project–adapted teaching materials in PDF format that are aligned with the learning objectives of the participating countries national curriculum.Other results of the project are: 
-website with available customized materials with tutorial,logo application with material base and tutorial,teacher training,promotional material(posters,flyer,Newslatter).The logo’s final look was based on the partners mutual agreement.Within the field are three hands with a mobile phone between them.The hands symbolize the activity,work,support,cooperation and solidarity. The application logo consists four puzzles of different colors,which contains one letter of the project's acronym.A heart made of four parts of different colors is drawn on the phone screen, which also symbolizes noble feelings and intentions towards the students for whom the application is intended.In the lower left corner is the mark GA-TE,which is the acronym of the project name in English.The logotype represents the idea of  help,engagement and modernization,new methodology.The project coordinator was in charge of creating the website.An IT specialist hired outside the consortium,was given common ideas and ideas about visual details and organization of the site in order to represent the flow of the project to make it easier for visitors to find their way around when searching and downloading materials.The site contains general information about the project,the project consortium,goals and expected results, news about the progress of the project,information about the dissemination of project results.The site contributes to the image and reputation of the project by making it visible and recognizable. Members of the project team from Zagreb created pages on social networks Facebook, Instagram, designed the look of flyers and Newslatter, and the project team from Slovenia edited the look of Twinspace. These platforms and promotional material served to spread the results and activities during the project. The analysis of national curricula of teaching subjects (mother tongue, mathematics,sience) from all three countries preceded the creation of PDF teaching materials. The analysis was carried out by collecting data and questioning teachers who work with students with developmental disabilities, and it contained key areas within the mentioned subjects for which they believe they need the most support in creating learning content. The customized learning material in PDF format was published on the project site before TM2. The PDF materials have been translated into 3 languages of partner organizations and are free to download. Within all 3 subjects, 10 topics with sub-topics were selected, which resulted in the creation of 152 teaching units. After the creation of the material, the creation of the application was started. The learning application is a digital form of PDF material and contains identical areas and teaching units systematically arranged and adapted to the specifics of students (highlighted important details, simplified display, moderate colors, systematized display - from simple to complex, from known to unknown). With the help of the application, students acquire knowledge in an interesting, adapted and innovative way, while developing learning skills and independence in work. The application has the same content as the PDF material. Its advantage is a motivational role in the learning process because it is used on digital devices. Students using the application to develop a wide range of skills, which the most important is independence. The lessons are enriched with audio, which represents an additional level of adaptability for those students who have not yet developed the skill of reading. Feedback on the accuracy of the completed task as well as the possibility of error reduces the feeling of frustration and makes the learning process fun and interesting. Pictograms from the Spanish website ARASSAC were used for the purposes of creating the material, for which we received written consent. The application itself is free to download and is available on two platforms, Google Play and the App Store. Training was also organized for teachers in all three countries for the use and independent production of materials, which caused great interest.The teachers experienced the process of creating the materials themselves and their application. In this way, they greatly improved teaching and learning competencies, as well as digital competencies.The created promotional material was used for the purpose of disseminating the results of the project.All project results are posted on the Project results platform.

2021-1-SE01-KA220-SCH-000024419.title: Sign language for beginners in Europe - Spread the sign
2021-1-SE01-KA220-SCH-000024419.summary:
<< Background >>

The desire to continue a long-time project – Spreadthesign – and the drive to provide a more innovative approach to make sign language (SL) content
available and accessible in different European countries, was what led us to the idea for this project. On one hand, we aimed to keep addressing the
target group needs – deaf pupils, their teachers, and families – namely through the production of new content in SL for beginners, which was an area to
be explored since many of those teachers and families were hearing and lacked knowledge and vocabulary in SL. That way, through the products we
produced, we intended to contribute to expanding their skills and competencies in SL and, therefore, to establish better communication processes with
their deaf pupils and children. This was an undeniable right of the deaf, to have access to education, culture, information, and other aspects of social life,
in their own language, the sign language. In this way, a new sign language – Serbian SL – was also added to the Spreadthesign dictionary, increasing the
number of partners and sign languages represented, and also providing more opportunities for the Serbian deaf and hearing to develop their SL skills and
promote accessibility.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of implementing the project was to develop content and materials in the sign languages of 16 partner countries, making them accessible to deaf
pupils and other beginners through a mobile app and a website. The project aimed to promote literacy for the deaf, enhance communication between the
hearing and the deaf, foster inclusivity, and provide an educational platform where deaf pupils can learn about different national traditions, geography, and
culture in their own national sign language. Additionally, the project seeked to expand vocabulary through an e-learning quiz, aiding cognitive
development and academic success. A key milestone was incorporating Serbian Sign Language, with 10,168 words/signs, making it accessible online for
the first time. The partnership of 16 organizations aimed to make sign language knowledge more widespread while promoting digital education and
awareness of the European context.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented several activities, including:
Development of a sign language learning tool – A resource for beginners containing everyday vocabulary, sentences, expressions, dialogues and short
texts.
Creation of video content in sign language – Each partner country contributed by producing videos presenting their respective sign languages.
Designing an educational quiz – A game-like quiz was developed to help deaf pupils learn the content in an engaging way.
Incorporation of Serbian Sign Language – A new partner (Serbia) was added to expand the Spreadthesign dictionary, increasing the available content for
European deaf individuals.
Project meetings – Both physical and virtual meetings were conducted, including sign language interpreters, to develop pedagogical scripts and
educational materials.
Hybrid meeting implementation – If necessary due to the Covid-19 pandemic, hybrid meetings were held to ensure flexibility in achieving project goals.
Testing and proofreading – The translations, videos, quiz, and mobile app were tested with teachers and deaf pupils from each country to refine the final
product based on user feedback.
Dissemination of results – Each partner shared the final products within their networks.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results of the project include:
Development of a mobile app for sign language learning
A new innovative feature that allows beginners to learn sign language (SL) through an intuitive and attractive interface.
Expansion of the Spreadthesign dictionary
The project builds upon the existing sign language dictionary (www.spreadthesign.com), making it more accessible and comprehensive with additional
sign language content.
Creation of new SL content
Country presentations in sign video format and an educational quiz were developed to enhance learning.
Increased awareness and accessibility – By using digital platforms (website and mobile app), more people can learn and access SL anytime and
anywhere.
Enhanced pedagogical and learning tools
The new materials support teachers of the deaf in their educational efforts.
Greater impact in deaf schools across Europe
Due to the existing widespread use of the Spreadthesign dictionary, the newly developed app and features will immediately benefit many deaf schools.
Promotion of social inclusion
The project contributes to increased literacy, social participation, and awareness about deaf communities in various countries.
Long-term educational and cultural impact

2021-1-SE01-KA220-SCH-000031523.title: Green Teachers for Green Kids
2021-1-SE01-KA220-SCH-000031523.summary:
<< Background >>

We focused on some facts:All the countries are discussing the issues of environmental pollution/climate change today.Most of them try to find some solutions to overcome this global problem.
There is a need to take global action to struggle with the problem.Education at an early age is important to solve sustainable solution.The three inevitable elements of education are teachers,students and parents.Environment is on the top of it and it is polluted considerably.We feel the need to raise environmental awareness to break the top chain link.The issue is too global to be addressed only in our own countries and requires cooperation.The fact that it is one of the top issues among European priorities has become a source of finance for institutions like us that have taken responsibility for environmental issues and brought us together for a transnational cooperation.It is of great importance to raise individuals who save the environment consciously,prevent environmental pollution,realize how serious the problem is. The way to make this possible is to raise/educate individuals/teachers and get the support of the parents.Thanks to our project, individuals with these skills were the outputs of our project.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to achieve many objectives,considering the main objective of our project to have a sustainable environment.The main issues were to find solutions/raise awareness for environmental pollution to a dangerous level,climate change,global warming and drought,unconscious use of raw materials and the importance of recycling. Our project ensured teachers/students/parents understand the importance of environmental pollution to a dangerous level,climate change,global warming/drought,unconscious use of raw materials,the importance of recycling,and maintain the idea of taking care of natural resources,get acquainted teachers/students with recycling technologies,establish environmental awareness.
Searching for solutions to problems together paved the way for people from different cultures to coalesce/become citizens of the world.Teachers' ability to experience transnational educational activities enabled them to develop new pedagogical methods/increase their motivation in this regard.The project contributed to the experience/reinforce future developments related to environmental education/creativity.It developed an understanding of different approaches.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented various activities during and after the project’s completion in addition to the LTT activities in the mobilities and to the support of the transnational project meetings for a successful project implementation.The budget was also crucial to achieve our project’s success.Therefore we can summarized that the project activities that will lead to the achievement of the project objectives/delivery of the planned activities/results are basically the Project management,properly-distributed tasks and responsibilities among partners,appropriate budget management,transnational collaboration/meetings, LTTs,skill-gaining,supporting teachers/family participation/contribution/support, and some other activities some of which are to create an Erasmus corner at school/institution,informe our community by organizing displays,meetings,competitions,Clean Environment Dictionary,write a journal with impressions about mobilities,environmental education for families,recycling:competitions and prepare ed products,celebration:International Day of Recycling,a trip to the recycling facility/center with students and
parents,competition for making costumes from waste materials,Erasmus Day,a fashion show,e magazine,World Wetlands Day celebrations,the practice/hobby gardens,World Water Day celebrations,planting activities,World Environment Day celebrations,beach/riverside/lakeside cleaning activity,a calendar on "For a more livable environment",kite festival and clean air and clean water activities etc.We held 3 transnational project meetings and 5 LTTs. The role of the NGO partner was important in the project.They provided specialized education/workshops/support to the school partners.The schools cooperated with each other and the NGO. We created project teams with well-defined roles.We established dissemination platforms.We gave importance to the evaluation/monitoring the project. We established a partnership with the organizations with the same issues/institutional needs,and with the awareness that the solution requires a transnational cooperation.We planned together what we could do to solve the problem thanks to this project.The transnational meetings/online meetings,the LTTs gave us the skills to show how to work more effectively/overcome the problems in cooperation. Brainstorming,discussions,respect to ideas,making common decisions,empathy/being understanding will be our key elements.We set standards/support a common culture/cooperation.We’ll share common experiences.We’ll carry what we experienced to our country.
Regarding the activities,we planned a content that raised awareness/sensitivity by developing correct attitudes/behavior,ICT/foreign language skills,green skills,transversal/basic skills of the participants/target group in a way that consider the sensitivity to the environment in accordance with the soul of our project. We ensured how to protect/not to pollute environment through practical activities,games,outdoor activities,trips,art,important national day/week celebrations,competitions,visuals,technology and fun. We created videos,corners,posters,logos,short movies,pictures,e-magazines,calendar etc. also using web 2 tools in school and LTTs,and use them ourselves.In this way,ICT skills of participants improved remarkably. In addition,the project activities supported the development of better school leadership/innovative teaching/assessment methods.We used innovative learning approaches,develop
creativity,support teachers in delivering competence-based teaching and develop assessment/validation of key competences. We attach great importance to and also focus on family participation/support to students.One of the biggest strength in the project was to benefit from the help/support of parents.Family support/participation was an effective force in gaining the desired behavior/skills.

<< Results >>

Considering all the activities, results and other outcomes of our project that we had during and the completion of it,we took actions and offer some tangible solutions/raise awareness for environmental pollution,climate change,global warming and drought, unconscious use of raw materials and the importance of recycling.For this purpose, we developed training materials by using web 2 tools. We used e-Twinning, social media, YouTube and create videos, bulletin boards, posters, logos, pictures and books to teach and learn about the environment etc. We created our own products of activities such as educational materials related to environment, trips, designing logos, competitions, a calendar, e-magazines, recorded videos, short movie, diaries, celebrations of important days and weeks in partner countries, the results of the questionnaires and creative products etc. The activities involved real life tasks. The results were viewed by colleagues from partner schools/organizations and wider community. The staff/teachers had greater understanding and responsiveness to social/linguistic/cultural diversity. They practiced foreign languages in real context. Their ICT competences are developed. Teachers knew different educational systems, compared them to their own. New experiences were incorporated in school/organization curriculum. This increased their motivation for professional development. They developed/reinforced their networks of partners, supported the development, transfered and implementation of innovative practices as well as the implementation of joint initiatives promoting cooperation and exchanges of experience at European level. Teachers/students had more positive attitude towards the European projects/EU values. They had a chance to work in a transnational project/developed their cooperation skills, got more aware of the importance of the environment at international level, contributed to the protection of environment thanks to this green project-an environmental project most of the products of which are digital. Our project produced outputs innovative for schools/organisations. It produced new learning opportunities/teaching materials to develop basic skills. Students learned by doing/developed the right attitude/skills towards environmental issues, improved learning skills, life skills, multiple intelligences, sense of initiative and entrepreneurship, environmental awareness, learned group-work and participate in learning process actively. Our project offers a method that our stakeholders can use as well.
