2021-1-SE01-KA220-SCH-000032448.title: Creating an ECO online Natural Fit Virtual Programs to Prepare Students for boostIng 21st century Skills 4 the Future (UNITY)
2021-1-SE01-KA220-SCH-000032448.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to the UNITY project after all partners had identified significant needs in education systems in particular in our own countries but in general also in other countries across Europe. Many schools lacked the tools, training, and resources to prepare students for the demands of a rapidly changing, digitalized world. Teachers often struggled to integrate STEAM education into their classrooms, leaving students unprepared for interdisciplinary challenges like climate change. Further, limited funding and support for primary-level STEAM education hindered the development of critical competencies. By joining this project the partners wanted to combine these different pillars in education, aimed to address these identified gaps, empower teachers with innovative methods, and equip students with future-ready skills through inclusive and sustainable approaches by creating a platform for everyone to use and to find all the material needed for the teacher. 

<< Objectives >>

The UNITY project, aimed to address pressing educational needs and achieve meaningful, long-term impacts for both students and teachers in both our countries and across Europe. For students, the project wanted to develop future-ready skills and mindsets essential for navigating a rapidly digitalizing world. Through project-based learning in STEAM, students would learn the importance of online collaboration, communication, and teamwork, gain diverse perspectives, fostering an understanding of smart and sustainable growth and lifelong learning. The project also aimed to enhance their career prospects by cultivating interest in science-based "smart jobs".For teachers, the project aimed to provide opportunities for professional development through innovative teaching methods and tools. How to adopt and blend digital tools with project-based approaches, equipping them to teach critical thinking, creativity, problem-solving, and cooperative skills.It also aimed to support teachers in engaging students in diverse learning styles and in incorporating real-life challenges into their curriculum. The project also wanted to achieve and enrich the understanding of EU values, practices, and policies, while strengthen the ability to network.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented a range of structured activities to ensure effective collaboration, dissemination, and the achievement of its goals. These activities has been the following as also described in the application:  

Transnational Project Meetings (TPMs):
Three in-person meetings held over the 36-month project duration, including a Kick-off meeting, a Mid-Evaluation meeting, and a Final Evaluation meeting. These meetings focused on managing the project’s budget, timeline, partner roles, task allocations, risk management as well as planning the important PR4 in particular, plan our ME:s and also evaluate the project and planning forward. The partners met in Malmö, Bursa and Glina for these three meetings and these meetings fulfilled their purposes well. A descision was made to exchange the meeting in UK for the meeting in Bursa since UK was withdrawn from the project. In the application it was stated that the second meeting was going to be in UK. 

Bi-Monthly Virtual Meetings:
A total of more than 30 virtual meetings were conducted to maintain regular communication, address emerging issues, and support ongoing collaboration among partners. These meetings have had high priority with all partners and has been the core of the project. The meetings have been held every third week in Wednesday afternoon apart from during the summer and winter holidays. Apart from these meetings we have held other more specified meetings in between these meetings. These extra meetings have sometimes been with all partners and sometimes with just some partners but this is accordingly to what the extra meetings have been about. A number of extra meetings have been held regarding the website in order to try to visualise as much of what the partners are all thinking and what is actually possible to do within the website tool. Other meetings have been specifically about some of the project results, working meetings where we have worked together on some tasks and about extra activities we were planning. These meetings are continuing every third week during the spring as well in order to plan both shared diseemination activities, workshops and the Award Framework we are going to work with during most of 2025 and this takes a lot of planning to conduct. Here eTwinning will play a big part, more of that below. 

Learning, Teaching, and Training (LTT) Activities:
Two LTT activities were carried out:
Important to note is that we really early on in the project decided to change from having the first LTTA in Sweden and the second in Italy to instead conduct them the other way around. This is because at the first meeting held in Malmö the coordinator told the partners that in May 2024 a very special event was going to be held. THis event occur every second year and is called InnoCarnival and it adresses the exact same challenges as UNITY and the project partners decided to start a collaboration with the organisors of InnoCarnival to enhance the project and the students participating. This turned out to be a successful change to make and has strenghtened the collaboration with InnoCarnival project leaders and also stakeholders through them. It also fit well into PR4 and made this project result successful. 

The first LTTA focused on training project staff to enhance teaching methodologies, digital skills, and the ability to integrate STEAM and project-based learning.
The second LTTA involved student participants, providing them with hands-on experience in applying STEAM principles to address real-world challenges like climate change. 

Multiplier Events:
Six national multiplier events and one international event were organized to disseminate project results and insights.

eTwinning Project:
In our application we were planning to organise for an international eTwinning initiative titled “UNITY” and even though we did get this started when we would have liked to due to all the problems that ESEP were facing which made motivating the teachers to join very hard we have also proven that hard work do give results because inspired from all the activities in PR4 both partners and teachers are really motivated to keep on working together towards our next Award Framework that will take place in the autumn of 2025 and for this purpose the eTwinning Twinspace will be the platform for communication and preparation not to mention sharing. We are now harvesting all the work from the project and have found a way of letting the project continue to thrive even though the project has officially ended.
These activities not only facilitated the project’s smooth management but also ensured collaborative dissemination, active participation, and impactful learning experiences for both teachers and students.

Additionally, the project produced tangible outcomes, including the PR1,PR 2, PR3 , PR4 and PR5.

<< Results >>

 The UNITY project delivered significant outputs and impactful results.A Curriculum on Skills Development using Project-Based Learning (PBL) and STEAM methodologies equipped students with future-focused competencies. A Web Platform and eLearning Modules included interactive chapters, video simulations, and a “projector” tool showcasing climate-related projects across schools, fostering collaboration.Ten Virtual Webinars and Seminars, including an EU-level session, provided teachers with tools to engage students and prepare them for global challenges. An Award Framework recognized outstanding climate change projects, culminating in an international ceremony and a revised methodology for future use.The “Save the World with Your Dreams” campaign inspires communities to act against climate change, extending the project's reach and lasting impact far beyond the end of the project. Here are an expanded list of concrete outputs and achieved impactful results: 

Curriculum on skills development (Result I):
Developed a curriculum focused on using Project-Based Learning (PBL) and STEAM to foster skills development among students. In this part the first thing created was an extensive report in what PBL is and how to use this method. Connected to this report 60 detailed lesson plans was created and they were all based on PBL, aimed towards sustainability and climate change in particular but also introduced and suggested a variety of digital tools to implement and work with the lesson plan in order to enhance the learning of the students but also to develop their language skills by giving them different ways of expressing themselves. 

Web platform and eLearning modules (Result II):
A comprehensive platform and eLearning modules were created, including chapters tailored for EU students and teachers.
10 video simulations/instructions were produced to enhance understanding.
The platform features a “projector” tool with a digital map, showcasing climate-related projects by students across schools and countries. This allows schools, students, and teachers to connect and collaborate.
Link to project platform: https://unity4future.eu/project-results/
 
Virtual webinars and seminars (Result III):
- Ten virtual training sessions were conducted altogether, with one additional session at the EU level, focusing on equipping teachers with skills to engage students and prepare them for a rapidly changing world. These also serves as online live LTTAs (Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities).
- Podcasts were also created adressing the urgent matters of sustainability and climat change and voices many students from different countries sharing their thoughts and ideas.

Award framework (Result IV):
- A methodological guideline was developed to award outstanding student and teacher projects on climate change, recognizing excellence and innovation.
- This guideline was used to conduct a pilot award work including first work on a national level with schools being encouraged to work with projects aligned with the project objectives and then compete on first national level. Each winner from each category being performed in the different countries then qualified to compete in an international award ceremony.
- An international award ceremony was performed with teams from all the countries and with judges from all countries as well.
- From the pilot the guideline has been updated according to feedback from partners, teachers and judges in order to make it easier to use and easier to implement. This new framework will be used in 2025 when the next award ceremony will take place.

Outreach campaign (Result V):
- The “Save the World with Your Dreams” campaign encourages students, parents, teachers, and schools to take meaningful action on climate change, significantly expanding the project's reach and impact.
- This result is mainly a forward going result where several plans has been formed by the coordinating partner with respectful help from all partners in both giving feedback, testing, disseminating and working to put it in a context.

2021-1-SE01-KA220-SCH-000032643.title: Sustainability from the Start: An Online ESD Curriculum for Early Childhood Education
2021-1-SE01-KA220-SCH-000032643.summary:
<< Background >>

The development and learning of values, attitudes and behaviour starts from birth, which makes early childhood education and care (ECEC) very
important. However, this is not always informing policy and decision makers. The partners in this project, Sustainability from the Start: An On-line ESD
Curriculum for Early Childhood Education, have for many years been actively involved in Education for sustainable development (ESD), with a childoriented
perspective. However, the results show that the success or failure with the projects depends on the ECEC educators, and especially on the ECE
teachers.The same conclusion is drawn by UNESCO in the 2020 ESD Roadmap. Since the Covid pandemic, professional communication and learning were often
moved to digital media, and e-learning grew as a field. However, for young children, the most important group to have ICT competencies are the ECE
teachers who then may plan, implement and monitor what ESD actions are suitable and relevant in the early years. This project integrates digital learning,
ESD and ECEC, focusing teachers and young children. We aim at a reorientation of all education towards sustainable development.

<< Objectives >>

The overarching aim is to produce a course in an App that promotes the awareness of ECE educators about sustainability related issues, such as climate
change, global warming and the importance of taking actions for transformative change towards a sustainable lifestyle. The early childhood years (birth –
8), represent an unequalled, but poorly tapped, window of opportunity to instil long-lasting sustainability-related skills, attitudes, and habits. All of the UN
Sustainable Development Goals impact young children. Through this project, children, their families, in-service and pre-service early childhood
practitioners, and teacher educators will contribute directly to the implementation of SDG 4.2, which recognizes the importance of pre-primary education,
and 4.7 about Sustainable development and global citizenship. The on-line curriculum includes activities relating to many or all of the UN SDGs, thereby
increasing knowledge about the goals and providing direct experience contributing to their achievement. In the longer perspective, we want to Increase
the number of participating preschools and universities to more countries in Europe and beyond.

<< Implementation >>

The project was carried out through a collaborative approach and shared responsibilities. We used 4 TPMs, additional 7 digital Project Board Meetings, 2
TLLs and 3 MEs. The teachers recruited for LTTs and workgroups have actively tried out the educational activities in the course and report enthusiasm
from the involved children. The course is already translated to 6 languages, three more than was mentioned in the application. Dissemination has been
prioritised the whole time and successively collected in a shared Dissemination file (on Teams) which ensures details and statistics of events, locations,
and participants. Reaching out to 13 394 teachers, researchers, and university students and 36 034 general public are amazing numbers.
The PMB-members have been active in reaching out to European networks (748) and NGOs (25), as well as 1285 communications with principals and
decision makers have been carried out during the project, which explains the readiness to download the App. The course is well received at international
Top Summits, like COP 28 in Dubai and ESD-NET/UNESCO in Tokyo, as well as at OMEP Regional and World Conferences beyond Europe, in Australia,
Canada, Japan, Thailand and the USA.
More than 3 200 downloads in 54 c

<< Results >>

The Project Management Board (PMB) has successfully met and surpassed the project goals set out in this application. The main results are the free
online course ‘Sustainability from the Start’ and ‘the ECE Academy App’ (AppStore / Google Play). The course integrates a variety of sustainability
concepts into teaching and daily life of young children. The course is offered in six languages, serving a diverse global audience. At the end of the project,
an exceptional interest has resulted in the course being downloaded in 54 countries, by 3 300 paprticipants. The App ECE Academy functions well with
few emailed questions from participants. The course is also implemented at nine universities in the five partner countries, Already, the exceptional interest
has resulted in the course being downloaded in 54 countries. Furthermore, the course was presented as an example of best practice at COP 28 in Dubai
and the UNESCO ESD-NET 2030 in Tokyo. Additionally, the Swedish National Agency for Education has included the course in their regular continuous
professional development programme.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000024278.title: Principles of quality education for teachers
2021-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000024278.summary:
<< Background >>

Nowadays, more and more children and students from diverse backgrounds with different needs are enrolling in kindergartens and schools. Educators and teachers are among the first to meet and work with them, which is why continuous professional development (CPD) is essential. However, it is equally important that the professional development activities they attend are of high quality. Research shows that the higher the quality of these activities, the better the process quality in classrooms. Therefore, we need well-trained and professionally supported CPD educators, as well as clear definitions of quality standards for implementation of CPD events.

With this project, we addressed a gap in this area, as there are no comprehensive documents in the broader European context that define these aspects, especially from the perspective of social justice, interculturalism, and human rights in education. We also tackled the need for professional support for CPD educators and raised awareness of the importance of using quality assurance tools in the selection, employment, and CPD of CPD educators.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project was to support the processes of selection, employment and continuous professional development (CPD) of CPD educators with high-quality tools and to enhance the quality of CPD activities for educators and teachers across the EU and beyond. The project aimed to do so in a way that promotes social justice, interculturalism, and human rights in education.

The specific objectives were to:
- Define a framework for high-quality continuous professional development (CPD) activities for educators and teachers, emphasizing social inclusion, interculturalism, and human rights in education;
- Strengthen the capacities of partner organizations and CPD educators to implement high-quality CPD activities that promote social justice, interculturalism, and human rights;
- Enhance the capacities of partner organizations to improve approaches to selecting, employing, training, and professionally supporting CPD educators.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, we analyzed existing employment and continuous professional development (CPD) practices for CPD educators and developed quality principles for their work. We designed a training program and created a handbook to support CPD educators in their professional growth.

Through the training, we supported CPD educators in strengthening their competencies for high-quality CPD delivery, reflection, self-assessment, planning their own professional development, self-care, and more. Partner organizations enhanced their knowledge and skills to support CPD educators in their professional growth (CPD) and in integrating topics such as social justice, interculturality, and human rights in education.

We also carried out dissemination activities to raise stakeholder awareness of the importance of high-quality CPD activities and the continuous professional development of CPD providers. PIQET tools enable long-term improvements in CPD practices across the EU and beyond.

<< Results >>

The key outputs of the PIQET project are:
PIQET Analysis: Existing Practices for the Recruitment and Professional Development of Continuous Professional Development Educators
PIQET Principles: Quality Principles for Continuous Professional Development Educators
PIQET Training Programme: Training Programme for Continuous Professional Development Educators
PIQET Handbook: Handbook for Continuous Professional Development Educators

Together, these outputs form the PIQET Toolkit, designed to ensure the quality of CPD and support CPD educators in their professional growth.

The project achieved a shared understanding of CPD quality among partners, improved CPD educators competencies for reflection, self-assessment, development planning, feedback delivery, and more; strengthened partner organizations’ capacity to support CPD providers, and reinforced the integration of social justice, interculturality, and human rights in education. Additionally, it increased stakeholder awareness of the importance of high-quality CPD and the need to reform policies on CPD educators selection, employment, and professional support.

2021-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000024430.title: Upgrading Global Education Across Subject Areas
2021-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000024430.summary:
<< Background >>

This project aimed to upgrade global education through the use of debate methodology, transdisciplinarity, and digital education. The results of this project provided teachers with the training, methodological framework, implementation toolkit, and digital tools necessary to carry out global education, thereby positively impacting students' lives. The proposed diverse partnership consisted of schools, universities, digital education specialists, global education experts, and debate-focused organisations. 

Teachers face increasingly difficult challenges in preparing students to become global and European citizens. They need support in the forms of methodologies and tools to help them navigate complex contemporary issues, such as climate change and the Covid-19 crisis, which involve multiple school subject areas and require interactive methods to engage students. European policymakers had, in principle, recognized global education as instrumental for instilling the importance of democratic values, justice, solidarity, and inclusion in young people. In recent years, young people have been advocating and protesting for a greener, sustainable future, women’s rights, and an end to discrimination, demonstrating that issues encompassed b

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of this project was to support effective education for contemporary problems based on four key elements:

1. Global education: This element emphasized global awareness, citizenship, responsibility, and green transformation. It encouraged students to consider multiple perspectives and the ethical implications of power and privilege, fostering responsible action.
   
2.Transdisciplinarity: This element focused on connecting learning across subjects and diverse perspectives. It aimed to prevent overspecialization, enabling students to tackle multifaceted problems and cultivate essential 21st-century intellectual skills.
   
3. Speech and Debate methodology: This interactive methodology combined independent research, teamwork, critical thinking, argument building, public speaking, and presentation skills. It engaged young people in political and contemporary issues, equipping them to develop viable policy solutions.
   
4. Digital education: Recognizing the importance of digital approaches, this element highlighted digital education as an asset. It emphasized its potential to overcome geographical and financial barriers, offering varied learning structures to accommodate different learning styles.

<< Implementation >>

The activities implemented under this project were aimed at producing high-quality results. The development of each result was overseen by a designated Result Manager. Result Managers worked with project staff and a group of 52 secondary-level teachers in different subject areas from Italy, Slovenia, The Netherlands, and the Czech Republic to:

- Develop project materials
- Implement those materials in 52 classrooms
- Provide and collect feedback on implementation
- Shape and adapt project results according to teacher and student needs

This process helped ensure the quality and applicability of project results in different local and national contexts, paving the way for better education outcomes and the use of project results across Europe. The two staff training events organised served the same purpose. In addition to training the participants to use the developed methodology, extensive feedback was collected to ensure the project’s results were responsive to the needs of their target group. The multiplier events in Italy, Slovenia, The Netherlands, and the Czech Republic served two purposes: introducing interested education professionals to project results and providing them with the opportunity to test and see them in action through sample classes.


<< Results >>

We have produced project results that are appealing and accessible to teachers across various subject areas, including political science, history, philosophy, geography, economics, ethics, environmental science, biology, STEM, culture studies, and literature.

R1: TRAINING MODULES FOR TEACHERS AND TRAINERS

Our project asked teachers to approach students from a novel, global, and transdisciplinary perspective to successfully address complex issues. This project result serves as:
- A self-learning guide for teachers and other educators
- A guide for training teacher trainers
- A guide for direct training of teachers and other school staff

R1 functions as a tool for continuous professional development, bridging the gap between the still very discipline-oriented teacher education and the transdisciplinary needs of today’s students. The topics covered include globalisation, wealth, and poverty; sustainability and climate; global health; identity, culture, religion, and border crossings; and noise, news, and neutrality.

R2: METHODOLOGICAL MANUAL

R2 is a methodological framework for the implementation of the pedagogical strategy and topics developed under R1. While R1 represents training materials for teachers, R2 focuses on their classrooms. R2 provides teachers with structured, step-by-step practical guidance and tools, leading them through the process of implementing the developed pedagogical strategy in both curricular and extra-curricular subjects and activities. This includes 10 lesson plans per topic with suggestions for use in a selection of relevant subjects, emphasising the transdisciplinary nature of complex contemporary problems, and 10 time-constricted modular exercises per topic which can be incorporated into other lesson plans.

R3: TOOLKIT FOR TEACHERS AND STUDENTS

R3 represents a collection of case studies of contemporary issues related to the five topics covered by R1 and R2 (globalisation, wealth, and poverty; sustainability and climate; global health; identity, culture, religion, and border crossings; noise, news, and neutrality). These case studies highlight and illustrate the interconnections between these areas and emphasise the necessity of transdisciplinary thinking about global issues. Building on debate methodology and specifically the models of motion analysis, this element explores several different models and strategies for analysing complex, multifaceted issues. The toolkit includes generalised structures and prompts that can be applied to different problems, providing teachers and students with blueprints for critical analysis that consider different perspectives, stakeholders, and value prioritisation.

R4: E-LEARNING PLATFORM

To ensure that project-developed content is readily available and maximally inclusive, we created an e-learning platform that transforms our content into a flowing e-learning tool with specific individualised learning plans for users. An attractive web environment significantly increases the impact and transferability potential of this project's results, making it more likely for organisations outside of our network to engage with the developed content. The website is developed as open-source and easily translatable content, allowing all actors within the EU to adapt the developed content to their national needs. User-friendliness and interactivity are the main reasons for the continual and broad use of materials available online.

2021-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000024606.title: THE ART OF TEACHING
2021-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000024606.summary:
<< Background >>

Many teachers and teaching assistants lack the training and resources needed to effectively support students with fewer opportunities in mainstream schools, limiting the potential for truly inclusive education. To address this, our project aimed to equip educators with innovative teaching tools and inclusive methodologies while fostering their professional and personal development. By bringing together experts in special and inclusive education, educational theatre and drama, cultural research, and information technology, we developed a training program that directly tackled the need for teacher training in inclusion. The project provided educators with competence-based learning strategies, engagement tools, and methodologies to create dynamic, inclusive, and effective learning environments for all students.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to enhance the quality of inclusive education by equipping teachers and teaching assistants with innovative methodologies and tools to support students with fewer opportunities in mainstream schools. By integrating drama methods, digital tools, and competence-based learning strategies, the project sought to empower educators to create engaging, dynamic, and student-centered learning environments.

Participants reported increased student engagement and learning retention, as drama-based teaching made lessons more interactive and memorable. Teachers observed greater creativity, confidence, and motivation in their students, as well as a stronger sense of classroom collaboration. The training provided educators with new strategies for inclusion, enabling them to better support students with diverse learning needs.

Teachers also highlighted the long-term impact of the training, emphasizing how drama-based learning enriched their teaching practice and helped them navigate unexpected situations in the classroom with greater ease. By fostering a supportive network of educators, the project ensured that its methodologies would continue to influence teaching approaches beyond the initial implementation. Ultimately, the pr

<< Implementation >>

The project encompassed a series of coordinated activities designed to train educators, develop innovative teaching methodologies, and promote inclusive education through drama methods and digital tools.

To ensure effective implementation, the Project Consortium conducted regular online working meetings, facilitating collaboration among partners and ensuring the smooth execution of project activities. One of the core elements was the Transnational Training Course, an intensive program where educators from participating countries explored the practical application of drama-based teaching methodologies.

A key aspect of the project was its international knowledge exchange, achieved through six online workshops that brought together teachers from different countries to share insights, discuss challenges, and explore new educational practices. To adapt these methodologies to local contexts, the project also delivered three National Training Courses, focusing on how drama methods can enhance inclusion in various educational settings. Additionally, six localized online workshops provided teachers with focused skill development and discussions tailored to their specific classroom needs.

To celebrate and disseminate project outcomes, the Online Festival of Educational Theatre and Drama showcased the creative work of educators and students, demonstrating the effectiveness of drama-based learning. In parallel, National Multiplier Events in each participating country introduced the project’s tools and strategies to a wider audience, encouraging educators to adopt these innovative approaches.

The culmination of the project was an International Conference, where findings were presented, and best practices were shared with educators, researchers, and policymakers. Finally, the project facilitated the presentation of good practices in schools, allowing educators to implement and demonstrate the impact of drama techniques in real classroom settings, further validating the effectiveness of the approach.

<< Results >>

Training Course: The Art of Teaching 
Developed a comprehensive curriculum for the training course titled The Art of Teaching, specifically tailored for primary school teachers and teaching assistants. Created a detailed plan of learning activities designed to integrate educational theatre and drama into primary education effectively. Produced multilingual teaching materials available in English, German, Croatian, and Slovenian, ensuring accessibility across participating countries. 

Collection of creative assessment activities
Compiled a collection of creative assessment activities to help educators evaluate students’ learning outcomes in innovative and engaging ways. 

ICT tools
Designed and disseminated three ICT tools to enhance the teaching and learning experience, merging technology with drama-based education. 

Educational Resources 
All curriculum and teaching materials are readily accessible to educators, providing a scalable model for use in other schools and regions. The ICT tools include features such as interactive storytelling, virtual role-playing, and drama scenario simulations, fostering creativity and collaboration among students. 

Empowered Educators and Students 
Teachers and teaching assistants who participated in the training reported greater confidence in implementing creative teaching methods. Students exhibited improved engagement and enthusiasm in lessons, reflecting the effectiveness of the innovative techniques introduced. 

Long-Term Benefits 
The project outcomes lay a foundation for continued collaboration among international educators.The resources developed are adaptable for future educational projects, encouraging widespread adoption of creative teaching strategies.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000027860.title: Virtual Reality based educational approach in tackling of Climate Change
2021-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000027860.summary:
<< Background >>

First of all, we performed surveys, for rang of introduction of Climate Change in education processin the partner countries. The surveys showed that besides this issue is addressed in formal education, traditional educational methods which are used for teaching of this topic offers mainly basic theoretical acknowledgement, usually with old facts.
Using of VR in education process is advanced education approach, which multiple times is overcoming the potential of traditional educational methods, and education systems must accept and accommodate on this fact. Recent decreasing of the prices of necessary Virtual Reality equipment makes this innovative educational approach acceptable to many educational institution on primary as well as on secondary level. With stimulation of teachers to accept the new methodology and with appropriated training programs in increasing of their skills and competences in using VR equipment and VR education software, all necessary pre-requests will be met.
The needs we addressed were learning more and increasing knowledge about clime changes among students, increasing capacity of using ICT in regular classes among students and teachers, using inovative pedagogical metod by introducing VR in lecturing.

<< Objectives >>

Our main  aim - to support awareness-raising about environmental and climate-change challenges, has been achieved. Our planned activities gave support to the testing of innovative practices (educational approach based on Virtual Reality software) to prepare children and school teachers to become true factors of change. New educational approach met the needs of school children (12 to 14 years age) to increase their overall acknowledgement about tackling of the Climate change phenomenon and to inspire them to take a real actions in „real life“ (e.g. saving resources, reduce energy use and waste, compensate carbon footprint emissions, increasing use of renewable energy sources, environment friendly transportation, etc.). Teachers have accomplished their skills and competencies about environment protection and together with pupils became true factors of change.Within the project implementation we also thought more widely. The project did not have an impact only on present schools' students, but with trained teachers, and developed VR-based education approach, ensured that also of students in the next generations will have the opportunity to be educated by using the innovative approach based on VR. 

<< Implementation >>

Within the project implementation we have implemented the following activities.
-	Development of an innovative ICT-based educational approach to increase student interest using Virtual Reality (free online virtual reality software and completely newly designed and created educational software related to climate change challenge and developed in Virtual Reality) that was enable students to understand adaptation strategies and climate change mitigation with a significant increase in their digital competencies.
-	Short-term training events for school teachers on how to use virtual reality equipment and educational software based on virtual reality in their daily lessons and blended mobility where students who were part of the wining teams in the schools compete in mixed transnational teams.
-	Long term teaching/learning assignment for students in primary school in using OER and VR-based educational software.
-	Organization of transnational project meetings for project management and monitoring  of the realized project activities. 
-	Organization of multiplier events.
-	Creating Intelectual outputs.


<< Results >>

Following Concrete project results have been achieved:
-	Development and adoption of three Project Results; IO1- Handbook for schools teachers: "Introducing of Climate Change related topics in STEM orientated school subjects",  IO2 - Virtual reality based educational software related with Climate Change topics and IO3- Document for establishing of long-term strategic partnership among different type of organisation for improvement of the educational processes in the regions of Velenje (Slovenia), Syros - Greece; Ludbreg - Croatia and Kochani – North Macedonia.
-	 16 school teachers with increased skills and competencies for using VR technology;
-	Established transnational teachers network (40 teachers from all four schools became familiar with the use of the eTwinning network module).
-	143 children from four schools with increased competences and skills for using VR technology in the learning process; as well as with increased acknowledgment for tackling of Climate Change phenomenon; 
-	Created Project website with best practices from project activities and with included created IOs which is available to teachers from other schools as well as for any other interested stakeholders on local, regional, national level; 
-	 197 relevant stakeholders have become familiar with advantages that new developed educational approach is offering versus traditional teaching methods /participants on each of the National multiplier events in Greece, Croatia, and North Macedonia as well as on the Final Project Conference in Slovenia).
-	An innovative ICT-based educational approach to increase student interest using Virtual Reality (free online virtual reality software and completely newly designed and created educational software related to climate change challenge and developed in Virtual Reality).
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000023695.title: Fun & Engaging STEM Activities For Tomorrow's World
2021-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000023695.summary:
<< Background >>

In the 21st-century technology world, it was inevitable for schools and teachers to be open to innovations. Innovative methods that meet today's world expectations and requirements, as well as the needs of children to be engaged in an inspiring environment, enable them to learn and succeed. Our partner schools revealed the weaknesses and strengths of their institutions by conducting SWOT analyses in their own schools. Based on the results, our project was created with the goal of raising highly qualified individuals for the future. 
It was focused on making more pleasant and enjoyable the learning of  Maths and Sciences. Science and maths contribute to developing students' logical-deductive minds and planning skills (competencies), among the main competencies in active citizenship. Moreover, sciences and maths helped abstraction processes from "doing" to "thinking" so enabling all students, including students with special needs, to be integrated in the activities. To extend students´ communicative, social, and problem-solving skills on an international level, including environmental awareness and sustainable approach in all actions of all participants.

<< Objectives >>

Support teachers with high quality teaching resources, Transfer of innovative STEM teaching methods to numerous teachers, to enable them to explore and share innovative tools and techniques, Boost a Europe-wide collaboration among  as well as education researchers and education professionals, exchanging innovative, effective and engaging approaches, Enable students to develop STEM and 21st-century skills including technology literacy, productivity, communication, problem solving, critical thinking, creativity, curiosity, decision making, leadership, entrepreneurship, acceptance of failure, social, language, intercultural skills and more, Explore the use of ICT (web 2.0 tools) in STEM education, to enhance its introduction in traditional teaching methods and create technology-rich learning environments for both teachers and students, Develop and enrich pupils’ understanding of the concept of "small changes in their daily lives" in an environmentally- threatened world, Include disadvantaged pupils in all project activities providing them with equal and fair learning environments and strengthening their self-confidence and hunger for learning and succeeding.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were carried out during the project process:
1. Education and information meetings of school staff
2. Kick-off staff Meeting in Ireland-TPM-implementation and coordination purposes. We got the chance to observe the working environment and facilities of the hosting organisation thus creating a stronger partnership between partners.
3. Student and teacher collaboration via the eTwitting platform during extracurricular lessons and special interest groups.
4. Short-term student and teacher mobilities - 6 LTT meetings
5.Online meetings with school coordinators to exchange views on student selection criteria for mobility through Zoom
6.School coordinators meeting for project initiation, planning and dissemination (Teachers in key roles of the project participated in all mobility)
7.Intellectual Output -digital platform creation and Multiplier Event
8.Creation of eTwinning, websites, Facebook and other social media for sharing, presentations, padlets, brochures, presentations
9.Excursions of pupils
10.Environmental activities
11.Workshops
12. National Webinars for teachers
13. Multiplication events physical and virtual

Pupils, project leaders and coordinators or the persons responsible for the final reckoning of the project took part in them. So, we obtained the following results:
- creating materials to promote our project on social media (Instagram, Twitter, Facebook pages), but also the outputs such as brochures, videos, web pages, booklets, calendars, project’s logo, pencil calendar, t-shirt, etc. dissemination by using (hymn, mascot, articles in the schools' websites, in the local press; flyers given to visitors during the Open Days or the Erasmus+ Days. The "pass a message" activity, initiated on the Etwinning - twin space,  accentuated to reach and share the practices through a large public in the school; students were encouraged to recycle, garden, bike ride, plant trees, and save energy sources at school and their daily lives.
-Activities between the mobility - presentations, giving information to colleagues about the project and mobilities, activities preparation for next mobilities, sharing the results with peers, Erasmus sign and a big bulletin board  at  schools, Erasmus corner where the countries flags and information about the previous and next mobilities , photos were also used
To facilitate understanding of the great challenge of academic cohesion at the personal level and in the European context, experiences of a new and inclusive approach were shared. (scientific, mathematical and pedagogical approaches)
The project activities were developed in order to achieve its objectives, therefore we implemented the following:
Problem-solving workshops, role play, game-based learning, interactive workshops delivered to students and teachers during the mobilities
Share best teaching practice 
Introduce schools/teachers/educators to content and language-integrated learning (CLIL), therefore developing cross-curricular teaching programme for the schools
Use of eTwinning in order to collaborate with the partner institutions and the final findings were published there being available for teachers across Europe 
Develop the Primary Science Education Platform, for the target groups to further develop their skills
Additionally, the mobility activities made it possible for both students and teachers to acquire knowledge about the partner institutions' geography, history, and culture, including how the institutions function, which is part of citizenship education. Through the development of the project output, we transferred innovative teaching methods to a large number of teachers. We helped students develop important transversal skills such as creative thinking, problem-solving, etc., which they can utilise in school and also in the near future in the labour market. 

<< Results >>

The most valuable output of our project was the education platform prepared by the Academy for International Science and Research, which significantly impacted a large audience.
The exchange of ideas, applications of science and mathematics, STEM methods, and techniques was conducted at the international level. Teaching and support competencies for students with fewer opportunities were strengthened. This supported the improvement of future employment prospects and socio-educational development, focusing on basic, cross-functional, soft, entrepreneurial, foreign language, and digital web tools.
Furthermore, project leaders from schools, along with Maths and Science teachers of partner schools, supported their professional development through training based on their respective school methodologies. The Hejny Method was applied as the basic teaching approach in Slovakia, while Greek schools focused on experiments and arts. Turkish schools shared their methodologies in Maths and Science through Inquiry-Based Teaching and the Invention Method. Croatian and Polish schools applied integrated theme teaching using life experiences in classes, and Swedish schools emphasized Maths and Science skills as the foundation of STEM education.
Students were exposed to learning foreign languages, enhancing their foreign language and ICT skills. Through successful mentorship, young students were encouraged to develop innovative, entrepreneurial ideas and actions. Pupils gained higher self-esteem by independently functioning in a foreign environment and being fully responsible for their actions and decisions.
Specific results achieved included:
Strengthening teachers' academic careers through participation in international mobility and practical cooperation in education.
Establishing long-term friendships and international cooperation among students from partner schools.
Improving the quality of partner schools through developing or applying innovative elements in learning and teaching environments.
Establishing long-term partnerships and knowledge sharing among teachers.
Increasing skills through experiences from different schools and countries.
Creating open, dynamic, flexible, innovative, and international schools.
Enhancing pupils' competencies to act responsibly towards the environment as Green European Citizens, promoting recycling and sustainable methods to reduce waste, save energy, and conserve water at school.
The project impacted the development of innovative and tested methods and tools across European and international scales in the fields of Mathematics and Science, social, communication and IT skills.
The project provided high-quality educational services, facilitating students' adaptation to an increasingly modern world and preparing them more effectively for the future.

2021-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000024680.title: Development through autonomy, self-responsibility and self-care: ePortfolios as a life-long-learning approach from secondary school to university
2021-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000024680.summary:
<< Background >>

Four out of five project participants took part in the TCA in Bratislava in October 2019, focusing on the topic "Building Partnership for a Learner-Centred Approach." The main idea, which was later developed into the project, was based on two primary needs: (1) building and developing learner autonomy and self-responsibility, and (2) integrating digital tools into teaching. The added value was the enhanced interconnection between teaching practice, teacher trainers, and teacher trainees, fostering a more cohesive and supportive educational environment. 
In the process of submitting the project the world situation in using digital tools in education changed. The pandemic situation in 2020 led to a significant revolution in education. Schools rapidly upgraded their technical infrastructure and provided teachers with the necessary equipment. However, this technological enhancement alone is insufficient. Teachers had  to and have to also consider the methodological aspects of online teaching and learning, such as the effective use of digital tools, the personalization of learning environments, and the fostering of meaningful interactions. Thus, methodological aspect of the project was significantly emphasised.

<< Objectives >>

The primary expected impact is building and developing autonomous secondary school learners who are ready to plan their own progress and self-evaluate it. The use of portfolios to develop autonomy has been proven to be an effective tool. To ensure this impact, it is necessary to prepare future teachers for this situation and to develop the life skills needed for the 21st century.
The primary aims were to prepare a methodological guide on using the learning management system Moodle (open course in Moodle) and the e-portfolio tool Mahara (open course in Moodle). An important result is the creation of materials on how to build and enhance learner autonomy (open course in Moodle) and practical guides and samples on using digital tools (Mahara sites and Moodle course). The use of these tools is interconnected, allowing users to immediately see what to expect and how to use the tools effectively.
Data collected before and after using Mahara for 10 months were analyzed. Two articles presenting the data have been accepted for publication, and two are under revision.
The added value was that learners involved in the project could see the possibilities of E+ school projects, as they were mostly aware of university schemes or possibilities.

<< Implementation >>

The main aim of the project was to create two key products focused on promoting autonomous learning among secondary school students and enhancing the digital competence of future educators.
The first product is an e-portfolio designed to support the development of self-directed learning skills in secondary school learners. The second product is a comprehensive course aimed at university teacher training students, providing them with the knowledge and skills to effectively use digital tools—such as e-portfolios and Moodle—to foster learner autonomy and develop the essential digital competencies recognized as key 21st-century skills.
Regular management and monitoring meetings were organized to track progress, review the timeline, and ensure the achievement of planned outcomes. There were also one-to-one meetings organised to help in the initial phase, especially when Mahara was introduced to schools.

An important part of the project was the Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities. The Max Beckman Schule had extensive experience with using Mahara, all secondary schools were experts in using digital tools for teaching different subjects, and the University of Presov had experience in developing autonomy and e-courses. Thus, two training activities (in 2022 at MBS Schule in Germany, and in 2023 at Jure Kastelan School in Croatia) were crucial for enhancing the quality of the project. Each meeting also provided space for progress reports, discussions on financial issues, and planning further activities. 
The e-portfolio was implemented at all secondary schools and in two subjects at the University of Presov. After the pilot session, the schools used The Student Course Engagement Questionnaire (SCEQ; Handlesman et al., 2005) to measure and evaluate student autonomy. At the end of the school year, after using the e-portfolio, the level of autonomy was measured again. At Gymnazium in Zilina, teachers also conducted interviews to learn more about the learners' attitudes. Interviews about the student attitudes were also conducted and analyzed at Giessen University. 
University - grammar school visits and observations were carried out in Slovakia and Germany. The university students provided positive feedback, not only regarding the use of digital tools in teaching but also on the information about running Erasmus+ projects at secondary schools. We see this as an added value since many of those students are now teachers, and we have received feedback indicating that they are already engaged in Erasmus+ activities.
The transnational meeting in Slovakia (2024) provided space for evaluation and the planning of dissemination activities. The meeting also resulted in a short video featuring participants' opinions on the Erasmus+ project and their experiences throughout the course of the project. This video is available on the project website: https://www.unipo.sk/filozoficka-fakulta/iaa/projektDASS/43595/.
Dissemination activities were organized in all participating countries (Slovakia - face-to-face, Croatia - online, Germany - both formats). Several texts have been or are planned to be published based on the knowledge and data gained from the project.
Furthermore, the data collected during the project regarding students' attitudes were analyzed and prepared for publication (some of which have already been published).

<< Results >>

The project planned two outcomes:
(1) teaching material on using digital tools (including sample lesson plans) 
(2) the course in LMS focused on methodological aspects of online teaching

The material on using digital tools presents 14 tools (including Mahara) and is supported with the video and samples, available online: https://portfolio.bildung.hessen.de/view/view.php?t=0ab8936d1996049818f7
It is a collection of digital tools  created by teachers for teachers. High schools teachers have chosen the most helpful and reliable digital tools and they presently work with. There is a simple description of the tool, basic data, payment information and some teachers´ tips and tricks on each page. The material is added with the  practical examples of use and ideas how to work with the tools. With each page the users can find also a screencast of the tool (Mahara - the e-Portfolio-Plattform also used for this collection, Actionbound, Bookcreator, Canva, Flippity, Genially, Kahoot, KITS - mindmap, etherpad, wordcloud and more, Learningapp, Mentimeter, Mindmaps: Bubbl.us, Nearpod, Taskcards: A Pinboard, Zeoob - Fake social media creator.

The aim of the LMS Course on Autonomy Development using ePortfolio is to provide the users with both technical and methodological insights into utilizing various digital tools to foster autonomy. The course equips students with the skills and knowledge necessary to effectively use Moodle as a teaching and learning platform in their future classrooms, as well as Mahara e-portfolio. Special sessions are dedicated to discussing autonomy development, utilizing digital tools, and digital CLIL (Content and Language Integrated Learning). Each session establishes clear learning outcomes, allowing students the flexibility to engage with the sessions in any order they prefer. All sessions are connected by the overarching theme of developing autonomy using ePortfolio. The link to the course is: https://e.ff.unipo.sk/course/view.php?id=169

2021-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000027903.title: Object Oriented Programming for Fun
2021-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000027903.summary:
<< Background >>

Our project aimed to help address the need to increase the number of ICT specialists in the EU and associated countries. We wanted to address this need by jointly developing a new way of teaching programming in secondary schools, namely object-oriented programming. The role of programming in computer science is similar to that of practical work in other sciences – it provides motivation and a context in which ideas are put to life. In addition to motivation from various EU sources, we can mention other needs that we wanted to cover with our project: stopping the declining number of students interested in STEM study programmes in secondary schools (student motivation), presenting STEM and especially programming as not being difficult to study. The only people who can reach secondary school students about this fact are their own STEM and programming teachers.
The EU aims to improve the digital skills of (1) citizens; (2) the workforce; (3) ICT professionals and (4) educational institutions. In our project, we focused on the fourth area mentioned - the education of secondary school teachers.

<< Objectives >>

Our project was aimed at secondary school teachers. They were our primary target group. Based on interviews with university teachers from the project consortium, there is a certain “gap” in understanding the basic principles of programming, especially in the case of object-oriented programming (OOP) among secondary school students admitted to informatics faculties of universities. It is very important that secondary school teachers understand what OOP is about. Unfortunately, we knew from our own experience that not all teachers understand the principles of programming correctly. This of course has an impact on students' education and their perception of programming. In our project, we wanted to prepare an overview of current methods, methodologies and concepts in programming for secondary school teachers, prepare syllabi and manuals (textbooks + online content). The main and unique mission of our international project team was to prepare curricula and project outcomes aimed at students and teachers learning and teaching OOP through game development with knowledge and skills related to the development process and collaboration in real and virtual environments.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented the following project activities:
* four transnational project meetings (Žilina, Ivanec, Pardubice, Ivanjica)
* one teaching and training activity for secondary school teachers (Dresden)
* six multiplication events (Žilina, Starý Smokovec, Zagreb, Pardubice, Belgrade, Dresden)
* five project results – a series of analyses of programming education in secondary schools and universities, a new curriculum for teaching object-oriented programming, a textbook for secondary school teachers (materials for preparing their lessons), a textbook for university students (future teachers of programming)

<< Results >>

* Analysis of the current state and identification of gaps in programming teaching
* Design of programming teaching with a new guiding idea
* Development of new curricula for programming teaching
* Materials for teachers - transfer of experience for current and future teachers
* Design of new curricula for accreditation bodies at secondary level
HE teachers from these countries prepared a gap analysis of programming teaching in their countries. Based on this, a new and innovative learning design for teaching programming was defined in cooperation with secondary school teachers. In parallel, HE teachers from UNIZA, UNIZG and UB created a new main idea (approach) of ​​teaching programming based on their national concepts. The selected learning design was also implemented in partner secondary schools. Based on the joint agreement of the partner organizations and associated partners, the development of a new generation of educational materials for secondary school teachers began. These materials include modern textbooks and supporting materials (worksheets, examples, methodology). All educational materials are published on an e-learning portal with free access.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000034395.title: PLATO'S EU: Philosophical Learning Applied To Online Surroundings in EU
2021-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000034395.summary:
<< Background >>

European Union recognized the need for more cohesive and inclusive society, with greater integration of its citizens embracing their active role in democratic life. Within this recognition, key areas such as education, training, and youth work are designated to support and develop the sense of common European values, social integration, interculturality, and notion of community affiliation. Taking this into consideration, as well as the urgent need for adjustment to the new and unexpected ways of life caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, European Union underlined the importance of new horizontal priorities: innovative practices in digital age. This paradigm of innovative practices in digital age includes the use of digital technologies, innovative and open pedagogical practices in education and training, as well as development of open education resources, open textbooks, and open source educational software. In our project we tried  to answer on this need, and offer a way to respond to the demand of developing open society through the use of innovative practices.

<< Objectives >>

By combining theoretical and practical approach, intertwining philosophical methods such as critical thinking and Socratic dialogue with digital resources, we aimed to tackle more cohesive and inclusive society, with greater integration of its citizens embracing their active role in democratic life, and not only strengthed capacity of individuals for adequate adjustment to digital challenges, but built a basis for enhancing the notion of shared European values, social integration, interculturality, and democratization.

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the project, we actively collaborated with the target groups on both the creation and validation of our individual outputs. We actively tested a series of workshops in target institutions in all partner countries. Also, all partners actively promoted the project, its objectives and outputs both at various popularization and professional events or through social and traditional media. In the end, we organized Multiplication Events (in number we exceeded the number of participants set in the project) in each partner country, which resulted in an offer to implement the results of the PLATO'S EU project in the educational process of current teachers in the Banská Bystrica region probably from 2024 onwards.



<< Results >>

We created  Online educational platform as a digital basis not only for resources created through the project’s lifetime, but also as a archive of other available materials, shared by willing parties. We also created the course of online workshops (2 moduls), which provide participants with necessary tools and strategies for better understanding of technological potential, and all benefits (but also dangers) which are offered with it. As project consortium was intended to function through close inter-sectoral cooperation, experiences of the partners, examples of good practices and feedback from the workshops was gathered and developed into digital open source manual CULTIVATING RESILIENT AND RESPONSIVE PERSONS: A Teacher’s Manual for Utilizing Philosophical Methods for and in Digital World.  Another output of our project is  THE PHILOSOPHICAL COOKBOOK: Recipes that Help you Remain Safe and Sane in Digital World - the non-formal manual for philosophy, designed to serve as a type of “philosophical cookbook” with “philosophical recipes” which general public can use to properly enjoy benefits of digital resources.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-2-AT01-KA220-SCH-000048927.title: Bürgerräte und andere neue Formen der Partizipation - in der politischen Bildung.
2021-2-AT01-KA220-SCH-000048927.summary:
<< Background >>

This project addressed new forms of political participation, and specifically Mini-Publics. 
Political Participation is one of the goals of Civic Education, and one of its main purposes: building participating citizens. 
Our project focuses on Civic Education in schools, and it addresses teachers’ professional development and students’ learning about political participation. 
When participation is taught in its traditional forms, it is going to influence what students will perceive their tasks as citizens to be. Teaching about voting and electoral systems are only a part of political participation. Therefore, new forms of participation should also be included in school curricula, especially if they can appeal to younger generations and nourish their engagement to sustain democracies.
For young people, Mini-Publics can be interesting for several respects: the minimum age of participation is 16, and many of them are about climate protection and climate justice. Young students who do not have the formal citizenship of the country in which they live can also participate in Mini-Publics. 
In MANTA we prepared several resources for teachers and students, so that these topics professional competences of teachers are improved.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of this project will be presented based on the different target groups of this project:
-	teachers of humanities (history, civic education, social sciences etc.): knowledge development of new instruments of citizen participation; popularising Mini-Publics and Citizens’ Assemblies as participation tool; learning how they can implement this topic in their subject; didactical knowledge of research based teaching;
-	students: motivation to be involved in decision-making at all levels; ability to discuss the potential and limits of participation instruments such as the citizens' council; improvement of civic skills; development of a questioning attitude; positive attitude towards complex issues; critical thinking and ability to develop arguments about political issues;
-	participating organisations: knowledge improvement of Mini-Publics; development of knowledge of the Erasmus+ programme for 1st time participants; improvements of project management skills; development of networks and cooperations;
-       education stakeholders: improve the quality of the educational offer for teachers on the topic of political participation


<< Implementation >>

To achieve the above-mentioned objectives, the following activities have been implemented:
- Production of a blended learning training to support teacher initial and continuing education;
- Production of a webinar with content specific to democracy, deliberative democracy and activities for students;
- Production of a research oriented workshop outline to explain principles of scientific research in social sciences, and workshop material with resources;
- Production of a video showing a research oriented workshop implemented with teachers and meant for teachers;
- Production of a compendium explaining 3 case studies of Mini-Publics;
- Production of 2 podcasts and corresponding videos with primary school and high school students. 

In addition to these, the partnership also organised several events:
-	5 partnership meeting took place in person 
-	1 learning, teaching, training activity event took place in 2023
-	16 online meetings
-       7+ Multiplier Events



<< Results >>

In the project, we realised the following outputs:
-	Project result 1 - Blended Learning Training
-	Project result 2 -  Webinars
-	Project result 3 - Research-oriented impulse materials for use in Civic Education lessons
-	Project result 4 - Short film - insights into a research workshop
-	Project result 5 - Compendium
-	Project result 6 - Podcasts

Other results were:
-	5 partnership meeting took place in person - which resulted in an upskilling of all staff involved, both on the topic of the project and on project management on a EU scale;
-	1 learning, teaching, training activity event took place in 2023 - which resulted into a feedback process for partners but also supported teachers in improving knowledge and methods to teach new forms of participation; 
-	16 online meetings - which resulted into better cooperation dynamics, facilitated partners cooperative work, and ensured the respect of project milestones; 
-       7+ Multiplier Events - which resulted into improved knowledge and methods to teach new forms of participation.

On the level of project management (including dissemination), the coordinator and partners developed the following tools:
- Quality Assurance Plan;
- Sustainability Plan;
- Templates (financial report, timesheets, timesheets tutorials, activity reports, dissemination reports, evaluation forms, table for risk analysis);
- Checklists for reporting;
- Agendas for meetings as well as corresponding minutes;
-  Interim report and final report;
- Dissemination: Dissemination Plan, website, logo, project leaflet, LTTA and ME programs, social media channels, video;
For detailed results, please refer to the respective parts in the reporting.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2021-2-PL01-KA220-SCH-000048581.title: Dream, Engage, Act and Re-act 4 the Future
2021-2-PL01-KA220-SCH-000048581.summary:
<< Background >>

In the face of the new social and digital context, we clearly need to create an innovative educational package that is able to provide, through new approaches to teaching and learning, appropriate platforms, resources and experiences that equip our teachers with the knowledge and skills needed to educate the younger generation in the emerging fields of artificial intelligence. AI gives children an advantage in life and allows them to learn more effectively. It is intricately woven into the way the world works, and the possibilities of AI are endless. Engaging children with AI is essential to preparing them for the future.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the DEAR FUTURE consortium was to facilitate and enable the development of a framework that will enable preschool teachers and students to acquire the 21st century skills and knowledge necessary to promote basic AI literacy by establishing a holistic approach in preschool education. We want to promote AI in preschool education because the Early Childhood Education and Care Strategy 2021-2030 states that "basic digital skills and competences are limited from an early age because preschoolers are at a high stage of development both physically and cognitively". The DEAR FUTURE consortium is aware that teaching AI is not easy because AI is very complex, non-specific and new for preschoolers. In order to reduce the complexity and abstraction of AI in teaching, we want to improve innovative approaches. In this context, we want to promote AI through an approach based on interactive storytelling (GIS) based on games. We chose the GIS system because preschoolers learn better through games and stories.

<< Implementation >>

Management activities were carried out; 5 transnational project meetings were held in: Turkey, Croatia, Bulgaria, Czech Republic and Poland; 2 LTTAs were held in Portugal and Czech Republic; courses for kindergarten teachers and seminars for parents were held; conferences were organised to disseminate the project and various other dissemination activities were carried out: visits to schools, presentations in the local area, etc.

<< Results >>

Project Results : 
-  Curriculum for teaching artificial intelligence in preschools through interactive game-based storytelling.
-  Online training course for preschool teachers on using interactive game-based storytelling approach in teaching artificial intelligence.
-  Internet platform and e-learning platform.
-  Set of audiovisual materials for preschool teachers - for use in teaching artificial intelligence through "interactive game-based storytelling".
INTANGIBLE RESULTS:
- Engagement of children in kindergarten in AI.
- Promotion of teaching and more active use of technology in AI teaching through sharing and holistic approach.
- Integration of online technology into teaching, training and knowledge about AI.
- Increase of students’ understanding skills in education.
- Strengthening of teachers’ attitudes towards EU organization and EU values.
- Engagement of teachers in AI practices and AI regulations across the EU.
- Students and teachers have the opportunity to communicate and cooperate with their foreign peers.
- Basic education of teachers and students in teaching through active assistance in teaching the educational environment and education outside the classroom and school environment.
- Increase of skills and profes
