2021-2-PL01-KA220-SCH-000048987.title: roboSTEAMKIDS: UPGRADING EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATION AND CARE THROUGH THE DIGITAL UPSKILLING OF TEACHERS AND THE INTRODUCTION OF AN INCLUSIVE STEAM AND ROBOTICS PROGRAMME
2021-2-PL01-KA220-SCH-000048987.summary:
<< Background >>

As partners, we applied for this project to address critical gaps in early childhood STEAM education and foster a future-oriented and inclusive learning environment. We recognized the lack of focus on STEAM education for young children, which is essential for preparing them for careers in digital and scientific fields. Additionally, we aimed to tackle the digital skills gap, highlighted by the 2020 DESI analysis, which showed that 57% of enterprises struggled to recruit ICT specialists.
Our efforts centered on empowering early childhood education teachers by equipping them with digital and pedagogical skills to modernize teaching, reduce disparities among EU member states, and bridge the digital divide. We prioritized promoting gender balance, inclusion, equity, and parental engagement in the educational process.
As the project progressed, we developed practical tools and resources to enhance early childhood education and care (ECEC) teachers' and parents' and caregivers' training in coding and robotics. We ensured the sustainability and dissemination of our results to create a lasting impact on STEAM education for early learners across all partner countries.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to achieve several key objectives by implementing this project. Our primary goal was to modernize early childhood education by equipping teachers with the digital and pedagogical skills needed to address the challenges of a rapidly evolving educational landscape. We aimed to strengthen the professional profiles of early education teachers, empowering them to implement innovative STEAM teaching methods and bridge the disparities in digital education across EU.
We sought to address gaps in ECEC teacher motivation, digital literacy, and the ability to engage students through updated pedagogical approaches. Additionally, we focused on promoting inclusion, gender balance, and parental involvement in the educational process. By doing so, we aimed to ensure equitable access to high-quality early education and to support the development of foundational skills in children for their future education and career prospects.
To achieve this, we provided ECEC teachers with practical tools and resources (i.e. platform, scenarios for lessons, digital badge system). Furthermore, we emphasized the promotion of European values, including respect, diversity, equality, solidarity, and inclusion, ensuring these were embedded in project results 

<< Implementation >>

We implemented a series of structured activities aimed at achieving the project’s objectives through three main project results (PR1, PR2, PR3), each with specific activities and deliverables:

PR1: STEAM & Robotics Handbook (https://robosteamkids.eu/pr1-handbook/)
Activities:
- Conducted research and ECEC policies documentation to map good practices in STEAM education and robotics across partner countries.
- Performed a needs analysis to identify gaps in ECEC teachers’ digital competencies and the integration of STEAM in early education.
- Mapped policies and professional development opportunities for ECEC teachers to design a competence framework addressing these gaps.
Results:
- Produced Desktop Research and Policy Documentation for every country along with overview presented as infographics.
- Virtual Study Visits Reports depicting characteristics among countries
- Focus Groups Reports indicating the scope of needs among target groups in every country (ECEC teachers and ECEC parents), potential elements of innovation, expected impact and transferability
- Methodology and Guidelines Handbook providing efficient methods to promote STEAM skills, including robotics and coding as the foundation for designing targeted professional development programs.

PR2: STEAM Toolkit for Teachers, Parents, and Children (https://robosteamkids.eu/toolkit/)
Activities:
- Developed the toolkit to improve teachers' profiles by providing resources for interdisciplinary STEAM education with a focus on robotics, coding, and environmental themes.
- Designed the professional development course to help teachers acquire critical skills for STEAM education.
- Created resources to teach children essential digital and life skills like problem-solving, collaboration, and creative thinking in a fun, exploratory environment.
Results:
- Syllabuses for 6 modules of the ECEC course in English and each partner country national language (Croatia, Greek, Italian, Polish, Romanian) exploring following topics: 1) Introduction to STEAM Education and Robotics in ECEC, 2) Methodologies and pedagogies: Project-based learning and cross-curricular work through STEAM and Robotics, 3) Digital upskilling as per the DigiComp, 4) Coding and Robotics, 5) Exploring the roboSTEAMkids programme, 6) The eco-system of the Open Badges
- Lesson plans for ECEC teachers for each of the 6 modules in English and each partner country national language (Croatia, Greek, Italian, Polish, Romanian)
- Activities packs for parents related to course in English and each partner country national language (Croatia, Greek, Italian, Polish, Romanian) 
- Webinars introducing the practical approaches to use the created content and work with children
- Pool of Resources providing materials and sources (with links and descriptions) recommended by each partner for ECEC teachers and parents further work

PR3: Inclusive Digital Platform (https://robosteamkids.eu/inclusive-platform/ ; https://academy.robosteamkids.eu/)
Activities:
- Built a multi-functional e-learning platform offering features like training syllabuses, webinars, assessment tools, and a collaborative e-community for teachers, educators, parents and ECEC-related stakeholders.
- Designed an Open Badges system to validate and assess teachers’ skills in STEAM and robotics.
Results:
- Inclusive and accessible platform that supports ongoing professional development and collaboration of ECEC teachers in English and each partner country national language (Croatia, Greek, Italian, Polish, Romanian)
- Manuals providing instructions and guidelines on how to exploit the platform to support the professional development of ECEC community in English and each partner country national language (Croatia, Greek, Italian, Polish, Romanian)

Through these structured activities and tangible results, we provided practical tools and resources for ECEC teachers, modernized teaching practices, ensuring strengthened collaboration among educators and stakeholders. We also reinforced the importance of inclusion, equity, and alignment with European values, ensuring the project’s long-term impact on early childhood STEAM education.

<< Results >>

The project delivered several concrete outputs and impactful results, organized into three main areas around each PR:
PR1 Results: We produced a comprehensive handbook that outlined main directions and efficient methods for promoting STEAM skills, including robotics and coding. This handbook provides foundational knowledge to design targeted professional development programs for early childhood education teachers, addressing their specific needs and gaps.
PR2 Results: We enhanced the existing curricula by introducing new resources and materials tailored to STEAM education. Our efforts will empower ECC community to develop investigative and innovative skills, fostering a foundation for life-long learning in an engaging and exploratory environment.
PR3 Results: We created an inclusive digital platform that significantly improve teaching and learning methods by supporting professional development and collaboration among ECEC teachers and stakeholders. By providing free access to all resources and tools, we attract ECEC teachers, but also students, parents and other relevant stakeholders (i.e. policy / decision-makers, branch associations, NGOs) and ensure the project’s long-term sustainability and possibly broadest applicability.
These outputs collectively contributed to modernizing ECEC practices, bridging gaps in digital competencies, and also promoting European values of inclusion, diversity, and equity.

2022-1-AT01-KA220-SCH-000086658.title: Fictional Science (FiSci) – Förderung von Textkompetenz im kritischen Umgang mit Fake News
2022-1-AT01-KA220-SCH-000086658.summary:
<< Background >>

It has never been easier to find information on a topic online. Thanks to digital transformation, information can be found and shared with just a few clicks. However, this also fuels the spread of disinformation and misinformation. 
This gives schools a key task: learners must be taught to critically examine information in (digital) texts and, if necessary, refute it. The project Fictional Science (FiSci) responds to this educational challenge by aiming to provide learners in multilingual teaching and learning contexts with tools to identify and discursively refute misinformation. Pupils not only need a critical and evaluative attitude when encountering (digital) texts, but also need concrete strategies and resources for verifying information. In addition, they need linguistic means to be able to refute false information in an argumentative manner. In multilingual learning contexts, the different linguistic prerequisites of learners in the critical use of texts must also be taken into account.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project FiSci was to develop a scientifically sound and empirically evaluated didactic approach that can be used to promote learners' text competence in critically dealing with fake news. This approach should be implemented in the form of teaching modules in German as a first, second and foreign language lessons, enabling learners to assess information conveyed by the media in terms of its factuality, helping them to avoid being misled by fake news and being able to refute false information in writing. The teaching modules should be tested, evaluated and optimised with approximately 600 learners. In order to make (prospective) German teachers familiar with the approach, numerous professional development measures should be developed and implemented (training courses, modules for the training and further education of teachers, didactic podcast series, online module implemented as an e-learning course), which are aimed directly at teachers or multipliers in the education sector. In addition, citizen science products (online game, podcast series, educational videos) should also be used to address a general public.

<< Implementation >>

The didactic approach FiSci was implemented in 16 teaching modules for German as a first, second and foreign language (secondary levels 1 & 2). Ten teaching modules are offered on the FiSci digital learning platform (www.fictionalscience.eu). Six special modules were also developed. They cover topics such as misinformation in the context of artificial intelligence or multilingualism. Furthermore, eight podcast episodes and four educational videos were produced. In addition, an online game, training modules, testing, observation and feedback tools were designed. All project results were tested, evaluated and optimised in practice. A handbook provides an overview of all outputs and provides theoretical background information and tips for their use in the classroom practice. All results were disseminated widely: three international training courses and five multiplier events were held. In addition, several scientific publications were produced and the approach was presented to both professionals and the scientific community at numerous events.

<< Results >>

Based on a scientifically sound and practically proven didactic approach, concrete resources and tools were developed for teaching and teacher training as well as for a general public (a digital learning platform: https://www.fictionalscience.eu, teaching modules, training modules for teachers, podcasts, educational videos, an online game, and much more, see https://fictionalscience.uni-graz.at/de/). These are intended to train a critical and evaluative approach to reading and to provide tools for uncovering deception in texts and refuting misinformation through discourse. They have been empirically evaluated and optimised, whereby the multimedia presentation of contentand design elements that promote autonomy have emerged as particularly important. The teaching materials are being tested for effectiveness in a linked intervention study with more than 200 learners in Austria. As feedback from dissemination and testing shows, the outputs are perceived as a very positive resource by teachers. This applies in particular to the text type refutation text, which has been introduced into German language teaching through the project.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-BE01-KA220-SCH-000085424.title: LA ROBOTIQUE HIER, AUJOURD'HUI, DEMAIN. SON INTERACTION AVEC L'ENVIRONNEMENT ET LE CLIMAT
2022-1-BE01-KA220-SCH-000085424.summary:
<< Background >>

Robotics is an extremely important element in today's life, whether in the everyday life of each individual, in industry, in research, in medicine. “Robots” are part of our daily lives. By building this project, the school's teaching team wanted to put students in direct contact with these various elements that we use every day, but which we know little about. The research and applications will therefore be discoveries for our students who will have the opportunity to better understand their environment. On the other hand, we had worked on a previous project which had shown the students the importance of the environment and climate in our lives. As we are living in a period of transition, of climate change, we wanted, secondly, to discover the interactions that exist or could exist between robotics and these two factors. All planned activities are therefore complementary and must provide answers to many questions relating to the future of our students.

<< Objectives >>

Our objectives were:
1. allow our students to get to know robotics and its evolution through the ages
2. get to know robotics in our daily lives
3. become aware of climate change around the world
4. connect robotics and the environment and climate
This project must be the basis of awareness of the environmental and climatological elements which are currently transforming. Through this project, we want to interest students in the worrying situation and, through our students, transmit new knowledge and real awareness to parents.

<< Implementation >>

http://involvement-of-robotics-in-e-c.e-monsite.com
During this project, we have
- carried out research on robotics, its meaning, its fields, its evolution. A lot of research has been carried out by the partners.
- exchanged all activity documents, learned from our colleagues
- grew up knowing a common language
- met foreign colleagues, discussed together the teaching, its conditions, the desires of the students.
- helps our students develop, encourages their interest in science.

<< Results >>

The partners carried out all the activities planned to better understand robotics and its “invasion” in our daily lives. We became involved in the interaction between robotics and our environment and climate. To achieve our objectives, we met robotics experts during the various mobilities. We were thus able to discover various activities relating to robotics and obtain answers to certain questions. This project also allowed our students to realize the importance of languages ​​in our European society. All our activities, our results, our activity reports, our mobilities can be found on our website: 
http://involvement-of-robotics-in-e-c.e-monsite.com

2022-1-BE02-KA220-SCH-000087366.title: Deplastify the Planet
2022-1-BE02-KA220-SCH-000087366.summary:
<< Background >>

The European Green Deal emphasizes the need for international cooperation to enhance global environmental standards. However, COVID-19 led to increased waste, such as plastic cups and packaging, and overflowing bins filled with used masks. Prior to the project's initiation, a survey at schools showed that students had alarmingly poor knowledge about the environment and recycling. Daily news reports highlighted the severe global plastic pollution issue, predicting that by 2050, there could be more plastic in the ocean than fish. It was crucial to deliver a strong, clear message on this issue as the aim of the project.

<< Objectives >>

Stakeholders learned initiatives and best practice examples from partners and applied ideas to reduce plastic waste at school. Through a cross-curricular approach and project-based learning, students explored ecological problems and found solutions to reduce them. Due to collaboration with partners, students learned more about EU citizenship, experiencing it through lectures, student exchanges, and different contacts. They strengthened their European identity/citizenship and improved their language skills.

<< Implementation >>

The main goals of the project were to reduce single-use plastic and raise awareness about its environmental impact. At the start, participants measured their average single-use plastic consumption, aiming for a 50% reduction by the end. This reduction involved not just buying less plastic, but primarily switching to recycled materials. By doing this, we aimed to instill lasting positive habits. Through dissemination, we shared our impact with all students and teachers at partner schools to ensure the project's sustainability. Tips and best practices were compiled into a E-book "Tips and tricks to reduce plastic at school"  for use by participating schools and other institutions. Additionally, we aimed to educate students about plastic pollution and the need to stop contaminating rivers, seas, and oceans. Activities at partner schools included best practice presentations, creating a professional comic book "Plastica's revenge", clean-up actions, Planet Earth Days, transitioning to sustainable materials, environmental education lessons, guest lectures, and recycling factory visits. These activities were organized during the 2 project years, including 6 exchange weeks between all the different partners.

<< Results >>

The project greatly impacted environmental education and awareness. We developed an E-book for schools with practical tips on reducing single-use plastics. Six participating schools presented on addressing environmental issues and minimizing plastic use. We also created a project website and social media channels for updates. A pamphlet titled "SORT IT" offered advice on reducing plastic waste and raising awareness. A comic book illustrated environmental problems in an accessible way. Local media covered the project, and an aftermovie documented the mobility exchanges.

The project raised environmental awareness among students, teachers, school staff, parents, local citizens, and politicians. It inspired new colleagues to join additional projects and training, empowered teachers with innovations in environmental education, and contributed to achieving the ECO school label. The "Green (ECO) School" concept attracted eco-conscious students. The project enhanced IT and language skills, increased awareness of long-haul flight impacts, and led to green initiatives like tree planting. Stays with host families also boosted participants' sense of European citizenship.

2022-1-BG01-KA220-SCH-000087073.title: S@fe future
2022-1-BG01-KA220-SCH-000087073.summary:
<< Background >>

Digitization in all spheres of life transfers a significant part of human relations from the real to the online space, which gives rise to a number of digital risks that its users face. Children and adolescents are undoubtedly the most vulnerable to these dangers. On the one hand, through the use of video content platforms, social media, apps, etc., children at an early age are significantly ahead of conventional education and are developing their fundamental digital competencies through trial and error. In the process, often due to inexperience and lack of deeper knowledge, they become victims of digital bullying. On the other hand, there is the considerable amount of time they spend in the digital space without exercising real, adequate control by parents and school.
Through the implementation of the "S@fe future" project, working solutions were developed for the prevention of digital bullying among children and adolescents, aimed at building a safe and secure digital environment that would allow them to develop and upgrade their digital competences, communicate and explore the possibilities of the online space without being at risk of becoming a victim of digital bullying.


<< Objectives >>

The main objective: 
Development and implementation of an integration model for building a secure and safe digital environment for the development of IT competences of adolescents and research of the digital space, ensuring the prevention of the risk of digital bullying, with the active participation of parents, teachers, non-pedagogical staff, students and NGOs.

Specific objectives:
1) Research the experience of the partners in terms of legal regulation, management and the possibilities of creating a safe digital space for adolescent students, ensuring the prevention of the risk of digital bullying and the involvement of parents, teachers, students, non-pedagogical staff and NGOs in this process.
2) Development, testing and impact analysis of the implementation of an integration model for building a secure digital environment for the development of adolescent IT competences and exploration of the digital space.
3) Broad publicity and unlocking public debate regarding providing a safe digital environment for adolescents, in which they have the opportunity to learn and build basic IT competences without becoming a victim of digital bullying, by improving communication in the school-child ecosystem parents.


<< Implementation >>

In its implementation, the ‘S@fe future’ project had the task of creating a safe and secure digital environment centered on the communication and learning needs of adolescents. For this purpose, we implemented the following work packages/activities:

1. Studies and sharing of experience and good practices in building a safe digital environment in the EU and partner countries, by: organizing focus groups; study of foreign experience and regulatory documents; exchange of experience;

2. Building sustainable mechanisms for increasing digital competences and limiting virtual bullying, through: Development and administration of an Inclusive Committee for digital protection in each of the partner schools; testing innovative techniques for conducting extracurricular lessons to develop digital competencies; organization of 6 thematic seminars; prepared a Strategy for digital safety in school education and an Action Plan for it.

3. Publicity of the identified problem and promotion of sustainable solutions - holding a Representative Conference at the end of the project.


<< Results >>

As specific results of the implementation of the project, we can indicate:
•	Prepared the Strategy for digital safety and limiting the language of hate in school education and a Plan for it
•	Development of Inclusive Digital Safeguarding Committees in participating schools to counter digital bullying and online hate speech.
•	Create a website - https://www.safe-future.eu/

Other achieved results of the activities:
•	Held focus groups with representatives of the target groups in the 4 schools in Bulgaria, Croatia, Turkey and Portugal.
•	Analysis of legislation and regulations, management and opportunities to create a safe digital environment for adolescent students in Turkey, Portugal, Croatia, Bulgaria and Poland.
•	Report of an online survey of good practices in the Netherlands, France and Germany.
•	Testing and adapting good practices following the example of Fundacja ECCC-Poland.
•	Organized 6 seminar trainings for students, teachers and parents.
•	Organizing 4 "The Human Library" meetings on "Safer Internet" day
•	Development of an anonymous mailbox - S@feBOX - for reporting digital harassment.
•	Ensured good publicity on the project topics.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-CZ01-KA220-SCH-000085763.title: The Welcoming Environment for Leading and Learning Project
2022-1-CZ01-KA220-SCH-000085763.summary:
<< Background >>

In the recent time, schools were confronted with a complex pack of challenges related to Covid-19 pandemic and war conflicts that resulted in migration and the necessity to accept pupils with a different mother tongue. In these rapidly changing societies, schools are under pressure to change. School leaders in partner countries are accountable for students´ and pupils´ learning outcomes, for teachers´ training and quality of teaching, for administration and reporting to the superior bodies, for budget and finance etc. There is also a growing demand for inclusive and multiculturally sensitive learning opportunities for increasingly diverse groups of students. School leaders need to master these new forms of pedagogy so that they can monitor and evaluate their teachers’ practice. Therefore, the partner defined the following areas of the school leaders´ needs that the project activities will address to: 
1. Vision and Plan definition.
2. Data and Resources utilisation. 
3. Techniques to empower teachers and cultivate leadership skills.
4. Making school a part of the Community.
5. Creating collaborative, inclusive learning environments.
6. Sustaining their enthusiasm and how to ignite the others.

<< Objectives >>

The school principals’ role is intensifying, the profession is ageing. Working conditions are often unattractive and partner countries are facing decreasing numbers of applications for principal positions. Deputy principals and teachers feel that the additional rewards offered to principals are too small to compensate for the large increase in workload. The partnership aimed at contributing to ease some of the school leaders’ tasks through:
1. Developing skills for effective school leadership and collaboration
2. Creating a network of institutions for future cooperation
3. Accessibility of improved and innovative materials for school leaders
4. Making school leadership an attractive profession
5. Creating a positive school environment where all pupils´/ students’ needs and talents are recognized and supported.
The main objectives of the project were:
• Increasing quality in the work, activities and practices of schools and institutions involved, opening to new actors locally and transnationally.
• Enabling transformation and change (at individual, organisational or sectoral level), leading to improvements and new approaches, in proportion to the context of each organisation.

<< Implementation >>

To achieve the above-mentioned objectives, we undertook the following steps:
1. We enabled exchange of good practice across the partner countries through training events thus upskilling school principals/other professionals. Each partner country organized a 3-day course aimed at effective leadership. Five training courses were delivered during the lifespan of the project. 
2. We created and maintained the project website (www.erasmus-thewell.eu) that offers good practice including a Methodology incorporating interventions, case studies and materials addressing the topic of effective leadership for inclusion.
3. We were collecting materials, good practice examples and doing research for the Methodology, through the exchange of good practice in partner countries, auditing, analysing and discussing what works well. 
4. We were continuously upskilling staff in partner countries. Participants who attended the learning activities then cascaded gained knowledge to their colleagues and managers inside and outside their organization. 
Of course, there was a robust system of the project management and organisation behind these concrete steps. Each partner appointed a project team that was supporting the project activities.  

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs we originally planned in the project application were as follows: 
1. Training Activities for School Leaders and other professionals in education. 
Result - 5 learning activities held, 200 school leaders upskilled to provide effective leadership. The task is completed.
2. Methodology on effective leadership for school leaders and educational managers.
Result - 1 Methodology issued in electronic versions in all partner languages. The task is completed.
3. The Well Project website (www.erasmus-thewell.eu), the main dissemination tool and a place of shared learning and experience.
Result - 1 website in all partner languages. The task is completed.
A positive outcome of our project, which we anticipated but did not initially include among the main project results, is the willingness and desire declared by all partner institutions to further collaborate on the training of school leaders, teachers and other education specialists in issues of modern pedagogy and approaches to creating a positive and safe school atmosphere. The contacts established during the project activities resulted in the preparation of a follow-up project application for the Erasmus+ Call 2025.

2022-1-CZ01-KA220-SCH-000086414.title: SUCCESS FOR EVERY CHILD in the virtual world and inclusion in the real world
2022-1-CZ01-KA220-SCH-000086414.summary:
<< Background >>

The priority was to create a safe environment that offer optimal conditions for every child without differences,so that they could experience success at school and develop their talents.The needs responded to the current situation,which reflected the consequences of distance education, brought problems in relationships and communication between kids,deepened the gap in digital literacy and highlighted the barriers faced by children from socially disadvantaged backgrounds.In recent years, migration has increased in Europe,which has brought additional challenges associated with the integration of children with different mother tongues.Therefore, the creation of an inclusive environment that would correspond to the specific needs of the wider community and respond to the current situation in schools became the most important need of the project.Inclusion should become an everyday reality and the project tried to set the conditions so that every child has access to quality education and can fully participate in school life.Emphasizing healthy relationships,open communication and promoting diversity,the project sought to make schools a place where every child can discover and develop their potential in a safe and supportive environment

<< Objectives >>

1 goal was a thorough focus on relationships and to analyze how individual procedures are interconnected in creating a safe environment. Bullying prevention must be seriously and systematically incorporated into schools.We strived for comprehensive strategies that won´t focus on consistent prevention,which includes  implementing adaptation stays.Goal of teaching kids with a different mother tongue was to support their language development and integration,which includes learning a new language,but also respecting and maintaining cultural identity.We  tried to raise awareness about the pitfalls that come with the virtual world.In an increasingly digitized society,it´s essential that kids understand not only the benefits but also the risks of online interactions.We support kids' digital skills,which will enable them to safely navigate the digital environment.We focused on education about safe behavior on social networks,privacy protection and ability to recognize dangerous situations in online space.Goals included training for teachers so that they too could adequately respond to kids' questions and concerns.Project aimed to improve climate and integrate prevention across schools,with aim of ensuring a safe,supportive lear.enviroment

<< Implementation >>

Activities contributed to creating a safe environment in schools.It was carried out by the staff of school counseling offices from all schools,through a model adaptation stay in the CR, in which teachers and kids participated.Implementation of adaptation stays led to creation of brochure with procedures and programs.Project included mapping of socially disadvantaged kids,preparation of a methodical booklet as inspiration for schools.Other activity was language cafes,whose programs were collected in brochure of examples of good practice.Meeting in Croatia focused on sharing experiences with language cafes. Pictograms serving as guidelines for safe behavior in the virtual world and related activities were created,which were tested in teaching and supported IT security, which was presented at meeting in Portugal.Project also included methodical support against bullying,where various programs for the school environment were developed.Results of the bullying questionnaires provided valuable data from schools.Teacher training and meeting in Spain stimulated the exchange of best practices,that contributing to project's improvement in school climate and safety.In Latvia, there was a final conference to disseminate the results to community

<< Results >>

The project produced outputs that positively influenced the school environment. Among the key outputs are the realization of adaptation stays, which enabled teachers and pupils to strengthen ties in class groups through various activities. During the meeting in the Czech Republic, a model adaptation stay was presented, where teachers and students actively participated in various activities. The developed almanac of adaptation stay programs and a handbook aimed at children from socially disadvantaged backgrounds contain best practices and inspiration for other schools. Another output is the language cafes, which made it possible to overcome language barriers and were documented in the almanac of examples of good practice. The meeting in Croatia promoted the sharing of experiences and activities related to these cafes. The emphasis on digital safety and the created pictograms for safe movement in the virtual world made it easier for students and teachers to understand this issue. Preventive programs against bullying, developed in cooperation with five European schools, contributed to the creation of a positive school climate.

2022-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000086238.title: iREFLECT! - Reflexivität für eine zeitgemäße Lehrkräfteaus- und -weiterbildung
2022-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000086238.summary:
<< Background >>

The iREFLECT project was developed to promote the systematic development of reflective competence as a fundamental key competence for professional pedagogical practice in all three phases of teacher training. Reflection forms the essential link between theoretical knowledge and practical application and is crucial for the continuous professionalisation of teachers.
We identified the need for a cross-phase approach that takes into account all three phases of teacher training: university education, teaching practice and professional practice. In each of these phases, prospective and experienced teachers need structured tools for reflecting on their pedagogical practice in order to further develop their practical skills – especially in the current era of constant change.
The project also responded to the need for practical, flexible reflection tools that can be used in both initial and continuing teacher training. The European dimension made it possible to include different education systems and cultures and to learn from each other. Through this learning, a toolkit was developed that takes heterogeneity into account.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of iREFLECT was to develop an innovative, scientifically sound and field-tested set of tools for the systematic promotion of reflective competence in teacher training. Specifically, we aimed to develop a comprehensive toolkit that integrates various reflection methods, processes and communication approaches and can be used flexibly for different target groups and contexts.
We wanted to create a set of cards that would offer teachers structured stimuli for reflection processes in all phases of teacher training, while at the same time being methodologically diverse and learner-centred. A central concern was to combine theoretical foundations with practical applicability, thereby contributing to the professionalisation of teacher training.
In addition, we pursued the goal of making the project results available as OER in order to enable broad, free use. Multilingual availability was intended to promote dissemination in various European education systems.
Another goal was multiplication through dissemination activities and training events in the network structures of the project partners.

<< Implementation >>

The iREFLECT project comprised a variety of coordinated activities for the development, testing and dissemination of the reflection toolkit. The focus was on the collaborative development of the iREFLECT card set by all six partner institutions, incorporating different educational contexts and traditions. Six face-to-face project meetings were held, during which visits and exchanges with local education experts enabled learning from differences.
For testing and further development, we conducted extensive workshops and lectures in all partner countries. In total, we carried out over 60 dissemination activities with 2,413 participants. These activities ranged from local workshops to national conferences and international conferences.
Special dissemination activities included presentations at BUKO 25, TCA Munich, the Erasmus+ annual conference in Bonn and DIPS 25 in Valencia. We also integrated the toolkit into existing training structures.
The project results were prepared as OER in five languages and published on the Erasmus+ platform. A scientific publication in the journal Schulverwaltung (School Administration) further ensures visibility.

<< Results >>

The central result is the iREFLECT toolkit with a comprehensive set of 61 cards: 30 cards on reflection methods, 7 on reflection processes, 6 on communication methods and 18 impulse cards with ‘powerful questions’. This scientifically based instrument enables a variety of methodological approaches.
A key result was the intensive examination of reflexivity in an educational context by all six partner institutions. The collaborative development deepened the understanding of different approaches to reflection in various European educational cultures.
The toolkit was published as an OER in five languages on the Erasmus+ platform and is available free of charge under a Creative Commons licence. In addition, a booklet and a digital LOGINEO version were produced.
The project results were successfully anchored in the institutions. The dissemination activities, with over 60 events and 2,413 participants, exceeded expectations. Participants actively engaged with reflexivity and tested the methods in their own practice. Recognition – including through a specialist article in ZS Schulverwaltung – ensures sustainable.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2022-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000088061.title: Mentoring elementary students and teachers about CONSENT
2022-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000088061.summary:
<< Background >>

Die Entscheidung, sich an diesem Projekt zu beteiligen, wurde von der dringenden Notwendigkeit motiviert, geschlechtsspezifische Gewalt (GBV) zu bekämpfen und die Gleichstellung der Geschlechter in Europa und darüber hinaus voranzutreiben. Daten aus den Partnerländern verdeutlichten sowohl das Ausmaß geschlechtsspezifischer Gewalt und Geschlechterungleichheit als auch den dringenden Bedarf an gemeinsamen Anstrengungen, um diese Herausforderungen durch Bildung, Sensibilisierung und politische Maßnahmen anzugehen. Das Projekt bot eine wertvolle Gelegenheit, innovative Instrumente zur Bewältigung dieser systemischen Probleme zu entwickeln, zu verbreiten und umzusetzen – Probleme, die Frauen und marginalisierte Gruppen unverhältnismäßig stark betreffen. Im Folgenden analysieren wir die spezifischen Bedürfnisse, die in den einzelnen Partnerländern identifiziert wurden, und erläutern, wie das Projekt diese gezielt anzugehen plante.

<< Objectives >>

Das Message CONSENT-Projekt wurde mit einer klaren Zielsetzung entwickelt, die im Einklang mit den übergeordneten Zielen steht, geschlechtsspezifische Gewalt (GBV) zu bekämpfen und Gleichstellung durch Bildung zu fördern. Als 24-monatige KA220-Initiative im Bereich der Schulbildung zielte das Projekt darauf ab, Grundschullehrerinnen und -lehrer zu beraten und zu stärken, indem sie mit innovativen Werkzeugen und Methoden ausgestattet wurden, um Kindern im Alter von 8 bis 12 Jahren Konsens (Consent) als Lebenskompetenz zu vermitteln. Durch die Integration von Consent Education in die Menschenrechtsbildung (HRE) strebte das Projekt an, eine Grundlage für persönliche Grenzen, Respekt und Kommunikation zu schaffen und gleichzeitig breitere gesellschaftliche Herausforderungen wie Mobbing, Belästigung und GBV anzugehen. Um dies zu erreichen, verfolgte das Projekt folgende Ziele:
Lehrkräfte und Pädagog:innen mit Fähigkeiten und Methoden zur Vermittlung von Konsens ausstatten (SO1)
Interaktive und kindgerechte Unterrichtsmaterialien bereitstellen (SO2)
Geschlechtsspezifische Gewalt durch sichere und unterstützende soziale Räume verhindern (SO3)
Das Wohlbefinden und die mentale Gesundheit von Kindern und Lehrkräften fördern (SO4) 

<< Implementation >>

Das Message Consent-Projekt führte eine umfassende Reihe von Aktivitäten durch, um seine Ziele zu erreichen: die Verhinderung von geschlechtsspezifischer Gewalt (GBV), die Ausstattung von Pädagog:innen mit Werkzeugen zur effektiven Vermittlung von Konsens sowie die Förderung einer Kultur des Respekts und der Empathie in der Grundschulbildung. Nachfolgend finden Sie eine detaillierte Übersicht der zentralen im Rahmen des Projekts durchgeführten Aktivitäten:
Entwicklung des Message Consent Handbuchs: https://messageconsent.eu/activities/
Erarbeitung von erlebnisorientierten Unterrichtsplänen:https://messageconsent.eu/activities/
Entwicklung der digitalen Lernplattform Message Consent (WP3 und WP4): https://hub.messageconsent.eu/
Durchführung von Fokusgruppen zur Bedarfsanalyse und Feedbacksammlung: 
Trainings- und Kapazitätsaufbau-Aktivitäten wie Workshops, Schulungssitzungen, interaktive Seminare und Pilotversuche
Sensibilisierung für Konsensbildung, indem eine breite Zielgruppe angesprochen wurde, darunter Lehrkräfte, Pädagog:innen, Eltern und Kinder
 Validierung der Projektergebnisse durch zyklische interne Überprüfung und externes Feedback

<< Results >>

Das Message CONSENT-Projekt erzielte zahlreiche greifbare und immaterielle Ergebnisse, indem Partner und Interessengruppen in eine kohärente Struktur von Aktivitäten und Ergebnissen eingebunden wurden. Nachfolgend finden Sie eine umfassende Übersicht:
Projektmanagement und Koordination (WP1)Effektiver Rahmen für das Projektmanagement, Partnerschaftsvereinbarungen
Handbuch und Unterrichtspläne für erlebnisorientiertes Lernen (WP2); Analyse und Sammlung von 35 Best Practices; Entwicklung des Message Consent Handbuchs, Entwicklung von 7 erlebnisorientierten Unterrichtsplänen;Durchführung von 7 Fokusgruppen-Interviews (WP2). Message Consent Digital Learning Hub und interaktive Schulungsmodule (WP3), Konzeption und Implementierung eines Digital Learning Hubs
Entwicklung von 21 Schulungsmodulen (Mikro-Lerneinheiten),Kapazitätsaufbau-Aktivitäten für Fachkräfte und Pilotbericht (WP4)
WP4-A1: Pilottraining des Personals – LTTA-Aktivität,WP4-A2: Empfehlungen und Anpassung der Materialien – 6 Fokusgruppen-Interviews; WP4-A3: 7 lokale Schulungen für Fachkräfte; Zusätzliche Pläne und Maßnahmen:Plan zur Evaluation und Qualitätssicherung,Plan für Nachhaltigkeit und Nutzung der Ergebnisse,Verbreitungs- und Kommunikationsplan, 2TPMs, 7Multiplyeven

2022-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000086363.title: Security and Privacy in Academic Data management At Schools
2022-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000086363.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to address the urgent need to protect student data in an increasingly digital education system. As schools adopt cloud-based technologies, we saw the necessity to raise awareness and provide guidance on data fragility, privacy, and security, especially in primary and secondary education. We aimed to raise awareness, share good practices, and develop tools to improve data literacy, privacy, and secure data management in schools.

We addressed the need to understand and manage the risks of using cloud-based EdTech, including privacy breaches, data misuse, and loss of control over student data by: raising awareness of data fragility among all educational stakeholders; equipping schools with tools to manage student data responsibly; enhancing digital and data literacy of teachers and school leaders; promoting safe, ethical, and legal data practices; supporting GDPR compliance.

<< Objectives >>

The project aims to raise data fragility awareness to representatives, teachers, and students to promote data treatment good practices. The objectives of the project are:

1.- Help schools understand the implications of data-driven decision-making in cloud-based educational environments.
1.1.- Expose to schools which problems about data fragility are related to current educational technology and data academic management.
1.2.- Raise awareness of data fragility issues such as data leaks, misuse, and unauthorized transfers.
1.3.- Train teachers and conduct workshops for school representatives, educators, and students on digital privacy and security.
2.- Provide tools and resources to protect the privacy, security, and confidentiality of students’ data.
2.1- Collect and publicly share good practices on students' data academic management.

<< Implementation >>

In our project, we implemented the following key activities:

- Build an open auto-assessment tool to raise awareness about data fragility and help detect privacy gaps in data academic treatment.
- Conduct teacher training and workshops at schools to spread data fragility issues and raise awareness.
- Edit a handbook of good practices as a resource to help improve students' data privacy, security, and confidentiality treatment processes.
- Develop an interactive web platform to publish the good practices of the handbook.


<< Results >>

The project delivered several concrete outputs, which are accessible at https://spadatas.eu/kit/, as follows:

- An open and public auto-assessment web tool to help primary and secondary schools detect privacy gaps and raise awareness about data fragility.
- A handbook of good practices and a set of Open Educational Resources (OERs) to support schools in managing student data in line with the GDPR.
- A searchable and interactive website to host and share the handbook and other results.
- Different applications and websites were developed to raise awareness about data fragility and support the protection of students' personal data.
- A Zenodo.org community was created to host additional open-access content (https://zenodo.org/communities/spadatas).

These outputs aim to enhance the understanding and implementation of data privacy, security, and confidentiality in academic settings. All resources are open-access and targeted at educational staff working with students’ personal data.

2022-1-FI01-KA220-SCH-000086671.title: STEPs Towards Ecological Planet
2022-1-FI01-KA220-SCH-000086671.summary:
<< Background >>

Climate change is already causing a wide range of impacts. These climate impacts threaten both the environment and our society. The EU aims to be climate neutral in 2050. The schools have a vital role in educating the students to be aware of the prevailing situation and the threats it poses to the world we are living in. The partner schools strongly needed a transnational cooperation to promote subjects such as: green skills awareness and development, sharing best practices among teachers, promoting ecological behavior and raising the awareness in our communities.  
During the project period, students were all the time in the center of activities both at the local and transnational level. The partner schools aimed at active students' participation and reached it well. The educational staff and managers of the partners also cooperated with parents and NGOs to encourage the students in reaching the goals of the project.  
Our project wanted to provide new opportunities to the staff and students to develop their foreign language skills through working with their European peers and colleagues on the mobilities and E-Twinning platform. Learning languages enables people to both discover foreign cultures and to broaden their perspectives

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were:  
O1: To raise both students’ and teachers' awareness and knowledge of the environmental issues and provide them with skills to change their behavior permanently, and starting from partner schools gradually promote this change in our communities by disseminating the outcomes of the project activities.  
O2: To provide access to the best practices of environmental education in other partner schools and apply these in our own education  
03: To help the students make decisions on their lifestyles to make it greener & healthier and more sustainable, thus helping them to leave a cleaner world to future generations by using the knowledge gained through the project activities.  
O4: To encourage students to stand up for and take action for the environment.  
O5: To promote the students' skills to cooperate with their peers on the subject matters of the project and thus help them to develop their foreign language and ICT skills and to understand their roles as active European citizens in a common European community.  
06: To encourage tolerance among pupils and educational staff coming from different cultures. 


<< Implementation >>

In order to achieve our goals we had a teacher training course, 2 TPMs and 4 LTTAs.  
Joint activities were organized locally and a project website was published. During the mobilities we had activities such as workshops, educational activities, field visits, meetings and information seminars, in which teachers and students gained insight regarding the project objectives. An eTwinning project was also carried out throughout the project. 


<< Results >>

As the main outcome we believe to have provided a permanent change in individuals' behavior to preserve the earth for new generations. Our students are aware of the limited resources of the earth and  capable of taking the essential action as environmentally literate citizens. In addition, we provided the participating schools with good practices in environmental education and published a handbook of educational activities as an outcome of this project. It is a Good practices collection, which includes 12 activities focusing on ecological literacy, climate change and sustainability issues. Thanks to LTTA activities, concrete outputs were developed, such as: Climate Summit presentations, Carbon Footprint calculations, Climate Change Escape Game, Articles, etc.

2022-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000085147.title: Enhancing secondary school STEM teaching and learning through the implementation of student-curated art-based exhibitions, utilizing methods of co-creation
2022-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000085147.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to this project in response to the urgent need to integrate STEM education into teacher training with a focus on eco-numerical skills, exhibitions, and co-creation. In the face of environmental challenges and technological advances, it's essential to equip teachers with innovative, interdisciplinary approaches. We identified several needs: a lack of training on integrating STEM into education in an engaging way, a lack of adapted and accessible teaching resources, and the need to harmonize educational practices on a European scale. The project aimed to transform STEM education by integrating interactive methods that foster student engagement and teacher skills development. Through the co-creation of exhibitions, the use of digital tools and the implementation of the Phygital Guide, STEM Virtual Toolkit and E-book, teachers were given access to concrete resources for adapting their teaching to today's challenges. Interdisciplinary collaboration between researchers, teachers and artists has enriched educational practices and stimulated students' interest in science.

<< Objectives >>

We have implemented this project to achieve several objectives:
Facilitate the integration of co-creation in STEM learning: Thanks to the pedagogical e-book and the toolbox composed of 3 modules and 9 sub-modules totaling 32 videos, 24 infographics and 9 quizzes, we wanted to diversify and enrich the pedagogical content to help students and teachers better understand STEM subjects.
Stimulate student and teacher engagement: The aim was to make learning more interactive and attractive, by actively involving students in creating content and organizing exhibitions. 
Offer practical resources: With a phygital guide, we provided information, advice and sources to help teachers and students integrate these innovative pedagogical approaches.
Introducing an innovative teaching method: Using student co-creation of exhibits, we aimed to make STEM learning more collaborative and active.
Thus, our main objective was to introduce an innovative pedagogical method for teaching STEM by actively involving students and making learning more accessible and engaging.

<< Implementation >>

To achieve the defined objectives, the activities carried out include tool development, co-creation with experts, testing and global dissemination:
The development of the e-book, Virtual Toolkit and Phygital Guide, translated into five languages, disseminated widely and adopted in various educational contexts have enabled teachers and students to design engaging and interactive STEM exhibits.
We conducted pilot tests in 5 partner countries through the implementation of Living Labs, SACs and school-based interventions offering hands-on experiences to over 110 students and 60 teachers. These initiatives demonstrated the applicability and replicability of the tools, while promoting an active and innovative pedagogical approach. The feedback has enabled us to improve the Beta versions developed in the 3 WPs and finalize the Alpha version. In addition, the IA board provided us with feedback from experts.
Finally, the dissemination events and the publication of the 3 results in Open Access on the project website guarantee a lasting impact beyond the official duration of the project. Its online accessibility enables widespread adoption and encourages the replication of best practices on a European scale.

<< Results >>

STEM-Xhibitions has enabled the creation of an educational e-book, a virtual toolbox and a phygital guide, translated into the five languages of the partners. Activities such as SACs, Livins Labs and interviews were also carried out. Pilot tests were organized in the five partner countries to present the project results to stakeholders. Our results were tested and adopted by the partner high schools (GLPK and IVANEC) as well as by two French schools, Collège Jules Verne and Lycée Jacques Vaucanson. The final event was attended by 65 participants (KPI:50), including the head of international relations at the Mairie des Mureaux.
Final evaluation reports revealed that, on average, 93.87% of participants rated each question above 7/10, with an overall score of 8.9/10 for the STEM Virtual Toolkit. Through our communications and website, our solutions have been consulted by users in 75 countries worldwide. The top ten countries in terms of engagement are France, Greece, Croatia, Cyprus, Serbia, Pakistan, Japan, the UK, Bosnia-Herzegovina and Italy, in that order.

2022-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000085607.title: Science Technology Engineering, Arts and Mathematics to Tackle Polarisation in Schools and the Community
2022-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000085607.summary:
<< Background >>

L'école, à l'instar de la société, est amenée à relever plusieurs défis en termes de cohésion et d'intégration sociale. Notre établissement scolaire, situé en zone rurale, accueille une part croissante d'élèves à besoins spécifiques (16%) ainsi que d'élèves nouvellement arrivés en France (3%). La communauté éducative est ainsi confrontée à la problématique de l'inclusion de ces publics au sein de la classe, de l'établissement mais aussi de leur environnement social, culturel et professionnel. 
3 lycées professionnels en France, Croatie et Turquie, 2 associations en Bulgarie, Pologne et 1 centre de formation à Chypre mobilisés autour de ces enjeux se sont associés au sein du projet STEAM to Tackle Polarisation in Schools and the Community. 
Le projet s'est proposé de répondre aux besoins des éducateurs souhaitant développer des démarches inclusives et émancipatrices pour des jeunes éloignés des apprentissages. L'approche STEAM nous a semblé pertinente parce qu'elle permet aux jeunes de développer les compétences du 21ème siècle, comprenant notamment la collaboration, la résolution de problèmes, la pensée critique et la créativité tout en leur apportant des connaissances en sciences, technologie, ingénierie,  arts et mathématiques.

<< Objectives >>

L'objectif principal de ce projet était pédagogique, le but étant de promouvoir l'approche STEAM, à la fois interdisciplinaire et transdisciplinaire dans des structures, écoles ou associations, en charge de l’éducation des jeunes et à la recherche de démarches favorisant à la fois l'intégration et l’inclusion au sein de groupes d’apprenants. Pour faciliter l'appropriation de la démarche STEAM, les partenaires ont choisi de créer des outils accessibles et utilisables rapidement par les enseignants, les formateurs et les éducateurs et porteurs de réussite pour les apprenants. Les résultats escomptés étaient d’abord pour chacun des 6 partenaires l’appropriation de la démarche STEAM, l’utilisation des outils créés, l’évaluation des résultats et, dans un second temps, la capacité pour eux d’accompagner dans le développement de la démarche STEAM d’autres structures de leur territoire. 
Le deuxième objectif était de constituer un collectif de structures très différentes, établissements scolaires et associations, capables de s’enrichir de leur expérience différente dans l’accompagnement des populations en difficulté. Ceci pour poursuivre la réflexion engagée autour de l’approche STEAM au-delà du projet et fédérer d'autres structures.

<< Implementation >>

La promotion de l’approche STEAM s’est concrétisée par la création collective d’un MOOC regroupant les activités d’apprentissage créées  : exercices favorisant la cohésion de groupe, tutoriels concernant l'utilisation des nouvelles technologies, formations entre pairs. La mise en place d'ateliers a permis ensuite de tester ces contenus en situation avec différents types de publics cibles : apprenants en difficulté ou en situation de handicap, jeunes décrochés du système scolaire ou encore réfugiés. La communication du projet auprès d’autres acteurs éducatifs – centres de formation pour adultes éloignés de l’emploi, collectivités territoriales dans le cadre de leurs projets à visée sociale, associations d’éducation populaire, parents -  a contribué à la promotion de l'approche STEAM. 
Le collectif s'est construit grâce à des réunions transnationales réunissant les partenaires autour de la découverte des spécificités sociétales de chacun et du travail concret de création collaborative des outils et ateliers de mise en œuvre de la démarche STEAM. Les réunions régulières en visio entre les partenaires ont permis une réelle appropriation de la démarche STEAM  et une expertise permettant l'accompagnement d'autres structures éducatives.

<< Results >>

- La création d'un MOOC en open source pour les enseignants, formateurs et éducateurs  a été réalisée avec les contenus suivants :  un cours sur l'utilisation des STEAM dans le cadre des projets éducatifs visant l'intégration et l'inclusion "Using Steam Education to tackle polarisation",  un cours sur l'utilisation des STEAM par les acteurs des territoires "Tackle polarisation in real life : a community based learning approach", une démarche d'apprentissage de la photographie et de l'élaboration de films, un kit d'utilisation d'outils numérique visant à faciliter la communication. 
- La mise en œuvre  d'ateliers STEAM avec les publics cibles a permis une expérimentation en situation : un moodle pour les apprenants, la réalisation d'un film par des élèves, la création d'une web radio, d'un plateau Web TV par les élèves et d'une exposition photo , des ateliers "hands-on STEAM activities" au Microsoft Innovation Centre, un séminaire socratique.
- Un réseau d'éducateurs, de formateurs, d'enseignants, de responsables des politiques locales d'éducation s'est créé grâce au travail de communication des partenaires auprès des média locaux et des réseaux sociaux.
- De nouveaux partenariats locaux ont vu le jour autour de la démarche STEAM.

2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000085554.title: Digital Interculturalism
2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000085554.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the urgent need for fostering intercultural competence, enhancing civic engagement, and developing digital literacy among students. The project addressed several key needs crucial in today’s interconnected, multicultural, and digitalized world:  
1. Intercultural Competence Development Students often lack the skills to communicate and adapt in diverse environments. The project aimed to promote understanding, tolerance, and empathy, overcoming prejudices and fostering cultural harmony.  
2. Adaptation to Globalization: Globalization has made cultural adaptation essential. The project provided opportunities for students to experience different cultures firsthand and view diversity as a unifying strength. 
3. Building Cultural Harmony: Modern societies need individuals who value differences while finding common ground. The project fostered respect for varied lifestyles, values, and perspectives. 
4. Psychological and Sociocultural Adaptation: Students needed support in developing emotional and behavioral skills for smoother integration into multicultural settings. 
5. Digital Skills and Citizenship: Digitalization requires students to use technology effectively for intercultural communication.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to enhance participants' intercultural competence, fostering awareness and appreciation of cultural differences while promoting European citizenship and values. Through creative drama activities, the project sought to help participants explore their own cultural identity, develop empathy, and adopt a balanced, tolerant attitude toward differences and conflict.  
Participants were encouraged to communicate and interact with individuals from diverse backgrounds, understand others' perspectives, and recognize cultural diversity as a shared heritage to protect and pass on to future generations. These activities aimed to nurture emotional intelligence, self-awareness, and the ability to empathize, laying the foundation for harmonious coexistence in a multicultural world.  
Additionally, we sought to develop participants' digital skills and motivate them to learn foreign languages, using engaging methods that promote active participation. The ultimate goal was to equip participants with the knowledge, attitudes, and skills necessary to become inclusive, active digital citizens while creating a guidebook to disseminate these practices.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented several key activities to promote intercultural competence and digital skills:
1. Creative Drama Modules: explored cultural similarities and differences through museum visits, fostering an understanding of shared social values, used food culture to express emotions, reduce prejudice, and understand diverse cultures, focused on conflict resolution through traditional games and sports, highlighting the cultural significance of these activities, promoted tolerance and empathy through music and dance, encouraging cultural understanding, used street culture to develop empathy and tolerance for ambiguity, exploring modern cultural expressions.
2. Digital Engagement: Ss created digital content (posters, videos) using Web 2.0 tools, reflecting on cultural experiences, our eTwinning project connected schools virtually, enabling distant participants to engage, pre- and post-activity evaluations were conducted using GForms to measure intercultural competence development.
3. Cross-Border Mobilities: Ss and Ts engaged in international exchanges, immersing themselves in hands-on cultural experiences.
4. Guidebook: an ebook was produced, incorporating drama activities to enhance cognitive, emotional, and behavioral skills. 

<< Results >>

1. Ebook on Intercultural Competence:  
   - A comprehensive guidebook, containing five modules based on creative drama applications, focuses on improving cognitive, emotional, and behavioral skills to foster intercultural competence. The guidebook serves as a valuable resource for educators and can be used to implement intercultural learning activities in schools. 
2. Digital Content:  
   - Ss created various digital materials, including posters, videos, and presentations, using Web 2.0 tools. These materials summarized their experiences and reflections on cultural diversity, which were shared on the project’s website and social media platforms. 
3. eTwinning Project:  
   - An eTwinning project was established, allowing schools to collaborate virtually and to share outputs.
4. Increased Digital and Language Skills:
The project improved Ss' digital literacy through the use of Web 2.0 tools and their involvement in virtual activities. Students also gained language skills by collaborating with peers from different countries
5. Dissemination: results were shared widely through social media, the project website, and local dissemination activities. This allowed other schools and educational communities to benefit from the resources.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000085807.title: VR/WE ARE - Modernizacija i unapređenje kvalitete nastavnog procesa primjenom tehnologija virtualne stvarnosti
2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000085807.summary:
<< Background >>

The idea for this project came from the desire to offer students something new and interesting. As they had already mastered programming and making 2D and 3D models in the optional IT course, the idea of ​​including VR technology in the teaching came up, which would thus become more dynamic, interesting, interactive and interdisciplinary. By talking with the school management, fellow teachers and students, and later by conducting a survey, it became clear that there is interest in interdisciplinary and interactive teaching that uses VR technology, both among teachers and among students. Since the idea is of high quality and could enrich not only our school curriculum, but also that of other organizations, it was expanded into an Erasmus+ project proposal. 
The needs that we addressed are the need for a new subject curriculum adapted to the needs and interests of students for 3D modeling and the use of VR technology, the need to create new teaching materials (virtual 3D models) for interactive teaching of different types, the need to develop students' digital skills and teachers, the need for an interdisciplinary approach to teaching and the need to provide equal opportunities to students with fewer opportunities.

<< Objectives >>

The goals were to introduce an interdisciplinary approach to teaching through the use of IT technology and 3D models that are created in computer science classes, based on the templates of teachers of other subjects (geography, fine arts, English, biology, mathematics, later and others). We wanted to increase the quality of teaching due to the introduction of new methods and forms of work through an interdisciplinary approach and the application of VR technology. The goals were to increase the competences of teachers (they learned how to use VR technology and include interdisciplinarity in their teaching, which will encourage mutual cooperation among teachers) and to increase the competences of students (how to make virtual 3D models, use VR technology, i.e. the development of digital skill). The goal was to motivate students to participate more actively in classes, to strive for personal and professional development, to become motivated to learn, and in the case of the Portuguese partner organization, as a result, students leave school less often. There is also an emphasis on eliminating differences in access and use of digital technologies for underrepresented groups, i.e. students from rural and economically weaker areas.

<< Implementation >>

We included the following activities in the project: teacher education on the use of VR technology in classes (switching on/off, how to access content, how to move through the selected 3d model, maintenance of VR glasses - how to store them, charge them, etc.); education of students on the use of VR glasses and 3d modeling (students learned about the user interface of tools, tools for manipulating 3D models, basic tools for modeling in 3D space, tools for creating and applying 2D textures, and the basics of 3D animation (rotation, translation, scaling)) ; creation of 3D models (a total of 19 models were created, of which 5 were determined by the project application and the other 10 were agreed upon by the partners at the beginning of the project, and each partner created one more model for added value to the project); creation of a manual on 3d modeling and the use of VR glasses; testing of created 3d models; development of the curriculum for the course on 3D modeling; analysis of project results; dissemination activities

<< Results >>

The concrete results of the project are created virtual 3D models, a total of nineteen of them, a digital manual for creating 3D models and the use of VR glasses that partners and other related organizations can use in classes. The project resulted in a new curriculum for optional computer science classes on 3D modeling and the use of VR technology. The handbook and curriculum are published on the project page on the TwinSpace platform.
As a result of the implemented project activities, the knowledge and competence of students and teachers increased. All students who directly participated in the project learned how to use VR glasses (switching on/off, how to access contents, how to move through the selected 3d model, maintenance of VR glasses - how to store them, charge them, etc.), all students got to know at least with the basics of 3D modeling, and students from all partner organizations who were previously involved in additional computer science classes or showed an interest in 3D modeling have mastered it at a level where they can be independent. All involved teachers learned to use the VR glasses in the manner described by the students.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000086061.title: Minecraft for AI and Coding Introduction in Primary Schools
2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000086061.summary:
<< Background >>

Our Minecraft Erasmus+ project tackles critical education gaps in Europe. We aim to equip future generations with essential skills: coding and AI. Coding underpins the digital world (Victoria, 2021) and fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and collaboration (Kaplancali et al., 2017). Despite high demand, the EU faces a programmer shortage (CBI Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 2021). AI in education is booming (https://bit.ly/366iB9h), promising a "fourth education revolution" (Seldon & Abidoye, 2018) with a profound impact on children (Gray, 2020).

Our project bridged these needs. Through Minecraft, we introduce young students to coding in a fun and interactive way, sparking interest in programming careers. We also connected AI and coding to Minecraft game based learning, familiarizing children with basic AI principles. Additionally, our created project resources can upskill teachers and digitize education. The project outcomes equip children with vital future skills, support teachers with new quality resources, and promotes game based learning with Minecraft education, making a significant impact on young learners and the therefore the EU's workforce.

<< Objectives >>

The AI-COSMIC project aimed to equip primary school students with basic coding skills and familiarity with AI principles through engaging Minecraft activities. These activities were built around the "AI Five Big Ideas," ensuring a strong foundation in key concepts like learning, creativity, computational thinking, and problem-solving with Minecraft built in AI.
The project also empowered teachers by educating them on AI and coding fundamentals, enhancing their ability to integrate these skills into engaging lessons using digital tools. This created a more dynamic learning environment for students and equipped teachers with the confidence to lead the way in this evolving educational landscape.
The project promoted game-based learning across subjects like mathematics and ICT. Minecraft's worlds became a platform for applying coding concepts, making learning not just effective but also fun and interactive.
We developed an accreditation system for each game's coding skills for primary schools. The "AI-COSMIC BADGES" provided a tangible recognition of student achievement, motivating them to continue developing their coding skills and fostering a sense of accomplishment.

<< Results >>

The AI-COSMIC project delivers a comprehensive toolkit for integrating AI and coding into primary education through Minecraft Education Edition.
