2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000089643.title: Transition to Primary School
2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000089643.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the critical challenges children face during the transition from early childhood education (ECEC) to primary school, a period that significantly impacts their future academic success. These challenges were not only visible to our ECEC educators and persisting throughout the years, they were also appearing in different EU countries, exhibiting a universal issue. We aimed to tackle the need for a structured, holistic, and cooperative educational approach that supports a smooth transition between these educational stages. Specifically, we focused on reducing the stress and adjustment difficulties that children, particularly those from disadvantaged backgrounds, often experience during this transition.

Our project responded to key gaps, including the lack of structured programs for kindergarten teachers to support school readiness, the absence of pedagogical and curricular continuity between ECEC and primary education, and the insufficient collaboration between teachers, schools, and parents. By addressing these needs, we aimed to ensure a smoother transition experience, reduce potential negative outcomes such as school failure and dropout, and promote inclusion and continuity for all children.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to achieve several key outcomes - our main objective (MO) was to transform the transition from pre- to primary school into a creative and positive experience for children, replacing the stress often associated with this phase. By doing so we sought to foster happy, confident, and collaborative children who were better prepared to navigate their new educational environment. To accomplish this, we focused on several specific objectives:

SO1. Supporting children's readiness: We aimed to equip children with the necessary skills to face the challenges of transitioning to primary school. 
SO2. Bridging the gap between pre- and primary school: We intended to create continuity between these two educational stages by developing an innovative transitional curriculum. 
SO3. Involving the entire school community: We aimed to engage all members of the pre-school and primary school communities, including parents, to build a supportive environment for children.
SO4. Leveraging digital tools for cooperation: We sought to utilize digital platforms to foster cooperation among pre-primary and primary staff and parents. 

Ultimately, we aimed to fill this gap and equip children with essential competences to thrive in their transition.

<< Implementation >>

In the UPSTAIRS project, we implemented several key activities aligned with specific objectives to support children’s smooth transition from pre-school to primary school.

WP1: Project Management ensured the coordinated execution of all tasks and effective resource management to keep the project on track. (MO)

WP2: Preparing the Soil for Smooth Transition focused on research and preparation, gathering insights to develop a framework that promoted children’s emotional well-being, independence, and resilience for primary school readiness. (SO2)

WP3: Building the Framework for Continuity developed an innovative transitional curriculum, bridging the gap between pre-school and primary school through pedagogical continuity and collaboration between educators. (SO1, SO2)

WP4: Digital Common Space created a platform for parents, early childhood educators, and primary school teachers to collaborate, providing resources to support children, especially those from disadvantaged backgrounds. (SO4)

WP5: Sustainability and Impact focused on ensuring the long-term use and impact of project outcomes, engaging policymakers, and developing strategies for scaling the tools and methodologies. (SO3)

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results of the UPSTAIRS project were significant in achieving the project's objectives. We produced several key deliverables:

Transition Readiness Framework: This included separate Guidelines and good practices, particularly focusing on the inclusion of disadvantaged children, to support emotional well-being and the development of adaptation and resilience skills for the transition to primary school.

Transitional curriculum for ECEC: We developed an innovative curriculum designed to bridge the gap between pre- and primary school, fostering pedagogical continuity.

UPSTAIRS digital space: This platform served as a collaborative space for educators and parents, housing a repository of resources, including activities and tips, while establishing a European community for ongoing collaboration.

Training and workshops: We conducted 3 LTTAs, 8 workshops, and 7 pilot programs to validate and refine the results of the project.

Dissemination: To maximize impact, we organized 7 multiplier events, 2 transnational conferences, and implemented social media campaigns to promote the project’s findings and tools.

These outputs ensured both the immediate effectiveness of the project and its long-term sustainability.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000089732.title: Media and Information Literacy: Learning to Think Critically
2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000089732.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the growing impact of online disinformation on young people, influencing their decisions on health, democracy, and social issues. The rapid spread of misinformation, especially via digital media, highlights the urgent need for media and information literacy in schools. Our goal was to equip students with critical thinking, problem-solving, decision-making, teamwork, ICT, and communication skills to navigate digital content responsibly. 
Aligned with the Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027) and the Media Services Directive (AVMSD), our project supported digital transformation in schools and the fight against harmful content. While EU countries implement these policies, change is still slow, making it essential for schools to take proactive steps.
By integrating media literacy into our curricula, we wanted to foster socially aware, open-minded individuals and empower teachers to drive these changes. As our project results will be available online, we hope to support lifelong learning for a wider audience.

<< Objectives >>

Our key objectives were to equip students with skills to analyze information sources, understand media messages, and make informed decisions in areas like citizenship, human rights, and digital content creation. We aimed to reinforce critical thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, ICT, and communication skills, helping students become more socially aware and open-minded.
Recognizing the dominance of virtual life, we wanted to teach students how to identify real information needs, filter content responsibly, and create quality media. Additionally, we wanted them to act as active citizens by addressing underrepresented topics and fostering intercultural dialogue.
To build digitally ready and resilient schools, we focused on teacher development, enhancing their ICT, language, and mentoring skills through innovative methodologies. Our 35 workshops, led by teachers and local professionals, aimed to promote common values and community engagement.
Key project results include "The Media and Information Literacy Handbook for Teachers" with 20 learning scenarios and a MOOC for students, ensuring accessibility for diverse learners. We also created an eTwinning/Twinspace platform to share our work within the EU educational community.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented activities aimed at developing a structured approach to Media and Information Literacy (MIL) across partner schools. While MIL was previously covered in various ways depending on individual teacher initiatives, we created a comprehensive framework to integrate it systematically.
We conducted 35 workshops for students and teachers, focusing on analyzing media content, responsible digital citizenship, and content creation. Teachers collaborated with local professionals to reinforce critical thinking, problem-solving, ICT, and communication skills.
A key outcome was the creation of "The Media and Information Literacy Handbook for Teachers" with 20 learning scenarios and the "Media and Information Literacy MOOC for students". The MOOC includes evaluation tools, accessibility features for students with learning difficulties, and self-paced modules, ensuring inclusivity.
Additionally, we worked towards introducing MIL as an extracurricular subject in partner schools and sharing results locally and nationally. An eTwinning/Twinspace platform was created to support collaboration and dissemination.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs of our project include 35 workshops for students and teachers, fostering media literacy, digital skills, and critical thinking through collaboration with local education authorities, professionals, and NGOs. These partnerships ensured a synergy between schools, institutions, and civic organizations, promoting lasting cooperation beyond the project’s duration.
Key project results are "The Media and Information Literacy Handbook for Teachers" and the "Media and Information Literacy MOOC for students," integrating civic education, ICT, language education, and sustainable development. The MOOC combines teacher training results, student-generated digital materials, and diverse educational methodologies. It remains dynamic, with updates and new media trends, ensuring long-term relevance.
Additionally, an eTwinning/Twinspace platform was created for resource sharing, and the coordinating school will continue updating questionnaires and quizzes on the digital platform. The project’s outcomes will be disseminated through seminars and teacher training events, ensuring sustainable impact and further educational development.

2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000089977.title: Green Science Teaching Materials for digital learning
2022-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000089977.summary:
<< Background >>

We wanted to undertake this project to address several key needs. We recognized the lack of elective courses that address specific and interdisciplinary topics such as geophysics and financial literacy and students’ interest in such content. There was a need for structured curricula that would enrich students’ education. Teachers express the need for high-quality and ready-made teaching materials such as worksheets, preparations for regular and field classes, and interactive content. We wanted to facilitate their daily preparation and improve the quality and diversity of teaching. We recognized the importance of collaborating with European partners to adopt new working methods and improve existing practices. The pandemic highlighted the need for digital tools that enable the evaluation and monitoring of students’ work in situations where it is not possible to hold live classes, so we decided to develop an application for physical education teachers. We saw the need to integrate multiple subjects into solving real-world problems, especially those related to sustainability and the environment. We saw the project as an opportunity to address these needs in a systematic and sustainable way.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of this project were multiple:
1. Development and implementation of new optional subjects for students of science and mathematics gymnasiums, especially in the areas of geophysics, numerical modeling and financial literacy, in order to enrich the offer of school curricula.
2. Creation of high-quality teaching materials - from worksheets and teaching scenarios to interactive materials - that will facilitate the work of teachers and enable the implementation of interdisciplinary and innovative teaching.
3. Exchange of experiences and good practices among European schools and institutions in order to improve teaching methods and expand cooperation between teachers and students.
4. Encourage digitalization in education by developing a mobile application that allows physical education teachers to evaluate student activities, even when face-to-face teaching is not possible, which is particularly relevant after the experience of the pandemic.
With these objectives, we wanted to ensure a lasting impact on the education system, improve the competences of students and teachers, and encourage innovation in schools across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, we carried out a series of activities aimed at developing and implementing interdisciplinary teaching scenarios and new teaching materials. The activities were piloted in classrooms and during mobility with international groups of students, and feedback helped improve the materials.
We organized mobilities for teachers and students, where practices were exchanged. We established new collaborations with faculties and institutions. A mobile application for monitoring students' physical activity was developed, freely available on Google Play and the App Store. Curricula for optional subjects were created.
In addition to regular communication between partners, we organized lectures, workshops and public events to promote the project results and ensure dissemination at local and international levels.

<< Results >>

The project has achieved significant concrete results and visible impacts. Numerous interdisciplinary teaching scenarios for both STEM and humanities have been developed, which have been successfully piloted in classes and during international mobilities, thus adapting them for effective application. A large number of exercises for Robotics have also been developed, as well as proposals for projects that students can work on Robotics and Numerical Modeling.
The curriculum for the optional subject Geophysics has been designed, the first of its kind in Croatia. The curriculum for Financial Literacy has also been developed for the initial and advanced levels. In addition, a mobile application for monitoring students' physical activities has been developed. At the very beginning of the project, a digital platform was developed on which all project activities are monitored and on which all materials resulting from the project are located.
Three manuals for teachers have been created; for Numerical Modeling, Robotics and Biology.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-IE01-KA220-SCH-000085941.title: Promoting Interest in STEAM Subjects to Reduce The Gender Gap
2022-1-IE01-KA220-SCH-000085941.summary:
<< Background >>

We know how important STEM education is for all of our students' futures. Through the project we set out to provide our students with skills that will prepare them for the fast and ever changing world we live in. These skills are not only relevant skills for their  working careers but also help them to be creative, flexible, confident and prepared for change in their lives and in the world around them. Thus helping them to be stronger, more resilient individuals. We also worked hard to create equality of access, opportunity and attitude to these subjects. We set out to prove that the belief that these subjects are more suited to boys is a stereotype. We are confident that we have changed this view among our students & they now feel there is no greater aptitude or ability in one gender compared to the other.
We showed our students that many women in the past made great contributions to these fields despite adversity & we looked at modern role models for students in these areas. 
Another goal was to increase overall interest in STEAM subjects and this was achieved through fun, interactive and practical activities. We used our school environments and real life situations to show the importance of our understanding of STEAM subjects.

<< Objectives >>

Our main goal was to increase interest in STEM topics among all of our students through fun, interesting, creative, collaborative lessons.
We wanted to reduce real & perceived gender inequalities in access to & attitudes to STEM topics in our schools & beyond. 
We wanted our girls to be as interested & engaged as their male classmates in STEM subjects.
We wanted to be inclusive & provide opportunities to students who otherwise mightn’t have access to them i.e. students from poorer backgrounds. We also wanted to help students with differing needs i.e. physical or neuro-divergent.
We wanted to expand our students & teachers communication & collaboration skills.
To increase our students' knowledge of and confidence in English.
To improve their ICT skills – means of communication, as a working tool i.e. computations, illustration etc.
We wanted to learn from one another & improve our basic skills i.e. learn new methodologies, practices and techniques. 
We wanted to improve key competences through a focus on STEM i.e. problem-solving, critical thinking, analytical skills, collaboration, adaptability, creativity and being able to work as part of a team.
We wanted to increase our students and indeed our own identity as European citizens.

<< Implementation >>

We worked individually & collaboratively with our Erasmus partners on STEM topics.
We focused on key competences i.e. collaboration, problem solving & creativity.
Girls were encouraged to be actively involved in the project. While promoting positive attitudes & engagement of girls we were careful not to promote any negativity in boys. We focused on collaboration rather than competition in the activities. The results of many experiments/games/activities showed that gender had no impact on the outcome.
There is a greater interest in STEM subjects in our schools from all pupils regardless of gender.
We provided opportunities to students who otherwise mightn’t have access to them i.e. students from poorer backgrounds went on trips. Neuro-divergent students were encouraged & supported with the activities. 
Each participant practised their language skills through daily interactions, shared learning & experiences. They improved their ICT skills i.e. graphing, design, PowerPoint presentations, videos, online surveys, virtual meetings etc.  
Teachers gained new teaching skills & methodologies & exchanged best practice. We raised gender & Intercultural awareness through collaboration with teachers & students from different countries.

<< Results >>

We created an E-book of Stem Lesson plans for teachers suitable for students aged 10 - 18.
We also created a booklet of Gender based activities and a video about Female Role Models. These role models were women who succeeded in the field of STEM in the past – often when women didn’t have access to an education let alone in the field of STEM.
A  Mobile App was created that will help other teachers who are writing Erasmus projects. It will help them to calculate their budget.
We also created video evidence of each short term exchange of students that can be seen on youtube channel. There is a link for each of them on our schools websites as well as the project website. 
A Project website was created that outlines the topics that were investigated over the duration of the project. It also has links to the materials produced also i.e. booklet of lessons. 
Erasmus Corners/Noticeboards were all put up in our school. They display the results of the activities as well as motivational slogans about women in STEM.

2022-1-IS01-KA220-SCH-000086050.title: Essence of Agriculture and Rural Traditional Hospitality
2022-1-IS01-KA220-SCH-000086050.summary:
<< Background >>

To tackle the common problems of marginalization in European rural agricultural areas and to address the needs of those societies for a highly skilled, competent and flexible workforce, guaranteeing social inclusion, sustainable use of regional resources and environmental protection, the EARTH project was designed and created with the means of a new and exciting approach towards Innovation and Entrepreneurship Education (IEE) in the form of a camp-method. 
EARTH project was designed to tackle the need for entrepreneurial empowerment among students in rural areas in Europe, who are significantly affected by socio-economic exclusion within partner countries. 
The project aimed at:
- Increasing students' and teachers' competences through active and creative entrepreneurial learning (IEE - Innovation and entrepreneurship education) 
- Providing education to foster the needs of rural communities in order to enhance their competitiveness and entrepreneurial skills
- Sustaining environmental development in rural communities
- Elevating the status of vocational training through Innovation and Entrepreneurial Education (IEE)
- Enhancing VET business partnerships aimed at promoting work-based learning in rural areas 

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we wanted to show results that relates to positive impacts on social, economic and political situation of the marginalized rural areas in EU through entrepreneurship learning/teaching. That included: 
- To increase students’ and teachers' competences through active and creative entrepreneurial learning.
- To provide education to foster the needs of rural communities in order to enhance their competitiveness and
entrepreneurial skills.
- To sustain environmental development in rural communities.
- To elevate the status of vocational training through innovation and entrepreneurial education (IEE).
- To enhance VET business partnerships aimed at promoting work-based learning in rural areas.

By doing that, we planned six LTT in six countries - entrepreneurial camps for students/teachers, for them to make "start-up" companies: 
- C1: Italy (Theme of the IEE camp: Green agriculture, local products and Tourism)
- C2: Spain (Theme: Economic and social importance of olive oil and wine)
- C3: Greece (Theme: Local products, culture and tourism)
- C4: Portugal (Theme: Wine, vineyards and Tourism)
- C5: Croatia (Theme: Bio-Agriculture and Tourism)
- C6: Iceland (Theme: Renewable energy and Tourism) 

<< Implementation >>

EARTH was implemented throughout the 24 months project's period within five Work packages, including:
WP1: Project management and Implementation, including  24 online Steering Group meetings to ensure proper communication and implementation and six face-to-face meetings during LTT activities 

WP2: Six Learning, Teaching, Training Activities (LTTA) in six countries (Italy, Spain, Greece, Portugal, Croatia, Iceland) with total of 24 students and 12 teachers in each LTTA

WP3: Production and creation of IEE-GUIDE (HANDBOOK) for IEE learning and teaching (Innovation and Entrepreneurship Education)
See: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1iGmaCH2LheMib7OWy1gOTwPIO4o3nE3g/view 

WP4: Web Platform, including all results 
https://igorsoldic.wixsite.com/earth

WP5: Dissemination Plan - including:
a) Multiplier Events in six countries (Different timings) 
b) One international dissemination event in Bucharest, Romania (19. september 2024) 
c) Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/search/top?q=eartherasmusplus
d) Instagram page: earth_erasmusplus 
e) Etwinning/Twinspace: https://school-education.ec.europa.eu/en/etwinning/projects/essence-agriculture-and-rural-traditional-hospitality/twinspace/pages/welcoming-ceremony-and-earth-logo-competition

<< Results >>

The EARTH project implemented all the above activities, as planned at the application stage.
The project team, consisting of high schools in six countries have made a lot of effort to plan and implement IEE-camps where students and teachers could learn about entrepreneurship and sustainability by exploring rural communities. The topic of each camp was based on the real needs of the local communities. Six countries hosted camps with a lot of workshops and expert presentation on entrepreneurship in each country. The project developed the cooperation between the students/teachers which were informed by institutions, organizations and different companies of agricultural products. Students and teachers were also informed and shared knowledge and experiences about rural sustainability issues. To reach the project's objectives, the project joined together education, institutes, government and the World of Work to work together in rural communities with any means they needed. In that way, the project introduced a systematic approach towards IEE for teachers and students, which can be embedded into any curricula in Europe.

2022-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000086101.title: Power of digitalization in fighting against climate change
2022-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000086101.summary:
<< Background >>

We believed that our project could provide  enrichment and a significant educational contribution to the training offered in the field of ecology/digital education with the aim of developing and “achieving” the goals of the 2030 agenda. In summary: we are familiar with and make use of innovative technologies as an important aid to search solutions in the fight against climate change. Students with no experience of their European peers who have never ‘experienced’ the daily lives of their peers, have developed a European consciousness by working towards the same goal thanks to the opportunity offered to them by the EU.
Main requirements:
 Train teachers to help students develop new and innovative skills by effectively using technology and knowledge to create models/products as solutions in the fight against climate change;
Promote intercultural knowledge by fostering a common European identity to overcome prejudices and establish friendly, collaborative relationships and open mindsets;
 Enable students to acquire knowledge about new technologies/energies and eco-friendly materials to propose innovations through the creation of environmentally friendly models;
Actively involve institutions, local communities, and families.


<< Objectives >>

It aimed to raise public awareness of climate change issues and encourage the search for solutions through 21st-century digital skills and innovative teaching approaches.  It promoted the development of students' ICT skills, as well as their personal and social skills that are not often developed through normal classroom teaching: creativity, teamwork, etc. The ITEC “Designing the Classrooms of the Future”strategies encouraged students to work on real-world problems throughout the project. 
The aim was to:
 improve the quality of teachers' digital teaching and learning methods
 Provide students with the opportunity to use new technologies appropriately
Enable students to get to know their European peers in daily life: comparing different realities
Provide the opportunity to integrate technological knowledge with other disciplines
Guiding students in research on local environmental issues and collaborate with environmental associations
Creating links between partners and developing innovative minds 
Making each participating institution more knowledgeable and open to other European institutions/projects 
 Creating useful products within the framework of the Erasmus+ KA2 partnership with the integration of local institutions


<< Implementation >>

The following planned activities were carried out:

website, brochures, e-books, E-Twinning space, articles, documentaries, Taskade, Wisemapping, Pecha Kucha, Instagram page, OER open source 
Each school had access to innovative teaching and learning platforms; students and teachers gained an international perspective and experience in creating new products/materials with their friends from other cultures to develop solutions to climate change
The results obtained from the implementation of the POfDigi project are tangible, in the form of intermediate and final products,and intangible, in the form of knowledge accumulated in science,digital /language skills, communication skills,positive attitudes towards life through the activities carried out 
Environmental exhibition “A greener Net” 
Guide ( use of digital tools in environmental issues) 
Project manual/ brochure  
News about the project in the local/ national press.
The training made it possible to:
  teach new digital techniques applied to study and design
  Undertake new innovative teaching models in different disciplines
 Train teachers
  Involve the school,local community,families,presenting knowledge and activities to raise awareness of the importance of protecting the environment through the solutions presented

2022-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000087575.summary:
<< Background >>

Our desires and needs were common with our partner countries.
We all needed to:
•	enhance our 21st-century skills
•	enrich curricula at the EU level,
•	receive professional training at the EU level,
•	add EU value and quality to our organizations,
•	create robots, drones, and e-materials for different school subjects through training,
•	effectively use Texas Instruments, Rover and Turtle programming, Microbit, Scratch programming, computer programming, Python programming, Zero Robotics, SPHERES, 3D printer materials, and develop LEGO Education products,

•	produce various educational materials to integrate into our curricula,
Thus, through sectoral cooperation with universities, training centers, and school partners, we had a great opportunity to exchange implementations from various perspectives to meet our needs.


<< Objectives >>

Our priority was to promote creative digital practices to enhance the digital literacy/readiness of teachers and students, emphasizing creative education to develop children's productivity. Educators acquired advanced coding and 3D skills to strengthen the curriculum.

We supported partner countries in learning basic and key competencies using high-quality digital resources. We reinforced the role of teachers in innovative teaching, improving the use of digital tools and fostering students' creative thinking, contributing to the 2021-2027 EU targets.

We encouraged teamwork, communication, collaboration, creativity, and the use of technology for productivity. 2022-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000088700.title: ECOSTEAM - Cooperation to improve ECOlogical behaviors through IBL and STEAM methodology
2022-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000088700.summary:
<< Background >>

The project supports schools in tackling water, energy, waste, and urban mobility issues through collaboration with external stakeholders, focusing on climate change and sustainability. Utilities often engage with schools to share knowledge and promote best practices. The project developed a methodology to help schools integrate stakeholders' educational input into STEAM subjects by interdisciplinary lesson plans and engaging student activities. The project developed an interdisciplinary teaching methodology based on PBL in which stakeholders bring technological innovations and best management practices to schools at local and global levels. The methodology addresses STEAM through real-life contexts, and students, at the end of the course, express themselves through civic journalism. Civic journalism stimulates critical thinking and strengthens young people's belief in their ability to contribute to innovation in daily best practices for environmental sustainability and climate change mitigation. The project implemented concrete dissemination activities through local events, contest for students, and international conferences that foster collaboration between schools and stakeholders.

<< Objectives >>

The core priority of the ECOSTEAM project is to bring concepts and European/global policies on the environment, in relation to water/waste/energy/ urban mobility, and the fight against climate change closer to students and fosters the collaboration between schools and Utilities. Educational resources developed in the project instil a change in behaviours, increasing the engagement of students encouraging entrepreneurial thinking and problem-solving attitudes related to sustainability. The smart solutions created by the students using PBL, civic engagement and creative communication promoted by ECOSTEAM engage students in relevant, stimulating and effective learning as future agents of active citizenship and policy making.
The project developed a learning methodology and didactic tools for secondary school education, adopting the integrated scientific subjects STEAM approach to awaken the students’ curiosity about sustainable development and climate change through Science and Civic Journalism. The methodology deals with water, waste, energy and urban mobility supporting the curricular teaching. The teaching materials produced by the project include innovative learning methodology and replicable Learning Plans and Learning Units.


<< Implementation >>

Partners following the proposal completed all planned activities:
 -Partners identified stakeholders who were invited in project’s actions.
- Surveys to schools and stakeholders provid information on experience, interest, and attitudes on project's topics
- Teaching materials selected from the web, described and organized into an online library.
 -A innovative learning methodology, rich in pedagogical and scientific contents, was developed.
 - 12 Learning Units based on ECOSTEAM methodology were created and tested.
 -a training course for teachers and related toolkit available on the ECOSTEAM website
- the piloting of the LUs at schools 
- a standard Learning Plan and 3 practical examples from schools on how to apply the Learning Unit in class interdisciplinary and with the support of stakeholders.
 -an interactive digital handbook, a step by step guidance with all the needed tools to apply the methodology
 -Videos and contents were created and broadcasted on radio, TV and social media.
 -A manifesto was created to promote connection between STEAM and sustainability 
 -During the ongoing of the project diffusion activities through national events, one international contest and international conference with published proceedings.


<< Results >>

The concrete outputs of the project are:
-a Summary Report of the surveys for schools and stakeholders, available in 4 languages (EN, IT, HR, EL) 
-ECOSTEAM Methodology guidelines in EN, IT, HR, EL
-12 Learning units, 3 units for each them (water, waste, energy, urban mobility) in EN, IT, HR, EL
-The ECSOTEAM Learning plan in EN, IT, HR, EL
-The training course toolkit for teachers to allow the application of the methodology
-3 national surveys report on the efficacy of the methodology, one summary report and the key reports in EN, IT, HR, EL to describe the effectiveness and potentiality of the methodology
-The handbook, easy to use digital pdf, contains all the didactic tools in a step by step pathway in EN, IT, HR, EL
-The videos and the slogan to broadcast the project results in EN, IT, HR, EL
-The ECOSTEAM manifesto for schools in the 4 languages to increase the interest of teachers and students in the project topics and STEAM
-The conference speakers’ presentations and the proceedings 
-The contest and the outcomes videos and articles from the students that stimulate in active citizenship 
-the Project Management Plan and Dissemination Plan to manage the ongoing of the project and diffusion campaign

2022-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000089578.title: Robots in aquatic environments to promote STEM and environmental awareness.
2022-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000089578.summary:
<< Background >>

The RoboAquaria project was conceived in response to a set of educational needs identified across European primary and lower-secondary schools, particularly in relation to STEM education, digital readiness, and environmental awareness. While robotics and digital tools are increasingly present in education, many schools and teachers still lack structured methodologies, validated resources, and contextualized learning scenarios to effectively integrate these tools into everyday teaching practice. At the same time, there is a growing need to strengthen students’ understanding of environmental sustainability and ecological challenges through engaging and interdisciplinary approaches. RoboAquaria addressed these needs by combining Educational Robotics with aquatic environmental contexts, enabling students to explore STEM concepts while developing awareness of biodiversity, ecosystems, and sustainability. The project also responded to teachers’ needs for professional support, practical guidance, and accessible digital resources to implement innovative pedagogical approaches in diverse school settings across Europe.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of RoboAquaria was to enhance the quality and innovation of STEM education in primary and lower-secondary schools through the integration of Educational Robotics and environmental education. The project aimed to strengthen teachers’ competences in adopting inquiry-based, technology-enhanced pedagogies and to support students in developing scientific reasoning, computational thinking, problem-solving skills, and environmental responsibility.
Specific objectives included:
•	developing a structured methodological framework for robotics-based STEM and environmental learning;
•	creating robotics toolkits and interdisciplinary lesson topics;
•	producing e-learning resources and Open Educational Resources (OERs) to support learning;
•	validating the developed materials through pilot activities in schools.
•	disseminating the project results and best practices beyond the project consortium.

<< Implementation >>

•	State of the art in relation to educational robotics, STEAM education and Environmental Education in each involved country and identification of good practices.
•	Mapping teaching methods with curriculum needs, focusing on the desired learning outcomes.
•	National report on best practices and specific recommendations on interdisciplinary teaching.
•	Teacher training on the developed toolkit.
•	Create open-source and low-cost toolkits that support educational activities.
•	Development of lesson plans which integrate the technological aspects taught with the robotic toolkit with the national school curricula.
•	Dissemination of the project results in local, national and international events and thanks to the project website and social media.

<< Results >>

The outputs are:
•	Pedagogical framework for the pilots and guidelines for the teachers (R1).
•	Training in educational robotics tools and specifically the RoboAquaria toolkit. Introduction to the eLearning toolkit and OERs (LTTA).
•	Modern pedagogies for sustainability competences integrating technology in teaching STEM (VAL).
•	RoboAquaria toolkits. Hardware toolkit (v1, v2, v3 - WetToolkit) developed for the project activities (R2).
•	eLearning platform with OERs MOOC (R3).
•	Dissemination and exploitation of the project outcomes in MEs (R4).

2022-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000090043.title: A Systemic APproach to social media and pre-adolescents through thinking skills education
2022-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000090043.summary:
<< Background >>

The ASAP project was developed to respond to a growing educational gap in how schools ad-dress children’s and preadolescents’ relationship with digital and social media. While young people increasingly grow up in digital environments, most school interventions focus narrowly on online risks, legal aspects or technical skills, often through reactive or emergency-driven ap-proaches.

Crucially, preadolescence is a critical yet underexplored phase of development, in which emo-tional regulation, judgement and identity are still forming, while exposure to social media inten-sifies. Schools, teachers and families frequently lack structured tools to address these challenges in a preventive, educational and developmentally appropriate way.

The project also responded to the limited implementation of the Personal, Social and Learning-to-learn Key Competence in school education, despite its recognised importance at EU level. ASAP addressed the need for a broader, structural form of digital and media literacy that helps learners understand how digital environments shape thinking, emotions, relationships and be-haviour, while strengthening school–family cooperation and inclusive educational practices.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing ASAP, the partnership aimed to strengthen the capacity of school communities to address digital and social media literacy in a structural, preventive and educational way.

The project sought to:
– generate a solid transdisciplinary understanding of preadolescents’ digital and social media practices;
– translate research evidence into an innovative Educational Model and Programme grounded in metacognition and experiential learning;
– equip schools, educators and families with practical tools to foster critical thinking, emotional awareness, responsible media use and wellbeing;
– support inclusive school environments and proactive prevention of cyberbullying and online harm;
– provide educators with a coherent training pathway and schools with clear Emergency Practic-es to manage critical situations;
– consolidate project evidence and lessons learned into policy-oriented recommendations sup-porting coherent and preventive approaches to digital and media literacy.

Overall, ASAP aimed to move beyond risk-based approaches and empower learners, educators and families to engage with digital media consciously, critically and responsibly.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented a coherent sequence of research, co-creation, piloting, training and dissemination activities.

It started with transnational desk and field research involving preadolescents, teachers, parents and school leaders to analyse digital and social media practices and needs. Based on these find-ings, partners co-designed the ASAP Educational Model and Programme through iterative devel-opment and five Co-Creation Workshops with local experts and target groups.

The Programme was tested and refined through multiple piloting phases in schools and non-formal education settings across partner countries. In parallel, an Educator Training Programme was developed and piloted to support effective implementation. 

The project also produced Emergency Practices for schools, policy-oriented outputs, and partici-patory dissemination activities, including a Collaborative Editorial Board involving young people, national events and international conferences.

<< Results >>

ASAP delivered a comprehensive set of research-based, validated and openly accessible results.

Key outputs include:
– transnational Desk and Field Research Reports on preadolescents and digital/social media;
– the ASAP Educational Model and Programme, including a Handbook with six Learning Units and practical teaching materials;
– “Every Kid Knows…”, an accessible set of digital cards introducing key concepts;
– ASAP Emergency Practices, a structured protocol for schools to manage critical situations;
– an Educator Training Programme supporting educators in translating the ASAP approach into classroom practice;
– policy-oriented outputs, including a White Paper and Key Recommendations.

The Programme was piloted with thousands of students, teachers and parents, receiving very high positive feedback. All outputs are available open access under a CC BY 4.0 licence and are already being reused in schools, training programmes and follow-up initiatives beyond the pro-ject.

2022-1-LV01-KA220-SCH-000087419.title: Carbon Neutral Schools
2022-1-LV01-KA220-SCH-000087419.summary:
<< Background >>

The EU aims to become the first climate-neutral bloc by 2050. Latvia, Lithuania, Italy, Belgium, and Croatia are mostly on track, though progress varies, as in Croatia’s 30% renewables share yet slow low-carbon strategy for 2030. More immediate action, like the EU's Fit for 55 package, is crucial to stay under the 1.5–2°C warming threshold. Carbon neutrality isn’t just for regions or towns but entire sectors. Schools can play a key role by teaching students to analyze climate data and understand how to address large-scale challenges, boosting overall resilience and economic growth.

<< Objectives >>

Carbon Neutral Schools strived to make one step closer to achieving EU Green Deal's objective to be the first climate neutral continent. During the project digital training materials for education institutions on ways how to reduce Carbon Footprint in their everyday life were developed. It is important that public institutions act as forerunners in achieving ambitious goals and even more important is that schools are among them, as present pupils is future society that mainly will work for the 2050 objective.

<< Implementation >>

The project was build on 3 core WPs: 1) Developing Factor Maps on factors that influence the willingness to reduce Carbon Footprint, 2) Developing interactive e-learning modules on ways how to reduce Carbon Footprint in educational institutions and 3) Developing a toolkit for Green Ambassadors that ensure sustainability of the project results as it will act as a main motivational tool to start thinking green and use main project result.

<< Results >>

The core results of the project are - interactive E-learning modules on Carbon Footprint reduction in Schools "Carbon Neutral School" will cover a variety of Carbon neutrality related topics such as: Climate change; Carbon neutrality and EU policies; Carbon neutral organisation; Understanding the carbon footprint; Guidance of the Greenhouse Gas Protocol and Carbon reduction pathways; Carbon budgeting and an interactive toolkit (e-learning format)  for Green Ambassadors that ensures sustainability of the project results as it acts as a main motivational tool to start thinking green and use main project result.

2022-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000085355.title: Inne spojrzenie na świat
2022-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000085355.summary:
<< Background >>

Through the project, we wanted to respond to the change in schools due to the digital evolution for which schools were not prepared, and this is mainly about new methods and forms of work in schools using digital tools. The Covid-19 pandemic made it necessary for schools to use digital tools, teachers were not always able to use digital education tools in remote teaching, which resulted in problems with adapting teaching methods and forms to the needs of students, and remote education was not followed by teaching methodologies, which could result in reduced motivation of students to work and thus reduced effectiveness and quality of teaching. Therefore, one of the aims of the project was to create interesting methods and forms of teaching using digital tools and, above all, photography. Today, most pupils use cameras, which are an integral part of everyday life, and pupils take a lot of photos, sometimes without knowing the basic principles of photography. Through the project, we wanted to give pupils basic knowledge about the basics of photography and the principles of taking good photos, while at the same time showing them that they can use their phones in an interesting way in the classroom. 

<< Objectives >>

The main aim of the project was to shape digital and key competences through photography, including, above all, the creativity of the students. The main objective of the project was linked to specific objectives that concerned students as well as teachers. The main specific objectives for the pupils were, in short, to learn the secrets of taking good photographs using the right framing, light and other means of expression, and to learn about photography techniques, copyright or the construction of the camera itself. With photography, we wanted to develop the pupils' basic competences in the project: teamwork, cultural awareness, motivation, creativity, sensitivity, tolerance, assertiveness and problem-solving skills. We wanted to familiarise pupils with the international environment and we wanted them to build friendships and acquaintances with respect for cultural differences. The teachers' specific objectives focused on the exchange of experiences on how to implement the core curriculum in an attractive way using photography. Teachers participated in the creation of innovative handouts and lesson plans using photography, thanks to which the motivation of pupils to work will certainly increase. 

<< Implementation >>

The project involved 5 short-term pupil-teacher exchanges, each involving at least 5 pupils from each country + 2 teachers. The theme of each mobility was different: photography in language teaching, photography in geography teaching, photography in biology teaching, photography in history teaching, and photography in mathematics, physics and chemistry teaching. In the initial phase of the project, the project was promoted in the school communities, followed by preparatory activities including the recruitment of students to the project. During the project, project evaluation activities were carried out, which focused on the initial, ongoing and final evaluations. The final phase of the project focused on the development of the project's tangible results and the dissemination of the project's results, as well as the final evaluation of the project. The project also included 5 photo and digital competitions for school students: for the project logo, the ‘Holiday World Look’ competition, the ‘Christmas World Look’ competition, the ‘Feelings’ competition, and a competition in the form of a city game for the best photo report. During the project, schools took part in Erasmus Days

<< Results >>

The following material results of the project were produced during the project:
- 5 photo and digital competitions were held,
- 5 photographic exhibitions were displayed in each of the schools involved in the project, 
- 26 lesson plans and handouts on the use of photography in school practice were produced,
- 8 presentations on photography,
The project produced the following intangible results, which were verified during the final evaluation by questionnaires for both students and teachers:
- 93.8 % of the pupils participating in the project developed their interest in photography,
- 97.9 % of the pupils participating in the project improved their language competences,
- 94.9 % of pupils developed their motivation and creativity,
- 91.9 % of the pupils developed the ability to cooperate in groups,
- 96% of pupils learned about the culture and sights of another EU country,
- 99 % of pupils made acquaintances and friends,
- 100 % of teachers, project participants started to use photography in their work,
- 100 % of teachers believe that the motivation of pupils to work in the project increased,
- 100 % of teachers increased their knowledge of the history and sights of another EU country
- 100 % of teachers stated that participation

2022-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000085655.title: MP Health Direct: Mental and Physical Health Direct Kierunek na zdrowie psychiczne i fizyczne
2022-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000085655.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to respond to the health needs of the community at that time, i.e. during the COVID-19 pandemic. Our activities were aimed at supporting participants in building their immunity in the particularly difficult autumn-winter period. The project combined the impact of a balanced diet, physical activity, psychological aspects and physiotherapy,  necessary in the face of chronic stress, which weakens the immune system.
We encouraged and convinced people to live a healthy lifestyle through proper nutrition and physical activity, drew their attention to the increasingly common posture defects, and raised awareness of the importance of ecology and charity. Through various workshops, participants learned to cope with stress and negative emotions, which improved their well-being and body performance.
Both students and local communities benefited from the project activities, which contributed to their personal and professional development. Our goal was therefore not only to improve health, but also to develop competences and civic activity, which in the long term will contribute to the strengthening of local communities.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to achieve important project goals aimed at the comprehensive development of participants. We involved students in the process of creating and implementing activities to encourage them to develop personally. They gained new knowledge and experience in the area of ​​health, which contributed to their better preparation for their future professional life.
Students learned to take joint responsibility for assigned tasks, which increased their self-presentation skills and raised their self-esteem. They developed teamwork skills, which in the future will improve their chances of employment. Participants gained valuable experience and developed key competences.
Study visits had a positive impact on the participants’ initiative, entrepreneurship and cultural awareness. Students had the opportunity to test their abilities, learn effective planning and cooperation. Study visits in their own country allowed them to better identify with the region and the country. Students developed key competences, including language, mathematical and digital skills. International cooperation has increased the prestige of schools and counteracted educational inequalities by engaging students with special educational needs.

<< Implementation >>

Project teams were selected in schools, all procedures were completed, and arrangements related to the implementation of the project were made on an ongoing basis.
Students prepared and selected the project logo.
The project social media accounts were created where articles, photos, presentations, and short reports from participants were posted.
Four study visits to Turkey, Romania, Croatia, and Poland were held along with planned activities. 
Local activities were carried out in all 4 schools, we celebrated European Mobility Week, World Cleanup Day, Health Day, Food Day. Additionally, each school carried out activities on different days: Turkey - Mental Health Day, Croatia - Spine Day, Romania - No Tobacco Day, Poland - Immunology Day.
We completed tasks related to: planning, preparing dishes with local superfoods that increase immunity, reducing waste; we took on challenges related to physical activity, physiotherapy, and psychology. Each school in its own environment took care of disseminating and promoting the project activities on school pages, in social media, among students, parents and in the local community. The project was disseminated during: open days, local events.

<< Results >>

The effective work of the project team, good communication and cooperation had a positive impact on the implementation time and the use of funds. 
Study visits and other activities allowed students to test their abilities, to demonstrate their own initiative, entrepreneurship, awareness, culture and taught them how to effectively plan and cooperate in a group, which will prevent leaving school early. Participants developed key competences, gained new friends, broadened their minds, learned how to take care of their physical and mental health. Professional competences increased. Due to participation of students with special educational needs, from rural areas and from homes with a difficult economic situation, we counteracted inequalities in education. 
There are many results linked with a healthy lifestyle and mental health, available to everyone: a 4-week training plan, the ABC of Health e-book, the joint e-book aimed at improving health, the portfolio of herbs and the project social media. We increased the immunity of participants and promoted a healthy lifestyle by combining diet, physical activity, physiotherapy and psychology. 
Project provided recommendations for partner countries, which strengthened local strategies.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2022-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000086129.title: Cybernetyka w edukacji wczesnoszkolnej - MEMA jako metoda nauczania
2022-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000086129.summary:
<< Background >>

The CybeMEMA project was a response to clearly identified needs of primary education teachers and pupils in the partner countries. The needs included:
- the necessity to apply a method in early education to facilitate and encourage children to learn mathematics and programming;
- increasing teachers’ motivation to use modern teaching tools at the stage when children begin their formal education;
- the search for teaching methods supporting understanding of cause-and-effect and algorithmic thinking;
- the need to introduce new teaching methods that make mathematics and STEM education easier and more effective.
During the project implementation, the initial indications confirming the effectiveness of the MEMA method in teaching programming and mathematics were validated. MEMA proved to be an innovative tool for working with children in early education. The project addressed the needs by developing, testing, and disseminating the MEMA method – an innovative  tool supporting the teaching of STEM subjects.
As part of the project, a comprehensive report describing the method was produced, along with four textbooks for teachers and pupils (grades 1–4), 53 lesson plans, and a website providing access to all the above materials.


<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to conceptualize, test, and disseminate, over the three years of its implementation, the MEMA method for teaching mathematics and programming at the early education level.
The specific objectives included:
- developing the conceptual framework of the MEMA method – available in four languages (English, Polish, Croatian, and Turkish);
- developing a teacher’s handbook (in four language versions);
- developing a student’s handbook (in four language versions);
- developing 50 lesson plans based on the MEMA method (in four language versions).


<< Implementation >>

The following key stages were completed:
- Conceptualization of the MEMA method – a detailed description developed in the form of handbook-reports, including its theoretical foundations, structure, and application in teaching mathematics and programming; 
- Development and publication of a teacher’s handbook for primary schools based on the use of the MEMA method in teaching programming – 4 handbooks were developed for grades 1–4;
- Creation of a student’s handbook for grades 1–4 – 4 workbooks were developed for grades 1–4, based on the teacher’s materials and containing tasks and exercises that support the development of algorithmic thinking;
- Development of 53 lesson plans applying the MEMA method, designed for grades 1–4 and compatible with the teacher’s handbooks and student workbooks; 
- Testing the effectiveness of the method – all educational materials were tested in three countries (Poland, Croatia, Turkey) among a group of 1144 pupils, with the participation of 34 teachers; conclusions were compiled in a comprehensive report;
- Dissemination of project results – through conferences, publications, webinars, and a project website providing full access to all project outputs.


<< Results >>

Project results achieved:
- Report/Handbook describing the MEMA method – a detailed description of the method, including its theoretical foundations, structure, and application in teaching mathematics and programming at the early education level (in 4 languages);
- Teacher’s handbook for primary school teachers “Programming with MEMA” – 4 handbooks for grades 1–4 in 4 languages (16 publications in total);
- Student’s workbook for grades 1–4 “Programming with MEMA” – 4 workbooks for grades 1–4 in 4 languages (16 publications in total);
- 53 lesson plans applying the MEMA method for grades 1–4 (available in 4 languages – 212 publications in total);
- Research report on the effectiveness of teaching with the MEMA method – testing conducted in three countries (Poland, Croatia, Turkey) among 1144 pupils and 34 teachers;
- Dissemination of project results – conferences, publications, webinars, and a website providing full access to all project outputs.
In addition:
- the “equipping” of the MEMA method with comprehensive handbooks and lesson plans;
- providing access to verified teaching tools based on the MEMA method;
- motivating early education teachers to apply innovative methods for teaching maths and programming.

2022-1-RS01-KA220-SCH-000085663.title: The Curious and Flourishing Schools - Positive Education in Building of Character Strengths and Virtues
2022-1-RS01-KA220-SCH-000085663.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project in order to address the needs teachers in primary schools have, especially those induced by the consequences of COVID19 pandemics. Teachers also cope with the constant degradation of their profession in spite of the fact how important it is. During discussions with partners, common problems arose (violent behavior among students both in real and virtual settings, demotivation and lack of interest among students) which seem enhanced under the  COVID19 pandemics. All of the partners agreed that there is a need for support both teachers and students in building up emotional and social skills that can help them cope with the alienation and fear for their mental and physical health. Both teachers and students need support in their personal growth and development threatened by altered circumstances in school and family life during and after the COVID19. Partner agreed that basic principles of positive education will help them overcome difficulties imposed by the lockdown and virtual lessons, and help them enhance feelings of personal well-being and in discovering personal strengths and virtues, as well as in discovering personal strengths and virtues, and new sources of motivation and enthusiasm.   

<< Objectives >>

With this project, we would like to apply The Curious and Flourishing Schools - Positive Education (PE) in Building of
Character Strengths and Virtues program in six schools in order to improve formal primary education as well as psychological well-being
and resilience among both students and teachers. Specific objectives of the project would be:
1.Creation and development of the program The Curious and Flourishing Schools - PE in Building of Character Strengths
and Virtues for implementing PE principles in the everyday lectures for students in upper classes in primary schools.
2.Creation and development of the training program for supporting teachers in building up their competencies for
implementing PE principles in everyday educational work 
3.Supporting teachers in building up their competencies for implementing PE principles in everyday educational work
4.Creation and development of the manual for supporting teachers for implementing PE principles in everyday educational
work 
5.Development of the research methodology for the evaluation of the effect the Curious and Flourishing Schools - PE in
Building of Character Strengths and Virtues program has in partner schools
6.Establishing the PE School Clubs

<< Implementation >>

Activities are divided into 5 work packages:
1. Management of the project
2. Positive education in primary schools -manual for teachers (manual-theoretical and practical part design, web promotion, dissemination among university students, online conference for the manual and the project promotion and dissemination of its results)
3. Design of the Training course of Positive Education in Primary Schools (The Curious and Flourishing Schools - Positive Education (PE) in Building of Character Strengths and Virtues program and workshops design, training for teachers according the program, monitoring, evaluation and adaptation of workshops for students )
4.  Positive education quality evaluation and research (research methodology design, battery of instruments design, research conduct, obtained data analyses, results promotion in scientific papers)

schools; Designed program The Curious and Flourishing Schools for implementing positive education in both upper and lower classes in schools; Total of 81 teachers trained through the training for supporting teachers in building up their competencies for implementing PE principles in everyday

2022-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000086772.title: POSITIVE PSYCHOLOGY INTERVENTIONS TO STRENGTHEN HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS' WELL-BEING AND MENTAL HEALTH
2022-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000086772.summary:
<< Background >>

We submitted the BE WELL project because we recognised the urgent need to systematically strengthen the mental health of high school students, which has declined further after the COVID-19 pandemic. Schools increasingly encounter adolescents facing anxiety, hopelessness, low self-esteem and other forms of psychosocial distress, while curricula often lack content that would equip them with effective coping strategies. 
The project addresses two key needs: strengthening the competences of teachers and school counsellors, and introducing Positive Psychology Interventions (PPI) – simple, prevention-oriented tools that support students’ well-being. PPIs have been proven to enhance character strengths, empathy, resilience, gratitude etc. Research shows that students, especially those from less stimulating socio-economic environments, often experience emotional and psychosomatic difficulties, while positive psychology programmes increase positive emotions, improve self-perception and reduce distress. BE WELL contributes to greater inclusion, better learning outcomes and a school culture that prioritises the mental health and well-being of students, teachers and school counsellors.


<< Objectives >>

With the BE WELL project, we aimed to strengthen systemic support for the mental health of high school students and develop a sustainable model for enhancing well-being in the school environment. We recognised the need to reinforce school counselling services and teacher competences, as they often lack high-quality and effective tools for promoting students’ mental health. The main objective was to train teachers and school counsellors to use Positive Psychology Interventions (PPI), which have been shown to reduce the risk of mental health problems and strengthen students’ well-being. We also sought to empower teachers and counsellors to improve their own well-being, as their role is essential for creating a safe and supportive learning environment. Another key aim was to help develop protective mechanisms for students—especially those from less stimulating socio-economic environments—to cope more effectively with psychosocial distress. The project focused on creating high-quality learning materials and tools that support the regular integration of positive psychology approaches into everyday school practice and contribute to a more inclusive school climate.

<< Implementation >>

In the BE WELL project, we implemented activities in line with the work packages. We first prepared the Good Practice Catalogue, identifying 30 PPIs and selecting 10 as the basis for the training content. Based on this, we designed the training curriculum, defining the content, structure and learning outcomes of 16 hours of workshops across four modules. We developed the Training Program Executive Working Plan (TPEWP) and digital materials e-Guidebook for teachers and e-Toolbook for students. The hybrid teacher training programme combined live workshops with self-directed learning. During the pilot phase, teachers applied selected PPIs in classrooms and documented their experiences. We conducted an extensive evaluation process, measuring the well-being and mental health of teachers and students before and after the training. Special attention was given to the effects on students with lower socio-economic status, identified through a dedicated instrument. We also organised a wide range of dissemination activities, including “BE WELL Week” with events, webinars and publications, and prepared policy recommendations for the long-term integration of PPIs into school practice.

<< Results >>

Key project results include:
• Good Practice Catalogue of PPIs: a systematic review, analysis and classification of 30 existing PPIs and the identification of 10 best PPIs based on PICO and RE-AIM methodology.
• BE WELL Training Curriculum with defined content and learning outcomes (4-module, 16-hour programme).
• TPEWP – Training Program Executive Working Plan, outlining all training activities by teaching hours.
• Digital materials: e-Guidebook for teachers (instructions for implementing PPIs, worksheets, PPT slides) and e-Toolbook for students (exercises and worksheets).
• Delivery of the hybrid teacher training programme (live workshops + self-directed learning).
• Pilot implementation of PPIs in schools, with all modules being implemented and tested with students.
• Evaluation report with data on training effects and feedback from teachers and students.
• Policy recommendations for national, school and individual levels.
• Dissemination activities, including “BE WELL Week” (conference, webinars, presentations), professional/popular articles and presentations at expert events.
