2022-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000087426.title: deutsch.info/olgea: Outdoor Learning of German and rising Environmental Awareness
2022-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000087426.summary:
<< Background >>

The deutsch.info OLGEA project addressed a significant gap in language education: the lack of structured, accessible resources for outdoor-based language learning, especially for teaching German as a foreign language. While the benefits of outdoor learning, such as improved health, motivation, and environmental awareness, are widely acknowledged, few tools effectively integrate it with language instruction. At the same time, concerns about sedentary lifestyles and their impact on student well-being and learning have grown. Schools are seeking ways to better connect education with real-life experiences and make the learning more relevant to everyday life. OLGEA meets this need by providing a complete set of ready-to-use materials and a clear framework that supports teachers in taking language learning outdoors. The project empowers educators with practical tools to offer engaging, movement-rich, and sensory-based lessons that are easy to implement and meet the evolving needs of today’s learners.


<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the deutsch.info OLGEA project was to promote a holistic, learner-centred approach to language education by moving German lessons beyond the classroom and into natural or urban settings. More specifically, the aim was to: (1) strengthen teacher competences in outdoor language learning (OLL) by providing practical, accessible resources; (2) increase pupils’ German language proficiency and environmental awareness through hands-on, movement-based learning; and (3) improve the availability of didactic tools for OLL across the EU. The goal was to empower educators to implement sustainable, interdisciplinary methods that support both cognitive and personal development while advancing the integration of outdoor language learning into mainstream educational discourse and practice. Given the limited research in this area, the project also aimed to contribute knowledge through evaluation, documentation, and dialogue - making a contribution to the groundwork for future curricular and policy developments.


<< Implementation >>

A central activity of the project was the development of the Guidelines for teachers on outdoor language learning: a practical, freely accessible resource introducing teachers to the principles and methods of outdoor language learning. The Guidelines offer self-paced learning and encourage reflection on teaching practices. To help teachers implement outdoor lessons, a set of fully developed, ready-to-use lesson plans was created, adapted to a variety of outdoor settings. These lessons were piloted in three partner schools in Slovenia, Croatia, and Lithuania, involving 99 pupils. The piloting enabled a comprehensive impact evaluation using tests and questionnaires (on language skills, motivation, and environmental awareness) as well as teacher interviews. Additionally, one lesson was tested by teachers in three more schools, involving 77 more pupils. Another key activity was the expansion of the deutsch.info Teachers’ Portal, adding a dedicated section for outdoor learning where all materials are openly available. Dissemination was carried out intensively through teacher workshops, university lectures, educational conferences, social media campaigns, and professional networks.


<< Results >>

The main outcome of the deutsch.info OLGEA project is the new outdoor language learning section on the deutsch.info Teachers’ Portal. It provides German teachers with comprehensive Guidelines on outdoor learning and 48 fully developed, ready-to-use lesson plans across 11 themes. The Guidelines not only introduce the fundamentals of outdoor learning but also support teachers in designing and adapting their own outdoor lessons. All materials are illustrated, downloadable, and structured to suit both novice and experienced educators as well as different natural and urban environments that might be accessible from different schools. An online version of the Guidelines is optimized for mobile use, allowing teachers to access content on the go. The resources were tested in real classes and improved based on teacher feedback. The project has raised awareness about the benefits of outdoor language learning, built teacher capacity, and enhanced student motivation, language engagement, and environmental awareness. Teachers from across Europe have already begun using the materials.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000086151.title: Minoritná kultúra ako prostriedok pre sebaidentifikáciu a posilnenie inklúzie v multietnickom prostredí
2022-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000086151.summary:
<< Background >>

The decision to submit this application gradually emerged during the implementation of our previous project JaSom. Through the project’s practical experience, as well as the extensive expertise of our specialized institution – the UMB Methodological Centre for Slovaks Living Abroad – we identified specific educational needs of children belonging to Slovak minorities abroad. Among these needs were not only concrete thematic areas but also a form of learning that is completely missing in the Slovak language: short educational films that guide users toward improving their language skills in a natural and engaging way. Since for Slovak children living abroad, Slovak is usually not a “foreign language” but rather a heritage language, we did not opt for a typical language course format. Instead, we identified the need for educational films focused on natural communication in Slovak, with gradually increasing language levels and progressively more complex topics through which Slovak communication is presented.
All the needs identified directly in the practice of Slovak minorities naturally led to a project concept, which we subsequently adapted to meet the needs of our partners.

<< Objectives >>

Through the implementation of the project, our primary goal was to provide children of Slovak minorities abroad and their teachers with modern didactic materials that enable them to learn in their mother tongue — in a format familiar to them from majority schools in their current countries of residence (in Western Europe and overseas) or in a form still missing from their minority schools, despite its growing necessity due to natural processes of assimilation (in countries with over 200 years of Slovak enclave or diaspora presence).
By creating 40 short educational films, we aim to support a comprehensive approach to teaching and learning languages by filling a gap in the available educational materials for children of Slovak minorities abroad. This will enable teachers educating these children to develop professionally and improve their pedagogical performance. At the same time, we expect that the use of the project’s results in the educational practice of Slovak minority schools and centers abroad will contribute to the self-identification of children and their parents, foster awareness of the positive value of ethnic and cultural diversity, and create conditions for further inclusion and personal growth of multiple generations

<< Implementation >>

A crucial prerequisite for implementing the project’s activity packages was highly efficient management. To achieve the intended outcomes, we carried out activities in three main phases:

* Needs mapping: Project partners organized workshops where the UMB coordinator of professional activities, together with a team of experts, prepared materials for verification and analyzed findings that were later applied in subsequent phases.

* Expert synthesis: The second phase focused on synthesizing findings from Slovak minority environments in partner countries, as well as from relevant academic literature and comparable materials at home and abroad. This synthesis was vital, as no similar work had been done in Slovakia, requiring a broad interdisciplinary perspective.

* Film production: The creation of educational films was the most demanding yet creative stage, combining footage from partner environments with acted sequences and animations. Dissemination activities further strengthened the quality of the final outputs.

All project challenges were successfully met, as demonstrated by the high-quality didactic films produced.

<< Results >>

The project resulted in 40 short didactic films that fully met its objectives and, in their quality and form, approach professional film productions. For each film, we created accompanying didactic materials designed to enhance their educational value. These materials include recommended teaching methods that teachers can adapt according to the age or proficiency level of their students, as well as examples of practical worksheets and similar resources.
All materials are freely available online, each with a summary description and guidance on how to use them. They are organized into thematic sections corresponding to the project’s partner countries. Each thematic section contains 10 films with a gradually increasing level of language complexity and presentation style, rated on a scale from 1 to 10. Before each film, there is a short description and the related didactic material.
Beyond the project’s original plan, the partners also produced several additional films. One of these — a documentary about the “Straw Bears” from Croatia — was successfully presented at an international festival.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-2-EE01-KA220-SCH-000099273.title: My Box Of STEAM
2022-2-EE01-KA220-SCH-000099273.summary:
<< Background >>

In the beginning of the writing process (2021-2022) project’ partners knew that PISA results (2018) showed that the underachievement rate is 22.4% in mathematics and 21.6% in science. This meant that the European Commission's ET2020 benchmark target to have an underachievement rate of less than 15% has not been reached. So, there were needs to promote interest and excellence in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) and the STEAM approach.  

Our previous research gave us the knowledge that in fact there are not so many interesting and cheap STEM materials available in partners’ countries and even on the Internet. 

<< Objectives >>

Our primary goal was to enhance primary school students' engagement in STEM by fostering inquiry-based learning and a multidisciplinary approach through storytelling, with a particular emphasis on including students with learning disabilities and encouraging girls. We aimed to help students recognize the skills they developed, promoting independent classroom activities by providing curriculum-aligned kits and accessible, replicable educational resources for teachers. 

Another key objective of our project was to cultivate students' abilities in collaboration, communication, creativity, and critical thinking, particularly through storytelling activities connected to STEM, as well as improving their oral expression and presentation skills

International collaboration in the development of STEAM teaching methodology with storytelling elements.

2022-2-IE01-KA220-SCH-000098059.title: coMics and IllustRations Augmented to tackle CLimate change in primary Education
2022-2-IE01-KA220-SCH-000098059.summary:
<< Background >>

The MIRACLE project was conceived in response to urgent educational needs arising from the climate crisis and its impact on young learners. Schools across Europe face the dual challenge of equipping pupils with scientific understanding of climate change while also addressing eco-anxiety, misinformation, and disengagement. At the same time, teachers require innovative tools that connect curricula to pupils’ lived experiences in creative and accessible ways. Our consortium applied for this project to fill these gaps by combining climate change education with digital creativity, comics, and augmented reality.

Needs assessments conducted at the proposal stage and confirmed during implementation highlighted limited availability of age-appropriate resources for primary education, insufficient teacher training on sustainability, and a lack of engaging methods to counter disinformation. The project also responds to European priorities such as the Green Deal, the Council Recommendation on learning for environmental sustainability, and the GreenComp framework.

MIRACLE directly addresses these needs by co-developing open educational resources, a teacher training programme, a MOOC, and an Augmented Classroom.

<< Objectives >>

The MIRACLE project set out to achieve ambitious objectives that respond to shared needs across European primary schools. First, it aimed to upskill teachers to deliver an action-based Climate Change Education Curriculum (CCEC), providing them with the pedagogical confidence and interdisciplinary tools to teach sustainability effectively. Second, it sought to enhance digital competences among teachers and pupils by encouraging whole-class co-creation of content, particularly through comics and augmented reality, fostering creativity and collaboration in the learning process.

A further goal was to support teachers in recognising and addressing eco-anxiety and eco-pessimism, equipping them with strategies to help pupils overcome fear, strengthen resilience, and develop critical thinking and media literacy skills in the face of disinformation. The project also set out to evaluate the educational value of comics literacy in climate change education, generating evidence on how visual storytelling and digital augmentation can improve scientific literacy and engagement.

Finally, MIRACLE aimed to embed a Whole-School Approach to sustainability, integrating its resources into national curricula, teacher training, and school action plans.

<< Implementation >>

The MIRACLE project was implemented through five interconnected work packages. 

WP1 Project Management set up effective coordination with monthly meetings, a Project Monitoring Committee, financial templates, and a Risk Assessment Plan, supported by accessibility, inclusivity, and green guidelines. 

WP2 Sustainability Mindset produced the MIRACLE Toolkit of five digital booklets on climate change, comics, digital augmentation, disinformation and educational scenarios. A three-day Teacher Training Activity was held, followed by pilots in schools across five countries, with validation data collected. 

WP3 MOOC began with a needs analysis, collection of over 130 Open Educational Resources, and development of the course structure and content based on WP2 results. 

WP4 Augmented Classroom carried out a needs analysis and teacher rubric to inform the design of AR-enhanced learning environments, with pilots and training in preparation. 

WP5 Dissemination established the website, newsletters, LinkedIn account, academic presentations, InfoDays, and an eTwinning space to ensure visibility, stakeholder engagement, and long-term impact.

<< Results >>

The MIRACLE project produced concrete outputs across all work packages. The MIRACLE Toolkit of five digital booklets provided teachers with practical resources on climate change, comics literacy, digital augmentation, and disinformation. A three-day Teacher Training Activity engaged 19 participants and was positively evaluated. Pilot testing in schools across five countries involved 365 pupils in pre-tests (244 in post-tests) and 40 teachers, generating validation reports that demonstrated improvements in knowledge, attitudes, and behaviours towards sustainability. The MIRACLE MOOC was designed, supported by a needs analysis and more than 130 Open Educational Resources, and was developed into a multilingual online course for teacher professional development. The MIRACLE Augmented Classroom (MAC) was launched with a dedicated needs analysis and teacher rubric, laying the foundation for an AR-based co-creation space for STEAM and climate education. Dissemination activities included a multilingual website, newsletters, LinkedIn presence, conference papers and presentations, an eTwinning project space, and InfoDays. Collectively, these results strengthened teachers’ competences and enhanced pupils’ engagement with sustainability.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2023-1-CZ01-KA220-SCH-000156079.title: Teaching School Readiness Through an ABA-based Preschool Programme
2023-1-CZ01-KA220-SCH-000156079.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the Ready4School project to address a critical gap in early childhood education: the lack of systematic training and evidence-based tools for preschool teachers supporting children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) during the crucial transition to primary education.
Key needs identified through literature reviews and research across partner countries revealed:
Teacher competencies: Existing research demonstrated that kindergarten teachers possess only moderate knowledge about inclusion and low self-assessment of their competencies as active participants in inclusive education of children with ASD. A systematic lack of education and training for inclusive educational practices was identified across all partner countries.
Assessment and curriculum gaps: Teachers lacked standardized assessment tools and specialized curricula for children with ASD. Without formal ABA training, educators struggled to create individualized programs, collect data effectively, and implement evidence-based strategies.
School readiness challenges: Research confirmed that children with ASD are emotionally less school-ready than peers, with difficulties in communication, social interactions, and behavior management. 

<< Objectives >>

The primary goal was to increase the quality of special and inclusive preschool programs for children with ASD and facilitate successful transition from preschool to primary education to: 1. Develop innovative tools: Create a comprehensive, evidence-based educational kit grounded in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) principles, yet adapted for easy implementation by educators without formal ABA training. This includes: developmental assessment with school readiness checkpoints, lesson plans with supporting materials, data sheets for monitoring and evaluating progress, mobile application for digital assessment, digital library of reproducible materials. 2. Build educator capacity: Train 3 trainers per partner country through pilot-testing, who would then train a minimum of 5 teachers in their countries, creating a multiplier effect and ensuring sustainable implementation. 3. Improve teacher competencies: Address the identified gap in preschool teacher training by equipping educators with practical skills in autism intervention, assessment techniques, and evidence-based teaching strategies. 4. Promote inclusion: Foster inclusive early childhood education systems by providing teachers with accessible tools for diverse learners. 

<< Implementation >>

WP1 - Project Management: Conducted transnational partner meetings (Croatia 2024, Greece 2025), established committees, and maintained regular online coordination meetings among the six partner organizations.
WP2 - Educational Kit Development: Conducted needs assessment across all partner countries, developed the School Readiness Teaching Curriculum with detailed lesson plans, created the Goal Bank and Task Analysis, and produced progress monitoring data sheets.
WP3 - Assessment Tool Development: Created the School Readiness Assessment Tool with developmental checkpoints, developed the Ready4School mobile application for digital assessment, and built a digital library of reproducible materials.
WP4 - Training Activities: Implemented pilot-testing training in Skopje (April 2025) with 22 participants from all partner countries, and conducted local teacher training activities in all partner countries (June-August 2025).
WP5 - Dissemination: Created project website (ready4school.eu), established social media presence, developed promotional materials, organized multiplier events in each partner country, and prepared newsletters and press releases to share project results with stakeholders.

<< Results >>

The primary deliverable was the innovative School Readiness Educational Kit, based on ABA principles and adapted for educators without formal ABA training. This kit included the School Readiness Assessment Tool (booklet format) with developmental checkpoints measuring critical school readiness skills across foundational skills, social interaction, and self-regulation domains. The project developed a complete preschool teacher-training curriculum that linked to detailed lesson plans featuring task analyses, teaching strategies, and reproducible worksheets. A significant technological achievement was the Ready4School mobile application, freely available on both Google Play Store and Apple App Store, which digitizes the assessment process, tracks student progress through color-coded graphs, and provides personalized recommendations. The project also created comprehensive progress monitoring data sheets, a goal bank with task analyses, and a digital library of materials. Beyond tangible outputs, the project trained 18+ trainers across partner countries during the pilot-testing event, who subsequently trained 90+ local teachers, resulting in improved teacher competencies and increased awareness of evidence-based practices.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2023-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000151276.title: ACT4CONSENT
2023-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000151276.summary:
<< Background >>

Across all EU Member States, the importance of consent is steadily increasing, as it is recognized both as a fundamental human right and as a topic that must increasingly be addressed in the education of young people. Today, consent extends across many areas of life: from interpersonal relationships to digital communication. Raising awareness of this crucial issue among young people helps to foster a culture of respect, self-empowerment, and open communication.

Despite its significance, however, the topic of consent has not been adequately incorporated into the curricula of education systems and youth work in many European countries. As a result, young people often rely on informal sources such as peers, the media, and the internet for information. Moreover, social norms and values that perpetuate harmful beliefs and attitudes about sexuality and relationships can make young people particularly vulnerable.

For these reasons, ACT4CONSENT has developed a new educational approach to support secondary school teachers, youth educators, young people, and parents in addressing and working on the topic of consent actively yet sensitively.

<< Objectives >>

The key objectives of the project were to:
(1) Increase awareness and understanding of the concept of consent: to ensure that all clearly understand what consent is and why it is important in all types of relationships. 
(2) Develop communication skills: Through drama and storytelling activities, all parties involved can practice communicating boundaries, desires, and feelings in a safe and supportive environment.
(3) Build empathy and respect: By exploring different scenarios and perspectives through drama and storytelling, all parties involved can develop a greater sense of empathy and respect for others.
(4) Address harmful societal norms and values: challenge harmful societal norms and values that perpetuate harmful beliefs and attitudes about sex and relationships and encourage critical thinking and reflection on these issues.
(5) Foster a sense of community: Through group activities and discussions, foster a sense of community and support among all parties involved where everyone feels comfortable and respected.
(6) Provide support and resources: to provide all parties involved with the resources and support they need to continue learning about and promoting consent education in their school and wider community.

<< Implementation >>

In its individual phases, ACT4CONSENT comprised the following main activities:
(1) Development, testing, evaluation, adaptation, and translation activities: Resources for a creative educational approach were created to address consent in secondary education and to support teachers and youth workers in working directly with young people on the topic using active, experience-based methods. All materials are available for free download in 7 languages on the project website, www.act4consent.eu. They can be flexibly adapted to the own needs.

(2) Dissemination and implementation activities: Information material (animated video, newsletter, and press releases from each partner organization) to present the project goals and results; the project website was created to provide information about the progress results of the project, Facebook was actively used to publish updates on the project, and target group-specific events were held for teachers and young people or parents. The diverse activities led to intensive discussions, raised awareness of the topic of consent in the partner institutions, schools, and among the public. The project contributes to the development of attitudes such as respect, openness, and tolerance.

<< Results >>

The following concrete results were produced within the ACT4CONSENT project:
(1) ACT4CONSENT CPD Programme consisting of 6 modules providing 30 hours of F2F and self-directed learning.
(2) Handbook for teachers consisting of 20 classroom-based activities -10 activities that use drama techniques and 10 activities that use storytelling techniques addressing topics related to consent.
(3) Resources for parents: 8 short videos (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gXvaz6i6XX0&list=PLOew_q29P48kzu9fBPtjY48DLsIM2UsZM) and 8 tipsheets.
(4) Resources for students: 8 short videos (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y_k7ZlXItY0&list=PLOew_q29P48k10W_mDA4hkOk6QH9SXhB8) and 8 tipsheets.
(5) One animation video (https://youtu.be/D1HifFP7KT4).

All these materials are available for free at www.act4consent.eu.
All resources can be used in a wide variety of contexts, including school and non-school learning spaces, different educational areas, and with young people aged 15–18. With some adaptation, they can also be used partly for younger children. Throughout the project, all partners contributed actively to the dissemination of ACT4CONSENT results, with over 220 activities and nearly 70,000 people reached, ensuring both local and European visibility.

2023-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000151560.title: Intergenerational Learning for Sustainable Households – IGL 4 Sustainable Households
2023-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000151560.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated to address the need for more engaging and practice-oriented approaches to environmental and sustainability education in secondary schools. While climate topics are increasingly present in curricula, learning often remains theoretical and insufficiently connected to students’ everyday lives and family contexts. At the same time, the potential of Intergenerational Learning (IGL) and citizen science is still underused in formal education, and teachers often lack concrete methods and ready-to-use tools to implement such approaches.
The project responded to the need to strengthen teachers’ competences in applying IGL and citizen science, foster collaboration between schools and families, and empower young people to act as agents of change for greener lifestyles. By doing so, it contributes to more inclusive, participatory and action-oriented sustainability education.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to strengthen environmental and sustainability education in secondary schools through the innovative use of Intergenerational Learning (IGL) and citizen science approaches. It sought to equip teachers with practical methodologies, tools and competences to implement engaging, action-oriented learning activities that connect classroom learning with students’ family and community contexts.

A further objective was to empower students to become active contributors to greener lifestyles by involving them in collaborative, inquiry-based activities together with older generations. The project also aimed to foster stronger cooperation between schools, families and local communities and to promote the uptake of innovative pedagogical practices across partner countries.

Overall, the project intended to contribute to more inclusive, participatory and impactful climate education in Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented a coherent set of development, training and piloting activities. An eBook was produced to provide secondary education teachers with a structured overview of the Intergenerational Learning (IGL) framework, highlighting its pedagogical benefits and practical application in schools. In parallel, a DIY Manual and a Virtual Toolkit were developed to support STEM educators in designing and implementing intergenerational citizen science activities.
Capacity-building was further strengthened through international mobility activities and targeted training events. Experiential Labs enabled hands-on testing of the developed methodologies, while Science Cafés and Science Fairs engaged students, teachers and families in participatory learning and community dialogue. Together, these activities supported the practical uptake and validation of the project’s innovative approach across partner countries.

<< Results >>

The project successfully delivered its planned results and met its core objectives. Key outputs include the IGL eBook, the DIY Manual and the Virtual Toolkit, which together provide educators with practical guidance and ready-to-use resources for implementing intergenerational citizen science activities in secondary education. These materials were tested and refined through mobilities, Experiential Labs, Science Cafés and Science Fairs across partner countries.
The project strengthened teachers’ competences in applying innovative, participatory methodologies and increased students’ engagement in sustainability-related actions. It also fostered stronger collaboration between schools, families and communities. Feedback from piloting activities confirmed the relevance, usability and transferability of the developed resources, demonstrating the project’s contribution to more inclusive and action-oriented environmental education.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2023-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000151350.title: Fostering inclusion and responsible citizenship in the classroom through sexual education
2023-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000151350.summary:
<< Background >>

FUNSEED was initiated in response to a clear need documented in academic studies and research: students are highly exposed to hypersexualized content through media and social networks, while teachers report a lack of specific training to effectively support and accompany them, as well as a shortage of reliable educational resources and insufficient institutional support to address issues such as consent, pornography, abuse, and affective relationships in an inclusive, respectful, and age-appropriate manner across different educational stages. Furthermore, Spain, Croatia, and the Czech Republic have distinct curricular frameworks and cultural sensitivities, which presents a challenge in developing common tools that are both shareable and adaptable to local contexts. The project has addressed these needs by creating shared educational resources, providing training and support to teachers, educators, and families, and promoting comprehensive sexuality education linked to inclusion, violence prevention, and responsible citizenship in the classroom.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to strengthen teachers’ capacity to deliver sexual education in a rigorous, inclusive and age-appropriate way. It sought to equip educators with scientific, pedagogical and emotional tools developed through training activities, cross-country exchanges and project materials (R1, R2, R3, R4, R5 and R6) so they could address sensitive topics with confidence and coherence. It also aimed at providing students with structured learning experiences based on participatory methods and pre-/post-evaluation, helping them understand their bodies, boundaries, consent, emotional development and healthy relationships. Another core objective was to create a shared European methodology grounded in evidence and adaptable to Spain, Croatia and Czechia, while respecting cultural diversity. The project further sought to encourage family engagement and strengthen collaboration between school and home. Overall, the goal was to promote inclusion and responsible citizenship through comprehensive sexual education, with the support of teachers, educators, and families.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented a set of research, training, and dissemination activities to improve sexual education in participating schools. It began with a peer learning activity in Croatia (A1), where partners identified needs, gaps, and good practices. Based on this analysis, Chiclana designed a training course focused on innovative methodologies and tools for teachers (A2). In the Czech Republic, a training session for teachers was organized based on this design, aimed at classroom application (A3). Siena and the partners worked on the design of the project's mobile App (A4). Trained teachers implemented training sessions for students of different ages in the three schools (A5). Short FUN SEED Talks were produced and published as resources for families and educators (A6), together with one-hour thematic webinars for teachers (A7) and an on-line peer training program called “Teachers Supporting Teachers” (A8). A social media campaign was carried out to raise awareness of evidence-based sexuality education (A9). The project concluded with an international conference presenting the results and common methodology to stakeholders (A10).  

<< Results >>

The project achieved a wide range of results aligned with its original objectives and exceeded expectations in several areas. A1 involved 30 teachers from Spain, Croatia and the Czech Republic and led to R1, a needs analysis identifying cultural challenges, media influence, training gaps and family communication issues, which became the basis for the project. R2, the SEED Training Course, developed with input from 19 teachers, offers trustworthy, age-appropriate, inclusive and practical content addressing issues such as pornography, emotional development and family engagement. R3 translated this course into classroom-ready guidelines with structured, age-specific activities. A5 piloting in schools showed significant improvements in students’ understanding of consent, boundaries and emotional well-being, as well as increased teacher confidence and better classroom climate (A5 Internal Result). Five short educational videos for families and teachers were produced (R5-SEED Talks) and the website and mobile app further support sustainability and networking. All objectives were met, in addition to strong teacher engagement, cross-cultural cooperation and growing demand for training.

2023-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000152904.title: SPEAK UP TO START UP A GREEN WORLD
2023-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000152904.summary:
<< Background >>

PRIMARY NEEDS: 
- The diversity of pupils in our classrooms. We have addressed the need to look for strategies to include pupils in activities with an international scope.
- Promotion of the scientific approach and active methodologies in the classroom, such as STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Maths) and TEAL (Technology-Enhanced Active Learning).
- Updating the use of methodologies that incorporate Information and Communication Technology tools. 
- Promote a culture of active participation in environmental conservation. 
SECONDARY NEEDS: 
- High rates of early school leaving, especially in Secondary Education and school failure. 
COLLATERAL EFFECTS: 
- Strengthening the internationalisation of schools. 
- Promotion of European identity and values.
- Interaction between pupils or teachers from different countries to improve their communicative competence in several languages (Italian, English and Spanish).
- Active participation of pupils in favour of environmentally relevant issues, and development of social and civic competences.
- Increased interest in science-related studies on the part of female pupils.

<< Objectives >>

The general objectives to be achieved are:
A. To favour the inclusion of students who are disadvantaged by different obstacles, and their relationship with other European peers.
B. To make students aware of the importance of caring for the environment and to develop in them a sense of responsibility as well as sustainable and proactive behaviour.
C. To acquire experience and skills in the use of ICT tools, promoting their use in order to favour the inclusion of all pupils.
D. Develop an active learning mode through creative learning, STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Mathematics) and TEAL (Technology Enhanced Active Learning).
E. To provide teachers with environmentally friendly teaching strategies and methodologies based on cooperation between European schools.

These objectives were formulated on the basis of the selected priorities: 
- Inclusion and diversity (objectives A and C).
- Environment and combating climate change (objectives B and E).
- Promoting interest and excellence in science, technology, engineering and mathematics and the STEM approach (D).

<< Implementation >>

The different activities were divided into five work packages, each of them taking place in the municipalities of the participating countries (Spain, Portugal, Italy and Croatia). The last work package took place in the city of Brussels. We have implemented:
-Training activities addressed to teachers (STEAM and TEAL) in the form of workshops and lectures given by experts in the field.
-Visits with students to natural areas, science museums and environmental centres in the participating countries.
-Pedagogical activities through STEAM and TEAL methodologies, with all students.
-STEAM and TEAL workshops.
-Discussions and recording of podcasts and audio.
-Activities related to the use of ICT tools and the use of eTwinning (ESEP), videoconferences to celebrate World Water Day and World Environment Day. 
-Visits to European institutions to present the pupils' proposals.
-Dissemination activities: articles in school digital magazines, use of social networks, talks to different areas of the educational community, interviews for school radio.


<< Results >>

1) MEASURABLE RESULTS:
-Web. 
-Video summary of each work package.
-Twinspace with public pages.
-Newsletters 1 and 2 in Italian, English, Portuguese, Croatian and Spanish.
-Podcast (5).
-Educational guide ‘Protecting the environment and combating climate change’. 
-STEAM classroom in each school, with the necessary equipment to carry out the activities.
-Manual of good practices in eco-sustainable centres.
2) UNMEASURABLE RESULTS:
-Development of intercultural competences and reduction of behaviours and attitudes denoting discrimination or racism in the school community.
-Improved access, participation, motivation and learning achievement of disadvantaged pupils.
-Promoting the inclusion of people disadvantaged by various barriers.
-Integration of good practice related to the environment and the scientific approach.
-Improvement in languages, management skills and internationalisation strategies.
-More positive attitude towards the European project and EU values.
-Development of knowledge and understanding of European education systems, acquiring competences, methods and professional practices.
-Integration of ICT in the activities.

2023-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000153474.title: Assistance for Skilled Environmental Teaching
2023-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000153474.summary:
<< Background >>

ASSET was initiated in response to a clear gap in the readiness of teachers to deliver effective climate and environmental education in European schools. As highlighted in the European Commission’s 2020 survey on climate education, teachers reported insufficient knowledge, resources, and empowerment to integrate environmental topics into their teaching practice. While most agreed that schools should play a central role in raising students’ awareness of climate change, the curriculum often lacked sufficient coverage and teachers frequently felt unprepared to address the topic.

Our consortium identified two core needs: 1. To strengthen teachers’ competences and confidence in environmental education; and 2. To provide them with accessible, innovative, and high-quality learning materials that could be integrated across different subject areas. Through this project, we aimed to respond to these needs by creating professional development opportunities, equipping educators with practical tools, and promoting cooperation with schools, NGOs, and teacher training organizations. ASSET addressed a key European priority: supporting teachers as drivers of sustainability awareness and equipping young learners to face climate change challenges.

<< Objectives >>

ASSET set out to address the insufficient preparation of teachers to deliver climate and environmental education, and the lack of adequate curricular focus on sustainability. Our main objective was to strengthen teachers’ skills and confidence in this field, equipping them with innovative tools and materials to better integrate environmental issues into their teaching practice.

More specifically, the project aimed to:

Develop an innovative methodological guidebook and a set of interactive learning materials, supporting teachers in delivering engaging, practice-oriented climate education (IO1 and IO2).

Create a policy toolkit to inform decision-makers and experts, providing recommendations for integrating scarcity-related environmental topics into primary education (IO3).

Apply a complex, interdisciplinary approach, focusing on key areas such as agro-farming, waste management, energy efficiency, water management, and biodegradation, in order to give teachers and students a deeper understanding of environmental challenges.

Disseminate and test these outputs through international and local events (teacher trainings, a student camp, dissemination workshops, and Climate Clubs), ensuring evaluation, visibility, and sustainability.

<< Implementation >>

During the project we successfully implemented all planned activities, ensuring a smooth and collaborative process among partners. The main achievements were:

- Development of intellectual outputs: We elaborated the ASSET Methodological Guidebook for Teachers (IO1) and the ASSET Environmental Learning Materials (IO2). 

- Capacity-building for teachers and students: We organized one transnational teacher training event (C1), where educators from partner countries were introduced to the guidebook and learning materials and exchanged best practices. In addition, we held an international student camp (C2), which allowed students to experience interactive environmental learning activities and provided an opportunity to pilot the project’s outputs in a real educational setting.

- Dissemination activities: Each partner organized at least one national multiplier workshop (E1–E7), reaching local teachers, schools, NGOs, and other stakeholders. 

- Final conference: At the end of the project, we held an international closing conference (E8), gathering representatives of educational institutions, NGOs, and policymakers. 

- Policy Toolkit (IO3): comprehensive set of recommendations and best practices for decision-makers.

<< Results >>

The project produced three main intellectual outputs: the ASSET Methodological Guidebook for Teachers, which provides a practical framework for integrating environmental topics into education; the ASSET Environmental Learning Materials, developed in seven thematic modules to support interactive classroom practice; and the Policy Toolkit, offering recommendations for decision-makers and experts. These outputs were tested and applied through a transnational teacher training, an international student camp, and national multiplier events, complemented by a final international conference that ensured wide dissemination and visibility. As a result, teachers enhanced their skills and confidence in climate education, students developed greater environmental awareness and motivation, and policymakers and stakeholders increased their understanding of how sustainability can be embedded in school systems. In addition, the project fostered knowledge transfer across local and international contexts, building networks and partnerships that will continue to promote climate education beyond the project’s lifetime.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2023-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000155244.title: Art for Heart's Sake
2023-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000155244.summary:
<< Objectives >>

‘Art for Heart’s Sake’, is an ambitious creative project designed to impact positively on schools’ ability to meet the needs of diverse groups. The project objectives are to promote inclusion and diversity and enhance key competences. These will be achieved through participation in creative arts. The project will particularly support disadvantaged and marginalised participants and those who suffer from poor mental health. It will promote creativity and its benefits, in all our organisations.

<< Implementation >>

The activities will be an exploration of individual cultural arts heritage, and collaborating to create a fusion of this knowledge into innovative arts resources: a playscript, dances, musical pieces, costumes, scenery, artworks, digital media and performance. These will be born out of students’ ideas, during transnational meetings and pursued by school communities thereafter. Key competences will be advanced during group work in schools and support for inclusion will ensure full participation.

<< Results >>

The project will result in a staff better equipped to meet the needs of students, synergies between organisations outside of education, happier, creative communities that encourage inclusion, diversity, better mental health and well-being. The project will result in green practices being embedded in schools and a suite of creative arts resources available open-source. Students will have enhanced key competences, and through transnational participation, have gained new experiences and friends.

2023-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000165096.title: Tell Your Mind: Voicing mental health conditions and promoting socio-emotional well-being in secondary schools

2023-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000155095.title: Plural Words
2023-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000155095.summary:
<< Background >>

Le projet Plural Words est né du constat persistant des inégalités de communication dans les écoles européennes. De nombreux enfants restent marginalisés par des troubles du langage, des handicaps auditifs, des troubles DYS, l’autisme, la trisomie 21 ou la barrière de la langue. Ces difficultés limitent leur accès aux apprentissages et nuisent à leur inclusion. Le projet répond au manque de formation et de ressources accessibles en Communication Alternative et Améliorée (CAA) dans les établissements scolaires. Il vise à combler le fossé entre les initiatives associatives et le système éducatif, encore peu familiarisé avec ces outils. Le partenariat européen, rassemblant experts de la CAA, enseignants et acteurs culturels, s’est donné pour mission de démocratiser l’usage de la CAA et de promouvoir une communication inclusive dès l’école primaire, afin de garantir l’égalité des chances pour tous les élèves.

<< Objectives >>

Plural Words avait pour objectif principal d’encourager l’usage de la CAA dans les contextes scolaires afin de rendre l’apprentissage plus inclusif et équitable. Le projet visait à former les enseignants et professionnels de l’éducation à ces approches inclusives et à leur fournir des outils concrets : mallettes pédagogiques, modules e-learning, et ressources en libre d’accès. Par une approche créative fondée sur les pictogrammes, les gestes et les supports visuels, le projet a cherché à renforcer les compétences de communication des élèves, en particulier ceux rencontrant des difficultés d’expression ou de compréhension. Enfin, nous voulions créer une dynamique européenne autour de la CAA, pour échanger nos expériences, confronter nos approches et progresser ensemble vers des pratiques éducatives plus inclusives et accessibles.

<< Implementation >>

Les activités ont été réparties en 5 work packages menés tout au long du projet par le partenariat : 
WP1 •  La gestion de projet (coordination générale du projet, suivi administratif et financier, évaluation et contrôle qualité) 
WP2 • Cadre méthodologique
A1/ Collection de bonnes pratiques
A2/ Guide pédagogique
A3/ Mallettes pilotes
WP3 •  Formation
A1/ Quiz pour les enseignants
A2/ Cours e-learning
A3/ Activité de formation à Mons (France)
WP4 • Mallettes de CAA
A1/ Mallettes de CAA
A2/ Séquences pédagogiques
A3/ Livre blanc
WP5 • Communication, dissémination et exploitation 
A1/ Communication
A2/ Dissémination 
A3/ Exploitation
À ces activités, s’ajoutent : 
-> l’organisation de 3 réunions transnationales en présentiel
-> l’organisation de  9 réunions virtuelles
-> l’organisation de 9 événements de dissémination en présentiel et en ligne ayant eu lieu en septembre 2025.

<< Results >>

Le projet Plural Words a permis la livraison d’un site internet multilingue (https://plural-words.eu/fr/) hébergeant l’ensemble des ressources du projet, dans les langues nationales des partenaires et en anglais :

2023-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000158225.title: CogniQuest
2023-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000158225.summary:
<< Background >>

Le projet CogniQuest est né d’un constat partagé par les partenaires : si la métacognition est largement reconnue comme un levier essentiel pour la réussite scolaire, elle reste peu mise en œuvre dans les classes, en particulier auprès des élèves de 8 à 12 ans. Les enseignants et éducateurs manquent de ressources concrètes, accessibles et adaptées à cet âge pour aider les élèves à réfléchir sur leurs stratégies d’apprentissage, leurs erreurs, leur motivation et leurs émotions.

Par ailleurs, de nombreux élèves rencontrent des difficultés d’apprentissage, un manque de confiance ou un risque de décrochage précoce, souvent lié à une faible maîtrise des stratégies d’apprentissage. Les partenaires ont identifié un besoin fort de ressources pratiques, inclusives et non stigmatisantes, capables de toucher des publics divers (élèves ordinaires, dispositifs relais, élèves à besoins éducatifs particuliers).

CogniQuest répond ainsi à un double besoin : outiller les enseignants avec des supports clés en main et permettre aux élèves de devenir des apprenants plus conscients, autonomes et engagés.

<< Objectives >>

L’objectif principal de CogniQuest était d’intégrer la métacognition dans les pratiques éducatives du primaire de manière ludique, accessible et durable. 

Le projet visait à :
1/ développer les compétences métacognitives des élèves (planifier, s’auto-évaluer, ajuster ses stratégies) ;
2/ soutenir les enseignants et éducateurs avec des ressources prêtes à l’emploi ;
3/ favoriser l’inclusion et la réussite de tous les élèves, notamment ceux en difficulté ;
4/ proposer une approche innovante combinant narration, jeu et réflexion guidée ;
5/ diffuser une culture de la métacognition au sein des établissements scolaires européens.

À travers une coopération transnationale, le projet souhaitait également garantir la transférabilité des outils à différents contextes éducatifs et linguistiques, tout en assurant un accès libre aux résultats.

<< Implementation >>

Le projet a été mis en œuvre sur 2 ans par 5 organisations européennes. 

Les principales activités ont inclus :
1/ la conception collaborative de guides pédagogiques sur la métacognition ;
2/ la création de 10 livres d’aventure intégrant des choix et des questions réflexives ;
3/ le développement d’une toolkit comprenant des affiches, des exercices de réflexion, des templates prêts à l’emploi et un jeu de cartes ;
4/ la constitution de groupes de travail associant enseignants, conseillers pédagogiques et experts ;
5/ des phases de test avec des élèves et enseignants dans les 5 pays partenaires ;
6/ l’organisation de réunions transnationales et d’événements multiplicateurs ;

Toutes les ressources ont été produites et traduites dans les cinq langues du partenariat (EN, FR, HR, PL, GR) et sont librement accessibles sur le site internet du projet : cogniquest.eu

<< Results >>

Les principaux résultats tangibles sont les suivants :
1/ 4 guides pédagogiques à destination des enseignants, éducateurs et professionnels de l’éducation,
2/ 60 outils pour les élèves, comprenant des exercices de réflexion et des templates prêts à l’emploi
3/ 4 affiches pédagogiques
4/ 1 jeu de cartes “Metacog’mission”  favorisant l’échange, la verbalisation des stratégies d’apprentissage et la coopération entre élèves ;
5/ 10 histoires, intégrant des choix et des questions réflexives pour encourager la prise de recul sur les processus d’apprentissage.
Ces ressources ont été testées et validées dans des contextes éducatifs variés, avec plus de 340 élèves et 25 enseignants directement impliqués dans les phases de test du projet.
Les résultats ont été valorisés lors des événements finaux, rassemblant 479 participants (enseignants, formateurs, chercheurs, décideurs éducatifs).
Enfin, plus de 50 000 personnes ont été touchées par les actions de dissémination. 

Le projet a ainsi contribué de manière significative à diffuser durablement une culture de la métacognition au sein du secteur scolaire européen, en proposant des outils concrets, accessibles et transférables à différents contextes éducatifs.

2023-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000159511.title: Des métiers pour une planète plus durable
2023-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000159511.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to this project following a mobility program in Finland for several school psychologists (CIO Dijon) in May 2022. We observed that the topic of "environmental issues" was not approached in the same way by Finnish and French students.
It therefore seemed important to create an Erasmus+ KA2 cooperation partnership project between several European countries.
The CIO Dijon and the Lycée Gustave Eiffel, with its science and technology-focused programs, decided to join forces on the project.

The objectives were to:

- help students combat eco-anxiety by enabling them to better understand climate issues and the solutions available in the partner countries (scientific, technological, and agricultural) ;
- empower them to be both observers and active participants in these solutions.

The goal for the partner countries was to show students from five countries the consequences of climate change in Europe and its impact on the new jobs that young people will be able to enter very soon. The Dijon CIO (the only European relay CIO in the Academy) wanted to implement its professional expertise in a European project, serving students.

<< Objectives >>

The partner countries aimed to develop the following skills in students:

- the ability to work in groups on shared topics prior to the exchanges.

- a sense of belonging to European citizenship.

- recognition of the contribution of science to the fight against climate change (for students who have chosen scientific specializations such as Engineering or STEM).

- psychosocial skills.

- English language skills.

- environmental awareness and an assessment of their own eco-anxiety.

- a sense of competence to meet the challenges of tomorrow related to climate change.

- the "ecological" dimension of the career guidance projects of final-year students.

For teachers and adults in the schools involved in the project:
- the ability to organize, coordinate, budget, and plan a large-scale project = to unite and involve adults with diverse profiles and skills around a project serving students from 5 different countries.

The partners wanted to place students in the role of researchers and agents of change.
To develop an understanding of sustainable urban development as a response to climate change.
To strengthen international cooperation.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented preparatory activities for the mobility program (pre-task activities + questionnaire on psychosocial skills).
We planned and organized the mobility sessions in the five partner countries and the activities during the mobility week.
These included company visits related to the theme chosen by the host country.
We initiated coordination efforts among the adults involved (teachers, guidance counselors from the CIO, headteachers, and administrators).
We created an eTwinning platform.
We sought to disseminate the project in each country and to local academic bodies: In France: Drareic, Maison de l'Europe, DSDEN21, and CIO Dijon. Each country participated in Erasmus Days and organized information sessions for families and participating students.

<< Results >>

The students produced videos (pre-task interviews with professionals in each country).
The students created a booklet, "J4SP in Action."
The teachers compiled all the teaching sequences implemented in each country into a booklet.
Two films were made by a professional during the first and last exchanges in France. These two films allowed the project to be disseminated to parents, teachers, and students at the high school, as well as to the staff at the Dijon Career Guidance Center (CIO).

2023-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000166552.title: SAY (Solidarity is About Youth ) : The voice of fraternity
2023-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000166552.summary:
<< Background >>

This project addresses several current societal issues. The rise of conservatism and nationalism is challenging democratic foundations and encouraging the resurgence of discrimination. At the same time, the Covid-19 crisis exacerbated social and educational inequalities, undermining the sense of national and European belonging among some young people, while limiting their access to cultural and artistic activities. These developments also highlight the fragility of the principle of solidarity and the limitations of formal education alone in responding to these challenges.

In light of these observations, several needs have been identified: supporting teachers with relevant training and educational resources; building bridges between formal and non-formal education; promoting the active participation of young people through popular education; ensuring equal access to inclusive citizenship and artistic education; promoting the European values of diversity and tolerance. 

These elements were highlighted in the Erasmus+ RAIN.BOW project report (2020) and at the Forum on the Future of Citizenship and Human Rights Education organised by the Council of Europe in 2022.


<< Objectives >>

1/ For young people:
 
Promote (European) citizenship
through learning values such as equality, fraternity, and solidarity
reflect on the principle of diversity by identifying forms of discrimination
develop their critical thinking skills
develop their ability to communicate with others
Promote artistic and cultural education
Develop young people's ability to analyze images and their messages
Encourage creativity through writing and photography workshops

2/ For educators/teachers:

Raise awareness of popular education methods
Strengthen their project-based teaching skills
Provide them with resources to enrich and diversify their citizenship education missions

3/ Main expected results:

Participation of 1,300 young people in choosing themes and photos
Creation of two toolkits for teachers
Training for 275 teachers
Participation of 10,250 students in the workshops offered
Organisation of a photo contest for students and creation of an exhibition
Creation of a website accessible in seven languages
Organisation of national and European dissemination events



<< Implementation >>

Activities carried out as part of the project:

1/ For consortium partners:
-Participation in training dedicated to image reading and writing, necessary to establish a common skill base before selecting photos and creating toolkits for teachers.

2/ For teachers:
-Development and provision of toolkits
-Implementation of training for the educational community
-Ready-to-use artistic and educational workshops

3/ For pupils/young people:
-Consultation with young people: participation in choosing the themes and photographs selected for the two editions
-Workshops organised by teachers using the toolkits 
-Participation in image reading and creative writing workshops 
-Sending postcards with messages of friendship 
-Organisation of a photo competition for pupils and creation of an exhibition based on the winning photos 

4/ For the visibility of the project:
-Creation of a European website available in seven languages. Educational resources, project news and a map of participating establishments are available on the website.
-Organisation of dissemination events: six national and one European.


<< Results >>

The concrete results of the project are the following: 

-Participation of 3,321 young people in choosing themes and photos (WP2)

-Creation of two toolkits of approximately 70 pages (one per year) for educators and teachers (WP2)

-389 teachers trained in the use of the toolkits, who continue to use them even after the end of the project (WP3)

-Participation of 46851 pupils in image reading and writing workshops (WP3)

-Organisation of a photo competition for pupils and creation of an exhibition based on the winning photos (WP3)

-46,851 pupils from 946 schools took part in sending 15,864 messages of solidarity in the form of postcards (photos taken by artists and texts written by young people) to their own countries and throughout Europe

2023-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000158622.title: Biljna pozornica
2023-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000158622.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we recognized the urgent need to raise awareness about the importance of the plant world and responsible human behavior towards the environment. By analyzing the current state of the educational system, we identified a lack of effective and innovative teaching methods addressing climate change and nature protection. The need we addressed was the development of new learning approaches through research work, teamwork, creative methods such as theatrical expression, and cross-curricular topic integration. Students actively participated in the process instead of passive listening, developing their own responsibility, creativity, and collaboration skills. Teachers created and improved teaching scenarios, and through dissemination, the project also influenced the wider community. With further use of the developed teaching scenarios in fields such as biology, chemistry, art, ecology, and more, both teachers and students involved will remain active participants in an educational process characterized by innovation in teaching methods. The long-term goal is to reduce the negative impact of human activities and encourage sustainable habits among all participants and the broader community.

<< Objectives >>

Within the project, we implemented various activities aimed at raising awareness about the importance of preserving the environment and the plant world. By creating educational scenarios, the participating organizations established a foundation for the final product that will serve as a tool for further education and promotion of sustainable development. Workshops were held in each participating country, focusing on specific environmental problems present in those areas, where participants worked together to find acceptable and practical solutions. The association moderated all activities using creative and informal methods to encourage active involvement and exchange of experiences. Special attention was given to innovative approaches to education, including stage performances where plants symbolically “spoke” about the need to protect the environment and their essential role in ecosystems. This approach enabled participants to gain new knowledge interactively, raise awareness of human impact, and be encouraged to share what they learned within their communities.

<< Implementation >>

In the project, we carried out activities aimed at raising awareness about the importance of protecting the environment and the plant world. By creating educational scenarios, the participating organizations laid the foundation for a final product to be used for further education and promotion of sustainable development. Workshops were organized in each partner country to address specific environmental issues and to develop acceptable and practical solutions. The association moderated these activities using creative and informal methods to encourage active participation and exchange of ideas. Special focus was given to innovative educational approaches, including stage performances where plants symbolically “spoke” about the need to protect the environment and their role in the ecosystem. This approach allowed participants to gain knowledge in an engaging way, become aware of the impact of human activities, and be motivated to share what they learned within their communities.

<< Results >>

The concrete results of our project included a range of tangible and lasting outputs, as well as additional achievements contributing to a long-term impact on participants and the wider community. We produced a book in digital and printed form, encompassing all key knowledge, experiences, and methods used during the project. Detailed educational scenarios were developed as tools for teachers and educators to convey knowledge about global warming, human impact on climate change, and the importance of preserving medicinal and spice plants. Presentations were held in partner countries based on project themes: Global Warming, Individual Impact, Art Analysis, and Medicinal and Spice Plants. Performances were organized as examples of good practice, promoting creative expression and environmental awareness. The project enhanced participants’ dramatic, artistic, creative, and teamwork skills, as well as language and digital competencies. Additionally, project activities emphasized the importance of recycling as a key step in preserving the planet, encouraging changes in habits and the adoption of sustainable practices in everyday life.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2023-1-IE01-KA220-SCH-000152387.title: Early childhood behaviour management training for preschool teachers through a digital game
2023-1-IE01-KA220-SCH-000152387.summary:
<< Background >>

This project responds to a critical gap in accessible, evidence-based training for preschool teachers working with children with autism. Preschool educators play a vital role in early development and wellbeing, yet many lack specialised preparation in Applied Behaviour Analysis (ABA). To bridge the gap between current practice and best practice, we developed an evidence-based ABA training package consisting of a comprehensive curriculum and a practical handbook. It provides hands-on learning across theoretical foundations, practical applications, and real-life case studies, equipping teachers to create positive, supportive and inclusive learning environments. To increase engagement and usability, the package is delivered in an innovative digital game-based format that supports self-paced learning. By investing in teachers’ professional development, we aimed to strengthen inclusive early years provision and improve educational outcomes for children with autism and their peers.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to improve the quality of support provided to children with autism by equipping preschool teachers with training and resources on evidence-based interventions. We also sought to raise awareness and increase understanding of autism among preschool teachers and the wider community through local awareness-raising events, strengthening inclusive practice. In addition, we aimed to empower teachers to deliver effective early interventions by developing and delivering a comprehensive training programme to enhance behaviour management skills and confident use of evidence-based strategies. Finally, we sought to reduce stress and burnout by providing the knowledge and tools teachers need to cope and be effective in their roles, supporting professional wellbeing and sustainability.

<< Implementation >>

We developed a comprehensive training and educational package, including curriculum materials and a practical handbook, providing preschool teachers with evidence-based ABA resources for supporting children with autism. We also designed a digital interactive game with branching scenarios to enhance the package, enabling learners to safely practise behaviour management strategies in realistic simulated situations. To support sustainability and wider reach, we delivered a train-the-trainer activity to build capacity among key educators to cascade the programme. Finally, we ran local teacher training activities in each partner country, delivering the package with hands-on learning adapted to local contexts and needs.

<< Results >>

The project supported the creation of more positive and safe learning environments for young children, including children with autism, by equipping preschool teachers to implement evidence-based ABA strategies that encourage participation, confidence, and development.

By strengthening teachers’ skills, resources, and confidence, the project helped reduce professional strain and supported wellbeing, with educators feeling better prepared to manage challenging situations and meet children’s needs.

Through improved early intervention and behaviour support practices, the project contributed to better conditions for children’s learning and development, particularly for children with autism, by promoting consistent, structured, and inclusive classroom support.

By building educator capacity and sharing evidence-based inclusive practice across partner countries, the project contributed to improving the quality of early childhood education and care provision, supporting longer-term strengthening of practice within participating settings.

2023-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000151980.title: English as Maths Speech
2023-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000151980.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project in response to the growing need to support students who are learning maths through a second language, particularly English. Studies on the relationship between English proficiency and success in maths have shown that limited English skills often lead to difficulties in understanding mathematical concepts, resulting in lower academic performance. Maths, while universal in many ways, still relies heavily on specific vocabulary, syntax, and logical reasoning, which can be a barrier for non-native speakers. In Greece, our partner university conducted a survey among international students and found that 75% of them felt insecure when learning in a language that is not their mother tongue. In Turkey, where classrooms often include students from various countries, 90% of teachers reported challenges in managing linguistic diversity in their classrooms. In Italy, it was observed that both graduates who continued their studies abroad and foreign students enrolled in their school faced significant challenges in understanding maths in English. EMS was created to address these needs by developing strategies and tools that help students overcome language barriers in maths and improve their academic success.

<< Objectives >>

Our main goal was to support both students and teachers who face difficulties in teaching or learning mathematics in English, especially when their language proficiency is not strong enough, despite appearing fluent in everyday communication. These challenges become even more significant in academic settings, where subject-specific terminology and complex reasoning are required. Through this project, we aimed to create a valuable and practical resource for students and teachers working or studying in a foreign country for various reasons.
The EMS project seeks to address a commonly overlooked gap in language education by introducing an innovative approach that connects language learning directly with mathematical thinking. Our objective was to enhance understanding, increase academic success, and promote more inclusive and effective teaching practices in multilingual and multicultural learning environments.

<< Implementation >>

Throughout the project, we implemented a wide range of local, regional, international, and virtual activities, each designed to serve different objectives.
At the local and regional level, we organized dissemination and informative meetings, collaborated closely with associated partners, and conducted multiplier events to raise awareness and promote the project's outcomes within our communities.
At the international level, we held online coordination meetings, transnational project meetings (TPMs), and Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities (LTTAs), bringing together partners from different countries to share knowledge, develop resources, and ensure consistent progress.
For virtual and dissemination purposes, we made active use of social media, engaged with the press and media outlets, and launched an eTwinning project to broaden outreach and foster collaboration among educators.
In terms of key outputs, two major results of the project include the development of an Open Educational Resources (OER) platform and a dedicated Mobile App, both aimed at supporting the teaching and learning of mathematics in English as a second language.

<< Results >>

The main concrete outputs of our project were the development of an Open Educational Resources (OER) platform and a Mobile App, both designed to provide rich educational content for teaching and learning mathematics in English. These tools include a wide range of materials that present key mathematical concepts in both the students' mother tongue and English, helping bridge the language gap that often hinders understanding and performance.
Through these outputs, we aimed to achieve the following results:
Increase students’ success in mathematics lessons taught in English
Improve students’ language proficiency, especially in academic and subject-specific English
Create a supportive learning environment for both educators and learners
Reduce the number of failures and dropouts among students struggling with language-related barriers in maths education
By combining language learning with subject content, our project addressed a critical need in multilingual classrooms and provided sustainable, accessible tools for long-term impact.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages
Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2023-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000159230.title: Back to the Games
2023-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000159230.summary:
<< Background >>

The consortium applied to B2Gs project to address the growing need for students to develop healthy habits, improve motor skills and counteract sedentary behaviour, which it is known to increasingly affect their cognitive functions and social-emotional skills, contributing to a lower school performance. Many schools reported limited integration of sport culture into daily learning, leaving students without structured opportunities to be active and to understand the benefits of physical activity for their well-being, strengthening teamwork, health awareness, inclusion and school success. The project also intended to respond to access inequalities to individual and group sports and facilities, ensuring that all students, regardless of background or socio-economic status, could participate to them. 

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of B2Gs project is to contribute to the physical, and therefore to the mental health and overall well-being of pupils and students by returning to the popular childhood games and preferable sports. The project will apply a holistic approach combining sports, games and DIY green activities as a cross sectoral aspect in the school education program thus triggering youngsters’ interest in sports activities.

<< Implementation >>

Besides WP1 for project management and implementation, the following activities have been carried out:
In WP2, partners conducted five national researches and produced one consolidated global report in English. This work combined desk research with interviews involving sports experts in each country, enabling a comprehensive understanding of students’ needs and local sport practices. Findings were summarised and used to refine and finalise the project’s learning objectives.
In WP3, based on the research, the partnership collaboratively developed 45 learning modules (instead of the 15 originally planned). Each module included clear written and visual instructions and guidance; a series of booklets was also additionally produced. The content went through several rounds of amendments and editing to ensure coherence, quality and alignment with the project’s goals.
In WP4, partners defined the platform’s technical and functional specifications and adapted all learning materials into an intuitive digital format. Internal peer reviews ensured consistency across languages and modules. The platform was then externally tested by students, teachers and experts, leading to final improvements before finalisation.

<< Results >>

1. The project conducted in-depth research in each country to define the content for sports, games and DIY green activities, providing a solid evidence base for all pedagogical choices. They were then consolidated into one global report. Students from diverse backgrounds interacted on equal terms, where participation was based on skills and collaboration rather than social status.

2. A set of 45 B2Gs learning modules (instead of the 15 originally planned) was developed, offering structured, engaging activities that promote movement, cooperation and well-being among students. In addition, a series of booklets addressing various topics about health and well-being was developed and included into the platform

3. The B2Gs digital platform was successfully created and made openly accessible, hosting all modules and resources in a user-friendly format. Content is available in each partner country’s language plus English and Ukranian. The platform was designed with accessibility in mind, ensuring that disadvantaged groups could fully benefit from the content.
