2023-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000161081.title: Teachers UPskilling for WELL-being in multicultural classrooms
2023-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000161081.summary:
<< Background >>

The Partnership decided to apply for this project starting from an internal  debate that focused on the following needs, concerning teachers who are working in multicultural environments: 
 
N1: Need to support School Teachers’ professional development and upskilling to apply innovative practices in multicultural and complex environments and culturally relevant pedagogies;

N2: Need to reinforce School Teachers’ sense of self-efficacy and well-being in multicultural and complex teaching environments to improve school climate and foster the creation of safe and inclusive teaching/learning environments;

N3: Need to include well-being of School teachers and attractiveness of the profession, by encouraging inclusiveness and self-efficacy in multicultural and complex environments in education policies;

N4: Need to create and circulate knowledge and resources about Professional Development and self-efficacy in Multicultural Classrooms in the School sector, to promote better pedagogical practices, increase teachers’ well-being and inform policies at EU Level.


<< Objectives >>

UPWELL focused on Professional Development and Teacher Self-Efficiency in Multicultural Classrooms in order to improve teachers well-being, and consequently provide a safe and inclusive space for the students. The Partnership aimed at reaching the following objectives: 

O1 : Contribute to the improvement of School teacher education practices by gathering data and creating resources to address multiculturality and complex challenges in the school sector.

O2 : Develop a sustainable, innovative and accessible training for School teachers to improve their self-efficacy in multicultural and diverse classrooms, support the well-being of School teachers and students, and foster the enhancement of inclusive and diverse learning environments.
O3: Develop and test jointly different models of Training for Trainers (virtual, physical and blended) in initial School teacher education and as part of School teachers’ continuous professional development.
O4: Develop sustainable collaboration between School teacher education providers, Research Institutes, and Continuous Education Organisations, with an impact on the quality of School teacher education in Europe. 


<< Implementation >>

The Development of the Training Strategy (WP2), the Curricula, courses and OERs (WP3), the Pilot Program (WP4) as well as dissemination activities (WP5), through content, target groups, formats, and attention to multilingualism, are oriented towards inclusion and diversity. More in details:

<< Results >>

Report on Teachers needs and skills;
Guidelines for The Curriculum design;
Joint Curriculum;
E.Learning Platform;
Transational LLT activity (ToT – Training of Teachers);
Local Pilot courses for Teachers.


This set of outputs allowed the achievement of the expected results, notably: 

R1 Collaboration and co-creation : UPWELL consortium brings together partners from different fields (Adult Education Providers, SMEs, Training Institutes) from 5 EU countries reinforcing the exchange of good practices among teachers. 
R2 Teachers Empowerment.
R3 Contribution to innovation of School trainers’ practices.
R4 Awareness and mainstream: UPWELL dissemination activities, as well as thorough evaluation and reporting process, culminated in the final version of the Joint Curriculum and related Recommendations,  as well as the Final Conference, has been a contribution for the improvement of Teacher Education Policies at a EU level.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2023-1-LV01-KA220-SCH-000124677.title: Sustainable Solutions
2023-1-LV01-KA220-SCH-000124677.summary:
<< Background >>

he Sustainable Solutions Project (S&S) was created to address the urgent need for stronger climate change education and the lack of resources available in schools. Across Europe, many students and teachers report limited understanding of climate change, while digital skills remain uneven despite being essential for the future workforce. Our consortium of seven partners, including schools, NGOs, and SMEs, came together to combine expertise in climate education and digital learning. Building on previous Erasmus+ experiences, the project focused on empowering teachers, students, and stakeholders with the digital competences needed to design, test, and communicate sustainable solutions. By integrating data analysis, digital literacy, and creative problem-solving into climate education, S&S aimed to close gaps in school curricula, support teachers with innovative resources, and inspire students to take action. The project also aligned with the European Green Deal, the UN Sustainable Development Goals, and the Paris Agreement, ensuring that local activities contributed to global priorities.

<< Objectives >>

The Sustainable Solutions Project (S&S) aimed to increase awareness of climate change and show how digital skills can help address it. Our objectives were to equip teachers, students, and stakeholders with the competences needed to collect and analyze data, design sustainable solutions, and communicate them effectively. We wanted to empower schools and communities to take an active role in the fight against climate change and to build a network of engaged individuals dedicated to sustainability.

To achieve this, the project delivered three intellectual outputs: the Sustainability Problem-Solving Toolkit to guide the design and implementation of solutions, the Eco-Tech Skills Curriculum to strengthen digital and technical competences, and EcoNet, an online platform connecting teachers, students, and partners. Together, these results increased the number of people with the skills and confidence to address environmental issues, supported schools in implementing real solutions, and created opportunities for sharing practices across Europe. By aligning with EU priorities such as the Green Deal, digital skills development, and sustainability education, S&S contributed to building a more climate-aware and future-ready generation.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through a series of structured activities that combined management, development, training, piloting, and dissemination. It began with the Kick-off Meeting in Latvia, where partners aligned objectives and responsibilities. Under WP2, we developed and piloted the Sustainability Problem-Solving Toolkit, supported by an online workshop on digital tools and climate change and local piloting events with teachers and students. WP3 focused on the Eco-Tech Skills Curriculum, tested through an LTT training in Greece, surveys, and classroom piloting to refine modules. WP4 produced EcoNet, a collaborative platform enriched with partner-created resources such as quizzes, videos, challenges, and storytelling, tested through the 3rd online workshop and local piloting. Dissemination activities included 7 multiplier events across all partner countries, extensive use of social media, newsletters, local seminars, and press articles, reaching thousands of stakeholders. Regular online partner meetings, mid-term and final meetings, and continuous quality monitoring ensured smooth coordination, budget control, and progress tracking. Together, these activities ensured the delivery, testing, and promotion of all intellectual ou

<< Results >>

The project achieved both concrete intellectual outputs and broader educational results. Three key resources were developed:

IO1 Sustainability Problem-Solving Toolkit: a practical guide with methods for analysing environmental challenges, planning solutions, and applying digital tools for data collection, monitoring, and communication.

IO2 Eco-Tech Skills Curriculum: a comprehensive eight-module curriculum covering climate awareness, digital mapping, sustainable design, data visualisation, and advocacy. Piloting confirmed its adaptability across classrooms and contexts.

IO3 EcoNet Platform: an interactive online environment offering quizzes, animations, challenges, and project templates, allowing teachers and students to exchange ideas and collaborate on sustainability actions.

Alongside these outputs, the project produced three international online workshops, a training and piloting event in Greece, and 7 multiplier events across partner countries. Dissemination efforts extended the reach to thousands.

The results went beyond materials: surveys confirmed increased awareness of climate change, stronger digital competencies, and improved collaboration between schools and stakeholders. Students gained confidence in problem-sol

2023-1-NO01-KA220-SCH-000159229.summary:

2023-1-NO01-KA220-SCH-000164844.title: DIGITAL CLEAN UP COMPAIGN
2023-1-NO01-KA220-SCH-000164844.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the growing need for awareness around the environmental impact of digitalization and media consumption. As students increasingly rely on cloud storage, streaming, and social media, we identified a lack of understanding about the hidden energy use and e-waste these habits generate. The project aimed to promote more sustainable digital practices through education, collaboration, and creative campaigns.
 
To meet this need, students explored the concept of digital pollution, participated in digital clean-up activities, and produced 55 campaign products to encourage behavior change. Awareness levels improved significantly, and the project fostered critical thinking, media literacy, and environmental responsibility. Teachers and students became more conscious of their digital footprint, and the campaign reached a wide audience through social media. The project addressed a real educational gap by combining environmental awareness with digital competence in a practical and engaging way.


<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to raise awareness of the environmental impact of digital habits and promote more sustainable behavior among students and their communities. By focusing on issues like energy use, e-waste, and digital overconsumption, we wanted to empower young people to take action—such as deleting redundant files, extending device lifespan, and reducing screen time. The project addressed key Erasmus+ priorities: fighting climate change, supporting digital transformation, and developing key competences. Through international collaboration, creative media production, and peer learning, students became more conscious of their digital footprint and gained skills in communication, critical thinking, and civic engagement. Our goal was not only to inform, but to inspire lasting change in digital behavior—locally and across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented a wide range of activities to raise awareness about digital pollution. Students participated in international exchanges in Slovenia, Croatia, and Norway, where they created posters, short films, and social media campaigns. Each exchange included expert talks, creative workshops, and collaborative group work. A key activity was the “Digital Clean-Up,” where students and teachers deleted unnecessary files and emails to reduce their digital footprint. Campaign materials were shared on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and the project website. Pre- and post-surveys measured awareness and behavior change. Social activities were also included to build friendships and promote intercultural understanding. Teachers supported students throughout, and all partners contributed to planning, logistics, and evaluation. A final teacher meeting was held in Spain to assess the project and complete the final report. The project combined education, creativity, and action to promote sustainable digital habits.

<< Results >>

The project produced a total of 55 campaign products, including 24 posters, 5 films for youtube, 18 short clips for social media content and 7 behind the scenes short clips, all created by students in international teams. A booklet summarizing key messages was also developed. These materials were shared on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, reaching thousands of young people across Europe. Four digital clean-up events were held, involving over 1000 students and teachers, resulting in the deletion of terabytes of unnecessary data. Surveys showed increased awareness of digital pollution, with students reporting behavior changes such as deleting files and reducing screen time. Teachers integrated the topic into lessons, and the campaign was presented at national and international events. The project fostered digital competence, environmental responsibility and intercultural collaboration.

2023-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000151657.title: Act eco-locally to change into eco-globally
2023-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000151657.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project because environmental education is rarely used in high school curricula in many European countries, especially in vocational schools, so it needs further exploration. We thought that students needed knowledge, skills, values & attitudes that would enable them to contribute to sustainable development & to organise or participate in ecological actions, which develop communicative & social skills. In this way they would become aware of the benefits of responsible interaction with the environment.
Many teenagers especially from vocational schools don’t have proper ecological & consumer habits. They aren’t aware of importance of ecological actions, protecting the nature, being green & climate changes. We noticed a strong need to arm students with ecological & consumer habits & eco skills to prepare them to become more conscious consumers, more active & more ecologically oriented European citizens.
The main purpose of having this partnership project was to create awareness that the existing environmental problems we face in today’s world are global & similar in European countries. We wanted our students to get to know new ways to protect the environment & learn how to act locally to change into globally.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project we wanted to raise awareness about environmental issues & encourage more sustainable behavior among students, teachers & the community. Our goals were to help young people understand the importance of protecting the planet, develop eco-friendly habits & take part in practical activities like clean-ups & upcycling workshops. We wanted to achieve changes in consumer habits, in attitudes towards recycling &climate change, to increase motivation to save &reuse products. Thus, our main objective was to develop the ecological awareness & active citizenship & to increase the quality & relevance of ecological activities in 6 partner schools.
Our goal was to develop in our students key competences (digital, linguistic, entrepreneurial, etc.) & skills needed for the society like: problem solving, critical thinking, teamwork, decision making & creativity. They were developed through local & international ecological activities in interactive forms & methods: workshops, lectures, study visits, debates, greening activities etc.
We also aimed to strengthen cooperation between partner schools, share good practices between teachers & give students the chance to learn & work together with others from different countries

<< Implementation >>

We carried out 2 TPMs (Getting to know each other in Poland & Closing the project in Turkiye) & 6 short-term teacher-student meetings called eco-workshops with: 6 public events called “Be eco”, 17 local green activities, 10 study visits to ecological institutions, 13 lessons observed. We established 5 eco-clubs.

We worked on the eTwinning platform & Twin space, disseminated the results on the project website, Facebook & Instagram. We carried out monitoring completing 13 monitoring sheets &evaluation activities. Turkiye organised a final conference where 6 final PPTs and 6 film from eco-workshops were presented.
In total 46 teachers &159 students from 6 partner schools were directly involved in the project.

2023-1-PT01-KA220-SCH-000154858.title: We are all beautiful in our diversity
2023-1-PT01-KA220-SCH-000154858.summary:
<< Background >>

All partner schools recognised the increasing importance of inclusive education. There was a clear need to address the exclusion of students based on differences such as disability, race, language, religion, gender, or socioeconomic background. Our aim was to respond to this reality by fostering inclusive practices in our schools and communities.
Inclusive education provided all students with the opportunity to develop the attitudes, values, and skills required to live and work in a diverse society. It also promoted more effective and equitable learning experiences for all. We strongly believed that inclusion was a lifelong learning process, benefitting individuals and societies alike, and grounded on the principles of respect, relationships, and responsibility – the three R’s of inclusion.
Through the planned activities, students acquired knowledge and skills on inclusion and diversity; developed empathy, self-confidence, and self-esteem; and improved key competences such as intercultural understanding, digital literacy, language and communication, teamwork, and decision-making.
We were convinced that inclusion could only be fully achieved through cooperation and the active participation of all.




<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to raise awareness about the importance of inclusion.
We aimed to offer participants meaningful opportunities to acquire knowledge, develop attitudes and build competences that would enable them to actively combat discrimination and inequality.
This learning process was intended to promote lasting changes in behaviour and mindset, encouraging participants to adopt inclusive practices in their daily lives.
They came to understand that every individual deserved to be valued, respected and supported. Only through active citizenship could we foster the values, attitudes, commitment and skills necessary for each person to realise their full potential and contribute positively to society.



<< Implementation >>

Throughout the project, we implemented a wide range of innovative and engaging activities specifically designed for teenagers and adapted to each subtopic related to inclusion and diversity.
We organised several workshops and game-based activities, which proved to be highly effective in fostering participation and reflection. These included:
•	Sports and physical activities that promoted teamwork and respect;
•	Music, dance and performing arts to explore identity and cultural diversity;
•	Creative writing and storytelling, using both contemporary and classical texts;
•	Poetry, drama and role-playing to develop empathy and challenge stereotypes;
•	Visual arts and photography to express inclusive messages;
•	Word games and board games that encouraged cooperation and critical thinking;
•	Debates and video production to give voice to students’ perspectives;
•	Use of digital tools and information technologies to enhance creativity and digital literacy.
These activities not only supported the development of key competences, such as communication, collaboration and critical thinking, but also strengthened students’ awareness of social inclusion, equity, and active citizenship

<< Results >>

Our project generated several tangible and meaningful outputs that could be used beyond the project’s duration. These included:
•	An eBook compiling all the didactic materials developed, which served both as teaching resources and reference materials for educators;
•	Brochures, posters, and postcards designed and produced by students to raise awareness about inclusion;
•	A collection of videos and podcasts created during the workshops;
•	An art exhibition of students’ work from the working teams.
The project also had a significant impact on the personal and social development of the participants. Through the workshops implemented in each work package, students improved their:
•	Communication and language skills (including foreign languages),
•	ICT and digital competences,
•	Critical thinking and problem-solving abilities,
•	Teamwork and friendship skills,
•	Self-esteem and respect for others
•	Empathy and openness to diversity.
The project also had a positive effect beyond the school context. The activities and results extended to the families of the participants, who, through school events — contributing with typical meals, dance groups, and online platforms — became aware of the project’s impact on the community.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2023-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000151960.title: Digital Powered Teaching
2023-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000151960.summary:
<< Background >>

The The Digital Powered Teaching (DPT)  was initiated to respond to the urgent need of partner schools to strengthen their digital readiness and integrate innovative technologies into everyday teaching. Before the project, teachers had limited experience in using digital applications and creating interactive learning materials, while schools lacked structured strategies for digital education. The COVID-19 period revealed gaps in digital competence, collaboration and resilience among teachers and students from partner schools. Therefore, the partnership aimed to improve teachers’ digital pedagogical skills, support the creation of open digital educational resources and promote cross-curricular approaches connecting sciences, arts, humanities, languages with technologies. Students needed more opportunities to develop transversal competences-digital, communication, creativity and collaboration-through international teamwork. The project addressed these needs by providing training, exchanges and joint digital creation activities, ensuring long-term improvement in digital capacity and educational innovation in all four schools.


<< Objectives >>

The four partner schools from Romania, Croatia, Greece and Cyprus have established this partnership, Digital Powered Teaching (DPT),  and set project priorities in order to improve their digital readiness, capacity, resilience and support teachers by implementing the following project objectives: 
O1. Consolidating the digital transformation and enriching the educational school offer of 4 European schools by creating and developing innovative digital didactic materials based on cross-curricular approaches, in a period of 2 years.
O2. Increasing the professional training of 32 teachers from 4 European schools in the field of digital transformation by using digital applications and creating new open digital educational resources for teaching subjects through a transdisciplinary approach, over a period of 2 years.
O3. Enhance the transversal key competences of 72 students (age 13-15 years old) from 4 European schools through using digital applications and creating learning materials, in a period of 2 years.

<< Implementation >>

The project activities were implemented through five work packages.WP1 covered project management: signing bilateral agreements, creating the Steering and Financial Committees, selecting project teams for students and teachers and developing implementation, communication, dissemination and monitoring plans. WP2 included four short-term student exchanges (Croatia,Cyprus,Greece,Romania), where 72 students participated in thematic workshops on sustainability, health education and languages, humanities and science, using various digital applications to enhance digital and communication skills. WP3 focused on collaborative creation and visibility: an online logo competition (111 logos created), continuous updates of the project platform and eTwinning page and four virtual workshops for 100 students after each mobility. WP4 targeted teacher training: one short-term training event in Cyprus and five virtual workshops on digital tools and applications and using project platforms.WP5 covered dissemination -two international online conferences,local/regional dissemination meetings,4 newsletters, articles, interviews and a social media campaign to promote project results and ensure long-term impact.materials created by teachers and students.

<< Results >>

The Digital Powered Teaching project produced a series of tangible digital and educational outputs that supported the achievement of its objectives and contributed to digital transformation in partner schools. A functional online project platform (design by HR team) and an interactive eTwinning page (managed by Greek team) were created and continuously updated with students’ and teachers’ digital materials.Four innovative sets of cross-curricular digital teaching resources have been developed and integrated into classroom practice,grouped into the Digital Collection of Open Educational Resources (OER). An international teacher training event and five virtual workshops improved digital skills in more than 32 teachers, while four short-term student exchanges and four virtual workshops promoted digital collaboration and creativity among more than 72 students.The logo competition engaged over 100 students from partner schools. Two international online conferences, four newsletters, media posts,interviews and dissemination meetings promoted the project results to wider audiences. Management and monitoring tools, implementation, communication, and dissemination plans, ensured effective coordination and sustainability of all activities.

2023-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000166887.title: Exchanging Memories - Memory of the Earth
2023-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000166887.summary:
<< Background >>

The Exchanging Memories – Memory of the Earth (EMME) project was born from the shared need of partner schools and UNESCO Global Geoparks to strengthen environmental education and digital innovation in European classrooms. Teachers across the consortium observed that while students were increasingly connected to technology, they were often disconnected from nature and unaware of the impact of human actions on the planet. 
The project addressed this gap by combining geoscience, culture, and sustainability education through modern teaching tools and experiential learning. By working together with geoparks, the partners aimed to make environmental learning tangible and engaging. By exploring Earth’s long history, students grasped the urgency of protecting it today and recognised their responsibility to safeguard it for future generations.
At the same time, the project responded to teachers’ professional needs — to integrate digital tools, interdisciplinary approaches, and inclusive practices into their teaching. EMME thus emerged as a collective response to the call for a greener, more innovative, and collaborative school education in Europe.

<< Objectives >>

The EMME – Exchanging Memories: Memory of the Earth project aimed to strengthen environmental awareness, digital innovation, and intercultural cooperation among students and teachers from Europe. Its main goal was to connect schools with UNESCO Global Geoparks, turning them into open-air classrooms where learners could explore the history of the Earth and understand the importance of protecting it.
Through joint activities, EMME sought to develop green skills and key competences such as teamwork, critical thinking, and scientific curiosity, while encouraging creativity through media and digital storytelling. Teachers improved their capacity to integrate environmental topics, ICT, and interdisciplinary methods into their lessons.
At the same time, the project aimed to build sustainable partnerships between schools and geoparks, promote Erasmus+ values, and create open educational resources — such as the #EMME Curriculum, the Mobile App, and student video documentaries - that can be used long after the project’s completion. Ultimately, EMME aimed to inspire a generation of responsible, eco-aware young Europeans, capable of transforming knowledge into concrete environmental action.

<< Implementation >>

The EMME project implemented a coherent set of activities combining curriculum design, digital innovation, field learning, and large-scale dissemination. It began with coordination meetings that established the workflow and ensured effective cooperation among schools and UNESCO Global Geoparks.
Under WP2, teachers and experts created the #EMME Curriculum, integrating geoscience and sustainability through classroom and outdoor activities. WP3 expanded the digital dimension with the #EMME App, developed collaboratively by all partners and aligned with the curriculum’s five themes.
WP4 connected students directly with Earth heritage through two international mobilities in the Azores and Hațeg, where they worked with Geopark specialists, conducted field research, and produced the Memories of the Azores and Memories of Hațeg documentaries. Each school also organised extensive follow-up events, workshops, clean-up actions, and awareness campaigns that multiplied the project’s impact.
WP5 ensured visibility and sustainability through the project website, social media channels, printed and digital materials, press, logo competition, and online conferences, making all results publicly accessible and widely used across partner communities.

<< Results >>

The EMME project produced a rich set of innovative and tangible results that connected environmental education, digital learning, and international cooperation. One of its main intellectual output, the #EMME Curriculum, offers a flexible educational framework. Developed with input from UNESCO Global Geoparks and translated into all partner languages, it is now widely used in classrooms and extracurricular eco-activities.
A second major output was the #EMME Mobile App, an interactive digital tool aligned with the curriculum themes. It supports experiential, inquiry-based learning and is already integrated into lessons and local educational programmes.
Students’ creativity and scientific understanding were captured in the two video documentary series — Memories of the Azores and Memories of Hațeg — produced during international mobilities and published on the project website and partners’ platforms.
The project also delivered a complete communication ecosystem: an official website, active Facebook and Instagram channels, printed materials, exhibitions, and press appearances, greatly enhancing Erasmus+ visibility. 
EMME strengthened long-term cooperation between schools and Geoparks, laying the foundation for future joint projects.

2023-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000152116.title: Digital platform for secondary school teachers on adolescent risk behaviours

2023-1-TR01-KA220-SCH-000160579.title: Özel Eğitimde Dijital Dönüşüm
2023-1-TR01-KA220-SCH-000160579.summary:
<< Background >>

Within the scope of our project “Digital Transformation in Special Education”, we aimed to improve the educational quality and life skills of students with special educational needs. To achieve this, we developed an ICT-based application tool, structured course modules and a digital documentation system. A data-driven framework was designed to monitor students’ development across all educational levels and to support teachers in implementing Individualised Education Plans (IEPs) in a more effective and measurable way.

Throughout the project, transnational meetings, short-term staff trainings and multiplier events were organised. Digital content was jointly produced with partner organisations, and a shared web platform was established to ensure access and knowledge exchange. Monitoring and evaluation activities were carried out collaboratively, with quality regularly reviewed to ensure sustainable and transferable results. The project was completed with the objective of strengthening teacher competencies and enabling more effective tracking of students’ individual progress.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to make the education process of students with special educational needs more outcome-oriented, measurable and achievement-based through the implementation of our project. We successfully developed an ICT-based product, a course module and a digital platform that enable holistic monitoring of students’ academic, social and cognitive progress. We also worked to create an integrated digital solution to help teachers prepare Individualised Education Plans (IEPs) in a higher-quality, evidence-based and more consistent way.

By focusing on digital transformation, we strengthened teachers’ competences and brought together project outputs in seven languages on a single platform to build a sustainable, international learning network among special education professionals. In addition, we offered decision-makers a practical and transferable model and supported dissemination by engaging local education authorities. In this way, we completed the project with the overall goal of improving quality in special education, reinforcing inclusive practices and supporting students’ individual potential more effectively.


<< Implementation >>

During the project, we held **four transnational kick-off meetings** and also ran **regular online coordination meetings** with our partners. We carried out a literature review, needs analysis and a current situation assessment. We developed an **ICT-based application tool**, a **course module** and a **digital documentation system**, prepared user guidelines for these tools, and established an **online training platform**.

Within the framework of learning, teaching and training activities, we organised **two short-term staff training events (LTTs)** and worked in a learner-centred way to ensure teachers could use digital tools effectively in practice. To promote and disseminate the project results, we implemented **multiplier events**, workshops and training-oriented sessions. Throughout the process, we conducted continuous online coordination, implemented monitoring and evaluation procedures, and took quality assurance measures with the support of our universities.


<< Results >>

Within our project, we developed an ICT-based **documentation and assessment tool** as a key output. Through this tool, we created a platform that systematically records the academic, social and cognitive development of students with special educational needs. We also ensured data privacy by implementing specific protective measures. In addition, we designed an **IEP preparation module** that supports teachers in making knowledge- and skills-based decisions. A mobile-friendly application was developed to monitor students’ progress, and a user guide was produced to ensure effective use.

We also created a **teacher-focused course module** consisting of digital learning content and established a **sharing-based web platform**. Through this platform, we disseminated educational materials and built an international space for knowledge exchange. Through the LTT activities we delivered, we aimed to strengthen teachers’ digital competences in an outcome-oriented way and reinforce inclusive education practices. Finally, by organising multiplier events and workshops, we supported the sustainability of the project results and delivered a practical, measurable and transferable model for special education.

2023-1-TR01-KA220-SCH-000166932.title: Çevresel sürdürülebilirlik etkinliklerinin yenilikçi dijital araçlarla fen eğitimine entegrasyonu
2023-1-TR01-KA220-SCH-000166932.summary:
<< Background >>

This project was applied for in response to the urgent need to develop an education-based and sustainable solution to the climate crisis, which currently poses a serious threat to humanity and our planet. The intensive use of fossil fuels, the rapid depletion of natural resources and increasing environmental degradation make it essential to achieve a transformation in individuals’ awareness and behaviour. It was considered that such a transformation can only be achieved through a systematic and high-quality educational process.
Key European and international policy frameworks, such as the Europe 2020 Strategy, the OECD Environmental Performance Reviews and the European Green Deal, clearly emphasize the critical role of education in promoting sustainable growth, improving resource efficiency and combating climate change. However, it was identified that within existing teaching and learning processes, environmental sustainability is not sufficiently addressed in a holistic, thematic manner supported by digital tools. This gap constituted the core need that this project aimed to address.
Through the project, it was aimed to increase students’ awareness of environmental sustainability, to foster positive attitudes towards nature.

<< Objectives >>

Implementing this project, the primary objective was to integrate activities designed in line with principles of environmental sustainability education into the teaching and learning process through innovative digital tools, and to foster students’ collective awareness of sustainability and positive attitudes towards nature. By promoting the effective use of digital technologies in education, the project also aimed to create a stronger space for communication and interaction on environmental sustainability among school-based actors.
In this context, the project aimed to develop an e-learning platform including learning outcomes related to environmental sustainability and its sub-components, to provide teachers with an easily applicable and innovative digital resource, and to increase students’ learning motivation through gamified educational content. In parallel, it was planned to support innovative approaches in school education by developing digital materials that complement the Science curriculum.
Another important objective of the project was to support teachers’ professional development in the field of digital methodology during the implementation process, to strengthen cooperation and alignment among international partners.

<< Implementation >>

The project consisted of 5 WPs and all planned activities were successfully completed. Within WP2, a Curriculum Booklet including 72 learning outcomes was developed under the themes of biodiversity, recycling, environmental stresses and renewable energy within the framework of environmental sustainability, and translated into seven languages. Based on these outcomes, an Activity Booklet containing 60 activities was produced, and a user guide for the e-platform was prepared.

Within WP3, an e-learning platform was established and integrated with Moodle to support the dissemination of project outputs. A teacher training event held in Estonia enabled 30 participants to gain competencies in scenario writing. Following the training, partners collaboratively produced 48 educational scenarios, 12 assessment tools and 12 interactive games, and the digitalisation of the content was completed through strong partnership cooperation.

Within WP4, four transnational meetings were organised in Türkiye, Croatia, Spain and Poland to review project progress, digital content development, budget and quality processes. Unexpected risks were effectively managed through strong coordination, and the project outputs were completed in a sustainable manner

<< Results >>

The project produced academic and digital outputs directly applicable at school level. A Curriculum Booklet with 72 learning outcomes structured under four sustainability themes (biodiversity, recycling, environmental stresses and renewable energy) was developed, along with a 60-activity Booklet translated into seven languages. In the digital dimension, 48 storytelling-based scenarios were converted into video materials, supported by 12 digital question banks and 12 interactive games. All resources were published on a Moodle-based e-learning platform with a User Guide to ensure accessibility and structured use. A staff training activity in Estonia strengthened the digital content development skills of 30 participants. The outputs supported digital transformation, environmental awareness and cross-border cooperation. Despite unforeseen challenges, including the loss of the Estonian partner representative, responsibilities were reorganised and all digital outputs were completed successfully, demonstrating strong partnership resilience, effective risk management and sustainable impact.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2024-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000243827.title: Bridging Borders through Citizen Science: Empowering Secondary Education migrant and local students in STEM via Citizen Science for Inclusive Science Literacy Development and Environmental Action.

<< Objectives >>

EcoStories seeks to empower secondary 12-15-year-old migrant students, their peers and teachers in Life Sciences, Design & Technology and Environmental Science classes to participate in Citizen Science projects for climate change whilst promoting migrants’ social inclusion through intercultural methodologies. << Implementation >>

EcoStories develops a Pedagogical E-book, a Customized Citizen Science Repository and STEM-based Lesson Plans. The objective of the project is to create a safe school environment and culture enhancing life-skills where phenomena of school aggression, bullying and hostility will not have place. 2024-1-MK01-KA220-SCH-000253777.title: AI Navigators: Empowering Teachers for the AI Era
2024-1-MK01-KA220-SCH-000253777.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The AI Navigators project aims to boost AI literacy among 120 teachers from North Macedonia, Bulgaria, Croatia, Serbia, and Belgium, fostering their ability to integrate AI into teaching. By training 20 AI Navigators and leveraging mentor-coaching, the initiative seeks to cultivate an educational environment that's innovative and open to AI technologies, thereby shaping future-ready classrooms.

<< Implementation >>

To realize our goals, we will develop a comprehensive AI competence model and produce e-learning materials, including at least 12 videos. The plan includes selecting 100 pilot teachers for AI integration training and executing a pilot phase in classrooms across the partner countries. Dissemination efforts will span informational meetings, social media engagement, and a final conference in Skopje to showcase project achievements.

<< Results >>

We anticipate equipping 120 educators (20 AI Navigators and 100 pilot teachers) with AI integration skills, creating a collaborative network among them across the partner countries. The project will generate a suite of AI-integrated lesson plans, positively shift perceptions towards AI in education, and ensure the broad dissemination of our innovative approach and its benefits to a wider educational community.

2024-1-NL01-KA220-SCH-000254064.title: Making maths more accessible using Game-based learning to create a more inclusive and less stressful environment in the learning of maths
2024-1-NL01-KA220-SCH-000254064.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to raise maths teachers’ and students’ awareness of the problem of maths anxiety (MA) and through that, enable more positive attitudes and ways of teaching and learning maths as well as lowering MA in the society. The main objective is to create a customisable digital learning game that maths teachers in primary and middle schools can use and adapt to increase awareness about MA and support students struggling with MA.

<< Implementation >>

Co-design of the game involves an iterative process led by a multidisciplinary team in which the game is created, tested, and refined with input from students and teachers. The co-design process is informed by a needs analysis which uncovers reasons for math anxiety and identifies effective practices for lowering it. Additionally, Teachers' Professional Development (TPD) will be created to equip teachers to use and adapt the game. Dissemination activities are conducted throughout the project.

<< Results >>

The project publishes a report and a visualized good practices brochure for teachers on the causes and consequences of MA and ways to lower it based on the needs analysis.
The MathifyMe Digital Game is publicly released for worldwide use.
The first results of the field tests and a video guide for the game will be published.
Teachers (n=100) in participating countries will have professional development on MA and the MathifyMe Digital Game. The TPD programme will be published for general use.

hr.name: Sveučilište Josipa Jurja Strossmayera u Osijeku

2024-1-NL01-KA220-SCH-000254671.title: FoodHeroes -From waste to taste
2024-1-NL01-KA220-SCH-000254671.summary:
<< Objectives >>

FoodHeroes aims to foster sustainable practices among students (14-18) through digital tools and interactive methods. Objectives include hosting educational workshops, launching the Waste to Taste challenge, developing a FoodWise digital campaign, implementing teacher training programs, establishing the EcoCuisine Hub, and integrating SustainaQuest. These efforts are designed to increase awareness and action on food waste reduction, enhance digital and environmental literacy.

<< Implementation >>

FoodHeroes will implement educational workshops, the Waste to Taste challenge, a FoodWise digital campaign, a comprehensive teacher training program, the development of the EcoCuisine Hub, and the integration of SustainaQuest. These activities aim to engage students and the community in sustainable practices, enhance digital literacy, and foster innovative thinking in food sustainability.

<< Results >>

FoodHeroes anticipates significant outcomes: enhanced student knowledge on sustainability, creation of 100+ unique sustainable dishes, engagement of 500+ community members, improved teacher competencies in sustainability education, over 75% active engagement in the EcoCuisine Hub, and a 60% participation rate in SustainaQuest. These results will cultivate a culture of sustainability and inclusivity.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-1-NO01-KA220-SCH-000257506.title: Unity in Motion
2024-1-NO01-KA220-SCH-000257506.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Well-being has a crucial impact on students learning outcomes and general satisfaction with life. We want to contribute to this and achieve no bullying and that all students have at least one friend in their class and in another European country. This will lead to better school results. We want especially to better the results for boys, as they score lower in several countries, and we believe an increased focus on physical activity and better and more varied lessons can contribute to this.

<< Implementation >>

We are going to plan, test and carry out, evaluate and adjust lesson plans with physical activity in school subjects. We will focus on the use of digital tools and technology throughout the process, while respecting the nature of each subject. We encourage both traditional and more modern activities. The students’ experiences will be important to adjust the lesson plans to fit students and teachers in our countries and others who have access to them through eTwinning.

<< Results >>

We expect an increase in the students’ well-being at school. Short-term this can be seen in their social interactions and in their school results. Learning requires feeling safe and included. An increased awareness of inclusion in school and systematic use of physical activities in classes are good methods to increase a sense of belonging and being a part of the community in and outside of school. Each school will have a collection of tried and tested lessons plans and teaching materials.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2024-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000256498.title: language eduCation for inclusion of immigrAnt minoRity studEnts
2024-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000256498.summary:
<< Objectives >>

In connection with dynamic migration wave and in response to educational challenges of primary school migrants we would like to integrate them into the society through the development a CLIL-based language course at different levels, thus facilitating their education process and co-existence in a multilingual environment. Through this course language educators will be better qualified and prepared for work in a multicultural environment.

<< Implementation >>

Main activities:
- Promotion
- Project Management
- 5 Transnational Project Meetings
- Training for language educators
- Development of project outputs: Methodological Guidebook/ CLIL language courses/ TELMS-based e-mentoring prog. incl. AI tools/ E-platform
- Piloting of CLIL courses
- Dissemination and Exploitation of project results, incl. multiplier events
- Overall Evaluation

<< Results >>

- Methodological Guidebook for language teachers supporting language education of migrant students
- 2 CLIL language courses including digital resources for Sts from migrant families:
- aged 7-14 (BICS/ CALP modules; level A1-B1)
- aged 11-14 (BICS/ CALP modules; level A1-B2)
- TELMS-based e-mentoring programme including digital tools & AI solutions supporting language education of migrant Sts
- E-platform gathering all outputs and enabling teachers to share their learning materials, ideas etc.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2024-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000243521.title: Ecological Education and Out-of-School Learning Activities
2024-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000243521.summary:
<< Objectives >>

With this project, ecological education will be realized in out-of-school learning environments in each partner country. Drama will be used as a method in these studies. The objectives of the project are;
-To develop action environmental literacy skills in students.
To develop social participation skills by enabling students to participate in activities in out-of-school learning environments.
-To support children's physical, cognitive and social development and to develop environmental awareness

<< Implementation >>

The piloting process will take place for 8 weeks in partners that are schools. Practices will mainly take place in out-of-school learning environments. There will also be a limited number of in-class activities (virtual applications, drama, etc.). In these activities, awareness will be raised about the importance of soil, trees, forests and oxygen for humanity. During the implementation process, activities such as planting trees, protecting animal habitats, etc. will be carried out.

<< Results >>

A student mobility (C2) will take place at ECOL.  All partners will organize local meetings (E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6, E7) where the project work will be explained and environmental issues will be discussed. Transnational meetings (M1, M2, M3, M4) and two staff trainings (C1) will be organized during the project activities. Project outputs: Ecological Education Program, Ecological Education Guide for Teacher, Outdoor Ecological Education: Interactive Book.

2024-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000251161.title: Împreună suntem mai puternici
2024-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000251161.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project will bring value in each partner school to the participants by developing key
competences, adaptive and functional behavioral transformations among students with special educational needs in order to form the capacity of social integration, communication, civic engagement, European multiculturalism and belonging, inclusion, tolerance and respect towards the people with special needs, diversity in all fields of education and raise the public awareness on the issue of disabilities

<< Implementation >>

Learning Teaching Training Activities, PowerPoint presentations, workshops, conference, study trips, two e- books, eTwinning project, dissemination activities, the preparation week before each mobility, the follow up week after the return from each mobility, social campaign on raising awareness on disabilities, interviews with participating people, activities on communication through art- paintings, sewing, theatre plays, sport, dance, games, song of the project, Calendar, sharing leaflets etc.

<< Results >>

Qualitative results: awareness about the European culture and belonging,  social campaigns on the disability, well-being, raising the
self esteem of the participating students, promotion of non- discrimination, tolerance and respect.
Quantitative results: E twinning project, e- books of the project, calendars, photos, project website
Facebook group, project song, fliers, articles, Conference, PowerPoint presentations, lesson plans, dissemination
activities, photo albums.

2024-1-RS01-KA220-SCH-000253208.title: Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning for Inclusive Education
2024-1-RS01-KA220-SCH-000253208.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Co-CREATE aims to enhance inclusiveness and digital transformation of educational systems of Croatia, Portugal, Serbia and Spain. Adhering to participatory, evidence-based, interdisciplinary and multi-stakeholder approach, and using the potential of Computer Supported Collaborative Learning (CSCL) it aims to enhancing secondary students’ (including students with special needs and disabilities – SEND) key competencies and teachers’ and policy makers’ digital and collaboration capacities.

<< Implementation >>

For 30 months Co-CREATE will create, contextualise and assess (quasi-experimental) CSCL practices within Design-Based Research (DBR) that will gather gifted and SEND students, teachers, experts in IT and inclusive education and policy makers. CSCL practices will be integrated on the existing free to use Platform and made available in six languages and for SEND students. Workshops, social media and multiplier events will promote Co-CREATE values, Platform and AI-supported Handbook for teachers.

<< Results >>

Over 1000 pre-& in-service STEM and class teachers, policy makers, local authorities and entrepreneurs will learn about Co-CREATE products through multiplier events; 400 CS teachers will improve their digital and collaboration competences through webinars. 1000 students will benefit from Co-CREATE (50 SEND). 30000 persons will learn from YouTube and social media content. A network of relevant stakeholders will be strengthened to continue collaborating on sustainable digital inclusive education.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2024-1-SE01-KA220-SCH-000243589.summary:

 -To identify and analyze good practices of the partner schools in the field of teaching nature protection skills to the students

2024-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000245085.title: With knowledge against bullying
2024-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000245085.summary:
<< Objectives >>

General objective of the project is to develop a systematic approach and programme for school bullying prevention. Approach and program will address the bullying situation in two countries, Slovenia and Croatia, which share a common past, culture, and socio-political situation.

<< Implementation >>

In Capacity building part we will collect and learn about good practices in the field of bullying prevention. Analysis of bullying situation in primary schools will be done, followed by framework, guidelines and workshop program development. After and extensive piloting of bullying prevention programme in Slovene and Croatian primary schools the impact evaluation and systematic approach proposal will be done.

<< Results >>

Main results:
•	Bullying prevention good practices data.
•	Data about bullying situation in primary schools.
•	Framework for collaborative approach and work of schools and other stakeholders in bullying prevention.
•	Guidebook "How can School implement bullying prevention program”.
•	Workshop handbook “The Role of School, Pupils, Parents and Community in Preventing and Dealing with Bullying”
•	Bullying prevention programme impact evaluation.
•	Systematic bullying prevention approach proposal

2024-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000254132.title: EduSkills+ Media2 - Building Media Skills Together
2024-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000254132.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We aim to enhance media literacy and foster responsible media use among children, teachers, and parents. Our goal is to create a learning partnership that addresses the challenges of children's media consumption, equips teachers with effective tools and methodologies, and actively involves parents in understanding and navigating the media landscape. This project seeks to establish a balanced approach to media use, ensuring safe and constructive engagement for children's wellbeing and development

<< Implementation >>

We will approach the needs of our target groups by collecting and evaluating good practices among our partners and by developing new methods. All ideas and activities will be tested with target groups through piloting activities with parents, teachers and children. We will offer F2F teacher trainings, workshops for parents and further learning materials online. An extension of the existing portal Eduskills+Media will be developed and a widespread dissemination will take place.

<< Results >>

Our project will deliver the Eduskills+Media Toolbox, providing kindergarten teachers with an introduction to media education, tested approaches, and activities. This Toolbox will facilitate partnerships between teachers and parents for effective media socialization and education of children. Additionally, we'll introduce new, innovative media education activities in kindergartens. All materials, including the Toolbox and activities, will be available in four languages on the Eduskills+platform.

2024-1-TR01-KA220-SCH-000253469.title: SAĞLIKLI VE GENÇ
2024-1-TR01-KA220-SCH-000253469.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Aiming to create a balanced nutrition culture and raise healthy generations by explaining the relationship between nutrition and health H.A.Y. plans to collect menus containing the traditional nutrition cultures of its partners in a book. We also want to introduce the EU GREEN DEAL "From Farm to Fork" strategy and draw attention to Food Waste by explaining the importance of organic agriculture in accessing healthy food.We also aim to improve our students' digital competences and language skill.

<< Implementation >>

Our final product will be a book. We will create traditional healthy menus. This will also provide intercultural interaction. We will create school gardens where we will do organic farming and we will do practical training where our students will recognise plants. This work will contribute to physical activities. We will provide methods to prevent food waste. We will contribute to our students' digital skills and language skills. We will prepare presentations, posters, brochures, videos.

<< Results >>

To create a healthy and balanced nutrition culture in students and families.
To explain the consequences of unhealthy nutrition
To introduce organic farming and Farm to Table Strategy
To introduce practices to prevent food waste.
To contribute to project-based learning, blended education models by processing the connection between health, nutrition and agriculture with different activities and studies.
Creating school gardens, exemplifying organic agriculture.
To prepare a book on these topics

2025-1-BE02-KA220-SCH-000359876.title: Breaking Roles, Inspiring Diversity, Growing Equality
2025-1-BE02-KA220-SCH-000359876.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We aim to raise awareness and responsivness among teachers regarding stereotypical thinking related to gender in interaction with ethnicity. By encouraging a multidimensional perspective and emphasizing an intersectional approach, we strive to enhance children’s well-being, especially those of minority groups. We aim to an enduring change within schools towards a gender-sensitive and inclusive environment in which a culture of respect and tolerance is cultivated and stereotypes are discussed.

<< Implementation >>

We start with a transnational kick-off meeting to exchange insights on gender-sensitive education. Schools and experts co-create the Teacher Toolbox with checklists, lesson activities, and a digital learning path, refining it through PLC meetings and feedback from minority groups. A Train-the-Trainer manual is developed iteratively, culminating in live training for school-internal trainers to ensure sustainable change towards a gender-sensitive and inclusive school environment.

<< Results >>

A toolbox featuring learning activities, guidelines for fostering diversity-sensitive interactions, and an online interactive tool co-designed with teachers for teachers. 
A manual for durable change in primary schools with an informative section, scripts, and activities to get the entire team on board.
The ultimate result is an inclusive school, with teachers equipped to create a gender-sensitive classroom and children empowered to make choices free from gender stereotypes.

2025-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000360652.title: Zahlandia – Game-based Learning Approach to Mathematics in Primary Education
2025-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000360652.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Early mathematical competences are key to mastering a number of important skills, yet there are still a lot of young students struggling with them. In this project we want to give these students the opportunity to learn better, more and with greater motivation by expanding a proven concept and an existing collection of analogue math games into a digital learning component that makes it more easily accessible, as well as studying its effect.

<< Implementation >>

In the project we are going to create a safe digital learning environment which can be used on tablets and mobile phones. Based on pedagogic research we are going to create a combination of board games and digital games that work in sync to help students in primary schools practice their math skills with greater motivation and better results. We will also be testing and implementing this approach in several primary schools.

<< Results >>

In the end we will end up with a digital learning environment with games to practice math skills, running as an app on mobile phones and tablets, which will complement an already existing and proven analogue board game approach that has been used successfully in German schools. We will also have guides for teachers, learning therapists and parents available and we expect to see greatly improved skills for the primary school students we want to test this with. Research results will be published.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2025-1-EL01-KA220-SCH-000351019.title: K12 Agile Learning of Programming with Educational Robotics
2025-1-EL01-KA220-SCH-000351019.summary:
<< Objectives >>

1) Develop programming skills to ALL students from as early as in primary education
2) Inflict Industry 4.0 agile learning and the agile way of project teams operation to students in primary education
3) Gamify the agile learning approach deploying educational robotics
4) Engage primary school students in task-, self- and team- evaluation activities, core of the agile learning sprints philosophy
5) Enhance teachers' digital capacity via asynchronous training platform
6) EU-wide distribution

<< Implementation >>

The variety of activities is extensive yet complementary. In the project we intent to implement:
Workshops, hackathons, multiplier events, creation of digital applications, online trainings, in-situ trainings, school visits, research, cooperative writing.
Agile learning scrum school lab activities focusing on programming educational robots are the heart of the ALPER proposal, as wel as online teachers' training and support activities on the effective use of the students' engagement assess tool.

<< Results >>

1 ALPER Curriculum & Teachrers' Training of 60 agile educational robotic sprints:
a) 60 3D digital designs to construct educational robots,
b) 60 system designs and automations with senssors and actuators
c) 60 software development algorithms for programming classes
1 Engagement Assessment Tool which will monitor and record
a) the active engagement time and
b) the way each student feels during each class and overall course.
Distribution by SCIENTIX to 51 countries and 1237 SCIENTIX Ambassadors.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2025-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000356243.title: Respect Connect. Creating Safer and more Inclusive School Environments
2025-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000356243.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Respect Connect project aims to prevent bullying and cyberbullying in primary schools by integrating innovative digital tools and SEL strategies. We will empower teachers, enhance students’ social-emotional skills, and foster safer, more inclusive learning environments. By enabling collaboration and best practices sharing among teachers and education professionals, we ensure a sustainable, long-term positive impact on European educational communities.

<< Implementation >>

The project foresees the: 
-Development of a gamified App with a Parent’s Guide
-Co-creation workshops with target groups 
-Development of the Educator’s Toolkit to enable the direct implementation at schools
-Teacher Training to equip them with the competencies needed to implement the piloting at schools
-Pilot Testing of the App and Toolkit with students
-2 TPMs
-A European Webinar for wider dissemination
-6 Multiplier Events
-Extensive dissemination activities throughout the project.

<< Results >>

The project will generate 3 Concrete Results:
-A gamified App
-A Parents’ Guide to enable the App usage outside school 
-The Educator’s Toolkit to integrate the App at schools and propose the SEL approach for bullying prevention. 
Respect Connect will enhance teachers’ skills, knowledge and self-efficacy in SEL and increase students’ social-emotional skills to prevent bullying. Partners will enhance their capacity to create apps and SEL resources and improve their CPD offer in this field.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2025-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000356472.title: Strengthening Teacher Training with AI through Remote-learning Spaces
2025-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000356472.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project aims to create teacher training programs and systems enhanced with AI tools, leading to increase teacher satisfaction, well-being, professional development (both pedagogically and digitally), and promoting inclusion and sustainability. All this accompanied by the establishment of international cooperation networks, with the goal of creating a more equitable and forward-thinking educational ecosystem that prepare students for the understanding and responsible, efficient use of AI.

<< Implementation >>

Development of an AI-enhanced teacher training platform
Organisation of AI training workshops for teacher training responsibles 
Design of a structured AI training pathway for teachers
Creation of AI-enhanced teaching resources (OERs)
Piloting the training pathway in 4 countries
Creation of 2 international AI communities of practice
Launch of a multilingual website
AI webinars organisation
Participation in international education events
Creation of IA guides for teachers, students and families

<< Results >>

The anticipated results include:
-Enhanced digital and AI literacy among educators
-A repository of open-access educational resources and AI tools tailored to diverse classroom needs
-Strengthened transnational networks fostering sustained collaboration and innovation
-Evidence-based policy recommendations for integrating AI into education
The project aims to contribute to the creation of a inclusive digital education community, supporting the goals of Erasmus+ 2025 and the Green digital sector
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2025-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000349739.title: CREATE A SUSTAINABLE WORLD BY THE MOTTO OF ZERO WASTE AND EDUCATE THE FUTURE CITIZENS OF EUROPE TO BE RESPONSIBLE FOR HOW TO REUSE, RECYCLE AND REDUCE THE WASTE FOR A BETTER FUTURE
2025-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000349739.summary:

Our primary goal is to increase awareness of waste management across all institutions, particularly within the schools to:
take meaningful steps towards a cleaner world
promote the recycling of various types of waste
develop a sustainable curriculum fostering responsible environmental awareness
demonstrate how waste can be transformed into artistic creations
enhance the European dimension by contributing to European added value for environmental and climate action through inclusive participation

Encouraging creativity among participants,
Building a foundation for a more sustainable, livable world,

Contributing to educational curricula,
Serving as inspiration for future environmental and climate initiatives
production of bio-paint
Reaching wider audiences to raise the impact of our PRs

2025-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000349769.title: GREEN SAVING with STEAM EDUCATION
2025-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000349769.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Environmental disasters caused by humans have increased with the spread of environmentally insensitive production. The starting point of this project is for future generations to internalize the facts of saving for a green environment. With the drama STEAM designs, students will develop habits to reduce wasteful consumption in daily life. Students will be prepared for their future careers by thinking analytically and developing environmental models for green savings.

<< Implementation >>

In this project, STEAM designs will be made together with drama. These designs will be aimed at developing an awareness of saving in nature. In the studies to be carried out, students will be presented with an environmental problem and will be helped to make designs to solve this problem. Teachers' professional skills for green saving will also be developed in the project. In addition, short-term student exchange will be realized in order for students to see the practices in different countries.

<< Results >>

In the project, students and participating teachers will gain meaningful awareness about green savings through STEAM designs. Students will develop their design skills on environmental issues. Students will develop awareness of nature conservation.  Five outputs will be created in the GREEN SAVE Project: 1. Green Saving Programme with STEAM 2. STEAM Teacher Training Module 3. Green Empathy with Drama Module  (for Teacher) 4. STEAM Activity Book (for students) 5. Saving Handbook for Green

2025-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000360968.title: EcoSkills for Tomorrow
2025-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000360968.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project integrates digital tools (VR, AI, coding, gamification) with sustainability education to equip students and teachers with 21st-century skills. It promotes hands-on environmental learning, cross-cultural collaboration, and school-based sustainability initiatives. Key outcomes include digital resources, student-led projects, and a European-wide challenge, ensuring long-term impact through educational integration and community engagement.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes LTTs and workshops on VR, AI, coding, and gamification for sustainability education. Activities include hands-on environmental projects, biodiversity tracking, energy-saving initiatives, and a Digital Sustainability Challenge. Schools will implement sustainability tracking apps, composting, and climate action plans. A Multiplier Event in Turkey will showcase results, ensuring long-term adoption and impact.

<< Results >>

The project will produce digital sustainability tools (VR platform, mobile tracking app, AI-driven resources), educational toolkits, and student-led environmental initiatives. Schools will implement long-term sustainability practices, and teachers will integrate digital learning into curricula. A Multiplier Event in Turkey will share best practices, ensuring wider adoption and lasting impact on sustainability education across Europe.

2025-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000366133.title: Go Green for a Sustainable World
2025-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000366133.summary:
<< Objectives >>

O1- Develop a curriculum that will use STEM and AI tools to raise awareness of climate change and environmental sustainability and promote ecological literacy.

2025-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000360813.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The Empowering Preschool Educators to Foster Resilience and Well-Being Among Children project aims to create a holistic approach to mental health by equipping educators, children, and parents with tools for socio-emotional learning (SEL). Educators will gain skills and digital resources to foster resilience in children, while parents will be actively involved as partners in the process, ensuring a sustainable and supportive environment for early childhood well-being.

<< Implementation >>

The project will develop a localized SEL toolkit with animated videos, lesson plans, and outdoor activities. Educators will be trained in SEL integration and digital tools, while parents will participate in workshops to support SEL at home. Pilot testing in kindergartens will evaluate the impact, and policy recommendations will be created to ensure the long-term adoption of SEL in early childhood education.

<< Results >>

The project will create a lasting impact on early childhood education by equipping educators with SEL skills and digital tools, fostering resilient and emotionally aware children, and strengthening parental engagement in SEL. A high-quality SEL toolkit will be widely accessible, ensuring long-term use. Through policy recommendations and digital resources, the project will influence education systems, making SEL a core part of early learning across Europe.

Increase participants' understanding of environmental education providing them with up-to-date training resources about environmental education. TREE project will allow secondary school teachers to integrate green practices and engaging activities related to environmental sustainability in their schools. This will enhance students’ green skills, promoting a broader approach to environmental sustainability and civic engagement.

<< Implementation >>

The TREE project will hold four training events in each country of the partner. Specifically, four main pillars will be addressed: Water; Energy efficiency; Biodiversity and hydroponics; Gardening and composting. Each partner school will oversee one of the pillars and design the experimental part of the project, that will be summarize in the TREE toolkits. Furthermore, four MOOCs of 8h each on the same topics will be developed throughout the project.

At least 10 teachers/trainers of the partner institutions attend 4 teacher training events about Water; Energy efficiency; Biodiversity and hydroponics; Gardening and composting. The TeachQuestPro project aims to modernize teacher training by integrating gamification and digital learning methodologies, equipping educators with innovative, student-centered teaching strategies. Pupil-led Response to the Effects of Climate Change on
Their Local Communities

Enhancement of climate change education and action in European schools through :
 869
Innovative, pupil-centred, action-oriented  pedagogies (STEAMing) for climate teaching and learning;
 
Increased pupil understanding, commitment and agency for impactful climate action;

2025-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000357304.summary:

This project introduces gamification to enhance inclusive education and address challenges such as the exclusion of students with special needs or migratory backgrounds and STEM skill shortages in the EU. Targeting teachers, facilitators, and students, it develops tools and skills to boost inclusion and STEM proficiency, fostering innovative teaching and long-term educational equity.

Manual Creation: Develop a manual as the basis for the training course.
Training Phase: Provide in-person training for educators to become "game operators" using gamification in STEM.
Testing Phase: Apply the methods in secondary schools and informal settings over 6-8 months, with periodic reports.
Online Platform: Share materials and feedback online for future use and scalability.

<< Results >>

Building community for marginalized students in schools and beyond.
Enhancing STEM interest, accessibility, and proficiency for all, including excluded groups.
Reducing school dropouts and improving academic performance.
Supporting mental health and well-being via anti-bullying and inclusive communication.
Training educators in innovative methodologies.
Strengthening cooperation across educational contexts.
Establishing EU-wide best practices for inclusive education.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

1. Increased Family Engagement. 
2. Together tool.

8. A model of family engagement in STEAM education that can be replicated across other schools in Europe.
