FOCUS project promotes responsible smartphone use to enhance student well-being and learning. It enforces smartphone-free policies in primary schools and structured smartphone pedagogy in secondary schools. The main aim is to develop and reinforce self-regulation skills in different student age groups and foster healthy digital habits.

<< Implementation >>

The project will develop pedagogical materials, policies, and tools for schools, teachers, students, and parents to support smartphone-safe education. The resources will be refined in diverse school settings through pilot use and the web-based self-assessment and recommendation tool. Stakeholder training, awareness campaigns and challenges will measure impact, refine strategies, and promote responsible smartphone use. Impact assessments and a sustainability plan will ensure long-term adoption.

<< Results >>

The project delivers Core Competencies for Smartphone Use and three key outcomes, offering inclusive guidelines and hands-on materials. The HEWRECA well-being framework ensures a balanced approach to technology in education. The SPARK pedagogy kit, with a core in mathematics but adaptable to all subjects, provides strategies for integrating smartphones into education. RESUME, a web-based self-assessment tool with a recommendation system, helps stakeholders evaluate&improve their smartphone use.

2025-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000359162.title: My Digital Self: Shaping Identity in the Digital Age
2025-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000359162.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The SELF-ID project aims to enhance adolescents' digital literacy, critical thinking, and resilience by addressing the impact of digital influences on identity formation, self-image, and self-esteem. It empowers students (ages 10-14) to differentiate between authentic and digital identities and provides teachers with tools to support them. The project fosters positive digital engagement through media literacy, gamification, and co-creation, contributing to well-being and inclusion.

<< Implementation >>

Key project activities include designing the SELF-ID intervention, which consists of training materials and an "analogue" table escape room. These materials will be piloted, evaluated, and finalized based on feedback. National events, such as webinars, a Train-the-Trainer program for teachers, and peer-learning events, will be held to disseminate the results. The project will conclude with a final symposium, bringing together stakeholders from all four countries.

<< Results >>

The main outcomes of the project include the SELF-ID Training Program Handbook and the SELF-ID Table Escape Room with a user manual. All training materials will be available online in a user-friendly format in English, Slovene, Croatian, Italian, and German for wider impact and further use. Expected long-term benefits include improved digital resilience, stronger identity formation with well-balanced self-image and self-esteem, and a more unified European approach to digital literacy education.

hr.name: Društvo za komunikacijsku i medijsku kulturu

2025-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000364758.title: Outdoor Play Labs - Integrating STEM & SEL Learning in Education
2025-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000364758.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to develop STEM and SEL skills in early childhood and primary education (3-10) through outdoor play.
1.Promote STEM learning through outdoor play: Engaging children in hands-on STEM activities
2.Foster SEL skills:Encouraging teamwork, communication, and emotional regulation through group play and problem-solving activities.-
3.Develop a scientific understanding of the environment:Instilling sustainable behaviors and environmental awareness in children from an early age

<< Implementation >>

The project will develop and pilot an Outdoor STEM Toolkit, train educators, and conduct Outdoor Play Events to engage children, teachers, and families. An online learning community will facilitate best practice exchange. Policy recommendations will be developed to integrate outdoor learning into education frameworks. Study visits and dissemination activities will ensure the project's long-term impact, fostering innovation in STEM and SEL education through outdoor play-based learning

<< Results >>

The project will deliver an Outdoor STEM Toolkit, train 40 educators, and engage 600+ children in outdoor learning. A digital repository will ensure long-term accessibility, while policy recommendations will shape education frameworks. Schools will integrate outdoor play, boosting STEM engagement. The project will strengthen cross-border collaboration, enhance professional development, and provide scalable methodologies, ensuring a lasting impact at local, national, and European levels.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2025-1-TR01-KA220-SCH-000353101.title: ASTRO-EDU: Empowering Teachers as STEAM Communicators in Astronomy Education
2025-1-TR01-KA220-SCH-000353101.summary:
<< Objectives >>

ASTRO-EDU aims to empower primary and secondary educators as effective STEAM communicators by enhancing their astronomy content knowledge, pedagogical skills, and digital literacy through comprehensive professional development. The project will co-design and disseminate an inquiry‐based toolkit enriched with digital resources to transform astronomy education, foster science communication and interdisciplinary learning, inspire student curiosity and build a sustainable network of educators.

<< Implementation >>

The project features collaboratively select, adapt, refine, co-design and translate a toolkit of STEAM-based astronomy resources and link the big ideas of astronomy to other disciplines through online meetings and an expert summer school in Phase 1. Phase 2  implements intensive professional development workshops for teachers and pre-service teachers (online and in-person).Phase 3 promotes community outreach through local school and public events, virtual seminars, and citizen science projects.

<< Results >>

Outcomes include enhanced competencies among teachers and preservice teachers, a replicable inquiry‐based toolkit featuring digital content and a sustainable network of science communicators. Anticipated results are improved classroom practices, increased public and student engagement through outreach events, a sustainable network of astronomy ambassadors, fostering greater scientific literacy and curiosity. it will provide interdisciplinary collaborations and influence local policy makers.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2026-1-BG01-KA220-SCH-000459740.title: HESTIA: Hydroponic gardens for Education in Schools – Technology and Innovation in Agriculture
2026-1-BG01-KA220-SCH-000459740.summary:
<< Objectives >>

HESTIA will create an innovative toolkit based on 3D-printed educational Hydroponic towers to:
Cultivate green skills & habits in school to fight climate change and create resilient communities
Increase students’ interest & excellence in STEM through practical STEM teaching utilising 3D printing & hydroponics
Improve school mental wellbeing through inclusive learning and mental health benefits of gardening
Focus on engaging girls & disabled students more effectively through inclusive STEM tools

<< Implementation >>

Project activities are:
-WP2 focused on teacher co-design of educational hydroponic towers & Lesson Plan Guides for classroom use
-WP3 focused on an e-course for teacher upskilling on sustainability, gardening, 3D printing, STEM  engagement & wellbeing in school, plus teaching materials for their class
-WP4 focused on long-term piloting the HESTIA toolkit in the real school environment
-WP5 focused on dissemination, sustainability and student-led community events for community knowledge transfer

<< Results >>

-Teacher upskilling on using hydroponics & 3D printing to: teach & increase interest in STEM, teach climate change resilience, improve mental wellbeing in school
-Effective upskilling of teachers & students in: practical green skills & habits to fight climate change, transferrable cutting edge digital skills
-Improved soft skills like collaboration & problem solving in students
-Improved engagement of girl & disabled students in STEM
-Wide uptake of novel teaching methods like HESTIA toolkit
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2026-1-CZ01-KA220-SCH-000457010.title: Climate Awareness and Resilience through Inquiry and Tree-centred Learning for School Education
2026-1-CZ01-KA220-SCH-000457010.summary:
<< Objectives >>

CLARITY strengthens climate literacy and STEM competences of pupils aged 9–15 through inquiry-based, tree-centred and data-driven learning combined with transnational comparison. Pupils complete a full inquiry cycle and co-design realistic, implementable school-based Climate Resilience Plans reviewed by experts and presented to local communities. Teachers gain the capacity to deliver accurate, inclusive, and emotionally safe climate education, with a focus on inclusivity.

<< Implementation >>

CLARITY develops and pilots a structured inquiry-based climate learning model rooted in tree phenology, local measurements and data literacy. In 20 schools, pupils complete a full inquiry cycle, produce Tree Reporter outputs, and co-design Climate Resilience Plans reviewed by experts and presented locally. Teachers receive structured training and peer exchange. A systems-thinking role-play game and a virtual international student conference strengthen analysis and European comparison.

<< Results >>

CLARITY delivers classroom-tested inquiry and data literacy modules, a validated Climate Resilience Plan framework, a climate communication guide for teachers and a systems-thinking role-play game, all published as open-access resources. At least 400 pupils and 40 teachers directly participate. The project strengthens climate literacy, data competence and girls’ engagement in STEM, while building sustainable European cooperation between schools, NGOs and higher education institutions.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2026-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000460210.title: Demokratische Transformationswerkstatt – Empowerment von europäischen Schüler:innen in der digitalen Ära
2026-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000460210.summary:
<< Objectives >>

DemLab strengthens democratic judgement and action competences as well as critical digital competence of secondary school students. The project develops a conflict-oriented educational format – the Democracy Workshop – using digital transformation conflicts as entry points for analysing political structures. It integrates EU key competences Citizenship and Digital Competence in a single, transnationally piloted format tested across three school types.

<< Implementation >>

DemLab develops a modular workshop concept (WP2) and pilots it at schools in Germany, Croatia and Türkiye (WP3). Results are documented on a multilingual open-access website – the Digital Column – and presented through action days (WP4). A Teachers Toolbox enables independent delivery without external support (WP5). MUMEM, as a public education authority, leads the Toolbox development and ensures transfer into regional training structures.

<< Results >>

Key results: 1) Modular Democracy Workshop concept with conflict prompts, moderation aids and reflection tools. 2) Digital Column: multilingual website with European comparative perspective. 3) Teachers Toolbox in four languages (EN, DE, HR, TR) as OER under CC BY-SA. 4) Action days at three partner schools (Gymnasium Isernhagen, Technical School Nikola Tesla Vukovar, Mahinur Cemal Uslu Ortaokulu Bodrum). Strengthened cooperation and sustainable educational resources for schools across Europe.

2026-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000462962.title: MINDtheSCREEN - Supporting Students’ Digital Well-Being and Social Inclusion through Socio-Emotional Learning in European Schools
2026-1-DE03-KA220-SCH-000462962.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen digital well-being, social-emotional competencies, and inclusive participation among young people aged 8–16. It seeks to support schools and youth organisations in addressing the challenges of digital environments by developing an integrated framework (DSI framework) linking digital well-being, SEL, and inclusion, and by equipping teachers and youth workers with practical approaches to foster responsible digital practices and supportive learning environments.

<< Implementation >>

To achieve these objectives, DIGI@WELL will design and develop a digital well-being assessment tool with a teacher dashboard, co-create pedagogical toolkits and training workshops for teachers and youth workers, pilot and implement these resources in partner schools and youth community centres across several countries. Feedback from teachers, youth workers, and students will be used to refine the tools, and the final resources will be prepared for multilingual open-access dissemination.

<< Results >>

The project will provide practical tools for teachers and youth professionals to strengthen young people’s digital well-being, SEL, and inclusion. Outcomes include a digital well-being self-assessment tool with a teacher dashboard and AI-supported feedback, evidence-based booklets and toolkits with classroom-ready activities, and training resources (e.g., guides, tutorials, FAQs). All results will be published as open-access multilingual resources to support transfer and long-term use.

hr.name: UDRUGA ZA PROMICANJE AKTIVNOG SUDJELOVANJA STUDIO B

2026-1-EL01-KA220-SCH-000463176.title: DigiLab4Teachers: Digital AI Pedagogy For Teachers
2026-1-EL01-KA220-SCH-000463176.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The rapid adoption of AI in European schools has outpaced teacher preparation. This project responds directly, training 75 educators across Greece, Türkiye, Croatia, Romania, and Spain to integrate AI responsibly into lesson design, counselling, and inclusive practice. Using an Adaptive MOOC, 24 H5P templates, and an AI Design Lab, participants advance from DigCompEdu Levels 1 and 2 to 3 and 4, supported by UDL principles that ensure equitable outcomes for all students.

<< Implementation >>

Our implementation follows four phases. A Needs Analysis shapes an 8-module curriculum built on real classroom conditions. Development produces an Adaptive MOOC, 24 H5P templates, and an AI Design Lab platform. During Piloting, 75 teachers across 5 countries test tools and 15 Master Trainers each mentor 12 to 16 peers, reaching 900 to 1,200 colleagues. Multiplier Events disseminate results and all OERs are uploaded to ESEP.

<< Results >>

This project equips 75 pilot teachers with practical digital skills, enabling 15 Master Trainers to reach 900 to 1,200 colleagues across five countries. Key outputs include an 8-module curriculum, an Adaptive MOOC, 24 no-code H5P templates, and an AI Design Lab. All resources are freely available as open educational resources. GDPR-compliant protocols and updated school policies drive systemic change, while integration into national CPD frameworks ensures lasting impact.

2026-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000450520.title: S.O.L.U.T.I.O.N.S. - Sustainability is an Opportunity to Learn Unity through Technology, Innovation, Our Nature and Social Inclusion
2026-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000450520.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The SOLUTIONS project aims to enhance inclusive education, environmental awareness, and digital innovation across Europe. It provides teachers with training on inclusion and climate education, fosters eco-friendly school initiatives, and promotes collaborative learning through digital tools. The project strengthens European cooperation, empowering educators and students to become active citizens and sustainability advocates, and tackling learning disadvantages & early school leavingin schools.

<< Implementation >>

The SOLUTIONS project includes teacher training (MOOCs,workshops, LTT programs),school-based initiatives (Green Roof,Sensory Garden,students challenges), digital collaboration (eTwinning,Goran’s Portal),and awareness campaigns (Eco-Influencers,Inclusion Escape Room,Flashmob for Peace). Mobilities to Ireland,Croatia,Bulgaria,Portugal,Denmark, Spain,Belgium will provide hands-on experiences and best practice exchanges,results and models that would not be achievable within a single national context

<< Results >>

The SOLUTIONS project will produce an eGuide with teaching materials, an interactive online platform (Goran’s Portal), OER and sustainable school initiatives. Teachers will improve their inclusive and environmental education skills, students will develop eco-awareness and digital literacy, and schools will integrate innovative methodologies. The long-term impact includes policy recommendations, strengthened European networks, and sustainable school practices.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2026-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000453227.title: LEARN4SUSTAIN
2026-1-ES01-KA220-SCH-000453227.summary:
<< Objectives >>

-Empower secondary school students to be active agents of sustainability, strengthening their critical thinking, research skills and civic participation.
-Support teachers through innovative methodologies such as Green Labs and challenge-based learning.
-Encourage cooperation between schools and European stakeholders and empower young people to design and present sustainable proposals.

<< Implementation >>

-Student-led research on sustainability challenges in different educational profiles and production of podcasts to communicate results.
-Teacher training in sustainability and active methodologies.
-Joint creation of a European kit for teachers. 
-Implementation of Green Labs in schools and peer-to-peer activities.
-Organisation of multiplier events, a European webinar and a final European event in Croatia to present student proposals.

<< Results >>

-Podcasts produced by students analysing sustainability challenges.
-A set of European tools for teachers on sustainability education.
-An accessible online digital platform for teachers and students.
-Proposals for eco-friendly school laboratories developed by students.
-European webinars and a final in-person event with policy makers.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2026-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000454796.title: ROOTS: Reconnecting Our Origins through Traditions and Shared Learning
2026-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000454796.summary:
<< Objectives >>

ROOTS aims to strengthen students’ sense of belonging and shared European identity through inclusive heritage education. We seek to transform local memories, traditions and intergenerational dialogue into structured, classroom-ready tools that promote inclusion, civic engagement and sustainable community participation across partner schools.

<< Implementation >>

We implement oral history research, intergenerational interviews and heritage mapping (WP2), co-design inclusive festival stations and a Board Game (WP3), run 20 local transfer cycles and mini-festivals (WP4), and consolidate results through a Digital Hub, dissemination seminars and a final European Heritage Festival (WP5).

<< Results >>

ROOTS delivers a European Memory Atlas, Storybook of Memories, Festival Programme Guide and Board Game, supported by at least 60 structured materials such as lesson plans, worksheets, inclusion templates and festival station cards. We document 50+ classroom sessions, 20 local mini-festivals and stakeholder partnerships, ensuring long-term embedding and European transferability beyond the project lifetime.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2026-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000456562.title: Virtual innovation center
2026-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000456562.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to boost students’ motivation in science learning through VR-based lessons that make abstract topics easier to understand. It seeks to improve learning outcomes with immersive, experience-based teaching, equip schools with sustainable VR labs, and build teachers’ long-term digital skills. It also promotes girls’ participation in STEM and inspires other schools to adopt VR in education.

<< Implementation >>

-The project includes two TPMs to define VR content and evaluate results, and two LTTAs to train teachers and test VR lessons with students. Teachers will gain digital and VR skills, while students experience real VR-based classes. Schools will be equipped with a shared VR platform, headsets and curriculum-based content, supported by a project website to ensure visibility and long-term impact.

<< Results >>

The project will increase students’ motivation, especially in science lessons, especially girls', through immersive VR-based learning. Teachers will strengthen their digital and pedagogical skills and apply them in real classrooms. Schools will gain a functional VR platform with curriculum-based content, supporting more interactive, inclusive and engaging learning. These results will help schools move towards sustainable digital education practices.

2026-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000463153.title: AI in Future Schools
2026-1-FR01-KA220-SCH-000463153.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project addresses the profound structural challenge posed by integration of Artificial Intelligence in education. For a pedagogically meaningful, ethical, and inclusive integration of Generative AI in schools, we aim to:
•	Strengthen teachers’ digital and pedagogical competencies through research-informed training.
•	Develop students’ AI literacy, critical thinking..
•	Establish sustainable AI Governance models  
•	Promote AI equity at school 
*       Inform policies

<< Implementation >>

The project is built on an Action-Research methodology with 8 partners from 6 countries (France, Türkiye, Germany, Serbia, Croatia, and Bulgaria) 
Around 6 mobility-based classroom experimentations is organized Action-research.
Key activities include:
AI Experimentations in classes , workshops about experimentation, AI Literacy Labs and Inclusive Workshops, development of GenAI Pedagogical Assistants for classes (in different classes, or subjects ..), transnational seminars, multiplier events

<< Results >>

AIFS will empowers the school communities which are involved in the project . 
AIFS will produce transferables resources: 
•	AI Pedagogy Handbook : guide for building pedagogical scenarii-models , Gen AI pedagogical assistants, for teachers in classes
•	Inclusive AI & Differentiation Toolkit
•	AI Governance Handbook: for implementing AI at school (charter, guidelines .;)
•	Competency Frameworks (teachers, school leaders ..)
•	Policy Recommendations (authorities,EU Digital Action Plan )
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2026-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000448923.title: Shaping Tomorrow with Artificial Intelligence
2026-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000448923.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The EDUCATION 5.0 project aims to:
- strengthen teachers’ AI literacy, ethical judgement and pedagogical autonomy;
- enable responsible, teacher-controlled AI use in ISCED 1–2 classrooms;
- translate EU digital education priorities into validated, classroom-ready solutions applicable across European education systems.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement:
- a shared European AI pedagogical framework and teacher training programme;
- a teacher-controlled AI Classroom Assistant validated in real schools;
- school-based piloting, impact evaluation and Train-the-Trainer activities;
- dissemination through national multiplier events and an open community platform.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver:
- a validated AI Classroom Assistant for ISCED 1–2 education;
- classroom-ready lesson scenarios and training materials;
- evidence-based impact and evaluation results;
- an open Education 5.0 Community Platform supporting reuse, scaling and long-term adoption across Europe.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2026-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000449220.title: Digital Wellbeing and Media Literacy for Teaching Peace and EU Values
2026-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000449220.summary:
<< Objectives >>

DIGI-PEACE aims to strengthen digital wellbeing, critical thinking and responsible digital citizenship among 12–15-year-olds, while equipping teachers and schools with practical, age-appropriate tools aligned with EU values. It will help students manage online pressure, misinformation, cyberbullying and harmful content, and support schools to embed safe, preventive digital wellbeing routines into everyday teaching and whole-school practice.

<< Implementation >>

Partners will conduct an EU-informed research and needs analysis, run School Innovation Studios to co-design and validate classroom scenarios, and develop DIGI-PEACE QUEST, a child-centred, non-addictive gamified platform with a teacher dashboard. Activities include cross-country classroom pilots, teacher trainings and mobilities, youth-led actions (#MyEUValues, Safer Internet Day, Digital Detox/Outdoor Wellbeing), webinars, stakeholder roundtables, and publishing multilingual open resources.

<< Results >>

Outputs include a validated Educational Digital Literacy Framework; 40+ scenario missions and classroom routines; DIGI-PEACE QUEST with a gamified tasks to complete, wellbeing check-ins and ethical teacher monitoring; and multilingual OER (Didactical Design Book, Educational Toolkit, EU Values Cards). Outcomes: improved source evaluation and safer choices by students, higher teacher self-efficacy, and sustained uptake via multipliers and a Sustainability & Exploitation Pack.

2026-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000454201.title: Game-Based Learning and Design Thinking in Secondary Education
2026-1-HR01-KA220-SCH-000454201.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to integrate STEAM education, digital innovation and environmental sustainability into secondary education by developing a transnational escape game pedagogical framework, strengthening teachers’ digital and climate competences, empowering students as STEAM co-creators, and scaling results through an open-access interactive digital hub and sustainable dissemination model.

<< Implementation >>

We will organise a 2-day kick-off meeting, co-design and validate a STEAM Escape Game Pedagogical Framework and Teacher Toolkit, conduct international teacher piloting with 24 teachers, implement three transnational student LTTAs involving 90 students to co-create escape games, develop and launch a multilingual interactive digital hub, and deliver six national multiplier events to ensure dissemination, institutional integration and long-term sustainability.

<< Results >>

The project will produce a validated STEAM Escape Game Pedagogical Framework, a comprehensive Teacher Toolkit, 12 teacher-designed and 9 student-created escape game scenarios, and a multilingual interactive digital hub with at least 30 resources. It will strengthen teachers’ digital and climate competences, empower 90 students, and reach 300+ stakeholders through multiplier events, ensuring sustainable impact.

2026-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000449843.title: NeuroArt - Metodi artistici ispirati alle neuroscienze per un'educazione inclusiva
2026-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000449843.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project addresses the critical gap in neurodivergent inclusion: despite half of EU systems promoting inclusion, students with ASD/ADHD continue to underperform by up to 0.8 SD vs. peers.

OS1 - Develop a validated ART framework (neuroplasticity + multimodal learning + embodied cognition + art);
OS2 - Train 120 European teachers (40-hour blended program + certification);
OS3 - Produce 100 multilingual, WCAG 2.1 AA-accessible OERs; 
OS4 - Sustainable digital platform for 5 years post-project.

<< Implementation >>

WP1 -Coordination and monitoring, 4 TPMs, reporting.
WP2 -Neuroscience literature review and research, co-design with 30+ stakeholders, ARTE framework development, database of 50 activities.
WP3 -Multilingual OER platform development, 30 additional teaching resources from teachers, 20 video tutorials, community forum.
WP4 -Blended training of 120 teachers, students from 8 pilot schools, 2 implementation cycles, data collection.
WP5 -Dissemination: 4 events, Policy Brief, website, sustainability

<< Results >>

PR1 - ARTE Framework, PR2 - Activity DB (50 validated activities), PR3 - Teacher Handbook, PR4 - Digital OER Platform, PR5 - Evaluation Report, PR6 - Policy Brief.Expected 
impacts: 120 trained teachers,approx. 2400 student beneficiaries with improved engagement/performance/well-being, measurable reduction of 
neurotypical/neurodivergent gap in 8 pilot schools, 8 ARTE schools embed in PTOF, CoP 80+ members post-project, 4 events with 400 pp, 3000+ OER visits.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2026-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000468514.title: Tracing Ancient Paths for Health, Wellness and European Digital Heritage
2026-1-IT02-KA220-SCH-000468514.summary:
<< Objectives >>

“Tracing Ancient Paths for Health, Wellness and European Digital Heritage” connects schools across Italy, Spain, Poland, Hungary, Croatia, and Türkiye to safeguard agro-pastoral heritage, promote environmental sustainability, healthy lifestyles, digital innovation, and circular rural development. Objectives include mapping transhumance routes, creating digital and educational tools, fostering youth wellbeing, and developing sustainable rural entrepreneurship.

<< Implementation >>

The project implements a Kick-off LTT for teachers, five thematic student and staff mobilities, Living Labs, and pilot activities in agro-pastoral heritage, health, and rural innovation. Outputs include a GIS Transhumance Heritage Map, multimedia archives, educational modules, recipe and business toolkits. Activities culminate in a Final Mobility in Italy with a Permanent Exhibition, conference, Open Badge ceremony, and policy roundtable.

<< Results >>

Expected results include a multilingual GIS Transhumance Heritage Map, multimedia anthropological archives, educational modules, recipe and startup toolkits, Open Badge certifications, and enhanced student competences in sustainability, heritage, and rural entrepreneurship. Outcomes also include six multiplier events, the Permanent Exhibition in Foggia, the European Transhumant Student Manifesto, and policy recommendations.
topics: Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas

2026-1-LV01-KA220-SCH-000448886.title: As They Fake, We Educate: Empowering Students with Critical Media, Multimodal & AI Literacy
2026-1-LV01-KA220-SCH-000448886.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our project aims to improve how teachers and students develop critical media, multimodal, and basic AI literacy. It will equip teachers with shared methods to teach and assess these competences, enable students to analyse media, recognise manipulation, and communicate responsibly, and ensure that these skills are accessible beyond the partnership through reusable classroom tools and e-learning resources, supporting inclusive and sustainable learning across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement a kick-off, mid-term and final transnational meeting; LTT for teachers to pilot IO1; LTT with students to pilot IO2; local piloting activities in each country; virtual piloting of IO3 with students; three thematic webinars; online coordination meetings; multiplier events; and continuous dissemination and impact activities supporting reuse beyond the partnership.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver three validated outputs: a teacher training programme (IO1), a classroom toolkit for students (IO2), and student e-learning pills (IO3). As a result, teachers apply shared media and AI literacy methods, students improve analysis and responsible communication skills, and schools reuse common tools. Impact extends to at least 500 external teachers and 2,000 students.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2026-1-NO01-KA220-SCH-000458502.title: Digital Clean Up Campaign 2
2026-1-NO01-KA220-SCH-000458502.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project equip schools to teach digital sustainability in practical, engaging ways. This matters because everyday digital use has a real environmental footprint and students need concrete habits to reduce it. We deliver classroom‑ready modules, a teacher toolkit and a student‑led campaign, piloted, translated and published on national platforms. Impact is tracked through teacher feedback, student reflections and quantitative indicators .

<< Implementation >>

The project is implemented through five structured work packages that move from research to development, piloting and dissemination.
Based on a cross‑country needs analysis the consortium co‑creates multilingual teaching modules on digital sustainability and a Student Engagement Toolkit, combining pedagogical design with student‑produced media.
The materials are piloted and effect is mesured in real classrooms, berfore partners publish the final modules and toolkit on national learning platforms

<< Results >>

The project will deliver ready‑to‑use teaching modules, a teacher toolkit and a student‑led Digital Sustainability Campaign, all tested, translated and published on national learning platforms. Schools gain practical resources for teaching digital sustainability, while students improve digital habits and communication skills. Teachers strengthen their capacity to address the environmental impact of everyday digital use.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

hr.name: Škola za Dizajn, Grafiku i Održivu Gradnju

2026-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000457479.title: Plastics Smart Europe
2026-1-PL01-KA220-SCH-000457479.summary:
<< Objectives >>

As coastal-based institutions, we aim to empower teachers as well-equipped citizen science educators who can address the invisible threat of microplastics and guide future generations. The project strengthens teachers’ competences through CLIL, interdisciplinary STEM and gender-sensitive pedagogy, supports curriculum integration with adaptable materials, enhances student engagement through immersive activities with a focus on girls in STEM, and fosters collaboration among partner organisations.

<< Implementation >>

The project provides teacher professional development through CLIL and STEM training to strengthen interdisciplinary and innovative teaching skills. Partners will develop ten digital microplastics education modules supported by enriched lesson plans and classroom resources. In addition, a Marine Microplastics Simulator and 360° immersive videos will be designed and tested to promote experiential, interactive, and student-centred learning in environmental and STEM education.

<< Results >>

The project will produce ten adaptable microplastics teaching modules, a Marine Microplastics Simulator (MMS), and immersive videos, along with a comprehensive teacher guide including curriculum-integrated lesson plans. These outputs will be supported by STEM-centred activities, interdisciplinary tasks, and enriched teaching materials that can be easily integrated into different curricula and used in immersive learning environments.

2026-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000452260.title: A.R.T.S.I. – Art, Rhythm, Therapy, Sensory Learning & Inclusion for Children with SEN
2026-1-RO01-KA220-SCH-000452260.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to improve inclusive school education for children with special educational needs by developing and piloting four creative, multisensory learning modules and strengthening teachers’ competences. Implemented by specialised schools in Romania, Spain and Croatia, the project builds European added value through transnational co-design, testing in diverse contexts and producing a transferable methodological guide and digital resources adaptable across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The project develops and pilots four creative learning modules (art, music, theatre/body expression and creative literacy) for students with SEN. Teachers collaborate through co-design, peer learning and transnational mobilities, including classroom observation and job shadowing. The results are consolidated into a European methodological guide and disseminated locally to support transferability, sustainability and wider adoption of inclusive practices in EU SEN schools.

<< Results >>

The project will involve 12 teachers/therapists (4 per country) by month 9 to deliver four A.R.T.S.I. modules and co-develop 4 accessible creative modules, each tested through two pilot cycles by M16. The modules will be piloted with 60 SEN students (ages 6-18), targeting ≥20% improvement in key skills. By M18, partners will publish an open-access European guide, 8 videos and tools, supported by 3 mobilities, 4 events and outreach to 300+ educators across Europe.

2026-1-SE01-KA220-SCH-000455360.title: Empowering Teachers for Inclusive and Sustainable STEM Learning in Schools Through Digital Tools
2026-1-SE01-KA220-SCH-000455360.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project aims to empower teachers to provide inclusive, sustainable, and bioeconomy-based STEM education. By
enhancing teachers' professional competencies through digital tools and innovative pedagogical approaches, it seeks to
create and disseminate inclusive, environmentally conscious, and STEM learning environments in schools. The project
supports teachers in permanently integrating these approaches into their lessons and fostering a sustainable educational
culture at the school level.

<< Implementation >>

The project will organize international learning, teaching, and training activities for teachers; and develop digital lesson
content for inclusive, sustainable, and bioeconomy-based STEM education. A teacher-focused digital e-book and e-learning
platform will be created and implemented in pilot schools. Furthermore, project results will be disseminated at local, national,
and European levels through online and in-person multiplier events.

<< Results >>

The project will strengthen teachers' professional competencies in inclusive, sustainable, and bioeconomy-based STEM
education. Tangible and reusable outputs will be developed, such as teacher-focused digital e-books, e-learning platforms,
school-based pilot application packages, and sustainable school guides. It will facilitate the widespread adoption of
innovative and inclusive STEM practices in schools, creating long-term institutional impact and a sustainable educational
culture for schools.

2026-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000457189.title: Animal-Assisted Interventions as Psychosocial Support for Students with Intellectual Disabilities
2026-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000457189.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen the use of animal-assisted interventions (AAI) as psychosocial support for students with intellectual disabilities. Through international cooperation, staff training, and practical implementation, partners seek to improve socio-emotional development, inclusion, and wellbeing of students while enhancing professional competences and developing shared guidelines for ethical and effective AAI practice.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement staff training, and group mobilities where students and professionals participate in animal-assisted activities in real educational settings. Partners will exchange practices and apply AAI methods directly with students. Activities will promote inclusion, experiential learning, and responsible interaction with animals, with strong attention to animal welfare, ethical practice, and safe learning environments.

<< Results >>

Expected results include improved socio-emotional competences and wellbeing of participating students and strengthened professional skills of staff in AAI. The project will produce an online guideline and handbook, organise dissemination events including a final conference, and create professional materials ensuring long-term use of results and wider impact in education, rehabilitation, and psychosocial support.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2026-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000462700.title: DAta TAles RevealIng Underlying Meanings through statistics
2026-1-SI01-KA220-SCH-000462700.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The DATARIUM project aims to strengthen statistical literacy in early compulsory education (ages 6 to 11) by developing a shared, research-informed conceptual framework for early statistical literacy grounded in statistical thinking. The project supports teachers in adopting inquiry-based and inclusive practices and promotes early data literacy in line with European priorities for key competences and lifelong learning.

<< Implementation >>

The project will develop a shared conceptual framework for early statistical literacy and translate it into curriculum-aligned learning activities and educational resources or primary education. The learning activities will be piloted and evaluated in partner schools across participating countries. Teachers will participate in structured training and collaborative exchange, supported by open educational resources to ensure effective implementation and transferability.

<< Results >>

DATARIUM will deliver a piloted and refined conceptual framework for early statistical literacy, a set of classroom-tested, curriculum-aligned learning activities, and trained teachers capable of implementing inquiry-based and data-informed classroom practices. All outputs will be openly accessible, supporting long-term sustainability, scalability, and adoption across diverse educational contexts.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2026-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000452805.title: Podpora pedagógov slovenskej minority v zahraničí - prvá učebnica slovenčiny ako materinského jazyka
2026-1-SK01-KA220-SCH-000452805.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The main goal is to support teachers and pedagogical staff of Slovak minority schools and centers abroad and improve their work by creating textbooks using Slovak as a mother tongue didactics, which we have identified as an important, currently absent need. 
We will include interdisciplinary relationships, RWCT methods (reading and writing for critical thinking), as well as multiculturalism and metalinguistic reasoning typical of multilingual children in the structure of the textbooks.

<< Implementation >>

To achieve the goals in the introduction - based on verifications by teachers from practice abroad - the author's team identifies topics from the educational curricula of the state educational program. Subsequently, we will create 2 textbooks in the form of interactive didactic materials on the website. We will verify the stages of textbook creation in partner countries by cooperating with teachers directly with their students - also at events with the aim of expanding the final target group.

<< Results >>

The main result will be a website with interactive didactic materials of two textbooks of Slovak as a mother tongue and methodological materials for teachers of Slovak minority schools and centers abroad. The sustainable result will be a significant improvement in the work of teachers and the educational process of students from Slovak minority schools and educational centers abroad - with an emphasis on students who are simultaneously maintaining their primary education in Slovakia.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000028037.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000028037.title: Upskilling counselling workers for remote, online services provision
2021-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000028037.summary:
<< Background >>

The COVID-19 pandemic significantly disrupted mental health services across the EU, increasing demand for care as people faced isolation, loss of income, anxiety and bereavement. Despite support for telehealth services, the mental health sector was reluctant to use ICT-based counselling due to a lack of trained staff able to conduct effective online sessions. This created a gap between the increased demand for support and the capacity of mental health workers.

The lack of training in remote mental health care limited the ability of workers to acquire the necessary skills. Strengthening both initial and continuing vocational education and training (VET) in this field is essential. European mental health workers need to develop technical skills (e.g. using digital platforms), organisational skills (e.g. creating a comfortable environment) and communication skills (e.g. communicating effectively online) to deliver optimal online consultations.

Since 2021, there has been progress in training mental health professionals for remote services, but comprehensive and continuous training is still crucial to fully bridge the skills gap.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to make available a curriculum with corresponding Open Educational Resources (OERs) for the continuous professional development of mental health workers, to address the emerging occupational & skills needs
related to the provision of ICT-enabled remote counselling services. The project’s specific objectives are to:
1. Document the skills required for providing online, remote mental health services
2. Define learning outcomes for a C-VET course for mental health workers on effective remote mental health services provision
3. Design, test and deliver a sector-validated online course for mental health workers to support digital, organizational and communication skills acquisition
4. Provide ready to use tools for mental health workers to facilitate the roll-out and support the provision of remote counselling services.

<< Implementation >>

Systematic needs analysis and skills mapping activities leading to the development of learning outcomes that reflect sector specificities and skills requirements for the provision of remote mental health services.
- Joint curriculum design of a continuing vocational training curriculum in remote mental health counselling for relevant professions
- Development of relevant teaching materials, a trainer's handbook and a learner's e-book to be made available as Open Educational Resources.
- To develop, test and deliver a Massive Open Online Course to increase flexibility and openness in continuing vocational education and training.
- Development of a toolkit to assess readiness and facilitate the introduction of online distance guidance services.
- Sharing project results through multiplier events and dissemination activities, inviting target groups to take up REMCO results and act as additional multipliers.

<< Results >>

PR1: 
Research report (in EN, DE, EL, FR, IT, RO and HR) including information on the methodology used (T1), an analysis of the challenges and work requirements of tele-counselling (T2), a collection of evidence on existing training provision for mental health professionals (T3) and the REMCO learning outcomes defined from this information (T4).

PR2: 
Curriculum (in EN, DE, EL, FR, IT, RO and HR), 
Learning materials in PDF format (in EN, DE, EL, FR, IT, RO and HR). 
Trainer's manual (in EN, DE, EL, FR, IT, RO and HR).

PR3: 
MOOC (in EN, DE, EL, FR, IT, RO and HR) with 6 modules including 7 videos, PP slides, MC questions, practical self-reflection exercises, case studies and real-life scenarios.

PR4:
Self-reflection tool with 30 questions (in EN, DE, EL, FR, IT, RO and HR)
E-BOOK (in EN, DE, EL, FR, IT, RO and HR)
Guidance protocol (in EN, DE, EL, FR, IT, RO and HR)
Good practice guide in EN
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000028121.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000028121.title: DIGITAL LEARNING PATHS
2021-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000028121.summary:
<< Background >>

We addressed the following needs:
NEED 1: The need of possibilities for individualized education. This is possible on our new developed OER-platform: Ariadna.eduaction, on which we developed, 40 learningpaths per technical field.
NEED 2: The need of a better coherence between the training courses and the needs in the industry: Therefore, all features of the platform Ariadna.education and the accompanying learningpaths are developed based on feedback from stakeholders of the industry.
NEED 3: The need to make VET- education more attractive. In the development of our learningpaths. Therefore In the development of our didactic material and learning paths, our starting point was always to captivate the students.
NEED 4: The need to adapt and improve the teaching practice. The developed learning paths give us the opportunity to diversify in teaching methods, which improves the quality of teaching as a whole.
In the projectteam, we built a collaborative platform with digital resources, on which any teacher can build his own learningpath. The international nature of the project ensured that there was input from organisations with different experiences and expertise, different specializations and different approaches.


<< Objectives >>

1) To design and build an online platform (https://ariadna.education/) for VET, with various resources, on which teachers can easily set up digital learning paths for their students. 
2) To encourage VET- teachers to use (and also develop it themselves) better training methods so that they can meet the
increasing need for quality in technical training.
3)To increase the cooperation of project partners (VET institutions) with the different stakeholders active in the vocational education and with the industry. 
4)To demonstrate to VET teachers, students and different stakeholders the need for new teaching methods and the benefits of these new methods. 
5)To identify the contribution of the digital learning paths to the integration of all students, in order to improve the inclusion of disadvantaged learners.
6) To promote innovative teaching methods in order to increase the influx into technical education, given the dire shortage of technicians on the labor market. 
7)To support the development of skills of project partners in project management (especially for project partners with little experience in project management) and in educational management.
8) To exchange know-how between the different partners and build a strong partner

<< Implementation >>

MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES:
A1:We drew up partneragreements between the coordinator and each partner.

A2:The original intention was to draw up a projecthandbook as a guide for the projectpartners. This was completed partially, but soon it became clear that a tailor- made advice worked better for each partner individually.

A3:We set up an internal workspace “dotedu.net”, containing all developed didactic materials and all documents used during TPM’s, LTTA’s, on line meetings and the used powerpoints and minutes and reports drawn up after those activities.

A4: We set up a steering committee with a group of people responsible to make management decisions. These persons were present during almost every meeting.

A5: After most TPM’s and LTTA’s, a report or minutes were drawn up.

A6:After each online meeting, minutes were drawn up.

A7:For every payment done by the coordinator to the partners, a payment note was drawn up, explaining the calculation of the payment. In June 2022 and in Augustus 2023, an overview of the already spent budget so far was sent to each partner.

A8 and A9: These activities only refer to the development of the interim and final reports for the National Agency.

A10: A Quality Assessment (QA-plan) was drawn up. This plan involved: baselinemeasurement, impactmeasurement, surveys to gather input and feedback from stakeholders for the development of didactic materials and the OER- platform “Ariadna.education”, evaluations by questionnaires of the TPM’s and LTTA’s.

A11: A general dissemination strategy was drawn up by the coordinator and each partner drew up his own dissemination plan as well.

A12: Each partner developed a proposal for a project logo. After voting, a final choice was made for the project logo. This projectlogo is added on each developed didactic material and on the OER- platform Ariadna.education.

A13: Several partners developed their own leaflets and used them during dissemination activities.

A14: Several partners developed their own posters and panels and used themduring dissemination activities.
 
A15: Project website: A part of the platform Ariadna.education is set up as project information (namely the tabs: “Project Information” and “News”).

A16: Dissemination on social media: every partner disseminated on social media.

A17: Most partners also disseminated via press releases.

A18: In the course of the project, two E-newsletters have been developed.

LEARNING ACTIVITIES:
-Learning activity 1 in Romania: Training in Digital Education for teachers. (9/05/22 12/05/22) 
-Learning activity 2 in Spain: Learning activity in Marine Technics for the partnerschool from Croatia/Sibenik. (24/04/23 28/04/23)
-Learning activity 3 in Croatia/ Sibenik: Cross curricular tests of digital platform and digital learning paths + training in digital tools for students and teachers. (8/05/23 12/05/23)




<< Results >>

TANGIBLE RESULTS:

The tangible results are:
1)A new OER- platform “Ariadna.education” (https://ariadna.education/), on which can be used existing digital learningpaths (as a student) or can be developed new learningpaths (as a teacher).The existing learningpaths are accessible via the tab “Learningpaths”. Each developed learning path is represented by a rectangle. Via the menu above, the desired kind of learningpaths can be selected. For each technical field, a different colour of rectangle is used.
The following number of learningpaths have been developed by the project team:
-Field Automation and robotics: 49 learningpaths
-Field Mechanics: 49 learningpaths
-Field Central Heating: 24 learningpaths
-Field Marine Technics: 43 learningpaths
-Field Construction: 41 learningpaths
All learningpaths are set up with the same structure: motivation phase, information phase and consolidation phase. The learning paths represent a process that the student must go through in order to learn about a particular subject. The way to go through a learning path is self-explanatory.
To be able to develop a new digital learningpath, an account is needed and can be requested from the Romanian partner. A manual on how to develop a new learningpath is added (via a link) at the bottom of the page “Project information” and after clicking on the button: Add new Learningpath.

2)A lot of didactic materials in the 5 technical fields, have been developed by the projectteam:
-Field Automation and robotics:
26 powerpoints, 14 powerpoints with narration, 12 videos and 1 textdocument have been developed.
-Field Mechanics:
47 powerpoints, 8 powerpoints with narration, 7 videos and 15 textdocuments have been developed.
-Field Central heating:
20 powerpoints, 6 videos and 14 textdocuments have been developed.
-Field Marine Technics:
7 powerpoints, 22 animations, 45 videos and 7 textdocuments have been developed.
-Field Construction:
12 powerpoints, 1 powerpoint with narration, 10 videos and 12 textdocuments have been developed

INTANGIBLE RESULTS:

Although there were signs among the participating students at the LTTA in Croatia/Sibenik (and later on) that students' motivation, independent study, self-evaluation, ability to catch up in learning subjects were stimulated, it was only at the end of the project possible to actually put this into practice. This is because the form of the learning paths and didactic material had to gradually evolve into a flexible form during the project duration. At the end of the project we were faced with the exam periods and shortly afterwards the summer holidays, so we actually missed the big breakthrough a bit. The expected breakthrough and also the success experience among the teachers will therefore occur at the start of the next school year. However, the members of the project team were already able to build a strong network with stakeholders.
Stakeholders also have the option to add didactic materials and learning paths to the platform themselves. Thanks to this feature and since the bond with the stakeholders has been forged, this provides great potential for the future.

2021-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000034849.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000034849.title: Trauma-Informed Practice For Workers In Public Service Settings
2021-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000034849.summary:
<< Background >>

The TIPS project built upon the successful Erasmus+ project “Post-traumatic Integration – Low-level Psychosocial Support
and Intervention for Refugees (PTI)”, which received great interest and a distinction as 'best practice'. During their dissemination activities, several partners were asked if the PTI project could be extended to support various professionals who come in contact with clients or people suffering from posttraumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) but do not have a professional training. The number of persons in Europe suffering from PTSS is likely to increase in the years to come, through migration from violence and natural disasters, and health issues. Based on a needs analysis, we found that especially in the public sector many professions are confronted in their work with clients having PTSS: labour office advisers, social benefit workers, housing department officers, lawyers, debt counsellors, just to name a few. All these professionals have their specific experience but no training how to deal with a person who suffers from PTSS, and therefore frequently misjudge their clients. Implementing trauma-informed counselling will help service professionals to understand and respond appropriately to the effects of trauma.

<< Objectives >>

The general objective of this project consists of raising the awareness about the occurrence of PTSS and equipping professionals working in the public sector with skills to assist them in identifying their clients, promoting their inclusion, and improving their own respective service or counselling work.
To reach these objectives, the specific project objectives were: • to compile guidelines for professionals working in the public sector to raise their awareness about the occurrence of PTSS among their clients, and increase their skills to identify PTSS among their clients and to promote their inclusion; • to develop specific cases that illustrate common work situations and show examples how to react to clients who are suffering from PTSS; • to develop concrete training materials that build on these guidelines and cases; • to enable networking and exchanges of experiences through an e-platform for the access to all contents and training materials; • to give immediate access to the products through the development of mobile applications for smart phones; and • to achieve sustainability by providing access to of the project outputs for at least five years after the end of the project, i.e., until 2028.

<< Implementation >>

This consortium had the unique chance not only to develop the outputs described in the next section, but also to raise the awareness about the occurrence of PTSS and to equip professionals working in the public sector with skills to assist them in identifying PTSS among their clients, promote their inclusion, and improve their own respective service or counselling work. Therefore, the partners have put a strong emphasis on project promotion and dissemination of project results: they have organised a number of project promotion activities, both during and at the end of the project life (including the 3-month extension period granted by the national agency in order to adequately organise the dissemination activities). They have focused, on the one hand, on the stakeholders of the project target groups, and have, on the other hand, also included representatives of the final beneficiaries to make sure that the project results are in line with their needs and requirements. To this end, the project partners have given effect to a number of public relations activities, in English and each of the partner languages, including the following: a specific project logo for the purpose of a strong visual appearance; a website with lots of information about the background and the outputs of the project; the production of flyers with a description of the project and its outputs; meetings with stakeholders and professionals working in the public sector; newsletters in several phases of the project; participation in national and European conferences for the dissemination of results; participation in monitoring conferences of the National Agency; and last but not least, multiplier events with stakeholders and professionals working in the public sector in each partner country.

<< Results >>

The project has developed a wide number of tangible outputs (results): 1) User-oriented Guidelines for professionals working in
the public sector to raise their awareness about the occurrence of PTSS among their clients, and equip them with skills to identify PTSS among their clients, promote their inclusion, and also lead to better working conditions; 2) a Catalogue with a Case Studies Collection illustrating the most common work situations and showing examples how to react to clients who are suffering from PTSS; 3) a Resource Pack with training and e-learning activities and quizzes related to the particular chapters of the Guidelines and Catalogue; 4) an Interactive e-platform with the access to all contents and training materials, including specially produced podcasts and videos; 5) Mobile applications for smart phones that will also give access to the materials. All these products will be available in English and all languages of the partnership, i.e. Croatian, Dutch, French, German, Greek, Portuguese, Slovak and Slovenian.
In addition, the following results have been elaborated with the budget for project management and implementation: 6) Website: the project
website (https://trauma-informed-practice.eu) provides all details of the project and the consortium; it is linked to the e-Training
platform and contains the project results, and will be maintained at least five years after the end of the project, i.e. until 2028; 7) Newsletters: each partner has compiled information about the project, its milestones and current activities, in three issues
during the project running (launch and background of the project; results from the development process; final results and multiplier events); 8) Flyers: they were produced in each language of the partnership plus English, and distributed at meetings with stakeholders and organisations, and serve(d) as entry point to obtain further information from the project website.
For the purposes of managing the project, regular in-person and online meetings were held, with prior invitations, clear agendas, extensive minutes, and monitoring procedures. Moreover, the many discussions within the consortium have led the partners to formulate a new project proposal, which has been submitted to Erasmus+ in March 2024.

2021-1-BE03-KA220-VET-000033175.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-BE03-KA220-VET-000033175.title: Nachhaltiges Gärtnern für eine gemeinsame Zukunft
2021-1-BE03-KA220-VET-000033175.summary:
<< Background >>

Die Bewerbung für dieses Projekt erfolgte auf Grundlage der gemeinsamen Zielsetzung der Partnerschulen, internationale Erfahrungen zu sammeln. Es wurde als äußerst wichtig erachtet, dass Studenten und Mitarbeiter von, in und mit anderen Ländern lernen. Dabei ging es nicht nur um die Erweiterung des beruflichen Wissens, sondern auch um persönliches Wachstum und die Reflexion der eigenen Einstellung hin zu umweltfreundlicherem Handeln privat und im Beruf. Durch die Kooperation sollte eine zeitgemäße Ausbildung angeboten werden, die die Ziele der nachhaltigen Entwicklung, den Umweltschutz und Maßnahmen zur Bekämpfung des Klimawandels in den Ausbildungsinhalten berücksichtigt. Um dies zu erreichen, war es notwendig, Wissen und Innovationen aus anderen Ländern und Regionen zu beziehen, zu erarbeiten, zu vergleichen und gemeinsam zu reflektieren. Dies war nicht nur für die Auszubildenden von Bedeutung, sondern auch für die Mitarbeiter, Lehrpersonen und Ausbilder, die auchdie kommenden Auszubildenden für die Ziele der nachhaltigen Entwicklung sensibilisieren und ihnen die erforderlichen Kenntnisse, Fähigkeiten und Fertigkeiten vermitteln werden. Zudem sollten die Auszubildenden für das Lernen und Arbeiten im Ausland begeistert werden. 

<< Objectives >>

Durch die Durchführung des Projekts sollte eine Zusammenarbeit zur Ergänzung von Unterrichtsinhalten und zur Vermittlung von Fähigkeiten und Fertigkeiten im Rahmen der gärtnerischen Aus- und Weiterbildung erreicht werden. Dabei wurde besonderes Augenmerk auf die Ziele der nachhaltigen Entwicklung, den Umweltschutz und Maßnahmen zur Bekämpfung des Klimawandels gelegt. Die Teilnehmer gewöhnten sich intuitiv daran, ihr Handeln hinsichtlich Nachhaltigkeit und Umweltverträglichkeit zu hinterfragen und nach „grünen Lösungen“ zu suchen. Da Lehrpersonen und Ausbilder nicht nur Begleitpersonen, sondern auch aktive Teilnehmer waren, trug diese Partnerschaft zum Ziel der kontinuierlichen Weiterbildung für Lehrer, Ausbilder und Erziehungspersonal bei. Dies führte zudem zur Weiterentwicklung der teilnehmenden Schulen und Institutionen insgesamt. Ein weiteres Ziel war, dem Fachkräftemangel vorzubeugen und die zukünftigen Fachkräfte optimal auf die Herausforderungen vorzubereiten, die in naher Zukunft auf dem Arbeitsmarkt erwartet werden. Durch den geschützten Rahmen und die relativ kurze Dauer der gemeinsamen Unterrichtseinheiten fiel es vor allem zurückhaltenden oder ängstlichen Schülern leichter, den Kontakt mit Unbekanntem herzustellen.

<< Implementation >>

Im Rahmen der Erasmus-Partnerschaft wurden verschiedene transnationale Projekttreffen und praktische Unterrichtswochen (LTT-Aktivitäten) erfolgreich durchgeführt. Diese Aktivitäten trugen wesentlich zur Erreichung der gemeinsamen Ziele bei, insbesondere zur Förderung des nachhaltigen Gärtnerns und des Klimaschutzes. Zusätzlich wurden drei weitere Aktivitäten in das Programm aufgenommen: eine spezielle Lehrerweiterbildung und zwei große LTT-Aktivitäten als Abschlusstreffen für die Auszubildenden. Virtuelle Projekttreffen (TPM): Um unnötige Reisen zu vermeiden und den ökologischen Fußabdruck zu reduzieren, fanden einige transnationale Projekttreffen (TPM) virtuell statt. Dies trug zum Klimaschutz bei und unterstützte den ökologischen Gedanken der Partnerschaft. Außerdem förderte es die Flexibilität der KollegInnen im Umgang mit Kommunikationstechnologien.
Es fand auch eine Integration von TPM in Lehrerweiterbildungen und LTT-Aktivitäten statt. Bei den drei internationalen und zwei internen Lehrerweiterbildungen und mehreren LTT-Aktivitäten wurden jeweils TPM entweder vorher oder nachher organisiert. Dadurch konnte die Managementarbeit von allen Partnern gemeinsam geleistet und überzählige Reisen vermieden werden, was ebenfalls zum Klimaschutz beitrug.
Folgende gemischte LLT-Aktivitäten wurden bei den verschiedenen Partnern durchgeführt: Der deutsche Partner veranstaltete die Aktivität zum Thema "Planung und Anlage von Staudenbeeten unter Berücksichtigung des Klimawandels und der Nachhaltigkeit". Der französische Partner behandelte das Thema "Funktionaler Ansatz von Trockenstein in seiner Rolle als Regulator des Ökosystems". Beim niederländischen Partner fand die Aktivität zum Thema "Lebendiger Garten - lebendiger öffentlicher Raum" statt. Beim lettischen Partner wurde das Thema "Planung und Gestaltung von Pflanzungen durch Nutzen der Vorteile moderner Technologie" behandelt. Schließlich behandelte der österreichische Partner organisierte die Aktivität zum Thema "Möglichkeiten des Anbaus von frischem Gemüse im Winter zur Reduzierung des Imports aus fernen Ländern". 
Da es sich um gemischte LTT-Aktivitäten handelte, mussten die Teilnehmer vor der Aktivität gemeinsame Aufgaben erledigen, während der Aktivität praktisch arbeiten, ihr Handeln gemeinsam reflektieren und über ihre Aktivitäten berichten. Einige Zeit nach ihrer Teilnahme an der LTT-Aktivität füllten sie nochmal einen Fragebogen aus. Dadurch setzten sie sich erneut mit den erworbenen Erkenntnissen und der inzwischen erfolgten Veränderung ihrer Einstellung oder Handlungsweise in Richtung Nachhaltigkeit, Umwelt- und Klimaschutz auseinander. Sie wurden nochmals an die Ziele erinnert und weiter motiviert, auf "grüne Lösungen" hinzuarbeiten.
Beim kroatischen Partner fand eine interne Weiterbildung für die Lehrpsersonen statt. Diese Aktivität drehte sich um das Thema "Möglichkeiten der infrastrukturellen Anpassung der Schule an die aktuellen Erfordernisse des Arbeitsmarktes und des Umweltschutzes". 
Die Teilnahme an den und die teilweise Mitorganisation der europäischen Lehrerweiterbildungen diente den Kollegen zum Knüpfen neuer und zum Ausbauen bestehender Kontakte sowie zur fachlichen und pädagogischen Weiterbildung. Diese internationalen Lehrerseminare trugen auch zur Verbreitung der Projektaktivitäten und -ergebnisse bei, da an diesen Seminaren auch Kollegen von anderen europäischen Gartenbauschulen teilnahmen, die nicht Partner im Projekt waren. Eine zusätzliche interne Lehrerweiterbildung wurde durchgeführt und zwei zusätzliche LTT-Aktivitäten wurden als Abschlusstreffen für die Auszubildenden organisiert, bei denen die Teilnehmer ihre in den vorherigen Aktivitäten erworbenen Kenntnisse und Fähigkeiten vertieften, in gemeinsamen Projekten praktisch anwandten.
Die Teilnehmer berichteten während und nach den LTT-Wochen über ihre Aktivitäten. Veröffentlichungen erfolgten auf der Homepage der Vereinigung der europäischen Gartenbaulehrer, in lokalen und regionalen Medien sowie in sozialen Medien und auf den Kanälen der jeweiligen Partnereinrichtungen, im Familien-/Freundeskreis, an der Arbeit und in sozialen Medien sowie im Umfeld der jeweiligen Partnereinrichtungen auf ihren üblichen Veröffentlichungskanälen. Zusätzlich wurde von einigen LTT-Aktivitäten Padlets erstellt, auf denen die EIndrücke und Resultate anschaulich zusammengefasst dargestellt werden. Es gab auch Veröffentlichungen über LinkedIn, in Newlettern von Betrieben, die wir während der Aktivitäten besichtigt haben oder die uns bei den LTT-Aktivitäten unterstützt haben. Ebenso wurden Berichte auf der Webseite der europäischen EUROPEA Vereinigung veröffentlicht oder on Schulzeitungen sowie auf der Webseite der kroatischen Provinz Varazdin.

<< Results >>

Das Ziel und somit auch Ergebnis dieses Projektes war die Zusammenarbeit zur Ergänzung von Unterrichtsinhalten und zur Vermittlung von Fähigkeiten und Fertigkeiten im Rahmen der gärtnerischen Aus- und Weiterbildung, mit besonderem Fokus auf die Aspekte der nachhaltigen Entwicklung, den Umweltschutz und Maßnahmen zur Bekämpfung des Klimawandels. Der Gartenbau ist so vielfältig, dass nicht jede Schule alle Bereiche allein abdecken kann. Daher beschränken sich die im Unterricht angesprochenen Themen hauptsächlich auf die am häufigsten angewandten und gefragten Fähigkeiten und Fertigkeiten in der näheren Umgebung. 
Umwelt, Umweltschutz und nachhaltige Entwicklung sind jedoch globale Themen, die über das nähere Umfeld hinausgehen. Aus diesem Grund war es wichtig, dass die Lernenden und ihre Lehrpersonen Einblicke erhielten, wie sich der Klimawandel in anderen Regionen äußert und welche Ansätze anderswo verfolgt werden, um dem entgegenzuwirken und im gärtnerischen Alltag nachhaltig und umweltschützend zu handeln. Die im Rahmen dieser international durchgeführten Unterrichtseinheiten erarbeiteten Fähigkeiten und Fertigkeiten bleiben bei den Auszubildenden wesentlich nachhaltiger verankert als die „üblichen“ Unterrichtsinhalte. Diese unterschiedlichen und für die meisten Teilnehmer unüblichen Lernmethoden trugen und tragen weiterhin zur Innovation der beruflichen Ausbildung im Gartenbau bei. Dies geschah unmittelbar bei den aktiven Teilnehmern und geschieht langfristig, indem Lehrpersonen und Ausbilder als aktive Teilnehmer mitarbeiteten und ihre Erfahrungen an ihren Heimateinrichtungen in folgenden Unterrichtsstunden, in anderen Klassen und in späteren Jahren weitervermittelten, wodurch sie zur Innovation der beruflichen Ausbildung beitrugen. Es geschah und geschieht auch dadurch, dass die Teilnehmer in ihren Klassen den anderen MItschülern von ihren Erfahrungen berichteten.
Durch dieses Gesamtergebnis wurden auch weitere Resultate erreicht: Die Teilnehmer gewöhnten sich intuitiv daran, ihr Handeln im Hinblick auf Nachhaltigkeit und Umweltverträglichkeit zu hinterfragen und nach „grünen Lösungen“ zu suchen. 
Durch die praxisnahen Unterrichte zu aktuellen Themen der Nachhaltigkeit und des Umweltschutzes wurde dem Fachkräftemangel vorgebeugt, und die zukünftigen Fachkräfte wurden gut auf die Aufgaben vorbereitet, die in naher Zukunft auf dem Arbeitsmarkt von ihnen erwartet wurden. Durch die europaweite Kooperation mit der europäischen Vereinigung der Gartenbaulehrpersonen sowie die Organisation von und die Teilnahme an den europäischen Lehrerweiterbildungen wurde eine Verbreitung über die Partnerschaft hinaus bei direkt betroffenen, aber nicht in das Projekt involvierten KollegInnen erreicht, was auch ein konkretes Resultat des Projektes ist. So trug unser Projekt nicht nur zur internen, sondern auch zur ständigen Weiterbildung von weiteren Lehrern, Ausbildern und Erziehungspersonal bei, was auch zur Weiterentwicklung anderer als der teilnehmenden Schulen und Institutionen führt.
Die im Rahmen der international durchgeführten Unterrichtseinheiten erarbeiteten Fähigkeiten und Fertigkeiten blieben bei den Auszubildenden nachhaltig verankert. Der Eindruck ihrer Teilnahme wirkte auch nach Beendigung ihrer Schulzeit fort, und sie setzten ihre in Richtung Nachhaltigkeit, Umwelt- und Klimaschutz veränderten Handlungsweisen auch in ihrer späteren Berufsausübung fort. Dadurch konnte sich die Wirkung teilweise auf Arbeitgeber, Kollegen und Kunden auswirken. Beispielsweise konnten den Kunden klimafreundliche Pflanzkonzepte, wassereffiziente Bewässerungssysteme oder die Verwendung von Naturstein angeboten oder empfohlen werden. Zudem wurde der lokalen Bevölkerung produziertes Gemüse angeboten und die Teilnehmer lernten Wintergemüse kennen und jahreszeitgemäß zuzubereiten. Auch bei der Anlage und Pflege von öffentlichem Grün oder der Dekoration des Friedhofs nach Methoden, die Nachhaltigkeit, Umwelt- und Klimaschutz gerecht wurden, wurden nicht in das Projekt involvierte Personen auf diese Arbeitsweise aufmerksam und zum Nachdenken oder Nachahmen motiviert.
Durch das Einbeziehen von Institutionen, die die Demokratie und den europäischen Gedanken näherbringen, wurde während der beiden Abschluss-LTT-Aktivitäten ein weiteres Resultat erzielt: Neben der fachlichen und umweltrelevanten Weiterbildung wurde die Aufmerksamkeit der Schüler und ihrer Begleitpersonen eben auf Europa und Demokratie gelenkt. In Zusammenhang mit den positiven Erinnerungen, die die Schülern mit den LTT-Aktivitäten verbinden, sollte daher auch dieser Gedanke nachhaltig verankert bleiben.
Ein weiteres sehr anschauliches Resultat ist die Auswertung des Fragebogens am Ende des Projektes. Dieser Fragebogen wurde allen Teilnehmern geschickt und die Resultate beim letzten TPM besprochen (Siehe Abschnitt Methodologie und Evaluation).
