2021-1-BG01-KA220-VET-000024853.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-BG01-KA220-VET-000024853.title: Professional Foreign Language Preparation of VET Students in Customer Service for Quality Tourism (ProTourism)
2021-1-BG01-KA220-VET-000024853.summary:
<< Background >>

The ProTourism project is set in the context of the demand for skills in the tourism sector in Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovenia and Serbia and the capacity of the VET sectors, especially VET schools in tourism, to respond effectively to this demand. According to the CEDEFOP study (2020) on the key skills employers demand from VET graduates, three key skills stand out:

- customer service
- communication 
- English.

The main needs and motives for the candidacy and the subsequent implementation of the ProTourism project are directly related to the demand for skills among employers, the need of professional foreign language teachers in tourism schools for up-to-date and relevant pedagogical materials on the topics of customer service, communication and English language, the lack of this type of material presented in each partner country, as well as, last but not least, the need of the students themselves in the tourism vocational schools for attractive and practically oriented content, which would be a tool for building stable communication skills and customer service in English in any tourism profession.

<< Objectives >>

The ProTourism project aimed to improve the quality of English language teaching in vocational schools in the tourism sector. It aims to provide VET teachers with pedagogical materials that are in line with the skills demand of employers in this sector. The professional skill areas we focus on are customer service and communication. Our project brings together five organizations from four countries where tourism is important, such as Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovenia and Serbia, in their efforts to support vocational schools in providing quality training in specific areas.

           In our project, we had set ourselves consistent and logical goals that will lead to the qualitative achievement of the set final result - the creation of digital pedagogical materials for specific professions in the tourism sector with a focus on customer service and communication. The overall completion of the project was structured into three overarching areas of activity: Activity I – Project Management, Activity II – Development/Implementation of Project Results and Activity III – Promotion and Sharing of Project Results. Each activity includes sub-activities distributed among the partners with a specific scope, time and a specific result.

<< Implementation >>

The overall completion of the project is structured in 3 overarching areas of activity within which sub-activities are distributed as follows:

Activity 1 - Management: Development of project management guidelines, tasks allocation of tasks between partners, continuous communication and cooperation process within the partnership, monitoring through internal Activity 1 - Management: Development of project management guidelines, tasks allocation of tasks between partners, continuous communication and cooperation process within the partnership, monitoring through internal progress reports; risk management; interim and final report to the Bulgarian national agency; organization of 4 transnational project and etc.
Activity 2 - Development:
Activity 2.1 – Development of pedagogical materials and upload to the platform. 
Activity 2.2 - Development of teaching materials. Instructional training of language teachers in the field of VET. 
Activity 2.3 - Pilot training of trainees in VET. 
Activity 2.4 - Evaluation and and fine-tuning

Activity 3 - Promotion and sharing: Creation of a website; 40 online publications; 15 thematic presentations at external events; organization of 1 multiplier event in Sofia. 

<< Results >>

The main tangible and intangible results of the ProTourism project can be divided into several thematic components:

– Set of digital pedagogical materials to support language training in VET schools with an emphasis on the topics of Customer Service and Communication.
– Instructing and training a total of 27 foreign language teachers by profession in VET schools from each partner country (Bulgaria, Serbia, Slovenia, and Croatia) on how to use the created digital pedagogical materials produced in their classrooms.
– 488 VET students in grades 10-12 participated in pilot activities.
– Within the framework of the project, we disseminated its activities and results to 850 stakeholders from all partner countries and beyond through 1 multiplier event, 40 online publications, 10 thematic presentations at external events, ongoing information, online articles in various media, etc.).
Among the achieved intangible results are: 
– Improved professional and digital competences of language teachers;
– Improved professional language competences of VET students;
– Improved skills of VET students in Customer service and communication for the Touristic sector;
– Improved quality and attractiveness of VET education in partnering institutions.

2021-1-BG01-KA220-VET-000033346.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-BG01-KA220-VET-000033346.title: HoReCa Zero Waste: Enhancing the access to OERs and greening the curricula
2021-1-BG01-KA220-VET-000033346.summary:
<< Background >>

Food waste has a huge economic, social, and environmental impact. Every year, nearly 59 million tonnes of food waste are generated in the EU (131 kg per capita). This represents a loss of €132 billion. 
The European strategic documents of recent years change the philosophy and approach to waste, and more specifically propose a transition from ecological waste management as a key factor for the protection of the environment and human health, to a policy of preventing its formation and its inclusion in the economic cycle, based on a "circular economy".
Based on the EU Circular Economy Action Plan, we believe that awareness is the first step to tackle the problem, and skills and competences to prevent waste become extremely important.
Carrying out activities in the field of professional education and training, we found that there is a lack of information and educational content on methods to optimize the use and storage of food, as well as on the importance of reducing food waste.
With the implementation of the project, we respond to these needs by providing new educational resources and promoting the acquisition of green skills in the HoReCa sector, in response to target 12.3 for sustainable development.


<< Objectives >>

The project focuses on education to prevent food waste in the HoReCa sector, incl. the application of innovative training methods, through the digitization of the training content for the professions "Cook" and "Waiter" and the development of new training modules for the prevention of food waste.
With the implementation of the project, we wanted to achieve the following specific goals:
- provision of accessible education and training programs, in line with individual needs and expectations through the use of participatory approaches and ICT-based methodologies
- Providing of modern and dynamic, committed and professional environment inside the HoReCa businesses: ready to integrate good practices and new methods into daily activities;
- open to synergies with organisations active in HoReCa training; strategic planning of professional development for staff in line with individual needs and organizational objectives;
- enhancing cooperation in the field of VET at the EU level through building a European Network for the adoption of more green skills in the HoReCa sector in response to the Sustainable Development Goal 12.3 target.


<< Implementation >>

The project focuses on food waste prevention education in the HoReCa sector and at the same time on a business model. It is targeted at various tourism stakeholders: hotels, restaurants, social partners, vocational education and training centers.
The following activities were implemented during the project:
1. Project management - planning, implementation and monitoring of the project based on cooperation between project partners
2. Implementation activities – joint development of the project results within the partnership, contribution of each partner with specific qualifications and experience to achieve the project objectives.
3. Activities for sharing and promotion: 5 national information days aimed at sharing, explaining and popularizing the results of the project have been organized.


<< Results >>

During the project, 5 intellectual products were created: (1) a methodology for adapting educational content in a digital environment; (2) Open educational resources have been created for the prevention of food waste - including written and video content; (3) Software has been developed - a module for trainers and mentors, including options for testing and adding files and training materials; (4) Software has been developed - a module for learners, including networking, learning, discussion, etc.; (5) An EU network has been established to prevent food waste in HoReCa.
Other results achieved:
- Improved collaboration between education and business, lifelong learning encouraged.
- Carried out cooperation and exchange, contributing to the organizational development of the participating partners.
- Created opportunities to influence the creation of better competences that are directly used for current or future occupations and the adoption of more circular economy solutions.
- Conditions have been created for learning in a digital environment, which ensures the continuity of the learning process.

2021-1-CZ01-KA220-VET-000025194.title: European Consulting Standards in Tree Work
2021-1-CZ01-KA220-VET-000025194.summary:
<< Background >>

The role of trees in urban environments is just as essential as in forest ecosystems. However, trees in non-forest greenery, similar to those in natural forests, are increasingly affected by climate change. With the growing interest in arboriculture and tree care, we have encountered varying levels of quality in assessment reports, which lack standardization.
While practical tree care can already follow technical standards developed under the first Erasmus+ project, Technical Standards in Tree Work (TeST), there were still no established standards for consultancy in tree care. To address this gap, we applied for another Erasmus+ project, European Consulting Standards in Tree Work, aimed at defining best practices and guidelines for consultancy in arboriculture.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we aimed to unify and refine best practices in tree consultancy across European countries. The project was designed to create high-quality materials defining the minimum requirements for professionals providing tree care consultancy.
As part of this effort, we reviewed the current state of knowledge and identified national specifications. The development of these tools helped improve communication between arborists, tree owners, tree managers, and other relevant stakeholders. Additionally, the project contributed to establishing a standardized qualification process and creating a foundation for effective training.
ECoST built on the development of European arboricultural standards, providing high-quality tools for recognizing best practices in arboriculture and urban forestry, as well as supporting training and certification of professionals.

2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000029639.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000029639.title: Green and safety skills for workers in bike based urban last mile deliveries
2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000029639.summary:
<< Background >>

The continuous growth of e-commerce, initially accelerated by the COVID-19 and later adopted as a lifestyle, has intensified the pressure on Last Mile Deliveries (LMDs), exposing inefficiencies in the courier and postal (CEP) sectors on the one hand, and leading to the emergence of the so-called "platform economy" linked to food delivery. As a result, there is a pressing and immediate need to rapidly train and deploy a skilled workforce to address these challenges in urban contexts across Europe. Social and corporate responsibility is a significant challenge for this fast-growing sector, where CEP operators are under pressure to contribute to environmental and social sustainability of their operations, addressing critical issues (air pollution, traffic , road safety).
To meet these challenges, many companies are transitioning to deliveries based on conventional /electric (cargo) bikes, for short-distance urban logistics. This shift aligns with the EU Green Deal and national strategies aimed at creating zero-carbon cities. Bike-based deliveries not only support environmental goals but also enhance customer satisfaction and service quality. Despite this momentum, disparities across Europe remain due to insufficient awareness.

<< Objectives >>

a.Define EU-wide occupational requirements for LMD bike-based operators, building on the ESCO skills chart. This update was urgently needed to reflect the evolving role of bike couriers, addressing trends in green skills, safety, non-violent communication, and environmental awareness.
b. In collaboration with CEP sectors and training institutions, design a tailored vocational curriculum and educational resources for students and trainers. The goal was to develop a curriculum that is adaptable to national non-formal training systems, compact, accessible, self-paced, and available in multiple languages.
c.Launch and pilot the training delivery methods broadly, then refine them with stakeholders to ensure ownership and local relevance. This approach maximized the reach of the pedagogical resources through a Virtual Open Online Course (VOOC).
d. In collaboration with CEP, education, political sectors, and industry representatives (CIE) and the ESCO committee, SAFE LMD aimed to initiate the recognition and validation of new skills for LMD cyclists and facilitate their integration into certification schemes at both national and EU levels.

This approach ensured aligning with evolving market needs, EUpolicy&“European Bicycle Declaration”

<< Implementation >>

- Conduct desk research and interviews to identify skills gaps and mismatches, and to define up-to-date occupational requirements for LMD cyclists.
- Structure a compact curriculum (ECQ Level 3-4) along with Open Educational Resources (OERs) on sustainable and safe bike-based LMD operations, to be delivered both while employed and prior to employment.
- Develop, launch , pilot, and fine-tune a self-paced vocational course for LMD cyclists, leveraging the flexibility of the VET format to meet the sector's specific needs.
- Raise awareness about the sectoral recognition of LMD cyclists' green and safety skills, as well as transversal skills.
- Launch, test and operate an online examination portal (on Bizexaminer, an external provider) to validate LMD cyclists' skills acquired through learning from the SAFE LMD courses, or different contexts.
- Initiate and follow-up the update of the occupational profiles of bicycle couriers and delivery operators in the ESCO skills chart, and create qualification specifications for LMD cyclists.
- Define, launch and pilot an online examination scheme to assess the skills and competences of LMD cyclists in the seven core areas covered in the curriculum, including green and safety skills, communication, and social responsibility.
- Engage stakeholders continuously throughout the project to recognize the relevance of SAFE-LMD learning outcomes and raise awareness of the need to support new qualification paths (including micro-skills) in relevant competence and qualification schemes.
- Advocate and raise awareness among key sector stakeholders through multiplier events and dissemination activities, including outreach to social partners working with groups with fewer opportunities, encouraging them to adopt and embed SAFE-LMD results in their own national contexts. 

<< Results >>

1_Common Competence Framework for LMD Cyclists
The Common Competence Framework for Workers in Urban Bike-Based Last Mile Deliveries outlines the essential attitudes, knowledge, skills, and behaviors required for the occupational profile of LMD (Last Mile Delivery) cyclists. This framework not only identifies the competencies necessary for operating bike-based delivery vehicles (skills demand) but also assesses the skills available in the labor market (skills supply) and highlights existing skill gaps. Rooted in skills intelligence, this matrix of core and functional competencies is pivotal in recognizing new trends and emerging occupational needs in urban logistics and cycle logistics, fostering the growth of sustainable LMD practices.  
A key highlight of the framework is its emphasis on the continuous development of competencies, recognizing that mastering the skills for safe and environmentally friendly riding is an ongoing process, rather than a one-time achievement. The framework encourages both formal and informal training as foundational tools, ensuring that LMD workers can build and sustain their skills over time. It also promotes shared values and common performance standards through the acquisition of transversal skills and competencies, advancing professionalization within the sector.

2_Curriculum Structure  
The SafeLMD Curriculum** features a well-structured learning program comprising seven distinct learning units, each designed to equip LMD cyclists with critical competencies. The units cover key areas such as:  
1. Knowing goods and packaging  
2. Handling and administrative procedures  
3. Road traffic regulations  
4. Bicycle characteristics  
5. Basics of safe riding  
6. Communication skills and customer service  
7. Social responsibility, entrepreneurship, and mentoring.  

This curriculum is comprehensive, with clearly defined learning outcomes that are integrated across all lessons, ensuring that LMD cyclists receive a holistic education to meet the demands of modern urban logistics. The Trainer’s Handbook and Learners’ E-Book further support this structure, offering accessible guidance for both instructors and trainees.

3_Open Educational Resources (OERs)
The development of Open Educational Resources (OERs) in six languages is a standout achievement. These OERs feature interactive content, including VOOC infrastructures that support self-reflection and self-evaluation of learning. Additionally, learners are empowered to provide feedback through a dedicated tool, fostering an environment of continuous improvement. This multilingual approach broadens access to learning and ensures inclusivity across different regions.

4_Online Examination and Certification
An innovative online examination scheme has been created to assess and validate LMD cyclists' green and safety skills. The system supports the certification of micro-skills, in line with the EU’s emphasis on increasing access to micro-credentials. This scheme offers a flexible pathway for cyclists to demonstrate their competencies and receive formal recognition for their expertise, contributing to the professionalization of the sector.

Updated Occupational Profiles and EU-Wide Qualification
One of the project’s landmark achievements is the update of occupational profiles and specifications, laying the foundation for an EU-wide vocational education and training (VET) qualification for LMD cyclists. This development standardizes training and qualifications across the EU, ensuring that LMD workers are recognized as skilled professionals in a rapidly evolving sector.

5_Outreach and Dissemination
To raise awareness of these achievements, the project organized four national information days in Germany, Croatia, Austria, and Greece, as well as one EU-wide dissemination event during VeloCity 2024 in Belgium. These events were promoted on the project’s website and across partner social media channels, including a highly engaged LinkedIn page with a strong following. The outreach effort reflects the project's success in creating significant visibility and impact across Europe.

2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000032990.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000032990.title: Developing innovative video competences for teachers of the Green Industry
2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000032990.summary:
<< Background >>

The VideoTeach project was launched to address skill gaps in video education within vocational education and training (VET). The partners, who had been working for years in both video education and the green industry, recognized a growing need to equip teachers with the skills to effectively integrate videos into digital teaching, a need intensified by the COVID-19 pandemic. The pandemic highlighted the rapid shift to digital learning and the increasing role of online video in education, revealing gaps in teachers' digital skills and resources. 

The need analyses conducted when preparing the application, showed that many teachers wanted/feel the urgency to improve their digital skills, particularly in creating digital content; this need was even stronger in rural areas. Teachers also required better support in terms of training, recognition of competencies, and clearer guidelines for integrating technology into their teaching.  

Apart from that, the project aimed to address the shortage of engaging educational materials in the emerging field of renewable energy. VideoTeach also responded to this gap by creating video content that simplifies energy-related complex topics which could be applied in VET schools. 

<< Objectives >>

The primary objective of the project was to develop educators' digital competences and promote video education as a key tool for teaching. This involved equipping educators with the skills and resources necessary to create high-quality video content for use in vocational settings particularly in the growing field of renewable energy technologies.

More specifically, VideoTeach aimed to: 
- Provide rural teachers with the digital skills and tools needed to create video-based educational materials, thereby bridging the digital divide and enabling these teachers to engage in modern teaching methods.
- Enhance education in the green industry by developing video-based methodologies and tools. This focus on renewable energy aimed to make complex topics more accessible and to increase both knowledge and awareness in this field.
- Support rural teachers' professional development by recognizing their digital learning outcomes, offering structured training, and creating a EU CV to enhance career growth and mobility.

Finally, VideoTeach aimed to foster international collaboration and promoted best practices in digital education. This ensured a lasting impact on educational practices and contributed to the sustainability of digital learning.

<< Implementation >>

Through the project, we have: 
- Implemented Coordination and Reporting activities and organized 5 transnational faces to face project meetings and online meetings almost on a monthly-based; produced the related documents and reports. 
-Implemented Monitoring and Quality Control measures and produced related documents/tools.

- PR1: Conducted a desk and field research and assembled a structured Competency Profile and an EU CV to recognize and promote video education competences in the green industry. 
- PR2: Developed a methodology with different steps to boost teachers’ path toward digitalization. Set up two online tools for self-assessment, recognition and training needs identification. Promoted the ex-ante online self-assessment tools among VET teachers.
- PR3: Created and delivered a comprehensive video training course to address identified skill gaps, enhancing teachers' proficiency in video-based education.
- PR4: Produced video resources on key green industry topics using innovative formats and incorporating real-world knowledge. This includes video-based storytelling and worker testimonies to align with current labor market demands.
- Set up the related platform to host all videos produced in the framework of PR3 and PR4.

- Organized and hosted a training activity that took place in October 2023, and which saw the attendance of 24 teachers/trainers.
- Organized and hosted 10 multiplier Events. 
- Designed a complete visual identity. 
- Issued 6 newsletters. 
- Created and animated 3 social media. 

<< Results >>

The VideoTeach project realized several concrete results (see full description https://videoteach.eu/results/) including: 

PR1: A Skill Needs Analysis Report, the Competency Profile of Video Teacher for Green Industry and the European Curriculum of Video Teachers for Green Industry.
PR2: A Methodology and Tools for competences assessment and recognition, including two online tools 1) for skill evaluation and suggestion of training contents and 2) for competences recognition.
PR3: The Video Teacher Self-Training Course for Green Industry; hosted both on https://videodatabase.eu/ and on https://www.youtube.com/@VIDEOTEACHProject and including 11 hours of lessons and quizzes. 
PR4: Video Teaching content for green industry; hosted both on https://videodatabase.eu/ and on https://www.youtube.com/@VIDEOTEACHProject and including 4 hours of contents developed by teachers who have been trained during the LTTA and who followed the Video Teacher Self-Training Course for Green Industry. 

- A multi-language instruction manual for facilitating the use of the video’s platform (extra result PR3/PR4)
- A training activity on digital education addressed at teachers. 
- 9 face to face and 1 online multiplier events.
- A complete visual identity including the Logo and templates; 6 newsletters; 3 social media (https://www.linkedin.com/company/videoteach-project/; https://www.facebook.com/videoteacheu;  https://www.youtube.com/@VIDEOTEACHProject). 

The VideoTeach project: 
- Improved digital skills among rural educators to support online, blended, and distance teaching methods.
- Increased capability of teachers, who took part in the activities and followed the online training to create video resources, integrating video education into traditional teaching practices.
- Enhanced attractiveness for green industry education thanks to the engaging teaching tools created.
- Improved the possibilities of teachers to address their skills gap regarding digital education.

2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000033042.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000033042.title: GENIE – Gamification & Education to Nurture Intrapreneurship at Enterprise
2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000033042.summary:
<< Background >>

A major obstacle undermining the innovation capacity of MSMEs (micro, small and medium-sized enterprises) in the EU is the inability to stimulate, mobilize and exploit the talent and innovation capacities available within the company. This is usually related to the lack of capacity and tools for MSME management and employees to overcome traditional mindsets and unleash the potential of "open innovation". MSMEs are still anchored in old-fashioned models where entrepreneurs/managers lead and employees/workers execute.

GENIE was developed as an innovative project that develops training and tools to promote intrapreneurship in MSMEs. Intrapreneurship has the potential to involve and engage employees and management in MSMEs to develop new ideas, business and management processes, products and services that support innovation, competitiveness and growth of MSMEs.
Intrapreneurship can be instrumental in shaping profound internal change to engage and empower people in the organization to be more resilient, sustainable and innovative.

<< Objectives >>

From the outset, GENIE had the very clear and concrete objective of "contributing to the competitiveness, growth and innovation of MSMEs through the development of innovative training tools, solutions and content". This overarching goal of the project was then broken down into specific objectives:
- Improve VET provision with innovative content for entrepreneurship development
- developing new solutions for vocational education and training, including a gamification approach
- Improve the involvement of MSME employees in the growth and competitive prospects of companies
- improving work-based learning opportunities for people already in employment and for new entrants to the labour market through jobs in MSMEs

GENIE should and has become a gamification and intrapreneurship inspired project for improved VET solutions to support the competitiveness of micro-enterprises. 
GENIE has a strong gamification component, but not in the "traditional" sense of gamification. The GENIE approach to gamification is based on the concept of an innovative human resource management model that encourages employees to come together and experiment with innovative teamwork techniques that culminate in intrapreneurship.

<< Implementation >>

Partners have initially set up the project's digital identity and an official 'online repository' for all project outputs, relevant news and updates.

The innovative GENIE Model of Intrapreneurship for MSMEs) was developed in PR2. The resulting product is not only innovative but more importantly it is multilingual, interactive and can be accessed in different formats which makes it reachable by wide segment of target population. 

Based on the above analysis in PR2, the partners developed in PR3 the training material and the GENIE board game (in addition to the application, an online version was also developed). The training content was organized in training modules, training fiches and case studies. A validation was carried out with over 170 participants. 

The "GENIE Adoption Suite" developed in PR4 includes a set of guidelines for users in micro-enterprises and the VET system to adopt, customize and implement the GENIE training and board game.
The VET Decalogue is the operational document intended as a "Call To Action" for stakeholders and representatives of the VET, micro-entrepreneurship and micro-enterprise development/promotion/support sectors and their employees.

<< Results >>

By realizing the GENIE activities it was possible to achieve an increased feeling of the own initiative and self-security  for the target groups through identification of (business) opportunities for value creation, brainstorming creative ideas, developing long-term visions, evaluating and justifying business ideas, identifying and evaluating the business context, promoting the entrepreneurial competence of employees, promoting motivation to get involved in the company and better manage risk and uncertainty.  

The partners developed the 4 PRs based on a "graduated methodological approach" that help to facilitate and support the acquisition of the above-mentioned skills by the target persons. 

PR1 is the GENIE OER platform for the visibility of the project and the use of best practices for "entrepreneurial" education at international level. PR2 is the innovative GENIE model for intrapreneurship in MSMEs. Based on the results of PR2, the partners have developed in PR3 11 training modules as well as the GENIE game and finally In PR4, we created the guidelines for the concrete implementation of the training courses (Adaptation Suite) as well as the concrete call to action for politics and business (Decalogue).
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000033276.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000033276.title: Adaptative learning paths for employabilty of people with different skills in the Stone Sector
2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000033276.summary:
<< Background >>

At least 16% of the EU working age population has a disability, many with the ability and the will to work.
People with disabilities constitute a significant potential for contribution to the economy and the labour market. The employment rate of disabled people is 50% as opposed to over 68% for non-disabled people, is already an indication that the potential of people with disabilities remains greatly underused. People with disabilities are almost twice as likely to be inactive compared to non-disabled people. Moreover, the likelihood of disability increases with age, and, in the light of the current EU demographic situation, the occurrence of disability is expected to increase. It is crucial to address the needs of people with disabilities in order to allow them to better integrate into the labour market and to participate in society. 
Employment is a determining factor for inclusion. The development of a Training path and Training Content on Therapies for Disabled based on Manufacturing Processes and Techniques employed in the Stone Sector involves having a tool for the recognition and validation of knowledge, skills and transversal capacities for promoting Labor Inclusion of disabled people in sectors as traditional as Stone is

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of this project were the following:
- To help the integration of people with disabilities into the world of work and to promote the development of skills and abilities through the stone sector.
- To raise awareness in education with learning phases in order to implement a series of steps, results that guarantee a good impact on the target group and a sustainable effect over time.
- Sensitise and create awareness in the companies of the sector about the recruitment of people with disabilities. 
- Providing employers with mechanisms to adapt workspaces to people with physical or motor disabilities.
- Encourage diversity in a sector as traditional as the stone sector, thus facilitating the promotion and awareness of equality at all levels.
- Provide support tools for the development of actions that enable the inclusion of people in vulnerable situations in the labour market, adapted to the digital transformation and focused on distance learning.
- Provide information, increase the strengths in labour inclusion and redefine the weaknesses.
- To provide digital training adapted to the current situation so that no person is left behind and to face the challenges that conventional training currently presents.

<< Implementation >>

During the development of the InclusiveStone project, the main activities implemented were:
- Handbook for an educational approach for people with different skills focused on transversal capacities in stone sector.
- Design and Organization of Training Paths and Development of a Course Curriculum.
- Implementation of 3 training pilot courses.
- Production of virtual reality (VR) immersive Adaptative Training Path.
- Project management activities (e.g. monitoring, controlling and managing the project, quality assurance, etc.)
- Dissemination activities (i.e. organization of 3 multiplier events, website development, posts in project’s social media and in partners’ websites, articles on e-journals, presentations on conferences, cross-links with other projects, etc.)

<< Results >>

R1 - Educational approach for people with different skills focused on transversal capacities in stone sector.
1-A1 Roadmap of the Methodology.
1-A2 Awareness of needs surveys to identify specific learning difficulties.
1-A3 Report of data analysis and conclusions.
1-A4 Handbook for an educational approach for people with different skills focused on transversal capacities in stone sector.
1-A5 Report on the results of First International Seminar in Split (Croatia)

R2 - Complete Training Path Guide for teaching stone sector's professions for people with different skills.
2-A1 Definition of Training Units and Learning Outcomes.
2-A2 Design and Organization of Training Paths.
2-A3 InclusiveSTONE Course Curriculum.
2-A4 Report on the results of Workshop in Cehegín (Spain).

R3 - VR-Adaptative Training Content and Evaluation.
3-A1 Implementation plan.
3-A2 Training materials.
3-A3 Defining and structuring the key VR-scenarios.
3-A4 Production of virtual reality (VR) immersive Adaptative Training Path.
3-A5 Define a Recognition and Validation tool for the assessment of all skills and transversal competences.
3-A6 Recognition and Validation of Knowledge, Skills and Competences.
3-A7 Implementation of the pilot.

More information: https://inclusivestone.eu/
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000034201.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000034201.title: VOIS - Virtual Open Innovation Environment for SMEs
2021-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000034201.summary:
<< Background >>

The partners applied for this project to address the critical need for local SMEs, particularly in the agri-food and bioeconomy sectors, to improve their abilities to modernise and innovate collaboratively in response to changing market conditions, digitalization, automation and emergence of IoT. These SMEs, crucial to regional economic growth, often lack the ability to independently reinvent their value propositions, leaving them vulnerable to market shifts. While open innovation (OI) is widely promoted, SMEs struggle with accessing the necessary skills and competencies typically found in larger firms and research centres. Recognising OI as key approach for SME innovation despite their limited resources, VOIS offers solutions to develop SME managers' professional competencies for effective OI engagement. It addresses the need to support the knowledge-based engagement of traditional SMEs in OI and collaboration for modernising and innovating the agri-food industry, while also enabling participating organisations to build the cross-disciplinary expertise necessary to support these businesses, foster collaboration, and develop relevant skills within SMEs and their supporting organisations.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the VOIS project, the partnership aimed to address the lack of access of local no/low-tech SMEs to OI competencies that are crucial for their competitiveness and ability to engage in meaningful innovation. By developing the Virtual Open Innovation Environment for SMEs the project contributes to increasing access to practical knowledge about the potential OI offers for more resilience, growth and involvement of SME in the agri-food and bio-economy sector. The project results offer SME managers and supporting organisations access to capacitating tools to develop their OI competency and to facilitate effective engagement in OI activities. 
Direct purpose of the project is the creation of a virtual environment integrating access to cross-disciplinary competences required for successful OI within 3 dimensions: 
1/ development of managers OI competencies to set OI at organisational level, 
2/ development of individual OI competencies of managers, 
3/ repository of resources available for SMEs support to OI processes. 
The partnership focused on the development of the direct result as well as on increasing internal competences of staff and organisations to better support knowledge-based SME engagement in OI.

<< Implementation >>

All planned activities were implemented, including management, dissemination, evaluation, and results development. 
In management, partners signed the bilateral agreements. The AdminProject space was created. A total of 4 physical meetings and approximately 8 online meetings were convened, including the KOM which was held online due to pandemic restrictions. All meetings supported and addressed consortium-wide and bilateral needs. 
Dissemination included the creation of (visual) materials such as logo, website, social media, leaflets, newsletters, press release, poster as well as a dissemination and exploitation plan.
Evaluation activities involved formulating a Quality and Evaluation Report, including the Interim Evaluation, Final Evaluation, TPM evaluations, External Advisory Board Consultations, Partners’ Evaluation Interviews. 
Regarding Project Results, the VOIS project produced as by application 1 key integrated tangible result – Virtual Open Innovation Environment, consisting of 3 areas, with 7 modules (instead of 6 as by application) for Area 1, 6 modules for Area 2, 1 repository with collection of 21 support tools in a form of either existing resources or real-life examples in Area 3. The activities for this project result included developing a methodology, research, content writing, graphical layout, translations, piloting, and modifications, as well as stakeholder consultations, platform development.
That resulted in an integrated open innovation (OI) environment with areas for i/ development of managers OI competencies to set OI at organisational level, ii/ development of individual OI competencies of managers, iii/ access point to open innovation resources for support of OI processes. Considering specific needs of SMEs managers as a target group struggling with significant resource limitations, including time limitations, the OI environment offers highly flexible practical training based on training within ICT environment with interactive and asynchronous professional training methodology.
To support dissemination and improvements during project implementation, key activities involved engaging stakeholders through personal contact, a webpage, newsletters, and social media. This included 7 multiplier events in 6 countries, internal and external piloting across 7 partner ecosystems, and promotional events during the initial piloting phase.

<< Results >>

The Virtual Open Innovation Environment for SMEs in a form of an online environment is the main tangible result. It consists of 3 elements:
Area 1 – Organisational Area: 7 modules as practical tutorial regarding open innovation strategies/methodologies for SMEs for capacitating participants to design them and implement them in their organisations:
-	Module 1 - The Open Innovation principle and Open Innovation process for agro-industry and bioeconomy,
-	Module 2 - Main pillars of open innovation strategy
-	Module 3 - Ensuring alignment between the OI strategy and the company objectives
-	Module 4 - How to build mindset toward open innovation in your SME.
-	Module 5 - Building win-win scenarios for open innovation projects
-	Module 6 - Adjusting your organisation to the requirements of Open Innovation
-	Module 7 - Building your Open Innovation ecosystem
During the research phase for developing the Area 1 methodology, it became clear that 7 thematic lines, rather than the 6 originally planned, were crucial for effectively equipping SMEs to handle OI challenges. As a result, 7 modules were developed instead of the initially planned 6.
Area 2 – Individual Development Area: 6 modules focused on development of OI Competencies of Managers as individual leaders focus on competencies required for their ability to manage activities in the scope of open innovation. Following the CMOI model:
-	 1. Building ability to work with people from different communities, disciplines and functions.
-	2. Managing collaborative innovation.
-	3. Knowledge management in-house and across organisations.
-	4. Communication and networking.
-	5. Cultural awareness.
-	6. Adaptability and flexibility.
Area 3 – Open Innovation repository – a resource base gathering already available tools and support measures for SMEs open innovation in the form of existing knowledge resources, as well as cases of application with lessons learned from SME perspective.
Also, other tangible materials were developed: dissemination materials (website, leaflets, newsletters, articles, press releases, presentations) and working materials including various plans, agendas, reports.
topics: Support for European and regional innovation and smart specialisation strategies

2021-1-DK01-KA220-VET-000025080.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-DK01-KA220-VET-000025080.title: Wellness In Digital Education
2021-1-DK01-KA220-VET-000025080.summary:
<< Background >>

The COVID-19 pandemic created the largest disruption of education systems in history, affecting nearly 1.6 billion learners in more than 19 countries on all continents. Education providers struggled to integrate Digital Learning into their curricula, i.e., how to reorganize their offer and delivery systems. The concerns were focused on the technical requirements of digital learning,  how to exploit the opportunities offered by these systems, how to integrate them into the curricular activity (blended learning), and what kind of skills and competencies teachers and learners should have, to optimize the use of these new tools. The lockdowns in 2020 -21 made it evident that digital learning is changing our approaches and ways of organizing interaction and expression. It also demonstrated that the overload from prolonged internet use was extremely tiring, physically and psychologically. Digital learning implies the need to cope and adopt a so-called “digital mindset”, and the wellness of each involved person (Trainer/teacher, learner). The WIDE project addressed the need for a holistic approach to digital learning: from curriculum design to the methodologies employed that ensure the well-being of both teachers/trainers and learners.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of WIDE were:
-	To address the personal and professional well-being of the educational process related to online/blended training which had been put at stake during endless hours of digital learning; 
-       To develop a digital platform and a holistic methodology for online learning;
-       To improve the competencies of teachers/trainers in the holistic approach to digital education,;
-	To contribute to the reinforcement of inclusiveness of education systems in the digital era;
-	To develop innovation for education policies;
-	To foster participatory and multi-stakeholder approaches to innovation in education.: and 
-	To integrate the dimension of well-being as a crucial one, evaluating the quality and the responsiveness of education systems, and the resilience of learners and teachers/trainers.

<< Implementation >>

•	4 Transnational project meetings and 1 online kick-off meeting. 
•	Monthly and ad hoc Zoom meetings: For providing status of activities, monitoring and quality control 
•	1 Teacher Training: A WIDE Open teacher training session held in Modena, Italy where all partners invited teachers to participate in a 3-day course.
•	6 Local Multiplier Events: Each project partner, except Italy who hosted the final conference, hosted a local multiplier event for local stakeholders 
         where the project and the concrete results were presented. 
•	Final Conference: Consorzio degli Istituti Professionali hosted a final conference for teachers and project partners. The project and the concrete results were presented, and the participants also had the opportunity to debate and discuss the outcome and the future of the project with the partners.
 •  Local networking with VET schools, teachers  and professionals
 • Dissemination: organizations' website & social media, newsletters, and the project's FB page: https://www.facebook.com/projectwide
-  PR1 Wellbeing in online/blended education analysis: survey, data collection & analysis, desktop research, bilateral meetings
-PR2  WIDE Methodological Framework - Developing methods, aligning theoretical framework with practice and the “Lov-e & Car-e-osity model” that was successfully implemented in Canada in 2020,  pilot testing of the methodology among a total of 1,134 students 
-PR3 Guidelines for inclusive digital education: development of the guidelines, discussion among partners, desk research on good practice and on case studies
-PR4 - E-learning path: development of the website and learning platform; defining the structure of the learning platform; development of the e-learning course 
-PR5 - Policy recommendation:  analyses of feedback fromPR2, 3 and 4. Discussion among partners; desk research on the current policies 

<< Results >>

The project has produced the following: 
N.B: Please see attached reports.
PR1: Wellbeing in online/blended education analysis report;
PR2: The WIDE methodological framework, 
PR3: Guidelines for integrating well-being into inclusive online education
PR4: WIDE e-learning path and E-earning platform in in EN, DK, IT, CR, FR, ES, GR  (https://academyofentrepreneurship.org/course/wellness-in-digital-education-en)
PR5: Policy recommendation for healthy online education. 
A  Project Management Handbook
A Quality Assurance Plan & Reports: Project Outputs, Piloting of Activities, Partner Meetings & Management
A Dissemination and Exploitation Plan
Teacher training event (C1) in Modena, Italy
6 Multiplier events 
1 Final Conference in Genova, Italy
 Communication and Dissemination Strategy along with Dissemination posts on social media
A project website (https://www.wide-project.eu/)
An Interim Report
A survey and Report aiming at collecting information regarding perceptions of students/trainees, teachers/trainers, and parents related to long-term exposure to distance learning and 

The WIDE Project has reached a total of 2,700 composed mainly of teachers, students, local schools and VET schools, parents, and other stakeholders. These target groups were reached through the project's various activities such as the international training event, online teacher training courses, piloting among students, surveys, and general networking activities of partners. 

Its online social engagement via the WIDE FB account, partners' own FB account other stakeholder's accounts, Linked-in, Tweeter (X), Instagram reached approx. 43.192 people (40,460 people on FB through 193 posts; 1074 on Linked-in through 22 posts: 1521 on Tweeter (X) though 16 posts; and 137 on Instagram through 14 posts).  

A bonus result of the project is that WIDE was able to issue European E-badges for teachers who were able to complete the course or modules of the WIDE training course for teachers. The project partners deemed that it would be advantageous to teachers to have the European E-badges as proof that they have undergone the course on well-being in digital learning. T-HAP, the partner from Cyprus, has categorized the skills and competencies
acquired through the WIDE training path using the ESCO categorization (https://esco.ec.europa.eu) to identify the capacities to be certified. Following, e-badges have been issued to all those who have completed the path and addressed the assessment tool of WIDE.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-DK01-KA220-VET-000033173.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-DK01-KA220-VET-000033173.title: Future agriculture requires motivation, education and retainment
2021-1-DK01-KA220-VET-000033173.summary:
<< Background >>

The aim of FARMER is to support the agricultural sector in overcoming the challenges regarding recruitment and the integration of sustainability into vocational education. As the agricultural industry is challenged with climate change, environmental issues, and rapid technological advancements, it is essential that students are equipped with the right skills to thrive in the sector. FARMER addresses these challenges, through the development of educators’ ability to teach cross-cutting skills within the context of sustainability. The needs we have addressed in this project focus on bridging the gap between the growing demand for skilled agricultural workers and the need for innovative teaching methods that engage students with sustainable practices. We worked on recruiting practices to enhance the attractiveness of vocational education in agriculture by focusing on the development of green curricula that align with both the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the needs of the agricultural industry. By improving the image of agricultural education and fostering an entrepreneurial mindset in students, we aim to support their career choices and encourage a sense of pride in pursuing a sustainable and impactful vocation.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the FARMER project, we aimed to equip educators with modern teaching methods and tools to better recruit, motivate, and retain students in agricultural education. Our goal was to strengthen vocational training by promoting hands-on, interdisciplinary teaching approaches that integrate sustainability, environmental awareness, and entrepreneurial learning. Through transnational cooperation and the exchange of best practices, we sought to enhance educators' ability to address climate challenges and improve the perception of agricultural careers. Ultimately, the project strives to create a lasting impact by fostering innovation in education and supporting the future workforce in the agricultural sector.

<< Implementation >>

In the project we held 5 learning teahcing and training activities in the project.
C1: Competency - mapping of the existing skills in the agricultural education today with the aim of identifying current skills needs/gaps.
C2: Setting up personal educational skills set to match the future needs.
C3: Identification of the future educational skills need with a specific focus on the challenges by the climate challenge.
C4: Setting up / defining new framework for agricultural learning content.
C5: Policy recommendation.
We held 6 TPM meetings, 3 physical meetings and 3 online.

<< Results >>

Analysis of Current Competences and Labor Market Indicators. 
Identifying Future Competences for Farmers.
An Educational and Didactic Manual.
A set of policy recommendations to support recruitment into Agro VET and enhance trainer upskilling.
Initiated Erasmus+ mobilities with students between the partners in the project.

2021-1-EL01-KA220-VET-000033247.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-EL01-KA220-VET-000033247.title: Advancing MuNicipal Circlular Economy
2021-1-EL01-KA220-VET-000033247.summary:
<< Background >>

In 2020, the EU generated nearly 59 million tonnes of food waste (FW), valued at €132 billion. Of this total, households contributed around 31 million tonnes of FW (53% of the total), while restaurants and food services accounted for approximately 5 million tonnes. The EU and its Member States are committed to meeting Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 12.3, adopted in September 2015, which targets to halve per capita food waste at the retail and consumer level by 2030, and reduce food losses along the food production and supply chains. To achieve this target, all key players from public and private sectors must work together to better identify, measure, understand and find viable solutions.
The ADVANCE project addressed the following needs:
- Identification of benefits, barriers and best practices in FW management for municipalities and HORECA SMEs.
- Improvement of knowledge and skills of municipal and hospitality sectors in FW management.
- Fostering of Circular Economy through better FW management practices. 
- Contribution to environmental sustainability, food security and hunger relief, cost reduction, compliance with regulations and community engagement. 
- Promotion of new technologies and solutions in FW reduction. 

<< Objectives >>

The ADVANCE project had the following objectives:
- To assess the current situation regarding food waste (FW) generation and management practices in selected municipalities and SMEs in the HORECA sector
- To develop a concrete set of Circularity Benchmarking Indicators that will be used to describe both the current status and the future monitoring of FW management in municipalities and HORECA SMEs
- To assess the gap between the baseline assessment and the requirements posed by EU and national regulations, setting realistic targets 
- To identify best practices in FW management 
- To develop two Gap Analysis tools for municipalities and HORECA SMEs aiming to assess (i) the knowledge of current and future personnel and (ii) the performance of the targeted entities
- To develop two Roadmaps (for municipalities and HORECA SMEs) and a step-by-step Action Plan regarding FW measurement, management and monitoring
- To create training/educational materials addressed to personnel of municipalities and HORECA SMEs 
- To develop an online platform which will include & host all the above, as well as further information (e.g. FW calculators).

<< Implementation >>

The main activities implemented were the following:

A. Prior to submission the consortium:
- was formulated
- conducted research to define the problem;
- identified and analysed the needs
- conducted an overall project planning and submitted the application form.

B. When the project was contracted and launched:
- NTUA developed a Project Management Plan (PMP) as the Coordinator, which set the main management tools and procedures;
- SIGMA developed a Risk Management Plan (as part of the PMP), which served as a risk management tool stipulating the main risks to the project activities, based on internal and external context;
- NTUA developed the Project Timeline (as part of PMP), which served as a main time management tool, containing the schedule of activities, task assignments and responsibilities and relevant deadlines;
- NTUA established a financial reporting mechanism with 6-month progress reports, which was mandatory for the partners;
- Horeca Partners, City of Novi Sad and City of Zadar developed the Sharing, Promotion & Use (SPU) Plan, which served as the main guideline for effective communication & dissemination with project target groups and stakeholders;
- SIGMA and D-WASTE developed the Quality Assurance Strategy (QAS), which served as a main quality assurance tool;
- the consortium as a whole planed thoroughly the development of Project Results (PR) including methodologies, templates and guidelines for execution of activities related to the respective PR;
- each PR was assigned to a PR Leader and each Task to a Task Leader who were responsible for the implementation and the corrective actions (refinements) based on the conclusions from performed external and internal evaluations;
- dissemination activities (i.e. organisation of multiplier events and stakeholder meetings, website development, posts in project’s FB and LinkedIn pages, posts on project partners’ websites, articles on e-journals, cross-links with other projects, etc.);
- NTUA monitored and measured the processes according to the plan, policies, objectives and requirements, Internal evaluation (peer reviews by all partners; assessment by QAS leader) & External evaluation (pilot tests with target groups).

C. Project Closure – The consortium implement the following activities:
- carrying out the last project meeting;
- planning of resources and actions to ensure sustainability of the project results after its end;
- preparation of final report on project implementation;
- final reporting, and guaranteeing post project developments and actions.

<< Results >>

ADVANCE produced the following concrete outputs and results:
- Baseline assessment (PR1) of the current waste food waste management practices in Municipalities and HORECA SMEs, which also included benchmarking to existing best practices in EU. Within PR1 primary questionnaire surveys were conducted to selected households, HORECA businesses and municipalities and FW Benchmarking indicators were developed for municipalities and HORECA SMEs. 
- Gap Analysis methodology and tools (PR2) between current and required, according to the EU targets, FW management practices relevant to food waste. The main outcome of the PR2 was an online tool hosted in ADVANCE Platform (PR5), which serves as a mechanism for target groups to assess their overall competences, capability and skills on Circular Economy and FW Management processes. To better serve its purposes, two separate tools were developed, one for HORECA SMEs and one for Municipalities. Each of these tools is comprised of two different sub-tools for high-level personnel (focused on the assessment of the organisation in relation to FW production and management) and existing/future employees (focused on knowledge assessment). 
- Development of ADVANCE Roadmap (PR3) to achieve the food waste targets set by the EU and the SDGs and catalyse synergies between municipalities and HORECA SMEs. More specifically, two different Roadmaps were developed (one for municipalities and one for the HORECA SMEs) that share common characteristics (e.g., they address actions required considering the EU and national strategies, focus on food waste prevention, develop a step-by-step action plan, etc.). The Roadmaps were established on the outcomes of PR1 and PR2 and used Circularity Gap Indicators (based on the benchmarking indicators and the gap analysis assessment) as its main tool to guide the required steps. A special part of the Roadmaps was devoted to demonstrate best practices and how Industry 4.0 can help municipalities and HORECA SMEs to achieve better food waste management and advance food waste prevention. 
- The ADVANCE Course (PR4) prepared a curriculum and developed training material broken down into certain learning modules and teaching units, covering areas of the whole spectrum of FW generation and management. The training course utilises a variety of proven online learning techniques (e.g., self-assessment questions, multiple types of sources for further information, etc) and is adapted to the needs of the predefined target groups to ensure maximum understanding, comprehension, and retention of the information presented.  The online training course is available online via the ADVANCE Platform and is accompanied by a training handbook.
- The ADVANCE Online Platform (PR5), which includes and hosts the above-mentioned tools and materials. Moreover, the platform aims to establish an on-line community around the issue of food waste generation and management and therefore includes related projects, videos and food waste calculator covering different needs.

2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000028196.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000028196.title: Using agile learning platforms to infuse circular economy knowledge with entrepreneurial spirit
2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000028196.summary:
<< Background >>

The Covid-19 pandemic significantly impacted education in all Member States, causing school closures and service suspensions that hindered efforts to up-skill and re-skill the labor force. The CIRCULO Train-the-Trainer programme aimed to address these challenges by enhancing the subject knowledge of VET professionals, fostering an entrepreneurial spirit among learners, and promoting understanding of circular economy principles. It focused on refining pedagogy and digital skills for high-quality online education, supporting sustainable development, and enhancing coaching and mentoring abilities. Led by GEINNOVA, the project sought funding to implement a transnational approach, involving VET teacher/trainers from multiple countries to share best practices and address labor market needs and twin transitions. This collaborative effort was supported by Erasmus+ funding.

<< Objectives >>

CIRCULO aimed to introduce a new hybrid learning approach that will enhance the entrepreneurial, digital, and green skills of VET educators in Spain, Ireland, Germany, Portugal, Cyprus, France, Belgium and Croatia. In doing so, CIRCULO sought to be a leading force in shaping a new learning approach that places digitalization at the core of VET professionals' roles.
The main objectives of CIRCULO were to: 
Create a comprehensive set of learning resources designed to enable VET students to acquire the skills necessary for the green and circular economy.
Promote the entrepreneurial mindset among young people by providing a series of interactive learning resources aligned with the Ideas & Opportunities framework of EntreComp.
Develop a new Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Train-the-Trainer (TTT) course for VET teachers and trainers, aimed at enhancing their skills to digitize learning offerings and methods. The course also included guidance and coaching measures to ensure effective implementation. 
Set up an online facilitated network across Europe for VET stakeholders, fostering the exchange of best practices, building professional relationships, and collaborating to devise solutions to current labor market challenges. 

<< Implementation >>

The innovation and a constant strive to expand entrepreneurial domain, in terms of knowledge, can significantly change and boost the EU economy, especially when taking into account the opportunities that exist as a result of the European Green Deal and the dual economic transition that is underway. 
The activities implemented by CIRCULO are:
A Local Stakeholder Forum was established to ensure that their views form an integral part of the project's work plan and development approach, and that key local stakeholders and associated partners are networked transnationally through the LTTAs and eNetwork, incorporating a European dimension to the results of the CIRCULO project.
A new train-the-trainer program for VET professionals was designed and implemented and piloted in France and Croatia. 15 VET teachers from 8 EU countries (Spain, Ireland, Germany, Portugal, Cyprus, France, Belgium and Croatia)  attended to validate training materials, share best practices and participate in activities to explore innovations in VET practices.
Organized local continuing professional development training activities, using a cascade model, involving VET professionals at the local level to deliver the CIRCULO Train-the-Trainer (TTT) program in a blended learning format.
The CIRCULO e-learning platform was designed and implemented with an integrated online electronic network, ensuring active management, facilitation and promotion throughout the second year of the project.
Each partner was actively promoting and sustaining the project throughout its duration, with a strong focus on establishing and managing Local Stakeholder Forums and fostering a vibrant eNetwork.
GEINNOVA organized a Transnational Conference in Spain, and successfully drew an international audience of 100 stakeholders.This conference was divided into four events, each tailored to different target groups.
CIRCULO’s Multiplier events were held in Ireland, Germany, Portugal, Cyprus, France, Belgium and Croatia. These ME focused on presenting the results and outcomes of the project, to VET professionals and trainers, senior managers and policy makers. 

<< Results >>

CIRCULO project put into life several project objectives. Besides creating a: Train-the-Trainer Programme for VET professionals, eLearning Platform and eNetwork; during the CIRCULO projects’ lifetime additional KPIs were achieved: 
There were 111 VET tutors who completed the TTT programme and were using the newly-created methods and tools during their everyday practice. 
12 CIRCULO learning sources are created to enhance the development of entrepreneurial mindset and circular economy principles.
174 main stakeholders and organizations attending the ME events in all of the partner’s countries. 
100 participants attended the Final Conference in Spain, including VET managers, organizations, academics, etc. In this event, CIRCULO project and all its results were presented. This conference was divided into four events, each tailored to different target groups.

2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000033135.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000033135.title: Development of an easy-to-read gardening book for professionals training people with intellectual disabilities
2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000033135.summary:
<< Background >>

The EU promotes the active inclusion and full participation of people with disabilities in society, in line with the EU approach to disability human rights, which means that disability is a rights issue and not a matter of discretion. This approach is also at the core of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD).
Easy Gardening. Erasmus + project (February 2022-February 2024) aimed to contribute to the social participation of people with disabilities by improving their vocational skills for employment.
“Vocational training fosters innovation, creativity and self-confidence.”
The current labor market means that many of our students with disabilities are unable to access employment.
The supply of vocational training for people with disabilities is limited. Adapted materials usually have to be developed by the teachers themselves, since they are not already designed. 
In addition, the subject matter was selected because it is one of the professions in which PWiD are most likely to find employment.

<< Objectives >>

This project, with partners from Croatia, Denmark, Greece, Portugal and Spain, sought to improve the training of trainers working with people with disabilities in the field of gardening and agriculture, providing them with adapted resources, so that such training has an impact on the employability of people with disabilities.
To this end, as operational results, it was intended to provide materials, tools and resources to students with intellectual disabilities, as well as to teachers, training staff, mentors, trainers, leaders of VET centers, to facilitate the incorporation of people with intellectual disabilities in training actions for employment.

<< Implementation >>

To this end, within the framework of the project, the following have been developed:
- the creation of a gardening/agriculture training manual in accessible format;
- the creation of a training manual for trainers in gardening, inspired by accessible practices and inclusive practices;
- the preparation, implementation and evaluation of a training course for trainers in gardening in accordance with the Universal Design for Learning;
- the provision of a platform for the training of trainers;
- the creating of a game to explore the fundamental principles and practices of sustainable gardening and agriculture.

<< Results >>

1: Organic Gardening Book (easy-reading) and Training Guide. 
The objective of creating this manual was to facilitate access to professional training for people with disabilities.  The trainers will train people with disabilities to follow the instructions in the book by themselves.
A training guide for trainers has also been developed to facilitate the use of the manual.
2: Capacity building course in Organic Gardening for professionals.
A professional capacity building course has been designed for professionals who train students with disabilities, with the aim of improving their specific knowledge of organic gardening.
3. Estrategic Game: The Easy Gardening Game

The materials have been developed in English, and have been translated into Greek, Danish, Croatian, Portuguese, Spanish and Galician. The materials have been published under open licenses and can be downloaded at: https://www.easygardening.eu and in and in the Erasmus+ results platform.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000034654.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000034654.title: Digital Mentoring and Traineeship
2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000034654.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated in response to the necessity of providing various resources and tools to effectively address training, socioeconomic entrepreneurship, and equal opportunities in rural contexts, along with their connection to Vocational Training.

In this regard, the principal resources generated by the project include the DIGITRAIN methodology (PR1), training materials tailored for students, teachers, institutions, and companies (PR2 and PR3), and the DIGITRAIN Portal (PR4).

Consequently, it has been demonstrated that the digital mentoring devised and implemented in this project serves as an innovative model for training and fostering talent in rural vocational training centers. Through digital metrics, educational institutions (comprising both teachers and students) and companies (comprising managers and mentors) can transcend geographical barriers and establish connections.
In summary, the DIGITRAIN Project and its outcomes have effectively addressed two primary objectives: promoting equal opportunities in rural areas of Europe (notably characterized by the rural nature of the partners and countries within the consortium) and fostering socio-labor integration.

<< Objectives >>

The project directly addresses two challenges of the European Union. Firstly, it tackles the imperative need for the development of small rural communities, which are often sparsely populated and geographically distant from urban centers, lacking easy access to essential resources. Secondly, it aims to counteract rural exodus by implementing measures to stabilize rural populations and enhance the socioeconomic and cultural conditions of rural environments. Consequently, the objectives set forth at the outset of the project align closely with those successfully achieved:
• Enhancing the quality and relevance of training activities within educational centers, thereby bolstering their capacity for transnational operations and fostering the internationalization of their endeavors.
• Devising, implementing, and evaluating a digital mentoring process tailored for Vocational Education and Training (VET) students residing in rural areas of Europe. This process not only encourages active participation but also facilitates the development of fundamental skills.
• Facilitating greater collaboration between VET educational institutions situated in rural locales and the business sector, thereby fostering collaborative initiatives that promote.

<< Implementation >>

The project has executed a comprehensive array of activities, encompassing diverse initiatives, which have yielded the four anticipated outcomes:
*PR1 is titled "Digital practices. Development of methodologies"* This result has had two notable products:
- Digitrain Mentorship Process.
- Digitrain Process Forms / Documents.
*PR2 is titled "Development of educational content"* This result has had two notable products:
- Educational Material.
- Competence Matrix.
*PR3 is titled "Development of Online Guides and Resources"* This result has had four notable products that have a modular structure with activities, online resources, joint work proposal, examples, etc.:- GUIDES FOR VET STUDENTS; FOR MENTORS; FOR VET CENTERS and FOR COMPANIES
*** PR4 is titled "Online digital portal for mentoring, internships and talent search" * (https://digitrain-portal.com/home)
All the PR and associated resources are available in the virtual Project Management Quality Plan (PMQP) that can be consulted at this link (https://acortar.link/c6oZGw) and are also available in open access at these links :
- project website: https://websites22.my.canva.site/digitrainproject#project-results
- DIGITRAIN portal: https://digitrain-portal.com/onlineResources/resource

<< Results >>

Since its inception, the project had meticulously outlined the achievement of four specific results, all of which have been successfully accomplished with a high degree of quality, utility, flexibility, diversity, and impact. These results are:
- PR1 is titled "Digital practices. Development of methodologies"
- PR2 is titled "Development of educational content"
- PR3 is titled "Development of online guides and resources"
- PR4 is titled "Online digital portal for mentoring, internships and talent search"
All resources generated in the different PR are under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license.
All the PR and associated resources are available in the virtual Project Management Quality Plan (PMQP) that can be consulted at this link (https://acortar.link/c6oZGw) and are also available in open access at these links :
- project website: https://websites22.my.canva.site/digitrainproject#project-results
- DIGITRAIN portal: https://digitrain-portal.com/onlineResources/resources
