2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000034851.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000034851.title: NUEVOS MODELOS DE NEGOCIO DE ECONOMÍA CIRCULAR PARA LA ACTIVACIÓN DEL RURAL EUROPEO
2021-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000034851.summary:
<< Background >>

El socio líder del proyecto es el ayuntamiento de Outes, un municipio rural de Galicia, completamente comprometido con la generación de valor en los sectores primarios y la promoción de servicios locales de calidad para afianzar a la población y evitar la migración a las ciudades.
Las necesidades compartidas con el resto de socios, y abordadas en el proyecto fueron:
- El envejecimiento de la población, debido al aumento significativo en la esperanza de vida y las tasas de natalidad más bajas.
- Abandono del medio rural, una tendencia conocida como "Europa vaciada", donde la población se desplaza del campo a la ciudad. España, junto con Países Bajos y Bélgica, tenía una de las menores poblaciones residentes en áreas rurales dentro de la Unión Europea.
- Falta de una red inteligente de apoyo al emprendimiento, tanto a nivel local como europeo, así como la carencia de instrumentos y metodologías adaptadas para el asesoramiento especializado en el ámbito rural.
- Falta de conocimiento sobre las oportunidades que ofrece la Economía Circular (EC).
Se buscaba maximizar el potencial de las oportunidades emergentes de resiliencia al cambio climático, como la Economía Circular, para alcanzar los ODS

<< Objectives >>

Esperábamos transferir conocimientos sobre EC y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de negocio basados en esta, a través del apoyo inteligente de los profesionales del área de desarrollo rural a los futuros emprendedores del rural europeo.
Objetivos específicos:
O1: Análisis de los factores de éxito que determinan la viabilidad de los modelos de negocio rurales de Economía Circular
O2: Fomentar la cooperación estratégica a nivel europeo a través de la creación de una red transnacional para la activación de los entornos rurales de la UE mediante la EC
O3: Crear un marco favorable para la transferencia de conocimiento de Economía Circular entre la comunidad y los centros universitarios y tecnológicos de la UE
O4: Favorecer la creación de mecanismos e instrumentos de apoyo y formación inteligentes que fomenten la innovación aplicada de cara al desarrollo empresarial en los entornos rurales europeos
O5: Dotar de nuevos conocimientos, capacidades y habilidades basadas en la EC, a los agentes de apoyo empresarial en el rural europeo
O6: Sensibilizar a la comunidad educativa de los centros de FP europeos acerca del enfoque de la EC y su potencial para las zonas rurales

<< Implementation >>

Se han organizado actividades en varios Grupos de Tareas para facilitar la ejecución del proyecto, asignando la coordinación a diferentes socios para garantizar un reparto equitativo:
GT1: Coordinación y Gestión, liderado por OUTES, se encargó de la gestión financiera y administrativa, la Las actividades se coordinaron entre los grupos de trabajo para ejecutar el proyecto, garantizando una distribución equitativa.
El WP1, dirigido por OUTES, gestionó las finanzas, organizó las reuniones y evaluó las actividades del 01.11.2021 al 28.02.2024 (con una prórroga de 4 meses aprobada el 5/04/23). WP2, dirigido por LAG ZS, se encargó de la comunicación, incluyendo eventos, desarrollo de la página web y diseño de la identidad. 
WP3, liderado por HWWI, asesoró sobre modelos de negocio rural sostenible del 01.11.2021 al 31.10.2023. 
WP4, dirigido por WIN, desarrolló competencias, cursos en línea y programas piloto del 01.07.2022 al 30.01.2024. 
WP5, liderado por CAPANNORI, construyó una red, diseñó Circular.Rur Lab, e impartió formación del 01.09.2022 al 28.02.2024.



<< Results >>

Los resultados obtenidos durante el ciclo de vida del proyecto generaron una batería de herramientas inteligentes de apoyo al emprendimiento circular.
Estas herramientas están a disposición del público en la página web del proyecto https://circularur.eu/, por lo que pueden ser utilizadas por profesionales del desarrollo rural y otros agentes para acompañar la transformación y el desarrollo de las empresas rurales ante los retos de la despoblación rural, la falta de relevo generacional y el cambio climático.
En relación con los Grupos de Trabajo específicos, se obtuvieron los siguientes resultados:
IO 1: Manual «Smart Guidance on Circular Economy Business Models for Rural Development» con metodología para el uso de herramientas y recursos.
IO2 Caja de herramientas para la especialización inteligente en nuevas oportunidades de negocio sostenible en el medio rural.
IO3 MOOC para el asesoramiento inteligente en nuevos modelos de negocio circulares.
IO4 Plataforma interactiva para la formación y asesoramiento inteligente de emprendedores rurales en economía circular.

2021-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000025093.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000025093.title: Nudge My Tour
2021-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000025093.summary:
<< Background >>

In the current context of climate crisis, and socio-economic instability, tourism faces unprecedented challenges. A paradigm shift is needed to re-think the way tourism activities are planned and managed, and to re-balance priorities when it comes to tourism development.
Within this context, human behaviour plays a crucial role. People are more aware of the need to travel more sustainably, however they find it hard to change their actual behaviour. 
Behavioural science can play a crucial role in helping to make the sustainable travel options the easiest and seamless, using insights about human behaviour, and to design more sustainable tourism activities and policies.
Tourism actors are aware of the need to address human behaviour, but they do not have the necessary knowledge to implement behavioural interventions. 
Behavioural science is starting to be applied to many issues related to sustainability, but its application in the tourism sector was still relatively unexplored.
We therefore decided to apply with the Nudge My Tour project to address this knowledge gap, and to make the knowledge about the application of behavioural approaches to tourism sustainability more accessible within the tourism ecosystem.

<< Objectives >>

The general objective of Nudge My Tour was to contribute to a better management of tourism flows and to a more effective planning of tourism destinations/experiences, in a post-Covid tourism recovery and beyond, through innovative methods based on behavioural science and the Nudge theory. 
The specific objectives were the following: 
- Raise the awareness of professionals working on tourism planning and management about the potential of the Nudge theory to positively influence the behaviour of tourists in a destination, towards the prevention of some of the negative effects of Overtourism, and equip them with practical tools; 
- Build & test innovative pedagogic tools to illustrate how behavioural insights can be applied to tourism flows management 
- Share examples of Nudges applied to tourism


<< Implementation >>

In the Nudge My Tour project we carried out the following activities:
The Nudge My Tour partners have co-developed pedagogic and awareness raising tools about the application of Nudging and behavioural science to the management of tourism flows. These tools are: 1) a Training Methodology aimed for current and future professionals in tourism planning and destination management, which covers the fundamentals of tourism sustainability and applied behavioural science (Annex 1); 2) an Informative Toolkit that visually explains the key topics addressed in the methodology (Annex 2); 3) a Compilation of nudges and other behavioural interventions applied to tourism (Annex 3).
The five project partners that carry out training, higher education and lifelong learning have tested the Training Methodology within their pedagogic activities. Based on the feedback from testing, the partners have revised the pedagogic tools. The testing sessions allowed to transfer the knowledge about behavioural approaches applied to tourism to 120+ professionals and university students in five cities.
A transnational Training of Trainers has been carried out in Paris, where a selected group of staff from the participating organisations learned how to use the three Project Results in their respective pedagogic activities, and beyond.
Several dissemination events allowed to involve stakeholders from the tourism sector, to share with them the pedagogic tools co-produced with Nudge My Tour and, more importantly, to discuss the relevance of applying behavioural approaches to tourism sustainability, and the importance of sharing knowledge about human behaviour.
CROSS-CUTTING ACTIVITIES: Project Management; Monitoring and Evaluation of project’s activities, results and impacts; Communication & Dissemination.

<< Results >>

In the Nudge My Tour project we achieved the following concrete outputs:
Firstly, we co-developed three pedagogic tools about the application of behavioural approaches to tourism sustainability:
-	A Training Methodology about the application of behavioural science to tourism sustainability, addressed to trainers and teachers who work in the tourism field, and who provide training and capacity building to tourism planning and destination management professionals, and to university (Master) students in tourism/destination management, tourism planning, destination marketing, etc.
-	An Informative Toolkit comprising 14 infographics that provide a visual summary of the key topics of behavioural science applied to tourism sustainability, also addressed in the Training Methodology. They are designed to be self-explanatory, but also to be integrated in the training courses when using the methodology.
-	4 animated videos that are also part of the Informative Toolkit, that aim to bring the infographics to life, illustrating some of the key concepts of tourism sustainability, decision-making, nudging, and the application of the knowledge of human behaviour in tourism.
-	A Compilation of nudges and other behavioural interventions, which provides concrete examples of how the behavioural approach can be successfully applied to tackle a tourism sustainability-related challenge.
Other important results have been achieved thanks to this project:
-	In general, this project allowed to set the stage on the topic of nudges applied to tourism sustainability, that was until now relatively unexplored. Nudge My Tour created a momentum, and the enabling environment for other initiatives that go in the same direction of using knowledge of human behaviour in sustainable tourism.
-	The team from the seven participating organisations directly involved in the project gained in-depth knowledge of the principles of tourism sustainability, behavioural science and nudging. They will now become ambassadors of the application of behavioural science within their own organization and beyond.
-	120+ students and practitioners in the field of tourism planning and destination management have received training on the topic of applied behavioural science, and are now sensitized about the relevance of behavioural approaches when it comes to managing a destination more sustainably
-	All partners have committed to keep using the pedagogic tools co-developed in their respective pedagogic activities, and in general to the keep working on the topic of applied behavioural science.
-	Among them, at least three have integrated in their curriculum a training course about behavioural sience and nudging applied to tourism, which will use the Nudge My Tour methodology, toolkit and compilation as pedagogic tools.

2021-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000030375.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000030375.title: HERO - Heritage Ecological Renovation for inclusion Opportunities
2021-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000030375.summary:
<< Background >>

Nous avons conçu ce projet pour répondre à des besoins pressants dans les secteurs de la restauration du patrimoine et de la construction en Europe. Le projet s'articule autour de 3 défis :

1 - Fournir aux acteurs de la formation à la restauration du patrimoine des outils pédagogiques efficaces permettant de former une plus grande diversité d’apprenants, en particulier ceux éloignés de la formation. Ces outils sont conçus pour aider les formateurs à adapter leur pédagogie aux nouveaux standards en matière d’inclusivité et d’écologie sur un chantier.

2 - Adapter les méthodes de formation à des profils ayant des besoins spécifiques, pour contribuer à créer des opportunités d’emploi pour des personnes éloignées du marché du travail dans une industrie en pénurie de main-d’œuvre.

3 - Inclure davantage la transition écologique lié au bâti dans les parcours de formation, afin de contribuer à décarboner cette industrie polluante

En collaborant avec des experts en restauration patrimoniale, en maçonnerie et en éco-construction, nous avons développé des méthodes de formation inclusives, durables et pratiques, renforçant l’employabilité des publics marginalisés et alignant la préservation du patrimoine sur la transition écologique

<< Objectives >>

1 - Renforcer les compétences pédagogiques des formateurs en restauration du patrimoine en leur fournissant des kits de formation complets, inclusifs et durables. Ces ressources prennent en compte les besoins spécifiques des apprenants en situation précaire ou sans expérience préalable dans la construction.

2 - Répondre à la pénurie de professionnels qualifiés en restauration du patrimoine dans l'UE en renforçant les compétences des formateurs et des apprenants dans les métiers de la construction traditionnelle. Grâce à des méthodes d’apprentissage pratiques et concrètes, nous contribuons à préparer des apprenants à des carrières dans la restauration et l’éco-construction, comblant ainsi le déficit de compétences dans un secteur clé pour la préservation du patrimoine culturel européen.

3 - HERO a intégré des considérations écologiques dans la formation à la restauration du patrimoine pour promouvoir des pratiques durables dans le secteur plus large du bâtiment. Le projet a développé et testé des modules, outils et techniques de formation éco-responsables, validés par des applications concrètes.


<< Implementation >>

Remarque introductive : nous pouvons conseiller de regarder la vidéo de présentation du projet (3min30) afin d'en avoir une vision globale du projet : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vGzR-fMWjT4

I - Structure et gestion

Pour assurer une collaboration efficace et un suivi constant, les stratégies de gestion suivantes ont été mises en œuvre :  
- Partage en ligne de documents : Un espace de travail partagé en ligne (google drive) a été créé pour faciliter la communication et l’échange de documents entre les partenaires, permettant des mises à jour en temps réel et un travail collaboratif.  
- Comités de pilotage bimensuels : Des réunions régulières tous les deux mois ont permis de suivre l’avancement du projet, de traiter des problèmes courants, des tâches en cours et maintenir une ligne de communication formelle.
- Réunions transnationales (TPMs) : 4 TPM en présentiel ont été organisés pendant la durée du projet. Ces rencontres ont permis d’évaluer le développement du projet à des moments clef, de partager des retours d’expérience issus des mises en œuvre locales et d’affiner collectivement les orientations stratégiques.

II - Activités Principales  

Les activités principales du projet HERO ont été axées sur la production, le test et la diffusion de ressources clés pour soutenir les formateurs et la communauté de la restauration patrimoniale :  

- PR1 : Cartographie des initiatives sur le patrimoine, l’inclusion et la durabilité  
HERO a débuté par une cartographie approfondie de 15 initiatives en Europe et en Méditerranée combinant restauration patrimoniale, inclusion sociale et durabilité environnementale. Cette analyse a permis d’identifier les bonnes pratiques et de poser les bases d’approches inclusives et écologiques pour le projet (lien : cutt.ly/ReH3gjoS).  

- PR2 : Prototypage d’un manuel de formation sur l’inclusion  
Le premier prototype de manuel, centré sur l’inclusion, a fourni des orientations pédagogiques aux formateurs pour mieux soutenir les groupes vulnérables en formation à la restauration du patrimoine. Cette ressource a permis d’adapter les méthodologies de formation aux besoins des apprenants en situation précaire pour favoriser leur engagement et leur montée en compétences (lien : cutt.ly/FeH3hm6j).  

- PR3 : Prototypage d’un manuel de formation sur la durabilité et l’éco-construction  
HERO a ensuite développé un second manuel, axé sur la durabilité et l’éco-construction. Ce manuel a équipé les formateurs d’outils et de connaissances sur les pratiques et matériaux durables, reliant l’artisanat traditionnel aux techniques respectueuses de l’environnement pour soutenir la transition verte en Europe (lien : cutt.ly/teH3zk9h).  

- PR4 : Test, adaptation et enrichissement des supports de formation  
Les prototypes des PR2 et PR3 ont été testés dans le cadre d’expérimentations locales et de deux sessions transnationales de formation. Les retours issus de ces tests ont permis de définir les améliorations à apporter au manuel final. Des fiches d’activité détaillées et des tutoriels vidéo ont été développés pour enrichir ces ressources. Ce processus itératif a garanti que les manuels soient pratiques, faciles à utiliser et efficaces dans des contextes réels (lien : cutt.ly/SeH3xcwy // playlist de tutoriels : cutt.ly/ZeH3xBQC).  

- PR5 : Livre blanc et diffusion via des événements multiplicateurs  
Le projet s’est conclu par un livre blanc compilant les conclusions et recommandations à destination de la communauté européenne de la restauration patrimoniale. Ce document proposait des étapes stratégiques pour intégrer l’inclusion et la durabilité dans la formation à la restauration. La diffusion du livre blanc a été intégrée à quatre événements multiplicateurs organisés tout au long du projet pour engager les parties prenantes, recueillir leurs retours et promouvoir les résultats et méthodologies du projet (lien : cutt.ly/9eH3cSte). 


<< Results >>

I – Résultats concrets et tangibles

HERO a généré des résultats concrets et impactants favorisant l’inclusion, la durabilité et la professionnalisation des pratiques de restauration du patrimoine en l’Europe. Ces résultats se déclinent en cinq grandes catégories, reflétant l’approche multidimensionnelle du projet.

1 - Cartographie des initiatives combinant patrimoine, inclusion et durabilité (PR1) : HERO a commencé par une cartographie détaillée de 15 initiatives de restauration patrimoniale en Europe et en Méditerranée, alliant préservation du patrimoine, inclusion sociale et durabilité. Cette analyse a posé les bases pour intégrer ces valeurs dans la formation patrimoniale. Le rapport a servi de ressource précieuse pour les formateurs et les décideurs, mettant en lumière des modèles innovants dans la restauration patrimoniale et l’éco-construction.

2 - Deux manuels de formation prototypés

- manuel sur la formation inclusive en restauration du patrimoine (PR2) : Ce manuel offre aux formateurs des méthodologies pour engager des apprenants issus de milieux vulnérables. Il couvre des approches pédagogiques adaptées à ceux rencontrant des difficultés avec les environnements d’apprentissage classiques, mettant l’accent sur la formation pratique par le geste, l’apprentissage par l’erreur, l’autonomisation et la motivation.

- Manuel sur les techniques durables et éco-responsables (PR3) : Le second manuel guide les formateurs sur l’intégration de pratiques éco-responsables dans la restauration patrimoniale. Il traite des techniques de construction durable et du choix des matériaux, tout en alignant les compétences patrimoniales avec les enjeux environnementaux.

3 - Kit de formation finalisé et supports pratiques (PR4)

- Tests sur le terrain : Les contenus des PR2 et PR3 ont été testés lors d’événements locaux et transnationaux, permettant d’affiner les ressources pour garantir leur efficacité et leur accessibilité.

- Modules Pratiques et Fiches d’Activités : HERO a développé des modules et fiches détaillées en réponse aux retours des sessions pilotes. Ces supports guident étape par étape les formateurs sur des activités comme la maçonnerie traditionnelle ou les techniques de construction durable.

- Tutoriels vidéo : Une série de vidéos a été produite pour démontrer visuellement les pratiques clés de restauration et de durabilité enseignées dans le programme, facilitant l’apprentissage autonome.


4 - Livre blanc et recommandations stratégiques (PR5)

- Livre blanc pour la communauté du patrimoine : Ce document, destiné aux décideurs, organisations de formation et institutions patrimoniales, synthétise les enseignements du projet et propose des recommandations concrètes pour intégrer inclusion et durabilité dans la formation.

- Plaidoyer et visibilité : Le livre blanc sert également d’outil de plaidoyer, encourageant les décideurs européens à relever les défis de la pénurie de compétences et de la durabilité dans le secteur patrimonial.

5 - Diffusion et Sensibilisation par des Événements Multiplicateurs

- 4 événements multiplicateurs : Ces événements ont réuni un large public d’acteurs des secteurs du patrimoine, de la construction et de l’éducation, permettant de diffuser les résultats du projet et de créer des partenariats.

- Dynamique d’internationalisation : La visibilité du projet a été renforcée par l’intégration des partenaires aux principaux réseaux traitant des questions de patrimoine au niveau européen (Europa Nostra, Eurocities, Union pour la Méditerranée), ainsi qu’en participant à différents groupes de travail internationaux (Comité d’experts sur le patrimoine culturel de la Commission européenne, rapport de recommendations pour une politique européenne de l’artisanat dans le cadre de la présidence belge de l’UE …)

II – Impacts plus larges du projet HERO

Les résultats du projet HERO vont au-delà des manuels et événements, en établissant des bases pour des pratiques à la restauration du patrimoine plus inclusives et responsables sur le plan environnemental. En s'adressant indirectement à des personnes en situation de précarité ou éloignées du secteur du bâtiment, HERO contribue à créer des opportunités d’emploi pour des individus souvent exclus, favorisant la cohésion sociale et l’autonomisation économique.

Le projet a également répondu au besoin urgent de renouveau des pratiques écologiques dans le secteur patrimonial, alignant ses actions sur les objectifs de l’UE pour une société plus verte et inclusive. Il comble le déficit de compétences tout en promouvant une croissance durable.

Enfin, à l’exception de Pour La Solidarité, HERO a été le premier projet de coopération pour les quatre autres partenaires. Ce projet a permis une internationalisation et une reconnaissance accrues des partenaires, comme en témoignent les prix Europa Nostra remportés par Acta Vista et Bao Formation en 2023, et par Boulouki en 2024, dans la catégorie « emploi, formation et compétences », rejoignant Dragodid, lauréat en 2011. Aujourd’hui, tous les partenaires participent à de nouveaux projets de coopération (Erasmus+, Creative Europe, FESI...) et bénéficient également du soutien de fondations privées pour s’internationaliser.

2021-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000034815.title: GREEN TO BLUE: IMPROVEMENT OF SUSTAINABILITY COMPETENCES IN THE FIELD OF FISHERY & AQUACULTURE
2021-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000034815.summary:
<< Background >>

Le projet Green to Blue se déploie dans un secteur de la pêche et de l'aquaculture confronté à des défis majeurs. La main-d'œuvre est peu qualifiée et vieillissante : 67 % des travailleurs ont un faible niveau d'éducation et 58 % sont âgés de 40 à 64 ans (STECF 2019). Bien qu'ils aient une vaste expérience en mer, ces pêcheurs sont vulnérables face aux changements environnementaux et réglementaires.

Les enjeux environnementaux, tels que la gestion des ressources naturelles, la prévention de la pollution marine et la qualité de l'eau, sont cruciaux. Le projet vise à améliorer les compétences des travailleurs en proposant des formations en gestion environnementale et en techniques durables. Il répond à la nécessité de professionnaliser les métiers de la pêche et de l'aquaculture et de créer des liens durables entre les acteurs du secteur, les centres de recherche et les organismes de formation.

Green to Blue aspire à gérer les innovations de l'économie bleue, aidant ainsi le secteur traditionnel à relever les défis futurs et à promouvoir la durabilité et l'innovation en Europe.

<< Objectives >>

*Introduire des compétences techniques environnementales dans les secteurs de la pêche et de l'aquaculture pour renforcer la gestion durable des ressources marines.
* Développer une offre de formation flexible et adaptable afin de répondre aux besoins spécifiques des travailleurs du secteur, en accord avec les exigences de la transition écologique des métiers.
*Améliorer la sensibilisation aux enjeux environnementaux et augmenter les compétences des travailleurs des secteurs de la pêche et de l'aquaculture, notamment dans les micro et petites entreprises, pour une meilleure prise en compte de l'impact environnemental de leurs activités.
*Créer une réponse structurée et collaborative impliquant les acteurs des secteurs de la pêche et de l'aquaculture, les organismes de formation professionnelle et le monde scientifique pour promouvoir une culture environnementale et apporter des innovations significatives dans le domaine.
*Accroître les opportunités d'apprentissage tout au long de la vie afin de garantir l'accès équitable à la formation pour la reconversion et le développement des compétences, contribuant ainsi à la création d'une société plus juste et inclusive

<< Implementation >>

•	Conduite d’une recherche scientifique et d’un dialogue avec les acteurs du secteur de la pêche/aquaculture 
•	Elaboration d’un état de l'art autour de la collecte des plastiques en mer et approche de l'économie circulaire dans le secteur de la pêche/aquaculture 
•	Mise en place des groupes de travail sur les territoires du projet pour recueillir les avis et les demandes des acteurs du secteur de la pêche/aquaculture 
•	Définition d’un cadre de compétences permettant une meilleure intégration de l’économie verte et bleue au sein du secteur de la pêche et de l’aquaculture
•	Développement du PROGRAMME DE FORMATION basé sur le cadre de compétences GREEN TO BLUE 
•	Mise en place d’une phase de test auprès des 
a) Travailleurs et opérateurs du secteur de la pêche et de l'aquaculture
b) Chercheurs et représentants des associations/syndicats/fédérations qui défendent les intérêts des pêcheurs/pisciculteurs
•	Définition d’un profil innovant aux compétences émergentes du projet, celui de "Sentinelle de la Mer"
•	Elaboration d’indications politiques sur l'importance du rôle des pêcheurs et des pisciculteurs dans le développement durable.
•	Mise en place de nombreuses actions de valorisation du projet générant des effets multiplicateurs en dehors des organisations participantes au niveau local/régional/national et européen


<< Results >>

R1: CADRE DE COMPÉTENCES GREEN TO BLUE: structure une vision complète des compétences requises dans le secteur de la pêche et de l'aquaculture pour intégrer le thème de la durabilité, couvrant les dimensions économiques, réglementaires, environnementales et climatiques, ainsi que la relation entre la recherche scientifique et les tâches quotidiennes des travailleurs. Adapté aux centres de formation professionnelle pour ajuster leur offre de formation en conséquence.

R2: PROGRAMME DE FORMATION GREEN TO BLUE: prépare les formateurs VET, les coaches et les tuteurs à mener des actions éducatives au sein des communautés de pêche, ainsi qu'à former les chercheurs, les organisations liées à la pêche et les décideurs. Le matériel pédagogique vise le développement de compétences en durabilité, économie bleue, collecte de déchets marins, économie circulaire, protection des ressources et efficacité énergétique, avec une attention particulière aux méthodologies didactiques.

R3: MANUEL & INDICATIONS POLITIQUES GREEN TO BLUE: comprend une étude sur les SYSTÈMES DE VALIDATION/CERTIFICATION pour promouvoir le nouveau profil de "Sentinelle de la Mer" avec des compétences émergentes du projet, ainsi que des INDICATIONS POLITIQUES soutenant son intégration et sa durabilité dans les cadres européens.

L'ensemble des résultats est disponible en EN, FR, IT, TK, HR, GR sur le site web du projet : https://www.greentoblue-project.eu/

2021-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000034840.title: Le Jardin des carrières – Construire des ponts entre les établissements éducatifs et les entreprises, par le biais de stages à distance et hybrides
2021-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000034840.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project during the Covid period. A significant need was to support students in their transition to the professional world, especially given the restrictions of the Covid-19 pandemic that made internships impossible. Additionally, we noticed a substantial lack of integration of IT and new media in education. Our goal was to address these gaps by offering online learning opportunities and improving the integration of IT in education, benefiting students while enhancing career orientation by providing access to relevant resources and information about careers. Thus, the theme of "virtual internships" seemed to be a perfect combination to address these aspects. Finally, for better adoption of the results, an online platform with clear resources and guidelines, as well as a motivating presentation, was essential, supported by continuous project activities to ensure its sustainability.

<< Objectives >>

Our objectives were as follows:

    Explore and develop new ways to offer pre-professional experiences to younger generations.
    Prototype and experiment with a digital internship model for learners needing internship immersion and/or career orientation.
    Reach secondary school learners and their teachers, providing them with digital resources to explore the world of work.
    Establish connections between educational institutions and companies.
    Facilitate contact between students and companies for internships.
    Promote collaboration among teachers from different institutions to address the transition from school to vocational training or university, and ultimately to professional life.
    Identify the needs of educational stakeholders and students to produce results that are genuinely used to ensure the project's sustainability.
    Encourage students to undertake internships, especially internationally.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented a series of planned activities to produce essential results for the project, in collaboration with all project partners.

First, we conducted a detailed needs analysis by carrying out three surveys in each partner country, allowing us to compare the situations regarding vocational training and internships.

Next, we produced a prototype of digital internships and developed 27 video modules designed for wide use. We organized pilot phases in various institutions to test the quality of these modules and promote their utilization.

These modules are hosted on a web platform, https://www.careergarden.eu, which we also developed to serve as a virtual campus and networking hub.

Concurrently, we developed a career guidance framework based on the survey results. We also organized a digital networking event for participating students, along with a digital exhibition highlighting the project's achievements.

Training events were organized in different partner countries to disseminate the project and work on the specific concepts of the project. Finally, we organized multiplier events to support the dissemination of the project results to the general public.

<< Results >>


The results are ; 
•	Production of an analysis and sustainability guide
•	Production of a Career Guidance guide: Intended for teachers in versatile educational structures, this guide helps integrate career guidance and skills development into their courses.
•	Creation of 27 video modules from 5 sectors: 
•	Development of a website: https://www.careergarden.eu, includes all videos, educational resources, and results, accessible to a wide audience for free.
•	Design of educational and interactive resources: 
•	Implementation of a digital exhibition: The "Career Garden" exhibition showcases the entire project, highlighting participants' achievements and learnings.
Additionally, other noteworthy results include enhanced cooperation between educational institutions and businesses, as well as recommendations and actions to further strengthen the project. Working on the project's outcomes provided valuable insights into each country's school and vocational training systems. Participants in the training, piloting, and dissemination events found inspiration for their work and career paths and discovered the European Union and the benefits of the Erasmus+ program.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000025338.title: Zero Waste Catering Lab
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000025338.summary:
<< Background >>

In view of many years of experience in dealing with the topic of Zero Waste in the vocational program for chefs and
confectioners, Slava Raškaj Center is familiar with the large amount of waste generated in the process of food
preparation in the hospitality industry. That is why it formed a consortium of experienced partners from the hospitality
education sector at the level of vocational schools, adult education, and private entrepreneurs and associations in the
hospitality industry to jointly research, create, test, and put into use new digital tools

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to contribute to vocational training, adult learning, and the business catering sector by creating new digital tools in
education with Zero Waste outcomes. These educational tools sholud provide enhanced learning in Zero waste subjects and
at the same time create and improve business models towards Zero waste principles. Creating the "CaterinLAb"
application, "CateringLab" e guide, and "CaterinLab" video guide we will raise knowledge and awareness for many
students, restaurant managers, farmers, and end-users to work and to live by Zero Waste principles. Innovative Zero
Waste CateringLab application should enable the connection of local producers, restaurants, and catering products
consumers.  

<< Implementation >>

In our project we implemented:
: 1. Zero Waste catering Lab application /site -
creation and management of a platform/website to connect catering businesses, local farmers and responsible customers
- Leading partner Galileo; 2. Creation of a Zero Waste Catering Lab – e-guide - for training students and chefs to prepare
a meal according to circular food economy by eliminating waste, supporting local farmers, using Zero waste delivery;
creating jobs and ensuring that people have access to healthy, local food - Leading partner "Slava Raškaj" 3. Creation of
a Zero waste video guide database - it will contain the video recipes and video clips of the Zero-waste kitchen
management process - Leading partner Poster (HR) B) 4 Partners project meetings to be held in: - Croatia, Zagreb; -
Italy, Rome; - Belgium, Brugge; - Slovenia, Celje. C) 4 multiplier events to be held in Italy, Croatia, Slovenia and Belgium
D) 3 LTTs in Italy, Belgium and Croatia E) Dissemination activities F) Project management activities


<< Results >>

The digital tool Zero Waste Catering Lab  is solving  the problem of networking and it s bring together local producers, farmers,
and restaurants, connects them all with the end-user through the web application. Through the same application, the
end consumer of food can order a meal that is prepared in a zero waste way and delivered with the lowest
carbon footprint, ensuring that its action has a positive impact on the environment. Students of two VET catering schools
had the opportunity to learn how to use the application, through LTT activities and through the Catering guide, and
their knowledge is also  improved through Catering Lab video guide, containing visual and practical instructions for all
interested chefs, students, entrepreneurs on how to achieve zero waste food delivery processes.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000025498.title: Innovative and Sustainable Pedagogies for Digital Green Case Study-based Teaching 4 VET
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000025498.summary:
<< Background >>

Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the opportunities to provide VET students in logistics and transport with practical training in the workplace are highly limited if not inexistent.
Therefore, it is necessary to quickly find appropriate solutions that would at least partially substitute practical training but would also be used after the completion of the pandemic situation. A potential solution is an integration of living case studies into the VET teaching and learning practice that will later also be applicable in blended teaching and learning situations. 
However, several empirical surveys conducted in EU  VET institutions by consortium partners during 2018-2021 revealed that VET teachers lack:
- digital skills,
- case-study based teaching skills,
- cooperation with the logistics industry,
- green skills.

The target groups that this project addresses includes VET teachers in logistics and transport, trainers in logistics and transport, and higher education teachers in logistics and
transport. Other stakeholders are VET teachers in other fields of VET, headmasters of VET institutions, relevant ministries and other governmental bodies responsible for VET, and the
logistics and transport industry.

<< Objectives >>

Therefore, the key objective of the Sustain4VET project is to develop an inventory of living green case studies and innovative pedagogies for collaborative online living case study-based teaching. In addition, VET teachers will be trained in the use of innovative pedagogies for online case study-based teaching, and be able to test the designed case studies and innovative pedagogies in practice.
This project even aims to start activities with national bodies for systemic integration of developed pedagogies into the educational framework of French, Slovene, Croatian and + VET in transport and logistics.

<< Implementation >>

The 2nd and 3rd project activities aim to provide at least three innovative pedagogies in online living green case study-based teaching, including a pedagogical guide for the implementation of the pedagogies. In the 4th activity of the project, the event will be organised to train VET teachers in the use of innovative pedagogies and living green case study-based teaching. 
In the 5th activity, VET teachers will test online case study-based teaching and learning with their students ("learning by doing").

The project will produce six intellectual outcomes (IO):
- IO1: Set of logistics and transport green living case studies for collaborative online case study-based teaching and learning in VET in logistics and transport.
- IO2: Pedagogical guide for VET teachers in logistics and transport and trainers in logistics and transport for the development and design of living case studies appropriate for online
teaching and learning.
- IO3: Set of innovative pedagogies for online living green case study-based teaching and learning in VET in logistics and transport.
- IO4: Pedagogical guide for online living case study-based teaching and learning for VET in logistics and transport.
- IO5: Online training in innovative pedagogies for online living case study-based teaching and learning for VET teachers in transport and logistics.
- IO6: Testing innovative pedagogies by VET teachers in transport and logistics.

<< Results >>

IMPACT on VET teachers in logistics and transport & trainers & higher education teachers:
- encouraging the collaboration between VET teachers and representatives of the logistics and transport industry,
- to obtain the capacity to reflect on, document, and effectively communicate the case study,
- to evaluate the applicability and relevance of the developed living case studies to their teaching contexts, and
- to design and develop a reliable and fact-based living case study, relevant to the logistics and transport industry,
- increasing the knowledge and skills in new pedagogies suitable for living case study-based teaching and learning in the online environment,
- increasing the knowledge and skills in new pedagogies suitable for living case study-based collaborative learning,
- critical examination of the strengths, weaknesses and requirements of innovative technologies used in online teaching and learning,
- helping VET teachers (trainers and higher education teachers) to obtain the capacity to reflect on, document, and critically evaluate innovative pedagogies for their teaching practice,
- increasing the knowledge and skills in implementing new pedagogies suitable for collaborative teaching and learning in VET,
- increasing the knowledge and skills in implementing new pedagogies collaborative online teaching and learning,
- increasing the knowledge and skills in available technologies and tools that support these pedagogies (e.g., Zoom, Moodle, CourseWork – Canvas, Panopto, Mediathread),
- increasing the knowledge and skills in different types of pedagogies, such as problem-based learning, discussion, debate, intimate debate, public hearing, trial, jigsaw, and role-play,
- continuing the development of teacher cognition in new pedagogies,
- having hands-on experience with teaching and learning in a collaborative online environment,
- developing skills in modelling online case study discussions,
- developing skills in strategies for engaging students in case study-based learning,
- getting acquainted with the challenges and problems of online case study-based and learning,
- increased awareness of the difference between traditional (class-based teaching) and online case-based teaching,
- increased awareness of the difference between different engagement strategies,
- making connections between new concepts and existing theoretical knowledge,
- the increased ability of application of the theoretical concepts in practice,
- developing digital skills,
- developing intercultural skills,
- providing opportunities for life-long professional development and teacher cognition,
- developing problem-solving skills,
- developing decision-making skills in complex situations,
- developing skills in quantitative and/or qualitative analytical tools,
- developing intercultural skills,
- developing soft skills,
- developing English language skills.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000025725.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000025725.title: Communication skills  and diversity competence for students of vocational Schools for Medical Professions: Design thinking for participatory medicine
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000025725.summary:
<< Background >>

Vocational education of future healthcare workers plays a crucial role in preparing them to enter the workforce of fast-evolving medicine. One of the crucial changes healthcare system is facing is preparing the workforce and patients for participatory medicine (PM) approach in which the role of patients is changed to more proactive. PM suggests for patients to work in collaboration with their doctors and nurses and take more responsibility for their own health. This change in patient's role has neither been reflected in classrooms nor in the offer of continuous professional development for the teachers in medical vocational schools. DesignCARE addresses the gap identified in vocational schools in field of PM. The project team translated its expertise into training for the teachers and course for students which included different PM aspects: communication skills, empathy, diversity competence, responsible research and innovation and participatory medicine itself. Training in diversity contributes to improving understanding, interaction and communication between the healthcare worker and patients with different backgrounds. Diversity competency can help promote equality, ensuring patients receive treatment according to their needs.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective is to design, pilot, implement and evaluate the DesignCARE curriculum and course for the students in secondary and post-secondary medical vocational schools that will help them to engage in participatory medicine through the promotion of the development of communication skills and diversity competence, in line with ethical principles.
Besides creating the DesignCARE program, the goal of the project is also to train the teachers to be able to design a course that encourages skill development, research-based learning, creativity, and student cooperation among peers and with their teachers.
We will train the teachers to use inclusive, collaborative design thinking methods as an innovative educational strategy. Design thinking is a mindset and approach to learning, collaboration, and problem-solving. In practice, the design process is a structured framework for identifying challenges, gathering information, generating potential solutions, refining ideas, and testing solutions.
The students will profit by gaining increased capacity to learn in online learning as well as in the group environment, which focuses on both knowledge and skill development. 


<< Implementation >>

The activities within the projects were the following: 
DesignCARE 1st transnational (kick-off) meeting – the first meeting was held on February 21, 2022, at which UNIST presented the project, main goals and results, partners voted on the Steering Committee members, platforms to be used for meetings and materials (Google Meets, Google Drive). A financial, communication and dissemination plan, as well as a Quality Assurance Plan were presented. The partners designed the logo. All materials are available to partners on the Google Drive platform.
Training – the activities in the project include staff and student training. Staff training allowed the participants to acquire the competencies necessary for the successful implementation of the project. Immediately after the kick-off, the Training on design thinking for curriculum design; training on diversity competence and communication skills; training on participatory medicine and ethics and RRI was held. Work on curriculum design (curriculum map, learning outcomes) also started that week.
The focus groups - In order to get the input from all relevant stakeholders, two focus groups were organized, one by Colegiul Mihai Eminescu (May 2022) and one by UNIST (June 2022). 
Curriculum framework - The topics with learning outcomes to be covered by the course were defined in the following period, in terms of knowledge, technical and life skills, attitudes and values for each of the topics, as a part of the curriculum framework.
The second transnational meeting was held in September 2022 in Copenhagen, Denmark, where partners had media communication skills and creation of video content training, and the creation of the online content for the DesignCARE online course started. The decision on the best option for an online server that can be accessed by all partners and is user-friendly was made, which was Moodle Mod. In the following period, the partners continued to work on the creation of the content: written, video and additional materials and creating the activities and evaluation for students. 
DesignCARE 3rd transnational meeting – the final meeting was held in Bacau, Romania, on March 30-31, 2023. During that time, the partners assessed the content of the thus far designed course and activities and discussed the preparation for the pilot testing of the curriculum and course for the students of two medical vocational schools at secondary and post-secondary levels in the EU.

Piloting the DesignCARE: after the materials were uploaded and the course on the Moodle Mod platform was ready, the piloting started in July with students of Colegiul Mihai Eminescu in Romania. After summer, the piloting continued in Croatia in September, with students from Medicinska škola Pula. We additionally included eight students from Medicinska škola Split, which is not a partner in the project, but was highly motivated to participate.

Web page and Facebook page were created.
https://mefst.unist.hr/znanost/erasmus-projekti-11479/designcare/11958 
https://www.facebook.com/Communication-and-diversity-Design-thinking-for-participatory-medicine-102287092408845 


<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results produced by the project are:
1.	The curriculum framework with learning outcomes for the development of communication skills and diversity competence in participatory medicine; 
2.	Online course consisting of 5 modules: Participatory medicine, Diversity, Communication with patients and relatives, Empathy, Ethics and Responsible Research and Innovation (RRI). Educational materials and resources to foster students’ development of transversal skills and key topics knowledge, include 23 videos and video transcripts, 6 obligatory texts, quizzes and 14 activities and assignments to be performed online or in person in a classroom;
3.	Capacity building of at least 15 trained teachers able to implement the educational resources designed in daily teaching;
4.	50 students trained (knowledge and skills development), with certification and badges; 
5.     Evaluation of Train the trainer activity and Evaluation of DesignCARE pilot;
6.	Coordination and participation of all partners and stakeholders in the co-creation process;
7.	Internationalization of the participating organizations.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000025762.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000025762.title: Florcert za budućnost - majstor
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000025762.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was created as an upgrade of previous projects of schools in the FlorCert network and expansion of the network towards new partners with the general desire to standardize knowledge and skills for the profession of florist/florist. As a result of the previous project, an e-book translated into 7 languages ​​with basic professional educational content was created.
By analyzing the previous project and conducting a participant survey, we observed:
1. Great need for professional training of teachers and mentors at employers from basic to master level
2. Care of the environment from the aspect of sustainable development and the use of biodegradable materials in the cultivation and use of flowers
3. The need for better communication in the triangle of student, teacher and mentor at the employer, especially in unforeseen situations (COVID)

<< Objectives >>

The general and long-term goal of the FFF-M project was to create a competent teacher and mentor for employers with broad views on the profession.
The goals for achieving this long-term goal were:
- to systematize the competencies of teachers and mentors at employers
- develop training modules for teachers and mentors at employers
- create a guide through the modular training of teachers and mentors at employers
- raise awareness of care for the environment, climate change
- raise awareness of the importance of using biodegradable materials, waste disposal and recycling
- create interactive content
- develop a new digital tool for communication, monitoring and evaluation in the student/teacher/mentor triangle

<< Implementation >>

Activities of the FFF-M project:
- 3 planned LTT activities
- 5 planned live transnational project meetings
- 1 extra TPM in Sweden - receiving diplomas for the master's exam by the Swedish Chamber of Crafts
- 3 events with multiplying live action
- 3 online events with multiplying live action
- 16 hangout meetings
- 2 meetings with teachers  in live
- dissemination activities in partner countries - various workshops, lectures, meetings at local, regional and national level

<< Results >>

There are three concrete results of the project that are published on the project website with simple and free access for all interested parties. All results were translated into Croatian, Italian, Slovenian, Serbian and Swedish.
1. Guide to the modular training of teachers and mentors at employers according to FlorCert, which contains modules with the necessary learning outcomes
2. Interactive content and sustainable development content to supplement existing educational content for the floristry profession - videos with short content, educational content with current topics and associated tasks
3. App florist tools - development of a new tool adapted to the floristry profession prepared for better communication, monitoring and evaluation in the student / teacher / mentor triangle
Project participants adopted new soft, social competences, perfected their knowledge of the English language, improved and strengthened ties between
partners and strengthened cooperation for new projects in the future, gained self-confidence, improved professional knowledge and skills, developed social and intercultural competences, critical thinking, developed new ICT competences and thus contribute to a better digitization of the learning process.
