2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000028068.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000028068.title: Green Skills & Practices for Postal Services to implement the European Green Deal
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000028068.summary:
<< Background >>

Significant international events like the adoption of the Paris Agreement and the increasing importance of the UN Sustainable Development Goals have signaled the urgent need for global business sustainability. GreenPosts draws inspiration from existing initiatives aiming to implement a concept and approach towards greening human capital and the economy by introducing associated skills for transitioning to a circular and greener economy. With over 600,000 postal offices worldwide, 660,000 vehicles, 250,000 motorcycles, and airplanes covering billions of kilometers annually for mail delivery, postal services and 5.5 million workers consume electricity, water, and paper, all impacting the environment. The project addresses the demand for sustainable business by empowering employees, preparing them for a shift to a greener economy by equipping them with skills necessary to support sustainable development. Through education on implementing the European GD and supporting the UN's SDG, particularly those targeting climate change mitigation and sustainable urban development, the project aims to reduce the postal sector's negative environmental impact. A pilot course has been conducted for testing and adapting educational materials. 

<< Objectives >>

Local postal services are engaged in various environmental activities but it's not always easy for them to keep up with the science and EU policies to create an adequate and comprehensive long-term plan focused on the right priorities, using the latest evidence and achieving better results.The project presents clear and tangible benefits for all involved stakeholders. It will enhance core skills and competencies in leadership, citizenship, and action, supporting green and social initiatives with proven environmental benefits for the region and local communities. It also promotes social cohesion, integration, and inclusion, offering advantages and more opportunities for everyone.
The goals of this project were to establish a training program that will enable staff in local postal offices to:
•	Set a clear, long-term direction with flexibility to adapt to new evidence and circumstances.
•	Ensure robust and credible reporting, management, and accountability.
•	Establish strong local leadership and a more integrated delivery framework.
•	Provide resources, create incentives, and support sustainable funding, including from the private sector.
•	Ensure that everyone plays their role in creating the improved environment we all desire.

<< Implementation >>

During 24 intensive months, the following activities were conducted through concrete methods:

Initial project management activities laid the foundation for the project implementation. These activities include:
1. Initial and Internal Work Meetings: Partners' initial and internal working meetings were regularly organized, initially several times a month, later at least once a month, providing an excellent opportunity for internal networking. Additionally, 4 transnational meetings were organized; the first was held online due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, and the remaining three were conducted in person in Bulgaria, Greece, and Cyprus. Croatia also hosted a three-day LTT activity. Alongside GreenPosts-related activities to achieve results, dissemination activities were conducted. Furthermore, 4 multiplier events involving relevant stakeholders were held. Partners shared best practices and information facilitating continuous improvement, effective carbon management, as well as climate change mitigation and adaptation.
2. Establishment of the Project Plan: This included a work plan and a Gantt chart with 4 revisions approved by the NA, a budget plan for project activities, clear distribution of responsibilities among partners, the appointment of members to the Quality Control and Monitoring Committee, identification of project indicators and intended outcomes, and the creation of a communication and dissemination plan.
3. Project Management Handbook: A project management handbook was developed, comprising templates for management reports and team contacts.

Detailed, In the project management and implementation, the following results were achieved:
1. Partnership Contracts: Partnership contracts were signed between the lead partner and each project partner at the project's outset to ensure its smooth execution.
2. Project Implementation Plan: A comprehensive project implementation plan was developed along with initial reporting, detailed action plans per PR, activity schedules, project information, meetings, project activities, tasks, and deadlines.
3. Establishment of a Work Monitoring System: A work monitoring system was established.
4. Communication Scheme among Partners: A communication scheme was established among partners using platforms such as OneDrive, Microsoft Teams, email, and WhatsApp.
5. Project Indicators and Outcomes: Project indicators and outcomes were defined along with agreed-upon quality standards for content, usability, and appearance.
6. Financial Regulations and Reporting Overview: A financial regulation and reporting overview was created, consolidating management and reporting tools used by partners, including templates for biannual reporting and reporting guidelines.
7. Budgetary Handbook: A budgetary handbook, incorporating templates and timetables for budget monitoring, was developed.
8. Interim and Final Reports: Interim (semi-annual) and final reports were produced as required by the National Agency.
9. Additional Documents: Dissemination Strategy and Exploitation Plan, Quality Assurance Plan, and the project website (https://greenposts.eu/) were developed.

Dissemination activities funded within the project management and implementation encompassed:
1. Visibility and Communication Strategies: Strategies for visibility and communication were developed.
2. Networking and Presentations: Project networking occurred regularly to enhance project visibility through various events, such as presentations to 40 members of the Environmental Working Group (WG) and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) of PostEurop (European postal operators association) and to 150 participants of the HP Academy for Middle Management, including face-to-face conversations at formal and informal gatherings.
3. Project Identity and Logo: A project identity/logo was designed and used across various materials and communications related to the project.
4. Project Website: The website www.greenposts.eu was developed and launched for easy access to project information and linking to other websites and platforms.
5. Reporting Activities: Regular reporting on dissemination activities was done to the project manager through dissemination reports and board meetings.
6. Newsletters and Materials: Four newsletters, brochures, and other dissemination materials were created.
7. Corporate Outreach: Information about the project was shared on official corporate pages, like the Croatian Post's EU Corner, and partners' corporate pages and social media.
8. Internal Communications: Information about the project was regularly shared through corporate communication channels such as the intranet, magazines, and weekly bulletins.
9. YouTube Channel: A YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@GreenPosts.Project) was established for project-related content.

The Steering Committee meetings were held regularly via the Microsoft Teams platform, at least once a month, and more frequently if necessary. Meeting minutes and results were uploaded and shared with consortium members on OneDrive or sent via email in a timely manner.

Activities to achieve specific project outcomes were also conducted:
1. Development of "GreenPosts Assessment Tool": This tool was designed, tested with 5 employees from partner postal organizations, and best practices were collected and included in a Synthesis report. It was refined and translated into Greek, Bulgarian, and Croatian from English.
2. Course Structure Design: A structure for the "Implementing European Green Deal in Posts" course was designed. Course materials (9 lessons) were translated into Greek, Bulgarian, and Croatian from English. The course was piloted with employees from partner postal organizations, and participants received a certificate upon completion.
3. Video Interview Material: A questionnaire and guidelines for video interviews were developed. Material for "Peer to Peer Success Stories videos" was recorded, edited into 4 videos, translated, subtitled, and uploaded to the project's YouTube channel. These videos were then shared on social media, project websites, partner organizations' websites, the EPALE platform, and multiplier events.
4. Development of "Virtual Think Tank" Features and Content: A handbook and guidelines for using the VTT were created. The VTT was tested and refined, and stakeholders were invited to register and participate.







<< Results >>

During the project implementation, an innovative online platform called the Virtual Think Tank was developed, along with a training program for employees on implementing measures from the European Green Deal in the postal sector. This training program is available in English as well as in the languages of the partner countries involved in the project. Additionally, four video interviews were recorded, available in English and the national languages of the project partners.

As a result of a three-day LTT activity involving 21 representatives from 5 partner organizations, a teacher's guide was created.

In summary, the main outcomes were:

1. Development of the GreenPosts Assessment Tool: Designed and developed, this tool was tested with 5 employees from partner postal organizations (4). It gathered best practices from European and global postal organizations, which were included in the Synthesis report. After refining the Assessment Tool, it was translated from English into Greek, Bulgarian, and Croatian.

2. Design of the "Implementing European Green Deal in Posts" Course: The course structure was designed, and training material (9 lessons, each comprising four sections: lesson description, training material, PowerPoint, and a quiz) was translated from English into Greek, Bulgarian, and Croatian. The course was piloted by 265 participants, employees from 4 postal partner organizations on the project. (https://vtt.greenposts.eu/login/index.php)

3. Creation of Video Content: Questionnaires and guidelines for video interviews were made. Material for "Peer to Peer Success Stories videos" was recorded and after editing (4 videos), translated into the national languages of the partners alongside English, with subtitles added. These videos were uploaded to the project's YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@GreenPosts.Project) and shared on social media, the project's website (www.greenposts.eu), partner organizations' websites, the EPALE platform, and at multiplier events (4).

4. Development of the Virtual Think Tank (VTT): The VTT's features and content were designed and developed at https://vtt.greenposts.eu/. A handbook and guidelines for using the VTT were created. After testing and refinement, the VTT saw 402 registrations, at least 100 of which were from external (non-partner) organizations connected to the project's theme.

Four multiplier events were held in Croatia (40 participants), Greece (27 participants), Bulgaria (25 participants), and Cyprus (27 participants). Each postal organization (project partners) conducted one in their country, involving relevant stakeholders who weren't project partners.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000028182.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000028182.title: Hybrid Learning Lab for Industry 4.0 Mechatronics
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000028182.summary:
<< Background >>

Recent development in Industry 4.0 has changed industry at global scale. Role of secondary vocational school is to prepare students for this new working environment. We recognized the need for improvements in IVET curriculum for mechatronics at the upper secondary school level. Several relevant needs emerged that can improve the education: 1) Student competences must be incorporated into curriculum: solving challenges, creativity, innovation, entrepreneurial skills, ability to build relationships, advance research. 2) Secondary schools must anticipate and respond in time to fast needs of the industry 4.0 related labour market. The speed of change in companies is getting faster and the ˝shelf life˝ of relevant knowledge is shorter. IVET providers must become more flexible and responsive, renewing their offer according to changes in industry, ensure more freedom in curriculum goals and learning outcomes, offer more personalized learning choices for IVET students, and facilitate peer-to peer learning and mobility.  3) Need for simulating wider use of technology-enabled learning, including combination of physical space and virtual platforms. Increase diversity and volume of collaboration among peers from different EU member states.

<< Objectives >>

1)	Reinforce the capacities of 3 initial IVET centres/ secondary schools for development of curriculum in the field of mechatronics at the upper secondary level in response to fast changing Industry 4.0 related market needs.
2)	Strengthen capacities of IVET teachers from 3 initial IVET centers/ secondary schools for collaboration in the delivery of the curriculum framework.

<< Implementation >>

1)	Comparative analysis of IVET systems in Croatia, Estonia and Portugal was carried out to ensure good quality of curriculum framework for industry 4.0. Report was delivered as Project Result 1.
2)	Short term joint staff trainings were conducted to exchange competences and know-how practices between teachers included in the project. 
3)	Based on outcomes of activities 1 and 2, a curriculum model was developed ˝Hybrid Learning Lab for industry 4.0 Mechatronics˝, or Project Result 2.
4)	Methodological guidelines were developed as Project Result 3.
5)	Pilot- tested the ˝Hybrid Learning Lab for industry 4.0 mechatronics˝ curriculum in IVET centres/ schools in Estonia, Portugal, and Croatia. VET centre/school delivered elective subject to a group of students from different countries, as part of short-term physical student mobility, and exchange of competences between teachers.
6)	Dissemination: project-based web platform was designed, and multiplier events were organized to share the experience about the project development.

<< Results >>

1)	Enhanced competences of teachers and staff from IVET centres/ schools from Croatia, Estonia and Portugal that are included in teaching mechatronics.
2)	Comparative analysis of mechatronics curriculum in upper secondary school level.
3)	Flexible curriculum framework that enables agile and future oriented competence development in mechatronics for Industry 4.0
4)	Methodological guidelines that demonstrate quality factors required for hybrid collaboration between schools and are pilot tested in 3 Croatia, Estonia and Portugal.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000028202.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000028202.title: Art2Business - key entrepreneur and digital skills for future artist
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000028202.summary:
<< Background >>

Our premise is that young artists need to receive education for business skills (entrepreneurship, law, economics, financial management, digital skills, marketing, communication, social network content management, etc) during their high school education so they can have a higher probability of success in making a living practising their art form. Artists can do business through several very different business models, but during their education, they are not even familiar with how to legally sell their work or services. Globally, cultural and creative industries have shown great resilience to crises, so future artists should be well informed about the opportunities offered to them for various types of cooperation in the global marketplace.
Lack of education makes it very difficult for artists to work because they spend too much time gathering information, and often because of ignorance, they work illegally, do not pay taxes, avoid doing business internationally, work without contracts, and so on. Circumstances and market conditions have changed drastically for artists who are unprepared to act professionally in this market. Artists need to acquire a new set of skills to respond to these market changes.

<< Objectives >>

We need to cooperate to improve our artists' influence, impact, and success on the labor market. We also need to share experiences, exchange good practices, and cooperate to transfer our work to higher-level expanding and internationalizing educational activities of institutions and participants. In cooperation with our partners, we produced an innovative vocational curriculum that covers basic knowledge and skills that young artists need for a quality professional start, either as entrepreneurs (freelancers, independent artists, self-employed) or company employees. This innovative curriculum did not exist in any art secondary vocational school in the Republic of Croatia or in the programs of similar high schools in the region (Slovenia, Austria). After its development, the curriculum will be applied more widely than in the Republic of Croatia. It is also applicable in both secondary and higher vocational education and training. The project had the aim to educate: 
- students (in the piloting) to be self-sufficient and self-reliable in running their business careers 
– teachers to implement the materials of the new curriculum to benefit of the students 
- already finished artists in business/IT/digital skills they are curre

<< Implementation >>

During the project, the participating organizations produced, piloted, evaluated, and published a new curriculum consisting of 3 modules covering the topics of entrepreneurial, IT, and communication skills for artists and designers. Partners first analysed the available research, agreed on a methodological framework of the curriculum, produced curriculum outcomes, produced learning and teaching materials, and then piloted the course through LTTA. Throughout the process and especially after the piloting the curriculum has been amended and improved according to evaluation results. The final curriculum document and all learning and teaching materials are published online and have been presented at the final conference in each partner country. Also, all materials are available in all partner languages and English.

<< Results >>

The outcome of the project is a curriculum for the implementation of a new course. Through the project, experts developed a curriculum and learning and teaching materials that educate teachers and students in vocational schools for art and design professions. 
The curriculum consists of 3 modules: 
• Entrepreneurial skills for artists in creative industries 
(1) legal and fiscal framework for artists 
(2) pricing strategy, sales, and negotiation skills 
• IT skills for artists in creative industries: 
(1) setting up a self-promotion website with appropriate content 
(2) webshop implementation 
• Communication skills for artists in creative industries: 
(1) writing an artist statement and creating a portfolio 
(2) relationship building with clients and institutions 
(3) social media presence. 
Modules have been methodically developed, and their content is adapted to the specific needs of students and teachers of art schools who will implement the program. All of these topics are adjusted to the real needs of artists and designers after their graduation, in order to become a part of the labor market. All learning materials are made based on examples and case studies. Piloting of the modules of the new curriculum has been organized as a 5-day LTTA in Maribor with students and teachers from Maribor and Zagreb. The rest of the project activities (transnational meetings and dissemination events) have led to good practices exchange among partners. Teachers and schools gained new knowledge and experiences to improve teaching and learning methods, personal skills improved to ease communication across borders, such as intercultural and language skills. Students participating in the piloting of the project had raised skills and competencies for future careers and this is an advantage position over their peers. During the next years HDLU will use the curriculum and learning materials to produce a series of seminars for artists that will be publicly and permanently available on the HDLU website and video platform.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000033115.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000033115.title: COnscious PEsticide FArming practices with Agricultural High School Students
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000033115.summary:
<< Background >>

Analysis of previous periods (done by Rojas, 2014) showed that global pesticide sales increased by 289% in a period of 10 years only. It was estimated that the World Pesticide Market would grow at an annual average rate of 5% (Anonymous, 2014b), and global pesticide sales would  reach $ 1 million in 2020. over these years, the uncontrolled and unconscious use of chemical drugs caused the chemical control programs to become ineffective. Pesticide derivatives, transformation products, metabolites, degradation products resulting from the use of pesticides in food and agricultural products can cause toxicological pollution. After comperison of curriculae in our partner countries we realized there is little training or proper courses on pesticide management, their proper use and reduction methods. Therefore we were encouraged to firstly raise awareness of the importance of pesticide analyses, secondly to provide methodological tools for its proper and controlled i.e. conscious use. First and foremost among our local communities and young people – highschool students, future farmers and / or landlords.



<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the COPEFA project were to encourage and train Agriculture High School students, particularly those in the food department and future farmers, in several areas related to pesticide use. Firstly, to teach them how to effectively manage the use of pesticides. Secondly, to learn about the potential damages that can result from pesticide use. Lastly, they would be made aware of alternative methods that can be employed to reduce the use of pesticides. Overall, the COPEFA project aimed to equip students with the necessary knowledge and skills to adopt more sustainable and environmentally-friendly farming practices.

<< Implementation >>

The project included 7 work packages (WP), 5 Transnational partner meetings (TPM), 5 Multiplier Events as follows:
WP1 Preparation activities – after project approval the 1st online meeting was organized by the coordinator in December 2021, for the partners to get to know each other, discuss the project details, the roles and responsibilities of partners, timetables, the budget. A presentation has been delivered by Osmangazi Ilce Milli Egitim Mudurlugu (Turkey) representative Oya Gürel, summarizing the main points of the project: objectives, activities, outputs. During the preparation phase the coordinator sent the Partner contracts to every Partner, set up a social media project page (Facebook), created templates for project management, visibility and reporting, a Google drive folder where all relevant project related documents were shared and made available for all partners. The second online meeting was held in January, 2022. At the meeting, the date of the Kick-off meeting, hosted by the coordinator (SšDalj), was set for April 2022. During March 2022, Partnership Agreements were signed, after which the first part of the budget - approved funds - was transferred to the partners. According to the agreement and as stated in the Partnership Agreement, the coordinator transferred the funds to the partners in three payments according to the principle of 40%+40%+20%.
WP2 E-learning module and the COPEFA e-learning platform (IO1) has been developed and set up by the Italian partner IOFA Bagnoregio. IO1 first version was presented during the KICK-OFF meeting in Croatia in April 2022. Due to partner change in the first phase of the project (February 2022), this activity was prolonged and its finalization was delayed. The planned period for WP2 was 02 – 05/2022 but due to necessary changes, translation and finally piloting activities it was completed during the second year of the project. WP2 also included three more online meetings (in May and June 2022) aiming to finalize IO1 properly and according to what was planned and written in the application form. 
WP3 Public Spot: A public service announcement was evaluated by the NA as a not eligible project output and separate WP. 
WP4 Preparing framework for healthy agriculture application: A framework for Good Agricultural Practice mobile application included research, collection and processing of data necessary for the creation of the Framework for the COPEFA mobile application (IO2). All partners conducted detailed research on pesticide usage in their countries, labelled the most used crops, fruits and vegetables and pesticides used in their farming and growing. An excel sheet has been created by the leading partner of WP4 Bilecik Universitesi, Turkiye, who prepared the Framework according to data collected by all partners. The final version was translated to all partners’ languages. The implementation period for WP4 was 05 – 07 /2022 without any delays or problems. 
WP5 Healthy Farming Practices Mobile Application included creation and set up of the COPEFA mobile application (IO4). Leading partner was URE Berlin, Germany. Prior the final version of the app, a beta version of the application and user manual was set up and tested by all partners; terminology and data in the app were meticulously checked before launching to Google Play and Apple Store where it is available for download. The final version has been tested among teachers and students in partner countries. The implementation period for WP5 was 11/2022 – 04 /2023 without any delays or problems. 
WP6 COPEFA Guidebook included collection, ordering, conducting of all relevant project data (basic information, partner info, project results, information on conscious pesticide use in farming, pesticide management pieces of advice), visual design, proofreading of the Guidebook (IO5). Leading partner for this WP was SšDalj, Croatia. After the final version was completed in English, IO5 was translated into all partners’ languages. The implementation period for WP5 was 03 – 05 / 2023 without any delays or problems.
WP7 Pilot sessions and reporting included activities related to piloting project results IO1 e-learning platform and IO4 COPEFA mobile application. IOs were piloted and tested among teachers and students of agriculture high schools in partner countries in Italy, Croatia, Turkiye and Romania. Reports on piloting were mostly conducted as discussions with users in order to collect feedback and if necessary, improve or correct features of IO1 and IO4.  

5 TMPs were organized and implemented: Kick-off meeting in Dalj, Croatia in April 2022 hosted by the coordinator Srednja škola Dalj; TPM2 (public spot advertisement preparation and E-learning
platform evaluation) in Bursa, Turkiye in September 2022 hosted by OMEM; TPM3 (good agriculture practice mobile app framework work and mobile app study) in Bagnoregio Italy in December 2022, hosted by IOFA Bagnoregio; TPM4 (good farming mobile app evaluation and Guidebook study) in Alexandria, Romania in February 2023, hosted by LTNB Alexandria; TPM5 (Evaluating the project results-multiplier event planning, dissemination, final report information) in Berlin Germany in October 2023, hosted by URE Berlin. All documents related to TMPs can be found on this link https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GSISVQZ3jxhbVxAqlU8go1AShvomobKA?usp=sharing

5 MULTIPLIER EVENTS (ME) were organized and implemented during October 2023 – in Croatia hosted by the coordinator, in Italy hosted by IOFA Bagnoregio, in Germany hosted by URE Berlin, in Turkiye hosted by OMEM and in Romania hosted by LTNB Alexandria. MEs were implemented after all project outputs have been finalized, reviewed and all partners evaluated them as successfully completed. MEs were organized according to description in the application form. The coordinator prepared a sample for ME report for all partners to use. The aim of MEs was to disseminate project results in our local communities but also on regional or international level where possible. All documents related to MEs can be found on this link https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Zjt4dAqk0y_eT8sqZ_RMYZW36wjSPDN2?usp=sharing
Project management was implemented throughout the project and included: support for a day-to-day coordination and ensurance of quality of both, the management processes and project results; Project monitoring and Evaluation; communication procedures (internal and external), creation and sharing of visibility materials to be used during the project; exact planning of TPM and other relevant events, reporting instructions (narrative and financial reporting templates); Quality Assurance & Evaluation; Administrative Coordination; to collect and maintain contractual documents (consortium agreement, etc.), to produce periodic reports; document production and archive; Financial reporting.

Monitoring and evaluation was implemented throughout the project, responsible partner was OMEM, Bursa Turkiye. A complete Quality Assurance and Monitoring Plan document has been conducted and shared on the project’s GoogleDrive and can be found on this link https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/16qRjMF1-n7z5MYmv-yzCm588E_w18h1h?usp=sharing

Dissemination of project results and project in general was carried out by all partners on regular basis according to the dissemination plan. In order to keep record of dissemination activities an excel sheet was created by the coordinator and shared on GoogleDrive. Dissemination activities included sharing, testing and evaluation of the e-learning platform and the COPEFA mobile application in the first place among agriculture high school students and teachers but also among the local community and other relevant stakeholders during Multiplier events, Erasmus days, various scientific and educational seminars and fairs, teachers’ meetings, etc. Also, three Newsletters have been created to disseminate the project progress and results. Each partner disseminated the project via promotion of using all intellectual outputs that came out while running the project. The partners used project website and their institution's official website to attract the target groups around. Project activities were disseminated on seminars and presentations in the local community and on regional levels. Even though the coordinator, as applicant organization coordinated the execution of all dissemination activities with the help of OMEM partner , each project partner adjusted the existing or developed their plan of dissemination and exploitation of the project taking in mind the target groups. 
Coordinating partner OMEM with its experience in dissemination in EU projects managed dissemination activities to a great extent. As it is a regional educational public body, they have an official extensive power/status which played a major role in the dissemination activities for the project, nationally and on a European level. Dissemination tools were developed (leaflets, website, Facebook presence, mailing lists of stakeholders) in all partner languages. 
All documents related to dissemination can be found on this link https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ztrJ_oLw15ZjgDARsGXdU9SZVmDOAeZD?usp=sharing









<< Results >>

1. e-learning module has been prepared and COPEFA e-learning platform was set up by IOFA Italy with contribution of all partners; aim of this output was to create a digital tool for teaching and learning about pesticides and methods how to use them more conscious and controlled. The e-learning platform is available in all partners’ languages. Target groups are vocational high school teachers and students but also all interested parties in sustainable agriculture and eco-friendly farming. 
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/187_DbhuaXMBZPjL2CUF8JvnD9_naNsOD?usp=sharing
https://www.copefa.eu/
2. Framework for the COPEFA mobile application has been prepared by Bilecik Universitesi, Turkiye with contribution of all partners. Prior the finalization of this output , a research was conducted by all partners for selected crops and pesticides used in their countries. These research results were incorporated into the final version of the framework.  https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1P9pIbKwL_vLF8Uhaf2MLPX-acFIJgtc3?usp=sharing
3.COPEFA mobile application has been created and set up by URE Berlin, Germany with contribution of all partners. The mobile application is available for Android and IOs and is available on Google Play and Apple Store for download and use in all partners’ languages. Target groups are vocational high school teachers and students but also all interested parties in sustainable agriculture and eco-friendly farming.
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/17Ud4aw2MJsM5ltnPCB3q6T73LM_DGfiO?usp=sharing
4. COPEFA Guidebook was prepared and conducted by Srednja škola Dalj, Croatia with contribution of all partners. It is the final output of the project and summarizes the main points of the project (objectives, partners, project results) aiming to provide information on conscious pesticide management. Target groups are vocational high school teachers and students but also all interested parties in sustainable agriculture and eco-friendly farming. 
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1sKA3hqj3lkNxuHmquJwGYe5ZbWVeRYs_?usp=sharing

2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000033253.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000033253.title: Digital Education on the Farm to Fork strategy
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000033253.summary:
<< Background >>

Although there has been a positive development in the adoption of digital learning solutions in European countries, the Covid-19 pandemic has limited the ability of VET professionals and educators to share their knowledge and provide training, especially in the agricultural and food sectors. Traditional educational techniques in the form of work-based learning and training have dominated this sector for many years, but the growing demand for digital education across Europe is changing this structure. Therefore, the creation of digital education and training materials for sustainable agriculture as part of the Farm to Fork strategy would not only fill the gaps for digital learning, but also accelerate the transition to more sustainable food systems and production practises in Europe. Citizens and actors in food value chains need a change, as current food systems are not able to solve environmental, social, health and food security issues in Europe and elsewhere. It is therefore important to look for innovative solutions to ensure the resilience of both structures. DG FARMER's project would accelerate the transition to sustainable food systems by training and educating professionals and educators

<< Objectives >>

The project will develop a training toolkit (result 1) and a self-assessment (result 2) of trainees' skills in sustainable agriculture in digital form, which will form the main content of the Farm to Fork e-learning platform (result 3). Train and educate VET professionals in the agri-food sector in the use of innovative digital tools; - Promote digital education ; - Promote the Farm to Fork strategy and other EU policies related to agriculture to further disseminate knowledge and education; - Promote practices based on sustainable, smart and inclusive growth of the agri-food sector; - Equip target groups with innovative working tools; - Raise awareness of the systematic link between human well-being and biodiversity conservation. 

<< Implementation >>

Monitoring and evaluation activities: The consortium organized the project planning, implementation and evaluation functions by applying a logic model throughout the project. The basic logic model that will be used in project development defines the following five key areas: Resources/Inputs <lock>></lock> Activities <lock>></lock> Project Outcomes <lock>></lock> Outcomes <lock>></lock> Impact. These five key areas of the logic model are applied to each project activity: 1. activities: The planned project activity and the tasks to be completed are described in detail. 2. Results: The desired/expected results to be achieved as a result of the planned activity are stated. 3. Resources/Inputs: Data and resources required to support the implementation of the activity. These include human resources, expertise, feedback and input from stakeholders, etc. 4. outcomes: Identification of the short and long-term outcomes expected/desired for the activity. 5. Impacts: Description of the long-term impacts expected at local, national, European and international level as a result of the project and how each activity will contribute to achieving these impacts. 
Implementation activities: A Project Steering Committee (PSC) is formed at the start of the project to oversee the progress of the project and consists of one representative from each partner appointed to this project. A project work plan is developed at the beginning of the project to guide the execution of the work throughout the implementation period to ensure that the roles, responsibilities, rights and obligations of the partners are clearly defined and to ensure consensus and clarity within the consortium on reporting processes, technical and financial management, means of communication, decision-making processes, conflicts and other issues. The roles and responsibilities of each partner are formalised and confirmed in comprehensive partnership agreements signed between the lead applicant and each partner. The results managers have been selected on the basis of their expertise, capacity and relevant experience. The lead deliverable manager was responsible for the coordination of activities and allocation of resources as well as for the quality assurance of the deliverable and reports to the project coordinator. A set of specific tools are developed and applied throughout the project duration, including a) a project contact list, b) a project folder on Google Drive.

<< Results >>

The DG FARMER project developed innovative curricula and digital learning methods. More specifically, the project developed a training toolkit and a self-assessment of trainees’ skills in sustainable agriculture in digital form, which form the main content of the Farm to Fork e-learning platform. The following results were achieved: Development of an e-learning toolkit "The Farm to Fork: Towards SustainableAgricultural Systems"; self-assessment of trainees’ sustainable agriculture skills; and Farm to Fork e-learning platform. The following objectives were achieved: - Promote motivation, skills and attitudes to develop sustainable agriculture with regard to the Farm to Fork strategy; - Raise farmers' awareness of the benefits of switching to sustainable food production practices and running an environmentally friendly farm; - Innovate and create a digital learning system for the agri-food sector to improve the quality of education and training; Create an online network for farmers, VET professionals and trainees to collaborate with educational institutions, local authorities and the agri-food industry; - Providing a comprehensive online learning environment linking theory and practice; - Strengthening capacities within partner organizations to promote digital education for sustainable agricultural development and the importance of the "Farm to Fork" strategy; - Raising public awareness of local, unsustainable agricultural production practices and consumption patterns; - Raising awareness of the systematic link between human well-being and biodiversity conservation for European society and economy.
In addition to the outputs, the partners also delivered: - A concrete overall work plan and activity-specific work plans describing all necessary steps and procedures for the smooth implementation of the project (structure, tasks per partner and responsibilities, project milestones, communication arrangements and reporting); - Minutes after each partner meeting, written and submitted by the organization hosting the meeting in collaboration with the project leader; - A quality assurance plan for the whole project process, covering the entire course of the project, to ensure that all activities are carried out effectively and lead to the desired results based on the quality standards agreed in the partnership; - A dissemination strategy with a detailed description of the dissemination tools and activities needed to reach the target groups and a final report on the dissemination activities at the end of the project; - Lists of participants of all local national events; - Project logo; - Production of informative printed material (brochures, posters, etc.); - 4 newsletters were developed after key project milestones in the partners' languages and distributed to relevant stakeholders. - Feedback questionnaires from members of the target group who participated in the local events and trainings; - 5 multiplier events (HR, GR, BE, ES, CY) for the target group and project stakeholders as part of the dissemination and exploitation activities in each country; - Local pilot workshops.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000034642.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000034642.title: Developing Innovative, Modern and Hands-on Digital Teaching Materials with a Focus on Robotics, Cloud and IoT for VET
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000034642.summary:
<< Background >>

The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly reshaped global job markets and economic conditions, leading to a heightened demand for jobs. Data from the World Bank shows that 80% of countries were unprepared for the shift towards digital education brought on by the pandemic, exacerbating challenges in achieving the United Nations' 2030 Sustainable Development Goals, specifically the goal to promote inclusive and sustainable economic growth and employment. The pandemic's disruption of education for 1.4 billion students has also hindered national development goals. 
Our project addresses these challenges by aiming to enhance digital education in the European Union and establish a robust digital education infrastructure for future generations, with a focus on innovation. The primary goal is to identify digital gaps in Robotics, Internet of Things (IoT), and Cloud Computing within Vocational Education and Training (VET), developing corresponding educational materials and an assessment system through interdisciplinary training. 


<< Objectives >>

The main goals of our project focused on enhancing digital education and training within the EU, particularly in response to shifts brought by the COVID-19 pandemic. The project successfully targeted several key objectives:
1) Development of Digital Skills and Innovative Technologies: We aimed to improve the teaching environment through the development of digital skills and the integration of innovative technologies such as Robotics, IoT, and Cloud Computing.
2) Assessment and Feedback: By using innovative assessment methods, we guided students in identifying areas where they lacked skills, thereby increasing their motivation to learn through timely and necessary feedback.
3) Promotion of Distance Education: Recognizing the growing importance of digital education due to the pandemic, we promoted distance education systems to enhance accessibility and continued learning.
4) Vocational Education and Training Enhancement: We focused on promoting continuing VET, ensuring easy access to content through our distance learning platform, and aligning students’ skills with labour market needs.
5) Strengthening Partnerships: The project supported strong partnerships between business and educational institutions

<< Implementation >>

Using the ADDIE methodology  (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation and Evaluation) a range of targeted activities was implemented to achieve our objectives in enhancing the skills and knowledge of VET students and teachers in Robotics, Internet of Things (IoT), and Cloud Computing (R-IoT-C). These activities were carefully designed to support the educational and professional development of our participants at various levels.
1. Transnational Project Meetings (TPMs): We held 3 TPMs (Samobor, Rome, Tenerife)
2. Development and Distribution of Intellectual Outputs (IOs): We developed three key Intellectual Outputs aimed at addressing the needs in R-IoT-C education:
•	IO1: A self-assessment tool to enhance the coding and programming capabilities of students.
•	IO2: Comprehensive learning materials to provide up-to-date content in the project's focus areas.
•	IO3: A Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) that served as a platform for wider dissemination of the course materials and facilitated accessible learning.
3. Multiplier Events: We held 3 Multiplier Events (Spain, Lithuania, Croatia)
4. Evaluation and Monitoring Activities: We established a rigorous monitoring and evaluation framework that included both formative and summative assessments. This framework helped in assessing the effectiveness of the activities and making necessary adjustments. Feedback was collected through surveys, interviews, and direct observations.
5. Dissemination and Public Engagement: Despite challenges with social media engagement, we compensated through active participation in live events such as innovation fairs and external conferences. These activities were crucial in promoting the project outcomes and engaging with a broader audience.
6. Pilot Testing and Implementation of learning materials: Pilot testing of the developed tools and educational content ensured that the materials were effective and met the needs of the target audience. This was complemented by continuous updates and improvements based on feedback from the pilot activities.
7. Collaboration and Networking: The project facilitated extensive collaboration among partners and stakeholders, fostering a network that supported the exchange of ideas, shared best practices, and enhanced the overall quality of the educational offerings.
These activities collectively contributed to the project's success, ensuring comprehensive coverage of educational needs in R-IoT-C technologies and equipping students and teachers with essential skills.


<< Results >>

To achieve our project goals, we've developed several key intellectual outputs:
IO-1: Self-Assessment System: We've created a valid, reliable, and useful self-assessment tool to help students gauge their proficiency autonomously that offers self evaluation test and recommendations in English, Italian, Spanish, Lithuanian, Croatian, Romanian, and Turkish language available on: https://learn.riotc4vet.eu/

IO-2: Hands-On Teaching Materials for R-IoT-C: Innovative teaching materials will be developed in the fields of Robotics, IoT, and Cloud Computing (R-IoT-C). These materials are tailored for future professions and will be compatible with the new evaluation system. These materials are available as books in project results platform in English, Italian, Spanish, Lithuanian, Croatian, Romanian, and Turkish language.

IO-3: E-Learning Platform Development: An e-learning platform was designed to deliver training to Vocational Education and Training (VET) students and beyond, enhancing accessibility and reach. This learning platform offers 105 courses from Robotics, Internet of Things and Cloud computing in English, Italian, Spanish, Lithuanian, Croatian, Romanian, and Turkish language available on MOOC: https://learn.riotc4vet.eu/
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000034896.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000034896.title: e-School bank
2021-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000034896.summary:
<< Background >>

The goal of the e-SB project is to develop a digital platform for vocational schools with education programs for the profession of economist and similar programs that we will use in classes and for the implementation of students' professional practice in the field of banking and finance. In order to achieve this, we needed both intellectual and financial resources, which we received through the Erasmus+ partnership and international cooperation with project teams from Italy and Portugal. With this partnership, we have developed a teaching model that we will use mostly in the subjects Banking, Accounting and Practice Companies. We started the project after seeing the state of the educational system regarding professional economic subjects, which chronically lacks the implementation of practical classes. The previous form of teaching was uninteresting to students, i.e. they were not interested in active participation in classes that did not follow world trends, which resulted in a lower level of professional competence of students and a mismatch with the needs of employers. By implementing project results in secondary schools with education programs for the profession of economist, students will gain concrete practical knowledge.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project results in classes, we enabled schools and students to carry out professional practice in the field of banking and finance, notably to students of secondary vocational schools, in order to develop their professional competencies that they will use in their professional and personal lives. At the organizational level, we enabled the schools participating in the project to gain experience in international cooperation and strengthen their abilities and achieve high-quality innovative results. The students who use these results in class got a sense of real life and work in the financial world by doing professional practice at school. Project enabled them to practice that they never had, since the protection of personal data (GDPR) in financial institutions such as banks, is something that cannot be solved in any other way, that is, banks cannot accept students for practice, nor will they ever be able to because of the confidentiality of their clients' data. Teachers can access students with up-to-date information from the world of finance and banking. We achieve better educational results - students are more motivated to learn, have greater freedom, are more creative, have a better picture of reality...

<< Implementation >>

Through the project, we held numerous development meetings, one meeting in both  partner schools in Lisbon and Molfetta, and one meeting in our school in Dubrovnik. We also held 2 transnational meetings, one kick-off meeting, 3 final conferences, one in each partner country, and Webinars for teachers. Of the transnational meetings, we conducted the first online - First check up meeting, which was attended by almost all members of all teams, 4 members from each partner country and 4 members of the Croatian team. The coordinator of the first CHECK UP meeting was a school from Portugal, and it was held on December 20, 2022 in the duration of 90 minutes. The goal of the meeting was to see how far the implementation of project activities has come, as well as a review of possible difficulties and suggestions for improvement. At the meeting, the students of the school presented part of the work done related to the e-SB application (evidence in the attachment). The tasks and responsibilities of each team for the next period were also revised. The second meeting - Second check up meeting - online - which preceded the preparation of the final meeting in Dubrovnik, the final conferences and the completion of all project results, is a meeting that we used to evaluate what was achieved, finalize all activities and tasks of all teams and plan final conferences, delegate specific tasks for conferences and upcoming dissemination activities in partner countries. We were supposed to hold the third  KICK-OFF meeting at the very beginning of the project, but in the end we held it in Dubrovnik in March 2023 in accordance with all the changes and consents received from the Agency for Mobility and EU Programs. Respecting the date of the meeting, we adjusted the agenda, and the activities at this meeting mostly related to testing the functionality of the program, the application, the compatibility of the application with the program, the texts of the website, and for further coordination of the project implementation and preparation for the final meeting. We held the first development meeting in Portugal in May 2022, then one in Italy in October 2022, and at the very end, the last development meeting - piloting the project and project results in Dubrovnik in May 2023, when we conducted simulations of the finished project results together with all the students who participated in the realization of the project.

<< Results >>

ll the results of the project are in line with the strategic priorities of the Action Plan for Digital Education and the goal of involving students, teaching staff and schools in digital transformation. Likewise, they are in line with the first strategic priority of the Action Plan, the development of a successful digital education ecosystem, by strengthening capacity and critical thinking in secondary education on how to use the possibilities of digital technologies for teaching and learning.
OUTPUT 1 - e-School Bank program (e-SB) is the main intellectual result of the project, it represents an upgrade and an innovative approach to education using digital technologies. The E-SB program, modeled after the programs used by international banks, contains all the bank's departments with accompanying documentation, explanations of individual items and instructions for use. The main purpose of the program is to provide students and teachers of secondary vocational schools with economic programs a platform for the implementation of students' professional practice in the field of finance.
OUTPUT 2 - The e-SB website is modeled after commercial banks, teachers use it in their teaching, and we are continuously updating and improving it.
OUTPUT 3 - e-SB application intended for students as users of banking services. The application was created on the model of commercial bank applications with an emphasis on a user-friendly interface intended for students.
OUTPUT 4 - A digital brochure, one of the main dissemination products of the project, accompanied by an attractive visual identity created by the students of all teams.
OUTPUT 5 - Guide for using the e-SB program and application, will contain detailed instructions for accessing and using the program for
students and teachers.
OUTPUT 6 - Webinar for teachers - intended for the education of school teachers with the aim of better familiarizing teachers with the way the e-SB program works, in order to integrate it into their curriculum and implement it in teaching processes.
Expected outcomes of project activities on organizations: integration of a wider range of learning methods, project-based collaboration, mutual learning, workshops and virtual places for collaboration; capacity building and networking, better information, more competitive position of schools, attracting more motivated students; more modern, dynamic and professional environment within the school, more modern learning and teaching methods. The program fit perfectly into the school curriculum because it included most of the cross-curricular topics; sustainable development (no waste of paper, toner, school materials, notebooks, etc.); expansion of the network of collaborators and partners at HR and EU level, easier finding of new partners for future projects; strengthening of the School's project team, easier development, registration and management of new projects; finances for carrying out all activities, connecting schools and students on a daily basis in the Republic of Croatia.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2021-1-HU01-KA220-VET-000033052.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-HU01-KA220-VET-000033052.title: LEarning And Development in micro- and small enterprises
2021-1-HU01-KA220-VET-000033052.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated to address a critical gap in training opportunities for MSEs, particularly businesses with fewer than 50 employees. While medium-sized enterprises typically benefit from formal or informal training programs, smaller firms, especially micro-companies with up to 9 employees, show little to no participation in such initiatives. This lack of training engagement, both internal and external, is further compounded by a reluctance to accept external advice, which hampers their potential for growth.
Our preparatory research and extensive literature review highlighted a significant supply-side and demand-side failure regarding training offerings for MSEs. It was evident that a pedagogical approach tailored to motivate these companies' owners and managers was required. By developing a targeted project like LEAD, we aimed to bridge this gap and offer a new, innovative solution in the entrepreneurial environment, helping MSEs recognise the benefits of systematic retraining and adopt a forward-looking vision for their companies' development. This project has been crucial in understanding the unique barriers faced by these firms and in providing tailored interventions to enhance their long-term competitiveness-successes

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to gain recognition for the specific training and development requirements of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) at local, national and European levels. A key objective was to differentiate and address the specific attributes of MSEs, including the number of employees, annual income, industry sector, competitive pressures, and their position in the business lifecycle. Our ambition was to provide a multifaceted evaluation of their needs and to develop tailored training and advisory strategies. 

In addition to these theoretical achievements, we sought to provide MSE owners, managers, and external advisors with practical tools through the creation of a comprehensive Handbook and accompanying teaching materials. To validate these resources, we planned pilot training sessions, measuring success through both qualitative and quantitative indicators. Furthermore, the project aimed to disseminate its findings widely across the European entrepreneurial space and demonstrate its long-term value through a robust sustainability plan. Lastly, in light of the impact of the COIVD-19 pandemic, we prioritised digitalisation, enabling a blended curriculum to facilitate international sharing of the results.

<< Implementation >>

The project has delivered a series of activities designed to meet the training requirements of micro and small enterprises (MSEs). Our initial focus was on continued research into SME-related subjects. In particular, we concentrated on the training requirements and motivation strategies required for owners, managers and employees of MSEs. This research led to the first project result (PR1), a comprehensive preparatory study analysing firm-specific training needs. 

Building on the findings of PR1, we have created a Handbook (PR2) for MSE owners, managers, employees, and external advisors. We then created blended learning curricula (PR3), enhancing existing partner institutions' training programmes for MSE stakeholders, including future managers and advisors. To refine the training materials, pilot courses were conducted across partner institutions, and feedback was incorporated into the final curriculum.

Throughout the project, we held six partner meetings and multiple web meetings to ensure continuous management and quality control. In line with the project's national and EU objectives, we implemented a robust dissemination plan, utilising multiplier events, websites, and social media to share results. Finally, we developed policy recommendations to maximise long-term impact.

<< Results >>

The project was successfully delivered, achieving all planned tangible outcomes. The first Project Result (PR1) comprised a comprehensive preparatory analysis of training requirements and advisory strategies tailored to Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs). This analysis distinguished between micro and small firms based on criteria such as size and development stage, thus establishing the basis for subsequent project outputs.

The second output (PR2) was a practical, easy-to-access guide (Handbook) for MSE owners, managers, and external advisors. It addressed their specific training needs and provided strategies to motivate engagement with training provisions. A key result was the development of tailored curricula for two distinct target groups: students (future MSE managers) and current MSE owners, managers, and advisors. These curricula included primarily online courses, with minimal face-to-face elements.

Furthermore, the project generated follow-up recommendations for educational decision-makers to support human resource development in the MSE sector. Finally, a follow-up project was conceptualised to ensure the sustainability of these achievements.

2021-1-HU01-KA220-VET-000034777.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-HU01-KA220-VET-000034777.title: CAP Transfer of Information Via Assessment, Training and Extension
2021-1-HU01-KA220-VET-000034777.summary:
<< Background >>

For the 2021-2027 Multiannual Financial Framework, the European Commission called for the modernisation of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). The new CAP has a key role to play in supporting the European agricultural sector, managing the transition to sustainable food production systems and strengthening European farmers' efforts to contribute to the EU's climate objectives and environmental protection goals set in the European Green Deal, and related strategies such as the Farm to Fork, Biodiversity Strategy and the Organic Action Plan.
In their daily lives, farmers encounter the CAP primarily through subsidies and grants, which often have a decisive influence on their management directions. In many cases, however, they are not sufficiently aware of the rules and conditions for implementing certain measures. As the efficiency and competitiveness of agricultural production can be enhanced in line with higher environmental and agro-ecological standards, for farmers to be able to apply these solutions in a professional, effective, successful and sustainable way, Assessing the farm from an environmental perspective is an essential first step in the transition process.

<< Objectives >>

The main aim of the project was to develop a farmer-centred assessment and training system by connecting the EU's new Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) requirements with proven, innovative, sustainable eco-management practices, in favour of better implementation of the various measures, increased uptake of support, improved efficiency in production and protection of the natural environment.  Our objective was that farmers better understand conditionality, eco-scheme and rural development regulations and their linked undertakings, they choose (supported by a farm assessment tool) and participate in the certain schemes with more responsibility and awareness, carrying out the measures more consciously and effectively.

<< Implementation >>

Project coordination
Project management and monitoring
Activities for intellectual outputs (project results)
Communication and dissemination
Quality assurance
Events and meetings (Learning Teaching Training Activity, transnational partnership meetings, multiplier events, online meetings, and many others)

All activities of implementation are described in the next sections.

<< Results >>

PR1 CAP Eco-Practice Knowledge Base
https://cap-tivate.eu/kb
This module allows users to access information from both angles of finding financial support and implementing good agro-techniques for more sustainable farming. Additionally filling out a short questionnaire at start allows the preparation of the farmer profile, to be reused during the searches for relevant content.

PR2 Eco-Farm Assessment Tool
https://cap-tivate.eu/ead/guide/en
EAD = Eco-farm Assessment and Decision support. The tool is a digital self-assessment approach for farmers and advisors to assess ecological sustainability at farm level, consisting of sustainability indicators that provide information on the current state that can help farmers in their decision-making process. 

PR3 Knowledge Management Platform (IT modules)
https://cap-tivate.eu/
The main goal of developing the Digital Platform is to present a one-stop-shop access to all the other innovative results of the project, and support the exploitation of those results. The digital platform hosts all the web-basd modules mentioned in this section. 

PR4 Learning (OER) modules
https://edu.cap-tivate.eu
The project offers a user-friendly online learning platform that is designed to equip agricultural advisors and farmers with the knowledge and skills they need to implement sustainable practices.

PR5 Methodology and Implementation Guidelines
https://cap-tivate.eu/handbook
The publication was prepared to serve as a guide for practitioners working in the field, including especially farmers, their advisors, as well as other extension workers and supporting experts, to help farmers navigate and make the most of the new Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). The content of the Farmer Handbook was made available in four languages and in various formats, including online document viewer, stand alone downloadable PDF file, and printed hard copy version as well.

2021-1-IE01-KA220-VET-000034787.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-IE01-KA220-VET-000034787.title: Empowering Creative Circular Entrepreneurs
2021-1-IE01-KA220-VET-000034787.summary:
<< Background >>

To provide tailored re-skilling & upskilling for self-employed & unemployed creatives to achieve circularity & address the need for a bespoke VET programme, aligned with the diverse needs of 3 key target groups: TG1: Current & Aspiring Creative Entrepreneurs ECCE - many creatives are self-reliant/small businesses on whom Covid had a devastating impact.  ECCE provides upskilling to embrace the circular economy as a key tool to renew their business, reduce costs & change their relationship with resources & waste in a way that yields a strong economic return. TG2: VET Schools, Enterprise Centres, Networks of Creatives. Fresh content was needed in terms of resilience & sustainability, preparing trainees to future proof their creative businesses. For many, the needs was to understand the circular economy as a subject to be taught & as a practice to be implemented in creative businesses. TG3: Regional & sectoral policy & decision makers, creative & craft networks, & environmental network. The creative sector is often earmarked as a regeneration strategy & leading generator of jobs, economic diversification, & cultural engagement. A cross collaboration approach ensured this would be a greener & more sustainable economic activity.

<< Objectives >>

ECCE was conceived with 4 objectives, all achieved successfully: 
(1) Understand & tackle the weaknesses & strengths of the creative industry, with particular focus on circular economy potential for positive business impact. PR1 achieved via our CREATIVES & JOB OPPORTUNITIES EXPLORATORY PANELS addressing research gaps on specific challenges & opportunities 
(2) Upskill the VET community to train creative entrepreneurs how to explicitly implement circular practices into their own business, while providing the knowledge & skills to people to learn how to start-up their own circular enterprise. PR2 achieved via our Training Course 
(3) Build & maintain connections between creative entrepreneurs, educators & unemployed creatives through intelligence sharing, opportunity giving & mentoring, facilitated by an online platform. PR3 achieved via KNOWLEDGE SHARING PLATFORM & OERS 
(4) Ensuring long term viability & continued implementation of circular models through a ‘Zero-Waste’ Circular Workshop Guide, aiding entrepreneurs to meet regularly & promote their circular businesses to customers & a wider supportive network within business & local government. PR4 achieved via zero-waste marketplace event guide for creative entrepreneurs.

<< Implementation >>

ECCE realised four Results (R1-R4) as well as horizontal activities.  Each partner was assigned leadership or co-leadership of at least 1 result and/or horizontal activity aligned with their specific field of expertise. 

All organisations were involved in all tasks. 

PR1 exploratory panels and research sought to   fills gaps on specific challenges and opportunities of the circular economy for Creative Entrepreneurs in keyimpact areas of circularity and best practice. It was pilot tested with 81 users  from our 3 target groups and downloaded 2351 times, surpassing the target of 400 by over 5 times.

PR2: Circular Economy for Business Training Course is a 6 module  online training course and self assessed learning quiz addressing the business and individual levels and providing knowledge and resources needed for circular transformation of creative businesses. It was user tested by 55 creative businesses and 12 Trainers/Educators. 587 participants have already taken the course (target 500). 
 PR3, A Knowledge Sharing Platform and OERs.  The platform has 66 members and allows direct Peer-to-Peer communication and intelligence sharing. PR3 features more than 30 case studies and relevant articles. 72 users pilot tested the output made up of 45 creatives and 27 educators, to positive feedback.   To date, there were 1550 visitors to the OER page.


PR4: Guide to creating a “zero-waste” circular Market Place is an accessible step-by-step guide that instructs creative entrepreneurs how to run no waste
marketplace events. Partners ran marketplace events in four countries to test the resource, and over 50 user testers provided feedback on the document. The guide was downloaded 774 times and the cases studies downloaded 202 times. 

Active dissemination activities ran throughout the project with all partners contributing resulting in exceeded targets for newsletter reach, social media reach and 38,048 unique visitors to the website.
Quality Management & Evaluation activities were implemented by all partners. while sustainability activities are contributing to the sustainability of the project. 
4 Multiplier events were held with 331 attendees.

<< Results >>

Four PRs & their tasks were 100% achieved. Four national language versions achieved,
PR1 Creatives and Job Opportunities Exploratory Panels.
RLP was responsible for PR1 The Creatives and Job Opportunities Exploratory Panels.  Partners  established four regional think tanks ( Creatives and Job Opportunities Exploratory Panels) in Roscommon, Ireland; Berlin, Germany; Croatia; and Athens, Greece. The formula was to bringi together a panel of creative entrepreneurs, VET educators, those working with the unemployed, creative sector networks and development agencies to share best practice approaches and co-creating solutions that are responsive to real need in the regions. Each country held 3 panel meetings over the lifetime of the project, they1. Researched  the challenges and opportunities faced in their regions and explored.developed action plans on how adapting to a circular economy approach can transform their creative practice and businesses. 
2. Involves creative professionals in developing innovative solutions that will future proof their employability and resilience in the face of potential crises. 
3. Reached out and involved unemployed people to learn and upskill from creative and VET trainers in implementing circular economies in employment or self-employment. 
Roscommon Ireland – The first meeting took place on the 28th April 2022 and there was 26 people in attendance. Individuals from the creative sector, the circular sector as well as policy makers were in attendance. A survey was circulated to the attendees to establish a baseline of knowledge. The results showed how some of the individuals attending were unsure about what circular economy was, while some individuals were carrying out best practices within their business/home life. The second meeting took place on the 14th October 2022 and there was 67 people in attendance. Individuals from the creative and circular sector was in attendance along with policy makers and local media. The focus of Panel meeting 2, was to delve deeper into the collective panel understanding of circular creatives. The meeting included a workshop with Circular Economy expert Carrie-Ann Moran from Circular Fashion Ireland. The Last meeting took place on the 24th February 2023 and there was 29 people in attendance. Individuals from film, tv, gaming, animation, immersive, virtual production, and creative technologies were all in attendance. Panel 3 began with a quick explanation of the circular economy's fundamental principles and key goals as they relate to this digital creative industry sub sector. 
Berlin – Germany – The first meeting took place on the 8th July 2022 and had 8 people in attendance. here were some insights given by the artists, which can be used for the next project results: They were generally not very badly hit by the pandemic as they are anyway not profit-oriented, and they received state help. Indeed, for some of the artists, the pandemic was an opportunity of free time to focus on their own artistic work in an unrestricted way. Information / guide about available funds / prize-competitions is something they would be mostly interested to know about, because ‘fund-restriction’ is usually their biggest challenge. The second panel meeting took place in November 2023 and there was 7 people in attendance. The right host who was well aligned with the topic, therefore inviting participants was easier. The discussions around ‘When is a brand circular’ was encouraging. Metrics such as average no: of times an apparel such a t-shirt is worn and how increasing the average directly contributes to circularity and sustainability was insightful. The focus should be on making sure that • The Products lasts as long as possible • The Products are produced with as less waste as possible and • We know what will happen to the product at the end The Final Panel meeting took place in May of 2023 and had 8 people in attendance. The right host who was well aligned with the topic, therefore inviting participants was easier. Also, the space and location of SLP Galerie provided an advantage by providing the right ambience for people to relate to the topic easily. The discussions started by going around ‘How to implement Circularity in arts’. However, in contrast to the previous panel, this panel naturally gravitated to one of the vital angles of sustainability, which is, financial sustainability. 
Athens – Greece – The first meeting took place on the 24th of may 2022 and there was 22 people in attendance. During the first Panel meeting, the project's background, goals, and the project's vision were presented, along with a broader perspective. Three keynote speakers shared their personal experiences to educate participants about the essence of Circular Creatives. They provided insights into what Circular Creatives entails through their own experiences. 1. Andreas Stefanidis, President of Academy of Entrepreneurship highlighted the significance of entrepreneurial activities in the creative sector in Greece 2. Christos Alefantis from Shedia Art shared When and how the “Shedia Art” project started its operation, what It has to offer and what the future holds 3. PR2 Circular Economy for Creative Business Training Course
