2021-1-IE01-KA220-VET-000034865.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-IE01-KA220-VET-000034865.title: RevitaLESE EU: Revitalising EU Long Established Social Economy Organisations.
2021-1-IE01-KA220-VET-000034865.summary:
<< Background >>

The partnership applied for this project to address a clear need that each of us recognised was missing in our respective countries, and indeed the EU. While there are substantial supports for setting up a social enterprise, and assistance in those early years, there was little support existing for social enterprises and social economy organisations that had been in existence for 5-7 + years. Little is available in terms of ongoing training and supports, or in helping organisations to scale up or modernise (European Commission, A map of social enterprises and their eco-systems in Europe, 2015). Often, it is these Long-Established Social Economy (LESE) organisations that require support to reinvigorate themselves and review their social mission and business model to ensure they can continue to be a successful business. Therefore, the project consortium set about creating a training package aimed specifically at LESE organisations that would assist them in breathing life back into their businesses, reviewing and updating their social mission and their existing business model. 

<< Objectives >>

The goal of this project was to revitalise the European social economy sector & provide support for organisations beyond the startup phase. We did this through the creation of a training programme (PR1), produced an impact report & study of ongoing training needs (PR2) & launched a Europe wide hub of information & resources relevant to the sector (PR3). More specifically, the project set out 5 key objectives:

1. Support LESE organisations to review & update their social mission to be more impactful & adapt their business models to be more effective.
2. Ensure that LESE organisations are ready to adapt to a greener and more digital business ecosystem & lead the way in driving a sustainable economic model that works for people & the planet.  
3. Increase the visibility & understanding of the social economy in Europe & its socio-economic contribution by establishing a LESE EU network & information hub.
4. Research & present how various education stakeholders serving the European social economy can use our model & better support the ongoing needs of LESE organisations through education and training & provide a model for replication.   
5. Build the capacity of partner organisations & stakeholders to support social economy members.

<< Implementation >>

Management activities took place throughout the lifetime of the project. This began at the project inception phase and continued throughout. The lead partner, The Wheel, appointed a project manager for the project to ensure its overall success. From the outset, a Microsoft Teams group was created with all project partners, and this served as our primary communication tool throughout the project. (See Annex 5.20) Partners were able to work collaboratively using a shared SharePoint site which was linked to our MS Teams group. Partners were also able to avail of the private chat function to keep in touch with the lead partners if any issues arose.  

The lead partner set about creating 1 pagers (see Annex 5.22-5.24) on each Project Result before the project officially began. This ensured that partners were able to get a brief snapshot of the project result – who was involved, working days, activities and timeline. Further into the project, these 1 pagers served as useful tools when organisations were going through staff changes and new people were brought into the project.  

The Project Management handbook, see Annex 5.15, was created to coincide with the 1st partner meeting in Athens, Greece. Partners had an input into the document and a conflict resolution framework was created. Following the 1st partner meeting, the lead partner agreed with all partners that it was important to have 6-weekly calls to discuss project updates and progress. Each of these meetings had an agenda, to which all partners fed into and presented various agenda items. See Annex 5.1-5.14. Each transnational partner meeting gathered evidence such as sign in sheets, photos, certificates of participation, presentations and agendas. See Annex 1-Annex 4.  

Financial reporting activities were scheduled into partner work plans from the outset of the project. The lead partner created timesheet templates and quarterly reporting templates, see Annex 5.17 & 5.18, for each partner which corresponded with their working days for each project results. The partners were required to complete their timesheets and quarterly reports every 3 months and submit to the lead partner. The project manager then reviewed the timesheets and quarterly reports and was available to address any questions or concerns that were outlined in the report. The timesheets were then used to ensure partners were completing their required tasks on time and reflecting accurate spending. Timesheets were reviewed by the lead partners Director of Finance also prior to administering partner payments.  

Quality assurance and project monitoring – Knowl SE led on this activity and monitored the project management in consultation with all partners. Surveys were shared with all partners every 6 months and these survey results were then reported on during our 6-weekly online meetings. Partners had an opportunity to rate the overall management of the project, express general thoughts and observations and suggest any ideas for improvements. The lead partner took on all suggestions and addressed them during partner meetings. The results of the internal project evaluation surveys were very positive, see Annex 13.6-13.9. These surveys served as a risk analysis and risk mitigation measure as partners were free to flag any issues in an anonymous way.  

Delivery and management of project results was an important activity during the project. The lead partner ensured that each project result lead established a timeline for their PR and assigned tasks to relevant partners. PR leads then gave regular updates on progress during the 6 weekly online check in meetings. The project manager met individually with other project result leads to ensure they had sufficient support and were adequately resourced to complete their project results. Detailed timelines for each project result were also included in the Project Management Handbook.  

Impact, dissemination and sustainability – these 3 elements were important throughout the project and were discussed from the outset by all project partners. Skills Zone Malta was the dissemination lead and created a dissemination plan and designed all branded materials for use by all partners for the duration of the project. Skills Zone monitored partner progress with dissemination also with the Monitoring Tool, see Annex 12.17. More information about dissemination can be found later in the report. Impact and sustainability was an important aspect of PR2, led by DCU. At the first transnational partner meeting in Athens, partners engaged in conversations about how to ensure the sustainability of the project, beyond the lifetime of the project. Partners felt the alumni network would be key to ensuring the project continues to grow and disseminates. More information about impact and sustainability can be found below, and in the PR2 report. See Annex 7.14. 

<< Results >>

The most successful result of the RevitaLESE project is that 96 long established social economy organisations, across 6 partner countries, have been trained in how to revitalise their social mission and business model. The project contained three distinct project results: PR1: EU Training Modules. The Wheel led on this project result, with input from all partners. Five modules were produced which addressed the needs outlined previously regarding the importance of supporting long established social economy organisations to become more sustainable and innovative to ensure longevity. Each partner conducted a training needs analysis with various LESE organisations in their countries and the results of the TNA allowed for the partnership to tailor the PR1 training modules to the needs of our target audience. Focus groups were then held in each partner country to get a better understanding of the training needs analysis responses. See Annex 6.5-6.9. Attendees of the focus groups were those who had participated in the training needs analysis, all of whom identified as a long-established organisation in their own country. The focus groups were an additional element to the project that the partnership feels really improved our training offering for the social economy. By listening to those who would take part in the training, we were able to tailor it to their needs and ensure the programme could be as impactful as possible.  

Each module consists of a comprehensive, interactive PowerPoint presentation, a lesson plan for the trainer(s) with guidelines and a resources pack. See Annexes 6.10 - 6.15. Online learning and online tools were used in various ways by partners, dependent upon the country and how familiar the audience was with certain tools. Modules 2 and 4 were designed to be half-day online webinars which allowed participants to become more familiar with the online world and collaborating with others outside of their organisation.  

PR1 Module content creation process:  
6-15 July: Prep content plans using the learner outcomes and pedagogical approach   
18-22 July: Module 1 creation   
25-29 July: Module 2 creation (WEBINAR - shorter module)   
1-5 August: Module 3 creation   
8-12 August: Module 4 creation (WEBINAR – shorter module)   
29 August -7 September: Module 5 creation   
8-16 September: Review and finalisation of all modules - implement any outstanding suggested changes   
16 September: Deadline to share 5 modules with partners for review   
26 Sept - 28 Oct: Implement partner feedback to modules. 1 week per module over 5 weeks   
28 October: Deadline to share 5 finalised modules with partners  
See Annex 6.10-Annex 6.15 for the full suite of training materials in English, Latvian, Greek and Croatian.  

PR2: EU Validation, Impact and Sustainability report. Dublin City University (DCU) led on this project result, with input from all partners. This element of the project focused on piloting the training materials created in PR1. Two pilot rotations were held in 6 partners countries. The overall goal was to train 100 LESE organisations and 96 were reached after a successful targeted advertising campaign. After Pilot 1, partners met online and at our third transnational partner meeting in Cyprus to discuss feedback from pilot 1 and suggested changes to create a more comprehensive, well tested training package. Following this meeting, each partner made required changes to their local versions of the training content ahead of Pilot 2. Pilot 2 took place over Summer 2023 over a period of 12 weeks. For detailed information on how each partner ran their pilots, please see Annex 11.1 - 11.6. Data collected from the pilot rotations was then analysed by the project result lead and formed the basis of the Validation, Impact and Sustainability report. Digital badges as a tool for skills recognition were used in this project and their effectiveness and use is outlined in the PR2 report, based on feedback from pilot participants and partners.  

The report was compiled by DCU and reviewed and outlined various elements of the project – the pedagogical approach, learner outcomes framework, and case studies from each partner country illuminating the range of Europe’s social economy. The report also focuses on the current and ongoing needs of LESE in Europe. See report here: https://revitalese.eu/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/RevitaLESE-Validation-Impact-Sustainability-Report.pdf  

Pre training survey, post training survey and post training impact survey were created as part of PR2 and shared with all partners ahead of the pilot rotations. The data and feedback from these surveys was crucial to allow the partnership to improve the training and measure the impact it had on pilot participants. See PR2 report for a full analysis on the impact.  

Digital badges were used to validate learning for all pilot participants. Digital badges were new to all partners, except The Wheel, who led on digital badge creation and management. To gather uniform data from all partner countries, 3 questions were asked per digital badge across all 6 partner countries. A useful learning from our hybrid/blended learning approach for the training was that providing a link to download the digital badge during in person training sessions was not always useful. To provide a solution to this, The Wheel created a RevitaLESE branded QR code per digital badge which allowed pilot participants to easily scan the code with their mobile phone and apply for their digital badge immediately after the training had finished, to provide the partnership with their instant thoughts on that module.  

The testing of the PR1 training materials took place in the PR2 pilots: 
Pilot 1 took place February/March – May 2023 (3 months)   
Partner meeting in Cyprus May 2023 – Pilot 1 was completed by then and discussed. 
June – implement any changes after pilot 1 ahead of pilot 2 kick off   
Pilot 2 took place June/July – September 2023 (3 months)  

PR3: RevitaLESE EU Network and Hub. Social Innovation Centre, Latvia, led on this project result and this element of the project is key to the sustainability of the overall programme. The key aim of this project result was to connect LESE organisations in each partner country with each other to create a self-sustaining network. A website was created, https://revitalese.eu/,  which hosts all project results including the 5 training modules and the EU Validation, Impact and Sustainability Report. The website also contains content created by each partner – 18 blogs, 17 case studies, a project video and 18 podcasts. The EU Hub website contains a wealth of information for the social economy – all content was created by the social economy, for the social economy. All content, including the 5 training modules, available in English, Greek, Croatian and Latvian are freely available on the website and will be accessible for at least 5 years following project completion.  

Website update: with prior approval from the NA, the RevitaLESE PR3 EU Hub and Network is now hosted on www.revitalese.eu This new website allows us to exclusively host RevitaLESE content and allows those interested in our training materials and content to view and download in an easily accessible manner.  

As part of the plans for the RevitaLESE network to be self-sustaining, the partners created a LinkedIn network group for pilot participants across Europe to network and share ideas/ask questions etc. LinkedIn was chosen as a suitable platform as it is well known and utilised in each partner country and most of the social enterprises, we encountered had a presence on LinkedIn. https://www.linkedin.com/groups/14189646/ An interactive map was also created by the partnership and is featured on the project website. https://revitalese.eu/eu-network/ This map allows social economy practitioners to view other organisations across Europe and provides contact details to enable networking and possible future project collaborations.  

In addition to the LinkedIn network group, the partnership also created a LinkedIn Pilot Trainers group. This was a private group for those who had taken part in the train the trainer event in Croatia to keep in touch while running the pilots in each partner country. This proved a useful tool as trainers could update each other on what went well in each module and what activities pilot participants really enjoyed. Throughout the project, a key component was networking and partnership building. To further enable this, each partner held networking sessions in their countries and the partnership held an international networking session to encourage collaboration. See Annex 8.9 for an overview of the networking meetings. 
Finally, to celebrate the success of the project, the PR3 lead led on creating a project video which outlines the project results, partners and resources created. This video is available to view on the project website, with subtitles in each of the 4 partner languages. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5hHc6MNTJwA&t=1s  

The overall outcome of the RevitaLESE project was realised through all three project results, in combination with other project activities such as: training, multiplier events and project management activities. LESE organisations that took part in the programme remarked: ‘The content was brilliant and very relevant to the work I do’. ‘Each session was interesting and gave me knowledge and tips I can use in my daily working life.’ ‘I enjoyed every session; the trainers were experts and gave me tips to use for my organisation.’ ‘The group work provided a wonderful opportunity to learn from each other and spark off each other and think in different ways.’ 

The RevitaLESE project has ensured that the social economy is better understood and more easily recognised in each partner organisation and pilot participant organisation. Training has been made freely available for long established social economy organisations across Europe and the partnership views the creation of the RevitaLESE EU hub as crucial to the success of the project long term.

2021-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000032987.title: Valueable Safety at Work
2021-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000032987.summary:
<< Background >>

WHY THIS PROJECT 
People with intellectual disability -ID- (0,1% of EU citizens) are discriminated and marginalised. Pandemic has worsened their condition and their digital exclusion is even more evident. The e-learning about Health and Safety at work, developed whitin this proposal and included in the set of tools aimed at supporting a successful job inclusion, helped them to get basic skills at home or at the training centre with their tutors, increasing their employability also with a facilitated access as trainees or workers in the hospitality companies of the Valueable network, with internships duly prepared and managed. 
NEEDS ADDRESSED 
When employed, workers with ID are among the most vulnerable. There are almost no examples of Health and Safety training being provided to workers with ID in a manner they can understand. Vocational training for people with ID has been carried out exclusively through face to face or on the spot activities. The lock-down period has highlighted how the time "suspended" both in training and at work could be quickly turned into digital mode. However, people with ID have been struggling to cope with the poor or total lack of accessibility to digital education, particularly in vocational training.

<< Objectives >>

OVERALL OBJECTIVE
Promoting the social and professional inclusion of people with intellectual disabilities especially, but not only - in hard times of pandemic, when they risk to be further marginalised. 

PURPOSE
Enhancing the access of at least 84 European trainees/workers with ID to VET and employment in the hospitality sector, through a tailored and digitalised vocational training spread by the Valueable network.

<< Implementation >>

ACTIVITIES
1) Design and development of the e-learning course on “Health and safety at work” in easy to understand format, addressed to (potential) workers with ID and available in 8 languages (English, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Croatian, Hungarian, Turkish).
2) Field testing of the e-learning course by trainees/workers with ID, through internships and/or job placements at Valueable hospitality companies on a local level and abroad. 

METHODS
1) Development of the PROJECT RESULT: background analysis, design of the structure of the course and presentation at the kick off meetinting to the consortium, shared development of the prototype of the course, readability analysys of the contents of the course through Readability Analyzer, digitisation of the course in e-learning, field testing and its evaluation, final release of the e-learning course. 
2) TESTING through internships and work experiences of people with ID at local level (minimum 3 months) and abroad (3 weeks), in hospitality companies, with decreasing tutorship. 
3) VOCATIONAL TRAINING ACTIVITIES which: a) deploy digital tools and methods to deliver quality and inclusive education (e-learning course in easy to uderstand language) b) incorporate digital online technology into subjects pecific (health and safety at work) training and work-based learning.
4) Use of easy-to-understand (ETU) resources for people with ID. English ETU contents of the e-learning course have been analysed through the Readability Analyzer  a specific software, to measure contents readability, usability and accessibility by the most commonly indexes used for analyzing English-language texts, such as: Flesh Reading Ease and Gunning Fog Scale Level (both indexes examine the number of syllables and sentence length), SMOG Grade (concerning the number of years of education required to comprehend the text under consideration) and Dale-Chall Score (dealing with lexical complexity, based on a corpus of words that can be defined as simple).

<< Results >>

PROJECT RESULT 
The e-learning “Health and safety at work” course, in easy-to-understand language/format, in 8 languages (English-master,
Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Hungarian, Croatian, Turkish), tested by 132 people with ID (expected: 84 people with ID, meaning 12 testers with ID per 7 VET provider) and 30 tutors, from 9 European countries (Italy, Spain, Portugal, Germany, Hungary, Croatia and Turkey which are all part of the consortium, plus Ireland and Malta who joined the extented testing).

OUTCOMES AND IMPACT
People with ID: a) increased empowerment, b) increased digital skills, c) increased job inclusion opportunities. 
VET providers: a) increased competences in supporting job inclusion of ID workers, b) increased digital educational skills.
Hospitality companies: increased knowledge and awareness on ID-related issues. 

LONG-TERM BENEFITS 
a) Long-term more effective VET of people with ID. 
b) Long-term improvement of attitudes of different stakeholders (hospitality managers and entrepreneurs, employees and citizens in general) towards people with ID.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000033291.title: U-Mar - Enhancing underwater archeology to make it an innovative tool for developing sustainable & creative tourism
2021-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000033291.summary:
<< Background >>

From the need assessment on the enhancement and promotion of underwater archaeological heritage and the creation of sustainable underwater archaeological tourism products, carried out by the LP and PPs prior the project drafting, a number of shortcomings and gaps were observed. While the valorisation of tourism connected to underwater cultural heritage can bring benefits from an economic point of view and its development is closely linked to the preservation of the environment and the seas, the assessment of the current situation in underwater archaeological sites highlighted the low specialization/training of cultural operators and the absence of experts with knowledge on how to create underwater archaeological itineraries. In fact, operators' competences are limited to the interpretation of the heritage and the collaboration with diving centres, but they lack of skills on the management, valorization and capitalization of these sites. 
All PPs, therefore, shared the need to work on a project to tackle these gaps by developing an innovative training course and new methodologies to create Underwater Archaeological Heritage Interpretation Centres on land, to make this heritage more accessible and closer to a wider audience. 

<< Objectives >>

The general aim of the project U-Mar was to develop the knowledge and the enhancement of heritage related to underwater archaeology, through the following specific objectives: 
1) Training professional figures with specific skills in underwater archaeology, how to valorize it and how to manage these cultural sites. The project trained new experts capable of fostering the touristic offer of these sites from multiple points of view, thanks to an ad hoc innovative training course. 
2) Developing sustainable and environmentally friendly tourism around underwater archaeology, improving the tourist-cultural offer and expanding the reference target of users. 
3) Provide guidelines for organizations that want to develop strategies for enhancing the underwater archaeological heritage, with different possibilities of application depending on the context and with a particular focus on the creation of underwater archaeological itineraries, with their specific heritage and on the professional’s skills required. 
4) Increase knowledge of the underwater archaeological heritage and the importance of its conservation and enhancement, not only by tourists, but above all by young people and
local communities living in those territories. 

<< Implementation >>

The project objectives were achieved through the implementation of the following activities, organized into WPs:
WP1 - PROJECT MANAGEMENT - Coordination, technical & financial management 
WP2 - NEW TRAINING COURSE ON UNDERWATER ARCHAEOLOGY FOR CULTURAL OPERATORS - Implementation of one Transnational Training for Trainers for the development of a New Innovative Training Course on underwater archaeology for cultural operators and the realization of 5 on-site testing training in PPs’ countries 
WP3 - DEVELOPMENT OF U-MAR E-LEARNING PLATFORM – Assessment & research activities, followed by the technical design of the Platform and a confrontation phase with stakeholders. Information was then collected and materials/contents uploaded on the Platform, making it ready for the launch.
WP4 – CREATION OF INTERPRETATION CENTRES ON UNDERWATER ARCHAEOLOGY – Starting from a Research on the state of art and collection of inputs/materials, PPs’ defined the learning pathways and storytelling, ending in the set up of the Interpretation Centres 
WP5 - COMMUNICATION AND DISSEMINATION – Transnational & Local dissemination plans were realized, followed by the- implementation of the set communication activities and the organization of 5 multiplier events. 

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results of the U-MAR project are:
R1. The creation of the NEW TRAINING COURSE on underwater archaeological sites for cultural operators. 
Explanatory videos were made for the first 6 learning units; for the 7th one, related to legislative topics, a descriptive pdf was made.
R1.1. 5 on-site training courses, one in each PP country, to test the new realized training course 
R2. The E-LEARNING PLATFORM to access the U-Mar NEW TRAINING COURSE on underwater archaeological sites for cultural operators. 
The U-Mar platform, in addition to a general overview of the project itself, offers information on specific training opportunities on underwater archaeology in partners’ countries; on tourism offers to discover underwater archaeological itineraries in the various project partner countries; on best practices identified during the Project which have been included in the course.  
R3. The development of INTERPRETATION/LEARNING CENTRES on Underwater Archeology, one in each partner country, located along the Phoenicians' Route - Cultural Route of the Council of Europe. 
Thanks to these 3 main results, the project also: 
- laid the groundwork for the formalisation of a specific training course for those who work or want to work in underwater archaeological sites, to be included in vocational training programmes or in other training institutions (already done by partners CEIMAR in Spain and ICUA in Croatia). 
- Promoted the accessibility of underwater sites to all types of visitors through the enhancement of digital tools.

2021-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000033335.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000033335.title: NEXT-MUSEUM: Stimulating digitization at small and medium-sized museums through the enhancement of the Digital Curator
2021-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000033335.summary:
<< Background >>

NEXT-MUSEUM was conceived in the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic as a response to overcome the difficulties encountered in the museum field. In particular, the proposal aimed to support small and medium-sized museums in their digital transition through the professional figure of the Digital Curator. The main addressed needs are summarised in: 
-Partner universities involved in supporting local cultural actors in cultural promotion initiatives were interested in working on the concrete application of digital tools to the cultural promotion sphere of small museums, and also to incorporate it in the expertise of their departments; 
-Partners with non-academic profile who directly manage exhibits and cultural initiatives in museums (FMC, NMZ and ALICANTE) were looking at 
elaborating and testing digitization strategies more oriented to the external promotion of the museum and in particular to audience involvement activities, expanding the direct competences of museums’ staff; 
-External museums and cultural professionals involved in the action needed to identify tailored strategies to exploit simple, user-oriented technologies and develop targeted competencies to identify, assess and respond to the developing challenges in the CCS.

<< Objectives >>

The action has set the general objective to provide small and medium-sized museums with a new generation of specialized EU professionals working in the CH sector, equipped with a recognised, cross-cutting and high-level digital skillset: the Digital Curator (DC). 
By working both at museums’ institutional levels and at target beneficiaries’ (professionals) level, the specific objectives of the project have been to: 
1) encourage the digitisation of cultural heritage in the management of small and medium-sized museums; 
2) improve the digital skills of museum professionals specifically related to cataloguing and resource management 
3) improve the digital skills of museum professionals specifically related to heritage promotion, storytelling, and public accessibility 
4) provide a model for museum organizations that want to approach digitalisation along two main paths: (a) instruments and resources for the digital training of museum operators; (b) Strategies for the exploitation of digital resources to broaden visitor experiences 
5) encourage and test public involvement in digital initiatives undertaken by participating museums, all while assessing the theoretical skills of digital curators in the field. 

<< Implementation >>

MUSEUM-NEXT has implemented activities on 4 main levels: 
- Background research and desk analysis oriented to the production of Guidelines for the adoption and proper use of digital technologies 
- Transfer of knowledge in museum digitalization by means of a transnational training for digital curators for exchange of competences and mutual upskilling, followed by 3 local training activities organised in the museums targeted by the project in Italy, Spain and Croatia; 
- Design and implementation of pilot testing actions in the 3 targeted local museums, which were conceptualised during the local trainings thanks to the transfer of knowledge from the transnational training and the customisation of skills; 
- Elaboration of a strategic vision for the 3 museums targeted by the project for a digital transition plan, by means of defining a DOP-Digital Operational Plan for the adoption of digitization in small and medium-sized museums.

Communication and dissemination activities have also been carried out all through the project implementation for target engagement, audience reach and capitalisation of produced results. 

<< Results >>

NEXT-MUSEUM produced: 
R1-Guidelines for the adoption and proper use of digital technologies, an in-depth analysis of the state of  art on digital transition, best EU practices, available VET opportunities, SWOT analysis of 3 targeted museums. 
R1 contributed to: raise awareness on the professional figure of Digital Curator;a shared overview of the most adequate tools and strategies to be used by Digital Curators in small-scale museums.

R2-Open pilot actions in the 3 targeted museum using digital tools & technologies. Scientific projects have been produced to illustrate the context, as well as a joint training report of all learning activities that led to their design. 
R2 contributed to: streamline target museums’ digital literacy and expand the cultural offer;mitigate Covid-19 negative effects;stimulate employment of Digital Curators;increase audiences’ accessibility to culture. 

R3-Digital Operation Plan for the adoption of digitization in small and medium-sized museums, which contributed to: support the recovery of small/medium museums;a shared vision for the increase of digital competencies in local museums;disseminate awareness on Digital Curation and the integration of digital museum planning in multilevel governance.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2021-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000034836.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000034836.title: DIGICULT – Cultural Heritage: a source of resilience and learning through digital education
2021-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000034836.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to address the challenges in the cultural sector caused by COVID-19; the pandemic highlighted the need for innovative practices in promoting, communicating and accessing cultural knowledge and it uniquely impacted VET systems. Our goal was to create an e-learning pathway for VET learners integrating digital tools, cultural heritage and environmental awareness, aligning with EU Commission and SDGs goals. 
The project matched our mission of enhancing education through digital transformation, multidisciplinary approaches and international cooperation. DIGICULT allowed us to develop and implement new educational methodologies, leveraging our expertise in digitalization and cultural education.
Key needs addressed by DIGICULT:
• Youth empowerment and skills development for VET learners
• Professional development for trainers with new tools and methodologies
• Enhancing digital literacy and cultural awareness among learners
• Promoting environmental awareness and sustainable practices
• Preserving and promoting cultural heritage through digital technologies
• Fostering international cooperation and exchange of best practices
DIGICULT aimed to bridge cultural heritage, digital transformation and environmental sustainability.

<< Objectives >>

Our overarching goal was to create synergies between cultural heritage and digital education to enhance VET overall effectiveness and impact. 
We aimed to achieve several key specific objectives:
• Implementing an innovative educational pattern that serves as a replicable model, addressing challenges in the cultural sector.
• Designing and implementing innovative practices for the promotion, communication, access and transmission of knowledge.
• Focusing on digital and green transitions to align with the Council Recommendation on VET for sustainable - competitiveness.
• Addressing the increased awareness of the need for technological improvement in both VET and cultural heritage sectors brought about by the COVID-19 crisis.
• Ensuring cultural heritage remains a source of resilience, inspiration, joy and solidarity, even when experienced remotely.
• Developing innovative learning methods and empowering guidance services to help individuals adapt to new labor market requirements.
• Preparing VET trainers and learners for new roles in the digital era, fostering resilience and readiness for personal and professional life.

<< Implementation >>

With the valuable cooperation of all partners, all activities were implemented and the planned results produced, albeit with some minor changes to the implementation schedule.

PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION (more details in the specific section)
In the initial phase, the project coordinator - CIOFS - drafted the Project Management Plan, aimed at ensuring the successful initiation, implementation and termination of the project, providing for the financial and administrative management of the project, monitoring and problem management. This plan was reviewed and updated, in collaboration with all partners, during the development of the DIGICULT project. 
The 2 project governance bodies - the Coordination Unit (composed of two representatives from CIOFS, 1 from TDS and 1 from FAI) and Steering Committee (composed of 1 representative from each partner organization) - were also formed at the beginning of the project. Over the 30 months of the project,  numerous Coordination Unit meetings were held in order to facilitate the management of the grant, supervise and monitor the progress of the project, direct the progress of the work toward the objectives, ensure compliance the project schedule and optimize the overall impact, plan the internal communication and policy processes. During each transnational meeting, Steering Committee (SE) meetings were held regularly. There have also been extraordinary meetings of the SE in order to address urgent matters and make timely decisions.

FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT AND BUDGET (more details in the specific section)
Budget and time monitoring have been regularly conducted by CIOFS, which collects semi-annually an activity and financial report from each partner. These reports illustrate the activities carried out, the results achieved, and the costs incurred, including a breakdown by type of activity and a justification of the total expenses, linked to the resources used and the activities performed.

TRASNATIONAL PROJECT MEETINGS (more details in the specific section)
All scheduled project meetings have been carried out: 11 transnational project meetings, including on-line kick-off meeting,  3 meetings in-person (1 in Dublin-IE and 2 in Turin-IT) and 8 remote meetings. It should be noted that 1 of the planned remote TPMs was conducted in-presence for the reasons given below.

COMMUNICATION AND DISSEMINATION STRATEGY  (more details in the specific section)
TDS was the responsible partner and as such organized everything necessary for communication activities both within the partnership and externally to the target groups. From the beginning, the CIOFS project manager has provided the partnership with an online repository that has been a crucial virtual place for the development of the entire project. All partners has free access to the repository, which proves to be a key tool for ensuring transparency and immediacy of materials and information.
The main communication activities of TDS and the project partners were:
• presentation of communication activities
• communication and dissemination plan 
• digicult logo and visual guidelines
• digital forms
•  website
•  e-brochure
•  social media management (facebook, instagram, linkedin)
•  qualitative questionnaires on communication activities
•  press releases
•  participatory events
•  semi-annual communication reports.

INTERNAL MONITORING/EVALUATION (more details in the specific section)
In order to ensure the quality of all tasks performed, an Evaluation and Quality Plan was created by IZTZG and approved by the Consortium, at the beginning of the project. Every 6 months each partner completed a specific Internal Monitoring/Evaluation questionnaire.
IZTZG prepared the planned evaluation reports, gathering information and data from partner reports. For the external evaluation, IZTZG created an external evaluation questionnaire and guide.

PROJECT RESULTS
DIGICULT was implemented through a structured approach consisting of three distinct phases, each supervised by continuous evaluation activities. These phases were subdivided into specific activities aimed at achieving targeted tasks and precise project outcomes.

Phase 1 TOWARDS AN INNOVATIVE CURRICULUM FOR THE CULTURAL HERITAGE DIGITAL EDUCATION 
Project Result 1 DIGITAL CULTURAL HERITAGE: AN INNOVATIVE CURRICULUM 
Phase Leader: UNIC. 
Participating Organisations: CIOFS, TDS, FAI, eMundus, NCK, IZTZG and BJC.
• Activity 1.1: definition of the training methodology, identifying best practices and innovative curriculum so as to manage the challenges of a digitally-empowered education system. Task leader: UNIC. 
• Activity 1.2: developing the strategy on how to welcome learners with cultural needs in a digital context. Task leader: TDS.

Phase 2 IMPLEMENTATION AND VALIDATION OF THE E-LEARNING DIGICULT PATHWAY 
Project Results DIGICULT E-LEARNING PATHWAY AND VALIDATION
Phase Leader: CIOFS. 
Participating Organisations: TDS, FAI, UNIC, DIGIPRO, eMundus, NCK, IZTZG and BJC.
• Activity 2.1: creation of the content of the training modules and labs on the most innovative key areas, identified by partners, as relevant for developing new digital, methodological/relational competences as well as specific knowledge and skills. Task leader: BJC. 
• Activity 2.2: development of digital educational resources for modules and labs in different formats (e.g., webinars, video-recordings, case studies, slides, e-books, articles, work projects and role-play) suitable for testing the DIGICULT pilot course. Task leader: UNIC. 
• Activity 2.3: piloting e-learning pathway and finalisation of the modules + mobility activities. Task leader: CIOFS.
• Activity 2.4: validation carried out by means of qualitative observation and feedback during the course, as well as specific evaluation. A report was  issued documenting the areas of improvement and the strengths of the course contents and the eLearning platform. Task leader:  eMundus.

Phase 3 CREATION OF THE DIGICULT EDUCATIONAL GAME 
Project Result DIGICULT EDUCATIONAL GAME
Phase: DIGIPRO (supported by FAI, TDS, UNIC and eMundus  in GAME development). 
Participating Organisations: FAI, TDS, NCK, eMundus, CIOFS, BJC, IZTZG, UNIC (from January 2024 replacing NCK  in GAME development)
• Activity 3.1: Design of the DIGICULT educational game. Gaming techniques were applied to cultural heritage: not only it created something fun but it also inspired creativity, engagement and even social change. A selected group of VET learners vas called to contribute, through piloting, to design the DIGICULT educational game, which is centred on the development of contents and competences acquired during the DIGICULT pathway. Task leader: DIGIPRO (supported by FAI, TDS, eMundus, UNIC instead of  NCK).
• Activity 3.2 - Realisation of the DIGICULT educational game. Starting from the initial idea, DIGIPRO developed the contents and the design of the gaming activities. It is declined in the form of an educational game, a quiz format, which includes questions to be answered in order to test the users. It also include a scoreboard to motivate them. Questions are displayed in text, images and several add-ons. The game is released in a nonlinear form so users can jump from stage to stage. Task leader: DIGIPRO (supported by FAI, TDS, eMundus, UNIC instead of  NCK).

The project methodology emphasized maximizing learner engagement through alternating meetings and practical activities. This approach allowed participants to immediately apply acquired skills. The use of digital tools, such as an e-learning platform, social networks and the creation of digital outputs (e.g., the design of a virtual game), was integral in enhancing practical involvement and fostering professional development.
To ensure the long-term sustainability of DIGICULT, the consortium committed to making all educational resources, materials and tools available on an open-source platform. This platform will be linked to partners' websites and its impact will be amplified through promotion, dissemination and application in various contexts.

LTTAs
LTTAs C1 and C2 were implemented as planned and detailed below.

MULTIPLIER EVENTS
3 events were realized in Lithuania (instead of 1) and a final event in Italy, both in presence and streaming as detailed in the specific section.

<< Results >>

The DIGICULT project has achieved several concrete results:
• Development of an innovative e-learning pathway: DIGICULT has created an engaging e-learning platform that focuses on developing disciplinary, key and life skills. This platform enhances learners' competencies in areas such as communication in mother and foreign tongues, digital literacy, social and civic competencies, initiative and entrepreneurship and cultural awareness, aligning with the recommendations of the European Commission and the European Council.
• Integration of technology in Vocational Education and Training: the project has improved the use of technology in VET by adapting pedagogies to develop digital skills and encouraging greater interaction with technology. This includes the use of alternative, inclusive learning channels that are flexible and adaptable to new contexts.
• Enhanced learning and teaching practices: through the innovative e-learning pathway, DIGICULT has promoted more efficient learning and teaching practices. Trainers and teachers have experienced a new mixed teaching approach that integrates digital tools, foreign languages and learning-through-practice methodologies.
• Engagement of young people at risk: the project has effectively motivated learners, including those at risk of leaving school, by transforming their knowledge and passion for digital tools such as video games and social media into skills useful for their professional future.
• Collaboration with partner countries: this collaboration has allowed learners to acquire additional skills and exchange views, thereby broadening their perspectives and enhancing their learning experience.
• Strengthening digital and technological skills: DIGICULT has focused on strengthening the digital and technological skills of "digital natives," particularly within the context of cultural heritage. This has made learners more aware of the impact of digital technology in this field.
• Promotion of resilience and digital competences: the project has increased learners’ resilience by promoting and implementing competences necessary for digital transformation in the cultural heritage sector.
• Enhanced engagement with cultural heritage: DIGICULT has enhanced the digital possibilities for learning and engaging with cultural heritage, making it more accessible and engaging for learners.
• Equipping beneficiaries with new skills: the project has equipped its beneficiaries with new life, technical, pedagogical, and creative skills, preparing them for future challenges and opportunities.
• Increased awareness and use of European cultural heritage: DIGICULT has encouraged a broad and conscious use of European cultural heritage in VET, increasing awareness among VET learners and trainers in the field of culture and cultural heritage.
• Sustainable and lasting impact: the project’s results are designed to have a lasting impact at local, regional, national and European levels. All project outputs will remain available to stakeholders, ensuring the continuity of DIGICULT and serving as a resource for future actions.
• Contribution to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): DIGICULT contributes to the United Nations 2030 Agenda by addressing several Sustainable Development Goals, including quality education (Goal 4), gender equality (Goal 5), decent work and economic growth (Goal 8), responsible consumption and production (Goal 12), and partnerships for the goals (Goal 17).
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-MK01-KA220-VET-000024929.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-MK01-KA220-VET-000024929.title: Interoperability of Qualifications -by building Sustainable Digital credentials Infrastructure
2021-1-MK01-KA220-VET-000024929.summary:
<< Background >>

To contribute at interoperability of qualifications, and respond to the new world of globalization and technology, by:
- Developing and adopting common methodology for modular learning, based on learning outcomes and micro-credentials
- Participate in European Digital Credentials Infrastructure, developing under Europass platform
Both needs are identified as one of its 12 flagship actions In the NEW European skills agenda, published on 1 July 2020, to support the quality, transparency and uptake across the EU:
 Action 10: A European approach to micro-credentials
 Action 11: New Europass platform
And are parts of Communication for achieving the new European Education area by 2025.
This project contributes at standardization and quality, in the field of VET and AE education.

<< Objectives >>

Main objective of this project is: Contributing to the quality assurance in VET and AE, by adaptation of private VET/ AE providers to the sustainable model of certification based on micro credentials, and introduction of digital tool for issuing digital certificates, compatible with the Europass Digital Credentials Infrastructure (EDCI), with full implementation of the standards, modules and credits for qualifications and trainings they provide. 

SO1 Adopting common principles and methodologies in regular work of AE/VET providers, to enable interoperability of qualifications;
SO2 Improve quality standards at AE/VET providers on European level;
SO3 Introduce digitalization in systems for certification; and
SO4 Facilitate validation of non-formal and informal learning.

Target group are VET and AE providers (non-formal) across the Europe, beneficiaries of their services, practitioners and policy makers in the field of VET and AE and wider all stakeholders active in those fields.
The project aims, VET and AE providers to go digital, minimize the need for paper documents and issues all documentation directly to the learners’ portfolio. 

<< Implementation >>

A. Project Management Activities

Our project implemented range of project management activities to ensure successful coordination and execution. These activities included:
- Coordination of the project and establishment of communication mechanisms among partners.
- Clear division of tasks and responsibilities among partners.
- Organization of events, activities, and provision of operational capacity.
- Provision of logistics and proper documentation.
- Project administration, reporting, budget planning, and cost management.
- Selection of experts and participants.
- Ensuring quality in implementation.

B. Implementation Activities
1. Transnational Project Meetings
The project delivered two physical meetings and 12 online meetings (10+2) for project partners. These meetings facilitated collaboration, discussion, and decision-making.
2. Project Results
PR1: Mapping of applied methodologies in developing existing curricula of accredited trainings at AE/VET providers and creating a benchmarking report with recommendations for developing a common methodology.
PR2: Research and development of a common methodology for adapting existing curricula to modular learning based on learning outcomes and micro-credentials.
PR3: Establishing infrastructure for digital certification compatible with the Europass model and digital credentials.
PR4: Developing guidelines for VET/AE providers on how to introduce the micro-credentials digital credential model into their certification systems.
PR5: Creating policy recommendations for improving national systems for quality assurance in VET and AE by implementing standards and principles from European models.
3. Multiplier Events
We conducted five multiplier events, per one event in each participating country and one online event in cooperation with the All Digital Network, involving a wider international community.

4. Learning, Training, and Teaching Activities
Joint Staff Training 1: Training on implementing a common methodology for curricula development based on learning outcomes and micro-credentials.
Joint Staff Training 2: Training on integrating a digital certification system into the regular work of AE/VET providers.

C. Monitoring and Evaluation Activities
Monitoring and evaluation infrastructure was established at the first transnational project meeting. A "Quality Management Plan" with clear qualitative and quantitative indicators was adopted at the start of the project. All partners were responsible for checking, controlling, and fulfilling tasks to achieve these indicators.

D. Dissemination Activities
An extensive dissemination strategy was implemented to optimize the project's value, strengthen its impact, and transfer its achievements to other contexts.

<< Results >>

Main Outcomes

The IQ-DigitS project achieved significant measurable and intangible outcomes during its implementation phase.

Measurable project results:
PR1: Prepared and published the "Mapping of applied methodologies in developing existing curricula of accredited trainings at AE/VET providers" and a benchmarking report with recommendations for developing a common methodology.
PR2: Developed, published, and implemented a common methodology for adapting existing curricula to modular learning based on learning outcomes and micro-credentials.
PR3: Established and implemented infrastructure for digital certification compatible with the Europass model and digital credentials.
PR4: Created and published guidelines for VET/AE providers on introducing the micro-credentials digital credential model into their certification systems.
PR5: Prepared and published policy recommendations for improving national systems for quality assurance in VET and AE by implementing standards and principles from European models.
Trained staff on implementing the joint methodology for curricula development based on learning outcomes and micro-credentials.
Trained staff to integrate the digital certification system into regular work.

Intangible results of implementation activities:
- Improved transparency and quality standards of VET/AE providers.
- Enhanced strategic and cross-sectoral cooperation among different VET and AE providers across Europe.
- Increased internationalization of European VET and AE providers.
- Higher flexibility and opportunities in VET and AE.

Measurable results of project management:
- Developed a communication plan.
- Established partnership cooperation.
- Signed agreements.
- Established monitoring and reporting system.
- Prepared reports.
- Conducted transnational meetings.
- Maintained proper documentation for each activity.

Intangible results of project management:
- Ensured smooth project implementation within budget and on schedule.
- Enhanced international cooperation.
- Improved management competencies in EU projects.
- Increased quality in the preparation, implementation, monitoring, and follow-up of EU/international projects.

Measurable results of project dissemination and awareness raising:
- Developed a dissemination plan.
- Launched a social media campaign.
- Delivered multiplier events.
- Posted web publications on partner websites.

Intangible results of project dissemination and awareness raising:
- Broad outreach to and well-informed and motivated target groups.
- Positive attitude towards the IQ-DigitS project and its values.
- Good attendance at project events and the creation of an IQ-DigitS community through social media and networking events.

Measurable results of sustainability:
- Developed a sustainability and exploitation plan.
- Conducted awareness campaigns for other VET/AE providers.

Intangible results of sustainability:
- Increased IQ-DigitS community.
- Growing number of VET/AE providers implementing the IQ-DigitS concept.
- Rising interest from public authorities and stakeholders in the IQ-DigitS concept.

Staff training events:
November/ December 2022: Training on implementing the joint methodology for curricula development based on learning outcomes and micro-credentials.
June 2023: Training on integrating the digital certification system into regular work.

National conferences and webinars:
E1: IQ-Digits National Conference, North Macedonia.
E2: IQ-Digits National Conference, Italy.
E3: IQ-Digits National Conference, Austria.
E4: IQ-Digits National Conference, Croatia.
E5: IQ-Digits Webinar: "How to integrate micro-credentials and the digital certification system into the regular work of AE/VET providers"
