2021-1-MT01-KA220-VET-000025011.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-MT01-KA220-VET-000025011.title: Virtual & Augmented Reality Trainers Toolbox To Foster Low Carbon Tourism & Related Entrepreneurship
2021-1-MT01-KA220-VET-000025011.summary:
<< Background >>

At the time of the proposal submission stage, the VINCI partners realised that there was a need to foster low carbon good practices in the tourism sector.   The EC had  launched the 'Green Deal' action plan with the intent of making the EU's economy more sustainable by turning climate and environmental challenges into opportunities and making the transition just and inclusive for all. As clearly outlined in this action plan, the main economic actors i.e. EU businesses, consumers and citizens, were expected to be the driving force behind this transition towards a low-carbon and climate resilient continent.  Clearly the EU tourism sector was a significant contributor to CO2 emissions. Thus there was a need to adapt low carbon practices in this sector to help meet the EU's ambitious 2030 targets. The partners realised the need that stakeholders such as tourists, agents, and hotels needed education and resources on low carbon tourism.    Hence the VINCI partners planned to address these needs by providing VET trainers/tourism mentors with a set of innovative training resources they could use with different tourism stakeholders/learners to help them learn at their own pace, time on how to plan green travel paths and activities.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, the partners aimed  to foster a shift towards low carbon tourism (LCT) and foster related entrepreneurship.  To achieve this, the VINCI project pooled  experts on Climate Change/Sustainability, Tourism, Entrepreneurship, work-based training, VET Curriculum development and digital technologies.  The partners thus set these objectives:
 
OB1: to develop an innovative curriculum on LCT activities and related entrepreneurship; 
OB2:  to raise awareness through 'best practice' case-studies of how tourism stakeholders can generate less CO2 emissions in all three phases of travel tourism; 
OB3: to develop a set of modular training resources on LCT activities and related entrepreneurship, some of which will be Augmented and/or Virtual Reality based to better engage learners; 
OB4: to develop the VINCI Toolbox consisting of a repository of digital training resources on LCT, including an m-/e-Learning platform to help stakeholders acquire skills on LCT even at their place of work & home;
OB5: to develop a Trainer's e-book intended to guide VET trainers on specific training units and/or styles relevant to different tourism stakeholders;
OB6: to widely disseminate the project results and how to manage LCT.

<< Implementation >>

The main project activities implemented during the VINCI project were as reflected in the rest of this final report related to:

- Preparatory activities;
- Project management activities;
- Results (R1 - R4) planning and development work;
- Results peer reviewing, testing and refinement activites ;
- Knowledge sharing/exchange activities between the partners including via online meetings and face to face meetings
- Knowledge sharting outside the partnership through press releases, newsletters, social media posts, multiplier events, project webpage updates and other means.

<< Results >>

The conrete outputs /results that emerged from the VINCI project are:

R1: An Innovative Curriculum on Low Carbon Tourism concepts and related Entrepreneurship; 
Besides access from the webpage at www.vinci.eumecb.com, the Curriculum can be directly accessed from:  https://tinyurl.com/b7wv3m3k

R2: A Set of Twelve AR/VR based Case-studies of how stakeholders can generate less CO2 emissions in different phases involved in tourism; 
During the course of the project, these case-studies were found useful by stakeholders and as a matter of fact, the partners produced more i.e. a total of 34 case-studis.  Besides access from the webpage at www.vinci.eumecb.com, the R2 case-studies can be directly accessed from:  https://tinyurl.com/2xtuctmk 

R3: The VINCI 'Low Carbon Tourism and related Entrepreneurship' Digital VET Toolbox; 
The toolbox integrates the different resources together including the curriculum, case-studies, fact sheets e-/m-learning course etc.   Besides access from the webpage at www.vinci.eumecb.com, the R3 VINCI Toolbox can be directly accessed from:   http://www.camis.pub.ro/vinci/

R4: The VINCI Trainers Guide e-Book on Low Carbon Tourism and related Entrepreneurship.
Besides access from the results section on the webpage at www.vinci.eumecb.com, the R4  Guide can be directly accessed from:  https://tinyurl.com/9mtdbp7n

In addition to the above, other concrete results that emerged from the project as detailed later in this report include:
-	Various VET trainers/learners, EU citizens and tourism stakeholders becoming more knowledgeabl on low carbon tourism
-	Various VET trainers/learners, EU citizens and tourism stakeholders willing to use the VINCI toolbox and results
-	VINCI partners willing to apply the project concept to new sectors 
-	Better visibilty of the partners at both the EU and national level.

2021-1-MT01-KA220-VET-000025354.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-MT01-KA220-VET-000025354.title: SMARTLY - Neets' Employability in the Green & Digital Economy
2021-1-MT01-KA220-VET-000025354.summary:
<< Background >>

Investments in the green and digital economy are recognized as essential for post-pandemic recovery and are expected to catalyse significant transformations in both our economy and society. These sectors, underscored by institutions like the International Labour Organization (ILO), are projected to reshape existing job markets and unlock future employment opportunities. In light of this, various partners across the EU have united to address the pressing need for inclusivity and sustainability in this transformation, particularly by enhancing the involvement of inactive youths—specifically those who are Not in Employment, Education or Training (NEETs)—in re-joining the workforce. The Smartly project was conceived as a response to this imperative, aiming to empower NEETs to access and excel in training and employment opportunities within the Green and Digital Economy. Through Smartly, our objective was to bolster the employability of young individuals, particularly NEETs, and to collaborate with Public Employment Services (PES) across Europe to align their efforts with the demands of the labour market in these sectors through relevant and effective profiling questionnaires and training programmes completing the Youth Guarantee.

<< Objectives >>

The project commenced with a comprehensive research phase, which focused on NEETs at both EU and partner-specific levels, as well as sectorial needs. This research triggered the development of an enhanced and innovative profiling tool designed to measure green and digital skill sets, as well as aid PES staff in guiding NEEYs into Green and/or Digital career pathways. Additionally, research findings informed the creation of two training programs centred on green and digital skills for NEETs, which underwent validation and mainstreaming processes to ensure readiness for accreditation submission. Involving stakeholders such as NEETs, employers, and PES staff ensured comprehensive input and alignment with all involved parties' needs. The project aimed to have PES and other entities adopt an improved profiling and training approach, enhancing NEETs' competences for the Green and Digital sectors. Ultimately, the project results were disseminated widely through participants’ networks with the aim of transferring solutions to other organizations delivering the Youth Guarantee in Europe.

<< Implementation >>

To achieve the results, the partners implemented the following activities: desk research, needs analysis, and data analysis; interviews with stakeholders; online and offline communication activities; writing of project reports and elaboration of findings; creation of a digital tool for the enhanced Green and Digital profiling questionnaire; and identification and description of learning outcomes, pedagogical assessment tools, learning methods, and training materials.

<< Results >>

Smartly project generated the following results: a survey and needs analysis, design of training content for Green Jobs and Digital Jobs, development and testing of enhanced Green and Digital profiling questionnaires, organization of multiplier events, and wide dissemination and promotion of project results.

2021-1-NO01-KA220-VET-000028166.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-NO01-KA220-VET-000028166.title: Corporate social responsibility in tourism sector
2021-1-NO01-KA220-VET-000028166.summary:
<< Background >>

To address the critical need for integrating Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) within the tourism sector, aligning with the sustainable development goals of Agenda 2030. Our collective experience has highlighted the critical importance of CSR for sustainable corporate growth in tourism. The project successfully achieved its aim to address the need for innovative training programs to tackle emerging challenges, update Continuous Vocational Education and Training (C-VET) programs reflecting Agenda 2030 priorities, and create accessible training systems to overcome educational barriers. Additionally, the consortium developed a modernized training methodology to meet new demands, promote CSR principles as key drivers for sustainable development, and develop pathways that match tourism business needs with C-VET offerings.
The CSR4T project also addressed target group needs by fostering a sustainable mindset, equipping businesses with knowledge and approaches for responsible management, and providing expert guidance on CSR implementation. It supports businesses in transitioning to sustainable practices and integrates digital corporate responsibility. By addressing these needs, the project successfully provides sustainable solutions.

<< Objectives >>

The CSR4T project aims to achieve several key objectives centered on advancing sustainable tourism and fostering innovation within the  VET sector. Our primary goal was to help tourism businesses align with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development by embracing the principles of CSR. This includes making these businesses more responsive to internal issues such as people management, diversity, equality, inclusion, and physical and mental well-being, as well as external emergencies like climate change and environmental pressures.

Additionally, the project seek to contribute to VET innovation by adopting co-creation principles and engaging direct and indirect beneficiaries (tourism businesses, CSR consultants, and trainers) in the design, delivery, and evaluation of training programs. This approach aims to enhance transversal, digital, and green skills. We also focus on CSR training processes among tourism MSMEs to improve acceptance and adoption, facilitating impactful actions transferable across Europe. The project strives to develop a new operative model for C-VET of experts, trainers, and consultants, promoting CSR principles in the tourism sector. We ensured active involvement of final users in producing market-driven results

<< Implementation >>

 In our project, we implemented a structured framework comprising four phases, each with specific activities aimed at achieving project objectives:

Planning Phase: This initial phase focused on establishing a viable partnership and laying down administrative foundations. Key activities included signing grant agreements, setting up project management structures, organizing a kick-off meeting, and defining core team assignments.

Management and Coordination Phase: During this phase, we concentrated on managing and coordinating project activities effectively. This involved networking with stakeholders, facilitating communication channels, conducting consultations, organizing events, creating quality plans, mitigating risks, and ensuring transparent documentation through an online system.

Executing Phase: This phase centered on implementing the project's core outcomes. Activities included conducting desk research, preparing frameworks, hosting online workshops, defining competencies, developing e-learning toolkits, piloting training programs, adjusting content based on stakeholder feedback, and validating workshop outcomes. Additionally, policy recommendations were developed through online collaboration and guideline formulation.

Sharing and Promotion Phase: In the final phase, we disseminated and promoted project results to a wider audience. This involved various dissemination activities such as sharing outcomes, engaging stakeholders, and promoting the relevance and utility of project results through targeted communication and promotional efforts.

<< Results >>

Project results:

1)CSR DESIGN THINKING FOR COMPETENCE FRAMEWORK OF TOURISM CSR EXPERT
- Objective: To understand user needs, challenge assumptions, and define problems to identify alternative strategies and solutions for CSR in tourism.
- Output: Developed a competence framework aimed at updating the skills and competencies of target groups in CSR principles. This framework enhances the ability of these groups to innovatively and responsibly address CSR challenges in the tourism sector.

2)E-LEARNING TOOLKIT TRAINING COMPETENCES DESIGN AND PILOTING TRAINING AND VALIDATION
- Objective: To design and pilot a training program and modules based on the insights from the first project result.
- Output: Created a specific and tailored e-learning toolkit to update the skills and competencies of experts who support tourism organizations. This toolkit ensures that these experts can effectively transfer CSR knowledge and principles to tourism businesses, thereby aiding in sustainable business development.

3)POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS DIRECT TO RELEVANT STAKEHOLDERS IN TOURISM SECTOR
- Objective: To foster an environment conducive to implementing CSR principles within tourism businesses.
- Output: Developed policy recommendations aimed at relevant stakeholders, including governments. These recommendations are designed to increase awareness and engagement with public sector efforts to promote CSR, thereby enhancing the impact and sustainability of CSR strategies in the tourism sector.

All project results can be accessed on the project's website: http://csr4tourism.eu/results/
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2021-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000033036.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000033036.title: Recover outdated machines using arduino for scalling up ESTEAM and green skills in VET students
2021-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000033036.summary:
<< Background >>

The labor market is constantly evolving.The skills and qualifications required change over time.Europe's digital transformation will see an acceleration with the rapid development of new technologies, such as artificial intelligence, robotics, cloud computing.Digitization affects the way people live, interact, study and work. Although from the digital transformation many opportunities are emerging, currently the greater risk is given by a poorly prepared society to face the future.Digitalization allows for global connectivity, which is crucial in today's interconnected world, facilitates innovation by providing tools and platforms for collaboration, experimentation. Transdisciplinary skills, such as flexibility and openness to new ideas,enable individuals to adapt to changing circumstances and learn new skills.We addressed the following needs:raises ethical questions and the impact on society, social responsibility, the improvement the daily life using robots and digitalization, understanding the complex interactions between technology, society, and the environment, optimizing resource use and reducing waste, developing entrepreneurial competences. 

<< Objectives >>

- promote a high level of employment through the creation of a competent, qualified and adaptable work
force for economic change; - support and strengthen the development of key competences for all, starting from a young
age and throughout life; - promote the acquisition of skills in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM),
taking into account links with economic sustainability and the environment; - facilitate the acquisition of skills by promoting multiple learning approaches and contexts, also with the appropriate use of digital technologies in education, training and learning; - provide support to all learners, including those in disadvantaged conditions or with specific needs, so that they express their full potential; - Provide innovative tools and skills to trainers.

Overall, using digitalized devices in daily life, develops of social competencies, entrepreneurial and green skills contribute both to the development of professional skills and to personal skills. Using digitalization and transdisciplinary skills are interconnected, as both are essential for navigating the complexities of the digital age and driving innovation and progress.


<< Implementation >>

In line with the most advanced processes in the world of makers, Arduino, 3D printers, digital manufacturing, and 4.0
industry, the project aims to provide high-quality digital skills, and to encourage entry or return to the world of work. To
achieve these goals and focus on innovation, the partnership has identified a specific field of intervention: the recovery of obsolete machinery through Arduino. This will happen thanks to the development of 3 main PR: PR1 Experts Program
Toolkit. The objective of this IO is to create a training material that provides the project’s target groups with high quality
knowledge and skills needed to modernize existing machineries in order to make them “smart” and more adapted to the
nowadays requirements of the manufacturing industry. PR2 ICT Tool for Competence Assessment (incl. User’s guide of
the ICT tool). The main aim of the ICT tool for Competence Assessment will be to evaluate the knowledge and starting
skills of the target group, identification of the needs of the specific target groups that need to be addressed in order to
provide them with useful skills so that they can enter the world of work PR3: Gamified e-learning Platform The "Gamified
e-learning Platform” served as an open education digital platform for the provision of the training material developed
throughout the project. In this way the target group formed will be able to exploit the knowledge acquired to modernize the machinery present in various production sectors and no longer used. Will be able to enter / return to the labor market, thanks to new innovative skills that will acquire in the field of electronics, computer science, interaction design, as well is in social innovation, entrepreneurial competencies and green skills. 


<< Results >>

 Project result 1:
  The objective of this PR was to create a training material that provides the project’s target groups with the knowledge and skills needed to modernize existing machineries in order to make them “smart” and more adapted to the nowadays requirements of the manufacturing industry: flexibility, friendly interfaces, ability to produce customized products, etc. The result provides the skills needed to update the machinery software, to upgrade the existing automation or to add new hardware, while leaving the mechanical parts unchanged and making machines again or otherwise competitive. The Experts Program Toolkit include the following main topics: - Design and Engineering of simple parts needed for machinery revamping - 3D printing for production of the parts needed for machinery revamping - Open source hardware relevant for machinery revamping - Open source software relevant for machinery revamping - Design of software interfaces - Economic benefits of machinery revamping – Social benefits of machinery revamping - Environmental benefits of machinery revamping - Case-studies related to successful old machinery modernization.
The innovative aspects of PR1 are related with the fact that it is designed based on the open-source phenomenon and makers movement considered as tools for increasing the sustainability, both in environmental and social terms, through extending the life cycle of countless machines. The result has a big transferability potential. Apart from being incorporated in the project’s website, it is also released as an Open Educational Resource available for use, re-use or adaptation by VET providers, companies, Youth workers, professionals, consumers, etc. Although it is designed for VET, WP1 can be used in Higher Education, Adult Education, for internal training in appropriate companies, etc. with only some minor modifications or adaptations. WP1 has a modular structure so, if necessary, only some of the sections can be used, in very different fields. For example, some VET schools may be interested only in the software sections, some companies may be interested only in the hardware sections while some consumers may be interested only in Arduino or 3D printing. The Expert Program toolkit is structured in modules, each of these having a theoretical and a practical part containing means of developing relevant skills. The modules are: Recover outdated machines (devices) using Arduino technology, Social Innovation, Entrepreneurial Skills and Green Skills (www.romuas.eu).
The expected impact is to increase the quality and the number of VET students and graduates able to apply open-source technology in order to give new life and capabilities to old machines and, consequently, a bigger number of revamped machines and positive environment and social effects. As the project’s approach can bring substantial economic advantages to those owning or revamping the machinery, we expect a large adoption of it, especially by the small companies and by the consumers, leading to an even greater impact of PR1. https://www.romuas.eu/experts-program-toolkitco/ 
Project result 2:
The main aim of the PR2 is to ensure identification and diagnosis of the needed competencies of the beneficiaries of the project by the ICT tool (internet version). The main content of the tool is the standardized competency profile of the end users of the project to define the individual training path to improve the diagnosed competency gaps and match them with the training materials/modules which are developed through the project, so as to follow the necessary and proper training path. The main innovativeness aspect of the proposed tool is the online format availability as well as its competence to calculate and provide specific and focused results for the user, calculated according to each country's data and situation. According to the results, the tool is in position to propose the necessary training designed for the current user, according to his/her needs raised – connecting in this way the project’s outputs usage and essence to the end user (would be and newly entrepreneurs). The ICT Tool for Competence Assessment is accompanied by the user’s guide. It explains all possibilities of this ICT tool to facilitate the work with the tool. The user’s guide is available in English and national languages of the project partners. The results and activities of the particular Output will be evaluated internally as well as during the pilot testing by the project beneficiaries and experts. The PR Leader had the responsibility of coordinating the macro-design and micro-design phases and to set up the ICT tool. The project partners tested it internally. All national versions of the ICT tool are hosted in the e-platform / database which was especially developed to host the Project Outputs https://moodle.romuas.eu/course/index.php?categoryid=11.  Through this initiative, the partnership ensured the free access and availability of the project Outputs, after the end of the project. Moreover, the development of the tool (layout and content) is designed in such a way that will be applicable for future updates/upgrades and transferability initiatives by other EU countries and organizations, in addition to the proposed partnership. At the beginning of the design activity of the questions, a diagnosis of the competences was designed, created by the PR2 leader. Afterwards, based on the modules in PR1 the partners agreed on a series of statements. The initial assessments are included in this platform and the final assessment can be found on the PR3 platform. We decided this to help those who attend the course. 

Project result 3:
The gamified e-learning platform is an innovative way to engage distant learners into the training procedure. Many people desire to attend training courses, though, for some reasons they cannot physically participate in conventional training programs. E-learning courses are a popular way to give access to knowledge for those people. The gamified e-learning platform hosts all the training materials and the tools that consist of the training program. The visitors  have the option to register themselves at the platform and create their personal profile. The platform is user-friendly and supports a chat room where the registered members can communicate with each other in pairs, groups or in a common forum. The platform is available in all partners’ languages.
The contents are uploaded on the platform in all the languages they have been produced. The platform uses MOODLE. Avatars were created (one girl and one boy) for each language. Each person must register on the platform, they follow the initial assessment (PR2). After that, they follow the gamified platform (PR3), choose the language, and enroll in the courses. After they complete one or more modules, they can follow the final assessment test for certification.  https://moodle.romuas.eu/course/index.php?categoryid=12
The innovative platform developed by the Erasmus+ Romuas project represents a revolution in online learning, standing out as a dynamic eLearning tool with Gamification. Focussing on crucial areas such as Recovery of Outdated Machinery/Equipment with Arduino Technology and 3D Printing, Social Innovation, Entrepreneurial Skills and Green Skills, the course offers a unique educational experience.
Available in five languages (English, Romanian, Croatian, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese), global accessibility is a priority. The course is free, ensuring that the knowledge and opportunities provided by this innovative platform are within everyone's reach, especially for students. What's more, its user-friendly and original design, combined with interactive games using H5P technology, make learning an engaging experience.
The highlight of this platform lies in its intuitive approach aimed at a younger audience. The course flow is designed to be easily understood, keeping users engaged and motivated throughout their educational journey, through games and interactions. 
The platform incorporates cutting-edge technologies to provide a robust and interactive learning experience. Based on Moodle, a widely recognised learning management platform, it offers a solid and scalable infrastructure. The H5P technology, integrated into the platform, elevates the educational experience with elements of gamification, making learning more engaging and dynamic.
The methodologies adopted on the platform reflect contemporary approaches aimed at effective learning. eLearning, as the main component, provides flexibility and accessibility, allowing users to progress at their own pace. Gamification not only adds playful elements, but also motivates students through challenges and rewards. Practical learning is promoted through modules dedicated to the Recovery of Outdated Machinery/Equipment with Arduino technology and 3D Printing, providing a practical application of the knowledge acquired. Active learning, essentially participatory, encourages students to get actively involved, ensuring a deep and lasting understanding of the concepts presented.

2021-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000034794.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000034794.title: iNTANGIBLE: Digitizing Intangible Cultural Heritage amidst the digital shift
2021-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000034794.summary:
<< Background >>

The main reason to implement the project was to increase awareness about the importance of preserving intangible heritage, that is part of the partner countries heritage, in spite of its immateriality. Intangible cultural heritage represents a feature of our lives that unites the partner countries and the European understanding as a whole. The digitization of this type of heritage poses a number of questions which we tried to find an answer to by means of this project. 
Considering the rapid digitization of sectors across the globe due to international lockdown measures, project partners identified the subsequent increased demand in cultural sector to specialize professionals working in the digital field and upgrade their competences. 
The established common national needs were as follows:
-Defining and recognizing comprehensive curricula to reinforce core competencies of VET and C-VET users in digital themes. 
-Starting with a shared definition, develop specific systematic methodologies and procedures for digitization, presentation, and preservation of intangible cultural heritage. 
-Contributing to public consciousness and understanding of shared cultural heritage .

<< Objectives >>

Project objectives were therefore designed so to answer the identified needs:
-To undertake a study of the methods, templates, and models suitable for intangible cultural products will be conducted to define a standardized framework used by the partner participating countries in digitization, presentation, and preservation of intangible cultural heritage. 
- To implement and develop appropriate training in cultural heritage digitization so to adapt to the digital shift 
- To encourage innovation in the cultural sector, aiding the application of these digital skills in their professional lives.
- To develop curricula on principles and methodologies for digitizing intangible cultural heritage 
- To deliver such knowledge through a virtual learning platform to enhance the education and practical skills of the target groups, VET users.
- To develop an accessible and creative training curriculum, content, and e-tools for less time-consuming and cost-effective learning and teaching. 
- To assist trainees in improving their digital skills in preparation for a work environment that is becoming increasingly standardized.

<< Implementation >>

1.	Project management and coordination: 
The project leader and the partners understood it is critical that all steps and procedures are completed on time and that concrete and measurable goals are established for the project as a whole, as well as for each process and operation. This meant that all project participants showed a thorough understanding of the project's goals, priorities, outcomes, tasks, and phases. 
Management, quality control, and assessment of project activities were ensured throughout the project thanks to the direction provided by the Project Management Plan (P1), Evaluation and Quality Assurance Plan (P2), Dissemination Plan (P3), and Sustainability and Exploitation Plan (P4). 
To build a solid base, all materials were jointly created, all partners contributing to the process.
These plans explicitly stated and set the project's guidelines, as well as the partners' duties, mission and
responsibility distribution, risk mitigation processes.
2.	Elaboration of project results
All partners contributed thoroughly and responsibly to the creation of the project results.
3.	Undertaking of training activities
A 6h online training followed by an onsite training were carried out as part of the training activities necessary to increase the digital skills of cultural professionals
4.	Communication and dissemination of project results
All partners contributed to the dissemination of the project results, organizing each a multiplier event to ensure the presentation of project results to  the local communities.


<< Results >>

The project goal was to create a methodology and educational package focused on ICH digitisation that can be further used as a tool by cultural workers who want to develop their digital skills in their professional field. This task was completed using an integrated strategy. The consortium began by conducting a Field and Desk Research on the needs
of Cultural Creatives in ICH digitization (R1). Although a preliminary needs analysis was completed during the proposal
writing, the survey identified gaps which consequently needed to be examined in greater detail. Moreover, the first result focused on the needs of cultural workers as well as the existing literature, theory and methodologies surrounding the subject of ICH digitization. The findings were then incorporated into the Framework and Guidebook on ICH Digitization which formed the second result, accompanying the training course. 
All the project results were then integrated into the project's e-learning framework, that is the third result, serving as both an online training platform and as digital archiving map for participants to digitally archive ICH on a collectively created digital community map.

2021-1-RS01-KA220-VET-000028060.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-RS01-KA220-VET-000028060.title: Enhancing Skills for Sustainable and Eco-Friendly Tourism
2021-1-RS01-KA220-VET-000028060.summary:
<< Background >>

As part of the shift towards nature conservation, many tourist destinations and visitors became increasingly aware of tourism’s impact on the environment. Strengthened environmental awareness led to a demand for less conventional destinations, prioritizing nature reserves with clear environmental policies over crowded tourist spots. As a result, tourist locations adopted eco-friendly practices, and more visitors evaluated the sustainability of hotels and holiday destinations. This movement favored local culture, rural areas, and preserved nature reserves over mass tourism. In line with consumer preferences, green skills became essential for tourism and hospitality employees. According to the EU Commission Skills Panorama (2015), environmental awareness included knowledge and abilities to minimize human impact. The hotel industry particularly demanded such skills, integrating green practices. The ESSEFT project addressed skills mismatches by developing three-month courses for tourism professionals and students, aligning education with labor market needs. These courses, while not part of formal curricula, provided certificates to enhance employability.

<< Objectives >>

The overall goal of the project was to enhance green skills, knowledge, values, and attitudes among working-age adults and students in tourism, supporting sustainable social, economic, and environmental outcomes. The ESSEFT project aimed to address the green skills mismatch among tourism and hospitality employees, particularly in the hotel sector, and to facilitate job transitions. Students in tourism were also targeted to improve their green skills for better school-to-work transitions. These goals were pursued through several objectives: (1) researching green skills mismatches in the tourism labor market; (2) engaging professionals from profit organizations to share expertise with both employees and students; (3) integrating university teaching tools to foster innovation in vocational education; (4) developing digitally available curricula and a learning platform focused on labor market needs; (5) producing digital learning materials with zero paper usage; (6) delivering short-cycle sustainable tourism courses with certification; and (7) making policy recommendations based on project findings.

<< Implementation >>

The project objectives were achieved through various activities. The context and status of green skills mismatches among working-age adults and students were analyzed at both national and international levels. Efforts were made to include long-term unemployed individuals, offering them opportunities to enhance employability. Consumer preferences were examined, focusing on travelers who opted for eco-friendly hotels. Training programs were developed with input from industry professionals to equip participants with essential green competencies. Learning curricula were tailored to meet labor market demands in sustainable hotel practices. An online platform was created to facilitate training, combining digital courses with limited in-person sessions. Participants who completed the program received certificates, and student feedback was gathered to refine vocational education curricula. Finally, policy recommendations were formulated to integrate green skills and sustainability competencies into vocational education and training (VET) programs, ensuring long-term improvements in the tourism sector.

<< Results >>

The project delivered four key intellectual outputs as a result of its activities. First, a report was compiled analyzing the green skills mismatch in the tourism and hospitality labor market. Second, a handbook titled *Green Skills and Sustainable & Eco-Friendly Tourism* was created, along with a tailored ESSEFT short-cycle learning course curriculum. This curriculum included six sequential training modules covering various green practices within the hotel industry. Third, an online learning platform was developed to support remote training and resource accessibility. Lastly, the project implemented the ESSEFT short-cycle learning courses and formulated policy recommendations to enhance sustainability-focused education and workforce development in the tourism sector.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2021-1-RS01-KA220-VET-000028203.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-RS01-KA220-VET-000028203.title: Vektorski svet
2021-1-RS01-KA220-VET-000028203.summary:
<< Background >>

Graphic design is a profession that is constantly changing and developing at a rapid pace, school systems are not fast enough to keep up with all these changes. These changes directly affect the labor market because graduates are expected to possess knowledge that is currently current and in demand. That is why innovations are needed in school systems that will keep graphic design in step with the times.
The creation of an international curriculum, which was obtained through a detailed analysis of the program and the labor market in this country, translated into a digital textbook that will be used as a methodical aid for teachers in teaching. In the partner countries (Serbia, Portugal, Croatia and Slovenia), there was no curriculum analysis, nor was there a graphic design manual, so the need for such a teaching tool was essential.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of the project was to improve the teaching of professional graphic design subjects adapted to the labor market in partner schools in Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia and Portugal.
The specific goals are:
A detailed analysis of the plans and programs of teaching professional subjects of graphic design in these four countries with emphasis on good practices and deficiencies in teaching in order to develop modern teaching.
Creation of a digital textbook for the subject of graphic design that is adapted to the labor market and current software solutions.
Improving knowledge and software skills of teachers.
Establishing a network between schools in order to cooperate and improve teaching.

<< Implementation >>

The activities of this project are:
Detailed analysis of the curriculum in Serbia, Slovenia, Croatia and Portugal.
Writing a digital graphic design manual that has a content adapted to the labor market and modern software.
Training for teachers to improve knowledge and software skills as well as use of the newly developed manual.
Testing of textbooks in the form of five-day lessons of all partner schools.
Analysis and Handbook Promotion Conference.
Promotion of the manual through media, internet, eTwining events and meetings.

<< Results >>

The implementation of this project contributed primarily to a better understanding of the current situation in the teaching of this group of subjects and pointed out the shortcomings of parts of the curriculum that need to be upgraded, modernized and adapted to the labor market with current software used for work. One of the main results of this project is the creation of a digital handbook, which until now has not existed in teaching in this content and which will bring refreshment to the school system. This innovation also influenced teachers who improved their knowledge and skills, which they will pass on to the next generations. Also, we expect that the analysis we conducted will affect the umbrella educational institutions in these countries in systemic changes to plans and programs. With this project, we have achieved a continuation of the network of partnerships with future partners that will cooperate in the future and after completion in the improvement of teaching and cultural events. And the most important result of this project is the improvement of students' knowledge and the availability of textbooks that they will use in class.

2021-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000028000.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000028000.title: training on Building InfoRmation models integrated with Geographical InformaTion
2021-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000028000.summary:
<< Background >>

To reduce costs, environmental impact and carbon footprints, the construction and geospatial (mapping) industries are demanding new approaches for urban planning, asset design and information management. One approach in this development is bringing together BIM (Building Information model) and GIS (Geographic Information System) technologies. By connecting these technologies, the construction processes and management of assets such as buildings, roads, and other essential public facilities will be improved. However, such an integration requires high expertise from professionals of both domains. According to surveys within the stakeholders in Sweden, Italy, Spain and Croatia, there is a lack of skilled personnel and vocational education and training (VET) courses addressing the competencies required to achieve BIM/GIS integration. Existing  VET programs across Europe for civil engineers, architects, land surveyors, geographers and other professionals working in the built environment and urban management, usually include courses in BIM or GIS, but not their intersection. As a consequence, professionals of these domains rarely know how to solve problems where a unified approach to BIM and GIS data management is needed.

<< Objectives >>

There is a clear need on the labour market for BIM/GIS integration competences. BIRGIT project’s main objective was to bridge the gap between supply and demand of BIM-GIS integration skills by developing new sets of learning material and to introduce such courses within the partnership. Projects using both BIM and GIS data require knowledge about data, operations and processes in both disciplines. To fulfil this need, new learning materials aiming at developing the necessary skills to integrate BIM and GIS have been developed. These materials are providing knowledge on methods and mechanisms (mostly software tools and data modelling) and practical application cases. One major impact was the improvement of quality of the VET programs within the partnership and the possibility of using the learning materials by other training providers as well. As an example, the courses provided by the DIS4SME project are to a large extent based on the BIRGIT project results.

<< Implementation >>

The project work was grouped into activities based on budget items, namely Project Results (PR), Multiplier Events (ME), Project Management (PM) and Transnational Project Meetings (TPM). 
The PR activities were grouped into four main activities. PR1 investigated the market requirements (in each participating country) and the desired learning objectives were specified. PR2 focussed on the adaptation of existing GIS/BIM training materials and its translation to different languages and national needs. PR3 was the core activity of the project, where new learning materials were developed and translated to national languages. PR4 was focussing on the testing and the updating of the learning materials.
In total 6 ME’s were organised, one in each participating country. The interest of these events was exceeding our expectations and generated a very wide interest within the professional community.
The aim of the PM and TPM activities was to assure that the project operations were on track and that the project would reach its goals. The dissemination and sustainability activities were also important tasks of the PM activities. Additional PM tasks were related to quality assurance and risk management.

<< Results >>

Three sets of learning material have been created and they have, together with pre-existing materials being translated to the languages of the partnership. In total, the learning material corresponds to around 10 ECVET/ECTS. The material contains lectures (slide sets with lecture notes), videos, assignments (with data sets and normative solutions), and reading suggestions. The learning materials are provided under Creative Commons open licenses. 
In order to optimize the spread and usage of these results, several dissemination actions have been carried out, specifically addressing training providers, employers as well as trainees. A website and social media platforms have been used for dissemination purposes. In addition, six multiplier events have been organised, where various stakeholders have been informed  about  and discussed the new learning materials being produced.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000028065.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000028065.title: UP- & REskilling Sustainable Tourism in a new digital era
2021-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000028065.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the challenges faced by the European tourism sector post-COVID-19. The pandemic disrupted traditional tourism models, emphasising the need for adaptation through digital experiences and sustainable practices. These factors became crucial for tourists when choosing destinations, making them essential for the competitiveness and recovery of the tourism industry.
These factors became key in shaping tourists’ decisions about which destinations to visit. The project was designed to address these needs by focusing on the upskilling of local officials, tourism professionals, and organisations by equipping them with the necessary knowledge to harness digital innovation and sustainability. This was achieved through continuous education and training, allowing stakeholders to adopt new approaches that would drive the sector's recovery.
We identified skill gaps among local business actors and provided targeted training solutions. Scalable programmes were developed to help tourism businesses integrate digital solutions, and cooperation between local authorities and business actors was strengthened through the creation of a learning ecosystem focused on sustainable tourism.

<< Objectives >>

When preparing for this project, we identified a general objective, as well as a number of specific objectives. The general objective was to increase the digital skills of the actors in the field of sustainable tourism while promoting new learning pathways to contribute to the recovery of the sector. We then defined three specific objectives, the first one being to identify gaps in the skills of the local business actors and develop training solutions accordingly; the second one to develop re-scalable training solutions for business actors in the field of tourism related to new digital solutions to be applied locally; and the third one to improve cooperation between the local authority and the business actors by developing a learning ecosystem focused on sustainable tourism.

<< Implementation >>

The project implementation was based on the following activities:
• Project coordination meetings (M1-M15-M30) (Vänersborg, Rijeka, Parma-SERN) and online coordination meetings 
• A transnational seminar aimed at discussing the results of the survey and at exchanging practices 
• Peer review activities between representatives of the local ecosystems of the partners 
• The organisation of 4 multiplier events to promote and disseminate the project results 
• Joint work for the achievement of the project results: A map of the training needs of the local ecosystem, a C-VET training package for sustainable tourism professionals, a guide for follow-up activities at ecosystem level.

By organising the different methodologies and training activities under a mutual partnership like in this project, the participants were able help each other work towards common solutions and shared objectives in a more effective manner than what would have been otherwise be possible if they had had to do it on their own domestically.


<< Results >>

The project achieved the following outcomes:
• In relation to the first objective: to identify existing gaps in the skills of the local business actors in the field of sustainable tourism. The following outcomes and results were achieved:
 -A Map of the digital training needs the local sustainable tourism ecosystem was created 
- Increased knowledge about the training needs of the professionals and civil servants 
- Improved understanding of the local ecosystem digital skills gaps.
• In relation to the Specific Objective 2: To develop re-scalable training solutions for business actors in the field of tourism related to new digital solutions to be applied locally. The following outcomes and results were achieved: 
- Improved digital skills among local business actors in the field of sustainable tourism
- A better use of open data at local level among civil servants and professionals
- A set of new training contents was developed
- Best practices were discussed and mutually exchanged
- Peer review methodology was shared among partners and modelled to the specificity of the business sector
- A training package for the actors of the local sustainable tourism ecosystem was created
• In relation to the third specific objective: To improve cooperation between the local authority and the business actors by developing a learning ecosystem focused on sustainable tourism. The following outcomes and results were achieved:
- Increased contacts between the local ecosystem and the municipalities 
- A long-term approach to C-VET and learning at local ecosystem level adopted in the partner organisations 
- Improved knowledge of decision-makers about the local ecosystem 
- Guidelines for follow-up activities and continuous upskilling of the local ecosystem on sustainable tourism were developed

2021-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000028102.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000028102.title: Developing Digital Business attraction skills through continuing VET at work in the local public sector
2021-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000028102.summary:
<< Background >>

The needs the project partners wanted to address were: 
-Develop effective business attraction skills in medium-sized municipalities as the primary challenge they face is not only promoting themselves as attractive tourist destinations but also positioning themselves as appealing locations for work and investment. 
-develop new competencies among municipal employees, foster a competitive business climate, and create tailored place value propositions. 
-Establishing cross-functional teams with the expertise to attract and facilitate investment has been a priority. 
-Support the digital transformation of services has become an essential trend in business attraction, particularly accelerated by the COVID-19 crisis.
Competition for businesses and investments has increasingly shifted online, requiring municipalities to enhance their digital capabilities. 
-build business attraction skills while also closing the digital gap. By adopting modern approaches to online branding and marketing, municipal staff have been equipped with the necessary tools to create globally accessible place value propositions. This digital evolution ensures that municipalities remain competitive in an increasingly interconnected and digitalized word.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the BAS (Business Attraction Strategies) project, the project partners aimed to enhance the business attractiveness of European cities
by equipping local authorities with the necessary skills and digital tools to attract and retain investments. The project addressed the evolving needs of
municipalities in a competitive global environment, where digitalization and innovation are crucial for economic growth. The BAS project empowered local
authorities to position their cities as competitive business hubs. 
Key objectives achieved: 
- Enhancing Digital Competencies for Business Attraction 
- Fostering Knowledge Exchange on Business Attraction Strategies 
- Developing a training needs analysis, a toolbox on business attraction management and an E-learning platform with 2 modules on digital business
attraction skills as training sources available for any interested user.

<< Implementation >>

Main activities: 
- TPMs :Three in-person transnational project meetings took place in Pforzheim (DE), Dubrovnik (HR), and Parma (IT). These TPMs provided a platform for partners to discuss the progress of the project results and facilitated the exchange of ideas. In addition to the in-person meetings, three online TPMs were organized. 
- Seminar “Improving Business capacities skills in Municipalities” Hosted by Orust: during this seminar, project partners presented the content of the toolbox, which included strategies, tools, and best practices for attracting and managing businesses. The seminar included group work sessions where
partners could brainstorm and collaborate on the practical application of the toolbox. It was also an opportunity to visit local companies in Orust, giving participants firsthand exposure to business practices and challenges in the region. 
- Dissemination activities and final Events:To share the results of the project with a broader audience, several dissemination activities were planned and five dissemination events were organized in 5 countries.

<< Results >>

The project aimed to equip municipal managers and civil servants with digital competencies for business attraction, focusing on enhancing skills and strategies for attracting and retaining new businesses. Concrete outputs developed are: 
- Training Needs Mapping and Analysis: This will provide a comprehensive assessment of the training needs of municipal staff across different countries,
creating a foundation for tailored tools and resources. 
- Toolbox on Business Attraction Management: This practical toolkit will guide municipalities on organizing and managing business attraction, including
strategies to involve various stakeholders in investment support and business growth. 
- E-course on Digital Business Attraction Skills: An online training course aimed at municipal staff, building on key elements from the toolbox, to
strengthen digital business attraction strategies. 
Additional tangible results include: 
- A Project Website for public access to information, project updates, and the e-course. 
- A Quality Management Plan to monitor and improve the quality of the project. 
- A Sharing and Promoting Plan outlining dissemination strategies and target groups. 
- A risk management plan

2021-1-SI01-KA220-VET-000028108.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-SI01-KA220-VET-000028108.title: Arboriculture as an essential Technique for managing urban green areas
2021-1-SI01-KA220-VET-000028108.summary:
<< Background >>

According to Eurostat and OECD statistics, 72% of the EU population lives in urban areas. The results indicate a continuous growth of cities and population density, and the transformation of urban areas, especially in Central and Eastern Europe, due to the expansion of built-up areas that destroys green spaces. Urban trees are crucial for addressing climate change, social and environmental issues, as well as health and economic benefits. They remove air pollutants, reduce surface temperatures, mitigate wind effects, lessen stormwater runoff, provide shade, recreational and aesthetic benefits, and enable social interaction while reducing visits to healthcare facilities. However, urban tree mortality in the EU is very high, with their lifespan averaging only 7-28 years compared to up to 100 years in rural areas. The main reasons are inadequate maintenance and a lack of skilled workforce. Urban areas suffer from a gap in knowledge and skills, as workers often lack basic training in planting, maintenance techniques, and pest and disease identification. Partner countries have almost no programs at level 4 EOK. The European Arboricultural Council's vision is to improve urban tree health and increase the number of trained professionals.

<< Objectives >>

The Arbor Tech project aims to address the urgent need for green skills, as the EU targets becoming the world's first climate-neutral region by 2050. Expert recommendations for preserving urban environments emphasize that only professional arborists, who handle planting, pruning, and other arboricultural practices, can perform regular tree maintenance. The project's goal is to provide a professional approach to urban greenery demands through an appropriate vocational education program (level 4 EQF).
The project includes:
-A comprehensive assessment of educational needs in arboriculture and comparison with existing vocational education content.
-Development of an innovative curriculum, “Arboriculture for Gardeners,” and its integration into formal and informal education programs at EQF level 4.
-Establishment of an e-learning platform and enhancement of the learning process through digital means.
-Creation of a physical and virtual dendrological laboratory.
-Development of educational materials for the “Arboriculture for Gardeners” program.
-Creation of a handbook for engaging participants with fewer opportunities
-Promotion of arboriculture and its importance for urban areas through further education and European reference tools

<< Implementation >>

Partners prepared a REPORT assessing educational needs among EMPLOYERS and EMPLOYEES in arborist services, reviewing existing arboriculture content in vocational training. This included data analysis for each country, resulting in 3 NATIONAL REPORTS and a JOINT REPORT on VET in arboriculture. From these findings, we developed a new CURRICULUM: “Arboriculture for Gardeners - VET program for Students (EQF 4).” Partners created content for FOUR PROFESSIONAL MODULES: Tree Biology and Pedology, Plant Identification and Selection, Tree Pathology, and Tree Care Operations and Work Safety. The E-LEARNING PLATFORM features these modules and a VIRTUAL DENDROLOGICAL LABORATORY with descriptions of 90 urban trees and shrubs. We designed a user-friendly platform accessible on tablets and mobile phones. Partners set up 3 PHYSICAL DENDROLOGICAL LABORATORIES in SI, HR, and SK and collected dendrology collection. A HANDBOOK FOR EMPLOYERS was created to assist in including individuals with special needs.5-DAY TRAINING for teachers at Arboretum Volčji Potok (SI) and Ljubljana was organized and 3 MULTIPLIER EVENTS. Parteners was engaged in various DISSEMINATION ACTIVITIES including website and social media.

<< Results >>

ArborTech project results are available on: https://learning.arbortech-erasmus.eu/

PR1 
-Summary Report on the state of vocational education and training for arborists
-3 National Reports (SI, HR, SK)
 
PR2 - Dendrology lab
-3 phisical dendrology laboratories as learning units/classrooms in three VET school centres: Biothniški center Naklo (SI), Gospodarska škola Čakovec (HR), Stredna odborna škola Pruske (SK)
-Virtual dendrology laboratory with description of 90 trees and shrubs growing.

PR3 - Curriculum 'Arboriculture for Gardeners' - Blended VET program for students
The curriculum includes 40 hours of blended learning in four specialist modules: 1)Tree Biology and Pedology 2)Plant Identification and Selection 3)Tree Pathology 4)Tree Care Operations and Work Safety

PR4 -  'Arboriculture for Gardeners': Blended learning program contents and associated training materials
The content and learning materials available on the e-learning platform include: a textbook with the content of the four professional modules, self-assessment tools
 
PR5 - 'Arboriculture for Gardeners': Educationa platform for blended learning 

PR6 - Guidelines for employers for inclusion of people with mild disabilities in aroboriculture

2021-1-SI01-KA220-VET-000034641.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-SI01-KA220-VET-000034641.title: Digital Content Development for Integrating Cloud Technologies into Formal and Distance Vocational Education
2021-1-SI01-KA220-VET-000034641.summary:
<< Background >>

We submitted this proposal to tackle challenges in the educational system, particularly a standardised approach to education that fails to adapt to the various learning abilities and preferences of students. Our project aims to develop new educational approaches that respond to the different needs of students with varying levels of analytical, creative, and communication skills. We focused on addressing these demands in the context of open and remote learning.
We focused on addressing the absence of personalised learning experiences in educational settings that commonly utilise a standardised approach. This creates a particular challenge in distance learning, as the dynamics of teacher-student interactions differ significantly from those in conventional settings. 
We introduced AI to develop flexible learning materials and assessments tailored to each student's specific needs and learning styles. This approach enhances fairness and accuracy in remote education evaluations, ensuring they meet ethical assessment standards.
The motivation for this project came from the potential of AI to transform educational methods, enhancing student engagement and effectiveness in various settings. 

<< Objectives >>

Our project aimed to enhance the educational skills of teachers and students by integrating Cloud Computing and Artificial Intelligence over a 24-month collaboration with partner organizations. We focused on providing educators and learners with a solid foundation in Cloud Computing, optimizing digital education delivery, and improving engagement through practical, real-world applications. Additionally, we sought to personalize learning experiences using AI to adapt materials to individual needs, aiming to create a more interactive and efficient educational environment for modern students and educators.

<< Implementation >>

To efficiently accomplish our project goals, we organised the implementation into seven separate work packages (WPs), with each managed by a partner organisation chosen for their particular strengths and skills. The tasks encompassed by these work packages consisted of:
WP1: Project Management (Overseeing and organising the project, guaranteeing efficient collaboration among all stakeholders and timely achievement of project milestones)
WP2: Development of IO1 (Developed through activities focused on creating Educational Framework on Cloud Computing.)
WP3: Development of IO2 (Dedicated to preparing Assessment Platform for Digital Contents. This platform was specifically built to integrate AI technologies for the purpose of assessing and improving student learning outcomes in the field of Cloud Computing education)
WP4: Development of IO3 (Dedicated to preparation of the Online Education Platform for Cloud Technology. The objective of this platform is to offer easily accessible and useful educational platform and encourage a dynamic learning atmosphere.)
WP5: Dissemination (The activities encompassed promoting the project's accomplishments through many media channels, coordinating seminars and conferences, and actively involving stakeholders both within and outside the educational domain.)
WP6: Quality control and monitoring (Prepared and executed ongoing monitoring and assessment of project activities and outcomes. This facilitated the implementation of quality control measures and enabled the adaptation of methods in accordance with feedback and evolving requirements during the duration of the project.)
WP7: Sustainability (The activities in this package aimed to guarantee the lasting effect and ongoing existence of the project outcomes. This entailed strategizing for the continuation of project outcomes after the funding period and investigating options for sustained assistance and allocation of resources.)

<< Results >>

The Educational Framework on Cloud Computing (IO1) is a carefully formed framework that is specifically prepared for vocational education and training (VET) with the aim of improving knowledge and skills in the field of cloud computing. This framework includes a guidebook (which is published in two parts) that provides in-depth teaching modules specifically tailored to improve the digital skills of students and teachers in vocational education and training (VET).
The Advanced Assessment Platform (IO2) is a platform that enhances the evaluation process by customising it to accommodate the distinct learning styles and needs of individual students. This system enables fair and more accurate assessments in remote learning scenarios.
The IO3 platform is an e-learning platform specifically tailored for cloud technologies. It serves as a dynamic storage of learning resources connected to cloud computing. These materials are readily accessible to learners of diverse backgrounds and varying levels of proficiency. The system enables interactive education by integrating digital innovations and is meant to be customised and implemented in various educational environments.
We have established strategies to ensure the project outcomes remain sustainable beyond the initial phase of funding. This included plans for the continuous administration and maintenance of the online platforms and educational resources (see attached Sustainability and Exploitation Plan).
We undertook a range of dissemination activities, including arranging workshops and participating in conferences, to spread knowledge about the project's accomplishments and actively involve a broader educational and technological community.
By implementing systematic monitoring and evaluation, we were able to accurately measure the effectiveness of our actions and outcomes. This ensured that our efforts were in line with the initial project benchmarks and were adjusted as needed in response to feedback and evolving requirements.
Each of these results has significantly contributed to the progress of educational practices in the field of cloud computing, particularly in the context of vocational training. These efforts have not only enhanced the educational experience for students but have also provided teachers with advanced tools to facilitate effective instruction in an increasingly digital culture.

In the project we also additionally prepared and published a scientific Monography, which was not initially forseen in the project, but it is now successfully published and openly available through the project website and of FOS publishing website.

2021-1-SK01-KA220-VET-000034882.title: RESTART – Resilience and Training for SMEs
2021-1-SK01-KA220-VET-000034882.summary:
<< Background >>

Pandémia COVID-19 ovplyvnila všetky aspekty spoločnosti a hospodárstva EÚ a sveta. V EÚ sú sociálno-ekonomické dopady pandémie najviditeľnejšie, nevynímajúc priority programu Erasmus+: 1. ekosystém odborného vzdelávania a prípravy bol ovplyvnený z hľadiska obsahu a štruktúry; 2. mikropodniky, malé a stredné podniky (MMSP) v EÚ museli prehodnotiť svoje obchodné modely, aby sa prispôsobili novým trhovým podmienkach; 3. COVID-19 tiež urýchlil trendy v oblasti digitalizácie a vznik nových pracovných pozícií a spoločností. Zároveň bolo potrebné pochopiť, či je ekosystém odborného vzdelávania a prípravy EÚ primerane vybavený na to, aby sprevádzal mikro, malé a stredné podniky (MMSP) a pracovníkov na tejto transformačnej ceste. Konkrétne slovenské prieskumy uvádzajú, že kríza sa priamo dotkla viac ako 15 000 spoločností a 41 000 živnostníkov. Viac ako 4 z 10 podnikov uviedli, že v reakcii na meniace sa podmienky prispôsobili svoje výrobky/služby. Až 26 % MMSP začalo alebo zvýšilo svoju podnikateľskú činnosť online. To naznačuje ochotu a schopnosť využívať nové kapacity a prístupy k podnikaniu pre udržanie si konkurencieschopnosti. 

<< Objectives >>

Hlavným cieľom projektu RESTART bolo vyvinúť inovatívne odborné tréningy s cieľom vybaviť európsky ekosystém odborného vzdelávania a prípravy obsahom vychádzajúcim z potrieb trhu, ktorý by sprevádzal MSP a európsku pracovnú silu na "ceste odolnosti" pri opätovnom štarte v postpandemickom sociálno-ekonomickom kontexte. Cieľové skupiny: 1. MMSP, ktoré potrebovali znovuobjaviť a prispôsobiť svoje obchodné modely a operácie novej post-covidovej situácii; 2. Pracovníci a odborníci, ktorí sa potrebovali prispôsobiť rýchlo sa vyvíjajúcim pracovným podmienkach a vznikajúcim pracovným pozíciám prostredníctvom nadobudnutia inovatívnych a dôležitých zručností a kompetencií; 3. Ekosystém odborného vzdelávania a prípravy v EÚ, ktorému chýbal relevantný a aktuálny obsah a vzdelávacie kurzy, ktoré by sprevádzali MSP a pracovnú silu na tomto rýchlo sa vyvíjajúcom trhu; 4. Systém podpory podnikania, ktorý potreboval aktualizovať a modernizovať svoju ponuku.
Ciele 1. Aktualizovať a modernizovať systém podpory podnikania 2. Podporiť MSP a pracovnú silu EÚ na "ceste k odolnosti"; 3. Zlepšiť príslušné zručnosti a kompetencie v aktuálnych témach odrážajúcich potreby trhu; 4. Podporiť prenos znalostí a prispôsobenie podnikateľských modelov v MSP.


<< Implementation >>

Výsledok projektu 1 - pod vedením IWS bola vytvorená platforma otvorených vzdelávacích zdrojov (OER) RESTART, ktorá slúži na poskytovanie vzdelávacích tréningov a zdieľanie operačných nástrojov s poskytovateľmi odborného vzdelávania a prípravy, MMSP a ich zamestnancami. Platforma OER je k dispozícii tu: https://www.restartproject.eu/ a je preložená do 6 jazykov (angličtina, chorvátčina, španielčina, taliančina, maďarčina a slovenčina). Platforma RESTART OER funguje ako digitálny archív znalostí všetkých výstupov vytvorených v rámci projektu. Funguje aj ako online úložisko kreatívnych nástrojov a zdrojov. DEMO video o Platforme: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BVAb7dsV-bQ. 
Výsledok projektu 2 - Inovatívny podnikateľský model projektu RESTART ktorý je dostupný na RESTART OER Platforme: https://www.restartproject.eu/model.php.
Výsledok projektu 3 - Tréningy a nástroje RESTART sú bezplatné a plne dostupné online na platforme RESTART OER tu: https://www.restartproject.eu/training.php?lang=EN.
V rámci 4. projektového výsledku (PR4) – Stanovisko projektu RESTART a Usmernenia pre používanie vytvorených tréningov sú uverejnené tu: https://www.restartproject.eu/guidelines.php.

2021-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000024755.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000024755.title: Innovative curriculum to evaluate MARIne fishery discards as raw PET food for sustainable Europe
2021-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000024755.summary:
<< Background >>

Over three billion people rely on the biodiversity of the oceans and coasts for their livelihoods. However, today we see that 30 percent of the world's fish stocks are overfished. The FAO estimates that total fish production in 2018 was 179 million tonnes and about 88% of the mentioned amount was used directly for human consumption and the remainder (12%) was described as being used for “non-food purposes” and “waste”. . Reducing bycatch and discards is an important issue for fisheries management. Not only ecological impacts on biodiversity, but also economic losses are enormously tragic problems worldwide. MARIPET planned and implemented the merger of various sectors such as fishing, animal nutrition and pet food production with the support of various professional groups such as fisheries experts, veterinarians, seafood specialists and pet food manufacturers. MARIPET supported enough importance to revalue discarded fish which is increasing day by day. MARIPET was created because converting discarded fish into an ingredient for pet food is an almost new topic and requires multiple professionals as it is a multidisciplinary project.

<< Objectives >>

The implementation of the project demonstrated possibilities for using discarded fish species that arise from commercial fishing and cannot be evaluated in animal feeding. It is an undeniable fact that with the realization of this goal, effective solutions have been found to some ecological problems caused by climate change. Sustainable food management is necessary to make more efficient use of the portion earmarked for human consumption due to the growing world population and diminishing food resources. However, the possibility of using some of the discarded marine products in animal feed will once again demonstrate the importance of ecosystem-based fisheries policies. By 2030, UNDP aims to double the income of families involved in agriculture and animal husbandry while reducing exploitation stocks by half. All United Nations heads of state and government have signed on to this goal in “Life Below Water,” the 14th title of the Sustainable Development Goals. Therefore, addressing the pressure on food supplies caused by climate change and global warming has become a critically important task. The practices developed by MARIPET helped raise awareness about the valuation of discarded fish as animal feed.

<< Implementation >>

The dissemination kit and the main tool for disseminating the MARIPET results on social networks (Instagram @project_maripet), local and national press, television channels, dissemination activities and multiplier events with stakeholders, meetings with target groups, and organizations, meetings with fishermen and representatives of the pet food sector and municipalities. University teams also encouraged students to use the project website and learn about managing fisheries waste, reducing food waste and using discarded fish for healthy pet food. They also focus on communicating results to all stakeholders in the field of fisheries management and healthy animal nutrition, environment, ecological and sustainable food resources.

<< Results >>

Unfortunately, the commercial concerns this circumstance raises among fishermen often undermine fishery engineers' solutions to reduce discards. In reality, most scientific studies emphasize that reducing discards in fisheries is not such a simple process and that current catch-based fishing techniques fail to successfully eliminate it. Although this cannot be completely prevented, with logical solutions, discarded fish can be converted into other sources that become economic products for various sectors. MARIPET accepts that fish, even if it is economical for human consumption or is thrown away, has high nutritional value. This idea led to the important result that discarded fish could be used as an ingredient for the pet food industry. The second intended outcome of the project is to demonstrate the transformation steps and processes through a training module for industry professionals ranging from fishermen to pet food manufacturers. While the training program is carried out by the project professionals, an economical business model was also demonstrated. The aim of MARIPET was not only to create a training program but also to establish a sustainable transformation chain as an economic policy for fisheries and animal food production. Another important result is the creation of an exchange platform for project experts, training participants and representatives of the relevant industry. As the project has repeatedly emphasized, the fishing and pet food sectors are developing very quickly and the experiences from the project activities also hold great potential for rapid ageing. The platform will keep the project topic quite dynamic and provide up-to-date information coming from MARIPET experts. The dynamic action in the plenary session has great potential to bring this transformation sector into industry.

The main results of the MARIPET:
Innovative curriculum including 5 modules with training courses
A virtual dedicated environment with an online education kit
Establishment of discard fisheries  and pet food trainers/experts platform - European Discard  Fisheries and Pet Food Production Guidebook/e-book Training workshops
Multiplier events in five countries
Quality Management and dissemination reports
