2021-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000025424.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000025424.title: Developing a novel and digital curriculum for aircraft maintenance practical training
2021-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000025424.summary:
<< Background >>

The aviation industry is growing rapidly in Turkey and Europe, creating a strong demand for highly qualified aircraft maintenance engineers (AMEs). However, the existing practical training curricula are outdated, lacking pedagogical orientation and industry relevance. Current training materials often provide only task lists without clear implementation methods or assessment criteria, resulting in graduates who are insufficiently prepared for real maintenance operations. We applied for this project to develop a modern, pedagogically sound, and industry-driven practical training curriculum. Our goal is to bridge the gap between educational programs and industry needs, reduce the costs and time spent on additional on-the-job training, and produce AME graduates who are immediately capable of performing maintenance tasks effectively. By ensuring continuous industry input through a web-based platform, the curriculum will remain dynamic and aligned with evolving aviation standards.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective was to design a structured, pedagogically sound, and industry-aligned practical training curriculum for aircraft maintenance engineer (AME) candidates. We aimed to create a Practical Training Task (PTT) Book by identifying representative practical tasks for key EASA Part-66 modules (7, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, and 17), supported with detailed execution methods, tool lists, worksheets, training needs analysis (TNA), and evaluation forms. We also wanted to build a web-based platform to ensure that educators, maintenance engineers, and organizations could continuously suggest new tasks and improvements, keeping the curriculum up to date with industry needs. Beyond producing better-trained graduates, we sought to establish stronger collaboration between educational institutions and the aviation maintenance industry, positively impacting the employability and readiness of AME students across Europe and Türkiye.

<< Implementation >>

Industry survey, Practical Training Task (PTT) Book, worksheet designs, training needs analyses, and assessment forms, pilot training sessions, result evaluations, dissemination events, project website development.

<< Results >>

We produced an Industry Needs Report, a Practical Training Task Book, a Training Needs Analysis Book, a Worksheet Book, a Practical Assessment Book, a Follow-up Report, and launched a web platform to keep the curriculum updated with industry inputs.

2021-2-LU01-KA220-VET-000050926.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-LU01-KA220-VET-000050926.title: Small steps to bigger success – developing knowledge/capacity building program for entrepreneurs to foster – through micro learning - better and more successful succession in the family business (SiFB)
2021-2-LU01-KA220-VET-000050926.summary:
<< Background >>

The primary motivation for applying for this project stemmed from the acute awareness of the challenges and needs faced by family businesses during the succession process. Family businesses constitute a significant portion of the economy in Europe, with up to 90% of companies in some countries being family-controlled. These businesses are pivotal in generating employment and contributing to economic growth. However, succession in family businesses is often fraught with complexities, risking business continuity and job losses. Many young successors lack the necessary business knowledge and face time constraints that impede their ability to prepare adequately for taking over the business. Additionally, there is a general lack of tailored educational programs that address the unique challenges of family business succession. By applying for this project, the aim was to address these specific needs by developing a digital, modular educational program that would equip current and future generations of family business owners with the essential knowledge and skills for successful business transfer.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to achieve several critical objectives through its implementation:
Education and Skill Development: To prepare both the current (1st generation) and next generations (2nd and 3rd generation) of family business owners for a more efficient and successful transfer of management and ownership. This was to be accomplished through a custom-designed online learning program focused on micro-learning to facilitate easy and flexible learning.

Innovative Learning Methods: To enhance engagement and information retention, introduce and utilize innovative learning methods such as micro-learning and gamification in educational content.

Digital Accessibility: By creating a fully digital and online program, the project aimed to increase the accessibility and flexibility of learning opportunities for family business members, enabling them to learn at their own pace and according to their individual needs.

Research and Tailored Content: To conduct research in multiple countries to understand the unique challenges and needs related to family business succession, and to use these insights to develop tailored content that is directly applicable and beneficial to the target audience.


<< Implementation >>


1.	Primary Research (PR1): Conducted extensive research in partner countries to identify the specific challenges and requirements of family business members in the succession process. This research included analyzing existing data from the Erasmus+ SUFABU project and conducting interviews.
2.	Data Analysis and Report Creation (PR1): Analyzed the data gathered from the research to understand the prevalent challenges in family business succession, serving as the foundation for developing the tailored learning modules.
3.	Program Design and Development (PR2): Based on the research findings, a tailor-made microlearning program was created. This program focused on succession planning in family businesses and was designed in microlearning units to facilitate easy content absorption.
4.	Recording and Post-production (PR3): Each partner institution was responsible for preparing specific microlearning units.
5.	Development of Learning Website (PR4): Website where all the microlearning units and other educational materials were made accessible to the target audience.
6.	Dissemination and Outreach: Participation in family business events and the organization of multiplier events in each partner country to showcase the project results, as well as preparing scientific research paper to be presented at the conference and published in journal.
7.	Continuous Feedback and Iteration: User feedback was continually solicited and used to refine and improve the educational content and the website.


<< Results >>

1.	Interviews and Detailed Report
Conducted interviews with family businesses across the partner countries. These interviews provided in-depth insights into the challenges faced during the succession process.Compiled a comprehensive report based on the interviews and additional literature review. This report outlined key challenges and needs identified during the interviews, offering a nuanced understanding that informed the development of the educational program.
2.	Tailored Online Learning Program: A comprehensive, modular online learning program specifically designed for family business succession. This program included a variety of microlearning units, each addressing different aspects of succession.
3.	Educational Materials: A range of supporting materials was produced, case studies and gamified website that leads interested participants through a family succession journey through short videos and questions.
4.	Learning microlearning Website: A website where all materials are accessible. Website www.sifb-eu.com
5.	Dissemination Events
As an additional output we created a research paper that will be published.

2021-2-PL01-KA220-VET-000049069.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-PL01-KA220-VET-000049069.title: Too Good To Go  - Waste Free Economy Transformation for SMEs
2021-2-PL01-KA220-VET-000049069.summary:
<< Background >>

Project Partners were involved in several pro-ecological projects. They realised waste management alone wasn't enough to combat climate change and aimed to introduce waste-free economy models. They identified four key hindrances:
Lack of clear connection between individual behaviour and its impact on environmental transition.
Slow pace of change and irregularities typical of circular economy.
Feeling of impotence due to the problem's size and lack of concrete proposals for SMEs.
Lack of feedback on the effectiveness of actions taken by SMEs.

The Project aimed to enhance education and training for local communities by sharing approaches and best practices on waste-free economy. It sought to leverage existing resources for transition and reconcile information from various sources. Additionally, it offered support to communication campaigns by improving the capacities of Partner organisations in environmental strategic development and targeted activities.

Partners also wanted to help SMEs with challenges such as:
Lack of knowledge and understanding of waste-free economy processes.
Lack of awareness of benefits for SMEs and the environment.
Lack of real-life examples, guidance. competencies needed, tailored materials and trainings

<< Objectives >>

The Project set of objectives was correlated with the needs of the target groups: SME leaders and managers, VET educators as well as Partner organisations’ employees and reflected the global market trends. SMEs, with over 100 million employees in the EU are a driving force behind huge changes. In the case of transformation from waste management business models to waste-free ones, the necessary change influenced all aspects of organisations' operations: internal and external.
Based on the pre-project analysis as well as intensive consultations within the Partnership, Partners pursued 3 main objectives:
1 Encouraged SME leaders to start the transformation process and develop Waste Free Economy Policies and Implementation Action Plans for their organisations and to set examples for other SMEs.
2 Catalogued and developed SMEs' leaders and Project Partners’ competencies necessary for successful transition to the Waste Free Economy, and encouraged their development as sustainability change agents
3 Equipped VET providers with ready-made learning structures, best practice examples, and tools to support the adaptation of their training offers to SME leaders and staff needs to develop the skills needed in the area of sustainable developmet

<< Implementation >>

CORRELATION OF OBJECTIVES WITH PROJECT ACTIVITIES
The strength of this Partnership and the quality of Project outcomes is the direct result of the real engagement and true dedication of all Partners to the highest quality of cooperation and support throughout all activities. The Partnership was already cooperating when the proposal was written and when the Project was approved for financing, the Partners verbalised the already tested communication procedures, quality assurance processes and the need for qualitative feedback at all stages of project progress. 
In detail, the following activities were driving the project results development:
Objective 1 was implemented to a large extent via Result 4 - Waste Free SME Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) development as well as the dissemination activities that were taking place online and offline throughout the Project duration. The MOOC comprises an array of resources and tools needed to assure SME leaders that the transfer to a waste-free economy model was worthwhile and doable.  Partners believe that the very involvement of SMEs in Results development and dissemination activities would encourage their leaders and employees to enter the transformation process as pioneers so they would become change agents for their sector. And so that happened. Result 1 through Result 4 supported that objective with activities demanding involvement of SME leaders and staff as well as  partner organisations and their staff, setting a clear path for transformation with best examples (Result 1), tools and processes for transformation planning and performance (Result 2), indispensable competencies (Result 3) and resources for their development (Result 4). The activities were ranging from designing questionnaires and participating in interviews and consultations through extensive research to hours spent on transferring theoretical knowledge to practical information, designing tools and describing case studies in a practical and motivational way, gathering structured feedback to make sure the resources and tools and  useful and palatable for busy entrepreneurs  and finally presenting the content in all Results in such a way that it would be useful for VET educators. The whole process, although very demanding, was very engaging for all Partners.
Ad Objective 2:
The second objective was targeted mostly by Result 3 tasks, where all partners explored in depth business models of successful organisations that had undergone waste-free economy transformation, to describe one of the sources of their success – the competencies of the people who were behind it (Result 1/Task 3, Task 4). To do this activity, according to the same model and up to the same quality, the process for running the interviews and gathering information was described to make sure the gathered data is comparable. The state-of-the art scientific process was used to select, analyse and describe competencies as sets of behaviours, attitudes and knowledge needed at the managerial and employee level to pursue successful transformation. They constituted the basis for the content of the educational modules in Result 4 – the MOOC to be used for VET skills development and also served as a practical tool for SME leaders and HR specialists to assess in-house competencies and plan their development either on their own or through VET educators.
Ad Objective 3:
Due to well-structured activities and strictly monitored procedures for Project Results development, all of them turned out to be an excellent source of expertise for VET providers as well as SME managers who would like to start employee training. VET trainers together with Partners were engaged in activities related to the MOOC content development (Result 4), as described above. Since the MOOC was designed to be the source of knowledge about waste-free economy, Partners meticulously selected the adequate, most updated content, enriched it with best practices from Result 1, a step-by-step guide for assisting SMEs in waste-free business model transition; with methods and worksheets developed during Partners collaborative activities in the Learning Teaching and Training Activity (LTTA) and procedures from Result 2, the Competence framework as a reference point for recruitment and development, and a set of modules targeting the skills and knowledge from Result 3 indispensable in SMEs for successful transformation. While working on the set of worksheets, the Partners implemented a very detailed, multi stage verification process, testing them on their own organisations, gathering feedback and introducing changes before inviting external testers to apply a very similar testing procedure.

CORRELATION OF RESULTS WITH PROJECT ACTIVITIES
Activities of Result 1 led to the development of a Compendium of waste-free economy transformation success stories from SMEs. The activities included: setting the criteria for selection, selecting the companies and conducting preliminary interviews with SMEs; thematic mapping of the company examples and selection to narrow the number of SMEs to the ones that can be further interviewed for case studies; structuring the business cases and interviews by developing a business case structure together with interview procedure and an interview guide and running the interviews; preparation of the SMEs Business case compendium that answered the set of questions such as: how SME started; what it took to make the waste free economy transformation, what support was needed, what competencies were needed, how the competencies were developed; the present situation, encountered challenges, why was the transformation successful, what are their recommendations for other SMEs.
During the LTTA, Partners defined the methods for incorporating waste-free economy principles into business strategies. These were later used in practice and verified in the course of implementation of Result 2: Step-by-Step Policies Portfolio and Action Plans development through activities such as: market research, mult-layer and multi stage designing and testing the tools for practicality and functionality. Each Partner appointed a waste free model Project team with a leader and each team conducted activities (e.g workshops, team meetings, inhouse observations, job shadowing ) to design new Policy and Action Plan on organisational level. All partners contributed working on their policies and action plans, consulting and brainstorming for one another. Next, each set of policies was reviewed by at least one other partner. In the following activity, waste free model project teams in 6 organisations conducted evaluation (focus groups, questionnaires) of the process they went through, to define areas for improvement in the process of designing policies and evaluate and polish tools and templates. On the basis of evaluation conclusions, final versions of the tools, templates and processes used to design the Policies and action plans were prepared. Then the final version of the revised tools, templates and processes descriptions was developed.
Result 3: The Competence model for new jobs required by SME waste-free economy model transformation was developed through 5 tasks supported by Partners’ analysis. The activities included: identification of jobs and occupations that the waste free economy in SMEs requires, designing and running an online survey to selected respondents, conducting structured interviews with employees in jobs related to waste free economy, conducting structured interviews with owners / managers whose positions are related to the waste free economy, development and testing of the initial competency model, defining the final competence framework.
Production of the MOOC (Result 4) included developed waste-free economy educational content as described above and adapted Results 1-3 deliverables. This was achieved through activities such as: defining the scope & objectives of the modules through additional questionnaire surveys with SMEs’ specialists, owners & managers; developing MOOC modules content (content typologies were selected & designed according to the needs) together with the adaptation of the Result 1, 2 & 3 deliverables; developing MOOC infrastructure and designing learning experience (appropriate platforms were identified and the suitable one selected based on the strict criteria described in the Proposal); developing MOOC structure & functionalities including the authoring of descriptive materials for facilitating the participants’; writing online texts to present the content in an efficient and appealing way; integrating testing methodologies; launching the MOOC course, reviewing it and testing inside the Partners’ organisations and evaluating with external target groups users. 
All four Project Results were translated and cultural adapted to Partner languages: PL, IT, BG, HR and LT.
6 National Information Days in PL (2), IT, BG, HR and LT were organised for the months corresponding to implementation of the MOOC that comprised all Results so that SMEs could see the path for waste-free model transition.
Transnational Project Meetings were correlated with the work on Results and were planned at key times for specific Results development.

<< Results >>

2Good2Go Project produced the following concrete Results:
Result 1: Compendium of waste-free economy transformation success stories from SMEs
Result 2: Step-by-Step Policies Portfolio and Action Plans and an online CIRCULARITY ASSESMENT TOOL
Result 3: Competence model for new jobs required by SME waste-free economy model transformation with indications for learning modules
Result 4: MOOC - “Waste Free SME” including adaptation of Result 1, 2 & 3 deliverables: a. lessons learnt and business cases b. a set of documents (templates/procedures) describing the implementation process for Waste Free Economy Policies with revised tools & evaluation conclusions with instructions to design and lead the transfer to the waste-free economy model in an SME c. competence model for new jobs required by the SME waste-free economy model which could be used for SMEs personnel development or recruitment d. knowledge modules to develop the specific competencies defined in Result 3.
Result 5:  Starting with active participation in LTTA and following up with Result 2 activities, 6 Partners developed state-of-the-art policies & action plans for introducing a waste-free economy model and started the transformation process in their own organisations. 
Result 6: ‘Let’s Not Waste’ LTTA provided knowledge, skills and tools for transition to the no-waste economy model, the competencies to work on other Project results and the stamina to promote the changes loud and wide.
Result 7: Two additional SMEs also developed waste-free transformation policies and action plans with the help from the Partners and selected the starting activities for the transformation.
Result 8: The Project idea and Results were shared and promoted at 6 National Information Days in IT, PL (2), HR, LT and BG with the presence of SMEs owners, managers, employees & VET providers as well as representatives of a broader public of interested stakeholders both with interest and influence in the educational field but also in sustainability and climate change. During the events the Compendium of waste free economy success stories from SMEs, the Step By Step process of transformation to waste free economy model, newly defined competencies for the waste free transformation and beyond and MOOC educational modules to develop indispensable competencies were shared. The role of competences and policies development in the transition to CE was shared. Altogether 268 participants were present (with 180 originally planned in the Proposal).
Result 9: The Partnership delivered tools and materials for promotion of project Results. They were addressed to a transnational audience, in order to inform, promote, and build a solid case for the uptake of results by sectoral stakeholders, and stimulate the cross-sectoral adaptation of results and/or the development of corresponding materials in the fields of VET and waste free economy. To this end, all promotional materials took into account intercultural considerations, and were designed in PL, LT, IT, HR, BG, EN. They include: 
1.	Project website; regularly updated - total number of page views on webpage: 4757, all downloads (Compendium + other uploaded results on webpage) – 337 of which Compendium had 232 downloads.
2.	Online social media accounts; successfully run during project lifetime: LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram. All KPI were exceeded, finally partners published much more posts that indicated in the proposal (100):  Facebook – 130 posts, Instagram - 84 posts, LinkedIn - 110 posts, website - 29 posts. Total number of followers was also exceeded: 239 instead of 200 from the proposal. Total number of Target groups’ members reached by total sharing & promotion activities: 7025 (target from the proposal: 1000).
3.	National Information Days (mentioned earlier) - the total number of event participants (268) exceeded the KPIs partners included in the proposal (180).    

Non-tangible results:

Result 10: The transformation of thinking started among the majority of all those involved in Project activities – be it the Partners, SME representatives, local authorities represented at Infodays or VET educators. They expressed interest in having a say in slowing down the climate changes by implementing the changes towards a waste-free models whether the business or individual level. 
Result 11. SME employees participated in the project development learnt about the waste-free economy concept and the influence they could have on the environment. They also developed an understanding that their actions mattered and could set good examples when they adopted the methodology necessary for the transition and implemented the process.
Result 12: Partners’ organisations' Project and out of Project staff broadened their knowledge about the waste-free economy and the tools and methods for the transition towards it, as well as their implementation; they experienced a tremendous change in their attitude and started “living the change''.

Partners expect that created results will still influence and serve target groups after project completion:
1.	Success stories will encourage organisations to transit to waste free economy models.
2.	Step By Step Policies Portfolio and Action Plans allowing SMEs to go through the transformation process.
3.	Competence model for new jobs required by SME waste free economy model will serve as a source for identifying knowledge gaps in SMEs
4.	MOOC will equip SME employees and leaders with knowledge and tools to design waste free economy implementation plans in their organisations and with skills to deliver and promote that change as well as to become the true sustainable development believers.
5.	VET providers will be equipped with tools and methods for working with their clients
6.	Project partners will initiate and foster the process of implementing waste free economy models in their organisations

2022-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000085812.title: Providing access points to work-based online learning environments for diversity management in multi-ethnic, age-diverse workforces
2022-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000085812.summary:
<< Background >>

One of the main concerns was the promotion of diversity and integration in the workplace. 
The importance of promoting diversity and integration in order to create a more inclusive and productive working environment was emphasised. 

Firstly, there was a clear need for social inclusion and diversity management in European companies. The project aimed to develop innovative digital learning resources to help business owners, managers and employees to effectively understand and implement diversity management. 

Secondly, there was a need for continuing professional development and lifelong learning for VET professionals. 

Thirdly, there was a need for promoting innovation and digitalisation in VET. 

The main focus was on promoting the use of digital open-source platforms to facilitate access to learning resources.
This included the creation of a suitable platform for VET professionals to improve their teaching and training activities on the topic of diversity.
 
DIVERSITe MOOC platform. https://diversitemooc.eu  

Last but not least, there was a need for international exchange and cooperation.

<< Objectives >>

The project had several main objectives, which were aimed at meeting the needs of the modern world of work and vocational education. 

Firstly, the project supported employers in mapping the diversity in their organisations and developing diversity management strategies. This should help create an inclusive working environment where all employees are treated equally, regardless of their background. 

Secondly, the project aimed to educate employees about diversity issues and provide them with a range of resources to help them advocate for diversity in their workplace. This should raise awareness of diversity issues and encourage employees to actively contribute to creating an inclusive work environment. 

Thirdly, the project aimed to upskill VET professionals so that they could use the full range of DIVERSITe outputs and gain confidence in working and teaching in online environments. This should help to improve the quality and relevance of VET and promote continuing professional development and lifelong learning.

<< Implementation >>

Development of learning resources for smartphones: interactive infographics and e-zines were developed to help business owners, managers and employees better understand and implement diversity management. 

In-service training for VET professionals: A comprehensive in-service training programme was developed to train VET professionals. This programme included modules on diversity management, micro-learning and the use of digital tools and platforms. 

MOOC platform: A Massive Open Online Courseware (MOOC) platform was created where all learning materials and Open Educational Resources (OERs) can be accessed. https://diversitemooc.eu 

Piloting and training: The materials developed were piloted in various countries. This included training business owners, managers and employees, as well as supporting the development of diversity management strategies in companies. Dissemination and sustainability strategy: 

Comprehensive strategies for the dissemination and sustainability of the project results were developed. These included the creation of communication tools, the establishment of social media channels and the organisation of multiplier events in various countries.

2022-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000088070.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project focuses on three major objectives. First, creating awareness for the importance of mental health for the VET sector and education in general. Second objective is the development of learning opportunities so that the VET sector can build competences necessary to face the mental health pandemic. Third, the project aims at creating change by further reaching out to interested learners, but even more importantly to VET executives and principals, as well as policy makers.

<< Implementation >>

The activities are contextualized in the phases creating awareness, creating learning opportunities and creating impact. Activities foreseen in the project are a social media campaign, a podcast series, a self-evaluation tool to identify learning needs; regarding learning opportunities a blended learning program MENTAL HEALTH AMBASSADORs is developed, that is adoptable from educational organizations. Finally a strategy paper for VET and a policy paper seek impact along a huge conference.

<< Results >>

The project has achieved to create substantial impact in the VET and educational sector in general by raising the awareness for mental health issues as relevant context factor of future relevance. Throughout the project various diverse learning opportunities rose the knowledge and competence level of a remarkable number of people. And finally a relevant community came into being, that is sustained far beyond the project end and manages to develop long-term network structures.

2022-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000088799.title: #businessgoesviral - Empowering MSEs to achieve digital transformation through upskilling young employees
2022-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000088799.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project because, through our work with companies, education providers and young employees, we identified a structural gap: digital skills – particularly in online marketing and social media – are insufficiently developed in many micro and small enterprises, even though they are increasingly crucial for visibility, competitiveness and employee retention. At the same time, many young employees already possess relevant digital skills from their everyday lives, but these are rarely recognised, systematically developed or used in a professional context. Existing training offers are often too time-consuming, too theoretical or financially difficult to access for smaller businesses. From the perspective of education providers, there was also a clear need for more flexible, modular learning formats that can respond more quickly to labour-market demands. The project addressed precisely these intersections: it combined the upskilling needs of SMEs, the underused potential of Generation Z and the demand for low-threshold, workplace-oriented learning formats into a practical, digital and Europe-wide transferable approach.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to support micro and small enterprises in building their digital visibility in a strategic and resource-efficient way by systematically using and professionalising the existing skills of young employees. At the same time, Generation Z was to be empowered to confidently apply their digital competences within company processes and thereby take on new roles, responsibilities and development perspectives. Another objective was to provide education and training providers with a concrete and practical entry point into microlearning and micro-credentials and to demonstrate the benefits of these formats for flexible, labour-market-oriented continuing education. At a broader level, the project sought to show how innovative learning formats can contribute to the digital transformation of companies – particularly in rural and structurally weaker regions. All objectives were geared towards creating sustainable structures: through open educational resources, transferable didactic concepts and the integration of results into existing educational and business contexts.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented in several consecutive phases. First, the needs of micro and small enterprises, young employees and education providers were analysed and translated into the design of a modular micro online course. The course and accompanying materials were developed in multiple languages and tested in a pilot phase with participants from different countries. Feedback from the pilot phase was incorporated into the further development of the content, didactic approach and technical implementation. In parallel, the partners produced practice-oriented supporting materials: a guideline for companies, a white paper for education providers, and a talent check to make young employees’ competences more visible. In addition, targeted dissemination and sustainability measures were carried out, including social media activities, direct outreach to relevant target groups, and three multiplier events in different partner countries. Project coordination ensured consistent quality, scheduling and goal achievement through regular coordination meetings, feedback loops and systematic monitoring.

<< Results >>

The core output was a practice-oriented micro online course consisting of six modules, developed on the basis of a survey on the digital competences of Gen Z. The course includes short videos, text-based content, quizzes, transfer tasks and further recommendations, and is accessible via a learning platform with progress tracking and certification. Upon completion, participants received a digital badge at EQF Level 3, which could be shared on LinkedIn.
During the pilot phase, 35 participating micro and small enterprises implemented concrete social media strategies and established professional online presences for the first time. Results on learning impact, usability and workplace application were systematically analysed. These findings were used to develop a guideline for MSEs with practical recommendations and best practices, as well as a white paper for education providers on quality criteria for microlearning and micro-credentials. In addition, a talent check for Gen Z was created to make existing competences visible and identify development needs. The outputs were complemented by dissemination and sustainability plans, multiplier events and structured documentation of outreach. All results were published as open access.

2022-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000088708.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000088708.title: Nature benefits: from theory to practice
2022-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000088708.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project in order to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge on Ecosystem Services and its practical implementation. Managing natural areas requires a deep understanding of conservation, restoration, funding opportunities, and stakeholder engagement. However, professionals and volunteers often face challenges in applying complex concepts to real-world management.
This course provided essential skills to improve management planning, communication, and restoration efforts while integrating the wide range of societal benefits that nature offers through Ecosystem Services. Strengthening the competences of site managers and other environmental experts is crucial for protecting healthy ecosystems and restoring degraded ones.
We have addressed the needs of the practitioners not only to enhance their expertise but also to develop effective strategies for integrating this knowledge into their organizations. By strengthening their ability to apply Ecosystem Services concepts in practice, they can drive meaningful conservation efforts and amplify the impact within their networks. We addressed the needs to enhance funding, improve management, planning, and ensure long-term nature conservation.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project, we aimed to equip nature and site managers—both professionals and volunteers—with essential knowledge and practical skills gathered from years of research and expertise from educational institutions, NGOs, and other organizations. By transferring this knowledge, we sought to enhance their ability to protect, restore, and manage natural areas effectively while ensuring these ecosystems provide lasting benefits to society. Strengthening their competences enables better decision-making, improved management planning, and access to new funding opportunities. Ultimately, our goal was to bridge the gap between theory and practice, empowering participants to integrate Ecosystem Services into their work and amplify conservation efforts at local and regional levels for the long-term well-being of both nature and communities.
The main aim of the project was thus twofold: 
1. to develop a training course that would enhance participants' understanding of ecosystem services and nature’s benefits;
2. to empower the experts to apply this knowledge directly in their daily practice. 

<< Implementation >>

Definition of learning objectives, the  profiles of the students, detailed strucure, form and content of the course, including the development of a course guide, programme, assignments and supporting course materials and content overview
To create a course tailored to participants' needs and interests, we have developed a pre-course survey and post-course evaluation questionnaires  for all three modules as well as the entire course. Adaptation, improvement of the TUNE IT English course into four national courses in Belgium and The Netherland, Croatia, Turkey and Ukraine. The course was also offered in four national languages to enhance accessibility and relevance. This approach ensured that regional-level professionals, who are accustomed to working in their native language, could fully engage with the content. Adjustment and tuning to usability after the project to enhance usability. The Handbook produced reflects on this process and makes available the revised course materials, that incorporate user feedback, and optimized content delivery to ensure long-term relevance and accessibility for participants. Development of project website, videos about the course and the concept Nature Benefits. Development of Practitioners Brief.

<< Results >>

We have developed, organized, and delivered five TUNE IT (Nature Benefits: From Theory to Practice) courses in five languages (English, Croatian, Dutch, Turkish, Ukraininan). More than 180 experts have been trained by over 40 trainers and lecturers. Additionally, 66 organizations were involved, contributing by sending participants, supporting the course organization, and aiding in content development.

2022-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000088728.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000088728.title: Digitale Qualifizierung von Krankenschwestern und -pflegern zur Verwaltung der immer stärker nachgefragten Telecare-Dienste für die häusliche Fernüberwachung
2022-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000088728.summary:
<< Background >>

The Telenursing project was designed to address the need for digital health literacy and telecare skills among nurses and caregivers. The COVID-19 pandemic and the aging population have increased the demand for remote healthcare services, but many healthcare professionals lack the necessary digital skills to use telecare and remote monitoring technologies effectively.
The project aimed to train nurses and midwives in using digital tools for Teleconsultation, and Telemetry to improve home-based care. We explored different ways these technologies can be applied, such as remote assistance for patients with restricted mobility, which also can be expanded to support in natural emergencies, and healthcare delivery in war conditions.
Through collaboration at local, national, and EU levels, we developed practical training tools to help professionals integrate telecare into their daily practice. This contributes to more efficient healthcare services, better patient support at home, and a stronger foundation for digital healthcare solutions in the future. The project also supports the broader European digital transformation strategy by equipping healthcare professionals with the skills needed to operate telecare technologies efficiently

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to enhance digital skills and employability for nurses and midwives by aligning training with European Qualifications Framework (EQF) standards. It focused on developing structured learning content to equip healthcare professionals with essential telecare and remote healthcare skills.
A key goal was to strengthen digital training competences for professionals and trainers, ensuring inclusive and high-quality education. The project promoted collaboration between national and international healthcare stakeholders to support scalable and adaptable training across different healthcare systems.
An Open Source Learning Repository was created to help professionals transition to digital healthcare services. In some cases, such as in Germany, the training materials were integrated into existing healthcare training programs, demonstrating the project’s potential for scalability and broader adoption by healthcare institutions across Europe.
The project also aimed to raise awareness of digital skills in healthcare, empowering nurses and caregivers to adapt to new social and technological challenges in digital health and telemetry.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through a series of activities designed to develop and enhance digital skills in telecare for nurses and caregivers. The first phase focused on research and needs analysis, identifying skill gaps and training requirements in digital healthcare. Based on this, learning materials and toolkits were developed to provide structured, practical training.

A key part of the project was the creation of digital and virtual tools, including an Open Source Learning Platform to support remote learning. Pilot training sessions were conducted with healthcare professionals to test and refine the materials. In some cases, such as Germany, training content was integrated into existing healthcare vocational education programs.

To ensure impact and sustainability, we engaged in stakeholder collaboration at local, national, and EU levels, facilitating knowledge exchange between healthcare institutions, policymakers, and training providers (Final Conference). The project also developed guidelines and recommendations for future telecare training integration.

<< Results >>

The project produced concrete outputs aimed at improving digital telecare skills for nurses and caregivers. A comprehensive needs analysis identified real-world challenges in digital healthcare, guiding the creation of structured training materials focused on skills development for healthcare professionals.

A user-friendly digital platform was developed, providing accessible training modules on key areas such as Communication Skills, Technology Knowledge, Patient Assessment, Acute Condition Management, and Chronic Condition Management. These modules ensured that healthcare professionals could evaluate patient conditions remotely, manage urgent cases, and apply digital tools in tele-nursing.

The project also piloted training programs, with some materials integrated into existing healthcare education programs in Germany. Additionally, it fostered collaboration among institutions, policymakers, and trainers, ensuring long-term sustainability in digital healthcare education.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2022-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000086786.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000086786.title: An Excellence based Curriculum for the Improvement of LEAN & Green Management Skills in SME
2022-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000086786.summary:
<< Background >>

ExCurS was developed to improve support for SMEs in an integrated LEAN, sustainable and digital transformation. In the participating regions, many SMEs needed to increase efficiency, reduce environmental impact and advance in digitalisation, but lacked management competences, tailored training and simple self-assessment tools.
Industrial partners and clusters identified gaps in sustainability, process optimisation and strategic management. Universities, VET providers and consultancy organisations observed that existing training offers were fragmented, weakly connected to market needs and lacked practical tools linking organisational diagnosis with skills development pathways.
ExCurS addressed these needs through a modular SME-oriented curriculum, based on excellence and focused on LEAN and GREEN competences, an EFQM 4.0-aligned self-assessment, and a blended learning platform. This enabled the identification of skills gaps, the allocation of appropriate training and the strengthening of SME competitiveness, sustainability and resilience.


<< Objectives >>

With the development of the ExCurS project, the consortium aimed to strengthen the capacity of SMEs, managers, employees and learners (education and training) to address LEAN management, environmental sustainability and digital transformation in an integrated and practical way. The project sought to reduce the gap between organisational strategic needs and individual skills development through an excellence-based approach.
One of the main objectives was to design and validate an innovative curriculum focused on LEAN and GREEN competences, tailored to the realities of SMEs and aligned with European priorities on sustainability, climate action and employability. The training content was designed to be practical, modular and directly applicable to real business challenges.
In addition, ExCurS developed a self-assessment methodology aligned with the EFQM 4.0 model, enabling the identification of skills gaps and improvement priorities, facilitating its use by non-expert SMEs and directly linking assessment results to relevant training pathways. The project also promoted a work-based blended learning environment and strengthened cooperation between VET providers, higher education institutions and the industrial sector.


<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the ExCurS project, the consortium carried out a set of activities including project management, research and analysis, content development, tool design, validation, translation and dissemination, in line with the approved work plan.
The partners applied continuous management and a quality assurance system based on a governance structure, regular meetings, financial and time monitoring, and the Quality Gate methodology. Conceptual analyses and reviews of European projects and methodologies related to LEAN management, sustainability and digitalisation were carried out with the support of an external Advisory Board, resulting in a structured portfolio of training modules.
An EFQM 4.0-aligned self-assessment tool was designed and adapted, validated and simplified for non-expert SMEs. The project developed 12 multilingual training modules and 39 additional modules in English, following a common structure. A blended digital learning platform was implemented, offering interactive content and practical application. The results were translated and validated through pilot activities in Spain, Germany, Croatia, Ireland and Romania, and disseminated through the project website, events and sustainability measures.

<< Results >>

As a result of the ExCurS project, the consortium developed tangible, validated and transferable results that addressed the needs of SMEs, VET providers and other stakeholders in the fields of LEAN, Green and digital management. One of the main outcomes was the development of the ExCurS excellence-based curriculum, focused on LEAN management, sustainability and digital transformation, and aligned with the EFQM 4.0 model. An EFQM-based self-assessment methodology was designed and validated, including both a comprehensive and a simplified version, enabling organisations to assess maturity, identify gaps and link results to targeted training.
The project also developed a multilingual library of training modules (51 modules) and a blended digital learning platform. These results were translated, tested and improved with the involvement of partners and stakeholders, ensuring high quality, relevance and transferability. Altogether, the project outcomes positioned ExCurS as a validated and reusable solution for European SMEs and training organisations, supporting sustainable use beyond the period of EU funding through European cooperation and open access to resources.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2022-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000087933.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000087933.title: RegenerAction
2022-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000087933.summary:
<< Background >>

Within the framework of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, addressing urgent challenges of digitalisation, innovation, ecological transition, and social inclusion, the consortium aimed to establish a common framework for a new figure in urban regeneration and social action. This role, emerging from the Italian PNRR debate, holds the potential to activate communities, initiate participatory co-design, and foster social and cultural entrepreneurship projects if fully recognized by public authorities.

Envisioned as both individuals and social organizations (e.g., cooperatives, associations, enterprises), this figure serves as a bridge between Public Administration and civil society to enable Public-Private-People-Partnerships (PPPPs). The project addressed key needs: (a) providing methodological support to local action groups, practitioners, and aspiring Urban Community Builders; (b) defining skills and knowledge frameworks for youth entering the workforce and adults undergoing career transitions; and (c) rethinking the relationship between local communities and policymakers.

<< Objectives >>

The project established a framework for the Urban Community Builder (UCB), a role promoting ecological values and fostering citizen engagement in urban regeneration ("regeneractions"). This initiative addresses ecological challenges—psychological, social, and environmental—drawing on Félix Guattari’s Three Ecologies. The UCB framework equips individuals and organizations to bridge gaps between public administrations and communities, enabling participatory processes and social innovation. Drawing on experiences from Paris, Matera, Rijeka, Évora, and Valencia, the framework was developed collaboratively using the living lab methodology, emphasizing inclusivity, plurality, and trans-local exchange. It defines the skills, knowledge, and practices needed to empower UCBs to lead ecological, urban, and peri-urban initiatives effectively. This trans-disciplinary approach also provides innovative training modules applicable across Europe. The project aims to increase UCB employability and support community development through sustainable social innovation. Its outcomes offer tools to foster active citizen participation, encourage partnerships, and drive impactful ecological and social transformation across diverse local contexts.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, the consortium carried out various activities:

- Kick-off meeting in Paris: A two-day meeting to launch the project and connect with UCBs from Seine-Saint-Denis.

- Desk Research and Focus Group: Partners analyzed national regulations and best practices of UCBs, creating the Profile & Competence framework through research and local focus group interactions.

- Meeting in Rijeka: A TPM hosted by Urbani Separe focused on developing the competencies framework and drafting training modules.

- Local Pilot – Living Labs: Consortium members tested and refined previous results through direct engagement with local UCBs, contributing to the Final Training Package.

- European Pilot Training: A transnational event in Matera where UCBs from five countries collaborated, trained, and networked over two days.

- AR Manifesto: Co-created with UCBs under the guidance of Arteria Lab and artist Miguel Januario, translated into five languages.

- Policy Recommendation: A concise document for policymakers based on the project's outcomes.

- Sharing and Promotion Activities: Online promotion led by Innohub and offline efforts by local partners, including dissemination events and academic publications quoting Regeneraction.

<< Results >>

- Regeneraction Handbook: A concise guide available in Italian, French, Croatian, Spanish, and Portuguese. Role, skills, and foundational knowledge required by Urban Community Builders (UCBs) to initiate (trans-)local "regeneractions."
-Training Modules for Urban Community Builders: five contributory modules, these training resources are designed to facilitate the exchange of knowledge and best practices among UCBs. The consortium also opened collective online spaces, enabling broad participation and the crowdsourcing of information from interested stakeholders.
-Podcasts: These podcasts, also accessible on Spotify and other platforms, summarize the training modules while incorporating concrete examples of activities developed through Living Lab events.
-Visual AR Manifesto: Co-designed during the EU Pilot Training in Matera, this manifesto was created through a collaborative workshop led by artist Miguel Januario (@Maismenos). It has been translated from English into French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, and Croatian, reflecting its international relevance.
-Policy Recommendation Document: brief report aimed at policymakers and academics, it draws insights and and guidance from outcomes of the project.

2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000086554.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000086554.title: Razvoj digitalnih oblika učenja i novih certifikacijskih programa u području arborikulture i urbanog šumarstva na razini JI Europe
2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000086554.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address several key needs within the arboriculture and urban forestry sector, particularly in Southeast Europe. Currently, there is a significant lack of available, standardized training and certification for professionals in this field. While many countries in Western and Central Europe have established certification centers for European Tree Worker certificates, such centers do not exist in Southeast Europe. Additionally, the lack of digital learning platforms tailored to arboriculture further limits access to quality education. With this project, we aimed to fill these gaps by creating a digital learning platform, a non-formal curriculum for the education of European Tree Workers, and establishing a certification center in Croatia. Through this, we will promote professional development, sustainability, and the adoption of European standards in urban forestry.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to achieve several key objectives:

To contribute to the digitalization of the vocational training system in arboriculture and urban forestry through the establishment of a virtual certification center.
To enhance the quality of work of the involved organizations and institutions by developing a certification program in arboriculture, addressing common needs in the forestry sector in Southeast Europe.
To adapt the existing vocational training programs for the profession of European Tree Worker for Southeast Europe, ensuring a long-term positive impact on organizations involved in training in this field.
To improve the educational system in urban forestry and arboriculture through the development of a unified European publication and supplementary digital tools.
To raise awareness among local authorities and other stakeholders about the need to promote ecological sustainability in line with EU policies and strategic green space planning.
To strengthen the international engagement of organizations through the exchange of good practices and improve their work with end users.

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the project, we carried out several key activities to achieve the set objectives:
-Development of the e-learning platform: We developed a digital platform that enables non-formal learning, e-learning programs, and the training of professionals in the field of arboriculture and urban forestry. This platform allowed participants to access educational materials and certification through digital tools.
-Development of a non-formal certification program: We created a new certification program tailored to the needs of Southeast Europe, based on European standards. The program covers theoretical and practical aspects of working with trees and prepares participants for the profession of European Tree Worker.
-Adapting the existing programs for European Tree Worker to the specific needs of Southeast European countries, with the integration of new technical skills and standards.
-Development of a unified European publication providing educational materials for vocational training in arboriculture.
-Development of three specific urban forest management strategies for cities in Germany, the Czech Republic, and Croatia.
- Connecting stakeholders and exchanging best practices.

<< Results >>

We achieved several concrete results:
- Established a digital platform as a certification center in Southeast Europe for urban forestry and arboriculture. This digital platform provides users with access to educational content and certification programs remotely, making the learning and certification process more accessible.
- Created a non-formal certification program for ETW: We developed a tailored certification program for the European Tree Worker profession, specifically designed to meet the needs of Southeast Europe. This program includes both theoretical and practical training, allowing participants to obtain a European-recognized certificate
- Developed a unified European publication covering key knowledge in arboriculture and urban forestry. The publication has been translated into multiple languages and is available to all participants as a reference material for vocational education
- Created three urban forest management strategies in Germany, the Czech , and Croatia.
- Raised awareness among stakeholders and local authorities about the importance of ecological planning and sustainability in urban areas through workshops and seminars
-The project resulted in the strengthening of the capacities of involved organisations

2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000086943.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000086943.title: Joint Mentorship: Better cooperation for Better VET
2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000086943.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the gaps in cooperation and communication among VET stakeholders—ministries, agencies, schools, companies, chambers, social partners, students —which are essential for a quality and functional VET system. Despite good intentions, stakeholders often work independently, which is leading to fragmented efforts and insufficient sharing of information. Teachers lack time to monitor students at workplaces and maintain regular contacts with companies, while in-company mentors often lack pedagogical training and accessible, flexible learning options. Students also need better feedback and motivation which can be provided through digital tools like e-logbooks. By improving stakeholder dialogue, formalizing cooperation through MoUs and developing an innovative e-platform and e-learning modules tailored to mentors’ needs, the project directly responded to these identified needs, enhancing the quality of work-based learning and VET in project countries.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to enhance the quality of VET by improving cooperation and communication among all key stakeholders—ministries, agencies, VET schools, companies, mentors, chambers, other social partners and students. We wanted to establish structured, sustainable cooperation mechanisms at local and regional levels, formalized through Memoranda of Understanding, to foster joint efforts in strengthening work-based learning. Additionally, the project intended to build mentors’ pedagogical capacities through flexible and available on-demand e-learning modules, addressing the lack of accessible training. In Romania, additional objective was to develop a training program for mentors. Another project objective was to develop a modern e-platform to facilitate efficient communication, track student progress and promote digital skills among students and mentors. Overall, these goals aimed to create responsive, collaborative and high-quality VET systems better meeting labour market needs in partner countries.

<< Implementation >>

The consortium implemented a series of coordinated activities to enhance VET quality. These included two study visits (to Croatia and Belgium) to exchange good practices in work-based learning and numerous thematic/regional meetings and communication/multiplier seminars in partner countries to initiate and foster stakeholder cooperation and discuss cooperation challenges in VET. Partners developed Systematic guidelines on cooperation and communication for Quality VET, along with a Good Practice Handbook and signed Memoranda of understanding to formalize collaboration at different levels. An Educational animated video was produced to present stakeholder roles. Four e-learning modules for mentors were designed, developed, translated and launched on the e-platform and national platforms, accompanied by a marketing campaign to raise awareness among mentors and encourage their participation. These activities engaged VET teachers, mentors, companies, representatives of different authorities and students.

<< Results >>

The project produced several concrete outputs that contributed to improving VET quality. Four e-learning modules for mentors were developed, 3 of them aligned with the national frameworks, one universal and translated into partner languages, and launched on accessible e-platforms, with altogether 175 mentors enrolled. A mentoring program was created in Romania to address local needs. The Systematic guidelines on cooperation and communication for quality VET, accompanied by a Good practice handbook, were finalized to support and enhance stakeholder collaboration. Six Memoranda of understanding formalized cooperation among VET stakeholders. Two study visits enabled knowledge exchange on best practices. Numerous thematic meetings, seminars, and communication events engaged over 900 participants, strengthening networks in partner countries. An Educational animated video was produced to present and clarify stakeholder roles. Marketing campaigns promoted these tools, reaching tens of thousands. These outputs enhanced cooperation among stakeholders, mentor pedagogical skills, digital competencies, and the overall quality and inclusiveness of VET across partner countries.

2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000086983.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000086983.title: Smart home models in VET
2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000086983.summary:
<< Background >>

VTSNS contacted us in 2022and we were happy to accept cooperation. Besides the growing need for energy and finding ways to save it in the era of energy insecurity it was an answer to the request of the local employers we interviewed in 2019 stating that is a shortage of technicians with skills and knowledge on smart homes.After discussing the project within team we realized companies will be key to learn and to provide our partners support needed to do the same.We contacted several companies and they expressed same problems; lack of skills and information about benefits of smart homes. Smart Touch Osijek offered support the project and help us to introduce students with skills. VTSNS previously developed the model and had ideas and methodology to share. We found establishing cooperation with similar schools would benefit efforts as teaching in the international environment would be a good first step for them to enter EU labour market. In the KA1 project we started cooperating with IKNX Ingeneria Cordoba.Other schools agreed as skills are needed and not many learning programs available. All of the partner schools are educational centres of their region and found necessary to offer students these programs I the future.

<< Objectives >>

Main objectives of the project were: create smart home models for teaching/training purposes, develop VET programmes on smart home technology and produce teaching materials to be used along with the smart home models in the newly created programmes.
We created: Five smart home models, toolkit in several languages for creating smart home models and vide content, Guidelines on instruction methods; Short programmme with 30 ECTS on smart home technologies developed and accredited; Smart Home Club programme developed and delivered; Innovated existing courses with new smart home content; and A variety of VET resources on smart home technologies (teacher’s book, student reader, glossary, video and animated short film), Smart Home VET Net formed by the partnership through webinars for VET professionals outside the partnership and Smart Home Open Days. Objectives correspond to the selected priorities Environment and fight against climate change and Contributing to innovation in vocational education and training via the results attained and their content. Technology is new which offers innovation to VET, and more importantly, directly contributes to lower energy consumption which reduces carbon emission and energy poverty.


<< Implementation >>

WP1: TMs, Management Plan development and adoption, Risk Plan development and adoption, Quality Assurance and Quality Control Plan development and adoption, Procurement of material and equipment for smart home model, Collaboration with smart home industry, Management of activities and monitoring of execution
WP2: Smart home model planning, Smart home mobile application or hub development, Smart home model building  and testing, Toolkit for creating smart home models
WP3; Defining modalities of instruction,  Development and accreditation of a short  programme of studies on smart home technology, Smart Home Clubs programme development, Smart Home Clubs programme piloting and evaluation, Innovating existing courses with new smart home content.
WP4:Workshop for VET organisations on the project, Creation of instruction materials, Peer reviewing, Glossary of terms frequently used in smart home technology, Video on making the model and its operation, 'Home Smart Home' animated short film
WP5: Dissemination Plan development and adoption, Project visual identity creation, Project website development and maintenance, Newsletter and media, Five national webinars for VET staff, National Smart Home Open Days, Smart Home VET Net formation


<< Results >>

Results of the project are: 
Five smart home models developed within the partnership, toolkit in several languages for creating smart home models, video and nimation content, which guides those intending to develop such a model in VET organisations outside the partnership.
Guidelines on instruction methods; Short programmme with 30 ECTS on smart home technologies developed and accredited; Smart Home Club programme developed; Smart Home Club programme delivered; and Existing courses innovated with new smart home content.
Preparatory workshop for VET teachers and trainers on the project; and A variety of VET resources on smart home technologies (teacher’s book, student reader, glossary, video and animated short film).
The project website as a display of all activities and results achieved; Newsletter; and The Smart Home VET Net were created and expanded on the basis of webinars for VET professionals outside the partnership and and Smart Home Open Days.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000087760.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000087760.title: Innovate and participate in digital and green transition of VET and Tourism
2022-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000087760.summary:
<< Background >>

The motivation for this project originates from a participatory approach to sustainable tourism development. This approach begins with the idea that tourism developed without the involvement of the entire society and without an environmental perspective cannot be sustainable. Society’s involvement is envisioned through Citizen Science and the Open Innovation 2.0 paradigm, where Vocational Education and Training (VET) institutions and students are part of the solution. By being part of the solution, VET gains relevance in driving sustainable tourism innovation and in meeting the future needs of the real tourism sector, ultimately preparing VET students to better meet the demands of future workplaces.

This project addresses needs related to sustainable tourism development by engaging VET institutions and the community in the process. These needs include digital tools and methodologies for citizen science and participatory approaches in tourism, improved digital and green skills, and enhanced capacity for VET institutions and other stakeholders to collaborate on new, innovative concepts.


<< Objectives >>

VET in tourism, as currently practiced, faces significant challenges in meeting the present and future demands of digital and green transformation. Without innovation and close collaboration between VET institutions and the world of work, these transformations will remain out of reach for both sectors. The development of digital and green skills must be coordinated to achieve these goals. Therefore, the project's objective is to address the issues within the tourism sector by empowering VET institutions to be part of the solution. By tackling these challenges through the VET educational process, the aim is to align education with the current and future needs of the tourism industry.

Overall objective is to innovate role of VET in digital and green transformation of tourism. 
Specific objectives: 
-to develop innovative digital tools and methodology for applying quadruple helix and citizen science concepts in mapping attractions and environment monitoring 
-to use InnoVET solution to improve digital and green skills of target group  
-to ensure that methodology and materials are adapted for sustainable replication and use of project results during and after the project 
-promotion of InnoVET on national and EU level as good practi

<< Implementation >>

Project developed InnoVET - innovative digital tools and methodology for applying quadruple helix and citizen science concepts in mapping attractions and environment monitoring. InnoVET solution was developed from two perspectives: IT solution-web based application and methodology/educational materials. Piloting, testing and implementation of solution was done with lead from VET schools, tourism boards and NGOs in 9 pilot locations. Visibility and dissemination activities included mix of different activities focusing on making the project visible in the VET and tourism community, but also to general public. During the project implementation solution was tested and replicated in additional locations with intentions to establish a model for sustainable use project of results in not just partner organisations but in VET and tourism sector. 
Important note: all links with evidence and supporting documents are available in attached Annex: Overview of supporting links for the project report
All results (handbooks, information about application and mapping results, best practice examples are available on lead partner website: https://visitkarlovaccounty.hr/hr/erasmus-innovet/


<< Results >>

Project contributed to VET innovation by introducing digital and green innovative concept of:  
- developing IT tool and methodology to engage VET students in sustainable tourism development  
- applying digital solutions that are easy to use in VET, have clear purpose in educational process, and are in line with need for digital and green skills,  
- supporting quadruple helix approach where VET teachers and students are equal partner in the innovation process. 
Project result and innovation is change of paradigm where VET is not following world of work but participating as equal partner in defining new trends and needs. 
Output is InnoVET solution with 4 components: 
“Digital and social transformation of mapping tourist attractions: manual with answers to crucial questions of who, what, when, where and why” 
“The application of citizen science in mapping tourist attractions: manual with tools for practical application in vocational education and professional studies in tourism” 
InnoVET application for tourism attraction crowdsourcing& environment monitoring
“Innovative development of sustainable tourist products: manual for the application of digital technology and citizen science in evaluating tourist attractions"

2022-1-LT01-KA220-VET-000086933.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-LT01-KA220-VET-000086933.title: C@RE Augmented learning approach for personal care
2022-1-LT01-KA220-VET-000086933.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project intends to respond to the lack of qualified workers that the sector of care is facing on. As suggested in 2021 Long-Term Care Report Trends “TECHNOLOGIES COULD BRING SEVERAL BENEFITS to this sector and THIS REQUIRES MORE AND MORE SPECIFIC SKILLS” (SPC and EC 2021). In fact, the main learning strategy of the C@RE project is based on the concept of AUGMENTED LEARNING, an on-demand learning technique in which the environment adapts to the learner, TO DEVELOP NEW SKILLS.

<< Implementation >>

The C@RE activities will:
- Deliver a COMPETENCE FRAMEWORK with NEW DIGITAL AND RELATIONAL & EMOTIONAL MANAGEMENT SKILLS required by the labor market (WP2)
- Release a TRAINING COURSE with training scenarios created around the new needs of care workers (WP3)
- Create a SOCIAL LEARNING MOTIVATIONAL PLATFORM, with the materials developed as AR components (WP4)
Activities regarding management, communication, exploitation and sustainability will be foreseen to assure its smooth implementation.

<< Results >>

Project activities will achieve the following RESULTS:
1. A competence framework for care workers inspired by 2 TYPES OF SKILLS IDENTIFIED AS NECESSARY (NEW DIGITAL AND RELATIONAL & EMOTIONAL MANAGEMENT SKILLS) IN THE CARE SECTOR
2. A training course based on learning scenarios to motivate and trigger a problem-based learning approach in care workers 
3. A social learning motivational platform that will include training materials competences framework as well as augmented reality components.

2022-1-MK01-KA220-VET-000086178.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-MK01-KA220-VET-000086178.title: Master 4.1: Enhancing quality assurance and promotion of the master craftsman exam
2022-1-MK01-KA220-VET-000086178.summary:
<< Background >>

We have  applied  for this project to improve the Master Craftsman exams in North Macedonia and partner countries like Croatia and Slovenia. Our main goal is to enhance the evaluation process and improve the public image of vocational occupations. The exam, aligned with the VB level of the National Qualifications Framework, emphasizes craftsmanship mastery. We aim to maintain the exam's quality and relevance while encouraging active participation from craftsmen. Building on insights from our previous project, Master.4.0, we see the need to improve skills for assessing the practical aspects of the exam. Our mission focuses on enhancing the image of vocational educators and addressing labor deficits where vocational education is essential. Craftsmen with master's degrees are crucial for executing practical tasks and contributing to a skilled workforce. Increasing their numbers will improve workforce quality, as they bring valuable experience. Our application seeks to develop exam programs, streamline evaluations, enhance perceptions of vocational occupations, and make crafts more appealing in partner countries.

<< Objectives >>

The Master 4.1 project aims to achieve several key objectives:
Enhance Master's Exam Programs: We will develop and update master craftsman exam programs and catalogs in North Macedonia and Slovenia, aligning them with EU standards to ensure quality and relevance.
Improve Evaluation Processes: We will strengthen the capacities of evaluation committees conducting the exams in each partnering country, leading to better evaluation and quality assurance.
Enhance Public Image: The project will boost the public perception and attractiveness of vocational occupations and crafts by raising awareness of the master craftsman exam and promoting the craft sector as a viable career choice.
By achieving these objectives, the project seeks to address the needs of craftsmen and the vocational education sector, establishing the master craftsman exam as a symbol of entrepreneurship, career advancement, and knowledge transfer. It also tackles challenges such as the lack of program development experience, inadequate methodology, and public image issues related to crafts.
Through strategic partnerships and advanced technologies, the project aims to improve the methodological approach, transparency, and quality of the exam. 

<< Implementation >>
