2022-1-MT01-KA220-VET-000087326.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-MT01-KA220-VET-000087326.title: Cities Go Climate Neutral
2022-1-MT01-KA220-VET-000087326.summary:
<< Background >>

Cities cover about 3% of the Earth's surface area but produce more than 70% of greenhouse gas emissions (UN Habitat). It is estimated that by 2050 almost 85% of the population of Europe will live in urban areas. Due to the high concentration of people, infrastructure, housing and economic activities, cities are particularly vulnerable to the effects of climate change. A typical example is the phenomenon of the urban heat island, in which the temperature in urban centres is higher than that in their suburbs. Zero carbon footprint and developing urban resilience are vital to avoiding human, social and economic losses, while improving the sustainability of urbanization processes to protect the environment and mitigate the risk of disasters.

The main need address by the  project is the limited resources available to municipal employees and other stakeholders at a local level regarding digital training materials on designing strategies for climate neutral cities such as Climate City Contracts and to support the promotion of the EU policies focusing on the transition to climate neutrality such as the European Green Deal, EU 2030 Climate & Energy Framework as well as the Sustainable Development Goals of the UN Agenda 2030.


<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to enhance and upskill the competences of municipal employees in order to enable them to design climate neutral cities strategies, such as Climate City Contracts. Furthermore strengthen the innovation and design capacity of Municipality employees regarding urban sustainable development by training them specific in strategy design and entrepreneurship. By increasing the capacity of professionals to deal with Climate Neutrality issues accurately and efficiently, they will be better equipped to transform their local authority with green initiatives and actions, in that way combating climate change locally. Furthermore, they will be able to promote and disseminate sustainable good practices to the local community, and mobilize other local stakeholders towards climate neutrality. The target group participants will be equipped with innovative digital learning tools, as well as trained on how to use them and involve them in their work, and enable distance learning. By training and upskilling professionals in designing climate neutral city strategies, sustainable development and digital innovation, they will be in a better position to assess and combat modern market needs and trends, especially regarding climate issues.

<< Implementation >>

Several activities were implemented during the project under the different work packages. These include:
- Development of a roadmap for designing local strategies covering a diverse set of topics which is available in a pdf document of xx pages as well as a digital versions on the project website / online hub. A promotional video of the roadmap was also created
- Development of an open source online course for municipal staff and other stakeholders , available in all partner languages
- Selection of success stories from the different partner countries, interviews with selected stakeholders and filming/production of 10 short videos available on YouTube
- Development of an Online Hub linked to the project website including all the project resources
- Communication, outreach and dissemination activities through various channels across all participating countries

<< Results >>

The concrete results achieved during the project and on its completion are:
- Roadmap for Designing Local Strategies for Climate Neutral Cities to upskill municipal employees;
- «Transition to Climate Neutral Cities» training course;
- «Success Stories of initiatives for the Transition to climate neutrality in cities» videos;
- «Transition to Climate Neutral Cities» Online Hub
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000086143.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000086143.title: Studies Practices In agRIculTUrAL hIgh School sTudents
2022-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000086143.summary:
<< Background >>

Hydroponic agriculture represented a priority for agricultural high schools, because there was a lack of educational materials in this field and only traditional agriculture is studied in pre-university agricultural education. Through SPIRITUALIST project we have addressed the needs of teachers and students, farmers and all those interested to be informed and educated through a useful training materials. So, we must start by educating students through their teachers, to include the training materials in their class, in order to raise the awareness and pass the knowledge to the students. Partners agreed that the best way to do that was to inspire, educate and encourage the teachers, first, to take action, through a training course in this field. Throuhg SPIRITUALIST we highlighted a significant gap in agricultural education: the underrepresentation of hydroponic agriculture and a crucial issue : the limited focus on hydroponics. This oversight is particularly concerning given the growing interest in the potential of this modern farming method.While traditional farming practices are essential, the emergence of hydroponics as a viable and sustainable method of food production warrants more attention in educational settings.

<< Objectives >>

SPIRITUALIST project`s partners focused on: introducing the concept of hydroponic agriculture to school educators, raising awareness regarding hydroponic agriculture among teachers, students, parents, teaching the target groups in order to be the transmitters for a new way of plants cultivation, which can be done whatever the season, for ensuring a sustainable food suply and natural resourses. It is well known that lack of knowledge and skilled labor are the biggest obstacles to the development of this cultivation method. Thus, SPIRITUALIST promotes education in the field of hydroponic agriculture, providing better trained graduates and makes education in this field accessible and easy to use.  Aware of the crucial role teachers play in shaping the students skills, partners aimed to inform and educate, first of all, the educators, by designing a useful training materials about hydroponic agriculture. The introduction of hydroponic agriculture concept in class and the organization of the electiv course was another main objective of SPIRITUALIST, so that the skills and knowledge acquired by the teachers will be passed to their students. Partners aimed that SPIRITUALIST will impact the whole comunity, not only the schools.

<< Implementation >>

Partners implemented Project Management & Implementation activities, within SPIRITUALIST project.
The 4 Transnational Meetings played a crucial role in the implementation of the partnership. 
The face-to-face meetings were complemented by online project meetings. 
The trainig event, with a duration of 4 days, held in Italy, aimed to increase the range of training abilities of the teachers with a set of knowledge, skills and competences related to hydroponic agriculture.
Setting up and organisation of Moodle platform piloting sessions with high schools students is another activity aimed at identifying possible gaps. Also organizing a hydroponic agricultural visit for students and established an application area in agricultural high schools, provide students with practical training in these areas and conduct hydroponics production under the supervision of teachers. Creation of hydroponic agriculture elective course content which was a weekly activity with students.Establishment of a case pool for the exchange of experience and information among students and teachers on duty. 
All partners carried out various types of activities, aimed at disseminating the project`s goal, specific objectives, the project results, the expected impact

<< Results >>

As an overall result, SPIRITUALIST contributed to the development of hydroponic agriculture in agricultural high schools, considering that in agricultural schools there was no notion of hydroponic agriculture and no educational materials to cover the need of teachers and students to improve their knowledge in this agriculture of the future. It was developed an innovative training course based on didactic materials (6 modules for teachers, 6 modules for students, lessons plans and teaching resources), an interactive e-learning platform with free access for all users. In this way, students from agricultural high schools, teachers, students from vocational high schools and agricultural universities, as well as farmers have acquired the necessary knowledge and skills for hydroponic agriculture as a result. Furthermore, being a digital application,  Interactive E-Curriculum, Hydroponic Agriculture Case Pool and Mobile App assisted and will assist teachers and students in developing digital literacy. All these were aimed to contribute to the development of new educational and training methods in vocational education.The overall result could also be translated into the introduction of good practices that are conducive for hydroponics
topics: Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

2022-1-RS01-KA220-VET-000088446.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-RS01-KA220-VET-000088446.title: Reducing Food Waste and Rescue Surplus Food Supplies
2022-1-RS01-KA220-VET-000088446.summary:
<< Background >>

Wast amount of food waste is generated annually across the EU, from production to consumer levels, resulting in significant economic, social, and environmental costs. Reducing this waste, whether packaged or raw, can improve resource efficiency, sustainability of food production, lower GHG emissions, and enhance public health in Europe and globally. Research indicates that targeted training programs could be instrumental in this effort by increasing awareness of food waste volumes across the Food Supply Chain, addressing environmental impact and tackling the ethical implications of global hunger (affecting nearly 12% of the population).
This project will help participants assess factors that drive food loss (self-assessment tool), identify and evaluate solutions to mitigate waste (e-learning hub), develop tools and operational strategies and address logistical challenges that generate food loss (methodology framework). It will emphasize the role of digital tools in recovering lost food. Collaboration among diverse project partners, including food waste experts, chambers of commerce, technology providers, VET trainers, NGOs, project managers and dissemination organizations, will improve the competence of all partners in this field.

<< Objectives >>

Τhe general objective of the project is to raise awareness of the importance of the problem and its possible solutions at all levels, to all actors at every step of the supply chain. Project will contribute to food rescue from waste and promote global efforts and collective action towards meeting the Sustainable Development Goal Target 12.3, which targets to halve food waste at the retail and consumer level by 2030 and reduce food losses along the food production and supply chains.
The objectives are focused on the following directions:
- Establish effective synergies and communication channels between humanitarian actors and food loss generators
- Support food loss generators in assessing and measuring food waste and related factors
- Equip humanitarian actors with tools for end-to-end food rescue chain management
- Foster innovative practices for food rescue among all food loss generators
- Enhance training for humanitarian staff involved in food distribution
- Help Ho.Re.Ca. companies and supermarkets evaluate their environmental impact
- Ensure compliance with EU regulations on food safety, hygiene, traceability, liability, etc.
- Promote a common interpretation of EU rules on surplus food redistribution across Member State

<< Implementation >>

ReS-Food consortium implemented the following activities:
UNS had developed the Project Management Plan which served as a roadmap for project implementation and communication; Project Work Plan which lists all the project’s activities and tasks and the expected time of implementation to produce a Project Result,
All project partners have signed bilateral Partnership agreements,
SIGMA had developed the Risk Management Plan, which was served as a risk management tool stipulating the main risks to the project activities,
CSKIK had developed the Dissemination and Exploitation Strategy,which was served as the main guideline for effective exploitation and dissemination,
SIGMA had developed the Quality Management Plan,which was served as the main quality assurance tool,
ALL PARTNERS: Development of main project results:Methodological Framework and e-Learning Hub,
Targeted dissemination via organizing national project multiplier events in each partner country,
Developed plans of resources and actions to ensure sustainability of the project results after its end,
Organization and attending of all project meetings,
Final reporting, including guaranteeing post project developments and preparation of final report on project implementation.

<< Results >>

ReS-Food Project Results are the following:
PR1: State Analysis Assessment Report based on an online Europe-wide assessment and interviews with environmental and food security experts,
PR2: TOOLBOX with all required tools including templates, methods, bibliography, and charts that can be used by the target group to contribute to the food distribution process,
PR3: Methodological Framework aiming to identify, communicate purpose, and select surplus food producers, define quality acceptance criteria per food category, and provide logistical support requirements for food collection and distribution,
PR4: Self-Assessment Tool with queries designed for senior managers or executives of SMEs and large enterprises within the HORECA & Supermarket sector aiming to assess their practices and actions related to the management of food waste 
PR5: Online two-fold Training Course in food management (for food waste generators and humanitarian organizations) designed to help companies in the Ho.Re.Ca. sector reduce overall food loss by passing on edible food to those who need, thus also reducing the negative impact on the environment 
All results are available on project website in English, Greek, Croatian, Hungarian and Serbian language.

2022-1-SI01-KA220-VET-000086392.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-SI01-KA220-VET-000086392.title: Prenos simulacij v medicini
2022-1-SI01-KA220-VET-000086392.summary:
<< Background >>

The TRANSSIMED project was initiated to address critical gaps in vocational education and training for healthcare professionals in Southeast Europe, particularly in the field of primary care emergency response. In Slovenia, Croatia, and North Macedonia, professionals working in primary healthcare are only rarely exposed to life-threatening situations in their daily practice. This lack of exposure, coupled with insufficient simulation-based training, contributes to reduced confidence, teamwork inefficiencies, and ultimately, compromised patient safety. 

There was a clear need to establish a structured and sustainable system of simulation-based training for primary healthcare teams in partner countries. Professionals in Slovenia, Croatia, and North Macedonia lacked opportunities for regular, practical training in managing life-threatening situations, which led to reduced preparedness, low self-confidence, and increased safety risks for patients. At the same time, there was no established system for training the trainers in simulation education at the vocational level. Additionally, vocational education in the region did not fully align with international guidelines promoting simulation in healthcare education.

<< Objectives >>

The main aim of the TRANSSIMED project was to establish sustainable, competence-based education system using simulation methods in primary healthcare, with a particular focus on vocational training. We aimed to improve patient safety and the quality of care by enhancing the preparedness of healthcare professionals to manage life-threatening situations through realistic and ethical training environments. 

Specifically, we wanted to: 
-Develop a two-level competence model for trainers in simulation-based education; 
-Provide structured culturally adapted training for basic and advanced simulation trainers tailored to education systems in all partner countries; 
-Promote the use of innovative teaching methods, (simulation based and serious gaming); 
-Align simulation-based education methods in healthcare with European quality standards in education
-Create a roadmap for implementing simulation-based education in other healthcare systems; 
-Raise awareness among policymakers and education providers about the importance of simulation in vocational education and training. 
-Achieve long-term implementation of simulation training in line with international standards. 

<< Implementation >>

1. We established a project office and a core board, ensuring regular online and in-person meetings for smooth coordination. 
2. In Slovenia, we developed d piloted a two-level competence model for simulation educators and trained basic and advanced trainers from all partner countries. 
3. Newly trained basic trainers then delivered simulation-based training to primary healthcare teams in Croatia and North Macedonia using locally adapted programmes.
4. We developed a practical Handbook for institutions aiming to establish simulation-based education centres, and created the ABCDE mobile app (game) to support training in critical situations, following the internationally recognised assessment approach.
5. We produced and presented a Roadmap to support the transfer of simulation-based education to other countries. 
6. Dissemination included conferences, publications, national events, and a project website. All activities were supported by continuous evaluation and digital tools to ensure quality, accessibility, and sustainability.


<< Results >>

1. Two-level Competence Model: A validated framework for basic and advanced simulation trainers in primary care was developed to support scalable training.
2. Training Programmes: Curricula for both levels included practical sessions, evaluation, and certification. Piloted in Slovenia, adapted for use and piloted in Croatia and North Macedonia.
3. Locally Adapted Education: Training programmes were culturally and systemically tailored and delivered to primary healthcare teams in partner countries.
4. Roadmap: A roadmap for stakeholders to establish simulation-based education in non-project countries.
5. Handbook: A practical handbook for setting up training centres
5. Digital Tools: We produced a serious game (ABCDE) , audiovisual materials, and digital content to support interactive and remote training.
6. Network of Trainers: A cross-country network of trained educators and simulation institutions was established for future collaboration.
7. Dissemination: Results were shared via EPALE, web page, national events, conferences, policy briefs, and a public online platform.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2022-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000089562.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000089562.title: The Usage of Multipurpose Tasks in Maritime Simulation
2022-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000089562.summary:
<< Background >>

82.84% of world trade is carried out by sea and the need for qualified labour force in the field of ship machinery is increasing day by day. Practical training is critical for students studying in the field of ship machinery and maintenance, but these trainings cannot always be carried out effectively due to high costs and safety risks. The COVID-19 pandemic has revealed the necessity of digitalisation in vocational education, but the lack of practical courses in the distance education process has emerged as an important problem.

This project aims to develop an innovative digital simulation for ship engine education, to provide students with a realistic workshop experience and to create an interactive platform that supports the learning process. By supporting digital transformation in vocational education, the project contributes to a repeatable, safe and cost-effective education process that is suitable for students' individual learning speed.


<< Objectives >>

With this project, we aimed to digitise vocational education in the field of ship engine and enable students to overcome the limitations they face in practical training. By developing an interactive simulation-based training platform, we aimed to enable students to practice preventive maintenance, fault detection and ship machinery management.

In addition, we aimed to improve the quality of vocational education and to develop digital content suitable for hybrid and distance education models, thus making ship machinery education more accessible, repeatable and cost-effective. The open-source education platform created within the scope of the project will not only be limited to the project partners, but will also contribute to international vocational education communities and help to close the qualified labour force gap in the maritime sector.


<< Implementation >>

Within the scope of our project, various activities were carried out to support digital transformation in ship engine education. First of all, needs analyses were conducted through surveys and meetings with teachers, students and industry representatives, and deficiencies in education were identified. Accordingly, a simulation was developed and an interactive virtual laboratory environment was created where students can learn technical subjects such as preventive maintenance and fault detection in practice. At the same time, an open source-based learning management system was integrated into the simulation and training modules were designed for use.

Pilot applications were carried out to test the project outputs and the system was improved according to the feedback received. In the final phase, training seminars and workshops were organised for project partners and dissemination activities were carried out through meetings with national participants and sector representatives. Thus, an innovative educational environment that improves the quality of vocational education and supports applied learning has been created.


<< Results >>

Within the scope of the project, an innovative training platform supporting interactive and digital learning processes for ship engine training has been developed. One of the most important tangible outputs was the training simulation on preventive maintenance and fault detection. This simulation enabled students to reinforce their theoretical knowledge with practical experience and increased the use of digital tools in vocational training.
As another output, 21 different training scenarios were prepared to be used from the simulation.
In addition, a learning management system supporting the simulation was created and the integration of simulation scenarios and training scenarios was ensured. As a result of pilot applications, the system was tested and technical improvements were made with the feedback received. In addition, trainings were organised for teachers and students and project outputs were disseminated through national meetings and webinars. Thus, a sustainable education model supporting digital vocational education has been put forward.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-2-IE01-KA220-VET-000099488.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-2-IE01-KA220-VET-000099488.title: LOTUS: Resilience in VET Education
2022-2-IE01-KA220-VET-000099488.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for LOTUS because the consortium identified an urgent need to strengthen the digital readiness, resilience, and employability of the VET community in the aftermath of COVID-19. The pandemic exposed gaps in digital pedagogy, with many teachers struggling to adapt to online and blended learning, while learners faced disrupted training, uncertainty about careers and increased stress. VET professionals required support not only to improve digital skills and create quality digital content, but also to build confidence, motivation and change management capacities. Learners needed resources to strengthen career management skills and transversal competences such as adaptability, teamwork and problem-solving, as well as strategies to cope with stress and future disruptions. LOTUS was therefore designed to meet these needs by developing an in-service training programme to build teachers’ digital pedagogy, a Toolkit to support learners in preparing, searching and securing employment, and a MOOC on resilience for both educators and learners. In this way, LOTUS responded directly to local and national partner needs while also aligning with European priorities on digital transformation, resilience, and labour market adaptability.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing LOTUS, we wanted to achieve a measurable improvement in the digital readiness, resilience and employability skills of the VET community. For VET professionals, the goal was to strengthen their capacity to design and deliver high-quality digital pedagogy, create engaging digital content and build confidence in navigating the digital transformation of education. For learners, we aimed to modernise career guidance provision by equipping them with practical tools to prepare, search and secure employment in a changing labour market, while also supporting the development of transversal skills such as adaptability, teamwork, problem-solving and critical thinking. A further aim was to promote resilience and well-being among both educators and learners. The project set out to provide strategies for coping with stress, managing change and maintaining motivation in uncertain times recognising that these qualities are as essential as technical and vocational skills for long-term success. LOTUS sought to create a set of open-access, practical and innovative resources that would have lasting impact beyond the project lifetime embedding them in everyday VET practice while also contributing to European policy priorities.

<< Implementation >>

LOTUS delivered a comprehensive set of activities across five work packages. In WP1, the Project Management Committee coordinated activities through regular meetings, financial reporting, risk reviews and structured QA and impact assessment ensuring smooth delivery. WP2 focused on the digital readiness of VET professionals: we designed and piloted an in-service training programme aligned with DigCompEdu, used the SELFIE tool for evaluation, trained 128 teachers and held a transnational activity with 12 first adopters. An Open Badge framework was created to recognise competences. WP3 developed and piloted a Toolkit of interactive infographics to support career management tested with 133 learners and validated by Local Stakeholder Panels. WP4 produced a MOOC on resilience with three themes and six units, tested with 60 stakeholders and later reaching 962 active users. WP5 implemented the dissemination plan, establishing six Local Stakeholder Panels (67 members), publishing newsletters and press releases, engaging 213 stakeholders at multiplier events, contributing articles to EPALE and reaching more than 38,000 people overall.

<< Results >>

LOTUS delivered all of the core outputs originally promised. In WP2, partners produced the LOTUS Competence Framework, developed through a Training Needs Analysis and validated against DigCompEdu. Building on this, we designed, peer-reviewed and implemented the In-Service Training Programme for VET Professionals, delivered through a modular structure addressing digital pedagogy, hybrid facilitation and media-rich content creation. The first pilot was held at a transnational training workshop in Portugal, combining 36 hours of blended instruction and marking the launch of the LOTUS Community of Practice, followed by local implementation in all partner countries. In WP3, we created 18 Interactive Infographics for Career Management each with embedded QR codes linking to bespoke mobile learning environments. These were complemented by a Tutor Handbook with lesson plans, case studies and methodologies for educators. In WP4, we developed the LOTUS MOOC on Resilience, comprising 12 hours of self-paced learning with units on personal development, social skills and lifelong learning. The MOOC also integrated innovative features such as a journaling tool for reflection. All resources are freely available in partner languages as OERs.

2023-1-BG01-KA220-VET-000158373.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-BG01-KA220-VET-000158373.title: Enhancing the skills of VET providers in the field of 3D technologies
2023-1-BG01-KA220-VET-000158373.summary:
<< Background >>

According to the European Commission, making Europe greener and more digital are twin challenges member states need to address. 3D technologies (printing, scanning, modelling) offer wide applications across sectors from architecture and construction to automotive and pharmaceutical industries, providing advantages such as customisation, design flexibility, speed, cost-efficiency, and rapid prototyping.

The 3DAcademy project was developed to address identified needs in both the VET community and the 3D technology industry.

VET institutions have invested substantially in STEM laboratories and 3D equipment but often lack qualified trainers to effectively utilise this equipment. VET teachers require ongoing training to stay current with technologies, while students need resources to develop practical skills relevant to the labour market.

In Bulgaria, Serbia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, no structured online learning resources in 3D technologies existed in local languages. VET institutions struggled to incorporate 3D equipment into curricula, resulting in STEM facilities remaining underutilised rather than serving as active knowledge-generation hubs.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the 3DAcademy project was to enhance the capacity of VET providers to offer training in and through 3D technologies (printing, scanning, modelling) to increase the uptake of new teaching approaches relevant to current and future needs of the economy and labour market. The project aimed to foster cooperation between 3D technology companies and VET providers to bridge the skills gap and enhance the quality of education and training.

Four specific objectives guided implementation:
•	SO1: Develop an online training platform providing flexible, self-paced learning with interactive digital materials in 3D technologies.
•	SO2: Provide a comprehensive training methodology and curriculum catering to the learning needs of VET educators, students, and entry-level industry staff.
•	SO3: Analyse existing qualification frameworks and initiate approval procedures for qualification standards in 3D technologies at EQF levels 1-3.
•	SO4: Disseminate results and promote use among target groups and stakeholders, engaging industry experts to ensure relevance to labour market needs.

<< Implementation >>

Project management (WP1): BICC coordinated the 10-partner consortium through four transnational meetings (Sofia, Belgrade, Zagreb and 1 online) and 18 online meetings.  

Online platform development (WP2): Partners mapped existing platforms, developed methodology, and created the 3DAcademy multilingual platform featuring nine learning modules (five basic, four advanced), self-assessment tools, glossary, automated certification, and digital badges. Content was localised into five languages and pre-tested with stakeholders.

Blended training programme (WP3): Partners researched existing training offers and assessed 3D technology equipment across approximately 170 VET institutions. Two comprehensive training manuals were developed (Newcomers and Advanced Trainers). A Train-the-Trainers workshop in Zagreb trained 12 educators, followed by piloting with 65 students across four countries.

Qualification framework (WP4): Partners developed three microcredential programmes for Bulgaria, Croatia, and Serbia, initiating national approval procedures with VET authorities.
Dissemination (WP5): Partners implemented a social media campaign (195 posts, combined reach exceeding 234,000), organised eight dissemination events engaging 242 part.

<< Results >>

The project produced the following concrete outputs:
Online platform: The 3DAcademy platform (https://3d-academy.eu/) provides nine learning modules in five languages (EN, BG, HR, SR, BS), with self-assessment tools, glossary, automated certification, and digital badges.
Training programme: Two comprehensive manuals were developed – Manual for Newcomers and Manual for Advanced Trainers – including lesson plans, learning scenarios, practical assignments, tools packages, and evaluation instruments. All materials are available in five languages.
Trained educators: The Train-the-Trainers workshop trained 12 VET educators in teaching and using 3D technologies to enhance the teaching process. Piloting engaged 65 students and 8 trainers across Bulgaria, Croatia, Serbia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Qualification frameworks: Three national microcredential qualifications were developed and submitted or prepared for submission to national VET authorities.
Dissemination impact: The social media campaign achieved 195 posts with a combined reach exceeding 234,000 individuals. Eight events engaged 242 participants. All results are freely accessible as open educational resources through the project website and Erasmus+ Project Results Platform.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2023-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000155846.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000155846.title: Deep Tech & Robotics for Human-Centered Manufacturing Systems
2023-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000155846.summary:
<< Objectives >>

-A common reference and Methodology for working, education and training in manufacturing

2023-1-EL01-KA220-VET-000166512.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-EL01-KA220-VET-000166512.title: Safer driving behaviour for last-mile-delivery professionals through digital and multidisciplinary training
2023-1-EL01-KA220-VET-000166512.summary:
<< Background >>

The project addresses the urgent need to improve the road safety skills and driving performance of last-mile delivery two-wheelers, who are among the most vulnerable road users and experience high accident rates due to their working conditions being constantly on the road. 
Despite EU progress in road safety, fatalities and serious injuries among motorcyclists, cyclists, e-scooter and e-bike riders remain disproportionately high. In Mediterranean countries, where climate conditions favour two-wheeler-based deliveries, the rapid expansion of e-commerce and food delivery services nowadays has further increased exposure to road safety risks, particularly related to driver fatigue, distraction, high traffic density and limited access to structured professional training.
The needs addressed by this project relate to the lack of tailored and practical vocational education and training for last-mile delivery professionals. By combining physical and digital training activities, the project aims to improve driving behaviour, risk awareness, enhance professional qualifications and contribute to safer urban mobility for all road users, in line with Erasmus+ VET priorities and EU road safety objectives.

<< Objectives >>

The SaferDeli project aimed at enhancing the road safety skills of last-mile delivery two-wheelers (motorcyclists, cyclists, and e-scooter riders) who are vulnerable road users with high accident rates. The goal was to develop and implement an advanced and holistic vocational training approach, customized to their work-based needs.
Being aware of the challenges of road safety education of the specific sector, the focus of the partnership was on jointly developing the multidisciplinary material and virtual learning platform as well as implementing the in-person seminars, to properly train them on specific topics (i) that are relevant to their everyday tasks, (ii) that really concerns them in real-life, and (iii) that really attracts their interest. To this end, the effective mix of digital and in-person training methods on VET was exploited to upskill and protect delivery professionals from being involved in road accidents and, ultimately, reduce work-related accidents while supporting safer, more sustainable and responsible riding.

<< Implementation >>

SaferDeli addressed road safety challenges faced by last-mile delivery two-wheeler professionals, aiming to enhance their driving behaviour through the following key activities:
-	Exchange of good practices on education and training of last-mile logistics
-	Data collection through stated preference questionnaire survey to delivery professionals in partner countries to analyze training gaps and needs
-	Development of customized training material structured in the format of an online self-paced open course of 9 Modules, available in 6 languages
-	Development of a gamified virtual learning platform for delivery professionals with interactive elements, tested by experts and end-users, available in 6 languages
-	Elaboration of scenario-based examination scheme for skills assessment and certificate acquisition
-	Implementation of in-person training seminars of professionals per country
-	Definition of strategies and recommendations for uptaking project results, supported by stakeholder engagement and signed Letters of Intent
-	Realization of final event in Cyprus for wide dissemination of tools developed
-	Dissemination through the website, social media, e-newsletters and participation in several external events achieving wide reach.

<< Results >>

SaferDeli delivered a set of outputs aligned with its objectives. Effective coordination mechanisms, knowledge-exchange activities, exploitation actions, stakeholder engagement and LoIs, led to:
- A blended vocational training procedure including online activities (smart virtual learning platform, open course, examination scheme) and in-person ones (seminars, meetings, framework)
- An online open course with interdisciplinary training material on road safety tailor-made for last-mile-delivery professionals given in an attractive way in 6 languages, along with relevant qualification certificate exams
- A virtual learning platform incorporating the training material of the course in a gamified format with interactive elements, quizzes, etc.
- Trained delivery professionals through vocational training sessions on road safety and driving behaviour with experienced trainers
- Strategies and recommendations to pave the way towards integrating competences of enhanced driving behaviour into existing requirements for delivery two-wheelers, supporting the long-term use of project results
- Closer cooperation & upskilling between the academia, vocational and private sector for the common goal of innovative VET on urban logistics and safety
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2023-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000153245.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000153245.title: Big Data unites the Sciences and the Arts
2023-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000153245.summary:
<< Background >>

One of the main aims was to promote the use of Big Data by using free hardware accessible and user-friendly techniques. Another aim was to increase equal opportunity and combat discrimination. It should be noted that discriminatory treatment comes from fear and ignorance that lead to prejudices linked to rejection. We therefore deem that knowledge is the best antidote against discrimination. But,  
In current education, immersed in digital transformation, understanding of digital techniques and tools is greatly needed in order to process and analyze a great deal of data. We consider that the use of real data can be a means to increase socio-cultural awareness among the participants. With creating datasets on specific topics, we wanted to promote the use of truthful information, increasing ethical and cross-cultural values that should lead citizens committed to their surroundings. The purpose of generating datasets linked to the diverse countries involved in the project was to enhance the knowledge of other cultures so that the richness of Europe’s cultural diversity could be properly understood.    


<< Objectives >>

Mainly: addressing the digital transformation through the use of Big Data and the awareness of the importance of using truthful information to generate scientific analysis on science, art, development cooperation, multiculturalism, inclusion, empowerment of women in STEAM disciplines, democratic values and diversity of the European countries. Specifically: increasing knowledge and importance of data digitalization; improving the employability and employment approach of students to the labor market; fostering the fight against planned obsolescence by recycling electronic and IT equipments; promoting digital skills and capabilities for innovation and business entrepreneurship by stimulating the participants with fewer opportunities and encouraging female students to take an interest in STEAM fields; fostering knowledge about European common, democratic and civic values among participants in the project; boosting awareness of reducing, recycling and reuse of IT equipments, clothing, books, etc.; discovering and sharing new forms of digital teaching during visits to each country and making participants aware of the importance of realizing collaborative projects with regions affected by natural disasters and/or developing countries.

<< Implementation >>

In order to capacitate participants to tackle successfully challenging computing tasks related to the creation of Dataset, there have been training sessions -online and on-site meetings in the mobilities-  about Data mining techniques to empower all partners in creating forms and organizing information in spreadsheets. Next, having established the importance of a deep understanding of the application of statistics, participants started to gather specific data in their respective countries. Then, all the project partners implemented their computing skills by practicing how to create arff files. Participants have also been visiting institutions and companies closely related to Big Data in the different countries. On the other hand, several recycling workshops have been carried out in which participants have learned how to proceed in order to give a second life to many varied materials. These cultural programmes and all the collaborative activities mentioned have broadened our personal perspective on other cultures and traditions, which contributes to bringing European citizens closer together and strengthening the bond between them.

<< Results >>

Students and teachers have created a large dataset on EU knowledge. And a second test to measure their digital skills. More than 3.000 people answered the questions and the survey results were analyzed. In addition, a health dataset with blood pressure measurements and physical data of more than 100 people was made at  the mobility of Croatia to then analyse them. In the different upcycling workshops, attendees have elaborate diverse items from varied materials and customized second hand clothing. These crafts have been sold in charity scholar markets and all the money obtained has been used for NGOs projects. The coordinator team has created different training materials about the WEKA platform (tutorials, tests, practices, etc.) as well as a website in which they have been sharing all these materials, and Spanish teachers have developed a Java application to process and display the UE test. On the other hand, each school has carried out research about a particular topic, elaborated a dataset, analyzed the data and made the results known. Finally, some visits have been made to organisms and companies linked to Big Data (this information at annex)

2023-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000153677.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000153677.title: KITS DE AYUDA EDUCATIVA EN EL ÁMBITO DE LAS ENFERMEDADES RARAS: LLEVAR LA REALIDAD DE LAS ENFERMEDADES RARAS A LA FP
2023-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000153677.summary:
<< Background >>

Rare Diseases (RDs) include thousands of diverse pathologies of low prevalence, usually chronic, with very severe sequelae and an unfavorable prognosis. But due to the lack of knowledge about these RDs (a lack of training and information from care specialists), the professionals who care for those who suffer from them run the risk of being negligent and even harmful to them.
Especially in Vocational Training (VET), there is very little curricular content related to RDs: teachers do not have specific training, and experts are not sufficiently involved (generating less qualified professionals and inclusion problems for people with RRS), which makes specific training, educational resources, and a multidisciplinary training approach essential.
In order to address these needs, our network of expert entities in RDs developed this project, with which we have provided the VET teaching programme (in health and socio-cultural services) with specific contents in RDs, a course for VET teachers, and a training methodology with specific OERs,  achieving an enormous impact on future professionals and on the well-being of people with RDs.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of this project were to transform Vocational Training (VET) into a more inclusive and accessible education for people with RDs, encouraging them to develop their studies in equity, in addition to training future professionals without RDs in the care of this target group, avoiding possible negligence due to the lack of current knowledge about RDs, opening new paths to employability.
Specifically, we have met objectives related to:
1. The Network of entities, such as improving our quality of work, activities, and practices by enhancing our sustainability and digital processes; develop our capabilities to work transnationally and across sectors; and addressing the priorities and needs common to the field of VET and RDs.
2. VET, such as promoting training in RDs in health and socio-cultural services vocational training; to improve teachers’ practices and training in RDs; and to transform VET and its action towards people with RDs through innovative digital methodologies.
3. People with RDs themselves, such as promoting the inclusion and safety of those who suffer from them; raising awareness of RDs in Europe; and facilitating access for students with RDs to VET.

<< Implementation >>

All the activities planned and successfully implemented within the framework of the project were structured in 5 Work Packages:
‒ WP1. PROJECT MANAGEMENT: general coordination, technical and quality monitoring, periodic virtual meetings, initial training of participants, and application of transversal approaches in inclusion, sustainability, and digitalization.
‒ WP2. DEVELOPMENT OF THE GUIDE: design and drafting of the Guide for the inclusion of students with RDs in VET, selection of participants, the M1 
‒ WP5. DISSEMINATION: creation of the Dissemination and Sustainability Plan, development of the Website, campaigns on social networks, 5 Multiplier Events (2 in ES, IT, PT, FR), creation of the Advisory Service, and creation of a European Network active in 12 countries, reaching more than 2500 beneficiaries.

<< Results >>

During the course of the project we have developed, in addition to several tangible, structural, and learning outcomes, 4 main results:
‒ A METHODOLOGICAL GUIDE (R1) for the inclusion of students with RDs and on the use of educational kits for the care of these students in VET.
‒ The EDUCATIONAL KITS (R2) themselves for the care of people with RDs (educational materials for teachers and students of vocational training in health and sociocultural services).
‒ The VIRTUAL COURSE (R3) to train VET teachers in the use of resources and methodology.
‒ An ADVISORY AND GUIDANCE SERVICE FOR TEACHERS (R4) by experts in RDs.
These results are complemented by the tangible results (R5: the project website and its dissemination materials and R6: the European Network itself), structural results (R7: improvement of networking and the international impact of entities, R8: improvement of sustainability and digital practices of entities, and R9: improvement of synergies between entities and VET), and learning results (R10: development of students’ competences, R11: development of teachers’ competences, and R12: improvement of the educational competences of students with RDs).
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2023-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000154369.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000154369.title: Mental Health Toolkit for Human Resources Managers in the workforce
2023-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000154369.summary:
<< Background >>

The MH4HRM project was designed to address the growing need to integrate mental health and well-being into human resource management. Digitalisation, increasing psychosocial risks, workplace pressure, and changes in working environments have highlighted the limited preparedness of many organisations to effectively manage mental health issues in the workplace. Key needs identified included the lack of specialised training for HR professionals, the shortage of practical and digital tools, the need to reduce the stigma associated with mental health issues, and the improvement of organisational capacities to promote healthy, inclusive, and resilient work environments. MH4HRM addressed these challenges through European cooperation, the exchange of good practices, and the development of innovative training resources aimed at strengthening mental health management within organisations.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of MH4HRM was to enhance the competencies of human resource professionals and people managers in preventing, identifying, and effectively managing mental health challenges in the workplace. The project sought to provide both technical knowledge and transversal skills, develop innovative digital tools, raise awareness of psychosocial risks, and facilitate the exchange of good practices among experts in mental health, vocational education and training, and human resource management. In addition, MH4HRM aimed to promote the use of digital learning methodologies, improve the responsiveness of vocational education and training to labour market needs, and foster an organisational culture focused on well-being, inclusion, and employee support. Ultimately, MH4HRM contributed to the creation of healthier, more resilient, and more sustainable workplaces across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through five work packages that combined project management, research, content development, digital innovation, validation, dissemination, and sustainability activities.The project began with an analysis of European best practices in workplace mental health management to identify relevant competencies, tools, and methodologies for HR professionals. Building on these findings, the consortium developed a 60-hour training programme together with a range of practical resources designed to support the prevention and management of psychosocial risks in the workplace. Subsequently, a digital learning ecosystem was created, comprising an e-learning platform, a web/mobile application, microlearning videos, and podcasts, all available in multiple languages. The resources were piloted and validated by HR professionals and companies from Spain, Portugal, Italy, Greece, and Croatia, enabling the consortium to refine and improve the content based on participants’ feedback and practical experiences. In parallel, dissemination and stakeholder engagement activities, including multiplier events and a final conference, helped maximise the visibility, sustainability, and long-term impact of the project results.

<< Results >>

MH4HRM developed a comprehensive workplace mental health training programme for HR professionals, together with an e-learning platform, a web/mobile application, microlearning videos, podcasts, reports, practical materials, and support resources for organisations. The resources were piloted and validated in five European countries, demonstrating significant improvements in participants’ confidence, knowledge, and readiness to address mental health issues in the workplace. The project also established a European network of around 195 stakeholders, promoted the exchange of good practices, and raised awareness of the importance of mental health for employee well-being and organisational sustainability. Thanks to its multilingual, digital, and open-access nature, MH4HRM provides an innovative, transferable, and sustainable solution that will continue to benefit HR professionals, companies, training providers, and policymakers beyond the project's lifetime.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2023-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000158794.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training

Using EU Green Deal & GreenComp we will focus on building educators’ pedagogic competences in the areas to technical green and soft skills development through immersive digital resources. For VET learners, the dual model of intervention proposed will achieve positive vocational outcomes for learners building their future careers.

We will host virtual, in-person training activities & tailored multiplier events and seminars. All resources and materials developed will be accessible, open source and widely disseminated through the GREEN SHOOTS online dissemination channels.

2023-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000156509.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000156509.title: Good Job!
2023-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000156509.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Good Job! aims to support the transition of young people with learning disabilities and difficulties from school to adulthood and employment. The projects enables educators to identify the potential and difficulties in young people, then empowers them as Transition Mentors to support the young people through coaching and mentoring and finally reaches out and facilitates sustainable and inclusive transition policies between VET and school education institutions and socially responsible employers.

<< Implementation >>

The partnership uses a robust management plan, including a system for quality assurance, impact evaluation and dissemination strategies to first research and prepare the content of a competence Assessment tool. Secondly, the partnership introduces adapted coaching and mentoring techniques and trains educators to become Transition Mentors. Finally, schools and employers are supported to work together on transition solutions for the target group. All outputs are tested, finalized and disseminated.

Finally, to enhance transition policies in training institutions and inclusion in workplaces a Transition Mentor’s Toolkit and Sustainability Pack for organisations are designed to facilitate the inter-institutional application of the Good Job! approach.

2023-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000159807.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000159807.title: Text it Easy!
2023-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000159807.summary:
<< Objectives >>

There are methods to reduce inequalities in the written word. Plain language is an international standard that facilitates the comprehension of written information in paper and digital form. Text it Easy aims to disseminate clear language in all professional sectors, first and foremost in the field of professional training, to improve access to information and communication for all citizens and thus promote their inclusion and involvement in society.

<< Implementation >>

This project will involve research, resource development, and evaluation to produce a Methodology and Operational Framework for writing plain language texts in a learning context. Training, both face-to-face and online, for the VET community will transfer skills within and outside the partnership.

Finally, we would like this project to be the starting point for a Europe-wide reflection on reference materials for all European languages and an associated scoring function to easily evaluate the clarity of texts.

2023-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000160047.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000160047.title: Careers for Carers
2023-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000160047.summary:
<< Background >>

The Career for Carers (CforC) project arose from the challenges observed at European level concerning careers in elderly care. Indeed, European Union countries are currently facing a double challenge in this area. On the one hand, due to the ageing population observed in most Member States and the resulting increase in the number of elderly people losing all or part of their independence, the demand for staff in the elderly care sector is also growing. On the other hand, this ageing also applies to current members of the sector, which is already facing a shortage of staff coupled with a lack of attractiveness of these professions. The consortium has therefore identified the need to create new innovative tools to attract, raise awareness and train young people (aged 18-29), who themselves face higher unemployment rates than the rest of the population. The project is therefore betting on young people as an opportunity to adapt our societies to demographic challenges while cultivating intergenerational relationships.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the Careers for Carers (CforC) project was to address recruitment challenges in the elderly care sector by developing innovative tools to attract, raise awareness and train young people (aged 18-29) in these professions. The project therefore targeted young people who were interested or potentially interested in the field of elderly care and who wished to acquire the necessary skills and knowledge. The specific objectives of the project were: 1) to use gamification to introduce young people to the themes and field of elderly care, 2) to provide e-learning training modules to acquire the basic knowledge required to move towards qualifications for these professions, 3) to develop a booklet of good practices and advice for building a career in the field of elderly care.

<< Implementation >>

The implementation of the project was divided into five work packages (WPs), including a ‘Project Management’ WP and an ‘Impact and Dissemination’ WP.
WP2 ‘Escape Game’ consisted of the preliminary design (A2.1), then the development and testing (A2.2-A2.4) of an escape game before the project's target groups participated (A2.6) in this tool. This escape game was intended to be an innovative tool to attract young people aged 18 to 29 (students, students in a care-related field, unemployed people, NEETS) to careers in personal care, particularly elderly care.
WP3 ‘Training’ consisted of the development (A3.1-A3.5) of e-learning training content on the basics of elderly care for the project's target groups. The aim was to follow up on the escape game by giving them the keys (A3.7) to start taking an interest in careers in elderly care.
WP4 ‘Career counselling and best practice booklet’ consisted of the development (A4.1-A4.3) of a booklet serving as a guide for young people wishing to build a career in the elderly care sector.

<< Results >>

During the implementation of the project, the consortium produced four major results: 1) A virtual escape game on the reality of elderly care, designed to attract and raise awareness among young people about careers in this sector in an innovative way. 2) E-learning modules enabling learners to acquire basic knowledge before moving on to qualifications for working in elderly care professions. 3) A booklet of best practices and advice to support young people in their career guidance and development in the elderly care sector 4) A model for career guidance sessions related to care professions
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2023-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000154168.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000154168.title:
Development of Joint Curriculum for First Responders on the
Tactical Procedures in the Use of Force and First Aid
2023-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000154168.summary:
<< Background >>

First responding police officers cover all lines of police work and their actions have to be planned and implemented almost instantly, regardless of the incident, disaster, attack or crime. On top of everything, their conduct is often under the public eye. All that put a lot of pressure on their daily job and require well-practiced skills and sharpness. However, these categories of police officers have the least educational opportunities after the basic training, and their later trainings take place in-house - which is why they differ quite a bit on national level, and even more so on the EU level. First responders must be trained to deal with a wide array of potential emergencies and security issues and this project aims to standardize these trainings and, consequently, improve and harmonize the conduct of first responders. Its goal is to develop an international training concept for enhancing skills in first responders through interactive learning. This concept will allow project partners to create, test and introduce an innovative training practice, tailored to the needs of adult learners, specifically uniformed police officers.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective was to improve, harmonize and standardize conduct of first responders in partner countries, in tactics and techniques in the use of force and first aid - through the new curriculum and training manual that the partners developed jointly. It enabled teaching staff, experts and participants of pilot trainings to exchange experience and good practices in both teaching methods and police tactics. Ultimately, it will make first responders better equipped for daily challenges.

<< Implementation >>

Analysis of current partners’ national curricula on the use of force and first aid, and development of a joint curriculum for first responders on the use of force and first aid, with manual for the trainers and train-the-trainer workshop.
Implementation of the developed curriculum in four pilot trainings in partner countries.
Dissemination of the intellectual outputs among the trainers who conduct trainings on the use of force tactics and techniques and first aid, through train-the-trainers workshop.
Wider dissemination of the results through project web site and closing conference.


<< Results >>

PR1 Joint curriculum and training manual developed;
PR2 Four pilot trainings in partner countries implemented;

2023-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000156640.title: Blended Sustainability Training for Livestock and Animal Food Production
2023-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000156640.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project to address the crucial, complex, and mutually threatening relationship between the livestock sector and climate change. Existing agricultural vocational education (VET) curricula were deficient, lacking comprehensive content on climate change mitigation, adaptation, and sustainable animal production. A needs analysis confirmed that sustainable livestock was not a separate course but only a module within existing lessons, and that students and teachers lacked sufficient knowledge about the EU's Farm-to-Fork strategy and the livestock sector’s emission reduction targets. The project addressed the need to train a qualified workforce capable of implementing enterprise-based solutions for sustainability and filling the skill mismatch in the labour market. 

<< Objectives >>

The primary objectives were to:
-Contribute to EU targets on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving food safety, and supporting the Farm-to-Fork strategy.
-Increase the knowledge and skill levels of VET students, technicians, and farmers by developing educational materials focused on sustainable livestock and food production.
-Prepare VET students better for the job market in agricultural vocational high schools.
-Ensure the adaptation of enterprises to new conditions by providing a sustainability specialist workforce.
-Bring innovation to VET by creating the first online platform, curriculum, and mobile application focused on sustainable animal husbandry in the partner regions.

<< Implementation >>

The key activities implemented in the work packages included:
-Creating educational content for an online learning management system (LMS). This content covered environmental impacts, sustainable animal husbandry, sustainable animal-based food production, and new technologies in agriculture.
-Developing and piloting a new agricultural high school elective curriculum in sustainable animal husbandry.
-Organizing an LTTA on automation systems and sustainable livestock in Slovakia.
-Providing practical training and on-the-job observation activities in cooperation with agri-businesses in Croatia, Romania, and Turkey.
-Organizing an international student-teacher joint workshop (LTTA) in Turkey focusing on practical business-school cooperation.
-Developing an online case pool of application to integrate practical training with distance learning. 
-Developing a digital flash cards application to include game-based learning on the topic of sustainable animal husbandry. 
-TPMs to strengthen collaboration between partners
-eTwinning project to spread the project impact to non-partner schools, students and teachers.


<< Results >>

- An e-learning platform (PR1) was created to provide accessible online education on sustainable animal husbandry. 
- An elective curriculum for agricultural high schools (PR2) was created to integrate sustainability topics into vocational education. 
- A sustainable livestock case pool (PR3) was created to provide real-life examples and best practices for teachers and students. 
- A digital flash cards mobile application (PR4) was designed to support interactive and flexible learning. 
In addition to these products, a permanent education network was established between vocational high schools and universities to encourage ongoing cooperation, support new studies, and improve the quality of vocational education in agriculture.

2023-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000150559.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000150559.title: Green Skills 4 VET
2023-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000150559.summary:
<< Background >>

The GS4VET project was created to bridge the gap between the VET system and the production world regarding Green Skills, within the context of European and national priorities set by the Green Deal, the 2030 Agenda, the Paris Declaration, and the Recovery Plan. High environmental impact sectors were selected (Agriculture, Mechanical, Textile-Fashion, Logistics-Transport), tasked with addressing concrete sustainability challenges by transferring environmental issues from the business to the educational context. The proposal promotes synergies between the VET system and the economic fabric to integrate the school-business supply chain, facilitating the transfer of real cases and supporting the adaptation of training offers to sustainability priorities. The project develops and experiments with interdisciplinary programs to introduce curricula focused on green skills at mono-sectoral and inter/cross-sectoral levels, adopting work-based learning and innovative methodologies such as the Flipped Classroom. These new VET curricula, integrating sustainability as a standalone or transversal subject, are designed to train students and teachers prepared to consciously drive the Green Transition, supporting European and national objectives.

<< Objectives >>

In line with the priorities “Environment and Climate Action” and “Adapting VET to Labour Market Needs,” the project pursues the following GENERAL OBJECTIVES: a) to transfer real environmental sustainability challenges from high-impact production contexts into VET to integrate the School-Business supply chain and align demand and supply. It develops green skills in teachers and learners, innovates curricula according to labour market needs, and introduces sustainability as a standalone or interdisciplinary subject, with work- and problem-based programs designed and tested based on real scenarios; b) for the priority “Inclusion and Diversity,” GS4VET develops learner-centered inclusive learning methods aimed at motivating vulnerable students, those with low performance, cultural/linguistic barriers, or at risk of dropping out.
The SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES correspond to the implemented Work Packages: WP2 fosters dialogue between VET and businesses to familiarize with concrete sustainability issues; WP3 and WP4 develop and validate for transferability, respectively, inclusive mono-sectoral and inter/cross-sectoral educational programs based on innovative and engaging approaches such as work/problem-based learning and the Flipped Classroom.

<< Implementation >>

All WP activities were completed, achieving objectives and meeting indicators. In WP2, sectoral analyses were carried out for each VET Provider, identifying sustainability problems in the four sectors. Four business testimonial pathways were conducted, including guided visits, discussions, and challenge launches from business partners to students. A didactic case was designed for each VET Provider, with multi-format materials and feedback forms. In WP3, students studied the cases and completed feedback, while teachers developed and tested 4 mono-sectoral programs with business support. WP4 included in-person training to design inter/cross-sectoral cases, followed by didactic adaptation, individual study, development, and work-based testing of 4 programs, with remote collaborative work between students and companies from different countries and sectors. All 8 programs were validated by the partnership and released as OER, confirming effectiveness, feasibility, and replicability, with multilingual guidelines released as OER. WP5 delivered 5 multiplier events featuring presentations, results sharing, stakeholder dialogue, and feedback collection.

<< Results >>

The project produced concrete results in all WPs. WP2: 4 documents to design didactic cases and feedback forms to transfer real sustainability issues related to the involved sectors into VET; 4 business testimonial pathways as described above; WP3: 5 educational programs to introduce sustainability in VET at a sector-specific level. WP4: training materials to design inter/cross-sectoral didactic cases; 4 educational programs to introduce sustainability in VET at the inter/cross-sectoral level. Multilingual guidelines for replicability (WP2, 3, and 4). OTHER OUTPUT from WP3 and WP4 for reuse include open templates for: documentation of materials for didactic case construction; feedback forms (students) and summary sheets (teachers); evaluation forms (companies); 2 reports validating Green Skills developed in WP3 and WP4 with reference tables (GreenComp, ESCO, EQF frameworks) and web resources; 2 impact assessment reports of WBL-based experiments, with related indicators and recommendations for replicability; step-by-step replication of WP3 experiments; individual satisfaction monitoring for multiplier event audiences.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
