2023-1-LV01-KA220-VET-000166919.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-LV01-KA220-VET-000166919.title: Seafarers Experience Appealing For Shore
2023-1-LV01-KA220-VET-000166919.summary:
<< Background >>

The SEA4SHORE project was initiated to address critical workforce challenges in the European maritime sector. Seafarers typically spend less than five years at sea due to the profession's demanding nature, leading to a significant loss of invested educational resources. Simultaneously, shore-based maritime industries face a severe shortage of qualified personnel who possess actual sea experience. We applied for this project because there was no standardized, digital mechanism to help seafarers transfer their highly valuable competencies to land-based roles. The project addressed the urgent need to map transferable skills and provide accessible career guidance. By bridging this gap, the project sought to increase the attractiveness of maritime Vocational Education and Training (VET), promote occupational mobility, and ensure that the vital skills acquired at sea are not lost but effectively utilized within the broader European maritime economy.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objective of the SEA4SHORE project was to increase the attractiveness of maritime Vocational Education and Training (VET) and facilitate the smooth transition of seafarers to shore-based careers. Because the average working time at sea is often less than five years, valuable skills and training investments are frequently lost. Simultaneously, shore-based maritime sectors face a critical shortage of personnel with practical sea experience. To resolve this imbalance, we aimed to map and promote alternative shore-based career paths, ensuring that the informal and non-formal competencies acquired at sea are formally recognized and effectively transferred to land-based roles. Our concrete goals included developing a comprehensive competency map for shore-based job profiles and creating an innovative, multilingual online platform and assessment tool. Through these outputs, we sought to foster continuous professional development, increase occupational mobility across Europe, and strengthen the overall maritime labor market by systematically matching experienced seafarers with the companies that desperately need their specialized skills.

<< Implementation >>

The SEA4SHORE project was implemented across five highly structured work packages. We began with comprehensive research to map shore-based professions. This involved identifying 125 national career profiles across our partner countries, analyzing specific labor market needs, and creating detailed job descriptions. Following this, we developed the Shore Integration Platform. We gathered direct industry feedback through targeted questionnaires and formulated 61 real-world case studies of successful officer transitions to create robust educational content. To operationalize this data, we programmed and rigorously piloted the Seafarers Shore Integration Tool, an interactive digital assessment platform allowing seafarers to evaluate their transferable skills. Finally, we executed an extensive dissemination strategy. This included hosting five national multiplier events across Europe and a final international conference in Latvia, directly engaging 367 stakeholders to officially launch our digital tools and ensure the project's long-term sustainability.

<< Results >>

The SEA4SHORE project successfully delivered several concrete, high-impact results designed to facilitate the transition of seafarers to shore-based careers. The foundational output was a comprehensive Competency Map and Needs Analysis, which identified and detailed 125 specific shore-based maritime career profiles across our partner countries. Building on this research, we developed the Shore Integration Platform, an innovative, multilingual awareness hub containing 61 real-world case studies of successful officer transitions and robust VET pedagogical reports. The technological centerpiece of the project was the Seafarers Shore Integration Tool, a fully functional, rigorously piloted online assessment application. This interactive tool allows seafarers to evaluate their competencies against ESCO based profiles aligned with EQF and STCW standards to determine their readiness for specific land-based roles. Furthermore, our dissemination efforts resulted in the successful execution of five national multiplier events and one final international conference, directly engaging 367 key industry stakeholders, while our digital outreach achieved over 2,700 unique platform visitors.

2023-1-MK01-KA220-VET-000162058.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-MK01-KA220-VET-000162058.title: Advancing Digital Education with Open Learning Environment
2023-1-MK01-KA220-VET-000162058.summary:
<< Background >>

The ADELE project was a direct reaction to the fact that digital transformation of vocational education and training on the European continent was in dire need. Through the COVID-19 pandemic, the process of educational delivery had completely changed and revealed some serious flaws in digital preparedness of vocational institutions and their employees. Our four secondary vocational schools consortium in North Macedonia, Croatia, and Slovenia realised that teachers and learners needed enhanced digital literacy to keep pace with the fast-changing labour markets.
The two had worked together before in the ERASMUS + IDADOHS project that created an open learning platform of educational resources. Although the technical infrastructure was available, there was an obvious missing element in terms of high-quality STEM content to fill such a setting and a consistent training on how to utilize it. Educators in our schools were not confident and competent in developing digital learning contents and learners were not able to access many interactive technological enhanced materials in their home learning situations. An additional necessity that was discovered by us was the necessity to have inclusive and accessible educational resources. 

<< Objectives >>

The ADELE project pursued three interconnected strategic objectives aligned with European educational priorities.

First, we aimed to advance STEM digital transformation by enhancing the open learning platform developed in our previous IDADOHS project, incorporating innovative technologies including artificial intelligence to provide personalised learning pathways and interactive assessments for vocational students.

Second, we sought to promote inclusion and diversity by applying universal design principles and culturally responsive pedagogy throughout all developed materials, ensuring learners with visual, auditory, or cognitive differences could fully access educational content.

Third, we committed to creating high-quality open educational resources released under Creative Commons licensing, enabling free use, adaptation, and sharing across European vocational institutions. This supported lifelong learning opportunities beyond our immediate partnership.
Underlying these objectives was our goal to strengthen educators' digital competencies, building their confidence and skills to develop and deliver technology-enhanced instruction that prepares students for modern labour market demands.

<< Implementation >>

ADELE project involved 4 work packages that were interdependent and took place over a 24 months period. A good project governance was developed by having strong transnational partner meetings in North Macedonia, Croatia, and Slovenia, and with online arrangement of coordination meetings applying digital tools such as Asana, GoogleMeet  and VIBER. The 28 educators of the partner institutions were trained during two intensive workshops in Zagreb and Gostivar on topics of digital content creation, use of platforms, and accessibility standards and universal design principles. The main action was the creation of 24 STEM courses in English (out of our target of 20) five courses each of the partner and four more courses of outside collaboration schools. All the contents were released as open learning resources on the IDADOHS platform. Such dissemination activities were held as local workshops to over 200 educators, presentations at large-scale events like Educational Rendezvous MASSUM 2025, INOVA-MLADI 2025 innovation exhibition, and the UP conference and careful quality assurance assessment efforts were carried out by specific partners charged with the responsibility of accessibility review, peer assessment and stakeholder feedback.

<< Results >>

The ADELE project created 24 high-quality STEM courses in English (vastly surpassing our initial goal of 20) and included such disciplines as electrical engineering fundamental, computer programming, automation systems, mechanical design, and digital technologies. Every course was released as open educational resources on the Creative Commons licensing on the improved IDADOHS open learning platform, which currently boasts superior accessibility functions. The project directly prepared 28 educators (six professors and one administrator per partner institution) as developers of material and administrators of the platform, and all participants were provided with Europa pass certificates of the competences gained. Data on pre- and post-assessment showed that on average, trained educators were able to improve in scores in digital competency by 35%. Promotional events spread out among more than 200 other educators in the three partner countries at local workshops and four larger promotional events. The consortium also worked on a system of comprehensive digital content development training methodology in vocational education, quality assurance framework to assess open educational resource and best practice principles.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2023-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000155267.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000155267.title: NuGamers Creative orientation activities for a more gender-inclusive gaming education
2023-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000155267.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for NuGamers to respond to a clear skills and equality gap in the European gaming sector. Although women increasingly play games, they remain strongly under-represented in both gaming education and the industry (around 20–24% of students in partner VET programmes, 23% of employees in Sweden), limiting diversity of teams, content and perspectives.

Our VET and HE partners offering game-related courses (Futuregames, XAMK, AUC) had a shared need to attract more women, but their orientation activities and curricula were not yet explicitly designed from a gender-inclusive perspective. Staff involved in outreach and programme design reported low awareness of gendered barriers, few concrete tools, and little specific training.

The partnership therefore sought Erasmus+ support to co-create a solid knowledge base on gender bias in gaming education, and to turn it into practical handbooks and creative tools that help VET and HE providers design more inclusive curricula and orientation activities, address stereotypes and harassment, and ultimately increase women’s participation in gaming and related STEM paths.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to change how VET and HE providers in the gaming sector design and run their programmes so that girls, women and gender-diverse learners feel invited, supported and able to succeed. Concretely, our objectives were to: 1) increase knowledge and awareness of gender bias and barriers in gaming education and careers; 2) strengthen the capacity of VET and HE staff to think and act in a more gender-inclusive way when planning curricula, teaching and guidance; 3) create practical, research-based resources – a fact sheet, handbook and toolkit – that offer ready-to-use activities for outreach, orientation and classroom work; and 4) ultimately help VET providers attract and retain more women in game-development studies, building a more diverse and inclusive European games sector.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented a coherent sequence of activities linking research, co-design, production and dissemination. First, partners carried out desk research on women in gaming and focus groups with female students and developers in Sweden, Finland and Croatia; the findings fed into the NuGamers fact sheet. We then held a transnational co-design lab and local validation labs with VET/HE staff, school teachers and students to shape the handbook on gender-inclusive curricula and orientation practices.

For the toolkit, we first organised an online co-creation lab with educators and learners, then developed the set of creative orientation tools and tested them in Sweden with both VET and secondary school students. In parallel, we produced six episodes of a podcast on women in gaming, which served not only as a dissemination action but is also integrated into the toolkit as a practical educational tool. Throughout the project we ran regular partner meetings, developed a dissemination strategy, built and populated the project website, and carried out an awareness campaign including social media, newsletters, a podcast on women in gaming and national/international events targeting VET providers and other stakeholders.

<< Results >>

NuGamers delivered three core intellectual outputs: a research-based Fact Sheet on women in gaming, a practical Handbook for VET and HE providers, and a Toolkit with ready-to-use activities for learners, families and staff. These resources were co-created with VET teachers, game-industry professionals and female students, and tested in Sweden with VET and secondary-school groups. We also produced six podcast episodes featuring women in game development, used both as a dissemination channel and as a practical learning tool within the toolkit. In addition, we developed an easy-to-use interactive online presentation (Genially) offering a visual, clickable overview of the project’s key findings and tools; this extra resource, not originally foreseen in the application, makes it easier for schools to explore and reuse the NuGamers materials in workshops and orientation events. The fact sheet was expanded to include six personas and their journeys based on the data gathered from focus groups. The personas are a fact-based service design tool that is useful for getting to know the user-base or customers, meaning the female students in this instance.

2023-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000158327.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000158327.title: PV Experts - Photovoltaic & Photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) technology for advanced VET curricula
2023-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000158327.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was developed in response to the increasing demand for skilled professionals in the renewable energy sector, driven by the transition away from fossil fuels and the growing importance of sustainable energy solutions. As the solar energy market continues to expand, there is a clear need for vocational education and training (VET) systems to provide learners with up-to-date technical skills that match labour market needs.

We applied for this project to address gaps in knowledge and skills related to photovoltaic and related renewable energy technologies among VET educators and students. The project aimed to strengthen STEM competences, support workforce mobility, and encourage entrepreneurial thinking through innovative and practice-oriented learning approaches.

In addition, the project responded to the need for more inclusive VET education, particularly for migrant and refugee learners. By promoting intercultural awareness and involving migration experts, the project addressed the need for inclusive training methods that ensure equal participation, cooperation, and social inclusion within renewable energy education.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to reduce skill gaps in the photovoltaic, solar thermal, and photovoltaic-thermal sectors by improving the knowledge and competences of VET educators and trainees in response to the growing demand for solar energy. The project aimed to increase VET students’ employability by providing them with relevant skills aligned with current labour market needs and EU priorities.

The project also aimed to support VET trainers by providing an interactive handbook and practical guidance on how to teach solar energy fundamentals, smart monitoring systems, and related technologies using innovative and engaging methods. At the same time, it sought to promote inclusive education by supporting the active participation and integration of migrant and refugee students in VET learning activities.

Another key objective was to develop VET students’ practical skills in photovoltaic installation, monitoring, and maintenance through dedicated training modules, preparing them for careers in the solar energy sector.  Moreover, the project aimed to introduce Open Living Labs as a long-term approach to encourage collaboration between VET students, educators, experts, businesses, and other stakeholders.

<< Implementation >>

Through WP2 (Interactive Handbook), interviews and online discussions were carried out with experts from the solar energy and migration sectors to support the development of the handbook. The content of the PVExperts Handbook was translated and pilot tested in each participating country. These activities contributed to informing VET educators about labour market shortcomings and the growing demand for new skills in the solar energy sector. 

Within WP3 (The PVExperts Module), activities focused on developing and improving VET students’ skills in photovoltaic installations, automated and intelligent monitoring, and maintenance. The PVExperts Module was translated and pilot tested in the participating countries. These activities supported students in acquiring the competences needed to pursue a career in the solar energy sector.

Within WP4, methodologies and guiding resources were developed to support the implementation of Open Living Labs as a long-term intervention. The Living Lab approach was applied as a real-life, user-centred learning environment to enhance collaboration between VET students and experts and to support co-creation, knowledge exchange, and active student participation.

<< Results >>

The project achieved the following concrete outputs and results, available at https://pvexperts.eu/results/:
-WP2:The PVExperts Interactive Handbook for VET educators (available in English and in all partners' languages), available at https://pvexperts.eu/handbook/
-WP3: The PVExperts module for VET students aiming to update future European workers' skills (available in English and in all partners' languages), available at https://pvexperts.eu/courses/pv-experts-module/
-WP4:The PVExperts Innovation and practice days; field trips (final video and Field Trips implementation guide available in English and in all partners' languages, available at https://pvexperts.eu/field-trip/); open living labs (full session recording and Open Living Lab Implementation Guide available in English and in all partners' languages, available at https://pvexperts.eu/open-living-lab/) ; information days; science cafes; gamification days (Escape Rooms, board games, puzzles, etc.); makerspaces with different workshops on solar and PV applications and the possibilities for internships.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2023-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000157139.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000157139.title: Rail Interlocking System Simulation
2023-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000157139.summary:
<< Background >>

Our project application is based on two main reasons, both general and specific:
1- General: The increasing dependence of global trade and national economies on railway networks, but the inadequacy of the educational infrastructure to support this growth in the face of crises such as the pandemic.
2- Specific: The shortage of qualified human resources in the field of railway signaling systems and the fact that education in this field is high-cost, risky, and has limited application opportunities.
Signaling systems are systems where practical training in a real environment is difficult due to their safety-critical structures. This situation brings with it problems such as lack of application and student-labor market mismatch. The COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 period has made hybrid education and simulation-based learning solutions mandatory.
The RISS project aims to address these needs by:
- Addressing the shortage of qualified workforce and employment,
- Creating a digital, accessible, and sustainable educational infrastructure,
- Enabling practical learning in signaling education in a digital environment,
- Reducing the skills gap between VET students and the expectations of the sector.

<< Objectives >>

The RISS project aims to develop an innovative, digital, and application-based vocational training model in the field of railway signaling systems. Within the scope of VET (Vocational Education and Training), the goal is to support and improve the practical training component, which is often lacking in distance learning processes, using digital tools. The project's implementation has enabled the transfer of interactive environments such as classroom experiments and applied projects to the virtual world. In this context, the project's objectives are:
- To develop realistic simulation software for railway signaling systems,
- To provide a learning environment that integrates theoretical knowledge with practical application in vocational training,
- To enable students and instructors to perform safe, risk-free, and repeatable applications,
- To increase the digital capacity of VET institutions and align them with the EU's digital transformation and skills agenda,
- To produce standard, scalable, and scalable training outcomes that will increase employability in the railway sector.
To achieve these objectives, the project has three concrete outputs:
- RISS Training Simulation,
- Training Modules,
- Training Platform (LMS).

<< Implementation >>

The following activities have been carried out to achieve the project objectives:
- Pedagogical Design Studies: Educational content and scenarios have been determined in accordance with the needs of the sector, students, and teachers.
- Development of Interlocking System Simulation: An interactive simulation software based on real signaling logic has been developed.
- Creation of Application Scenarios: Real-life training scenarios such as failure situations and operation scenarios have been prepared.
- Online Learning System (LMS) Setup: An online platform has been created in which simulations, educational content, and student monitoring and evaluation tools are integrated.
- Pilot Applications and Feedback Processes: The developed content was tested with VET students and teachers, and improvements were made based on feedback.
- Dissemination and Promotion Activities: Dissemination activities were carried out in the Czech Republic, Croatia, Italy, and Türkiye to share the project outputs. 
In addition, within the scope of 5 work packages; a total of 6 meetings, including two opening and closing meetings, and online meetings, and two learning activities were carried out.

<< Results >>

The following key tangible outputs were obtained within the scope of the project:
1. RISS Training Simulation: Enabling students to practice signaling control, maintenance, and troubleshooting in a virtual environment,
2. Training Scenarios (Modules): Designed for use within the simulation, including switch control, signaling, and 20 different digital application scenarios,
3. LMS: An open-source training platform integrated with the simulation and scenarios, both web and mobile-based, capable of student tracking and evaluation.
All this content is accessible at https://simulentra.com/riss. Other important results and materials of the project are:
- User Guides: Pedagogical and technical guides for teachers and students on the use of the simulation and platform,
- Digital Coaches: Expert teachers who have learned and can apply the training content development methodology,
- Dissemination Tools: Project website, e-newsletters, social media accounts, and eTwinning project,
- Strategy documents and project supporting documents: Communication and Quality Strategy Management Plans.

2023-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000159321.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000159321.title: Development of Vocational Training of High-Speed Train Maintenance
2023-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000159321.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the need for a quality-assured training model supporting the certification system for rail system vehicle maintenance personnel. While occupational standards and certification were already defined, a structured training design was missing.

With mandatory certification introduced, the sector required better-qualified staff and improved workforce skills. The needs analysis showed that candidates struggled in certification exams without proper training and emphasized the importance of accessible digital learning tools.

Therefore, the project aimed to develop innovative curricula aligned with labor market needs, support digital transformation in vocational education, reduce skills mismatches, and prepare candidates for certification and employment. Ultimately, it contributed to improving the quality of vocational education and strengthening a sustainable skilled workforce in the railway sector.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project, we aimed to develop a new-generation training design that complements the certification system for rail system vehicle maintenance personnel. The project focused on creating a high-quality vocational education model supported by digital and traditional learning materials and aligned with labor market needs.
We also aimed to integrate a training module into a mobile application, implement a pilot training program, and certify successful candidates. By offering international internship opportunities and supporting the employment of at least five participants, the project sought to establish a strong link between vocational education and the labor market.
Additionally, the project aimed to reduce skills mismatches, promote continuous professional development, and enhance the competencies of candidates, ultimately improving the overall quality and sustainability of vocational education in the railway sector.

<< Implementation >>

Within the scope of the project, transnational project meetings, online meetings, and a workshop were organized to define the methodology and ensure the quality of the outputs. The project results were shared with sector stakeholders at the final conference.
A competency-based training design was developed in line with occupational qualifications, and both digital and traditional training materials were produced. Following this, a pilot training program was implemented, and participants who successfully completed the program were included in the certification process.
An international internship program was organized to strengthen participants’ professional skills, and successful candidates were supported in their transition to employment. In this way, an integrated model covering training, certification, and employment was successfully implemented.

<< Results >>

The High-Speed TrainING project produced several concrete outputs. Seven training programs and seven textbooks were developed for the rail system vehicle maintenance profession. Digital learning materials were created, and a mobile application was launched to support flexible access to training content. An official project website was also established to disseminate results and resources.

A pilot training program was successfully implemented, followed by a certification exam to validate participants’ competencies. Additionally, an international internship program was organized for successful candidates, and at least five certified participants were supported in gaining employment in the railway sector.

These results contributed to improving the quality of vocational education, supporting digital learning, reducing skills gaps, and strengthening the connection between training and employment.

<< Results >>

Certainly, here's a more streamlined description of the components:

Training Format: "Digital Learning for Biodiversity Conservation in Agriculture" - Designed for researchers specializing in biodiversity and agriculture.

E-learning Course: "Farmland Biodiversity Management" - Tailored for farmers.

BioCheck APP: This app offers element analysis and provides customized recommendations for crop diversification, rotation, natural pest control, and addressing alien species for various farm zones

2024-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000250823.summary:
<< Objectives >>

WILDFIRE wants to achieve a stronger alignment of policies and VET instructions for squads, commanders, and instructors in forest firefighting in Europe. For this reason, WILDFIRE goals coincide with the European DigCompOrg in relation to its blended learning elements, EQF and learning descriptors. WILDFIRE fills a knowledge gap for firefighters, reduce numbers of victims, as wildland firefighting goes beyond local and/or regional conditions, and its impact will increase with climate change.

<< Implementation >>

With its multi-level approach, WILFIRE will involve different firefighters in its project activities. The successful implementation of WILDFIRE is based on a coherent and comprehensive VET scheme with a competency matrix and a policy recommendation. The sequence of work is: 1. policy recommendation to have a framework and public interest to develop the squad VET scheme (2), then VET scheme for commanders and then for instructors. This will lead to the first wildland firefighting handbook.

<< Results >>

WILDFIRE results will be follow priorities of EQF, learning descriptors, and with DigCompOrg for the BLE. It will try to overcome intergovernmental barriers in the fire service through this VET cooperation. To this end, WILDFIRE partners will engage with policy makers and educators at EU, national and regional levels to maximize dissemination of its results. It is expected that a goal-oriented network will be established across Europe, which will continue after the end of the project as an OER.

BD Viticulture
Adaptation of the biodynamic viticulture concept to the conditions of Eastern Europe
2024-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000256155.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Biodynamic agriculture strives for environmental-friendly wine production. In Eastern Europe the development of Biodynamics is stagnating because the concept is not adapted to the specific conditions. Wanderschule and 4 leading national biodynamic organizations elaborate an adapted Biodynamic viticulture concept to support the wine growers in conversion. In each country trainings will be installed with the support of associated professional partners of the vocational training institutions.

<< Implementation >>

24 case studies of Biodynamic pioneers/experts will be elaborated to better understand the specific conditions. In regional conferences the lessons learnt will be discussed and a catalogue of recommendation published. In each country a new conversion training will be developed, tested, evaluated. The results are shared with interested wine growers gathered in the vocational training centres and professional regional wine associations and other national organisations in the Biodynamic movement.

<< Results >>

The project will accelerate the conversion rate of Eastern Europe wine growers to Biodynamics. 24 case studies help to understand the learnt lessons of pioneers and create a recommendation catalogue. In each participating wine country a new training will offer VET students, wine growers, trainers the chance to update their knowledge. The results will be shared internationally (EPALE). The project will also help to adapt cultivation concepts for other crops (olive or orcharding) or other regions.

2024-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000246935.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000246935.title: Influencing careers of VET students
2024-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000246935.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because VET students are increasingly influenced by social media, digital professions and influencer culture when thinking about their future careers. Many young people see influencing as attractive, flexible and financially promising, but they often do not understand the professional, ethical, financial and psychological realities behind this work. At the same time, VET teachers and career guidance experts are not always equipped with tools to discuss influencer careers and other emerging digital professions in a structured and realistic way. The project addressed the gap between students’ everyday digital lives and formal career guidance in VET schools. We wanted to support students to make more informed career choices and to help educators guide them with more confidence. The project also responded to the need for stronger cooperation between VET schools, non-formal education organisations and local stakeholders in Croatia, Germany and Serbia.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to contribute to better career orientation of VET students in the digital era, with a special focus on influencer careers and social media-related professions. The first objective was to educate VET students to make informed career choices as potential influencers or digital professionals, understanding both opportunities and risks of this field. The second objective was to empower VET teachers, career counsellors and associated experts to provide modern career guidance that reflects current labour market changes, social media trends and young people’s real interests. The third objective was to strengthen cooperation with VET schools and local stakeholders, and to increase the capacities of partner organisations in supporting career management for emerging professions. Through these objectives, the project promoted critical thinking, digital responsibility, financial literacy, employability and more realistic understanding of digital careers.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through four work packages. In WP1, partners carried out project management, coordination, monitoring, online meetings, reporting and final evaluation. In WP2, the consortium developed the Toolkit “Empowerment of VET students on making informed career choices in influencer careers” and piloted it with VET students in Croatia, Germany and Serbia. In total, 72 students participated in the Toolkit piloting workshops. In WP3, partners developed the Curriculum “Empowering VET teachers and experts on career management in the influencer era” and tested it through local training courses for educators and associated experts in the three countries, involving 34 participants. In WP4, the project developed the online project platform and organised three national multiplier events in Croatia, Germany and Serbia, reaching 93 stakeholders from VET, career guidance, youth work, adult education and employability fields.

<< Results >>

The project produced three main results. The first result is the Toolkit for VET students, containing conceptual guidance and practical workshops on personal branding, digital skills, job search, online communication, credible sources, influencer culture, privacy and career action planning. The second result is the Curriculum for VET teachers and experts, structured as a six-day programme with three modules on influencer work and marketing, career management methods, and the role of social media in career development. The third result is the Online Project Platform, which gives open access to project information and resources and supports sustainability after the project end. Other results include piloting workshops with 72 VET students, training courses with 34 educators and experts, and multiplier events with 93 stakeholders. The project also strengthened cooperation with VET schools and improved partners’ capacities to address digital career guidance in a realistic and responsible way.

2024-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000252411.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000252411.title: Virtual Reality for Tourism
2024-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000252411.summary:
<< Objectives >>

VR4T’s goal is to build a bridge between the educational content on VR tools and technology, and the need for new tools in training for touristic activities. It will present the tools that can make tourism more sustainable and modern.

This bridge will provide a methodology that will upskill VET teachers who will train students wishing to work in the tourism sector, and to equip professionals in the tourism sector with VR-applied knowledge to use VR in their tourism service provision.

<< Implementation >>

Activities will entail a curriculum based on the training needs of VET teachers and professionals in the tourism sector, focusing on the innovative aspect of VR technology in reshaping tourism. It will be an OER and can be attended via an e- learning platform. A video will be created promoting the use of VR in VET education for tourism.

VET teachers and professionals will be trained on the content of the curriculum during a training activity, and 20 VET students/country will test the OER.

<< Results >>

The project will have 2 results:
-VR4T Curriculum will focus on the creation of educational content based on the results of the state-of-the-art research done by the partners in preparation for the project development. The modules will allow a blended learning approach.
-VR4T digital learning space will serve as the educational platform for the training course and the repository of learning material and tools. It will also host a video to promote the use of VR in VET education for tourism.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000255960.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000255960.title: Social Innovation Incubators for Inclusive Digital Healthcare
2024-1-HR01-KA220-VET-000255960.summary:
<< Objectives >>

With the INVITE project, we want to support the digital revolution happening in the European healthcare system by increasing digital and professional skills in the field of inclusive digital healthcare among teachers and students in medical vocational schools. We will also support the transformation of medical vocational schools into drivers of social innovation in digital health improving health outcomes for all, especially those who are most vulnerable.

<< Implementation >>

In the project, we will design, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive training program for vocational medical students and their teachers focusing on inclusive digital healthcare. Next, we will establish student social innovation support initiatives in each partner school. We will offer teachers training necessary for fostering social innovations in schools using open pedagogy and design thinking methods.

<< Results >>

The project will result in a new curriculum and open educational resources for the INVITE program, the creation of a Social Innovation Toolkit for Inclusive Digital Healthcare, and the establishment of Social Innovation Incubators in 3 European schools. Piloting the Social Innovation Incubators will result in innovative solutions tailored to the needs of the older people who are often left out of the benefits of digital health.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2024-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000255388.title: Transforming Education: Achieving Innovation through Challenge-based-learning
2024-1-IT01-KA220-VET-000255388.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The TEACH Project aims to provide VET teachers and students (aged 13-18 years) with tools and stimuli useful for developing in the field of New European Bauhaus (NEB), by means of innovative teaching methodologies framed in Challenge Based Learning (CBL). This method fosters self-directed learning, problem-solving on NEB values and active participation. Through research and experimentation, TEACH validates CBL's effectiveness and provides EU-wide implementation guidelines.

<< Implementation >>

The TEACH Project will gather partners to co-design materials for a training course on CBL, specifically   targeted for VET teachers and created to be a user-friendly self-training tool. Afterwards, a European Challenge centered on NEB topics will be launched, together with a mentorship tailor-made programme for VET schools. The winners will travel to Bruxelles to be hosted during the NEB Festival in spring.

<< Results >>

OUTPUTS
CBL Toolkit
E-learning materials on CBL
CHALLENGE FACILITATOR profile
European Challenge on NEB topics

OUTCOMES
CBL validation
The providing of tools will enhance students and teachers skills
A community of Young NEB Innovators
An European Community of Practices on CBL
The Challenge and the dissemination events will reinforce the transnational perspectives of partners

2024-1-LV01-KA220-VET-000254680.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Through the Rural Impact project, our aim is to provide rurally based young VET learners with access to targeted, quality VET programmes that will help to build their skills to be successful social entrepreneurs. Through the business incubation projects planned in WP4, we also aim to support these young social entrepreneurs to access important business development supports that are often lacking in rural areas. We also aim to support VET providers to tailor their VET offer to rural areas.

<< Implementation >>

We are going to implement:
1. Social Entrepreneurship online modules to 25 young VET learners (aged 18 to 35), living in rural areas in each country. 
2. Upskilling modules to 7 VET professionals in each partner country to help them to adapt their VET offer to rural areas.
3. Transnational piloting with 12 VET professionals – 2 from each partner country to achieve European added value for VET professionals.
4. Social enterprise incubator projects with 5 VET learners in each country.

<< Results >>

We will develop these results: 
No.1 - Social Entrepreneurship e-Modules for Rural Youth Entrepreneurs – 10 e-Modules, each of 60-90 minutes in duration, addressing key topics to build the social entrepreneurship skills or VET learners.
No.2 – Up-skilling for VET Professionals so that they can deliver the social entrepreneurship training programme to VET learners based in rural areas.
No.3 - Rural Impact Incubators to provide a tangible link to young entrepreneurs who complete online modules.

2024-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000248974.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000248974.title: Soft skills - ensuring professional performance of coaches
2024-1-RO01-KA220-VET-000248974.summary:
<< Background >>

The “Soft skills – ensuring professional performance of coaches” project addresses the need to improve the communication skills of coaches working with children and adolescents, in a context where the current generation is strongly influenced by excessive technology use and a sedentary lifestyle. The project has strengthened coaches’ professional skills and improved communication with parents.
The results show that transversal skills are essential. The new methods learned during the training activities have led to more effective communication in clubs and better relationships between coaches, parents, and children, increasing the motivation of young athletes under 14.
In many clubs, coach education focuses mainly on technical aspects, without including communication, sports psychology, or modern pedagogy—factors that contribute to demotivation and dropout. The project addresses these gaps by developing soft skills such as communication, empathy, conflict management, and understanding children's emotional development, through courses and exchanges between Romania, Hungary, and Croatia.
An innovative element of the project is the creation of an online learning and de-stressing platform to support coaches’ continuous education.

<< Objectives >>

We developed new attitudes that could influence the quality of training and contributed to the development of children, both from a sports perspective and in character building. To facilitate access and ensure sustainability, working tools were created to support the coaches’ activities.
Our objectives were:
Developing coaches through the use of new technologies and the implementation of the online application.
Training coaches from a technical, physical, and tactical perspective.
Improving the communication skills of football coaches.
Establishing a partnership with PMFC – Labdarúgó and ŽENSKI NOGOMETNI KLUB MEĐIMURJE ČAKOVEC for the development of football coaches – we aimed to strengthen the institutional partnership among the three partner organizations through the exchange of good practices, constructive discussions and conclusions, as well as by adopting methods and tools that would be used in coaching activities.
Exchanging experiences with partners.
Reducing the number of children who dropped out of football before the age of 14 – we aimed for the learning and development process to help decrease this phenomenon.
Promoting inclusion and gender equality.

<< Implementation >>

Each work package involved concrete activities. Thus, the main activity that had a significant impact was the training of coaches. Coaches had the opportunity to work with communication specialists, psychologists, and experienced trainers. The activities were organized in a suitable environment, allowing discussions about the challenges each coach faces in their own country.

The main activities carried out include:
Training for coaches: Improving coaches’ communication with children in the under-14 age category;
Exchange of experience: Sharing experiences with the two partner clubs and implementing the knowledge gained in their own academy;
Online education for everyone: An online platform to help de-stress coaches before matches and training sessions;
Dissemination of project results: Sharing the outcomes of the project.
In addition to the activities carried out within the project, I was also involved in other initiatives within the club, such as organizing and delivering workshops for coaches, both online and face-to-face. Coaches from partner countries participated in the online sessions, creating valuable opportunities for international exchange, sharing best practices, and strengthening the professional network.

<< Results >>

The project improved coaches’ skills in the three partner countries, particularly in communicating with children, engaging parents, and enhancing personal and professional development. Positive changes in the attitudes of children during training sessions, as well as of parents, were observed—intangible but important outcomes.
The project also increased club prestige in the community and attracted new members through “open-door” events and social media promotion.
Tangible results include:
Training workshops for coaches
Guide for Football Coaches
An online platform for coaching support
Parent meetings
Observation of matches and training sessions
Over 100 coaches were trained, educational materials were produced in Romanian, English, Croatian, and Hungarian, and over 100 coaches engaged via the online platform. Coaches gained better communication and empathy skills, athletes benefited from a positive environment, and clubs strengthened relationships with parents, improving player retention.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2024-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000249811.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000249811.title: Building capacities of European social economy support organisations in facilitating scaling of later-stage social entrepreneurs
2024-1-SE01-KA220-VET-000249811.summary:
<< Objectives >>

91% of social entrepreneurs in Europe wish to scale their enterprises. Although VET provision for this target group has increased in recent years, very few SESOs (e.g. incubators/accelerators/networks) currently provide training programmes linked to scaling. This project therefore aims at building the capacities of support organisations and their ability to support scaling. Through that we will ultimately support Social Entrepreneurs (SEs) across the European market to scale their enterprises.

<< Implementation >>

Based on data collection and validation of needs, partners will produce and user-test a new Self-assessment tool and Guide on scaling for SESOs. These deliverables will be disseminated to the wider sector through a series of webinars, a helpdesk and an online campaign. Partners will also individually develop new in-house training tools linked to the topic of scaling, aided by a process of peer learning, and user-testing, that will enable more widespread adoption of scaling programmes for SEs.

<< Results >>

The Self-assessment tool and Guide should build capacities of European SESOs on how to establish a scaling support programme. Dissemination of these deliverables should reach at least 55 organisations external to the consortium. Partners’ individually developed training tools should deepen expertise on scaling and increase the quality of their support programmes. These tools and training material will benefit SEs across Europe, leading to a more vibrant and well-functioning social economy.

2024-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000250623.title: GÜVENİLİR ASANSÖRLER İÇİN ASANSÖR EĞİTİMİNE YÖN VERİYORUZ
2024-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000250623.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The aim is to provide competence in final inspections of elevators to elevator industry employees, thus increasing the number of safe elevators and enabling access to inspected and problem-free elevators. The project also aims to raise awareness among students in departments such as Electrical, Electronics, Mechanical, Mechatronics, and Electronic Communications about elevators, and to meet the need for trained personnel in the industry through education and standardization activities.

<< Implementation >>

.The activities to be implemented in the project include creating an educational kit, presenting elevator inspection instructions as training videos and online modules, providing certified face-to-face and online courses, publishing country elevator reports, organizing seminars and focus group meetings, workshops, LTTs and TPMs. The aim of all these activities is to equip elevator industry employees with competence and increase the number of safe elevators in the sector.

<< Results >>

It aims to increase awareness and competency levels of elevator industry workers and to increase the number of reliable
elevators by increasing the number of educated workers through the creation of an educational kit, standardization
curriculum, and data pool on a website that will be installed based on the project work packages. The focus is on improving
knowledge of Safe Elevator Standardization and increasing the awareness level of elevator industry workers.

-Create and Implement a professional development course that will help professionals teach CSE inclusively. This not only contributes to innovation in vocational training but also enhances the overall quality of care and support for
individuals with autism.

2025-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000360402.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000360402.title:
DigIDe PRO - Digital Tools for Intellectual disability and dementia:
Professionalisation, Resilience, Outstanding care
2025-1-AT01-KA220-VET-000360402.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project is to address a critical gap in the vocational training of professionals working with people with intellectual disabilities (ID):  ID and dementia. 
We aim to respond to this need by developing high quality training materials for formal caregivers of people with ID with a specific focus on dementia and ID. The project will contribute to the promotion of skills relevant to the current labour market, based on a sound need analysis and it will foster a more inclusive society.

<< Implementation >>

The project encompasses several key activities: conducting country-specific need analysis and publishing the results in an comprehensive report; compiling a Caregiver Toolkit, including resources, open access instruments and an e-book on dementia and ID in 5 languages; developing a Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) on ID and dementia; organizing two Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities (LTTA) for 10 formal caregivers; implementing dissemination activities to share the project´s results.

<< Results >>

R1 Country reports: results of the needs analysis, available training resources and opportunities, good practices and methodologies.
R2 Caregiver Toolkit: a comprehensive toolkit for caregivers on methods of early recognition and strategies in caring for people with ID and dementia.
R3 The “Caregiver Handbook on Intellectual Disabilities and Dementia”, an open access ebook organized in the form of 100 most frequently asked questions about dementia and ID
R4 MOOC on ID and dementia, 4 ECTS

2025-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000355020.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000355020.title: Sky innovators
2025-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000355020.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to develop an innovative, AI-powered drone system for efficient forest monitoring and sustainable reforestation. Key objectives include enhancing local capacity through hands-on training for 100 stakeholders, reducing forest monitoring costs by 30%, and providing real-time data for decision-making. By integrating advanced technology with environmental management, the project fosters scalable, cost-effective solutions to combat deforestation and promote sustainability.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement AI-driven drone monitoring for deforestation and reforestation efforts, conduct five hands-on training sessions for 100 participants, and develop a web platform for real-time data analytics. Activities include software development, field tests, environmental data analysis, and capacity-building workshops. These actions aim to deliver scalable solutions for forest management while fostering digital skills in vocational education.
A timeline is inlcuded in the annexes.

<< Results >>

The project is expected to deliver a fully functional AI-powered drone monitoring system, reducing forest monitoring costs by 30% while providing real-time environmental data. Outcomes include a user-friendly data analytics platform, enhanced reforestation strategies, and a comprehensive training program for 100 participants. The initiative will foster technological skills and sustainable practices, offering a scalable model for future environmental conservation efforts.

2025-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000359074.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000359074.title: Pathways 2 Progress
2025-1-BE02-KA220-VET-000359074.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to create an inclusive and adaptable training framework that improves migrant integration into the labour market. It equips trainers with tools to assess prior learning and learning needs, support diverse learning pathways, and facilitate language and cultural adaptation. By analyzing and adapting best practices, the project ensures targeted training approaches. The development and pilot testing of specialized training modules will enhance utility and scalability.

<< Implementation >>

Next to project management and communication & dissemination, P2P includes research and analysis, developing guidelines, conducting desk research, interviews, and surveys, leading to an analytical report on prior learning & support needs. It then develops training modules, an itinerary, and a guide for trainers, ensuring cross-sectoral accessibility. Pilot testing follows, refining content through small- and large-scale training iterations, with evaluations leading to final recommendations.

<< Results >>

The project results include guidelines for conducting analysis, national desk research, stakeholder interviews and focus groups, and an analytical report summarizing best practices and recommendations. It delivers three training modules on prior learning validation, adapting learning pathways, and language/cultural adaptation, plus a Guide for Trainers. Results are tested through pilot trainings, with findings published in a digital learning hub and P2P magazine.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business
Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

2025-1-CZ01-KA220-VET-000352944.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-CZ01-KA220-VET-000352944.title: IT Solutions through VR Integration
2025-1-CZ01-KA220-VET-000352944.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our project aims to promote digitalization in education, to enable teachers and students to use Virtual Reality and mobile technologies effectively.It aims to increase students' motivation, make learning more interactive and develop digital skills by integrating innovative methods into lessons.Participants will gain skills to use digital tools in a sustainable way.The developed VR modules and mobile application will support both face-to-face and distance learning, promoting equal opportunities.

<< Implementation >>

Within the scope of the project, training workshops on VR technology and mobile application usage will be organized for students and teachers. Following this, VR-based learning modules and a mobile application will be developed. These tools will be tested in pilot schools and refined based on user feedback. Additionally, teacher training sessions, online seminars, peer-to-peer workshops, and dissemination activities will be conducted to ensure widespread use and long-term impact.

<< Results >>

The outputs of our project are a VR-Based Learning Platform, Mobile Application, Lesson Plans and Educational Materials, Teacher Training Modules, Dissemination Materials, and an Impact Analysis and Evaluation Report. As a result, a usable VR-based platform and mobile app will be developed, enhancing students' digital skills and making learning more interactive. Teachers will effectively integrate digital tools, promoting equal opportunities in education.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2025-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000350211.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training

2025-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000350211.summary:

CyberABLE project aims to create a digital training toolkit on cybersecurity for VET teachers and to provide VET students an up-to-date training opportunity that develops missing skills, highly demanded in European job market.

OBJECTIVES
- To empower VET teachers with a digital training platform: CyberABLE Virtual Campus, using instructional design, that aligns VET education with job economy
- To develop Cybersecurity competence of VET Students using EQF-ECVET mapped Training Curriculum

-DEVELOPMENT of Online Didactic Resources, Cybersecurity Competence Framework, CyberABLE Virtual Campus, EQF-ECVET mapped Curriculum and Pedagogical handbook for transferablility
-CAPACITY BUILDING of project staff
-PILOTING of project methodologies and results by target users and beneficiaries
-CONSULTING with NATIONAL CYBER EXPERTS
-NATIONAL MULTIPLIERS + DISSEMINATION to enhance networking and collaboration with VET teachers and potential user plus FINAL CONFERENCE in Germany
-PROJECT REPORT

CyberABLE will develop Open Educational Resources in English, Danish, German, Croatian, Slovenian:

PR1. Online Database of 120 didactic resources for Cyber Security VET teachers
PR2. Cyber Security training curriculum design, EQF-ECVET mapped

PR4. Pedagogical handbook for facilitating transferability
PR5. Dissemination Conference & National Multipliers
PR6. Project management reports

2025-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000352279.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000352279.title: Integrated Sustainability Approach for the Effective Navigation of Emerging Critical Transformations (Green & Digital & Economic)
2025-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000352279.summary:
<< Objectives >>

X-VET aims to equip VET institutions, educators, and learners with structured sustainability and digital learning skills, ensuring alignment with the EU Green and Digital Transition. The project develops innovative training frameworks, a MOOC on Integrated Sustainability, and sustainability-driven hackathons, fostering experiential learning and industry collaboration. It also provides certification and disseminates results to ensure long-term impact, driving sustainable transformation in VET.

<< Implementation >>

- Develop the X-VET MOOC, providing structured learning pathways for VET stakeholders.  
- Design a Hackathon Guide to implement local Sustainability Hackathons to foster real-world problem-solving.  
- Conduct Training of Trainers programs, equipping educators with sustainability-driven teaching strategies.  
- Establish a certification system for formal recognition of acquired competencies.  
- Ensure widespread dissemination & upscaling through multiplier events, conferences, & partnerships.

<< Results >>

X-VET will equip VET institutions with sustainability-focused digital learning tools, ensuring long-term impact. The MOOC will provide structured learning for VET leaders, educators, and learners. The Hackathon Guide and local hackathons will foster real-world sustainability solutions. Certification aligned with EU micro-credentials will validate competencies. Over 100 educators and 600 VET learners will benefit, driving sustainability integration in VET education and governance.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2025-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000361332.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training

2025-1-DE02-KA220-VET-000361332.summary:
<< Objectives >>

-Enhance VET education in agro-tourism with the Integration of digital tools, sustainability practices, and innovative learning methods.
-Develop an inclusive, modernized curriculum to equip VET learners with skills in digital marketing, IoT, and eco-tourism.
-Increase employability and entrepreneurship in rural areas, especially for individuals with fewer opportunities.
-Strengthen collaboration between VET institutions, businesses, and policymakers for long-term impact.

-Insights&Needs Analysis:Conduct surveys and studies to identify specific gaps and best practices in agro-tourism.
-Curriculum&Module Development: Create structured learning materials 
-E-Learning & Virtual Farm Tours: Develop an interactive platform and 360° virtual experiences for hands-on learning.
-Pilot Testing &Training: Validate the curriculum

-1 e-learning platform

2025-1-DK01-KA220-VET-000350987.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-DK01-KA220-VET-000350987.title: Boosting Employability Through Transversal skills Enhancement and Readiness with Future-focused Integral Training
2025-1-DK01-KA220-VET-000350987.summary:
<< Objectives >>

BetterFit project aims to bridge the gap between vocational education and labor market needs by equipping VET students with five key transversal skills: Innovation Management, Agile Methodology, Artificial Intelligence, Global Cultural Effectiveness, and Collaborative Intelligence. BetterFit seeks to enhance employability, reduce skill mismatches, and prepare a future-ready workforce through innovative, labour market-aligned training resources using pragmatic pedagogy approach.

<< Implementation >>

BetterFit will conduct a comparative analysis of NQFs in 5 countries to develop a training curriculum design in alignment with ECVET, which will support creation of and pilot Global Employability Master Skills training modules. We will develop animated video kits, and a VET Educator Handbook, all available as OER in six languages. Activities include transnational meetings, VET educators capacity-building training, a stakeholder conference and 5 national multiplier events to disseminate results.

<< Results >>

BetterFit will deliver a  Training Curriculum aligned with ECVET, a set of 36 animated videos, Global Employability Master Skills training and a VET Educator Handbook. The multilingual resources in English, Danish, German, Croatian, Slovenian and Italian will enhance transversal skills for improving employability, foster European transferability, ensuring long-term impact through a sustainability plan, ensuring continued use of resources beyond the project's duration.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2025-1-EL01-KA220-VET-000361497.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-EL01-KA220-VET-000361497.title: Reclaiming Biodiversity through the Treasure of Indigenous Breeds
2025-1-EL01-KA220-VET-000361497.summary:
<< Objectives >>

R-BIObreed fosters biodiversity conservation by supporting the breeding of indigenous livestock breeds. It builds a cross-sector network involving academia, businesses, and regional authorities to tackle climate change, food security, and rural sustainability. The project integrates VET education, digital tools, and market strategies to enhance livestock resilience, economic viability, and sustainable agricultural practices in Southern Europe.

<< Implementation >>

R-BIObreed will implement training, research, and digital innovation to support indigenous breed conservation. Activities include developing a VET curriculum, launching a digital platform and mobile app, conducting field trials on climate-adaptive breeding, and engaging stakeholders through policy recommendations and market strategies. The project fosters cross-sector collaboration, ensuring sustainable livestock practices, biodiversity protection, and economic resilience in Southern Europe.

<< Results >>

R-BIObreed will deliver a VET curriculum, a digital platform and mobile app for knowledge sharing, and training modules on sustainable livestock management. It will establish field trials for climate-adaptive breeding, create policy recommendations, and develop certification and market strategies for indigenous breed products. The project will foster biodiversity conservation, economic sustainability for farmers, and cross-sector collaboration, ensuring long-term impact.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2025-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000354329.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000354329.title: ChessAIThon - Chess Artificial Intelligence Hackathon
2025-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000354329.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Support VET teachers in implementing the most innovative teaching solutions based on the use of universal language of Chess for developing VET student preparation to face the job market challenges and expectations develop a more aware and practical oriented comprehension of principles of coding and artificial intelligence and reinforce transversal key competences through problem based learning approaches addressed to VET students.

<< Implementation >>

Involve VET Schools in a cooperative effort to create Chess based effective, structured and curriculum-relevant training solutions in order to motivate students and develop their soft skills and combine this with imparting fundamental concepts of AI.

Engage students in a transnational learning by doing experience through which they will be challenged in both the aspect of solving and evaluating real chess scenarios and that of training an AI to solve chess problems

<< Results >>

Comprehensive training materials for VET teachers focused on how to train students in the use the principles of chess, computing, and artificial intelligence (IA) essential for being prepared to the job market.
Online database featuring real-life chess scenarios and related lesson plans
International competition providing a practical arena for participants to apply their acquired knowledge and skills in training
Artificial intelligence in solving chess problems

2025-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000356026.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000356026.title: Net Zero Heroes – Advancing the role of Women in Green Tech Sectors
2025-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000356026.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The Net Zero Hero project aims to attract more women to VET programmes in the green tech sector through awareness campaigns and role models showcasing successful careers in STEM. It will develop a bespoke mentoring programme led by women for female VET learners and provide specialised green guidance training for VET teachers, career guidance officers and trainers to enhance their understanding of green career opportunities and promote female talent for greater inclusion in the net-zero industry.

<< Implementation >>

1) Develop a digital library featuring 35 Green Tech Role Models across Europe
2) Implement a year-long Social Media Awareness Campaign to promote female talent in green tech
3) Design and deliver a CPD Programme to 84 VET professionals providing 24 hours of flexible training on green career guidance
4) Develop the Net Zero Hero Mentoring Toolkit integrating six mentoring approaches using the OECD Green Guidance Model
5) Establish Net Zero Hero Mentoring Circles 
6) Host 7 Multiplier Events

<< Results >>

1) Increased visibility of women in green tech
2) Strengthened career guidance in the net-zero industry with trained VET professionals applying inclusive green career guidance approaches
3) Transnational learning and exchange opportunities ensuring best practices are shared and scaled across 7 EU countries
4) Enhanced mentorship offering guidance and networking opportunities for female learners in green careers
5) A sustainable model for female participation in the green transition across the EU

2025-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000365433.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000365433.title: Transformación Digital para la Excelencia en Formación Profesional: Innovando la Educación a través de Tecnologías Avanzadas
2025-1-ES01-KA220-VET-000365433.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to modernize vocational education by integrating advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence, IoT, cybersecurity, robotics, 3D printing, and quantum computing. Its objective is to enhance the digital skills of students and teachers, strengthen the connection between education and industry, and promote innovative and inclusive methodologies. Additionally, it seeks to develop an e-learning platform and practical demonstrators to ensure applied learning.

<< Implementation >>

The project will develop an e-learning platform with interactive modules, provide training for teachers in advanced technologies, create practical demonstrators in vocational training centers, and organize mobility activities for students and teachers. Transnational meetings, training workshops, and job shadowing activities will be conducted. Inclusion strategies will be applied, and dissemination events will be organized to maximize impact and sustainability.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver an e-learning platform with content on advanced technologies, enhance digital skills for teachers and students, develop practical demonstrators in vocational training centers, and promote the integration of innovative methodologies. Additionally, it will strengthen the connection between education and industry, foster digital inclusion, and create replicable materials that ensure a long-term impact at the European level.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2025-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000358483.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000358483.title: Hospitalité et Accueil Régénératif des Territoires
2025-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000358483.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project aims to revitalise rural areas by integrating new residents, thus stimulating the local economy. By developing targeted training courses, we will strengthen the skills of local actors for better management and revitalisation of their communities. By building a model of sustainable hospitality, we will support the economy while preserving the environment. Finally, we will experiment with and structure inclusive reception policies.

<< Implementation >>

Identification of innovative practices for welcoming new arrivals and tourists. Development of a digital hub to disseminate good practices and facilitate exchanges. Full-scale test for the integration of new inhabitants and regenerative tourism. Synchronous and asynchronous training and transnational training courses to structure a regenerative welcome model, supplemented by inspiring visits. Establishment of the scientific committee and capitalisation work

<< Results >>

The project aims to revitalise rural areas by adopting a regenerative approach to hospitality. It strives to integrate newcomers in a sustainable way and to transform tourism so that it is more in line with local values. The development of training courses and sharing platforms enables the skills of local stakeholders to be strengthened. By experimenting with inclusive policies, the project aims to create innovative hospitality models that promote social cohesion.
topics: Reception and integration of refugees and migrants
Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

2025-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000358698.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2025-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000358698.title: BY YOUR SIDE
2025-1-FR01-KA220-VET-000358698.summary:
<< Objectives >>

By Your Side aims to open the mental health conversation within European mobility by creating meaningful resources which can be used by mobility stakeholders to facilitate their daily work and improve mental health support for candidates participating in work-based mobility programmes abroad.  These tools aim to accompany mobility stakeholders to better manage mental health concerns during European work-based mobility programmes.

<< Implementation >>

The activities in the BYS project are results focused, to improve the resources available to mobility stakeholder at each stage of mobility. We will design and create innovative tools which can be applied when dealing with Mental Health concerns during mobility. These tools will be digital and free to access. The resulted will be test by 10 sending organisations, 10 intermediary organisations, 20 host companies, 10 accommodation providers and 50 trainees in evaluation workshops in 5 countries.

<< Results >>

The results created will be meaningful resources to support mobility stakeholders in their daily work when supporting candidates who are struggling with their mental health at each stage of the mobility abroad. The results will consist of Mental Health Guide and Process to use for pre-mobility, educational online tools and protocol for during mobility and a “toolkit”. These results will be available 6 European languages and will be free to access and have trans-sectoral potential.
