2026-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000466179.action_type: Cooperation partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000466179.title: Strengthening Judicial Capacity for Human Rights in the Digital Era
2026-1-TR01-KA220-VET-000466179.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project will develop a European judicial training framework addressing human rights in the digital era. Main activities include the creation of case-based learning materials, development of digital training modules, establishment of a shared legal terminology on digital rights, pilot training with judicial professionals and refinement of the modules based on feedback, followed by impact evaluation and sustainability planning.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement activities including the development of a European judicial training framework, preparation of case-based learning materials, creation of digital training modules and a shared legal terminology on digital rights. Pilot training sessions will be organised with judicial professionals, followed by refinement of the modules, impact evaluation and sustainability planning.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver a European judicial training framework (PR1), case-based learning materials and digital training modules (PR2), a shared legal terminology on digital rights (PR3), and a Pilot & Impact Toolkit (PR4). These results will strengthen judicial knowledge, promote consistent interpretation of digital rights and support the integration of innovative digital training methods into judicial education.
topics: Human rights and rule of law

2021-1-BE05-KA220-YOU-000028791.title: #YouCreath
2021-1-BE05-KA220-YOU-000028791.summary:
<< Background >>

Let’s go back in time. 
March 2020. Suddenly life stops. Technology arises. The artistic and cultural world start a fight to survive, finding new platforms.
March 2020. Suddenly life stops. Schools close their doors. Open air spaces are forbidden. No play and no game make youngsters a dull… wait. Not actually dull, but their incarcerated in their own homes and centers where their opportunities to express themselves in an artistic way are no longer available.

May 2021. Four European countries, Portugal, Belgium, Croatia and Spain, start to think that social networks are all around us. They are scared. They think youth, art and culture are going to split up for ever. Both sectors express the urgent need for a creative intervention.  Until they think how to get benefits from the social networks. Why not building up an app that links youth, art an culture? Yes! Let’s make our weakness our most valuable strength.

March 2023. Life is at full speed mode. Everything went back to the way it was. And finally, the YOUcreaTH app is working. Young people can meet and find (firstly in the digital world of course) their artists. Young artists can show their work to other artists and art lovers.  The number of users is increasing day by day.

<< Objectives >>

1) Increase the visibility, resilience and sustainability of young people involved in the creative and cultural sector on medium and long term, based upon a ‘joint venture’ between youth and culture.
2) Serve as a concrete ‘guide’ and ‘orienting tool’ for young people to engage themselves in the cultural sector, to explore interests and get inspired.
3) To increase the participation, accessibility, discovery and engagement in their communities.
4) Increase accessibility and visibility towards different communities, including minorities and (young) people with fewer opportunities.
5) Enabling the networking of self-contained artists and organizations dealing with art and culture, creating an effective platform for long-term collaborations. 


<< Implementation >>

In order to let artists and art lovers to create the content of the app and to know about the app, we’ve carried out different activities:
1) Artistic workshops: 
Graffiti
Theatre
Painting
Photography
Robotics
T-Shirt decoration
Swimming with mermaids, 
DJ, 
balloon sculpturing, 
handicraft, 
litografy, 
creative writing, 
wood art
Dance
Artistic Deco
Acting
Calligraphy
2) Multiplier events:At least one per country to introduce the app to the general public and to start creating new networks.
3) Transnational meetings and activities with local artists.
4) Media interviews so a broader amount the people get to know about the project and the app.


<< Results >>

Concrete results:
- The YOUcreaTH app (the most important result) https://www.youcreath.eu/app/
- A website were you can find all the info about the project: https://www.youcreath.eu/
- a digital projectbook that discribes the time line of a project: https://www.youcreath.eu/story/
- Number of people in the app
- Media interviews (may be here we can put the links to the interviews and articles)
- Number of artists that are interested in the project


Other results:
- Incredible times for young people in the Artistic workshops.
- Knowing other European countries 
- Meeting lovely people
- The start point for an artistic network
- A message of encouragement so young people can follow their artistic dreams.
- a working tool (app) to connect young people (with fewer opportunities) to art and culture. 
- a save space to get to know , as a young person, new interest.
- Network building between art/culture organisiations and Yourhwork.

2021-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000028868.title: Raising EU Awareness through accessible documents for youth
2021-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000028868.summary:
<< Background >>

European institutions use 24 official languages, but more than half of surveyed youth lack understanding of the EU, with the Treaty of the Functioning of the European Union, the foundation for EU youth action, spanning over 300 pages in complex "legalese." The challenge lies in bridging this gap between official documents and young people's reality. READY, built on successful projects of the YES Forum, focuses on promoting Active Citizenship, EU awareness, political engagement, and Social Inclusion. Previous initiatives revealed that disadvantaged youth show interest in EU and national politics given the right opportunities. During the previous projects, we witnessed that the EU treaties are still very far from young people’s daily life. READY project addresses this disconnection by making EU provisions easier-to-understand and more accessible to youth by fostering literacy competencies of young people. Since 2020, the YES Forum has been providing easy-to-understand documents to empower young people and enhance their understanding of the treaties' significance in their lives.

<< Objectives >>

READY aligns with the objectives of the European Youth Work Agenda and seeks to reconnect youth work with EU treaties. Our focus has been on making these treaties accessible to all, fostering an increased sense of citizenship and empowering young people to exercise their rights. Through multiplier events and a Brussels conference involving youth, organisations, and policymakers, READY contributes directly to the Bonn Process, promoting and recognising youth work. We engaged both with young people and youth workers, emphasising literacy competencies and political awareness. By combining a personal approach to the EU and research on treaties conducted by young people, READY aimed to make EU provisions and policies accessible, bring young people closer to understanding the EU, and trigger their interest in the EU policies. The project aimed to enhance awareness of the EU's impact on citizens' daily lives, improve the quality of youth work through innovative approaches, and enhance the skills of current and future youth workers.

<< Implementation >>

READY mainly consisted of Transnational Project Meetings (TPMs), Local Activities, Trainings and Multiplier Events in 3 Phases. As a result of each phase’s activities a Project Result was produced. Young people with fewer opportunities were directly involved as participants in all project activities. TPM #1, in Stuttgart, DE (04/2022): All partners participated to help further fine-tune the project so that it best met the needs of youngsters with fewer opportunities. TPM #2, in Zagreb (10/2022): Youngsters from partner organisations took part in the discussions to include the young participants in all steps of decision-making. Local activities of Phase 1 "EU Ready to Read," incl. 1st Training "I read, I understand" in Strasbourg (12/2022): A group of young participants from each partner took part in local meetings before and after the 1st Transnational Training in Strasbourg. There, they received training on Europe, EU politics, the role of treaties and policies, and techniques to design effective infographics. The young people were responsible for deciding which of the relevant provisions from EU treaties and policies, translated into easy-to-understand language, would be transformed into visual content with the use of infographics. Besides expanding their competencies by trying out new methods during the training activities, youth workers were in charge of supporting the young participants in local meetings to carry out the research activities. TPM #3, in Pau (03/2023): Youngsters from partners again took part in the discussions to include the young participants in all steps of decision-making. Youth workers supported the participants in voicing their opinions and presenting their group’s first infographics. Local activities of Phase 2 "EU Ready to See," incl. 2nd Transnational Training "I understand, I use" in Lucca (07/2023): After new preparatory local activities, all young participants gathered to receive further training activities on EU citizenship and how to communicate about the EU. They provided input for the recommendations on what the risks are of having EU language so distant from the reality of young people. They were accompanied by youth workers, who learned how to communicate about the EU in a language easy-to-understand and free of jargon, thereby broadening their scope of professional skills for participatory youth work. Transnational Project Meeting 4, in Brussels (11/2023): Youngsters from partners took part with youth workers to reflect on the project, give feedback, and discuss the dissemination of project results. At the end of the project, we organised 4 national Multiplier Events “EU ready to promote” in Croatia, France, Greece and Italy and 1 EU showcase event “EU Ready for ALL” in Brussels (BE) to disseminate and promote READY project’s activities and results. Exceeding our initial expectations and following the project application evaluation, YES Forum also organised a national multiplier event in Germany to disseminate to project results to the target group in Germany. 

<< Results >>

According to the German Federal Ministry for Family Affairs, Senior Citizens, Women, and Youth, three core challenges were identified that needed to be addressed by youth workers while supporting young people in their path to adulthood: qualification, independence, and self-positioning. The READY project aimed to tackle all these three challenges throughout three phases: 
1. Qualification: Project Result #1 “EU READY to READ, Easy-to-understand versions of EU Provisions”: throughout the 1st phase, young people were in touch with the most relevant provisions of the EU and that concern them directly. Because treaties and policies tend to be seen as hard to understand and far from the daily lives of the young people, they are often neglected as a topic that also needs to be addressed to young people. Through local activities and participation at the TPMs, they were able to better understand the functioning of the EU. As a result of this phase, the “EU READY to READ, Easy-to-understand version of EU provisions” has been published. This publication translated the complex EU provisions into easy-to-understand language with the support of young people, youth and social workers and EU lawyers. 60 articles from 6 different EU Provisions (mainly from the TFEU and TEU) were presented in a more accessible language in this publication which is available in all partner languages (English, Croatian, French, German, Greek and Italian). We also included a glossary at the end of the publication as an additional tool to help young people understand the complex terms better as their meaning could not be simplified but its importance is more than significant in understanding EU language and everyday life.
2. Independence: Project Result #2 “EU READY to SEE, Easy-to-understand infographics on EU Provisions”: during the first Training “EU: I read, I understand”, young people had the independence to choose which of the relevant provisions from the first result “EU READY to READ” they find more important and they feel more connected to in order to present them in easy-to-understand infographics. During the training, they received training sessions on how to produce quality infographics, and started manually planning and producing their own visuals in small groups. Following the training, during the local activities of Phase 2, the young people had the autonomy to visually represent and digitalise the chosen relevant provisions as they feel that fits better. In the second training “EU: I understand, I use”, the young participants finalised the infographics with youth and social workers. As a result of this process, the project published “EU READY to SEE, Easy-understand infographics on EU Provisions” which gathers 28 infographics on EU provisions with short explainers and references to the first READY publication. This publication is also available in all partner languages (English, Croatian, French, German, Greek and Italian). In addition to this, we also provide the infographics in each language as separate images on the project website so that it can be used easily by interested parties.
3. Self-positioning: Project Result #3 “EU READY to DISCUSS, Key Messages & Policy Recommendations” having the knowledge (Result 1) and the confidence to apply it independently (Result 2), young people were able to provide key messages addressing policymakers on their needs for an easier to understand language from the EU. These key messages were reflected within the Project Result 3 “EU READY to DISCUSS, Key Messages & Policy Recommendations”. This publication builds on the activities and results of the initial phases of the READY project, namely, "EU READY to READ" and "EU READY to SEE”. With the common aim of bridging the gap between the EU and young people, the first phase concentrated on translating chosen EU provisions into easy-to-understand language, while the second phase focused on crafting engaging and comprehensible infographics about specific EU topics. This publication is part of the third and the last phase of the project, and includes key messages directly from young people’s contributions during two trainings which took place in Strasbourg (FR) and in Lucca (IT). Additionally, youth workers and practitioners added to the recommendations by sharing their own expertise. This publication is available in all partner languages (English, Croatian, French, German, Greek and Italian).
In addition to these, the project partnership produced and promoted 2 videos recorded during the trainings to reflect and promote the project activities which were shared on the social media channels of the project partners.

2021-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000028921.title: DIYverse
2021-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000028921.summary:
<< Background >>

Diversität ist kein Defizit, sondern eine Ressource, die uns auf allen Ebenen, lokal bis global, helfen kann, soziale Herausforderungen zu meistern. Das Projekt "DIYverse" setzte genau daran an, indem es dabei unterstützte, innerhalb von Bildungseinrichtungen der non-formalen Jugendbildung Strukturen aufzubauen, die Diversität bei Jugendlichen als Chance begreifen und diese aktiv fördern. Innerhalb des Projektes wurden zwei Projektergebnisse erarbeitet, die beide auf die Förderung von Diversität als Ressource abzielen. Dabei wurden zwei Themenschwerpunkte definiert: Förderung eines ressourcenorientierten Bewusstseins gegenüber Diversität und Förderung aktiven zivilgesellschaftlichen Engagements, insbesondere bei marginalisierten Jugendlichen. DIYverse hat zwei Zielgruppen angesprochen. Die primäre Zielgruppe waren Einrichtungen der non-formalen Jugendbildung und ihre Mitarbeitende. Die entwickelten Ergebnisse wurden so konzipiert, dass sie das pädagogische Portfolio und die Strukturen der Einrichtungen ergänzen und somit eine nachhaltige Wirkung bei der sekundären Zielgruppe der Jugendlichen entfalten. DIYverse animiert mit seinen Ergebnissen die zukünftige Generationen sich aktiv für ein friedvolles Miteinander einzusetzen.

<< Objectives >>

Das Projekt DIYverse wirkte auf verschiedenen Ebenen, stellt aber vor allem die persönliche Entwicklung und den Kompetenzerwerb von Einrichtungen der non-formalen Jugendbildung (primäre Zielgruppe) sowie den Jugendlichen (sekundäre Zielgruppe) selbst in den Fokus. Über die verschiedenen Projektinhalte wurden sie ermutigt und befähigt, sich aktiv auf lokaler und europäischer Ebene für eine offene Gemeinschaft einzusetzen. Für eine nachhaltige Stärkung und Förderung der Jugendlichen sowie deren Engagements lag der Fokus des Projektes auf den beteiligten Einrichtungen. Die entwickelten Projektergebnisse trugen dazu bei, dass die beteiligten Einrichtungen auch in Zukunft den Herausforderungen der Jugendbildung und somit der sekundären Zielgruppe der Jugendlichen gerecht werden, indem sie die drei Kernbereiche des Jugendsektors, nämlich Beteiligung, Begegnung und Befähigung, aktiv angingen. Das soziale Projektbüro (PR1) stärkt das Bewusstsein für Diversität als Ressource, da die sozialen Projektbüros sich vor allem an Jugendliche richten, die einen erschwerten Zugang zum Projektmanagement haben. Die Silent LABS (PR2) sensibilisieren für unsere gesellschaftliche Vielfalt und geben marginalisierten Gruppen eine Stimme.

<< Implementation >>

Im Fokus des Projekts DIYverse standen die beiden Projektergebnisse, die beide auf ihre Art und Weise die beteiligen Partner und weitere Einrichtungen, insbesondere der non-formalen Jugendbildung über das Projektende hinaus unterstützen. Beide Produkte können als Erweiterung des jeweiligen Portfolios der Einrichtungen in ihrer Arbeit mit den Jugendlichen gezählt werden. Für die optimale Entwicklung und spätere Anwendung der beiden Projektergebnisse wurden wie geplant zwei Trainings (C1 & C2) umgesetzt. Die Trainings wurden genutzt, um die Fachkräfte der beteiligten Partner und somit die Partnerorganisationen selbst nachhaltig zu stärken. Neben der Sensibilisierung für Diversität als Ressource wurden gezielt die beiden Projektergebnisse in den Fokus gestellt. Die gemeinsame Auseinandersetzung mit den Projektergebnissen führte nicht nur zu einem Kompetenzzuwachs bei den Teilnehmenden, sondern lieferte auch wichtige Erkenntnisse für die weitere Arbeit an den Ergebnissen. Zudem wurden insgesamt 4 multinationale Projektmeetings (M1-M4) umgesetzt, pro Partnerland eins. Neben der notwendigen regelmäßigen Abstimmung auf Projektebene wurden die physischen Treffen genutzt, um das Arbeitsumfeld der Partnerorganisationen besser kennenzulernen und sich international mit weiteren Stakeholdern zu vernetzen. Das Projektmanagement wurde durch regelmäßige, monatliche Online-Meetings (Jour Fix) ergänzt. Für die Verbreitung der Projektergebnisse wurden in jedem Land mehrere Multiplikationsveranstaltungen umgesetzt (E1-E4). In Absprache mit der NA wurden gezielt mehrere Multiplikationsveranstaltungen pro Land angegangen, um insbesondere das Silent LAB gezielt in verschiedenen Kontexten vorstellen zu können.

<< Results >>

Innerhalb von DIYverse wurden zwei Projektergebnisse entwickelt, die sich an Einrichtungen der non-formalen Bildung richten und zur Verbesserung der Arbeit im Bereich der Jugendbildung beitragen werden. Ziel des gesamten Projektes und somit auch der beiden PRs war die Sensibilisierung für Vielfalt als Chance unserer heutigen Zeit und Gesellschaften. In PR1 wurde die Sensibilisierung auf institutioneller Ebene vorangetrieben, indem eine konkrete Handlungsmöglichkeit entwickelt wurde, wie Diversität als Ressource genutzt werden kann. In PR2 wurden Best-Practice-Beispiele für Vielfalt gesammelt bzw. das Tool genutzt, um marginalisierten Gruppen eine Stimme zugeben und somit zur Sensibilisierung der Gesellschaft beizutragen. Beide Leitfäden zeichnen sich neben der inhaltlichen Beschreibung der Tools noch durch die vier nationalen Beispiele aus. Die nationalen Beispiele bieten dabei nicht nur einen Mehrwert für die involvierten Partnerorganisationen, die dadurch die beiden Projektergebnisse auf ihre Bedürfnisse hin entwickeln und implementieren konnten, sondern dienen auch weiteren Organisationen der non-formalen Jugendbildung als Inspiration, die entwickelten Projektergebnisse nicht nur anzuwenden, sondern auch auf ihre Gegebenheiten anzupassen. 
Der Leitfaden zum Aufbau eines sozialen Projektbüros ermöglicht es zukünftig weiteren Jugendeinrichtungen die strukturellen und inhaltlichen Voraussetzungen für eine professionelle Begleitung von Jugendlichen im Bereich des Projektmanagements zu schaffen. Ein soziales Projektbüro erweitert die Möglichkeiten der Einrichtungen. Die Befähigung junger Menschen ihre eigenen Ideen in Projekte zu überführen, führt sowohl zu einem besseren Zugang als auch zu einer stärkeren Einbindung der Zielgruppe. Der Leitfaden zur Entwicklung eigener Silent LABs führt die Lesenden schrittweise durch die einzelnen Entwicklungsschritte. Die nationalen Silent LABs machen durch konkrete Anwendungsbeispiele das Tool greifbarer und zeigen zugleich die Bandbreite der Einsatzmöglichkeiten auf. Die Projektergebnisse und vor allem der dahinter stehende Entwicklungsprozess liefern nicht nur verständliche und anwendbare Tools für die Jugendbildung, sondern haben auch im Partnerkonsortium für die Weiterentwicklung der Kapazitäten und die Erweiterung des eigenen Portfolios geführt. Die durchlaufenen Prozesse und die entwickelten Teilergebnisse wie Steckbriefe der nationalen Projektbüros, Beschreibung der darin schon entwickelten Projekte oder eine Kurzübersicht der nationalen Silent LABs sind in einem Padlet festgehalten und ergänzen die beiden Leitfäden.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2021-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000029056.title: JustNow - A Toolbox for Teaching Human Rights: Blended-Learning Edition
2021-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000029056.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the JustNow project to address significant gaps in human rights and historical education. The strategic partnership aimed to further develop methodical and didactic materials that integrate human rights education with simulation games and diversity learning methods. Given the success of our previous MICC project, which involved immersive, week-long simulations but faced limitations such as language barriers and economic constraints, JustNow 2.0 sought to expand access and impact. By creating a versatile blended-learning platform with modules, audiovisual content, and interactive elements, we aimed to make human rights education more accessible and engaging for diverse youth audiences. This project was crucial to support youth workers and educators in delivering high-quality, adaptable educational experiences that address contemporary issues like misinformation and civic engagement. The development and translation of materials into multiple languages, including German, Polish, and Croatian, were essential to ensure broad and inclusive access.

<< Objectives >>

The JustNow project aimed to achieve several key objectives by developing a comprehensive learning platform. The core goal was to create a freely accessible, web-based platform offering diverse educational materials that could be downloaded and utilized by a broad audience. The platform is designed to support youth work specialists, young peer educators, teachers, volunteers, and others involved in human rights and history education. By providing high-quality, free resources, the project sought to amplify the impact of these materials across participating countries and beyond. We intended to enhance and diversify existing educational offerings with a focus on contemporary and diversity-conscious approaches. The platform, building upon the previous JustNow project, includes learning modules, animated films, timelines, and texts, which are intended to engage users and facilitate learning about human rights and historical contexts in a dynamic way. The expected outcome was not only to reach more users but also to foster synergy with existing educational initiatives. The project aimed to create significant ripple effects through multiplier events and training courses, thereby reaching thousands of beneficiaries directly an

<< Implementation >>

The transnational project meetings were a cornerstone of the JustNow project, fostering collaboration and deepening the partnership among the involved organizations. These meetings, held in Berlin, Zagreb, and Krzyżowa, allowed partners to gain firsthand experience of each other’s working environments, thereby enhancing mutual understanding and cooperation. By visiting different countries, 39 participants gained invaluable insights into diverse cultural contexts, which helped them adapt project strategies to fit various educational landscapes. Hosting these meetings in different settings provided valuable perspectives on the operational dynamics of each organization, strengthening the partnership and ensuring that the project’s implementation was informed by a rich diversity of experiences. Additionally, these face-to-face interactions cultivated stronger relationships among partners, which facilitated smoother communication and more cohesive teamwork throughout the project's duration.

The multiplier events were crucial in extending the reach and impact of the JustNow project beyond the immediate circle of partners. Organized across various European countries, these events brought together 170 participants from 19 different nations, significantly surpassing the initial expectations. The importance of these events lay in their ability to disseminate the project’s intellectual outputs—such as animation movies, activity plans, and timeline cards—to a broader audience, thereby amplifying the project’s educational impact. Multiplier events served as powerful platforms for sharing knowledge and resources with educators, youth workers, and other stakeholders, who then applied these materials in their own contexts. By engaging participants from diverse backgrounds, the events not only ensured that the JustNow materials reached a wider audience but also promoted cross-cultural dialogue and the exchange of best practices in human rights education. The success of these events in attracting participants from 19 countries highlighted the universal relevance of the project’s themes and the effectiveness of the materials in addressing contemporary challenges in human rights education. Moreover, these events were instrumental in creating a ripple effect, where trained participants became multipliers themselves, disseminating the JustNow materials within their networks and communities. This cascading impact was essential for achieving the long-term sustainability and broader adoption of the project’s outputs. The direct engagement of participants through workshops, discussions, and hands-on activities ensured that the educational tools developed during the JustNow project were not only distributed but also effectively integrated into various educational settings across Europe and beyond.

In summary, both the transnational project meetings and the multiplier events were vital in enhancing the collaboration among partners, enriching the project’s implementation, and ensuring that its educational materials reached and benefited a wide and diverse audience. These elements of the JustNow project underscored the importance of strategic planning, cross-border cooperation, and targeted dissemination in achieving impactful and lasting outcomes in educational initiatives.

<< Results >>

The project produced three new animation movies, initially planned for translation into four languages, but through the extensive efforts of the MICC Alumni Network and the project partners, these movies were translated into numerous additional languages, ensuring a wider audience. Additionally, 20 activity/workshop plans were developed, doubling the original target of ten, and translated into four languages, enhancing their accessibility. A new and unplanned component, 13 sets of timeline cards with accompanying activity/workshop plans, was also introduced, adding further depth to the educational toolkit.

The initial goal of reaching 5,000 young people and youth workers directly, and 20,000 more through networks, was overwhelmingly surpassed. An internal evaluation revealed that JustNow materials reached over 72,000 beneficiaries from 125 countries. More than 6,000 individuals were directly engaged through multiplier events and dissemination activities, including the use of JustNow materials in the MICC Program sessions, and at prominent events like the NECE Festival in Madrid and the Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging+ Conference in Chemnitz.

The project’s digital footprint is equally impressive. The JustNow website has attracted over 19,440 visitors from 123 countries, resulting in 6,200 downloads of educational materials. The animation movies on YouTube have been viewed more than 60,000 times, with an average watch time of 64%, indicating strong viewer engagement.

Furthermore, the JustNow materials have become integral to other educational initiatives, such as the "Roots and Borders" project by Kreisau-Initiative e.V., where the animation on decolonization is regularly used to deepen participants' understanding. The ongoing collaboration between Kreisau-Initiative e.V. and its partners ensures that the JustNow Toolbox will continue to evolve and reach even more beneficiaries through accredited seminars, training sessions, and multiplier events under Erasmus+ Key Action 1.

This project has not only met but vastly exceeded its original objectives, creating a lasting legacy in human rights education, with materials that are being used, shared, and expanded upon worldwide.

Human rights and rule of law

2021-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000029101.title: Learning in Youth Work of 21st century
2021-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000029101.summary:
<< Background >>

Upon developing and refining the project proposal, the consortium once again engaged with the 245 youth workers to research about their needs and situations they face. A total of 216 responses were received, revealing a notable shift: a doubling (64%) of respondents had engaged in some form of educational work with youth using online platforms. However, a similar proportion struggled to develop structured online courses and educational activities. This data illustrates the increasing necessity, prompted by the "new normal" of the COVID-19 reality, for organisations to transition their youth work to online platforms, despite persisting gaps in skills, competencies, and knowledge. The project aimed to bridge these gaps by merging the fields of digital technology and youth work/non-formal education, two areas that have not traditionally intersected significantly within European youth work contexts.

<< Objectives >>

Learning in Youth Work of 21st century, as an initiative developed by consortium covering areas of Germany, Balkan region and Scandinavia region, planed to achieve following objectives: - Bring positive and long-lasting effects on participating organisations and sector of youth work by enhancing knowledge management with new innovative resources for development of educational activities within youth work and training models/curricula in order to provide quality youth work educational activities that will address needs of each specific target group. - Support youth workers and educational trainers in acquiring and developing key competences as youth trainers (of other youth workers) in the field of developing and using e-learning materials and online courses in youth work; and marketing strategies and tools for higher involvement and promotion of activities for youth. - Engage into intensive dissemination and exploitation activities of existing and newly produced products and attract more youth organisations and youth workers on using the new innovative tools and approaches, and thus increase quality and quantity of educational youth work activities.

<< Implementation >>

Main project activities are categorised into following sections: - Transnational meetings (2 meetings; 1 preparatory and 1 evaluation meeting) - Development of educational materials and online learning courses (3 manuals and 3 online learning courses) - Educational trainings for youth workers, based on the developed educational materials (3 trainings throughout the project implementation) - Follow-up activities and piloting of developed materials in 4 countries / local communities where partner organisations are based - 4 national conferences (Sweden, Germany, Croatia and Serbia) in format of 1 day multiplier events; for sharing developed materials and results of activities. 
Flow of the implementation of project activities, summarised list: -Signing contract of YP DE with German NA -Signing bilateral agreements between applicant and other partners -Preparatory meeting. Tools for administrative and financial, communication and time management monitoring will be agreed. Updating the calendar of the activities. Agreement on the next steps within the project. -Development of R1 -Implementation of LTTA1 -Development of R2 -Follow up activities to be implemented by
participants of previous LTTA in their local communities, and by youth workers involved in development of R1 -
Development of R3 -Implementation of LTTA2 -Development of R4 -Follow up activities to be implemented by
participants of previous LTTA in their local communities, and by youth workers involved in development of R3 -
Development of R5 -Implementation of LTTA3 -Development of R6 -Follow up activities to be implemented by
participants of previous LTTAs in their local communities, and by youth workers involved in development of R5. -National Multipliers events – 1 per partner organisation/country; 4 in total. -Final evaluation project meeting. -Reporting.

<< Results >>

During the implementation period of this project, partners produced, as planned in the project application, 3 Manuals and 3 Online courses: R1 Manual “How to design a learning experience”; R2 Online learning course “How to design a learning experience”; R3 Manual “Online and e-learning in youth work”; R4 Online learning course “Online and e-learning in youth work”; R5 Manual “Digital marketing and using digital tools in youth work”; R6 Online learning course “Digital marketing and using digital tools in youth work”. Each of the 3 manuals were also translated to partners’ languages (German, Serbian, Croatian and Swedish) except Manual R5 “Digital marketing and using digital tools in youth work”, which wasn’t translated it to Swedish. 
Also 3 LTTAs were implemented: LTTA 1 “How to design a learning experience” in Zadar, Croatia, 13.-20.09.2022; LTTA2 “Online and e-learning in youth work” in Berlin, Germany, 09.-17.01.2023, LTTA 3 “Digital marketing and using digital tools in youth work” in Novi Sad, Serbia, 17.-24.07.2023.

2021-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000029233.title: Prevention of cyberbullying and peer violence among youth
2021-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000029233.summary:
<< Background >>

In the digitally-transformed landscape intensified by Covid-19, youth interaction patterns are evolving. Digital platforms, while fostering community, also unveil challenges like cyberbullying, especially impacting marginalised youngsters. The lines between virtual and real blur, demanding an adaptive youth work approach. While youngsters navigate these platforms confidently, there's a gap in understanding the full implications. Peer relationships, crucial during teenage years, face both positive and negative digital influences, from fostering self-esteem to intensifying peer pressure. With profound psychological impacts, including depression and even suicidal tendencies among bullied individuals, the role of youth workers becomes paramount. Yet, traditional engagement methods fall short in this digital age. Our project aims to rejuvenate youth work, equipping workers with modern tools, promoting cross-sectoral collaboration, and emphasising peer education to holistically support youngsters in this digital era.

<< Objectives >>

-	Empower youth workers and peer educators/leaders among marginalised youngsters for prevention of cyberbullying and peer violence among youth, through development of inspiring and innovative Curriculum, LTTA and the Online course for youth workers’ training.
-	Empower marginalised, discriminated and bullied youngsters in coping mechanisms and dealing with cyberbullying and peer violence, through innovative Toolkit with workshops for vulnerable youngsters.
-	Exchange good practices and further develop quality strategic partnership among partners from 3 European countries with different realities in regards to cyberbullying and youth peer violence prevention.

<< Implementation >>

The project was rolled out methodically, with clear timelines and distinct activity types. 

Kick-off Phase: 
M1 - kick-off project meeting (01-2022): This transnational project meeting laid the foundation for the entire project, ensuring everyone was on the same page and establishing the direction moving forward. 

Development & Collaboration Phase: 
O1 - Toolkit (02-2022 to 08-2022): A comprehensive toolkit was developed to educate and support youngsters, peer educators, and leaders in preventing cyberbullying and peer violence. 
M2 - second project meeting (06-2022): This transnational meeting served to assess the progress after the toolkit's development. 
O2 Curriculum (07-2022 to 11-2022): A curriculum aimed at empowering youth workers and peer leaders to prevent face-to-face peer violence was introduced. 
M3 - third project meeting (12-2022): A review meeting to gauge the project's progression after the curriculum's introduction. 

Digital Transformation & Training Phase: 
O3 - Online Course (12-2022 to 05-2023): This initiative transitioned the curriculum into a digital platform, making it accessible to a wider audience. It aimed at enhancing youth worker skills, emphasising cyberbullying prevention. 
C1 Training of Trainers (06-2023): Specialised training for trainers to ensure effective dissemination of prevention techniques against cyberbullying and peer violence. 

Public Engagement & Dissemination Phase:
E1, E2, E3 Open Conferences (07-2023 to 08-2023): Series of multiplier events held in RS, HR, and DE respectively, focusing on raising public awareness and engaging stakeholders on the subject of cyberbullying and peer violence prevention. 

Conclusive Phase: 
M4 – Final evaluation project meeting (08-2023): This transnational meeting served as a wrap-up, evaluating the project's impact, successes, and areas of improvement. This systematic approach ensured a thorough and holistic addressing of the challenges faced by youth in terms of cyberbullying and peer violence, and the capacity-building of youth workers to tackle the same.


<< Results >>

Intellectual Outputs:

    O1 Toolkit:
        Purpose: A comprehensive resource to aid youngsters and peer educators/leaders in identifying, addressing, and preventing aggressive behaviours among youth.
        Components:
            Theoretical concepts and methodologies for quality prevention.
            A set of 10+ workshops targeting cyberbullying and peer violence prevention.

    O2 Curriculum:
        Purpose: A 7-day training material focused on empowering youth workers and peer leaders to counter face-to-face peer violence.
        Components: Detailed session outlines, annexes, and additional recommendations for multiplication / facilitation.

    O3 E-learning course:
        Purpose: A digital resource focused on cyberbullying prevention, aimed at youth workers and aspirant peer educators/leaders.
        Accessibility: Designed for widespread reach, being free and easily available globally.

All the above intellectual outputs are available in English, German, Croatian, and Serbian, catering to multiple countries where these languages are official.

Direct Results:

    Utilisation of Outputs:
        15 multipliers across partner organisations utilised the intellectual outputs during their youth work. In this way also testing for its efficacy both at a personal and organisational level, aiming to refine processes and practices in youth-related activities.
        90 youngsters (30 per country) benefited directly from these outputs through the actions of these multipliers.

    Youth Trainer Empowerment:
        11 youth trainers participated in the Learning Teaching Activities (LTTA) and are subsequently empowered to educate other youth workers and peer leaders.
        Post-project, these trainers will organise smaller training sessions in their native organisations, thereby indirectly benefitting another 20-30 youth workers who will be equipped to use the project’s outputs in their daily activities.

    Local Impact:
        84 local multipliers/youth workers across three countries empowered during the multiplier events. The focus was on accentuating the significance of youth work in averting cyberbullying and peer violence, and ensuring the necessary support structures are in place for at-risk youth.

In sum, the project not only produced valuable, multilingual resources for the prevention of cyberbullying and peer violence but also ensured the empowerment of a significant number of youth workers, trainers, and multipliers, amplifying its impact across multiple countries.

2021-1-DK01-KA220-YOU-000028491.title: Game ON
2021-1-DK01-KA220-YOU-000028491.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated in response to the growing interest among young people, both male and female, in e-sports. Reports indicate that 54% of the European population aged 6-64 engage in video gaming, with 74% of players falling within the 15-24 age range. Although many video games have significant learning potential, this learning often occurs unconsciously, with players not recognising or reflecting on the knowledge and skills they acquire while gaming.
 
The project builds upon and draws inspiration from the feedback received from youth workers across Europe who participated in a training course organised by Fora on the same theme in 2019. 

The project addressed the partners' needs to strengthen young people's competences and active learning, innovate their educational approaches by leveraging young people's interest in gaming, enhance their capacity to utilise video games in an educational context, and extend their reach to hard-to-reach youth.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to harness young people's existing interest in video games and transform it into intentional learning by enhancing the capacity of youth workers to support young people in developing essential competencies by gaming. 
 
The following objectives were identified to contribute to the project aim: 
- To develop at least 20 non-formal methods using video games as a tool for learning;
- To fight against stereotypes regarding video games and help youth workers realise the potential in using them in their work with young people;
-  To empower 155 youth workers and other stakeholders to use video games as a tool for learning. 

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented the following activities:
1.	Conducted three transnational meetings and four online project meetings.
2.	Researched young people’s motivations for playing video games, exploring both intentional and incidental learning, as well as their connections to real-life scenarios.
3.	Developed 20 educational methods collaboratively, based on 18 popular video games among youth.
4.	Tested the development methods with young people aged 14 to 21. 
5.	Trained 24 youth workers from partner organisations on how to effectively use the developed methods and video games in their activities with young people.
6.	Organised Multiplier Events to disseminate project results among stakeholders at both local and national levels.
7.	Carried out broader dissemination activities to reach a wide audience of stakeholders, promoting the project results and encouraging their practical application.

<< Results >>

The project concrete outputs and results are:
1. A Toolkit available as an open educational resource containing 20 educational methods using video games a learning tool. 
2. 208 young people aged 14 to 21 (with a few over 21) involved research and testing phases of the method development;
3. 24 youth workers trained to use the methods developed in their educational programmes with young people;
4. 210 stakeholders reached through Multiplier Events fostering understanding on the potential of video games as an educational tool and raising awareness on the project results;
5. 1899 stakeholders reached through dissemination activities (not counting social media);
6. New cooperation between the partners and stakeholder emerged at local level;
7. Strengthen organisational capacity of the partners in the projects and an extended reach to young people through innovative educational approaches.

2021-1-DK01-KA220-YOU-000028539.title: BANG! - Bridging All Next Generations
2021-1-DK01-KA220-YOU-000028539.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to the BANG! project with the aim of addressing needs within European high schools. The project's emphasis on empowering youth to actively engage in and enhance their skills when it comes to creativity, mental health and well-being and co-creation resonates with our values at Kaospilot. 
One of the key aspects that drew us to apply for this project during COVID19 is its commitment to leveraging digital technologies to create inclusive learning environments. At Kaospilot we have been developing inclusive learning environments for over 30 years - and during COVID19 we needed to adapt to the changing world in order to keep providing this value to educators and young students. 


<< Objectives >>

The overall objective of the BANG! project was to enable Europe’s youth to tackle an increasingly complex world, by supporting young learners and their educators with a tailored digital and blended learning framework and programme geared towards developing creativity, well-being and co- creation….
-To equip youth with the ability to understand new concepts, think critically and creatively and act entrepreneurially to develop and apply new ideas. 
-To support youth succeeding in a digital and interconnected world while working with innovation, creativity, critical thinking, problem solving, communication and collaboration. 
-To provide society with active youth focused on new socially oriented solutions for existing and emerging problems. 
- To support youth developing a practice around their well-being. 

<< Implementation >>

For our project implementation, we prioritized digital education content creation through webinars, designed to actively engage students in shaping their personal and educational journeys while inviting them to contribute to the development of the BANG! project from its early stages.

Throughout the project lifespan, we held transnational meetings in partner countries to facilitate collaboration, exchange ideas, and ensure alignment across all project activities. These meetings served as crucial milestones in our journey toward achieving our project objectives and both students and their educators we highly engaged in these meetings. 

Additionally, we organized an international Summer Lab, which we later called a 'Learning Innovation Festival.' This event served as a platform to involve young learners and their educators in a blended learning program, gathering valuable feedback for the project at large, gave the students involbed a chance to connect across countries, and moreover, it provided an opportunity to disseminate project outputs.

To ensure widespread dissemination and maximize the impact of our project, we conducted national showcases, also known as multiplier events, in each partner country. These events marked the culmination of our project, where we presented and promoted our results to various local and global stakeholders.

<< Results >>

Through collaborative efforts with teachers and students from all participating partner countries, we have co-created a learning framework and a collection of learning activities. This framework reflects diverse perspectives and ensures relevance across different cultural contexts.
Our final project website serves as a central hub, providing easy access to our framework and an additional toolbox of activities that are well tested and co-creatged by educators and their students from all partner countries onvolved. All of the resources on this website is Open Educational Resources (OERs) available for download and translated into five languages (English, Danish, Italian, Greek, and Croatian).
We have developed a project brand, which includes a logo, a user-friendly website, and active social media channels.
During the project we have.. 
- Documented all project activities through photos and videos, capturing key moments which are to be found on our project website and our social media channels. 
- To support partners and participants in disseminating and maximizing the impact of the project results, created a dissemination kit. This kit includes templates for presentations, leaflets, and other promotional materials.

2021-1-DK01-KA220-YOU-000028972.title: SOUP Sharing
2021-1-DK01-KA220-YOU-000028972.summary:
<< Background >>

The interest in being an entrepreneur amongst youngsters are growing, however the difficulties in getting an initiative starting can be overwhelming, both in terms of lack of financial support, but also in terms of knowledge thereof. We had come across a concept that could, with adaption, be a possible solution that embarked both issues. 
We wanted to create a supportive community and an event for gathering in order to network and help young entrepreneurs follow their dreams and learn how to implement projects or start a small business. By setting up a SOUP event we furthermore wanted to give the power to the people by implementing a democratic voting system, where the audience members themselves got to vote on the most interesting project of the event. Community driven activities, we believed would be the way forward and we wanted to explore the impact an event like this could have as well as the cultural differences needed to reach the intended goal. 

<< Objectives >>

We aim to create a community of support, by having the people of the community donate and vote for a project to be funded. In this way the project funded will already have a seed planted in the community and gained an interest from possible clients/users to be involved in the outcome of the project. Not only will the community gain awareness into the ideas of local entrepreneurs, the entrepreneurs themselves will have the opportunity to test out their idea, to see if there is a market for their proposal. They will at the same time also be guided with suggestions of how to improve their initial idea to make it more suitable for the market.
We will host workshops on various topics for both the entrepreneurs and the community to gain knowledge and experience and to hopefully gain a sense of initiative to implement a project themselves.
We aim to build a strong independent community that has the ability to support itself on its own in a circular economy.
“The money the community donates will resonate into something else of value for the community”
The aim for the E+ project is to apply this method of thinking into other European cities and to create a network across borders for entrepreneurs to develop even bigger projects together.


<< Implementation >>

In the duration of 2 years we had;
4 TPMs - each held at a different location and country
3+ local events hosted by each partnering country, meaning 3x8=24 local events reaching hundreds of young people and building a community
Creation of a guidebook as project result, combining all the finds and data of cultural differences and how to set up your own SOUP event. 
8 multiplier events - each partner hosted a multiplier event locally to share the project result in terms of a guidebook. 
1 LTT - which turned out to be more of a compact training on how to do SOUP events, where we used to guidebook as reference and could share the results through this training as well. 
Social media campaign, which is still ongoing. 

<< Results >>

We created a digital publication of how to implement SOUP events in Europe, based on the experiences of the partnering countries and which cultural aspect, you should take into consideration when implementing. We up-skilled ourselves and all the stakeholders involved in the cultural differences and how to work together on a common goal, that requires detailed knowledge of legislation in the European countries as well as the local communities cultures, which can have a subculture, that has different needs and wishes for them, than the main culture of a certain country.

2021-1-EL02-KA220-YOU-000029015.title: Social and Sustainable skills for young NEET population
2021-1-EL02-KA220-YOU-000029015.summary:
<< Background >>

The SOSUSK consortium aimed at facing an important challenge related to the NEETs' skills and competencies and also fostering their sustainable opportunities for employment and self-employment with specific attention toward social and green entrepreneurship. It allowed them to engage in dialogue with various stakeholders to explore possible solutions for creating economically, socially and environmentally sustainable enterprises.

SOSUSK was thought, designed and structured to fully respond to the needs of the target group:
• Access to digital education and innovative training opportunities allowing them to find their job placement, thus, contributing to more prosperous and stable societies
• Tackling youth unemployment, especially for NEETs by upskilling their entrepreneurial skills
• Acquisition of new competencies and skills that can allow them to be employed or transform entrepreneurial ideas into start-ups with positive social, economic and environmental impact
• Full awareness of the role and importance of the educational and training system to sustain their potential and employment opportunities

<< Objectives >>

SOSUSK sought to upskill NEETs (especially those living in remote or rural areas) to enhance employability, develop social and green entrepreneurial opportunities, and allow them to engage in dialogue with various stakeholders to explore possible solutions for creating sustainable enterprises. 

In this context, SOSUSK’s objectives were to:
• Promote digital education among young people
• Improve the social inclusion of NEETs through the starting of new social enterprises
• Ingrain the green and digital transition in the DNA of the EU’s Youth
• Support young people with key competencies needed to transform entrepreneurial ideas into start-ups with positive social, economic and environmental impact
• Facilitate innovative learning practices as a response to the COVID-19 pandemic by developing an online educational toolkit
• Promote practices based on sustainable, smart and inclusive growth
• Equip youth organisations with innovative working tools to invest in young people’s potential and social capital
• Create a space for European organisations to network and come up with clear ideas aiming at boosting youth participation, social change and better understanding of the EU values and concepts

<< Implementation >>

Project Management: As the project coordinator and in close collaboration with all partners, the Academy of Entrepreneurship (AKEP) ensured SOSUSK’s smooth implementation throughout its life cycle. AKEP prepared the bilateral agreements for the partners to sign, prepared and shared with all partners the Project Management Manual (Action Plan, a guide that contained all project activities, allocation of responsibilities and timeframes), the Code of Conduct, and the templates for periodic financial reports & financial/budget management. It also set up a collaboration and storage tool (Google Drive), created the Risk Management Plan, arranged monthly online meetings with the partners to evaluate the state of the art and working progress, share opinions and take strategic decisions for the next steps, organised the first Transnational Meeting in Athens, and prepared the Interim and Final Reports. Regarding the TPMs, BREZA organised the second one in Osijek (HR) and ARESEL organised the third one in Bucharest (RO)

Dissemination: CCITABEL (Dissemination leader) created the project’s visual identity (logo, templates, letterheads, leaflets, newsletters, etc.), the project website (https://sosuskproject.eu/), the social media pages (Facebook, LinkedIn), the Dissemination Plan, and prepared the dissemination report for the activities undertaken by each partner in assigned periods. The partners translated all dissemination material into their national language to ensure the project’s impact at a national level. Regarding social media planning, the consortium adopted a rotation scheme where each partner was responsible for the social media posts for one month and then rotated with the other partners until the end of the project. A relevant part of dissemination was the organisation of the national Multiplier Events that attracted 203 participants in total. Last but not least, AKEP created the Exploitation Plan to ensure the sustainability of the project and its results after the end of SOSUSK’s life cycle.

Quality Assurance: BREZA (QA leader) ensured the project’s quality through evaluation surveys (bi-annual, quality of project results, TNMs, training activity, Multiplier Events). 

Project Results: 
PR1 - Good practices collection and analysis on innovative digital learning methods for green and social entrepreneurship: SWUNR and ARESEL (PR1 leaders) defined the structure and guidelines for the desktop research and the collection of best practices. A specific document was produced defining the selection criteria, collection process and templates. The partners proceeded with the desktop research and identified at least 3 practices each based on the set criteria. SWUNR compiled the analysis report integrating all partners’ inputs. The report provided a comprehensive understanding of all the issues related to education on green and social entrepreneurship and the need for skills and knowledge improvement for NEETs. The partners provided their comments and suggestions to be analysed and included in the finalisation of the report in EN and afterwards in all partner languages. 
PR2 - E-learning toolkit for green and social entrepreneurship: AKEP (PR2 leader) compiled a methodological guide that included training objectives, key findings derived by PR1, the structure of training modules, modules allocation, guidelines for desktop research and pilot testing, and relevant templates to be used. Glocal Factory (co-leader) developed the peer review process in the context of this activity. The methodological guide was reviewed and accepted by all partners. The partners researched and reviewed already existing training material to avoid repetition and identified potential gaps for the development of the modules. Each partner identified 3-5 training resources, and after reviewing and comparing the content, they started developing the 7 modules (1 module/partner). To ensure a better quality for the e-learning toolkit, each partner reviewed one module of a different partner by completing a specific template. Based on the feedback, the partners made the necessary adjustments to the modules and translated them into their national language. AKEP created guidelines and specific tools for preparing and implementing the pilot activity in each country in consultation with the partnership. 217 participants in total validated the toolkit. Following the provided feedback, the partners made the necessary changes to finalise the toolkit in EN and the national languages.
PR3 - Web-based accelerator program: MOBAD (PR3 leader) developed the platform, set it into use, and shared with the partners a template for the content of the platform so that each partner adapts their module accordingly. MOBAD created 2 videos for each module using an AI tool and AKEP provided the FAQs for the platform. Then, it was tested by youngsters during the transnational training activity and, after its validation, it was translated into all national languages.

<< Results >>

SOSUSK produced 3 main outputs/results:

1) PR1 - Good practices collection and analysis on innovative digital learning methods for green and social entrepreneurship: The final result was an Analysis Report that included best practices across Europe regarding digital learning for social and green entrepreneurship. It was translated into all national partners' languages (GR, IT, HR, BG, FR, RO, PL).

2) PR2 - E-learning toolkit for green and social entrepreneurship: An e-learning toolkit that provided a practical framework for developing specific and targeted entrepreneurial skills and incorporated innovative digital learning methods in the learning process. The toolkit, in a modular format, included the following topics:
- Definition of the legal framework of Social and Green Entrepreneurship in partner countries
- Creation of a Social Business Plan/guidelines for an online plan presentation
- Creation of a Financial Plan and access to funding opportunities
- Entrepreneurship and climate change.
- Ways of adopting Sustainable Development Goals in the entrepreneurship sector
- Presentation of EU policies related to entrepreneurship through animated videos
- Pitching: How to present ideas

Each partner conducted a pilot testing to validate the content of the toolkit with 15 youngsters/country. Upon its finalisation, the partners translated it into all national partners' languages (GR, IT, HR, BG, FR, RO, PL).    

3)PR3 - Web-based accelerator program: The web-based accelerator program is an interactive education platform for early-stage social and green entrepreneurs. This web platform (https://portal.sosusk.eu/login) includes all the modules of the e-learning toolkit in digital format along with a FAQ section. 

A 5-day transnational training took place in Warsaw (Poland) during which 4 youngsters/country tested the online platform to assess its effectiveness. Following their feedback and the necessary amendments, the partners translated the platform (Home page, FAQ section) into all national partners' languages (GR, IT, HR, BG, FR, RO, PL). 

Besides these 3 main results, SOSUSK also delivered the following:
- Project website: https://sosuskproject.eu/
- Project logo
- Dissemination Plan
- Exploitation Plan
- 1 SOSUSK promo video
-  3 newsletters (translated into all national partners' languages)
- 10 articles 
- A project leaflet
- 4 videos from the training activity in Warsaw
 - Risk Management Plan
- Quality Assurance Plan
- 6 national Multiplier Events

The main results of SOSUSK have been uploaded on the Erasmus project dissemination portal.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2021-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000028527.title: Sex Education as the best Weapon against Gender Violence
2021-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000028527.summary:
<< Background >>

Sex education is a legal requirement in almost all EU countries, but the content and quality vary. According to the report "Policies for sex education in the EU" of the European Parliament (2013), the Nordic countries and Benelux have sex education of the highest quality, while the states of eastern and southern Europe have poor or non-existent programs. Although sex education is integrated into the school curriculum in Greece, Spain and Croatia, it is rarely implemented. In addition, according to the School Education Gateway survey on sex education (2019), most teachers, parents and institutions support sex education in schools, however there is no support for educators to manage information and education is limited to human body and its development. We intend to respond to the PROPOSAL FOR A RESOLUTION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT, on the situation of health and sexual and reproductive rights in the Union, within the framework of women's health (2019/2165 (INI), in the section that promotes comprehensive sexuality education for the benefit of young people, urging Member States to ensure access to comprehensive and scientifically correct sexuality education for all primary and secondary school students.

<< Objectives >>

We start from the idea that a good sexual education will prevent behaviors related to gender violence and for this we establish the following objectives: 1-Identify what content, what frequency and what quality have sexual education programs destined to young people (13-18). 2-Carry out a research which will show that effective sex education prevents sexist violence. 3-Develop a guide of good practices about health and affective-sexual rights of young people. 4-Develop an identification plan that includes all those macho attitudes related to sexist violence.
5-Establish a prevention and action manual that explains what to do in case such attitudes appear. 6-Train formal and non-formal teaching professionals. 7-Establish a   support and information program for families in the area of sexual education. 8-Involve young people in the realization, application and conclusion of materials. 9-Integrate young people in the promotion of the materials and activities created, with the aim of structuring them in three lines of action: identification, action and behavior change. 10-Instruct through interaction with young people in the relation between sex and technology.

<< Implementation >>

1-We are going to carry out a research work on the information on sexual education that our general impact group has (young people from 13 to 18 years old), at the beginning, in the middle and at the end of our project, with the aim of knowing the point of initial departure, the impact of our activities on the process of our project and the impact of our activities on the results of the project. 2-We will create an interactive platform, in which all the agents involved in our project will collaborate, from sexologists, team doctors, educators, families and young people that should serve as an example of good habits in the affective-sexual relationship that involve healthy behaviors in relationships sexual behavior among young people, with the aim of establishing behaviors that help prevent the appearance of sexist behaviors, which lead to future gender violence. 3-The young people who take part in our project will perform rap rhymes in which prevention and warning messages are launched, in the face of measures that can be considered as gender violence, related issues such as jealousy, possession, verbal violence, loss of self-esteem, etc. These rhymes will be organized and will result in a video clip, each rhyme will be accompanied by a dance, collecting all the rhymes and dances, for the development of a video clip that helps to raise awareness and disseminate the reality of our project. 4-We are going to create four teaching modules in which we can train and qualify educators in the fields of formal and non-formal teaching. Finally we are going to record a final product, in which we will diversify our tasks, in relation to using different work tools in order to summarize aspects related to the problems of our project, relaunching the leading role of young people, who are an active part and target group of our summary materials: 1-Video-comic 2-Community theater 3-We will establish an Escape Room, with questions and answers about sex education. 4-Creation of a podcast on sexual education in the family environment.

<< Results >>

Relation to Activity 1: Documentary and research work reports Relation to Activity 2: Creation of an interactive platform with 4 rooms: The platform will have four rooms: 1-A room in which young people when they click, will have to select whether they are facing a sexist attitude or not. 2-Another room in which young people can choose a topic associated with the affective-sexual relationship between young people and will refer them to academic information on the topic. 3- Another room where young people can click on news related to sexist attitudes. 4-A last room in which young people can click on song titles and it will show them a song paragraph, which they will identify with good or bad relationship habits.
Relation to Activity 3: Elaboration of a video clip will be subtitled and you will have the option of the five languages, Spanish, Croatian, Polish, Greek and English. Relation to Activity 4: 4 modules will be developed and the topics are: 1) Education for the prevention of sexually transmitted diseases. 2) Education in acceptance and sexual diversity (LGBTIQ
+). 3) Education for the treatment of sex in technology. 4) Affective-sexual education for the prevention of sexist violence . Relation to Activity 5: As a final product, we will record: 1-Video-comic (On the experience of gender violence). 2-Scenes from community theater (about sexting, for example). 3-The Escape Room game (Questions and answers about sexual information). 4-The podcast (The treatment of sex in families).
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000028869.title: Podcast Empléate en Cultura
2021-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000028869.summary:
<< Background >>

The PEC Project (Podcast Employ yourself in Culture) is a cooperation association for youth, led by the Integra Cultural Association (INTEGRA) and with partners from Greece (MOSAIC POLITISMOS & DIMIOURGIKOTITA (MOSAIC), ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND SOCIAL ECONOMY GROUP (EKO ), Italy (STEPP STRATEGIE SERVIZI SVILUPPO SRLS (STEPP), Associazione Italy Meet Indonesia (IMI), Associazione Arte Cultura e Sanità ETS (ARCUSAN) and Croatia (Culture Hub Croatia (CHC).
This project was born from real needs that each country of the participating partners has in common and which can be summarised in three main ones:
-Need 1: Combat the high rate of youth unemployment in the project countries (https://es.statista.com/estadisticas/488897/tasa-de-paro-juvenil-en-los-paises-de-la-ue/);
-Need 2: Promote entrepreneurship, as none of the countries are among the first 30 most favorable countries to entrepreneurship (https://thegedi.org/global-entrepreneurship-and-development-index/); 
-Need 3: Support the cultural sector in a very difficult time due to the restrictions generated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project, the partners aimed to create innovative contents that promotes employability and entrepreneurship of young people in the cultural sector. Specifically, the project aimed to achieve n.3 specific objectives:

Objective 1: Promotion of the employability of young people in the cultural sector;
Objective 2: Promotion of youth entrepreneurship in the cultural sector;
Objective 3: Dissemination of European cultural heritage among young people in the participating countries.

Thus, the project aimed to promote knowledge among young people about employment opportunities and entrepreneurship in the cultural sector, through interviews in video format that have been made available to the public through the project website and profiles on social networks.
In addition, the project aimed to give a boost to the cultural sector, greatly affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, promoting its appeal to young people, not only as something worthy of admiration and respect, but also as a source of opportunity to be used and disseminated.


<< Implementation >>

These are the main macro areas of activies we implemented:
1.	Project Management Activities – to better assure the achievement of project objectives, results and partnership collaboration;
2.	Project Results Development Activities – to achieve the project objectives;
3.	Project Dissemination and Communication Activities – to disseminate about the project, its results, the partnership and create impact

Our achive activities:
•	N. 1 Kick off meeting online
•	N. 3 Transnational Project Meetings (Italy, Spain and Croatia)
•	N. 3 Online Project Meetings 
•	N. 1 Learning and Teaching Activity (Spain)
•	Project Website
•	Youtube Channel + Facebook and IG Pages
•	Google Drive and Whatsapp group between the partners
•	PR1: Videos on employment and entrepreneurship in culture; Leading Partner: STEPP;
        Description: Videos of professionals that serve as an example to follow and a source of inspiration. 2 videos per partner in their country language + English subtitles;
•	PR2: Podcast on employment and entrepreneurship in culture; Leading Partner: MOSAIC;
         Description:8 episodes (1 Greek, 1 Croatian, 1 Italian, 1 Spanish + 4 in English) each partner will talk about its own cultural heritage and the employability and entrepreneurship opportunities it offers, while the English episodes will talk about the cultural heritage of the four partner countries and the opportunities that exist for employability and entrepreneurship.
•	Dissemination: more than 3000 youth and youth workers reached by different project social media, podcast , video.
         Dissemination Specific indicators:
              1 Dissemination & Exploitation Plan
              1 Official Website
              1 Project Logo Design (& Visual Identity)
               4 Social Media platforms ( Instagram, Facebook, Youtube and Spotify)
                e-Newsletters





<< Results >>

Considering the 3 main macro areas of activities we implemented, these are the concrete outputs and results we achieved with our project:

1.	Project Management Activities Results: 
-	Project Timeline and Workplan;
-	Project Financial spreadsheet;
-	Timesheets;
-	Google Drive Folder;
-	WhatsApp group for internal communication;
-	Kick-off meeting online (March 2022);
-	N. 3 ETO (1 intermediate meeting in Italy (June 2022), 1 intermediate meeting in Spain (February 2023), 1 final meeting Croatia (November 2023);
2.	Project Results Development Activities Result:
-	N. 14 Video Interviews (PR1) in Italian, Greek, Spanish, Croatian and English subtitles. Available on Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCexxDFVuU57H6C5VUlgzSig
-	N. 10 Podcast Episodes (PR2) in Italian, Greek, Spanish, Croatian and English. Available on Spotify: https://open.spotify.com/show/5EBAqNlBIrnQpALpm0MwUN?si=82e0c9bedf48449d&nd=1&dlsi=b3698940c2d9470f
Through these videos and podcast episodes, it is intended that young people discover the employment opportunities offered by the sector directly, first-hand, through professionals who are already in this field, who narrated how they managed to dedicate themselves to culture and what tools or job search platforms exist in the sector, as well as the possibilities of entrepreneurship, which are highly relevant in the artistic sector. This way, it is expected that young people who listen to the podcast program or watch the videos, increase their skills and abilities when looking for a job within the sector.
-	N.1 Learning,Teaching and Training Activity (19-23 Sept. 2023 La Coruña, Spain) with youth workers who participated to discover new ways of transmitting knowledge on entrepreneurship in the cultural sector to young people, to help their employability.
Number of participants: 24 ( 21 youth working and 3 accompagning person).
3.	Project Dissemination and Communication Activities Results: 
-	Dissemination Plan Document available on Google Drive
-	Project Identity (logo, letterhead, power point presentation) available on Google Drive
-	Project Official website (https://www.pecproject.eu/)
-	Project Official social media pages (Facebook, Instagram, Youtube and Spotify)
-	N.4 Multiplier Events (1 Italy, 1 Croatia, 1 Spain, 1 Greece): 120 presential participants and an online dissemination.
