2021-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000029106.title: RefugeesCode: Acceleration of labour market integration of third country nationals through digital competencies
2021-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000029106.summary:
<< Background >>

The two main needs that we wanted to address with this project were the Demand for digital skills in the EU and the social inclusion of refugees, migrants and asylum seekers. During our research phase, we found that more than a third of the European labour force lacks basic digital skills and digital skills gaps are emerging (Digital Economy and Society Index, 2020) and that 80% of companies in Southern and Eastern Europe found difficulties to source valid candidates for their ICT positions (DSJC, 2020). On the other issue, youth unemployment in Europe is at almost 20% and Greece, Spain and Belgium are counted among the 5 European countries with the highest unemployment for non-EU-born people, with 29.0%, 19.9% and 13.8% respectively (Eurostat, 2019). Tackling these common needs with the expertise of the created consortium for this project, our approach was to establish a fully-functioning Tech Academy in Madrid to target these needs at a local level.

<< Objectives >>

(1) Support refugees, migrants and asylum seekers (RMAS) in Europe in acquiring and developing digital skills and key employability competences for the digital sector: Transfer knowledge and good practices to establish a fully-running tech academy for RMAS in Madrid; Develop and improve existing tech academies within the partner organisations by sharing experiences and best practices & conducting qualitative research on how to improve partnerships with the private sector; Develop a network of organisations working towards labour inclusion for RMAS within the tech sector.

(2) Accelerate labour market integration of RMAS in Europe: Conduct qualitative research on how to develop impactful partnerships with the private sector, especially directed towards beneficiaries employability; Disseminate the results of the research conducted and contribute to developing other employability projects within and beyond this project; Share experiences and best practices for teachers and youth workers to implement training on soft skills and employability in tech academies for RMAS; Foster socio-educational and personal development, as well as participation in civic and social life of RMAS at a European level.




<< Implementation >>

The activities that we implemented during our project were:

Activity 1: Coaching programme for Madrid for Refugees: During this 40 day period, Madrid for Refugees received personal and intensive support from OCC Spain in developing a solid base for the implementation of our tech academy in Madrid. With support of two experienced professionals from OCC Spain, Madrid for Refugees has received training in order to:
- Learn new tools and project management methodologies to effectively run the academy
- Further develop their current technical curriculum
- Support our students in the most broad-possible way (to offer legal, psychological and other forms of support)
- Create a larger volunteer community of tech and employability volunteers
- Increase our social media presence and visibility
- Extend our partner network, both in non-profit and the profit sector
- Receive best practices in running a complete tech academy, on the short and long term

Activity 2: How to run a non-profit tech academy: an exchange of best practices 
This training was based on sharing knowledge and best practices on the following aspects of the management of tech academies and other digital skills educational programmes for migrants and refugees:
- The role of a Head of Education
- The role of employability skills training
- The curriculum and how to improve it
- Management of extensive volunteer communities
- Keeping the community of students, volunteers and partners alive
- Useful management tools
- Involvement of ESC Volunteers in the academy
- Organising Online Job Fairs
- Further involvement of other EU and Erasmus+ project opportunities

Activity 3:  How to offer more than education: the importance of additional services to beneficiaries
This training was based on the activities that are carried out in MigraCode Barcelona, where students can benefit from free psychological, legal, gender, technical and language support. In this activity partners were encouraged to bring their (1) knowledge and experience on offering additional support to their beneficiaries, or (2) needs to help their beneficiaries. Best practices on offering additional support and knowledge were shared and discussed by all partners. Suggestions for improvement and/or further implementations were be given, which will lead to concrete plans.

Activity 4: Presentation of research results on “How to develop impactful partnerships with the private sector”
During this online activity, the results of our qualitative research for developing and improving partnerships with the private sector were presented, which was followed by a brainstorming workshop on how to improve and update our respective techniques on developing impactful partnerships with the private sector. All 5 partner organisations participated in this activity, conducting local qualitative research by interviewing potential private organisation partners in the digital sector or with digital needs.


<< Results >>

The results and outputs expected at the beginning of the project that we have achieved were:

(1) Successful implementation of Madrid For Refugees pilot course on software development for Refugees, Migrants and Asylum Seekers (RMAS) tailored to the needs of the Spanish market, involving 769 working hours on HTML, CSS, Javascript & Vue.js. 31 volunteers participated in this pilot course, covering teaching, mentoring, coordination, and partnerships. 17 RMAS students enrolled and we completed the course with a graduation rate of 53%. The graduated and also non-graduated advanced students have also participated in workshops to improve employability prospects and were supported by our team in their job searches.

(2) We generated and released six pieces of documentation for knowledge-sharing purposes, as well as a course syllabus for the pilot, four project impact reports, and additional dissemination materials (attached).

(3) We facilitated a total of 30 knowledge-sharing and best practices sessions and discussions throughout the project within 2 transnational meetings and 4 international activities, engaging the full consortium of five organizations in all sessions.

(4) The relationship between the consortium partners was established and reinforced throughout the project, leading to initial steps of the creation of a strong consortium to not only participate in joint projects, but to keep facilitating knowledge-sharing, experiences and learnings, cross-collaboration, implementation of common tools and metrics for impact and shared resources. 

(5) We fostered 12 partnerships with non-profit and private sector organizations within the Madrid RMAS and Digital ecosystems. One of those partnerships with the private sector has covered the coordination costs for the course pilot.

All project goals were achieved.
topics: Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

2021-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000029188.title: e-Makers
2021-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000029188.summary:
<< Background >>

Climate change is becoming increasingly harmful, prompting social enterprises to find solutions and create environmental impacts. Digital transformation opens various opportunities for social enterprises to tackle environmental challenges such as access to clean water, electricity, and education. 

However, it is noted that 71% of social entrepreneurs struggle with financial sustainability. This situation highlights the need for more support and digital-based training for young entrepreneurs, especially those in environmental social enterprise. 

Digital transformation can promote the growth and financial stability of social enterprises. Effective tools such as gamification methodology can enhance training for youth in this sector, enabling them to use digital tools in tandem with entrepreneurial skills to address societal and environmental problems.
(Source: [https://blogs.lse.ac.uk/businessreview/2020/06/11/self-sustainability-the-dilemma-at-the-heart-of-socialentrepreneurship/, https://www.pure.ed.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/15495710/Games_final_JRC78777.pdf])

<< Objectives >>

The project aims to nurture environmental social entrepreneurship among the youth through digitization. The specific objectives include enhancing the digital competencies of youth workers, promoting social entrepreneurship and environmental awareness among youths, and developing organizational capacities for innovative social entrepreneurship training.
The project strives to strengthen social entrepreneurship activities, develop advanced digital skills, improve soft and professional skills and enhance cross-border communication among youth workers.
 It also aims to adapt gamification methodology, contributing to the sustainability of social enterprises, and internationalization strategies. The project aims to build a sustainable society by improving green and soft skills of the youth.


<< Implementation >>

Activities were designed to meet the identified needs in the field of social entrepreneurship. Each activity and the output supports the objectives of the project. The main activity of the project is the development of three intellectual outputs. 
Through transnational meetings, LTT activity, and multiplier events, the quality of the outputs were intensified. 
Accordingly, the development of the intellectual outputs: 
-The non-formal training toolkit of digital social entrepreneurship: 
It was produced for the youth workers to improve their skills and resources to train young people on social entrepreneurship and environmental challenges including digital opportunities. The training materials included in the toolkit were designed by non-formal learning methodologies. In this way, the transversal and soft skills of young people are enhanced as well as the social entrepreneurship skills. 
-LTT activity was significant to assess the quality of the training materials and to make necessary improvements. 
-The manual for digitalization of social enterprises: 
It was developed to enhance the advanced digital skills of the youth workers. The manual covers all stages and the workflows in social enterprises, including data management, financial management and marketing, education, research, and capacity-building activities for environmental issues. 
EU&PRO has been an associated partner for organizing virtual classes for youth workers after completing the output. Through these virtual classes, youth workers have received training on digital opportunities to be employed in different stages of social enterprises. Thus, EU&Pro based the three days of training on the first two outputs that have been developed for the E-makers project. You can see the training recorded in E-makers website: https://e-makers.org/en/training.aspx?Id=125 
On the one hand, the functionality of training materials in the online manual was tested, and on the other hand, youth workers gained invaluable skills and resources to improve the sustainability of their enterprises. 
-Virtual Board Game: 
This improves the social entrepreneurship skills of youth workers and young people in innovative and enjoyable ways. The game is instructive for the target groups since players will learn the fundamentals of social entrepreneurship, the models of social enterprises, and how to achieve sustainability while playing the game. 
Playtesting sessions were implemented to test the game with youth workers from partner institutions. The first test was carried out in Cagliari, with TDM volunteers and partners of the consortium during the last international meeting of the consortium. https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/1LT8_OgAKevpel1tWwiyaSreJ3J_VwTKS 
Through these playtesting sessions and feedback received from participants, improvements were made to the game. In fact, due to technical issues, we have delayed the delivery of the project in order to have the game in a high quality.
Website for the game: https://www.emakersgame.com/ or in the website of the project https://e-makers.org/en/default.aspx#Results where you also can fin the manual for the game.
Furthermore, the virtual board is available on online platforms without any costs or limitations. In this way, the project will reach more target groups beyond the European borders.
- LTT activity: 
The activity aims to improve the social entrepreneurship skills of young people aged between 18-30. Young people who are working to fight against environmental challenges in youth initiatives, university clubs, or individually were encouraged to implement their innovative ideas in social enterprises through this activity. 
All training materials was designed to equip young people with the necessary skills and competencies. Moreover, through LTT activity, the toolkit was tested whether the training materials are of the desired quality or not. 
-Transnational Meetings: 
Through the meetings, the quality of the project outputs, the time and budget management, and the general project management were regulated by all partner institutions. These meetings strength the coordination and communication between partners. 
In this way, a productive working environment was ensured to improve the quality, effects, and scope of the activities. 
-Multiplier Events: 
During the multiplier events and dissemination activities, project outputs and results were introduced to the target groups, NGOs, decision-making authorities, and individuals. Thanks to these activities, the awareness of environmental problems and social entrepreneurship will be increased in society.


<< Results >>

The project produced both tangible and intangible results on participants, target groups, participating institutions, and broader circles. Three intellectual outputs were the most significant tangible results of the project. 
The intellectual outputs are been used by the participating institutions to improve youth workers' digital competencies and promote social entrepreneurship training of young people. 
The non-formal toolkit and the online manual, as tangible results, enhance the quality of management, research, marketing, and youth work in the participating institutions by strengthening the social entrepreneurship skills and advanced digital competencies of youth workers. 
In this way, the partner institutions satisfy the needs of their target groups with innovative and comprehensive resources. 
Moreover, transnational cooperation enables the participating institutions to produce quality results to improve the sustainability of social enterprises and the social entrepreneurship skills of young people.  Youth workers will become much more competent in managing all stages in the workflow of the social enterprises by completing the project and integrating the intellectual outputs into the everyday activities of the participating institutions. 
Furthermore, a virtual board game adds value to the capacities of the participating institutions by increasing their recognition and reputation at the international level. 
The project activities enhance the know-how of all partners, improving capacities and professionalism to work at the EU level, and strengthening their networks across Europe. 
Furthermore, the participants from all partner institutions have benefited from the results produced during the project. The project's outcomes create the ideal setting for participants from partner institutions to develop more modern, professional, and open working environments. Transversal and soft skills obtained throughout the project implementation add value to the work culture in the institutions. 
The project results enhance the management, teamwork, and communication skills of managing staff and project working groups in all participating institutions. Other expected results of the project are as follows: Youth workers have been provided comprehensive training materials on advanced digital skills to manage the workflow of social enterprises in all stages, including financial management and marketing, data management, research, education, and capacity-building for environmental issues. 
Youth workers have been equipped with innovative tools, training methodologies, and materials to train young people on digital social entrepreneurship and environmental challenges. 
The outputs of the project strengthen the non-formal training capacities of the youth workers and, in this way, the necessary quality human resources are provided for the sustainability of the social enterprises. 
Through the implementation of the intellectual outputs, young people received quality tips, clues, or information on social entrepreneurship. 
Through non-formal training activities, young people’s social entrepreneurship skills, as well as soft skills such as teamwork, communication, and initiative skills, have been enhanced. 
The awareness of environmental issues has been increased among young people, and they have been encouraged to take action to solve these problems and to become E-Makers as can be seen after analyzing the evaluations and the video created for the LTT in Soria.. The project results have been disseminated to wider circles so that other social enterprises will benefit from the training materials and tools produced during the project. The awareness of environmental challenges will be increased in society. In this way, the social enterprises will be able to build relationships with other interest groups, institutions, and initiatives across the boundaries.

2021-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000029293.title: Young people and SDGs
2021-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000029293.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project to address the needs identified during the 2012 United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development. The development of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) was initiated to succeed the Millennium Development Goals, aiming to integrate all aspects of sustainable development into the global agenda. Disability is explicitly mentioned in various SDG sections related to education, employment, inequality, accessibility, and data collection. Recognizing the importance of addressing these issues, our Erasmus+ proposal, "Young People and SDGs," was created. The project addressed the pressing needs of raising awareness about the SDGs, fostering inclusion for people with disabilities, encouraging dialogue among young people, and nurturing active citizenship to contribute to a more sustainable future .

<< Objectives >>

The Erasmus+ proposal "Young People and SDGs" aimed at contributing to the awareness of young people about the Sustainable Development Goals and promoting the inclusion of people with disabilities (PWD). The initiative sought to achieve this by fostering an active dialogue among EU young people with and without disabilities, with the intention of building future active and informed citizens of the EU.

The specific objectives were as follows:

SO1: The promotion of active citizenship, engagement, and participation of young people through facilitating a dialogue on the 17 SDGs to effectively include PWD.

SO2: Empowering young people to take on an active role in their communities and the environment at local, European, and international levels.


<< Implementation >>

The objective was pursued through the following activities and phases:

Phase 1 involved conducting research to exchange knowledge, methodologies, and best practices regarding non-formal educational activities that encourage youth participation and engagement. It began with a field research initiative and was followed by a national desk research conducted by all partners, resulting in a comprehensive research report. This report aimed to understand the needs necessary for implementation in the guide and course.  The guide  and the online course placed a significant emphasis on environmental considerations, as well as social inclusion and participation.

Phase 2 entailed the development of a guide intended to serve as a fundamental resource for stakeholders to implement activities that promote the participation of both individuals with and without disabilities, specifically in advancing the SDGs. The guide was translated into all the languages of the consortium.

Phase 3 involved the development and implementation of a training course for over 70 youth workers, with more than 10 youth workers participating per organization. These workers not only honed their professional and personal skills but also learned to implement the acquired methodologies in diverse environments. The online training course was uploaded to the PREDIF training platform. The course focused on providing specific training to youth workers on the SDGs and non-formal educational activities, aiming to enhance the involvement of young people with disabilities and fewer opportunities in cultural and educational activities.

R2 comprised various phases:

Phase 1 concentrated on equipping youth workers with essential skills to promote youth participation and awareness of the SDGs. This involved the development and facilitation of three practical workshops led by 4film on creating videos and accessible material. PREDIF provided instructions on accessibility, and FARE gave guidance on creating promotional materials. Segments of the workshops were recorded to broaden their reach among youth workers.  Additionally, the activities for promoting the SDGs among young individuals included piloting activities. After completing the online course and workshops, the youth workers applied their learned knowledge and practices through these pilot activities. Face-to-face workshops were conducted from the youth workers to the young people to teach about the SDGs and create accessible and concise videos to promote the 17 SDGs.

In Phase 2, youth with and without disabilities and fewer opportunities participated in creating videos about the SDGs, which were then shared within the community to raise awareness and initiate discussions about the SDGs.

Phase 3 involved an online competition and contest, where each video won a specific category.

Furthermore, all partners ensured extensive dissemination and promotion of the project results, augmenting the project's multiplier effects and ensuring the transfer of the model.

They organized multiplier events at local levels and conducted dissemination activities throughout the project's duration, both locally and nationally. This involved leveraging online media channels such as social networks, websites, etc., actively engaging various stakeholders.

<< Results >>

The project comprised two primary Results (R):

R1: Development of a research report and the creation of an accessible, targeted online toolkit guide for Young Individuals with Disabilities (YDs) aimed at empowering all young people with disabilities through the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The toolkit guide involved initial research into non-formal educational activities, methodologies, and documentation relevant to implementing youth activities for SDG development. It also gathered best practices from partner countries regarding youth activities for individuals with and without disabilities. The guide placed a significant emphasis on environmental considerations, as well as social inclusion and participation.

Furthermore, following the research and the toolkit guide, an online awareness-raising training course was developed to emphasize the importance of SDG implementation in society. It also concentrated on involving young people in these activities and fostering collaboration for SDG development. Additionally, it highlighted good practices in youth activities, equipping youth workers with the requisite knowledge, competencies, and skills to engage with young people and ensure the inclusion of Persons with Disabilities (PCDs).The training course also placed a significant emphasis on environmental considerations, as well as social inclusion and participation.

R2: Pilot action - Implementation of activities promoting the SDGs, aimed at Youth Trainers (YTs): After the completion of the course, YTs were encouraged to apply their acquired knowledge and practices by creating accessible short videos, organizing photo exhibitions, and conducting events to promote the 17 SDGs for the inclusion of Junior Citizens with Disabilities (JCDs).

This pilot action encompassed several outcomes:

Conducting three practical workshops on these activities, encompassing video creation using devices such as tablets and mobile phones, proficient editing with accessible and free tools, strategies for marketing on social media platforms to disseminate videos and posters, and ensuring accessibility using non-professional tools based on basic rules. The youth works implemented piloting activities with the young people, promoting the SDGs
Collaborative video creation: Each country collaborated with youth organizations, where young people with and without disabilities, assisted by youth workers, created the videos with the topic of SDGs,choosing one or two SDGs per video.  The objective of the videos were to create awarness and pormote the SDGs and the soical inlcusion.
Hosting an online competition and disseminating various video winners categories.
Summarizing:

Outcome of R1:

- Research report
- Online Toolkit: Toolkit guide in 7 languages and an online training course.

Outcome of R2:

Conducted three workshops on creating videos and accessible materials.
Facilitated piloting activities by youth workers to educate young people on SDGs and produce videos.
Creation of videos by young people and youth workers on SDGs, followed by a contest to identify winners in specific categories. Each video was recognized in a specific category. Dissemination of videos.

2021-1-FI01-KA220-YOU-000028901.title: Inclusion Is On
2021-1-FI01-KA220-YOU-000028901.summary:
<< Background >>

Inclusion is On based on the need to rethink youth free-time activities in the post-pandemic world. The project aimed to raise awareness on how to ensure more inclusive and accessible free-time activities for diverse youth and thus, for example, contribute to preventing exclusion and radicalization.

<< Objectives >>

-Share good practices and other interesting experiences and/or materials among the partner organizations and from different perspectives.
-Develop new tools to promote social inclusion based on the needs of each partner organization.
-Increase the levels of knowledge of partner organizations on social inclusion in the context of youth free-time activities.
-Disseminate and educate youth workers in Europe, especially the partner countries, to the materials of the project.

<< Implementation >>

-One transnational project meeting in Croatia.
-Five international learning, teaching, and training activities in Finland, Estonia, Hungary, Czechia, and Italy. These included familiarizing the participants to the topic of the project as well as the diverse local contexts, workshops, study visits and guest speakers, an innovation camp, recording a podcast and a final training seminar for youth workers. 
-Multiplier events in all partner countries to disseminate the project results towards the end of the project.
-Online meetings.

<< Results >>

-Initial and final surveys on social inclusion for youth workers in partner countries.
-Tool pack with good practices and tools to promote social inclusion in youth free-time activities.
-Innovation model to create new tools to promote social inclusion.
-Webinar/training model to support the adoption of the contents of the tool pack.
-Podcast series summarizing the main topics of the project and gained experiences.

2021-1-FR02-KA220-YOU-000028696.title: CodER: Teaching coding and microcontrollers to young people through virtual Escape Rooms
2021-1-FR02-KA220-YOU-000028696.summary:
<< Background >>

The CodER project became a focal point for Digijeunes, Kalimera, C.I.P., RITE, Challedu, and AKMI due to their shared acknowledgment of pressing educational gaps. Digijeunes, focusing on youth tech education, identified a programming knowledge deficit, prompting exploration into this technical domain. Kalimera, committed to pioneering digital education, embraced CodER to introduce gamified escape rooms, aligning with their innovative teaching ethos and sparking interest in programming.
 C.I.P., with a cross-sectoral approach, aimed to equip youth with coding skills, emphasizing problem-solving and critical thinking. Their focus on training unemployed youth found fulfillment in CodER's gamified escape rooms, engaging educators across diverse fields. RITE's alignment with CodER was rooted in their vision for innovation and technology transfer, addressing programming challenges and promoting socially valuable coding education.
 At AKMI and Challedu, a commitment to dynamic vocational education led them to recognize CodER's  potential. Both sought to bridge the theory-practice gap, preparing students for the evolving job market by offering hands-on training in real-world programming applications.


<< Objectives >>

The consortium, driven by a collective vision, embarked on a mission with diverse goals in targets, content, and quality. Digijeunes aimed to equip youth workers with theoretical and practical tools in programming, extending the focus to inspire girls, unemployed youth, and NEETs. The goal was to motivate them to acquire new technical and soft skills through engaging learning experiences. 
C.I.P. focused on transferring essential programming knowledge through non-formal education, using escape rooms for gamified impact. Integration of online tools enhanced learning effectiveness. RITE empowered youth workers with fundamental programming knowledge, addressing youth unemployment through innovative methods like educational escape rooms, gamified processes, and VR elements.
AKMI aimed to inspire and empower youth through the CodER project's Escape Room platform, targeting youth unemployment with tailored training. Challedu sought new tools and skills in emerging technologies, integrating them into internal activities. Through gamification, Challedu aimed to elevate the learning process for young people, aligning with the consortium's mission to foster skills for the modern labor market.


<< Implementation >>

In terms of the project results, the consortium created and developed main deliverables.
All partners actively engaged in the entirety of project activities, attending transnational in-person meetings and monthly online meetings. At these sessions, one or more project managers represented each organization.  There were 1 or 2 representatives from each organization in each in person meeting. These took place in Athens in October 2022 and June 2023. The consortium run 18 online meeting in total. These took place every month via Zoom calls, they lasted on average 1 hour and gathered on average 6 representatives from across the consortium.
As part of the project we implemented a number of pilot tests, aiming to experiment the educational ressources developed by the consortium. Pilot tests took place in Cyprus, France, Greece and Croatia, across May 2022 and November 2023 with a dense pilot test agenda in each session. As a total, 164 people participated in the pilot tests, this said the number of participants in each session varied significantly across different countries and organizations. Each pilot test was systematically followed by an evaluation questionnaire aiming to gather qualitative feedback concerning the ressources from the beneficiaires directly involved in the experiences.
A comprehensive round table discussion was orchestrated, bringing together a diverse group encompassing youth workers, professionals, and experts in programming, design, and technology. The primary objective of this activity was to engage with individuals entrenched in the tech sector, seeking valuable insights and feedback regarding the pertinence of the resources envisaged by the consortium for development. This insightful event transpired in June 2022 across various countries through Zoom, attracting a total of 32 participants.
Moreover, as part of PR3, a scenario competition was initiated. Each organization invited young individuals to fully develop an Escape Room scenario centered around programming and microcontrollers. In each organization, one or more teams were assembled to compete for the top three scenarios. Guided by the local organization, each team crafted a storyline encompassing riddles and activities designed to facilitate learning about coding and microcontrollers. Digijeunes created templates for the young participants, providing a structured framework for inputting the relevant information for their envisioned escape room scenarios. Additionally, C.I.P, Challedu, Kalimera and Digijeunes organized and hosted individual multiplier events for the project. Throughout project implementation, each organization played a proactive role in ensuring the success of the collaborative efforts, dissemination and improvement of the content materials.


<< Results >>

The tangible outputs of the project encompassed several components, including the CodER Module, the CodER methodological and pedagogical guide, the CodER Escape Room Scenarios Handbook and resources, the CodER inspirational scenarios, the CodER youth participants' winning scenarios, and the Digital Escape Room Generator.
C.I.P. spearheaded the development of the CodER Module, overseeing its separation into two parts. Their responsibilities included work distribution, module material development, ensuring overall homogeneity, and providing assistance as needed. The first part focused on a coding module, emphasizing programming basics and the Python language. The second part aimed to impart basic knowledge of microcontrollers and embedded systems to youth organizations. Consortium-wide desk research aligned learning objectives with market-required skills. The CodER Module was translated into partner languages, promoting transferability across European youth organizations.
Challedu, leading the second result, crafted the framework for CodER's methodological and pedagogical guide. The guide targeted youth workers and educators in STEM fields, covering educational escape rooms, learning programming through escape rooms, and teaching coding methodology. Each partner organized round table discussions, with Challedu overseeing the guide's structure and main creation. Chapters were assigned to RITE and AKMI for drafting, with feedback provided by all partners. The guide was subsequently translated into partner languages.
Digijeunes led the third result, developing six ready-to-use Escape rooms on coding and microcontrollers from scratch. This encompassed physical and digital scenarios, each with guides for youth workers and participants, clues, and complementary materials. Inspiration scenarios and contexts were published on the website, accompanied by two introductory videos. A scenarios contest allowed participants to design their escape rooms, with winners receiving a 200 euros voucher. All scenarios were translated into partner languages.
RITE developed the Escape Room Generator platform, integrating mini-games based on programming languages and microcontrollers. The platform enables users to create unique digital escape rooms with customizable characters, backgrounds, themes, items, and music. Users can publish their scenarios, and examples are provided for inspiration. The platform supports user accounts for saving work and is available in all partner languages, fostering inclusivity and accessibility. 
In relation to learning outcomes, the participants in the project developed a comprehensive range of technical and soft skills. The youth involved in the initiative cultivated proficiency in programming, including the capacity to comprehend computer code, differentiate among various programming languages, and grasp computational logic—such as constructing fundamental elements like variables and conditionals. Additionally, they honed their aptitude for applying their knowledge of computer code to fine-tune programs, as well as gained competence in programming electronic sensors and actuators. Simultaneously, they acquired essential soft skills such as problem-solving, teamwork, patience, perseverance.
For youth workers, the project fostered the development of a number of skills, including the proficiency to conduct hands-on workshops on computer coding. They gained the capability to discern and select coding learning resources tailored to their target audience. Moreover, they acquired an understanding of technical jargon in both computer coding and physical computing, as well as a grasp of the fundamental building blocks of computational logic. Additionally, they cultivated the ability to align practical educational activities with various roles in the tech sector, such as computer programming and engineering, and successfully incorporated gamification methodologies into their educational practices.

2021-1-FR02-KA220-YOU-000029769.title: Youth, believe in you and become an entrepreneur !
2021-1-FR02-KA220-YOU-000029769.summary:
<< Background >>

Le taux de chômage élevé des jeunes dû au manque d'opportunités, de confiance en soi, aux difficultés sociales et économiques a motivé notre initiative pour trouver des solutions innovantes pour favoriser l'insertion sociale et professionnelle des jeunes. 
En Croatie et en Macédoine du Nord, le taux d'exode des cerveaux est élevé. En Lituanie, seuls 47,6% des jeunes sont en emploi et en Roumanie 24,5% sont au chômage en 2020. 
En France, la crise sanitaire a aggravé chez les jeunes, des difficultés économiques et sociales, générant une baisse de confiance en eux. Les soutiens à leurs projets ont diminué avec les relations sociales. L'entrepreneuriat a pourtant augmenté, comme une ouverture vers l'insertion socio-professionnelle.
Si les jeunes semblent intéressés par cette voie, ils sont freinés par le manque de connaissances, compétences (pour 2/3), la peur de l'échec (pour 1/2), le manque de modèles d'entrepreneuriat, d'expériences ou de réseaux professionnels, de ressources financières, et leur faible crédibilité face aux clients potentiels.
Certaines entreprises ont du mal à recruter des jeunes et à les retenir dans leurs effectifs. Nous devons donc rapprocher le marché du travail et les jeunes.

<< Objectives >>

A travers notre collaboration, nous souhaitons : - promouvoir l'entrepreneuriat à travers des actions de sensibilisation afin d'informer les jeunes sur l'entrepreneuriat, de développer l'initiative, le sens des responsabilités, la capacité d'innover et d'éveiller le leader en eux. Nous aimerions trouver des outils innovants et des processus efficaces pour y parvenir. Informer les jeunes sur l'entrepreneuriat est la première étape si nous voulons qu'ils réfléchissent aux projets entrepreneuriaux comme moyen d'emploi. - dynamiser le projet entrepreneurial des jeunes, notamment ceux qui ont moins d'opportunités. Nous améliorerons l'accompagnement des jeunes qui souhaitent devenir entrepreneurs en développant un programme de mentorat et en leur offrant la possibilité de participer à des ateliers européens afin de dynamiser le développement de leur entreprise.

<< Implementation >>

- Pour créer un guide de l'entrepreneuriat social des jeunes, nous avons rassemblé les pratiques innovantes de chaque partenaire. Ensuite, nous avons créé une formation pour les animateurs de jeunesse afin de créer les outils les plus intéressants. Lors de cette activité d'apprentissage européenne en France, nous avons enrichi le manuel de leurs expérimentations et noté les conditions de réussite.
- Pour développer un programme de mentorat efficace, nous avons identifié les étapes: recrutement, formation des mentors, préparation des mentorés, suivi, évaluation. 
Après avoir développé la formation des mentors, nous l'avons testée au niveau européen: comment construire une relation de qualité à travers le développement personnel, puis évaluer l'impact de la formation des mentors sur le développement du projet entrepreneurial des mentorés. Les leçons apprises et meilleures pratiques sont rassemblées dans un guide. 
- Pour organiser des ateliers permettant des échanges entre jeunes européens porteurs d'un projet entrepreneurial: un moyen pour eux de se sensibiliser à  la responsabilité sociale et environnementale, de rencontrer des chefs d'entreprise inspirants, et visiter des entreprises européennes. Et pour les animateurs de jeunesse, de disposer d'un guide d'organisation de tels ateliers.

<< Results >>

Résultats:
IO1- Création d'un manuel avec des activités innovantes pour promouvoir l'entrepreneuriat chez les jeunes de 16 à 30 ans
IO2 - Création d'un programme de mentorat: 
IO3 - Création d'un programme européen de formation pour les jeunes porteurs d'un projet entrepreneurial

1ère réunion transnationale Skopje avr.-22
2e réunion transnationale Zagreb juin-23
3è réunion transnationale: En ligne 12 juillet 24
4è réunion transnationale: En ligne 10 octobre 24

Activités d'apprentissage et d'enseignement :
- Formation d'animateurs jeunesse pour apprendre à mettre en œuvre les activités du manuel à Nantes en mars-23
- Formation des mentors  à Skopje juil.-23
- Organisation d' ateliers du programme européen de formation des jeunes : à Vilnius du 4 au 8 mars-24 et à Bucarest du 10 au 24 mais 24.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000028570.title: Depolarization Activism for Resilient Europe
2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000028570.summary:
<< Background >>

In recent years we noticed growing polarization in Europe and have become increasingly concerned about the fact that it tears communities apart and prevents people from coming together in order to solve common challenges. In addition to this, the disillusionment of youth in regards to democracy combined with the lack of belief that their voices can be heard has led to a loss of faith in the system. Furthermore, the presence of anti-European/anti-systemic/populist political parties is a legitimacy and stability threat.
All of these issues are spilling over into the classroom with many teachers unsure how they should address this challenges. Numerous educators we work with expressed a need for classroom-compatible materials that would allow for discussion about these topics without alienating and further polarising their students. 
The materials created during the DARE project allow teachers to cover various topics (polarization, Euroskepticism, xenophobia, populism, discrimination, exclusion and disenfranchisement) while at the same time providing new learning and teaching methods as well as approaches that strengthen European identity, citizenship, values and prevent radicalisation through promoting and amplifying youth voices.

<< Objectives >>

The 'DARE - Depolarization Activism for Resilient Europe' project was a strategic partnership aimed at creating innovative educational materials for both formal and non-formal civic education, applicable in online and face-to-face contexts. These materials aimed to inspire civic engagement and activism among young people, addressing issues such as radicalization, exclusion, racism, xenophobia, homophobia, and discrimination that undermined European values. The project's objectives were: 
a) To develop original blended-learning educational materials promoting depolarization, fostering youth civic engagement, supporting European values, enhancing critical thinking, and strengthening youth resilience in times of crisis. 
b) To empower teachers, educators, and youth workers by providing materials enabling them to address complex contemporary topics using pedagogically innovative methods.
Our goal was to provide educators with the means and confidence to address these difficult challenges as well as remind youth that their thought and participation are not only welcome but of paramount importance for the health of European democracy.


<< Implementation >>

The implementation of the 'DARE - Depolarization Activism for Resilient Europe' project involved several key activities:
a) Four (4) transnational project meetings were carried out, each hosted in one of the partner organization's countries. 
First introductory meeting, hosted by the project beneficiary Hrvatska edukacijska i razvojna mreža za evoluciju sporazumijevanja - HERMES, took place in Zagreb (Croatia). Project meeting lasted from January 27th to January 30th. Two working days were devoted to detailed planning of project management, timeline and communication, also brainstorming about the topics of educational materials each partner organisation should create.
Second meeting took place in Mostar (Bosnia & Herzegovina) where a detailed timeline and work division on intellectual outputs creation was finalized (methodological guidelines, educational materials, videos). An important part of the meeting was defining the procururement criteria for animators and translators. 
Third meeting took place in Belgrade (Serbia). The meeting’s focus was on the fine-tuning and final edits of the materials, enhancement of inclusion and multiperspectivity elements, cross-national and intercultural adaptations.
The last Transnational project meeting took place in Berlin from  February 28 until March 3, 2023. The meeting was focused on the multiplier events and additional dissemination planning. 
b) The creation of educational materials in 6 project languages: 
Ten (10) DARE to Care Activist Interview Feature Videos with accompanying lesson plans;
Ten (10) Modern Challenges Animated Videos with accompanying lesson plans;
European Values timeline cards set with accompanying lesson plan;
Radicalisation Awareness Training materials;
Healthy Conflict & Constructive Dialogue Classroom - Educators' Guide to Depolarisation
c) In-person and online multiplier events were held in each partner country, engaging over 300 teachers and educators in the dissemination process. 
d) The project has successfully established a website that consolidates all the educational materials developed throughout its duration. This digital platform serves as a comprehensive repository, facilitating seamless access and dissemination of the project's outcomes.


<< Results >>

The outputs and results of DARE project are the following:
1) The “Healthy Conflict & Constructive Dialogue Classroom - Educators' Guide to Depolarisation” was created. The purpose of this manual is to build educators’ and youth workers' skills in the domain of addressing and successfully engaging with polarizing topics. The Guide consist of a theoretical section, explaining the phenomenon of polarisation from a sociological and psychological perspective, as well as activities and exercises that build skills in depolarization of communication, empathy and a willingness to engage with people who hold diverse perspectives. 
2) Each partner organization created two (2) “DARE to care” feature interview videos, each highlighting a different young activist that provides a positive relatable example of civic engagement. The videos are applicable in classrooms throughout Europe due to the universal nature of the topics they cover. The following videos are created: 
Animal welfare - created by HERMES
Historical human rights education -  created by HERMES
Cyberbullying -  created by Kreisau Initiative e. V.
International Youth Exchanges -  created by Kreisau Initiative e. V.
Entrepreneurship & Self-employment - created by Mreža Zapadnog Balkana
Civic engagement -  created by Mreža Zapadnog Balkana
Debate education -  created by Otvorena Komunikacija
LGBTQIA+ rights -  created by Otvorena Komunikacija
Interreligious dialogue -  created by Transform
Social cohesion -  created by Transform
3) Each project partner created scripts for 2 key-themed short animated educational videos, together with accompanying lesson plans. The animated videos frame concrete modern challenges in our society. Each partner organization concentrated on topics that they had experience with while also taking into account the nuances of their own country context. Nevertheless, all the addressed topics remain applicable to the other countries represented by the partner organizations due to their universal nature. The following animated videos were created:
- Polarisation - created by HERMES 
- Nationalism -  created by HERMES
- Where are you from? -  created by  Kreisau Initiative e. V.
- Nationalism -  created by Kreisau Initiative e. V.
- Peace building & Active Citizenship (Chocolate riots) -  created by Mreža Zapadnog Balkana
- Emigration -  created by Mreža Zapadnog Balkana
- Pollution -  created by Otvorena Komunikacija
- Mental health -  created by Otvorena Komunikacija
- Radicalisation -  created by Transform
- Violent extremism -  created by Transform
4) The European Values Card Set consists of a mix of European Union history, events, notable individuals, culture, institutions and events, accompanied by contemporary dilemmas and questions about the role and importance of European values in our societies. They provide an interactive teaching tool for educators that allows them to introduce the very important but often neglected topic of European Values. 
5) The Radicalisation Awareness training is a training program for teachers, youth workers and educators on the topic of radicalisation. The training program is based on knowledge sharing with the aim of providing educators with information that helps them understand the process of radicalisation (both online and offline), identify groups at risk, recognise the signs of radicalisation, and learn about inspiring practices for prevention and intervention. 
6) Project website: https://depolarisation.eu
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000028821.title: Youth Moving
2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000028821.summary:
<< Background >>

YOUTH MOVING aimed to enhance care leavers participation in democratic life in Europe, through their empowerment as active citizens, especially addressing how to connect with, express their views and be heard by stakeholders in the alternative care field. For children and young people who have experienced living in alternative care, separated from their biological family, the process of growing up is extremely demanding because they are often left without formal support and a functional social network. 
The aim and activities of this project were focused on strengthening the competencies of people working with youth from alternative care, to encourage youth to actively participate in society, to overcome limitations and to provide opportunities for young people to express their opinion. All of the above empowered young people from alternative care and we advocated for the improvement of the entire alternative care system, because the voice of those who know their reality and problems the best are now heard by people who work with them and by policy-makers.

<< Objectives >>

1. Investigate the involvement of young people from alternative care in democratic processes in society.
2. Raise awareness about the need of inclusion of young people from alternative care in democratic processes in society.
3. Promote international cooperation of people working with youth from alternative care.
4. Promote cross-sectoral cooperation of organizations and institutions working with youth from alternative care in representing the views of youth in the society

<< Implementation >>

Through the project we produced 2 project results and activities related to them:

PR1) Developed curriculum of workshops to encourage young people to actively participate in society
1. Conducted research on the involvement of youth from alternative care in democratic processes through desk research and interviews
2. Investigated good EU practice examples for active involvment of youth from alternative care in democratic processes in the community
3. Developed training materials for youth workers, based on research conducted with the aim of encouraging and teaching young people to get involved in democratic processes in the community *** after development of the material, an LTT activity was organized - training in which youth workers and young people from alternative care participated, and where developed materials were implemented
4. Translation to all partner languages
5. Pilot training materials on one group of young people in each partner country
6. Dissemination

PR2) Developed video material for raising public awareness 
1. Preparation of the video production: finding suitable stories, creating scenario
2. Filming of the video materials
3. Editing the video materials
4. Translation to all partner languages
5. Dissemination

<< Results >>

Youth Moving project produced 2 project results:

PR1) Curriculum of workshops aimed at encouraging the participation of young people from alternative care in the democratic processes of society
PR2)Video material for raising public awareness and policy makers awareness about the importance of participation of young people from alternative care in democratic processes

Project benefited more than 300 people through:
1. Empowering organizations involved in the project to actively advocate that views of young people from alternative care in designing the services they need and receive are taken into account
2. Enabling partner and associated organizations to share knowledge, insight into good practices and design the most appropriate forms of work with young people from alternative care for their more active role in society and reduction of social isolation
3. Expansion of knowledge and competencies of people working with youth from alternative care in the field of active involvement of these young people in democratic processes in society

2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000028981.title: LETsTALK: developing gender sensitive mental health program for young people
2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000028981.summary:
<< Background >>

COVID-19 pandemic further aggravated and accelerated the further deterioration of already impaired mental health of young people globally (local centers, schools, universities closed, mental health services interrupted, family distress and increased fear). This all pointed the need to support all those working with young people to gain better
knowledge on mental health of young people, particularly to provide support to recognize when to provide support and call on for the expert support. The consortium of this project decided to search for the support of the youth work which can be a safety net for all young people in times of uncertainty. MH promotion can be a crucial point in youth work. Youth workers should be empowered in promoting and maintaining the MH of young people, particularly those facing intersectional and other vulnerabilities. Young people of different genders, according to research and practice, have different mental health difficulties and gender socialization influence how they deal with difficulties and accordingly seek and receive support. This and other gender connected aspects of MH should be examined and taken into account when tailoring and providing MH services to young people.

<< Objectives >>

The overall objective of the project is to strengthen the capacity of youth workers in supporting young peoples’ mental health with focus on gender sensitive approach to MH issues. Specifically: 1) Providing Policy analyses and recommendations related to young people’s
mental health on EU and national level, with focus on the gender perspective; 2) Strengthening capacities of partner organizations and youth workers to support young people's mental health; 3) Developing the gender sensitive tools for understanding and supporting one's own mental health for young people, and 4) Disseminating the developed knowledge and resources in 4 partner countries and on EU level. With implementation of this project, the partner
organizations will be able to offer training for youth experts in improving young people’s mental health and available resources via the developed digital platform that is visibly promoted on their websites and social media and their local, regional and national networks of stakeholders in the youth sector. 

<< Implementation >>

The consortium consisted of 4 CSO with complementary expertise in youth work and adolescent mental health, from Croatia (FFE), Greece (KMOP), Italy (CSC Danilo Dolci) and Serbia (CZOR) implemented a wide spectrum of activities. Besides 4 transnational partner meetings and one joint learning event, numerous meetings, collaborations and work sessions took place in order for the project results to be developed. The consortium conducted in each country national activities that lead to the creation of Policy Analyses and Recommendations related to young people’s mental health on EU and national level, with focus on the gender perspective. These activities involved policy analyses, interviews, mapping the best practices and discovering the gaps, creating country specifics and comparative findings. In order to create Gender sensitive Youth Mental Health Program and Toolkit Resources the consortium exchanged the knowledge and developed Program Curriculum for youth workers in the area of Youth mental health, Handbook for youth workers and Workbook for young people. The transnational learning event gathered 30 participants from the consortium organizations and young people which aimed at deepening the understanding of the gender and MH as well as exchanging knowledge and best practices. In order to create a Digital Platform supporting young people's mental health, with all the resources and materials available in 5 languages, each partner accordingly participated in creating the national language content. With the aim of sharing and dissemination of project results, multiplier events were organized in each partner country including more then 120 participants. Extensive online promotion and sharing of results was carried out. Each partner used their
promotion channels, dissemination practices, resources and policy influence to maximize the reach of the project results
and achievement in their national contexts.


<< Results >>

The project produced numerous insights, practice and scientific inputs, best practices, training curriculum and related publications as well as a digital platform with publicly available project results (PR). The PR1 is a POLICY ANALYSIS AND RECOMMENDATION ON YOUTH´ S MENTAL HEALTH GENDER SENSITIVE NEEDS, a document based on the policy analyses and field research in 4 partner countries, aimed at the decision and policy makers, but also the managers and experts in the field of youth mental health and youth work. It informs the key persons and youth experts on the importance of gender sensitive approach to youth mental health, explain the difference we see in young people of different genders facing mental health issues and help them tailor and implement efficient policies and strategies to address the issues and provide the needed support systems. This also serves as a starting, evidence based point to achieve mutual understanding among EU members participating in the project (and more widely), to show which actions are necessary in the field of supporting young people's mental health and that dedication is needed to this topic. Also, it contains valuable information on the importance of a gender sensitive approach to mental health, because the needs and issues differ, and often the mental health messages and approaches are ignoring that fact. The PR2 is a GENDER SENSITIVE YOUTH MENTAL HEALTH PROGRAM AND TOOLKIT RESOURCES, a program curriculum and related publications for youth workers and young people. The program consists of: (a)Training curriculum with the description of the program, list of learning outcomes, list of references, duration and type of the certificate; (b) Handbook for youth workers consisted of: (1) The importance of gender
perspective on mental health of young people from developmental perspective; (2) Recommendations of mental health
experts on what youth workers can do to provide better gender-sensitive support to young people; and (3) Gendersensitive
pedagogical tools and interventions in supporting young people’s mental health. The (c) Workbook for young people consists of different self-reflective, informative and interactive handouts for young people to work through so they are appreciative of the importance of mental health and more caring for themselves and their peers. Through the developed Gender sensitive youth mental health program with toolkit resources all youth workers, youth experts and youth in the EU will have the most relevant and up to date program that corresponds to the detected needs of all involved target groups. As it is disseminated through the PR3 - website and platform, it reaches not only youth workers and experts but also young people and gives them resources to better understand their state, and also to have all necessary information on how to improve their mental health. The PR3, a DIGITAL PLATFORM YOUTH MENTAL HEALTH is the innovative interactive Digital platform that aims to tackle gender-sensitive mental health issues while applying an inclusive approach to all young people. The website platform contains the RESEARCH AND POLICY SECTION (a compilation of up-to-date reports on the impact of COVID-19 on mental health of young people together with the identified good practices on policy and service level, and gender issues); TRAINING COURSES SECTION (with the program tested at national levels and designed during the testing phase with the collaboration of all youth workers and hub youth group (PR2); RESOURCES AND MATERIALS SECTION (with the digital materials, pedagogical resources, tools and instruments that partners and

2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029040.title: Web-Lab
2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029040.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project because, through surveys conducted on a sample of 50 young people, we noticed their dissatisfaction, especially those with fewer opportunities who face challenges when choosing a job or continuing education after the interruption or completion of secondary education. We also noticed that the resources that should help them in their personal and professional orientation are mostly based on one or the other area. In this sense, the goal of our project was to promote mobility, cooperation, quality, inclusiveness, fairness, excellence and creativity among young people, as well as active participation in society, removing the obstacles they face. Researching the available resources, we saw that there is a need for a web platform that will be easy to navigate and will be based on content that is really important and useful for young people to acquire basic skills and get an insight into what awaits them in the workplace. We achieved this by conducting focus groups and workshops in partner countries in order to individualize the needs identified in advance and finally confirm them on a representative sample of young people. The young people involved had numerous proposals and suggestions for the content.

<< Objectives >>

Our main goal was to define the key needs of young people with fewer opportunities in order to facilitate their access to the labor market and increase competitiveness. By conducting activities with young people, we tried to empower them and point out their existing qualities, and then involve them in the process of designing and evaluating topics and content for the web platform that are permanently available to them in all partner languages. We also encouraged young people to exchange contacts and thus create support networks at the national and international level that will serve to encourage each other and share opportunities for participation and potential employment. Among ourselves, we tried to mobilize additional help that young people will be able to seek at any time, which, along with interactive content on the platform, will provide them with motivation for further educational and business development. We decided to create the contents in such a way as to enable young people to discover the desired business orientation or at least eliminate occupations they do not want to deal with. Our goals were to motivate and encourage young people to become more actively involved in society and successfully enter the labor market.

<< Implementation >>

The activities we implemented during the project are:
1. Two to three focus groups and one to two workshops (changes occurred as a result of the epidemiological situation and assessment for better implementation of activities, which is why instead of two activities with fewer participants, one activity with more participants was conducted)
2. The Web-Lab web platform was created as the main product of the second project result
3. Interactive content, webinars, quizzes, crossword puzzles, pop-up windows and videos of entertaining and educational content were created, as the main product of the third project result.

<< Results >>

During the implementation of the project, we achieved the following results:
- focus groups (60 young people) and workshops (81 young people) were organized for young people with fewer opportunities in order to determine and define the contents that were placed on the Web-Lab platform;
- a scientific article was published based on the results from PR1, which explains the methodology and approach in working with young people;
- 25 people who work with young people participated in the LTT activity on digital competences and work with young people with fewer opportunities;
- a free, educational and entertaining web platform was created that offers content in all partner languages;
- 12 webinars were created (2 per partner);
- contents were created for the web platform that enable young people to discover skills and qualities, facilitate educational and business orientation and the acquisition and development of additional skills and competencies.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029086.title: Partnerstvo za izradu digitalnog sadržaja za mlade i osobe koje rade s mladima
2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029086.summary:
<< Background >>

In their regular work, student dormitories have recognized the need of young people for additional facilities that will enable them to arrive more easily and adapt to a new environment and to have a better quality stay in a new environment. Homes, as institutions that take care of young people all day long, organize numerous workshops for young people and monitor the development and improvement of the skills and competencies of their users. Through numerous contents and workshops conducted by student dormitories and thus supplementing the formal education of dormitory users, the need for digitalization of the entire process of monitoring and education of persons working with young people and the young people themselves was seen. By introducing digitization into the regular work of student homes, everyday work with young people has been improved, and the employees of the homes, people who work with young people, have been given the opportunity to adopt and improve their own work with young people and to get closer to young people in a digital environment. It has been proven that young people better accept cooperation in a digital environment, absorb information faster and communicate with each other more easily.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project, we wanted to create an application that will enable young people to transfer the necessary knowledge and information to each other in a format that is very close to young people, a digital format. By creating a framework in which young people can guide other young people and give them useful information, a less stressful and faster assimilation of young people into the new community in the student dormitory and the new environment is enabled.
In the second part of the application, it is possible to monitor the work of young people and their development of skills and competences. Given that these are young people at an extremely sensitive age, when they are subject to various influences from the media, society, and friends, it is important to provide them with quality activities outside of school and monitor their progress and interest. Digitization of work monitoring has enabled people who work with young people to devote more time to direct work with young people and a greater possibility of individual access to young people. 

<< Implementation >>

The main goal of this project was the creation of digital content (application) with two modules. The first module is intended for young people in order to facilitate everyday life outside the place of residence, while the second module is intended for people who work with young people, and contains all information related to special and optional programs. The second module has the greatest effect on the overview of all activities in one place, reducing the time required for administration, which ultimately results in more time for quality frontal work with young people. Workshops were organized with young people in which young people played an active role in order to produce high-quality modules. Content testing is carried out after creating digital content in order to determine whether the created digital form corresponds to the real needs of young people and people who work with young people. At the end of the project, presentations were held for institutions that care about young people, volunteer organizations, associations.

<< Results >>

The main result is the creation of digital content for young people and people who work with young people. In the first part, it provides information for young people in a generally accepted and modern way, which implies a digital form, quick and easy access to information. The content of the information itself will influence the easier adaptation of young people in a new environment, reduce stress and many unknowns during everyday life outside the place of residence. In the second part, the content is intended for people who work with young people in order to speed up the process of monitoring the development of young people and thus have more time and opportunities to devote themselves directly to working with young people. The created application is available at the link: https://klikmeapp.com.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029124.title: NFE Box Set
2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029124.summary:
<< Background >>

With this project, we aimed to strengthen the capacities of our parent organizations, associated partners, youth workers, teachers and young people who participate in the work we do and the values/competences we promote. 
The created project results, an online and an offline version, is an answer to the need assessed as a result of interviews with youth workers, organizations, trainers and facilitators. 
An analyse of this field survey made clear that in the field of youth work there is an very large number of different tools, methods and exercises but they are largely focused on one priority, competence or problem. Many educators do therefore focus mainly on 1 or few competences and youth priorities. 
An answer to this was the creation of 1 toolbox which covers minimum 5 different youth field priorities. This under the format of an educational board game, both offline and online possible.  With the use of Design Thinking approach,  gamification techniques and regular testing during the process, such a toolbox is now created. The toolbox follows the principles of non formal education and simplifies the process of acquiring new competencies, and additionally increases the creativity of the learners.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the NFE Box Set project, we aimed to strengthen organizations, individuals and young people and consequently increase the quality of work with young people. Through the principle of universality, which is the main aspect of the NFE Box Set project, diminishing the problem of complexity in the realization of games / exercises. Due to its easy application and adaptation, facilitating greatly working with young people and other target groups on the defined youth priorities. Hereby strengthening the capacity of organizations in the non-formal and formal education sector, as well as increase the capacity of young people.
Creating a large impact at the local level, primarily due to the networked way of working of the partners and associated partners whom supports in the implementation of the project. Furthermore, once the partners are involved in many Erasmus+ projects, and many international trainings, an additional impact at the European level is also expected. 
This project also aimed at reinforcing the sustainability of each one and of the youth field in general, once from the very start, there was a full adaptability (e.g. offline and online combination) foreseen towards different possible future reality scenarios.

<< Implementation >>

During the project we maintained ongoing communication throughout our organized online communication channels (e.g. Messenger, Whatsapp, email), but also during the 4 TPMs and other activities in Europe that we participated in and cooperated with each other. During the TPMs we double checked our time and budget control of the project, and we created the design of the boardgame and APP, visibility brochures (hard copy and in digital form). Additionally, we created the Video tutorial on how to use the boardgame/app.
We realized 2 in depth evaluations for the boardgame and one for APP, evaluation of the every TPM, and the final evaluation of the project.
All results we disseminated throughout our social media (e.g. Facebook profiles, Instagram profile) 
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1F3ThD4ezvWeeza1MYqgLFcPOvdC_DW31xB3CDNF-kGA/edit?usp=sharing
We took a close look to the all evaluation reports and we included the suggestions during the development of the outputs, according to our Design Thinking methodology applied. We had foreseen to organize 5 Multiplier Events and at the end we realized 8 MEs.

<< Results >>

Concrete results of our project are;
1.	NFE BOX SET Boardgame (2 approaches to participate at the exercise, and 6 covered topics with debriefing) https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1yOzK6jk3YQCAbqF03DP_SwhDLIDTIHdO
2.	NFE BOX APP www.nfe-box.com
3.	Nfe BOX SET web site included in the APP platform www.nfe-box.com
4.	NFE BOX Manual (in 5 languages) https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1WzCOCLjQ_pVzDQBK6Ad0PqNozCQcFI3L
5.	Video tutorial https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7iFwThoKbyk&feature=youtu.be
6.	Logo and design for NFE BOXSsetlogo project – Google disk
7.	 Evaluation during the test phase and final evaluationevaluation – Google disk
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
