2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029200.title: How to score a Youth Goal?
2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029200.summary:
<< Background >>

The overall aim of this project was to foster youth engagement and youth participation by mapping the implementation of European Youth Goals in European and national policy contexts, identifying participation methods and creating training curricula for practitioners and policy makers to transfer this knowledge into practice, knowing that this link between research, policy and practice will contribute to the successful implementation of the European Youth Strategy (2019-2027). By choosing the European Youth Goals (EYGs) as the overarching framework of the project we are responding to the wants and needs of almost 50.000 young people who actively contributed to their creation. The partner consortium of this project includes 4 national youth councils that have had the role of coordinator of the European Youth Dialogue process in their countries, and what each partner noticed within its national and European context is that the weakest point of the EUYD process is its implementation. As EYGs are one of the outcomes of the EUYD process, we wanted to accelerate their implementation through our project objectives.  As National youth councils we all gathered member organisations that are active on local and or regional level. 

<< Objectives >>

First objective of our project was to provide National working groups members and other stakeholders as well as decision makers, on all levels from local to European with existing knowledge on implementation of the Youth Goals. First objective was focused on the “what” while the second was looking to answer the question “how”. Our second objective was to support and encourage meaningful youth participation by providing participation tools gathered in one place. By developing 4 training curriculas, our third objective was to create all the necessary preparation work for any youth organisation or institution to transfer the knowledge of both implementation and youth participation in regard to the Youth Goals. Therefore, the overall aim of KA2 „How to score a Youth goal“ project was to foster youth engagement and youth participation by mapping the implementation of European Youth Goals in European and national policy contexts, identifying participation methods and creating training curricula for practitioners and policy makers to transfer this knowledge into practice.

<< Implementation >>

To accomplish the first objective, we mapped and research examples and policy practices from different EU countries as well as research EU policy level on EYGs implementation, after which we jointly created recommendations to improve EYGs implementation at national and European level. Partner Ondrej Barta conducted preparation work and analyzed data provided by research and information from each partner in the consortium for the production of project result 2/IO2. All of these different examples and practices were needed to ensure a large variety of successful practices out of which ten would be translated into case studies. All findings were summarized in one cookbook that was reflected and commented on by all partners. IO3, the training curricula was also tested  in practice thus making it useful for youth organizations, young people and decision makers. First step to that goal was for all partners to discuss what kind of training curricula they’d find useful and based on that input as well as results from IO1 and IO2, Dypall produced that curricula. Besides discussing it inside a partnership consortium it was tested via LTT activities on different target groups to see how useful/successful it is and where there are opportunities for improvement.

<< Results >>

We achieved our first objective of EYG implementation by gathering in one publication good practice examples and creating recommendations and conclusions. Our second objective was achieved through the creation of a “Cookbook of youth political participation” which was developed based on a combination of theoretical research background and 10 case studies of successful youth participation. After that, we combined the first two outputs and made them easier to share and transfer knowledge on how to use them through designing and testing training curriculums for different target groups.
To ensure that we created something useful, we tested that method on different stakeholders and actors in the field of youth policy like representatives of national youth councils, youth organisations (both national and international) as well as decision makers and individual young people after which we incorporated the results of the evaluation obtained through testing into the training curricula and further dissemination. 
Concrete project outputs were: 
One publication - good practice examples of EYG implementation, with recommendations and conclusions.
„Cookbook of youth political participation” - combination of theoretical research background and 10 case studies of successful youth participation.
Training curricula for 4 target groups (national youth councils, youth organisations (both national and international) as well as decision makers and individual young people – testing through LTT activities.
topics: Reaching the policy level/dialogue with decision makers
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029208.title: Using Social Entrepreneurship as a Leverage for Unemployed Youth in the Post-Covid 19 Era
2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029208.summary:
<< Background >>

The Covid 19 pandemic directly influenced the increase of unemployment rates for young adults not in employment, education or training (NEET), with women and other vulnerable groups being the most affected. This is particularly true for countries such as: Hungary, Romania, Italy, Slovenia, Czech Republic and Croatia where prior to the pandemics, 1 in 4 young individuals aged 15-29 belonged to the NEET category. To combat these rates, the European Council emphasized the urgent need for education and training along with awareness raising in a period of digital and green transition. In response, the partners in the project used their expertise in education,  entrepreneurship and mental health to launch blended educational programs for NEETs (20-30), with priority given to women and other vulnerable groups.
The beneficiaries of the program had an opportunity to develop social and practical competences as well as proactive mindset. Moreover, they got access to international networks and resources through platform. The new program intended to make them ready to found/join social businesses and become proactive change-makers who will inspire and mobilize their peers.

<< Objectives >>

The main purpose of this project was to stimulate engagement and entrepreneurship, increase employability of NEETs (20- 30) and provide equal access to education to all. The individuals enrolled in the new educational program developed social and practical skills and competences as well as a proactive mindset, while simultaneously getting access to international networks and resources. The new program intended to them ready to found/join social businesses and become proactive change-makers who will inspire and mobilise their peers. As program alumni, they will further contribute in combating unemployment and embracing sustainability, leading to faster accomplishment of SDGs 8, 3 and 4.

<< Implementation >>

The project activities were aimed to creating the major output of the project, a customised blended educational program that tackled the skill and competence gaps on a per country basis. The program involved 57 participants, both in the pilot and the official launch of the program, directly increasing participation in education and training. 39 out of registered participants completed the educational programme. Along with the blended educational program, a transnational online learning and networking platform was be established to connect participants with peers and key stakeholders on an international basis, encouraging exchange of experiences and best practices.
The project also had four transnational meetings as well as three multiplier events.

<< Results >>

The end result is a newly created program through which the knowledge and practices of the SIA and YHO are shared on transnational basis, changing the lives of  57 individuals located in the partner countries. In addition, an international online learning and networking platform was established to connect the beneficiaries with their peers as well as with key stakeholders on an international basis, encouraging exchange of experiences and best practices. The program and the cooperation between the partners will continue beyond the duration of the projects on this and other projects. Beneficiary partners will tray run the program on country specific basis with continuous advice from the lead partner in the upcoming years.

2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029253.title: Joyful Entrepreneurship
2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029253.summary:
<< Background >>

The project successfully increased the capacities of organizations in working with youth on social entrepreneurship by developing a comprehensive Impact Entrepreneurship methodology. It addressed two key areas: combating youth unemployment and enhancing the quality of youth work in entrepreneurial education. 
To implement effective NFE programs, partners enhanced their capabilities in social entrepreneurship (SE) education, guided by an innovative methodology. The Impact Entrepreneurship Methodology, encompassing online tools, manuals, and training methodology, empowers youth workers and organizations. This comprehensive approach provides easy access to new knowledge and methods, practical tools for both online and offline use, and improves the quality of entrepreneurial education.
The project's impact extended to meet the partnership's needs: increasing capacity for online and offline youth engagement at various levels, educating youth workers in new methodologies, and promoting SE as a solution to financial crises and youth unemployment. It also addressed the needs of young people, who sought business skills and opportunities to create their own jobs, often as the only viable employment option.

<< Objectives >>

The project boosted the capacities of partner organizations in social entrepreneurship education for youth, both online and offline. The key goal was to develop the Impact Entrepreneurship Methodology, which includes online tools for young entrepreneurs, instructional manuals for youth workers, and training activities for effective methodology implementation.

Objectives:
1. Enhancing digital competencies of partner organizations through the design, upload, and management of online tools.
2. Developing skills of youth workers in Non-Formal Education (NFE) for both online and offline settings, including the creation of NFE activities and manuals detailing the methodology.
3. Creating a new, accessible methodology for Social Entrepreneurship (SE) education, involving partners from education, youth, and business sectors, basing it on scientific research, incorporating NFE methods, and making it applicable across various environments and levels.
4. Developing entrepreneurship competence in young people by creating an educational program to assist and support them in developing their SE ideas.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes several key activities to achieve its objectives:
- Four transnational project meetings to outline deadlines, set milestones, assign roles and responsibilities, strategize dissemination, and evaluate progress.
- Regular project management activities, conducted monthly or quarterly through online video conferencing, focusing on managing the partnership, developing organizational capacities, and advancing project outcomes.
- The development of four distinct project results, with each partner leading one based on their expertise.
- Dissemination activities that partners conducted throughout the project to spread awareness of the project and its results.
- LTTA activity for youth workers from partner countries aimed at supporting the project's objectives, implementing the methodology effectively, and enhancing youth work capacities.
- Monitoring and evaluation activities, including partnership evaluation, mid-term and final assessments of project results, and participant feedback.
- Six multiplier events hosted by each partner in their respective communities, involving local, national, and international youth workers, policymakers, and stakeholders to broaden the project's impact.

<< Results >>

The project delivers four key results designed to support young people and youth workers in developing entrepreneurial skills:
1) Shape It Up!: This interactive tool guides young people through forming their entrepreneurial ideas with questions covering market analysis, financial projections, target groups, competition analysis, etc. It's designed to suit an audience without previous knowledge about entrepreneurship.
2) Entrepreneurial Self-Awareness Inventory: An online questionnaire composed of a series of professional online psychological tests to support young people in assessing their personality traits, abilities, and inclinations towards entrepreneurship. Completing this Inventory provides insights into their strengths and areas for development in entrepreneurial competence.
3) Impact Entrepreneurship Online Course: This course offers video lessons that provide the theoretical knowledge and practical examples needed to develop a social entrepreneurship idea. It covers topics outlined in the Shape it Up! Tool, offering context and explanations, but can also be used independently for those interested in just the theory or examples of shaping a social entrepreneurship (SE) idea.
4) NFE Methodology: This includes Non-Formal Education (NFE) methods and materials for youth workers to conduct workshops, supporting young people to transform business ideas into social entrepreneurial initiatives. The methodology is adaptable for workshops at local, national, and international levels, detailed in a PDF manual.
All these results are accompanied by digital manuals for youth workers, providing instructions on their application in youth work.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Quality and innovation of youth work

2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029385.title: LGBTIQ Youth affirmative mental health approaches
2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000029385.summary:
<< Background >>

Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and other self-identified queer (LGBTIQ) youth have higher rates of mental health issues than people in the general population. This could be due to neglect, lack of support, discrimination, trauma, abuse, etc that could potentially lead to poor mental health, suicide, substance abuse, anti-social behaviour, at risk sexual encounters, depression, stress, anxiety etc. 
To tackle some of these issues and to create a support network, community of practices and peer support networks we wanted to explore body-oriented approaches in working with LGBTIQ youth mental health that could potentially lead to regaining strength, power, self-esteem and self-acceptance within this cohort. 
„LGBTIQ Youth affirmative mental health approaches” is a project which strengthens capacities of partner organisations in the field, creates a network of Eu community of practices, upskills youth workers and mental health professionals from the field and exchanges good practices through the development of innovative project results based on the concept of Body oriented mental health as a tool for working with LGBTIQ youth mental health in Europe.

<< Objectives >>

Main objective of the project was to increase the quality of mental health in the young LGBTIQ population in the EU. 
Specific objective 1: To develop innovative model of affirmative mental health approach to LGBTIQ youth population based on the partners experiences in affirmative mental health approaches in working with LGBTIQ youth such as: sports, embodiment, dance, trauma sensitive yoga, movement, theatre and culture. 
Specific objective 2: To strengthen the capacities of the organisations in the LGBTIQ mental health field.


<< Implementation >>

To ensure we are reaching our objectives we implemented following activities: 
- Transnational project meetings (3 online and 4 in person),
- Study visits and testing of the project results,
- Production of 3 Intellectual outputs:
* Guidebook for community of practices (including research in the field),
* Educational videos on different LGBTIQ youth mental health approaches and
* LTTA Training Outlines to train the trainers who work with LGBTIQ youth. 
- Multiplier events

Study visits and testing of the project results activities took part in partner countries with aim of applying and testing the new competencies gained through the research and development of the different mental health approaches while spreading new knowledge and skills among other youth workers and mental health practitioners on European levels but also strengthening capacities of the organisations included in this project. 
Production of 3 intellectual outputs aimed at sustainability of the project while ensuring youth workers, young people, diversified mental health professionals from the field and also educators in Europe could benefit from it and implement those approaches in their support work with LGBTIQ youth. 


<< Results >>

This project produced 3 key outputs. 
1. Guidebook “Queer Youth Work: Resource on LGBTIQ Youth Affirmative Mental Health Approaches” was developed specifically for the youth workers and mental health practitioners working with LGBTIQ youth. This Guidebook equips them with skills on how to tackle their bias and make their approaches more affirmative, inclusive and introduce them to more diverse approaches. The focus is placed on skills development of the youth workers and mental health practitioners working with LGBTIQ youth in understanding, empowerment and discovering personal resources. 
2. LGBTIQ youth affirmative mental health educational videos are short but powerful series of visual materials available for free usage of all interested in this field. Each video breaks down specific topic for the youth workers, mental health professionals, educators, but also parents and youngsters themselves. 
3. LTTA Training Outlines provide very practical in detail examples of implementation of different techniques for working with LGBTIQ youth aimed for youth workers and mental health practitioners.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000030341.title: Spikey's Clinic for Professional Dreamers
2021-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000030341.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the rising issue of burnout among youth workers, especially exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. Our goal is to support "professional dreamers" like youth workers and community facilitators by providing them with tools and resources to manage their mental and emotional well-being. We aim to prevent burnout and enhance their capacity to continue fostering community cohesion and resilience effectively.
Our project addresses several critical needs of youth workers, especially exacerbated by the pandemic. First, we are highlighting and addressing the increased mental health challenges faced by youth workers due to the pandemic, focusing on their mental and emotional well-being. Second, we aim to advocate for greater social and institutional recognition and validation of the roles and contributions of youth workers, recognizing their importance and impact. Third, we are developing tools and strategies for peer support and supervision to effectively prevent burnout. Finally, we believe in integrating playful and educational methods to relieve stress and promote a positive work environment, ensuring that youth workers can sustain their vital contributions to the community.


<< Objectives >>

Through this project, we aimed to raise awareness about the mental and emotional wellbeing challenges faced by youth workers and prevent burnout by enhancing peer support and supervision. We sought to improve the quality and innovation in youth work by developing tools that promote mindfulness and reduce stress. Additionally, we aimed to foster international collaboration and exchange good practices among partners. Ultimately, we wanted to empower youth workers by celebrating their role, promoting positive self-commitment, and enhancing their contributions to the community despite the pandemic’s challenges.


<< Implementation >>

We implemented the following activities in our project:
1)PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION ACTIVITIES
- detailed project planning, online meetings, formation of work teams, communication, documentation of activities, monitoring, financial arrangements, dissemination, evaluation, reporting

2) TRANSNATIONAL PROJECT MEETINGS: Four meetings were held, each corresponding to different phases of the Dragon Dreaming methodology.
TPM1 - kick-off meeting Rijeka  (Croatia) 03-2022
TPM2 - Greece 09-2022
TPM3 - Italy 11-2023
TPM4 - Rijeka (Croatia) 05-2024 

3) LTTA: Conducted two LTTA sessions, known as "Spikey's Clinics," to develop and test methodologies and tools (Zlatna Greda (CRO) and Rabhka Zdroj (PL).

4) INTELLECTUAL OUTPUTS AND ACTIVITIES
IO1 - Methodology - based on the best practices from the partner organisations in well-being, peer coaching and stress management
IO2 - Spikey´s Deck of Remedies - printed and online version of cards (designing the excercises, testing, evaluating, graphic design, distributing)
IO3 - "Professional Dreamers" educational video documentary series - 25 interviews with youth workers, in which they shared their firsthand experiences dealing with workplace stress and adopting nurturing practices
 
5) Multiplier Events: Organized five events to disseminate project results and share innovative practices (2xCroatia, Greece, Italy, Poland)

Phase-Based Activities:
Dreaming: Shared experiences and developed the “Spikey's Clinic for Professional Dreamers” methodology, focusing on mental well-being and burnout awareness.
Planning: Refined the methodology and designed the “Spikey's Deck of Remedies” deck of cards, enhancing youth work tools (web and printed version).
Doing: Implemented and analyzed the “Spikey's Clinic” methodology and produced the “Professional Dreamers” video documentary series.
Celebrating: Finalized project results, conducted a closing conference, evaluated the project, and planned for ongoing collaboration.


<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results of our project include three key deliverables and several broader impacts. First, we developed the “Spikey's Clinic for Professional Dreamers” methodology, a comprehensive approach for training youth workers in peer coaching and stress management. This methodology includes practical guidance, peer coaching scenarios, and a collection of stress management tools, all facilitated by Spikey the crochet dragon, who serves as an engaging mascot traveling across Europe to help youth workers share their challenges.
Second, we created the “Spikey's Deck of Remedies” card deck, a self-care tool designed specifically for youth workers. This deck provides mindfulness-inducing and stress-relieving activities, beautifully illustrated and based on the Spikey's Clinic methodology, to help youth workers manage stress effectively. “Spikey's Deck of Remedies” is available in printed form and in digital on our web: spikeysclinic.eu. 
Third, we produced the “Professional Dreamers” educational video documentary where we conducted 25 interviews with youth workers, in which they shared their firsthand experiences dealing with workplace stress and adopting nurturing practices. Videos are available on our YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/@SpikeysClinic 

Other significant results of the project include enhanced organizational capacity, with improved peer support and stress management competencies among participating organizations. The project also fostered cross-sectoral cooperation, strengthening our network and ability to collaborate with other organizations in youth work and education, especially on an international level. This cooperation is underpinned by a Memorandum of Understanding (attached in Annexes section), ensuring sustainability and future collaboration.
Additionally, the project raised awareness of self-care, resilience, and adaptability among youth workers, along with skills in stress management, space and time management, and human resources management. It also fostered positive attitudes such as openness, empathy, gratitude, appreciation, and honesty within the youth workers' community.
Finally, the project’s results were widely disseminated through digital channels and multiplier events, ensuring that its impact reached a broad audience and laid the groundwork for ongoing efforts to nurture self-care and prevent burnout among youth workers.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000028810.title: SPACE4US – A model of blended-experiential learning for the empowerment of young women
2021-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000028810.summary:
<< Background >>

Nei suoi 2 anni di implementazione, SPACE4US si è posto il principale obiettivo di offrire un panel di strumenti di elevata qualità e dall'alto potenziale di trasferibilità/riuso per l'empowerment e la formazione inclusiva di ragazze adolescenti in condizioni di svantaggio ed a rischio di marginalizzazione sociale. Il progetto si è posto il principale obiettivo di lavorare con due tipologie di target principali: 1) gruppi target di ragazze adolescenti ed educatori. Ad ispirare il progetto è stata l'identificazione nei vari paesi della partnership (n.7, per 9 partner) di problematiche variegate e crescenti per ragazze vulnerabili, determinati da fattori culturali, di background socio-economico delle famiglie, di fenomeni di stigmatizzazione sociale che ne inficiavano la piena inclusione, cittadinanza attiva e successo nei diversi contesti relazionali ed educativi.

<< Objectives >>

SPACE4US ha inteso sviluppare e testare un modello innovativo e integrato per l'empowerment individuale e collettivo di giovani donne, basato su attività di apprendimento esperienziale, per favorirre l'inclusione sociale di ragazze  a rischio di emarginazione. Le attività implementate erano dirette  al target prioritario ed agli educatori, allo scopo di formarli per  renderli in grado di utilizzare  metodologie creative per progettare e realizzare tali attività, coinvolgendo i destinatari in condizioni di vulnerabilità.
Un  obiettivo chiave di SPACE4US è stato quello di fornire un quadro il più possibile aggiornato dei diversi contesti che generano disuguaglianza e emarginazione delle ragazze:, come la provenienza da famiglie patriarcali, famiglie culturalmente svantaggiate, scuole incapaci di affrontare il bullismo, l'esposizione dannosa ai social media, l'esposizione a comportamenti e contesti devianti, situazioni di abuso, ecc. e specifici ulteriori fabbisogni  rilevati neii diversi paesi europei della partnership. 

<< Implementation >>

Nei 24 mesi di implementazione, i partner, rispettando quanto previsto dal progetto candidato ed approvato, hanno realizzato le seguenti azioni prioritarie: 
- Sviluppo ed implementazione sul campo di una metodologia delle ricerca sociale propedeutica all'individuazione, coinvolgimento e formazione dei gruppi target, nello specifico ragazze adolescenti vulnerabili. Da questa azione è derivato l'output intellettuale n. 1 - STORIE DI FRAGILITA'.
- Progettazione, sviluppo, test nei diversi contesti locali di un curriculum formativo per educatori e youth workers, direttamente imegnati nell'implementazione di attività educative e di formazioneinformale con ragazzi/e vulnerabili per favorire l'acquisizione di specifiche competenze in materIa di progettazione ed implementazione di metodologie creative per la formazione, l'inclusione e l'empowerment, (Output n. 2 - CURRCULUM).
- Progettazione, sviluppo e test nei paesi della partnership, direttamente con i gruppi target, di un kit di metodologie e materiali didattici per la formazione inclusiva e l'empowerment di ragazze vulnerabili, (Output 3 - TRAINING TOOLKIT)
- Progettaziobne e sviluppo di una piattaforma digitale per l'erogazione della formazione di educatori e Youthworker, in relazione al curriculum formativo sviluppato (OUTPUT n. 4)
- Implementazione di una strategia di comunicazione e disseminazione traversale, realizzazione di campagne mirate ai target, attuate in nciascun paese partner.
- Attuazione di un piano trasversale di monitoraggio e valutazione per la verifica della qualità di azioni realizzare e prodotti sviluppati. 

<< Results >>

Il progetto ha realizzato i risultai attesi. Nello specifico: 
- OI 1 - RICERCA SOCIALE - STORIES OF FRAGILITIES
- IO2 - CURRICULUM SULLE METODOLOGIE ESPERIENZIALI PER EDUCATORI E YOUTHWORKER
- IO3 - TRAINING TOOLKIT PER L'APPLICAZIONE DELLE METODOLOGIE ESPERIENZIALI
- IO4 - PIATTAFORMA DIGITALE PER L'APPRENDIMENTO.
Accanto ai prodotti sopra citati e descritti nel dettaglio nella sezione deidcata del report, grazie all'attuazione di una strategia di comunicazione e disseminazione multicanale, SPACE4US è stato in grando di sensibilizzare stakeholder pubblici e privati, educatori, policy makers, e un più ampio pubblico, sui temi del disagio giovanile e sui fabbisogni di inclusione del target prioritario, ragazze adolescenti vulnerabili, a rischio di marginalizzazione. Il progetto è inoltre risucito a formare oltre 100 educatori su innovativi approcci per l'apprendimento esperienziale, socio-emozionale e per l'empowerment, nei vari paesi europei ed è riuscito a sviluppare un panel di risorse formative e di ricerca di grande valore europeo, fortemente riutilizzabili/capitalizzabili e trasferibili ad altri contesti educativi e target.

2021-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000029045.title: CITYFUL - Empowering youth workers to engange young people, NEETs and drop-out through the 3rd Sector in the EU
2021-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000029045.summary:
<< Background >>

CITYFUL è stato indirizzato ad un target specifico: i giovani NEET europei. Con la pandemia la quantità di NEET è aumentata, e ha bisogno di essere al centro del discorso sociale, di ricevere stimoli per l’attivazione, per il reinserimento scolastico, formativo o lavorativo o per approcciare il mondo del lavoro per la prima volta nella maniera più corretta. 
Con CITYFUL abbiamo voluto dare uno stimolo a tutti i giovani che al momento hanno perso interesse nel lavoro, nella formazione e nella scuola mostrando loro l’esistenza del terzo settore e presentandolo non come una scelta di secondaria importanza rispetto al lavoro del mondo “for profit” ma come una vera e propria opportunità per reinserirsi ed attivarsi.  
CITYFUL è inoltre indirizzato a Youth Workers europei, figure fondamentali per il reiserimento e l’attivazione dei NEET. Grazie al progetto abbiamo esteso a youth workers una serie di principi didattici, metodologici ed operativi per affrontare, incontrare, stimolare, attivare, riattivare, coinvolgere e rendere protagonisti i NEET dei vari territori e delle varie comunità di riferimento.

<< Objectives >>

L’obiettivo generale di progetto è supportare i NEET dei territori di riferimento, fornendo loro un gioco educativo tale da favorire sia la loro attivazione/riattivazione che un cambiamento nella loro visione del mondo del terzo settore. 
Nei confronti dei NEET, CITYFUL ha due obiettivi principali: favorire la loro attivazione e/o  riattivazione tramite la produzione di uno strumento ad essi vicino e familiare, il gioco digitale e presentare loro una possibilità di impegnare il proprio tempo a loro generalmente sconosciuta o, nella maggior parte dei casi, sottovalutata: il terzo settore. Un secondo obiettivo è quello di mostrare il terzo settore come un'area  professionale, valorizzante e appagante. Il terzo è un’area cruciale per l’economia europea, per il welfare state dell’unione, per i lavoratori degli stati membri,  è un settore che può offrire ai neet una serie di risposte interessanti ai loro bisogni formativi, educativi e professionali. Altro obiettivo di progetto è quello di fornire agli youth workers una serie di competenze e di strumenti utili ad avvicinare, affrontare, attivare e/o riattivare i giovani NEET. 

<< Implementation >>

Tramite CITYFUL sono state implementate le seguenti azioni: 
- 3 meeting transnazionali di progetto (di cui due online - kick off e final meeting) dedicati al Project Management, con lo scopo di agevolare i processi di comunicazione e cooperazione; - 2 Work Group meeting dedicati all’analisi dei bisogni, al co-design di progetto (arricchiti grazie a un percorso online guidato da Itinerari Paralleli), all’analisi e valutazione dei risultati e alla disseminazione; - 2 Project results: 1 gioco educativo digitale denominato CITYFUL ed un Handbook destinato agli youth workers; - 1 Learning Activity transnazionale, in Italia, con giovani e Youth workers provenienti dai paesi di progetto che per 4 giorni hanno partecipato alla formazione ed al gioco CITYFUL testandone potenzialità, usi e difficoltà ed hanno acquisito competenze e strumenti per essere antenne moltiplicatrici dei benefici delle attività, coinvolgendo altri giovani in attività di “peer to peer education” al ritorno nel proprio paese.- 3 Multiplier events nei 3 paesi di progetto, volti a raggiungere il maggior numero di stakeholders (youth workers, scuole, enti del terzo settore, istituzioni pubbliche) possibile. Il progetto ha visto l’implementazione delle attività all’interno di una serie di fasi: - Analisi dei bisogni dei Neet nei diversi paesi di progetto, con scambio di buone pratiche tra operatori del settore - Co-design e produzione del gioco digitale e dell’Handbook per youth workers.- Valutazione: sono stati raccolti i risultati ed i feedback quantitativi allo scopo di valutare il raggiungimento degli obiettivi prefissi per i risultati di progetto. 

<< Results >>

I project result del progetto sono due: il gioco educativo digitale CITYFUL e l’Hanbook per youth workers. 
Il gioco è uno strumento digitale, un edu-game e una metodologia per gli youth workers, per sostenere un nuovo modo di approcciare i giovani in difficoltà, i NEET e i gruppi fragili che vivono nelle nostre comunità, fornendo loro un gioco per promuovere la loro attivazione/riattivazione mentre scoprono come il terzo settore e l'imprenditoria sociale possono creare un impatto positivo nelle nostre città, sfidandoli a risolvere missioni sociali mentre esplorano i loro quartieri. L’Handbook è un vero e proprio manuale d'uso, frutto della formazione online rivolta agli animatori giovanili. Si tratta di un manuale d'uso strutturato e completo per il gioco, in grado di fornire non solo le informazioni tecniche e pratiche per giocare, ma anche suggerimenti e strategie per condurlo, oltre a fornire una contestualizzazione dello strumento. I due prodotti hanno l'obiettivo comune di formare e fornire strumenti agli youth workers in grado di supportarli nel loro lavoro e nell’affrontare, supportare e attivare/riattivare giovani NEET. Inoltre è stata fatta una formazione diretta durante la learning activity in italia dove giovani e youth worker provenienti da diversi paesi hanno testato ed imparato a giocare a CITYFUL, inoltre è stato un momento di scambio interculturale per i giovani. La disseminazione del progetto è stata un’attività fondamentale che ha visto la creazione di 3 multiplier event in 3 paesi diversi e percorsi educativi peer-to-peer che hanno coinvolto i partecipanti della Learning Activity.

2021-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000029203.title: COOLTOUR - Millennials for Cultural Heritage
2021-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000029203.summary:
<< Background >>

La pandemia di Covid-19 ha esercitato una pressione senza precedenti sul settore culturale. In risposta a tali sfide, gli operatori culturali e i custodi del patrimonio hanno adottato strategie innovative, utilizzando in modo estensivo la creatività e le soluzioni digitali per mantenere il contatto con il pubblico. Questo approccio ha richiesto l'apprendimento di nuovi linguaggi comunicativi, essenziali per attrarre un pubblico più vasto e, in particolare, le giovani generazioni.
L'impatto della pandemia ha inciso profondamente anche sulla vita quotidiana dei giovani, sollevando la necessità di riscoprire la propria identità e rafforzare il senso di appartenenza e connessione con le proprie comunità. In questo contesto, i giovani hanno dimostrato notevole creatività nell'uso dei social network per la diffusione di contenuti culturali, guadagnando l'approvazione delle istituzioni culturali verso tali iniziative digitali. Parallelamente, il riscoprire e valorizzare tradizioni e storia locali può potenziare la consapevolezza individuale e collettiva, la resilienza e promuovere la condivisione culturale, consolidando il legame con la comunità.
Il progetto COOLTOUR si pone come risposta a queste esigenze emergenti. 

<< Objectives >>

Il progetto si è prefissato i seguenti obiettivi:
1. Lo sviluppo di strumenti digitali all’avanguardia e di strategie comunicative efficaci volte a stimolare le giovani generazioni nella creazione e condivisione delle proprie percezioni e emozioni relative al patrimonio culturale. Tale iniziativa mira altresì a promuovere competenze fondamentali e abilità essenziali tra i giovani.
2. Il miglioramento e l’aggiornamento delle competenze dei gestori del patrimonio culturale per abbracciare linguaggi moderni, approcci innovativi e strumenti digitali, rafforzando così la loro capacità di interazione e gestione in un panorama culturale in evoluzione.
3. Accrescere la familiarità con i processi legati al patrimonio culturale ed aumentare la consapevolezza tra i giovani riguardo al potenziale del patrimonio stesso nel contribuire alla costruzione di una cittadinanza europea informata, che valorizzi le identità locali e la diversità culturale.



<< Implementation >>

Il progetto si è articolato in un insieme coordinato di attività strettamente interconnesse, finalizzate al conseguimento degli obiettivi prefissati. 
Inizialmente, il consorzio ha condotto indagini di tipo desk e field study riguardanti i temi focali del progetto, quali l'interazione tra i Millennials e i siti archeologici, l'analisi delle migliori pratiche relative a applicazioni e piattaforme preesistenti per la valorizzazione di tali siti, nonché le necessità dei gestori del patrimonio culturale in merito allo sviluppo di un dialogo efficace con la generazione dei Millennials.
I risultati preliminari hanno giocato un ruolo cruciale nella definizione delle caratteristiche iniziali dei due principali Risultati del progetto:
- Toolkit (R2): concepito come un manuale pratico, il toolkit offre agli amministratori del patrimonio culturale uno strumento facilmente utilizzabile per integrare pratiche e attività volte a rendere l'interpretazione dei siti più appassionante e coinvolgente per i Millennials.
- Piattaforma (R1): questa componente del progetto consiste in una piattaforma digitale innovativa progettata per stimolare l'interazione attiva dei Millennials, permettendo la raccolta dei loro contributi nella creazione di contenuti e narrativa relativi al patrimonio culturale. La piattaforma integra tecnologie multimediali di avanguardia, blog e social media per generare un'interfaccia dinamica tra i gestori del patrimonio culturale (CHM) e i Millennials.
Le fasi di test per entrambi i Risultati sono state condotte attraverso due mobilità internazionali di grande rilievo:
- C1 si è concentrata sull'esplorazione della Piattaforma da parte dei Millennials per valutare le sue funzionalità, erogare formazione specifica sui metodi di comunicazione digitale e raccogliere feedback.
- C2 ha coinvolto i partner del progetto, comprendenti giovani e professionisti del settore, per testare la metodologia del Toolkit e sviluppare progetti pilota nei vari paesi.
I feedback acquisiti durante queste mobilità sono stati impiegati per perfezionare i Risultati e preparare i progetti pilota. Questi ultimi, realizzati nei paesi dei partner, hanno offerto un'opportunità per testare i Risultati in diversi contesti e con vari gruppi target, permettendo ulteriori raccolte di feedback e approfondimenti sulla replicabilità dei risultati e delle metodologie.
Le versioni definitive dei Risultati sono state poi diffuse tramite Eventi Moltiplicatori, canali di comunicazione diversificati e una conferenza finale online. Parallelamente, il progetto ha attuato un piano di comunicazione e diffusione continuo, attraverso il quale le attività principali e i risultati sono stati divulgati mediante newsletter, presenza sui social media, il sito web del progetto, iniziative locali e nazionali, ed Eventi Moltiplicatori.



<< Results >>

Il progetto ha prodotto i seguenti Risultati:
Piattaforma (R1): Questo risultato si concretizza in una piattaforma digitale all'avanguardia che facilita un coinvolgimento attivo dei Millennials e la raccolta dei loro contributi per la creazione di contenuti e narrazioni legate al patrimonio culturale.
Toolkit (R2): Si tratta di un manuale pratico che i gestori del patrimonio possono utilizzare per arricchire il loro percorso interpretativo, rendendolo più accattivante per i Millennials.
Linee guida (complementari a R2): Queste consistono in un documento comprensivo (oltre 100 pagine nella versione inglese) che articola l'approccio metodologico e teorico ai temi trattati, integrando evidenze scientifiche, citazioni, casi di studio e prassi del Toolkit.
Il progetto ha inoltre rafforzato le competenze dei gestori del patrimonio culturale verso linguaggi moderni, approcci innovativi e strumenti digitali.
In questo contesto, i gestori del patrimonio sono stati impegnati in varie attività di miglioramento delle competenze digitali e comunicative, tra cui ricerca, co-sviluppo delle Linee guida, del Toolkit e della Piattaforma, mobilità internazionale, test degli strumenti a livello nazionale nei progetti pilota, e condivisione di feedback e conoscenze con i colleghi durante eventi nazionali e internazionali. I 50 gestori del patrimonio coinvolti nei progetti pilota hanno attestato, mediante strumenti di valutazione, l'acquisizione di nuove conoscenze e competenze relative ai percorsi interpretativi e agli strumenti di comunicazione digitale, esprimendo la volontà di riutilizzare le conoscenze acquisite. Riscontri simili sono stati ottenuti dai gestori del patrimonio partecipanti agli Eventi Moltiplicatori e al Café Online internazionale.
Il progetto ha inoltre sensibilizzato i giovani sul potenziale del patrimonio culturale nel costruire una cittadinanza europea che valorizzi le identità locali e la diversità culturale.
I Millennials sono stati coinvolti in una serie di attività mirate a valorizzare le identità locali e la diversità culturale, inclusa la mobilità internazionale in Serbia e attività locali presso i siti del Patrimonio dei territori di appartenenza. Tutti i giovani coinvolti nel progetto hanno riferito di aver sviluppato nuove competenze nella gestione del patrimonio, di sentirsi più connessi al proprio patrimonio e di avere mi maturato un maggiore senso di appartenenza alla cittadinanza europea.

2021-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000030193.title: Let Young be Resilient!
2021-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000030193.summary:
<< Background >>

Un progetto sull'intelligenza emotiva, finalizzato a rafforzare l'uso delle capacità socio-relazionali degli animatori giovanili nelle organizzazioni private. Nel contesto europeo, molti progetti sono attualmente finalizzati all'educazione socio-emotiva, in particolare nell'ambiente scolastico, come consapevolezza condivisa che essa sia un importante elemento di benessere soggettivo. I vantaggi dell'utilizzo di un approccio relazionale sono ben noti, grazie a molteplici ricerche scientifiche nel contesto dell'insegnamento scolastico, ma da qualche tempo è stata prestata molta attenzione anche a organizzazioni e istituzioni complesse e al luogo di lavoro. In particolare, questo progetto è stato destinato a coloro che lavorano con giovani, giovani svantaggiati, vulnerabili, non occupati e con particolari bisogni socio-emotivi. Per questo il progetto ha voluto fornire agli youth worker  un modello di intervento e un approccio nuovo al tema dell’allenamento delle competenze emotive dei giovani fornendo anche esempi di attività e di percorsi formativi non formali. 

<< Objectives >>

Il nostro progetto ha inteso migliorare le competenze degli operatori giovanili ne diventare attivatori e facilitatori della resilienza dei giovani, della loro intelligenza emotiva e delle competenze socio-relazionali, con particolare riguardo ai giovani a rischio di esclusione e disagio sociale. Concentrarsi sull’Intelligenza Emotiva e sulla Resilienza come specificità, è dunque una scelta dettata dall’analisi di contesto dei 4 paesi partner che conferma come i nostri giovani (16-30) in condizione di disagio (lavoro, formazione, situazione personale) spesso siano sprovvisti delle life skills di base necessarie per affrontare le sfide della vita e le situazioni di stress, difficoltà ed emergenza, a partire proprio da una dotazione emotiva adeguata. Abbiamo voluto sperimentare un modello appositamente ideato partendo dalla dimensione auto-valutativa e dagli strumenti formativi per creare competenze che siano professionalizzanti e spendibili nella pratica professionale degli Youth workers, migliorando le loro competenze di allenatori delle competenze emotive dei giovani. 

<< Implementation >>

L’intero progetto è concentrato sulla formazione delle competenze e delle soft skills (competenze trasversali) in ambito socio emotivo. Quindi gli obiettivi principali sono proprio relativi al miglioramento della condizione degli operatori giovanili e dei giovani, in termini di dotazione di competenze emotive e life skills per affrontare i momenti di difficoltà, di emergenza e di disagio. Le azioni previste sono tutte state focalizzate sulla migliore riuscita dell’obiettivo principale ovvero quello di favorire non solo la conoscenza, ma soprattutto l’applicazione dell’Intelligenza Emotiva nella pratica quotidiana di lavoro con i giovani. Le attività sono state finalizzate ad aumentare la dotazione di conoscenze, informazioni ma soprattutto competenze pratiche (emotional life skills) che possano “assistere” gli operatori giovanili durante il loro lavoro con i giovani AZIONI: studio-fruizione di un percorso di autovalutazione tramite bilancio delle competenze per comprendere i propri prerequisiti, in termini di competenze della sfera “psicologica”, il sapere e il saper fare in termini di capacità di ascolto, empatia, comprensione. Questa azione si sostanzia nel lavoro previsto dalla seconda opera intellettuale (risultato 2), che verificata nella formazione degli youth worker e nella sperimentazione del risultato 3. 

<< Results >>

I risultati del progetto sono stati : 1 evento per lo staff delle organizzazioni partecipanti, finalizzato a formare lo staff del partenariato rispetto all'utilizzo degli strumenti ideati, e a potenziare le loro competenze di formatori (professionali) e fornire loro uno strumento di auto-valutazione e valutazione delle competenze emotive dei giovani con cui lavorano. Lo strumento è stato testato e validato su un campione di 800 giovani, informatizzato (mediante google-form). È stata realizzata anche una pubblicazione contenente le linee guida rispetto all'uso dello strumento di bilancio di competenze socio-emotive e un toolkit con i moduli formativi e le attività da utilizzare nelle sessioni formative con i giovani. 
Sono state organizzate 4 sessioni di sperimentazione del modello.

2021-1-LT02-KA220-YOU-000029006.title: More than Reliable Online Education
2021-1-LT02-KA220-YOU-000029006.summary:
<< Background >>

The decision to apply for the MORE project under Erasmus+ KA2 was driven by the pressing challenges faced by youth centers and workers during the COVID-19 pandemic. With activities halted and collaboration limited, youth organizations urgently needed innovative solutions to continue their essential work. The project was conceived as a response to these needs, aiming to equip youth workers with tools and resources to effectively engage with young people and communities, even amidst global disruptions.The call for new approaches was echoed by youth center directors, highlighting a readiness to embrace any initiative directly benefiting their operations. The project's collaborative nature, involving four NGOs across Europe – Association Active Youth (Lithuania), Europejskie Centrum Mlodziezy (Poland), Predict CSD Consulting (Romania), and Brodoto (Croatia) – exemplifies a commitment to transcending geographical barriers for the greater good of youth empowerment. By focusing on the development of key competencies and providing educational resources, MORE aims to ensure that youth workers are not just surviving these challenging times but thriving in their roles, thereby securing a resilient and educated future for the youth they serve

<< Objectives >>

-Develop an educational program for YWs: This program is designed to equip YWs with relevant competencies and skills that align with the changing status quo, including education, training, and digital skills. The idea is to prepare them for the evolving landscape of youth work.
-Innovate practical learning methods: We aimed to develop a more professional and innovative approach to practical learning, tightly linked to active participation in youth work. This involves creating methods that are engaging, practical, and applicable in real-world scenarios.
-Promote global access to free education: to foster a mindset that emphasizes the importance of global access to free education. This includes highlighting opportunities and ways for YWs and youth to develop further.
-Establish a Global Online Network among Youth Workers: The creation of a global online network for YWs is essential. This network facilitates learning from each other, sharing experiences, and collaborating on a global scale.
Achieving objectives is expected to significantly improve the field of youth work. It's not just about responding to future lockdowns or emergencies, but also about providing YWs with skills and support that are relevant in on/offfline contexts. 

<< Implementation >>

In the MORE project, we implemented a comprehensive set of activities, each meticulously designed to enhance the skills of youth workers and the operational efficacy of youth centers in both online and offline environments. The activities included:
Research on Needs/Wants of Youth Workers and Centers: This initial step involved identifying the specific needs and wants of youth workers and centers to enhance their hard and soft skills.
Training Course in Croatia: A course was conducted in Croatia to train staff in the preparation of online courses, equipping them with the necessary skills for digital education.
Pilot Online Course: We launched a pilot online course to lay the groundwork for the finalization of a comprehensive online curriculum titled “Video Production From A to Z”.
Set of 9 Online Courses (plus Pilot Course)- 'MORE Specialized Education': These courses were designed to boost the organizational and individual skills of youth workers, particularly in engaging with youth effectively.
Training Course in Romania: This course focused on drafting a program for practical seminars that were later conducted in each partner country.
Recorded webinar series “MORE from Youth Workers”: where the expertise and good practice were shared in the partner countries.
Practical Seminars for Experienced Youth Workers: These seminars provided a platform for experienced youth workers to share their expertise and best practices.
'MORE Knowledge to Practice' Handbook: This handbook was created to help youth workers adapt learning methods and tools in their daily practices.
Recorded Webinar Series 'MORE from Youth Workers': A series of webinars was recorded, featuring insights and experiences from youth workers.
Publication of 3 Online Magazines 'MORE Insights': These magazines included informative articles, success stories from the target group, and recommendations for learning opportunities.
Multiplier Events: The project hosted 2 face-to-face and 2 online multiplier events in Lithuania, Poland, Romania, and Croatia to promote project results, Erasmus+, and to facilitate networking among youth workers and other stakeholders.
Mentorship Program 'MORE Guidance': This program connected youth workers with professionals in specific fields for individual guidance.
Development of 'MORE Diverse' Online Platform: An online platform was developed to host all the educational resources mentioned above.
The aim was to create a sustainable and impactful learning environment that not only addresses current needs but also anticipates future challenges in youth work.

<< Results >>

Extensive Research on Youth Workers' Needs: Conducted detailed research to identify specific needs and preferences of youth workers and centres. This was pivotal in tailoring the subsequent training and resources to enhance both hard and soft skills relevant for working in varied environments.
Training Course in Croatia: Implemented a key training course in Croatia, attended by 6 project team members. This course was essential for equipping staff with the skills needed to develop and prepare online educational materials effectively.
Training Course in Romania for Seminar Drafting: This training course, with 10 participants, focused on drafting a program for practical seminars. It was a foundational step towards creating a comprehensive handbook.
Pilot Online Course on Video Production: Successfully launched on UDEMY, this course garnered considerable attention, enrolling 2,421 students by January 1st, 2024, and achieving a high satisfaction rating of 4.23 out of 5 stars.
Comprehensive Set of 9 UDEMY Courses: Surpassing the initial goal of 8, a total of 9 courses were created on various topics, ranging from graphic design to project writing. Each course was well-received, with ratings between 4 and 5 stars, indicating the high quality and relevance of the content totalled in 12,878 enrolled students by January 1st, 2024.
Multiplier Events Across Partner Countries: Conducted both face-to-face and online multiplier events in Lithuania, Poland, Romania, and Croatia. These events served not only to disseminate the project's findings and resources but also to provide a vital networking platform for youth workers and stakeholders. The multipliers were attended by 516 participants in total.
'MORE Guidance' Mentorship Program: This innovative program successfully connected 20 professionals from diverse fields with youth workers, offering mentorship sessions across partner countries. It stands as an ongoing opportunity for youth workers seeking individualized guidance.
Development of the 'MORE Diverse' Online Platform: This platform acts as a central hub for all the project's resources, facilitating easy access and interaction among users, and ensuring the longevity and continuous engagement with the project's outputs.
'MORE from Youth Workers' Webinar Series: A series of 4 informative webinars were held across the participating countries. These webinars provided a platform for experts to share their knowledge, discuss best practices, and engage in Q&A sessions, drawing in numerous participants. The webinars attracted 153 participants in total.
Practical Seminars for Experienced Youth Workers: Four two-day seminars were conducted in the project countries. These seminars combined theoretical knowledge with practical examples and hands-on exercises, creating a rich learning environment. The total attendance at these seminars provides a measure of the project's direct impact on the field. The seminars attracted 114 participants in total.
'MORE Knowledge to Practice' Handbook: This 125-page handbook has been a significant resource, aiding youth workers in adapting to and learning new techniques and online tools. Its download count is a testament to its utility and popularity. The handbook was downloaded by 136 people in total.

2021-1-NL02-KA220-YOU-000028647.title: Don’t worry, Be You: Fostering Youth & Community Wellbeing
2021-1-NL02-KA220-YOU-000028647.summary:
<< Background >>

Our partnership has applied for this project based on the premise there was a big need to work on the topic of mental health amongst youth, especially after the pandemic. We also applied for this project with the idea that we saw a lot of youthworkers wanting to have access to tools and knowledge to work with this topic in an easy accessible format which can help them support youngsters before their situation turns very serious or clinical. The context was that a combination of isolation, inactivity and a broader loss of purpose due to strict lockdown measures imposed by Covid-19 outbreak in 2020-2021 left many young people close to breakdown. 

Our project addressed the following needs:
1. Development of a model and tools to better deal with the fear of uncertainty, building resilience and raising awareness of what can support one's well-being in times of various challenges on societal level, incl. pos-pandemic period. 
2. Equipping and empowering of youthworkers to become well-being coaches 
3. Supporting young people cope to find new meaning in their lives through self-care practices tailor-made for youth. 
4. Lastly our project has contributed to the need for support and conversation on a community level. 

<< Objectives >>

The overall project goal is to equip young people with fewer opportunities with knowledge, techniques and competences how to live a happier and fulfilled life, and to foster wellbeing in their communities by combining game-based community-building practices with advocacy work and training youth workers as health & wellbeing coaches to provide better assistance to young people and thus increase the quality of European youth work. Specific project objectives are split in 4 dimensions: 
1. Individual Mental Health: support awareness raising of young people and youth workers about mental health & wellbeing and develop a methodology to foster well-being through non-formal learning methods. 
2. Collective Mental Health: develop competences of young people in community-based initiatives with a focus on sustainability, ecological awareness and collaboration (with a possibility for the schools and non-formal learning institutions to use this model). 
3. Empowerment: empower young people use all the created tools in the project and become role models for other young people and communities to engage in a change process. 
4. Advocacy: empower young people to become role models in the community and influence policy 

<< Implementation >>

The key project activities executed were based on the development of four Project Results which are linked to four pillars of the Don’t Worry Be You model and the LEMC learning method: 

1. Learn: A 160 page Wellbeing Workbook (PR1) focused on empowering and equipping youth workers and offering youth activities that enhance well-being, based on 6 pathways, covering (a.o.) emotional, physical and mental content, exercises and reflection. 
2. Embody: 10 Embodiment Video Tutorials (PR2) embodiment practices support youth and youthworkers to increase to connect to the signals in their bodies as a channel of communication of their well-being. 
3. Mindfulness: A 21 day Mindfulness Challenge (PR3) with 21 podcasts and exercises that can be hosted in app or chat channels with groups that want to connect to present moment and feel grounded and safe. 
4. Connect: The Good Deed Game (PR4) and Guide for organizers and facilitators has been developed to support community well-being by an engaging activity that give community members and networks sense of purpose and connection to other people as an antidote to isolation.  

The project were developed in the first part of the program, kicked off by a transnational project meeting in Berlin in march 2022. 

The results were tested and trained to youth workers of all partners in a Learning and training activity in Zagreb in october 2022. Key feedbacks were used to improve and finalize the first three project results and afterwards the development of the Good Deed Game started. 

Early 2023 the results were tested by the partners in a series of local 4-pillar workshops and test rounds with end-users; youthworkers and disadvantaged youth. 

A part of this group and other youth were invited to blended mobility event, transnational learning and training activity in Italy in early may 2023. 

Youngsters left empowered and equipped to replicate DWBY content, set up local well-being projects, strongly connected as a network and part of regional teams preparing to implement Good Deed Games. 

The project results were translated and offered in 6 languages (English, Dutch, Croatian, Greek, Italian and Bulgarian) and are now available for free download from the project website www.dontworrybeyou.org. 

The results were presented in the 6 countries during multiplier events to an audience of 170 European multipliers and disseminated through a network of partners and associate partners inside and outside the European Union to thousands of people through online activities, newsletters, campaigns, additional workshops and social media. 


<< Results >>

We developed four accessible, attractive, profound and comprehensive tools that have been tested, used and disseminated, which we repeat here again;  

1. Learn: A 160 page Wellbeing Workbook (PR1) focused on empowering and equipping youth workers and offering youth activities that promote well-being, based on 6 pathways, covering (a.o.) emotional, physical and mental content, exercises and reflection. 
2. Embody: 10 Embodiment Video Tutorials (PR2) embodiment practices support youth and youthworkers to increase to connect to the signals in their bodies as a channel of communication of their well-being. 
3. Mindfulness: A 21 day Mindfulness Challenge (PR3) with 21 podcasts and exercises that can be hosted in app or chat channels with groups that want to connect to present moment and feel grounded and safe. 
4. Connect: The Good Deed Game (PR4) and Guide for organizers and facilitators has been developed to support community well-being by an engaging activity that give community members and networks sense of purpose and connection to other people as an antidote to isolation.  

We have now *20* youth workers from Croatia, Netherlands, Greece, Bulgaria, Germany and Italy trained to be wellbeing coaches with a high skill level for the topic mental health & wellbeing. 

We have set up a network of youth and youngsters in the 6 partner countries that are part of our informal youth council and international community, applying DWBY content in their projects. It raised their level of confidence and contentment, gained skills of self-care practices, as well as a sense of initiative and ownership;

We have disseminated the materials to more than 170 youth workers in 6 European countries who not only learnt together, but also raised their awareness about the importance of mental health & wellbeing in youthwork. 

Our indirect dissemination through newsletters, online messaging, social media and other dissemination activities have reached 170 + youthworkers and professionals directly, many more indirectly and dissemination activities of partners individually and as a collective have reached 300.000+ views. 

Our partner organisations have strengthened their profiles on a regional and national level as advocates of conscious and inclusive wellbeing work within their community, various follow up projects have been executed or planned to continue implementing DWBY and well-being work. 

300+ community stakeholders and policy makers become involved in the project activities to design and support youth initiatives and wellbeing policies at local, as well as regional and international level, strengthened by the culture of collaboration and solidarity. 

In the middle-long term, the project will continue to seek to facilitate better understanding of the importance of mental health topic for youth and communities, involve young people in the process of designing wellbeing policies as co-creators and change makers, and create new value of sustainability for communities through a common focus on wellbeing. This will take place under the umbrella of the YEPP Europe network of which all organizations have now become members of. The next step after focussing on developing, testing, implementation and dissemination is in the coming years increase the application and dissemination of the materials through local activities and international activities amongst partners.

2021-1-PL01-KA220-YOU-000029297.title: Join the Game
2021-1-PL01-KA220-YOU-000029297.summary:
<< Background >>

Choosing a career, teenage girls often reject masculinized occupations (those in which there are more men than women, or are considered "masculine" in the social consciousness). This applies to both vocational and higher education.  Girls do not take these occupations into account, despite the fact that they are in greater demand on the labor market and are associated with better wages, as research shows. This is due to the stereotypes young women encounter from an early age. Due to their beliefs about their own abilities and predispositions (deepened by the formal education system), they have a very limited career path. Young women, after graduating from education, decide to take up a profession that requires them to give up one of the social roles assigned to women (responsibility for running a home, raising children, caring for parents, etc.). This project was created to provide people working with girls and young women with tools that will respond to this problem.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project is to create tools and work out a working method for youth workers and popularize them in order to encourage girls and young women to work in masculinized professions (i.e. those considered stereotypically performed by men), and thus - to improve their situation on the market work.

<< Implementation >>

Three LTT activities took place during the project:
C1: safe space training,
C2: urban games training,
C3: tool-kit training.

Four intellectual outputs were developed:
R1 (IO1): The "Join the game" Urban Game - instructions and description
R2 (IO2): The "Join the game" Urban Game - how to adapt?
R3 (IO3): The "Join the game" Urban Game - tips for playing, roles and tasks for organization and youth workers
R4 (IO4): The "Join the game" - how to play in the real world.

There were also 3 transnational partner meetings and 4 dissemination events.

<< Results >>

1. A "safe space" method was created and disseminated (how to create conditions for working with girls so that they feel safe), and thanks to this they are not afraid to try their hand at breaking stereotypes). The method is created as a checklist - making it a simple tool to work with.
2. A universal tool was created - an urban game - which can be adapted to own needs, but still will respond to the needs we have identified. The urban game "Join the Game" familiarizes participants with roles models, who have achieved success in a profession considered stereotypically "masculine".
3. A guide to game customization has been created, so that you can adapt it to your own needs.
4. Guidelines for conducting the game were created - how to lead and support the participants to make the game a success.
5. Nine audiovisual materials were created. They can be used as tools to introduce the topic of women on the labor market. These are interviews with girls and women who already work in professions considered "masculine". These videos can be a pretext for a conversation about opportunities and limitations regarding a professional career.

2021-1-PT02-KA220-YOU-000028838.title: Digital Marketing for NEETS
2021-1-PT02-KA220-YOU-000028838.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the DIGMA project to tackle the pressing needs of NEETs by harnessing the growing digital economy's potential. Recognizing the widening gap between the digital skills possessed by young adults and the market's demand, especially in the digital marketing sector, we aimed to bridge this divide. 

Our objective was to provide NEETs with practical digital marketing skills, making them more employable and connecting them to the fast-growing online marketplace. This initiative was spurred by the increasing importance of an online presence for businesses, as underscored by the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to a significant investment of companies in digital presence. 

Thus, we aimed to meet these critical needs: 
1. Enhance the employability of NEETs by equipping them with digital marketing skills and competencies
2. Bridge the gap between the needs of the labour market and the professional competencies of young people
3. Raise awareness to the escalating importance of ICT and digital marketing skills in different spheres of life 
 
The project was designed to innovate by integrating NFE opportunities, “Experienceship” abroad, and a problem-based learning approach, addressing NEETs' educational and emotional stability needs.

<< Objectives >>

The DIGMA project was initiated to empower NEETs through education and practical experience in digital marketing, aligning with the vision to enhance their employability and integration into the digital economy. 

Our main objectives were:
1. Enhance Employability: To significantly increase the employability of NEETs by equipping them with the skills and experiences necessary to secure positions within the digital marketing sector. This initiative aimed at directly linking their new-found digital marketing competencies with market demands, facilitating their workforce transition.

2. Boost ICT Skills: To elevate the ICT competencies among young people, addressing the critical need for digital literacy in today’s technology-driven world. Our objective was to familiarize NEETs with basic digital tools and to deepen their understanding and practical skills in digital marketing, contributing to their personal and professional growth.

3. Raise Digital Marketing Awareness: To cultivate an understanding of the importance of digital marketing across various life spheres. This included promoting self-marketing skills, enhancing the digital presence of youth centers, and demonstrating the value of digital marketing to companies. 


<< Implementation >>

The implementation of our project was structured around a series of carefully planned activities designed to achieve our defined objectives. These activities were carried out collaboratively and were executed successfully. Below, we outline the key activities that were an integral part of the project's implementation:

1. Management & Monitoring: utilizing a suite of management tools, we ensured that the project remained on track and outcomes were achieved efficiently, and within the foreseen budget. 

2. Project results: to achieve our project goals, we implemented a set of structured activities which built up on each other, and culminated in concrete project results (Reports, Guidebooks, Trainings, Experienceship and E-Portal)

3. Dissemination & Multiplier Activities: following a detailed dissemination plan, we focused our efforts in the dissemination of project results and main events, aiming to reach a wide audience. In addition, we organized a set of Multiplier events in partner countries, as ultimate dissemination activities. 

4. Sustainability: since the first stage, the project aims to be impactful and sustainable. Thus, a series of activities were implemented to guarantee project sustainability and extended impact. 


<< Results >>

Our project successfully produced an array of concrete outputs and results:

1. DIGMA Educational Program: A comprehensive digital marketing curriculum tailored to the learning needs of NEETs. This program comprised several modules covering essential digital marketing tools and strategies, from understanding customer behavior to mastering various online advertising channels.

2. Train-the-Trainer Program: An innovative training framework for youth workers, equipping them with pedagogical methods and digital tools to engage and educate NEETs.

3. Guidebooks and Online Resources: Two sets of guidebooks were developed - one for youth workers and one for NEETs, providing step-by-step instructions into digital marketing. Accompanied by online resources, these materials facilitated self-paced learning and reinforced training content.

4. Experienceship Opportunities: The project facilitated job shadowing/ experienceship opportunities abroad, allowing NEETs to gain real-world experience in digital marketing. This exposure helped them apply theoretical knowledge in practical settings, enhancing their employability.

These outputs result from gathered efforts to realize our vision and deliver impactful resources to NEETs and Youth Workers.

2021-1-RO01-KA220-YOU-000028678.title: Green Genesis Startup
2021-1-RO01-KA220-YOU-000028678.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the urgent need for Europe's transition to a green economy, recognizing it as both a significant challenge and a remarkable opportunity for the continent's recovery and development. This initiative was motivated by the growing momentum of youth-led protests across the EU, which have effectively demonstrated the impact and importance of young voices in shaping environmental policies at both national and European levels. Furthermore, the European Union's emphasis on promoting entrepreneurship within the green economy, particularly among younger generations, highlighted a crucial gap in collaborative business models and the necessity for more green startups and companies. These entities are essential in different sectors for creating sustainable job opportunities, yet they face challenges in expanding their markets due to a lack of qualified personnel.

The primary goal of our project is to foster the development of "green young entrepreneurs" and to provide young individuals with the skills and knowledge required for employability in the green economy. By doing so, we aim to fill the existing gap in the labor market and support the EU's vision of becoming the world's first climate-neutral conti

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, our objectives were to contribute to entrepreneurship development and the creation of new job opportunities. These goals were achieved through a series of practical solutions, including capacity building of partner organizations, the design of an open, innovative, accelerated educational program for green and entrepreneurship skills, and mentorship.

Our specific objectives included:
- Developing an open innovation program that equipped young people with skills and knowledge in the green economy and entrepreneurship.
- Training young people in specific green and entrepreneurship skills.
- Creating an online mentorship platform to support young people in further developing their business ideas in the green sector.
- Establishing successful mentorship relations between young people and mentors in the green economy.

Our target group encompassed youth workers, staff members, young people, stakeholders (including policymakers, green businesses, consumers), unemployed young people, potential entrepreneurs, young entrepreneurs, and organizations operating in the public, educational, non-profit, and business sectors.

By the end of the project, young individuals had gained the knowledge and skills necessary t

<< Implementation >>

To achieve the objectives set, the project carried out 2 Intellectual Outputs (IOs):

1. Green Economy and Entrepreneurship Program (Green Genesis Startup Camp): The main goal of this program (GreenCamp) was to equip young people with skills and knowledge in the areas of the green economy and entrepreneurship.

2. Green Mentorship Platform: The Green Mentoring Platform, as a new initiative, aimed to encourage and motivate youth through the shared knowledge and experience of senior community mentors who have made positive contributions to society.

<< Results >>

The project resulted in several significant outcomes and impacts on the target group, which included young people and organizations working in the green sector and entrepreneurship development. These outcomes were as follows:

- The emergence of new green entrepreneurs working in industries with high growth potential.
- An increase in competencies among the youth, facilitating their ability to find quality job opportunities.
- The opportunity for young people to receive online mentorship from business experts, which helped them advance in their careers and increased their chances of becoming entrepreneurs or acquiring the necessary and demanded green skills.
- Businesses, educational institutions, non-profits, and public sector organizations working with youth had the chance to witness the impact of the innovative educational Acceleration program. They saw firsthand the methods for creating support programs to boost green entrepreneurship and create job opportunities for young people in the green industry, thus contributing to the reduction of the unemployment rate.
- The project attracted young people to the green sector, which offers rewarding and enjoyable careers to both women and men.
- It led to innovative learning and teaching approaches, offering more aligned degrees and curricula at vocational and university levels, ensuring students gained the skills needed for success.
- The project facilitated the transition between education and the labor market.

In terms of transnationality, the project provided the chance to work on a European scale with different partners, incorporating various visions and contributions to address a common problem. Specifically, it offered non-formal training based on thematic content relating entrepreneurship to the circular economy, presenting a unified package for “green jobs.”
