2021-2-HU01-KA220-YOU-000050143.title: Figyelünk rád!
2021-2-HU01-KA220-YOU-000050143.summary:
<< Background >>

A Szent Gellért Társaság azzal a céllal alakult meg, hogy támogassa a magyarországi és határon túli magyarság hátrányos helyzetű térségeinek és társadalmi rétegeinek integrálását a társadalomba, és a munkaerőpiacra. A Társaság az elmúlt években felkutatta a fennálló problémákat és fejlődési akadályokat, amelyek megoldására különböző aktivitásokat dolgozott ki, és realizált. A szervezet számára prioritás a fiatalok társadalmi és munkaerőpiaci helyzetének támogatása és felismerte, hogy mennyire fontos a fiatalok mentális egészség megőrzését célzó programok realizálása, ezért külön prioritásként tekint a mentálhigiénés tevékenységre, különös tekintettel a szenvedélybetegségek megelőzésére, a különböző élethelyzetekből eredő krízisek esetén történő támogatás nyújtásra. A Társaság 2018-ban vett részt először drogprevenciós programsorozat szervezésében, amely az Európai Unió finanszírozása által a "Drogmegelőzés határok nélkül”- NoDrugs név alatt futó projekt megvalósítása volt. A projekt a Szent Gellért Társaság és a Szórvány Alapítvány (Ro) partnerségében realizálódott, és lezárulását követően mind két szervezet szükségesnek látta, hogy az aktivitásait ezen a területen fejlessze, ezért pályázott négy partnerével erre a projektre.

<< Objectives >>

A Szent Gellért Társaság keretében a “NoDrugs" programnak köszönhetően önkéntes fiatal szakemberekből álló szakmai team jött létre. Az ERASMUS + program kezdeményezőjeként a szervezet fejleszteni kívánta a prevenciós tevékenységét és megalapozni ezen a területen való hosszútávú részvételét. A Társaság azzal a céllal és elkötelezettséggel kezdett el tevékenykedni a drogprevenció területén, hogy nem kioltani, “konkurenciát” csinálni kíván a jelen levő szervezeteknek és szolgáltatásoknak, hanem kiegészíteni és támogatni kívánja azokat, ezért az aktivitások szervezésekor és kivitelezésekor külön figyelmet fordít az innovációra, és a hasonló célú szervezetekkel való együttműködésre. A pályázatban résztvevő többi szervezet tevékenységének is részét képezik a fiatalokkal való interakció és a fiatalok mentális egészségének fejlesztése, de eddig kevesebb drogprevenciós aktivitásuk volt, viszont mind érzékelték a téma fontosságát, és a célcsoportjaik veszélyeztetettségét, ezért tartották fontosnak, hogy elmélyítsék a szervezet tagjainak drogprevencióval kapcsolatos tudását, átgondolják a szervezet drogprevenciós aktivitását és lehetőségeit és elkezdjék a regionális aktorokkal a kapcsolatfelvételt. 

<< Implementation >>

A projekt tevékenységei két nagy csoportra oszthatók:
1. Adminisztratív és szervezési feladatok;
2. Ifjúságsegítők bevonásával végzett tevékenységek.
    Adminisztratív és szervezési feladatok
1.1. Az első transznacionális találkozóra Szegeden került sor. A rendezvényen a partnerszervezetek előadást tartottak, bemutatták szervezeteiket, megvitatták korábbi munkáikat, tapasztalataikat, kérdéseket tettek fel egymásnak. A projektmenedzser team bemutatta az összes aktivitást és tevékenységet. Elfogadtuk a projekt munkatervét és a kockázatkezelési tervet.
1.2. A havi rendszerességű online találkozók lehetővé tették a különböző problémák megvitatását, a folyamatos projekt monitoringot. 
1.3. Transznacionális találkozó Eszéken (Horvátország)
A nemzetközi találkozó célja az volt, hogy lehetőséget teremtsen a partnerszervezetek számára felmerülő projekt menedzsment és szakmai kérdések megvitatására, fő hangsúlyt a tanulmány írás módszertanának lefektetésére helyeztünk valamint az egyes szakmai kérdésekre.
1.4. Zárókonferencia Salzburgban (Ausztria)
A  záró transznacionális találkozó mely egyben a projekt záró konferenciája is volt, célja a projekt lezárása és a közös tanulmány bemutatása. A partnerszervezetek aláírták az együttműködési nyilatkozatot, melyre alapozva tovább tudjuk a projekt eredményeit fejleszteni. 
2. Ifjúságsegítők bevonásával végzett tevékenységek
2.1. Kapcsolattartás és kommunikáció a regionális szervezetekkel és multiplikációs rendezvények szervezése
Az ifjúságsegítők összegyűjtötték és adatbázisban rendezték azokat a szakmai és nem szakmai szervezeteket, amelyeket releváns partnernek tekint a szakmai környezetben. 
A multiplikációs rendezvényeken célja a projekt ismertetése, népszerűsítése és  szervezetek közötti kapcsolatépítés volt.
Multiplikációs  rendezvények (Salzburg, Temesvár, Szabadka és Eszék)
2.2. Ifjúságsegítők képzése Szerbiában
Az ifjúságsegítők négynapos képzésén Szabadkán készségfejlesztést végeztek. Az ifjúságsegítő egyik lényeges feladata a megelőzés; korszerű drogprevenciós műhelyek szervezése a hátrányos helyzetű társadalmi csoportokhoz tartozó fiatalok számára. Ezért az oktatás (műhelyfoglalkozások) témái a szenvedélybetegség kialakulása, a fiatalok drogfogyasztási szokásai, a serdülőkor pszichológiája, a serdülőkori deviancia, az innovatív drogprevenció - kortárs támogatás, segítő módszerek (irodalomterápia, meseterápia, pszichodráma, támogató beszélgetés technikák stb.), az ellátórendszerek kompetenciája és bemutatása.
2.3. Ifjúsági segítők workshopjai
Országonként három önálló műhelymunkát készítettek az ifjúságsegítők. Feladatuk volt felvenni a kapcsolatot a célcsoporttal, megszervezni a workshop idejét és helyét. A foglalkozásokhoz műhelytervet és ütemtervet készítettek, amit egyeztettek a képzőkkel.  A foglalkozások után önreflexiókat írtak, melyeket az ifjúságsegítők szupervíziós értekezlete alatt dolgoztak fel. 
2.4. Az ifjúságsegítők szupervíziója
A fiatalokkal való munka magában foglalta a fiatalok mentorálását és irányítását, hogy fejlesszék lelki, testi, érzelmi, mentális és szociális készségeiket, hogy egészséges felnőtté váljanak. Az ifjúságsegítők felelősek ebben a fejlesztési folyamatban; ezért fontos, hogy segítsük őket egyéni és szakmai fejlődésükben. Az ifjúságsegítők is fiatal szakemberek. Sok kihívást jelent számukra a fiatalokkal való munka a gyakorlat hiánya, a tapasztalatlanság és egyéb nehézségek (például a korcsoport közelsége). A szupervízió lehetőséget biztosított a fiatal szakemberek számára, hogy megosszák szakmai tapasztalataikat, megbeszéljék félelmeiket és bizonytalanságukat, negatív érzéseiket és megtalálják a kompetenciahatáraikat.
Ennek a programnak a tartalma gyakorlati workshopok, pszichoszociális támogatás, kompetenciafejlesztés, kiégés megelőzés, kapacitásépítés, közösségfejlesztés, szakmai problémák megvitatása volt. 
A projekt során a következő aktivitásokat valósították meg a partner szervezetek:
A partner szervezetek szakmai kompetenciáinak fejlesztése a drogprevenció témakörében. Ennek az aktivitásnak a célja a tájékozódás és információgyűjtés volt. A pályázó szervezetek fontos célja, hogy hosszútávú prevenciós szolgáltatás kidolgozása, ezért fontos volt megismerkedni a regionális, országos és nemzetközi drogpolitikával. A szervezetek felkutatták saját országaik által képviselt drogpolitikát, megismerkedtek az Európai Unió által képviselt irányelvekkel és lehetőségük volt megvitatni, összehasonlítani más partner ország drogpolitikáját is. Tapasztalataikat nemzetközi tanulmány kötetben foglalták össze.
A partner szervezetek a projekt eredményességét feltérképező kérdőívben ezt az aktivitást nagyon hasznosnak vélték.
A partner szervezetek a projekt során létrejött új ismereteik alapján elkészítették saját akció terveiket, amelyben összegezték a szervezetek jövőképét és célkitűzéseit a droprevenció témakörében, mely része a nemzetközi tanulmánynak. Ez a folyamat a legtöbb szervezet esetében a vártnál is eredményesebbnek bizonyult.
Regionális és nemzetközi kapcsolatépítés: Kiemelt eleme volt a projektnek, hogy a szervezetek a lehető legtöbb regionális, országos drogprevenciós szervezettel és intézménnyel felvegyék a kapcsolatot, megismerjék azok munkáját és szolgáltatását, akikkel később együttműködve tovább fejlesszék a projekt eredményeit.
Multiplikációs eseményeket szerveztek és egy egységes adatbázis készítettek, amely tartalmazza azoknak a szervezeteknek a listáját, akik az adott régióban aktív szereplői a drog prevenciós aktivitásoknak, illetve olyan szervezetek szerepelnek az adatbázisban, akik potenciális partnerek hiszen aktivitásaikba bekapcsolható a partner szervezetek célcsoportja.
Ez fontos aktivitás volt a terület feltárási folyamatban. Az ifjúságsegítők elektronikus, telefonos és személyes megkeresésekkel kezdeményezték a potenciális partnerszervezetekkel való együttműködést. Egy űrlap kitöltését kérték a szervezeteket, amely alapján dokumentálták őket a partnerszervezetek között. A legtöbb szervezet nyitott volt az együttműködésre. Ennek ellenére az egyes országok (Magyarország, Szerbia, Horvátország) partnerszervezetei által megkeresett szervezetek többsége nem vállalta az űrlap kitöltését, így csak az online felületeken található információkra hagyatkozhattak. Egyes országok ifjúságsegítőitől kapott visszajelzések alapján ez a projektszakasz volt a legnehezebb (Magyarország, Szerbia). A partnerek visszajelzései alapján is ebben volt a projekt a legkevésbé hatékony, és ezen a ponton kell a továbbiakban még dolgozni. A projekt láthatóságának és népszerűsítésének sikeressége sem valósult meg annyira, mint amennyire szerették volna a szervezetek.
A partner szervezetek ERASMUS+ program keretében szerzet közös tapasztalatai. A partner szervezetek többségének már volt Uniós átlal finanszírozott projektje de nem ebben a programban és ebben a formában nem volt lehetőségük együtt dolgozni, ezért a partnerség is egy új kihívásokkal teli aktivitás volt, a szakmai mellett a  projekt managmentben szerzett új ismeretek tekintetében is. 
A partner szervezetek saját drogprevenciós aktivitása az ifjúság segítők tevékenységén keresztül hatékonyabbnak bizonyult, mint ahogy azt a partnerségben részt vett szervezetek a kezdetekben gondolták.
Az ifjúság segítőknek kulcsfontosságú szerepe volt a projektben, ezért fontos volt az ifjúság segítők képzése, ismereteik bővítése és munkájuk nyomon követése, tapasztalataik feldolgozása. Az ifjúság segítők feladata a fiatalok közötti folyamatos jelenlét és a fiatalok elakadásában a segítő beszélgetéssel való értő és figyelő támogatás nyújtása volt. Az ifjúság segítő a projekt során regionális és nemzetközi kapcsolati hálót épített ki, szakmai tapasztalatra tett szert és bővítették a tudásukat.  Az ifjúság segítőknek különböző korosztályú fiatalok számára, eltérő módszertanú, típusú drogprevenciós  műhelyfoglalkozások megszervezése, részvevők toborzása és lebonyolítása is fontos feladata volt. Az ifjúság segítő munkájával népszerűsítette a szervezetet és a programot.
A műhelyfoglalkozásokat a foglalkozáson részt vett fiatalok nagyon pozitívan értékelték és a partnerség is a projekt legerősebb elemeként tekintett az ifjúság segítőkkel kapcsolatos aktivitásokra és az általuk ralizált programokra.
6. A partnerek projekt implementálása közben szerzett új ismereteiket, a projekttel kapcsolatos tapasztalataikat egy nemzetközi tanulmány kötetbe összegezték, amely elsődleges célja volt a partnerség jövőképét és lehetőségeit, elhelyezni ahogyan a programot is a drogprevenciós lehetőségek palettáján. A nemzetközi tanulmány összegzi a partner szervezetek által képviselt országok drogpolitikáját és a szervezetek tapasztalatait és szakpolitikai véleményt is formál, amellett, hogy összegzi az egyes partnerek jövőképét.



<< Results >>

A projekt során összesen 11 főbb aktivitás keretében összesen 33 program valósult meg.
A projekt főbb aktivitásai és eredményei:
drb nemzetközi együttműködési szerződés, amelyet a projekt záró konferenciáján a partner szervezetek közösen írtak alá, amelyben kifejezik a jövőbeni együttműködési szándékukat a témában, a projekt eredményeire alapozva, ezzel is elősegítve a projekt hosszútávú hatásának fenntarthatóságát.
drb transznacionális találkozó, mely a projekt nyitó konferenciája is volt (10 résztvevő fő, plusz egy fő online), ahol a partner szervezeteknek a szerződéskötési folyamat után lehetőségük volt személyesen is találkozni (Szegeden). Ennek az eseménynek a célja a szakmai csapat megismerkedése, a partnerség és a szervezetek bemutatása, korábbi aktivitások megismerése. A szervezetek bemutatták egymásnak a szervezeteik profilját, célkitűzéseit a projektben, egyeztették a projekt során vállalt feladatokat, határidőket (gantt diagram ismertetése), kereteket, együttműködési szabályokat, és a projekt céljait összegezték, ezek alapján elfogadták a projekt munkatervét. Továbbá fontosnak találtuk, hogy a szervezetek közösen készítsék el a projekt SWOT analízisét és együtt gondolják végig azokat a kételyeket, veszélyeket, gyengeségeket, esetleg félelmeket, lehetőségeket és erőforrásokat amelyeket a projektben látnak, amelyet felhasználva a projekt implementálás zökkenőmentesebbé válhatott, és részévé vált a kockázatkezelési tervnek.
drb nemzetközi partner találkozó a projekt félidejében (Eszék), amely egyúttal lehetőséget teremtett a szervezetek számára a projekt realizálása során felmerülő nehézségek megvitatására és tapasztalatok cseréjére, másrészt pedig jó gyakorlatok megismerésére is lehetőséget biztosított (13 részvevő fő).
drb záró konferencia (15 résztvevő fő), (Salzburg) ahol bemutatásra került a teljes projekt aktivitás, a valamint az elkészült nemzetközi tanulmány, amellett, hogy aláírásra került a jövőbeni együttműködést szabályozó szerződés. 
1. drb nemzetközi tanulmány, amely magába foglalja az adott ország és az unió prevenciós politikáját, a kapcsolati hálózatot, a szervezetek közös jövőbeli céljait a drogperevenció területén.
15. drb online partner találkozó, amely biztosította a havonta egyszeri kommunikációt a partner szervezetek között és lehetőséget biztosított a projekt lebonyolításával kapcsolatos problémák megvitatására. Minden megbeszélésen a partnerek projekt koordinátora vett részt.
drb szakmai képzés  Szabadkán (15 résztvevő fő), amelyen a partner szervezetek ifjúság segítőt képezték szakemberek. A képzés célja volt, hogy a segítő szakmát tanuló vagy pályakezdő fiatalok szakemberek szakmai kompetenciáit és drogprevenciós ismereteit bővítsük, egységes szintre emeljük. A képzés a drogprevenció minden színterével, a függőség kialakulásának okaival, a függőség formáival és a segítő beszélgetés, az asszertív kommunikáció és műhelyvezetés technikáival foglalkozott.
Szervezetenként 3 műhely lebonyolítása (15 darab - műhelyenként átlagosan 15 fő), amelyet a képzésben részt vett ifjúságsegítők szerveztek, terveztek és vezettek. A műhely vezetéseiket az ifjúságsegítők önreflexióba foglalták, amely segítette az élmény feldolgozást és a szakmai tapasztalat megvitatását a szupervíziós eseményen. 
1. drb. szupervíziós esemény (Temesvár) az ifjúságsegítők számára, amely lehetőséget adott a fiatal szakemberek számára, hogy feldolgozzák, megvitassák és elemezzék az általuk megtartott műhelyeket és lehetőséget kapjanak, hogy a további munkájuk javítása érdekében, felhasználják a szupervizó során szerzett szaktudást. 
5 drb. Helyi/regionális/szervezeti akcióterv kidolgozása, amely legfőbb célja, hogy a partner szervezetek megismerjék a regionális és a nemzetközi droghelyzetet, drogpolitikát és a drog prevencióval foglalkozó szervezetek aktivitását, ezt követően megpróbálják felvázolni saját szervezetüket és annak lehetőségeit, prevenciós tevékenységének jövőképét.
4 drb. Multiplikációs esemény, ahol lehetőség volt a partner szervezeteknek ismertetni a projektet és felvenni a kapcsolatot más drogprevenció területén tevékenykedő szervezettel.
1. drb. egységes szervezeti adatbázis létrehozása, amely tartalmazza azoknak a szervezeteknek a listáját, akik az adott régióban aktív szereplői a drog prevenciós aktivitásoknak, illetve olyan szervezetek szerepelnek az adatbázisban, akik potenciális partnerek hiszen aktivitásaikba bekapcsolható a partner szervezetek célcsoportja.

2021-2-NL02-KA220-YOU-000051021.title: Anne Frank Youth Network – Remembrance & Action for Equal Rights
2021-2-NL02-KA220-YOU-000051021.summary:
<< Background >>

The AFH, Krzyzowa and HERMES applied for the Erasmus+ K2 grant to answer the needs of the existing international youth network, Anne Frank Youth Network, by tackling post-pandemic challenges and redeveloping outdated educational materials.  
In 2021, a year and a half into the pandemic, prolonged uncertainty brought diverse challenges. This period was mostly spent online – working, learning, and facing an onslaught of negative news, some classifiable as conspiracy theories or disinformation. The imposed social distancing and self-isolation amplified pre-existing societal issues. In many cases, youth became disillusioned with democracy, with a decline in participation driven by a loss of faith in the system. 
In recent years, various threats to European values created tensions across Europe. These included challenges with integrating newcomers, growing nationalism, increasing polarization and a questioning of European cohesion, identity and future. 
The mission of the partner organizations mission became especially pressing with the rise of antisemitic incidents and Holocaust denial. We recognize the importance of Holocaust education for youth and its direct impact in behavior and understanding of different forms of discrimination.

<< Objectives >>

The AFYN (RE)ACT cooperation's objectives are:  
a) Expanding young people's understanding of the Holocaust and developing innovative ways to foster remembrance amid the declining of knowledge and engagement about the Holocaust and issues related to it. 
b) Improving the skills of youth with prior experience as peer educators by increasing their international competences turning network members into youth leaders. 
c) Developing innovative educational materials and activities that increase the ability of youth, their schools and communities to engage in prevention as well as educational and awareness-raising responses to various forms of discrimination. 
d) Strengthening the quality and relevance of AFYN and its activities across Europe by consolidating its past successes and the evolution of its materials to promote youth civic engagement. 
e) Partner organizations learning from each other's experiences and perspectives, fostering European exchange. 
The partnership is meant to promote non-formal education that generates a collaborative, inclusive, youth-led and action-oriented learning space to address various forms of discrimination, polarization, and the disenfranchisement of various ethnic, sexual, and religious groups 

<< Implementation >>

The project's cooperation partnership implemented the following activities:  

A. TRANSNATIONAL PROJECT MEETINGS  
1. In “AFYN (RE)ACT Kick-Off Meeting”, the partners formulated their cooperation's fundamental guidelines and processes (communication, timeline, general frame for production of different project results, the utilization of each partner’s networks, project management, reporting, monitoring and evaluation, quality assurance mechanisms).  
2. In “AFYN (RE)ACT Materials Draft Review Meeting”, partners conducted a peer review of the draft versions of produced project results to ensure the materials’ quality.  
3. In “AFYN (RE)ACT Materials Finalization & Multipliers Events Planning Meeting”, partners provided near-ready drafts of their project results. This meeting’s focus was the fine-tuning and final edits of the materials, enhancement of inclusion and multiperspectivity elements, cross-national and intercultural adaptations. During this meeting, partners also made clear plans for the dissemination of project results, especially drafting the plans and programs of different multiplier events and partner cooperation and participation therein.  
4. In “AFYN (RE)ACT Project Evaluation & Sustainability Meeting”, following the conclusion of all the multiplier events, the partners gathered to compare the evaluation and dissemination results of the AFYN (RE)ACT project. They also conducted introspective and reflective analyses of the cooperative partnership, explored opportunities for further cooperation, and outlined AFYN (RE)ACT project's follow-up and sustainability action steps within each organization’s purview and networks.  
 
B) PRODUCTION OF PROJECT RESULTS, i.e. different sets of mutually reinforcing and complementary materials that will strengthen and advance AFYN's mission and activities through enhancing its digital, educational and structural infrastructure:  
1. AFYN website  
2. AFYN digital platform  
3. AFYN Digital Resources Collection  
4. AFYN Digital Engagement Strategy  
5. AFYN Toolkit 2.0  
6. AFYN Activities Set for Civic Youth Engagement  
7. AFYN Follow-Up Activities Framework  
8. AFYN Outreach Guide  
9. AFYN Facilitators' Handbook  
10. AFYN International Youth Forum Organizers' Manual  
11. AFYN MERL Policies and Tools  
12. AFYN Safeguarding Standards  
13. AFYN Long-term Sustainability Strategy  

C) MULTIPLIER EVENTS & LEARNING ACTIVITIES: Multiplier events each that brought together 25 youths from 4 countries for 2–3-day project-results dissemination events:  
1. AFYN (RE)ACT NL Youth Forum '23  
2. AFYN (RE)ACT PL Youth Forum '23  
3. AFYN (RE)ACT CRO Youth Forum '23
4. AFYN International Youth Forum '24 (learning-teaching-training activity bringing 50 youths from 12 countries from throughout Europe for a 5-day training event) 
Multiplier events that took place online, each bringing together 25 youths from various European countries for a full-day online training using project results:  
5. AFYN (RE)ACT Digital Forum - Digital Engagement  
6. AFYN (RE)ACT Digital Forum - Historical Human Rights Education  
7. AFYN (RE)ACT Digital Forum - Civic Engagement  

<< Results >>

The AFYN (RE)ACT project set up a structure for upscaling existing tools and materials for AFYN by funding the development of 13 concrete project results (listed above), as well as implementing various multiplier events for youth exchange input and feedback. In developing the concrete project results and events, the project paved the way for the development of additional valuable outcomes (all necessary components of the project results and events) including a new visual identity, solidified definitions and policies for AFYN, as well as welcoming new AFYN members. Outcomes for the AFYN (RE)ACT project can be seen at the youth, partner organization and AFYN levels: 

At YOUTH level: 
90 youths participated in multiplier events + 50 youths participated in the learning-training activities, as new AFYN members, who each organized an estimated 3 peer education follow-up activities. The project results (educational materials, tools) have reached ~6,300 youths. An additional 1,500 youths were reached through various digital engagement activities (digital multiplier events, social media campaigns, etc.) New AFYN members have:  
1. Improved knowledge about the Holocaust; 
 2. Increased awareness about the various forms in which antisemitism expresses itself in modern society; 
 3. Increased resilience in addressing the issues of antisemitism, racism, xenophobia, discrimination, and other forms of intolerance such as hate speech; 
 4. Enhanced critical thinking and self-reliance skills when it comes to considering own personal responsibility in making a positive contribution to society, especially in the face of various dangers challenging peace, European values and cohesion; 
 5. Deeper understanding and higher levels of active citizenship and community involvement as evidenced through AFYN youth participation in volunteering, activism, social movements, public interest advocacy campaigns; 
 6. Gained new competences and tools to counter and address manifestations of racism, antisemitism, xenophobia and other forms of intolerance; 
 7. Gained the necessary competences to collaborate with young peer educators around ‘understanding, respect and dialogue’ in school contexts; 
 8. Learned how to mentor, collaborate with and support young people who launch social media campaigns/outreach educational activities; 
 9. Learned how to create and foster an ‘atmosphere of active dialogue and understanding’ in the schools; 
 10. (youth participating in peer-education activities) - Increased inspiration by the youth positive role-modeling of active citizenship. This overall increased awareness and sensitivity towards the problems of antisemitism, racism, xenophobia, and other forms of intolerance in society were fostered in youth primarily through two modes: their direct involvement in their own educational process (where they co-designed their learning experiences, as well as took charge in passing on knowledge to their peers) and the innovative approaches to Holocaust education. 
11. Exchanged and learned new perspectives from other European youth peers, fostering an inclusive European identity among them. 

At PARTNER ORGANIZATION level: 
Each partner organization worked with 3 young people actively participating in the project as active members and/or interns/junior staff. Owing to the emphasis on building both digital and structural infrastructure, as well as systematization and standardization of quality assurance mechanisms, partner organizations have improved their own youth work standards and practices during the AFYN (RE)ACT duration. They now have enriched toolboxes of innovative methods, approaches and pedagogies in addressing these complex issues through (non-formal) education as well as strengthened expertise in using webinars and social media as educational instruments.  

At ANNE FRANK YOUTH NETWORK level: 
 The Anne Frank Youth Network overall, as result of this KA2 project, has: 
1. A consolidated legacy of past successes, in the form of 
 a. Newly created digital infrastructure (website & digital platform); 
 b. Updated educational materials and tools (revised and improved existing materials and tools + newly created educational tools and materials in historical human rights education and youth engagement domains); 
 2. A strengthened partnership coalition, with a new model of sustainable functioning, enhanced through 
 a. New digital infrastructure; 
 b. Regional hubs activities; 
 c. Newly created MERL mechanisms and tools. 
 d. Long-term strategy
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2021-2-PL01-KA220-YOU-000050273.title: New Global Learning - Youth Workers as Global Learning Facilitators
2021-2-PL01-KA220-YOU-000050273.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to support youth workers and youth organizations in facilitating learning and informed discussion about complex global issues, thereby inspiring active citizenship. Young people which advocate for crucial issues like sustainability and human rights often face barriers from fake news and echo chambers. They need high quality of education on those topics provided by youth workers. We applied for this project to create high quality educational materials - e-learning platform and educational materials which give knowledge on those four pivotal topics, which are in the area of interest of young people. 
Because all of these topics fall under the umbrella of global learning, we created this educational tool and pursued other project activities which were aimed to promote this concept among youth workers and give them possibility to increase their knowledge and gain skills crucial for teaching about them. 
Through this project, the organizations in this partnership have increased the quality of their programs and the support they offer to youth workers, attracting and retaining more youth workers. As a result, youth workers have received enhanced training and tools tailored to their specific needs. 

<< Objectives >>

The goal achieved by project is the increade level of support of  youth workers and youth organizations in delivering meaningful global learning across the EU. Thanks to creating innovate educational tool - e-learning platfom and educational materials - the possibilities of target group to deliver high quality of education has increased. We utilized the combined knowledge of three participating organizations FPD, ADK and IDEA to teach about four pivotal topic areas of the project, captured in the form of teaching based on debating methodology. 
We supported the youth workers and learning of people who were direct participants of the project and also the people reached within our network. We involved youth workers and members of youth clubs who were presented with the project results. Over all activities - both working and creating and testing project results and realising project activities we were promoting an idea of global learning and teaching about debating methodology. 
The main goal which is achieved is creating a digital educational space, which provides the high quality educational materials for the youth workers, members of youth clubs and other participants  involved in the activities conducted by our organizations. 

<< Implementation >>

Main activities implemented:
1. Creating all three declared results: 
R1: Training modules for youth workers and trainers
R2: Youth worker toolkit on approaching contemporary issues
R3: E-learning platform for individuals and groups
2. The developed materials reached while testing around 51youth clubs. The workshops was conducted by 
- Polska Debatuje reached in total 7 youth clubs while testing 
- IDEA reached directly 6 youth clubs - also worth to mention that while testing R2 - the testing sessions was conducted for Junior WSDC Dutch team - there are 5 members of it - which are at the same time members of their local youth clubs - it increased the indirect impact, thanks to sharing the knowledge from this project to local clubs 
- ADK reached - ADK thanks to their structure managed to reach 42 youth clubs - throught the youthworkers who participated in testing process - this advantage of ADK helped as to strongly boost up the dissemination and reach of the project.

2021-2-PT02-KA220-YOU-000051037.title: UNISON
2021-2-PT02-KA220-YOU-000051037.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the urgent need in equipping youth with essential knowledge about art and cultural heritage. Our goal is to prepare emerging artists beyond mere performance for the diverse demands of today's musical and theatrical scene. This project aims to instill in students a sense of responsible behavior in the arts, covering aspects like access, communication, and understanding rights. In today's digital age, where much interaction occurs online, there's a crucial need to reignite young people's motivation for intercultural awareness and arts engagement. By collaborating with partners, we aim to create a multicultural environment where young artists gain practical insights into global practices in music, art, and drama. This collaboration with educational and cultural institutions promises to enhance education quality and mutual understanding, while also providing new opportunities for artists, locally and internationally. In summary, our application seeks to educate youth about art and cultural heritage, promote intercultural awareness, and offer practical training in a rapidly changing digital and multicultural world.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, our primary aim was to achieve several overarching objectives aligned with UNISON's values and the program's general objectives, like Equal Opportunities for Emerging Artists; Building New Audiences; Circulation of Operators and Works; Increasing Cultural Participation; Promoting Social Resilience and Inclusion; Generating Jobs and Growth; Strengthening European Identity and Values; Capacity Building for International Engagement. The impact of the project was multiple, like Creating interactive and cohesive learning environments where students feel empowered and responsible for their learning; Facilitating European cooperation, and the exchange of best practices among educators; Supporting schools in addressing challenges such as early school leaving and disadvantage; Enhancing proficiency in English language and ICT skills among participants, thereby improving their employability and adaptability in a globalized world; Overall, the project aims to leave a lasting impact by empowering emerging artists, fostering cultural exchange, promoting inclusivity, and contributing to the growth and resilience of the cultural sector.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented various activities to achieve its objectives: Three transnational meetings were organized to facilitate collaboration and planning among project partners. Four LTTAs were conducted to bring together students and trainers for collaborative work on project topics. Activities included co-creation sessions, artist training, performances, theatre workshops, symposiums, and educational techniques exploration. Participants were actively involved in activities rather than being passive spectators, enhancing the learning experience. The "flipped classroom" method was employed, with participants receiving materials for self-study before exchanges to deepen their understanding of topics.  Each exchange lasted five days and focused on specific themes such as opera, artist training, performances, theatre workshops, drama techniques, and musical performances.
The project targeted young artists aged 15 to 25, as well as trainers in music, art, literature, and foreign languages. Participants came from various educational backgrounds and levels of performance, including disadvantaged groups facing social and economic challenges or learning difficulties.
 The participants produced various project products including exhibitions, multimedia/video presentations, films, mind-maps on cultural heritage, interviews booklet, artistic portfolios, and documentation on the learning platform.
The trainers oversaw all project phases, from planning to product delivery and guided throughout. They communicated and collaborated with colleagues to ensure the project's success and effectiveness.
Overall, the project utilized a range of activities and strategies to engage participants, foster collaboration, and achieve its goals of enhancing cultural understanding and artistic skills development.


<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results of our project encompass a variety of outcomes like increased Awareness of Cultural Heritage through activities such as research on traditions and educational models; Enhance Collaboration Among Students by fostering collaboration and teamwork in project activities; Boost Intercultural Awareness through the exploration and celebration of cultural traditions from partner countries. Utilization of Modern Learning Methods Participants were exposed to modern techniques to improve classroom engagement, attention, and curiosity, enhancing the learning experience. Elevate Motivation Levels by providing engaging and meaningful learning opportunities. Improved Student-Teacher/Trainer Relationship through collaborative work and mutual respect; Development of Educational Practices, the project contributed to the development of curricular and extra-curricular education practices integrating historical heritage into the curriculum; Access to New Trainer Networks the participants gained access to a new network of trainers across Europe, fostering the exchange of ideas, training methods, and problem-solving strategies. Creation of Presentations and Reports, various materials were created for assessment and dissemination purposes. International Symposium and European Festival event were organized to showcase cultural diversity and artistic talent. Research on traditions, training for emerging artists, performances inspired by culture, and the creation of a multifunctional platform (https://unisonproject.info) for presenting cultural heritage and promoting emerging artists' popularity was achieved. Overall, the project successfully produced tangible outputs, facilitated knowledge exchange, and promoted cultural understanding and artistic development among participants.

2021-2-SI02-KA220-YOU-000048089.title: Ustavimo osamljenost, pričnimo prostovoljiti!
2021-2-SI02-KA220-YOU-000048089.summary:
<< Background >>

The project represents a response to the growing hardship among youth, resulting from isolation and loneliness, particularly visible during and after the Covid-19 pandemic. The partners' own experience as well as national-level research had demonstrated the potential positive impact of volunteering. All partners are active in the field of inclusive volunteering, youth volunteering and work with youth with fewer opportunities. We wanted to pay more attention to youth, especially as young people were expected to provide solidarity and sacrifice during the pandemic to the benefit of the vulnerable, while their hardship and eventual consequences in years to come were largely ignored. The situation was worse for those who do not have a safe home environment and whose economic status had worsened due to the pandemic.
The project addressed the needs of youth facing the consequences of the increase in loneliness and social isolation, particularly volunteering and youth organisations that are accessible to youth and can thus provide adequate support through volunteering activities. Additionally, an initiative to implement systemic support for volunteering as a means to alleviate loneliness amongst youth was addressed to the policy makers.

<< Objectives >>

Our project aimed to reach the following goals:
- raise awareness on the significance of volunteering in tackling social isolation amongst youth;
- support the work of youth and volunteering organisations to involve young volunteers;
- recognise and select innovative, effective, and transferable practices:
- provide organisations all over EU with information on best practices and opportunities within volunteering;
- identify the needs of youth to start volunteering and their needs for volunteer assistance;
- develop a methodology for establishment of volunteering programmes and participatory approaches, and mentoring standards for working with lonely youth;
- empower national and regional volunteering centres and networks to offer support to NGOs in the field of loneliness;
- gain better understanding of volunteering as an opportunity for personal growth, development, acquiring competencies, professional development and strengthening social networks amongst young people;
- actively advocate for youth volunteering and volunteering assistance for young people on all levels;
- raise awareness on needs of youth and opportunities to adopt measures encouraging systemic development of volunteering and its infrastructure.


<< Implementation >>

Project activities:
1. research of practices in youth volunteering to tackle loneliness, isolation and exclusion in several countries, presented in an e-publication;
2. we identified best practices that are transferable, interviewed young volunteers, beneficiaries and their mentors; findings presented in an on-line publication;
3. Voice of Youth on-line campaign, identifying challenges and needs of the youth with the input of youth, youth workers, policy makers and others;
4. we researched the role of volunteering centres and networks in combatting youth loneliness; proposals for future inclusive practices to benefit youth; the findings were presented in an on-line presentation.
5. handbook for volunteering organisations aiming to improve identification of loneliness amongst youth and provide tools to respond to it through volunteering;
6. policy recommendations pertaining to youth loneliness, isolation and social exclusion;
7. 6 TPM, taking advantage of the travel to participate in events and visit relevant organisations in the partner countries;
8. 4 multiplier events for international audiences;
9. dissemination of results on web pages, social networks, newsletters and in the scope of regular activities of partner organisations

<< Results >>

Project results and deliverables:
R1: Research and analysis of CSO challenges and responses in e-form;
R2: Best practices compendium, in e-form; including a video of statements;
R3: On-line campaign Voice of the Youth based on world-cafe findings;
R4: Building bridges to volunteer communities – guidelines for volunteering centres and networks; in e-form
R5: Understanding and addressing loneliness among young people: handbook for volunteering organisations and volunteer mentors, including key findings pf R1, R3, R4 and R6; in e-form and in print;
R6: Policy recommendations for policy makers on EU and national levels; in e-form.

2021-2-SI02-KA220-YOU-000048355.title: Nomadland: digitalni nomadi - priložnost za evropsko podeželje
2021-2-SI02-KA220-YOU-000048355.summary:
<< Background >>

The European countryside is facing the challenge of youth emigration, which is a consequence of a lack of employment and educational opportunities. However, especially after the COVID crisis, a new trend is emerging: remote work. Thus, on a global scale, the number of younger digital nomads, who are rediscovering the countryside, is increasing. Digital nomadism can be a positive example for the countryside, as it contributes to the immigration of young people to the countryside in a short term. In fact, 42% of digital nomads are aged between 25 and 42 years. New solutions are also needed for youth work in the countryside. Youth work is often associated with urban areas, whereas the countryside requires different solutions – interdisciplinary and inclusive. The project was related to the European Youth Goals, especially the sixth goal, A Step Forward for Rural Youth, which highlights a positive image of the countryside and more opportunities for young people.

<< Objectives >>

Within the framework of the project, Id20 Institute was joined by the ATPERSON (Spain), INI-Novation (Germany), and Udruga Prizma (Croatia). All partners operate in the areas facing youth outmigration. Throughout the project, we explored the field of digital nomadism and identified to what extent it can be linked to the field of youth work in the countryside. By reviewing good practices, we found out positive examples in Europe that can serve as a model for other areas. We believe that the countryside is suitable not only for retaining young people but also for attracting digital nomads (and other urban residents). In the project, we particularly wanted to highlight the regions in which we primarily operate – Idrija, Cuenca, Bergstrasse-Odenwald, Iž, and Gračac. The project focused on the stories of young people, as they are the ones who connect and make a place interesting for living. 

<< Implementation >>

Within the framework of the project, we:
-	conducted research on how digital nomadism can positively impact the development of youth and the quality of youth work in rural and peripheral areas. We presented our work in a special magazine, Nomadland;
-	created a guide, Beyond the City Lights, which assists youth workers, decision-makers, and others in attracting digital nomads;
-	developed the Nomadland platform, where the countryside is showcased through the stories of young people and digital nomads in rural areas;
-	organized 4 local and 1 pan-European event for youth workers, where we developed more than 20 solutions to attract digital nomads to the countryside in connection with youth work and brought together young people, decision-makers, and youth workers to create new ideas for the local community;
-	prepared the first strategy for attracting digital nomads to the countryside, with a special emphasis on youth work;
-	organized training for youth workers, which connected and united 20 youth workers from across Europe.
The Nomadland project, in addition to providing new solutions for youth work in the countryside, also highlighted young people who, with digital nomads, gained new opportunities in the local environment.

<< Results >>

Within the framework of the project, we developed:
-	Nomazine (IO1), a magazine featuring 21 good practices, 12 interviews with digital nomads, and a survey of digital nomads.
-	Beyond the City Lights guide (IO2), a unique guide for establishing retreats in the countryside, offering valuable information for financing such retreats and the first strategy for attracting digital nomads to the countryside in the field of youth work.
-	The Nomadland platform (IO3), serving as an entry point for young people (digital nomads) seeking life and opportunities in the countryside.
-	Events (E1-E4) through which we pilot tested our work in 5 project areas, discovered more than 20 ideas in the local environment, and empowered young people in finding solutions.
-	An online webinar (E5), through which we introduced the project to over 50 youth workers across Europe, uncovering new opportunities for the development of youth work in the countryside.
-	A strong dissemination, reaching a broad target group in the fields of youth work, rural development, digital nomadism, and even tourism.
topics: Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas
Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas

2021-2-SK02-KA220-YOU-000050550.title: Virtuálna realita ako podpora ochrany pred vyhorením cez neformálne vzdelávanie
2021-2-SK02-KA220-YOU-000050550.summary:
<< Background >>

With the project, we solved needs that were focused on specific problems:1/young people do not have the psychological resistance to the burden and the problems that have arisen 2/Youth workers lack methodological support in leading and educating young leaders 3/Youth workers lack modern technologies that provide them with better support and guidance of young leaders.
The project was based on our experience as well as that of others who work with youth and volunteers. In the research report on the motivational factors of young people-volunteers, we subsequently found that after their initial enthusiasm, they often feel fear during their activities after a certain period of time, leading to stress leading to burnout and leaving the activity.  The activities of volunteers set in this way affect their mental health. Preventive activities to prevent this are absent in their support. This fact of youth burnout was confirmed by OECD statistics and the Cleveland Clinic. All this led us to create a support system using modern technologies for youth workers, which will have a preventive effect on young people so that they do not get into a state of burnout. The implementation of virtual reality into education will serve this purpose as well

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we were focused on the following goals:
1/ Improve the quality of non-formal education by introducing the method of using virtual reality. 
2/ Increase methodical support of youth workers for work with young leaders from various groups. 
3/ To support the implementation of educational blocks with the application of virtual reality in education when working with youth. 
The project followed the Erasmus + priority for youth: increasing digitization, strengthening education with digital tools of virtual reality.
With the project, we wanted to achieve support for the mental health of young people, their resistance to stress, and to create modern technological tools that will be applied in the non-formal education of youth.


<< Implementation >>

The activities implemented in the project were:
1/ Creation of a set of simulation activities in virtual reality aimed at preventing stress and burnout when working with youth with case studies. Part of this activity was a survey aimed at revealing the most used and requested ways and techniques of burnout prevention. And the case studies that formed the basis of the virtual environment.
2/ Creation of a methodology for non-formal education of youth workers with a focus on preventing stress and burnout among young leaders using virtual reality simulation activities. 
This activity was complemented by the pilot training for youth workers, where the created methodology was verified.
3/ Creation of a Manual for youth workers on how to implement educational blocks, i.e. a methodology with virtual reality simulation activities for working with young leaders.
The prepared outputs from these activities were presented at the international multiplication event - Conference for youth workers "Burnout out".
Dissemination activities and transnational project meetings of the project teams of partner organizations were part of the activities. 
All activities were managed through the Management and implementation.


<< Results >>

The results and outputs of the project are:
1/ Output: A set of simulation activities in virtual reality aimed at preventing stress and burnout when working with youth with case studies. Created application for virtual reality called "VR odolnosť (VR resilient)" can be downloaded to virtual reality glasses Oculus Quest 2 or similar glasses. 
Result: Users of a set of virtual reality simulation activities gained a new method in working with youth.
2/ Output: Methodology of non-formal education of youth workers aimed at preventing stress and burnout among young leaders using virtual reality simulation activities.
Result: Youth workers using the methodology acquired the competencies necessary for training young leaders to prevent burnout. 
3/ Output: Manual for youth workers on how to implement educational blocks, methodology with virtual reality simulation activities for working with young leaders. 
Result: Users of the manual received practical information on how to work with the methodology and the virtual reality incorporated in it.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
Quality and innovation of youth work

2022-1-AT01-KA220-YOU-000086358.title: Greening Financial Literacy
2022-1-AT01-KA220-YOU-000086358.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the lack of Green Financial Literacy (GFL) among young people. Despite EU and OECD efforts, the link between finance and climate change was missing in education. When covered, it was often superficial and shaped by financial sector actors rather than independent civil society organizations. Additionally, non-formal educational opportunities were scarce, leaving youth without tools to understand and advocate for sustainable finance.

The project tackled these gaps by developing educational materials and training young people as peer educators. It empowered them to spread knowledge on sustainable finance and take action. By integrating non-formal learning, it filled a major gap in youth engagement, equipping participants with financial and project management skills to advocate for GFL independently.

Through collaboration between civil society organizations in finance, environmental protection, and youth work, the project strengthened capacities and created accessible, action-oriented financial education.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to address the lack of Green Financial Literacy among young people by creating innovative educational approaches and fostering collaboration between civil society organizations in finance, environmental protection, and youth work.

1: Building partnerships on GFL – Strengthening cooperation between organizations to exchange knowledge and best practices, establishing a network to promote GFL across Europe.
2: Developing new educational practices – Creating and testing informal education formats, including a train-the-trainer program, to build partner capacities and ensure sustainable GFL education.
3: Empowering youth as active citizens – Engaging young people as peer educators to promote GFL, equipping them with essential knowledge and the ability to implement initiatives independently.
4: Expanding GFL awareness beyond partner countries – Sharing results across Europe through digital learning events, a toolkit, and multiplier activities, supporting the EU’s climate goals.

By integrating GFL into youth education, the project enhanced innovation in youth work, promoted active citizenship, and contributed to climate action in line with EU priorities.


<< Implementation >>

WP2: Learning Phase
A digital learning assessment (A1) identified knowledge gaps among partners to tailor the training. In digital learning events (A2), each partner hosted two half-day webinars on GFL, sharing expertise and producing supporting materials. These insights were compiled into a booklet (A3), providing a structured knowledge base for further activities.

WP3: Creating Phase
A workshop conception Hub in Greece (A1) set the basis for the workshop concept. Afterwards the workshop and training materiels were developed and adapted to local contexts (A2) A train-the-trainer format was created (A3), enabling young people to become peer educators. These concepts were tested and evaluated (A4), ensuring practical relevance. Activation methods to engage youth were collected, conducted, tested and evaluated (A5, A6). The results were compiled into a toolkit (A7) for broader dissemination.

WP4: Outreach Phase
An Outreach Conception Hub (A1) in Croatia coordinated dissemination and network-building. Multiplier events (A2–A6) were held in each partner country and transnationally, engaging youth sector stakeholders to promote GFL, demonstrate project results, expand networks, and increase recognition of the materials.

<< Results >>

WP2: The digital learning assessment facilitated stronger partner relationship. A total of 8 digital learning events were held, including webinars and online workshops. Each partner hosted 2 events.  Accompanying materials were produced for every event. Partners also enhanced their digital capacities. A comprehensive booklet was created in English, compiling insights from the digital learning events. It was translated in partner languages.
WP3: A workshop concept and a train-the-trainer format  were developed and adapted to local contexts. Training materials such as working papers and slides were created. A set of activating methods was developed to engage youth on GFL. A toolkit was produced in English, compiling all the outcomes, methods, and evaluation results from WP3. It was translated into all partner languages. In total 56 Peer Educators were trained and 507 young people participated in workshops. 
WP4: A partner meeting in Croatia conceptualized the outreach phase. In total 123 stakeholders attended national Multiplier events, 46 the international event online.
topics: Economic and financial affairs (including funding issues)

2022-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000085897.title: "Prevention of youth radicalisation through education and empowerment of youth workers"
2022-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000085897.summary:
<< Background >>

Young people are particularly susceptible to radicalisation and violent extremism, especially through online content, due to their extensive use of digital tools and platforms. At this critical stage in their development, they are building their identities, learning new skills, and forming their perspectives on the world. Exposure to violent or hate-driven content during this formative time poses significant risks.

Recognising the challenges young people face in their communities and the digital landscape, the project partners analysed the current educational and interaction opportunities available. This analysis led them to collaborate on solutions that address these risks. The partners understand the long-term harm radicalisation can cause if left unchecked and are committed to providing proactive prevention measures.

Through this project, we developed resources designed to support youth workers and educate young people. These tools aim to prevent radicalisation while promoting social inclusion and unity across Europe.



<< Objectives >>

Aim:
Developing and strengthening capacities of youth workers and youngsters in preventing and combating radicalisation through development of educational methodologies and tools that support online and offline anti-radicalisation youth work.

Specific objectives:
•	Raising awareness on negative impacts of radicalisation and educating young people (mainstream and marginalised) on anti-radicalisation through the development of inspiring handbook, toolkit, as well as the e-learning platform.
•	Empowering youth workers and improving knowledge management of our organisations in theory and practice for building competences of youth workers in prevention and combating radicalisation through the development of innovative curriculum and the e-learning course.
•	Exchange good practices and further develop effective partnership among partners from 6 European countries (and beyond) with different realities regarding education, awareness and practices on anti-radicalisation and its prevention among the community.


<< Implementation >>

-	partnership meetings in (2 in-person meetings in Croatia and Italy and 16 online meetings)
-	Intellectual outputs: O1 Handbook, O2 Toolkit and O5 e-Learning platform for empowerment of youngsters in active citizenship and advocacy for prevention and combating anti-radicalisation; O3 Curriculum and O4 Online course for raising competences of youth workers and youth peer leaders in the topic, all translated in 
-	1 mutual training of trainers
-	6 local trainings of trainers
-	4 national multiplier events
-	2 international multiplier events
-	additional dissemination activities within the larger networks and platforms of ours, as well as additional meetings with policymakers and local municipality offices for youth


<< Results >>

•	Handbook on preventing and combating radicalisation among youngsters in Europe; in 7 languages.
•	Toolkit for empowering youngsters on advocacy for anti-radicalisation: Consists of theoretical guidance and 12 workshops to empower young people; in 7 languages.
•	The pilot phase involved more than 60 young people and 18 youth workers from partner organisations across all regions.
•	Curriculum "Empowering youth workers for NFE for prevention and combating radicalisation among youth"; in 7 languages.
•	E-Learning Course aimed at training youth workers and peer leaders, providing accessible, flexible learning in anti-radicalisation; in 7 languages.
•	E-Learning Platform; with resources to facilitate interactive learning and collaboration.
•	Training of Trainers (Greece) for 16 youth workers to become trainers and multipliers in their local communities.
•	6 Local Training Courses reaching 53 youth workers across 6 countries to promote further education in their communities.
•	Multiplier Events: National conferences in Croatia, Italy, Serbia and Greece, reaching 92 participants; International conferences: in Belgium and Germany, with 63 participants from across Europe.

2022-1-FI01-KA220-YOU-000087520.title: PROACTIVE ECOLAND
2022-1-FI01-KA220-YOU-000087520.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to project as we wanted to create an educational game/exercise that concretely supports participants in gaining awareness for climate change and competence building towards environmental sustainability.  Results also support participants in transferring the achieved learnings into concrete actions in their communities.
The educational methodology used provides a straightforward link to the implementation of activities at a local level, and encourages all relevant stakeholders to support a ‘earn by doing, “motivating others through actions and leading by example approaches.
The online platform created serves as an additional space for inspiration, action taking peer-support, sharing good practice and networking. Additionally, all educational materials can be downloaded from here: https://proactive-ecoland.com
The project outputs create young people & youth workers empowerment to conceptualise and share innovative ideas and actionable solutions, facilitating their translation into community-based initiatives. This approach aligns with core principles of youth work, emphasising the educator’s role in fostering critical thinking, collaborative problem-solving, and practical application of knowledge within local contexts.

<< Objectives >>

Inspiring, motivating and supporting the implementation of positive changes in our local communities in relation to green sustainability, supported by a global platform to share solutions and ideas.
We incorporated the below objectives within an educational exercise (methodology) where we used several gamification techniques to increase engagement of young people, educators and other stakeholders (e.g. policymakers).
 
Answering the expressed needs and interests of the young people we support.
Raising awareness of the impact of CO2 footprint of everyday actions.
Launching ideas and concrete sustainable actions contributing towards (already partly) solving environmental problems in our communities and wider.
An online platform sharing local actions/solutions, increase the action effectiveness through peer support and inspire other communities.
Sharing local successes to encourage change at a local government engagement level and influence local ‘green’ policy making.
Supporting the adoption of self-sustainability concepts.
Supporting young people in their (pro)active role in integrating sustainable solutions into everyday life.
Creating environmental behavioural changes within the transnational dimension.


<< Implementation >>

Key Activities
Kick-off (Finland, Dec 2022): Focused on logistics, monitoring, reporting, and brainstorming outputs (board game and online platform).
TPMs: Spain (Apr 2023) finalisation of game prototype; Croatia (Sep 2023) incorporation of feedback; (Belgium Feb 2024) Progress evaluation; (Portugal Jun 2024) impact testing and production strategies.
Testing: The testing phase targeted young people and youth workers, gathering feedback to support game enhancement. 
Phase 1 (198 respondents): Primarily young people.
Phase 2 (83 respondents): Target group shifted to older youth (19-30) and youth workers (30+)
Multiplier Events: Partners organised events for youth workers, educators, young people and volunteers to promote Experiment Ecoland methods.
Training Course (May 2024, Finland): Focused on game facilitation, sustainability, and actionable strategies. Evaluation showed high scores, with facilitators rated 4.8/5 and workshops 4.5/5. Participants created eco-plans for local initiatives.
Impact: 87% of participants reported increased sustainability awareness. Outputs continue to inspire global local actions. Evaluation insights https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1QwhuzZqyz72tElnvFtpZdY8v9VmqX3SIGE3xyruCYKI/edit#responses

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs
EXPERIMENT ECOLAND BOARD GAME
An engaging gamified educational boardgame with 37 missions in 6 different languages, designed in an accessible and inclusive way, which supports playability and is aesthetically pleasing.
FACILITATOR MANUAL
In 6 languages, approx. 23 pages, with different game options.
PROACTIVE ECOLAND WEB APP https://proactive-ecoland.com/
A multifunctional landing page where all materials can be downloaded and success stories uploaded; it is also a platform of user generated content of concrete environmental actions with documentation and contacts.
INSTRUCTIONAL VÍDEO
The instructional video is a step by step supportive tool that enables (new) facilitators to adopt and implement the gamified exercise in the way it is designed.
SHORT VÍDEOS FOR SOCIAL MEDIA
Short videos on different topics such as indoor air, light pollution, green roofs and ocean pollution.
WEBSITE with MISSIONS- NEWS: accessible from the platform but also: 
www.ecolandnews.eu
www.proactive-ecoland.com/news
 
Besides the environmental knowledge impact, the game demonstrates significant improvements in cross-cutting competencies such as teamwork, problem-solving, and leadership among young participants.

2022-1-FR02-KA220-YOU-000086653.title: ECHO NETwork - Etic Common Human Open Source network
2022-1-FR02-KA220-YOU-000086653.summary:
<< Background >>

Au sein de nos différentes organisations, nous œuvrons pour promouvoir l'émancipation des individus et défendons un apprentissage de qualité, accessible à tou·te·s (Déclaration d'Incheon 2015).
Chacune de nos organisations œuvre, depuis plusieurs années à : la création d'outils pédagogique, d'ateliers de sensibilisation et d'accompagnement à l'utilisation du numérique et/ou agit pour une transition vers un numérique éthique et durable, la protection des droits des personnes.
Constatant l'importance du numérique au sein de nos sociétés et dans le quotidien des citoyen.ne.s, notamment chez les jeunes, nous souhaitions développer des outils qui pouvaient ainsi permettre aux travailleur·euses de jeunesse, aux représentant·es d'associations de jeunesse et aux jeunes d'être en mesure de pouvoir choisir un numérique éthique, à échelle européenne. Au regard des différents contextes nationaux, nous souhaitions porter un engagement à échelle de l'Europe sur ces questions, grâce à un consortium d'associations en provenance de 5 pays différents de l'Union Européenne. 

<< Objectives >>

L'objectif global du projet était le suivant : Promouvoir la citoyenneté numérique auprès des jeunes, à travers les associations d'éducation populaire, avec le soutien d'organisation de défense des droits humains. 
Afin de répondre à cet objectif global, nous souhaitions répondre aux objectifs spécifiques suivants :
- Échanger des pratiques entre les associations d'éducation populaire et les organisations qui œuvrent pour la transition vers un numérique éthique et responsable
- S'outiller dans le domaine du numérique et des nouvelles technologies par le biais d'alternatives éthiques, respectueuses de l'environnement et des droits humains : par l'utilisation de logiciels libres et une sobriété numérique.
- Développer ses connaissances en matière de politiques européenne sur les droits numériques et le respect des libertés (protection des données).
- Mettre en réseau des acteurs d'associations de jeunesse, d'éducation populaire et des organisations de défense des droits humains. 

<< Implementation >>

Afin de répondre à nos différents objectifs, nous avons mis en place différentes activités : 
En 2023, nous avons organisé 5 activités de rencontres de travailleur·euses de jeunesse (visite d'étude) : 
- Séminaire de rencontres autour de "Vers un numérique éthique" en France (Janvier 2023)
- Visite d'étude "Les réseaux sociaux : outil d'éducation politique ?" en Allemagne (Mars 2023)
- Visite d'étude "Les pédagogies de l'Education Nouvelle pour former au numérique éthique" en Belgique (Juin 2023)
- Visite d'étude "La formation à distance, les outils respectueux de l'environnement" en Italie (Septembre 2023)
- Visite d'étude "Accessibilité du numérique et droits sur internet" en Croatie (Décembre 2023). 
Ces activités ont permis au consortium de travailler des productions et ressources pédagogiques à destination des travailleur·euses de jeunesse, des jeunes, des représenant·es d'associations de jeunesse et des élu·es politiques sur l'année 2024. 
Le consortium s'est retrouvé en présentiel et en distanciel pour construire ces productions qui ont été partagées et diffusées à la fin du projet. Des comptes rendus de ces rencontres sont disponibles en ligne. 
Les programmes (agenda) et comptes rendus (brief) des visites sont en annexes.

<< Results >>

À la fin du projet nous sommes en mesure de diffuser l'ensemble de nos productions via un site internet, qui nous a permis de mutualiser nos ressources et un accès libre aux personnes intéressées des questions numériques. 
Le site internet est disponible en suivant le lien suivant (en anglais et en français) : https://echo-network.eu/ 
Via ce site internet vous retrouvez les productions suivantes : 
- Référentiel de ressources sur les questions de numérique éthique et alternatives existantes 
- Cartographie des acteur·trices du projet et/ou qui oeuvrent dans le domaine du numérique éthique
- Démarches d'animation pratiques et théoriques à destination des travailleur·euses de jeunesse pour sensibiliser les jeunes
- Plaidoyer pour un numérique éthique, humain et ouvert à destination des pouvoirs publics (à échelle européenne mais également transposable à échelle nationale et locale)
- Guide "de survie" sur le numérique éthique à destination des représentant·es associatifs
Ces productions sont aussi en annexes de ce rapport.

2022-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000086395.title: EDI GO – Introducing the organizational approach to integration of Equality, Diversity, Inclusion Model in working with young people
2022-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000086395.summary:
<< Background >>

Considering the many years of experience of cooperation with organizations and public institutions that work with young people, FFE and partners recognized that the organizations usually
implement specific and/or partial activities aimed at prevention and combat of discrimination as well as promotion of equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) values. Also, their existing policies and practices in working with young people are rarely evaluated and improved in such a way that different people, experiences and voices are included in all aspects of their organizations.
Our society is changing, and so is the demographic profile of Europe: the number of refugees in Europe is increasing, society is becoming more diverse. There is also increasing awareness of the unresolved issue of gender equality. At the same time, technological development, with the increasing presence of artificial intelligence, is affecting the way we live and work, increasing the need for new competences on improving inclusive environments for young people to prosper. In this context, social diversity and inequality are hotly debated, and access to education and lifelong learning, has become a high priority to ensure that no one is left behind.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, FFE and partners wanted to create resources and materials to support different types of organizations that work with young people to evaluate their policies and practices in the context of EDI values, to recognize room for improvement and to be empowered to initiate positive EDI changes in to his work.
The created materials would enable the experts working young people to review the inclusive practices within their organizations so diverse young people, experiences and voices are included in all aspects of their organization. This was especially important bearing in mind that one third of young people in Europe are at risk of poverty and social exclusion, many do not have access to their social rights and many continue to face multiple discrimination, experience prejudice and hate crimes.

<< Implementation >>

The organizations from Croatia, France, Greece, Italy and Spain as the first activity of the project, map key issues in applying EDI practices through 50 individual semi-structured interviews with people who work with young people and 15 focus groups with 99 young people (16 - 25 years) from 30 organizations.
The research resulted in a comparative report, but also provided guidelines for the development of EDI resources: Toolbox - Charter Mark with recommendations, Self-evaluation tool and Inclusive language Guidelines, also The training for trainers package - with curriculum for EDI training and training materials for experts in work with young people (created and used for national trainings in 5 countries), and a publication that includes 12 good practice examples on improving EDI policies and practices. The final activities of the project were extremely valuable: national multiplier events and an international conference where all developed materials were presented to numerous participants, and in addition, many experts in youth work had the opportunity to network and plan future cooperation on EDI topics.

<< Results >>

1. identified issues and challenges implementing EDI practices (with 99 young people and 15 experts in working with youth from 30 organizations, in 5 countires), within the research report “Key issues in applying EDI in youth organizations – experience of five EU countries”
2. developed Tool Box “Resources for improvement of EDI practices using the whole-organizational approach” in 6 languages
3. developed Training curriculum “ Breaking barriers, building bridges: The trainer’s blueprint for EDI success”
4. implemented 28-hour international training for experts from partner organizations
5. developed EDI Training for Trainers Package (curriculum in e, and work materials in 6 languages)
6. empowerment of youth workers on improving EDI practices in their organizations in 5 countries - national trainings with 86 participants
7. collected 12 good practices from 5 countries in the publication “Good practices of  Equality, Diversity and Inclusion in organizations”, in 6 languages
8. developed EDI GO online platform with access and explained steps for working on EDI practices for all interested stakeholder 
9. disseminated results and resources developed within EDI project through international and national events with 249 participants

2022-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000087391.title: “My City Through Time”. Exploring our cities through historic and civic education.
2022-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000087391.summary:
<< Background >>

When applying for this project, the partners started from the idea that the cities we live in are not neutral, but they communicate through their public spaces certain values that citizens often do not recognize and are not aware of. That lack of knowledge and understanding is making citizens less active and less competent to reflect on their beliefs, values, and the changes within the societies they live in. 

The need for the partner organizations was to develop new methods and tools to work with young people on the topics of historic civic education, modernize their curricula, and have a stronger impact on the young people they are working with. The second need identified was to improve youth work and to contribute to its recognition through innovative methods and recommendations. 
Finally, the needs identified for the young people were to understand the reality around them and to be more able to approach complex topics critically. Furthermore, young people expressed the need to become more aware of the political history, messages, and values their cities are communicating, as well as to better understand their local history and its connection with European and world trends.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, the partners wanted to contribute to the recognition of youth work and its practices, by combining methods and tools from youth work and historic and civic education. They also wanted to improve their, skills, and competencies in youth work and in dealing with project topics, to become more successful in their work with young people, and to gain more visibility and recognition on local and European levels., partners wanted to have an impact on young people directly and indirectly involved in the project, to get new knowledge, raise awareness about the project topics, develop critical thinking, and motivate young people to be active citizens., the partner wanted to contribute to young people’s ability to combat radicalized discourses and nationalistic and populist narratives, deconstruct stereotypes and prejudices, promote inclusion, and support democratization processes and European values. The partners wanted to create new and innovative methods and tools, tangible project results that will contribute to the improvement of their work and in creating better and inclusive activities and programs for the young people in their local communities and Europe.

<< Implementation >>

Implemented activities:
Kick-off meeting – January 2023, Zagreb
Creation of R1 – 7 publications “My City Through Time”, February – April 2023
2 local dissemination events (youth and youth workers) – May 2023, all the partner countries
Second transnational partner meeting – June 2023, Berlin
Creation of R2 – toolkit and educational cards, September 2023 – December 2024
Local dissemination event - February 2024, all the partner countries
Training for youth workers – March 2024, Barcelona
Final event and third transnational partner meeting – May 2024, Thessaloniki
Creation of R3 – Recommendations, May-June 2024
Online campaign – May 2023 – May 2024

The partners implemented all the planned activities, following the project’s time plan created in the preparation phase. Only the kick-off meeting that was originally planned for December 2022 was moved to January 2023, because there was no common date all the partners were available in December. 

<< Results >>

The tangible outputs of the project are: 
7 publications “My City through Time” including three to five thematic units from partner cities and their translations to all the partner languages; 
the toolkit, also translated to all the partner languages, 
educational cards, both digital and physical copies, in English and partner languages; 
recommendations on how to improve youth work through historic-civic education, in the partner languages. 

Intangible outputs of the project were: 
For the partners and other organizations working with youth - increased ability to work with young people and to address topics from the field of historic-civic education; new methods and tools created, which will have a positive impact on their everyday work; improved the capacities of the organization to deal with the project's topics with young people in activities on the local and European levels.
For the young people - raising awareness of the historical and social processes that changed their societies; improved their knowledge about the project's topics; decreased radicalization and combat stereotypes and prejudices; strengthened democratic values and promoted European values and active citizenship
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Quality and innovation of youth work
