2023-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000166472.title: Report Hate: Building up possibilities for young people to report and strengthening youth work in working against hate speech
2023-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000166472.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Hate speech threatens democracy and social cohesion in many countries of the EU and around the world, as numerous national and international studies show. Especially young people have already come into contact with and/or been directly affected by hate speech. With ReportHate, we want to give young people the opportunity to become active. We are developing the first transnational hate speech reporting portal especially for young people ever.

<< Implementation >>

In Hungary, North Macedonia and Kroatia new reporting possibilities are set up and framed in a transnational reporting portal, promoted by an accompanying social media campaign targeting on young people. Together with partners from Germany, Israel, Slovakia and Spain and with connections to the International Network Against Cyber Hate, to the European Youth Information and Counselling Agency (ERYICA) and with local youth work structures we create a strong network.

<< Results >>

Three new reporting possibilities for hate speech are created. One transnational hate speech reporting portal with focus on young people is developed and promoted in a broad-based social media campaign. Local stakeholder networks are established. In the second year of the project, reports of hate speech from the partner countries with reporting possibilities are received and documented. The reports received will be published in a final analysis comparing the countries.

2023-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000167094.title: Creative youth work on prevention of negative impact of social media influencers on youth
2023-1-DE04-KA220-YOU-000167094.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the growing negative influence of social media influencers on young people’s self-esteem, mental health, and well-being. While some argue that influencers can inspire and motivate young people to pursue their goals and aspirations, others suggest that they can have a negative impact on young people's mental health and well-being. On the positive side, some influencers use their platforms to promote positive messages and provide a sense of community for their followers. However, we wanted to address the negative influence, to make sure that young people will critically assess the information received from the media and do the same when considering to create content for the public. The project addressed the need for youth to develop critical thinking and media literacy, while also equipping youth workers with innovative tools to address these challenges in line with European standards and policies.


<< Objectives >>

The main goal was to prevent the negative impact & influence of social media influencers on youth. This was part of the general efforts towards responsible use of the internet both by young people, but also the responsibility to provide online safety from the public institutions & private companies. It is the role of young workers to empower young people in critical thinking and media literacy. It is also their role to advocate based on the EU standards protecting young people on internet.

The specific objectives of the project were:
1.	To empower youngsters in critical thinking and media literacy through developing a toolkit with a set of innovative workshops and tools.
2.	To empower youth workers in creativity for prevention of negative impact of social media influencers on youth, through developing curriculum.
3.	To build the capacity of youth workers to advocate towards local and national governments on implementing the European standards protecting young people on the internet such as Audiovisual Media Services Directive (AVMSD), Digital services act and the European strategy for a better Internet for children.


<< Implementation >>

The following planned activities were implemented: 
-	Project management activities, including kick-off, mid-term and final evaluation online meetings
-	Toolkit for empowering youngsters in critical thinking and media literacy for prevention of negative impact of social media influencers – in 7 languages 
-	Curriculum: Empowering youth workers in creative methodology for prevention of negative impact of social media influencers on youth – in 7 languages
-	Online course: Youth workers in advocacy action for implementation of European standards for protecting young people on the internet – in 7 languages
-	Piloting the toolkit in Germany, Croatia, France, Estonia, Italy and Serbia
-	Organising local training courses for youth workers, based on the Curriculum in all participating countries
-	Organising Multiplier events (5 national in Italy, France, Estonia, Serbia and Germany and 1 international conference in Croatia)
-	Additional dissemination activities and meetings, as well as the Online hackathon on the topic of internet safety and the impact of influences.


<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results of this project were:
-	Developed and published Toolkit in English, translated in German, Croatian, Estonian, French, Italian and Serbian
-	Developed and published Curriculum in English, translated in German, Croatian, Estonian, French, Italian and Serbian
-	Designed and accessible Online course in English, translated in German, Croatian, Estonian, French, Italian and Serbian
-	122 youngsters engaged in piloting activities for the Toolkit
-	96 youth workers participated in local training courses based on the Curriculum
-	16 youngsters participated in the “Online” Hackathon
-	188 participants in the multiplier events organised throughout participating countries
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2023-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000158122.title: Heritage Stewardship
2023-1-ES02-KA220-YOU-000158122.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project at the time to respond to the growing need to involve young people from different backgrounds (education and youth work, creating synergies) in the preservation and promotion of Europe's natural and cultural heritage, while also addressing youth unemployment and social exclusion. The project aimed to empower young people by providing them with skills and knowledge in heritage management, digitization, and entrepreneurship. 

Thanks to the partners' analysis, we were able to identify a lack of awareness among young people about the value of European heritage (and its importance) and its potential as a tool for real inclusion, environmental sustainability, and employability. In addition, there was a need to strengthen partnerships between youth and educational organizations in Europe and to develop the capacity for youth work to become more intercultural, innovative, and participatory. Through this initiative, we sought to create opportunities for young people to connect with their communities, develop new skills, and become active managers of heritage and social change.


<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to promote employability, social inclusion, and cohesion among young Europeans from different backgrounds by involving them in the preservation, promotion, and innovation of natural and cultural heritage, based on the needs we had identified. Our goal was to raise awareness of the importance of heritage as a shared European value and as a powerful tool for the empowerment of young people and active citizenship, so that they would feel it was their own. Specifically, we sought to:
- Involve young people directly in the research and mapping of heritage sites, both tangible and intangible, to strengthen their sense of identity and belonging.
- Develop new skills and social abilities among young people and youth workers through non-formal education, digital tools, and intercultural learning, creating a network of committed young people and youth workers who know how to support them.
- Create strong and lasting connections between organizations across Europe to increase capacity in the heritage and youth sectors.
- Ultimately, our goal was to inspire a new generation of cultural and environmental managers prepared to tackle the social and ecological challenges we face today.

<< Implementation >>

The project was structured around four main areas: European natural heritage, cultural heritage, digitization, and employability in the heritage sector. We carried out all the activities we had proposed in the application in the four partner countries, including:

- 4 training courses for youth workers to develop skills in heritage education, sustainability, and digital tools.

- 16 local youth workshops involving more than 200 young people, who conducted research on 200 heritage sites and led local community actions.

- 2 intellectual outputs: the interactive heritage management map and the guide for cultural and environmental managers, both created jointly through the collaborative work of young people.

- 20 environmental and 20 cultural events aimed at promoting local heritage and youth participation.

- 1 European online conference to facilitate transnational dialogue among young people on heritage and sustainability.

- 4 multiplier events to disseminate results, share best practices, and engage stakeholders. 

- 4 transnational partner meetings to coordinate efforts, evaluate progress, and strengthen international cooperation.

<< Results >>

The project delivered two intellectual outputs (IO's):
- The Heritage Stewardship Interactive Map, Mapping 200 heritage sites across Europe researched and documented by young participants.
- The Cultural and Environmental Stewards Guidebook, a practical resource for youth workers to engage young people in heritage-based education, sustainability, and entrepreneurship.

Beyond these, the project resulted in:
- Over 200 youth and 60 youth workers trained in heritage stewardship, digital skills, and non-formal education methods.
- Strengthened partnerships among 8 organizations from 4 countries, with improved capacity in transnational cooperation and youth work.
- Creation of local youth communities actively involved in environmental and cultural actions.
- Increased awareness among participants about the value of European heritage as a tool for inclusion, identity-building, and professional growth.
- Widespread dissemination of project results through 4 multiplier events and the online unconference.

2023-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000158264.title: Media and Information Literacy for climate change and environmental topics
2023-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000158264.summary:
<< Background >>

Digital technologies have made media ubiquitous, shaping public debates and influencing perceptions on crucial issues like climate change. While these platforms provide access to information, they also serve as echo chambers for disinformation. Here, media literacy comes into play.

Very often, traditional and digital media amplify the urgency of the climate crisis, communicate key facts about climate change, and debunk climate change denial and other conspiracy theories. It is crucial for people to understand how this content is produced, for what purposes, and based on what sources. Without trust in climate change science, policymaking in a democratic society can’t address the serious threats in the future.

The need for this project lies in the insufficient level of media and information literacy (MIL) among youth in understanding sustainability. While many youths engage with MIL, it is rarely connected to climate issues. Youth workers often lack the skills and resources to integrate MIL into climate related education, and there is a shortage of accessible training materials and up-to-date research on young people MIL competences. Collaboration between organizations is also lacking, limiting the exchange of best practices.

<< Objectives >>

The project focuses on raising partners' capacities and providing practical tools for youth workers and youth, starting with research showing the real-time situation in involved countries. The research collected data on youth media literacy in Croatia, Portugal, and Estonia by engaging 731 young people, analyzing reports, and publishing a study report. An educational toolkit with 20 workshops was created for youth workers to support young people in critically consuming media, ensuring its practical use. Furthermore, 310 young people improved their media literacy skills through an interactive online course, while 62 youth workers received training to implement local activities. The project also focused on broad dissemination, reaching 30+ organizations, 300+ youth workers, and 1000+ young people outside direct project activities through online outreach and local conferences in the three partner countries.

<< Implementation >>

The project started from the implementation of research and collecting relevant data and presenting them, moved to the development of a toolkit for youth workers and an online course for youth; and continued to direct dissemination of the outputs among youth workers and youth organisations, actively involving 310 young people in an online course and educating 62 youth workers of partners for implementation of 20 educational workshops dealing with media and information literacy in green topics.


<< Results >>

731 young people involved in the research providing a broader picture of 3 involved countries, a Toolkit with 20 educational workshops, Online learning course for youth - 310 young people raised their competencies in media and information literacy, 62 youth workers raised their competencies for local-level activities and workshops, 1000+ young people, 300+ youth workers and 30+ youth organisations, including 4 network of organisations learned about new methods and tools that they can use in their everyday work on these topics.

2023-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000164006.title: Improving Civic Education in Vocational Education and Training
2023-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000164006.summary:
<< Background >>

Projekt “Improving Civic Education in Vocational Education and Training” pokrenut je kako bi se odgovorilo na potrebu za kvalitetnijim građanskim obrazovanjem u strukovnim školama. Iako strukovne škole pohađa velik broj učenika, građanske teme u njihovim kurikulumima često su nedovoljno zastupljene. Članice konzorcija: Gong (Hrvatska), Funky Citizens (Rumunjska) i CGE Erfurt e.V. (Njemačka) godinama zagovaraju unapređenje obrazovnih politika i sustavno i kontinuirano provode neformalne programe aktivnog građanstva za mlade (i druge skupine). Sve tri organizacije također su uspostavile suradnju s brojnim školama, učiteljima, školskim administratorima i drugim stručnjacima. Sve tri organizacije zagovaraju promjene u obrazovanju, posebno u području građanskog odgoja i obrazovanja. Međutim, nisu imale zajedničku, na dokazima utemeljenu zagovaračku poziciju o tome kako poboljšati građanski odgoj u strukovnom obrazovanju. Zato im je ovaj projekt omogućio da kroz istraživanje postojećih praksi, usporedbu pristupa u različitim zemljama i razvoj preporuka za donositelje odluka i stručnjak dobiju značajnu komprativnu perspektivu, upoznaju se bolje s pristupima poučavanju građanskog odgoja u strukovnim školama u različitim zemljama EU. 

<< Objectives >>

Glavni cilj projekta bio je doprinijeti povećanju razine građanske pismenosti i participacije mladih, osobito onih koji pohađaju strukovne škole, kroz jačanje kapaciteta organizacija civilnog društva i razvoj na dokazima utemeljenih zagovaračkih alata. Specifični ciljevi uključivali su obogaćivanje znanja organizacija civilnog društva i mladih o postojećim praksama građanskog obrazovanja u strukovnim školama, jačanje kapaciteta partnerskih organizacija i drugih relevantnih dionika za zagovaranje unapređenja obrazovnih politika u području građanskog obrazovanja te razvoj zajedničkih, na dokazima utemeljenih zagovaračkih pozicija koje će poslužiti kao temelj za daljnje djelovanje na nacionalnoj i europskoj razini i potaknuti sustavne promjene u obrazovnim praksama. Članice ovog konzorcija željele su da kroz ovaj projekt mogu kompetentno predstaviti različite pristupe poučavanju građanskog odgoja u nekoliko europskih zemalja, s posebnim naglaskom na to kako se to provodi u strukovnim školama, da dubinski razumiju način na koji se građanski odgoj poučava u njihovim državama te glavne izazove njegove provedbe u strukovnom obrazovanju kako bi ovo znanje sustavno prenosili drugim organizacijama mladih/udrugama. 

<< Implementation >>

Tijekom provedbe projekta realiziran je niz povezanih aktivnosti usmjerenih na istraživanje, analizu i zagovaranje s ciljem unaprjeđenja građanskog obrazovanja u strukovnim školama. Izrađena je komparativna analiza praksi građanskog obrazovanja u sedam europskih zemalja te izrađene studije slučaja u svakoj partnerskoj zemlji. Rezultati istraživanja predstavljeni su na okruglim stolovima u Hrvatskoj, Njemačkoj i Rumunjskoj, čime je potaknut dijalog s relevantnim dionicima.
Na temelju prikupljenih podataka partneri su izradili zagovaračke dokumente i preporuke za nacionalnu i europsku razinu. Kroz uključivi konzultacijski proces s akterima iz područja obrazovanja prikupljeni su komentari i izrađena finalna verzija preporuka za kvalitetnije građansko obrazovanje. Projektni rezultati predstavljeni su i na europskoj razini kroz sastanke s europskim i regionalnim mrežama, dok su ključna zagovaračka pitanja predstavljena na završnim konferencijama u partnerskim zemljama. Sve aktivnosti pratila je kontinuirana informativno-edukativna kampanja putem tradicionalnih medija, društvenih mreža i mrežnih stranica organizacija.

<< Results >>

Kao konkretni rezultati projekta ostvarena su dva istraživačka i zagovaračka outputa, koji su doprinijeli boljem razumijevanju i unaprjeđenju građanskog obrazovanja u srednjim strukovnim školama. Izrađena je komparativna analiza praksi građanskog obrazovanja u sedam europskih zemalja, koja je pružila uvid u sličnosti, razlike i ključne izazove u provedbi građanskog obrazovanja. Provedena je i studija slučaja u tri zemlje (Hrvatskoj, Rumunjskoj i Tiringiji (saveznoj pokrajini u Njemačkoj) koja je obuhvaćala fokus grupe, online ankete i intervjue s učenicima, nastavnicima, stručnjacima i predstavnicima organizacija civilnog društva, čime su prikupljeni podaci o iskustvima i potrebama različitih dionika. Rezultati tih istraživanja predstavljeni su na nacionalnim okruglim stolovima u svakoj od partnerskih zemalja, gdje su sudionici imali priliku raspraviti nalaze i predložiti smjernice za daljnji rad. Na temelju dobivenih uvida započeta je izradu triju zagovaračkih dokumenata (position papers) s konkretnim preporukama za unapređenje građanskog obrazovanja u strukovnim školama. Osim istraživačkih rezultata, projekt je ojačao kapacitete partnerskih organizacija za provođenje međunarodnih istraživanja i zagovaračkih aktivnosti.
topics: Reaching the policy level/dialogue with decision makers

2023-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000165938.title: Regional School for Political Development
2023-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000165938.summary:
<< Background >>

Young people in Croatia, North Macedonia, and Serbia often feel distant from politics due to low trust in institutions and limited opportunities for structured political education. Yet, they are highly motivated by climate and green policy issues, which transcend borders and align with EU priorities. The partners, therefore, designed the Regional School for Political Development (RSPD) to bridge this gap. Building on their long experience in civic education and the Council of Europe’s network of political schools, they set out to create a regional programme that would connect democratic participation with the green transition. RSPD combines intensive seminars, mentoring, and cross-border networking to help emerging leaders understand democratic processes, design evidence-based green policies, and advocate for their adoption. The curriculum was shaped by a needs analysis, application data, and baseline questionnaires, ensuring that the content addressed participants’ real learning needs and broader democratic and environmental challenges in the three countries.

<< Objectives >>

The overall goal was to empower and motivate young leaders to participate actively in democratic life and contribute to the UN Sustainable Development Goals, with a special focus on the green transition.
Specific aims were: (1) to create a cooperative, cross-border educational and networking programme that promotes active citizenship and European values while linking democratic participation to climate and environmental challenges; (2) to provide in-depth knowledge, practical skills and sustained mentoring so that participants can research, develop and advocate evidence-based green public policies; (3) to establish a durable, transnational network of young civic leaders for long-term exchange, mutual learning and joint initiatives. 
Planned outputs included a tested joint curriculum and digital learning materials, an active alumni community and a set of innovative policy proposals developed, publicly presented and ready to inform decision-makers at local, national and European levels.

<< Implementation >>

Key steps included joint curriculum design, training of facilitators and creation of a shared digital platform for materials and mentoring. An open call generated over 120 applications, from which 30 participants (10 per country) were selected through a transparent, competitive process ensuring gender, ethnic and geographic balance.
The core learning path consisted of three residential seminars—Croatia (institutions and dialogue), North Macedonia (policy design and implementation), Serbia (advocacy and leadership)—complemented by regular online meet-ups and structured mentoring.
Experiential elements enriched the programme: a field visit to Rijeka and Krk to observe circular-economy practices and a study visit to Brussels, where participants engaged directly with EU institutions and green-policy NGOs.
Communication and dissemination accompanied every stage, from the initial call to the final conference, with weekly social-media and website updates, press outreach, and presentations at international forums (World Forum for Democracy in Strasbourg, Alpbach Forum, and the UNECE Regional Forum on Sustainable Development).

<< Results >>

The project delivered all planned outputs and more. A joint RSPD curriculum and digital platform were created and tested. A diverse cohort of 30 young civic leaders completed the full programme of three regional seminars, supported by continuous mentoring, a field visit to Rijeka and Krk, and a study visit to Brussels.
The policy-work component exceeded expectations: six policy proposals—on circular economy, energy efficiency, waste management, climate adaptation and sustainable urban development—were researched, drafted and publicly presented, surpassing the original target of four.
Communication and outreach goals were also met or exceeded through an active online campaign, regular media coverage, and presentations at major international events.
An independent external evaluation confirmed the programme’s relevance and high quality, documenting strong gains in participants’ knowledge, practical skills and confidence to apply democratic and green-policy approaches in their communities.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2023-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000166168.title: Seed2STEM: Planting the Future of Education
2023-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000166168.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for SEED2STEM because we identified a growing gap between the skills young people need for future employment and the learning opportunities available to them, particularly in STEM and sustainable agriculture. Young people, especially those with fewer opportunities and those living in rural areas, had limited access to practical STEM education that demonstrates how digital technologies can solve real world challenges. At the same time, youth workers often lacked accessible methodologies and educational resources to deliver engaging STEM activities without advanced technical expertise. We also recognised that agriculture is increasingly driven by digital innovation, automation, and IoT technologies, yet it remains underrepresented in youth work and is often perceived as an unattractive career path. Through this project, we addressed these needs by combining STEM education with sustainable agriculture in a practical, non formal learning environment. We developed innovative educational resources that enable young people to strengthen their digital, green, and transversal competences while exploring technology based solutions for sustainable food production. 

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to promote innovative STEM education by connecting digital technologies with sustainable agriculture through practical, non formal learning. Our objective was to strengthen the employability of young people, especially those with fewer opportunities, by developing their digital, green, and transversal competences, including programming, problem solving, teamwork, and critical thinking. We also wanted to increase young people's interest in STEM careers by demonstrating how technologies such as IoT, embedded systems, and automation are applied to real challenges in agriculture and food production. Another key objective was to strengthen the capacity of youth workers by providing them with innovative, freely accessible educational resources, practical methodologies, and digital tools that enable them to deliver engaging STEM activities without requiring advanced technical expertise. At organisational level, we sought to strengthen cooperation between youth organisations and higher education institutions, combining technical expertise with non formal education methods to develop high quality educational resources.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented five interconnected work packages covering project management, development of educational resources, testing, validation, and dissemination. We developed the AGRO STEM Platform as an open digital learning environment and created the AGRO STEM Curriculum, IoT Curriculum, and AGRO STEM Game, including complementary educational methodologies and learning materials. These resources were co-created by youth organisations and a higher education institution, combining technical expertise with non formal education approaches. We organised three transnational project meetings to coordinate implementation and three learning mobilities where youth workers tested the developed resources, strengthened their competences, and exchanged good practices. We also organised national focus groups in all partner countries, involving more than 140 young people and over 30 youth workers in testing and evaluating the project results. Their feedback was systematically incorporated into the final versions of all educational resources.

<< Results >>

We delivered four complementary educational results that support innovative STEM learning through sustainable agriculture. The AGRO STEM Platform provides free access to all project resources in a user-friendly digital learning environment. The AGRO STEM Curriculum introduces programming, digital agriculture, embedded systems, and FarmBot technologies through practical learning scenarios adapted for non formal education. The IoT Curriculum offers structured video tutorials and practical activities that strengthen digital competences and understanding of connected technologies. The AGRO STEM Game, together with its educational methodology and complementary board game, enables young people to explore STEM concepts through interactive, game based learning. Beyond these outputs, more than 140 young people and over 30 youth workers participated in testing and validating the resources, ensuring their quality, accessibility, and relevance. The project strengthened the competences of youth workers, enhanced cooperation between youth organisations and higher education institutions, increased the digital capacity of partner organisations, and established a sustainable European network.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2023-1-IE01-KA220-YOU-000166576.title: Menstruation: Empowerment and Sustainability
2023-1-IE01-KA220-YOU-000166576.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because:
- many women and gender‑diverse people still lack affordable, sustainable menstrual options, which directly affects their dignity, health, and participation in society.
- education is one of the most effective tools for breaking this cycle—yet high‑quality, accessible menstrual education is inconsistent across EU countries.
- we wanted to create a project that aligns with the European Pillar of Social Rights, especially in the areas of gender equality, equal opportunities, education, and health.
- we identified a chance to make a practical, measurable impact by empowering youth leaders and communities with knowledge they can immediately use.

What needs we addressed:
Period poverty creates economic, educational, environmental and gender‑equality needs. Many cannot afford menstrual products, and awareness of low‑cost reusable options is low. Menstrual education is also inconsistent across the EU, which limits informed choice. Commonly used disposable products generate major plastic waste and have health impacts that most are not aware of. Without this knowledge gender equality cannot be realised. The project also supports EU requirements for awareness‑raising on sustainable menstrual products.



<< Objectives >>

Our objectives for the project were:
The overall objectives of the project are:
- to increase the internal capacity of the 8 partners
- to create a cohesive suite of training resources on menstruation and sustainability that builds upon the work done to date in
the field, incorporates elements found to be the most effective in existing programs, and scaled up for use on an EU level
- to raise awareness of single use plastic waste from menstruation in line with the legislative requirements set down by the
Single Use Plastics Directive (2019) with the aim of reducing plastic waste
- to support the move from a linear to circular economy in line with EU aims under the Circular Economy Action Plan (2020),
one of the main building blocks of the European Green Deal
- establish national contexts for menstruation education across Europe to ensure the training course developed achieves the
appropriate tone when conveying information on menstruation
- to combat period poverty and promote gender equality in line with the right to adequate menstrual health and education


<< Implementation >>

WP2: 
- Audit project partners’ work on the topic and identify existing resources and gaps - completed 
- Conduct an international desk based study into work on education on reusable menstrual items on a local, regional and national level, to include compilation of 10 best practice case studies. - completed 
- Undertake a review of the legislative and economic backdrop to menstrual protection choices in the 8 partner countries - completed 
- Undertake review of narratives around menstruation in 8 partner countries to include a youth survey - completed 

WP3: 
- Develop the training resources, the train the trainer course content and supporting materials - completed

2023-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000158678.title: Facilitating Artificial Intelligence TecHnology in Youth Work
2023-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000158678.summary:
<< Background >>

Il progetto FAITH nasce dalla consapevolezza dell'avvento di massicce quantità di AI disponibili anche in modo gratuito. Il settore dello Youth Work non è immune a queste trasformazioni e, al contrario, deve sfruttare appieno le opportunità che questi strumenti possono offrire. FAITH nasce per migliorare la qualità dello youth work e ridurre le inefficienze attraverso l'uso di strumenti di
AI. Eravamo e siamo convinti che l'AI rappresenti una rivoluzione senza precedenti per il mondo del lavoro e riteniamo che sia necessario sfruttare appieno le opportunità che questi strumenti offrono per garantire un lavoro di alta qualità e per mantenere la competitività rispetto ad altri attori del settore.

<< Objectives >>

Obiettivi del progetto FAITH:
1. Efficientare i processi dello Youth Work;
2. Potenziare la capacità delle organizzazioni giovanili di analizzare ed agire sui bisogni dei giovani e della comunità locale
di riferimento;
3. Offrire agli Youth Worker competenze sull’utilizzo delle AI nel loro campo di attività;
4. Valutare l’impatto dell’AI sullo Youth Work;
5. Favorire la cooperazione tra organizzazioni giovanili, attraverso l’esplorazione dell’utilizzo di sistemi di AI.

<< Implementation >>

Il progetto si è composto di quattro macro-fasi:
FASE 1: Analisi dei processi delle organizzazioni parter e identificazione dei KPI;
FASE 2: Identificazione degli strumenti basati sull’AI utili per i processi identificati e produzione di bozza del manuale d’uso;
FASE 3: Test degli strumenti AI identificati, valutazione dell’impatto degli strumenti e finalizzazione del Manuale sull’uso
dell’IA nello Youth Work;
FASE 4: Disseminazione del Manuale.

<< Results >>

Il risultato principale è stata la produzione e pubblicazione del Manuale sull’utilizzo dell’Intelligenza Artificiale nello Youth Work, dove per ogni processo critico identificato si segnalano gli strumenti più idonei, indicazioni per l'uso ed una stima sulla difficoltà di adozione, accompagnato dai una analisi comparativa dei vantaggi e delle limitazioni. Altri risultati rilevanti sono i White Paper contenenti l'analisi dei processi svolta su ciascuna organizzazione partner, così come il Glossario dei KPI, un manuale tecnico-operativo essenziale per lo svolgimento dell'analisi comparativa e contenente la definizione degli indicatori di performance per ciascun processo analizzato, assieme alle istruzioni per l'implementazione dei test.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2023-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000165642.title: M.E.D.I.T.erraNEW: Mediation, Emotions, Dialogue, Interculturality, Talents to foster youth social inclusion in the Mare Nostrum
2023-1-IT03-KA220-YOU-000165642.summary:
<< Background >>

M.E.D.I.T.erraNEW was created in response to the need to address the educational challenges posed by the Mediterranean context, with particular reference to the inclusion of young people (aged 13–17) with a migration background.
The partner organizations operate in the educational field and have identified, through their on-the-ground experience, the need to strengthen educational offerings aimed at empowering and promoting the active citizenship of young people with a migrant background between the ages of 13 and 17. In particular, the project focused on five educational areas:
1.	Linguistic and Intercultural Education
2.	Conflict Mediation, Culture of Peace, and Active Citizenship
3.	Intercultural and Interreligious Dialogue
4.	Personal Well-being and Emotional Development
5.	Arts and Talent Enhancement
At the same time, beyond the educational need, the partners also recognized the necessity of strengthening the managerial skills of organizations working in the field of non-formal youth education, with the aim of attracting resources to support educational activities and ensuring the sustainability of the organizations themselves.


<< Objectives >>

The direct beneficiaries of the project are the youth workers of the partner organizations who work with the target group: young people aged 13–17, with particular attention to those with a migrant background.

The direct impact of the project activities includes:
The innovation of educational projects through the exchange of good practices and cross-fertilization among organizations.
The enhancement of educators’ competences through Job Shadowing (JS) activities, where educators were able to directly test in the field the effectiveness of the partner organizations’ good practices.
The strengthening of the managerial competences of organizational staff through a training programme focused on key topics in socio-educational sector management:
Project Management & Reporting
Impact Evaluation
Institutional Communication
Digital Tools
Advocacy
European Solidarity Corps.


<< Implementation >>

The project has completed all planned activities.
Under WP2, all three Job Shadowing activities were carried out, involving 54 educators, with the aim of fostering the exchange of good practices and strengthening the competences of trainers and educators, thereby improving the educational offer addressed to young people aged 13–17.
The first session took place in Tuscany (29/04–03/05/2024)
The second session was held in Rome (30/05–02/06/2024).
In the second year, the third Job Shadowing was implemented in Croatia (Križevci–Zagreb, 07–11/05/2025), coordinated by the local partner.
Under WP3, all 6 out of 6 online training sessions for staff were completed, focusing on transversal competences to strengthen the sustainability of the organizations.
WP4 included communication activities at both local and international levels, including the presentation of the project at UNESCO on 2 December 2025.
Further details on the implemented activities will be provided in the sections dedicated to each individual WP.


<< Results >>

The following outputs were produced:
WP2: A 51-page Creation Kit for youth workers, available in six languages ​​(Italian, English, Spanish, French, Croatian, and Arabic), which brings together seven best practices from partner organizations in five training areas, described through methodological factsheets, and five case studies of cross-fertilization, replication, and adaptation to different socio-cultural contexts. The kit is available online and downloadable:
https://www.new-humanity.org/educazione-alla-pace/una-nuova-visione-educativa-introduzione-al-kit/
https://www.new-humanity.org/en/news/a-new-educational-vision-for-the-mediterranean/
WP3: A repository of training sessions available in six languages ​​on transversal skills for organizational sustainability
WP4: Project website, brochure in English, presentation to UNESCO, final brochure in Italian and English, 27 dissemination events, and 4,229 participants.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

2023-1-LT02-KA220-YOU-000161075.title: VR the Future
2023-1-LT02-KA220-YOU-000161075.summary:
<< Background >>

Youth work is increasingly expected to respond to digital transformation and to the needs of young people growing up in immersive, media-rich environments. However, the initial needs analysis conducted by the consortium showed that youth workers lacked practical competences, methodological guidance and accessible tools to meaningfully integrate VR and 360° technologies into their daily practice. Existing digital youth work approaches were often theoretical, with limited no-code, ready-to-use solutions.
In addition, young people demonstrated low awareness of civic participation opportunities and limited engagement in volunteering and community life. The project addressed the need for innovative, engaging and inclusive methods to foster youth participation, civic engagement and social inclusion, especially for young people with fewer opportunities. “VR the Future” responded by combining technological knowledge with practical youth work methodologies.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to strengthen digital competences of youth workers and mainstream innovative digital youth work practices, particularly through VR and 360° video technologies.
Specific objectives were:
1. To develop a methodological guidebook supporting the integration of VR and 360° video in youth work.
2. To design, implement and evaluate at least six interactive teaching and learning scenarios addressing civic engagement, volunteering, social inclusion and mentoring.
3. To increase youth participation and awareness of community involvement opportunities through immersive learning experiences.
4. To promote smart and innovative youth work in line with the EU Youth Work Agenda.
Through these objectives, the project sought to empower youth workers as digital facilitators and support young people in becoming more active, informed and engaged citizens.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through four main work packages:
1. Project management and quality assurance, including steering committee meetings.
2. Development of a methodological guidebook (OER, translated into four languages), including national status reports, good practices and practical guidance on no-code VR content creation.
3. Development, testing and evaluation of six interactive VR/360° scenarios, translated into partner languages and accompanied by facilitation materials. WebVR versions were created to ensure accessibility without VR equipment. Youth workers were trained to use and apply the tools.
4. International and local training for youth workers.
5. Needs analysis of youth workers. 
6. Webpage creation.
7. National and international promotional events.

<< Results >>

The main tangible outputs include:
1. A freely accessible methodological guidebook on 360° and virtual reality usage in youth work in English, Lithuanian, Latvian and Croatian.
2. Six interactive VR/360° movies with alternative endings, addressing civic participation, volunteering, mental health and drug abuse.
3. WebVR versions of all sex movies ensuring access via PC, laptop or tablet.
4. Accompanying facilitation materials for youth workers in all partner languages.
5. A project website and LMS hosting all materials.
6. National and international promotional events and online dissemination reaching wide audiences.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

Deaf people and Deaf youth have their mother tongue in sign language and many of them struggle to read a spoken language
MUFFIN aims to improve the inclusiveness of Deaf youth in marine education, approaching marine habitat and visiting museums and aquaria by creating a lexicon for marine "terms" avoiding “fingerspelling“  (dactylology) and giving a sign name to 40 marine species in 5 sign languages.

The signs and video documentaries produced will be at the same time scientifically correct and attractive for Deaf Youth, facilitating the access of Deaf people to marine habitat, providing an educational tool for museums and aquaria as well as schools and educational context.

2023-1-PL01-KA220-YOU-000155098.title: Muzolingua International vol.2
2023-1-PL01-KA220-YOU-000155098.summary:
<< Background >>

We decided to apply for the project because we work with a target group of young people who often lack the skills necessary to be competitive in the labour market. Many of them need support in developing soft skills, creativity, teamwork and self-confidence. We believed that music could be an effective and engaging tool to address these needs and to help young people develop these competences in a practical and motivating way.

The project was also inspired by the great success of the first Musilingue project. The previous partnership consisted of only four organisations, but the results were very positive. Therefore, we decided to expand the partnership and involve more organisations in order to increase the project’s impact both on partner organisations and on young people participating in the activities.

One of the key needs was to strengthen international cooperation and create a methodology that could be used by other organisations working with youth. Another important goal was to introduce international music workshops as a permanent element of the educational activities offered by our organisations. Young people were able to gain new skills, improve their collaboration in multicultural groups and imrove.

<< Objectives >>

Through the realization of this project, we aimed primarily to enhance the employability of young people by equipping them with practical and transferable skills that could support them in their future professional and personal lives. We wanted participants to develop competences such as teamwork, creativity, communication, and self-confidence, which are essential in today’s labour market.

Another important objective was to improve the digital skills of young people. By introducing them to various online tools and digital platforms, we wanted to increase their awareness of how technology can support creative work and collaboration, particularly within the cultural and creative sectors.

The project also aimed to strengthen cooperation between partner organisations from six countries. By working together, we wanted to exchange experiences, improve our methods of working with young people, and develop practical methodologies that could be used in the future. As a result, the project contributed not only to the development of participants, but also to the long-term capacity building of the partner organisations.

<< Implementation >>

All activities planned within the project were successfully implemented, and in many cases we achieved even more than originally expected. In addition to the planned programme, we managed to increase the visibility of the project by organizing more concerts than initially foreseen. During each music camp, more than one final concert was held, which significantly contributed to promoting both the project and the idea of using music as a tool for developing young people’s skills.

Another important achievement, which had not been originally planned, was the organization of additional local activities. Together with the partners, we decided that whenever a local cultural event or activity was organized, we would ask for the opportunity to present at least one song created within the project and briefly introduce the project, its objectives, and its outcomes. All hosting institutions were very supportive and agreed to give us time to present the initiative.

We were also invited to present the project during a congress for cultural institutions from across Europe in Kraków. We decided to demonstrate our results live through a musical performance, which proved to be a great success and further strengthened its visibility.

<< Results >>

Unexpected result of the project occurred during the final concert in Brussels. During the event, we openly addressed the issue that some young participants involved in the project were unable to attend because they did not receive visas. We highlighted that it is unfair when motivated young people who actively contribute to European cultural cooperation cannot participate due to administrative barriers. After the concert, the Consulate General of Turkey approached us and said that our statement showed an important problem and that we had done more for the country than we could imagine by raising this issue publicly. He even asked if he could use this argument in future discussions, which gave us hope that the project may contribute to real change.
Another positive outcome was the increased activity of the young participants. Many of them created their own local bands, built social media networks and became more engaged in musical and cultural initiatives. A large number of participants also began promoting folk music in their communities.
During interviews with participants we discovered something we had not expected: their listening habits had changed. On their playlists folk songs presenting EU heritage appears.

2023-1-PT02-KA220-YOU-000156550.title: Youth-led ECO community projects for prevention of school drop-outs
2023-1-PT02-KA220-YOU-000156550.summary:
<< Background >>

Being involved in creating educational programmes for different target groups in Europe and beyond, we were deeply concerned with the issue of early school dropout, which still remains a challenge across Europe. While some countries have already reached the EU’s 2030 target of reducing dropout rates, others continue to struggle, especially in certain regions. For example, Portugal has made overall progress, but areas such as the Algarve still face alarmingly high dropout rates. In Serbia, too, the numbers remain above the target, particularly for vulnerable groups.

We applied for this project because we saw a clear need to bring in some new and practical approaches that could motivate young people to stay engaged with education. Our aim was to connect schools with youth workers and involve students in social and environmental projects within their communities. With this approach we wanted to create learning experiences that felt meaningful and relevant, while also building cooperation between teachers and youth organisations.


<< Objectives >>

The main aim of this project was to contribute to the faster decrease in school dropout rates in our communities/countries, by providing additional approaches through offering quality youth work on involving students at risk into activities and programmes of initiating and implementing (eco) community projects, as a part of their service learning engagement and development of their competences for life, in interaction with their community.

The specific objectives of the project were:
1. Empowering youngsters in organising (eco) community projects and strengthening their competences for life through innovative toolkit and online course on initiating and implementing activities within green community service and learning programmes;
2. Empowering youth workers’ capacities in collaborating with schools on reducing the school dropout rates through developing community service and learning programmes for young students (mainstream and at risk) - through innovative curriculum;
3. Exchange good practices among 4 European countries with different realities regarding school dropout rates and the active citizenship of youth in communities and increase partnership on multiplication of the project results Europe wide.


<< Implementation >>

We have successfully implemented all the proposed project activities that include the following: 
•	Online kick-off meeting
•	Outputs:
-	Toolkit of youth work for organising eco community projects as a methodology to prevent school dropout
-	Online course for youngsters on step-by-step in organising eco community projects
-	Curriculum for educating youth workers in collaboration with schools on reducing school dropout rates through developing community service & learning programs
•	Online mid-term meeting
•	Piloting of Toolkit and Online course
•	Local training courses of youth workers in Portugal, Croatia, Italy, and Serbia
•	4 multiplier events in Portugal, Croatia, Italy, and Serbia
•	Evaluation meeting


<< Results >>

•	Developed and published Toolkit for developing youngsters’ relevant competences, in 5 languages (EN, PT, IT, HR, RS).
•	Accessible Online course for youngsters with step-by-step organising community projects, in 5 languages.
•	Developed and published Curriculum for training youth workers on developing community service/learning programme for prevention of school dropout, in 5 languages.
•	84 young people across the 4 countries of the project partners took part in piloting workshops for the Toolkit.
•	Total of 117 registered users successfully finalised the piloting version of the online courses and provided the valuable feedback.
•	53 youth workers across the 4 countries participated in the local training courses based on the Curriculum.
•	At least 16 teachers (four per country) expressed satisfaction with the quality and usefulness of the outputs.
•	A total of 136 representatives participated in the three national and one international conference, meeting the planned target.
-	At least 12 additional dissemination meetings were held (three per partner country), enabling direct engagement with organisations, institutions, and stakeholders.
-	A follow-up cooperation project idea was discussed and conceptualised.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2023-1-PT02-KA220-YOU-000160531.title: Padrões de Qualidade para Técnicos de Juventude
2023-1-PT02-KA220-YOU-000160531.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was developed in response to a structural gap in the youth sector at European level: despite progress in youth policies and the development of young people’s skills, there remains a lack of clear and operational quality standards for youth workers.
These professionals play a central role in empowering young people, but their work is often characterised by low recognition, a lack of a structured framework and inconsistent quality standards across contexts, which limits the impact of interventions.
In this context, the project addressed three main needs: the definition of a transnational framework of quality standards based on real-world practices and skills; equipping youth workers with practical tools and methodologies to improve the quality of their work; and strengthening the recognition of youth work by promoting links between practice, research and public policy.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to develop and validate a European framework of quality standards for youth workers, designed to guide, structure and improve professional practice in the sector.
The project’s central objective was to strengthen the capacity of youth workers by identifying and systematising key competences, effective practices and working methodologies, which were then translated into a practical handbook applicable in different national contexts.
At the same time, the project sought to promote the adoption of approaches based on non-formal education, active participation and critical thinking, contributing to a more intentional, structured and impact-oriented intervention with young people.
Another key objective was to strengthen the link between practice, research and public policy, ensuring that the project’s results are evidence-based and aligned with European standards.
The project aimed not only to improve the quality of the work carried out, but also to contribute to the recognition and appreciation of the role of youth workers in community development.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through a coordinated set of activities organised into different phases. Initially, coordination meetings and an in-person kick-off meeting were held, enabling the partners to align their objectives, methodologies and roles.
This was followed by a phase of research and data collection, including an analysis of good practices, a literature review and consultation with youth workers, with the aim of identifying key competencies and the sector’s needs. This process was reinforced by collaboration with a scientific body, ensuring methodological consistency and quality in the analysis.
In parallel, capacity-building activities were prepared and implemented, aimed at knowledge sharing among partners and the development of the skills of the professionals involved.
Based on the data collected, the project’s main output was developed: a quality standards manual for youth workers, structured around practical tools and applicable guidelines.
Finally, dissemination and scaling-up activities were carried out in different countries, promoting the results among relevant stakeholders and reinforcing the potential for utilising the outputs

<< Results >>

The main output of the project was the development of a European handbook of quality standards for youth workers, which sets out key competencies, effective practices and intervention methodologies, providing a practical tool that can be adapted to different contexts.
In addition to this central outcome, the project produced a set of intermediate outputs, including a compilation of good practices, data collected from youth workers and analytical contributions underpinned by a structured methodological approach, reinforced by collaboration with a scientific body.
In terms of outcomes, the project contributed to strengthening the skills of the partners and practitioners involved, enhancing their capacity to plan, implement and evaluate higher-quality interventions. It also promoted greater integration between practice, research and public policy, contributing to a more structured vision of youth work.
Furthermore, the project aimed to increase the visibility and recognition of the role of youth workers, creating the conditions for the adoption of the standards developed by other stakeholders at local, national and European levels.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2023-1-SK02-KA220-YOU-000159836.title: Service-learning in fostering youth civic engagement, diversity, and social inclusion in the CEE region
2023-1-SK02-KA220-YOU-000159836.summary:
<< Background >>

Service-Learning is a educational strategy integrating community service with curriculum-based learning. It enables young people to apply knowledge to real challenges while developing civic competencies, social awareness, and resilience. It is widely recognised as an effective approach to strengthening civic engagement, inclusion, and active citizenship. However, SL remained underdeveloped and unevenly distributed across CEE region. EU analyses (2017, 2020) show lower civic participation among youth in CEE compared to Western Europe. The Citizenship Education at School in Europe report (2017) confirmed that civic education is often disconnected from real-life contexts. A mapping study by Matej Bel University (2019) identified key gaps: dominance of ex-cathedra teaching, lack of shared good practices, insufficient competencies among professionals, and low youth civic engagement. Based on this evidence and partners’ experience, key needs were identified: lack of shared quality frameworks, limited capacity-building resources, absence of recognition mechanisms, missing digital tools for reflection, and weak advocacy and policy integration. SLIPSTREAM project addressed them through a coordinated, evidence-based transnational approaach.

<< Objectives >>

The SLIPSTREAM project aimed to advance service-learning as a recognised methodology for civic education and youth development across the Central and Eastern European region through five interconnected objectives: to establish a Regional Service-Learning Award as a quality-recognition mechanism celebrating outstanding SL projects by schools and youth organisations; to develop a comprehensive, transferable package of tools, quality standards, and training curricula equipping youth workers and educators with skills to design and implement high-quality SL experiences; to create a user-friendly digital Reflection Tool — the CEL Platform — supporting young people in structured self-reflection during and after SL experiences; to build and implement a coordinated advocacy campaign for SL at local, national, and European levels, raising its visibility and policy relevance; and to strengthen the professional capacities of partner organisations and create conditions for long-term sustainability and regional scaling of SL practice beyond the project period. All objectives were aligned with Erasmus+ horizontal priorities of Common Values, Civic Engagement, and Active Citizenship, and with the cross-cutting priority of Inclusion and Diversity

<< Implementation >>

WP2 – Two full RSLA cycles were delivered. In 2024, the Award covered Slovakia, Bosnia&Herzegovina, Kosovo, and Romania, receiving 114 applications with 27 advancing to international jury. In 2025, Croatia and Czech Republic joined, with 127 applications received and 25 advancing. Public ceremonies were held in each partner country, with international ceremonies in Banská Bystrica (2024, 138 participants) and Tuzla (2025).
WP3 – Service-Learning Toolkit - an open-access SL toolkit comprising a Handbook with Quality Standards, a Capacity Building Curriculum were developed. All resources were piloted through national trainings and validated via structured feedback.
WP4 – Reflection Tool - the CEL Platform – digital reflection tool was developed. Development followed a four-phase participatory process, culminating in public launch following pilot testing with 266 young people and 69 educators across partner countries.
WP5 – Advocacy Campaign–partners prepared Country Context Reports, CEV led Ambassador Training in Brussels (12 ambassadors), local advocacy actions in each partner country, EU-level advocacy, and a Final Advocacy Event in Brussels were implemented. A CEE Regional Advocacy Report with policy recommendations was produced.

<< Results >>

•	Two full Award cycles completed; Award infrastructure (rslaward.eu, submission tools, evaluation materials, manuals) fully developed and operational for future use.
•	SL Handbook with Quality Standards: Comprehensive open-access handbook covering all phases of SL implementation.
•	Capacity Building Curriculum: Training curriculum for educators and youth workers.
•	CEL Reflection Platform, digital reflection tool for youth was developed, publicly launched and operational across partner countries;
•	CEE Regional Advocacy Report including policy recommendations for all partner countries was dveloped

2023-2-BE05-KA220-YOU-000182214.title: And.Period - Menstrual Education against the taboos and prejudice
2023-2-BE05-KA220-YOU-000182214.summary:
<< Background >>

AndPERIOD – menstrual education against taboos, addressed the lack of inclusive menstrual conversations and education among young people. We identified that menstruation is still surrounded by stigma, misinformation, and gendered assumptions, which negatively affect the wellbeing of people who menstruate**. In our local communities, we noticed that many young people lacked safe spaces to talk openly about menstruation, especially those who do not identify as women. Thanks to framework of ERASMUS+,we as partnership aimed to create an international (un)learning experience that would empower youth workers and young people to challenge taboos, share knowledge, and challnage the narratives surrounding the period. Through this project, we responded to the need for inclusive and safe spaces for our participants, that need to embrace the menstruation as a natural and diverse experience, not limited to a single gender identity, presenting it as only hygenic and/or reproductive process. We also wanted to strengthen youth participation and cooperation across Europe in tackling health-related inequalities. 

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to empower both young people who menstruate,and those who don´t inviting both groups to the much-needed-conversation and reflections.  As partnership ( 5 organisations from 5 countries) for 18 months we were actively promoting menstrual education as a tool for inclusion, health equity, and social transformation. We have raised awareness about menstrual health beyond the gender binary, challenge taboos and stigma, and foster safe spaces for dialogue and (un)learning. Through non-formal,and informal, education activities, we sought to equip participants and our youth workers with knowledge and competences, confidence and critical thinking in order to (start ) loooking at period from an intersectional&holistic point of view. Both for thir own experiences and in their communities and cultures.By connecting youth workers and organizations across Europe, we also aimed to exchange good practices, co-create inclusive educational materials, and strengthen the capacity of the youth sector to address menstruation as a human rights and public health issue, that shows as how we treat those who menstruate in our socioeconomic and cultures spheres.  

<< Implementation >>

The project included a series of non-formal educational activities designed to explore menstrual health from an inclusive and intersectional perspective,on both locla and international level. At all moment, we as project coordinators and trainers, have highlighted the facts that we are not health workers, nor are we planning on menstrual cycles from biological aspects. We aimed to create the saffest space posible to explore what menstruation is, what role that is have, how is it seen, and question stigmas and shame arround it, on individual and public level.  We organized 3 international learning activities-one MYW and two YE. Local workshops were held for youth, focusing on personal stories, narratives and getting to know cycles and selfcare methods, menstruation and sustainability, poverty etc. All activities were designed to foster safe, empowering spaces and promote active participation of young people in shaping the narrative around menstruation. We´ve produced inclusive educational materials “”AndPERIOD workshops for youth activities “” for youth organizations. Thanks to our international campaign, almost 70 people from Palestina and Ukraine have recieved ( sustainable ) menstrual products.  

<< Results >>

Some of the most notable results that were achieved were: 

- Participation of almost 90 participants from more than 15 countries have attended our LAs,gaining much needed inputs and space to dedicate, for the very first time, 5-6 days to talk about menstrual cycles  

- Thanks to those activities we have created a toolkit “”AndPERIOD workshops for youth activities “” with workshops and shared model of projects that external organisations are invited to use and adapt to their own contexts (pdf attached)  

- Crowdfunding campaign that reached more than 15.000 people, and provided menstrual kits for almost 70 people in Palestina and Ukraine, thanks to colaboration with ActionAID.  

- The project also fostered the development of safe spaces and peer support networks, contributing to long-term community impact.  

- almost 40% of participants have changed their menstrual products to more sustainable ones – now using menstrual cup, or reusable underwear or pads. 

- New networks of both local and international partners that will join future actions and ( Erasmus+) projects

2023-2-BG01-KA220-YOU-000176867.title: Youth Placemaking Balkans
2023-2-BG01-KA220-YOU-000176867.summary:
<< Background >>

The Youth Placemaking Balkans project was initiated to tackle interconnected challenges across the Balkan region, where a history of conflict and displacement has left many young people traumatized and disillusioned. Current economic and political instabilities have further discouraged civic participation, created trust issues, and eroded entrepreneurship. To combat this, the project directly addresses a critical lack of civic initiatives in small and disadvantaged areas where limited volunteering opportunities deprive youth of platforms to practice democratic skills. Additionally, poor city planning and underinvestment have left cities without active public spaces, forcing young people into isolation or loitering in abandoned areas. This disconnection and political apathy frequently manifest as destructive behavior, including violence and vandalism. By utilizing the placemaking for active recreation approach, the project empowers youth to co-design and reshape their everyday public spaces to reflect their actual needs. This collective process transforms public care into an incentive for active citizenship while building essential life skills such as leadership, critical thinking, continuous learning, and collaboration. 

<< Objectives >>

The primary goal of the Youth Placemaking Balkans project was to promote active youth citizenship and civic engagement by integrating youth needs and voice into community placemaking initiatives. The project sought to establish a regional movement supporting local, youth-led activities that empower young people to become active citizens through spaces designed for them. To realize this goal, the project partnership targeted specific operational objectives. The project aimed to identify youth needs in public spaces and integrate them into a framework, building capacity through an online course and eighteen national workshops. Additionally, it aimed to develop youth entrepreneurial skills by facilitating twelve youth-led placemaking interventions across six countries, letting youth direct co-design and action planning. The project implemented six national structured dialogues with civic organizations and public administrations to integrate youth input into urban design policies. Finally, the network was upscaled to a regional level to reinforce cross-border cooperation through mentorship meetings. 

<< Implementation >>

The project implementation delivered regional research, capacity building, physical youth-led interventions, and policy dialogues. Under Work Package 2, partners mapped existing good practices by selecting five initiatives per country for thirty regional case studies. They conducted three youth focus groups per nation to identify urban needs and launched an interactive online co-design course, which successfully graduated more than two hundred participants. Three national capacity-building workshops were also executed in each country. For Work Package 3, youth directly spearheaded twelve physical placemaking transformations across the region, consisting of one large-scale and one small-scale intervention per country. Young participants managed stakeholder coordination, community consensus, and action planning. Each physical intervention concluded with tactical pop-up celebrations to activate the spaces, followed by a national structured dialogue with local policy-makers to establish functional, long-term advocacy networks. Finally, Work Package 4 upscaled the network to a regional level, utilizing two online regional mentorship meetings and a final transnational conference in Bulgaria with fifty external field experts.

<< Results >>

The project achieved its goals, exceeding targets. In management, it established a Project Handbook, a shared drive, and ran three transnational meetings in Belgrade, Skopje, and Sofia. Research led to a regional study and 18 focus groups involving 244 young people across six nations. This data shaped an interactive e-learning course that reached 211 certified completions, doubling the target of 100. Workflows also led to 18 workshops training 523 participants with Youthpass certificates.

Practical implementation delivered 12 youth-led interventions (six tactical, six large-scale physical transformations like calisthenics parks, murals, and sports hubs), mobilizing over 530 community members. These were leveraged for six National Youth Structured Dialogues with municipal authorities. Upscaling featured two regional online mentorship meetings on Zoom and a conference in Sofia gathering 144 delegates from eight countries. Finally, the communication campaign achieved a total reach of 1,860,745 individuals, backed by 43 media partnerships and 14 TV/radio appearances.

2023-2-HR01-KA220-YOU-000184352.title: Taking Matters Into Our Own Hands: Employment and Entrepreneurship
2023-2-HR01-KA220-YOU-000184352.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was developed in response to the barriers faced by deaf and hard-of-hearing youth in the labor market, including long-term unemployment, underemployment, lower wages, inadequate workplace accommodations, and communication challenges.
These difficulties are further compounded by the limited availability of educational resources tailored to sign language and specific communication needs, restricting opportunities to acquire new skills and reducing competitiveness.

At the same time, youth workers and educators often lack the specialized knowledge, tools, and methodologies needed for inclusive practice and effective support, making quality mentoring and career guidance more difficult.

The project therefore aims to address these challenges by creating accessible and tailored educational resources, empowering deaf and hard-of-hearing youth to participate more effectively in the labor market, and strengthening the capacities of the professionals who support them.

Its goal is to promote equal participation and inclusion, enhance the skills and competencies of the target groups, and provide sustainable tools for learning and professional development.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to empower two closely linked target groups: youth workers, often the first point of contact for mentoring and career guidance, and deaf and hard-of-hearing youth. Its main goal was to increase the employability of deaf and hard-of-hearing youth, improve their labor market position, and foster independence, professional confidence, and social inclusion.

For youth workers, the project strengthened their capacity to work with youth with hearing impairments through educational materials and targeted training, providing knowledge of the group’s specific needs, the impact of hearing loss on education and employment, and practical guidance for mentoring and developing employability and entrepreneurial skills.

For deaf and hard-of-hearing youth, tailored online courses and resources enhanced skills, competitiveness, and awareness of career opportunities suited to their abilities, including self-employment and virtual assistance.

The project improved understanding of youth needs, collaboration between the two groups, and mentoring practices, creating conditions to increase employability and strengthen labor market outcomes for deaf and hard-of-hearing youth.

<< Implementation >>

Several interconnected activities were implemented to empower youth workers and deaf and hard-of-hearing youth. A curriculum was developed for youth workers, providing knowledge of the impact of hearing impairments on education, socialization, and the labor market, along with practical guidance on communication, mentoring, and career support. A toolkit with detailed workshops was created for deaf and hard-of-hearing youth to strengthen employability and entrepreneurial skills. Two online courses further prepared youth for the labor market, self-employment, and virtual assistance roles.

All resources were specifically designed for deaf and hard-of-hearing youth, being content-, structure-, and communication-adapted to their needs, and integrated into an interactive online depository available in 5 languages with additional educational articles, ensuring easy access and long-term use. Resources were tested through trainings and workshops to ensure quality and practical relevance.

5 online social media campaigns and the project’s Facebook page promoted the resources, while dissemination workshops and a final conference presented outcomes, launched the platform, and supported networking among youth, professionals, and organizations.

<< Results >>

The main outcomes of the project include the development of a curriculum for youth workers, a toolkit for educators, two online learning courses for deaf and hard-of-hearing youth, an interactive, accessible online platform, and the project’s Facebook page. All resources were tested with the target groups, are permanently available, fully digitalized, and accessible in five languages, ensuring long-term usability and practical relevance.

Key results also include five online awareness campaigns and the final conference, which promoted the resources, increased visibility, and engaged a wide range of stakeholders. Additional outcomes include a higher-than-expected reach and participant numbers at trainings, workshops, and the conference, demonstrating strong interest and relevance.

The project had a strong inclusive dimension, as deaf and hard-of-hearing youth were employed as external contributors, directly participating in the development of educational resources and gaining practical work experience. The online courses are fully adapted to their communication needs, supporting self-paced learning, employability, and professional development.
