2023-2-RS01-KA220-YOU-000185011.title: YouthSpeakUp: Empowering Youth with Debate
2023-2-RS01-KA220-YOU-000185011.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address clear gaps in access to debate education and its sustainability. While interest in debate among educators and youth workers was high, many lacked the knowledge and structured resources needed to establish and maintain debate clubs. In practice, we observed educators motivated to introduce debate, but without clear guidance on methodology, club management, or long-term development.
This resulted in two key challenges. First, the absence of standardised, accessible materials made it difficult to start new clubs, particularly outside major urban centres and for youth with fewer opportunities. Second, existing clubs often depended on the knowledge of a single individual; when that person left, clubs frequently became inactive within one to two years.
At the same time, young people had limited opportunities to develop critical thinking, argumentation, and active participation in democratic processes.
The project addressed these needs by providing structured educational and organisational resources, strengthening the capacities of teachers and youth workers, and creating conditions for sustainable, transferable debate practices across different contexts.


<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to strengthen the quality and accessibility of debate-based non-formal education through three main objectives. The first objective was to build the capacity of youth workers and educators by providing practical tools, methodologies, and resources that would enable them to independently learn, teach, and implement debate activities. The project aimed to strengthen their skills and confidence while reducing reliance on informal transfer of knowledge.

The second objective was to increase accessibility to knowledge and teaching methods by creating structured, beginner-friendly, and freely accessible materials that could be used by individuals regardless of prior debate experience or location. Particular attention was given to underserved communities and young people with limited access to debate opportunities.

The third objective was to harness young people's sense of initiative and democratic participation by promoting critical thinking, argumentation, independent research, and constructive dialogue. Through strengthening debate activities and supporting the creation of sustainable debate clubs, the project aimed to encourage active citizenship and meaningful participation in democratic life.



<< Implementation >>

Three in-person transnational partner meetings were organised: TPM1 in Serbia hosted by Open Communication, TPM2 in Croatia hosted by Croatian Debate Society, and TPM3 in the Netherlands hosted by IDEA. Regular online meetings were held throughout the project for coordination and monitoring.

Development activities included drafting, reviewing, testing, translating, adapting, and designing the debate manual, organisational manual, glossary of debate terms, and educational video materials. Video activities included script writing, filming, editing, translation, and voice-over production. CDS wrote and recorded sepratly scripted videos tailored to the need of Croatian youth

Three focus groups were organised to review and improve the debate manual, organisational manual, and video materials.

Dissemination included 2 events in Serbia (74 participants total), 2 events in Croatia (40 participants total), 1 event in the Netherlands (40 participants), and 2 international online dissemination seminars (84 participants). Materials were additionally shared with debate clubs, schools, youth organisations, partner websites, social media channels, and IDEA's European network.

<< Results >>

We produced and translated a comprehensive debate manual and an organisational manual. The debate manual consisted of two parts: Beginner’s Debate Course, focused on debate skills and methodology, and Topical Workshops, focused on on specific topics in the context of debate. The organisational manual provided practical guidance on establishing and maintaining debate clubs, A glossary of debate terms was also developed to improve accessibility and ensure common understanding.

We also developed educational video materials that exceeded the original scope. Instead only the English videos being voiced and Serbian, Croatian and German having subtitles, we produced full voice-over versions were created in Serbian and German. Additionally, 11 sepratly scripted videos were produced specifically for Croatian youth and youth workers. In total, more than 800 minutes of voiced educational content were created.

Beyond outputs, the project directly trained 238 educators and youth workers, including 154 participants in in-person events and 84 in online events. These results strengthened educator capacity, improved access to debate education, and supported the creation and sustainability of debate clubs.

Our objective is to fill the gap of awareness concerning food waste; promote food waste avoidance skills in households.

<< Implementation >>

Local testing phase: No. 5 local activity called " Engaging Youth workers in Food Waste Action ". Participants: 2 trainers and 2 youth workers and educators from participating organizations to take part in the Local Activities.. BLENDED MOBILITY - participants: no. 20 young people per partner country belonging to the category of primary target group (18-30) will be involved in the local workshops.

<< Results >>

Training Format with tools of Non-Formal Education and guidelines for direct use by youth workers - ZERO Toolkit for young learners, covering 3 main topics: Food Waste and Climate & Environment; and Food & Health - Package of Workshops to be implemented during the Blended mobility Program - One Digital Game designed and created with the codesign methodology, covering two topics: Food Waste and Nutrition. - 1 Web Platform complying containing all the materials produced in the project

●	Foster active citizenship through engaging youth in awareness raising campaigns and peer support;

Activities: Mapping and creation of Booklet on MH good practices of YICs; Development of Mental Health Training Course for YI Workers; ToT MH Training Course; Development of Online Training Course; Forming international group of Young Activists and artists; Implement peer to peer MH awareness raisin campaign; Creation of Art Mobile Exhibition; Virtual Art Exhibition event; Dissemination Events on ERYICA GA 2025 and 2026.; Sharing practices and dissemination cross-sector international Conference.

We expect our project to yield significant outcomes, including enhanced mental health support for youth through improved training and resources for youth information workers. Additionally, we anticipate increased engagement of young people in mental health advocacy and peer support activities, fostering active citizenship and community resilience.

2024-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000256078.title: Providing Empathy and Care in non formal Education
2024-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000256078.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our objective in the "PEACE" project is to introduce mental health support through integrated sustainability in the youth work sector, at first focusing on debate-based youth work and then expanding our impact

We want to integrate mental health awareness as part of an integrated sustainability approach in youth debate clubs, elevate mental health literacy and well-being support skills among youth workers, develop resources, establish partnerships between youth work and mental health providers

<< Implementation >>

Mapping of sectoral experiences and knowledge transfer between institutional and NGO partners within the project consortium
Update existing curriculums so that they reflect the need for mental health/integrated sustainability and work in 200 youth clubs
Organise 8 national and two international training events for empowerment of youth workers
Setup a 9-module, 18-day, digitally certified youth worker qualification course
Create lasting cooperation between youth work and mental health providers

<< Results >>

The success of this project will make our youth work more inclusive and more supportive of the different needs and realities young people face.

This will happen when a network of over 200 youth debate clubs starts implementing activities that include developed methods and over 200 educators implement new skills and knowledge in their youth work.

As an ultimate outcome, we want to assert developed educations and protocols as the quality standard for youth overall well-being support in youthwork
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2024-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000256672.title: Peer power to empower
2024-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000256672.summary:
<< Objectives >>

With this project we want to tackle the rising anxiety issues among youth with fewer opportunities. Amazonas, Aspira and HumanCapiAct have significant roles working with them in local communities, as a place gathering a pool of volunteers. So, the practical solution we want to give with this project is to create a 3C peer to peer program for young people with fewer opportunities in order to prevent anxiety by empowering their three characteristics - competence, confidence and connection.

<< Implementation >>

Creation of the 3C peer to peer program aimed at empowering young people with fewer opportunities.
Creation of guidelines for program implementation.
Training course for testing the program.
Piloting the program in local communities. 
Creating e-learning platform for the created program and guidelines.

<< Results >>

The expected outcome of the project is created a 3C peer to peer program for young people with fewer opportunities in order to prevent anxiety. Online instructional training for youth workers, that will instruct them on how to support young people/volunteers in conducting the program. Lastly, the manual focusing on three characteristics aimed at strengthening in young individuals with the goal of reducing anxiety.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2024-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000256779.title: Resilient Roots: Nurturing Youth Wellness in the Climate Crisis
2024-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000256779.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Project focus on the problem of eco-anxiety where young people feel hopeless about the future, or powerless in the face of climate change. Project objective is to strengthen capacities of youth workers to help young people in dealing with eco-anxiety while at the same time empowering them in developing ideas and actions to make changes positive for the environment, society and economy. Partners from Croatia, Greece, Italy and Slovenia will develop innovative education program, methods and tools.

<< Implementation >>

Main project activities are: 1) Collecting best practices and developing questionnaire for measurement of eco anxiety, creating guidelines for youth on how to recognize and reduce anxiety and Creating innovative methodology for youth workers, new resources available online in 5 languages, TtT program 2) Train youth workers, piloting developed methods in International Youth Eco-camp in Greece and in organizing local youth eco-actions in each country, 4) Dissemination.

<< Results >>

Expected project results are: 5 organizations in 4 countries increased capacities to train youth workers to nurture youth wellbeing, mental health and their sense of initiative in the climate crisis, 50 youth workers participated in training for innovation in working with youth, 100 young people participated in program and initiated actions to make positive changes for the environment. Dissemination activities increased the number of youth workers familiar with new methods and resources.

SIRIUS - CENTAR ZA PSIHOLOSKO SAVJETOVANJE, EDUKACIJU I ISTRAZIVANJE

2024-1-LT02-KA220-YOU-000256610.title: Initiating New Standards in Journalism: Supporting (formerly) Incarcerated Groups with Honor and Tact (INSIGHT)
2024-1-LT02-KA220-YOU-000256610.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project focuses on the relation between media and crime, and a young person’s role in it. Our objectives include refining media representation through empowering young media representatives, supporting social reintegration of young (ex-)convicts, improving media literacy, and raising awareness about respectful portrayal of marginalized groups. We aim to achieve these by facilitating collaboration, providing training, and organizing events that challenge stereotypes and promote inclusivity.

<< Implementation >>

The project will have 4 WPs: 1) Project Management, 2) Research and Training, 3) Local activities, and 4) Communication and Dissemination.
WP2 activities: research, training & workshops.
WP3 activities: social events, need-based soft skills development program, activities for (ex-)convicts and young media representatives; launch of the exhibition and multiplier events; creation of the handbook.
WP4: high-level public conference; media campaigns; workshops with universities; result dissemination.

<< Results >>

Our project will change the future landscape of crime journalism, making it more humane and, thus, making it easier for (young) (ex-)convicts to reintegrate. The project will engage 153 young media representatives and 202 (young) (formerly) incarcerated people. It will equip both groups with skills that foster a more inclusive society and less biased news coverage. Through awareness raising activities, 200,000 people will be reached, leading to a more informed and empathetic society.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-1-NO02-KA220-YOU-000244518.title: Switch to ECO
2024-1-NO02-KA220-YOU-000244518.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The "SWITCH TO ECO" project aims to foster eco-friendly lifestyles among youth, improving environmental consciousness and actions. It seeks to strengthen partner organizations' capacities, facilitating knowledge transfer and equiping youth workers (50) with green practices they will incorporate in their work. The project also aims to bridge the eco-practice gap between countries with varying environmental performance, promoting the adoption of innovative sustainability practices across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

We are going to implement learning teaching training activity (25 participants), 3 transnational partners meetings, joint module design, online training for youth workers (50), development of the Environmental toolkit and development of mobile app for youth led initiatives.

<< Results >>

The project expects to achieve an increased understanding and adoption of eco-friendly practices among youth, the successful implementation of youth-led environmental initiatives, and the creation of a sustainable network of youth through a mobile application. Main results are a) produced modules, b) Enviromental Toolkit and c) mobile application. Additionally, the project aims to raise awareness about ecology, sustainable living and importance of "doing" and reacting on climate changes.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-1-NO02-KA220-YOU-000248357.title: NextGen - Humanity and Civic Participation Hubs for Inclusive Growth
2024-1-NO02-KA220-YOU-000248357.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The "NextGen" project aims to:  Bridge the accessibility and engagement gap for youth with fewer opportunities in distanced communities;  Foster  hubs for participation and creation;  Enhance digital literacy; Create a digital space for youth to connect, collaborate, to voice their ideas and needs;  Enable stakeholders to understand and address the specific needs and challenges of youth distanced from mainstream urban life, ensuring that responding services are relevant and effective.

<< Implementation >>

The project will assess community needs through dialogue with youth living in distanced communities, develop hubs for youth engagement and co-creation, empower youth with new knowledge and skills, launch an interactive digital platform for broader reach, conduct capacity-building for organisations and decision makers, and run campaigns highlighting youth engagement importance and challenges in distanced communities.

<< Results >>

Expected results include: Enhanced access to and participation in civic, cultural, and educational activities for youth in distanced communities; Increased digital literacy of youth, preparing them for active digital citizenship; A network of partnerships across Europe fostering equality in youth engagement; Policy recommendations and guidelines to support the replication and scaling of successful revitalization and inclusion of distanced communities; Stronger, more resilient communities.
topics: Reception and integration of refugees and migrants
Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas

2024-1-NO02-KA220-YOU-000251102.title: Youth Empowerment through Role Models – A Social Sports Development Program
2024-1-NO02-KA220-YOU-000251102.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our project seeks to enhance social sports for youth by empowering them and enhancing volunteer training. We'll initiate programs for inclusion, engagement, and personal growth, cultivating role models to inspire wider community involvement. It includes research and the development of an innovative curriculum, professional workshops, youth exchange and a robust dissemination plan. Anticipated results are higher involvement, skilled volunteers, stronger communities and shared best practices.

<< Implementation >>

- Develop a comprehensive training program for professionals;
- Professional development workshops to cultivate innovative training methods in youth sports and social activities; 
- Develop and implement social initiatives where young participants will be encouraged to develop and implement their ideas in order to become role models;
- Conduct an in-depth literature review on role-model impact for the development of an educational playbook;
- Organizing networking and community-building events.

<< Results >>

Our project is designed to improve youth skills, development, and social inclusion. We aim to train volunteer coaches to boost community involvement, refine youth work practices, and promote social cohesion through community programs. We anticipate enhancing youth's sense of belonging and mental well-being, fostering holistic growth and lifelong civic and sports engagement, setting a sustainable model for future youth and community initiatives.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2024-1-PL01-KA220-YOU-000243430.title: Youth Wellbeing Recovering Kit
2024-1-PL01-KA220-YOU-000243430.summary:
<< Objectives >>

How to support youth mental health if we can’t recognize what is a mental health issue? And on what basis do we advise youth to seek professional support? RECOVER aims to increase the cognitive and practical capacity of youth workers in order to 1. identify the (early) symptoms of mental health and wellbeing issues among youth, 2. to provide meaningful guidance to prevent health-related symptoms from becoming problematic, and 3. support youth in seeking suitable professional help.

<< Implementation >>

VALIDATION: carry human-centred analyses to validate identified needs and update work plans and the topics to be tackled.

DEVELOPMENT: co-design respective learning and training materials that convey the necessary competences based on the analyses.

CAPACITATION: empower the youth workers through newly designed outputs such the joint trainings, toolkit and manual.

ADVOCACY: increase the awareness of the community and provide policy recommendations and establish consultations with policymakers.

<< Results >>

1: Training on human-centred Participatory Approach for Staff
2: Methodological Manual on human-centred Participatory Approach 
3: Self-Analysis Participatory human-centred Workshops
4: Stocktaking Report of Context-specific Self-Analyses 
5: RECOVER Toolkit for Youth Workers
6: RECOVER Train the Trainers Program
7: RECOVER Local Pilots with young people
8: RECOVER VALORISATION FRAMEWORK and Impact plan
9: RECOVER MEDIA CAMPAIGN and community local events
10: RECOVER Policy Recommendations
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

Project proposal aims to establish an inclusive environment for youth with special needs via a purposefully tailored program encompassing Drama, Dance, Art, Yoga, and Sports activities, collectively referred to as (D DAYS) activities. Following activities will be implemented: 
- Project management activities 
- Tailored training events for capacity building of secondary school teachers in increasing of their skills to implement Drama, Dance, Art, Yoga, and Sports activities in their work with mixed teams of secondary school students and Youths with special needs.
- Activities related to the practical implementation of the newly created Transnational Inclusive Club's operation program
- Sharing and Promotional activities

<< Results >>

- Created and implemented tailored training programs for secondary school teachers
- Established Transnational Inclusive Club with branch-clubs in municipalities of Santa Maria da Feira - Portugal, Kochani - N. Macedonia, Piraeus - Greece and Daruvar Croatia
- Created and implemented Transnational Inclusive Club's Operational Program in four municipalities
- Created and implemented a Sharing and Promotion Plan with diverse communication strategies towards different types of relevant stakeholders

2024-1-RS01-KA220-YOU-000249918.title: Build UP: Building system resilience for youth achieving independence
2024-1-RS01-KA220-YOU-000249918.summary:
<< Objectives >>

By implementing Build UP we want to achieve:
1. Improvement of the support system for youth leaving alternative care, based on modern knowledge and principles of systemic resilience;
2. Enhancement of competences of youth service providers in building resilience through their services;
3. Strengthening cooperation of service providers in the fields of youth work, social care, education and health.

<< Implementation >>

Besides PMI, we will implement:
1. Mapping good practice examples of quality youth services, via realization of 1 meeting, 3 study visits and creation of 1 publication
2. System resilience model development, via realization of 2 model development and testing events, creation of 1 publication
3. Training for youth workers, via development of a training and its testing
4. Model implementation and dissemination, via local activities and promotion and dissemination events.

<< Results >>

- 1 model for a support system for youth leaving alternative care is developed, based on principles of systemic resilience
- 2 publications on contemporary knowledge on systemic resilience and good practice examples are created
- 1 training module for youth workers for respecting principles of systemic resilience in planning programs for young people is developed
- Innovations are introduced to participating countries' systems, and the resources are available on national and international level

2024-1-SK02-KA220-YOU-000257444.summary:

A4, KONTEJNER and Sonic Acts work at the forefront of the mainstream within the field of contemporary culture and art, with a focus on sonic practices and innovative uses of technology. In this project, we aim to create and disseminate accessible, innovative models and methodologies of non-formal and informal learning that employ current trends in audio and music production that reflect broader technological and societal changes.

We develop and deliver 12 long-term NFL modules, based on which we create educational manuals that are catered to a wide array of needs and interests. We build a community space + 3 local communities and an international community, through community building activities and a youth camp. We consult experts, exchange skills & knowledge and train the teachers who are part of the project. And we disseminate the results through a combination of online methodologies and physical and hybrid events.

- empowered and educated youth
- youth workers with higher skills and more awareness of the needs of disadvantaged youth

2024-1-TR01-KA220-YOU-000257867.title: Climate Change Awareness in the Mediterranean from Youth Perspective
2024-1-TR01-KA220-YOU-000257867.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to raise awareness amongst youth about the impact of climate change on the Mediterranean and the importance of preserving marine environments. It seeks to empower them as active participants in these areas and enhance their knowledge and skills in sustainable environmental practices.

Focusing on the effects of climate change on the Mediterranean, the project aims to strengthen young people's awareness of environmental issues and their capacity to generate solutions.

<< Implementation >>

The project aims to educate and engage youth on the impacts of climate change on seas, especially the Mediterranean Sea. Activities will include developing educational modules, and workshops, creating an online learning platform, and preparing research reports focusing on environmental conservation strategies. These activities will enhance youth awareness of environmental issues and enable them to develop sustainable solutions.

<< Results >>

The expected outcomes of the project include a comprehensive training module, an interactive e-learning platform, and the publication of a research report and youth declaration containing the views of young people on the impact of climate change on the Mediterranean. These outcomes will increase the youth's knowledge and awareness of environmental issues while contributing to the development of sustainable environmental management and conservation strategies at regional and international levels.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Quality and innovation of youth work

hr.name: Priority Actions Programme Regional Activity Centre

2024-2-DE04-KA220-YOU-000279154.title: ECO Reboot
2024-2-DE04-KA220-YOU-000279154.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Through the training of youth workers, a collaboratively developed curriculum, developed green learning spaces and an awareness campaign, organisations are able to inspire young people for local ecosystems and thus encourage their active participation in the protection and (re)construction of these ecosystems. ‘ECO Reboot’ thus contributes to the fight against climate change by actively involving the young generation in environmental protection at local level.

<< Implementation >>

‘ECO Reboot’ is based on a clear structure. A preparatory phase including the kick-off meeting, is followed by four phases, in each of which an ecosystem is intensively analysed from different perspectives over a six-month period. For each ‘ecosystem phase’, an international training course on this ecosystem will be implemented and local activities will be organised. Each partner will also organise a multiplier event. In total, 4 training courses and 4 multiplier events will be realised.

<< Results >>

The concrete results of ‘ECO Reboot’ at the end of the project are a basic curriculum for teaching green skills in the field of youth education with a special focus on the preservation and restoration of local ecosystems (WP2), the design and construction of green learning centres (WP3) and the development of interactive media products for teaching content outside the ‘natural context’ of ecosystems (WP4). Together, this will contribute to climate protection.

2024-2-DE04-KA220-YOU-000279357.title: Ensuring accessibility of digital and online resources for youth with disabilities
2024-2-DE04-KA220-YOU-000279357.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project goal is to foster an inclusive digital environment that enhances accessibility and empowers youth with disabilities, addressing the critical need for digital inclusivity. This project aims at mitigating the digital divide by ensuring that digital spaces and online resources; especially ones developed within youth work sector, are accessible to all, particularly focusing on youth with disabilities who are often marginalised in digital environments.

<< Implementation >>

-4 Transnational project meetings
-Curriculum “Designing & implementing accessible educational digital content & activities”
-Online course for youth workers
-Transnational Training of trainers
-Local training courses
-Toolkit “Assistive technologies & accessible digital content - workshops for activities with youngsters with disabilities” and piloting workshops
-Online course for youngsters with disabilities
-Online platform
-4 Online campaigns for 4 key results
-5 transnational conferences

<< Results >>

In 6 languages:
-Curriculum
-23 youth trainers at ToT
-5 local TCs gathering 75 youth workers
-Online course for youth workers, piloted on 30 youth workers
-Toolkit
-Pilot workshops with 75 youngsters with disabilities (YwDs) in 5 countries
-Online course for YwDs, piloted on 30 YwDs
-Online project platform with 20 educational articles
-4 Online campaigns reaching 30,000 YwDs & 3,000 youth workers; engaging 10,000 youngsters & 600 youth workers
-5 international conferences with 176 participants

2024-2-EL02-KA220-YOU-000272335.title: Young Organizers Using Technology for Hybrid Innovative IoT Solutions and Collaborative Tools
2024-2-EL02-KA220-YOU-000272335.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The YOUTH-IIT project empowers young entrepreneurs by integrating IoT training with collaborative tools like Arduino, ESP32, and Trello. It fosters entrepreneurial mindsets and practical IoT skills, emphasizing sustainability through energy optimization and waste reduction. Targeting young people with fewer opportunities, including NEETs, the project aims to nurture a generation of tech-savvy, environmentally conscious entrepreneurs, contributing to economic innovation and sustainability.

<< Implementation >>

The YOUTH-IIT project will implement five work packages over 30 months, covering studies, research, IoT content development, an e-learning platform, and the YOUTH-IIT App. Activities include translations, sharing campaigns, and testing in four EU countries. The project emphasizes environmental sustainability through IoT training, targeting energy efficiency and climate change mitigation. Results will be disseminated via online platforms, webinars, and conferences to maximize impact.

<< Results >>

The YOUTH-IIT project focuses on empowering 200 young entrepreneurs, including women and Ukrainian migrants, through an e-learning platform to develop IoT and collaborative skills. It promotes sustainable business practices, improving energy efficiency and reducing waste to support climate action. Extensive outreach ensures visibility, empowering women and migrants as primary beneficiaries.

2024-2-ES02-KA220-YOU-000291505.title: YOUTH RURAL EMPOWERMENT
2024-2-ES02-KA220-YOU-000291505.summary:

To address rural depopulation, aligned with the EU Strategy for Rural Recovery, young people will be empowered with key soft skills and strategic rural planning. Youth workers will be trained to mentor and support rural youth, equipping them to enhance their communities' vitality and sustainability. This initiative will build young people's confidence and competencies, enabling them to drive local development and attract newcomers, fostering long-term community resilience.

1.Best practice Collection. Research on best practices on rural youth policies.
2. Training Modules for youth workers to mentor youth in soft skills and strategic rural planning.

 20 youngsters in the Rural Learning Exchanges.

Products:

P2. Toolkit for Youth.
P3. Toolkit for Youth Workers.
P4. Video Pills/Infographics.
P5. Rural Experience Videos.

Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

2024-2-FR02-KA220-YOU-000270214.title: RISE - Resilience, Inclusion, and Sustainability through Empowerment in Climate Advocacy
2024-2-FR02-KA220-YOU-000270214.summary:
<< Objectives >>

RISE aims to empower young people, particularly from vulnerable situations, by enhancing their skills in climate change advocacy and environmental literacy. Through capacity-building, mentorship, local and transnational awareness campaigns and actions, RISE will equip youth to lead initiatives addressing the intersections of climate change, migration, and conflict, ultimately fostering resilient and informed communities.

<< Implementation >>

The RISE project will implement key activities across 5 work packages, including:
- Transnational capacity-building training for 30 young people.
- A mentorship programme to guide youth in creating a transnational climate awareness campaign.
- Thematic online roundtables to disseminate the goals and key themes of the project.
- Pilot actions at the local level to address climate issues.
- Advocacy Days for in-person engagement and replication of the transnational campaign in local communities.

<< Results >>

RISE’s expected results include:
- 30 young people trained in advocacy and environmental literacy.
- A youth-led transnational awareness campaign addressing climate change, migration, and conflict.
- Local pilot actions in 5 countries to foster community-driven climate solutions.
- Engagement of expert stakeholders in thematic roundtables and mentorship initiatives for further capacity-building.
- Increased youth engagement and leadership in climate advocacy.

2024-2-FR02-KA220-YOU-000292285.title: Expanding New Generations’ Access to Governance and Engagement
2024-2-FR02-KA220-YOU-000292285.summary:
<< Objectives >>

OVERALL:
• Boost youth workers' abilities to engage youth in active civic participation and enhance their understanding of democratic processes.

SPECIFIC:
• Equip youth workers with tools and methodologies to foster civic and political competences among young people.

• Develop and distribute innovative, participatory resources that encourage youth to understand and influence civic life.

• Empower youth to take initiative, fostering informed engagement and responsible citizenship behaviors.

<< Implementation >>

• Development of a Civic and Political Participation Competence Framework for youth and youth workers;
• Creation and testing of participatory educational resources to enhance understanding of civic engagement;
• Co-design of interactive forums to foster active participation and democratic engagement among youth;
• Compilation of action sheets and guides for youth workers on promoting civic participation;
