1) Reinforce the skills of youth workers by developing and disseminating practical tools to better support young people's mental health and prevent eco-anxiety
2) Give young people a voice to highlight their experiences and resilience in the face of climate challenges
3) Promote transnational cooperation and learning between organisations, while ensuring the sustainability of results through freely accessible multilingual tools

<< Implementation >>

Main project activities:
-Mapping and exchange of youth mental health practices
-Co-development and testing of training tool for youth workers
-Youth exchange on ecoanxiety
-Local media labs and youth voices add-on to the training tool
-Game development with youth co-design & testing
-Finalisation and translation of all outputs
-National and transnational training courses for youth workers
-Creation of support resources and online toolkit on the project website
-5 national multiplier events

<< Results >>

We expect the following outcomes:
-A multilingual training tool on eco-anxiety among young people for youth workers
-A series of creative productions made by young people (podcasts, videos, digital campaigns) to share their experiences of eco-anxiety
-An innovative educational game on ecoanxiety (EarthWise) in 6 languages, designed with young people
-An online platform bringing together all the developed materials
-A sustainable base of trained multipliers
-A structured dissemination strategy
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

hr.name: Institute for Research and Development of Innovations in Education EDUKRATIA

2026-1-FR02-KA220-YOU-000466487.title: Resonant bodies : incarner nos archives
2026-1-FR02-KA220-YOU-000466487.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Sustainably strengthen the skills of LGBTQIA+ young people and the professionals who support them, through analytical, creative, archival and participatory practices.
Increase the inclusion, visibility and recognition of LGBTQIA+ experiences in the European public sphere by promoting their active participation in cultural and civic spaces.

<< Implementation >>

Organisation of European learning mobility programmes and collective creation workshops.
Implementation of a skills transfer between partners.
Development of a methodological tool for collecting archives and an ethical protocol for secure digital dissemination.
Creation of tools to ensure the visibility, sustainability and transferability of the project: an interactive online map, collective European works and a methodological guide to replicate the project.

<< Results >>

Acquisition of sustainable and valuable skills (creative, analytical, digital and civic) by young participants.
Production of archives and collective creations to be disseminated.
Development of transferable methodological tools for professionals.
Capacity building for partners and creation of a sustainable European network promoting LGBTQIA+ inclusion.

2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000454019.title: Good Life: Youth Work for Fostering Resilience and Wellbeing in Complex Times
2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000454019.summary:
<< Objectives >>

GOOD LIFE aims to strengthen youth workers’ capacity to address rising psychosocial pressure and digital risks among adolescents by developing and testing a structured non-formal curriculum that integrates emotional resilience, digital risks and harms, personal (civic) agency. Through cross-national validation and multiplier trainings, the project will equip young people with skills for emotional self-regulation & wellbeing, digital risks awareness, self-efficacy and civic agency and initiative.

<< Implementation >>

• Research + youth focus groups in three countries to validate needs (90+ youth)
• Development of the GOOD LIFE European curriculum (30 exercises, activities, explainer animations across 3 thematic areas)
• Testing and refinement during one LTTA (12 youths + 6 youth workers)
• 2 international multiplier training seminars (46 youth workers/educators)
• Structured follow-up implementation and reporting (~1000 youths reached)
• Europe-wide GOOD LIFE materials promotion campaign (100k)

<< Results >>

• Increased capacity of 46 youth workers to address digital harms and psychosocial pressure
• Enhanced 'toolbox' of 100 youth workers (through GOOD LIFE online seminars)
• Improved youth self-regulation, digital awareness, sense of civic agency (~1000+ youth reached)
• Validated curriculum framework, transferable across EU
• Strengthened cross-national cooperation, standards in youth wellbeing and digital resilience
• Sustainable uptake of GOOD LIFE materials beyond the project duration
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

hr.name: Hrvatska edukacijska i razvojna mreža za evoluciju sporazumijevanja

2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000454026.title: Empowering Young Europeans for Democratic Participation through Public Speech
2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000454026.summary:
<< Objectives >>

VOICE UP! aims to empower young Europeans (16–30), including those with fewer opportunities, to strengthen democratic participation through public speech, deliberation and collaborative decision-making. The project enhances the quality and innovation of youth work by developing a European Competence Framework and Training Toolkit, creating structured participatory spaces and fostering sustainable dialogue between youth and community actors at local and European level.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement 7 local Voice Circles (monthly youth-led deliberative spaces), 3 Transnational Public Speech Academies, and youth-led local initiatives. The project will develop a European Competence Framework and Training Toolkit for youth workers, create a Youth Democratic Labs methodology and an online hub, and result in a European Youth Speech Festival to showcase youth voices and strengthen structured dialogue.

<< Results >>

VOICE UP! will deliver a European Competence Framework, an open-access Training Toolkit, a Youth Democratic Labs methodology and a digital hub. At least 210 young people and 35 youth workers will strengthen democratic and communication competences. The project will establish sustainable participatory spaces, increase inclusion of marginalised youth, and reinforce structured dialogue between young people and community actors at European level.
topics: Reaching the policy level/dialogue with decision makers

2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000455269.title: Ready-for-Crisis: Empowering Youth from Climate Awareness to Survival Skill
2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000455269.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to equip 500+ youth with practical survival literacy and preparedness for climate and social crises, mitigate eco-anxiety by replacing fear with agency through psychological resilience and panic-control training, innovate youth work by professionalizing the sector with new "crisis-ready" tools and capacity building for youth workers and drive civic action through youth-led research to map local risks and engage community stakeholders.

<< Implementation >>

We will design and deliver an integrated training cycle: 3 capacity-building webinars for youth workers followed by 10 local workshops for youth. We will mentor 6 youth-led research projects to map local risks, presented at an international online seminar. A key highlight is the Preparedness Skills Youth Camp in Croatia for hands-on survival training. All results will be finalized in a comprehensive 60-page "Ready-for-Crisis" Guide and hosted on an open online resource platform.

<< Results >>

Tangible results consist of the "Ready-for-crisis" Guide (featuring 6 youth-led research projects and 10 workshop plans in 4 languages) and an open online resource platform with crisis-response materials. Key outcomes: 500+ youth with increased resilience, survival literacy, reduced eco-anxiety, alongside professionalized youth workers equipped with innovative competences to deliver disaster-response youth activities and services.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000459882.title: Digital and Career Pathways for Young People with Lived Cancer Experience
2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000459882.summary:
<< Objectives >>

DigiPath aims to strengthen confidence, career clarity and digital readiness among young people aged 18–30 with lived cancer experience. The project seeks to develop and validate a structured Youth Reintegration Toolkit that supports their transition into education, employment and independent adult life, while strengthening inclusive and employability-focused youth work practices.

<< Implementation >>

The project will conduct a cross-country needs assessment, develop a modular Youth Reintegration Toolkit, organise a Train-the-Trainer activity and implement three national pilot cycles. Results will be disseminated through national multiplier events, a European webinar and open-access publication of the toolkit.

<< Results >>

DigiPath will produce a validated, open-access Youth Reintegration Toolkit including session plans, facilitator guidance and accessibility tools. It will train multipliers, engage young participants in pilot cycles and reach stakeholders across Europe, strengthening inclusive, employability-oriented youth work practices.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000462063.title: Sustainable Hub for Adolescents' Potential and Entrepreneurship in EU
2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000462063.summary:
<< Objectives >>

SustainAbility Hub equips 21 young people and youth workers from Croatia, Romania and Serbia with practical sustainable entrepreneurship skills, producing 12 investor-ready business plans, 3 open-access multilingual resources and reaching 120 additional young people through peer workshops. The project strengthens partner organisations' capacity and contributes to the green transition through ESG-aligned education and wide dissemination via the SustainAbility Hub platform.

<< Implementation >>

The project delivers structured desk research and focus groups across 3 countries, three progressive residential trainings, inter-training mentoring, peer workshop facilitation by trained youngsters, and a comprehensive dissemination strategy including the SustainAbility Hub platform, a 10-episode podcast series, national webinars and a final international online conference. Three intellectual outputs are co-created and published in four languages

<< Results >>

12 investor-ready sustainable business plans, 6 trained youth worker mentors, 3 open-access intellectual outputs in 4 languages, 120 additional young people reached through peer workshops, a live multilingual SustainAbility Hub platform maintained for 3 years post-project, a 10-episode podcast series, and strengthened organisational capacity across 3 NGOs in Croatia, Romania and Serbia to deliver sustainable entrepreneurship education independently.

2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000465070.title: New Ways of Inclusion: Redesigning Access to Culture for Youth
2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000465070.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to enhance cultural access for youth with disabilities by developing inclusive educational resources, digital tools, and practical guidelines. It strengthens youth workers' skills, promotes active participation of young people in Croatia, Slovenia and Estonia, and fosters innovation in accessible cultural content. Through collaboration and digitalization, the project ensures sustainable improvements in inclusive cultural engagement.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement educational exchanges, including study visits in Slovenia, Croatia, and Estonia, to share best practices in inclusive youth work. It will develop a handbook with recommendations, create an online platform with resources, and design micro-learning courses for youth workers. Dissemination activities, such as a final conference and an online campaign, will promote the project’s results and raise awareness of accessible cultural tools.

<< Results >>

The project will produce a comprehensive handbook on inclusive cultural access, an interactive online platform with practical resources, and 10 micro-learning courses for youth workers. It will enhance the capacity of partner organizations in providing accessible cultural content and foster increased participation of youth with disabilities in cultural activities. The final conference and dissemination efforts will ensure the sustainability and visibility of the project’s impact across Europe.

hr.name: Association for the Promotion of Creativity and Equal Opportunities Alternator

2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000466596.title: Resilient Youth Workers
2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000466596.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen the wellbeing, emotional resilience and long-term professional sustainability of youth workers, particularly those supporting young people with fewer opportunities in rural and low-resource contexts. It responds to identified burnout risks and limited organisational support by developing structured, evidence-based learning tools tailored to real youth work environments.

<< Implementation >>

The project will co-develop a shared theoretical framework and four structured learning modules on burnout prevention, self-regulation, professional boundaries and crisis support. The modules will be delivered through an interactive e-learning platform and complemented by peer reflection workshops. The programme will be piloted with at least 60 youth workers in Croatia, Slovenia and Portugal, followed by evaluation and dissemination.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver an evidence-based framework, four digital learning modules and structured peer reflection workshops supporting youth worker wellbeing. Participants will gain practical tools to manage stress, strengthen resilience and apply healthy professional boundaries in daily practice. The results will support professional sustainability in youth work, particularly in low-resource and rural contexts, and provide a transferable model for wellbeing-focused capacity building across EU.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000468203.title:
ECHO - Eco-emotions, Collective Horizons and Opportunities.
Strengthening youth preparedness through youth work responses to climate emotions
2026-1-HR01-KA220-YOU-000468203.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We will strengthen participation of young people in democratic life and their preparedness by understanding their eco-emotions, and how those affect their learning & engagement. Through participatory evidence gathering from youth workers and young people, we will translate research findings into practical educational tools helping youth workers to support emotional resilience, agency and participation. We will promote these tools widely across youth work, education and sustainability networks.

<< Implementation >>

The project combines research, participatory learning and tool development. Partners will conduct desk research, focus groups with youth workers and Youth Participatory Action Research involving young people as co-researchers. Based on findings, we will co-create educational tools and train youth workers to address eco-emotions and responses to them. The tools will be tested with youth and youth workers and improved based on feedback, then disseminated through youth and sustainability networks.

<< Results >>

• a research report analysing eco-emotions and their impact on youth participation;
• a participatory research handbook describing Youth Participatory Action Research methods for working with eco-emotions;
• set of practical educational tools for youth workers addressing eco-emotions and sustainability engagement;
• Theory of Change and an evaluation framework will guide implementation and impact assessment.
dissemination materials and knowledge sharing activities promoting the results.

2026-1-LT02-KA220-YOU-000466441.title: Game Changer – Non-Formal Youth Education with E-sports
2026-1-LT02-KA220-YOU-000466441.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to integrate esports into youth work as a structured tool for non-formal education and youth engagement. It will support youth organisations in overcoming barriers related to resources, knowledge, and safe implementation of esports activities. Through esports hubs, youth worker training, and practical guidance, the project will transform gaming into a supervised learning environment that develops teamwork, communication, creativity, and critical thinking while promoting inclusio

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement research, training, piloting, and dissemination activities. Partners will analyse existing esports practices and train youth workers to integrate esports into youth work. Three esports hubs will be established in Lithuania, Malta, and Croatia to host structured youth activities, mentoring, and local tournaments. Project results will be consolidated into a practical guidebook and disseminated through online channels and stakeholder events.

<< Results >>

The project will produce three operational esports hubs in partner organisations, engaging around 400 young people in structured esports-based learning activities. It will directly strengthen the capacity of at least 50 youth workers to use esports in youth work and non-formal education. A guidebook on integrating esports into youth work will be developed and disseminated. The project will also improve youth engagement, digital competences, teamwork, and inclusion of young people.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2026-1-NL02-KA220-YOU-000461402.title: RE.Play - Roleplay Education Play Again
2026-1-NL02-KA220-YOU-000461402.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Develop a transferable methodology for immersive roleplay in youth work, and an interactive Card Deck allowing youth workers to design their own simulations. Strengthen inclusion through adaptable formats, accessible to disadvantaged youth. Provide open-access resources (digital and print), and build a network of trained youth workers and young ambassadors who apply and disseminate the approach across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The project is structured into four work packages. 
WP1 ensures management and quality assurance. 
WP2 develops and validates the Simulation Strategies and Roleplay Tactics Card Deck through research and a RE.Play training course. 
WP3 tests immersive simulations in a youth exchange and produces the Big Simulation Case Study Methodology. 
WP4 ensures dissemination, multiplier events and long-term uptake across the European youth field.

<< Results >>

Simulation Strategies and Roleplay Tactics Card Deck – An innovative, user-friendly design tool, allowing youth workers to create and adapt immersive simulations using modular, question-driven prompts.
Big Simulation Case Study Methodology – A transferable, practice-based guide, documenting a real immersive simulation tested in a youth exchange, including facilitation steps, templates, and inclusion strategies.
Trained youth worker multipliers(ambassadors) in simulation-based youth work.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2026-1-NO02-KA220-YOU-000462839.title: Democratic Preparedness Lab
2026-1-NO02-KA220-YOU-000462839.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We aim to develop practical, evidence-based ways to work with democratic preparedness as a relational and trainable competence. Our WPs will 1) train youth researchers 2) co-create a toolbox of educational materials 3) train youth workers and other stakeholder in democratic preparedness 4) operationalise youth participation in research and educational tool development 5) share our process, findings, and tool cross-sectorially.

<< Implementation >>

Train 21 youth researchers, conduct participatory action research in 3 cycles, deepen the partners’ competence in participatory approaches to research and development, conduct 3 training activities for different target groups (for different WPs), create a series of webinars both international and national, pilot, produce, and test toolbox of educational materials about and for democratic preparedness

<< Results >>

Results will include 1 online platform; modular toolbox (produced in 14 exemplars for the partners); facilitator’s guide; partners’ staff improved competencies in creating educational materials; 21 youth researchers trained; 21 persons trained in webinar creation; 4 international webinars; 21 national webinars; research report of methodology, process, findings, and usage; 1 academic publication
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Quality and innovation of youth work

2026-1-RO01-KA220-YOU-000465501.title: VOICE-IN - Youth co-design for public policy: Strengthening meaningful youth participation in policymaking
2026-1-RO01-KA220-YOU-000465501.summary:
<< Objectives >>

VOICE-IN strengthens meaningful youth participation in public policymaking across Romania, North Macedonia, Croatia, and Germany by moving beyond symbolic consultation toward genuine co-design, institutional dialogue, and digital civic engagement. The project builds democratic resilience by equipping young people with policy literacy and advocacy skills while strengthening institutional capacity for youth-inclusive policymaking.

<< Implementation >>

The project delivers capacity-building workshops for 200 youth, transnational peer learning, and a joint participatory methodology. Youth co-design activities - thematic working groups, policy labs, and deliberative forums - produce policy-ready proposals presented to institutions through structured dialogue, youth hearings, and an EU-level event in Brussels.

<< Results >>

VOICE-IN produces a validated transnational methodology toolkit, 200 trained youth participants, minimum 25 policy-ready proposals formally presented to institutions, an expanded digital participation platform, a comparative research publication, and a European policy brief. Five national multiplier events and a final regional conference disseminate transferable models for participatory policymaking to practitioners and policymakers across Europe.
topics: Human rights and rule of law
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2026-1-SI02-KA220-YOU-000450595.title: NextGenWORKS: Preoblikovanje prihodnosti dela skozi oči mladih
2026-1-SI02-KA220-YOU-000450595.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The primary objective is to empower 120 NEET youth with digital competencies and the use of AI to enhance their employability. We will develop an innovative digital Hub, a MOOC academy, and a practical curriculum, enabling youth workers across six countries to modernize their mentoring approaches. The project aims to bridge the digital divide, promote the ethical use of technology, and establish a lasting European model for the faster activation of vulnerable youth in the labor market.

<< Implementation >>

We will implement five key phases: 1. Project management and consortium coordination; 2. Transnational research on NEET needs and digital skills gap analysis; 3. Development of the NextGenWORKS Hub, MOOC academy, and AI handbook for youth workers; 4. Implementation of pilot "Labs" – practical workshops for NEET youth across six countries; 5. Dissemination of results through national multiplier events, video production, and a final transnational conference in Novo mesto to ensure systemic impact.

<< Results >>

Key results include: 1. Transnational report on NEET digital needs; 2. NextGenWORKS Hub with an open-access MOOC academy and AI tools; 3. Digital handbook for youth workers; 4. Educational video series on AI for employability; 5. 120 empowered youth with Digital Open Badges. The main outcome will be a strengthened partner network and a signed Memorandum of Cooperation with stakeholders, ensuring a lasting impact on the modernization of youth work and social inclusion across the EU.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2026-1-SI02-KA220-YOU-000453791.title: W.I.L.L.  Dobrodošli v inkluzivnem učenju za življenje
2026-1-SI02-KA220-YOU-000453791.summary:
<< Objectives >>

With this project, we address the gap between declarative and actual youth participation. Our objective is to develop and validate a structured W.I.L.L. model that enables youth organisations to systematically plan, implement, and sustainably embed quality participation. The project strengthens youth workers’ competences and enables young people to achieve real influence and visible outcomes, thereby contributing to the quality and professionalisation of youth work.

<< Implementation >>

Transnational development of the model, pilot implementation of youth-led direct actions in four countries, professional validation through national seminars, external evaluation, strengthened dissemination and integration of the model. Youth workers will co-create the model, test it in real-life settings, and reflect on the impact of youth-led local initiatives. The final phase includes methodological refinement, Implementation Guide and establishment of a Community of Practice.

<< Results >>

The project will result in a professionally validated, transferable, and operational participation model (W.I.L.L.), supported by an Implementation Guide and practice-based examples. Youth workers’ competences and organisational capacities for sustainable youth engagement will be strengthened. The project will contribute to the systemic improvement of youth work quality, greater meaningfulness of youth participation, and the strengthening of democratic culture in the partner countries.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2026-1-SK02-KA220-YOU-000451985.title: YOLO. Youth Owning Life Offline
2026-1-SK02-KA220-YOU-000451985.summary:
<< Objectives >>

YOLO aims to improve young people’s digital wellbeing and mental health by promoting a healthier balance between online and offline life. The project will design and implement YOLO Camps that combine mindfulness, sport, creativity and community building. It also seeks to equip youth workers with innovative methods, integrate peer mentoring and digital tools, and give disadvantaged groups inclusive opportunities to strengthen resilience.

<< Implementation >>

The project will create six adaptable YOLO Camp scenarios, organise camps in all partner countries, and involve 180 young people and 60 youth workers. Activities include workshops, role play, outdoor challenges and reflective sessions. Results will be documented in an E-Book, adapted to local languages, and validated with stakeholders through testing and policy recommendations, ensuring quality, inclusiveness and long-term usability.

<< Results >>

YOLO will deliver a European Camp Model supported by tested scenarios, an E-Book with lessons learned, and Policy Recommendations for youth organisations. The Camps will improve the emotional and social competences of participants, especially disadvantaged youth, while providing youth workers with practical tools to address digital wellbeing. The project also contributes to European cooperation by creating transferable resources that strengthen innovation and quality in youth work.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

101050128.title: ASH MA - Art, Science and Health MA programme
101050128.summary: The ASH - Art, Science & Health – MA programme is envisaged as a two-year international graduate programme which aims to explore, re-imagine, and define the contribution of contemporary art in social wellness. The program will be designed by three participating universities and one non-governmental organization: University of Zagreb, Croatia, leading the consortium as a main beneficiary, representing The Academy of Fine Arts; Ionian University, Greece, representing the Department of Audio and Visual Arts; Singidunum University, Serbia, representing Faculty of Media and Communication; and KONTEJNER | bureau of contemporary art praxis, a non-governmental organization from Croatia. The main goal of the project is to set up a socially and globally relevant high-quality MA programme in contemporary arts based in practice and theory on transdisciplinarity and cross-sectoral cooperation, at the intersection of art, science and health. The project structure will follow the predefined joint mechanisms of the EMDM call on two levels. Firstly, the organizations included in the consortium will aim to design the joint standards regarding the administrative and technical requirements needed to be implement by three participating universities. Furthermore, the organizations will work to develop joint student standards, requirements, and learning outcomes as well. Secondly, the goal will be to design ASH programme curriculum, including the programme structure, methodology, content, and courses. This will be done through regular working sessions of people included in the project team, organized both in person and online. The initial content will be tested through a pilot course organized in each participating country which will be used to gain a necessary feedback on the quality of the draft programme. By the end of the funding period, the organizations will start the process of self-evaluation as a prerequisite for programme to be recognized and acknowledged on the European scale.

101050613.title: DSGN-PALL-CARE - Design and Implementation of Master Degree in Palliative Care
101050613.summary: The Design and Implementation of Master Degree in Palliative Care project aims to strengthen the capacities of partnering organisations to provide state-of-the-art transnational education and training practices in palliative care, answering the growing need for palliative care providers and raising the awareness on the importance and necessity of palliative care among the general public in the EU and wider. The project is implemented by three higher education institutions: the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Health Osijek (Croatia), University of Maribor Faculty of Health Sciences (Slovenia) and University of Sarajevo (Bosnia and Herzegovina). With the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Health Osijek as the project coordinator, the partners will design and develop a fully integrated and sustainable joint Master study programme in palliative care proposal. Given the rising need for palliative care services, there is also a growing need for highly educated professionals who will provide those services. As Master level university education in palliative care is available in few countries, the project will explore the best practices and innovations abroad and encourage students to seize the mobility opportunities. It will allow the partners to identify the need to improve the knowledge and competencies of teaching staff for the development, implementation and continuous improvement of learning by working in order to acquire the necessary competencies during the 15 months of project implementation and allow their further development after the project ends. The partners will exchange knowledge and best practices through regular communication, meetings and a study visit. The joint Master programme proposal in palliative care, which will fully comply with the requirements of the EHEA, will enable the partnering organisations to set the ground for an innovative approach to teaching, learning and training and set the ground for a future joint Master programme in palliative care.

hr.name: SVEUCILISTE JOSIPA JURJA STROSSMAYERA U OSIJEKU, FAKULTET ZA DENTALNU MEDICINU I ZDRAVSTVO OSIJEK

101239560.title: MaStER_G - Master Study of Environmental Resilience to Geohazards
101239560.summary: The MaStER_G (Master Study of Environmental Resilience to Geohazards) project proposes a pioneering international master's program focused on environmental geotechnics and geohazard management bringing together institutions from Croatia, Serbia, North Macedonia, Iran and Brazil. Addressing key Erasmus+ priorities of environmental resilience, regional collaboration and educational inclusion, the program responds to increasing challenges posed by climate change and geohazards across the Western Balkans and beyond. Based on comprehensive needs analysis, the project will develop an integrated curriculum leveraging multidisciplinary expertise and real-world field experiences. Through its innovative "learning by sharing experience" methodology, students will study at actual geohazard sites while engaging in cross-border knowledge exchange through an interconnected network of six international laboratories. The program combines traditional engineering education with advanced digital tools and AI-supported learning, emphasizing critical thinking and practical problem-solving skills. Market analysis confirms strong employment prospects with the civil engineering sector facing workforce aging challenges. Through strategic partnerships between Higher Education Institutions and industry stakeholders MaStER_G aims to develop professionals capable of addressing complex geological and environmental challenges while fostering long-term regional resilience to geohazards.

101240586.title: EMDI BAG - Erasmus Mundus Master Degree in International Business & Geopolitics
101240586.summary: The aim of the EMDI BAG project is to develop a joint Master programme in International Business & Geopolitics, which is highly relevant in today’s world where global economic and political dynamics are deeply intertwined. The study programme will aim to equip students with analytical skills to assess geopolitical influences on business decisions, enhance strategic resilience and promote international collaboration through an interdisciplinary and multinational approach. By incorporating real-world case studies, partnerships with global institutions and student mobility pathways, the programme will ensure a comprehensive education that meets the needs of business and policy makers. The promotion of EU values, the focus on sustainable ecosystems and the innovative teaching structure make the programme a unique and timely addition to the higher education landscape and strengthen the international dimension of the European Education Area. Developed by 10 participating institutions, 7 members of the DIVERSE European University Alliance with the Seal of Excellence and 3 non-European partners, the programme will create an authentic international learning experience for students from all over the world while fostering transnational collaboration between teachers and researchers from the participating institutions. The project will bring together a total of 20 senior study field experts and curriculum design experts with clearly assigned responsibilities in the development of the curriculum and curriculum-related content and outcomes, as well as quality assurance experts with experience in transnational quality assurance of transnational higher education. The development of the joint study programme with student mobility embedded in the curriculum will follow the European Approach to Quality Assurance of Joint Programmes and the project will conclude with the submission of the study programme for accreditation to an EQAR-registered agency.

101241110.title: PIGMENTS - PaInts and coatinGs: Material Engineering, desigN and innovative Technologies for Sustainability
101241110.summary: The proposed EMDM titled “PIGMENTS – PaInts and coatinGs: Material Engineering, desigN and innovative Technologies for Sustainability” aims to address the growing demand of the job market for skilled professionals in the sustainable coatings and paints technology sector, which is currently underrepresented in higher education across Europe. This master’s program will be developed by a consortium of higher education institutions from Europe and Canada, in consultation with leading industrial associations in the subject area. The master’s program will focus on innovative technologies in paint and coating materials, with a strong emphasis on environmental sustainability and digital transformation in compliance with the EU Strategic Agenda 2024-2029 and Erasmus+ programme priorities. The curriculum will provide students with a broad, interdisciplinary technical skillset, including surface engineering, formulation engineering, nanotechnology, Industry 4.0 tools, etc. In addition, the program will include languages and soft skills such as critical thinking, project management, and industrial property, which will further enhance graduates' employability and competitiveness in the job market. The main goals of the project are to collaboratively develop a cohesive and fully integrated Master’s program curriculum, formalize a comprehensive framework for administrative operations, student services, accreditation, and awarding policies, and establish a compelling value proposition and business model to attract high-quality students from around the world.

101049277.title: EMMIE - Erasmus Mundus Master in Impact Entrepreneurship
101049277.summary: Our societies are currently facing major changes and challenges, being climatic, environmental, technological (digital and gene), demographic (including migration), economic (poverty) and, ultimately, ethical (values). In order to face these challenging issues, our world needs to be reinvented. It needs innovations that matters! In particular, our societies require more entrepreneurs with mindsets, skills, and sense of purpose needed to thrive in a rapidly changing world. Impact Entrepreneurship refers to the process favouring the creation and growth of enterprises that are ethical, transparent and has meaningful impact on our lives and society. Unlike non-profit, they focus on creating social impact through market strategies. Impact entrepreneurs focus on the triple bottom-line: Profits-People-Planet, to achieve the appropriate balance between each dimension. The mission of this master is to contribute to the education of a new generation of impact entrepreneurs. Its ultimate vision is to contribute the creation of an inclusive economy driven by equity values that give meaning to living together by creating human, ecological and economic value through an entrepreneurial approach. Erasmus Mundus Master in Impact Entrepreneurship (EMMIE) is an innovative 90 ECTS Master based on full mobility. EMMIE is supported by a consortium composed of three upscale European Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) in management, innovation and entrepreneurship whose excellence has been recognized by European and international accreditations from independent organizations. The ambition is to position that Master as a key international reference on the European Landscape in order to recruit the best international students willing to develop their skills and competences to build entrepreneurial projects having a positive impact over one of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of United Nations (UN) with a special focus on the climate and social inclusion challenges.

101050446.title: PROMISE - Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Sustainable Mineral and Metal Processing Engineering
101050446.summary:
The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Sustainable Mineral and Metal Processing Engineering-PROMISE is being established due to the awareness of increasing demands in the quantity and diversity of minerals, metals and materials as we move towards renewable energy, electromobility, digital communication and other clean-energy technologies. The EMJM PROMISE aims to produce world-class mineral processing engineer postgraduates and future leaders to support the sector into a sustainable future. PROMISE is a two-year and 120 ECTS Master’s Programme. The language of instruction in PROMISE is English and incentives to learn the partners' national languages which will provide a broad multidisciplinary education in the sustainable recovery of valuable minerals and metals. The consortium organizing PROMISE consists of four Universities, the University of Oulu-Finland, the Montanuniversität Leoben-Austria, the University of Zagreb-Croatia and the University Tecnica Federico Santa Maria-Chile. These partners complement and strengthen each other by involving top-level mineral processing laboratories, pilot plants, analytical equipment and recognized scholars and experts. In addition, the consortium has strong ties with the processing industry and a cluster of 31 mining companies, research centres, suppliers and universities demonstrated their endorsement to this program (as associate partners) this provides an excellent environment for the success of this master programme.
Students will have broad competence with specialisation in the main areas of mineral beneficiation emphasised in better mineral recovery from primary and secondary sources, metal recycling (urban mining), by-product recovery meeting the demands of today's industry and environmental protection as an integral part of the circular economy. Students will move to at least three HEIs. Upon completion, students will be awarded multiple master’s degree Diplomas and a Diploma Supplement.

101050466.title: DAFM - Sustainability in Agriculture, Food Production and Food Technology in the Danube Region - Danube AgriFood Master
101050466.summary:
Sustainability in Agriculture, Food Production and Food Technology in the Danube Region (Danube AgriFood Master – DAFM) is a two-year (120 ECTS) joint degree master in English.

It is a unique blend covering the whole food supply chain from a sustainable combination of ecologycal and conventional agriculture, food safety, soil, water and climate issues, biotechnology, energy systems, which are hot issues worldwide, also proven by the world pandemic as well as the extended circle of DAFM supporters (ministries, companies, NGOs). The added value of DAFM is the combination of special expertise and complementary strengths of each university  in a jointly integrated, interdisciplinary curriculum.

Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Hungary (MATE), Czech University of Life Sciences, Prague, Czech Republic (CULS), University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna, Austria (BOKU), University of Zagreb, Croatia (UNIZG), Banat’s University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine „King Michael I of Romania”, Timisoara, Romania (BUASVMT), Slovak University of Agriculture in Nitra, Slovak Republic (SUA) and University of Novi Sad, Serbia (UNS) offer up-to-date, research based teaching contents and methods to students with a BSc and background in natural, technological and economic sciences.

DAFM Alumni have academic knowledge focusing on the Danube Region (perfectly transferable to any other river basin area), as well as transversal skills (critical thinking, foreign languages, intercultural competences, entrepreneurial qualifications).

The acquired skills and comprehensive knowledge enables graduates to successfully work for public offices, research institutes, development agencies, regional advisory companies, wholesalers/retailers, food-processing companies, NGOs  and governmental institutions. Involvement of companies and similar stakeholders guarantees the constant analysis and update of  the curriculum with regard to job-market needs.

101050597.title: JMPMB - EU-CONEXUS Joint Master Programme in Marine Biotechnology
101050597.summary: The joint Master programme in Marine Biotechnology is a transnationally integrated multidisciplinary programme that provides high-quality academic education and professional competencies for professionals working or intending to work in the area of marine biotechnology. Integrating the skills map studies previously described, the programme has been designed so that it entirely covers the marine biotechnology pipeline from biodiscovery to market launch enabling the student to integrate in a variety of professional careers in the Marine Biotechnology sector. The joint Master programme in Marine Biotechnology (JMPMB) will be delivered by six partner universities (Universidad Católica de Valencia (Spain) – Programme Coordinator University, La Rochelle Université (France), Agricultural University of Athens (Greece), Universitatea Tehnica de Constructii Bucuresti (Romania), Klaipėdos Universitetas (Lithuania), Sveučilište u Zadru (Croatia) in association with two Associated Partners (Waterford Institute of Technology (Ireland) and Universität Rostock (Germany) and in collaboration with a large number of stakeholders from companies and research centres. The six universities and partners joined together to merge their strengths and know-how in an interdisciplinary JMPMB and to offer the students to study at an international inter-campus European University.

101081356.title: NeuroData - International Master in Brain and Data Science
101081356.summary:
Modern neuroscience has reached a point where progress requires analyzing vast amounts of data, a skill not traditionally provided to neuroscientists. At the same time, data scientists lack specialized training in neuroscience, thereby lacking a significant perspective that influences the quality and depth of their insights. A new academic trend where neuroscience is introduced as a separate educational track at the undergraduate level further hinders the ripeness of specialists as their education lacks essential features.
These developments drive the pressing market demand for combined brain and data expertise in neurotech, technological innovation, healthcare, and education. These conditions present a unique opportunity for educational innovation in the form of an out-of-the-box educational pathway focusing on the intellectual mobility of multidisciplinary scholars into the growing field of neuro-data science.
In modern science, breakthroughs often occur at the intersection of multiple disciplines. The proposed project presents a highly needed yet lacking synergistic training program in brain and data sciences. It aims to develop an integrated multidisciplinary curriculum in brain and data sciences to cultivate researchers with in-depth knowledge in both fields. Students will be trained in foundational neuroscience and data science during the first program year while applying these skills to analyze neural data during their second year. 
Students will study and research in leading institutions and countries. This holistic approach to students’ training will enable them to forge new mindsets and approaches while increasing individual contributions to a knowledge-based economy and society. Introducing this program to European HEIs will create a new generation of multidisciplinary scholars, highly skilled in investigating the most complex problem faced by the human race: the human mind and brain in health and disease.

101128126.title: RePIC - Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Redesigning the Post-Industrial City
101128126.summary: Eight members of the European University of Post-Industrial Cities (UNIC) have collaborated to create the integrated transnational study programme Redesigning the Post-Industrial City (RePIC), a two-year, English-taught joint master degree with 120 ECTS. Building on the complementary strengths of the vibrant UNIC Partnership and involving a broad range of associated partners from government, industry, and the public, RePIC provides for visionary, future-oriented perspectives on the city and a life-changing physical and virtual student mobility experience. RePIC fosters multidisciplinary and cross-cultural thinking to critically respond to issues of superdiversity by placing inclusion and mobility at the very core of its new inter-university campus, and thereby transcending cultural, national, and disciplinary boundaries. RePIC students can meaningfully engage in shaping society by developing an understanding of post-industrial cities and their environments and by creating research-based solutions to advance urban transformations. Based on a rigorous curriculum, RePIC serves as a catalyst for innovative education putting a spotlight on engaged research and evidence-based practices such as City Labs. Our ambition is to build a global knowledge and innovation community committed to the co-creation, co-design, and co-production of transformative approaches to more sustainable and resilient urban futures around industrial heritage settings and cities in transition. RePIC will enrol its first students in fall 2023. The intake of students takes place annually, with an anticipated cohort size of 60 students. Graduates will be awarded a joint master degree that will allow them to make a difference in this challenging world and transfer the community responsibility orientation of the course into society.

101180476.title: EU-CORE - EUropean master on COntrol of Renewable Energy systems
101180476.summary:
The EU-CORE Project (“EUropean master on COntrol of Renewable Energy systems”) is a 2-year Joint Master’s Degree that will
be operated by École Centrale de Nantes (ECN), Brandenburg University of Technology Cottbus-Seftenberg (BTU) and the
University of Zagreb (UNIZG). The objective is to train top-level world-wide engineers in the design of advanced technologies of
Renewable Energy Systems Control and contribute to the creation of a new generation of graduates needed to secure European
environmental and energy ambitions of the “Green Deal”. The existing programmes linked to the Renewable Energy Systems in
the Erasmus+ framework seem to be focussing on one source only; none of them seems to be covering the main renewable energy
sources and their associated control issues in the way offered by EU-CORE. Thanks to a selection of top-level academic and
industrial partners, the skills developed throughout the EU-CORE project will be keys to a large number of positions and careers
in the renewable energy industry. The Consortium partners complementarity makes students attend specific fields, in which the
partners are internationally recognized. Thus, students will be trained in Wind Energy System Control, Energy Storage
Management, Control of Solar and Hydrogen Systems and their integration into the grid. To be fully in line with labour market
requirements, the Academic Programme is completed by soft/transferable skills training during Winter/Summer Schools. By this
way, EU-CORE offers a high permeability between education, research, innovation, soft-skills, industrial needs, and environmental
concerns. To complete the harmonisation of EU-CORE within the higher education and research EU landscape, the Programme
performs a joint EU initial accreditation and will deliver a Joint Degree. To summarise, EU-CORE will train future experts in the
RES field and will consequently contribute to the EU climate-neutral objectives by 2050.

101089709.title: EU-CONEXUS Plus - A significant step forward for the European University for Smart Urban Coastal Sustainability
101089709.summary: EU-CONEXUS Plus is mainstreaming, deepening and expanding the European University for Smart Urban Coastal Sustainability EU-CONEXUS. Building on established strategic cooperation structures, joint activities and procedures EU-CONEXUS Plus introduces three former associated partners as full members, creates a legal entity for the implementation of joint actions, continues the set-up of a joint infrastructures and stabilises the scope of cooperation chosen around the thematic focus “Smart Urban Coastal Sustainability” (SmUCS) while covering all missions of a university: education, research, innovation and service to society. A special focus is laid on the empowerment of students’ self-governance and their initiatives. Regarding education, joint course programmes on SmUCS on all levels, micro-credentials to broaden flexibility, personalisation and LLL aspects and special modules aiming at attracting BSc students to research are planned. Training on pedagogical methodologies and tools is intensified. Support for the development of study programmes proposed by the teaching community will be centralised. For research, the Joint Research Area is further supported by enlarged mobility programmes, networking events and the introduction of scientific management staff promoting the linkage of research activities on SmUCS. Regarding innovation, a support service is established around knowledge and technology transfer promoting entrepreneurial mindsets and creativity among staff and students. The already established Career network widens its scope of action by offering trainings on job readiness and facilitating work-based experiences. The EU-CONEXUS Stakeholder Academy further enhances the close connection with partners’ ecosystems, with a special focus on regions, cities and ports. Outreach to local communities is achieved by continuing the successful international school contest and the organisation of cultural festivals in a local setting.

101089757.title: SEA-EU 2.0 - The European University of the Seas Alliance navigating towards modern and co-transformative inter-campus life; people-driven, planet-friendly and knowledge-based progress for all
101089757.summary:
SEA-EU 2.0 is a geographically-balanced enlarged university alliance with a coastal and marine-maritime character as its hallmark. The distributed inter-partner open  governance will consolidate transformative structures and dynamics that reinforce complementarities, multiculturalism and multilingualism in its nine nodes.

Through proven internal and external evolving dynamics, SEA-EU 2.0 channels its own development while unfolding into a decisive co-transformative EHEA and ERA actor, intensifying the effect of high quality European HE missions. 

The integration of the social, green and digital transitions equips SEA-EU to spark the new genion of European HE Campus life into advanced forms of blended interactions, mobilities and international collaborations. In alignment with an encompassing set of multi-level policy targets (6 Commission priorities for 2019-24, UN SDGs…), SEA-EU 2.0 long-term vision reflects and reinforces the core European values based on people-driven, planet friendly, and science-based progress.

Education and training approaches will offer exclusive lifelong learning opportunities to students of all ages. By blending academic rigor with citizen science, professional knowledge and policy vision, SEA-EU 2.0 will become a role model for novel knowledge integration pathways. Furthermore, R&I multi-stakeholders’ co-creative processes (inclusive, international, interdisciplinary and intersectoral collaborations) will result in a) novel ways to generate real societal impact of all HEIs’ missions; b) targeted and more effective knowledge transfer, and c) long-lasting entrepreneurial ecosystems. This will highly influence the design and implementation of modern integrated dissemination and communication plans with feedback and feedforward co-creation loops informing the SEA-EU 2.0 presence in society.

101089770.title: YUFE 2030 - Young Universities for the Future of Europe (YUFE) Alliance 2030
101089770.summary:
In only 2 years the YUFE Alliance (Young Universities for the Future of Europe) has developed a leading model of a student-centred, equalitarian, open and inclusive European University, and is fully committed to make the next step towards an innovative, globally competitive, and attractive European Higher Education Area. YUFE will continue to make our shared dream become a reality: the emerging of a unique, holistic, diverse, and innovative European University by 2030. 

YUFE has developed a ground-breaking vision where education, research & innovation, and societal impact seamlessly interconnect in seven pillars fostering our joint goal in education: to provide high quality, open and flexible European academic curricula, the education for the future, for life-long learners of all backgrounds (II). Academic research, innovation (III), and societal responsibility leading to impact (IV) are fully integrated in the YUFE ambition. YUFE Digital University will provide for the development of both digital tools and instruments and digital policy frameworks and skills (V).  

YUFE identity and values (I) are reflected in all Alliance’s activities and are prominent in the narratives that YUFE brings forward in its sustainable strategy, with the aim to establish a socially responsible European University, working together to develop a people-centred, inclusive, and open European University for their students, staff and communities. 

To achieve these ambitious goals, the YUFE Alliance is moving towards a federation-like structure with an inter-university YUFE campus in the long term. Institutional development provides a hub leading to new models of governance, management processes and staff development (VI). Finally, via dissemination and capacity building (VII), YUFE is all set to serve as a role model and influence and push transformation across and beyond the existing European universities.

101089937.title: EU4DUAL - European Dual Studies University
101089937.summary: EU4Dual will form the first European University dedicated to dual studies characterised by the fact it combines two places of learning, where, the university, emphasises "theory" and the workplace, emphasises "practice". Our 9 partner institutions, and our network of over 35 associate partners will work together to mobilise: education, research and innovation and service to society at the regional level with the mission to use transnational dual education to help Europe address major societal challenges. These Grand Challenges include: - future of work - green economy - healthy living Our collaboration will, by 2025 lead us to: • establish a sustainable cooperation mechanism that founds the “European Dual University” and provides for its longterm operations and funding; • set up a Centre of Excellence on Dual Education, which promotes research, knowledge exchange, capacity building and development of the sector; • implement new learning pathways for dual education whereby most of our programmes include research, teaching or internship elements from at least two members of the institution • launch 2 new joint masters programme, a joint dual doctorate programme and a joint micro-credential portal, offering continuing career development and new skills created by us as well as our industry partners • launch an ecosystem of joint research projects, at micro-, meso- and macro-level supporting our grand challenges • create an unparalleled transnational work-based learning scheme with strong support from international business • Provide mobility experiences for at least 50% of our staff and students Our innovative management model will see students, companies and regions lead the institution, by holding most voting rights in our management structures. Beyond 2025, we intend to grow the university to include members from 20 countries, and become the world’s premiere dual-studies institution in terms of quality, size and breadth of activities.

101123496.title: UNIC - The European University of Cities in Post-Industrial Transition

hr.name: SVEUCILISTE U ZAGREBU SVEUCILISNI RACUNSKI CENTAR

101124491.title: COLOURS - COLlaborative innOvative sUstainable Regional UniverSities
101124491.summary:
The European University Alliance COLOURS (COLlaborative innOvative sUstainable Regional univerSities) unites 9 universities with around 126,000 students and 12,300 staff members in Croatia, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Spain, Sweden, North Macedonia and Latvia. These institutions are joined by 55 Associated Partners who will act as collaborators and multipliers in regional innovation ecosystems. The COLOURS approach, linking Open Innovation, challenge-based teaching and impact-driven research to regional Smart Specialisation Goals, will initiate social and technological innovation affecting over 21 million citizens. 
All COLOURS universities are regional drivers of innovation, united by a deep commitment to 
a) foster a profound transformation in academic institutions, implementing a more COLOURful definition of academic excellence, 
b) enhance sustainable and participatory regional developments across Europe, acting as a role model for more COLOURful regional innovation ecosystems, 
c) contribute to a Triple Transition of European regions: green, digital and social. This transition will embrace organisational and institutional change to strengthen territorial resilience and innovation capacities.

63 CoLab innovation processes will actively involve more than 3.000 students and stakeholders. 27 student Hackathons will foster co-creation. 10 IMAGINE events and 90 open internship projects will integrate challenge-based research and education into existing curricula. 27 challenge-based seminars will offer multidisciplinary learning experiences for all students. At least 10 double degree programmes, 3 joint degrees, 36 field studies, 8 summer schools and a digital CoHub will substantially increase the spectrum of education and learning within and beyond the Alliance. 70,000 students and staff will participate in multilingual events. 36 challenge-based school sessions will involve more than 1.000 learners. 108 public engagement events will reach over 1.5 Mio citizens.

hr.name: Sveučilište Josipa Jurja Strossmayera u Osijeku

101177157.title: EUNICoast: The European University of Islands, Ports and Coastal Territories
101177157.summary:
EUNICoast is a pioneering European University Alliance focused on the unique challenges and opportunities of European ports, islands and coastal regions, blending sustainability, education, research and innovation, and community engagement. 

EUNICoast aims to nurture the human dimension of ports and islands, two distinct yet intertwined elements, by creating an educational environment that merges the dynamism of ports with the interconnectedness of islands. We envision a world where ports not only facilitate trade but also cultivate cultural exchange, where islands are not isolated outposts but crossroads for the transmission of innovations. 

With 12 member universities and 88 associated partners, we offer a broad perspective to effectively tackle the complexities of Europe’s Blue Economy. Our ports and islands connect Europe to the world: South to Africa through Sardinia and the Balearic Islands, West to the Americas through the Azores and French Antilles, North to the Baltic, East towards Asia through Burgas and Patras. 

By working together to advance our educational, research, innovation and engagement missions, we aim to (1) Help build strong foundations for the next generation of European and global students and citizens who are engaged, aware and willing to contribute to meeting sustainability; (2) Foster a multicultural, multilingual and inclusive European education, research, and innovation environment which is open to the world; and (3) Enhance the joint capacity of the partner universities to better respond to the societal and environmental challenges faced by island and coastal communities. 

By enhancing our collaboration across all these dimensions, and by engaging with external stakeholders, EUNICoast can make an unmatched contribution towards the sustainability of ports, islands and coastal communities across Europe and the world – and help put universities at its centre.

101177370.title: European University on AI in Curricula, Smart UniverCity and (Return)Mobility (EUonAIR)
101177370.summary:
The EUonAIR European University Alliance aims to enhance education through AI across Europe by fostering education, research, and mobility. We are 10 main and 20+ associated partners, benefiting the 85.000 students, 13.400+ faculty and staff, and 13.2 million citizens in our regions. Our OBJECTIVES are: establishing a sustainable and long-term governance structure, promoting AI education, enhancing open AI research and innovation, promoting holistic human mobility, developing an immersive and virtual MyAI Campus, engaging with cities for smart and green solutions, and raising awareness about developments in AI and education. Our KEY RESULTS include: revolutionised higher education and research through AI via an inter-university governance structure, innovative AI-driven education, development of an immersive, virtual MyAI Campus; enhancement of open research in AI; holistic mobility for enriched knowledge exchange; strengthened engagement in smart, green urban development collaborations with universities across Europe; effective communication strategies for public awareness and responsible AI practices; inclusive and accessible education; strengthened partnerships for knowledge sharing; and human return mobility support that enriches education experiences across Europe.
Our KEY OUTPUTS include: a functioning inter-university governance structure, 1 comprehensive AI-focused course catalogue, the foundation for 5 BSc, MSc, and PhD programmes, open access to educational resources, 1 prototype for a collaborative research platform, 1 Centre of Excellence for Responsible AI and Education, 1 Holistic Mobility Support Center, 1 Return Mobility Assessment Unit, 1 War Migrants Programme, 1 MyAI Campus virtual platform, 1 EUonAIR Smart & Green UniverCity Lab. 
By integrating AI into learning and governance, EUonAIR strives to make education more accessible, inclusive, and sustainable, addressing the technological, social, geopolitical, and educational challenges of our time.

101087193.title: Partner UP - Partnerships and stakeholder engagement for Upskilling Pathways
101087193.summary:
The project intends to improve the implementation of Upskilling Pathways (UP) by identifying and engaging new stakeholders, establish and improve cooperation mechanisms and implementation plans with them. 
The consortium, coordinated by EAEA, consists of 11 full and 4 associate partners. The full project plan will be developed in 6 countries (HR, CY, EL, IT, LV, RO) and EU (EAEA & eucen). In 5 countries (HR, CY, EL, LV, RO), the NGO partners will work with their ministries / agencies (HR, LV full partners, other countries associate).
Objectives:
Engage in peer learning with the other partners about what works well in their contexts / countries
Analysis of existing / missing cooperation mechanisms + stakeholders
Enable meetings between relevant stakeholders and agree on cooperations
Develop implementation plans for further stakeholder engagement and cooperation 
Share experiences & outcomes of the project at the national level, in Europe, with relevant institutions and organisations

Overall, the project intends to have a systemic impact on the implementation of UP by developing new cooperation mechanisms.

The 1st phase will (WP 2) provide information in identifying existing and missing stakeholders through analysis. 
The next phase is WP3, development groups. They bring these stakeholders together and enable cooperation, trust-building and discussions on improving the implementation of UP.
The last phase is implementation plans (WP5), which will deliver realistic & ambitious road maps.
Study visits and dissemination (traditional dissemination, webinars at national levels, a final European Conference)
The main outcomes: analyses, implementation plans, Lessons Learned (recommendations), reports of other activities; website with all the results, also in a virtual map / repository

The consortium consider the project as a launching pad for future steps, transfer to other organisations / countries and additional more / better implementation for UP.

hr.name: AGENCIJA ZA STRUKOVNO OBRAZOVANJE I OBRAZOVANJE ODRASLIH

101087526.title: CitizensXelerator - Citizens Xelerator for democratic and civic participation
101087526.summary:
Citizens Xelerator project aims at strengthening the democratic and civic literacy and social empathy of low qualified adults and contributing to a systemic change on the regional/national/European approach and strategies fostering adults’ participation in democratic life, embracing the common values and civic engagement. The project has 4 specific objectives:
-SO1 To upscale and test the potential of the European tool LifeComp: The European framework for the personal, social and learning to learn key competence as a resource to promote the literacy and key-competences of low skilled adults
-SO2 To develop, test and mainstream a model and resources for the assessment and development of personal, social and learning competences of low skilled adults
-SO3 To create, provide and apply microlearning sessions fostering the financial, entrepreneurial, digital and sustainable literacy of low skilled adults, through the upscaling of complementary European tools and projects;
-SO4 To launch a model and kit pilot action for democratic and civic participation, fostering its multiplication and mainstreaming at regional, national, and European levels.
The consortium will ensure the concretization of these objectives by creating and implementing 3 main products:
D2.1 LifeComp cards collection with cards to support the life skills assessment and activities for competences’ reinforcement
D2.2 Citizens Xelerator Model and Kit with guidelines for the establishment and promotion of the Citizens Xelerator Action Lab in partners’ countries and supports for the implementation of the think tank, civic and democratic initiatives, celebration days and microlearning sessions.
The target groups are adult education professionals and providers, low skilled adults and civil society organizations and during 24-months, the consortium expects to involve 50 professionals from the partnership/associated partners and mobilize around 2500 low skilled adults in the events and pilot action to be promoted.

101132300.title: RALExILA - National Registries of Adult Learning and Education to support the deployment of Individual Learning Accounts
101132300.summary:
To improve access to training opportunities for adults, there is an increasing need to improve quality of Adult Learning and Education (provisions and methods), efficiency and equity of access systems (clarity of information and learners understanding of opportunities, also funding and guidance services) and finally supporting a stronger level of attractiveness for any learner toward lifelong learning.

In this context, the project ‘RALExILA - National Registries of Adult Learning and Education to support the deployment of Individual Learning Accounts’ aims to develop a model and a proof of concept for an integrated information system of the national registries for training opportunities, with a methodology based on interoperability, accessibility and inclusiveness, looking at quality of ALE provision.

Objectives
•	Support systemic change in ALE governance with collaboration of all relevant stakeholders.
•	Identify contextual aspects and needs for deploying training information systems.
•	Analyse good practices of existing systems and training registries.
•	Define an adapted quality and governance framework and interoperable system model, based on holistic vision of ALE quality, participatory approaches for governance, user experience and European Learning Model.
•	Test and refine framework and models, to support implementation and exploitation.

Audience and results
•	20 authorities, 40 ALE organisations, 20 learners and 10 experts involved in co-design.
•	20 good practices analysed.
•	500 participants involved in events.
•	10,000 people reached by dissemination activities.

Main outputs
•	Report on framework, content and needs analysis for the implementation of national registries for ALE in Europe.
•	Handbook for the National Registries for ALE (quality assurance and governance frameworks, system model).
•	Dissemination and Exploitation Strategy, designed with project participants through national co-design workshops.

101132759.title: Atollo Project
101132759.summary: This project aims to empower learners with disabilities by creating inclusive digital materials. Through a consortium of partners from Croatia, Bulgaria, Austria, Germany, Iceland, Norway, Ireland and Australia, including an EdTech company, universities, schools for children with SEN, public authorities, and NGO, we will analyse and compare existing programs, develop innovative digital tools and create high-quality digital educational content. We will pilot and test the digital materials and evaluate their implementation and then focus on the improvement of developed digital materials based on the feedback from the learners, teachers and experts. The result of the scientific evaluation of the use of digital materials will be an inclusive digital education toolkit that will contain advice and instructions for everyone who works with it, and uses digital educational materials for children SEN. We will use a user-centred design approach to ensure that the materials are accessible and inclusive for learners with various types of disabilities. This iterative process of improvement will help us create digital materials that are effective and engaging. Furthermore, the project will provide capacity building for teachers to use developed digital materials effectively. The expected results include a cutting-edge set of digital learning materials, capacity building for teachers and an inclusive digital education toolkit for policymakers and education institutions. We will share our findings and outcomes through various channels to reach a wider audience, including policymakers and education institutions, and create awareness about the importance of inclusive digital materials for learners with disabilities. The project will have a direct impact on the involved schools and their learners as well as a broader impact on the underrepresented group of children with disabilities, their educators and wider academic community through research paper derived from this project.

hr.name: MINISTARSTVO RADA, MIROVINSKOGA SUSTAVA, OBITELJI I SOCIJALNE POLITIKE
Škola za odgoj i obrazovanje - Pula

101132761.title: DIGITAL FIRST - Digital tech as the first language: Informatics for digital natives
101132761.summary: At the very dawn of the new millennium, it has been predicted that the 21st century will be turbulent one, characterised by variability, uncertainty, chaos and ambiguity. We are not even over its first quarter, and the prognosis is proving to be more than accurate: Brexit and its consequences, COVID-19, the war in Ukraine, but also the birth of the generative AI, human genome decoded, successful mission to Mars. A human being was never much of an oracle, but now, at least, we are painfully aware of how much we truly don’t know. As educators, what we do know, is that despite of all this lack of clarity, we still need to give our children the skills and tools to succeed in their own times and their own lives. And we know that one of the crucial, if not THE crucial, skill is the ability to understand the digital world. For this, we need strong, modern approaches to teaching informatics. DIGITAL FIRST is exactly that – an attempt to devise a new, innovative pedagogical approach to informatics, which respects the fact that children we teach have been born into the digital world, they do not know any other way: digital is the language they speak, they currency they exchange. We argue that 21st century children are often more fluent in digital language than in their mother tongue. And just like in language acquisition, native speakers learn how to express meaning in a sentence (function) and not how to conjugate verbs (structure), we argue that the same principle should be applied to teaching informatics for digital natives. DIGITAL FIRST will form a European informatics teachers network, animated through a series of dialogue clubs, in which the functional approach will be co-created and co-designed. Piloted in 10 EU countries, together with teacher training catalogues, we believe this high-quality inclusive method to teaching and assessing will help our children become active, responsible and ethical digital EU citizens.

101132828.title: Quality of Interaction of the Virtual Auditorium
101132828.summary:
The Objective of the Virtual Auditorium project is to contribute to the strengthening of Europe's innovation capacity by developing innovative solutions in education and training and promoting cooperation between EdTech industry and Public Education Sector; 

The Virtual Auditorium project will have the following Specific Objectives: 
SO1 - Identifying, developing and testing innovative approaches that have the potential to be mainstreamed in order to improve education and training systems
SO2 - Launching pilot actions to test solutions to present and future challenges with a view to kick-starting sustainable and systemic impact; 
SO3 - Contributing to development of an evidence-based quality assurance framework via incorporation of calculation of Quality of Interaction into that
SO4 - Promotion of cross-sectoral cooperation in-between of EdTech & Public Sector

The project will focus on a practical challenge identified – Quality of Interaction does not have a defined numeric value how to evaluate it, moreover it is not being determined with AI lead models. 

Quality of Interaction depends on two main components: Course content and Type of person in Learning. 

Course content is changeable, Type of the Person in learning not, in order to increase the Quality of Interaction, HEI should be able offer course content appropriate to Type of Learner. 

In order to offer course content according with max QoI and accordint to Type of Learner teachers should have tools that can determine Types of Learner for each person in the class - project will develop an LMS-based application that will determine that

In order to achieve that determination of QoI becomes mainstreamed, project should put serious effort in making QoI as part of Evidence Based Quality Assurance Framework.

All project successes, challenges and results will be communicated into European Digital Education HUB, which in March 2023 had more than 2500 members.

101132853.title: THINK TWICE - Think Twice: Supporting the Development of Media Literacy in Education
101132853.summary:
In order to support the formal education system that is still limping behind the rapid changes in the way we learn and communicate with each other, the Think Twice project creates opportunities for competence development of learners and educators, capacity building of education providers, and proposals for policymakers making decisions on curricula content, initial and CPD education of teachers in the area of media and digital literacy. 
There are several target groups of the Think Twice project. Firstly, educators working in formal learning contexts – in primary, secondary or adult education. In addition, some of the project activities will also target university students in a teaching track, i.e., future teachers in order to provide quality training opportunities on incorporating media literacy in education for both initial teacher education and continuing professional development of practicing teachers. Secondly, the project will directly target learners of various ages in order to provide a practical tool for media literacy development educators can use with: children aged 8-12, teens, and adults. Thirdly, the project will target education decision-makers at institutional level (school managers, education managers, principals/heads) and regional/national level (governmental public bodies overseeing primary, secondary or adult education).
