Lastly, the project will target communities as a whole through the production of a social media campaign, raising awareness and knowledge of disinformation and misinformation.

101132887.title: TINKER - an auThentIc learNing and gender inclusive frameworK for tEaching infoRmatics in schools across Europe
101132887.summary:
Within the Path to the Digital Decade proposal, specific targets were proposed for 2030 according to which EU and Member States will equip at least 80% of people with at least basic digital skills and increase the number of ICT specialists to 20 million, with convergence between men and women. According to the latest Digital Economy and Society Index, only 56% of Europeans have the basic digital skills (DESI,2022) whereas there is a gender imbalance at different levels and age groups in ICT related fields. Informatics Education is a powerful vehicle for meeting the set targets and developing the digital skills of all citizens.  According to the Digital Education Action Plan 2021-2027, using innovative and motivating approaches to teaching informatics, can help develop skills in problem-solving, creativity, and collaboration and foster interest in STEM related careers while tackling gender stereotypes. Yet, informatics education is still fragmented with regards to its content and curricula, and the pedagogical approaches for teaching and assessing informatics across schools in Europe. 

The aims of the project are: 
•	Promote the use of a pedagogical framework for teaching and assessing informatics on the grounds of authentic learning and contemporary gender inclusive practices, in upper primary and lower secondary education. 
•	Prepare teachers to create authentic learning environments, following gender inclusive practices when teaching informatics.
•	Support mutual learning across Europe, to adopt evidence-based pedagogy in teaching and assessing informatics.
•	Engage policy makers across the EU in discussions about informatics teaching and assessment to improve teacher practices and digital skills in Europe.

 Through the activities of the project more than 100 schools will be engaged and more than 1000 teachers will be prepared to teach and assess informatics in an authentic and gender inclusive approach.

101259291.title: DigPlay - Unlocking digital potential through gaming
101259291.summary:
DigPlay is a forward-looking Erasmus+ project that reimagines how digital competences are assessed in secondary and vocational education (VET), especially for learners aged 14–19 who are underserved, disengaged or underrepresented in digital learning and future career pathways. By embedding assessment into familiar and motivating digital spaces—video games—the project transforms evaluation from a static test into an engaging, formative journey.
Aligned with the European Digital Competence Framework (DigComp 2.2) and anticipating the forthcoming evolution of DigComp 3.0, DigPlay maps gameplay behaviours to transversal digital skills such as collaboration, content creation, safety and problem-solving. The project introduces a robust, scalable assessment methodology that reflects how young people naturally learn and interact with technology, offering a progression model with personalised feedback and career guidance.
Through cross-sectoral cooperation, the project will develop the DigPlay assessment framework, train educators and business mentors, pilot activities in 20+ schools across five countries, and deploy a digital platform for tracking learner progress. It places strong emphasis on inclusion—particularly of girls, rural youth and learners at risk of exclusion—by lowering barriers to participation and building digital confidence through culturally relevant learning experiences.
DigPlay supports the objectives of the Digital Education Action Plan and Erasmus+ horizontal priorities by fostering innovation, equity and digital transformation in education. It contributes to policy and system-level change by producing tools, data and demonstrators that inform national strategies and support EU efforts to ensure that 80% of citizens have basic digital skills by 2030. DigPlay helps ensure that every learner’s digital skills are recognised and valued in ways that reflect how they actually use technology.

101259496.title: INCEPTION: A new era of VET Excellence
101259496.summary:
The INCEPTION project, A new era of VET Excellence, will initiate a fundamental shift in how CoVEs collaborate and innovate, planting the seeds for a more interconnected, efficient, and impactful VET ecosystem across Europe. 

The main Concept  is to : Connect existing CoVEs to skills ecosystems/CoVE in other economic sectors ; & Promote best practices & transfer of best practices among COVEs addressing manufacturing industry, concerning VET Quality and standards; Attracting and developing talent & provide relevant learning and cooperation solutions

Specific Objectives include to: 
Ensure the systematic impact of COVE initiatives, by updating and implementing their methodologies towards the local and national engagement 
Transfer of the CoVEs methodologies 
Roll out of the recognition, teaching and learning synergies  
Promote and enlarge each COVE networks at regional and national level

101259602.title: SCIFINE - Scientific Capacity through Inquiry for Foundational Impact and Networked Engagement
101259602.summary: SCIFine aims to enhance STEM learning in early childhood and primary education through inquiry-based, constructivist and open-schooling approaches. Targeting Portugal, Slovenia and Croatia, the project develops adaptable teaching resources, trains educators and teachers and engages parents and communities to create inclusive and sustainable STEM learning ecosystems. By addressing educational inequalities, fostering motivation, and aligning with EU digital and green priorities, SCIFine supports systemic change through collaboration among schools, families, policymakers, regional authorities and science organisations. The project’s evidence-based methods and policy recommendations aim to improve foundational skills and prepare children for future challenges in a digitally and environmentally evolving Europe.

101259716.title: JIBE - Joint Qualification for Innovative Building Efficiency
101259716.summary:
The building sector, responsible for 40 % of energy use and one-third of global CO2 emissions, plays a vital role in achieving a low-carbon economy by 2050. To meet these goals, buildings must evolve into smart, adaptive nodes within the energy grid. As smart building technologies, powered by AI, IoT and big data, proliferate, the demand for highly skilled professionals grows exponentially. The JIBE project addresses this emerging skills gap in the smart building and electrotechnical sector through an innovative joint approach to vocational education and training (VET).

The general objective of the project is to develop and test innovative joint approaches in the electrotechnical sector in HVET between HR, SI, IT, SRB, AT, and SL for a highly skilled and mobile workforce contributing to innovation at practice and policy-level in VET. 
The specific objective of the project is to develop and test joint qualification at EQF level 5 for the Expert in Building Intelligence together with an innovative framework for recognition, mobility, and attractiveness of VET in line with industry needs.

To achieve these objectives, JIBE builds its joint qualification on detailed skills mapping and the active involvement of employers to ensure direct alignment with real-world demands. A flexible learning structure will underpin the qualification: a comprehensive curriculum, modular micro-credentials, digital learning materials, collaborative projects and a digital twin of a smart home. 
All frameworks and learning structure will be tested, including mobility of teachers and a summer school for students.  The project is acctevlly supported by policymakers as full and associated partners ensuring long term sustainability and a successful roll out of the joint qualification between VET providers from 6 countries.

hr.name: OBRTNICKO UCILISTE - USTANOVA ZA OBRAZOVANJE ODRASLIH

101259941.title: DC4Democracy - Fostering Digital Competences for Safe and Democratic Deliberations in the EU
101259941.summary:
Democratic systems in Europe are facing increasing challenges. Trust in institutions is declining, for example, only 11% of young Europeans believe democracy functions effectively. Simultaneously, political participation is shifting to digital spaces, where youth are vulnerable to disinformation, polarization, and manipulation. According to the EC, 63% of young people regularly encounter online disinformation, yet only 9% have received training to recognize it. In this context, building civic resilience demands competences for critical, ethical, and informed digital engagement. In response, a growing number of digital democracy courses have been introduced into secondary education curricula across Europe. However, without robust tools to assess these competences, progress remains difficult to track and sustain.
DC4Democracy addresses this need by advancing the assessment of digital deliberation competences (skills that enable one to engage meaningfully and responsibly in digital democratic life). Aligned with DigComp, the project will co-create a multilingual framework and toolkit for assessing these competences across Europe.The consortium includes ten partners from seven countries bringing together universities, policy institutes, VET providers, schools, and a company. This ensures alignment with pedagogical, technological, and policy goals and broad access to diverse educational settings. DC4Democracy follows a multi-phase methodology combining literature mapping, focus groups, expert consultation, a Delphi study, and agile development. Pilots will be implemented in five schools and VET institutions, involving 1,600 students and 60 educators. The main output will be a classroom-ready toolkit featuring self-assessment instruments and branching video scenarios simulating real-life democratic decision-making. Ultimately, DC4Democracy envisions a future where all young people are empowered to become informed, critical, and responsible participants in digital democratic life.

2021-1-BE01-KA210-ADU-000034110.title: SUpporting family CaregivErs of adultS with mental health problemS
2021-1-BE01-KA210-ADU-000034110.summary:
<< Background >>

During the 24-month project, we achieved the following:
1) Shared good practices for supporting family members of people with mental health problems in Europe.
2) Shared training programmes to support family members of people with mental health problems.
3) Shared national and international awareness campaigns for the social inclusion of adults with mental illness and their family caregivers.
The need to include mental health among the priorities of the public health agenda was increasingly recognized by the European Union following the launch of the Commission's Green Paper on Improving Mental Health in 2005. The horizontal priority of inclusion and diversity in adult education was linked with spreading awareness about the needs of adults who are family caregivers of people with a mental illness such as schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. This led to a society with less stigmatization of adults with mental health problems.
The adult education priority on improving the availability of high-quality learning opportunities for adults was linked with the sharing of successful training programmes for families of people with mental health problems, such as the program used by the Belgian partner Profamille and Prospect used by EUFAMI.

<< Objectives >>

The proposal for the project SUCESS was formulated as a result of a growing awareness among the partners about the needs and problems faced by caregivers of individuals with mental illness. This concern led to the creation of the project partnership and the respective development of the project proposal, aiming to assist the project’s main target group, which comprises these informal carers.
The role of families and carers of people with mental health issues proved to be crucial. Families needed to recognize what well-being meant in their lives - to identify and discover their role. Families of adults with mental illnesses such as schizophrenia had to find their own well-being in a way that would allow them to maintain self-esteem and resilience - a sense of purpose and personal fulfillment. Many organizations in Europe, such as Similes and EPIONI, actively participated in creating, changing, and monitoring laws and regulations on mental health at both national and European levels. The SUCESS project promoted high-quality learning opportunities for adults who were families of people with mental health problems.

<< Implementation >>

The activities we implemented are:
1) Partners shared good practices and examples of successful mental health promotion events, including video productions in which they had been involved and the ways they provided support to family caregivers.
2) A training was conducted at the University Psychiatric Hospital in Croatia, accompanied by a study visit to a Day Care Center (4-6 July 2022).
3) The "Caring for Carers" Conference and a PROSPECT Training session, in collaboration with our associate partner EUFAMI, were held in the context of the Athens project meeting (16-17 June 2023).
4) Two study visits by EPIONI in Brussels took place on the 28th of October and the 18th of November 2023.
5) A final meeting in hybrid form was organized on the 21st of February 2024 in Brussels to present the Good Practice Guide.

<< Results >>

Compilation and Sharing of Good Practices: The project successfully compiled and shared good practices and examples of successful mental health promotion events. This included video productions showcasing the involvement of partners and the support mechanisms provided to family caregivers, serving as a valuable resource for organizations and individuals working in the field of mental health
Educational and Training Sessions: The project conducted a specialized training session at the University Psychiatric Hospital in Croatia, enhancing the skills and knowledge of participants in dealing with mental health issues. Additionally, a PROSPECT Training session was held in collaboration with EUFAMI, focusing on empowering family caregivers of people with mental health problems.
Conferences and Meetings: The "Caring for Carers" Conference, held in Greece, provided a platform for discussing challenges and strategies related to caring for individuals with mental health issues. Furthermore, the final meeting in hybrid form in Brussels presented the Good Practice Guide, summarizing the project's findings and recommendations.
Study Visits: Two study visits by EPIONI in Brussels facilitated the exchange of good practices between partners.

2021-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000034007.title: Tools for Education with Artistic Perception for Open Transmission
2021-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000034007.summary:
<< Background >>

The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the critical role of education professionals who have continued their work despite crises. This has reinforced the importance of rethinking our pedagogical approach to meet modern challenges. The current trend emphasizes ‘soft skills’, engaging learners’ emotions and senses. Our partnership has sought to merge the fields of art and education to enrich the educational offer and training tools. This initiative aimed to diversify teachers’ resources, while offering new perspectives to artists by learning how their art could serve as a pedagogical vehicle. This collaboration between artists and educators is based on fundamental similarities. Artists bring a unique perspective by evoking emotions to facilitate learning. Educators have essential skills for structuring effective educational programs. This merger broadens artists’ horizons, diversifying their sources of income and cultural impact and, beyond individual benefits, it promotes social inclusion by diversifying educational opportunities.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to help education evolve to meet the changing needs of society and the economy. Integrating art into education prepares learners for a complex future, where creativity, problem-solving, and communication are key. We wanted to find ways to engage new learners and encourage them to engage in learning that goes beyond simply acquiring knowledge, but rather engages emotions, involving the whole body and the senses, rather than just the brain. Today, to create deeper understanding and retention of knowledge, it is necessary to generate enthusiasm, arouse curiosity, and engage learners throughout their educational journey. This makes learning less difficult and sometimes even less painful. By finding artists who volunteered to participate in this project, we wanted to demonstrate that this was possible and accessible. After Covid-19, it was also important to help people reconnect with each other, to help them rediscover the desire to play and to reconnect with their own creativity. Learning in positive, relaxing atmosphere, without the pressure of failure, spark creativity.

<< Implementation >>

First, we tried to bring together the artists and the actors of the training. Find the words to convince them of their value in a knowledge transmission project. Once the network was formed, we set up workshops, to test methods and concepts from the artistic world, such as theatre, literature through reading and creative writing, painting, photography, films to awaken to culture and study society. We have also implemented activities such as workshops in which tested teaching different topics and subjects (foreign languages, civic engagement, intercultural competencies) with the use of different arts. We also organized focus groups. We have also set up other workshops, this time for artists, to make them aware of their place in teaching and education and to explain to them the norms, objectives, and possibilities of the application of their art. Finally, in each partner country, we led working sessions for everyone, educators, and artists, to accompany them, through one artistic discipline, to consider the other, i.e., the learner and the trainer, with a new eye. It was an effective way for better communication between the two parties, methods that facilitate inclusion and diversity through acceptance of oneself and each other. 

<< Results >>

Our separate workshops in each country, from which we have produced documents that will be deposited on the results platform. We have built several guides for interested educators or artists, as well as a curriculum that summarizes the different applications. We have created a padlet on which each participant, if they wish, artists or trainers can create their file and write their CV and contact details for future collaborations, as well as a Facebook page that has attracted many visitors. Our Croatian partner participated in a conference on education, and two professional papers will be published in Conference proceeding.  The exchange and comparison of good practices between the operators of the countries involved enriched the project and offered new insights and operational developments. Transnational links have been created during our activities, which are already announcing projects at the end of TEAPOT.
topics: Reception and integration of refugees and migrants
Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2021-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000034948.title: Local food tour
2021-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000034948.summary:
<< Background >>

In the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region, we noticed a strong development gap between wine tourism, which is highly developed in our region, and food tourism, the poor relation of tourism.
We have in all our territories products under SIQO Signs of Identification of Quality and Origins but no tourist promotion of IGP/AOP labels.
Faced with this observation, it seemed very interesting to us to work on the issues related to the development potential of this sector, which can be a sector as promising as wine tourism.
We therefore wanted to carry out collaborative work to build a professional figure that meets the needs of companies and the development of this sector which is still fallow.
All the partners were particularly sensitive to bring this theme within their development structures.

<< Objectives >>

- Know the reality of food tourism in the partner territories
- Have a vision of the actions undertaken to promote this tourism
- Know the needs of companies and the obstacles to this development
- Ultimately think how collectively which methodological and educational tools to train our target audience in the valorization of their agricultural/agri-food productions.
How to open companies and small production units to the public in order to
discover their know-how?.
Collectively think up a training strategy in the field of culinary and/or gastronomic tourism/promotion of productions under SIQO (labels and quality products) and then build a training course entitled: Culinary heritage facilitator.

<< Implementation >>

To achieve a shared vision of our objectives, we have carried out the following actions:
Field work to assess the weight of food tourism to do this, research work was carried out (interviews, documentary research), this work gave rise to 1 territorial diagnosis of food tourism in each of the territories
We continued by constructing a questionnaire and conducting telephone or in-situ interviews to assess the needs of small or large companies.
More than 50 questionnaires were submitted.
We carried out 3 mobility between partners (France-Spain-Croatia) to know the realities of the partner countries, meet territories, initiatives to act on the promotion of culinary tourism, training sessions and collective work to analyze the results of the questionnaires and define, according to the needs expressed, the figure of the "culinary tourism facilitator" profile.


<< Results >>

6 diagnoses in each of the partner territories
1 Technical proposal to rehabilitate lost recipes
1 questionnaire created collectively
more than 50 questionnaires submitted
3 meetings between partners (France-Spain-Croatia)
2 new projects have been submitted by the partners under the SUDOE program
A figure of animator of culinary tourism is taking shape and will have to be the subject of a next Erasmus KA2.
topics: Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

hr.name: Regional Foundation for Local Development ZAMAH

2021-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000034950.title: Entrepreneurial Skills for REsilience in CREATive sector
2021-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000034950.summary:
<< Background >>

Creative professionals (freelancers), students and people employed in the creative industries even before the COVID-19 pandemic had problems with management, funding, and marketing training activities. During the pandemic, these problems were accelerated as a result of the above shortcomings. The project responded to the needs of people from the cultural and creative sector, whose ability to perform or sell their was prevented or significantly reduced due to the COVID-19 crisis. Based on the research conducted by CREA, it was established that the sector lacks the knowledge and skills necessary for running a business or acting as freelancers in the market in the area of ​​basic financial literacy, information on sources of financing at the local, national or EU level, and especially business planning and internet marketing. Therefore, it was decided to develop 4 e-learning modules in the project, which are available free of charge to all interested participants, in order to strengthen their economic position and facilitate access to funding sources. At the same time, we wanted to raise the capacities of both involved organizations in the use of digital tools and the creation of e-learning educational programs.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to develop a digital education platform with e-learning modules and digital tools for one of the sectors that suffered more during the COVID crisis. We developed modules for financial literacy, business planning, funding options, and online marketing for the cultural and creative sector and provided free access to all people who need this knowledge to be more resilient and boost their digital skills and capacities. We wanted to develop e-learning modules in cooperation with people who belong to this sector and know their problems and main challenges in order to achieve accessible and usable e-learning materials that will be useful in both countries. Also, we wanted to build cooperation among our organizations and strengthen capacities in using digital tools for project management and digital education. Also, the green element was very important so we decided to create all materials in digital form. This was the first project of this kind for both organizations so we wanted to learn how to manage and implement fully digital projects.

<< Implementation >>

The activities in the project are:
- project management with online and in-person meetings in which all steps in the project were planned and developed (visual identity of the project, methodology of the e-learning programmes, curriculum and communication and dissemination plan)
- an event in Varaždin, Croatia where the project is presented to a wider audience and workshops where experiences in the creative sector are exchanged between Spanish and Croatian experts and a detailed program plan is developed (press conference with reportage on regional TV and local newspapers and news portals)
- a creation of an online learning platform recreate-educate.eu with the modules: Financial literacy, Sources of funding, Digital Marketing and Business plan design - these were the key activities in the project that took the most time and resources. A trilingual platform was developed with an accessibility plugin, the LearnDash plugin for e-learning education
- final conference in Madrid, Spain with the best students from both countries, evaluation of the e-learning modules in the context of purposefulness, accessibility and interactivity
- dissemination, evaluation and follow up

<< Results >>

In the project, we developed a methodology guide for our experts in order to create e-learning materials based on research among the representatives of the creative and cultural sectors. The trilingual e-learning platform on the address www. recreate-educate.eu was developed with four e-learning modules: M01 Financial literacy for CCI, M02 Sources of funding for CCI, M03 Digital marketing and M04 Design of business plan for CCI. 
The most important thing in lessons for adult participants is the applicability of knowledge in practical situations they encounter at work or during the design of creative or artistic projects. As all the e-learning modules were rated very good in this category (the lowest average rating is 4.05 and the highest is 4.28), we believe that they fulfil their purpose and that participants improved their knowledge and entrepreneurial skills. Recognition of their skill is provided with digital certificates they get online after the successful finish of every module. A thorough evaluation of all modules is carried out, and we get results so we can build future materials and updated teaching methodology with fresh insights and conclusions.
topics: Economic and financial affairs (including funding issues)

2021-1-HU01-KA210-ADU-000034034.title: Fiume Crisis Project -  An Edularp Development Project for Adult Education
2021-1-HU01-KA210-ADU-000034034.summary:
<< Background >>

Three organizations from three EU countries (Italy, Croatia and Hungary) came together to explore and learn from a sensitive issue in their respective histories: The case of the Free City of Fiume.
We applied because we believe that using a historical setting with an adequate amount of creative freedom can enable its elements to provide meaningful tools for reflecting upon contemporary questions. This particular setting provided us with an intriguing entanglement of different cultural, ideological and political elements and belief systems. 
It was the hundred-year anniversary of the Fiume City State which gave topicality to the subject in the manner of  “looking back for seeing further” This means that while it forms a tool of historical memory, it also acts as a way of addressing current socio-political issues.
We used this historical backdrop as an example of how populist politics work and the project can become a tool for sensitization and reflection, for raising political awareness amongst European citizens.
The partnership wanted the cooperation of the three organizations for the purpose of the historical connection, similar interests and the exchange of different practices and experiences.

<< Objectives >>

OBJECTIVES
OBJECTIVE #1 - COOPERATION & MOBILITY - (This objective responds to the PRIORITY #1)
A. To strengthen the cooperation between the partner organizations that implement larp as an adult educational tool.
B. To increase the mobility of game-designers implementing larp as an educational tool on the European level. 
C. To get the created larp games implemented and organized in all partner countries to increase access to high-quality training opportunities using larp as a method.
 
OBJECTIVE #2 - IMMERSIVE ADULT EDUCATION (PRIORITY #2)
A. To create a bundle of educational larp scenarios using Fiume - Rijeka Free City - independent city-state period as historical context.
B. Develop a digital manual from these scenarios. The documentation, the scenarios, and the manual will be used as a tool for adult education..
C. Share these outcomes with a wider audience via EPALE and other online forums.
 
OBJECTIVE #3 - ENGAGEMENT & PARTICIPATION (PRIORITY #3)
A. To give experience to participants (both designers and players) that demonstrates the importance of active citizenship.
B. Promoting European values of personal freedom, human dignity, solidarity, and social responsibility.

<< Implementation >>

During the course of the year-long cooperation, the three organizations involved their experts and external specialists from various fields such as history, game design, experience design, and theatre to implement 5 activities.  Our main goal was to create a gamified informal immersive adult education methodology and a set of tools that uses the historical context of Fiume’s / Rijeka’s short-lived independence following World War I to teach adults about political radicalization, populist rhetorics and propaganda.

#1 - LECTURES - Three online lectures by historians and one panel discussion on the topic of the city-state period of Fiume. 
#2 - GAME DESIGN COURSE - An educational game and larp design course for the residency participants coming from different fields
#3 - RESIDENCY - one-week residency in Rijeka for participants and trainers from each country, where we created the three larp scenarios.
#4 - EDUCATIONAL GAMES - Implementation of the Edularp scenarios created during the residency. Game testing and dissemination process at roleplaying-related events with members of our target audience.
#5 - DIGITAL MANUAL - Publication of a digital manual of the scenarios created during the residency. 

<< Results >>

- 4 videos of the online Fiume Lectures
- 3 videos of the Educational Game Design Course
- A digital manual published via EPALE and other online platforms. The manual consists of the three full-fledged, tried and tested educational larp scenarios 
- A Fiume Crisis website showcasing all main outputs & results of the project - linked to all the websites of the partners - http://parallelworlds.foundation/fiume-crisis

Intangible results: Experience in administering a European project gained by the lead organization, empowerment of the organizations in terms of innovative tools, educational efficiency, international recognition, and financial self-sustainability. The partner organizations gained experience in the field of international cooperation, got to know each other's practices in depth, expanded their network of relationships, and developed their communication skills and the visibility of their organizations.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000034912.title: Innamorato della tua forma
2021-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000034912.summary:
<< Background >>

In 2020 the COVID-19 pandemic led to severe restrictions in Europe and worldwide, including the closure of non-essential activities due to increased infections and deaths. A significant impact was the significant increase in teleworking among employees. Although teleworking has had advantages and disadvantages for health, a serious problem that has emerged is obesity, with its associated risk of musculoskeletal disorders, metabolic diseases, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases. The World Health Organisation has predicted a future 'obesity pandemic' by 2030, as many people spend hours at home, in isolation, with little exercise and a more sedentary lifestyle. This project was created to address obesity in these circumstances. It focused on aspects such as physical activity, education, management, psychological and dietary aspects. Research, surveys and experiments were used to develop best practice recommendations online, actively involve the target audience and create a common strategy to tackle obesity, eating disorders and lack of physical activity among European citizens working from home. 


<< Objectives >>

As an overarching objective, a strategy to combat obesity and eating disorders among EU citizens working remotely, together with a unified approach to promote best practices, was to be initiated. 
The specific objectives of the project were:
1)To understand and analyse the relationship between the obesity problem and sedentary, poor and disordered eating, the importance of healthy and sustainable nutrition and physical activity 2) To address the psychological aspect of the obesity problem and the effects of social exclusion due to this critical issue and linked to the increased use of telecommuting 3) To implement an "ad hoc" training programme and a sharing of best practices 4) disseminate the experience of "ad hoc" training, verifying the effectiveness of all the actions implemented to combat the criticality of obesity due to the sedentary nature of teleworking

<< Implementation >>

Four events were organised to develop the project and achieve the set goals: the kick off meeting in Drama (Greece), the second meeting in Zagreb (Croatia), a workshop in Lille (France) and the closing meeting in Rome (Italy). During these events, web pages were set up to promote surveys, research, best practices and skills in the fight against the problem of obesity or excess from in work-from-home situations. Afterwards, a learning platform was set up to train the group of volunteers on sustainable healthy diets, physical activities and psychological aspects related to obesity. All training results and best practices were disseminated. 

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs were the creation of a guide with the best practices and to create a model of training "ad hoc" to follow in order to combat the problem of obesity, poor diet and lack of physical activity among teleworkers, in order to avoid the risk of physical and psychological suffering and social exclusion and disseminate these results, best practices and tools to the partners involved on the project, to the targets of the project, the other stakeholders, institutions, individuals and all those who are interested in them.

2021-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000034923.title: ERASMUS + INTERAGING
2021-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000034923.summary:
<< Background >>

Promoting Erasmus+ among all citizens and generations is the priority the project responds to, addressing a target group of the population that records very low participation rates. The project proposal stems from the partners' experience in different specific sectors: communication, non-formal education - both in adult and youth sectors - and intergenerational dialogue. In outlining the context, the partners referred to data collected in small-scale research at the local level; the framework of official data; and the resources available on Erasmus+ Project Results, EPALE, and SALTO. The set of collected data confirmed what had been hypothesized as a premise: the low knowledge and participation of the elderly population in the Erasmus+ program and the weakness of collaboration activities between organizations with different target groups (young and old) within the program. 

<< Objectives >>

By promoting the Erasmus+ Programme in its principles and in the opportunities it offers to organisations and people, through actions at local and transnational levels and in a perspective of intergenerational dialogue, the project wanted to contribute to the construction of a common European identity, involving new organisations and people in a process of discovery of the Programme. The specific objectives we aimed to achieve are 1. to improve the participant's organisation capacities in seizing the opportunities that the Eramsus+ Programme offers them; 2. To increase older people's knowledge of the Erasmus+ programme and to foster their active participation in the Programme. 3. To improve the capacity of cooperation between youth organisations and organisations for older people to achieve common objectives. 

<< Implementation >>

The activities carried out were the following: Activity 01. Organization, at the local level, of a series of meetings aimed at promoting and deepening the Erasmus+ Programme, its values, strategies, objectives, and opportunities. Activity 02. Implementation, at the transnational level, of a non-formal learning training activity. Activity 03. Implementation, at the local level, of a series of meetings for the dissemination of the results of the learning training activity. Activity 04. Creation of an online training module built by exploiting and rationalizing the results of previous activities. 

<< Results >>

The planned activities led to the following concrete outputs 1. Materials for the presentation and promotion of the Programme Erasmus+ in the context of reference; good practices selected through the Erasmus+ project results platforms, EPALE and Salto; tools for the evaluation and replicability of the proposal, as a result of the whole cycle of activities carried out. 2. Adhesion to the program of 14 new organizations through the creation of OIDs, as a result of the activities carried out at the local level by each of the partners and at the transnational level collectively. 3. Three project drafts for new small-scale Erasmus+ projects as a result of the activities carried out at the transnational level. 4. Online training module for the promotion of the Erasmus+ program within the EDA sector as a result of the whole cycle of activities carried out, both at local and transnational levels. As an additional result, a collection of written interviews with the participants has been created in the form of a PDF.

2021-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000034929.title: Padri in gioco
2021-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000034929.summary:
<< Background >>

The project started from an analysis of the 2019 statistical data on female employment compiled by the European Commission, which shows that on average, in the EU, the employment rate of men is higher than that of women (74% and 63% respectively); the gap between these rates increases with the number of children (with three or more children 58% for women, 85% for men). This structure is observed in the vast majority of Member States. These data have inspired this project, which aims to encourage change in the behavior of fathers in order to give women the opportunity to reconcile motherhood and work. With the pandemic linked to Covid-19, this problem has become even more acute. But the real problem is that women cannot afford to devote the same energy as their male colleagues to their careers.The Project is therefore born from this
reflection: why should women always be responsible for the responsibility of caring for their children? And the Fathers? And here is the Family Model and the "Male Work Model" that "forgets mothers" must be put in
Discussion: Fathers should do their part. Rebalancing the distribution of tasks and responsibilities of the Fathers, the load could be evenly distributed.

<< Objectives >>

The project's objective was for to foster a change in the behavior of fathers in order to give women the opportunity to reconcile motherhood and work. Childcare and family management are almost always the sole responsibility of women / mothers. The aim was therefore to raise awareness among fathers and understand their importance of their role in this area so as to rebalance the tasks and responsibilities within the family on both parents.
The specific objectives were to make fathers aware of: 1) the need for working mothers to be able to continue working and not to have to choose between maternity and work; 2) the importance of their role in the care and growth of children; 3) the importance of its own contribution in the management of the family and the home. The priorities that have been selected are the following: 1) environmental sustainability: in every organizational phase attention has been paid to the eco-sustainability of the activities. Moreover, environmental-friendly behaviour has also been promoted in the formulation of the training content; 2) inclusion and diversity: both the training activities carried out "at a distance" and the mobility have guaranteed an inclusive participation. 

<< Implementation >>

The awareness of fathers was take place through a series of training activities: Mobility in Finland, a country that gives great importance to the issue, where it was be possible to share the experiences of Finnish fathers; to understand the needs of the woman / mother in the period from pre to post childbirth; aimed at making the father understand how to manage the needs of children in the first years of life in order to be personally responsible for them. There were two other transnational mobility: in Rome in Italy and in Zagreb (Croatia). On these occasions the participants discussed and analysed the various aspects of the problem, shared good practices and discussed possible solutions. Local stakeholders were involved in each meeting. Many participants announced their intention to continue working with partners on these issues beyond the end of the eligibility period. 

<< Results >>

The results achieved concern the change in the way of seeing fathers with respect to their role within the family. Through targeted questionnaires it was possible to evaluate the learning of the basic notions and the most correct behavior to be held in certain circumstances and situations that arise in daily life.(results here https://www.piattaformaprogetti.eu/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/FATHERS-AT-STAKE-PADRI-IN-GIOCO-RISULTATI-1.pdf-1-1.pdf)  It was also be possible to evaluate through a satisfaction questionnaire if this course is considered significant by the fathers. All results have been published in open source mode and easy to download and use on the project’s official website https://www.piattaformaprogetto.eu/padri-in-gioco/. The results were also integrated with the activities of other projects coordinated by EuroMamme.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2021-1-PL01-KA210-ADU-000035068.title: "Akademia Aktywnych Babć i Dziadków"
2021-1-PL01-KA210-ADU-000035068.summary:
<< Background >>

We wanted to implement this project because so far we have not had the opportunity to implement activities within the framework of "Adult Education". We believed that due to the implementation of local activities with seniors by all partner organizations of the project - it would be natural to take these activities to the international level. We wanted to enrich the elderly with a set of competences that they need for everyday functioning. In addition, we wanted to confront the needs of adults in Poland, Serbia and Croatia, show common features and differences.
The project responded to the specific needs of the elderly participating in it, such as: the desire for social and family activity of the elderly, and at the same time the need to exchange experiences and skills from different countries, in order to show both the common features and diversity that can contribute to deepening knowledge, not only scientific, but also cultural and social.
The project also responded to the needs of learning how to overcome cultural and social barriers, the need to create in every region of the country environments conducive to social inclusion of people whose task is to promoting equality and justice at all ages.

<< Objectives >>

Through the project, we wanted to support the social development of the elderly, improve their family relationships through active participation in upbringing and caring for grandchildren, and at the same time including them in social life, improving the quality of
life through educational and mental development. The results we would like to achieve are: • increase in social activity i
volunteering of seniors • increase in knowledge and skills in the field of social involvement and working with/in a group
• organization of free time for the proper development of yourself and your grandchildren • improvement of well-being and condition
physical activity, • cultural activation and developing interests, • increasing intergenerational integration through volunteering
senior for children, youth and adults • increasing access to culture and cultural activation • promotion
various forms of activity • cooperation after the end of the project • increase in knowledge in the field of psychology • growth
key competences and skills in the personal development of seniors, but also important from the perspective of proper
children's development.

<< Implementation >>

Three joint mobilities of adult learners were carried out during the project: In Poland (Zboiska), Croatia (Lovran) Serbia (Tara)

<< Results >>

The following results were achieved as part of the project: overcoming cultural and social barriers and stereotypes by getting acquainted with a different culture, increasing the tourist and recreational activity of people aged 60+ through participation in an organized international trip, as well as increasing digital awareness, acquiring new qualifications and skills by the PU from the scope of computer use and the use of the Internet and social media, increase in self-confidence, in particular in international contacts. In addition, an increase in the knowledge of project participants in the field of the thematic issues raised in the project was noticed.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2021-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000029347.title: Moj samooskrben dom v času korona krize
2021-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000029347.summary:
<< Background >>

With specific, environmentally friendly educational content, we wanted to achieve that the target group of unemployed people in the economically demanding corona times learn to take care of a self-sufficient home with as little money as possible. So that they learn to prepare basic and absolutely necessary products at home that are used in everyday life (natural cosmetics, cleaning products) and to grow basic herbs and vegetables for everyday use. That they know how to prepare simple and healthy meals from their own grown or processed ingredients. In this way, in addition to acquiring elementary skills that ensure the basic existence of the individual with the minimum necessary costs and resources, they also strengthen their competences and improve their positioning on the labor market. We strengthened them with knowledge and skills, and at the same time influenced their motivation, self-image, self-initiative, increased social inclusion and strengthened their social network. By promoting the use of environmentally friendly, natural ingredients and the sustainable management of natural resources, we wanted to help preserve nature and reduce the carbon footprint at the same time. 

<< Objectives >>

With the project we wanted to achieve the following objectives:

Objective 1: Our first objective was to prepare the content of educational activities for unemployed people
Objective 2: Our second objective was to implement innovative free educational content for unemployed people
Objective 3: Our third objective was to involve and train 300 unemployed persons in the project
Objective 4: Our fourth objective was to establish a digital and physical project brochure in Croatian and Slovenian language


<< Implementation >>

For the successful implementation of the project, we prepared and carried out the following activities:

- Preparation of contents, methods and action plan for educational
activities for unemployed people
- Implementation of educational activities for unemployed persons
- Creation of a digital project brochure
- Production of a project brochure in printed form
- Dissemination of project results
- Project management and quality assurance


<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results of our project were as follows:

Result 1: We prepared the content of educational activities with designed practical and theoretical frameworks and work methods for the target group
Result 2: We carried out innovative workshops (30 workshops) with a practical and theoretical framework on the topic of a self-supporting home for unemployed individuals
Result 3: We trained 273 unemployed persons who acquired new knowledge, skills and competences
Result 4: We produced a digital project brochure and a printed project brochure
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000034987.title: Opolnomočenje starejših pacientov za pravilno uporabo zdravil
2021-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000034987.summary:
<< Background >>

In our work at the pharmacy, we noticed the need to empower patients who are treated with medicines. Especially in the case of the treatment of chronic non-communicable diseases and in the case of elderly patients, who find it more difficult to find their way in the modern healthcare system, which is increasingly digitized. These patients find it more and more difficult to find their way in this system, moreover, it is a population group that is accompanied by frequent polymorbidity, which modern medicine treats with polypharmacotherapy. It is cheaper for society when the treatment can be carried out at the patient's home, which imposes an important responsibility on this, since only the correct use of drugs enables the full use of the prescribed pharmacotherapy. Due to several factors, elderly patients have greater challenges in ensuring the correct use of medications. With the project, we wanted to address, above all, the recognition of potential problems that the elderly have when using medicines and the appropriate resolution of only these. For this purpose, we prepared and carried out various activities.

<< Objectives >>

With the implementation of the project, we wanted to find out which problems elderly patients encounter with drug treatment and which of the solutions can best help them with the spa. We wanted to empower elderly patients who use drugs to treat chronic non-communicable diseases for the correct use of drugs, which is the basis or necessity for effective and safe pharmacotherapy. Through cooperation with partners from Croatia, we wanted to exchange opinions and good practices and prepare appropriate solutions with our joint efforts.

<< Implementation >>

We included various activities in the implementation of the project. When preparing the content of the activities, we first conducted an analysis of the situation, where we tried to identify important areas that needed to be addressed through surveys of various stakeholders, both patients and medical staff. We then offered the participants a variety of content: lectures, applied workshops (on the topics: hypertension or cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease as well as modern digital solutions in the field of healthcare, health and pharmacy) and a personal consultation with a pharmacist regarding medication use.

<< Results >>

Conducting 20 public lectures on the topic of correct and safe use of medicines for the elderly who use medicines for the treatment of chronic non-communicable diseases. Implementation of 40 application workshops on the treatment of chronic non-communicable diseases. Each workshop is dedicated to a specific chronic non-communicable disease or problem: hypertension, diabetes, asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, applications for monitoring drug treatment on electronic mobile devices. conducted 202 individual consultations with a pharmacist on the correct use of medicines and produced 202 personal medicine cards in Slovenia and Croatia. Designed an innovative international educational module for the elderly on the topic of correct and safe use of medicines, which can be transferred to other areas in Slovenia and Croatia and throughout Europe (translation into other languages ​​required). Acquisition of data on patient challenges in drug treatment, which we include in the education of the lay (patients) and professional (doctors, pharmacists) public.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000035010.title: Približevanje evropske razsežnosti oddaljenim podeželskim območjem
2021-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000035010.summary:
<< Background >>

The mission of participating organizations operating in rural peripheral areas is to ensure social inclusion, primarily of vulnerable groups, and to influence the sustainable development of remote areas. Based on a joint needs analysis, we have formed a common partnership aimed at addressing the key needs of target groups and enhancing the quality of work in organizations. Through international cooperation, we aimed to strengthen mutual trust, elevate the level of work with rural populations, and provide quality educational programs in rural areas. The key needs of the target groups included a low level of social inclusion, a lack of digital skills linking them to the world, and a lack of knowledge regarding environmental protection and health. To prevent the social exclusion of this vulnerable rural population and ensure the sustainable development of border areas, it is essential to establish and ensure the long-term provision of social welfare, educational, cultural, and other programs, as well as their intercultural connection at the international level. We aimed to provide high-quality learning programs tailored to their needs to acquire significant new knowledge necessary for daily functioning in a rapidly changing society.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to: provide high-quality learning opportunities for adults in remote rural areas tailored to their needs; improve the competencies of partner staff; strengthen European cooperation and bring a European dimension to remote rural areas; identify specific needs in the areas of digital technology, culture, coexistence, environmental protection, and health. Through the implementation of 24 workshops, we aimed to involve at least 15 participants per workshop and connect adults in remote rural areas through educational and cultural activities via four international events. On a long-term basis, we aimed to sustainably enhance the quality of work of partner organizations by designing learning programs, improve the competencies of adult education staff, and establish and maintain long-term international partnerships in adult education.

<< Implementation >>

1.Leadership and coordination: We ensured communication and coordination among partners, reviewed the achievement of project objectives, appropriately documented project progress, and evaluated the implementation. 2.Needs analysis for adult education: We organized a roundtable with representatives of partner organizations and target groups, developed methodology - questionnaires for the target group, conducted data collection and analysis and created a detailed education plan. 3.Staff training: We developed and implemented a training program and created a training manual for staff. 4.Training for target group individuals in the field of digital technology: We conducted workshops and international online meetings. 5.Training for target group individuals in the field of culture and coexistence: We conducted workshops and international events. 6.Training for target group individuals in the field of environmental protection and health: We conducted workshops and international meetings. 7.Evaluation: We conducted interim and final evaluations.
8.Collaboration with the local community and dissemination: We conducted project presentations in the local community, carried out posts on social media, media coverage, promotional videos.

<< Results >>

We produced reports of the board meetings and project reports, developed frameworks for identifying specific needs of target groups for education across different areas using a common method for needs assessment. We created a common methodology for data collection, evaluation and implementation plan. The gathered needs were incorporated into an education plan for the target groups. A training program for staff was developed and implemented, resulting in 10 trained individuals from the partnership capable of conducting training for target groups. We conducted 12 workshops on digital technology, involving at least 180 participants, and held 2 international online events with at least 80 participants. 10 workshops on culture and coexistence were conducted, involving at least 150 participants, along with 2 international events with at least 80 participants. 6 workshops on environmental protection and health were held, with at least 100 participants, along with 2 international events with at least 80 participants. We conducted 32 evaluations after each activities. There were 8 project presentations conducted in the local community. We achieved 8 media publications and 30 social media posts, as well as 4 short promotional videos.
topics: Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

2021-1-TR01-KA210-ADU-000030121.title: F.A.C.E- Fight Against Crises Effectively
2021-1-TR01-KA210-ADU-000030121.summary:
<< Background >>

FA.C.E. project aimed to address are primarily related to crisis communication and the impact of climate change on natural disasters. The project seeked to raise awareness about the importance of crisis communication and reduce the risks associated with environmental disasters. The project also aimed to provide training and information exchange to help organizations and institutions better prepare for and respond to crises.

Secondly, the earthquakes in our country showed that crisis communication is very important and there were very few projects written when we examined the project database on this subject. 
In fact, the latest developments in our country show that we really need more projects and cooperation on crisis communication.
International cooperation is essential to tackling climate change and effects of disasters. Overall, the FA.C.E. project is a response to the growing recognition of the need for better preparedness and communication in the face of environmental crises. By providing training, awareness-raising, and information exchange, the project aims to helped  organizations and institutions better manage these risks and minimize the harm caused by disasters. 

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the project are to raise awareness about climate change and its impact on natural disasters, create a sustainable digital platform that promotes cooperation between European countries and institutions on environment, climate change, and disasters, design the project in an eco-friendly manner and incorporate green practices in all facets, provide inclusion and diversity in all fields of training, build the knowledge of government officials at all levels, civil society, and the private sector through sharing experiences, lessons learned, and good practices on disaster risk reduction and crisis communication, develop a society that is more prepared for disasters, exchange information on lessons learned about good practices, policies, plans, and measures for crisis communication and disaster risk reduction, and develop ways of dealing with disinformation in crisis and disaster situations. The ultimate goal of the project is to contribute to global environmental protection andf crisis communication efforts  by actively working with developed and developing countries on a common platform.

<< Implementation >>

Visits were made to many institutions related to crisis communication and the environment. Information meetings were held in these institutions. In addition, training was given on project topics. 

A video documentary was created with the images and videos of the project. And also ; two eco-calenders and pleantable leaf seeds for project dissemination were made. In order to raise awareness of climate change, authorized persons were talked to in the institution.
The website "http://facegreenchallenge.com/" was established to raise awareness about the environment. Project reports giving detailed information about the project were written. Participants were surveyed. Saplings were planted on behalf of F.A.C.E project. In addition, a waste system was established in our institution. Also,  dissemination meeting was held in our organisation.


<< Results >>

Within the scope of the project, 2022 and 2023 eco-calendars were designed. In addition, the plantable leaf was designed and used for the dissemination of the project. The contents prepared for the training were uploaded to the project website.
Other Results:

  • Raised awareness of the target audience on disasters caused by climate change.
• Improved work and methods to be green offices / institutions.
• Benefited from and applied the crisis communication methods of other countries.
• Created awareness of EU projects for our institution and other state institutions and organizations.
• Learned the correct communication techniques that should be used during the crisis and were able to deliver the right information to the public with this method.
• Continued coordination of partner institutions. New experts were met through project partners and new projects were written with them. Project partners were hosted at the International Forum on Disaster Communication 2023  of our organisation.
