2021-2-CZ01-KA210-ADU-000050475.title: Education and empowerment for transition to community
2021-2-CZ01-KA210-ADU-000050475.summary:
<< Background >>

The project focused on supporting people with mental illness to recover and integrate into the community after returning from hospital or long-term residential care. Hospitalizations, especially long-term hospital or facility stays, are often significant turning points in the lives of people with mental illness. They often spend many weeks, sometimes months or years in hospital and completely lose normal daily routines, contact with loved ones and the environment, and coping strategies. The post-discharge period tends to be challenging, some have low motivation to continue treatment and there is a high risk of suicide. To date, there has been no comprehensive training program in the Czech Republic, Estonia and Croatia to support people with mental illness in this area.  As all three partner organisations are involved in the field of mental health care and adult education, they have combined their knowledge and skills to create an education program and support people with mental illness to return to the community.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to support, empower and strengthen the core competencies of people with mental illness prior to discharge from a psychiatric ward or hospital in order to support their recovery and return to the community through a developed training module including specific information, practical tools and space for reflection and sharing of experiences.

<< Implementation >>

1, Creation of the training module
2, Pilot training and evaluation
3, Updating of the training module and creation of video clip
4, Final conference and dissemination

<< Results >>

A training module has been developed for people with mental health problems to support recovery and return to the community after discharge from a psychiatric hospital or residential facility. It focused on three key topics: recovery, communication and safety. All three partner organisations were involved in its development and each team included trainers with their own experience of mental illness and recovery.
A total of 62 people with mental illness were educated and empowered for transition to the community in all partner countries.
Staff from 2 psychiatric hospitals, 1 residential facility and 1 recovery college gained knowledge and practical tools to empower people with mental health problems to recover and integrate into society.
A pilot training session was conducted, and the training module was evaluated and modified based on the experience and feedback.
A short video was produced to present the training module and the experience of the development and pilot teaching in all three partner countries.
Professionals and stakeholders have been informed and the training module has been made available to others who can use it in mental health care and in supporting people with mental illness to return to the community.

2021-2-DE02-KA210-ADU-000048970.title: Parents for Parents: adult education online courses around pregnancy, childbirth and life with a newborn
2021-2-DE02-KA210-ADU-000048970.summary:
<< Background >>

Both organizations are in close contact with new parents and parents to be, in Germany and Croatia, respectively. New parents frequently pointed out the gaps in the established birth preparation courses: the lack of certain information and how some given information was misinterpreted by parents. Hence the felt need to create something to fill those gaps and flank the classical midwife led birth preparation courses. Even more often did we hear about how new parents felt underinformed and overwhelmed by the first weeks with a newborn. Whenever we spoke to people we heard how valuable “approved parental knowledge” was to them. This approach is also supported in existing research (cfr. Pålsson et al (2018) DOI: 10.1891/1058-1243.27.3.163)
Hence the concrete need for high-quality, peer-approved information and orientation for parents around pregnancy, childbirth and the first time with a newborn. Mother Hoods’s goal was to create such courses, as inclusive as possible, whilst RODA’s goal was to make post-COVID adaptations to the most attended course and adjust video materials for people with impaired hearing. 
All courses needed a reliable and easy to use Learning Management System that also allowed for future development. 

<< Objectives >>

The aim was to create a resource for expectant parents, especially women, to expand their knowledge and capacities with high-quality adult learning online antenatal courses. The courses should be suited for text-to-audio apps, the visual /auditive material subtitled or transcripted. The project also aimed at increasing the capacities of the partner organizations in providing free, high-quality, low threshold, online adult education courses that meet the needs of all users, including those who are hearing impaired, with a special regard to “parents approved” tips and evidence-based content around maternal mental-health.
Mother Hood (MH) could benefit from Roda’s experience, who created their first e-learning platform during the COVID-crisis and were ready to share their experiences and know-how, so that MH could start building a platform without “beginner's mistakes”, learning from what Roda had already done and what had been proven successful. At the same time, our organizations wanted to build capacity by sharing experience on working as parental advocacy organizations in different areas of Europe, on working with parents, ideas on ways to convey useful and important knowledge and information to parents and scaling advocacy work.

<< Implementation >>

The project grouped around 5 Main Activities for the creation of 2 new e-learning courses (German), 2 post-Covid course up-dates (Croatian), incorporating barrier-free content and creating a user-friendly Learning Management System.
Particular exemplary activities: 
- 1 kick-off meeting at the Croatian partner, mentoring in “best-practice” around the creation of peer2peer, adult education eLearning for new parents as well as a very valuable best-practise guide for ERASMUS+ project management. It also highlighted how similar the basic needs of parents around maternity care are in our two countries.  
- 2 online mentoring webinars: 1 on online course authoring software and 1 best-practise for creating course video content for the formats (both proving extremely valuable and time-saving for the project)
virtual (sub-)group meetings (e.g. creative and thematic teams, regular virtual bi-national team exchanges) not only advancing the project but also developing a cohesive power after covid-crisis fluctuations in volunteer-based organizations
- launch event in Bonn, creating an important interdisciplinary space for parents, midwives, gender-equity politicians, psychologists, social workers, sparking new collaborations and projects.

<< Results >>

Major outputs:
2 websites with peer2peer adult education online courses, including the hosting platform and LMS (https://kurse.mother-hood.de/ and https://edukacija.roda.hr/), 
 
Secondary outputs and dissemination materials:
2 EPLAE blog posts: “Accessible, approachable, inclusive - The PregChiLi Project: A Transnational Peer2Peer Guide for Becoming and New Parents” (Part I, Part II)
2 articles in professional Midwifery journals (1 published, 1 submitted) 
2 press-releases, 
Social Media campaigns (continuing after project end)
 
Other non-public results in accordance with our application:
1 kick-off meeting; 1 detailed project implementation plan; 1 detailed dissemination plan, 11 monitoring meetings; 2 online workshops, 1 interdisciplinary live event in Bonn, Germany as well as the evaluation and assessment of course success (continuing) and assessing needs for future updates and sequelae (continuing)

2021-2-DE02-KA210-ADU-000049280.title: Caring Arts
2021-2-DE02-KA210-ADU-000049280.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we recognized the pervasive nature of discrimination and exclusion in our society. Our participating organisations observed a division in their work: their projects are dealing either with so-called inclusion or with gender justice but rarely connecting both. We wanted to overcome this artificial separation. We sought to address the topics within the arts, theater and education sectors in particular. The main need we addressed was to create an accessible art and education space where marginalized people can participate and feel safe, welcome, valued and seen. Recognizing that ideas of accessibility and care vary across different communities, we saw the necessity of incorporating diverse and transnational perspectives. Our project brought together queer feminist and disability justice activists from European regions to explore, discuss and experience the creation of accessible learning and creative spaces. We did this through the following activities: a close collaboration between partners and participants that was deepened in two hybrid educational trips to Munich and Vienna (one week each) and the creation of a website to share and diffuse some of our work. 

<< Objectives >>


    1. Promoting a Collective Understanding of Care: Care is often seen as a personal responsibility, predominantly shouldered by women - often tied to global inequalities through care chains. The project aimed to shift this perception by emphasizing care as a collective social issue.
    2. Building a Network to Articulate Mutual Care: The project sought to establish a transnational network and partnership.
    3. Addressing Divisions and Promoting Intersectionality: Participants noted a division in their work between projects focused on so-called inclusion and gender justice. The project aimed to overcome this division. 
    4. Highlighting Marginalized Voices: The project aimed to prioritize, center and amplify the voices of marginalized individuals, particularly disabled female, non-binary, and trans* theater pedagogues and curators. 
    5. Creating Relaxed and Accessible Spaces: the project aimed to develop a learning framework and practical experience in creating relaxed and accessible spaces that inherently embody principles of care.
    6. Sharing and difusing project results: Finally, the aim was to share the art, methods, thoughts and processes that been part of that journey for other educators and artists.

<< Implementation >>


1. Dreaming about Caring Arts - Methodological Online Laboratory:
        ◦ around 40 meetings with partners and / or partcipants thoughout the project
        ◦ Held internal workshops on:
            ▪ "Needs Assessment in Project Planning" in July 2022
            ▪ "Accessibility in Social Media" on 12th January 2023
        ◦ internal skill-sharing sessions and knowledge transfer on topics such as easy language, image descriptions, alternative texts, audio description and neurdivergent needs 
        ◦ collective curation of website creation and content creation, with content production and accessibility work carried out by participants 

        ◦ 2. "Caring Arts Lab Munich" Adult Educational Training:
        ◦  4th to 10th October 2022 in Munich
        ◦ 15 participants based in three partner countries 
        ◦ organization team developed the framework, while participants conducted workshops

        ◦ 3. Caring Arts Lab Vienna" Adult Educational Training:
        ◦  10th to 16th September 2023 in Vienna
        ◦ 15 participants from partner countries
 

<< Results >>

    1. Online Laboratory Meetings and 2 in-person training for adult education
        ◦ regular online meetings for exchange, organisation and skill-share
        ◦ two one-week trainings for adult education

    2. Creation of a Multimedia Website 
        ◦ Conceptualized, prepared, and collectively curated a multimedia website
        ◦ includes videos, texts, images, audios on methods and practices by participants and documentation of the common work
        ◦ The website can be accessed at www.caring-arts.org

    3. Sustainable change in partner Organizations
        ◦ more awareness for digital accessibility
        ◦ Implemented measures to enhance accessibility in workshops and educational work, including COVID prevention measures, alternative seating arrangements
        ◦ Revised work flows and practices to prioritize accessibility internally and with our target group

    4. Formation of Network
        ◦ Established a network of individuals who expressed a desire to continue working together
        ◦ Some partners applied for further funding to sustain collaborative efforts
        ◦ Fostered interpersonal and professional relationships 
        ◦ Some partners plan a new project together focusing on mental health

2021-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000048979.title: Empowering vulnerable women through financial education
2021-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000048979.summary:
<< Background >>

We decided to apply to this project to address the need of our beneficiaries- vulnerable women survivors of gender based violence and migrant women to learn new skills related to financial management and career management in order to gain independence and economic empowerment. according to current research across the EU, women have less financial education than men. the gender gap is particularly significant when it comes to financial literacy such as managing their budgets, savings or choosing convenient financial products. women survivors of gender-based violence are particularly vulnerable, since they were oftentimes under the control of their abusive partner and had no access to family finances. with this project we enabled 15 vulnerable women from Croatia and Italy to learn new skills related to financial management, savings, career managing, finding a better job, and using social capital. the two trainings they attended enabled them to set their long and short-term career goal s and to elaborate strategies and plans on how to realize them. a compendium containing relevant topics and outcomes of the trainings was created and disseminated to other interested stakeholders thorough partners’ websites and social media accounts. 

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project was to encourage the empowerment and the participation of the most vulnerable women
in their economic and social context.  specific project objectives were objectives:
1. to provide the basic theoretical and practical tools necessary for a proper financial literacy of women living in vulnerable
situations and economic and/or social difficulties;
2. to improve the knowledge of financial issues, especially those related to the management of own money and savings;
3. to strengthen women's self-esteem and their active participation in economic and financial processes within the
community;
4. to raise community awareness of women's financial literacy needs.
All project objectives were realized as planned.  A total of 20 vulnerable women from Croatia and Italy were empowered to be fully integrated in their socio-economic context through the participation in two 4-day trainings which were organized in Rome (June 2022) and in Zagreb (October 2022). Through information events, final conference and media campaign relevant stakeholders and other community members were informed about the specific needs of this target group. 


<< Implementation >>

The following activities were implemented: 
Activity 1 project management and coordination -the objectives of this activity were to encourage the partners' participation  in the activities and management; to ensure the achievement of project results and to define an internal monitoring procedures. 
Activity 2 transnational mobility 1 was held in Rome, Italy from 6-9 June 2022. A total of 14 vulnerable women from Croatia and Italy participated in the training which provided participants with basic knowledge related to finances, budget planning and savings management. 
Activity 3 transnational mobility 2 was held in Zagreb from 24-27 October 2022. During four days, 15 vulnerable women from Italy and Croatia learned new skills and worked on their careers through a series of topics related to career management and planning. 
Activity 4 project outputs: compendium and video - 2 videos and the compendium were developed by Progeu with inputs from AWHZ and Observo and are available on partner websites and social media accounts.  
Activity 5 communication and awareness-raising on project issues - through information events, final conference and media campaign relevant stakeholders and other community members were informed about the projec

<< Results >>

THE RESULTS AND OUTPUTS OF THE PROJECT ARE:
- Better knowledge of participants related to financial issues and money management 
- Improved competences of participants to make informed decisions in the economic and financial fields;
- enhanced self-esteem of women participating in the activities;
- improved capacity of women to actively participate in their economic and social context;
- increased awareness and knowledge of the community and EU citizens on women's financial literacy needs;
- 2 transnational courses (4 days each) addressed to a total of 20 vulnerable women were organized
- at the end of the 2nd transnational course 14 personal dairy booklets were developed by 14 vulnerable women who participated in the training. 
- 1 compendium containing details and materials of the training courses was developed and is available on partner websites in English and national languages: 
- 2 videos with testimonies of women during the trainings were created: https://www.instagram.com/p/ci-soggrrni/
https://youtu.be/e8q3pwb9hui
- 1 awareness-raising campaign on social media of partner organizations was implemented.

2021-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000049075.title: Virtualna realnost u kontekstu tretmanskih vještina
2021-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000049075.summary:
<< Background >>

Probation officers and treatment officers in the prison system work with offenders with the goal of achieving changes in behavior, attitudes, development of life, social and soft skills in order to better reintegrate into the community and become useful members of their communities. We applied for this project to enable officers who work with offenders to be educated and develop digital tools for learning and practicing the skills of working with offenders in the field of establishing a therapeutic alliance. The mentioned topic / skill is a prerequisite for any work with offenders, and evidence-based research and meta studies show that this very skill is a predictor of the success of any treatment. By improving the competencies of treatment officers, we provide a better level of service to offenders, we contribute to the motivation to change of offenders, that is, by using this approach in work, our end users - offenders, have a greater chance of reintegration into society, improving resocialization and rehabilitation, and reduced chances of recidivism. 

<< Objectives >>

Implementing the project activities, we wanted to achieve 4 key objectives: 1- strengthening the capacity and quality of work of probation officers (RH) and treatment workers of the prison system (RO) - to work on improving and maintaining the quality of work with offenders.
2-development of new digital tools in the field of work with offenders - to use modern technologies in the education of staff, but also to see the potential in working with offenders in the field of treatment and rehabilitation.
3-strengthening the knowledge and competence of treatmant / probation officers - on a professional and personal level, to improve the work of employees with the aim of ensuring better quality work and preventing burnout at work.
4-improvement of competitiveness, competence and motivation to change offenders - by providing competent employees in the field of rehabilitation, we improve the level of service that we as a society or system provide to offenders with the aim of preventing recidivism, improving rehabilitation and social inclusion. By providing a higher quality level of service, we improve the chances of offenders to acquire  social and life soft skills neccesary for resocialization back into the community and quality life. 

<< Implementation >>

Project activities were implemented in groups:
1-preparatory activities, project coordination and management; included kick-off meeting, meetings of project partners and communication related to the implementation of the project, coordination of project activities and cost monitoring.
2-development of digital tools and their adaptation in the education of probation officers and treatment officers; it included the development of scenarios and the recording of educational material that was adapted for Virtual Reality (VR) and which is used for the education of officers with VR, but can also be used as educational material without VR.
3-the implementation of the education, included the creation of a workbook on the topic of Establishing a therapeutic alliance and the implementation of a 30-hour education of the in Bucharest, for 20 participants (10 Hr and 10 Ro).
4-dissemination of newly acquired knowledge; it included presentations, participation in Congresses, Conferences, Summer Schools, Presentation of project results, TV feature, not only  for  dissemination but for project visibility.
5- evaluation of project activities; it included the evaluation of training, VRa and the project, and a report was prepared.

<< Results >>

A key and concrete result of the project is the educational material in digital form, which is available via a link for free and without restrictions. Can be used with or without VR. 20 officers improved their competences, knowledge and skills related to building relationships with offeners. We achieved all the planned indicators that indicate the results of the project implementation. We have created and printed 250 workbooks in Romanian, Croatian and English, participted in various events and conferences to diseminate results and knowledge. We managed to purchase 3 sets of glasses for VR, which remain for permanent use for education and further development of VR in work with offenders.
On the educational platform there are educational materials (5 presentations related to the skills of establishing a therapeutic alliance), video materials (for use with VR or without - a total of 12 scenarios related to the skills in a true/false version) and materials for testing knowledge through a scoring system.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000049289.title: e-odrasli
2021-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000049289.summary:
<< Background >>

The need for such a project stems from the fact that digital technologies have become an indispensable part of everyday life. Those who are less proficient in new technologies remain socially excluded, a digital divide occurs. In the pandemic that is behind us, we have seen how the oldest remain isolated because they do not have the necessary skills to navigate the digital world.

The project "e-adults" was conceived to meet the needs of people over 45 years of age for the development of digital skills. The extremely positive reaction of the participants after the lecture confirms that there is a great need for informal education for adults, because due to insecurity when handling digital technologies, an individual cannot perform an action for which he has knowledge. Such educations are very important for people who are "afraid" of new technologies. That is why a great focus through education was placed on the safe search of Internet content, on the importance of information, checking the accuracy of information and on the safe use of social networks.

<< Objectives >>

Goals of this project:

Offer people over the age of 65 to acquire or improve their digital competences so that they can become active citizens and be socially involved in the digital world.

Offer people aged 45 to 64 to acquire or improve their digital competences so that they can become active citizens and be socially involved in the digital world.

Design, implement, monitor and evaluate a curriculum that will train and/or perfect the digital competences of older people in order to guarantee their activity, social presence, e-governance, e-access, co-participation and personal development.

Systematically support active aging, access, social inclusion, participation and personal development using a digitalized learning ecosystem, as well as through e-services

Upgrade lifelong learning opportunities provided by adult education institutions, as well as improve teaching materials and resources used by institutions to meet the needs of senior citizens

Maximizing the use of digital resources to reduce the harmful impact on the environment (digital handbook)

<< Implementation >>

As part of this project, the following activities were successfully carried out:

1. Focus groups (Partner organizations each conducted two focus groups in order to identify the needs of project participants)

2. Examples of good practice (Partner organizations have collected examples of good practice from various sources)

3. Adaptation of existing programs (Based on the data collected through the first two activities, the existing program was adapted to meet the needs of the project participants)

4. Pilot implementation of the program (Both partner organizations implemented the pilot program. Project participants reacted very positively to the program. The only minus was that 30 hours was not enough for them)

5. Preparation of a manual for participants (Based on the experience gained from the implementation of this project, a manual was created that is adapted to the target group)


<< Results >>

Four focus groups with the target group were conducted (each partner conducted two), in order to determine the specific needs of persons aged 45 to 64 and persons older than 65 years.

Examples of good practices were collected and teachers were trained on the specifics of educating the elderly.

Based on examples of good practices and analyzes conducted on the basis of focus groups, old programs were adapted

Two pilot trainings were conducted (each partner conducted one training)

A digital manual was created in Croatian and Slovenian
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000049326.title: Improvement of Digital Skills of People with Intellectual Disabilities
2021-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000049326.summary:
<< Background >>

During the Covid crisis, our efforts to support people with intellectual disabilities revealed their limited digital knowledge and skills, hindering their ability to effectively utilize digital technologies and enhance their quality of life. We also discovered that individuals with intellectual disabilities who access the internet are highly vulnerable to deception and the potential for significant harm, as they lack awareness of online dangers and misinformation. Furthermore, we identified a lack of digital proficiency among caregivers, limiting their ability to provide efficient support.
Our search for suitable education and training programs for people with intellectual disabilities highlighted a significant gap, with a lack of dedicated and customized courses tailored to their specific needs. Recognizing that digitalization is a key priority for the EU in the coming years and acknowledging that people with disabilities cannot be left isolated, we decided to develop and implement an educational and training program.
The proposed program aimed to empower caregivers to educate people with disabilities in the field of digital skills, equipping them for the use of digital technologies in their daily lives. 

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the project were  as follows: To train associates of non-governmental organizations working with people with intellectual disabilities in teaching digital technology skills to enhance the social inclusion, independence, and quality of life of individuals with disabilities. To align the project with the horizontal priority of Inclusion and diversity in all fields of education by empowering the target group to teach people with disabilities and include them in education and training activities.
To address the horizontal priority of Addressing digital transformation through the development of digital readiness, resilience, and capacity by equipping the target group with digital knowledge and skills that can be transferred to people with disabilities, ultimately improving their quality of life. To enhance the integration of people with intellectual disabilities into the local community by acquiring digital skills, in line with the priorities of bridging intercultural, inter-generational, and social divides and fostering community cohesion.


<< Implementation >>

There were three activities implemented in the project:

Development of Educational Program and Material involved analyzing the needs of the target group, exploring the current state of the field covered by the project, and developing a training program. The main output was a comprehensive handbook that covered essential topics, including how to effectively teach and train people with intellectual disabilities, the significance of empathy for successful education and inclusion, and digital skills necessary for their inclusion.
Development of the Web Platform consisted of several tasks. First, there was a focus on ensuring usability and accessibility. This involved analyzing user needs, conceptualizing the platform accordingly. A software requirements specification was then created to outline the features and functionalities of the platform. A prototype was developed and tested. 
Pilot Education: In this activity, preparations were made for  pilot .The pilot education was conducted in accordance with plan and program developed in the previous project activity. Throughout the pilot phase, valuable feedback from  participants of the education program was gathered and utilized to improve the educational materials and the web platform.

<< Results >>

The outputs are as follow: : A specialized training program was developed for individuals who support people with intellectual disabilities. The program aimed to enhance their skills and knowledge in effectively assisting and guiding people with intellectual disabilities. A comprehensive handbook was created specifically for educators involved in the project. This handbook served as a practical guide, providing valuable information, A web platform was designed and developed in accordance with principles of usability, accessibility, and the software requirements specification. Extensive testing was conducted to ensure its functionality and effectiveness. The project involved the implementation of pilot education activities. These activities included preparing the necessary conditions for conducting face-to-face and online training, selecting representatives of the target groups in Croatia and Slovenia, organizing blended education that combined online and face-to-face components . The successful realization of the above-described outputs and achievements has made it possible to fulfill the main objectives of the project, which include the education and training of caregivers of people with intellectual disabilities.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2021-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000050744.title: Složno po vještine
2021-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000050744.summary:
<< Background >>

People with visual impairment due to obstacles caused by disability as well as social and physical barriers belong to an extremely sensitive group at risk of marginalization and social exclusion. Unfavorable economic situation, non-competitive occupations, prejudices of the environment and their own limitations caused by disability are some of the reasons why it is difficult for them to find employment and material security for more active inclusion in the community. In addition to unemployment, one of the most common obstacles to active participation in the life of the community is the inaccessibility of the environment, as well as information about rights and opportunities, which makes it significantly more difficult for them to spend quality free time, along with insufficient social contacts and socializing.
The Applicant and the Partner found that the problems faced by visually impaired people are universal, that is, they know no territorial boundaries. Precisely for this reason, the knowledge and skills acquired through previous work are an opportunity to use this project to upgrade existing knowledge, transfer mutual experiences and examples of good practice, and come up with new solutions together.

<< Objectives >>

The Project objective is to empower visually impaired people in the field of communication, social and digital skills so that they can compete equally on the labor market when finding employment or changing jobs.
The project "Unanimously to obtain skills" is aimed at increasing the competences of adults (18-50 years old) with visual impairment (blindness or low vision) who are members of the Croatian Association of the Blind and the Association of Associations of the Blind and Visually Impaired of Slovenia. By participating in the Project, visually impaired people will be better able to cope with the challenges they face today - lack of communication skills, insufficient and/or unsatisfactory social interaction, insufficient and/or inadequate digital literacy and overcoming language barriers in communication and everyday life.

<< Implementation >>

Activity 1. PROJECT MANAGEMENT - administrative and logistical part of the implementation of the project activities (all the necessary actions for the safe and quality implementation of the activities).

Activity 2. OFFLINE WORKSHOPS - 2 offline workshops with the aim of strengthening the communication, social and digital skills of people with visual impairment.
The first cycle of workshops was organized in Croatia at the Hostel - Educational Rehabilitation Camp for the Blind in Premantura (Istria). The secound cycle of workshops was organized in Slovenia in Izola.
The program included communication workshops in the context of job search and assertive/nonverbal communication; a workshop to strengthen digital skills (presentation of assistive technologies; LinkedIn; Apps; Resume; ) and various outdoor socialization and sports activities.
Activity 3. ONLINE WORKSHOPS - 6 online workshops with the aim of strengthening communication, social and digital skills (LinkedIn; CV; the concept of entrepreneurship and self-employment, activities and opportunities offered within the framework of the European Union; possibilities offered by Microsoft 365.)
Activity 4. INFORMATION AND VISIBILITY - informing the general public about the Project.

<< Results >>

The implementation of the project ensured the following concrete results:
- Increased communication and social skills of 33 visually impaired people
- Increased digital literacy of 33 visually impaired people
- The participants are more skilled in communicating in English
- Volunteers gained experience working with visually impaired people
- The applicant and Partner are empowered to implement the Erasmus+ program

Additional results:
- Exchange of experiences on employment opportunities between participants;
- Easier overcoming of communication barriers and consequently greater relaxation when communicating in a foreign language
- Increased network of social contacts and networking of blind and partially sighted persons from Slovenia and Croatia
- Improvement of teamwork and group work and more efficient structured problem solving
- Participants are better acquainted with the Erasmus+ program itself and the possibilities it offers
- Active exchange of experiences and information about the legal, social and social position of the blind and partially sighted in both countries
- Laying the foundation for further cooperation in new projects
topics: Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

2021-2-NL01-KA210-ADU-000048930.title: FeASibility of Implementing the Essential Skills Program for Adult EducatIon ORganizations, Educators, and Learners
2021-2-NL01-KA210-ADU-000048930.summary:
<< Background >>

The Erasmus+ KA210-ADU project seeks to pilot the Essential Skills Program (ESP) in Europe, enhancing soft skills for adult learners in Croatia and the Netherlands. Prompted by the Covid-19 pandemic's impact on work, necessitating remote skills, the project will adapt the U.S. ESP for European adult education. It will offer free training to young adults, the unemployed, and migrants, and aid NGO workers through soft skills assessment.

Exe-Leren and Ambitio College are collaborating to tailor the ESP to European needs, aiming to improve staff competencies and education quality. Exe-Leren's involvement complements their ComPas platform, which showcases skills in various contexts, while Ambitio College will develop relevant training programs.

The initiative promises mutual benefits through shared expertise, capacity enhancement, and essential skills development in line with labor market trends. It also supports the European Commission's green economy goals by fostering adaptable, resilient, and innovative skill sets.

<< Objectives >>

The Erasmus+ project aims to adapt and test the U.S.-developed Essential Skills Program (ESP) within adult education sectors in Croatia and the Netherlands. The ESP is centered on enhancing soft skills, crucial in today's labor market. The project's ambition is to assess the feasibility of ESP in Europe, providing free access to young adults with low skills, the unemployed, and migrants, and equipping NGO workers with a robust soft skills assessment tool.

The initiative intends to define the prerequisites for successful ESP implementation in Europe, ensuring it supports stakeholders in up-skilling and reskilling efforts. This is particularly focused on creating employment pathways that are aligned with labor market trends, including the burgeoning green job sector. The project targets a diverse group, including young adults, school dropouts, NEETs, and migrants facing labor market entry challenges, aiming to enhance their employability through improved soft skills.

<< Implementation >>

The project activities centered on assessing the viability of the Essential Skills Program in Europe.
1. Analysis of the needs and problems of target groups: This involves documenting assumptions about stakeholder and adult learner reactions, defining expected needs, and beginning segmentation for targeted approaches.
2.Building and Testing with Minimum Viable Product (MVP): The project managers from both organizations determined the feasibility of ESP through access to essential skills training courses, use of self-reflection guides, and analysis of survey data.
3. Analyzing and Comparing Results: This step includes interviewing participants, analyzing feedback, and iterating based on the responses to refine the MVP.
4. Determining Feasibility, Desirability, and Viability: The Dutch partner will lead in reporting on the feasibility and implementation of ESP, with results shared across networks to benefit stakeholders.
5.Implementation of Surveys and Usability Testing: To evaluate the interaction of targeted ESP users with the program and to assess the achievement of project goals.
6. Small experiments: Conducted to test the value and growth potential of the project, ensuring it provides better value for money than alternatives.

<< Results >>

Conducted a comprehensive feasibility study to evaluate the ESP's introduction across Europe. Developed and rigorously tested Minimum Viable Products (MVPs), including tailored adult training courses, a train-the-trainer program, and employer-focused soft skills assessments. Implemented detailed surveys and usability testing to measure ESP's user engagement and project objectives achievement. Actively engaged a diverse group of stakeholders, incl. adults, educators, & employers, to test and provide iterative feedback on the ESP, which informed further MVP development. Enhanced professional development through strengthened partnerships and improved staff competencies in evaluation methods and skills-based training approaches. Results & best practices were disseminated via the Erasmus+ results platform, EPALE, own websites and social media enhancing the ESP's visibility. Utilized project insights to inform future Erasmus+ project applications and to broaden the ESP's integration within European adult education organizations. Linked ESP learning outcomes with labor market data from Cedefop and EURES, ensuring the training provided aligns with current and emerging job market demands, particularly in sectors prioritizing green skills.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
