2021-2-PT01-KA210-ADU-000049880.title: DigitalGo
2021-2-PT01-KA210-ADU-000049880.summary:
<< Background >>

Digital literacy among the elderly in Europe has become increasingly important in recent years as technology continues to play a larger role in daily life. However, many older adults in Europe still struggle with basic digital skills, such as using a computer, a smartphone or navigating the internet. This can limit their ability to access important information and services, as well as prevent them from fully participating in the digital economy and its benefits. DigitalGO aims at including the elderly population living in rural communities in the digital transformation. It achieves this goal by supporting them with basic digital literacy and at the same time, acknowledging their relevant role as “keepers” of valuable intangible cultural heritage. This way, the inherent experience of the elderly is collected to then be shared as a community asset. Furthermore, the transnational European approach fosters the building of a learning community, promoting synergies with other initiatives. Over 10 months, the project successfully implemented a pilot learning program with Erasmus+ support in four EU rural regions, improving digital skills in writing, photography, audio and video from elderly people and ensuring their intangible wasn' lost

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were: 
1. Foster digital skills among elderly people living in European rural regions, and by doing so, engage them in the global digital transition. 
2. Design and create a basic digital learning programme tailored for adults with low previous digital literacy. 
3. Collect and place value on intangible cultural heritage kept within rural dwellers, pointing out these regions’ meaningful legacy and preventing it from being lost. 
4. Create a learning network which connects elderly people all across the EU, promoting cooperation and exchange among them and their communities, by exploring digitally available tools and digital transformation-related opportunities.

<< Implementation >>

The project was run by four partners, experts in their related fields - ACDIPE (PT) - coordination and communication, INTRAS (ES) - program design for the elderly, AS.FOR.IN (IT) - program design for trainers, Museum of Slavonia (CR) - exhibition. The program covered practical digital performance concepts in four modules – writing, photo, video, and audio, adapted and tailored to elderly people’s needs and context. A bigger engagement and learning success was ensured as, while attending the course, participants actively contributed to the co-creation of a hybrid exhibition which showcased their knowledge & expertise about local traditions, festivities and crafts. An exhibition and a virtual museum were the result of the work of the elderly and a window into their world, united with one theme (although diverse in many details). The project handbook was designed to summarise and make accessible the project results containing the syllabus, training materials, materials for social workers and the insights of all participating groups: trainers, learners, organisers, hosting organisations, etc. This enables the replication of the project.

<< Results >>

During four sessions, of at least two hours each, twenty-seven participants from four countries joined together to improve or acquire digital skills. From these co-creation sessions, tailored according to participants' needs, audio, video, writing and video content were produced and later organized to be exhibited online and in the Museum of Slavonia. The content produced by the participants came from intangible heritage they shared during the sessions as memories, songs, poems, traditions, recipes, handicrafts and others. In order to support trainees and trainers to develop the session and get results two guides were developed: Syllabus for professionals and Syllabus for Learners. With the experience gained during the process, a project handbook was developed, so others can implement similar activities. All these resources are available on the project webpage:;https://www.digital-go.eu/#/resources and in the EPALE space. The final outcome of the project - the exhibition - is available in four different languages: 
• English: https://360.digital-go.eu/en/ 
• Portuguese: https://360.digital-go.eu/pt/ 
• Italian: https://360.digital-go.eu/it/ 
• Spanish: https://360.digital-go.eu/es/ 
• Croatian: https://360.digital-go.eu/cr/

2021-2-RO01-KA210-ADU-000048413.title: The Heritage and Adult Education
2021-2-RO01-KA210-ADU-000048413.summary:
<< Background >>

In both Romania and Croatia there are hundreds of museums and thousands of organizations operating in the cultural sector and carrying out educational activities. Their target audience is usually formed by the students and the "hard core" of connoisseurs, in terms of attracting adults to activities, including low-opportunity categories, being recorded only timid attempts. In addition, although in the museum area is a long and rich in national and international collaboration in the field of cultural heritage exchanges and traveling exhibitions, we do not know, so far, about an initiative that would bring up the issue of collaboration in the field of adult education. Moreover, in the Romanian case, there are just 6 museum that have implemented E+ adult education (AE) projects, all of them being focused on the collaboration with AE providers and NGOs, not on collaboration with other museums in order to exchange good practices acquired and developed into this field.
Therefore, our initiative comes with the idea of collaboration at an EU scale among museums (not leaving aside other types of organizations) in the field of AE, using the cultural heritage as a resource, the base need for the partners being to adapt their educational offer

<< Objectives >>

The initial objectives (general and the SMART ones) were totally achieved:
- Increasing the organizational capacity of the partners.
- Increasing the level of transferability of methods and good practices, developed by the 2 promoters, within the cultural institutions of the partner countries, through transferability events.
- Increasing awareness on equality, non-discrimination and social inclusion, on heritage related activities, but also on the E+ for a minimum number of 20.000 adults.
- Increasing the visibility of the promoters.
- SO1: Increasing the organizational capacity of the 2 partners, by raising the competences of 10 members of staff that will be involved in organization of 2 bilateral mobilities, transferability events and publishing a guide/magazine, during 14 months of implementation.
- SO2: Increasing the level of transferability of methods and good practices in the area of adult education.
- SO3: Increasing awareness on equality, non-discrimination and social inclusion, on heritage related activities, but also on the funding program.
- SO4: Increasing the visibility and the capacity of promoters by establishing, strengthening, continuing and expanding an international partnership in the field of adult education.

<< Implementation >>

Within the project "The Heritage and Adult Education" were proposed and carried out the following activities:
A1.1. Mobility in Zagreb, 27th of June – 2nd of July 2022 (6 days).
A1.2. Mobility in Bucharest, 19th – 24th of September 2022 (6 days).
A2.1. Transferability event in Zagreb, 14th-16th of November 2022 (3 days).
A2.2. Transferability event in Bucharest, 14th-16th of November 2022 (3 days).
A3. Online conference, 3rd -4th of April 2023 (2 days).
A4. Editing the magazine “Heritage & Education”, 17th of November 2022 - 30th of April 2023 (a bulletin, edited and printed online and offline, containing 23 works in 128 pages).
A0. Promotion, dissemination and partnership enlargement, 1st of March 2022 - 30th of June 2023 (+ 6 additional days of offline transferability, enlargement and dissemination activities, 3 in Zagreb and 3 in Bucharest, June 2023).

<< Results >>

The project has the following results:
•	12 days of bilateral activities, involving 81 individuals from eight organizations.
•	Three days of transferability events held simultaneously at the MNIR and AMZ (over 250 participants).
•	The online conference "Heritage Education in a museum context, with 27 lecturers from seven museums participating. A total of 113 conference attendees were recorded.
•	A publication, "Heritage and Education Bulletin," ISBN 978-973-0-38372-0, edited and printed in 500 copies, distributed for free in Romania and Croatia, as well as online on the websites of the two partners. 
•	Four museum education programs, analyzed, rebranded, and integrated into the educational programs of the two partners.
•	Dissemination, transferability, and sustainability events.
•	10 members of the partners' staff directly involved, and having the opportunity to develop their personal and professional competencies.
•	Over 500 participants were engaged in the project's activities, and several hundred thousand citizens were informed about the project, partners activities, adult education domain, and the funding program.

2021-2-SI01-KA210-ADU-000048077.title: Gradi kakovost, zagotovi uspeh
2021-2-SI01-KA210-ADU-000048077.summary:
<< Background >>

Quality assurance in adult learning is becoming an increasingly important component of adult learning. Quality assurance has become an integral part of developing adult learning at the national level. In Slovenia and Croatia, a system of internal quality assurance based on self-evaluation is also included in the adult education legislation and, as such, is mandatory for adult education organizations. The information obtained through self-evaluation helps organisations make further decisions on the necessary improvements in the organisation, which in turn means improving the work done so far and demonstrating social responsibility towards the environment in which they operate. The project compared the two quality assessment systems, intending to digitise data on the satisfaction of participants and teachers in adult education. As the two Croatian organisations (POU Čakovec and DANTE) are new to quality assessment, and LU Lendava has many years of experience, we presented our Croatian colleagues with examples of good practice and empowered them to continue to improve the quality of their work in the field of quality assessment. 

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the transnational cooperation was to compare and standardise the quality assessment procedures in the selected fields and to upgrade them with examples of good practices, exchange of experiences, and digitization of the quality assessment process in the chosen fields, which constituted the first steps towards quality assessment in adult education at the transnational level. The project activities have created an optimised quality assurance process for the delivery of non-formal education programmes, identified standard components and differences in the implementation of self-evaluation, and influenced the thinking of adult educators on the importance of assessing and ensuring the quality of all educational services not only at the organisational level, but also at the national and transnational level. Digitization has shortened and facilitated while creating a more organic approach to quality assessment and ensuring that quality assessment in non-formal adult education programmes in the future will be unified at a transnational level and more streamlined as the data generated will be faster and easier to process. The project has thus marked the start of a unification of the quality assessment process.

<< Implementation >>

quality of our services. We carried out two-day model visits to each of the partner organisations, where we got to know the quality assurance work of each organisation, exchanged first-hand experiences, and, based on these, made a plan for implementing improvements within each organization. Based on the exchange of experiences and the two methods of quality assessment based on self-evaluation, we decided at the partnership level which quality assessment indicators to assess at the transnational level, and for this purpose, we developed an online platform with questionnaires in all three languages that can be digitally processed. We then conducted a pilot quality assessment on the selected indicators (satisfaction of participants and staff in non-formal adult education programmes) and appointed a quality monitoring panel at the transnational level. We have also prepared an action plan to introduce changes in the selected indicators at the transnational level and will follow up on the implementation of the changes after the end of the project.

<< Results >>

As part of the project, we: 
1. We prepared a comparative analysis of quality assessment between the Slovenian and Croatian models based on self-evaluation. The document also includes a comparative study of the legislation on quality assessment and a comparison of quality indicators and standards by which quality is assessed in adult education. The resulting comprehensive document is also presented on an online platform.
2. We embarked on model visits, where we had the opportunity to present the quality assessment system and share examples of good practice with our esteemed colleagues. These visits were also about learning and gaining insights from each other's experiences, fostering a spirit of continuous improvement in our project.
3. Based on the expected points of both models, we selected two indicators that can be assessed in both countries and developed questionnaires.
4. Set up an online platform containing all the project's intellectual outputs and test the online questionnaires.
5. Based on the results of the questionnaires' online testing, produce a self-evaluation report at the transnational level.
6. Prepare an action plan for implementing the changes
7. Appoint a quality monitoring committee at the transnational level

2021-2-TR01-KA210-ADU-000048627.title: COOPERATION FOR INTEGRATION UNDER FINANCIAL INCLUSION OF CURRENT REFUGEES AND NEWCOMERS
2021-2-TR01-KA210-ADU-000048627.summary:
<< Background >>

Removing barriers for expanding financial access for refugees has been one of the most crucial issues in countries which have high refugee population. Project partners consist of Greece and Croatia which have high refugee population after Türkiye. The countries hosting large numbers of refugees, local communities often experience a high level of poverty problems and have to take precautions, regulations and practices regarding the financial problems of immigrants. Common problems of refugees in different countries may allow to reduce the problems to be experienced in the future.

We applied for this project to indicate the preferences and expectations of refugees and highlight general priority issues, clarify the main gaps between the legal frameworks and actual practices through sharing the best practices of with a multi country perspective.  Clarifying the best practices of a multi-country perspective to eliminate the deficiencies in the financial integration was another need that we have addressed through search conferences and semi structured interviews.

<< Objectives >>

In carrying out the project, we wanted to achieve the goals that below emphasized.
1. Clarifying the best practices of a multi-country perspective to eliminate the identified deficiencies in the financial harmonization and integration studies for the target group.
2. Conducting semi-structured interviews to determine refugees' financial inclusion, and financial literacy knowledge, skills and competence levels in all partner countries.
3. Developing a roadmap for relevant institutions and organizations in order to increase financial inclusion, financial access, and financial literacy levels of the refugees

<< Implementation >>

During the project, we implemented all work packages as we have stated in the project proposal.
First, we have made a comprehensive research of previously identified needs and gaps in financial inclusion of the refugees. In the second workpackage, we have organized search conferences for refugees to discuss the financial inclusion, financial access and financial literacy in all countries. In the third workpackage, we
conducted semi-structured interviews to determine refugees' financial inclusion, and financial literacy knowledge, skills and competence levels. We have visited the partner countries and been as an observer during the interview process.  In the last workpackage, we have made dissemination and communication activities among partners, target group and policy makers. We organized conferences together researchers and finance professionals with refugee representatives and government administrative officials to ensure the exchange of information and the dissemination of not only best practices but also the issues and challenges that need to be addressed to promote financial literacy and inclusion.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs of the project; Search Conferences Report, Semi-structured interview reports and Financial Inclusion Guidebook. According to the search conference results, the level of national welfare, its relationship with the sustainable development goals (SDGs), and financial literacy level appear as the top most significant factors that affect the inclusion of refugees in Turkey (Syrians under temporary protection) into the financial system. Furthermore, digital transformation is the first factor that supports the development of financial inclusion. Semi-structured interview results indicate the local language problem as the most significant barrier for refugees for all countries. Financial inclusion guidebooks and reports have already addressed the necessary implications for regulators and policy-makers in all countries
topics: Economic and financial affairs (including funding issues)
Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

2022-1-BE02-KA210-ADU-000083541.title: A Theatrical Museum Experience
2022-1-BE02-KA210-ADU-000083541.summary:
<< Background >>

In this project the partners wanted to exchange good practices to create interactive and immersive experiences in a museum context, while training educators and delivering tangible results. We also tried to focus on vulnerable target groups during the project. The method applied was mainly learning through experiencing. The main need we addressed was: how to attract, educate and entertain visitors in a museum using dramatic expression. The partners in this project wanted to extend their knowledge, experience and network in the field, they also wanted their actors/educators to gain more experience using drama in education.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted the partners involved to expand their knowledge and understanding of their respective target groups, to improve their communication with the target groups, to increase their know-how of non-formal education and the use of drama in an educational or museum context, to develop their skills and competencies in writing pedagogical materials, to increase their competencies in working together with international partners, and to share what they have learnt with other organizations.


<< Implementation >>

During and in between the TPM and LTT meetings, we organized meetings and discussions on our evolution (including permanent evaluation), practical workshops, museum visits, guided tours, interviews with educators from other organizations, and we made a brochure and some accompanying videos to share what we have learnt and to help museums start using drama.

<< Results >>

The most concrete output is our brochure with accompanying videos, which can help museums implement drama in their daily activities. Other results are: better knowledge of our target groups, better know-how of non-formal education and the use of drama in an educational or museum context, improved skills and competencies in writing pedagogical materials, improved competencies in working together with international partners, and an extended network because we worked together with several other organizations/museums in Belgium, Croatia and Sweden.

2022-1-BE02-KA210-ADU-000084755.title: In Search of Professionalism for DeafBlind Sign Language users: exploring the existing ones and considering the missing ones
2022-1-BE02-KA210-ADU-000084755.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the critical needs of empowering deafblind sign language users in Italy. Recognizing them as the primary target group, our goal was to inspire and empower them to become trainers for future assistants and interpreters. The project provided role models, concrete actions nationwide, and immediate financial support, resulting in positive impacts. Increased awareness of unique needs and enhanced self-confidence were observed among deafblind sign language users in Italy. Regarding our second target group composed of service providers and policy makers, since there is a crucial need of professional service providers for deafblind sign language users in Italy, we wanted to raise awareness among interested and aspiring service providers such as deafblind interpreters and deafblind assistants on deafblind topics as well as on how to become professionals and allies of deafblind users in Italy. We addressed those needs by creative a supportive environment where deafblind sign language users could actively contribute to the development of future professionals in their country, thanks to the positive impact of role models from partner organizations in this project. 

<< Objectives >>

The project had the following concrete objectives: 
- Promoting transnational exchanges and knowledge sharing among European and national deafblind organization
- Increasing awareness about the importance of professionalism in services for deafblind sign language users
- Empowering deafblind sign language users to advocate for their rights to quality services and to become trainers of deafblind professions. 
- Developing awareness-raising materials at the European level

The envisioned results encompassed the creation of a network of European and national deafblind organizations, heightened awareness among Italian deafblind participants as well as a part of the service providers and policy makers in Italy, empowerment of deafblind sign language users in Italy, and the collaborative development of a Deafblind Professionalism Awareness Pack by partner organizations. These outcomes were designed to not only address immediate needs but also establish a foundation for ongoing advocacy and collaboration in the realm of deafblind services in Italy and beyond.

<< Implementation >>

The project featured two key activities. The "Experts and Preparatory Meeting" gathered deafblind  representatives, the Italian events coordinator, and the media officer. Over four days, the team exchanged expertise, discussed, and crafted materials for the Deafblind Professionalism Awareness Pack. This included three days of intensive preparation to host workshops and lectures, with the fourth day dedicated to preparing the subsequent "Deafblind Professionalism Awareness Seminar." During this phase, a promotional video for the seminar was produced in collaboration with the media officer.

The "Professional Awareness Seminar" attracted about 80 participants from Italy, and some European countries, including deafblind individuals, service providers, and policymakers. The workshops and presentation have outlined professionalism standards, explored the importance of allyship, provided insights into specialized interpretation, detailed assistant responsibilities, explored the unique identity of deafblind individuals, advocated for rights and equal access, and defined roles within services. Post-seminar, the expert team spent three days evaluating results, reflecting on future pack utilization, and working on it for its publication. 

<< Results >>

The project achieved the expected concrete outputs that are the Deafblind Professionalism Awareness Seminar and the publication of the Deafblind Professionalism Awareness Pack. Those results were exceeding our expectations as the initial target of 50 participants was surpassed with 80 participants at the Seminar, where active engagement occurred between participants and experts. Notably, service providers, aspiring deafblind assistants, and policymakers demonstrated commitment to enhancing professionalism in services. Deafblind participants expressed interest in becoming trainers, and seven of them established a working group with financial support for nationwide advocacy in Italy. The project also expanded networks, strengthened relationships among partner organizations, and garnered heightened commitment from the European Deafblind Union (EDbU) for a European approach on Deafblind professionalism. Moreover, representatives from other countries such as Spain, Germany and France attended the Seminar and showed increased interest in working in the same perspective as the project organisations. Finally, the Deafblind Awareness Raising Pack has been published on the webpage of the project and disseminated at the European level.

2022-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000082548.title: BRIDGING DIGITAL AND LANGUAGE SKILLS GAPS FOR ADULT PROFESSIONALS
2022-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000082548.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the "Digital SkillsUp" project in response to the critical need to address the digital skills gap among adult learners and educators across Europe. The rapid digital transformation in various sectors has highlighted a significant deficiency in digital literacy, particularly among adults who are either entering the workforce or seeking to enhance their employability. This gap poses a considerable challenge, as it limits individuals' ability to participate fully in the digital economy, access essential services, and engage in lifelong learning.

Moreover, educators themselves often lack the necessary digital competencies to effectively integrate technology into their teaching practices, which further exacerbates the issue. The need to upskill both adult learners and educators was evident, especially in light of the increasing reliance on digital tools and platforms in education and the workplace.

The four institutions involved in this project are dedicated to adult education, and based on our extensive experience in this field, we identified a clear necessity for a specialized training module.

<< Objectives >>

Enhance Digital Literacy: Equip adult learners with essential digital competencies, enabling them to navigate and utilize digital tools effectively in both personal and professional contexts. This would improve their employability and ability to participate fully in the digital economy.

Empower Educators: Provide educators with advanced training in digital teaching tools and methodologies. This would enable them to integrate technology into their teaching practices more effectively, leading to improved educational outcomes for adult learners.

Foster Collaboration: Strengthen collaboration between educational institutions and the digital industry. By doing so, we aimed to ensure that the training provided was relevant and up-to-date with industry standards, thereby maximizing its impact.

Promote Lifelong Learning: Encourage a culture of continuous learning among adult learners and educators by developing a sustainable model for digital skills training that could be adopted and adapted by educational institutions across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

All the activities were implemented in the project. Development of Training Modules: Created a comprehensive "Skills-Up Training Toolbox" that included modules on digital language tools, gender-inclusive language, and digital networking. Each module was designed to be user-friendly and accessible, with interactive elements such as quizzes, case studies, and practical exercises.
Resource Compilation: Curated a set of resources, including guides, tutorials, and best practices, to support both trainers and participants in effectively utilizing digital tools. The toolbox was made available in multiple languages to ensure wide accessibility.
Online "Train-The-Trainers"
Trainer Preparation: Conducted an online "Train-The-Trainers" program to equip educators with the knowledge and skills needed to deliver the "Digital Skills Up" training effectively.  You-Yes! Platform was used for the trainings and to recopilate all the information and to ensure the widespread impact of the "Digital Skills Up" project, various dissemination activities were conducted. These included organizing workshops, seminars, and presentations to share the project's outcomes with a broader audience, including educators, policymakers, and other stakeholders.

<< Results >>

The "Digital Skills Up" project produced several outputs. The "Skills-Up Training Toolbox"* was developed, offering user-friendly modules on digital language tools, gender-inclusive language, and digital networking. An "Online "Train-The-Trainers" Program" equipped educators with the skills to deliver these modules effectively. The "You-Yes Platform" served as the hub for all training activities, facilitating access to resources, enabling communication, and supporting data-driven improvements. Dissemination Events: included both online and in-person conferences, leading to 10 agreements with public and private institutions to continue using the project's materials and platform, ensuring the project’s sustainability and broader impact.

2022-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000082878.title: “Fins into the water - Mediterranean Sea Literacy into practice”
2022-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000082878.summary:
<< Background >>

The Mediterranean region is a unique and diverse place that is visited by millions of people every year who usually carry out leisure and water sport activities. There Coastal and Maritime Tourism users and providers (CTM) however many times they lack knowledge, time and tools to do their activities in a more environmentally friendly way. Furthermore, there are several languages in the region, and CTM users and providers lack harmonized resources to learn more about marine protection. Moreover, these sectors are vulnerable for changes in the environment due to climate change such as heatwaves, biodiversity loss, extreme events jeopardizing their functioning. The knowledge gap between visitors, providers and their collaboration and participation in marine conservation and ocean literacy is obvious and solutions for this issues are needed. Education and awareness raising play a key role to advance behavioral changes and mitigation of environmental problems with the inclusion of CMT users and providers in the Mediterranean.

<< Objectives >>

The overall aim of the project was to spread ocean literacy in general, and more specifically Mediterranean Sea Literacy awareness for the CTM users and providers and to the general public to advance understanding and  behavioural changes related to coastal tourism. 
Ocean literacy and its 7 principles are an already well-known terms, however there is a lack of understanding and awareness of the MSL principles, in spite of the fact that the region and sea is one of the most fragile regions on the world, experiencing several pressures, mostly coming from the tourism sector.
The project aimed at providing up-to-date knowledge, tools and information to the target groups and to the general public in all the languages of the Med, because everything starts with education. These materials are easily understandable, engaging but also in-depth and very informative. Building on these materials, the project aimed to visit target group members in person to implement all the materials and enhance the understanding of the MSL principles. Therefore the project created a network of stakeholders in the watersport sector who were made aware of the environmental problems and now have the knowledge to transfer this information to their clients.

<< Implementation >>

The Fins into the Water project aimed at enhancing behavioural changes in the minds of the CTM users and providers and spread ocean literacy in the region with the following activities: 
- Translate the Mediterranean Sea Literacy (MSL) guidebook that is built on the 7 ocean literacy principles tailor made for the Med into all Mediterranean languages,
- Gather resources, teaching materials and best practices related to ocean literacy in the region that can be used by the target group members and create an easily accessible database for the public,
- Launch  a Resource map with these resources that interactively and visually shows the different materials divided by water sports and regions,
- Develop brief but engaging visual materials such as infographics and videos explaining the MSL principles,
- Implementation and Dissemination actions of in-person visits to water sport centres, aquariums, NGOs where partners carried out on-the-spot trainings for CTM users and providers and shared with them the project materials,
- Local and international actions where in-person events shared results,
- Final webinar served as a closing event for the project to disseminate all materials to the target groups
- Online dissemination on social media

<< Results >>

The Fins into the Water project has gathered the following outputs and results:
- MSL brochure in all the Mediterranean languages (Spanish, Catalan,French, Italian, Greek, Croatian, Turk, Hebrew and Arabic) plus Maltese as an additional language. However, the design of the Turk, Hebrew and Maltese versions is still pending.
- 150 resources, teaching materials in sea literacy have been collected by partners and uploaded to the Database and Resource Map,
- 113 Organizations, water sport centres have been reached out mostly in person to disseminate project materials, and raise awareness on the topic and advocate for individual and collective actions,
- 7 local events were carried out in person to engage mostly local communities such as school children, youth, tourists, water sport enthusiasts, scientists etc. and promote sea literacy,
- A final online webinar available for anybody interested to learn about the Med, where 92 registered and 45 attended from all over the world,
- Participation in a final event by organizing a workshop at the EMSEA Annual Conference with participation of 15 people from different disciplines to brainstorm on marine issues and how their solutions can be implemented in water sport centres.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2022-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000083116.title: Mayores Embajadores
2022-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000083116.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to enhance the participation of Older Adults (PPMM), migrants, and women in community development, recognizing their invaluable life experiences as essential for promoting social inclusion and cohesion. There is a significant need to address issues of social isolation, exclusion, and the underrepresentation of these groups in decision-making processes and community activities. Older adults, especially women, often encounter barriers that hinder their active contributions to society, while migrants frequently struggle with integration and visibility in their new environments.

This project aimed to elevate their voices, reduce social exclusion, and encourage intergenerational and cross-cultural dialogue. By creating opportunities for these groups to share their experiences—through exhibitions, emotional intelligence workshops, and multimedia storytelling—we sought to boost their confidence, foster emotional resilience, and ensure their contributions were recognized. Ultimately, our goal was to cultivate a more inclusive environment where everyone’s input is valued, benefiting both the individuals involved and the broader community, fostering a sense of belonging and empowerment.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to celebrate the role of Older Adults as vital social resources and cultural ambassadors within their communities. We sought to empower them as Major Ambassadors (MAEM), facilitating their active participation in civic life and enabling them to convey shared values across generations. By recognizing their contributions, we envisioned creating opportunities for intergenerational learning, where citizens of all ages could appreciate the richness of cultural heritage.
Given the Canary Islands' unique geographical position as a crossroads of Europe, America, and Africa, we aimed to leverage this setting to foster intercultural cooperation. We anticipated addressing the marginalization and social isolation faced by older adults, combating the negative perceptions that label them as burdens.
Ultimately, we aspired to restore purpose and motivation to their lives, helping them regain self-esteem while enriching community life through their stories, traditions, and experiences. By showcasing their culture in engaging ways, we hoped to reduce loneliness and enhance community cohesion, ensuring that their invaluable contributions are celebrated and recognized, benefiting both individuals and society as a whole.

<< Implementation >>

In our project, we implemented a range of activities designed to engage older adults and other community members effectively. First, we created an identifying LOGO to represent the MAEM project, enhancing its visibility and identity. We launched the MAEM website, serving as a window to the world, providing essential information and resources.
To communicate our objectives, we designed a FLYER outlining the project’s aims and a POSTER that encapsulated its essence. We conducted a COURSE on Social Competence, focusing on Emotional Intelligence for Adults, equipping participants with valuable social skills.
The MAEM MAGAZINE was published to visually showcase the stories and contributions of older adults, serving as a graphic exhibition of their experiences. We produced an INCLUSIVE MULTIDISCIPLINARY DOCUMENTARY, highlighting the narratives of older adults and promoting their voices within the community.
Additionally, we organized exhibitions of GOOD PRACTICES that presented motivating examples, such as lived stories, migration experiences, contributions of exemplary women, and nature protection efforts. These activities fostered connections and encouraged active participation among diverse community members.

<< Results >>

The project yielded several concrete results that significantly impacted the community. First, we observed a noticeable increase in the participation of older adults, who felt valued for their contributions and creativity showcased during the EXHIBITIONS OF GOOD PRACTICES. These exhibitions not only highlighted their innate qualities and hobbies but also promoted a sense of pride and motivation among participants.
The project successfully fostered interrelationships within the community, enhancing collaboration across various sectors. This bidirectional approach enabled us to create synergies that maximized the effectiveness of our interventions. As a result, community members became more actively involved in addressing current social issues, demonstrating a stronger commitment to collective well-being.
Moreover, the publication of the MAEM MAGAZINE and the production of the INCLUSIVE DOCUMENTARY served as vital platforms for sharing stories, thus raising awareness about the experiences of older adults, migration, and environmental protection. Overall, the project not only empowered older adults but also enriched the community’s cultural tapestry, promoting inclusivity and shared understanding among all generations.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2022-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000082012.title: Économie circulaire sur les petites îles d'Europe
2022-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000082012.summary:
<< Background >>

Small European islands are laboratories for sustainable development and innovative, environmental and technical solutions. They share similar challenges and common solutions to ensure the sustainable management of their environment. However, the isolation, the scarcity of resources, the limited space, in other words the insular character, a priori reduces the range of solutions to preserve them. Thus, the circular economy and solutions against climate change in these territories have become a priority to promote more sustainable development. Preservation and protection of resources, reduction and recovery of waste, development of eco-responsible tourism... Innovative, effective and easily replicable solutions exist locally and deserve to be shared with other European islands and beyond. This is why this project, based on 4 pilot islands and partners similar in terms of the challenges faced, and different in terms of their operating methods, expertise, culture and geography, made it possible to strengthen their skills, to exchange good practices and cooperate at European level to guarantee more sustainable territorial planning.

<< Objectives >>

This project fully responded to the general objective of meeting the needs for exchanges and strengthening the knowledge of managers of small European islands in terms of circular economy and adaptation to climate change, via the specific objectives:
-Strengthen the capacities of small islands and less experienced European organizations to work in networks
-Strengthen the technical skills of project partners in the aforementioned areas, and sustainable territorial planning. Sharing experiences is essential to strengthen their resilience to climate change. The objective was also to strengthen the capacities to use the SMILO sustainable territorial management tools (territorial diagnosis and strategic plan) and for SMILO to strengthen its technical capacities linked to the subjects of the project and its capacity to lead the islands towards sustainable territorial approaches.
-Strengthen European cooperation, through dialogue, the implementation of co-constructed activities, including welcoming a delegation on their own island, and the creation of common results with European partners 
-Enrich the SMILO catalog of concrete actions dedicated to disseminating good island practices

<< Implementation >>

The project aimed to develop exchanges between partners from small European islands. Four transnational inter-island meetings were organized on the small project islands: Frioul (FR), Gozo (MT), Hvar-Pakleni (HR) and Sifnos (GR). The programs for these meetings were determined according to the skills needs of the partners in the field of the circular economy and solutions to climate change. Local experts trained the partners as well as local participants (local stakeholders, including public authorities, local NGOs, residents, etc.) with an average of more than 50 participants per event. Thus, these meetings allowed participants to exchange with other islands on the circular economy in order to gain skills in this area and in sustainable territorial planning, to defend island ecosystems, to promote European cooperation and to develop more sustainable management of their own territory by drawing inspiration from the training and good practices shared during inter-island meetings. Good practice sheets have been written and shared widely to promote the project and the circular economy on small islands.

<< Results >>

The project made it possible to create within the SMILO network a strengthened exchange group with a view to transferring know-how in the field of the circular economy, climate change and sustainable territorial planning/management. The experimentation of an innovative model of inter-island cooperation enabled the organization of an inter-island meeting co-constructed by the partners (4 in total, including: exchanges of good practices, field visits, training, etc.): 50+ sustainable solutions exchanged, 200 people strengthened in technical capacities (local stakeholders, European island partners, SMILO, etc.)
8 good practices with high potential for replicability written, which will continue to be used/disseminated in the long term 
The partners were able to put the SMILO methodology into practice for sustainable territorial planning: 4 island committees, a consultation body bringing together the main stakeholders to agree on a shared vision of the sustainable development of the island in the long term (dynamics of continuous improvement thanks to the SMILO methodology). 
3 new EU islands (Gozo, Sifnos, Pakleni) and strengthen its cooperation with Frioul.

2022-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000082412.title: Osnove korištenja računala i pametnih telefona za treću životnu dob
2022-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000082412.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we recognized the real needs of our fellow citizens, especially those aged over 60 in our community. We observed that despite existing computer usage education, there is a lack of a specific and tailored program for older individuals. Our goal was to develop a program that would focus on their specific needs, a program that would save them time in their daily activities and improve their communication with family and friends, enable them to read news online, and enjoy their free time more. 
Additionally, we noticed that older people often aren't involved in education due to financial constraints. Through this project, we wanted to provide a high-quality learning opportunity, with special attention to adapting program activities to their needs. Through collaboration with partners, we have developed a program that, besides helping our fellow citizens, will be sustainable and beneficial for both partners in future activities. We have also facilitated intergenerational exchange of experiences and knowledge, contributing to adult education inclusivity and diversity.


<< Objectives >>

Through the implementation of this project, we aimed to develop a customized educational program for individuals aged over 60, focusing on computer and smartphone usage. The objectives were to enhance digital skills, promote social inclusion through online communication, and contribute to a better aging process by providing older individuals with tools for active participation in the digital world. Furthermore, the project had a long-term vision – creating a sustainable program for partner organizations and raising awareness about the importance of digital literacy among older individuals. Through international collaboration, the goal was to exchange experiences and enhance educational practices. The project team aspired to bring about positive changes in the lives of older individuals, contributing to their improved quality of life and social inclusion.

<< Implementation >>

As part of our project, we implemented various activities to achieve our set objectives. We developed a customized educational program for individuals aged over 60, with a focus on digital skills. Activities included needs analysis, participant engagement, organization of educational sessions, online communication using tools like Zoom, collaboration with local associations and institutions, and regular evaluation of participant progress. Additionally, we established international collaboration with partners from North Macedonia, exchanging experiences and adapting the program based on shared insights. The goal was to promote digital inclusion, improve participant skills, and ensure the sustainability of the program in the local community.

<< Results >>

The project on the Basics of Computer and Smartphone Usage has achieved significant results. A comprehensive program tailored to the needs of the community's older population has been developed. Project participants demonstrated positive changes in their habits and behaviors, acquiring new social skills. The project fostered connections among education participants within the community, strengthening social networks. Organizations have expressed interest in the long-term utilization of the program, and the results have been disseminated through organization websites, newsletters, local online portals, and the Erasmus+ platform. Furthermore, the project contributed to raising awareness about the importance of supporting older individuals and enhancing collaboration between organizations and local communities. The held educational sessions raised awareness about the inclusion of senior members of our sociey.

2022-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000082786.title: Osnaži me za posao!
2022-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000082786.summary:
<< Background >>

SOS4JOB is a continuation of partnership from Erasmus+ project ASPIRE, in which research and testing of feasibility of implementing Essential Skills Program in Europe was carried out to increase accessibility for different target groups with the aim of creating better learning opportunities that match the needs of different workplaces. In that project employers and employees saw the value of applying soft skills in the workplace and they greatly contribute to productivity of every organization, while the unemployed/employed (tested one ESP module) stated they wanted education with multiple tasks, but on Croatian and Dutch. Considering that there is no structured education in soft skills in Croatia and Netherlands, it was necessary to adapt ESP for European market by developing additional digital workbooks, implement soft skills training in three languages and make a comparative analysis of situation before and after training. The implementation of ESP resulted with public awareness of importance of soft skills, provided an innovative opportunity to learn about soft skills, contribution to development of flexible learning offers adapted to educational needs of adults and aim of providing education in a digital environment.

<< Objectives >>

The project implemented an innovative online training - Essentials Skills Program in the field of most wanted soft skills on the labour market, which resulted with the public awareness of the importance of soft skills education at the local, regional and European level. It was also provided an innovative learning opportunity about soft skills to target groups (unemployed and employed persons, participants of other partner education programs and teachers in adult education) and carried out an analysis of the target groups with the aim of measuring the level of existing knowledge before and acquired skills after the training and the quality of the developed training. The implementation of the training contributed to the development of flexible learning offers adapted to the educational needs of adults, as well as to the goal of providing education in a digital environment. In this way, the developed program will be included in the education offer of the partners after the project so that other individuals can be empowered in soft skills.

<< Implementation >>

Three activities were carried out within the project. Digital workbooks were created on the e-learning platform Moodle for the 10 most wanted soft skills in English, Dutch and Croatian as additional learning material containing theory with problem-based interactive closed-type tasks from real business and private situations, video materials and questions related to green practices to encourage the adaptation of green practices. In this way, the participants were enabled to upgrade and develop their skills as an additional benefit and facilitated the use and understanding of Essential Skills Program content. An innovative online ESP training in the field of development of the 10 most wanted soft skills was conducted on the Canvas and Moodle platform for three target groups (unemployed and employed people, participants of other partner education programs and teachers in adult education). Upon completion of the implementation, three analyses were done for the target groups per partner based on the collected questionnaires, which provided valuable feedback on the level of acquired knowledge in the field of soft skills, satisfaction with individual training segments, and advantages/disadvantages and suggestions for improvement.  

<< Results >>

Concrete results are:
- 10 workbooks in English, Croatian and Dutch language for 10 ESP modules developed
- 131 participants educated from Croatia, Netherlands, Greece, Bulgaria and Spain 
- evaluation and self-evaluation conducted and data analysed and published in 3 analyses in English, Croatian and Dutch language
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000082923.title: Nauči da budeš! - edukacijom žena do povećanja rodne ravnopravnosti na tržištu rada
2022-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000082923.summary:
<< Background >>

Motivation for the project is based on the partner's long-term work with adult women, helping them with everyday challenges in the business world. Zaposlena d.o.o. in 2014. designed and launched a project that help women through mentoring with the purpose of making it easier to overcome challenges in women's careers called "Mentoring as a form of networking among women". Mentoring of women also gave rise to the idea of the project because stereotypes were observed during the discussion, which confirm detected limiting factors of adult women in business takeoff. Also, Associazione Eurokom's analysis confirmed the need to increase the level of knowledge and awareness of adult women on this topic on the labor market and the need to develop an innovative program that would complement the adequate educational offer that would further empower adult women on the topic gender equality in the labor market because long-term bad effects on the labor market have been expressed and statistically confirmed when it comes to pay, promotion, social and other issues. EU data emphasize that only 67% of women are employed while 78% of men are, women in the EU earn 16% less per hour than men on average, and their pensions are 31% less.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of the project is to increase the equality and labor competitiveness of unemployed women and women who are changing careers by providing them new knowledge and skills about gender equality in the labor market. The goal of the project significantly contributes to the Strategy for Gender Equality 2020.-2025., and the promotion of equality between women and men as a task of the European Union in all its activities. Almost 30 women from Croatia were involved in the project, and 23 women from Italy who, after completing the education, gained knowledge that they did not have before the education, which helped them to be more competitive on the labor market.

<< Implementation >>

The main project activities that contributed to the realization of the project goal are the development of an innovative program to increase knowledge and skills about gender (in)equality and the labor competitiveness of adult women on the labor market, education according to the newly developed innovative program, and the implementation of a series of activities for the purpose of spreading and promoting the results project.

<< Results >>

Project results: 1. we developed an innovative program to increase knowledge and skills about gender (in)equality and the labor competitiveness of adult women on the labor market; 2. we conducted training to increase the knowledge and skills of adult women about gender (in)equality and the labor competitiveness of adult women on the labor market (topics about: the European Union for gender equality, gender equality in the EU and in Croatia, labor laws, gender equality, discrimination, gender stereotypes, HUP's activities in the field of gender equality on the labor market, digitalization and Linkedin as the most important social network in the business world, gender-sensitive language and its use, ethical business, entrepreneurship in practice, public appearances, job interview and about what questions are inadmissible, CV, sexual discrimination in the workplace, mentoring as an important tool in the business world, also tropic about good practices in the field of gender equality within companies) attended by 25 women from Croatia and 23 women from Italy; 3. we organized round table: Dialogues on gender (in)equality in Italy and Croatia.

2022-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000084060.title: MenCare
2022-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000084060.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated to address the concrete needs of the participating organizations and their target groups. With over seven years of experience in the area of fatherhood education, we recognized challenges in recruiting fathers for long-term participation and the need for digital alternatives due to the pandemic. Additionally, the existing Program T methodology required updating to address the evolving social landscape and maximize impact.
To innovate and improve our practice, we aimed to develop new approaches and tools in fatherhood education. We sought to widen the network of fatherhood education experts by providing training and capacity-building opportunities for professionals and students in the updated methodology. 
Despite our increased capacities, we were able to reach only a limited number of fathers directly. To address this gap, the project developed targeted promotional and educational video materials to reach a wider audience of men, promoting the benefits of engaged fatherhood and fostering positive change in the community. Through these efforts, we aimed to create lasting impact and meaningful change in the lives of fathers and their families.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project we aimed to promote equitable parenthood as a key aspect of gender equality. Our goals included increasing the capacities of partner organizations for successful gender-transformative initiatives and strengthening the competencies of experts working with families and men to promote engaged fatherhood. We sought to develop more gender-equal attitudes and behaviors in parenting among men as well as enhance their parenting skills.
We wanted to upgrade and innovate our methodologies and activities with fathers to make them more relevant and impactful. We wanted to involve more professionals in the work with men on equal parenthood and train them with the skills and knowledge needed for successful gender-transformative interventions. Also, we aimed to reach a broader audience of fathers through educational and awareness-raising activities.
We strengthened our partnership with MÄN, sharing experiences and expertise. We improved our methodology and adapted a new approach, enhancing our capacities and those of professionals working with fathers, as well as fathers facilitating groups. We created innovative formats for fathers to learn and connect with other fathers, even in areas we could not physically reach.

<< Implementation >>

Programme Study Visit to our partner organization MÄN from Sweden
Facilitator Training in Sweden
Methodology Revision of Program T
Piloting Fathers' Groups 3 fathers groups organized
Training Sessions for Experts, 2 with professionals and one with fathers.
Educational Material for Fathers - 10 videos (3 promotional videos and 7 podcasts)

<< Results >>

- 1 3-day visit organized in the field of fatherhood work in Sweden for 10 participants from Croatia
- 1 2-day training on the topic of fathers' groups organized for 4 participants from Croatia
- Program T methodology reviewed and updated 
- Fathers' groups methodology (Small room) adapted for the Croatian context 
- 3 fathers' groups established in Zagreb and 1 fathers group in Osijek
- 25 fathers participated in fathers' groups 
- 3 3-day training sessions (Program T) organized for a total of 43 participants 
- 1 3-day training session (Small room) organized for 10 participants 
- 10 educational and awareness-raising videos produced 
- 558 955 people on the national television channel (HRT) and 516 310 people reached through social media
 
The project contributed to the capacities of partners for implementing effective gender-transformative educational activities with men with the goal of promoting equitable parenting. Professionals and fathers were directly trained for fatherhood work in our capacity-building activities and we reached hundreds of thousands of men with our online and offline educational and awareness-raising activities. Participants of all the activities gained new knowledge and developed new attitudes.

2022-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000084545.title: Education and Training of Deaf Sign Language Interpreters
2022-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000084545.summary:
<< Background >>

The 15 out of 10,000 European citizens are deaf people who use sign language. In Lithuania and Croatia sign language is recognized as mother tongue of the Deaf, which is an independent language with its own grammar. According to the UNCRPD, "Persons with disabilities shall be entitled, on an equal basis with others, to recognition and support of their specific cultural and linguistic identity, including sign languages and deaf culture." but also "Recognizing and promoting the use of sign languages." The activities implemented in this project are based on the UN CRPD and promote the rights of the Deaf. It is mandatory for the Deaf, sign language users, to have the access to sign language interpreter (SLI) so they are included in to the society. To have inclusive society, the Deaf have to have qualified and educated SLI which have to be part of lifelong learning process. It is common to have hearing SLI which is the bridge between deaf and hearing world. Together with hearing SLIs, there are Deaf SLIs that are bridge between Deaf and hearing SLIs. Deaf SLIs are needed in cases when the communication mode of a deaf person is so unique that it cannot be adequately accessed by hearing SLIs.

<< Objectives >>

Hrvatski savez gluhih i nagluhih (HSGN) and the Lietuvos kurciuju draugija (LKD) are the national Deaf associations in Croatia and Lithuania that gather more than 17000 deaf and hard of hearing persons. With this project we (HSGN and LKD) wanted to make positive impact both on our organizational scope (project and training management) but also on their educational scope (improving skills and knowledge and acquiring new ones). 

Also, it was meant to improve collaboration with institutions, sign language interpreters, entities that promote the rights of persons with disability and international partners.

The objectives achieved:
- Inclusion: deaf people have a more effective sign language interpreting system and service, as well as the same opportunities and rights both personally and professionally as hearing people, including the ability to act as sign language interpreters.
- Implemented accessible digital tools for the deaf community, such as educational modules in video format.
- Raised the quality of educational material for the training of deaf sign language interpreters.
- Reduced disparities between deaf and hearing sign language interpreters.
- Increased social and institutional awareness.

<< Implementation >>

The DeafSLI project directly addressed the needs and objectives identified by Croatian and Lithuanian Deaf associations, aligning these activities with the project's overall goals. These activities encompassed several key components:
- Comprehensive Training Module Development: A cornerstone of the project was the creation of a training module specifically designed for both deaf and hearing sign language interpreters. This module fostered collaboration and knowledge exchange between these two interpreter groups, drawing on their unique strengths and perspectives. 
- Targeted Training in Croatia and Lithuania: Following the development of the training module, the project facilitated its implementation in both Croatia and Lithuania.  
- Accessible Learning Resources in Video Format: Recognizing the visual learning preferences of the deaf community, the project undertook the significant task of converting the entire training module into video format.
- Dissemination and Sustainability: The project's impact wasn't limited to training sessions.  A dedicated project website and a comprehensive dissemination plan were developed to ensure widespread awareness of the project's resources and achievements.

<< Results >>

This strengthens interpreting teams, empowers deaf interpreters, & ultimately bridges communication between deaf & hearing communities. The DeafSLI project aimed to strengthen the capacities of sign language interpreting teams, both deaf and hearing, by providing information about teams with diverse backgrounds and experiences in interpreting. DeafSLI boosted collaboration and skills for deaf & hearing sign language interpreters.
- A training module & guide (now public) equipped participants & fostered knowledge exchange. Deaf & hearing interpreters collaborated on curriculum development.
- Training addressed specific roles & ethics for each interpreter type, leveraging strengths of both perspectives.
- Exercises facilitated discussions on interpreting & fostered a respectful, inclusive environment.
- All training modules were converted to video for the deaf community's visual learning preference. These public videos benefit both deaf & hearing interpreters, & serve as a resource for sign language programs.
- A project website & dissemination plan promote the project & its resources through social media, partner websites, & media channels.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-HU01-KA210-ADU-000081859.title: Portal Convention about Roleplaying in Adult Education
2022-1-HU01-KA210-ADU-000081859.summary:
<< Background >>

Parallel Worlds (HU), Terrible Creations (CRO) and Nausika (PL) came together to create the 11th edition of the Central Eastern European live-action role-play convention, PoRtaL in 2023. By taking on the organisation of the gathering of this large community, we aimed to give a specific focus to the convention and turn our attention towards the role and contributions of larp in the adult education sector. With this project, reaching beyond the convention itself and including several programme elements and tangible open-source results, we aimed to widen, develop, engage and strengthen the PoRtaL community by bringing them together on a more regular basis - through online platforms as well and to establish larp as a tool and methodology for adult education.

<< Objectives >>

#1 - CONVENTION
To create a high-quality educational event for the Portal community and experts of the adult education sector. To invite top-tier professionals and create a learning and networking possibility.
To develop a digital manual and a podcast on how to organise PoRtaL, combining the knowledge of previous organisers. To structure the know-how and methodology among current and future organisers.
To create visibility, engagement and participation in the community.

#2 - COOPERATION & MOBILITY
To share know-how and strengthen the cooperation of partner organisations applying larp as a tool of adult education.
To increase the mobility of game-designers implementing larp as an educational tool on a European level.
To create, run and share educational larp scenarios in all partner countries and beyond to increase access to high-quality training opportunities using larp as a method.

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT& ENGAGEMENT
To develop, engage and strengthen the community around roleplaying and education.
To establish a sustainable development of involved communities and demonstrate active citizenship.
To promote European values of personal freedom, solidarity, social responsibility and lifelong learning.

<< Implementation >>

Portal Organizer’ Workshops and Podcast - a series of workshops where organisers shared knowledge, discussing the challenges and opportunities of organising Portal events. These talks were recorded and edited into a podcast format so that we can share them with future Portal organisers.

Event Design Workshops - a series of sessions held with the help or external professionals to form the profile of PoRtaL 11. These workshops included ideations, planning and consultations as well as a team-building and training of volunteers of this year’s Portal.

Digital Presence & Social Media - our digital presence included partner organisations’ platforms (websites, newsletters, social media), the project website, facebook, instagram, youtube and spotify channel where we disseminated the project results and shared all relevant information.

Edu-Larp Scenario Writing Contest - an open contest resulting in well-designed educational larp scenarios played and disseminated in partnercountries and beyond.

Portal Convention - the 2023 edition of PoRtaL, the main meeting place of the Central Eastern European larping scene.

Dissemination Events - events where the contest winning larp scenarios could debut in all partner countries.

<< Results >>

Portal Talks Podcast - we created 9 (+2 being processed by the streaming platform) podcasts discussing the history of Portal and how to organise a convention
Lessons learned - a written document gathering experiences and learnings lon organising Portal from a personal point of view
Future of Portal or Portal 11 meets Portal 12 and 13 - a script and recording of the meeting between organisers of Portal 11 and future organisers of Portal 12 and 13 
Portal Lectures - freely available videos of the live streamed lectures from the Portal convention
Photos - a compilation of photos immortalizing the events of the Portal convention in 2023
3 contest winning larp scenario and their manuals in 4 languages (EN, HU, CRO, PL), freely available for all
An exhibition about the roots and history of Hungarian fantasy camps, an important predecessor of the Central Eastern European larp tradition and its catalogue both in Hungarian and English 
A three-day international convention focusing on the connection of larp and adult education
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-HU01-KA210-ADU-000084347.title: Orienteering for All - Improving high quality learning opportunities for volunteers of orienteering events
2022-1-HU01-KA210-ADU-000084347.summary:
<< Background >>

“Tájfutásért-Pécs” Alapítvány and Orijentacijski klub Varaždin are working on the field of orienteering for more than 25 years.The main objectives of these organizations are:improving the technical background of orienteering sport; supporting and organization of orienteering events; helping the awareness raising in connection with environmental protection and health-conscious behaviour
The operation of both partners is based entirely on the work of the volunteers.
In recent years, we have found that the knowledge of volunteers preparing and organizing orienteering events is beginning to wear off, and it is hard to keep up with changes in the sport such as new forms of disciplines and related rules and new technical solutions, like cartography software and the SI timing system, the spread of online and GPS-based solutions, etc. Therefore, the number of volunteers is decreasing and they cannot acquire up-to-date knowledge. The previously typical courses were missing and they are not efficient anymore. We also hoped that the actions carried out in international cooperation bring concrete, measurable knowledge expansion to our volunteers already after the pilot actions, thus facilitating the day-to-day operation of our organizations


<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project is to improve the number and the quality of volunteers participating in the preparation, organization and implementation of orienteering events, through the following objectives.
Firstly, we wanted to identify the training needs of volunteers, the available and missing training materials and teaching methods that can be used.
Secondly, we wanted to make optimal combinations of these needs-methods-materials-participants and test the theory through various pilot actions.
Finally, after the evaluation we wanted to share our findings with organizations working in the field of training volunteers for orienteering event organizers.


<< Implementation >>

The activities of the project were arranged in 5 work packages. 
WP1Management and coordination
WP2was about analyzing and identification of learning areas to be developed, and applicable methods. Mapping of available training materials, best practices and planning of the pilot actions. We made a survey and expert interviews to map the needs of the target group. We had a 2-days workshop in Mecsek in the beginning of the project. Based on these a team of experts in orienteering and in adult learning elaborated the “Map of learning areas”. We made an analysis of possible education methods and developed a methodological summary feasible for teaching/training volunteers. We also collected the available applicable Hungarian, Croatian and International training materials and guides. Based on this and further groupworks we elaborated a complex piloting plan.
In WP3 we conducted pilot actions for testing the methods identified in WP2. After the selection of the volunteers participants and the preparation of the necessary tools and equipment we organized various events
In WP4 we evaluated the results of the pilot actions and drafted recommendations for further education programs
WP5aim was the communication and dissemination of the results

<< Results >>

During the project we organized 15 events and tested 12 methods with the participation of more than 50 adult volunteers and 100 youth participants.
The concrete outputs of the project activities are:
The “map of learning areas” - This ’map’ shows us not only the roles and skills needed for the event-organizers but also the connections and the complexity of the work. Besides the variety and number of the separate fields it demonstrates us also the necessity of teamwork. 
Collected available training materials - We collected the Hungarian, Croatian and International training materials and guides useful for event controllers and volunteers as well. The learning materials are not always easy to find, especially in Croatian language, but more and more materials can be found on the Internet.
We also developed a methodology in which we explored the available training methods.
In the Training “Matrix” we collected which methods were tested in which event.
Finally, we made a summary and proposal about our findings.
As a concrete result of the project implementation our volunteers’ knowledge and motivation level elevated already after the pilot actions, in parallel the communication and cooperation in and among of our organizations.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-RO01-KA210-ADU-000082243.title: Enabling Urban Passenger Drivers to Provide an Integrated Service
2022-1-RO01-KA210-ADU-000082243.summary:
<< Background >>

We are a very new company on the market and now are trying to grow. We face some problems that are interfering with our development need. One of these problems that concerns us a lot is related to the drivers and being a major one we addressed it within this project. The problem is that our drivers that do not know how to communicate with the clients, they are beginners and nonprofessional drivers, unprepared when it comes to dealing with various types of contexts. These problems had impact also on the drivers - feeling isolated in their experience; they feel unlucky (e.g. when a passenger doesn’t pay for the ride), think that they are bad at the job (e.g. when unpleasant moments appear, passengers don’t tip or give bad ratings because the service was bad), or even affected by the numerous difficult scenarios they can be exposed to during a single day in a busy big city. These problems have also an impact on the TCD service quality in long term. Given the complexity and dimension of the problem, TCD do not have the resources to address it and Erasmus program is considered to be a solution. Moreover, the cooperation with the partner – experienced institute in training – had an impact on TCD capacity to develop projects. 

<< Objectives >>

We are a small company created 4 years ago. We provide ride-sharing transportation for passengers in urban areas, working with non-professional drivers as our employees. Very soon we realised that working in this field we faced a lot of challenges: legislation (not “friendly” for small enterprises), understanding passenger behaviour is vital, lack of teamwork skills of the non-professional drivers.
Based on the problem identified through the focus-groups in our organisation with drivers and with other companies acting in ride-sharing transportation for passengers in urban areas, we set as objectives:
1.	improving our drivers communication skills,
2.	increasing quality of our services and
3.	developing our cooperation capacity at European level through creation of a network of ride-sharing transportation companies.
In order to achieve these objectives, we proposed and implemented very concrete activities. Main activities reffered to analyse the complexity of the ride-sharing transportation phenomenon, training communication package for our drivers in digital format.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented 5 activities:
1.	Research - a study of the target group (quantitatively and qualitatively) through a set of questionnaires and in-depth interviews, was developed as the base for training and the digital guide content.
2.	Training - training materials based on partners’ expertise and research findings. Training sessions: Communication Skills 1, Communication Skills 2, Personal Branding, Self Defense, First Aid, Mental and Physical Health, Multicultural Differences and Diversity.
3.	Digital Guide - a website, accessible via mobile, desktop, and tablet, with comprehensive information, easy to read, and summary of all the knowledge produced in this project. 
4.	Visibility, Promotion, Dissemination – project's visual identity (logo and minimal branding), a basic website (to post project roadmap and updates) and profiles on main social media platforms (updates, news, etc): Facebook and Instagram. 
5.	Project management was implemented over the project period of 18 months through close cooperation between partners and also at the project management teams.
