2022-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000082623.title: New Sustainable Rural Tourism Learning Opportunities for Women in Border Areas
2022-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000082623.summary:
<< Background >>

Rural tourism provides valuable commercial and employment opportunities for people in rural areas that are confronted with the growing challenges. Without these opportunities, people may be forced to relocate to more populous areas, often resulting in separated families and economic leakage in the local community. Having in mind EU environment policies and the rural tourism, the aim of the project was to create a knowledge base for starting family projects, going towards sustainability. Rural tourism enables valorization of women’s work in rural households and creation of new jobs and their employment. Economic effects of female entrepreneurship which is created in rural tourism and activities relating to it are women’s securing of their economic empowerment. In order to give an impulse to the rural tourism development, empowering women through education was seen as the first and most important step. Since the Erasmus+ Program supports training assignments at adult education organizations, the opportunity for support of courses and training is recognized as a good chance to design an innovative training program focused on women from border area of three partner countries and on rural tourism.

<< Objectives >>

General objective of the project was to improve capacity of women living in border areas through creating high quality and easily accessible learning opportunities for sustainable rural tourism
Specific objectives were:
- To create high quality training methodology and digital platform for women living in border areas for sustainable rural tourism
- To educate pilot group of women from border areas of Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia for sustainable rural tourism
Project aimed to contribute to the priority “Improving the availability of high quality learning opportunities for adults”. 
In addition, Project contributed to the two more themes:
- Creating and promoting learning opportunities among all citizens and generations – since Project provided new
approach in education and support to women in border areas to improve their skills and knowledge for rural tourism
- Stimulating innovative learning and teaching practices – since Project provided modern way of support to women to switch from traditional agriculture-based households to more advanced – tourism-oriented approach which can create better possibilities to improve their incomes and quality of life in general.

<< Implementation >>

Main activities in the Project were:
1. Project Management (The project was managed by IPP with contribution from the partners from Croatia and Slovenia)
2. Initial press conference in Serbia (The conference was organized as a hybrid event – as an in-situ event for 11 representatives and on the internet with 17 participants on Zoom and with 172 people reached it on the FB live stream)
3. Initial partner meeting (3 day partner meeting in Serbia)
4. Development of training methodology and manuals for trainers (Training methodology was created in a form of an e-book with practical tests for trainees and presentations for trainers in 4 languages)
5. Creating a digital platform for rural tourism (platform is available in 4 languages on https://ruraltourism.ipp.rs)
6. Mid term partner meeting (3 day partner meeting in Croatia)
7. Training of trainers (11 trainers trained)
8. Presentations for tourism and BSO in Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia (3 presentations for total of 42 representatives of BSO present)
9. Pilot trainings in Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia (3 trainings with 39 participants)
10. Final partner meeting (3 day partner meeting in Slovenia)
11. Final press conferences in Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia

<< Results >>

The main project results are:
- Training methodology for training of women from border areas in rural tourism prepared and available online on on https://ruraltourism.ipp.rs in 4 languages (ENG, SLO, CRO, SRB)
- Training of trainers organized and 11 people from partner organizations trained to educate women from border areas for sustainable rural tourism
- 39 people trained for sustainable rural tourism through pilot trainings– 13 in Serbia, 15 in Croatia and
11 in Slovenia (30 of them was women)
- Digital platform for sustainable rural tourism created, available online in 4 languages (English, Serbian, Croatian and Slovene) and promoted: https://ruraltourism.ipp.rs
- 3 presentations for 42 representatives of organizations that support rural economy and tourism development organized
- 3 Facebook pages dedicated to dissemination of project results created in 3 languages (SRB, CRO, SLO)
- Several articles on project published in media

PROJECT „EURECA“ HAS BEEN IMAGINED AROUND THE IDEA OF HOW WE CAN IMPROVE COMMUNICATION OF CLIMATE CHANGE PROCESS AND ECOLOGICAL CRISIS LINKED TO IT BY GOING BEYOND SCIENTIFIC FACTS AND MAINSTREAM TECHNO-ECONOMIC SOLUTIONS. CLIMATE CHANGE IS ALSO AN EMOTIONAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL PROCESS AND THESE NEEDS HAVE TO BE ADRESSED AND SPOKEN ABOUT AS A PART OF HEALING PROCESS, BOTH FOR HUMANS AND FOR THE ENVIRONMENT

FROM THE PROCESS OF WORK WITH EXPERTS FROM DIFFERENT FIELDS DURING THE COURSE OF PROJECT, WE WANTED TO CREATE A GUIDE THAT WILL CAPTURE AND ADDRESS THE MYRIAD OF ELEMENTS NEEDED TO EXPAND THE AWARENNES OF A BIGGER PICTURE RELATED TO THE CLIMATE CHANGE PROCESS AND ECOLOGICAL CRISIS

2022-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000083718.title: Upoznaj toksičnost - živi bezbedno
2022-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000083718.summary:
<< Background >>

We live in the 21st century where a large number of chemicals that we use on a daily basis are synthesized through various products. In this way, we expose our bodies to a large number of compounds, many of which have been shown to be toxic in tests. Toxic substances also enter the body through inhalation of outdoor and indoor air as well as through water and food. To understand the hazards and risks associated with the widespread use of chemicals, it is important to know how and when they are toxic. The toxic potential of chemicals is studied in the scientific discipline of toxicology, which is not included in primary and secondary school curricula. There is a lack of understanding of toxicity among the general public, especially at a time when we are surrounded by information from various sources that is very often unreliable and inaccurate. As professors of toxicology and prominent scientists in the field, we believe that the general public needs reliable scientific information and the basics of toxicology in order to live safely with chemicals and achieve a high level of health and environmental protection.

<< Objectives >>

With the MeeTox project, we wanted to investigate how the population understands the concept of toxicity and whether toxic substances can be found in products that we use every day and that are considered safe. Are these facts worrying and where do people look for information about toxicity and the safe use of different products? Having identified the need for education, we created educational materials, presentations and videos, prepared texts and then developed an online course that adults can take to familiarize themselves with the basics of toxicology and understand the difference between potential toxicity and the risk of harm to health. The creation of the originally conceived booklet, which has evolved into a comprehensive publication, the MeeTox book “Meet the toxicity – live safely”, covering various topics, also provided an opportunity to introduce toxicology as a science to a lay audience. By acquiring toxicological knowledge, each individual is enabled to critically engage with, recognize, evaluate and effectively use information about toxicity. In this way, they can protect their health and preserve the environment through responsible behavior.

<< Implementation >>

Within the MeeTox project, Mee the toxicity, live safely, all twelve project activities were carried out: from the creation of a website and the establishment of a social network, the exchange of experiences between the Serbian and Croatian research teams, surveys among the population to understand the concept of toxicity, the creation of educational materials, the creation of presentations and video materials on specific topics, the creation and implementation of an online course and the production of the publication Meet the Toxicity - Live Safely. In addition, intensive activities to disseminate and utilise the project results were carried out during the project period and continued after the end of the project. The exploitation of the results will continue in the future. The MeeTox project and the expected results were discussed several times in guest appearances in the media. In the near future, the media will talk about the possibility of using the results of the MeeTox project and learning about toxicity from renowned experts and professors of toxicology so that we can live (with) chemicals safely.

<< Results >>

The concrete results of the MeeTox project are the creation of a questionnaire, obtaining ethical approval and surveying the population to understand toxicity. The need for education was identified by producing a report on the survey. The research conducted led to announcements at the leading scientific meetings on toxicology in Europe and the world. With the participation of more than 40 toxicologists from Serbia and Croatia, educational materials were produced to introduce toxicology to lay people. The teaching materials and the MeeTox book itself consist of three parts: The first part teaches the basics of toxicology education, what toxicology deals with and how it contributes to the preservation of health, as well as the contribution of regulation. In particular, it shows what information should be included on product labels and declarations so that we can use, store and dispose of them safely. It covers the main toxic chemicals, where we are exposed to them, what effects they can have and, most importantly, practical advice on how we can reduce our exposure. In particular, it looks at drug abuse, the harmful effects of smoking and the most common causes of poisoning in children, adults and animals.

2022-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000084279.title: Dostizanje kvalieta u nastavi znakovnih jezika
2022-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000084279.summary:
<< Background >>

Through this project, Gradska Organizacija Gluvih Beograda (Belgrade Deaf Organization) and Hrvatsko Društvo Prevoditelja Znakovnog Jezika (Croatian Association of Sign Language Interpreters) aimed to address the growing demand for a high-quality textbook to learn Serbian Sign Language (Srpski Znakovni Jezik or SZJ) and Croatian Sign Language (Hrvatski Znakovni Jezik or HZJ) at the beginner's level. This textbook was developed based on a meticulously designed curriculum, crafted in close collaboration and consultation with deaf users of SZJ and HZJ. By actively involving deaf individuals and a select group of experts in SZJ and HZJ, the project produced a pioneering textbook. The textbook provides an overview of the fundamental principles of SZJ and HZJ grammar, supplemented by a diverse range of video materials in both languages. These resources are intended to enhance the learning experience and facilitate the acquisition of SZJ and HZJ at the beginner's level.  

<< Objectives >>

Through the implementation of the project, the aim of GOGB and HDPZJ was to enhance the educational offerings of SZJ and HZJ by crafting tailored curricula for novices alongside a high-quality textbook. An additional focus was to integrate individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing into the teaching framework. Since 2022, GOGB has spearheaded nationally accredited programs dedicated to organizing SZJ courses ranging from A1 to B2 levels according to the CEFR standards. These courses are structured within Module 1, followed by Module 2, which caters to students aspiring to become proficient Serbian Sign Language interpreters. 
However, the endeavor to develop instructional materials for SZJ and HZJ encountered substantial challenges due to the scarcity of research and documentation surrounding these languages. Instead of drawing from a wealth of documented linguistic examples, the authors found themselves relying on the expertise of a select few sign language linguists and a cohort of fluent SZJ and HZJ deaf signers. This necessitated a meticulous process of selecting topics and grammar units for the textbook, with frequent revisions and verification stages.

<< Implementation >>

All the activities outlined in the project proposal were successfully executed. These activities include:

1.	Formation of the project team at the project's commencement, followed by the inaugural meeting of the team.
2.	Dissemination of information to the deaf communities in Serbia and Croatia regarding the project's significance and objectives, primarily through social media channels.
3.	Development of a curriculum tailored for beginners to learn Serbian Sign Language (SZJ) and Croatian Sign Language (HZJ).
4.	Convening the second project team meeting to deliberate on potential reviewers, designers, editors, proofreaders, and printing houses.
5.	Holding the third project team meeting in Zagreb, during which decisions were made regarding authors, reviewers, designers, editors, proofreaders, and printing houses.
6.	Creation of the beginner-level textbook for learning SZJ and HZJ.
7.	Printing and distribution of the textbook.
8.	Promotion of the textbook through a dedicated conference.
9.	Training sessions conducted for prospective deaf educators.


<< Results >>

The project has yielded the following concrete outputs: 1. A tailored curriculum designed for beginners to learn Serbian Sign Language (SZJ) and Croatian Sign Language (HZJ); 2. Beginner-level textbooks for learning SZJ and HZJ: a. Raičević Bajić, Dragana, Vera Jovanović, & Mihailo Gordić. 2024. Srpski znakovni jezik: Početni nivo. Beograd: Gradska Organizacija Gluvih Beograda. ISBN: 978-86-901655-5-1;  b. Kavčić, Dorijana, & Angel Naumovski. 2024. Udžbenik hrvatskoga znakovnog jezika. Zagreb: Hrvatsko Društvo Prevoditelja Znakovnog Jezika. ISBN: 978-953-50943-0-2; 3. Workshops for prospective deaf educators/teachers of SZJ and HZJ held at the Belgrade Deaf Organization in Belgrade from January 28, 2024, to 1st February 2024, and at Gradske knjižnice - Knjižnice grada Zagreba, Odjel za djecu i mladež, multimedijalna dvorana, Trg Ante Starčevića 4in Zagrebfrom 23rd January to 27th January 2024.;  4. The conference "Dostizanje Kvaliteta u Nastavi Znakovnih Jezika" (Achieving Quality in Sign Language Teaching) held on January 31 in Belgrade, with representatives from the Ministry of Labour, Employment, Veteran, and Social Policy, as well as teachers from the School for Deaf and Hard of Hearing Children "Stefan Dečanski."

2022-1-SE01-KA210-ADU-000084791.title: Sociopsychodrama: The Languages of Peace
2022-1-SE01-KA210-ADU-000084791.summary:
<< Background >>

Context behind us applying was that the COVID-19 world pandemic illustrated well enough just how mental health is relevant and integrated into each aspect of our body, mind and society and how much is it important for people to be in groups even when they cannot be. 
During long periods of lockdown in several countries, including the countries relevant for this project action, we have seen how human capacity for resilience and overcoming uncomfortable situations are important when a person is locked down in small spaces and faced with conflicts. The increase of violent conflicts within families and societies are telling us that we need to invest more in education on mental health care for professionals, and for the general population as well. Countries all over the world, including the countries of our origin, still rather heavily invest in militarisation than in education, health and social services. In general, mental health care is still focused rather on an individualistic approach and challenged by the need to integrate the body and mind in treating it all at once. However, the recent pandemic and recent war in Europe has shown us that we need to include the Social in the concept of mental health. 

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to help professionals who work in the field of mental health, social work, education, public policies and research to advance and develop these competencies which can help them to bring new effective strategies and practices into their work in order to make these processes more efficient for their clients, learners or communities they work with.
In the globalized world where polarization is increasing, while democracies are threatened, and the war and the climatic changes oblige many human beings to migrate and to become refugee, in addition with the unfair distribution of resources and the growing of poverty, there is a need to face these challenges which affect all social levels from the planet level to the country and community level, the family and individual level. Sociopsychodrama as a method learns people who work with groups how to deal with all these issues and therefore is important to be available as a training to as many professionals who work with groups as possible.
The main objective of this project was to contribute to the efforts of transforming conflicted communities and societies,healing traumas and building long term peace by increasing the competencies of the professionals, practitioners and trainers

<< Implementation >>

We had 3 webinars where each webinars consisted of 4 zoom sessions, so it was in total 12 zoom sessions.
Also, we had 5 days of Spring school where participants met at the University of Zadar and were able to learn in presence and exchange knowledge with more experienced professionals from the field of Sociopsychodrama. Also, we had 2 follow up meetings on zoom in order to evaluate the whole process of webinars and spring school and to be able to reflect about curricula development.
The program of webinars, spring school and curriculum is uploaded where the project results are https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/projects

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results which were planned inside the project are:
- successfully done 3 Webinars and Spring school in Zadar
- written and printed and published The Handbook of Sociopsychodrama
- published and uploaded to many platforms electronic version of the Handbook of Sociopsychodrama
- written curriculum
- learned 32 professionals basics of sociopsychodrama and how to use it working with vulnerable, marginalized and discriminated groups
Results that were not planned (overachieved results):
- we created a website for the project https://discoveringlanguagesofpeace.weebly.com/
- published as electronic e book "Collection of group stories made by participants" (uploaded on project platform)
- published "Collection of group stories made by participants"  as appendix to electronic version of the handbook
- Dissemination of project and handbook in the sociopsychodrama conference held in
Sweden in Stockholm from 16.8.-19.8. where Jana Damjanov had a lecture about it.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2022-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000082118.title: Spodbujanje razvoja kognitivnih sposobnosti starejših s pomočjo art terapije - fraktalne risbe
2022-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000082118.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project because we are familiar with the field of elderly care and the growing issue of dementia among older adults, which poses a significant challenge for society. In the project, we addressed the need for the inclusion and empowerment of older adults, which will improve their cognitive development; this, in turn, leads to the prevention of dementia, its delay, or slower progression. In doing so, we focused primarily on older adults from communities with fewer opportunities (rural environments).

<< Objectives >>

With this project, we aimed to achieve greater inclusion and empowerment of the elderly, while also aiming for positive effects on the cognitive development of older adults. Consequently, we aimed to reduce the risk of dementia. We also sought to increase the competence of organizations and staff working with the elderly. Additionally, we wanted to inform and motivate the public to implement and engage in alternative approaches when working with older adults (such as art therapy with fractal drawings).

<< Implementation >>

We conducted the following activities:
- Organized workshops for older adults in Slovenia and Croatia;
- Provided training for new mentors in Croatia and Slovenia;
- Prepared and published the handbook "Skillful Hands, Active Minds" in both Slovenian and Croatian;
- Conducted an evaluation, which resulted in a study, with findings published in a professional journal and presented at two international conferences;
- Held 4 exhibitions of fractal drawings from participants involved in Slovenia and Croatia. The last two exhibitions included closing events. In Slovenia, this was a larger event, which was also filmed, with the video published on YouTube;
- Coordinated the project to ensure its successful completion;
- Promoted the project by continuously informing the professional and general public about its progress, participation, and results. We continue to do this today, even though the project has already concluded.

<< Results >>

Specific results:
- 130 participants were involved. 117 completed the entire workshop cycle, and they assessed their condition in the final evaluation. Using a paired t-test, we compared their condition before and after participating in the activities and found that, on average, participants' health improved, as did key aspects across all three measured areas (cognitive, emotional, and concentration/attention).
- 8 new mentors who are already independently leading activities.
- Published handbook in both Slovenian and Croatian.
- 4 exhibitions of fractal drawings from the participants (over 100 people attended just one of the exhibitions in Brežice).
- Numerous posts on social media.
- Several articles published in local newspapers.
- A radio broadcast on the national Radio Prvi station.
- Two international conferences where we presented the project results ...

- Two scientific papers are still awaiting publication.
- Ireland and Turkey have expressed interest in adopting the program for their elderly populations.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000084787.title: Digitalno pri odraslih, Digitalno? Nič bat.
2022-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000084787.summary:
<< Background >>

During Covid-19, all public institutions closed and every business moved to the Internet. We found that the older population is not skilled at handling digital devices (smartphone, tablet, computer), and especially newly created applications (zVEM, eUprava, e-Građani). We discussed the problem of educating social care workers, who provide care for the elderly in institutions and those who provide home care, on how and in what way to educate the elderly on using online applications. We discussed the elderly’s actual needs, which we found out using survey questionnaires.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of our project was to educate social care workers, empower our target group and introduce them to modern digital technologies in a pleasant way, by training and offering basic assistance to the target group with the aim of helping them find their way in the modern world. These are mainly older people who are not the most technologically proficient and are the most exposed to social exclusion.

<< Implementation >>

For the project, we carried out the following activities: prepared a program for developing basic digital competences of the target group and a program for informing them about the project; provided a multilingual approach; implemented a pilot program of informing, developing digital competences and empowering the target group; evaluated the pilot program by measuring the impact of the program on users and introducing improvements; implemented a program to ensure social inclusion and maintain the already developed social skills of the target group.

<< Results >>

As part of the project, we made multilingual survey and evaluation questionnaires.
We prepared 6 educational materials in Slovenian, Croatian and Hungarian, which helped us in educating adults in digital skills. We prepared learning materials for the basic use of Facebook, Viber, Youtube, eUprava, zVEM and e-Građani. 
With the help of these educational materials, we educated our target group, i.e., elderly people over 60 years of age. On the Croatian side, these were residents of the retirement home Dom Svete Ane, and on the Slovenian side, users of services that provide living assistance at home, and a few others who do not use those services, but wished to participate. 
We held joint workshops and conducted individual and group trainings for the target group.

2022-2-BE01-KA210-ADU-000099383.title: I Share my Knowledge and Have an Active iMPACT on my Community
2022-2-BE01-KA210-ADU-000099383.summary:
<< Background >>

Our project aimed to empower women in caregiving roles to find practical solutions to daily environmental challenges they face. Despite initiatives like the European Green Deal and UN recognition of women's role in sustainable development, gender disparities persist. Women are underrepresented in environmental decision-making and are disproportionately affected by energy poverty. Our goal was to increase mothers' involvement in promoting activism, communication, and community engagement on energy, climate, and sustainability issues. We wanted to provide the knowledge to empower them to become active agents of environmental change, creating a healthier environment for their families and communities.

<< Objectives >>

Our aim was to discover innovative ways to engage and participate in addressing the environmental crisis. We established three goals for our project. Firstly, we wanted to help our organizations understand and address the environmental crisis caused by human behavior. Secondly, we aimed to improve the skills of our trainers and mentors when working with adult women. Thirdly, we wanted to empower mothers to take action, ask questions, debate, and proactively build a healthier and more sustainable relationship with the environment. Our ultimate goal was to encourage women to proactively initiate change by inspiring their families and communities to engage in more environmentally friendly behavior. 
Considering the profile and interests of our trainers, we were enthusiastic about exploring themes related to climate change by promoting active citizenship and civic engagement on environmental issues, building closer understanding of EU actions on environmental protection, and encouraging alternative forms of participation through artistic expression.


<< Implementation >>

We completed all 5 activities as planned, namely: A1. Training-for-trainers & exchange of expertise on environmental protection, sustainable development and community activism: a training by guest lecturers and expertise exchange among the project team members. - A2. A summer retreat for women: Moms for the environment. A 7-day retreat for 10 women (5 from each country) in Šibenik, Croatia. 4 trainers (2 from each partner institution) also participated & delivered training. The participating mothers created Guidelines for understanding environmental protection and economic sustainability. - A3. Multiplier events. 4 in total took place: 2 events for families, young people and all interested in climate issues (one in BE & HR each); an additional presentation for university students (BE) and a joint consortium participation at the HOPE 2023 fair in Brussels to present the projects’ outputs. - A4. Transnational project team meetings: 2 meetings of the 4-person project team took place, as planned. - A5. Project Management & Administration: The project team executed planned activities, monitored progress, and reported regularly to stakeholders. Follow-up ensured completion of deliverables and identified areas for improvement.

<< Results >>

The following results and outputs, set out in our project proposal, were planned and delivered: (i) 4 of our female trainers and mentors received training and participated in an exchange of expertise on building the knowledge and skills needed to educate adult learners about environmental protection and to trigger community activism; (ii) 10 women/mothers, participated in a 7-day summer retreat and learned about environmental protection and sustainable development, thus deepening their leadership and advocacy skills; (iii) Guidelines for Understanding Environmental Protection and Economic Sustainability were written, published and disseminated online, particularly to the Erasmus+ community and on a dedicated project website. (iv) Fellow mothers and young people, in numbers more significant than planned, participated in multiplier activities and learned about sustainable living. (v) The capacities of our two institutions to provide adult education in the area of environmental protection were significantly enhanced and will be utilised in future projects.

2022-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000098281.title: STEP FORWARD
2022-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000098281.summary:
<< Background >>

The project STEP FOWARD was developed based on the need of modernizing the education process.In the digital age, embracing digital transformation is a matter of becoming more competitive, and in some cases, even a matter of survival in business and education. The main goal of the project was to offer support to adult educators in using digital technologies in adult education by developing digital pedagogy and providing guidance in form of guidebooks and workshops on how to use digital tools in their teaching and upskill their knowledge.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project we wanted to improve teaching skills in different on-line mode of learning, introduce educators to current educational trends and implementation possibilities, provide practical ideas on how to use technology to enhance their current tasks and work plans, enhance their motivation for using technology in the classroom, encourage them to create their own digital teaching materials by implementing good andragogical practices and strategies into digital learning and finally to increase their competences and confidence in selecting appropriate ICT tools for andragogic and didactic purposes. Also we wanted our educators to broaden their horizon by connecting with colleagues from other countries by participating in project and creating new connections and network support.

<< Implementation >>

- DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION GUIDEBOOK - a complete, up-to-date written guide following the latest trends in digital education translated and adapted into 4 languages available in PDF
- DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION WORKSHOPS - 5 one-day workshops in all partner countries with complimentary Moodle Classroom designed to follow the workshop scenarios and test the skills in the digital classrooms, and try out different activities using ICT as well as self-evaluation of the participants for total of 77 participants 
- DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION ONLINE FESTIVAL OF KNOWLEDGE - was organised online in each partner country to present the project and its results and provide expert talk through 3 podcast episode up to an hour where in total 5 experts were engaged in talking about latest trends in digital transformation with 213 participants in total
- MICRO LEARNING CARDS FOR EDUCATORS were created for educators learning to promote digital transformation in all educational institutions - cards are available online in Moodle classroom and are designed as memory cards. 
- 4 face-to-face partners meetings and more than 20 on-line meetings during the project

<< Results >>

One digital transformation guidebook translated in 4 languages and available in PDF format. Five Digital transformations workshops held in all participating countries. Organised digital festivals of knowledge in all participating countries, each partner organized one festival with different subjects - three festivals in total, with professionally filmed podcasts for wider engagement. Micro-learning Cards available in Moodle classroom. In addition, partners from Serbia wrote scientific articles scheduled for publication later in 2025.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000100770.title: Learning Together: know-how exchange of incubators to better support adult learners
2022-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000100770.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the "Learning together" project to address the need for enhanced support for adult learners, particularly those interested in entrepreneurial and innovative activities. The project aimed to fill gaps in the provision of lifelong learning opportunities focused on entrepreneurship, social innovation, and crowdfunding. Firstly, we wanted to increase the skills of partner organisations’ staff - Brodoto in providing support in social entrepreneurship, and SBHS in providing support in crowdfunding - both in our existing programmes. The target groups included adults from rural areas, those with fewer opportunities, and individuals seeking to develop skills in social or green impact projects. We identified a lack of tailored support for these groups and aimed to provide specific training and capacity building to help them succeed in their ventures.


<< Objectives >>

Objectives were to:
-Permanently adopt skills/knowledge acquired via project implementation in future learning / incubation programmes
-Involve and train at least 3-3 members of both organisations in peer-to-peer sessions
-Enrich own support programmes&test in pilot workshops
-Implement 4 peer-to-peer learning sessions for staff
-Involve and raise capacities of at least 5-5 entrepreneurial adult learners from Croatia and Austria in the pilot workshops
-Gain new skills & knowledge from activity #1 and by participating in new workshop in partner countries
-Publish open calls for participation for target groups in Austria and Croatia (2). The point of open calls is to advertise the
news about the incubation programs, so that as many people in partners' areas find out about it.
-Implement 4 pilot workshops for innovative adult learners in Croatia
-Implement 4 pilot workshops for innovative adult learners in Austria
-Involve at least 10 adult learners in pilot workshops (at least 5 per country)
-produce at least 4 podcasts


<< Implementation >>

In Activity 1, peer-to-peer learning sessions were held between partners to exchange expertise in crowdfunding and social innovation. Each partner brought unique knowledge to enhance adult learning programs for adults with innovative ideas. Sessions were organised: two live (in Zagreb and in Graz) and each partner implemented 4 of each online, with continuous online communication and mentoring. 10 sessions in total.

In Activity 2, both countries ran pilot workshops simultaneously. Through established communication channels (social media, newsletters, mailing lists) the participation was promoted as open calls. The project included a Crowdfunding Academy in Croatia and an SBHS incubation programme in Austria. In Graz, SBCS/SBHS conducted 5 workshops, including one on crowdfunding with Brodoto support. In Zagreb, Brodoto held 4 workshops, including one on social business development with SBHS support. 

In activity 3, partners recorded podcasts with an aim to promote the project results, promote social entrepreneurship and alternative financing methods. 


<< Results >>

In Activity 1, concrete outputs were the implementation of the 10 peer-learning sessions and related 6 assignments completed that resulted in increased knowledge of the staff of the project partner organisation. The skills and knowledge developed during the peer-learning sessions were on the topic of executing a crowdfunding workshop for SBCS/SBHS and on how to hold a social innovation workshop for Brodoto.

In Activity 2, concrete outputs were the 9 pilot workshops (4 in Croatia and 5 in Austria) organised for 23 innovative adults (9 in Austria and 14 in Croatia). The pilot workshop resulted in an increased knowledge of innovative adults in three main topics: (1) crowdfunding, (2) social innovation (impact analysis) and (3) entrepreneurship (legal aspects, recruiting employees/finding co-founders, finding investors).

Activity 3, one podcast was jointly made in English. 3 additional were recorded in German, and 2 in Croatian - 6 in total. First podcast had two guests (+the project team), while the native speaking podcast had one guest. They are online on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, Google Podcasts.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000101863.title: Green up!
2022-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000101863.summary:
<< Background >>

We applyed for this project to exchange various green sustainable skills that will develop human resources within partner
organisations, develop key competences of their staff, start new non-formal educational activities and entrepreneurship
initiatives, and promote social inclusion of marginalised groups. By investing in team capacity building and acquiring new knowledge, we can enhance our problem-solving abilities, boost innovation, improve collaboration, and increase overall productivity. Additionally, continuous learning helps our team to stay updated with the latest trends and best practices, thereby enabling us to adapt to changing work environments effectively.
Another reason is to build a global network of partners and professional contacts that we can share in the future.
Our needs were empowerment of our skills,  inclusive participation: ensure that the project is accessible to people of all backgrounds, including marginalized and disadvantaged communities, capacity building, raise awareness about the importance of sustainability and permaculture.
Cultural exchange with different country provided us firsthand experience of a new culture, language, and new skills and metods how to adress to a problem.


<< Objectives >>

1. Implementation of new knowledge and skills in the field of sustainable development and permaculture, with the aim of
empowering persons engaged in education, especially for marginalized social groups.
This was achieved through a 5-day trainings, organized by each of the partners involved in the project with a user group
that includes marginalized social groups with whom it is even more challenging to conduct educational activities (eg
homeless, people with intellectual disabilities and adults).
The second level of positive change refers to the:
2. Empowerment of users through the exchange of knowledge and skills and the creation of a future common platform for

organizations after the completion of project activities.

2022-2-SI01-KA210-ADU-000101303.title: OPOLNOMOČENJE OVIRANIH ZA AKTIVNOSTI V NARAVI
2022-2-SI01-KA210-ADU-000101303.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to empower people with disabilities (especially users of UVID, learners in COOKT and LURS, and individuals with disabilities in the broader community) + to create sustainable activities for them (which we would integrate into our regular operations), bringing added and lasting value. Simultaneously, we aimed to educate and develop new competencies among staff caring for disabled.

We focused on the following needs, aligned with the priority areas of Erasmus+ (inclusion and diversity, environment and combating climate change), which we identified among people with disabilities during our operations:

Lack of physical activity (according to WHO data, the disabled population is the least physically active but disproportionately prone to chronic illnesses that physical activity prevents)
Insufficient time spent actively in nature (physical activity in nature is particularly beneficial; besides the advantages of physical activity, being in nature provides fresh air and close contact with nature, which is fundamental for fostering an appropriate relationship with the environment and a more sustainable way of life)
Inadequate provision of techniques for maintaining/enhancing mental health
Need for greater sensory integration

<< Objectives >>

Our primary goals were twofold:
1. Empowering adults with disabilities (mental and/or physical) to engage more fully in outdoor activities, utilizing all senses, while simultaneously promoting a sustainable mindset.
2. Acquiring new competencies for staff working with individuals with disabilities, enabling them to further empower people with disabilities.

To achieve this, we aimed to:
- Facilitate the inclusion of individuals with disabilities in outdoor activities, particularly cycling and therapeutic horseback riding, by removing barriers preventing their participation.
- Foster a heightened sense of environmental care among individuals with disabilities.
- Develop sustainable activities to enhance sensory integration in nature, utilizing natural materials.
- Combat the stigma that "people with disabilities don't engage in physical activity."
- Expand inclusive sports activities and promote equality for all.
- Improve the physical and mental health of individuals with disabilities and staff.
- Enhance the capacity of smaller partners for international cooperation and development.
- Incorporate new sustainable activities into the regular operations of project organizations: inclusive cycling and outdoor sensory integration.

<< Implementation >>

Activities for staff working with individuals with disabilities:

Staff education on caring for the health of individuals with disabilities (lectures/workshops on the importance of sports for physical and mental well-being of individuals with disabilities, adaptations of sports activities for them, first aid, hippotherapy, basic psychological support, and motivation).
Practical training for companions in safe and enjoyable cycling for people with disabilities.
Staff education on inclusive nature care.
Training on mental health care for individuals with disabilities (mindfulness techniques, meditation, sensory integration).
Organized outdoor gatherings with nature conservation education and sensory integration.
Presentation of creative works as sensory use best practices.
Activities for individuals with disabilities:

Physical health care (motivation workshops, first aid, proper movement, hippotherapy).
Cycling on adapted bikes.
Practical education on inclusive nature care.
Workshops on maintaining and enhancing mental health.
Workshops activating all senses in a sensory park.
Outdoor activities in nature for individuals with disabilities - hiking, Nordic walking, and therapeutic riding.

Other: dissemination, project management.

<< Results >>

- New knowledge for staff at the UVID and COOKT, disability organizations, VDC, and relatives of disabled (importance of physical activity for physical/mental health, practical adaptations of sports activities for disabilities, first aid, psychological support, mindfulness, meditation, sensory integration, nature conservation).
- Improvement of personal assistants' competencies at the UVID and introduction of new knowledge into their training program.
- Enhancement of teachers' competencies and introduction of new knowledge into the regular COOKT program.
- Acquisition of new knowledge for individuals with disabilities (importance of physical activity for mental/physical health, basics of first aid and self-help, adapted cycling, therapeutic horseback riding, nature conservation, mindfulness, meditation, sensory integration, activation of all senses, outdoor sports activities...).
- 2 adapted bicycles for individuals with disabilities (simple tricycle and high-quality tricycle with electric support).
- Regular program of inclusive cycling.
- Establishment of a sensory park in Krapinske Toplice (mobile sensory path, communication board).
- Increased care for nature in target groups and partner organizations.

2022-2-SK01-KA210-ADU-000094883.title: Vzdelávanie o kultúrnom dedičstve Slovákov
2022-2-SK01-KA210-ADU-000094883.summary:
<< Background >>

Many people, both older and younger generations, do not have much knowledge about the traditions, folklore, architecture and historical events that unite Slovaks and Croatians. The main motivation for submitting the project was to raise awareness of the target groups, improve their quality of life with an emphasis on adult education - the cultural heritage of Slovaks. Given that Aktív-Relax has been organizing joint informal meetings with a partner organization in Croatia for more than 6 years, it wanted to establish and develop formal cooperation focused on education focused on the cultural heritage of individual mobilities of partner organizations. As a new applicant in the program, we saw an opportunity to develop mutual cooperation, the subsequent process of educational activities in the field of civic engagement, cultural and community life of citizens, as well as environmental protection. Education in this area helped participants understand that cultural heritage is the basis of the identity of every nation, to realize the values ​​of cultural heritage, which strengthens pride in one's own culture and its dissemination abroad. By creating a space for cross-border connections, there was transfer of knowledge and experiences.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal during the two-year project was to get to know the cultural heritage of Slovaks and Croatians. Strengthening common values, civic engagement of selected target groups from among adults and seniors from both Croatia and Slovakia. Building and expanding mutual cooperation between the participating organizations. Part of this goal was the mutual exchange of experiences of organizations, learning about traditions, establishing and maintaining cultural, social, international contacts with an emphasis on supporting active European citizenship and transferring the European dimension to the local level with the subsequent development of communities in the Dolný Kubín region in Slovakia and in the Selca Municipality in Croatia. The goal was closely linked to the selected priorities such as common values, civic engagement and active citizenship, improving the availability of educational opportunities for adults, activities focused on inclusion and diversity, the environment, development of key competences and creativity of target groups with a lack of opportunities.

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the project, we held a joint meeting in the city of Dolný Kubín and in order to plan the activities resulting from the project, such as presentations of partners and their activities, presentation of the project, division of tasks and designation of responsible persons, creation of a time schedule, specification of mutual expectations, discussion of the needs of the involved target groups. During the mobilities, educational activities were focused on gaining knowledge about cultural monuments and cultural heritage of Slovaks, visits to partner organizations and local institutions, observation of their activities, meetings of community members in the educational program about the cultural heritage of Slovaks and Croatians, active European citizenship - volunteering at all ages and examples of good practice in environmental protection on the island of Brač. The result of the activities was the creation of a Slovak-Croatian phraseological dictionary, presentations of Slovak and Croatian cuisine, music and literature. The project implemented activities focused on inclusion, creating interpersonal relationships, and social activities focused on developing key adult competencies needed for the 21st century.

<< Results >>

The specific outputs of the project were 4 joint meetings aimed at raising awareness of cultural heritage, creating interpersonal relationships between the people involved. The outputs of the program for individual mobilities were planned through communication channels via - MS Teams and WhatsApp. The educational outputs were getting to know natural and cultural monuments by completing excursions in Kukučín's House, Orava Castle - the history of the Turz and Draškovič families, the town of Selce - the place of work of M. Kukučín, visits to partner organizations and local institutions, interest groups and volunteer groups. Other outputs were aimed at getting to know partner organizations with local institutions, interest groups and volunteer groups. The joint output was the creation of a phraseological dictionary, recipes for Slovak and Croatian cuisine, an introduction to active citizenship, examples of good practice in the field of volunteering and the environment. Joint quizzes and workshops were positive results of the project. The final meeting took the form of a video conference, with content focused on the presentation of activities, feedback from participants, and a recap of acquired knowledge and skills.

2023-1-DE02-KA210-ADU-000157649.title: Fighting Fake News and Enhancing Critical Thinking Skills for Business Opportunities of Unemployed Citizens
2023-1-DE02-KA210-ADU-000157649.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated to tackle the increasing influence of fake news on business decision-making, particularly among unemployed citizens and small business owners with limited digital skills. The spread of misinformation on social media had led to poor financial and business choices, highlighting the urgent need for media literacy and critical thinking education. Many adults lacked the ability to verify information sources, making them vulnerable to manipulation.

By applying for this project, the partners aimed to empower individuals with the necessary skills to critically assess news, enhance their digital resilience, and make informed decisions. The project also sought to support organizations working in adult education by developing innovative non-formal training programs and digital tools. Strengthening cooperation among organizations in Germany, Croatia, and Portugal was a key objective, ensuring the exchange of best practices and the creation of sustainable learning opportunities. The project contributed to the European goal of improving digital literacy and combating misinformation​.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to enhance critical thinking and media literacy skills among unemployed citizens and small business owners, helping them make informed business decisions in the face of widespread fake news. A key objective was to:
1. Strengthening International Collaboration – Establish a network of organizations in Germany, Croatia, and Portugal to share best practices and enhance cooperation in adult education.
2. Developing Non-Formal Education Program– Create training program to improve critical thinking and media literacy, helping unemployed citizens and small business owners recognize and counter fake news.
3. Empowering Organizations – Support less experienced organizations inside and outside partnership consortium in understanding the impact of fake news on business and equipping them to provide better training and resources.
4. Creating a Digital Educational Platform – Develop an online tool to provide accessible, high-quality training materials and improve digital skills among adult learners and educators.
By empowering educators and individuals with new skills and resources, the project wanted to contributed to a more informed society capable of recognizing and mitigating the impact of fake news.

<< Implementation >>

The project included key activities to enhance media literacy and critical thinking among unemployed citizens and small business owners. It began with a kick-off meeting in Berlin, where partners set objectives, planned strategies, and established cooperation.

A research study in Germany, Portugal, and Croatia analyzed the impact of fake news on business decisions, involving 124 respondents. Each country identified potential beneficiaries, mapping 55 institutions for targeted outreach​.

Based on the findings, partners developed the "Coherent Minds" education program, designed to train adults in detecting and combating fake news. A training session in Croatia tested the program with 17 educators​.

To expand access, an online education platform was created, featuring a digital handbook, e-learning courses, and interactive quizzes​. Transnational meetings in Portugal and Croatia ensured collaboration, while an online multiplier event with 36 participants shared best practices.

Local multiplier events reached 27 participants in Croatia, 25 in Germany, and 10 in Portugal, expanding awareness and engagement. The project successfully built a network of adult education organizations, fostering long-term cooperation in adult education.

<< Results >>

The project achieved significant results in enhancing media literacy and critical thinking among unemployed citizens and small business owners.

A research study with 124 respondents across Germany, Portugal, and Croatia led to three national reports on how misinformation affects business decisions​. Based on these findings, partners developed the "Coherent Minds" non-formal education program, tested in Croatia with 17 trainers​.

A digital education platform was created, offering an e-learning course, digital handbook, and quizzes to make training widely accessible​. Additionally, potential beneficiary mapping identified 55 institutions, ensuring targeted outreach and collaboration.

To maximize impact, the project held an international online multiplier event with 36 participants and three national events: 27 participants in Croatia, 25 in Germany, and 10 in Portugal. These events strengthened awareness and dissemination​.

The project successfully built a transnational network of adult education organizations with 55 contacts, fostering long-term cooperation, shared knowledge and experience between project partners and equipping communities with tools to combat fake news.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2023-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000154504.title: Empleo Protegido en Europa
2023-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000154504.summary:
<< Background >>

After many years working in the field of employment guidance for people with disabilities, we have detected that the special employment centres, which is the model of protected employment in the case of Spain, carry out the largest number of hirings of people with disabilities compared to ordinary companies. For us, true inclusion is that which is carried out under equal conditions to the rest of the workers. From this arose the need to know the other models of sheltered employment in Europe, to make a comparative table in which to analyse the similarities and differences, as well as to take testimony from people with disabilities who currently develop their professional activity in sheltered employment. Always seeking to improve the working conditions of the group, we consider it important to initiate the process of creating a new model of sheltered employment under a quality framework that allows them access to employment, where their needs are respected without diminishing their labour rights (salary, leave, adaptations, etc.). Therefore, with this project we address the inclusion of people with disabilities in decent working conditions.

<< Objectives >>

With this project we wanted to develop a European quality framework that would unify the model of sheltered employment in all the countries that make up the European Union, bringing together the positive aspects of each of the employment policies that are currently being applied, and improving those aspects that are not working well.
The general objective was:
- To produce a report highlighting the needs and proposals for the creation of a European quality framework for sheltered employment in Europe.
The specific objectives were:
-To get to know the situation of sheltered employment in the countries of the project consortium.
-To share experiences and good practices among the partner countries.
-To develop tools to measure the effectiveness of the different models of sheltered employment.
- To raise awareness and promote the improvement of employment conditions for people with disabilities.
-To describe the most appropriate sheltered employment models according to the type of disability.
-To seek the involvement and collaboration of the Public Administrations and the business fabric in the quality insertion of people with disabilities.
The priority of this project is the Inclusion of people with disabilities in equality.

<< Implementation >>

In the development of the project we have carried out all the activities proposed at the beginning of the project.
1. A registration form was designed, in which all the partners participated, in order to collect the information we wanted to analyse, and once this information had been collected, we drew up a comparative table of the different models of sheltered employment in Europe.
2. We carried out a satisfaction survey of workers with disabilities, using a Google form questionnaire, and analysed the results obtained. 
3. We have elaborated the report, where we propose a new model of sheltered employment from a new paradigm based on the social economy. 
4. The multiplier event was held on 19 June 2024 in the three partner countries of this project, where we presented the data obtained during the research phase and presented the new model of sheltered employment.
5. Finally, all the planned transnational meetings (Croatia, Spain and Romania) were held, where we had the opportunity to share experiences, create synergies and get closer to the culture of each country.

<< Results >>

The results that we have shared on the Erasmus+ results platform, and on the EPALE platform, has been a single document that unifies the three expected results. This document consists of a first part in which the new model of sheltered employment is presented and in which the following sections can be found: 
1. INTRODUCTION
2. THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK
3. SHELTERED EMPLOYMENT IN EUROPE. DATA OBTAINED FROM THE RESEARCH CARRIED OUT WITHIN THIS PROJECT.
4. RESULTS OF THE SATISFACTION SURVEY CARRIED OUT ON PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES CURRENTLY WORKING IN SHELTERED EMPLOYMENT.
5. PROPOSAL OF THE NEW MODEL OF SHELTERED EMPLOYMENT.
NEW PARADIGM OF SHELTERED EMPLOYMENT FROM THE SOCIAL ECONOMY.
6. BIOGRAPHICAL REFERENCES
Next, we have attached a comparative table of the different models of sheltered employment in Europe, where all the data collected and their detailed analysis are shown.
Finally, we have added a second annex with the graphs of the results of the satisfaction surveys in the three countries and an analysis of these data.
We have considered that unifying all the results in a single document is much more practical for those who access the Report.

2023-1-FI01-KA210-ADU-000154916.title: ART FOR SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITIES
2023-1-FI01-KA210-ADU-000154916.summary:
<< Background >>

Each organization wanted to develop its own expertise and activities, while also gaining new networks and experience in international cooperation.

The organizations involved in the project were very different both in terms of their activities and operating environments, so learning from each other was essential. In Croatia, there is particular expertise in theatre, circus, and various forms of community-engaging activities. At Revontuli Adult Education Centre, distance learning has been especially developed, and the institute has had, for example, a poetry recitation group for a long time. Järvilakeus Adult Education Centre, in turn, has special expertise in producing films with amateur resources.

The goal was to gain new inspiration from each partner for the organization’s own activities and to identify new development areas that could also be implemented through future project cooperation.


<< Objectives >>

The aim was to create and promote learning opportunities for local residents and to better understand the differences and similarities between different groups of people and nationalities. Another goal was to create opportunities for new acquaintances and to promote digital skills. The overall objective was to increase the socially sustainable development of communities through sociocultural and artistic activities.

The  project sought to promote contacts especially between Finnish and Croatian adults interested in non-verbal communication, video production, and performing arts. Another important goal was to become familiar with the diverse environments of the partners and to discover interesting sites for filming and photography. The aim was to find ways to communicate without words and, more generally, to increase courage in interacting with people from different cultures.


<< Implementation >>

The project began with a webinar in which the project’s objectives were presented and each partner introduced their activities. In joint online planning meetings, the encounters were designed, with each partner responsible for the practical arrangements and implementation of their own meeting. Each meeting included not only a diverse introduction to the partner’s activities and the local community, but also an evening event or performance open to as wide a local audience as possible. In addition, the meetings included a wide range of community activities that involved local residents as well as project partners. In the final webinar, the activities and achievements of the project were reviewed. 

The project implemented very diverse workshops and activities, including the following: in Kittilä and Sodankylä, an international poetry workshop and a “colour bath” for adults were held. In Croatia, workshops were organized on circus arts, group singing, and animation techniques. In Kauhava, a short film was produced in international cooperation. At each meeting, there was also a remote connection to the participants’ own organizations, where short updates shared with several voices  -"Saying Hi to the folks at home."

<< Results >>

In cooperation with the project partners, a humorous short film titled “Where is Mutteri” https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5Cbj2GeT8AY was created, allowing participation even with limited language skills.

Through the project, participants gained new knowledge in areas such as clowning, shadow theatre, color bath workshops for adults, and the use of poetry as a source for drama improvisation.We also received excellent information about the different ways distance learning can be implemented.

The open events organized within the project also brought together people from diverse backgrounds and through the visits, local residents had the opportunity to learn about different cultures. 

The project also led to new contacts, which have already resulted in further activities as well as ideas for follow-up projects and continued collaboration.We plan to continue cooperation with both our Finnish partners and Croatian collaborators through follow-up projects, guest performances, and artist exchanges. Building on the knowledge, relationships, and artistic results of ART-S-COM, we aim to develop new creative initiatives that continue connecting communities through art.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2023-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000154044.title: HOPE4HEALTH
2023-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000154044.summary:
<< Background >>

We signed up for the project because we recognized the need for a well-designed education program aimed at strengthening the competencies of team cooperation and interpersonal relationships within therapy teams. The key starting point of the project was the recognition of the importance of strong relationships within the therapy team (professional staff and/or volunteers who implement equine assisted therapy for different users) as one of the key elements of successful equine intervention. During the project, we developed a new educational program "Competencies of a good therapy team", which addressed the specific challenges that organizations face in this area. Among the main challenges are unclear division of work tasks, organization of volunteer tasks and effective communication with them, lack of clear communication, disagreements within therapy teams, high turnover of team members, burnout of overburdened individuals, and difficulties in maintaining a high quality of daily work. The program is designed with the aim of strengthening team dynamics, improving cooperation and ensuring a higher quality of work with users.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we set the following key goals:
Increasing team competencies, personal knowledge and skills for adults
Encouraging non-formal learning activities for persons and organisations in rural areas 
Improving the quality of equine assisted therapies for users with fewer opportunities
Development of a new educational program for workers and volunteeers in equine-assisted programs
Creating a support network for organisations in Republic of Croatia and Republic of Slovenia
Encouraging innovative approaches: We introduced new approaches to the work of therapy teams into the project, such as structured educational programs, better work organization, and innovative methods for working with volunteers and users.
Sustainability and long-term impact: We adhered to the core values ​​of the Erasmus+ program and contributed to the sustainable development of the competences and quality of work of therapy teams, which ensures long-term benefits for individuals and organizations.
With these goals, we not only improved the knowledge and skills of the participants, but also directly contributed to a better quality of therapies and created new opportunities for international cooperation and networking.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, we conducted an analysis based on which we prepared and developed an innovative educational program "Competencies of a successful therapy team". The program was implemented in three modules: module 1 in Slovenia, module 2 virtually and module 3 in Croatia, combining theoretical workshops and practical exercises. After the program was implemented, an evaluation was carried out, based on which we improved the final results. We created working materials in three languages ​​(Slovenian, Croatian, English) that are freely available on the project partners' websites. We presented the project results at the international HETI congress, the Slovenian symposium, a virtual discussion on the occasion of Erasmus Day and shared them via social networks and YouTube, bringing the project closer to the wider public.

<< Results >>

During the project, the following indicators were achieved:
● 1 educational program was prepared in three languages ​​(Croatian, Slovenian, English).
● 1 public tender was published for the inclusion of participants 
● 15 participants from Croatia and Slovenia were included in the educational program.
● 2 multi-day practical workshops were conducted in Croatia (module 3) and in Slovenia (module 1).
● 1 virtual Zoom workshop was conducted (module 2).
● 15 certificates for participation in the education were issued.
● A comprehensive evaluation of the project was conducted via an evaluation questionnaire.
● The educational program was presented to Croatian Association for Equine-Assisted Interventions (Croatia, December 2023).
● The project was presented at the international HETI congress (Hungary, June 2024).
● The project was presented at a professional symposium in the field of horse-assisted interventions (Republic of Slovenia, October 2024).
● The educational program was presented at the Erasmus Days  (Slovenia, October 2024).
● The training materials were published on the websites of the project partners (Croatian, Slovenian, English).
● A promotional video of the educational program was published on the YouTube channel.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas
