2023-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000155794.title: Raising Awareness for a Greener Tomorrow
2023-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000155794.summary:
<< Background >>

The main motivation of the project was to contribute to global efforts in addressing environmental protection and combating climate change through the development of educational materials, sharing knowledge and experience, and raising general awareness about green topics. The project dealt with multiple aspects of environmental education, with an emphasis on waste management, environmental protection, green skills, energy and resource savings, and climate change. By collaborating among three educational institutions in the field of adult education and a public waste management company, a high-quality exchange of knowledge, experience, and practices on green topics was enabled, particularly focusing on waste management and environmental protection, thereby producing quality project outcomes. The project focused on the need to improve the competencies of educators and staff in adult education for more effective teaching on green topics. Additionally, it addressed the need to create learning opportunities and possibilities for adult learners in the areas of waste management and green topics. By disseminating the project results, alongside educators and adult learners, we also aimed to promote general awareness about green topics.

<< Objectives >>

The specific goals we aimed to achieve through the implementation of the project are:
1.	To improve the competencies of educators and staff in adult education for more effective teaching on green topics, with an emphasis on waste management.
2.	To create learning opportunities for adult learners in the fields of waste management and green topics, as well as the issues of environmental protection, including ways in which they, as individuals, can contribute daily to solving these problems.
3.	To develop innovative educational resources on green topics – a methodological manual, curriculum, and a digital educational-informative tool for waste sorting – which will be publicly available for use by educators, adult learners, and other interested parties.
4.	To raise awareness about green topics and promote sustainable practices in the field of waste management and green topics in general.
5.	To encourage cooperation and the exchange of knowledge and experience on green topics and waste management through cross-sectoral collaboration among partners from three countries, supported by practical examples such as study visits to local waste management facilities during transnational meetings.


<< Implementation >>

Within activity A1, we conducted continuous project coordination and management, and held online meetings. Through activity A2, we carried out in-depth research on the current state of waste management in the three partner countries, conducted an analysis and assessment of the interests and preferences of 154 adult learners regarding environmental education and green topics, and organized the first transnational meeting. Through activity A3, we developed a methodological handbook for educators working with adult learners for more effective teaching on green topics and held the second transnational meeting. Within activity A4, we created a curriculum to raise awareness of environmental topics among adult learners, piloted the curriculum through workshops with 51 participants, and organized the third transnational meeting. Through activity A5, we developed the project website, conducted an analysis of household waste data in the partner countries, and created a digital educational and informational tool on proper waste sorting. 

<< Results >>

Concrete results: 1.) A developed Report on the state of waste management in HR, SI, and MK and the needs of adult learners (154 learners surveyed), which provides a comprehensive analysis and served as the basis for developing educational resources within the RAGT project. 2.) A developed Methodological Handbook for adult educators on waste management, environmental protection, and health risks, also for local communities and stakeholders in the environmental sectors. 3.) A developed Curriculum to enhance the competencies of educators in adult education, providing them with new opportunities to enhance teaching through this innovative educational resource. 4.) Successfully piloted workshops on environmental topics based on the created RAGT curriculum with 51 participants. 5.) A developed project website with all project results. 6.) A developed digital tool for waste sorting that informs the public on proper waste separation with 51 items in its database. Additionally: 3 TPMs, 5 virtual meetings, 3 visits to waste management facilities.

2023-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000155811.title: Terapijska snaga vrtlarenja
2023-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000155811.summary:
<< Background >>

 The position of the Pulac Branch, which provides half-day care services for adults with intellectual disabilities, on a green area of ​​40,000 m2 (outside the city), allows the implementation of new work activities in a natural, calm environment, which is important for the therapeutic effect of gardening. Such a location, to which the citizens of our city gravitate (walking, picking asparagus, etc.), supports the integration of people with disabilities through meetings and socializing with citizens in the garden, i.e. the integration of users into the community.
The application is the result of the desire for an innovative approach in working with people with disabilities, expanding the range of services that the Center otherwise provides, through therapeutic gardening.

<< Objectives >>

 By implementing the project, namely by building a vegetable garden, an orchard and a sensory garden adapted to users, we wanted to improve the quality of life of people with intellectual disabilities by enriching the social services provided by the Rijeka Rehabilitation Center.

<< Implementation >>

Activities carried out:
- Education and introduction to good practices at the partner CUDV Draga, Slovenia (followed by transfer of knowledge and skills to users)
- Construction and arrangement of an orchard, vegetable garden and sensory garden and management of its development 
- Procurement of tools, materials, seeds, seedlings and fertilizers necessary for work
- Active involvement of users in work activities
- Creation of an e-manual on the topic of therapeutic gardening 
- Final project conference and presentation of results

<< Results >>

The specific outcomes and other results of our project are:
- Increased number of professional workers trained in providing innovative types of complementary-supportive forms of rehabilitation, i.e. work activities with therapeutic and restorative characteristics for the users of the Center (they are familiar with the basic principles of horticultural rehabilitation)
- Conceptually designed and built a functional therapeutic vegetable garden, sensory garden and orchard, educated employees, in cooperation with the users, with the professional supervision and mentoring of the Slovenian partner, transformed the existing green areas into a functional vegetable garden, orchard and sensory garden
- At least 15 users of the Center, people with intellectual disabilities and associated disabilities and people with autism spectrum disorders, were involved in the activities of creating a vegetable garden, orchard and sensory garden and planning and planting certain species and cultures, and maintaining it
- A joint e-manual on gardening was created and published
- A final conference was held at which the results were presented

2023-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000160133.title: Neka bude kratko i jasno: Uvod u asistivnu tehnologiju za osobe oštećena vida
2023-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000160133.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to support blind and partially sighted adults with accessible digital education and employment tools. Many lack training to use assistive technology, which leads to exclusion and reduced independence.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to improve digital and labour market skills of visually impaired persons. We also wanted to strengthen intersectoral collaboration, Erasmus+ project-related skills, and professional growth among consortium members.

<< Implementation >>

The project activities were divided into three main parts: A1, A2 and A3.  
A1 covered horizontal activities including project management, quality management and promotion and visibility.  
A2 produced an online handbook about employing visually impaired people. 
A3 created an OER platform with nine video lessons on assistive technology.  

<< Results >>

The first output was an accessible online handbook about employing visually impaired people. It is available in English, Slovenian, Croatian, and Spanish, in audio, docx, PDF, HTML, and EPUB formats.
The second output was a virtual platform with nine video lessons on assistive technology. The videos are available in the same four languages. All materials are free and accessible to blind and partially sighted users.
Partners gained experience in creating accessible digital content. New partners learned how to implement Erasmus+ projects.
The consortium improved international cooperation through regular exchange and teamwork.
Stakeholders and the wider community gained knowledge about the needs of visually impaired people, accessibility, and assistive technology for employment and inclusion.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2023-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000152375.title: Parliamo di noi, i rom
2023-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000152375.summary:
<< Background >>

The decision to participate in this project come from the need to address anti-Gypsyism and improve the representation of the Roma community in the media. Over the past 15 years, the spread of social media and the rise of private television have amplified hate speech and false news against Roma. Due to their marginalisation and low levels of education, the community often lacks the tools to respond to these injustices and counter distorted narratives. This project responded to the need to train Roma adults in digital, interpersonal and creative skills, which are essential for telling their stories in an authentic and positive way and building links with the media.
The project also aimed to strengthen the participating organisations in international cooperation, in particular through Erasmus+, by providing them with tools to work internationally. The Serbian and Croatian organisations wanted to gain more recognition from Roma adults in order to improve their work with the community on the ground. This was done by involving some Roma adults in a mobility project, an opportunity often denied to them, but also through events.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the project were:
- To counter intolerance and discrimination against Roma communities by promoting self-narrative through the media;
- To train 15 adults (30-50 years old) from the international Roma community in the world of information, storytelling, media-related digital skills and networking, making people from the Roma community active protagonists of information.
- To produce a manual in several languages with the basic rules of journalistic communication;
- Improve the access of Roma organisations to the Erasmus+ programme.

<< Implementation >>

The project activities were
1) A cycle of 7 online workshops for 17 adults (the age of some participants did not match the expected age range) from Roma communities in Italy, Serbia and Croatia on information, storytelling, digital skills and networking;
2) Production of a manual in 4 languages (Italian, Serbian, Croatian and English) with the basic rules of journalistic communication;
3) A face-to-face seminar for 15 adults from the Roma community with the participation of international journalists (Dalibor Tanic, editor-in-chief of the portal www.portal-udar.net; Gordana Nešović, editor of the daily radio programme Romano Them - Svijet Roma; Daut Qylangjiu, editor of the Roma desk at Radioteleviziji Kosovo) in Croatia.
4) Awareness-raising and project presentation event in Serbia.
5) Establishment, registration in Serbia and presentation of the Roma World Journalists Federation; collection of membership from participating journalists at the event in Serbia;
6) Project coordination.

<< Results >>

The project was successful in its aim to combat intolerance and discrimination against Roma:
- by training 17 Roma adults (albeit with some elements of a different age than originally planned) in the world of information, storytelling, digital media skills and networking, enabling them to be active protagonists of information and to tell their stories;
- by creating a handbook in 4 languages (Italian, Serbian, Croatian and English) with the basic rules of journalistic communication, downloadable from the social pages of the associations and from Romni's LinkedIn page, available on the FLIPHTML5 platform;
- by publishing lessons on Romni's YouTube channel;
- through the establishment of the RWJF;
- to improve the access of Roma organisations to the Erasmus+ programme and strengthen their competences.
In addition, thanks to the wide dissemination at European level and in the Balkan region, through radio, TV, articles and social media, we raised interest in the project at international level, so much so that some associations asked our partners to replicate the project with them, as it was considered to be of great interest.

2023-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000164811.title: In-Salads: Promoting Sustainable Food and Healthy Nutrition through Intercultural Salads Exchange
2023-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000164811.summary:
<< Background >>

The reasons encouraging partners to realize the project were related to three areas: the need to promote sustainable education; the need to promote social inclusion and the need to improve digital citizenship skills. The needs were identified in groups of fragile students/learners with a migration background.
Concerning sustainability, the need was identified to:  
- promote healthy nutrition and sustainable for  environment; 
- promote the choice of healthy and sustainable diets to reduce the risk of chronic diseases and reduce the environmental impact related to food consumption; 
- train people to make informed decisions about their diet and to reduce the impact of food consumption on health and the environment. 
Concerning inclusion, the need was identified to:
- share different cultural traditions on cooking and eating;
- involve migrant people to create an inclusive environment and enhance different cultures.
Concerning digital citizenship, the need was identified to: 
- promote experiential and collaborative learning by using digital storytelling
- encourage participation with innovative tools like the social hackathon approach. 


<< Objectives >>

The INSALDS project achieved the following specific objectives: 
- To train adult educators on facilitating intercultural exchange through food and digital story telling;
- To train students/learners on video production and digital storytelling techniques;
- To train  students/learmers on food stainability;
- To develop recipes for cross-cultural salads
- To create videos introducing cross-cultural recipes.
The project achieved the planned objectives and also contributed to developing a higher intercultural sensitivity and awarness of environmental sustainability of food consumption in local communities. The local communities also improved the inclusion process by developing attention and a sense of welcome towards the intercultural recipes tested within the project workshops. Participation of migrant people in the context of public space was enhanced. In particular, participation in urban gardens activities and presentations of the project results were opportunities to improve intercultural interaction and to offer migrant people opportunities to value their cultural background .

<< Implementation >>

The activities implemented were: 
- kick off meeting in Italy in Udine 1/2 February 24 with 13 participants (3 F4S, 4 CPIA Udine, 2 Aupex, 2 Dante, 1 Egina)
- training on line of trainers on digital story telling and video production techniques: 25 March 24 (with 7 participants + 1 trainer) and 26 March 24 (with 8 participants +1 trainer) 
- training of trainers on food sustainability and healthy nutrition  in Portugal (18, 19, 20 March 24) with 7 participants (2 CPIA, 2 AUPEX, 2 DANTE, 1 Idanha - a - Nova municipality) and 4 trainers from F4S.
- creation of 3 local groups to produce intercultural salads and videos documenting the salads production process. The people involved were: 45 CPIA Udine, 14 AUPEX, 10 Dante
- creation of video tutorials illustrating the intercultural recipes: the partners developed numerous video recipes (11CPIA Udine, 8 Dante, 14 AUPEX)
- participation of local working groups representatives  (11 CPIA Udine, 2 Dante, 2 AUPEX, 1 F4S) in Bevagna to attend SHU and creation of the APP https://www.insaladsproject.eu   and Instagram account https://www.instagram.com/insaladsapp?igsh=MWdyY2RlcXRpdmhiaQ==
- promotion, communication and dissemination activities documented in https://www.insaladsproject.eu/it/home

<< Results >>

The project results achieved are: 
- Adult educators trained in facilitating intercultural exchange through food;
- Participants trained on video production and digital storytelling;
- Participants trained on food sustainability;
- Cross-cultural salad recipes developed ;
- Recipes video presentation created;
- Participation in Bevagna SHU 4-7 July 2024 
- dissemination during SHU 5 July 2024
- APP and Instagram account creation https://www.instagram.com/insaladsapp?igsh=MWdyY2RlcXRpdmhiaQ== .
Other results are related to communication and dissemination activities: 
- creation of an accessible website and publication of video recipes 
- public presentations for citizens 
- articles to describe the activities published on websites
-project presentations  during relevant events, as conferences of the GREEN school network in Italy; presentation at the Folk High Schools of Extremadura in Spain and  participation of F4S in the Raiana Fair in Portugal. 
- articles to disseminate the activities on websites
- articles published on the EPALE platform and other platforms. 
The Project's website garnered 1,177 visits and 344 users. The most used social media platforms were: Facebook 9470 impressions; Instagram 4088 impressions, LinkedIn 1517

2023-1-LT01-KA210-ADU-000161637.title: Active Aging for our green and healthy lifestyle
2023-1-LT01-KA210-ADU-000161637.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the GREENAGE project to address the urgent need for promoting green skills and active, healthy aging through non-formal adult education, aligning with the EU’s Green Deal, Skills Agenda, and Green Paper on Aging, as well as the UN Decade of Healthy Ageing (2021-2030). The project tackles the lack of training programs in Lithuania and Croatia that integrate ecological awareness and sustainable decision-making for adult learners. Despite the emphasis on green skills in EU strategies, non-formal education in these countries lags in fostering active aging and environmental responsibility. Additionally, low participation rates in lifelong learning among adults, especially the 55+ population, in both nations highlight the need for enhanced educational services. By uniting international perspectives, the project aims to empower adult educators, increase adult learner engagement, and promote sustainable, healthy aging, contributing to national challenges and global sustainability goals.

<< Objectives >>

The GREENAGE project aimed to promote healthy and active aging through enhanced green skills and ecological behavior among adult learners. Its objectives were:
1) Create a non-formal training handbook and videos for adult educators to foster adult learners' green skills, active aging, and healthy lifestyles.
2) Develop competencies of adult educators and trainers by conducting pilot training and refining the handbook based on their feedback.
3) Encourage adult educators and decision-makers to integrate ecological behavior, healthy practices, and green skills into their programs through dissemination measures.

<< Implementation >>

The GREENAGE project implemented the following activities:
1) Developed a handbook and short videos, “Green and Healthy Lifestyle for Active Aging,” for adult educators and learners.
2) Tested the non-formal training handbook and videos through a pilot training-of-trainers event.
3) Organized local and international dissemination events, including workshops, training, a Final Project Conference, and publications in local media and social media.
4) Held two transnational project partner meetings to facilitate collaboration and project coordination.

<< Results >>

The GREENAGE project delivered the following concrete outputs and results:
1) An open-source handbook, “Green and Healthy Lifestyle for Active Aging” (93 pages, 4 parts, 3 languages), published on partner websites for adult educators.
2) 6 short digital films, published on partner websites.
3) A 3-day training for adult educators in Croatia, engaging 8 adult educators.
4) 2 pilot workshops in partner countries, engaging 34 adult educators and trainers.
5) A final online conference with  59  international participants.
6) 4 media releases, 8 posts on partner websites and Facebook, and 2 articles published on the EPALE platform.

2023-1-PL01-KA210-ADU-000159875.title: Razem bezpieczniej
2023-1-PL01-KA210-ADU-000159875.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project to address significant gaps in the preparation of caregivers and those who support them in their work with seriously and terminally ill people. The goal was to develop their emotional and social competencies, which are necessary in the face of the challenges of caring for people at the end of life. We noticed a lack of didactic scenarios in the field of thanatopedagogy in the Polish education system, despite the fact that the topics of death and bereavement are extremely important. The project promoted a holistic approach, encompassing the physical, mental, social and spiritual aspects of care. It also responded to the growing need to educate paraprofessionals - people without full medical training, but who support the care of the aging population. We developed scenarios for teaching basic caregiving skills and tools for their verification, designed for formal and non-formal education. Through international cooperation, we created a method that takes into account environmental and social factors, making it a universal tool to improve the quality of life of patients and their families.

<< Objectives >>

In implementing the project, we wanted to respond to the urgent needs of those involved in caring for the seriously and terminally ill - both formal and informal caregivers, as well as families and the patients themselves. Our goal was to create the conditions for informed, empathetic and professional support for people at the end of life and to increase public sensitivity to the dying process. We believe that openness to the subject of death, understanding of emotions and the ability to communicate are crucial for dignified accompaniment in the last moments of life. We developed training scenarios and validation tools as a foundation for further education and professionalization. We aimed to increase the emotional and social competence of caregivers, fill the educational gap in thanatopedagogy, promote a holistic approach to the needs of patients and their caregivers, and educate paraprofessionals. We also aimed to create tools for formal and non-formal education and to initiate social change, leading to greater awareness and understanding of the process of passing away.

<< Implementation >>

The project developed, tested and disseminated an emotional support programme for carers of terminally ill people. An international team with experts from three countries was set up to establish a management structure and timetable for activities. A review of the literature and existing educational programmes was conducted, producing country reports identifying gaps in the support system. This was followed by interviews with patients and their carers and a design thinking workshop (24 hours in total), resulting in the design of a training programme. A 24-hour course, methodological guide and validation tools were developed and translated into partner languages and English. The programme was tested with each organisation - a total of 36 participants in the pilot. Revisions to the materials were made after feedback was collected. The results of the project were presented at conferences (three national, one international) and in the media. The project supported the development of professional competences in palliative care and strengthened international cooperation. The effects will be long-term - improving the quality of emotional care and the preparation of carers.

<< Results >>

The project created a comprehensive competency workshop program (24 hours+ guide) to develop the social and emotional competencies of those supporting terminally and terminally ill patients and their loved ones. The program included lesson plans, practical exercises, educational materials and assessment and self-reflection tools. It focused on emotional communication, empathy, attentive listening, recognizing the needs of patients and working with difficult emotions. The program was tested in practice during 6 pilot workshops ( each 24h), and 36 participants successfully completed the training and validation process. The project strengthened international cooperation in the exchange of knowledge, experience and good practices, developing models of coordination and communication. A network of contacts with organizations working in the fields of palliative care, psychology and education was expanded, increasing the potential for implementing further initiatives. The project was successful, producing tangible educational and social results and laying a solid foundation for further activities in thanatopedagogy and community support.

2023-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000157454.title: Apoteka – prijatelj zdravog potomstva
2023-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000157454.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated in response to the consistently low breastfeeding rates in Serbia, which pose a significant public health concern. According to national statistics, only 12.8% of infants are breastfed, despite strong evidence that breastfeeding significantly contributes to both maternal and child health. Although the National Program for Breastfeeding Support was launched in 2018 to address this issue, the activities have not been fully implemented across the country. One of the key unmet needs is the lack of reliable information available to mothers about the safe use of medications and supplements during breastfeeding. As a result, many women unnecessarily stop breastfeeding when they need to take medications, due to fear of harming their child. This highlights a critical gap in public health education and service provision. Pharmacies, being the most accessible healthcare institutions, have the potential to bridge this gap. Pharmacists are ideally positioned to provide expert, evidence-based guidance on the safety of medications during lactation. The Ministry of Health has issued National Guidelines for Medication Use During Breastfeeding, equipping pharmacists with the necessary tools to offer accurate counseling.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were:
•	To promote and support breastfeeding as a national public health priority, in alignment with WHO and UNICEF recommendations that view breastfeeding rates as indicators of a society's health potential and development.
•	To increase breastfeeding rates by offering education and support through accessible healthcare professionals, particularly pharmacists.
•	To empower pharmacists to provide reliable, guideline-based information about the safety of medications, vaccines, vitamins, and herbal remedies during breastfeeding.
•	To educate pregnant and breastfeeding women about:
o	The nutritional and developmental benefits of human milk for the child, including support for physical, emotional, cognitive, and sensory development.
o	The health benefits of breastfeeding for mothers, such as reduced postpartum depression, less bleeding after childbirth, decreased anemia risk, faster return to pre-pregnancy weight, and long-term protection against osteoporosis and some cancers.
•	To improve medication adherence, safety, and effectiveness through pharmacist-led counseling, ultimately leading to better health outcomes for both mother and child.

<< Implementation >>

The project included several key activities: launching a dedicated subpage and social media profiles to improve outreach and engagement; designing digital educational and promotional materials (brochures, posters, stickers, videos); developing a web application for accessing the National Guidelines on medication use during breastfeeding; organizing symposia and online training sessions for healthcare professionals to strengthen their counseling capacity; managing project implementation; and printing and distributing educational materials through pharmacies and health centers. Each activity aimed to increase awareness, knowledge, and support for breastfeeding among women and healthcare providers.

<< Results >>

Concrete project outputs included a fully functional web application with regularly updated guidance on medication safety during breastfeeding; a wide range of open-access educational and promotional materials; trained health professionals with improved skills in breastfeeding support; strengthened partnerships between pharmacists and healthcare institutions; and increased visibility of breastfeeding support topics in the public sphere. These results directly supported national and EU-level priorities in maternal and child health promotion.

2023-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000153497.title: Senior Synergy: Empowering Lifelong Learning and Healthy living through Community Events
2023-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000153497.summary:
<< Background >>

The SenSyn project was developed in response to the growing need for innovative and inclusive educational opportunities for older adults. Partners observed that seniors are often excluded from structured learning despite their motivation to remain active, healthy, and socially engaged. The project therefore aimed to strengthen the competences of adult educators working with seniors and to develop modern, digital, and easily accessible tools that promote lifelong learning and well-being in later life.
At the same time, the project addressed the need for greater awareness of the importance of active ageing and intergenerational solidarity within local communities. By developing a digital database of good practices, a training programme, and a practical toolkit for trainers, SenSyn provided sustainable resources for organisations and educators working with seniors across Europe.


<< Objectives >>

The SenSyn project aimed to promote active ageing and lifelong learning among seniors and to improve the competences of adult educators working with older learners. The main objectives were to develop innovative, inclusive, and accessible learning opportunities that support seniors in maintaining physical and mental well-being and to create new educational tools that adult educators could use in their daily work.
Through transnational cooperation, partners developed a Digital Database of good practices, a Training Programme for empowering lifelong learning and healthy living, and a Toolkit for trainers. These results strengthened the professional skills of adult education staff, encouraged intergenerational learning, and promoted active participation of seniors in community life.
The project also aimed to raise awareness about the importance of active and healthy lifestyles after retirement and to reduce stereotypes about ageing. By combining educational and recreational activities, SenSyn contributed to the inclusion of older adults in lifelong learning and created sustainable learning models that can be transferred and used across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

Project Management where partners developed the Project Management Handbook, the Evaluation and Quality Assurance plan, Risk Management plan, Dissemination plan, and the Sustainability plan. Partners created the project logo and website to ensure visibility, and hold regular online coordination meetings. 

Second activity focused on research and the development of the Digital Database of good practices in active ageing and adult education. Partners collected and analysed over 40 examples of innovative practices, which served as a basis for the web tool.

At activity three the consortium developed and piloted a Training Programme combining educational and recreational modules for seniors. Each partner tested the programme nationally and provided feedback for improvement.

Activity four produced the Toolkit for trainers and delivered training sessions for future educators.

Finally activity consisted of four large-scale community events (Senioriade) and a final conference in Samobor, which together reached more than 500 seniors and numerous educators, ensuring visibility, dissemination, and sustainability of project results.

<< Results >>

- Digital Database of innovative educational practices and tools, containing over 40 examples of good practices in active ageing and lifelong learning;
- Training Programme for empowering lifelong learning and healthy living, consisting of 8 educational and recreational modules, developed, piloted, and validated in partner countries;
- Toolkit for trainers, providing methodological guidance, lesson plans, and practical approaches for implementing the SenSyn programme in the future;
- Project website available in English, Slovenian, and Croatian language, serving as the main platform for dissemination and exploitation of results;
- Four community events (Senioriade) and a final conference in Samobor, reaching 711 seniors, 91 organisations, and 20 trained adult educators.

Beyond these tangible outputs, the project resulted in improved cooperation among adult education institutions, enhanced skills of trainers, and increased awareness of active ageing and healthy living at both national and European levels.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2023-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000156306.title: Krepitev osebne odgovornosti v zaporniškem sistemu za trajnost v družbi
2023-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000156306.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project with the aim of supporting teachers and other staff working in the prison system in developing competencies for planning and implementing sustainable practices in their teaching or their work with incarcerated persons. Both partner organizations identified, based on the results of surveys and focus groups, a need among teachers and other prison staff for training in sustainable development and the integration of sustainable practices into their work or teaching of incarcerated individuals. The prison administrations of the Republic of Slovenia and the Republic of Croatia have endorsed the project as well, as it offers numerous benefits for the prison system.  By strengthening the responsibility of incarcerated individuals for reducing energy and water consumption, the impact on the environment is reduced, and the costs for the prison system are also lowered. Incarcerated individuals gain a sense of value and usefulness, which can lead to better rehabilitation after serving their sentence. The project has a positive impact on the wider community, as it raises awareness of environmental issues within the prison system as well. The project aligns with EU legislation.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to promote a culture of sustainability among teachers and staff in the prison systems of two countries, so that sustainable practices would become an integral part of the prison environment.
By encouraging collaboration and the exchange of best practices between the two countries, we aimed to: - develop a training program for teachers and prison staff focusing on sustainable practices and how these can be integrated into daily routines when working with incarcerated individuals and within educational programs, - raise awareness about sustainable practices, - improve the competencies, knowledge, and skills of teachers and other prison staff in the field of sustainability, - train multipliers who can transfer knowledge in the field of sustainable development, - develop resources and teaching materials that teachers and prison staff can use to promote responsibility among incarcerated individuals for implementing sustainable practices, - foster cooperation and knowledge exchange between teachers and staff in the prison systems of two different countries, - promote best practices and effective approaches to sustainable education and daily routines in working with incarcerated individuals.



<< Implementation >>

1.	Project management and coordination activities – We established a project team and appointed project leaders from both partner countries. The project team and leaders were responsible for planning, communication, monitoring and control, financial tracking, quality assurance, risk management, stakeholder engagement, and organizing project meetings. 2. Research (needs analysis) and development of the "Activation for Sustainable Development" program – This included training multipliers, preparing an overview of good sustainability practices in both countries, and developing a Competence Catalogue and the "Activation for Sustainable Development" training program. 3. Pilot implementation of the "Activation for Sustainable Development" training program – We carried out two pilot trainings (one in Croatia and one in Slovenia). Each pilot implementation involved 10 teachers and staff members working in the prison system. Two evaluations were conducted to assess the effectiveness of the pilot sessions. 4. Dissemination activities – We developed a dissemination plan and implemented communication activities. We also prepared a digital book and posters and organized a final conference.

<< Results >>

 - 7 multipliers trained in sustainable development, - a list of good practices for implementing sustainability principles in work with incarcerated individuals, - a Competence Catalogue for the "Activation for Sustainable Development" training program, - the "Activation for Sustainable Development" training program for teachers and prison staff, - 2 pilot implementations of the "Activation for Sustainable Development" training program, - 2 evaluations of the pilot implementations of the training program for teachers and prison staff, - dissemination plan - a final conference conducted. Concrete outputs produced through the project include two digital books of good sustainable practices within the prison system (one in Slovenian, one in Croatian), distributed to all prisons, and 50 framed posters (covering 7 different topics) for prisons and both partner organizations' administrations, serving as reminders for teachers, staff, and incarcerated individuals to engage in sustainable behaviour. The digital books are intended for teachers and prison staff to encourage sustainable actions among incarcerated individuals. In addition, two project subpages were created on the websites of both partner organizations for results.

2023-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000157749.title: Providing a better future for Ukrainian refugees through digital learning
2023-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000157749.summary:
<< Background >>

The war in Ukraine has forced millions of people to flee their homes and seek safety in European countries. Many of these refugees, particularly women and young adults, face psychological challenges, cultural barriers, and difficulty integrating into the host society. We applied for this project to address the urgent need for mental support and empowerment of Ukrainian refugees in Slovenia and Croatia. Our goal was to help them build resilience, regain a sense of control, and develop mental skills to support their integration into the labour market, education system, and local communities. The project is led by performance psychologist Sara Isaković, whose own family had to move abroad when she was three years old due to the war in Yugoslavia. Her personal experience gives this initiative a deeper layer of empathy and understanding. Through digital content and in-person workshops, the project offers practical tools for motivation, goal-setting, and adaptation to a new life.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to support the integration of Ukrainian refugees into host countries by developing and delivering a Mental Training Programme. We aimed to equip refugees with practical mental skills such as motivation, goal-setting, emotional resilience, and self-confidence—essential tools for building a new life in a foreign environment. By offering user-friendly digital content and in-person workshops, we wanted to improve refugees’ access to quality education, enhance their employability, and promote mental well-being. Another key goal was to foster a sense of community and belonging by connecting refugees from Slovenia and Croatia, encouraging peer support and shared experience. Through collaboration between Ukrainian associations and project partners, we also aimed to strengthen support networks and create long-term impact across the EU.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented in two main phases. First, we conducted a needs assessment through interviews with Ukrainian refugees and stakeholders in Slovenia and Croatia, supported by a desk review of existing educational resources. This informed the design of the Mental Training Programme, a digital learning tool consisting of 32 short, interactive video lessons in English with Ukrainian translation. The content focuses on motivation, goal-setting, resilience, and emotional well-being. We collaborated with FranklinCovey Adria to structure the educational design, wrote scripts, filmed and edited all lessons, and published them on https://4uture.thinkific.com. In the second phase, we organized two in-person workshops in Slovenia and Croatia, led by psychologist Sara Isaković. Participants were encouraged to become ambassadors of the programme. Many came from Ukrainian governmental and non-governmental organizations.

<< Results >>

Ukrainian refugees received a comprehensive set of tools through a 3.5-hour online masterclass with psychologist Sara Isaković, equipping them with essential psychological techniques for adapting to life in a new country. Two impactful live training events followed: the first in Zagreb (April 28, 2025) with 30 participants, and the second in Ljubljana (May 12, 2025) with 32 participants. Both events were organized in collaboration with local Ukrainian associations. Participants were encouraged to act as ambassadors, sharing the acquired knowledge within their communities. Both Ukrainian organizations reported that participants were thrilled with the content, particularly Sara’s clear and relatable way of explaining psychology and guiding practical exercises. Partner associations committed to further disseminating these tools across their networks in Croatia, Slovenia, and other European countries—thus multiplying the reach and fostering wider social integration.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

2023-2-DE02-KA210-ADU-000175080.title: Interactive Map for Cross Country Inspiration for Climate Change Prevention
2023-2-DE02-KA210-ADU-000175080.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the urgent need for accessible, practical, and inspiring climate education across Europe. Building on the successful outcomes of the C4CC project, we recognised that the rich collection of national climate-related resources had strong potential for cross-border transfer but remained inaccessible due to language barriers and format limitations. In particular, there was demand for resources that promote intergenerational learning, digital literacy, and actionable engagement in climate change prevention. This project addressed those needs by translating and updating materials into English, developing a perpetual wall calendar, and launching an interactive EU climate map.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to increase the reach and relevance of climate change education by creating accessible, multilingual, and multimedia learning tools that could be used by institutions, educators, and the public across Europe. Specifically, we wantedto translate, digitise, and promote existing C4CC resources to enable their cross-border use, foster digital readiness among partners and learners, and enhance climate awareness at local, regional, and EU levels. Through the creation of the perpetual wall calendar and interactive map, we wanted to offer entry points for action-based learning and to inspire everyday climate-conscious decisions. By targeting teaching bodies and local institutions, we aimed to reach a wide network of learners and decision-makers who could amplify the project’s message and impact.

<< Implementation >>

The project involved four main activities. In Activity 1, all partners except SZM translated climate change resources from the previous C4CC project into English, including case studies, tasks, and subtitling videos.Activity 2 focused on the creation of aperpetual wall calendar by FIP, featuring monthly climate change topics linked to the online resources. The calendar was developed in all project languages and integrated QR codes connecting to the Climate Map platform, serving as the main offline entry point to project materials.Activity 3, led by SZM, developed the online interactive calendar and Climate Map. This platform includes filtering by country, language, and topic, hosts downloadable wall calendars, and links to the C4CC resources. QR codes on the calendars facilitate direct access to the digital map, enhancing user engagement.Activity 4 covered promotion and management. JFV handled overall coordination, finance, risk, and communication. INQUIRIUM focused on impact and sustainability, ISR ensured quality assessment, and FIP managed branding and design, supporting SZM with branded materials.

<< Results >>

The project delivered a rich set of results to support climate education and action: 
- Climate change materials in Croatian, French, German, Greek, Italian and Romanian are available in the native language and in English. 
- Irish and Maltese resources are available in English. 
- Climate videos have received additional subtitles on YouTube and all materials have been organized for easy access on the project webpage - https://climate-map.eu/. The collection includes videos, case studies, and practical tasks showcasing monthly high- and low-tech solutions to climate challenges.
 
- Six perpetual wall calendars were produced in different languages, each featuring monthly climate themes and QR codes linking directly to the online resources. These are freely downloadable and serve as a creative offline gateway to digital tools. 
- A fully functional, visually engaging online Climate Map was developed, offering all materials and calendars with filtering options for easy navigation. It is integrated on the project webpage. 
- The project engaged decision-makers, expanding its audience across the EU, and building a solid foundation for future collaboration and long-term impact.

2023-2-EE01-KA210-ADU-000179098.title: TRAINING: EASY TOOLS FOR FOREIGN LANGUAGES EDUCATORS
2023-2-EE01-KA210-ADU-000179098.summary:
<< Background >>

Based on preliminary research, as well as 15 years of experience in the field of teaching foreign languages ​​and feedback from colleagues who participated in our workshops, we concluded that educators teaching foreign languages ​​to adults lack practical knowledge of using active exercises for work (teaching without a textbook) with adult students.

This opinion was later confirmed by the results of a questionnaire conducted as part of the project. When asked how many books about active methods of teaching foreign languages ​​you know, the majority answered 1-5 books. It means that active methods of teaching foreign languages ​​to adults are in demand.

We decided to create a collection of exercises for the implementation of which there are only 6 simple things available to every teacher: paper, markers, paper tape, scissors, rope and a ball. These items fit easily into a small box and can be kept in the classroom at all times.

To inspire teachers to use the exercises described in the book, we with partners planned workshops (offline and online) and filming video clips where the authors talk about their favorite exercises. These videos were also supposed to open from the book via a QR code.


<< Objectives >>

Our main goal was to create and maintain a European community of foreign language teachers who use active learning methods in the classroom and popularize active learning methods among colleagues. 

We wanted to exchange experience with colleagues from different EU countries on the use of active exercises in foreign language lessons with adult groups.

And also, using synergy, create a new joint collection of exercises that would include 5 types of activity games: energizers (active games), exercises for expanding vocabulary, exercises for consolidating grammar, exercises for communication and exercises for developing writing.

Based on this handbook, we planned to conduct a series of online and offline trainings to inspire EU teachers to put the exercises into practice. 

In order to inspire not only current, but also future colleagues (educators of foreign languages ​​for adults), we planned to film videos with the authors of the exercises, where they would clearly and in detail talk about the most interesting exercises.


<< Implementation >>

This project consisted of 9 activities: 

1. Preparatory meetings. Necessary for preliminary acquaintance and attunement with the direct participants of the project.

2. Preparation of the workshop program. We needed to agree on the typology of exercises, to explore what types of exercises we already have and what types of exercises we would need to develop together. 

3. Conducting workshop in Estonia with partners. Here we directly developed a collection of 100 exercises and games.

4. Training for foreign language educators in Tallinn. International teams presented the exercises to their colleagues in practice. 

5. Production of the training-based video materials. Project participants recorded video instructions for their games.

6. Open online workshop for European educators. To support the community of foreign language teachers from the EU, we shared exercises from the collection.

7. Production of the book for educators. There was editorial work on a selection of exercises and technical layout of the book. 

8. Follow-up meeting. Final feedback from participants. 

9. Project management. To implement a multi-component project, we needed clear project management.


<< Results >>

1) A unique handbook “EASY TOOLS” has been developed, consisting of 100 exercises (65 pages) and games that can be played using only 6 things: paper, markers, a ball, paper tape, rope and scissors. 

You can download the collection here: https://erasmus.gamekeskus.ee/

So far, 440 people have downloaded the book from the site. Then everyone could forward the book to an average of 5-6 colleagues; it can be predicted that about 2,000 teachers are currently actively using the book.

2) 14 videos with the authors were filmed and posted: https://www.youtube.com/@gamekeskus4017/videos

3) A workshop for teachers was held in Tallinn (99 registrations, 60 participants)

4) An online workshop was held for teachers from the EU (393 registrations, 173 participants)

5) Activities were carried out to dissimilate the project
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages
New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2023-2-FR01-KA210-ADU-000180790.title: Iles Durables - Des petites îles européennes mobilisées pour le développement durable de leur territoire

2023-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000170957.title: Advanced doula training
2023-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000170957.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because of the lack of advanced doula training in doula associations in Croatia and Iceland. While doulas from both organisations receive basic training, there was no structured way for them to further develop their skills, especially when supporting traumatic births, pregnancy loss, and survivors of sexual violence. This, combined with the lack of business skills, what we also addressed, led to higher stress and withdrawal from doula roles, leaving communities with less active doulas and those active ones often burnt out.

Additionally, advanced trainings are often too expensive and require travel abroad, making it inaccessible for doulas with often unstable income. 

This project provided free, high-quality training, equipping doulas with essential skills to overcome those challenges while improving the availability of learning through Erasmus+.

By partnering internationally, we combined Croatian expertise in human rights in childbirth and burnout prevention with Icelandic expertise in parent-infant bonding creating a sustainable training model that can be used beyond this project. The project directly addressed the needs of doulas, expectant families, and the wider birth support community.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to support the professional growth of doulas in Croatia and Iceland through the exchange of experiences and best practices which would lead to and be a part of a new Advanced doula training. We aimed to create a curriculum mostly focused on supporting in challenging situations and creating sustainable businesses for doulas. We wanted to implement this free training for actively working doulas of partner organisations, ensuring they gained practical, applicable skills to improve their services and make their business more sustainable.

The plan was to make this curriculum applicable to different cultural contexts, so doulas beyond Croatia and Iceland can benefit from it, especially within future Erasmus+ projects. 

We also wanted to raise awareness about human rights in birth within other birth workers and local communities, increase the visibility of doula work and organisations and create international relationships which would set ground for spreading of this new training to more countries, to upgrade standards of doula profession internationally, for their own empowerment and the wellbeing of the families they support.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented a series of activities:
- Planning sessions: Presidents of both associations held many online meetings to define the steps for each country and prepare materials.
- Needs identification workshop: A psychological workshop brought together Croatian and Icelandic doulas for their first meet-up and identification of needs.
- Two field trips: Doulas traveled to their international partners to gain new competences in which the other team was more skilled. The curriculum, materials, videos and online platform were created in in-person sessions. 
- Training weekends: ADT was carried out simultaneously in Croatia and Iceland, through-out a 8 month period, in which - 60 doulas were trained. Each month was dedicated to one topic which answered participants’ needs with a monthly training weekend, resources on the online platform and homeworks. 
- Workshops for parents: A human rights in birth workshop was held in Croatia and a Rebozo techniques for birth workshop took place in Iceland.
- Project presentations and dissemination: The ADT was presented at the European Doula Network Meeting to promote further adoption. Parents and midwives in both countries were engaged through workshops, presentations, websites, and social media. 

<< Results >>

These are project’s key results:

ADT Curriculum: A structured 8-month program covering human rights in childbirth, trauma-informed support, pregnancy loss, parent-infant bonding, and business skills—designed specifically for doulas using non-formal education methods. 

Educational Materials: Manuals, video lectures, and an online platform were developed for this and future Advanced Doula Trainings.

International Knowledge Exchange: Croatian and Icelandic doulas learned from each other through field trips and workshops, strengthening long-term collaboration.

60 Trained Doulas: Doulas completed ADT (8 training weekends + homeworks), gaining confidence and new skills to better support families and make business sustainable. 12 doulas registered new businesses, 6 of them quit their current jobs. 

Workshops for Parents: Human rights in birth and Rebozo techniques workshops provided parents with free birth preparation.

European Doula Network Presentations: ADT was introduced to a wider audience, encouraging its adoption and Erasmus+ opportunities and achieving the adoption of new education standards.

Sustainable Training Model: The curriculum and materials will continue to be used in future projects for continuous doula education.
topics: Human rights and rule of law

2023-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000174760.title: Sustainable fortifications for seniors learning hub
2023-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000174760.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because it aligned with our shared goals in cultural and heritage management, focusing on the sustainable development of fortified sites and creating engaging programs for adult visitors, especially elderly citizens.  By developing tailored programs for seniors, the project aimed to create meaningful opportunities for their participation in cultural and educational activities. These objectives supported our commitment to inclusive, sustainable, and innovative heritage site management. The project addressed the need to enhance sustainability knowledge and green skills and equipping staff to implement environmentally responsible programs. It also fostered community involvement and lifelong learning for elderly visitors through meaningful activities. By exchanging best practices, the project enhanced inclusivity, impact, and sustainability, transforming heritage sites like the Šibenik fortifications, Rasnov Fortress, and Kaunas fortifications into community learning hubs that promote cultural exchange, environmental awareness, and social engagement. The project also met partner institutions' needs of empowering staff with the skills to deliver sustainable and inclusive programs. 


<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to achieve several key objectives focused on upskilling, networking, and fostering innovation among cultural heritage managers. Our primary goal was to support the development of sustainable, socially inclusive, and green management practices for fortified heritage sites. Specifically, we seeked to create new programs and activities designed to increase the participation and engagement of adult visitors, particularly seniors. Through these efforts, we aimed to promote the inclusion of elderly citizens, empowering them to actively participate in cultural heritage activities while raising their awareness of the important connections between cultural heritage and sustainability. Our main goal was to transform fortified heritage sites into dynamic learning spaces for local communities. We aimed to raise environmental awareness and encourage civic participation, especially among elderly visitors, making these sites centers of lifelong learning and sustainable development. This project was about more than just improving the skills of heritage managers—it was about creating real, lasting change in how communities connect with and benefit from their cultural heritage.

<< Implementation >>

Project partners carried out various activities to ensure effective collaboration, knowledge sharing, and the development of sustainable, inclusive programs for senior citizens at cultural heritage sites. A kick-off meeting was held in the first month to establish readiness and clarify next steps for project execution. Throughout the project, ten online progress meetings facilitated regular monitoring, smooth implementation, and cooperation among partners. On-site hubs were organized in Šibenik, Rasnov, and Kaunas, focusing on cultural engagement, knowledge sharing, and tailored activities for senior citizens. To ensure the project addressed the specific needs of seniors, meetings and surveys with seniors were conducted, with feedback used to refine activities. Three local events in partner regions showcased the project’s results and celebrated the involvement of senior citizens in developed programmes. To secure long-term cooperation, cooperation agreements were formalized with senior associations. One of the most important project outcome was an online brochure “Sustain4Seniors in Cultural Heritage Sites Roadmap”  which documents lessons learned, innovative ideas, and activities to inspire broader adoption.

<< Results >>

The project delivered significant outputs and long-term results aligned with its goal of fostering sustainable and inclusive management of fortified heritage sites. Each partner developed new program for seniors which includes sustainable, inclusive activities, ensuring long-term implementation  Three on-site hubs in Šibenik, Rasnov, and Kaunas facilitated knowledge sharing and cultural engagement. Each partner hosted a final event at the end of the project to present the achieved results to their local communities. These events have showcased and publicly launched the developed programmes and promoted signed agreements with seniors’ associations to ensure the sustainability of newly developed programmes and activities and to present the online project brochure. Online Brochure: The “Sustain4Seniors in Cultural Heritage Sites Roadmap” compiled lessons learned and innovative ideas to inspire other heritage sites. Cooperation Agreements were signed with senior associations guaranteeing the continuation of programs and inclusion of elderly citizens. Partner organizations gained practical expertise in sustainability, green management, and community engagement through peer learning hubs.

2023-2-PL01-KA210-ADU-000179067.title: Empowering adult educators - exchange of best practice for the benefit of local communities
2023-2-PL01-KA210-ADU-000179067.summary:
<< Background >>

The "EmPowerUp" project was created out of motivation to build integrated, active and engaged local communities. The project responded to the needs resulting from the observation of phenomena such as anonymity and isolation in urban space, as well as challenges related to the influx of migrants and refugees, which require new, more inclusive methods of work.

The main needs addressed by the project were:
• The needs of adult education staff (educators, animators), who needed support, new methods and refreshed approaches.
• The needs of adult members of local communities, who often demonstrate passivity and lack of civic engagement, and in the case of new residents, lack of identification with the place of residence. The project aimed to strengthen their civic competences and sense of initiative.
• The needs of partner organizations, striving to develop the competences of their employees, exchange best practices and contribute to the implementation of the vision of lifelong learning and social inclusion.
To meet these needs, the project focused on equipping educators with practical work methods, such as Neighbourhood Activity Zones, storytelling, SELcoaching and participatory art.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal was to strengthen and develop the competences of adult education staff – educators, animators and leaders. It was assumed that their personal, social, creative, linguistic and learning competences would be improved.

The project aimed to equip educators with various, practical methods of working with local communities, including in the context of working with groups of diverse nationalities, migrants and refugees. These methods included Neighbourhood Activity Zones, storytelling, SELcoaching and participatory art.

By developing the competences of educators, the project was to have a positive impact on adult members of local communities, strengthening their civic competences and sense of initiative. The aim was to create more engaged, competent and active societies.

Additional goals included transferring the acquired knowledge to other educators in institutions, social organisations and ensuring social inclusion through citizen participation. In the long term, we planned to include the methods learned in the organisation's permanent offer.

<< Implementation >>

The first activity was a training workshop for trainers, which took place in Bulgaria. Its aim was to exchange and learn the best methods of working with local communities used by each partner. The workshop was attended by 11 educators, animators and leaders from partner institutions, who strengthened their competences and acquired new tools.

The second activity concerned the creation of a guide with practical tips. This guide was a practical description of the work methods presented at the workshop, available in PDF format, translated into the languages ​​of the partners and English. Its aim was to make the new methods available to a wide group of educators in Europe.

The third activity was to organize a Neighborhood Forum in Poland, in Łódź. The aim was to practically apply and test the learned methods of working directly with the local community and to disseminate the project results among other professionals from the adult education sector.

The last activity was project management. It included all necessary administrative and communication tasks, such as regular online meetings, preparation of contracts, risk management, reporting and dissemination of information about the project and its results.

<< Results >>

The project results include primarily:
- Training of 11 educators, animators, leaders from partner organizations - Participants were equipped with new methods of working with diverse communities.
- Development of a guide with work methods (PDF in 5 languages).
- Organization of a Neighborhood Forum with the participation of approx. 70 people - The Forum enabled practical application of the methods learned and dissemination of the project results, supporting cooperation and networking.
- Practical implementation of the methods learned in local work, in partner countries, which enabled integration and stimulation of civic activity of adult members of local communities (residents)
- Talks between the VVI Foundation and the city of Sofia on the creation of Local Activity Spaces.
- Implementation of the methods learned in Łódź in the new place of activity of the VVI Foundation.
- For the STREFA Foundation - the first experience of participation and coordination of an international project resulted in gaining new skills and strengthening language competences

2023-2-PL01-KA210-ADU-000181890.title: CLIMATE FOR READING
2023-2-PL01-KA210-ADU-000181890.summary:
<< Background >>

The "Climate For Reading" project complemented and expanded the existing activities of the partner libraries, addressing the important issue of promoting reading among adults in the context of growing secondary illiteracy and the consequent need to develop key competencies. Reading is the foundation of education – there's no doubt about that. Libraries from four European countries participated in the project: Croatia, Norway, Poland, and Slovenia, which jointly explored ways to reach the target group. The project's main goal was (and still is) to promote reading, raise its standards, and thus educate intelligent, creative, engaged, and responsible citizens who actively participate in democratic life.

<< Objectives >>

The project's main goal was (and remains) to promote reading, raise its standards, and thus educate intelligent, creative, engaged, and responsible citizens who actively participate in democratic life. Other goals:
- exchanging experiences within an international project group on promoting reading among adults,
- developing scenarios to facilitate reaching identified groups of adults who do not read or read sporadically,
- conducting workshops to strengthen educators' skills in effective reading promotion,
- developing key competencies,
- promoting modern technologies for promoting reading,
- conducting a debate on the role of contemporary libraries in modern society,
- integrating the library community and improving language skills.

<< Implementation >>

The project included four transnational project meetings, which included the exchange of best practices, educational workshops, scenarios of action for selected target groups were jointly developed, a debate on the role of contemporary libraries in modern society, and the promotion of local cultural heritage.
Furthermore, to implement the acquired knowledge and skills, a series of local activities were conducted, involving 55 librarians/educators. Project results were ensured to become part of regular library practice. Transparent project management principles were implemented to ensure high-quality project implementation.

<< Results >>

The project improved access to cultural and educational content for the following groups: men, migrants, people with reading difficulties (e.g., dyslexia), and seniors. New, implementable, and replicable action plans were created for the aforementioned groups of non-readers and occasional readers:
-	„How to attract men to reading and to the library“
-	„Migrants as adult non-readers” 
-	„Engaging seniors in library: best practices“
-	“"Reading for All” – Inclusive Library Initiatives for Adults with Reading Challenges". 
Six workshops were held to strengthen educators' skills in effective reading promotion. New technologies were popularized to facilitate access to library resources. Practices were developed and implemented to include new groups of readers, and key competencies were developed. Two videos were created, along with four articles on EPALE, in the magazins, and online. An open debate was held on the role of contemporary libraries in modern society. The library community was integrated and language skills improved. 
The results are sustainable, embedded in practice, publicly available through various channels, easily communicated, and maintained by experienced educators.

2023-2-RS01-KA210-ADU-000185109.title: Educational response to improve finding missing children
2023-2-RS01-KA210-ADU-000185109.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the RESPONSE project to address the urgent need for better education, awareness, and community response in cases of missing children. The project targets adults, especially parents, who often lack the knowledge and tools needed to act effectively when a child goes missing. It also involves the wider community, which needs clear guidance on how to provide support, and the media, which plays a key role in disseminating accurate and timely information.

Our motivation stems from the lack of efficient policies and public preparedness in both Serbia and Croatia, despite growing efforts to establish child alert systems. The project directly supports the launch and implementation of Serbia’s new child alert system PRONAĐI ME and aligns with advocacy efforts in Croatia.

By educating adults, raising public awareness, and promoting cross-sector collaboration, RESPONSE contributes to a safer environment for children. It strengthens prevention, builds local capacities, and helps ensure swift and coordinated action when children go missing.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the RESPONSE project was to improve learning opportunities across all generations by focusing on the issue of missing children and the importance of a child alert system. Through this, we aimed to enhance awareness, preparedness, and education among adults, especially parents, on how to act swiftly and effectively in such cases.

Specifically, we wanted to achieve two key objectives:

1. To educate and inform adults by organizing educational sessions and creating accessible resources (brochures, videos, handbooks) that equip them with the necessary knowledge and skills to respond appropriately in cases of missing children, including how to use the child alert system.

2. To raise public awareness, especially among parents, about the issue of missing children and the importance of early, coordinated community response.

Ultimately, the project aimed to empower adults and community members to play an active role in child protection by strengthening their capacities to prevent and react in crisis situations.

<< Implementation >>

The RESPONSE project began with the development of a tailored educational package for adults on the topic of missing children. Two three-day workshops were held—one in Osijek and one in Novi Sad—with participation of experts from both countries (5 from Serbia and 5 from Croatia), including psychologists, social workers, educators, and communication officers. As a result, we produced two educational videos, a brochure, and a guideline designed for use in adult education, primarily targeting parents.

More than 20 educational sessions were conducted in various locations in Serbia and Croatia. Dissemination activities included the distribution of brochures, active use of social media, and public street actions in Osijek and Novi Sad to mark International Missing Children's Day.

Two final conferences were organized, one in each country, to present project results and raise awareness about the issue of missing children and the importance of child alert systems. To ensure smooth cooperation, two partner meetings were held (kick-off in Novi Sad and final in Osijek), while regular coordination took place online via email, Zoom, and Google Workspace.

<< Results >>

The RESPONSE project significantly improved awareness and preparedness among adults, especially parents, regarding missing children and the importance of child alert systems. Through educational sessions conducted in cooperation with schools, social welfare centers, and local institutions, over 400 adults were informed and empowered to respond effectively in critical situations. These sessions promoted stronger community engagement and fostered intersectoral dialogue. Representatives of the police took part in the final project conference, contributing to a panel discussion that encouraged cross-sectoral learning and collaboration.

The project strengthened cooperation between the two partner organizations: Center for Missing and Exploited Children from Serbia and from Croatia, both dedicated to the issue of missing persons. By exchanging experiences and practices and jointly developing educational materials, both organizations improved their capacities to support communities and institutions more effectively. RESPONSE created a foundation for sustainable cross-border cooperation in protecting children and raising public awareness.

2023-2-SI01-KA210-ADU-000185203.title: Knjižnica spreminja svet
2023-2-SI01-KA210-ADU-000185203.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We strengthen international partnership, connect libraries, facilitate exchange and circulation of knowledge, ideas, practices and experience of professional staff, develop competencies of employees, improve the quality of adult education in libraries, and spread positive influences in the local, regional and national area. We encourage learning people to make positive changes in the areas of green literacy, sustainable development, climate change, biodiversity, healthy lifestyle and well-being.

<< Implementation >>

We will select 12 good, innovative adult education practices from the participating libraries, test them, evaluate them, improve them and present them in a freely accessible e-manual. For the successful implementation of the project, we will hold 7 online meetings, a live preparatory meeting, 4 mobilities, 4 final conferences and many dissemination activities. We will include interested target groups of adult learners in the testing of good practices and show how libraries can change the world.

We will create a publicly available e-manual of innovative practices, a teaching material with described practices, work methods, procedures, necessities, literature. With the implemented activities we will support sustainable development,  green strategies and curricula for the future of adult education, which will effect society.

2024-1-DE02-KA210-ADU-000251246.title: Planting Stories - Self-Directed Learning Pathways
2024-1-DE02-KA210-ADU-000251246.summary:

We aim to create 10 "Planting Stories Self-Directed Learning Pathways -  that enhance the relationship between individuals and household plants, transforming the care and development of these plants into a learning pathway.
