2024-1-FI01-KA210-ADU-000248540.title: Sharing innovative approaches that support adults living with Mental hEalth coNditions and Their fAmiLy CAREgivers in Europe
2024-1-FI01-KA210-ADU-000248540.summary:
<< Background >>

MENTAL-CARE was conceived in response to a critical need in European mental health care. We applied for the MENTAL-CARE project to address gaps in cooperation and communication among mental health users, professionals, and family members in Europe. Although they share recovery goals, ineffective communication, limited shared decision-making, and weak collaboration often undermine outcomes, increase relapse risk, and contribute to caregiver and professional burnout.

In Croatia, Finland, Greece, and Spain, collaborative practices require closer evaluation, and evidence-based communication strategies are not consistently implemented. Families frequently lack sufficient support, while professionals face high workloads and emotional strain.

MENTAL-CARE addressed these challenges by assessing current practices, strengthening communication through international workshops in Croatia and Belgium, and aligning findings with research evidence.

Key outputs included a comprehensive Good Practices Guide, educational sessions in 2025, and awareness events during European Mental Health Week 2026. These actions promoted more collaborative, recovery-oriented, and sustainable mental health systems.

<< Objectives >>

The MENTAL-CARE project aimed to strengthen structured cooperation and effective communication among mental health users, professionals, and family members to improve recovery outcomes and system sustainability.

1) Improving quality of life
We promoted recovery-oriented, person-centered practices that enhance autonomy, social inclusion, participation, and shared decision-making for adults with mental health conditions.

2) Strengthening communication skills
We developed practical competencies—active listening, empathy, clarity, and constructive dialogue—across all three groups to reduce misunderstandings and improve coordinated care.

3) Preventing relapse and burnout
We sought to reduce illness recurrence, caregiver burnout, and family distress by clarifying roles, fostering early intervention, and supporting resilient care partnerships.

4) Enhancing professional satisfaction
We improved collaborative capacities and therapeutic relationships, contributing to better teamwork, lower stress, and higher job satisfaction among professionals.

5) Ensuring sustainable impact
We produced a comprehensive Guide integrating research and project findings;  practical tools to institutionalize effective cooperat. in recovery orientation.

<< Implementation >>

The MENTAL-CARE project delivered research, training, and awareness activities to strengthen cooperation among mental health users, professionals, and families.
We developed the Good Practices Guide: Supporting Adults with Mental Health Conditions and Their Family Caregivers in Europe, accompanied by video materials, providing practical recommendations for recovery-oriented collaboration.
A learning activity at the University Hospital Vrapče in Zagreb included study visits to rehabilitation day centers, showcasing community-based mental health practices. A second learning activity in Stockholm, organized with EUFAMI, focused on improving communication and cooperation through interactive workshops.
National awareness events were held in Finland (6.5.26), Greece (20.5-24.5.26), Spain (7.5.26), and Croatia (19.5.26) during European Mental Health Week/month to disseminate results and promote dialogue.
The project began with a hybrid Kick-Off Meeting and workshop on World Mental Health Day.

Guide Practices Guide activity includes:  A structured literature review; identification and documentation of good practices; accompanying video illustrations; integration of insights from all three stakeholder groups  

<< Results >>

1) Scientific publication and Good Practices Guide
University Hospital Vrapče prepared a literature-based review article submitted to Social Psychiatry and shared with stakeholders. It forms the introduction to the Good Practices Guide: Supporting Adults with Mental Health Conditions and Their Family Caregivers in Europe, a key project output providing practical recommendations for collaborative, recovery-oriented care.
2) Educational videos
Partners in Croatia and Spain produced recovery-oriented videos featuring professionals, family members, and individuals with lived experience. All partners contributed to script development and review.
3) Learning activities
The Zagreb learning activity strengthened knowledge, communication skills, and exchange among professionals, families, and users from Croatia, Spain, Finland, and Greece.
The EUFAMI learning activity increased awareness of family carers’ challenges, improved understanding of EU policies, strengthened European networks, and included review of the draft Guide and videos.
4) Awareness events
Events during European Mental Health Week in 4 countries raised awareness of family support, community-based services, and good practices in soc. psyc., encouraging in cult. exchange.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2024-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000252783.title: From Burnout to Balance: Supporting Educators' Well-Being
2024-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000252783.summary:
<< Background >>

Le projet a été conçu en réponse aux profondes transformations du système éducatif et à l’augmentation du stress professionnel observée chez les enseignants et formateurs, amplifiée par la pandémie. Les partenaires ont identifié des besoins communs liés au manque d’outils pour gérer le stress, soutenir la santé mentale et promouvoir le bien-être au travail. Dans plusieurs établissements, les équipes éducatives faisaient face à la surcharge psychologique, à la difficulté de concilier vie professionnelle et personnelle, ainsi qu’à un sentiment de dévalorisation du métier. Le projet a visé à combler ces lacunes en développant des ressources et des pratiques de soutien adaptées aux contextes locaux et européens. À travers des mobilités d’apprentissage et des ateliers collaboratifs organisés en France, en Espagne et en Croatie, le partenariat a permis aux participants d’acquérir de nouvelles compétences, d’échanger des expériences et de renforcer une culture éducative fondée sur le bien-être, la collaboration et la résilience. Il a également favorisé la création de réseaux européens durables entre établissements engagés dans la promotion de la santé psychologique et de la qualité de vie au travail dans l’éducation.

<< Objectives >>

Le projet visait à améliorer la gestion du stress et le bien-être des enseignants, formateurs et personnels éducatifs, conformément aux priorités européennes de développement professionnel et de santé mentale au travail. Les partenaires ont cherché à créer et à mettre en œuvre des programmes de soutien offrant des ressources, outils et stratégies pratiques pour prévenir l’épuisement professionnel. Les objectifs principaux étaient de former le personnel éducatif à la gestion du stress par des activités individuelles et collectives, de favoriser la diffusion des savoirs acquis au sein des établissements et de renforcer la coopération entre enseignants, formateurs, experts en santé mentale et organisations professionnelles. Le projet a permis d’accroître la sensibilisation aux questions de santé psychologique, d’améliorer la capacité à identifier et gérer les signes de burnout, de renforcer la communication avec les spécialistes et de consolider des réseaux européens favorisant la collaboration et l’échange de bonnes pratiques dans le domaine du bien-être éducatif.

<< Implementation >>

La mise en œuvre du projet s’est appuyée sur une gestion continue et une communication étroite entre les partenaires tout au long du projet. Ces deux dimensions transversales ont garanti la coordination efficace, le suivi administratif et la diffusion constante des résultats. Le projet a débuté par une réunion de lancement en Croatie, au cours de laquelle les partenaires ont défini la méthodologie commune de formation et harmonisé les objectifs pédagogiques. Deux sessions « Train the Trainers » ont ensuite eu lieu en Espagne et en France, rassemblant des enseignants, formateurs et experts des trois organisations partenaires. L’activité de coaching et de mentorat, initialement prévue sur six mois, a été adaptée en raison des contraintes d’emploi du temps des enseignants des trois pays. Les partenaires ont donc mis en place des ateliers locaux (séances de yoga, relaxation, workshops en établissement, cafés pédagogiques), deux webinaires internationaux animés par des experts européens et un événement final en ligne. Cette approche collaborative et inclusive a renforcé les échanges interculturels, stimulé l’innovation pédagogique et posé les bases d’un réseau européen durable pour la promotion du bien-être dans l’éducation.

<< Results >>

Le projet a généré plusieurs résultats concrets et durables. L’un des principaux produits a été le Rapport d’évaluation sur le stress et le burnout des enseignants et formateurs, élaboré à partir d’un sondage mené dans les trois pays partenaires. Ce document a permis d’identifier les besoins réels du personnel éducatif et a servi de base à la conception des contenus et programmes de formation développés dans le cadre du projet. Les sessions « Train the Trainers » en Espagne et en France ont formé des groupes d’enseignants et formateurs, tout en produisant des supports pédagogiques et des ressources numériques mises à disposition sur le site du projet. Deux webinaires internationaux ont favorisé l’échange d’expériences entre experts européens et la création d’une communauté d’apprentissage active. Les ateliers locaux, combinant relaxation, coaching et mentorat, ont renforcé la mise en pratique des compétences acquises et la cohésion des équipes, donnant lieu à un rapport de synthèse rassemblant les pratiques et contenus développés dans les trois pays. Le projet a enfin diffusé une culture de bien-être et de collaboration durable, dont les résultats continuent d’être exploités et partagés au sein des réseaux éducatifs européens.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2024-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000252961.title: Connecting Inhabitants to Rural Culture
2024-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000252961.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to promote training in rural heritage for stakeholders in the cultural sphere. The goal is to use it as a training tool so that everyone can learn from rural heritage. The project aims to promote the acquisition of knowledge about rural heritage for both rural and urban residents. It aims to establish an intercultural dialogue to encourage the sharing of good practice and foster a sense of European identity.

<< Implementation >>

The project is built around two central areas of work. The first is the training of stakeholders in the cultural sphere, through the sharing of good practices discovered through mobility, and the enhancement and preservation of heritage. The second is to educate rural and urban populations about rural heritage, to raise public awareness of it and make it accessible to all, by holding Heritage Days and disseminating this heritage on a local and European scale.

<< Results >>

The project aims to change the mentality of target groups in the long term through activities and the sharing of good practices, and to strengthen cultural policies. The project aims to reduce the divide surrounding rural heritage, in order to develop public and professional knowledge, and thus make it a central element in the connection between local people and their territory. Enhancing the value of this heritage and disseminating this knowledge is therefore the main expected outcome.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2024-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000245070.title: Blended Learning in adult education: improved Online&Offline teaching Methods for better employability and active citizenship 5.0
2024-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000245070.summary:
<< Background >>

The project responds to clearly identified needs in adult education, especially after the COVID-19 pandemic, which highlighted the lack of quality and flexible learning opportunities, particularly in native-language content. A gap in digital skills was identified among adults—especially older people, the unemployed, NEETs, and persons with disabilities—limiting their access to the labor market, public e-services, and active participation in society.

At the same time, partner organizations needed to strengthen their capacities in digital pedagogy and blended learning to ensure high-quality, practical programs for target groups.

The project addressed these needs by developing inclusive and flexible digital skills programs and training educators in modern teaching methods. This improved access to lifelong learning and increased active citizenship. Transnational cooperation enabled knowledge exchange, innovative content development, and adaptation to diverse users, ensuring higher quality and long-term sustainability of results.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to improve the quality and accessibility of adult education in digital skills through transnational cooperation, with a particular focus on people with fewer opportunities.
Specifically, the project had two key objectives. The first was to strengthen the capacities of partner organizations by developing educators’ competences in digital pedagogy and the use of IT tools in teaching, thereby improving existing and creating new educational programs.
The second objective was to develop and implement innovative blended learning programs for adults, enabling them to acquire digital skills needed for employability and active citizenship.
By achieving these goals, the project contributed to greater inclusion, improved access to lifelong learning, and strengthened digital competences among target groups such as older adults, the unemployed, persons with disabilities, and NEETs.

<< Implementation >>

Workshops on digital pedagogy and the use of IT tools in teaching were conducted, followed by the development of internal plans for the digital transformation of educational programs. Knowledge transfer workshops for other organizations were also organized, along with pilot and blended learning programs for target groups (digital skills for active citizenship, basic and advanced IT skills).
Three digital manuals for educators and learners were developed, jointly created, translated, and made publicly available through e-learning systems. In addition, two functional e-learning platforms were established and integrated into partners’ websites, incorporating elements of digital accessibility and enabling access to educational content as well as support for blended learning.
Project management and dissemination activities were carried out in parallel, including partner coordination, evaluation, and promotion of project results.

<< Results >>

Educators from partner organizations were trained in digital pedagogy and the use of IT tools in teaching, and two internal plans for the digital transformation of educational programs were developed. Knowledge was transferred to partner organizations through joint workshops.

Two functional e-learning systems were established, providing access to educational materials and supporting blended learning. Both partners finalized three planned online courses, while TICM developed an additional course on the use of smartphones.

Three digital manuals for educators (digital skills for active citizenship, basic and advanced IT skills) were developed, made available in multiple languages, and publicly published via e-learning systems.

A total of 9 (planned 8) blended learning programs were implemented for 94 participants (planned 46), improving their digital skills.

The project contributed to greater accessibility of flexible and inclusive adult education programs, as well as long-term sustainability through publicly available materials and e-learning tools.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2024-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000253810.title: Zaboravljena generacija - ne zaboravite učiti!
2024-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000253810.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we recognized the “forgotten generation” – older people and persons with disabilities who are often excluded from lifelong learning. While children and youth encounter climate change topics in schools, older adults rarely have such opportunities, especially in rural and isolated areas. Many feel insecure, believing they lack the knowledge to understand complex processes, yet they leave the largest carbon footprint and at the same time suffer the most from climate impacts – from heatwaves to extreme weather events.
Through our work in Eko Brezna and the local community, we saw how much older people wish to be included, but lack accessible and tailored educational programs. That is why we designed a program that explains climate issues in a simple and understandable way, while also linking climate literacy with health, financial, media, and digital literacy. With this project, we aimed to restore their sense of value and contribution, empower them to become active members of society, and encourage them to pass new knowledge on to younger generations. Their role in tackling climate change is equally important – and must not be forgotten.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to increase the climate literacy of older adults and persons with disabilities (PwD), who are often excluded from education and highly vulnerable to climate impacts. We developed a non-formal learning programme that connects climate literacy with everyday life skills (health, finance, media, digital literacy) to provide practical tools for decision-making. An important goal was to introduce innovative andragogical methods: we tested the “Climate Fresk” and created our own climate cards adapted to older adults and PwD, enabling learning through play and discussion.
We also aimed to train educators to work with this target group and ensure delivery of workshops directly in local communities. Through a strong media outreach (radio, TV, articles, videos, picture book), we reached those unable to attend in person. Strengthening partner capacities and building a cross-border cooperation network were key priorities.
Ultimately, the goal was to empower older adults and PwD to become active participants, to share climate knowledge within their families — especially with younger generations — and to ensure they are recognised as relevant contributors in climate change adaptation.

<< Implementation >>

Throughout the project, we carried out activities focused on improving the climate literacy of older adults and persons with disabilities (PwD). We started with a needs assessment survey involving 278 respondents, which served as the basis for developing the education program for the target group and the Training of Trainers (ToT). A ToT was implemented for 13 participants from 9 organizations, and innovative learning tools were developed – after testing the “Climate Fresk” method, we created our own climate cards fully adapted to older adults and PwD.
A total of 14 workshops were held in Croatia and Serbia, engaging more than 130 participants. The workshops also served as a pilot for evaluating and adjusting the methodology based on user feedback.
To ensure a wide outreach, total of over 100 educational and informative media outputs were produced (radio, TV and newspaper, video materials) 23 EPALE articles, accompanied by more than 170 social media posts and 70+ website publications. Furthermore, 12 round tables and both an opening and a final conference were organized. All materials were published online (websites, social media, YouTube, EPALE), securing strong visibility and long-term sustainability of project results.

<< Results >>

The project delivered concrete and measurable results. A needs assessment was conducted and used to develop the climate literacy education programme, the ToT curriculum, the climate literacy handbook and the trainers’ manual. A ToT was carried out for 13 participants from 9 organisations; all completed their practical teaching during workshops and received certificates. We developed an innovative educational tool – climate cards – tested during 14 workshops in Croatia and Serbia with more than 130 older adults/PwDs, increasing their climate, health, financial, media and digital literacy.
A substantial number of educational outputs were produced and published: 43 radio reports, 2 TV reports, 5 newspaper articles, 10 video materials, 26 social media posts, 26 website posts and 23 articles published on the EPALE platform, as well as a picture book and digital handbooks. 12 round tables and both opening and closing conferences were organised.
Beyond tangible outputs, the project increased older adults’ confidence and motivation, strengthened partners’ capacities and fostered a sustainable cooperation network that will continue educational activities after the project’s completion.

2024-1-HU01-KA210-ADU-000251940.title: Healing nature and mind through land art
2024-1-HU01-KA210-ADU-000251940.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to promote environmental awareness and mental well-being by integrating land art and nature therapy elements, enhancing community cohesion and creativity in rural areas both on local and transnational levels. Objectives include cultural exchanges and knowledge transfer among participating and supporting organisations to implement land art and nature therapy practices. For long-lasting impact, activities will be integrated into local eco-touristic strategies.

<< Implementation >>

Activities include study visits in Croatia and Hungary, transnational workshops about land art and nature therapy, handbook creation and municipal strategy alignment, community planning of land art sculptures in 2 Hungarian villages, a land art and photo exhibition, plus an accompanying transnational conference in Hungary about integrating land art into nature therapy.

<< Results >>

Expected results include trainers skilled in land art and nature therapy, successful land art installations enhancing rural landscapes and eco-touristic offers of participating rural villages, improved community well-being and environmental consciousness, increased cultural exchange, and a sustainable model for integrating art with nature conservation and mental health promotion.
topics: Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas

2024-1-LT01-KA210-ADU-000254733.title: Stressed Out, Chill Out: Finding common mechanisms to reduce stress, increase positivity and overcome work- related anxiety through digital sharing and mobility exchanges for Women Professionals
2024-1-LT01-KA210-ADU-000254733.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for SOCO to address the urgent need for accessible, inclusive support for migrant women across Europe especially Ukrainian, facing high stress, anxiety, and social isolation while adapting to new countries. These women experience emotional disconnection, digital exclusion, and limited access to culturally appropriate mental wellbeing resources.
We created a low-threshold digital learning environment focused on stress reduction, mindfulness, and resilience building. Our approach promoted peer support and digital literacy as key empowerment tools. Through 12 multilingual learning modules, a digital guidebook, and structured collaboration between partners in Lithuania, Croatia, and Greece, we helped women overcome inclusion barriers.
SOCO enabled participants to develop coping strategies, connect with peers facing similar challenges, and access culturally sensitive support. We strengthened cooperation between adult education providers, supported community engagement, and fostered digital transformation in adult learning. Our comprehensive approach empowered migrant women with practical tools to build resilience, enhance digital skills, and thrive in their new environments across Europe.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to create meaningful support for migrant women, especially Ukrainian refugees, who were struggling with stress and isolation while adapting to new lives across Europe. Many of these women lacked access to culturally appropriate mental health resources and faced barriers connecting with their new communities.Our goal was to develop practical, accessible digital learning tools focusing on stress management, mindfulness, and building resilience. We created 12 multilingual modules in total covering mental health awareness, work-life balance, and active citizenship that women could access at their own pace. Through partnerships in Lithuania, Croatia, and Greece, we piloted these resources with 40 diverse participants, gathering feedback to improve content and usability. We wanted to foster peer connections, helping women share experiences and support each other through similar challenges.Beyond individual support, we strengthened cooperation between adult education providers and contribute evidence-based approaches for supporting displaced populations. We created sustainable resources that other organizations could adapt and use via digital platforms.

<< Implementation >>

Throughout the SOCO project, we implemented a structured series of activities following our approved operational plan. We began with project management setup, monthly virtual coordination meetings, and clear role distribution. A virtual kick-off meeting launched the project, followed by a gap analysis and stakeholder research to identify key needs of migrant women. These findings informed the first SOCO Lab in Athens, where we co-designed the SOCO platform, developed the initial learning scenarios, and drafted the guidebook. Feedback was gathered and used to refine materials. The second SOCO Lab focused on updating the teaching scenarios, validating results through surveys, and preparing the final dissemination package. We piloted the modules in all partner countries and engaged participants in evaluation. Finally, we hosted the SOCO Workshop in Lithuania to present the finalized modules, digital guidebook, and case studies, and to gather final feedback before submission of our final report.


<< Results >>

The SOCO project produced several key outputs aligned with our objectives. We developed and piloted twelve digital learning modules on stress management, resilience, digital wellbeing, and civic participation, each available in English, Croatian, Lithuanian, and Greek. A comprehensive SOCO Digital Guidebook was created for educators and facilitators, summarizing our approach, learning scenarios, and best practices. We conducted one in-person and one online SOCO Lab (Croatia and Greece) and one final dissemination workshop in Lithuania, involving over 60 migrant women a majority of which were Ukrainian. We also created a shared digital workspace, ran structured validation surveys, and collected feedback to improve our materials. Dissemination was carried out through social media, EPALE blogs, and community networks, ensuring wide visibility and open access to all resources. The project strengthened cooperation between adult education providers and improved partner capacities in digital learning and inclusive outreach. All outputs were made available in the SOCO digital hub, where all project results were collected in one place, making them convenient and practical.

2024-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000243624.title: Putevi inkluzivnog učenja: prilagođavanje programa obrazovanja odraslih za osobe sa stečenim motoročkim smetnjama
2024-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000243624.summary:
<< Background >>

The Qualifications Agency, through the competences of the PROAEA Center, approves the status of a publicly recognized organizer of adult education activities, if the conditions in terms of personnel, space, equipment and teaching resources are met. One of the elements of the program relates to accessibility for people with disabilities. We applied for the project in order to point out the possibility of adapting adult education programs for people with acquired motor disabilities, as well as the need to help adult education service providers adapt training to the specific needs of PWDs through a manual with guidelines. In order to create as comprehensive a manual as possible, we connected with partners with many years of experience in relevant fields such as defectology, special education, information technology and training and employment of (persons with disabilities) PWDs. The target group, i.e. people with acquired motor disabilities, was selected because this type of disability requires the least adjustments, which we consider a good starting point for the improvement of inclusive educational practices.

<< Objectives >>

The project envisions a transformative impact on various key stakeholders, addressing the urgent need for inclusiveness practice in adult education, particularly focusing on individuals with acquired motor disabilities. Specialized training for adult educators/trainers to improve competencies in inclusive teaching methodologies is aligned with
with the priority "Improving the competencies of educators and other personnel involved in education and leadership". The initiative is indirectly aimed at adult students with acquired motor disabilities, with the aim of removing obstacles in education (theme: disability), improve accessibility and improve their employability (theme: employability). Directly by addressing the needs of this specific demographic, the project aligns with the overarching priority of “Inclusion and diversity in all areas of education, training, youth and sports". The strategy implies the adaptation of existing programs, providing a tailored approach that takes into account the unique requirements of persons with motor disabilities. 

<< Implementation >>

The project encompassed a series of structured activities, including coordination meetings aimed at defining the implementation plan and delegating responsibilities among project teams. A comparative analysis of the educational and legislative frameworks of the three participating countries was conducted to ensure relevance and adaptability. Based on these findings, a training manual applicable across all partner countries was developed. Info-sessions were organized to raise awareness about the needs of persons with disabilities (PWDs) and to gather valuable feedback from potential users of the manual, which was then integrated into its final version. Lastly, the project results and the finalized manual were promoted to relevant stakeholders and interested parties to support broader dissemination and impact.

<< Results >>

The project resulted in several concrete outcomes, beginning with the establishment of a clearly defined framework for collaboration through the initial meeting, which clarified roles, responsibilities, and expectations among partners. Expert consultations provided practical insights into inclusive education tailored to the needs of adults with acquired motor disabilities, which were translated into actionable guidelines and strategies for future activities. Continuous stakeholder engagement, particularly with advocacy groups, ensured that feedback guided the refinement of project approaches, keeping them aligned with real-world needs. Crucially, individuals with lived experience were actively involved, ensuring that the project was co-created with those directly affected. As a result, the project not only produced practical tools but also raised awareness within local communities, fostering broader dialogue and long-term commitment to inclusive education practices.

2024-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000244829.title: InclusiGardens: Digital and Sustainable Pathways to Social Inclusion through Urban Gardening
2024-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000244829.summary:
<< Background >>

InclusiGardens responded to the social exclusion and food insecurity faced by vulnerable urban adults - unemployed, low-income and low-skilled people and other marginalised residents - who often lack access to green spaces, affordable fresh food and inclusive, practical learning opportunities. At the same time, free, accessible and multilingual adult-education resources on sustainable urban gardening were scarce, and many adult educators lacked ready-made, inclusive materials on the topic. We applied for the project to address these needs together: to give disadvantaged adults low-cost, hands-on skills to grow their own micro-gardens for self-sufficiency, food security and wellbeing, and to equip educators with open, reusable resources. A transnational partnership between Slovenia, Croatia and the Netherlands allowed us to combine permaculture, adult-education and digital-design expertise and to reach a far wider European audience than any single organisation could alone.

<< Objectives >>

Through InclusiGardens we set out to: (1) promote social inclusion, accessibility and equal opportunities for vulnerable urban adults; (2) create free, open and multilingual digital education resources on sustainable urban micro-gardening that are genuinely tailored to their needs; (3) build the green and digital skills of both learners and adult educators; (4) use innovative, inclusive methods - including gamification, serious games and hands-on workshops - to engage groups that usually face barriers to participation; and (5) contribute to the green transition and the fight against climate change by spreading sustainable, low-cost, zero-waste gardening and cooking practices. Alongside these learner-facing aims, we wanted to strengthen the three partners' own capacities in inclusive adult education, digital content creation, gamification and Erasmus+ project management, and to build lasting cross-border cooperation that could support future joint initiatives across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented six interconnected activities between December 2024 and May 2026. A1 covered project management, coordination, monitoring and evaluation, including 18 online meetings and two transnational partner meetings. A2 created the InclusiGardens Digital Hub and ran a continuous, hybrid dissemination campaign. A3 produced a five-module e-Toolkit on sustainable urban micro-gardening, informed by focus groups. A4 developed a 30-recipe Zero Waste Micro-Garden e-Cookbook. A5 produced inclusive gamification strategies, an expert roundtable, five game scenarios and four serious educational games. A6 synthesised all results into the Empowering Urban Micro-Gardeners Curriculum, piloted through workshop series in Slovenia, Croatia and the Netherlands. The activities were carried out across the three partner countries, and every output intended for the public was published openly online in all four project languages - English, Slovenian, Croatian and Dutch.

<< Results >>

The project delivered the InclusiGardens Digital Hub (8,200+ visitors against a target of 1,000; 11,100+ page views; 20 posts on the project website); a five-module e-Toolkit (560+ downloads); a 30-recipe Zero Waste e-Cookbook (900+ downloads); inclusive Gamification Strategies with five game scenarios (530+ downloads); and the Empowering Urban Micro-Gardeners Curriculum (530+ downloads). As added value beyond the application, the partners created four serious educational games - three digital games on the Hub and one print-ready card game, 'Windowsill Wonders' (180+ downloads). Engagement included 18 co-creation focus groups with 87 in-person and 34 online participants (121 in total), an expert roundtable with five experts, and three pilot workshop series across the three countries. A hybrid dissemination campaign - social media, four newsletters (1,410+ downloads), printed flyers, in-person events, EPALE posts and other channels - reached an estimated 75,000+ people. All public resources remain free and open in four languages.

2024-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000253396.title: INSPIRE: Inclusive Narratives Shaping Perspectives - Integrating Real-life Experiences
2024-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000253396.summary:
<< Background >>

We identified a need for a systemic, interdisciplinary and digitally supported improvement in the understanding of disability, contributing to greater awareness and a more inclusive society. Persons with disabilities still face discrimination, stigma, social exclusion and a lack of adapted approaches, often due to insufficient understanding. Through the project, we addressed the need for:
- greater inclusion of persons with disabilities in society, based on their active participation,
- development of innovative education and awareness-raising approaches that better reach end users through a stronger emphasis on visual, especially video-based methods. Visual storytelling supports understanding of complex content, while personal narratives foster empathy and provide insight into lived experiences and needs of persons with disabilities,
- connecting experts from different fields (social work, psychology, healthcare) to develop more holistic and effective approaches to disability,
- promoting green practices among persons with disabilities, who are often overlooked in environmental policies, despite equal rights and potential to actively contribute to the sustainable transformation of society.

<< Objectives >>

Through the project, we aimed to improve the understanding, treatment and inclusion of persons with disabilities in society. The main project objectives were:
- to improve understanding of disability, challenges and needs of persons with disabilities, thereby contributing to a more inclusive and empathetic society,
- to increase social awareness of disability and reduce stigma and discrimination,
- to contribute to a more inclusive and equal society,
- to develop modern non-formal educational content that is more integrative, visually engaging, and based on real-life examples and situations,
- to raise awareness among professionals about the interconnectedness of disability and the need for a holistic, interdisciplinary understanding that goes beyond individual professional fields,
- to involve persons with disabilities as active co-creators of knowledge and identification of their own needs,
- to promote sustainable behaviour among persons with disabilities, who are often overlooked in environmental policies,
- to establish international cooperation between partners and experts from social work, psychology and medicine,
- to support the digital transformation of participating organisations.

<< Implementation >>

We produced videos in which persons with diverse disabilities share their personal stories, experiences and challenges. These authentic narratives provide insight into the realities of living with a disability and highlight gaps in inclusion practices.
Based on these video stories, we developed visually supported and multidisciplinary educational materials in the form of videos and PDF resources. The materials are intended for both the general and professional public, and contribute to a better understanding of disability and its impact on everyday life. They strengthen awareness, empathy and acceptance of diversity, while also supporting the improvement of existing practices and the integration of different professional fields within the biopsychosocial model.
The materials were widely disseminated through digital channels.
The project also included sustainability activities. Through recycling workshops, we involved persons with disabilities and their relatives, who are often overlooked in environmental initiatives despite their important role in building a sustainable and inclusive society. Participants gained both awareness of sustainability and practical skills in recycling and creating products from recycled paper.

<< Results >>

- Videos featuring authentic stories of persons with various disabilities from Slovenia and Croatia: 5 educational videos, 6 personal testimonies (5–20 minutes), and 22 one-minute highlight clips with key messages. All videos include subtitles in English, Slovenian and Croatian, and were widely disseminated via Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, the project website, and targeted email dissemination through digital newsletters.
- More than 100 pages of expert content in the form of 5 educational PDF publications, which combine lived experiences of persons with disabilities with accessible explanations of medicine, social work and psychology. The materials are visually engaging and also published as digital flipbooks, enabling an improved user experience with page-flipping functionality.
- 4 diverse paper recycling workshops for persons with disabilities with motor, sensory and cognitive impairments.
- Contribution to increased awareness and deeper understanding of disability and reduction of stigma. Through digital communication channels alone (project social media profiles), the project reached more than 370,000 views by April 2026.
- 2 media features about the project (Siol, Ovtar24).
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000274380.title: TechGuardians: Fostering Resilience and Well-being Through Tech
2024-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000274380.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because all partner organizations identified a clear need to strengthen the knowledge and skills of their staff in two connected areas: digital literacy and mental well-being. We work with adult learners, including vulnerable groups, and we saw that digital exclusion, stress, and limited well-being support can directly affect adults’ access to learning, services, and participation in society. The project responded to the need to improve staff competences, exchange practical methods between partners, and develop a shared resource that could continue to support adult education work after the project ended.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we wanted to achieve three main objectives: to facilitate the exchange of experiences and best practices among partner organizations, to strengthen the capacity of the partner organizations to integrate digital literacy and mental well-being into their programmes and work with adults, and to develop a transnational network of professionals who can continue exchanging knowledge and resources in the future. 

Through these objectives, we aimed to equip the partner organizations with the tools and knowledge needed to create educational programmes addressing mental well-being and digital literacy, thereby contributing to the improvement of the quality of support and education provided to adult learners, including vulnerable and marginalized groups.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented four main project activities. 

First, we carried out coordination, evaluation, and dissemination activities, including regular online and in-person partner meetings, monitoring of project progress, evaluation of activities, and dissemination of project results. 

Second, we implemented the Wellbeing and Stress & Trauma training and experience exchange in Tenerife, Spain, where partner staff took part in training on mindfulness, well-being, and trauma-informed practices, followed by a joint best practice exchange. 

Third, we implemented the Digital literacy training and experience exchange in Ohrid, North Macedonia, focused on enhancing digital literacy skills and methodologies for staff from partner organizations (including digital tools, inclusive digital learning, and practical methods for adult education). 

Finally, we developed a digital brochure as an open educational resource bringing together the main knowledge, tools, and best practices generated through the project.

<< Results >>

The main concrete output was a digital brochure that brings together practical methods, tools, and best practices related to digital literacy, well-being, stress, and trauma-informed work in adult education. Other key results included improved competences of staff members in the partner organizations, especially in the areas of mindfulness, trauma-informed approaches, and digital literacy, as well as stronger capacity of the organizations to develop more inclusive and tailored educational activities for adults. The project also strengthened cooperation among the partners and created a basis for continued collaboration and future Erasmus+ initiatives.

2024-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000291871.title: HER[AI]TAGE: Preserving Intangible Cultural Heritage and Environmental Knowledge Through AI Technology
2024-2-HR01-KA210-ADU-000291871.summary:
<< Background >>

The main motivation behind the HER[AI]TAGE project was the need to preserve endangered cultural narratives, personal memories, and traditional ecological knowledge of older generations and to pass them on to new generations in a modern and accessible way. The project aimed to address the gradual loss of this valuable part of intangible cultural heritage, particularly knowledge related to the local ecosystems and waterways of the Mura, Drava, and Danube rivers. At the same time, we recognised the need to strengthen the digital competences of adult educators and create new learning opportunities focused on the responsible and creative use of artificial intelligence and generative AI. By combining oral history, digital storytelling, and AI technologies, we aimed to increase access to cultural heritage, foster intergenerational knowledge transfer, and raise awareness of the links between cultural heritage, the environment, and sustainable practices.

<< Objectives >>

The specific objectives we aimed to achieve through the implementation of the project were: 1. to collect, digitally preserve, and make accessible personal memories, traditional ecological knowledge, and cultural narratives of older people from communities along the Mura, Drava, and Danube rivers; 2. to foster intergenerational knowledge transfer and raise awareness of the importance of preserving intangible cultural heritage and local ecosystems; 3. to use artificial intelligence and generative AI to develop innovative ways of interpreting and presenting the collected stories through illustrations, audio content, and digital storytelling; 4. to strengthen the digital competences of adult educators and develop practical educational content on the use of AI and generative AI in adult education, cultural heritage preservation, and environmental protection; and 5. through transnational cooperation between partners from Croatia, Slovenia, and Serbia, to develop a publicly accessible digital collection, educational resources, and exhibitions that make the collected heritage available to a wider audience.

<< Implementation >>

Throughout the project, we implemented five interconnected activities. Under A1, we carried out continuous project coordination, management, and cooperation among the partners. Through A2, we developed common guidelines for data collection and conducted field interviews with older people in Croatia, Slovenia, and Serbia. Under A3, we transcribed, categorised, edited, and systematised the collected stories and established a publicly accessible digital database of stories. Through A4, selected stories were further interpreted using generative artificial intelligence; we created AI-generated illustrations and audio narrations, developed a digital story collection, and presented the results through exhibitions in the partner countries. Under A5, we developed a multilingual website and e-learning platform, organised a round table on the use of AI in adult education, created three practical online courses on the use of AI, and launched a virtual exhibition. Throughout the entire project, we continuously disseminated the project activities and results and worked to ensure their accessibility to the wider public.

<< Results >>

The concrete results of the project were: 1. 68 older people from Croatia, Slovenia, and Serbia were interviewed, resulting in 182 oral testimonies and stories related to cultural heritage, local landscapes, and ecosystems being collected and digitally archived; 2. a publicly accessible multilingual digital database of the collected stories was created; 3. 36 stories were selected and two AI-generated illustrations were created for each, resulting in a total of 72 visual interpretations; 4. 36 AI-generated voice narrations were produced in four languages, together with an interactive digital story collection; 5. three free online courses were developed on the use of AI and generative AI in adult education, cultural heritage preservation, and environmental protection; 6. a virtual exhibition was created and four physical exhibitions were organised to present the project results to the public. The project also established a multilingual website and e-learning platform that brings together the project results and ensures their continued public accessibility and use.

2024-2-MK01-KA210-ADU-000278661.title: Enhancing Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Skills for Public Administrators and Civil Servants
2024-2-MK01-KA210-ADU-000278661.summary:
<< Background >>

North Macedonia faces significant gaps in M&E frameworks, evaluation culture, and, most critically, in civil servants’ skills and knowledge of M&E. The lack of comprehensive training and education on M&E for civil servants is a major obstacle. This results in poor monitoring and a lack of evaluation for many national policies. Without targeted education and continuous professional development in M&E, civil servants are unable to effectively contribute to evidence-based decision-making. 
Recognizing the urgent need to address this, two partners identified these critical gaps and prioritized the development of a robust training program, leveraging the expertise of a Croatian EU partner for curriculum development and implementation. The project to enhance M&E skills among North Macedonian civil servants was designed to place training and education at the cеnter of reform, to improve transparency, accountability, and evidence-based decision-making, and to align the country more closely with EU standards. Building the capacity of civil servants through focused education and training in effective M&E is essential for assessing and improving the national public policy impact and efficiency.

<< Objectives >>

Enhance M&E Capacity for Public Administrators and Civil Servants and raise evaluation  culture among public administrators and civil servants in North Macedonia by providing practical training to 60 participants. Its objectives included improving participants’ abilities to design, monitor, and evaluate development projects for more effective public service delivery. 
Strengthen Collaboration between North Macedonia and EU Partners, particularly the Croatian Evaluation Society, to facilitate the transfer of EU standards in M&E and help to prepare North Macedonian institutions for managing EU structural funds. 
Promote Accountability and Better Decision-Making in Public Sector Projects by equipping participants with robust M&E tools and approaches, thereby supporting transparency, improved project management, and more effective use of public resources. These objectives are closely aligned with the country’s priorities for capacity building, stronger governance, and EU integration.

<< Implementation >>

Even not in the original plan of activities, the project recognized a need to organise a Roundtable meeting with national stakeholders in order to promote the training and to learn from stakeholders about the status of evaluation practice in the public administration. The participants were from the Prime Minister's Cabinet, the General Secretariat, and ministries and municipalities.
The project developed and implemented a comprehensive training program consisting of five curricula covering key M&E topics and practical exercises in drafting M&E reports. The program was developed and delivered by national and international experts, tailored to the needs of civil servants. 
Four separate training sessions, each lasting 3 days, were delivered to a total of 62 participants, who received certificates upon completion. 
Additionally, the project included an Assessment of training effectiveness through participant feedback. 
An important part was a four-day study visit to Croatia, where 13 training participants were engaged in discussions and knowledge exchange on EU M&E practices. These activities aimed to strengthen M&E capacity, foster collaboration with EU partners, and promote the practical application of M&E tools in public sector.

<< Results >>

The project’s concrete outputs included the development and delivery of five tailored Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) training curricula for public administrators and civil servants. Four training sessions, each lasting 3 days, were conducted for 62 participants who received certificates of attendance, thereby enhancing their M&E skills. Within this activity, the project developed a PP Presentation for each curriculum, as well as a guide for trainers to be used for new trainings. To promote the training program, the suitable promotion materials were developed and used for the project promotion.
A post-training evaluation report based on participant feedback and recommendations was produced to inform future capacity-building efforts. 
The project also organized a study visit to Croatia for 13 participants, enabling expert discussions, networking, and practical exposure to EU M&E standards during the visits to a number of relevant institutions. 
Additionally, a team of national and international experts was established, and a non-formal network of professionals from North Macedonia and Croatia was created. These activities led to strengthened M&E practices and improved project implementation in participating organizations.

2024-2-MK01-KA210-ADU-000286479.title: Развој на вештини за управување со зелени патишта
2024-2-MK01-KA210-ADU-000286479.summary:
<< Objectives >>

2024-2-SI01-KA210-ADU-000291135.title: Enhancing Digital Skills and Social Inclusion for Migrant Women Through Transnational Cooperation
2024-2-SI01-KA210-ADU-000291135.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the DIGIT@LLY INCLUDED project because, through our work with adult immigrants, we identified a need for more targeted support in developing digital competences and strengthening the social inclusion of migrant women. Migrant women often face several barriers at the same time, including limited knowledge of the language of the host environment, insufficient familiarity with public services, low confidence in using digital tools and limited opportunities for active participation in the community. As many services related to health, employment, education, public administration and everyday life are moving into the digital environment, a lack of digital skills increases the risk of social exclusion. The project therefore addressed the need for an inclusive, practical and individualised approach that supports greater independence, access to information and easier integration into the local environment.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to strengthen the digital competences and social inclusion of migrant women and to develop a transferable support model based on individualised learning plans, practical learning and mentoring support. The objective of the project was to train educators for working with migrant women and other vulnerable groups, to develop useful materials for preparing individualised learning pathways, and to pilot a programme that combines functional digital literacy, the use of digital public services, social activation and creative expression. Through transnational cooperation between the Slovenian and Croatian partner organisations, we aimed to exchange experience, identify differences between implementation environments and the needs of target groups, develop common approaches, and create solutions that adult education organisations can continue to use after the end of the project.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through 4 interconnected activities. 
•	Within the Management and Coordination activity, we carried out project management, partnership coordination, regular partner meetings, monitoring of implementation. An introductory meeting in Idrija, regular monthly online meetings and a final partner meeting in Zagreb were carried out. 
•	Within the activity Training Educators to Design Individual Upskilling Pathways, we implemented training for educators on the preparation of individualised learning plans, initial needs mapping, inclusive working methods, digital tools, career support and EU values. A handbook, tools and supporting materials were developed. 
•	Within the activity Empowering Migrant Women, we implemented a 40-hour pilot programme Empowering Migrant Women in Slovenia and Croatia. The programme included initial mapping, individualised learning plans, functional digital literacy, the use of digital public services, support for employment and social inclusion, and evaluation. 
•	Within the activity EU Values in Focus, we carried out project promotion and dissemination, a photo contest, online posts, presentations of results, publication of materials, and multiplier events in Zagreb and Idrija.


<< Results >>

Within Management and Coordination, the project was successfully managed through a kick-off partner meeting, monthly online meetings, and a final transnational meeting.
Within Training Educators to Design Individual Upskilling Pathways, seven educators were trained, a handbook and practical toolkit for developing individual learning pathways were produced, an informational PDF leaflet on the Upskilling Pathways approach was developed, and two workshops for educators were delivered.
Within Empowering Migrant Women, a database of 20 migrant women was created, two public calls and six meetings with local organisations were organised, a 40-hour pilot curriculum with learning and evaluation materials was developed, two pilot programmes were implemented, individual learning pathways and evaluation data were prepared, 11 migrant women successfully completed the programme, and a PDF leaflet presenting the programme, results and future use was published.
Within EU Values in Focus, a communication and dissemination plan, project logo, website and social media content, local media coverage, a photography competition, and two multiplier events were successfully delivered.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2025-1-BE02-KA210-ADU-000364051.title:
Shaping Sustainable Futures: Donut Economics for Culture 
and Cooperatives
2025-1-BE02-KA210-ADU-000364051.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Doughnut Economics helps societies and organisations operate within ecological limits while upholding social justice. This project aims to develop an educational course specifically for cooperatives and cultural organisations in Belgium and Croatia. By providing tools to create distributive and regenerative organisations, it will equip participants with practical skills to enhance resilience, well-being, and sustainability, while fostering peer learning and transnational collaboration.

<< Implementation >>

The course will be developed with feedback from the target groups to ensure it meets their needs. It will then be delivered, followed by an in-depth transnational meeting for engaged participants. Key takeaways will be published and actively disseminated through local and international networks, and the project will conclude with an evaluation to assess its impact and effectiveness.

<< Results >>

The project expects to engage 100 multipliers who will be equipped with the knowledge and skills to apply the tools that Doughnut Economics provides, enabling transformative practices in their own ecosystems and work communities. Furthermore, this contributes to the wider impact of tackling climate change and ensuring that our societies operate safely within planetary boundaries while simultaneously ensuring a good life for all.

2025-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000353412.title: Circular Connections: Repair, Share and Care
2025-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000353412.summary:
<< Objectives >>

CiCo tackles a gap in sustainability education: the lack of accessible, hands-on learning spaces where communities can actively practice repair, reuse, and resource-sharing. While policy frameworks promote sustainable consumption, everyday citizens often lack the skills and support to integrate these practices into their lives. By transforming LoTs and RCs into local hubs for sustainabilty learning, CiCo will equip individuals with practical green skills, strengthen repair and sharing culture.

<< Implementation >>

CiCo will combine knowledge exchange with hands-on application for immediate impact and long-term replicability. 
Key actions:
Know-how exchange: Peer learning through mentoring and job shadowing
Capacity building: Volunteer training and structural improvements for LoTs & RCs
Pilot phase: Community-driven testing of improved service models
Sustainability Ambassador Program: Citizens leading peer-learning green activities
Replication guidelines: A best-practice framework for broader replication

<< Results >>

By project’s end, CiCo will have:
Established Croatia’s first fully operational LoT in Pula, fostering borrowing and resource-sharing.
Expanded Ljubljana’s RC with structured volunteer support and increased accessibility.
Piloted 2 sustainability learning centers, integrating borrowing, repair, and education.
Trained at least 5 sustainability ambassadors per partner to lead peer-learning workshops.
Created best-practice guidelines for replication across Europe.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

The goal of the project is to develop intercultural competencies for people working with refugees and migrants, as well as to
design innovative approaches in working with this vulnerable group. We want to create a socially responsible integration
model and participate in building an intercultural society that fosters openness, tolerance and solidarity, where asylum
seekers, persons under international protection and foreign workers feel safe and welcome

Together with our partner organization, we will design an innovative digital handbook and presentations on the topic of
intercultural competencies and create a new digital platform for their presentation. We will organize workshops and

2025-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000358665.title: Theatre Training for the Re-activation of UnEmployed
2025-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000358665.summary:
<< Objectives >>

TTRUE aims to support the reactivation of long-term unemployed individuals and NEETs through a theatre training program, which includes training in various fields (from digital skills to budget management, from event organization to communication in English). The program is designed to provide participants with both soft skills (such as communication and self-confidence) and hard skills (such as foreign language proficiency and the use of digital tools).

<< Implementation >>

TTRUE first involves a recruitment phase in the three project countries, aimed at reaching the disadvantaged categories indicated (specifically the unemployed, both young NEETs and long-term unemployed). This is followed by a co-design phase of the course and the theatre training program, and finally the implementation of the course and the production of a final performance. The project also includes, as the last phase, the implementation of an international and local dissemination strategy.

<< Results >>

TTRUE aims to support the social and, subsequently, the professional reactivation of a diverse group of 45 to 60 unemployed individuals from Campania, Croatia, and Greece. The project expects to positively impact the participants' skills, both from a technical perspective (digital skills, communication, etc.) and on a more personal level, encompassing self-confidence, responsibility, and public speaking abilities
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2025-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000365153.title: CIVICA – Promoting active citizenship and entrepreneurship through civic agriculture initiatives
2025-1-IT02-KA210-ADU-000365153.summary:
<< Objectives >>

CIVICA aims to enhance the knowledge and awareness of adults from diverse backgrounds—especially unemployed individuals aged 18- 40 and N.E.E.T.s —by introducing innovative models of civic agriculture and sustainable agricultural practices. The project highlights existing opportunities in this field to inspire participation, encourage the launch of new civic agriculture initiatives, and increase citizen engagement in agriculture across both rural and urban areas.

<< Implementation >>

CIVICA includes various activities focused on civic agriculture, such as a study of best practices, policies, and funding opportunities; study visits and partner meetings in Italy, Greece, and Croatia; local workshops and events; video materials and a digital platform with a manual, mentoring tools  and an exhibition. The project will conclude with three multiplier events, including a final conference, to disseminate results and promote citizen engagement and social inclusion in agriculture.

<< Results >>

The results of CIVICA include a baseline study report, three study visits for at least 36 participants and partners meetings in Italy, Greece, and Croatia, a minimum of 30 hours of onsite and online workshops, events, and videos, three multiplier events with at least 90 participants in total. The project will also develop a digital platform with an exhibition, a manual with practical guidelines for newcomers in civic agriculture, and 10 selected beneficiaries of the platform's mentoring tools.

2025-1-PL01-KA210-ADU-000361875.summary:

We want to better support self-esteem, belonging and building mental resilience for people with special needs. We need new forms of influence, unusual for our work in the countryside, Likovni centar gallery from Croatia wants to create a model of art education based on clay, which can also be used by educators like us, i.e. without art education. The quality of the mission activities of our organisations

2025-1-PL01-KA210-ADU-000362028.summary:

Through international cooperation with a partner from Croatia, we develop the competences of adults, test plant cultivation in small spaces and disseminate knowledge among city residents, encouraging them to take green initiatives in their homes.

Testing and implementing crops on windowsills and balconies will allow you to check and adapt best practices. Then we will conduct stationary training for, among others: 100 city residents and we will create educational materials - instructional videos and guides, which we will disseminate online to increase ecologi

3. Promotion of the guide to all adults from vulnerable groups
4. Disseminating the project to other EU countries where adults have the same needs
