2025-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000363956.title: Save the Earth-dispose pharmaceutical waste smartly
2025-1-RS01-KA210-ADU-000363956.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The first goal is the education of pharmacists, patients with polypharmacy, and parents with children under 12 about pharmaceutical waste (PW) and its environmental and health consequences. The second goal is the motivation and encouragement of the public to change PW disposal habits. The long-term goal is increasing the rate of people properly disposing of PW, contributing to environmental protection, reducing antimicrobial resistance development, and improving public health across the region.

<< Implementation >>

The project activities include the creation and development of educational and promotional materials and digital tools. Educational activities include Continuing Medical Education sessions for pharmacists and online and live workshops for patients with polypharmacy and parents with children under 12 years, complemented by awareness and info days. Public campaign and dissemination activities will enable reaching out to more people, encouraging them to properly dispose of PW.

<< Results >>

The main outcome will be improved knowledge of PW among pharmacists, patients, and parents. This result may contribute to the increased rate of the public properly disposing of PW in the future. Changed practice and habits regarding PW can contribute to the realization of the European Green Deal and Sustainable Development Goals principles. Digital resources would ensure long-term access to disposal information, promoting sustainable waste management and environmental responsibility.

hr.name: Udruga za promicanje razvoja ljekarnika i zdravog života Progressus

2025-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000361633.title: Igrifikacija, gozdna terapija in zelene spretnosti - novi učni pristopi v naravi za opolnomočanje odraslih oseb z motnjami v telesnem in duševnem razvoju
2025-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000361633.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The Nature&Disabilities project aims to improve the skills of educators and caregivers in Slovenia and Croatia working with adults with physical and mental disabilities, to encourage to incorporate as many activities as possible from the regular curriculum and leisure time into nature all year round, to inspire with new learning approaches such as gamification, forest therapy, green skills, which have been proven to improve the lives and empower individuals with special needs.

<< Implementation >>

In Slovenia and Croatia, we will conduct a study on the state of education for adult individuals with physical and intellectual disabilities, their needs, learning specifics, the frequency of use and awareness of new learning approaches. We will organize two outdoor workshops for them and publish an e-handbook on gamification, forest therapy, and green skills for adults with special needs. A workshop and an online seminar will be organized for their educators and relatives.

<< Results >>

The project will reasearch the situation in both countries, which will be a long-term benefit for all those involved in or making decisions about adults with disabilities. It will raise awareness about the proven benefits of gamification, forest therapy, green skills for this vulnerable group. It will empower educators with competencies in new nature-based teaching approaches. The e-manual will serve as a lasting practical aid. The dissemination will influence lasting local and systemic changes.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

hr.name: Udruga osoba s intelektualnim teškoćama Istre

2025-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000365817.title: ECO CARE: Odgovorno ravnanje z zdravili za zdravje in okolje
2025-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000365817.summary:
<< Objectives >>

With the implementation of the ECO CARE project, we aim to improve the awareness and skills of chronic patients, caregivers, and volunteers regarding the safe and sustainable use of medicines, reduce the amount of unused medications, and promote responsible disposal of pharmaceutical waste. We will develop educational videos, guidelines, workshops, and awareness campaigns that will enhance the quality of care for chronic patients and reduce the environmental and health impacts of medications in

<< Implementation >>

In the ECO CARE project, we will conduct 4 regional and 8 virtual workshops for caregivers, produce 3 educational videos, develop guidelines for the safe use of medicines, design an awareness poster, and implement the ECO CARE challenge. We will organize dissemination activities, including publications on EPALE, Erasmus+ Project Results, and social media. The materials will be distributed to pharmacies, hospitals, and patient organizations for long-term use.

<< Results >>

The ECO CARE project will enhance caregivers' knowledge of the safe and sustainable use of medicines, reducing improper disposal of pharmaceutical waste. We will develop 3 educational videos, guidelines, an awareness poster, and the ECO CARE challenge, conduct 16 workshops, and ensure the availability of materials through pharmacies, hospitals, and online platforms (EPALE, Erasmus+). We expect greater public awareness, improved patient care, and a reduction in discarded medicines.

hr.name: UDRUGA LIJECNIKA, ZDRAVSTVENOG OSOBLJA I RODITELJA DJECE S PRIRODENIM SRCANIM GRJESKAMA I DRUGIM SRCANIM BOLESTIMA "VELIKO SRCE MALOM SRCU"

2026-1-CZ01-KA210-ADU-000454343.title: Small Climate Wins – An Adult Learning Model for Engaging Passive Citizens
2026-1-CZ01-KA210-ADU-000454343.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to develop and validate a structured non-formal adult learning model that strengthens climate literacy, communication and participatory decision-making competences of urban citizens. Through the Small Climate Wins framework, it empowers adults to initiate dialogue, engage neighbours and implement small, climate-friendly improvements in shared spaces, contributing to more cooperative and climate-resilient communities.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement needs mapping and desk research, develop the Small Climate Wins competence-based learning model and educational toolkit, organise a Train-the-Trainer session, conduct a pilot workshop with adult citizens in Prague, carry out structured evaluation and validation and implement visibility and dissemination activities including the Green Corner Challenge, exhibition, digital campaign and final conference.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver a validated Small Climate Wins learning model, a competence-based mini-curriculum, Facilitator Guide, Conversation-in-a-Box toolkit, Active Citizens Handbook and evaluation framework. At least 30 adults will improve climate literacy and participatory skills. The model will be published as open-access and disseminated through exhibitions, media outreach and a final conference, ensuring transferability and long-term use.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2026-1-DE02-KA210-ADU-000465226.title: UnaVersity for Sustainability: Developing forward-thinking adult education services that use community access to support Just Transition
2026-1-DE02-KA210-ADU-000465226.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The European Green Deal risks leaving vulnerable populations behind. We aim to transform Adult Education into a bridge for the "Just Transition." Our objectives are to: 
1) Equip adult educators with innovative Non-Formal Education tools to teach complex climate topics; 
2) Empower marginalized adults (rural populations, LTUAs) to voice their local environmental/infrastructure needs; and 
3) Build transnational project management capacity between our German and Croatian partner NGOs.

<< Implementation >>

Over 18 months, we will implement: 
1) The co-creation of the "UnaVersity Toolkit," containing practical methodologies like Eco-Social Labs and Dialogue Circles; 
2) A 5-day Transnational Study Visit in Germany to train 14 adult educators; 
3) Local Pilots in DE and HR, where educators test the Toolkit on 60+ marginalized adult learners; and 
4) Multiplier Events to share our localized climate-education frameworks with regional policymakers and AE providers.

<< Results >>

Results include: A highly transferable, multimedia "UnaVersity Toolkit" available in EN, DE, and HR. A network of 14 cross-border adult educators upskilled as "Green Deal Multipliers." Direct, grassroots empowerment of 60+ marginalized learners who gain practical green skills and a civic voice. Finally, the project will result in elevated organizational capacity for both NGOs, enabling them to lead larger, systemic European climate-education initiatives in the future.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2026-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000449771.title: PARLONS 2030
2026-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000449771.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The PARLONS 2030 project aims to develop and validate a curriculum and a pedagogical toolkit integrating the Sustainable Development Goals into French language teaching in adult education. It seeks to enhance methodological quality, strengthen teachers’ digital competences, and create a transferable pedagogical model validated across different European contexts.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement four main activities: project management and coordination; collaborative development of a structured curriculum and digital toolkit; two transnational workshops for methodological alignment, teacher training in open-source tools and European validation; and dissemination and transfer sessions, including a European online event and local training activities to ensure sustainable use of the results.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver a structured curriculum and a validated digital toolkit tested in three European contexts, including at least 30 SDG-based teaching units. It will strengthen teachers’ methodological and digital competences, create a transferable model for adult education, and ensure wide impact through open-access publication and training activities reaching over one hundred educators.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

hr.name: Društvo za kulturnu suradnju Francuska alijansa Osijek

2026-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000451592.title: CREATE: Participación creativa para el diálogo intercultural en la educación de personas adultas
2026-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000451592.summary:
<< Objectives >>

CREATE promotes inclusion, intercultural dialogue, and participation in adult education through creative, low-threshold methods. It provides practical tools for facilitators and engages migrant families and people with fewer opportunities through art and storytelling. It creates safe spaces that strengthen trust, social connection, and sustainable community participation.

<< Implementation >>

CREATE will implement facilitator training and family creative workshops in three countries. At least nine facilitators will be trained through a practical guide and an online session. Each country will organize three creative workshops involving adult migrants through art, crafts, and storytelling. The results will be documented in digital storybooks and shared through dissemination and sustainability initiatives at the local and European levels.

<< Results >>

CREATE will train facilitators, implement nine creative workshops in three countries, and increase the participation of adult migrants in inclusive learning. Participants will strengthen their confidence, social connection, and intercultural understanding. The project will produce a Quick Guide for Facilitators, digital storybooks, and reusable outreach materials for at least 15 organizations.

2026-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000458431.title: Raíces con Arte y Danza: Creación de una identidad europea compartida a través de talleres inclusivos de expresiones artísticas tradicionales para personas con discapacidad.
2026-1-ES01-KA210-ADU-000458431.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Promote social inclusion and European identity through inclusive flamenco (Spain) and Nijemo Kolo (Croatia) workshops for 30 people with disabilities. Develop artistic skills, foster European awareness through virtual exchange, empower participants as spokespersons, raise societal awareness by making their talents visible, value both traditions as shared cultural heritage, and strengthen transnational cooperation between partner organizations.

<< Implementation >>

Four main activities:

1) Management and coordination with an initial meeting in Seville, 6 virtual meetings, and participant selection.
2) Weekly theoretical and practical workshops for 8 months, 4 intercultural virtual meetings, and creation of an accessible digital repository.
3) Two public performances (Spain and Croatia) and a transnational meeting in Croatia.
4) Ongoing dissemination, website, YouTube, accessible edition of materials, open days, and sustainability plan.

<< Results >>

- 30 people with disabilities develop social, artistic, and personal skills through the workshops provided.
- Virtual meetings and the repository foster European awareness.
- Public performances raise awareness among 100 attendees, and participants, as spokespersons of the process, improve their self-esteem and empowerment.
- A replicable methodological guide is created for use across Europe.
- Transnational cooperation is strengthened by signing a future collaboration agreement.

2026-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000452625.title: SKILL-GREEN: Simple Climate Actions for Everyday Life & AI-Supported Learning Tools
2026-1-FR01-KA210-ADU-000452625.summary:
<< Objectives >>

SKILL-GREEN aims to bridge the gap between environmental awareness and daily behaviour among adults with fewer opportunities. It will increase participants’ confidence in everyday green decisions (O1), ensure that at least one small green habit is tested and monitored (O2), equip educators with low-threshold visual tools (O3), and embed the Green Micro-Learning model into partner institutions for sustainable continuation beyond the project period (O4).

<< Implementation >>

The project will be implemented in four phases. A1 will ensure structured management and monitoring. A2 will conduct a transnational needs analysis with at least 120 adults and develop 30 Insight Cards with AI-supported templates. A3 will produce StoryFrames and 6 micro-videos. A4 will implement Community Green Circles in four countries and compile an open-access multilingual Toolkit with a sustainability plan.

<< Results >>

SKILL-GREEN will produce a Green Basics Snapshot, 30 Insight Cards, a StoryFrames booklet, 6 micro-videos and a tested Community Green Circles model compiled into a multilingual open-access Toolkit. At least 120 adults will participate, with 70% increasing environmental knowledge and 50% testing at least one new green habit for 8 weeks. At least 60 educators will use the materials, strengthening institutional capacity and long-term sustainability.

2026-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000451696.title: NATUREscapes: Nature-based soundscapes for adult learning
2026-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000451696.summary:
<< Objectives >>

NATUREscapes aims to combat digital fatigue in adult education. This will be achieved by: 
O1) Developing calm technology tools (Web App) to help learners regulate stress and restore focus;
O2) Equipping educators and adult education centres with "Re-naturing Strategy" to manage classroom anxiety; and
O3) Building deep sensory connection to Mura-Drava biosphere, transforming passive listening into active environmental stewardship through acoustic ecology

<< Implementation >>

NATUREscapes implements 6 activities:
-A1 ensures project management
-A2 researches digital stress and produces "Re-naturing Strategy" Manual
-A3 records 12 high-fidelity soundscapes, 6 360° immersive videos and 3D photo spheres of Mura-Drava region
-A4 develops "NATUREscapes Web App" (ambient mixer, map, focus timer)
-A5 pilots these tools with 30 learners in rural SI and (semi-)urban HR to validate stress reduction
-A6 disseminates results via digital campaign, EPALE, and 2 local launch events

<< Results >>

NATUREscapes tangible results include: 
1) A Web App featuring ambient mixer, 12 immersive audio/visual soundscapes, customizable pomodoro-style learning tool; 
2) An Educator’s Manual teaching restorative pedagogy; and
3) A DIY Field Recording Guide for citizen science. 
Through intangible results, NATUREscapes aims for reduced anxiety for 30 pilot participants, enhanced well-being competences for 20 educators, and increased public awareness of Mura-Drava acoustic heritage across the EU

2026-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000457556.title: Jačanje inkluzivnosti kulturno-baštinskih lokaliteta i organizacija
2026-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000457556.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Project InSite focuses on cooperation and knowledge exchange between cultural heritage sites and disability organisations from Croatia and Slovenia, with the aim of increasing their accessibility and inclusiveness. Through capacity building of management and operational staff, as well as the development and introduction of accessible services and interpretative content, the project contributes to strengthening inclusive practices in cultural heritage.

<< Implementation >>

Project InSite is a cooperation and professional development process aimed at improving accessibility at partner heritage sites. It is implemented through online training on sensory and cognitive accessibility for management staff; specialised workshops for staff working with visitors; development of inclusive tours and accessible video, audio and printed materials at sites managed by Fortress of Culture Šibenik and Cultural Centre Krško; and inclusive public events presenting the results.

<< Results >>

The project will contribute to the long-term development of partner organisations by strengthening management and operational staff competences in sensory and cognitive accessibility in cultural heritage and by introducing inclusive services and accessible content that remain part of the regular offer at sites managed by Fortress of Culture Šibenik and Cultural Centre Krško. Partners will develop a shared model that can be further applied and adapted in their future programme development.

hr.name: Public cultural institution Fortress of Culture Šibenik

2026-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000457575.title: Pathways to Participation: Civic Integration and Democratic Engagement of Ukrainian Adults in Europe
2026-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000457575.summary:
<< Objectives >>

“Pathways to Participation: Civic Integration and Democratic Engagement of Ukrainian Adults in Europe” addresses the gap between protection and participation by strengthening the capacity of adult education providers to support displaced Ukrainian adults in navigating national and European civic structures and engaging confidently in democratic life. The project embeds a participatory, transferable model for inclusive civic integration across European contexts.

<< Implementation >>

The project will jointly develop a practical Civic Participation Toolkit and test it through three pilot cycles with displaced Ukrainian adults in Zagreb, Osijek and Prague. Based on real-life implementation and evaluation, the model will be refined and presented publicly. A two-day online training will equip adult educators and civic organisations to apply and adapt the methodology across Europe.

<< Results >>

Pathways to Participation will result in displaced Ukrainian adults taking clearer, more confident steps into community and civic life, with a better understanding of how institutions work and how to engage with them. Educators and organisations will leave with a practical, tested approach they can immediately apply. The lasting result is a ready-to-use model that strengthens democratic participation within integration processes across Europe.
topics: Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

hr.name: UDRUGE CENTAR ZA MIR, NENASILJE I LJUDSKA PRAVA - OSIJEK

2026-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000464873.title: Kreativna inkluzija - Model integracije stranih radnika u Hrvatskoj
2026-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000464873.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Through the project “Creative Inclusion”, a model will be developed and tested to strengthen social inclusion and intercultural understanding between foreign workers and the local population. Through creative and participatory workshops, participants will build trust and better understand workplace culture and employment rights, educators will enhance their competencies, and the organisations involved will develop a transferable and sustainable integration model applicable in Croatia and Europe

<< Implementation >>

The project runs a series of creative and participatory workshops for 50 participants and 8 educators: clay for non-verbal communication, identity collage, stop-motion animation “My Journey”, food and music for social cohesion, and work culture in Croatia. Educators learn methods for heterogeneous groups, exchange good practices with Asturia, and develop a documented, transferable “Creative Inclusion” model for use in other organizations and European contexts.

<< Results >>

The project will help participants better understand other cultures, build trust, and connect with the local community. Educators will learn new methods for working with mixed groups, and the organizations will gain a tested and documented “Creative Inclusion” model that can be applied in other contexts, contributing to greater inclusion and reduced stereotypes.
topics: Human rights and rule of law

2026-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000465077.title: Community Learning for Care and Active Ageing
2026-1-HR01-KA210-ADU-000465077.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project will support  adult learners (informal carers, low-skilled adults) and  older adults (65+) to improve self-care, digital literacy, resilience, and community-based elder support skills. Partners will co-create and pilot a modular training programme and practical toolkit, deliver all activities inclusively, foster social participation and community engagement, and ensure sustainable integration of results into local adult education and community services for wider replication.

<< Implementation >>

Recruit and engage  participants through local outreach, organise participatory workshops to identify and prioritise key learning needs of adult learners and older adults; co-create a modular training programme for carers and a practical toolkit for older adults, develop, pilot and refine accessible materials; deliver structured face-to-face training sessions; organise dissemination and multiplier events, and ensure sustainable integration of results into local adult education and community.

<< Results >>

Adult learners (informal carers, low-skilled adults) and older adults (65+) will gain practical skills in self-care, digital literacy, resilience, and community-based elder support. Results include one validated two-part modular training programme for adult learners and one accessible toolkit for older adults, strengthened confidence, social networks and engagement, plus increased awareness of their role in supporting communities, with adaptable outputs ready for broader local replication.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2026-1-NL01-KA210-ADU-000449181.title: Rooted Voices - Practical Values for Migrant Women’s Participation
2026-1-NL01-KA210-ADU-000449181.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The "Rooted Voices" project aims to strengthen migrant women’s confidence, participation and sense of belonging through non-formal, value-based learning. By Month 12, at least 60 migrant women (30+) will improve communication, self-expression and digital confidence, while partner organisations will enhance their capacity to deliver inclusive, low-barrier adult education activities.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement coordinated management, value-based workshops, creative handcraft and game-supported sessions, AI-supported digital storytelling, community actions and dissemination activities. Learning will take place through local group sessions, online exchanges and simple digital tools, ensuring safe, accessible and participatory learning environments.

<< Results >>

Expected results include increased self-confidence and participation among migrant women, a shared Values-in-Action Toolkit, 12 digital storybooks, short support videos and practical guidance for facilitators. Results will remain openly accessible and reusable, supporting long-term inclusion, community engagement and adult learning practices beyond the project.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2026-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000460510.title: Retirees’ Engagement in New media and Environmental Wisdom
2026-1-SI01-KA210-ADU-000460510.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Objectives: 
- promote retirees’ participation in innovative adult education; 
- identify key digital and green skills; 
- upskill/reskill retirees through podcasting and eco-wisdom learning, 
- strengthening community and intergenerational exchange.

<< Implementation >>

Activities: 
- A1 management/QA + 2 online TNMs; 
- A2 “Tea-Time With…” podcast method + training; 
- A3 “Eco-Wisdom at Home” materials + piloting + 3 intergenerational workshops/country; 
- A4 dissemination (website, EPALE posts/webinar, national events, final media event).

<< Results >>

Results: 
- implementation/QA/dissemination plan; 
- 15 podcasts (5/country); 
- 3 sets of training materials; 
- 3 online training seminars; 
- interactive website; 
- 4 dissemination actions incl. final conference; 
- 1 open-access practice paper.

2021-1-BG01-KA210-SCH-000031244.title: Young European Explorers
2021-1-BG01-KA210-SCH-000031244.summary:
<< Background >>

The aim of our project was to apply innovative teaching methods aimed at fostering students creativity, self-motivation and
learner autonomy using PBL, webquests, peer-learning and learning-by-teaching, developing and implementing activities based on environment, history, folk culture and sports of the partner countries.General objectives were: development and integration of new teaching approach- PBL through ICT methods, carry out activities aimed at developing the digital skills of students and educators, introduce new technologies in schools, cultivate our students' natural enthusiasm for learning, their curiosity and creativity, while boosting their motivation and self-confidence through the use of enjoyable activities, develop and strengthen social skills appropriate to real and virtual interactions, spread the use of new technologies to support educational action, development of partnership with other countries in order to ensure mutual exchange of knowledge and best practices.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project we wanted to achieve three main things: exchanging of good practice in the field of ICT and especially PBL trough ICT methods,European cooperation and teaching the core 21st century skills.Our organizations were really motivated to implement this project because we were searching for new approaches that would make learning fun,interesting and motivating for our students.We wanted to boost the European dimension in our school-community and gave our students various opportunities of getting
in touch with students from other countries and cultures.We needed to find ways to teach our students the core skills in the 21st century: cooperation, critical thinking, research skills, creativity, communication, cross-cultural, understanding. By using innovative learning methods,the teachers were expected to be able to hone such skills needed to take part in 21st-century life,which is creativity,critical thinking,communication skills and also collaboration skills of students.

<< Implementation >>

We started with the launch of a project website,eTwinning platform-Twin Space and Facebook group of our project.This project website was created in the phase of preparation but it will be maintained and be active till the end of the project and even after the end of the project, where friends from all school partner schools can share information about the impact of this project. A Club ”Young European Explorer-”forming a project team of 15 students and 2 reserves. This club was implemented every Monday of the week for the two–year period of the project.The aim of this club was to organize different extracurricular activities.Workshops, meetings, cultural trips and trainings were implemented. Presentations and different materials were created and shared with all partner schools’ students.The school club was established with the help of experts and educators working in the field of PBL and ICT.Students participated in workshops at all level of activities described. International meetings which were four were implemented.There was an implementation of a transparent selection procedure of the participating students.Parents’ meetings were implemented in order the idea of the Erasmus + programme and the project.

<< Results >>

Participants gained more knowledge about the use of multiple applications and social media as an educational tool and improved engagement and thus improved communication between students and teachers.They acquired the skills to manage a new ICT applications and to use them in the learning process.We explored and promoted an increasing awareness of European citizenship and different cultures in Europe and we boosted the European dimension in our school-community.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-BG01-KA210-SCH-000032412.title: Cut the Cord! Respect, Educate, Protect! (CC-REP): Shifting from Digital Natives to Digital Citizens
2021-1-BG01-KA210-SCH-000032412.summary:
<< Background >>

Our application for this project stemmed from a critical recognition of the evolving digital landscape and its impact on young people and the broader community. We identified a significant gap in awareness and understanding of digital citizenship—a concept that encompasses not just the use of digital technologies but also the responsibilities and ethical behaviors associated with them. Our objectives were multifaceted. Firstly, we aimed to transform the mindset of our students and the school community from being mere digital natives, who are adept at using technology, to becoming informed digital citizens, who understand the implications and responsibilities of their digital footprint. This transition was vital in preparing them for a world where digital interactions are as consequential as real-life ones. Secondly, we sought to embed the principles of digital citizenship into our curriculum and school culture. This meant not only educating students but also involving teachers, parents, and third parties in the conversation. We conducted workshops, seminars, and interactive sessions that fostered dialogue and understanding about topics such as online safety, digital ethics, and the impact of digital actions. 

<< Objectives >>

The project was designed to create a ripple effect, encouraging students to disseminate their learning to their families and communities, thereby amplifying the impact of our initiative. We emphasized the importance of critical thinking, empathy, and ethical decision-making in the digital realm. In retrospect, the project not only addressed the immediate need for digital citizenship education but also laid a foundation for ongoing dialogue and development in this area. The enthusiasm and engagement we witnessed from participants have been a testament to the project’s success. Our students have now become ambassadors of digital citizenship, demonstrating a profound shift from their initial passive engagement with digital technologies to a more responsible, informed, and proactive stance. This transition, we believe, is pivotal in shaping a safer, more respectful, and ethical digital world. Our project, aimed at instilling digital citizenship among youth and the broader community, successfully transformed students from digital natives to responsible digital citizens. Central to this was raising awareness about ethical online behavior and integrating digital citizenship into our curriculum.

<< Implementation >>

During our project, we implemented a range of activities designed to instill digital citizenship: Our project implemented several key activities to promote digital citizenship: Workshops and Seminars: We held interactive sessions on online safety, ethical behavior, and digital footprints, tailored for various age groups. Curriculum Integration: We infused digital citizenship concepts across subjects, reinforcing responsible digital behavior through academic activities. Community Engagement: Events with parents, teachers, and local community members were organized to broaden the digital citizenship dialogue. Student-Led Initiatives: Students spearheaded peer education, digital literacy campaigns, and online safety drives. Online Resources: We created platforms for information access, discussions, and sharing experiences in digital citizenship. Feedback Sessions: Regular evaluations were conducted to assess activity effectiveness and gather insights for improvement. These initiatives aimed to ensure a deep understanding and adoption of digital citizenship principles among all participants. Through these activities, we sought to create a comprehensive and immersive experience for all participants.

<< Results >>

Our project has successfully increased the awareness of our target groups in digital citizenship. We have supported and contributed to local, national, and international strategies, reforms, and policies in this area. One of the key outcomes was our contribution to advancing the Digital Education Action Plan. Additionally, we have effectively focused on several national priorities through our initiatives. In terms of theoretical implications, our project has offered valuable insights into digital citizenship, enriching the existing body of knowledge. Practically, we have made significant strides by integrating digital citizenship concepts into the curriculum. This integration has not only educated our students but also provided a model that can be replicated in other educational settings. Overall, the concrete outputs of our project include a series of educational workshops, seminars, community engagement events, and the development of online resources and platforms. These activities have collectively contributed to a deeper understanding and practice of digital citizenship among our students and the wider community.

2021-1-CZ01-KA210-SCH-000031448.title: Zdravá krajina - Poznej svou krajinu v ČR a v Chorvatsku
2021-1-CZ01-KA210-SCH-000031448.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was focused on the environmental and geographical education of secondary school students based on oriented research of selected localities in their mother country. The motivation to implement the project was based on the demand of pedagogues to increase the attractiveness of studying natural sciences based on the interactive involvement of students in their own research. The purpose of the project was to establish friendship and cooperation between partner schools, to acquire knowledge about the qualities and problems of the landscape in the region of both partner schools, to acquire skills in the field of orientation and work with geographic data with the involvement of digital technologies and the development of key competencies, and to improve the geography and natural science training of students. Within the project, modern teaching methods implemented in the natural environment and in local farms and eco-centres were used. Thanks to the project, students were able to connect theory with practice and better understand and retain the acquired knowledge. The project continued to the worldwide climate changes associated with the loss of water in the wild, which fundamentally reduces biodiversity.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of the project was to expand the students' knowledge of the local region and its ecosystems - to learn to identify the environmental problems of the landscape and to connect theoretical knowledge with their own research, which will promote their interest in science and environmental protection. Thanks to the international cooperation, the participants of the project realized that disturbed biodiversity and the threat of ecosystems is not only a problem of their country, but a global problem, the solution of which must involve both individuals (personal responsibility) and the whole society.


<< Implementation >>

As part of teamwork, students learned to cooperate and share their own observations, search for information, work with it and then present it. The international nature of the project gave the students an insight into the environmental problems of the landscape in another country, when the goal should be to understand that global climate changes have the same denominator across all countries – ignorance of natural natural processes and an unsparing approach to the environment.

<< Results >>

As part of the implementation of the project, posters on the given topics, interactive presentations/videos on the given topics, a Czech-Croatian and a Croatian-Czech geographical and ecological dictionary were created, and greenery was planted with local actors involved. In addition, the students took part in an orientation-oriented survey of the landscape, workshops and visited eco-centers and eco-farms.

2021-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000032418.title: "Distance Learning Gateway"
2021-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000032418.summary:
<< Background >>

Our world has been hit by coronavirus pandemic for more than a year. Because of this pandemic, many things have changed in our lives. Sometimes we are under lockdown and as teachers we have to arrange our lessons online. As we are used to having most of our lessons face to face, we have difficulty in having our lessons online. This situation makes it difficult for both teachers and students. As teachers, we must use different methods and digital tools so as to make the lessons clear and understandable and increase the students' attention and motivation. On the other hand, the students should also adapt to this transformation and use digital technology in a positive way. At the beginning of the academic year, we held general management and teachers' meeting, during which school needs and students’ situations have been  carefully examined. Many teachers, especially language teachers, expressed that both teachers' and students' digital skills should be developed and the school project team agreed that a project about developing ıct skills is in need. 

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to achieve collaboration among partners about innovative practices in distance, virtual, flipped, blended learning processes.
- gaining new digital competencies  
- having and actualizing knowledge of ICT and new Technologies 
- contributing to digital education of the partner schools -Using web 2 tools effectively 
- contributing to distance learning process 
- raising awareness of rapid technological and digital change in the world 
- developing teaching profiles of educators

2021-1-DK01-KA210-SCH-000031309.title: The EUnique SIDE - Social Inclusion, Digital Evolution
2021-1-DK01-KA210-SCH-000031309.summary:
<< Background >>

This project arose from the coronavirus impact, negatively affecting the ordinary flow of mainstream education. Teachers and pupils were looking for new skills and ways to adapt to learning concepts such as distance learning and online lessons. The SELFIE report by the EU demonstrated 43% of European schools lacked basic digital skills, and 71 million students attending schools in Europe needed to develop their skills for the digital society. Moreover, results from surveys we carried out to determine the digital capacity of pupils and teachers showed that 4% of pupils had no device and 14% no Wi-fi, 15% signal problems, all of which indicated the economical or geographical obstacles they faced. Also, 67% of pupils and 81% of teachers preferred school education instead of online education. The reason we believe is that although 86% of pupils spent at least 4 hours a day with online lessons, 20% of them found it ineffective and 61% of teachers had an increased workload or stress due to online teaching. All of it indicated the need for a better adaptation to digital transformation. Thus, this project was an opportunity for strengthening cooperation and exchange in digital education at EU level and for practical local implementations.

<< Objectives >>

Our objectives were built on digital literacy and language learning. Our goal was to address the digital transformation by improving digital capacity of both teachers and pupils and simultaneously promoting social inclusion. Also, we aimed to 1. motivate teachers and pupils to cope with COVID-19 crisis 2. foster the skills and confidence of teachers and pupils in the appropriate and effective use of digital technology in learning and teaching 3. create a chance for teachers to learn innovative approaches in education 4. tackle disinformation through education and training 5. allow pupils to learn at their own pace, making learning personal and engaging 6. show respect and tolerance toward diversity 7. use digital tools to innovate processes and ICT products 8. keep up to date with the digital evolution 9. increase the competencies of teachers to manage a diverse group of pupils 10. learn about the history of digital learning 11. encourage productive learning outside the classroom or in an online environment 12. touch on the key components of digital competence identified by The Digital Competence Framework 13. hold local, technological and art events specific to each country to promote the knowledge of different cultural traits 

<< Implementation >>

Three mobility activities: 
1. Denmark - Teaching and Didactics Platforms: focus on teacher training, disinformation and digital platforms and the didactic part of English teaching.
2. Croatia - Creative Learning: book reading and use of Stop Motion Studio App to create visual representation of a book scene that convinced others to read it.
3. Portugal - Individualised Learning: creation of digital recipe books, media literacy and disinformation, coding classes using ICT for interactive stories and cultural events. 
Additional activities in between mobilities: 
•	Digital Designs for T-shirts - creation of T-shirts in different designs using digital apps 
•	Traditional Cultural Activities – exchange of traditional cultural activities e.g. dance, recipe and game
•	Digital Learning Day - joint celebration creating tips for online safety
•	European Language Day - joint celebration translating national phrases and idioms into the various partner languages.
•	Erasmus Days - project presentation at a webinar as part of the Croatian Erasmus Days event
•	Europe Day - a joint celebration with a quiz about the European Union. Creation of short video using the Stop Motion Studio App


<< Results >>

Increased knowledge on students with fewer opportunities and especially dyslexia, and on practical didactics and teaching. Focus on ways of combining theory and practical teaching to create more creative and motivating teaching especially for students with special needs. Co-teaching and co-planning between teachers from the different partner schools. For example, after discussing with Danish teachers and specialists, teachers from the partner countries were able to adapt their regular lesson plans so as to include some of the new methods and techniques and apply them in class. 
Training using many different digital tools, and thereby increased digital skills among students and teachers – skills that can be transferred to outside the classroom and the schools. The Croatian and Portuguese teachers shared their new knowledge from activity 1 within their school, and to other teachers, both by word-of-mouth and by sharing video presentations.
Products:
●	Stop Motion Book trailers – based on a English literary work. 
●	Knowledge on media literacy and disinformation
●	Digital recipe books using Book Creator
●	Interactive stories using Scratch
●	T-shirts in different designs 
See attached "project timeline and documents on PRP" for info.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2021-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000031424.title: OUR TIME IS NOW! DIGITAL EDUCATION 4ALL
2021-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000031424.summary:
<< Background >>

The "Our Time is Now! Digital Education 4All" project was requested to address several key needs in early childhood education. These needs include:
Integration of New Technologies: The need to integrate new technologies into the educational environment to improve the quality of education and adapt digital methodologies to the needs of the student body.
Teacher Training: The need to train teachers in the appropriate use of new technologies and applications for early childhood education.
Linguistic Competence in English: The need to promote English linguistic competence in students as a means of international communication.
Access to Technology: The need to facilitate access to new technologies for students at risk of social exclusion.
Exchange of Experiences: The need to exchange experiences and good practices with other educational centers that have experience in digitalized classrooms.
With these fundamental needs, we aimed to address current challenges and improve the quality of education in the early childhood education environment.

<< Objectives >>

By executing the project, the following results and benefits were expected to be achieved:
Comparative Final Document: final document containing a comparison between practices and experiences developed by each partner in relation to the use of new technologies in the classroom.
Collaboration Network: The project sought to establish a collaborative network between different early childhood education centers in Europe.
Digital Transformation: The project was expected to serve as a digital transformation project in the early childhood education stage, promoting the innovative use of new technologies.
Teacher Training: The objective was to train educational teams by providing them with innovative tools in order to develop key competencies in students.
Access to Technology: The aim was to facilitate access to new technologies for the population with fewer opportunities, promoting digital inclusion.
In summary, the main objective of the project was to generate a positive impact on the quality of education, promote digital inclusion, and foster collaboration and the exchange of experiences at the international level in the field of early childhood education.

<< Implementation >>

Training: Training courses have been provided for teachers with the aim of acquiring new knowledge in new technologies applied to the classroom.
Exchange of Experiences: Activities have been carried out to exchange experiences and good practices with the different European partners, in order to enrich knowledge and educational practice.
Development of a ToolKit: We have worked on the elaboration of a final document containing an exchange of practices and experiences developed by each partner in relation to the use of new technologies in the classroom.
Creation of a Collaboration Network: The aim was to establish a collaboration network between different early childhood education centers in Europe, promoting cooperation and knowledge exchange.
Implementation of Innovative Practices: Innovative practices have been implemented in the use of new technologies in the classroom, to improve educational quality and adapt digital methodologies.
All activities have been designed to address the specific objectives of the project and generate a positive impact on the educational environment of early childhood education.

<< Results >>

1. ToolKit "Technology as a tool not an answer": A final document has been created containing a comparison of practices and experiences developed by each partner in relation to the use of new technologies in the classroom. This document provides an overview of the different strategies and approaches used, as well as the results obtained.
2. Collaboration Network: A collaboration network has been established between different early childhood education centers in Europe, which has facilitated the continuous exchange of knowledge, experiences and good practices.
3. Digital Transformation: The project has contributed to the digital transformation in the early childhood education stage, promoting the innovative use of new technologies and their effective integration into the educational environment.
4.	Teacher Training: It has been possible to train educational teams by providing them with innovative tools, which has contributed to the development of key competencies in students.
5.	Access to Technology: The project has facilitated access to new technologies for the population with fewer opportunities, promoting digital inclusion and equal educational opportunities.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000032423.title: Ruralship Empowerment of Education (Formal, Nonformal, Informal)
2021-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000032423.summary:
<< Background >>

We have requested this project because in rural environments the change from primary to secondary is more pronounced, since normally one changes town (there are no institutes) and we have seen that the same situation is repeated in other countries in rural environments, so we have wanted to address the issue of school failure and in particular the benefits and potential of formal, non-formal and informal education in rural environments. We have wanted to address the issue of difficulties, from a positive approach, that is why we have tried to avoid talking about school FAILURE and we have always used positive terms such as the potential of education or the synergies between formal, non-formal and informal education. .
Throughout the project we have addressed topics such as culture, folklore, languages, the benefits of rural life and the needs of educational entities in these environments. Isolation, lack of resources, lack of motivation, few users...

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to FIGHT AGAINST SCHOOL FAILURE that can occur when having to change from primary school in a rural environment to a secondary school in a neighboring city. We need to empower boys and girls before that moment arrives and equip them with resources and skills that will help them overcome all those difficulties that they will encounter due to having grown up in a rural environment.
In addition, another objective was to improve the quality of our educational work through learning by SHARING GOOD PRACTICES AND LEARN FROM OTHER EXPERIENCES of comprehensive education in the rural world.
Finally, we have tried to generate synergies between educational entities in the rural world of formal, non-formal and informal education, while at the same time wanting to create international partnerships.

<< Implementation >>

Throughout the project we have had periodic coordination meetings, both virtual and in person. And at the local level, we have been organizing the work to create the results of the project, such as the 3 games that we have developed.
Also at the local level, we have had cooperation activities between the entities of each country. Furthermore, as we have been fortunate to have many local partners who have helped throughout the process, the local activities of the project have been very enriching. We have tried to focus on cooperation between formal and non-formal education entities (schools and associations), also adding the value of informal education and the educational spaces generated by city councils and public institutions.
When we already had the games designed, we have done dissemination activities to make them known and in recent months we have also had (schools) activities within E-twinning as a result of this project.

<< Results >>

Games: We wanted to create 2 games, but in the end we developed 3 because in the meetings and brainstorming sessions, we thought it would be interesting to take advantage of the material we were creating a little more. So we have made a "families" type card game, a story-telling game with 4 dice and a "trivial" quiz type board game.
E-twinning project: The 4 schools involved have created their e-Twinning profiles (3 of them did not have it) and have begun to collaborate in a project that has already had its first "material" fruits: an exchange of Christmas postcards between the 4 schools (they have been sent by post and each school has received those from the others). Thus, a path of cooperation begins that we hope will last for many years.
Good practices: during these months of the project we have been discovering and understanding the good work of each rural territory and the best ideas to connect formal-nonformal-informal education, always with the aim of improving quality and reducing the risk of school drop-out.
Web: A web portal with all the created materials and project information
...and lots of learnings and good memories for both the entities and the people involved.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education
Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

2021-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000027272.title: Spretni i sretni
2021-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000027272.summary:
<< Background >>

In today's world, technology plays a very important and big role and has become part of human everyday life. Today's children no longer spend the vast majority of their free time on playgrounds, riding bicycles, or climbing trees, but instead spend time sitting in front of screens playing various types of video games and watching television and YouTube channels. Through participation in this project, first of all, we wanted to encourage children to think about their health habits and their sustainability in the future. Various environmental care and recycling activities were carried out throughout the project. The goals of the project are indirectly related to the preservation of the environment and the development of awareness of climate change.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to introduce children and parents to healthy eating and living habits and encourage them to engage in daily physical activities. We wanted to encourage children to spend more quality free time without technology. Secondary goals were to encourage the creativity of students and teachers, cooperate with partners from other countries and regions, and thus open school doors and action in an EU environment, encourage the active involvement of students from participating schools in activities outside of compulsory education, and create EU citizenship.

<< Implementation >>

In the project, we carried out various activities in which students, parents, and teachers were involved. The activities we implemented are: Making our own gardens, "Handicrafts", "Days without Technology" and exercise "I practice, you practice, we practice." After the activities, we created a guidebook for children "Skillful and Happy" which connected all the activities into one and a cookbook with healthy food. We recorded an anthem for the project called "Zdrava hrana". Complete project activities which we implemented in the project can be seen on our website: http://os-bakar.skole.hr/erasmus/spretni_i_sretni and Youtube Channel: https://www.youtube.com/@skillfulandhappy8431/videos

<< Results >>

The desired effect of the project at the local and regional level was to encourage students and parents outside our institutions to change behavior in nutrition and self-care and awareness of the opportunities that are in our environment that greatly facilitate our health care. We wanted to encourage schools outside the project to think about a healthier lifestyle. At the national level, we wanted to encourage more frequent and comprehensive conversations about healthier habits of school children. All of the results and concrete outputs of the project can be seen on our website: http://os-bakar.skole.hr/erasmus/spretni_i_sretni and Youtube Channel: https://www.youtube.com/@skillfulandhappy8431/videos

2021-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000027294.title: Math 4you & 4me
2021-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000027294.summary:
<< Background >>

According to SWOT analysis, all schools had a problem with low student's rate in Mathematics skills and majority of the students were in some sort of disadvantaged status. Also analyse of the European Comission's „PISA 2019 and EU (Striving for social fairness through education)“ (Dec, 2019) in which it was seen: Underachievement rate in mathematics, 2018 [%]: Poland 15%, Czech Republic 20%, Croatia 31%. It was necessary to motivate students to learn mathematics and offer them interesting ways of learning that include ICT, but also tasks that arise from everyday life situations.
Due to the insufficient knowledge of teachers about how to plan to use digital tools during online classes, there was a poor realization of educational outcomes in all three schools. There were gaps in knowledge that we identified and then improved the learning and teaching of mathematics in the three partner schools.


<< Objectives >>

It is expected that students will be more motivated to learn mathematics. We wanted the students to improve their knowledge of the English language. We wanted them to improve their presentation skills and learn to work in a team. Students met their peers from other countries and learned about their culture and customs. Students are expected to improve cooperation in different age groups and multicultural groups.
We wanted students to change their perception of mathematics as a difficult and inaccessible science. Students should have understood that mathematics is used everywhere. The students saw the importance of education. We wanted them to use information and communication technologies more. Students became more open. Students are expected to be willing to take on challenges.
We wanted to provide economically and socially disadvantaged students with equal opportunities to participate in activities. 

<< Implementation >>

The teachers prepared mathematical tasks related to everyday life. They researched digital materials to motivate students to work on mathematical activities. 
Schools were working on joint project activities and identifying, sharing and scaling up good practices. Through project activities, we used ICT tools and interactive panel to achieve goals. Students don't like to go in front of the blackboard and solve problems, but solving problems on the interactive panel everyone likes. They think they are playing, but they are actually learning.
 Students worked in mixed teams, which consisted of students from all three partner schools. The tasks were related to everyday life, which was an additional motivation for the students. For example: The students calculated the speed at which they moved on the bicycle and calculated the driving route or try to guess the weight of the animals that live on Brijuni.
Students created and made materials for mathematical tasks. They motivated younger students to learn mathematics using materials they made themselves. We celebrated PI Day, World Multiplication Table Day, International Day of Women in Mathematics. The teachers have organized a Mathematics Evening for students and their parents.

<< Results >>

We learned to use new ICT tools to improve the quality of teaching: Kahoot, Wordwall, Genially, Crossword Labs, Canva, Filmigo, Socrative, Mentimeter, Eductify, Matematico, Matlandia.   We used informal teaching methods and created materials related to everyday life that we presented in the teacher's manual. We implemented four eTwinning projects. We used tools for formative evaluation: Tricider, Forms, Quizizz.  Teachers and school management gained new experiences and improved their organizational skills. We used the project website, Twinspace, Facebook project website and school websites for better visibility of our activities and promotion of project results.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000031220.title: Beyond Borders: BUDDİES  not BULLIES.
2021-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000031220.summary:
<< Background >>

We, the partners, applied for this project because while we were working on the eTwinning project with the same topic we discovered that peer bullying is a common problem and harms behaviour and mental development. Since students start their social life at kindergarten and school after their families, we concluded that there is some undesirable behaviour among our students. The pandemic period made things worse because the students were frequently in cyberbullying situations on both social media and digital gaming platforms. The information is based on the Questionnaire we created at the end of the eTwinning project. Afterwards, we had evaluation meetings to determine the needs of our schools and the areas we need to improve to make our students save. 

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to show the importance of raising awareness of peer bullying and cyberbullying, to understand it correctly and take necessary precautions and develop feasible intervention programmes to prevent bullying in our schools. For every intentional and unintentional peer bullying, we aimed to eliminate the students' complaints, to guide them, to increase their interest in school, to increase their motivation, to create an atmosphere of tolerance among them, to encourage them to develop an attitude toward bullying, to increase awareness and teacher them respect, to create a democratic class and remove disadvantages, to contribute to the spiritual development of our students. In all this the inclusion of their families and the collaboration were vital. What is more, we wanted to take the best from all three educational systems to achieve the goals of the projects and get a high-quality and effective solution. Our main goal was to increase the self-confidence of our students and to develop empathy skills. 

<< Implementation >>

Through this project, we had many activities and here they are: presentation of the host school, logo creation and selection, each country presentation, theatre show on bullying and developing empathy concluded with a Kahoot quiz, group sports games to reduce peer bullying, local dance in mixed groups, quiz hunt game in mixed groups, presentations of the schools, workshop on cyberbullying, working on ebook and magazine about cyberbullying, safely using social media, role-playing and information sharing activities. In all these activities the main goals were shared with the host school and the partner schools, as well. The activities were student-centred and technology-supported. At the end of each mobility, we had a dissemination and evaluation meeting with all the participants to see if the goal had been achieved. 

<< Results >>

Our students became aware of every aspect of bullying and cyberbullying. Most of the aspects were unknown to them by that point. Many of them hadn't realized that they were bullied at some point in their life. By being aware of these aspects, they became intolerable of any kind of bullying, they memorized the action plan for what to do and when and how. Because of the strong international cooperation between our schools, we can say that our goals are achieved.

2021-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000031362.title: My eco friendly school
2021-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000031362.summary:
<< Background >>

The main reason for applying for the project was the desire to raise greater awareness of the impact of garbage on our environment among students, teachers, parents and the wider local community, as well as introducing them to strategies for recycling, reuse and reducing the production of such garbage. Our wish was to develop environmental literacy and sustainability in everyone and to raise environmentally friendly generations that will lead to a greener, better environment. We wanted to test new methods for teachers to raise new generations who think green, so that these students, as adults, will be able to choose more environmentally friendly decisions in their daily lives.
During the project development, every partner school will apply to be a certificated ECO-SCHOOL, so that all the goals reached during the project will be kept alive also for years after.
This will surely raise the quality of primary school education, providing teachers with competence and knowledge to conduct 3Rs activities, focusing on a topic that is not currently considered as priority in most European primary schools. We strongly believe that environmental education should be a focus to care of, at every age.

<< Objectives >>

OBJECTIVES 
•	to help participants create and maintain a sustainable environment through education,
•	improve pupils’ skills and competences in environmental education and sustainability of schools,
•	identify, develop and test 3R best practices with teachers of pupils aged 10-13years in the four countries,
•	raise professional/digital skills and competences of the teachers to improve education quality level,
•	engage school's staff, pupils and families in opportunities to learn about environment, waste and sustainability,
•	provide advice and guidance on how to write a successful proposal and plan a sustainable project, related to concrete needs and objectives
 SECONDARY AIMS: 
- raise awareness of materials used in every-day life, 
- distinguish which materials are recyclable and which are not,
- learn to make compost,
-raise awareness in pupils, teachers and families, of the massive use of plastics 
-help families to use natural products to replace chemical ones,
 -focus on waste reduction,
-learn how to reduce the use of materials and resources in our every-day life
-learn how to properly separate garbage for recycling,
 -reuse any kind of material that we would throw away,

<< Implementation >>

The project activities are designed on active learning methods and collaborative activities and we hope at the end of the project, each participant will be able to use the taught techniques effectively. Thanks to the 4 physical and 4 virtual staff training and project activities with students we managed achieve the project aims.

2021-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000031321.title: La progettazione europea nelle scuole superiori: strumenti innovativi e digitali in una piattaforma di formazione permanente
2021-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000031321.summary:
<< Background >>

The EUMind-School project was born from an awareness of the importance of training the next generation of professionals in European project design, for two main reasons - as of today, the European projects designer is a professional figure widely in demand, both in the public and private sectors; - knowledge of the tools and methodologies underlying European projects design inevitably entails a change of mentality in the persons trained: it opens the mind, allows to analyse the complexity of reality, facilitates multidisciplinarity, aims at effectiveness, transparency and feasibility. This is why it is essential to transfer these skills. Thanks to the close cooperation between the project partners and the network of schools it has been working with for years, the main needs identified that we have addressed during the project were - Bridging the gap between the relevance of European design and the demand for specific skills related to it in the world of work, and the curricula in EU high schools - Strengthening and updating high school teachers' European design skills - Facilitating integration between teachers of different subjects - Modernising and internationalising high school studies.

<< Objectives >>

The EUMind-School project was born out of an awareness of the importance of training the professionals of the next generation in the field of European projects designing, planning and drafting, with the concrete objective of creating a permanent platform, equipped with our innovative and digital Toolkit, for teachers and school staff in secondary schools. The EUMind-School project aimed to: Generate a new awareness in high school teachers on the value and opportunities associated with European projects - To improve the level of knowledge and competence on European planning already starting from high school Encourage active teaching through innovative teaching methodologies based on Design Thinking - To encourage interactions between schools in joint initiatives at transnational level upon shared innovation and educational needs.

<< Implementation >>

Specifically, the partnership developed a shared platform (Activity 1: Toolkit) that contains - three training modules, presented in 4 different languages (EN, IT, HR, GE) and in a creative and interactive mode (short video tutorials + in-depth library + quiz/assessment exercises) - a form/template for the realisation of the project idea - a list of digital tools for remote co-design, which is also functional for peer-review. All tools have been tested and validated through 6 national workshops and 1 transnational online workshop (Activity 2) and the project ideas, submitted through the project (at least 12), have been evaluated in peer-review mode between project partners and teachers involved during the transnational networking meeting. This platform responds to the priorities of the programme, on the one hand, by supporting teachers and students in acquiring new competencies and, on the other hand, by facilitating the acquisition of new skills and competences, by fostering digital transformation in schools and offering more interactive and dynamic methods for distance learning. Also to respond to the precise needs of the labor market of the present and of the future. 

<< Results >>

The main result of the project is a platform that contains (Acitivity 1: Toolkit): three training modules, presented in 4 different languages and in a creative and interactive way a form for the realization of the project idea; a list of digital tools for remote co-design between schools also functional to peer-review. 31 teachers have been trained and 9 schools have been involved. The students trained, in turn, have been around 600 (20 per classroom).
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff
Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2021-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000031501.title: Putting Music and Drama in play against Peer and Cyber-Bullying
2021-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000031501.summary:
<< Background >>

The main objective of this work was  to prevent and reduce aggressive behaviors among school children -to make bullying prevention a priority in our schools .Every student has the  right to feel emotionally and physically safe while at school. We tried to make sure every student understood what bullying is and that it is unacceptable-We  established classroom rules with specific examples of what is acceptable and unacceptable. We identified  the most socially-vulnerable students at the school and established intervention for them, and determined what makes them feel successful. We helped  them to  develop friendships and make connections at the school through joined work in music and drama projects. -We empowered  the school’s bystanders The key was to  break the silence surrounding bullying. And what best way to break this up  than through drama and music plays that addressed those issues -by inspiring – and at the same time we ensured teachers and administrators were committed to addressing bullying. Bullies always feel empowered and victims feel like no one cares. With music and drama programs this issue was  addressed  by assigning prestigious roles to bullied children and developing partnership with parents 

<< Objectives >>

•	Prevention of Aggressive Behaviors: The main goal was  to reduce bullying among school children by making bullying prevention a priority. This involved establishing clear classroom rules about acceptable behaviors and intervention programs for socially vulnerable students. 
•	• Empowerment and Awareness: We empowered bystanders in schools to break the silence surrounding bullying, primarily through music and drama activities. 
•	The project aimed to develop empathy, understanding, and good citizenship among students and achieve Parental and Community Involvement. 
•	The project  aimed to developed partnerships with parents to support and extend the impact of the program beyond the school environment. Increasing parental involvement is seen as a critical step in deterring school bullying


<< Implementation >>

•	Activities was focused on learning, teaching, and training, with emphasis on musical performances, workshops, and collaboration among students and teachers from different countries. These activities were  tailored to address various aspects of bullying and its prevention
 • Rehearsals and performances of musicals on peer bullying.
 • Workshops on cyber-bullying.
 • Learning and singing the European Union anthem.
 • Joint dance and thetre performances 
•	Ice-breaker activities and discussions 
We :
•	 made a logo of the project 
•	 made a Jiingle as musical symbol of the project  
•	 Set up a website of the project 
•	 set up  dissemination events

2021-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000027221.title: Różnorodność czyni nas wyjątkowymi.
2021-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000027221.summary:
<< Background >>

The focus of the project activities was the promotion and dissemination of social inclusion, cultural diversity and tolerance in education. The increasing social, ethnic and religious diversity in Europe creates both opportunities and challenges for entire societies. According to forecasts, social diversity will continue to increase. At the same time, recent Eurostat surveys show that intolerance and social exclusion are on the rise and that some social groups feel alienated. This leads to cases of social tension and unrest. Education has a key role to play in preparing societies to deal with these phenomena. It also plays an important role in the political socialisation of European citizens. Addressing ethnic, religious, social, health and other forms of diversity is a critical aspect of education. A culturally and socially sensitive educational approach has the potential to effectively promote the inclusion of people from different social groups. Thus meeting the challenge of building tolerance in individual European countries.

<< Objectives >>

The main aim of this project was to exchange best practices in the context of an active approach for tolerance and social inclusion, in the field of ethnic, religious and physical diversity. Especially: 
- understanding the importance of diversity in the youth environment; 
- sensitising youth to the difference they meet in their environment; 
- developing empathy; 
- increasing the ability to analyse and evaluate the reality around us; 
- disseminating attitudes of tolerance and openness among students and teachers.


<< Implementation >>

Teachers took part in 5 days of mobility at a partner school in Greece, Spain, Poland or Croatia to exchange experiences in the context of promoting tolerance and diversity in the school environment and beyond. Students participating in the project went on a week-long school exchange to Spain, Greece, Croatia or Poland, in order to take part in anti-discrimination workshops and to test and improve scenarios developed by teachers. 

<< Results >>

Main results of the project: 
- preparation of 4 scenarios of anti-discrimination workshops aimed at disseminating the idea
of social implementation, openness to diversity and tolerance,
- conducting anti-discrimination workshops for students of schools from Spain, Poland, Greece, Croatia and implementing the plan of the workshops in the curriculum of these
schools. 
Thanks to this, we managed to gain the scale effect, disseminating the project results beyond the direct group of students.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
