2021-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000027282.title: Różnorodność, która może łączyć.
2021-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000027282.summary:
<< Background >>

Primary School No. 5 in Swarzędz implemented teacher training projects within the Erasmus+ program. The team of teachers who took part in these trainings, expanded their base of international connections, introduced new solutions and good practices learned while observing the work of other european countries teachers, and as the next step, they wanted to involve students in an international cooperation. An excellent opportunity to implement this intention are projects of international cooperation between schools. We invited schools that have similar needs to us, to cooperate. Through the eTwinning platform, got in touch with the future coordinator from the primary school in Recale, Italy, and from the primary school in Hrvatska Kostajnica, Croatia. Each side was eager to join the project on cultural diversity. Schools submitted to the joint project indicated the need to develop intercultural dialogue, because they function in environments where immigrants with children come. They have some experience with this and were willing to share it. Showing a broader horizon of cultural diversity was to support the process of opening up to new experiences in international contacts.


<< Objectives >>

Primary School No. 5 in Swarzędz implemented teacher training projects within the Erasmus+ program. The team of teachers who took part in these trainings, expanded their base of international connections, introduced new solutions and good practices learned while observing the work of other european countries teachers, and as the next step, they wanted to involve students in an international cooperation. An excellent opportunity to implement this intention are projects of international cooperation between schools. We invited schools that have similar needs to us, to cooperate. Through the eTwinning platform, got in touch with the future coordinator from the primary school in Recale, Italy, and from the primary school in Hrvatska Kostajnica, Croatia. Each side was eager to join the project on cultural diversity. Schools submitted to the joint project indicated the need to develop intercultural dialogue, because they function in environments where immigrants with children come. They have some experience with this and were willing to share it. Showing a broader horizon of cultural diversity was to support the process of opening up to new experiences in international contacts.


<< Implementation >>

For acquainting the communities from the schools engaged in the project, the eTwinning project "Let's meet each other. Variety that units." was used. https://school-education.ec.europa.eu/en/etwinning/projects/lets-meet-each-other-variety-unities. School communities were presented with the assumptions of the Erasmus+ project that is coming into force. On the basis of joint arrangements, three five-day meetings of international groups were prepared and conducted. At school in Croatia, then in Italy and finally in Poland. Meetings of school delegations were a time of special mobilization of entire school communities. The host school had to prepare a detailed timetable involving teachers, young people, families and local authorities. Each meeting was a great challenge, the first experience of this type for all of us. That's why you could feel every effort to ensure the highest quality of these meetings. All elements of the plan were repeatedly consulted during online meetings, by correspondence (via e-mail) or in groups created for this purpose on WhatsApp. Project teams faced challenges that required efficient management, teamwork, organizational skills and support from the local community.


<< Results >>

During the visit of delegation groups, classes, workshops, trips, integration meetings and joint games were organized. The host school has always tried to involve as many people as possible from its community. It was successful and indeed this week of project activities was an important time for all students, teachers and those of the parents who responded to the invitation to cooperate, because they understand the value of this type of activity.
The search for common features of our cultures was supported by classes during which a dictionary of three languages ​​was created, covering basic concepts from everyday life. Vocabulary cards have been created, on the basis of which conclusions can be drawn about the proximity of cultures. Together, the genesis of similarities and differences was sought.
In other classes, a timeline was created. All groups were prepared for this task. During its implementation, important historical events were compared and their common or different causes and effects were sought.
Music groups and regional dances were presented in each of the schools. The flageolet workshops according to the innovative method of Mr. Wojciech Wietrzyński initiated learning to play this instrument.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2021-1-PT01-KA210-SCH-000032333.title: Integrating Cultural Heritages to the Digital World

2021-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000034315.title: CLICK- CLEAR LEARNING IN COMPUTER KNOWLEDGE
2021-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000034315.summary:
<< Background >>

Too often we see children and adults who misuse or abuse technology without being sure what they are doing. The problem is not so much what users do not know, but what is considered the appropriate use of technology. Parents point out that children spend a lot of time spending their time on devices and have violent behavior. Parents are not aware of the risks of device usage in excess and without the guidance of the adult and do not know about the existence of parental control solutions;  Highschoolers from all 4 partner schools use devices for fun; existing educational content is considered unattractive and boring;  Devices are used because they do not know other ways of spending their free time in the family; Educators have mixed opinions in what the usage of devices in teaching situations in concerned. Teachers pointed out that there is not enough digital educational content; The motivation of the project lies in the desire to change the current perception of devices not being  considered educational tools but just a means of entertainment. Good practice guides will develop a network of future users and will be enriched with the subsequent experience.

<< Objectives >>

The project aims at enhancing safe device use for educational purposes. O1 Creating a learning environment to acquire digital skills and integrate them in the educational process using devices for 80 teachers, 800 disadvantaged high schoolers and 800 parents in 4 partner high schools O2 Raising the number of  beneficiaries who use devices as an efficient learning tool O3 Increasing parents’ awareness of the safe use of modern  technology (from 200 
 parents to 800- 75%) until June, 2023 as compared to January1, 2021
One of the important objectives of school education is building skills and abilities, and in this respect technology can be used as a means of  integrated education. In the future education will be highly computerized, so the younger generation should have competencies in using the technology, just as past generations used the paper and the  pencil in their times. The project supports innovative practices in a digital area by introducing devices as an efficient learning toolThrough the inclusion of the 800 high school students from disadvantaged groups , we will ensure social inclusion.


<< Implementation >>

Project activities will be organized in a sequential, end-to-start order, that is, linking the end event of the previous activity to the beginning of the next activity. For children: monthly learning workshops will start in the 4th month of the project with every month dedicated to a web2tool. The monthly frequency keeps up children's interest and empowers them to practice and improve the assimilated knowledge. The workshops will be integrated into the daily routine For parents: there will be 1 Parenting course on how to handle children’s use of technology, in the 6th month of the project, and 1 course on safe use of electronic devices in the13th month of the project. This course will raise awareness of the parents’ decisive role in
the teenagers relationship with the 'devices and connection to the virtual world and will analyze good practice in using
devices at home. The teachers will participate to monthly activities, and
responsibilities will be shared equitably to avoid stress. They will participate to 2 courses on improving digital
competences. These training events will be organized by teachers or volunteers and will benefit from the presence of students.

<< Results >>

Output 1-Methodical Guideline for the Integration of Digital Applications in the Didactic Scenario in English and project languages; raise up to 90% of teachers using devices to facilitate learning; raise up to 75% of the number of disadvantaged students using devices as a learning tool; O3 Increasing parents’ awareness of the safe use of modern technology (from 200 parents to 600- 75%) until June, 2023 as compared to january1, 2021 Results: Output 2-A Guide of Good Practices (in English and project languages) to be used by parents to ensure safety use of electronic devices; 600 trained parents through a course on parenting on safe use of technology, and more parents aware of how to safeguard their children when using such technology. The use of devices in high-schools facilitates the transmission and assimilation of new knowledge in an attractive way, thus raising the efficiency and the quality of learning.new skills for 80 teachers, 1 course for 600 parents; modern learning environment, 100 printed advertising brochures; 10 advertising materials in the media (like press or TV).A Guide of Good Practices (in English and project languages) to be used by parents to ensuresafety use of electronic devices;
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000034318.title:

(5 je za: otroci, vzgojitelji, starši, zunanji sodelavci, družba)
2021-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000034318.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because analyzes of the situation in both kindergartens showed us that:
*children with fewer opportunities need different approaches to achieve the same goals as other children; that they need additional did. aids and need to be additionally supported during their development, because only in this way will they be able to become more confident and active in everyday events, as well as more active co-creators of the European environment.
*the key competencies (for working with children with fewer opportunities) among professional kindergarten workers are too few and too weak, and they need to be strengthened both in terms of different approaches to working with children with fewer opportunities and to strengthen them personally - so that they are satisfied and happy at work, that they have confidence in themselves, in the educational system, and that they are thus strengthened and more adaptable to changes in everyday life.
From both analyses, we extracted the fact that employees who are happy at their workplace feel trust and respect, and are able to share these competences further, primarily among children, and especially among children with fewer opportunities.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to achieve the following goals:
C1- to empower children with fewer opportunities for greater active participation in everyday life in kindergarten, the local environment and the EU; to teach them additional cooperation skills - to empower them in the areas of active participation, to raise their self-esteem, to understand their possibilities despite fewer opportunities; better equip them with skills and knowledge so that later in life they will be more successful, cooperate more easily, be more confident in their abilities and thus become more active later in cooperation in the local environment and in Europe.
C2- equip educators with such knowledge and competences that they can offer children with fewer opp. a sufficiently supportive and active environment that would enable them to participate more, because dissatisfaction at the workplace and neglecting the feeling of happiness at the workplace reduces trust, respect and self-belief, in educational system, and this makes employees less adaptable to changes in everyday life, less self-confident when working with children and less active citizens.
C3-we want both children with fewer opportunities and kindergarten teacher to create inclusive environment 4all.

<< Implementation >>

The activities will be:
 - initial m.= the introductory meeting was first held in each participating partner organization, where we agreed on the selection and work-as professional colleagues to participate in LTT activities. At the internal meeting, we prepared material for the initial meeting (kick off meeting via the ZOOM application) of the two partner teams. Also, each partner internally prepared a basic plan for that task (responsibility).
The ZOOM meeting was attended by all members of the internal team for the Erasmus+ project (8 members of the E+ K.Hrastnik team and 7 members of the E+ K.Rijeka team).
- LTT activities took place twice in Hrastnik Kindergarten and twice in Rijeka Kindergarten. Each meeting had a common note - the acquisition of key competences of educators for happiness in the workplace and, consequently, to strengthen competences for working with children with fewer opportunities.
-- international meetings for children with fewer opportunities (all on-line): we held a series of meetings with different children (individual, collective, group) on different (pre-arranged) topics.
- management and project management;
-dissemination with multiplicative;
-HIGH5 Academy;
-multisensory romm

<< Results >>

We achieved the following results and outcomes:
R1- adequate equipment of rooms and accessories for children with fewer opp. (for children with special needs, we arranged multi-sensory  rooms for the development of all senses by including sensory integration; for children from socially weaker backgrounds - a socially and emotionally stimulating environment with a safe corner in the shared (sensory) room; acquired more children's literature in their mother tongue for immigrant children and arranged a corner for relaxed speech in the native language (supported by book and picture material);
R2- we conducted training for 7 participants from the Hrastnik K. and 7 participants from the Rijeka K. under the title ambassador of the HIGH5 Academy. On  65-hour training, we prepared precise strategies for introducing more work happiness into every organization, founded 'Happy team' which as multipliers, further educate their colleagues about the importance of their own happiness and satisfaction in the workplace, which together ensure a more stable and strengthened employee, who is able to cope with daily changes and which is thus able to strengthen, among others, children with fewer opp. The website was created,which is publicly accessible.

2021-1-SK01-KA210-SCH-000031488.title: NATURE AND PHOTO
2021-1-SK01-KA210-SCH-000031488.summary:
<< Background >>

In most schools used teaching methods do not keep up with the requirements of nowadays, in terms of the required professional qualifications and the interests of the students.There is a lack of experimentation and interaction.Students are often sceptical about the usefulness of the material taught. 2021-1-TR01-KA210-SCH-000031242.title: Creating a Global ESL Classroom via Web 2.0 Tools
2021-1-TR01-KA210-SCH-000031242.summary:
<< Background >>

With the transition to distance education during the pandemic, we realized that digitalization is inevitable in the field of education and both students and teachers had experienced some difficulties during the online classes, specifically while using Web 2.0 tools. In addition, the partnership had also identified the lack of motivation felt by a number of students in the SWOT analysis carried out for the 2018-2023 strategic plan, which identified the need to find more efficient language teaching methods and techniques to improve the teaching of a foreign language and support technology-addicted students so that these could use their skills in a more productive way.
 We applied for this project as it centers on the integration of Web 2.0 tools into  teaching of English as a Foreign Language with a dynamic and innovative approach to language education. This initiative not only harnesses the power of technology to engage and motivate students but also cultivates a collaborative and interactive learning environment. The project enhances language acquisition by embracing contemporary methodologies, preparing both teachers and learners for the digital era, and contributing to a more effective and globally connected language education. 

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, the partnerships aimed to go beyond the traditional classroom through the following:
•	Facilitate enhanced interactivity and engagement in the learning process, offering students opportunities to collaborate on projects, share ideas, and receive immediate feedback.
•	Provide tools for authentic language use by incorporating multimedia elements, such as videos, podcasts, and interactive simulations, thereby promoting practical language skills. 
•	Improve communication skills by engaging students in online discussions, and collaborative writing platforms with students from other countries. 
•	Foster a more student-centered approach, by accommodating diverse learning styles and promoting self-directed learning. 
•	Encourage technology-addicted students to use technology for more useful purposes and to support lifelong learning.
By implementing the integration of web 2.0 tools in foreign language education we also aimed to work in cooperation with European countries and establish a cultural connection.
Overall, the use of Web 2.0 tools in EFL classes enriches the educational experience, making language learning more dynamic, relevant, and aligned with the demands of the digital age. 


<< Implementation >>

The project was launched with a virtual meeting that provided the partnership  to define strategies, assign individual partner tasks, share best practices, and refine teaching strategies. 
It was followed by the Teacher Training Course on Web 2.0 tools in the Netherlands, equipping all partner teachers with the knowledge and skills needed for innovative language teaching aided by Web 2.0 Tools.
In addition, each country hosted an LTTA tailored to its focus: Turkey emphasized Enhancing Speaking & Listening Skills, Portugal targeted Reading & Writing Skills, while Croatia focused on Web 2.0 tools for enhanced presentation skills.  Our intent was to empower teachers, engage students, and elevate language learning to new heights across borders. Mobilities in each partner country brought these practices to life, allowing participants to witness firsthand the impact of Web 2.0 tools on language education and to engage in immersive, cross-cultural experiences that enrich teaching methodologies.
To foster international collaboration and provide a platform for shared learning experiences, in addition to the European School Education Platform (TwinSpace) a Common International Weblog was created to  showcase the language learning journey.

<< Results >>

The implementation of our multifaceted approach to language education, enriched by Web 2.0 tools, has yielded tangible and transformative outcomes. Through dedicated online meetings, Teacher Training Course in the Netherlands, we have fostered a robust global learning community. Teachers are now equipped with the expertise to harness the power of Web 2.0 tools effectively, enhancing their teaching methodologies.
The LTTA’s have brought about noteworthy results in each partner country. In Turkey, the focus on "Enhancing Speaking & Listening Skills through Web 2.0 Tools" has led to a marked improvement in oral communication proficiency. Portugal's emphasis on "Enhancing Reading & Writing Skills through Web 2.0 tools" has resulted in enriched literacy capabilities among students. Meanwhile, Croatia's focus on "Web 2.0 Tools for a Better Presentation" has improved students' ability to convey ideas effectively.
Collectively, these initiatives have not only elevated language learning experiences but have also established a foundation for sustainable international collaboration and cultural exchange. Our project has successfully merged technology and pedagogy, creating a lasting impact on language education.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2021-1-TR01-KA210-SCH-000032316.title: Climate Change Deserves to be in the Curricula
2021-1-TR01-KA210-SCH-000032316.summary:
<< Background >>

We wanted to include environment and climate change in the course curriculum because when we examined some curricula, we found out that they were not included in the course content. We thought that students should make positive behavioral changes by frequently being exposed to environmental and climate change. Considering that we need to include environment and climate change in the course curriculum.we planned to use a latent learning method, therefore teachers of all levels would not fall behind in their curriculum in general. We thought of including a digital learning path to attract students' attention. We planned to raise students' awareness by placing stimuli about the environment and climate change within latent learning. Since this teaching will be carried out simultaneously by many lessons, students will easily gain awareness and result in behavioral change. 

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to achieve an awareness of environment and climate change for students and enriched training methods for teachers who could upgrade themselves throughout our project. We aimed to provide related instructions for teachers in terms of integrating environment and climate change into their curriculum latently and digital game competence and soft skills. Our objective is to make a meaningful contribution towards mitigating greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, aligning with the European Union's established target. This endeavor hinges upon the successful adoption of behavioral changes pertaining to environmental stewardship and climate resilience.We targeted to create an e-brochure, an e-book and a handbook for teachers. We considered creating an implementation of orienteering for students to explore a specific natural vicinity and the essentials of environment and climate change.

<< Implementation >>

Our initiative commenced with a compact seminar led by our Croatian partner, exploring environmental and climate change topics. Subsequently, presentations delved into the contributions of partner countries to climate change and governmental efforts in mitigation, along with exemplary organizational practices. Carbon footprint assessments were conducted using a free application, with results shared with Croatian leadership for comparison at project culmination. Romanian team members facilitated training sessions on digital game-based and latent learning techniques for project participants. These educators then produced 10 digital games each for students and teachers from partner countries, fostering engagement with environmental issues. A collaborative effort resulted in the creation of a Teachers’ Handbook and an orienteering activity utilizing the digital games. Our outreach extended beyond beneficiaries to encompass additional institutions and trainers, involving informational sessions, press releases, announcements, and webinars to disseminate project insights. 

<< Results >>

Tangible results are project introduction film, eBrochure, eBook, Project website, eTwinning project, Handbook called ‘Teachers’ Handbook’, which presents how to integrate environment and climate change into curricula using digital game based learning activities with the power of latent learning, including the partnership and project info, the digital games used for the project, trainings on latent learning, sample lesson plans regarding the aim of the project, the results and analysis  of carbon footprint calculation, and the webinar presenting the inevitable need of environmet and climate change integration into curricula of all partners' countries.

Intangible results are the students with awareness on environment climate change, English language competences, improved soft skills, better self-confidence and more tolerated towards other people from other countries with enlarged perspectives; the teachers who developed themselves in environment and climate change, the inevitable existence of it in the curricula of all types of branches and domains.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-TR01-KA210-SCH-000032340.title: Evliya Çelebi'nin Atının Sırtında Zamanda Yolculuk
2021-1-TR01-KA210-SCH-000032340.summary:
<< Background >>

The fact that our students have insufficient knowledge on issues such as cultural heritage and European common heritage and that students are not sufficiently interested in such issues is sometimes revealed in lessons and activities. Based on this, according to the survey conducted in all partner schools, it was observed that 61,95 % of the students do not have sufficient knowledge and interest in historical and cultural heritage. As a result, more than half of the students at partner schools unfortunately aren’t aware of the cultural heritage and values, which lead us to apply for the project. On the other hand, globalisation, which is defined as an international integration arising from the exchange of products, ideas, cultures and world views, leads to the weakening of the local cultures of countries and the elimination of differences in order to create a uniform culture. In this context, it was considered that this project should be implemented in an international framework through intercultural information exchange in order to raise awareness among young people from different cultures on cultural heritage in order to protect the European common heritage to ensure that cultural heritage is preserved for the next generations.



<< Objectives >>

We wanted to achieve to ensure that students firstly gain awareness about their own tangible and intangible cultural heritage and to raise their level of awareness, to encourage students to interact with the peers from different cultures and to raise their awareness of the similarities between cultures and the common heritage of Europe ,to enable students to build a bridge between cultures by making use of cultural diversity and to recognise common values and to understand that cultural diversity is a richness that contributes to the common European heritage ,to revise the information described by Evliya Çelebi in the light of today and to arouse students' sense of curiosity by making comparisons between civilisation of that period and that of present,to enable students to shed light on the cultures of the places travelled, perhaps unknown or forgotten by the people of the places visited,to improve students' communication skills and foreign language skills by communicating with individuals of different languages, religions and cultures,to create awareness about environment and climate change by comparing past environmental conditions with present ones, to develop students' digital skills, to reach more people by this project.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented virtual mobility via presentations by using video clips or slides. At the physical mobilities, students drew the historical and cultural elements described in the Seyahatname in the cities of the project before the mobilities and after the cities were visited they  prepared and exhibited the collages by comparing them with their current state. All the cities of the project were visited and cultural elements were determined whether they still exist or not. Notes, photos and videos were taken. Mixed teams were established and digital and real posters were made about these elements.Some of the 26 kinds of compotes and local food that Evliya Çelebi tasted in these lands were prepared and taste by mixed teams of partners. Some stories from The Seyahatname were revived. Common words among the partners were searched. Drawing activities of some artifacts were performed. Past and present elements were compared. Some endemic plants were planted. Virtual magazines or video presentations were prepared. Ebru (art of marbling) activity was performed. A common songs choir was performed. Culture Street was established. Agiant canvas painting activity was prepared by common groups. A final virtual and physical booklet was published.

<< Results >>

According to last online survey which was performed by the participants after the mobilities,all the questions were replied mostly as ‘Yes’ 80.5%.This means we reached our initial goals interms of green environment,digital skills,cultural awareness,language skills,communication skills,social skills,common European hetitage awareness,tangible and intangible heritage awareness. The survey results were uploaded on the digital platforms of the project. By recognizing cultural similarities and differences,the sustainability of these riches were ensured. Curiosity was awakened in students.Intercultural learning and international cooperation were ensured. Students were more socialized thus their foreign language skills and digital skills were developed.The students became more sensitive about the environment through the virtual and the physical mobility activities. Surveys of surviving places after each mobility were filled in all by the project members and comparing past and present documents were formed. A virtual magazine including all the activities of all the mobilities and comparisons between past and present conditions of the tangible and intangible heritage has been prepared. Finally, it has been published as a booklet.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2021-2-FI01-KA210-SCH-000051088.title: EMPOWERING YOUNG CHILDREN TO ACT ON CLIMATE CHANGE
2021-2-FI01-KA210-SCH-000051088.summary:
<< Background >>

During our project preparation stage, we made a research on tools, materials and articles about climate change education in
kindergartens. We noticed that there was a lack of materials, training or awareness for Pre-K to Grade 1 and 2 teachers and
we would like to rectify that by creating and designing materials to empower teachers and young children about climate
change through play and creative drama with an emphasis of being outdoors as well as provide training for teachers and
equipping them with toolkits to conduct sessions in schools. Our main goals were; raise awareness of teachers in pre-school institutions about climate change and to establish a connection with nature in children through effective tools for young children such as games and drama, and to develop the ability to adapt and take precautions against climate change. The needs were to establish an international dialogue, enable the emergence of a climate action network and tackle the lack of materials and training to empower Pre-K to Grades 1 and 2 teachers and young children through experiential learning in a positive way.


<< Objectives >>

Objectives of our project: 
 1) Creating a network for training, discussions and brainstorming sessions with institutions from European countries like Croatia, Finland, Portugal and Turkey. It is important to understand each country's position about climate change, their government policies, local sustainability efforts and their educational materials on climate change action (if any).
2) Creating new, innovative tools on sustainability and climate action related teaching materials for Preschool levels.
3) Designing and building toolkits and policies to accompany curriculum to foster nature based activities and climate education.
4) Drawing up plans with teachers and relevant stakeholders of the schools on how to implement environmentally friendly practices in schools and the communities around them.
5) Getting experience on Erasmus Plus opportunities and building partnerships for future projects.
6) Knowing creative drama and game based activities as a tool for climate education.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities of the project were;  3-day climate education and sustainability training course in Finland,
5-day creative drama and play-based learning training course in Turkey for adaptation to climate change, Elaboration of Climate Education toolkit for educators, Elaboration of Climate Education and sustainability in kindergartens Policy document through a 2 day project meeting in Portugal, an online dissemination activity and other local dissemination activities run by our partners.

The collaborative work throughout the implementation can be seen and found on the partners common google drive here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1yrEZKOPA8xnu6j6HG9sq_YaN7yji4954?usp=share_link 

<< Results >>

Policy Recommendations for Climate Education and a Climate Education Toolkit for Kindergarten Teachers was created as outcomes of the project which can be downloaded in 5 languages (English,Finnish, Portuguese, Turkish and Croatian)

POLICY RECOMMENDATION
'Children Act on Climate Change' Policy for Kindergartens is a policy proposal for kindergartens. It is a strategic approach for making schools more nature friendly, productive and aware of climate change. 
.
CLIMATE EDUCATION MANUAL FOR EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATORS
This toolkit introduces the concept of Climate Education, presents best practices in Europe, and offers a selection of 15 games and activities to engage children indoors and outdoors, as well as conclusions and references. It is addressed to teachers and parents who could use it as a guide to connect children to nature, which is essential for adaptation to a changing climate. The toolkit is dowloadable in 5 different languages.

2 online meetings, 3 video clips of the transnational activities are other outputs of the project. 
Please find all the outputs of the project on the following link: https://www.learninginnature.com/empowering-young-children-to-act-on-climate-change
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000048378.title: Cultural minorities as a valuable source for a better inclusion: Integration Not Assimilation
2021-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000048378.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we felt our local Italian minority, specifically the youth, would benefit from experiencing how another minority manages to survive despite lacking population and funding. Also, our students, while capable in the ICT department, lacked equipment and specific skills required in the modern world. We felt that combining ICT skills and equipment with the issues minorities face might strengthen their sense of belonging and raise awareness. The needs we have addressed include ICT equipment, software, courses and a cultural exchange, all aimed at addressing the aforementioned issues.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to promote a sense of belonging to one's minority, to view it as an asset rather than a hindrance, and to raise awareness on the issues minorities face, specifically the Italian one in Rijeka (Croatia), and the Croatian one in the region of Molise (Italy).

<< Implementation >>

- Web design course
- Web page maintenance
- Photography and cinematography course
- Production of a short film
- Cultural exchange in Molise, Italy
- Cultural exchange in Rijeka, its surroundings, and Istria, Croatia
- Zoom and Viber meetings
- Surveys

<< Results >>

Outputs: Web page, short film, press articles, TV appearances, photos, ICT equipment, course diplomas
Other results: cross-cultural dialogue, establishment of new partnerships, new ICT skills (web design, photography and filmmaking)

hr.name: Srednja Talijanska škola - Rijeka Scuola Media Superiore Italiana - Fiume

2021-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000048412.title: DIFFERENT BUT TOGETHER!
2021-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000048412.summary:
<< Background >>

Through continuous monitoring of students, we have noticed that students are increasingly using digital aids: smartphones and tablets. All information is readily and easily available to them. All this causes short-term memory in students and reduced cognitive abilities. They are showing less and less interest in lasting values (necessary for lifelong learning) and find it very hard to express themselves. Through conversations with students and conducted surveys, we have noticed their poor knowledge about their own culture and traditions. Another problem we have noticed is poor oral communication of students. They tend not to communicate verbally with each other which results in increased difficulties with expressing their own opinions, attitudes and feelings. By including students in drama workshops it was noticed that through role playing students work much more easily in a team, take a stand and express their view on different topics. That was especially noticed in students with behavioral difficulties.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of the project is to develop students' awareness about the importance of preserving cultural heritage as a guardian of our own national identity. By getting to know the culture and traditions of other nations, by noticing similarities and differences between nations and their traditions, we wanted to increase tolerance and acceptance of the different and diverse among students. This path is a step towards creating a peaceful coexistence between nations. Moreover, implemetation of dramatic methods in classes encourages a relaxed atmosphere that enables students to express themselves easily and icreases their creativity and self-esteem. Such approach provides easier mastering of teaching content and reduces inappropriate behavior in class. By learning about new digital tools students will be able to present the project and its results from their own perspective.

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the project, we organized visits to several cultural institutions (theatre, museum, library) and got to know their activities and employees. We researched the customs, legends and traditions of project participants. We participated in the creation of the project logo. In mobilities we organized numerous workshops and activities. In Austria we were introduced to various drama methods under the expert guidance of a drama pedagogue. In Croatia the students and their teachers prepared two theatrical performances by William Shakespeare using the knowledge gained in Austria. We also attended handicraft workshops (making licit hearts and ceramic vessels, workshop of Lepoglava lace ). In Turkey we got to know their legends through dramatic methods. In Poland, under the expert guidance of professional actors, students mastered the basic techniques important for acting and tried to solve the problem of bullying through a dramatic presentation. A workshop on making traditional souvenirs - Macrame and preparing traditional food (pierogi) was organised. As a part of mobility activities, each participating organisation organized excursions where we got to know the history and traditions of the hosting country.

<< Results >>

Project resulted in a direct acquaintance with the historical and geographical features of the partner countries and their traditions along with the expansion of our knowledge, which was limited to textbook material. This way the participants of the project activities are encouraged to respect those who are different while developing mutual acceptance and tolerance. By organized visits to cultural institutions (theatre, museum, library) students had the opportunity to see its activity and employees (screenwriters, directors, costume designers). The next important result is active application of dramatic methods adopted in project activities conducted by drama pedagogue and academic actors. These methods are applied in classes and in school events intended for the wider local community (students and their parents, colleagues, local population). Using digital tools all the results were presented to the
participating organizations and the wider community. The results were presented on the school website, local newspapers, the  official website of the projects and on Facebook page. Each organisation created an e-book that is available on the Erasmus+ Project Results Platform. The results were also presented at dissemination events.

2021-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000048840.title: RECYCLE RE-CONSUME
2021-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000048840.summary:
<< Background >>

Food waste is one of the biggest today’s problem. Our project aimed to convert recyclable and reusable food into a new product ready for consumption in order to minimize food waste and contribute first to our institutions’ economy and then to global economies that will embrace new ways of consuming food. With simple precautions on a daily bases, we can prevent the food considered waste from actually becoming waste. We also aimed to draw more attention to raising awareness that food that is thought to be a leftover can be recycled and consumed. With that, significant reductions in food waste can be decreased, although our main goal was to increase consumers' awareness about food waste and disseminate the knowledge whenever possible. The needs addressed in this project were based on a survey applied to target groups (students, aged 15-19, studying in the culinary sector or hotel management), where we realized that in today's educational system for before mentioned sectors is a wide gap in knowledge about Recycling -Reconsuming. Our goal was to raise awareness among students who are soon to be employed in the culinary industry about the amount of food that is thrown away every day and the possibilities of recycling and reconsuming it

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project we wanted to reduce the negative consequences of food waste, which is a global problem, also we wanted to increase the awareness of our students who were participating in the project, to raise awareness about food waste. We aimed to contribute to the economy of the institutions and countries by recycling the edible parts of the food that are thought to be waste and making this widespread.

<< Implementation >>

We had 3 activities implemented in our project: 1. Making recycled food from stale bread, 2. Making recycled products from vegetable and fruit peels; 3. Making recycled products from vegetable and fruit juices. Before each activity we had seminars "How to..." with teachers and students.

<< Results >>

Our students gained knowledge, awareness and sensitivity about waste. We ensured the sustainability of the production of recycled products to reduce food waste in our schools. Our students shared their achievements and knowledge gained on the project to their friend circles and made this project reach large masses. We increased awareness about food waste, which has become increasingly dangerous on a global scale, and hope we reduced some economic losses.
topics: Economic and financial affairs (including funding issues)

2021-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000049445.title: Growing young ECOlogists with STEM
2021-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000049445.summary:
<< Background >>

In the past, all schools were involved with different projects, mostly at national level regarding several topics. Furthermore, they showed a sincere interest in the activities of each project and urged us to continue our effort in the future. As cultivating environmental awareness seems imperative for the future generations we thought that starting a project that gains insight in the consumption of energy and the use of R.E.S. as well as recycling would make the future citizens of the European Union more active in school. School buildings should be transformed into sustainable ones and, although the progress will be rather slow, we need to find a starting point. This is the main reason that we applied for this project.
Therefore, we share the strong conviction that by projects like ours we can change the involvement of this process and consequently reduce the deterioration of the environment. Educating young people about the ways they can handle environmental issues in schools as strategic places can promote the change of habits in individuals but also attract the interest of the authorities to make radical changes.


<< Objectives >>

We aimed at promoting an understanding in depth of the crucial value of environmental education and how it will help us to become a more active citizen of the 21st century.
-raising ecological awareness
-promoting inclusive eco-education
-upgrading teaching methods
-providing an opportunity for exposure of new researches
-defining and sharing good practices
-developing transversal, entrepreneurial and organizational skills
-promoting the use of foreign languages and STEM


<< Implementation >>

Three face to face transnational meetings were held, in Greece, Portugal and Croatia in which training sessions for students and teachers will be held.
Two virtual workshops followed with discussion took place through an online platform for the implementation of the activities.
One dissemination event and three open days were organised
All the activities beside the three physical meetings were uploaded to our YouTube channel and the website of the project for wider dissemination


<< Results >>

The main results were:
- the production of an Energy Efficiency Certificate for each partner and the calculation of the ecological footprint
- the use of eco friendly bins in each school
- the implementation of STEM applications at the school laboratory 
- guidelines, best-practice examples, video records of the experiments/workshops
- an online learning platfom and project website

Finally students and teachers benefited from a cultural and linguistic point of view

2021-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000050918.title: Zelena škola
2021-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000050918.summary:
<< Background >>

One of the basic goals and levers of development in the EU today is the "Green Deal", turning to green energy sources, but also creating and spreading awareness of the need for a different attitude towards nature and its resources. And while turning to green energy sources can be solved relatively easily by decisions, prohibitions or tax motivations, the issue of developing awareness of the need for a different attitude towards nature and treatment of nature is much more difficult - it implies changes in the paradigms of learning, behavior and thinking.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal in that changes is to teach those who learn how to change the established paradigms when it comes to the relationship with nature. Learning about nature in nature itself is far more effective than the same learning indoors in the classroom.
To ensure competences for teachers and educators to hold lessons in nature using the method of informal learning.
Empower - show students that their smartphones can be a tool in nature study and informal learning.
Improve students' IT skills in processing data collected through field study during field trips.


<< Implementation >>

All planned activities have been implemented in the project. In addition, some others were added for which the need but also the possibility was shown, which significantly enriched the results of the project.
Introduction to school in nature - outdoor activities are the basis for all other activities that are carried out or can be carried out. Before the trip to nature, teachers fill out a questionnaire about their attitudes towards informal learning in nature. During the trip to nature, the children are then introduced to the tasks and the way to realize them.
Using a smartphone to photograph and detect plants - school.
Observing nature and noticing details - collecting natural materials for later work - preschoolers
Elaboration of what was learned in class - creation of a digital herbarium as one of the examples.
Making souvenirs from objects found in nature - preschoolers
Creating a curriculum for teaching in nature using an informal method

<< Results >>

The results were outstanding!
A website has been created that contains many photos of plants with accompanying captions in four languages.
Several collections of souvenirs, greeting cards and other children's handicrafts were produced from objects found in nature, which are presented on the website.
The Curriculum for holding informal classes in nature for elementary schools was written and presented on the website.
A Curriculum for activities in nature for kindergartens has been written - the curriculum is presented on the website.
A manual for creating a digital herbarium has been written.
Educational games in nature are explained, as well as the way of making individual works of school and preschool children. Everything is shown on the website.
About a hundred teachers and educators from 3 countries acquired competences for conducting informal classes in nature.
A short film showing the activity was recorded.
Through the dissemination of the project, several schools are still interested or have already started to implement the elements of the project in their environment, which shows that the project activities will continue.
Tuhobić PD summer camp program will take place according to the Curriculum of the Green School project.

2021-2-HU01-KA210-SCH-000051494.title: Climate Guardians
2021-2-HU01-KA210-SCH-000051494.summary:

Our goal:
1-Develop their skills in subjects such as creating, choosing and using board games.
2-Develop measurement tools (e.g. instructions, checklists, rubrics) for assessment through games.
3-Integrate the global theme of "climate change" into lessons and develop maximum awareness of climate change, using the power of games developed for pupils' age.
4-Enhance computational and algorithmic thinking skills through designing, game development, code writing, ICT literacy,

1-Develop their skills in subjects such as creating, choosing and using board games.

3-Integrate the global theme of "climate change" into lessons and develop maximum awareness of climate change, using the power of games developed for pupils' age.

Digital citizenship skills, collaborative work.

3-The LTT activities and the "Climate guardians" games will provide teachers with a new teaching method and game-based education, the activities will support their professional work.

<< Implementation >>

During the project work we had regular online meetings. The kick-off meeting was also held online.
There were 3 LTTA activities, which were detailed in the activities section.
There was board game making, during which we developed board games together with students on the topics of environment, climate change, sustainability, tested them and prepared lesson plans for using the games in teaching. 
We have also developed games from other nations and tested them to see how understandable and enjoyable they are for children.
A questionnaire was drawn up asking children and students for their views on the extent to which teachers use play in their lessons.
To what extent do they prefer teaching to be playful.

<< Results >>

1 website and 1 facebook page were created to publicise the results of the project.
4 board games and lesson plans were produced. 2 questionnaire surveys were also carried out. 
During the LTTAs, we got to know each other's natural treasures and the educational policies of the national parks. 
We learned about the Union's and Unesco's efforts in the field of environmental education.
We exchanged experiences on the current situation in the 4 countries, the state of STEM education in schools, curricula, gamification and the use of non-formal tools and methods in education.

2021-2-IE01-KA210-SCH-000051442.title: Ecological Literacy for a Sustainable Future
2021-2-IE01-KA210-SCH-000051442.summary:
<< Background >>

The project has partners from Croatia, Romania, Ireland and Turkey.  The initial contacts was through eTwinning with all partners seeking a project on Biodiversity
and Ecology.  We recognised, post-Covid, the urgent need to implement ecological and biodiversity awareness programmes in schools as our pupils are the decision-makers of the future.  We decided to combine our skills, interests and knowledge to develop a unique Ecological Literacy programme to use in partner schools.  
 We started a little bit  because of staff changes so contracts were late. 
We had a few online meetings to meet, kickstart the project and to split tasks between partners. 
Pupils were at the core of the project.  To improve their ecological literacy, to develop communication skills as well as collaboration skills and
to enhance cultural awareness and intercultural competence they engaged in a range of mobility and virtual activities.
The representatives of each partner presented their school educational system and their town and their country .
  The tangible results of the project were the presentations, the Ecological literacy intelligence student guide, the website. The intangible results were the development of collaboration skills.


<< Objectives >>

We set out to inform our pupils of the issues and to motivate them to take initiatives to protect the environment and to raise awareness of Ecological and Biodiversity issues that face us all..  We wanted the pupils to be at the centre of their learning and to develop their ecological literacy,  enhance communication and collaboration skills,.  The goals involve creating knowledge and awareness of the issues that are common to all partners and to develop strategies and a toolkit to enable pupils and schools to tackle these issues into the future.  Students become aware of the richness of plant and animal diversity on the planet through the content produced-in terms of the Ecological booklet and other materials, presentations, lessons and pupil projects..  Teachers share information and strategies during mobilities and these findings and results are brought back from the meetings and shared with the pupils and general school community..  Shared knowledge will lead to positive actions in terms of protecting the sustainability of biodiversity and in developing knowledgeable,  proactive and caring citizens for the future.  Our pupils will see that we need to work together and form a united front to tackle common worldwide issues.

<< Implementation >>

Range of activities, both virtual and face-to-face as part of the four mobilities. 
Croatia-Drama-global food system links to climate change, Online pupil meeting videos on climate change and links to food and agriculture.
Food-Climate change link.-each school showed an interactive good practice
Prepared sustainable action plan for schools. Seminar on the impact of agriculture on the environment and climate change.
Ireland: Wind energy electronics workshop.  Making Paper workshop.  Pupil presentations: Alternative energy sources.
Teacher visit-Wind farm, lesson on the future of Wind energy for schools and the community.
Turkey Mobility: Class visit:-Building biodiversity loss reversal models, pantomime activity and alternative assessment tools for the topic of 
ecological life and environmental pollution.  Prepared content for An Interactive Guide: Ecological Literacy Guide. Guide presentation.
Virtual mobility-Plants and fauna from each country. Workshop-Building Biodiversity loss reversal models, 
-Romania--An Interactive Guide: Ecological Literacy, recycling fashion show and creative recycling exhibition
-Virtual activity: environmental awareness quiz(Kahoot) Ecosystem rope game
Worked on permacult design and butterfly garden



<< Results >>

The tangible results are the presentations, lesson plans, the Ecological literacy intelligence student guide, the website, the quizzes and the eTwinning site.   Partners have a toolkit of resources, strategies and experiences to utilise and share with other schools in their country. 
The intangible results are the development of collaboration and communication skills for pupils and teachers.  Also the development of digital skills, of sociable skills 
and acceptance of others views and opinions.   There are many inter-cultural benefits as teachers and pupils engage and collaborate with partners from a range of countries..  Communication and social skills are enhanced and further developed as are teacher and pupil self-esteem and confidence.  
Teachers gain professionally from interactions with partners.
Long term benefits are personal development and motivation to take part in future international projects. Partners created added value in innovative educational approaches. Teachers passed on what they have learnt to their school and community.  Partners have forged real-concrete partnerships and schools will continue to share best practice in tackling issues related to Climate change and threats to ecology and biodiversity,

2021-2-IT02-KA210-SCH-000048153.title: Comprehensive emotional and sexuality education from primary school
2021-2-IT02-KA210-SCH-000048153.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the XSE Erasmus+ project to address the urgent need for proper sexual and affective education during puberty to primarily counteract misleading online contents, gender-based violence and health risks. In Italy, 44% of children aged 11-12 are exposed to pornography, much higher than the global average. This premature exposure distort their understanding of sexuality and relationships, leading to potential sexist and aggressive behaviors and compromising their emotional development. Given the long history of sexual education in some EU countries, Italy and Croatia still lacked comprehensive curricula. XSE aimed, and finally contributed, to bridge this gap by promoting international educator exchanges and introducing advanced sexual education programs in these countries. By adopting best practices from more progressive countries i.e. Finland, XSE sought to build cohesive European societies that value self-care and mutual respect from a young age via the development of concrete, transferable Open Educational Resources around emotional and sexuality education, tailored on the needs of educators and community members, such as parents, while being active with primary-age kids.



<< Objectives >>

Firstly, we sought to educate children about sexuality from early childhood, following recommendations from the WHO and the Cologne Center for Health Education. Our goal was to promote healthy, aware, and balanced development through holistic sexual education that provides impartial and scientifically accurate information, fostering respectful and open attitudes for building equitable societies.
To support the continuous training of educators working with children aged 6-9 on emotional and sexual literacy, and to enhance soft skills and inclusive, respectful attitudes, XSE had the following objectives:
- Enable educators to adopt best practices and innovative methodologies to teach the cognitive, emotional, physical, social, and legal aspects of sexuality.
- Deepen understanding and support for parenting, recognizing the crucial role families play in shaping gender stereotypes and emotional expression.
- Enhance programs to strengthen soft skills through emotional literacy, proven to reduce bullying and sexual harassment, and improve self-esteem, conflict management, trust and cultural sensitivity.

<< Implementation >>

The consortium implemented the following activities:
- Identification and collection of 12 inspiring practices for emotional literacy aimed at sexuality education of children in puberty age, gathering them in a multilingual Compendium;
- 3-days Study visit to 3 inspiring realities in Finland, alongside meetings with 3 well known local experts;
- Development of a multilingual toolkit for educators (applied methodologies are: art therapy, humanistic coaching, psychodrama, dialogue on feelings, sexuality and relationships), having been piloted in 3 countries, within 3 schools and 1 cultural association, involving tot. 53 kids and 34 parents in 4-9 sessions per country;
- Exploitation of results at the national level in the form i.e. of policy reforms (Croatia) and follow up initiatives within schools (Italy), as well as at the European level in the form of a concept note to be submitted in the spring 2025 Erasmus+ KA2-SCH deadline as a full proposal by the consortium and beyond.

<< Results >>

XSE developed tools to support the continuing education of educators/operators who work with children 6-9 years on the issues of emotional and sexual literacy, for better soft skills and more inclusive and respectful attitudes:
- 1 multilingual (EN, IT, HR, PT) Compendium on the cognitive, emotional, physical, social and legal aspects of sexuality for pubertal children. This compendium also included direct experiences gathered through interviews with European sectoral experts;
- development and transnational pilot of a comprehensive Toolkit (EN, IT, HR, PT) for emotional literacy tailored for primary school children across Europe. This toolkit, aligned with WHO guidelines, enables children to acquire essential knowledge around 4 learning units: Relationships; Equality, Diversity and Gender;  Violence and staying safe; Human body and Sexuality and Sexual behavior;
- concept note to be submitted in the spring 2025 Erasmus+ KA2-SCH deadline as a XSE follow up.
At the end of the project, the professional involved are more able to:
- refer to and adopt good practices and innovative methodologies on the project subject;
- deliver programs and creative activities aimed at strengthening the children's sexualy literacy using XSE materials.

2021-2-IT02-KA210-SCH-000048370.title: Comm-Edu: Community agreements for Education
2021-2-IT02-KA210-SCH-000048370.summary:
<< Background >>

The health crisis related to COVID-19 has led to a general impoverishment of educational offerings, hitting especially recreational and cultural activities aimed at promoting active citizenship and the acquisition of soft skills by younger people.
According to the European Commission document "School Policy-A Comprehensive and Integrated Approach in the Fight against School Dropout," school policies should be based on a comprehensive and inclusive vision of education based on the centrality of the student, in which high-quality education is accessible to all. To this end, it is essential to adopt a comprehensive and integrated approach. 
The dimension of integration, referred to as the global approach, feeds on knowledge and expertise pertaining to different fields, and is achieved by virtue of collaboration among professionals working in different fields. This approach implies a cross-sectoral view and closer cooperation with a wide range of stakeholders (cultural bodies, youth services, local authorities, the third sector, businesses, etc.) and the wider community.


<< Objectives >>

The overall objective of Comm-Edu was to promote an innovative approach to educational provision in the area of active and European citizenship in order to combat educational poverty and early school leaving, based on the creation of educational communities at the local level that involved public-private partnerships and the most relevant stakeholders.

The specific Objectives were: 
-Analyze needs and good practices at the European level on active citizenship education through the involvement of the educating community (global approach);
-Promote the development of educating communities at the local level, laying the groundwork for the creation of a replicable model;
-Elaborate a template, valid for diffeent European countries, for the establishment of educating communities at the local level;
-Promote awareness of project issues among local communities, also fostering student involvement and participation within the local communities


<< Implementation >>

The main activities implemented within COMM-EDU were:
A1: Kick-off meeting, necessary for the start of the project
A2: Preliminary research (Preparation), on education for active citizenship through the involvement of the educating community (global approach)
A3: Establishment of the educating communities at the local level (Implementation), which took the form of meetings with local educating community members in order to investigate the possible role of the community in the educational process of local young people
A4: Transnational project meeting and co-design workshop: held in Assisi, Italy, led to the emergence of the main points to be included within the community agreement template
A5: Elaboration and translation of the Community Agreement template valid for all partner countries and developed based on the research report and meetings with the educating community held in the previous months
A6: Organization of a final event in each partner country
A7: Project management and Dissemination of results.



<< Results >>

The main outputs of the project have been:
1) Research report on local community involvement in the process of youth education 
2) Template "Community agreement," between public, private, school and third sector entities through which to establish communities of practice underlying the model of educational offerings dedicated to local youth, available in 5 languages
3) 4 events in the 4 partner countries

Other results were:
-Establishment of a dialogue between students and communities
-Improvement of the educational offer dedicated to students 
-Creation of European-level connections at all educational levels
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2021-2-IT02-KA210-SCH-000050323.title: Experimenta: a community-based approach to STEM education
2021-2-IT02-KA210-SCH-000050323.summary:
<< Background >>

EXPERIMENTA wanted to address the need of  promoting a holistic approach to STEM subjects, based on empirical learning, peer education, and the community involvement in the education process of young students.  Indeed, the project focused on the creation of a community of practice based on collaboration between schools, families and external stakeholders.
In light of the need in European educational contexts to promote STEM paths from a young age, EXPERIMENTA was intended to be an attempt to apply a new methodology in different educational contexts. The results produced play a key role in the practical application of the principles underlying the EXPERIMENTA project, making it possible to replicate our pedagogical model based on a holistic and practical approach in other European contexts.
The project idea originated from a good practice promoted for over 10 years by the Project coordinator based on the use of scientific methodology, particularly the experimental one.
EXPERIMENTA addressed two key following priorities:
1.Promoting interest and excellence in STEM 
2. Tackling learning disadvantage, early school leaving and low proficiency in basic skills. 

<< Objectives >>

In the light of the need of stimulating interest in STEM careers among students in Europe and promote youth employability, educational institutions must rely on innovative and practical methods, engaging students in challenging activities and matching new educational needs to the teaching curricula. EXPERIMENTA combines practical approaches to promote STEM learning based on the principle of "Open schooling", which is achieved through collaboration between the schools and their local community.
The specific objectives (SOs) of the project were: 
SO 1) Improve the educational offer for schools in the field of STEM, through the definition of practical tools and the exchange of good practices from different EU countries
SO 2) Provide teachers with tools to facilitate the experimentation of the project's methodology within their own school contexts
SO 3) To improve students' knowledge competences and skills in STEM subjects through a project-based approach, experiential learning  and peer education methodology
SO 4) Promote students' protagonism, the development of communities of practice on STEM education at the local level, creating a model replicable in all European countries.


<< Implementation >>

- A1 Kick-off meeting: carried out at the beginning of the project.
- A2 Research: Preliminary research on innovative STEM practices and collection of best practices; Elaboration of a Report on the results of research activities and guidelines for the development of STEM teaching activities/reality tasks; 1st draft of the Booklet. 
- A3 Pilot Action: Teachers and the students involved in the previous phases trained their peers on the project's methodology and tools. At the end of A3 in Italy and Croatia, a transnational evaluation report was delivered. The final version of the Booklet was delivered after A3. 
- A4 Students’ learning activities: Students presented the Booklet during the FESTIVAL OF SCIENCE AND PHILOSOPHY. The training also allowed participants to meet educational communities and other members of the local community and share their experience on STEM education. 
- A5 Final events: each partner organization held a final event to disseminate the project results and  stimulating stakeholders to use the open schooling methodology.  Over 150 people attended the final events.
- A6 PM and communication: implementation of activities aimed at ensuring  proper project management, sharing and promotion of project  results. 

<< Results >>

EXPERIMENTA provides for the development of concrete results that are sustainable and reusable even after the end of the project. 
The Booklet is the main result of the project and it is a tool addressed to teachers. The document contains the principles, methodology and possible activities (both the good practices developed in the partner countries and the authentic material created by the classes involved) to be implemented in the classroom following the Experimental methodology. To maximize the re-use of the Booklet, the document is available in IT,HR,ES.
Besides the Booklet, the Consortium successfully  achieved the following results:
- Report of the experimentation, containing the results of the pilot action in the countries involved (2 national evaluation reports and 1 joint report on the pilot action).
- Transnational training of students during the FESTIVAL OF SCIENCE AND PHILOSOPHY
- 4 final events in 3 partner countries.
In addition to the results foreseen in the application, an additional document was produced concerning the presentation and evaluation of the final events implemented in Italy, Croatia and Spain.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
