2021-2-LV01-KA210-SCH-000050375.title: Sporto dabā jeb esi vesels nākotnei
2021-2-LV01-KA210-SCH-000050375.summary:
<< Background >>

The priority topics of the project are different
involvement and motivation of young people from social groups to continue their education, inclusion of marginalized young people, communication and
the development of socialization skills. These topics were chosen because they were relevant in all 4 partner schools, as well as on national scales. By solving these issues, it was possible to realize the educational goals in schools and the horizontal goal of the project. The human body works better when it does sports. The brain works better, you will sleep better at night, sports help
various health problems will be avoided, as well as various psychological problems - unjustified - are reduced
tantrums, depression, a person becomes more self-confident. In addition, sports among young people promoted various social
skills. Taking into account the above, by focusing directly on physical activities in the open nature and in groups, we aimed to return young people to social life and socialization from the consequences of introversion caused by covid-19 restrictions.

<< Objectives >>

The distance learning process and the emergency situation related to COVID-19 have reduced the opportunity to socialize and participate
in sports lessons and competitions. For some young people, sport was the motivating element to study, go to school, meet with
to like-minded people. This situation had a significant impact on young people's decisions and attitude towards education as a future path. But outdoors
classes and physical activities allow you to continue improving yourself physically and mentally just as successfully as indoor sports. Only
you have to find the most suitable and appropriate one for you. That's why we set the achievable results to share our experience with sports
types in each partner country, which can be done in nature both alone and in groups. As a result, create a map with
for well-maintained and safe sports places in nature in every country and offer this information to municipalities, tourism and sports
centers. We also planned to create 3D models with recommendations on how to diversify the possibilities of sports activities in nature in each country.

<< Implementation >>

The project has its own logo, chosen by the students during the first mobility. During the project mobility and presentations, we shared our experience with sports
types in each partner country, which can be done in nature both alone and in groups. . As a result, a map was created with
for well-maintained and safe sports places in nature in every country and offer this information to municipalities, tourism and sports
centers. Local orientation routes have been created, which help to get to know the surroundings of educational institutions of partner countries better.
Activities in nature, led to planning, organizing, solving unusual situations, overcoming obstacles. The project carried out research on outdoor sports opportunities in each country and developed a recommendation for one of the partner countries
how and what else could be added. Recommendations created in 3D models and in the form of presentations using Tinkercad or another program, or
making from various environmentally friendly materials.

<< Results >>

The project achieved the following results:
- Our students gained new knowledge about the possibilities and types of outdoor sports in partner countries and learned about them in Latvia.
- Partner schools exchanged information about nature sports and shared it in their school.
- We have created a Padlet European map, which will show the types of nature sports available in EU countries.
- We  have created a 3D models with TINKERCAD or as a handicraft to supplement natural sports places in each country;

2021-2-PL01-KA210-SCH-000048197.title: Papier czy plastik? Papierowe, plastikowe... przetworzone (nie zaśmieca), jest jak nowe.
2021-2-PL01-KA210-SCH-000048197.summary:
<< Background >>

We conducted research in partner schools to identify the needs on which we based the project assumptions. We observed the need to increase ecological awareness among target groups in terms of learning how to segregate waste, take care of the environment, re-use materials and save energy and water. We wanted to develop students' key competences such as: developing social skills, communicating in a foreign language, innovation and creativity, and cultural awareness. We believed that by participating in the project, students and teachers would increase their motivation to learn and search for new solutions. We saw the need for students with special educational needs and fewer opportunities to participate in the project to strengthen their sense of self-esteem and belonging to the school and local community. We also wanted to promote equality and counteract discrimination. We believed that cooperation in an international group would have a positive impact on improving communication in a foreign language. The variety of activities, including remote cooperation, would contribute to the improvement of participants' digital competences, and the implementation of the project would effectively support the development of schools.

<< Objectives >>

Our goals were: increasing the ecological awareness of project participants, motivation to learn among students and teachers, social inclusion of students with special educational needs and fewer opportunities. The mentioned objectives were consistent with the following priorities of the Erasmus+ program: horizontal: environment and combating climate change and social inclusion; sectoral ones: developing key competences, promoting a comprehensive approach to teaching and learning foreign languages, supporting teachers, principals and other educational staff in their professional development. It was the first Erasmus+ project for Polish and Croatian schools, we wanted to gain experience in this area.

<< Implementation >>

There are 9 stages. We completed all of them. Stage I - initiation of cooperation, approval of regulations, assignment of tasks, dissemination of information about the project, development of the project management procedure, schedule of activities, recruitment regulations. Stage II first mobility to Croatia - 4 cultural workshops, dictionary of phrases in Croatian, school newspapers, presentations about Croatia, project song, Europasses, exhibitions of photo reports from the mobility. Stage III: workshops on sorting waste, food collection, activities and Christmas meeting, logo competition for fabric bags. Stage IV - activities related to mobility to Portugal - cultural workshops, glossary, photo exhibitions, presentation about Portugal, Europasses, information on schools' websites. Stage V – Young ecologist's week, posters for Earth Day, 3 films about ecological campaigns, planting trees, collecting waste paper and bottle caps. Stage VI - mobility to Poland - cultural workshops, dictionary of phrases, wall displays, presentations about Poland, Questing. Stage VII- lanyards. Stage VIII – teacher mobility to Portugal, SWOT analysis, "Clean Up the World" campaign. Stage IX – evaluations, eco-cleaning eco workshops.

<< Results >>

Tangible results: Trello, Twinspace, information on the websites of schools, supervisory institutions, social media, project documentation, logos and project T-shirts, posters, roll-ups, information boards, information and educational corners, leaflets, workshops about the EU and partner countries and ecological, lesson plans, dictionaries, presentations, project song, Europasses, collection of recyclable materials and animal food, online meetings, Christmas decorations, fabric bags, teaching packages, planted trees, posters and films, Mini Questing, quiz, evaluation results, reports collective, lanyards, 4 mobilities, pedagogical innovation - Young Ecologist Week, participation in #ErasmusDays.
Intangible results - increase in: knowledge about the EU and partner countries, ecological awareness, IT skills and work planning, motivation to learn, linguistic and social competences, professional competences of staff, cultural awareness, personal development of participants, improvement of the quality of school work, including examples of good practices into school work , teachers starting to learn English.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-2-PL01-KA210-SCH-000049220.title: the Best Tip for Healthy Diet: “Cook It Yourself and Keep Away from Fast Food”
2021-2-PL01-KA210-SCH-000049220.summary:
<< Background >>

We wanted to start cooperation with foreign primary/secondary schools in Europe since we know that this experience can help us to  broaden our horizons. Getting to know different cultures makes us more aware of the need to have respect for everybody. We also want  our students  to practice their foreign language skills, mostly English. Our students developed their interests during extracurricular activities, such as subject, artistic and sports circles. Our school encourages pupils to acknowledge the importance of leading healthier lifestyles, paying more attention to diet and nutrition, consequences upon the environment, taking up sports and connecting with nature.  
The topic of a healthy lifestyle and healthy eating is carried out through preventive programs: concerning healthy eating and counteracting childhood obesity, promoting a healthy diet among students by providing children with fruit, vegetables and dairy products, and educational activities carried out in schools. The menu for lunch is prepared in accordance with the principles of healthy eating for children.  We participate in the Milk at School program, the aim of which is to give every student a chance to have a carton of fresh milk every day. 


<< Objectives >>

We wanted to achieve different  results, but mostly our aim was to improve various skills such as: better self-esteem, team work skills, English speaking skills, IT skills for our students, colleagues and us. The implementation of the project also offered  an opportunity to get to know other cultures and their customs. It can help the students  ( their parents) to achieve multicultural knowledge and  build tolerance to others. The most important, however, was: 
- to find out more about health, healthy lifestyle, and food
- to empower participants’ skills and knowledge so as to adopt a balanced healthy lifestyle
- to foster quality and multidimensional improvements in participants’ lifestyle 
- to exchange good practices at international level
- more understand the people-nature connection, explore the surrounding nature, explore and conclude on the impact of human activities on environment, the way nature affects our health
- to  communicate health-related information to participants, strengthen human relationships and establish effective team building spirit, friendly competitions that tackle project topics from various angles, supported through team cohesion and proactive lifestyle.



<< Implementation >>

- Presentations about  "Educational systems across Europe" and asking questions about these systems in Poland, Türkiye, Croatia, Local Good Practice Examples: Fostering Inclusion
- Poster Presentation to Advertise the Project Designed
- Video presentations “My routine”- every country presents the presentation showing: everyday activities, physical exercises, free time, activities/distractions, hobby
- Group game - 2 truths and one lie about un/healthy habits 
- Ecological education - The Termal Waste Treatment Plant in Kraków  
- “My favourite free time activity” - sport activity in Gymspace 
- Workshop ( Health and hygiene” conducted by a specialist in the medical field) in  the Department of Nutrition Technology, Workshop „Nutritional value of agricultural goods
-  The trip to Wieliczka salt mine  
- Visual representations - exhibition, of healthy lifestyle „Spices and medicinal herbs-amazing benefits“
- European Food Fair - participants bring traditional food from their countries 
- Inerview of our students guests on school radio
- Story of success- documentary visit to a nearby farm
-  exchange of good practices: clean-up campaign 
- field trip-documentary to a nearby protected area 
- Balancing Body, Mind and Soul Workshop.

<< Results >>

The participants had the oppurtinity to  learn from each other,  to transfer positive aspects identified in foreign educational systems to their own schools, to appreciate and respect European cultures.
Students’ active involvement in interactive activities developed ability to sum up information, digital skills, critical thinking ability, stimulate creativity, healthy habits by applying knowledge into practice, strong sense of nature connectivity.
The planned results have been achieved. Concrete results are visible, f.ex. in  the cookbook and a board game that we made in Croatia LTTA. The positive result is the huge interest among students for the  next Erasmus+ projects, and a fact that our students established strong relationships with other teenagers from the project. One student from Poland spent a month last summer as a guest in one of our student's house in Croatia.We see that our students who were  involved in the project much easier volunteer for all kinds of research projects after this experience. 
Next result is the expansion of knowledge regarding a healthy lifestyle, eating habits. Both in Croatia, Turkey, students participated in culinary workshops. These recipes can be utilized and share.

2021-2-RO01-KA210-SCH-000048350.title: Special Hearts for a Beautiful Earth
2021-2-RO01-KA210-SCH-000048350.summary:
<< Background >>

One of the priorities of the institutions involved in the project is the green initiative. The project was primarily addressed to students with special needs, with disabilities, who unfortunately make an additional effort to understand the major changes in contemporary society, the climate changes. Starting from the need to help these children to adapt, to help them to acquire a proactive behavior towards the environment, to help them understand that only by acting they can also contribute to saving the planet, from the need for the valorization of these children, we created this project, a project for "special hearts". The project also addressed the need for understanding the causality of climate change and the acquisition of methods of prevention and action against the degradation of the planet by the other educational actors involved in the project, teachers and parents. Trying to look from a positive perspective, we live in a society that does not understand the importance of recycling and protecting the environment. but which shows potential in acquiring proactive behaviors. Our role as educators is to shape these personalities in the direction of transforming this Planet into a more beautiful place.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project we want to make a change, we want them to develop key competencies, basic skills, we want the participants in this project to acquire capacities and resources for adaptation and integration, to form skills for action in various situations, to acquire proactive behaviors in relation to the environment, we want our actions to count in the community out of concern for the environment. We also want to improve the communication skills of the participants, to develop the psycho-emotional side of the special children involved in the project, to create people involved in the community, who care. We also set out to acquire knowledge related to the way in which we can recycle, reuse, reduce, to create art objects from recyclable materials, to create a piece in which environmental issues are highlighted, to set up a vertical garden with an impact for the school community. The well-being of the trainees is another priority of the institutions involved in the project.

<< Implementation >>

The "Special Hearts for a Beautiful Earth" project was structured on six activities. Three of the activities were transnational activities, hosted by each institution involved in the project. In these activities, specialists in the field of special education participated. Problems related to the environment were addressed, courses were held by specialists. Also, the project teams from the three institutions discussed about the stages of the project, the proposed objectives and the way in which these objectives will be achieved, about the progress of the activities, the possible difficulties that may arise, about the responsibilities of each institution, about the ways in which we will communicate during the project, about how we will publicize the project, about how we will disseminate the information.
The other three activities were local activities, organized at the level of each institution. The activities involved students, teachers and students. They received information about recycling, about how important recycling is for our planet, about how we can recycle, reuse, reduce the amount of waste. They collect waste. They create  art-crafts. We create a play with the students. And in the end we arranged a vertical garden.

<< Results >>

Concretely - all participants in this project became more aware of the environment, more aware of the negative consequences of socially inappropriate behaviors, learned how to recycle properly, how to reduce the amount of waste and how to reuse some objects, learned to create objects from recyclable materials. Participating students together with the coordinating teachers created a play with the aim of sensitizing the community. And in the end, the students together with the teachers and parents arranged a Vertical Garden in all three institutions involved in the project with the aim of reducing the effects of pollution and creating a sense of well-being.
Implicitly, the participants developed their communication skills, practical skills, social skills and proactive behaviors. Through their involvement in greening activities, they have contributed to the well-being of the local community.The students with special needs felt valued through their involvement in greening activities, creating objects, through their involvement in the play and through their involvement in the practical activities of setting up the Vertical Garden. Thus, the motivation for learning increased and the possibility of school dropout decreased considerably.

2021-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000048937.title: Z melodijo do inkluzije - glasba, medij vključevanja otrok s posebnimi potrebami
2021-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000048937.summary:
<< Background >>

Projekt smo prijavili, ker smo opazili pomanjkanje socialnih in glasbeno-kulturnih izkušenj in priložnosti za otroke s posebnimi potrebami. Otroke s posebnimi potrebami redko najdemo v glasbenih šolah ali celo na koncertih zaradi svojih omejitev, bodisi fizičnih, duševnih ali šibkega socialno-ekonomskega statusa njihove družine. S tem razlogom, smo za glavni medij povezovanja, komunikacije in učenja izbrali glasbo. Glasbeni pouk pospešuje ohranjanje fizičnega in psihičnega zdravja, izpolnjuje človekovo željo po igri in komunikaciji ter utrjuje občutek po samopomembnosti. Z odpiranjem poti v sistem glasbenega izobraževanja smo želeli dati učencem s posebnimi potrebami možnost razvoja glasbenih potencialov ter pridobivanja glasbenih spretnosti in znanj enakovredno ostalim učencem.

Potrebe ki smo jih obravnavali so potreba po vključenosti, zabavi in učenju otrok s posebnimi potrebami (inkluzija, socialni kapital, samopodoba, enake možnosti, dobro počutje, individualizirano/prilagojeno učenje). Pri tem je bilo najpomembnejše to, da bodo pridobljeni občutki sprejetosti, pomembnosti in vključenosti v družbo, trajni.

<< Objectives >>

Z izvedbo projekta smo želeli prispevati k višji inkluziji otrok s posebnimi potrebami v kulturno-umetniško sfero družbe. Želeli smo združiti znanja in kompetence priznanih glasbenikov ter otrok s posebnimi potrebami ter vzpostaviti prostor za ozaveščanje in medsebojno učenje. Želeli smo, da otroci preko glasbenih delavnic in druženj razvijajo samopodobo, pridobivajo trajnostne izkušnje, krepijo glasbene spretnosti in znanja ter dobijo priložnosti, do katerih sicer nimajo dostopa. Z rezultati projekta smo želeli sensibilizirati javnosti z dejstvom in dokazi, da otroci s posebnimi potrebami z veliko zagnanostjo ter vsesplošnim veseljem in neposrednostjo, zmorejo res veliko če jim pri tem pomaga univerzalen jezik – glasba. 

<< Implementation >>

Za čas trajanja projekta smo izvedli pet aktivnosti - pripravo koncepta in vsebine glasbenih delavnic ter metod dela; izvedbo glasbenih delavnic za otroke s posebnimi potrebami v sodelovanju s priznanimi glasbeniki in pedagogi; primerjalno analizo izvedenih delavnic in njihovega učinka; razširjanje projektnih rezultatov ter projektno vodenje in zagotavljanje kakovosti.
Osrednja in najbolj obširna je bila izvedba glasbenih delavnic za otroke s posebnimi potrebami v sodelovanju s priznanimi glasbeniki in pedagogi. Tako smo v sklopu projekta izvedli skupno 16 glasbenih delavnic, ki so jih vodili priznani slovenski in hrvaški glasbeniki kot so: Maja Keuc, Alenka Godec, Zoran Predin, Ditka, Rok Terkaj, Nuška Drašček, Slavko Ivančić, Žiga Kožar, Robert Pikl, Alex Mladenov, Sabrina Hebiri, Zvonimir Bajević, Luka Pešutić, Tomislav Modrić, Goran Rukavina in Branko Trajkov Trak. Na koncu smo organizirali še zaključni koncert, v Sloveniji je potekal v Špas teatru Mengeš, na Hrvaškem pa v Teatru EXIT. 
Vsaka od aktivnosti je bila časovno in vsebinsko načrtovana ter usklajena s partnerji iz Hrvaške. Trudili smo se, da preko izmenjave mnenj in izkušenj soustvarjamo kvaliteten projekt. Časovnice smo se dosledno držali.

<< Results >>

Konkretni rezultati vezani za planirane aktivnosti so sledeči: izdelan  program in vsebina glasbenih delavnic z oblikovanimi metodami dela; oblikovane metode dela; izdelani reciklirani didaktični pripomočki; izdelan akcijski načrt; izvedenih 15 glasbenih delavnic in 2 koncerta; izdelana primerjalna analiza; oblikovana zavihka na spletnih straneh obeh šol - sprotno informiranje o poteku projektnih aktivnosti; 50 objav v času trajanja projekta; doseženih več kot 1000 oseb; več kot 15 objav o aktivnostih v okviru projekta na Facebook strani OŠ Roje; doseženih več kot 5000 tisoč oseb; objave o projektu v medijih v obeh državah (časopis, spletni portali, radijski intervjuji); izdelan natančen načrt upravljanja projekta z vključenim komunikacijskim in finančnim načrtom; izvedeni dve srečanji partnerjev v živo, eno v Sloveniji, drugo na Hrvaškem; izvedeni redni mesečni spletni sestanki; redna komunikacija preko Whatsappa; stalen nadzor nad kakovostjo izvedbe in potrebne izboljšave; redno mesečno poročanje.

2021-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000049929.title: Kompetentni za poučevanje v naravi - sodobni pristopi poučevanja
2021-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000049929.summary:
<< Background >>

The lever for our project is not only global trends in education and teaching and the question "What kind of planning or is the learning environment suitable for the 21st century?", as we started from our own needs of both institutions. Namely, with the help of a SWOT analysis, we found that teaching in nature is our weak area, but it is important at this time, as it encourages movement, which is not enough today due to the modern, sedentary lifestyle. V. Štemberger (2012) also notes that outdoor lessons improve the immune system and strengthen immunity. The form of the work also encourages observation, additional research and discovery of something new. Nature encourages students to reproduce and connect already acquired knowledge. Students see the point in learning in nature, as they realize that knowledge is not just about getting grades. However, if the appropriate use of ICT is added to this, we help students to be more motivated and engaged in learning. All this requires a sovereign and competent teacher. By implementing the activity, we wanted to strengthen the professional growth and competence of the professional profile of teachers. That they will cope with teaching in the 21st century.

<< Objectives >>

The nature of learning arouses strong interest nowadays, as does the creation of environments for successful learning. All this requires a sovereign and competent teacher. With the project, we wanted to train teachers to create or use such learning environments, so that they would be able to recognize a potential space from the natural environment where student-friendly lessons can take place, supported by the meaningful use of ICT.

<< Implementation >>

We carried out joint training activities and thus checked the designed trainings for teachers, and above all Croatian and Slovenian teachers exchanged examples of good practices, as it was planned that each school would exchange 7 teachers and 6 students in two years. We planned and implemented student mobility from the point of view of implementing teaching in nature with applications and short-term joint events for staff training. As part of this, the participants attended classes, participated in school activities, planned and tested teacher training.

<< Results >>

With us, all participants gained by participating in the project; children from kindergarten, students of different age groups from both primary schools, professional workers, parents, local community, random tourists and general professional public. In the proposed project, we have developed three modules of practical training (learning in nature) for our teachers, as support for those who adopt and develop basic skills and key competences. We designed, planned and successfully set up a learning path named Treasures of Pišece, which raised the quality of the goal set in the application form (design and set up a water learning trail). As part of this, we created presentation flyers, postcards, brochures, and a website. Other results include the introduction of annual project weeks in the school's LDN (annual work plan), which is based on the integration of national and international projects with an emphasis on teaching in nature. As part of the project's dissemination, a manual for teaching along the learning path Treasures of Pišece is being prepared, based on the successfully implemented lessons of the teachers in our institution.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000050241.title: Razvoj kulturnega kapitala romskih učencev
2021-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000050241.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project because of the need to reduce inequalities in the educational achievements of Roma and majority pupils. The organizations involved in the project often come into contact with members of the Roma community in the course of their work. The gaps in cultural capital and reading literacy between Roma and majority pupils are already very pronounced when they enter school and widen during their schooling. The project is based on the recognition that the cultural capital and basic literacy levels acquired are not only the result of the school system but are shaped in the family environment, and that due to the specific way of life in the Roma community, children do not develop the cultural capital of a legitimate culture, which is reflected in their performance. In order for Roma children to make up for this shortfall, cultural capital needs to be systematically developed. One of the ways in which the partners have seen how to successfully address this challenge is through activities to develop reading literacy among Roma pupils, thereby reducing the differences in the level of cultural capital between pupils. To address the needs of Roma pupils, the project has developed a curriculum and didactic materials.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to develop the reading literacy of Roma pupils by creating innovative additional content that will help teachers raise the level of cultural capital and reading literacy of Roma children in order to make up for the deficit with which these pupils enter the education system. This will have long-term positive effects on their academic performance and other areas of their lives. By developing a curriculum and didactic materials based on a preliminary analysis of the situation, we wanted to offer additional support to teachers and pedagogical staff in their work with Roma pupils. At the same time, the project also aimed to increase the participation of Roma pupils in school and extracurricular activities.
Objectives we set ourselves in the project application were:
-to compensate for the lack of cultural capital of Roma pupils,
-develop reading literacy among Roma pupils,
-to strengthen the role of teachers in raising the level of cultural capital of Roma pupils,
-strengthen teachers' activities to enhance the raising of cultural capital in Roma pupils,
reduce the disparities in literacy and cultural capital between Roma and majority pupils,
-develop innovative approaches and tools for working with Roma pupils.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were carried out under the KULko project:
1. Using the method of semi-structured teacher interviews, we analyzed the current level of cultural capital of Roma pupils in the partner primary schools and compiled the results into a report.In addition, we interviewed teachers from the partner primary schools or kindergarten units who have direct insight into the development of Roma children in the pre-school period, when the basic elements of cultural capital and reading literacy are formed in the process of primary socialization.
Based on the results of the first activity, a common curriculum for raising the level of cultural capital of legitimate Roma culture was developed, covering the areas that proved to be the most pressing.
3. We have prepared a variety of didactic materials that follow the curriculum and serve the needs of the implementation of the activities to raise the level of basic cultural capital and reading literacy according to the curriculum.
4. We piloted the curriculum activities in partner primary schools and involved Roma pupils in the preparation of the school newsletter.

<< Results >>

The concrete products and other outputs of the KULko project are:
- A research report on the analysis of the current level of cultural capital and the level of reading literacy of Roma pupils (20 classroom teachers and educators involved).
- A common plan to raise the level of basic cultural capital of Roma pupils.
- A collection of didactic materials for the implementation of activities aimed at raising the level of basic cultural capital and reading literacy of Roma pupils on the basis of the curriculum developed
- Pilot implementation of the curriculum activities in Croatia (21 Roma and 9 non-Roma children*).
- Pilot curriculum activities in Slovenia (10 Roma and 10 non-Roma children)
- Publication of a school newsletter for Roma pupils in a Slovenian partner primary school.
publication of a school newsletter for Roma pupils in a Croatian partner primary school.
- The research report, the curriculum, and the collection of didactic materials are available in three languages: the national languages of the partner countries (Slovenian and Croatian) and English.
* Non-Roma children were included in the activities alongside Roma children with the aim of cooperative learning, which increases motivation and interaction.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000050408.title: Učenje z gibanjem zunaj
2021-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000050408.summary:
<< Background >>

Need for Increasing Quality Physical Activity for Children
Our main motivation for implementing the project was to provide children not just with movement, but with quality movement. We are aware of the significant positive effects of physical activity, not only on health but also on brain development and, consequently, overall development.

Support for Educators
As professionals, we understand the importance of approaching the development of 'movement pedagogy' systematically, starting with enabling quality training for educators and the possibility of exchanging developed practices. Only such professionals can create stimulating learning environments, which outdoor play areas certainly are.

Raising Awareness Among Parents
Based on professional articles and our own observations in practice, we have also found that parents are poorly informed about the positive effects of physical activity and need ideas and guidance regarding activities they can do with their children. Therefore, workshops and a manual were created, which can be used by both educators and parents.

Creating Lasting Outcomes
Both the manual and the play area are results designed with sustainability in mind.

<< Objectives >>

Not only deepen the professional knowledge of educators about the importance of outdoor physical activity for the holistic development of children by providing continuous professional support but also encourage lifelong learning. With the development of neuroscience, insights in the field of learning and teaching are rapidly evolving, which means they need to be continually updated. Therefore, it is essential to establish a system of lifelong learning.

Exchange and critically evaluate examples of physical activities for implementation in various areas of the curriculum through practice.

Raise awareness among parents about the importance of outdoor physical activity for the holistic development of children. If we want parents to contribute to the quality of education, we must ensure that they are not only familiar with the pedagogy and didactics applied in the preschool education and care system but also understand the reasons behind these practices. To take it a step further, we need to equip parents with the knowledge that enables them to actively participate in education, which means they urgently need to understand the methods of education and care that kindergartens provide to children in early childhood.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, we carried out the following activities:
1. Professional training on the importance of physical activity and its integration into various areas of the curriculum, conducted in Slovenia. The unique aspect of this training was that the first three days involved a combination of professional observation, while the last two days allowed participants to practically implement the acquired knowledge.
2. Workplace observations conducted at the partner school in Croatia.
3. Establishment of outdoor learning play areas with didactic materials in both partner organizations.
4. Development of a handbook for educators and parents, available in electronic form.
5. Workshops for parents on the importance of physical activity for the quality development of children in both partner organizations.

<< Results >>

The specific results:
- two outdoor learning play areas with didactic materials in both partner institutions.
- an electronic professional handbook with examples of physical activities for all areas of the curriculum, available in both partner languages.

Other project outcomes include:
Acquired knowledge about managing and participating in international projects, as this was the first such project for our organization.
Increased awareness among employees about the importance and necessity of lifelong learning.
Heightened interest in learning foreign languages among employees, as they wish to exchange practices more broadly, not just with neighboring countries.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2021-2-TR01-KA210-SCH-000048293.title: Searching Ecological Alternatives of Life
2021-2-TR01-KA210-SCH-000048293.summary:
<< Background >>

SEAL partners believed it was crucial that the young people understood their actions and larger mechanisms that pollute the earth and everybody had to take responsibility in order to reduce pollution and even prevent it.
In SEAL, schools were actively encouraged to focus on environmental problems, conduct campaigns for the preservation and restoration of the nature and develop long-lasting solutions. 
SEAL provided participants with environmental knowledge and equipped them with sustainable green skills necessary for their daily lives. Students were exposed to real life cases to better acquire environmental learning. Teachers were trained to teach environmental topics using non-formal and experiential methodology.
The overall aim of SEAL project was to bring a social learning approach into education in which students and teachers would learn, understand and interpret the world around them. This was realized through experiential learning workshops, educational and cultural visits, seminars, sport events and youth campaigns for environment to raise awareness of sustainable ways of recycling, finding new energy sources and gain an understanding about a more sustainable environment.

<< Objectives >>

SEAL project was designed to serve for the visions of European Environment Policy for 2020, ‘Towards a greener and more sustainable Europe’ and set its project objectives in line:
1. protect, conserve and enhance the nature,
2. turn into eco-schools which are resource-efficient, green and adopts low-carbon school practices,
3. safeguard students and teachers from environment-related risks to health and wellbeing.

SEAL also supported ‘Environmental and Climate Goals’ of Erasmus+ program, which declared projects aiming to “support awareness-raising about environmental and climate-change challenges”, would be prioritized. SEAL project aimed to prepare students to “become true factors of change (e.g. save resources, reduce energy use and waste, compensate carbon footprint emissions) and cover education and sport activities to enable changes for consumption habits and lifestyles”
SEAL also established circumstances in which project participants would develop their cultural, social, innovative, multilingual and ICT skills and improve knowledge of respect and responsibility for others.

<< Implementation >>

SEAL project implemented local, virtual and transnational activities to reach project objectives. These were:
1. Exchanges of teachers, students and youth workers,
2. Trainer Training Course and in-service teacher trainings,
3. Evaluation and increase of ecology levels of SEAL partner schools,
4. Seminars, Workshops, Micro-Teaching Sessions, Educational Visits and Volunteering Actions on Environmental Topics,
5. Outdoor Sporting Events,
6. eTwinning project of SEAL.

<< Results >>

The SEAL project produced:
1. 2 e-books and a Web Page,
2. Ecology Level Evaluation tool,
3. Posters, Brochures, Greenspaces, Project Corners,
4. Surveys, Researches, Lesson and Task Plans,
5. Reports, Videos, Campaigns, Posters, Poems, Brochures and Phone App plans. 

SEAL had an impact to improve:
1. Transfer of best environmental education methodologies,
2. Ecology Levels of schools,
3. Participants’ green, digital, intercultural, foreign language, civic and project management skills,
4. Teachers’ professional skills at partner schools.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-2-TR01-KA210-SCH-000050221.title: Müzikte Dijital Sesler
2021-2-TR01-KA210-SCH-000050221.summary:
<< Background >>

The main reason for applying for this project is the rise of digitalization in the field of music education and the increasing potential for students to engage in digital music-related activities. The storytelling of digital music highlighted in the project and the efforts to develop students' musical expression skills serve the purpose of enhancing their creativity and supporting their social-emotional learning. The international dimension of the project is important as music is a universal phenomenon and has the potential to reach large audiences through powerful tools such as social media and the internet. The international strategy allows students to interact interculturally and develop their language skills. Our application also includes efforts to focus on students' needs to develop 21st century skills and to encourage students' active participation by creating interactive learning environments that include activities related to digital music. This project aimed to strengthen students' skills and competences related to digital music.

<< Objectives >>

When this project was implemented, teachers and students found opportunities to develop lifelong competencies and personal values. The project allowed the partnership of five stakeholders to form an international team with planned project activities and focus on specific competencies. The Making Digital Music project targeted creativity, academic groundedness, social and emotional learning, digital notation reading and writing skills to meet the needs for 21st century skills. Support work started with the e-Twinning project "Digital Music for Social-Emotional Learning and Creativity", which aimed to develop students' expressive skills through music. The project encouraged students' participation by creating interactive learning environments that took place in six countries. The Digital Music project provided students with the ability to search for information, write musical scenarios, communicate with notation, perform and evaluate tasks. Other key objectives of the project included cultural interaction, development of language skills, providing equal opportunities for disadvantaged students and strengthening students' skills in digital music.

<< Implementation >>

The five main activities of the project are: Kick-off Meeting (Turkey): This meeting, which took place from July 9-14, 2022, hosted 19 participants and gave them the opportunity to celebrate the start of the project and set goals. Digital Music Workshop (Greece): Held in Greece from 8-13 October 2022, the workshop enabled 10 participants to develop their digital music skills. Creative Digitality and Notation (Spain): Held in Spain from 14-19 January 2023, the event aimed to deepen 10 participants' understanding of creative digital skills and notation. Digital Music for Storytelling (Turkey): Held in Turkey from April 15-20, 2023, the event focused on helping 10 participants develop their storytelling skills using digital music tools. Notes on Air (Croatia): Held in Croatia from June 10-15, 2023, this activity aimed for 8 participants to learn the process of publishing musical scores digitally.

<< Results >>

Digital Music Training provided participants with a broad digital music skill set. 
E-Twinning Project preparations offered an interactive learning environment integrating digital music to support academic, social and emotional development. 
E-Book Output aimed to deliver an e-book output of effective digital music stories integrated into different topics. Cultural and Language Development allowed participants to develop their language skills through intercultural interaction. 
Equal Opportunities prioritized eliminating disadvantages by using ICT skills of disadvantaged students. 
Educational Materials included educational materials developed for students and teachers. International Cooperation promoted international cooperation and experience sharing through a six-country partnership. 
With Musical Production and Performance, students learned about musical production processes and developed their musical skills. Digital Literacy provided students with skills such as information seeking and communication. Digitalization in Music Education supported students' interaction with digital music at a time when digitalization in music education is on the rise.

2022-1-BG01-KA210-SCH-000084037.title: Keep Calm and Go Green
2022-1-BG01-KA210-SCH-000084037.summary:
<< Background >>

С този проект искахме да повишим осведомеността относно изменението на климата и устойчивостта на околната среда чрез различни съвместни дейности. Искахме да насърчим критичното мислене, социалните, комуникативните, творческите умения за писане, анализирането и чуждоезиковите умения както на учителите, така и на учениците. Използвайки инструменти на Web 2.0, дейности за творческо писане, анимации и 3D моделиране и печат, ние подобрихме дигиталната грамотност и ИКТ уменията на учителите и учениците. Развихме техните креативността и културното съзнание.

<< Objectives >>

Целите, които искахме да постигнем и реализирахме:
- Да се засили разбирането, критичното мислене, разсъждението и социалните умения на учениците;
- Да се подобрят ИТ уменията на участниците;
-Да мотивираме учениците да използват технологични инструменти и Web 2.0 инструменти;
- Да повишим осведомеността им за дигиталната грамотност;
- Да включим повече участници от различни среди;
- Да създаден среда за неформално обучение;
- Да насърчим уменията за творческо писане на учениците;
- Да насърчим работата в екип;
- Да насърчим взаимното обучение.

<< Implementation >>

Започнахме проекта с информирането на училищните общности за идеите и целите на проекта,формирахме работни екипи,получихме на родителски разрешения,създадохме акаунти на проекта в социалните медии,използвайки платформи като Whatsapp, Facebook, Youtube Channel.Във всяко училище се създаде Еразъм ъгъл на проекта,където се представяха постоянно новостите около проекта.Създадохме плакати, лога, слогани, организирахме мобилности с учители и ученици със специфични задачи и дейности – създаване на история за изменението на климата,анимиране на тази история и създаване на 3D модели за принтиране на тази история.Бяха организирани лекции за анимация и 3d моделиране.Подготвихме презентации за 3Rs,Работилница за климатични колажи-Образователна и основана на факти, позволява разбиране за кратко време как работи климатът и какви са причините и последствията от климатичните смущения.Бяха организирани и работилници по рециклиране, където учениците изработваха нови предмети от вече използвани и им придаваха ново предназначение.Засадихме дървета.Създадохме страница Twinspace където добавихме всички партньори и ученици,и която развихме особено добре и в детайли.На тази страница учители и ученици практикуваха всички нови програми, които научиха 

<< Results >>

Постигнахме резултати и продукти като: Лого на проекта, слоган и плакати; Плакати за Деня на побратимяването; Писане на история за изменението на климата; Анимации и плакати за изменението на климата; Анимация на история за изменението на климата (Супер полярна мечка); Песен за устойчивостта на околната среда в акростих; 3D талисмани за изменението на климата и устойчивостта на околната среда; Съвместна викторина Kahoot за изменението на климата и устойчивостта на околната среда; 3R презентации в страните на партньорите по проекта. Всички учители и ученици получиха информация за изменението на климата и устойчивостта на околната среда. Дейностите за борба с изменението на климата насърчават социалното съзнание. Благодарение на дейностите, които изградихме върху основната тема за борбата с изменението на климата, развихме дигиталните компетенции на нашата целева аудитория. Практичните дейности, които бяха проведени, комбинираха теоретичния принос по въпросите на устойчивостта с конкретни действия за насърчаване на обучението за устойчивост на околната среда. Учениците придобиха значението на устойчивия живот, разбирането на Европейския съюз и чувството за принадлежност към него чрез неформални дейности.

2022-1-BG01-KA210-SCH-000084364.title: Heal The World!
2022-1-BG01-KA210-SCH-000084364.summary:
<< Background >>

The main goal of this project is "Implementation and sharing of innovative pedagogical practices aimed at building adaptability and resilience - sustainable models of behavior and formation of knowledge, skills and attitudes in children to deal with uncertainty, anxiety, stress and aggression." Big percentage of the various problems faced by parents, educators and therapists in recent years can
to be summarized in three groups of deficits, which are manifested as sensorimotor, speech and behavioral /aggressiveness, hyperactivity, anxiety/.
Resilience in humans is the ability to meet the blows of life and not just survive, but to develop and move forward. This approach is more of an attitude, an attitude, an understanding, a supportive environment.
The actuality of the child's health problem requires the application of forms, methods and means established in practice for the physical and
his mental development, search for ways to prevent and improve health. We teachers from the kindergarten and primary school approved and shared familiar world, but new in education, tools and approaches to work, and the learning and communication children-teachers-parents more complete, harmonious and inspiring.

<< Objectives >>

When we filled out the application form for this project, we were guided by the words of Maria Montessori:
"Everyone talks about peace, but no one educates for peace. In this world, one educates for competition, competition is the beginning of every war. When one begins to educate for cooperation and being
we offer each other solidarity, from that day on we will have started to educate ourselves for peace." Today, alas, they sound even more relevant against the background of ever-increasing tensions and conflicts.
Raising physically healthy and cheerful children is an important task of any modern society. The need for psychosocial support in education for both students,
so too for teachers. Reduction of motor activity, deformations in physical capacity, neuro-psychological
disorders, hypertension, obesity, stress, aggression, irrational eating are problems of the century. The anatomical-physiological and cognitive characteristics of preschool and primary school-age children require targeted development of their motor skills and physical ability through movements, games, music and emotion.
This project is a rather successful attempt to unite the holistic approach to man and the achievements of modern pedagogical science.

<< Implementation >>

We, the teachers in all European educational institutions, are looking for more and more opportunities for natural countermeasures to stress, such as unstructured free play and outdoor play. Activities and outcomes were aimed at each of the triad: child, teacher, parent in equal collaboration. We focused on contemporary modern holistic informal approaches and methods, which we approved and implemented in our pedagogical practice, striving to respect the principles of learning by doing and experiencing according to the needs and desires of the learners. Among the positive aspects of this type of learning are self-initiative and personal involvement, change and growth. Symbolically, we called the topics of our main activities "therapies", because we think that the emphasis on applying the used techniques will be an easier way to the possibility of restoring the internal balance in each child - physical, mental and spiritual balance.
Yoga therapy - practicing yoga for children
Fairy tale therapy - telling and creating fairy tales and theater;
Color therapy – use of visual arts;
Music and Rhythm therapy - by playing, singing and dancing;
Green eco therapy - eco workshop - work in the garden or with eco materials;


<< Results >>

To preserve the children, to develop the process of resilience in them, this is the huge task facing teachers in Europe today. This approach is attitude, attitude, understanding, supportive environment, upbringing
children the ability not only to survive, but to develop and move forward through art, physical activity, a healthy lifestyle. To awaken and develop their potential: sensory, movement and motility, adaptation, emotional and kinesthetic intelligence.
Specifically, in the activities of the Heal the World project, each partner institution was able to implement new and different educational practices in the educational process in the areas of physical education, visual arts, language and literature, music and ecology.
In this way, we also aim to achieve our main priority in school education: Developing high-quality early childhood education and care systems. Approved, established and applied in our practical work as teachers of methods and approaches for the prevention and improvement of the health of children and students, purposeful development of their motor skills and their physical capacity through movements, games, music and emotion.
