2022-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000083326.title: Digital Power
2022-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000083326.summary:
<< Background >>

Through the Digital Power project, we wanted to make ourselves fit for high-quality, inclusive and accessible digital education in Europe in line with the Digital Education Action Plan. As digitalization is an issue that affects us all, we were keen to compare how other countries are dealing with the challenges of digitalization and thus learn from each other.
With the help of this project, we wanted our teachers and students to improve their digital competences and to increase their awareness of digital security. Better use of innovation and digital technology should enable teachers to help students develop the relevant digital skills they need for life and work in an age of rapid digital change. 
A particular focus of our program has been to invite and empower girls to play a more active role in the digital world. 
By providing participants with a set of skills that enable them to use language in a communicative way, respect and learn about different cultures, combine knowledge from different sources and use technology safely and actively on a regular basis, we are helping to shape a great generation that will not need to complete additional training after graduation to be ready for the job market.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted our teachers and students to get to know and try out new digital tools during the activities, which would improve their digital skills. Teachers and students should learn how to use new Web2.0 tools and be inspired by jointly developed videos, presentations and links for the project website, eTwinning and social media.
The teachers should then use the digital tools in their own lessons or adapt them for themselves, supported by the project's own guidelines and a handbook.
All students, including girls, the socially, educationally and economically disadvantaged and refugees, should be able to participate in the activities. Through collaborative and communicative work with their national and transnational peers in English, students should not only improve their creativity and problem-solving skills, but also acquire important linguistic and intercultural competences. Furthermore, they should recognize the dangers of the Internet and learn how to navigate the Internet more safely.
All of this should aim to better prepare students for their future lives and careers in the digital age.

<< Implementation >>

In our activities, we explored media literacy and creatively integrated digital apps and tools into the classroom, including bionics, virtual reality, and programming with Lego robots, mBot2, VinciBot, drones, and 3D printers. 
We engaged with nature through an orienteering activity using the digital tool MapRun. Students utilized green screen technology to create videos highlighting environmental issues. 
Our project focused on digital skills such as media literacy, digital storytelling, coding, and robotics through media creation projects, encouraging participants to produce their own content (articles, videos) and understand the production process and ethical considerations. Participants developed digital stories using multimedia elements like text, images, audio, and video, creating interactive stories or choose-your-own-adventure projects on platforms like Book Creator. 
In addition to these activities, we engaged in cultural exchanges, including baking cookies, hosting cultural evenings, and visiting local towns, museums, and sights. These experiences fostered connections among participants and improved their English skills, enhancing their understanding of both digital tools and cultural diversity.

<< Results >>

The project results collectively support digital competency, cultural exchange, and environmental awareness in school education. 
A significant outcome was the enhancement of digital skills among students and teachers, who gained expertise in digital tools, coding, media literacy and content creation, preparing them for effective engagement in the digital landscape. 
The project ensured inclusive participation by involving all students, including girls and those facing social, educational, and economic disadvantages, fostering a sense of belonging and equal access to learning resources. 
Cultural exchange was promoted through activities like "Culture Stands", which strengthened participants' social skills and respect for diversity. Additionally, orienteering and sustainability sessions raised students' environmental awareness. 
To sustain and showcase the project outcomes, we produced a Guide Book for teachers and an e-magazine. We established digital platforms, including a project website and social media accounts to share resources widely and engage the community. Evaluation tools, such as surveys, measured improvements in digital readiness, ensuring the project's impact was effectively assessed.

2022-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000084338.title: European games
2022-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000084338.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to promote international awareness of Fair Play and to teach students moral values such as tolerance, respect, and solidarity. Given the increasing social isolation and the loss of basic social rules, especially during the pandemic, there is an urgent need to instill positive behaviors in students through innovative and sustainable approaches such as games, theater, and intercultural collaboration. Traditional teaching methods are often ineffective and fail to reach all students.

Our project aims to creatively and playfully convey values, foster conflict resolution, and strengthen intercultural understanding. It addresses challenges like bullying, discrimination, and a lack of social skills by engaging students in a dynamic learning process. By collaborating with transnational partners, we seek to develop new perspectives and methods that extend beyond the classroom, preparing students for successful and respectful lives in a globalized world.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to raise awareness of Fair Play values and establish them as fundamental principles for daily life and the school context. Our goal was to teach students tolerance, respect, solidarity, and morally responsible behavior to prepare them for successful and accountable lives in a globalized world.

Through collaboration with partner schools from different countries, we sought to analyze cultural differences, highlight commonalities, and develop innovative approaches to promote fairness and conflict resolution. The project intended to empower students through games, theater, and creative activities to strengthen social skills, reflect on rules, and enhance intercultural communication.

In the long term, we aimed to improve educational experiences, foster cohesion within schools, and create a model for other educational institutions that establishes Fair Play as a sustainable method for moral and social learning. The results were to be shared globally to achieve a broader impact.

<< Implementation >>

As part of our project, we carried out activities to promote Fair Play and strengthen intercultural competencies. The partner schools in Germany, Slovakia, Croatia, and Turkey focused on the following areas:

1. Traditional games: In Turkey, outdoor games were used to teach fairness and teamwork.
2. Digital and outdoor games: Croatia organized activities involving digital games, robotics, and coding, as well as outdoor games with children to foster creativity and social skills.
3. Cultural and school-based activities: In Slovakia, a city game with cultural elements, a field game, and a "Traditional Day" at school were organized, featuring workshops, games, drama, improvisation theater, and peer learning, all centered around Fair Play.
4. Folk dances, music, and classroom games: Germany focused on folk dances, music, and games presented by students in classrooms to enhance intercultural understanding.

The results were reflected upon, documented, and published in a European game book. 

<< Results >>

Our project achieved tangible outputs with lasting impact.

A key outcome was the creation of a European game book, documenting traditional, digital, and creative games to promote Fair Play, which was published on school websites and internal sharing platforms.

The activities enhanced students' intercultural competencies, teamwork, and conflict resolution skills. They learned to view Fair Play as a social and moral attitude. Workshops, games, and cultural activities provided authentic learning experiences, embedding values such as respect, tolerance, and solidarity.

Teachers incorporated the developed games and methods into their classes and schools, acting as multipliers. In the long term, the project fosters cultural exchange, raises awareness of Fair Play, and offers schools new approaches to teaching values. It strengthens social cohesion in schools and beyond.
topics: Human rights and rule of law

2022-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000081574.title: ECOhéroes. Nuestra misión: salvar el planeta
2022-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000081574.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was requested because it was innovative and because of the possibility of sharing experiences with European schools. The starting point was the consideration that part of our students presented a lack of responsible and sustainable attitudes and habits, especially in the personal, family and school spheres. On the other hand, teachers also needed to improve sustainable and pedagogical actions in their teaching practice, and it was considered that this project would be a great opportunity to exchange good practices with partner countries, as well as contribute to raising awareness among students and teachers about the environmental and social impact of aspects of their daily and educational actions and thus be able to improve them. In general, the entire Educational Community of our schools could also benefit from this project, through raising awareness and incorporating good sustainable practices that are respectful of the natural and social environment in their lives and daily routines. 
The needs addressed have been related to the development of activities aimed at creating environmental and social awareness in the different educational communities of Spain, Italy and Croatia according to the Sustainable Development 

<< Objectives >>

The objectives initially proposed for the development of the project were the following:
 1. Identify and understand the causes of the environmental and social problems that affect our planet and our immediate environment, as described by the "Sustainable Development Goals" of the 2030 Agenda.
    2. Raise awareness and acquire good practices for the protection and improvement of the social and natural environment to achieve the "Sustainable Development Goals" of the 2030 Agenda.
    3. Internationalize education in schools through collaboration with other countries within the framework of eTwinning and the Erasmus+ community.
With the execution of the Project, we hoped that the students would learn to recognize the main environmental problems, the impact of human beings and the social inequalities that currently affect their immediate environment and the environment of other countries. It was also our hope that the different Educational Communities would acquire good practices directed towards improvement of the surrounding environment, and therefore diminishing our negative impact on Europe's natural and social environment.

<< Implementation >>

Most of the activities designed in the project have been developed as initially planned and have been carried out through the seven missions that we had entrusted to our ECOhéroes. The activities have directed all intervention actions in the natural and social environment, raising awareness among students, teachers and families towards the use of sustainable and environmentally friendly practices and the involvement of local corporations.
Point out the motivation of all the students when receiving the letter about the different missions they had to carry out, the exchanges of experiences between the different schools by video calls, and the activities prepared by the receiving schools of the two teacher mobilities, Italy and Spain. 
It is our intention to continue with many of the actions already started and/or develop others similar to those described in the Project since we consider that they are not temporary and that we must continue working so that all Educational Communities continue with the commitment to the use of good practices to improve our environment and our planet.

<< Results >>

The good results obtained have been related to the knowledge of the seventeen United Nations Sustainable Development Goals by the three Educational Communities and have served to improve their impact on the natural and social environment, as well as raising awareness of sustainable development of the planet through cooperation, participation and civic engagement. In addition, each partner country carried out actions in the immediate environment to develop these sustainable development objectives and the schools shared the different ways of achieving these objectives and their results, learning from each other.

2022-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000081932.title: Effective Use of Technology in Education
2022-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000081932.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the growing need for effective use of technology in education while fostering social inclusion and combating discrimination in schools. European schools face challenges in engaging students, promoting intercultural understanding, and tackling prejudice. Through this project, we aimed to create an environment where students and teachers collaborate, explore European values, and embrace diversity. By incorporating Google tools and apps in English lessons, we wanted to make learning more engaging, enhance creativity, and encourage self-expression, steering students away from negative behaviours. The project also supported teachers by providing opportunities to exchange best practices and incorporate modern teaching methods using digital resources. The LTTAs focused on vital themes such as discrimination and religious tolerance, promoting intercultural communication skills and peer learning. Our ultimate goal was to inspire students and educators to create inclusive, tolerant, and technologically empowered learning environments.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to foster a more inclusive, engaging, and technologically advanced educational environment. Our primary goals were to combat discrimination, promote European values, and improve students' enthusiasm for learning, ultimately enhancing their academic performance and personal development. We sought to strengthen students’ digital literacy, analytical thinking, and intercultural communication skills through the integration of technology education lessons.

Through the LTTAs and activities such as workshops on tolerance and cultural and religious visits,  we wanted students to gain empathy, mutual respect, and a deeper understanding of diversity. The project also aimed to empower teachers by providing innovative tools and methods to create engaging, impactful lessons. By developing an e-book, hosting workshops, and exchanging best practices, we intended to leave a lasting impact on both teachers and students. Ultimately, the project aimed to nurture a generation that embraces diversity, collaborates effectively, and embodies the values of tolerance and cooperation. We also aimed for the relationships that were fostered during the project into extent into the future.

<< Implementation >>

Spain held practical seminars on the use of Canva, Flipgrid, and Powtoon, to create virtual lessons and presentations which the students and teachers could then use throughout the project. The ebook diary (see annex) was originally created using these tools before being converted into epub using book creator. The presentations on the schools and culture that were given were created using Canva.(see annex).
In Croatia we used online tools for e-books  with the week's focus on religious tolerance. Rather than each country presenting an English literature course, as stated in the original project, we talked about the literature of each country and turned our presentations into ebook format (see annex) as we considered this more culturally enhancing. 
In Turkey the focus was combatting discrimination, and we used digital tools to create quizzes and cartoons on the topic. To increase the project's unity and cultural aspect, Turkey organised cultural activities and other team-building events during the week. Students and teachers of all three countries stayed together in the same hotel during the week, eating every meal together and participating jointly in every moment of the day, increasing unity.


<< Results >>

The concrete outputs of the project include a set of project management documents, a project website, a Facebook page, dissemination materials, and lesson plans focused on tolerance and cooperation. We also produced an e-book diary and an e-book on tolerance as well as a presentation on the literature of the 3 countries.  In terms of educational content, workshops, computer-based English lessons, and  computer-based literature lessons were developed. Additionally,  events focused on tolerance and religious studies were organized.

The project’s broader results include enhanced student engagement and motivation, with improved academic performance and increased understanding of cultural diversity. Students developed better communication skills, particularly in foreign languages, and gained an appreciation for European unity. Teachers exchanged best practices and innovative teaching methods. The project fostered cultural, educational, temporal, and interpersonal bridges, creating lasting connections among students and educators from different European countries.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-FR01-KA210-SCH-000081983.title: TIME TO MAKE PEACE WITH NATURE
2022-1-FR01-KA210-SCH-000081983.summary:
<< Background >>

 The whole team had made the same observation : environmental problems threatens our world and makes it vulnerable.
We believed and still believe as teachers that we have a great responsibility in terms of preventing global warming. And, we agreed to say that informing and educate on global warming was essential and becoming urgent.
Besides, it was necessary to implement a green policy into our respective schools and involve the wole school community ( students, teachers and the staff  as well) and family about climate change.
Moreover, we believed that belonging to a transnational team was important because climate issue does not concern one country, but Europe and even the whole world.
So, through our project we intended to reinforce or to develop a policy on the issue.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted  to raise awareness to nature, to have more than basic knowledge on global warming and to encourage students ( as well as grown-ups ) to react and to act and also be able to identify and find solutions to problems related to nature.
At the end of the project, students and teachers have developped awareness on the countries’ respective issues : climate change, water footprint and carbon footprint, recycling and upcycling, zero waste and green consumption, and on natural disaster.
Our goal was to inform and warn on natural disasters, know how to prevent them and how to protect oneselves.
One of our target was also to be an environmental friendly consummers by recycling or upcycling, reduce our carbon / water footprint and reduce our waste..

<< Implementation >>

For each mobility, our goal was to propose activities leading to reflexions. We wanted to organize tangible activities  that could be used in our classes. Each mobility had the same pattern : a cultural, historical discovery and an immersion with a focus on the issue. In Croatia ( Natural Disaster. ), a visit in a park enabled us to see the consequences of flood,  a conference reinforced our understanding. In Turkiye,( water and carbon footprint) with the conference of a university teacher and of an environmental engineer, we benefited from specialists’ point of view inciting us to questions ourselves ( students and teachers as well ) on our consumption and we tried to find solutions to lower our water/ carbon footprint. All  visits enabled us to notice the consequences of climate change, alarmed us on the consequences of man’s excessive activities. On the whole the mobilities presented ecological issues and offered alternatives to handle the problem. Thus, in Finland a seminar on the consummer’s role permitted us to think over our individual behaviour. In France, recycling companies invited us to change our behaviour. In Portugal, among other things we symbolically planted a tree. On the whole, we have been active participants.

<< Results >>

As can be seen in our padlet  we shared lessons. Beyond this central activty, the mobilities allowed us not to be mere teachers but also witnesses of real issues. Our experiences in our partners’ contries enabled us to give concrete examples to our students and to avoid those ready-made documents that we can find in school books. We have been able to present the issues not only as teachers but as witnesses.
Thanks to our project we acquired an individual and collective awareness of the European territory.
We are no longer aware of climate issue at a small scale, as we discovered and exchanged about our partners’  different actions. 
The project encouraged us to share our experiences through different means : the creation of an etwinning project linked to our project, the participation of a challenged created by the regional administration of one our country, meetings, the inscription in eco school, 
As a result, we changed and develop our school environmental policy  by creating  plans and new objectives. Now our aim is to further our project.
All the changes can be discovered in the partners’ results of the project in the padlet : https://padlet.com/erasmuspad2023/erasmuspadlet-time-to-make-peace-with-nature-aoul6de99ff3b34

2022-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000081507.title: Reviving rural areas through sustainable tourism
2022-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000081507.summary:
<< Background >>

Following numerous climatic and social changes, we wanted to raise awareness and educate students about the importance of sustainability. Our schools applied for the project to make students better and more responsible citizens, to become more aware of the importance of the local and traditional, and to accept new ways of considering and dealing with some everyday problems that require different approaches and ways of solving them by the global changes we are witnessing.
We focused our goals on education and implementation of the above in students' everyday lives. We concentrate on several concrete goals, of which we single out the following: the importance of raising awareness of potential dangers and risks associated with unsustainable ways of travelling (carbon footprint share), protection of cultural and ecological heritage (traditional food, folklore, etc.), practising more sustainable activities that would increase implemented impacts on the Earth and  
reduced negative input on the environment, and increased engagement as proactive EU citizens.

<< Objectives >>

New generations of students need to be aware of their responsibility towards the future of our planet. They should be guided towards a new vision that prioritizes cultural and natural heritage for sustainability. The project aimed to raise students' awareness of nature and its needs following the period of pandemic-induced isolation. It also highlighted the detrimental impact of human activity on the environment. The project encouraged students to embrace a new philosophy of life centred on cooperation, respect, and dignity. By involving students in sustainable development and tourism, the project aimed to focus on the local environment. This served to help students understand local perspectives, appreciate local values, and recognize the significance of customs and traditions. Students were prompted to observe the downsides of mass tourism in the three countries participating in the project and were encouraged to actively work towards preserving diversity and protecting the environment. Through the project activities, students had the opportunity to experience sustainable lifestyles, learn how to contribute to environmental protection, and boost the local economy.

<< Implementation >>

During the initial stages, preparatory activities took place, including training sessions to familiarize the three countries with EU policies and institutions, online meetings for students to discuss ideas and project work, online meetings for teachers to share ideas and organize project steps, international visits to experience new cultures, and initiatives to promote sustainable travel and rediscover underdeveloped areas. The results were monitored through questionnaires for students, parents, and teachers. Additionally, there were meetings with teachers, students, and parents from our school and nearby schools to share the project experience and results through photo exhibitions, interviews, and videos. Students also acted as ambassadors for their school and presented the project results to other students.


<< Results >>

Our young students had the opportunity to meet with their foreign partners, enabling them to broaden their minds and knowledge. They were open to new perspectives, ways of addressing and solving problems, and new behaviours. This experience helped them become more aware of the importance of sustainable travel and the re-evaluation of rural areas, which hold rich traditions and values. They also realized the significance of protecting the environment as their present and future home. Additionally, they learned to appreciate diversity and promote European values. As a group, they created a joint concluding video where all participants shared their experiences and insights. This video was shared through various digital channels and intended to serve as a motivational tool for future international student activities. Moreover, they designed a code of behaviour for sustainable tourism, which they printed and distributed in schools.
Throughout the project implementation, we developed instructional materials using the CLIL (Content and Language Integrated Learning) method.
topics: Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

2022-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000082385.title: CAREFUL KIDS
2022-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000082385.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project since the teachers in each of the partner organizations had noticed that technology was starting to dominate the physical and mental development of our students and resulting in maladaptive behaviors such as hyperactivity and distraction, further confirmed through observations of the counseling teams at each institution (psychologist/pedagogist). The situation was only exacerbated due to the fact that our teachers were not sufficiently educated or qualified to address this issue by applying activities that could increase the level of motivation and attention among children in kindergarten and preschool (4-6 yo). The internally distributed surveys among our partners' employees confirmed what was already observed and discussed; the survey results demonstrated that an overwhelming 90% of the respondents felt inadequately trained for attention and motivation developing activities in formation education.
The project Careful Kids was designed to specifically address this need in a systematic and structured way and add a transnational dimension to it in the sense that both teachers and organizations could share their best practices and learn from each other in order to improve the children's well-being.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project Careful Kids,  the main goals we wanted to achieve were as follows:

1. To address the shortcomings in education and qualification observed among our teachers by providing them with the opportunity to gain craft knowledge, skills and experience in order to improve the children's attention and motivation in preschool education through  mindfulness, Intelligence Games, Orienteering, Rhythm activities, and
2. To increase the capacity of all the partner organizations by transferring knowledge on these issues to our students and institutions.

More specifically, our goals were also:
1. To be able to integrate activities about attention and motivation into our school subject contents,
2. To produce a guide material for Attention and Motivation activities for preschool education, and
3. To increase our rate of attention-motivation activities in our schools from 15% to 30%, as aimed per our strategic plans.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented the following activities in our project:

1. Attention development activity with MINDFULNESS
2. Attention development activity with ORIENTEERING
3. Attention development activity with INTELLIGENCE GAMES
4. Attention development activity with RHYTHM ACTIVITIES

Publication of Handbook on Attention and Motivation games, to be used by our own educators and other institutions interested in improving their rates of attention and motivation among children

Horizontal activities: Dissemination, Localization and Piloting, Evaluation

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and other results of our project were as follows:

- Four (4) fully implemented LTTAs - attention development activities on different topics (Mindfulness, Orienteering, Intelligence Games, Rhythm) on four different locations, 
- Produced guide materials for attention and motivation education in preschool education,
- Developed teachers' professional skills to integrate attention and motivation into school subject contents in preschool education,
- Acquired and learned new approaches and activity practices on Mindfulness, Orienteering, Intelligence Games, and Rhythm in education on
attention and motivation education,
- Improved rate of giving place to attention and motivation improving activities in our kindergartens (initially planned from 15% to 30%, actually realized from 17.84% to 32,24%)
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000082711.title: Think globally, act locally
2022-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000082711.summary:
<< Background >>

We want to make a turn from the traditional transfer of knowledge towards innovative, new teaching methods: research and project teaching, team work and purposeful use of ICT. With this project we want to empower teachers in teaching about sustainable development. In order to achieve this, continuous training and sharing of good teaching practice is necessary. Teachers who go on mobility share their knowledge with other teachers in the school so the whole school benefits, especially our students. We want to connect with schools in Europe and enable our students to make international contacts with their peers and strengthen self-confidence, improve communication and presentation skills. We want to increase students' interest in climate change and increase their motivation to participate in activities related to environmental protection.



<< Objectives >>

We want the topics of sustainable development to be more represented in the school curriculum in order to train students for active participation in environmental protection at the local and national level. It is
necessary to encourage discussion and learning about environmental protection, to influence the change of attitudes and daily habits, and to encourage green action in society.
The activities proposed in this project seek to help students understand how climate change affects the Earth. Students are encouraged to act to make the world a better place. During the project, students raise awareness and spread knowledge about sustainable development. 

<< Implementation >>

Students actively participated in activities related to sustainable development such as painting exhibitions, created essays, comics, and leaflets, created digital and written materials in the form of posters, brochures, leaflets. Students created usable products from waste and used materials. Students worked in school gardens. Students visited places where they had the opportunity to meet and see examples of sustainable development: Technical Museum Zagreb, Aquatika Karlovac, Munster Museum of Natural History, Krka National Park, an example of sustainability in the local community of Murau. The following days were marked: World Water Day, Earth Day, World Environment Day, European Car Free Day, Earth Hour. Interesting lectures with concrete examples were held: the importance of groundwater; about an invasive type of cancer in Croatian rivers;  the concept of the New European Bauhaus. The project encouraged students to participate in environmental protection initiatives: activities related to the signal cancer, an invasive species in the Korana river, which originates in the NP Plitvice Lakes  and flows through our municipality. Students participated in the campaign of wrapping trees with jute to protect the trees from beavers.

<< Results >>

School curriculum enriched with projects related to climate change, sustainable development and environmental protection. Improving awareness of the European dimension through intercultural cooperation.
Students initiate activities in the local community related to environmental protection and take responsibility for their future. Teachers wrote reports after the mobilities. Planned activities are described and photos are attached. Students recorded videos, exhibitions were organized. Brochures were created to spread information about our activities to a wider audience. 
A handbook for teachers with topics of sustainable development was created. The results, which include visual artwork, essays, comics, and leaflets, will serve as valuable educational materials and continue to raise awareness about the importance of taking action for a sustainable future.
We disseminated the activities through the school's website, the social networks Facebook and Instagram and through the project's website.
https://sites.google.com/view/think-globally-act-locally/project-results
http://os-barilovic.skole.hr/erasmus/ka210_think_globally_act_locally or new page https://test-os-barilovic.cms.skole.hr/k210-think-globally-act-locally/
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000082831.title: Marine Robots for better Sea Knowledge awareness
2022-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000082831.summary:
<< Background >>

MASK project application was done because of the COVID-19 pandemic related impact on education and environment. While the pandemic created many negative impacts on school education including lack of hands-on classes, it also created opportunities MASK wished to explore, e.g. a shift towards e-learning. Similarly, digital skills of students were affected and disparities aggravated during the pandemic. On the other hand, COVID-19 had positive impacts in the environment with a reduction in pollution but it also had less visible negative impacts, e.g. increased medical garbage (surgical masks, COVID tests, etc). Finally, universities with e-learning capabilities can transfer the recent advances in the Artificial Intelligence (AI) and robotics fields to high school students.

MASK project addressed the need of providing high-quality theoretical and practical classes even in pandemic contexts with mobility restrictions. In addition, it answer the need to fight the digital divide and to exploit the remote possibilities to allow any student anywhere in the planet to perform robotics experiments and learn AI which is an urgent need for the future workforce. Finally, MASK addressed the need for better awareness of the COVID-19 environmental

<< Objectives >>

The overall goal that the project wanted to achieve was to improve the knowledge of high school students and their teachers in the area of marine robotics and AI applied to environmental monitoring by giving special attention to remote access to infrastructures capabilities. MASK wished to achieve a wider awareness on environmental issues that can be tackled by marine robots; a higher number of students attracted to STEM; an increased use of remote learning technologies; more similar cooperation and exchange initiatives. This was reflected in 5 objectives:
1 encourage interest in both students and teachers towards robotics, artificial intelligence, and STEM in general, by stimulating students to work in STEM-related projects;
2 engage and keep students motivated, with the goals of a) contributing to a decrease in dropout rates and b) encourage a STEM career for every student;
3 increase the digital competences and skills of both students and teachers, with an emphasis on applications in robotics and AI;
4 exploit the possibilities introduced by remote access to provide high quality lectures and perform remote robotic trials;
5 raise awareness about climate change and environmental protection and mitigation, using marine robotics.

<< Implementation >>

The project was divided into 5 activities: Learning marine robotics and Artificial Intelligence (AI), Training the trainers, Remote testing of marine robots, Robotics educational activities at sea and Dissemination at major event. Out of these activities, four were targeting mostly the virtual format while the fourth one was focused on experiments at sea in Croatia (twice). We implemented all five activities as planned.

The first activity consisted of high-quality lectures from the university partners towards the students focused on the basics of marine robotics and Artificial Intelligence (AI) and their applications (especially environmental protection). 

The second activity involved the teachers to make sure that their digital skills are increased and that they are fully ready to support the students throughout the project.

The third one allowed students to perform hands-on robotics testing remotely while the fourth one was composed of testing of robots at sea in real environments twice in the project. 

Finally, the fifth activity included dissemination at an international conference and this was done twice overdelivering what was initially promised.

<< Results >>

The most tangible result is an introductory interdisciplinary study course targeted for high school students on marine robotics and AI and their applications to environmental issues. The course is composed of a series of lectures performed by the universities and it is replicable and usable by not only the participating organisations but by any other high school as the course it is available in the Erasmus+ Project Results Platform

Moreover, the project is increased the awareness of environmental issues by collecting real garbage from the ocean and allowing the students to witness first-hand the impact of pollution at sea. MASK increased as well the capabilities of students both in remote piloting and piloting robots at sea and the interest of students and teachers in this field. In particular, a follow-up project has been submitted due to the strong interest of the schools of continuing learning about marine robotics and AI and one of the schools submitted another project proposal related to AI.

Finally, the wide dissemination and experience from this project is being replicated/extended through other projects and Master thesis at the Universities involved.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-HU01-KA210-SCH-000081028.title: Creative and Original Development in Education
2022-1-HU01-KA210-SCH-000081028.summary:
<< Background >>

Within the scope of small-scale partnerships, our project, "Creative and Original Development in Education" (CODE), aimed to support innovative learning and foster the creativity of young minds. Digital skills and materials were developed as part of the project. The traditional school environment was transformed into an innovative school environment. 
The development of our students' foreign language skills was supported. The project also facilitated the recognition of different cultures and their educational settings, enabling the transfer of best practices to our schools.
We have met the need for an educational approach in our schools that focuses on product and innovation transfer. Our students' interdisciplinary thinking skills, technological literacy and three-dimensional thinking abilities have developed. Awareness of art and sports has been supported.

<< Objectives >>

We contributed to raising awareness of European citizenship through tolerance and respect for diversity. Our students enhanced their self-motivation and communication skills. With students possessing adequate digital skills, we supported the labor market. We increased interest in STEAM subjects among our students, especially female students. We fostered trust in science and technology. Activities were conducted to promote participation and align with the green and digital agenda.

Our synergistic partnership, aimed at developing cross-skills, has shown that we are ready for the Europe of the future, with the awareness it has created not only in technology but also in innovative science teaching methods.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, four short-term international mobility activities were carried out with the themes 'Benefits of Science and Technology to Society,' 'How to Integrate Science and Technology with Everyday Life,' 'What to Do to Be an Active European Citizen,' and 'Technology Is a Perfect Tool.’

We conducted training sessions on STEM, STEAM, coding, 3D design, robotics, MicroPython, digital art, and the 5E and 7E instructional models. In our institution the number of lessons of STEAM subjects is relatively low compared to the other partners although there is huge demand for it. By sharing and exchanging good practices the target groups received a lot of additional information including applications, teaching methods and digital content. During the cooperation with the transnational partners all participants learnt from the other. (See Annexes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
https://school-education.ec.europa.eu/tr/etwinning/projects/code-0/twinspace/pages
