<< Results >>

We developed digital materials and transferred best practices for an innovative school environment. Our teachers became aware of new pedagogical practices. Interest among female students in STEAM subjects increased, and awareness of active European citizenship developed. During the project, we used digital tools such as Canva, Voki, Kahoot, Google Forms, and Drive. We designed the project logo and posters. Logos ensuring EU visibility were used on badges, posters, invitations, agendas, and certificates. 

Before each mobility, we held online meetings with teachers, families, and students. We created mailing groups and launched an eTwinning (ESEP) project, encouraging participation from both students and teachers. A project website was created to share our activities and school introductions. We actively used school websites, participants' Instagram and Facebook pages, and YouTube channels for sharing. Visits were organized to science and technology centers, museums, and energy production facilities. 

Additionally, we held seminars, conferences, roundtable discussions, fun games, activities to learn local languages, and presentations introducing the school and region.

2022-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000081784.title: Together We win
2022-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000081784.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we recognized a pressing need for better education and awareness regarding environmental issues among our students. We identified a lack of sufficient information on critical topics such as sustainable development, ecosystem preservation, climate change, biodiversity. It became evident that our students lacked understanding regarding the finite nature of resources, distribution challenges,  pollution levels, and the degradation of natural habitats, all of which threaten our planet's future.
To address these gaps, our objective was to implement an educational initiative that not only raises awareness but also inspires concrete actions to combat environmental degradation. We believe it's paramount to instill environmentally friendly habits in our students to contribute to the preservation of our planet. Our project aimed to promote sustainability across various aspects of life, including school practices and responsible environmental behavior aligning with the values and vision of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Through this project, we aimed to involve students from partner schools in collaborative, interactive, and engaging activities focused on sustainability.


<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, our primary objectives were  to enhance students' awareness and understanding of environmental issues, including sustainable development, ecosystem preservation, climate change, biodiversity, and waste management.We sought to inspire behavioral change among students by instilling in them the importance of adopting sustainable practices in their daily lives.
By engaging students in hands-on experiences and using modern ICT tools, we aimed to make learning about environmental issues more compelling and accessible.
We aimed to foster collaboration and cooperation among students from partner schools, as well as with experts and teachers. Through joint activities and projects, students would have the opportunity to learn from each other and benefit from diverse perspectives on sustainability.
By promoting sustainability across various aspects of life,  we aimed to contribute to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) outlined in the agenda.
Overall, our goal was to empower students to become informed and proactive agents of change who are committed to preserving the environment and creating a sustainable future for generations to come.


<< Implementation >>

In our project, we implemented a range of activities aimed at achieving our objectives of raising awareness, inspiring behavioral change, fostering collaboration, and promoting active participation in environmental sustainability. Some of the key activities included interactive Workshops and Seminars to educate students about various environmental issues, biodiversity loss and endangered species 
 We developed and delivered thematic language units in the digital book that focused on environmental topics, incorporating relevant vocabulary and concepts into the lessons. 



<< Results >>

The "Together We Win" on Sustainability and Biodiversity project produced several concrete outputs and notable results. These included the development of language learning modules focused on sustainability and biodiversity, multilingual educational resources, and interactive digital tools and online platforms. We organize dworkshops, seminars, field trips, and community projects that provided hands-on learning experiences and opportunities for intercultural exchange. Additionally, dissemination materials such as reports and best practice guides were produced to document the project's processes and outcomes.
It led to increased language proficiency among participants, particularly in environmental vocabulary and discussions. It also enhanced cultural awareness and sensitivity, fostering greater understanding of how different cultures approach sustainability and biodiversity. Participants developed a deeper understanding of these environmental issues, leading to more environmentally conscious behaviors. Educators involved in the project improved their teaching practices through professional development opportunities. The project's activities and outputs had a broader impact also on the community

2022-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000082804.title: OUR LEARNING SPACE : OUTDOOR EDUCATION
2022-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000082804.summary:
<< Background >>

With the Covid 19 epidemic that started to be seen in the world in 2019, our students started to study at home. This situation has restricted students' access to nature and caused them to move away from their natural environments and forget the geographies they live in. With the epidemic under control, schools started education again. After the epidemic, educational activities in schools were increasingly confined to the walls of classrooms, causing students to move away from nature and not recognize the environment they live in. At the same time, taking students away from their computers and placing them within the walls of the classroom caused social and academic disorders in students.

This project aimed to solve this problem by developing quality outdoor education in schools. In this context, the following needs were met in our project.
* The need for teachers' lack of knowledge and skills in order to carry out outdoor education in our schools was met.
* Teachers' need for international knowledge on outdoor education was met.
* The need to eliminate the indifferent attitude of students towards the environment and nature they live in was met.
* The need to eliminate students' indifference towards lessons and school was met.

<< Objectives >>

At the beginning of the project; An analysis study was conducted for students and teachers in our school to learn about the reflections of the Covid 19 epidemic on the school. According to the analysis results, students mostly wanted lessons to be held outdoors. However, it has been noticed that teachers lack skills in implementing outdoor education. Thereupon, our school aimed to solve the problem on an international scale by collaborating with other institutions in the European Union. In this way, we wanted to aim to improve teachers' outdoor education competencies. At the same time, we wanted to achieve the following goals in our project;

* We wanted to improve the competencies of teachers so that outdoor education can be carried out in our schools.
* We wanted our teachers to gain experience in international cooperation in outdoor education.
* We wanted our teachers to specialize in outdoor education.
* We wanted our schools to implement innovative education-training methods.
* We wanted outdoor education to be learned locally and internationally.
* We wanted to learn the advantages and risks of outdoor education in practice.
* We wanted students to have improvements in academic-social-psychological areas.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented 6 Activities in our project. We implemented 4 of these activities as a mobility activity, 1 as a virtual meeting activity and 1 as a dissemination activity. The activities carried out in the project are as follows.

1) Italy Activity: Teaching the educational processes for outdoor education and solving the problems encountered in education were taught.

2) Portugal Activity: What are the academic studies on outdoor education at local, national and international levels and how the course should be planned were taught.

3) Croatia Activity: The effects of out-of-school activities on students and the methods of measurement and evaluation in outdoor activities were taught.

4) Turkey Activity: Teachers learned how to design areas for outdoor education and how to choose areas for outdoor education.

5) Virtual Activity: In our mobility activities, the missing trainings were completed and the problems encountered in practice were solved.

6) Dissemination Activity: In order to achieve the aims and objectives of our project, activities to be carried out locally, dissemination activities and the management area of the project were planned.

<< Results >>

The goals and objectives included in the content of our project have been achieved. In this context, firstly, the forms specified in the project were applied to teachers and students. The concrete results achieved are as follows.
* Teachers' implementation of outdoor education in their lessons (according to the results of the applied form) reached 82% from 13% in one year.
* Teachers' skill levels in outdoor education have increased from 46% to 92%.
* The proportion of students who stated that they were bored with the lessons at school and the place (classroom) where the lessons were taught decreased from 63% to 9%.

At the same time, the following activities were carried out as concrete outputs in our project together with the partner schools.
* In our project, a book about what outdoor education is and its implementation stages was created and distributed to all stakeholders. 
* In our project, sample outdoor lesson plans were created for all teachers to use and distributed to all stakeholders. 
* An android phone application for outdoor education was produced together with partner schools.
* Outdoor education was presented at an international conference and produced as a book and article with ISBN number.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2022-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000083848.title: S-TEAM: Schools Team-up using hackathon for girls' inclusive STEM
2022-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000083848.summary:
<< Background >>

The S-TEAM project addressed the significant shortage of women in STEM careers and education across the EU. Despite women representing 52% of the European population and 57.7% of graduates in the EU, they account for only 2 in 5 scientists and engineers. The underrepresentation of women in the digital sector at all levels is a concerning issue, and attitudes toward STEM subjects among girls decline dramatically between ages 15 and 16. Recognising the critical role of schools and teachers in eliminating the gender gap, the project raised awareness and provided equal opportunities in STEM education. The project addressed the need to improve STEM training for schools by integrating ad hoc practices to promote female participation, providing hands-on experiences, encouraging teachers to support STEM pursuits, showcasing real applications of STEM subjects, and instilling confidence in equal opportunities. By involving a school, an educational centre, and an association in transnational cooperation, the project comprehensively addressed the factors influencing girls' interest in STEM. The use of Hackathon further emphasised the project's commitment to fostering girls' inclusion and addressing gender equality in STEM.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objective of implementing the S-TEAM project is to enhance the accessibility and appeal of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) subjects for girls, ultimately diminishing the gender gap evident in the selection of STEM-related educational pathways. The project strategically targets the age group of 11-14, recognising this period as crucial for intervention, as gender stereotypes have yet to firmly establish themselves in the educational trajectories of students, thus preventing potential future discouragements. Specific objectives include: 
- Develop integrated training paths for STEM subjects that incorporate practices and models encouraging equal participation and recognition of girls.
- Facilitate the exchange of best practices among European schools to enhance STEM training courses and implement effective strategies for reducing the gender gap.
- Make STEM subjects accessible and tangible for students aged 14-14, emphasising female inclusion through gamification and Hackathon.
- Promote the European dimension in participating schools by involving teachers and students from diverse European countries through online and in-person forums.


<< Implementation >>

The activities implemented in S-TEAM project are the following: the initial phase consisted of evaluating national and local context regarding the inclusion of women and girls in STEM disciplines in schools. After, partners engaged in online meetings to exchange best practices and experiences in STEM teaching and girls' inclusion. The result was the development of a transnational STEM training course and a memorandum of best practices for teachers. This methodology was tested simultaneously in the three schools, each representing a partner country (Italy, Spain and Croatia).  The testing phase lasted four months and involved simultaneous activities in three classes per school.  These activities consisted of introductory lessons, project work (Local Hackathon) and project presentations. For each school, one winning group of students were selected and participated in a European Hackathon in Rimini, Italy. The Hackathon concluded with a final conference attended by professional women in STEM disciplines. Awards were presented, including special recognition for the girls. Each school received three advanced STEM toolkits for ongoing projects and replicability.


<< Results >>

The concrete outputs of the S-TEAM project are the transnational inclusive STEM training course designed for both girls and boys enhancing the knowledge and skills of students in STEM disciplines. The Memorandum of Best Practices tailored for teachers outlining the most effective modalities, actions, and tools that educators can employ to implement a girls' inclusive STEM course. The European Hackathon, providing a platform for students from the three participating countries to work together to bring their innovative STEM projects to fruition. The results of the project encompassed awareness-raising on gender inequality in STEM, development of educational strategies and interventions to promote gender equality in this field, improvements in STEM teaching methodologies with a specific focus on addressing gender disparities, increased knowledge and curiosity among students (especially girls), and the ultimate goal of achieving higher and enduring female participation in STEM-related careers.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-LT01-KA210-SCH-000084732.title: Go Europe Green with EPAS
2022-1-LT01-KA210-SCH-000084732.summary:
<< Background >>

Alytus Jotvingiai Gymnasium has been the European Parliament Ambassador School since 2019 as well as the Ambassador of the STEM School Label project on the European and national levels. In 2022 the Lithuanian EPAS team invited two active EPA schools from Greece and Croatia to cooperate in the project "Go Europe Green with EPAS" as well as celebrate the 2022 - the year of European and Lithuanian Youth. The main need for the partnership was to get the international youth activated together taking part in the non-formal learning activities, developing network, integrating green practices into various aspects of the project and getting to know about the European Green Course. Creating "Ecological routes" was symbolically and practically chosen as an attractive innovation for  young people to work on as well as a useful product for the wide society. The project was a composite and integral means of implementing horizontal and school education priorities on the European and national levels.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to involve 16-18-year-old students from Lithuania, Croatia and Greece with different interaction level at schools: less active students, Student Council members and the EPAS teams, who want to build a sense of responsibility for the environment.
In harmony with the strategic needs of all three schools, we set three main objectives in the project:
1.	To develop international cooperation among 3 EPA schools, raising awareness of EU initiatives in the European Green Course and contributing to Europe’s continent to become eco friendly continent;
2.	To promote the leadership of young people encouraging their involvement in the civic and environmental engagement activities in each country and learning non formally;
3.	To improve XXI st century competencies – communication, digitalization, leadership, problem solving, critical thinking, initiative and social skills – and apply them in creating the main project outputs and other results.

<< Implementation >>

There were three main stages planned in the project - EPAS International Cooperation, Creating and testing ecological routes in Croatia and Spreading the voice of "Go Europe Green": from idea to European networking in Greece. Before, during and after the study visits in each country we implemented the following activities:
•	Leadership activities: team building, networking, project logo contest;
•	Communication workshops in each country to create chat groups for communication, movies about their own school, share ideas and opinions;
•	Non formal learning activities in order to get knowledge about ecological problems around the world;
•	Social and initiative activities to promote a sense of environmental responsibility;
•	Digitalization activities to create ecological routes in each country and test by the students from Lithuania, Croatia and Greece; presentation materials;
•	Study visits in each country in order to learn and participate internationally; 
•	Dissemination activities: WordPress blog of the project was created and the information of the project team, activities and ecological routes had been posted there; conferences and the tour of sharing the results of the project.

<< Results >>

1.	An international network of Go Europe Green schools was created.
2.	The weblog “Go Europe Green with EPAS” was created in order to promote activities and results.
3.	3 study visits organized in Lithuania, Croatia and Greece.
4.	7 ecological routes were created in Lithuania, Croatia and Greece, which were published on Google Maps (2 routes), and on the global travel network www.wikiloc.com 6 routes). 
5.	All participants acquired knowledge on Europe’s Green Course politics, environmental problems in each country and skills through practical sessions: lectures, international conferences, discussions, trips to national parks, reserves, visits to cultural heritage objects in partner cities, drawing up routes according to the visited objects.
6.	All participants improved their leadership, problem-solving, English, digital and civic competencies.
7.	There were 2 international conferences organized in Croatia and Greece and a tour of sharing results nationally in Lithuania. 
8.The results of the project are a methodological and practical example for other schools and societies internationally in order to promote their living places as green environments, participate actively and learn to become eco friendly communities.

2022-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000081537.title: AN INSPIRING NETWORK FOR A SUSTAINABLE PLANET AND AN INCLUSIVE RENEWED EDUCATION
2022-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000081537.summary:
<< Background >>

In September 2022, a survey among our students highlighted significant challenges post-Covid-19, such as difficulty focusing during online classes, separating home life from school, and dealing with distractions. These issues resulted in academic and behavioral problems upon returning to school. We observed a lack of engagement, concentration difficulties, procrastination, missed deadlines, and increased aggression and anxiety among students
To address these, we prioritized promoting common values, civic engagement, and emotional intelligence. We wanted to enhance students' understanding of these values and entrepreneurial skills. Aligning with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, we also prioritized fighting climate change and developing students' green skills, integrating values education, community engagement, inclusivity, and environmental education
We needed to improve digital skills through project activities, helping students gain 21st-century competences necessary for school, work, and life, to make students more focused and responsible for their future and the planet's sustainability. Over a three-year period, we aimed to reduce the issues identified, support European citizenship, and share best practices locally.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to
-address the academic and behavioral challenges our students faced post-Covid-19, such as difficulty focusing, procrastination, and increased anxiety. Our primary goal was to promote common values, civic engagement, and emotional intelligence. We sought to help students understand and practice these values, develop entrepreneurial skills, and improve their emotional well-being
- foster environmental awareness and action in line with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development 
-develop students' green skills through values education, community engagement, and environmental education and fight against climate change, inspiring our entire school community
-enhance our students' digital skills and 21st-century competences, preparing them for success in school, work, and life while striving for a sustainable planet, to encourage creative and responsible thinking about global sustainability
-help students become more focused and responsible, support European citizenship, and share best practices locally
By integrating the common values, civic engagement and environmental sustainability issues, we aimed at meeting the needs of the participating organisations' teachers, students and stakeholders

<< Implementation >>

In Poland-workshops on entrepreneurial skills, common values, emotional intelligence to equip students with life skills for sustainability as a sustainable planet requires teaching common human values
In Ankara-workshops on composting and climate change, a planting activity by TEMA, visits to the Museum and Endemic Valley to learn about extinct and endemic species
In Croatia we discussed green skills and sustainable lifestyles, created a digital board, attended a workshop on natural wastewater treatment,  explored biodiversity through a tour organized by Zagorje Nature Center
In Slovakia we focused on digital, entrepreneurial, green skills. Students took part in an escape room contest, a workshop on climate change using the TPRS method, built a 3D Food Chain Pyramid 
In Sinop we made a digital board, dissemination materials: an online ebook, a digital board, a printed booklet, a curriculum integration and a project report plans
Local activities -visits to welfare agencies, tree planting, poem writing, sharing project gains at schools, researching endemic and endangered species, organizing vegan lunches and upcycling activities, exchanging street games, preparing presentations on natural disasters and future dangers for humanity

<< Results >>

This project was based on a needs analysis of our partner institutions. We aimed to
-reduce the % of teachers who observed a loss of motivation and concentration in students from 75% to 40%. Post-project surveys indicated 100% of teachers noticed positive changes in student motivation and concentration
-reduce the % of teachers who observed negative behavioral changes in students from 80% to 50%, with 80% reporting positive changes post-project
- increase the % of teachers who felt equipped to promote entrepreneurial skills and environmental sustainability from 29% to 80%, achieving this target
-decrease the % of students who felt unmotivated to study from 80% to 30%, resulting in an impressive 8.2% post-project
-decrease the %of students lacking knowledge on sustaining the planet from 70% to 20%. Post-project, 100% of students reported having sufficient knowledge.
We evaluated each activity, culminating in an evaluation report shared with all partners. This report confirmed that the project met all its objectives and enhanced the European dimension of the participating organizations. The project provided a sustainable vision to inspire students to meet the European Union's targets for skills, competences, values, and profiles.

2022-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000081541.title: ZRÓBMY CHOCIAŻ COKOLWIEK
2022-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000081541.summary:
<< Background >>

The analysis of the school's needs showed that it is important to educate young people in the conscious use of the Internet. Such education is closely related to the improvement of key competences. The implementation of this type of intentions on an international scale meets the school's need to develop international contacts and methodically enriches the ways of influencing and shaping appropriate attitudes of young people. Moreover, the problem addressed in this project is independent of geography or nationality. As part of the project activities, it was planned to create tools and processes leading to improvement of the actual situation. Of course, the problem is huge, and the results of our activities are only a small help in shaping appropriate attitudes online, which should be the task of all educators. Experience gained from other projects has shown that interpersonal contacts established during the project are long-lasting and perfectly enhance the improvement of key competences (especially communicating in a foreign language) and build a sense of European citizenship.

<< Objectives >>

The intention of this project was: to build teachers' awareness of the subject of educational work, and to shape students' critical attitudes in the perception of network resources and to involve them in creating actions supporting noble activities and to mobilize students to act in partnership with teachers to achieve noble goals. It was also planned that the project results will serve all interested parties as methodological tools to be used during classes aimed at shaping young people's criticism, understanding the threats of being online and taking responsibility for their behavior online. The project's objectives described in this way fulfill the necessary and important need for societies and communities to develop the ability to use the Internet wisely and honestly. A sense of responsibility is an inherent element of such education. Building teachers' awareness of shaping this type of attitudes in students is the starting point for their educational activities.

<< Implementation >>

In accordance with the adopted instructions, three meetings were held in partner schools, devoted to topics that make up the entire issue covered in this project. The main goal of the project was to build students' and teachers' awareness of the benefits and threats of using the Internet. The materials developed during the project were widely disseminated so that they could be used to shape appropriate attitudes of network users. Before the start of implementation, a meeting of representatives of partner schools was held, during which details related to project management were agreed. We have established cooperation with research workers from the JP II University in Krakow. Cooperation with a research institution in Warsaw was planned, but due to the costs (which increased significantly due to inflation), cooperation was initiated with a closer (in terms of distance) university, whose institute of media and social communication is recognized and its employees were willing to cooperate .
Before the meeting at our school, they conducted workshops in which partners participated online. During the meeting, further workshop sessions were held in stationary form.


<< Results >>

International cooperation during the project implementation provided many benefits to both students and teachers. The students improved their key competences, established friendly contacts with the participants, and experienced a wonderful educational adventure that shaped their sense of European citizenship and often changed their plans for further education. Teachers gain non-standard professional experience and learn the systems and methods of educational work of teachers from other countries. Cultural activities and trips carried out during the mobility allowed participants to learn about the history, culture and customs of partner countries. The completed project involved the entire school community through activities promoting the project, observations of subsequent project tasks, and participation in an event summarizing the project and presenting its results. In May 2024, at the Secondary School in Sucha Beskidzka, there will be workshops for teachers conducted by UJP II research workers on the topics covered during the project. The idea for such a training is the result of a project that showed how important it is to develop appropriate attitudes online and teachers need support in this aspect.

2022-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000082104.title: I Learn Better with Different Learning Methods
2022-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000082104.summary:
<< Background >>

We wanted to adapt our schools: students and teachers to the challenges posed by the modern world and developing technology and science, and to keep up with news in the field of learning and teaching in the 21st century. People currently need to have various skills, such as creativity, critical thinking, problem solving, and effectiveness use of technology, information management, cooperation and communication. Use of information and communication technologies help shape the educational process in accordance with the individual needs and characteristics of the students, providing different methods that can offer new opportunities in the learning environment (learning through art, online collaborative learning, learning in multiple environments, project-based learning and STEM). The aims of our project were:  to attract students' attention, to interest them in learning and maintain the high quality of teaching in our institutions by learning about various teaching methods; to make students comprehend the importance of museum and art education, to know STEM method and Project Based Learning Method, And equip teachers with modern technological tools and knowledge about IT innovations that can be applied to education.

<< Objectives >>

In our project, we aimed to contribute to the creativity and mental development of our students with multiple learning methods. 
The main objectivs were:
- To attract students' attention, keep their motivation and interest by enabling them to use ICT tools.
- To make students comprehend the importance of this relationship of museum and art education as the development of
knowledge, skills and personality.
- To develop students' characteristics such as research, self-confidence, responsibility and cooperation with project-based
learning methods.
-With STEM education, to enable students create realistic engineering designs by associating realistic life problems with the
contents of science, mathematics, technology and engineering fields and to contribute to their problem solving, innovation,
critical thinking, scientific literacy and high-level thinking skills.
- In line with our goals, with the "Development of Key Competencies", which is one of the horizontal priorities of the
Erasmus+ program, it is aimed to equip our students with Basic Competencies in Mathematics, Science and Technology,
Digital Competence, Learning to Learn, Cultural Consciousness and Awareness.

<< Implementation >>

We have created a project logo and project teams in each partner school. There were four mobilities for students and teachers to each of the partner schools. For dissemination of the project we designed and produced various products in printing press. More than 100 posters, 500 pens, 500 notebooks, 500 files, 30 badges, 1000 project brochures and 100 certificates were prepared by each school. Zoom meetings were held with the partners. The meetings served to prepare the project, prepare for mobility and evaluate the activities that have already taken place and discuss plans and further activities. Whatsapp gropup were created and used for comunication between coordinators and participants of subsequent mobilities. English corners were prepared at schools. Project website and fecabook page were created and all the activites done were shared there. We reported on all activities that took place during the mobility on our school websites and on our school fan pages in social media and by local media.

<< Results >>

The museum and art education which was done in Turkey helped the students to develop their creativity skills. It  helped teachers to organise museum activities in connection with the units in the curriculum and reflect museum education to interdisciplinary learning environments.With STEM education in Croatia students had an increase in their ability of analyzing real life problems and gaining entrepreneurship skills.By “involving our parents in the education process,” which is one of the goals of our organisations, our participants who did STEM activities had an increase at learning at home, production, new invention and cooperation studies.In this way, the trio of school-student-family bond contributed to the improved quality of life.After the classes they took on robotics and Web 2.0 tools in Spain,teachers started to use Web 2.0 tools in their classes and also they are able able to integrate these skills into their lessons. Project- based learning in Poland contributed to make the school environment of our participants more enjoyable and interesting.The participants learned different methods to use in their classes.They met with their colleagues from different nationalities in the EU. They improved their communication skills.

2022-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000082143.title: My Peer My Guide
2022-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000082143.summary:
<< Background >>

Although the problems we identified in the consortium schools were the same every year, we were having difficulty finding solutions. Traditional methods are not sufficient to solve these problems. We started looking for innovative solutions to these problems we identified. We decided that we could solve these problems with the peer counseling method. We applied a program screening inventory to 750 students in the consortium schools and tried to examine the 5 most marked items. In addition, we aimed to reduce early school leaving.
After the project, we re-administered the 50-question problem screening inventory to 750 students.The decrease rates in students' problems are given below.
1- A lot of time with technology  -48% -41.7%  --- Reduction Rate 13.12%
2- Bullying -44% - 27.9%  --- Reduction Rate 36.59.%
3- Business concern  -43,2% - 38 % --- Reduction Rate 35.34%
4- Can't control anger-41% - 30.8%--- Reduction Rate 24.87%
5- Low self-perception -39% 25.4% --- Reduction Rate 34.87%
The average of early school leaving was between 7% in our high school and between 5% and 11% in our consortium schools. After the project  the average of early school leaving is %4.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project is for students to solve their problems themselves with the power of natural friendship through the peer counseling method. During the project, many responsibilities were given to the student, including managing social media accounts. With the project, we aimed to solve the student problems that we had identified in the partner schools by using the Peer Counseling method, within 15 months, with 12 volunteer students we chose through Sociometry and individual interviews. While the language development, self-confidence, helpfulness, socialization, problem solving and coping skills of our peer counselors who participated in the project increased, school students had the experience of solving problems that seriously affect their lives.

<< Implementation >>

*Mobilities
-(Peer Counseling) A 20 hours Peer Counseling Course was given by a psychologist to 48 volunteer students determined by sociometry. The training of peer counselors included basic helping skills and the application of these skills. Ethical rules, basic principles, the role of the peer counselor, the methods and techniques of peer counseling were discussed practically in a multicultural environment by allocating peer counseling to the first mobility as it forms the basis of the project.
-(Future Employement Anxiety) We aimed to help our students solve their future anxiety problems with the Peer counseling method, by enabling our students to get to know themselves and their environment and determine their professional goals in line with their interests and abilities.
-(Effective use of Technology) It was aimed that this problem is at a universal level and that it has come to light under the conditions of the pandemic, that there are similar problems in every country and that common solutions to these problems are produced.
-(Bullying) In peer counseling with drama method, peer bullying were evaluated and immediate supervision will be made. In this way, peer counselors had the chance to see their shortcomings immediately.

<< Results >>

After the project, we re-administered the 50-question problem screening inventory to 750 students.The decrease rates in students' problems are given below.
1- A lot of time with technology  -48% -41.7%  --- Reduction Rate 13.12%
2- Bullying -44% - 27.9%  --- Reduction Rate 36.59.%
3- Business concern  -43,2% - 38 % --- Reduction Rate 35.34%
4- Can't control anger-41% - 30.8%--- Reduction Rate 24.87%
5- Low self-perception -39% 25.4% --- Reduction Rate 34.87%
The average of early school leaving was between 7% in our high school and between 5% and 11% in our consortium schools. After the project  the average of early school leaving is %4.
The project's social media accounts and website are accessible to people.
A publication called 'Compassionate Connections: The Art of Peer Counseling for Empowered Support' was prepared by the project team, explaining the subject of Peer Counseling and the project in detail.

2022-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000084213.title: My school gives me wings
2022-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000084213.summary:
<< Background >>

The project "My school gives me wings!" was born from the desire to respond to the need of students who belong to vulnerable groups to be integrated and valued in schools, so that they enjoy real chances of development. The need for the project, ensuring the inclusion of students from vulnerable groups and combating the phenomenon of bullying in schools resulted from the analyses, statistics, reports drawn up at the level of the schools involved in the project, as well as from studies by specialists who indicated that bullying is a worrying phenomenon that manifests itself especially among primary and secondary school students. In all three schools involved in the project, it was observed that, in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, the phenomenon of aggression, violence, hate speech, exclusion among students increased, the victims being especially students who came from vulnerable groups. Also, the refugee crisis in Ukraine represented a new challenge for schools that were put in the position of receiving refugee students who needed to be helped, integrated, treated with tolerance, so that they are not exposed to attitudes of isolation, rejection , because they could be perceived as "different" by the majority of students

<< Objectives >>

The objectives that we set out to achieve by carrying out this project, common to all the institutions involved in the project, were: 
O. 1 Knowledge and awareness of forms of aggression by students through their involvement in project activities during 2022
2024 
O. 2 Informing children about their fundamental rights and about their role in preventing and reducing the phenomenon of 
bullying through involvement in project activities in the period 2022-2024 
O. 3 Promotion of positive methods of socio-emotional education of child victims or aggressors for teachers and parents through 
their involvement in the activities of the project in the period 2022-2024.
By promoting these objectives, we aimed to contribute to the creation in the schools involved in the project of an educational environment characterized by the existence of positive interpersonal relationships, of well-being, the creation of an educational context that stimulates each student, helps him to participate, each feeling the sense of belonging to the school community, to be able to grow and develop personally, physically, emotionally adequately. We aimed to reduce the phenomenon of violence and bullying in schools and, at the same time, to reduce school absenteeism

<< Implementation >>

Management activities – carried out by all organizations involved in the project. These consisted of: setting up the project implementation team, carrying out the activities of organization, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, dissemination and promotion, communication within the project, at institutional and inter-institutional level, recognition of the learning results for the students and teachers involved. 
There were 3 transnational learning activities and they were carried out as follows:
1. My school bullying free zone school, took place in per. March 27-31, 2023 at Apeytio Gymnasium Agros, Cyprus, with the participation of students and teachers from the 3 organizations involved in the project, 3 teachers, 6 students from Romania, 3 teachers, 5 students from Croatia, 4 teachers, 8 students from Cyprus.
2. Children's rights, your rights, took place between 16-20.10.2023, at Osnova Skola Darda, Croatia, with the participation of 2 teachers and 5 students from Cyprus, 2 teachers and 5 students from Romania, 7 teachers, 10 students from Croatia.
3. My school gives me wings! - April 15-19, 2024 at the Gymn. No. 2 Videle, Romania, with the participation of teachers and students form Cyprus and Croatia. 

<< Results >>

The concrete results of the project were both tangible and intangible, respectively: 
The tangible results were: 
- project management documents: decisions, Gantt diagram, cooperation agreements, communication plan, monitoring, evaluation, dissemination of learning results, etc.
- project promotion materials: roll-up, posters, Erasmus corners in schools, leaflets, folders, etc.
- participation certificates for students and teachers, Europass documents
- the project's Facebook page, the project's website, the project's magazine, supporting guide material with proposed activities to prevent and combat bullying in schools 
- articles published in the press, in school magazines, in ANews magazine. 
The intangible results were: 
- a correct and efficient implementation of the project
- increasing the level of information of students, teachers, parents about the phenomenon of bullying 
- developing the skills of effective and correct management of the bullying phenomenon 
- reduction of bullying situations in the schools where the project was carried out by at least 30% and school absenteeism
- developing the European dimension and the capacity of the organizations involved to work at a transnational level

2022-1-RS01-KA210-SCH-000083390.title: S-Team: Socijalna inkluzija uz pomoć životinja
2022-1-RS01-KA210-SCH-000083390.summary:
<< Background >>

Special primary schools plan educational work according to the needs of students, and the goal is to develop their maximum potential. Each student requires an individual approach, which must be supported by resources that are not common in regular schools and work methods that require additional teacher education. The application of innovative and scientifically based techniques and work methods, such as animal assisted therapy, is one of the ways in which educational work can be improved and the process of learning and teaching can be made interesting and stimulating for students. Animal assisted therapy has its benefits in the academic field, but also in the field of physical, psychological, social, emotional development and behavior modification, which facilitates the inclusion of students in the community and increases their visibility in society.
The project developed additional teacher competencies that made the learning process more interesting and useful for students. In students, the development of basic competencies (academic, socio-emotional, communication), necessary for everyday life and work, was encouraged,  and in parents, it had an effect on increasing satisfaction with the progress achived by their children.

<< Objectives >>

The goals of the project were:
1. encouraging the professional development of teachers and their competencies for working with students with special needs through application of modern and scientifically based methods and techniques
2. development of social, psychological, speech- and language and academic competences and encouragement of socio-emotional development of students with special needs through the application of animal assisted  therapy
3. encouraging the social inclusion of students with special needs with the help of animals
4. developing tolerance and acceptance of diversity and adoption of European values through joint activities of students from different European countries.

<< Implementation >>

Several activities were conducted that directly involved teachers and students (as well as parents). Beside coordination and management of the project, the dissemination and evaluation of the implemented activities, which were taken care of by the members of the school project teams, the following activities were realized:
1. Project corner (within each school; created project logo)
2. International meetings (2 on-site in Belgrade and Rogaška Slatina;2 on-line)
3. School project on the topic of animal care (free performance by students:drawings, posters)
4. Activity in the animal shelter and veterinary station
5. Visit to the ZOO and Equestrian Club
6. Exhibition on the topic of animal protection (protected and endangered animals; free performance by students: drawings, PPT)
7. Workshops with animals (2 workshops for teachers, more workshops for students, depending on the needs of the students and the possibilities of the school)
8. Making shelters for animals (from recycled material)
9. Creation and translation of the handbook for the application of animal assisted therapy for students with special needs (HRV, SRB, SLO, ENG)
10. Three LTT activities for students and teachers (Vukovar, Rogaška Slatina, Belgrade)

<< Results >>

1. At least 10 teachers and professional associates of each partner school acquired basic knowledge about the principles, forms and methods of applying animal assisted therapy in educational work with students
2. At least 20 students with developmental disabilities in each partner school involved in various structured activities in school and outside of school that include animals (classrooms, extracurricular activities, activities in the local community)
3. Achieved 3 joint transnational learning, training and teaching activities in which students from all three partner schools participated, which included the practical application of animal assisted therapy.
4. Prepared a manual (Handbook) with examples of good practice for the application of animal assisted therapy in work with students with special needs (developmental disabilities) in Serbian, Croatian, Slovenian and English.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000081476.title: Merim lokalno - vplivam globalno
2022-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000081476.summary:
<< Background >>

With the project I measure locally - I influence globally, we wanted to properly empower and train teachers to properly implement protocols and measurements within the GLOBE program, which is one of the world's leading programs for young people to observe and benefit the environment, where the correct implementation of measurements is extremely important, so that they these authorities and to help NASA scientists. The GLOBE program is relatively new in Slovenia and the teachers are meeting it for the first time, so they have no concrete experience. Teacher training must be conducted by GLOBE trainers who have been involved in the program for many years and have extensive experience. That's why we depended on foreign mentors here. In our case, we are extremely lucky because of the proximity of neighboring Croatia, which has been included in the GLOBE program for more than 25 years, and this was the only sensible solution, so that we can properly train Slovenian teachers with their help. We also included students in the project, who learned from their Croatian peers, and who transferred the new knowledge to their classmates and shared it more widely (with research assignments on an international scale and at the first GLOBE games in

<< Objectives >>

Through project activities, we wanted to provide appropriate training for Slovenian GLOBE teachers and their students. Our main goal was therefore teachers equipped with appropriate knowledge, who learned how to perform measurements correctly and who have already begun to expand their knowledge further. Among the goals of the project were appropriately qualified students who, under the guidance of teachers, carried out measurements, prepared research assignments, video guides, participated in GLOBE games and, through their achievements, inspired the rest of their peers for GLOBE. Among the goals of the project were also written, video and photo products. Each participating institution recorded one video guide for the chosen protocol (which will further serve as a help to newcomers to the project, as we realize that it is easier to tackle such matters if you can observe the progress of the measurement than if you just read the instructions). The video guides are freely available and will be presented at the beginning of each school year to the schools that will implement the GLOBE program (we will continue to update the guides). Each institution also prepared a research assignment according to all GLOBE regulations (hypotheses, res

<< Implementation >>

In order for the project to run smoothly, the project partners met at the beginning and carefully planned all the planned activities and created guidance and educational materials, which later served to help the participating teachers and students. During the project, we held practical-educational workshops (mobility of teachers and students) at both partner schools in Croatia (in Zadar and Omiš), where Croatian teachers and students presented selected protocols in theory and measurements through practical activities in the field. We held the first GLOBE event in Slovenia (GLOBE Games), where participating institutions presented their research tasks and participated in the GLOBE run, where they tested their knowledge in various tasks, teachers presented examples of good practices, and at the final event we analyzed the entire of the project and set guidelines for the continuation of the activities. Throughout the entire duration of the project, the students, under the guidance of teachers, carried out measurements, prepared video guides and wrote a research paper. Since the measurements are tied to the use of certain measuring devices, we provided each institution with a package of measuring instruments and a weather house so that

<< Results >>

The greatest result is certainly the knowledge acquired by the teachers and students who directly participated in the project and were able to concretely connect them with environmental topics and the goals of sustainable development. They transferred this knowledge to their work and spread it to others who were not directly involved in the project. With this, they "made sure" the visibility of the GLOBE program itself, and it is a great achievement that interest in it began to grow (by the end of the 2023/24 school year, 20 new schools joined). Among the concrete products, I can count the created video guides and students' research assignments, as well as examples of teachers' good practices. Both (teachers and students) gained new contacts/acquaintances during the mobilities, deepened their knowledge also in the cultural and linguistic fields (the children understand and speak Croatian very poorly, so part of the activity was also held in English, since the entire website and the GLOBE database works in English). GLOBE coaches from both Croatian schools have enriched their portfolio and brought their knowledge to the international level. An important result is the acquisition of the title of the first GLOBE trainer in Slovenia,
