2022-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000083352.title: Green little heroes
2022-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000083352.summary:
<< Background >>

Our motivation for this project was formed from a needs analysis of the partner organisations and their interest in activities related to environmental protection and the strengthening of green skills in pre-school children and children in the first six years of primary school. While all partner organisations have been involved in a number of national projects on ecology for a number of years, each in its own way trying to create a change of habits among employees and children, there has been no significant progress due to a lack of innovative and creative approaches. So we decided to join forces and pool our knowledge to tackle the issue in a new way. In a fresh, creative and, above all, modern way. The needs we addressed were: an increased knowledge and awareness of environmental issues among teachers, children and families, collaborative efforts among parts to share knowledge, experiences, and strategies, a combination of theory and practice that ensures comprehensive learning for teachers and children, activities designed to engage children actively and make them feel important in the effort toward a cleaner environment and a way for preschool teachers and teachers to integrate environmental topics more frequently. 

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of our project were:
*Making children aware of the importance of green skills and the need for environmental protection.
* Encourage families, employees, and community members to adopt environmentally friendly habits through practical ideas and instructions.
* Present and raise awareness of the concept of "reduce, reuse."
* Bring together diverse generations, cultures, and social backgrounds to collectively address environmental challenges.
* Promote creativity and innovative approaches
* Promoting Green Tourism
* Developing Key Competences of Professionals
* Empower teachers with skills, good practices, and innovative teaching methods.
* Enhance their digital literacy and integrate ICT tools into teaching.
* Support the professional and personal development of teachers
* Encourage teachers to model healthy, sustainable lifestyles 
* Organize inclusive activities such as "green days," virtual events, and a final conference to share findings and results with the public.
* Strengthen ties between children, teachers, parents, and local communities to act collectively as guardians of the environment.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, we implemented numerous activities that ensured the achievement of set goals as well as the preparation of project results.
In addition to regular meetings of project teams and coordinators within individual partner organizations, we organized three online meetings. These meetings played a key role in: evaluating implemented activities, preparing evaluation questionnaires to measure progress in the knowledge and application of green skills, financial management, planning of  LTT activities.

We conducted five LTT meetings, which focused on the following themes:
Green ICT, 
Green Play, 
Green Tourism, 
Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, 
Sustainability in Education and Everyday Life.
Each meeting was structured to include both a theoretical component  and a practical component . This approach ensured that participants gained new knowledge, examples of good practices, and ideas for further use in their work.
As part of the project, we also organized two "Green Day" events, which were aimed at promoting the project and its results and encouraging discussions and active participation.

The most important multiplier event was the final conference, where all key project results were presented.

<< Results >>

As part of the Green Little Heroes project, the following results were developed:
* Project Logo - A visual identity representing the project's mission and objectives.
* Project Mascot - Geofilos, a character that promoted the project's visibility and motivated participation among children and other stakeholders.
* Project Brochure in 6 Languages - informational material tailored to each partner language, designed to promote and present the project to a broader audience.
* Project Diary - a document capturing all key project activities, including photos and summaries of achieved goals.
* Book of Traditional Games - a collection of traditional games from partner countries, fostering intercultural understanding and the preservation of cultural heritage.
* Tourist Guides for Partner Countries - guides showcasing sustainable and eco-friendly tourist spots and activities in partner countries.
* Collection of Didactic Materials - resources designed to support teachers in integrating topics of sustainability, green skills, and environmental awareness into their teaching.
* Final Conference Proceedings - a publication summarizing the presentations, outcomes of the conference, and key achievements of the project.

2022-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000083793.title: Krive so čebele
2022-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000083793.summary:
<< Background >>

With this project, we aimed to increase environmental awareness and enhance sustainability skills among pupils and staff. Our main goal was to encourage pupils to actively preserve nature and understand the critical role of bees in the ecosystem. Key objectives included raising awareness about bees' importance to food security, fostering a responsible attitude toward nature, and, in collaboration with our partner school, OŠ Slatine, promoting intercultural dialogue. Pupils engaged with peers from Croatia, learning about their culture, language, and traditions, thus developing multicultural competencies and an understanding of European values. We sought to enhance pupils' digital and communication skills, providing hands-on experience with digital tools through project activities while strengthening intercultural competencies. The project also contributed to the development of practical skills and craftsmanship, increased social inclusion, and encouraged innovative approaches to learning. Through project implementation, we aim for lasting changes that positively impact both partner schools and the local communities, enabling pupils, teachers, parents, and others to transfer acquired knowledge and skills to future generations.

<< Objectives >>

With this project, we aimed to boost environmental awareness and enhance sustainability skills among participants from both our school and our partner school. We sought to encourage pupils to actively preserve nature, understand bees' importance to the ecosystem and food security, and develop a responsible attitude toward the environment. The project raised awareness of climate change issues. Collaboration with our Croatian partner school fostered a sense of European identity and solidarity, contributing to pupils' personal and social growth. Through shared activities, pupils explored peers' culture, language, and traditions, realizing multicultural principles and European values. By using digital tools, they enhanced their digital and communication skills, documenting activities in Slovenian, Croatian, and English. Involving parents and the local community strengthened social skills and intergenerational connections. Practical learning was emphasized as pupils helped create a bee sensory path, building craftsmanship, self-esteem, and motor skills. Through active participation of all envolved in our project, we strived to achieve lasting, long-term changes to benefit future generations.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, we carried out activities focused on strengthening learning competencies, intercultural collaboration, and enhancing green skills. A preparatory meeting was organized to outline guidelines and planned activities. We conducted three educational mobilities for student and teacher exchanges with partner schools. Participants engaged in olive harvesting, organic soap making from natural local ingridients, and creating a honey recipe booklet, gaining valuable practical skills and understanding sustainable practices. One key activity was setting up a bee sensory trail, designed with natural materials and bee motifs. We held two concerts in Ljubljana and Split, enabling students to exchange cultural experiences and connect with peers. Regular evaluations were conducted to assess progress and adapt activities to achieve desired outcomes. All activities were documented on both schools’ websites and will also be available on ESEP and eTwinning platforms, ensuring wider access to project achievements and partnerships. The project actively involved parents and the local community, raising awareness of sustainability and strengthening the role of bees in our ecosystem.

<< Results >>

The bee sensory path was designed by pupils and teachers from both partner schools. Composed of natural materials and interactive points, it promotes learning through a holistic approach. The trail has become a symbol of sustainable values and a long-term educational tool for all generations. We plan to integrate it into the Bee Path of the Municipality of Ljubljana, making it accessible to the wider public. Students compiled a honey recipe booklet and recorded a bilingual video about pollinators, both available on the schools' websites. Together with students from the partner school, they harvested olives, participated in oil pressing, and produced natural soaps from local ingredients. They created a sensory book titled »Krive so čebele« (Blame it on the Bees) printed in Braille and featuring a QR code for audio access. The opening of the bee sensory trail and both concerts in Ljubljana and Split were carefully planned, accompanied by our project mascot, Mila the Bee, using a fresh approach to raise environmental awareness. By sharing events on websites and social media, we increased visibility for both schools, ensuring sustainable outcomes that have become valuable resources for all participants' learning processes.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000083905.title: (PRE)HRANA za TRAJNOSTNI RAZVOJ
2022-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000083905.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was designed to address the growing need for education focused on sustainable development, science, and early childhood development. We recognized the importance of fostering respect for the environment and sustainable habits from an early age. The project aimed to provide children, educators, and parents with authentic learning experiences outside traditional classrooms. Therefore, specific learning environments such is educational farm and educational gardens were developed. Emphasis was placed on learning through exploration, particularly in natural settings such as educational farms and gardens, with the goal of influencing consumer habits and promoting ecological responsibility.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives were:
1. To transform a farm into an educational farm and a yard into an educational garden, creating multifunctional learning spaces with a focus on inquiry-based and problem-solving learning.
2. To develop high-quality teaching materials that support inquiry-based learning in both newly developed environments.
3. To promote knowledge about sustainability, scientific skills, and environmental awareness among children, parents, and professionals.
4. To strengthen cross-border cooperation and the exchange of best practices between Slovenian and Croatian kindergartens.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were carried out as part of the project:
• Establishing a "Food Lab" as an educational and research laboratory for food processing.
• Constructing a greenhouse and raised garden beds to explore different farming methods.
• Organizing workshops for parents and professionals, including cooking workshops focused on the sustainable use of food.
• Publishing the cookbook "What to Do with Food Waste" to promote sustainable food practices.
• Conducting professional training sessions for educators on creating high-quality teaching materials and incorporating innovative teching methods.
• Hosting exchanges, job shadowings and knowledge-sharing sessions to enhance educational practices among partners.

<< Results >>

* An educational farm is established, including the "Food Lab," which is fully equipped for hands-on, research-based learning and food experimentation.
* Raised garden beds and a greenhouse are build, providing children with opportunities to learn about planting, cultivation, and the principals of seasonal farming.
* High-quality teaching materials and manuals are developed to support inquiry-based learning.
* The cookbook "What to Do with Food Waste." Is published and distributed.
* The professional competencies of educators are enhanced through training sessions and joint workshops.
* Environmental awareness is improved, and sustainable habits are fostered among children and parents.
* Cross-border collaboration is strengthened, enabling the sharing of innovative educational practices among project partners.

2022-2-BG01-KA210-SCH-000095704.title: Промяна с половин градус
2022-2-BG01-KA210-SCH-000095704.summary:
<< Background >>

The aim of the project is to prepare teachers to deal with the complexity of the subject by making it factual and in view of local, regional and international situations, using different approaches.
The second goal is to prepare students (as the next generation) to become real agents of change and to learn about the collective responsibility to protect the environment and prevent further harm.
The ultimate goal of the project is to prepare teachers by creating a teacher's guide and teaching materials with simple, practical activities that they can use in their daily classes without overloading the teaching content.

The target group of this project are:
Target group 1: Teachers.
Needs: Lack of training and teaching materials are the main obstacles for teachers to include the topic in lessons.
Target group 2: Pupils in ISCED level 3 schools (14-16 years)
Needs: Students need to understand what it means on a practical level to reduce the global temperature below 2 degrees Celsius. The changes that are required locally and nationally.

<< Objectives >>

Objectives:
*Increased ability of teachers to teach global warming topics and concepts
*Increased cross-curricular competences of teachers in junior high and high school: ability to relate global warming topics between different subjects and better understand the complexity of the topic, from different perspectives.
* Increased communication between teachers, across disciplines, adapting schedules and curricula that limit teaching opportunities
*students will be better informed about the science behind global warming, but also about how institutions and people deal with problems of this magnitude
*improved capacity to prepare individualized, informal training

<< Implementation >>

Activity 1: Project management and dissemination - This activity consists of two parts - project management and dissemination. The activity covered the management of the project and the dissemination of the results, throughout the 12 months.

Activity 2: Teacher's guide:
The guide was divided into two parts:
1.Introducing Global Warming to School Teachers – scientific background;
2. Implementing Global Warming Education in the Classroom

Activity 3: Toolbox for teachers - Free-to-use collection of tools, resources and classroom activities focused on global warming and climate change

<< Results >>

1. A teacher's guide with accessible materials, methodological content related to the topic of global warming. The guide include information, ways and techniques of communication specifically designed to effectively approach students with scientific, civic and cultural aspects.
The teacher's guide is translated to partners languages

2. Free-to-use collection of tools, resources and classroom activities focused on global warming and climate change:
30 classroom activities
30 infographics
30 short videos
All activities are translated into partner languages

2022-2-BG01-KA210-SCH-000097380.title: Steam in times
2022-2-BG01-KA210-SCH-000097380.summary:
<< Background >>

Math related disorders can start to be noticeable from preschool age according to the articles. For this reason, it is important to engage and motivate students to learn mathematics in a less anxiolytic matter, meaning trying to avoid the drill-in method because students with SLD often have difficulties with memorizing numbers by hearing them,
learning to count, sorting, corresponding numbers to objects and so on.
By employing methodologies, such as "game-based pedagogies" and "experiential learning", as well as by assimilating the
concept of "manipulation through history", the project Steam builders in times aspires to bring a hands-on math approach in
primary education classrooms. Such a conclusion has been based on the rationale (and the broad agreement) that math
manipulation activities can change the perception of mathematics, especially by developing and strengthening its language,
different from the school language and scientific popularization. In this sense, math manipulations through history must
propose materials, spaces and actions that are not easily repeatable in other situation

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of this project was to engage students in STEAM while creating an enjoyable learning environment. Engaging students in STEAM was critical because of its importance. Students developed math anxiety early on, often due to the way this subject was taught in a drill-like manner, hence relying upon memorization instead of understanding and experimenting. For this reason, the project focused on engaging students in primary education in a cross-curricular approach to STEAM with the help of history to better understand the applications of science and mathematics throughout the times and how they eventually evolved to what it was at that time. This approach aimed to explore the historical heritage behind the scientific and mathematical development we had at that time while motivating students to pursue these fields in an enjoyable and non-formal way. Math and history had intersected for thousands of years after all. This project provided the support educators needed to implement manipulations in their lesson plans and improve the hands-on approach to STEAM subjects, especially to help prevent math anxiety from primary education, preparing students for a better experience with these subjects later in their education.

<< Implementation >>

All activities planned in the application form have been implemented with the participation of the three partners. The Manipulating math throug history manual; 36 Manipulation blueprints and 36 Pedagogical materials have been created. The guide will help teachers to adopt a cross-curricular approach and link the STEAM curriculum to European heritage and history principles. It is practical and user-friendly, with a clear structure and concrete explanations in situations to facilitate daily use by the target groups. 
The blueprints consist of exercises and manipulatives to provide all the necessary information for the teacher, but also plans, graphic representations of manipulatives for reproduction, scale models or building blocks of activities.
The pedagogical material corresponds to each plan with explanations for introducing the materials in the lesson (introduction, application, checking, testing). This product describes in detail the lesson plan and the activities implemented in it. These pedagogical materials are examples of how to structure a lesson by integrating the drawings and activities.
Tips "Do's and don'ts" were also created to help teachers.
All the products have been translated into 4 languages.

<< Results >>

At the outset of the project, our primary goal was to engage students in STEAM education in an interesting manner, actively involving them in the process. Many students fear mathematics, which is traditionally taught through memorization and repetition. Through the project's multidisciplinary approach and hands-on learning, students were given the opportunity to explore the historical context of scientific and mathematical developments and how they have shaped the modern world. During the testing phase, conducted after the project results—pedagogical guidance, blueprints, and teaching materials—were ready, it was demonstrated that we had succeeded in stimulating the natural curiosity of the children. They approached the tasks with enthusiasm in a relaxed and informal environment, understanding the enduring connection between mathematics and history. Teachers received useful resources and support for incorporating practical activities into their lessons and teaching strategies. In this way, the goal of reducing mathematics anxiety in young students and equipping them with the skills and confidence necessary for their future development was achieved.
Grant amount allocated to the activities was sufficient.

2022-2-BG01-KA210-SCH-000098034.title: Delay now for a successful future
2022-2-BG01-KA210-SCH-000098034.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to enhance the long-term success and well-being of children by developing their delayed gratification skills. Recognizing the pivotal role teachers play, we aim to equip them with effective tools and methodologies to foster these skills in the classroom.
Our survey revealed specific needs among primary and kindergarten teachers, including:75% needing additional motivation techniques for students; 89% requiring new methods to develop students' self-discipline and self-control; 91% wanting to create a learning environment that promotes motivation; 84% interested in participating in related activities.
Project Goals are: 
- Implement innovative methods to sustain students' interest and effort.
- Provide approaches that help students develop self-regulation and perseverance.
- Offer strategies for fostering an environment that promotes long-term educational outcomes.
- Deliver comprehensive training to enhance teachers' instructional strategies and classroom management.
Our project addresses the critical need for developing delayed gratification skills in children by empowering educators with the necessary resources and training, ultimately benefiting both teachers and students.

<< Objectives >>

Our project aimed to achieve several key objectives that benefited both educators and students, fostering a conducive environment for long-term success and well-being. We focused on enhancing student development by equipping them with delayed gratification skills, teaching self-discipline, and self-control, and building mental toughness and emotional resilience using techniques like grit and positive psychology.
For educators, we provided innovative teaching strategies and equipped them with step-by-step methods for character development and trust-building. Our goal was to support their professional growth and effectiveness in creating classrooms that promoted long-term educational outcomes and personal development.
We addressed broader educational and social issues by implementing strategies to help students manage their use of technology and reduce the risk of addiction. The project aligned with educational priorities, supporting the development of social competencies necessary for promoting active citizenship and lifelong learning. It enabled students to acquire critical life skills essential for personal and academic success, ensuring they were well-prepared for future challenges.

<< Implementation >>

Throughout the project, we implemented a range of activities aimed at achieving our goals effectively. Through research and analysis, we explored and developed the concept of delayed gratification and its implications for education. Surveys were designed and distributed to primary school teachers across three countries. The aim was to gather insights into their challenges and needs regarding the development of delayed gratification skills among students. We developed comprehensive training materials: a Competency Matrix, a booklet, and a teacher training program. We ensured that all training materials were designed with accessibility in mind. We conducted pilot testing of the training materials that allowed us to gather feedback, and identify areas for improvement. We organized and facilitated training workshops (LTT) for teachers, focused on the practical implementation of delayed gratification strategies in classroom settings. Throughout the project, we monitored the progress of activities, collected feedback from participants, and evaluated the impact of the training program. Through these activities, our goal was to empower educators with the necessary skills and resources to promote delayed gratification among students. 

<< Results >>

The implementation of the project was aimed at improving delayed gratification skills among students aged 7-11 years. We have developed a comprehensive booklet containing best practices from European education systems and research, equipping teachers with practical strategies, activities, and case studies. In addition, a companion book tailored for teachers includes exercises designed to engage students and encourage patience, persistence, and self-control.
We conducted a structured training course for educators, equipping them with knowledge and teaching methodologies to effectively integrate delayed gratification skills. Teachers gained experience using pre- and post-assessment tools to assess student progress.
As a result, teachers report improvements in students' persistence, work ethic, and engagement with tasks requiring sustained effort. Students developed essential soft skills such as patience, self-discipline, and resilience, contributing to improved classroom behavior and academic achievement. Overall, the project aimed to create a foundation for long-term behavioral change and academic success among students, fostering a positive learning environment conducive to growth and development.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-2-BG01-KA210-SCH-000101910.title: Дигитално приобщаване и разнообразие
2022-2-BG01-KA210-SCH-000101910.summary:
<< Background >>

ПГМЕ реализира първия си проект по програма „Еразъм+“ през 2015 г., именно по КА2, с фокус върху бизнес процесите и мениджмънта в образованието. Ефектът от този проект върху последващата работа в училището ни показа на практика ползите от програмата и ни направи много по-активни участници в нея. В момента имаме две акредитации по КА1 – в училищното и професионалното образование, както и няколко проекта по КА2: един успешен проект в професионалното образование като бенефициенти, един като партньор и още един като партньор в училищното образование.

На базата на натрупания опит и след задълбочен анализ на нуждите на ПГМЕ подготвихме настоящия проект. Основните нужди и цели на ПГМЕ са свързани с подобряване на организацията на преподаване и обучението в училище чрез повишаване на професионалната компетентност и квалификация на педагогическите кадри, както и с повишаване качеството на практическата подготовка, адаптивността и възможностите за заетост на учениците. Още през 2015 г. училището разработи План за европейско развитие и интернационализация, а през 2020 г. прие Стратегия за интернационализация и „Еразъм“ план на ПГМЕ. Стратегическите партньорства за нас са ключов фактор, който ще ни помогне да реализираме тези цели.

<< Objectives >>

Основната цел на проекта е да повиши капацитета на учителите за ефективно преподаване и учене по основните предмети от общообразователната подготовка и прилагането им в усвояването на знания и умения по предметите от професионалната подготовка. В тази връзка се цели и оптимизиране на връзката между общото образование и неговото практическо приложение в професионалното образование, както и успешната трудова реализация на учениците. Повишаването на осведомеността относно различните възможности и механизми за подкрепа на учениците с по-малко възможности, чрез адаптиране на подхода към техните специфични нужди, е важна цел, продиктувана от променените социални и демографски условия в ЕС. След пандемията от COVID-19 стана неизбежно прилагането на електронното обучение, което изисква използването на нови, иновативни подходи и методи на преподаване и учене. Друга важна цел е повишаване на капацитета на училищата, включително участващите партньорски организации, както и привличането на нови партньори. Социалното приобщаване на ученици с по-малко възможности, мигранти, бежанци или от семейства със социално-икономически затруднения е фактор, който пряко влияе върху пазара на труда и недостига на квалифициран персонал във всяка икономическа 

<< Implementation >>

Дейностите, заложени в проекта са в две направления:
=Управление на проекта:
Цялостното управление на проекта, включително изготвянето на междинния отчет е направен от ПГМЕ Пирдоп. С всеки партньор бяха подписани партньорски споразумения през месец май 2023 г. Всеки партньор изпълни възложените му с партньорското споразумение дейности и управлява определения му бюджет, като представя отчет пред ПГМЕ след всяка мобилност. На първата партньорска среща, която се проведе онлайн през месец март,  бяха обсъдени и приети всички организационни въпроси, времеви график,  разпределение на бюджета по дейности и партньори. Бе сформиран и екип за управление с ръководител координатора от страна на  ПГМЕ и членове - по един представител на всеки партньор.  Бяха определени и лица за контакт - по един представител на всеки партньор.  Организирахме шест официални онлайн партньорски срещи – преди подписване на партньорските споразумения, преди всяка мобилност и заключителна след приключване на събитията за разпространение на резултатите.
=Организиране на семинари/ обучения:
Заложени и изпълнени са четири обучения/семинари, по едно за всеки от партньорите. Темата на обучението за всеки партньор е свързана с най-силната страна на съответното училище.

<< Results >>

Проектът приключи успешно и безспорно можем да кажем, че от всички реализирани проекти досега, този е най-успешният и най-релевантният за нас. Същото мнение споделят и нашите партньори, като всички изразихме желание да продължим сътрудничеството си в бъдещи проекти и програми. Всеки партньор пое отговорност за изпълнението на дейностите и постигането на заложените цели.
Всички планирани обучения бяха проведени в съответствие с приетия график. Всяко училище демонстрира своите силни страни по време на организираните обучения, като в същото време в диалог обсъждахме и възникналите проблеми, както и възможните решения. Оказа се, че въпреки различията в профилите на училищата, имаме много общи теми и близки проблеми за решаване. Основната дейност и цел на проекта – обмен на добри практики и създаване на трайни партньорства – бяха постигнати изцяло. В обученията участваха представители от всички училища, като някои участваха във всички обучения, а други – в едно или две, в зависимост от темата. По този начин осигурихме надграждане на резултатите, по-широко разпространение и по-добро внедряване на добрите практики във всяка организация. Разбира се, остана време и за културна програма.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-2-DE03-KA210-SCH-000097399.title: Using mobile phones as a tool to improve STEM skills
2022-2-DE03-KA210-SCH-000097399.summary:
<< Background >>

Our vocational college - as well as our partners - is increasingly working on digitalising the school in all possible areas and would also like to break innovative ground here.  In addition to the school organisation, this naturally also affects the individual subjects. As colleagues who teach STEM subjects have so far participated little in European projects due to concerns and fears about communicating in English, we saw this as a very good opportunity to focus on actively involving them in European work. Our pupils have considerable learning deficits in the STEM subjects and have lost some of their enjoyment for this reason. Our female pupils in particular are often still stuck in stereotypes that STEM subjects are more for boys. We want to counteract these attitudes with our project. In addition, we wanted to utilise the European dimension of the project and promote the linguistic, social and intercultural skills of both teachers and pupils and emphasise our commonalities as Europeans. We want to improve school education as a whole.

<< Objectives >>

The  main objective of the project was to increase motivation in and during lessons in the STEM subjects by incorporating the mobile phone, which is very much used by pupils, and utilising its potential.  We tried to take innovative paths and show the pupils how to use their mobile phones efficiently and in a fun way (activity) by using suitable apps, learning platforms, etc., but also through related excursions and workshops. However, we also addressed the critical use of the device (e.g. data security, rules of behaviour, etc.). Overall, we wanted the pupils to improve their IT skills.  It was also very important to us to raise awareness of the fact that girls and women in particular are also successful in STEM subjects. This target group was particularly addressed in the project.  The topic of ‘environmental protection and climate change’ was also taken into account. We paid attention to environmentally friendly measures when implementing the project (public transport, paper reduction, etc.). Other objectives were also achieved, including the promotion of social, intercultural and (foreign) language skills.

<< Implementation >>

We started with a joint online English course and IT training to lay the foundations for our joint work. There was a lively exchange between the respective project coordinators via email, WhatsApp and a Moodle platform, which we used to upload materials. Unfortunately, we had some (technical) problems with the eTwinning platform at the beginning, so we switched to Moodle. As indicated, we first organised a kick-off meeting for the teachers in Italy, followed by project meetings with teachers and pupils in Croatia, Spain and Germany. At the last meeting in Mönchengladbach, a science fair was also organised to disseminate the results. An agenda was drawn up in advance for all meetings and presentations and activities were prepared by the students (e.g. video, PowerPoint presentations). Some of the students stayed with host families during the meetings.  In addition, an eTwinning project was carried out in which the pupils developed and evaluated apps and quizzes on the STEM subjects. The project website https://www.besmart-project.eu/home was also developed, on which the progress and results of our project are documented.

<< Results >>

Many of our results are documented on our project website https://www.besmart-project.eu/home and on the eTwinning platform. We have learnt many innovative and creative methods in various workshops on how to use the mobile phone efficiently, e.g. by using the phyphox app in physics, how to construct a mobile phone-controlled bedside lamp or use robots, but also how to record and edit experiments, create learning videos or use learning apps. This will benefit both pupils and teachers in their future teaching development. Lesson plans have been developed and published on the website.  We have tried to share our experiences and suggestions in various places, besides the website through publications on our school websites, by using social media channels, newspapers, during school events, at the Science Fair, etc.  In addition to the concrete results for the work in the STEM subjects, the project was also enriching for the general exchange between us partners, for the expansion of our IT and language skills, we have learnt a lot about other cultures and can use this in the future.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2022-2-DE03-KA210-SCH-000102194.title: Inclusive Equal Tales
2022-2-DE03-KA210-SCH-000102194.summary:
<< Background >>

The gender equality is one of the problems in the societies. As one of the reflections of this,inequalities in fairy tales had critical impact during children's formative years.Because of that reason we believed that fairy tales were needed to be reproduced according to the needs of the society.We identified our needs as equality and inclusiveness.We have combined these two needs with technological developments.So while we had been working on the fairy tales , we have rewritten them in today's requirements.Because fairy tales taught children how to deal with basic human conflicts, desires, and relationships in a healthy way; acquiring these skills can ultimately impact a child's health, quality of life, or even influence its values and beliefs in the future.
The ultimate goal of our project was to create awareness about both gender equality and social integration by developing digital and creativity key skills with fair tales,bringing together mentally disadvantaged individuals and normally developing individuals.In this project,students diagnosed with mental disability has been experienced gender confusion in the conceptual skills included in the adaptive skills.


<< Objectives >>

In order to contribute to the correct and positive teaching of the concept of equality between men and women to children, we had  outputs that would lead us to our goals in our projects.
* Our animation film; aimed to introduce all our students who were at different mental levels to the correct gender patterns and raised awareness about this issue with fair tales, which was one of the works to be done in our project.
* Writing fairy tales and make 3D graphic drawing and learning animation programs ; aimed to improve technological skills.While we had been integrating the all levels of students normally developed students had improved their skills for mentally low-developed students.

<< Implementation >>

With the principle of inclusivity and paying attention to the concepts of gender equality,we had presented a mini-theatre show where all participants had taken part in finding a local fairy tale from each participating country,wrote the determined tale with graphic animations suitable for the digital age,made graphic animated short films.We realized  LTTs,and 1 online TPM  with totally 110 participants.

While working on tales all partners had a change to search their own traditional local tales.They presented them to other partners.And they showed the new rewritten form of the traditional .So all partners had a chance to investigate the differences of the characters and they understood that equality changes to country to country and to age to age.

<< Results >>

The biggest expected result in our project was to  raise individuals who has been  with their digital sufficiency, were conscious of gender equality, rejected the stereotypical roles assigned to them, and gained awareness of differencies and their own thoughts and identity.During the mobility we organized activities to raise awareness;
*All the countries rewrote the traditional tales which had inequal characters with new equal characters.
*All the participants write a theatre script and performed the  theatre with disadvantaged students.
*Participants were introduced the drawing graphic design programs to write new rewritten tales. 
*Participants draw characters and made digital tale ebook
*Participants made animation film together

2022-2-DE03-KA210-SCH-000102272.title: Young Creators
2022-2-DE03-KA210-SCH-000102272.summary:
<< Background >>

The project idea originated at Primary School Trnsko where students developed a great interest in 3D-printed gaming miniatures and wanted to find out in art class how they were made. Teachers at the school, realizing that they didn’t have the skills to teach the skills that the students were interested in, reached out to art professionals of Ingenious Knowledge and ArtQuest who were willing to work with them.
We decided to apply for this project because 3D modeling and using 3D printers to print out the results are skills that are in high demand and they are becoming increasingly valuable. Unfortunately there are very few teachers who have the right skills, which is the main reason why students can’t acquire these skills in school. Not only have we identified the need to learn 3D sculpting and 3D printing in schools, we have also seen an increasing interest and demand on the side of the students. We believe that modern school education needs to provide practical skills that are useful in the rapidly changing world in order for the students to be prepared for the work life of tomorrow.
During the project we have seen exceptionally high motivation when we showed students our gaming miniatures, confirming this approach.

<< Objectives >>

Our objectives were to help teachers get started with 3D modeling and 3D printing with an easy guide for beginners. We also wanted to implement 3D printing in various forms in school and make enough learning materials available to encourage teachers and students to develop their skills. This should open a path to self-guided learning, allowing students to gain an interest in the makerspace movement.
All partners also had the objective to grow their own experiences in bringing innovation to education and sharing highly relevant digital skills that they are passionate about.

<< Implementation >>

Meeting in Croatia: Here we formed the project team and connected the staff members so that they would work together well. We also outlined the work and launched the work on the teacher guide and the digital learning materials.

Work Phase: Each partner worked on the guide for teachers and on the materials. This meant creating materials, trying it out with students and then doing redesign based on teh feedback.
 
Meeting in Sweden: We implemented the results in the partner schools and ran a training with teachers. We also planed the implementation phase.

Implementation phase: We implemented 3D design and 3D printing activities in the partner schools and reached out to other schools as well. We disseminated the guide and the training materials.

<< Results >>

Results include a guide for teachers and digital materials (sculpted miniatures as examples, half-done models to train specific skills) for students to work on as well as instructional videos. These results were shared widely with a network of schools. Active teachers at Trnsko school and at Rålambshovsskolan received training and implemented 3D sculpting courses. Students acquired new digital art skills and learned how to construct something in 3D and print it. The results are currently used by more than 10 other schools outside the partner network.

2022-2-DK01-KA210-SCH-000092536.title: Tailoring STEM Skills
2022-2-DK01-KA210-SCH-000092536.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the need for innovative and engaging STEM education in our schools. We identified a gap in students’ interest and proficiency in STEM subjects and recognized the need to equip them with the skills required for future careers in a rapidly changing world. Our schools needed new methods to integrate STEM into the curriculum, focusing on creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving. This project aimed to inspire students to explore STEM through practical, hands-on experiences and foster collaboration between educational institutions and businesses. By adopting new teaching approaches and improving digital skills, we sought to enhance student motivation, develop key competencies, and make STEM more accessible and appealing. The project also aimed to strengthen partnerships across schools in Europe, promoting a culture of innovation and preparing students for future challenges by cultivating skills that are essential in the global labor market.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were to promote interest and excellence in STEM education, develop key competencies in school education, and introduce innovative teaching and learning approaches. We aimed to enhance collaboration between educational institutions and businesses, fostering real-world connections for students. Additionally, we focused on promoting soft skills such as critical thinking, communication, creativity, and collaboration among students. The project also aimed to contribute to the digital transformation of school education, making schools pioneers in adopting new, effective methods for teaching STEM. Ultimately, we wanted to cultivate future-ready learners, equipped with the skills needed for the labor market and empowered to drive social change.

<< Implementation >>

In our project, we implemented a variety of activities to achieve our objectives. We began with the preparation phase, including the creation of a project board, design of a project logo, and development of the project website. We also organized e-Twinning studies, a project logo competition, and designed information cards for dissemination.
Meetings were held to introduce the project to students, teachers, parents, and local administrators, providing an overview of the project and its partners. We promoted the project through these meetings and created awareness of the importance of STEM education.
Throughout the project, we organized exchanges and transnational meetings to facilitate collaboration and knowledge sharing between partner schools. These activities were complemented by regular evaluation meetings to assess progress and impact. The results were shared through a dedicated website and in public exhibitions for the local community and wider audiences.

<< Results >>

We successfully integrated STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) as an innovative education model in participating schools, promoting best practices in teaching and learning.
Project FB-page: A fully functional FB page was created, serving as a platform for sharing resources, outcomes, and updates.
Student Competencies: Students developed crucial soft skills such as critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration, with a focus on real-life problem-solving in STEM fields.
Multinational Network: A strong network was built among schools across different countries, allowing for continued cooperation and shared STEM resources beyond the project’s duration.
Exhibitions and Dissemination: Local exhibitions showcased the project’s results to a wider audience, including parents, local authorities, and the general public, raising awareness about the value of STEM education.
Educational Materials: We developed teaching resources, including guides and e-books, which will continue to be used after the project's completion.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2022-2-EL01-KA210-SCH-000095376.title: Everything Stars With Health
2022-2-EL01-KA210-SCH-000095376.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to respond to an urgent need observed in all four participating schools: an increasing number of students facing issues related to obesity, unhealthy diets, and lack of awareness about hygiene and well-being. The COVID-19 pandemic further underscored the importance of regular and healthy nutrition, hygiene, and immunity in combating illnesses. Teachers and parents noticed not only physical health concerns but also rising cases of hyperactivity and inattention in class. Our schools aimed to instill long-term healthy habits, enhance awareness around nutrition and cleanliness, and develop inclusive practices to support students from all backgrounds. The project also aimed to promote transnational collaboration and equip teachers with skills in digital tools, green competencies, and multicultural communication.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the Everything Stars With Health project, our primary aim was to promote healthier lifestyles among students and build lasting change through education, innovation, and inclusion.
First, we aimed to reduce obesity among students aged 6 to 20 using a mix of formal, informal, and non-formal educational methods. Through engaging activities and awareness campaigns, we wanted to encourage healthier eating habits, regular physical activity, and better self-care.
Second, we sought to create and apply innovative learning tools, including an OER (Open Educational Resource) e-booklet and a practical e-handbook on healthy living and balanced nutrition. These resources were designed to be accessible, reusable, and adaptable across different learning environments and schools.
Third, we worked to enhance key competencies—such as digital skills, English language proficiency, and environmental awareness among pupils across partner schools. We used collaborative platforms, creative digital tools, and hands-on tasks to support this goal.
Finally, we aimed to promote inclusion and social equity, particularly for students with fewer opportunities. 

<< Implementation >>

The project included five key activities (C1 to C5), each held in a different partner country:
•	C1 (Greece): Awareness training on healthy life, healthy  nutrition, information
•	C2 (Turkey): Healthy eating: Healthy meals, healthy eating activities
•	C3 (Croatia): Healthy life, preparing balanced nutrition brochures
•	C4 (North Macedonia): Use of masks, awareness, mask design studies
•	C5 (Greece): Documentation of these activities, surveys, evaluation, dissemination


<< Results >>

Throughout our project, we achieved a wide array of concrete outputs and impactful results that directly supported our overarching goal: to embed healthy living and nutrition habits into the everyday lives of our students and their wider communities. One of the most significant outputs was the development of a comprehensive e-booklet and e-handbook on health and balanced nutrition, compiled collaboratively by all partner schools. Students and teachers also produced creative materials like slogan posters, masks, brochures, banners, logo, videos, healthy menus recipes, presentations, photo album consisting of photos of healthy eating activities,  school erasmus board which were showcased during school events and used to promote health awareness by using Web 2.0 tools for example, creating fruit avatars with Bitmoji and talking fruits and vegetables using chatterpix. We also organized workshops, exhibitions, and health-themed events that involved families and other schools, local communities, ngo, extending the project’s impact beyond the classroom.

2022-2-ES01-KA210-SCH-000094541.title: TIME TO ACT GREEN
2022-2-ES01-KA210-SCH-000094541.summary:
<< Background >>

Our school is part of a network of Educational Centers that meet a series of requirements to obtain a green label, but we wanted to advance in the indicators and continue expanding our green agenda. The program seemed both an incentive and a challenge, as it made us reflect on how to focus on different actions to make progress in this area while also sharing this experience with other European centers with a similar profile to ours.

<< Objectives >>

Increase the environmental awareness of all members of the educational community, with a special focus on students, bringing them closer to other realities and ways of doing things, sharing experiences, and improving their level of English and intercultural communication skills.

<< Implementation >>

- Plant the seed
- 2d animation
- More sustainable water and energy consumption activity
- Waste management and recycling 
- Digital animation classes
- Gardening sessions at schools



<< Results >>

The exchange of information on activities related to environmental issues has been highly satisfactory, as well as the practices carried out by the students. Those who have traveled had the opportunity to see firsthand the physical aspects of the program, such as soil, plants, waste collection organization, etc. This experience has greatly enriched both the students who participated in the program and the teachers, and, indirectly, the participating schools. Various initiatives have been implemented, leading to changes in different aspects such as reflection, waste collection and management, gardening, and landscaping within the school, with broader implications for environmental services, carbon sequestration, climate change resilience, etc. These experiences have been shared with the entire educational community, but especially with students who have voluntarily participated in environmental tasks or committees.
Additionally, the program has allowed us to create a positive impact on our surroundings by seeking information and building partnerships within our local area. Organizational structures and lines of work have been established that will continue to bear fruit even after the program has ended.

2022-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000092351.title: Coding Kids! - An intersectoral collaboration for the development of digital pedagogy in STEM education
2022-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000092351.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address various needs identified within our organization and among our partners. RITE sought to provide comprehensive technological solutions to educators and institutions, especially in early childhood education, as part of their commitment to research and innovation. CMP needed EU-funded opportunities to develop pedagogical tools, upskill staff, and establish collaborations across the EU to modernize early childhood education through non-formal methodologies. Their specific focus was on enhancing their daily work at their children’s daycare center. Varpelis kindergarten recognized the imperative for digital transformation in education and aimed to innovate teaching methodologies, particularly in STEM subjects, to equip young learners with competencies relevant to the future. By forming a consortium with international and cross-sector partners, we aimed to harness diverse expertise and experiences to create innovative educational tools that address the evolving needs of early childhood education, promoting competency-based learning in STEM and contributing to the cultivation of essential skills for the digital era.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to achieve several objectives:
Support Digital Transformation: Develop digital pedagogy tools and innovative learning approaches to support the digital transformation in early childhood and primary education.

Promote STEM Interest: Introduce coding skills to children aged 5-12 through creative learning resources to foster interest and excellence in STEM fields.

Establish Collaboration: Establish international and cross-sector collaboration to create comprehensive educational resources.

Address Gender Disparities: Make the project appealing to young girls and promote gender equality in STEM education to address gender disparities.
Overall, the project aimed to modernize education, particularly in STEM fields, and ensure that children are equipped with essential skills for the digital age.

<< Implementation >>

Project Management & Coordination: Ensuring effective coordination among international partners, overseeing project progress, and managing resources to achieve project objectives.

Multiplier Events: Organizing events to disseminate project outcomes and engage stakeholders, promoting the use of the educational resource developed.

Development of Open Educational Resource (OER): Collaboratively creating a multilingual educational game-based Android app aimed at fostering STEM skills and promoting excellence among children aged 5-12.

Training Activity for Educators: Conducting a 3-day short-term joint staff training event focused on the development, usability, and reusability of the OER. This training involved 11 relevant staff members from partner organizations and associated stakeholders, ensuring they were equipped to effectively utilize the educational resource in their respective contexts.

<< Results >>

Development of Coding Kids! Android app: A tangible outcome is the creation of the Coding Kids! app, enhancing coding & STEM learning for children aged 5-12 through digital technology and game-based methodology.
Motivation of Partner Staff for STEM: At least 12 staff from partner organizations were motivated to promote STEM education, reflecting a commitment to advancing STEM initiatives.
Expansion of Network & reputation: The project established an international consortium, expanding collaboration & positioning the organization as a hub for educational innovation.
Dissemination of Expertise & Knowledge: Expertise in STEM education and digital transformation was shared, advancing educational practices & fostering interest in STEM subjects.
Introduction of Innovative Learning Methods: Innovative learning methods rooted in competency-based education, particularly in STEM, were successfully implemented to enhance engagement & effectiveness.
Enhanced Interest in STEM Subjects: The Coding Kids! cultivates early interest in STEM, sparking curiosity & encouraging exploration of coding skills.
Contributions to Digital Transformation:We supported educators in adapting to the digital age, contributing to ongoing digital transformation
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

hr.name: CENTAR ZA RAZVOJ I UČENJE MALI PRINC

2022-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000093942.title: Raising Youth Generation Through Financial Literacy
2022-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000093942.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we believed that, in line with the current strategies of the Republic of Croatia and the EU, financial literacy is one of the key topics. As a secondary school that educates students to acquire competences for the profession of economists, and based on previous research conducted on the level of financial literacy in the Republic of Croatia, it has been proven that students of economics schools have greater knowledge on this topic than the average citizen of the Republic of Croatia. We believed that this was an excellent basis for educating peers in the country and other EU member states. Also, with this project, we wanted to reward the most successful students for participating in various activities in European cities so that they would have the opportunity to develop their language and social competences, but also to get acquainted with different cultures within Europe. Participation in Erasmus projects regularly results in meeting friends, gaining new experiences and developing long-term relationships with partners. We hope that in the future we will have the opportunity to participate in more projects and enrich our knowledge about Europe and the various topics that represent its essence.

<< Objectives >>

Our project is based on learning and using financial literacy and increasing their motivation to learn about real life in other European countries in the context of future job choices. It is very important to equip students with knowledge and skills that will be crucial for further education and job search in the future, not only in their own country but also abroad. We need our students to see how teenagers live in different countries, and we would like to achieve this by finding a solution together to promote a stronger European Union.
Our specific objectives are:
• to prepare young people for effective participation in economic society,
• to learn how technological tools and spaces provide creative opportunities for business activities, social interaction, where and how to earn, spend and save money wisely,
• to make decisions with economic significance in modern and future European societies,
• to provide young students with a background in the application of critical skills such as numeracy, computer literacy and critical thinking.
• to help young students understand concepts of money that are considered age-appropriate,
• to improve their understanding of financial concepts and products, and to build financial skills and com

<< Implementation >>

Activities we have implemented in your project are:
1. Basic Financial Terms - September 2023
Students created a quiz on basic financial terms, a booklet with a comparison of the prices of goods in the countries participating in the activity, and a booklet with basic financial terms.
2. My Future of Finance - May 2024
During the activity, students presented jobs of the future, created a platform for the exchange of goods, created virtual posters on the future of finance, as well as a handbook of financial literacy education.
3. Sustainable Finance - September 2024
During the activity, students had the opportunity to create a booklet on sustainable finance, participate in a Kahoot game, visit institutions, and create a coloring book on sustainable finance.
4. Digital Finance - March 2025
This activity was held online and organized by the First School of Economics in Zagreb. During the activities, students had the opportunity to listen to numerous lecturers on the topic of digital finance, participate in the creation of a booklet on the glossary of digital finance, and also compete in a quiz on knowledge of terms from this area.

<< Results >>

Here are the outputs from activities:
