2022-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000094047.title: Role models for pupils with disabilities
2022-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000094047.summary:
<< Background >>

The project objectives was to support young learners in becoming more confident through success stories in which they can identify themselves, strengthen inclusion and diversity in the classrooms and foster the development of pupils’ key competencies and basic skills. We focused on ability and disability in this project, because pupils with disabilities may have average or above average intelligence, but repeated academic failure weakens their confidence and self-esteem. Many struggle with school success and are at risk of early school leaving. Thus, it is crucial to start strengthening self-confidence in the early years of schooling.Inclusive classrooms need books and stories that support inclusive goals and offer the possibility for identification for all pupils. Children need good role models to support their development and shape their behaviour, their relationships, and the decisions they will make; because they are affected by the stories they read. Characters with disabilities are often presented as ‘poor little things’ who are dependent, passive and unable to defend themselves, and we wanted to change that. Also, stories enhance literacy skills, develop vocabulary, improve learn language and story structure.

<< Objectives >>

The concrete objectives of this project was to support young learners (aged 6-10) in becoming more confident through the collection of success stories in which they can identify themselves, strengthen inclusion and diversity in the classrooms and foster the development of learners’ key competencies and basic skills (literacy and digital skills) and provide inclusive learning resources for learners and teachers.
Through the development of confidence (the confidence and self-esteem play a crucial role in education), we wanted to tackle learning disadvantages and support the prevention of early school leaving.Truly inclusive classrooms need books and stories that support inclusive goals and offer
the possibility for identification for all pupils and all children need good role models to support their development.Despite the efforts to create more inclusive stories and inclusive classrooms in
general, research shows that contemporary children’s literature often reproduces stereotypes, and children’s literature that accurately portrays characters with a disability is one tool that can be used to promote awareness, and enhance inclusion and understanding, while strengthening basi competences (literacy and digital skills).

<< Implementation >>

During the project, we carried out several activities, in addition to project management, promotion and dissemination of the project, 2 partner meetings were held (1 in site and 1 online), and the project website and etwinning project were created, as a way of disseminating the project results. In addition to the mentioned activities, 3 publications were created, a guidebook for teachers (how to develop confidence and self-esteem in children with special needs), a collection of e-stories (in which children with disabilities are accurately portrayed) and a ready-to-use tool for teachers to create their own stories with the students. An evaluation of the created materials was also carried out, which showed that they are applicable, useful and stimulating for students and teachers.

<< Results >>

1. a guidebook for teachers on how to strengthen and develop the confidence and self-esteem of pupils with disabilities, as those play a crucial role in their education. The finished and evaluated guidebook is available on the project website (https://www.rolemodelsproject.eu/resources/) and is publicly and freely available for download in 4 languages (English, French, Italian and Croatian).
2. a collection of 8 role model success e-stories for learners with disabilities which accurately portray disabilities. In each story, a main caracter is a child with different disability (eg autism spectrum disorder, dyslexia, intellectual disabilities, ect.), but also with different abilities. The stories are written in simple vocabulary and language (so-called easy-to-read material), with simple illustrations, and are adapted to students aged 6 to 10 years. The stories are publicly and freely available in 4 languages on the project website https://www.rolemodelsproject.eu/resources/ 
3. workshops - a redy-to-use tool for teachers,educational professionals and pupils with disabilities. A guidance how to create the stories with students with a range of options, technical tips and recomendations, also available on project web site.

2022-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000094365.title: An awareness A person
2022-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000094365.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to tackle low language awareness and limited digital skills among students and teachers. Many learners, especially those from socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds, lacked motivation and opportunities to develop language competencies and master 21st-century tools. Teachers needed updated pedagogical approaches, such as CLIL and Web 2.0, to foster interactive, learner-centered environments. There was also a strong desire to expand cultural horizons and forge collaborative ties with European partners. By working with schools in other countries, we aimed to exchange proven methods, enhance digital proficiency, and foster intercultural understanding. Our goal was to provide equal opportunities for students and teachers to improve language competence, adopt innovative digital strategies, and experience meaningful collaboration that benefits both academic success and personal growth. Bridging the digital gap was crucial to ensure equitable access to modern learning. By prioritizing language awareness and cultural exchange, we sought to build a stronger sense of European identity. Ultimately, this project offered a vital platform for continuous professional development and enriched student experiences.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to strengthen language awareness, enhance digital competencies, and increase cultural sensitivity among both students and teachers. By integrating innovative teaching methods such as CLIL and Web 2.0 tools, we sought to create engaging, learner-centered environments that would motivate students—especially those from socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds—to improve their communication skills. Another key goal was to broaden participants’ intercultural understanding and foster a sense of European citizenship through collaborative activities, cultural visits, and shared projects across partner schools. Ultimately, we wanted to encourage continuous professional development among educators, ensure equitable access to high-quality educational resources, and cultivate an inclusive community where language learning and digital fluency open doors to future opportunities.
We also aimed to reduce early school leaving by demonstrating the real-world relevance of language and digital mastery. By promoting peer collaboration across national borders, we hoped to reinforce mutual respect and shared problem-solving approaches. Finally, through diverse cultural perspectives, we aspired to spark a genuine passion for lifelong learning

<< Implementation >>

We organized a series of interrelated activities designed to advance language awareness, digital competencies, and intercultural understanding. First, we formed Project Execution Teams to oversee planning, budgeting, participant selection, and dissemination. We then held four Learning Education Training Activities (LTTAs) in Croatia, Portugal, Romania, and Turkey, where teachers attended workshops on CLIL methodology, Web 2.0 tools, and functional language use, supplemented by cultural visits to strengthen real-life language application. After each LTTA, the participating teachers hosted student workshops in their home schools, ensuring that newly learned practices benefited at least 80 students. We also maintained Erasmus+ Corners in each school, updated eTwinning and social media platforms, and published bulletins summarizing each mobility’s outcomes. Pre-test and post-test surveys, along with regular feedback sessions, measured our progress toward greater language and digital fluency. Finally, we showcased all project outputs—such as digital materials, e-brochures, and cultural stories—through virtual exhibitions, school events, and a dedicated project website.

<< Results >>

Concrete Outputs
We produced a range of Web 2.0-based digital materials (e.g., Storybird narratives, Thinglink projects, digital posters) and published an e-brochure on linguistic and cultural awareness featuring activities from each partner country. Four teacher workshops introduced innovative tools and CLIL strategies, each summarized in an LTTA bulletin. We created a website, maintained a dedicated eTwinning space, and opened social media channels to share progress. Erasmus+ Corners displayed updates in every school, while “Foreign Languages Student Communities” engaged 80+ students in post-mobility workshops.

Other Results
Teachers and students reported stronger digital competencies and heightened enthusiasm for language study. Cultural visits fostered intercultural respect, strengthening a sense of European identity. Through collaborative lesson planning, teachers integrated these new techniques into their regular curricula. Students greatly appreciated the hands-on digital tasks, finding them relevant to modern learning styles. Finally, bridging the digital gap offered many disadvantaged learners equitable access to cutting-edge tools, confirming that our objectives were effectively met.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2022-2-IT02-KA210-SCH-000094171.title: IMAGENDER- promoting digital IMAge education to contrast GENDER stereotypes
2022-2-IT02-KA210-SCH-000094171.summary:
<< Background >>

Taking the value of the Gender Equality Index, elaborated by the European Institute for Gender Equality (EIGE) and considering it as a comparative element between the countries involved in the project, it is possible to trace different positions and approaches about this kind of topic. Some countries are more virtuous and some are less. Sweden and Finland, for example, are closer to the target value of 100, while Italy and Croatia are around 60. However, a broader look at the evaluation indicators reveals a still slow progression with respect to the achievement of true equality in terms of access to certain study paths (e.g. STEM), positions in management or representative roles, equal pay, and distribution of the burden of care. An inequality that it was interesting to analyse and debate through different narratives conveyed by the culture industry and especially the audiovisual industry. The project partners shared practices, methodologies and contents in order to use videos, films, spots in image education courses aimed at minor students and to prevent discriminatory attitudes.

<< Objectives >>

With the realisation of IMAGender, the partners collaborated in a process of research, exchange, prototyping and experimentation of good practices in the educational field, promoting media literacy paths in schools in the partner countries. The process started with a collaborative analysis of best practices at European level, with national focuses in the territories involved. This snapshot led us to consider as best practice projects differing in theme, methodology or output processing, to finally elaborate an ‘IMAGEnder’ methodology with which to experiment in pilot classes and multidisciplinary interest groups, workshops and activities for reflection and debate on how implicit and explicit stereotypes are represented or overturned in audiovisual cultural industry products: animated films, commercials, viral videos on social platforms.

<< Implementation >>

A1 - set up operational tools for monitoring the project (PM handbook, workplan, monitoring tool, communication and dissemination plan) and shared them with the partners during the kickoff meeting, promoted regular monthly meetings and opened a Facebook page in two languages ITA/ENG.
A2 was divided into research sub-actions: each partner elaborated a theoretical research on the state of the national debate with respect to the project topics and one on European (sometimes international) best practices as inspiration. Everyone analysed and evaluated the searches of others through an internal ranking tool.
A3 - The most representative moment of the project was the transnational meeting where we can meet each other in person, experience and discuss the methodology and activities. Representatives from partner countries, together with local educators and students participated in two training days on the IMAGEnder methodology.
A4 - Each partner proposed workshops and activities learned in schools and territories.
A5 - Each partner organised a community event to experience and debate the effectivness of the pathway.

<< Results >>

Nel corso del progetto, oltre agli strumenti operativi per la gestione interna, sono stati prodotti:
- 1 research report for booklet production
- 1 downloadable booklet containing the theoretical research, the methodology development pathway and examples of activity sheets that can be reproduced in class/community groups
- videos, images and attendance certificates with the specifications stated in the submitted project.

2022-2-LT01-KA210-SCH-000093612.title: Digital Trace of Cultural Heritage
2022-2-LT01-KA210-SCH-000093612.summary:
<< Background >>

The project aimed to address students' lack of knowledge about cultural heritage and enhance their digital skills. Many teenagers spent increasing time on virtual games and social media but had limited awareness of their own and other cultures.  
Despite being part of the curriculum, cultural heritage topics lacked engaging learning methods. Surveys showed 39% of students had little and 48% average knowledge of tangible heritage, while 57% had average knowledge of intangible heritage. Digital skills were also underdeveloped, with 71% having little or average knowledge of digital tools and 8% never using them.  
The project integrated technology into learning through interactive activities, digital maps, and animations, fostering creativity and critical thinking. It also promoted intercultural cooperation, equal participation, and international exchanges, strengthening school partnerships, improving teachers' competencies, and encouraging community involvement in cultural heritage dissemination.

<< Objectives >>

In implementing the project, we aimed to increase students' knowledge of cultural heritage - to provide them with the opportunity to better understand the tangible and intangible heritage of their own and other countries. To develop digital skills - to promote students' ability to use digital tools, create interactive educational tools, digital maps and animations. To develop critical thinking and creativity - to promote an analytical approach to cultural heritage, its protection and relevance in the modern world. To improve intercultural cooperation - to ensure the participation of students and teachers in international exchanges and to promote knowledge of different cultures. To strengthen the international school network - to strengthen cooperation between schools in different countries, share good practices and improve teachers' competences. To promote community involvement - to involve parents and local communities in cultural heritage preservation and digital education activities.
The project was focused on long-term impact, aiming to provide new knowledge and skills, and to shape students' and teachers' attitudes towards cultural heritage.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, we implemented various activities aimed at cultural heritage awareness and digital skills development.
4 international mobilities took place:
- Lithuania (“Recognition”) - participants learned to recognize and analyze tangible and intangible heritage, created virtual exhibitions and interactive educational games.
- Croatia (“Rebounding”) - students delved into European cultural heritage, created digital calendars, virtual exhibitions and maps.
- Romania (“Realizing”) - participants compared traditions of different countries, prepared interactive tasks with digital tools and created animations with virtual reality tools.
- Turkey (“Rebuilding”) - Participants analyzed historical figures, the significance of the Silk Road, created virtual museums and completed the creation of an interactive map depicting cultural heritage.
We developed digital skills:
- Participants used various digital tools: ArtSteps, PictroMap, Unity 3D, Flipgorilla, Kahoot, Canva, etc.
- We organized creative workshops.
Intercultural cooperation took place:
- We did an eTwinning project.
Community involvement and dissemination of results:
- Events were organized in schools, presenting the results of the created digital heritage map and animat

<< Results >>

A project page has been created, which contains an interactive digital cultural heritage map-ebook, marking the objects of tangible and intangible cultural heritage of Europe. This map depicts the works of students from thirteen European countries, reflecting the cultural aspects of different regions.
The ebook also contains various works of students, in which they creatively present the cultural heritage of European countries. In this book you can find: videos created by students about the most important cultural objects and traditions, posters and slides, which visually present the cultural features of different countries, drawings and illustrations, revealing the attitude of young people to cultural heritage, interactive projects that allow you to get to know the history and traditions of Europe in more depth.
https://sites.google.com/view/dtch/collaboration/joint-activities?authuser=0
The eTwinning project has been created and is currently underway, allowing for continued cooperation between schools, sharing good practices and digital tools.
https://school-education.ec.europa.eu/en/etwinning/projects/digital-trace-cultural-heritage/twinspace/pages

2022-2-LV01-KA210-SCH-000100653.title: Art is smart: Art as a tool of social inclusion
2022-2-LV01-KA210-SCH-000100653.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to improve school performance of students with special needs (ages 10–20) by using art therapy to develop their motor, cognitive, emotional, and social skills. Many of our students face challenges such as low self-esteem, anxiety, communication difficulties, and a lack of motivation due to limited progress despite great effort. Through this project, we aim to help them express themselves, feel successful, and strengthen their confidence by using creative methods adapted to their abilities. The project also improves everyday life skills, reduces learning-related stress, and supports inclusion in the classroom and wider community. Teachers and school staff gain new tools and insights by learning from partners in Poland, Latvia, and Croatia, strengthening professional capacity and enriching school programs. Key outcomes include 5 international LTT activities, over 100 students involved in regular art therapy, and a multilingual manual of good practices in special needs education.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project was to improve performance of special needs students of all partners schools by using various art therapies. We wanted to develop their motor, cognitive and social competences, but also empower students to express themselves, gain self-confidence to use their potential in academic, social and everyday life.  We also wanted to reduce our students' stress related to the learning process, prevent early school leaving due to lower achievement and encourage students to build on their strengths during the learning process. Art therapy methods turned out to be perfect because of easy adjustment to the level of development and abilities.
The second, but equally important reason was to increase the knowledge, skills and competences of teachers from partner schools in the use of various methods of broadly understood art therapy. We wanted to exchange our experience and the possibility of cooperation with foreign partners increased the dynamics and attractiveness of the project.

<< Implementation >>

We carried out a wide range of art-based activities in each partner school, all aligned with the project plan and tailored to the needs of our students. Techniques included ebru (drawing on water), canvas and silk painting, soap and candle making, macrame, music, wet felting, origami, paper wicker, recycled crafts, and cooking. Some were part of learning, teaching, and training activities, while others were stand-alone workshops.
Our goal was to make activities engaging and skill-enhancing—supporting motor skills, coordination, imagination, attention, persistence, motivation, self-confidence, and social skills like communication and teamwork. In total, 11 macro activities were completed.
In addition to local events, we held two transnational meetings for teachers, five international LTTAs for students and teachers, and two major online meetings. Each school also set up a project corner to showcase progress.
The final result is an online teacher’s manual—available to all—which serves as both inspiration and a practical guide for using art therapy methods in special education.

<< Results >>

Participating in the project provided an excellent opportunity to explore various forms of art therapy suitable for students with intellectual disabilities. Key outcomes include:
1. At least 5 teachers or professionals from each partner school gained knowledge of art therapy methods through project and LTT activities – totaling a minimum of 25 trained staff.
2. At least 20 students per school (ages 8 – 20) engaged in structured art therapy activities both in and out of school, reaching a minimum of 100 students overall.
3. Five joint LTT activities were organized, each hosted by a different partner school, involving at least 2 teachers and 2 students from each school – totaling at least 10 students and 10 teachers per event.
4.A practical handbook on art therapy was created in English and translated into Croatian, Polish, and Latvian, offering examples of good practices for inclusive education.
Additionally many students traveled abroad for the first time, boosting their social skills through international experiences. Strong cooperation among partners led to plans for future Erasmus+ projects, building on the success of this one.

2022-2-MT01-KA210-SCH-000095051.title: Digital Dimension Improves Green Life
2022-2-MT01-KA210-SCH-000095051.summary:
<< Background >>

The main motivation for putting forward this project application was the need to shed a brighter light on the phenomenon of “Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)” through education in schools. The application submitted here was considerate of the ongoing and new-growth strategy; the document “Towards a Sustainable Europe by 2023” published by the European Union, that aims to transform EU into a prosperous society where there are no net emissions of greenhouse gases in 2050. The economic growth also plays a vital role towards this strategy. Hence this project planning presented 4 main stages: Green Schools, Green Citizenship, Green Minds and Green Life. 
The global objectives of the Digital-Dig Project are to work towards realizing the “The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)” targeted by the UN and EU Commission. By this is was emphasized the importance of a sustainable life and our contribution to the solution of problems related to climate change. The aim to implement “Sustainable development” in Education was discussed in detail and it was decided that teaching new competences such as critical thinking, improving problem solving and decision making skills are as important as other academic subjects. 

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives achieved by the implementation of this Project were to provide relevant  knowledge about “Sustainable Development”, and it’s implementation in schools of the participating countries. The knowledge and good practices gained is then to be displayed for dissemination through various platforms. Results of the project are in fact to be available online for a wider audience, this increases the validity of the work done, as after the funding period it will remain a sustainable resource for the communities in European partnership. Wide dissemination increases the sustainability of the project.
This main objective could only be reached by the teamwork, collaboration and support of school staff, school leaders and other educational stakeholders.

<< Implementation >>

Specific activities were introduced and implemented in the Project in order to achieve the targeted goals. 
-2 physical student Exchange programs held in 2 different partner countries (2 teachers, 4 students in each)
-2 teacher trainings held in 2 different partner countries (“Learning and Acting for a Better Future” and “Digital Skills”)
-2 online modules before each students’ mobility
-collaboration with companies/municipality/NGO for each student mobility
-workshops and outdoor activities about how to make schools greener (Green Schools) 
-study visits for local authority about discovering e-citizenship and digital platforms (Green Citizenship)
-workshops and study visits about sustainability (Green Citizenship-Green Schools)
Also, tangible  results:
-2 Digital Learning Units (LU)
- 2 short movies
-2 e-books
-2 Digital puzzles 
To be found: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1JXQ4Q88MDfVfsaX0t6ayEiRfrExw6RjB?usp=sharing

<< Results >>

Tangible output results that were created by the partners using digital tools through the mobilities were created:
-2 Digital Learning Units (LU)
-2 short movies
-2 e-books
-2 Digital puzzles 
Also, respective school websites were updated with activities of each mobility, as well as ESEP and social media accounts of the Dig-Dig project. Results achieved also included the increase in awareness of the importance of Green Schools, the introduction and implementation of green practices, increase in awareness on climate change, opportunities to students in alternative education students and respective school staff, improvement in communication skills and language skills, development in digital skills during teaching and learning and the understanding of EU identity.

2022-2-NL01-KA210-SCH-000102141.title: A Peace Education Package for teachers and Students
2022-2-NL01-KA210-SCH-000102141.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project with the goal of leveraging our unique collection of stories, objects, and diaries from children affected by war to enrich educational practices in Europe. We recognized an urgent need to empower teachers and educators with resources that facilitate discussions around the complexities of war, the resilience of the human spirit, and the importance of peace. Our aim was to bridge the gap between historical knowledge and emotional understanding, providing educators with tools to engage students in meaningful dialogue about conflict, empathy, and reconciliation. Through this international seminar we enabled educators to bring these critical lessons into classrooms around Europe. By doing so, we aimed to foster a more informed, empathetic, and compassionate generation of students. With millions of Ukrainian and other refugees in Europe, we consider this effort to be timely and needed.

<< Objectives >>

The project had these stated objectives and aimed to:

1. Develop a context-sensitive approach on how to promote educational insights on the prevention of conflict and peace promotion in different school contexts, empowering teachers and students to co-create learning materials. Kids’ experiences are at the core of this work.
2. Develop student-centered tools to promote peace education. Such tools will be teacher friendly, fit the curriculum and help students develop key insights. They will be available in English and all PPs’ languages.
3. Empower teachers & educators to become active promoters of peace education in all targeted areas.
4. Expand high school students’ awareness and knowledge about conflict prevention, peace 
promotion & peace building, motivating them to learn more and take action.

<< Implementation >>

Here is a brief overview of main activities:
1. International Seminar Series: We hosted three-day-long online sessions, where educators were introduced to our collection and the foundational concepts of peace education, human rights, and dealing with past conflicts.
2. Development of Activity Plans: In collaboration with experts, educators developed activity plans tailored to their classrooms. These plans utilized the museum's objects, stories, and diaries to create engaging and educational content.
3. Mentorship and Support: We provided ongoing mentorship and support to educators as they implemented these activity plans in their schools. This included feedback sessions, additional resources, and expert consultations to ensure the successful integration of the program into diverse educational settings.
4. Evaluation and Feedback Mechanism: Post-implementation, we conducted evaluations through forms and discussions to assess the impact of the activities, gather insights for improvement, and upgrade our educational packages based on real-world classroom experiences.
5. We created an online toolkit and shared project outputs (ready-to-use activity plans) there and on the Erasmus results platform.

<< Results >>

The project achieved notable results:

1. Successfully conducted three online seminar sessions for over 50 educators across Europe, focusing on peace education and conflict resolution.
2. Activity Plan Development: Facilitated the creation of innovative activity plans, directly impacting classroom discussions on war, peace, and empathy.
3. Student Engagement: Hundreds of students engaged in meaningful activities, developing critical thinking and empathy towards war-affected peers.
4. Feedback Mechanism: Collected and utilized educator feedback to refine and enhance our educational resources.
5. Networking: Laid groundwork for a Teachers Network for Peace in Serbia as a spin-off initiative, promoting collaborative peace education efforts and becoming a legacy of this project.
6. Museum Engagement and study trips: Inspired study trip visits to the War Childhood Museum by schools from Croatia and Serbia, extending learning beyond the classroom.
7. Resource Enhancement: Expanded the Peace and Justice Education Resource Center of the War Childhood Museum with a new Teachers for Teachers toolkit, making it a valuable tool for European and global educators.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2022-2-NO01-KA210-SCH-000101487.title:
Outdoor Environmental education (EE) and education for
sustainable development (ESD) via Eco teachers and
Students
2022-2-NO01-KA210-SCH-000101487.summary:
<< Background >>

The reason why we applied for this project was to experience and learn that the outdoor evironmental education for sustainable development, led by eco-conscious teachers and students, is crucial because it fosters a deep, experiential connection with the nature. It helps learners understand the impact of human actions on ecosystems and equips them with practical skills to address environmental challenges. By promoting sustainable practices, eco education empowers individuals to take responsibility for preserving natural resources and encourages lifelong environmental stewardship, ultimately contributing to a more sustainable future. Outdoor environemtal education is vital for sustainable development because it immerses studens in real-world environmental issues, making learning more engaging and impactful. 
The needs we addressed was and mutual work  between Eco teachers guiding students in exploring natural ecosystems, understanding bioderversity, and recongnizing the delicate balance required for sustanibility. 

<< Objectives >>

we wanted to help students develop critical thinking, problem solving, and teamwork skills while gaining a direct understanding og the environmental challenges we face, such as climate change, desforestation, and pollution. By learning outdoors, students experience the interconnectedness of human and natural system, reinforcing the importance og sustanaible living. 

<< Implementation >>

Eco teachers played a key role in the activities of the environmental ethics and responsibility, helping students understand how their actions can contribute to preserving the planet for future generations. Futhermore, the activities implemented in the project, promoted active citizenship by empowering students to take action in their communities, from conservation efforts to advocacy for sustainable policies. We are sure that the outdoor environmental activities in this project fosters a  generation of environmentally conscious individuals who are equipped to address the ecological challenges og today and ensure a healthier planet for tomorrow. We had big focus both on how we implement and what kind of activities we wanted to have with the students. 

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs and other results in this project:
Students and teachers develop a deeper understanding og environmental issues, leading to more sustanaible behaviors in daily life. 
Participants gain hands-on experience in conservation practices, such as waste management, water conservation, and biodiversity monitoring. 
The creation of eco-friendly school gardens, composting systems and creating activities with the other studens and teachers at schools that reduce environmental footprints.
We can also se a behavioral change on adoption og sustanible consumption habits among studens, teachers, and their families. 
In Norway the hole school took part of an Eco-Awareness campain. We organized and lead awarness campaign promoting issues and sustanaible solutions.

2022-2-PL01-KA210-SCH-000091856.title: Undiscovered world
2022-2-PL01-KA210-SCH-000091856.summary:
<< Background >>

The teachers/students parents in partner schools noticed that Science is  considered boring and extremely difficult  by school students and they aren't motivated to learn it. But thanks to learning and understanding Science subjects the students:
- can develop problem-solving skills - they learn to think logically and solve problems,
- can be aware of technology - learning the basics of how certain devices work can help them develop ideas of their own and invent new technology,
- can help develop literacy and language-they practice their writing skills and expand their vocabulary at the same time,
- can learn team work - Science is a collaborative team exercise as it must go through a process of peer review before we can use it,
- can help separate fact from fiction and create ability to make informed decisions-as a result as citizens, they can contribute more to the society in a positive and thoughtful way. 
Our project was aimed then at making a difference in students attitudes towards Science subjects - as they had rather negative one and they found these subjects boring, difficult and unnecessary.  When we teach Science in a new, innovative way and students gain Science related-knowledge they  learn the skills mentioned above.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were:
1. boosting students motivation to learn Science by:  increasing the participants' awareness of importance of learning Science by presenting benefits/advances of science and proving Science helps us understand our world and then improving students performance in Science;  making science attractive to young people by presenting science through mysteries, puzzles and great efforts of scientists trying to reveal them and then developing passion for Science.
2. improving students’ skills of teamwork and cooperation by doing project work, 
3. increasing the participation of pupils with the greatest educational needs, including children in unfavourable situation (those with limited access to various educational forms due to geographical, economic, health and/or cultural reasons) and those with fewer opportunities,
4. promoting an active citizenship by teaching students how to live with other people creatively as well as by coping with new challenges of living together. Additionally, students  developed the ability to ask questions, collect information, organise and test their ideas, solve problems, and apply what they learn. 

<< Implementation >>

In the project we implemented the following activities:
- Ancient Undiscovered World - students did some research on ancient science and technological achievements, a ppt was prepared. Students investigated the things which are still unexplained in ancient Science. During the activity they discussed the topic , the mysteries and visited Mastic Museum which shows how ancient people produced  mastic.
- Undiscovered space – students found  out about  space explorations, they prepared a choice of films and a list of space „issues” waiting to be discovered. They also learnt about things which we use every day and we have them thanks to space exploration. They visited Planaterium in Lisbon too.
- Undiscovered human body - students found  out about mysteries in human body and presented them as an online quiz/game. They showed body functions in a creative way. They listed the things we are not 100% sure in our bodies. They took part in a workshop with a paramedic. 
- Unexplained phenomena- students worked on unexplained phenomena, strange ones and presented it as a storytelling activity. They made a presentation about unexplained things in our world.They met with an expert in unexplained phenomena.  
- Project webpage.

<< Results >>

Tangible (concrete)  results:
1.  Presentations: of the achievements of ancient Science, of space exploration, unexplained phenomena.
2.  Presenting the body functions and life process in creative way - as a pantomime, using gesture, body language, pictures, videos-pictures.
3.  Presentation of mysteries of ancient Science, space, human body, phenomena.
4.  A list of films about space, UFO and a list of things waiting for their discovery.
5. Webpage on Facebook.
Intangible results:
The is a change in students' attitudes towards Science - they find it important in lives and at school. Participants learnt about ancient civilisations,  Space achievements,  about human body, life processes and how important  the awareness of these processes is. They practised their English and developed digital skills. Students also fostered civic competence and  knowledge of social and political concepts and structures (democracy, justice, equality, citizenship and civil rights). They learnt to cooperate, tolerate the differences, understand different customs, lifestyles.
These activities were part of curricula of History, Physics, Biology, Geography.  The activities, their results were presented to school community and to the local authorities.

2022-2-PL01-KA210-SCH-000098574.title: Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles
2022-2-PL01-KA210-SCH-000098574.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the PROSLIFE project to address the urgent global need for sustainable living practices, in response to increasing resource demands and the ongoing threats of climate change and biodiversity loss. By 2050, with a projected global population of 10 billion, our lifestyle choices will significantly impact the planet. Therefore, it is essential to educate future generations on sustainable living to build resilient communities and promote environmental stewardship. 
The project aimed to address these needs by equipping educators with the knowledge and tools necessary to teach sustainable lifestyles in schools. This aligns with global educational goals such as the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, particularly SDG Target 4.7, which emphasizes the need for education to promote sustainable development. PROSLIFE seeks to introduce sustainability principles into education systems, empowering teachers and students to adopt sustainable practices and foster a deeper connection with their environment.



<< Objectives >>

By implementing the PROSLIFE project, we aimed to achieve the following key objectives:
1. Develop sustainability competencies among teachers and students, fostering awareness of the impact of overconsumption and promoting responsible consumption (SDG12).
2. Enhance educators' skills to effectively teach Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) and guide the sustainable growth of societies through innovative and digital tools.
3. Encourage international collaboration, expanding the capabilities of schools and promoting European cooperation through project-based activities and transnational meetings.
4. Build active citizenship and empower individuals to make sustainable lifestyle choices that consider social, economic, and environmental impacts.
5. Involve disadvantaged groups, ensuring inclusivity in education and participation in local and international sustainability projects.
Through these objectives, we aimed to transform teaching approaches and embed sustainable lifestyle education into everyday learning, ultimately fostering more sustainable communities.


<< Implementation >>

In the PROSLIFE project, we implemented the following key activities:
1. Teacher Competency Development: Teachers enhanced their skills to follow the Pathway to Sustainable Lifestyles Education throughout the project.
2. Creation of Teacher Training Content: We developed specialized training materials for teachers, focused on promoting sustainable lifestyles.
3. Online Content Creation: Teachers learned how to create online educational content to ensure effective e-learning.
4. Development of E-learning Modules: We designed and implemented e-learning modules specifically tailored for sustainable lifestyles education.
5. Training for E-learning Platform Use: Teachers received training to effectively use the e-learning platform and promote sustainable lifestyle education within their schools and communities.
These activities supported the overall goal of embedding sustainable lifestyles education into teaching practices across participating schools.


<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results of the PROSLIFE project include:
1. Professional Development for Teachers: Teachers gained a deeper understanding of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG-12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).
2. Enhanced Competencies: Teachers developed key skills, values, and attitudes to help their students become more aware of their consumption habits and act as sustainable consumers.
3. Creation of E-Learning Modules: Teachers developed and implemented e-learning modules aimed at promoting sustainable lifestyle education, providing a digital resource for educators.
4. International Collaboration: Teachers collaborated with international colleagues, exchanging best practices and strengthening their approach to sustainable lifestyle education.
5. Support from School Leaders: Awareness raised about Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) led school leaders to support the integration of sustainable lifestyle education in their institutions.

2022-2-RS01-KA210-SCH-000098315.title: Improving knowledge and skills by connecting the sustainable development goals oriented towards the topic of water with the curriculum for primary schools
2022-2-RS01-KA210-SCH-000098315.summary:
<< Background >>

Our motivation stems from the needs of teachers and their interest in linking curricula and regular school lessons with sustainable development goals. Through the questionnaires we conducted in previous projects and while writing this one, there emerged an opportunity to improve their knowledge and skills. Additionally, we aimed for more active student involvement and the expansion of their knowledge and skills. We have focused on water and food along with the environment. We live in a time when water scarcity is increasingly intensifying, more and more food is being wasted, and there are more hungry people, all of which affects the environment and exacerbates climate change. Considering that food production creates the greatest burden on water pollution, we have focused on this issue. We connected this with the fact that in elementary schools, there is no dedicated education on sustainable development, even though it is legally prescribed, but teachers do not have the materials and tools to implement it. Finally, but not least importantly, for our own strengthening as an organization dealing with these issues, fostering connections, and cooperation.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal is to establish a connection between sustainable development goals and the curriculum for elementary schools through topics related to water, food, and environmental protection. The specific objectives are: 1. Improving the level of knowledge and skills of teachers in the field of sustainable development goals oriented towards the topics of water, food, and the environment, as well as the 2030 Agenda. Also, 2. Enhancing the ability of teachers to transfer knowledge and skills about sustainable development goals related to the topics of water, food, and the environment to students through pilot demonstrations of practical work.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities, aside from project management as the foundation of the project, also include three transnational meetings. We organized webinars, initially for team members, and then each partner organization organized separate webinars for teachers in each country. Based on the webinars and research, we started preparing a handbook in collaboration with schools, which was tested in schools and demonstrated through Water Day at the end of the project. As part of the dissemination activities, we organized multiplier events where we presented the project, activities, and results. Besides the transnational meetings planned by the project, we also met as a team twice more during Water Days and multiplier events in Slovenia and Croatia.

<< Results >>

Specifically, the result is improved knowledge and skills of teachers and their newly developed ability to transfer knowledge and skills to students through sustainable development goals on the topics of water, food, and the environment. To achieve this, we prepared a Handbook with basic content on the topics of water, food, and the environment; a methodology for application in teaching, 17 worksheets encompassing 33 activities, and recommendations for extracurricular and outdoor activities. Another result is the webinars that each partner organization can continue to conduct, enhancing their regular activities. About 100 teachers were educated, and 3000 children were involved in the project. Three Water Days and three multiplier events were organized, with a total of over 100 participants.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-2-RS01-KA210-SCH-000100833.title: Putevima Antičkih civilizacija
2022-2-RS01-KA210-SCH-000100833.summary:
<< Background >>

Ancient locations represent a significant part of the history of both countries and Europe’s history, which is why we thought it is important for the participants to be familiar with them and to expand their knowledge about them as well as their consciousness about the importance of those locations in their local communities and wider. The locations we have visited in our country are Felix Romuliana, as an example of explored, mapped, preserved and publicly accessible archaeological location, as well as Viminacium and Narodni muzej u Zaječaru. We became familiar with the work of ES Grohote during the cooperation in two KA1 projects, which is why we decided to explore those archaeological locations and facts about them together and help their popularity and preservation. Since this topic is not developed in this way through the school programs in our countries, we thought that this project would be meaningful for the students and the teachers as well as the wider public. The product of this project, The digital guide, is a useful educational, didactic tool for all three partners of this project and it influences the popularization of this topic among the children of school age on the territory of Serbia, Croatia and wider.

<< Objectives >>

The students and the teachers of both schools visited Felix Romuliana location and had the chance to see an example of a well explored ancient archaeological location as well as visiting Viminacium. The experts from the Narodni muzej u Zaječaru introduced them to the museum’s permanent setting, as well as with the archaeological location Felix Romuliana. They learned about the ways of exploring, marking and preserving such locations and were trained for mapping archaeological locations, as well as expanded their digital competencies while they worked on the digital guide. Considering the fact that the product of this project is a digital guide called “Following the paths of ancient civilizations”, written in three languages and created to be an additional educational tool intended for the wider public, they had an opportunity to learn about how to present historical locations to the public. The students and teachers of both schools became familiar with the historical locations in both countries and based on the research and mapping they worked on creating, planning and making the digital guide, with the assistance of the participating teachers and parents and by using ICT tools.

<< Implementation >>

Participants met through online meetings, planned the further steps, tasks, agreed on the way of writing documentation and chose the tools for making the Digital guide. The first mobility:the visit of the participants form Grohote to the participants of Tvrđava, preparation for the visit and visit itself to Narodni muzej u Zaječaru and to Felix Romuliana, an interview with a curator, a workshop about the techniques of mapping, a visit to Viminacium, working on the collected materials and its preparation for the Digital guide.The second mobility: the visit of the participants from Tvrđava to the participants from Grohote, getting to know Šolta and the school Grohote, visiting the archaeological locations on the island, the process of mapping, gathering the material,planning and beginning of the making of the Digital guide. Next phase: making the guide in cooperation with one of the parents of a participant of the project.Dissemination: the process and the product itself are presented on the web pages of the partners, their social media,the posters in schools,on the teachers’ meetings,online portals, parent-teacher meetings and through a festival open to wider public.The results are shown on the Erasmus+ platform and ESEP platform.

<< Results >>

The final product of the project is the Digital guide made in Serbian, Croatian and English language, which is important for developing the language competencies of the students. The Guide is a part of the program for the fifth and the sixth grade of both schools. It is available to the public on the websites of the partners, their social media and on the ESEP platform and because of that it is available to everyone as a didactic tool. Since it is in digital form, the changes in it are possible by the next generations of the students of the 5th and the 6th grade of these schools. Working on this project allowed the teachers participants to develop their cross-curriculum competencies, it empowered the students to explore, gather, work on the materials, it developed their digital skills, their communication, cooperation and the presentation of materials. We also expect more interest from the local community for preserving archaeological and historical locations, as well as for visiting museums. The Digital guide will be used by the students of next generations and using it they will expand their knowledge about the archaeological locations on these territories.

2022-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000097024.title: Two sides of beauty and the river between them
2022-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000097024.summary:
<< Background >>

We approached the project with the aim of enriching the learning experience of our students by involving students and teachers from other European countries. Our main objective was to develop communication skills in English, Croatian and Slovenian and to promote teamwork skills between teachers and students. Through joint work and creativity, we aimed at a better understanding of the common European space in which we live.
Participation in the project helped to develop competences and awareness of European values, improved communication in foreign languages, better understanding of the arts and increased interest in STEM subjects. At the same time, we developed digital skills and improved the use of information and communication technology (ICT), fostered teamwork and raised awareness of pollution and the depletion of natural resources as well as the importance of sustainable development.
An important aspect of the project was to enable the students with special needs the opportunity for equal participation in all activates.


<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to offer a genuine opportunity to develop communication skills in English, Croatian and Slovenian. Our aim was to enable students to actively speak and write in English, especially on scientific topics, in order to enrich their vocabulary in the language. At the same time, we wanted to broaden their knowledge about the depletion of natural resources through real-life experiences.
By involving professional artists the level of authentical learning and the motivation for Stem subjects were significantly  increased.
Participation in international groups was crucial for developing team skills and intercultural competences. This approach was aimed at developing a better understanding of the European space and how it works. Collaboration with external experts such as scientists allowed us to tackle challenges in environmental topics and to introduce new learning approaches.
The partnership with the school was set up to give the school a first experience of European cooperation and project work. Together we have increased the level of internationalisation and cosmopolitanism of both schools.
The most important result of this project is the new knowledge, experience and enhanced capacities of both pupils and teachers.

<< Implementation >>

We carried out the following activities: 
- developing and planning of the concept, content and activities and common writing of the application form. We developed a research and project approach and strategies to strengthen intercultural competences and the European dimension among teachers and students. We designed activities that promoted creative expression and eco-sustainability among participants from both schools, including parents.
The list of activities contains: presentation films in a foreign language, design of the project logo, production of tourist leaflets in a foreign language, creation of mathematical teaching sheets, 3D planning, design of picture books, production of imaginary maps, computer design of theatre sheets, production of invitations, public performance at the Ljubljana City Museum, design of the website, preparation of dissemination material and preparation of reports on the activities carried out.
We carried out two project meetings with the teachers and principals and two students exchanges in Osijek and Ljubljana. 
We also published the project monograph.
Different project management, evaluation and dissemination activities were carried out.


<< Results >>

- Project website 
- Participation in social networks
- Conducted surveys 
- Production of the presentation movies
- Photographic material as documentation 
- Exhibitions at both schools and in The Museum of Ljubljana
- Material with tourist information and  leaflets
- Tourist guiding 
- Different project reports (school annually reports, intermediate and final project report) 
- Project logo 
- Project Monograph 
- English - Croatian - Slovenian dictionary 
- Different dissemination material (articles, hoodies, invitations)
- Erasmus+ corners
- Surveys to measure the impact of the project
- Live performances 
- Theater sheets 
- Teaching material for project activities
- 3D plans and models of different buildings and bridges
- Innovative maps drawings for visual presentation of project data
- Science experiments with water 
- Illustrating picture books 
- Developed basic communication skills of scientific terms in English, Slovenian and Croatian 
- Developing communication skills in Croatian, Slovenian and English
- Computer-aided design of materials to promote project events
- Project management documentation
- Drone footage
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-2-SK01-KA210-SCH-000101430.title: Capturing sustainable lifestyle in short videos
2022-2-SK01-KA210-SCH-000101430.summary:
<< Background >>

The partnership was formed for a long time before the application of the project, initially the KA210 SCH application was focused on media literacy, but during the re-application, the goals were extended and a sharper focus was placed on European priorities - Digitization and ecology.
The main motivation (need) was international cooperation, which enabled students and teachers to travel and actively participate in the small partnership KA210 in the school sector, which managed to get involved at the basic level in the research and implementation of HR sea cleaning, the processing of rare TR herbs, and to expand their horizons in the field of sustainable construction and farming in the Slovak Republic. The development of digital and film making skills were the visions and needs of the cooperating schools in this post-covid period. The joint need of the partners to direct the pupils to a sustainable lifestyle and at the same time to develop their digital and filmmaking skills fulfilled the content of a very innovative school partnership.

<< Objectives >>

1. GOAL
The main goal of the project was to teach students to live a fully sustainable lifestyle.
In three international mobilities and during 21 months of cooperation, the partner schools tried to teach pupils the skills to protect themselves
environment. The goal was to lead students to environmental awareness in various areas...
 For example: how to save resources in schools, many things are often unsparingly thrown in the trash, with the students we solved strategies for using raw materials in a new way (ideas for recycling).
2. GOAL
During the duration of the project, the students acquired all the necessary technical skills of using digital media and being responsible
dealing with them. They also acquired the skills of working with data sources on the Internet - how to process information and
work safely on the Internet. Among these competences was to master the proactive formation of one's own skills, to design one's own digital creation, to know and apply the basic rights and obligations of the virtual space, etc.
3. GOAL
To create together meaningful, interesting activities for students during the main educational time, as well as outside of class, which is what we wanted to strengthen the learning motivation of pupils.

<< Implementation >>

All planned activities, online meetings took place as planned: (3 INTERNATIONAL MEETINGS).  The adjustment against the plan was the implementation of the Film Festival and the evaluation of the student works competition during M3A in Croatia onsite (instead of one more online - originally planned as M5 ONLINE ACTIVITY - Film Festival), the reason was taking into account the younger age of the students of the partner school from TR.
M0 - Opening online meeting of ZOOM meeting coordinators
M1A - First mobility - Short educational meeting of pupils SLOVAKIA - workshops: media literacy, digital skills, ecological construction and farming
M1B - Implementation - tasks of partners, project work of pupils 
M2A - Short Pupil Exchange Event TURKEY - workshops: digital skills, film editing, ecological activities - boats made of plastic bottles, getting to know the unique medicinal herbs of the region and their processing. 
M2B - Implementation - tasks of partners, project work of pupils 
M3A - Short educational meeting of pupils - Film festival - CROATIA - workshops waste sorting - separate ECO landfill, filmmaking professions, ecology of the sea - its protection (implementation of EM balls) and verification of the results for sea cleaning. 

<< Results >>

Specific outputs for project: a set of short films, documentaries, which are proof that the students worked on their technical skills, thought about a sustainable lifestyle, created scenarios, tried out the role of "influencers".

The product of "fermented balls" that clean the sea can be considered a scientific work, because the Croatian partner also completed measurements for the result of ecological cleaning.

In addition an 18-page photo bulletin/brochure summarizing the output of the entire project is also a document intended for public sharing of the results, contenting links for to the videos produced by pupils and evaluation of the project

All set aims have been implemented in details, the project objective became a guide for joint and individual activities.

2023-1-AT01-KA210-SCH-000161301.title: Wir sind Kinder dieser Erde
2023-1-AT01-KA210-SCH-000161301.summary:
<< Background >>

We aimed to raise awareness among children about environmental and climate protection and to show them ways to act responsibly with resources, animals and people. Each school contributed its strengths: the Austrian school as a "Healthy and "Water School," and the Croatian school as part of the international eco-school network. This diversity created a valuable foundation for intercultural and professional collaboration. At the elementary school in Vienna, where many pupils come from socially disadvantaged families, there was a great need for targeted environmental education. Our goal was to provide these children with knowledge and skills they could pass on to their families. In Croatia, there is also room for development in implementing European environmental standards, and schools can serve as role models. We wanted to promote European values such as inclusion, diversity, and tolerance. Our pupils benefit from instruction in multiple native languages, which supports language development and intercultural understanding. During the visits, children learned about different school systems and life realities—contributing to their personal development. Our project aimed to encourage teachers to establish international collaborations.

<< Objectives >>

With our project, we aimed to bring together teachers and students from different countries to explore our shared habitat—the Earth—from various perspectives and to develop a global awareness for environmental protection. By engaging with the biological diversity in these countries, we sought to strengthen understanding and promote a mindful approach to the environment. A central goal was to learn from each other and to gain new ideas for teaching and everyday school life through exchange. The diversity of education systems offered the opportunity to discover and incorporate new methods, thereby expanding both students’ and teachers’ professional and personal skills. The project also supported language development: children could be taught in their native language while English was used as a common language to enhance communication skills. Erasmus served as a bridge between cultures and education systems, providing enriching international experiences and fostering sustainable environmental awareness, intercultural competence, and personal growth.

<< Implementation >>

In the first half-year, we focused on the activity Getting to Know the Countries, during which our project logo, theme song, and mascot were created. The pupils learned about the partner countries through creative contributions such as e-books, Padlets, pinboards, and games. In the second half-year, the emphasis was on the topic of Environment. We explored "Handling Wast–Turning Old into New," where the pupils learned to sort waste properly and became waste professionals themselves. We compared life in cities and on the countryside and developed actions related to Sustainability. The third half-year centered on World Children's Day and the Partnership with People with Limited Opportunities. To the World Children's Day, the schools organized workshops on children's rights. There were collaborations with various groups; Austria addressed homelessness and elderly people, while Croatia worked with children from a special school and seniors to help and bring joy to these groups. In the final half-year, we dedicated ourselves to the topics of Animal Protection and Proper Animal Care and Therapy Animals. Over the two years, four school visits took place, along with monthly online meetings that further enriched exchange and collaboration.

<< Results >>

Our project is documented on the eTwinning platform, featuring detailed descriptions, photos, links to e-books, videos, meeting recordings, and other materials. For each phase, digital presentations were created using Canva, providing a structured overview of activities and results. Each school designed its own Padlet, which was published on the school websites and made accessible to partner schools, allowing students, teachers, and parents to have continuous insight into the project. A shared project logo was designed, professionally implemented, and used on T-shirts, bags, posters, and all project materials. The project song, "We Are Children of This Earth," was rehearsed in multiple languages, recorded in a sound studio, and performed. A rescued street dog became the mascot, named "Flipi," which was graphically designed and incorporated into our e-books. For each activity, initial and final evaluations were conducted. Numerous e-books were created using Book Creator. Additionally, both analog and digital games were developed. Our school visits were documented in diaries, photo books, and videos. There were also informational events for teachers and reports published in the local press.

2023-1-BG01-KA210-SCH-000153690.title: Mathfluencers
2023-1-BG01-KA210-SCH-000153690.summary:
<< Background >>

According to PISA results, the underachievement rate exceeded 30% in Romania (46.6%), Bulgaria (44.4%), and Croatia (31.2%).
Students are engrossed in social media and spend a significant amount of time online. Even in classrooms, it has been observed that some students are often busy tweeting or using Facebook during lectures.
The solution we propose is the use of social media as a learning tool.
Our innovation bridges students' desires (spending time on social media) with their need to improve mathematics literacy and academic achievement.
Our target group consists of high school teachers (ISCED 3).
Needs:
Embedding social media tools in education requires a shift in the role of teachers, who must act as guides and mentors, enabling and facilitating self-regulated learning processes.
There is a lack of didactic methodologies, toolsets, and training programs for teachers that would facilitate this transition and enable them to assume this new role.
There is a need for valid pedagogical concepts and methods for learning with social media. New approaches to support teachers, learners, and administrators are essential.


<< Objectives >>

The aim is to revolutionize the way students perceive mathematics by fostering a genuine appreciation for the subject through the use of social media, ultimately leading to improved math literacy and higher academic achievement.
The objective is to equip teachers with the knowledge and skills needed to effectively integrate social media into their teaching. Additionally, the project aims to develop training programs for teachers on creating engaging and impactful social media content related to mathematics.
Specific Goals: Equip teachers with the knowledge and skills to effectively use social media to create engaging content, empower teachers to innovate and be creative in using social media for education, leverage social media to create interactive learning activities that reinforce mathematical concepts, including principles, formulas, and real-world applications.
Objectives: Develop training program for teachers on creating impactful and engaging social media content related to mathematics. Through the project’s outcomes, provide professional development opportunities and equip educators with tools to enhance their classroom instruction.

<< Implementation >>

The main activity was bridging students' wants (spending time on social media) and needs for increasing levels of mathematics literacy and academic achievement.
To reach this, we did:
Exploration of ways to create influential social media content related to math - Reported on current stats, identified gaps, and documented good practices.
Creation of social media clubs and spaces and engaging content related to math – pages and profiles on the most popular social media platforms. We periodically published content related to mathematics and collected feedback from teachers and students. Based on the feedback, we improved the content.
We analyzed all surveys to conduct an in-depth analysis of the results, based on which we created training for teachers.
Development of teachers' training - Developed the content - Created and implemented effective lesson plans for using social media to increase math literacy.
Piloted teacher training at participating schools and updated the program.
Produced the final version of the training concept and design.
Translated the materials into the languages of project partners to ensure broader accessibility and impact.

<< Results >>

The main project results and outcomes are:
Exploration of ways to create influential social media content related to math - Report on current stats, identified gaps, and documented good practices.
Social media clubs and spaces – Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok.
Surveying students and teachers during all phases of implementation to ensure that activities and results bridged needs and wants - surveyed >360 students and >60 teachers in partner countries.
Analysis of the survey results - Report based on analysis of the surveys and feedback received during social media campaigns.
Prepared training for teachers, tested in 3 schools, and translated into partner languages.

2023-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000152891.title: Empowering Digital Literacy for Tomorrow
2023-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000152891.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because, in the 21st century, digital literacy is a key factor. For students to excel academically, they must be proficient in using technology, while teachers must have the necessary skills to effectively integrate technology into their lessons. It is also crucial for the future workforce, as many jobs already require basic digital skills, a trend that is expected to grow. With the rise of digital services, digital literacy is also vital for active participation in society. Furthermore, youth members need to be able to use digital tools and platforms to plan and implement their activities. By applying the knowledge and skills gained, this project hada positive impact on the partners involved and better prepare everyone for the future.

As a result, we believed that this project was essential for equipping students, teachers, and youth association members with the necessary skills and knowledge.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to empower participants with essential digital literacy skills by offering both the knowledge and opportunities necessary to use digital technologies responsibly and effectively. Its primary goal was to enhance participants' digital readiness, resilience, and capacity by focusing on skills development, practical applications in real-world settings, and providing exposure to various ICT tools. Moreover, the project also supported professional development for teachers, helping them integrate technology into their teaching methods. In addition, it sought to raise awareness among participants about the risks associated with cybercrime and the ethical use of technology, ensuring they were well-equipped to navigate the digital landscape safely and responsibly.

<< Implementation >>

Over the course of the 15-month project, a series of four mobilities were planned, each taking place in a different partner country. One of these mobilities, which occurred in Turkey, was exclusively for teachers, educators, and youth leaders, providing them with specialized opportunities for professional development and collaboration. The other mobilities involved a wider range of participants, including pupils from the partner schools, as well as teachers and representatives from the partner NGOs. This approach aimed to foster a collaborative and inclusive environment, where both students and educators could engage in cross-cultural exchanges and share knowledge.

In addition to the physical mobilities, the project also aimed to reach a broader audience by organizing a virtual mobility. This online event, conducted on a dedicated platform, allowed more pupils to participate, ensuring that the project’s impact extended beyond the immediate mobilities. To further amplify the project's outcomes and ensure its sustainability, various dissemination activities were planned. These activities were designed to share the results and experiences of the project with a wider community.

<< Results >>

The project aimed to enhance participants' digital skills, foster greater digital readiness, and promote a deeper understanding of different cultures, all while ensuring improved digital safety and the integration of technology to elevate the quality of education. Teachers were expected to show significant improvements in their digital competences, particularly in how they integrated technology into their teaching methods, making learning more engaging and effective. The project sought to achieve these goals by equipping both educators and students with the tools and knowledge necessary for navigating the digital landscape.

As part of the project’s outcomes, a variety of digital resources and training materials were developed to support the promotion of digital literacy skills. These materials were designed not only to aid in learning but also to serve as tools for sharing knowledge. In addition to training resources, a range of dissemination materials were created, including brochures, posters, websites, and social media accounts. These platforms played a crucial role in spreading awareness about the project's objectives, sharing valuable information, and ensuring the sustainability of its impact by reaching a wide audience.

2023-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000155233.title: what changed-how reflected
2023-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000155233.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the need for greater curiosity-driven learning and balanced subject importance within our education system. We observed that curiosity and intrinsic motivation often played a minor role in traditional classrooms, and we saw an opportunity to create an approach where students could explore and engage with history, art, and humanities actively. Research, like Freeman’s study, had emphasized that curiosity was key to deep, active learning, yet many education systems overlooked this, leading to disengaged students. 
Additionally, subjects like art, literature, and physical education often received less emphasis compared to math and science, despite their critical role in fostering creativity, empathy, and personal growth. By creating a project that highlighted these areas equally, we offered students the chance to develop diverse skills and engage more deeply with their own heritage and society. This project met the dual need for an education that motivated through curiosity and valued all subjects equally, allowing students to develop holistically as critical thinkers, collaborators, and creative problem-solvers.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to foster curiosity-driven learning, encourage balanced subject engagement, and create opportunities for students to explore both local and European history through an interdisciplinary approach. Our primary goal was to help students develop a deeper understanding of significant historical events—both global, like the Industrial Revolution and WWI, and local events specific to each city. By connecting these events to art, literature, and poetry, we wanted students to see history as a living subject that shapes culture, society, and individual perspectives.
We also sought to address the unique needs of students with artistic talents and those facing challenges with concentration, aiming to engage them in meaningful activities that boost motivation and self-expression. Through quizzes, surveys, and collaborative projects, we wanted students to improve critical thinking, teamwork, and digital skills while gaining confidence in their creative abilities. Ultimately, our goal was to create a well-rounded, inclusive educational experience that valued all subjects equally, encouraged intellectual curiosity, and equipped students with tools for lifelong learning and civic engagement.

<< Implementation >>

In our project, we carried out a series of interesting activities focused on historical and cultural research. We started with each partner country preparing assignments before the mobility: we created videos explaining the causes and effects of the Black Death, the Industrial Revolution and the Renaissance, we produced a documentary about its representation in literature, we created an online art gallery of related images, and we created poetry booklets on these topics. During the mobility, students presented their digital projects, worked in mixed national teams and used 3D printers to create objects related to the Black Death, the Industrial Revolution and the Renaissance. We also tasked students with researching local events and their local impact, resulting in digital posters. Our Turkish partner provided guidance for creating lesson plans on the Black Death, the Industrial Revolution and the Renaissance. Visits to museums and workshops on the Black Death, the Industrial Revolution and the Renaissance further deepened students’ learning. In addition, school clubs (literary, painting and poetry) in each partner country organized activities to further explore these topics.   

<< Results >>

The project produced concrete results that enriched students’ knowledge and skills while fostering interdisciplinary learning. Key results included short, informative videos on the causes and consequences of the Black Death, the Industrial Revolution and the Renaissance, a documentary film highlighting protagonists in literature related to the Black Death, the Industrial Revolution and the Renaissance, an online art gallery with detailed information about paintings depicting the period, and 3D printed objects inspired by historical themes. The school clubs (literary, painting and poetry) also produced a wealth of materials related to these themes.
