2023-1-NL01-KA210-SCH-000153894.title: Seeking Justice: From Nuremberg to The Hague
2023-1-NL01-KA210-SCH-000153894.summary:
<< Background >>

The "Seeking Justice" project was developed in response to a significant gap in citizenship and history education across Europe concerning international justice mechanisms. While many curricula include the Nuremberg Trials, there is limited attention given to contemporary justice processes such as those of the International Criminal Court (ICC). This gap has become especially pressing in light of ongoing conflicts, where issues such as war crimes and crimes against humanity have resurfaced in public discourse. The project addresses the need for secondary school teachers and students to better understand how societies respond to serious crimes through international law. It also aims to demystify the concepts of justice and the rule of law, making them more accessible to young people. The project helps schools promote civic engagement and a deeper appreciation of human rights and democratic values across different European contexts.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to empower secondary school teachers and students with a deeper understanding, methods, and intrinsic interest to engage critically with the concept and practice of international justice. By exploring how societies address serious crimes such as war crimes and crimes against humanity, we envisioned the project to bridge a gap between historical education and contemporary global issues. We promoted critical thinking and debate, human rights education, empathy, and inspired active citizenship and strengthened the European identity through experiential learning. Specifically, the project aimed to: (1) develop an easily approachable, time-saving Toolkit on international justice; (2) promote the Seeking Justice educational model; (3) build transnational networks among educators and learners; and (4) support schools in incorporating international justice into their curricula.

<< Implementation >>

The project's activities began with a 2-day in-person seminar for teachers in The Hague (February 26-27, 2024), which was followed by a 4-day in-person workshop for students (April 08-11, 2024). To broaden participation, we also organised virtual 2-day seminars for teachers and students across Europe (September 18-19 and October 14-16, 2024). A central component was the co-creation and testing of a Toolkit for educators based on the model of the project's face-to-face programme, developed with input from project participants and piloted in classrooms in Croatia and the Netherlands. The project also included regular online coordination meetings, formative and summative evaluations, and dissemination activities.

<< Results >>

The main output of the project was a freely accessible, online Educational Toolkit designed to support secondary school teachers in addressing topics related to international justice. The Toolkit includes background materials, classroom activities, and guidance for using resources such as live-streamed ICC trials. It was co-created with input from teachers and students and pilot tested in schools in Croatia and the Netherlands. It is available in 3 languages (English, Croatian and Dutch).

The project also delivered impactful learning experiences through in-person and virtual seminars. Teachers gained confidence and practical strategies for teaching and organising trips about justice and human rights, while students deepened their understanding of international law and civic responsibility. The project also raised awareness of the ICC’s work and the role of peace and justice NGOs, particularly in post-conflict societies.

We also have a growing network of interested educators and aspiring students, which we aim to develop into communities of practice in the future.
topics: Human rights and rule of law

2023-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000152267.title: Social Inclusion With Sport
2023-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000152267.summary:
<< Background >>

One of the most important problems for immigrants is identity conflict. After some time, they begin to feel that they do not belong to their own country or to the country in which they live. Sport has a unifying power and brings people together.  Team sports games can help build new relationships based on trust and acceptance, break stereotypes and overcome conflicts.
Sport encourages refugees to work together towards a common goal. The collective energy of sport can be therapeutic, transformative and healing. Our partners from Croatia and Hungary already have experience in this field, and we schools from Poland and Turkey wanted to benefit from their knowledge and promote equality through mixed sports activities.
Increasing the number of Erasmus+ school-based educational projects related to migrants and refugees in Europe can increase participants' knowledge and awareness about migration and create a pan-European network of teachers, trainers, trainers and sports staff who work in Erasmus+ projects related to migrants and refugees.

<< Objectives >>

The "Social Inclusion With Sport" project promoted social integration. through sport among people from various social groups, including ethnic minorities, people with disabilities, and people from difficult backgrounds. We have strengthened:
•social integration, sport brought together people from different social groups, cultures and environments, showed that they can meet, cooperate and develop their passions together, build bonds and a sense of belonging
•social competences, such as teamwork, communication, responsibility and self-discipline, 
• interpersonal skills, such as communication, cooperation in groups, teamwork in a sports context, the ability to face challenges
• health promotion. lifestyle, sport can be an important element in encouraging physical activity as a way to improve physical and mental health 
• talents, sport is an opportunity to discover and support sports talents among people from various backgrounds, giving them a chance to develop in sports
•promotion of equal opportunities, everyone, regardless of origin, social status or physical limitations, has the right to participate in social and sports life.
• educating society about the problems of social exclusion, we showed how sport can contribute to solvin

<< Implementation >>

There were two virtual meetings (starting and final meetings), sports tournaments with all partners and 3 mobilities. The first one took place in Płock, Poland with 3 employees (physical education teachers, sports staff, coaches) from each partner. The second mobility took place in Budapest, Hungary with 4 students and 2 physical education teachers, coaches from Poland, Croatia and Turkey.  The third mobility took place in Zagreb, Croatia with 4 students and 2 physical education teachers from Poland, Croatia and Turkey. We also held face-to-face meetings with families to support them before and during the various mobilities.

<< Results >>

The "Social Inclusion With Sport" project aimed to promote social integration through sport, especially in relation to marginalized groups. We have shown that sport promotes tolerance, solidarity and many other sporting and European values, such as:
• development of interpersonal skills, as participants learned cooperation, communication and teamwork, which promotes social integration;
• improved physical health, as regular participation in sports has shown that it can lead to improvements in the physical condition and overall health of participants;
• an increase in self-confidence, as participants gained confidence in overcoming their own limitations;
• community building, because through the project we contributed to the creation of stronger social bonds in local communities, which favors integration;
• education about equality and diversity, as participation in the project led to greater awareness of problems related to discrimination and equality;
• cooperation with local organizations, because thanks to the project the partners were able to establish cooperation with local sports clubs, schools and other organizations, which strengthens the community.

2023-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000158725.title: Water, Air, Soil - What is your Superpower?
2023-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000158725.summary:
<< Background >>

The implementation of the project ‘Water, Air, Soil - What is your Superpower?’, addresses the growing need to increase environmental awareness among young people and develop STEM skills. The project addresses the challenges of increasing environmental degradation by promoting pro-environmental attitudes, active citizenship and action for local communities. We recognised the need to equip students with knowledge about the dangers of a consumerist lifestyle and practical skills to use modern technology (drones, robots) to investigate air, water and soil quality.

In addition, the project supports social inclusion by offering equal opportunities to students from different backgrounds. It enables international cooperation, the development of language and scientific competences and integration into local communities through panel discussions with experts, authorities, local residents, as well as students from other schools. We want the knowledge and experience gained to have a real impact on environmental action, contributing to positive local and global change.

<< Objectives >>

In implementing the project ‘Water, Air, Soil - What is your Superpower?’, we wanted to achieve several key objectives. First and foremost, we wanted to raise environmental awareness among young people and foster attitudes of environmental responsibility. Students were not only to learn about the dangers of air, water and soil pollution, but also to learn how to analyse and counteract them in practice.

Another aim was to develop STEM skills through the use of modern technologies, such as drones and robots, in environmental research, which supports the development of competences useful for non-formal education and future careers.

We also wanted to support the return to active social life after the isolation associated with the COVID-19 pandemic, with the project creating a space for face-to-face collaboration, sharing experiences and rebuilding peer relationships that were restricted during the pandemic.

We also sought to promote social inclusion, international integration and inspire local communities to take action to protect the environment.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project ‘Water, Air, Soil - What is your Superpower?’, we realised three key international mobilities:

‘POWER is all around us’ (Poland) - students investigated air pollution using a professional drone. The results were analysed and compiled by the students and shared with the school community and local authorities .

‘Water World’ (Portugal) - activities focused on water management. Participants, using equipment provided from the University of Aveiro laboratory analysed water quality in different locations and presented the results at a meeting with scientists and the community.

‘From Garbage to Garden’ (Croatia) - students investigated soil pollution and also learned about soil management by visiting the Institute of Adriatic Cultures and Reclamation of Karst Areas, where interactive exercises and lectures were held.

In addition, we carried out activities to promote the project as well as monitoring and evaluation, which allowed us to assess the effects and adapt the activities to the needs of the participants.

<< Results >>

The project ‘Water, Air, Soil - What is your Superpower?’ at the M. Skłodowska-Curie High School No. 1 in Ostrzeszów was successful in raising the environmental awareness of students and teachers. As part of activities carried out in Poland, Portugal and Croatia, participants studied water, soil and air quality, learnt about modern environmental technologies and exchanged experiences. Pupils took part in lectures at universities, workshops and practical activities.

As a result of these activities, the students prepared proposals for pro-environmental measures for local authorities, incorporating ideas from different countries. From Poland - supporting the replacement of cookers with modern heating devices, promoting RES, expanding cycling infrastructure, among others. From Portugal - saving water, protecting water ecosystems and promoting sustainable agricultural practices. From Croatia - investing in the protection of soil and its biodiversity, supporting measures for sustainable agriculture and monitoring soil health with drones.

The project has significantly contributed to increasing youth involvement in environmental protection and international cooperation, providing an impetus for environmental action at the local level.

2023-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000160452.title: All we need is green!
2023-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000160452.summary:
<< Background >>

 
Climate change and environmental degradation pose a threat to Europe and the entire world. Actions to protect the environment and combat global warming should be a priority in every sphere of human life. By implementing this project, we wanted to develop and strengthen the ecological attitudes of students, parents, and the local community. Another goal was to find ways to use waste, reduce its production and energy consumption, and implement among students, and through them also parents and the local environment, an attitude of care for the environment and combating climate change. We also felt the need to strengthen digital competences and raise the level of education through the exchange of experiences at the European level.

<< Objectives >>

“All we need is green!” aimed to encourage students, teachers, and anyone interested in the topic of sustainable development to implement simple steps to raise ecological awareness, which engaged them as responsible citizens in actively changing their environmental habits for the better. The planned activities included meetings with partners, joint work on solving institutional problems, and promotion of good environmental practices. The activities culminated in the “Eco Revolution” event, aimed at popularizing our ideas among the local community with the participation of local authorities and the support of experts. Our goal was also to develop key competences of students and digital skills of students and teachers, so that they serve sustainable development.

<< Implementation >>

All planned activities were carried out in the project:
1. Partner meeting in Poland - establishing the principles of cooperation, schedule of activities, assignment of duties, workshop preparation of teachers - project participants - for using IT tools in communication, implementation of activities, and development of project results in work with students.

2. Project activity within the mobility in Croatia on the topic of sustainable food, under the slogan "You are what you eat". Indicating to participants the need to make appropriate food choices and selection of packaging, aimed at reducing the amount of waste.

3. Project activity during the mobility to Portugal, the aim of which was to make participants aware of the need to apply the 5R principle in ecology - refuse, reduce, reuse, recycle, rot.

4. Project activity during the mobility in Poland under the slogan of energy efficiency "Keep unplugged" and Eco Revolution - a happening using previous activities with the promotion of a pro-ecological attitude among the residents of the city,  and community of the school.
5. Promotional and dissemination activities - seminar in Poland, meeting with experts on ecological problems, and summary of the project.

<< Results >>

The increase in students' ecological awareness, cooperation skills, exchange of experiences, the knowledge about the ecological threats to our planet of all project participants resulted in the creation of specific products proving the achievement of the results planned during the activities. These are recordings, photos, the videos documenting the work on the project, as well as specific results of students' work using the acquired digital competences, but not only. 2023-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000153970.title: Digital Education for Innovation in School
2023-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000153970.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project as we wanted to address the problems each school faced: they had logistics and technology, but teachers used it seldom; students were not interested in learning; classes were not motivating and interesting for students; early school leaving and absenteeism were high; no opportunities for cooperation. 
This project enabled teachers to integrate technology in their lessons for real, making students interested and motivated to attend and graduate school. Students and teachers discovered their partners’ culture and educational system, developed and improved creativity and critical thinking by creating, studying and working together with their partners. 
The teachers learned to create digital teaching materials, adapted to their and their students' real needs, used new technology, learned by practicing, developed their creativity and problem-solving skills, worked in mixed international teams, developed collaborative and communication skills in English, enhanced students’ motivation and improved their learning outcomes. 
The students used technology for learning, improved their communication skills in English, met new people, developed and improved their general knowledge about these countries and EU.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives we aimed at were: 
- to develop and improve the digital skills for 15 teachers in three European schools, by increasing the number of classes using digital tools and resources at 80%, so that they could deliver more interesting and motivating lessons for their students; 
- to develop and improve 75 students’ motivation and interest in learning, so as to increase their learning results by 10% and their school attendance at 100%; 
- to set-up a real and working collaborative network among 3 European schools, to carry out all the activities of the project, and to develop and create 1 common digital resource to be used during and after the end of the project.
We wanted to offer teachers and students the opportunity to collaborate, to learn by exchanging good-practice examples, share experience and ideas in order to create, use and take advantage of innovative and modern teaching and learning techniques involving technology, and to develop their digital skills and key competences. We wanted the digital component of the education in these schools to be developed and improved, and new practices and resources to be created and integrated into daily activities by teachers.

<< Implementation >>

The activities implemented in our project were:
1. Transnational project meeting in Romania at Lorin Salagean Technical High School, 11-15 December 2023. 2 teachers from Croatia, 2 teachers from Slovakia. 
2. Training for teachers in Croatia at Gimnazija Metkovic, 5-11 February 2024. 5 teachers from Romania, 4 teachers from Slovakia. 
3. Workshop for students in Slovakia at SOSE Trnava, 25-31 March 2024. 4 students and 2 teachers from Romania, 4 students and 2 teachers from Croatia. 
4. Creating the digital resource, online, 1-31 May 2024. Once a week, 15 teachers met online to discuss the progress of the resource and to share ideas and good-practice examples 
5. Summer Camp for students in Romania, Croatia and Slovakia, organized in each partner school, 1-5 July 2024. 26 students from Romania, 29 students from Croatia, 25 students from Slovakia, and 30 teachers (15 teachers, 5 teachers/ school, project team members and 15 teachers, 5 teachers/ school, who assisted the classes). 
6. Final dissemination event in Romania at Lorin Salagean Technical High School, 12-16 May 2025. 2 teachers from Croatia, 2 teachers from Slovakia. 
7. Project management activities, online and in-person, 01.12.2023-31.05.2025.

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs: 1 digital resource for students created by 15 teachers in the 3 partner schools; 1 teacher’s book accompanying the digital resource for students; 1 webpage of the project; social media profiles of the project (Facebook and Instagram); the blog of the project; the official logo of the project; presentations; common Google Drive.
Other results: plans of the project (communication, implementation, dissemination, (self-) evaluation, monitoring); 1 transnational project meeting organized; 1 training workshop for teachers organized; 1 workshop for students organized; 1 summer camp for students organized in each country; dissemination events.  
Intangible results: 15 teachers use technology 80% more in their current activity; 80 students were 100% involved in the activities of the project; 80 students have 10% better learning results and 100% better school attendance; 15 teachers and 80 students broadened their horizons, developed their digital and communication skills in English; 80 students gained knowledge about other countries; the images of the schools in the local communities improved; the project team is 100% more confident and learned how to better manage a transnational project.

2023-1-SK01-KA210-SCH-000164572.title: Majstri techniky - manuálne zručnosti sú na nezaplatenie
2023-1-SK01-KA210-SCH-000164572.summary:
<< Background >>

There is a lot of talk about the shortage of skilled, creative young people in the labor market who are willing to become masters – craftsmen – and replace those retiring. We at SEA participated as guests in the "Modelarska Liga" competition in Croatia, where we saw children aged 8 to 14 from elementary schools enthusiastically competing in creating wooden products on small machining tools. The competition focused on developing technical skills and promoting inclusivity, as teams of children with special needs were also given the opportunity to compete on equal terms. We wanted to bring such a competition to Slovakia.

Our first step was to inspire technology teachers with this idea. Therefore, we asked our Croatian colleagues to share their experiences with us. We also approached colleagues from Slovenia, where the situation is similar, to form an international team. This is how the project was born, which we wanted to continue with an international competition.

All three organizations have experience in informal education and organizing workshops for teachers in our countries, but we lacked experience with an international project. We wanted to try it out, gain visibility abroad, and open the door to international cooperation.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to use the experience of Croatian teachers to train 10 technology teachers from Slovakia and 10 from Slovenia. This would help them involve children from marginalized groups, refugees, children with disabilities, and girls in working with small machining tools during lessons or after-school clubs. The goal was to improve their skills and open up more opportunities in the labor market.

Through this project, we wanted to show that informal education in technology can be fun and accessible to a wide group of children. However, for this to succeed, teachers need to be inspired – which is why we trained them. Since competitions are a great motivational tool in informal education, we chose to use them as well. We planned to organize national rounds of the Masters of Technology competition in Slovakia, Slovenia, and Croatia, so teachers and their teams could compare results.

With this project, all three organizations aimed to improve our skills in international teamwork, gain experience with an EU project, and raise awareness among foreign organizations with similar goals.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented 9 activities: 
1. Governance and financial management
2. Project promotion
3. Recruitment of teachers for the project
4. Teacher training
5. Creation of educational materials
6. Project kick-off workshop
7. National Masters of Technology competition in Croatia
8. National Masters of Technology Competition in Slovakia
9. National Masters of Technology Competition in Slovenia

<< Results >>

The specific outputs and outcomes of our project were:

1. We trained 10 teachers from Slovakia and 10 from Slovenia, guided by 10 teacher-trainers from Croatia, to engage children from the target group in non-formal education in Techniques and help them improve their basic skills.

2. We organized national Masters of Technology competitions in Slovakia, Slovenia, and Croatia, where healthy children, children with special needs, those from marginalized groups, and girls competed in teams on equal terms.

3. We created web site and educational materials in four languages (Croatian, Slovak, Slovenian, and English), including 22 worksheets with tasks, exercises, and methodological procedures, as well as 11 instructional videos for working with small machine tools—all freely available on the project website (LINK TO WEB).

4. We established the foundation for sustainable national competitions in all three countries and prepared for an international Masters of Technology competition, with potential for expanding to other European countries.

5. As a participating organization, we gained valuable experience working in an international team and project.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2023-2-AT01-KA210-SCH-000179533.title: "Orchesterstudien" - Grundlagen und Methoden für erfolgreiche internationale Jugendorchesterarbeit
2023-2-AT01-KA210-SCH-000179533.summary:
<< Background >>

In recent years, the Johann Joseph Fux Conservatory has established itself as an institution that organises major orchestral projects and as a centre for international endeavours within the Styrian music school landscape. This has given rise to the idea of expanding orchestral activities to include international collaborations on the one hand and, on the other, to draw important insights from these projects, which can then be made available to other music schools and conservatories as a guide and motivation. International co-operation should not simply be started ‘blindly’, but should be very targeted. It was therefore very important to find out the ‘dos’ and ‘don'ts’ in this area. These serve the further ‘orchestral endeavours’ of the conservatory and the Styrian music schools, but also the partner institutions in the Alpe-Adria region and beyond. The main beneficiaries will be music school directors, teachers, but also pupils and parents.

<< Objectives >>

The project should answer the following basic questions: What are the benefits of international co-operation in youth orchestras? Why should an orchestra be founded across national borders at all? To what extent do directors, teachers and pupils benefit from this? What is actually necessary for an international project to work well? And what can we learn from it? What processes take place within an international youth orchestra? Are there differences between the nations, including between the genders? These questions were always at the forefront during the preparation, rehearsal phases and concerts of the newly founded ‘Youth Orchestra Alpe Adria’. 

<< Implementation >>

In order to create a comprehensible and tested guideline for future international youth orchestra projects, an exemplary project - the Youth Orchestra Alpe Adria - was needed, which was accompanied by a study consisting of three detailed questionnaires. The participating musicians were asked to answer questions on the categories ‘nervousness/pressure’, ‘organisation’, ‘cooperation with musical directors’ and ‘community and network’ before the start of the project, during the rehearsal week and after the project was completed, and to give their honest feedback. In order to develop these questionnaires as practically as possible, discussions were held in advance with students, graduates and professors from Graz University of the Arts. The intention of the project was analysed from all sides and it was possible to develop relevant and in-depth questions as the basis for the study. At the same time, it was also decided when the questionnaires should be distributed to the musicians during the course of the concert project. 
The project programme consisted of a registration and selection phase, a rehearsal phase and three concerts at home and abroad. The first concert took place in Graz, the others in Slovenia and Italy. 



<< Results >>

The main motives for taking part were their own musical development, familiarisation with new repertoire, the project as an addition to their own artistic CV and collaboration with renowned conductors. 

After the intensive rehearsal period, the instrumental skills improved.  

The team spirit, the making of new friends and the positive effect of the community on dealing with nervousness and pressure are particularly noteworthy. 

Joint team-building activities are essential in a project for these age groups. Particular care must be taken when selecting the right musical director for a youth orchestra. When planning the rehearsal week, a sufficient number of sectional rehearsals, appropriately intensive work with the conductor and free time must be balanced. 

The choice of concertmaster must be carefully considered in advance. Changing the concertmaster is a ‘no-go’. 

Even if the change was a major challenge, working with different conductors and their individual language trained the musicians in self-management and adaptability. 

Several musicians reported a strengthening of their self-confidence and their own seriousness as musicians. 

Others reported more patience, social openness and respect for other cultures.

2023-2-EE01-KA210-SCH-000185056.title: What's Out There
2023-2-EE01-KA210-SCH-000185056.summary:
<< Background >>

In light of recent curriculum changes in Estonia, the importance of cross-curricular approaches in general education has significantly increased. As a basic schools, us and our project partners frequently observe our students struggling to connect academic learning with practical, real-life applications. While students require continuous support and motivation to engage meaningfully with their studies and to really learn effectively, teachers need to deepen their understanding of modern educational resources and teaching methodologies. 

Our school is located on an island, where the surrounding natural environment plays a vital role in our daily lives. As educators, we aim to instill in our students a strong appreciation for the value of a clean and healthy environment, and to inspire them to take an active role in its preservation. Environmental education is not only relevant to our local context but also serves as a unifying theme among all project partners, each representing a coastal country.

With these shared goals and challenges in mind, initiating this project felt like a meaningful and worthwhile endeavor.

<< Objectives >>

The project integrated themes of environmental awareness, innovative teaching and learning practices, and healthy lifestyles, aiming to foster competence building, providing experience with diverse environmental and cultural contexts, and enhancing the effeciency of teaching and learning. We expected the involved students to improve their knowledge on natural sciences and environment, as well as to raise their motivation to see the link between learning and real life, and teachers to gain insights for designing and implementing cross-curricular studies in the field of natural sciences. 

We relied on international partnerships to provide fresh perspectives and explore new approaches—it's often invigorating to see how others operate, as it helps us re-evaluate and refine our own methodologies. 

For both students and teachers, the international collaboration was intended to broaden horizons on both personal and academic levels. It also aimed to encourage more confident interaction with peers and colleagues, not only for social engagement but also for academic cooperation. 

<< Implementation >>

During the project both international and local activities took place, eTwinning was used in parallel as a platform for sharing and preserving memories and experiences throughout the project.

Four international study sessions - one to each partner school- were implemented involving students and teachers from all partner schools. Additionally, all the participating schools implemented local  activities in their schools and/or communities to promote environmental consciousness, effective learning/teaching practices, and healthy living and attitudes. 

There were on-going activities taking place in each project partner school over the course of the project such as photographing the cycles of nature around the school, measuring the rainfall, and carrying out activities around school gardens. 

Twice during the project international video conferences were held, bringing together students and teachers from all four partner schools. These meetings helped keep the project topic alive and maintained student engagement throughout the process.

As a result of the project, the involved schools developed examples of cross-curricular teaching modules in the field of natural sciences, as well as tested the teaching modules with their students. 

<< Results >>

Tangible results:
- A dedicated eTwinning TwinSpace page was created, showcasing the range of activities carried out by all partner schools.
- Four international study sessions were organized- one to each partner school- forming the core of the project’s experiential learning component.
- Local level activities were implemented in participating schools, and ongoing online collaboration kept up to ensure continuous engagement and focus.
- Cross-curricular teaching modules in the field of natural sciences were developed for enriching the curriculum and actively engaging students, latter also offering lasting value to educators beyond the project.

The cooperation between the four EU partner schools fostered a network for long-term collaboration. It supported the sharing of best practices, mutual learning, and increased institutional capacity to implement further interdisciplinary and international projects.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2023-2-FR01-KA210-SCH-000176300.title: ETHICS
2023-2-FR01-KA210-SCH-000176300.summary:
<< Background >>

This ETHICS project was an innovative way to help students improve their skills and competencies and feel more confident at school and in their lives.
Indeed, between the last 2 PISA evaluations, reports reveal no progress in reading for our two countries since the previous evaluation (only within OCDE average results), as well as a persistent lack of efficiency in teamwork. Digital literacy isn't at a higher level. Although students are familiar with new technologies, they do not necessarily know how to use them constructively for their studies or future professional lives. Furthermore, personal and transversal skills such as entrepreneurship,  teamwork, problem-solving and creativity are not necessarily developed through traditional school activities. 
The PISA report also indicates that self-confidence and cooperation are declining among students. They feel more anxious, less open-minded towards diversity and more prone to bullying. We can observe in our schools that the COVID period increased these feelings.
Another point is some of our students get fewer opportunities (rural areas, health problems, modest family background). They mix with difficulties with the others.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of our ETHICS project was for our students to DEVELOP A COMMON SET OF COMPETENCIES (core competencies and transversal skills, our main priority), all of them being part of the Key competencies defined by the European Parliament as essential for lifelong learning. Developing their skills and competencies helped them to become more self-confident and plan an ambitious future.
The other objective, linked to priorities "Inclusion and diversity" and "Participation in democratic life, common values and civic engagement", especially for the part "Common values" was FOSTER TOLERANCE, which means:
- Develop open-mindedness of our students
-Foster a sense of inclusion among the members of our educational community (students, teachers, parents, etc.).
That's why we chose a topic inspired by the European motto “United in Diversity” about EUROPEAN VALUES to develop their feeling of being part of a group (of a school, of a country, of Europe).
We wanted them to understand that the EU has been built on a shared basis, as emphasised in the Treaty of Lisbon, with a common cultural heritage. 


<< Implementation >>

We implemented seven common activities: three virtual activities, two physical activities, and two activities to create common exhibitions.
A1 (Creation and choice of a common logo): helped students to get involved in the project and feel a rightful member of it.
A2 (European Common Culture Exhibition): Each school participated in creating posters for a common exhibition to acquire knowledge about European foundations and the origins of their values.
A3 (Writing of the song): students collaborated to write the lyrics of a common song about European values.
A4 (Performing of the Song): in Croatia, they practised together to sing this common song during an event.
A5 (Values in Sports Exhibition): Each school participated in creating posters to describe the implementation of European values in Sports.
A6 (Values in sports and day-to-day life): Students discussed their positive experiences with implementing values in sports, day-to-day life, and Erasmus+ projects.
A7 (Inclusive sports competition): sports in mixed groups: Croatian, French, disabled students and adults.

<< Results >>

OUTCOMES:
-> Progress in the acquisition of skills and competencies:
Through the activities, we measured and observed improvements at several levels:
Teamwork, the drive to do research, to read, English language (written and oral communication), and digital competencies.
-> Positive evolution in the knowledge of the European common culture, at the origin of the European values (we will focus on Human Rights, Human Dignity, Equality and Freedom) measured by comparing the answers of two questionnaires.
→ Positive evolution of tolerance and the inclusion feeling measured by comparing the answers to questionnaires.
PRODUCTIONS
-> A committed common song, written by students and inspired by European values, performed during an event.
-> Success in the organization of an event, an inclusive sports competition, as some values are shared by both sports and the European Union: Equality and respect, which also means fairness, inclusion, and freedom to practise.

2023-2-FR01-KA210-SCH-000180719.title: Les écoles européennes avec le pouvoir inclusif de la musique.
2023-2-FR01-KA210-SCH-000180719.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we wanted to address several key challenges observed in our schools. One of the main issues was peer bullying, which negatively affects students’ well-being, self-esteem and academic success, sometimes leading to absenteeism or dropout.
We also identified a lack of motivation among students, learning difficulties, and limited social inclusion, especially for those from disadvantaged backgrounds. At the same time, teachers needed more innovative and engaging methods to support diverse learners.
Another important need was to promote multilingualism, intercultural awareness and European values such as tolerance and cooperation. Many students had few opportunities to interact with peers from other countries or to use English in real-life situations.
Through this project, we aimed to create a more inclusive, motivating and supportive learning environment by using music as a tool to foster collaboration, creativity and communication.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to improve students’ well-being, motivation and academic engagement by creating a more inclusive and supportive school environment. One of our main objectives was to prevent and reduce peer bullying by developing students’ social skills, empathy and sense of belonging.
We also wanted to promote inclusion, especially for students with fewer opportunities, by giving them the chance to participate in international experiences and collaborative activities.
Another key objective was to enhance students’ language skills, particularly in English, while fostering intercultural awareness and European values such as tolerance, respect and cooperation.
In addition, we aimed to use music as an innovative teaching tool to encourage creativity, teamwork and active participation. Finally, we sought to support teachers by sharing good practices and developing new pedagogical approaches through international cooperation.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented a wide range of collaborative and student-centred activities during the project. These included interventions and workshops on preventing peer bullying, where students and teachers explored strategies such as restorative practices and awareness-raising.
Students actively participated in music-based activities, such as creating original songs, performing, and learning traditional dances. They also worked in groups to analyse songs, create posters, instruments and present their work.
Cultural activities were an essential part of the project, including visits, intercultural exchanges and a final concert involving all participants. Students were hosted by peers, which strengthened their intercultural understanding.
Teachers collaborated to design lesson plans, share good practices and upload resources.
Finally, evaluation activities, reports, and dissemination through eTwinning, videos and publications ensured the visibility and impact of the project.

<< Results >>

The project produced several concrete outputs and meaningful results. Students created original songs, performed in concerts and developed artistic productions such as posters. Teachers collaboratively designed lesson plans integrating music into teaching, which were shared as examples of good practice.
We also developed an eTwinning TwinSpace to share resources, as well as evaluation reports, newsletters, podcasts, photos and videos to document and disseminate the project. Certificates of participation were delivered.
Beyond these tangible results, the project had a strong impact on participants. Students improved their English language skills, creativity, self-confidence and teamwork abilities. Their intercultural awareness and openness to European values increased significantly.
Importantly, the project contributed to reducing peer bullying, increasing students’ motivation to learn and strengthening their engagement with school, thus helping to prevent early school leaving.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2023-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000180505.title: U šumi kao u učionici
2023-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000180505.summary:
<< Background >>

The main aim was to encourage the development of forest pedagogy (FP) in Croatia and Slovenia and to strengthen the capacities of those who will implement FP in practice. We entered the project together with partners with whom we already had established cooperation in the field of FP; the Open University Gospic where the MF Istria held a training on forest pedagogy, and with the kindergarten from Pazin and the primary school from Buzet where we have conducted workshops with children in the forest. All of the aforementioned institutions have shown a strong desire to continue cooperation in the field of forest pedagogy through joint projects that will develop this concept in Croatia. Through joint cooperation, we respond to the need for the development of structured education in forest pedagogy for educational experts and others interested in implementing FP in own work with children. In order to have a strong foothold in theory and practice, we invited the Forestry Institute of Slovenia into partnership, an experienced partner in implementing forest education, as they have already published several manuals and conducted workshops with children and adults. MF Istria has already collaborated with them within EU FP group.

<< Objectives >>

The objective was to primarily educate educational experts on the methods of work in forest pedagogy that they will further implement in their work with children. We intend to raise awareness of the importance of FP for the healthy development of children and to introduce project partners (PPs) and the public to all the benefits of forest pedagogy. Existing examples of good practices in forest pedagogy were presented through the project so PPs learned about different approaches and models of implementing FP. There was a knowledge transfer of experienced partners to less experienced in order to strengthen their competences as future forest pedagogues. We organized forest pedagogy seminars not only for PPs but also for external participants. Educational institutions and other interested parties were invited, with the aim of professional development of educators in the field of FP. Through the project, we established a network of forest pedagogues in Croatia and Slovenia and international cooperation as well. Our goal was to jointly initiate the development of structured education and a training for forest pedagogues through the development of training modules and educational materials for education of future forest pedagogues.

<< Implementation >>

Through the project, we carried out 5 activities:
1. International training in forest pedagogy and learning about good practices (27 and 28 March 2024 in Ljubljana)
Lectures and workshops on FP, visits to examples of good practices, a seminar on FP was organized with 25 external participants.
2. Education of future forest pedagogy educators in Istria (22 and 23 May 2024 in Buzet)
50 external participants in the FP seminar. The workshops held by PPs; Forestry Institute and MF Istria members.
Visited examples of good practices in FP.
3. Education of future forest pedagogy educators in Lika (22 and 23 October 2024 in Gospic)
Visited examples of good practices in FP. 10 external participants attended the FP seminar. Workshops held by less experienced PPs that got educated during the project and are strengthening their competencies through practical implementation. Lecture by expert on working with children with developmental disabilities in the application of FP activities.
4. Creation of an e-manual for the education of educators
Composed of 3 chapters; Forestry/ Pedagogy and lifelong learning/ Forest pedagogy.
5. Final project conference in Istria (25 March 2025 in Pazin)
  A FP seminar was held with 80 external participants.

<< Results >>

The project resulted in the following outcomes and results:

- Education and strengthening of the competences of a large number of  teachers and educators who will implement the FP methods in their future work. Around 300 participants educated in the frame of our FP seminars. 
- PPs have integrated gained theoretical and practical knowledge into the work program of their own institutions. A school and a kindergarten initiated a continuous FP program with children as a result od the project activities and an expertise gained in the project.
- An interactive e-manual  "In the Forest as in the Classroom" was created for education of educators in forest pedagogy.            It brings comprehensive knowledge of forestry, pedagogy and forest pedagogy with numerous practical examples for direct implementation.
- The project activities were well covered by the media in Istria, Lika and Slovenia, informing the entire public about the benefits of FP for the healthy development of children and thus contributing to raising awareness about the importance of structured children's play in the forest.
- The project established a network of forest pedagogues in Croatia and Slovenia and strengthened international cooperation of the partners.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
