2023-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000184266.title: NEMOPHILIST ECONUTS FOR GREEN PLANET
2023-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000184266.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was inspired by the slogan "The goal of life is to make your heartbeat match the beat of the universe"; and the need to re-establish the balance between nature and human beings. The application addresses the urgent need to fight climate change, noting that 90% of climate change is caused by humans. It addresses the need to educate the young generation as eco-friendly individuals and the necessity of raising awareness about recycling, citing that 520 kg of waste produced by one person in a year can be recycled. Additionally, it aims to fulfill the "resource efficient Europe"; objective within the EU 2020 Strategy.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives are to: Educate the young generation as eco-friendly individuals conscious of the environment. Prepare a school recycling program to be integrated into the school curriculum. Reduce the carbon footprint by 7% via calculating carbon footprints of partner schools. Raise consciousness across Europe regarding global warming, climate change, and reforestation. Develop participants; digital skills and green skills through web tools and project activities.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented a mix of physical and virtual activities centered on environmental themes: Recycling and Reuse of Waste: An activity in Italy focusing on recycling policies, workshops, and eco-fashion shows. Climate Change: A virtual training event led by the Turkish team involving seminars and workshops. Protection of Environment and Natural Resources: An activity in Türkiye involving visits to wetlands, eco-friendly building workshops, and upcycling. Green Planet with WEB 2.0 Tools: A virtual activity led by Romania to teach digital tools for nature conservation content. Alternative Energy Sources: An activity in Croatia focusing on renewable energy, including building water mills and solar power generation workshops. Continuous Activities: Planting trees, calculating carbon footprints, preparing a project magazine, and designing organic gardens.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs (products) of the project are listed as: 1. School recycling program. 2. Mini Forest Area at schools.
3. Project magazine. 4. Project website. 5. Organic gardens. 6. Carbon footprint report. 7. Nemophilist Econuts organic handbags. Other expected results include raising awareness and consciousness among students about environmental protection, reducing carbon levels at partner schools, and creating behavioral changes towards using natural resources efficiently.

2023-2-HU01-KA210-SCH-000178417.title: Our Planet, Our Heritage
2023-2-HU01-KA210-SCH-000178417.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated to respond to increasing environmental challenges and the growing disconnection between people and nature caused by urbanisation. The partners recognised that reduced contact with the natural environment contributes to issues such as climate change, biodiversity loss, and resource-related problems, therefore there was a strong need to raise environmental awareness among students and teachers.
Another important need was to strengthen the understanding and preservation of cultural and natural heritage, especially UNESCO World Heritage and intangible cultural values, which are often underestimated or treated mainly as tourist attractions.
The project also addressed educational gaps, as topics like Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and environmental studies were not sufficiently integrated into primary education. Therefore, the partners aimed to support teachers with new methodologies and provide students with opportunities to engage in research, problem-solving, and experiential learning.



<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to increase awareness and understanding of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and UNESCO World Heritage among both students and teachers. A key objective was to help participants better understand climate-related problems and encourage them to take responsibility for environmental protection.
Another important goal was to develop participants’ digital, green, and STEM/STEAM skills, while also promoting common values and active engagement in solving ecological and community-related issues. The project also sought to motivate students and teachers to participate in local environmental actions and to find innovative, technology-based solutions to these challenges. 
In addition, the project intended to build networks with environmentally conscious institutions and strengthen cooperation with local authorities. Overall, it aimed to improve the quality of education by introducing new methodologies and increasing engagement with sustainability topics in schools.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through a series of structured Learning, Teaching and Training Activities (LTTAs), combining physical and virtual meetings across the partner countries. These activities focused on sustainability, cultural heritage, and innovative educational approaches.
The first activity in Croatia focused on green skills and environmental sustainability, including workshops, field visits, and experiential learning in nature. This was followed by a virtual meeting in Spain dedicated to Sustainable Development Goals, where participants explored digital tools and created online educational materials.
The next activity in Hungary focused on STEM-based approaches, including LEGO robotics, environmental education, and hands-on experiences related to sustainability. This was followed by a virtual meeting in Croatia, where participants explored design thinking and UNESCO tangible and intangible cultural heritage, contributing to the creation of an eBook and a virtual museum.
Finally, the project concluded with a physical mobility in Spain, which provided experiential learning through cultural, environmental, and field-based activities, including heritage exploration and sustainability-focused projects.

<< Results >>

The project resulted in a wide range of tangible and intangible outputs that supported both teaching and learning processes. One of the main outcomes was the creation of a comprehensive eBook related to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), developed in a creative way using WEB 2.0-based digital tools, which can be effectively used by teachers in different subjects.
In addition, participants developed a Virtual Museum presenting UNESCO World Heritage, as well as tangible and intangible cultural heritage from the partner countries. A significant part of the project was the collaborative collection and analysis of UNESCO tangible and intangible cultural heritage from the perspectives of the three participating countries, which served as a basis for several project outputs. Another important product was a collection of materials supporting sustainability education, including a thematic eBook on traditional sustainable cuisine based on zero-waste principles. Furthermore, a set of guidelines titled “20 Rules for Ethical Tourism” was created to promote responsible behaviour when visiting cultural and natural heritage sites.
The project also produced less tangible but equally important results, such as improved digital, green, and STEM.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2023-2-HU01-KA210-SCH-000178474.title: ACTI: The ACT Initiative: Sparking Inclusion Through Active Cross-Cultural Collaboration by using Physical Movement and Games as an Innovative Learning Tool for Diverse Learners
2023-2-HU01-KA210-SCH-000178474.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we recognized a strong need across our partner schools in Hungary, Croatia, Spain, and the Czech Republic. Traditional classrooms have long relied on static teaching methods that don’t engage all learners—especially students with ADHD, learning disabilities, or those at risk of dropping out. We wanted to find a way to energize our classrooms, make learning more inclusive, and address student disengagement. Movement-based learning—using physical activity and games—offered an innovative way to meet those needs. At the same time, we saw the importance of integrating digital tools to boost creativity, digital literacy, and personalized learning. Our aim was to bridge the gap between body and mind in education, and build classrooms where all students—no matter their learning style—could thrive.

<< Objectives >>

Our objectives were really clear from the beginning. First, we wanted to integrate movement-based learning into traditional high school teaching. That meant helping teachers redesign lessons to include physical activity and dynamic games. Second, we were focused on inclusion—making sure students with diverse needs felt seen, heard, and supported. Third, we wanted to strengthen students’ digital skills by embedding educational technologies into our approaches. Fourth, we worked to build a collaborative network among our teachers—so we could learn from each other and grow together. And finally, we prioritized gender equality and participation—making sure all voices were represented in both physical and digital learning spaces.

<< Implementation >>

Throughout the project, we carried out a variety of activities. We started with transnational meetings between our partner schools—those were essential for building the foundation of trust and collaboration. We then rolled out training workshops for teachers on how to use movement-based learning and digital tools in practice. After that, each school worked on adapting their curriculum—so that subjects like history, biology, and language included physical activities, role-playing, or digital storytelling. We created a shared set of lesson plans, designed student-led activities, and used tools like interactive whiteboards and apps for gamified learning. Along the way, we constantly evaluated our impact, gathering student feedback and adjusting methods as needed. Our activities weren’t just about implementation—they were about empowerment, experimentation, and reflection.

<< Results >>

Our most tangible result was the ACTI Guidebook and Associated website-a comprehensive, practical resource for teachers who want to use movement and digital tools in inclusive education. We also created modular training materials for educators and a shared library of lesson plans. Teachers developed new teaching methods, and students created digital portfolios and videos that reflected their engagement in the project. Most importantly, we saw a significant increase in student motivation and focus. Many students who were previously disengaged became more involved in their learning. Our partner schools reported better classroom dynamics, stronger collaboration among teachers, and a positive shift in school culture. We also set up a sustainability plan, so that the tools and practices we developed would continue being used after the project’s official end.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2023-2-HU01-KA210-SCH-000178747.title: #girlpower - Interactive stories of women who formed our lives
2023-2-HU01-KA210-SCH-000178747.summary:
<< Background >>

Project Girlpower aimed to address a need identified in the partner countries: very few women are mentioned in history books and educational materials, even though the Central European region can boast outstanding women such as Marie Curie, Ilona Zrínyi, or Milada Horáková.
The goal was to present role models to girls aged 10-14 from various fields – history, science, culture, sports – who could serve as inspiration for their career choices and strengthening their self-esteem.
Girls today still have few adequate role models, while statistics show that they choose STEM fields at lower rates, even though there are great opportunities in this area. Gender stereotypes remain present in society – in many places, people believe that a woman must choose between family and career.
The project aimed to break down these stereotypes by demonstrating that women are capable of exceptional achievements in all fields.
The project was developed with partners from six Central European countries (Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Slovenia).

<< Objectives >>

The overall goal of Project Girlpower was to motivate girls aged 10-14 in the above-mentioned six partner countries to recognize the potential within them and become valued, respected members of society.
The project sought to present as examples women who have made a name for themselves through extraordinary achievements and can serve as role models for the next generation. The aim was to demonstrate that the stories of these women are also significant in a regional context, as the Central European countries share a common historical background.
Presenting various career path models and drawing attention to the possibility and importance of free choice were considered essential.
The project was intended to supplement school education with cultural-historical insights, spark girls' interest in history, and help them with career choices.

<< Implementation >>

The two-year project was divided into three main phases: content development, application development, and project communication.
Content development (January–December 2024): Each partner selected 5 women from their country. Following this, 30 complete profiles were created. Every profile was translated into English and all six national languages (Polish, Czech, Slovak, Hungarian, Croatian, Slovenian), and the accompanying illustrations were also produced. (See FTP 1.)
Application development (January–August 2024): The user experience (UX) plan was completed, which designed the application's usage, followed by the user interface (UI) design, which planned the graphic elements. The application was filled with unique features, and the finished application was uploaded to the two largest digital stores (Apple's App Store, Google's Play Store). (See FTP 2.)
Project communication (January–December 2025): The visual Brand Book was completed, along with the continuously updated Facebook page (www.facebook.com/projectgirlpower) and website (www.girlpowerapp.com), as well as educational materials for teachers and parents. Digital campaigns and in-person presentations were also organized. (See FTP 3.)

<< Results >>

Content results:
1.	Detailed presentations of 30 women across five categories.
2.	Every profile available in 7 languages (English + 6 national languages).
3.	30 unique, high-resolution illustrations for each featured woman.
4.	6 educational materials for teachers.
Technical results:
1.	Functional mobile application for iOS and Android platforms.
2.	Swipe functionality, chronological navigation, favourites feature.
3.	User-friendly UX/UI design.
Communication results:
1.	Brand Book with unified visual identity.
2.	Active Facebook page (www.facebook.com/projectgirlpower) with regular posts.
3.	Fully functional website (www.girlpowerapp.com).
4.	More than 10,000 newsletters sent in total.
5.	In-person presentation sessions and off-site classes at partner schools.
6.	Quiz games and drama activities for the primary target audience.
7.	Exhibition, television interviews, presence at career fairs.
8.	Musical animations and visual content for the age group. (See FTP 4.)
Long-term impact:
1.	The application and website will remain accessible after the project ends.
2.	Partners continue promoting the application at the national level.
3.	A knowledge base has been created that can later be expanded with additional countries and figures.

2023-2-LV01-KA210-SCH-000169866.title: STEM ON
2023-2-LV01-KA210-SCH-000169866.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we recognized a strong need to modernize teaching and learning practices in our schools through innovative, inclusive and motivating STEM education. Traditional teaching models are not enough to prepare students for a rapidly changing world marked by digital transformation, sustainability challenges and increasing demand for STEM skills. This project provides an opportunity to introduce practical STEM learning scenarios, strengthen teacher training and create an environment that fosters curiosity, creativity and problem-solving skills, while promoting inclusion, diversity and equal access to learning. By collaborating with partner schools, we can share experiences, test new methodologies and create impactful tools that benefit the entire educational community. The need for innovation in teaching methods. Teachers need new pedagogical tools and approaches that go beyond traditional teaching and engage students through experiments, interdisciplinary work and real-world problem solving. STEM activities provide students with the competencies needed to understand sustainability challenges and make informed decisions. The school becomes open to international collaboration.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project, we wanted to foster innovation in the classroom by using STEM lesson plans and practical kits that introduce new, inclusive and engaging approaches to teaching and learning. Our goal was to modernize STEM education in our own and partner schools, support digital and environmental education, and ensure that all students have equal access to high-quality learning opportunities. Overall, the project aimed to strengthen scientific culture, promote active and experiential learning, support digital and ecological transformation, and increase innovation, inclusion, and collaboration within and between participating schools. To equip teachers with the skills to implement experimental, interdisciplinary, and digitally supported STEM activities, improving their teaching methods and professional development. To assess how new STEM lesson plans affect student motivation, engagement, and learning outcomes, as well as teacher effectiveness in STEM education. Educators were tasked with developing an online platform - an E-book integrated with the project website, which would host all STEM lesson plans created and approved during the project. 


<< Implementation >>

Throughout the project, a wide range of learning, training and teaching activities were implemented in the partner schools. These activities allowed students and teachers to apply theoretical knowledge through practical STEM research, fieldwork and workshops. Study visits to universities, science centres, technology companies and cultural venues provided participants with valuable insights into regional development and demonstrated how STEM fields contribute to local development. Fieldwork, environmental analysis, water quality testing, coastal studies and renewable energy observations were carried out during all face-to-face meetings. Teachers supported the co-creation of lesson scenarios during the collaboration sessions, also allowing students to develop, test and improve prototypes of the lesson scenario platform. Digital learning enhanced collaboration, virtual exchange and dissemination. Cultural activities complemented the project’s educational programme. All activities were organised in schools during school hours whenever possible, in line with Erasmus+ principles, in addition to cultural orientation assignments after school. Study visits illustrated practical examples of sustainability. 

<< Results >>

The main product of the project is an e-book documenting methodologies, scenarios, results and recommendations for the development of STEM in each of the partner schools. It is a digital platform hosting all STEM learning scenarios that have been tested, validated and downloadable. The learning scenarios have already taken place in each of the partner schools during face-to-face meetings. It is a set of innovative, inclusive STEM material kits ready for use. The project also resulted in the exchange of teachers’ experiences and improved digital and STEM teaching competences, and improved student motivation and participation in STEM subjects, especially for disadvantaged students. The effectiveness of STEM scenarios in all partner schools has been jointly analysed. Cooperation between partner schools has strengthened, allowing schools to exchange ideas and best practices. The exchange of students and teachers provided direct intercultural and academic experience. The project integrated technology into lessons to improve teaching and learning. In addition, schools benefited from access to resources and funding, supporting sustainable innovation. Systematic sharing of results helped to disseminate successful practices.

2023-2-LV01-KA210-SCH-000170061.title: Not Bullies All Buddies
2023-2-LV01-KA210-SCH-000170061.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied because we believe that every student deserves to feel safe, accepted, and valued at school. Peer bullying has been a serious problem that affected our students’ emotional well-being, academic performance, and self-esteem. We wanted to create this project that addresses this issue through awareness, education, and positive action.
The needs we addressed included the lack of awareness about the types and impact of bullying, the need to promote empathy and respect among students, and the importance of encouraging bystanders to speak up. We also focused on building peer support systems and fostering an inclusive school culture where differences are respected. By participating, we hoped to help create a school environment where kindness replaces cruelty and students become allies instead of enemies. Working with international peers gave us new perspectives and strategies, making our anti-bullying efforts even stronger.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we wanted to create a safe, respectful, and inclusive school environment where every student feels valued. Our main goal was to raise awareness about peer bullying and its harmful effects on mental health, relationships, and academic success. We aimed to help students recognize different forms of bullying—verbal, physical, social, and online—and understand the importance of empathy and kindness.
Through this project, we wanted to empower students to speak up, support one another, and take a stand against bullying. We also focused on turning bystanders into active defenders and promoting the idea that everyone has a role in building a positive school culture. Additionally, by working with international partners, we aimed to exchange ideas, understand cultural differences, and find common values that unite us against bullying.
Ultimately, we hoped to build stronger friendships, improve communication among peers, and spread the message that schools should be places of support—not fear.

<< Implementation >>

1)Anti-Bullying Workshops in Latvia( give me a hand exercise, designing project logo, create anti-bullying poster,);
2)Don’t be a Bully Workshops in Italy(presentation of an interactive powerpoint slide about types of bullying, Random Acts of Kindness, designing Bullying Scenario Discussion cards);
3)I choose Kindness Workshops in Turkiye: A week of anti-bullying activities and cultural trips to experience an incredible Erasmus+ culture through all the memories we shared (anti-bullying t-shirts, paper chains of kindness);
4)Bully Proof Classroom Workshops in Croatia:  the "Earth Scavenger Hunt" and the "Anti-Bully Tree."

<< Results >>

We created a Bullying Prevention and Intervention Procedure Manual. It is consisted of:
1.Definition: what is the program and how it works.
2.Prevention:create good school culture, assess scope of bullying, students activities, program mentors.
3.Intervention:What to do if you see bullying, what to do if bullying is reported.
We created awareness materials and workshops : We created posters, brochures, school boards through anti-bullying workshops which were shared within our schools and on facebook to spread awareness widely.
We made presentations about cyber-bullying that engaged students, teachers in open conversations about bullying and how to prevent it.
Through Erasmus+ mobilities, students from different countries worked together, exchanged ideas, and developed empathy and intercultural understanding.
Most importantly, we observed improved student attitudes—more kindness, better cooperation, and increased willingness to report or stand against bullying.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2023-2-PT01-KA210-SCH-000178115.title:
We are the future - Civic Education, Democracy, Inclusion
and the Environment
2023-2-PT01-KA210-SCH-000178115.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we identified common needs in our school communities related to the lack of democratic and civic participation among young people, often marked by indifference, low self-esteem, and poor expectations conveyed by disadvantaged family backgrounds. We recognize that students are underrepresented in the decision-making processes that affect their lives, and it is essential to create spaces for active involvement that promote European citizenship skills, social inclusion, and sustainability. The schools involved were already developing environmental and social intervention initiatives, but we felt the need to deepen and share experiences, as well as to innovate methodologies, particularly through hybrid learning. The project thus responded to the urgent need to connect young people to their communities, empower them to intervene critically and creatively, enhance the role of the European Union, and strengthen collective awareness for the preservation of democracy, equality, and a sustainable future.


<< Objectives >>

With the implementation of this project, we aimed to develop active citizenship among young people, providing them with the skills to recognize cross-cutting concerns among European youth and propose solutions to the problems that directly affect them. We sought to empower them as agents of change, aware of the importance of their social and political intervention, strengthening their connection to local communities and the European space. We also sought to foster values of common belonging, perseverance, solidarity, initiative, critical thinking, and resilience, preparing them for a more just and sustainable European future. The project also aimed to bring young people closer to the functioning of democratic institutions, promoting equal opportunities, inclusion, and awareness of global challenges such as climate change and social inequalities. In short, we wanted students to become active, informed, and motivated European citizens who could contribute creatively and collaboratively to building a more democratic, supportive, and sustainable society.


<< Implementation >>

The project activities focused on three cross-cutting themes identified as common to the three countries involved: democracy, social intervention, and environmental awareness. Within this framework, three workshops on democracy were implemented, allowing students to explore the functioning of democratic systems and reflect on their civic participation. Three workshops on active citizenship were also held, focusing on volunteering as a form of social intervention, and three workshops on environmental awareness, promoting sustainable behaviors. Two field trips dedicated to practical environmental activities were also carried out, with the aim of strengthening students' connection to their surroundings. In the artistic field, three creative activities were carried out: a tile mural, a wall mural, and works of art made from recycled materials, promoting artistic expression and ecological awareness. Nine activities were developed to promote the identity and cultural heritage of the partner countries, as well as two activities focused on European identity and institutions, fostering a sense of belonging to the European Union.


<< Results >>

In terms of tangible results, the objectives would be achieved if 15 students and 6 teachers from each school participated in face-to-face activities in the three partner countries and if at least three external organizations collaborated in the activities, contributing to the implementation of the program. Three creative activities were also planned through workshops, with the sharing of creative techniques, namely a tile mural, a wall mural, and works of art made from recycled materials collected from cleaning public spaces. After each mobility, a dissemination session would be held in each school to share knowledge. Three manifestos were also planned, which would culminate in a final manifesto. A 5% increase in participation in extracurricular activities and improved performance in English were estimated.
In terms of intangible results, it was hoped that there would be an increase in active participation skills, with social and environmental actions, greater awareness of the role of the European Union and a stronger sense of belonging, the development of critical thinking, greater interest in democratic processes, and the strengthening of digital skills.

2023-2-RS01-KA210-SCH-000175495.title: Stare igre za novo vreme
2023-2-RS01-KA210-SCH-000175495.summary:
<< Background >>

Working with children, we noticed that they spend less and less time outside, playing, and much more time in front of the screen, which negatively affects their psycho-physical growth and development. We wanted, with a project like this, to make them interested in outdoor physical activities, and at the same time awaken and encourage a series of skills in them such as cooperation, empathy, mutual respect, tolerance, nurturing and promoting their own and other people's traditions. The common needs of all partners were the development of competence for interculturality, communication and cooperation with other institutions aimed at training and learning from examples of good practice. Participating in this project, we improved civic European values, the principles of a democratic society, respect, appreciation, and acceptance of diversity. Some of the research in school showed that improper physical posture with students occurs due to lack of physical activity. Activities in the project directly respond to this need. Disrupted value system in society, attitude towards education, insufficiently planned creative work in teaching are some of the needs of partner organizations that have been improved by the realization of this project.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we wanted to motivate and enable students and adults to spend more time outside, playing traditional children's games and less in front of the screen. We reached this goal by fulfilling a number of specific goals. 
The key points we wanted to activate were improvement of students' physical activity, their dexterity, better development of social skills, communication and empathy, tolerance, concentration, resourcefulness, verbal and physical skills, self-confidence, fair play, acceptance of defeat, respect for diversity, respect for opponents, cheering culture. By making equipment and polygons, students developed fine motor skills that were neglected by using new technologies; working on a digital book they developed the skill of teamwork with a mutual product at the end; by game tournaments they improved their physical dexterity and strength, and at the same time worked on soft skills. During the implementation of the project activities, they simultaneously represented their own culture and tradition, and at the same time got to know the culture and tradition of other nations. Shortly, by participating in the games, the students worked simultaneously on their physical and spiritual development.

<< Implementation >>

During the realization of the project, we implemented four activities.
The first one is Project Management and Implementation and it includes all planned tasks and activities from the beginning to the end of the project. This activity includes initial project work activities, everything done before and after each LTT meeting, as well as project dissemination and promotional activities. 
The second one is the creation of equipment and polygons for the games. The production of the equipment and polygons was realized in partner schools, and presented at the LTT meeting in the partner school in Slovenia and includes a demonstration of the use and presentation of the equipment and polygons made by students.
The third activity is Creating a digital book. This activity was implemented in partner school in Croatia and represents a creation of a mutual digital book of all partner organizations. Previously, each partner organization created its own digital book. 
The fourth and the last activity is the Organization of a tournament in traditional children's games and it was realized in partner school in Serbia. Here, the students put into practice the games for which they made the equipment and which they described in a mutual digital book.

<< Results >>

The outputs and results of this project are: equipment and polygons, digital book, both in electronic and printed edition, logo, poster and mascot of the project, Erasmus corner in each partner organization, project banner, YouTube channels of the project, video-webinar on traditional children's games, eTwinning project and eTwinning group, social networks (Facebook, Instagram), Tree of Rules, Tree of Friendship, presentation of the project to other schools, presentation of the project to colleagues from other European countries, article in Rijeka's "Novi list", article in "Politika", a report on TV Una, celebrating important dates, a brochure on children's rights, a calendar on the topic of children's rights, announcements on the websites of partner organizations, open classes in partner schools, Europass certificates, certificates from each LTT meeting.

2023-2-RS01-KA210-SCH-000178094.title: "TALLER Together: Embracing Tolerance in Our School"
2023-2-RS01-KA210-SCH-000178094.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our objectives are cultivating inclusive, diverse schools; promoting tolerance and empathy; fostering civic engagement, democratic values, and human rights education. We ensure equal educational opportunities, celebrate differences, and encourage student participation. Our curriculum includes anti-discrimination policies based on human rights principles. The objectives result in a teachers' manual to instil these values in primary school students.

<< Implementation >>

We will implement two virtual trainings for teachers, providing them with valuable tools and insights to incorporate tolerance education into their classrooms. The project features three LTTs held in different partner countries. Serbia hosts the LTT titled "From Self-Discovery to Inclusivity: Tolerance's Transformative Journey," while Croatia hosts "Bridging Hearts: Connecting Nations Through Tolerance," and Italy oversees "Navigating the Path to Tolerance: Faith and Media"

<< Results >>

The creation of e-brochures focused on various tolerance-related topics, the development of action plans to enhance tolerance education within partner schools, the analysis of pre- and post-survey questionnaires to gauge the project's impact, the establishment of a dedicated project website and social media accounts, the creation of an interdisciplinary teachers' manual for tolerance education, and the empowerment of 54 students and 18 teachers to become advocates for tolerance and inclusivity.
topics: Human rights and rule of law

2024-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000247473.title: What about us
2024-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000247473.summary:
<< Background >>

The central goal was to raise students' awareness of global environmental problems (climate change, waste management, biodiversity). The project provided a structured platform for imparting knowledge and developing practical skills for sustainable behavior in everyday life.

Environmental protection is viewed and implemented differently in each country; various methods are used, and different institutions bear the primary responsibility.
Schools also address the topic of environmental protection in different ways.

<< Objectives >>

The Erasmus+ program aims to strengthen cooperation in Europe. The partnership between schools from four different countries facilitated an important cultural exchange. The students learned to collaborate across geographical boundaries, understand different perspectives on environmental protection in their respective countries, and jointly develop solutions to global challenges.

The project also focuses on imparting important interdisciplinary skills.

Communication in a common language, usually English, was encouraged. The use of digital tools for project communication and documentation was required, thus strengthening digital skills. Working on shared project goals in international teams enhanced teamwork and problem-solving abilities.

The project addressed the schools' need to supplement classroom instruction with practical, real-world, and motivating projects. Excursions, workshops, and litter clean-ups made learning more experiential and effective. The establishment of sustainable practices (energy concepts, school gardens, recycling systems) was intended to be integrated into everyday school life beyond the project's duration.

<< Implementation >>

In this project, we visited waste and recycling facilities, conducted tours of sewage treatment plants and waterworks, received guided tours of sewage treatment plants and waterworks in Hamburg, had a professional guided tour of Plitvnica Lake National Park, and during a visit to salt pans, the students gained insights into salt production and related environmental aspects. We attended a lecture on "sustainability" at the Goethe Institute in Zagreb, visited the Museum of Water Supply in Zagreb, carried out a forest project in Sweden and summarized it in a podcast, and at the partner school in Konya, the students jointly developed an environmental log for our project and printed it on bags made from recycled material.

<< Results >>

Project documentation: Reports and presentations of the various activities.

Public relations materials: Flyers, posters, and articles for local newspapers or school websites.

Digital presence: Information for the school website, a podcast, and social media pages (such as eTwinning pages or Facebook) where activities, photos, and results were shared.

School-based initiatives: The introduction or improvement of recycling systems, school gardens, and energy-saving measures in the partner schools.

The most important intangible outcome is the increased awareness and understanding of environmental issues and sustainable practices among the participating students and teachers.

Improved language skills (especially English), digital skills, teamwork, problem-solving skills, and project management skills among the participants.

The development of friendships and understanding between students from Croatia, Turkey, Sweden, and Germany has contributed to breaking down stereotypes.

The establishment of long-term relationships between the participating schools and teachers, which may have led to future joint projects.
A more sustainable lifestyle and environmentally conscious use of resources in everyday life.

2024-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000249716.title: VO in Energy – vocational orientation in schools as a significant contribution to the energy transition in rural areas
2024-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000249716.summary:
<< Objectives >>

With this project we want to support teachers, teamers for school projects and all multiplier who are working in the field of vocational orientation by handing them over the most effective methods/a role-play to motivate young students to pursue a career in the renewable energy sector - a field of work that will become increasingly important in the future and is indispensable for a future worth living in Europe and the entire world.

<< Implementation >>

Within the project, we plan two analogue meetings. These will focus on exchanging methods for the target group (meeting 1) and developing the role-playing game (meeting 2). The schedule will also include excursions to companies / other stakeholders related to renewable energies. Throughout the project duration, there will be several digital exchange sessions for sharing and improving the developed methods/roles for the role-playing game. Several expert presentations will enrich the meetings.

<< Results >>

To achieve this, we expect the development of 5 methods specifically tailored to the needs of the target group of students in vocational orientation in various European countries. In addition, by the end of the project, a fully developed role-playing game in 4 languages should be available, which sensitizes and motivates young people across Europe for careers in the energy sector. As an extra, we hope to establish strong partnerships that will lay the foundation for future collaborations.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2024-1-EE01-KA210-SCH-000247464.title: GreenLoop: Education for a Circular Future
2024-1-EE01-KA210-SCH-000247464.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project aims to integrate CE principles into curricula, enhancing sustainability awareness and interdisciplinary collaboration among students and teachers. It includes developing educational resources, facilitating workshops, and fostering partnerships for experiential learning. The goal is to strengthen analytical skills, promote active European citizenship, and enhance schools' educational and international cooperation capabilities.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement activities focused on sustainable design, teaching students to create eco-friendly solutions. Waste management activities will educate on reducing, reusing, and recycling. Renewable resources sessions will explore sustainable energy and materials. Lastly, we'll develop contemporary CE lesson plans, equipping teachers with innovative tools to integrate CE principles across subjects, promoting a holistic understanding of sustainability among students.

<< Results >>

The project will boost environmental awareness and critical thinking among students, enhancing teamwork, communication, and problem-solving skills through CE challenges. It will empower teachers to deliver interdisciplinary CE lessons, fostering student engagement in sustainability. Students will gain analytical skills, exposure to real-world CE solutions, and professional networking for sustainability careers. International collaboration will enrich teacher exchanges on sustainable practices.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000250626.title: ECOLOGY IS ANYTIME ANYWHERE
2024-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000250626.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the urgent need for environmental awareness and sustainable behavior among students in response to global challenges like climate change and biodiversity loss
. Our schools identified a critical gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application; therefore, we sought to provide hands-on, innovative experiences that connect nature with modern technology
. A core motivation was promoting inclusive education, ensuring equitable participation for students from all backgrounds, including those at risk of disadvantage
. The project also addressed the need for students to develop essential 21st-century skills, such as digital literacy, critical thinking, and problem-solving
. For our staff, it provided vital professional development in using digital tools and inclusive teaching methodologies through the exchange of best practices
. Finally, international cooperation was essential to foster intercultural dialogue and develop joint solutions to shared ecological challenges, reinforcing our institutional capacity and the students' sense of European identity.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to significantly enhance students’ awareness and understanding of environmental challenges, specifically climate change and biodiversity loss, while fostering more responsible and sustainable daily behaviors. A core objective was to develop essential 21st-century competences, including critical thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, and digital literacy, by integrating nature with modern technological tools and innovative methodologies. We also focused on promoting inclusive education, ensuring equal participation and access for all learners regardless of their socio-economic or cultural backgrounds to reduce educational gaps. For teachers, the project sought to strengthen professional competences in using ICT and adopting inclusive teaching strategies through the exchange of best practices. At a partnership level, we aimed to build robust transnational cooperation and intercultural dialogue among partners from Italy, Croatia, Türkiye, and Spain. Finally, the project contributed to broader goals such as the United Nations Agenda 2030 and ensuring long-term impact through the dissemination of collaborative educational resources.

<< Implementation >>

During implementation, we executed a wide range of interactive, student-centered activities across our partner schools. We began with a Kick-off Meeting to define roles, followed by a logo design competition to shape our visual identity. Monthly thematic workshops were held locally: “Sport is Fun” and “Yummy Healthy Snack” promoted well-being, while “Green Artists Green Influencers” focused on reuse and digital storytelling. Students engaged in research-based tasks like “What happens in the world?” and “What awaits us in 2100?”, creating virtual galleries of future visions. A key collaborative output was the “Smart World Gardening E-Booklet”. We organized transnational mobilities in Spain, Croatia, Italy, and Türkiye, where participants engaged in practical tasks like making recycled paper, pixel art, and exploring local ecosystems. All activities integrated ICT and Web 2.0 tools for real-time documentation and sharing. We monitored progress through pre- and post-tests to measure ecological awareness and behavioral changes like waste sorting. This approach ensured active participation and cross-border collaboration, effectively blending nature with modern technology for inclusive environmental education.

<< Results >>

The project yielded diverse concrete outputs and measurable results. Tangible products include the collaborative “Smart World Gardening E-Booklet,” the “Erasmus+ Eco-Book” containing environmental drawings, and a Virtual Gallery. Students developed digital resources like storyboards, photo journals, and videos, alongside creative artworks from recycled materials. Beyond physical outputs, pre- and post-tests confirmed a significant increase in students' ecological awareness and a shift toward sustainable daily habits, such as waste sorting and water conservation. Participants strengthened essential skills including digital literacy, critical thinking, and collaboration. Transnational mobilities in Italy, Croatia, Spain, and Türkiye fostered meaningful intercultural dialogue, improved English language proficiency, and a deeper sense of European identity. For teachers, the project led to enhanced professional competences in ICT and inclusive pedagogical strategies. At an institutional level, cooperation was solidified, increasing schools' capacity for future international partnerships. Finally, broad dissemination of results via school exhibitions, social media, and the ESEP platform ensured a lasting impact on local communities.

2024-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000252241.title: Learning:Dance it, play Music, play Game
2024-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000252241.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was created to improve awareness and inclusion of students with special educational needs (SEN) in the partner schools. The schools identified the need for more inclusive educational practices and more cooperation between teachers, students and families. Through music, dance, games and outdoor activities, the project aimed to support SEN students’ participation, social adaptation and wellbeing. The project also promoted digital competences through the creation of lesson plans, short educational videos and online dissemination activities.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to improve inclusion and awareness about SEN students through creative and participatory activities. Another objective was to help teachers develop more inclusive methodologies that could be used in everyday classroom practice. The project also promoted European values such as equality, respect for diversity, cooperation and active citizenship while encouraging intercultural dialogue and teamwork between the participating countries.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, the partner schools carried out mobility activities in Italy, Croatia, Spain and Türkiye focused on inclusion, SEN awareness and innovative educational approaches. Activities included workshops, seminars, outdoor learning, music and games activities, environmental awareness projects and the creation of educational videos and lesson plans. During Erasmus+ Days, an additional activity about marine fauna conservation and whale watching was organised in Tenerife, culminating in the creation of a book about the marine fauna of the participating countries. The partners also organised online meetings, dissemination activities and workshops throughout the project.

<< Results >>

The project increased awareness about SEN students among teachers, students and families in the partner schools. Teachers improved their skills in inclusive education and shared practical methodologies related to music, games, outdoor learning and digital tools. The project also produced lesson plans, short educational videos and dissemination materials that can continue to be used in the future. The mobilities strengthened cooperation, intercultural understanding and communication between participants from different countries, while encouraging more inclusive participation of SEN students in school life.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2024-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000254010.title: Future Guardians: Cultivating Eco-Leadership in Young Minds
2024-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000254010.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our planet is facing quite serious problems and many of these problems seem to be worsening with every passing day.Human-driven global warming and pollution are causing a massive increase in natural disasters, warming and cooling periods, and extreme weather events. If we don't act today, it might be too late for future generations.Our main objective is to raise environmentally responsible and aware future citizens who are equipped with the skills to improve the planet.

2024-1-FR01-KA210-SCH-000251027.title: Blue Sea: Our Cultural Heritage, Our Environmental Responsibility
2024-1-FR01-KA210-SCH-000251027.summary:
<< Background >>

Our aim was, in particular, to raise awareness among the school community and young students about the importance of preserving marine ecosystems and to combat plastic pollution, overfishing, and climate change.
The project encouraged students to take an active role in environmental protection, cultural heritage preservation and European cooperation, strengthening their sense of responsibility and active citizenship. 
As most of the locations involved were coastal regions and islands vulnerable to climate-related risks, we wanted to raise student awareness regarding sustainable practices and their role in mitigating environmental challenges, specifically by reducing plastic waste and conserving marine biodiversity;
- to improve students' language and communication skills by providing opportunities to interact with peers from different linguistic backgrounds. During regular video conferences, our students,especially those from the Caribbean islands, communicated fluently with their European counterparts. 
These served as real-world opportunities for language exchange, and we always value such moments of in-context assessment.

<< Objectives >>

The intended outcomes were as follows:
*   increased cultural awareness and appreciation among students as they discovered the rich cultural diversity of Guadeloupe, Porto, Croatia, and Sardinia;
*   a better understanding of environmental issues and the importance of responsible environmental management, with students actively engaging in local cleanup efforts and conservation activities;
*   the establishment of ongoing cultural exchange programs, fostering lasting friendships and promoting tolerance and intercultural dialogue;
*   student- and teacher-led initiatives to preserve local cultural heritage sites, including organized cleanup and restoration projects;
*   the development of leadership skills among students as they took the initiative to organize events, campaigns, and awareness-raising activities within their communities;
*   accumulated interdisciplinary learning, with students and teachers exploring the connections between cultural heritage, marine biology, environmental science, and other fields;

<< Implementation >>

The "Keep the Sea Plastic Free" project in Sardinia focused on environmental responsibility and reducing plastic use.
"Heritage by the Adriatic" in Croatia explored coastal cultural heritage while fostering cultural awareness.
"Volcanic Heritage & Sustainable Waters" in Guadeloupe focused on volcanic heritage, the water cycle, and water management practices.
"Wind & Wave Culture Quest" in Portugal explored clean energy production from wind and waves, promoting environmentally friendly technologies.
During the exchange visits, we were immersed in these themes and experienced them firsthand. 
This enabled us to understand our partners' way of life.

<< Results >>

The project produced a range of concrete educational, digital and dissemination results directly linked to the objectives established in the original application. Each partner developed 10 interdisciplinary lesson plans related to the theme of its mobility activity, resulting in a total of 40 educational resources covering environmental sustainability, cultural heritage, climate change, marine ecosystems and STEAM-related topics. 
These materials were designed for different age groups and are available through the project TwinSpace.
The partnership also produced traditional recipe cards linking food, cultural heritage and sustainability, a photographic record of the four mobility activities, video materials containing contributions from students, teachers, parents and members of the school communities, and extensive documentation of the activities and their learning outcomes. 
The project strengthened environmental awareness, intercultural understanding, foreign-language communication, digital competence, collaboration and active citizenship. 
Participants and teachers also gained practical experience in interdisciplinary and experiential learning. Dissemination within the partner schools and local communities were made.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-1-FR01-KA210-SCH-000253786.title: Let's build citizenship bridges!
2024-1-FR01-KA210-SCH-000253786.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our objectives are providing a high-quality foundation and a solid civic foundation for our future adult citizens, founded on values of respect and integration to strengthen European sentiment. The objectives promote interdisciplinary, through active methodologies to improve ICT skills and collaborative learning in an international context, which also allows language skills to be developed. We want to offer our students the essential tools to work for a sustainable world.

<< Implementation >>

All the participants will participate in lectures,researches, prepare scripts, presentations, videos and quizzes about Civic and environmental engagement.In addition to actions at school level, we will have 3 LTTA 1TM that will help us achieve our project objectives and achieve the planned results. These will serve for better coordination between teachers and to share actions and innovative teaching methods/practices . Students will share their experiences, developing their European citizenship.

<< Results >>

For students:
- raise awareness of the importance of being a citizen committed to the fight against intolerance and climate change;
- deepen knowledge of ICT and languages;
- realize that academic success is within everyone’s reach.
For teachers:
- reinforce their knowledge about the diversity of the world;
- develop innovative practices to combat school failure;
- promote collaboration.
Together: building a more tolerant and united Europe.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2024-1-FR01-KA210-SCH-000254188.title: Against all odds
2024-1-FR01-KA210-SCH-000254188.summary:
<< Objectives >>

"Against all odds" project is driven by a strong commitment to social responsibility within educational institutions. By
focusing on key competences, civic engagement, and STEM education, we aim to equip students with the necessary
knowledge and skills to make informed and responsible decisions regarding gambling. Furthermore, our dedication to
promoting the physical and mental well-being of students underscores our commitment to their holistic development.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement multiplier events, educational materials development, workshops on preventing addiction,
identifying risky behaviors, and awareness enhancement campaigns. Transnational meetings will ensure effective planning.
Open public events will promote awareness, and these events will continue beyond the project's conclusion. The project
aims to address gambling addiction among youth, emphasizing responsible gambling, mental health, and social
responsibility.

<< Results >>

The expected results of the project include the development of educational materials on gambling and probability, increased
awareness of the risks associated with gambling, the identification of risky behaviors among students, improved knowledge
of probability and informed decision-making, the creation of an educational toolkit, impactful videos for awareness, continued organization of open public events, and enhanced social responsibility among educational institutions.

2024-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000243439.title: The Universal Language of Sports: Our Common Values
2024-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000243439.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was developed in response to the shared needs of our partner schools to increase students' participation in sport, promote healthy lifestyles and strengthen common European values through education. Although each partner school had experience in different sports, students had limited opportunities to explore how sport contributes to inclusion, gender equality, intercultural dialogue and active citizenship. Teachers also identified a need to exchange innovative teaching practices, compare physical education curricula and improve their professional competences through international cooperation. The project addressed these needs by focusing on three sports that represent the sporting identity of each partner country: football in Croatia, basketball in Lithuania and volleyball in Türkiye. Through learning mobilities, practical workshops, school visits and cooperation with coaches and sports professionals, participants experienced different educational systems and sports cultures. The project also responded to the need for stronger European cooperation by encouraging teamwork, mutual respect, fair play and intercultural understanding while creating sustainable educational resources for future use.

<< Objectives >>

Through the implementation of the SPORTVALS project, we demonstrated that sport is a powerful educational tool for promoting healthy lifestyles, social inclusion, gender equality and common European values. The project increased students' knowledge of sports culture and encouraged active participation in football, basketball and volleyball while strengthening awareness of fair play, teamwork and intercultural understanding. Students also developed communication, cooperation, self-confidence and motivation for lifelong physical activity through international learning experiences. Teachers enhanced their professional competences by observing different physical education systems, exchanging innovative teaching methods and jointly creating educational resources. At the organisational level, the project established sustainable international partnerships, strengthened the European dimension of school education and produced long-term educational outcomes, including the Curriculum Integration Teacher Workshop Report with practical teaching materials and recommendations for integrating sport, healthy lifestyles and European values into everyday teaching.

<< Implementation >>

The SPORTVALS project was implemented from 1 December 2024 to 31 May 2026 in partnership with schools from Croatia, Lithuania and Türkiye. Regular online meetings ensured effective planning, monitoring and communication. Three international mobilities focused on football, basketball, volleyball, healthy lifestyles and European values through sport. Activities included sports workshops, PE lesson observations, visits to schools, sports clubs, universities and sports facilities, meetings with athletes and coaches, teacher workshops, cultural activities and evaluation sessions. Participants exchanged good practices and compared approaches to sports education. A shared Google Drive repository ensured transparent project management and access to documentation. Project visibility was achieved through eTwinning TwinSpace, the project Instagram page, school websites and local media. Additional activities included sports tournaments, Erasmus Sports Corners, surveys, evaluations, student diaries and the Curriculum Integration Teacher Workshop Report with lesson plans, ensuring sustainability beyond the project.

<< Results >>

At the end of the project, all planned objectives were successfully achieved and valuable results were created for future use. Three international mobilities in Croatia, Lithuania and Türkiye enabled students and teachers to gain knowledge and experience about football, basketball, volleyball, healthy lifestyles, gender equality, inclusion and European values through sport.
The main project outcome was the Curriculum Integration Teacher Workshop Report, including lesson plans, good practice examples and recommendations for integrating sports topics into education. Teachers exchanged innovative methods, compared PE curricula and strengthened their professional competences.
Partner schools established Erasmus Sports Corners, organised sports tournaments, promotional activities and final presentations. Visits to sports clubs, academies and meetings with athletes and coaches expanded participants’ understanding of European sports systems.
Project impact was measured through tests, student diaries, portfolios and evaluations, showing increased awareness of healthy lifestyles, sports values, equality and European citizenship. All materials were stored and shared through Google Drive, eTwinning TwinSpace, school websites and media.

2024-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000244822.title: See you SEA benefits!
2024-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000244822.summary:
<< Objectives >>

By implementing this two-year Erasmus+ project in our schools, we want to influence changes in school curricula throughout the EU, with the aim of responding to the needs of young people. Mindfulness activities, self-care and care for the nature that surrounds us need to be part of the school curriculum. This Erasmus+ project will give students strategies for mental relaxation but also ways of living by the seas and oceans with the aim of a sustainable lifestyle.

<< Implementation >>

Erasmus+ project activities refer to the 3 main following types of activities: mental health and physical health activities and activities for sustainable development of seas and oceans. Through these types of most important project activities, several sub-activities are connected: activities to introduce protected marine areas of the EU, self-help activities related to the sea, activities of active citizenship - participation in beach cleaning and proposals for preservation of marine biomes.

<< Results >>

The most important tangible project result is a Handbook with LS on the topic of mental and physical health of young people using the immediate natural environment - in our case, the sea. Among the results, there will be a website and an eTwinning project. There will also be a digital board game related to knowledge and preservation of the sea and mind. Of the intangible results, the most important is the development of soft skills and self-help skills in order to better cope with the stress.

2024-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000249899.title: Luka kao temelj egzistencije i društvenog napretka- jučer, danas, sutra
2024-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000249899.summary:
<< Background >>

Our three schools have always been committed to Erasmus because we believe that it is a program that opens many doors and connects differences in the best possible way. Education in modern times requires the acquisition of multiple skills and knowledge that are not achievable in the regular teaching process. Observing the structure of schools and their everyday lives, we concluded that we would gain a lot of new experiences by connecting with other European colleagues. The needs we wanted to meet were the strengthening of our own values ​​within the European civic dimension, with a special emphasis on developing critical thinking and entrepreneurial visions in teachers and students. All partners in the project come from similar regions and that is why they are so complementary. The lack of European experience was the main motive for working on the project. Also, together we realized that we have a common point in the port as the foundation of the region's existence. We saw in this a great opportunity to gain new experiences.



<< Objectives >>

We wanted students to increase their knowledge of assessing their own values ​​and skills in the area of ​​entrepreneurial thinking. Teachers also wanted to improve their skills in transmitting these types of knowledge in each subject.
Above all, it was to increase their interest in the world around them, in which there are many problems
The project also wanted to achieve the following:
- better contact with reality involving economic entities and the production of various creative materials based on what was seen in the field.
- participation in a large number of workshops and meetings, conversations, developing entrepreneurial skills and ideas, spreading a sense of usefulness.
- development of skills related to work in tourism and food and transport, which are important segments in the economy of port areas
- raising awareness among students and the environment about the place in which they live, through the past, present and future, strengthening the English language as a language of communication,
-connecting with new people and learning about life in different conditions
- development of key competencies
- emphasis on the ecological and civic dimension

<< Implementation >>

We have implemented activities related to deepening critical thinking, an entrepreneurial way of understanding things, new digital opportunities, debate as a way of exchanging opinions and views in the teaching process. We have included more practical work in the teaching process, which we will carry out with greater emphasis on innovative thinking. We have especially focused on developing students' motor skills and turning theory into reality.
Through the implementation of the project, we have implemented all planned activities, and even more.First of all, instead of the planned two teachers per mobility, we took 3 teachers, because we achieved quality budget management in a joint agreement.
We carried out all planned activities through mobilities in Italy, Greece and Croatia (visits to ports, container terminals, maritime faculty, ecological association, port warehouses, coast guard, oil storage for port needs, visits to historical ports and sites, naval cemeteries, maritime photography museums). All activities were then followed up by student work on presentations, discussions, blogs, questionnaires, videos, etc.




<< Results >>

Through a large number of activities and work on their analyses, students achieved a high level of independence and strengthened their skills in navigating different new situations with new colleagues and teachers
- they increased their communication in English
- they developed new forms of tolerance in different cultures and mentalities
- they adapted to staying in unfamiliar families
- they learned the value of the port as an important economic and transport hub throughout different times
- they learned about the importance of maritime professions
- they addressed the topics of ecology in maritime areas, especially in terms of maintaining clean seas and proper food storage
- they created a series of videos, photographs, presentations, blogs, digital works, and surveys related to the topic
- they participated in the presentation of the project outside the school premises
- the teachers promoted the project at the County expert council of teachers
- they regularly informed the Teachers council about the progress of the project
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2024-1-HU01-KA210-SCH-000248009.title: SOBER: Stop, Observe, Breath, Expand, and Respond
2024-1-HU01-KA210-SCH-000248009.summary:
<< Objectives >>

By sustaining a diverse, inclusive, equitable and international partnership, we want 
13-16 year olds: to reduce stress, anxiety, engage with the world around, have a positive effect on various aspects of mental health, improve communication and emotional awareness and reinforce empathy competence

NGOs: to favour the self-directed progress and promote the human growth
