Mindful lifetyle will be thought as the way of life in all involvers' mind

2024-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000245626.title: MENS SANA IN CORPORE SANO. Food, nutrition, eating habits, health and disease at European schools as an (inter)cultural mirror
2024-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000245626.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to provide students with reliable and accurate information regarding food because we know how much physical and mental health are connected to a healthy diet and also wants to give space to the social and psychological function that food has both as a basic component of every convivial occasion , and because the pleasantness of the physical appearance, a natural consequence of an adequate diet, represents a clear facilitator of positive interpersonal and social relationships.

<< Implementation >>

The project will propose useful activities to increase the level of attention to lifestyles, to the coherent choice of the type of food and drinks consumed; to health, understood as the prevention of eating disorders and diseases and the attitude to a healthy mind in a healthy body, involving the five senses on a sensorial and emotional level; will propose a learning process, understood as a proactive desire to learn about tradition, types of foods and also consumption methods.

<< Results >>

Results will be strategies for intervention and promotion of healthy and sustainable nutrition and indispensable synergy between subjects involved in educational actions which will be increasingly stronger and coordinated, to continue to have a positive impact on lifestyles in favor of healthy behaviors and sustainable, also with the common objective of reducing inequalities and improving health of tomorrow's adults, given strategic importance for the country and for the well-being of citizens
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000254926.title: Wellness Well Web; WWW
2024-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000254926.summary:
<< Background >>

The Wellness Well Web (WWW) project was designed to address the increasing need to support students’ well-being in educational environments. In recent years, schools have faced growing challenges related to students’ mental health, emotional regulation and adoption of healthy lifestyles.
The project aimed to respond to these needs by integrating well-being into education through a holistic approach combining arts, music, sports, nutrition and mindfulness practices. In addition, the project promoted inclusion, diversity and intercultural understanding, contributing to the development of responsible and active citizens.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were:

To improve students’ awareness of mental health and well-being
To promote healthy lifestyle habits through education
To develop students’ social, emotional and intercultural competences
To support teachers in adopting innovative teaching approaches based on the 5E model
To foster inclusion, diversity and active participation
To strengthen cooperation between partner organisations at European level

<< Implementation >>

During the project implementation, we carried out a coherent set of activities aligned with the initial objectives:

- 12 virtual coordination meetings involving both staff and students  
- Continuous collaboration through digital tools (Google Drive, eTwinning platform, project website and social media channels)  
- 4 transnational mobilities hosted in Croatia, Türkiye, Poland and Italy  
- 3 project newsletters to disseminate results  
- Development of 1 academic paper based on pre- and post-test data collected from participating students  
- Design and implementation of 12 lesson plans focused on arts, nutrition, sports and music, based on the 5E instructional model  
- Creation of 1 Open Educational Resource (OER) for teachers  
- Production of 8 DIY short educational videos  
- Organisation of 1 online seminar on balanced nutrition with an external expert  
- Organisation of 1 online student congress on well-being  
- Implementation of 5 multiplier events at local level  
- 1 Learning, Teaching and Training Activity (LTTA)


<< Results >>

The project successfully delivered all planned outputs and achieved its objectives.

The main tangible results include:

- A comprehensive OER for teachers, including a literature review, structured lesson plans and methodological guidelines on well-being through arts, music, sports and nutrition  
- An academic paper based on pre- and post-test data collected from students in four partner schools, showing measurable improvement in awareness of well-being and healthy lifestyles  
- A series of short DIY educational videos (1–2 minutes) published online to promote student engagement and dissemination  
- An online student congress on well-being, where students actively presented their work and shared experiences  
- An online seminar led by an external expert on balanced nutrition  
- 5 multiplier events involving local communities and stakeholders  

In addition, all outputs were made accessible through digital platforms (project website, eTwinning and shared repositories), ensuring sustainability and wide dissemination.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000257685.title: The Magical World of Math
2024-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000257685.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we recognised a widespread need to make mathematics more engaging, inclusive, and connected to real life. Many students perceive mathematics as abstract and complex, which can lead to low motivation and poor confidence. Our schools also identified a need for innovative teaching strategies that combine mathematics with culture, history, technology, and games. By addressing these needs, the project aimed to reduce anxiety surrounding mathematics, promote creative and collaborative learning, and demonstrate to students that mathematics is present in everyday life and throughout European cultural heritage

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to make mathematics more engaging, accessible, and meaningful for students. We aimed to demonstrate that mathematics is not only a school subject, but also an integral part of culture, history, technology, and everyday life. By implementing the project, we aimed to increase students’ motivation and confidence, reduce anxiety about learning mathematics, and promote innovative teaching methods for teachers. Another important objective was to encourage international cooperation and cultural exchange, helping students and teachers to develop teamwork, communication skills, and a stronger sense of European identity.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented a series of international mobilities and year-long school activities that combined mathematics with games, culture, history, and technology. In Italy, Greece, Croatia, and Turkey, students and teachers took part in workshops, seminars, cultural visits, and collaborative projects that linked mathematical concepts to traditional games, the Golden Ratio, and modern technology. Participants co-created strategic board games and later transformed them into digital applications. Alongside the mobilities, online activities through eTwinning and Twinspace ensured continuous collaboration, resource sharing, and dissemination of knowledge. All activities were documented and compiled into a digital eBook, which included lesson plans, worksheets, and teaching resources to support sustainability. 

<< Results >>

The project produced a wide range of concrete outputs and results. The main intellectual output was a digital eBook containing lesson plans, worksheets, and teaching materials that show how mathematics can be taught through games, culture, history, and technology. Students created original strategic board games and digital applications, which demonstrated mathematical reasoning in practice. Teachers developed innovative lesson activities that are now available for broader use. Additionally, the project produced videos, photos, presentations, and online resources that were shared through eTwinning and Twinspace. Beyond these outputs, the project achieved significant results in student learning: participants gained greater confidence in mathematics, improved their problem-solving and teamwork skills, and developed intercultural awareness and a sense of European identity. Teachers strengthened their professional skills and motivation, ensuring that the project’s impact will continue in future initiatives.

2024-1-LV01-KA210-SCH-000243828.title: Transformation of informal music education of Croatia, Latvia and Spain in the digital era
2024-1-LV01-KA210-SCH-000243828.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project objectives are:
1) to create the digital ON-LINE EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS for the children music schools and hobby classes of ES, HR and LV using the new approach of the creative and productive music education of the 21st century;
2) to increase the DIGITAL CAPACITY of the music teachers through testing and practicing the new approach of productive music education in ES, HR and LV.

<< Implementation >>

Project activities: 1 online kick-off meeting; 3 transnational meeting/training/testing events in ES, HR and LV; 3 dissemination events/concerts with the local communities in ES, HR and LV; 1 online digital music book developed by all partners; 3 videos (in Youtube) about the practical advice on usage of the new music education approach in ES, HR and LV; 3 evaluation surveys after training/testing events, communication activities in social media of ES, HR and LV, project management activities.

<< Results >>

1) Educated 24 teachers about the theoretical & practical usage of the creative/productive music education approach in children music schools & hobby classes of ES, HR, LV ; 2) prepared & tested on-line education material with arrangements of 6 songs of ES, HR, LV & 3 refugee songs from Ukraine; 3) organized 3 transnational meeting/training/testing events & 3 dissemination events (for at least 240 people) in ES, HR, LV; 4) 3 evaluation surveys; 5) at least 20 posts & articles in social media.
topics: Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas
Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

2024-1-NL01-KA210-SCH-000256686.title: Developing a better curricular connection between pre-college and higher music education
2024-1-NL01-KA210-SCH-000256686.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project endeavours to establish a European reference framework and ensure quality assurance for the specialised pre-college level of music education, fostering a cohesive curricular alignment between pre-college music education (Pre-CME) and higher music education (HME).
It seeks to pinpoint, deliberate, and establish key competences, learning outcomes, and standardised quality measures that strengthen the interconnection between the levels of musical education.

<< Implementation >>

Mapping:
Gather data on integrating competence-based learning outcomes in Pre-CME and their correlation with HMEI admission requirements.
Field Study:
Explore learning outcome implementation in pre-college music education through reports, examples, and educator experiences.
Dissemination:
Share findings online via websites, newsletters, and a dedicated project website. Disseminate results through targeted activities like meetings, seminars, talks, webinars, and conferences.

<< Results >>

A report on European specialized Pre-CME, emphasizing competence-based learning outcomes and their correlation with HME admission criteria. The report give insight into pre-college music education, focusing on the transition to HME.
Included is a set of competences and learning outcomes for Pre-CME, serving as a reference for curricula development. The report supports further studies and encourages exploration of changes in pre-college music education frameworks.
topics: Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas

2024-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000248783.title: Listen To Your He(ART)
2024-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000248783.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for Erasmus+ funding because we believe that climate challenges don't violate borders. The collaboration between Poland, Romania, Lithuania, Croatia, and Turkey was a response to the exchange of intercultural experiences, corresponding to teachers who understand that climate change is global, the effects are often local, and that the best solutions emerge from dialogue and the sharing of diverse perspectives. We applied for the project to enable the transformative power of art (music, theater, technical arts) as a tool for empowerment. Essentially, art allows students to express their "I can do something organic," which is crucial for their mental health and social well-being, and to activate their activities in an interdisciplinary environment.

We addressed the gap in the teaching staff's competences regarding the division of various fields of knowledge and science (interdisciplinarity). The project became a space where teachers teach, like environmental studies with music, visual art, photography, and theater.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal was to equip students with competencies that would allow them to navigate a changing world. Understand the mechanisms of nature, climate change, and threats, and explain difficult concepts and phenomena in an accessible and engaging way using non-traditional teaching methods.
Strengthen and develop students' agency. Through creating songs and works of art, students became active creators of messages. Engaging students, including those from disadvantaged groups, in international activities strengthened their development, discovering their talents and passions that might have remained undiscovered in traditional teaching.
For the teaching staff, the goal was to break down barriers between subjects and teach holistically. Implement interdisciplinary projects recommended in current teaching. Develop and test new tools (scripts, guides) that enhance the teaching process and build better relationships with students.
Collaboration with partners aimed to build a European identity: Understanding that climate protection is a shared challenge that requires solidarity across borders. The goal was to exchange good practices and create universal educational materials.

<< Implementation >>

Four working meetings were held with all partners from Lithuania, Romania, Turkey, and Croatia (hours 4). These meetings focused on project organization, preparing documents, organizing field trips, preparing artistic and climate workshops, establishing School Clubs, preparing exhibitions, performances, and preparing a conference summarizing the project in Poland, as well as collecting current information regarding the project's implementation.
Two mobilities were organized and implemented: to Croatia from May 12th to 14th, 2025, and to Romania from November 23rd to 29th, 2025. Both meetings took place according to the planned program. Additionally, participants visited both Valpovo and Bacău.
Each school organized School Art and Climate Action Clubs. Students worked there, learning about climate threats and developing ways to combat them. They learned about new tools and methods of artistic expression in music, painting, dance, theater, etc., which helped them present climate issues. This led to the preparation of performances in schools and exhibitions of their works. A summary conference was organized in Poland, presenting the results of the project participants' work and promoting the project idea within the community.

<< Results >>

Material Project Results
1. E-Guide for Teachers: A comprehensive compendium containing ready-made lesson plans that combine climate education with artistic expression. This is a key tool for ensuring the project's sustainability.
2. Musical Theatre and Choral Performances: A series of original performances and concerts in which music became a vehicle for environmental knowledge.

2024-1-RS01-KA210-SCH-000248989.title: Panel mladih Poverenika za zaštitu ravnopravnosti – Mladi za ravnopravnost
2024-1-RS01-KA210-SCH-000248989.summary:
<< Background >>

Children and young people in Serbia are exposed to various forms of discrimination, most commonly due to age, but also based on nationality, ethnicity, or health condition. In 2023, the Commissioner received 135 age-related complaints, 62% of which concerned minors, while 78 complaints were linked to education and professional development—representing 13% of the total. However, school programs rarely address how to recognize and respond to discrimination, as such content is mostly covered in the elective subject of civic education, attended by less than half of all students. This highlights the need for a widely implemented, peer-adapted program promoting equality and tolerance. Experience shows that peer education is highly effective, encouraging active participation and exchange of personal experiences. The Commissioner’s Youth Panel has already carried out several initiatives, though with limited donor funding and a need for regular member renewal. The new cycle of the Panel aims to enhance awareness of discrimination, strengthen the institution’s visibility, and foster understanding of European human rights standards among young people.

<< Objectives >>

With this project, we wanted to influence the reduction of the level of discrimination against children and young people by better informing them about their rights and available protection mechanisms. Previous experience has shown that peer education gives good results when it comes to educating children and young people about recognizing and responding to various forms of discrimination. We also took into account that the human capacities of the Commissioner are not sufficient to have a wide coverage across primary and secondary schools in the Republic of Serbia, so the formation of a network of peer educators was one of the solutions. In addition, we wanted to systematize our previous experiences, practices and needs analysis into an education program on protection from discrimination, suitable for wider application in the education system and which will enable sustainability and long-term planning.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, a network of peer educators was developed, which significantly contributed to increasing the coverage of children and young people involved in training. Peer educators proved to be an important resource in the process of informing and empowering peers, because through personal example and active engagement, they encouraged the improvement of equality among young people. In parallel, an educational program was developed for students aged 12 to 18, focused on recognizing and responding to discrimination. The program was enriched with practical examples and working methods adapted to target groups, while the accompanying guide enabled teachers and educators to apply the content in a clear, interactive and age-appropriate manner. This provided a high-quality and sustainable tool for further spreading knowledge and developing the capacities of young people in the field of protection against discrimination. Aside from that, we implemeted 5 peer educations in schools in Serbia and organized a final conference for presentation of the project results.

<< Results >>

We achieved the following results: 21 total trained peer educators, developed educational program with accompanying guide, 111 students who attended peer education, 55 persons attended the final conference

2024-1-SE01-KA210-SCH-000247076.title: Nature in the Eye of a Digital World
2024-1-SE01-KA210-SCH-000247076.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to enhance digital competence and creativity in education by integrating technology with outdoor learning. The need for this initiative arose from the increasing demand for digitalization in schools, particularly after the COVID-19 pandemic, and the recognition that outdoor learning can be an effective complement to traditional classroom teaching. By collaborating with schools from different countries, we aimed to exchange best practices and develop innovative teaching methods that engage students in meaningful learning experiences.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to strengthen teachers' digital skills and pedagogical approaches by incorporating technology into outdoor education. Through this, we aimed to encourage creativity and innovation in teaching while promoting engaging and effective learning environments. Additionally, the project sought to facilitate international collaboration and knowledge exchange among partner schools, allowing educators to share best practices and inspire one another. 

Another important goal was to develop digital tools and lesson materials that enhance student engagement and learning outcomes. By combining digitalization with outdoor learning, we wanted to create new opportunities for interdisciplinary teaching and practical, real-world applications of knowledge. Finally, the project aimed to foster intercultural awareness and cooperation, helping teachers and students gain a broader perspective on education and learning practices across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The project was carried out through a series of structured activities designed to enhance both theoretical knowledge and practical skills. Workshops and training sessions were organized to introduce teachers to digital tools and their application in outdoor education.

<< Results >>

The project achieved the objectives defined at application stage by translating the core concept of combining digital tools with outdoor learning into concrete teaching practice across partner schools.

Concrete outcomes include lesson plans and learning scenarios developed and tested in multiple subjects, including Arts, Geography, Natural Sciences and Physical Education, as well as a shared bank of digital tools used for collaboration, outdoor learning, content creation and assessment.

A key achievement was the successful implementation of structured LTTAs with clear learning outcomes, supported by extensive participant feedback. In addition, the World Wildlife Day activity exceeded expectations in reach and measurability by engaging 271 students across four countries in an e book and quiz activity.

No original objectives were abandoned. Where schedules were adjusted, the changes were made to maintain or improve quality and to ensure that objectives were still achieved.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000250723.title: Razvijanje in izdelava didaktičnih igrač in iger
2024-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000250723.summary:
<< Background >>

Although professional staff in all partner institutions already had experience in creating didactic toys, this work was often fragmented and not sufficiently systematic, particularly in terms of inclusion, sustainability and digital support. There was a clear need to strengthen professional competences for designing and producing high-quality, purposefully structured didactic toys.
Another identified need was the lack of a structured system for sharing and reusing self-made didactic materials. Many valuable teaching tools remained stored within individual classrooms and were not accessible to the wider professional community. Staff also expressed the need for additional knowledge about using sustainable and natural materials and for meaningful integration of digital tools into daily pedagogical planning.
By connecting kindergartens from different cultural and educational contexts, the project aimed to strengthen professional confidence, innovation and motivation among staff and to improve the overall quality of early childhood education.


<< Objectives >>

Kindergarten Slovenska Bistrica aimed to improve the quality of pedagogical work through the development of high-quality didactic toys, including toys adapted for children with special educational needs. A key objective was the establishment of a digital library enabling systematic collection, borrowing and reuse of didactic toys and promoting the exchange of good practices.
Dječji vrtić Vukovar aimed to strengthen staff competences in using didactic toys in daily pedagogical practice, particularly in learning through play, movement and outdoor activities, and to support the development of children’s basic STEAM competences.
Kindergarten “7 Septemvri” Pehčevo aimed to increase the use of natural and locally available materials in toy production, connect traditional knowledge with modern pedagogical approaches, enhance international cooperation and upgrade its website to provide access to project content for professionals and parents.


<< Implementation >>

The project included international partner mobilities, professional workshops with external experts and practical development of didactic toys and games. Partners designed, tested and implemented toys made from sustainable and natural materials, including adaptations for children with special educational needs, and integrated them into daily pedagogical practice.
Regular digital cooperation took place through online meetings and the eTwinning platform. Each month, one partner prepared professional materials and led a joint discussion on selected topics related to didactic toys and games. The project also involved parents through workshops, presentations and guidance, and results were disseminated through partner websites and communication channels. The project concluded with a comprehensive final evaluation.


<< Results >>

The project resulted in the development of 55 high-quality didactic games and toys, including 17 toys designed for children with special educational needs. All toys were developed in accordance with professional, pedagogical and sustainability principles and are actively used in daily educational practice.
A digital library of didactic toys was established, enabling a structured overview, borrowing and reuse of the developed toys. The platform supports more systematic, accessible and professionally aligned planning of educational activities. A publicly accessible catalogue of didactic toys and a Parent Guide on high-quality didactic play were also prepared.
Project results were published on the official websites of partner organisations, ensuring broad accessibility at local and international levels. The kindergarten in North Macedonia also upgraded its existing website.
The project strengthened international cooperation, established regular professional exchange among partner organisations and created long-term partnerships. Children gained access to more diverse and higher-quality didactic materials, while educators enhanced their professional competences and international collaboration.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000269223.title: NO TIME  (Nature Observing Together: Integrating Monitoring for Ecosystems)
2024-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000269223.summary:
<< Background >>

The NO TIME (Nature Observing Together: Integrating Monitoring for Ecosystems) project was designed to strengthen students' environmental awareness and develop their knowledge and skills in the field of nature conservation, biodiversity and sustainable living. The partner schools recognized the need for a more innovative approach to environmental education through experiential learning, fieldwork and international cooperation. The needs analysis showed that many students have limited access to international projects and that they need to further develop digital, communication and civic competences. It also highlighted the importance of exchanging good practices between schools from different European countries in order to improve the quality of teaching. The project responded to these needs by bringing together students and teachers from Croatia, Portugal and Bulgaria in activities focused on nature observation, ecosystem monitoring, digital tools, sustainable habits and learning about the cultural and natural heritage of the partner countries. Special attention was paid to the inclusion of students with fewer opportunities and to creating an inclusive and supportive learning environment for all participants.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to raise students' awareness of environmental protection and biodiversity conservation through practical activities, international cooperation and the use of digital technologies. The project activities would encourage students to observe nature, understand local ecosystems and adopt responsible environmental behavior. The project also aimed to develop students' knowledge of plant and animal species, improve the digital competences of students and teachers using digital tools, and promote sustainable development, recycling and responsible use of natural resources. In addition, it would strengthen cooperation, communication and intercultural competences through international cooperation, empower students for active citizenship and enable the exchange of good practices among partner schools. Special attention was paid to the inclusion of students with fewer opportunities, ensuring equal access to all project activities. The project also supported the Erasmus+ priorities of digital transformation, inclusiveness and environmental sustainability.

<< Implementation >>

Students and teachers from all partner schools participated in educational, ecological and intercultural activities. This included nature observation, ecosystem research, plant and animal species identification and flora mapping using digital tools and online platforms. Students participated in workshops on environmental protection and clean-up actions, sustainable development and recycling, made birdhouses and feeders from recycled materials, beautified school gardens and the Green Roof, celebrated environmental events (e.g. Earth Day, World Water Day, etc.). Intensive online collaboration through the eTwinning platform enabled participants to exchange research results, photos, presentations and other digital content, while various digital tools were used to create videos, interactive materials and joint project results. International mobilities provided opportunities for workshops, field trips and visits to natural sites in partner countries, promoting the exchange of experiences, innovative educational practices and the European dimension of the project. The project results were widely disseminated through school websites, social networks, local media, parent-teacher meetings and public events.

<< Results >>

More than 60 teachers and 250 students from all three partner schools participated in the project activities and 12 mobilities were achieved for each school within the LTTA. Students’ ecological awareness was increased through practical activities such as nature observation, flora mapping, school gardening and building birdhouses. It also strengthened the digital competences of students and teachers by using tools including Padlet, Canva, Google Maps, Book Creator, Genially, LearningApps, Kahoot and TwinSpace to create digital content and joint project outputs. International cooperation improved intercultural understanding, communication skills and European identity. All project objectives were achieved, with particularly strong results in student engagement, digital outputs, international cooperation and long-term integration of project outputs into school activities.

2024-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000287092.title: Cut the waste
2024-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000287092.summary:
<< Background >>

The motivation for all our schools to join this project is to internationalize our schools, to discuss, compare, and transfer good practices regarding how to motivate students to promote an inclusive society, and also to learn more about sustainability in daily life. 
At the beginning of the project, we conducted a SWOT analysis among the teachers and students of all three schools. Common goals and needs we addressed:
1. To learn more about the sustainability of the school, about the types of waste and its sorting. 
2. Connecting with peers from other schools and countries and exchanging experiences.
3. Strengthening of language competencies for all students and teachers involved in the project.
4. Participation in European projects with other schools.
5. Inclusion of marginalized groups of students in work with their peers within the school, as well as work in an international environment. All the mentioned needs were addressed in three mobilities with students, as well as all other acctivities we conducted during the entire project.

<< Objectives >>

We set the objectives for this project. THE GENERAL OBJECTIVE was:
1. To promote sustainability and inclusion in everyday life practices.
THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES were:
1. To learn about the types of waste in the household and at school, how to recycle and reuse it, and to promote sustainable practices in gardening, visiting the sea, cultural sites and handling electronic devices for all students and their local communities.
2. To share the results of the project and disseminate them to the local community and schools, as well as to other schools in the countries involved.
3. To educate all students in the schools involved in the project, as well as other schools in our countries, about sustainability and its importance in everyday life.
4. To raise awareness of the importance of active citizenship of all students by developing their intercultural knowledge, sense of tolerance and acceptance of human diversity, non-discrimination and non-segregation.
5. Acquisition of foreign language skills (English) to overcome communication barriers and maximize opportunities for social and professional inclusion worldwide for target groups.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, they carried out a large number of activities aimed at achieving the goals of this project. We carried out three mobilities with students. Before each mobility, we selected students through a competition that was transparent, publicly available to everyone and inclusive. We included students with fewer opportunities. We prepared the selected students before each mobility: pedagogically for the activities that would take place during the mobility, we carried out language preparation because the main language of the project was English, and we also prepared them culturally for the visit to another country. Teachers involved in the project teams of all three schools prepared teaching scenarios for each mobility. During the mobility itself, we organized activities to get to know the students, then we worked on the teaching scenarios. We visited local waste disposal companies in each city to learn more about their work, and representatives of local authorities with the aim of introducing them to the project goals, activities and EU funding. We also visited nature parks. Throughout the project, students completed assignments, quizzes, and practical work, and the project team disseminated the project.

<< Results >>

The concrete result is three student mobilities. For the mobility in Italy, 7 students from Spain, 8 from Croatia and 15 from Italy were involved. For the mobility in Spain, 11 students from Croatia, 8 from Italy and 15 from Spain were involved. For the mobility in Croatia, 8 students from Spain, 8 from Italy and 15 from Croatia were involved. The results of these mobilities are strengthened students' competences and knowledge related to the topic of each mobility by 15% (which we verified with knowledge tests), strengthening language competences by 39% (verified with knowledge tests), more separated waste in bins at school by 25%, 4 activities carried out on each mobility, one of which was public. The result of the project is also 10 teaching scenarios for a total of 14 hours of teaching with sustainability topics from different areas that are applicable for subjects such as ecology, biology, homeroom teacher classes, vocational subjects in technical schools related to waste reduction in electronic activities. The scenarios have been downloaded 264 times in Croatia in the first four days after its publications. Partners in Italy and Spain shared the scenarios wiht 10 other schools as we planned.

2024-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000291370.title: Small Steps Lead to Big Changes
2024-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000291370.summary:
<< Background >>

We increasingly observe a range of health challenges among preschool children, including poor dietary habits, low physical activity, and emerging emotional and behavioral issues such as reduced concentration, irritability, and aggression. Many children spend excessive time in front of screens and consume fast food, sweets, and sugary drinks, negatively affecting their overall health and well-being.
Recognizing the pivotal role of early childhood education in prevention, we used our educational context as a foundation to foster lifelong healthy habits, socio-emotional skills, and holistic development. Through daily activities, we promoted physical activity, balanced nutrition, self-regulation, and emotional stability.
Through this partnership, we developed innovative and sustainable strategies to promote healthy lifestyles from the earliest age. We aimed to bring children closer to nature, raise awareness about sustainability, and emphasize the benefits of natural, wholesome foods. By doing so, we empowered children to make informed choices that enhance their health, well-being, and contribute to the wider community, while fostering capacity building, cross-cultural learning, and evidence-based educational practices.

<< Objectives >>

The objective of the project was to strengthen educators’ competencies in promoting healthy lifestyle habits, mental health, and environmental awareness. We aimed to equip educators with the skills to plan and implement engaging, developmentally appropriate activities that foster children’s physical health, emotional balance, and environmentally responsible behavior.
A key goal was to develop three thematic brochures for parents, as well as a comprehensive educators’ handbook containing effective methods, strategies, and recommendations for integrating environmental education and healthy lifestyle principles into daily kindergarten practice.
The project also aimed to enhance educators’ digital skills and their ability to creatively and purposefully apply ICT tools in working with children. By motivating children to spend time outdoors, adopt healthy habits, and develop a responsible attitude toward nature, we sought to raise broader societal awareness of these important topics.
Finally, the project aimed to foster knowledge exchange and the dissemination of good practices by training and empowering other educators, enabling them to implement similar initiatives in their own institutions and strengthen transnational cooperation 

<< Implementation >>

The project encompassed a series of structured and collaborative activities designed to enhance educators’ competencies and promote the overall well-being of children. The main activities included three Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities (LTTAs) focused on the following themes: Strategies for Promoting Children’s Mental Health, Steps Toward a Healthy Lifestyle, and Integration of Technologies and Applications in Physical Activity. These international educational events provided participants with new methodologies, practical tools, and opportunities for professional development and experience exchange.
Local activities with educators were also organized to apply the knowledge and skills acquired during the LTTAs. These activities directly contributed to the creation and piloting of the final project outputs.
A Handbook for Educators was developed, containing methods, practical examples, and recommendations for integrating environmental education and healthy lifestyle principles into everyday kindergarten practice.
Finally, training sessions were conducted with educators from other regions to disseminate the project results, promote good practices, and strengthen collaboration within the wider educational community.

<< Results >>

The project achieved a series of concrete and significant results that directly supported its objectives. A recognizable project logo and website were created to ensure visibility, effective dissemination, and communication among partners, educators, and parents. To engage children in a child-friendly and stimulating way, digital cartoon characters were developed, representing the project’s core values and conveying messages about healthy lifestyles, mental health, and environmental care.
Three parent brochures were produced, each with a specific thematic focus: Outdoor Games, Mental Health Tips, and Healthy Eating Habits and Sustainable Lifestyles. These materials provided families with practical advice and ideas on how to support children’s physical and emotional well-being at home.
For educators, a comprehensive handbook was developed, containing validated methods, activity proposals, and pedagogical guidance for integrating environmental education and healthy lifestyle principles into everyday kindergarten practice.
Finally, each partner institution designed an outdoor learning space, representing a lasting and sustainable result that will continue to benefit children beyond the project’s duration.

2024-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000293842.title: BE GREEN BE HEALTHY
2024-2-HR01-KA210-SCH-000293842.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project wants to draw students' attention on the impact that human activities have on the environment with particular regard to our eating habits . 2024-2-IT02-KA210-SCH-000286152.title: Significance of Sustainability
2024-2-IT02-KA210-SCH-000286152.summary:
<< Background >>

This project was initiated with the aim of instilling sustainable habits in individuals in the areas of global warming, environment, and climate change, and limiting negative consequences starting from schools. Through this project, individuals are given the chance to take an active role in the fight against these issues. We know the importance of raising individuals with sustainable habits; the transformation of teachers and students into agents of change will be a powerful catalyst for the transformation we need. The most important need that brought together the partner organizations in this project was the need to overcome the shortcomings in experience and practice in the field of sustainability. In addition to this need, efforts were also made to address other needs such as internationalization, increasing institutional capacity, developing collaborations with transnational institutions and colleagues, developing current and different teaching methods and techniques to instill sustainable habits in individuals, and networking.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of our project is to transform students into "agents of change" by instilling sustainable habits integrated into their daily lives. We aimed to extend the project's achievements beyond the school boundaries, positioning our students in leading roles in civic-participatory public activities to create a wave of social awareness.
Our strategic objectives are shaped by the following headings:
- Sustainable Behavioral Transformation: To achieve lasting and measurable behavioral changes that reduce ecological footprints by increasing participants' environmental awareness. - Institutional Capacity and Internationalization: To address gaps in implementation between partner institutions and develop innovative methodologies in environmental education through transnational collaborations.
- Training Change Agents: To enable teachers to integrate environmental education into the curriculum; to transform students into individuals who take active responsibility for climate change. - Networking and Shared Vision: To develop a common stance and a strong institutional vision against global problems by facilitating the exchange of best practices across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

Within the scope of our project, four physical mobilities and one virtual mobility were carried out. Project activities were supported by local initiatives. Teachers and students participated together in all mobility activities.
Mobility 1 focused on reducing fast fashion habits, promoting slow fashion, and encouraging responsible consumption and production behaviours. Mobility 2 promoted the repair and reuse of electronic devices instead of immediately discarding them when they malfunctioned. Mobility 3 aimed to reduce plastic use, encourage biodegradable materials, and promote the creation of new objects from waste plastic. Mobility 4 addressed sustainability in furniture, toys, and decoration through the reuse of wooden materials to create board games. Mobility 5 (virtual) focused on food waste sustainability, food waste prevention, and behaviours aimed at reducing food waste.
In addition, outdoor events, campaigns, and social responsibility initiatives involving civic participation were organised during each mobility period.

<< Results >>

The tangible results of the project are:
- An interactive website
- A basic level e-book
- An e-brochure
- An e-Dictionary
- An educational song
- Various classroom activities, civic participation-supported outdoor activities, campaigns, and social responsibility projects focusing on developing sustainable habits.
- Sample in-class activity plans (5) that allow for the exploration of sustainable living principles

Other results of the project include:
- Initiatives were taken to help students and families change unsustainable habits.
- Students experienced behaviors such as buying and using second-hand products.
- Teachers were helped to become leaders who promote sustainable living and green skills.
- Students and teachers reviewed their social and professional roles by becoming individuals with sustainable competencies.
- Public events and social media campaigns were organized to draw attention to RCP through civic participation and increase RCP awareness in the community. In addition to the achievements obtained, awareness has been raised about all of the EU's policies in the field of "Green Transformation".

2024-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000293349.title: MEDVEDKI UPANJA - do znanja in veščin na igriv način
2024-2-SI01-KA210-SCH-000293349.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project with the aim of professionalizing our organization, which operates as a non-governmental, non-profit institution of private law. Regardless of its clear focus and goals, the NGO sector rarely meets the financial requirements to execute projects that are highly important for society, yet often perceived as merely alternative in a broader context.
The core mission of our organization is to create a space for inquiry-based learning. Practical work in Slovenian public schools reveals staff burnout, the challenge of managing various modern behavioral issues among children and adolescents, and a lack of room to explore new, structurally more demanding learning approaches. All too often, traditional schooling methods prevail; though updated with contemporary practices, they fail to develop into sustainable solutions.
At the Institute for Art Research Maribor, we draw on our first-hand pedagogical experience to ease the burden of academic curricula through art, utilizing handicraft, visual arts, and theatrical methodologies.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project, we aimed to make pupils feel like active co-creators of the learning process. We designed the creative upcycling of textiles into functional products, alongside interactive educational content, in a way that is accessible and not overly demanding for the students. At the same time, it introduces current global topics that are sufficiently distinct from the mandatory school curriculum. This prevents academic pressure or fear of grading and negative consequences if the material is not immediately mastered. The integrated digital content is short, concise, and offers numerous entry points for discussion beyond the standard curriculum. The fact that this content is embedded directly into an appealing final product provides significant added value to the entire process.

<< Implementation >>

Four key activities were implemented within the framework of the project. The first activity was an international project meeting in Maribor, aimed at introducing and networking the partner and participating organizations, experts, individuals, and involved pupils. The second activity focused on the creation and direct realization of the project outputs; it took place within the local environments of all participating countries and served as preparation for joint presentations. The third and fourth activities consisted of international mobilities to Konya (Turkey) and Novigrad-Cittanova (Croatia), where the final presentation of achievements and dissemination of results took place during the "Days of the Bears of Hope" events

<< Results >>

The concrete tangible results (project outputs) represent an integrated model that successfully combines sustainable development, the circular economy, and the digitalization of education. The core outputs of the project are unique bear puppets and toys, which are the product of the handicraft and fine motor skills of the pupils from the Janko Padežnik Primary School in Maribor. The items were predominantly hand-sewn, emphasizing the importance of preserving traditional craft skills among youth.
Utilizing textile remnants based on upcycling principles, the creative hands of the children also crafted a wide range of functional products, such as unique keychains, decorative pillows, headwear, scarves, and handmade notebooks. These products serve as a physical medium for spreading environmental messages and raising awareness about biodiversity.
A significant pillar of the project is its digital component. Participants from the Institute for Art Research Maribor developed interactive digital content embedded into innovative, ready-to-scan QR codes affixed to the products. Furthermore, the Institute designed the original framework for the educational game "The Past."

2024-2-TR01-KA210-SCH-000281083.title: Exploring Technology, Human Intelligence, and Comparative Ethics in AI

There will be four international mobilities for cross-cultural exchange and collaboration. Students and AI systems will be tested on ethical scenarios, with results analyzed and shared. Additionally, we will organize dissemination events and publish the final comparative analysis report for broader educational impact.

<< Results >>

The comparison between human and AI responses to ethical dilemmas will provide valuable insights, published in a final report. Additionally, we aim to strengthen cross-cultural collaboration, raise awareness of ethical issues in AI, and provide resources that can be integrated into educational curricula across partner schools and beyond.
topics: Human rights and rule of law

2025-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000350151.title: Música para el Crecimiento: Integrando Sonido, Melodía, Ritmo y Movimiento en la Educación Infantil
2025-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000350151.summary:
<< Objectives >>

To promote the comprehensive development of participants through musical education and rhythm exploration, fostering global learning experiences that stimulate the sensory-motor, cognitive, linguistic, emotional, and social development of students. To discover the world around them and improve their relationships and communication with others. Additionally, European citizenship is promoted, an ecosocial component is integrated, and key competencies are encouraged.

<< Implementation >>

The project is structured around four fundamental activities that encompass the exploration of the world through sound, the creation of melodies from the heart, and the exploration of rhythm and movement. These activities aim to promote environmental awareness, artistic expression, and comprehensive development through music and movement. The final evaluation will serve to collect the results, achievements, and learnings obtained.

<< Results >>

Development of sensorimotor, cognitive, linguistic, emotional, and social skills by the participants.
Music Box: A toolkit that compiles best practices, educational resources, and effective methodologies for teaching music and integral development through music. This guide will facilitate the replicability of the project and promote educational innovation as well as musical learning in different educational contexts.

2025-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000352427.title: Innovative Peer Support
2025-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000352427.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Through this project, we aim to combat peer bullying by raising awareness, developing innovative strategies, and fostering inclusive school environments. By equipping teachers with practical tools and promoting cross-cultural collaboration, we strive to reduce bullying incidents, enhance students' social-emotional skills, and create safer, more supportive educational spaces for all.

<< Implementation >>

We will conduct teacher training workshops, develop inclusive activities using Web 2.0 tools, organize film screenings and role-play sessions, and facilitate cultural exchanges. These activities aim to raise awareness, build empathy, and equip educators with strategies to combat peer bullying and promote inclusive school environments.

<< Results >>

We expect to achieve increased awareness of peer bullying, enhanced teacher skills in addressing bullying, and the creation of inclusive school environments. Additionally, we aim to develop practical tools, foster cross-cultural collaboration, and reduce bullying incidents through innovative strategies and activities.

2025-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000358185.title: INSPIRE – INclusion, STEAM, Promotion of well-being & InteRcultural Exchange
2025-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000358185.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to promote inclusion and diversity in education, enhance students' interest and excellence in STEM, and improve well-being at school. It seeks to bridge the gender gap in technology, foster responsible AI use, and develop digital skills. Additionally, it strengthens intercultural collaboration among students and teachers, creating a more inclusive, innovative, and future-oriented learning environment.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes hands-on STEAM workshops, AI and digital skills training, and collaborative challenges to promote inclusion. Students will work in international teams, developing projects that integrate STEM and social responsibility. Well-being activities will address screen time balance and mental health. Dissemination will involve social media, Erasmus+ platforms, and school events to maximize impact.

<< Results >>

The project will enhance students’ digital and AI skills, increase interest in STEM, and promote inclusion and well-being. Teachers will adopt innovative methodologies and improve international collaboration. Schools will integrate project outcomes into their curricula, ensuring long-term impact. Dissemination activities will raise awareness in local and educational communities, fostering a more inclusive and technologically prepared future.

2025-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000362937.title: Full STEAM ahead!
2025-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000362937.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Full STEAM ahead! aims to enhance the teaching of STEAM in formal and non-formal educational centres by designing and
implementing innovative, inclusive, engaging, and easily replicable teaching proposals that foster meaningful learning for all.
It also seeks to streamline teaching efforts, facilitate the digital transformation of teachers and students, popularise STEAM,
and establish a framework for genuine access to a variety of classroom proposals through active methodologies.

<< Implementation >>

The project involves the design,implementation, testing and dissemination of innovative didactic micro-sequences and
practical experiments in STEAM in short video format applicable to Early Childhood, Primary and Secondary stages. These
micro-sequences are aimed at solving a problem posed in the form of a question and will be carried out step by step with the
active participation of students using low-cost materials, under an investigative approach based on UDL and active, handson
methodologies

<< Results >>

A collection of quality modular digital products (micro-sequences and practical experiments in STEAM) based on a
competency-based educative approach for active, inclusive, motivating, and participatory student learning will be created.
We aim for the implementation of these products in classrooms of real educational centres both inside and outside the
project to serve as a driving force for methodological change towards the popularization and democratization of STEAM and
digital transformation.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2025-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000365932.title: Connecting Teaching and Research for better Learning
2025-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000365932.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The CTRL+ project aims to develop research leads, reference figures in their schools who sustain teacher inquiry communities that: 
-Integrate relevant academic research results into teaching interventions;
-Collect, analyse and act on data from teaching, through cycles of peer observation and reflection; and
-Systematise and share professional knowledge.
The final goal is to foster continuous improvement in teaching skills, student outcomes and increased trust in teachers as professionals.

<< Implementation >>

To achieve this, CTRL+ combines:
-Face-to-face and online capacity building for Erasmus+ teams, supported by a Moodle course;
-Development of guides, observation tools and systematised research engagement practices hosted on the website; 
-Multiplier training sessions and implementation of inquiry cycles with school staff;
-Qualitative analysis of the impact of research leads and peer observation;
-Networking and dissemination activities to raise awareness and increase uptake of results.

<< Results >>

The expected results of CTRL+ are:
-Evidence-informed interventions to address local challenges in the partner schools;
-Trained staff in schools who can lead teacher inquiry cycles;
-Embedded mechanisms and tools for designing, monitoring and measuring the impact of interventions;
-Online training resources for prospective research leads and schools to develop strategies for engaging with research; and
-An emerging European-level network of teachers committed to evidence-informed practice.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff
Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2025-1-FR01-KA210-SCH-000353430.title: Bien être et apprendre autrement

2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000350326.title: Echoes of the Past: Crafting Future Leaders Through Heritage and Environment
2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000350326.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to foster awareness of cultural and natural heritage as drivers of social and economic development. By integrating heritage-based learning into education, it seeks to enhance students' 21st-century skills, promote intercultural understanding, and encourage sustainable practices. The project will also strengthen collaboration among partner schools, empowering participants to preserve heritage while contributing to community growth and environmental sustainability.

<< Implementation >>

The project will involve various activities, including transnational study visits, student presentations, collaborative workshops, and cultural exchanges. Participants will explore heritage-based entrepreneurship, visit significant natural and cultural sites, and engage in peer-learning sessions. Digital tools, social clubs, and creative projects like vlogs and blogs will support knowledge sharing. Teachers will integrate project results into curricula and organize sustainability-focused events.

<< Results >>

The project will lead to increased awareness of the importance of cultural and natural heritage in social and economic development. Participants will develop key skills such as critical thinking, collaboration, and intercultural communication. The project will also produce educational materials, best practices guides, and student-led projects like blogs and videos. Schools will adopt sustainable practices, and the project's impact will extend to local communities and educational networks.

2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000351687.title: Artificial Intelligence is Coming
2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000351687.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project modernizes English language education by integrating AI tools to enhance students’ speaking, listening, writing, reading and digital literacy skills. It boosts teacher competencies through targeted training, develops AI-supported lesson plans, and establishes a collaborative learning framework. The goal is to foster innovation, inclusivity, and lifelong learning, aligning with European educational priorities.

<< Implementation >>

The project will involve teacher training workshops, the creation of AI-supported lesson plans, and interactive activities to engage students in real-world language tasks. Schools will develop digital libraries and host dissemination events, such as workshops, presentations, and online campaigns. Collaboration between institutions will be fostered through virtual meetings, eTwinning projects, and shared resources.

<< Results >>

The project expects to achieve improved language proficiency and digital skills among students, increased teacher readiness to use AI tools, and stronger collaboration between partner institutions. Outputs will include lesson plans, a digital resource library, and dissemination materials. Long-term results include enhanced inclusivity, better educational outcomes, and alignment with European goals for innovation and lifelong learning.

2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000352946.title: Ethical dilemma: AI or me?
2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000352946.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The core objective is to develop teachers' and students' competencies in independent, responsible, ethical, and informed use of AI tools in creative writing by production of the guidelines and teaching scenarios applicable to various educational and cultural contexts.Transnational mobility will enable the internationalization of institutions and create a vivid learning community, sharing good practices at schools and in the local communities.

<< Implementation >>

The activities will be international, live and online: 
1. Collaborative planning workshop and design of innovative educational materials in Trabzon	
2. Creative writing workshop with human-supervised use of artificial intelligence in Alba Iulia
3. Debate workshop on ethical dilemma: " AI in creative writing - yes or no?" in Czestochowa	
4. Festival of AI-assisted poetry in Varaždin.

<< Results >>

We expect the following results:
1. Teachers acquire digital and pedagogical competencies needed for teaching with AI and create innovative educational materials
2. Students created a multimedia collection of 40 poems in various European languages using AI under human-supervised conditions
3. Students debated on ethical dilemma: "AI in creative writing - yes or no"
4th all participants organized an AI-assisted poetry as an international community that promotes European values and diversity.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000354561.title: OD EKRANA BJEŽI UŽIVO SE POVEŽI!
2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000354561.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Nowadays, mobiles have become a medium by which we perform a lot of daily activities in every sphere of life. The negative sides of their excessive use like alienation or loss of contact with reality are being ignored. The educational system pays too little attention to the negative sides of the excessive use of mobiles in the development of adolescents. Therefore, with this project we want to encourage young people to spend quality time in society without being distracted by electronic devices.

<< Implementation >>

The activities we will implement will focus on group dynamics and sports recreation, paying special attention to the inclusion of students in disadvantaged socioeconomic positions, from geographically dislocated areas and members of national minorities and migrants. On each mobility, we will engage in team sports in order to achieve social cohesion, while with group dynamics activities we will practice "face to face" communication in a foreign language, in order to improve communication skills.

<< Results >>

We expect students to get to know each other better in an international environment, to recognize the value of "face to face" communication so that our diversity becomes a resource, not an obstacle. Through the Offline Incubator and Infographics, we will educate the target group about the benefits of disconnecting from digital devices and encourage the creation of quality interpersonal connections with an emphasis on two-way communication.

2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000356214.title: Aktivan život - zdrava budućnost - Program za izborne aktivnosti u učeničkim domovima
2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000356214.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project will develop the optional activity "Active life - healthy future", along with the creation of digital materials with the aim of raising students' awareness of the importance of movement and environmental awareness.
The goal of the project is to encourage student dormitories to include the activity "Active life - healthy future" in their annual plans and programs, which will have a preventive, curative and formative role in terms of quality use of students' free time.

<< Implementation >>

During the duration of the project, three meetings will be held with the aim of the project teams working together to achieve and monitor the results. Furthermore, two student mobilities will be carried out in Croatia and Poland, during which the activities mentioned below will be held related to the achievement of the project's goals. During the project, workshops on the environment, sustainable development, e-cycling and functional fitness training will be held. Final conferences will be held

<< Results >>

A program was developed for a completely new optional activity "Active life - healthy future", which will be included in the Annual Plan and Work Program of the Varaždin Student Home and the curriculum of the partner school in the following school years. Developed digital skills, competences for teamwork, increased level of self-confidence among students and that the same program will be available and implemented in all other homes and secondary schools throughout Europe.

2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000356497.title: Artificial Intelligence for Teachers
2025-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000356497.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to enhance AI literacy among elementary and high school teachers, improve teaching methodologies through AI integration, and develop comprehensive AI educational materials. It focuses on fostering a COP for continuous professional development in AI education, influencing educational policies and practices, and ensuring the sustainability and scalability of project outcomes. The project also prioritizes inclusivity, catering to educators with diverse AI proficiency levels.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement a Kick-off Meeting in Zagreb, develop AI-focused Educational Materials, create a Knowledge Assessment Tool, and conduct a Transnational Meeting for evaluation. An Interactive Online Course will be launched, followed by a Piloting and Mentorship Program for real-world application. The project concludes with a comprehensive Dissemination activity to promote outcomes and share learnings widely.

<< Results >>

The project is expected to enhance AI literacy among educators, improve teaching methodologies through effective AI integration, and lead to the creation of high-quality educational materials. It aims to establish a supportive community of practice, positively impact student engagement and learning, and foster a broad adoption of AI in education. The project anticipates influencing educational policies and demonstrating sustainable, scalable models for AI integration in teaching.
topics: Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

The main objectives of the project are:

3. Equipping participants with lifelong skills such as teamwork, problem-solving, and innovation in sustainability.

2025-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000356049.title: Empowering Schools: Balancing Digital Life and Social Engagement
2025-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000356049.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We want to build empowering schools that raise individuals who care about their families and friends, who are sensitive to their surroundings and environment, who have active minds and take an active role in society, who uphold and internalize the European Union citizenship values, and who live in peace without excluding others. Thus, we aim to equip our schools with various recreational activities and attractive clubs so that our students will choose to live in real life, not in virtual world.

<< Implementation >>

The 4 transnational mobilities have 4 focal topics: physical-mental health, European values, digital well-being and civic engagement. The first mobility will be held at the Croatian NGO which will organise panels, lectures and workshops for teachers. The second will be hosted by Turkish school where sports activities will be carried out. The Greek school will design creative writing activities. Lastly, the Italian school will put forward speaking activities with the help of AI and Web2 tools.

2025-1-NL01-KA210-SCH-000351546.title: Fostering Critical Thinking in Genocide Education Through Child Survivors' Testimonies
2025-1-NL01-KA210-SCH-000351546.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The GE-CT project aims to strengthen teachers’ and educators’ competences in genocide education by focusing on children’s experiences in genocide. It will develop engaging, student-centered educational materials, co-created by experts, teachers, and students. Through teacher training, pilot testing, and classroom exhibitions, the project will enhance critical thinking, historical awareness, and empathy, ensuring sustainable use of resources in schools.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes developing 8 expert-designed activity plans on children in genocide, complemented by 5 teacher-created plans during training seminars. Teachers will be trained in their use and will pilot test them in schools in Croatia and the Netherlands. Students and teachers will co-create bilingual classroom exhibitions based on the materials. The project will also include evaluation, dissemination, and digital publication of resources for long-term use.

<< Results >>

The project will produce 8 expert-developed and 5 teacher-created activity plans on children in genocide, available online for widespread use. At least 10 trained teachers will implement these plans, benefiting 200+ students. Four bilingual classroom exhibitions will be co-created, engaging schools and communities. The project will strengthen teachers' competencies, enhance students' critical thinking, and ensure sustainable access to genocide education materials.

2025-1-PT01-KA210-SCH-000352676.title: Next-Gen Classrooms: AI, Inclusion and Innovation
2025-1-PT01-KA210-SCH-000352676.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to foster inclusive education and entrepreneurship by integrating AI and assistive technologies, ensuring equal learning opportunities for all students. It seeks to develop essential skills such as creativity, problem-solving, and adaptability while promoting an entrepreneurial mindset. Through hands-on activities, collaboration, and digital tools, participants will strengthen teamwork and prepare for future careers in an inclusive and technology-driven society.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes workshops and digital collaborations. Key activities involve AI and assistive technology training, virtual company creation, entrepreneurship challenges, study visits, role-playing, and inclusive business design. Participants will engage in cultural exchanges, digital content creation, and eTwinning collaborations to develop skills, raise awareness of inclusion, and promote innovation. Non-formal learning methods will ensure an interactive and impactful experience.

<< Results >>

The project will enhance entrepreneurial, digital, and inclusive skills among participants. Expected results include the creation of virtual companies, business plans, digital resources, posters, videos, and podcasts. The project will support the development of soft skills, shaping participants into more well-rounded individuals. Strengthened collaboration between schools and businesses will ensure long-term impact, fostering innovation, social responsibility, and a more inclusive workforce.

2025-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000350314.title: Each Young Excluded is a New Potential
2025-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000350314.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our project aims to enhance digital literacy among students by adopting a student-centered approach, equipping them with social skills to strengthen social interactions. Simultaneously, it aims to support students in coping with social exclusion in the educational environment by enhancing teachers' knowledge and skills in pedagogical approaches, developing adaptive
teaching methods, implementing inclusive education practices, and providing students with various learning opportunities.

At the event in Romania, 3 students and 2 teachers from Turkey, Croatia, and Latvia will participate. In the event in Turkey,there will be 3 students and 2 teachers from Croatia, Romania, and Latvia. The event in Latvia will involve teacher training with 3 teachers each from Turkey, Croatia, and Latvia. The event in Croatia will include 2 teachers and 4 students from
Latvia, Turkey, and Romania. Additionally, virtual meetings and cultural integration activities will also be organized.

<< Results >>

Through our project, we expect 20 teachers to improve their teaching methods and 48 disadvantaged students to enhance their digital and social skills, thereby reducing the risk of exclusion.  We aim to raise environmental awareness and create awareness about sustainability, social integration, and cultural diversity. This process will increase students' access to equal opportunities, strengthen academic success and social responsibility, and provide a solid foundation for their future.

2025-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000359177.title: Smart Media, Internet Literacy & Ethics
2025-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000359177.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project aims to help teachers and students recognize how media shapes their perceptions and beliefs, develop critical and independent thinking when interpreting media content, and assess its values and consequences. It also seeks to enhance problem-solving skills, encourage responsible content creation, and enable them to identify, avoid, and critique harmful or offensive media.

<< Implementation >>

All activities are carefully planned to achieve the project's objectives, including the eTwinning project, workshops, courses, institutional visits, project logo creation, comics, mobility reports, dissemination efforts, promotional materials, educational videos, special event days, exhibitions, and public events with media coverage. Additionally, an Internet Safety Guide for students will be developed.

<< Results >>

After the project, we expect both short-term and long-term effects. Participants will share their workshop and training insights to raise awareness about media literacy, responsible digital content creation, combating fake news, and maintaining a healthy relationship with technology. Benefits will include improved communication skills, continued collaboration, and further international engagement.
