-To give ideas to other schools about what can be done about peer bullying.
-Increasing the behavior of our students and other students in keeping the environment clean and using recycling bins as necessary.
-Express the subject (more effectively) with digital materials
- To recognize and promote the values and culture of the European Union.

2025-1-TR01-KA210-SCH-000361527.title: Breaking the Walls: Addressing Social Isolation in the Age of Social Media
2025-1-TR01-KA210-SCH-000361527.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We want to build up digital well-being, emotional resilience, and social inclusion by equipping students with the skills to navigate the digital world responsibly while maintaining real-world connections.
By the project’s end, participants will be more digitally aware, emotionally resilient, and socially engaged, creating a lasting impact on schools and communities.

<< Implementation >>

To achieve our project objectives, we will implement three international mobility activities, workshops, and training sessions focused on digital well-being, emotional resilience, and social inclusion.

<< Results >>

Expected Results for Teachers:
    • Better teaching strategies 
    • Increased confidence 
    • Mental health and online safety. 
    • A network of international educators
Expected Results for Schools & Communities:
    • Sustainable digital well-being programs 
    • Stronger international partnerships
    • Greater awareness among parents and local stakeholders 
 We expect participants to be more digitally aware, emotionally resilient, and socially engaged, ensuring big impact on education

2025-2-MT01-KA210-SCH-000371243.title: Blue Future: Sustainable Living with Water Literacy
2025-2-MT01-KA210-SCH-000371243.summary:
<< Objectives >>

In our EU-wide project, we want to draw attention to the global water crisis and raise public awareness in line with the  policies and strategies of the European Union for the protection and sustainable use of water resources. The project, which  is a partnership of secondary schools across the EU, aims to increase water literacy through workshops, trainings, field  observation trips and experiment-based learning methods.

<< Implementation >>

The target group of the project consists of teachers and students working in educational institutions. In the academic supported trainings organized by the host institutions in the project, participant teachers will be given training on Water  Literacy. Student-centered activities, travel observation activities, experiment-based learning environments based on  scientific methods will be organized and students will be made aware of water literacy.

<< Results >>

With the activities of the targeting teachers and students,the development of water literacy awareness at the social level will  be ensured.The trainings to be given to teachers will ensure the professional development of teachers in this field and will be  integrated into the education services of the institutions.The project activities will provide the opportunity for the exchange of  good practices among the participating institutions and the dissemination of EU culture

2026-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000466832.title: BRIDGE
2026-1-DE03-KA210-SCH-000466832.summary:
<< Objectives >>

German and Croatian students work together to reimagine and artistically enhance real places from their communities, using immersive technology. Two student exchanges, supported by teacher preparation meetings, result in immersive exhibition where visitors experience collaborative virtual artworks. The project builds sustainable partnership between schools while demonstrating innovative pedagogy integrating digital tools, place-based learning, and cultural exchange.

<< Implementation >>

(1) Teacher Preparation Meeting in GER (11/26)—pedagogical alignment and technical training. (2) Teacher Preparation Meeting in CRO (3/27)—technical deepening and logistics finalisation. (3) German students travel to Split (5-6/27)—collaborative digital art-making with Croatian peers, exploring student-identified places. (4) Croatian students travel to GER (11/27)—reciprocal exchange and artwork refinement. (5) Immersive Exhibition (11/27-02/28) —collaborative artworks in both locations.

<< Results >>

1) immersive virtual artworks co-created by German-Croatian students (2) Professionally curated immersive exhibition in both GER and CRO, featuring VR installations and supporting documentation. (3) Exhibition catalogue, video documentary, and digital archive preserving student work and project process. (4) Comprehensive educator resource guide enabling other schools to replicate the project. (5) Sustained international partnership

2026-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000451510.title: Active Lifestyles: Connecting Europe through Physical Activity, Healthy Living, and Nature.
2026-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000451510.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project combats screen dependency and eco-anxiety through a "One Health" approach. Objectives: 1) Improve mental well-being via "Digital Detox" and nature therapy; 2) Transform sport into eco-action (Plogging/Reforestation); 3) Build resilience and inclusion through cooperative sports (Herri Kirolak) and adventure challenges; 4) Create a European Network of "Healthy Schools" that integrates active habits and sustainability into their daily curricula, ensuring lasting institutional change.

<< Implementation >>

We implement a "Journey through Elements" via 3 physical mobilities and 2 virtual summits: 1) Portugal (Blue): Plogging, kayaking, and water analysis; 2) Spain (Green Mind): "Digital Detox", Forest Bathing (Shinrin-Yoku), and reforestation; 3) Croatia (Green Peaks): Adventure hiking (Skywalk) and heritage orienteering. Virtual activities include a Creative Hackathon and a Policy Summit. Methodology relies on Service-Learning and gamification to merge fitness with civic engagement.

<< Results >>

Outcomes include tangible Open Educational Resources (OER): 1) "The Healthy School Charter" (policy paper adopted by schools); 2) "Green Mind Manifesto" (mental health guide); 3) "Comparative Water Report" (Science); 4) "Active Heritage Maps" & Final Documentary. Impact: Participants will demonstrate reduced stress (measured by Mood Meters), improved digital hygiene, and enhanced self-esteem. Schools will integrate these protocols, ensuring a legacy of active well-being policies.

hr.name: Srednja škola Fra Andrije Kačića Miošića

2026-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000454801.title: Resilience, Empathy, Safety, Prevention, Cooperation, Together
2026-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000454801.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Equip educators with evidence-based bullying prevention tools (15+ lesson plans, protocols)
Develop children's resilience through cognitive-behavioural games and emotional activities
Foster empathy via neuroscience-backed routines and perspective-taking exercises
Prevent cyberbullying with age-appropriate digital safety curricula and parent strategies
Create sustainable whole-school frameworks aligned with EU child protection standards

<< Implementation >>

4 LTTAs: 5-day trainings in Portugal/Romania/Croatia & Spain (bullying prevention/SEL strategies)
Cascade training: 170+ teachers trained (60 per LTTA participant)
15+ lesson plans developed for ages 3-12 (resilience games, digital safety)
Whole-school frameworks implementation (policies, monitoring systems)
Parent workshops (digital safety, empathy building)
Final multiplier event (100+ educators across Europe)

<< Results >>

25%+ bullying reduction across partner schools (observation grids)
170+ teachers trained via cascade model
1,200+ children gain SEL/resilience skills (ages 3-12)
15+ lesson plans and digital toolkits (open-access)
4 whole-school frameworks with EU-standard policies
20,000+ external reach (website/social media)
Sustainable expertise networks for KA220 follow-up

2026-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000456762.title: Smart Drops: AI-Driven Ecological Literacy for Water Sustainability and Wellbeing Promotion
2026-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000456762.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our project,Smart Drops, aims to strengthen water sustainability literacy among students aged 14–18 in Mediterranean regions affected by climate pressure. The project integrates structured environmental inquiry into school curricula using accessible digital tools and international cooperation. It seeks to improve students’ ecological knowledge, digital data skills and active citizenship,while strengthening schools’ capacity to embed sustainable education in long-term planning.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes AI-Driven Eco-Training for teachers, transnational mobilities focused on ecological field research, water data collection and intercultural exchange, and local long-term activities on climate and water management. Students participate in hybrid sustainability walks, policy workshops and youth dialogues. Results include a Digital Activity Booklet and a Water-AI educational map, embedded in school practice.

<< Results >>

The project targets a 40% increase in correct responses in environmental literacy surveys. Students will produce at least 10 local case studies and 20+ environmental data points for the Sustainability Map. A Water-AI Trend Map will be generated. Participation aims at 50% students with fewer opportunities. Dissemination includes 500+ website views, 100+ booklet downloads and interaction from at least 3 external schools and 100 external stakeholders.

2026-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000458428.title: Green Decisions: From Awareness to Action
2026-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000458428.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our project aims to transform eco-literacy from awareness into measurable action by developing decision-based tools that enable students to analyse, track and change their environmental habits. It strengthens teachers’ capacity to integrate water literacy, sustainability and digital tools into daily practice through transnational collaboration and shared reflection. It also integrates sustainability into school development and action plans, which ensures continuity beyond the project period.

<< Implementation >>

The project will be implemented through 4 interconnected activities progressing from exploration to action. Students will investigate real environmental challenges through field observation, produce environmental media outputs, design EcoShift action models, and apply behavior-change tools such as decision-based scenarios, habit trackers, and commitment cards. Each stage will be piloted in partner schools and disseminated through webinars and multiplier events to ensure transfer and replication.

<< Results >>

4 project activities will produce eco-literacy lesson plans, EcoShift behavior-change models, decision-based scenarios, and an Environmental Learning Guide (final output). Students will demonstrate measurable improvements in environmental responsibility and critical decision-making. Results will be disseminated via 4 webinars, 4 multiplier events, eTwinning, 4 e-newsletters, a press release, and the Erasmus+ Project Results Platform to ensure replication and long-term institutional integration.

2026-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000462922.title: "Brújula Inclusiva: Educación para los Valores Europeos y la Sostenibilidad."
2026-1-ES01-KA210-SCH-000462922.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project "Inclusive Compass_ Education for European Values and Sustainability" seeks to revitalize rural educational communities by addressing the digital divide and promoting European values. Our primary goal is to equip students with the tools to perform sustainability audits and use Artificial Intelligence (AI) ethically to solve local challenges. By modeling rural sustainability scenarios, students will transform from passive observers into active problem solvers.

<< Implementation >>

We will train teachers in Project Base Le to update 60% of curricula. Students will conduct sustainability audits and use ethical AI to model solutions for rural challenges, personalizing tasks for SEN learners. We’ll organize civic debate tournaments for 70% of pupils to link local issues with EU values. To ensure equity, 40% of project leadership roles will be held by students with fewer opportunities. Results include a digital toolbox of AI-driven rural solutions and a civic engagement guide.

<< Results >>

Curricula: 60% of school subjects updated with PBL methodologies and AI tools.
Student Competencies: 70% of pupils mastering civic debate and ethical AI for local sustainability audits.
Inclusion: 40% of leadership and coordination roles held by students with fewer opportunities.
AI Learning Models: Development of personalized learning paths specifically designed for SEN students.
Digital Toolbox: A shared repository of rural sustainability scenarios and a Civic Engagement Guide for rural school

2026-1-FI01-KA210-SCH-000450755.title: GREEN LAB "Generating Resilient Education and Environmental Networks: Local Action Beyond borders"
2026-1-FI01-KA210-SCH-000450755.summary:
<< Objectives >>

G.R.E.E.N. L.A.B. is about turning students into eco-conscious leaders. We want to move beyond the classroom, helping young people develop "green" thinking and active citizenship through real-world experience. By connecting students across Europe, we’ll help them see how local actions solve global problems. Our goal is to empower them to realize that their daily choices—no matter how small—can build a more sustainable, collective future for us all.

<< Implementation >>

We are bringing this project to life through a mix of local action and international adventure in Finland, Hungary, Croatia, and Turkey. Students and teachers won't just study nature; they’ll observe biodiversity firsthand, create digital content, and solve problems together. By using Erasmus+ tools and traveling for transnational meetings, we’re blending digital innovation with face-to-face cultural exchange to make environmental education truly interactive.

<< Results >>

Beyond just better grades, students will walk away with a deep-rooted sense of environmental responsibility and sharpened digital skills. They’ll produce their own videos and resources, leaving a digital legacy for other schools to follow. The real result, however, is the lasting change in school culture: sustainability will no longer be a "topic" we teach, but a way of life that encourages students to keep taking the lead long after the project ends.

2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000449685.title: Teaching Beyond the Basics – Preparing Future Teachers for Advanced Differentiation in IT Education
2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000449685.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen the competences of future IT teachers in advanced differentiated and inclusive teaching, develop and validate 12 adaptable teaching scenarios and establish sustainable cooperation between university, school and non-formal partners. Through mentoring, international collaboration and pilot implementation, the project creates tested educational resources and long-term capacity for high-quality inclusive STEM teaching.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes six main activities: establishing a shared pedagogical framework and needs analysis; mentored local practice in advanced differentiated IT teaching; transnational job shadowing and comparative learning; collaborative development of 12 teaching scenarios; pilot implementation and evaluation in schools and non-formal settings; and final consolidation and dissemination of results through an open-access handbook and workshops.

<< Results >>

The project will produce a validated portfolio of 12 advanced differentiated IT teaching scenarios, an open-access practice handbook and strengthened competences of future teachers in inclusive STEM teaching. It will establish sustainable cooperation between partner organisations and create tested pedagogical models that support long-term improvement of teacher preparation and classroom practice.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

hr.name: Sveučilište Josipa Jurja Strossmayera u Osijeku

2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000450613.title: What You Eat - Change The World
2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000450613.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen inclusive education and ecological awareness through practical learning. Students will develop professional and ecological skills through activities such as food management, waste reduction, and eco-garden cultivation, with active participation. It emphasizes inclusion of students with special needs and fewer opportunities and supports communication skills and teacher collaboration.

-  Eco-integration and plant workshops
-  Workshops, lectures, and collaboration with universities, farmers, food producers, and eco-organizations
-  International eco-picnic
- Publication of an e-book with ecological tips, recipes, and green practices from European regions
- Students will share project videos on various online platforms

<< Results >>

- Improvement of green practices and ecological competencies
- Increased active participation of students
-  Promotion of social inclusion
-  Publication of an e-book with ecological tips, recipes, and characteristics of European regions
-  Greater knowledge and awareness of the degradation of natural food resources and ways to address it
-  Strengthening European identity
-  Improvement of language skills
-  Increased sense of connection of students with their region and country

2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000451539.title: CULTURALLY responsive teaching for a more INclusive classroom (CULTURALLY-IN)
2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000451539.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The pupil population is increasingly diverse (Roma, Turkey, Ukraine, Syria, Asia), requiring pedagogical changes to integrate refugees and migrants. Our overall aim is to enhance the professional capacities of 15 staff members to transition from standard special education to Culturally Responsive Teaching (CRT). Specific aims focus on bridging intercultural gaps, adapting teaching practices, and ensuring the school remains a stabilizing, inclusive force for all families.

<< Implementation >>

The activities are: 1) Development of a culturally-responsive teaching toolkit for teachers and staff: It serves as a means for teachers & staff to adopt culturally-responsive teaching (CRT); 2)Piloting the toolkit in primary schools: i.e. testing CRT w/15 staff at partner schools; 3) Follow-up visit & workshop at FIDS for teachers & staff; 4)Sustaining results & future cooperation arrangements; incl. 3 local conferences, project sustainability plan, & final conference.

<< Results >>

The main results include: 1) A validated CRT Toolkit (multilingual e-document + 9 YouTube videos) providing methods to address biases for migrant/minority pupils. 2) 15 staff members gain CRT capacities by piloting the toolkit and participating in the FIDS follow-up visit; documented via digital logbooks and assessment report. Sustainability is ensured via a formal sustainability plan (with final internal review), local conferences, and a final event in Krško.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

hr.name: Centar za odgoj i obrazovanje Tomislav Špoljar

2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000452384.title: Vještine za učinkovit obrazovni dizajn za inkluziju
2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000452384.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Through the implementation of the Project, we will achieve that students with special need and all other students who are at risk of exclusion achieve educational outcomes that match their capabilities, because current practice shows that they often fall behind in educational results, more because of an insufficiently focused approach, than because of their special needs. It is very important that we strengthen their key competences for lifelong learning and make them confident lifelong learners

<< Implementation >>

The Project will develop a Manual for an Individualized Approach to Teaching that will cover all important segments of teaching work with students with disabilities. Part of the Manual will be an innovative digital tool - an Application for assessment and support procedures for students with disabilities, which will enable teachers to easily assess the needs of their students and, in their everyday work, build on their knowledge and skills through appropriate support strategies.

<< Results >>

We expect the Handbook with the Application to be a useful tool for individualized support for each student, with a special emphasis on younger students, as it is always important to intervene as early as possible through procedures appropriate to the student's abilities and needs. Ultimately, in the long term, we expect students with special needs to realize their true potential and achieve a higher level of educational results.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000453750.title: Drama for Real Empathy, Attention, and Mutual Collaboration
2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000453750.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The DREAM project aims to transform learning through drama-based education that strengthens wellbeing in school, fosters empathy, and promotes active participation. By connecting students and teachers across borders, the project builds inclusive, creative environments where young people develop communication skills, confidence, and social responsibility while schools grow into supportive, collaborative communities grounded in shared European values.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement four international drama trainings led by Try Theatre experts, four student exchanges and four teacher exchanges (5 days each), four local drama workshop cycles, the creation of Educational Materials and a Video Handbook, and structured dissemination activities to ensure sustainability and long-term impact.

<< Results >>

The project will result in improved wellbeing in school, stronger empathy and active participation among students, and enhanced teacher competences in drama-based education. It will produce practical Educational Materials and a Video Handbook, foster lasting international cooperation, and embed inclusive, creative teaching methods sustainably into everyday school practice.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000457178.title: 21st Century Skills Development With Drama
2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000457178.summary:
<< Objectives >>

21st century skills are the sum of the skills that today's students need to be successful. Some of the 21st century skills are:
critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, communication, leadership, productivity. One of the most effective methods of
developing these skills is drama. Early childhood is a critical period in the development of personality. Drama is a method that supports children's imagination and creativity and enables them to learn through experience (Cottrell, 1987.).

<< Implementation >>

-Increase access to "affordable and quality early childhood education and care"
-Improving the competences of trainers and other adult education staff
-To provide opportunities to develop 21st century skills
-With drama, which is expressed as pretending, children learn through experience
-While the child exhibits an emotion, thought, event using techniques such as improvisation and role playing, all areas of development are supported positively

<< Results >>

- 3 international meetings
- 20 local events
-A1 Training will be organized to increase the equipment of the participants. A workshop will be organized with the
participation of experts in the field of drama
-Opportunity to observe good examples on site
-We will develop educational content/activity plan based on drama technique that contributes to the development of 21st
century skills
-Virtual and face-to-face meetings will be organized
-Trainings/seminars will be organized for professionals
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000466941.title: Little Bodies, Big Emotions - Movement, Rhythm and Culture in Early Childhood
2026-1-HR01-KA210-SCH-000466941.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Objective of the Project MOVEmotion is to improve quality and inclusion in early childhood education by integrating movement, rhythm and cultural heritage into preschool practice. Strengthen emotional wellbeing, cooperation, cultural identity and intercultural learning for children aged 3-7. Exchange good practices among educators, co-create thematic modules linking emotions with movement and cultural elements, implement pilot activities, and produce inclusive methodological materials and tools.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes transnational educator exchange workshops, co-creation of four thematic modules connecting emotions, movement and cultural heritage, pilot implementation of modules with children in partner kindergartens, design of the CroNor Rhymes Booklet by children, and final community events to share results. Educators will document and reflect on activities, adapt them for inclusion, and produce joint methodological materials for wider use.

<< Results >>

Expected results are shared thematic modules (compiled in one digital module manual) as inclusive methodological materials for educators, documenting movement-based practices and local traditions, together with CroNor Rhymes Booklet. Educators' competences in emotional development, inclusion and movement pedagogy. Piloted activities with evidence of impact, strengthened cooperation between partners, and increased community awareness through final public events and digital dissemination.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2026-1-HU01-KA210-SCH-000453651.title: „Felfedezni, megérteni, megőrizni” –A természetismeret tanításának új módja digitális csendben
2026-1-HU01-KA210-SCH-000453651.summary:

To emphasize the importance of protecting our natural environment. Form accountable behaviour and create a sense of responsibility about nature. Renew the methods of teaching Science and share the implemented good practices that we discover. 
Motivate the students to learn foreign languages. Improve the efficiency of their learning processes. Move to a higher level of our teaching and refreshing the teaching skills of our colleagues. Build international partnerships and promote Erasmus+ projects

• Hungarian colleagues visit Čepin's school and nature reserve sites in Croatia
• Curriculum development on the field of teaching Science in the primary school

• On-site Science lessons at Lake Balaton

Students learn about protecting the natural environment in real language situations while they are also improving language competences, communication competences and creativity. 
Teachers build international partnerships and increase the level of their cooperation and problem solving skills while also 
developing new teaching methods and ideas. 
The two participating schools will carry out curriculum development to make teaching Science more efficient and enjoyable in their schools.

2026-1-HU01-KA210-SCH-000455613.title: Building Early Intercultural Competence in Primary Education
2026-1-HU01-KA210-SCH-000455613.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen early intercultural competence in primary education by fostering mutual understanding, respect for diversity and inclusive classroom dialogue. Trough structured cooperation between Hungarian and Croatian partners, it seeks to develop, pilot and validate a practical intercultural toolkit that support teachers in creating inclusive, democratic and culturally aware learning environments.

<< Implementation >>

The project will follow a structured development process including joint design, collaborative toolkit creation, pilot classroom implementation and evidence-based revision. Six intercultural lesson modules will be tested in primary classrooms, supported by teacher reflection tools and micro-assessment instruments. Finalised materials will be prepared for digital dissemination and wider reuse.

<< Results >>

The project will result in a pilot-tested intercultural toolkit for primary education, measurable improvements in pupil awareness and teacher confidence, and strengthened transnational cooperation between partner institutions. The finalised materials will be digitally accessible, supporting inclusive practices and enabling sustainable small-scale European school collaboration.

2026-1-HU01-KA210-SCH-000463330.title: A demokrácia olimpiája
2026-1-HU01-KA210-SCH-000463330.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project is not only an educational experience, but also an emotionally and socially defining experience that helps 
students to become more open, accepting and responsible citizens. Better understanding of minority rights and advocacy. 
Recognise the value of cultural diversity 
Develop tolerance and intercultural skills 
Increased interest in social and political processes 
Encouraging active citizenship 
Long-term dialogue

<< Implementation >>

Visits to participating schools: Rijeka, Cloppenburg, Székesfehérvár. Activities and programs:
Rijeka: The focus will be on sports and the Olympic Games. During the sports competitions, will promote fair play, cooperation, and the development of life skills. 
Cloppenburg: Better understanding of democratic values and processes, presentation of "ABC of Democracy," simulation games 
Székesfehérvár: learning about local government, creating a Student Rights Charter.

<< Results >>

Students understand the principles of democracy and recognise their own role in community decision-making.They will be more motivated to get involved in the life of the school and the local community.Participating in international 
teamwork will help them to be more open and accepting of other cultures and perspectives. 
They will improve their collaborative skills as they will have to work with students from different backgrounds.New initiatives 
in schools,such as student olympics,debate club.

2026-1-IE01-KA210-SCH-000462026.title: Integrating home visiting into non-formal play and learning ECEC settings
2026-1-IE01-KA210-SCH-000462026.summary:
<< Objectives >>

: The project will expand access to high‑quality, inclusive non‑formal ECEC by strengthening practitioner skills, integrating home‑visiting into the TOY for Inclusion model, and creating shared guidelines that improve support for marginalised children and families (multiple generations and the wider family system) across partner countries. It will enhance practice, build capacity and influence local, national and international policy to reduce educational disadvantage.

<< Implementation >>

We will implement a programme of online knowledge‑exchange webinars, practitioner action‑learning cycles, and three transnational study visits in Ireland, Croatia and the Netherlands. Partners will co‑develop updated TOY for Inclusion guidelines integrating home‑visiting, produce shared resources, and carry out dissemination activities to strengthen non‑formal ECEC practice across countries.

<< Results >>

The project will strengthen practitioner skills, update TOY for Inclusion guidelines with home‑visiting, and improve non‑formal ECEC quality. It will enhance Play Hubs and home‑community learning, increase support for marginalised families, build their socio‑educational capital, and promote wider policy recognition of inclusive, community‑based ECEC models that help children reach their full potential.

2026-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000454928.title: From Awareness to Action: A School Partnership on Carbon Responsibility
2026-1-IT02-KA210-SCH-000454928.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our main objective is to help students connect climate change to their own daily habits and understand how simple choices affect their carbon footprint. We aim to move from general awareness to measurable action through a shared carbon audit, student-led Eco Club activities and baseline–endline comparison. By the end of the project, students should be able to analyse, reflect and take realistic responsibility within their local context.

<< Implementation >>

Partners will jointly design a simple carbon audit framework and implement it through Eco Clubs in each school. Students will collect local data, reflect on daily habits and compare findings transnationally. Based on results, they will plan small-scale actions such as awareness initiatives, monitoring activities and Eco Boards. Outcomes will be documented through a joint documentary, digital magazine and Green Toolkit.

<< Results >>

The project will produce a shared carbon audit framework, structured monitoring tools, a joint eco documentary, a digital magazine and an open Green Toolkit. Students are expected to demonstrate increased carbon awareness, stronger analytical skills and documented behavioural shifts through baseline–endline comparison. Schools will strengthen Eco Clubs and integrate sustainability more systematically into daily practice.

hr.name: Osnovna škola Ivana Gorana Kovačića Sveti Juraj na Bregu

2026-1-MK01-KA210-SCH-000459224.title: Blue Labs for Schools – Young Guardians of Water Ecosystems
2026-1-MK01-KA210-SCH-000459224.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Blue Labs for Schools connects students from Lake Ohrid (North Macedonia) and Korčula (Croatia) to protect freshwater and coastal ecosystems through practical school-based environmental action. The project strengthens environmental literacy, promotes sustainable behaviour and intercultural cooperation, and develops a transferable “5 Tips to a More Sustainable Blue School” model supporting the European Green Deal and EU Biodiversity Strategy.

<< Implementation >>

During the 12-month project students implement three one-week school challenges (waste audit, plastic reduction and sustainable fashion) and participate in two learning mobilities focused on biodiversity, wetland resilience, coastal clean-up and composting. Pupils collect environmental data, test practical sustainability solutions in schools and co-create five “5 Tips” posters compiled into a digital brochure shared through Erasmus+ platforms.

<< Results >>

Students gain stronger understanding of pollution pathways, biodiversity protection and circular economy principles. Schools introduce improved waste sorting, plastic reduction practices, composting demonstrations and biodiversity-supporting actions. Five reusable lesson models and a digital “Blue School” toolkit will be published on the Erasmus+ Results Platform, reaching at least 300 additional pupils and supporting long-term environmental education.

2026-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000453721.title: Competent Teachers: From Inquiry to Success
2026-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000453721.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We want to help our teachers move from traditional lessons to active learning. We will improve their skills in Inquiry Based Learning, Design Thinking and metacognitive strategies by at least 40%. We want our students to grow in critical thinking, problem‑solving and self‑regulation by at least 25% in many subjects.

<< Implementation >>

We will have 1 transnational project meeting in Poland, 3 LTTAs (Turkey-IBL, Spain-Design Thinking with IBL, Croatia-Metacognitive strategies with IBL), a 10‑month eTwinning project, create 3 teachers’ guidebooks and 120 lesson plans, run IBL/DT/reflection lessons in all schools and hold final online sharing meetings with parents, local schools and other partners.

<< Results >>

We expect 48 teachers to improve their skills in IBL, Design Thinking and metacognition by at least 40% and over 320 students (eTwinning+classes) to improve critical thinking, problem‑solving and self‑regulation by at least 25%. We will create 3 guidebooks, 120 lesson plans, common tools for observation and reflection, a rich eTwinning TwinSpace and stronger, long‑term EU cooperation between the 4 schools.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2026-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000462882.title: Green Minds, Bright Future
2026-1-PL01-KA210-SCH-000462882.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project is to enable primary school students to gain age-appropriate knowledge and awareness about climate change and environmental issues.The goal is to improve students climate literacy and raise their awareness of natural resource conservation,recycling, and renewable energy.Environmentally conscious behaviors will be supported through STEAM-based activities, the e-book prepared at the end of the project will transform the acquired knowledge into a lasting educational resource.

<< Implementation >>

Our project plans STEAM-focused activities at local,virtual, international levels to raise environmental awareness climate change consciousness.Locally, awareness will be created through seminars, workshops,scientific projects.In virtual events,students will engage in interactive activities on digital platforms.At the international level, an e-book will be prepared and collaborative projects will be carried out.This multi-layered approach aims to spread environmental awareness on a global scale.

<< Results >>

The project aims to support students in making informed decisions on environmental issues by improving their climate literacy. Through STEAM-based activities, students' scientific thinking and problem-solving skills will be strengthened. Families and local communities will be involved to raise awareness about climate change. The gains made regarding renewable energy and the conservation of natural resources will be shared nationally and internationally through an environmental awareness e-book.

2026-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000456279.title: ECOkids learn about nature in nature
2026-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000456279.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The "ECOkids" project trains teachers in outdoor and STEAM pedagogy to combat the sedentary lifestyle of the new generation. We aim to improve inclusion for 25% of vulnerable children (Roma, with special educational needs, from vulnerable backgrounds) by transforming the garden into an equitable space. The focus is on developing sensory resilience and motor skills, resulting in a European e-book with OER resources to ensure the long-term sustainability of green education.

<< Implementation >>

We will implement four LTT (learning test - long-term learning project) mobilities focused on outdoor Montessori (Turkey), STEAM integration in the "Relaxation Garden" (Romania), and socio-emotional validation (Italy/Croatia). Key activities include experiments, games for inclusion, and digital pedagogy workshops, the creation of an e-book with video tutorials. The project aims to standardize green pedagogy for teachers and students, and ensure the long-term sustainability of its initiatives.

<< Results >>

Expected outcomes include 108 educators trained in outdoor pedagogy and 600 children (25% with few opportunities/SEN) with improved sensory resilience and motor skills. The tangible outcome is a European e-book with RED video tutorials, standardizing green education. We anticipate a 50% increase in inclusive engagement through the “Garden of Relaxation” methodology, ensuring long-term institutional sustainability and a validated framework for transnational cooperation through Europass Mobility.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2026-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000460617.title: Let's Build Our Future Together!
2026-1-RO01-KA210-SCH-000460617.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The main aim of this project is to enhance students’ awareness of sustainability and a green environment while strengthening their digital and 21st-century skills through STEM-based learning and improving teachers’ professional competencies in STEM practices.

-To increase awareness of sustainability and environmental responsibility
-To enable students to develop technology-based solutions to environmental problems
-To foster students’ 21st-century skills,
-To strengthen teachers’ stem skills

<< Implementation >>

It will proceed as project-based learning.
-Schools will conduct local sustainability and green environment campaigns.
-Robotic solutions will be developed for environmental problems.
-They will design "their own sustainable spaces" using 3D design software.
-They will make their own projects sustainable and add a new dimension to what they have learned by using augmented reality.
-We will ensure the dissemination of the project through lesson plans, a project catalog, and scientific articles.

<< Results >>

-Awareness of sustainability and green environment will increase among students and teachers.
-Students will produce technological solutions to problems related to sustainability and green environment.
-Students will develop computational thinking, 3D design, analytical thinking, innovation, digital, social, cognitive and language skills.
-Teachers will develop skills in using new digital applications, project-based work, STEM course development and interdisciplinary work.

2026-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000453899.title: Rastišče prihodnosti: povezovanje znanosti, tehnologije in trajnostnih poklicev skozi šolske vrtove
2026-1-SI01-KA210-SCH-000453899.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project is to strengthen students’ STEM, digital, green and entrepreneurial competences and empower teachers through experiential, interdisciplinary learning.It focuses on upper primary students who are making their first educational and career decisions, with a strong emphasis on increasing girls’ motivation, confidence and long-term interest in STEM and green careers. The project also builds sustainable cooperation between schools, local communities and expert partners.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes international teacher training, student workshops  and international learning mobilities. The central learning environment is the school garden as a teaching polygon for interdisciplinary and problem-based research and learning. Students explore smart systems, green and technical professions, programming and the entrepreneurial development of products from the school garden,  with a special focus on the inclusion of girls in STEM and meetings with STEM role models.

<< Results >>

Project results include a learning lab with a smart garden bed, concrete student  products using the “Co-funded by the EU” emblem, and tested didactic models. A key outcome is a publication with guidelines, descriptions of project activities and examples of good practice, available in print and as an open-access e-publication for other schools. The project strengthens student and teacher competences, sustainablepartnerships and interest in STEM, especially among girls.

2021-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000032848.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000032848.title: Participation in Civil Protection Planning
2021-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000032848.summary:
<< Background >>

Needs can be retrieved firstly in the high rate of youth unemployment.
Second, civil protection system needs the right skills; the first thing that catches the eye is the heterogeneity of required skills and competences and their degree of specificity.
Third, volunteers’ wish to transform a passion into a job. What moves a person to become a volunteer is a strong will to help the others, a passion in doing that; our society, tends to lose the idea of passion connected to a job; and a job done with passion is destined to achieve more and better objectives.
Finally, the development/support of entrepreneurial spirit and entrepreneurship skills is fundamental to reinforce the link between training activities and job market and improve employability.
The project have also responded to other target group’s needs (public administration, citizens) as it has become clear how an informed and involved community is better prepared to respond to an emergency and better equipped to fulfill public authorities’ indications.


<< Objectives >>

PARTICIPRO aimed at improving the employability of young people in the field of civil protection planning.
The project also aimed to create a tool for participation in Civil Protection planning, flexible enough to be used both as a working and a learning tool; in addition, the project aimed at selecting and training 10 young persons. 
The project also intended to sensitise citizens and public authorities so they will better cooperate in case of natural disasters.
Finally, PARTICIPRO aimed at increasing democracy and share common values, by stimulating civic engagement and participation. 



<< Implementation >>

The main activities of the project were: the Basic training, the Tool Co-Designed Workshop, the Piloting, the Forward Looking Workshop. 

The PARTICIPRO Basic training consisted of three components: civil protection context, civil protection planning, participation in civil protection. 

The PARTICIPRO Tool Co-Designed Workshop consisted of 3 phases or workshop: preparation, implementation, feedback. The implementation workshop was composed by 3 activities: meeting with stakeholders, study visit, public event. 

The piloting of the PARTICIPRO tool took place in parallel in the two countries, also to overcome the obvious language barriers with some stakeholders.T he piloting was composed of three sessions: participatory session with administrators and those involved in civil protection planning and management; participatory session with citizens, selected based on their representativeness and exposure to the risk identified in the previous session; participatory session with the two previous groups. 

The Participro Forward Looking Workshop was composed by 3 phases: preparation, implementation, feedback. The implementation workshop was composed by 3 sub-activities.

<< Results >>

The project intended to design participative tools for project management, which would be made immediately available to start participative processes also in civil protection planning. This would have also allowed the partnership to stress the importance of the active role of citizens as relevant stakeholders in civic life and in building resilient communities.

Another concrete output of the project was the production and delivery of the Family Emergency Plan. This plan was discussed and analysed together with the citizenship, as a useful tool both to train prevention thinking in ordinary times and in times of emergency in order not to panic and to have a track to follow.

2021-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000032916.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000032916.title: Incubatori Europei per Erasmus
2021-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000032916.summary:
<< Background >>

IN4Erasmus originates from the awareness of the crucial role of business incubators and accelerators in Europe. The growing importance of such entities in entrepreneurship development, specialised training (VET, youth, businesses, professionals, local authorities) and sustainable social and environmental development is evident, as supported by the “Policy Brief on Incubators and Accelerators that Support Inclusive Entrepreneurship” (OECD, 2019), which documents the presence of over 900 incubators in EU.

The post-pandemic challenges and the EU 2030 strategies for the “Twin Transitions” in green and digital have heightened the urgency for these entities to enhance organisational capacities through international collaboration.

In this context, aligned with the priorities of the Erasmus+ programme, IN4Erasmus addresses the needs of business incubators and accelerators to strengthen capacities, skills, and opportunities in the following areas:
•Erasmus+ programme and European programmes (small-scale priorities)
•International cooperation
•Innovative solutions and practices for internationalisation
•Entrepreneurial training with a focus on inclusion, digital development and sustainability

<< Objectives >>

The implementation of IN4Erasmus has consistently aimed to achieve the following objectives:
•Expansion of the competencies of Innovalley and Startup Campus Germany through capacity building and the transfer of know-how from IHF and UNIDU
•Increase in opportunities and facilitation of access to the Erasmus+ programme, culminating in new proposals and initiatives
•Promotion of the European dimension for local organisations
•Enhancement of skills for international cooperation
•Mapping and transfer of dynamics of incubators at the EU level
•Improvement of the quality of solutions and work practices of the partners
•Development of skills with a focus on inclusion, digital development, and green initiatives for the partners
•General enhancement of organisational capacities of incubators and accelerators

Furthermore, the project’s objective has been to ensure European value through comparison of different realities and European contexts, fostering exchange of collaborative experiences at international level. The analysis of European practices, the promotion of networks and collaborations, and the strengthening of E+ project design capabilities, culminating in new initiatives, have contributed to ensuring the project’s European value.

<< Implementation >>

IN4Erasmus has carried out two main activities during the implementation phase:

A1 – Capacity Building in Erasmus+ and other European projects:
•Design and implementation of a training programme in EU project management, focusing on common elements of European projects and the Erasmus programme
•Development of targeted educational materials for business incubators

A2 – Mapping of the internationalisation dynamics of business incubators:
•Collection and analysis of data on the internationalisation dynamics of business incubators
•Organisation of training meetings to identify and discuss virtuous models
•Ongoing development of supporting materials

These activities provide basic tools for international cooperation and a set of virtuous models in various countries and European contexts as inspiration for the definition of future development strategies.

Simultaneously, essential horizontal activities have been implemented, such as:
•QA and Monitoring and Evaluation: Constant evaluation of activities to ensure adherence to objectives
•Valorisation and Dissemination: Enhancement of resources obtained through the dissemination of results
•Admin: General management to ensure the proper conduct of activities

<< Results >>

During the implementation of IN4Erasmus, the following results were achieved:

ACTIVITY 1
•A Capacity Building programme through 10 online meetings
•11 training fiches on EU project management and the Erasmus programme
Intangible Results:
Improvement of skills and capacity for Innovalley’s (P0) and SCG’s (P3) staff in project design and access to Erasmus+ projects
•Reinforcement of collaborative skills within the consortium

ACTIVITY 2
•Internal methodology for a common analysis
•Selection and analysis of 34 case studies from various European countries and contexts, illustrating an overview of incubators’ internationalisation solutions
•34 illustrated summary sheets (fiches) for the 34 case studies
•A summary matrix with 6 dimensions to understand the different tools and approaches identified, complementing the conducted analysis
•5 thematic meetings among partners to discuss in-depth the methods and results of the analysis
•A comprehensive report with the evaluation of the mapping activities
Intangible Results:
•Enhanced understanding of models and solutions adopted by other organisations
•Overview considering various diverse contexts
•Strengthening of internationalisation strategies

2021-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000037820.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000037820.title: Up-skilling in Remote Working through Exploring the Relatively New Phenomenon of Co-working
2021-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000037820.summary:
<< Background >>

The project directly addresses the needs and goals of the participating organisations as their main aims are to helpeffectively prepare young people for their working lives.   Businesses across public and private sector increasingly recognize the benefits of hiring and retaining remote workers. Societal trends also push more businesses towards adopting more flexible working policies and allowing at least partial telecommute. As more and more people are planning to transition to remote work, VET educators have to contribute to such changes, which is why our project caters for the need of both VET educators and young people. The project is of significant importance for teachers to develop particular attitudes, be more confident and creative in applying different learning methods, styles and techniques. We are aware that the methods and styles should be in line with a more learner-centred approach which redefines the traditional student-teacher relationship in the classroom and can include collaborative research projects, group projects, debates, study teams, peer-to-peer teaching as face-to-face classroom instruction is integrated with online components that helps to extend learning beyond the classroom or school day.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the project are to attract more attention to the need of incorporating new working practices into a training process as they are not covered by the vocational school curricular in the slightest. As it is a small-scale
project, we intended to spot some good practices, develop a model course syllibus and some relevant course contents to generate greater interest to this burning issue. We were able to produce some more innovative and more varied educational resources; including open educational resources, related to Co-working, for VET learners who at the present do not possess the needed key skills to work remotely. We wanted to familiarise educators and, respectively, their students, with new working practices, namely Co-working so as to meet the needs of the labour market and to bridge the gap related to skills mismatches between Education&Traning and the world of work. We also aimed to extend the supply of learning opportunities tailored to the needs of learners so that they could enhance their 21st century skills  and become more responsive to the market requirements. By  building capacity of organisations to work transnationally and across sectors we contributed to young people' higher employability.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented the following main activities:
1. Teachers/Students Exchange ''The phenomenon of Co-working - Good practices''.
2. Training event ''Co-working: challenges and possibilities''. 
3. Field Day Event “Rural Co-working".
4. A Multiplier Event ''My Co-working experience''.
The other activities included the project management that counted on the clarity of the work plan and task division. We constantly specified the tasks and used indicators to monitor the progress, assigned responsibilities to ensure delivery of all the key products and provide an efficient communication framework for the partners to work collaboratively. Every partner organisation had a responsibility for a part of the project as every partner was obliged to set up projects teams and organise regular project meetings to analyse, summarise and plan the project activities. Every project partner kept communication with the coordinating school and all the partners as well as with the co-working communities in their regions/countries, implementing  one Mobility event, making all the recordings of every workshop and developing particular teaching resources related to the Co-working course syllabus and contents. Every partner also dealt with dissemination.

<< Results >>

We produced the following results: 
1. Compendium of good Co-working practices /it is created as a Canva book/ and contains workshop/training session scenarios as well as teaching/learning materials for the Co-working course;
2. The course syllabus and contents "Co-working" in both printed and on-line versions /flipbook/.
3. Flipbook ''Coworking in the Partners' countries''.
4. Flipbook ''Coworking around the World''.
5. The project blog https://eucoworking.wixsite.com/eu-coworking.
As for the intangible results, we managed to attract more attention to the issue of
interdisciplinarity in the field of remote working practices for VET practitioners as it brought together disciplines as diverse as business studies, cultural studies, geography, migration studies, IT, sociology of tourism; we drew
attention to cross-fertilisation between disciplines, the issues it raises, and the difficulties people encounter; we also helped realise the necessity to look at Co-working spaces are a pioneering way for humans to interrelate to one another as
the coworking movement emphasizes its community building aspect. One of our first and foremost project results is that some VET organisations have started including Co-working in their curricula.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2021-1-MK01-KA210-VET-000029937.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-MK01-KA210-VET-000029937.title: Комарци-векторски предизвик за јавното здравје во Цеверна Македонија и пошироко
2021-1-MK01-KA210-VET-000029937.summary:
<< Background >>

After the eradication of malaria from the last century until the year 2013,there was no mosquito research in RNM. Mosquito species were not monitored,their resistance to biocides was not monitored and the population had minimal knowledge or was not informedhow to contribute to the fight against mosquitoes.Since 2013,monitoring of the mosquito species has begun,but medical entomology  not been sufficiently understood and little investment has been made in it. Being aware of the public health hazard of mosquitoes as carriers of viruses, bacteria,etc.that cause diseases in humans,we would like to spread our knowledge,the knowledge of our partners to the affected persons and thewider population,andcertainly the most important thing is to train people and improve the mosquito control in RN Macedonia by introducing a program to monitor mosquito resistance to biocides.With the above activities, we will raise the level of public health protection,for a better understanding of medical entomology as a science,raising eco-awareness among the population,raising awareness of responsible work of the concerned persons,following new methods in the fight against mosquitoes and strengthening of intersectoral cooperation and the ONE HEALTH approach.

<< Objectives >>

Mosquito controkl is a very complex process that includes several measures.We have been implementing some of the measures at national level,but it is not sufficient.For better control,it is also necessary to monitor the resistance to biocides due totheir mass use.In RNM there is a lack of specialists who would implement that measure and that was our main motive for this project- to educate staff on  the procedure of testing the adult mosquito resistance to biocides.This would be a step forward towards successful control,safer health of the population and the environment. Among other things,it is of great importance to keep the attention of the population towards medical entomology as a science which is very little  taughtabout.Our aim is to educate citizens about their role in the fight against mosquitoes and how to protect themselves,raise their environmental awareness, influence them to change their behavior towards the environment and all together contribute to a higher level of safe public health.To  encourage the target institutions to work dedicatedly,to increasetheir financial support,to share good practices,to follow international innovative measures,since the biological control should be ourfor thedevelopment of an ent.

<< Implementation >>

At the beginning of the project,we created flyers that the students distributed to the population door-to-door.We implemented workshops where we trained the students with more information about mosquitoesin order toshare it andwe discussed the most common questions from the people.We visited the laboratories of the partnersaccording to the project plan and they organized workshops. According to the trainings andguidance  given by the partners,we acquired laboratory equipment and biocide resistance testers.We conducted the pilot testing,which was successful and weare planning to repeat it next season to compare the results.An International Conference titled as the project was also organized,in which the coordinators,partners,representatives of the target institutions,veterinarians,municipalities,media, etc.actively participated.In cooperation with the partners from the University of Osijek,we prepared another flyer that was distributed by the students throughout the kindergartens.Children aged 6-7 were included in kindergartens from semi-urban areas and different nationalities.We showed them the development cycle of the mosquitoespresented through plasticine.Webrought them coloring books to coloring them and understand more vividly

<< Results >>

Although the start of the project was delayed, in addition to the set goals, we managed to achieve more. By visiting our partner Sapienza University, we managed to educate people about mosquito resistance testing. This activity led us to the goal of obtaining the absolutely most important and concrete result. Next was educating the population from door to door and visiting children in kindergartens, during which we managed to explain the life cycle of the mosquito and what is the role of the people in the fight against mosquitoes and to create generations with eco-awarness, a higher culture and that pass on to their parents and relatives. Through the television and written media, we spoke publicly about our activities with the project and introduced the population in detail to the importance of medical entomology as a science. By visiting the Benaki Plant Pathology Institute, the entomologists upgraded their knowledge of SIT and from there the idea to introduce the technique in Macedonia with joint cooperation. By installing GPS devices in the vehicles where the ULV devices are mounted, we have strengthened the controlled terrestrial adulticidal disinsection.

hr.name: Sveučilište Josipa Jurja Strossmayera u Osijeku

2021-1-RS01-KA210-VET-000032909.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-RS01-KA210-VET-000032909.title:
Sticanje novih znanja i iskustva na primerima dobre prakse - edukacija učenika u
oblasti srednje stručnog obrazovanja poljoprivrednih škola
2021-1-RS01-KA210-VET-000032909.summary:
<< Background >>

1.	Practical classes are conducted in the conditions available to the school. Due to the lack of material and technical possibilities, some modules cannot be fully implemented. In this way, students partially achieve the competencies provided by the curriculum. In that case, teachers try to make up for the shortcomings by improvising. By implementing the project, we expect to expand experiences and perfect new teaching methods by looking up to the work of modern technologies in partner countries. All this was taken into account when choosing topics and modules for the implementation of practical teaching in mobility, especially according to EU standards.

<< Objectives >>

2.	The aim of the mobility was to provide students with practical training in the realistic conditions of agriculture, food production and processing. By implementing the project, our goals were to strengthen quantitative and qualitative values in professional education. Through schools´ cooperation and mobility activities, we have provided better quality of education and facilitated the flow of labor on the European labor market. By participating in the project, the students upgraded and perfected the practical skills and competencies they acquired at school through regular classes as they were attending practical classes abroad. This made them adaptable to the demands of the labor market, starting their own business and establishing mixed international mini-companies. While working in production, students strengthened their sense of responsibility and work discipline. Through the implementation of the project, each school had the possibility of implementing and using modern ICT technologies in the realization of their educational profiles´curriculum.
The project is a kind of support for the professional development of teachers through mastering European standards in secondary vocational education.

<< Implementation >>

3.	During mobility, students performed the following activities:
ALEKSINAC: familiarization with the basic principles of hydroponic production of strawberries, theoretical classes – learning about the equipment and software for control and management; practical classes - monitoring of measurable parameters; entrepreneurship workshops - preparation of stands and exhibition materials; work in the greenhouse and harvesting of strawberries; a tour of cultural, educational and tourism potential of the local environment; Virtual Companies Fair; evaluation of project activities.
MARIBOR: ecological approach to new green technologies, fruit processing, new approaches to marketing, harvesting, practical processing of fruit into juice and fruit drying;  a tour of vineyards, wineries and wine shops and wastewater treatment plants; an entrepreneurship workshop - "Think like an entrepreneur", presentation of a Start up Company - EU Cohesion Fund - an example of good practice of youth self-employment.
ČAKOVEC: theoretical class - the process of producing apple juice and apple chips; a visit to the local OPG; practical classes - the process of producing apple juice and apple chips; an entrepreneurship workshop - virtual teams, organization and f

<< Results >>

4.	By performing work tasks, students acquired the following skills and competences from several areas of agricultural production and food processing:
1. Skills of applying software for control and management of the production process,
2. Skills of monitoring measurable parameters and responding to changes in the storage and care of strawberries,
3. Work in the greenhouse production conditions,
4. Developing entrepreneurial skills through functioning of entrepreneurial companies,
5. Work skills in the direct production process.
Through the realization of the cultural program, the students acquired basic knowledge about the language, culture and customs of the local environment.

2021-1-RS01-KA210-VET-000034541.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-RS01-KA210-VET-000034541.title: EASY CHECK ( new technologies in learning - new way of thinking)
2021-1-RS01-KA210-VET-000034541.summary:
<< Background >>

1.	We applied for this project as the school Tehnoart Belgrade because we saw that there is a need in teaching to implement the modernization of teaching in secondary vocational schools in the subject of Statics. The needs that we have seen are actually the needs of the students in order to modernize the teaching process in the subject of Statics.

<< Objectives >>

2.	The project will bring the realization of new teaching methods (correct application of computers in the field of mechanical engineering), improvement of the scope, and, above all, the quality of what was learned during schooling. Also, the result will be an application for machine calculations (which currently does not exist).

<< Implementation >>

3.	The following activities were carried out by Technoart Belgrade:
a.	1. Analysis and preparation of the teaching process
b.	2. Teaching - comparative method
c.	3. Evaluation
d.	4. Preparation for changing the plan and program
The MIS association carried out the following activities:

f.	2. Design and projecting
g.	3. Programming
h.	4. Implementation
i.	5. Support and maintenance

4.	The concrete result of the project is the Easy-check application, which serves in the teaching process for calculating the center of gravity of polygons, single-node contact forces, two-node contact forces, and arbitrary force systems.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000029875.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000029875.title: Go-car-go Plus
2021-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000029875.summary:
<< Background >>

Motivation to apply for the project was to revive Go-Car-Go project, which was successfully implemented before the Corona time and stopped naturally when schools were closed. Our idea was to start the project in partnerships with primary schools and Educational Institute from Austria, which we had cooperated with in the past, to manufacture a similar little car, upgraded with an electrical drive. The project enabled primary schools to improve their STEM competences, which they lack as their pupils can acquire them only within the optional subject called technics and technology. The project of manufacturing a little car based on the chassis, which was the same for all primary schools, encouraged team work so the pupils developed their creative skills when upgrading the chassis, learnt about material properties when choosing appropriate materials, searched for the most appropriate spare parts to build the car, developed their business skills, improved their manual skills as the pupils had to build their own little cars themselves. 
School Centre Ptuj succeeded in raising the interest of the primary school pupils for technical/shortage occupations in terms of increasing the number of enrolled students in such programs.

<< Objectives >>

The basic aim of the project was for all of the primary school teams to manufacture a unique electrically driven little car and present it at the final meeting. All the activities enabled the primary school pupils to improve their STEM competences and to get to know the technical programmes (occupations) provided by School Centre Ptuj. The project activities enabled School Centre Ptuj to promote its technical and above all shortage occupations, for which there is a great demand on the job market. By implementing the project, we also wanted to reduce the number of dropouts in secondary schools.

<< Implementation >>

The main activity of the project was to manufacture an electrically driven little car. The rest of the activities, which supported the main one, included manufacturing of the chassis for little cars, organizing working meetings to be able to plan in detail, analyse and compare participants’ work, exchanging experiences and reporting about project development, developing  Go-Car-Go mobile app and the internet site to promote the project and shortage occupations, and last but not least organizing the final presentation and competition of driving little cars.

<< Results >>

The very concrete final outcome of the project was 7 unique electrically driven little cars, which were presented at the final meeting at the School Centre in Ptuj on 19th May 2022. Those cars were the result of a very successful project work of all project partners, who participated in all phases of the project, from its planning to the final product. 
Every of the planned activities was successfully finalized and influenced pupils’ interest for technical occupations. The indirect goal of the project was also to convince as many pupils as possible to continue their studies at technical schools in which we greatly succeeded. This school year we recorded a 24% increase in the number of students in mechanical engineering programmes. It can be established that the project Go-Car-Go had a great impact on that because there are a lot of newcomers who took part in the project when they were still in their primary schools.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2021-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000032917.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000032917.title: HIGHER EDUCATION FOR ROMA
2021-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000032917.summary:
<< Background >>

The application was based on the observations and experiences of the project partners in their work with members of the Roma community.  In recent years, there has been an increase in the enrolment of Roma in secondary schools, especially in vocational and technical secondary education programmes, both in Slovenia and Croatia, and this is also true for the partner secondary schools. These schools also face a high drop-out rate among the Roma community, who often struggle to reach minimum standards, do not attend classes and consequently leave school early. Educational institutions strive to ensure that Roma students achieve better learning results, successfully complete secondary education and become competitive with the majority population on the labour market, which would have a significant impact on improving their socio-economic situation and the development of the Roma community itself. In our experience with the Roma community, we have brought together partners from Slovenia and Croatia, as we face similar challenges and over the years we have developed examples of good practice that can be modified and transferred to the secondary school level to address the current needs and challenges of Roma pupils and secondary schools

<< Objectives >>

Students from vulnerable groups, including Roma, have higher drop-out and retention rates. The HEDROM project was primarily aimed at improving the quality of vocational and technical education, making it inclusive for all students, and consequently influencing their success at the secondary level of education. We saw an opportunity to do this by training professional staff who work with Roma pupils and to raise their professional competences in working with Roma, as they are the ones who have the biggest impact on the quality of education through their work.
The specific objectives we set in the application form:
To prepare the basis for the revision of the training programme developed within the GEM (Erasmus+) project, which is aimed at training adult educators who work with Roma, and to adapt it for secondary school teachers, on the basis of the project activities. 
Prevent early school leaving and failure in vocational and professional education among Roma. 
Empower secondary school teachers to work with Roma students.
Raise the educational level of the Roma community and consequently influence their competitiveness in the labour market.


<< Implementation >>

The following activities were carried out under the HEDROM project: 
1. Secondary research on enrolment and drop-out trends of Roma pupils in secondary vocational and professional education programmes.
2. Focus groups with teachers who face difficulties in teaching Roma*
3. Collecting examples of good practice from Roma who have successfully completed secondary vocational or professional education.
4. Adapting the GEM curriculum to meet the needs of teachers in vocational and technical secondary education programmes.
5. Pilot LTT in Slovenia.
6. Pilot LTT in Croatia.
7. Providing guidelines for secondary schools providing secondary and vocational education programmes attended by Roma students.
*In addition to the activities planned in the application form, we also conducted a focus group with Roma pupils, as we realised during the project that we also needed their opinion and perspective for the successful implementation of the other activities.


<< Results >>

The specific results of the project are
Secondary research about the trends of enrollment and dropout of Roma students in secondary schools,
Analysis of the focus groups with teachers on the topic of problems in teaching Roma and the Roma pupils, 
A collection of success stories of Roma,
Adaptation of the GEM programme to the needs of teachers in secondary vocational and technical education,
Trained secondary school teachers to work with Roma,
Guidelines for working with Roma pupils for other vocational and technical secondary schools.
The results have been translated into the national languages of the partners and English. Due to the bilingual environment in which the two Slovenian partner organisations are located, and in particular, for the needs of the DSŠL, the latter will also arrange translations into Hungarian, which will further contribute to the dissemination of the results both in the local environment and at international level.
The main result of the project with a long-term impact will be the trained teachers of the partner schools who participated in the pilot LTT. The new knowledge and skills will definitely contribute to solving the challenges in the field of Roma pupils' education, which was the projects aim
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education
Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff
