2021-2-DE02-KA210-VET-000048022.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-DE02-KA210-VET-000048022.title: Powered by Reuchlin: Digital Intercultural Education for the 21st Century
2021-2-DE02-KA210-VET-000048022.summary:
<< Background >>

In 2022, the Reuchlin Year was celebrated in Pforzheim/Germany. The important son of Pforzheim, Johannes Reuchlin, was part of a network of European humanists that also included Erasmus of Rotterdam. With their pathbreaking ideas and principles, they were pioneers of today's European values and still shape our understanding of education, freedom and humanity. How did these values and ideals arise, to what extent are they still relevant for us and our organizations today? Can they show us ways forward in today's world, where we are confronted with a multitude of challenges such as climate change, social inequalities and threats to our democracy? And especially, how can we find contemporary formats to introduce youth to these messages? What user-oriented methods and innovative tools are there to bring the relevance of humanistic values closer to young people? These were questions that we and our international partners in Vicenza/Italy, Osijek/Croatia and Czestochowa/Poland addressed in our project.

<< Objectives >>

With this project, we aimed to strengthen international cooperation and improve skills together with our partners. Social changes (digitalization, climate change, the trend towards polarization, growing diversification of the target group) challenge us to think more flexibly, to adapt previous formats, and to work together to find solutions.
In a first step, we explored the meaning of humanistic values and their relevance for solving today's challenges. In a second step, we developed new approaches to reach young people with these messages. The focus was on user-centered project development, agile project management, digital tools, low-barrier/interactive/participatory projects, and transnational formats. 
The joint learning units and the sharing of experiences in the development and implementation of projects in the consortium led to further development of competencies regarding project management, blended learning formats, "green twinning" and evaluation methods.


<< Implementation >>

We started with a joint information phase in which we looked at the influence of the Humanists on the values of Europe and at project development and project management. This information was processed by all partners on site and supplemented by their own research and projects. In the learning activity, we tried out the project "Reuchlin digital" in Pforzheim and learned various modern methods and digital formats for the contemporary communication of European values to young people.  On this basis, all partners developed their own projects in their city with the respective target group. The experiences and findings from the projects were evaluated in the evaluation months (alternating lead of the partners). In addition, each partner conducted a short training session for the consortium in their evaluation month. At the final event in Frankfurt, an overall evaluation of the contents and the course of the project was carried out and it was noted how the partners would like to anchor, continue and disseminate the experiences gained and successful formats in their organisations.

<< Results >>

The partners were able to expand their digital competences as well as their knowledge and skills in project management, project development, European values and climate protection. The positive experiences and enrichment through international cooperation were particularly valuable. 
Testing new formats, young people in Osijek created explanatory videos on Johannes Reuchlin, humanism and European values, as well as a script and a film about Reuchlin's life and humanism. Czestochowa presented an exhibition with a digital quiz, lectures and workshops on humanism and tolerance, Vicenza developed the Academy for Humanism and Work "Human Work", which has been offering free weekly webinars starting in autumn 2022. Pforzheim offered school packages consisting of variable modules and organised an international video clip competition and an Instagram action on the theme "My object of humanity". Young people produced over 15 video clips, some of which can be seen here
https://reuchlin-eu.pforzheim.de/materialien.html#c109175

2021-2-DK01-KA210-VET-000049884.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-DK01-KA210-VET-000049884.title: Inclusion of Young NEETs Into The Labour Market
2021-2-DK01-KA210-VET-000049884.summary:
<< Background >>

Our application for this project came from a deep understanding of the challenges faced by youth with special needs in the realm of employment and inclusion. In Europe, youth unemployment is a significant issue, leading to social consequences and diminished quality of life. This is particularly true for the NEET group (Not in Education, Employment, and Training), comprising 14.2% of 15–29-year-olds in the EU. Among them are youths with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, anxiety, depression, and other challenges, who find it difficult to integrate into both the educational system and the labor market.
Our motivation was to develop creative, practical strategies for inclusion, supported by transnational exchanges of experiences and collaborations between public administrations, NGOs, and the private sector. Given that one-fifth of the EU population is expected to have some form of disability by 2020, it's crucial to address their social and economic situations.
This project proposed an inclusion platform and basic training modules to facilitate the exchange of experiences and improve service delivery for NEET beneficiaries. Our approach is long-term, focusing on sustainable development and in-depth understanding of local contexts

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, our aim was to enhance the inclusion of vulnerable young NEETs with special needs into the labor market. We sought to develop effective ways to integrate these individuals into workplaces and equip companies with the skills to involve them in various work tasks. Among them are youths with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD.
A key goal was to foster the acquisition of new knowledge and inspiration among participating parties, trainers, and professionals.
Specifically, we aimed to create:
- An open platform for labor market inclusion, offering resources for social service staff, private companies, especially social enterprises, and NGOs to include NEETs.
- An online training package with hands-on materials providing practical knowledge about labor market inclusion for youths with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD..
Our objectives were aligned with the priorities of advocating inclusion and diversity in education, training, youth,  We aimed to increase vocational education and training flexibility, addressing the needs of NEETs currently excluded from the labor market, and fostering common values, civic engagement, and participation.


<< Implementation >>

In our project, we implemented a range of activities to meet our objectives:
1.	Training Needs Assessments and Study Visits in Denmark: We conducted comprehensive assessments to identify the specific training needs for staff and support staff. This was complemented by study visits in Denmark, which provided practical insights and learning opportunities.
2.	Learning Sessions and Materials: We developed and provided learning sessions and materials for both staff/support staff and for companies. These resources were tailored to equip participants with the necessary skills and knowledge for inclusion practices.
3.	'Training of Trainers' (ToT) in Romania: We carried out a ToT in Romania, where participants engaged in ToT courses. This initiative was aimed at enhancing the teaching and training capacities of our employees on a national level.
4.	Pilot Inclusion Activities Locally for NEETs: We initiated pilot activities at the local level, directly engaging with NEETs. These activities were designed to test and refine our inclusion strategies in real-world settings.
5.	Multiplier Events: We organized various multiplier events. These events served as platforms to share our experiences, learnings, and best practices, dissemination.

<< Results >>

The tangible products of our work include:
1.	Comprehensive Needs Assessments: Conducted in the three partner countries, these assessments provided invaluable insights and lessons, forming a foundation for strategies in inclusion practices.
2.	Inclusion Platform with E-Learning Modules: We developed a dynamic online platform featuring a suite of e-learning modules and resources. 
3.	Enhanced Cooperation Experience: The project fostered a collaborative environment, leading to fruitful exchanges between project partners, public organizations, and private SMEs. 
4.	Training of Trainers (ToT) Program: Our ToT program has effectively equipped trainers with the skills and knowledge necessary to disseminate inclusion practices more widely.
5.	E-Learning Materials: Tailored e-learning materials focused on the inclusion of young NEETs have been developed and tested through local pilot training programs, ensuring practical applicability and relevance.
6.	Learning Sessions and Materials for Staff/Support Staff and Private Companies: These resources, complemented by seven informative videos, have significantly enhanced the capability of staff and companies in supporting NEETs.

2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000049821.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000049821.title: Razvoj inovativnih metoda učenja korištenja pametnih tahografa u svrhu jačanja procesa digitalizacije i dekarbonizacije prometa
2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000049821.summary:
<< Background >>

The partner consortium applied for this project because it saw the need to provide professional drivers and transport personnel with the possibility of vocational education and training in the field of using new generation tachographs, which would increase the level of quality of their work in the transport sector. The project addressed the following needs: 1) the need for a uniform way of using digital and smart tachographs with the aim of reducing potential device manipulations; 2) the need to create a new vocational education and training program for members of the target group; 3) the need for regional harmonization of the use of tachograph devices and harmonization of the new program with the European qualification framework; 4) the need to introduce new learning outcomes in the transport sector; 5) the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions through learning about eco-driving.

<< Objectives >>

With this project we wanted to achieve the following: 1) To develop a non-formal curriculum for professional drivers and transport personnel in the field of using the new generation tachographs; 2) To develop a new digital platform that will contain all learning material related to new generation tachographs and eco-driving, as well as the E-learning system intended for distance learning of professional drivers and transport personnel; 3) To upgrade the capabilities of participating organizations to perform vocational eduaction and trainings for their target groups, and to better connect with other stakeholders in the transport sector; 4) To promote green practices and sustainable development principles within the transport sector.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were implemented during the project: 1) Kick-off meeting (held in Nova Gradiška, Croatia); 2) Four transnational meetings (two in Ljubljana, Slovenija; two in Nova Gradiška, Croatia); 3) Non-formal curriculum development for vocational education and training of professional drivers and transport personnel; 4) Development of webinar titled DeCarbo Traffic; 5) Development of the DriveLab digital platform and the accompanying E-learning system; 6) Test trainings for professional drivers and transport personnel; 7) Training-of-Trainers; 8) Final multiplier events (one conference in each participating country) and final meeting (Zoom meeting).

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs of the project were the following: 1) Developed a non-formal curriculum for professional drivers and transport personnel in the field of using the new generation tachographs (curriculum available in Croatian, Slovenian, English language); 2) Developed digital platform DriveLab and an E-learning platform intended for distance learning of professional drivers which consists of all materials created during the project; 3) Developed webinar DeCarbo Traffic (available in Croatian, Slovenian, English language) and uploaded to DriveLab platform; 4) Created an Excel and PDF form consisting of partner organizations working in the transport sector to whom the project outputs will be disseminated after the project; 5) All project outputs available in digital form. 
The following result was achieved: 1) Strengthened the capacities of participating organizations and the transnational dimension of partnership due to developed non-formal curriculum and DriveLab platform to perform trainings for their target groups.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000050320.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000050320.title: GreenTech Entrepreneurship Challenge
2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000050320.summary:
<< Background >>

Our organizations are working on the development of the innovation ecosystem in Croatia and North Macedonia, where we cooperate with various stakeholders who co-create the ecosystem, but until now vocational schools were not represented in this important process. From our experience in conducting entrepreneurial programs and competitions for various groups, we are aware of the power of change that this approach has, and we wanted to apply it in this project. Motivated by the idea of ​​integrating the development of entrepreneurial thinking with the development of ecologically sustainable innovations, we wanted to implement a project that would involve students from technical vocational schools in the process of creating business ideas based on green and sustainable technologies. We addressed the need of the labor market by improving students' competences regarding problem solving, team collaboration, creativity and innovation. We addressed the countries and world’s need for innovation in the field of green technologies by equipping young students with knowledge and skills to develop solutions. We addressed the needs of vocational schools by equipping them with modern educational materials and new creative tools and techniques.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to give an educational experience to schools, teachers and students which emphasizes the importance and need for entrepreneurial mindset and innovations in the field of green tech. We wanted to bring two organizations together and exchange and collaborate by developing best outputs that can be used in regional and international context. We wanted to bring closer the local companies that are innovative and green with students who are interested in possibly working in those companies by developing innovative technologies. We wanted to raise awareness of students and schools as well about climate change and sustainable practices that are needed in order to gain new curriculums and new practical work in the field of green tech.

<< Implementation >>

Our project team, comprising partner organizations from Croatia and North Macedonia, effectively managed the project and its activities. We designed a web platform and promotional strategy and opened new communication channels with our project's target groups. We created educational materials on entrepreneurship and innovation for higher-grade vocational students, which we disseminated via Google Classroom. We conducted 22 workshops across ten schools and provided teacher education in both countries.

Students developed innovative solutions, which they presented in school and interschool competitions, receiving valuable feedback and advice from industry partners from both countries. We shared our project activities through various channels, including online webinars and onsite events with partners from other projects. Finally, we summarized our learnings in a lessons learned document that provides guidance for developing and implementing a student innovation competition.

<< Results >>

Our project's results and outputs are a) developed educational materials which describe best practices, procedures and steps in organizing similar innovative competitions. b)developed a web platform where project organizations, partners and other stakeholders are mentioned and where all materials are open and accessible to others interested in the project. 
c) collaborated with 10  vocational schools from Croatia and North Macedonia
d)implemented 22 workshops for students in Croatia and North Macedonia
d)created 20+ students solutions which are sustainable and  innovative
e)organized 9 school competitions where students presented their solutions in front of local entrepreneurial ecosystem
f)organized 2 inter school competitions where students and teachers from all school gathered and competed for best prizes
g)gathered 8 partners from industries who are interested in student’s innovations in the field of green tech 
h)organized a 1 international event where we connected the teachers and stakeholders from those two countries on an online webinar and discussed the topic of innovation in the field of green tech with vocational students.

2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000050920.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000050920.title: RobotTheater: how can robots become an integral part of theater plays
2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000050920.summary:
<< Background >>

Robotics is a popular discipline in the field of technical sciences that includes knowledge from mechanical engineering, electrical engineering and computing. Although there are many initiatives in the field of robotics, it is still not present as subject in schools, but as an extracurricular program. Theater and drama, on the other hand, are a combination of art and the humanities and are present in schools through the mother tongue and literature subjects, as well as extracurricular programs. In the literature, it is possible to find several attempts to combine these areas, but this is often unavailable to schools due to lack of the necessary equipment, high costs and specific knowledge from both areas. This project, using the partners' domain knowledge, aims to explore and bring the combination of these areas closer to schools. Additionally, traditionally robotics is associated with boys, while theater is more associated with girls. Reducing these prejudices encouraged us to implement the project. Through work on a multidisciplinary project of a theater play with robots, everyone involved will have the opportunity to learn the basics of both fields, thus earning the confidence and potentially choosing it as their career path.

<< Objectives >>

The RobotTheater project focuses on building a new model of cooperation between the technical, artistic and humanistic fields with the aim of improving the exchange of knowledge and reducing the gender gap among young people.
The main goal of the project is to increase interest in both, robotics and theater, develop innovative learning materials and resources, build educators' capacities, and improve mutual understanding and cooperation between professionals in these fields through interdisciplinary projects.
Therefore, the specific objectives of the project are: (1) exchanging good practices among partner countries, (2) providing tools, methodology and approaches to facilitate the acquisition of the necessary skills for learning and teaching about robotics and theater, (3) increasing the interest of teachers in acquiring competencies that they need for multidisciplinary projects involving robotics and theater, (4) developing informal learning aimed at strengthening theater and robotics professionals, and (5) creating a comprehensive guide that includes a methodological framework, video guidelines, and an action and recommendation plan for robotics and theater professionals.

<< Implementation >>

In order to achieve the goals of the project, a whole series of activities was carried out:
-	work on the preparation of a Comprehensive guide for professionals in the field of robotics and theater. The work itself was carried out in three phases: (1) theoretical background in the field of robotics and theater, and research of literature and existing examples of their interaction, (2) description of practical implementation and advices for creating theatrical performances with robots and (3) action and recommendation plan with a detailed description of the creation of theater performances with robots and advices on how to make the performances realistic and interesting for the audience
-	two short term joint staff trainings where the capabilities of robots in the theater were tested and seven examples of plays with robots were recorded. The first training was held in Trbovlje, Slovenia, and the second training in Ivanić-Grad, Croatia
-	two multiplier virtual events in Croatia (110 participants) and two live multiplier events in Slovenia (53 participants) where the target audience was presented with the results of the project, advices and practical examples of how to make theatrical performances with robots.

<< Results >>

The concrete output of the project is RobotTheater - Comprehensive guide for professionals, available in three languages: Croatian, Slovenian and English. The Guide is intended for teachers and educators in the field of robotics and informatics, as well as in the field of theater, language and literature. It promotes a multidisciplinary approach and the development of 21st century skills. It consists of seven sections: 
(1) robots and robotics, 
(2) theater and theater art, 
(3) robots in theater, 
(4) implementation of robots in theater, 
(5) development of a play with robot-actors, 
(6) robots, theater and school and 
(7) educational robots. 
As additional materials to the Guide, nine theatrical plays with robots have been prepared and recorded, and the recordings are freely available online. Each of these plays uses a different type of robot and the roles of robots and humans in the plays are different, in order to show the full range of possibilities offered by robots in theater. All these examples are described and analyzed in detail in the Guide.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000050927.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000050927.title: Promoting VET in computer, electrical/electronic and mechanical engineering to reduce skills mismatch
2021-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000050927.summary:
<< Background >>

Based on European skills and job surveys, skills shortage and skills mismatch were identified as significant areas of concern. Analyses on a European level show a skills shortage in computer, electrical/ electronic and mechanical engineering (CEME) as top occupational areas. Additionally, even though student and NEET career counselling is an integral element in the Austrian, and significantly less in Croatian (education) system, initiatives for student counselling and individual orientation tools addressing the promotion of VET and jobs in CEME are lacking. As majority of senior students of primary education and the secondary level and especially NEETs do not have the necessary experience and knowledge to gain more direct insight into VET and job options related to CEME, counselling and orientation support is required. As a consequence of inadequate career counselling an alarming number of young people are registered as NEETs. Along with that, many career counsellors lack in appropriate tools and skills to provide information and motivation for a career path in CEME. This project has directly addressed those needs, providing new digital solutions and tools to foster student and NEET career orientation.

<< Objectives >>

With the aim of improving the promotion of VET occupations and the introduction of career counselling in technical occupations as a very important component of the education system, project has focused on the exchange and application of good practices in three main areas: promotion of VET in electrical engineering, computer science and mechanical engineering; estimation of primary school pupils' capacities and abilities and orientation through individualized digital tools; and assistance in introducing the individualized career counselling concept for VET students and NEETs. The project has introduced a modernized approach to student career couselling taking into account the interests and the way young people communicate in present days - through digital channels and using multimedia platforms for gathering information and receiving feedback on their prospective career paths. 

<< Implementation >>

The main activities that this Project has implemented are as follows: 

1. Analysis of good practice examples: field visits to ÖSB Consulting in Vienna and to Technical School and Croatian Employment Bureau in Karlovac: job shadowing activities;
2. Design, development and maintenance of a multimedia platform for the promotion of technical VET including short video films introducing and promoting CEME occupations;
3. Creation of competence check tool and digital self-assessment tool for senior primary school students;
4. Development of the concept of the individualized career counselling for VET students and NEETs.


<< Results >>

1.	Analysis of good practice examples of ÖSB Consulting and of Technical School Karlovac and its partners in CEME which resulted in understanding similarities and adapting and adopting good Austrian practices in Croatian education system in the field of career counselling; 
2.	Design, development and maintenance of an online multimedia tool for promotion of technical VET which resulted in creation of a three-lingual mulitimedia platform that serves as basis for all information sharing and free usage of project tools including 6 videos thet represent different occupations; 
3.	Created concepts and free online tools of digital competence check and self-assessment tools that help students to explore their level of preferences and interest in CEME; 
4.	Created concept of the individualized career counselling tool for teachers and counsellors of VET students and NEETs which introduces a new concept and document that will serve as basis for development of further individual student counselling -  documents describing the process and requirements for student counselling; 
5.	Dissemination of project results - results were presented online, in person, through media, round table.

2021-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000048044.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000048044.title: PESCA SOSTENIBILE E MENU' “NARRATIVI” IN ADRIATICO
2021-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000048044.summary:
<< Background >>

In a global context in which sustainable consumption of natural resources has now become necessary, indispensable and unavoidable for the future livelihood of communities, education is undoubtedly one of the most powerful tools we have to trigger an ecological transition that is first and foremost cultural. Therefore, the AdriEATic project was born out of an awareness of the importance of educating professionals of the next generation, on the basic principles of sustainability and how to translate them into concrete tools for change. Teachers of Hotelier Institutes were chosen as the target group, precisely because food plays a fundamental role in shaping the environment, economy and society we inhabit, and fish resources are no exception, especially in the Adriatic, one of the most productive and consequently most overexploited seas in the Mediterranean. In this context, introducing teachers to the concept of narrative menus as best practices and equipping them with the necessary tools to create them and transfer this knowledge to students can become a powerful tool to make restaurants real places of innovative experiences, related to food sustainability, local traditions and environmental protection.

<< Objectives >>

The overall goal of the project was to educate teachers at Hotelier Institutes, the main target group, on the value and opportunities related to the basic principles of sustainable fishing and environmental protection, so that the transfer of this knowledge to students can generate in them a critical consciousness and competence on the good practice of narrative menus, in order to educate them on the use of food as a means of global change. 
Specifically, the AdriEATic project created a permanent platform that aimed to:
- improve the level of knowledge on sustainable fishing actions and best practices in EU in teachers of hotelier institutes and culinary schools; 
- introduce knowledge of territorial marketing and the good practice of the "narrative menu" in the said institutions, so that restaurants also become places of knowledge of values, such as the seasonality of seafood products and the sustainability of their consumption;
- encourage active teaching, through innovative teaching methodologies based on European best practices;
- encourage networking among the institutions involved and interactions between fishing cooperatives and the restaurant sector.

<< Implementation >>

The AdriEATic project consisted of two main activities: 
- Activity 1 involved the co-generation and implementation of the Toolkit intended for teachers of hotelier institutes, consisting of digital training modules, aimed at exploring best practices on sustainable fishing and the supply chain at sea and on land, indications on sustainable fishing and territorial marketing, for the purpose of the creation of the narrative menus. 
- Activity 2 involved experimentation and validation of the Toolkit through the formulation of the narrative menus, with field verification of the effectiveness of the training modules by other teachers and expert validation. 
- During the course of the project, in order to reuse savings in a concrete and productive way, it was decided by mutual agreement between the partners to carry out an additional activity, which included the creation of printed booklets in three languages (IT-HR-EN), encapsulating the heart of AdriEATic and the narrative menus created, to be distributed to the hotelier institutes in the territories (Italian and Croatian), for greater dissemination of the project and whose file will be available and freely downloadable on the AdriEATic platform.

<< Results >>

The main outcome of the project is an online platform, structured as a real guide on EU best practices of sustainable fishing and fish supply chain, fundamentals of food storytelling and narrative menus, as well as a technical-scientific guide on the main Adriatic fish species and their sustainability tenor, understood as seasonality, minimum size, fishing techniques and local traditional fishing methods.
The toolkit is structured in three training modules, presented in 3 languages (IT-HR-EN) and in a creative and interactive mode; it contains a template sheet for the creation of the narrative menu and a web-forum for sharing among schools, also functional for peer-review. Four schools (2 Italian and 2 Croatian) were involved and a total of 15 teachers were trained (3 more than originally planned). From the teachers' training work and their consecutive processing with their respective classes, 14 narrative menus were produced.
An additional activity, not initially placed in the proposal, was carried out to ensure greater dissemination of this work: printed booklets were created in three languages, containing the heart of the project to be distributed in the territory and whose file can be downloaded from the online platform.

2021-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000048305.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000048305.title: Empowering the professional profile of people with migrant background
2021-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000048305.summary:
<< Background >>

“Language is one key to a successful integration”. 
Partners decided to apply for “JobLinguo” because they wished to support migrants in their community in having better job prospects and be a stronger presence in the labour market, specifically for what concerns three of the sectors in which they have difficulties in being employed (public administration, financial and insurance activities, agricultural field).
When applying for a job, knowing the sectoral language related to it can be a crucial criterion of selection for an employer. 
Through the implementation of “JobLinguo”, the Consortium answered the needs of migrants with previous studies or working experience in the above-mentioned sectors that were lacking sectoral language knowledge in the national language of the hosting country. The format of the deliverables that were created answered the educational needs of adults when it comes to foreign language learning, especially in the case of sector-specific vocabulary.
In addition, as a consequence, some of the needs of potential employers from the above-mentioned sectors were also met, thanks to the training of potential employees with a good knowledge of the sectoral language related to certain sector-specific tasks.

<< Objectives >>

“JobLinguo” was aimed at a. supporting the job market inclusion of people with migrant background through improving their professional profile in terms of sectoral language and b. adapting the training offer of VET providers and other stakeholders to the linguistic needs of people with migrant background.
The Consortium wanted to support the identified target group to get equal opportunities in job seeking in three sectors in which it is necessary to know a specific vocabulary and communication cannot be covered in a common foreign language (such as English for example). 
The goal was to create a programme that was in line with the training needs of adults with a migrant background when it comes to foreign language learning. The programme and materials were envisaged as adequate tools for group and individual learning, allowing potential users to continue the learning process even outside lessons.

<< Implementation >>

The project implementation was structured into four activities:
1. The first activity was dedicated to all the management and monitoring activities, together with the physical partners' meetings.
2. The second activity was dedicated to the development of the language programme covering the agriculture, public administration, finance and insurance sectors. Firstly, a methodology was developed for the preliminary research and consisted of instructions on how to extrapolate secondary data from academic publications/reports or institutional data relevant to the project topics, as well as three distinct questionnaires to be used for surveying and interviewing potential employers from the three sectors. At the end of the research phase, two short reports were elaborated. Based on the results of these reports, guidelines to be used for the development of the programmes were provided and lessons, exercises and graphic materials were elaborated for the creation of three eBooks as well as the storyboards for the 2D games. 
3. The third activity was dedicated to the implementation of the local trainings.
4. The fourth activity was dedicated to the online dissemination of the project and the implementation of the local dissemination events.

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs
Sectoral language programme
The programme is structured in three courses: agriculture, public administration, finance and insurance.
Each course comprises an eBook and a 2D game.  The eBooks are designed in a way to combine reading, listening and graphic representation to provide a comprehensive learning experience adequate to the learning needs of adults with a migrant background with a basic level of knowledge (A1-A2) of the national language of the hosting country. The 2D games are designed in a way that learners can test their knowledge dedicating it between 5 and 10 min every day. 
The programme has been developed in Italian, German, Croatian, Slovenian and in English for stakeholders operating in other countries.

Monitoring Report
The Monitoring Report contains information related to the learning achievements of the four local training programmes implemented by partners in their countries as well as a last section dedicated to the evaluation and feedback provided by learners.

Other results
The learners involved in the local trainings have improved their sector-specific linguistic knowledge.
Stakeholders operating in the VET sector positively evaluated the programme and are interested in using it.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2021-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000049677.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000049677.title: Synergic TRaining to Enhance Entrepreneurial and Technological Skills
2021-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000049677.summary:
<< Background >>

In 2020, NEETs (Not in Education, Employment or Training) reached the worrying average rate of 23.3 per cent (ISTAT 2021). This phenomenon has both a social cost (the more a person experiences this condition, the higher the risk of accumulating disadvantages in accessing the world of work, developing deviant behaviour, physical and mental health problems, and impoverishing social relations) and an economic cost. According to the Eurofound report (2011), an economic loss related to the NEET phenomenon in Europe was estimated at 153 billion in 2011. To contrast this phenomenon, the EU has placed the reduction of youth unemployment and the strategy to effectively engage as many young people as possible in employment at the centre of its policy agenda. NEETs were mentioned in the policy discussions of the Europe 2020 flagship initiative 'Youth on the Move'. 
In light of this, the project piloted new interventions to create training opportunities for NEETs. STREETS aimed to enhance in young people, entrepreneurial, digital and technological skills, which are among the 8 key competences for lifelong learning outlined in the 2018 European Recommendations.


<< Objectives >>

In implementing the STREETS project, the following objectives were to be achieved through the creation of the model and subsequently the realisation of training courses for NEETs (target group).

- to increase entrepreneurial and empowerment skills in order to promote an entrepreneurial propensity in the young target group 
- to increase skills and competences in the field of digital design and technological innovation in order to be able to manage the phenomena related to the digitalisation of production processes linked to the Digital Revolution process in the world of work; 
- consolidate transversal skills (effective communication, stress management, motivation, leadership, team work); 
- involve all stakeholders in order to strengthen the network between the world of vocational training and the world of work;
- to arrive at the description of units of learning outcomes that can be assessed (by using tools created ad hoc and administered as pre- and post-tests) and, therefore, can be used in the description and assessment of professional profiles.





<< Implementation >>

During the lifetime of the STREETS project, 4 macro-activities were implemented:

- Coordination and monitoring (A1): the implementation of these activities (transnational and online meetings, Management Handbook, whatsapp group, mailing list, "STREETS Project" folder on google drive), transversal to the overall project duration, allowed to guarantee the quality and full implementation of the activities through a general coordination mainly oriented to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the project. 

- Creation of the STREETS model and training kit (A2), which led during the first 3 months of STREETS' lifespan to the realisation of the methodological guidelines and training materials.

 - STREETS training pathway" (A3), which envisaged for the following 8 months the realisation of blended pilot courses and workshop activities in Italy, Croatia and Slovenia.

-Dissemination transversal activities (A4) that allowed the partnership to disseminate and transfer, through a strategic framework and the use of the website (www.streetserasmus.eu ), the facebook (streetserasmus) and instagram (streetserasmus_plus) pages, the knowledge and results achieved by STREETS.


<< Results >>

With reference to the objectives set in the STREETS project, the following outputs were achieved:

- Thanks to the pilot training courses and workshop activities, there has been an increase in the skills examined (both skills in the field of entrepreneurship, digitalisation and technology and transversal skills such as effective communication, stress management, motivation, leadership, team work) assessed through quantitative and qualitative indicators. 
- Thanks to the accreditation procedures implemented by the partners, the training course was formally recognised in Italy and Slovenia, which made it expendable in the curricula of young NEETs;
- Thanks to the dissemination activities carried out with the stakeholders interested in the project initiative, all partners had letters of interest signed.

All tangible results (methodological guidelines, training manuals, evaluation tools and power points in English, Italian, Croatian and Slovenian) were uploaded on the official website www.streetserasmus.eu.

2021-2-TR01-KA210-VET-000048266.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-TR01-KA210-VET-000048266.title: Green Design for Future
2021-2-TR01-KA210-VET-000048266.summary:
<< Background >>

With our project, researching the necessary issues to carry out the design phase of the infrastructure projects to be realized in the transportation sector in an environmentally sensitive manner in accordance with the 8th Environment Action program, and identifying the bottlenecks for the actions to be taken within this scope had provided progress in the relevant key areas. Therefore, on behalf of the future, the European Union; -Meeting the greenhouse gas emission reduction target of 2030 and realizing the transition to climate-neutral order by 2050, -Strengthening natural capital, protecting, preserving, and strengthening biological diversity, -Production and consumption activities should have been evaluated and financed in terms of contributing to the objectives of reducing the pressure on the environment and climate (especially in the energy, industry, infrastructure and construction, transportation, and food sectors). The Green Design for Future project would contribute to the activities of expanding the network of all partners and would enable them to participate in new collaborations.

<< Objectives >>

Within the scope of our project, our main goal had been to investigate the necessary issues to carry out the design phase of the infrastructure projects to be realized in the transportation sector in an environmentally sensitive manner in accordance with the 8th Environment Action program and to identify the bottlenecks for the actions to be taken within this scope.
In this context, the main goal of our project had been directly related to our horizontal priority of combating environment and climate change, and the activities to be realized with the participation of each partner in the activities we would carry out within the scope of the project had also been related to our priority "Contributing to innovation in vocational education and training".

<< Implementation >>

Project duration;  2 partnership meetings in Turkiye (Kick-off and Closing meetings), 2 transnational partnership meetings (one in Zagreb, Croatia and one in Bucharest, Romania), 3 online meetings, and 1 final conference were organised.

<< Results >>

Our project had the following results:
We reached the determined quality results of the project, within the budget and on time,
We supported those working on Green Design with continuous vocational and technical training activities,
We increased sectoral communication and created sustainable effects by coming together with sector stakeholders. We ensured effective use of project outputs by sector stakeholders.
The outputs were successfully mainstreamed .

2021-2-TR01-KA210-VET-000049694.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2021-2-TR01-KA210-VET-000049694.title: Güzellik Uzmanlığı Eğitiminde  Ortak Yaklaşımlar
2021-2-TR01-KA210-VET-000049694.summary:
<< Background >>

The beauty industry is constantly evolving, creating new job opportunities, and the number of institutions providing education in this field, employees, and manufacturing companies is increasing day by day. This growth in the industry has led to certain problems. Issues such as the quality of beauty centers, the quality of vocational training centers, the professional and personal development of beauty experts, and the lack of a university in our country offering a four-year undergraduate education mean that the responsibility of training instructors/experts falls on vocational education institutions.

As BDA, our mission is to improve the quality of vocational training, to provide our trainees with high-quality vocational education with up-to-date information, and to create employment opportunities. For this reason, by collaborating with international institutions, we aim to contribute to the quality and capacity development of the beauty industry by training professional beauty experts who have received good education in accordance with EU standards, to observe and examine innovative and complementary studies in different institutions in EU countries, and to transfer knowledge about regulations.


<< Objectives >>

To elevate the educational quality of beauty specialists in the industry to an international level, establish common approaches in terms of educational and sectoral collaborations across nations, discover diversities, ultimately increase their employability, and contribute to the quality and capacity development needed by the sector.
To provide our trainees with high-quality vocational education with up-to-date information about equipment, devices, materials, and cosmetic products used in the industry, ensuring their employment, and fostering their personal development to give them a sense of being global citizens.
To ensure that education is provided at a standard that has the knowledge, skills, and experience necessary to meet the demands of the business world.
Moreover, this project aims to benefit women’s employment since beauty salons are spaces where a significant proportion of employees are women.
To increase and internationalize collaboration by creating a beautiful and reliable international umbrella with institutions in the field of vocational training, thereby contributing to the internationalization strategy.”


<< Implementation >>

The activities we wish to implement in our project (for quality and capacity development) are under the following headings:
        
	•	Methods and techniques applied in the beauty industry
	•	Review of educational curricula
	•	Usage of medical devices
	•	Examination/observation of cosmetic/chemical laboratories
	•	Monitoring of new technologies/applications
	•	Holistic skin/body health practices
	•	Massage and energy therapies
	•	Entrepreneurship and business management
	•	Inviting expert doctors/academics for presentations
         and online meetings.
      


<< Results >>


Initially,we examined the curriculum programs applied by the University,Vocational High Schools, and Private Academies in Cosmetology,Skin Care and Beauty departments in all partner countries. In our country and in European countries,we observed that vocational education institutions training beauty experts exhibited many common approaches in various aspects of the field. We noticed that some practices are more important in one country and less in another. For example, in our country, beauty experts perform skin care more with cosmetic and medical devices, whereas in Poland and Croatia manual practices are more predominant, and in Portugal, knowing the anatomy of the face,hands, and feet is very important, whereas in our country,understanding the skin is more important.
We observed the international dimension of industry collaboration and legal procedures. In the partner countries, because the sector and educational institutions are more collaborative, teachers who work in connection with the sector and are part of the sector remain up-to-date in terms of professional knowledge
Based on these examinations, we created statistical data from the parameters of the training needs analysis of beauty experts and salons in the countries.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-CZ01-KA210-VET-000081613.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-CZ01-KA210-VET-000081613.title: Rakousko-uherské kořeny a vzájemné vazby
2022-1-CZ01-KA210-VET-000081613.summary:
<< Background >>

We decided to apply for the project mainly due to the need to share and exchange our experience with the effort to develop the educational process in terms of innovative methodology of teaching economics and its close connection with practice.
We would like to contribute to innovation in vocational education, to develop key competences and to keep up with the needs of today's world. 

<< Objectives >>

By implementing our project, we want to achieve that each student sees the world in context and at the same time is able to develop their own potential. One of the means is cross-sectional days, when the student combines knowledge from all subjects into one unit.
At the same time, international cooperation on cross-cutting days deepens the interaction between schools in Europe and contributes to the removal of social and psychological barriers between students.

<< Implementation >>

All activities listed in the project were implemented and their implementation exceeded expectations in terms of benefits both for the students and teachers, and participating organisations. 
The project included various types of activities that were covered by the unifying theme of common roots and mutual ties of the participating countries and schools. The activities focused on developing cultural awareness and interest in history (activity Historical research, Letter to the ancestors), other activities aimed at developing professional knowledge and skills (activity Preparation for the 29th International Trade Fair of Practise Enterprises and activity Visit at the 29th Trade Fair of Practise Enterprises), and the most important activities in the form of cross-sectional days aimed to connect language and professional knowledge, while at the same time developing the soft skills of the project participants (activity Cross-sectional days in Krakow, Bratislava, Buje and Prague, and activity Reflexion of the stay in Krakow, Bratislava and Buje). 

<< Results >>

The project followed two lines and the results can be divided into two areas which are closely related  in terms of the project: 
1) The first line is the students' way through the two year project which led to the strengthening of their professional knowledge, language and communication skills, to the proficiency in the digital and IT field and at the same time, to the development of their soft skills. 
The concrete output is a brochure of the results of the historical research in terms of the impact on mutual relationships in Krakow (see the attachment), and a catalogue of students' work introducing individual activities (e.g. presentations, letters to the ancestors, posters proposing new uses for the fortresses around Pula in tourism, interactive map of mutual relations). The outputs also include videos and reports made by students after each cross-sectional activity.
2) The second line is the work of teachers who acted as consultants and mentors and evaluated the methods used on cross-sectional topics and in individual activities. The result is a methodological manual which can be used by teachers at any type of school as as an inspiration for the organization of cross-sectional days and projects.
