2022-1-ES01-KA210-VET-000082630.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-ES01-KA210-VET-000082630.title: Intelligent Tourism Destinations
2022-1-ES01-KA210-VET-000082630.summary:
<< Background >>

Small cities in inland territories present difficulties when planning and developing actions aimed at tourism not only as an economic engine, but also as a reference for sustainable local development that relies on the cooperation stakeholders in the field of tourism to strengthen the supply the value chain based on principles of sustainability, digitalization and training. In this sense, the cooperation of 4 European cities with similar characteristics has been necessary, which detected that tourism is based on an industrial bubble whose management has been based on promotional actions to achieve a greater influx of visitors without being aligned with factors that conform smart tourist destinations. Therefore, the needs that were detected were: 1) Tourism planning and management, improving fundamental aspects of governance, sustainability, accessibility, connectivity, innovation, tourist information and online marketing; 2) Creation of stakeholder’s network to collaborate and cooperate with the aim to improve tourism development; 3) Creation of tourist destinations aligned with other sectors to balance the positive and negative effects of tourism development.

<< Objectives >>

The general objective sought to be achieved is to find new vocational training solutions to improve the development of capacities of civil servants and professionals working in public administrations in the tourism field, to expand the leisure offer in sustainable tourist attractions. The specific objectives were: 1) To increase professionals skills (civil servants and entrepreneurs) to expand the leisure offer and the tourist attraction of small cities, offering additional experiences based on culture, digitalization and sustainable solutions; 2) To strength capacities for local tourism development, between small and medium-sized cities, offering short-term stays in an easy-to-visit environment; 3) To improve capacities of small municipalities to develop new tourism products based on digitalization and sustainability through the promotion of new tourism businesses and the citizen participation process to guarantee a positive impact on the territory.

<< Implementation >>

During the 18 months of project execution, all the activities planned in the application form have been carried out, which were planned in 5 work packages:
1) Research and mapping on capacity development in tourism: each country carried out a search and report on good practices related to capacity development across Europe. Surveys were also conducted.
2)Co-creation workshops: 3 workshops were held in each country and one internationally in Online format, in which public employees, entrepreneurs and VET professionals of tourism sector participated with the aim of discussing smart tourist destinations and planning for tourism development. sustainable, integrated and quality in the cities that work together in this project.
3)Guides and Recommendations aimed at the stakeholders involved to help their training in intelligent and sustainable tourism planning.
4)Management, control and evaluation of activities by the coordinator and those responsible for each work package to ensure the quality of the activities and results.
5)Dissemination and communication of activities, project progress and downloadable materials.

<< Results >>

The ambition of the project has been to explore and develop tailor-made tourism plans for small and medium-sized cities, where the protagonists of the sector (public and private) are the drivers of their own professional development, which have inspired, supported and trained each other in a Community of Practice (peer-to-peer). It has been possible to develop the tangible results that were planned in the proposal and quantified them based on quantitative indicators: creation of a network of 45 agents from the 3 countries representing the public and private sectors, more than 200 stakeholders participating in the online survey; participation of 45 agents in the Co-creation Workshops; information to at least 3,000 recipients through different dissemination channels, design of 3 training itineraries; inclusion of at least 50 agents interested in the topic through communications and 1 Guide with recommendations to improve capacity in planning smart tourist destinations. Likewise, valuable results reports have been developed and have served to understand opinions and the current context, and also synergies have been created between tourism target groups.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000084244.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000084244.title: Žuti patuljak
2022-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000084244.summary:
<< Background >>

There are several needs that partner schools have identified in their institutions. Primarily, it is the modernization of electrical engineering teaching. The Croatian national curriculum for this profession dates back to 1996, while the Slovenian one is more modern, from 2018. The partners recognized the importance of acquiring vocational skills of students based on practical work in accordance with the needs of the labor market. Therefore, it was necessary to empower vocational teachers to create teaching content that will enable students to acquire specific vocational knowledge and skills. Teachers should be able to see good examples of practice in school and in the real sector in order to implement knowledge in their work. The topic of renewable energy sources is part of the existing curricula and an important social topic, so the need to promote awareness of sustainability and energy efficiency was imposed. One of the schools’imperatives is to implement an internationalization strategy in order to increase the attractiveness of vocational education.

<< Objectives >>

The implementation of the project aimed to modernize the vocational teaching of the electrical engineering department by creating a practicum (collection of exercises) on the topic of photovoltaic systems that will be used in teaching. It was important that the exercises were based on practical work and the modular principle - that they connect different levels of knowledge and skills and different vocational subjects. This results in higher quality vocational education for students and easier adoption of learning outcomes. The aim was to provide teachers with professional training, exchange of good practice and monitoring of modern trends in the profession, and institutions to establish various partner collaborations, strengthen management skills and better quality vocational education.

<< Implementation >>

The main activity of the project was the creation of a collection of exercises Photovoltaic systems. Different types of project team meetings, learning and teaching activities were realized: lectures, workshops, practical work. In addition to live meetings, members of the project teams also met online in order to better realize the project's goals. As part of the activities, the project teams visited various institutions and companies dealing with renewable energy sources. Teachers are provided with expert lectures on the topic of the project. The students participated in the testing of the practicum - laboratory and workshop exercises where the effectiveness of the created exercises was examined. Field classes, workshops and lectures on the topic of renewable energy sources are organized for the students. During the entire project cycle, dissemination and evaluation activities were carried out.

<< Results >>

A collection of tasks (practicum) Photovoltaic systems for teaching electrical engineering was created in Croatian and Slovenian. Practicum is an open educational content that consists of learning outcomes, exercises, a list of required materials, instructions for teachers and other relevant information. Two versions of the racks for the photovoltaic module used in the exercises were made. Accompanying documentation was created for them - 3D drawings, an elaboration and a lesson for teaching mechanical constructions. In addition, two English language teaching lessons were created with the topics of renewable resources and solar energy to improve students' language skills. The project logo and the project website were created. The website contains general information about the project and partners, descriptions of implemented activities, project results, dissemination materials and other relevant information. Good cooperation between schools continued and new cooperations with different institutions and companies were established. Students are provided with practical work at school and the acquisition of specific professional skills, while teachers have excellent experience in project work, skill development and lifelong learning.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000081592.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000081592.title: Piccoli Musei in viaggio
2022-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000081592.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was born from the desire to give national and international visibility and strength to small local museums, which hold the historical culture of the territories in which they are located. Thanks to the collaboration of associations working in the same field, they can organize important cultural museum events. Small museums are true hidden treasures, but at times difficult to reach. Therefore, the project aimed to provide educational and digital tools to the participating organizations in order to help small museums "get discovered" within Europe and to spread the culture they house.

The target of the project was small museums and local cultural organizations. The reasons behind the conception and implementation of the project were to provide the target group with specific and adequate technological tools, to increase their knowledge on the digitization of local heritage to improve its accessibility, and to promote the dissemination of an innovative approach among museum managers in local contexts.



<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to help small museums enhance their strengths in promoting local cultures. 
The specific objectives have been to improve digital, marketing, and communication skills in the museum sector, share good practices among small museums and local organizations in the digital sector, and increase the international dimension of museums. The planned activities concerned specific training courses and cooperation between partners thanks to which participants have learned how to use different digital promotion tools. 

<< Implementation >>

The planned activities concerned: the collection of information on all the advertising tools that the EU and the projects financed by it make available to museums; the inclusion of the Museums participating in the project on these platforms/webapp; specific training in the field of museum digitization also using the results of the Erasmus "Museum Sector Alliance" (Mu.Sa) project; the production of a practical guide "Small museums on the go" that helped other museums grow.


<< Results >>

The results have been the ceration of practical tools to simplified the inclusion of the Museums on all the identified tools (platforms and various apps); the definition of a long-term digital strategy; the preparation and dissemination of a practical guide for small museums, the increase in the number of face-to-face and online visits for the museums involved; at least one school in the territory of each partner discovered very distant museums and small, often hidden treasures.

2022-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000083332.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000083332.title: VET jest atrakcyjny! - promowanie kształcenia i szkolenia zawodowego (VET) przez doradców zawodowych
2022-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000083332.summary:
<< Background >>

The ‘VET is attractive!’ project was developed in response to several key VET needs:
1. aligning education with labour market needs. The project aimed to increase the attractiveness of vocational education by improving the quality of educational programmes, adapting them to labour market requirements and strengthening cooperation between schools and employers.
2. Increasing labour market opportunities: The aim was to provide vocational school students with more employment opportunities through the development of their competences, including practical preparation for work in modern enterprises within the framework of dual education.
3. support of vocational counsellors. The project focused on supporting career counsellors by equipping them with knowledge, tools and examples of good practice. This was crucial in order for them to be able to advise young people and parents more effectively in choosing a career path.
4. improving the image of vocational education: The project also aimed to change the perception of technical and industrial professions as attractive, inspiring young people to choose such educational paths.

<< Objectives >>

The main aim of the project was to increase the attractiveness of vocational education and training by providing vocational counsellors with the knowledge, practical methods and examples of good practice needed to provide guidance and counselling services to school students, as well as their parents and teaching staff. The project also aimed to strengthen cooperation between educational institutions and business by developing and creating examples of good practice and recommendations to assist young people in choosing a career path related to the technical industry and to improve the overall image of vocational education. The knowledge and competences acquired during the study visits to Poland and Croatia acted as a form of support and supplementary support for specific competence gaps identified by practical vocational teachers and entrepreneurs. Thanks to international cooperation and project activities such as study visits and workshops, the project provided an opportunity to exchange good practices and experiences between partners from Poland and Croatia, strengthening vocational education in both countries.

<< Implementation >>

Two 5-day study visits to Croatia and Poland were organised for 21 people, including representatives of teachers of practical vocational training, management staff of secondary technical schools, vocational counsellors from Poland and Croatia. Participation in the study visits enabled the exchange of good practices and information on education and VET in Poland and Croatia. Participants had the opportunity to compare the Polish and Croatian education systems, including dual training, and became acquainted with interesting and innovative teaching methods, work techniques and the organisation of the course of lessons. Workshops were also organised for a wide range of stakeholders in Poland and Croatia, which were attended by a wide range of participants (vocational counsellors, entrepreneurs, teachers/vocational supervisors, representatives of secondary technical schools, representatives of local government units (JST), representatives of research units and non-governmental organisations dealing with issues of vocational education including dual training) and representatives of the project team. A good practice guide for enhancing the quality and attractiveness of VET was developed. 

<< Results >>

The project ‘VET is attractive!’ has produced numerous results. The development of the competences of 21 people (including: vocational counsellors, teachers of practical vocational training) from Poland and Croatia made it possible to strengthen cooperation between schools and businesses and to better support students in their choice of career path. A report ‘Examples of good practice with recommendations’ was produced in three languages, providing guidance on dual education and cooperation between education and business. The number of participants in the dissemination workshops in Poland and Croatia was increased, significantly broadening the scope of the project. Workshops and study visits demonstrated the attractiveness of VET, supporting its positive image. The project has enabled the establishment of lasting relationships between schools and companies, which can be developed in further initiatives and projects. Dissemination of the project's results in social media and during various events increased its visibility and positively influenced the image of dual education in the partner countries . The project has created a solid foundation for further international cooperation and the development of initiatives to promote VET.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2022-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000084911.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000084911.title: Think Green
2022-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000084911.summary:
<< Background >>

The project responds to three main needs common to all partners.
1. Modernization of educational directions - a change in market philosophy and the challenges related to climate change force the labor market to become more interested in understanding the mechanisms of sustainable development and ecology, which translates into the need to supplement the content taught in the courses offered.
2. Internationalization - international cooperation and exchange of students and staff is an important condition for maintaining and improving the quality of activities and the basis for the development plans of each school.
3. Motivation of staff and students - the experience of remote work and the pandemic has affected the attitude and approach to school duties of both staff and students. The change in the form of education, although not very popular with students, has resulted in a break from the traditional format of classes and has shifted the emphasis to learning outcomes. One of the observable effects of the pandemic is also, for example, reduced periods of concentration, reluctance to sit at desks for long periods or a change in the form of acquiring knowledge towards interdisciplinary. All of this was reachable within the project.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to identify and collect proposals for supplementing vocational education curricula (to the curricula of computer science and technology, printing technology and food and fashion design) with recycling content. As a result of its implementation, the partners' curricula includes such elements, and recommendations and proposals regarding the content of teaching will be forwarded to other schools and institutions supervising vocational education in partner countries and the European Union.



<< Implementation >>

The project involved the implementation of three educational projects in the form of preparation and implementation of study visits in the peer-to-peer learning method, the exchange of experiences and good practices by the school staff and putting them together as recommendations and discussing them at the conference. The whole is complemented by the meetings - starting and ending and activities between the meetings.
Kick-off meeting
Study visit to Poland
Study visit to Turkey
Study visit to Croatia
Conference
Summary meeting

<< Results >>

As a result of the project recommendations are developed to supplement the curriculum for different directions vocational education. In addition, 42 students participated in study visits abroad in the form of educational projects prepared under the supervision of teachers, 150 students participated in workshops conducted by project participants, and around 30 representatives of Polish schools in the project conference, plus representatives form Educational Department.

2022-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000081547.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000081547.title: Make it green
2022-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000081547.summary:
<< Background >>

The partnership of the project was formed by three schools for catering and tourism so we found the the theme of the project oriented towards a development of a carbon-free society very interesting.
We are aware of the problem of wasted food, mass tourism and waste which could be transformed in a new product. That was also the reason of our orientation towards the problems which we are dealing with most frequently in schools for catering and tourism. Thus the goal of our project was finding solutions to the above problems with green tourism, waste-free cooking and circular economy - gifts made from waste materials.

<< Objectives >>

The theme delt with in the project was covering all of the above mentioned goals:
- Green tourism - to promote green and smart tourism in the local environments of individual partner organizations
- Waste-free cooking - to find solutions by following the principles of »zero« waste
- Waste as a business gift – to give wasted materials a new story, new usefulness and added value by recycling and reusing them.


<< Implementation >>

In the range of the project we carried out three short-term mobilities of students and teachers, each in one of the cities of our partner organizations. We organized two visits, the first one to Rovinj to educate the staff about the theme of the project itself and the second one at the end of the project to Maribor to conclude the project by analysing the goals achieved. We carried out two virtual meetings of coordinators, one at the beginning of the project to determine timelines and tasks and
another after 12 months to provide a short analysis of the project.

<< Results >>

The results of the project are:
- a booklet of recepies translated in all of the languages of our partner schools and in English. The booklet is in pdf. form as well as in a printed version;
- a tourist arrangement for a mushroom picking weekend presented in a local environment by a partner organisation;
- a business gift made by melting used bottles which added to the materials used a new useful value;
- video spots presenting the content of the project with materials used;
-  articles about the project published in different media.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

hr.name: Strukovna škola Eugena Kumičića Rovinj - Scuola Di Formazione Professionale Eugen Kumičić Rovigno

2022-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000083218.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000083218.title: Digital transformation is making its way into businesses - developing key performance indicators to boost sector productivity
2022-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000083218.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied because we are part of the EU umbrella organization FIEC, in which several working groups are being set up to discuss key sectoral priorities, trends, situation and issues related to working paper MULTIANNUAL WORKING PROGRAMME FOR EU SOCIAL DIALOGUE (2020-2022) approved by all members. In the latter, some activities are focused on VET. One of the thematic VET priorities is to contribute to the green and digital transitions and support the construction sector in these transitions, promote vocational and education training, and adapt training systems to digitalization and other technological developments. The new skills requirements for the workforce in terms of technology and digitalization highlight the need to upskill the workforce and also to train young people to future-proof the industry. Curricula and training need to be adapted to the reality of construction sites, where the use of digital tools and equipment will continue to increase. We needed to take action to raise awareness of this issue across less developed Balkan areas, identify specific targeted initiatives and mobilize national decision-makers to support the adoption of the digital transformation process
+We attracted 2 newcomers in the E+ partnership.

<< Objectives >>

The key objective of the project was to foster digital transformation within the construction sector by developing and implementing key performance indicators (KPIs) to enhance productivity across Balkan. We aimed to address the sector's need for modernization through the adoption of digital tools and practices, facilitating a smoother transition to a more efficient and technologically advanced industry. 2 years ago, before the project started, the construction sector in Slovenia, Croatia, and North Macedonia faced significant challenges, including low levels of digital maturity, fragmented approaches to digital adoption, and a lack of standardized metrics for assessing digital performance. To address these shortcomings, we aimed to:
-Enhance Digital Maturity
-Develop KPIs
-Promote Digital Skills
-Facilitate & Encourage Stakeholder Collaboration
Its overarching goal was to create a sustainable and scalable framework for digital innovation in the construction industry, ultimately contributing to increased competitiveness and productivity at both national and EU levels.
It also sought to capitalise on the strengths of two new project partners, HGK and ECNM.The introduction of these to the E+ programme aimed to build their capacity.

<< Implementation >>

Phase 1:
1.1 IPM Meeting in Skopje: KOM
1.2 Comparative Analysis: Assessment of the current state of the construction sector.
1.3 KPI Development: Creation of a KPI matrix for construction contractors with input from consortium partners and external experts.
1.4 Stakeholder Engagement: Conducting interviews and roundtable discussions.
1.5 Reporting: Review of results and preparation of a phase report.
1.6 Educational KPIs: Development of KPI tables for secondary vocational schools.
Phase 2: 
2.1 IPM Meeting in Zagreb
2.2 Project Specification: Detailed project specification for the DIG-IN-KPI digital tool.
2.3 Tool Development: Creation and translation of the online self-assessment tool for digital maturity.
2.4 Stakeholder Collaboration: Ongoing collaboration with target groups across three countries.
2.5 Data Collection: Invitation to construction companies to use the tool and provide data.
2.6 Pilot Testing: Conducting control interviews and testing the alpha version of the tool.
2.7 Data Analysis: Analysis of results and interpretation by an external contractor.
2.8 Reporting: Review of results and preparation of a phase report.
Phase 3: 
3.1 Final IPM in Gornja Radgona
3.2 Promotion
3.3 Evaluation
3.4 Recommendations

<< Results >>

The DIG-IN-KPI project achieved several significant outcomes:
R1: KPI table for construction companies- contractors
R2: KPI table for educational institutions
R3: Report on the work - phase 1 of the project
R4: Web application to assess the digital maturity of companies and organisations (multiple languages: EN, HR, SI, MK)
R5: Evaluation and commentary of the results obtained in the web application
R6: PUBLIC PRESENTATION OF RESULTS on 18 April 2024, MEGRA fair, Slovenia.
R7: CAMPAIGN TO DISSEMINATE THE FINDINGS AND UTILISE THE PROJECT RESULTS.
These results have not only met but in some cases exceeded our initial objectives, demonstrating the project's success in advancing digital transformation in the construction sector.

2022-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000094467.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000094467.title: Support of VET in gastronomic sector towards CO2 neutral kitchen
2022-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000094467.summary:
<< Background >>

The effects of climate change are visible around the world, and it is projected to become even more frequent and intense in the coming decades. Agricultural production and food preparation account for 26% of total global CO2 emissions in the world. Both Slovenia and Croatia have adopted their recent low-carbon growth strategies and have committed to reducing CO2 emissions and halting climate change, but there is not enough information and education regarding the possibility of reducing CO2 emissions related to the production, preparation and serving of food. Also, the general public is not very informed about the consequences of their food choices. Given the number of vocational schools related to tourism and catering (30 in Slovenia and 96 in Croatia), the number of catering businesses (about 4000 in Slovenia and 5500 in Croatia) and the attention of the wider public related to nutrition and healthy living, this project had a visible contribution to the increase of knowledge about climate change both to professionals and to the general interested public, thus contributing to the achievement of the goals of the European Green Plan - by 2050 Europe should be a climate-neutral continent.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to develop and implement VET educational program for students and teachers on climate change and CO2 emissions, to increase the knowledge of the catering/gastronomic sector and awareness of climate change, business greening opportunities and reduced CO2 emissions as well as to make the gastro sector and wider general public aware of climate change and implications for climate change and CO2 emissions resulting from the production and preparation of food and our food choices. In this way, all target groups (VET students, teachers, restaurants’ managers and the general public) were informed on the small steps that can contribute to the reduction of climate change. In particular, attention was focused on the gastronomic sector - VET education in that area, as well as business entities - restaurants, etc. who already have orientations towards zero waste practices, and who can proceed the message to the general public about the possibilities of reducing CO2 through the choice of dishes – groceries and methods of meal preparation in everyday life. 

<< Implementation >>

5 key activities were carried out through the project:
(i) The analysis of the situation in the VET related to  catering / gastronomic sector in the Republic of Croatia and Slovenia was related to the assessment of knowledge about the impact of the food preparation on climate change and CO2 emissions;
(ii)   Based on the results of the analysis the VET educational programme for students, teachers and gastronomic sector was developed and tested in Croatia and Slovenia related to climate change and green business in gastro sector in form of power point presentation, 4 short videos and Climate Cookbook;
(iii) a special group of activities that were implemented was focused on implementation of the VET educational program for students, teachers and the gastro sector as well as for general public on climate change and CO2 emissions and beyond – the circular economy and green business in the hospitality/gastro sector ; 
(iv) During the project, a group of activities related to Promotion and visibility was implemented
(v) During the project, activities related to project management were implemented.


<< Results >>

The following key results achieved during the project: 
•	Report on knowledge and skills of students, teachers in VET and gastro sector in the field of circular economy, climate change and CO2 emissions with recommendation for VET educational program on climate change and CO2 emissions in the gastronomic sector.
•	VET educational programme for students, teachers and gastronomic sector in Croatia and Slovenia related to climate change and green business in gastro sector was developed and tested.
•	Climate Cookbook was prepared – a manual on climate change and CO2 emissions in catering with examples of calculating CO2 emissions of individual dishes and examples of selected recipes with their CO2 footprint. 
•	Pilot education was conducted in LURS based on the prepared VET educational content available on-line and improved VET educational content on climate change and CO2 emissions and green business in the catering/gastronomic sector. 
•	Two educational workshops were conducted at the Film Food Festival in Zagreb and at the Days of Rogaška Slatina. 
•	In two restaurants – Sun in Rogaška Slatina in Slovenia and Lari & Penati in Zagreb in Croatia, menus were made with the calculation of CO2 emissions per each meal offered.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

hr.name: INSTITUT ZA RAZVOJ I MEDUNARODNE ODNOSE

2022-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000101066.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000101066.title: Dobro ugođena edukacija umjetničkih pedagoga
2022-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000101066.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The goal of the project Well-tuned education of art pedagogues is to modernize and raise the quality of art education  through training of pedagogues and the use of digital tools. We make art educators aware of the importance of networking and continuing education in the field of profession and digital literacy. Our mission is to preserve the inherited tradition of art education, modernize and popularize it and continuously find new quality contents for colleagues and students.

<< Implementation >>

We are going to design a digital handbook and online lectures together with partner organizations and create a new digital platform to present the handbook and lectures. Dissemination of results is achieved through the Online Summit of Art Educators. It is an ideal medium for easy and fast transfer of new knowledge to a large number of users, it is adapted to groups with fewer opportunities and does not depend on the epidemiological situation. We will translate manual and lectures into English.

<< Results >>

We will successfully educate 500 art educators about innovative teaching methods and new digital tools. 200 art pedagogues will apply new professional knowledge in teaching and make it attractive for students of the digital age. These art educators with new knowledge and skills will become more competitive in the European labor market.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2022-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000096197.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000096197.title: Digital capacity building for VET Trainers
2022-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000096197.summary:
<< Background >>

Economies with a skilled workforce are more resilient to economic shocks and grow faster. The EC states that a more efficient investment in training could have an impact of up to 0.4-0.6% of GDP growth and for the period 2021-2027, the EC has established for the first time the specific objective of increasing of the percentage of citizens with basic digital skills, from 56% in 2019 to 70% in 2025. The project partners operating in the VET sector have identified the need to achieve a new balance between the need to renew their teaching in presence and use of increasingly digitalized tools corresponding to the needs of a constantly evolving job market. The Partner Organizations, teachers and trainers therefore agree on the need to acquire and make DigCompEdu increasingly operational by promoting its reinterpretation through a participatory comparison between peers to increase their digital skills and to propose teaching approaches, methodologies and applications in modern educational environments also in order to determine an increase in the attractive value of the entire VET system.

<< Objectives >>

The Digital capacity building for VET Trainers - VET-Di.Ca.B. project - develops in the context of Digital Transformation by expanding the preparation, resilience and digital capabilities of VET teachers, trainers and operators, and intends to achieve the development of small-scale cooperation that starts from a re-reading shared and participatory of DigCompEdu” (2017). The project is contextualized in a post-pandemic relaunch phase in which on the one hand there is the need to renew and relaunch in-person training and on the other to optimize and not waste the results obtained in the pandemic period in terms of acceleration towards greater use of digitalised educational and training environments. With its implementation the project aimed to:
-Facilitate the construction of new partnerships and stimulate the peer-to-peer exchange of practices/experiences;
-Improve and strengthen the digital skills of VET trainers/teachers/operators;
-Promote a bottom-up participatory discussion on DigCompEdu for the renewal of training through the application of tools and technologies in digital environments;
-Improve the level of attractiveness of the VET system.

<< Implementation >>

The activities carried out refer to the following macro areas of activity envisaged in the WorkPlan:
1.Development of a partnership based on participatory peer-to-peer discussion and the exchange of risk management, coordination, monitoring and prevention practices.
2. Implementation of a capacity-building path composed of n3 International Lab and characterized by participatory bottom-up and relational/in-person approaches alternating with digital/virtual environments. The activity plan was aimed directly at trainers, teachers and operators of the VET system starting from the indications of DigCompEdu. The Capacity building Multi-Lab Program for Vet-Trainers path was characterized by being a process of comparison and exchange of practices, experiences and proposals developed by partners who operate with different levels of digitalisation and in different educational environments.
3. Development and definition at the end of the training course of a new common and effective structured methodological proposal contained in a Guidelines document and an attached Video-Tutorial.
4. Dissemination and transferability of results through national events and multi-modal-media communication plan.

<< Results >>

The following concrete results and outputs were achieved:
- Shared, effective and efficient management of the resources assigned by the Erasmus+ Programme.
- Facilitated dialogue and exchange of practices between Partners with the development of active transnational cooperation for the sustainability and follow-up of the Project.
- Implementation of a transnational peer-to-peer Multi-Lab Training Program for Vet-Trainers, thematic and characterized by a participatory bottom-up relational approach, by learning-by-doing methodologies, team building and coaching and by multi-disciplinary and inter-sectoral comparison alternating face-to-face activities with online meetings. The result is identified in the search for common answers and in the development of new integrative and concrete methodological proposals to encourage the growth of the digitalisation of the VET system and enhance educational work in the presence of trainers and teachers.
- Concrete results are the development of OER materials: methodological guidelines and practical video tutorials.
- Creation of workshops for the dissemination of results and to multiply the impact and follow-up of the project.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2022-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000097423.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000097423.title: Resilienza attiva contro il cambiamento climatico attraverso modello di serra mobile
2022-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000097423.summary:
<< Background >>

A prototype of a mobile greenhouse had already been designed by the students of the ITT Majorana in Milazzo: this innovative project, however, had suffered a setback from Covid-19, leaving the children with a sense of unfinished. This project met several needs:
1) allowed the students to restart an exceptional idea, give them the cultural/scientific tools to improve it and thus plan its exploitation in the long term;
2) allowed the Istituto Majorana in Milazzo to better enter the Erasmus programme, with the primary intention of improving the fundamental scientific tools to make young people competitive in the world of work;
3) allowed the Croatian agricultural institute, which also presented itself new to E+ KA210 VET, to learn about a more innovative type of mobile greenhouse than the traditional one used so far in the school grounds by the Applied Agriculture Department and its Agricultural Machinery Development Department;
4) has introduced green subjects closely linked to climate change into the curriculum of pupils, bringing them in step with global needs, creating students who are not only more useful to the labour market but increasingly aware of these issues.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to increase the level of innovation of the training provided by the professors of the institutes involved in the project. the Maiorana Institute in Milazzo, Italy and the Sumrska Skola, in Croatia.
The parallel objective was to increase the competitive advantage of the students of the institutes involved in the world of work. Everything was developed with a view to resilience to climate change.


<< Implementation >>

The project has included the implementation of the following activities:
A01 - Research and scientific framework (Logical Framework);
A02 - Training teachers: Training course in Cyprus for teachers and training for students;
A03 - Construction of mobile greenhouses in Italy and Croatia;
A04 - Piloting: installation of mobile greenhouses and pilot phase in Italy and Croatia;
A05 - Dissemination of project results.

<< Results >>

The concrete results obtained were:
- Desk research;
Logical Framework in available in 4 languages;
- Scientific dialogue between the two institutes (report);
- Two mobile greenhouse prototypes.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-2-SI01-KA210-VET-000095764.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2022-2-SI01-KA210-VET-000095764.title: S SODELOVANJEM DO NOVEGA UČNEGA MODULA ZA KOMPETENTNO IZVAJANJE POMOČI NA DOMU
2022-2-SI01-KA210-VET-000095764.summary:
<< Background >>

The European Union is facing an aging society, where an increasing number of elderly residents will require home care assistance. Consequently, more institutions are providing home care services with personnel of varying levels of training. In the labor market, those who perform home care often possess informal education (through various courses, etc.) and are frequently insufficiently trained.
In Slovenia, secondary schools offer a three-year educational program for Nursing Assistants. This program equips students with skills for delivering quality healthcare services at home but does not cover home assistance tasks, as this need did not exist when the program was originally developed. Traditionally, graduates of this program were employed in healthcare facilities and nursing homes. However, there has been a recent surge in demand for personnel trained to provide home care assistance.

In response, two schools, in collaboration with DEOS (which monitors labor market needs), have developed an updated learning module and a teacher’s guide. As educational institutions in the field of healthcare, the schools recognize their social responsibility to address societal needs. hey strive to improve the quality of life for the elderly.

<< Objectives >>

Enhancement of the learning module for secondary vocational education within the Nursing Assistant program, titled Home Economics, along with the publication of a teacher’s guide for teaching basic and advanced content related to the Home Economics module.
Alignment of education with labor market needs, addressing the growing demand for personnel trained to assist the elderly at home due to an aging society and the deinstitutionalization of care.
Improvement of competencies for students with fewer opportunities, equipping them to adequately prepare for employment, gain international experience, and boost their self-confidence and skills.
Exchange of experiences with a partner school in Croatia (SŠ Čakovec) and create a teacher’s guide.
Integration of modern pedagogical approaches and digital competencies for teachers and students, accompanied by the development of a teacher’s guide with teaching guidelines.
Collaboration with DEOS, an organization providing elderly care, to gain insights into practical needs for home assistance and ensure the high-quality implementation of the module.
Development of teaching materials, including educational videos, a teacher’s guide, and presentations on nutrition for the elderly.
Dissemination.

<< Implementation >>

Analysis of educational content, labor market needs, and legislation in Slovenia and Croatia.
Observation of best practices in the delivery of home care assistance.
Conducting surveys for students on their prior knowledge of home care assistance.
Selection and testing of educational content during the 2023/2024 school year at SGLŠ Postojna, SŠ Čakovec, and in the field in collaboration with DEOS.
Designing a teacher’s guide with guidelines for teaching the Home Economics module.
Translation of the guide into Croatian and English, followed by a review process.
Conducting workshops with nutritionists for teaching staff and students on healthy nutrition and meal preparation.
Organizing student exchanges between SGLŠ Postojna and SŠ Čakovec (twice).
Student attendance in classes in the partner country and evaluation of the educational content.
Regular partner meetings (in-person and via Zoom) – 8 times.
Communication among partners and management of project documentation.
Publication of the teacher’s guide on the EPALE platform, social media, by e-mail  and school websites.
Recording and publishing 5 educational videos on YouTube.
Organization of an international event on October 11, 2024.

<< Results >>

Teacher’s Guide for implementing the Home Economics module in Slovenian, Croatian, and English.
Report on the needs of the Slovenian labor market in the field of elderly care.
Review of existing legislation in Slovenia concerning deinstitutionalization and home care assistance.
Report on the needs for providing home care assistance.
Analysis of the survey conducted among students from Slovenia and Croatia.
Final survey showing the usefulness of the Home Economics subject.
Report about knowledge transfer and student practice at DEOS.
Workshop for students on elderly nutrition.
Reports on eight partnership meetings.
Reports on two student mobility exchanges.
CANVA workshop conducted with students.
Programs for education and training in the fields of nursing, elderly care, and home care assistance.
Presentation: Nutritional guidelines for elderly people, presented in Slovenian and Croatian.
Educational videos on preparing meals for the elderly and providing home care assistance (5 videos).
Procurement of equipment for Home Economics classrooms at both schools.
Creation of promotional materials and a leaflet to disseminate project results via email and the EPALE platform
Implementation of an international event to disseminate project
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2023-1-FR01-KA210-VET-000165553.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-FR01-KA210-VET-000165553.title: Réhabilitation Aéronautique
2023-1-FR01-KA210-VET-000165553.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to strengthen European cooperation within our institution and provide our students and teachers with a framework for practicing technical English, essential for communication and documentation in the aeronautical field. The project also aimed to promote European technological exchanges by bringing together schools with complementary skills to develop practical and collaborative activities.

We encouraged communication between partners, notably through a transnational meeting in Zagreb, which helped clarify the host school’s needs and allocate tasks according to each institution’s skills and equipment. The first meeting in Seville strengthened cohesion and teamwork among students and teachers, with these connections maintained throughout the project via mobilities and digital exchanges.

In practice, Colomiers manufactured the structural elements, Seville produced the control wheels and mechanical components, and Zagreb carried out the final assembly. The fabrication and assembly of the parts were successfully completed. Students were assessed using a competency grid, earning a bonus for their exam, and their work was highlighted during the final presentation event in Zagreb

<< Objectives >>

Strengthen transnational cooperation between partner schools by promoting the exchange of methods, skills, and best practices in the aeronautical field.

Develop the technical skills of students and teachers, particularly in the fabrication, assembly, and maintenance of aircraft components, while using technical English as the professional language of communication.

Enhance the attractiveness and quality of vocational training by providing students with the opportunity to work on a concrete and rewarding project, and by demonstrating the role of European collaboration in skills development.

Ensure effective coordination and task allocation among partners to guarantee the successful execution of fabrication, assembly, and testing activities on the Morava L200 aircraft.

Produce concrete and lasting results, such as the fabrication, assembly, and complete documentation (plans and assembly manuals), which can serve as educational and technical references for future students.

Promote the project and the skills developed through communication events involving local partners and industry professionals.

<< Implementation >>

Within the framework of this project, several activities were implemented to promote European cooperation and the development of technical skills among students and teachers. Transnational meetings, notably in Zagreb, allowed the clarification of the host school’s needs and the allocation of tasks among partners, while ensuring follow-up and coordination through digital exchanges.

The mobilities to Seville, Colomiers, and Zagreb enabled students to work hands-on on the fabrication, assembly, and maintenance of the Morava L200 aircraft components, validate technical solutions, and document processes. Each school contributed according to its expertise: Colomiers for structural elements, Seville for control wheels and mechanical components, and Zagreb for the final assembly and painting. Students were assessed using a competency grid, earning a bonus for their exam.

Finally, a final event in Zagreb allowed the presentation of the achievements, demonstrated the functioning of the aircraft’s flight control system, and highlighted the collaborative work to partners and the public.

<< Results >>

The concrete achievements of this project include the fabrication, assembly, and maintenance of parts for the Morava L200 aircraft by students from the three partner schools. Colomiers produced the structural elements, Seville manufactured the control wheels and mechanical components, and Zagreb handled the final assembly, adjustments, and painting. Students also prepared plans, assembly manuals, and technical procedures, ensuring the reproducibility and sustainability of the skills acquired. The mobilities allowed for the validation of technical solutions, experimentation with assembly and maintenance methods, and the strengthening of cooperation between partners.

Among the other results, students developed their technical English skills, facilitating professional communication and documentation. They were assessed using a competency grid, earning a bonus for their exam. The final event in Zagreb provided an opportunity to present the achievements, demonstrate the functioning of the aircraft’s flight control system, and showcase the skills and collaborative work to partners, professionals, and the public.

2023-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000156124.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000156124.title: Green people - Green working skills
2023-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000156124.summary:
<< Background >>

We have applied for the ABOUT GREEN project to educate teachers on the techniques of building miniature self-sustaining houses using recycled or ecological materials, and on the application of renewable energy sources and new technologies in installations. The project aims to adapt vocational education to the needs of the labor market, teach green skills and facilitate the transition to a climate-neutral economy. The exchange of knowledge between partner organizations and the development of a digital platform will enable teachers to acquire new skills and competences.

The project addresses environmental and economic challenges, including climate change, greenhouse gas emissions, poverty, disruption of the natural balance and changes in the environment. The project also responds to the need for environmental awareness and education on biological and ecological topics. Croatia has a high rate of youth unemployment, and the mismatch of educational programs with labor market needs increases the risk of educational failure. The project aims to help the local community, especially after the earthquake in Sisak-Moslavina County, by building miniature sustainable houses that are environmentally friendly and cheaper. 

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the ABOUT GREEN project, we wanted to achieve several key goals. First, to create a manual that brings together the knowledge of partner organizations and establish a digital platform for online courses on sustainable construction, the use of recycled materials and renewable energy sources. The goal is to educate teachers, students, small and medium-sized enterprises and the general public about green construction and renewable energy sources. The project seeks to improve teachers' knowledge of ecology, sustainable construction and the use of recycled materials, and to support teachers in acquiring new skills. By creating a digital platform, access to knowledge will be made available to all interested parties. The manual will be adapted and translated into the languages ​​of the partner organizations, including English. International cooperation between Croatian and Dutch teachers will enable the exchange of knowledge and experience, and the development of innovative approaches to teaching students. The project will result in training staff to teach sustainable construction and the use of renewable energy sources, and increasing the possibility of participating in larger and more complex projects.

<< Implementation >>

The activities carried out in the ABOUT GREEN project included several key steps. First, the consolidation of existing knowledge among partners through continuous communication and meetings. The first meeting of the partners was held in Croatia, where green architecture topics were discussed and a digital manual was created. Students created a model of a tiny house, workshops and a photo exhibition were held. The second meeting was held in the Netherlands, where the partners focused on creating a digital manual and workshops on green roofs and bio-glue. They visited TU Delft and Green Village, where Croatian students prepared a quiz on green architecture. The creation of a digital platform and an online course was a key activity. The partners worked together on the creation of the platform by sending materials and communicating via video meetings and emails. The third meeting of the partners was held in Croatia with the aim of eliminating difficulties and doubts, and several workshops were also held. The last activity included testing the digital platform and the online course among target groups, with a high percentage of passing the final exam. These activities enabled the acquisition of new knowledge and skills.

<< Results >>

Concrete results of the ABOUT GREEN project include teachers’ understanding and application of green architecture principles. Quantitatively, 24 teachers from Croatia and the Netherlands completed a 15-month training course on sustainable building techniques. Seven workshops were held on topics such as green roof construction, green materials, energy-efficient building, heat pumps, energy plantations and bio-glue production. A model of a sustainable tiny house was created, and 87% of participants reported an improved ability to integrate green design into their teaching. Qualitatively, participants agreed that the theoretical concepts came to life in the prototype, which increased their awareness of the accessibility of sustainable building. Teachers jointly developed a digital platform and a manual with interdisciplinary lesson plans, which they later piloted in their schools. A Dutch school piloted the use of a tiny house model as a teaching aid, which generated high student engagement and cross-curricular learning. By combining theoretical learning with practical practice and peer collaboration, the project directly improved the capabilities of educators in green architecture.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2023-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000158700.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000158700.title: EcoVentures: Nurturing Student Innovations in Green Business
2023-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000158700.summary:
<< Background >>

In our application for this project, we were motivated by the urgent need to take action in response to climate change, biodiversity loss, and the overconsumption of natural resources, as highlighted in the SOER 2021 report by the European Environment Agency. Existing educational systems, particularly within the Vocational Education and Training (VET) sector, often fail to adequately and appropriately address these and similar challenges due to the prevailing economic perspective of the labour market. Within this context, we identified the need to establish an educational programme focused on sustainability, one that fosters the development of ecological and socially responsible skills. The objective of the project was to develop educational modules based on Project-Based Learning (PBL) to equip students with practical and innovative entrepreneurial skills aligned with the principles of sustainable development. In doing so, we aimed to contribute to the development of the green economy, encourage international cooperation, and empower learners to become entrepreneurial while being mindful of the social and environmental impact of their actions.

<< Objectives >>

Through the implementation of this project, we aimed to enhance the capacities of vocational education by developing an innovative module based on PBL.The goal was to empower both learners and educators—not only in applying the PBL methodology but also in fostering a sustainable learning environment.The project sought to equip students with the ability to develop business ideas that address the ecological,social, and economic dimensions of sustainability.The project aimed to strengthen awareness of individual and collective responsibility towards the environment, promote social inclusion, and prepare learners for the demands of green and sustainable entrepreneurship.Given that the vocational education sector often lags behind in addressing social and environmental priorities due to the dominant economic perspective of the labour market, our objective was to integrate Sustainable Entrepreneurship Education into the regular teaching process.The project activities were focused on developing a contemporary educational approach through which sustainability-related content was implemented into educational institutions.By doing so, the project supported the development of green and environment responsible entrepreneurship. 

<< Implementation >>

The implementation of the project encompassed a series of carefully planned activities aimed at achieving the defined project objectives. In the initial phase, a kick-off meeting was organised to establish collaborative relationships and define the activity plan and timeline for the realisation of project results.One of the key activities was the implementation of the LTTA, during which participants acquired knowledge and skills in the field of Project-Based Learning  and the integration of sustainable entrepreneurship into the educational context. A comprehensive training programme was developed, consisting of four thematic modules on sustainable entrepreneurship, intended for teachers, lecturers, and mentors in the field of vocational education and training VET.As part of the project, a TPM was also held at the partner organisation in Türkiye. Additionally, a digital booklet was created, showcasing best practices in sustainable and socially responsible business from the partner countries and other EU member states.In the final phase of the project, a pilot implementation of the training programme was carried out in educational institutions, which provided valuable insights and feedback for its further improvement. 

<< Results >>

The project resulted in the development of an innovative educational module titled "Sustainable Entrepreneurship Education" (Result-1), specifically tailored for use in vocational schools, as well as a digital booklet of best practices in sustainable entrepreneurship across Europe (Result-2). Through the project, participants enhanced their knowledge and awareness of the ecological, social, and economic dimensions of sustainable development. Teachers were empowered to implement the Project-Based Learning approach. As part of the project, an LTT activity was carried out, during which participants acquired knowledge and skills focused on project-based learning and the integration of entrepreneurship development programmes into educational institutions.
The educational programmes were piloted as planned and subsequently evaluated to ensure their alignment with real-world needs. The evaluation conducted among both teachers and students demonstrated the module’s positive impact and provided a solid foundation for its future implementation and further development. The project contributed to the education of environmentally conscious young entrepreneurs and supported the objectives of the European Green Deal.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2023-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000167244.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000167244.title: The Ugly side of Beauty
2023-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000167244.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we recognized the urgent need to address the environmental challenges posed by the beauty and skincare industries, which continued to generate significant waste despite increasing global and EU efforts toward sustainability. This project provided us with an opportunity to focus on education, skill development, and raising awareness about sustainable practices within the sector. The beauty industry requires a shift toward more sustainable practices, such as reducing waste, adopting renewable ingredients, and using eco-friendly packaging. Our goal was to promote these practices and encourage responsible consumer behavior among future generations of users, ie VET students and their teachers. There was a clear need to equip teachers, mentors, and students in VET with the skills necessary to support the green transition. Through this project, we aimed to enhance educational quality and foster a workforce well-versed in sustainability. Also, with the project we strengthening the cooperation between educational institutions and businesses that is essential for aligning VET programs with labor market needs.  

<< Objectives >>

One of the project's core objectives was to raise awareness about the life cycle and environmental impacts of personal care products. We sought to learn from businesses that have integrated green models into their operations, addressing not only packaging but also waste management protocols and eco-friendly ingredients. This knowledge was intended to be transferable to future students and apprentices in beauty and cosmetic occupations. Also, we aimed to strengthen VET mentors in the beauty sector by focusing on sustainability and green skills strategies. Teaching young people about environmental responsibility from an early age fosters a sense of stewardship for the planet.Key EU policies, such as the Green Deal and the EU Skills Agenda, highlight the importance of education in promoting environmental sustainability. By implementing this project, we sought to achieve several objectives: raise awareness (Increase understanding of the environmental impacts of cosmetics), reduce waste (Influence practices that lead to less waste generation in the beauty sector), empower educators (equip VET mentors with knowledge and strategies for sustainability).  

<< Implementation >>

There were 4 project activities: A1. Job Shadowing – Environmental Sustainability in VET; A2. Multiplier Workshops; A3. Training Programme - Sustainable Business Practice; A4. Green Booklet. The project also included management and dissemination activities. In A1, 6 representatives from partner organizations participated, gaining insights into the French VET system for beauty and cosmetic occupations and programs. The focus was on content related to ecology and environmental issues,specifically how these topics are approached through VET,curriculum design, and school activities. A2 involved the organization of 2 workshops to transfer knowledge from A1 to other VET mentor teachers involved in apprenticeships. Each workshop included at least 6 craftsmen/mentors.A3 focused on training where 6 mentors were introduced to sustainable business solutions from the Occitanie region, including ecological-oriented businesses, green marketing, packaging, products and ingredients in haircare and skincare products, as well as waste management in the beauty and cosmetic industry. The final activity, A4, was a summary of the project results in the form of a booklet that covered terminology related to environmental sustainability for VET schools. 

<< Results >>

Each project activity resulted with measurable and tangible outcomes and results:
A1. 1 job shadowing programme; 6 participants’ individual reports; 1 short comparative analyses about vocational education
in France and Croatia
A2. 2 multiplier workshops programme, 1 recommendations and conclusions document
A3. 1 “Sustainable business practice” training programme attended, 6 Certificates of attendance in training programme
A4. 1 green booklet
-5 partner meetings.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business
