2023-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000165007.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000165007.title: Coalizione per le competenze nei mercati contadini
2023-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000165007.summary:
<< Background >>

The proposal comes from an analysis conducted in 2022 by the World Farmers Markets Coalition, in collaboration with the "Udruga Hrvatskih Tržnica" and "Xarxa de Consum Solidari" associations, which focus on global food systems. This analysis highlighted the need to promote more sustainable production models, such as farmers' markets. The project aims to make the sector more competitive by bridging the digital divide that is still widespread in agriculture, facilitating access to qualified training designed to be accessible in both delivery and content, specifically regarding farmers' markets.

This initiative addresses the need to build a culture of sharing and continuous improvement—essential elements for tackling modern agricultural challenges. In this context, the promotion of the Erasmus+ program has become a key tool for generating these opportunities. Additionally, it has been an opportunity to create partnerships among local, national, and international stakeholders for exchanging knowledge, resources, and best practices aimed at enhancing the competitiveness and sustainability of businesses. These alliances are crucial for participating in community projects that support the agricultural sector.

<< Objectives >>

The project primarily aimed to strengthen the role of farmers' markets as key tools for a more sustainable food distribution system, in line with the European Green Deal and the Farm to Fork strategy. The central objective was to reduce the digital divide among farmers by providing them with essential skills and tools for digital farming, which are crucial for innovation and sustainability in the sector. This was achieved through the development of an asynchronous platform and the creation of a suite of professional training materials.
Both the platform and the content were co-designed with the collaboration of 12 market operators and 6 farmers. This ensured that the platform's functionalities effectively addressed the needs expressed by industry stakeholders. Additionally, using the aforementioned tools, the project aimed to enhance the competitiveness and resilience of the agricultural production system. An important focus was also on promoting awareness of the Erasmus+ program and the opportunities it offers.

<< Implementation >>

The project's activities were carried out through three actions focused on specific objectives.
Activity 1, "Co-design and activation of the asynchronous platform," led to the development of AcademyOnline, designed to provide an accessible training experience. This activity involved 12 market operators and 6 farmers.
Activity 2, "Creation and sharing of content," resulted in the co-design of a suite of asynchronous educational materials, translated into the languages of the partners, for a professional training program for farmers and market operators. Additionally, this activity promoted the Erasmus+ program through the organization of three events and targeted communications. The content was co-designed by the same working group from Activity 1.
Activity 3, "Testing and promotion," involved the launch of the final platform, its promotion, and the dissemination of the project. In this activity, promotional materials were created, digital content was shared on the partners' channels, and three in-person meetings were held in Italy, Spain, and Croatia to present the project and its results, along with three organized online meetings.

<< Results >>

Throughout the project, the expected results were achieved at every stage. In Phase 1, a co-design process for the platform (Academy Online) took place, involving 18 beneficiaries. There was a needs and context analysis conducted, with 158 questionnaires collected to assess skills and willingness to use technology. An e-learning platform was created, along with a user guide translated into the various languages of the partners. Additionally, 18 interviews were conducted, yielding testimonials (16 written and 2 video).
In Phase 2, training content was developed, including a welcome section made up of 3 materials, 8 training modules containing 10 subtitled videos, 8 PowerPoint presentations, 4 translated best practice videos, and 5 organized meetings. Technical evaluations were also conducted, along with 3 Erasmus Days events, 2 articles, 14 posts, 3 beneficiary testimonials, and 1 Erasmus+ PowerPoint presentation.
In Phase 3, the platform was launched, along with 3 dissemination events, a promotional materials kit, 20 social media posts, and a dedicated project page on the WFMC website, plus 3 organized online meetings.

2023-1-RS01-KA210-VET-000165590.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-RS01-KA210-VET-000165590.title: Primena IKT alata u nastavi preduzetništva
2023-1-RS01-KA210-VET-000165590.summary:
<< Background >>

Our school educates students who attend the subject Entrepreneurship in the final grade. Еxisting textbooks are often too demanding and do not contain enough ICT tools that would make it easier for students to acquire knowledge. That is how the idea came about to participate in a project with schools from European Union countries that actively use modern digital tools in teaching. Our students, members of the entrepreneurial section, are already participating in competitions in the field of entrepreneurship, which further encouraged the need for an innovative approach. The students showed great interest in the application of ICT tools and the availability of teaching materials in electronic form, which was the first sign that we should think about the project. Through its implementation, students will improve their digital competences and achieve better results, while teachers will apply modern teaching methods. The school is already involved in three Erasmus+ projects and has a motivated teaching staff, ready for innovation. The project will also benefit the local community, as schools in the area will be able to use the teaching materials and experiences gained during the project implementation. 

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project Application of ICT tools in entrepreneurship education is to improve the digital competences of teachers and students, acquire new knowledge and skills in the application of ICT tools in entrepreneurship education, as well as prepare for the modern labor market. Improving digital competences and using ICT tools would contribute to strengthening the formal and informal education of students. Teachers would improve their methodological and didactic skills and modernize teaching by applying modern technologies in entrepreneurship education and other subjects. The benefit of the project is also intercultural learning of students and the development of skills that contribute to better coping in a new and unfamiliar environment. Teachers would implement the acquired knowledge in teaching and learning plans. The implementation of the project will have a positive impact on the overall work of the school, strengthen the network of international contacts and partnerships, and the project results and teaching materials will be included in the school's education strategy. The benefits of the project will also be felt by the local community, surrounding schools, as well as the students' parents.

<< Implementation >>

The project planned and implemented six activities: Preparatory visits - project management in Slavonski Brod and Smederevo, Project implementation in Slavonski Brod and Smederevo, Project implementation - creation of teaching materials and Promotional activities - dissemination of the project. During the preparatory visits to both schools, the project participants got acquainted with the working methods of the partner school, the profiles they educate, agreed on the dynamics of the project implementation and defined tasks for all participants. During the 3rd and 4th activities, 4 students and 3 teachers each visited Slavonski Brod and Smederevo, got acquainted with the work of the school, attended classes in Entrepreneurship, Politics and Economy and other subjects, where ICT tools were applied in teaching, and got acquainted with the cultural and historical sights of the city. In the 5th activity, the teaching material Guide to Entrepreneurship was developed in Serbian and Croatian. The project was disseminated by teachers from both partner schools in schools in the city and surrounding areas, at the Teachers' Council, Professional Councils, and Professional Meetings.   

<< Results >>

The project yielded excellent results. Teaching was improved by using ICT tools, new teaching materials and modern methods in teaching entrepreneurship. Students improved their digital and professional competences, acquired new knowledge and skills, as well as the ability to create a personal CV and portfolio, which improved their position in the labor market. Teachers developed digital, communicational, ethical and entrepreneurial competences, as well as awareness of the importance of applying modern technologies and teaching methods used in the EU. New teaching units were included in the curricula. Positive evaluation results confirmed the success of the activity. The teaching material Guide to Entrepreneurship was well received by colleagues, with the remark that they will use it in teaching. One of the important outcomes is the increased interest of teachers in participating in Erasmus+ projects and applying new methods in teaching. After the presentations, several colleagues from elementary schools requested support in developing projects, which contributes to the expansion of the Erasmus+ program.

2023-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000156692.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000156692.title: KARIERNA SOBA POBEGA V PRIHODNOST - POKLICI PRIHODNOSTI IN KOMPETENCE PRIHODNOSTI
2023-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000156692.summary:
<< Background >>

Understanding trends, current challenges, and opportunities for career development, along with the simultaneous development of digital skills and future competencies, is crucial for effectively planning the education of both young people and adults. According to leading global experts, most of the professions in which young people will work in the future do not yet exist, and more than 40% of existing occupations will need to adapt over the next ten years. At the same time, it is also important to understand that certain professions are slowly disappearing due to technological advancement. All of this requires a more tailored approach in the field of career guidance. Career advisors or guidance professionals (especially in schools) often struggle to keep up with developments in technology and the fast-paced changes due to their heavy workloads. However, they are aware that staying up to date is essential for providing high-quality career guidance. Young people and their parents must also be equipped with this knowledge and understanding. To raise awareness and strengthen the educational potential thru engaging gamification and interactivity, this is what the digitalized mobile career escape room "into the future" is. 

<< Objectives >>

The goal is to introduce digitalization into existing career guidance through the use of an escape room. Within the project, we aimed to create a digitalized and mobile Career Escape Room into the Future, thereby encouraging interest in various career opportunities and promoting social inclusion in an innovative and motivating way. The escape room is intended for career orientation and is designed as an inclusive and stimulating innovative learning environment, also suitable for people with lower possibilities and opportunities l. It supports the development of key competencies for the professions of today and the future.

<< Implementation >>

- The partners exchanged experiences and analyzed the market in the fields of career orientation, future professions and 
  competencies, the use of technology in career guidance, and escape rooms.
- We developed the conceptual and content framework, created the application, and digitalized the pilot version of the mobile 
   Escape Room into the Future.
-  Career counselors were trained to implement the escape room.
-  We tested the pilot setup, carried out pilot sessions, and conducted evaluations for both the primary and secondary target 
   groups.
-  We ensured the promotion and dissemination of the KARPO project.


<< Results >>

 - The partners exchanged experiences and established long-term international cooperation, which will serve as a foundation for developing new approaches in career guidance.
-  Partners were trained in the latest methods of using escape rooms in career guidance.
-  Introduction of digitalization into career guidance.
-  Pilot implementation of a mobile digitalized escape room in both Slovenian and Croatian leanguage. 
-  Career counselors acquired new knowledge and tools, while other target groups gained access to innovative career guidance using new methods.
-  The booklet Career Escape Room into the Future was published in Slovenian, Croatian and English language.

2023-2-DK01-KA210-VET-000174643.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-2-DK01-KA210-VET-000174643.title: Structured Program for Enhancing Employability by Developing Future Ready Skills
2023-2-DK01-KA210-VET-000174643.summary:
<< Background >>

The SPEED project was driven by several key needs:
1.	Enhancing Employability: We created a digital training platform (GEMS-mATP) to help VET students develop transversal skills, improving their job prospects.
2.	Addressing Skills Mismatch: We aimed to bridge the gap between VET courses and employer needs by focusing on skills like innovation management, design thinking, and emotional intelligence.
3.	Supporting VET Teachers: We empowered VET teachers with digital tools and techniques, enhancing their readiness and resilience in using gamification for teaching.
4.	Responding to Economic Challenges: We addressed the decline in youth employment due to the pandemic and the Ukraine war, which led to job switching and limited opportunities.
5.	Sustained Use and Dissemination: We ensured the results were shared among VET schools for sustained use beyond the funded cycle.
These needs were identified through feedback from VET teachers and a brainstorming workshop with various stakeholders, highlighting the urgency to enhance VET education’s relevance to job market needs.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to empower VET teachers by providing them with digital tools and techniques through an innovative microAPPs training platform (mATP). This platform helped them develop their digital readiness and resilience, especially in using gamification methods for teaching.

For VET students, we created edutainment-based, visually rich content to boost their cognitive skills and innovative thinking. This content was designed to help them generate new ideas and approaches, making them more employable in their chosen fields and building their competence for cross-sector employability.

We also focused on sharing the project’s results with VET schools to ensure that the benefits would continue to be used and exploited even after the funding period ended.

<< Implementation >>

In the SPEED project, we carried out several key activities:
1.	Kick-Off Meeting: We started with a meeting in Croatia, where all the partners came together to set things up, clarify procedures, and make sure we all agreed on our goals.
2.	Developing GEMS-mATP: We created the Global Employability Master Skills microAPPs Training Platform, featuring 48 microAPPs in English, Croatian, German, and Danish. This platform focuses on essential skills like Innovation management, Design Thinking, Emotional Intelligence ,Global cultural effectiveness, Concentration and Focus, Negotiation and Conflict Resolution
3.	Dissemination Conference: in Denmark, we presented our results, including the GEMS-mATP, and facilitated networking and discussions on best practices and future collaborations.
4.	Final Meeting: In Denmark, we reviewed our progress, finalized the project results, and discussed how to sustain the project’s impact beyond its funding period and by integrating the feedback from VET stakeholders who participated in the conference.
5.	Project Management: Throughout the project, we made sure everything was coordinated well, quality was assured, and tasks were completed on time. all tasks were implemented as per proposed budget

<< Results >>

Global Employability Master Skills microAPPs Training Platform (GEMS-mATP): Developed a digital training platform with 48 microAPPs in English, Croatian, Danish, and German. These microAPPs covered key skills such as innovation management, design thinking, emotional intelligence, global cultural effectiveness, concentration and focus, and negotiation and conflict resolution. The GEMS-mATP is available as an Open Educational Resource and is compliant with GDPR gudelines as it does not capture any personal data of the VET students/trainees. The multilingual versions of the GEMS-mATP can be accessed on the project website: https://www.speed-erasmusproject.eu/
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2023-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000170056.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000170056.title: Reciklaža u praksi: novi kurikulum za voditelje reciklažnih dvorišta
2023-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000170056.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address specific labour market needs in the field of waste management, particularly in light of the increasing number of recycling yards in Croatia and Serbia and the corresponding shortage of qualified personnel to manage them. In both countries, there is no formally recognized qualification for recycling yard managers, which poses a barrier to employment and sectoral development. We identified the need to develop a non-formal education programme that would enable individuals with secondary education to acquire the relevant knowledge and skills. At the same time, the project responds to the need to strengthen the institutional capacities of organizations engaged in adult education and vocational training, as well as the growing demand for digitalization of learning processes. Our aim was to create a curriculum based on ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) principles, accompanied by modern digital tools to facilitate flexible distance learning. This approach seeks to enhance the employability of VET learners and improve the overall quality of vocational education and training in the field of sustainable waste management.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project, our aim was to contribute to the enhancement of vocational education and training in the field of waste management, with a particular focus on Croatia and Serbia, which represents the overall objective. We recognized the need to train personnel qualified to work in recycling yards and therefore set a specific objective to develop a high-quality, practice-oriented educational curriculum for the training of individuals in recycling yard management. In addition to the curriculum itself, we sought to ensure a modern and flexible approach to learning by developing digital tools that enable distance learning, thereby making the content more accessible to a wider group of users. Furthermore, the project aimed to strengthen the capacities of both the participating and external organizations by empowering professionals in vocational education and promoting the importance of sustainable waste management. In doing so, we strived to ensure the long-term sustainability of project outcomes and achieve a broader impact on society and the environment.

<< Implementation >>

We successfully implemented a series of key activities. We began with an initial meeting that brought together all partners to establish a detailed activity plan and clearly define project objectives. This was followed by the development of a curriculum for recycling yard management, during which we created educational content tailored to the needs of the labour market. The first transnational mobility meeting was held, enabling the exchange of experiences and ideas with international partners. We introduced digital learning tools for the curriculum, thereby increasing the accessibility of educational materials and facilitating a modern, flexible approach to learning. A training session was organized for VET professionals, aimed at enhancing their competencies. The second transnational mobility meeting further strengthened collaboration among partners and provided an opportunity to evaluate progress made. A practical training module was conducted for a test group of learners, equipping them with the hands-on skills and experience required for successful labour market integration. Through dissemination and promotional activities, we informed the broader public

<< Results >>

Through the implementation of the project, we achieved tangible results and significant outputs. An innovative curriculum was developed, aimed at non-formal training of participants for the effective management of recycling yard operations. The curriculum was designed in accordance with labour market needs, providing practical competencies required for employment or self-employment in the recycling sector. To facilitate access to educational content, accompanying digital tools were created to enable online learning and flexible use of materials. This significantly improved the accessibility of non-formal education, particularly for participants in remote or underserved areas. The number of vocational education and training (VET) professionals was notably increased, both within partner organizations and beyond, through additional training and exchange of experiences throughout the project. Furthermore, the continuous collaboration among representatives of the three partner organizations strengthened their mutual partnership, enhanced cooperation, and laid a solid foundation for future joint projects and initiatives in the field of sustainability and waste management.

2023-2-SE01-KA210-VET-000181128.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-2-SE01-KA210-VET-000181128.title: Empowering Micro Destinations for Sustainable Tourism
2023-2-SE01-KA210-VET-000181128.summary:
<< Background >>

Micro destination development is closely related to the fields of destination development through who is involved, but in the processes it's closer to placemaking. Micro destinations, which are smaller and less well-known destinations, often have unique cultural, natural, and historical assets that can attract visitors. These attractions are not limited to sites, and can include intangible assets such as traditional festivals, local cuisine, biodiversity, indigenous knowledge, heritage sites, and storytelling. These assets can be used to develop sustainable tourism strategies that preserve local identity and heritage while ensuring economic benefits for local communities. However, these destinations are also vulnerable to the negative impacts of tourism, such as hyper-seasonality, swings between over- and under-tourism, environmental degradation, and cultural commodification. Additionally, regions and municipalities struggle when it comes to streamlining methods for managing the developing clusters of micro destinations and retaining competence on micro destination development. With this project we wanted to find solutions and methods to work actively with these challenges and special needs.  

<< Objectives >>

The general objective of the project was to contribuite to the development of knowledge sharing and capacity building among tourism stakeholders across Europe. Specific objectives were:
- promote the implementation of sustainable tourism strategies in micro destinations that benefit both visitors and local communities.
- increase the understanding and skills related to sustainable micro-destination development for policy makers and planners. These skills include cross disciplinary understanding of the impacts on sustainable tourism in the micro destination as a whole from decision and policies made in its parts.
- increase the awareness of community based approaches for placemaking and micro destination development, an area where the knowledge and research from academia seldom meets reality.


<< Implementation >>

Two main activities were implemented in the project: Collection of good practices for sustainable
micro destination development and a seminar called "Sustainable and responsible tourism: promoting microdestinations". The first activity focused on benchmarking best practices across four countries in the EU for the sustainable development of established and emerging micro destinations and collect the good practices identified that are most suitable for transferability in a handbook that includes guidelines and methods. The Croatian Kvarner Region led the collection of good practices supported by the Expert partner Svedest on how to collect good practices and producing templates for the complete collection. Halland region, SIA Liepaja and Kvarner Region held local workshops with key stakeholders to identify good practices to present. SERN held a local workshop with the assisting partner Municipality of Borgotaro, Italy. The workshop formats was digital or physical, depending on the destination's situation. The second activity was a 3-day transnational Seminar organized in Sweden by the project coordinator with the support of the Swedish partner SveDest and focused on the empowerment of tourism micro-destinations.  

<< Results >>

The project produced 3 concrete outputs:
1. A framework of good practices for the sustainable development of established and emerging micro destinations that includes guidelines and methods that can be applied by regions and municipalities to develop and manage micro destinations in a more sustainable and resilient way. The format of this output is a handbook containing examples and best practice from different destinations in Europe. 
2. Increased awareness and adoption of sustainable tourism practices among tourism stakeholders, including tourism organisations, community members, municipalities, local government, and other public partners. Thanks to the project we managed to put the finger on challanges many micro destinations face. This in turn resulted in possible working methods for sustainable and resilient micro destinations that benefit both the sustainable growth of local communities and responsible visitors.
3. Thanks to the project we strengthened the networks and partnerships between tourism stakeholders across Europe, enabling them to learn from each other and share good practices. This will in turn strengthen the capacity of regions and municipalities to develop sustainable and resilient tourism micro-destinations.

2023-2-SI01-KA210-VET-000176584.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-2-SI01-KA210-VET-000176584.title: WaterWise
2023-2-SI01-KA210-VET-000176584.summary:
<< Background >>

In Slovenia and Croatia many irrigation systems used in agriculture are still outdated and manually operated, which leads to inefficient use of water and energy. At the same time, VET mechatronics programmes offer only limited opportunities for students and teachers to work with real smart-irrigation technologies, data-driven control and sustainability topics in an integrated way. Both partner schools identified a need for a modern, practice-oriented curriculum and teaching tools that connect mechatronics, automation, digitalisation and environmental protection, and that can be embedded into regular vocational programmes. We therefore applied for this project to design and pilot a modular training programme and a smart irrigation system prototype, in order to upgrade the competences of teachers for teaching specialised technical subjects and to improve students’ technical and green skills. The project also addresses the need to strengthen long-term cross-border cooperation between TŠC Maribor and Pomorsko-tehnička škola Dubrovnik in the field of sustainable irrigation and quality assurance in VET.

<< Objectives >>

Our main objective was to modernise vocational education in the field of mechatronics and related technical programmes by using the topic of smart irrigation as a concrete, real-life context. We wanted to develop and test a modular training programme and practical teaching materials that integrate automation, sensors, programming and sustainable water management, and can be used directly in regular lessons. At the same time we aimed to improve teachers’ competences for planning and delivering interdisciplinary, project-based learning, and to give students more hands-on experience with designing, building and testing a real smart irrigation system. Another important objective was to strengthen long-term cross-border cooperation between TŠC Maribor and Pomorsko-tehnička škola Dubrovnik, so that teachers and students can exchange good practice, jointly develop materials and create a basis for further cooperation in green and digital transition in VET. 

<< Implementation >>

During the project we organised three transnational project meetings (start, mid-term, final) to plan work, agree on the curriculum, monitor progress, review finances and close the project. We implemented two training activities: the first LTT in Dubrovnik focused on theory and curriculum development, where students and teachers learned about smart irrigation and automation, analysed existing practice and co-designed the modular training programme; the second LTT in Maribor focused on piloting, where mixed groups of teachers and students programmed and tested the prototype and workstations, visited a university and institute and reflected on how to integrate results into regular VET programmes. Within PR1–PR4 we designed the modular curriculum and carried out the needs analysis (PR1), developed and built the prototype and workstations (PR2), created the project website and web application with quizzes and open access to materials (PR3), and prepared the e-textbook, lesson plans, worksheets and assessment tools (PR4). We also organised a multiplier event in each country and other dissemination activities. Project management ensured coordination, quality assurance and reporting. 

<< Results >>

The project produced several concrete outputs and changes in practice. We prepared a joint needs analysis for Slovenia and Croatia and, on this basis, a modular curriculum in three languages on smart irrigation that can be integrated into VET mechatronics and related programmes. We designed and built a functional smart irrigation prototype and 16 training workstations that allow students to work with sensors, controllers and data in a realistic setting. We developed an e-textbook, detailed lesson plans, student worksheets and assessment tools to support project-based learning around the prototype. We also created a project website and web application to navigate the prototype, access quizzes and provide open access to all materials, so that other schools can easily use and adapt them. Through the LTT activities and joint work on PR1–PR4, teachers improved their competences in interdisciplinary, practice-oriented teaching, while students gained technical, digital and green skills and valuable experience of international teamwork. The project strengthened long-term cooperation between the partner schools and laid the foundations for future joint initiatives.

2023-2-TR01-KA210-VET-000174451.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2023-2-TR01-KA210-VET-000174451.title: YAPAY ZEKA İLE DESTEKLENEN GÜNEŞ ENERJİ SİSTEMLERİNİN KURULUMU BAKIMI , TAMİRİ VE DEPOLAMA SİSTEMLERİNE YÖNELİK EĞİTİM DOKÜMANLARININ HAZIRLANMASI VE ENERJİ VERİMLİLİĞİNİN ARTIRILMASI
2023-2-TR01-KA210-VET-000174451.summary:
<< Background >>

Within the scope of this project, the need for up-to-date, practice-oriented, and accessible vocational training materials in the field of AI-supported Solar Power Plants (SPP) was addressed. It was identified that there was a lack of high-quality digital content and standardized training resources for technical personnel, students, trainers, and entrepreneurs working in the renewable energy, electrical-electronics, and information technology sectors.
To address this need, e-modules, training videos, and virtual learning materials were developed and made accessible to the target groups. In addition, awareness of digitalization, environmental sustainability, and energy efficiency was increased. The project also contributed to the objectives of the European Green Deal and supported the employability of the target groups by strengthening their vocational knowledge, practical skills, and access to innovative learning resources.

<< Objectives >>

Within the scope of this project, up-to-date, accessible, and practice-oriented vocational training content was developed in the field of AI-supported Solar Power Plants (SPP). In this context, e-modules, training videos, and digital learning materials were prepared for technical personnel, students, trainers, and entrepreneurs, thereby facilitating access to relevant and up-to-date knowledge.

In addition, digitalization was supported, awareness of environmental sustainability and energy efficiency was increased, and contributions were made to the objectives of the European Green Deal. The employability of the target groups was also supported by strengthening their vocational knowledge and competencies. Furthermore, knowledge and experience sharing and cooperation among the partner countries were strengthened, inter-institutional interaction was enhanced, and the institutional capacities of the participating organizations were improved through the project.

<< Implementation >>

Within the scope of our project, complementary activities were implemented to achieve the defined objectives. First, a Management and Monitoring Team was established to ensure effective coordination among the project partners, and regular meetings were conducted. As part of the needs analysis, surveys were administered to the target groups, and the e-modules required by the sector were identified.

Accordingly, e-modules were developed in the field of AI-supported Solar Power Plants (SPP). To support these modules, training videos and an animated virtual prototype were created. In order to improve accessibility, multilingual and subtitled digital learning materials were also produced.

In addition, international meetings, technical visits, and institutional visits were organized to facilitate the exchange of knowledge and experience. Access to project outputs was provided through the project website and virtual platforms. Within the scope of dissemination activities, seminars were organized, and press releases and promotional materials were prepared. Finally, the project results were evaluated, and a sustainability plan was developed to support the continued use and dissemination of the project outputs.

<< Results >>

As a result of the project, concrete digital learning materials were developed in the field of AI-supported Solar Power Plants (SPP), including e-modules, training videos, and an animated virtual prototype tailored to the needs of the target groups. These materials were prepared in multiple languages with subtitles and made accessible to a broad audience.
In addition, a project website and virtual platforms were established to facilitate access to the project outputs. Dissemination materials, including posters, brochures, press releases, and promotional videos, were also prepared. Through seminars and meetings, the project results were presented to the target groups, thereby increasing awareness and supporting the dissemination of the developed outputs.
Furthermore, the project increased awareness of digitalization, environmental sustainability, and energy efficiency, while contributing to the improvement of vocational education quality and facilitating access to relevant knowledge and learning resources. Cooperation among the project partners was strengthened, the institutional capacities of the participating organizations were enhanced, and the project contributed to the objectives of the European Green Deal.

2024-1-AT01-KA210-VET-000250045.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-AT01-KA210-VET-000250045.title: Interlace: Art and Action in Contemporary Dance Education
2024-1-AT01-KA210-VET-000250045.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Dance educators disseminating creative dance in diverse communities play a crucial role in developing said communities. This is why it’s imperative that the educators develop their skills whilst understanding the critical value of inclusivity. We provide dance educators with an opportunity to learn how to make their approach inclusive. These approaches concern all pedagogical methods and tools that aim to make students feel acknowledged, empowered, situated in their physical and creative bodies.

<< Implementation >>

MARC will engage 3 dance educators in a peer-to-peer exchange; they will be teaching a community group, reflecting on their experience, and disseminating their observations nationally. Multimedia Hut will provide young dance educators with a modular program focused on developing skills for working with community groups. Wiener Tanzwochen will include MARC and Multimedia Hut in developing parts of the program of their symposium geared towards dance educators that work with community groups.

<< Results >>

Dance educators are expected to have more inclusive methods and tools available when teaching creative dance to diverse local community groups. They have a fine grasp of the non-verbal strengths of dance for inclusivity. They gain more competence in creating situations for self-directed learning processes with diverse groups. They know better how to address the needs of diverse student groups. An online resource offers open access to principles and guidelines of inclusive dance teaching.

2024-1-DE02-KA210-VET-000246364.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-DE02-KA210-VET-000246364.title: Navigating ESG Regulations: A Guide for SMEs
2024-1-DE02-KA210-VET-000246364.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and management-related CVET providers (including trainers and consultants) in understanding and responding to the growing complexity of EU corporate sustainability regulations, particularly the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and related ESG frameworks.

Many SMEs lack the capacity, resources, and accessible tools to navigate the emerging and constantly evolving sustainability-related regulatory landscape. At the same time, trainers and consultants often require up-to-date content and practical methodologies to effectively support these businesses. The ESG-REG project addressed these gaps through its activities and outputs.

The project also aimed to strengthen the institutional capacity of the partner organizations by facilitating knowledge and expertise exchange between more experienced partners and newcomers - both in terms of transnational project management and the thematic area of corporate sustainability regulations.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the ESG-REG project was to raise awareness and build capacity among SMEs, trainers, and consultants in the field of sustainability reporting and ESG compliance. We aimed to simplify complex EU corporate sustainability regulations and provide practical guidance through the development of the ESG-REG Guide and complementary training activities.

Specifically, we aimed to:

- Support SMEs in understanding and applying ESG and CSRD-related requirements in their operations;
- Equip CVET providers, trainers, and consultants with tools and content to integrate ESG topics into their services;
- Strengthen the skills of project partners in training content development and design, stakeholder engagement, and transnational collaboration;
- Foster collaboration and knowledge exchange across sectors and countries to promote sustainable business transformation.

<< Implementation >>

The project was structured around three core activities.

First, partners worked on project management, communication, and outreach, ensuring coordinated implementation and visibility through internal tools, a project website, and social media. Through ESG-REG Spark Sessions, the target audience was regularly engaged throughout the project to discuss ESG-related topics.

Second, the consortium developed the ESG-REG Guide by researching and simplifying EU corporate sustainability regulations. This process included joint working sessions, content curation, and a testing phase involving external stakeholders. Based on feedback, a summary version of the Guide was also created and translated into partner languages.

Finally, the ESG-REG Education Series offered practical training events in each partner country. These sessions supported knowledge transfer by demonstrating how ESG principles and the Guide can be applied in real business contexts. Interactive and collaborative formats were used across all activities.

<< Results >>

The project delivered several key outputs:

- ESG-REG Spark Sessions, which shared regular updates and project insights with stakeholders.
- ESG-REG Guide, a user-friendly resource simplifying complex ESG and CSRD-related regulations, including VSME, EU Taxonomy, EUDR, CSDDD, CBAM, and EUFLR.
- ESG-REG Guide Summaries in English, German, and Croatian for quick reference.
- The ESG-REG Education Series in all partner countries which supported practical application of the Guide and summaries
- Additionally, internal outputs included a Communication & Dissemination Plan, a Code of Conduct, and a methodology for organizing stakeholder engagement activities.

2024-1-DE02-KA210-VET-000248929.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-DE02-KA210-VET-000248929.title: FIGHTing Youth Unemployment through Digital Skills and Interactive Education
2024-1-DE02-KA210-VET-000248929.summary:
<< Background >>

Unemployed and NEET young people face persistent challenges entering the labour market, often due to a mismatch between their skills and employers’ needs. VET programmes in many European countries still lack sufficient focus on digital and entrepreneurial competences demanded by the modern economy. Our organisations recognised these shared challenges among the participating countries that includes: limited digital readiness of VET educators, lack of innovative educational materials, and weak links between training and the labour market. The project was designed to bridge this gap by developing a curriculum and interactive online courses focused on virtual assistance, self-employment, and digital entrepreneurship. Through this initiative, we aimed to enhance the employability of unemployed youth, strengthen educators’ capacity, and support the adaptation of VET systems to the realities of the digital labour market. For this reason, the project involved three main target groups: partner organisations (VET providers), VET educators and unemployed/NEET citizens from our local communities.

<< Objectives >>

The project objectives were following:

1. Raise capacities of partners for empowering unemployed young people’s employability and entrepreneurial skills, through active participation in development of new educational materials, and through organising local level training courses for VET educators of partners.

2. Develop a comprehensive curriculum for educators and VET providers for enhancing entrepreneurial and selfemployment skills of unemployed young people; containing plan of learning for educators and workshops for organizing trainings.

3.Raise knowledge and skills of 45 VET educators for using the educational curriculum to empower unemployed young people’s employability and entrepreneurial skills; through 3 local trainings organised in each of the participating countries.

4. Develop 2 interactive gamified online learning courses for unemployed young people, empowering their employability and entrepreneurial skills and their knowledge and skills for work as virtual assistants and finding entry level jobs in the field.

5. Present project outputs to wider audience of VET educators and VET providers in local communities of partners, and ensure further use of the educational materials; through 3 local multiplier conferences

<< Implementation >>

The project consisted of six main activities implemented collaboratively by partners from Germany, Croatia and Estonia. It began with a Content Development Partners’ Meeting in Berlin, where roles, timelines and quality assurance mechanisms were defined. Pannonia Consulting led the creation of a comprehensive curriculum for VET educators on virtual assistance and entrepreneurship. Each partner then organised local five-day training courses for 45 educators in total, testing and refining the curriculum. Learning Library developed two interactive online learning courses, “Empowering My Entrepreneurial and Self-Employment Skills” and “Virtual Assistant Work as an Unemployment Solution”, that are accessible in four languages. Finally, three local multiplier conferences were held to present results, gather feedback and foster future cooperation. All activities were implemented according to plan and managed to achieve all set KPIs, ensuring strong transnational collaboration and wide dissemination.

<< Results >>

The project produced several tangible and sustainable results. A comprehensive 10-day curriculum for VET educators on virtual assistance, entrepreneurship and self-employment was developed and published in four languages. Forty-five VET educators from Germany, Croatia and Estonia were later trained to apply the new curriculum in their daily work activities within VET institutions.  Two interactive online learning courses were created: “Empowering My Entrepreneurial and Self-Employment Skills” and “Virtual Assistant Work as an Unemployment Solution”. Those are providing practical, gamified learning for over 200 unemployed young people. Each partner hosted a local multiplier conference, presenting results to educators, policymakers and youth. The project also strengthened partners’ capacities for digital education, improved cross-border cooperation in the VET sector, and promoted digital readiness, inclusion and employability across partner communities.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000244845.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000244845.title: Tkanje, Ekologija, Poučavanje, Inkluzija, Harmonija
2024-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000244845.summary:
<< Background >>

Both project partners, through their long-term work with people with intellectual disabilities and mental illnesses (PIDMI), have noticed the need for their training in simple vocational occupations adapted to their educational abilities. PIDMI have very few opportunities for education, finding employment and equal participation in society. Further education programs for them are almost non-existent, especially in small communities. We recognized weaving on a loom as a professional skill that our beneficiaries can master, which will increase their level of socialization, get the opportunity to work in a safe environment and acquire the necessary skills for independence, staying in the family and avoiding institutionalization. The beneficiaries should be more satisfied, more confident in themselves and strengthen their self-esteem and increase their chances of employment in the labor market. In this way, we contributed to the reduction of emotional and psychological problems that occur when they are not occupied with work tasks appropriate to their abilities. At the same time, they will be less dependent on their family and more prepared for some form of independent life when there are no longer any parents to take care of them.

<< Objectives >>

The overall goal of the project was to increase the employment opportunities of people with intellectual disabilities and mental illnesses (PIDMI) by increasing their social inclusion. We achieved everything we wanted:
•	To enable PIDMI to acquire new skills and knowledge in order to feel useful, more satisfied and less aggressive
•	To educate trainers to be qualified to educate PIDMI and work with them in order to increase their competitiveness in the labor market, and by introducing volunteers to the project to increase their visibility and motivation to get involved in the work of associations
•	To raise awareness of the public and the local community about the needs and opportunities of PIDMI, present them to potential employers, show the results of their work and thus make the public aware that PIDMI can be part of a contributing community, not just a burden and expense
•	To ensure that employees increase their competences for working with PIDMI, associations expand the scope of services, improve occupational therapy and achieve transnational cooperation
•	To take care of environmental protection and recycling in order to show that unique products can be created from recycled materials, while preserving traditional crafts


<< Implementation >>

Important project activities were training trainers to work with PIDMI on a loom and educating PIDMI to work on a loom.Through these activities we enabled people who didn't know or had little knowledge about weaving to learn to weave and through contact with PIDMI we connected with them, learned how to encourage them to work and work more independently.The connection was also achieved through joint participation in actions to collect old clothes,thereby protecting the environment and emphasizing the importance of recycling, socializing during the trainer's practice where we worked on preparation for weaving,preparation of the loom and all auxiliary tasks necessary for weaving.The training participants participated in the creation of a digital manual and video tutorials that provide an innovative approach to teaching PIDMI.In addition to these activities, we carried out project management activities, dissemination and public events that were important for the sustainability of the project, connecting and cooperating with partners and promoting the results and goals of the project.Weaving looms necessary for work were acquired, and public awareness of PIDMI's possibilities was raised by organizing exhibitions and round tables.

<< Results >>

Through the project,we established cooperation with two vocational schools that participated in the preparation of an informal training program for trainers, developed a training program for OMIT, acquired 2 large looms and 12 smaller table looms, educated 8 trainers in carpet weaving and working with OMIT on these jobs, together with 12 OMITs organized a total of 16 workshops at which 20 carpets for exhibitions and another 20 test carpets were woven, conducted 6 public actions to collect old clothes,held 2 round tables with employers, vocational schools, municipalities and city institutions, held 2 exhibitions of woven carpets, created 1 promotional brochure for the project, created 1 digital manual in Easy Language and 11 video tutorials on weaving jobs. Other results are:acquired over 350 kg of old clothes ,12 partner meetings organized, a poster about the project created, a Facebook page for the project opened, a digital manual for weaving jobs created, an introductory and final conference for the project organized,3 TV reports about the project recorded and published,2 radio shows, 1 radio announcement, 4 articles published in newspapers and 6 on portals, a total of 10 users occasionally participated in workshops with OMIT.

2024-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000251356.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000251356.title: Integrated Action for Building VET Curricula and Training Opportunities in Croatia & Portugal for Digital and Green Transformation in the Footwear Sector
2024-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000251356.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project because the Croatian footwear sector was facing a clear need to strengthen its VET offer in response to the green and digital transition. Croatian footwear companies increasingly need workers, technicians, managers and future professionals with practical skills related to sustainable materials, circular economy, waste reduction, digital design, prototyping, and Industry 4.0 solutions. At the same time, Croatia lacked a structured, flexible and sector-specific VET offer for footwear, especially one that could quickly respond to the needs of companies and support both upskilling/reskilling of employees and the attraction of young people to the sector.
The project addressed the need for stronger cooperation between education providers, business representatives and sectoral experts at transnational level. By bringing together HUP, the Faculty of Textile Technology and CTCP, the project connected Croatian labour-market needs with Portuguese expertise in footwear innovation, sustainability, digitalisation and VET. The project was therefore designed to develop agile, ready-to-use curricula and training opportunities that support modern, labour-market-oriented and innovative VET response for the footwear sector.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we wanted to contribute to the modernisation of vocational education and training for the footwear sector in Croatia and Portugal, with a specific focus on the green and digital transition. The main objective was to develop innovative, flexible and ready-to-use short-term curricula that could respond to the real training needs of footwear companies and support the upskilling and reskilling of workers, technicians, managers and future professionals.
We also aimed to strengthen the competences of teachers, trainers and in-company tutors by providing them with new knowledge, methods and tools related to sustainability, circular economy, digital design, digitalisation and other emerging sectoral topics. Another important objective was to improve cooperation between VET providers, higher education, business organisations and companies, by linking Croatian needs with the advanced Portuguese experience in footwear innovation and training.
Overall, the project aimed to build the capacity of the partner organisations to offer more agile, labour-market-oriented VET solutions and to create a stronger transnational partnership capable of supporting the long-term green and digital transformation of footwear sector.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through four main groups of activities. First, we implemented project management, coordination and quality assurance activities, including the establishment of cooperation procedures, regular communication, coordination meetings, monitoring of progress, reporting and quality control. These activities ensured transparent and effective cooperation between HUP, the Faculty of Textile Technology and CTCP.
Second, we implemented activities related to the development of innovative and agile curricula for the green and digital transition in the footwear sector. This included analysis of training needs, exchange of expertise between Croatian and Portuguese partners, review of relevant green and digital topics, and the development and adjustment of ready-to-use curriculum.
Third, we implemented training activities for trainers, teachers and tutors, focused on strengthening their capacities to deliver new contents and apply more modern training methods and tools.
Finally, we implemented piloting and dissemination activities, including workshops and communication activities aimed at testing the relevance of the developed solutions, presenting the project results, and promoting their future use by VET providers.

<< Results >>

The project produced several concrete outputs. The most important one is the short-term curriculum for the green and digital transition in the footwear sector. It was developed as a practical and flexible VET resource, and it was translated into English, Croatian and Portuguese. We also developed a manual for trainers, teachers and in-company tutors, also available in three languages.
In addition, we carried out a survey among footwear companies and relevant stakeholders and analysed the results in order to better understand training needs and compare them with the experience of the Portuguese footwear sector. The project also produced supporting documents and materials, including quality and management documents, evaluation materials, dissemination materials, reports, the project website and the Shoepro Knowledge Hub, where the main results and useful learning resources are available in one place.
Other important results came from the implementation process itself. These included the learning visit and activities in Portugal, the collaborative work of the three partners, training activities for trainers and teachers, validation and piloting workshops, stakeholder feedback and dissemination events.

2024-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000245142.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000245142.title: AURALIZE – Innovative Course in Room Acoustics and Auralization for Sound Professionals
2024-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000245142.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The main objective of AURALIZE is to provide innovative vocational training in room acoustics and auralization to a wide array of attendees studying or working in disciplines such as architecture, theatre, music, sound engineering, acoustics and applied acoustics, media technology, computer science, web industry, and other immersive technologies. The project will contribute to the innovation of sonic quality and sonic thinking in our digital future and current quality of communication.

<< Implementation >>

Within the project, we will develop and implement an innovative vocational training course in room acoustics and auralization for audio professionals and students, which will improve their knowledge and skills in management of acoustic and sound digitalization. 2024-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000255839.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000255839.title: SCREEN
2024-1-IT01-KA210-VET-000255839.summary:
<< Background >>

SCREEN was applied for in order to respond to concrete skills needs in the cinema and audiovisual sector, especially among professionals, technicians, trainers and small creative organisations working in contexts where learning is often informal, fragmented and not sufficiently recognised. The partnership identified a need for more structured VET pathways able to connect technical film competences, digital transformation, green awareness and community-oriented approaches. 
The project also addressed the gap between industry practices and training provision, supporting professionals who need to update their competences in response to changing technologies, production methods and labour market expectations. 
SCREEN therefore focused on upskilling and reskilling cinema professionals, strengthening the link between VET providers and audiovisual companies, and testing flexible learning models that could valorise previous experience, non-formal learning and emerging professional profiles in the cinema sector. 
These needs were fully aligned with the project priorities on adapting VET to labour market needs, increasing the attractiveness of VET, digital skills and green skills.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of SCREEN was to improve the skills and competences of professionals and organisations in the cinema and audiovisual sector through a VET-based, modular and transnational approach. The project aimed to design an integrated training model for cinema professionals, combining upskilling and reskilling pathways and addressing technical, digital, green and transversal competences. 
A further objective was to support the standardisation and transparency of learning outcomes in a sector where many competences are acquired through practice, work experience and non-formal learning. SCREEN also intended to strengthen cooperation between VET actors, film companies and creative professionals in Italy, Croatia and North Macedonia, creating a small but concrete European learning hub for cinema VET. 
The project finally aimed to test training activities with sector professionals, collect feedback from participants and stakeholders, and prepare conditions for future use of the curriculum, including possible links with micro-credentials, mobility pathways and further professional training initiatives.

<< Implementation >>

The partnership implemented a set of connected activities covering curriculum design, training delivery, impact assessment, management and communication. First, partners worked on the SCREEN COMP curriculum, identifying key competences for cinema professionals and structuring modular learning units connected to technical, digital and green skills. Training materials, syllabi, exercises and learning resources were prepared to support upskilling and reskilling pathways. Secondly, the partners organised and delivered pilot training experiences addressed to cinema and audiovisual professionals, using flexible and blended approaches and collecting feedback from participants. The project also developed work on validation and recognition of learning outcomes, with attention to EQF-based approaches, non-formal and informal learning, and the possible use of micro-credentials. Management activities ensured coordination, partner meetings, monitoring and reporting. Communication activities included online dissemination, social media updates, events, workshops and audiovisual materials aimed at sharing the project experience with professionals, VET actors and wider creative communities.

<< Results >>

SCREEN produced a set of concrete outputs and results for the cinema and audiovisual VET sector. The main output was a modular curriculum for cinema industry professionals, structured around competence units and connected to upskilling and reskilling needs. The project also produced training materials, syllabi, exercises and reference learning resources to support delivery and future reuse by partners. 
Pilot training activities allowed professionals, trainers and creative workers to test the proposed learning paths and to provide feedback on their relevance, usability and connection with real sector needs. 
SCREEN also generated a validation-oriented framework for learning outcomes, with attention to EQF principles, recognition of non-formal and informal learning and possible micro-credential approaches. At organisational level, the project strengthened cooperation among TUCEP, 4Film and Peripetija and created a transnational basis for future initiatives in cinema VET, including further training, mobility and collaboration with stakeholders. 
Communication results included dissemination events, online promotion, audiovisual contents and increased awareness of VET opportunities for cinema professionals.

2024-1-SK01-KA210-VET-000243782.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-1-SK01-KA210-VET-000243782.title: Zelené a digitálne vzdelávanie
2024-1-SK01-KA210-VET-000243782.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was created in response to the need to modernise vocational education and adapt it to the challenges of the 21st century – digitalisation, ecological transformation and the development of key competences for sustainable development. The partners perceived that pupils had limited knowledge of the principles of the circular, shared and digital economy, lacked the link between theory and practice and lacked knowledge of how these principles affect everyday life and the future labour market. At the same time, teachers needed new methodological approaches, digital tools and opportunities for international cooperation. The project therefore responded to these needs by developing innovative curricula, materials and methodologies for the green and digital economy, which were tested in real teaching and integrated into school curricula. It focused on developing pupils’ digital, environmental, social and entrepreneurial skills, strengthened teachers’ professional competences and supported cooperation with regional partners and companies.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to innovate vocational education by integrating the principles of the green and digital economy into teaching, to develop key competences of students and to support a modern, sustainable and inclusive learning environment. The project aimed to bring students closer to the connection between economy, ecology and technology and to guide them towards responsible behaviour, creativity and the ability to apply themselves in a rapidly changing labour market.
The main objective was to create innovative curricula, materials and methodologies that would link theoretical knowledge with practice and bring the topics of circular, shared, digital and knowledge economy into teaching. The project also aimed to strengthen the digital and environmental skills of students and teachers, develop critical thinking, entrepreneurship and the ability to work in a team.
Another objective was to support cooperation between schools and regional partners, develop professional competences of teachers through international exchange of experience and increase the attractiveness of vocational education. The project was to create a model school that combines digital innovations, ecological values, and the European dimension of education.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented a series of educational, creative and dissemination activities aimed at connecting the green and digital transformation in education. At the beginning, there was an initial preparatory phase, during which we created a project team, a schedule, monitoring tools and communication channels between partners.
This was followed by work activities focused on creating and testing outputs: we developed curricula, methodologies and teaching materials for teaching the circular, shared, knowledge and digital economy. Teachers from both partner schools collaborated on the design of exercises, tests, worksheets and designs for extracurricular activities and excursions.
The project also included workshops, professional excursions and joint meetings of students, which supported their creativity, teamwork and practical skills. The outputs were tested in both countries and continuously adjusted according to feedback.
We also implemented two international meetings aimed at evaluating the progress of the project and exchanging experiences. The final phase included dissemination seminars, presentations of results, satisfaction surveys, and a final evaluation of the project's impacts on all participants.

<< Results >>

The project brought several long-term usable results that contributed to the modernization of vocational education and the improvement of the quality of teaching at both partner schools. The project created curricula and educational standards for new thematic areas - circular, shared, digital and knowledge economy. These documents were followed by teaching texts, worksheets, exercises and tests.
The teachers jointly prepared a methodological manual that offers specific suggestions for teaching, project tasks, activities for students. The outputs also include proposals for extracurricular activities and excursions, aimed at supporting environmental thinking, digital innovations and connecting teaching with practice.
In addition to tangible outputs, the project also brought significant intangible results. Students developed environmental and digital competencies, learned to work in a team, think critically and present their own ideas. Teachers acquired new pedagogical and methodological skills that they use in teaching innovation. The project became an impetus for the inclusion of green and digital economy topics in school curricula, thus gaining a permanent and sustainable character.

2024-2-EL01-KA210-VET-000265831.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-2-EL01-KA210-VET-000265831.title: Advancing Accessibility and Professional Skills for the Visually Impaired
2024-2-EL01-KA210-VET-000265831.summary:
<< Background >>

AccessPro project was developed to respond to the clear and persistent gap in vocational education and employment inclusion for visually impaired persons (VIPs). Across partner countries, we identified a common lack of practical, accessible tools to support VIPs in building digital skills and preparing for the labour market. At the same time, VET providers reported a lack of guidance and training on how to deliver inclusive instruction tailored to learners with visual impairments. Existing solutions were either too generic, inaccessible, or not adapted to real workplace contexts.

We applied for this project to collaboratively design and test a targeted response: a Toolbox and Trainer Guidelines that would be usable, accessible, and grounded in actual needs. The project aimed to support both VIP learners and trainers by creating digital, inclusive, and transferable resources. By addressing these needs, AccessPro sought to foster more equitable access to skills, employment, and lifelong learning for visually impaired persons in Europe.



<< Objectives >>

The AccessPro project set out to achieve the following specific objectives:

O1: Increase the employment opportunities for visually impaired persons (VIPs) by equipping them with essential digital skills and vocational training tailored to their needs.

O2: Strengthen the capacity of educators and trainers to deliver high-quality, inclusive vocational education to VIPs.

O3: Foster social inclusion by ensuring that VIPs have equal access to vocational education and training opportunities, enabling them to participate fully in society.

O4: Increase awareness about the challenges faced by VIPs and advocate for policies that support their inclusion in the workforce.

O5: Enhance collaboration between European partners to exchange best practices in vocational education for VIPs and promote the adoption of innovative approaches.

Through these objectives, we aimed to create real, practical change — not only by producing accessible tools, but by improving how education is delivered to VIPs, how trainers are supported, and how inclusion is understood and practiced in vocational systems across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The ''AccessPro'' project implemented seven core activities. First, we established a solid foundation through structured project management, communication, and financial oversight (A1). We then conducted transnational research (A2), including a literature review, surveys with over 100 VIPs, focus groups, and round tables with professionals. Findings informed the development of the Toolbox (A3), which includes accessible tools to support digital skills and job readiness. Each partner contributed content aligned with their expertise, and CBU ensured accessibility. We also created comprehensive Trainer Guidelines (A4) and piloted them in a 3-day Train-the-Trainer event in Greece with 10 experts. Feedback led to refinement and finalization. We then designed the AccessPro training platform (A5), user-tested with VIPs and trainers, and hosted all project materials. In A6, we delivered 12 online training sessions to 60 VIPs. Finally, dissemination (A7) included local events, newsletters, a final conference, and a long-term sustainability plan.

<< Results >>

The AccessPro project delivered three major outputs: 
(1) a comprehensive Toolbox for Employment and Digital Skill Enhancement, tailored for visually impaired persons (VIPs)
(2) a set of Trainer Guidelines for VET professionals, designed to support inclusive training practices
(3) an accessible online training platform hosting all project materials, available in multiple formats and languages. 

These resources were based on in-depth research and user feedback, ensuring their practicality and relevance. We also conducted 12 online training sessions for 60 VIPs, a 3-day Train-the-Trainer event, and multiple awareness-raising activities. The project strengthened cross-border collaboration and improved the capacity of educators to work with VIPs. Beyond tangible products, AccessPro fostered inclusion, increased awareness about accessibility in VET, and promoted the adoption of digital tools that directly improve the employability and digital readiness of visually impaired individuals.

2024-2-ES01-KA210-VET-000288697.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-2-ES01-KA210-VET-000288697.title: eLearning Architects: Designing the Future of the Labor Market
2024-2-ES01-KA210-VET-000288697.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was developed in response to the lack of specific training programmes for the emerging role of the eLearning Architect, a key profile in the growing digital education sector. Despite the strong increase in demand for online and personalised learning, there are still no standardised curricula or enough qualified educators to train these professionals.

The partner organisations identified a shared need: to strengthen their digital training capacities and provide real employability opportunities for young people and professionals in VET and non-formal education.

- Backslash aimed to equip its educators and unemployed young people with digital competences aligned with the Spanish labour market.
- Pannonia needed to strengthen its capacity to deliver advanced e-learning programmes and train new professionals in the field.
- LIBERO, in turn, sought to modernise its educational offer and improve youth employability in Serbia.

In this way, the project addressed a structural gap in the European education and training system.

<< Objectives >>

The overall objective of the ARCHILAB project was to contribute to the development of VET by enriching the labour market with qualified professionals in the field of distance education. To achieve this, the project pursued four specific objectives: (1) to develop an innovative non-formal educational programme to train future "eLearning Architects" and address an existing gap in the labour market; (2) to create and implement digital resources that improved access to the curriculum and enhanced the training process; (3) to strengthen the operational and pedagogical capacities of the partner organisations by training staff in e-learning design and development; and (4) to establish a cooperation network among educational institutions, sector partners and experts to support knowledge exchange and the continuous updating of the curriculum in line with the latest eLearning trends.

<< Implementation >>

The project was structured around 6 interconnected activities. Four coordination meetings were held (A1) — 1 virtual kick-off, 1 in-person meeting in Valencia, 1 virtual mid-term review and 1 virtual closure meeting — to plan, monitor progress, validate results and adjust implementation. In parallel, an analysis of the gap between labour market needs and VET provision in Spain, Croatia and Serbia produced national reports and a joint transnational report that informed the curriculum design. Based on this evidence, the non-formal VET curriculum "eLearning Architects" was developed (A2) and adapted into an open-access e-learning platform (A3) supporting self-directed learning in e-learning design and management. A transnational training in Serbia (A4) was then delivered to 9 professionals from the partner organisations, who later carried out local mentoring activities (A5) with 9 young people with fewer opportunities. Dissemination and sustainability (A6) ran throughout the project through workshops, final conferences, social media and sectoral events such as the European VET Digital Learning Forum.

<< Results >>

R1 - "eLearning Architects" non-formal VET curriculum: an 83-hour training pathway designed to train professionals able to design, develop and manage digital learning experiences in VET contexts, aligned with the EQF and available in English, Spanish, Croatian and Serbian. Developed on the basis of prior labour market and VET needs research in Spain, Croatia and Serbia.
R2 - "eLearning Architects" interactive learning platform: an open-access digital learning platform featuring modules, quizzes, video tutorials and an e-learning ecosystem map, available in 4 languages, supporting self-directed learning in e-learning design and management.
R3 - 9 VET professionals from the partner organisations trained in Belgrade (Serbia) and subsequently involved in local mentoring activities with 9 young people with fewer opportunities (3 per country), applying the methodology in real contexts and acting as multipliers.
R4 - Strengthened cooperation among the partner organisations and greater visibility of the project results in VET and digital learning sectoral spaces, such as the European VET Digital Learning Forum.
