2024-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000277504.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000277504.title: EcoCraft: Integrating Sustainable Food, Wine, and Environmental Practices
2024-2-HR01-KA210-VET-000277504.summary:
<< Background >>

Our schools applied for this project to respond to growing environmental, educational, and social challenges affecting our schools and local communities. Society is producing increasing amounts of organic waste, relying heavily on plastic and chemicals, and replacing traditional food production methods with unsustainable practices. At the same time, practical knowledge about fermentation, composting, natural food preservation, sustainable wine and food production, and zero-waste approaches is gradually being lost. This project was developed to strengthen the attractiveness, quality, and practical dimension of vocational education. Our schools face challenges such as decreasing student motivation, dropout risks, geographical isolation, and limited opportunities for international learning and practical experience. Through hands-on activities, workshops, and international cooperation, we aimed to strengthen students’ practical competences, environmental awareness, entrepreneurial thinking, and employability. We also wanted to address the need to preserve cultural heritage, traditional recipes, and local knowledge while promoting inclusion, intercultural learning and the exchange of sustainable practices between partner organisations.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to improve vocational education by developing practical skills in sustainable food, wine, and environmentally friendly production while promoting zero-waste principles and responsible consumption. We wanted participants to gain hands-on knowledge of sustainable practices such as fermentation, composting, bioenzyme production, ecological food preservation, sustainable wine and honey-based products, and natural packaging alternatives. Another key objective was to increase environmental awareness and encourage behavioural change by reducing food waste, plastic use, and dependency on chemicals, while promoting sustainable everyday habits in schools and local communities. The project also aimed to strengthen inclusion, intercultural cooperation, and social participation by involving participants with fewer opportunities, including students from disadvantaged backgrounds and students with disabilities. In addition, we wanted to preserve traditional recipes and local knowledge, strengthen cooperation with local producers, farmers, small businesses, and experts in sustainable practices, and exchange innovative ideas and teaching approaches between partner organisations.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented all planned activities through practical workshops, educational visits, and community activities focused on sustainability, zero-waste practices, and cultural exchange in Portugal and Croatia. In Portugal, students and teachers prepared traditional Croatian and Portuguese dishes using local ingredients during food competitions and zero-waste culinary workshops. They participated in composting activities, explored local markets and regional produce, prepared honeybread and other traditional dishes, and donated prepared meals to homeless individuals to promote inclusion and social responsibility. In Ilok, participants joined workshops on bioenzyme production from organic waste and ecological beeswax food packaging as sustainable alternatives to plastic, and as a solution for cleaning and plant treatment. In Zagreb, participants attended workshops on honey wine production, authentic and imitation honey identification, beeswax lip balm production, urban beekeeping, they visited local producers, and participated in a traditional licitar workshop. We also produced brochures, guides, posters, videos, and other materials to share sustainable practices with schools and local communities.

<< Results >>

The project produced several concrete outputs and achieved significant educational, environmental, and social results. Key outputs included workshops, practical demonstrations, brochures, leaflets, posters, recipes, and online materials focused on bioenzyme production, ecological beeswax packaging, zero-waste cooking, fermentation, and honey wine production. A project website and social media dissemination activities were also created to share results with schools and local communities.
Participants gained practical vocational skills in sustainable food production, eco-friendly agriculture, organic waste management, and sustainable culinary practices. The project successfully integrated new sustainable methods into school curricula, ensuring long-term impact on future students and teachers. Environmental results included increased awareness of plastic use, food waste, and chemical dependency in agriculture, while promoting recycling, composting, biodiversity protection, and eco-friendly production.
The project also strengthened international cooperation, inclusion, and intercultural understanding by involving students with fewer opportunities, teachers without international experience, local businesses, and community members.

2024-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000274210.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2024-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000274210.title: Green Waves: Young Entrepreneurs for Sustainable Tourism in the Mediterranean
2024-2-IT01-KA210-VET-000274210.summary:
<< Background >>

Mediterranean coastal tourism drives the economies of Italy, Greece and Croatia, but it also puts real pressure on the environment and cultural heritage of the region. Mass tourism brings overtourism, damages ecosystems, and concentrates income in a few summer months, leaving local communities exposed for the rest of the year. At the same time, young women in these three countries have strong entrepreneurial potential but limited access to targeted training, professional networks and practical tools to enter sustainable tourism as founders and change-makers. We designed Green Waves to work on both problems together: pushing the Mediterranean tourism sector toward a more responsible, diversified and deseasonalised model, and investing in young female entrepreneurship as one of the drivers of that shift.

<< Objectives >>

Green Waves set out to: (1) equip young women aged 20–30 from Italy, Greece and Croatia with the entrepreneurial and environmental skills needed to develop and launch sustainable tourism initiatives; (2) raise awareness of the Mediterranean’s natural and cultural heritage and the importance of protecting it; (3) build a transnational network of young Mediterranean women entrepreneurs committed to responsible tourism; and (4) produce training resources that are open-access and reusable beyond the consortium.

<< Implementation >>

We structured the project across five Work Packages. WP1, led by Impact Hub Rome, handled strategic, administrative and operational coordination for the whole partnership. WP2, led by Pokreni Ideju / Impact Hub Zagreb, designed and launched the open call, managed applications and selection, and prepared the learning materials. WP3, led by Eventi Nomadi, delivered the online training programme: seven sessions made up of two lectures, four co-creation workshops and a final online pitching event, plus an individual mentoring pathway for each participant. WP4, led by Impact Hub Labs, organised the two-day transnational final event held in Rome on 17–18 April 2026, bringing participants from all three countries together for project presentations and public stakeholder engagement. WP5, led by Impact Hub Rome, built the project’s visual identity and ran communication and dissemination for the full project lifecycle.

<< Results >>

Against an original target of 27 participants (9 per country), Green Waves enrolled 22 young women: 9 from Greece, 7 from Italy and 6 from Croatia. They took part in a seven-session online training programme covering sustainable tourism, business modelling, territorial marketing, storytelling and pitching. Participants produced 22 individual problem statements, Business Model Canvases and pitch decks, and a mentoring programme involving 10 experts (6 of whom acted as mentors) delivered 15 hours of tailored support. The project closed with a transnational final event at Impact Hub Rome, where the selected participants’ projects were presented to an expert panel and external tourism stakeholders. 1 project was launched in July 2026. A participant-led WhatsApp community has stayed active beyond the official project end. Dissemination activities reached thousands of stakeholders through the project lead website, blog post, social media, EPALE platform. Project materials remain openly available, while the learning approach and educational resources can be replicated. The project established a transnational network of trainers and participants that continues to foster collaboration and knowledge exchange beyond the project lifetime.

2025-1-FR01-KA210-VET-000351267.title: Global Responsibility in Eco-friendly and Ethical Nutrition & Sustainable Knowledge for Innovative Low-impact Living and Services
2025-1-FR01-KA210-VET-000351267.summary:
<< Background >>

GREEN SKILLS est né de besoins communs à deux établissements professionnels français et croate accueillant notamment des jeunes issus de territoires ruraux, disposant de peu d’opportunités de mobilité internationale. Les élèves avaient besoin de mieux comprendre comment la transition écologique transforme leurs futurs métiers, mais aussi de développer leur anglais, leurs compétences numériques et transversales, leur autonomie et leur ouverture européenne. Le partenariat réunissait deux secteurs complémentaires – chauffage, climatisation et énergies renouvelables en France, hôtellerie-restauration en Croatie – afin de confronter les pratiques professionnelles et de réfléchir ensemble aux compétences du « Green Worker of Tomorrow ». Le projet visait également à renforcer l’internationalisation des deux établissements et à valoriser la voie professionnelle auprès des jeunes, des familles et des communautés scolaires. 

<< Objectives >>

GREEN SKILLS visait à préparer les élèves aux évolutions environnementales du monde professionnel en leur permettant d’identifier et d’appliquer des pratiques plus durables dans leurs futurs métiers. Le projet devait développer leurs compétences professionnelles, linguistiques, numériques et transversales grâce à des activités collaboratives et à des situations concrètes de mobilité. Nous souhaitions également renforcer leur autonomie, leur confiance, leur capacité à coopérer et leur ouverture interculturelle, tout en rendant plus concrètes les valeurs et les opportunités offertes par l’Union européenne. Enfin, le partenariat devait favoriser l’échange de pratiques entre enseignants, renforcer la dimension européenne des deux établissements et produire des ressources pédagogiques transférables à d’autres élèves. 

<< Implementation >>

Pendant douze mois, les élèves français et croates ont alterné activités locales, coopération numérique et rencontres européennes. Après une phase de préparation et une évaluation initiale, ils ont fait connaissance sur eTwinning, créé l’identité visuelle du projet et participé aux Erasmus Days. Ils ont observé les pratiques durables dans leurs formations et en entreprise, étudié des restaurants et recettes, créé des ressources numériques et préparé les mobilités à distance. Deux mobilités, à Bergerac puis à Virovitica, ont permis de travailler en équipes transnationales sur la cuisine durable, les pratiques professionnelles écoresponsables, l’Eco-Restaurant Blueprint et les Green Worker Checklists, mais aussi de rencontrer des professionnels et de découvrir les territoires partenaires. Le projet s’est achevé par la finalisation des productions et une évaluation comparative de son impact. 

<< Results >>

GREEN SKILLS a produit des ressources pédagogiques communes, des jeux numériques, des recettes fusion franco-croates, des projets d’éco-restaurants et des « Green Worker of Tomorrow Checklists » en anglais, français et croate, désormais affichées dans les espaces de formation et réutilisables par les futurs élèves et enseignants. Le TwinSpace conserve et diffuse les productions et les étapes du projet. Les évaluations menées avant et après les mobilités montrent également des évolutions dans la communication en anglais, l’ouverture interculturelle, l’autonomie et la compréhension des green skills dans le contexte professionnel. Les mobilités ont créé des relations fortes entre les élèves et renforcé leur intérêt pour de futures expériences européennes. Le projet a enfin accru la coopération et l’internationalisation des établissements et a contribué à la création d’un nouveau partenariat Erasmus+ VET.

<< Objectives >>

The project brings together 3 VET schools to explore AI’s role in education. By working collaboratively, we aim to enhance AI and digital literacy among staff, understand both opportunities and risks, and develop ethical AI teaching strategies. Through research, teacher training, and the creation of open-access educational resources, the project ensures responsible AI integration in schools, strengthening international cooperation and digital innovation in VET.

The project will conduct AI literacy research to assess current knowledge and identify training needs. A teacher training program will equip at least 8 educators with AI skills and digital methodologies. ACTA Connect Conference, enabling dissemination, networking and long-term embedding of AI innovation in public VET system
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

2026-1-BG01-KA210-VET-000451500.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-BG01-KA210-VET-000451500.title: NEXTGEN-SKILLS: Future-Proof VET Employability
2026-1-BG01-KA210-VET-000451500.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We aim to bridge the VET-labor market gap by aligning with the 2020 Council Recommendation and Osnabrück Declaration; Facilitating systemic best practice exchange mapped to EQF/ESCO frameworks, achieving a 25% improvement in student competency scores through a metrics-based system, and providing formal validation via Validated Digital Portfolios. We prioritize institutionalizing results into permanent curricula and strengthening digital readiness with AI and data analysis tools.

<< Implementation >>

The project follows sequential phases: launch events, needs analysis, and skills mapping. Core implementation includes three transnational trainings (LTTA) in Spain (pedagogy), Croatia (soft skills), and the Netherlands (AI and digital literacy). These are followed by local pilot testing, mentorship, and a capstone real-world application event in Bulgaria. Management focuses on quality assurance and mapping outcomes to ESCO, while dissemination ensures a systemic legacy.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver EQF 3/4 and ESCO-mapped lesson plans, a VET Trainer Handbook, and Validated Digital Portfolios using secure Digital Credentials for fraud-proof skills recognition. Key outcomes include AI-optimized CVs, a 25% competency improvement, and systemic VET-industry synergy. Sustainability is ensured through school board resolutions for curriculum integration and an open-access digital legacy on Erasmus+ platforms for at least three years.

2026-1-EL01-KA210-VET-000451620.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-EL01-KA210-VET-000451620.title: Green & Digital Skills for Sustainable Hospitality Careers
2026-1-EL01-KA210-VET-000451620.summary:
<< Objectives >>

To develop and pilot two hybrid, competence-based training modules in sustainable hospitality and digital tourism services, to strengthen green, digital and transversal skills of adult learners, to validate blended learning in real VET contexts and to integrate the modules sustainably into regular training provision in Greece and Croatia.

<< Implementation >>

The project will coordinate and manage activities online, co-develop two hybrid modules (2 in-person seminars + 3 Moodle/SCORM units each), pilot them with minimum 40 adult learners in Greece and Croatia, evaluate and refine materials, develop a Trainer’s Guide, and implement structured dissemination and institutional integration actions.

<< Results >>

Two validated hybrid training modules and one practical Trainer’s Guide available in Greek , Croatian and English, improved green and digital competences of minimum 40 adult learners, tested blended learning methodology, measurable learner progressmstrengthened cooperation between VET providers and tourism stakeholders and sustainable integration of the modules into regular training offers.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

hr.name: Uciliste Ambitio ustanova za obrazovanje odraslih

2026-1-ES01-KA210-VET-000455148.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-ES01-KA210-VET-000455148.title: WORKWISE: Human Skills for Sustainable Careers
2026-1-ES01-KA210-VET-000455148.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Adapt continuing vocational training to the real needs of the labour market, complementing technical training with soft skills that are directly applicable to the productive environment.
Improve career advancement opportunities for young workers, strengthening their autonomy, leadership skills, decision-making and continuous learning.
Foster common European values in the workplace, promoting responsibility, cooperation and active participation.

<< Implementation >>

Activity 1: Development of the training manual and interactive case studies on soft skills
Activity 2: Editing of training videos
Activity 3: Project management, quality and dissemination plans

<< Results >>

WORKWISE will develop a structured training manual on soft skills, 28 interactive case studies based on real-life situations in the workplace, and 30 short training videos. All resources will be available on an open-access website and will be disseminated through multiplier events and European platforms.

2026-1-FI01-KA210-VET-000457596.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-FI01-KA210-VET-000457596.title: AI-Supported Innovation and Co-creation for VET
2026-1-FI01-KA210-VET-000457596.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to create and test a simple, transferable model that leverages artificial intelligence as a co-developer to support innovation and development in vocational education (VET) providers and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). By focusing on a human-centered and inclusive approach, the initiative seeks to address practical skill gaps and participation barriers, ensuring that AI integration enhances human decision-making, ethical awareness, and broad inclusion.

<< Implementation >>

The AICO project encompasses several key activities. Management and coordination ensure smooth operation. Model development involves two sprints: Sprint 1 includes evaluation and pilot testing over 2 days, while Sprint 2 focuses on adaptation for a second context within the same timeframe. Following development, model refinement enhances accuracy, leading to the creation of a comprehensive toolkit. Finally, dissemination and sustainability strategies will ensure long-term impact of the outcomes.

<< Results >>

The project results include:
1. AI co-developer model
•	8–12 pages
•	Process diagram
•	Implementation checklist
2. Facilitation guide
•	10-15 pages
•	3 sprint scenarios
•	Prompt templates
•	Ethical reflection template
3. SME casebook
•	Minimum 6 cases
•	2 pages each
•	Problem → Process → Result → Reflection
4. Ethical & inclusive AI framework
•	1-page principles document
•	1-page self-assessment checklist

All materials will be practical, accessible and transferable.

2026-1-FR01-KA210-VET-000450004.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-FR01-KA210-VET-000450004.title: Pouvoir d'agir de l'enseignant : Passage de la violence au vivre ensemble pour un climat favorable à l'apprentissage
2026-1-FR01-KA210-VET-000450004.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We want to support teachers by empowering them to help young people move away from violence and towards peaceful coexistence during learning time, thereby  restoring a climate conducive to work.
Our objectives must enable us to understand the mechanisms that trigger aggressive behaviour in order to combat discrimination through preventive or remedial actions, so that these attitudes do not hinder the development of our young people's skills.

<< Implementation >>

To combat aggressive behaviour that disrupts lessons and demotivates teachers and pupils, we wish to implement:

- a workshop to identify discriminatory behaviour and preventive or corrective actions to be taken
- a social utility initiative led by students, providing a space for innovation and experimentation for teachers
- training for teachers to explore and promote preventive measures to combat discrimination

<< Results >>

-Identify and understand the mechanisms that trigger aggressive behaviour.
-Combat discrimination and prevent ideological extremism through preventive action.
-Train teachers to create, explore and promote prevention measures.
-Measure the impact of experimental teaching practices on young people's behaviour towards each other and towards teachers. The results will enable teachers to restore a positive educational dynamic.

2026-1-FR01-KA210-VET-000450632.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-FR01-KA210-VET-000450632.title: Food is Not Waste: From Farm to Table – Sustainable Vocational Education for the Future
2026-1-FR01-KA210-VET-000450632.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to reduce food waste across the entire farm‑to‑table chain by strengthening VET with sustainable and climate‑responsible practices. We want to equip learners and teachers with practical skills in sustainable food management, raise awareness of the environmental and social impacts of waste, promote responsible professional behaviours and integrate sustainability into VET curricula and fostering cooperation with local and European partners.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement practical workshops, farm‑to‑table learning activities, food‑waste audits, and training sessions on sustainable food production and responsible consumption. Partners will co‑create teaching materials, run awareness campaigns, organise school exhibitions, and collaborate with local producers. Digital resources, open educational materials, and international exchanges will support the integration of sustainability and climate‑responsible practices into VET programmes.

<< Results >>

The project is expected to increase learners’ skills in sustainable food management, reduce food waste across VET institutions, and strengthen climate‑responsible behaviours. It will produce practical teaching materials, food‑waste audits, and farm‑to‑table learning activities. The project will also enhance cooperation with local producers, improve VET curricula, and raise public awareness of the environmental, social and economic impacts of food waste.

2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000453898.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000453898.title: EcoTrackers - Exploring Forest Ecosystems through Geocaching and GIS
2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000453898.summary:
<< Objectives >>

EcoTrackers is a vocational education project integrating digital tools and outdoor experiential learning to enhance students’ labour-market skills in forestry, veterinary medicine and environmental protection. Students use GPS, basic GIS and QR technologies to design interactive educational trails in protected natural areas. The project strengthens digital and green competences while promoting environmental awareness and the One Health approach, fostering teamwork and civic responsibility.

<< Implementation >>

Students and teachers will participate in workshops on GPS, basic GIS and QR technologies as preparation for field-based learning. Working in international teams, students will design, map and test an interactive educational QR trail in a protected natural area. The trail will include 10 QR learning points related to forestry, animal species and environmental features, promoting the One Health approach and labour-market skills. Evaluation, peer feedback and public dissemination will follow.

<< Results >>

EcoTrackers will result in three interactive educational QR trails, each with around 10 learning points in protected natural areas. Students will strengthen labour-market-relevant digital and green competences through practical use of GPS, basic GIS and QR technologies in real field conditions. Teachers will develop interdisciplinary and experiential teaching methods, and the project outputs will remain available for long-term use in schools and local communities, fostering sustainability.

2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000456026.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000456026.title: 3D Printing Goes Green
2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000456026.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Professional expertise in polymer recycling is to be transferred to VET teachers to bridge the gap between industrial standards and vocational education. An inclusive, trilingual Modular Handbook will be developed to provide flexible STEM learning paths for students of all capacities. Furthermore, school facilities will be transformed into a sustainable closed-loop system where plastic waste is repurposed into recycled filament for 3D printing.

<< Implementation >>

Project activities will be initiated with structured management to ensure seamless collaboration. Technical research and professional development training will be conducted to master the complexities of plastic recycling, filament production and 3D printing with upcycled materials. This will lead to collaborative development, testing and validation of a trilingual Modular Handbook. Finally, a conference and dissemination activities will be organized to share and promote results.

<< Results >>

Expected results include a validated, trilingual Modular Handbook and an operational closed-loop workshop. Teachers’ expertise in plastic recycling and filament production will be enhanced to support new classroom practices. Sustainable methods will be integrated into the regular curriculum, ensuring that students gain hands-on experience in 3D printing with recycled materials while developing environmental awareness and advanced STEM skills.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000462791.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000462791.title: Accordion Connects: Advancing Digital Transformation and Attractiveness of Vocational Music Education
2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000462791.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Accordion Connects project aims to modernise vocational accordion education, strengthen quality, innovation and European dimension in VET music education through a small-scale partnership. It will embed digital transformation and blended learning in accordion training, enhance digital and transversal competences of learners and teachers, increase the attractiveness and inclusiveness of VET pathways, and build sustainable capacity for future European cooperation.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement transnational cooperation activities including joint development of a Digital Accordion Primer containing 20 lessons co-created by Croatian and Slovakian students, peer-learning, transnational workshops, workshops with Bratislava Music academy and Accordion Orchestra Slavonski Brod, public performances and dissemination via open-access platform and professional networks.

<< Results >>

The project will result in a structured open-access Digital Accordion Primer and the integration of blended learning into regular VET practice. It will strengthen digital, pedagogical and transversal competences of learners and teachers, enhance the attractiveness and quality of vocational music education, and build sustainable institutional capacity for international cooperation, contributing to lasting impact at learner, teacher and institution levels.

2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000465975.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000465975.title: From Foundations to Future Cyber Careers in VET
2026-1-HR01-KA210-VET-000465975.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen cybersecurity education in VET by increasing teachers' competencies through train-the-trainer activites and co-creation with industry experts and empowering diverse learners through a progressive blended pathway. It seeks to increase digital competence, confidence and career awareness while developing a transferable, resource-efficient model for international cooperation.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement co-development workshops, create modular blended learning materials, provide mentored school-based implementation, organise career orientation sessions, and conclude with a transnational bootcamp. Continuous monitoring, feedback and dissemination will ensure quality, inclusion and sustainability.

<< Results >>

The project will produce tested blended cybersecurity training, strengthen teachers' capacity, increase students' confidence and career awareness, and provide publicly accessible learning materials. Participating schools will gain improved readiness for digital transformation and sustainable international cooperation.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2026-1-NO01-KA210-VET-000452064.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-NO01-KA210-VET-000452064.title: Biocircle skills: VET training for organic waste to resource transformation
2026-1-NO01-KA210-VET-000452064.summary:
<< Objectives >>

BioCircle Skills addresses the gap in VET curricula for circular bio-economy skills by developing training materials for organic waste valorisation through vermicomposting. Objectives: strengthen partner capacity in European cooperation, conduct a 3-country needs analysis, develop a 5-module VET curriculum, create accessible learning resources (videos, Resource Book, repository), validate through pilot testing with ~45 learners, and ensure dissemination to 80+ VET institutions across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

Six activities over 15 months: (1) Online kick-off with partnership agreement and quality framework. (2) 3-country needs analysis producing 50-page gap report. (3) Curriculum development: 5 VET modules, 4-5 videos, 80-100 page Teachers' Resource Book, digital repository in 4 languages. (4) 5-day training mobility in Croatia for 9 educators. (5) Pilot testing with ~45 learners across 3 countries. (6) Dissemination to 80+ institutions via Erasmus+ Platform, EPALE, webinars and partner networks.

<< Results >>

50-page Gap Analysis Report on curriculum gaps across 3 countries. 5-module VET curriculum (60 pages) at EQF Level 3-4. 4-5 demonstration videos subtitled in 4 languages. Teachers' Resource Book (80-100 pages) with lesson plans and assessments. Digital repository with 5-year hosting. 9 trained educators, ~45 pilot-tested learners with documented learning gains. Materials adapted for secondary students (15-18). All outputs CC-BY-SA licensed, reaching 80+ VET institutions and 300+ downloads.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2026-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000453619.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000453619.title: Work-Based Learning for Professional Readiness
2026-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000453619.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Our overall goal is to narrow the gap between the classroom and the job site. We would like VET students to transition from passive learning to Work Ready Professionals who are versatile and possess the soft skills demanded by modern-day employers. Through the deployment of a standardized Work-Based Learning (WBL) framework, we hope to establish a perpetual connection between VET schools and the job market. This way, every work experience will be a launching pad to a career no mere formality.

<< Implementation >>

The project has four consecutive steps, and each one increases our confidence and capability. First, we'll pinpoint the actual skills that employers are interested in. Then, we'll develop Mentor Toolkits that can be used to train companies to successfully mentor students. After that, we'll work to design a Digital Tracking Portal that students can use to view their progress in real time. Finally, we'll launch a pilot that has students working out and proving their skills in real-world settings.

<< Results >>

The main factor will be VET students entering the job market with a verified Digital Portfolios. They will have a tangible competitive advantage over others during the interview process. The project will implement the WBL Quality Framework and the Digital Tracking Portal as open-source solutions for all educational institutions to embrace. Furthermore, through the Business-VET Alliance, we want to ensure long-term relationships with companies, thereby reducing the unemployment in our regions.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2026-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000459223.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000459223.title: AI in evaluation research - opportunities, challenges, dilemmas
2026-1-PL01-KA210-VET-000459223.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims at addressing the challenge of lack of sector-specific practical guidance on the AI use in the evaluation research by developing specific knowledge on trends, needs and potentially transferable practices, and by developing commonly discussed principles (ethics) adapted to evaluation practices within three sectors: governmental (central and regional), private and social.

<< Implementation >>

The project involves three subsequent activities:
Activity 1: Mapping and collecting trends, needs, good practices, principles and standards for the use of AI in evaluation research.
Activity 2: Consolidating at the European level the trends, needs, good practices, principles and standards for the use of AI in evaluation research.
Activity 3: Disseminating the project products and results to a wider evaluation community in partner countries and among NESE members.

<< Results >>

The main project's outputs include:
1. A publication presenting collected and consolidated trends, needs, and potentially good practices for the use of AI in evaluation research.
2. Infographics presenting principles and standards for the use of AI in evaluation research.
3. Three mini-conferences combined with nine online workshops to disseminate the project's products and results to wider evaluation communities in three partner countries.
4. Evaluation research principles (ethics) at EU level.

2026-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000451192.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000451192.title: ChemPreneurs; Innovating Chemistry Education with AR/VR
2026-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000451192.summary:
<< Objectives >>

CHEVR aims to improve the professional skills of VET teachers by introducing AR/VR technologies into vocational education. The project seeks to improve teaching quality, make schools more competitive, and better connect learning with labour-market needs. By supporting teachers in using modern digital tools, the project promotes long-term innovation and helps students prepare for today’s technological workplaces.

<< Implementation >>

The project will organise teacher training workshops, partner meetings and learning activities to develop AR/VR modules for chemistry and vocational subjects. Teachers and students will create virtual simulations, test them in real classrooms and receive feedback from companies and innovation partners. Each school will also implement activities locally, followed by a final meeting to evaluate results and plan future use.

<< Results >>

CHEVR will produce validated AR/VR learning modules, teacher implementation guidelines and a transferable immersive VET model. Teachers will strengthen digital-pedagogical competences, and schools will embed innovative methodologies into curricula. Companies will confirm labour-market relevance and may use selected modules for training. The project enhances quality, safety, motivation and long-term competitiveness in VET.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2026-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000462305.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000462305.title: From Coal to Code: Understanding Digital Systems and Artificial Intelligence through Mining
2026-1-SI01-KA210-VET-000462305.summary:
<< Objectives >>

CoalToCode strengthens students’ critical digital literacy by exploring digital systems and AI through the comparison of coal mining and cryptocurrency mining. The project connects industrial heritage with contemporary digital systems, develops a practical learning scenario for vocational education and creates an educational exhibition encouraging reflection on the environmental and social impacts of digital technologies.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement several interconnected activities: a structured student reflection on digital systems and AI, development of a learning scenario for vocational education, creation of an educational exhibition comparing coal mining and cryptocurrency mining, pilot testing of the learning materials in classrooms and the museum, and dissemination activities to share the results with schools, educators and the wider public.

<< Results >>

The project will produce a transferable assessment questionnaire, learning scenario on digital systems and AI for VET education, an educational exhibition linking industrial heritage with digital technologies and an evaluation of students’ reflections. The project will strengthen critical digital literacy among students, increase teachers’ capacity to address digital systems in an interdisciplinary way and promote wider public awareness of their the social and environmental impacts.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2026-1-SK01-KA210-VET-000450328.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-SK01-KA210-VET-000450328.title: Whey pathways for clean water and  value
2026-1-SK01-KA210-VET-000450328.summary:
<< Objectives >>

1. Develop a practical WHEYWAY micro-skills package for VET and workplace learning in SK, HR and NMK.
2. Support the green transition by reducing pressure on local water systems through workable routines and documentation.
3. Build capacity of trainers and dairy SMEs to apply the tools in training and daily operations.
4. Ensure uptake beyond the partnership via a Replication Kit and exploitation pathway.

<< Implementation >>

1. Kick-off: transnational start-up meeting to align roles, methodology, quality assurance and evidence rules.
2. Baseline + co-design: needs mapping in 3 countries, then develop the package (5 modules, Trainer’s Guide, rubrics, SOPs, Decision Tool v1).
3. Validation: Train-the-Trainers, 3 workshops and 3 dairy micro-pilots to test and upgrade to Decision Tool v2.
4. Dissemination and replication: final event + 2 webinars and Replication Kit.

<< Results >>

1. Outputs: Baseline Report; validated 5-module curriculum; Trainer’s Guide; rubrics; SOP templates; Decision Tool v2; 3 pilot case studies.
2. Competences: 9-12 trainers trained and 75+ workshop participants with measurable improvement.
3. Evidence: 3 completed micro-pilots proving routines under SME constraints.
4. Uptake: 100+ stakeholders reached with documented follow-up interest.
5. Sustainability: Replication Kit and reusable formats for continued use.

hr.name: Sveučilište Josipa Jurja Strossmayera u Osijeku

2026-1-TR01-KA210-VET-000459905.action_type: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training
2026-1-TR01-KA210-VET-000459905.title: Connected CNC & Maintenance – OT-Safe Routine Packs for VET Workshops
2026-1-TR01-KA210-VET-000459905.summary:
<< Objectives >>

SAFE-STEM equips VET workshop teachers and learners with practical OT (Operational Technology) safety competences for connected manufacturing. Three VET schools from Turkiye, Croatia and Italy bridge the gap between increasing machine connectivity in workshops and the lack of structured safety training. The project develops cross-disciplinary resources combining mechanical, electrical-electronic and digital perspectives on OT risks, making STEM-VET more attractive and industry-relevant.

<< Implementation >>

Six activities over 18 months: project coordination with newcomer mentoring; risk mapping through workshop observations and a meeting in Bursa; co-development of 8-10 OT-Safe Routine Packs with cross-partner peer review; pilot testing with minimum 60 learners in three countries and a revision meeting in Osijek; design of a low-cost Mini-Lab Blueprint; and dissemination through stakeholder sessions, a webinar, a final meeting in Potenza and publication on Erasmus+ platforms.

<< Results >>

8-10 OT-Safe Routine Packs as open educational resources in four languages, containing risk scenarios, correct procedures, STEM-coded checklists and teacher guides. A Teacher Application Model for integrating OT safety across CNC, electrical and ICT disciplines. A replicable Mini-Lab Blueprint with setup cost below 2,000 EUR. A Pilot Evaluation Report with evidence from three countries. A curriculum integration roadmap. All published on the Erasmus+ Results Platform, EPALE and eTwinning.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-1-ES02-KA210-YOU-000031103.title: NGO Village
2021-1-ES02-KA210-YOU-000031103.summary:
<< Background >>

La transformación digital ha llegado en los últimos años a cada sector de la economía. Las ONGs, como actores clave en el ámbito social para la Unión Europea, y una parte vital de la estrategia Europa 2020, no pueden quedarse atrás en este asunto. Sin embargo, según la encuesta sobre transformación digital de ESADE-PwC de 2017, el 56% de las ONGs no tienen iniciativas digitales. Además, solo el 8% de las ONGs afirmaron tener una estrategia digital definida. De estos datos podemos inferir que muchas organizaciones están perdiendo muchas oportunidades que la transformación puede ofrecerles en un gran número de ámbitos. Si observamos las razones para esta falta de digitalización, según la encuesta
mencionada previamente, el 55% de las organizaciones comentan la necesidad de formación de sus empleados en habilidades digitales, y el 50% afirma que la falta de presupuesto es un obstáculo para la digitalización. Entendemos transformación digital como la implementación de recursos tecnológicos y habilidades digitales que mejoran el desempeño de una organización. 

<< Objectives >>

Son objetivos prioritarios del proyecto:
- Promover la digitalización en las ONGs, aumentando su capacidad de generar impacto en su público objetivo.
- Aumentar el atractivo de las oportunidades de cooperación Erasmus+ como medio para internacionalizar y profesionalizar las organizaciones juveniles.
- Mejorar las competencias y habilidades digitales de los trabajadores de las ONGs, haciéndoles capaces de implantar estrategias digitales en sus organizaciones y aumentando su competitividad.
Estos objetivos están totalmente alineados con las prioridades del proyecto, y con los objetivos de las asociaciones a pequeña escala.
Al finalizar el proyecto, esperamos los siguientes resultados:
- Al menos 200 descargas de nuestros materiales.
- Al menos 200 visualizaciones de cada videotutorial.
- Al menos 10 reacciones a nuestras publicaciones en redes sociales.

<< Implementation >>

Este proyecto ayuda a las ONGs y sus trabajadores a avanzar hacia la digitalización. Lo hicimos con las siguientes actividades:
Creación de un toolkit de herramientas, habilidades, y competencias digitales. En él incluiremos infografías, videotutoriales, guías teóricas y actividades de gamificación.
Realizamos una serie de webinars divididos por temáticas de la digitalización

<< Results >>

Al finalizar el proyecto, hemos conseguido los siguientes resultados:
- Al menos 200 descargas de nuestros materiales.
- Al menos 200 visualizaciones de cada videotutorial.
- Al menos 10 reacciones a nuestras publicaciones en redes sociales.
- Al menos 100 suscriptores en nuestro canal de youtube.
- Al menos 100 organizaciones manifiestan que el material ha sido de utilidad para digitalizarse.
- Al menos 160 trabajadores manifiestan que el material ha aumentado su formación.

hr.name: HRVATSKI URED ZA KREATIVNOST I INOVACIJE

2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000027439.title: Motivate to Engage
2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000027439.summary:
<< Background >>

EDUnaut and BIOM are 2 different organizations that have in common the same underlying goal - offering support to at-risk children and youth without adequate parental support.  Our partnership was united by a single vision: to empower these young individuals by equipping them with the tools to change their mindset, self-regulate in times of stress, and nurture essential soft skills. Therefore, MTE project aimed at fulfilling the needs of our youth workers; improving capacity of each partner organization by exchanging out practices and learning from the other partner.  Methods needed to widen our knowledge and expertise were: psychology, stress management, problem based learning and experiential learning (BIOM's expertise); lifelong learning skills development, foreign language learning, sexual health counselling (EDUnaut's expertise). Our aim was providing the synthesis of effective methods and activities that can be used to foster motivation and fully engage youth participation. Our unified efforts and project results were meant to be helpful to us in our daily work, but to other European professionals working with youth who need practical resources, as well.

<< Objectives >>

Being intrinsically motivated, having the right set of key competences for lifelong learning and having skills to deal with stress will help youth to make better career and general life choices. Before the project, our youth workers did not have all the necessary tools to achieve this aim and we wanted to change it by giving them useful materials. Our project's objective was learning from the experience and expertise of our project partner to fill in the gaps missing in both of our organizations. We needed this to continue working effectively with youngsters on their motivation. Therefore, the main objective of the project was producing results that would be used by the participating organizations’ youth workers in their daily work- Guidebook and Reflection kit (set of cards with instructions). We wanted to create helpful material, effective and beneficial and not only to us, but for others like us - youth workers, teachers, psychologists, care workers in other countries, working in different contexts with young people. 

<< Implementation >>

We implemented several activities: Guidebook for the youth workers and the Reflection kit, first meeting (in Split), final meeting (online) and dissemination activity (delivered online). In addition to this, we held many online meetings and several internal workshops.  
However, the main and central activity of our project was a continuous work of both organizations during the course of almost 2 years in order to thoroughly prepare the results (work on the Guidebook and Reflection kit) This work consisted of the content development, research, material systematization, writing draft material for the chapters, editing, proofreading, suggesting alternatives to the partner, re-writing and correcting, pilot testing and feedback sessions, refining, editing of the results upon the feedback from youth and youthworkers
We developed the above mentioned tools, specifically Reflection Kit, in a co-design process - gathering feedback from both youth workers and youngsters in order to tailor the results to their needs and increase user experience, as well. 


<< Results >>

Motivate to Engage project results are Guidebook and the Reflection kit.
MTE Guidebook:  This comprehensive guide is a valuable resource for youth workers, teachers, psychologists, care and social workers. It is packed with strategies, activities, and insights on how to guide young individuals in their journey of personal growth and motivation development. It is divided into 2 parts: theoretical and practical part (activites). Available in: English, Croatian and Hungarian language.
MTE Reflection Kit: The Reflection Kit, featuring a set of 26 thought-provoking cards, is designed to aid young people in self-reflection and fully engage youth participation.They are intended to make it easier for the youth worker to talk about and reflect on the feelings experienced by youth. Cards are accompanied with brief instructions on their usage. 
These results are the didactic material enabling youth workers to use different tools to:
work on the development of youth intrinsic motivation; improve their key competences; teach youth methods to overcome stress, obtain information on how learning and teaching approaches set in a group context and based on experience can have a unique effect on the development of young people.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Quality and innovation of youth work

2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000027441.title: Ready 2 Help - priprema i odgovor mladih na krizne situacije
2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000027441.summary:
<< Background >>

Crisis situations, caused by human activity or nature, have a significant impact on the psychological state of citizens who are affected by it. Depression, anxiety, panic and fear are the most common consequences of crisis situations, and such states of citizens should not be ignored. Ignoring the mentioned mental conditions often leads to fatal outcomes - self-harm or even suicide, or to other chronic mental health conditions that make everyday function and quality of life difficult. For this reason, it is necessary to provide timely and high-quality first aid, psychosocial assistance and support to citizens, especially to the most vulnerable. Given that volunteers and employees of partner organizations did not have enough capacity to provide quality and correct assistance to citizens in crisis situations, the project provided training for employees and volunteers and the exchange of young volunteers. Through the implementation of project activities, the capacity of partner organizations to work with young people was strengthened, including them in volunteer programs and training them for work in crisis situations so that the response to them would be timely, high-quality and appropriate.

<< Objectives >>

The general goal of the project was to support active European citizenship, especially young people, and to increase the international cooperation of Red Cross societies throughout Europe. The general goal was achieved through specific goals: 1. To improve cooperation between the RC Čakovec, Osijek and Maribor societies and 2. To increase the capacities of partner organizations for work with young people with an emphasis on crisis situations. Through the cooperation of partner organizations, we wanted to increase the capacities of organizations, their quality of work in regular activities, but also in work with young people. The realization of international cooperation opened the possibility for organizational changes and exchange of experiences. Training young people in the field of democratic life, civic activism, human rights and the principles of the Red Cross Movement directly contributes to the priority of encouraging young people to engage in civic activism, promoting alternative forms of participation and developing a sense of initiative among young people. The activities of preparing for the response to crisis situations are related to the priority of the environment and the fight against climate change.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were carried out:
1. The training of employees of partner organizations for work with young people during a crisis situation refers to the organization and maintenance of educational activities for 15 employees for a total duration of 10 days. 1 additional training was held for 8 employees.
2. The training of young volunteers - members of the intervention teams includes conducting 1 set of the theoretical and 1 set of the practical part of the education for 30 young volunteers.
3. The exchange of young volunteers - members of intervention teams was held in partner organizations with the aim of practicing the acquired knowledge and skills of young volunteers, gaining experience, getting to know the work of OCD's and participating in regular activities and volunteer actions of partner organizations.
4. The activity of management and promotion included the holding of partner meetings with the aim of monitoring the implementation of project activities and the holding of meetings with the aim of analyzing responses to previous and planning responses to future crisis situations. As a result, an Analysis of responses to previous crisis situations and a joint response plan to future crisis situations was created.

<< Results >>

This project strengthened the cooperation of partner organizations, strengthened the capacities for the implementation of international cooperation projects and improved work with young people, with a special emphasis on motivating, involving and coordinating young volunteers during crisis situations.
We achieved the following results:
1. Education was held for employees with the aim of strengthening their capacity to work with young people during crisis situations for 10 days.
2. A total of 29 employees were trained in the field of crisis management and leading youth intervention teams in crisis situations.
3. One additional employee training was conducted, 8 employees participated.
4. One set of theoretical part of youth education was conducted, consisting of 5 educations, a total of 34 young volunteers participated.
5. One set of practical part of youth education was conducted, consisting of 9 educations, a total of 27 young volunteers participated.
6. 17 young volunteers took part in the youth exchange for a total of 7 days and completed 269 volunteer hours.
7. One initial, 4 partnership and 3 working meetings were held.
8. Analysis of responses to previous and a joint response plan for future crisis situations was created.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000029320.title: Learning by Doing Good - Supporting Learning through Youth-led Community Projects
2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000029320.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to advance both organisations’ practices of supporting young people in implementing youth-led community engagement actions, as a tool that contributes both to participatory learning of young people and to community development. At the same time, youth workers had the need to develop their competencies in supporting young people's experiential learning processes through the design and implementation of youth-led community engagement actions enabling their self-directed learning from those actions. Both organisations had the need to systemize their existing knowledge related to young people’s participatory learning, community engagement and active participation through the creation of an innovative and more structured approach to informal learning. In this way, sustainable mechanisms of active participation and involvement of young people in organisations’ activities and community were developed and the visibility of organisations in the field of youth work was enhanced. Both organisations needed to strengthen external networks and partnership in serving communities and broadening society by promoting innovative youth-led practices thus stressing the importance of different youth work approaches.

<< Objectives >>

Through the implementation of the project activities, we wanted to improve both organisations’ practices of supporting young people in implementing youth-led community engagement actions, as a tool that contributes both to participatory learning of young people and to community development. We wanted to make the learning process more participatory in relation to young people included, and to put focus on supporting young people to plan and organise their learning objectives and processes, based on which they would decide how to design and implement their community-based projects. We also wanted to provide the youth workers with necessary competences and skills to support the process of self-assessment and planning of the learning objectives of young people, and then facilitate the process of developing their community-based projects. The project practice was systemized in a set of guidelines which can be followed in other activities aimed at empowering young people to actively participate, as well as in the training of youth workers. By implementation of project activities and creation of diverse and new content within local communities, the visibility of organisations and youth work at local level was enhanced.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented all of the foresaw activities: coordination activities among partners and the elaboration of Guidelines, the 7 days long international training for 10 youth workers (5 Slovenian and 5 Croatian), the activity of designing of the training for young participants, 2 National trainings for young participants (10 participants in Slovenia, 8 participants in Croatia), the activities of designing and implementation of the youth-led community engagement actions (3 in Croatia and 6 in Slovenia) with continuous mentoring support (individual and group) provided by youth workers and the 3 days international study and evaluation meeting in Ljubljana which involved the project coordination team, youth workers, and young people who designed and implemented youth-led community engagement actions in the local community. The promotion and dissemination activities were going on during the whole period of project implementation: promotion of project activities on social media profiles and in direct contacts with possible participants, public calls for participants for project activities with young people, surveys in local communities (needs assessments), youth-led community actions.

<< Results >>

The main project output was that both partner organisations advanced their practices of supporting young people in implementing youth-led community engagement actions thus contributing both to participatory learning of young people and to community development. It occurred through 3 project results: 1) The organisations, through the analysis of their existing approaches, methodologies and practices, improved capacities for supporting participatory project-based learning; 2) 10 youth workers improved their competencies in the fields of participatory planning of learning objectives and facilitating and supporting young people’s learning process through the process of planning and implementation of the community actions; 3) 18 Young participants had the possibility to critically assess their needs and interests, plan personal learning objectives and actively participate by developing and implementing community actions contributing thus to the achievement of the pre-planned learning objectives, with continuous support by youth workers. The implementation of all project activities resulted in development of Guidelines for supporting active participation of young people within the local community through youth-led actions.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000029421.title: Digitalni prozor u svijet MD
2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000029421.summary:
<< Background >>

During the years, SDDH has recognized the need to improve the competences of those who work with young persons with muscular dystrophy (MD). MD is a rare, progressive disease that causes muscle weakening. Early onset of symptoms leads to faster progression and muscle weakness leads to the inability to walk independently and to reduced mobility in general. Progression of disease is reflected primary on the physical level, but it also has a big impact on socio-emotional development. This results in social inactivity, anxiety, impaired self-confidence etc. The field of work with young persons with MD is demanding and therefore the Project aimed to empower people who work with young persons with MD and provide them the knowledge and skills of creating work methods that will be widely applicable and available. The absence of an attractive communication channel has a negative effect on empowerment of young persons with MD, and due to the increased concern of their parents, they are exposed to overprotective relationship. It is necessary for people working with young persons with MD to master the techniques to discover and present their potential and abilities in order to create an affirmative environment for their inclusion in society. 

<< Objectives >>

The general goal of the Project was to improve the capacities of organizations involved by improving knowledge and skills of Youth Workers (YW) who are working with young persons with MD. By strengthening the competences of YW we wanted to empower them to be able develop innovative work methods of empowering youth with MD for a more active role in the society. Digital technologies are advancing rapidly, and the goal is to follow this pace and use new methods of communication with whom young people can relate to. In order to create a stimulating environment, it is necessary to improve the digital competences and media literacy of YW. Specific goals were to encourage YW to discover and develop the potential of young persons with MD by applying new knowledge and skills, to know how to use digital tools to present abilities of young persons, and to instruct young persons to use assistive technology. By exchanging valuable experience between partners, the goal was to obtain an additional level of innovation and encouragement in working on the specific needs of young people. The aim of the Project was also to make the created work methods and tools available to every organization that have young people with MD as their target group. 

<< Implementation >>

Project activities included: Three two-day transnational meetings with the partner organization conducted at the beginning, during, and at the end of the Project; Activities to strengthen the capacity of Youth Workers to work with young persons with MD: a Talent development program through 5 modules on recognizing and developing potential and abilities; Educations on the use of digital tools;  on How to organize and conduct online campaigns and About assistive technology; Study trip to Slovenia; Round tables: Live one on examples of good practice in working with young people with MD and Online one on assistive technology; the organization of National events with the aim to raise awareness and promote the potential and talents of young persons with MD; Online campaigns about the importance of assistive technology for communication and inclusion in the community and about the importance of digital tools in promoting their capabilities; Volunteer activities; Participation in research, guided discussions, interactive workshops; hosting of Forum Theater, Promotional events, Creation of promotional and educational content and manuals, Presentation of participant's impressions and holding a Final conference for the public and media. 

<< Results >>

SDDH and DDS Partnership agreement has been implemented; 3 transnational meetings were held; Training programs and education for YW were conducted; Good practice examples on working with young people with MD were shared during a Study trip on which a short video was made; a Volunteer action has been conducted;  Guided discussions on the achievements and goals of youth with MD, Interactive workshop about self-presentation and Online Round table on assistive technology (AT) were held; Erasmus Days 2022 were marked; National events (Talent show SDDH and Šovtalentov DDS) were held; Online Campaign about AT and potential of persons with MD was carried out and also Videos about AT have been translated; Young persons with MD participated in the research conducted by Faculty of Education and Rehabilitation Sciences; one YW authored the afterword and was an editor of the book written by a young person with MD; Digital leaflet on AT was created; Young persons provided an overview of transnational cooperation on the Project through a column, graphic design and podcast; Participants impressions were published; Manual for working with youth with MD in Croatian and Slovenian language was published and the Final press conference was held.

2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000031047.title: Kreativni placemaking - put prema aktivnom europskom građanstvu
2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000031047.summary:
<< Background >>

Creating a space for young people in which they can express themselves creatively and strengthen their capacities for responsible participation in the community is an important element of the development of the individual itself, as well as the foundation of a democratic society. But this process becomes unfeasible when the element of young people as active and responsible citizens is missing and when the local self-government leaves out young people as equal participants from the entire process.  In order to be actively involved in the development of the community, they need to be given knowledge, information and skills to strengthen their self-confidence, develop critical thinking and, take an equal position in society. What is the most important moment for the project is precisely the expressed need of the young people themselves to be actively involved in the processes of advocating the creation of content for future youth programs in public spaces that are unused or partially used. We have united all expressed needs of young people through the creation of unique educational work methods and the development of online tool for the creative design of public spaces for youth content, which is available for free use.

<< Objectives >>

With this project, we wanted to develop international cooperation between three partner organizations that share common values ​​in the inclusion of young people in the processes of participation in decision-making in local environments by working on advocacy and putting into operation the public spaces of cultural heritage that abound in all three countries by applying and developing the methodology " placemaking" (designing public spaces for youth activities). Spaces of cultural heritage are a common European value, as are active young citizens, and by connecting these two dimensions and creating a new multidisciplinary educational interactive tool: LOCUS: creative placemaking toolbox, our goal was to contribute to organizational strengthening, strengthening of people who work with young people, the young people themselves , and finally the community in which we operate. Mutual exchange of experience and practices, mutual learning and sharing of common values ​​in the field of placemaking enabled the ultimate goal of raising awareness of the importance of active civic participation among young people.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented four main project activities: Transnational partnership meetings; International training; Development of the "Placemaking Tolbox" tool and Multiplying events at the national/local level

<< Results >>

Exchanged knowledge, experience and common values ​​in the field of creating public spaces for youth content with the dimension of cultural heritage between partner organizations; Developed educational methodology for creating public spaces for young people through an online tool: LOCUS: Creative placemaking toolbox; Drafted policy recommendations by all three organizations for the creation of public spaces for youth activities and delivered to local governments; Ensured exchange of knowledge among persons who work with young people about common European values ​​of creating active citizenship.

Other results of the activity are: Three transnational partner meetings were held in all three partner countries; Agreed creation of all informative, educational, evaluation and promotional activities; Developed project monitoring plan and schedule, developed project evaluation; Developed international training curriculum; Developed online tool - LOCUS: Creative placemaking toolbox; Organized and conducted three national dissemination events (Karlovac, Tampere, Nicosia); A new social educational methodology was presented.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000033834.title: Transnational Cooperation For Social Exclusion Escape
2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000033834.summary:
<< Background >>

The TC4SEE project was based on the motivation to establish a transnational consortium that worked with the most disadvantaged target groups of youth in order to share knowledge, experience and good practices thus finally researching and developing an innovative e-learning material. The developed SEE e-Toolkit was designed in a way that helped improve young disadvantaged persons soft skills, digital skills and promote social inclusion through game-based learning methodology that will remain available to youth with and without disabilities. In a such way this material will continue to serve as a powerful tool for social inclusion, education, engagement, empowerment and international connections among disadvantaged youth and their non-disadvantaged friends. The members of the consortium are continuing the work towards the social inclusion of the most disadvantaged youth by implementing other Erasmus+ funded project's, for example CABPS is a partner on a Erasmus+ Ka2 SSP CSI: MART where they will develop activities for the blind people based on the mindfulness and art therapy; while EUROPA2020 and WT have continued to collaborate on a new Erasmus+ KA2 E4D project aimed to promote democracy values among the young  people in the EU.

<< Objectives >>

We successfully achieved all the project objectives. Firstly, we promoted and developed non-formal education methodologies that tackle inclusion, equity, excellence, creativity, diversity and innovation in education, training and youth by using innovative methodologies such as gamification and e-learning specially designed for disadvantaged youth. Secondly, We have established and developed transnational cooperation between organizations that work with youth with disabilities and youth with fewer opportunities in order to exchange of knowledge, information and resources for innovating such youth work. Finally, We managed to utilize digital tools, resources and creative digital and game-based methodologies in order to innovate learning processes and increase their quality so that they have addressed the issues of social exclusion of our specific target group. 

<< Implementation >>

All the activities of this project were implemented online through the use of free online communication and collaboration tools such as Slack, Skype, Google Drive, Canva, Balabolka (conversion to audiobook)... We held 3 online translational meetings followed by 5 online conference calls/work groups in order for the consortium members to get to know each other, share knowledge, information and work together on the creation of the final output. In total 9 staff members from the consortium were involved in implementation of the project's activities. The Quality management activity ensured the proper methodology in regards to the recognition of youth work by creating digital badge and Youthpass certificates as a recognition of learning achievements, promotion and implementation of EU instruments in order to validate the competences acquired by the participants and staff during their participation in the project activities. In total 20 innovative board games accessible to the youth with disabilities were developed, pilot tested with 37 participants in all partner countries, published in 5 national languages, converted in accessible files for the people with visual impairment and shared during the #ErasmusDays2022 with 138 persons. 

<< Results >>

The project's main purpose was to tackle the social exclusion of the most disadvantaged youth groups by finding and creating innovative learning opportunities that allowed them to participate in pilot testing activities equally so that they could gain much-needed skills while collaborating with their peers without obstacles. During the development of the project's main output, the consortium managed to develop 20 board games completely accessible to youth with disabilities. We addressed digital transformation through the development of digital readiness, resilience and capacity priority which has been addressed through the creation of an E-Toolkit published in pdf., audiobook and epub files with the corresponding translation in all the partner languages: English, Croatian, Bulgarian, Greek and Spanish. In the SEE e-Toolkit the most innovative solutions were presented regarding the main project's topic which was to bring new innovative educational activities and tools which will be used in order to improve soft skills and digital skills in the target group. The project's main output is available for download on the project's web page, Erasmus+ Results Platform and Salto Youth web page.

2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000033863.title: Inclusion through Activism, Communication and Tolerance
2021-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000033863.summary:
<< Background >>

The motivation for the project has emerged naturally from our two organizations' previous experience with young people. Issues related to belonging, social inclusion, fairness, equality and effective communication have repeatedly resurfaced among all the groups of young people we work with, pointing to a growing difficulty among 18-25 year olds to "fit in," to find their place in society. This is particularly prominent in those who consider themselves different in any way: excluded/discriminated against due to their minority status. A need has emerged to produce a program which would tackle issues related to social exclusion, discrimination, inequality and lack of channels for civic activism and democratic participation. In our work, our trainers have also identified a tendency to reach young people mostly from the capital cities and from middle class families. Such young people are not immune to social exclusion and challenges, however, they often have more in common with similar status young people in other EU countries than with immigrants and NEET in their own country. We felt the need to place diverse groups of young people under the same roof and to create a safe environment for discussing contemporary social challenges.

<< Objectives >>

The iACT project had 2 objectives. Firstly, to increase the capacities of our two partner institutions for work with diverse groups of young
people, especially with youth facing economic obstacles, through international cooperation on the development of joint new activities. Secondly, to empower young people from different economic backgrounds for civic participation on local, national and European level by nurturing their sense of initiative and promoting equality and non-discrimination. We planned to and engaged in exchange of expertise, the enhancement of trainers' skills, and in the empowerment of young people through their direct involvement in the preparation and implementation of activities. We also wanted to help young people build understanding of contemporary issues related to inclusion and diversity and develop confidence to address them, initially, verbally, and later on, through activism.

<< Implementation >>

The project team planned and implemented 5 main activities, as follows:
Activity 1: Training-for-trainers: exchange of expertise on innovative media for youth engagement and empowerment (2 in-person modules organized and one external training completed),
Activity 2: Interactive educational program for young people on inclusion, non-discrimination and democratic participation (an in-person program of 4 courses of 9 1.5-hour sessions each organized, or a total of 36 sessions in Brussels and Zagreb)
Activity 3: Short digital course on social inclusion and equity in democratic societies,
Activity 4: Multiplier events (9 events organized),
Activity 5: Transnational project team meetings (4 in-person meetings organized).

<< Results >>

The following results were planned and realized:
Tangible
• 6 trainers completed training & participated in exchange of expertise on innovative media for engagement of young people, including such enabling digital and blended learning;
• An interactive 10-month long educational program on inclusion, non-discrimination and democratic participation for young
people (18-25 years old) was developed and piloted;
• 34 young people, 18-25 years of age, completed the interactive educational program, including minimum 14 young people facing
economic obstacles;
• A short free-access digital course on inclusion and equity, non-discrimination, democratic participation, communication and self-expression was developed in English and distributed to schools, NGOs and online communities;
• A YouTube channel on young people's engagement with topics related to inclusion, equality and non-discrimination was created and maintained;
• 9 multiplier events were organized promoting the project on local, national and EU level.
Non-tangible
• Capacities were developed for work with diverse groups of young people, in particular such facing economic obstacles, of our 2 locally-operating NGOs;
• The transnational cooperation of our NGOs was developed.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2021-1-NL02-KA210-YOU-000027423.title: Young Boss - business idea generator for youngsters with lesser opportunities
2021-1-NL02-KA210-YOU-000027423.summary:
<< Background >>

Young people, who have lesser opportunities, often have a distance to the labour market. Their lesser opportunities can stem from their background, living situation or other. This can cause young people to be less able to find work. To help young people gain the skills, which can help them to find jobs, the project developed a programme, in which they learn about entrepreneurial skills. These skills help them strengthen their position on the labour market.  

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the Young Boss project were set in the proposal as:  
- Create more awareness on (social) entrepreneurial opportunities amongst youngsters with lesser opportunities between 13-17 years old
