- Promote entrepreneurial behaviour and invigorate the development of entrepreneurial skills amongst youngsters with lesser opportunities between 13-17 years old  
- Provide practical tools to engage youngsters with lesser opportunities between 13-17 years old in (social) entrepreneurship  

Young Boss had as goal to reach these objectives by developing and testing a methodology which will engage youngsters with lesser opportunities in (social) entrepreneurship. Young Boss aimed to guide these youngsters from through all stages of developing their business idea, testing etc. up until the realisation of the business. This is directly linked to the selected priority which is focused on youth (social) entrepreneurship.

<< Implementation >>

During the projects lifetime the partners have implemented several activities: 

- Planning and preparation Young Boss- business idea generator (A1)  
- Planning and preparation Young Boss - business idea generator (A2)  
- Implementation and follow-up Young Boss – business idea generator (A3)  
- Young Boss Promotional video (A4).  
 

KADO was responsible as lead for the first three activities and Dom Mladih for the last one.  These were all divided into sub activities.  

A1 was divided into: - creating an activity work plan. – organizing a kick-off meeting to kick-off the project. A2 did not have sub-activities. A3 was divided into: - testing the material created in A2 - organising a TPM – follow up on the material created and tested. A4 was divided into – planning and preparation of the video – development of the video – follow-up (organisation of event).  

<< Results >>

In the first phase of the project the partners were able to create research to ask input from teachers and mentors which worked in the field. The partnership received 11 responses to these surveys. The information given, was a confirmation to continue with topics, which the partners were already inclining to move towards.  

During the second phase the partners used the input gathered in A1 to develop a programme. This programme was divided into 6 workshops. Each workshop discusses different topics, to help mentors or teachers teach the youngsters in an active way. Activities and assignments are an active part of the programme. 

After the development of the workshops, both partners have tested the materials and based on the feedback the final version of the programme has been made.  

The last outcome is the video, which were created during the testing. After which they were put together.

2021-1-PL01-KA210-YOU-000031086.title: Wybór należy do ciebie
2021-1-PL01-KA210-YOU-000031086.summary:
<< Background >>

We embarked on the "The Choice is Yours" project to support LGBTQ+ youth in entering the job market. In local communities, we identified exclusionary environments, both in schools and workplaces. The lack of training for educators further complicates the situation for young LGBTQ+. A report from the European Commission confirmed that discrimination in employment still persists. As project leaders, we decided to counter this issue by creating training materials, recommendations, and fostering awareness in the work environment.

The decision to apply for funding stemmed from the belief that international partnerships hold significant potential in addressing these challenges. Our aim was to establish universal standards of communication and collaboration, fostering social integration for LGBTQ+ youth while also considering potential employers.

We applied to collectively enhance opportunities for youth, elevate the skills of youth workers, and exchange knowledge internationally. Our goal was to demonstrate that we possess the tools to support LGBTQ+ youth and create conditions for their dignified lives. This endeavor reflects our passion and commitment to positive change, benefiting both young individuals and potential employers.

<< Objectives >>

As part of the "The Choice is Yours" project, our aim was to support LGBTQ+ youth in overcoming societal barriers and shaping unified communication standards. By developing the skills of youth workers and potential employers, we sought to promote equality, justice, tolerance, and civic engagement. In collaborative efforts with Greece, Croatia, and Bulgaria, we organized meetings, training courses, and a concluding conference.

Our objectives included raising social awareness, understanding the needs of LGBTQ+ youth, and training and motivating youth workers. Our efforts aimed to improve job offerings for youth, strengthen organizational structures, and enhance the project's visibility at the European level. The target groups encompassed project staff, youth workers, engaged youth, potential employers, and youth organizations. Our actions are intended to have a lasting impact on the environment, creating a space for equality and acceptance in society.

<< Implementation >>

1) Kick-off meeting (Leszno, Poland): During the partner meeting in Poland, we conducted a study visit to Wrocław, delving into the best practices of "Stowarzyszenie Różnorodności Społecznej UP-DATE".

2) LTTA (Athens, Greece): We participated in a training session that expanded our knowledge of gender identity and the diversity of the LGBTQ+ community. Workshops such as "living library" and theatrical workshops helped us better understand the challenges faced by LGBTQ+ individuals in the job market. During the study visit, the "Emfasis Foundation" also presented the issue of homelessness among young LGBTQ+ people. Our experiences, including participation in a festival of queer short films, were a valuable contribution to the development of our publication.

3) Conference (Wrocław, Poland): The conference served as a platform to present recommendations for employers and educators. We discussed the project stages, showcasing significant progress in creating an inclusive environment. Workshops aided in understanding the challenges of young LGBTQ+ individuals and support strategies. We also joined the Wrocław Equality Parade, emphasizing our commitment to equality.

<< Results >>

Within the project, a publication titled "Recommendations for potential employers and youth workers working with young LGBTIQ+" was created. This publication organizes knowledge through a glossary, supporting youth workers, teachers, and educators with training materials and document templates. For potential employers, it provides guidance on responsible management, dealing with negative attitudes, preparing an inclusive recruitment process, and case studies.

Additionally, content for young LGBTQ+ individuals guides them on constructing CVs, applications, and preparing for job interviews. The publication includes a list of organizations where they can seek support. Our guide serves as a roadmap for those working with LGBTQ+ youth and employers, promoting a work environment based on respect, empathy, dignity, and tolerance. It is significant support for young LGBTQ+ individuals, and the partnership's recommendations could become uniform standards in Europe and beyond.

2021-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000033900.title: #ReciklirajSE
2021-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000033900.summary:
<< Background >>

Young people have innovative "green" ideas and not enough opportunities to make concrete initiatives and be heard. Our project allowed them to express their opinion, share it with their peers and the world! We are convinced that the 1st step in the fight for environmental protection really happened only when we were able to look at recycling more broadly and understand it as a process of carefully separating everything that is useless/no longer serves its purpose. At the EU level, we introduced young people to some responsible approaches to recycling for the well-being of people and nature. But in order to raise awareness, we first had to take off our rose-colored glasses and change our view of the world! The project allowed young people to simply choose a different filter, put on a different color of glasses and start thorough recycling, both at home and in the world. Recycling, based on breaking false beliefs and creating a new, greener future, actually started right in our heads - with recycling - not only of waste (black glasses), but also of our own thoughts/emotions (red glasses). values/priorities (yellow glasses) and attitude to the Earth (green glasses: they also included respect for natural resources, love for animals.

<< Objectives >>

-Establish partnership, exchange of conceptual/experiential practices, increase the quality of youth work. - draw attention to the importance of recycling, - raise environmental awareness, spread good practices about responsible consumerism and environmental protection - encourage youth to take their own initiatives - offer young people the opportunity for experiential learning, through joint activities bring different, including green, practices closer to each other, which are contributed to their physical and mental health/well-being - to strengthen the competences of volunteers, youth, pedagogic, advisory workers in the field of environmental protection and personal growth (recycling of thoughts/emotions, waste/attitude towards nature) and to ensure their transfer into practice - Spread results among other related org. at the local/national/EU level - Take care of the social inclusion of young people, promote active citizenship/volunteering in the field of environmental protection - Through the tool, we drew attention to the fact that recycling really starts with a person, who must tackle 4 fundamental areas (4-steps), recycling waste, recycling attitudes towards the Earth, recycling of thoughts/emotions, values/prioritities.

<< Implementation >>

We carried out the following project activities: KICK OFF MEETING, where we consolidated partnerships and set good plans for the overall success of the project, 3. INTERNATIONAL PROJECT MEETINGS, where we encouraged young people to create a greener future through active citizenship and social inclusion), ON-LINE CAMPAIGN, we enabled young people to share their environmental protection initiatives, INTERNATIONAL PROFESSIONAL CONFERENCE, where we drew attention to the wider importance of recycling for human well-being - recycling of thoughts/emotions - and nature. CREATION OF THE E-PUBLICATION, which we produced in 4 languages: English, Slovenian, German and Croatian, (dissemination and e-promotion of the results).

<< Results >>

E-PUBLICATION (4-module concept), written in the languages ​​of all organizations. and English, it included theoretical-practical steps and instructions for users, thereby enabling the implementation of informal education; due to its broad approach, it was also suitable starting material for potential transfer to other activities/industries/sectors - it was also available after the project was completed. The e-CAMPAIGN #recycleyourselffirst (anticipated organic reach of 16,000 - took place on 65 FB/IG profiles) with the help of the symbolism of glasses of different colors (each color = 1 area of ​​recycling) encouraged young people to give their own initiatives, which were visible based on the keyword #recycleyourselffirst to the wider international public. The INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE was held in SLO (at least 150 participants present), it hosted local (including a lecturer from the Austrian part.org.) and foreign experts and promoted the results.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2021-2-BE05-KA210-YOU-000048717.title: "Can you hear our rivers?"- Sava and Scheldt Youth Parliaments Cooperation
2021-2-BE05-KA210-YOU-000048717.summary:
<< Background >>

The Scheldt river basin and the Sava river basin (a tributary to the Danube), although located in different climatic regions, were recently both heavily affected by similar environmental problems, such as droughts and floods produced by climate change, and pollution by agriculture, industry and shipping. In the conducted small scale youth partnership, both Scheldt and Sava youth parliaments joined forces in exploring how climate change and pollution impact their rivers, and what possibilities for active participation in environmental decision-making there were for themselves and other young people living in these river basins.

<< Objectives >>

The project established a small scale youth partnership between the Scheldt and Sava youth parliaments with the goal to improve international environmental youth work in the 7 countries that are crossed by the rivers Scheldt (France, Belgium and the Netherlands) and Sava (Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Hercegovina and Serbia). Both the Sava and Scheldt youth parliament have the objective to build capacity and to empower youngsters living in the two river basins, to enable them to actively participate in the environmental policymaking process. For this purpose, we wanted that the youngsters had the chance to participate in two one-week exchanges, in Belgium and in Croatia, in order to debate and exchange with scientists and policymakers, to improve their environmental work, to learn from each other, to improve the quality of their extracurricular youth work, to be empowered and to be coached to develop podcasts and art projects. We also aimed that the 2 group exchanges served to develop common values among youth from seven countries in- and outside the EU, and mutual inspiration to promote the active participation of youth in environmental policy processes.

<< Implementation >>

Two one-week exchanges were developed and successfully carried out. The 1st one in September 2022 in Ghent in Belgium (Scheldt side), the 2nd one in April 2023 in Zagreb in Croatia (Sava side). 10 young people from Sava Youth Parliament and 10 young people from Scheldt Youth Parliament were selected and had the chance to participated in the 1st exchange, 8 other young people from Scheldt side (not 10 because 2 cancelled at the last minute) and 12 other young people from Sava side participated in the 2nd exchange.
During the two exchanges mainly but also within the 2 years, young people had courses on podcast and video editing, creatively worked together (painting frescoes, designing logos), met several experts and guides, recorded interviews, received presentations on various topics (river basins, climate change, biodiversity, flooding, youth engagement etc.). They exchanged between them and get to know the rivers by different ways : biking, rafting, solar panel boat, by foot, by bird watching...

<< Results >>

The first overall result of this project was to empower youngsters living in the two river basins, to enable them to actively participate in the environmental policymaking process related to their river basin. Throughout the two international exchanges that were organised within this small-scale partnership, the youngsters were capacitated on their personal skills on the one hand (knowledge English, daring to speak for a group of strangers, intercultural learning, etc), and technical skills related to environmental policy making on the other hand (being in contact with policy-makers, making their point of view clear to them, learning more about preservation/climate change/pollution through experts and the impact this has on their daily lives, understand the role a youth parliament can play, etc.). 
Secondly, the project aimed to improve environmental youth work at organizational level of the Sava and Scheldt youth parliaments, and to strengthen the organisations (GoodPlanet Belgium and ISRBC) that support these youth parliaments. Through the various exchanges, project-related communication and collaboration, and mutual learning both organisations and youth parliaments feel stronger and more connected than before.
topics: Reaching the policy level/dialogue with decision makers
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2021-2-DE04-KA210-YOU-000050779.title:
YOUNG CLIMATE PROFESSIONALS (YCP)
Empowerment programme for “Green literacy and civic education for a sustainable Europe”
2021-2-DE04-KA210-YOU-000050779.summary:
<< Background >>

THE CIVICS has applied to create a space for youth from across Europe to come together and enhance their green literacy competencies by strengthening their communication and project management skills. Through a mix of expert inputs from a diverse field of environmental and sustainability topics as well as peer-to-peer learning and the conceptualization and development of their own project ideas participants were encouraged to develop their own agency as multipliers. 
THE CIVICS has realized that there is a discrepancy among different European countries when it comes to the level of green literacy. Especially, between the Eastern European countries and Western European/Scandinavian countries. Within this programme, THE CIVICS aimed at creating space for these different country contexts and perspectives to be heard and to acknowledge that the European Green Deal has to take different approaches in different countries in order to be successful. With the YCP programme, THE CIVICS caters to these different needs accordingly and enables knowledge transfer among participants. 


<< Objectives >>

THE CIVICS aimed at promoting active citizenship and social entrepreneurship among young adults from 10 European countries (Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, France, Germany, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Spain, and Sweden) with its green literacy pilot project Young Climate Professionals (YCP). At its core, the programme wanted to enhance the individual’s sustainability competencies and empower participants to become agents of change in their own communities.  

<< Implementation >>

The YCP programme consisted of 4 activities. The first three were online activities which lasted 4 hours each and took place on Saturdays (01.10.2022; 03.12.2022; 04.02.2023) via Zoom. Miro and Slack were used as tools for working and communicating among the group. The last activity was a three-day YCP Campus which took place in Berlin (30.03.-02.04.2023) as an in-person event consisting of expert talks, fishbowls, workshops, a Gallery Walk, and a field trip to the floating university.

<< Results >>

Each activity was documented on the website and social media channels of THE CIVICS and through the process facilitation in charge. The documentation includes Zoom recordings as well as screenshots of the Miro board and handouts created by the participants as well as the presentations of the individual speakers. THE CIVICS MagicMonday format via a Slack channel has resulted in an extensive toolbox that entails links to insightful reads, podcasts, videos, and funding opportunities and which has been made public on the website of THE CIVICS and can be used by YCP participants and anyone interested to brush up on their green literacy skills.
During the Gallery Walk at the YCP Campus in Berlin three winners out of all projects were curated and received the mini grant which is supporting the implementation of their project idea running from May 2023 – June 2024. The winners from Bulgaria, Croatia, and Lithuania will need to report to THE CIVICS regularly and all materials and documents produced within these projects will be made publicly available through the YCPs themselves and THE CIVICS.

2021-2-EL02-KA210-YOU-000051533.title: Sustainable Organ Networking and Innovative Cooperation
2021-2-EL02-KA210-YOU-000051533.summary:
<< Background >>

The two partners decided to excel their operational and collaboration skills, through the organisation of a number of transnational activities implemented in both Syros and Zadar allowing them to offer advanced artistic and cultural options in the future events they will be organising.
A core need has been that local and transnational groups of young artists from the two countries and beyond discover more creative solutions through their participation in the SONIC activities, which, especially in the case of their participation in the operation and targets of the digital platform are in harmony with their age and their everyday engagement in digital tools.

<< Objectives >>

The SONIC partnership addressed from the very beginning -and will continue to- young artists aged up to 30 years and their engagement in the organ culture of local remote communities like Syros and Zadar are, as well as, audience developement. The two collaborating organisations prioritised artistic evolution and audience development at the local, national and EU level. The project aimed to develop a digital tool for engaging artists of all different forms of arts, including composers, in their annual festival activities.

<< Implementation >>

The implementation part of the project was in line with the proposed and approved schedule of activities which were planned to serve the needs, the objectives and the common vision of the two partner organisations.
In specific, the partnership addressed the value of the Project Management Activity for ensuring a sound project implementation, the design and operation of the Digital Artistic Space Platform, the implementation of the Artistic Workshops in both Syros and Zadar, the Organ Concerts in Syros and Zadar and the Communication and Dissemination activity for ensuring visibility and achievements promotion at the transnational level.

<< Results >>

Local artistic resources, as well as, national and European were further reinforced through connecting the one with
another during the implementation of the project activities and, in specific, through the implementation of the organ
workshops and concerts, as well as, through the development and operation of the Digital Artistic Space Platform.
The activities proved also impacting to further enhance audience development in the local and national artistic communitied of both countries.

2021-2-ES02-KA210-YOU-000047844.title: Proyecto Guíanos para la formación y consolidación de las iniciativas y las redes europeas en Castilla -  La Mancha
2021-2-ES02-KA210-YOU-000047844.summary:
<< Background >>

This project was born with the main objective of increasing knowledge and experience in the management of international projects with young people among the social organizations that are part of EAPN Castilla-La Mancha. It was assumed that a large part of the 56 organizations that make up the network did not have experience in this field, something that could be corroborated with the first research activity of this project. In this way, the aim was to offer entities the necessary training and experience so that they could start implementing Erasmus + projects and thus be able to benefit from the multiple advantages that being part of this type of European actions entails.

<< Objectives >>

-To increase knowledge and experience in the management of international projects with young people among
EAPN-CLM network entities in Castilla - La Mancha.
-To detect the level of access and use of European funds of the entities of CLM.
-To facilitate the transmission of knowledge and good practices with European entities.
-To promote the creation of an area and a strategy for European projects among CLM entities.
-To initiate the presentation of European projects for CLM organisations.

<< Implementation >>

Exchange visits and knowledge of good practices between Castilla - La Mancha and European organisations (PT, BG
and POL).
- Analysis of the capacity and access to European initiatives in the social organisations of Castilla - La Mancha.
- Guide for the creation of an area and a strategy for European projects.
- Initiation to European projects
- Dissemination and multiplier events

<< Results >>

- Analysis of the capacity for the management of European initiatives in CLM.
- Carrying out international exchange visits.
- Guide for the creation of an area and a strategy for European projects.
- Dissemination of the guide among third sector organisations that are part of EAPN-CLM.
- Accompaniment and guidance to present at least three European initiatives before the end of the project in collaboration
with the organisations participating in the project.
topics: Economic and financial affairs (including funding issues)

2021-2-ES02-KA210-YOU-000048071.title: E-learning platform for citizenship education: Escape for Democracy
2021-2-ES02-KA210-YOU-000048071.summary:
<< Background >>

We recognized a pressing need to address the lack of democratic participation among young people, particularly in rural areas of EU countries. Despite their eagerness to engage in EU projects, our youth lacked sufficient knowledge of EU values, social, cultural, & historical heritage, and demonstrated limited interest in democratic processes. We saw an opportunity to bridge this gap by developing innovative e-learning materials focused on citizenship education. E2020 joined to innovate education to engage youth in democracy through gamification. Walktogether aimed to promote gamification and NFE for active citizenship. Viimsi focused on using gamification to educate local youth about democracy, integrating e-learning materials into their youth center activities. Kalimera expanded into citizenship education through the E4D project, collaborating with local partners to enhance youth engagement in rural areas. We aimed to empower youth with comprehensive knowledge of political systems, democracy, and human rights to foster active engagement in democratic participation. Our goal was to equip them with the skills to contribute meaningfully to our community and the EU.


<< Objectives >>

Through transnational and intersectoral collaboration, this consortium aimed to contribute to democratic participation across EU member states by creating powerful e-learning solutions based on gamification and digitalization of non-formal education aimed at youth. By understanding the importance of working together across sectors to bring education into the digital age, the results of this project directly contributed to teaching and promoting European Values, Democratic participation, the principles of unity and diversity, as well as the EU's diverse social, cultural, and historical heritage. The main objectives established through E4D were:
-The consortium established and developed transnational cooperation between diverse intersectoral organizations, exchanging knowledge, information, and resources to contribute to the digitalization and innovation of youth work in order to foster the values of democratic participation for youth.
-An e-learning module was developed based on digital gamification and non-formal education in order to teach and promote European Values, Democratic participation, the principles of unity and diversity, as well as the EU's diverse social, cultural, and historical heritage.


<< Implementation >>

Project Management & Coordination: Ensured smooth implementation of the work plan, aligned administrative procedures with EU requirements, and facilitated monthly steering group meetings and transnational meetings to oversee progress and ensure timely delivery of milestones.
Quality Management, Research Validity, & Evaluation of Content: Developed a robust quality assurance plan which included regular evaluations, quality reports, & validation of project processes and educational materials.
E-learning Platform - Escape for Democracy: Created an open-source e-learning platform www.escapefordemocracy.com featuring 3 digital educational escape rooms on citizenship education supported by a comprehensive handbook with research results and educational scenarios.
Dissemination & Exploitation: Implemented a wide-reaching dissemination strategy, including developing a detailed plan, creating visibility materials, managing social media and website updates, and organizing multiplier events to engage stakeholders in the youth sector and policy-making.
Activities were designed to enhance democratic participation among youth, promote EU values, and ensure the sustainability and widespread impact of our project across EU member states.

<< Results >>

We created 3 digital educational escape rooms for EU citizenship education, accompanied by a handbook featuring 9 scenarios and a toolkit. Our e-learning platform, www.escapefordemocracy.com, offers interactive modules in multiple languages, including English. These tools significantly improve youth understanding and engagement in democratic principles and European values, bolstered by digital certificates.
E4D aligned with the EU Youth Strategy, involving 113 young people in pilot testing events across four countries during Erasmus Days 2023, surpassing our target of 40 participants. This initiative aimed to deliver comprehensive citizenship education and empower young individuals with essential political knowledge and human rights awareness.
We forged associated partnerships among diverse organizations across EU member states, promoting knowledge exchange and digital innovation in youth work to enhance democratic participation. We also showcased our educational resources during a KA1 TC in Spain to engage international organizations.
We delivered innovative learning opportunities within the EU and served as a model for youth practitioners globally, encouraging similar approaches to foster democratic engagement among young people

2021-2-HR01-KA210-YOU-000048928.title: Creative Learning Environment for Environmental Protection
2021-2-HR01-KA210-YOU-000048928.summary:
<< Background >>

We wanted to strengthen the capacities of partner organizations (PO) to work with youth in the fields of culture, art, art therapy, environmental protection, and sustainable development and contribute to the quality and innovation of youth work in PO. POs needed to network and get to know active youth work stakeholders, knowledge of art therapy, sustainable and recycled art to be able to introduce new practices in youth work, and knowledge of the way of working and opportunities for youth in the cultural and creative industry, and the need to strengthen the capacity to work with youth in the field of visual art and sustainability, using an interdisciplinary approach and continuous work with youth on the topics of environmental protection and sustainable development. By implementing the project, we responded to the needs of youth by providing more opportunities for youth with fewer opportunities (FO) in the field of visual art, nature protection, and sustainability, so that youth with FO would be more active and engaged in nature protection. Through the exchange of knowledge, experience, and good practices, POs ensured new and improved practices of working with youth and integrating new methods into their daily work.

<< Objectives >>

Main: Strengthen the capacities of partner organizations to work with young people in the fields of culture, art, sustainable development, and nature protection using an interdisciplinary approach, art therapy, and non-formal education methods. Specific: to increase the sense of initiative of youth with fewer opportunities by giving them the opportunity and supporting them to implement their ideas into works of art and for good causes through the exchange of knowledge and skills in the fields of visual arts, nature protection, and sustainability; to provide equal opportunities for youth with fewer opportunities to participate in the socio-cultural life of the community and increase social inclusion through continuous art workshops; to contribute to the development of youth work in rural areas, quality, and innovation, by strengthening the capacity of partner organizations in the fields of art therapy, visual art, sustainability, and nature protection. By exchanging knowledge, experience, and good practices in youth work on the topics of environmental protection and sustainable development using visual art as a tool and art therapy, the partners wanted to strengthen capacities to increase their quality and innovation in youth work.

<< Implementation >>

1. Kick-off conference to inform the target group about the start of implementation, context, activities, and networking of relevant stakeholders in the field of youth work; 2. Job shadowing to enable partner organizations to exchange knowledge and experience in the preparation and implementation of artistic and cultural activities, to transfer good practice in the organization of activities with and for young people (artists), and to ensure the introduction of new good practices in the work of partner organizations; 3. Art therapy education to develop the competencies of the staff of partner organizations and develop new innovative methods for youth work through the provision of basic knowledge about art therapy and practical work; 4. Local activities that provided youth with fewer opportunities equal opportunities to participate in the socio-cultural life of the community and social inclusion, and practical work for people who were shadowing the work of partner organizations and education about art therapy to use and practice newly acquired skills and knowledge. 5. A toolbox to raise the quality and innovation in work with young people. 6. Final conference to inform and test the tools and methods from the toolbox.

<< Results >>

The Kick-off conference was held in Zadar and Camara de Lobos, attended by a total of 29 people.
4 people participated in the job shadowing in Zadar and Camara de Lobos (partner organizations) and developed knowledge and skills.
Held education about art therapy in Veli Iž, where 10 people participated and increased knowledge about art therapy, work methods, basic principles, art therapy theoretical models, different types of creative techniques in art therapy.
A total of 31 art workshops were held in Zadar, Gračac and Camara de Lobos, in which 64 young people with fewer opportunities participated.
10 recycled artworks developed.
2 street art exhibitions were held in Zadar and Camara de Lobos.
Developed Toolbox: A Creative Learning Environment for Environmental Protection.
The final conference was held in Zadar, Veli Iž, and Camara de Lobos, attended by 36 people.
Tested tools from the "Toolbox"
The general public was sensitized about the importance of nature conservation and encouraged to recycle.
Increased staff knowledge and capacities of partner organizations in the field of art therapy and the organization and implementation of art activities with and for young people on topics related to nature protection and sustainability.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

hr.name: Udruga za poticanje razvoja ljudskih potencijala i kreativnosti - Prizma

2021-2-HR01-KA210-YOU-000049418.title: Step Forward Effective Projects
2021-2-HR01-KA210-YOU-000049418.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was designed in partnership with the Portuguese org. Agoraveiro, with whom we previously had partnerships on Erasmus+ projects and informal cooperation in various activities. We detected the problems we face, our own weaknesses and strengths, and areas in which we can learn from each other and achieve positive changes in our communities - this primarily refers to work with youngsters, similarities and differences in the ways of involving volunteers, improving our own way of work guided by the experience and good practices of the partner org. The field of work overlaps with working with young people on active participation, and the problems in local communities are similar (discrimination, exclusivity, similar youth unemployment rates, difficulties related to the pandemic - inability to perform regular activities, mental health problems, stress, increased anxiety). Mentor's most expressed needs were structuring and improvement of work with volunteers, and Agoraveiro's improvement of communication skills and coping with stress of volunteers and employees. We responded to these through a series of live and online activities - exercises, role-playing games, discussions, actions in the local community, sharing materials.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of the project was to contribute to the participation of young people in democratic life by strengthening the capacity of partner organizations to implement quality volunteer programs and more efficiently encourage young people to become active citizens. With the project, we wanted to enable people who work with young people, as well as young people themselves, to acquire new knowledge and develop skills, to connect with young people from other local communities, to recognize and become aware of the problems that communities face, and to come up with constructive and effective solutions together.

<< Implementation >>

The project consisted of the following activities:
A1 - Kick-off meeting with the aim of agreeing and creating a detailed plan for the implementation of project activities, held in Split in April 2022, attended by 4 people - employees of the organizations Agoraveiro and Mentor.
A2 - Training "Volunteer - mentor" with the aim of familiarizing participants with the work of two organizations, development of fundamental competencies, held in Split in July 2022, 12 young people from both organizations participated.
A3 - Work group for the creation of a volunteer involvement strategy, held in Aveiro, Portugal in September 2022, 12 young people participated.
A4 - Online activities with the aim of monitoring project implementation, additional connecting of participants and strengthening of transversal skills, held from August 2022 to April 2023, attended by 14 employees and volunteers of two organizations
A5 - Final evaluation meeting with the aim of evaluating the project, held in Aveiro, Portugal, in June 2023, attended by 9 employees and volunteers of two organizations.


<< Results >>

14 employees and volunteers of two organizations participated in the project activities. Through the "Volunteer-mentor" training, the participants got to know the work of two orgs and the way to involve volunteers, through a series of exercises they strengthened the social and emotional skills necessary for active participation (communication skills, assertiveness, empathy), created a "volunteer-mentor" profile and defined the skills needed to perform this role. Then, as part of the working group, they laid the foundations for the development strategy of the volunteer program of Mentor (which they elaborated and implemented in detail in the coming months), but they also got to know the work of the partner organization in more detail, practiced communication and presentation skills, planning and organizing projects. Additionally, a workshop on stress and burn-out was held, as a complement to the activities held online. Through online activities, participants identified their own stressors and assessed their stress level, adopted different coping techniques, supported each other, and planned joint and local activities. Both organizations held activities in the local community related to the project's topics (free hugs, workshops).

2021-2-HR01-KA210-YOU-000049952.title: I Contribute to Sustainable Tourism and Search for Ways to Travel Better
2021-2-HR01-KA210-YOU-000049952.summary:
<< Background >>

We have addressed two types of needs: our own institutional ones and the needs of the young people active in our organizations. On this particular project, these two types of needs have found a common intersection in the fields of environmental protection and sustainable economic development, in particular sustainable travel and tourism. Our trainers have been increasingly feeling insufficiently knowledgeable about environmental and climate change topics, and have looked for opportunities to increase  our institutional knowledge and capacities in order to be able to respond to the demand by young people to explore the topic. We also share with our young participants the concern for the future raised by the now visible impact our behavior has on the environment.  We have thus applied for the project in order to increase our capacities to understand the environmental and climate changes taking place in the world in order to be able to effectively engage with young people and activate them to trigger changes in their own behavior and in their societies and communities. As the topics covered by the project are global, an international approach was needed and Erasmus+ presented an excellent opportunity to work cross-nationally.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we have hoped to achieve two objectives: 1. to build up the capacities of our organizations to understand and address the environmental crisis caused by human behavior, specifically by modern travel practices, and 2. to empower young people to take action by asking questions, building a healthier and more sustainable relationship with the environment, and acting as a factor of change by encouraging other members of their generation to engage in more environmentally-friendly travel practices and in more creative forms of civic activism. We wanted to build our institutional capacities for work with young people on challenging topics (in particular environmental protection), to empower them to think critically and to engage with their communities, and to start building partnerships across Europe for work on common projects. Because of the profile and interests of our trainers, we were also very keen on exploring the themes of environmental protection and fight against climate change by encouraging active citizenship and civic engagement on environmental topics, and promoting alternative forms of participation through artistic expression. 

<< Implementation >>

The project envisioned the implementation of 5 activities and we completed successfully and on time all of them. The implemented activities were:
A1. Training-for-trainers and exchange of expertise on environmental protection, sustainable tourism and youth activism.
We had training by guest lecturers from outside of our organizations and expertise exchange for the 4 members of the project team.
A2. Summer retreat for young people.
A 7-day summer retreat for 12 young people (6 from Croatia and 6 from Belgium) was organized in Šibenik, Croatia. 4 mentors/trainers (2 from each partner institution) also participated in & delivered training at the retreat.
A3. Production of a Sustainable Travel Video Guide for Young Travelers.
The 12 young people participating in the summer retreat created a video guide  available on YouTube which consisted of 4 chapters.
A4. Multiplier events.
Multiplier events turned out very popular and we exceeded the number of implemented events. We organized 6 presentations of the project in secondary schools (3 in each country) instead of the planned 4.
A5. Transnational project team meetings.
3 transnational project team meetings (start-up, interim and final) of the 4-person project team have taken place online

<< Results >>

We achieved all planned results and created all planned outputs as listed in our project proposal. Namely: 
 • 4 of our trainers increased their knowledge and built skills needed to educate young people about environmental sustainability and to trigger behavioral change in them by participating in training and exchange of expertise, 
• 12 young people, 18-25 years of age, learned about sustainable development and environmentally-friendly travel practices participating in a summer retreat in Šibenik, Croatia,
• Awareness of the effects of travel on the environment in tourist areas was raised by creating a Sustainable Travel Guide for Young Travelers in video format. It consists of 4 chapters, has been created by the 12 young participants in the summer retreat, and uploaded and disseminated on YouTube, on Facebook, and to the Erasmus+ community. 
• Awareness about sustainable travel was raised in 112 young people (near 3 times the planned number) aged 14 - 19 (secondary school pupils) through 6 peer lectures/multiplier events. Half of the events (3) took place outside of the capitals or in less developed areas.
- Our 2 partner institutions' capacities to work with young people in the area of environmental protection were increased.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

hr.name: Međunarodni centar za umjetnost / International Arts Centre

2021-2-HR01-KA210-YOU-000050577.title: Glasovi mladih za društvene promjene
2021-2-HR01-KA210-YOU-000050577.summary:
<< Background >>

Partner organisations Pride Parade Association and LORI focus on advancing and protecting human rights of LGBTI+ persons. That includes working for the youth (workshops, trainings etc.), with and by the youth (public actions, campaigns…), with the emphasis on LGBTI+ young persons who often engage in various activities mostly as volunteers and beneficiaries. Both organisations have recognised the need to strengthen their capacities and increase quality of their work with LGBTI+ youth. Specifically, partners identified the need to build their capacities by educating and empowering LGBTI+ youth for active civic engagement, so that they would be more equipped to partake in various partner organisations’ activities. With this project we ensured space for them to increase their knowledge and skills in the field of understanding and protecting LGBTI human rights, the opportunity for personal and professional growth through education, exchanging experiences and connecting with other young LGBTI+ people, as well as for implementing concrete actions. Mutual learning and study visits among organisations increase their capacities in empowering and providing psychosocial support to LGBTI+ youth, community organising and youth work.

<< Objectives >>

The main project objective was to strengthen the capacities of partner organisations in youth work and to increase knowledge and skills of LGBTI+ youth for active civic engagement. With this project our desire was: 1. To exchange good practices and to improve the knowledge and skills of youth workers in partner organisations, 2. To empower and to educate LGBTI+ youth for active civic engagement and 3. To increase the capacity of organisations by engaging LGBTI+ youth in their work. The needs assessment showed that LGBTI+ youth often lack empowerment and networking to be the initiators of change and engage more actively in creating social changes. In the long-term, educating and empowering young LGBTI+ persons, engaging them in activities, all strengthen organisations' capacity development. Additionally, by exchanging good practises, experiences and knowledge, partner organisations aspired to build their capacity in 1. youth work and methodology of working with LGBTI+ youth and 2. empowering and providing psychosocial support to LGBTI+ youth.

<< Implementation >>

The main project activities were: 1. Study visit from LORI to Pride Parade Association (aimed at increasing LORI strengths in terms of youth work), 2. Study visit from Pride Parade Association to LORI (aimed at enhancing their capacities for providing psychosocial support for LGBTI+ youth and working on reducing LGBTIQ-phobia in education, 3. Training course for LGBTI+ youth on Human rights of LGBTI+ persons and active citizenship, 4. Study visit of LORI Youth Group to the Youth Group in Slovenia (PRIDE Connects), 4. Developing digital resources aimed at empowering LGBTI+ youth, 6. Implementation of one joint action of LORI and PPA youth groups in Rijeka, Croatia and 7. Project management.

<< Results >>

The main project results are: 1. Enhanced knowledge of youth workers on engaging the youth in active civic engagement (three persons from LORI), 2. Increased knowledge of youth workers on providing psychosocial support to LGBTI+ youth and combatting LGBTIQ-phobia in educational system (three persons from Pride Parade Association), 3. 12 LGBTI+ young persons from Croatia and Slovenia educated on LGBTI human rights and active citizenship through 5-day training (seven from Croatia and five from Slovenia), 4. Five LORI youth group members gained insight into good practices in community organising for LGBTI+ youth on study visit to Pride Parade Association youth, 5. 16 LGBTI+ young persons from Croatia and Slovenia engaged in organising one joint activity in Rijeka, 6. One action of informing the public about the position of LGBTI+ youth implemented by Croatian and Slovenian youth, 7. Four digital resources aimed at empowering LGBTI+ youth created.

2021-2-IT03-KA210-YOU-000045090.title: Cooperation for social inclusion of the visually impaired youth through mindful art therapy
2021-2-IT03-KA210-YOU-000045090.summary:
<< Background >>

In Europa, circa 30 milioni di persone con disabilità visiva affrontano ostacoli significativi, come il supporto inadeguato, l'accessibilità limitata, i pregiudizi sociali e la disoccupazione, che spesso portano all'isolamento. Il progetto ha coinvolto organizzazioni e operatori giovanili soddisfando i bisogni di apprendimento in riferimento alla mancanza di competenza per lavorare in maniera adeguata con i giovani con disabilità e disabilità visive, promuovendo il benessere di questi ultimi e migliorando anche le competenze dello staff in chiave europea.  
L'organizzazione italiana ha rafforzato le sue partnership nell'UE per innovare attività basate sulla mindfulness, mentre l'organizzazione croata ha acquisito nuovi strumenti e metodi per assistere i giovani con disabilità visiva. Prosvasi ha inoltre capitalizzato sulle opportunità di sviluppo professionale a livello europeo.
Il progetto ha introdotto una nuova metodologia, basata ull’arteterapia e le pratiche mindfulness, promuovendo un'educazione inclusiva per giovani con disabilità e disabilità visive  favorendo la diversità e l'uguaglianza.


<< Objectives >>

Attraverso l'implementazione del progetto, abbiamo raggiunto diversi obiettivi chiave:
- Abbiamo instaurato e promosso la collaborazione transnazionale tra diverse organizzazioni, facilitando lo scambio di conoscenze, informazioni e risorse. Questo ha notevolmente migliorato l'innovazione nel lavoro giovanile destinato a persone con disabilità visive.

- Abbiamo promosso l'avanzamento delle metodologie di Educazione Non Formale (NFE) che mirano a rafforzare l'inclusione, l'equità, la creatività, la diversità e l'innovazione nell'istruzione, nella formazione e nello sviluppo giovanile. In particolare, abbiamo introdotto l'utilizzo di metodologie innovative come l'arteterapia basata sulla mindfulness, specificamente adattata per i giovani con disabilità visive.


<< Implementation >>

ll progetto ha implementato:
Project Management (A1)  ha garantito una fluida attuazione del piano di lavoro, rispettando gli standard Erasmus+ e le fasi preposte nella proposta progettuale.
Quality Management, Research Validity, and Evaluation of Content (A2)  ha mirato a mantenere la qualità e la coerenza dei processi e dei risultati del progetto durante tutta la sua durata. PROSVASI ha preso in carico la supervisione dell'implementazione delle attività del progetto per garantire il rispetto degli standard di qualità.
E-book/Audiolibro "Mindful Art Therapy for Youth with Visual Impairments: A Methodological Guidebook" (A3) ha posto le basi per il raggiungimento degli obiettivi del progetto presentando buone pratiche nel lavoro giovanile con giovani non vedenti. L'e-book ha fornito risultati di ricerca e attività innovative di ENF basate sull'arteterapia e mindfulness, sia il manuale che l'audiobook si possono scaricare in inglese, croato, italiano e greco.
A4: Dissemination and Exploitation (A4) si è concentrata sulla massimizzazione dell'impatto della disseminazione attraverso una strategia dettagliata. CABPS ha coordinato quest’attività, assicurando l'aderenza alle linee guida e il monitoraggio.

<< Results >>

Le attività di questo progetto, attraverso la ricerca scientifica, l'inclusione dei migliori esempi di buone pratiche nei paesi partner (e in generale in Europa) e lo sviluppo di una serie di attività ad hoc, approfonditamente analizzate e sviluppate nei dettagli,   hanno portato alla creazione di una guida metodologica appositamente progettata.
Sviluppate in entrambi i formati, ebook e audiolibro, queste guide introducono un approccio innovativo al lavoro giovanile. Questo approccio combina armoniosamente i poteri trasformativi dell'arteterapia e della filosofia della mindfulness con le metodologie di apprendimento non formale. Specificamente progettate per i giovani con disabilità visive, queste risorse offrono un quadro pionieristico per migliorare il loro sviluppo personale e il benessere dei giovani con disabilità e disabilità visiva, includendo per esempio delle pratiche  mindfulness condotte con un linguaggio adatto e adeguato per persone con difficoltà visive.

2021-2-IT03-KA210-YOU-000049345.title: VIV (Volunteering Inspired by Values)
2021-2-IT03-KA210-YOU-000049345.summary:
<< Background >>

The motivation for this project was rooted in the aspiration for an open, democratic and vibrant society based on the active participation and volunteer engagement and VIV project vision to bring new insights, prospective and means for strengthening the impact on volunteering on the inclusion, diversity, tolerance, solidarity and European rights and values. 
Over the last two decades, volunteering has progressively gained in importance around the world but it’s not recognise yet its role in the promotion of civic participation, social inclusion, strengthening of values therefore there was the need of volunteer programmes that could bring more dialogue, inclusion, diversity, tolerance, solidarity and European values into the life of the community
At the same time not all the organizations were aware of the fact that times are changing and with them also the priorities of the volunteers, especially when we talk about young people and so it was necessary to make them reflect upon new strategies to enage new volunteers.



<< Objectives >>

The project objectives were focused on creating a partnership that combined and merged different expertise in the field of youth, volunteering and values, putting an emphasis on capacity building of target groups and participating organisations in regards to leadership competencies that contribute to raising the impact of volunteer programmes to be more responsive to the actual trends/challenges.
In particular project VIV aimed to: 
1. Raise the impact of volunteer programmes in the context of fostering inclusion, diversity, tolerance, solidarity and European values; 
2. Increase the quality of work and practice of volunteer involving organisations opening to new trends and strategies for more value based volunteering; 
3. Strengthen value based leadership competences and tools in creating and leading volunteer programmes for youth; 
4. Strengthen transnational cooperation in evidence based practice, creating  inspiring and enabling environment for youth volunteering.


<< Implementation >>

During the project four activities have been implemented:
1. Research study “Volunteering for More Value” conducted to highlight the current state of volunteering in line with values, giving concrete conclusions and directions for development of volunteering for more value. 
2. Volunteering for More Value booklet, with guidelines for volunteer involving organisations in raising the quality of their volunteer programmes in line with value-based approach, 
3. Educational curriculum: From Volunteer Management to Leadership to contribute to the transformation of volunteer managers to leaders capable to create/lead volunteer programmes responsive to actual trends/challenges 
4. Final event “Volunteering Inspired by Values” in Croatia in order to present the project achievements.


<< Results >>

- A research study was conducted to highlight the current state of volunteering. 98 organizations answered questionnaires and 63 youngsters took part in 6 focus groups.
- 300 copies of the booklet “Volunteering for More Value” were published, 100 in each partners’ language, with guidelines for volunteer involving organisations to raise the quality of their volunteer programmes. The booklet were distributed to 300 organizations, 100 for each partner countries. 
- 3 national dialogues were organized to discuss the contents of the booklet with volunteers 
- 9 good practice stories were collected in videos
- a volunteer diary was prepared and translated into the language of each partner to support the volunteering experience of young volunteers
- 300 copies of the diary, 100 in each language were printed and distributed
- The training: “From Volunteer Management to Leadership” was developed to give new competences to volunteer managers to prepare them for the new challenges of volunteering.
- The curriculum, 18 hours, was piloted involving 15 organizations in each country, 45 in total.
- A national conference “Volunteering Inspired by Values” was held in June in Zagreb, attended by 37 participants to present the project achievements.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2021-2-NL02-KA210-YOU-000047859.title: United in Diversity
2021-2-NL02-KA210-YOU-000047859.summary:
<< Background >>

The united in diversity small scale partnership project was conducted to specifically : 

Increase adult educators’ capacity to work and provide key tools for social cohesion, community empowerment, citizen participation and social inclusion to individuals from minority communities such as the African diaspora communities. 

The UID small scale strategic partnership project addressed and fostered equal opportunities and ensured the youth workers from Muevete Por Europa, Stichting Codine and Eutopia were active participants in the social life in their respective countries by combating negative social behaviours like suicide, self-harm, depression, loneliness and racism amongst their youth communities. 

The needs also addressed by the project were related to promoting equity and inclusion for participants from disadvantaged backgrounds and those with fewer opportunities compared to their peers amongst the participating organizations leading to a trickle down effect in their communities and countries at the end of the project.

<< Objectives >>

The UID project sought to capacitate staff from the participating organizations to develop competences and skills to address diversity and inclusion at the workplace and at the local community level.

 The major thrust was also to raise more awareness on promoting the inclusion of young people with fewer opportunities such as youth from minority groups, migrant communities and the African Diaspora in EU projects since there is a general lack of participation of migrant communities and minorities in youth projects.




<< Implementation >>

Stichting Cosine implemented  a Long-term mobility of youth workers in the form of a training workshop, whereby the youth participants from Croatia and Spain converged in Amsterdam, in Netherlands for a diversity and inclusion training. 

There was also a follow-up job shadowing in Sleen where the partner organizations attended and saw first hand how Stichting Codine works with young people from diverse communities in the implementation of its projects. 

There was also an online training course that was delivered to the youth workers from the partner organizations. This was delivered by Inercia digital given their background and experience in the ICT sector. 

The Short-Term Joint Staff Training Event aims to mobilize a total of 21 staff members for the full 7 days programme. The participants will be drawn from the participating partner organizations such as Inercia digital, Codine and MMEutopia. 

There was also the joint staff training conducted in Zagreb, Croatia with the main goals of  training partners’ staff on how to implement diversity and inclusion policies and programs in their youth work.

<< Results >>

The comprehensive diversity and inclusion short-term training program results provided concrete ways to engage in respectful and positive interactions in the workplace while reducing discrimination and prejudice based on factors such as gender, ethnicity, race, sexual orientation, age, religion, physical and mental ability, and socioeconomic status amongst the youth workers.

The project has led to the creation of a consortium of interconnected young people conscious about diversity and inclusion since the participants of all phases of the project have kept in contact and continuously share knowledge and resources on their activities and efforts to address diversity and inclusion at their community level.

There was also the raising of knowledge and key competences on working with contemporary virtual tools when working with young people from minority backgrounds in daily youth work.

There has also been networking and collaboration of amongst the partner organizations and concrete plans for implementation of follow-up projects building on the learning outcomes from the UID small scale partnership project.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2021-2-PL01-KA210-YOU-000048038.title: Locally across boarders
2021-2-PL01-KA210-YOU-000048038.summary:
<< Background >>

We recognize the critical importance of addressing the social challenges exacerbated by the pandemic, especially concerning young people. Several reports showed alarming trends such as decreased social commitment, emotional distress among youth, and limited opportunities for volunteering and civic engagement. These issues directly impact the wellbeing and development of our communities.
The needs address through this project included: 
Youth Isolation and Emotional Wellbeing- the pandemic has led to increased emotional problems among young people, with limited social contact and excessive screen time affecting their mental health.
Decline in Volunteering and Civic Engagement:- the decrease in volunteering opportunities has weakened community ties and civic participation, leaving young people with fewer avenues to contribute
Lack of International and Interpersonal Connections - young people need opportunities to build global connections, collaborate with peers, and engage in meaningful civic activities to foster personal growth and community development. 
Skill Development and Confidence Building - engaging in civic projects empowers young people by teaching them valuable skills, boosting confidence, and demonstrating

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the project were linked to the civic involvement, participation and common values. It encourages young people from PL, HR, IT together with their teaches/educators to civic engagement on the local and international level and in the same time how to learn through it. It teaches them to see social problems, to look for solutions and to implement them. The project enables young people to participate in democratic, social and civic life in an effective way. 
Our achevement was to gather and form youth teams, trained them and give them possibilities to grow and act for local community, using innovative and useful methodology of service learning. Paralelly we worked with proffesionals with different backgrounds (cultural NGO, social NGO, schools, public institution) in order to show them new method and prepare them to work within this method.

Young people got to know their peers from other countries, learnt about the social issues from their local communities, shared the knowledge and good practices from their societies and they cooperated together to solve several local problems. They also strengthened their social and intercultural competences and critical thinking. 

<< Implementation >>

- we established and supported 12 national volunteering projects according to service learning methodology (prepared, organised and realised in cooperation by young volunteers from 3 partner countries under supervision of trained youth workers),
- wrote 1 booklet about how to implement youth initiatives with service learning dedicated to youth workers, educators, teachers and volunteer coordinators. It has been transleted into polish, italian, croatian and english.
- wrote 1 booklet for young volunteer leaders’ guide which which contain tips for work with Service Learning and how to stay motivated during the whole process of the project's realisation. It has been transleted into polish, italian, croatian and english.
- 1 online event (conference) at the end of the project with a presentation of completed youth projects and their output, good practices and experiences from international cooperation,
- 3 transnational meetings connected with trainings for young people and youth workers
- 3 national trainings for mentors of the youth projects.
- more than 20 partner meetings online

<< Results >>

- 88 young people from Croatia, Italy and Poland worked on their initiatives
- 12 youth workers learnt and found out about service-learning methodology and increased their knowledge
- 142 numbers of registrated participants on our online conference about service learning methodology
- 12 youth workes increased their knowledge about service learning and e-volunteering
- 1 booklet about steps in service learning for young people - a comperhensive guidelines for youth in English, Polish, Croatian and Italian
- 1 booklet about service learning methodology for trainers/educators/youth workers in English, Polish, Croatian and Italian
- thanks to the project, our organisations started to organise international youth projects and cooperate with young volunteers from different countries.
- SCW became more recognizable as a service learning experts within polish educators and youth workers
- SCW established strong cooperation with 4 new local organizations
- VSP.odv established strong cooperation with Liceo Berti and wants to continue promoting service learnig methodology
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

hr.name: Udruga za razvoj civilnog drustva SMART

2021-2-SE02-KA210-YOU-000048602.title: Laboure HotSpot
2021-2-SE02-KA210-YOU-000048602.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project in response to the complex challenges faced by European young people transitioning from education to employment. These issues lead to broader societal and economic problems, including a lack of trust in institutions and political disillusionment. Youth organisations confront numerous obstacles in empowering and representing young people. Recognising these challenges, and considering EU initiatives like the European Solidarity Corps and EU Youth Strategy, we saw the need for direct involvement of youth in shaping solutions. Our project aims to unify diverse youth voices and share best practices across Europe, creating equal opportunities for all. This initiative is crucial for improving young people's positioning in the employment market and empowering both individuals and youth organisations.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project, we aimed to build the transnational and cross-sectoral working capacities of NGOs active in youth work, particularly in the fields of employability, digital content technologies and practices, and new learning approaches. We contributed to the digitalization of the learning process by creating an e-learning platform, thereby enabling distance learning. By achieving the project goals, we contributed to the fulfillment of the objectives of the Erasmus + program.

<< Implementation >>

All activities were carried out in accordance with non-formal working methods. In addition to conducting transnational meetings, we held international training sessions for youth workers, developed a new learning program, and digitized the entire process. These activities were carried out in parallel in all the countries involved in this project, at both the local and international levels.

<< Results >>

The project successfully created a guidebook that systematized, in one place, all the obstacles existing in society that prevent young people from accessing the labor market. This guidebook contained new methods and approaches for youth workers who work with young people with fewer opportunities. Additionally, the project developed a digital platform that now enables distance learning for all stakeholders in the field of youth inclusion in the labor market.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

hr.name: UDRUGA ZA PROMICANJE AKTIVNOG SUDJELOVANJA STUDIO B

2021-2-SE02-KA210-YOU-000048641.title: New learning systems for environment protection
2021-2-SE02-KA210-YOU-000048641.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied to address pressing EU environmental issues. Aligned with the EU's 2019-2024 green focus and the 2021-2027 climate action emphasis, our goal was to raise waste management awareness, given the rising waste in states like Croatia and Sweden from 1995-2019. Misunderstandings persisted about waste treatments; Eurostat data showed waste incineration increased by 30 million tonnes between 1995 and 2019.

Furthermore, we aimed to boost youth civic engagement. Notable disparities existed in youth volunteering across Sweden, Croatia, and Germany. We sought to introduce sustainable approaches like 3R and C2C, promoting growth and jobs.

Finally, enhancing collaboration between local entities and youth in environmental endeavors was pivotal, demanding innovative strategies in waste management and protection.

<< Objectives >>

Our project had several objectives:
Elevate youth awareness about EU-stressed environmental challenges.
Boost youth volunteering in environmental protection across three countries.
Strengthen partner organizations for local collaboration and environmental risk mitigation.
Localize European waste management insights, reflecting national and EU laws.
Offer inclusive environmental tools for disadvantaged youth.

To fulfill these:
We crafted a learning system about waste, using EU and country-specific data.
Hosted trial training for 45 youths using our manual.
Readied youth workers from three partners for the training.
Created a digital directory of local waste management stakeholders.
All objectives align with our mission: spotlight environmental issues, emphasize youth engagement, and provide fresh strategies for waste management through robust training and collaboration.

<< Implementation >>

Throughout the project, we implemented several activities:
Kick-Off Meeting: Initiated our project's journey.
Creating Visions: Workshops to brainstorm sustainable local community ideas.
Digital Depository: Developed a platform to house shared resources.
Structured Dialogue: Discussions to foster local change.
New Learning System: Produced an innovative training manual.
Learning for Frontliners: A transnational exchange of best practices.
Youth Workers Academy: Training sessions for youth facilitators.
Performance Assessment Training: Evaluating new youth-focused methods.
Digital Multiplicator Event: An online event to amplify our impact.
These activities were integral in advancing our innovative training, shaping digital tools, and fostering best practice exchanges among partners.

<< Results >>

Throughout the project's duration, we achieved several significant outcomes:

Digital Depository for Local Youth Work: We established a comprehensive online platform to store and share vital resources tailored for youth engagement.
New Training Manual: In alignment with our dedication to environmental protection, we produced a detailed training manual that now serves as a guide for educators and activists.
Innovative Learning System: We launched an e-learning module specifically designed for frontliners, further strengthening our educational reach.
Strengthening Partner Organizations: Our concerted efforts ensured that collaborating organizations were better equipped to work with the youth in environmental protection.
Inclusive Participation Methods: Recognizing the importance of inclusivity, we crafted unique methods to ensure the active participation of young individuals with disabilities.
To foster an ethos of community sharing and to pave the way for future projects, all our results have been made publicly accessible as open resources for the broader EU community of youth workers.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2021-2-SI02-KA210-YOU-000049932.title: RadioAktivizem
2021-2-SI02-KA210-YOU-000049932.summary:
<< Background >>

Climate change is the biggest and most dire crisis of our age. At the same time, the problem cannot be addressed on just the national scale.
The "RadioAktivizem" project connected and engaged youth from three different countries (Slovenia, Croatia, Austria) through three partner organisations; they researched the topics of environmentalism and prepared a series of podcasts that addressed a wider, international young audience, educating them on the climate justice and done its part in preparing them to tackle the crisis we are facing.

RadioAktivizem is an international project, collaboration of three independent radio stations together with environmentalists, and has encouraged critical thinking in youth on the topic of environmentalism and climate change, trained them in media and radio work and emancipated them as the citizens of Europe.

The main goal of the project was the formation of international community of young radio workers and activists, engaged in the climate justice movement, through the means of the independent radio media.

<< Objectives >>

The main goals of the project were:
- formation of international youth radio community, addressing the local, regional, national and international level of climate justice subtopics,
- set-up of the digital platform for podcast distribution and inter-exchange of shows and materials in order to spread the reach of the audio content to a wider young radio audiences,
- engagement and education of 50 young radio workers through the audio workshops and work on the episodes (research, journalism work, moderation, technical aspect, production).

<< Implementation >>

During the project we facilitated the following activities:
- audio workshop organisation - studio recording and production workshops on all three radio stations,
- production of 36 podcasts on local-national subtopics of climate justice,
- 4 international partner meetings with production of 4 partner episodes of podcasts,
- set-up of online platform for publishing and distribution of podcasts,
- emmission of all 40 episodes on each of the partner radio stations (Radio MARŠ - Maribor, Slovenia; Radio Student - Zagreb, Croatia; Radio Helsinki - Graz, Austria).

<< Results >>

Results of the RadioAktivizem project:
- 36 podcasts on local-national subtopics of climate justice (shared production of partner stations),
- 4 partner episodes,
- project website with all 40 episodes,
- emmision of all 40 episodes on each of the partner radio stations (120 emmissions - Radio MARŠ - Maribor, Slovenia; Radio Student - Zagreb, Croatia; Radio Helsinki - Graz, Austria)

hr.name: Udruga za razvoj medijske i gradanske kulture Radio Student

2021-2-SI02-KA210-YOU-000050499.title: Pozitivna izkušnja na prostem
2021-2-SI02-KA210-YOU-000050499.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project because we wanted to upgrade the knowledge of youth workers in the field of outdoor education, provide them with a healthy working environment and offer everyone involved opportunities to spend as much time as possible in nature or elswhere outdoor. In addition, we wanted to raise awareness in our local communities of the untapped potential for working with young people in nature and to contribute tested tools for transformative learning experiences to the common treasury of knowledge. The project represented an enrichment of our programs and a new opportunity for young people (even young people with fewer opportunities) both on an individual and group level. We offered them and the youth workers opportunities for active engagement, care for their physical and mental well-being, more movement, less contact with technology, outdoor activities instead of indoors, teamwork, initiative taking, care for nature. It was also important for us to get to know and connect with organizations that work with young people in nature, and to exchange knowledge with them.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to develop activities and tools for positive experiences of outdoor education, while also enabling the professionalization of youth workers and offering young people the opportunity for transformative and informal learning experiences that contributed to their personal growth. Our aim was also to implement methods from this field, to expand our knowledge in the local environment and to raise awareness of the (untapped) potential that this type of work brings to various organizations in our environment.

<< Implementation >>

The project activities were (1) introductory meeting in Slovenia, (2) implementation and testing of tools in local environments for young people with fewer opportunities and online meetings of partner organizations, (3) study visit to Croatia, (4) co-creation of online content with tools for outdoor education and its presentations in local environments, (5) final meeting in Italy where we evaluated the work done and talked about further plans.

<< Results >>

The results of the project are:
- trained and empowered youth workers for the outdoor education approach
- proven methods and tools for use in ours and transferable to other (local) organizations
- opportunities for young people (with fewer opportunities) and support for active participation in society
- consolidated partnership with a vision in which we connect internationally and operate locally
- knowledge for quality youth work in rural areas
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2022-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000080891.title: Fight fake news - Preserve mental health
2022-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000080891.summary:
<< Background >>

The information is crucial for communication, but it is simultaneously susceptible to misuse, leading to the spread of fake news. Social media, as a significant channel for information exchange, does not require source citation, making it challenging to establish the reliability of information. The problem is compounded by misinformation, negatively impacting people's mental health in terms of anxiety, depression, and fatigue. Since there is no unified approach to addressing the impact of fake news on mental health at the EU level, taking action within the local community provides the best foundation for disseminating positive results.The most effective approach has been the use of critical thinking and analysis, which is why planned activities would focus on strengthening critical thinking through innovative digital non-formal training.Partner organizations recognize that reaching young people is easiest through the internet. Therefore, working with young people to empower critical thinking should be based on innovative digital tools.NGO's are the best actors for primary community intervention, and they will disseminate the developed innovative tools and methods to their network of collaborators from other sector.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project, we aimed to establish collaboration with less experienced local organizations in Greece and Spain within a similar scope of activities.
