Our goal was to achieve an international dimension in our work and develop innovative non-formal education programs to involve a greater number of young people with fewer opportunities in the critical examination of news and content available on portals and social media.In this way, we sought to enhance the quality of the participating organizations' work with young people.The project aimed to strengthen the capacities of youth workers from organizations that have not participated or have limited experience in implementing international training.The objective was to enable them to promptly recognize the impact of fake news on the mental health of young users and equip them to constructively respond to the needs of young people with fewer opportunities.The project aimed to develop new digital tools focused on improving the quality of training for young people in recognizing the distinction between reality and media representation. It aimed to strengthen the capacities of participating and collaborating organizations in using innovative digital tools in future work.

<< Implementation >>

Through this project, transnational project meetings were conducted in Croatia, Greece, and Spain. Media literacy training was carried out in each participating country, and new non-formal methods were developed for representatives of collaborating organizations with the aim of preparing the development of a new training program. A non-formal training program on the topic "The Impact of Fake News on the Mental Health of Youth" was created, along with a manual for individual work on strengthening the mental health of disadvantaged youth. Accompanying digital tools were developed, including a digital manual, e-training program, quizzes to enhance critical thinking, and more. A training session for trainers was held, providing youth workers from participating organizations with the skills to implement the developed program with young people in their communities. The final activity involved the collaborating organizations working to disseminate the results achieved in the previous project activities. A database of supporting organizations was established, and efforts were made to expand the network of participating organizations with the goal of disseminating project results.

<< Results >>

1.Quality and innovative practices have been developed for working with youth with fewer opportunities in areas that correspond to the needs of the involved organizations and beyond
2.An international dimension of action has been realized among the participating organizations, facilitating the exchange of best practices
3.Active citizenship in the local community has been supported by incorporating a European dimension into the work of the involved organizations
4.The capacities of participating organizations to work with youth in the field of mental health have been strengthened through the development of new digital tools and training program
5.The transformation of the actions of the involved organizations from traditional to digital has been supported.
6.The NGO sector has been strengthened to operate in crisis situations and times of significant exposure of youth to fake news
7.Contributions have been made to preserving European values among youth susceptible to manipulative actions by anti-European actors
8.A non-formal education program Impact of Fake News on Mental Health has been developed along with a Manual for Individual Work on Strengthening and Protecting the Mental Health of Young People with Fewer Opportunities
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000081830.title: Including all persons for a Greener Future
2022-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000081830.summary:
<< Background >>

GREEN-IN focused on persons w/disabilities & young persons (esp. b/w 18-30 years of age).
In Varazdin County, HR & Cavriago, IT, there are >2400 persons w/disabilities. Many of them have down's syndrome, muscular dystrophy, and conditions that prevent them from being socially included. They are living with their families/parents. During COVID-19, they lacked access to support (e.g. physiotherapy, individual support, physical activities geared to their needs), had limited social interaction, and were at high risk of illness. The pandemic also impacted young persons’ mental well-being. 1/3 young persons doubt that they can find work in sectors they are trained in and lack opportunities to participate in local actions. There was growing demand for persons in medical & social care fields, as the pandemic (& post-pandemic period) required skilled persons to assist the most vulnerable. Also, environmental protection was considered (due to climate change & the need to reduce pollution) as there had not been local events that included persons w/disabilities in such activities. Via an approach based on these needs, the project resulted in new support for persons w/disabilities, and young persons gained new skills in line w/market trends.

<< Objectives >>

The overall aim of the project was to enhance the inclusion of persons with disabilities in the community by including youth in the actions of non-profits. The specific project aim was to enhance the capacity of young persons as active citizens to support persons w/disabilities in their efforts to be socially included in the wider community.  By achieving these aims, the partnership has been able to contribute to efforts in EU communities to create conditions that contribute to social inclusion in communities.  Specifically, the aims were prepared in a way so that the project directly contributed to enhancing access to (social, community) services for persons with disabilities (esp. youth), and promoting/encouraging young persons to participate in local actions. The project approach (which included training, workshop, and nature-based actions targeting young volunteers and persons with disabilities) built the capacities of young persons (5 in Croatia, 6 in Italy) to assist persons with disabilities. This in turn contributes to not only activating young persons to engage in locally based actions over the long-term, but also to supporting persons with disabilities to live more independently and with dignity in their communities. 

<< Implementation >>

The project activities were: 1) Preparation and selection of candidates: The activities were organized in a manner to identify and confirm young volunteers in the project. The project targeted young persons b/w the ages of 18-30 from Croatia (HR) and Italy (IT) who wanted to contribute to the social inclusion of persons w/disabilities. 5 participants from Croatia and 6 from Italy were selected; 2) Setting up the training programme for young volunteers: This included organizing focus groups in HR and IT (3 focus group meetings in HR and 2 in IT – inputs received from 43 stakeholders); 1 training programme focusing on young volunteers; 1 volunteer guidebook; 3) Organizing workshops & training:  This included in-situ training for volunteers in Croatia and Italy & 2 workshops (1 in HR & 1 in IT) that brought together target groups from both countries to share best practices & gain capacities;  4) Organizing nature based-actions (re: environmental protection) in Cestica and Cavriago; 2 events with IT and HR participants ; 5) Evaluation & monitoring: via collecting feedback from participants per event and an evaluation report 6) the Final conference (in Cestica) & project sustainability (developing a long-term cooperation agreement).

<< Results >>

The results were: 1) 1 training methodology aligned to young volunteers (& that could be for other professionals) so they can work with and support persons w/disabilities. This included the development of the training programme and implementing it via workshops and in-situ training in each country; 2) 11 young volunteers (5 from HR & 6 from IT) trained via 2 workshops, in-situ training (30 hrs in HR & 30 hrs in IT based on the training programme) in each country and nature-based actions; 3) 1 innovative concept re: environmental protection tested & evaluated: This result was achieved via the Nature-based actions in Cestica, HR & Cavriago, IT:  This concept contributed to promoting social inclusion in environmental protection actions. By having young persons/volunteers from HR & IT participate, they had the opportunity to learn how to support persons w/disabilities to take part in such actions and about the benefits of volunteering in their communities; 4) Long-term cooperation agreement b/w partners & new projects:  The partnership concluded a cooperation agreement at the final conference in Cestica. The agreement includes a description of a new project for ERASMUS+ KA220, which expands on these project results.

hr.name: Zivot i Radost, udruga za djecu s teskocama i osobe s invalidetom

2022-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000082521.title: Zeleno educiraj, društveno profitiraj!
2022-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000082521.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project "Educate green, socially intervene!" to address the growing needs of young people for education in the fields of social entrepreneurship and environmental sustainability. Our analysis showed that many young people face challenges in finding employment and often lack the necessary skills and knowledge to launch their own entrepreneurial initiatives, especially in the field of environmental sustainability. This project aims to enhance the capacities of partner organizations to provide education that will enable young people to develop their ideas, become active participants in their communities, and engage in creating more sustainable solutions. Additionally, we want to address the issue of social exclusion, with a particular focus on including young people with fewer opportunities who often find themselves on the margins of society. Our goal is to create a supportive environment that fosters innovation and promotes the values of social responsibility.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of the project "Educate green, socially intervene!" was to strengthen the capacities of partner organizations in providing educational activities focused on social entrepreneurship, particularly in the context of environmental sustainability. We aimed to encourage young people to develop entrepreneurial skills and initiatives that are environmentally conscious and socially responsible. Through the project, we also hoped to increase the involvement of young people with fewer opportunities, enabling them to access resources and knowledge that would help them integrate into society. This would contribute to improving their life prospects and reducing social exclusion. Additionally, through the implementation of the project, we spursued to promote the values of innovation, sustainability, and community, thereby creating a foundation for future activities that will support the development of local communities and social entrepreneurship.

<< Implementation >>

Within the framework of the project "Educate green, socially intervene!", numerous activities were carried out with the aim of empowering young people and the staff of partner organizations. We conducted training sessions for the staff on the concepts of social and green entrepreneurship, which included theoretical foundations, practical examples, and innovative working methods. Based on these training sessions, two educational modules were developed, which will serve as a foundation for future youth training. Additionally, a comprehensive guide was created that contains all relevant information about social entrepreneurship, and a project website was established to serve as a resource for young people. The first pilot training for youth was held as part of the project and included interactive workshops and group activities. Furthermore, we carried out dissemination activities through social media and local media, which increased the project's visibility and ensured the engagement of the local community. Additionally, dissemination activities were carried out in the local communities of both partner organizations (a green forum and a green lunch).

<< Results >>

The project "Educate green, socially intervene!" resulted in significant achievements. A group of young people, including those with fewer opportunities, was educated and gained the knowledge and skills necessary to develop their own business ideas in the field of social entrepreneurship. A Guide containing important information and resources was created, along with a project website that will continue to serve as a valuable tool for future participants. Additionally, the visibility and recognition of partner organizations within local communities were increased, opening up new opportunities for collaboration and networking. New partnerships were established that will facilitate the further development of social entrepreneurship, while participants in the pilot training gained useful contacts and inspiration for their future projects. In this way, the project contributed to strengthening social cohesion and promoting sustainable business practices.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2022-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000083117.title: More than sport
2022-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000083117.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we had realized that organisations we collaborate with, are using sports as a tool for inclusion and personal growth, but they didn't know exactly how to leverage it to improve social skills and empower youngsters with fewer opportunities. In our work we have seen how sports could help their work. This project was our chance to create a program that would show organizations how to use sports effectively. Our surveys had found that while people knew sports were powerful, they didn't know how to use them well. We wanted to fix that by working together and giving organizations the right tools.   

We addressed the need for structured programs by combining Amazonas' experience in using sports for social skills with Empoderar's expertise in psychosocial programs. Our research found a desire among local organizations to learn how to use sports as empowerment tools for disadvantaged youth. Previous evaluations showed sports' effectiveness in personal development. With over 88.1% of respondents reporting improved quality of life, our structured program empowered organizations to reach more youth with fewer opportunities.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project we created structured program for organisations working with youngsters with fewer opportunities in order to encourage their personal development and sustainable social transformation.

Other specific objectives we have achieved are: 
1. Systematic methodology for engaging young migrants and youth from economically disadvantaged backgrounds through sports and physical activities is developed.
2 Widely available programme for empowering young migrants and youngsters with poor socio - economical
background troughs sport and physical activity is created.

With implementation of this objectives, we provided practical frameworks and resources that organizations can now utilize to effectively support and empower youth with fewer opportunities, and ultimately contributing to their holistic development and integration into society by using sport.

<< Implementation >>

In our project we have implemented following activities:

1.  Kick off meeting which was consisted of preparation of project in general, partner agreements.
2.  Creation of workshops consisted work on theoretical framework and workshops content.
3.  Partner meetings on which we were discussing all stages of project.
4.  Testing workshops with youngsters with fewer opportunities in both partners organisations in which 57 youngsters in both organisations participated.
5. Manual creation consisted creation of content, translation to Croatian, English and Portuguese and dissemination of one, by both of partners. 55 organisations were directly informed about the manual and project.
6. Training for trainers was held in Croatia and organised by Amazonas that empowered 23 youth workers to use created programme by this project.
7. Project management that was consisted through all the project and was agreed on first kick-off meeting between organisations on agreed document - delivery on time, budget planning and distribution and dissemination and evaluation activities of project. 


<< Results >>

The outcomes of our project include:

1. Systematized programme "More than sport" in a form of manual which is widely available to organizations working with youth with fewer opportunities is created. On Amazonas and Empoderar's websites it is available on English, Croatian and Portuguese and free to download.

2. Manual as a core of programme consist 10 lessons with workshops which aim is to empower youngsters with fewer opportunities using sport and physical activity as a tool. The evaluation impact has shown the increase on the perception of development of the skills and positive impact on their self-esteem.

3. 5 youth workers from partner organization Empoderar and 18 youth workers from Croatian organizations that do not participate directly in the project, but collaborate with Amazonas, are educated how to use materials created by project in activity training for trainers. 

4. 55 organizations in Portugal and Croatia participating in project are directly informed about project results and they received manual created by project. They were in informed in five dissemination activities, one live in Portugal and one online event, and in Croatia one live event (conference) and two online events for Croatian organisations

2022-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000084840.title: Survivorska inicijativa
2022-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000084840.summary:
<< Background >>

In order to raise the capacities of youth workers for active participation in the activities of organizations to help children and young people undergoing treatment for malignant disease and after treatment. This group of users is sensitive and they go through difficult treatments, malignant diseases are rare and there are not many people with that experience to be able to support them. In online meetings before the start of the project, organizations' needs were analyzed and it was confirmed that children undergoing treatment in Skopje do not receive adequate support, that SANO has a problem gathering young people with experience in the treatment of malignant diseases, and Krijesnica, which has a group of young people for 10 years, has a problem with by maintaining their group because the members are a specific group.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project was to strengthen the capacity of partner organizations to provide assistance and support to children and young people facing malignant diseases. It was necessary to transfer knowledge and experience from Krijesnica to SANO and their youth workers, and to encourage and increase the motivation of Krijesnica youth workers in order to provide mutual peer support and help children and young people in treatment.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were carried out:
- Preparatory visit to SANO in order to monitor their work by Krijesnica and analyze their capacities and decide which support program is suitable for implementation in Macedonia by SANO
- The arrival of SANO youth workers in Zagreb in order to monitor the work of Krijesnica and their improvement of the competences and capacities of organizations
- Creating a manual for gathering and maintaining a group of young people treated for malignant diseases
- Testing the program of providing support to children and young people after treatment

<< Results >>

The results of the activities carried out, which are satisfactory for both organizations, are: 6 people participated in monitoring the work of the organizations and their competences and experience were raised, a manual was created for gathering and maintaining a group of young people treated for malignant diseases, a support program was created for children undergoing treatment in Skopje, which SANO's youth workers will implement, a multilingual brochure with SANO's activities was created, the support program in Macedonia was successfully tested, the activities and interest of the Mladi Krijesnice group increased, the capacities and experience of the staff of both organizations increased.

2022-1-MK01-KA210-YOU-000083607.title: The United Wellness Project
2022-1-MK01-KA210-YOU-000083607.summary:
<< Background >>

As a group of young resident doctors, we recognize the health challenges in North Macedonia, including the factors contributing to chronic diseases. Research highlights the impact of early deaths and healthcare costs due to preventable conditions. To address this, we launched the United Wellness Project, focusing on educating youth across our nation about three key pillars of wellness: sleep, nutrition, and physical activity. These factors play a crucial role in disease prevention and overall health enhancement. Our project aimed to empower young individuals to make informed health choices, ensuring they lead fulfilling lives to their fullest potential. Insights into childhood obesity and nutrition have further shaped our project's core principles. The need for increasing health literacy and health culture was the main leading factor in the project’s creation.

<< Objectives >>

Our project aimed to raise awareness among young individuals in our country and partner nations about the importance of holistic well-being. Leveraging social media, the internet, and in-person workshops, we tailored our approach to resonate with each generation. Our empowered students became ambassadors, contributing to our objectives of establishing online resources for widespread access. Additionally, we sought to initiate dialogues with policy makers, school administrators, and ministries in North Macedonia, specifically addressing the nutritional offerings in student dorms and kitchens. Armed with the scientific evidence gathered through the project, as well as insights from the practical workshops and meetings, our approach aimed to introduce evidence-based strategies into these discussions.

<< Implementation >>

The United Wellness Project encompassed a diverse array of activities, successfully executing all proposed endeavors outlined in the initial project proposal. Our journey began with a comprehensive research survey spanning North Macedonia, Croatia, and France, elucidating the attitudes and connections young individuals hold toward the three facets of wellness. Concurrently, we diligently established a trilingual project website, housing a wealth of resources, articles, BMI calculators, and nutritious recipes in Macedonian, English, and Albanian. With workshop materials finely tuned, we conducted impactful sessions nationwide, fostering awareness and understanding. A pivotal study trip to Croatia not only deepened collaboration but also expanded the project's reach to an additional country, where workshops ignited transformation. Simultaneously, leveraging research insights, we initiated vital discussions on nutritional policy changes. Our advocacy for more calorie-dense, protein-rich foods persists as an ongoing dialogue, extending well beyond the project's conclusion.

<< Results >>

The project has generated several tangible outcomes:
The project launched a multilingual website offering valuable nutrition resources, wellness articles, recipes, and BMI calculators, accessible in three languages: Macedonian, English, and Albanian.
An active Instagram profile was established, strategically targeting the younger demographic to amplify project outreach and engagement.
Conducting a research survey across three countries—North Macedonia, Croatia, and France—proved instrumental. The survey findings not only informed the refinement of workshops but also provided an evidence-based foundation for advocating policy changes.
Engagement with the Ministry of Education marked the commencement of a constructive dialogue concerning policy adjustments related to nutrition within student dorms and kitchens.
The initiative's reach extended widely with the successful execution of one hundred workshops within Macedonian high schools, fostering awareness and knowledge dissemination.
A study visit to Croatia further fortified collaboration through partner meetings and a student-focused workshop.
Lastly, preparations are underway for a forthcoming publication centered around the results of the survey

Para todas as organizações, incluindo as que tinham maior experiência, a melhoria da capacidade de gestão e de implementação de projetos internacionais foi também uma prioridade, assim como promover a cooperação transnacional e aumentar a rede de parceiros;

2022-1-RO01-KA210-YOU-000084372.title: Non-Formal Education Activities for the inclusion of people with disabilities
2022-1-RO01-KA210-YOU-000084372.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project out of the desire to help young people with various disabilities integrate much more easily into their communities. Many people do not know how to collaborate or communicate with people with disabilities and as a result they feel isolated and marginalized.
  Own resources are not enough to reach the target group in a qualitative way.
Each disability has a need, its own approach that can only be achieved by working in this field. This is how the internal need to increase expertise in working with young people with disabilities appeared.
A partnership was formed between the organization from Croatia which works more with young people with mental disabilities, Cyprus - young people with mental disabilities, Romania - with young people with visual disabilities. We approached the need to help the community through the trainings developed at the local level. Thus, the need to help other organizations to work with young people with disabilities is great because many of them do not have qualified staff to organize specific activities. More than that, even at the level of each community, there were requests from the youth workers to be helped to organize activities for young people with disabilities.

<< Objectives >>

Through the project, we wanted to promote inclusive activities for people with disabilities through non-formal education.
Thus, we achieved the following objectives that we proposed when we conceived the project:
1. To create a brochure that includes a series of non-formal work methods that aim to integrate people with disabilities in various activities;
2. To train 56 youth workers at the local level from Romania, Cyprus and Croatia, 11 more people than we initially proposed;
3. Let's involve 223 young people, 80 of whom have different types of disabilities.

<< Implementation >>

Within our project, we have implemented several activities:
A5 - I created a handbook that contains a series of information about the project, but also the most important - aspects / methods that, with the help of art as therapy, improve non-formal activities for young people with disabilities in particular.
A6 – I organized an international course where I trained 12 youth workers from partner organizations how to work with people with disabilities.
A7 – We organized local training courses in which we trained 44 youth workers from the local level who implemented activities in their communities.
A8 - We organized local activities with young people, such as inclusive workshops attended by 223 young people, 80 of whom - with different disabilities.
A9 – We evaluated the learning process and the success we achieved.

<< Results >>

1. A Handbook that is accessible free of charge on the project's website, facebook and also made available  and in printable to all youth workers from the 3 partner organizations. It is available in English, Romanian, Croatian and Greek;
2. 56 youth workers were trained to carry out non-formal activities with young people, including young people with limited opportunities;
3. 33 NGOs / institutions have become more inclusive because they have youth workers trained to work with people with disabilities;
4. 223 young people were involved in non-formal education activities where they experienced various inclusive activities.

2022-1-RS01-KA210-YOU-000084647.title: Анимирај се!
2022-1-RS01-KA210-YOU-000084647.summary:
<< Background >>

While working with youth, we noticed a rising need to develop digital, creative and social skills, which had become especially emphasized during the pandemic, when the youth was limited to online activities. Animation, as an especially creative and interactive form, proved to be an ideal tool for the development of these skills. 
Even though the technology considerably advanced and animation apps became more accessible, we recognized a few key problems: 
Lack of systematic beginner courses: Most available tutorials were aimed at advanced users, which made them inaccessible for our target groups. 
Outdated methodologies: Colleagues from the region and further used methodologies based on analogue techniques more than 40 years old, which were not applicable in the modern digital context. 
Technical challenges with transition to online work: We attempted to adapt traditional workshops to the digital space, but we realized that we need a new approach that includes modern tools and methodologies. 
The project goal was to solve these challenges and offer a modern, accessible and educational animation learning platform to the youth. Special attention was given to youth from sensitive groups. 

<< Objectives >>

The project had three basic goals:

-Modern methodology development: The goal was to conceive and test a youth work methodology suitable for adopting beginner knowledge and skills in the field of animation, while utilizing digital tools. We wanted to use this methodology in further work with youth, both online and in person.

-Creation of an inclusive animation course: We planned to create a systematized beginner course, adapted to the youth from various socioeconomic and educational environments. The course was to contain simple, intuitive video tutorials adapted to the digital age. 

-Popularization of animation in youth creativity: The goal was to utilize a growing interest for digital tools and contribute to a wider application of animation as a tool for learning and creative expression. We achieved this by:
-Empowering youth to independently create animations.
-Education of youth workers for course and methodology application in their work
-Project promotion through social media, public events and festivals. 


<< Implementation >>

Preparation and organization:
An online meeting was held and a digital coordination and communication space was set up. 
Monitoring and evaluation plans were created. 
Assembly of a group of 65 youth from various environments, including those from sensitive groups (rural areas, no parental care, and development difficulties), which was used for testing and course adaptation. 

Material and tool development:
Youth work methodology, a film-methodological handbook production 
Production of an animation course in the form of short, accessible tutorials.
Abilities of the formed youth group were examined, and course and methodology were adapted accordingly. 
Project description.

Education and promotion. 
Two online and two in-person lectures for youth workers were held. 
Organized workshops and online meetings with youth. 
Project presentation on festivals and other public events: MMfest, VAFI i RAFI, Festival of children and youth filmmaking of Serbia, Banja Luka Animated Film Festival; Nature and Music festival “Regina fest”, and on the C

<< Results >>

-Methodology: production and improvement of an innovative film-methodological handbook supporting digital transformation in youth creativity. 
-Animation course: Production and improvement of a systematized beginner course, accessible to youth from sensitive groups and suitable for online learning.
-Project description: informative and well-structured description, offering practical pointers about the course, so it’s applicable by other organizations in their work.
Youth creative results: 150 young participants (including sensitive groups: rural environments, no parental care, and those with development difficulties) created their own animated films/clips, numbering 13 animated films, 94 reels and 273 animations. 
Advanced training: Six most successful participants received a 40 hour advanced training in a professional studio. 
Youth worker education: 136 youth workers obtained basic knowledge in applying animation in youth work.
Animation popularization: Through social media activities, public events and festivals, the project considerably contributed to the popularization of animation in youth creativity.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2022-2-CZ01-KA210-YOU-000091332.title: BE INFORMED NOT DISINFORMED
2022-2-CZ01-KA210-YOU-000091332.summary:
<< Background >>

Cílem projektu Be informed, not disinformed bylo posílit schopnosti účastníků ověřování informací v médiích a kyberprostoru v době zvýšeného rizika dezinformací. Zaměřili jsme se na aktuální témata, válku na Ukrajině a migraci uprchlíků. Snažili jsme se porozumět a řešit problémy související s
dezinformacemi a témat polarizujících společnost. Zároveň jsme se během každé z aktivit soustředili na specifika dezinformační scény v každé zúčastněné zemi.

Spolupracovali jsme s partnerskými organizacemi a odborníky na dezinformační scénu (během každé aktivity proběhla prezentace experta na určité téma), zahrnuli jsme novináře, redaktory a experty na mediální prostor. Středobodem projektu bylo zvýšení informovanosti, zodpovědného přístupu k informacím a jejich ověřování.

Se zúčastněnými organizacemi jsme došli k shodě, že toto téma je v dnešní společnosti aktuální. Soustředění na problematiku fake news v mezinárodním kolektivu nám umožnilo ji řešit originálně, inovativně, efektivně a se znatelným dopadem na jednotlivce. Mezinárodní spolupráce v kontextu organizace Be informed, not disinformed nám poskytla představu a základ pro naši práci s mládeží a především know-how pro vznik a realizaci budoucích projeků.

<< Objectives >>

S projektem jsme chtěli dosáhnout, čeho se do určité míry snažíme dosahovat v našich každodenních životech. Tedy přemýšlet nad informacemi, které k nám v určitém kontextu přicházejí, být kritičtí, brát ohled na zdroj informace. Postřehli jsme, že řada mladých lidí nepovažuje otázku fake news za důležitou, nebo se jí vůbec nezabývá. Vnímáme ovšem, že i mladí lidé, kteří téma dezinformací vnímají jako důležité, by potřebovali k aplikaci kritického přístupu popostrčit. Z vlastních zkušeností jsme zjistili, že sdílením poznatků z různých geografických, ekonomických, náboženských i etnických kontextů lze nastartovat dialog, který bude přemýšlet nad problematikou z různých úhlů pohledu a přinese inovativní nápady a postupy. Věříme, že se nám to implementací projektu Be informed, not disinformed podařilo.
Vzhledem k tomu, že naše organizace je velmi mladá, bylo dalším aspektem k realizaci tohoto projektu vytvoření dlouhodobější mezinárodní spolupráce.
Konkrétní cíle projektu zahrnovaly: 1) rozšíření povědomí o dezinformacích 2) propojení partnerských organizací, 3) sdílení poznatků o dezinformační scéně mezinárodně, 4) představení programu Erasmus+ a prezentaci výsledků práce národním a mezinárodním institucím.

<< Implementation >>

V rámci projektu Be Informed Not Disinformed (BIND) jsme implementovali 4 mezinárodní aktivity, přípravné online schůzky a fyzické evaluační meetingy (viz níže).

Stěžejní částí projektu byly právě 4 vícedenní mezinárodní aktivity. Na aktivitách bylo přítomno 16 účastníků (včetně realizačního týmu) pocházejících ze čtyř zemí partnerských organizací. Aktivity byly logisticky designované totožně: každá aktivita se skládala ze tří programových dnů a dvou cestovních. První aktivita proběhla v slovenském Čunovu (Bratislavě), druhá ve Wroclawi, třetí v Zagrebu a poslední v Praze. Pořadí aktivit bylo oproti původní žádosti přizpůsobeno potřebám partnerů a ostatním okolnostem, aby mohly být aktivity hladce realizovány co nejkvalitněji v jejich plném rozsahu. 

Krom těchto aktivit jsme realizovali více schůzek. Vždy přibližně dva měsíce před aktivitou jsme naplánovali online schůzku s hostujícím partnerem, na které jsme potvrdili rozdělení povinností a domluvili zajištění logistických záležitosti (ubytování, expert, venue, apod.). 

V rámci českého realizačního týmu jsme také realizovali více přípravných a evaluačních schůzek. Evaluační meetingy probíhaly online po každé aktivitě, a finální fyzické evaluační setkání po poslední aktivitě. 

<< Results >>

Jedním z hlavních výsledků projektu je zvýšení kompetencí našich organizací na poli práce s mládeží. Partnerství rozdílně zkušených organizací nám pomohlo ve zkvalitnění praxe a zvýšení organizačních kompetencí.
Stěžejním výsledkem je poté zvýšení kompetencí jak účastníků tak mládeže a veřejnosti na poli odhalování dezinformací, mediální gramotnosti a povědomí o důležitosti tohoto problému. 
Neméně důležitým výsledkem je propojení organizací se zájmem o boj s dezinformacemi. Kromě partnerských organizací jsme navázali kontakt např. s Českou tiskovou kanceláří a také s experty v jednotlivých zemích.
Výsledkem je také šíření povědomí o programu Erasmus+. Informace o programu byly součástí workshopů i online kampaně.
Kromě samotných aktivit je dalším výsledkem online diseminační kampaň. Informace jsme šířili na sociálních sítích, pro co nejlepší oslovení naši cílové skupiny. Veřejnosti jsme zprostředkovávali obsah programu projektu i informace o organizacích a příležitostech. Dalším výstupem je také v současnosti probíhající solidární projekt Be Informed Not Disinformed: School edition, který jsme napsali na základě pozitivních zkušeností z implementace projektových workshopů, které jsme se rozhodli rozšířit do středních škol v ČR.

2022-3-DE04-KA210-YOU-000099662.title: BUSINESS PRIDE
2022-3-DE04-KA210-YOU-000099662.summary:
<< Background >>

"To support diversity in business and demonstrate how our identities can drive both societal impact and entrepreneurial success."

We applied for this project because we identified significant gaps and pressing needs in empowering LGBTQ+ youth in entrepreneurship. Despite societal progress in recognising diversity, LGBTQ+ youth remain underrepresented in entrepreneurial spaces. Their unique challenges—ranging from societal stigma to limited access to knowledge, and recognition—create barriers to their full participation in the labour market and business opportunities.

Needs Addressed by the Project:
-Stigma and Stereotyping:
LGBTQ+ youth often face discrimination, stereotyping, and marginalisation in their communities, which limits their confidence and ability to start entrepreneurial ventures.
-Knowledge and Skills Gap:
Many LGBTQ+ youth lack access to business knowledge, financial literacy, and entrepreneurial skills.
-Opportunity gap for LGBTQIA+ youth
-Support for Youth Workers: who are often key supporters of LGBTQ+ youth, require better resources and training to address the needs of this marginalised group effectively.
-Networking gaps: 
Lack of trustworthy and supportive role models for LGBTQIA+ learners.

<< Objectives >>

The primary aim of this project is to empower and support LGBTQIA+ youth entrepreneurs by addressing the challenges they face and creating opportunities for their growth. Specifically, the project sought to achieve the following objectives:
-Encourage Skill Development:
Provide LGBTQ+ youth with the skills, knowledge, and attitudes required to succeed as entrepreneurs, focusing on business development, financial literacy, and leadership.
-Analyse and Share Insights:
Understand the opportunities and gaps LGBQTIA+ face in entrepreneurship in partner countries and local comunities.
-Strengthen Mentorship:
Connect LGBTQ+ youth with experienced entrepreneurs and LGBTQIA+ mentors to provide them with guidance, role models, and supportive mentorship to get support for entrepreneurship and business challenges.
-Empower Youth Workers:
Equip youth workers with training and resources to better support LGBTQ+ youth in their entrepreneurial journeys, ensuring they can effectively address their unique needs.
-Healthier integration of LGBQTIA+ in businesses and workforce.
-Dissemination of project ideas and results and expand it to local authorities & organisations.
-Design and disseminate an interactive handbook and BUSINESS PRIDE platform.

<< Implementation >>

All activities implemented in the project:

1.  Project Management:
Ensured effective monitoring, quality assurance, and smooth project execution through regular communication and progress tracking.
2.  Kick-Off Meeting and Study Visit:
A 3-day activity in Germany included a 1-day kick-off meeting to align project goals and strategies, and a 2-day study visit to the Digital Tech Academy Erlangen (FAU), enhancing the knowledge of 11 youth workers in business and start-ups as well as understanding LGBTQIA+ representation in business.
3. Handbook Development:
A practical guide for LGBTQIA+ youth entrepreneurs, their allies, and youth workers, developed through focus groups, research, piloting, and professional graphic design.
4. Business Pride Platform Development:
An online empowerment hub (tech support by TIR) was designed and launched, providing resources to support LGBTQIA+ youth in entrepreneurship, workplace integration, and personal success. Also with mentorship guidelines, a contact database, and a Facebook group to connect and support LGBTQIA+ youth.
5. Dissemination and Exploitation Activities:
Concluded with a meeting in Poland to share outcomes, engage stakeholders, and promote the handbook and platform for wider impact.

<< Results >>

Results:

1. Analysis Report:  Findings are based on survey responses from 172 individuals (112 LGBTQIA+ & 60 allies , expert interviews,
and insights from the participatory visit in Nuremberg, Germany.  It highlights key challenges such as funding barriers, discrimination, and regional disparities, while emphasising opportunities through mentorship, digital platforms, and tailored resources for
LGBTQ+ entrepreneurs. 

2. Interactive Handbook: Practical support guide for LGBTQIA+ youth entrepreneurs, their allies and youth workers. (78 pages available in EN,DE,PL,HR)

3. Business Pride Platform: An online empowerment hub featuring resources, educational materials, mentorship guidelines, and a contact database to connect LGBTQIA+ youth with mentors. The platform also includes a Facebook group for networking and collaboration.

4. Handbook and the online platform tested and Implemented by 30 youth trainers and learners in partner countries, with insights documented in a report.

5. Engagement of 3000+ youth workers, LGBTQIA+ learners and their allies through the platform, handbook, and findings. 

6. 3 Multiplier events in partner countries.

2022-3-ES02-KA210-YOU-000093812.title: LINKIN' HISTORIES: Promoción de la identidad europea y puesta en valor de la Europa plural, diversa y multicultural a través de la visibilización de procesos históricos entre la juventud
2022-3-ES02-KA210-YOU-000093812.summary:
<< Background >>

El proyecto LINKIN' HISTORIES se inspiró en la necesidad de conocer las historias de vida de personas mayores a las que a menudo no se escucha. Además, quería comprender la crisis actual de los valores de la UE, con un crecimiento del sentimiento antieuropeo, así como el aumento de los discursos antiinmigración, racistas y xenófobos. Teniendo esto en cuenta, el proyecto sirvió para derribar prejuicios que constituyen obstáculos para muchas personas, especialmente para los inmigrantes. Además, el proyecto respondió a la necesidad de fomentar el pensamiento crítico y la participación política entre los jóvenes, al tiempo que promovía su papel activo haciendo visibles importantes cuestiones políticas con productos audiovisuales de gran impacto basados en historias de vida.
Por último, el proyecto pretendía desarrollar una metodología innovadora y participativa que pudiera reproducirse, lo cual era un interés de los socios del proyecto. 

<< Objectives >>

Promover los valores europeos, la identidad y el compromiso con la UE entre la juventud europea.
Contribuir a la construcción de una sociedad plural, diversa e inclusiva que promueva la igualdad y la no discriminación.
Promover la participación juvenil valorando la creatividad, la comunicación, el pensamiento crítico y la investigación como herramientas para orientar la acción política.

<< Implementation >>

-Reunión de lanzamiento en Riga para el plan de trabajo y la coordinación del proyecto.
-Desarrollo de una guía metodológica por Jovesolides, basada en la experiencia de la defensa de los jóvenes. 
- Formación de formadores e intercambio de buenas prácticas. Una formación de cuatro días en Zagreb, Croacia, a la que asistieron formadores (8) de los países participantes. 
-Talleres sobre investigación histórica y narrativa audiovisual. Se celebraron talleres sobre investigación histórica y narrativa audiovisual con 45 jóvenes, que dieron lugar a 15 proyectos audiovisuales creados en colaboración. 
-Producción de 15 Productos Audiovisuales. Los 45 jóvenes participantes, guiados por facilitadores, aplicaron la metodología desarrollada para crear proyectos audiovisuales basados en su investigación histórica. A continuación, la metodología se aplicó a la producción de 15 productos audiovisuales. 
-Eventos de difusión y publicación de libros. El proyecto se presentó en un festival audiovisual en Benicàssim (España) y en dos eventos locales en Letonia y Croacia. Por último, el libro «Linkin' Histories: United Generation» documentó el proyecto, haciendo hincapié en la investigación y la participación de los jóvenes.

<< Results >>

El proyecto ha conseguido:
- 1 Guía metodológica diseñada, publicada y traducida a los tres idiomas de los países socios (croata, letón y español)
- 7 educadores juveniles formados para planificar y dirigir procesos educativos con jóvenes a nivel local, utilizando la guía metodológica previamente diseñada  
- 15 talleres educativos para jóvenes organizados en los 3 países, en los que participaron 45 jóvenes. 
- 15 productos audiovisuales elaborados por jóvenes a partir de talleres locales.
- 1 Libro «Linkin' Histories: Generaciones Unidas» que recoge todo el proceso del proyecto.
- 1 Vídeo resumen del proyecto.
- 1 Festival audiovisual en el que han participado 43 personas.
- 2 Eventos locales de difusión con la participación de 30 personas.
- Al menos 36 publicaciones en medios sociales en el marco de la campaña de comunicación

2022-3-ES02-KA210-YOU-000096259.title: YOUTH 4 OUR RURAL PRODUCTS
2022-3-ES02-KA210-YOU-000096259.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The main tangible result of the project is the development of an ICT e-toolkit with information, instructions and practical advices for Youth Workers to teach young people to be entrepeneur sustainably with local products and how to promote them creatively. The other results are the development of the skills of the staff of the participating organizations to plan, deliver and facilitate this training to the Youth Workers.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, 3 activities are planned. The 1st one has to do with the design and creation of the first module of an e-toolkit with information and instructions on how young people can be entrepreneur with km0 products from their rural community. The 2nd is the development of module 2 of the e-toolkit, which will contain examples and practical cases. The 3rd is a pilot seminar where the Youth Workers will participate to test the e-toolkit and be able to guarantee the success of the course

<< Results >>

We hope that, after carrying out the last activity proposed in this project, rural youth, many of them immigrants, are trained for entrepreneurship and feel motivated to do so by taking advantage of the resources offered by their rural community with local products. In this way, we would meet our general and specific objectives, by reducing the unemployment rate in these areas, we would improve the green economy with sustainable practices for the environment.

2022-3-FR02-KA210-YOU-000092585.title: Non-competitive activities for inclusion
2022-3-FR02-KA210-YOU-000092585.summary:
<< Background >>

Le but du projet était de répondre aux défis des jeunes dans un monde dominé par la compétition et l'individualisme, aggravés par la révolution numérique et des crises successives. Ces facteurs provoquent isolement, problèmes de santé mentale et exclusion sociale, en particulier chez les jeunes avec moins d’opportunités.
Les jeunes ont besoin d’interactions positives, de coopération et d’activités constructives pour devenir des citoyens responsables et engagés. Mais, les activités physiques traditionnelles sont souvent compétitives et excluantes. Pour répondre à ce besoin, nous avons proposé des activités non compétitives, qui favorisent la coopération, la confiance et l’inclusion de tous.
Le projet visait à enseigner, promouvoir et développer les activités du cirque, de la danse, de l’éducation en plein air et des jeux coopératifs. 
Le projet répondait à deux grands besoins :
1.	Celui des jeunes travailleurs, en leur offrant de nouveaux outils et méthodes pour intégrer et éduquer les jeunes ayant moins d’opportunités de manière inclusive et équitable.
2.	Celui des jeunes eux-mêmes, en leur offrant des activités pertinentes et inclusives qui favorisent leur expression, leur reconnaissance et leur participation active à la société.

<< Objectives >>

Les objectifs du projet étaient :
•	Former les partenaires aux activités non compétitives en tant qu’outil de travail jeunesse, en partageant des bonnes pratiques et en leur permettant de découvrir des activités alternatives qu’ils ne connaissaient pas auparavant.
•	Développer des activités accessibles aux jeunes avec moins d’opportunités, en formant les partenaires à de nouvelles méthodes qui favorisent l’inclusion et le développement des compétences personnelles et sociales des participants.
•	Promouvoir et diffuser l’utilisation des activités non compétitives comme des approches attrayantes et inclusives, au-delà du consortium de partenaires.
Le projet visait à :
•	Augmenter la capacité des travailleurs jeunesse et des organisations participantes à inclure et soutenir les jeunes.
•	Accroître la participation et l’inclusion des jeunes avec moins d’opportunités dans les activités de travail jeunesse.
•	Valoriser et faire reconnaître les activités non compétitives comme une forme valide et innovante de travail jeunesse.
Le projet visait à transformer les pratiques des organisations partenaires et à améliorer l’inclusion des jeunes marginalisés grâce à des approches participatives et adaptées aux divers besoins des participants.

<< Implementation >>

Nous avons mis en œuvre les activités suivantes :
•	Réunion de lancement pour établir les bases du projet et définir les objectifs communs.
•	Cartographie et collecte de données pour identifier les besoins, les pratiques existantes et les ressources disponibles.
•	Réunions transnationales pour coordonner les partenaires, partager les avancées et ajuster les actions.
•	Mobilité d’apprentissage pour les travailleurs jeunesse, afin de leur offrir des formations sur les activités non compétitives et les méthodes inclusives.
•	Développement d’un manuel de bonnes pratiques, compilant les expériences et connaissances acquises au cours du projet.
•	Mise en œuvre d’activités dans les pays partenaires, pour tester et adapter les méthodes auprès des jeunes avec moins d’opportunités.
•	Événements multiplicateurs organisés dans les pays partenaires pour partager les résultats et les impacts du projet avec un public plus large.
•	Campagne de sensibilisation pour promouvoir les activités non compétitives et leur impact positif sur l’inclusion et la diversité.
•	Réunion finale pour évaluer les résultats, partager les apprentissages et préparer les étapes futures.

<< Results >>

1.	Livrables :
•	Manuel de bonnes pratiques sur les activités non-compétitives (cirque, danse, éducation en plein air, jeux coopératifs), destiné aux éducateurs et travailleurs de jeunesse pour préparer, mettre en œuvre et évaluer ces activités.
•	Une mobilité d’apprentissage pour les travailleurs de jeunesse, favorisant l’acquisition de nouvelles compétences méthodologiques et pédagogiques.
•	De multiples activités locales dans les pays partenaires, atteignant au moins 180 jeunes.
•	Une base de données regroupant les besoins et évaluations des jeunes, ainsi que des recherches sur les activités non-compétitives.
•	un site web : https://noncompetitiveactivities.wordpress.com/
2.	Résultats qualitatifs :
•	Renforcement des compétences des travailleurs jeunesse en matière d’inclusion et d’éducation non formelle.
•	Amélioration de la participation des jeunes dans les activités éducatives et civiques.
•	Création d’un réseau international entre les partenaires et leurs organisations.
3.	Dissemination et sensibilisation :
•	Organisation d’événements multiplicateurs atteignant au moins 150 participants.
•	Campagne de sensibilisation visant à promouvoir l’utilisation des activités non-compétitives et à augmenter les téléchargements du manue

2022-3-HR01-KA210-YOU-000094402.title: Greenwashing = Brainwashing
2022-3-HR01-KA210-YOU-000094402.summary:
<< Background >>

Our organization, in collaboration with partners, has submitted this project because we have recognized an urgent need to raise awareness and knowledge about climate change, especially among young people. We have observed a significant gap in understanding the impact of everyday activities on the environment and the seriousness of greenwashing, which is not sufficiently discussed, particularly at a time when more companies advertise themselves as "green" and "sustainable," giving a false picture of their operations. Our goal has been and remains to empower young people, especially those with fewer opportunities, through education on climate and environmental issues, so that they can think critically and act responsibly towards the environment. By implementing a variety of activities (trainer training, training for young people on climate and environmental literacy, study visits, creation of handbooks and digital tools, etc.) through this project, we wanted to provide tools for recognizing greenwashing and encourage changes in behavior that lead to a sustainable lifestyle. This project directly addressed these needs, offering practical knowledge and solutions for young people and organizations, strengthening their capacities.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of our project was to empower organizations involved in the project to carry out sustainable development activities and reduce ecological footprint, to encourage the green transformation of youth work, and to establish an international collaborative network for the exchange of knowledge and practices. Our intention was to raise awareness and knowledge about greenwashing among young people and the organizations that work with them, and to develop the ability to recognize and constructively respond to this phenomenon. We aimed to develop and implement innovative digital tools that would facilitate the measurement and reduction of ecological footprint, as well as to create a handbook that would serve as a guide through the principles of sustainable development for youth organizations. Additionally, the objective was to create a declaration that would be signed by other organizations at the European level to promote climate-neutral activities in youth work. Through this project, we strived to expand the collaborative network at the European level, support green transformation and change the ethical climate, develop educational materials for educating young people about greenwashing, and support active citizenship 

<< Implementation >>

Within our project, we implemented a series of key activities aimed at achieving the project's goals and addressing identified needs. The activities were diverse and included:
1. Three transnational partner meetings
2. Environmental and climate literacy training (local training for young people in each partner organization)
3. Creation of the Green Manual
4. Study visit
5. Development of digital tools (a web calculator for measuring ecological footprint)
6. Training for trainers
7. Three local trainings and the establishment of a working group for the Green Declaration
8. Online international conference

<< Results >>

1.Green Manual: Successfully developed and distributed, the Green Manual is a handbook for working with youth that contains detailed guidelines for conducting climate-neutral activities. The manual served as a foundation for educating young people about ecological sustainability and offered practical advice for reducing ecological footprints. It has been translated into four languages (English, Dutch, Spanish, and Croatian), making it accessible to a wider community of youth workers.
2.Web Calculator for Measuring Ecological Footprint: An innovative digital tool has been developed that allows young people and organizations to easily calculate their ecological footprint and identify areas for improvement. The tool is available at: https://greenwashing-eu.com/
3. Local Trainings on Environmental and Climate Literacy: Three trainings were conducted that equipped young people to think critically about greenwashing and eco-manipulation.
4. Training for Trainers: Youth workers were trained to use the web calculator and the Green Manual in their work with youth. This ensured the dissemination of knowledge and skills necessary for promoting sustainable practices within and outside their organizations.
5. The Green Declaration was created

2022-3-HR01-KA210-YOU-000097125.title: SAVE AND GAME – Escape Game for Energy Sustainability
2022-3-HR01-KA210-YOU-000097125.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project in order to provide an opportunity and new innovation for youth workers and young people. By engaging and empowering we wanted to contribute to addressing environmental and climate challenges aligning with the principles established in international conferences such as the Earth Summit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
Through this project, we aimed to help increase awareness among young people about environmental issues, improve the communication skills of youth workers in sustainability topics, and promote scientific citizenship and green skills among both youth and youth workers. Additionally, we wanted to prepare young people for the future workforce that is increasingly focused on the green economy.        
Finally, by satisfying the needs of youth and youth workers and thus creating good quality material capable of preparing them to become true agents of change for a sustainable future, the project addressed the needs of young people.




<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we achieved the following objectives:

Objective 1: To increase awareness among young people about environmental challenges and the importance of collective responsibility in addressing them.

Objective 2: To enhance the skills of youth workers to effectively communicate with young people about sustainability and position them as agents of change.

Objective 3: To foster a sense of scientific citizenship and green skills among young people through interactive tools, preparing them for a future workforce centered around the green economy.


<< Implementation >>

To achieve these objectives, several implementation activities were undertaken:

A.1 Trainers Material : A training guide for youth workers was developed, containing easily understandable technical information and resources to equip them in engaging youth effectively.

A.2 ER & Toolbox: Ready-to-use educational, both physical and video, games were created to facilitate learning on sustainability, energy conservation, consumption reduction and climate change.

A.3 Action Sheets & Examples: Action Sheets and examples of good practices were provided that should help in implementing sustainable practices in local communities. 

All followed by A.0.3 Communication activities. We also implemented a 2 days long transnational meeting in Italy.




<< Results >>

The first result was an interactive guide for youth workers on sustainability which is a comprehensive resource that addresses waste reduction and consumption efficiently. Guide, in four different languages (Croatian, Italian, English and French), can be found on the project website. 2 Added tests, a tool to evaluate the sustainability level of individuals “What is your ecological footprint?" and a tool to evaluate your level of eco anxiety “Are you eco anxious?” were a valuable addition to the guide.                                                                                                                 

Secondly, 3 escape games were created, two physical and one digital. They were developed to impart basic scientific knowledge and promote engagement in sustainability. On the Save&Game project website youth workers and teachers can find a compilation of useful tools (toolbox with game instructions and visual materials) for recreating these escape games. 

Another, very useful materials are 10 Examples of best green practices already implemented in Belgium, Italy and Croatia and 13 action sheets that are helpful for replicating successfully different initiatives on a local level.

2022-3-HR01-KA210-YOU-000098924.title: Engaging youth in culture
2022-3-HR01-KA210-YOU-000098924.summary:
<< Background >>

The youth is, in many cases, a passive observer of heritage sites and cultural institutions. Our project sought to improve this passive role, transforming youth into active co-creators. We aimed to shift the paradigm by encouraging them to shape local activities and policies, fostering their participation in decision-making processes, and nurturing a sense of ownership over their cultural heritage. The idea was to share experience from our organizations, which has shown that youth can effectively self-organize in functional structures and build capacity to develop impactful cultural projects and programs. Our mission was to equip young individuals with practical tools, enabling them to engage with culture holistically and advocate for the changes they desire.

With this project we addressed common values, civic engagement and participation, focusing on the development of intercultural competences and participation in the democratic life and we also brought culture closer to young people. The project also tackled the internal needs of organizations. We aimed to cultivate a more modern and professional working environment - one that embraced innovation and was open to incorporate new methods and synergies from other organizations. 

<< Objectives >>

With this project, we aimed to:
1. Empower youth engagement with culture: our project aimed to create tools that empower young people to actively engage with culture. These tools were developed based on the extensive experience of both organizations in this field.
2. Enhance organizational capacity and youth management skills: we sought to strengthen the capacity, professionalism, and improve youth management competences and skills of both organizations. This was achieved through shared experiences, knowledge exchange, and the adoption of innovative non-formal education methods. Our goal was to equip youth groups beyond their local communities. 
3. Foster awareness of long-term impact: by encouraging youth participation and involvement today, we aimed to raise awareness that their actions and engagement can shape future policies and practices.
4. Create an innovative methodology for engaging youth in culture: the main result of the project was a handbook with steps on how to engage youth in culture. The handbook was promoted and shared among stakeholders.
5.Facilitate cross-cultural exchange: lastly, our project aimed to facilitate the exchange of experiences between Eastern and Central European countries facing similar challenges

<< Implementation >>

Throughout the project we carried out the following activities:
- Project administration and coordination: planning and tasks, monitoring partners' working process, keeping contact with each coordinator of the project's intellectual outputs, scheduling meetings, writing reports and evaluating activities (1/4/2023 - 31/3/2024)
- Transnational project meetings: 1st one in Ivanić-Grad, Croatia (3/5/2023 - 5/5/2023) and 2nd one in Cluj-Napoca, Romania (22/3/2024 - 25/3/2024)
- LTTA1 staff training for the preparation of the handbook and acquiring new skills for engaging youth in culture, in Bucharest, Romania (19/6/2023 - 23/6/2023)
handbook writing and publishing: collecting case-studies and relevant research, developing methodology, conducting testing with youth and rewriting the final results, print and publishing; remote in Croatia and Romania (1/7/2023 - 1/2/2024)
- LTTA2 handbook pilot training with youth during 3 day workshop activities in Ivanić-Grad, Croatia (24/1/2024 - 29/1/2024)
- Multiplier events: 1st conference in Ivanić-Grad, Croatia (6/3/2024) and 2nd conference in Cluj-Napoca, Romania (23/3/2024)
- Dissemination activities: PR activities on social media, contact with media and local stakeholders, design develo

<< Results >>

The main outcome of the project is the handbook “How to engage youth in culture” which was written in cooperation between two organisations, based on intensive staff training and methodology development, which was later on tested with youth from Croatia and Romania. The testing was carried out in a three day workshop “Handbook pilot training with youth” which showed that young people are capable of conducting their own project in culture with the help of facilitators. Besides, it showed that youth are more enthusiastic if they are the ones making decisions and leading the whole process. The testing served as a learning method to both the young participants and the facilitators, because the facilitators learned about possible ways of engaging young people in culture, while the youth learned how to create and implement their own project from start to finish. The Handbook was printed in 100 copies, which were given out to partners and stakeholders and other interested participants during the dissemination process in 2 multiplier events, in Croatia and Romania. The exchange of experiences with stakeholders and their interest tell us that it will definitely be useful for cultural workers in museums, associations, libraries etc.

2022-3-HR01-KA210-YOU-000101382.title: Kreni na zeleno...
2022-3-HR01-KA210-YOU-000101382.summary:
<< Background >>

SOIH applied for a project with the aim of actively contribute to the social inclusion of young persons with disabilities (PwD) and Youth workers in combating climate change.
New paradigms established by the Sustainable Development Goals, The European Green Deal and The National Development Strategy of the Republic of Croatia 2030 demand that the approach to the management of PwD associations is completely based on the principles of sustainability.
By founding the Forum of Youth with Disabilities in 2018 we laid the foundations for an active gathering of youth with different types of disabilities, members of PWD associations.
Climate change represents a challenge that the entire society is facing, and young PwD, as part of the world's largest minority, undoubtedly feel its consequences. Through their activities within the Forum, they have shown that they have a strong influence on spreading awareness of the importance of stopping climate change and that they consider as a key topic. Therefore the project was based on the knowledge that, through the education of young PwD and cooperation with partners, we can support the sustainability program, improve the rights of PwD through the green agenda, and help fight the climate crisis.

<< Objectives >>

The general goal of the project was to raise environmental awareness and encourage green activities in PwD associations through the activism of young PwD and YW.
Education of young PwD and YW on relevant environmental protection topics strengthened competences for advocating positive changes in local communities and encouraged environmental activism. YW were empowered to act towards PwD associations with the aim of changing the paradigm of office business and applying green standards in the work and daily activities of employees. One of the specific goals was to establish international cooperation and peer networking of young PwD through the transmission of good practices, which was achieved through the involvement of youth in the campaigns implementation and the creation of promotional materials, thereby encouraging inclusive volunteering. Also, through the creation of the Handbook of green business of disability associations and video that encourage activism and contribute to the "green office" paradigm, we wanted to provide PwD associations, as well as other organizations, with advocacy tools that will serve as inspiration for further efforts to preserve the environment and promote inclusive action in local communities.

<< Implementation >>

The project comprised several key activities: four transnational partner meetings, two online and two in Croatia and Serbia; education on environmental protection covering topics such as the National Development Strategy of Croatia, the European Green Deal, GreenComp, SDG, technical environmental protection standards, eco labels, and life cycle cost assessment; enhancing physical and communication office accessibility and promoting green transportation; two campaigns aimed at encouraging PWD associations to adopt sustainable and green practices, supported by research and creation of educational tools like handbooks and videos; fostering youth activism through engaging activities and developing educational and promotional materials like leaflets and posters; organizing study visits focusing on advocacy, mobility of PwD, working with youth, and assistive technology; implementing the European Mobility Week Campaign; addressing the position of PWDs in Croatia and Serbia, and promoting green sustainability related to SDG and CRPD; and concluding with final conferences for the public and the media.

<< Results >>

The Partnership Agreements were implemented, along with partner meetings. Research assessed organizations' application of environmentally responsible practices. The project enhanced youth with disabilities' and YW's knowledge of environmental protection, strengthening advocacy skills for local community changes. YW's competencies for working with youth improved, and disability associations were encouraged to adopt green standards. A Handbook for Green Business in disability associations and an educational video in Croatian and Serbian with sign language translation were developed and promoted, alongside other educational materials in both languages. Two transnational learnings exchanged youth work experiences and good practices. International peer networking of youth with disabilities was established, facilitating good practice transfer. Young PwD were encouraged to engage in inclusive volunteering campaigns. International collaboration was established for further joint program implementation on sustainable development, environmental protection, and digital connectivity, promoting the project in Croatia and Serbia.
