2022-3-NL02-KA210-YOU-000095989.title: The Present for the Future – Boosting Youth Social Entrepreneurship that Matters
2022-3-NL02-KA210-YOU-000095989.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we wanted to further implement activities in the field of social entrepreneurship, by expanding the scope and impact at a European level. The goal of this project was to boost social entrepreneurship by actively and meaningfully engaging with the youth sector. The needs we wanted to address and have addressed were that of promoting more skilled youth workers/young social entrepreneurs through non-formal learning activities. 

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to support youth social entrepreneurship to increase innovativeness, quality, relevance and meaningfulness of youth work, which would result in boosting social inclusion of people from specific disadvantaged backgrounds. Six objectives were created. O1: Collaborate with like-minded organizations to disseminate and further enhance our models to harness the power of social entrepreneurship for a more inclusive society. O2: Develop a social entrepreneurship model that is: innovative; non-formal-learning-based; transnational; youth-lead and youth-oriented. O3: Train 6 youth workers per country on how to act as facilitators of our innovative social entrepreneurship model. O4: Engage, empower and connect 45 young social entrepreneurs per event through conducting 3 events, facilitated by youth workers for young social entrepreneurs on the topics of: Boosting inclusion and diversity & Fostering equity and equality & Supporting people facing socio-economic difficulties. O5: Directly address the needs of at least 300 people from disadvantaged backgrounds. O6: Raise awareness of youth social entrepreneurship, updated with Erasmus+ agency approval detailed in the Awareness Raising Activity.

<< Implementation >>

We conducted six online workshops with our three partner organizations, where we introduced our respective organizations and ongoing projects. Two workshops were dedicated to interactive collaboration, offering feedback on each other's work, discussing shared challenges, finances, planning, and hypothetical scenarios of starting anew. We executed three events in The Netherlands, Croatia, and Denmark by the end of May 2024. Additionally, three job shadowing activities were implemented to showcase our offices and work processes to our partners. Following each event, we held feedback sessions to improve our The Present for the Future model. Subsequently, we distributed our newly created model (a how-to guide for young social entrepreneurs) to 10-15 interested young people per country for testing. After refinement, we made it openly accessible online for anyone interested in utilizing it.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs of our project included: a feedback survey for our guide, a project website showcasing important results, reproducible methodologies outlined in the guide for young social entrepreneurs, training materials like case studies, interactive tasks, and 'further readings', reports from events, a promotional leaflet, event photos/videos, and a comprehensive catalogue and toolkit. The toolkit features checklists, case studies, references, and an event-tutorial to inspire offline event organization. Additionally, a Memorandum of Understanding was established. Further results encompassed: 3 large meetup events to boost young social entrepreneurs and their organizations, online workshops fostering idea exchange and best practices sharing with partner organizations, youth gaining practical knowledge through training and events, establishment of networks and partnerships, knowledge-sharing opportunities, acquisition of new skills, and the structured assessment, recognition, and certification of informal and non-formal learning achievements through the training of youth. These initiatives contributed to personal and professional growth for both partner organizations and young social entrepreneurs.

2022-3-NO02-KA210-YOU-000098011.title: Promotion of the virtual world of “Metaverse”
2022-3-NO02-KA210-YOU-000098011.summary:
<< Background >>

The ProMeta project was initiated to address the emerging significance of the Metaverse and its potential impact on society, particularly the youth. It identifies a crucial gap in the digital competencies of youth workers, aiming to enable them to better engage with young people in digital environments. 

Bridging the Digital Knowledge Gap: It seeks to update youth workers' skills to keep pace with technological advances, ensuring they remain relevant and effective.
Enhancing Communication: Improving interaction between youth workers and young people through the Metaverse, creating more engaging experiences.
Promoting Safe Navigation: Aims to guide young people safely through the Metaverse, highlighting educational opportunities while mitigating risks.
Supporting Learning: Focuses on developing guidelines and educational programs to recognize and validate non-formal and informal learning experiences.
Fostering Collaboration: Encourages alignment with EU policies and collaboration among organizations to innovate in non-formal education in the youth sector.
By equipping youth workers with essential skills and knowledge, ProMeta strives for a more inclusive, innovative, and safe digital environment

<< Objectives >>

The ProMeta project aims to utilize the Metaverse as a tool for youth workers to foster better engagement with young people, enhancing both their personal and professional development in navigating the next generation of the internet within a digitalized and rapidly changing society. The project seeks to develop digital skills and competencies in forward-looking fields such as VR/XR/AR, which are crucial for Europe's future sustainable growth and cohesion. It contributes to stimulating innovation and bridging Europe's knowledge, skills, and competencies gap. Additionally, ProMeta supports and facilitates transnational and international cooperation between organizations in education, training, and youth fields. It promotes non-formal and informal learning mobility, active participation among young people, and cooperation, quality inclusion, creativity, and innovation at the organizational and policy levels in the youth field. The expected outputs include the development of a Guideline on Metaverse for Youth Workers by Non-Formal learning methods and the creation of Audio-Visual digital content on Metaverse in the field of Youth.

<< Implementation >>

The ProMeta project implemented a cohesive set of activities to harness the Metaverse for youth work enhancement. It began with project management and coordination to ensure effective partnership and a kick-off meeting to align goals and responsibilities. The project developed a Guideline of Metaverse for Youth Workers, providing a vital resource for navigating the Metaverse. Local training sessions were organized to disseminate these guidelines among youth workers, coupled with an evaluation meeting in Croatia to assess progress. To bolster learning and engagement, non-formal education modules were created as audio-visual digital content, including podcasts and videos. An international workshop offered further education and exchange of Metaverse-related practices among youth workers. Lastly, a pilot implementation at the local level engaged young people directly, allowing the practical application of learned skills and evaluation of their impact in real-world scenarios. This holistic approach aimed at equipping youth workers with the necessary skills and knowledge to effectively engage with the digital and rapidly evolving landscape of the Metaverse.

<< Results >>

The ProMeta project achieved significant results:

Guideline Development: A comprehensive guideline on the Metaverse for Youth Workers was developed using non-formal learning methods, serving as a key resource for youth workers to navigate and leverage the Metaverse effectively.
Audio-Visual Digital Content: The project created educational audio-visual content, including podcasts and videos on the Metaverse, aimed at enhancing learning and engagement within the youth sector.
Training and Workshops: Over 100 participants were involved in the guidelines and audio-visual educational content, with local training sessions and workshops further educating and engaging youth workers.
Dissemination Activities: Nearly 50 youth organizations were reached through various dissemination activities, such as newsletters, social media posts, and e-tools, effectively spreading the project's findings and resources.
Social Media Engagement: The project successfully increased interaction and followers on its social media platforms (Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn), with at least 37000 people joining or interacting with these pages.

2022-3-PT02-KA210-YOU-000093108.title: Engaging youth through digital storytelling
2022-3-PT02-KA210-YOU-000093108.summary:
<< Background >>

We aimed to enhance youth involvement in active citizenship and Erasmus+ programs, crucial as interest waned, particularly among rural and economically disadvantaged youths, exacerbated by COVID-19. Recognizing the significance of understanding EU values and mobility opportunities for the Union's future, our project emphasized raising awareness of EU values, unity, diversity, and historical heritage. The pandemic highlighted the urgent need for a coordinated EU effort to bolster education and adapt to the digital transition effectively. 

<< Objectives >>

By addressing the aforementioned challenges, we had a number of objectives that aimed to empower youths to participate actively in shaping their communities and benefiting from the opportunities offered by Erasmus+. Through these efforts, we hoped to foster a sense of belonging and responsibility among young people towards the European project. 

 

The project aimed to establish transnational cooperation to innovate youth work and promote European values, fostering active citizenship in Erasmus+ mobility programs. The digital storytelling app featuring interviews and testimonies of EU program participants, aimed to engage youth in digital youth work and promote European values, unity, and diversity. The project included a youth exchange activity to enhance digital skills. Partners involved young people to understand their opinions on the EU and Erasmus+, assess reasons for non-participation, and discuss potential remedies. Additionally, short video testimonies were gathered to motivate youth to participate in Erasmus+ projects. All the project activities ensured the project served the needs of target groups and educational objectives. 

<< Implementation >>

The activities we implemented included  

A1, A2 and A3 - to ensure smooth project management, quality assurance, dissemination, and exploitation through structured processes and coordination among partners. 

A4 - to Establish transnational cooperation to innovate youth work and promote European values, fostering active citizenship in Erasmus+ mobility programs. Through this we organized transnational project meetings in Portugal and Croatia to network, share best practices, and review project progress. 

A5 - to first collect video testimonies from EU youth to motivate participation in Erasmus+ projects and provide an interactive platform for youth engagement and skill development. After to develop a digital storytelling app featuring interviews and testimonies of EU program participants, engaging youth in digital youth work and promoting European values, unity, and diversity. 

These activities aimed to serve the needs of target groups and educational objectives effectively. 

<< Results >>

The project yielded significant outcomes, including an innovative digital storytelling app created by youth participants from partner and other EU countries, showcasing good practices in Erasmus+ mobility and offering filmmaking and animation resources for youth workers. Activity 1 resulted in established consortium, virtual meetings, reports, and budget claims. Activity 2 produced a quality management plan, surveys, and reports. Activity 3 generated a dissemination plan, branding materials, social media accounts, newsletters, press releases, and multiplier events. Activity 4 led to established consortium, meetings, presentations, and reports. Activity 5 involved task force meetings, interviews, open calls, testimonies, youth exchanges, animations, video editing, app development, a documentary, translations, and evaluation reports. These outputs reflect comprehensive efforts to promote European values, youth engagement, and Erasmus+ opportunities.

2022-3-RO01-KA210-YOU-000096793.title: Fostering STEM education for youth through educational cartoons methodologies and e-learning technologies
2022-3-RO01-KA210-YOU-000096793.summary:
<< Background >>

Research funded by the European Commission, including this project, shows that: STEM studies and careers have low attractiveness, and labor market demand in STEM sectors remains unmet (PISA 2018 and 2022 reflect poor results in Romania, Cyprus, and Croatia);vulnerable groups continue to face social exclusion in various areas, including education; in the three countries, digital illiteracy remains high, despite digital skills being taught from middle school; linguistic diversity is still not recognized as a valuable cultural resource.
In response to these needs, this initiative proposes: digital transformation through the development of an e-learning platform for STEM education, based on cartoons; improving STEM learning through attractive digital methods; enhancing social inclusion by developing the civic skills of young people; improving digital skills for education specialists and students; raising awareness of linguistic diversity as part of the common European cultural heritage.
The objectives achieved converge towards the program priorities as established: Addressing digital transformation through development of digital readiness, resilience and capacity  and Increasing quality, innovation and recognition of youth work.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project we wanted to:
1. Develop a creative e-learning platform, based on visual arts and aimed at fostering STEM education to youth, development of digital skills among youth and youth practitioners, raising awareness on social inclusion to youth, & promotion of the diverse European cultural heritage in terms of language dialect among youth and youth professionals.
2. Integrate animation technologies and creative learning within educational processes through the creation of a unique innovative methodology that aims to make the most of cartoons as a pedagogical tool to teach STEM & to provide the youth practitioners and students with the tools to create their own educational cartoons in order to innovate learning


<< Implementation >>

WP1 Horizontal Activities and Dissemination:
A1- Project management and implementation
A2- Evaluation and quality assurance 
A3 – Dissemination and exploitation
Partnership agreements were signed, and a kickoff meeting on March 10, 2023, defined roles and communication channels between partners. Budget transfers were done. Regular Zoom meetings tracked management, dissemination, research & development activities
Development of a quality assurance plan.  Surveys on satisfaction, communication and evaluation of the outputs were conducted.
Development of a dissemination plan, logos, certificates, and press releases.  Creating a website in English, Croatian, Cypriot, and Romanian, hosting results produced and resources. Creating regular posts on the established channels followed by reports. 
WP2 Cartooned Development Phase:
Research: Creating a 3-part research methodology for STEM, socially excluded youth, and cartoon tools. Each partner conducted country-specific research based on focus group and interview inputs, followed by a comparative analysis.
Development: Creating a 10-session learning program through a role model education methodologies. Elaborating scripts and cartoons revised during piloting.

<< Results >>

The main outputs are: 
WP1 
14 TM meetings during project period, timetable, plans for quality assurance and dissemination, interim report, surveys and reports for quality & dissemination completed 
WP2 A1 
1 Methodological framework for STEM education for youth (7-13 ) 
1 template with 3 types of research/parts(STEM, social inclusion, tools and methodologies) /partner
 3 research analyses with 3 parts: 1 is focused on Maths, physical disability inclusion and 2D traditional & digital techniques, 2nd is focused on Chemistry, neurodivergent inclusion and 2D techniques and 3rd is concentrated on Physics, and refugees & 2d drawing as a technique.
1 conclusion of the analysis of the research that incorporates also tools and resources related to the development of animations and educational cartoons
WP2 A2 
1 learning programme for youth (13-18) that includes the development of digital skills, STEM education and awareness of social inclusion through role-model education methodologies developed
3cartoon scripts developed by partners made in both EN and partners'  language 
3 cartoons synchronised in 3 language dialects of the partners published on the website of the project https://www.cartooned.jednamladost.hr/project/our-cartoons/

2022-3-RS01-KA210-YOU-000098994.title: U korak sa inkluzijom
2022-3-RS01-KA210-YOU-000098994.summary:
<< Background >>

Persons with disabilities, often referred to as "the world's largest minority," generally experience poorer health, lower levels of education, and lower economic status, along with higher rates of poverty compared to persons without disabilities. This places them among groups with fewer opportunities. The project "Catch Up with Inclusion" is based on the right to active participation in cultural and artistic creation. Progress in fostering an inclusive culture is often measured by physical "access" to facilities rather than active participation by persons with disabilities. Cultural and artistic services for children and youth with developmental challenges and disabilities are few, limited in duration and resources, and often characterized by passive support. In the countries of the participating organizations, various acts provide opportunities for persons with disabilities to showcase their talents and skills through engagement in cultural life with equality and non-discrimination. However, in practice, many cultural venues, services, and content remain inaccessible to them. Few cultural and artistic programs are designed for persons with disabilities, are state-funded, and are mostly available to those in larger cities.

<< Objectives >>

The general objective is to improve the quality of cultural/artistic life for young people with disabilities from Serbia, North Macedonia, Croatia, and Bulgaria through creative non-formal learning, participation, and mobility. Specific objectives: 1. Ensure equal participation of young people with disabilities and make them visible in cultural/artistic programs; 2. Boost the self-confidence of young people with disabilities by developing their capacities; 3. Raise awareness and sensitize local community audiences about the artistic/creative potential of young people with disabilities; 4. Reduce social distance between young people with disabilities and those from the general population through joint participation in artistic workshops/programs. Participants are enabled to contribute their knowledge and skills through activities that involved intensive interaction, exchange of ideas, and practical artistic/creative work. The collaboration between young people with disabilities and local volunteers allowed for the discovery of shared values (empathy, solidarity) and the development of critical thinking (information, analysis) through joint experiences in dance, acting, and drawing.

<< Implementation >>

Educational activities for young people with disabilities and from the general population were organized on topics such as creating social media content and film shooting techniques. Through a series of online and in-person rehearsals, young people with disabilities and from the general population were prepared for performances at festivals in Zaječar (Serbia) and Rijeka (Croatia), participation in the program marking International Day of Persons with Disabilities (Skopje, North Macedonia), and presenting artistic work in Vidin (Bulgaria). By attending various workshops (drawing, puppet work, storytelling), activists and young people with disabilities were introduced to additional creative techniques. The engaged volunteers established deeper contact with the target group. Through participation in the omnibus film creation “Color the World,” young people with disabilities increased their visibility. Continuous work and collaboration with artistic mentors have enhanced the competencies and capacities of the target group and organizations. Visits to other cities and countries have improved the quality of life for young people with disabilities.

<< Results >>

The specific results are: the project logo, the creation of project profiles “Catch Up with Inclusion” on social media (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok), the realization of two drama-dance performances showcased at the “Art Zone for All” festival (“Boy from the Water” 2023 and “Drops of Life” 2024, Zaječar, Serbia) and at the ecological film night within the “Sila Fest” (“Boy from the Water” 2023, Zaječar, Serbia), one dance performance (“Six Translations Looking for an Author” at the Festival of Inclusive Scene “Turnaround” 2024, Rijeka, Croatia), one presentation of artistic work methods (2024, Vidin, Bulgaria), three films (omnibus “Color the World,” “Catch Up with Inclusion-Art Zone 2023,” and “Catch Up with Inclusion”). More young people with disabilities than planned were involved. Collaboration with the EU office in Serbia funded additional activities, expanded collaboration of artistic mentors on other projects, established contact between two schools for persons with disabilities and developmental challenges (Serbia and Croatia), and achieved greater project visibility on social media than planned.

2022-3-RS01-KA210-YOU-000101745.title: Mladi za mlade da zajedno rade
2022-3-RS01-KA210-YOU-000101745.summary:
<< Background >>

Our main motivation for applying was the fact that it is necessary to foster a more integral and systematic approach when it comes to the relationship between the systemic policy level and the particular level of practice in youth work, with the regular collection of research data as the linchpin between these two planes. Both policy and outreach which are not informed by data are inefficient and inadequate. The space for adapting fieldwork practices based on research insights is often limited by the legal and strategic framework in place, and in order for data collection to bring about meaningful results it has to be intentional and operational. Many organizations working with marginalized youth face these hurdles and lack the sufficient knowledge, skills and experiences to either begin or further the process of participating in youth policy and advocating for policy reform in accordance with the principles of inclusion of key populations and evidence-based policy creation. We set out to develop the tools necessary for efficient tackling of the issues organizations face both in policy and in outreach, to help them effectively strengthen their position and optimize their approach when it comes to participating in public policy.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objective of this project was to build capacities and competencies (knowledge, skills and experiences) of organizations working with youth who participate in nightlife, youth who use drugs, at-risk and marginalized youth, for participating in youth policy and advocating for public policy reform. The overall goal that we wanted to achieve through this objective was to sustainably contribute to the process of enhancing the safety of the above mentioned categories of youth and improving their position.

<< Implementation >>

Over the course of the project, the following activities were implemented:

- an initial meeting was held to outline the work plan and make arrangements; 
- parallel, uniform research efforts were conducted in the three countries and a summary report of their results was published; 
- a training course on concepts of youth nightlife safety was held; 
- a training course on participating in decision making processes and public policy creation was held; 
- a Manual for participating in youth policy as the main project output was published and distributed as an open-source youth work tool; 
- the project and its outputs were promoted and three national multiplier events were organized to that effect; 
- a final meeting was held to discuss the course of the project and its results, as well as to map out possible space for further cooperation relating to the topic and content of this project.

<< Results >>

The main results of this project, which worked toward the achievement of project objectives, were: 

- participants from partner organizations received necessary knowledge, skills and experience to conduct applied research, conducted said research and shaped the insights gained from it into a summary research report; 
- participants in the first training course acquired competences regarding nightlife safety; 
- participants in the second training course acquired competences regarding participation in youth and public policies and advocating for policy reform; 
- materials developed on the project were shaped through collaborative work of the partners into the Manual and distributed as open-source resources for youth work; 
- seamless and constructive cooperation with partners was achieved and the partners worked in synergy to maintain the highest possible quality of project activities and results and make these results and outputs as accessible and visible to the target groups as possible.

2022-3-TR01-KA210-YOU-000098376.title: Smart-Social Rural Entrepreneurship Programme
2022-3-TR01-KA210-YOU-000098376.summary:
<< Background >>

As part of the project, a ‘Needs Analysis and literature review’  was carried out involving the participating countries, enabling the challenges faced by young farmers and youth organisations in the countries involved to be identified. Here's a more detailed description of the needs: #Lack of Social Entrepreneurship Training Adapted to Young Farmers' Realities; #Limited Access to Agricultural Technologies and Skills Development for Young Farmers; #Youth Workers' Training Needs in Facilitation, Agricultural Technologies, and Social Entrepreneurship #Bridging Gaps in Youth-Rural Organisation Cooperation through International Networks; #Addressing Young Farmers' Barriers to Sustainable Business Development. That said, the project responded to the aforementioned needs by equipping young farmers with digital and social entrepreneurship skills, as well as by creating and solidifying a support network made up of youth workers and local organisations. Overall, the holistic approach, based on the priorities of the Erasmus+ programme (digital transformation, inclusion and sustainability) adopted by the project ensured an effective and sustainable response to the challenges identified by the ‘Needs Analysis and Literature review’. 

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to equip young farmers with technological agricultural skills and social entrepreneurship competencies so that they could create innovative and sustainable social enterprises. To achieve this, an online learning platform was developed, where training content tailored to the needs identified was made available. It is worth mentioning that over 110 young farmers registered on the online learning platform and that the project resulted in the creation of 11 new social initiatives. Additionally, one of the project’s main objectives was the capacity-building of youth workers, ensuring they acquired the skills needed to support and guide local young farmers. In practical terms, the project included non-formal education initiatives targeting youth workers, such as the activity “3.1 Gençlik Çalışanlarına Yönelik Kolaylaştırıcı Eğitimi,” where 12 youth workers received training focused on facilitation methods and non-formal education practices to be applied with young farmers. Finally, the project also promoted international cooperation, developing a network comprising 30+ organizations.The network fosters the exchange of good practices and innovative solutions for rural challenges. 

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were carried out as part of the project, taking into account the needs identified and the objectives set:

1.	Needs analysis and literature review: 
1.1.Needs analysis and literature review; 
1.2.	Project kick off meeting;
1.3.	Press conference; 

2.	Curriculum and Online Learning Platform Development:
2.1.	Development of Training Content for 'Technology-Oriented and Environmentally Sensitive Social Entrepreneurship for Young Farmers';
2.2.	'Facilitator Support Mechanism' and 'Online Learning Platform';
2.3.	Implementation of Content for Farmers;
2.4.	Project Closing Meeting and presentation of the 9 social enterprises;

3.	Facilitator Training and Rural Social Entrepreneurship Network Launch: 
3.1.	Facilitator Training for Youth Workers
3.2.	Rural Social Entrepreneurship Network Launch

Through these activities and the methodologies adopted, it was possible to achieve the proposed objectives and respond to the needs identified by the ‘Needs analysis and literature review’. 


<< Results >>

The “Smart-Social Rural Entrepreneurship Programme (S-SREP)” project delivered significant results aligned with its mission. In concrete terms, the following outputs were achieved:
- Conducted a needs analysis and literature review, resulting in a comprehensive report;
- Developed training content on “Technology orientated and environmentally sensitive social entrepreneurship for young farmers”;
- Created and implemented an online learning platform;
- Trained and prepared 12 youth workers;
- Supported the establishment of 11 social enterprises led by young farmers benefiting from the project platform;
- Established a “Rural Social Entrepreneurship Network.”

2023-1-AT01-KA210-YOU-000160510.title: be up 4 green sport
2023-1-AT01-KA210-YOU-000160510.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project targets financially disadvantaged youth with limited access to outdoor activities, providing a knowledge and awareness-building process. Participants can identify their sportive interests and consider their impact on the environment. The project also raises awareness on environmental sustainability. Additionally, it aims to enhance the partner organizations capacities to plan and carry out projects, develop new skills, exchange knowledge and build long-term cooperations via Erasmus+

<< Implementation >>

1 - meeting between organizations and representatives of youth target group
2 - online meetings to select participants & plan camp
3 - First Aid Course attended by one member of each partner
4 - implementation of environmentally sustainable sports camp in Austria (expression of needs of target group)
5 - meeting to evaluate feedback from participants and organizations
6 - writing a final report dissemination of the project, with local follow-up activities and measures to boost project visibility

<< Results >>

The project gives guidance to participants to: realize their needs are being met, expressing their opinions, experiencing new outdoor activities, minimizing environmental impact. Participants are also encouraged to be more critical of their surrounding environment and think of their behavior to improve it. Associations involved will benefit by building long-lasting partnerships, exchanging expertise, developing methods to address participants' needs, using feedback to create further projects.

2023-1-BG01-KA210-YOU-000151633.title: Стъпки към Еразъм+
2023-1-BG01-KA210-YOU-000151633.summary:
<< Background >>

Възможностите на Програма Еразъм+ са много и трябва да имат авен достъп всички организации и неформални групи. Често обаче, едица организации от селски райони или с нисък административен капациет или без опит по Еразъм+, остават извън обсега на възможностите на Програмата. В тази връзка нашият проект искаше да отговори на тези нужди и да създаде условия за равен достъп но възможностите на Програмата. Нашият проект отговори на нуждите от повишаване на капацитета за работа по проекти, финансирани по Еразъм+, както на младежки организации, така и на неформални младежки групи. Включихме младежи и организации, ръководени от бежанци, бягащи от войната в Украйна, както и от отдалечени и селски райони. Създадохме условия за споделяне на опит и създаване на партньорства за бъдеща работа на европейско ниво. Учебното помагало, което разработихме и пилотирахме отговори на нуждата от развитие на умения за създаване и работа по проекти за мобилности с фокус младежки обмени и мобилности за младежки работници.

<< Objectives >>

Проектът имаше за цел да насърчи и повиши качеството на младежката работа сред младите организации/неформални групи, които нямат опит, за да направят своите първи стъпки по програма Еразъм+. Фокус на проекта бяха организации/неформални групи, които работят с младежи-бежанци от Украйна, младежи с по-малко възможности, изолирани групи от селски райони.
В допълнение проектът насърчи работата в партньорство, междукултурно общуване, споделяне на европейските ценности, популяризиране на Еразъм+.

<< Implementation >>

Целите бяха постигнати чрез съвместни срещина екипа, обучение и споделяне на опит за повишаване на административния капацитет, изработване на План за устойчивост на организациите/неформалните групи, Меморандум за подкрепа и публични събития за споделяне на резултатите от проекта.
Проектът прилагаше подхода за трансфер на знания от опитна организация към организации без опит или с малък опит.

<< Results >>

Резултатите, които постигнахме са:
-Подготвени млади хора (лидери на групи и младежки работници) с нови знания и умения, които да разработват и организират свои проекти според специфични нужди и възможностите на Еразъм+;
-Подобрени възможности за професионално развитие и израстване на младежки работници и на младежки лидери;
-Създадени възможности за приобщаване на младежки работници и на младежки лидери, които са бежанци от Украйна към възможностите на Еразъм+;
- междукултурно общуване.

2023-1-CY02-KA210-YOU-000150520.title: YOU FOCUS
2023-1-CY02-KA210-YOU-000150520.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the critical needs related to the inclusion and support of youth with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) that is recognized as one of the most common disorders affecting young people, often leading to significant challenges such as social exclusion, educational difficulties, stigma, and discrimination. The needs we addressed were rooted in the lack of knowledge and awareness about ADHD among youth workers, communities, and even individuals experiencing the condition. We identified gaps such as:
- Insufficient information and data on ADHD prevalence among young people.
- A mismatch between the needs of youth with ADHD and the strategies youth workers employed to support them.
- Limited inclusive strategies and safe environments tailored for youth with ADHD.

These challenges showed the necessity of promoting knowledge transfer, building inclusive practices, and creating tools and resources to empower youth workers and organizations working with youth with ADHD (especially those located in the participating countries: Cyprus, Romania and Croatia).

<< Objectives >>

YOU FOCUS aimed to achieve several objectives aligned with the priorities of inclusion, diversity, and social engagement. By implementing the project, we successfully:
- Facilitated knowledge exchange and shared best practices, enabling partner organizations to enhance their strategies for inclusion.
- Educated members to plan and organize awareness campaigns and more specifically, through collaborative activities and targeted training, participants were equipped with the skills necessary to design and implement impactful awareness campaigns.
- Provided youth workers with in-depth knowledge about ADHD while they gained practical tools and expertise, enabling them to understand ADHD better and support young people facing this challenge effectively.
- Fostered an open environment where participants were encouraged to discuss health conditions such as ADHD, share experiences, and combat societal and self-stigma.
- Equipped young people with the knowledge and skills needed to adopt healthier practices during adolescence, with the goal of avoiding challenges related to ADHD

<< Implementation >>

During the course of the project, we implemented a series of carefully planned activities to meet our objectives:
A1.  We established a detailed project plan, clarified roles and responsibilities, and monitored progress regularly.
A2. A physical meeting was held in Croatia to launch the project, introduce stakeholders to the objectives, and finalize the working methodology. This meeting also included awareness-raising activities to engage local stakeholders.
A3. We conducted extensive research and developed the "YOU FOCUS Toolkit," which provided youth workers with practical knowledge, strategies, and activities to support young people with ADHD.
A4. A four-day training event in Cyprus equipped youth workers with hands-on skills to identify and support youth with ADHD. The sessions combined theoretical knowledge with practical exercises, using the Toolkit as a foundational resource.
A5. We created a psychoeducational activity book designed to engage and support youth with ADHD. 
A6. During October, we organized many awareness events, webinars, and local activities to highlight the challenges faced by youth with ADHD
A7. Logo, poster, flyer, presentation, infographics, newsletters, social media posts etc

<< Results >>

- The "YOU FOCUS Toolkit" for Youth Workers was developed as a comprehensive resource containing practical strategies for supporting youth with ADHD, educational materials on ADHD awareness, and activity packs designed to foster inclusion and skill-building. The toolkit was shared with participating organizations and made freely accessible online for broader dissemination.

- An Activity Book for Youth with ADHD was created as a psychoeducational tool to help young people manage their condition. This resource combined engaging activities, mindfulness exercises, and practical advice for improving focus and self-regulation. It was made freely available through partner websites, the Erasmus+ platform, and other public repositories.

- The awareness campaign materials included infographics and educational videos, tailored for platforms like TikTok to engage young audiences effectively. These materials were widely shared through social media and used during local events to promote ADHD awareness and social inclusion.

- A training program for youth workers was successfully organized in Cyprus, featuring a four-day session that equipped participants with the knowledge and skills necessary to support young people with ADHD.

2023-1-CZ01-KA210-YOU-000161615.title: Boccia League of Nations - Příležitost pro sport a inkluzi
2023-1-CZ01-KA210-YOU-000161615.summary:
<< Background >>

The main reason was our long-term support for the development of sport and physical activities for young people with all types of disabilities who play sports at an amateur level or even do not sports at all. In the sport of boccia, we have a number of long-standing international partner organisations with whom we have discussed the issue of boccia development and we have agreed that there is a general lack of a professional supply of free and quality information from which not only sports clubs, but especially leisure, educational or therapeutic facilities that can offer this sport to their clients, whether as a form of post-injury therapy, leisure activity or inclusion, could draw. The project focused on youth because of its importance. To shape them, to provide them with a social group background, to bring them among new friends thanks to the inclusive nature of sport and, in rare cases, to start them on the path of a professional athlete. Our biggest impetus has been the lack of equipment, the lack of good information (especially for those working with and educating the target group) and also the personal exchange of experiences, as this is something that has the greatest added value across all activities.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to achieve a closer connection between organizations and sports clubs focusing on and working with youth with disabilities and to achieve mutual international cooperation in the development of an inclusive form of this sport. This is the only way to achieve long-term development and support across European countries, exchange of knowledge and know-how. Furthermore, we wanted to equip individual NGO with basic sports equipment, which will enable those who cannot afford the equipment to start playing the sport and enable the organizations to present the sport in schools, workshops, etc. We consider education to be key and therefore we set as a goal to connect with experts in various fields that generally affect the world of physical activity, sport, the NGO sector and youth work. The aim was to educate those who work with youth and provide them with much needed knowhow. The final goal was to summarize everything in a guidebook that would be freely accessible to all. The aim is to disseminate the knowledge gained without exception. Thus, the project as a whole has been developed with specific objectives and activities that have an impact not only on specific individuals but also on the general public working in the sector.

<< Implementation >>

The first activity was international partner meeting to introduce the organisations and their activities to each other, to establish personal contact with the representatives, to discuss the actual content of the project so that the activities could be adapted as much as possible to the actual needs of the individual partners. An important point was the handover of sports equipment to all partners. Other activities were a series of 8 webinars. Their content, the individual experts and the targeting was developed in cooperation with all partners. The aim was to set out 8 basic topics, to bring the best experts on the individual webinars topics and to preserve the know-how through the recordings of the webinars so that everyone can draw on them in the future. Important activities were also two workshops, which focused on practical knowledge of the boccia and theoretical in the field of organizing and conducting sports events, promotion and marketing. All with the aim of educating the partners and their colleagues, staff and other individuals who apply the knowledge gained in their work with youth with disabilities who also attended the workshops. All the know-how gained is summarized in a guidebook, links for webinars are included.

<< Results >>

We were able to provide quality equipment for each partner and hand them over during the international meeting. The meeting led to the strengthening of relationships and ensured the smooth running of the project. We achieved a great success in organising a series of webinars where we achieved the participation of international experts from different European countries. These were university professors, experts from the field, Paralympians and the information obtained is of great value and is a deep know how. The participation of these experts reached the professional level. We were especially grateful for the way these speakers appreciated the whole project and its added value. We also achieved a great success in the workshops, with Paralympians and youth coaching experts participating as experts in the practical workshop, and organizers of major international sports inclusion events participating in the theoretical workshop. The final output of the project in the form of a guidebook achieves a high value, mainly due to the combination of know-how, graphic output and overall good readability. To be environmentally friendly, we provided everything we could in electronic form and kept printouts and waste to a minimum.

2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000150424.title: Pan Flute - Let’s Engage in Climate Action
2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000150424.summary:
<< Background >>

As stated in the application, the involved organisations aimed to create a method to raise awareness about environmental issues, preservation, and eco-anxiety, enabling local action and promoting climate initiatives. We applied for this project because we believe real change comes from connecting youth to their environment and nature. Our goal was to provide tools for youth to build a personal connection with nature and their communities in a sustainable way, while addressing eco-anxiety.
The organisations wanted to tackle these issues creatively, as traditional youth work methods needed radical updates, especially after the Covid pandemic. Using Erasmus+ support, we developed a joint curriculum with innovative methods for youth workers, addressing both climate awareness and mental health, including eco-anxiety.
Additionally, our organisations needed to build capacity for international collaboration in Erasmus+. As newcomer organisations (Aiki En from Croatia and Human and Tree from Romania), this project marked our first step towards European-level cooperation.


<< Objectives >>

Our project had three objectives.

By implementing this project we wanted, first of all, to create a methodology of eco-activism youth work. This is meant to contribute to the solution of the growing problem of the environment, climate change, and the spread of eco-anxiety among young people. To achieve this we decided to join forces and co create this project in which we build a handbook for youth workers on the topic of nature connection.
A second objective  was to test the methodology contained in the handbook with our target groups, in our local realities, so we can improve it if needed and make it impactful.
And third but not less important was to raise the capacity of our organisations to work locally and regionally on eco-activism youth work and to build the strength and knowledge of our organisations to collaborate in international projects and in Erasmus+ and ESC programs.

Moreover, these methods were also needed in our daily work with youngsters, and we achieved that aim also.


<< Implementation >>

In the project we implemented the following activities: 1.project management, 2.building the intellectual output, 3.testing methods on local/regional scale, 4.two transnational meetings and 5.local conferences for dissemination and multiplication of the results, that took place in each partner country.  
All activities implemented in this project were non-formal and informal: 1. activities of connecting with nature in non formal embodiment methodology (embodiment, centring, grounding, role play games, enacting situations, dance, visualization, conscious breathing, mindfulness, Shinrin Yoku, etc)
 - activities based on eco-psychology methods (nature wanders, buzz groups, active reviewing, individual and group reflection, journaling, storytelling, nature dialogue, active imagery, symbolic artwork, drumming and rhythm,  etc)
 - activities that are focused on volunteering (Human library on volunteering, Hero’s journey model   on evaluating and planning volunteering experiences, storytelling and role play games, etc)

The decision-making process was carried out according to the principles of sociocracy, where we respected the opinion of each individual member and decisions were made in accordance.


<< Results >>

The project achieved key outputs: international cooperation in Erasmus+, increased organizational capacity locally and internationally, greater visibility in local communities, and enhanced knowledge sharing. We improved project management, organized workshops and events, and exchanged good practices between partner organizations.

A major result was the youth worker manual Pan Flute – Give me a bio break, focused on nature connection. It was translated and printed in four languages (Eng 155, Cro 50, Ro 90, Lv 15; total: 310) and made available as an E-book. Between 01.09 and 02.12., the project webpage had 152 visits, and the E-book was downloaded 262 times (Cro 143, Eng 82, Ro 33, Lv 4), also shared on the Salto Youth portal. Additionally, 12 short reels on nature connection were shared on partner platforms.

The Croatian organization secured a new partnership with a Zagreb high school and applied for a joint local project. The Romanian organization partnered with a high school and youth group, gaining municipal support and outdoor spaces for activities. The Latvian organization expanded eco-activism and nature connection in training courses, youth exchanges, and volunteering projects.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
