2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000156901.title: Think Green, Act Local
2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000156901.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to seize new opportunities to strengthen the capacities of partner organizations in youth work, sustainable development, environmental protection, and social entrepreneurship. Our aim was to create healthier, more supportive environments in local communities to motivate young people toward personal growth, inform them about EU youth programs, help them overcome challenges, promote active participation, and raise awareness of the value of non-formal learning and volunteering.By recognizing the real needs of young people and their communities, we supported the development of new working methods, the exchange of good practices among partners, and laid the groundwork for long-term cooperation and greater inclusion of youth with fewer opportunities. The project connected local and international organizations and initiatives, fostered the exchange of knowledge and innovative approaches, and encouraged the use of sustainable practices in youth work—ultimately contributing to youth empowerment, community development, and stronger organizational collaboration.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to strengthen the capacities of partner organizations for higher quality and more innovative work with young people with fewer opportunities, in the fields of sustainable development, environmental and nature protection, and social entrepreneurship. Our goal was to develop and apply new non-formal methods and tools in youth work in order to empower young people in society, encourage their greater involvement in the community, and raise awareness of important environmental and social issues. We also wanted to enable the exchange of knowledge, experiences, and good practices between organizations from different communities and countries, and to empower the staff of partner organizations through education, experiential, and non-formal learning. Through this project, we sought to create an encouraging environment for young people and equal opportunities for all, open new possibilities for cooperation and networking between organizations and youth through a digital platform, and inspire other organizations to improve existing or create new services and activities for young people with fewer opportunities in the thematic area.

<< Implementation >>

Kick-off conference + Kick-off meeting;Training for working with youth for representatives of the "Krka" association; Local activities for youth in Croatia (research on the needs and issues of young people, painting and distributing canvas bags, campaigns and workshops on EU policies and programs for youth, mobility, non-formal education, volunteering, youth activism, and establishing the Youth Club);Local activities for youth in Italy (online research for youth on habits regarding sustainability and environmental protection, workshops on the 3R, recycling, reuse, and making eco-book houses, cleaning actions, initiatives on European citizenship and youth mobility, EU functioning, activities for informing youth about EU policies and combating climate change);Training on sustainable development, environmental and nature protection, social entrepreneurship for representatives of the "Noi@Europe" organization;Online platform "Learn, Exchange, Act and Apply", ;Development of the "Green and Youth, learning tools" manual and working materials in Italian, Croatian, and English;Mentorship - Monitoring the work of partner organizations;Final conference + final partner meeting; Project management; Promotion and dissemination of the project

<< Results >>

Increased knowledge of staff and the capacities of partner organizations in the fields of youth work with fewer opportunities, sustainable development, environmental protection, and social entrepreneurship; 4 staff members of partner organizations developed knowledge and skills, adopting informal methods and approaches in the thematic area through mentoring activities;A manual "Green and Youth, Learning Tools" with informal methods and tools was created.; An online platform "Learn, Exchange, Act and Apply" was developed; 250 young people actively participated in local youth activities in Italy and Croatia; A Youth Club was established in Lukar; 3 videos were created about the project, its activities, and the achieved results;3 book-sharing boxes were built and placed to promote the reuse of items in the local community; Increased public awareness of the importance of working with youth with fewer opportunities ;563 young people in Croatia and Italy participated in the survey; 800 cotton bags were painted and distributed to promote ecological awareness; Young people gained new knowledge and skills on ecological and social topics, EU opportunities, activism, and non-formal learning.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Quality and innovation of youth work

2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000157269.title: Iskustvo tugovanja mladih kao resurs za osobni rast i razvoj
2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000157269.summary:
<< Background >>

The project "Youth grieving experience as a resource for personal growth and development" was designed for young people aged 18 to 29 who have experienced grief due to the death of a close person. It was developed in response to the lack of such services in the Republic of Croatia and the general absence of structured support for grieving youth at the societal level.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were to:
•	Strengthen the professional capacities of the Association "Children First" and the Silesian University in Opava in the field of working with grieving youth;
•	Provide professional support to young people experiencing grief due to the loss of a loved one through the preparation and implementation of a pilot group support programme;
•	Inform both professionals and the general public by disseminating the knowledge and experiences gained in working with grieving youth.


<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, a training course for professionals from Association "Children First" was held in Opava (Czech Republic), focused on providing support to individuals dealing with grief. The training was delivered by experts from the Faculty of Public Policies at the Silesian University. Following the development of the pilot group support programme for grieving youth, two cycles of ten workshops were held, as well as a two-day experiential learning workshop in nature titled "Reflect, Share, Contribute!". To raise awareness among professionals and the wider public and to disseminate the results and experiences from the implementation of the support programme, five audio podcasts were created and published. Additionally, support materials were developed for young people experiencing grief and the general public. An online handbook was also written and published in both Croatian and Czech, containing experiences and recommendations for working with young people who are grieving the death of a close person. The project's outcomes and experiences were also presented at a round table for professionals.

<< Results >>

Key results achieved through the project include:
•	A 5-day training programme on working with grieving individuals was organized, prepared, and implemented, with 7 professionals from the Association "Children First" trained by the partner institution Silesian University in Opava;
•	A structured psychoeducational group support programme was developed for young people grieving the loss of a close person;
•	Two cycles of 10 workshops were held, strengthening the resilience and coping skills of 9 young participants;
•	A two-day experiential learning workshop in nature was conducted, attended by young people involved in project activities and professionals (12 participants);
•	A working partner meeting for the development of the handbook was organized and attended by 10 professionals;
•	An online handbook (in Croatian and Czech) was created and published, offering best practice recommendations for supporting grieving youth, based on the knowledge and experiences gained during the project;
•	Five audio podcasts were published, sharing young people's experiences of participating in the project activities;
•	A professional round table was held to present the project activities, outcomes, and experiences.

2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000162061.title: Stimulating environment for the integration of young people with disabilities
2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000162061.summary:
<< Background >>

The beneficiaries of the association Kamenčići are people with intellectual disabilities, and most of them, in addition to health issues, share the same problem – social marginalization. All activities of the association are aimed at better and more meaningful inclusion of its beneficiaries in society through various programs, as well as providing them with services they need but cannot obtain elsewhere. Applying for this project was an opportunity to strengthen the capabilities of the association’s staff by acquiring new knowledge and skills in order to better support their beneficiaries. Since we had previously cooperated with an association from Hungary, we realized that we face similar challenges. Through this project, we aimed to enhance the competencies of both organizations to provide higher quality services to our beneficiaries, improve their work and life skills, and enable them to become equal members of the community.

<< Objectives >>

Through the implementation of this project, we aimed to strengthen the capacities of the organization in a way that would allow us to offer services and activities to beneficiaries who have completed their education but, being unprepared for the labor market, found themselves spending most of their time at home, completely excluded from the community. With this project, we wanted to "bring" these beneficiaries — in both partner organizations — out of their homes by gradually integrating them into the community, starting with workshops and social activities with people of similar abilities, and progressively including them in community life by developing their cognitive, motor, and social skills to levels that would allow them to participate more easily and fully in various social settings.
Another goal of this project was to encourage empathy and volunteering among high school students, making them aware that there are people in their community with fewer abilities, but who are by no means less valuable, and to actively involve them in volunteering activities to help reduce the stigmatization of people with intellectual disabilities in the wider community. 

<< Implementation >>

During the project, 40 workshops were held as part of the local activities within the two partner organizations. At the Kamenčići association, five workshops were held for each of the following: papier-mâché, gardening, weaving, and ceramics. In the partner organization, as planned by the project, six workshops were held for each of the following: planting and gardening, as well as papier-mâché and recycling, along with four art workshops, three sensory integration workshops, and one environmental clean-up workshop. An opening and a closing conference for the project were also organized.Additionally, potential volunteers attended a training session on volunteering, delivered by the president of the Kamenčići association.As part of the knowledge exchange activities, there were two study visits. In the first, employees and beneficiaries of the Fogd a Kezem association visited Šibenik, where they attended weaving and papier-mâché workshops, participated in physiotherapy exercises alongside Kamenčići’s beneficiaries, and took part in joint art workshops. Employees and beneficiaries from the Kamenčići association later visited Pécs, where they participated in sensory integration workshops, recycling workshops, and candle-making works. 

<< Results >>

The concrete results of the project implementation are:


Two strengthened civil society organizations in two EU countries, with employees improving their work capacities, knowledge, and skills in working with marginalized groups, as well as establishing networking as a foundation for future collaboration as a continuation of this project.

More than 30 people with intellectual disabilities better integrated into society, with increased independence in work and daily life, improved motor and cognitive skills, and education on the importance of planting, environmental protection, and healthy lifestyle habits.

Increased or newly developed empathy among 10 volunteers from the medical school, who received education on various methods of working with people with intellectual disabilities, which will assist them in their future careers and help eliminate prejudices against people with disabilities.

The wider public was sensitized to the abilities of people with disabilities when given opportunities, as well as to their need for more meaningful inclusion in society, while other civil society organizations were encouraged to apply for Erasmus+ calls themselves.

hr.name: Udruga osoba s intelektualnim teškoćama Šibensko - kninske županije "Kamenčići"

2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000162169.title: Going green in youth work using IT
2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000162169.summary:
<< Background >>

We addressed several key needs of youth organizations and NGOs, including needed skills development in green organizational management, access to resources like specialized handbook and templates and a dedicated GreenIT platform, and increased awareness of sustainability. Project promoted digital transformation through use of IT tools, fostered collaboration among organizations, and enhanced advocacy skills for environmental policies. Additionally, the project emphasized collective action and long-term sustainability planning, empowering youth to become environmental leaders and advocates.

We applied for this project because all the partners are dedicated to promoting environmental sustainability within youth organizations especially with use of digital tools. Given the urgent challenges posed by climate change, we felt it was essential for youth organizations to incorporate green management practices into their operations. 

Project directly addressed the need for practical tools that can empower youth organizations to adopt green management practices without relying too much on external experts and the demand for accessible, centralized information on green practices specifically designed for the youth sector.


<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project "GreenIT" was to ensure environmental sustainability of youth organizations by using green organizational management practices, focusing on use of IT tools, in order to enable NGOs across Europe to use new, environment friendly, sustainable and digital approaches in their work.

One of the primary objectives (SO1. To enhance the capacities of NGOs in the youth sector in the use of green organizational management practices in their work by creating specialized handbook and templates) was to equip youth organizations with the knowledge and tools necessary to adopt green organizational management practices. 

Establishing the "GreenIT" platform (SO2. To create „GreenIT“ platform open for NGOs in the youth sector in order to provide them with relevant information and materials to use in their work) was essential for providing ongoing access to relevant information and resources. 

We also wanted to drive awareness about the importance of environmental sustainability within the youth sector through social media and advocacy campaigns (SO3. To promote the use of green organizational management practices in the youth sector).


<< Implementation >>

1. Kick-off PTM: We initiated the project with a team meeting to establish roles, responsibilities, and timelines.
2. Creation of the Green Organizational Management Handbook and Templates: We developed a comprehensive Green Organizational Management Handbook containing ten specialized templates to facilitate the implementation of these practices.
3. Second PTM: We focused on reviewing progress, discussing challenges, and preparation for the upcoming phases of the project.
4. Creation of the GreenIT Platform: We developed and tested the "GreenIT" platform, that provides access to the handbook and templates, promoting collaboration and sharing of best practices.
5. Third PTM: We evaluated the outcomes of the platform testing and finalized the plans regarding Advocacy campaigns, ensuring that we effectively address the needs of the youth organizations.
6. Dissemination and Advocacy Campaigns: We conducted social media campaigns and three advocacy campaigns in partnering countries to raise awareness about green organizational practices. 
7. PM and Administration: Throughout the project, we maintained ongoing management and administrative tasks to ensure smooth operations, effective communication,and accountability among all partners

<< Results >>

R1. We developed a comprehensive handbook, available in English, Croatian and Serbian, designed specifically for youth organizations on Green Organizational Management. This resource provides practical guidelines on implementing green organizational management practices, including strategies for waste reduction and energy conservation, with a focus on using different IT tools.

R2. We created ten specialized Green Organizational Management templates that youth organizations can use to streamline their implementation of sustainable practices. These templates cover various aspects of green management, making it easier for youth organizations to set goals and track their progress effectively.

R3. We created GreenIT Platform (www.greenit-project.eu), an online platform that serves as a centralized resource for youth organizations regarding green organizational management. The platform was published and tested with 27 NGOs, gathering feedback to enhance its usability and effectiveness. 

R4. We successfully implemented social media campaigns and three advocacy campaigns in partnering countries, which raised awareness about the importance of environmental sustainability and encouraged youth organizations to adopt green practices.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000167296.title: Youth Employability data relevance, gathering and processing
2023-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000167296.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was developed in response to the growing need for youth organizations, including our own, to improve their capacity in data-driven decision-making. While youth employability remains a key priority across Europe, many organizations lack the necessary tools, skills, and knowledge to collect, process, and use data effectively to inform their strategies and programs. This gap limits the impact and sustainability of their work. The project addresses this challenge by equipping partner organizations with practical competencies in data gathering, analysis, and application. It also responds to the need for better alignment between research, practice, and policy in the field of youth work. By strengthening the digital and analytical capacity of youth workers and promoting evidence-based approaches, the project contributes to more informed, impactful, and innovative youth employability initiatives at local and regional levels.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to strengthen the capacity of youth organizations to use data effectively in their work, with a specific focus on youth employability. We aimed to equip youth workers, project managers, and staff with the knowledge and skills to gather, process, analyze, and apply data in strategic planning, project development, and communication. By doing so, the project sought to promote data-driven decision-making, enhance the quality and impact of youth initiatives, and foster innovation within the sector. In addition, the project aimed to develop practical outputs such as a joint publication and a series of articles that showcase the use of data in youth work. Through training, workshops, peer learning, and collaboration, the project also intended to improve transnational cooperation, support digital transformation in youth work, and contribute to a more evidence-based and responsive approach to tackling youth employability challenges across partner regions.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through a series of interconnected activities designed to build capacity, promote collaboration, and produce meaningful outputs. It began with a kickoff event during Dubrovnik EXPO, bringing partners together and ensuring a shared understanding of the project. A training on data gathering and processing was held in Belgrade, equipping participants with key skills in statistics, data collection, and analysis. Each partner then conducted a six-month data gathering and processing process in their local contexts. Based on the collected data, a workshop in Senj focused on how to interpret and use the results to develop publications, strategies, and improve project writing. This was followed by the creation of a collaborative publication and eight articles on youth employability. The project concluded with a hybrid closing event in Belgrade, where results were presented and shared with stakeholders. Throughout the project, dissemination and project management activities ensured visibility, coordination, and impact.

<< Results >>

The project resulted in several concrete and tangible outputs. A key achievement was the collaborative publication summarizing the findings from the data gathered by partner organizations on youth employability, highlighting trends, challenges, and opportunities in the partner regions. In addition, eight thematic articles were produced, focusing on various aspects of youth work and employability, and shared in English and partner languages. These materials serve as practical resources for youth workers and organizations beyond the partnership. The project also contributed to the development of new skills among youth workers, particularly in data collection, analysis, and application. It enhanced the digital and analytical capacities of partner organizations and strengthened cross-border cooperation. The events organized - including the training, workshop, and closing event  promoted peer learning, stakeholder engagement, and visibility, ensuring both local relevance and broader European impact.

2023-1-HU01-KA210-YOU-000155714.title: The Value Of Waste
2023-1-HU01-KA210-YOU-000155714.summary:
<< Background >>

Célunk az volt, hogy a fiatalokkal foglalkozó szakembereket gyakorlati eszközökkel lássuk el a fenntarthatósági kihívások – különösen a hulladékprobléma – kezeléséhez, nem-formális oktatás segíségével. Régióinkban a fiatalok klímatémák iránti elköteleződése alacsony, a zöld gyakorlatokat sokszor trendként kezelik, nem mély meggyőződésből követik ezeket. Hiszünk abban, hogy ifjúsági munkásként felelősségünk a fiatalokat olyan eszközökkel támogatni, amelyek elősegítik egy élhetőbb jövő megalapozását. A mai környezeti válságban a klímavédelem már nem választás kérdése – elengedhetetlen és megkerülhetetlen feladat. Partnerszervezeteink már rendelkeznek fenntartható gyakorlatokkal kapcsolatos tapasztalattal, amelyeket meg kívántunk osztani egymással és másokkal, hogy inspiráljuk, támogassuk a fiatalokat. A zöldrefestés és a felszínes elköteleződés helyett valódi, mélyebb kapcsolódást akartunk létrehozni, a hulladék témáját vonzó és kézzelfogható módon megközelítve. A partnerek a saját szakértelmüknek megfelelő releváns hulladéktípusokra – textil, műanyag, szerves – összpontosítottak és osztották meg tudásukat.


<< Objectives >>

A Value of Waste projekt fő célja az volt, hogy kíváncsiságot és cselekvést ébresszen a hulladék témájában– amely a klímaváltozás egyik jelentős okozója –, és környezeti, valamint társadalmi kihívásként mutassa be azt. Szerettük volna megváltoztatni a hulladékról alkotott képet: értékként tekinteni rá, és felelős, fenntartható alternatívákat népszerűsíteni a mindennapi szokások helyett. A projekt célja az volt, hogy egy olyan együttműködő teret hozzon létre az ifjúsági munkások számára, ahol tudást, eszközöket oszthatnak meg egymással országhatárokon átívelően. Gyakorlati és könnyen használható eszközöket fejlesztettünk ki a zöld készségek elsajátításának elősegítésére, a hulladékcsökkentés, az újrahasználat és a körforgásos szemlélet előmozdítására. Célunk volt a fiatalok vezetői szerepének és önbizalmának megerősítése is, hogy közösségükben a fenntarthatóság szószólóivá válhassanak. Helyi szinten releváns hulladéktípusokra – textil, szerves és műanyag – fókuszáltunk. Ezek segítségével szeretnénk a csökkenteni a klímaváltozatás kapcsán érzett csüggedséget, és erős alapot képezni tartós, alulról jövő változásokak. 

<< Implementation >>

A Value of Waste projekt során sokféle tevékenységet valósítottunk meg az ifjúsági munkások megerősítése és a fenntartható viselkedés ösztönzése érdekében. Három nemzetközi tanulmányutat szerveztünk, mindegyiket más hulladéktípus – textil, szerves és műanyag – köré építve, amelyek gyakorlati műhelymunkákat, releváns helyszínlátogatásokat és közösségi tanulást tartalmaztak. Közösen fejlesztettünk ki innovatív oktatási eszközöket, például a „Be the Change” társasjátékot és kvízkártyákat, hogy játékos módon vonjuk be a fiatalokat a fenntarthatóságról szóló diskurzusba. 12 tematikus hírlevelet készítettünk gyakorlati ötletekkel, több mint 450 feliratkozót elérve. Helyi műhelyeket és közösségi eseményeket tartottunk, például a zágrábi VoW Fesztivált, amelyen több mint 190 látogató vett részt. Elindítottunk egy Instagram-oldalt, és befogadó intézkedésekkel támogattuk a kevesebb lehetőséggel rendelkező résztvevőket – például nyelvi segítségnyújtással és a vidéki fiatalok bevonásával.

<< Results >>

A projekt számos kézzelfogható eredményt és valódi hatást hozott. Létrehoztuk a fenntarthatóságot támogató „Be the Change” társasjátékot és kvízkártyákat, melyek az ifjúsági munkában segítik a környezeti nevelést. Tizenkét tematikus hírlevelet adtunk ki a textil-, élelmiszer- és műanyaghulladék témáiban, több mint 450 feliratkozóhoz eljuttatva. Három nemzetközi tanulmányutat, több mint 12 helyi workshopot és egy nyilvános fesztivált is szerveztünk, ahol több mint 190 látogató vett részt. Elindítottunk egy dedikált Instagram-oldalt és online tanulási anyagokat. A részt vevő ifjúsági munkások gyakorlati eszközökkel, készségekkel és tapasztalatokkal gazdagodtak, a partnerszervezetek pedig erősítették kapcsolati hálójukat. A kérdőívek és visszajelzések alapján a résztvevők több mint 70%-a változtatott a mindennapi szokásain. A projekt fenntartható szokásokat népszerűsített, új szemléletet hozott a hulladékról, és megalapozta a jövőbeli kreatív, befogadó és közösségi kezdeményezéseket.

2023-1-IT03-KA210-YOU-000153555.title: CARE: Climate action role-playing experience
2023-1-IT03-KA210-YOU-000153555.summary:
<< Background >>

Il progetto CARE è stato sviluppato per rispondere a tre esigenze principali identificate in Europa:

1. Bassa consapevolezza sui cambiamenti climatici tra i giovani (16-30 anni): nonostante l'urgenza della crisi climatica, i giovani spesso percepiscono il cambiamento climatico come un problema distante e complesso, con scarsa fiducia nell'azione collettiva. Solo il 9% dei giovani crede che il mondo agirà abbastanza rapidamente (UNEP, 2008).

2. Necessità di strumenti educativi innovativi per gli youth worker (YW): gli YW mancano di strumenti coinvolgenti e interattivi per sensibilizzare i giovani. La crisi climatica genera ansia e paura, ostacolando l'impegno sociale (EU IPOL, 2020).

3. Scarso utilizzo dei giochi di ruolo (GDR) nell'educazione ambientale: i GDR si sono dimostrati estremamente efficaci per promuovere consapevolezza e azione, ma il loro utilizzo è ancora piuttosto ridotto.

CARE ha contribuito a colmare queste lacune creando un gioco di ruolo educativo, formando YW e coinvolgendo giovani attraverso esperienze interattive e partecipative.

Ha inoltre fornito una concreta esperienza di crescita per l’applicant (newcomer) e le organizzazioni coinvolte, potenziandone l’azione e la rete



<< Objectives >>

Gli obiettivi del progetto CARE erano tre:

1. Fornire strumenti educativi innovativi agli youth worker (YW): L’obiettivo era creare un gioco di ruolo (GDR) che permettesse agli YW di sensibilizzare i giovani sul cambiamento climatico (CC) in modo interattivo ed emotivamente coinvolgente. Questo approccio puntava a colmare la mancanza di strumenti educativi efficaci per affrontare un tema complesso come il CC, spesso percepito come distante dai giovani.

2. Sensibilizzare i giovani (16-30 anni) sui cambiamenti climatici: L’obiettivo era utilizzare il GDR per rendere i giovani più consapevoli dei meccanismi del CC, coinvolgendoli in situazioni pratiche e motivandoli ad agire. Si è scelto questo approccio perché i giovani, pur essendo tra i più colpiti dagli effetti del CC, mostrano spesso sfiducia verso l’azione collettiva.

3. Migliorare la capacità delle organizzazioni partner: CARE mirava a rafforzare le competenze organizzative, gestionali e di rete delle ONG coinvolte, creando collaborazioni transnazionali e scambi di buone pratiche. Questo era necessario perché le organizzazioni partecipanti avevano esperienza limitata nella gestione di progetti internazionali e nell’uso di metodi innovativi come il GDR.


<< Implementation >>

Oltre alle attività di Project managing CARE ha implementato diverse attività suddivise in tre fasi principali:

1. Ricerca e Networking: Ogni partner ha svolto ricerche locali per identificare stakeholder interessati e raccogliere opinioni sul cambiamento climatico tramite questionari. Questo ha permesso di creare una rete locale solida per supportare le attività successive.

2. Sviluppo del Gioco e Formazione: È stato sviluppato un gioco di ruolo educativo sul cambiamento climatico, curando sia l’ambientazione che la meccanica di gioco. Sono stati poi organizzati seminari virtuali e un training internazionale in Croazia per formare 15 operatori giovanili (5 per partner) all’uso del gioco, approfondendo sia le dinamiche di facilitazione che il contesto scientifico.

3. Implementazione Locale e Disseminazione: Gli YW formati hanno condotto 36 sessioni locali nei tre paesi partner, utilizzando il gioco per coinvolgere giovani tra i 16 e i 30 anni. Inoltre, sono stati organizzati eventi di disseminazione locale finali per condividere i risultati e promuovere l’uso del gioco. Il progetto ha incluso attività di comunicazione web costante per tutto il progetto e un evento finale, garantendo un’ampia diffusione e sostenibilità.


<< Results >>

Gioco di ruolo educativo sul cambiamento climatico: È stato creato un GDR progettato per sensibilizzare i giovani sui problemi legati al cambiamento climatico. Il gioco è stato sviluppato in versione digitale e alcune copie fisiche, il tutto in quattro lingue (italiano, inglese, polacco, croato), garantendo accessibilità e diffusione.

Formazione di youth worker: 15 YW provenienti da Italia, Polonia e Croazia sono stati formati per facilitare l’uso del gioco durante un training internazionale. Questi YW hanno acquisito competenze innovative e strumenti pratici per l’educazione non formale

Attività locali e sensibilizzazione dei giovani: Gli YW formati hanno condotto 36 sessioni di gioco nei tre paesi partner, coinvolgendo oltre 360 giovani tra i 16 e i 30 anni. Le attività hanno aumentato la consapevolezza sui cambiamenti climatici e promosso l’azione concreta a livello locale

Rafforzamento della rete tra organizzazioni: Il progetto ha migliorato la cooperazione tra i partner, consolidando una rete transnazionale e aumentando le capacità organizzative delle ONG coinvolte.

topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2023-1-LT02-KA210-YOU-000165246.title: Power of Volunteering
2023-1-LT02-KA210-YOU-000165246.summary:
<< Background >>

Projektą „Power of Volunteering“ inicijavome siekdami skatinti jaunimo įsitraukimą į savanorystę ir supažindinti su savanorystės sistemomis bei tradicijomis skirtingose šalyse. Projekto metu buvo siekiama suteikti jaunimui praktinės patirties, ugdyti pilietinius ir socialinius įgūdžius, skatinti tarpkultūrinį bendradarbiavimą bei atsižvelgti į jaunimo įvairovę ir mažesnes galimybes turinčius dalyvius.

<< Objectives >>

Projekto tikslas – skleisti savanorystės idėją ir kultūrą, suteikti jauniems žmonėms galimybių auginti savo įgūdžius ir kompetencijas, įkvepiant juos įsitraukti į savanorišką veiklą ir parodant išskirtines šalies sąlygas ir galimybes savanoriauti. 

<< Implementation >>

Projekto metu įvyko penki tarptautiniai renginiai Lietuvoje, Italijoje, Kroatijoje, Kipre ir Turkijoje. Veiklos apėmė praktinius užsiėmimus, vizitus į NVO ir savivaldybių skyrius, diskusijas, edukacinių plakatų rengimą, tarpkultūrinio mokymosi užsiėmimus, dalyvių įtraukimą į realią savanorystę bei finalinių video kūrimą. Visose šalyse partneriai užtikrino renginių logistiką, dalyvių pasiruošimą, viešinimą ir rezultatų sklaidą.

<< Results >>

Projekto metu tiesiogiai pasiekta 77 jaunų žmonių, o netiesiogiai – daugiau nei 150 per renginius, viešinimą ir bendruomenines iniciatyvas. Bendras online viešinimo pasiekiamumas siekė apie 10 000 žmonių. Sukurti penki motyvaciniai video, parengta edukacinė medžiaga ir lankstinukai apie savanorystę. Dalyviai įgijo socialinių, pilietinių ir asmeninių kompetencijų, sustiprėjo tarptautiniai ryšiai, organizacijos pagerino projektų valdymo ir komunikacijos įgūdžius. Projektas buvo plačiai viešinamas per socialinius tinklus, vietinius renginius ir partnerių kanalus, užtikrinant, kad rezultatai būtų prieinami visuomenei ir naudojami ateityje.

2023-1-NL02-KA210-YOU-000155134.title: Girl Boss Collective - Empowering Young Women to Start a Business
2023-1-NL02-KA210-YOU-000155134.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because of the underrepresentation of women in the field of entrepreneurship across Europe. According to Eurostat, only 23.7% of entrepreneurs in Spain, 30.5% in the Netherlands, and 32.6% in Croatia are women. This highlights a significant gender gap that needs to be addressed, especially when it comes to young women. Through this project, we aimed to inspire women at a young age in entrepreneurship, as the earlier they can be inspired, the more dedicated and committed they will become. Therefore, we wanted to create a project that empowers girls aged 13 to 18 by providing them with entrepreneurial skills and encouraging them to pursue entrepreneurship as a viable career option. Through practical tools, mentorship from female role models, and non-formal learning opportunities, we sought to address the need for gender diversity in entrepreneurship, contribute to economic growth, and inspire a new generation of female entrepreneurs. This project is not only about improving employability but also about encouraging confidence, innovation, and leadership among young women.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objective of the project was to empower young women, aged 13 to 18, to explore entrepreneurship and develop the skills necessary to start and manage their own businesses. We aimed to increase awareness of the opportunities available in the (social) entrepreneurial world, especially for girls who may not typically be exposed to such possibilities. By doing so, we wanted to address the gender gap in entrepreneurship and contribute to a more balanced representation of women in business.
Furthermore, the project aimed to provide youth workers with the resources and training to inspire and guide girls toward entrepreneurship. We also aimed to create a dynamic and engaging learning environment where young women could network, collaborate, and learn practical skills. In the long term, we hope to encourage a generation of confident, skilled, and innovative young female entrepreneurs who can contribute to economic growth and gender equality.

<< Implementation >>

Key activities implemented:
GBC Toolbox: A practical toolbox with non-formal learning activities to inspire girls aged 13–18 to explore entrepreneurial opportunities. The toolbox includes exercises on topics like finance, personal skills, marketing, sustainability, and planning. There are two versions: one targeted for the girls and one guiding youth workers on how to use the tools and activities. 
GBC Database of Female Role Models: A database of 22 inspiring female entrepreneurs from the partner regions, who were willing to share their stories to inspire young women. 
Girl Boss Bootcamp: A bootcamp to bring together young women, youth workers, and female entrepreneurs for hands-on learning sessions organised by each partner. The bootcamp combined several activities developed in the toolbox and the database. 
Also two transnational meetings were held to facilitate the discussion of planning, monitoring, and evaluation of the project’s progress, ensuring alignment with the project’s goals. Moreover, during the project duration, we engaged in promotional activities (e.g. online flyers, social media posts, direct contact with youth organisations and schools) to recruit participants and raise awareness about the project’s goals. 

<< Results >>

Key outputs and results:
1 GBC Toolbox: A toolbox with 15 activities focused on entrepreneurship, divided among 5 categories: Getting to know your inner entrepreneur, Idea generation, Valuing ideas, Business idea & Business model. This toolbox is available in 4 languages (English, Dutch, Croatian, and Spanish) and in two versions for the two target groups: girls and youth workers. Moreover, the toolbox includes a variety of online and offline activities. 
2 Female Role Model Database: A regional database of inspiring female entrepreneurs who provided mentorship and guidance to young women. The database includes profiles of 22 female entrepreneurs from Croatia, Spain and the Netherlands. The female role models made entrepreneurship more relatable and accessible by showcasing success stories from similar backgrounds.
3 Girl Boss Bootcamp: A 3-day bootcamp in each partner country, where young women and youth workers participated in non-formal learning activities and connected with female role models. This event helped boost entrepreneurial skills and fostered collaboration.
Overall, the project raised awareness about female entrepreneurship, improved youth worker capacity, and empowered girls to explore entrepreneurial opportunities.

2023-1-NO02-KA210-YOU-000160326.title: Supporting Youth in Understanding Renewable Energy Solutions
2023-1-NO02-KA210-YOU-000160326.summary:
<< Background >>

In order to meet the growing need for education and awareness regarding sustainable energy among young people, particularly high school students between the ages of 14 and 19, the SUNRISE project was started. SUNRISE sought to provide students with the fundamental knowledge and abilities in the field of sustainable energy solutions and associated employment prospects, acknowledging a knowledge gap in this area. Through the provision of educational materials, training sessions, and practical experiences, the project aimed to provide young people with the means to make significant contributions to the sustainable energy industry, eventually promoting employment and tackling the issues posed by climate change. By focusing on sustainable development, youth empowerment, and skill development, this project is in line with Erasmus Plus KA2 collaborative partnerships goals.

<< Objectives >>

The SUNRISE project's main goal was to increase high school student's interest in and knowledge of sustainable energy while also giving them the tools they need to pursue future employment in this industry. The project's second main goal was to inform youth about the value of renewable energy sources and how they can help combat climate change. Project helps students develop green skills that increase their employability by giving them theoretical and practical information about sustainable energy. The project also provided materials and advice to help students investigate job options in the sustainable energy industry. SUNRISE promotes cross-border sustainable practices, intercultural learning, and educational content enrichment through transnational collaborations.

<< Implementation >>

The SUNRISE project carried out a series of activities to engage young people in sustainable energy education. Project management began with a kick-off meeting, setting clear goals and responsibilities among partners to ensure effective coordination. Key activities included developing a Handbook on Sustainable Energy, which introduced students to core concepts and career paths, alongside interactive local training sessions. An evaluation meeting followed to assess and refine these sessions.
The project also produced educational videos to enhance learning access, organized an International Workshop for knowledge exchange with professionals, and conducted a pilot implementation, allowing students to apply their knowledge practically and strengthen their skills in sustainable energy.

<< Results >>

The SUNRISE project produced significant educational outputs and achieved wide-reaching dissemination. The Handbook on Sustainable Energy was shared with 116 schools, providing essential information on renewable energy topics and career options. Local training sessions engaged over 150 students and 10 educators, who participated in interactive activities designed to deepen their understanding of green skills.

Through targeted dissemination efforts on social media platforms, the project reached approximately 30,000 views. Positive feedback from students and educators demonstrated a strong interest in sustainable energy careers, underscoring the project’s success in raising awareness and fostering interest in this field.

2023-1-NO02-KA210-YOU-000160671.title: TALE - Tools for Active Listening and Empowerment
2023-1-NO02-KA210-YOU-000160671.summary:
<< Background >>

The TALE project was designed to address the lack of inclusive, participatory, and trauma-sensitive tools for working with vulnerable youth. Both partner organisations identified a need for structured methods that would allow young people, particularly those facing systemic barriers (such as NEET status, care experience, or ethnic discrimination), to express their stories, reclaim their narratives, and participate in shaping public discourse. The project aimed to empower these youth by using storytelling as a tool for self-reflection, communication, and social advocacy, while also providing youth workers with methodologies grounded in active listening, ethics, and peer-based learning.

TALE also sought to contribute to wider societal change by challenging prevailing narratives around vulnerability and encouraging empathy, dignity, and solidarity. At the organisational level, the project responded to the need for sustainable, research-informed resources, the expansion of peer-led approaches, and the strengthening of transnational cooperation in the youth sector.


<< Objectives >>

The projects main objectives were to:

1. Research and explore perspectives of vulnerability in project partner countries

2. Raise awareness about the diversity of vulnerable youth

3. Empower vulnerable youth to speak up and share their stories

4. Educate youth workers in their work with vulnerable youth and how to empower them through storytelling

To achieve this, the project aimed to carry out qualitative research capturing the voices and lived experiences of young people facing structural exclusion. These insights would form the basis for a co-created curriculum for youth workers and peer educators, offering adaptable, trauma-informed tools for supporting self-expression, resilience, and active participation.

In parallel, the project intended to build a multilingual digital platform as a long-term space for collecting and sharing personal stories. The platform would promote empathy and inclusion by presenting youth narratives within an accessible, visually engaging environment.
By combining research, practice, and digital tools, TALE sought to shift how vulnerability is perceived—centering youth voices and building the capacities of those who support them.

<< Implementation >>

Implementation followed the work package structure. 

WP1 focused on comparative qualitative research, led by Løvetannakademiet. A total of 30 semi-structured interviews were conducted with youth and youth workers in Norway and Croatia, using a shared methodology. Insights were compiled into an 18-page publication with analysed data and thematic findings.

WP2 was led by DKolektiv and focused on the co-creation of the TALE curriculum. Two focus groups with 20 youth and peer educators were held to test and refine the content. The curriculum was then piloted with 30 participants in both countries through a two-day training in Croatia and a condensed 4-hour session in Norway. Feedback informed the final version, prepared as a digital 40-page handbook.

In WP3, DKolektiv developed and launched the TALE platform, featuring an illustrated virtual community built around 42 anonymised youth stories. The platform includes a story submission tool, project resources, and multilingual content (EN, HR, NO).

WP4 was adapted due to force majeure. The planned conference was replaced by a national dissemination event in Croatia, reaching 32 participants from 26 youth organisations.


<< Results >>

WP1: 20 youth and 10 youth workers interviewed with shared methodology. EN report (18 pages) published. One 2-day in-person partner meeting in HR.
 WP2: Modular curricula (4h and 2 days) developed. 3 focus groups (20 participants) in NO and HR. Curriculum piloted in short (NO) and long (HR) format with 30 participants. TALE publication (40 pages) in EN, NO, HR.

 WP3: Platform launched (tale-platform.com) with 42 youth stories, 2 publications, 3 blog posts, and “Share your story” section.
 WP4: Dissemination held during Croatian Youth Network Assembly (32 participants from 26 orgs).
 
Meetings:
 WP1: 1 physical meeting (HR). WP2: 2 online meetings. WP3: 2 platform coordination meetings. WP4: Final partner meeting (NO) held online.
All planned coordination and review meetings were completed, either in-person or online. Communication was supported through shared folders and regular digital check-ins.

 Adjustments:
 Shifted to digital-only publications for sustainability.
 Final event in NO replaced by dissemination event in HR.
 Final partner meeting in NO switched to online meeting.
 The project reached its intended professional audience and youth stakeholders. Outputs are now in active use.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2023-1-PT02-KA210-YOU-000156172.title: Ecofeminism: work towards an equal and green youth
2023-1-PT02-KA210-YOU-000156172.summary:
<< Background >>

A ideia deste projeto surgiu por intermédio daquele que é o trabalho da XX Element e que permitiu a identificação de um conjunto de necessidades relacionadas com o ecofeminismo. Sendo uma organização experiente nas questões da inclusão e igualdade de género, foi ao longo do trabalho com os jovens que compreendemos duas necessidades: (a) que os nossos TJ precisavam de complementar o seu conhecimento e de descobrir/explorar novos métodos e ferramentas inovadoras de trabalho com os jovens para estas temáticas e (b) necessidade de quebrar com o desconhecimento por parte dos jovens sobre o ecofeminismo e, por consequência, com a baixa sensibilização para as desigualdades e obstáculos enfrentados pelas mulheres/raparigas neste domínio.
Estas necessidades aliaram-se às necessidades dos jovens, enquanto beneficiários finais da ação, uma vez que se verificou junto dos jovens intervencionados pelas organizações que existia necessidade de (a) adquirir mais conhecimento sobre a temática, (b) desenvolver competências chave e experiências de aprendizagem europeias e (c) conseguir ter oportunidades de desenvolvimento pessoal e social.


<< Objectives >>

A desigualdade de género coloca barreiras à participação e inclusão das mulheres/raparigas. “As several UN world conferences and reports by numerous NGOs point out, women are the first victims of environmental deterioration but also play a key role in the defence of nature.” (Puleo, 2017).
Neste sentido, este projeto quis despertar e capacitar as organizações ativas na juventude para a temática do ecofeminismo, com vista à criação de oportunidades equitativas de desenvolvimento pessoal, social e ambiental.
Objetivos:
- Promover a inclusão social das raparigas e mulheres através da aliança às práticas sustentáveis (ecofeminismo).
- Promover o desenvolvimento de competências temáticas, metodológicas e de aprendizagem ao longo da vida junto dos técnicos de juventude (TJ) para que possam dinamizar uma ação inovadora/inclusiva junto dos jovens;
- Reforçar a capacidade dos TJ e organizações de modo que possam inovar o setor da juventude;
- Reforçar a capacidade dos TJ e organizações no trabalho com jovens em menos oportunidades (MO), sobretudo no que à desigualdade de género respeita;
- Promover a multidisciplinaridade e qualidade metodológica no trabalho jovem.



<< Implementation >>

Foram implementadas 3 atividades:
1. Planeamento e Gestão, Preparação e Acompanhamento, que integrou as atividades regulares do projeto. Foi feito o desenho do Plano de Ação.

2023-1-RS01-KA210-YOU-000165999.title: The Roadmap for Jobs of the Future
2023-1-RS01-KA210-YOU-000165999.summary:
<< Background >>

The main motivation to apply for this project were the results of analyses conducted by 3 organizations in the consortium and experience from other youth organizations. Results showed that youth workers should develop methodologies and tools to support young people on their career path, especially in post-pandemic conditions.

Feedback received from IT companies and young people in Serbia; youth workers from Croatia and young people from Portugal, showed that the young are interested in remote jobs. For young people a particular challenge is work-life balance and a lack of flexibility in work and working hours. For remote-first and IT companies remote culture is a system to attract young people and reach many youth outside of big cities.

Based on all these recommendations, and gained experience in work with young beneficiaries and youth workers, the consortium organizations developed a comprehensive tool to respond to needs which we have addressed in the project. The toolkit contains solutions, suggestions and recommendations for young people on how to position themselves in the labour market, obtain skills and how to reach stakeholders from their prospective areas of interests. 

<< Objectives >>

The goal of the project was building the capacity of three organizations in the project consortium in order to raise the quality level of youth work in the field of strengthening the employability of young people. 

Our consortium wanted to develop the competences of youth workers, bring the EU dimension to their work, and finally create tools and methods for supporting young people to find their way in today’s labour market.

During the project our team delivered on 3 specific objectives:
1) to promote the network exchange of knowledge, the best practices and the European perspectives among youth workers and our organizations in the consortium in order to improve our everyday operations and achieve greater impact to our beneficiaries;

2) to equip and empower youth workers for supporting young people to find their way in today’s labour market and to improve their employability;

3) to create better career prospects for young people with fewer opportunities by identifying new ways of cooperating with diverse stakeholders in the field of employability for young people


<< Implementation >>

Our team implemented 9 activities in the project:

- The First transnational meeting in Portugal was hosted by Agora Aveiro. All partners learned about the best practices from one another at that time. The project management and activities for 2024 were defined then. 
- Project management of the grant was an ongoing activity: 2 to 3 persons from each organisation were available every month during all project activities.  
- Study visit in Serbia and exchange of the best practices took place in March 2024 in Belgrade. INAT Centre organized a 3-day event to create the toolkit survey for the beneficiaries and toolkit structure. 
- Toolkit and training development took place from July 2024 until May 2025 when International training for youth workers was held in Zagreb. These 2 activities were the peak of the project, requiring most effort and most satisfaction from team members.
- Dissemination occurred throughout the project with regular online posts. The biggest impact was achieved after the toolkit was published. 
-The 2nd and 3rd transnational meeting were held online in May 2024 and February 2025. 
- Final online transnational meeting in June 2025 was dedicated to final dissemination efforts and preparation of the final report.

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs of this project are the designed toolkit, developed and realized training, dissemination of toolkit and all project results during in-person events and online channels.  
The toolkit was developed by recommendation of youth workers and organizations from 4 countries. 
The result of the training was improvement of skills for 21 youth workers and representatives of the project consortium. They shared the best European perspectives in the international community and learned to support young people in improving their employability.
Over 625 young people and youth workers downloaded the Toolkit. We have organised 3 dissemination events in 3 countries and we presented the Toolkit at 2 other Erasmus+ projects in 2 EU countries as a part of the dissemination. These events have gathered 182 participants in total.

The consortium created better career prospects for youth with fewer opportunities, as we built capacities for youth workers who work alongside disadvantaged youth. At least 3 people per organisation were hired and increased their financial well-being.
 
All organisations from this consortium were invited to Erasmus+ projects (total 12-15 new projects): youth exchanges, teaching courses and Youth@Work conferences
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2023-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000160936.title: Romski vplivneži
2023-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000160936.summary:
<< Background >>

We decided to implement the RomIn project because we recognized a clear need within our partner organizations to promote the personal development and social inclusion of young Roma and to create visible positive role models within the Roma community. Years of experience have shown that young Roma often lack access to positive role models with whom they can identify, as influential figures on social media are mostly members of the majority society. As a result, they lack representative role models, which affects their life aspirations, self-image, and sense of self-worth. With this project, we aimed to fill this gap, providing young Roma with access to inspiring stories and role models from their community, and motivating them to develop their potential and become more actively involved in society. The project thus addressed a multifaceted gap: the lack of positive role models, the invisibility of successful Roma, limited access to motivational content, and the need to strengthen the capacity of organizations working with the Roma community.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to encourage personal development and empower young Roma, with the primary goal of presenting examples of successful Roma who inspire and motivate younger generations and the broader community with their stories.
The key objectives:
to promote the development of personal resources among young Roma through role models from the Roma community and to train Roma to work with young people from their own community;
increasing the visibility of successful Roma and promoting positive and successful role models within the Roma community and the wider society,
increasing young Roma's access to information, education, and opportunities for personal and professional development,
encouraging the inclusion of young Roma in informal education and learning (through the stories we collected, we wanted to encourage young people to engage in informal learning, training, and activities for personal growth)
strengthening cooperation between Roma and majority organizations and communities
addressing important European values of inclusion of vulnerable groups and promoting the strengthening of active citizenship and participation of young Roma at the local, national, and European levels.

<< Implementation >>

We carried out several activities aimed at empowering young Roma and promoting positive role models within the Roma community and wider society.
The key activities:
Collecting stories of successful Roma: we collected 34 stories of Roma who inspire younger generations and serve as positive role models
Establishment of an online platform: we presented the collected stories on a web platform created specifically for this project, which is available in all national languages of the partners and in English. In addition to presenting the stories, the platform also contains information about the project and the partnership and serves as a tool for disseminating results and promoting the personal development of young Roma. The platform encourages young people to develop personal resources, a positive self-image, and active involvement in the community.
Training implementation (LTT activity): We also organized a 5-day training for 13 Roma from three countries, where participants developed personal resources and skills for working with young people. The aim of the training was also for these young people to become positive role models in their communities and thus contribute to greater motivation and inclusion of other young Roma.

<< Results >>

We established the ROM-IN web portal for young Roma, available in Slovenian, Croatian, German, and English. It provides information about the project and its partners, stories of successful Roma, and motivational content for personal development. The portal serves as the main tool for sharing project results and promoting positive role models within the Roma community.
We developed motivational tools that encourage young Roma to discover their potential, build self-confidence, strengthen a positive self-image, and actively participate in their communities.
A collection of 34 stories of successful Roma from various fields and partner countries was created to serve as positive examples and inspiration for young Roma.
As part of the project, we trained 13 (young) Roma in a 5-day LTT activity, equipping them with skills for working with young people and acting as role models and motivators in their communities. A training program was prepared, translated into partner languages, and published on the web portal.
The project concluded with a final conference, where we presented results, exchanged experiences, and strengthened cooperation among participating organizations and communities.

2023-2-EE01-KA210-YOU-000168327.title: Empowering You(th): Building Psychosocial Resilience in Vulnerable Communities
2023-2-EE01-KA210-YOU-000168327.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the "YOUTH BUILD" project because I am deeply committed to supporting the mental health and well-being of vulnerable young people. I believe that building psychosocial resilience is essential for helping youth overcome adversity, develop self-confidence, and thrive in their communities. This project aligns with my passion for empowering marginalized youth by providing them with the tools, support, and opportunities they need to grow into strong, resilient, and active contributors to society. The YOUTH BUILD project addresses key gaps in psychosocial support for vulnerable youth. At the organizational level, there is a lack of expertise, resources, and focus on emotional well-being. Nationally, youth face high rates of mental health issues, social exclusion, trauma (especially among refugees), and limited support for those with disabilities or from disadvantaged backgrounds. The project responds by providing inclusive, strengths-based support to build resilience, promote mental health, and empower youth as leaders in their communities.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to strengthen the psychosocial resilience of vulnerable youth by equipping them with the skills, tools, and support needed to overcome adversity, improve mental well-being, and develop a strong sense of self-worth. Through this project, we wanted to empower young people to become confident, capable, and active participants in their communities, while also building local capacity to provide inclusive and sustainable psychosocial support.

<< Implementation >>

Kick-off Meeting and Planning Session
Brought all partner organisations together to align on project objectives, timelines, and roles.
Development of Psychosocial Support Tools
Created and piloted two key tools: the Resilience Assessment Compass and Strengths-Based Coaching Cards, designed to assess and strengthen youth resilience.

Local Youth Workshops

Conducted psychosocial workshops in each partner country (Estonia, Poland, Croatia) focusing on emotional intelligence, coping skills, and problem-solving.

Peer Mentoring and Youth Leadership Training

Trained selected youth to become peer mentors and community leaders, empowering them to support others and lead local initiatives.

Community Engagement Activities

Facilitated youth-led projects and participation in decision-making processes at the community level to build confidence and promote active citizenship.
Final Evaluation and Dissemination Event
Held a closing event to share project results, tools, and lessons learned with stakeholders, including educators, youth workers, and policy-makers.

<< Results >>

Resilience Assessment Compass:
A comprehensive tool designed to evaluate individual strengths and needs of vulnerable youth, guiding targeted support.
Strengths-Based Coaching Cards:
Interactive cards used by youth workers to facilitate strength-focused conversations that empower youth.
Resilience Champions Digital Platform:
An online space to identify, connect, and nurture resilient youth leaders, fostering peer support and engagement.

Training Materials and Sessions:
Two online training sessions delivered to 30 youth workers and volunteers on how to implement the tools effectively.
Other Key Results:
Enhanced Capacity of Youth Workers:
30 professionals and volunteers integrated new psychosocial tools into their practice, improving support quality.

Empowered Youth:
Vulnerable young people developed greater resilience, coping skills, and leadership abilities through workshops and mentoring.
Strengthened Peer Networks:
Establishment of peer mentoring initiatives and community engagement activities to sustain ongoing support.

2023-3-BG01-KA210-YOU-000180593.title: Green Opportunity
2023-3-BG01-KA210-YOU-000180593.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project “Green Opportunity – Re-design the Future” to address the need for youth-friendly tools that help young people from Bulgaria, Croatia, and Greece adopt more sustainable lifestyles aligned with the principles of the circular economy. The project responded to the lack of accessible, practical ways for youth to engage with environmental issues and rethink unsustainable production and consumption models.
It aimed to tackle the negative impacts of the “take-make-dispose” linear economy by empowering young people to take action through daily habits and community initiatives. Our goal was to involve youth in activities that build green skills, promote behavioral change, and support sustainable development.
The project provided engaging educational content through animated videos and a practical toolkit, offering concrete tools, techniques, and examples of circular practices. These resources were shared via social media and online campaigns from partnering organisations from Bulgaria, Croatia, and Greece to reach a wider audience and inspire responsible consumption.

<< Objectives >>

The project set out to equip young people with practical tools, methods, and knowledge that they could implement in their daily lives to support the shift toward a circular economy. Through a combination of educational animated videos and a  practical toolkit, and exchange of good practices, the project aimed to raise awareness, encourage behavior change, and foster responsible, eco-friendly habits.
We wanted to address the needs of young people—particularly those already engaged in green topics—by offering them opportunities to learn, take initiative, and lead by example in their communities. The objectives also included encouraging non-formal educational initiatives, supporting youth workers in sustainability education, and developing open educational resources that could be widely shared and reused.
In alignment with the EU Youth Strategy 2019–2027, the project sought to strengthen youth participation, digital literacy, creative learning, and intercultural dialogue. By bringing together young people, youth workers, volunteers, and civil society actors from three countries, the project fostered collaboration, knowledge exchange, and long-term impact through shared values and a common vision for sustainability.

<< Implementation >>

From April 2024 till  June 2025, we successfully implemented a wide range of activities that laid the foundation for the project’s goals.
In June 2024 we held a transnational kick-off meeting in Greece, where partners defined roles, agreed on communication procedures, and developed a risk management and quality assurance plan. Ongoing coordination ensured smooth implementation and regular progress monitoring.
In July 2024 we held a workshop in Sofia focused on exchanging good practices in youth work related to sustainability. As part of good practices exchange we  visited the interactive educational center for separate collection of packaging waste of ECOPACK BULGARIA, whose goal is to educate children and young people about the benefits of separate waste collection and recycling.
In Zagreb, Croatia, we combined learning with action through a workshop and river cleanup. Participants explored issues related to plastic waste and resource recovery, gaining hands-on experience.
Two major intellectual outputs were developed: ten short educational videos and a practical toolkit offering guidance, tools, and examples for youth workers and educators.
To share the results, we organized multiplier events in all three partner countries.

<< Results >>

The “Green Opportunity – Re-design the Future” project produced a set of concrete outputs and impactful results aligned with its objectives. We developed two key intellectual outputs:
A multilingual Circular Economy Toolkit, available in English, Bulgarian, Greek, and Croatian, containing practical guidance, ready-to-use activities, best practices, and facilitation tips for youth workers and educators. Ten short educational videos, five professionally produced and five created by young volunteers, covering topics such as recycling symbols, plastic waste reduction, zero-waste tips, greenwashing, eco fabrics, and sustainable travel.
All the intellectual outputs are freely available on the project’s webpage - https://bap.bg/green-opportunity-go/ where all the project information is available in Bulgarian and English.
Two international workshops were organized: In Sofia, partners exchanged good practices and visited a waste separation facility. In Zagreb, discussions focused on textile sustainability, EU regulations, and included a river cleanup action. We also organized local multiplier events in each partner country.

2023-3-CY02-KA210-YOU-000182324.title: Boost Your Digital Intelligence
2023-3-CY02-KA210-YOU-000182324.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to respond to a clear skills gap affecting young people with fewer opportunities in Cyprus, Croatia, and Romania. Studies have shown that negative trend of youth unemployment was greatly caused by the lack of digital skills. Even more,the EU Digital Education Plan (2021-2027) states that more than one in five young people across the EU do not possess basic level of digital skills.Youth NEET lack practical digital competences and struggle to enter the labour market. Many have limited access to structured training. Some also face disability, migration background, or long-term unemployment, which further restricts their options. Evidence at EU level shows uneven digital skill levels and links between ICT competences and employment outcomes. In Romania and Croatia youth unemployment remains above the EU average. In Cyprus, advanced digital skills remain below EU benchmarks. Local employers report gaps in basic and applied digital abilities. These patterns indicate a structural need rather than isolated cases. The needs the project addressed for youth NEET were: Increase the digital readiness, Strengthen the employability, Promote equal access to digital skills, Support employability and entrepreneurship. 

<< Objectives >>

The digital economy is transforming the world of work, and youth in need are at risk of being left behind. Additionally, youth in need face additional barriers to employment, such as lack of education and training, discrimination, and poverty. Studies have shown that negative trend of youth unemployment was greatly caused by the lack of digital skills.
The concrete objectives were to:
• Increase the digital readiness, resilience, and capacity of youth and more specifically youth in need
• Strengthen the employability of youth in need by developing their digital skills and competences
• Promote equal access to transition in the labor market for youth in need through digital skills development
• Support youth employability, inclusion, and diversity in all fields of education, training, youth

Regarding Young people the project wanted to:
• Provide them with the digital skills and competences they need to succeed in the digital economy and labor market.
• Help young people to overcome the barriers in the digital economy.
• Promote equal access to digital skills for all 
• Help young people to develop the skills and competences they need to find and maintain employment.
• Help young people to participate more fully in society.


<< Implementation >>

The project included four main activities. First, partners carried out project management tasks. Regular online meetings were held. Three transnational meetings took place. Roles, timelines, risks, and budget issues were reviewed. Quality control and reporting procedures were applied throughout. Second, training sessions were delivered in each partner country. More than ninety young people and thirty youth workers took part. Topics covered basic digital tools, online communication, project management software, and online safety. Sessions also addressed career planning and personal development. Mentoring support followed for selected participants. Moreover, business plans for participants who showed extra interest were developed. Third, the consortium developed a practical manual. The content focused on digital competences, youth support methods, and inclusive practices. Accessibility guidance was included. Finally, dissemination and national piloting sessions were organized. Results were presented to local stakeholders. Project materials were shared online. Social media channels and a website were used to widen outreach. Lastly participants due to their new qualifications got jobs. 

<< Results >>

The expected outcomes and results are:
• At least 90 youth in need will participate in digital skills training programs
• At least 75% of participants will improve their digital skills and competences
• At least 25% of participants will find employment and at least 4 will start their own businesses within one year of
completing the training programs
• Resources and tools will be developed and shared to support youth in need in developing and using their digital skills
• To raise awareness of the importance of digital skills for youth in need among policymakers, employers, and the general
public

This project had a significant added value on a EU level by:
• Contributing to the EU's Digital Single Market strategy
• Helping to reduce youth unemployment
• Promoting social inclusion and diversity
• Providing a model for other EU states to follow

The project also contributed to the EU's Sustainable Development Goals by:
• Promoting inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all (SDG 8)
• Reducing inequality within and among countries (SDG 10)
• Ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education and promoting lifelong learning opportunities for all (SDG 4)
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market
