2024-1-MK01-KA210-YOU-000250780.title: Empowering STEM Students with Employability Skills for Professional Excellence
2024-1-MK01-KA210-YOU-000250780.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated to respond to a clear gap in employability and communication skills among STEM students, particularly those enrolled in engineering programmes in North Macedonia. Employers consistently report that young engineers possess excellent technical expertise but often lack the ability to communicate effectively, present ideas clearly and perform confidently in interviews and team environments. The absence of soft-skill development during studies significantly limits their employment opportunities and career growth. Moreover, students from rural areas and those with fewer opportunities face additional challenges accessing career-development resources. STEMployability was therefore designed to strengthen youth employability through structured training in communication, self-presentation and professional development, while also promoting inclusivity and empowering participants to overcome socio-economic barriers. The project tackled both national and European priorities by equipping STEM students with transversal and digital competences essential for integrating into the modern labor market and contributing to sustainable innovation-driven growth.

<< Objectives >>

STEMployability aimed to tackle key employability challenges among STEM students in North Macedonia, especially in engineering disciplines. It sought to build crucial communication and professional skills so students could present technical ideas effectively, perform well in interviews, and develop a mindset suited to modern labor market needs.
Core objectives were:
-	Enhancing verbal and non-verbal communication and self-presentation for effective engagement with varied audiences. 
-	Strengthening interview and job application skills to improve employment readiness.
-	Promoting social inclusion by reaching and supporting students from underrepresented groups, reducing career barriers.
-	Advancing digital transformation by integrating tools like Europass to boost digital literacy and awareness of European standards.
-	Raising environmental awareness by embedding sustainable practices in all project steps.
These objectives directly supported Erasmus+ horizontal priorities of addressing inclusion and diversity, as well as digital transformation, and the youth‑sector priority of employability, empowering future engineers to thrive and lead responsibly.

<< Implementation >>

During the one-year implementation period, systematic project management facilitated effective planning, coordination and communication among partners. This foundation enabled five two-day in-person trainings for STEM students held at the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering in Skopje. A total of 117 students from all technical faculties participated, with purposeful inclusion of gender balance and students from rural areas and fewer opportunities. An inclusive, competence-based methodology was applied that combined peer-to-peer learning, simulations and digital tools, adjusted to students’ experience levels. The training blended short lectures, group case studies, role-plays and peer-to-peer learning to meet individual needs. Participants created or updated their Europass CVs via the EU digital platform and engaged in mock interviews and assessment centres to apply new skills. Preparation included developing training materials and evaluation forms for feedback and quality assurance. Dissemination was carried out via project website, social media and local press coverage. The project also included tree planting and green promotional materials, aligning with environmental targets. All activities met high standards and timely delivery.

<< Results >>

The project delivered significant, concrete outcomes and measurable impact. Across 117 participants, communication, interviewing and presentation skills improved noticeably. Post-training evaluations from 80 respondents revealed that over 90% rated the trainings as excellent for clarity, relevance, trainer efficacy. Students reported boosted confidence and better interview preparedness; one shared, “Before this, I’d never practiced job interviews. Now I feel ready to apply.” Digital skills were enhanced by completing or updating Europass CVs on EU platform in line with EU digital, green and entrepreneurship competence frameworks. All participants received the "How to Get a Job" ebook, Youthpass certificate and summarized Training Handbook, reinforcing ongoing skill development. Dissemination reached over a thousand individuals via social media, 18 press articles published on online portals in different stages of the project and an open-access project website. Environmental consciousness was promoted through tree planting and sustainable promotional materials for each participant. Partner institutions increased their capacity to deliver inclusive employability training, bolstering sustainability beyond project closure.

2024-1-NL02-KA210-YOU-000250066.title: Bystander to Upstander: Building a Culture of Intervention
2024-1-NL02-KA210-YOU-000250066.summary:
<< Background >>

With the rise of digital technology, online violence, such as sexual harassment, bullying, and abuse, has become a growing concern, especially among young people. These experiences can have serious short- and long-term effects, including anxiety, depression, and isolation. Online harassment often reflects the same structural inequalities seen offline, such as gender-based violence (GBV), sexism, homophobia, transphobia, racism, islamophobia, ableism, and other forms of discrimination. 
In both the Netherlands and Croatia, data show high levels of online harassment among youth, particularly girls, young women, and LGBTIQ+ youth. Yet many young people lack the tools, support, or confidence to intervene or seek help. Bystander intervention is recognized as a key strategy to prevent violence and empower individuals to act when witnessing harmful behavior. 
This project addressed these issues by linking GBV and discrimination prevention with practical online bystander strategies. It aimed to build the capacities of youth workers and young people through training, resource development, and safe spaces for discussion, fostering more inclusive, supportive communities both online and offline.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to achieve three interconnected objectives focused on preventing GBV and promoting gender equality, especially in online spaces. First, we wanted to strengthen the capacities of the partner organizations by exchanging knowledge, tools, and practices in the areas of violence prevention, bystander intervention, and gender-transformative work. This objective was rooted in the belief that sustainable change starts with well-equipped professionals, and it laid the foundation for this collaboration and the development of new, shared methodologies.
Second, we aimed to educate and empower youth workers and professionals who engage with young people. By offering training and practical resources, we wanted to create a broader, transnational network of practitioners capable of addressing online violence and discrimination effectively and inclusively.
Finally, our goal was to engage and empower young people themselves to recognize, challenge, and respond to violence and harmful behaviors, particularly in online spaces. Through co-created educational programs and awareness campaigns, we promoted active bystander intervention and supported young people in becoming agents of change in their communities.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, we implemented a series of interconnected activities designed to build capacity, create practical tools, and engage both professionals and young people.
The first activity was a capacity-building process between partner organizations to strengthen our shared knowledge and approaches to GBV prevention and gender equality through bystander intervention and gender-transformative work. Together, we co-created an innovative method and developed resources for online bystander intervention, tailored to the needs of youth and youth workers.
We held Training-of-Trainers (ToT) sessions in both the Netherlands and Croatia, along with a joint online session, reaching professionals working with youth in various contexts. These trainings focused on equipping participants with knowledge and tools for addressing online violence and promoting safe, inclusive environments.
Workshops were also held with young people in both countries, using a newly co-created educational module. Finally, we launched a youth-centered awareness campaign to promote online bystander intervention and encourage peer-led discussions and actions in digital spaces.

<< Results >>

The project successfully achieved its objectives through coordinated international activities and active engagement of professionals and youth. A one-week study visit in Croatia strengthened partner collaboration and knowledge exchange on bystander intervention and gender-transformative approaches. Together, the partners co-created a practical Toolkit for youth workers and educators to prevent online violence, featuring explanations of online harassment, interactive workshops, facilitation tips, and adaptable reflection exercises.
Through Train-the-Trainers sessions in Croatia and the Netherlands, 31 professionals were introduced to the co-created toolkit; enhancing their knowledge and confidence to apply bystander methodologies. Educational workshops reached 94 young people, who reported improved understanding of online harassment and stronger motivation to act as upstanders. The Toolkit was widely shared online and during trainings, while the From Bystander to Upstander awareness campaign reached over 1.3 million people across social media, significantly amplifying public awareness and engagement on online safety and active bystander behavior.

2024-1-RO01-KA210-YOU-000245002.title: Re-Wild
2024-1-RO01-KA210-YOU-000245002.summary:
<< Background >>

The needs identified and addressed though the Re-Wild project are: 
*Youthworker’s needs of developing youth work competencies  through specialized nature-based trainings. 
*Empowering the youth workers to address the rising problems of disconnection( to nature, themselves and community) , indifference towards nature and environment, apathy and eco-anxiety
*Develop capacity of Youth workers through more nature-based methods, to address "green" topics in innovative ways
*Contribute to raising quality in youth work with innovative curricula
*Addressing the need of nature-connection in youth from our communities through innovative nature-based methodology.

At the end of the Re-Wild project:
* The three partner organizations have increased their capacity to engage in Nature-based Youth Work (N.B.Y.W.).
* 9 youth workers have gained competencies to implement N.B.Y.W. 
*118 young people have increased their connection with nature.
*N.B.Y.W. Practice Model has been created, with non-formal activities 
*Three organizations have increased their capacity to work at the European level.
*Five new international projects are planned for submission in October 2026 and February 2027.

<< Objectives >>

By the end of the project we aimed to achieve the following:
O1. To increase the organizational capacity of the three partner organizations to successfully engage in Nature-based Youth Work (N.B.Y.W.) in their specific communities.
O2. To develop specific competencies of 9 youth workers to carry out N.B.Y.W. in their setting by participating in three separate nature-based specialized trainings and a preparatory phase.
O3. Nature-based youth work practice model was created, with non-formal activities specifically adapted to the three communities the organizations were working in.
O4. A common strategy towards addressing the underlying causes of the climate crisis affecting youth through nature-based methodology was created.


<< Implementation >>

A1.PROJECT MANAGEMENT -  flowing through the whole project to the final end
A2.Preparatory phase - 3-month online prepping of youth workers.
A3.Training 1 - Wild Mind Intensive - 6 day residential training - Romania 
The training in Romania, 6 days of intensive research, developing nature-based competencies based on N.F.L. methods.
A4.Training 2 - Council and Mirroring Intensive - 6 day residential training - Latvia 
The Council and Mirroring intensive focused on the competencies needed to successfully guide nature-based work, both individually and in groups.
A5. Training 3 - Nature and the Human Soul intensive - 8 week online training 
The third training, the Nature and the Human Soul, was an 8-week online training. It focused on the Eco-centric Human Developmental Wheel Model. 
 A6.Transfer-of-knowledge Workshops in local communities 
We created 26 new methods and tested them with local youth, then compiled a nature-based Re-Wild Guide as an intellectual output.
A7. Transnational work meeting - 6 days residential - Croatia 
The transnational meeting took place in Croatia, in which the 9 youth workers involved in the project worked on all dimensions of the project.
A8.Conferences and workshops for dissemination and multiplication

<< Results >>

The concrete output is the nature-based practice model we created in this project called Re-wild - Guide for Youth workers. This is an innovative intellectual result containing 26 non-formal methods created by the 9 youth workers involved in all phases of this project. 
Available for download here: 
https://www.omsicopac.org/re-wild-proiect-strategic-european/

Other results of the project:
*118 young people who developed their capacity to connect with nature
*9 youth workers who developed their competencies to create and facilitate human development experiences anchored in nature
*82 youth workers who benefit from the Re-Wild Youth Worker Guide, reached through dissemination events
*5 new projects planned to be submitted, three in October 2026 and two in Feb 2027
I.Training Course on Re-Wild Methodology for youth workers to be applied in Romanian NA in Oct 2026
II.Youth Exchange with Re-Wild Methodology to be applied in October in Croatian NA
III.One KA2 Partnership focusing o Re-wilding and Community gardens to be applied in Romanian NA in October 2026
IV.A Solidarity project in teams for Re-wilding youth to be applied in Feb 2027 in RO NA
V.A Nature-based Education System in Preschool to be applied in Feb 2027 in RO NA

2024-1-TR01-KA210-YOU-000245431.title: Music for Cognitive Advancement and Inclusive Change
2024-1-TR01-KA210-YOU-000245431.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the MUZICAD project to respond to the limited availability of inclusive, practical, and accessible educational tools for young people with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), particularly in non-formal education and youth work contexts. Many autistic young people face barriers to social participation, communication, and emotional expression, while educators and youth workers often lack adaptable methodologies to support their inclusion. Music was identified as a powerful medium to address these needs, as it supports emotional expression, interaction, creativity, and social engagement without relying solely on verbal communication. The project aimed to bridge the gap between artistic practice and inclusive education by developing structured, music-based activities that are easy to implement and transferable across different educational settings. MUZICAD also addresses the need for capacity building by providing practical resources that promote inclusion, diversity, and equal participation.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the MUZICAD project was to promote the social inclusion, active participation, and personal development of young people with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) through structured, music-based learning approaches. By using music as an inclusive and non-verbal tool, the project aimed to enhance communication, social interaction, emotional expression, self-confidence, and participation in group activities. A key objective was to design and implement a practical and transferable handbook that provides educators, youth workers, therapists, and families with clear guidance and adaptable music-based games suitable for both formal and non-formal education settings. The handbook was developed to respond to real educational needs by offering low-cost, easy-to-use activities that can be adapted to different abilities and contexts. The project aimed to strengthen the professional capacity of educators and institutions, raise awareness of inclusion and diversity, and foster cooperation at local and European levels. Through transnational collaboration and the sharing of good practices, MUZICAD sought to ensure the sustainability, accessibility, and long-term impact of its results beyond the project duration.

<< Implementation >>

Within the MUZICAD project, a range of interconnected activities were implemented to support inclusive learning through music for young people with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). The partnership carried out collaborative work to design, test, and refine music-based educational games, drawing on the experience of educators, therapists, and youth workers from different countries. These activities included practical workshops and pilot implementations in which the games were applied in small group and individual settings. Feedback from educators was used to improve the activities and ensure they were adaptable, low-cost, and suitable for both formal and non-formal education contexts. Based on this process, the MUZICAD Handbook was developed as a core project output, providing structured guidance and clear instructions for each activity. In parallel, a project website was created to host the handbook, activity descriptions, and demonstration videos, supporting access and dissemination of the project results.

<< Results >>

The MUZICAD project produced clear and concrete outputs that support inclusive education for young people with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). The main project result is the MUZICAD Handbook, which presents a structured collection of music-based educational games designed to support communication, social interaction, emotional expression, and participation. The handbook was developed collaboratively and made available in multiple language versions to increase accessibility and transferability. Another key output is the MUZICAD Project Website, which provides open access to the handbook, activity descriptions, and demonstration videos supporting practical implementation. The digital format enhances the visibility and usability of the project results beyond the project duration. In addition to these tangible outputs, feedback shared by educators who used the resources indicated that the music-based approaches were perceived as useful and relevant for inclusive educational practice. The impact of the project was primarily assessed through an evaluation survey conducted with educators.

2024-1-TR01-KA210-YOU-000255753.title: Public-NGO Cooperation in Combating Addiction in Times of Crisis and Disaster
2024-1-TR01-KA210-YOU-000255753.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project in response to the increasing problem of substance addiction among young people, especially during crises and disasters. Events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, the war in Ukraine, and the earthquakes in Türkiye have negatively affected young people’s mental health, increasing vulnerability, risky behaviors, and social instability.
The project addressed key needs such as raising awareness about substance abuse, strengthening young people’s coping skills, and improving help-seeking behaviors in crisis situations. It also responded to the need to enhance the knowledge and capacities of youth workers and professionals working in this field.
In addition, there was a clear need to strengthen cooperation between public institutions and NGOs, as existing collaboration was limited. The project also focused on disadvantaged young people affected by social and disaster-related challenges, aiming to build resilience and promote inclusive support mechanisms.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to reduce the impact of substance addiction among young people, especially in times of crisis and disaster. Our main objective was to increase awareness about the risks and consequences of substance abuse and to promote preventive approaches among youth and youth workers.
We also aimed to strengthen young people’s resilience, coping strategies, and help-seeking behaviors in challenging situations such as disasters, migration, and social instability. Another key goal was to enhance the knowledge, skills, and professional capacities of youth workers and stakeholders working in addiction prevention.
In addition, the project sought to improve and institutionalize cooperation between public bodies and NGOs, creating a sustainable collaboration model. Finally, we aimed to produce practical outputs to support policy development and improve intervention strategies in combating addiction.

<< Implementation >>

Within the project, we carried out several dissemination and awareness-raising activities. Six infographic layouts prepared within the project were displayed in public institutions and NGOs working on addiction prevention, such as Yeşilay and the Red Cross, to increase awareness.
In addition, we set up a project stand at a festival area to support dissemination. During the festival, we had the opportunity to reach more than 150 young people who visited our stand. We shared project outputs such as agendas, pens, brochures, and infographic materials, as well as our experiences and observations gained throughout the project.
Through short activities, interactive discussions, and direct sharing, we engaged with young people individually. These activities contributed to strengthening awareness and consciousness among youth in line with the project’s main objective of combating substance addiction.

<< Results >>

The project achieved several concrete outputs and measurable results. One of the main outcomes was an increase of at least 10 points in participants’ substance addiction awareness test scores, showing the effectiveness of the activities.
Additionally, 6 infographic layouts on substance addiction in the context of disaster and crisis management were developed and widely disseminated through public institutions and NGOs, contributing to awareness-raising.
A comprehensive e-booklet on Public-NGO cooperation implementation strategies was also produced, providing practical guidance for stakeholders.
Furthermore, an academic article focusing on addiction and cooperation between NGOs and public bodies was prepared, strengthening the scientific dimension of the project.
Overall, the project enhanced participants’ knowledge, strengthened institutional cooperation, and increased public awareness on addiction prevention.

2024-3-CZ01-KA210-YOU-000286093.title: Future Shift: Empowering Educators for Post-Growth Transformation
2024-3-CZ01-KA210-YOU-000286093.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we identified a growing gap between the rapidly developing field of post-growth research and the lack of accessible educational tools that would allow young people and educators to engage with these ideas in practice. Simultaneously, across Europe, young people increasingly experience climate anxiety, economic insecurity, and frustration with responses focused only on individual lifestyle changes rather than systemic causes. At the same time, educators often lack practical methodologies for facilitating critical discussions about systemic solutions to the problems of climate change, inequality and the possibilities of social transformation. 

Both partner organisations, NaZemi and Institute of Political Ecology (IPE) observed rising interest in post-growth education through their summer schools, workshops, and educational programmes. We applied for this project to deepen our expertise and experience in the topic of post-growth within non-formal education, become European pioneers in this field and also learn from one another. 


<< Objectives >>

Our main objective was to make post-growth and transformative education more accessible for non-formal educators across Europe by creating practical, ready-to-use educational methodologies. We aimed to develop Post-Growth Transformative Education Handbook featuring eight educational activities focused on post-growth. The handbook should be readily used in non-formal educational contexts. We wanted these materials to help educators go beyond simplified discussions about sustainability and enable young people to critically explore systemic issues and relationships between economic growth, climate change and inequality. 

Given that transformative post-growth education is still a relatively new and emerging field, we wanted to create opportunity for in-person exchange, mutual learning, and future collaboration through an in-depth week-long gathering for non-formal educators from different European countries. This gathering was meant to serve as the foundation for building a loose European network of post-growth educators, where they could share methodologies, plan future projects, and collectively strengthen the impact of post-growth education across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through two interconnected core activities. The first activity focused on the development of a publication called: Transformative Education for a Post-Growth Future: A Collection of Workshops. During this phase, both partner organisations collaboratively created educational methodologies combining post-growth research with transformative education approaches. We have developed and piloted 11 educational methodologies with 242 youth covering topics such as: post-growth businesses, policies, strategies of transformation and many others. 

The second main activity was an international gathering for non-formal post-growth educators held in Czechia. The event brought together 16 educators and youth workers from 10 European countries for experiential learning, sharing educational practices, testing the newly developed workshops, giving feedback, and planning future cooperation. The gathering also served as a foundation for building an emerging European network of post-growth educators.


<< Results >>

The main tangible result of the project was the creation of the publication called: Transformative Education for a Post-Growth Future: A Collection of Workshops published in English, Czech, and Croatian as an open-access digital resource. The handbook contains theoretical introductions to transformative education and post-growth, alongside eleven newly developed educational methodologies designed for non-formal educators.

Another important result was the organization of the international gathering for educators, which strengthened participants’ competencies in transformative education and knowledge of post-growth and fostered exchange between organisations from different European countries. The gathering also laid the foundations for an ongoing European Post-growth Educators Network that will continue sharing resources, methodologies, and opportunities for cooperation beyond the project period.

In addition, the project increased awareness of post-growth education within the field education for sustainable development. The dissemination activities helped reach educators, youth organisations, and sustainability initiatives across Europe, contributing to the growing recognition of post-growth as a solution to today's problems.

2024-3-DK01-KA210-YOU-000266565.title: Empowering youth for true climate action
2024-3-DK01-KA210-YOU-000266565.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was developed in response to the growing challenge of greenwashing, which increasingly undermines genuine climate action and misleads young people who are highly motivated but often lack the tools to critically assess environmental claims. Research and practical experience of the partner organisations highlighted that youth and youth workers are exposed to a high volume of sustainability messaging, yet lack structured, accessible methods to distinguish between authentic and misleading practices.

At the same time, organisations identified a clear gap in youth work: the absence of practical, digital tools and engaging educational content that connect climate literacy with real-life examples. This need was particularly evident among young people in remote and disadvantaged contexts, where access to quality climate education is limited.

The project therefore addressed the need to strengthen critical thinking, improve climate literacy, and equip youth workers with innovative tools and methodologies to support young people in engaging with climate action in an informed and meaningful way.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to strengthen the capacity of young people and youth workers to recognise and challenge greenwashing, while promoting genuine and informed climate action. A key objective was the development of an innovative digital Green Benchmark Tool, enabling youth and organisations to critically assess environmental claims and adopt more responsible practices.

In parallel, the project sought to create a Story Hub consisting of 30 educational articles, designed to translate complex climate and sustainability issues into accessible, real-life learning content. Another important objective was to equip youth workers with the knowledge and practical skills to integrate these tools into their educational activities through a structured capacity-building process.

Furthermore, the project aimed to foster cooperation between partner organisations and expand their competencies in green and digital youth work. Finally, it intended to actively engage young people through dissemination and campaign activities, raising awareness and encouraging meaningful participation in climate action.

<< Implementation >>

The project was implemented through a coherent set of interconnected activities designed to ensure both development and practical application of results. It began with an online kick-off meeting, where partners aligned on methodology, roles, and timelines, ensuring a structured and coordinated implementation process.

A key activity was the study visit to Greenland, which provided participants with direct insights into climate change realities and authentic case studies. These findings informed the development of the Green Benchmark Tool and the Story Hub.

The core implementation phase focused on creating the digital tool and 30 educational stories, followed by a 5-day capacity-building workshop for youth workers, where participants were trained to apply the project outputs in practice.

Finally, the project included community events, multiplier activities, and a climate action campaign, ensuring dissemination of results, engagement of young people, and validation of the developed tools in real educational contexts.

<< Results >>

The project successfully delivered all planned results in line with the defined objectives. 

1) A functional Green Benchmark Tool was developed, providing youth and organisations with a practical method to assess environmental claims and identify greenwashing.
https://www.trueclimateaction.eu/results/
2) The Story Hub was completed with 30 educational articles, offering real-life case studies and accessible content that supports climate literacy and critical thinking among young people.
3) The capacity of youth workers was strengthened through an international training, where 12 participants were equipped with the competencies to integrate the tool and educational materials into their daily work. 
Partner organisations enhanced their capacities in green and digital youth work, improving their ability to implement sustainable practices and cooperate internationally.
4) The project established an international network of more than 30 organisations, ensuring continued cooperation, knowledge exchange, and long-term sustainability of results. 
5) The climate action campaign exceeded expectations, reaching over 1,000 young people and stakeholders, significantly increasing awareness and engagement in climate action.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2024-3-FR02-KA210-YOU-000279720.title: Musique et Langues Minoritaires Régionales
2024-3-FR02-KA210-YOU-000279720.summary:
<< Background >>

The MUS-LaMiRé project addresses the cultural and linguistic loss of European minorities (Occitan and Arbanesh). It empowers musicians aged 13–30 through non-formal learning, combining music and tech to prepare them for the professional world.

Key Pillars & Outcomes:
Digital Skills: Solved tech gaps via a 150-hour hybrid training on P2P cloud and live audio technologies, upskilling 15 European musicians.

Mobility & Roots: Formed the Small European Orchestra of Linguistic Minorities (POEM). Held 3 residential workshops in Italy (Guardia Piemontese), France (Lentigny), and Croatia (Zadar) to connect youth, schools, and local artists with their heritage.

Media Visibility: Battled the invisibility of minority languages with a social media campaign. Featuring over 120 multimedia assets (posts, interviews, reels), it gained 45,079 views and 1,460 interactions, engaging younger generations.

<< Objectives >>

With the MUS-LaMiRé project, we set ourselves the objective of revitalizing the heritage of European linguistic minorities, starting with Occitan and Arbanesh, using music and digital innovation as the main tools, and promoting social inclusion and intercultural dialogue among youth. In particular:
Creation of a transnational artistic network: We united the 15 young musicians in the POEM orchestra, offering a space for study and non-formal cooperation.
Enhancement of digital skills: We wanted to bridge the technological gap of the participants. This objective was achieved through 150 hours of online training focused on P2P cloud, live recordings, and 3D video backdrops.
Dissemination and mass impact: We wanted to give visibility to endangered languages. Thanks to a targeted strategy on Facebook and Instagram with 131 posts, we generated over 45,000 views and 1,460 interactions.
Synergy with local communities: We implemented 3 residential workshops in Italy, France, and Croatia, which culminated in public concerts capable of raising awareness among the population regarding the value of cultural diversity.


<< Implementation >>


The MUS-LaMiRé project was implemented through a series of synergetic activities, structured in a hybrid format:
Management and Selection: After an online Kickoff meeting translated into 3 languages (277 views) and published on delay on the partnership's Facebook pages, we launched a transnational selection call that led to the selection of 15 young European musicians aged 13 to 30 to form the POEM orchestra.
Digital Training: We delivered 150 hours of hybrid training to create a common repertoire of 10 tracks.
Mobility and Residential Workshops: We implemented 3 on-site workshops in Italy (Guardia Piemontese), France (Lentigny), and Croatia (Zadar). The youth deepened their knowledge of Occitan and Arbanesh cultures with local masters, combining orchestral practice with the promotion and knowledge of minority languages.
Dissemination: We implemented a continuous digital communication strategy with 131 posts (including photos, interviews, and viral reels) on Facebook and Instagram, reaching over 45,000 views, and held 3 final concerts open to the public.

<< Results >>

The MUS-LaMiRé project delivered significant tangible outputs and community impacts across four key areas:

The POEM Orchestra: Established the Petit Ensemble Européen des minorités linguistiques, selecting 15 young musicians (ages 13–30) through a transnational call managed in 4 languages (French, Italian, Croatian, and English).

Repertoire & Training: Produced a shared repertoire of 10 Arbanesh and Occitan tracks. This was developed through 150 hours of digital training and an online repository, where youth co-created arrangements under teacher supervision.

Events & Mobility: Conducted 3 residential workshops and 3 live concerts in Guardia Piemontese (Italy), Lentigny (France), and Zadar (Croatia). Highlights included an eco-sustainable lake concert and urban flashmobs.

Digital Dissemination: Launched dedicated web sections and published 131 multimedia contents (posts, reels, interviews) on Facebook and Instagram, gaining over 45,000 views and 1,460 direct interactions, alongside an official YouTube video-concert.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2024-3-HR01-KA210-YOU-000295206.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was applied based on several basic needs that we fulfilled during the implementation.
1. The need of all three involved organizations to exchange knowledge and experience in order to strengthen themselves in the long term and to achieve a greater impact in the field of climate activism through joint action.
2. To increase influence in the activist-artistic field in general through the organic connection of artistic practices and green activism. The need to create a common, unified methodology that connects art and activism. In this way, it becomes much more interesting and accessible to young people.
3. We wanted to improve our approach, communication and work with young people from geographically isolated areas. Given that we all work with young people, we have noticed how difficult it is to involve and motivate young people in geographically isolated areas and even reach them. Part of the project activites was aimed precisely at a long-term solution to this problem.

<< Objectives >>

The two main goals of this project were:
1. In the long term, strengthen the capacities of all three organizations involved in the project through: empowerment and systematic education of the involved members, joint creation of a unified methodology in the field of environmental activism, and the launch of a new international digital platform.
2. Through a series of local activities (live and online), involve a larger number of young people with fewer opportunities for active participation in the field of climate activism. Strengthen their capacities and connect them with the involved organizations in the long term.

3. Mapping and initial education for young people Portugal (combined)
4. The first transnational education and exchange of knowledge - Portugal (live)
5. First virtual education and review (online)
6. Mentoring session 'Climate fiction' (online)
7. Mapping and education for young people Italy (combined)
8. Second transnational education and knowledge exchange, Italy (live)
9. Second virtual education and review (online)
10. Mentoring session "Boiler house" (online)
11. Mapping and education for young people Croatia (combined)
12. Third transnational education and knowledge exchange, Croatia (live)
13. Third virtual education and review (online)
14. Launching the 'Climate f(r)iction' platform and setting up educational materials (online)
15. Information campaign and implementation of the 'Climate f(r)iction' competition (combined)
16. Final virtual conference and meeting (combined)

<< Results >>

1. 514 young people from 3 countries were empowered through local lectures and workshops in the field of climate activism.
2. 9 members of the three involved organizations acquired new skills and knowledge and increased their capacities through three mentoring sessions, practical tasks, three live international meetings and other activities.
3. 19 schools in three countries were included in the process of mapping geo-isolated students and 3 documents were created with the mapping results.

2024-3-SI02-KA210-YOU-000296379.title: BadgeUp
2024-3-SI02-KA210-YOU-000296379.summary:
<< Background >>

Za BadgeUp smo se odločili zaradi izziva, ki ga zaznavamo pri delu z mladimi: kako podpreti ustvarjalnost brez izgube strukture in mlade spodbuditi, da idejo izpeljejo do konca, ne le začnejo. Mladim največkrat ne manjka navdiha, ampak imajo težavo odločiti se za eno pot in premagati strah pred neuspehom. Izziv smo prepoznali kot skupnega mladim v Sloveniji in na Hrvaškem, zato smo nanj odgovorili s čezmejnim partnerstvom, kjer se mladi iz obeh držav učijo drug od drugega.

Naslavljamo tri prednostne naloge:

Kakovost, inovativnost in priznavanje: strukturirana pot z vrstniško vodenimi "accountability" skupinami za spremljanje napredka ter sistem značk za priznavanje dosežkov.

Aktivno državljanstvo, iniciativnost in podjetnost: udeleženci prevzamejo odgovornost za lokalni izziv in vizijo spremenijo v dokumentiran rezultat, ob tem razvijejo razporejanje virov, prilagajanje glede na povratne informacije in javno predstavljanje dosežkov, kar naslavlja tudi osamljenost mladih.

Vključevanje in raznolikost: program je brezplačen in odprt za vse profile mladih, ne glede na predznanje ali okolje, kar znižuje vstopne ovire do podpore.

<< Objectives >>

Cilj projekta BadgeUp je bil 32 mladim iz Slovenije in Hrvaške ponuditi strukturirano pot za pretvorbo osebne ideje v dokončan rezultat in s tem premostiti vrzel med zamislijo in izvedbo ter okrepiti vodstvene kompetence. V ta namen so bile oblikovane accountability skupine, kjer so udeleženci na srečanjih v živo in na spletu medsebojno spremljali napredek in si pod mentorskim vodstvom nudili medsebojno podporo. Sistem značk (BadgeUp) je zagotovil jasno priznavanje dosežkov in aktivno vključenost mladih v evalvacijo za povečanje kakovosti in inovativnosti v mladinskem delu.

Projekt je spodbujal tudi aktivno državljanstvo, iniciativnost in podjetnost, saj je vsak udeleženec prevzel lastništvo nad lokalnim družbenim ali okoljskim izzivom in svojo vizijo pretvoril v dokumentiran rezultat, ki naslavlja konkreten izziv v njegovem okolju. Ob tem so razvili prenosljive kompetence za zaposljivost, kot so načrtovanje virov, prilagajanje na podlagi podatkov, koordinacijo z deležniki in javno predstavitev dela.

<< Implementation >>

Additionally, we strive to increase youth employability, ensure LGBTQIA+ inclusion, and alleviate stress related to post-Covid and the war in Ukraine.

<< Implementation >>

The project activities will unfold over a 12-month period, guided by two core principles: learning by doing and innovative approaches. These include seventeen online meetings (Coordination/Evaluation/Kick off and Final evaluation meeting), and a training course on M.I.N.D. for mental health, creation of intellectual outputs (a printable digital project booklet and online library of materials including a podcast series), and a final retreat for sharing the project results with a broader audience.

<< Results >>

The MIND project aims to enhance youth workers' skills in mindfulness, inclusion, non-judgment, and diversity for mental health. Expected results include improved mental health support for youth, practical tools for youth workers, increased collaboration among organizations, and the creation of a comprehensive MIND booklet, podcast  and other audio resources. The project will foster long-term partnerships, promote inclusivity, and empower youth to address mental health challenges.

2025-1-IE01-KA210-YOU-000353715.title: Improving Mental Health Education and Awareness for Youth Workers
2025-1-IE01-KA210-YOU-000353715.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to enhance the professional development of youth workers by creating and testing a training course on mental health, inclusion, partnership working, and non-formal education. It seeks to improve local youth work practices, equip youth workers with practical tools, and foster international collaboration. Through feedback and dissemination, the project will ensure sustainability, providing youth workers with skills to support young people’s development across different countries.

<< Implementation >>

The project will start with a gap analysis to identify training needs. A five-day course on mental health, inclusion, partnership working, and non-formal education will be developed. Youth workers will be recruited to pilot the course and provide feedback. The course materials will be translated and localized for wider use. Multiplier events will be organised to promote the course and engage more youth workers, ensuring the training reaches a broader audience.

<< Results >>

The project will result in 9 youth workers testing and providing feedback on the course, 4 multiplier events reaching 100 participants, and 3 partners completing translations and adapting materials to local needs. A follow-up Erasmus+ proposal will be developed to extend the course, while each partner will run the course locally at least once a year. The collaboration will result in a comprehensive course ready for local delivery, enhancing youth workers' skills across the participating regions
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2025-1-IE01-KA210-YOU-000354504.summary:

2025-1-IT03-KA210-YOU-000354443.title: PATH: Participatory Approaches to Training in Histor
2025-1-IT03-KA210-YOU-000354443.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to foster historical awareness and critical thinking through participatory education. By engaging youth, teachers, educators and local communities in heritage education, active citizenship and cultural participation, it promotes dialogue on collective history. Through workshops, exhibitions and a best practices toolkit, the project enhances educational methodologies and strengthens the capacity of organizations to integrate inclusive historical narratives into their work.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes training, workshops, a collection day and dissemination activities. Partner organizations will exchange methodologies through job shadowing and training on participatory heritage education. Workshops for different targets will explore collective history. The collection day will gather personal stories, leading to an exhibition.

<< Results >>

The project will result in increased capacity for educators, youth workers and cultural practitioners through training and knowledge exchange. Young participants will gain new skills and awareness of historical and cultural heritage through participatory workshops. Local communities will engage in storytelling and memory-sharing activities. Key outputs include two exhibitions in Milan and Zagreb and a best practices toolkit, ensuring long-term impact and replicability across Europe.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2025-1-IT03-KA210-YOU-000366010.title: Youth for Climate Justice: Building Capacities for Local Impact
2025-1-IT03-KA210-YOU-000366010.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen youth organizations' skills in climate advocacy and democratic participation, promoting transnational cooperation and environmental education. We want to engage young people in local decision-making, develop practical awareness tools, and create a network of activists for climate justice.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes online training sessions, two transnational meetings with workshops and conferences, National Forums in each participating country, local training sessions for dissemination, focus groups, and surveys to collect data and create a Handbook on best practices in climate activism.

<< Results >>

The project will lead to greater youth awareness and participation in climate issues, the creation of accessible educational materials, and the adoption of effective advocacy strategies by the involved organizations. The strengthened partner network will ensure sustainability and replicability of activities.

2025-1-NO02-KA210-YOU-000356006.title: Healthy Environment Activities for Learning Together in Harmony
2025-1-NO02-KA210-YOU-000356006.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Today's youth face physical inactivity, isolation, and mental health challenges due to digitalization. Our project aims to improve youth's well-being by reconnecting them with nature through outdoor activities, peer education, and digital resources. We will develop healthy habits, reduce isolation, increase environmental awareness, and train peer leaders in health and sustainability, creating lasting impact through structured nature-based programs and comprehensive training materials.

<< Implementation >>

The project implements three main activity streams:First, local nature-based wellbeing activities in each country focusing on nutrition, physical activity, and mental health over 12 months. Second, three international training events in Turkey (nutrition/mental health),Spain (adapted outdoor sports), and Norway (nature connection/mindfulness). Third, development of digital resources including a peer leadership training program, e-training manual, and online platform to ensure sustainable impact

<< Results >>

Expected results include: 70% of participants developing regular physical activity habits, 65% reduction in stress levels through nature activities, 70% adoption of eco-friendly practices, and training of at least 10 peer leaders. The project will also produce sustainable digital resources including a peer leadership training program(R1), e-training manual(R2), and online platform(R3) to ensure long-term impact across partner countries.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2025-1-PL01-KA210-YOU-000351514.title: EvalCards: The Mobile Evaluation Toolkit
2025-1-PL01-KA210-YOU-000351514.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to improve the quality and innovation of youth work by developing a mobile toolkit of 40 evaluation and reflection methods and providing training for youth workers. By fostering international collaboration and capacity-building, the project addresses Erasmus+ priorities of increasing the recognition of youth work, introducing new learning methods, and supporting the continuous professional development of educators.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement three main activities:
(1) Develop a mobile toolkit of 40 evaluation and reflection methods for youth workers,
(2) Host an international workshop to foster knowledge exchange and create innovative methods, and
(3) Organize local training sessions for 45 youth workers, enhancing their capacity to use the toolkit. These activities align with Erasmus+ goals of improving the quality and innovation of youth work.
(4) Organize dissemination events in 3 countries (150 pax)

<< Results >>

The project will result in a mobile toolkit of 40 evaluation and reflection methods, accessible in three languages (Macedonian, Croatian, and Polish). It will train 45 youth workers in using these methods, enhancing their capacity to evaluate and improve youth programs. The project will also foster international collaboration and innovation, directly contributing to Erasmus+ goals of increasing the quality and recognition of youth work across Europe.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2025-1-PL01-KA210-YOU-000360932.title: Think Twice (It's Alright): Creating International Partnerships in Battle with Disinformation
2025-1-PL01-KA210-YOU-000360932.summary:
<< Objectives >>

1) Creating a platform for sharing experiences in the field of disinformation among organisations.
2) Improving youth competences in detecting and battling disinformation.
3) Sharing knowledge within international cooperation to improve youth work with an emphasis on the Białystok region.
4) Introducing the Erasmus+ program to partner organizations and young people across participating countries.
5) Sharing project results with international institutions to promote education on disinformation.

<< Implementation >>

In each partner country, we will organize meetings for 16 participants. Meetings will include a teambuilding activity, followed by sharing best practices in youth work related to the topic. During the meetings, we will visit local organizations working in the field of disinformation and education. Together, we will prepare a brochure and implement a workshop for local youth in Białystok. After the workshop, a brainstorming session will be held to improve future versions followed by evaluation.

<< Results >>

1) An increase in the competencies of organizations in the field of youth work and the coordination of international projects.
2) An increase in young people's competencies in identifying disinformation and raising awareness of the importance of the issue.
3) The creation of an international network of organizations engaged in combating disinformation to improve their work.
4) The dissemination of the Erasmus+ program’s reach, its opportunities, and values among youth.

2025-1-PT02-KA210-YOU-000352916.title: YMWB - Youth Mental Well-being
2025-1-PT02-KA210-YOU-000352916.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The YMWB project aims to enhance mental health support for youth, particularly those from marginalized backgrounds. Key objectives include equipping youth workers and educators with tools to address emotional regulation and resilience, through trainings and a comprehensive manual on youth mental well-being. The project seeks to raise awareness of mental health issues and ensure long-term sustainability by integrating resources into ongoing practices, ultimately creating a lasting positive impact

<< Implementation >>

The YMWB project will implement several key activities, including training for youth professionals, focused on emotional regulation strategies; a comprehensive guideline on youth mental well-being. Outreach through workshops and social media will raise awareness about youth mental health issues, while community events will gather feedback to ensure developed tools effectively meet the needs of young people, fostering support and resilience.

<< Results >>

The YMWB project is expected to enhance the capacity of youth workers and educators to support young people's mental health, particularly in emotional regulation. We anticipate the development of a manual that provides practical strategies for addressing youth mental health challenges. We also aim to implement a training for trainers on how to utilise the developed guidelines, hence increasing awareness on these issues among stakeholders.

2025-1-RO01-KA210-YOU-000362886.title: S.H.I.E.L.D.: Întărim Democrația, Combatem Dezinformarea
2025-1-RO01-KA210-YOU-000362886.summary:
<< Objectives >>

O1: Increasing the media and digital competencies of 20 youth leaders (18-30 years old) from Romania, Croatia, Greece, and Turkey, and 4 partner organizations.
 O2: Forming a group of 20 youth leaders capable of organizing civic initiatives and actively contributing to the development of their communities.
O3: Informing 2000 young people from partner countries about the dangers of disinformation.
 O4: Developing the ability of youth leaders and partner organizations to combat extremism and hate

<< Implementation >>

1.- Kick Off Meeting.
2.- Meeting 1: "Fake News and Democracy: The Threat of Disinformation".
3.- Meeting 2: "Communication and Counter-Narratives for Democracy".
4.- Meeting 3:  "Youth Leadership in Defending Democracy".
5.- Dissemination activities & events.
6.- Final meeting & closing event.

<< Results >>

The project aims to enhance the media and digital skills of 20 youth leaders and 4 partner organizations, form a group of leaders capable of organizing civic initiatives, inform 2,000 young people about the dangers of disinformation, and develop their ability to combat extremism and hate speech. These results will contribute to strengthening democracy by promoting active youth involvement and combating disinformation in their communities.

2025-1-RS01-KA210-YOU-000351819.title: YOUTH RISE - Reduce anxiety, Improve literacy, Strengthen resilience, Engage in action
2025-1-RS01-KA210-YOU-000351819.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Main objective is to empower youth to improve their climate literacy, strengthen climate resilience, reduce climate anxiety and engage in climate action. We also want to develop and apply innovative holistic approach to climate education of youth, improve access to knowledge and to increase youth's motivation to engage in educational and climate activities, enhance competences and skills of youth workers, improve capacities of partner organizations and share the knowledge and best practices.

<< Implementation >>

1. Project management
2. Development of Climate Education Methodology and Capacity Building of Youth Workers
3. Pilot workshops for youth and youth mobility Camp
4. Communication and dissemination

<< Results >>

-Research „Climate emotions - how climate change changes us“ on 180 youth 
-Non-formal innovative educational program 
-Head-heart-hands handbook with guidelines for youth workers 
-Climate game
-Mobile application
-6+ youth workers from 3 countries trained in 3H methodology

2025-1-RS01-KA210-YOU-000366198.title: Jedan korak bliže - inovativni pristup za podršku mladima u riziku
2025-1-RS01-KA210-YOU-000366198.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We want to improve work with young people at risk by strengthening the capacity of youth workers and organizations that work with young people. It aims to develop and strengthen the competencies of youth workers and everyone who works with young people through specially designed acitivities for youth workers, in the field of mental health, occupational therapy and social entrepreneurship;Creation of an innovative tool for working with youth - a therapeutic plan; Strengthening partnerships

<< Implementation >>

The activities planned by this project are:
1. Kick off meeting
2. Study visit
3. Training for youth workers - One step closer
4. Creation of a therapeutic plan
5. Dissemination Serbia
6. Dissemination Croatia
7. Management (ongoing throughout the duration of the project)
8. Evaluation meeting

Built capacities for at least 12 youth workers in the field of mental health, therapeutic-educational programs and social entrepreneurship
New knowledge was acquired about a sustainable, ecologically social enterprise 
A "therapeutic plan" was developed and implemented.

2025-1-SE02-KA210-YOU-000366229.title: Digital Dojang - enabling digital transformation in youth sports
2025-1-SE02-KA210-YOU-000366229.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project aims to modernize youth sports training, enhance digital competence, and strengthen international collaboration. Key objectives include:

- Train youth workers and coaches in digital tools like Daedo Gen 3.
- Develop a structured digital training model for easy adoption.
- Create high-quality digital training resources such as videos and manuals.
- Strengthen international cooperation in digital youth sports.
-  Ensure long-term sustainability of digital training methods.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes 7 core activities to ensure effective digital transformation in youth sports:

Project management to oversee coordination and communication.
Kickoff workshop in Croatia to align strategies.
Surveys to assess the needs of coaches and athletes.
Development of a structured digital training method.
Digital launch event of digital methods
Creation of digital training resources such as videos and manuals.
Final dissemination event in Croatia to share results and ensure adoption.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver tangible and lasting results that improve digital competence in youth sports and support sustainable innovation.

50+ coaches and youth workers trained in digital tools.
10+ sports clubs adopting the digital training model.
10+ digital training resources (videos, manuals, interactive modules).
200+ participants engaging with training materials.
Increased international collaboration and a stronger network for future projects.
Sustainable digital training in youth sports

2025-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000357305.title: Razvoj mladinskega mikromedija
2025-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000357305.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The creation of a youth micro-media is based on the ideas of youth and supported by mentors. A working methodology is developed, a set of technical and software tools is prepared and everything is tested in practice. Increasing knowledge about media production and raising awareness about media literacy, especially in the light of the development of artificial intelligence and fake news, will result in greater digital competences for organisations, youth workers, school mentors and young people.

<< Implementation >>

The project consists of project management, participation of 6 mentors in 14 online meetings, dissemination, promotion, organisation of a mentors' expert meeting in Pula and Kamnik and participation of 6 mentors in each of them, preparation of a Mikromedia Guidebook, preparation of a Mikromedia Toolkit, organisation of a field visit in Pula and Kamnik and participation of 6 mentors and 12 young people in each of them, and implementation of 8 webcasts in Kamnik and Pula.

<< Results >>

The Mikromedia Guidebook brings together theoretical knowledge on media, journalism, technology and programming. 8 webcasts are used to test the Guidebook in practice. The Mikromedia Toolkit puts the theoretical knowledge from the Guidebook into practice in the form of a video. 2 micromedia tools are set up, 6 mentors trained and 12 young people involved. The results are not only tailored to the youth sector, but are applicable in any setting, including schools, and further empower them.

2025-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000362770.title: Civic Influencer Academy
2025-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000362770.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project addresses polarisation and extremisms by empowering young people for digital active citizenship. Through education, mentoring, networking and content creation, the Civic Influencer Academy will enable young people to develop digital skills, co-create counter-narratives and strengthen European values. Partners will gain new knowledge and connections for further collaboration, and young people will have a space for activation and influential participation in democratic processes.

<< Implementation >>

Development and implementation of the Civic Influencer Academy program with a 4-day boot-camp, a 6-month mentoring program and supporting materials
Conclusion of the academy with a public event, which we will co-create with the young participants (presentation of their work, discussion on topics related to online activism and active citizenship)
2 online presentations for the youth sector (in Slovenia and Croatia)
Dissemination activities

<< Results >>

Developed, tested and disseminated Civic Influencer Academy program with 4-day boot-camp, 6-month mentoring program and supporting materials
20 trained young people who create min. 60 counter-narrative artivistic videos to raise awareness about European values
4 empowered trainers
Strengthened partnership for work at the intersection of digital active citizenship-youth work and established foundations for future (co)operation
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2025-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000365321.title: LUFT - aktivacija ulice in mladih z manj priložnostmi
2025-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000365321.summary:
<< Objectives >>

With the LUFT project, we aim to actively address the issue of young people on the streets and offer them alternative forms of activities in an innovative, active, and inclusive way. Through these activities, they will be able to identify themselves, develop, and leave a positive impact on society as well as on their personal growth and development.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, we will carry out the following activities:

- PLANNING, MANAGEMENT, COORDINATION, AND EVALUATION OF THE PROJECT
- DEVELOPMENT OF A PRACTICAL CONCEPT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF TRAINING FOR THE ACTIVATION OF YOUTH AND THE "STREET" YOUTH
- PROJECT VISIBILITY AND PROMOTION
- PREPARATION OF A DIGITAL BROCHURE FOR PROMOTIONAL PURPOSES AND TRAINING OF "LUFT" CONCEPT TRAINERS
- IMPLEMENTATION OF FIELD ACTIVITIES AND ACTIVATION OF "LUFTARJI"
- DISSEMINATION AND EXPANSION

<< Results >>

The main results of the project are as follows:

Activation of young people from the streets
Inclusion of young people in socially beneficial projects
Development of an innovative approach to working with youth
Positive impact on current and pressing issues of youth on the streets (violence, drugs, vandalism)
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2025-1-TR01-KA210-YOU-000351554.title: PAYLAŞIN, DEĞİŞTİRİN, GELİŞTİRİN
2025-1-TR01-KA210-YOU-000351554.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The goals we aim to achieve by implementing this project are to promote the concept of volunteering, equip participants with valuable skills in the field of volunteering, and make a societal contribution. The aim is to spread volunteering activities to a wider audience, increase the community's interest in volunteering, and strengthen the understanding of volunteering at the local

<< Implementation >>

Trainings will be organized to develop important skills such as volunteering, leadership, communication, teamwork, crisis management, and social responsibility, with a focus on improving crisis management and problem-solving skills. Volunteering projects targeting local communities (such as helping the elderly and disadvantaged individuals, as well as activities in the fields of sports and youth) will be carried out.

<< Results >>

The goal is to promote the culture of volunteering, allowing participants to develop their personal and societal skills, while creating social impact through volunteering activities. This project aims to increase participation in volunteering activities and raise awareness in the community about the value and importance of volunteering.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Quality and innovation of youth work

2025-2-FR02-KA210-YOU-000370315.title: MultiLingui: Bridging Academic Multilingual Expertise with Cultural and Artistic NGO Practices
2025-2-FR02-KA210-YOU-000370315.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The main goal of “MultiLingui: Bridging Academic Multilingual Expertise with Cultural and Artistic NGO Practices" is to connect the rich multilingual knowledge and practices of academia with on-the-ground work of cultural and artistic NGOs by:

1.Bridging the gap between academia and NGOs in multilingualism.

2.Enhancing the (multilingual and socio-linguistic) competencies and awareness of young people.

3.Facilitating knowledge transfer between NGO practitioners regarding multilingualism.

<< Implementation >>

Our four key activities will create pathways for dialogue, adaptation, and integration of academic knowledge into fieldwork capitalizing on the crossed expertise of its multilingual experts and NGO practitioners:
1.Management and research phase to ensure professional and academic expertise.
2.Testing phase at local level on young learners of partners communities.
3.Communication and dissemination to a broader audience.
4.Results production: booklet and impact study benefiting NGO practitioners.

<< Results >>

By fostering European collaboration, sharing expertise in the field of multilingualism, and producing transferable results like the booklet and impact study, we seek to enhance the effectiveness and inclusivity of NGO fieldwork while amplifying the impact of academic insights.

Through this transdisciplinary approach, the project aspires to build bridges between theory and practice, empowering communities and organizations to thrive in culturally diverse and linguistically rich contexts.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Teaching and learning of foreign languages
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2025-2-FR02-KA210-YOU-000376465.title: InFormal Creativity: Unfolded
2025-2-FR02-KA210-YOU-000376465.summary:
<< Objectives >>

-Provide effective, practical creativity-development tools for youth workers and educators
-Support wider community of educators with easy-to-use, engaging creativity methods in various creative approaches (theatre, animation, visual tools and podcasts) through an interactive ToolBank
-Develop innovative methodologies that increase effective participation as well as boost creativity exploring synergies between the approaches
-Strengthen young people’s creative confidence

<< Implementation >>

A1 Project management and coordination
A2 7-day training for 20 educators training educators on usage of creative methods - theatre, podcasts, visual thinking and animation as well as exploring synergies among the approaches.
A3 Creation of the open Interactive ToolBank (≥16 methods + ≥5 hybrid), translated in Hungarian, French, Polish and Croatian.
A4-7  4 national multiplier events in partner countries
Ongoing dissemination, monitoring/evaluation, local pilots and sustainability actions.

<< Results >>

-20 educators trained in using creative methods: theatre, podcasts, visual thinking and animation and empowered to promote creativity learning;
-at least 5 newly developed creative educational hybrid methods 
- an open ToolBank (EN+PL/FR/HR/HU) with ≥16 ready-to-use methods and ≥5 hybrid ones;
- 80–120 youth engaged in local pilots, showing higher creative confidence and collaboration;
- 4 multiplier events reaching wider community of educators, youth NGOs and other practitioners from the field.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2025-2-FR02-KA210-YOU-000382664.title: ImmuniFact: building immunity through critical thinking and fact-checking
2025-2-FR02-KA210-YOU-000382664.summary:
<< Objectives >>

ImmuniFact will build the capacity of youth workers in New Caledonia, Spain, and Croatia to counter disinformation and support young people’s critical participation in democratic life. Through an innovative learning methodology combining prebunking and debunking activities and a Media Literacy Compass, youth workers will be equipped to help young people critically assess digital content, resist manipulation, and reduce polarisation.

<< Implementation >>

The project will include eight key activities: effective project management; a needs assessment with young people and youth workers; a cross-country CoCreate Hub in New Caledonia; the design of an innovative learning methodology; the creation of the Media Literacy Compass; a transnational Training of Trainers in Croatia; in-country peer-to-peer training of youth workers; and multiplier events in New Caledonia, Spain, and Croatia to share results and promote the long-term use of the tools.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver four main results: a needs analysis report identifying the media literacy challenges faced in the three territories; a comprehensive package including the methodology with prebunking and debunking activities and a digital Media Literacy Compass; a pool of trained youth workers able to apply the methodology and cascade it to their peers; and multiplier events to share and promote the results among youth organisations, schools, policymakers, and communities.

2025-2-IS01-KA210-YOU-000367703.title: STAY – Skills for Thriving, Agency and Youth Engagement
2025-2-IS01-KA210-YOU-000367703.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to reduce quiet quitting among youth (18–28) by raising awareness of early disengagement and building communication and boundary-setting skills. It will develop the STAY Handbook and a multilingual Engagement & Quiet-Quitting Risk Scanner, pilot them with youth, and strengthen collaboration among organisations and educators to support sustained engagement.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement several key activities: co-create the STAY Handbook; design and launch a multilingual Engagement & Quiet-Quitting Risk Scanner on a simple STAY platform; hold a 2-day in-person kick-off in Iceland to lock workplans; run a 5-day capacity-building workshop for 12 youth workers; deliver Quiet Circles (one per country) for 15 young people each; and roll out a transnational STAY Engagement Campaign combining social media challenges with community pop-ups.

<< Results >>

Results:
1. Open-access STAY Handbook (4 languages) adopted by youth workers
2. Multilingual Engagement & Quiet-Quitting Risk Scanner live with 200 unique uses; 
3. 12 youth workers trained (Youthpass) and 3 Quiet Circles piloted (15 youth each); 
4. Campaign reaches 1,000 youth, driving 200 handbook downloads; 
5. Partners embed tools and routines for sustained engagement.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2025-2-IT03-KA210-YOU-000375227.title: Mind in Motion : Move. Include. Nature. Develop.
2025-2-IT03-KA210-YOU-000375227.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Mind in Motion aims to build resilience, strengthen inclusion, and enhance digital readiness among young people and youth workers. The project will empower 45 youth and 18 youth workers to design practical tools for well-being and participation. By combining mindfulness, outdoor activities, and creative inclusion, the project addresses stress, isolation, and limited access to supportive youth work practices.

<< Implementation >>

Three transnational mobilities will be implemented: in Türkiye (My Mindful Routine on yoga and mindfulness), in Italy (Nature for Inclusion with outdoor walks and challenges), and in Croatia (Creative Inclusion Map through arts and sports). A transversal digital strand will coordinate online meetings and co-create the Mind&Move Toolbox, integrating all methods. Dissemination will use Erasmus+ platforms and social media campaigns.

<< Results >>

MIND project will produce concrete youth-led outputs: 21 Mindful Routines, a Nature for Inclusion Journal, a Creative Inclusion Map, and digital Toolbox Guidelines. Together they form the Mind&Move Toolbox, hosted online for two years. Directly, 63 participants( 45 young and 18 yourh worker) will gain resilience and facilitation skills. Indirectly, 300 youth and youth workers will access and apply the results via Erasmus+ Results Platform, SALTO, and partner networks.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2025-2-IT03-KA210-YOU-000385046.title: RECLAIM PEACE - Youth-led pathways for critical peace education, democratic participation and resilient preparedness
2025-2-IT03-KA210-YOU-000385046.summary:
<< Objectives >>

RECLAIM PEACE aims to strengthen young people’s ability to live and act in a Europe where peace can no longer be taken for granted. The project will create safe spaces where youth can process fears, build resilience and develop civic competences through Critical Peace Education. Its objectives are to: validate an innovative non-formal learning pathway on peace and preparedness; empower youth to resist disinformation and polarisation; and support their active engagement in democratic life.

<< Implementation >>

The project follows a clear pathway: it begins with participatory mapping of youth perceptions, followed by a transnational workshop in Rovereto where youth workers and participants co-design the framework. Local Peace Labs then test the approach, creating safe spaces for resilience and civic engagement. Insights are transformed into a Position Paper, validated with stakeholders in Croatia. Outputs will be published online and promoted through multiplier workshops and peer-to-peer campaigns.

<< Results >>

The main tangible outputs of the project are: a validated pathway on Critical Peace Education; a practical toolkit for youth workers; a youth-led Position Paper for decision makers. Intangible results include stronger socio-emotional resilience, critical thinking and digital literacy among 60 young people; increased quality and visibility of the partner organisations’ youth work; renewed dialogue between youth and local institutions; 30 local multipliers and 40 peer ambassadors activated.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2026-1-DK01-KA210-YOU-000454976.title: Redesigning STEM programmes in a 21st century way - inclusive and green
2026-1-DK01-KA210-YOU-000454976.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to develop greener and more inclusive STEM programs for youth (MO1), increase engagement of marginalized or underrepresented groups in STEM (MO2), and create a replicable methodology for youth centres to improve their STEM activities (MO3). It ensures youth gain practical skills in sustainability, intercultural understanding, and collaboration while empowering youth workers to implement innovative, inclusive, and environmentally conscious non-formal education approaches.

<< Implementation >>

Activities include A1: project management, quality assurance, and dissemination; A2: brainstorming sessions, methodology development, co-creation of inclusive STEM programs, and a Capacity Building Activity in Denmark; A3: promotion, recruitment, delivery of 12 youth-led sessions, creation of national InterSTEM showpieces, and reflection to produce a digital e-certification framework; A4: multiplier events in Croatia and national events to showcase results.

<< Results >>

Expected qualitative outcomes include enhanced youth interest and engagement in STEM, increased environmental awareness, improved inclusion of diverse youth, and stronger youth worker capacity to design and evaluate programs. Quantitative results include 6 trained youth workers, 30 youth participants, 36 STEM sessions delivered, three multiplier events, two videos and one reel, two newsletters, and one digital e-certification framework ready for replication in youth centres across Europe.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2026-1-FR02-KA210-YOU-000449612.title: Mindful Media
2026-1-FR02-KA210-YOU-000449612.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Mindful Media empowers care‑experienced youth and youth workers with skills, tools and confidence to critically engage with digital media, recognise AI‑generated content, counter disinformation, and raise public awareness of digital resilience. Through non‑formal, inclusive and creative learning across Europe it strengthens digital/AI literacy, ethical and accessible media production, civic participation, intercultural peer support and advocacy to influence public discourse.

<< Implementation >>

- Kick off meeting (France)
- Project launch and media literacy training (online)
- Research and development
- Digital media content creation training activity (Czechia)
- Film production
- Online dissemination and distribution
- Post-production training activity and Democratic Cabin (Croatia)
- Final meeting (online)
- Awareness campaign (inclusive of online and physical screening and presentation events)

<< Results >>

-Improved CEY digital/media/AI literacy to assess content 
-Increased civic engagement and youth participation
-Greater intercultural competence and cooperation  
-Youth‑led media promoting democratic values and combating disinformation
-Practical training modules and dissemination materials
-Films and exhibitions raising public awareness  
-Expanded outreach via national/EU networks and accessible platforms  
-Stronger partner capacity for inclusive, participatory digital education
