2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000454913.title: ''SAFE-CLICK” – Strengthening digital literacy And saFEty online of young people from small cities and rural areas
2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000454913.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project aims to strengthen youth workers  capacity to address algorithm-driven digital risks affecting young people aged 14–18 in small towns and rural communities. Objectives include identifying practical challenges faced by youth workers, developing a SAFE-CLICK Skills Framework, creating a Trigger-Based Response toolkit, building facilitation competence through training and piloting, and supporting sustainable uptake of the model by youth organisations and municipalities.

<< Implementation >>

Activities include needs mapping and research, development of the SAFE-CLICK Skills Framework and Trigger-Based Response T-Kit, internal testing and refinement, Training for Trainers, pilot implementation in Croatia and Slovenia, an online awareness campaign, national dissemination events, a European round table and replication workshop with municipalities. Project management ensures coordination, safeguarding, monitoring and quality throughout the project lifecycle.

<< Results >>

Expected results:
SAFE-CLICK Skills Framework developed
Trigger-Based Response T-Kit with 9 scenario-based modules created
8 youth workers trained through Training for Trainers
Pilot implementation involving 30 young people and 18 youth workers in Croatia and Slovenia
Online awareness campaign reaching approx. 42,000 young people
2 national dissemination events and 1 European round table implemented
Replication workshop engaging municipalities for future adoption
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

hr.name: ASSOCIATION FOR YOUTH EMPOWERMENT AND SECURITY

2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000456789.title: ZeroWaste - Small Actions, Real Impact!
2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000456789.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to develop and test the ZeroWaste Action Lab, a practical learning-by-doing framework for rural youth in Croatia, North Macedonia and Turkey. Through interactive Learning Labs, young people will experiment with sustainable habits, reflect on their consumption and take local climate action. The project also strengthens youth workers with innovative, action-based methods that can continue beyond the project.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes a transnational co-creation meeting to design the ZeroWaste Action Lab, followed by Field Labs in each country where rural youth test sustainable practices over several months. We will run a Digital Badge and Storytelling Campaign, train youth workers through a Facilitator Accelerator, organize Community Impact Days and hold a final international meeting to share results and ensure sustainability.

<< Results >>

The project will result in a tested ZeroWaste Action Lab framework with 5 Learning Labs available in 4 languages. At least 45 rural young people will complete real-life ZeroWaste experiments and 45 youth workers will gain practical methods to continue the approach. The project will also generate youth stories, community engagement events and stronger cooperation between rural organizations working on sustainability.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas

2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000458359.title: Off the Radar
2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000458359.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen youth mental well-being by developing and testing accessible, community-based methods addressing stress and eco-anxiety. It will empower young people through co-creation, build youth worker competences, and produce the open-access Silent Struggles Toolkit to support inclusive, low-cost well-being practices across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement five main activities: project management and coordination; a 5-day Transnational Exchange of Practices for youth workers; a 6-day Youth Co-Creation Week where young people test and adapt methods; a research phase and Local Well-being Labs in each country; development of the open-access Silent Struggles Toolkit; and local and European-level dissemination, including offline events and online promotion.

<< Results >>

The project will produce tested and youth-validated well-being methods, a digital open-access Silent Struggles Toolkit, and strengthened competences of youth workers in supporting mental well-being. Young participants will gain practical coping skills and confidence. Local communities and organisations will benefit from accessible tools and stronger cooperation, ensuring sustainable use of results beyond the project.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000460368.title: Resilient Rainbow - za razvoj otpornosti i inkluzivnu podršku mladima
2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000460368.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Project aim is to improve quality and sustainability of support for LGBTIQ+ youth by strengthening resilience of youth organisations and workers, and by developing youth work methodology. Project will standardize mental health care for youth workers,enabling them to work with (multiply) vulnerable LGBTIQ+ youth. Organizational capacities will be enhanced through development of new methodology, while increasing youth skills for emotional well-being and active participation in the digital sphere.

<< Implementation >>

Main activities include:
1.	Exchange of youth work methodologies among partners;
2.	Training for youth workers to strengthen their resilience and develop skills for working with multiply vulnerable LGBTIQ+ youth;
3.	Development of a Protocol for working with (multiply) vulnerable LGBTIQ+ youth;
4.	Training for LGBTIQ+ youth aimed at empowering their mental health and active, safe digital participation;
5.	Production of 2 video podcasts;
6.	Dissemination of project results:online,in Croatia and S

<< Results >>

Key results:
1.	Strengthened resilience of at least 6 organizations;
2.	Empowered 14 youth workers from 6 CSOs (HR/SRB) for working with (multiply) vulnerable youth and creating inclusive support systems;
3.	Developed Protocol for working with multiply vulnerable LGBTIQ+ youth;
4.	Empowered 16 LGBTIQ+ youth for mental healthcare and safe digital engagement;
5.	Created 2 podcasts for LGBTIQ+ youth;
6.	Dissemination of project results reached 25 professionals and 40 young persons in Croatia and Se

2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000462792.title: Participativno kazalište i digitalni alati za otpornost mladih
2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000462792.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The PLAYSAFE project aims to develop and test an innovative model for preventing risky behaviours among young people (15–19) by combining participatory theatre and digital tools. The project will strengthen the competences of at least 15 youth workers in Croatia, North Macedonia and Sweden and support young people in building resilience, reflection skills and informed decision-making.

<< Implementation >>

The project will develop and standardise the Playsafe model through international cooperation between partners, train 15 youth workers, implement pilot workshops with at least 150 young people and disseminate results. Activities include participatory theatre methods, digital reflection tools, international meetings, pilot implementation and the development of an open-access digital handbook.

<< Results >>

The project will produce a tested Playsafe prevention model, train 15 youth workers and involve at least 150 young people. Expected results include improved competences of youth workers, increased resilience and life skills among young people, and an open-access digital handbook enabling other organisations to replicate the model in different contexts.

2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000463663.title: Digital DeLAY: Youth work bridging science and families
2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000463663.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project builds the professional capacity of youth workers in Croatia and Italy to address the impact of digital and algorithmic environments on child development. We translate complex scientific research into a practical delay philosophy for families. By creating research-based tools and establishing a cross-sectoral bridge between science, youth work, and local communities, we provide parents with actionable strategies to navigate digital challenges and adopt digital delay.

<< Implementation >>

We will implement four main activities: a preparatory research mapping to align scientific data with youth work needs; a trans-national training for staff to master the delay methodology; a series of community dialogues and pilot workshops with parents; national awareness campaign; and a final dissemination phase. This includes the creation of an open access digital repository, a replication guide and a networking event in Croatia to ensure the project results reach a wider audience.

<< Results >>

We expect a significant increase in the expert competence of our youth workers and the creation of a validated visual toolkit for families. Tangible results include a functional digital repository and a follow-up roadmap for long-term sustainability. The project will lead to a reinforced network between local institutions and NGOs, ensuring that the digital delay philosophy becomes a permanent part of our community service and a reusable model for the European youth work sector.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000465404.title: Reel Change - Film kao alat za rad s mladima na postizanju društvenih promjena
2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000465404.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The objective is to strengthen intercultural dialogue through participatory filmmaking practices and to enhance the capacities of partner organisations to implement innovative and inclusive youth work programmes. Specific objectives are improving the quality and innovation of youth work, strengthening young people’s participation in democratic life, developing critical thinking, media literacy and digital competences, promoting inclusion and equal participation, creating sustainable results.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes monthly online coordination meetings between partner organisations, a two-day training course for youth workers, 8 local and 13 online workshops for young people, two 3-day international film camps (in Serbia and Croatia), post-production of audiovisual works, the development of a methodological handbook, and public presentations and dissemination through media and social networks. The involvement of diverse stakeholders in partner organisations ensures capacity building.

<< Results >>

Expected results include three completed audiovisual works, a developed participatory film methodology and a published handbook describing the methodology, as well as two public presentations of the audiovisual works. The project will result in strengthened civic competences of young people, enhanced organisational capacities of partners and youth workers, increased awareness of discrimination, intolerance and social polarisation, and stimulated public dialogue on the project’s key themes.

2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000466130.title: GAMES4IMPACT
2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000466130.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to improve the quality and impact of sustainability-focused game-based learning in youth work by developing a structured facilitation framework aligned with GreenComp. It strengthens facilitation standards, improves learning transfer from gameplay to sustainability competences and civic agency, and reinforces organisational capacity through shared documentation and knowledge transfer, moving from intuition-based practice to an evidence-informed practice.

<< Implementation >>

The project includes an introductory partner meeting, research and preparation phase, a method clinic for framework development, and Youth Labs in two countries. Partners co-create and test a facilitation methodology, consolidate it during a design sprint, and finalise an open-access Guide. Results are shared through a local training and targeted dissemination activities.

<< Results >>

The project will produce a structured facilitation framework aligned with GreenComp and an open-access Facilitation Guide with practical tools. It will generate documented Youth Lab evidence, shared quality standards and improved knowledge-transfer systems. Results include stronger facilitation consistency, increased competence impact on young people, and enhanced organisational capacity for structured, evidence-informed youth work.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000466909.title: Young Cultural Voices: Inclusive Cross-Border Education for Emerging Cultural Workers
2026-1-HR01-KA210-YOU-000466909.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to strengthen young people’s professional competencies, employability and capacity to actively shape cultural discourse in Slovenia and Croatia. It seeks to establish sustainable cross-border cooperation between curatorial and cultural journalism education, while structurally embedding inclusion, accessibility and participatory practices into non-formal cultural learning.

<< Implementation >>

The project will implement two structured education strands (curatorial and journalism), cross-border lecture exchanges, four mobility visits, joint public events, accessibility trainings and institutional capacity-building sessions. Participants will engage in mentoring, collaborative production, exhibition-making, editorial publishing and public presentations in both countries.

<< Results >>

At least 30 young people will complete structured non-formal education and produce tangible professional outputs (texts, concepts for cultural programs, exhibition contributions). Cross-border networks will be strengthened, a professional exhibition realised and at least 10 articles published, 2 journalistic and 1 curatorial educational cycles delivered, and inclusion standards embedded institutionally. Participants will gain skills, confidence and employability readiness.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2026-1-LT02-KA210-YOU-000468570.title: Creative Paths in Youthwork
2026-1-LT02-KA210-YOU-000468570.summary:
<< Objectives >>

We aim to strengthen the capacity of NGOs in outdoor education, equip youth workers with innovative tools for community building, and create a safe and inclusive environment where young people can learn, grow, and actively participate. Through the exchange of best practices and the development of a practical workbook, the project contributes to improving the long-term quality of youth work and promoting cross-border cooperation.

<< Implementation >>

We will organize a kick-off meeting, conduct local studies, hold a workbook development seminar, carry out testing through local activities, host an Inspiration Day, and conclude with a final festival. The activities will include workshops, surveys, interviews, and group exercises. Each phase is designed to contribute to the creation and refinement of a practical workbook, video materials, and new outdoor methods that youth workers can apply in their communities.

<< Results >>

Key results will include a multilingual outdoor education workbook with accent to Art Therapy, accompanying video materials, and new methods tested in practice. At least 100 youth workers and volunteers will directly benefit, while more than 500 young people across the partner countries will experience enhanced activities. The project will create a lasting impact by strengthening the capacities of NGOs, promoting inclusion, and establishing outdoor education as an effective tool in youth work.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Quality and innovation of youth work

2026-1-LV02-KA210-YOU-000459339.title: CORE 2.0
2026-1-LV02-KA210-YOU-000459339.summary:
<< Objectives >>

This project addresses the growing mental health challenges and digital passivity among youth in Latvia, Italy, and Croatia. We aim to empower 60 marginalized young people by merging audiovisual storytelling with emotional resilience training. Our goal is to transform smartphones from sources of anxiety into tools for self-expression and stress regulation. By developing a methodology we build the capacity of 12 youth workers to facilitate safe, creative spaces for vulnerable groups across the EU

<< Implementation >>

We will implement five core activities: Project Management to establish a coordination framework, and Methodology Development to co-create an interdisciplinary AV-resilience toolkit. A Transnational Meeting in Latvia will provide "train-the-trainer" sessions for 12 staff members. We will then conduct Local Pilot Workshops for 60 marginalized youth to test the tools. Finally, Dissemination activities, including showcase events and a webinar, will share results EU-wide.

<< Results >>

The project will deliver a validated Methodology Package, including a trauma-informed Facilitator Handbook and a mobile-friendly Digital Toolkit. We expect 60 marginalized youth to gain increased digital agency and emotional resilience, evidenced by 60 individual audiovisual stories. Additionally, 12 youth workers will acquire hybrid competencies in AV production and mental health support. All resources will be available on the Salto-Youth Toolbox to ensure EU-wide transferability.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

hr.name: Aiki En Udruga za promicanje skladnog zivljenja

2026-1-PL01-KA210-YOU-000449664.title: Youth Workers for Sustainable AI Use
2026-1-PL01-KA210-YOU-000449664.summary:
<< Objectives >>

Develop a youth work calculator and 3-module eLearning on AI’s environmental impact, train 12 youth workers to apply them in non-formal education, and run youth-led awareness actions reaching 1,000+ young people. Strengthen partner cooperation and provide open, multilingual resources for wider reuse.

Kick-off co-design workshop; develop and test the AI Environmental Impact Calculator; create a 3-module Green AI eLearning course with certificate; deliver an international capacity-building workshop for 12 youth workers; run a youth-led awareness campaign (60 posts + 3 local workshops); organise a final 2-hour online dissemination conference for 30 external participants.

<< Results >>

Multilingual AI Environmental Impact Calculator and 3-module Green AI eLearning course (open, reusable). 12 youth workers trained. 1,000+ young people reached. Uptake: 100+ calculator uses and 100+ course completions within 6 months. Partner organisations strengthened through shared methodology, cooperation and reuse by 30+ organisations.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work

2026-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000468615.title: ALT HUB START
2026-1-SI02-KA210-YOU-000468615.summary:
<< Objectives >>

The project aims to increase the active participation of young people in alternative cultural centres and transform them from passive visitors into active co-creators of programmes. Its objective is to develop their project management and digital competences, strengthen the capacities of youth workers, and establish a sustainable “Youth Co-Managed Hub” model that will revitalise the centres in the long term through new content produced by young people.

<< Implementation >>

The project will include overall project management and coordination, the development of the “Youth Co-Managed Hub” model, the creation of international youth production teams, and the implementation of 9 events in three countries. It will also organise 3 training sessions for youth workers and 3 transnational partner meetings. Activities will include evaluation and dissemination of results at local and European levels.

<< Results >>

he project will involve at least 45 young people in the co-management of cultural centres and the implementation of 9 events in three countries. It will include 3 transnational partner meetings and 3 training sessions for youth workers. Young participants will develop project management and digital competences. The “Youth Co-Managed Hub” model will be developed, and a sustainable regional network will be established for future European projects.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

101103641.title: ContinueUP - Co-constructing the continuum between initial teacher education and continuous professional development
101103641.summary: The ContinueUP project addresses the question how more, and more effective teacher education and training can be offered to teachers across the continuum of initial and continuous teacher education and training. It achieves this by piloting processes and outputs at initial teacher education (ITE) and continuous professional development (CPD) level which on the one hand develop teachers’ capacity to benefit from online training opportunities, and on the other hand reduce barriers to take-up such opportunities. The project establishes a network of ITE and CPD providers that will co-construct and deliver an education and training programme across the continuum of ITE and CPD. The programme consists of an ITE module and a CPD MOOC which are both addressing teachers’ use of digital tools for professional engagement. The delivery of the module will be implemented jointly, allowing student teachers from different countries to study together. Student teachers are then encouraged to continue their learning by following the MOOC. By participating in the ITE module, student teachers will be better prepared to participate in and continue their learning through online and blended learning formats once they enter the profession. In-service teachers will benefit by developing their capacity to engage in more advanced online mobility activities and CPD opportunities. The co-construction process used for the development and delivery of the education and training programme also introduces mobility experiences to teacher educators and trainers, for them to be able to better promote such experiences amongst teachers. The co-construction process also aims to increase the effectiveness and cost-efficiency of developing new teacher education and training programmes. Furthermore, the project will pilot processes that can lead to the formal recognition of teacher CPD MOOCs, gaining valuable insights how to address barriers for the take-up of non-formal online learning formats by teachers.

101104564.title: ACIIS - ACADEMY FOR CREATIVE, INNOVATIVE AND INCLUSIVE SCHOOLS
101104564.summary:
The project ACIIS - Academy for creative, innovative and inclusive schools intends to set up a network of teacher trainers at pre-service and in-service level together with schools to promote innovative teaching methods which use drama techniques and drama digital tools as a means to include children with differences within the school and support their education and development.

Providers of initial teacher education and providers of continuing professional development will train student teachers and in-service teachers. They will engage school teams in designing and trying out teaching strategies and innovative digital drama tools, while schools will give feedback and help to develop effective forms of    virtual, in life and blended trainings for teaching languages, humanities and science in inclusive education.

ACIIS project will:

87 teachers from school lab teams at Pilot training courses, and 81 teachers – newcomers at International training courses who will then incorporate new teaching strategies and ICT drama tools into their teaching practice.

Train 75 teacher trainers who will then incorporate the innovative pedagogies into their training courses and lead same training with up to 1.125 teachers during the lifetime of the project.

ACIIS will carry out three innovation camps where teachers, students, professors, school leaders and representatives from public authorities will work together on defined challenges of inclusive education. Generated concepts will be used for developing drama ICT tools and other teaching resources.

Furthermore, ACIIS will organize 11 Fairs of creative teaching ides in order to share good practice and enthuse more teachers about using ACIIS strategies and tools for 495 educational stakeholders.

Finally, ACIIS plans to prepare policy brief including recommendations for educational policy change, which will be shared at 4 Round table discussions and final event across Poland, Austria, Slovenia, Italy and Croatia.

hr.name: Škola za odgoj i obrazovanje - Pula

101104631.title: acaSTEMy - Trans-national STEM teacher education focussing on transversal competence and sustainability education
101104631.summary: Teachers play a key role in preparing future generations of transversally skilled people and are thus pivotal in the context of green and digital transitions. Despite this, teachers report a lack of professional development opportunities, esp. related to digital skills, mobility, and peer mentoring. The goal of acaSTEMy is to develop a systemic support structure for high-quality, research-based STEM teacher education from pre-service education to continuing professional development (CPD) that includes mobility as an essential building block. The project envisions transversally competent and motivated STEM teachers who are well equipped to prepare their students for future careers, the nature of which is difficult to foresee. Building on numerous previous activities of acaSTEMy partners, the focus of the project is to: (1) develop, pilot and promote various distance and blended learning models in combination with international mobility and mentorship;  (2) improve STEM teachers’ digital competences for meaningful pedagogies;  (3) support the competences and pedagogies of STEM teachers for sustainable and up-to-date education by developing CPD courses to address major challenges, such as environmental sustainability,  green deal, global health and immigration as well as methodological aspects, such as teaching diverse classes, combating science anxiety, and fostering gender-sensitive teaching. AcaSTEMy’s bottom-up alliance brings together providers of pre- and in-service teacher education, as well as practice schools from eight (8) countries to develop and test mobility models and programmes for effective and accessible professional learning. In addition, the partnership network includes STEM teacher associations, ministries of education and  Academies of Sciences to provide input for developing a policy framework for purposeful and systematic teacher mobility and to inform broader science education policies at national and European levels.

101249336.title: Living Smart Schools - Well-being and resilience of principals and teachers for an inclusive multicultural Education in Europe
101249336.summary:
The project aims to design and support the school of the future by enhancing educational settings, empowering teachers and principals, and promoting quality, equity, and sustainable practices in education, and it has 5 specific objectives:
(SO1) To contribute to policy and social recognition of the profile of school principals, emphasizing their pivotal role in driving innovation and enhancing quality in education.
(SO2) To endow school principals with competences and create opportunities to envision schools as thriving learning communities and create regenerative learning spaces.
(SO3) To endow pre-service and in-service teachers with competences and resources to address teaching and learning challenges, effectively manage multicultural classrooms, foster school well-being, and enhance students' literacy skills.
(SO4)  To advance teaching and learning by adopting innovative methodologies, promoting literacy, leveraging AI, digital tools, and sustainable practices while enhancing well-being and resilience in schools.
(SO5) To strengthen collaboration by fostering lifelong peer learning and networking among principals, in-service teachers, and higher-education students across Europe.
With a duration of 36, the consortium plans to promote 49 national and international events, engaging 500 participants, including principals, in-service and pre-service teachers, students and policymakers, inside and outside the consortium. 
Three main results will be developed, implemented and provided as part of the Living Smart Schools academy:
1. Learning and Creative Leadership Programme, addressed to principals 
2. In-service Teachers’ Training Programme, addressed to in-service teachers 
3. Teachers’ Pre-Induction Programme,  addressed to pre-service teachers (higher-education students)
In the 3rd year of the project, the consortium will prepare a Living Smart Schools sustainability and long-term action plan (D6.2), fostering the sustainability and exploitation of the project.

101249392.title: ImSTEAM - Immersive STEAM Education Academy
101249392.summary:
ImSTEAM (Immersive STEAM Academy) is an innovative Erasmus+ Teacher Academies project designed to transform STEAM education in European secondary schools through immersive technologies (VR/AR/MR). The project addresses a critical "contextualisation gap" identified in PISA assessments, where students struggle to apply abstract STEAM knowledge to real-world problems.
Working across five countries (Greece, Italy, Belgium, Croatia, and Slovenia) with varying PISA performance levels, ImSTEAM brings together 17 partners including universities, schools, educational technology experts, and policy facilitators. The consortium will develop a comprehensive framework that aligns STEAM competencies with the PISA 2025 assessment framework and delivers them through immersive, scenario-based learning experiences.
Key outputs include: the ImSTEAM Pedagogical Framework mapping contextualised competencies; a modular teacher training program with 19 micro-courses; an Immersive Education Platform with AR/VR learning scenarios; a Cross-border Teacher Mobility and Mentoring Program; and an Open Badge Factory for recognizing acquired competencies.
The project employs a three-phase methodology of Alignment (mapping STEAM skills to PISA competencies), Classification (embedding them in real-world contexts), and Operationalisation (creating immersive learning scenarios). A structured Ambassador Program and peer-to-peer knowledge sharing mechanisms will multiply impact, while sustainability is ensured through a self-sustaining Teachers' Academy and Content Sharing Platform..

566093-EPP-1-2015-1-HR-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.action_type: Capacity Building for youth in ACP countries, Latin America and Asia
566093-EPP-1-2015-1-HR-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.title: Seeding Social Innovation in Local Communities
566093-EPP-1-2015-1-HR-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.summary: This project aimed to promote active youth participation in their communities and to build youth workers’ and youth leaders’ capacity to maximize youths potential for social innovation and entrepreneuership in tackling the problems of youth unemployment and for promoting social inclusion, social innovation, gender empowerment and sustainable human development in participating communities. Social entrepreneurship and youth active participation in inovative actions, especially in difficult economic times, have become a form of self-employment for many, allowing people to be self-contained and, at the same time, to make a difference in society.The project consisted of a several international and paralel local acitivities of eight partner organization within a period of 16 months. Central activities were two transnational capacity builiding seminars for youth workers in Vietnam and Croatia; 8 mulitiplication seminars in participating countries, 8 job shadowing activities; production of one Toolkit and of one Manual  for Youth Workers and relevant institutions; two practical projects - one YWs amateur documentary DVD and one International Festival: Idea Manifestation - Bringing International Minds Together in Zadar, Croatia.  Beside direct participants, with this activities we wanted to reach wider audience and to inform  you(th) about the concept, methods, and values of youth participation, social entrepreneurship in the youth sector, as well as provide you(th) with real life examples of young social entrepreneurs in action.Specific goals:- Raising awareness on the role that the young people can play as active Global Citizens - Analyzing how young people in different countries understand and view  unemployement issues - Identifying the barriers to active youth participation young people from disadvantaged areas face in their daily lives- To teach youth social entrepreneurship, provide them with a good understanding of the world, encourage critical thinking and self-confidence, while instilling the abilities required to become social sensible leaders and active citizens.- To explore the principles of youth entrepreneurship and the ways which they could be applied- To build up entrepreneurial competences of participants in view of improvement of  their capacity for creation of sustainable social initiatives as key elements of the work in the youth field- Promoting the recognition of Youth Work and non-formal learning-To build capacity of youth led organization for sustainability and social innovationProject is imagined as social process in which participants voluntarily trough interactive non-formal methods develop personal, social, and professional profile as well as competences for further learning.

573278-EPP-1-2016-1-NL-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.title: Fostering an inclusive and diverse youth environmental movement across Africa and Europe
573278-EPP-1-2016-1-NL-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.summary: This project builds connections among youth workers from 15 European and African environmental and social justice organisations that are part of the Friends of the Earth International (FoEI) federation, for mutual learning, skill sharing, joint campaign planning and cultural exchange, with the aim of building a more diverse and inclusive international environmental youth movement.FoEI and the project partners have a long history of campaigning on today’s most urgent environmental and social issues. Yet, in both Africa and Europe, they face a common challenge in enhancing the engagement of youth of different age, gender, race, and socio-economic background in their work. This project will build on the existing expertise and competences related to youth work leading to creative tools, methods and strategies for strengthening the diversity and inclusivity of youth in the environmental and social justice movement from the national to the global level. The project will build the capacity of youth workers in Cameroon, Togo, South Africa, Nigeria, Uganda, Mozambique, Liberia, Belgium, Ireland, Germany, Norway, Netherlands, Austria, and Croatia, by:- Building the practical skills and leadership of youth workers within environmental and social justice organisations to work more effectively with young environmental advocates;- Fostering cross-regional collaboration and networking between youth workers from environmental and social justice organisations in Europe and Africa; - Developing a methodological framework for youth workers of environmental and social justice organisations to enhance inclusiveness and diversity of youth, with a particular emphasis on gender, class, race, indigenous peoples and human migration.Project activities include a regional project launch meeting, four cross-regional learning workshops, and a mobility exchange program in which a youth worker from one African organisation will be hosted by youth workers from a European organisation and vice-versa for a 10-day joint learning and exchange. Each European partner is paired with an African counterpart working on a similar environmental justice topic, such as coal; monoculture plantations; land grabbing; fracking, forest and climate as to allow youth workers to develop concrete cross-regional campaigns to test the tools and methods for engaging young women and men from different backgrounds more effectively. Throughout the project, participants will document 'best practices' for ensuring inclusivity and diversity of underrepresented youth populations and that are rooted in the realities of today’s young people from Europe and Africa. These ‘best practices’ will be shared with FoEI’s 75 national member groups across all continents and incorporated in the planning templates of environmental and social justice organisations at national, regional and international level. This in turn will contribute to building a more inclusive and diverse global environmental youth movement.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

573290-EPP-1-2016-1-BE-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.action_type: Capacity Building for youth in ACP countries, Latin America and Asia
573290-EPP-1-2016-1-BE-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.title: Peers To Peace: Peer learning and Peer support for Capacity Building in international volunteer work
573290-EPP-1-2016-1-BE-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.summary: “Peers to Peace: Peer learning and Peer support for Capacity Building in international volunteer work” was a worldwide project that involved 25 different partners in 24 countries from Asia, Africa, Australia, and Europe. The key focus of the project was the peer approach. Through peer-learning and peer-supporting in the following areas of expertise: knowledge management, volunteer management, project management and fundraising the capacity of project partners was improved. This applied on small scale in the single events and on a large scale with upgrading the online tool for peer-support. This tool facilitates an easier access to resources and (exchange of) information and further stimulates possibilities for innovation and capacity building of project partners and International Voluntary Service movement as a whole.    The project spanned over 21 months and included 3 main mobility events: a Peer university on volunteer and knowledge management in May 2017 in Poland, a Learning seminar on knowledge management and fundraising in July 2017 in Malaysia, and Training on project management in March 2018 in Greece. Besides these mobility activities, 3 capacity building events were organized as part of the project: 1) a steering team meeting in January 2017 in Germany, 2) a crucial Technical Meeting in November 2017 in the UK, as well as 3) an Evaluation meeting combined with a final event in June 2018 in Belgium. Moreover, exchange of EVS volunteers took place between Europe and Asia (3 volunteers from Asia hosted in Belgium and Greece; and 1 European volunteer hosted in Malaysia), promoting transnational non-formal learning mobility and supporting an exchange of experiences between Program and Partner Countries. The main target group of the project were youth leaders, youth workers, volunteers and activists, for a total of more than 100 people directly involved, who acted as multipliers within their sending organizations and contributed to the setting up and implementation of the peer learning system thanks to their experience. Participants came from a great variety of countries and this increased the intercultural dimension of the project and its impact, guaranteeing a real exchange and strengthening the networking capacities of the organizations. Projects results were shared among partners and within the networks they belong to. These included: 1) SCI-Moving Forward - a handbook for volunteers and staff members in SCI and partner organizations focusing on increasing the understanding of how SCI works internationally intended to support greater participation and knowledge transfer among International Volunteering Service organizations, including important chapters on finances, knowledge management and volunteering within SCI; and  2) innovative online peer- learning platform that has been newly integrated in SCI’s Members Area allowing for direct exchange of knowledge and experience among SCI members.  The participation of other major IVSO networks, such as Coordinating Committee for International Voluntary Service (CCIVS), Network for Voluntary Development in Asia (NVDA), and Voluntary Workcamps Association in Nigeria (VWAN, central NGO in Africa) enriched the project with diverse inputs on volunteering and youth work in their context.

581603-EPP-1-2016-2-BE-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.action_type: Capacity Building for youth in ACP countries, Latin America and Asia
581603-EPP-1-2016-2-BE-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.title: Training of trainer in Citizenship Education: Global Responses in Preventing Radicalization
581603-EPP-1-2016-2-BE-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.summary: The project ‘Training of trainer in Citizenship Education: Global Responses in Preventing Radicalization’ , aims to develop capacities of educational and youth work practitioners (teachers and youth workers) to work on combating violent radicalization, by designing and delivering educational programmes that promote Global Citizenship EducationIt is set up as cooperation among 8 partner organisations: Out of the Box International-Belgium, Center for Intercultural Dialogue-Macedonia, Realization-Croatia, Kenya Scouts Association-Kenya, Centre for Community Regeneration and Development-Cameroon, SJ Vietnam, Secondary School Nace Budjoni Macedonia, and NARXOZ UNIVERSITY, Kazakhstan. The project provide participants with the theory and tools necessary to design, implement and evaluate effective training programmes for global citizenship education and bridges educators from schools and youth organization in the promotion of anti-radicalisation and citizenship education.The project will create a community of practice, of educational practitioners in formal and non formal education with specific skilss to act upon antiradicalisation using approaches of global citizenship education when working with young people, in their respective fields inclusing formal education and youth sector. It will also develop a set of 4 E-course Modules, who will be used to engage young people from all over the world in the combating of violent radicalisation and promotion of human rights and dignity.Project Activities include 2 Training of Trainers, Blended Learning with Online Courses, Study visit in Brussels, and National activities. The project main outputs are Toolkit on Education for Global Citizenship in Combating radicalization and Online Learning Platform. It will involve around 400 direct beneficiaries who will act as multipliers on the topic od EGC in their communities and on global level.

581644-EPP-1-2016-2-LV-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.action_type: Capacity Building for youth in ACP countries, Latin America and Asia
581644-EPP-1-2016-2-LV-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.title: Digital gamificiation for youth engagement
581644-EPP-1-2016-2-LV-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.summary: Fostering participation of youth and active engagement by interactive and attractive tools in one of key priorities nowadays in the youth sector. Usage of digital gamification elements as new form of youth engagement, development of attractive and innovative methods of youth work and support open educational resources is high on European wide youth work agenda. Gamification is the application of game elements and digital game design techniques to non-game areas, such as business and social impact challenges. That is a psychology - and motivation-based approach to increase the motivation, engagement and contribution of the target audience, as well as stimulate achievement of the necessary results through their active involvement.During the project stages, research of the elements and tools of gamification was made. The handbook, gamification training (including curriculum) to educate the youth organizations about digital gamification, creation of the game by use of templates and applications, involvement and education on various topics was developed, organized and published. The topics included democracy, unemployment, civic engagement, human rights, youth entrepreneurship, environmental education, social responsibility and active participation in community activities for youth leaders and youth workers.The project aimed to:1) Facilitate youth engagement in European, Asia and Latin America countries through developed on the spot and online video training and handbook;2) Promote the cooperation between youth organizations and organizations in the education and training fields and stakeholders; 3) Promote new forms of youth work, use of open and flexible learning, open educational resources (OER) and better exploitation of the ICT potential; 4) Encourage and educate youth organizations to use and create new tools for youth participation, using new technologies; 5) Disseminate results. The project had also youth workers’ mobility’s during which they were trained on the topic of gamification and increased their personal and professional qualification, got new insights on their local issues and shared skills and knowledge. Due to the change of partner ICT solution was not accomplished, but more efforts were redirected towards Handbook and other project’s activities.The project had initially following results planned and achieved:1) Handbook "How to succeed with digital gamification for youth". A 40 pages’ educational material printed in 8 languages and extended e-version of 100 pages’ handbook in English. All materials are available in partners ‘languages and published for free in partners’ web pages and it the main applicant’s  library at: http://socialinnovation.lv/en/ygame-project-all-results/;2) Curriculum, workshop and online training as open educational resource “Gamification as a tool for youth engagement", available at platform https://ej.uz/ygame;3) Transnational conference “Play for changes”, which took place in Riga, in January 2019 and gathered around 50 youth workers and young people from all around the world, from all partnering countries;4) Experience exchange visits, where European partners shared the experience with Latin America and Asia organizations while networking with local representatives and their experience as well as shared project’s results and gamification concept.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

581720-EPP-1-2016-2-PL-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.action_type: Capacity Building for youth in ACP countries, Latin America and Asia
581720-EPP-1-2016-2-PL-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.title: GO_PRO! - Regional Programming Centers
581720-EPP-1-2016-2-PL-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.summary: Idea of GO_PRO! Network was positively recognized by United Nation. In the annual World Summit of the Information Society (Zurich 2015) it was nominated to prestige prize, as one of 30 best ICT capacity building initiates. It was also described in WSIS Stocktaking Report 2015 as one of good practises. In Poland the project was nominated to a prize: New Technologies Locally 2015, which is annually granted by Polish – American Cooperation Foundation. It was described as one often best initiatives of 2014. Network was supported also by Reading and Writing Foundation – Public Libraries 2020 initiative, as one of 6 best initiatives involving libraries. Our current project Regional Programming Centers was nomited to WSIS prize (WORLD SUMMIT ON THE INFORMATION SOCIETY PRIZES 2020) in the capacity building category as one of 20 best ITC initiatives.Within Erasmus+, together with our partners, we wanted to promote this idea furthermore, allowing other Youth to develop their programming skills and fully participate in digital world. Partners all together agreed, that learning to code is important because of:1. The needs of the labour market – programming specialists are one of the most needed professional groups, basic programming skills will be useful for the majority of positions based on the computer work 2. Media education - computer illiterate group are vulnerable to exclusion;3. Innovative economy - creating software and new tools and services are the pillars of the innovation economy.Within the project GO_PRO! we built the capacity of partner organizations and they are able now develop ICT skills and support digital and social inclusion of Youth in local communities. We also wanted to create a special space (non formal education centers) for developing ICT and programmingskills. The basic idea for it - is to use the existing infrastructure, only reconfigure it. To create previous GO_PRO! Centers we cooperated with partner organizations – schools, libraries, NGOs. Well-equipped educational centers can create great conditions for modern programmingeducation, which especially important in developing countries and/or rural areas.Partners got the knowledge, skills and tools to organize interesting IT lessons, what also allowed(during so called Coder Clubs) youth to develop programming skills during their free time, using the equipment under the guidance of a volunteer. Coder Clubs are based on challenges. Each week there was a new problem, new challenge, which Club had to solve together! Youth needed to learn new things about algorithm, build a robot using Lego Mindstorms, and then program it properly. Sometimes the challenges had forced Youth division into smaller groups. They competed with each other to create best solution, this way they were stimulated to gave all their energy and enthusiasm to solve particular problem the best possible way.The project included 2 mobilities for Youth Workers, each of them helped undeniably them to be better teachers/ educators/ animators of ICT competences in their own communities. Each Partner organization received grant for proper equipment, in order to lead innovative and interesting ICTworkshops in their areas. During the Code Week (X of 2017 and 2018) we to organized collaborative awareness rising actions in order to promote network and for self-development purposes. We had in mind, that encouraged/empowered youngsters or children develop so quickly, that volunteers need to be trained constantly to provide quality ICT workshops.The project is extremely innovative but based on an easily replicable model - that we tried to share in detail with partner organizations. Another innovative element is that project activities were specifically designed to develop a new set of entrepreneurial and digital competences which are in today’s digital society crucial for both: employability and active participation of young people in the society.

581754-EPP-1-2016-2-DE-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.action_type: Capacity Building for youth in ACP countries, Latin America and Asia
581754-EPP-1-2016-2-DE-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.title: MILONGA - International Volunteering towards fraternity
581754-EPP-1-2016-2-DE-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.summary: According to the Global Unemployment Trends for Youth 2015 report of ILO, youth unemployment rates remain stable at 13%, but are still well above the pre-crisis level of 11.7%. Consequently, affected young people worldwide start out with weaker early-career credentials and show lower confidence and resilience in dealing with labour market opportunities and setbacks over the course of their working lives. Effects that are further enhanced by the growing mobility between systems and sectors (education, training, family, labour market, permanent employment, unemployment, etc.). In this “liquid” context, it is crucial to reinforce those capacity building opportunities which allow young people to get actively involved, gain skills and demonstrate their potential.As the Erasmus report study in 2014 highlights, 92% of employers are looking for transversal skills, such as openness to new challenges, problem-solving and decision-making skills, confidence, tolerance towards others’ values and behaviours, while 64% consider an int’l experience as important for recruitment. In this context, int’l volunteering can be a valuable tool as it facilitates the:- initial exposure to the world of organized work: it represents an important trial period and gives chance to experiment and put preferences in practice - “employability” through the improvement in soft skills, such as knowledge of other countries, ability to interact and work with individuals from different cultures, adaptability, foreign language proficiency and communication skills.- Documented work experience.- re-entry into regular work after breaks.This impact depends on the quality of host organizations’ staff which often differs across countries showing an unbalanced distribution of opportunities. It is, thus, fundamental to set easily accessible and comprehensive tools, methodologies and guidelines for the efficient management of such opportunities through training, coaching and mentoring. Moreover, youth unemployment challenge requires a multi-stakeholder approach: in this sense, Latin American partners’ experience highlights a virtuous practice of networking among NGOs, enterprises, universities and local institutions and offers a wider range of youth capacity building activities, adding to the int’l volunteering the possibility to participate in internships and other training opportunities. The project will indeed enhance the quality of partner NGOs’ staff to provide int’l volunteering opportunities; identify and develop areas of synergy among stakeholders in the youth and volunteering fields in order to ensure collaboration and exchange of good practices, scale-up and improve existing youth-related programmes according to labour market needs and using ICT technologies. It aims at both increasing the quantity of youth volunteering opportunities available globally and improving the quality of the volunteer experience, which is crucial for the long-term sustainability of the project
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

589774-EPP-1-2017-1-HR-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.action_type: Capacity Building for youth in ACP countries, Latin America and Asia
589774-EPP-1-2017-1-HR-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.title: A Path to TranSportAction
589774-EPP-1-2017-1-HR-EPPKA2-CBY-ACPALA.summary: “A Path to TranSportAction” (APTSA) is a project involving a total of 5 organizations from Europe (Croatia, Italy, Bulgaria) and Latin America (Brazil and Peru), whose main aim is to enhance the capacity of youth organizations and stakeholders in all partner countries and beyond to use Sport in combination with high-end Non Formal Education methodologies for fostering a gender-inclusive approach to Sport practices, contrasting sexism and gender stereotypes and promoting equality and mutual respect among genders in disadvantaged rural areas in Europe and in Latin America.Gender discrimination and inequality is a well known structural phenomenal of endemic proportion in both the European and the Latin American region. Across the different national and cultural realities composing the Consortium,  the development of a concrete gender equality is impeded by persisting barriers and discrimination against young women.  The aforementioned barriers are both of material nature (i.e.  disadvantages in access to the labour market, lower wages as compared with male peers, lower presence of women among the higher tiers of the business and public sectors) as well as related to the social and existential spheres wherein the diffusion of a still considerable machist mentality  determines more or less socially sanctioned forms of stereotyping and prejudice confining young women to established roles and conduits. The most extreme manifestations of such mentality lay at the root of widespread phenomena of verbal/psychological  violence and, ultimately, physical aggression against women.The low levels of female participation in the Sport field are an important component of the wider dynamics of gender-based disadvantage. Indeed, the general prejudice considering Sport as an almost exclusive field of male engagement, coupled  by the machist self-representations which permeate most Sport sub-culture, represent at the same time a telling effect and a critical self-perpetuating mechanism of gender stereotyping and discrimination. At the same time, Sport represents a powerful educational vehicle through which disadvantaged targets can acquire crucial soft skills, transversal skills and positive attitudes of self-confidence and active participation representing the key component of any grassroots process of empowerment. Through its inner dynamics of peer-interaction and fair competition among people with diverse backgrounds (cultural, ethnic, gender etc.), Sport provides also an invaluable experiential path to promote mutual respect and deconstruct prejudicesThe use of Sport in combination with Non Formal Education methodologies is a long-standing driver of NGO social action to promote empowerment and dialogue processes through a grassroots approach in a variety of contexts.
