Jointly developed and implemented new curricula in Textile and Clothing production; Validation, dissemination and practical application of the main outputs with the support of EU Universities and Business associations; An appropriate and validated framework for ongoing training and competence provision to the TCLF professionals; A digital and entrepreneurial TCLF quality training certification scheme; Fostered regional cooperation in education between partner universities.

612364-EPP-1-2019-1-LT-EPPKA2-KA.title: Social Sciences and Humanities in intersectoral Outreach for better education and sustainable innovations
612364-EPP-1-2019-1-LT-EPPKA2-KA.summary:
<< Background >>

SHOUT has chosen to design educational programmes (for students, teachers and professionals) and an innovative SSH traineeships scheme according to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) in order to tackle the biggest challenges of today’s and tomorrow's society and make traineeships and educational activities grounded reaching tangible results. The merger of SSH disciplines and SDGs is a sweet spot where competencies and job postings will meet with the impact to immediate career to students.

<< Objectives >>

To strengthen intersection between education, research and innovation (through an improved knowledge triangle scheme); To create a well-functioning ecosystem where the role of HEIs will be strengthened when dealing with SDGs challenges in the wider socio-economic environment;To create a mechanism allowing students to acquire skills, competencies and experiences through mission-based research activities focused on real-world problems.

<< Implementation >>

The constant collaboration gave an opportunity to come up with solutions from different angles that are suitable for various sectors. The research conducted by the SHOUT consortium has highlighted the crucial role of SSH in the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The implementation of educational programmes and SHOUT traineeships focused on strengthing the knowledge, skills and competences of SSH students, teachers, professionals.

<< Results >>

SHOUT has generated research-based, piloted results for stronger connection between universities and businesses while addressing today's challenges by imploying a mission-based approach and targeting disciplines of Social sciences and Humanities that usually participate less in addressing challenges hindering to reach Sustainable Development Goals. Different outputs (analysis, educational programmes, promotional campaigns, etc.) were produced in order to tackle this issue from various angles.

612425-EPP-1-2019-1-FR-EPPKA2-KA.title: Acoustics Knowledge Alliance
612425-EPP-1-2019-1-FR-EPPKA2-KA.summary:
<< Background >>

In the past decades, we have witnessed unprecedented economic growth and technological development. Apart from numerous positive aspects, it has also brought unfortunate consequences and challenges that need to be overcame and dealt with. As one of these consequences, the noise has become a societal issue and a recognized health hazard. The challenges reflect in an ever-growing number of products and solutions with acoustics-based features that require appropriate knowledge in acoustics

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed at developing 5 innovative, interactive, and free online courses on acoustics: Acoustics Fundamentals, Psychoacoustics, Acoustics Simulation and Auralization, Electroacoustics and Room and Building Acoustics. The vision of this English-language acoustic courseware was to design and combine lessons and practical cases within an innovative online experience, stimulating the development of knowledge and allowing solving of issues connected with acoustics in a broader perspective.

<< Implementation >>

The course material has been implemented and released on the Acoucou website. Clicking on “ASKnow” allows to access to the five new courses developed in the frame of this project . The major deliverable of this project for our target groups consists in the release of the courses on this open-access web platform. A large number of dissemination actionsnhave already been carried out to promote the new courses, and these will be supplemented by other actions even after the end of the project.

<< Results >>

The Courses have been integrated on the user-friendly and open access ACOUCOU platform. Each course consists of 30 lessons and 2 practical cases. The lessons are divided into 3 parts

612466-EPP-1-2019-1-NO-EPPKA2-KA.title: Best practices of pedagogical chatbots in higher education
612466-EPP-1-2019-1-NO-EPPKA2-KA.summary:
<< Background >>

The issue of increasing educational attainment is gaining importance in the national and international debates on higher education. The student-educator ratio in Higher-Education is high, causing:- Educators can’t promote digital communication like asynchronous communication with students or tasks like formative assessment in their teaching, and - students don’t get personalised feedback to increase their learning nor have an effective way to get connected to others with similar study goals.

<< Objectives >>

PROJECT'S MAIN OBJECTIVES:-Increased student engagement: We focus on engagement between students and educators facilitated by chatbots-Improved feedback loops: We focus on increasing the frequency and accuracy of feedback between educators and students-Improved student success: Project pilots are designed with the overall goal of decreasing dropout rates by using chatbots-Knowledge sharing: Join a learning community of educators, to learn about chatbots and share your practical experiences.

<< Implementation >>

EDUBOTS has the goal of improving educational attainment in EU higher education. We do that by exploring best practice use of chatbots and creating a learning community of Educators in EU. EDUBOTS has contributed to massive collaboration among educators across courses, institutions and countries; with open, digital knowledge sharing communities, aiming to stimulate entrepreneurial skills of their users. We have also encouraged student-to-student collaboration by integrating the chatbots.

<< Results >>

-cMOOC ‘Introduction to Chatbots, for Educators’: This online course and community of practice is designed for Educators in Higher Education and created to co-explore the best practice use of chatbots. It is a multicultural community with members from all over Europe.-Differ chat, which has been developed in order to connect students in universities, especially newcomers-Pilot rounds-Hubert-Edubots blog-Research outputs from project partners-Chatbot Conferences-Webinars-Research papers.

621585-EPP-1-2020-1-CY-EPPKA2-KA.title: Knowledge Alliance for Evidence-Based Urban Practices
621585-EPP-1-2020-1-CY-EPPKA2-KA.summary:
<< Background >>

KAEBUP identified a ‘rupture’ at the point where academic research and teaching should ‘flow’ into the professional world in urban practices. It proposed to mend this rupture by creating a coherent, seamless flow of skills and research into the professional world, strengthening the links between academia and businesses to mutually benefit from the tools that teaching and research can provide to enterprises and from the experience of evidence-based practice.

<< Objectives >>

KAEBUP main objective was to create an international educational and training method offering participants the opportunity to engage with professional environments, learning how research can be the basis for innovative professional practices and what businesses in the field of planning, architecture and urban design require from academia, thus providing students with the skills to enter the professional world and inspiring HEI staff to innovate through research.

<< Implementation >>

KAEBUP achieved its objectives by implementing three ‘pathways to evidence-based urban practice’: 1. Innovating learning and teaching through knowledge exchange and skills development working on real-life urban projects. 2. Understanding and developing business models for evidence-based urban practices. 3. Co-creating urban knowledge through multiple modes of exchange and involvement of students, teaching and company staff in teaching, research and practice.

<< Results >>

Online open access module on Social Entrepreneurship and Evidence-Based Design for Sustainable Urban Development; Open access Educational Recources; Research to Practice online platform; Teaching and training method guidelines embedding professional practice; Toolkit for developing transversal skills in urban studies; Portfolio of business models for evidence-based urban practices; Portfolio of research activities and results applied to real-life urban projects

621689-EPP-1-2020-1-ES-EPPKA2-KA.title: University Spin-offs Alliance: From the idea to the market through mentoring and transnational entrepreneurial teams /SPINTeams
621689-EPP-1-2020-1-ES-EPPKA2-KA.summary:
<< Background >>

SpinTeams project was born from the need of connecting HEIs and the business world, through the cooperation of HEIs and Chambers of Commerce and Industry, as well as with real companies. In this sense, strong bonds of cooperation have been established at each participating country between a HEI and a Chamber. This has allowed foster the alliance between higher education and business by developing entrepreneurial mindset and skills, and to introduce entrepreneurship education in any discipline.

<< Objectives >>

To act twofold:To reinforce the entrepreneurial and business capacities of Advanced studensts, Phd students and start ups and Spin-offs founders, by developing entrepreneurship training modules with HEIs and business support organizations.To reinforce the internal and external strategy and tactics of HEIs in developing entrepreneurship support schemes and in open HEIs to external entrepreneurship support ecosystems in the Regions/Countries they are located

<< Implementation >>

Different stages where the project is impacting on target groups: Training and appointment of HEIs Entrepreneurship coaches, Training of Students, Phds and researchers, start ups and Spinoffs, Mentoring schemes, International cooperation of Mentors/investors, enetrepreneurship projects, companies, HEIs and Chambers of Commerce and Industry through online platform. The project has also achieved the engagement of participants at international level.

<< Results >>

- 3 training webinars for creating the role of “Entrepreneurship Coaches" at  partners HEIs ".- 8 modules online training course for improving entrepreneurial and business skills for advanced students, Phd  and researchers (the spin-off/start- ups founders).- Handbook "Building entrepreneurial support ecosystems for HEIs" so that supportive ecosystems can be created or fostered around HEIs at local/regional level.- Guide on "Mentoring and peer learning.

hr.name: TERA TEHNOPOLIS DRUSTVO S OGRANICENOM ODGOVORNOSCU ZA PROMICANJE NOVIH TEHNOLOGIJA INOVACIJA I PODUZETNISTVA

621750-EPP-1-2020-1-DE-EPPKA2-KA.title: Women Entrepreneurs in Regional Inclusive Entrepreneurial Ecosystems
621750-EPP-1-2020-1-DE-EPPKA2-KA.summary:
<< Background >>

Women make up about 60% of higher education graduates, yet they are underrepresented in start-ups. Despite increased participation of female students in entrepreneurship education at HEIs, they still lag behind men in pursuing entrepreneurial careers. Female graduates are also less embedded in regional entrepreneurial ecosystems, with fewer participating in incubation programs, seeking funding, or joining networks. Many do not feel sufficiently invited to these opportunities.

<< Objectives >>

- Increase the share of female graduate entrepreneurs and ensure they are firmly integrated into regional entrepreneurial ecosystems across Europe. - Inclusion of entrepreneurship education and support programmes from a gender and structural perspective. - Make women feel invited to the entrepreneurship scene while going beyond the boundaries of Higher Education into their regional entrepreneurial ecosystem, and ensure that female entrepreneurs can become a key part of these.

<< Implementation >>

The WeRIn project utilized a design sciences approach which involved four stages: 1. Research and Discovery assessed gender inclusivity in entrepreneurship programs across partner countries.2. Design and Development created the WeRLearnIn Approach and a Community of Practice.3. Pilot Testing validated the approach in partner universities.4. Dissemination and Sustainability ensured the project's longevity through educational resources and local events.

<< Results >>

The WeRIn project developed the WeRLearnIn Approach, an inclusive learning method for female students and aspiring women entrepreneurs in higher education, connecting universities with the regional entrepreneurial ecosystem. Educators and programme managers were trained to implement it. Tools and other resources were compiled in the WeRIn Toolbox. The project co-designed and pilot-tested these with stakeholders, creating a supportive learning community for students and aspiring entrepreneurs.

hr.name: TEHNOLOSKI PARK VARAZDIN DOO ZA INKUBACIJU INOVATIVNIH TEHNOLOGIJSKIHPODUZECA

2020-1-BG01-KA227-YOU-094974.title: BOOST - Boosting Outstanding Omnicompetent Successful Talents
2020-1-BG01-KA227-YOU-094974.summary:
<< Background >>

Проект „BOOST: Boosting Outstanding Omnicompetent Successful Talents“ е 24-месечно стратегическо партньорство, съ-финансирано по програма Еразъм+ на Европейския съюз, имащо за цел да създаде възможности за обучение и личностно развитие за младите хора в Европа, като предостави интерактивни образователни формати и методи, базирани на развитието на трансверсални умения.

Специфичен проблем, който проект BOOST засяга, е развитието на трансверсални умения чрез специално разработени инструменти, които подчертават значението им за ефективното и целенасоченото личностно и професионално развитие на младите хора в ЕС. BOOST функционира чрез подход на международно сътрудничество, който включва организации, които си взаимодействат с целевите групи по проекта, а консорциумът включва неправителствени и младежки асоциации с богат опит и признати активни младежки политики.

<< Objectives >>

Основните нужди, които проект BOOST обезпечава са:
• Повишаване на уменията и възможностите за заетост;
• Модернизиране на образованието, обучението и младежката работа;
• Фокус върху младите хора.

<< Implementation >>

 Качествени образователни и изследователски дейности, фокусирани върху развитието на трансверсалните умения на младите хора;
 Разработване, тестване и популяризиране на онлайн обучителна платформа – BOOST МООС, целяща да развие трансверсалните умения на младите хора. Платформата за електронно обучение е онлайн ресурсен център за трансверсални умения, който включва различни ресурси, подходящи за младите хора;
 Разработване на практически наръчник BOOST за младежки работници, който да улесни развитието на трансверсалните умения на младите хора, с които работят;
 4 международни срещи по проекта – дейности по управление и разработване на съдържание и 2 събития за разпространение на резултатите във всяка държава;
 Осигуряване на устойчивост на резултатите, поради значението на темата, устойчиви резултати за младежко развитие и широко разпространение на неговата използваемост и значение в страните партньори и в целия ЕС.

<< Results >>

• Овластяване на млади хора и младежки работници чрез всички дейности и резултати по проект BOOST;
• Практическа, подходяща за младежи електронна платформа за обучение – МООС, за развитие на трансверсалните умения на младите хора;
• Наръчник BOOST за младежки работници.

2020-1-CY02-KA227-YOU-002022.title: Enhancing GLAMs through youth engagement during the COVID-19 crisis
2020-1-CY02-KA227-YOU-002022.summary:
<< Background >>

In the Covid-19 crisis, the cultural and creative sector was one of severely hit in Europe, since the physical condition of their activity so far had led most cultural institutions to focus almost exclusively on the face-to-face modality. 
Most of Galleries, Libraries, Archives and Museums (GLAMs) were unprepared regarding the effect of the pandemic including a sudden loss of incomes well as a severe of their relationship with their audiences.  According to the findings of a survey led in Spring 2020 by NEMO (the Network of European Museum Organisations), involving 1.000 museums in 48 countries, they reported a loss of income reaching up to 75-80%. 
The dramatic decrease in global tourism activities, as predicted by OECD, was expected to induce an even larger long-term decrease of income for European Museums. Although digital activities of cultural institutions pre-existed (virtual exhibitions, digital collections of open access resources), they were too few to counterbalance the overwhelming effects of the pandemic. To support and demonstrate solidarity with the cultural and creative sectors, many young people followed remotely digital activities organised by GLAMs.

<< Objectives >>

The GLAMers project had 4 objectives.
Τhe first objective was to collect the main use cases emphasizing youth engagement as a means of GLAM recovery during the COVID-19 pandemic.
The second objective was to build on the current results and create a digital repository of learning resources, enriched by a newly conceived training suite and webinars for GLAMs and youth organisations.
The third objective was to allow GLAMs put in practice knowledge so acquired by organizing real events at their premises where youth (young individuals and youth communities) had a vital role. Five events took place across Europe. Thus, GLAMs had benefited from counseling by project partners to first carry out and then assess the digitally enhanced activities involving youth at their premises. Implementation and assessment tools were part of the methodology that will be developed to support GLAMs during these stages.
The fourth objective was to map social change to check how the project had been able to tackle the identified need and propose sustainable solutions.

<< Implementation >>

The GLAMers project created a pool of advice and training opportunities for GLAMs and youth organisations, in the form of:
1.	a collection of use cases emphasizing youth engagement as a means of GLAM recovery during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
2.	an open access digital library, containing digital resources, modular online training and webinars. 
3.	through face-to-face, online or blended activities (as it was possible due to the covid19 pandemic)
4.	The GLAMers supported GLAMs in implementing and then assessing the digitally enhanced activities involving youth. 
The project emphasized the social change at pan-European level, through development in attitudes, stances and behaviours among GLAMs and also among youth, with respect to cultural and civic values. This proved the need for a transnational dimension to mobilise a critical mass able to support the rebirth of the sector at pan-European level.

<< Results >>

The first project output was a report presenting surveys and interviews with GLAM professionals, background research on the use of digital media for youth engagement, and a selection of 15 original initiatives organised by European GLAMs. The long-term goal is to enhance dialogue within the cultural sector about the challenges and opportunities of using digital media to connect with young people in a time of crisis and change.
The second output was the creration of an open access digital collection of 30 digital resources, plus a 5-module online training suite and webinars for GLAMs and youth organisations. These training sessions were of national and pan-European reach as they were carried out in English and in partner languages ( Greek, French and Croatian). 
The third output was the organisation of real events at selected GLAM's premises where youth (young individuals and youth communities) had a vital role. Thus, GLAMs benefited from counselling by project partners to first carry out and then assess the digitally enhanced activities involving youth at their premises. The fourth output was a report mapping the social change mobilised by the project, emphasizing social values with youth at their core.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-CZ01-KA227-ADU-094205.title: City Stories - Cultural Treasures for Language Learners
2020-1-CZ01-KA227-ADU-094205.summary:
<< Background >>

The basic premise for the project was based around the fact that we wish to share stories from different cultures within the EU in order to foster intercultural competencies and awareness; whilst at the same time providing interesting, stimulating and motivating content for language learners and teachers.
When cultural content appears in language teaching materials, particularly for adults, it is quite traditional in its approach, even when using  'modern' technology such as videos. All three of the educational partners have regular contact not just with their teachers but also locally, nationally and internationally through attending and hosting events; and also being part of networks, such as International House, GSS and regional associations.  There is clearly a need and desire, especially during and post-pandemic, for resources that are meaningful, motivational, modern and innovative. Digital Escape Rooms meet this as they are an exciting, interesting and engaging way to collaborate and learn.
Good stories are amazing learning tools and DERs give an exciting, engaging, language learning experience. By combining both we  created a resource that can be used at all levels of ability, both in a typical classroom context or online.

<< Objectives >>

In general terms, our project aims to introduce innovative and interactive teaching materials, produced through creative writing and based on the cultural heritage of various European regions. Therefore, enhancing both creativity and intercultural awareness is a process that is embedded in every single stage of our project. 
Our specific objectives were: 
- the development of innovative and interactive educational tools in the form of "escape room" type activities 
- the development of teaching materials and tools to implement various teaching activities 
- the development of creative writing skills 
- the development of creative and critical thinking skills, designed to augment the motivation of both teachers and students on selected training courses 
- an increasing awareness of European cultural heritage among adult learners 
- an increasing awareness of inter-cultural differences and an appreciation for these differences 
- the promotion of cooperation between education sectors and the expansion of networks of cooperation at local, regional and EU level 
- an increased awareness of the need for lifelong learning among adult students

<< Implementation >>

Output activities
-wrote 18 stories based on local legands, culture and traditions
-designed and built an online story editor to create digital escape rooms (DER), not exclusively for stories or langauge learning
-created over 36 DERs using the editor, with the stories as a base
-wrote an online handbook, a guide to using the story editor

PMI activities
-held 3 Transnational Meetings, 1 live, 1 online and 1 hybrid
-ran 3 external multiplier events, one in eah partner country 
-held several internal training events
-produced Dissemination and QM plans

Additional support activities
-branding and promotional activities including the creatrion of a logo, Facebook page, and website
-over 60 targeted dissemination activies to promote the project and its outputs; reaching all stakeholders across a variety of channels (see report for details)
-piloted the stories (and published) and the DERs, collecting feedback from students and teachers
-held several short online metings focused on status updates and ensuring alingment across activities
-collected impact data on different stages of the project, primarily through surveys and interviews (see report for details)
-continually conducted quality management activites (see report for details)

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs
- set of 18 stories, which we published, from 3 regions of Europe
- simple to use online app used to create DERs, known as the story editor
- story editor allows creation of for rooms, content, tasks and transitions. Task types: multiple choice, drag and drop, gap fill, rewrite sentence, scrambled text, order images, question with multiple answers, matching exercise, and classification
- handbook to the story editor, a guide to its use
- website to host the DERs; both those created as part of this project and submitted by other users (if approved). Other information about the project is also available here
- set of 36 DERs using the story editor, derived from the 18 stories, all available on the website
Other results
- improved creative writing skills leading to increased skills and job satisfaction
- developoment of relationships between individuals and partner organisations
- deeper understanding of other EU cultures
- greater awareness of Erasmus+ and stronger reputation of partners in local teaching communites and wider networks, e.g. International House
- piloting involved schools from several EU countries with positive feedback
- feedback results indicate both enjoyment and benefits from the materials
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2020-1-CZ01-KA227-ADU-094406.title: Empowerment of social inclusion groups though creativity and cultural works
2020-1-CZ01-KA227-ADU-094406.summary:
<< Background >>

Culture is not just another affected sector in need of public support during this time of crisis. In fact, culture can accelerate socio-economic recovery from the pandemic. Employing and engaging artists could play an important role in ensuring cultural diversity and fostering inclusive dialogue. The COVID-19 pandemic has laid bare the deep inequalities in cities, resulting in some places and people being disproportionately affected.  
A post-COVID-19 community should foster social inclusion, build accessible public spaces and civic institutions, safeguard all forms of cultural heritage, protect and support culture professionals, promote diversity, creativity and innovation, and integrate the arts and culture sector into its recovery and develop new skills and competences to enhance the creativity process. The artists need to improve their digital skills and receive new competences connected with promotion, offering and support their work using online platforms, international e-residencies and tools. On the other hand, there is a need to extend the competences of the cultural workers in terms of facing the new circumstances and providing recovery plans to emerging artists using as an advantage their inclusion background.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were linked to supporting emerging artists from social excluded groups to get upskilled and recovered after the COVID-19 pandemic. This was achieved by:
•Introducing and examining the situation of the artists with social inclusion background in the new post-COVID 19 circumstances (country reports and online research)
•Equipping the artists with new skills heling their social empowerment and using the topics part of the training curriculum (IO2)
•Assessing and pilot the knowledge, skills and competences acquired through non-formal learning of the curriculum modules (10 learning modules, IO3)
•Accelerating digital transformation and use of digital means to adapt to the way creative products, cultural goods and events are created, managed, disseminated, accessed, and consumed (Digital Open Art Studio of IO4)
•Reinforcing the cross-sectoral and international cooperation with focus on creativity and artistic empowerment and strengthening the cooperation and networking between organizations from 7 EU Countries
•Provide a recovery plan for artists, using more digital and resilient recovery
•Equip cultural workers with skills for equity, diversity, and inclusion challenges in the learning environment

<< Implementation >>

IO1-Supporting Artists from social exclusion groups in post-COVID 19 period, aiming to assess the situation of the culture and community in the post-COVID 19 period and to present possible methods and techniques to support artists from social inclusion groups
IO2-Training Curriculum for Empowerment of social inclusion groups though Creativity and Artworks, aiming to elaborate and test a training plan for empowerment of social inclusion groups though their direct involvement in artistic and creativity activities
IO3-Testing of the Training Curriculum, aiming to assess and pilot the produced training materials at local and international level
IO4-Digital Open Art Studio Platform linked to the creation of a platform for artists, arts educators and arts organizations working with social exclusion groups such as refugees and asylum seekers in Europe and beyond, Romani and others
7 Multiplier events to test the training curricula produced as part of IO2 and to enhance the artistic and creativity of the selected adult learners
One Open Art Studio in Thessaloniki, as a Short-term joint staff training event for the testing and piloting of the project methodologies and materials, as it is combining theoretical and practical exercises.

<< Results >>

Research Report developed to identify and analyses the artists’ needs, missing competences, and tools in the field of learners (artists) and teachers’ training (cultural workers) as well as the steps/procedures that have to be followed and the issues which have to be addressed in order to establish and sustain an inclusive and successful learning environment. 
Train-the-Trainer Package was developed in order to offer the trainers a practical overview of the training function, by demonstrating the best practices and latest techniques in training methodology and delivery. The content of the Package are available in English and in all the partners’ languages. The partnership carried out 1 LTT activity (C1) with 29 participants, more specifically artists and art workers. The Train the Trainers and the primary testing of the project Outputs was implemented during the National Multiplier events "Local Art Studios".
Learners’ training programme consisted of 10 curriculum lessons and materials and their practical testing though 10 online webinars training among 250 artists.  
Online Platform to host collaborative virtual environments “Digital Open Art Studio”, providing e-residency for 45 emerging artists with their artworks and creations

2020-1-DE02-KA227-ADU-008199.title: Taste of Harmony
2020-1-DE02-KA227-ADU-008199.summary:
<< Background >>

The EU has placed integration high on its political agenda, investing into education programmes to facilitate integration of foreign-born individuals into overall population. But adaptation to a new culture and a new environment presents a stressful time for foreign nationals.

Hence it is not unexpected that foreign-born individuals need a special approach and help in order to be able to engage in positive, friendly social contact with local-born adult members of the local community. The issue of creating authentic intercultural dialogue is one that crosses national borders and requires a joint effort.

To overcome these obstacles, in this project we developed a set of creative, and engaging resources and materials. Since adult education presents a wide target area and a diverse profile of learners, a variety of perspectives is needed to tackle the many variables at play. 

The core idea of Taste of Harmony is bringing people from different cultures together around the kitchen table and let them share their experience around cooking and cuisine (a topic everybody loves to speak about). Taste of Harmony combines this with various opportunities for adult learners to start creative processes using modern tools of mass communication.

<< Objectives >>

The project was created to contribute to a measurable and visible improvement of:
• Intercultural dialogue through sharing cultural/personal stories and meaning embedded in recipes
• Key digital competences (content creation, communication, and security) related to sharing recipes and personal stories
• Societal integration of foreign-born (expats, migrants, asylum seekers, and refugees) adult members of the local community
• Online and face-to-face interaction of native-born and foreign-born adult members of local communities in partner countries

<< Implementation >>

1) CURRICULUM for a COURSE (30 + 30 h)

Curriculum for a blended learning course (30 hours classroom, 30 hours self-directed) to bring together local and foreign-born participants and make them share their experience, use local language and do steps into using modern media (audio, video) for sharing recipes. Including pilot courses for testing.

2) E-LEARNING PLATFORM

To support the self-learning activities of the above-mentioned course

3) BITE-SIZED LEARNING RESOURCES

We produced a set of materials such as info-graphics,texts, pictures, videos, audios, tasks and riddles, for quick use (e.g. 1-5 minutes per item), to support the aims of the project. These materials have been published in various social media channels.

4) RADIO SHOW / PODCAST 

32 podcast episodes with experts and non-experts, about food, culture, cuisine, in all languages of the project. 

5) TRAINING COURSE for educators 

We designed a three days workshop for adult educators to get acquainted with the materials of the project so that they become able to set up Taste of Harmony groups and courses in their home countries / organisations

<< Results >>

1) Curriculum for a blended learning course (30 + 30 h) - available in 5 languages (EN, DE, IT, GR, HR) 

2) E-learning platform to support the above 

3) 50 bite-sized learning materials, published to the broader public via social media (in all 5 languages)

4) Podcast with 32 episodes on the topic (mostly English,but also in local languages)

5) Concept for a staff training for educators to enable them to use the above materials.The training concretely implemented once with teachers of participating organisations.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-DE02-KA227-ADU-008267.title: Viral Visions - deconstructing art immunity
2020-1-DE02-KA227-ADU-008267.summary:
<< Background >>

Arts and culture are areas that suffered particularly from the Covid 19 pandemic and were not considered essential to the system. After this impressive and depressing experience, the impact of which we can still feel today, the partners of the project have decided to make a contribution that strengthens the presence of the arts, which is more necessary than ever for our society and its citizens. 
The aim of the project is to use mediation processes to raise awareness of contemporary artistic processes and new forms, and at the same time to tap into the enormous creative potential of each individual and to communicate individual potential. 
Together we have put together a selection of tried and tested processes and methods that show how art and creative action can provide tools and new perspectives for building resilience and innovation, as well as creating expressiveness and offering strength to work on social and political issues. The materials and instructions, as well as a wealth of contributions on individual artistic practice, are available for free use at www.viral-visions.eu.

<< Objectives >>

The project partners create proven artistic methods and approaches for training programmes in adult education to activate the creative potential of citizens of all ages.
Each partner systematically develops questions based on the specific cultural context in order to provide a selection of good examples of how art, creative activities and approaches, provide tools and new perspectives to strengthen resilience and inventiveness as well as creative expression in otherwise non-artistic citizens (lay people).
The participating artists and arts facilitators develop a workshop concept that clearly presents artistic processes for creativity development. From this, trainings can be derived that can also be applied by non-professional artists.
Overall, the project serves as a self-reflection on the relevance of art, the strengthening of the creativity of citizens and audience development. It addresses the target group A of mediators: artists, art and adult educators and B: the target group of recipients from the institutional cultural sector and from community work.

<< Implementation >>

Creation of a google drive platform on which all documents are stored.
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1exPZ1FDbCXPsz4ZEVrSihBsHsAePeFuW
Development of logos; creation of Instagram and FB account: https://www.facebook.com/viralvisionseurope
Instagram: @viralvisionseurope for external communication
 Digital meetings (t.w. monthly); Transnational meetings according to plan; Final event with artistic presentations and audience participation.  
-Construction of a digital handbook linked to a web domain (including images, documents, videos, podcasts) = best practice examples on the impact and relevance of arts and culture for the development of personal skills 
-Testing and teaching of the developed methods and approaches in 2 workshops (C1 and C2) 
Development of a curriculum for C1 and C2:Workshop on art access and creativity promotion 
Podcasts on artistic positions and methods from the participating institutions as well as from contemporary art and cultural mediators - two per partner in all languages, plus more for inspiration, most in English and German. Creation of a website to present the project, the partner, aswell as the Produkts asr Pocasts, Handbook and Curriculum.

<< Results >>

A freely available CURRICULUM in all participating languages for the implementation of a workshop lasting at least one week to teach artistic approaches and methods and to stimulate the participants' own creativity. 
A free available HANDBOOK with two tried and tested examples from each partner of good practice in participation in artistic projects with artists and lay people - also suitable for community work  
Several, all free, PODCast on cultural practices, artistic positions and social relevance of art, culture and education. Two podcasts have been produced for each partner in all project languages, as well as about 40 more in English. The podcasts also illustrate from a more complex perspective how the project partners work. 
WEBSITE, which describes the project, presents the activities of the partners and refers to their medilae communication, all materials and products are hosted here. The website will be maintained for 5 years; the partners can also post their current activities there. 
All participating organisations continue to work with the viral visions approach, and new projects have been launched among themselves.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-DE04-KA227-YOU-020844.title: New normal: Art is Moving Online
2020-1-DE04-KA227-YOU-020844.summary:
<< Background >>

The situation with the Covid 19 pandemic has changed the way we all live and work. Artists were not immune to these new changes and were greatly affected as most of the presentations of their work and interactions with audiences were and are based on face-to-face encounters such as exhibitions, shows, plays, performances etc. 
With the project proposal, our consortium created tools that helped the artists to combat the Covid 19 situation, reach their target audience and give them the opportunity to present their work, earn an income and overcome the Covid 19 situation.
This project addressed the needs of young dancers and performers who wanted to successfully continue their regular work with the help of digital tools and technologies. It helped them to stay in touch with their existing audience, but also to reach more people by using online platforms and social media. They learned how to adapt their usual face-to-face activities to develop and implement them online. They discussed how to use the skills and competences acquired to improve the overall quality of their work in the long term and had the opportunity to learn from each other and share their experiences and examples of good practise in relation to the Covid 19 situation.

<< Objectives >>

- To connect the youth sector and youth organisations with the cultural sector (especially dancers and performers) and policy makers to start a dialogue between these three parties and create new opportunities for artists and performers given the Covid 19 situation.
- Strengthen the skills of youth organisations for their work to empower dancers and artists in local communities to create opportunities to engage with audiences through the development of online activities.
- Develop a platform with a portfolio of all artists involved in the project as a place where they can meet and promote their online and live activities
- To offer new educational opportunities to young artists - especially by acquiring skills and knowledge to adapt their activities to the online environment and increase the visibility of their work
- Improve the skills of dancers and performers to cope with the Covid 19 pandemic in the industry and make them more resilient
- Improve the skills of dancers and performers through the development of online courses: video production, use of social media and the internet to reach audiences (especially youth) and engage them in the arts; social media strategy and content development for artists.

<< Implementation >>

- Online Platform for artists and youth organisations
- Manual with Guidebook: supporting aspiring young artists in our local communities.
- Learning-teaching-training activity (LTTA) – training course: Youth work support to inspiring artists and art in our local communities.
- Online course for youth workers: Supporting aspiring young artists in our local communities through our youth work activities.
- Online course: Performers and dance artists in role of developers of online activities as a way of engagement with audience and presentation of their work
- Online course: Digital marketing and using digital tools for promotion of online activities by artists

<< Results >>

- Youth sector, the cultural sector and decision makers started a dialogue between them to create new opportunities for artists and performers.
- Strengthened the skills of youth organisations in their work to promote artists in their local communities, to create opportunities to engage with audiences through the development of online activities.
- Created a safe online space (platform) where they can meet and promote their online and offline activities
- enabled young artists to gain new educational opportunities - in particular by acquiring skills and knowledge to adapt their activities to the online environment and increase the visibility of their work
- CCS in local and national communities are better able to address the issues they face due to the pandemic. With new digital knowledge and skills, they are better equipped to work and create in conditions of lockdown and/or restricted movement, and are also able to network within and outside the sector.
- Skills of dancers and performers increased through developed online courses.
- NGOs are able to develop and/or improve practises to meet the needs of disadvantaged groups and to address differences in learning outcomes related to geographical and socio-economic inequalities

Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-DK01-KA227-ADU-094201.title: Sharing practices in the use of Art for adults with Mental health problems
2020-1-DK01-KA227-ADU-094201.summary:
<< Background >>

Art therapy as a recognized discipline by mental health experts yields numerous advantages, including enhanced self-esteem, an outlet for emotions, a sense of control, and self-discovery. 
However, there are still challenges to the practical use: 
1. Resistance and Stigma: Societal stigma around both mental health and artistic expression could deter both professionals and people from participating in art therapy, impacting its accessibility and effectiveness.
2. Lack of Support and Standardization: Art therapy needs ressources and framework to exist just like any other. So unlike more structured therapeutic approaches, data and KPIs on the efficacy and values of art therapy can vary immensely.
3. Ethical and Emotional Concerns: Any therapy can sometimes uncover deep-seated emotions and traumas. So Art Therapists needs also to be well-trained to handle a wide set of challenges. Balancing artistic exploration with emotional well-being requires careful navigation to ensure the process is therapeutic rather than retraumatizing.

This all leads to a blind spot in the practical use and scaling of art therapy practices and knowledge gaps as to the diversity of practices.

<< Objectives >>

Our goal is to expand learning opportunities for mentally challenged adults, helping them recognize concealed emotions through art. Art therapy complements conventional mental health treatments, managing behaviors, processing feelings, and boosting self-worth. It fosters a sense of accomplishment, promoting confidence and social integration.

The paramount merit of art therapy lies in providing a wholesome channel for adults with mental health issues to express emotions. Art can capture complex feelings like sadness or anger when words fall short. Amidst the stress of battling anxiety, depression, or trauma, creating art offers relief and relaxation.

We wanted to help both the project partners, the wider network of stakeholders, the mental health - and the art community - and also the wider public to get a better and wider understanding of the possibilities of using art therapy in practice - whether for destigmatization, prevention, treatment, or rehabilitation.

<< Implementation >>

The partners made a series of study visits to get hands on experience from the partnering countries. This lead to a continuous and strong dialogue about differences and practices to cultural and organizational implementation of creative and/or artistic practices.

In addition, the partners gathered a series of good practice cases, that were gathered into a website repository and a digital booklet. And the partners also used the inspiration from practical activities and initiatives in one partner country (Portugal) into a transfer of this good practice into a new dissemination and knowledge sharing event - a festival for art and mental health - in a new partner country (Greece).

<< Results >>

1. A website with a case collection of good practices for the use of art in mental health services
2. A digital booklet with these practices also, combined with a series of summaries of various aspects of the use of art and creativity for mental health
3. The development and transfer of a communication and dissemination concept for the use of art and creativity for mental health - a public festival with a mixed participation of both professionals, informal carers, mental health patients, art practitioners, and public health decision makers and community stakeholders.

2020-1-EL01-KA227-ADU-094627.title: READ-IN-CLUB: READ-INg for CuLtUres across Borders
2020-1-EL01-KA227-ADU-094627.summary:
<< Background >>

The Creative and Cultural Sector belongs to those segments of society which were mostly affected by the 2020 novel COVID-19 crisis, causing enormous social turbulence in European society: EU citizens experience the ‘new normality’ of staying at home and living under lockdown. While human interaction has been seriously wounded under these critical circumstances, EU values for social cohesion, inclusion, intercultural dialogue, community engagement, understanding of the “other” and tolerance, all of them conveyed by arts and culture, have been into a great challenge.

The project READ-IN-CLUB: READ-INg for CuLtUres across Borders derived from the need to equip our society with those skills and competences which are essential to ensuring a swift and smooth recovery from the crisis. In READ-IN-CLUB, the art of literature and the institution of book clubs and reading communities, together with the power of digital technology, comprise powerful facilitators of informal learning and dialogue and create a supportive cultural environment where people are encouraged to become innovators and effective lifelong learners.

The READ-IN-CLUB project was a 20-months Erasmus + project involving 6 partners from 5 different countries.

<< Objectives >>

The initial objectives of the READ-IN-CLUB project were: 
To develop a cross-sectoral approach for cooperation - established in the EU values which are generated and conveyed by the art of literature.
To address the challenge of ingraining the educational aspect of reading clubs for social inclusion and intercultural dialogue in the “digital, post- COVID agenda” of the book industry stakeholders.
To qualify reading clubs coordinators through enhancing their training skills and digital competences and rendering them “Lit.Mentors” of intercultural dialogue.
To develop and deliver a digital reading club platform, innovative training materials and content methodologies to successfully meet the needs of reading club coordinators and their communities and empower them at all levels.

The READ-IN-CLUB targeted professionals of the book industry who organize and coordinate the operation of reading clubs or other educational activities related to literature: writers, authors, translators, directors and, representatives of private and public libraries, moderators of reading clubs/book clubs, managers of publishing houses and literary organizations, publishers, editors or even members of reading clubs.

<< Implementation >>

In order to achieve the objectives of the project, the consortium implemented a series of activities, including: 

- need analysis through bibliographic research, surveys, and interviews with stakeholders. 
- Virtual seminars and design of an educational program. 
- content development for the educational program. 
- design and development of an e-learning platform. 
- collection of best practices, workshop activities, tools and methodologies. 
- organization of public events. 
- creation and distribution of newsletters, press releases and articles. 
- creation and operation of digital channels of communication (website, Facebook, Instagram)
- online and physical meetings
- involvement of external participants
- evaluation and quality assurance tests. 

All the above were supported by 3 main horizontal activities: The Project Management and Implementation, the Quality Assurance and Evaluation Methodology and the Dissemination Plan.

<< Results >>

The main results of the READ-IN-CLUB project are: 

A. READ-IN-CLUB Research Report (IO1): It summarizes the impact of COVID 19 in the CCS and the book sector specifically, based on desk research and reports collection. It outlines the value of reading clubs in adult developement and, finally it incorporates data from 5 countries – GR, CYP, HR, SL, and CR – to showcase the needs of reading clubs & identify the training gaps of reading club coordinators in interpreting literature as a tool for intercultural dialogue. 

B. the Virtual Training Seminars for «Lit. Mentors» (IO2): It is the educational program that attempts to integrate in the reading communities’ context the cultural, social and education dimensions of literature for intercultural dialogue and social inclusion.

C. the #Read-IN-ClubDigital (IO3): It is a digital common space dedicated to the promotion, awareness-raising, and knowledge-sharing on issues related to books, reading clubs, and cultures. It includes the website, the e-learning platform, and a social platform for book clubs. 

D. the READ-IN-CLUB e-Manual (IO4): It is a practical toolkit full of guidelines, instructions and case studies that help book club coordinators to transform their clubs into life-long learning environments where intercultural dialogue and skills building are taken place, using all the tools of the READ-IN-CLUB project. 

E. 6  INFO DAYS aiming to raise the awareness of the public for the project and its deliverables. 

F. The involvement of approximately 324 external participants. 

G. The development of a digital community via social media with 779  followers.
 
H. The development of database with a series of reading clubs from Greece, Cyprus, Hungary, Slovenia and Croatia.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-ES01-KA227-SCH-095571.title: LETS SHARE OUR TREASURES
2020-1-ES01-KA227-SCH-095571.summary:
<< Background >>

When pupils go to school they meet others from diffrent socio-cultural backgrounds and have opportunities to make new experiences in a new social environmwent.We, the partners from,SPAIN-the coordinator,TR-RO-HR-LT and IT have an enormous responsibility to ensure that our pupils develop cultural awareness and are engaged in acts of citizenship,not only within our schools and surrounding areas,but as active members of the global community and each partner organisation brings different experience and competences regarding educational systems,history and cultures in their countries. So our needs were to ensure our students gain social skills to allow an intercultural citizenship using the art and creativity.

<< Objectives >>

Our special goals were;

a)	To make pupils aware that all individuals may be different.

b)	To reduce the influence of media and social media on pupils.

c)	Providing cultural fusion by breaking prejudices among children.

d)	To teach the pupils the basic elements of different beliefs.

e)	Adopting the importance of respecting individual differences on ensuring peace in the society for the pupils,their parents and teachers.

<< Implementation >>

Organizing project team with teachers with different skills, abilities, knowledge who were willing/able to work in a team collaborating with other teachers/students, to be able to remain united in any conditions and find solutions that project would bring.
organizing student work teams and obtaining parental consent for participation in activities and all other consents for filming and photographing students during activities
identifying the most suitable methods for creating a final products
implementation of the project activities in the curriculum hours
creating work schedules outside of class hours for students and teachers (mobilities LTTA and TPM)
methods of communication (especially during Covid 19 pandemic)
monitoring of activities and evaluation
control of effectiveness and efficiency of the activities implemented 
elaboration of  Common questionnaires 
The Monitory of activities, comparing activities, comparing, observing  students’ behavior during the activities,  measuring the efficiency of budget spent, observing the attitude of students working together for project, measuring  the quality of final products and their sustainability

<< Results >>

We made  digital boards for dissemination. we created a project logo contest to choose our logo,  we created presentation and videos to meet partners, we chose a mascot for each country and created a panel, we celebrated special days like flamenco day and erasmus day, we created a claendar, we made christmas card exchanges, We made  ebooks with traditional recipies  and traditional cloths,we made digital presentations of noble prizes, sportsman and oscar winners that were explained by groups during mobilities. We visited historic and cultural places in each partners country and created a video. we explored one World heritage site of each country and students made presentations . We learnt and dance folklor and traditional dances form our host partners. Students illustrated tradictional songs from each country. 2020-1-ES01-KA227-SCH-096093.title: EUREKArt: Communicating European Science Research Knowledge through Arts
2020-1-ES01-KA227-SCH-096093.summary:
<< Background >>

The project is completely in line with EU ideas, which encourage and strengthen the development of critical life skills.This covers social and learning-to-learn competencies,critical thinking and creativity, collaboration in STE(A)M. these project was submitted because it clearly shows a method for improving the development of skills and competencies that reinforce and foster creativity, as well as promoting quality, innovation, and work recognition to support the creative potential of young students, thereby contributing to the recovery and resilience of the cultural and creative sectors.Furthermore,It was born COVID. At such a crucial moment, there was a need to establish alternate routes to education, assure rapid recuperation, reinforce pupils' basic skills, and promote equitable chances for everyone. we created this initiative to encourage student innovation while also assisting the cultural sector. this project reinforces intersectoral cooperation with an approach aimed at creativity. it promotes social inclusion through art, fostering innovative approaches to intercultural and participatory dialogue that connect stakeholders in the fields of school education, training & organizations of the creative and cultural sector.

<< Objectives >>

The purpose of this project was to produce wide societal benefits by creating connections between the visual and performing arts and nanotechnology, based on the curriculum of secondary schools.
Encourage and develop students' curiosity about the process that leads from creativity to culture creation.
Develop an interest in scientific knowledge with social value through an educational synergy between the visual and performing arts together with nanotechnology. 
Develop innovative practices in the field of education, by combining performing and plastic arts with nanotechnology.
Provide young adults with the necessary tools and skills to find creative and innovative solutions that allow them to face unprecedented social risks and challenges. 
Furthermore, the initiative includes free tools for instructors who want to combine scenic and plastic arts into their syllabus, which can be downloaded on the website. 
The consortium employed a variety of various learning resources, materials, courses, and training modules, as well as artistic and cultural initiatives with an educational focus, to address the demands of developing informal and non-formal education and boosting the development of skills and competencies.

<< Implementation >>

Dissemination activities: Together with the email campaign that each partner has sent to their network, different dissemination activities were carried out at the TPM in Croatia to raise awareness of the work of the project and the celebretation of the ERN in Split. Spain, the Etxebarri Science Week and the ERN in Zaragoza during which external public could prove with their hand the real application of the concept and methodologies created by the partnership. the multiplier events held. 
Pilot activities: A pilot experience was carried out in each country in which the adequacy of the materials was tested and materials were changed where needed.In Italy, the A. Volta institute has piloted different techniques of the project proposal that can be seen as a way of disseminating these methodologies to external teachers and different students from the school.
Implementation activities: All countries did the work of looking for centres to implement the activities developed, for which training sessions were also held in Zaragoza within the LTTA. At this training activity, 20 people took part (including 5 from the partnership) and the public was made up mostly of teachers with different backgrounds, researchers and educators.

<< Results >>

Experiential and synergistic workshops to approach the plastic arts through nanotechnology with an introduction section on the principles of nanoscience by expert researchers followed by its subsequent application in the fabrication of plastic works using these techniques.
Experimental workshops to approach the performing arts through nanotechnology via a theatrical performance: dramatic representation through scientific demonstrations of how art and theatre are connected to nanotechnology.
A didactic guide that explores further into the scientific understanding of different topics. this guide that explains in depth all the scientific concepts and develops the theoretical basis. It also proposes a series of workshops and experiments to be carried out. In addition, as a complement to the guides, there are five videos explaining the concepts and experiments
The artistic part : workbooks to use in class. there are five themes covered with activities related to the concepts and provide a glossary of terms.
In the theatrical part, there are 6 workbooks, 5 topics covered explaining concepts related to theatrical skills. In addition, it has another 3 videos explaining concepts related to theatrical theory and story development.

2020-1-ES02-KA227-YOU-016715.title: Art and creativity to reactivate youth participation during/after COVID19
2020-1-ES02-KA227-YOU-016715.summary:
<< Background >>

COVID19 has hit our daily lives in many ways. Human relationships, the priorities of our life, our leisure activities and free time, everything is changing and readjusting. And in this context, youth participation and educational leisure, which were already a complicated issue before the pandemic, are much more so now. The restrictions on social life and collective activities are causing youth associations and participation to drop to a minimum (in favor of collective health) and the impact it has on society in general is something we want to find out. In addition, we have seen these months ago that creativity and art in general have been an excellent tool to activate and motivate youth.

This project addresses the needs of the organizations that present it, concerned about the reactivation of youth participation by applying the most appropriate creative and artistic tools. All the entities agree that the impact of COVID on the participation of young people in activities is being very great and we need to reinvent ourselves and learn from each other.

<< Objectives >>

1. Analyze the impact that COVID19 is having on youth participation and youth associations
2. Search and share good ideas based on art and creativity for the reactivation and adaptation of participation and associationism to this new reality COVID19
3. Improve the quality of youth participation systems in our environments through the use of artistic and creative tools
4. Get the young people from the municipalities that participate in the project to develop a transnational youth initiative project that gives continuity to this project

<< Implementation >>

A) General coordination:
-Formal agreements and partnership contracts with partners
-General monitoring of progress and achievement of objectives
-Project reports (intermediate and final)
-Accounting and treasury of the project (transfers and control)
-Quality control of good practices presented by partners

B) Continuous and final evaluation
- Preparation of evaluation surveys and forms
- Data collection and adjustment proposals if necessary
- Control over the quality of the expected results in each phase

C) Analysis of the impact of COVID19
- Preparation of initial documents
- Preparation of survey forms
- Compilation and synthesis of conclusions
- Translation of the final document and publication

D) Compilation of good practices
- Search and description of 15 good practices by country
- Preparation of good practice sheets
- Translation and adaptation of the sheets
- Layout of the final result and publication at https://artandcreativity.eu/

E) Local actions
- 1 workshop with young people 18-30 years of (at least) 4 hours, face-to-face or virtual
- Visibility in social networks
- Publication on the web platform

<< Results >>

The results of this project have been:

-Analysis of the impact of COVID19 on youth participation, educational leisure and associationism. 
 
-We have carried out a compilation of good practices on the use of creativity and art to promote and support associations and youth participation in times of COVID19. In it we can find examples and good practices that we have experienced and are experiencing in our respective countries during and after the pandemic. This compilation consists of several sheets that we hope will be used as a catalog of ideas for all youth professionals in Europe (or the world). 
 
-In each country, we have held at least one workshop with young people putting into practice some of the good practices presented, so that they have been able to analyze and draw conclusions about their effectiveness.
 
-We have carried out different actions to disseminate the project
 
-We have prepared a Transnational Youth Initiative for the future among the young people participating in the different entities of the project.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Quality and innovation of youth work

2020-1-ES02-KA227-YOU-016744.title: Feminist aesthetics for political poetics
2020-1-ES02-KA227-YOU-016744.summary:
<< Background >>

The Theater of the Oppressed (TO) arises as a response to the urgency of building forms of theatrical representation that do not judge the oppressed for the oppressions they face and, at the same time, overcome the individualism of the stage approach to conflicts. The proposal of this technique is an aesthetic and political investigation, which seeks to reveal the social structure that determines the reproduction of daily oppressions. 
3 transnational exchanges have been carried out to consolidate the European Network of Theater of the Oppressed, enabling the exchange of knowledge and practices, transmission of dynamization skills and application of the methodology for the prevention of violence.
At the same time, for each territory, multiplier work has been carried out in youth groups: Training of "curingas" (facilitates activities, coordinates groups, promotes participation; systematizes practical experience contributing to the development of the Method. Violence prevention and detection activities, and gender inequalities;  Construction of theatrical pieces of protest. Online exchanges and laboratories by proximity (Croatia-Slovenia; Barcelona-Amiens), to share processes, results and evaluation.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project has been to strengthen, at a European level, the systematized and networked work methodology, based on the aesthetics of the oppressed, improving the skills for its multiplication and application in the prevention of gender violence. We have articulated the fabric of current facilitators or multipliers (curingas), as a space for the exchange of good practices and collective resources. At the same time, interventions were carried out in the different local areas, such as pedagogical and preventive work in different groups of young people as a way of preventing violence in general.

<< Implementation >>

The activities that we have carried out are directly related to the objectives and the stages foreseen in the project:

- Training and training for the development of the curingas in each territory.
- Scenic creation (small pieces of t. forum or scenes) to share among existing groups, as well as through specific workshops that have taken place, either in the field of formal education (in schools, institutes and universities, as specific activities within its programming or as activities that were part of specific projects outside school hours) either in the field of non-formal education (in civic and social centers, youth organizations, NPOs), or in Festivals, events and conferences specific.
- Training and training at the local level for new curingas so that they can become benchmarks in their territories to detect, address and prevent violence and gender inequalities through the methodology of the theater of the oppressed.
- Participation in exchanges and online laboratories to share work processes.
- Exchanges and samples between groups and territories, based on the mobility, both of the process and of the results.

<< Results >>

The main objective of the project has been to strengthen, at the European level, a systematized and networked work method, based on the aesthetics of the oppressed, which allows improving the skills of the curingas in youth work and the application of the methodology as a tool for the prevention of violence in various fields. During the execution of the project we have:

-Articulated the current fabric of multipliers (curingas), as a regular space for the exchange of good practices and collective creative resources.
-Analyzed through theatricality, the structural mechanisms that sustain patriarchy and searched for alternatives for action and promotion of gender equality.
-Carried out interventions in local areas, such as pedagogical, preventive and citizen participation work for young people in the various territorial groups.
-Trained and replicated the methodology in different groups of young people as a way of providing them with practical tools in violence prevention.
After finishing the project we have achieved:
- Multiply the methodology, generating new groups of Theater of the Oppressed that are making it possible to expand the network and guarantee its continuity and sustainability.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Quality and innovation of youth work

2020-1-ES02-KA227-YOU-016766.title: Global Artists - Social and Labour Entrepreneurship with young artists
2020-1-ES02-KA227-YOU-016766.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was requested to promote measures that would allow young artists to respond to the challenges and difficulties derived from the situation of the COVID19 pandemic, especially focused on improving their business and social skills, complementing those they receive in formal education. The situation in Europe generated by the pandemic crisis had a very significant impact on this group of young people: unemployment and structural vulnerability that even today (two years later) is still observed in this group.

<< Objectives >>

The general objective of the project was to contribute to the business and social training of 60 young artists from four different countries through an innovative and creative approach.
This general objective would be achieved by achieving three specific objectives:
O.E.1 - Increase the knowledge and skills of young people about entrepreneurship in the field of art and culture.
O.E.2 - Provide knowledge and tools for active social and community participation through art and culture.
O.E.3 - Approaching social participation and the world of employment through participation in social organizations in the environment.
O.E.4 - Approaching social participation and the world of employment through the use of information and communication technologies.
Although it is true that the project was finally granted, it needed readjustment in relation to those objectives that sought both direct training with young people, as well as their participation in social organizations in the area. Since the intellectual products related to the direct training of young people and practices were not granted. However, the final activities tried to cover these aspects also more limitedly.

<< Implementation >>

As stated in the project and granted by the National Agency, the following were carried out:
- 2 transnational coordination meetings, for the organization and coordination of the project. One of them online, due to the still existing blockades due to the pandemic.
- Preparation of a manual guide for young artists for business and social entrepreneurship. That includes information on self-employment, social participation and social activism, with didactic units to be a useful and transferable tool to other contexts when working with young artists.
- Multiplier events in each of the countries. In which young artists participated and both information, training and cultural and social activities were offered in coordination with other social agents in the context. The objective was to disseminate the project, the manual guide prepared and facilitate access to real training experiences with young artists, social organizations and social activist artists.

<< Results >>

Regarding the concrete results:
- More than 60 young artists from four different countries have received professional and social training through an innovative approach.
In addition to this result indicating the scope of the project, each specific objective had its associated expected result.
R.E.1.1 - More than 60 young people have had a greater knowledge and skills about entrepreneurship in the field of art and culture.
R.E.2.1 - More than 60 young people have had a greater knowledge and tools for active social and community participation through the contribution of art and culture.
R.E.4.2 - 1 open face-to-face/online seminar have been held on the possibilities of information and communication technologies for social and labor participation.
The results associated with the training and internships in social organizations were not achieved as proposed by reducing the intellectual results of the project and therefore the budget. This affected the results R.E.3.1; R.E.3.2; R.E.4.1; R.E.1.2; R.E.2.2
