2020-1-FR01-KA227-SCH-095534.title: Geometrician's views
2020-1-FR01-KA227-SCH-095534.summary:
<< Background >>

Les mathématiques sont souvent perçues comme étant difficiles et formalistes par les élèves, ce qui peut engendrer de l'anxiété à leur égard. Pour y remédier, certaines études suggèrent de proposer des contenus stimulants afin de restaurer la confiance dans l'enseignement des mathématiques. Ce projet propose d'introduire la culture mathématique à travers la culture artistique pour impliquer les élèves. Les objectifs incluent la découverte de la culture mathématique à travers l'art et la science, le développement de la créativité et de l'imagination, la promotion du travail collaboratif et la création de productions artistiques et numériques diverses et variées. Le public cible comprend les élèves de la maternelle jusqu'au lycée ainsi que le grand public. Le projet a été mené de manière transnationale pour étendre le projet "Regard de géomètre" en France et observer comment les mathématiques sont enseignées dans d'autres systèmes éducatifs. Le projet vise à changer les mentalités et les préconceptions sur les mathématiques à travers une aventure enrichissante qui promeut la cohésion européenne à travers les mathématiques et les arts.

<< Objectives >>

Le projet KA225-SCH-095534 Geometrician’s views (GV) est une coopération internationale dans le domaine de l'éducation. L'objectif de cette initiative est de permettre aux élèves de la maternelle jusqu'au lycée d'explorer la culture mathématique à travers l'art et la science. Des partenaires de 5 pays différents sont invités à échanger des approches innovantes pour enseigner les mathématiques, et les élèves sont invités à créer des livrables collaboratifs à l'intersection entre les mathématiques et les arts.

<< Implementation >>

Le projet avait pour objectif de proposer des activités pratiques aux élèves des écoles partenaires en France, Roumanie, Croatie, Italie, Serbie et Grèce. Ces activités comprenaient notamment la mise à l'essai de brochures éducatives et la réalisation d'ateliers pratiques pour créer des supports d'exposition sur des concepts mathématiques. Le budget alloué au projet a permis l'achat d'équipements et de matériaux nécessaires, ainsi que l'engagement de partenaires associés et la mise en place d'une campagne de diffusion. Pour assurer une bonne coordination, des réunions mensuelles internes ont été organisées. La collaboration entre les différents pays a été facilitée grâce à l'utilisation d'outils partagés tels que Google Drive, des rapports de réunion, des listes de tâches et un outil de gestion de projet. Le suivi de la production intellectuelle a également été assuré, ainsi que la coordination d'ateliers pratiques au niveau local.

<< Results >>

Le consortium a produit trois types de livrables : des tutoriels pour la mise en place d'activités mathématiques et artistiques en classe (IO1), des affiches d'exposition sur les arts et les mathématiques (IO2) et un musée virtuel (IO3) utilisant le logiciel Neotrie. Les tutoriels sont divisés en deux brochures et couvrent 48 sujets mathématiques, comprenant des activités pratiques et une connexion avec l'application Neotrie. Les affiches d'exposition couvrent les mêmes sujets que les tutoriels et visent à faciliter un dialogue entre un chercheur et un artiste, chaque affiche étant imprimable dans divers formats. Le musée virtuel est en réalité virtuelle et comprend plusieurs parties, avec des activités géométriques interactives liées aux créations produites en classe par les élèves pendant le projet. Un manuel d'introduction a été produit pour guider les utilisateurs dans la découverte du logiciel, et un casque de réalité virtuelle est nécessaire pour visiter le musée virtuel.

2020-1-HR01-KA227-ADU-094674.title: Crafting the Inclusion: Crafts and Practices in non-formal education for increasing social inclusion
2020-1-HR01-KA227-ADU-094674.summary:
<< Background >>

Working with marginalised groups in non-formal education and by means of arts is still marginalised. That is the reason why most European programmes like Erasmus+ or ESF call for inclusion of marginalised groups by raising the skills of educators and of the marginalised groups themselves. Marginalisation is recognised in major EU documents focused on raising employment, social affairs & inclusion (e.g. European accessibility act, European Disability Strategy 2010-2020, Preamble of the UN Convention) to which this partnership contributes. Through inclusive practice, partner organisations experienced that (hand)crafts play a significant role in raising social inclusion and cultural awareness, developing some of the EU's Key Competences, or even developing basic motoric skills. They can be thought nonverbally and are ideal for sharing in international context. CRAFT:IN focuses on educators (but not excluding marginalised groups) as they can transfer the new knowledge into a new environment and bring positive changes. However, educators and organisations in inclusive crafts lack international experience and cross-border cooperation - which they are provided for at CRAFT:IN that aims to share, educate, motivate, and promote.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of CRAFT:IN is to share good practices between partner organisations that work in the field of inclusive crafts. This is highly important as professionals, volunteers, and all others working with marginalised groups get marginalised themselves - leaving them with low finances and low self-esteem. By providing an international platform to partner organisations, CRAFT:IN has given them an opportunity to share their local craft that can be used in working with marginalised groups, to network and to gain international experience, to raise their Key Competences of employability and to promote inclusion of locals and marginalised groups in a process of cultural exchange between participants and local community that occurs when educational activities of CRAFT:IN end with a public presentation/exhibition of the work done by the participants and, more widely, when educators of CRAFT:IN publish the details of their crafts in educational materials such as eBrochures and eVideos. CRAFT:IN also aims to start a long-term network and continue motivating those working in inclusive crafts to develop new practices, grow and get recognized for the important work that they do.

<< Implementation >>

CRAFT:IN consisted of three main activities: educational (5 LTT Learning, teaching and training workshops), promotional (5 exhibitions of crafts & works done by the participants at workshops, follow-up workshops and presentations held upon return, and continuous campaign on social media online), and managerial (3 Transnational project meetings and monthly online meetings for PM's). Each partner hosted an LTT event where they shared the craft they are masters of, while some hosted an additional project managers' meeting. Activities were accompanied by publications of 5 eBrochures and 10+ eVideos that were made as step-by-step guidelines that others from outside of CRAFT:IN partnership can use and recreate in order to do their own inclusive work through crafts. To support the participation of members of marginalised groups (especially people with disabilities), partners had activities of aimed at supporting the special needs of such participants (of which there were 15% of all CRAFT:IN participants). Throughout the duration of the partnership partners campaigned via social media and published free and open-source educational materials online, in an effort to promote inclusive crafts, inclusion, and equality of marginalised groups.

<< Results >>

During the 18 months of implementation, 76 participants joined CRAFT:IN activities (11 of which were people with disabilities or members of other marginalised groups, such as refugee from the war in Ukraine) where they shared/learned new/different handcraft and skills for inclusive work, raised their employability through development of Key Competences: Multilingualism (working in English language); Entrepreneurship; Cultural awareness and expression, and raised their self-esteem with a public exhibition and work in international setting. By hosting and participating at 5 LTT workshops with 5 public exhibitions (limited due to COVID-19), partner organisations expanded their human resources, developed new educational programmes (new crafts), and networked on EU level. 


RESULTS
- 3 Transnational Project Meetings
- 5 educational Learning, Teaching, and Training events for inclusive craft
- 5 exhibitions/discussions with local community (limited due to COVID-19)
- 76 participants (including local participants)
- 6 follow-up presentations/workshops
- 1 online toolkit with 5 eBrochures and 10+ videos
- 100+ participants' products
- 14000 inclusive crafts campaign (online promotion via social media & website)

2020-1-HR01-KA227-ADU-094703.title: Facing the Fear of Public Speaking in a Foreign Language
2020-1-HR01-KA227-ADU-094703.summary:
<< Background >>

Many people have some level of fear when speaking to others in public whether it is an informal or formal speech, seminar, sales presentation, etc. at school, at your job, during some formal event, or informally meeting people anywhere at any time. They just don’t feel that comfortable. The first important function associated with drama is fostering speaking skills and overcoming stage fright. Teaching speaking skills are spread among European countries but is not provided so much in adult education offer with drama techniques that is added value to motivation, and creativity, fostering the inclusion of adults in adult education.
The FIGHT THE FRIGHT project proposed an innovative approach that uses performance disciplines including drama and storytelling to build a package of innovative learning educational resources to build key transversal skills of adults.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project in 5 different European countries, partners were keen to:
- develop key and transferable competencies, impacting adults' private and professional lives - foreign language competence, interpersonal communication, self-empowerment, and self-esteem
- reinforce the introduction of drama techniques in teaching and learning essential skills and competences
- improve adults' learning performance 
- enhance employability and improved career prospects for adult learners
- modernize the education and training offered to adult learners
- increase adult participation in learning
- increase competencies of adult educators and staff for motivating the participants and supporting the persistence of adults in learning
- increase the use of open online portals for implementing blended learning and increasing the flexibility of training programs, supporting self-directed learning, and supporting the exchange of best practices and experiences among adult education staff.

<< Implementation >>

Project partners have developed, piloted, and disseminated:
- Curriculum for developing public speaking in a foreign language using drama techniques – TAKE THE STAGE. This curriculum comprised a guide for trainers piloting the curriculum (lesson plan) with a detailed description of additional exercises, ppts, and video tutorials with guides to exercises. Partners piloted those lessons partially as a face-to-face course and another part online with a total of 81 direct participants, also tackling the issue of public performance online.
- A guide for adult education professionals on using drama techniques in teaching and learning – SET THE SCENE
- an online platform for developing public speaking skills – COME ONLINE with additional self-directed learning resources (WebQuests - developed for each of the modules from the Curriculum).
Partners trained the adult education professionals with the needed knowledge to conduct the workshop and enhance their skills to deliver the needed training together with using a digital supportive box of knowledge in working with the target group.
All partners held the multiplier events, and different promotional and internal workshops for greater dissemination and promotion of project achievements.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and project results produced in the FIGHT THE FRIGHT project are the following: 
- TAKE THE STAGE (IO1) - Curriculum for developing public speaking in a foreign language using drama techniques.  This curriculum comprised lesson plans for 6 different modules and additional materials and resources for learning such as exercises, ppts, and video tutorials with guides to exercises. 
- SET THE SCENE (IO2) - A guide for adult education professionals on using drama techniques in teaching and learning 
- COME ONLINE (IO3) - an online platform for developing public speaking skills – with additional self-directed learning resources (6 WebQuests - developed for each of the modules from the Curriculum).
All developer outputs are originally developed and implemented in English language but are also translated into 5 partner languages for greater exploitation and adaptation opportunities in the future.

New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-HR01-KA227-ADU-094771.title: Digital Approaches for Intergenerational Cultural Education
2020-1-HR01-KA227-ADU-094771.summary:
<< Background >>

Since the introduction of LLL concept (90s of the 20th century), new challenges for learning have been found in demographic changes and the use of advanced digital technologies. Learning in the third age is becoming increasingly important due to changing demographic trends and balance, social, economic and health challenges, which implies necessary learning in older age through different educational, cultural and creative activities, in different places and environments, offering diverse content and tools for learning.
The attempt to integrate digital tools and content opens up many opportunities and challenges for organizations involved in the education, especially in the period of big crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic, when the importance and increased need for the use of digital tools and content came to the fore and the resistance of seniors and teachers was noticeable.
The COVID-19 pandemic has encouraged partner organizations to try to answer the question of what are the advantages and limitations of using digital tools and content in the educational process, and how to assess where the limit of using digital technology is, and when it cannot replace direct contacts, direct physical activity, real movement and tactility.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project is the exchange of partners experience on the advantages and disadvantages of using digital tools and content in educational, cultural and creative programs (e.g. arts, literature, film, music, dance) that play an important role in the education of seniors, especially in the period of the COVID-19, i.e. what are the advantages and disadvantages of digital and virtual learning, with an emphasis on moments when physical contact and closeness are irreplaceable.
The goal was to analyze and share experiences to what extent digital knowledge, tools and content contribute to achieving personal goals, fulfilling wishes for healthy and active aging, cognitive curiosity, needs for self-realization, emotional and social contacts, while identifying compensatory mechanisms that can correct digital limitations in times when physical contact is not possible, but the need for physical activities remains.
Also, how by attending cultural and creative programs, seniors can additionally build and understand their own cultural identity as part of intangible cultural heritage, i.e. how these activities play an important role in meeting educational, cultural and creative needs, which contributes to active and healthy aging.

<< Implementation >>

The DAICE project carried out the following activities:
exchange of good practices among partners in the field of implementation of educational, cultural and creative programs and activities, which include the use of digital tools and content in the educational process
exchange of good experiences among partners regarding the advantages and disadvantages of using digital tools and content in the implementation of educational, cultural and creative programs and activities
involving employees and external collaborators of partners, as well as participants of the third-life program in project activities, in order to gain insight into new digital knowledge, skills and competences that are needed in the education of senior people
visiting different organizations within the framework of LTA (3) and TPM (4) activities that implement educational, cultural and creative programs and activities for senior people, in order to adopt other experiences in the field of using digital tools and content, while consulting about their experiences when creating educational, cultural and creative content, which can be adopted and implemented in the organization and implementation of educational, cultural and creative programs intended for senior people.

<< Results >>

The concrete results of the DAICE project are:
included 6 partner organizations in the exchange of good practices and experiences in the field of implementing educational, cultural and creative programs and activities, which include the use of digital tools and content in the educational process, as well as the exchange of experiences related to the advantages and disadvantages of using digital tools and content in the implementation of educational , cultural and creative programs and activities,
organized and implemented 3 LTAs (Zagreb, Ulm and Belgrade) and 4 TPMs (Zagreb, Ulm, Belgrade and Timișoara) in which more than 80 employees, external associates and participants of partner organizations participated
partners visited 30 organizations in the field of adult education and culture in order to exchange good practice with organizations that are not part of a formal project partnership
35 external experts presented the work of their organizations, which gave partners insights into new approaches to using digital tools and content, primarily for working with the elderly through cultural and creative programs
Based on the activities and results of the DAICE project, a new Erasmus+ KA2 project was developed and reported (03/2023).
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-HR01-KA227-ADU-094782.title: Creativity for innovation
2020-1-HR01-KA227-ADU-094782.summary:
<< Background >>

This project was created as an answer to the COVID-19 crisis that has, among other sectors hit the educational and creative sectors the most. The idea was for the educational sector to collaborate with creative ones, as to find a better solution for future challenges within our local community and our organizations. As educational organizations, in COVID-19 we had to make a switch and balance traditional and e-learning. There was a need to incorporate more creative tools to stimulate and empower participants for new knowledge and new skill learning in a digital environment. The need for creative solutions was also detected inside organizations in order to strengthen the competencies of staff to adapt and create new solutions. On the other hand, our partner from the creative sector had a need in improving English teaching competencies, as they were developing their manual Alternative Ways, a way of learning a second language for refugees. With the Callan Method, we have helped them to gain more knowledge and tools to incorporate into their teaching.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of this project was to implement creative and innovative methods in the work of the involved organizations. Our goal was also to improve the competencies of teachers and nonteaching staff in creative solutions when dealing with new challenges at work. One of the goals was also to improve methodology and skills for working with refugees and other vulnerable groups. The value of this project was seen in the program of education that is adjusted to different target groups. For example, the knowledge gained through activities was implemented in work with vulnerable groups such as refugees, other adult learners, professionals, and the general public.

<< Implementation >>

Throughout the project we have carried out 5 main activities: we organized 2 Transnational meetings and 3 LTT activities. 
The first LTT activity was in Zagreb where participants had training in the Callan method and creative methods of learning the English language in the school Initiative Centre for Education. Participants had training in the Callan Method and how they can incorporate the segments of it in their language teaching. The method was presented in depth following the presentation of extracurricular activities like Book Club and  Cook & Chat workshop.
The second LTT was organized in Italy in Florence on the subject of creative writing. The creative writing exercises were immersive and participants were engaged in several topics of creative writing with an emphasis on language learning with this method. Along with exercises in creative writing, partners have gained knowledge of the CLIL method of learning a language that helped us improve methodological skills in this area. 
The third LTT was in the Netherlands in Amsterdam where participants had training in Storytelling and Alternatives Ways method of learning a language.
We have organized the final project evaluation and dissemination of project activities successfully.

<< Results >>

The expected learning outcomes were reached, as participants improved their reading, speaking, and listening skills in English, self-confidence in speaking the English language, and gained a better understanding of the Callan Method. Teachers have implemented elements of the Callan method in their work when teaching a second language for higher stages, using the question/answer elements of the method and practicing speed in speaking. Second, participants have gained skills in how to engage students in creative writing and the CLIL method and how to create learning materials for those two methods. The methods were used in further training courses and business workshops for higher stages and Book Club. And lastly, participants have gained skills in Storytelling and teaching by the Alternative Ways method. The storytelling method was implemented in the work of organizations in several segments: team building, and workshops for refugees, while the Alternative Ways method was used to train teachers on how to creatively engage pupils in lover stages and those who have difficulties in studying a  second language. All the methods were implemented in organizations' work on some level. All participants have gained intercultural experience.
topics: Reception and integration of refugees and migrants
Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2020-1-HR01-KA227-SCH-094766.title: Introducing of Digital Heritage in educational process
2020-1-HR01-KA227-SCH-094766.summary:
<< Background >>

The project idea presents a highly innovative approach which offer implementation of Digital Heritage in educational process by creation of an immersive applications that are based on 360-degree video and targets the students’ education in the importance of Cultural Heritage. This led to more attractive education programmes, use of participatory approaches and ICT-based methodologies which are in line with individual students needs and expectations in present digital society that we are living.

<< Objectives >>

How to define and implement Cultural Heritage preservation in school education in line with needs and expectations of present generations of students, was the central question for the Project partners in the preparatory phase of this project proposal, and using of the ICT-based Digital Heritage approach with creation of 360-degree videos was chosen as the most suitable one. Today there cannot be any doubt that this new field in education and professional training has to be promoted on an individual as well as institutional level.
Project main objectives were: Development of innovative educational approach with introducing of Digital Heritage in education process by using of 360-degrees videos; Establishing a teachers network for transnational cooperation by using of eTwinning networking module; and Promotion of advantages of long-term transnational strategic partnership among different type of organizations in development of innovative educational methodologies.

<< Implementation >>

Project Partners have determined as the best approach a combination of following activities: transnational project meetings, short-term joint staff training events,  long-term teaching assignments and short-term exchanges of groups of pupils. development of Intellectual outputs and multiplier events.
The main aim of project meetings were coordination among project partners, on-time preparation of main events as well as monitoring of the realised activities and resolving of the notified challenges that may occur.
Intellectual outputs were key project components as the results which have to be achieved: IO1- Guidelines for school teachers "How to implement a Digital Heritage in education process by using of 360-degrees videos"; IO2- Digital Heritage 360 degrees videos enhanced by animated 3D elements; IO3- Strategic Action plan for long-term transnational partnership among different types of organizations in improving of educational process in regions of Veliki Bukovec/Ludbreg, Bratzinovo and Kochani by using of innovative methods and best practices. 
Main aim of those events were to present performed project activities and achieved results in front of the interested stakeholders.

<< Results >>

- Creation of min 9 Digital Heritage 360-degrees videos enhanced by 3D elements, with desired quality that can be used in education of the current and future generations of students in project partners schools;
- Developed Guidelines for school teachers "How to implement a Digital Heritage in education process by using of 360-degrees videos";
- Established teacher's network by using of eTwinning module, as the main pre-request for further partnership and cooperation in increasing of teacher's skills and competences for exchanging of good practices;
- Created Strategic Action plan for long-term transnational partnership among different types of organisations in improving of educational process in regions of Veliki Bukovec/Ludbreg, Bratzinovo and Kochani, with aim to stimulate its development by using of best practices and innovative education methods;
- Increased attractiveness of the education process and fostering of the students creative potential with implementation of "activity - based" educational approaches;
- Increased awareness on regional, national and international level about the importance of introduction of Cultural Heritage preservation in education process by using of VR
education materials and benefits that this technology is offering for more attractive and efficient education process in schools (through dissemination material, social events, project
multiplier events, ect.)
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-HR01-KA227-SCH-094792.title: Act Communicate and Transcend
2020-1-HR01-KA227-SCH-094792.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we recognized the opportunity to enhance the quality of school education and language teaching through the introduction of arts, which is in alignment  with the European Union's vision of promoting multilingual competence.  The main recognized need was to address challenges in teaching foreign languages, especially English, because of declining proficiency. Our response was an innovative drama-based curriculum, training materials, a unique assessment tool, and an interactive e-learning platform. By doing so, we aimed to increase students' motivation, engagement, and improve their speaking skills, while at the same time fostering intercultural understanding. The project also aimed to enhance teachers' competences, encouraging lifelong learning and practical classroom application. The additional goal of this cross-sectoral international partnership was to provide networking opportunities and potential future partnerships for project partners, while at the same time improving their internal capacities and know-how.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of our project were to enhance the learning of English as a foreign language, specifically focusing on improving speaking skills. This was accomplished by developing a  drama based activity curriculum, a set of training materials, comprehensive speaking assessment rubric, and an inclusive e-learning platform that combined all intellectual outputs and was accessible in all partner languages. On a broader scale, the project aimed to promote innovative teaching methods across Europe. To achieve these goals, we wanted to focus on equipping English language teachers with drama skills and knowledge, enabling them to apply drama activities effectively in their classrooms through the curriculum, lesson plans, rubric, and e-learning platform. This approach facilitated professional development among teachers, enhancing their pedagogical and digital skills while fostering a deeper understanding of language and culture.  Through teachers' involvement in the project, students at A1, A2, and B1 levels of English in primary and secondary schools across partner countries benefited as well, improved their English speaking skills and became more engaged and motivated in classroom setting.

<< Implementation >>

We developed four intellectual outputs which were translated into all partner languages for wider accessibility. The outputs in all partner languages are available in PDF form for download on project website: https://esldramaactivities.eu/web/icerik/resources-for-teachers 
Four transnational project meetings were held (in Croatia, Bulgaria, Italy and Romania) to bring together project partners in order to discuss project progress and make decisions. In a similar manner, three Learning Teaching Training activities were held (in Croatia, Turkey and United Kingdom), providing teachers from associated partner schools and partner representatives with valuable training on effective drama-based teaching techniques, assessment methods and a usage of e-learning platform. Two multiplier events were held in Croatia and Turkey to disseminate project aims and outcomes, to a broad audience, both achieving the goal of set number of participants attending the events. Face-to-face dissemination and piloting activities were conducted by teachers in order to transfer gained skills and knowledge to students and colleagues. Dissemination activities, such as social media posts, newsletters, eTwinning updates were regularly used to reach wide audience.

<< Results >>

Development of curriculum with the content of improving speaking skills via implementing drama activities, training materials for drama-based curricula/learning activities (drama handbook created by Teatar Tirena and 24 lesson plans), a unique assessment rubric for drama-based curricula and an E-Learning Platform which consists of all previously mentioned outputs, downloadable in PDF form in all partner languages and 3 CEFR levels (A1, A2 and B1). It also includes a Moodle course which has text and infographic training materials and quiz. Primary and secondary resources platform section gives a chance for teachers to upload their own materials (document, multimedia) and to exchange experiences through forum. Video tutorials section has 12 sample lesson implementation videos, 12 tutorials on how to implement lessons and and 12  training videos on how to integrate drama to improve speaking skills. A digital manual for using the eLearning platform has also been created in all partner languages as a comprehensive guidebook. Other results which were realized are the following:  3 LTTA activities with 72 participants, 2 Multiplier Events with 110 participants in attendance, 10 piloting activities with approximately 80 students present.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
Teaching and learning of foreign languages
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-HR01-KA227-YOU-094720.title: Sound experiments – new approaches to non-formal learning in music
2020-1-HR01-KA227-YOU-094720.summary:
<< Background >>

The project "Sound Experiments - New Approaches to Non-Formal Learning in Music" was based on the idea of developing new educational modules for non-formal learning through the use of tools for creating experimental sound and music for young people aged 13 to 20.
Unlike traditional music schools whose program is based on traditional musical and pedagogical methods, starting with music scores and classical harmony, through this project we wanted to put an emphasis on listening, mutual sound research and co-creation among participants and their mentors. The project strived to offer a wider understanding of music and what music can be, and to educate youngsters in the field of group improvisation, music creation in the digital environment, instrument creation, sound art, spatiality of the sound as well as the intersection of auditive and visual arts. Among other important needs and goals, the project focused on encouraging creative and artistic liberty, establishing an alterative approach in music education, broadening youngster's auditive perception and encouraging their openness to other and different.

<< Objectives >>

Through the project we wanted to create 6 educational modules that strive to offer youth a wider understanding of music and encourage creativity and experiment through group improvisation, instrument creation, live digital music, sound art, spatial sound, and field recording. As part of each module, a manual was developed and made available on the official website of the project (www.soundsweird.org), so that each module could easily be recreated in a group, a classroom or at home. 
The idea behind the project was to develop the modules through learning with physical presence in the form of workshops that lasted for a shorter or longer period of time (from several weekends to up to 6 months) but also to create a virtual environment for learning, that would offer materials and tools developed during the workshops that could be used by anyone interested in experimental sound methodology. The virtual learning environment was also created as a space for interaction and exchange of music creations, with an option to upload and share them with other users.

<< Implementation >>

All partners have developed and implemented two educational modules (6 in total). Sonic Acts from the Netherlands implemented the modules "When I Sound I Am Speaking" and "Listening to Sampling". The first module was created as an introduction to field recording, writing and recording text, and creating soundscapes, while the second module cultivated an understanding of the history and techniques of electronic music sampling. A4 from Slovakia developed the modules "Music in the Digital Space - How to Live Code? 1 and 2". The modules introduced the basics of innovative tools and live coding for creating interactive music and visuals, using user-friendly programming languages. KONTEJNER from Croatia developed the modules "Collectiveness: Creating Sounds Together" and "Spatial Sound". The first module focused on joint experimental music creation by teenagers and was dedicated to group and free improvisation. The second one dealt with the physicality and spatial qualities of sound, as well as the creation of spatial sound artworks. After the development of the modules, a Youth Camp was organized in Klanjec, Zagreb, where 5 participants from Zagreb and Bratislava took part, with an online participation by participants in Amsterdam.

<< Results >>

The outcome of the project is an online learning platform for sound experiments called soundsweird (www.soundsweird.org). It is an educational platform for non-formal music learning and experimental approaches to sound for youth in the age 13 to 20. It contains information about six educational modules with workshops that emphasize listening, mutual sound research and co-creation. Part of the platform are downloadable manuals for each workshop that are intended for workshop leaders and educators who would like to teach the module themselves. The manual describes the structure of the workshop in meticulous detail, and provides context as well as extensive background information. It includes valuable tips for teaching the workshop, as well as links to online resources for further research. The platform contains an archive of audio files that were created during the workshops. Users are also welcome to upload sound files to the platform and make them available for others to listen to. There is also a 3D environment within the platform where users can wander around and explore sound recordings and audiovisual works that were made in the context of the project.

2020-1-HR01-KA227-YOU-094777.title: Young Volunteers in the Cultural Events – Lessons Learned from COVID-19 Crisis
2020-1-HR01-KA227-YOU-094777.summary:
<< Background >>

In response to the impact of COVID-19 on volunteer programmes, volunteer coordinators from the European Capitals of Culture came together to address the common challenges faced by their programmes. As the pandemic brought about a sharp decline in cultural events and international cultural cooperation projects, volunteer coordinators were forced to adapt and find new ways to support volunteers and adjust volunteer activities.

One of the biggest challenges was managing volunteers during a crisis, and ensuring their mental health was protected. This led the volunteer coordinators to work on developing transferable resources and best practices that could be used to support volunteers in overcoming the effects of the pandemic. These resources included information on crisis management, mental health support, and personal development, all of which are essential to successfully managing volunteers during these challenging times.

The volunteer coordinators also sought collaboration with partners outside of their sector to create a comprehensive approach to addressing the challenges. The partnership brought valuable expertise and experience, enabling a more comprehensive approach to supporting volunteer programmes.

<< Objectives >>

The formation of the YOUNGETEERS partnership aimed to address the challenges faced by volunteer programmes due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The partnership's interdisciplinary approach to volunteering in culture was critical to ensuring the long-term success of these programmes and mitigating the broader impact of COVID-19 on cultural and creative sectors. 

The specific objectives of YOUNGETEERS were:
1. To strengthen participating organizations by training staff and improving their capacity to work with volunteers and develop sustainable crisis-resilient volunteer programmes  
2. To exchange good practices among partners and strengthen cross-sector international collaboration
3. To design and test innovative educational tools, like educational LARP, based on the needs of young volunteers, to strengthen bonds between volunteers and mentors and help volunteers develop future competences 
4. To develop high standards, methods and tools for youth workers and mentors working with young volunteers, especially in crisis management and personal development.

<< Implementation >>

These were the main activities:
1)PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION ACTIVITIES
- detailed project planning, online meetings, formation of work teams, communication, documentation of activities, monitoring, financial arrangements, dissemination, evaluation, reporting.

2) TRANSNATIONAL PROJECT MEETINGS
TM1 - Kickoff Meeting, 6/2021, Croatia	
TM2: Mid-Term Review Meeting, 9/2022, Greece
TM3: Final Meeting, 12/2022, Serbia	

3) INTELLECTUAL OUTPUTS AND ACTIVITIES
IO1: Designing and testing methodology for training youth workers to manage volunteers in culture during crisis situations.
IO3: Production of YOUNGETEERS Manual on Volunteering in Culture - Lessons Learned from COVID-19 Crisis (preparation, writing, proofreading, editing, design, publication).

4) LEARNING/TEACHING/TRAINING ACTIVITIES
C1: Short-term joint staff training, Bulgaria, June 2022 - Prior to mobility, the participants were involved in online training sessions.

5) MULTIPLIER EVENTS
Dissemination events were organised in Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Poland, Italy, and Greece.

<< Results >>

The YOUNGETEERS project achieved several concrete outputs and results in accordance with its objectives. These results include:

-	The design and testing of a new methodology for training youth workers to manage volunteers in culture during crisis situations.
-	The creation of a manual for volunteer management in culture during crisis situations.
-	An improvement in the quality of youth work in participating organizations, based on the increased competences of the staff.
-	Shared good practices among partners and enhanced cross-sector international collaboration.

These results are aimed at addressing the challenges faced by volunteer programmes due to the COVID-19 pandemic and ensuring their long-term success. The new YOUNGETEERS methodology and manual provide guidance and best practices for managing volunteers in culture during crisis situations, while the increased competences of the participants involved in the project result in improved quality of youth work in participating organizations and their associates.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-HR01-KA227-YOU-094791.title: Digital Creative Writing Communities
2020-1-HR01-KA227-YOU-094791.summary:
<< Background >>

Our consortium got together and applied for this project to address the pressing need for innovative and engaging teaching methodologies that foster critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills among young people. The partners focusing on debate in their youth work noticed they need tool to support creativity and critical thinking rather than uniform expression. 
We set out to bridge the gap between formal and non-formal education, and between creative and IT sectors, by developing open-source, structured resources for teaching creative writing. We sought to empower youth workers with effective tools and methodologies that they could use to inspire their students and enhance learning outcomes. We aimed to develop results that are open to all youth workers, creating cross-sectoral benefits between youth work and formal education. Additionally, we wanted to provide young people, especially those with limited access to creative learning opportunities, with an engaging platform to explore their creativity and improve their skills.
The project was also a response to the increasing need for digital learning tools that are not only functional but also engaging and user-friendly.

<< Objectives >>

Through the implementation of this project, we aimed to achieve the following objectives:
- Develop and disseminate an open-source creative writing teaching methodology suitable for online environments, accommodating both guided and self-directed learning
- Create an implementation toolkit containing literary tools, writing prompts, and other resources that educators can utilize in diverse educational and national contexts
- Design and launch a user-friendly e-learning platform featuring which would engage and motivate young learners
- Support youth workers and other educators in adopting more engaging teaching styles that foster critical thinking, innovative thinking, creative potential, analytical skills, problem-solving skills, and increased comprehension
- Provide young people, particularly those with limited access to creative writing resources, with an opportunity to explore their creativity, improve their skills, and express themselves
- Foster a collaborative network among youth workers, teachers, and IT organizations, promoting the exchange of ideas and best practices
Ultimately, we wanted to enhance the learning experience for young people and contribute to their cognitive and emotional development through creative writing

<< Implementation >>

Creative writing manual - we wrote, edited, adapted and translated the creative writing manual.

Implementation Toolkit - we wrote, tested, edited, adapted and translated a toolkit that includes various ways to facilitate creative writing workshops or integrate creative writing into non-formal or formal education. Based on user feedback, we also developed lessons connecting this content with mental well-being and other aspects we discovered creative writing can be used for. We uploaded and organised this material in OER.

We developed, designed, optimised, tested and published an E-learning site based on O1 and O2 results (startwriting.eu). It can be used as a standalone tool, but it’s best used in a hybrid environment and is supported by additional examples of use and best practices guide.

Staff Training & Youth Mobility: We organized two mobility events that allowed educators and young people to engage with the project materials.
We held 87 workshops and 16 focus groups with young people and educators analyzing needs, use and gathering feedback on our work.

Dissemination: The project outputs were shared widely to reach as many educators and young people as possible, promoting the benefits of creative writing in education.

<< Results >>

Creative Writing Manual: This educational resource is a comprehensive guide for education about creative writing in an online and offline environment. It is modular and adaptable, catering to different learning styles and levels.

E-Learning Platform: We developed an engaging and interactive e-learning platform, startwriting.eu, which features creative writing sessions for beginner and advanced learners. The platform is designed following gamification principles, allowing users to track their progress unlock bonus content and use the tool online and offline.

Implementation Toolkit: This toolkit is an open-resource catalogue of materials that youth workers can use to enhance creativity and engagement in youth work or education. It includes a selection of writing prompts, argumentation exercises, and more and is made available as an OER or PDF. Our materials can be used in various settings and are adaptable to the needs of different learners and topics. Alongside the workshops, we developed various supporting tools that youth workers can use to facilitate the teaching and learning. These tools include analysis guidelines, story-building models, and world-building exercises.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-HR01-KA227-YOU-094793.title: 4-M Storytelling
2020-1-HR01-KA227-YOU-094793.summary:
<< Background >>

Before developing the 4M Storytelling project, Youth Association Varaždin Underground Club (V.U.K.) had three years of experience in involving, connecting, empowering, and positioning young people in political and social processes through arts and creative expression. The main idea was to create a modular method that would convey our experiences, and the experiences of our project partners to young people, youth workers, and various organizations. 

Moreover, we have noticed that cultural and creative sectors are essential in terms of their economic footprint and employment, spurring innovation and making a positive social impact in different fields for youth. Such sectors are composed of non-profit organizations, creative individuals, and micro-firms that are often operating on the margins of financial sustainability. Many of the organizations use arts and culture as a tool for youth work in their local communities, while research confirmed that they lead to a wide range of positive outcomes for youth and children. Research also confirmed that artistic and cultural activities in a community contribute to building local social networks, rather than doing so in a formal, educational form. Therefore we wanted to do everything we can to unleash the full creative and artistic potential of young people.  One way was to use storytelling which was not an innovative method, but we recognized it as an essential part when developing the 4M Storytelling method. 

Based on everything, we have addressed the following needs:

a) Need for organizations working in the cultural and creative sector to empower their capacities through networking, exchange of good practice, and developing innovative solutions in the youth (cultural) work;
b) Need for young people to experience arts and cultural participation, as well as to express themselves creatively.

<< Objectives >>

Objectives were divided in 1) main objective and 2) specific objectives. 
The main objective of the project was to develop the 4-Module Storytelling method as an innovative and creative approach for creative self-expression, networking, social
inclusion, and stronger positioning of young people in political and social processes, through arts and cultural participation based on transnational collaboration and knowledge between partner organizations.

To achieve the main objective, 4 specific objectives were defined: 
1) Capacity building of partner organizations and their representatives by exchanging knowledge and experience that will contribute to the development of 4-M Storytelling;
2) Development of methodology for an online and offline training course for youth (culture) workers;
3) Empowering and supporting youth (culture) workers to develop activities using the 4-M Storytelling method;
4) Promoting arts and cultural participation of young people, interculturalism and social inclusion of young people with fewer opportunities.

<< Implementation >>

Activities were divided into: 
1) 3 Transnational partners meetings - 2 of them were organized in Varaždin, Croatia, 1 was in Austria;
2) 1 Test-It! Learning & Teaching Training in Croatia;
3) Local activities with youth workers and young people to test the 4-M Storytelling method organized and implemented by 7 partner organizations in Austria, Croatia, France, Italy and Slovenia;
4) Multiplier events organized and implemented in Austria, Croatia, Italy and Slovenia;
5) 7 online meetings via Google Meet communication tool. 
6) 1 online training;
7) 8 digital stories were created by 8 partner organizations;
8) 1 innovative educational method developed

<< Results >>

During the project, 5 Working Packages are implemented. 

WP 1 - PROJECT MANAGEMENT
- more than 16 partner representatives strengthened their storytelling skills
- 3 TPMs were held 
- 3 meeting reports were created
- 1 internal project manual developed
- 1 medium-term evaluation report prepared
- more than 6 online partnership meetings related to the course of the project were held
- multiplier events organized (min 200 participants)

WP 2 - DEVELOPING 4-MODULE STORYTELLING METHOD
- 1 online questionnaire was created
- 1 document with researched methodology and practices was created
- 1 working and 1 final version of the document on the innovative educational method were created
- working groups were created (visible also on our digital server on Discord - https://discord.gg/TnkytaNS) 

WP 3 - TEST PHASE
- training methodology (w/ reports) on using the 4-M method created

2020-1-IE01-KA227-SCH-082933.title: Creativity, Critical Thinking, Collaboration & Communication for Schools
2020-1-IE01-KA227-SCH-082933.summary:
<< Background >>

During the crisis of the COVID-19 pandemic, the European cultural and creative sectors were severely impacted; the majority of cultural institutions engage with audiences onsite in close proximity with visitors and participants and therefore ceased to operate during imposed restrictions. The pandemic has also impacted youth and adult populations throughout Europe resulting in the loss of employment as well as a reduction of educational opportunities. The EU 2020 Strategy acknowledged that education and training can help tackle key challenges Europe is currently facing and particularly in light of the current global pandemic. The 4Cs project was launched in response to the need to digitally transform the way in which students are engaged, by supporting teachers and educators to develop skills, reflect on their practice and to evaluate their teaching with students. The project builds competencies for educators and students around the 4Cs of 21st century skills: critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, communication. It is an extension of the Erasmus+ Creative School project through the development of additional opportunities around the areas of competencies, particularly in and around the digital curriculum, and evaluation tools.

<< Objectives >>

The 4Cs project was created in direct response to the first Intellectual Output of the Creative School project and the findings in the initial report. Throughout the duration of the Creative School project, museum, science, arts and heritage professionals, creatives, digital practitioners and makers are encouraged to share good practices; learn from each other; explore ways of engaging with teachers and students in schools in the development of learning resources; as well as disseminate the processes and outcomes. 
Working on the same principles and audiences, the objective of the 4Cs project in three key areas where educators / teachers need support:
- Clear methodologies: educators need to be supported in having concrete and practical methodologies to implement creative activities on critical and creative thinking.
- Developing competences: educators need skills-set (competency framework) based on soft skills or competences students can acquire developing their own creative and critical thinking.
- Support for evaluation: educators do not know how to evaluate students on critical and creative thinking therefore there is a need to develop a methodology for evaluation.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented three main activities::
- Developing a competency framework for teachers, educators and children derived from the 4 Cs of 21st century thinking skills based on the project activities developed during the Creative School.
- Creating and testing a reflective practices toolkit to be used by teachers and educators to help with assessment, professional and curricula development using the CRAFTED methodology (Cross-curricular and inter-disciplinary, Respectful, Adaptable, Flexible, Thinking routines and strategies, Electronic/Digital, Differentiated) for a creative curricula developed in the Creative School project.
- Proposing an evaluation toolkit grounded on research with project participants and based on the Europeana Impact Framework. The cultural heritage sector works for society as a whole, but it is not always easy to see whether the expected objectives are achieved. Undertaking an impact assessment can help participants better understand, assess and present the impact of their activities. This activity introduced impact assessment by introducing the participants to the specific language of impact assessment and help them make strategic choices to guide their way.

<< Results >>

The 4Cs project aims to use creative and innovative methods and tools developed throughout the Creative School and apply them to the evaluation and self-development of learning modules created for children, teachers and educators. More importantly two core ingredients of the aforementioned projects
 the 4Cs project has built upon, are creativity and critical thinking skills for teachers, educators and students in schools. These skills are central in the education and development of students in schools across Europe. The key results achieved by 4Cs project were:
1. Improved capacity of European teachers and educators, and increased creativity in preparing new lessons using the wide educational potential present in European heritage institution.
2. New skills developed through creativity and the arts.
3. Supported digital transformation by engaging with audiences through digital cultural heritage and using creative innovative practices.
4. Developed confidence in intercultural dialogue approaches.
5. Increased awareness of the European teacher’s community and museums professionals on the relevance of teaching pupils how to develop their own creative and critical thinking capacity.

2020-1-IT02-KA227-ADU-095329.title: Building cultural intelligence and raising awareness of diversity through artistic disciplines
2020-1-IT02-KA227-ADU-095329.summary:
<< Background >>

The ACT-IT-OUT partnership took the opportunity of the extraordinary Erasmus for Creativity Call (K227) to face together the problematic framework generated by the pandemic in people in relation with the others. Starting from the key competence for lifelong learning and European citizenship, artistic and cultural expression, we co-designed a targeted path aiming at strengthening cultural intelligence, as a specific competence indispensable for acting consciously in increasingly globalised environments. Investing in cultural intelligence and being able to comprehend and accept differing cultures and their diversity, is one of the keys to success in all areas of our lives. It allows for societal inclusion which is a fundamental component for a just and equitable society.
Some people are culturally intolerant; they view the world through the lens of their own culture, without appreciating the different views and standpoints of other cultural perspectives, without recognizing the added value deriving from dialogue. Cultural intolerance is the root cause of xenophobia, racism and unilateralism, and therefore often leads to regional and global tensions and conflicts.

<< Objectives >>

ACT-IT-OUT aims to support adult learners across Europe to use the artistic disciplines to develop their own cultural intelligence and to promote an appreciation of cultural diversity throughout European society. To achieve this aim, we developed three core intellectual outputs and we worked with our associate partners to develop a project that is relevant and fit-for-purpose.
To offer open educational methods, tools and resources using the disciplines of Photography, Poetry and Performance to be implemented in adult education pathways.
Indirectly, the consortium intends to contribute to overcoming stereotypes and prejudices with respect to people with different origins and cultures, and to concretely commit ACT-IT-OUT partners, as adult education agencies, to combating all forms of discrimination through a creative educational proposal.

<< Implementation >>

In the 3Ps Programme, ACT-IT-OUT partners used the medium of Photography to support adult learners to develop their cognitive awareness of culture – to capture photographs that represent understandings of different cultures, and the support adult learners to develop their own understanding of their own culture and how this impacts their own perspective of the world, and of other cultures.
To address the emotional component, based on the photographs that adult learners take, project partners supported learners to plan and script short poems that aim to capture their feelings and motivations related to cultural issues. Penning these poems also supported adult learners to evaluate their emotional responses to certain aspects of culture, and to self-assess their motivation for developing their cultural intelligence.
Lastly, to address the physical component, adult learners were supported to develop their skills as performers. In the performance resources developed as part of this programme, learners are encouraged to develop their skills to perform the poems that they have written, but also to include actions, gestures and movements that are synonymous with their own culture, and with other cultures.

<< Results >>

Three intellectual outputs:
3Ps Curriculum - Photography, Poetry and Performance - consists of a manual for tutors with lesson plans, a handout for learners, a handout for self-directed learning for both the tutors and the learners. The suite of 36 resources are introduced by short videos in English and subtitled in all partners’ languages. The estimated time of 36 hours of face-to-face or synchronous training can obviously be dilated and sized according to the specific learning objectives and context.
Induction Training Programme for adult educators to support professionals to deliver the 3Ps Programme, and to harness the full potential of the online learning environments. Each of the three modules includes 7 hours of face-to-face setting, and 7 hours of self-directed learning.
MOOC, CoP and OERs: The MOOC includes the 3Ps resources, the Induction Training Programme, the collection of further OERs, and the CoP as sharing space for learners and educators.
The training programmes were piloted in the 7 EU countries involving 154 learners and educators, the two Joint Training Activities engaged 40 participants, and 409 are the registered users on the MOOC. We directly informed 240 participants through the Performance Workshops.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-IT02-KA227-SCH-095493.title: VR@Geoparks
2020-1-IT02-KA227-SCH-095493.summary:
<< Background >>

VR@Geoparks focuses on promoting high-quality school education with the aim of providing teachers with all the knowledge and VR tools needed to demonstrate the benefits of e-learning and represent the situation of awareness and use of different methodologies and tools in school education. The project aimed to create innovative resources for teachers by providing them with the necessary skills to include geoparks as educational hotspots in the school curriculum, as well as acquire an international perspective, practice remote working methods, develop digital skills, create resources based on immersive experiences .
The partnership involved three schools located in areas where there are Geoparks and two Geopark management bodies belonging to the Unesco Global Geopark network. The activities and intellectual outputs of this project provide the opportunity for students and teachers to explore the Geoparks, from different perspectives, giving students endless options for navigating the GeoPark. It also allows teachers to create educational resources using the App as the starting point of their pedagogical planning and dynamics.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to involve as many colleagues, students and staff as possible in the project, so that we can achieve a global approach to our resources, a wider co-working network.
We also aimed at
*improve student learning and engagement in geography, science, history, or literature by offering a deeply immersive sense of place and time;
* create VR and AR resources, teaching materials for teachers as Open Educational Resources (OER);
* sensitize teachers/students about geoparks in the sustainability of life in nature;
*promote inclusive education.
Although virtual reality has been implemented in European schools for a long time, in some of the partner schools it was still little applied. Therefore, during the duration of the project, during the mobility, we gained experience and learned how to use virtual reality tools. With this, we wanted to enrich the daily teaching in our schools with something that we consider very important for the modern and future life of the students. Besides the students, the experience of the teachers has allowed them to be modern teachers in line with the modern achievements of Europe.

<< Implementation >>

We created the project website https://vrgeoparks.eu/ and fb page https://www.facebook.com/vrgeoparks/, Erasmus+ corners, logo competition, promotional products, geoparks club, organized TPM Meetings and LTTA training activities, Final Conference, as well as Project IO 1 Ouputs (Database) IO 2 (Guides) and IO 3 (VR App).
In particular, we have carried out four TPM activities: in Italy, (virtual cause of Covid) in Croatia, in Turkey and in Hungary. In addition, several online meetings for project and activity management.
We carried out three teaching and learning activities for the teachers and staff of the geoparks involved
*Madonie Geopark in Sicily(LTT1)
*Holy Cross Geopark in Poland(LTT2)
*VR activity in Portugal (LTT3).
We learned a lot about the geology, geomorphology, flora, fauna and vegetation of the geoparks involved in the project, actively contributing to the creation of guide materials, app hotspots, lesson plans, games, etc.
In the Final Conference each partner had to present the results of the project and the activities carried out.
After each mobility, surveys and meetings were held in schools, municipalities and with various stakeholders.

<< Results >>

The IO-s of the project have been realised: the VR@Geoparks database, the VR@Geoparks guide (online and printed), the VR@Geoparks app, and further lesson plans and geoactivities also online. We have also edited a brochure in 6 languages to promote and disseminate the results.
Flyers, brochures in several languages, folders, banners, flags, gadgets, PowerPoint presentations, lesson plans, methods of working with students, various teaching materials have been produced. Also:- Zoom online meetings, Facebook page and group, WZ group,- Lesson plans, eTwinning, Twinspace, etc.
During the mobilities in Sicily and Poland the teachers saw firsthand the geological formations with scientific methods in a fun and interesting way. Their awareness and knowledge of the environmental issues and sustainability of the Geoparks has increased. During the activities, all participants focused on cooperative learning (working in teams or with partners), critical thinking and discussion, hands-on activities and action strategies with real-world applications.
After the LTT activities in Portugal, teachers/staff learned how to create virtual reality experiences through the VR@Geoparks app.

2020-1-LV01-KA227-ADU-094488.title: I. We. Society.
2020-1-LV01-KA227-ADU-094488.summary:
<< Background >>

The situation in the project partner countries in 2020 showed that steps needed to be taken to improve the situation with the most vulnerable social groups in all the project partner countries.
The project “I.We.Society” focused on creating digital programs in 6 sectors of adult education using formal, non-formal and informal learning possibilities. The chosen adult education sectors were as follows:
• young not working mothers
• re-immigrants
• young retired people
• disabled people
• young unemployed adults
• young working adults.
All those social groups are the so-called fragile society groups that need special attention. 6 digital courses were created in English consisting of 10 programs. Afterwards, the created programs were translated in 6 native languages of the project partners.

<< Objectives >>

The project " I.We.Society." focused on creating digital online courses with an aim to increase the number of adults participating in the lifelong learning process. The courses address different age and social group audiences:
* not working mothers
* re-immigrating people
* recently retired people
* people with disabilities and low-level competencies
* young not working adults
* young working adults
Some of the groups often have bigger problems with reintegrating into the labor market or society. The aim of the created courses was to raise adults' interest to turn to learning. In many cases digital courses that could be studied remotely assist to that. Besides creating the digital courses the project concentrated on promoting the professional skills of adult educators through sharing their expertise on different adult education themes and offering practical learning materials.

<< Implementation >>

The aim of the project “I.We.Society." was to :
* research the situation with adult learning in the project partner countries
* share expertise on innovative adult teaching methods
* provide help to different groups of society, including the so-called vulnerable groups - people with disabilities, low-level competencies, re-immigrants, young not 
  working adults
* create an online program for adults focussing on the needs of the 6  most vulnerable groups of society. The chosen adult education sectors will be as follows:
* young not working mothers
* re-immigrants
* young retired people
* people with different disabilities and low levels of skills and competences
* young not working people
* young working people
All 6 created digital courses consist of 10 programs and were created in English and then translated into 6 project partner languages. 
There were 6 transnational project meetings, each of them consisting of:
* report on some adult education theme in each country
* analysis of the created digital programs
* seminar for adult educators on a certain theme of adult education.
After every project meeting the partners had 2 tasks:
* to continue work at creating the digital courses
* to create 2 -3 activities on the theme discussed in the seminar.
After the planned courses were created, they were piloted in all the partner organizations. If needed, the courses were improved before publishing them. The project finished with multiplier events in each partner country. Dissemination activities were carried out throughout the whole project implementation time.

<< Results >>

In the framework of the project "I.We.Society," the following outputs were created:
* presentation of the situation with different adult social groups in all the partner countries
* an online training program "i.We.Society." was created consisting of 6 programs and 7 subchapters

2020-1-LV01-KA227-ADU-094532.title: Development of the Entrepreneurial MIND-SET in creative persons
2020-1-LV01-KA227-ADU-094532.summary:
<< Background >>

The COVID-19 pandemic has not only limited the way people can relate to each other and perform their most basic every-day-tasks, but has also had a significant impact on the regular delivery of education, training and youth policies. At such a critical time for our societies, access to quality education is proving, more than ever, to be essential to ensuring a swift recovery, while promoting equal opportunities among people of all backgrounds. 

One of the sectors hit the most by the pandemic were youth and creative industries. The main directions we see creative industries need support:
• to be leaders and initiators
• to be innovative in their creations
• to be ready to face any new unexpected risks and societal challenges
One of the skills that will solve all the above mentioned challenges is Entrepreneurship, which is an absolute "must-have" skill in now days tech-dominated world. Proposal aims not only to give entrepreneurial skill to creators, but actually will focus more on Entrepreneurial MINDSET development.

<< Objectives >>

The OBJECTIVES of the project were:
* Development and implementation of innovative practices of teaching Entrepreneurship MIND-SET to creative and young persons
* Increase sense of initiative and entrepreneurship among all people, especially among Youth and Creative persons;

DIRECT target groups of the project:
* Persons, who are studying or working in creative industries
* Youth and students, especially those who are close to choosing their career paths
* Representatives of education institutions that teach any of creative industries

INDIRECT target groups of the project are:
* Young people, as Entrepreneurial Mind-Set is not only valuable for persons in creative industries, it increases the quality of life of any person
* Society in general

<< Implementation >>

The project has produced a modern asymmetric e-learning course on developing an Entrepreneurial Mind-Set. The course focuses on characteristics the individual should have in
order to be a successful entrepreneur - Decisiveness, Goal setting, Time management, Confidence, Initiative, Accountability, Self Motivation, Resilience, Humility and ability to work in
teams are part, but not all characteristics that the e-learning course modules teach. The advantage of creative and young persons is that they all have some kind of creative skill that can be
used in building own business, but to be successful, they need to have the right mind-set and the developed e-learning course modules will help.

In total 5 interactive e-learning modules were developed: Decisiveness, Confidence, Accountability, Resilience and Humility. Total number of slides for all modules is 241 and being also developed in all partner languages it overall makes 1687 slides.

<< Results >>

* Module #1 - DECIVENESS - ability to take decisions quickly and confidently. One's ability as a decision-maker will make or break it's future successes or at the opposite end, ability not to take decisions usually failure of the intended business. Being decisive takes practice to master and it begins with small decisions in the business of daily life. Subsections developed on GOAL SETTING and PRIORITISATION OF TIME.

* Module #2 - CONFIDENCE - knowing how to act confidently when one actually do not know what should be done. The module will teach to pretend that one knows, what they are doing. There is a difference between looking confident and being confident: "Fake it, until You make it" - it’s not a secret that self-confidence is one of the most powerful characteristics of successful people. It is extremely important in any sphere, place, or circumstance. One should have confident gestures, voice, and behavior, which will have a crucial role on one's way up to success. Subsections of the module are for TAKING AN INITIATIVE and PERSUASION.

* Module #3 - ACCOUNTABILITY - taking responsibility for own actions and outcomes. Everything depends on one's choices, not outside factors or powers. There are no EXCUSES,
one can not blame others in its wrong choices. Subsection of this module is for SELF-MOTIVATION

* Module #4 - RESILIENCE - quality of recovering quickly from failure and adversity. Resilience is about one's ability to learn from its own mistakes and NOT TO BE AFRAID TO
MAKE MISTAKES. Subsections of the module is for TENACITY and FLEXIBILITY.

* Module #5 - HUMILITY - freedom from pride or arrogance and the quality or state of being humble. Along with humility comes coachability — the ability to be coached. If one wants to
accomplish big things in life, one need to be willing to learn from others and nourish a growth mindset.
