2020-1-PL01-KA227-ADU-095748.title: Creative at home
2020-1-PL01-KA227-ADU-095748.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project because we noticed the emerging negative effects of the COVID-19 epidemic on numerous sectors of the economy, most notably on the cultural sector in Europe. The crisis has affected the financial stability of many cult institutions and their sense of security. Many artists and people working in the area of creative industries have lost the opportunity to earn money and have been faced with the challenge of using online tools in their daily work. Our project responded to the need to:
1. Professional and social activation of artists.
2. Helping artists in areas such as: conducting effective artistic classes, commercialization of educational activities in accordance with the principles of solidarity economy, reaching potential recipients, promoting activities or selecting appropriate equipment for issues and situations.
3. Increasing self-esteem and social inclusion of adults belonging to groups at risk of exclusion.
The need for activation was noticed before the start of project activities, which is why we applied for the possibility of its implementation. Although there are now many free tools available on the Internet, we have noticed a lack of a site where they would be collected in one place.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the Creative at home project was to develop an innovative model of online art education for adults who want to develop their creativity, and consequently also their entrepreneurship, and for adults belonging to groups at risk of exclusion. Our project focused on working together to develop tools, materials and solutions to help artists re-activate professionally after the COVID-19 pandemic. By creating a website where we collected free tools for remote work, manuals, lesson plans and tutorials, we responded to the challenges currently faced by artists-educators who want to conduct educational activities online. The tools were created based on cooperation and exchange of experiences between Partners. Thanks to the video recordings and instructions available on the website, we expanded the artists' knowledge of the available creative tools, which in turn led to their professional and social activation. In addition, all participants of the project meetings and trainings developed their interpersonal skills through travels and international workshops. work in
intercultural team was developing and allowed to raise the competences of project participants.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the "Creative at home" project, we have implemented the following activities:

1. We have developed the result of intellectual work in the form of a website: www.creativitycluster.eu on which we have placed:
- 57 online tools in the form of guides in the following categories: video, audio, cooperation, online meetings, ar and vr, presentations, graphics, coordination, screen recording.
- 51 videos on yt with tutorials on online tools,
- 8 videos of site, team, artist training.
- 3 manuals on marketing, selection of tools and online meetings,
- 1 artist research summary.
- workshop scenarios for download from the website.

In addition, we set up a profile on Facebook: www.facebook.com/creativeathomeproject and on YouTube: www.youtube.com/channel/UCQQCSA1dNO8gxY_s58YtHvg

2. We organized international project meetings in:
- Poland: November 25-28, 2021.
- Spain: May 23-26, 2022
- Croatia: August 29-September 1, 2022
- Greece: 21-24/11/2022
3. We organized a training for artists in Bologna, Italy on September 19-23, 2022.
4. We organized dissemination events:
SPAIN - 04/21/23
GREECE - 24.04 and 03.05.23
CROATIA - 09.05.23
ITALY - 09.05 and 26.05.23
POLAND - 23.05.23

<< Results >>

During the project:
1. a strong partnership of five organizations from Poland, Italy, Spain, Croatia and Greece was built, thanks to which members (employees and volunteers) had a chance to develop their digital and language competences, learned new methods of working with artists, using free online tools for video , audio, cooperation, online meetings, ar and vr, presentations, graphics or coordination.
2. an interactive creativity toolkit was created, which consists of: a website containing a compendium of knowledge, links to tools and applications, a methodology for conducting art classes for adults online and tutorials.
3. workshops and discussions were held, which led to deeper reflection on the most important aspects of remote art education.
4. 4 international meetings were held
5. we exchanged experiences and strengthened ties between our organizations as well as established lasting partnerships by organizing an international training for artists in Bologna in September 2022. Artist-educators tested the developed tools and methodologies of online work,
6. we organized 5 dissemination events.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-PL01-KA227-ADU-095915.title: Culturavirus - the art of new communities
2020-1-PL01-KA227-ADU-095915.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was intended to support the three partner organizations, as well as local communities, to function in times of crisis (caused mainly by the pandemic) using community arts methods and new technologies. The pandemic made access to the community difficult, the acquisition of knowledge and skills among staff was limited - hence responding to difficult situations - previously unheard of and unknown, and working with the community became a challenge itself. In our organizations, we saw how strongly isolation, fear and uncertainty, less activity among residents, but also volunteers, affected us. We knew that it was culture, especially the community arts track, that would be able to help us rebuild communities. The project was to bring together three cultural organizations, their strengths and advantages - not in the spirit of complaining about the situation, but rather sharing best solutions in the area of cooperation and adult learning. We wanted to inspire the project participants to develop, test and experiment in the area of their organizations and culture. The need for this project that Coronavirus outlined was supplemented by new conditions - the war in Ukraine and migration.

<< Objectives >>

Through the implemented mobilities, we wanted to integrate community arts methods and tools into the daily work of educators and employees of our organizations. The project was designed to:
- develop knowledge and skills in public participation and tools used in engaging adults, and transfer them to local communities,
- equip teams with digital skills, but also cultural and language skills,
- develop skills to work with other cultures, in a diverse work environment,
- build the capacity of organizations and individuals to manage international cooperation projects and at the same time support the local community, including the arts,
- integrate artists, leaders and volunteers around an organization, so that they can better plan their development and identify needs, learn from experience,
- support the creative and organizational competencies of local artists, activists, so that they are able to work effectively with adults and build lasting relationships,
- learn examples of grassroots cultural initiatives, as well as the specifics of how local communities function,
- disseminate the ABCD model - to work within the community more on resources and less on needs.

<< Implementation >>

- we organized 3 mobility programs,
- we organized a total of 20+ visits to other local organizations that build the capacity of the entire district and carry out activities for adults - we were able to see in practice how to effectively reach them
- we learned about the effects of local artists working in the spirit of community arts 
- we organized a workshop on engaging the community in activities - how to communicate, fundraising, practical aspects of working with adults, etc.
- we organized a workshop on values and the ABCD method,
- we organized cross-cultural walks in the area where partner organizations operate, including with the participation of residents, as Migrantour,
- we exchanged experiences related to the functioning of our organizations in the digital world - we organized an online workshop on the use of technology in our organizations, 
- we strengthened the organizational competencies and motivation of our project participants by involving them in the preparation of visits and workshops in their country and informing them about the Erasmus+ program 
- we disseminated the knowledge gained in our organizations through evaluation meetings with other staff.

<< Results >>

Our project produced a number of products that we share as inspiration for other individuals and organizations:
- 3 five-day mobility programs - we put the programs in so-called infopacks, which served as a source of knowledge about mobility for all participants.
- 4 newsletters with information about the organizations and their projects that we got to know during the Culturavirus project - each time the newsletter was distributed to all participants after the mobility and one final one addressed to all people participating in the project
- 16 videos of the project summarizing each day of the project and a final video of the entire project
- album with selected photos from the project
- template of online evaluation questionnaire
- template of the agreement with the participant (not obligatory for projects of this type) 
- a website with information about the project, participating organizations, etc.  
- publications in the social media of our organizations.
The results of the Culturavirus project are visible in our organizations. Most importantly, our project has resulted in our organizations being enriched with leaders with new organizational, cultural and linguistic competencies that they gained in the project.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-PL01-KA227-SCH-095251.title: Creative Vibs
2020-1-PL01-KA227-SCH-095251.summary:
<< Background >>

The 'Creative Vibrations' project was designed to show that in an interesting way, through attractive forms and methods of teaching, such competences as creativity and cultural awareness, which are important in today's world, can be shaped as life skills. We believe that shaping attitudes such as creativity and cultural awareness will contribute to the development of pupils' specific skills, which will have an impact on their self-realisation throughout their lives. Creativity seems to be very important today, as it will make pupils more open to new experiences, respectful of their colleagues at school, or more independent in planning and carrying out their professional work later in life. Creativity is a human characteristic that each of us is born with, and it is the school's task to shape it in such a way that it becomes a life attitude, thanks to which pupils will think creatively and creatively, to think creatively and creatively, to solve problems, to be open to new ideas and at the same time to be aware that they may be criticised. By participating in the project, we wanted the participating organisations to be seen as modern, developing organisations, looking for new solutions in working with students.

<< Objectives >>

The main aim of our project was to foster creativity and innovation through art. Creativity nowadays is not only about thinking outside the box, it is also about facing problems, making changes and often taking risks. Creativity goes hand in hand with innovation, because whoever is creative is also innovative. Education through the arts is an excellent way of fostering creativity and innovation. Performance, film and performance seem to be attractive tools to achieve the main goal of the project. In the modern school, film and theatre are important educational tools. Used skilfully, they contribute greatly to modernising the teaching-learning process. The changes taking place in education should take film and theatre into account, as it is not only a useful didactic tool, but also an important cultural text that is attractive to young people. Through the implementation of the project together with a cultural institution, the teachers wanted to learn about methods and forms of working with pupils from the arts in the broadest sense of the term, which could be used in their work with pupils, which would increase pupils' motivation to work, develop their passions and interests regarding the arts and develop creativity and innovation.

<< Implementation >>

The project carried out 5 short-term pupil exchanges in each partner country. The theme of each exchange was a different art form, namely theatre, film, photography and stop-motion animation, music and film. During each mobility trip, students developed their creativity through a different art form. The theme of the mobility in Poland was: Shaping students' creativity through theatre. The theme of the mobility in Greece was: Shaping pupils' creativity through film. The topic of mobility in Italy was: Shaping pupils' creativity through dance. The theme of mobility in Croatia was: Shaping pupils' creativity through photography and stop-motion animation. The theme of the mobility in Portugal was: Shaping pupils' creativity through music. The project also included 3 short-term training programmes and 1 short-term online training programme during which staff from cultural institutions provided training in methods and forms used in the arts in youth work. Staff from cultural institutions also supported the workshop activities conducted for pupils during the short-term pupil exchanges.

<< Results >>

The project's material results include theatrical performances created by the participants, short films, virtual walks, stop-motion animation, music concerts and dance performances. Teachers from the schools were able to exchange experiences, get to know how a cultural institution works and what methods and forms its employees use. In the project, working methods and forms of work will be developed that can be transferred to school work in the future. Through participation in the project, pupils have improved their key competences, which will enable them to be more effective on the labour market in future, and the school and cultural institution have gained more prestige in the local community. The project has made it possible to establish lasting contacts with cultural institutions and to exchange experiences, which in future will contribute to a greater shaping of pupils' creativity in schools through the methods and work they have learnt in the arts.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2020-1-PL01-KA227-SCH-095438.title: Art Rallies Together Internationally with Students and Teachers
2020-1-PL01-KA227-SCH-095438.summary:
<< Background >>

We have been struggling with Covid 19 all over the world. In most countries, schools closed and we started teaching online. In our schools, we noticed that our students quickly lost interest and focus in online lessons. And this brought students failure in school. It became really difficult to return to class when students felt unhappy and lost. For most of the students, this was a completely new experience and they encountered many difficulties. Some people didn't like it, some didn't want to accept it, but distance learning was inevitable at that time. The problem continued for many months. Students and teachers were often required to wear masks to class and this was inconvenient and art students could be the most affected as they require implementation and practice. They need face-to-face communication. And if they don't have that chance, they feel left out. Thanks to this project, we experienced open and remote learning, so art crossed the walls of the school. The implementation of the project helped the students of our schools to return to normal functioning in the school space.

<< Objectives >>

As part of our project, we wanted to try open and distance learning in the field of art. We wanted to turn the difficulties related to the pandemic to our advantage through open-space classes and effective distance learning. Visual arts students don't need walls to study. If they need walls, they need them to paint on them! Through the implementation of the project, we wanted to:
- show students the riches of European artistic culture
- increase students' self-confidence
- enhance students' artistic experience
- give participating teachers a chance to interact with different artistic cultures
- encourage and motivate students to use the arts as a means of social, cultural, economic, political and historical knowledge of their own country as well as partner countries, in order to expand the space where they should feel valued
- develop language and artistic skills through artistic implementation activities in order to avoid school failure
- develop creativity, communication and promote teamwork through international activities to stop discrimination
- to diversify teaching-learning methods of the art through a practical-experimental and active-interactive approach.

<< Implementation >>

We have delivered effective and exciting art lessons. Our students saw various good practices in the open space and had the opportunity to experience them with art educators and painters. This increased their imagination and creativity. Implementing this project internationally provided participants with a good and fun learning experience. Before the trips, the partners held on-line meetings. The host country was in charge of the distance learning meetings. Its teachers and artists provided the necessary theoretical information to all participants. And the participants watched some art lessons online before the mobilities.
Main activities
Poland (Gliwice): created a WhatsApp group for good communication, project website, "Gilding technique" class;
Turkey: "Arts of marbling", opened an Instagram account of the project and shared the works;
Croatia: "Gothic Art", preparation of the YouTube channel ARTIST, preparation of evaluation surveys;
Poland (Gdańsk): "Photography activities", preparing an album with design works, filming and sharing the works
Italy: "Pencil drawing", evaluation surveys;
Sweden: "Oil Paintings", an exhibition of paintings.

<< Results >>

The results at the project level were closely related to the proposed objectives and activities. As a result, students were encouraged and motivated to use visual arts as a means of expanding social, cultural, economic, political, historical knowledge about their own country as well as about partner countries in order to expand the space where they feel valued. The project also aimed to prevent school dropout and school failure by conducting inclusive educational activities aimed at developing social, artistic and digital skills. Another result of the project was a reduction in the number of students leaving school and the failure rate in the implementation of inclusive educational activities aimed at developing artistic and digital skills in order to encourage students to come to school. The creativity of the participating students, communication skills and teamwork were successfully realized. Various products have been developed, such as: banners, posters, drawings, paintings, art exhibitions, videos, photo albums, surveys. The implementation of the project also translated into the knowledge gained by the participants during the mobility.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2020-1-PT02-KA227-YOU-007634.title: Our Emotions Are the Same: Inclusion Through Art
2020-1-PT02-KA227-YOU-007634.summary:
<< Background >>

In the formal education system, there is still an excess of measuring the rational intelligence of young people through quantitative data, ignoring the emotional coefficient and, therefore, the socio-emotional capacities of young people, contributing to youth social exclusion, especially in those who have fewer opportunities. Thus, this project intended to promote social inclusion, intercultural dialogue and the empowerment of young people through activities to promote self-knowledge and self-regulation of their own emotions.

NEEDS
1. Creation and/or reinforcement of alternative and innovative methods and tools for the development of socio-emotional skills in young people, complementing their training in areas where formal educational systems reveal gaps;
2. Development and sharing of good practices in the field of socio-emotional empowerment of young people with the aim of enhancing emotional intelligence and acceptance of diversity, thus contributing to social inclusion;
3. Creation and/or development of cooperation networks between bodies active in the field of art and/or NFE for the implementation of joint initiatives aimed at promoting social inclusion and empowerment of young people.

<< Objectives >>

General:
Promoting social inclusion, equal opportunities and the empowerment of young people, through self-knowledge and emotion regulation activities with dance-inspired methodologies, complementary to those employed by formal education systems.

Specifics:
1. Enhance intercultural dialogue and promote tolerance and acceptance of diversity, namely through activities that make it possible to know one's emotions and recognize them in others;
2. Boosting the creative and artistic spirit of young people through methodologies inspired by dance and activities foreseeing an artistic product (photographic self-portrait);
3. Contribute to the quality and recognition of youth work through the sharing of good practices, focusing on the planned Training Course;
4. Create and/or strengthen collaboration networks between organizations active in the field of art, social inclusion and non-formal education;
4. Increase the capacity of organizations (and their technicians) to operate at a transnational level and to carry out joint initiatives aimed at promoting participatory, alternative and attractive learning methods.

<< Implementation >>

1. Conception, management and preparation: regular project management and coordination activities;
2. Transnational Meetings (3): face-to-face management, coordination and content creation meetings held in partner countries;
3. Training Course: competence development activity aimed at youth technicians;
4. Local events: activities developed locally by each organization, based on the close relationship between the organizations (and their educational agents) and the young people who are part of our target group;
5. Blended Mobility: competence development activity aimed at young people;
6.Local Dissemination Events (two, one approximately in the middle and another at the end): presentation to the local community of the work carried out throughout the entire project. In the final event, after the local sessions, the objective is to present the work carried out in terms of self-portraits;
8. Monitoring and evaluation: regular monitoring and evaluation activities.

<< Results >>

TANGIBLE
-News;
-E-Book w/ methodology;
-Photos;
-Monitoring reports.

INTANGIBLE ASSETS
- Participatory methodology for the socio-emotional development of young people, which can be adjusted to different territories and social contexts;
- Development of the capacity of organizations to conceive and implement projects and initiatives at national and/or transnational level;
- Development of networks between participating organizations and stakeholders;
- Training of youth technicians w/compet. crucial to improve your intervention;
- Training of young participants with key skills for their integral development:
-Personal, social and learning to learn: improvement in the ability to reflect on oneself, to relate and collaborate with others;
-Cultural sensitivity and expression: due to methodologies inspired by dance and recognition and respect for different cultures;
-Citizenship: through interaction with other young Europeans, carried out in a safe environment;
-Literacy and multilingual: ability to communicate and interact effectively with others in the mother tongue and a foreign language;
-Entrepreneurship: increasing creative and critical thinking skills and transferring ideas to action.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Quality and innovation of youth work

2020-1-RO01-KA227-SCH-095699.title: LITTLE ARTISTS ACROSS EUROPE
2020-1-RO01-KA227-SCH-095699.summary:
<< Background >>

The project idea came when implementing the educational project "The colourful world of Emotions", which focused on extracurricular activities, including art activities that contribute to the personal development of preschoolers, addressing the socio-emotional side of their evolution. Noticing the impact such a small project had on children and their enthusiasm, we decided to develop it into a larger Erasmus+ project on arts and their potential to stimulate children’s creativity. All the partners involved carried out a SWOT analysis regarding the place of arts in the National Curriculum and in their schools. The conclusions were that the negative aspects (teachers not sufficiently qualified; insufficient funding and material resources; insufficient participation of parents or lack of interest; insufficient number of teachers etc.) can be overcome by taking advantage of the opportunities offered by an international partnership and valuing the strengths of each institution involved: training teachers, introducing extra curriculum artistic and cultural activities like dancing, singing, literature and drama, visual arts, foreign languages; organizing events for children such as contests, exhibitions, shows, introducing ICT innovations etc.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we aimed to achieve the OBJECTIVES:
-to develop children's creativity, aesthetic sensibility and interest in cultural activities, their social and emotional skills, communication skills, problem-solving skills;
-to improve the partners’ institutional ability to involve kids in artistic activities, by jointly identifying innovative methods of teaching and practicing arts, but also to get the local community and cultural organizations involved in the school activities;
-to experiment best practices from different educational systems and to introduce new approaches of organizing the educational process;
-to develop the teachers’ ability to have a more creative approach in their teaching activities by integrating art elements and digital tools;
Through the project, we aimed at identifying techniques, methods and best practice approaches that all the partner institutions can apply successfully.
Particularly important was to stimulate European cohesion between children, teachers and communities.The cooperation of educational institutions with different systems of education and the contribution of each school through sharing expertise and generating of new ideas respectively leads to innovation in education.

<< Implementation >>

In order to stimulate children's creativity by means of ARTS during our 2-year project, we grouped our activities as it follows: MUSIC and DANCE, VISUAL ART ACTIVITIES during the first project year, LITERATURE AND THEATRE during the second project year. 
During the first project year, the children and teachers got involved in activities such as: music activities based on the Orff method, discovering other countries' traditional dances, visual arts activities (drawing, painting, modelling, paper mache, quilling, origami), modern dance activities. 
During the second year, we concentrated our activities on children's literature and theatre. We began by studying each month a story written by a writer from the countries involved in the project and we ended by proposing our children to become writers themselves and create a story or a fairytale. The result was a collection of original stories created by children and also illustrated with their drawings.
The teachers involved developed their skills and their capacity to include art and digital tools in the educational process, the training activities for the teachers (webinars, workshops, experience exchanges, training courses) helping them enrich their knowledge and cultural horizon.

<< Results >>

The project results were:
-the project website;
-"Erasmus corner" in every partner institution;
-the project logo;
-Musical and art contests;
-A 2023 calendar with images taken during the project implementation aiming to promote the project to the local community and raise its visibility.
-Presentations of the recorded dance activities and also of the musical activities specific to each partner institution;
-Exhibitions organized in the partner institutions/ public institutions displaying different visual art techniques;
-Art catalogue displaying children's works of art.
-Theater performances;
-best practice methodological guide on techniques used in visual arts activities "PRACTICE MAKES PERFECT";
-DVD: “International Collection of Traditional Dance and Music”
-Multilingual dictionary for children which was conceived as a collection of daily words and phrases in all the national languages of the partners accompanied by an illustrative picture;
- "Stories for children" - a collection of stories created and illustrated by the children;
- the project newspaper "News from the Colorful World of Art";
- exhibitions of drawings/paintings representing aspects from the studied stories;
-eTwinning project based on our Erasmus+ project;

2020-1-RS01-KA227-YOU-094560.title: The Melting Pot
2020-1-RS01-KA227-YOU-094560.summary:
<< Background >>

Cultural institutions are reporting that youth are less interested in the offer of the traditional cultural content. According to the Eurostat, 94% of youth in the EU-27 made daily use of the internet, and 92% of youth used mobile phones for that purpose. Cultural institutions need to follow the development of technology and create interactive methods and approaches in presenting cultural content to young people. Partners considered the recommendations from the EACEA final report "Access of young people to culture" where it's emphasized that access and participation are the key elements for ensuring the cultural rights of young people, therefore, it is recommended to “take into consideration the non-users, through surveys, contacts with communities and NGOs. Analyse the reasons for not coming, and what it would require bringing different audiences to the institution. The use of new technologies, non-formal educational programs and volunteer activities may help to engage them. Equip staff with the expertise and skills to manage cultural diversity and intercultural dialogue. This may require the setting up of training and discussions also in networks and partnerships with other cultural and academic institutions and with NGOs, etc."

<< Objectives >>

The partnership overall aim was to bring cultural institutions closer to all young people through youth work programs by applying interactive, innovative methods and tools, as well as create preconditions for the professionalism of youth workers and employees in cultural institutions.
Specifically:
 - To increase visibility and recognition of youth work and cultural institutions’ potential to respond to the identified needs of various youth groups at local, national, regional and EU level.
- To raise the quality of youth work across the region by introducing innovative and creative methods integrated into culture and arts programs. 
- To increase the professionalism of youth workers and employees in cultural institutions by creating curricula for their education. 
- To establish cross-sectoral cooperation among youth workers and cultural institutions at the national and regional 

<< Implementation >>

3 national and 1 comparative research on the needs of various youth groups related to culture conducted in 3 countries involving 567 youth (284 with less opportunities).
Curricula for education of youth workers in cultural institutions and 6 youth work programs applicable in various cultural institutions were developed.
3 youth work programs, lasting 4 months, involving 60 youth conducted in cultural institutions by 6 youth and cultural workers from 3 countries.
Booklet containing 51 innovative and creative methods used in cultural activities for various youth groups, reflecting Croatian, Serbian, Macedonian and EU level. 
Study visit in Serbia for 12 youth workers and cultural institutions representatives.
National events organised in 3 countries involving 37 journalists from national, regional and local media and 68 youth, youth workers and cultural workers . 
Regional conference in Croatia, organised for 30 youth workers, various cultural institutions and authorities from regional and national level, from 3 countries.
Visibility and promotional actions reaching youth workers from 164 organisations and 50 cultural institutions from 3 countries and up to 218.000 people of the wider public.

<< Results >>

Detailed insight into the answers of way youth does not participate in cultural activities, as well as insight into possible approaches and appropriate methods to change the situation. Collected regional and EU innovative methods enriched the capacity of youth workers and employees in cultural institutions and resulted in quality provision of services for youth. Created Curricula and 6 Youth Work programs increased professionalism of youth and cultural workers. 7 multiplying events raised awareness of relevant stakeholders (youth from fever opportunities, youth and cultural workers, decision makers and journalist) at national and regional level about importance of investing in youth work services in cultural institutions and its positive implication on youth development. Journalists motivated to report about youth, youth work and culture at the national and regional level. Study visit to Serbia built capacity of 12 youth workers and cultural institutions by gaining knowledge and new insights about innovative good practices applicable for creation of youth work programs in cultural institutions. Laid foundation for fruitful cross-sectoral cooperation among youth workers and cultural institutions at national and regional level.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-SI01-KA227-ADU-093594.title: OPEN HANDS: With Tradition into Modernity
2020-1-SI01-KA227-ADU-093594.summary:
<< Background >>

The partners of the Open Hands project decided to apply as a response to the crisis of the COVID 19 epidemic, which had consequences for the actions of all organizations. The central goal of our project was to show that art and creativity, even in the best times of crisis, represent an opportunity, inspiration and motivation for creation, as well as a stimulus for various forms of education and networking. Before applying for the project, due to the restrictions of the epidemic, our partners were faced with the cancellation of the activities of implementing informal education programs for adult minority members and learning adults in the field of culture and art. We faced limited access to minority and artistic content, a reduction in the number of educational workshops, a reduction in financial resources and the cancellation of cultural and artistic activities of our participants. The consequences were felt most by our participants, as they were denied education, artistic creation and socializing, which is essential for their social inclusion. We addressed the need for skills development and social inclusion through creativity and art. Specifically, we celebrated cultural differences, social differences and geographical distance.

<< Objectives >>

With their knowledge and experience related to (minority) cultural heritage and contemporary art, each organization contributed to the realization of the following project goals: 
- the implementation of an educational process in the minority cultural heritage and contemporary art, which included flexible approaches to the education of adult minority members, based on the exchange of good practices of partner organizations, 
- the implementation of international staff training activities in Serbia and Slovenia and the implementation of the mobility of adult learners in Croatia Open Hands, 
- Art Colony Erasmus Istra 2022, the creation of the final online gallery Open Hands and the creation of the online publication Catalog of Creativity, 
- the active involvement of at least 9 educators and 30 adult learners, to improve the use of online tools and creative-artistic content in teaching and improve the knowledge, skills and competences of the target groups for more effective use of cultural, educational and economic opportunities on the labour market, 
- developing an international minority-cultural partnership of various organizations from Slovenia, Croatia and Serbia to improve the quality of work in non-formal adult education.

<< Implementation >>

To achieve the project goals, we carried out various activities that contributed to the successful exchange of good practices between partner organizations. For successful coordination of project activities, we held two international project meetings (Zagreb and Tavankut), and for quality exchange of good practices, three learning, teaching and training activities. The first two (Tavankut and Prebold) were intended for educational staff, who exchanged different work methodologies in simulated learning processes and strengthened creative, digital, entrepreneurial and civic skills, emphasising intercultural dialogue. The third was the mixed mobility of learning adults at Erasmus Istra Art Colony, through which we strengthened the knowledge and skills of members of minorities and other learning adults. We have created a trilingual website for the project, which contains vital information about the project, project activities and results, and the Oprte roke gallery and the online publication Catalog of Creativity. In addition, we implemented local teaching processes based on the exchange of good practices. For dissemination, we produced unique artistic postcards and art products and organized a one-month exhibition in Izola.

<< Results >>

The products of the project are a trilingual website, unique art products, an online gallery Open Hands, a bilingual online publication Catalog of Creativity and several types of unique promotional postcards. The results of the project are the successful exchange of good practices between partners, strengthened international cooperation, which resulted in the implementation of new projects (Young wEKO and Protect your diversity), implementation of all planned project activities, increased participation in all teaching activities (a total of 49 of the planned 36 participants), a new learning programs of the applicant, with innovative digital tools (3D environments, 360-degree films, online classroom), several educational workshops conducted at all, the introduction of additional capacities (place) for work at the Croatian partner, increased cultural tourism visits and sale of unique handicrafts of the Serbian partner, enhanced competence of the participants and organizational skills of the partners. We also highlight the remarkable media response to the project, strengthened dialogue with decision-makers and experts at the local and national levels, and the impacts that are most evident on the participants and organizations.

2020-1-SI01-KA227-ADU-093635.title: creICTivity
2020-1-SI01-KA227-ADU-093635.summary:
<< Background >>

The partners share interest in creativity in education and saw its potential in ICT education. At the same time, we wanted to offer a new and more ambitious approach to ICT education of adults to take advantage of the fact that everybody is creative on some level.
We wished to address 3 needs of adult education.:
- Increase the visibility of creativity in adult education and knowledge of educators about its benefits education 
- Provide adult educators with methodological support to foster creativity of their students
- Provide educators and students a creativity based alternative to education of low ICT-skilled adults to address the problem of large digital gap in Europe

By addressing this needs we wanted to improve the learning outcomes od low ICT-skilled adults as practice and experience consistently shows that traditional ICT courses don’t provide them with lasting practical knowledge. We believe that by fostering creativity and engaging their higrer level thinking processes will make them better students with better results and knowledge retention.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to bring creativity to the attention of the adult educators and to describe it in an understandable and practical way. Ultimately we anted to motivate the adult educators to foster creativity as a skill that can be learned and improved and that supports learning of ICT but also problem solving and ctitical thinking. 
We also wanted to increase the ability of adult educators to foster creativity of their students in practice by providing them with didactical and methodological support. 
Finally, we wanted to to address the obstacles that adults face when learning to us ICT and give the students and the teachers an alternative and highly engaging educational approach to address the problem of digital gap in Europe. Additional goal was to increase the creative and learning potential of adult learners with low ICT skills. They are often poorly equipped with skills for learning and by incrising their ability to understand the topic of education, to reflect on their own abilities and to critically examine the ways to reach solutions, their overall ability to learn and be more independent thinking will increase.

<< Implementation >>

Project management included financial monitoring and project progress monitoring, communication among partners and with stakeholders and evaluation activities.

- 6 TPMs were organized, 5 in person and 1 (kick-of) as on-line meeting due to covid 19
- 5 design thinking workshops were implemented to better understand characteristics of the target groups and the attitude of ICT mentors towards creativity and ICT education.
- 1 LTTA was organised in Germany 
- 5 pilot rainings were organized in each partner countries except Turkey to test the creICTivity methodology and approach and to test the structure of ICT modules.
- 5 multiplier events were organised for dissemination of the project results among stakeholders.
- Dissemination activities were conducted via different channels to reach the stakeholders that could not be reached in-person.

<< Results >>

2 intellectual outputs
1 Using creativity to support adults in ICT education - Teaching methodology for adult educators. This is the theoretical part, presenting creativity and its use in ICT education.
2 creICTivity learning modules and creativity enhancing games and Design thinking workshop guidebook. This part contains ICT learning modules, creativity enhancing games and various tips for educators. Added also isesign thinking workshop guidebook.
12 adult educators participated in the project as ICT mentors (2 from Slovenia, Poland, Croatia and Spain and 4 from Germany) and are able to use the creICTivity project results for ICT education.
58 vulnerable adults with low ICT skills participated in the project and have improved their ICT skills and their ability to bettery analyse ICT cghallenges.
4 Newsletters were created and published all partner languages.
At least 500 stakeholders were reached through various communication channels.
Project logo and visbility scheme was created.
Evaluation report prepared.
Project Facebook profile created and active.

2020-1-SI02-KA227-YOU-015867.title: Webbing theatre
2020-1-SI02-KA227-YOU-015867.summary:
<< Background >>

In the years 2020-2022, the epidemic of the new corona virus made a big impact on the lives of all people. Theater activities and activism, which are based on live contact, community building and solidarity, socializing and cooperation, were among the most affected areas. Before starting the project, we asked ourselves "How to proceed?" We searched for and found the answer during the Webbing Theatre project - by transferring the practice to the web.

Since we were aware that techniques that have been developed for thousands of years in live contact cannot be easily digitized by simply placing them in front of a web camera, during the project we had time for in-depth consideration, an experimental, so to speak laboratory approach and an exchange of different opinions, approaches and experiences on how to make theater work online and keep it in contact with young people and youth workers.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project was to create an international and diverse community of multipliers, youth workers, who primarily work as activists and theater practitioners, who use the theater of the oppressed in their work with young people, and young people who participated in online activities (workshops, festivals, performances) equip with competences:
- critical thinking,
- proactive civic attitudes,
- creative expression and
- social engagement.
Together, we shook up and developed new methods of operation and forms of artistic expression, which enabled fruitful and relevant operation even in the changed circumstances in which we found ourselves.

Addressing such global problems also required a global understanding of reality, so the international nature of the project was necessary for the exchange of opinions and views, experiences and approaches. At the same time, it was necessary to draw attention to the listed topics in the widest possible context, at the international level and at the EU level (gender equality, environmental protection, social inclusion, non-discrimination, active citizenship...).

<< Implementation >>

During the project, we carried out the following activities:
- regular national (local) and international meetings in participating organizations and between partner organizations,
- national online theater workshops, laboratories, seminars,
- international online workshops as part of the international theater festival,
- international online theater festival Gledališče splet (performances and workshops),
- the Webbing Theater manual in four languages (Slovenian, English, Croatian, German),
- partner meetings in each of the partner countries,
- dissemination of the manual through online channels and addresses of individual partner organizations,
- online regular meetings of the international team,
- the international multiplication event From Webbing theater to the Theater of Relationships,
- current and final evaluation and planning of operations and, above all, cooperation in the future.

<< Results >>

The results of the Webbing Theater project are:
1) Preparation, translation, design and dissemination of the Theater of Intrigues manual (online use of GZ techniques - instructions for exercises and short video exercises).
2) Created a community of young activists/artists and youth workers who used theater methodology online with young people.
3) Around 12 youth workers as primary beneficiaries, who have expanded and developed their skills in facilitating theater techniques oppressed online among young people or other youth workers.
  4) Around 150 secondary beneficiaries (young workers who attended the online festival and performances as visitors), who became part of the dialogue about pressing social issues at performances or workshops through theatrical and activist methods.
5) A developed training program for youth workers in the theater of the oppressed online as a form of youth work, collected in a solid handbook.
6) An increased proportion of young men and women workers who participated in activist-theatre practices in the local, national and international environment online.
7) In-depth cooperation at the local and national level from the point of view of each partner organization.

2020-1-SK02-KA227-YOU-002746.title: Too RecyCOOL for School
2020-1-SK02-KA227-YOU-002746.summary:
<< Background >>

We recognized the critical need to develop resources for non-formal education, catering to the interests of youth seeking materials for their free time, home schooling and as support materials for lockdowns.

We aimed to heighten awareness among the youth about the far-reaching impact of the fashion industry on the environment and society. By exploring the entire value chain, from production to consumption and textile waste, we aimed to cultivate conscientious practices among the youth.

We provided edu materials: based on the requirements of young people, educators, and youth workers.

We bridged the gap with formal education: the void in formal edu settings concerning the fashion industry, our project contributed to filling this gap, offering valuable resources to enhance existing curricula.

We empowered educators and youth workers: to equip colleagues in the field of education and youth work with specialised materials, empowering them to effectively incorporate fashion industry education into their professional practices.

Through innovative approaches such as video lessons, we made learning from home attractive and convenient for young learners, maximising the project's impact on youth empowerment and sustainable practices.

<< Objectives >>

1. Develop edu materials: The primary focus was to create relevant and up-to-date educational materials on the fashion industry. These resources were intended to benefit both formal and non-formal edu settings, enriching the learning experiences of youth.

2. Foster collaboration with youth: Collaborating with young people, including Star Teams within Fashion Revolution teams, was a key goal, while responding to their request for understandable edu materials.

3. Educate young participants in project methodology: An important objective was to educate the young participants about the methodologies employed during the project. The aim was to inspire and equip them with valuable skills, motivating them to use these methodologies in their future careers.

4. Synchronise methodologies among experts: The project focused on educating and synchronising methodologies used by all experts involved. This cohesive approach aimed to expand their knowledge, expertise, and collaborative experience.

5. Strengthen partnerships and relationships: Building strong partnerships and fostering relationships among project partners. This collaborative approach aimed to create a foundation for future collab, promoting ongoing cooperation and mutual growth.

<< Implementation >>

1. Workshops on methodology: to harmonise methodologies and lesson creation processes. Topics, formal education subjects, and lesson structures were decided to ensure unified outcomes.

2. Methodology development and testing outcomes: methodologies were created, implemented, and tested on diverse youth groups across different countries and education systems, ensuring comprehensive evaluations.

3. Seminar in Bratislava in May 2022: a significant meeting brought all partners together, focusing on video lessons' structure and guidelines for their creation.

4. Transnational meetings: regular gatherings provided a platform for teams to collaborate, discuss progress, and plan future activities.

5. Multiplier events: each partner hosted events to promote and disseminate project outcomes.

6. Project team meetings: regular meetings ensured progress tracking, workload management, and overall team cohesion.

7. Project management team meetings: project managers convened to coordinate efforts and facilitate smooth execution.

8. Constant communication: communication via email and Slack maintained transparent progress updates and task planning.

9. Project website: a dedicated website was developed to showcase and upload final outcomes.

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs:
LESSONS
- 50 text lessons about fashion industry
- 50 video lessons based on those text lessons
- Methodology on how to educate these lessons for hearing impaired target groups

Other outputs:
TEAM - PEOPLE
- More experienced young people (Star Teams) within fields of project, from participation in creating content and visual of lessons, their testing, and in some teams even with project management
- More educated and experienced experts who participated in project
- More experienced team members with work within Erasmus+ project, including development of managerial skills of project managers
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-TR01-KA227-ADU-098764.title: New e-Artistic English Learning Approach for Adults
2020-1-TR01-KA227-ADU-098764.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was prepared by taking into account the quarantine practices and the difficulties experienced by adult education during the Covid-19 period. The Covid-19 period has negatively affected many people all over the world, both physically and mentally. This process has created significant difficulties in both daily life and education. Studies have been carried out to overcome these difficulties in areas such as youth, school education and university education. However, there has not been enough work done for adults and in the field of adult education. This situation has increased the tendency of adults to be affected negatively and brought adult education to a standstill. At this point, the starting point of the project was to continue the foreign language education of adults by using digital storytelling to overcome this crisis.

<< Objectives >>

The project aims to develop digital competencies for adult education and adult learners to continue foreign language education. It strives to produce methods that will make adult education suitable for distance education and self learning. For this, digital storytelling will be used, which, unlike traditional learning methods, overlaps with the holistic approach of the CLASS approach (Communication, Language, Art, Social Sciences). With the artistic approach of digital storytelling, it is aimed to eliminate the negative emotions of adult learners such as anger, fear, anxiety and stress, which have increased due to the pandemic, through artistic production. The horizontal objectives of the project are to increase the basic digital skills of the target groups, to provide them with qualified employment opportunities, to increase intercultural dialogue among adults and to support social inclusion by conducting interdisciplinary studies with artistic activities.

<< Implementation >>

Needs Analysis: A comprehensive needs analysis was conducted to identify the digital skill gaps and preferences of adult learners towards DST-based learning.
Intellectual Output 1 and 2 were developed.
Communication: Communication channels such as WhatsApp, email, and monthly Zoom meetings were established to ensure effective coordination among partners.
Collaboration: Successful collaboration was achieved by exchanging information, expertise, and ideas with partner organizations.
Dissemination: Project outputs, results, and activities were shared on project web site, Erasmus+ platforms and EPALE to reach a wider audience.
Training Workshops: Training workshops were organized to introduce adult learners and educators to DST tools and techniques.
Testing and Feedback: Adult learners provided feedback to test the toolset and StoryLand platform, which was used for improvements.
Evaluation: The project progress was regularly evaluated, and the impact of the outputs on adult learners' English learning process was measured.
Multiplier Events: Multiplication events were organized to promote project outputs and create awareness among stakeholders.

<< Results >>

Two concrete outputs were produced in the project.

- Digital Storytelling (DST) Training Toolkit
- E-learning Platform (StoryLand)

The first output has been a resource for adult learners to develop their foreign language skills, digital proficiency, digital storytelling and artistic skills. With the toolkit produced, it is aimed that those who use this resource will start from basic digital competencies and reach the level of producing a professional digital story. The output consisted of five chapters and was produced in accordance with adult education. In the output, it is assumed that the users are at the beginner level. However, it is designed in such a way that users with basic digital competencies can continue from the next sections. In addition, this is a resource that trainers can use.

The second output is prepared for the artistic, cultural and social contributions of foreign language teaching to adults. This platform aims to set an example for self-learning and distance education practices in adult education. The platform has ready-made video lessons, external resources, self-learning section and interactive sections where users can share their own content.

2020-1-UK01-KA227-ADU-094526.title: Virtual Inclusive Cultural Entrepreneurs
2020-1-UK01-KA227-ADU-094526.summary:
The Virtual Inclusive Cultural Entrepreneurs (VICE) project has 5 partners from 4 countries: UK, Sweden, Austria, and Croatia. Each bringing complementary skills and expertise in the fields of adult education, teacher training, post-digital cultures, archives, museums, and cutting-edge learning technology.

According to a report by UNESCO at the height of the global lockdown, 95% of museums had closed and 9 out of 10 countries had closed their World Heritage properties. This unprecedented crisis has shone a light on how the entire cultural sector itself is weakened by this collapse. This has resulted in many intangible cultural practices being disrupted, which has an impact on the cultural life of communities. 
In addition, whilst social distancing becomes the norm, meeting or collaboration technologies that help remove physical obstacles between people are quickly becoming essential and are predicted to last well beyond a post COVID situation.
For many culture and heritage organisations technology that enables worthwhile experiences in virtual reality or 3D is still often cost-prohibitive, this has only been made worse by the financial situation in the cultural sector during and post-COVID.
In recent years, more and more GLAM organisations working in an intercultural perspective have increasingly started to re-examine and re-assess existing collections using different perspectives, which include the viewpoint of individuals and communities. Local communities can supply information regarding its history and community context, the GLAM organisation can respond by setting up a program with the objective of working collaboratively with communities and academics – to explore the meaning of objects and share stories, beliefs, and opinions around them. An extension to the idea of co-curation at the core of the VICE project is the innovative concept of GLAM organisations, businesses, cultural entrepreneurs, and communities working together to exploit artistic and cultural capital and assets through the development of programs of Adult Education in Cultural Entrepreneurship through a Virtual platform.

In response, the VICE project has 3 core objectives:
1.Develop formal education skills and competencies in Adult Educators and prospective cultural entrepreneurs that facilitate the development, creation, production, and preservation of assets that embody cultural, artistic, or other creative expressions and create cultural value and wealth for both creative producers and consumers of cultural services and products.
2. Enhance the acceleration of digital transformation and use of digital means in the GLAM and cultural sectors by creating an open-source platform that will enable collaborative learning through the creation of interactive 3D virtual exhibitions facilitated by custom 3D avatar/ guides that can be viewed in virtual reality (VR) or on a mobile device or PC.
3. Develop a handbook and new interactive digital toolkits and resources to support formal and informal learning activities that foster creativity, cultural entrepreneurship, collaboration, use of archives and cultural assets, storytelling, media production, culture and multiculturalism and sustainability;

Outputs include:
1.	VICE Interactive Methodology Handbook and Implementation plan
2.	VICE Open Source 3D Educational Exhibitions Platform
3.	VICE Continuous Professional Development Curriculum, Course & Learning Outcomes Matrix (LOM)
4.	VICE Digital Tool Kits
Participants will include adult educators, museum education officers, (prospective) cultural entrepreneurs, archivists, community & special interest groups and their students and groups.

It is expected that the VICE project will increase the numbers of people accessing professional development training through the VICE CPD Course and Digital Tool Kits to improve skills in using innovative methodologies, technology, and tools in adult education; and enhance personal and professional competences of adult learners, GLAM professionals, and educators in the cultural sphere. The project also aims to provide awareness about cultural entrepreneurship and increase the number of active cultural entrepreneurs in Europe through awareness, the handbook, course, and toolkits.
Furthermore, the VICE project will increase the number of open-source digital learning tools/ e-learning and resources, materials, courses, platform, and online collaborative channels to foster creativity, culture, and multiculturalism within adult education, cultural entrepreneurship, museums, and the community and will provide an open-source platform that enables the creation of 3D exhibitions with custom avatar guides that can be experienced through virtual reality (VR) or in 3D on a tablet or PC. This type of technology is often cost-prohibitive, and the VICE platform will enable a much larger number and range of organisations to access this type of technology across Europe and potentially the globe.

2020-1-UK01-KA227-ADU-094604.title: Motivate to Create (M2C): promoting inclusion in adult education through artistic and cultural Social Action Projects
2020-1-UK01-KA227-ADU-094604.summary:
<< Background >>

As described in the application, Motivate to Create (M2C) was designed in response to (a) a range of factors in Adult and Community Education and within the Creative, Cultural (including the arts) Industries (CCIs) precipitated by the Covid crisis and (b) a new impetus for ‘social action as adult education’, at community level. We wanted to combine the traditions and values of Europe’s community and participatory arts practice with Social Action Projects (SAPs) to support learners and communities, in a crisis context and post-pandemic, benefitting more people and places.  Opportunities created in this vibrant part of the economy are ‘out of reach’ for many. Those from privileged backgrounds are more than twice as likely to land a job in a creative occupation, dominating key creative roles, shaping what goes on stage, page and screen. Rinova, and our partners, set out to diversify voices, provide learning activities, tools, resources and courses for community facilitators working in adult and community education in disadvantaged communities via a transnational community of practice (CoP), sharing and exchanging learning, and developing a common approach to organising arts-based SAPs rooted in community development practice.

<< Objectives >>

Our purpose was to foster creativity and nurture talent, generated through participatory artistic and creative processes, supported by innovative, case study-based learning methods. M2C aimed to draw out the expression and creativity of all groups and ages in society, and to act as a catalyst for changes within a community through ‘place-based’ neighbourhood development.
Specific objectives were to:
- Exchange learning and practice across Europe from a systematic inquiry into social action in the context of non-formal arts-based learning 
- Reinforce creativity in education and the resilience of the cultural and creative sectors through social action, participatory and intercultural dialogue 
- Maximise the transferability of the project’s outcomes and results across Europe by developing a common approach and language. 
Concrete results proposed included:
- 30 SAP facilitators validate the M2C results through pilot testing, contributing learning and working together
- 150 adult learners supported by the 30 facilitators
- 250 stakeholders directly engaged in multiplier events and local consultations and engagements, with another 5,000 via dissemination and engagement over the project lifetime

<< Implementation >>

In summary our key activities were:
Establishment of a new transnational consortium. Five TPMs (4 in person, one online) – all of which were well attended and highly interactive.  
In each country, an extensive programme of outreach and engagement in our communities with tutors, trainers, community workers and learners.. 56 SAP facilitators took part in a series of online and in-person co-creation, validation events to form a community of practice developing their capabilities and validating the results. 

16 SAP facilitators from 5 countries attended and participated in a highly engaging 3 day transnational joint staff training (LTT) event for community facilitators.

Design, test and validation of 3 OER Intellectual Outputs 
An interactive, creative programme of dissemination – from producing and promoting a dedicated website, to active digital dissemination through partner channels, to local outreach and community engagement in local contexts with target groups and stakeholders.
A PDCA (Plan, Do, Check, Act) evaluation cycle (in person transnational meetings - online monitoring and participation, with ‘stock takes’ from formal evaluation questionnaires duly recorded and fed back, as provided for in our project Quality Plan.

<< Results >>

We generated a range of original, rich and multilingual learning and development contents for our target groups. IO1 includes What is a Social Action Project? M2C’s approach to SAPs. Who do they involve?  Methodological aspects. What’s the added value of SAPs? Why use this methodology? IO2 is Four Online Learning Modules providing practical learning resources for delivering arts-led SAPs, covering: Engagement; Frameworks for arts-led Social Action; Leadership and Social Change; Reflecting on Learning. IO3 M2C Pocket Guide has practical tips, tools and methods for organising arts-led social action and managing group dynamics.

In the event we exceeded the quantitative targets set in our objectives. In addition to the participation numbers in the previous section, 56 SAP Facilitators (target 30) and 419 adult learners (target 150) in communities outside formal learning were supported by the facilitators through the SAP programmes; 279 stakeholders (target 250) took part in Multiplier Events and local engagement events. M2C was disseminated to another 35,160 (target 5000) online and on social media. The project results are freely available in 5 languages on a webplatform www.motivatetocreate.eu with news and information about M2C.

2020-1-UK01-KA227-ADU-094683.title: Urban Survival Kits
2020-1-UK01-KA227-ADU-094683.summary:
<< Background >>

University of Atypical  For Arts and Disability (UofA) applied for this project as we had identified an opportunity to engage Adults with Disabilities in an innovative and exciting transnational programme of creativity and learning.  Inspired by our own professional artist Julie Mc Gowan, we engaged in a process of research and exploration around how this programme would be delivered. 

Julie's idea was to create an accessible travel kit for Adults With Disabilities (AWD) that would be done through exploring different cultures, arts and creativity skills and this became the foundation of this programme.

We saw this programme as having wider benefits, in that it would provide social, travel and integration opportunities for AWD in their local communities. We hoped that this would improve mental health and wellbeing, their self-esteem, practise active citizenship and to assist them with future independent travel . The UofA saw this as a valuable opportunity to engage in transnational comparison, discussion and sharing of the provision of opportunities for AWD across different cultures, establish links and a network between the partner countries.

<< Objectives >>

To create an accessible travel kit for Adults With Disabilities (AWD).
To create transnational learning opportunities for AWD exploring different cultures and learning arts and creativity skills.
To provide opportunities for AWD to improve their mental health and wellbeing, their self-esteem and to practice active citizenship.
To establish links and a network between the partner countries involving the development of  equity and accessibility resources for AWD.
To create a support framework for learners/AWD.
To support AWD with the development of organisation and planning skills to assist them with future independent travel

In a broad sense, we wanted to contribute to Erasmus+ objectives of HORIZONTAL: Skills development and inclusion through creativity and the arts, and HORIZONTAL: Social inclusion. By doing so, we would also develop the skills of our staff and beneficiaries, and promote social inclusion of persons with disabilities.

<< Implementation >>

3 day event - training of all partner countries staff who will be working directly with the AWD throughout the project. Experimenting and exploring access and learning options that could be adapted to effectively engage AWD in the wider programme 
5 day learning event - the five partnering countries took part in the learning programme which included digital training, craft activities, the development of a multisensory digital trail,  social activities and site visits to Botanic Gardens and Ulster Museum in Belfast.
5 day International Exhibition event in Belfast and a series of live and online workshops.  Artwork created during the workshops fed into the completion of the exhibition.
Exhibition at local level in Belfast in the Atypical Gallery.  This  was the first public facing event and included talks to the public about the programme.
Project partners exhibitions at a local level.  Each partner organised an exhibition  in their own countries and these were promoted and showcased online also. The programme activity also included 4 TPM which engaged the programme managers in each of the five  nations in cross-cultural communications and cultural understanding in relation to AWD.

<< Results >>

5 local showcase Exhibition/events including award ceremonies to celebrate learner achievements
International exhibition including gallery tours and artist talks.
16 module curriculum for the blueprint / template on how to make your own Urban Survival Kits
4 Digital learning and exhibition programme modules
An E-manual - instructions for each of the learning modules
45 bespoke urban survival kits designed to meet individual needs
Communication Cards - Product deck of 53 playing cards (100 decks) i.e. flash cards with pictograms to be used for nonverbal communication for local and international travel
Creation of craft and digital multi-sensory maps of sites in each country
Digital Trails is an online interactive map of local and international journeys.
Development of friendships between partners and participants across the five nations
Strong working professional relationships including a  commitment to future partnership working.
