2020-1-AT01-KA226-HE-092617.title: Crisis-Resistant Digital Education and Training
2020-1-AT01-KA226-HE-092617.summary:
<< Background >>

The decision to apply for this project was driven by the challenges faced by educators during the COVID-19 crisis. The sudden and rapid changes in teaching methods due to the pandemic presented a need for immediate adaptation to online education. These emergency transitions, referred to as emergency remote teaching, aimed to replicate in-person teaching but proved to be difficult to achieve. The urgent shift to online education lacked the systematic and structured development typically required for effective online courses. Educators, already working at full capacity, were tasked with keeping pace with rapid changes while grappling with the challenges of fully virtual education.
In general, the development of an online university course typically takes six to nine months, which was not feasible due to the urgency of the situation. Additionally, many universities lacked sufficient support personnel familiar with online teaching practices, resulting in suboptimal course delivery in the virtual environment.
Despite the rushed implementation of online courses, educators and students made significant efforts to adopt and implement online teaching practices. However, the high workload of teaching staff led to challenges in transferring course materials and organizing virtual courses. Students also encountered difficulties and obstacles during the transition to online education. It is crucial to gather and share lessons learned and best practices across different institutions within the engineering education community, including acknowledging and addressing mistakes made during this rapid transition.
Furthermore, it is important to focus on the sustainability of online practices and their integration into regular programs in the post-pandemic era to maximize their perceived benefits. Educators without prior experience in digital technologies faced particular challenges, leading to misconceptions about online teaching and a lack of awareness about the potential benefits that structured online courses or hybrid education can offer. In the absence of universally accepted guidelines for digitizing different types of lectures during an ongoing crisis, educators had to rely on their own knowledge and skills rather than scientifically based and proven approaches.
Given this steady demand to deliver high-quality education continuously and avoid disruption by unforeseen incidents, the needs to be addressed are therefore to develop and validate a structured approach to adapt teaching activities to crisis scenarios and to foster collaboration and exchange between educators on best practices during the crisis.

<< Objectives >>

The project’s main objectives were based on the underlying idea to support educators with a structured approach to adapt teaching activities to a crisis and guidelines synthesized from the learnings of the COVID-19 pandemic. Therefore, being able to recognize the scope and difficulties that come with varying boundary conditions imposed by a crisis and efficiently transition to a fully online course, which can uphold the expected quality in the delivery of education.
The focus of the research activities revolved around the development of a framework, a knowledge hub and practice-oriented crisis-resistant guidelines that provide the educational tools and methods as well as the expertise and experience necessary for the rapid adaptation and digitalization of lectures in case of a crisis. 
Three main intellectual outputs were proposed:
-	Framework for the rapid adaptation and digitalization of education and training in the event of a crisis (IO1). The framework defines various “crisis scenarios” that allow past, present and future crises to be identified and categorized and their impact on education and training to be determined. In addition, a distinction is made between lecture types such as oral presentations or individual exercises. These crisis scenarios and lecture types comprise a matrix, whereby the framework suggests favourable tools and methods in each case.
-	Knowledge Hub for a crisis-resistant education and training (IO2). The Knowledge Hub takes the form of an interactive website, which enables educators to search for and exchange expertise and experiences related to crisis-resistant education and training.
-	Practice-oriented crisis-resistant guidelines for the rapid adaptation and digitalization of education and training in the event of a crisis (IO3). The practice-oriented crisis-resistant guidelines contain detailed descriptions of how to implement the most favourable educational tools and methods, thus providing educators with a clear and structured way to adapt their own courses to the given circumstances.
The project focused on “product development” courses for two reasons. Firstly, the variety of activities and tasks in product development leads to the use of a variety of lecture types. Secondly, the transition to digitized education and training has been slow, despite great progress in the digitalization of products and the product design process itself. Therefore, product design courses offer an ideal candidate for the validation of the proposed crisis-resistant tools and methods. This project requires that all participating partners have a deep understanding of educational systems and methodologies, that they use ICT tools and online learning approaches on a daily basis and that they have used them long before the crisis. The consortium of four partners TUW, UL-FME, UNIZAG-FSB and POLIMI has set itself the goal of improving teaching activities by adopting innovative approaches. It has a long tradition of working together on different educational projects and working with innovative ICT tools. Previously, UL-FME and UNIZAG-FSB worked together on EGPR and NARIP and took on TUW for the project CASPROD. TUW, UL-FME, UNIZAG-FSB and POLIMI have been working together on the Erasmus+ project ELPID, in which an e-learning platform was being set up to meet the demanding needs of project-based design courses. Currently, all four partners are currently working together on the Erasmus+ project ProHackin’, focused on employing open innovation practice through product hackathons, which will thus demonstrate how to create a link between industrial companies and students. The CResDET project expands the research scope by introducing the perspective of delivering crisis-resilient education.
The expected impact of the project, its activities and its results varies according to the actors involved. The main target group were lecturers in mechanical engineering and engineering design in higher education. The framework developed enables them to assess different educational tools and methods and to choose the most appropriate approach for their own courses. In addition, the knowledge hub enables the easy exchange of expertise and experience related to crisis-resistant education and training. Finally, the practice-oriented crisis-resistant guidelines help educators to respond to rapid changes and adapt their courses accordingly. In addition, the educators participating in O2 had the opportunity to use modern technologies and to make their courses crisis-resistant under the direct guidance of the project partners. Another important target group were students of mechanical engineering and engineering design students in higher education. Thanks to the outputs, the students do not have to interrupt their education in case of a crisis. Instead, they benefit from the immediate implementation of modern educational tools and methods. Furthermore, students that participated in O2 had the opportunity to work on innovative projects in the field of engineering design and gained experience in collaboration and teamwork in a virtual environment using state-of-the-art ICT tools. Finally, all educators and students outside the product design domain will also benefit from the project, as it will bring different insights to educators who teach students mature enough to participate in a digital learning environment.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented a series of activities (A1-A18), Transnational Project Meetings (TPM1-TPM4)  and Multiplier Events in adherence to the proposed project plan. Below is a description of all activities:
A1 Project kick-off (lead TUW, M1-M2): Since the Covid-19 situation did not allow for a physical TPM1, it was held online. The objective was to plan and detail the project activities according to the project timesheet and project proposal. Furthermore, all involved personnel were briefed regarding the legal, financial and administrative aspects of the CResDET project.
A2 Budget management (lead TUW, M1-M13): Budget control has been continuously executed through the means of monitoring project costs, identifying potential cost changes, and planning corrective actions within the given budget frame.
A3 Time management (lead TUW, M1-M13): Time management has been continuously executed through the means of monitoring the adherence to schedule, identifying potential causes for delay, and planning corrective and preventive activities. Special attention was given to reach the critical milestone of delivering the preliminary framework during the final period of O1 (M6-M9).
A4 Quality management (lead TUW, M1-M13): Quality management has been continuously executed through the means of evaluating intermediate project results and micromanagement of additional tasks (that are related to the quality aspects of the project and are not specified within this listing). During bi-weekly meetings, the agenda usually contained items regarding administrative aspects of the project, project management issues and discussions/ feedback on project results.
A5 Definition of common lecture types and crisis scenarios (lead TUW, M2-M5): The activity comprised two parts: establishing an overview of lecture and assessment types and determining a general approach to characterize crisis scenarios. A review of engineering curricula in the higher education sector was carried out by TUW. Research activities related to crisis scenarios comprised reviews of disruptive events and subsequent synthesis of conditions that affect the delivery of education. All partners described the impact of COVID-19 on their courses, by applying the proposed crisis conditions characterization scheme.
A6 Definition of possible educational tools and methodologies (lead POLIMI, M3-M7): A literature study has been carried out to establish educational objectives for course adaptations and to support the transformation by providing educational tools and methodologies. Applicants of the framework are provided with materials to facilitate student learners' profiles as well as a list of common educational tools and methodologies (educational items) that has been revised to suit mechanical engineering curricula. The list matches educational items to student learning profiles and suggests how to use them in regular on-site classes and in a fully remote setting. 
A7 Selection of the most suitable educational tools and methodologies (lead UL-FME, M5-M9): During TPM2, each educational item had been reviewed with regard to its suitability for engineering education and assessed for its applicability to learning styles, lecture types and their respective levels of digitalization in a two-step assessment round. Round one: all partners independently evaluated each item and proposed new product development-specific items. Round two: group discussion evaluating individual judgements, followed up by subsequent consensus-finding discussions. Building on the findings, a preliminary process model for the framework was generated.
A8 Development of an exchange platform (knowledge hub) for crisis-related expertise and experience (lead UNIZAG, M10-M14): Aspects of this activity included determining a layout of the platform structure and defining how mechanical engineering and engineering design educators can be guided through the application of the framework, as well as interact with and contribute to the platform. Currently, the platform is still under construction but already features articles on the contents of the framework for dissemination purposes. In the period of M4-M6, a Covid-19 Response Questionnaire has been conducted. Preliminary results were used to improve the framework and served as a trial for the covid-response questionnaire, which will be disseminated through the knowledge hub web platform.
A9 Preparation of the summer semester courses (lead POLIMI, M10-M13) & A12 Preparation of the winter semester courses (lead UL-FME, M16-M19): All partnering Higher Education Institutions were individually responsible for conducting course preparatory activities including: deciding on which educational items to implement, searching for lecturers to cover all topics that are relevant for that year's project, the definition of the course schedule, recruiting students (attracting, screening and selecting), and preparing course material. The same activities were conducted jointly for the common product development course that is being carried out in the Erasmus+ Project ProHackin’.
A10 Implementation of the summer semester courses (lead TUW, M12-M15) & A13 Implementation of the winter semester courses (lead TUW, M19-M22): All partnering HEIs were individually responsible for: the execution of the course, monitoring students, conducting student interviews and gathering feedback on the adapted course, organization of reviews, virtual lectures, projects assignments. At the end of the summer semester, all project partners jointly examined students' feedback and discussed insights to further steps for the development of the framework and guidelines for educators in O2 and O3.
A11 Analysis of the results from the summer semester courses (lead UNIZAG-FSB, M15-16) & A14 Analysis of the results from the summer semester courses (lead POLIMI, M22-23): Gathering feedback, performing the evaluation, assessing results, deriving findings. Publishing the results on the knowledge hub
A15 & A16 were focused on selecting the most suitable educational tools and methodologies for each crisis scenario and lecture type and creating practice-oriented crisis-resistant guidelines for the implementation of the proposed tools and methodologies (O3). These guidelines provide educators with a clear and structured path for implementing the approach in their own lectures. Like before, the results are disseminated at an education-related journal or conference.
Multiplier Event ME1 was used for disseminating project results and to invite external educators to participate in the implementation of the educational tools and methodologies. Additionally, experts from the industry were invited to share their insights into the continuation of activities and knowledge preservation during COVID-19.
TPM 1-4 were held to assess the results of the preceding activities for quality and comprehension, project management activities and to prepare for the upcoming phases of the project.
The dissemination events at the conference series Engineering & Product Design Education International E&PDE and International Conference on Research into Design ICORD were used to present the established IOs to academia, receive feedback on the proposed framework methodology and involve other educators by sharing their gained experience from COVID-19.

<< Results >>

First and foremost, all of the intended project outputs proposed in the project application have been accomplished. The concrete project outputs and tangible results are described below:
-Framework for the rapid adaptation and digitalization of education and training in the event of a crisis (IO1). The framework defines various “crisis scenarios” that allow past, present and future crises to be identified and categorized and their impact on education and training to be determined. In addition, a distinction is made between lecture types such as oral presentations or individual exercises. These crisis scenarios and lecture types comprise a matrix, whereby the framework suggests favourable tools and methods in each case.
The framework defined in IO1 comprehends and guides through four main outputs, containing resources for the adaptation and digitalization of lectures covering the following aspects: 
IO1-A5_Course Types and Assessment Approaches reviews common course types and assessment approaches and introduces levels of technological support from “no technical support” to “fully virtual classrooms”. Generic layouts of how said course types and assessment approaches can be realized given a certain technological support level have been subsequently characterized to aid educators with their implementation in their own courses.
IO1-A5_Crisis Scenarios enables a generic description of disruptive crisis events, by introducing a set of characteristic crisis conditions with varying degrees of severity to provide the educator with assistance while assessing the crisis event. Crisis conditions can be grouped as either general, higher-education related or personal. General crisis conditions apply to the population within the affected area and are related to restrictions in mobility, the availability of electrical power and connectivity failures such as telephone or internet connections. Higher-education-related conditions refer to the accessibility of institutional infrastructure, availability and accessibility of learning resources and educational personnel to deliver education. Personal conditions are restricted only to the equipment necessary to receive or deliver education. Depending on the severity of restricting crisis conditions (e.g. lockdown, travel ban), an educator is supported in choosing among physical, hybrid or completely-online teaching modes. 
IO1-A6_Review on Educational Objectives, offers a review of student- and teacher-centred perspectives on educational objectives and methodologies. The emergence of a crisis requires to rethink of the delivery of the course with reference to its Intended Learning Outcomes, which are important in pedagogical exchanges so that educators and students can match their expectations on the purpose of any exchange. This review should aid educators, in designing the appropriate strategies, tasks and instructions, so that the intended outcome is met and to address different types of student learning profiles. From a students' perspective, it helps to clarify the objectives of taking a course. 
IO1-A7_Educational Items Table maps common teaching approaches, methods and tools to suitable lecture types from IO1-A5 and types of students learners from IO1-A6 and suggests how to implement said items in a physical or completely online course format. Findings from implementing educational methods and applying the framework were continuously incorporated into the table.

-Knowledge Hub for a crisis-resistant education and training (IO2). The Knowledge Hub takes the form of an interactive website, which enables educators to search for and exchange expertise and experiences related to crisis-resistant education and training.
The knowledge hub website (www.cresdet.eu) features three main sections that are relevant for educators that want to apply the framework to their specific crisis scenario and contribute to the exchange of best practices. In the Knowledge Hub tab, educators can find reflections from partaking project partners on how their course design changed from before, during and after COVID-19, they can contribute by filling in a COVID-19 response survey. In the framework tab, all framework domains and processes are displayed on a process diagram, featuring a description of each process and links to the resources of the framework. 

-Practice-oriented crisis-resistant guidelines for the rapid adaptation and digitalization of education and training in the event of a crisis (IO3). The practice-oriented crisis-resistant guidelines contain detailed descriptions of how to implement the most favourable educational tools and methods, thus providing educators with a clear and structured way to adapt their own courses to the given circumstances. 
IO3_ Guidelines for engineering educators to design resilient online environments based on the learnings from implementing the framework, this document guides through the application of the framework.
IO3_Comparison of educator's ad-hoc and systematic response to a crisis scenario establishes a general model of ad-hoc subject adaptation to a disrupting situation and draws a comparison between it and the proposed framework, thereby outlining the strategies to make emergency remote teaching more effective.
IO3_Implementation and validation of the CResDET framework describes how the project partners from University of Zagreb adapted their teaching activities in the summer semester of the academic year 2022/2023 to a relocation of all faculty facilities and associated activities. Although not a typical crisis scenario, the significant changes provided an opportunity to implement and validate the framework. Through a case study approach, the framework was validated, and necessary revisions were made based on the experience.
IO3_Applying the CResDET Methodology to enhance the European Product Development Course in Pro Hackin’: describes how the project partner applied the framework methodology to a virtual product development course with an industrial partner.

2020-1-AT01-KA226-HE-092663.title: Digital inclusion
2020-1-AT01-KA226-HE-092663.summary:
<< Background >>

Education can be seen as a powerful instrument for enhancing an inclusive society. Democratic principles need to be taught in school to reduce discrimination and exclusion, which can negatively affect students’ performance. Considering these aspects the aim of the project was to create a platform, where students, teachers and teacher trainers can educate themselves about topics related to (digital) inclusion such as Digital Gaps, Digital Worldmaking or Digital Storytelling. The project team aimed at addressing the needs for more information about these topics as well as at supporting teachers in the process of education to develop an inclusive way of teaching. Different people were included in the developing process to ensure, that the tools make sense considering particular challenges (for teachers with special needs, multilingual teachers and hard-to-reach teachers). Beside topics about digital inclusion the project team offers an online Plattform (www.digitclue.net) which is digitally inclusive itself in terms of different and easy language/s, easy accessibility or the possibility to use it offline. In order to meet the demands of teachers, they were involved in the entire process of the DIGITClue Project.

<< Objectives >>

The aim was to create a HUB, which is an online Platform where different material can be collected and provided for the specific topic "digital inclusion". Regarding the HUB (www.digitclue.net) two different aspects were crucial. Firstly, the idea was to provide material, tools, apps and concepts about digital inclusion for people who are working in educational institutions. The focus was on pre-service teachers (students), in-service teachers (teachers) and university staff (teacher trainers at the university). The second aim was to make the HUB inclusive itself to also support teachers, who are often left excluded such as multilingual teachers or far-to-reach teachers. These educators, but also others, should find a platform where they can educate themselves about digital inclusion, get ideas for teaching and working with students and on how students can be supported with digital tools. Furthermore, the project consortium wanted to contribute to the dissemination of the topic in different - often ignored - language areas (Turkish, Czech, Croatian, Romani, German, English) through the multilingual platform.

<< Implementation >>

The project partners from Dresden, Zadar and Vienna met monthly via Zoom to discuss the latest information, outcomes and needed outputs (IO1/IO2/IO3/IO4) and to keep in touch for exchanging information, address difficulties and craft new ideas. 
Three Transnational Project Meetings took place to discuss the Project Management, time sheets, budget and reports. The first one took place via Zoom because of Covid-19 under the lead of DIU Dresden in January 2022. The second meeting took place in Zadar under the lead of UNIZD in May 2022. The last Project meeting took place in Vienna under the lead of University of Vienna in February 2023. Besides that, two LTTA's (Learning, Teaching, Training Activities) were carried out. The first one took place in May 2022 at the University of Zadar and a primary school in Gospic (Croatia). The focus was on the presentation of developed material and the feedback of local teachers to get a deeper insight of their needs. The second LTTA was held at the University of Vienna in February 2023, where students from teacher training tried out different concepts and tools and gave feedback, as well as new ideas.
In February 2023, the final conference (Multiplier Event) took place at the University of Vienna.

<< Results >>

The project team created a HUB, which contains the digital, technical, pedagogical and didactical outputs of the project. As there are three different target groups (pre-service teacher, in-service teacher, university staff) different handbooks were created. The handbooks provide all concepts, tools and materials in one pdf-document to download and work with it offline, as well as in six different languages. The website has different sections (Easy Learning, Portfolio, DI Map, Handbooks, Cooperation)
The project team created 13 concepts (Digital Inclusion, Inclusion, Digital Divide, Digital Gender Gap, Digital Queer Gap, Digitalisation, Digital Storytelling, Digital Age Gap, Digital Culture(s), Cyberethics, Digital Worldmaking,  Digital Literacy, Digital Transformation) for the target groups to read. Based on these concepts there are different didactical tools one can try out. Most of the tools can be used in the classroom and worked on with students. All of the tools contain digital apps and websites to create individual perspectives on the topics. Beside that the team also created a so called “D.I. Map” which stands for Digital Inclusion Map for people from all over the world to share their experiences or relevant material.

2020-1-AT01-KA226-VET-092394.title: Next Generation Web 4.0 Entrepreneurs
2020-1-AT01-KA226-VET-092394.summary:
<< Background >>

The BFI believes strongly in corporate social responsibility and therefore wishes to contribute to society by engaging in projects where the Institute's knowledge and experience can be of benefit in addressing key social issues such as key skills development. The project offers a unique opportunity to participate in shaping this future and preparing the next generation of entrepreneurs for the challenges and opportunities of Web 4.0. As an innovative and visionary educational institute in the digital world, we see the importance of equipping young people with the necessary skills to succeed in an increasingly connected and technologically advanced environment. With the growing demand for digital literacy and entrepreneurial innovation skills, in today's rapidly changing economic landscape, it is critical that young people not only have the technical skills in Web 4.0, but also develop the entrepreneurial mindset to create innovative solutions to tomorrow's challenges. The Next Generation Web 4.0 Entrepreneurs project provides the platform to put this belief into action and make a lasting contribution to the development of the high-value knowledge economy.

<< Objectives >>

Web 4.0 is also changing the future of business.  Web 4.0 is consumer driven, putting them firmly in the driving seat. The future of Web 4.0 is meant to revolutionise the daily lives of humans. By creating interrelationships between human and machine, Web 4.0 will give users unique and interconnected social and personal lives. It is a wide open development field awaiting the vision and creativity of a new cohort of creative entrepreneurs.
The proposed in-service training will address 3 specific issues:
•	tutors as learners themselves - in this training module tutors will learn about three different but related topics essential to the success of the eSMART project
•	tutors as facilitators of learning in remote, online environments - in this module tutors will examine different pedagogic approaches with a focus on challenge-based learning theory and how to use digital breakouts, online educational escape rooms and WebQuests as learning frameworks
•	tutors as developers of new digital media-rich learning resources and how best to present them to potential learners in appropriate online settings - in this module tutors will be introduced to open-source software

<< Implementation >>

The following activities have been implemented during the project lifecycle:

1.  Learning, Teaching, Training Activities
C1 In-service Training Part A -The Symbiotic Internet; 
All partners sent a minimum of 2 appropriate and affiliated VET tutors for this 3 days event.
C2 In-service Training Part B -Building the pedagogic and technical skills of VET Tutors
All partners sent a minimum of 2 appropriate and affiliated VET tutors for this 3 days event.

2. Multiplier events 
251 participants attended the ESmart workshops. 
During the Multiplier Event, all the resources created in the project were presented.
The Multiplier Events were a great success both in terms of maximising project promotion of the ESmart Results. 
There is high potential for exploitation as the VET managers, business support organisations and 
policy makers in each country that participated in the Multiplier events stated that they will definitely use the resources for their trainings and share them with other VET educators and all relevant stakeholders.

2020-1-BE01-KA226-SCH-082714.title: Covid-19, school digital accelerator
2020-1-BE01-KA226-SCH-082714.summary:
<< Background >>

La pandémie due au Covid19 a permis de déceler à la fois de graves lacunes dans la transmission de travaux aux élèves durant les confinements successifs : lacunes chez les enseignants dans les programmes utilisables pour créer les dossiers destinés aux élèves, manque de connaissances dans les principaux programmes de microsoft, manque de matériel informatique dans certaines familles d'où impossibilité pour ces enfants de s'approprier les matières qui leur étaient destinées. Nous avons eu la chance que l'Agence Nationale lance une candidature à projet pour pallier à ce genre de phénomène apparu en ce moment délicat pour toute la communauté éducative. Cette possibilité de poser une candidature fut certes une chance à la fois pour les enseignants et les élèves. Nous nous sommes dirigés vers un projet qui nous permettrait de répondre aux besoins face auxquels nous nous sommes trouvés durant cette période difficile. En rédigeant la candidature, nous avons pensé à permettre aux enseignants de recevoir des formations nécessaires pour assurer leur rôle et puis de pouvoir transmettre ces nouvelles connaissances acquises vers les élèves impliqués dans le projet. Les établissements contactés pour travailler en collaboration connaissaient des difficultés similaires et souhaitaient pouvoir répondre à leurs besoins grâce à ce projet.

<< Objectives >>

Notre objectif principal était double: favoriser une amélioration des connaissances informatiques dans le personnel enseignant et transmettre ces connaissances vers nos élèves respectifs. Grâce à ce travail en deux étapes, nous voulions construire une dynamique qui réponde aux difficultés rencontrées durant cette période de pandémie. Pour répondre favorablement à cette idée, il fallait que les enseignants des écoles partenaires demandent des sujets de formations leur permettant de s'améliorer. Une quarantaine d'enseignants partenaires dans le projet ont ainsi rempli le document sollicitant un domaine précis, une demande spécifique dans les programmes microsoft. Grâce à des formations données en visioconférences anglaises grâce à Technobel, nos objectifs ont pu être atteints et nos élèves ont pu bénéficier d'apports nouveaux dans le domaine nformatique.

<< Implementation >>

La première partie du programme visait les enseignants. Ces derniers ont ainsi reçu des formations qui répondaient à leur questionnement. Des formations concernant Word, Excel, Power Point, la vidéo ont été données par monsieur Lannoo de l'organisme Technobel. Grâce au questionnement, il a pu répondre aux enseignants et leur a permis de s'améliorer dans ces domaines. Après chaque formation, des travaux ont été demandés aux enseignants ayant suivi la formation. Une quarantaine d'enseignants des huit écoles partenaires ont ainsi pu suivre ces formations et en faire, ensuite bénéficier leurs élèves.
De même, des travaux ont été demandés pour utiliser les nouvelles connaissances reçues. Rédaction de lettres avec présentation correcte, utilisation du publipostage pour un envoi de lettre à diverses personnes, insertion d'une image dans un texte sur word, insertion d'une page horizontale dans un dossier vertical, création d'une affiche, lettre d'invitation, création d'un cahier de cotes sur excel, construction d'un power point avec insertion musicale, construction d'une vidéo.

<< Results >>

Résultats : quels résultats concrets et autres résultats votre projet a-t-il produits ?
Les formations données par Technobel ont répondu aux attentes des enseignants partenaires et leur ont apporté réponses aux questions qui avaient été posées dans le document initial. Les différents domaines approchés ont permis aux partenaires d'acquérir des nouvelles connaissances, ce qui constituait l'objectif primordial de la première partie du projet. Les travaux demandés à la fois aux enseignants et aux élèves par la suite nous ont permis de nous rendre compte des connaissances acquises par les acteurs dun projet. Les partenaires ont dû construire une affiche dédiée à l'exposition "Napoleon" qui avait lieu au même moment à Liège. Les enseignants ont dû construire un cahier de cotation avec utilisation des formules adéquates et leur permettant, à chaque moment, de connaître les élèves en difficultés.
Les élèves ont pu manipuler correctement et avec plus d'efficacité les programmes usuels de microsoft, mais également à manipuler de nouveaux programmes mis à leur disposition durant les mobilités en Croatie et en Espagne. L'efficience des mobilités a ainsi été démontrée et n os élèves sont revenus de ces déplacements avec de nouvelles connaissances qu'ils devront certes utiliser régulièrement mais avec également l'envie de nouvelles découvertes.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2020-1-BG01-KA226-VET-095185.title: Piloting Virtual Practical Trainings for Culinary Arts VET
2020-1-BG01-KA226-VET-095185.summary:
<< Background >>

COVID-19 pandemic set a serious challenge before the educational sector and reconfirmed the need of integration of digital resources in education. Still, the transition to digital education has been much smoother and easier to organize for some vocational fields than for others. The professions and qualifications that rely on human creativity, attitude and interactions have not been considered as appropriate for distance learning. Though there are some attempts for digitalization of VET for service-sector professions (besides the IT-based ones), the practical trainings and examinations are still delivered in-class and through physical presence in most EU countries. Accordingly, the practical trainings in VET curricula for obtaining qualifications in these professions were severely affected and interrupted during COVID-19 lockdown regimes as VET-providers were not prepared to organize them in distance or blended mode. However, the provision of uninterrupted VET programs is vital for keeping VET learners in training and for preventing drop-outs.
Therefore, VET@HOME creates and pilot a standard unit-based syllabus model for virtual practical training courses within the VET for the profession “Cook” and suggests a new approach.

<< Objectives >>

The overall aim of VET@HOME is to reinforce the ability of VET institutions to provide high-quality, inclusive digital education in culinary arts adapted as to the post-COVID19 operation standards in the food-and beverage industry.
The specific objectives were to:
- develop a model unit-based syllabus for virtual practical training courses in VET for the profession “Cook”;
- create an on-line platform for the virtual delivery of practical training courses for partial qualification for the profession “Cook”;
- equip VET-providers with a common Protocol and Guidbook how to utilise virtual resources in practical training;
- sustain the attractiveness of VET in the culinary arts and post-crises recovery by outlining paths for recognizing the outcomes of practical training in distance mode.

<< Implementation >>

1. Development of model unit-based syllabus for virtual practical training courses in VET for the profession “Cook”
2. Development of VET@HOME e-learning platform for the delivery of virtual practical training courses for partial qualification for the profession “Cook” with 5 pilot courses, adapted for distance-mode guided or semi-guided delivery
3. Development of a Protocol and Guidebook for trainers and company tutors in culinary arts on how to conduct on-line VET practical training courses
4. Development of a Roadmap for integration of distance-mode practical training learning outcomes in VET qualifications, including recommendations for policy reforms in VET in the partners’ countries.
5. Organization and conduction of a Joint short-term staff training with 14 representatives of the project partners for exchange of experience and expertise in structuring and development of tools for digital practical training
6. Promoting the developed outputs and consulting their applicability via Final Conferences in 5 countries with more than 230 participants in total attending the multiplier events
7. Organization of Peer coaching session at IC for 22 trainers, teachers and experts in VET beyond the project partners

<< Results >>

The project delivers the following outputs and other results:
1. Output 1: A model unit-based syllabus for virtual practical training courses in VET for the profession “Cook” – in 6 languages (EN, BG, ES, PT, NM and HR)
2. Output 2: An e-learning platform for the delivery of the virtual practical training courses for partial qualification for the profession “Cook” with 5 pilot courses – in 6 languages 
3. Output 3: A Protocol and Guidebook for trainers and company tutors in culinary arts on how to conduct on-line VET practical training courses – in 6 languages 
4. Output 4: А Roadmap for integration of distance-mode practical training learning outcomes in VET qualifications – in 6 languages 
5. A joint-staff training for VET-experts – a 3-days training event held in Bulgaria with 14 participants trained to use and build upon the project key outputs (O1, O2 and O3)
6. National-level conferences “Practical VET in the Digital World” in the 5 project countries – 8 events with a total of >230 participants (196 reported) informed about the project outputs
7. A pilot peer coaching session at IC for VET-trainers from institutions beyond the partnership – 1-day event in Dobrich, Bulgaria for teachers and experts in VET with 22 participants
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-CZ01-KA226-HE-094342.title: Inovation of artistic gymnastics lessons at High Schools with sports orientation
2020-1-CZ01-KA226-HE-094342.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the project because of the obvious need to support the teaching of artistic gymnastics at universities, especially because of the negative impact of covid on the educational process of students, especially in terms of practical subjects. The project was conceived so that students with limited practical learning, either due to unpredictable events or due to a combined form of study, could optimally prepare for a practical class in the gym and thus optimize the motor learning process. However, in addition to distance practical and theoretical preparation, we also wanted to focus on supporting and improving the effectiveness of gymnastic lessons in all their forms, as it is a sport where the individual acquires basic motor skills that can be used in all other sports. Based on the many years of the project partners' experience with gymnastics at the top and school level, we perceive problems with its inclusion in lessons during the last years due to the lack of physical preparedness of students, fear of injuries, etc... With this project we also want to contribute to overcoming these barriers that create obstacles for teachers and students on the way to gymnastics.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to strengthen the ability of physical education universities and other organizations to provide high quality education in the field of gymnastics, which is generally accepted by experts as one of the basic pillars of physical education, through the creation of innovative materials available in OPEN ACCESS mode, usable both in face to face and combined or distance learning.

<< Implementation >>

Within the project, international meetings with partners were held to discuss the quality of the work done so far, as well as to specify plans and divide tasks for the next project period. The first concrete step was the unification of the curriculum between the sports faculties of the partner universities. Following this, text and video proposals for the content of the intended audiovisual materials were created thanks to the work of teachers, researchers. With the help of technicians, these proposals were further implemented, hundreds of videos were made, as well as audio recordings of texts, all in the languages of the partner countries and in English. Furthermore, the technicians' job was to create an open access website. During the development of the materials, the quality and clarity of the parts were checked in the gymnastics classes of the partner organisations. Furthermore, according to the plan, audiovisual equipment was purchased for the gymnastics gyms for the possibility of presenting the created materials or streaming the lessons. Furthermore, all partners realized one or more dissemination events as planned, with more participants than originally planned. We also received feedback from an independent reviewer, an expert in both competitive and school gymnastics.

<< Results >>

The concrete result is the creation of comprehensive audiovisual materials supporting the teaching of artistic gymnastics. Compared to the plan, where we intended to create materials for teaching about 50 gymnastic elements, we have significantly increased this number to 81 gymnastic elements that students of sports faculties encounter. The materials approach the problem of motor learning in gymnastics comprehensively, thus they contain chapters on: execution of the element including the recording of the movement from the perspective of the trainee, biomechanical basis of the element, errors in execution, physical preparation, training methodologies, spotting, as well as worksheets for use in preparation for practical gymnastics lessons and test questions. We also cover topics such as the characteristics of gymnastics, its history and didactic principles in motor learning.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-CZ01-KA226-HE-094453.title: COVID-19 pandemic as an “opportunity window” for the transition towards new and more inclusive internationalisation through virtual mobility
2020-1-CZ01-KA226-HE-094453.summary:
<< Background >>

Our consortium decided to apply for the project to address the current needs of online education and the restrictions aligned with it. The COVID-19 pandemic significantly influenced education all around the world. It has also been the case in tertiary education. The established practices in education were challenged and altered in many ways. The bans on international travel and internal pandemic restrictions significantly influenced the international mobility of students and internationalization in general. Under such circumstances, COVID-19, however, opened the “opportunity window” for innovations in higher education practices. Nevertheless, every novelty takes some time to become established practice, if it happens at all.

<< Objectives >>

The project’s main objective was to reflect and learn from the transition towards new forms of online education among university staff and students by developing a manual of best practices and reactions to the pandemic in tertiary education. We wanted to use the synergy of the university network and develop supportive measures for the acceptance of innovative online forms of education among students and staff, who both were considered the main target groups. The project aimed to cope with the transition to online education in general, to better understand the concept of virtual mobility in particular and to support the inclusiveness of the students and university staff.
The goal was to help the target groups to be ready for the future situation necessitating intensive use of online educational and online supportive activities. A vital point of such project objectives involved the issue of virtual mobility of students and staff within international space since mobility, as was known before the outbreak of the pandemic, was ruined. The cooperation of the universities operating within different national contexts intended to make such a transition easier, thanks to the possibility of sharing the experience.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented several activities that helped to fulfil the planned objectives. We had over twenty online meetings of the project managers and a number of extra meetings of the individual working groups of each intellectual output, we conducted questionnaires, made content analyses, organised webinars, organised an in-person conference for over twenty participants and worked on the development of several outputs, which are described in other parts of the final report (e.g. development of the virtual mobility tools with the help of AR and VR technologies, development of the web application of best practices, development of scenarios of reactions and development of learning materials). From these, we can mention the implementation of a series of focus group sessions at all the universities of the consortium. During the focus group sessions, the various target groups of the project discussed the work tasks and outcomes of the project, brainstormed ideas and provided feedback to the staff members working on the project.
The project did not plan any Learning/Teaching/Training Activities and did not receive any funding for them.

<< Results >>

1) Virtual mobility tools – Several virtual tools have been established:
a) Online Student Café (accessed by anyone via a website browser or VR glasses)
b) Wood exploration and chainsaw training room (accessed only for teaching purposes with permission by BOKU moderator via website browser or VR glasses)
c) AR Stihl Chainsaw Daily Maintenance training scenario that can be accessed via the AREEKA APP by anyone
d) Floodplain 360° learning experience with two levels of difficulty (accessed by anyone via LMS Moodle implemented as H5P module
e) Virtual mass spectrometry lab with three AR training scenarios – AR Sample Preparation, AR Wardrobe Preparation and AR Measurement, which are all accessible via the AREEKA app by anyone.
f) Progressive Web App of the COVIMO project
2) A manual of good practices:  an online application to provide guidance for good and bad practices in online education (https://app.covimo.czu.cz/).
3) Scenarios of Reactions:  a) Scenarios of Reactions in higher education; b) Community Garden Summary and Guidelines.
4) Learning Materials Facilitating Inclusion into Online Education – two LMS Moodle modules created as learning materials and training toolkits enabling students and staff to adapt to online education.

2020-1-CZ01-KA226-HE-094462.title: Virtual Visiting Professors
2020-1-CZ01-KA226-HE-094462.summary:
<< Background >>

In the context of constraints appearing due to the COVID-19 pandemic, it has been demonstrated that teachers as well as students are capable of accommodating to teaching and learning patterns different from the traditional ones. Once new methods, techniques and organizational measures are put in place and combined with the necessary mental adjustments, what would have been formerly considered limitations may have turned out to be completely new opportunities. One such perceived COVID-19-related limitation-turned-out-to-be-opportunity was the internationalization of undegraduate education using new means of delivery.

<< Objectives >>

To identifiy and eliminate obstacles to teaching joint classes of students transnationally, establish viable process frameworks to facilitate the complete preparation and implementation of such courses, and develop a set of courses including teaching materials to enable validation of the concept and meaningfully initiate such a program. To enhance international cooperation of the partners and motivate students and teachers to become more international.

<< Implementation >>

Besides project management and the creation of the intellectual outputs, which included the implementation of the course methodology and the implementation of the OER methodology in all institutions, as well as the delivery of three pilot courses, the project included three Multinational Project Mettings, held in Kaunas, Osijek and Prague, a training event in Kaunas, and multiplier events held in Prague, Kaunas and Osijek.

<< Results >>

Nine undergraduate university courses, including syllabi and the pertinent sets of teaching and self-study materials in the form of open education resources. A documented methodology for developing further open education resources. Delivery of three of the courses, including complete e-learning support material, as pilots during the project with student participants from all the partner universities, validating the concept, capability to deliver, and quality of execution. All this based on the resolution of a joint implementation of such courses in different organizational and study program environments through a formal agreement.

2020-1-CZ01-KA226-HE-094464.title: Weeks of International Teaching - Inclusive and Digital
2020-1-CZ01-KA226-HE-094464.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project due to the profound impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education in 2020. The project demonstrates a proactive response to the challenges posed by the pandemic and a commitment to supporting educators and students in adapting to the new online teaching environment. By focusing on cooperation, networking, and the development of resources, we aimed to make a positive impact on education during these unprecedented times.  

The global health crisis necessitated a swift transition to online teaching, which presented numerous challenges for both teachers and students. The acquisition of new technical skills and the adaptation of teaching methodologies to the digital environment are indeed crucial for effective online teaching. By providing teachers with the necessary skills and knowledge, we aimed to empower them to excel in the digital teaching landscape and ensure quality education for their students. 

Moreover, by emphasizing the importance of cooperation and networking between organizations, we aimed to create a collaborative environment where knowledge and resources can be shared. This approach not only strengthens the educational community but also promotes collective learning and problem-solving.

<< Objectives >>

Project had 4 Intellectual Outputs (IO),Project Management Handbook,Dissemination Plan,Final Quality Report,Final Dissemination and Impact Report.Main results were the development of guidelines on International Weeks and e-Toolkit.Guidelines provide comprehensive recommendations and best practices for organizing international events covering various aspects,such as identifying competencies,analyzing teaching and learning methodologies in the context of global mobility and addressing security considerations in the digital world.They serve as a valuable resource for institutions planning and implementing similar international events, ensuring effective and successful outcomes.A complex Web-based e-learning Toolkit is an online resource designed to enhance international mobility&digital competencies in higher education.It offers a wide range of learning modules,interactive activities,multimedia resources,and collaborative tools,that can be accessed remotely,to support both students and teachers in their mobility experiences while improving their digital skills and knowledge.It also includes an assessment component to help measure and track competence growth,allowing users to monitor their progress and identify areas for improvement.

<< Implementation >>

Several workshops and events aimed at enhancing teachers' skills in digital teaching and providing a platform for participants to put their theoretical knowledge into practice happened: 
Workshops for Teachers (WS): 2 WS designed to introduce innovative tools, enhance skills and knowledge, and provide new approaches in digital teaching.They took place in Heraklion (2021) and in Luxembourg (2022). 
Weeks of International Teaching (WIT): events served as a platform for participants to put theoretical knowledge into practice.Through cultural activities, WS, and networking opportunities, participants had de opportunity to share best practices and enhance their intercultural competencies. WITs were held in Heraklion (2023) and in Brno (2022). 
Symposium "Enhancing 4 IN’s in digital teaching practices" aimed to disseminate the project's outcomes and share knowledge on organizing innovative and inclusive WIT. 
In addition, there were regular project meetings among the WITEA-ID members on a monthly basis.The Project Executive Board also holds monthly meetings to oversee the project's progress. Furthermore, there were specific meetings including the Kick-off meeting (held online), Intermediate meeting, Final meeting, and Final meeting 2.0.

<< Results >>

In addition to the activities,the project had 4 Intellectual Outputs (IO),Project Management Handbook and Dissemination Plan.The main results were the development of guidelines on International Weeks and e-Toolkit.The guidelines provide comprehensive recommendations and best practices for organizing international events covering various aspects, such as identifying competencies,analyzing teaching and learning methodologies in the context of global mobility, and addressing security considerations in the digital world.Guidelines serve as a valuable resource for institutions planning and implementing similar international events, ensuring effective and successful outcomes.The complex Web-based e-learning Toolkit is an online resource designed to enhance international mobility & digital competencies in higher education.It offers a wide range of learning modules,interactive activities,multimedia resources, and collaborative tools, that can be accessed remotely,to support both students and teachers in their mobility experiences while improving their digital skills and knowledge.It also includes an assessment component to help measure and track competence growth,allowing users to monitor their progress and identify areas for improvement.

2020-1-DE01-KA226-HE-005758.title: Practising Transnational Politics in Blended Learning
2020-1-DE01-KA226-HE-005758.summary:
<< Background >>

PATRAPO offered a singular opportunity to make an essential contribution to the development of a) teaching curricula in the participating institutions and b) the international MUN community within the European context. The project aimed at developing and teaching hybrid tri-national MUN preparation seminars in cooperation with universities from Madrid, Zagreb, and Fulda, and at developing the related teaching material. MUN is a worldwide practice of simulating the political processes and procedures of the UN. 
The project:
-	addressed the further development of the practice of MUNs.
-	helped to establish a transnational European network of three universities for training and conducting MUNs within the European context.
-	developed a training programme that combines teaching materials and hybrid trinational classes with best-practice models in a self-learning system in joint-blended learning environments.
-	enabled the productive fusion of skill training and the teaching of International Relations and transnational politics by jointly developing teaching kits for a two-semester series of online blended learning seminars. 
-	ensured the accessibility of training for MUNs by creating an open-access handbook and open access teaching kits.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project PATRAPO, the team was able to develop a best-practice teaching framework that:
-	can be obtained open access.
-	can be sustainably implemented in any faculty of International Relations, Political Sciences, or other related fields at any university. 
-	can be taught in a joint and blended manner in several institutions simultaneously and thus create networks between the involved universities, teachers, and participants. 
-	strengthens the practice-oriented approach of teaching International Relations and Political Science, which goes beyond teaching systems, functioning, and interests and reflects upon the daily routines and the unofficial aspects of making politics.
-	actively involves students in their learning as it requires them to conduct research and develop solutions.
-	can be adapted to integrate current and important historical, political, and situational changes.
 
Furthermore, by implementing such a teaching framework, the team wanted to achieve a more substantial representation of teaching with and for MUNs within Europe.

<< Implementation >>

–	Two seminar curricula were developed in a learning system. 
–	In each academic year of the project, two seminars for in-depth preparation for MUN were developed and carried out by the trinational group of university teachers.
–	Two MUNs took place in Fulda. The 2022 MUN was a hybrid conference, and the 2023 MUN was an in-person conference. In both conferences, students from all partner universities (including the associate partner from Edmonton and students from Ukraine) conducted a four-day MUN simulation. The conferences included a cultural programme to strengthen cooperation. 
–	Regular team meetings took place to plan, carry out, and evaluate the project’s progress.
–	Long-term implementation and sustainability was obtained because PATRAPO produced seminar structures, materials, and curricula through a learning system that will guide MUN seminars at universities and worldwide in the organisation and implementation of MUN seminars and conferences. 
–	The project built structures to provide long-term benefits by developing and strengthening several valuable and vital diplomatic competencies. It implemented a joint ECTS grading scheme and increased the networking competencies of the students through collaboration in the seminars.

<< Results >>

–	Outputs: The seminar series, the MUNs, and the development of teaching kits for two semesters plus a handbook on how to implement them. The latter three represent the IOs. 
–	Successful dissemination: The teaching kits and the handbook will be included in an open-access publication with Edward Elgar. The volume is edited by the Fulda PI (Prof. Wiesner) and the Project Vice Leader (Prof. Liste).
–	Dissemination to various audiences: The project targeted different audiences through social media, coverage in local newspapers, TV, and radio. 
–	Sustainable additions to teaching programmes in partner universities: The project permanently sustainably established the joint blended MUN training seminars at the partner universities as part of their respective study programmes. 
–	Long-term cooperation: The exchange and set-up of a blended learning seminar structure have fostered the cooperation between the European partner universities and the associate partner in Canada and have grown into a solid basis for further collaborations. A cooperation with UCU, Lviv, has been sustainably established.

2020-1-DE01-KA226-HE-005763.title: Creating social impact through customized digital teaching formats
2020-1-DE01-KA226-HE-005763.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the Erasmus+ project to address crucial needs in higher education institutions (HEIs) and contribute to positive social development. The European Commission's agenda highlighted the importance of societal engagement, yet mechanisms for civic involvement were underdeveloped. The pandemic emphasized HEIs' role in societal recovery, while the shift to online teaching posed challenges for disciplines relying on face-to-face interaction.

There was a digital literacy gap among HEI educators, hindering social impact. Our project aimed to provide easy-to-implement digital teaching formats, bridging this gap and fostering adaptable approaches. We aimed to provide knowledge of barriers and drivers of social impact teaching, offering user-friendly digital tools and strengthening the connection between science and society.

Ultimately, our goal was to improve online teaching performance, support the transition to hybrid environments, and bridge the digital divide among HEI educators. By addressing these needs, we aimed to transform higher education, enhance social impact, and strengthen HEIs' engagement with society.

<< Objectives >>

Our Erasmus+ project aimed to achieve the following objectives:
1) We sought to increase awareness and knowledge of successful digital teaching formats for social impact through a Best Practice Audit (IO1). 
2) We wanted to enable lecturers to increase their social impact through a digital social impact course toolkit, a user-friendly configurator (IO2). 
3) We aimed to achieve scalability of the configurator. Therefore, we conducted iterative pilot tests with social partners to refine it (IO3). 
4) Our project also focused on developing the skills of both educators and students in adopting societal challenge-based digital teaching formats. We aimed to disseminate the acquired knowledge to the wider public (IO4) and increase our institution's reach in society. 
5) Moreover, we aimed to create new ways for organizations to leverage digital technologies for social impact, improve the educational system, and strengthen the involvement of HEIs in broader societal issues. 
6) We aimed to empower educators and improve educational outcomes through a people-centered approach and by providing examples and bridging the digital divide, thereby also increasing the social outreach of our organizations.

<< Implementation >>

As part of our Erasmus+ research project, we implemented several activities.
1) In the research phase (IO1), we reviewed scientific literature, conducted a survey, and conducted 50 expert interviews to gather quantitative and qualitative data on social impact teaching. We identified 20 best practice cases. This culminated in a Best Practice Audit, which outlines key phases and success factors of digital social impact teaching.
2) We created a website and prioritized key features for the digital course configurator (IO2), integrating expertise in science-to-society transfer and digital teaching to achieve societal impact.
3) For the pilot phase (IO3), we first internally tested the configurator, designed pilot courses at multiple institutions, and delivered them in collaboration and cooperation with social organizations. Feedback from stakeholders was collected and used for further refinement.
4) We created guidelines and videos for the configurator as well as prepared course templates meant to give inspiration for further implementations (IO4).
5) As the last part of the project, we held multiplier events in Croatia, Slovenia, and Germany, further disseminating the project's outputs and achievements.

<< Results >>

Our project had a significant impact, producing concrete outputs and results. 
1) Our first concrete output is the comprehensive Best Practice Audit. We analyzed drivers and barriers of social impact courses through a literature review, surveys, and 50 expert interviews. This led to identifying three phases of social impact courses (design, delivery, reflection) and 20 best practice cases. So far, this report has been downloaded 593 times.
2) Our second key output is the digital Course Configurator, guiding educators through the design, delivery, and reflection phases with suitable activities and tools. It also includes a video and "How to" guidelines. The configurator empowers educators to address social challenges and effectively engage with social partners. Configured courses broaden students' understanding, fostering entrepreneurial and social thinking. So far, the pages of the configurator have been accessed by almost 1500 users.
3) We developed 20 pre-configured templates for social impact courses, inspiring lecturers.
4) Multiplier events were conducted, reaching 140 national and international participants and further disseminating the results.
5) An internal sustainability workshop created various ideas to foster further sustainability and use of the created outputs.

2020-1-DE01-KA226-HE-005783.title: Partnership for virtual laboratories in civil engineering
2020-1-DE01-KA226-HE-005783.summary:
<< Background >>

The project and the project partners aimed to revolutionize civil engineering education through the use of Virtual Reality (VR) experiments. The project sought to develop a VR concept for conducting experiments, to elaborate of an openly accessible platform for VR experiments, to collaborate with partners to create VR experiments for special laboratory facilities, and to generate an added value for all partners and Europe. It aimed to provide approved e-learning scenarios for a digital and collaborative learning environment, implement collaborative online learning opportunities for M.Sc. students, to enhance the quality and attractiveness of study programs by incorporating inclusive, sustainable, and integrated internationalization and digitalization of curricula with VR labs. The project addressed several needs, including the need to enhance competence by facilitating a better understanding of the learned material, especially in light of the challenges posed by the Covid-19 pandemic's impact on physical lab experiments, address the need for individual e-learning materials and didactics in the context of online learning, as well as prepare the next generation of the workforce for multi-disciplinary blended learning expertise.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the project were multifaceted, aiming to address various needs within the field of civil engineering education, especially considering the challenges posed by the Covid-19 pandemic and the transition to online learning. The primary goals included the development of a VR-based experiment concept, the elaboration of an open platform to host these experiments, and the integration of state-of-the-art VR experiments from each project partner's laboratories into this platform. Additionally, the project aimed to provide approved e-learning scenarios to facilitate digital and collaborative learning environments. This objective capitalized on the expertise and specialized facilities of our partners, particularly for the newly introduced jointly taught M.Sc. and Ph.D. courses in civil engineering. Another important objective was to implement collaborative online international learning opportunities for M.Sc. students across partner universities. Ultimately, we aimed to enhance the quality and appeal of study programs at the project partners, achieved through inclusive, sustainable, and integrated internationalization and digitalization of curricula, thus improving their international competitiveness.

<< Implementation >>

The project included several transnational meetings, starting with a kick-off meeting in Osijek (HR), followed by a didactic meeting in Bochum (D), a milestone meeting in Aveiro (PT), and a new-path meeting in Skopje (MKD). These meetings primarily focused on partner agreements, project status updates, and the planning of future project activities. Additionally, the project was promoted and disseminated at various venues (see section 6.2). Three learning and teaching activities were organized as part of the project. First, an e-tutor training course was conducted at Bauhaus-University in Weimar. This course aimed to provide lecturers with didactic principles and digital tools to support the development and implementation of e-learning scenarios. Furthermore, an advanced training course in Aveiro (PT) was divided into an online part and a one-week hybrid part (which was conducted twice, once in 2022 and once in 2023). The project also involved an international elective blended course “pilot course” module for structural engineering M.Sc. students, designed to serve as an example of collaborative teaching and learning, where the project's achievements were implemented and tested. The pilot course run from October 2022 to March 2023.

<< Results >>

The project produced significant results including three intellectual outputs: 1) Instructional Design Guide (which provides a methodological framework for didactics of the media learning environment); 2)  Methods and algorithms for the evaluation of digital learning tools evaluation (which includes the guidelines for evaluation and tools for quantitative analysis); 3) Set of remote-access experiments in civil engineering accessible via the virtual environment (including boundary layer wind tunnel experiments at RUB, non-destructive and destructive experiments on shaking table at IZIIS, and fire resistance tests at UA). In terms of learning and training activities, materials and teaching tools for advanced courses were developed, including tools and techniques for efficient employment of VR environments. The project also resulted in several publications and presentations to disseminate the project’s achievements. Additional results included an increase in the attractiveness of Civil Engineering studies, the training of M.Sc. and Ph.D. students for future demands in research and practice, as well as the strengthening of existing networks, and the establishment of new networks and partnerships with experts at different institutions.

2020-1-DE01-KA226-HE-005795.title: Inclusive digital education and laboratory training by connecting rail educational laboratories
2020-1-DE01-KA226-HE-005795.summary:
<< Background >>

With the change to distance learning during the Covid-pandemic the practical exercises in engineering study programmes were highly affected. It was the case that some universities, which offer lectures and exercises in the field of railway engineering, had to cancel the entire exercises and some universities developed digital material to replace the onsite exercises. With the extra call for digital education, we saw a perfect opportunity to develop our digital teaching concepts jointly between three universities and to network these institutions. Furthermore there was no teaching material developed on a European Level in the railway sector. As the European Railway sector is still very nationally influenced. But railways are taking a key role in the European Green Deal as a sustainable transport mode, hence it is necessary in that engineering students in Europe have a common understanding of the European railway sector. So that also a need that we´ve identified. Furthermore there is a current and also an arising lack of the labour force in the railway sector. Hence, the project was also possibility in the try out new European approaches for railway exercises.

<< Objectives >>

Our aim was to develop a digital teaching concept for railway exercises in order to have an alternative concept for exercises. Furthermore, the aim was to make the teaching material and concept as generic as possible. This would allow the materials and the concept to be used at European level for academic training in railway engineering, transport and traffic sciences, etc. In addition, documents will be developed that can support interested universities and other institutions if they want to develop academic exercises or set up their own laboratory.

<< Implementation >>

We developed our three Intellectual Outputs and presented them in a final event of the project to the interested audience. The final event was held at TU Braunschweig in February 2023 with guests from different European countries from the Railway sector. In week 49 (2022) a digital exercise with the students from the partner universities of the consortium and CVUT Praha was done. This test was one of the activities of IO 3 to test the developed teaching material. After the test we did a survey throughout the students and teachers to gain feedback of the concept. Furthermore it will be discussed between the partners and other Universities of the railway sectors to do this one week exercise again in the upcoming winter semester (2023) and in the upcoming years. Other universities that could be involved in that exercise will be from the railway sector and transport and traffic field.

<< Results >>

The project produced three Intellectual Outputs as mentioned in the in the proposal and above. IO 1 is a case study about the European railway sector. In this study we investigated the Railway sector in different European countries (mostly that countries were we had access to data). However, the focus was on the labour market and an analysis of the academic railway sector in Europe. IO 2 was focused on the didactical concept for teaching exercises this includes a main document and an extra handbook for trainers, this handbook supports trainers with digital exercises. IO 3 was focused on railway laboratories. This IO includes a main document, where the backgrounds are explained and other OER-teaching material that can be used by the interested audience. Furthermore the generic operational rulebook, the generic introduction for interlockings and the handbook for trainers (IO2) will be offered as documents/products via the IDEALCAREL homepage and by the participating instructions. However, via the Erasmus results platform just the three main documents will be handed in with the hint that there is the possibility to download the main products directly via the IDEALCAREL homepage.
