2020-1-DE02-KA226-VET-008072.title: Protecting the mental well being of our children during and after public health emergencies – digital training for teachers and educators
2020-1-DE02-KA226-VET-008072.summary:
<< Background >>

The Covid-19 pandemic has forced the education community to change teaching methods and students had to adjust to remote learning, deal with social isolation and cope with the uncertainty of the future. It is essential to recognise that students' mental health needs have been affected and that educators play a vital role in supporting them. 
Developing a project that includes the training of teachers on students' mental health needs during public health emergencies is critical in these times. ProWell adressed this need by building innovative learning using digital technologies for teachers and other educators. The ProWell curriculum offers knowledge, guidance and motivation to teachers and other educators to support children during and after public health crises. Teachers who have received the online ProWell training have developed several competences, for instance; how to identify and respond to students' mental health needs and how to foster a supportive and safe learning environment that promotes positive mental health outcomes. The covid-19 pandemic served as an example but the training developed can be applied in any public health emergency.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of this project was to address the mental health needs of children and adolescents during and after public health emergencies. Specifically, the project sought to achieve the following objectives:
1)	Conduct an observation, identification and analysis of training needs and opportunities for mental health support for students in response to public health emergencies.
2)	Support the development of blended and distance training programs that promote mental health wellbeing for children and young people during and after major public health emergencies.
3)	Develop innovative online resources and tools that teachers and educators can use to enhance their knowledge and skills in supporting students' mental health.
4)	Increase teachers' and educators' awareness and preparedness skills in supporting children and young people during and after major public health emergencies.
5)	Enhance partner capabilities to develop and deliver relevant training programs.
6)	Increase awareness and skills of organizations and other stakeholders on the newly produced training and the importance of promoting mental wellbeing in times of public health emergencies.
7)	Raise awareness and create relevant networks across the EU .

<< Implementation >>

1)Mapping of EU and national relevant training was conducted to identify the existing mental health support training available to students during and after public health emergencies. This activity helped to identify gaps in the current training provision and led to an intellectual output and the publication of a scientific article. Another one is still in preparation and will be published by Prolepsis.
2)Focus groups were organized to give voice to the target groups to understand their training needs and expectations. They were conducted in all partner countries. These insights were then used to design a training curriculum and content and develop the e-learning platform. 
3)An e-learning platform and mobile application were developed to provide distance training. The relevant training programs were delivered through the platform to ensure that it reached the target groups across the EU.
4)Guidance for academic institutions was developed to support their role. This guidance provided a framework for designing and delivering training programs that met the needs of the target groups. It also helped to ensure the sustainability of the project by embedding the training programs within the education system.

<< Results >>

The project focused on four main outputs:
The first intellectual output was a result of the focus group discussions and a review of the available training opportunities and programs for target groups in each country. Based on the work done in this output, an Ecosystem Mapping and Methodological Framework were created. Furthermore, alongside to the research work a scientific publication was generated at the TU Dresden.
The second intellectual output consists of the training curriculum and content and is delivered in seven different modules. The content was translated into all seven languages of the consortium: English, French, Greek, Spanish, Italian, Croatian and German.
The third intellectual output consists of an interactive online platform and mobile application, on which the digital training can be completed. It includes the previously developed content, a learning progress check, an evaluation, and a comment section.
A training adaptation toolkit was developed in the fourth intellectual output. It includes guidance for VET providers and academic institutions as well as activities for the implementation of the curriculum in face-to-face, blendend and online trainings.

2020-1-DE02-KA226-VET-008154.title: Fostering diGitalisation and bIonic transformation of SMEs through the development of a novel and innovative Training material for overcoming COVID-19 crisis
2020-1-DE02-KA226-VET-008154.summary:
<< Background >>

Many SMEs face challenges due to a shortage of skilled personnel and an aging workforce. Lifelong learning is crucial to address this issue and foster new capabilities. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of digitalization worldwide, revealing the vulnerability of European industry and the need for resilient organizations, especially SMEs. These enterprises are essential for driving innovation and contributing to a sustainable and digitalized economy. The challenge for SMEs is not just digitization but transforming into "Bionic" firms that combine technology with human and leadership capacities for superior customer experiences, productivity, and innovation. Digital technologies also support the achievement of sustainability goals and the transition to a circular economy. The GIST project aimed to provide innovative training for SMEs, with a focus on the furniture sector, to equip them with the necessary competences. By upskilling and reskilling workers, SMEs could embrace digitalization and contribute to a resilient and sustainable economic model. The project recognized the need for transnational cooperation, bringing together partners from six EU countries to ensure its success.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objective of the GIST project was to develop comprehensive training materials tailored to the specific needs of SMEs in the furniture sector, enabling them to successfully undergo digital transformation and evolve into "Bionic firms." Recognizing the prevailing issue of underinvestment in research, development, innovation, and digitalization within this sector, the project aimed to bridge the gap by equipping SMEs with the essential skills and competences necessary for effective digital transformation. This involved a focused approach on upskilling and reskilling the existing workforce, while simultaneously creating new job opportunities aligned with the requirements of a rapidly evolving digitalized industry. Additionally, the project's overarching ambition was to actively contribute to the realization of a more economically, environmentally, and socially sustainable Europe, reflecting its dedication to supporting the broader transition towards a sustainable future.

The GIST project successfully achieved its predefined objectives, which were as follows:

SO1: Defining the necessary learning outcomes by conducting a thorough analysis of the industry's current digital transformation needs.
SO2: Defining, developing, and validating the structure and methodology of the GIST training course through a collaborative curriculum involving stakeholders, target groups, and associated partners.
SO3: Delivering the training course through an e-learning Open Educational Resources (OER) platform and ensuring its protection under open licenses.
SO4: Conducting a comprehensive evaluation of the e-learning experience through a verification process and implementing improvements based on the project's findings.
SO5: Creating new employment opportunities for individuals equipped with the essential skills required for future integrative, sustainable, and digitalized industries.

These objectives were successfully accomplished, contributing to the overall success and impact of the GIST project.

<< Implementation >>

During the 24 months of the project, numerous activities were carried out, which can be summarized as follows:

Regarding the project implementation activities:

Development of a Quality Assurance and Risk Management plan, as well as monitoring, control, and evaluation of the processes.
Creation of a Dissemination and Communication plan, along with the production of dissemination materials and implementation of various dissemination activities.
Creation and maintenance of the Project Website.
Organization of 5 Transnational Project Meetings (TPMs), with 2 of them conducted through online sessions during the COVID period and 3 held in person.

Implementation of three Intellectual Outputs (IOs):

IO1: GIST Training Path Definition.
IO2: GIST Training Content Development.
IO3: Collaborative Platform and Verification Action.

A Learning, Teaching, and Training activity was carried out in Maribor, Slovenia.

Six multiplier events were organized, one in each partner's country, with the purpose of introducing the project and its context, presenting the GIST project and its e-Learning platform, demonstrating developed materials and instructional examples, and evaluating the event and its content, while gathering feedback from participants. The satisfaction rate among participants in all events exceeded 90%.

<< Results >>

We conducted a comprehensive study to assess the current skills, knowledge, and qualifications relevant to digitalization. Based on the findings, we identified the necessary learning outcomes essential for the development of the training course. Subsequently, we defined the methodology and established the learning paths, resulting in the creation of the Joint Curriculum.

Following this, we meticulously developed structured training content that effectively addressed the previously identified needs. We ensured that all materials were released under open Creative Commons licensing, promoting accessibility and sharing.

Moreover, we successfully created a user-friendly e-learning platform that seamlessly integrated content in all consortium languages. Rigorous testing and validation processes were conducted to ensure the quality and effectiveness of both the platform and the content. This platform serves as a valuable resource for learners and stakeholders.

As tangible outcomes, we have generated various reports available on the project website, which comprehensively describe and reflect a significant portion of the work accomplished. Additionally, we have created a multilingual platform featuring all the integrated training materials in seven languages: English, German, French, Polish, Spanish, Croatian, and Slovenian. Furthermore, the project's website features a dedicated news section that provides regular updates on transnational meetings, learning, 
teaching, and training activities, multiplier events, and more. These updates showcase the project's progress, achievements, and milestones, keeping stakeholders informed and engaged.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2020-1-DE03-KA226-SCH-093406.title: Enactive Learning in Mathematics at Home
2020-1-DE03-KA226-SCH-093406.summary:
<< Background >>

The EnLeMaH project has been created to contribute to the improvement and strengthening of secondary school mathematics learning, a discipline of vital importance for the future labour development of schoolchildren and their active participation in society. The teaching of mathematics, traditionally a difficult subject for many schoolchildren, has taken on a new challenge with the COVID crisis and the subsequent digitalisation process. Enactive learning of mathematics helps students to build a mental network that enables them to understand mathematical concepts and relationships and, above all, how to apply mathematics to everyday life. Enactive methods therefore help to increase the understanding and attractiveness of mathematics and contribute to a greater extent to reducing achievement deficits. To achieve this, it is necessary to first train mathematics teachers in the use of an enactive approach to teaching mathematics. Thus, this project has responded to such needs by helping teachers to (i) acquire innovative digital pedagogical competences to apply an enactive teaching and learning methodology adapted to the context of digital education and (ii) to create enactive materials/activities with focus on mathematical functions.

<< Objectives >>

EnLeMaH has been guided by a main objective on two levels: i) to contribute to the improvement of the teaching-learning process in secondary mathematics ii) using a digital environment. Following the growing need to adapt traditional teaching to digital learning environments, EnLeMaH oriented its work to the creation of a teacher training course (TTC) where it would be possible for teachers to learn to work a) on the one hand with simple and concrete materials that secondary school students could find at home and b) on the other hand by placing the classes in a digital space usable in a distance learning situation. All this, from an enactive approach to the teaching-learning of mathematics.
Taking mathematics teachers as the cornerstone of the improvement of the teaching-learning process, work has been done to equip them with the tools to design enactive learning environments for students themselves on the basis of a thoughtful and criteria-oriented theoretical foundation. This has not only contributed to increasing teachers' knowledge of the subject matter, but also to broadening their knowledge of how to act/interact appropriately from this methodological approach.

<< Implementation >>

The activities implemented during the two years have been comprised of elaboration activities, implementation or impact activities and dissemination activities. In the first group of activities, the creation of the TTC has been the most important. Alongside this, the creation of the course Guidelines and the placement of the course in a digital environment (moodle).
In the second group, the most important activity was the implementation of the TTC with mathematics teachers from the four participating countries, with more participants established as in the application. In addition, numerous Focus Groups have been held to evaluate the learning platform at different stages of its development, an external evaluation of the platform has been carried out at the end. Finally, regular online meetings and 3 Transnational Meetings (TM) have been held.
In the third groups, the holding of Multiplier Events (ME) in the four countries and with the attendance of more than 220 people has been the most important activity carried out. However, also of great importance has been the creation of the website, the social network communication, as well as a multiplicity of smaller dissemination events carried out during the life of the project.

<< Results >>

The central output is the moodle-based learning platform in which the teacher training course is hosted. With the help of this platform, teachers can independently acquire the competences in the field of interactive and digital learning according to the project's objective. In addition, this platform offers the possibility of being imported into local platforms, thus facilitating the work with EnLeMaH contents at school. The platform includes the Guidelines (another main result of the project), learning material for each of the modules, explanatory videos and a repository of enactive activities, among other activities.
In addition to the activities carried out for the quality control and evaluation of the different phases of the project, a series of events have been organised for the dissemination of the project, among which the Multiplier Events are worth mentioning.
The realisation of small TTC at different moments of the project and the work with secondary school mathematics students as part of the practical module of the TTC, have been one of the most relevant non-application results.
Another great result is UNIRI's creation of a 5 ECTS EnLeMaH course integrated into the mathematics education curriculum.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-DE03-KA226-SCH-093713.title: E-Learning through Videos in a European Setting
2020-1-DE03-KA226-SCH-093713.summary:
<< Background >>

The goal of the project ELVES was the development and dissemination of short online videos that cover the math curriculum in primary schools and can be used by math teachers and either integrated into their classes or used as a distance learning tool in situations in which students cannot be at school. The idea was to make the videos easily accessible on every device and easy to share for teachers.
PISA and other forms of evaluating education have shown that in many European countries students are severely lacking even basic skills in mathematics. This contrasts greatly with the goals the European Union has proclaimed in its 2020 strategy. In order to achieve smart, sustainable and inclusive growth and establish Europe as an Innovation Union, good math skills are needed. It is well known that mathematics are a stumbling block for young learners.
Since math skills are so strategically important it is highly relevant to find ways of teaching mathematics, even when a pandemic like the recent COVID-19 situation makes teaching difficult. Primary school teachers were especially badly prepared for handling distance learning because in most cases they have never learned it but the project results are helping with this.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to create an approach which would help out several target groups:
Primary school teachers have a way to show explanations of different math topics in primary school to their students, especially in a distance learning scenario.
Primary school students have a way to review what they learned at school and they can turn to the instructional videos if they miss school (for instance when they are sick).
Parents of primary school students can use the videos to support their children in learning mathematics, even if they themselves do not feel very qualified to explain it.

<< Implementation >>

Our activities were carefully planned in order to create the desired project results and reach the intended project objectives. We started with exchanging information and expertise before we did the research of the math curricula in the different countries. We then started a creativity phase in which we gathered ideas to implement. In this phase we first looked at the already existing knowledge and competences of the partners and made the best possible use of them. This phase also required a lot of creativity in order to come up with ways of motivating learners and appealing to our main target group both in content presentation and functionality. We also needed to come up with an easy way to get teachers involved.
The resulting scripts for the instructional videos were then turned into professional videos with attractive animations and voices. We translated everything into all project languages and we then shared it on the platform we created and disseminated it widely.

<< Results >>

The main results of the project are the creation of a web-based platform to share instructional videos that help students in elementary school learn as well as the instructional videos. 
We put a focus on mathematics and created a large collection of videos that focused on the topics covered in early math education. The topics were chosen after analyzing the curricula in the different project countries.

2020-1-DK01-KA226-VET-094178.title: Ready, Active and Digital
2020-1-DK01-KA226-VET-094178.summary:
<< Background >>

The partners all had experienced a need to equip education and training systems to face the challenges presented by the recent sudden shift to online and distance learning, including supporting teachers to develop digital competences and safeguarding the inclusive nature of learning opportunities, namely the aim was to REACT. And REACT digitally. Reinforcing the ability of education and training institutions and NGOs to provide high-quality, inclusive digital education across small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and public administrations was crucial for several reasons; a.o. empowering individuals and organizations: Digital education empowers individuals and organizations by enabling them to acquire relevant skills, increase their knowledge base, and stay abreast of technological advancements. It equips them with the tools to communicate, collaborate, and access information effectively, fostering a culture of lifelong learning. This empowerment strengthens the capacity of SMEs, NGOs, and public administrations to fulfil their missions, drive innovation, and contribute to societal development, and we wanted to contribute to such an empowerment - meeting evolving needs and challenges.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of the KA2 project REACT Digital is  to reinforce the ability of education and training institutions and NGOs to provide high quality, inclusive digital education. The focus was on building capacity to implement online, blended and distance teaching and learning; to develop digital competences of educators, trainers and teachers, enabling them to deliver high quality inclusive digital education; and to develop and use high quality digital content such as innovative online resources and tools. By the project we addressed the above mentioned needs by developing and implementing Training of Trainers Programme using the ICT and specific tools to deliver quality and inclusive education through online means and by developing specific e-learning materials for educational programmes in the field of project management and entrepreneurial skills. Our ambition was to develop of non-formal digital education by amplifying the competence and capacity of educational and training institutions as well as NGOs. Through the implementation of distance and blended teaching, and a strong emphasis on the development of Teachers Training modules we built on the anticipated that the quality of digital education will be significantly improved

<< Implementation >>

We implemented the project as planned in two phases:

The  first phase of the project contained all the preparatory activities for Learning, Teaching, Training Activity (LTTA) and delivering IO 1- materials for train the trainer course
(blended learning). In this phase, the training key topics were selected and the four training modules developed together with  project website. The common ToT was done in Copenhagen. 3 TPMs were held together with frequent online meetings. 

The second phase was delivering IO2: Developing the e-platform and specific e-learning materials, and development of the technical solutionI, all the materials for educational programs in the field of business and project management, namely: non-formal education programmes in Project Management for NGOs, Entrepreneurial skills for SMEs and Repository for public administration will be developed and uploaded to the e-platform..With an interactive approach among the implementation of platform, training modules and ToT, we executed the teacher training for core trainers in multiplier events (E1-E8), where in O2 we dealt with workshops with target groups (E9-E16). In all 233 new trainers were trained locally. 3+1 TPMs were held together with frequent online meetings

<< Results >>

The project results and outputs are:
- 1 project website and 2 social media developed and established
- 8 Training needs analysis for the ToT of core group
- 4 key topics and materials for the eLearning platform (entrepreneurship, project cycle mangement, communication, and teambuilding) - translated into partner languages 
- 1 common 5-days training program frame developed
- 1 eLearning platform developed and the 4 modules (Moodle) established (in all partner languages - drafted, tested and revised
- 1 ToT for core trainers from partners executed - 22 trainers trained 
- 1 Study visit in Denmark done
- 19 Multimedia tutorials for trainers – ICT tools and programmes (the project YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCJovnEsTNZylYpnz2Z9FWhg)
- 8 local  Training of Trainers – (Learning, Teaching, Training Activity (LTTA)), 126 trainers trained in the 8 partner countries
- 1 evaluation and reporting from the 8 local LTTAs
- 1 needs assesment analysis from 8 partner countries on the materials and topics for the triple helix of NGOs, SMEs and PA (public adm.)
- 1 project evaluation

2020-1-ES01-KA226-HE-096244.title: Digital and Entrepreneurial Skills for European Teachers in the COVID-19 World
2020-1-ES01-KA226-HE-096244.summary:
<< Background >>

COVID-19 caused a sudden and drastic change for educators worldwide. In a matter of days, universities had to transition to online learning, despite the limited resources and support available at the time. The pandemic exposed a significant gap between the needs of teachers and students and the available knowledge and resources, creating several challenges in the classrooms.
eDESK was designed to assist HE educators in exploring new modes of teaching and experimenting with Technology-Enhanced Learning, finding better ways to meet the needs of students, providing resources and support to develop their skills and integrating entrepreneurial competencies into their teaching practices. Aimed to bridge the gap between academia and the job market introducing entrepreneurial competencies that would help students’ employability.
With eDESK, teachers can access tested tools to help them develop their digital and entrepreneurial skills, and offered the educators participating in the project opportunities to meet and network with colleagues from 4 countries, equipping them with the skills and knowledge to navigate the changing landscape of education and prepare students for success in the future

<< Objectives >>

eDESK was designed to provide a solution to the challenges faced by European educators due to COVID-19, developing digital and entrepreneurial skills. By introducing new delivery modes to educators, eDESK aimed to adapt to the changing needs and scenarios of education through Technology-Enhanced Learning. The use of TEL allows educators to reach more students and create new opportunities for learning, and we aimed to promote the benefits of key entrepreneurial competencies among teachers and educators using the EntreComp framework. By focusing on these competencies, we help educators to find innovative solutions and contribute to improve students' employability.
The project wanted to support teachers in the conception, design, and implementation of their training and lessons knowing their students' needs and expectations, creating an approach where educators are encouraged to be innovative and to think outside the box to create new learning opportunities. Having the opportunity to interact with colleagues from other countries also enabled educators to network and share best practices to find synergies, leading to the development of new ideas and solutions, new opportunities for learning and preparing students for the future.

<< Implementation >>

Apart from PM activities (WP1), including among others organising the PM platform and internal comm. channels, setting up the QAC, follow-up meetings in Finland, Croatia, Portugal and Spain, or activities related to external communication (WP2) such as the webpage, social media, multimedia content or materials, eDESK implemented several activities to support educators in enhancing their knowledge related to entrepreneurial and digital skills. After the WP3 survey among educators of the 4 HEI partners of the project, leading to the design of the eDESK Methodology, integrated with EntreComp and DigComp frameworks, WP4 activities implemented the development and launch of a complete MOOC in 3 learning platforms, which included 11 modules and 50 training hours. WP5 led the design of teaching materials and produced a toolkit for educators, and a 3-day staff for teachers from the 4 countries, analysing how to incorporate the knowledge gained from the MOOC into their classes, the possibilities of hybrid teaching and worked on a portfolio to help them develop the 40 pilot experiences to test the eDESK materials with their students during WP6. Finally, WP7 activities focused on dissemination and organising 4 multiplier events in 4 countries

<< Results >>

eDESK produced a training methodology and tools for educators aimed at being replicable and scalable, tested to ensure the quality of the resources created. 
Main results:
An edited eDESK methodology, including findings from our survey within 167 educators from 4 HEI and case studies, available as an OER in 5 languages (ENG, SP, PT, CRO and FIN). Downloaded 795 times.
The “eDESK: Digital and entrepreneurial teachers for a fast-changing world” MOOC, with 11 different modules, 50 hours of training and materials like H5P, 51 videos, written texts, self-assessment tools, etc. With more than 1000 participants at MiriadaX, UC Moodle, FOI Moodle, and NAU platforms, and available for free. eDESK digital and multimedia guide has been downloaded 564 times.
eDESK Toolkit on the implementation of our methodology, to help educators to implement what they have learned in the MOOC into their classes, used in 40 pilot experiences in 4 countries. Available as an OER in 5 languages, by the time of this report it’s been downloaded 776 times.
A joint staff training with 46 participants from 4 countries. 
More than 3000 social media followers and 150000 visits to the webpage.
Multiplier events in 4 countries.
1 paper was published, 1 in preparation.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-ES01-KA226-SCH-096156.title: Integrating Special Needs Individuals into Digital-Holistic Education
2020-1-ES01-KA226-SCH-096156.summary:
<< Background >>

This project was requested after identifying a problem in ensuring a better inclusion in online education for students with specific educational needs (SEN), which became necessary during the COVID-19 lockdown period. Education had to rapidly adapt to working in this format, and in this process, the attention that SEN students required took a backseat, compromising their educational and inclusive needs. The addressed needs in ensuring their access to digital education, a lack of quality tools and resources for teaching these students through this methodology, as well as specific training for teachers and families who took on greater responsibility in this scenario of education outside of school.

<< Objectives >>

This project aimed to change the previous paradigm and mitigate the digital/social gap identified among students with special educational needs. The specific objectives of the project were:
1. Ensure that students with SEN had access to free materials to work on self-care, social, and everyday life skills.
2. Provide the European educational community and educational organizations with high-quality digital materials for working with these students on these skills.
3. Enhance the development of digital competence in the participating institutions in the project.
4. Foster a global European perspective among these students, as well as the involved teachers and families.
5. Present a module of lessons that would be useful for teachers and families working with this type of student.

<< Implementation >>

A research was conducted to identify the educational needs of teachers when it comes to instructing students with special educational needs in the context of online education, taking into account the cultural differences, teaching models, and legislation among the participating partners. Based on the results of this research, a series of topics related to social skills, self-care, and daily care were selected for primary and secondary education levels. Additionally, teachers and technical staff were trained in the four Learning, Teaching, and Training (LTT) activities of the project, and the intellectual outputs (IO1: Social Inclusive Module, IO2: Mobile App, IO3: Web-Platform) were prepared, which were subsequently promoted by the different participating organizations through two multiplier events and various project dissemination activities.

<< Results >>

After completing the project, we have obtained three Intellectual Outputs. IO1  is Digital Inclusive / Social Education Module that includes a guide with 24 teaching scenarios for primary and secondary students with SEN to work on social, self-care, and daily care skills in different applicable classroom, online, and potential lockdown scenarios. These activities have been reviewed to ensure they are adapted to the cultural environments where they will be implemented. IO2: Digital Education Content Whole (Mobile App) is a mobile application that, in the form of an interactive video game, allows students with special educational needs to work on these concepts through a total of 60 challenges for primary and secondary students. Finally, IO3 is an E-Learning Platform for Special Education that facilitates access and dissemination of the generated resources and application.

All the generated resources are available in English as well as in the languages of the participating project partners (Spanish, Portuguese, Polish, Romanian, Croatian, and Turkish).
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-ES01-KA226-VET-096090.title: 2B-DIGITAL: Digital competences for a successful adaptation and engagement to on-line VET teaching and learning
2020-1-ES01-KA226-VET-096090.summary:
<< Background >>

The reasoning behind 2BDigital is to diminish the impact of COVID-19. It highlighted the necessity for individuals to adapt to a digital society. 2BDigital addresses the urgent needs of VET teachers and learners, particularly those at risk of dropout. It supports effective digital teaching and learning, mitigating the impact of COVID-19 on education inequalities and youth unemployment. By enhancing teachers' digital pedagogical competencies, the project boosts student engagement in online education, reduces dropouts, and promotes transversal and digital competencies. Moreover, VET programs, have higher dropout rates compared to general programs, exacerbating equity concerns. The socioeconomic crisis resulting from the pandemic has increased inequalities and unemployment rates. Students with special educational needs and socioeconomic difficulties face additional obstacles to online learning. By providing high-quality, inclusive online training and supporting teachers' ICT skills for teaching, the project protects educational opportunities for all students, especially those at risk. Furthermore, it bridges the training gap, improves online education, and reduces dropout rates, ultimately promoting better outcomes for VET learners.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of 2BDigital encompass enhancing the transition of VET teachers to digital education by improving their teaching effectiveness and preventing burnout, and promoting higher engagement in online education among VET students to reduce dropouts and early leavings, and facilitate their personal and professional development for enhanced employability in the new digital society. The primary focus is on meeting the competence needs of teachers and students in their digital teaching and learning experiences. The project is a response to the current demand across partner countries to modernize VET and enhance the pedagogical digital competences of teachers. These competences will enable them to effectively adapt to online teaching and support student engagement, thus mitigating dropouts. Ultimately, the project aims to ensure equal learning opportunities for all students, both during and after this challenging crisis, enabling them to fully realize their potential. Additionally, the project encircles various dimensions, including education, social innovation and inclusion, and entrepreneurship. By integrating these aspects, 2BDigital strives to contribute to a comprehensive and well-rounded educational experience.

<< Implementation >>

By activities we presume : Newsletter, Events (conference, workshops, seminar etc.) , Emails, Interviews, Meeting, Specialized press –
industrial magazines, academic journals, radio broadcast etc., Social Media campaign, Printed materials, Internal communication channels
Overall, the project had an excellent reach among the target audience, partners, and their stakeholders. The total number of audiences reached during the duration of the project is 7.435.864. Complementary with Exploitation strategy, Dissemination shows serious commitment of thepa rtnership to the task. The goal of the dissemination, which was to promote the project, its results, and outputs primarily among VET teachers, providers and stakeholders, has definitely been achieved in all partner countries, and further. The partners have disseminated the project through 4 newsletters, several webpages, and social media posts. The information about the project was also disseminated through two presentations (delivered by all the Partners) at international/EU webinars. Those efforts have made it possible to guarantee the sustainability of 2BDigital outcomes and results.
---------------
watch the dissemination summary

<< Results >>

2BDigital achieved all the objectives initially discussed and presented with all partner contributions. Our key achievements are described below:
IO1: Exectured a comparative analysis for integrating frameworks (Entrecomp, LifeComp, and Digicomp, among others), created the initial 2BD Competences Framework, conducted multi-stakeholder consultations with experts, companies, and entrepreneurs, and improved and finalized the 2BDigital Competence Framework based on stakeholder feedback.
IO2: Designed the 2BDigital online teaching and learning methodology, developed the 2BD methodology based on models and practices, and performed online training for VET teachers based on their preferences and needs to be able to conduct classes within our methodology.
IO3: Designed our online assessment methodology, established a baseline, researched assessment approaches conducted, and upgraded our online competence evaluation tool, J4T, for usability and functionality, with translations of all partners' languages. Moreover, a set of teachers from all organizations conducted sessions using the 2BD methodology with their students to better their digital competencies.

2020-1-FI01-KA226-HE-092531.title: Developing Digital Physics Laboratory Work for Distance Learning
2020-1-FI01-KA226-HE-092531.summary:
<< Background >>

The DigiPhysLab -project stemmed from the disturbances to teaching caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. As campuses closed down, lecture-based teaching was moved to online format without major changes. But laboratory work, which is an essential part of physics education at the university-level, could not be moved online so easily. Many lab tasks relied on equipment only available on campuses. Ad hoc solutions such as using videorecordings of data collection etc. were used to retain some form of authenticity even when learning from home.

The use of mobile phones etc. to conduct lab work was not new, but the COVID-19 pandemic really highlighted the need to collect and develop physics lab tasks that would use modern digital equipment and be suitable for distance learning.

On top of the pandemic, recent reforms to physics lab work have called for a shift in focus. Instead of developing content knowledge (i.e. reinforcement of the lecture content), labs should focus on developing experimental skills such as experimental design and data analysis. There was a need for lab tasks that clearly focused on developing these experimental skills.

<< Objectives >>

Our objective was to support physics instructors around the world in implementing high-quality, experimental skills -focused lab tasks that are suitable for both in-campus and distance learning and that use the possibilites of modern digital technologies. This was to be achieved through three outputs: a set of 15 high-quality, experimental skills -focused lab tasks, a research-based framework for instructors who want to design new lab tasks and an evaluation instrument that can be used to evaluate individual lab tasks.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented LTT events in all of the partner organizations. There were 3 LTT events and they 1) allowed the staff and students of the participating organizations to provide input of the project team's work and thus improve the quality of the outputs and 2) allowed the project team a chance to learn about how physics lab work is implemented in different national context which aided the team in designing tasks that could be used in multiple contexts internationally and 3) the project team shared the status of the project to those present and presented the ideas and rationale behind physics lab tasks involving modern digital technology.

<< Results >>

1. We developed and piloted 15 high-quality, experimental skills -focused lab tasks. These tasks can be implemented in university physics lab courses around the world. Most of these tasks are novel and have been developed purely in the DigiPhysLab -project. Others are using ideas from earlier tasks but they have been refined to be experimental skills -focused.
2. We developed a research-based framework that can serve as a supporting tool for instructors who want to design new lab tasks. This sort of a framework was missing from the literature. The framework can also be used to classify existing lab tasks based on their properties.
3. We developed an evaluation instrument that can be used to evaluate individual lab tasks and how they are perceived by the students. The instrument consists of closed and open-ended items and is based on literature. The instrument is novel as previously available evaluation tools for lab work were targeting whole lab courses and not individual tasks.

2020-1-FR01-KA226-SCH-095358.title: Next Generation Digital Learning
2020-1-FR01-KA226-SCH-095358.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because Covid 19 crisis created serious inequalities within our school based in Tahiti, especially during containment period. At the period of call for project, our territory suffered from a very important lack of connection to internet. There was no fiber at all, very low banwidth internet access. Moreover, most families have a poor standard of living and could not offered a computer , tablet, laptop or smartphone to all of their children.  Teachers and students faced many problems to guarantee the pedagogical continuity to avoid the increase of drop out which is really important in French Polynesia, Moreover there is no wifi in the school for the students and as it is very large, the wifi dedicated to teachers is not available in all buildings.
As Covid 19 impacted all countries in the world, we discovered very quickly that many countries were facing similar problems even if their local 
 infrastructures and equipment allowed teachers and Children to work with distance learning, on a technical aspect. But teachers all had in common, the difficulties to be  trained to different digital tools during covid and beyond this period . The suddenness of the pandemic situation created panic .

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project, we wanted to achieve several objectives :

-To recognize new generation teaching tools through collaboration and partnership to share good practices on how to use these teaching tools, and to integrate new generation learning/teaching tools into educational programs.
-To enable individuals to receive education regardless of time and place by using communication tools.
-To develop the competencies of institutions to use synchronous and asynchronous distance education tools.
-To strengthen cooperation and network among institutions.
-To reduce educational inequalities in terms of access to technology.
-To develop an international network among colleagues and to encourage digital school applications.
-Ensuring that students actively participate in the distance education process and use information and communication technologies effectively in the learning-teaching process.
- To ensure that students actively participate in the distance learning process and use information and communication technologies to raise digital awareness of students in 21st-century digital skills.
-To draw the attention of public authorities to invest in infrastructures and dispatch them all other  the most unequipped territories
-Strengthen the digital skills and competences of teachers, and thus also of students

<< Implementation >>

Many digital  activities were implemented and were different from one country to another, according to the initial project. We had also   some common activities such as online meetings  Every country presented web tools to other partners during these on line meetings.
Each school organised LTTA (Learning Training Teachning Activities) to exchange examples of good practices, and to attend  different courses using digital Tools.
Other  activitities were devoted to each country such as creation and adminsitration of surveys to measure the improvement of digital tools practice among teachers and students of all schools, promotion of outputs for the Portuguese team .
Croatian activities were focused on creation of logos and posters, and testing of numerous tools with students: Canva, Mind map, Mentimeter, Microsoft teams, Google classroom, ..... We worked in eTwinning platform that was a part of this project.

French Polynesian team French team coordinated the project on all aspects but also  organised a training session on Book Creator, web tools testings
Turkish teams organised also LTTA sessions

<< Results >>

- Fairs with posters, exhibitions
- 3 surveys analysis  to measure the improvement of digital tools practice, country by country, among teachers and students.
- the common creation of a  free ebook in 5 languages (link ?) for any person who wants to learn digital tools
- awareness of public authorities, Teachers, Students of the importance of digital tools in Education
- the general feeling to be in a good position for the future, either for teachers or  Students, in order to overcome the difficulties due to  a pandemic  or any future crisis. We reduce the fear to learn alone.
-the creation of project management tools for the financial and administrative follow up of Erasmus projects (working hours, section by section)
- the discovery of unknown cultures
- the possibility of including countries from ultra-peripheric regions within european KA2 projects
- promotion tools of  this project (e twinning, press reltion, fairs....)
-we wanted to train teachers to use web tools of the 21st century , thus involving students in modern learning , which we achieved. All our students use on a daily basis some of the web tools we learned to use in this pproject, for example Canva.

2020-1-FR01-KA226-SCH-095602.title: The Virtual Museum of STEM
2020-1-FR01-KA226-SCH-095602.summary:
<< Background >>

The EU faces high underachievement rates in mathematics (22.4%) and sciences (21.6%) according to the latest PISA results (2018). The European Commission's target of less than 15% underachievement has not been met, and science performance has worsened. Innovative teaching methods are necessary to tackle these issues.

A report by DG EAC highlights the importance of learner motivation and engagement in STEM subjects, which often have a negative image as difficult and disconnected from real-life. This perception discourages students, particularly girls, underprivileged individuals, and those already struggling, from pursuing STEM careers.

The COVID-19 pandemic emphasized the need for tailored teaching and learning experiences. School closures necessitated adaptation to virtual classrooms, revealing the importance of increased interactivity and student autonomy. Underperforming students were particularly affected by closures, and even high achievers became disengaged. Educators must respond inclusively and prioritize students' needs to enable students to learn at their own pace.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project and its outputs, we pursued the following impacts:
- innovative teaching methods and digital skills for STEM educators,
- increased access to gamified/interactive pedagogical resources for STEM education in secondary schools,
- improvement of the distance teaching offer and experience for teachers and students
- improvement of performance in STEM among students,
- increased access to innovative learning methods, tools and environments for learners with learning and behaviour disorders (dys, ADHD, etc.),
- increasing the appeal of STEM subjects and careers for girls and marginalised groups, who are often less attracted by or directed towards these skills and subjects,
- increasing involvement and agency of students in their learning process (learning to learn competence).

<< Implementation >>

Target groups :
- secondary school students (aged 10 to 18), including students with fewer opportunities,
- secondary school teachers

The partners have created a virtual museum accessible from a web browser without an account, containing 60 collections on concepts and subjects in science, technology, engineering and mathematics taught at secondary level.
These collections contain interactive elements, information on the principles of the concept, its history, the key people involved in its development or discovery, and examples of its application in real life, in order to make STEM concepts more concrete for pupils.
This museum is accompanied by several guides for teachers, described in the next question.

The museum and its collections have been tested with 505 pupils and 16 secondary school teachers in the 5 partner countries.

To disseminate the project, the partners communicated throughout the project, reaching 264757 people. Multiplier events allowed to reach 132 participants.

<< Results >>

The practical results of this project are:
- the creation of the first European entirely virtual STEM museum,
- a pedagogical guide on virtual museums and their benefits for STEM education, including a chapter gathering teachers’ expectations and testimonies,
- A virtual STEM exhibition creation guide, to share the method developed in the project with anybody wishing to replicate a similar experiment (for other topics, etc),
- A short user’s guide for teachers to know how to integrate the use of the museum in their practice,
- 60 virtual collections related to the STEM program in secondary education, organised in 4 collections:
(1) the Science Exhibition (20 collections);
(2) the Exhibition of Technological Advancements (10 collections);
(3) the Contemporary Engineering Collections (20 collections);
(4) the Exhibition of Hidden Mathematics (10 collections).

Available in 5 languages (English, Croatian, French, Greek, Portuguese) on the project’s website : http://www.vmstem.eu/

2020-1-FR01-KA226-VET-094951.title: The VET-ification of Online Gaming through innovative challenge based learning
2020-1-FR01-KA226-VET-094951.summary:
<< Background >>

In 2018, 16.5% of young people aged 20 to 34 in Europe were neither in employment nor in training (NEET), which represents a significant number of people who are no longer in contact with the labour market or the education and training system in their country. To this number must soon be added the negative impact of COVID-19 on employment, which will increase exponentially. Furthermore, throughout Europe, women NEETs are much more numerous than men.

CASINO project therefore worked to develop innovative challenge-based educational resources that provide easy and attractive access to education and training for these target groups.

The aim was to address the lack of education, training and employment opportunities for NEETs, which can have long-term negative effects on their lives and on the economy as a whole, while at the same time empowering and building the skills of VET professionals working with disadvantaged young people.

<< Objectives >>

CASINO project aimed to develop training materials to make Vocational Education and Training (VET) more gamified through challenge-based e-learning while promoting social inclusion and equal opportunities.

This involved creating (i) digital games that can be accessed on smartphones or tablets and (ii) continuing education for VET professionals. All of this was to be accessible from a free, open access MOOC platform that did not require any prerequisites for use.

These resources based on integrated learning challenges aimed at developing the basic skills of NEETs and the digital skills of VET professionals. For the former, it was also to build their self-confidence and self-esteem in a tangible and immediate way, while helping them to realise that they have relevant and appropriate skills, regardless of their previous educational experience, and to encourage them to build up a portfolio of skills.

<< Implementation >>

In order to carry out the project, in addition to the transversal activities concerning (i) coordination and implementation, (ii) quality control and continuous evaluation of the process and (iii) dissemination and exploitation of the project results, the CASINO partnership has developed innovative tools by carrying out various activities (research, analyses, field experiments, creation of tools, etc.) and by soliciting different means and resources, both internally (from the organisations and the partnership) and externally (in the partnership's own networks and using other available resources such as EPALE). ) and by soliciting different means and resources both internally (from the organisations and the partnership) and externally (in its own networks and by relying on other available resources such as EPALE).

These new productions help to offer a wider range of activities that improve the quality of educational programmes by providing them with tools that appeal to the public because of their playfulness while developing their digital autonomy.

<< Results >>

The project produced 3 main outcomes: 

- 192 numerical challenge games in English, each with 4 levels and divided into 6 competences: literacy through reading comprehension; numerical reasoning and understanding through mathematical calculation; critical and creative thinking through problem solving; initiative through logical and spatial thinking; learning to learn through information retention and memory development; and digital and technological skills through basic coding exercises. 
24 of these games are translated into Croatian, French, German, Greek, Lithuanian, Portuguese and Spanish.

- an in-service training programme for VET professionals to increase their digital and pedagogical skills in online environments, to use CASINO resources with their learners, and to create their own resources in formats suitable for online teaching. 

- the platform https://casinoprojectmooc.eu which, in addition to the games, includes (i) a community of practice for VET professionals, (ii) a portfolio of competences for NEETs and Open badges which are awarded at the end of the games.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2020-1-FR01-KA226-VET-094952.title: Using Eduzines – interactive, transmedial learning materials for smartphones – to build strategic innovation skills of SMEs
2020-1-FR01-KA226-VET-094952.summary:
<< Background >>

La pandémie de COVID-19 a fondamentalement changé la façon dont les entrepreneurs européens envisagent leur avenir professionnel. En effet, même si l'innovation est un facteur critique de succès pour les performances des entreprises, elles se concentreront sur les efforts de redressement et les plans à court terme pour améliorer les revenus.
Le projet SIS-SME veut soutenir une croissance progressive des entreprises européennes, et veut les aider dans la mise en oeuvre d’une démarche d’innovation stratégique. Cela répond au besoin des entrepreneurs et PME d’améliorer leurs performances et de se remettre de la pandémie de COVID-19, ce qui va leur demander d’innover pour l’avenir.

<< Objectives >>

Le consortium engagé dans le projet SIS-SME a : 
*développé un programme de formation à l'innovation stratégique pour les chefs d'entreprise et les managers ;
*développé un compendium d’EduZines interactives sur le développement des compétences stratégiques des entrepreneurs en matière d'innovation ;
*développé une formation pour les tuteurs de l'EFP centré sur l'innovation stratégique dans le secteur des PME et sur la maitrise des outils pédagogiques et numériques.

<< Implementation >>

Les partenaires ont organisé plusieurs activités pendant les 2 années du projet:
*3 réunions transnationales, dont une en visioconférence, pour discuter de l’avancement du projet ;
*deux évènements de formation, pour explorer l’innovation stratégique et approfondir les outils pédagogiques numériques ;
*trois phases de pilotage, une par production intellectuelle ;
*8 évènements de dissémination, un par pays partenaire, pour présenter le projet au grand public.

<< Results >>

Dans le cadre du projet SIS-SME, les partenaires ont développé trois productions intellectuelles, adressée à deux groupes cible : 
*IO1 - Formation continue : adressé aux tuteurs de l’EFP, ce livrable se concentre sur le développement des compétences et connaissances des formateurs en termes d’innovation et de maitrise d’outils pédagogiques numériques ;
*IO2 - Compendium d'infographies interactives et EduZines SIS-SME : adressé aux entrepreneurs et manageurs de PME, ce livrable se compose de 8 EduZines interactives, axées sur l’innovation stratégique ;
*IO3 - MOOC SIS-SME et communauté de pratique : adressé à l’ensemble des parties prenantes, la plateforme regroupe les autres deux productions intellectuelles et offre aux utilisateurs la possibilité d’échanger avec des pairs en Europe.

2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094652.title: Virtual Business Skills Empowerment
2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094652.summary:
<< Background >>

Contemporary business environment is shaped with two interrelated processes, the fragmentation of value creation process and increasing penetration of digital technologies in every aspect of human living. Together these processes shape the business models of modern organizations and their demand for specific skills of employees. Some recent survey showed increase of 22 percent in telecommuting from 2017 to 2018. US figures show that about one third of all employed persons in US work remotely in virtual teams. As recent Covid-19 pandemic exposed, in times of crisis virtual teams become only means of functioning even for activities of intrinsically oriented organizations. It follows from there that being able to work in virtual teams is one of basic skills essential for employability of prospective graduates. However, while different aspects of digital transformation are covered in educational programmes of higher education institutions (HEIs) and even some high schools, the clear focus on building of skills for work in virtual teams is lacking. For European society to prosper in a digital era there is the need to empower European youth to harness benefits of work in virtual, multi-cultural teams.

<< Objectives >>

VIBES wanted to create educational and training content applicable in real world conditions of work in virtual teams closely aligned with priorities of Erasmus programme (2020):
- Fighting youth unemployment and providing youth with the skills required by the labour market, p. 5, VIBES created content to empower young Europeans with skills relevant for labour markets of tomorrow
- Improving the level of key competences and skills through cooperation between the worlds of education, training and work, p.26 - VIBES gathered academia, high schools, NGOs and business sector to provide unique educational content and equip students with basic skills for employability in a digital era
- Greater understanding and responsiveness to cultural diversity, p. 967 - VIBES consortium developed and validated a content that addressed multi-cultural work in virtual teams. This enhanced understanding of target group about the cultural diversity and contributed to embracing it as part of European identity.
- More strategic and integrated use of ICTs and open educational resources (OER) in education and training, p. 97 - VIBES created OER platform with all project materials and guidelines for their implementation in different socio-economic contexts.

<< Implementation >>

Building on EU’s Upskilling pathways initiative we implemented following activities:
- Mapping of skills needs for work in virtual teams among organisations using linkages of NGOs and SME involved in project.
- In depth country level and EU-wide mapping of approaches to development of virtual team skills in HEIs and high-schools
- Online multi-lingual educational content development aimed at empowering target group with skills for work in virtual teams
- Design and launch of virtual collaboration space on open source platform in form of open educational resource (OER)
- Developed guidelines for application of created content in different socio-economic contexts
- Provided testing and validation of project outputs on a sample of virtual teams at least 200 target group members under supervision of mentors from academia and business.

<< Results >>

The project resulted in following outputs:
- one pan-European and four (for Croatia, Estonia, Finland and Switzerland) country reports on practices in building of virtual team working skills at high-school, university and adult education levels (IO1).
-  Survey based Virtual team working skills framework (IO2)
- Multilingual online course prototype for virtual multicultural teamworking (IO3)
- Content development tool including curricula templates, course outline at high school, bachelor and master levels (IO3)
- Content development topics framework to illustrate how the VIBES approach can inspire and facilitate the development and design of diverse learning paths (IO3).
- VIBES digital learning hub on virtual skills, a virtual and interactive open education platform disseminated to more than 130 instructors, 30+ enterprises and 200+ learners from seven EU countries (IO4)
- Co-creation events with students and businesses involving over 400 target group members (IO5)
- Piloting based step-by-step guidelines for practitioners interested in applying VIBES course prototype (IO5)
-

2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094677.title: Relevant assessment and pedagogies for inclusive digital education
2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094677.summary:
<< Background >>

Unprepared shift from f2f to distance teaching and learning (DTL) during COVID-19 crisis was hard for HEIs. Mostly they were replicating average pedagogical practices from f2f teaching into a digital environment without any prior experience. Many students lagged behind due to lack of  equipment and adequate support. The innovative pedagogies can engage students and support their learning in f2f and online environments and teachers and students should be given tools and training to use innovative approaches. To succeed it is also crucial to have a co-creation process in place at the level of HEIs from across the EU. That inspired the design of our outputs and building this partnership. Our goals were related to  fostering the development of the necessary knowledge and competencies to use innovative pedagogies in an online environment. Our primary targets were HE teachers at partners, educational policy leaders and students and the specific objectives: to implement and evaluate innovative pedagogies; to support teachers to use relevant assessment methods; to provide support in the meaningful and ethical use of learning analytics and to boost capacity of HEIs for monitoring and evaluating the implementation of innovative pedagogies.

<< Objectives >>

The work was organized around the intellectual outputs, trainings and dissemination that included the development of: open educational resources and e-course for flipped classroom (FC) and work based learning (WBL) for use in online environment to provide teachers and students with research-based practical guidelines for FC and WBL in an online environment and as open e-course; toolkit for assessment of students in FC and WBL to provide HE teachers with unique and very practical toolkit (e-course chapter) which will include assessment scenarios for the implementation of innovative approaches, mainly peer assessment and project assessment (related to both WBL and FC) in different learning environments and within different HEIs; dashboard model that supports inclusive FC and WBL for teachers and students, tips and tricks for teachers on how to interpret data delivered on the dashboard, how to foster inclusiveness and help students at risk and how to ethically use students’ data; code of practice on impact analysis of innovative pedagogies with the main aim to use this unique opportunity to design, describe and test the methodology for impact analysis of innovative approaches in online education.

<< Implementation >>

Project was implemented as planned and partners cooperated successfully in a supportive and inclusive manner proving the highest level of flexibility during critical periods. The following core activities were carried out: co-creational development of  - 4 intellectual outputs and corresponding appendices,training materials, MOOC with 4 modules and research publications. Piloting of MOOC in 2022 (June-November) included development but also recruiting, onboarding and certification activities. Partners met regularly online and onsite as planned: kick-off Welcome RAPIDE was organized in M2 at FOI, Croatia, Meet2Flip in UK done in M5 at FOI, Croatia (due to covid-19 restrictions), Meet2Flip in Netherlands in M9, Meet2Flip in Germany in M14 and Final meeting - Keep Flipping in Croatia in M24. Project included 3 LTT events, 3 multiplier events and 1 final conference. Partners were very much involved in dissemination activities that included the dissemination via research papers and research events, as well as the dissemination via project web page, social accounts and mass media. The management of the project was administered at the Project Office at FOI. The project included well planned procedures of quality and impact assurance.

<< Results >>

The partners followed the project proposal to develop project results. All results have been achieved within the project lifetime, meeting all planned indicators: 4 intellectual outputs and their appendixes (IO1 OPEN EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES AND E-COURSE FOR FLIPPED CLASSROOM AND WORK-BASED LEARNING FOR USE IN AN ONLINE ENVIRONMENT; IO2 TOOLKIT FOR ASSESSMENT OF STUDENTS IN FLIPPED CLASSROOM AND WORK BASED LEARNING; IO3 LEARNING ANALYTICS FOR FLIPPED CLASSROOM AND WORK BASED LEARNING; IO4 CODE OF PRACTICE FOR HEIs ON IMPACT ANALYSIS OF INNOVATIVE PEDAGOGIES, 4 management supporting documents and corresponding reports (PROJECT HANDBOOK; QUALITY MANAGEMENT PLAN (+Quality REPORT);  DISSEMINATION AND COMMUNICATION PLAN (+Dissemination REPORT); IMPACT FRAMEWORK (+Impact REPORT)),  4 modules of RAPIDE MOOC (Module 1 - LET’S INNOVATE TEACHING, Module 2 -LET’S INNOVATE ASSESSMENT, Module 3 -LET’S INNOVATE SUPPORT, Module 4 -IMPACT ANALYSIS OF INNOVATIVE PEDAGOGIES), dissemination materials ( 20 research publications and posters, 2 podcasts, 1 talk show, more than 200 posts on social accounts, 1 webpage….) 
The tangible project results are available on the official project website: https://rapide-project.eu/index.php/en/results

2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094685.title: Digital Education for Crisis Situations: Times when there is no alternative
2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094685.summary:
<< Background >>

Our intention was to address the needs that we discovered before, during and beyond the COVID-19 pandemic in order to: 1) obtain a picture of the DE at partner institutions related to COVID-19 in order to foster the establishment of good practice for the future, both in emergencies and in normal teaching practice, as such a traumatic situation needed to be analysed with a transnational approach; 2) cover a certain lack of LIS OERs by offering spaces of collaboration and networking between Library and Information Science (LIS) institutions in order to develop into stable relationships strengthened by new projects; 3) continue  of the research in the digital education (DE) at European Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) that offer programs in LIS in order to strengthen the network of teachers and students that successfully operates since 2015 (see: einfose.ffos.hr), especially in regards to the organization and maintenance of summer schools which proved to be extremely successful; 4) answer to the Erasmus + call that stimulate the research that could shed light on how the European HEIs managed to cope with the unpredictable circumstances caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, including new approaches to DE and internship programs.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective was to investigate how the European LIS HEIs practice online education and use OERs in times when there was no other alternative, especially to analyse the perceptions and experience of all stakeholders involved. We followed the New Digital Action Plan, 2021-2027 in order to contribute to the realization of the EC's vision for high-quality, inclusive, innovative and accessible DE in Europe. We also intended to develop a DE ecosystem and create an online platform and data-driven systems; to improve the digital competencies of students and teachers; to employ open data and open science policy; and foresee changes in the labour market and skills mismatch. As related to the business sector, we intended to seek new models for stronger connectivity between employees and management, in crisis situations in particular, between HEIs and business, especially IT companies. We intended to provide the results of studies related to students, teachers and members of the host institutions where the internships were held during the pandemic. We also wanted to promote and strengthen internationalization in regards to strategic and structured cooperation between European HEIs and support of various types of cooperation models.

<< Implementation >>

According to the project’s plan, activities were carried out with visible results and the development of trust and confidence between partners. Although the COVID-19 pandemic measures prevented us to keep up with the original timeline, the Project Management Team prepared a revised timeline that allowed the successfull organization of: six Transnational Project Meetings (TPM), one virtual, one hybrid and four in vivo; two Summer Schools and two Tutorials – in vivo; four Multiplier Events (one in hybrid mode, other three in vivo). Two summer schools (DESS 2021 and DESS 2022) attracted 46 students from partners and associated institutions who actively participated in lectures, discussions, workshops and in completing the assignments. Two tutorials that aimed at transmission of expert knowledge by two partner institutions (Barcelona and SRCE) to other DECriS team members, helped in the acquisition of specialized skills necessary for producing quality OERs. In four Multiplier events, we can confirm that at all of them we had 231 participants from almost every European country, alongside with participants from Canada, New Zealand and several African and Asian countries, 132 of them joined on-site, others online (some from Ukraine).

<< Results >>

DECriS results are visible at the project website (https://decris.ffos.hr/), platform (https://decris.ffos.hr/platform/) and Dissemination Platform. The work done on six intellectual outputs was objectified in six reports after cunducted surveys and intensive discussions. Four events for dissemination and multiplication of results were organized: in Barcelona (hybrid mode) and in vivo in Sofia, Zagreb and Osijek. Two summer schools were held in Osijek (DESS 2021) and Hildesheim (2022). Two Tutorials were provided by Barcelona and by SRCE. We produced four basic documents for project management that were followed during the course of the work: Project Management Plan, Risk Management Plan, Dissemination Plan and Quality Assurance Plan. We also produced Calls for participation at MEs and the Final brochure for the ME4 as the last event included not only invited participants but the participants at LIDA (Libraries in the Digital Age) Conference which is internationally known and appreciated. These participants were also active in discussions about the DECriS project results and recommendations. For both tutorials we produced guidelines and offered assignments for present colleagues from partners’ institutions.

2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094696.title: Learning how to Teach, Teaching how to Learn. Facing Challenges of Global Change in Higher Education Using Digital Tools for Reflective, Critical and Inclusive Learning on European Historical Landscapes.
2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094696.summary:
<< Background >>

Following the successful Erasmus+ Ka02 HILAR project, we have decided to apply once again for the Erasmus+ KA02 Call that was oriented specifically on online teaching and learning in wake of Covid-19 pandemic. With the project, we hoped to address some of the issues we have come across while working on the HILAR project, as well as in everyday challenges of teaching in „new normal“. More specifically, during the implementation of HILAR project's activities the need arose to transfer some, if not all, didactic activities in the online or hybrid mode. Suddenly, a plethora of new issues came to light. A significant portion of teaching staff had no necessary experience, or even will, to participate in the new modalities of teaching. Thus, we had decided with EDITOR project we needed to approach the issue of online learning and teaching from the multiple scientific perspectives - archeology, art history and history for its content, and psychology, sociology and pedagogy for its creation and implementation.

<< Objectives >>

As previously noted, the project implementation is strongly connected to the underlying issues that served as an inspiration for its conception. Imperative of the project was to provide a framework for the education in the contemporary online environment, formed around the challenges that manifest themselves in the pandemic, as well as post-pandemic world. In Intellectual Output 1 we used skills and knowledge of sociologists and psychologists in order to create a better understanding of the problem, and receive the input from teaching staff. Thus, the basis for the conceptual framework behind the course was created. Input was reused in the context of Intellectual Output 2 – Guidelines and Tutorials for Teaching staff providing useful practical advice for teaching staff in contemporary online environment, based on the sample course that we created. Next, Intellectual Output 3 and 4 (mutually connected) were conceived in order to provide both the teachers, and the students, the online learning platform (course - MOOC) that can address the identified issues, and provide them both with satisfactory solutions.

<< Implementation >>

Given the online focus of the Intellectual Outputs, as well as the general context behind its inception, it seemed only natural to divert all of the activities to the online sphere. Thus, the testing and the online survey were both conducted online, along with all of the project meetings. The multiplier events, however, were held in vivo, once the sanitary conditions allowed it. A number of local, small-scale meetings were held at the individual Universities level (by the smaller teams working on a certain segment of an output). All of the key online activities had been documented.

<< Results >>

Out of 4 intellectual outputs, the three of them can be directly accessed, while one is intrinsically connected to the other (output in question being the digital library content (Intellectual Output 3) that was used in the Course (IO4) itself). Two intellectual outputs (1 and 2) are in the text format, one being a survey and its analysis, that can be used in further research dealing with sociological and psychological understanding of the key problems behind online, and digital teaching in general. The main output of the project, however, is the course (MOOC) itself, a culmination of sorts, summarizing and utilizing all of the previous results. Course was designed not only as a communicator of its content, but as an example of online teaching framework serving as a concrete example of how online teaching can be conducted.
