2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094713.title: Cloud cOmputing for Digital Education INnovation
2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094713.summary:
<< Background >>

The pandemic has shown the importance of online teaching. Robust digital education frameworks ensure quality education during disruptions, help distant students and build practical skills for the changing labor market. To address these needs, the CODEIN project aimed to modernize distance learning curricula and teaching methodologies in cloud computing and machine learning, adopting student-led teaching approaches to make education more dynamic and relevant to current industry trends. The project also aimed to enhance the digital education readiness of participating organizations and foster collaboration, peer learning, and the sharing of best practices among higher education institutions in Europe. Through a comprehensive set of activities, such as joint training programs, distance learning curricula, webinars on creating distance learning materials, and policy recommendations, the project contributes to the broader goal of improving digital education frameworks within the European Higher Education Area.

<< Objectives >>

Our main goal was to develop modern and inclusive teaching methods that will improve the digital readiness of higher education institutions and keep pace with rapid technological progress. We believed that adopting a learner-centered teaching approach would create a more engaging and effective learning environment. Our additional goal was also to address the gender gap in IT by implementing specific pedagogical strategies that would promote female student participation and success in IT courses. We have also planned to develop comprehensive distance learning materials such as webinars, case studies, and policy recommendations to improve online education practices generally. By promoting a transnational approach to education, we hoped to align our efforts with the needs of the global IT labor market, thereby improving employability, encouraging innovation and supporting gender equality in the IT sector.

<< Implementation >>

The CODEIN project is an initiative focused on enhancing distance learning methodologies and inclusivity within higher education IT courses, with a particular emphasis on female participation. The project has implemented a range of activities to achieve this objective, which are detailed below:
1.	Transnational Project Meetings: Facilitated discussions on project progress, partner responsibilities, project outputs, and planning of future activities.
2.	Intellectual Outputs:
•	O1. Methodology for Distance Teaching and Learning: The project developed a new methodology to make distance learning more productive and interesting, culminating in an e-book.
•	O2. Fifteen Training Webinars for Educators: Produced webinars providing training on developing distance teaching and learning materials, available in multiple languages (as subtitled videos)
•	O3. Two Distance Learning Curricula: Created intensive courses in cloud computing and machine learning, designed for accessibility and inclusivity, with materials made open access.
•	O4. Pedagogical Strategy for Teaching Female Students: Developed strategies and tools aimed at increasing the participation and success of female students in IT disciplines.
•	O5. Policy Recommendations: Published sets of policy recommendations on enhancing the participation of women in IT and promoting modular, open-access education in the cloud.
•	O6. Case Studies: Analyzed specific issues related to social inclusivity and innovative approaches to distance learning through descriptive and explanatory case studies.
3.	Multiplier Events: Organized events targeted at secondary vocational school students, NEETs, and female students in IT, aiming to disseminate project outputs and encourage participation in the developed courses.
4.	Learning/Teaching/Training Activities: The project conducted a DEI (Digital Education Innovation) summer school for professors and postgraduate teaching assistants to enhance their skills in distance teaching and assessment methodologies.

<< Results >>

The CODEIN project produced a variety of tangible outputs and achieved significant results, measured against both quantitative and qualitative indicators:
Quantitative Indicators
•	25 professors and postgraduate teaching assistants participated in the summer school, aligning with the expected number.
•	103 university students enrolled in the distance learning-intensive courses, meeting the project's target.
•	47 girls enrolled in the distance learning-intensive courses, fulfilling the minimum expected number.
•	7 NEET (Not in Education, Employment, or Training) individuals facing economic obstacles were enrolled in the distance learning-intensive courses, as planned.
•	58 students facing geographical obstacles participated in the distance learning-intensive courses, meeting the project's goals.
•	1 e-book was published, providing comprehensive documentation of the distance teaching and learning methodology.
•	Learning materials were translated into 5 sets in 5 languages, ensuring accessibility for a diverse audience.
•	15 webinars were developed, offering training for educators in higher education institutions on creating digital teaching and learning materials.
•	2 sets of policy recommendations were published, addressing women in IT and modular, open-access education in the cloud.
•	2 case studies were developed, analyzing the social inclusivity of higher education for female learners and economically underprivileged groups.
•	The project's website saw significant engagement, with a notable number of visits.
•	A considerable number of people attended multiplier activities, indicating widespread interest and engagement with the project's outcomes.
•	Several press conferences were organized, raising awareness of the project's activities and results.
Qualitative Indicators
•	The quality of the developed distance learning-intensive courses was high, offering valuable practical knowledge valued on the labor market.
•	The quality of the distance learning and teaching materials was excellent, facilitating effective and engaging learning experiences.
•	The summer school training program was of high quality, enhancing educators' capabilities in distance education methodologies.
•	The published e-book was well-received, effectively disseminating the project's methodologies and findings.
•	Project team members and target groups positively evaluated the project's activities, reflecting satisfaction with the project's implementation and outcomes.
•	The media coverage of project activities and results was extensive, contributing to the project's visibility and impact.

2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094728.title: Intercultural Communication and Linguistic Upgrade in a Digital Environment
2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094728.summary:
<< Background >>

The INCLUDE project was set in the context of the global onset of the COVID-19 pandemic that has brought immense changes to the manner people communicate and engage in professional activities. Language and intercultural communication (LIC) teachers at higher education institutions teach courses that heavily depend on communication and they have had to invest more time and effort into transforming their teaching methods and materials into ones that are applicable in online teaching. At the same time, LIC teachers are the ones who have to prepare their students for real-life communication in a virtual setting as well as to enable them to acquire the Global Competence. This project has addressed the needs of students of all partner universities to be able to participate in quality virtual mobilities, especially to students from underrepresented and vulnerable groups, as well as on an international scale the needs of LIC teachers who wish to implement similar methodology in their courses.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the INCLUDE project was to boost students' employability on a global scale by ensuring an inclusive, progressive, high-quality language and communication course in a range of languages (English, Croatian, Portuguese, Greek) at higher education institutions across Europe. The project involved three intellectual outputs oriented towards developing a high-quality course in Intersectoral communication skills in a digital, intercultural environment.

<< Implementation >>

Within the project the project team implemented a total of 11 online working meetings, 1 online kick-off meeting, 1 physical kick-off transnational meeting at ISAL Madeira, Portugal, virtual teaching and training pilot course with 30 students from three partner universities, a detailed research that resulted in a research study and scientific paper on the needs analysis, a detailed course curriculum on Intercultural Communication and Linguistic Upgrade in a Digital Environment, a coursebook / handbook written in 4 languages (original in English and translations into Croatian, Greek, and Portuguese). The project team has participated in numerous dissemination activities, such as radio and television news, news portal interviews, scientific and professional conferences, for the purpose of disseminating the results of the project. Also, in the final stage of the project, an online multiplier event was organised and disseminated among national and international associations of language and communication skills teachers that was attended by 104 participants from 6 countries.

<< Results >>

Within the project the project team developed:
1. A detailed research report (needs analysis) related to the implementation of a course in Intercultural Communication and Linguistic Upgrade in a Digital Environment - the research was carried out among students, teachers and industrial partners in the three project partner countries;
2. A detailed course curriculum in Intercultural Communication and Linguistic Upgrade in a Digital Environment;
3. A coursebook / handbook in Intercultural Communication and Linguistic Upgrade in a Digital Environment available in English, Portuguese, Greek and Croatian;
4. Participation in two scientific conferences (one in Portugal, one in Slovenia), submission of two additional paper proposals that were accepted (an international student conference organised by CEPS Kiseljak, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the international LSPHE conference organised by the University of York, and the University of Cambridge, UK). Information on the already held dissemination events are available here: https://include.vub.hr/index.php/dissemination/

2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094732.title: E-laboratory for digital education
2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094732.summary:
<< Background >>

Digital transformation entered the education system through the back door, but due to the COVID-19 pandemic, it gained global proportions. The pandemic is the cause of the biggest disruption in education and training in recent European history. According to some estimates, the consequences have been felt by more than one hundred million pupils, students, teachers and educational staff around the world, and many of them have turned to digital education in order to manage to bring the academic year to an end. Some of them had to completely rely on digital technologies for teaching and learning for the first time, and most of them need support in the transformation from classroom to online education.
It is clear to everyone that nothing will be the same again and that the world has been changed forever, the question is what to do and what steps to take in order to strengthen education and make it available to everyone.

<< Objectives >>

With the project, we wanted to digitally transform higher education through networking and spreading practices and knowledge so that we would be fully and on time ready for the new normal. The coming generations are more and more focused on digital technologies and it is necessary to keep up with them, and the issue of introducing quality online classes is certainly of global scale, and we are of the opinion that by connecting European countries and, what is more important, by later spreading the results of the project, a synergistic effect on improvement can be achieved digital skills of key stakeholders. The purpose of the project was to create sustainable partnerships of higher education institutions and other stakeholders in the EU with the aim of strengthening the ability to introduce teaching and learning on the Internet by developing digital pedagogical competences of teaching staff, finding innovative solutions for providing high-quality and inclusive digital education by developing and using quality digital content and tools adapted to local challenges and circumstances.

<< Implementation >>

We analyzed the conduct of online exams and applied good practices in the methodology that can be used by European countries. By creating a methodological approach, we provide students with stability, quality and education tailored to the European citizen. We developed a digital skills methodology, and created an e-learning platform that serves multiple purposes; initially as a place to connect all interested stakeholders in the domain of education who need a methodology for acquiring digital skills and introducing online exams, secondly as a place dedicated to all the activities created and implemented in the project. Third, as a Platform that will teach and educate other stakeholders using the trainings that can be found on it. Using the Platform as an influential means of dissemination, we actually want to create a strong sustainability of the project results, considering that they will be necessary in further European digital progress. We also conducted multiplying activities, conferences where we presented all the knowledge and results of the project. We also paid attention to project management and administration activities. We created the project's visual identity (including logo, letterhead) and the project's Facebook page in English.

<< Results >>

With the project, we created sustainable partnerships of higher education institutions and other stakeholders in the EU with the aim of strengthening the ability to introduce teaching and learning on the Internet by developing digital pedagogical competencies of teaching staff, finding innovative solutions for providing high-quality and inclusive digital education, development and use quality digital content and tools adapted to local challenges and circumstances
The results and outputs produced by the project are;
We networked organizations in the EU, exchanged resources, knowledge and expertise;
We enabled the development of digital pedagogical competencies of the teaching staff;
We designed and developed an e-learning platform;
We analyzed the implementation of online exams;
We have developed a methodology for conducting online evaluations (exams);
We have developed a digital skills methodology;
We designed and produced 7 modules with over 60 educational videos on the e-Learning Platform.

2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094780.title: Digital Empowering Trough HPC Education
2020-1-HR01-KA226-HE-094780.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the HiPowerEd project for several compelling reasons and with a clear vision to address a variety of pressing needs:
Democratizing HPC: High-Performance Computing (HPC) is indeed a highly exclusive technology, often only accessible to a select few. We saw the critical need to democratize access to HPC technology, to equip our young researchers and professionals with this transformative tool. This project gives us the chance to break down those barriers and make HPC a widely accessible tool.
Education Continuity: The global crisis has forced a shift in educational modalities, and the need for robust, flexible digital tools has never been more apparent. We saw the project as an opportunity to contribute to a resilient educational framework that can withstand such disruptions in the future.
Cross-Disciplinary Learning: HPC has wide-ranging applications across numerous scientific disciplines. We recognized the need to expose young learners to these possibilities, encourage cross-disciplinary learning, and inspire innovative thinking.

<< Objectives >>

Implementing the HiPowerEd project, we aimed to achieve several key objectives to promote digital education and prepare the young generation for the technology-driven future:
Democratize Access to HPC: Our primary objective was to democratize access to High-Performance Computing (HPC), making this powerful technology available to young researchers, professionals, teachers, and underrepresented groups.
Develop Digital Skills: We wanted to help young people develop the necessary digital skills to leverage HPC in various scientific fields, thereby enhancing their employability and readiness for the digital age.
Promote Interdisciplinary Learning: By exposing participants to the applications of HPC across a wide range of disciplines, we hoped to promote interdisciplinary learning and innovative thinking.
Foster Network Building and Mentorship: We sought to facilitate the formation of professional networks among participants and provide them with mentoring opportunities from renowned HPC experts.
Enhance Educational Resilience: Given the global crisis and the shift to remote learning, we aimed to contribute to the resilience and adaptability of the educational system during recovery and beyond.

<< Implementation >>

The kick-off meeting was conducted to officially start the project. During this meeting, project partners likely discussed the project objectives, timelines, roles and responsibilities, and other relevant details.
 The HiPowerEd Manual was created as an intellectual output of the project. The second transnational project meeting took place online. This meeting was likely held to assess the progress of the project, address any challenges or issues encountered, and plan for the upcoming phases or tasks. The Virtual Classroom was developed as an intellectual output. The third transnational project meeting was conducted. Similar to the previous meetings, this gathering likely aimed to evaluate the project's progress, exchange information and ideas, and plan for the remaining project activities. E-learning course was implemented as an intellectual output. This refers to the development and deployment of an online course or educational program related to the project's objectives or target audience. Several HiPowerEd conferences, also known as a multiplier event, was organized. Those events was likely open to a wider audience and aimed to disseminate the project's results.The closure meeting marked the end of the project.

<< Results >>

The project produced the following concrete outputs and results:
Curriculum and Lifelong Learning Resources: The project developed a curriculum program aimed at providing programming knowledge and raising interest in young people. It also demonstrated the benefits of professional development in technology and aimed to enhance the activities of young scientists and professionals by providing them with high-tech HPC (High-Performance Computing) and other digital structures. 
Intellectual Outputs: The project generated intellectual outputs in the form of a handbook, e-learning courses, and a "Virtual Classroom" (pilot courses setup). These outputs aimed to provide comprehensive resources for HPC adoption and usage, making it accessible to a broader range of users and sectors. The outputs were designed to address the sector-specific needs and reduce the barriers to entry by providing specialized technical skills and knowledge.
Multiplier Events: The project organized  HiPowerEd conferences, also known as a multiplier event.  It provided a platform for collaboration, knowledge exchange, and networking among scientists, researchers, educators, and professionals in various fields.

2020-1-HR01-KA226-SCH-094709.title: Our New Learning Innovative Network for Education
2020-1-HR01-KA226-SCH-094709.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project in order to develop students' and teachers' skills and competences in the field of online teaching and learning using digital technologies and to develop teachers' ability to teach students these skills with the useful and innovative digital teaching methods that are necessary nowadays to reach their goals and give interesting and motivating lessons using digital technology.

<< Objectives >>

The objective of this partnership was to develop teachers' and students' digital skills in order to improve the teaching / learning process. We also intend to cause a great impact at all levels of our educational communities, and provide students with quality opportunities to reinforce common European citizenship values, to improve their socio affective skills and be better prepared for the future.
The objectives we achieved were to equip teachers and students with skills and knowledge on the use of digital tools, increase their digital competence and strengthen teacher's skills based teaching practice through transnational cooperation and by adopting innovative, effective and new methods, increase their level of foreign languages, boost their communication and social skills and collaboration/teamwork, improve their socio affective skills through an international approach, use creativity and innovation, critical thinking, problem-solving and decision-making approaches, make the most of exchange of good practices and peer-learning, take personal and social responsibility in unpredictable situation, boost their cultural awareness and intercultural learning and promote a sense of European dimension.

<< Implementation >>

- making a questionnaire at the beginning of the project activities relating to the project expectations and general part relating to the actual knowledge about digital technology
- forming Erasmus+ clubs in each partner school
- regular meetings with the participating students and teachers
- making reports, minutes, visit plans, expenses charts
- evaluation questionnaires and analysis of the same
- involvement of the experts from other schools or other local/regional organisations which was of key importance for the learning/teaching/training activities
- organising all preparatory activities, mobility activities and follow up activities

- dissemination activities

2020-1-HR01-KA226-SCH-094735.title: Active learning through improved interactivity
2020-1-HR01-KA226-SCH-094735.summary:
<< Background >>

Constructivism, inquiry and problem-based learning, project and teamwork are beginning to play a significant role in the new educational process. Nevertheless, active learning is slow to catch on in practice. The reason for this lies mainly in the one-sided transmission of information to students. The main reason is that teachers do not have personal experience with active learning and therefore often do not know how to change their teaching methods. Students also do not have the habit, courage and freedom to spontaneously give answers and ask questions. Having identified the need for a tool to increase interactivity in the classroom in Croatia, especially at the beginning of the pandemic COVID -19, Project Coordinator Aquilonis, through research and communication with teachers, established contact with project partners who also expressed the need for a tool that would enable them to: increase interactivity in the classroom, it can be used ad hoc, it is free, it is open to anyone who wants to use it, it is easy to use, it allows exporting answers to other tools, it recognizes similar answers and groups them so that it can be customized and personalized. The results of this project are: LMS with 47 examples of best practices, lessons for self-study, software solution AudIT and interactive expert system for installation and use.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of the project is to improve interactivity in lectures. For this purpose, 47 new teaching methods were designed and developed, as well as the special tool AudiIT - with instructions for use and an interactive expert system. There are many software tools that teachers can use to check students' knowledge and ask questions, but each of them has at least some limitations. The first goal of the project is to develop and create AudIT (Audience Interactivity Tool), whose task is to help to activate students. It is a system that can work for a long time almost without maintenance, it can serve a large number of users, it allows instant questions and answers so that teachers and students can assess the level of knowledge before and during the lesson or discuss some challenges or ambiguities. Another goal of the project was to create practical methodological guides for use in the classroom in the subject groups of natural sciences, social sciences, language and literature, and personal development. The third goal of the project is to create a core of practitioners. During the project, teachers have used the tool in the classroom and developed methodological examples that form the basis for good practice.

<< Implementation >>

Design of the project's visual identity, website, content storage system, logo, memo, and presentations. Conducted dissemination activities, meetings, conferences, administration.
Kick-of meeting was held - defined activities with deadlines, leaders and deliverables, finances and communication were discussed, as well as dissemination of the project.
I. AudIT activities: a workshop was held on the functionalities of ICT tools, the possibilities of ICT tools in individual subjects were analyzed, the functionalities of AudIT were defined, user interface mockup document was created, the architecture and design of the future system were defined. These activities were followed by the development of AudIT and its testing. As a result of these activities, the AudIT system was created with instructions and expert systems for using and installing AudIT.

II. LMS activities: Workshop on interactivity and definition of the structure of self-learning materials with identification of the needs of teachers and students. Creation and coordination of initial methods, creation and correction of methods by subjects, selection and setup of the LMS and filling of the content with methodological instructions and examples.

<< Results >>

1) AudIT - a tool for improving interactivity in lectures with innovative features such as the evaluation of unique answers, the possibility to answer anonymously and under your own name, and to forward answers to other applications. This is a tool that, according to students and teachers, really motivates students to participate more acitvely.
2) To facilitate teachers' use of AudIT, an LMS (Learning Management System) was developed with methodological instructions and examples, as well as lessons for self-study.
3) An interactive expert system for use and installing, designed as a decision tree.
4) A set of documents useful for setting goals and monitoring results: Overviews of available ARS tools, AudIT - User Interface Design, AUDIT - Architecture and Software Design, AUDIT - Description, Program Specifications, Recommendations for Implementation (General Description, Software Specification, and Implementation Recommendation), Results of student and teacher pilot tests, Evaluations by renowned experts, AudIT User Manual (multilingual), AudIT - Technical Documentation, Inventory of needs of teachers and students (Inventory of needs ), Analysis of the LMS.
5) A series of dissemination products: Newsletters, brochures, manual.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2020-1-HR01-KA226-VET-094650.title: Digital reality - the basis of skills training
2020-1-HR01-KA226-VET-094650.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was applied for because there was an evident need for materials and tools that would encourage teachers, trainers and mentors in VET to accept innovative approaches and digital technologies for teaching and learning as well as for continuous professional development suitable for the digital age.
The need for this approach arose from the fact, which was made even more obvious during the COVID-19 pandemic, that the majority of teaching staff ( 60% / OECD), especially the middle and older generations, have not learned to work in digital environment.
In order to be able to teach the Z and Alpha generations, it is necessary that teachers and trainers first of all understand their students, colleagues and parents in the context of education, learning and teaching as well as in the context of the methods they should use. It's no secret that there is a disparity between the digital literacy of students and teachers. For this reason, it is crucial to train the teachers to work in a digital environment: how, when, what kind and with what purpose to use technology.
In order to implement this approach, it is necessary to develop tools that will make these processes simpler, more acceptable and quickly enforceable.

<< Objectives >>

Implementation of the project aimed to achieve the following goals:
1. Promote the Digital Reality technologies (AR, VR, MR and XR) in education, especially in VET,
2. Promote application of simulators for skills training in VET
3. Promote constructivist and collaborative approach in the teaching process
4. Learn how to learn using technology in teams consisting of teachers and students
5. Enable teachers and students to work / learn in crisis situations (e.g. pandemics)

<< Implementation >>

Activities in the implementation of the project were as follows:
1. 9 online meetings and 4 transnational project meetings were held.
2. Around 1250 emails were exchanged.
3. 6 intellectual outputs were developed,
4. One short-term joint staff training event was held,
5. 7 multiplier events were held,
6. 5 professional papers were presented at international conferences in Slavonski Brod, Paris (online) and Tokyo.
7. Dissemination activities were continuously carried out,
8. The entire implementation of the project was monitored with qualitative assessments and evaluation procedures.

<< Results >>

6 intellectual outputs were developed in the scope of the project:
1. Basics of digital reality – A handbook for teachers and trainers about how to use different virtual reality simulators for occupations in VET
2. VET library of DR – A database of digital reality content creators / developers
3. HOW TO... - Best practice examples from VET digital classrooms across Europe (platform for knowledge exchange)
4. Pedagogical guidelines for learning and teaching using DR technologies
5. Technical manual: Minimum conditions for education, training and testing in educational processes in virtual environment
6. Guideline for Online assessment: Tools and procedures to perform harmonized online assessment

2020-1-HR01-KA226-VET-094781.title: Training 4 Skills in Virtual Environment (T4SVEN)
2020-1-HR01-KA226-VET-094781.summary:
<< Background >>

In 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic caused a global socio-economic crisis, affecting the health and jobs of millions of citizens, and entailing school closures worldwide. The sudden transition from traditional teaching and learning to digital classrooms did not leave place for carefully designed online learning experiences that would allow learners to fully benefit from the digital transformation of education. VET was particularly affected by the school closure and the transition to emergency remote teaching as its distinctive work-based learning feature had largely been interrupted, putting practical training and the acquisition of skills for VET students at a considerable disadvantage. The virtual learning environment required teachers to demonstrate advanced digital skills and confidence in applying web-conferencing solutions. In addition, VET teachers needed to coordinate, create, and share training material for work-based learning with workplace mentors. In 2020, the Proposal for a Council Recommendation on vocational education and training called for increasing the digital readiness of VET providers through the promotion of digital and participative learning environments, accessible tools, and versatile digital pedagogies. The Council Conclusions on European teachers and trainers for the future from 2020 also recognized the importance of key competence development, as well as teaching contemporary VET skills. Well before the COVID-19 disruption, TALIS 2018 had confirmed that the use of ICT for teaching represented the second highest priority for the professional development of teachers. This project addressed the need for innovative, digital teaching approaches, including virtual reality, by developing teacher training, specifically in VET sectors that had taken the brunt of the COVID-19 crisis – tourism, hospitality, and transportation.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to support VET teachers in integrating digital technology with the specific areas of their teaching expertise by creating a set of digital open resources based on digital pedagogy principles and offering VET teacher training to contribute to improving teaching practices and enriching the methods of VET provision, specifically concerning work-based learning (WBL). The specific objectives were to: develop a framework on digital pedagogy in VET with specific focus on WBL;  develop and pilot an online course on digital pedagogy; and pilot peer reviews to evaluate teachers' coursework. By achieving these objectives, the project supported VET teachers with the challenges of teaching in digital and blended learning environment, encouraged networking and international cooperation through partnership between countries and different levels of education, supported networking between VET schools and the exchange of good practice through peer reviews, and promoted openness, inclusiveness and innovativeness of VET.

<< Implementation >>

Implemented project activities included a review and analysis of needs, required skills and challenges for teaching in the virtual environment, as a basis for the development of a conceptual framework and guidelines on digital pedagogy in VET with a focus on work-based learning. Based on the priority areas for competence development defined by the framework and guidelines on digital pedagogy, an outcome-based, modular curriculum for an online course on digital pedagogy was produced. In line with the curriculum, an online course with open-source course materials and learning scenarios was developed. Course platform that supported course delivery and a game-based, virtual reality educational platform were equally developed within the project, allowing teachers to explore different tools and approaches for increasing the effectiveness and attractiveness of teaching and learning in the virtual environment. Finally, peer review methodology was developed for assessing the final coursework of the trainees. 40 VET teachers from all participating countries piloted the online course on digital pedagogy in VET and engaged in peer evaluation of teaching scenarios they had created as part of their coursework. The project management and dissemination were supported by the organization of transnational project meetings and multiplier events.

<< Results >>

The key outputs and results involved the framework and guidelines on digital pedagogy in VET, with a specific focus on WBL, curriculum for digital pedagogy in VET, online course on digital pedagogy in VET with open-source training materials, web platform hosting the course, game-based virtual reality platform,  peer review guidelines and training resources. The online course featured three modules defined by the framework and the curriculum on digital pedagogy in VET: (module 1) Using Open Educational Resources (OERs) in e-learning, (module 2) Digital Pedagogy – Creating and Using Learning Scenarios, and (module 3) Augmented and Virtual Reality Technologies in Education. 40 VET teachers from all countries of the project consortium piloted the online course and participated in peer reviews of the coursework. The course supported VET teachers with the pedagogical and methodical challenges of teaching in digital and blended learning environments. A game-based, virtual reality educational platform allowed teachers to explore different tools and approaches for increasing the effectiveness and attractiveness of teaching and learning in the virtual environment. Through the course, VET teachers strengthened digital competencies and increased self-confidence in designing outcome-oriented, engaging skills training in VET, introducing innovative teaching methods, and balancing online and in-person instruction. Peer reviews of teachers' coursework allowed networking between VET schools and the exchange of good practices on using digital technology in education. The project also supported networking and international cooperation through partnerships between different countries and levels of education by organizing: one kick-off meeting, monthly coordination meetings of the project consortium, five transnational project meetings and a final partner meeting. Project results were disseminated to a broad audience of stakeholders in VET, universities, NGOs, and government bodies, as well as the primary target audience – VET teachers and schools.  Besides online dissemination activities, such as promotion through social media, the project kick-off conference was organized, alongside multiplier events in all countries of the project consortium, which contributed to engaging and informing project target groups of the project results. Finally, the project contributed to openness, inclusiveness, and innovation in VET by producing an innovative set of open resources for improving digital pedagogy approaches to teaching and learning in VET, which included a methodological framework and practical training resources that may be further adapted to different educational settings. In terms of long-term benefits, an innovative, open-source framework and course carries a high multiplication potential for transfer and adaptation by education providers, workplace trainers, policymakers and other stakeholders at national and European levels, in VET and beyond.

2020-1-IE01-KA226-VET-082937.title: Developing the digital and entrepreneurial competences of VET trainers to support agile entrepreneurship training
2020-1-IE01-KA226-VET-082937.summary:
<< Background >>

The pandemic greatly accelerated the need for digital transformation of VET and as a result the AGILITe project set out to build the capacity of VET teachers to: implement online and blended teaching and learning;  develop digital pedagogical competences enabling them to deliver high quality inclusive digital education; and use high quality digital content presented as EduZines putting innovative online resources and tools at their disposal. The ongoing professional development of educators plays a considerable role in ensuring the delivery of high-quality VET. Therefore, we wanted to address three key challenges simultaneously, by developing CPD programmes that promote DigCompEdu, EntreComp & the EU Green Deal. These programmes directly address the validated training and learning needs of VET tutors so that they could use and develop innovative and engaging learning resources to support VET learners. The in-service training programmes comprise toolkits of EduZines that build a competent understanding of these key skills. All resources are presented on the AGILITe MOOC and supported by the Community of Practice.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to enhance the digital competences of VET tutors, ensuring they were equipped with the necessary skills to navigate the digital landscape effectively. This enabled them to leverage technology & digital tools in their instructional practices, creating engaging, inclusive & innovative experiences for learners. AGILITe focused also on nurturing the entrepreneurial spirit among VET tutors fostering an entrepreneurial perspective and providing them with the necessary knowledge and skills to empower and inspire nascent entrepreneurs within VET. This involved developing their competences in areas such as opportunity recognition, risk-taking, creativity, and business planning, enabling them to effectively support aspiring entrepreneurs in their educational journey. AGILITe sought to build an understanding of the EU Green Deal and emerging business opportunities through the exploration of the principles of circularity. Through this integrated approach, we ensured that VET tutors received comprehensive training, covering the necessary digital, entrepreneurial, and sustainability competences set out in the call. The project created bespoke digital training tools accessible through the MOOC incrementally building tutor competences.

<< Implementation >>

Through the AGILITe project, we implemented the following activities:
1.) All partners participated in 3 TPM and 4 Online meetings to build the working ethos of the team and oversee the successful delivery of the AGILITe project
2.) 16 VET trainers completed the first piloting of the AGILITe resources at the LTTA in Croatia and through a cascading effect supported the local training of 89 VET tutors using the new in-service training and EduZines resources. All resources are presented and available on the AGILITe MOOC - https://mooc.agilite-project.eu/ in partner languages
3.) 280 learners engaged with the AGILITe EduZines to build their entrepreneurial competences and key circular economy knowledge
4.) 53 VET professionals and policy makers attended the AGILITe Final Conference in Ireland where the full suite of resources was presented resulting in further training and implementation actions
5.) 226 key stakeholders attended the AGILITe Future VET Symposiums held in Spain, Croatia, Greece, Cyprus, Germany, Norway, Portugal and Romania
6.) 59 active members participating in our transnational community of practice engaging and supporting each other to further develop their skills and exchange ideas on how best to modernise VET.

<< Results >>

The AGILITe project developed the following outputs:
IO1 - AGILITe DigCompEdu EduZines for building the digital competences of VET tutors comprises a toolkit of 6 EduZines addressed to the following: professional engagement, digital resources, teaching and learning, assessment, empowering learners, and facilitating learners' digital competence.
IO2 - AGILITe EntreComp EduZines for building an entrepreneurial spirit within the VET sector consists of 5 EduZines focusing on elements of EntreComp, namely spotting opportunities, creativity, vision, valuing ideas, and ethical and sustainable thinking.
IO3 - AGILITe EduZines for building an understanding of the principles for a circular economy within the VET sector comprises a toolkit of 8 EduZines each addressing a specific circular economy principle, such as design out waste, use renewables, think in systems, and think local.
IO4 - AGILITe MOOC and Community of Practice hosts the in-service training materials for VET tutors and supports the Community of Practice to exchange best practices and provide peer support.

In addition to the concrete project outputs, we delivered training to 105 VET professionals, 280 learners, and engaged 279 stakeholders through our multiplier events.

2020-1-IE02-KA226-HE-000781.title: Innovative Tools for Enhancing E-Learning Solutions in Universities
2020-1-IE02-KA226-HE-000781.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project in order to address the crisis stemming from the Covid 19 pandemic which compelled European universities to move their teaching activities to the online environment. Although most HEI’s had implemented E-Learning platforms many years ago, given the sudden shift to online learning, caused by the pandemic, many teaching staff and librarians experienced difficulties using these platforms. Staff had to adjust quickly and learn how to create and deliver online courses. 

Through the implementation of five Intellectual Outputs (IO’s), the project addressed the need to identify the gap between skills acquired in higher education and the demands of the real labour market,  identified and implemented best practices and designed methods for delivering high quality teaching courses, in digital environments. The project addressed the need to improve the current state of digital education in HEI’s, strengthened the cooperation between universities in the area of digital content creation and also introduced education in the field of digital content creation and copyright involving libraries and their professional development.

<< Objectives >>

The main project activities, that is the Intellectual Outputs, Joint Staff Training Events and Multiplier Events were focused on enhancing the professional development of teaching and support staff, in the field of digital education. The project was focused on primarily disseminating and sharing know-how and knowledge in the area of digital education, and the training of trainers as a strong point for the multiplication of learning outcomes and the realization of a common DIGITOOLS curriculum as the basis of the sustainability of the project and the acquisition of knowledge with a European dimension. The project also wanted to ensure wide reaching impact, uptake, and use of project deliverables among identified audiences and stakeholders. Therefore, training activities and materials were extensively disseminated and promoted within the network of universities and particularly via the Multiplier Events held during this project. Through the implementation of the key project activities, DIGITOOLS aimed to help university staff develop high quality online training courses and give them skills to create and deliver high quality digital content.

<< Implementation >>

The DIGITOOLS project succeeded in implementing all planned activities. 3 Transnational Project Meetings (TPM's) were held in the project as planned, in Ireland (Kick off), Romania and Spain (Final Meeting). Two Multiplier Events were held, hosted by partners from Romania (MBTT) and Croatia (UNIZG) as hybrid events with in-person and online participants. Both Multiplier events attracted large number of delegates with over 400 delegates attending the events as one of the achievements of the project. The DIGITOOLS project also delivered the 5 Intellectual Outputs (IO’s) as envisaged in the original project application. These IO’s include the DIGITOOLS Blended Curriculum (5 modules) as well as the Toolkit for the train – the –trainer theoretical programme (IO5), the Online Platform (IO4) and the Guide for Implementing eLearning in universities (IO5). All the DIGITOOLS Joint Staff Training events were successfully held during the project in HR (UNIZG) and in PT (IPP). In addition, the project also developed a highly comprehensive questionnaire and centralized report to ascertain the skills and competencies required to enhance digital tools and methods to help university staff deliver quality education through online means (IO1).

<< Results >>

DIGITOOLS produced the “Analytic Program Model (IO1)”, involving design & circulation of a comprehensive questionnaire to analyse the ways in which specific courses can be delivered through digital means applied in all HEI’s in the Consortium (Led by IPP). This IO produced an extensive centralised report with findings from all partners. The Toolkit for the train – the – trainer theoretical programme (IO2) (Led by TUS) was also produced featuring a theoretical handbook for trainers & other materials such as lesson plans, description of teaching methods. UTBV led delivery of the important DIGITOOLS Blended Curriculum (IO3) available on the DIGITOOLS Online Platform (IO4) (project website) which was delivered by MBTT.  https://www.digi-tools.eu/  

Regarding IO3, a six-module training program for university staff and professionals, in the field of digital education, was produced. The project also produced the Guide for Implementing eLearning in Universities (I05) led by UNIZG, focused on key topics within Digital Education, including LMS and digital content creation, implementation of training programmes, adapting content of educational programs to the needs of the labour market and interactive online tools for teaching & assessment.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Quality and relevance of higher education in countries outside Europe

2020-1-IS01-KA226-VET-082796.title: Lessons Learned during COVID: Transferability of Best Practice in European Education
2020-1-IS01-KA226-VET-082796.summary:
<< Background >>

The impact will hopefully both assist current education and training providers in coping with the new reality for teachers and learners alike, as well as to prepare us for future scenarios where schools have to adapt to unforseen circumstances.

<< Objectives >>

The purpose of the project was to seek out and collect good and innovative practices from the movers and shakers in European education and how they adapted their schools, education, training and teaching activities to the global Covid pandemic. ​By assembling real stories from educational and training providers across levels, the partnership sought to bring together a collection of proven reactive methods for dealing with any future situations where schools, teachers and learners have to adapt, change and react to uncontrollable outside forces.

This would also provide us an opportunity to look at possibilities to learn from the early adapters and seeks ways to implement good and innovative practices across different fields and levels of education. The main objectives were to collect and disseminate these practices, develop and deliver training seminars, as well as organise and test new approaches where teachers and trainers implement these practices within their own fields of education.

<< Implementation >>

During the project lifetime the partnership met with a broad range of schools on all educational levels, educational and research institutes, experts, teachers and students. These were higher education, teacher education, vocational education and training providers, comprehensive colleges, high-schools, primary schools and kindergartens, as well as both formal and informal adult education and lifelong training providers. The group visited rural and urban schools. Special needs institutions, highly specialised education, people on the forefront of cutting edge technology and early adapters in introducing new ICT approaches within education, as well as those still operating with basic equipment and lesser means.

<< Results >>

We've summarised the key findings of all participants in three videos provided on our website (www.best-edu.eu), as well as in summaries from each of the transnational meetings. There you will also find a range of keynotes and lessons focusing on good practice and practical lessons from a range of different teachers, trainers and experts in the hosting countries.

In addition the partnership attended two training seminars, in Iceland and in Greece, during which they both learned about using Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) in education, as well as the importance of human interaction and theatre based training possibilities in post-Covid schooling.

hr.name: Centar za odgoj i obrazovanje Slava Raskaj Zagreb

2020-1-IT01-KA226-VET-008931.title: DSA: Digital Skills 4 All
2020-1-IT01-KA226-VET-008931.summary:
<< Background >>

The "DS4All" project was born from the experience of digital distance learning required during the covid-19 pandemic, and tries to respond to the need to convey a critical use of a resource prescribed for a specific need, transforming it into a new opportunity for the entire context educational. At the basis of the project is the idea that thanks to the experience of people with Learning Disabilities we will be able to bridge the digital gap, which has grown over the years, in fact, even before distance learning, children were, in any case, present in our schools and young people who not only could have used the computer as a support tool for their study activities, but who specifically need it. When a student with specific difficulties is found in the classroom, the technological tool takes on the guise of a resource whose use arises from a special need and therefore cannot depend on the good will of the teacher, as well as during the pandemic, the use of digital it was an essential decision. But in both cases, what is evident is that without a critical, conscious and, let's add, creative use of technology, without a strategic and methodological approach, the risk of ineffectiveness of the technological equipment is high.

<< Objectives >>

The “DS4All” project was developed over two years, during which the Partners activated a virtuous circle of exchange, which had as its primary focus the experimentation of innovative teaching methodologies integrated with digital tools, in an inclusive perspective; together with a reflection on didactic programming capable of "changing the rules of the game", making distance learning agile and light, without giving up its important educational task. From the design point of view, the added value that the training exchanges  brought is attributable to the possibility of experimenting, by didactic leaders, teachers, educators, didactic tutors, trainers and VET designers, new digital tools and methodologies to enhance teaching integrated for students, especially those with specific Learning Disorders or Special Educational Needs.The dialogical meeting between VET operators and experts in the digital sector allowed the VET staff to be updated on new strategies for an increasingly effective and inclusive teaching, which is able to profitably use advantages offered by new technologies.

<< Implementation >>

Thanks to "DS4All" there was a real dialogic encounter, a contamination between professionalism, needs and intentions: the consequence of this integration consisted in an awareness of the possibility of applying teaching methodologies with a more experiential and proactive approach, able to improve the effectiveness of the teaching itself and in students stimulate reflexivity in learning also thanks to the enhancement of their digital skills. The first mobility was dedicated to training on the "flipped classroom" methodology in order to understand its essential components and the methods for successfully implementing it in the classroom. The second mobility envisaged a training exchange about some innovative teaching methodologies, based primarily on digital and IT resources and their inclusive potential, while the last mobility focused on the educational impact of Visual Learning. The meetings stimulated sensitivity towards critical and reflective approaches to the use of digital tools in teaching not only designed for those with specific learning disabilities or special educational needs but for the entire class group.

<< Results >>

The outcome of these exchanges will flow into: • Benchmarking analysis about the use of distance learning in partner countries and the integration of compensatory software; • “Webinar DS4All”, free webinars for direct target of the project; • Report on the applicability of the "Flipped Classroom" in the VET field; • Toolkit on didactical planning strategies in the VET field, able to integrate not only digital and IT resources but also a different temporal programming. Thanks to the constant collaboration with Associations and public bodies that support families and students with learning disabilities or from vulnerable groups, the project partners will have the opportunity to enhance a more sensitive approach to these needs in the Vocational Training Centers involved, this will create a positive impact on openness to change, so that new learning can be drawn from it.

2020-1-IT01-KA226-VET-009074.title: MoBlend – Educational Resource to enhance Virtual & Blended Work-Based Learning
2020-1-IT01-KA226-VET-009074.summary:
<< Background >>

The Covid-19 crisis has strongly affected the economic life and labour market as much as the school life.
All forms of education and training, including VET, have been disrupted, with WBL and apprenticeships being the most affected. During the lockdown, distance learning failed to reach between 5% and 20% of beneficiary students in Europe, including those living in rural areas, with poor IT literacy and limited economic means, as well as students with special needs.
In this context, there is a critical need to improve the quality of Virtual and Blended WBL (V&BWBL) and to ensure its inclusiveness. In order to reach the desired scenario, the needs of the target groups addressed by the project (VET Students, especially the ones with fewer opportunities and special needs, VET School Staff, Company Tutors) have to be satisfied.
The needs of the target groups have been analysed during the project design and the results highlight poor knowledge of adequate technological means (both VET students and Compay Tutors), a lack of trust (VET School Staff and VET students), engagement (VET students) and payoff (CompanyTutors) in and from V&BWBL.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of “MoBlend – Educational Resource to enhance Virtual & Blended Work-Based Learning” is to improve the quality of Virtual and Blended WBL initiatives and to guarantee an equal and inclusive access and participation to ensure its inclusiveness, especially for students with fewer opportunites and special needs.
The specific objectives are: 
O1) Support VET Students, VET School Staff and Company Tutors in improving the quality of V&BWBL; 
O2) Promote the inclusiveness of V&BWBL;
O3) Deepen the interest and trust in V&BWBL, affirming their value and match with the requests of the labour market;
O4) Develop a cross-border and cross sector synergy with the purpose of creating innovative uses of Virtual&Blended Work-Based Learning tailored to the needs of students with fewer opportunities and special needs, even afterwards the COVID era

<< Implementation >>

The activities planned aimed to achieve such objectives are: 
- development of a tailored learning course on digital tools and methods of V&BWBL
- design of an ad-hoc and user-friendly tool for the evaluation and validation of VET experiences
- Best Practice and existing policies research
- Awareness campaign
- Virtual WBL Test
- 4 Transnational Project Meetings
- 5 Multiplier Events

<< Results >>

The main results and impact of the project activities are the following:
- OER to improve the digital competences needed to perform V&BWBL
- WebtTool to monitor the progress and the results of VET mobilities 
- Compendium of Virtual VET Best Practices to learn from previous positive experiences
- Promotion and dissemination pack that includes: leaflets, logo, headed paper, social pages, newsletters, a website, articles on local/regional/national newspapers
- Community of Practice to promote cooperation and further development of virtual and blended WBL at the European level
- increased ability to provide a work based learning path through virtual or blended means;
- increased awareness and confidence of virtual WBL opportunites;
- increased digital skills, knowledge of IT tool for WBL, language skill and soft skills
- enhanced cooperation between organizations active in the VET field enabling mutual exchange and improvement of working methods and good practices;
- increased awareness of learning needs of students and especially those with FO and SN;
- deepened knowledge of OERs for the provision of training courses and learning activities;
- gained knowledge of Video pedagogy for the provision of training courses and learning activities;
- increased awareness of learning needs of students and especially those with FO and SN;
- increased training offer;
- fostered dialogue with political decision makers, public institutions and other stakeholders and increased its prestige at European level;
- increased network of organizations active in VET field at European level
- increased knowledge and management skills of the Erasmus + KA2 and KA202 projects
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2020-1-IT02-KA226-HE-095091.title: Online Internship in Tourism
2020-1-IT02-KA226-HE-095091.summary:
<< Background >>

During the pandemic and in the phase of exit from the emergency period, one of the critical issues of regular activities of the universities was internship. Most institutions, while prepared for online learning, were not ready for online internships. Work-based learning, often represented by curricular internships, is widely recognised as a fundamental step of the student toward professionalisation and transition from education to work. Internship allows students to gain experience in real work settings, test competences in context, and acquire new skills. After the pandemic, remote working took different forms by testing hybrid solutions or becoming the norm for some categories of workers, but it was not a coming back. The future of work is also online. Therefore, universities should equip the students with specific skills to be prepared for companies that use full or partial remote working arrangements.

<< Objectives >>

ON-IT focused on developing guidelines and resources to design and implement meaningful remote internships in higher education. Through the project, the consortium also aimed to deepen understanding of remote work and to detect needs to prepare students for the labour market.

<< Implementation >>

Starting from mapping experiences from higher education institutions and reviewing present literature and tools, the consortium worked on a potential model to support universities to integrate remote internships into the learning offer. Then, guidelines for the purpose were drafted by consulting involved targets all over the process as key informants and for feedback collection on potential models. A learning course for students to support the acquisition of competences needed for a digital labour market was developed and tested; procedures and tools for managing an online or hybrid internship were also developed to support the key players involved in the process, namely the students, the academic supervisor and the company supervisor.

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs, available from the project website and published under the licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, include
- “Experiences of Virtual Internship in Europe. How can virtual internships ensure meaningful work-based learning experiences?” (report) and an Online Map that contains the analysis of the mapping exercise.
- “Guidelines for the implementation of online internships in Higher Education” that aims to define quality criteria, processes and rules for implementing effective remote work-based learning at the university.
- Online and hybrid internship cases, which includes the outcome of the piloting phase, in the form of Guides for interns and supervisors for online and hybrid work-based experiences, and testimonials of internships, published onto the website.
- “How to succeed in online internship”, an online course composed of a set of learning materials consisting of eight modules, completed with activities.. In the ON-IT process, the passed tests of each module represented the evidence for the recognition of learning, which was certified through an open badge delivered by the ON-IT consortium.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2020-1-IT02-KA226-SCH-095596.title: Filling the Gap: Open Educational Resources for supporting teachers in distance learning
2020-1-IT02-KA226-SCH-095596.summary:
<< Background >>

“Filling the Gap: OER for supporting teachers in distance learning” has been designed with the aim of developing tools and strategies for distance and blended learning, thanks to the strengthening of methodological and digital skills of teachers and educators, in particular using the Open Educational Resources for integrated digital learning and for distance learning, with a specific focus on inclusive approaches.
The genesis of the project was situated within the scenario caused by the Covid-19 pandemic when the distance learning model was the only possible solution. Aware that teachers and educators were not ready for this sudden transition to online, the partner organisations considered it essential to support them by providing tools that would facilitate this new teaching methodology. Furthermore, the partnership were aware of the importance of guarantee education for all learners, developing digital learning materials that were also inclusive.

<< Objectives >>

The aim, achieved, of the project was to provide teachers and educators of European schools with tools and methodologies to support distance and blended learning activities. Specifically, the project focused on the development and strengthening of digital knowledge and skills and on the use of OER (Open Educational Resources) with a focus on the inclusion of students with intellectual disabilities and the well-being of teachers. To this purpose, the partnership developed and implemented two intellectual outputs: an online course on distance learning (MOOC on Distance Learning) and a kit of distance and blended learning activities (Distance Learning Activities Kit).

<< Implementation >>

For carrying out the project activities, the specific educational, digital and inclusive expertise of the partnership was fundamental. This is composition of the partnership, engaged in the promotion of an innovative online and blended learning method:
-4 secondary schools (LICEO FANTI, PLATON, BERNARDIN FRANKOPAN and COLEGIO HUERTA SANTA ANA)
-1 cooperative training center (IRECOOP ER)
-1 cooperative expert in digital and educational services (ARCHILABO')
-1 University specialized in Inclusive Education and Digital Solutions (UCLL)
The activities carried out can be summarized as follows:
A. Data collection for IO1 (MOOC on Distance Learning) and IO2 (Distance Learning Activities Kit)
B. Content creation for IO1; analysis and selection of activities for IO2
C. Expert training, feedback collection and content validation
D. Creation of the platform and translations of the contents
E. Test of the outputs (piloting) with external teachers
F. Final validation and dissemination

<< Results >>

MOOC ON DISTANCE LEARNING (IO1). It is an online training course available in 6 languages (EN, IT, HR, ES, BE, GR) dedicated to teachers and educators who want to develop or improve their skills in the planning, implementation and evaluation of educational online and blended activities, with a specific attention to OER and the inclusion of SEN students. It is composed of 4 modules: 1. Didactic planning, 2. Evaluation, 3. OER, 4. Inclusion and well-being. It is accessible for free through the Filling the Gap website and it uses the Open Badges certification system.
DISTANCE LEARNING ACTIVITIES KIT (IO2). The Kit, in 6 languages (EN, IT, HR, ES, BE, GR) is a web collection of 24 distance and blended learning activities selected from those developed by European teachers during the Covid-19 pandemic. The activities can be filtered by subject, age of students, duration, learning resources, tests, tools. A single specific page is dedicated to each activity which contains the description of the methodological steps necessary to carry it out, the assessment of skills and the suggested methods of communication. Each activity is linked to a specific lesson of the MOOC.

2020-1-LT01-KA226-HE-094740.title: Quality of Virtual Studies
2020-1-LT01-KA226-HE-094740.summary:
<< Background >>

Europe Education Area is based on Digital Education Action Plan which promotes youth mobility & information society. Challenges for student physical mobility because of social, financial etc. barriers, COVID crisis forces changes in HE & encourages preparation of the content of study subjects adapted to the remote work & validation of virtual mobility. This would also help to foster collaboration between HEIs in a virtual learning environment (VLE) & to create a virtual community. 
When developing ICT based teaching/learning studies, it is vital for teacher to be able to select the most appropriate study & assessment methods (ensuring academic integrity), provide necessary support system that would allow steering learning to the right direction. Thus, there was a need for comprehensive methodology, based on which teachers could effectively choose appropriate tools & methods for virtual studies. To date, there was no generalized methodology to ensure the quality of the virtual course & conduct studies in an engaging and motivating way. This problem existed not only in the HEIs in this project, but to other European HEIs as well.  Therefore, the solution to these problems was extremely relevant for the entire European HE sector.

<< Objectives >>

Overall aim of the project was to increase the quality of teaching/learning in virtual learning environment (VLE) & the study process by creating preconditions for the recognition of the acquired results during virtual mobility. 
Project was dedicated to educate staff of pedagogical and technological innovations & to transfer the good practices for cohesion in Europe in order for teachers to apply this information in their online subjects. Project also aimed to ensure the quality of studies, student motivation & academic integrity, recognition of study results by developing the internationalization of HEI at home (virtual student & teacher mobility, inter-institutional studies), provide necessary support system that would allow steering learning to the right direction. The formation of joint academic groups of different HEI for the creation of the study subjects aimed to expand students’ experience. 
This project attempted to solve the challenges presented above through 3 objectives: 1. Creating the methodology for teaching/learning in VLE. 2. Improving competencies of academic staff (teachers' didactic, digital competencies, gamification of the study process). 3. Pilot testing of the developed teaching/learning methodology.

<< Implementation >>

Overall aim of the project was to educate staff about pedagogical and technological innovations, apply them to online subjects, ensure the quality of studies, student motivation & academic integrity. 
Objective 1: develop methodology for teaching/learning & assessment in VLE
•	Activity 1.1: Case analysis of 5 countries of:
a) teaching/learning and assessment methods of VLE.
b) plagiarism prevention, academic ethics assurance processes & tools in VLE. 
c) tools and methods for student support and motivation promotion (study process gamification) in VLE.
•	Activity 1.2: Methodology of teaching/learning and assessment in VLE based on case analysis results and pilot-run.
•	Activity 1.3: Methodology translation to partner languages. 
Objective 2: improvement of academic staff competencies
•	Activity 2.1: Created TTT program, trained 20 teachers 
•	Activity 2.2: 4 local multiplier events and 1 international conference.
Objective 3: pilot-run of developed methodology
•	Activity 3.1: 4 VLE subjects developed according to the elaborated methodology and piloted by 80 partner HEIs students. 
•	Activity 3.2: Published 2 Scientific articles.
•	Activity 3.3: report on VLE methodology application practice (set of educational videos in Youtube).

<< Results >>

1.	5 countries’ case studies on teaching/learning & assessment (TLA) methods of VLE; plagiarism prevention, academic ethics assurance processes & tools in VLE; tools and methods for student support & motivation promotion (study process gamification) in VLE. 
2.	Methodology of TLA in VLE based on case analysis results & pilot-run was created in English & translated to partner (LT, FI, ES, HR) languages.
3.	1 international TTT “Teaching/learning in the VLE: possibilities, efficiency and quality”, 20 teachers attended.  
4.	The pilot run of the methodology. 4 online subjects (each 3 ECTS) were created in Moodle according to the developed methodology & tested by 80 students. 
5.	32 info sheets created.  
6.	Scientific article „Student Support & Motivation in Online Learning: Evidence From Pilot Online Course Implementation“ published in scientific journal „Applied Research in Lithuanian Applied Science Universities“.  
7.	a visual guide for HEI teachers (30 videos in Youtube) was created.
8.	4 local multiplier events organized in FI, ES, UK, ES, attended by 143 persons.  
9.	International conference to present the project results & outcomes was organized in LT, attended by 62 participants, 47 of which were from outside institutions.

2020-1-LT01-KA226-SCH-094825.title: Be-aware Re-aware and Re-discover curiosity and connection in education through outdoor learning. (Pop-up Learning)
2020-1-LT01-KA226-SCH-094825.summary:
<< Background >>

The sudden, unplanned transition to distance learning in the spring of 2020 threw educational institutions into a series of challenges — disrupting academic schedules, disrupting extracurricular programs, and reducing assessment and academic feedback cycles at many schools. Engaging students in learning and bringing back the joy of learning to them is not an easy challenge. Children today who are going through the coronavirus pandemic need a lot of educational games in different spaces, especially outdoors, to help them understand the radical changes that have affected so many aspects of their lives. And when kids go back to school, they need a lot of time to process all the changes they've been through. The curiosity and connection that comes from learning outdoors can be a much-needed antidote to the anxiety and stress of 2020. Decades of research and theory show that play is the primary way children make sense of the world around them. Outdoor pedagogy helps children develop better social, physical, academic, and psychological skills. Outdoor Learning has a positive effect on children's health, interesting activities motivate them, children experience the joy of creativity, and acquire new social competencies.

<< Objectives >>

OBJECTIVES:
- To strengthen the profile of teachers: To be creative and proactive in identifying and finding solutions to emotional or academic challenges that individual students face;
- To pilot a need-based virtual training program, which is based on digital-outdoor learning;
- To motivate the students in outdoor learning;
- To produce materials that facilitate the outdoor learning process;
- To prepare, adapt, and engage students in the new normal;
- To improve the students' and teachers' communication, cooperation, critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills;
- To raise cultural awareness and develop global skills of our students and teachers that are so necessary for the future;
- To increase cross-sectoral collaboration in the field of SCHOOL education;
- To strengthen European collaboration of the participating organizations;
- To increase experience in the management of long-term projects with multiple partners.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were implemented throughout the project:
1. Organized 6 online project team meetings via Zoom to resolve issues related to the project.
2. Organized 2 international project team meetings in Lithuania and Greece.
3. Created project logo, Facebook page "Pop-up learning" https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100070939972502 
4. Written 5 newsletters of the project to present project activities.
5. Prepared, organized, and playlisted YouTube virtual training. A total of 31 videos. About 400 participants took part in the virtual training.
6. Created https://pop-uplearning.org/ webpage to provide theoretical and practical information on the organization of outdoor education.
7. Prepared Tool-kit for Teachers to teach Outdoor Learning.
8. Prepared self-learning online course in Moodle platform https://rokvarpelis.vma.lm.lt/
9. Prepared Active games kit. The game conspectus includes 20 active games that can be played in nature while in the fresh air. 
10. eTwinning.
11. Organised more than 15 various dissemination events.
12. Project progress monitoring, activity evaluation, preparation of budget reports, documentation management, and qualitative and quantitative assessment of the project were carried out.

<< Results >>

OUTPUTS:
O1: The virtual courses: Teachers learn outdoor learning, and envision and implement outdoor learning wherever they are.
O2: Tool-kit for Teachers to teach Outdoor Learning
Created https://pop-uplearning.org/ webpage to provide theoretical and practical information on the organization of outdoor education.
Prepared self-learning online course in Moodle platform https://rokvarpelis.vma.lm.lt/
Prepared Active games kit.
