2020-1-MK01-KA226-SCH-094503.title: Sustainable Development Goals for Pupils
2020-1-MK01-KA226-SCH-094503.summary:
<< Background >>

During the pandemic period, it was realized that even though there are some online materials on the SDGs for educators to use, the materials are mostly designed for use in a classroom. Since the teaching process has changed to online classes, it was decided to develop materials that can be used in online teaching. The organizations wanted to help teachers and meet their needs when it came to online teaching, which is why it was decided to develop a curriculum with activities regarding the SDGs and also create a curriculum where they can learn more about online tools that they can use in their lectures. The learning materials that were created can be used both in online teaching and also in a classroom.

<< Objectives >>

The organizations wanted to design and develop learning materials that would help pupils develop the key competencies for the 21st century of critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving, and also teach them about Sustainable Development Goals. We wanted to support teachers and schools in having learning materials to teach their pupils about sustainable development, and the key competences of the 21st century, and to have them available for free online in their native languages.  Also, the organizations wanted to contribute to teachers developing their digital skills, to help them better deliver on distance learning and that is why we created a curriculum that covers different online tools and explanations to use them. The organizations also wanted to have all the developed materials in one place for easier access and that is why we created a website where they can access and download everything for free.
The overall objective of this project was to deliver an online platform that will teach pupils to promote and empower pupils towards more sustainable practices;
teach pupils key competencies (critical thinking, creativity and problem-solving); deliver online resources (teaching materials) that were built from the ground up to be creative and interactive in an online format; provide schools with free available online learning materials for their use, thus supporting their ability to provide remote learning opportunities; and teach teachers digital skills, in particular, related to distance learning.

<< Implementation >>

Throughout this project, the organizations had:
- 4 Transnational Projects Meetings (1st in Kochani, N.Macedonia; 2nd in  Stara Zagora, Bulgaria; 3rd in Karlovac, Croatia and 4th in Ohrid, N.Macedonia)
- 3 Intellectual Outputs (Output 1-Design and development of learning materials; Output 2-Design and development of online platform and Output 3 - Development of digital skills course)
- 4 Multiplier Events (each organization (4 organizations) held an event where they presented all the activities and results that were done and achieved in this project) 
Also, a logo contest was held where students from all schools that were partners could present their designs, also in Macedonia schools from all over the country were invited to take part. 
After the learning materials were developed, an open call was held for schools in all 3 countries for teachers to participate in and test the materials with their students.

<< Results >>

Output 1- Design and development of learning materials -  learning materials on the SDGs were designed and developed. The participants took into account feedback and contributions from teachers (with the testing). There are materials for each of the SDGs taking different shapes such as questions, quizzes, challenges, and interactive presentations.
Output 2 - Design and development of online platform - a platform was designed and developed that hosts the aforementioned learning materials as well as other presentations, articles and facts regarding the SDGs. Also, the Digital skill course in a form of a curriculum is posted on the website.
Output 3 - Development of digital skills course - a teacher training course was developed on digital skills related to distance learning. The Digital skill course in a form of a curriculum is posted on the website. In the curriculum, teachers can find different online tools with explanations and ways to use them in their teaching processes.

2020-1-NL01-KA226-HE-083098.title: European Open Platform for Prescribing Education
2020-1-NL01-KA226-HE-083098.summary:
<< Background >>

Clinical pharmacology and therapeutics (CPT) education in Europe has been found to leave students ill-prepared to prescribe medicines safely, both subjectively and objectively. This deficiency is primarily attributed to the persistence of traditional teaching methods, relying on textbooks and lectures. Research indicates that the acquisition of safe prescribing skills requires active training on real cases, known as a problem-based teaching approach. Transitioning from a conventional to a problem-based curriculum poses challenges.

The European Association for Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics has issued recommendations to enhance and standardize CPT education across Europe. One of these recommendations emphasizes intensified internet-based collaboration and resource sharing. Before implementing this initiative, we assessed the efficacy of online resources as teaching tools for CPT education. We conducted a comprehensive review of existing resources and conducted a survey among European CPT educators to gauge their perceptions of the online platform.

The COVID-19 pandemic further underscored the relevance and importance of online teaching methods in this context.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objective of this project was to foster international collaboration among CPT  educators by establishing the European Open Platform for Prescribing Education. This online platform was designed to act as a comprehensive repository aimed at facilitating the integration of problem-based education into local educational institutions. The platform encompasses various components:

- Collaborative Resource Creation: Resources created by and for CPT teachers.
- Resource Sharing: Existing educational materials are made accessible as open educational resources on the platform, encouraging knowledge dissemination and sharing among educators
- Teacher Training Tutorials: The platform offers a range of tutorials, both content-specific and focused on pedagogical techniques
- Interactive Discussion Board: An interactive discussion board fosters engagement and knowledge exchange among international colleagues
- Participant Recruitment for Research Studies: Educators can recruit participants for research studies related to CPT education

The development of this platform was guided by an international consensus study, ensuring alignment with the preferences and requirements of prospective users.

<< Implementation >>

The project's successful implementation was achieved through a series of strategic activities. Before the project's initiation, a framework consensus study provided a robust foundation. We began by conducting a thorough needs assessment among potential platform users, gathering their input through group interviews to prioritize collaborative content creation.

Concurrently, we developed the online platform using iterative cycles and rigorous beta-testing. Our initial goal was to create three resources, but the project expanded to include the development of seven resources. Additionally, we crafted a toolkit on open educational resources and intellectual property management, subjecting all content to rigorous testing and evaluation.

Dissemination efforts included participation in events such as the EACPT conference and a dedicated multiplier event to broaden awareness of the project's outcomes. Continuous evaluation was integrated, with ongoing assessment and final written evaluations from users to gather valuable feedback.

Our commitment extends beyond implementation; we are actively working to expand the platform's global reach, fostering international collaboration among CPT educators on a broader scale.

<< Results >>

The project has yielded significant and tangible outcomes, including:

Online Platform: The establishment of the European Open Platform for Prescribing Education, accessible at prescribingeducation.eu, which has attracted more than 70 active international  teachers collaborating to enhance and harmonize Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics (CPT) education. Weekly, new applicants continue to join this community.

Resource Development: The creation of seven high-quality, problem-based online resources and teacher courses for CPT education, featuring:
- A comprehensive guide addressing race-based medicine, diversity, and inclusion.
- An informative guide on leveraging chatGPT and artificial intelligence as educational tools.
- A modular teaching program focused on pharmacovigilance.
- Online international interactive case discussions.

Multiplier Event: A two-day, impactful multiplier event featuring a diverse range of speakers and workshops, enriching the knowledge and skills of participants and fostering collaboration within the CPT education community.

Scientific Publications: The publication of six open-access scientific articles, with five already published and one currently under consideration for publication.

2020-1-NL01-KA226-SCH-083122.title: ALCOR: Building TeacherParent Connections Through Digital Multilingual Learning
2020-1-NL01-KA226-SCH-083122.summary:
<< Background >>

European classrooms are becoming increasingly multilingual and culturally diverse. Yet, most education systems in Europe are
characterized by a monolingual ‘mind set’, with teachers who are ill prepared to teach students with diverse cultural, socio-economic and plurilingual backgrounds. Our objective was to support linguistically, socially and economically disadvantaged
primary school learners in Europe who are at risk of falling even further behind their peers as a result of COVID-19 school closures.
The ALCOR-project has giving the much wanted opportunity for European teachers to follow an intensive train-the-trainer teacher programme and a Massive Open Online Course (MOOC). Both are aimed at building professional teacher competence in three areas: 
(1) digital and blended learning, 
(2) plurilingual pedagogies and 
(3) engaging plurilingual parents through the use of multilingual (digital) learning resource.

<< Objectives >>

Our aim was to enhance teachers' skills in digital learning, plurilingual pedagogies, and involving parents.
• They grasp the significance of parents as vital partners and effective engagement methods.
• They now possess the ability to incorporate web-based learning into their teaching approaches.
• They can train and aid colleagues in creating 'language friendly' environments with strong parental support.

Parents from diverse backgrounds are now more engaged in the school community.
• They better understand their role in their children's school experience and well-being.
• They've acquired skills to collaborate effectively with teachers using multilingual digital resources.
Across Europe, educators, trainers, leaders, and policymakers recognize the importance of including plurilingual learners' mother tongue/home languages in primary education. They also value parental engagement for social inclusion, student well-being, and academic success.
Teachers and educators have successfully finished a Massive Online Course (MOOC) on Strengthening Teacher/Parent Connections.

<< Implementation >>

We had six IO activities
O2  = 	Background study on Building Parent/Teacher Connections through Multilingual Digital Learning through literature study and focus groups. 
O3  = 	Two White board animations on the relevance of multilingual pedagogies in classrooms 
O4 = 	Study Guide for Teacher Training Programme
O5 = 	Reports on the 4 LTT learning events 
O6 =	a construction of a educational Massive Open Online Course (MOOC)

Furthermore we had 4 LTT's organised and 4 Multiplier Events in the partner countries.

<< Results >>

A core group of eight primary school teachers has gained insight in the relevance and importance of the mother tongue/home languages of linguistically disadvantaged learners for achieving school success and how to integrate this into web-based learning. 
Parents, connected to the schools of the core group of teachers have become more involved in the school community. 
Colleagues in schools have been informed and trained by the participating teachers on multiligual strategies in lessons. 
We have furthermore: 
- a study on about multilingualism in education systems of partner countries 
- A Study Guide for Teacher Training Programm
- Two animated videos
- a MOOC which can be followed through Coursera. 84 professionals already did so! 
- 4 reports on the LTTs with insights of experiences of participating teachers.

2020-1-PL01-KA226-HE-096278.title: Innovative Competence in Online Higher Education
2020-1-PL01-KA226-HE-096278.summary:
<< Background >>

A significant challenge faced by academic teachers and university authorities following the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic was the lack of digital skills and knowledge of online teaching methodologies. The sudden shift to remote teaching highlighted the need for educators to have a strong understanding of digital tools and technologies and the ability to effectively deliver content and engage with students online. Additionally, many academic teachers were not familiar with the methodology and best practices for conducting online classes, which further compounded the challenge.
InCompEdu project  aimed at filling this gap of knowledge and develop innovative solutions to make it possible for teaching staff and, consequently, students to have high quality education and ease some of the challenges they faced.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project was to improve the quality of online higher education by providing academic teachers with the necessary skills and knowledge to effectively use tools and platforms in their teaching. In addition to building the digital competencies of academic teachers, the InCompEdu project also aimed to support University Authorities in improving the quality of online higher education. This was achieved by providing University Authorities with an understanding of the challenges related to online education, including the technical aspects and methodology of conducting online classes.  
Successful implementation of online teaching requires the integration of activities in many areas of the university's work, both related to IT and to the area of improving and evaluating the quality of education. The project aimed to present the experiences of European universities, possible IT solutions to be used, and a new approach to creating courses in a cross-sectional way, using DT methodology.
Overall, the Incompedu project aimed to provide academic teachers with the necessary skills and knowledge to adapt to the changing landscape of education, ensuring that they can provide high-quality online education to their students.

<< Implementation >>

In order to achieve the goals set out in the project, various activities were undertaken. These activities included conducting two extensive surveys, two rounds of Delphi studies, and market research on the functionality of available online teaching solutions. In addition, 57 of in-depth interviews were conducted with academic teachers to obtain information about good practices in online teaching. A short-term-training program was also organized in the area of Design Thinking workshops, aimed at developing scenarios for online classes. The knowledge gained from the training was utilized to conduct three DT workshops and evaluate new online teaching scenarios.
Furthermore, each of the project partners organized a Multiplier Event to share the results of the project and obtain valuable feedback from the participants which allowed the project results to be promoted on a wider scale and reach a wider audience.
To facilitate development of final outputs, coordination of work and ensurance of proper  quality partners organized 4 Transnational Meeting and 20  working meetings. We also organized several dissemination activities in the partner countries - workshops, conferences, meetings on local, regional, and national level.

<< Results >>

We produced 5 raports and elaborations and 1 collection of short clips presenting practical aspects of online teaching (Filmoteque)
Deliverables:
IO1 D1: "Report on identified challenges and problems that occurred during the transition to online teaching mode in the COVID-19 pandemic period",
IO1 D2: "Teacher Stories. Inspiring good practices – a booklet of educator stories",
IO2 D1: "Technical Platform Booklet. Review of available IT solutions for on-line education", 
IO2 D2: "Technical Platform Booklet. Software or tools used for online teaching activities and Delphi analysis on identified challenges and problems in online teaching",

In the last deliverable we included additionally a Guidebook on the use of Design Thinking in developing online lessons scenarios - which has been written in 7 languages, including 6 national languages of project partners.

2020-1-PL01-KA226-SCH-095530.title: DISTANCE-DIGITAL TEACHING AND LEARNING IN THE POST-COVID-19 ERA
2020-1-PL01-KA226-SCH-095530.summary:
<< Background >>

The unexpected pandemic of Covid-19 has caused a great alternation in the educational systems worldwide, whereas the health crisis had affected the school education of almost 1.6 billion children across 195 countries globally. In most countries, the pandemic brought about temporary closures of schools while digital learning became the new normality. These nationwide closures not only affect school learning but also impose new ways of teaching, bringing to light the importance of digital literacy, the use of technology tools, the resilience of educational procedures adn the readiness of educational bodies to offer constance high quality teaching, learning and assessment.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives were achieved through the design, development, pilot testing and evaluation of a FLEXIBLE LEARNING TOOLS KIT supported by a Cloud-Based PLATFORM and MOBILE APPLICATION aimed at supporting SCHOOLS in developing their own FLEXIBLE LEARNING ACTION PLAN to introduce FLEXIBLE LEARNING and DIGITAL LEARNING in their formal education.
Specifically, the project aimed to:
- Support schools to develop their own DISTANCE LEARNING ACTION PLAN that led to the modernization and digital transformation of their schools.
- Empower teachers through upskilling and re-training opportunities based on the provision of in-service training courses to help them design and deliver distance learning, while supporting students to pursue distance learning.
- Develop a series of capacity-building workshops both online and offline to support parents in their role, especially for younger children during distance learning.
- Support students in learning, personal and organizational skills in remote learning.

<< Implementation >>

The Di2LEARN project included the following activities:

2020-1-PL01-KA226-VET-095187.title: SmartZine based resources for soft skills development of graduates for work and life
2020-1-PL01-KA226-VET-095187.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because we saw an important need to support young people, especially representatives of Generation Z, in developing soft skills that are crucial in today's labour market. With increasing technology and digitalisation, it is observed that younger generations who have grown up in an environment full of technology often find it difficult to develop interpersonal and communication skills that are essential in the workplace. The SOFTee project aimed to counteract these difficulties by creating innovative educational resources to help young people develop these skills, increasing their employability and adaptability in a rapidly changing work environment. The SOFTee project aimed to bridge this gap by developing educational resources in SmartZine format that are not only attractive to young audiences, but also effective in developing their soft skills. EduZines, interactive infographics and other innovative tools created as part of the project aim to offer young people authentic and profound learning experiences that will help them better prepare for professional and personal challenges.

<< Objectives >>

The SOFTee project was created to support young people from generation Z who enter the labour market, often without sufficiently developed soft skills such as emotional intelligence, effective communication, problem solving, teamwork and the ability to act under pressure. Today's labour market increasingly values these competences, recognising them as key to career success. 
SOFTee aimed to bridge this gap by offering innovative educational tools in the form of interactive infographics and multimedia resources that were designed to engage young people and stimulate a deeper understanding and development of the necessary competencies. Training for teachers and trainers in the use of these modern tools was also a key element of the project.
In addition, SOFTee aimed to create a lasting impact on the labour market by increasing the employability of young people. Through the development of key soft skills, project participants were expected to become more competitive in the labour market, better adapted to the requirements of modern employers, which in turn was expected to foster their long-term professional development.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the SOFTee project, activities were implemented to develop soft skills among young people from Generation Z and to support educators in their work with this group. A key element of the project was the development and implementation of innovative educational tools, such as interactive infographics and multimedia EduZines, designed to engage young people and develop in them the competences necessary in the labour market. These educational resources are available in a format tailored to the digital preferences of Generation Z, enabling them to learn in a way that suits their lifestyles.
A training programme was developed for teachers and trainers from different European countries who were trained in the use of the new educational tools. These trainings were divided into two phases: the first focused on developing pedagogical skills related to delivering high-quality online learning, and the second on building digital competences to create media rich in educational content.
In addition, local outreach campaigns, aimed at raising awareness of the importance of soft skills and promoting the developed tools to young people and their teachers.

<< Results >>

As part of the SOFTee project, the results developed influenced the development of soft skills in young people and improved the quality of education in this area. One of the main outcomes of the project was the development and implementation of innovative educational tools, including interactive infographics and multimedia EduZines. These resources have been carefully designed to meet the needs and preferences of Generation Z, resulting in engaging and effective learning materials. They enable young people to develop key competences, such as communication, teamwork and problem-solving, in a way that suits their learning style.
Individual training materials were provided for teachers and trainers (3 each from the participating countries), who acquired the necessary skills to use the new tools effectively in their daily work with young people. These trainings increased the pedagogical competences of the participants and contributed to the quality of teaching in soft skills.
The SOFTee project not only provided state-of-the-art educational tools, but also created OER to have a long-term impact on education and the development of soft skills, which are crucial for the professional success of the young generation.

2020-1-PL01-KA226-VET-095626.title: Enanching SMEs' Resilience After Lock Down
2020-1-PL01-KA226-VET-095626.summary:
<< Background >>

The global shock caused by the COVID-19 pandemic prompted our consortium to initiate the ESMERALD project. The impact of the pandemic crossed social and economic boundaries - there was no precedent in history that we could build on. Estimates from institutions and reputable organizations such as the European Commission, the OECD, the WTO and the IMF predicted a significant drop in GDP, trade volume and overall economic growth. This unprecedented situation meant a huge, still largely undetermined impact on the economy. Micro and small / medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) were unanimously identified as the most vulnerable to economic risks.
A series of reports and surveys revealed the harsh reality already faced by SMEs across Europe. Surveys among Polish SMEs pointed to rising costs, reduced sales and anticipated labor shortages. 
Against this troubling backdrop, our consortium came together, driven by an urgent need for action. The ESMERALD project was designed in response to the said challenges, providing useful guidance, tools and training to these vulnerable businesses. Our ultimate goal was to increase their resilience and adaptability in the face of such unprecedented adversity.

<< Objectives >>

The goal of our consortium was to provide support and guidance to MSMEs grappling with the significant changes caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. We aimed to achieve the following 4 key results:
1. Development of the ESMERALD open educational resource platform: it serves as the central repository for the ”Micro and SME COVID Response Toolkit”. 
2. Creation of a comprehensive report on the impact of COVID-19 on Micro and SMEs: We sought to assess crisis and risk management solutions that could strengthen the resilience of SMEs to external shocks such as a pandemic. This report is a key part of the toolkit.
3. Providing training modules for SMEs: Using insights from the report and the toolkit, we sought to deliver innovative training modules for SMEs. 
4. Developing ESMERALD Guidelines and Manifesto: We sought to develop guidelines to encourage the adoption and use of ESMERALD in business support and vocational education and training (VET) systems across Europe. In addition, we created the so-called ESMERALD Manifesto to inform policymakers by providing factual evidence for policy-making in support of SMEs during and after the pandemic.

<< Implementation >>

During the first 3 months of the Project, the Cracow University of Economics (UEK) laid the foundation for the joint venture. A comprehensive project management plan was developed to provide clear guidelines for all subsequent project activities. 
Intellectual Outcome (IO) 1 - ESMERALD OER Platform: From June 2021 to May 2023, under the guidance of IWS, Partners co-created the ESMERALD Open Educational Resources (OER) Platform - a hub for all Project content.
IO2 - Comprehensive COVID Impact Report: from June 2021 to February 2022 Partners conducted research within their national entrepreneurship networks - to identify the most relevant trends that emerged during COVID-19. 
IO3 - COVID response toolkit - from February 2022 to May 2023, we focused on developing training materials for such a toolkit. From October 2022 to spring 2023, we conducted testing and validation with target groups.
IO4 - Guidelines for ESMERALD Mainstreaming and the Manifesto: from February 2023 to May 2023, under the leadership of the University of Dubrovnik, Guidelines for dissemination of ESMERALD results and the so-called "Resilience Manifesto" were developed. 
The Partners then led “dissemination events” (Multiplier Events).

<< Results >>

1. ESMERALD OER Platform: Our main product is the ESMERALD Open Educational Resources (OER) Platform. Available in six languages - English, Polish, Spanish, Italian, Croatian and Greek – at the address:  https://esmerald.eu/index.php   
2. Comprehensive reports on the impact of COVID-19 on MSMEs: the consortium conducted in-depth analyses in: Poland, Spain, Italy, Croatia, Greece, Belgium and the European Union. These reports provide a detailed analysis of the impact of COVID-19 on the financial and competitive stability of SMEs. We have consolidated all of the country-specific findings into: a "Comparative Report on the Impact of COVID-19 on Micro and SMEs."
3. COVID Micro and SME Response Toolkit: We developed a comprehensive toolkit consisting of 24 training modules designed to equip SMEs with the skills and knowledge necessary to adapt in a business environment transformed by the pandemic. 
4. ESMERALD Manifesto and Guidelines: The final output is the ESMERALD Manifesto, a document designed to influence decision-making for enhancing the resilience of SMEs in the face of external shocks. It is accompanied by a set of practical Guidelines to promote the application of the project's findings.

2020-1-RO01-KA226-HE-095517.title: Boosting the scientific excellence and innovation capacity of 3D printing methods in pandemic period
2020-1-RO01-KA226-HE-095517.summary:
<< Background >>

The BRIGHT project was seen as an opportunity to further advance the BRIGHT partners expertise and experience in 3D printing, build upon successful collaborations with medical institutions in previous National and EU projects. The BRIGHT project offered a chance to address a pressing need in the field - the lack of scientific excellence and innovation in both research and teaching, particularly in the context of the pandemic. By developing a curriculum in collaboration with medical institutions, the BRIGHT consortium was able to create a range of valuable teaching resources including e-courses, e-toolkit manuals, e-virtual laboratory platform, webinars and e-case studies for producing medical parts to support hospitals in time of pandemic. These resources were designed to equip professors with the necessary tools and methods that are needed to provide relevant knowledge, skills, and competencies to their students, enabling them to develop, produce and test medical parts using 3D printing technologies. With the pandemic highlighting the importance of such skills, the BRIGHT project's resources were seen as a vital step in meeting the needs of medical institutions and supporting hospitals during this challenging time.

<< Objectives >>

The BRIGHT project aimed to boost scientific excellence and innovation in research and teaching of 3D printing for medical parts. By collaborating with medical institutions, the BRIGHT consortium has managed to create a range of teaching resources to provide professors with tools to impart relevant knowledge, skills and competencies to the students. The ultimate goal was to prepare specialists in the field who could support hospitals during the pandemic and beyond. The BRIGHT project's success in developing new medical parts and promoting interdisciplinary knowledge exchange is a testament to its impact on the field. The BRIGHT project has also managed to foster collaboration among experts from different sectors through the organized events such as summer schools and multiplier events. By providing practical skills and competencies, the BRIGHT project has played a crucial role in addressing the urgent need for innovative solutions in the healthcare sector, especially during the ongoing pandemic. Teaching resources were utilized with the assistance of SMEs to address case studies in time of pandemic.The BRIGHT project's resources will continue to support not only students and professors, but also hospitals in times of crisis.

<< Implementation >>

The BRIGHT project high-quality teaching materials (e-courses, e-toolkit manuals, webinars and e-case studies) have been implemented in the virtual laboratory platform that has been produced by the BRIGHT consortium with open access and can be accessed free of charge on the BRIGHT project website, all these resources being shared, distributed, used and further on implemented in teaching activities that were realized with the students in time of pandemic at the level of BRIGHT consortium, but also at the level of other Higher Educational institutions that have been involved and have attended the events organized in the BRIGHT project. The BRIGHT consortium have been involved in organizing successfully events (summer schools and multiplier events) through which the provided resources that have been developed by the BRIGHT consortium were disseminated, used and implemented also by the SMEs that have attended the organized events and have been actively involved further on in supporting the implementing activities of the BRIGHT project related to the realizing of case studies that were made using 3D printing technologies by professors and students of BRIGHT consortium to support end-users (hospitals and patients) in time of pandemic.

<< Results >>

The BRIGHT project has surpassed expectations in terms of reached outputs & results. Besides the teaching resources that were realized by the BRIGHT consortium consisting in 7 course modules, 6 toolkit laboratory modules, 5 webinars, 1 virtual laboratory platform, resources that are focused on various disciplines that are essential for 3D printing technologies that can be used for producing medical parts to support hospitals in the time of pandemic, a significant achievement of the BRIGHT project consisted in the publishing of 7 academic ISI articles with impact factor + other 8 articles indexed in Scientific Databases, confirming the quality of the provided teaching & scientific resources produced by the BRIGHT consortium in time of pandemic. Publishing of 1 handbook, 1 Project guidebook & 1 toolkit manual that are related to biomedical engineering domain, organizing of summer schools events gathering more than 300 participants from 20 EU countries & Multiplier Events with more than 100 participants in time of pandemic, as well as the attracting of important SMEs who were involved in developing & producing of case studies to support hospitals in time of pandemic are also important outcomes of the BRIGHT project to be mentioned.

2020-1-RO01-KA226-VET-095726.title: Digital Education Readiness in Maritime and Inland Navigation
2020-1-RO01-KA226-VET-095726.summary:
<< Background >>

Digital education readiness through innovation in times of a massive shift towards the online environment in global learning is a permanent concern of education and training institutions that need to cope with the present requirements of their respective industry and of the labour market.  
DERIN partnership saw the setbacks of a period characterized by restrictions, but also the opportunities when solutions are necessary, aiming at addressing the challenges of the didactical staff thus tackling the needs of their students/ trainees, who should easily adapt to the working environment. In order for teachers to be ready for the digital era, continuous professional development is the natural way for them to choose in order to maintain the European competitiveness and high-quality education.
The six partners in as many EU countries (RO, BG, HR, NL, LV and EE) consider that a more efficient uptake of digital technologies for teaching and learning in a consolidated manner would help for the educational process to be maintained even when the traditional face-to-face approach is not possible 100% of the time.
Additionally, the need for safety in the sector was addressed by the proposed solutions as the practical training is mandatory.

<< Objectives >>

The general objective of the project was to enhance institutional capacities and multi-level transnational cooperation to ensure access to digital tools and technologies for every student/trainee, teacher/trainer.
3 specific objectives detailed on the plans of the partnership in order to reach their goal through activities and outputs: increased educational attainment of maritime & inland navigation personnel based on innovative learning environment for education, training and competence-assessment using innovative multimedia tools and applications and set up of wide transnational cooperation at EU level, improved capacity of VET institutes to provide digital training by increased level of digital competences of VET teachers/trainers in waterborne transport.
All project partners enhanced cooperation and improved their capacities by implementing a strategic partnerships project involving an innovative learning environment. High quality and efficiency of education and training and an increased level of digital competences of VET teachers/trainers in waterborne transport sector was ensured by the newly developed VR materials, the handbook for trainers and the policy guidelines and reports/ studies delivered and rolled out activities.

<< Implementation >>

DERIN activities included elaboration of intellectual outputs/ IOs, dissemination and quality assurance.
For the 1st IO, criteria were set up and relevant learning modules were to be shifted to an innovative environment, then the appropriate technology to be used in maritime and inland E&T was chosen, Virtual Reality. VR learning materials for practical activity were elaborated after procuring and testing VR headsets, 360-degree video cameras and selecting the appropriate VR platform for scenario creation and publication. Short-term joint staff training events were also organized in 2 partner countries.
For the 2nd IO, to build capacities of trainers and trainees for innovative multimedia tools and applications, a Train the Trainers’ toolkit for capacity building was developed consisting of the Handbook for trainers and the VR teaching/training materials. A Report of tools for creating and establishing a new European network (DeriNetwork) and Policy Recommendation and Guidelines were elaborated.
Internal workshops, project meetings and multiplier events contributed to reaching the goal of improved digital training of waterborne transport personnel through an increased level of digital competences of the teachers/ trainers.

<< Results >>

DERIN project delivered both planned outputs and all their elements: 
Virtual Reality learning materials for practical activity were elaborated after all planned steps were taken, and two LTT/ Train the Trainer sessions were organized for all project partners. Consequently, a report was elaborated as a possible model for future such activities and to emphasize the interest shown by the participants and their more than positive feedback. 
A toolkit for trainers to build their capacity in using innovative multimedia tools was elaborated, consisting of Handbook for trainers, a 97-page document elaborated by the project partners, includes detailed annexes, specific information and lessons learnt, all meant at getting the teaching staff interested in new technologies and offering loads of hints on what to do to create their own VR materials, and VR teaching/training materials as 4 scenarios for practical training. The 360-degree filming was done in different environments: in classrooms, on a training base, in a confined space, in simulators and on board a real operational vessel. 
A report on a new European network https://www.linkedin.com/showcase/derin-network/ and policy recommendations are also available for any interested party.

2020-1-RS01-KA226-HE-094555.title: DIGITAL EDUCATION IN VETERINARY STUDIES
2020-1-RS01-KA226-HE-094555.summary:
<< Background >>

The education of veterinarians complies with quality standards outlined in Directives 2005/36/EC and 2013/55/EU, and defined through the European System of Evaluation of Veterinary Training (ESEVT), certified through accreditation carried out by the European Association of Establishments in Veterinary Education (EAEVE), following Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).
Standards revolve around the list of Day–one Competencies, the body of knowledge that a faculty must provide for its students by the graduation date. The balance between theoretical and practical teaching must be maintained.
After the outbreak of COVID, faculties quickly responded switching to online teaching, using different platforms. Switching to online theoretical teaching has been almost seamless. However, hands-on experience, i.e. laboratory, microscopy, autopsy, indoor and outdoor clinical teaching, etc. was a big challenge during occasional “lockout” periods since there weren’t any suitable means to compensate at least for some of the topics. Idea was to improve ongoing online teaching materials with tools that would alleviate the performing of theoretical and practical lessons which in veterinary medicine, include mainly laboratory and clinical work.

<< Objectives >>

1) To upgrade the system of delivery of digital teaching material for distance and classroom learning (website e-learning platform);
2) To motivate  teachers to upgrade their abilities to produce higher quality digital teaching material;
3) To produce a substantial volume of digital teaching material that would provide students to learn theoretical data and to overcome skills related to laboratory and clinical work such as videos, digital photographs and micrographs collections, animated and static digital schemes, graphs, tables, presentations, digitalized handouts, etc.

<< Implementation >>

Within the scope of building the educative (DEVet) e-platform, a group of teachers plotted the model of the platform's internal structure, then the platform was programmed, tested, evaluated by teachers and students, and finally, fully integrated into the informatic network at FVMUB.
During the preparation of intellectual outputs, educative digital video clips were recorded, photographies of medical instrument sets, procedures, anatomy, microscopic and x-ray preparations were made, a large number of digital drawings, schemes, posters, and animations were prepared, as well as presentations in line with the veterinary curriculum, sets of numeric data important for clinical training were compiled and organized, hand-outs for all subjects on the first two years of studies were created and one e-brochure about the safety of teachers and students involved in veterinary training was written.

<< Results >>

DEVet e-Learning Platform was projected, programmed, activated, and put to use by all project partners; the platform was uploaded with intellectual products, i.e. digital educative material, produced during the project period. Hi-performance digital graphic equipment and software were purchased and installed at FVMUB. Various categories of educative material were produced, according to veterinary Curricula and Syllabi of all participating institutions: 117 video clips, 43 collections (~600 pictures) of micrographs, 31 collections (~400 pictures) of digital photographs, 95 animations/presentations, ~350 digital drawings, schemes, posters, 35 collections of various datasets, 56 collections of the material for education/orientation, 1 book/brochure “Manual about the health and safety protection of staff and students exposed to biological and chemical agents during their work”.

2020-1-SE01-KA226-HE-092537.title: Digital education in nursing
2020-1-SE01-KA226-HE-092537.summary:
<< Background >>

The DEN project aims to address the urgent need to adapt nursing education to the digital era that has emerged as a consequence of the COVID-19 pandemic. The transition required from traditional "face-to-face" teaching to digital formats was necessary to meet the unexpected challenges posed by the pandemic. This rapid shift created challenges for both teachers and students at all levels of nursing education.

The specific needs that the project seeks to address include a pedagogical adaptation within nursing education to effectively integrate digital learning environments. The project's focus is on interacting with students in the digital realm, particularly with a focus on international student groups. This strategic approach is motivated by the goal of reducing the shortage of nurses in the EU by providing students with opportunities for cross-border education.

To achieve this, a quantitative and qualitative analysis of the need was required, involving both students and teachers. Their opinions have contributed to the selection of appropriate digital tools with tailored pedagogy that would contribute to high-quality learning.




​

<< Objectives >>

The objective of this project was to promote the integration of digital teaching in nursing education, while concurrently acknowledging the value of traditional teaching methods. Our aspiration was to afford students in the EU the freedom to select educational institutions without being constrained by geographical barriers. Through the establishment of digital international classrooms, our aim was to broaden students' opportunities for international experiences, consequently advancing the mobility of nurses within the EU. Simultaneously, our commitment was to uphold the high standards of quality in nursing education.

This initiative unfolded irrespective of varying levels of digital competence among teachers and students, resulting in a diverse range of approaches to problem-solving. Each participant in the project navigated this uncharted territory uniquely, contributing to a rich and multifaceted experience.

In order to capitalize on the wealth of diverse insights, a joint evaluation was conducted during a hybrid LTT2. This collaborative platform brought together students from all participating faculties, providing an invaluable opportunity to assess and enhance our strategies. Through this multi-faceted approach, our goal extended beyond the improvement of digital learning integration to the cultivation of a collaborative culture.

<< Implementation >>

We commenced the project by conducting a comprehensive analysis of digital education within all partner organizations. This analysis encompassed both quantitative data obtained through a SWOT analysis, examining educational plans and digital activities along with their effects during the pandemic, and qualitative methods, including focus group interviews with students and teachers to gather insights into their experiences with digital teaching amid the pandemic. The outcomes of this analysis served as the foundation for planning and presenting potential digital tools that, based on the teachers' assessments, held potential value for nursing education at all levels.

Following the preparation, presentation, and testing of various tools during LTT1 with the participation of all teachers, a subset of tools was chosen for further preparation and implementation testing with students from all partner organizations. Tools such as video films, escape rooms, and Padlet, previously utilized in traditional teaching, were selected for pedagogical adaptation to digital teaching. These adapted tools were then tested and evaluated by students from all partner organizations during LTT2.

Qualitative research, conducted through separate focus groups, unveiled a lower level of digital competence among the teachers. Consequently, one of the project's outcomes is the definition of digital competences for teachers, derived from the Delphy study.

<< Results >>

Results:

1.Theoretical analysis of pedagogical possibilities for digital tools applicable to nursing education.
2.Results from a qualitative analysis of evaluations and experiences of digital teaching during the pandemic, conducted through focus groups with teachers and students.
3.SWOT analysis of partner organizations' educational plans and their digital activities during the COVID-19 pandemic.
4.Results from the Delphi study on adapting digital competencies crucial for nursing teachers.
5.Results from the planning and pedagogical preparation for digital components in various modules (LTT1).
6.Implementation of selected digital tools, pedagogically tailored for nursing education, across different modules tested and evaluated by an international student group (LTT2).
7.A handbook compiling both theoretical and practical experiences gathered during the DEN project.

Other results:

1.Effective digital pedagogy can facilitate interaction with students and offer high educational quality.
2. An international environment can positively impact students' learning by enhancing insights into each other's contexts and facilitating encounters with patients from diverse cultures.

2020-1-SI01-KA226-SCH-093610.title: Developing Digital Competence of Roma Children
2020-1-SI01-KA226-SCH-093610.summary:
<< Background >>

The pandemic has brought new challenges for all pedagogical profiles, in addition to adapting to work in an online environment, which need to be addressed as soon as possible. This is especially true for vulnerable target groups, who in these circumstances have even greater problems that may eventually become intractable. We have recognised that education must be accessible to all, regardless of socio-economic status or barriers. Roma primary school pupils' underdevelopment of basic digital literacy competences during distance education has in the vast majority of cases left them inactive, which has also been reflected in their academic performance. 

The project and the resulting materials and tools will have a significant impact on the ability of primary schools to facilitate and successfully provide inclusive digital education for Roma pupils and their equal participation in distance education through Roma assistants.

<< Objectives >>

The intellectual outputs will contribute to increasing the capacity to deliver online and blended teaching and learning at a distance, with a focus on developing the digital pedagogical competences of Roma assistants, enabling them to deliver high quality inclusive education. By developing innovative freely accessible educational resources in a digital environment, we will contribute to the transfer of their knowledge to one of the most vulnerable target groups in the education system, Roma learners. Roma assistants will be able to transfer the acquired digital knowledge and skills to Roma pupils who have poorly developed digital competences, using tools and an online platform, so that they can participate as actively, effectively and sovereignly as possible in distance education, which, according to the findings of the first wave of the COVID-19 epidemic, they did not have the opportunity to do.

<< Implementation >>

- Designing the survey questionnaire, its translation and conducting a survey among Roma assistants, teachers and head teachers of primary schools - creating a final report on the level of digital skills of Roma pupils.
- Development of a training programme for Roma assistants, with translations into national languages and English.
- Creation of curricula and various tools for learning and developing digital skills.
- Development of an online platform.
- Short-term pilot training of trainers in three countries.
- Conducting a parallel survey among Roma pupils.
- Multiplier events in all countries.
- Extensive dissemination activities.

<< Results >>

IO 1: Study of the analysis of the current situation and needs on the development of digital competencies among Roma pupils (in three countries).
IO 2: A training programme for Roma assistants.
IO 3: Curricula for the development of digital competencies in Roma pupils (class and subject level).
IO 4: Online platform (multilingual with access to all materials and resources).

Other results:
Creation of additional research and creation of a database with data on the digital skills of Roma pupils.
Roma assistants, other educational staff, and individuals trained and able to transfer the knowledge acquired to Roma pupils.

The flexibility of the produced materials and materials, which can be used for the digital skills development needs of other target groups with little or no input.

New knowledge and experience gained in the field of working with vulnerable target groups, expanding the network of partners and creating and building on existing project assets.

2020-1-TR01-KA226-VET-097591.title: Digitalizing on Railway Training
2020-1-TR01-KA226-VET-097591.summary:
<< Background >>

The global Covid-19 crisis offers the chance to reshape vocational education and training. The exposure of vocational education and training providers (schools & training centers) to long-term closures, which emerged in the first quarter of 2020 with the corona virus epidemic revealed the necessity of transforming physical classrooms and work-based learning spaces into digital learning environments. In an environment of uncertainty illustrated by unpredictable labor market forecasts and other Covid-19 economic and social indicators students had to continue to motivate their learning journey. VET providers and practitioners needed to be supported with all the tools and resources necessary to meet these challenges. Due to these needs, our Institution applied to the call for covid 19 in mid-2020. The needs we addressed were to transform skill-based vocational education programs into blended education programs and to prepare digital materials about these programs.

<< Objectives >>

With our project, we wanted to prepare a guide that will guide educators, learners or policy makers in the field of vocational and technical education with a methodology created in line with a hybrid education system that includes a mixture of physical and virtual learning. We wanted to assist VET providers in addressing the 'green and digital skills' demands, which are among the EU's post-2020 priority targets in their curricula and training delivery methodologies. We wanted to guide the training of students with high employability skills and sufficient skill intelligence required by the railway labor market. In addition, we aimed to increase the digital and scientific competencies of teachers and educators by re-emphasizing effective professional development.

<< Implementation >>

In order to obtain the outputs of our four project partners from three different program countries; Activities such as two workshops, four transnational partnership meetings, two pilot distance trainings, one conference, three capacity building trainings were held. Digital materials (especially VR applications) that were produced were presented during Eurasia Rail 2021 – International Railway, Light Rail Systems and Logistics Fair. Vocational high schools with rail systems departments were visited in Ankara, Eskişehir, Kocaeli and Kırıkkale and trainings were given on project introduction and project outputs.

<< Results >>

Within the scope of our project;
-Special blended/hybrid training programs were prepared for the professions of "Train Driver, Shunter, Traffic Controller, Railway Track Construction- Maintenance Repairer, Rail Systems Signalization Maintenance Repairer".
-15 digital learning contents specific to these training programs were developed.
-In addition, a guide to digital learning practices in vocational and technical education was prepared.

2020-1-UK01-KA226-SCH-094586.summary:

The project has been coordinated by the UK. The project partners are Macedonia, Greece, Croatia and Turkey. The project covers students aged 9-19 years. The project's primary target was to blend learning between class and virtual based lessons.

<< Objectives >>

- more intensive use of technology in educational environments 
- training from the abstract to a concrete method 
- fusion of real life and school education 
- making school more interesting and more fun 
- ensuring intercultural integration 
- ensuring the linguistic development of the participants

2020-1-UK01-KA226-VET-094508.title: Learning foreign languages online
2020-1-UK01-KA226-VET-094508.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was based on the background research conducted during the Covid-19 pandemic, which revealed a significant decline in employment opportunities across Europe. This situation presented an advantageous chance for individuals who were currently unemployed to enhance their skills in order to secure better jobs. Job search platforms also encouraged job seekers to utilise this time to improve their foreign language proficiency as a means to enhance their employment prospects. We realised that individuals looking to learn foreign language online needed thoroughly scrutinised tools that are not only free-of-charge but also engaging and easy-to-use. Despite the availability of a plethora of open-access resources, we are also aware of the fact that these are not prepared by experts or may even contain erroneous information, and learners’ ignorance about this misinformation cannot be ruled out. Furthermore, learners also lack the knowledge on how to maximise the learning outcomes and effectively utilise grammatical exercises to improve their language learning skills. Due to dearth of comprehensive and well-designed resources, the project output would be ideal in supporting the learners on their journey to learning a foreign language.

<< Objectives >>

The prime objectives of this project were to:
1.	provide a platform for foreign language learners who are engaged in learning online. A selection of high-quality resources/ OERs which were freely available online were compiled into a website. The resources for the website were selected by experts on the basis of set quality standards.  
2.	create an E-course to enable the foreign language learners to know how to use the resources available on the website. 
Both the outputs were created keeping a special focus on the learners from underprivileged backgrounds. The above-mentioned objectives were achieved through following Intellectual outputs:
1.	Compilation of OERs for learning foreign languages online for self-directed learner
2.	An E-course addressed to self-directed learners on how to use OERs to learn foreign languages

<< Implementation >>

The following set of activities were implemented during the course of the project:
2 Intellectual outputs
Transnational Project Meetings- 5 TPMs were foreseen, although due to travel restrictions caused by the pandemic, the Kick-off meeting was hosted online by Eurospeak due to which the final face-to-face meeting was hosted in UK in May 2023. Besides, 6 online coordination meetings were carried out to keep a close watch on the project.
Management activities –  Eurospeak, oversaw the management activities of the project including monitoring spending, coordinating communication, monitoring deadlines, and submitting reports to the NA. 
Dissemination activities – the partners, guided by Innovation Hive, carried out activities to disseminate information about the project. More information about dissemination can be found in the follow-up section of this report.
Evaluation activities - the project was evaluated against a set of indicators, both internally among the partners and externally with members of the target group. The project outcomes and processes were evaluated using questionnaires developed by the evaluation lead, Maksima.
Multiplier events - Events with a minimum of 30 participants were held in each partner country.

<< Results >>

The project produced the following Intellectual outputs:
IO1: Compilation of OERs for learning foreign languages online for self-directed learners, organised by language, CEFR level, and area of language learning (grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation, reading, writing, listening, and speaking) on the project website.
IO2: An e-course on how to learn foreign languages online for self-directed learners.
Management materials: management plan, agendas and minutes of meetings, Dissemination materials: dissemination plan,  newsletters, press release, leaflet, posters, branded materials, logo, articles, press releases, flyer, 3 social media accounts, 3 dissemination reports, impact questionnaire and website.
Evaluation materials: Questionnaires for partners, stakeholders, target groups, and experts, quality reports from each IO, both external and internal, plus 4 reports on the overall project processes 
Sustainability plan

2018-1-BE02-KA229-046927.title: Transforming FabLabs into STEAMLabs
2018-1-BE02-KA229-046927.summary:
PISA - an international indicator study on the skills and attitudes of 15-year-olds in mathematics, science and reading - shows that young people from many OECD countries score low to average with regard to these items.
While the number of top performers remains relatively high (but drops), the number of pupils who do not reach the basic level is rising. That basic level is the minimum level to be able to stand on your own feet in society. The difference between the weakest and strongest pupils is also large. Boys get a better score for science than girls. They also indicate much more often that they have fun and interest in science. For all pupils, those who have pleasure or interest also score significantly higher in the science test. There is a need for quality development in STEAM education in the EU.

In the past, we used a FabLab. A FabLab was a workshop where students (and in many cases a wider public) could use machines to realise a physical or digital (intermediate) product together. Although education is provided in a FabLab, this education is often limited to the use of the machines on offer. In the context of nursery and primary education, this was of course insufficient. After all, a context must be created around the machines that are used. Within the project 'Transforming FabLabs into STEAMLabs' we created additional learning activities, which are focused on designing, studying the machines themselves and how the machines can be combined. By framing these STEAM related learning activities in FabLabs, we create what we call STEAMLabs. In other words, a STEAMLab can be defined as a FabLab where students doesn't only focus on the realisation of an (intermediate) product, but where attention is paid to the entire process of getting from an idea to the realisation of an end product.

Today, the various participating schools are not only focusing on the use of a limited number of machines or on a limited number of techniques, but on the use of all machines discussed during the project. This makes it possible for them to offer a package that covers all aspects of STEAM (science, technology
engineering, art and mathematics). Within this package, attention was paid to didactic translation by using STEAM-oriented technologies. Some examples are 'Solving real problems', simulating an earthquake with Lego WeDo and using Ozobots within an architectural framework. 

All this was achieved by giving participating schools the opportunity to share their knowledge about FABLabs and
experiences between pupils, parents and teachers. The project 'Transforming FabLabs into STEAMLabs' turned FABLabs into fully-fledged STEAMLabs with dissemination to European schools.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2018-1-BG01-KA229-047823.title: The splendour of nature
2018-1-BG01-KA229-047823.summary:
According to the World Health Organisation, environmental factors could be responsible for up to 20 % of all deaths in Europe. Europe already has high standards for air quality, but in many cities, pollution remains above acceptable levels.  Pollution is a huge threat against which there are no forms of successful adaptation. The conservation of the environment and its diversity is a moral duty of man, conscious of being part of a broader ecological relationship in which he is inserted in the same way as the other endangered species and , for this ,needs protection. Another very important problem linked to unemployment, social exclusion, and poverty is early school leaving. There are many reasons why some young people give up education and training prematurely:personal or family problems, learning difficulties, or a fragile socio-economic situation. Some of the most common reasons that are the same for all school partners are addressed to a range of triggers and combines education and social policy, youth work and aspects such as demotivation and dissatisfaction . Based on these facts and having in mind the present situation concerning  the environment  in our regions and the number of drop-outs at our schools we decided to prepare this project. The countries involved in this project proposal are: Bulgaria (coordinator), Italy, Croatia, FYROM,France and UK.The age range of students is 14-19.The aim of our project:”The splendor of nature” is to make more investments in knowledge and encourage innovation and the development of more sustainable solutions to solve different environmental  problems. We would like to reduce threats from pollution common for the European region and to improve the standards of living adequate for the health and well-being of the population by providing opportunities for environmental democracy via the use of ICT and environmental protection activities, and raising awareness about environmental problems in order to result in positive development in our regions. The project activities focus on environmental education on the one hand and on the development and promotion of national reserves and natural heritage at the other hand. We would like to foster groups being at risk and motivate them to stay at school and show them that through studying they will be prepared to build their own future. Our plan is to offer students research project within areas that examine man's impact on the environment. In order to reach the objectives of the project we have planned 2 Joint Staff Training events and 4 Short-term exchanbges of groups of pupils.
 General objectives:
 -To create an environmental awareness in all students 
 -To raise the awareness about environmental problems 
 -To analyze and classify components of natural ecosystems in parks and natural reserves
 -To  raise the awareness on the high natural values of the areas and the chances involved  on local, national and international level.
 -To  reduce drop-outs by increasing the motivation  and satisfaction of students 
 Specific objectives:
 -To educate people to respect environment so that people can avoid speculation, pollution, desertification and deforestation. 
 -To improve and to develop the use of the English language and ICT  
 -To develop research skills for observing, recording, comparing, classifying ecosystems of our region
 -To increase public awareness about the factors threatening the life in nature
 -To promote  transnational cooperation and exchange.
 The tangible results expected by the project are: botanical manual; brochure of theoretical and experimental analysis of the; a virtual phrase book, an environmental protection e-magazine; a catalog with National parks of our countries; a booklet with extinct plants of each partner region; a CD with presentations;an interactive map; project  website;Facebook  page;dissemination materials;eTwinning(Twin Space) platform; PowerPoint presentations.The intangible results expected by the project are:
 Students will acquire new knowledge and an increasing interest in knowing more about plants and animals of different ecosystems, ecological education and applying all this knowledge in the field.The students will acquire the tools to benefit of the possible mobility opportunities for studying and working inside the European  space and surfing through the eTwinning and Facebook.Teachers will gain by strengthening communication between the students and themselves, exchanging ideas in the field of environmental protection  and the development of inter cultural dialogue with colleagues and students from partnering schools All schools will benefit by creating better relations between teachers, students and the community, making school more dynamic and stimulating for all.The importance of natural parks will be raised to the public.All schools will benefit by creating better relations between teachers,students and the community, making school more dynamic and stimulating for all.

2018-1-BG01-KA229-047898.title: Better Education for Students and Teachers
2018-1-BG01-KA229-047898.summary:
Nowadays science is not only facts, written in school books and learning by heart. Science is full of innovations and technologies. At the same time, there are more and more students showing poor results in education and not fulfilling their obligations regularly. Students are increasingly demotivated with curricular content and show less and less interest in studying. By using new tools, applications and digital materials in class the students are motivated to study in a different and interesting way. Furthermore, the curricular content is much easier to visualize and bring closer to the students. This is an important move towards interactive studying, an innovative one in which the students have more practical assignments. Unfortunately, not all teachers use the Internet and web applications in their classrooms. A big amount of teachers are using traditional teaching methods.
 Main Goals:
  Reinforce digital bridges of communication (in a learning and teaching concept);
  Perform good practices concerning strategies and tools that can be of use and help, both for students and teachers;
  Exchange of experiences and good practices and creating school dynamics that facilitate the overcoming of some difficulties;
  Obtain better performance in the European classrooms in the 21st century.

Schools from five countries have been taking part in the project: Bulgaria, Turkey, Romania, Croatia, and Poland. In the project were involved: more than 500 students, aged 11-16 years old; more than 100 teachers; 100 parents, over 20 000 of informed citizens of the municipality of school partners - through different mass media- TV, newspapers, Social Medias, eTwining, School Education Gateway and the Erasmus+ Project Results Platform. 
 
 Description of activities:
    Participants from the school partners filled two surveys(at the beginning and at the final stage) about their preferences on Internet websites, social media, and online games. 
    One short- term joint staff training event took place in Poland (October 2018) and a two-days visit in Croatia(December 2019). During the meetings, teachers exchanged good practices and techniques. It was shown that digital technologies are everywhere and they are impacting what, where, how and why students learn. Useful educational resources for different school subjects were summarized. 
     Three short- term exchanges of groups of pupils were conducted.  (Romania- March 2019; Bulgaria- May 2019; Turkey- October 2019) Students attended workshops and two training for practical digital skills for interactive open education. 
     Three online “BEST Competition” events took place for the students of the school partners. The topics of the competitions are: Maths can be fun(December 2018), Geography Games (February 2019) and English for Everyone(November 2019). 
      Two online pieces of training were organized for all teachers from the school partners: 1. How to use more effectively eTwinning and School Education Gateway (November 2018) 2. Digital skills for interactive open education (January 2019).  
     Parents, students, and teachers together discussed the overall impact of the project through creating an online document for collaboration. 
     An Educational Brochure was created. In the brochure are included educational websites and digital tools. 
     The eTwinning page of the project was updated regularly and students and teachers created different activities there. 
   This project summarizes the experience of five countries with digital educational resources and gives the opportunity of young students to meet peers with different cultural backgrounds. Students need more technologies in class, experiments, and demonstrations in order to be more competitive in their future realization. The project has developed a willingness for education and involving students, teachers, school staff and families. One of the most impressive benefits was the involvement of a big number of students in online games. With this method, more students were able to realize and feel the impact of the Erasmus+ program. 
 The results of the project have been disseminated via different channels –newsletters, presentations/publications to conferences/ workshops, online publications and presentations through social and contemporary media, and the Erasmus+ dissemination platform

2018-1-CY01-KA229-046851.title: Tracing our Cultural Heritage
2018-1-CY01-KA229-046851.summary:
“Tracing our Cultural Heritage” is a project devoted to European Cultural Heritage. Through our project, we  knew, appreciated and maintained for the next generation, our cultural heritage and at the same time, we met the heritage of our partners. And that is the importance of our project: We  focused to find out our similarities  that will help to reinforce a sense of belonging to a common European space.
 The main objectives of our project for the pupils were: become aware, respect and appreciate their own cultural (regional and national) heritage, discover the cultural heritage of the partner countries and find similarities with their own, recognize and show respect for different cultural practices and traditions, develop of critical thinking and use of technology and internet. 
 Teachers and staff of the school discovered and understood different education systems in Europe, different educational approaches, teaching methods and practices. Also they   improved language acquisition by communicating with other teachers, improved their computer skills and 
developed cooperation in teamwork.
 Our project had a  duration of 28 months (we got an extension of 4 months due to Cocid-19) and consisted of organizing numerous activities among partner children in the following domains, with emphasis on their traditional aspect: history of the schools (areas, countries), literature, customs, music, dance, art, song and gastronomy. To achieve this we   proceeded in 5 ways: internal reflection, production, sharing, common use of productions, then evaluation. Main tool of the project was a website dedicated to the project, on which we  published photos, videos, our creations and comments of teachers and pupils.
 Six schools from six different countries (Cyprus, France, Spain, Italy, Romania and Croatia)   participated to the project and the Cypriot school was the coordinator.  In the project were involved pupils, teachers, school staff, parents and local authorities. Each school   organized both short term exchanges of groups of pupils and joint staff training activities for teachers at the same time.  The Cypriot school organized a diversified activities, because of the pandemic. A total of 89 pupils (1 pupil with special needs) and 69 teachers   participated in L.T.T.A.
 The main results of the project were: presentation of the history of the region/town of each school (Power Point), posters devoted to an important historical monument on each country (in its area), presentation of  traditional art/craft on each school (Power Point in some countries or posters or books),CD with traditional music/song of each school, concert with traditional instruments, Cookbook with  recipes of traditional food of all partner countries, illustrated book (traditional folktale from each country) and finally the Creation of the Museum of European Cultural Heritage (exhibition) with all the similarities among the partners.
 By the end of the project, the experiences pupils and teachers  acquired,   increased the feeling of the European citizen and in addition, the project will lay the foundations for the recognition, assessment and protection of the cultural heritage as a long-term priority of the schools. 
 All the concrete results of the project will be in the libraries of each school and will be used in future activities and lessons. Also they will be sent to the local communities and to nearby schools.
