2019-1-DE03-KA229-059523.title: Education Systems in Europe - from Nursery School to Professional Career
2019-1-DE03-KA229-059523.summary:
Education systems in Europe - from kindergarten to professional life
 In this project, our students got to know the education systems in Europe and compared them.
 We live together in one Europe and have learned from each other to work together and the students  got to know each other well and became friends. There was a need to get to know the educational systems of other countries, because the prerequisites for (professional) work in Europe were set here.
 Six European schools from Bulgaria, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Austria and Turkey took part in this project together with about 280 students. The participating students were between 12 and 17 years old.
 Pupils from all types of middle school took part from our school.
 Since the project language was German, the German and Austrian students had a great advantage from which the students from other countries could also benefit.
 
 Activities were the creation of a project homepage and an etwinning page, the creation of presentations of our education systems from kindergarten to professional life, we created workpieces together, got to know different school types within our education systems, visited companies and universities.
 For our six learning, teaching and training activities, each student wrote a profile introducing themselves.
 
 All schools worked on all topics, starting with presentations on the work in kindergarten, followed by primary school, secondary level I and II,
 vocational schools with training, universities and apprenticeships. Unfortunately, Corona delayed the project work, so we had to catch up on a lot in the last few months.
 
Results were:
  
 - Pupils and teachers learned about good practice in our education systems
 - get to know the education system in the partner countries
 - Expansion of digital competence
 - Extension of social skills
 - Improving foreign languages, interest in Europe and other cultures
 - Create new contacts in Europe
 
 We want to prepare our students for life and work in a Europe that is aware of its global responsibility. This European dimension shaped our project and our schools.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2019-1-DE03-KA229-059581.title: Our Common Fundament: European Values
2019-1-DE03-KA229-059581.summary:
The project titled “Our Common Fundament: European Values“ has enabled participating staff and students to gain an insight into common values shared by our countries, the evolution of these values, and the meaning ot these values for the individual citizen, society and the European community as a whole. In this we intended to counteract rising protectionist and nationalist tendencies in member countries. Participants realized that the implementation of these values has not been completed but requires a continuous struggle to which they can, and must, contribute their share – considering at the same time the need for compromise in the face of diverging interests and aims. Dealing  with the immaterial and material cultural heritage showing both common values and and national idiosyncrasies served as a means to point out to the students the everyday reality behind the more abstract values. The aim in this lied in the creation of a common identity and the experience of the diversity of cultures in the participating countries as a form of personal enrichment.
 Becoming acquainted with a variety of national and regional characteristics such as traditions and aspects of cultural heritage in the partner countries  the foreign language and cultural competence of the participants had be enhanced.  Digital media and programmes such as Kahoot, Google maps or eTwinning were used to elaborate and present project results. An overall target was seen in enhanced competence concerning action and interaction of students, such as  foreign language skills, the use of digital media, the sharing and understanding of different perspectives and attitudes, the dealing with conflict situations, the use of compromise , and the art of debating. The use of simulation games played a central role in this.
 Partner institutions were high schools/grammar schools in the following 4 countries: Spain, Denmark, Croatia and Germany – all of which had gained experience in other international projects or exchange programmes, but now for the first time cooperated in a Strategic School Partnership. All project meetings followed a similar structure: Each meeting focused on specific content, i.e. each host country was allotted a specific set of values and a historic epoch. In addition to the students travelling to meetings at least one further class of each partner school was involved. The meetings were made up of 30 students ( 15 foreign guest and 15 host students) and ca 10 staff ( 6 guests and a minimum of 4 from the host school).
 This means a total of ca 300 students were involved, with an average of 25 per teacher; from this total the students who traveled to the meetings were chosen according to aptitude .
 The wide dissemination of materials and results was enabled through eTwinning to further use by the project classes in the times between meetings. Interactive apps were further the direct acquisition of project meeting results. A long-term cooperation with all partner schools is intended, with measure including eTwinning projects, bilateral exchanges, participation in an international UN simulation, and in a further Erasmus project. about the topic "Water - bridge, obstacle, resource, habitat and subject of arts and literature".
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2019-1-DE03-KA229-059588.title: Living in the age of migration - knocking on doors, knocking down prejudices
2019-1-DE03-KA229-059588.summary:
The context in which this project was developed is the present situation European countries find themselves in because of the mass migration of the last few years and the rise of hostile populist voices. The objectives of this project are therefore the reduction of the danger of possible present and future conflicts by furthering the communication between migrants and natives, by increasing tolerance and mutual understanding when the people get to know the different values and cultures better, by trying to increase the migrant families’ trust in local people and local institutions, and by helping migrant families and schoolchildren to cope with work at school.
In autumn 2019 we had a promising start with our project on migration following the schedule outlined in the application. After comprehensive consultations  as to content and organisation between the four partners we started with the practical implementation of the project with a staff training in Lüdenscheid/Germany. Colleagues from Croatia, Italy, Portugal and Germany were introduced into the practical opportunities of etwinning and twin space by an expert. A teacher from the German school presented the bookcreator app (by Google Chrome) and its many possibilities  for students and teachers to present their work in the colourful and attractive ebook format. Practical exercises followed. The first personal encounter of the participating teachers facilitated the collaboration in the years to come.
The first project meeting  with students took place like schedules in February 2020. Students and teacher met at der Escola Secundária Raunha D. Amélia in Lisbon/Portugal. After a round of introductions by the schools/cities, various aspects of the topic of migration were examined. The focus of this mobility was on a historical consideration of immigration and emigration in the four participating countries. Very diverse and carefully researched materials were presented and discussed. Official stakeholders gave talks and were interviewed, e.g. a representative of the Portuguese Amnesty International Organization.  The next scheduled meeting in Molfetta/Italy was planned in detail.
From March 2020 onwards everything changed due to the Corona Pandemic. The lockdown and ban on school trips went on for many, many months and it was initially unclear how and whether our project could be continued at all.
A number of online meetings of teachers followed and a total of 4 larger meetings with teachers and students involved. These meetings were carefully planned (with agenda and minutes kept) and sometimes had up to 60 participants. The participants created various films and presentations on the agreed aspects of migration: 1. Current situation of migrants/refugees in the participating countries 2. Opportunities for help. The results of these sessions can be found in our mutual ebook.
Because of the uncertainty as to when physical meetings would be possible again, the participating schools decided to extend the project twice by half a year, so that the total duration was  extended to 36 months (until August 31, 2022).
After the meetings in Molfetta/Italy, Dubrovnik/Croatia and Lüdenscheid/Germany had to be cancelled due to the pandemic, we decided in November 2021 - a point in time when school trips seemed to be plannable again - to stage a last meeting in Strasbourg - a location of the EU. The meeting was approved by the national agencies.
In March 2022, 60 students and teachers met in Strasbourg. During visits to the European Parliament, the Council of Europe and the European Court of Human Rights, aspects of the topic of migration were also addressed. A full day of seminars in the European Youth Centre in Strasbourg completed the visit, where further presentations were shown and the final production of our e-book was discussed.
In the course of the 3 years, many aspects of the topic of migration were illuminated and discussed in a variety of ways. The students got to know migration in its international dimensions and facets and were able to establish various contacts with students from the partner countries. The reports on the corona situation in the participating countries and schools and the associated sensitivities of the students were also discussed several times in the online meetings and gave all those involved profound insights.
topics: Reception and integration of refugees and migrants
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2019-1-DE03-KA229-059624.title: "Let me tell you a story"
2019-1-DE03-KA229-059624.summary:
Our project started in November 2019 with partners from Turkey, Great Britain, Croatia, Slovenia, Portugal and Germany. We´ve got in contact by mail and by whats app. And we started with our first travel to Turkey.
After the first LTT to Turkey we planed `monthly tasks´ to which all schools should devote themselves and to be shown on the website. This is being used as dissemination tool. (https://erasmustellastory.wixsite.com/site). And we continued partner meetings (online) very regular.
Until the epidemic Covid-19, everything was going on as it was planned in the project. With this epidemic, we couldn’t make LTT2 to Germany mobility – even everything was planed and also the local activities starting from March 2020, which were to be done at school with students. Schools in Germany and in other countries were closed for several times. Or they had only part time lessons on the main subjects. In the other countries it was nearly the same or schools were closed even longer. We (German coordinator) requested extension for our project until April 30th, 2022 and it was given to us. 
At last we had several online meetings during epidemic time with partners and agreed to wait and see the situation of the epidemic and then probably to continue the mobilities by the end of January 2021. The mobilities and local activities will be re-scheduled after the situation for epidemic is better. But epedemich situation went on and so our next LTT could start in October 2021 to Croatia. Children were not allowed to travel so it was a short-term training course for employees. So it was on our LTT to Germany in December 2021. Followed by the LTT to Slovenia in March 2022 – with children. But recognising time will be to short we ask again for a extension till 30th of October 2022 and it was given to us. Our last LTT tot he UK could take place with children in May 2022. We have been very glad that we could do all the LTTs!

Activities at school during the project:
We announced and presented the project details to students, teachers and parents. Under the theme `fairy tales from past to now´ we evaluated and discussed fairy tales from the past to now. How they have changed during the passing time?  A project notice board has been installed. Every school prepared a notice board where the activities and their results are published for school comunitiy. We drew fairy tale pictures in the classes. We examined `Maths stories´ – We researched together with several classes and found a lot of mathematic pieces in fairy tales – for exmaple ìn ` the wolf and the seven goats´. We developed a project logo – Children at all school created several logos and voted for one for their school. Then we had a voting of all schools and found a project logo out oft he six proposals oft he schools. A value dice was created. We made dice about the values. Values were tolerance/emphaty, respect, justice, responsibility, love, solidarity. Values were written on the die's sides and when the pupil threw it, they made up a story about that value. Using their own creativity. Project bulletins for publishing project and results were created. Reading with grannies and grandads and talk about elder fairy tales was part of the project just like a fairy tale presentation – After reading fairy tales or books children presentate about their stories. They do this in different ways. Science fairy tales – Could you imagine? – How would a fairy tale be in space? – Let your fanasty flow…We researched about national fairy tales writers – Get to know famous national fairy tale writers. Got in contact with writers of fairy tales or books for children. Asking them how they get their ideas and a lot more. Telling stories in different ways for example building puppets and tell by a shadow play. A trip to the library showed us – So many books….some of them are wellknown, a lot are here to get to know. Finding fairy tales we never heard before. Reading books with family and explore:  Does your family read? What do you read at home? What fairy tales are read? Who reads to whom? Being an author - students writing  startings and endings of stories – Let your fantasie flow. Not only when reading, but also when writing beginnings or endings, the children can explore fairy tales and let their imagination run wild. Creating a project newspaper, the children reflect on what they have learned and experienced and communicate it to the school community.
All partners tried to do their very best do work on the activities as far as possible during pandemic situation.

Aktivities during LTTs
During the trips to the partner countries, many different activities were carried out. There is not enough space to describe them in detail. In addition to getting to know the respective culture, a variety of workshops were offered in all countries, which gave us deep insights into various methods in dealing with fairy tales. For all involved, it was a great gain in knowledge and implementation in practice.

2019-1-DE03-KA229-059675.title: Think Global Support Local
2019-1-DE03-KA229-059675.summary:
With the essential project idea of "Think Global Support Local," we raised participants' awareness of sustainable, healthy nutrition throughout the project. The participants were encouraged at various levels to rethink their consumption behavior by learning about and experiencing the added value of regional products. The project background or context can be derived from the following guiding questions:
 
- Does it always have to be a lot or is high quality perhaps better? (Quality vs. Quantity)
 
- Do we really need superfoods from faraway countries for a healthy diet, or do regional products perhaps even offer the same nutrients?
 
- How can traditional, regional recipes help us with sustainable nutrition?
 
- How can long transport routes be avoided?
 
- How can food for our own consumption be grown on a very small area?
 
- How can food be preserved?
 
- What does traditional and industrial livestock farming look like?
 
- What are the characteristics of a healthy diet?
 
- Which regional sports and exercise activities can support a healthy lifestyle?
 
 
 
Many students and teachers from the five partnering schools were directly involved in the project by participating in the transnational learning activities. Other students as well as teachers were involved in the project by working out the project topics in class. Other participants included host families, local politicians, businesses and the press, who were involved in individual project activities. The participants were able to further develop their basic skills and key competencies (competencies in the areas of language, social learning, intercultural learning, team building, project management, methodology, didactics and documentation). 
 
As a joint project result, teaching units on the project activities were developed, which, in addition to documenting the course of the project, also contain didactic instructions on how to carry out individual activities. They will be published via the TwinSpace as well as via the results platform. The teaching materials can be disseminated and used in any school, also beyond the partner schools.
 
 
 
The originally planned conferences had to be adapted to the pandemic situation. Only the 1st conference could be held as planned. Due to the Covid-related project interruption of 24 months, during which no mobilities could take place, the project coordinators were in regular contact via video conference. With the resumption of mobilities, conferences were organized, conducted and evaluated under high pressure. Thus, the remaining five conferences could be carried out within six months.
 
 
 
C1; Conference Germany (November 2019) - Global Footprint.
 
HA (Homework): Comparison of global and regional food from and in partner countries.
 
KT (conference theme): Global footprint / awareness of consequences of own consumption behavior. Visit to a sugar factory / production of regional pancakes: pickert.
 
Urban Gardening: preparation of a planting action in the school garden "project fruits"/ useful areas in the public space / opinion poll "consumer behavior".
 
Objective: to raise awareness of global consequences of one's own actions / to point out new ways.
 
 
 
C2: Conference Italy (March 2020) - force majeur - cancelled due to Covid
 
 
 
C3: Conference Italy (March 2022) Food analysis/Green Cities
 
HA: Analysis of survey "consumer behavior“
 
KT: Bicycle tour to a National Park and visit to the hanging gardens in Milan for water sampling in public waters / laboratory experiments on food quality.
 
Goal: raise awareness of food ingredients / regional specifics Green Cities versus National Parks.
 
 
 
C4: Conference Spain (April 2022) - Healthy habits in European cities
 
HA: Usable green spaces for sports in urban areas
 
KT: Herb planting action, visit of regional food producers, climbing course
 
Goal: Raise awareness of urban exercise culture/offers
 
 
 
C5: Conference France (April 2022) - Nutrition, Health and Sports
 
HA: homemade versus convenience food
 
KT: Nutrition and sports games, Nordic walking, visit to regional food producers, nutrition tips, sports activities.
 
Goal: raise awareness of opportunities for healthy regional food and exercise.
 
 
 
C6: Conference Croatia (May 2022) - Zero waste everyday / flowers in modern gastronomy.
 
HA: Zero waste concept - What is zero waste?
 
KT: Zero waste everyday / useful plants, "Zero waste plant based kitchen" cooking class, hiking in the forest - plant science.
 
Goal: Rediscover regional useful plants and recipes.
 
 
 
 C7: Final conference Belgium (August 2022)
 
 Documenting results, processing results, evaluations, final report / agreements on further cooperation.
 
 Goal: Project conclusion, publication / dissemination of project results.
topics: Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas
Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

2019-1-DE03-KA229-059837.title: The Challenge of Being Happy in a European Society
2019-1-DE03-KA229-059837.summary:
Today, democratic European societies face various challenges. Therefore the aim of our project is to raise our students' awareness of the general foundations of a future democratic European society offering quality of life and enabling everyone to grow happiness. 
 There are four European schools that cooperate: a Croatian elementary school, a German and Swedish secondary school as well as a Portuguese comprehensive school. The project addresses students aged 14-16. 
 
 In a first step, our students will define the term happiness and assess individual sources of the latter. 
 Then, our students will create and carry out surveys to involve different generations and different social groups into our findings about individual sources of happiness and quality of life. 
 They will then analyse and abstrahize the findings in order to single out factors that allow us to universally grow happiness and improve quality of life, especially focusing on aspects that can be linked to democracy and thus to a future democratic, European society. 
 In a last step, they will outline practical guidelines and messages that help themselves and others to grow happiness in such a society. 
 
 Each mobility will involve individual actions creating happiness making it easier for the students to experience being an active part of society that is able to change something. We will call these actions "Actions for Happiness". 
 To be more concrete, here's a possible idea for an "Action for Happiness"  during the first mobility. Before the first mobility, our students will assess individual sources of happiness in their national teams. They will compare their findings on Twin Space and agree on one "Action for Happiness" which they will plan and carry out during the first mobility. The aim of this "Action for Happiness" is to make other teenagers their age happy. They can for example plan, organise and carry out a compliment day at school. 
 Involving those "Actions for Happiness" into the mobilities, we will raise awareness of the fact that individual happiness is closely intertwined with being an active citizen of a society, that is civicly engaged, takes over responsibility and is aware of the chances and possibilities a European democratic society can offer. Thus, our students will acquire and develop basic skills and key competences of civic engagement and responsible citizenship in a democratic, European society. 
 However, being part of a European society also involves the promotion of tolerance as well as the fact that the individuals are able to gain enriching intercultural experience. That's why our project will also enable the students to improve their intercultural skills. They will objectively become aware of their culture and compare it to the other participants' cultures. This will foster tolerance. The fact that the students will host and will be hosted will intensify this experience. 
 
 Each mobility as well as the time to prepare mobilities will involve the creation of one product that will summarize the individual findings in a creative way, for example an international poetic photo exhibition, a common documentary, drama performance etc. 
 The final dissemination products will be a touring exhibition including the most important findings of the previous mobilities and a text mural as a constant reminder. There will be advertisement banners as means to share the most important practical guidelines to grow happiness and improve quality in life, being presented by omnichannel. 
 
 The results of each mobility will be shared on our project's website and on TwinSpace. During the dissemination ceremonies, they will also be shared on school and community level. Students, parents and local media f.ex. newspapers and local radio stations, will be invited to the individual dissemination ceremonies. The final dissimination products will be pieces of work that will summarize the most important findings, can be shared in each participants' country and will remind us of the practical guidelines to grow happiness and to improve quality of life. The reminders will include QR codes that provide links to TwinSpace and our project's website. The practical guidelines will be shared on international school and community level e.g via social media and/or omnichannel. The reminders will be installed on the four school grounds. The inauguration ceremonies will be on schools' and local level, too. 
 
 The topics of happiness and quality of life as well as gaining intercultural experience will always be of wide interest and thus the participants will give oral reports and apply their newly acquired skills in different classes at the participants' schools.  They will also function as intercultural mediators supporting additional intercultural projects.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2019-1-DE03-KA229-059859.title: /kʌˌmjunɪˈkeɪʃən/ - Communication
2019-1-DE03-KA229-059859.summary:
A total of 6 schools from Germany (integrated comprehensive school), Poland (primary school), Croatia (primary school), Bulgaria (high school), Portugal (high school) and Spain (high school) were involved in the 3-year "Communication" project. The Spanish school dropped out at the end of the original 24 months. Communication holds a society together, from our ancestors to today's networked Europe, in which people with different cultural and linguistic backgrounds communicate and understand each other.
The plan that each school is visited by the partners with 4 students and teachers had to be deviated from because of the Corona regulations.
A total of 24 participating students and accompanying teachers were involved at the meetings, with the exception of Portugal (virtual meeting), Bulgaria and Poland (without German students). They should be accommodated with host parents. This was also not possible in Bulgaria, Poland and Croatia because of the pandemic.
The topic made it possible to address a wide student body and not exclude anyone from participating. While student exchanges appeal to the high-performing students, this theme provided an opportunity for each student to contribute. For example, children with a migration background are the focus when it comes to teaching the project participants the language of minorities. With funding from the EU, the project also enabled children whose parents could not afford a student exchange to participate in the mobility programmes.

The aim of this project was to provide the students with the necessary tools for communicative challenges and a tolerant attitude. The project should promote a multilingualism that is more than grammar and language rules. Communication should be considered as a whole: the combination of language, gestures (also sign language), facial expressions and other forms of communication such as dance, music. An understanding of communication should help to prevent prejudices and promote an open-minded attitude.
Other goals of the project were the integration of children with a migration background, the investigation of foreign language teaching and the acceleration of foreign language acquisition and openness to people with communication deficits.

The activities and results can be roughly divided into the areas of writing, culture, language and everyday life.
In the area of written communication, the students learned how people with disabilities communicate in writing. The students got an insight into Braille for the blind, sign language and phonetic transcription. The students wrote their names in Braille and introduced themselves in a video in sign language and phonetic transcription. They learned the Cyrillic alphabet and translated their names, and got creative, inventing a new language and composing sentences in the codes of planets and chemical elements.

In the field of culture, there was a drumming course and visits to art exhibitions. In workshops, the students produced traditional art in handicrafts. There was also a lot of dancing. The Yiddish dance "Chiribim Chiribam" was rehearsed, as was the choreography for "Jerusalema". A video was put together from this. The students wrote an essay about their individual talents and hobbies and exchanged ideas about them. Each student created a profile of themselves and in presentations about their homeland, the students got to know about the of life of others.
Language was illuminated in terms of local dialects. The students taught each other local expressions, the use of which is regionally limited. A dictionary was created with all the languages involved in the project. Differences and similarities became visible here and the students got a feeling for the language of others.
Another aspect was the everyday life of the students. They exchanged ideas in international groups. The influence of the pandemic on the reality of life was also important. Other topics were learning at school and the home country, which was presented in short presentations. A cookbook with dishes typical of the country was also created.
We know from experience that the effects of Erasmus projects are not only short-term, but that the participating students and schools benefit in the long term. Participation in the project should create self-confidence to face new challenges with confidence. Communication hurdles should be removed and conflicts due to misunderstandings should be avoided. The school gains new impulses for its own lessons through the experiences and the exchange with other countries. This happens, for example, through new learning methods and learning apps. The participants, both students and teachers, should serve as multipliers and pass on their new knowledge to their peers or colleagues.
topics: Reception and integration of refugees and migrants
Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2019-1-DE03-KA229-059947.title: SpoLinaria - A sportive journey through the healthy European culinary culture
2019-1-DE03-KA229-059947.summary:
Summary:
Building on our recognized need to promote possible concepts for combining healthy eating and physical activity, promoting foreign language skills at student and teacher level, and promoting the quality and motivation of continuing education within the teaching profession, we have an integrative, innovative concept developed.
In addition to dealing with the skills described, we have managed to formulate a tangible topic that is still relevant on a daily basis and to fill it with life.
The implementation was specified, planned and implemented on paper. Unfortunately, the pandemic did not allow us to hold it. Unfortunately, an extension of the project period could not be carried out due to existing travel bans.

In the following more details about what we have planned in our practical concept and hopefully can carry out in the future, if necessary in another project

 
 Goals:
 - Sustainable acquisition of skills about the importance of healthy nutrition
 - Sustainable motivation to move, try new things and develop and expand the joy of sporting activities
 - Increased motivation to acquire foreign language skills
 - Acquisition and development of key qualifications
 - Promotion of the importance and diversity of Europe in all its facets and promotion of European coexistence
 - Promotion of IT and media skills, based on the concrete examination of the same on the object cookbook, film production and documentation, communication with the partners and much more.
 
Number and profile of participants:
The directly participating groups of people would have referred to 7 students and 2 teachers from the partner schools. Furthermore, the nutrition group of our school, the municipality, parents, partners of the region as well as representatives of different institutions and associations were actively involved in the planning and implementation.
 
 Description of the activities ultimately envisaged in the project plan:
 - various sports activities: water skiing, kayaking, climbing (climbing forest / bouldering hall / climbing hall), hiking, wheelchair basketball and various small, local forms of play
 - Various seminars on the topic of "healthy lifestyle"
 - joint purchases and cooking parties
 - Creation of the "SpoLinaria" cookbook and movement book
 - Creation of a project accompanying film
 - Evaluation (form was still open)
 - Health Day
- Sports fun party at the German school
 
 Methodology:
 Our methodology aimed at a holistic, action-oriented and motivating approach. Authentic learning should take place at learning locations both inside and outside of school - we were able to plan this.
 The pupils should be encouraged to think and deal with the topic of the project in a cooperative and action-oriented manner. This should lead to the development of sustainable perspectives for a healthy lifestyle.
Media involvement on platforms for communication (video calls) and project planning as well as the creative design of end products (due to the situation only the presentation of the school via video) took place.
 
Results:
- A plan in the drawer to hopefully carry out the project in some way in the future.
- Participants dealt with the European Union and got to know its possibilities
- Expansion of media skills through the creation of a "teaching school video"
- Expansion of intercultural competence through project days in advance with the project group
- Extension of project management skills and problem-solving skills of teachers
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2019-1-DE03-KA229-059963.title: How to live healthy in digital times for media vet learners?
2019-1-DE03-KA229-059963.summary:
Our project "How to live healthy in digital times for media vet learners?" is a product of a partnership of four schools from Gjövik/Norway, Kiel/Germany, Maribor/Slovenia and Split/Croatia which are offering vocational education and training (VET) for students who want to work in the field of media later on. The media branch is a very fast changing and technological exigent. The working conditions are hard and affected by a global competition. That leads to challenges for professionals to stay healthy, as media professionals often work long days (and nights) in front of the computer. We want to show how students can deal with these challenges.
 Due to the lack of material, manual and awareness of health problems directly connected to the profession it is our objective to create a digital manual for physical exercises tailored for different professions. The digital manual wil be interactive and user-friendly to support acquiring and developing basic skills of students and hence also future workers.
 The number of participating students varies depending on the school and the number of VET media classes while the number of teachers is from 2 to 4 (PE, media and language teachers) with the possibility of other members of school staff being involved if necessary. The students are all users of media technology aged 16 to 20.
 The planned activities involve an initial staff training event in Maribor so as to prepare a detailed working plan combining physical mobility with virtual exchanges. Following it an exchange of groups of students will in Norway create a logo alongside with posters about lifestyles and habits and start film preproduction (storyboard). Continuing the storyboard preproduction previously started in Split we will gather actual materials later to be used in postproducation in schools it being films related to issues of healthy lives. Both meetings would involve students working in mixed groups preparing the material in an international spirit and experiencing work on a complex project. Everything done will be documented on a common platform and evaluated with the results being presented at next meeting in Maribor and the final dissemination and evaluation of department colleagues planned to take place in Kiel.
 Tasks and responsibilities will be equally distributed among partners and communication ensured via ICT modern tools such as Skype and eTwinning alongside with international meetings all involving measurable goals and objectives in terms of procedures, tasks and resources used. SELFIE is to be applied as a self -reflection tool and results will be published on eTwinning, Erasmus +,  in school newsletters following meetings and newspaper articles.
 The project will result in the above mentioned digital manual accessible at all times, also a website, posters, logo, video materials, articles and documentation reports all having informational and educational purposes. The longterm benefits of the stated activities are awareness being raised of the importance of physical exercise and availability of the digital materials used for exercising on a daily basis. 
 Our aim is not only the prevention of health damages. With this project we would like to establish a partnership of two northeuropean and two southeuropean schools with the same vocational education in one branch. We want to learn from best practise in the field of digital lessons, digital cooperation and European mobility. To establish a European project spirit, we will be a part of a Film festival in Maribor.

hr.name: Škola za Dizajn, Grafiku i Održivu Gradnju

2019-1-DE03-KA229-060009.title: Tiles -  A Cultural Journey  from the Past to the Future
2019-1-DE03-KA229-060009.summary:
The project “Azulejos-tiles a cultural journey” delivered what it promised: a creative dialogue and mutual awareness of tiles as an everyday item of art and function. A tangible result in each country is the friendship tiles mural combining the artistic heritage of all participating schools. The mural is a visual reminder of the project and partners involved valueing the students’ s achievements on a daily basis.
By the end of the deeplproject students and teachers are acquainted with the tile, its uses and functionality in daily life across the participating schools. All students and teachers involved are aware of the manufacturing process of tiles as well as the involved craftsmanship of drawing, painting and glazing the tiles before the fireing process. By means of digital platforms like “padlet” students were able to gain confidence uploading and sharing their creative output. Learning Apps like jigsaw creators helped to become playful and create new online content using the aesthetics of the tile.
As a first timer participating in an Erasmus+ Project and being the leading coordinator of five countries we managed to create awareness at our  German school for travelling abroad to explore cultural diversity and meeting other cultures. The impressions not only on the students that travelled but also on all participants of the Project day at our school during the visit of our international partners are long-lasting. This is noticed in the way students in all grades are still talking about this visit and the project day. The Erasmus+ Club has raised awareness and has become the most popular Club out of all the schools offered activities.

2019-1-DE03-KA229-060138.title: Active for Climate
2019-1-DE03-KA229-060138.summary:
The "Fridays for Future" movement has become a worldwide phenomenon in the past months showing the growing concern of young people about the Future of our planet. Scientists and politicians support this movement. But school strike is not the only possible reaction, young people need to be active and certainly are willing to do so.
 
 Our project "Active for Climate" is a first attempt to show students what can be done at a personal level and how change can be made possible: 
 Together with students from three European countries (Croatia, Italy and Spain), they discover the manifold challenges to stop global warming.
 Some of the responses can find common answers in every country, such as reducing energy and water consumption by using smart home solutions. Some of them depend on the specific climate and the geographical situation in a country, such as wind energy, PV or geo-thermal ressources. Students learn through this project how a problem we all share in Europe can have different solutions, but a common target. And they also learn that consumer habits need to change in order to permit a more sustainable agriculture to exist. Slow food can be one of the answers.
 In a global world, cooperation with people from other countries, having their own mentality and their way of looking at things, is an absolute necessity which needs to be acquired and trained. Through common experiences like roll plays and flash mobs and working all together on a technical device,  they will not only see a tangible result of their efforts, this project will enable students to better accept diversity in thinking and doing and contribute to a better mutual understanding.
 Another target of this project is to show young people new job opportunities in a fast changing labour market where a large number of traditional jobs will disappear, p.ex. in the automotive industry or the retail business,  and will be replaced by E-commerce, robots and AI. 
 Working for the climate together with our European partners can open new job perspectives for our students and help them finding their way in the labour market of the future.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2019-1-EE01-KA229-051570.title: With the Skills of the Future for a Successful Job and Life
2019-1-EE01-KA229-051570.summary:
The European Reference Framework of Key Competences defines the competences as each European citizen needs for personal fulfilment and development, employment, social inclusion and active citizenship. It invited Member States to ensure that their education and training systems are able to equip people with these competences.
 
 The aim of the project is to enable students to develop original solutions and ideas while relating them to concepts. The qualities that the students will gain overlaps with the abilities that the current business world requires nowadays. In the global sense, students need to improve these skills in order to adapt to the complex life styles that the competitive information era necessitate.
 
 This project has been designed for the purpose of improving our students' acquisition of basic skills. They will be familiar with the key principles and components of Project Based Learning. With this aim, 5 countries identified the needs of the students thanks to some surveys and the Erasmus +project that the 3 countries have been carrying out for the last 2 years. In Estonia, 3 teachers from each country will get a seminar about 21st century skills. Then in 4 countries with the help of the activities 5 students from each country will practice  these skills.
 
 We tailor the working methods based on participants', attitudes, needs and profiles to ensure high productivity.  The methodology is highly practical and participative. We embrace collaborative working methods which foster mutual learning and cooperation among partners. Our focus is upon learning in an interactive and international environment knowledge applicable to the real contexts and or /in the classroom. The pedagogical methods which we are going to use are; experiential training, best practices exchange, learning by doing, group and peer work activities. 
 
 Because surveys have proven that students tend to forget the knowledge after exams or after their graduation.21 st century skills are the skills that they will be using all their lives. However, the management of the project is not the system of putting the activities one after the other, it will be a set of operations including control, skimming, reporting procedures at all stages during the whole cycle. According to the strategic and European developments of the schools, leadership, creating strategies, taking effective decisions, planning, creating an organization culture, positive motivation towards learning, education management, Corporation with the stakeholders are the essential elements. This Project has been designed to fulfill all these necessities. And it is sustainable in terms of integration of competences into lessons and flipped classroom method.
 
  IMPACT:
 
  Students will ;
 - come forward with their ideas at all stages of development
 - try learned techniques and expand their new skills
 - know that mistakes lead to better learning, they will make them to gain their own aims
 - break down potentially overwhelming projects into manageable tasks
 - be more confident and aware of their needs to be successful in school and in life
 - be better equipped for life
 - improve attitudes about learning in school
 - improve self-esteem, social responsibility, problem solving strategies and communication skills
 
 TEACHERS
 Teachers and principals will:
 - become effective thinkers by assuming multiple roles and tasks
 - observe other countries’ administrative and educational methods and techniques, share
 experience, ideas and suggestions
 - promote good practices in education, cooperation and combined effective action in order to reach
 common goals
 - improve professional development by acquiring new training techniques in an innovative way to
 introduce key competences in the school curriculum
 - obtain concrete techniques and methods about 21st century 
 - improve the knowledge/techniques/methods to make the lessons more interesting within the classroom
 -establish relationship between the disciplines
 - use the results of the project as the materials for researching for other institutions and for European instruments
 
 Parents  and local societies will:
 - feel welcome in whatever region of the world they happen to find themselves
 - consider each individual on their own merits
 - not to refer to a special group but intend their message to be universal
 - oppose racism, tribalism, regionalism, religious bias and all kinds of segregation of any kind
 - be tolerant and respectful of other people's cultures
 - recognize that events happening in the far end of the world away from their country can have a real impact on their life
 - get interested in international news,- be positive towards European projects and values
 - add a value to the quantitive and qualitive commonwealth of the society
 
 All participants will:
 - be actively involved towards a better understanding of the real European dimension
 - improve communicative skills in foreign languages
 - get involved in strategic orientation of open and effective principals.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2019-1-EE01-KA229-051678.title: Yellow European Stars
2019-1-EE01-KA229-051678.summary:
In order to create the European Citizen Profile that values what to do for people and for the planet towards a sustainable Europe, six secondary schools from Croatia, Estonia, Italy, Portugal, Spain and Turkey with different backgrounds, but with common interests and concerns prepared the strategic partnership "YES" involving students aged between 14 and 18 years old in each school.
 
 By improving working methods, exchanging methodologies and sharing good practices this partnership aims to change the risky behaviour of youngsters in their daily lifestyle (bad eating habits, sedentary life, addictions); wrong attitude against people of different race, sexual inclination or different cultures; indifference and low integration towards youth with disability and indifference about essential and priority environmental  issues.
 
 This is a global project divided into six related main topics: Health and Sports; Cultural Heritage; Language, Ideals and Mentalities; E-Citizenship; Sustainable Green Cities (environmental issues); Tolerance. A diverse variety of activities related to the six topics will be promoted by the schools using informal and non-formal methods.
 
 The project will be lead and developed by two main working teams composed of teachers and students that will promote, organise and disseminate the activities in each school.
 
 Two types of learning, teaching and training activities will be included in the project: short-term joint staff training events where teachers will have training courses concerning the project theme and also study visits combining on-site visits to relevant organisations, presentations, and discussion workshops and short-term exchanges of groups of pupils that will give students the opportunity to experience international learning, reinforce their understanding of the diversity of European cultures and languages, develop new skills and competences necessary for their personal development and deepen each topic with special activities.
 
 DEOR planning for this project has been studied to give a high level of involvement inside and outside the organisations involving multiple stakeholders.
 
 The E-twinning platform will be our privileged common online database of experiences that will allow the intensive cooperation among all schools involved during and after the project as well as the dissemination of our experiences, activities and results. 
 
 The specific goals are to share experiences and to adapt learning programmes and teaching strategies in the participating schools considering sport practice, outdoor physical activities, healthy lifestyle education, cultural heritage values preservation, increase of environmental awareness, development of different languages, and change of mentalities, all through inclusion and integration.  
 
 We intend to improve the way of looking at diversity as a chance to improve themselves and others, discuss how different countries cope with social inclusion and equal opportunities, fostering integration and equal rights. Participants will be taught the importance of tolerance and non-discrimination, overcoming all forms of discrimination, and developing the feeling of belonging to one European community.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2019-1-EE01-KA229-051680.title: I See You, I Hear You, I Feel You
2019-1-EE01-KA229-051680.summary:
Misbehavior and bullying have been an inevitable part of our school lives. As a big part of social learning takes place in school, it is essential to shape students' attitudes in school. In this context, it is important to underline that moral education is not just a matter of individuals, mainly teachers, but it is the matter of the whole community.
 
 Despite many anti-bullying programmes conducted in schools, bullying and misbehaving is not significantly decreasing. Better results have come from value-based, evidence-based, school-wide practices that include both prevention and case management tools and which are based more on value creation. In this context, restorative practices are a good way to make changes, to transform the way schools address disciplinary challenges and misbehaviour.
 
 In this project, we will build a healthier school climate and communities, moreover, we are incorporating RP into our teaching to create a respectful dialogue between all parties of the school community and supportive atmosphere in lessons.
 
 For this project, 2 aspects of RP are primary: community building and use dialogue to respond to harm. We build a culture of belonging, a sense of community where every member is seen, heard and respected. We are aiming to incorporate RP into our teaching to show that positive classroom environment helps to achieve higher academic goals. 
 
 The project offers students an innovative and unique opportunity to develop their abilities, such as forming respectful opinion, teamwork, responsibility. The students are stimulated to form a mindset that will help them to become independent deciders, critical thinkers, objective and creative problem solvers, friendly connection builders and maintainers. The RP methods are integrated to build, maintain and restore relationships through community building/recreation, drama and social justice, environmental, virtual vs reality and sports topics. We built up the activities on these topics to engage as many school subjects as possible which makes school climate change a reality. The project will give a valuable addition and input to our curriculums, as we create lesson activities and plans based on RP to link the knowledge to real situations. 
 
 We will achieve this with well-planned activities, each of which will serve the set goals. We aim to:
 - create a change in a school climate
 - respond to and prevent harm that can be seen in: 
 * inclusive school culture (non-exclusive lessons)
 * fair decision-making practices
 * a safe and caring mental environment
 * effective and innovative learning and teaching by using RP methodology in lessons 
 * decreased bullying and other types of conflicts
 * achieved greater awareness of the respectful connections between people 
 * increased ability to respond to inappropriate behaviour
 * creation of understanding that misbehaviour seeks for more connection, not disconnection
 * students' ability to address the impact of their actions 
 * reduced numbers of disciplinary acts
 * increased confidence and satisfaction among students, staff and parents
 
 The activities are based on the active participation of the whole school community, their involvement, initiative, and teamwork. Students and teachers will develop a various range of skills, from realistic self-evaluation, school climate evaluation to emotional and behavioural self-regulation in various situations. We want them to be active listeners, critical thinkers, learners who express themselves freely in order to increase the efficiency of communication and build and maintain relationships. Planned activities promote our students to be more courageous to express their feelings and thoughts, to speak their mind and be more responsible for one's actions. Restorative circles will be the main methodology for our planned activities. Our target groups are students, teachers, school staff, administrative staff, parents, teachers and students from other schools in the local area. 
 
 The project will create baggage full of RP-integrated resources, free to use for all. 
 
 We will assess the project's field objectives effectiveness by:
 improved school climate assessment at the end of the project, nr of teachers using RP in lessons, nr of disciplinary reports per year, nr of RP methods integrated into lessons, School attendance records, nr of misbehaving students, nr of presentation for parents and students community on RP, nr of teachers creating the family groups, nr of subject curriculum changes, satisfaction surveys.
 
 The longer-term benefit of this project would be the changed school climate we can enjoy, and big experience resource we will create with our partners. The international cooperation will make this project and its achievements relevant to all participants, as we are changing the way of how we deal with bullying and disciplinary problems from now on. 
 
 All our materials will be available for EU teachers through our website, eTwinning platform and other free sources.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-EL01-KA229-062400.title: European Food Adventures
2019-1-EL01-KA229-062400.summary:
"Once upon a sweet day six girls met at a training course in Ankara, Turkey. They carried something related to food with them and they were strangely dressed. The girl from Turkey guided and hosted her new friends. They learned so much about that country and they had so nice time together and  that they signed the "contract of friendship". When it was time to leave, their friend from Croatia invited the rest to her own country to get to know that better and to strengthen their friendship. They all were very excited and thought that it would be a great idea to continue this journey to the rest countries. Furthermore, they decided to write a diary to keep their adventures alive and to give the opportunity to experience these beautiful places, to other people who would read it..."
 It's not just a fairy tale, it's the real story of the two years Erasmus project between the six schools from Greece, Turkey, Cyprus, Spain, Portugal and Croatia that met and are going to cooperate in the "European Food Adventures" project. 
 Diet is an important factor which affects people's health. The eating habits are adopted from early childhood. This is why particular awareness of the school is needed in this area. All partners have noticed that pupils have a more or less important problem with their eating habits and are worried about pupils' health. Children receive many wrong messages through advertisements of unhealthy snacks. Furthermore they eat a lot of fast food and junk food and have sedentary lives.due to overuse of technological devices. Teachers also noticed that pupils have a little European conscience as they have little or no knowledge of Europe and European Union. It’s a main objective of this project to raise awareness about good eating habits and happy lifestyle with physical activities. Concurrently the project involves a better knowledge of the European Union, European traditions through healthy food and exercise instilling into children's values such as respect to the national culture, heritage, national symbols, promotion of respect to foreign cultures and traditions and the equality of humans. 
 This project will give pupils the opportunity to improve English, ICT, presentation skills and research. The project is based on the idea of open learning and interdisciplinary work. Students and teachers will travel to partner countries to get to know each other, to work there together, to be in touch with their culture and education systems, to learn from one another and exchange ideas and experiences. They will build a garden, grow plants, watch their growth, visit farms, gardens, fields etc, they will cook and play, organize campaigns and presentations to the local community about healthy habits and the European dimension of the project. Common products will be: two books about traditional food and games, the story mentioned above at the begging of the text and two card games. There will be seminars to organize and many events. Happy moments with pupils' families, cooking, playing, trying to reach a better vision of life and give pupils strength in mind and body and knowledge, too. Working in teams with planned objectives will allow pupils to develop other important citizenship skills, helping them become sociable, tolerant, responsible, with confidence. 
 All the schools have students with special needs and those who are marginalized. Many of them don't like being at school and try to avoid learning. Because of this all the schools have decided to enrich their teaching methods with non formal practices and inclusive approaches and within this project it can be reached. Besides, the teachers will discover other European countries and cultures, meet European colleagues and educational systems, develop their awareness and knowledge about how to lead a healthy life, increase the use of foreign languages and ICT and discover different teaching methods in pedagogical approaches and school management and as a result they will make their teaching more attractive. The European dimension of the participating schools and their profile will be strengthened, too.
 Networking, social media, newsletters, flyers, presentations at meetings,conferences, on exhibitions, fairs, carnival fests, promotional material and products, the project website are the most important tools for the dissemination of our project, its progress and results.
 The main target groups are the teachers, pupils and their families. We estimate a total number of 4000 indirect participants who will learn about the project: parents and members of the local community, other schools, the online audience, will be indirect beneficiaries of the project activities by having access to the information provided by the project results and activities of dissemination.There is also an endless open number of possible indirect beneficiaries that can learn from the project in time, after the project remains available for useful guidance in the future, for the online audience.

2019-1-EL01-KA229-062406.title:
SCALES-Stop Canned food And Learn Eating
Smart
2019-1-EL01-KA229-062406.summary:
The Project “SCALE ”, is a common effort by four partners (TR,GR, SP and CR) focusing equally on Mediterranean Diet and outdoor activities in students in the age 6-12 .The project is in line with European Commission about Health and Wellbeing. The process engages  8 students,  2 students with special needs, teachers, physical education teachers, regional stakeholders and Experts in the field of Mediterranean Diet and Outdoor activities.  The transnational and interdisciplinary dimension of the Project - through the partner organizations and staff specialties – provides added value  and its educational outcomes by integrating different practices and outcomes taking also into account an approach outside the EU.
 The methodology includes three training activities based on non-formal education tools ,one
 transnational project meetings for the trainings elaboration and the production of tangible outcomes;
 a monitoring plan for the process assessment during its lifetime and a dissemination strategy to
 specific groups. Tangible outcomes : Virtual museum, Project broshure,a leaflet on how to read food
 labels, a website, CD-ROM, leaflets, t shirts, logo .The project also strengthens our capacity in the areas
 of organizational management, leadership and internationalization as well as in the area of training
 competences in line with individuals' needs and expectations. Expected impact is high and sustainability is ensured through the events and addressing specific target groups at regional/municipal and European level, so that to make project outcomes visible and exploitable by additional relevant stakeholders.

2019-1-EL01-KA229-062999.title: Back To The Roots-Back To The Future
2019-1-EL01-KA229-062999.summary:
The cultural sector has the capacity to be both a source of European identity and the setting for the development of innovative activities that boost job creation. European and national political authorities are aware of the need to resolve the unemployment problem which has become of vital importance to European integration. The cultural sector covers a wide range of economic and industrial activities. It includes activities connected with heritage, literature, press, music, entertainment arts, media and the audiovisual sector. Given the recent increase in cultural production and demand, the context industries represent an area of social interaction and economic activity in the present concept of the European Union. Europe's cultural heritage enriches our lives and provides inspiration for our cultural and creative industries. It enables economic growth, employment and social cohesion.
 
 The project will pay attention to the importance of cultural and historical heritage of Europe countries. Young people will be able to find out the job opportunities about culture. So, at first local regions then around Europe, the youth can create new jobs innovatively based on cultural and historical heritage.
 
 There are 6 partner schools; Greece, Turkey, Romania, Spain, Croatia and Italy. At least, 100 students and 65 teachers will take part in the project main activities and at least 1000 students or teachers will take part in local activities and other project activities.
 
 There will be 6 LTT planned activies to lead the achievement of the project's objectives. The first one is short term joint stuff training and the others are short-term exchanges of groups of pupils. During the all LTT activities, the participants will have a chance to visit tangible heritages and experience some intangible heritages of the host countries and use digital tools for promotion.The activities will support and increase consciousness for-profit and non-profit business management, marketing and communications related to cultural and historical values. The teachers will prepare task/project based activities plan for students for the activities.
 
 The schools involved in this Project will increase;
 -EU citizen and EU democracy consciousness,
 -their knowledge and implementation of entrepreneurship, 
 -their international cooperation capacity,
 -their awareness about European shared cultural values,
 -teachers and students motivation to be creative about cultural and historical values,
 -foreign language skills,
 -the usage of digital tools.
 
 The partnership of this project involve 6 partner schools from different countries of Europe. Thanks to this strategic partnership, we will be able to present and support the entrepreneurship for the safeguard of both cultural and historical heritage using innovative ICT's.

2019-1-EL01-KA229-063009.title: Inclusion through Arts
2019-1-EL01-KA229-063009.summary:
Our project involved six schools on primary level and targets students of age 6-12. Main characteristic of our project was that many of the participating students are Roma students or bilingual or students with special social and learning needs. It was based on the idea of integration of arts (oral narration, digital narration, music, drama and outdoor learning) in the process of learning and teaching mainly of Language subject. 
 Main priorities of our project were: social inclusion of the students, the supporting confrontation with the early school leaving (ESL) and disadvantage and the support of the "target groups" of each partner school to improve oral and written speech in Language Subject.  
Roma children were connected through our program with oral traditional fairy tales narration, music and drama and outdoor learning  to Language. In this way, they bridged their oral tradition and special characteristics of their origin with school knowledge, personal expression, and personal experiences.
 Through this method, students developed social skills of collaboration and communication. Students have made a step forward in social inclusion and through our project’s interesting activities they had a reason not to quit school. 
 From our experience, Narration and Arts encouraged children to communicate ideas, feelings, problems and solutions in both verbal and non-verbal ways. This took place in our 3 year project. Through arts students with learning disabilities and cognitive difficulties had equal school opportunities which proved to be beneficial both for the process of teaching and learning of those subjects and for the intercultural awareness of them. Digital narration and outdoor learning also greatly improved the student's impact and interest!
 Our project through narration, digital narration, music, theatrical play, fine arts and outdoor learning made a channel of communication for Roma and non Roma students and the cultural variety of Europe (Greece, Croatia, Czech Republic, Spain, Latvia, Finland).Especially through the material of the common activities that they did in classroom. 
 Scientifically, our project's objectives were based on Multiple types of Intelligence theory, Project based Learning, CLIL theory about billingual students, Art-based approaches and Outdoor Learning theory. All these theories were presented in six Training meetings that were organised. The benefits of the training meetings made teachers design more interesting activities for partner target groups. All Timetable activities combined specific aims of Language Lesson and Social aims.

2019-1-ES01-KA229-064069.title: Learning Outdoors - Vivid Exploration
2019-1-ES01-KA229-064069.summary:
In recent years there has been a cultural shift in our society that has resulted in reduced access to the outdoors for children due to different factors, including technological advances leading to more sedentary activities. There is evidence that increased physical activity is associated with improved brain structure and function in children. Therefore, we believe outdoor education for everyone, in an inclusive environment, is fundamental for children’s learning.
 However, technology has a positive benefit as well, and we want to teach the students to incorporate it into their lives in a healthier way.
 In addition, cooperative learning should play a significant role in our schools, since it helps provide experiences that develop both good learning and social skills. It helps to build positive relationships among students, which is important for creating a learning community that values diversity.
 Our project LO-VE will promote inclusive education, counteract students’ sedentary lifestyle while promoting positive use of technology, and make a long term and more vivid impression on their learning through the use of international, outdoor education. 
 
 Our main objectives are:
 -Foster social inclusion through innovative and cooperative methods. 
 -Make learning outdoors an integral part of daily learning activities.
 -Share this experience with other countries in order to build international connections.
 -Teach the students how to use technologies wisely.
 -Train teachers in innovative methodologies.
 
 We are six schools from Spain, Finland, Croatia, Czech Republic, Slovakia and Portugal.
 The groups who will take part in this project are: 1650 pupils from 6 to 15 years old, with 92 students from 10 to 15 years old attending the short-term international exchanges; 100 teachers per school, including tutors, English, and ICT teachers; families; and local authorities.
 
 We will include the following activities:
 ·Outdoor gymkhanas based on problem-solving learning. 
 ·Workshops, including yoga and meditation in nature, gardening and photography.
 ·Outdoor projects using Phenomenon and Project Based Learning (PBL): student will research their environment, process the information, and share it with project partners. Examples of products are touristic guides and video documentaries.
 ·Performances, which will be carried out during the meetings.
 ·Outdoor assemblies about project topics.
 ·An international club (eTwinning) that will help build international connections.
 
 There will be transnational learning meetings, where we will develop many of the activities listed above. Host schools will also offer teachers teaching observing, good practices exchange and training about innovative methodologies.
 Teachers will design different materials for the project, the final product being the LO-VE book: a compilation of outdoor activities grouped by competencies carried out throughout the two-year project.
 By actively taking part in many of our activities, all families will be given the chance to be involved in their children's education.
 
 We will use many innovative methodologies and tools focused on inclusion, including PBL, cooperative learning, gamification, and ICT, so they can offer a high quality education that compensates for social inequalities.
 Students will use cooperative learning strategies and the project will share the same approach establishing norms and protocols that allows teachers to: contribute, help and encourage each other, share, solve problems and give and accept feedback.
 
 The results and impact envisaged are:
 -Students will: have learnt to use technologies wisely, be able to work in teams, spend more time outside, have built international connections, and have developed the key competencies, particularly the social competence. 
 -Teachers will be more knowledgeable and satisfied with their jobs: they will be able to implement innovative methodologies thus provide a higher quality education.
 -Families will become more involved in school education. They will be aware of the sedentary lifestyle risks and the importance of spending time outdoors.
 
 This project will promote long-term benefits, since:
 -Both students and teachers will make life-long friends, develop deeper understanding of other cultures and school systems.
 -Teachers will be able to offer modern methodologies and thus influencing new student generations. 
 -Our schools will become sharing environments where teachers, students and families regardless their social background will be able to work together towards a common goal: the welfare of children.
 
 Why LO-VE? Because we know that when children have time to play outside they develop all of the basic skills that people everywhere must acquire: physical, social, emotional, and constructive skills, creativity and logic. Why LO-VE? Because sharing experiences with people from all around the world makes the moment more intense and memorable and helps forge emotional connections that transcend all barriers.

2019-1-ES01-KA229-064099.title: Our natural Heritage, food and folklore
2019-1-ES01-KA229-064099.summary:
This is a project which will be developed during two years. 
 Our team is composed by 5 different countries: Bulgaria, Croatia, Poland; Slovaquia and Spain. The project includes three countries which have previoulsy cooperated in a former Erasmus project and which want to develop European projects at their  schools due to the great results which it has had on their students.
 We join a partner who is expert on the topics developed in the project and a new partner which has never participated in Erasmus+, but which will be an added value to the project,  thus it can be also added to a numerous number of schools who are learning and evolving their participants’ needs and competences through Erasmus projects.
 All  of us have similar interests and each member is expert on one of the units of the project, which will contribute to an effective implementation of the project.
 
 Primary and secondary students will actively participate in the implementation of the activities and the mobilities. Although only 20 students from each school will directly participate in the mobilities, we will include almost the total amount of our student into the project, since they will contribute to the implementation of the different activities of the project, workshops and competitions.
 Our main objective is to make students aware of the  rich heritage and folklore which surrounds all our countries.
 Besides, we will try to provide them  with different models of teaching at all the schools in order they can consider different future job choices and we will contribute to preserve traditional local and natural elements of our heritage.Students will acquire and develop basic skills and key competences, essential to provide them with future oportunities, which will allow them to overcome their economic obstacles.    
 Our  project will also include the following objectives:   
 - Foster the European citizenship: we will promote tolerance and respect towards different cultures and ways of living. 
 -Preserve the natural heritage and traditions in our regions, promoting the intercultural education and the lifelong learning.
 -Motivate students by means of innovative practices, the use of new methodologies and digital tools. 
 -Develop a communicative approach of languages following the European dimension of learning.
 -Promote professional skills, vocational studies and traditional jobs; which will also be disseminated in our regions and countries.
 -Enhance the positive elements of our diets to promote healthy eating. 
 -Establish a long- lasting cooperation: we will continue working together in different projects and we will design and apply for new future Erasmus+ KA2 projects at our schools.
 
 Students will create different activities to work in the following topics:
 -Music and dancing: magazines, flipped videos to teach foreign partners, music and dancing competitions
 -Traditional arts and crafts: workshops, interviews, digital presentations...
 -Natural Heritage: documentaries, interviews to several authorities in their region; digital itineraries and maps using QR, photo collages
 -Traditions and celebrations: magazines, podcasts and videos
 -Gastronomy: traditional food workshops, production of vegetables, analysis of the evolution of our diet.
 
  We will develop actives methodologies focussed on the students, which promote a communicative approach of languages, and , which employ new digital activities to motivate students.
 Our project will be sousteinable in time, since it will produce didactic units, activities, tools, projects...which will be used in the following years.
 Our project will teach students to cooperate with new partners, promoting tolerance, respect and integration.They will improve their Linguistic competence, and have a better understanding of other cultures. 
 Teachers will learn that European cooperation strenght us and gives us more future opportunities.
 They will develop new teaching techniques, and know how to use new digital tools and methodologies. Besides, they will increase their Linguistic Competence, which will be very useful not only at a particular level, but to enrich the students' lessons.
 
 Finally, this project will also be useful to promote our Natural Heritage and folk in other countries promoting a soustainable kind of tourism which can create new future job opportunities in our region.
