2019-1-IT02-KA229-062644.title: Connect-enjoy mountains & learning outdoors
2019-1-IT02-KA229-062644.summary:
In daily interaction with our students and encouraged by contemporary research, we have noticed that young people increasingly escape into virtual worlds, which results in the reduction of their cognitive, affective and motor skills and increases the possibility of developing psycho-physical illnesses. For this reason, using the natural and socio-cultural resources around us, we have designed a project that inspires students to engage in experiential and field-based learning. Students would stay outdoors and learn and recreate themselves through a multidisciplinary program. In a fun and creative way, with the application of modern, innovative and interactive methods, they would study topics from different disciplines such as geography, biology, physics, maths, history, mother tongue and literature, visual arts and at the same time engage in physical activities. The project is intended for all students, especially those who do not have the opportunity to engage in recreational sports. However, our main concern it to provide opportunities for socially deprived students and those with impaired mental or physical health.
 Mountains and the surrounding highland areas are our underlying motive, namely, the preserved environment where activities and field research will be carried out in order to develop an awareness of the need for sustainable development. The purpose is not only to learn about material and immaterial heritage and build cultural identity, but also to find similarities and links with peers from other regions in nature conservation, ecological preservation, historical, geographic and geodetic specifics and monuments, local terrain features, sites of historical, cultural, ethnological or anthropological value, folk literature, customs, dance, music, old trades, language specifics, historical and geographic links that enable linguistic contacts and influences. With our partner schools, we would like to explore all these fields of interest and jointly discover the benefits of returning to nature and the need to respect and preserve environmental resources as a pledge for the future.
    Our plan is to design attractive activities that would enable students to master the basic skills of hiking, orienteering, skiing, sledging, walking and camping. Furthermore, the forest ecosystem and its benefits to the individual, society and all other living world would be explored with the help of reference literature and direct field measurements in the domain of biology and physics. We would learn about the most common types of trees, apply trigonometry in geodesy, search network tools and use them for altitude measurements and GPS locations, learn orientation skills, seek ways to build mountain trails and use mathematical measuring and calculation methods in all these areas. We would analyse the geological structure of soil by making mineral, rock and fossil collections and explore areas under legal protection and cultural monuments. Likewise, we would study regional linguistic diversity, language specificity, and detect linguistic interdependence resulting from similar geographical and historical development and influences among countries. We would look for similarities in nurturing folk literature, find common features and mountain motives, thus, together with the actual biodiversity observe folk mythology and tales we share and even create artwork from natural materials.
 Hence, we want to connect with local geodetic and ecological experts, hiking and walking instructors, licensed ski instructors, physicians and physiotherapists, ethnologists, curators, local writers, culinary educators, mountain rescue teams and environmental protection agencies.
 Our emphasis will be on creating interesting sporting competitions that take into account traditional culture, quizzes, presentations, posters, interactive maps, charts, picture exhibits, comparative dictionaries, geolinguistic atlases, anthologies of local tales, digital photo albums, video works, respectively, various entertaining and creative activities depending on the students' interests so that in a natural environment they can discover their strengths, talents and develop interests. We also intend to develop future learning scenarios to use and disseminate at schools, within the local and professional community and other formal and informal teaching. In the spirit of multiculturalism, by developing intercultural communication and finding biological, geographic, historical, artistic, linguistic and traditional meeting points with partner countries, we want to encourage our students to understand and respect other cultures and raise them as true European citizens. In this respect, we want to achieve long-term cooperation with our partner schools.
    In conclusion, our ultimate goal is to acknowledge that mountains can be conquered by all students regardless of their psycho-physical limitations, health or social problems.

2019-1-IT02-KA229-062782.title: Soft Skills for a better life
2019-1-IT02-KA229-062782.summary:
The project has been affected by the Covid 19 pandemia. The project started in September 2019 so we had only the opening meeting in November 2019 and then all went down. Despite this, the partnership was so strong, since the beginning that the project run regularly even if only online for the first two years. 
As The project has been designed to develop soft skills we can say that the challenge was really hard but in the end, we won because step by step students learned to manage relationships and collaborate with pairs without conflicts and by distance. In The situation of isolation, the project helped students and teachers to stay connected and continue to work even in pairs.
We can say that with this project we and our students reached :
-the ability to apply critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration and Emotional intelligence as the ability to read one's own inner world and that of others expressed their maximum during the lockdown time.
-the Improvement of self-awareness, decision-making and collaboration skills.
-the ability to apply problem-solving to daily life situations
Due to the age of students involved, we used Stories, Fairy tales and well-known literature for kids, we have given the students the possibility to start critical thinking, creativity and collaboration. They expressed feelings and emotions in a supportive environment developing their self-esteem.
STEAM ( STEM + ART) and Storytelling were important topics we developed together helping students to develop soft skills and transversal skills such as : 
 -Collaboration: Teamwork  working productively with the classmate, and foreign students and this was also for teachers working with peers and foreign peers; 
 -Communication and interpersonal skills developing excellent communication skills.  
 -Problem-solving: Guided the students in thinking outside the box and have excellent critical thinking skills.  
 -Concentration and Time management: managing energy and attention to accomplish more;
 -Leadership: It has meant getting a different role if it needs and guiding a group in the areas they have been assigned. It has meant being able to work in a group without conflicts and to share successes and failures at the same level.
We used active learning and collaborative learning as the central methodology. Tinkering and making were used by partner schools as potentially rich intellectual activities. Students made many products in a coordinated way not only in STEAM but also in literacy, literature and the arts. 
All activities we planned, have been designed in order to develop valuable skills, such as generating and testing ideas, gathering and making sense of evidence, developing possible solutions, and evaluating processes and outcomes, improving their critical thinking skills through issues which can be investigated, developing emotional intelligence and acting without fear. 
It was essential during the isolation and all project activities were helpful to manage the situation.
Teachers made the Rubrics which helped them to evaluate the progress in each project area

2019-1-IT02-KA229-062941.title: Tourism, Enogastronomy and Culture
2019-1-IT02-KA229-062941.summary:
The project focused the attention of our students on the peculiarities of the territory where they live. Discovering what the territory can offer in terms of environmental, artistic and monumental attractions, specific niche products coming from local farms or crafts, cultural events and what can be related to a so called style of life, the students learnt how these "products" can appear appealing to the partners' students for their enjoyment. The activities allowed the students to discover unknown perspectives related to the region or country where they live and how these distinctive traits can produce wellness, social cohesion, and chances of job and wealth. The challenge was that they had to present them in a captivating way to their partners and build with them a series of tours related with Culture, and Enogastronomy, and generically, with a style of life, specific of the area where they live. The students created different multimedia products (flyers, posters, videoclips, a website) where they presented and advertised specific tours related with "Tourism, Enogastronomy and Culture" in typical location of their area. They offered the outcomes of their work to selected stakeholders and local administrator, in a specific event closing the meetings. Every school granted the mobility of 24 students and 4 teachers, with a staff of other 4 teachers collaborating to the activities. The students of every school collected info and different materials related to the topic, shared them with partners via internet, worked in presence during the meetings to create a touristic offer based on tours, thought to promote some specific aspects of their own area.
They also worked virtually during the pandemic to share their different way to approach that situation and analyse how each country faced it. 
The main methodology was the "flipped classroom" and the "project work in team". The results achieved from this project are: - discovering of hidden peculiarities and increasing of the consideration that our students have about the territory where they live - understanding how these peculiatity can look appealing to people coming from other countries and cultures - learning how the resources of their own area can produce work and wealth - improving the students' English fluency in a work context - improving their ICT skills. On the long term the main benefit will be the enhancing of students and families' European sentiment, making them proud of their cultural heritages thanks to the activity of sharing them with the partners. Another aspect will be the contribution that the school may give for the promotion of the territory where is located, reinforcing the relationship with the social and economic istitutions at the local level.

2019-1-IT02-KA229-063083.title: Running Nature into School
2019-1-IT02-KA229-063083.summary: RUSH sheds light on Outdoor Activities as a holistic and inclusive approach to teaching and education, determinant of functional autonomy and quality of life. This project aimed at supplying students with the appropriate tools to become active agents and critical consumers, able to identify healthy practices related to their lifestyle and surrounding environment: the way that their habits are viewed can shape their perspective of health and wellness for the rest of their lives. Considering and recognizing that actively living their environment intersects with aspects of public health and equity, students have become not only informed consumers, but also citizens who can engage in many facets of the social system, from taking sports for fun to advocating for policies. It was prominent to undertake different approaches to Outdoor activities principles to bring intuition and awareness and guide the most profound principles of instinctive acting and health. Most of the school partners have already participated in Erasmus+ projects, hence they could strongly contribute to this proposal with their expertise. In addition, they are Mediterranean countries which allowed them to unify criteria and establish comparisons as regards the lifestyle culture. Likewise, the associated partners’ heterogeneity widened the project scope and became the perfect opportunity to enrich both, the activity contents and each student’s individual experience, above all the ones involved in the mobilities that are challenged with economical obstacles or learning difficulties. The target of this project was to empower our students to effectively engage with health issues through active problem solving, developing questions and investigating to find solutions, not only as a local problem but as a global European necessity. Habits, health and wellbeing, environment and social equality were the topics involved in the project in order to comply with Horizon 2020 challenges. It was intended to develop STEM subjects’ furtherly integrating them in active  European citizenship, health, demographic change and wellbeing. Beyond the scientific approach, Literature and Arts were conductors of detailed diachronic analysis of outdoor activities patterns in diverse cultural backgrounds. Other goals of RUSH were the acquisition of key competences, the promotion of innovation and creativity and training through transversal skills, such as critical thinking, creativity, initiative and problem solving. The relevant horizontal primary concern was social and educational value of European cultural heritage, and there were two additional priorities such as open education and innovative practices in a digital era and skill and competence acquisition. Consequently, all the activities have been designed for this purpose and have been distributed and shared on the Etwinning platform. Key contents were integrated within the current curriculum using alternate methodological procedures, such as cooperative learning, learning by doing, individual assignments and the development of cross-curricular activities. Tools were tailored to the activities and the objectives, offering space to student initiatives, implementing educational practices that purposefully stimulated structural meaningful cross-group interaction. Students were challenged by the life skills that are indispensable to become responsible and committed European citizens.They acquired an innovative outlook towards learning and motivation thanks to European relationships. They acquired scientific literacy and key STEM skills focusing on the connection between their lifestyle, health, society and the environment. Furthermore, the English language competence and the use of ICT tools have been improved. They increased their own cultural awareness and expanded their horizons by mobilities and experience. As regards the impact on teachers, it implemented new creative teaching methods and international European links have been established. For the whole educational community the project helped promoting wellness, a healthy lifestyle and above all entrepreneurship under a sustainable perspective and it was a stimulus for a more active and European teaching. We disseminated project results to the local communities, students' families, local authorities, bodies of professionals, City Councils, NPO's. Moreover, collaboration of the five partner schools tried to maximize exposure of the project's activities and results internationally. The sustainability of the project was guaranteed by means of the professional-social bonds created through RUSH. Also it continued through communication and further cooperation on Etwinning, the blogs and other exchanges of ideas affecting correlating issues such as protection of the environment and prevention of social disease, including it all in a more general health education.

2019-1-IT02-KA229-063230.title: European Virtual Business
2019-1-IT02-KA229-063230.summary:
CONTEXT
The XXI Century School has the task of educating young citizens and providing them with those useful and indispensable skills for the transition from the school world to the job world at European and international level.
In this context, the Erasmus + projects and especially those for the exchange of good practices, the experience of the EVB - European Virtual Business project represented for the five partner schools a precious opportunity to learn best practices for education at European level. Entrepreneurship, understood as a set of personal skills and as a mind-set to deal with the inclusion of the young new graduate in the world of work.

TARGETS
The five schools of the EVB partnership have similar fields of study, as they all have the technical-economic sector and classes of students of similar age (14 to 18 years).
Sharing of the school curriculum facilitated the identification of the project objectives which, despite the halt suffered by the project activities due to the the Covid-19 pandemic, remained unchanged; The objectives were:
- improving the quality, innovation and internationalization of school education and training through transnational cooperation
- the dissemination and systemization of open and innovative teaching methods
- the development of professional skills of schools teachers directly and indirectly involved in the project through the promotion of the culture of lifelong and continuous training
- the permeability between the different sectors of education and training
- the development of basic and transversal skills of learners on entrepreneurship education and foreign languages

ACTIVITY'
The achievement of these objectives required a working plan with responsibilities and tasks shared between the various project partners regarding the main project activities which were mainly of three types:
- Promotion, dissemination and enhancement of project activities and results: this was an activity transversal to the various partners and the various project phases and was carried out mainly at local level
- Organization of physical and virtual exchanges: as mentioned, the project stopped after the first exchange organized in Italy in November 2019. As a consequence the second exchange, scheduled for March 2020, was then organized only 18 months later in a virtual way; of the remaining three exchanges, one was held in blended mode, because some partners participated physically and others virtually, and the other two exchanges were only virtually created
- Monitoring of project activities by the coordinator and impact assessment: this activity was also transversal to the various project phases and involved all partners in virtual meetings every six months or so

RESULTS
The most important results were:
1) Creation of a project logo and promotional brochures and depliants
2) Organization of the project's info day at each school
3) N. 5 exchange of group of pupils, of which 1 only physical, 1 blended and 3 virtual
4) Creation of project social blog,  eTwining version of the project, and several web pages on the sites of the partner schools
5) Collection of good practices in entrepreneurship education: during the exchanges the partners were able to exchange their best practices on this topic and on innovative methodologies from "learning by doing" to "cooperative learning", choosing an interdisciplinary approach of various disciplines involved from time to time in the various exchanges.

LONG-TERM EXPECTED BENEFITS
EVB was the first European-level project for our school, the all-encompassing G. Spataro by Gissi: thanks to this first and demanding experience, we have seen a prospect of Europeanisation of the training offer that is actually feasible open up.
An Erasmus + team was set up in the Institute. They took care of the design and implementation and reporting of project activities, acquiring fundamental skills for the development of future projects at European and international level, also in collaboration with local stakeholders.
The goal of creating a European learning space for all five schools in the partnership, after the experience of EVB, appears more easily achievable.

2019-1-IT02-KA229-063342.title: MATHEMATICS WITH GAMES AND FUN IN ALL EUROPE
2019-1-IT02-KA229-063342.summary:
This project focused its activities taking into account the results of the 2017 PISA reports by comparing situations that cause differences in mathematics success. During the preparatory phases, effective activities were carried out to find the main reasons for these varieties in mathematics teaching, what are the sources of these great differences by sharing mathematics programs among the Partners. During the various Mobilities foreseen by this project, collaborative activities, exhibitions and university visits, short films were organized. The project facilitated the active participation of students in each partner Region even if carried out in virtual mode due to the Covid19 pandemic for which some Regions were only able to participate virtually. This gave the participating students the opportunity to use their skills, their free time and their energies to discover, disseminate and share with their peers. The main objective of the project was above all to develop key competences for students, which are essential in knowledge-based mathematics in order to increase the success rate in following the PISA assessments and make the quality of the learning and teaching of mathematics.
 
 ACCOMPLISHED RESULTS:
1. Exchange of knowledge and experience on the teaching and learning of mathematics between people from partner countries
 2. Acquisition of new ways of learning where a learning environment is created in which students can transform the knowledge and experiences learned at local and European level into skills.
 3. Training offer aimed at giving real future career opportunities to project participants
 4. Incentive for young people to take the initiative, be creative, use multimedia tools
 5. Use of new technologies and ICT to put into practice the acquired knowledge and exchange it
 6. Improvement of the language skills of the participants in a real context
 
 SHARING AND DISCLOSURE OF RESULTS:
 a) Website and Facebook page of the project.
b) PISA mini assessments organized on the Internet every year.
c) Math games and mind games played in other countries.
 d) Forum website for mathematics teachers from all over Europe where they can exchange their experiences and find partner countries for their next European projects.
 e) Short films prepared by the participants and memories of this project.
 f) Promotion of a higher education level in order to prevent early school leaving.
 g) Preparation of the project E-book which will be the story of the project as an eTwinning film
 
 IMPACTS OF THE PROJECT:
 The target groups of our project were students and teachers. The students were able to acquire their international point of view on mathematics showing more interest and curiosity towards these activities. They discovered how to use math subjects in their daily life. They gained self-confidence and used their imagination and creativity by participating in the various project activities whether they were in person or online. The teachers got to know
 and evaluate the different teaching methods and materials used for this purpose in other countries. This impact aided their professional development. The most coveted impact of the project was to increase the success of participating countries in PISA assessments and to help young people develop participation and understanding of other countries' mathematics learning methods, so that they can enrich their background. and their success in mathematics in their school life in subsequent years.

2019-1-LT01-KA229-060636.title: MATH, MUSIC AND ART WILL KEEP YOU SMART!
2019-1-LT01-KA229-060636.summary:
Nowadays many teachers have noticed the students' need for a more up-to-date, dynamic and interactive acquisition of skills and competences, especially in the STEAM field. The latest results of national and international tests (PISA, TIMSS) in all partner countries have shown it is necessary to improve students' Math competences. The European Schoolnet (EUN) also claims that STEAM skills are becoming an increasingly important part of basic literacy in today’s knowledge-oriented society, while, on the other hand, the EU needs more scientists and science aware citizens. 
 The primary objective of "MA(R)TH - MATH, MUSIC AND ART WILL KEEP YOU SMART" project is to use the interdisciplinary approach and connect Math (a subject with generally lower students' motivation) with Music and Art (subjects with generally higher students' motivation) to enhance their key competences in those fields. The second objective is to strengthen teachers' profile and raise the level of their professional competences so as to develop innovative teaching methods, take initiative in leadership in education and build capacity to work in transnational projects. Through cooperation with local institutions teachers are to strengthen their own and their students' civic awareness. The third objective is to include ICT knowledge and the working language of the project - English - in project activities so that both students and teachers also increase their digital, linguistic and communication competence.Finally, the same importance is assigned to the objectives of enhancing creativity, integrating students with fewer opportunities in project activities and promoting equality, as well as promoting other European values such as greater understanding of cultural diversity and a positive attitude towards students' and teachers' mobility for education and EU funded projects.
 MA(R)TH project will be presented to approximately 4100 students, teachers and staff, then parents in partner schools from 6 countries (Lithuania, Turkey, Greece, Italy, Macedonia and Croatia) and their local communities. Each school coordinator will form a team of teachers of the subjects the project is based on and students who will carry out the planned project tasks. Students' age is 13-18 and they belong to different cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds. Other participants will be members of local community and experts connected with the topics of Math, Music, Art and ICT.  Parents and members of local government will support the implementation of the project. MA(R)TH activities will include creating presentations, doing interviews, quizzes, questionnaires, writing texts, learning scenarios, drawing pictures, taking photos, composing music, making videos, participating in and holding teacher- student and student-student workshops, taking part in online meetings. Some of the topics to cover will be: fractions and music, Fibonacci series in painting, fractals, math in architecture etc.The project will have a website and a Twinspace where participants will share all created materials.Twinspace chat and online meeting option will also be used for collaboration. Virtual cooperation will be combined with 5 short-term exchanges of groups of pupils and 1 short-term joint staff training event. The short-term joint staff training event to be carried out during the first mobility will provide teachers with necessary competences on how to apply the interdisciplinary approach and use the new ICT tools (GeoGebra, Chrome Music Lab, create and maintain a website) and enable them to share good practices, their know-how, to connect and implement the rest of the project activities successfully.During the 5 exchanges involving students, they will continue to study different aspects of Math - Music - Art connection, develop their ICT and English skills, creativity and critical thinking, participate in workshops, study visits and share intercultural diversity. We believe the most important outcomes will be the fulfillment of the above set objectives.Concrete results students will produce at the end of MA(R)TH project are a depliant,  a GeoGebra e-book containing tasks, students' work, presentations, pictures, workshop learning scenarios and video materials, an e-photo album and a calendar. Impacts will include increased quality of education seen in improved key STEAM competences and basic ICT and language skills of students as well as in strengthened teachers' profile.All participants will also develop greater respect towards diversity and understand the need to promote EU values.Long-term benefits will be the following: increased capacity of partner schools for organizing future EU projects, increased cooperation among members of school teams as well as between schools and local community, new interdisciplinary innovative activities that can be included in school curricula and the availability of all produced materials on Twinspace for future use and upgrade by all eTwinning members.

2019-1-LV01-KA229-060410.title: "Birds have to fly!"
2019-1-LV01-KA229-060410.summary:
This school year saw the completion of the project "Birds have to fly!” which was focused on the enrichment of creativity, cooperation, and knowledge throughout “birds”. Thus, these years will be remembered as a bright, emotional, creative, communication, and knowledge-oriented unique Erasmus+ project years by many students and teachers of partnership schools!
It is a pleasure for me that all the works and creative activities proposed in the project application, the additional local school creative tasks and exhibitions were completed. We were hopeful, focused on the adventure, stepped out of our comfort zone, staged play lets, learned how to search for information and make more use of IT tools. For example, pupils from each partner school wrote the stories in their mother tongue and in English with sequels and illustrations, the following year when they met in the mobility, their stories, using the drama method, were performed in a collaborative process between the participants. Pupils learned two dances related to the theme of birds, it was interesting to see the different performances. Taking part in project work encouraged pupils to be active and built their self-confidence.
The theme of birds was widely sung in songs for every nation. Pupils from each partnership school sang the songs in their mother tongue, then sent their video with the performance of the song, the pupils in other partnership schools could learn it. Moreover, in one of the many meetings on the ZOOM platform, the pupils sang all the songs together in four languages in what turned out to be a positive and emotional concert. This school year, when European countries became "healthier", it was possible to carry out mobility.
During the project, we have designed, crafted, drawn and painted birds in a variety of techniques, the works were regularly exhibited in the Erasmus+ project corner, on the information boards, where they could be seen by the pupils, teachers, school visitors. The exhibitions were documented so that as many people as possible could see what was done, both on the Erasmus+ eTwinning website, on the School' website, and in the local newspapers. There was also bird watching in nature, bird feeders were placed, and pupils had the opportunity to gain more knowledge about bird life. Participants learnt more about the national birds of the partner countries by observing them and listening to ornithologist’s stories.
In the previous year, going to the other countries was impossible, we organized regular meetings on the ZOOM platform. One of the most memorable events was a quiz on birds, where each partnership school had 10 questions on birds. There was a tough competition. The pupils had a great opportunity to be creative, to develop the very important skill of public speaking, presenting their school, thus carrying the name of Jaunjelgava far across Europe, which is now known for its erudite pupils, its warm welcome in Latvia and the modern image of our school as a whole. As a great and motivating incentive for the most hard-working, and interested pupils during the project, they had the opportunity to visit our partner schools, to make new friends while living in host families, thus gaining a great life experience and broadening the horizons. A great added value of the exchange trips is the communication in English.
To do everything planned for the project, a lot of late hours had to be invested to develop dynamic communication and cooperation, organize successful pupils and teacher teams for exchange events, successfully implement all planned exchanges in mobility to other countries, to arrange transport/ accommodation, to arrange project documentation etc. There is joy, alternating with tiredness, and there is satisfaction because the work we have put in has borne fruit in the form of vivid emotions and useful new knowledge. It was a pleasure to have been able to give active pupils from different classes the opportunity to go on an unforgettable trip. These pupils took part in mobility to share the joy of their experience with their classmates, teachers, and parents. The teachers of our school had the opportunity to gain experience for their work and share their experience. The teachers were encouraged by the project coordinator I.Ermansone and were involved in the activities. I am proud of my colleagues who participated. Projects unite and motivate us! We shared our experience in the lessons, pupils told about their school, took part in the educational activities during the week. It was gratifying that we organizing all the exchanges in a very high quality, planned, involving students of different ages in educational activities.
It brings the school and teachers twice as much joy to have the parents of the pupils engaging and helping children to be active, learn well, take part in extracurricular activities, want to learn something new, be more open and talk about their school, and country with pride and confidence.

2019-1-LV01-KA229-060448.title: Sciences and Mathematics into Learning English
2019-1-LV01-KA229-060448.summary:
We want to develop this project in the context of our preoccupations for quality assurance for our education activity. The project is built in accordance with our institutional needs, of all partners: the need to diversify the didactic strategies in order to achieve better results in science and mathematics; the need to improve communication skills in a foreign language. Our objectives are: to improve the skills and competences in the field of mathematics and science, to improve the school results and the results of the semesters and final works (at the end of the end of the final year of the study), to increase the students' motivation to study English, mathematics and sciences, teachers will use the learning by new teaching strategies, developing communication skills in English for all participants, promoting skills related to the values of European citizenship - collaboration, acceptance of diversity, empathy, tolerance, mutual respect.
 6 schools from 6 countries participate in the project. 3 countries are at the first participation in this project. All schools are small schools. 3 of them are from rural areas. Partners are united by institutional features and needs. Will develop the project with students aged 10-14. At the level of the partnership, a common operational plan will be established which will include a common monthly activity. In the first year there will be especially preoccupations about science and in the second year there will be preoccupations mainly for mathematics. In most activities, science will intertwine with mathematics. Teachers will participate in two learning activities and students will meet twice a year.
 For each meeting there is a pre-set theme and organizational details. We want tangible results such as: project signs, studies, portfolios, video, photo albums, project log, blog for students, a project webpage, magazines, brochures. As non-tangible results, we want to have: halving the number of students with poor school results in science and mathematics in each of the partner schools; halving the number of drop-out pupils in each partner school; developing communication skills in a foreign language through direct communication and product development in this language (portfolios, studies, messages ...); teachers' use of modern teaching strategies such as Blended Learning, Content and Language Integrated Learning, flip classroom, peer learning, WebQuest, PBL- learning projects, learning-by-teaching, focus group. We expect a qualitative change at the level of: students' interest in science, mathematics, English; school drop-out; the performance of teachers of mathematics, science, English (materialized performances using techniques and methods leading to the participation of pupils in different projects, activities, regional competitions); community relations (student families will support school in their activities). We expect our students to change their civic
 attitude towards the environment positively because they will also address issues of citizenship interest such as water pollution, air pollution. A clear and well-implemented project develops the school institution (tangible products will also be used in other learning moments, with the other schools increasing the positive image). In this way, all the actors involved in the project will benefit.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages
Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-MK01-KA229-060272.title:
“Building a future” - Cultural Intelligence: The
Essential Intelligence for the 21st Century
2019-1-MK01-KA229-060272.summary:
Context:
 Culture is the fundamental building block of identity and the development of a strong cultural identity
 is essential to children’s healthy, sense of who they are and where they belong.The main idea behind
 the project is to develop awareness among children from an early age that diversity in our world
 make us culturally richer.
 In our country in 2017 year we realized an exploration with a goal to assess the children development
 according to the standards of early education and development as unbreakable tie from the national
 program in the kindergartens.The results has shown that the children from the marginalized families
 are having lower results in these measurements.One of the reasons beside the lower level of the
 parents conscious for active inclusion in the kindergarten is also the inappropriate approach of the
 teachers,by their different cultural identity.That is why there is a need for enhancement the
 competences of the teachers to work with children with different cultural and ethnic background as
 well as program enhancement with contents that will contribute to the children to develop empathy,
 altruism and assertiveness.
 Kindergartens from Croatia and Bulgaria also include children of different cultural backgrounds and
 need to exchange good practices in this domain of action.
 Kindergartens from Italy and Portugal have developed a range of strategies and activities that will
 enable us to make better changes in our program.
 We, primary school teachers, want to learn from each other, present our success stories and our challenges and work together to make a difference in our schools and communities.
 The main goal of the project is cooperation in the field of acquaintance and implementation of
 methods and forms of developing basic skills for children in the social-emotional domain using the
 cultural diversity in the European world. Participants will seek innovative solutions, new forms and
 methods of work which develop Positive Learning Outcomes in children such a: strong sense of
 identity, confident and involved learners, effective communicators. By promoting understanding of
 difference and diversity, early childhood educators will gain skills for teaching strategies and
 techniques which will help them to be more successful in assisting children and their families in
 building positive relationships among each others, with their peers and with their local
 communities.Objectives:
 - To help teachers identify their basic knowledge about cultural diversity and to provide them with
 practical strategies to improve performance when working across cultures.
 - To encourage staff to improve their cultural intelligence and to provide them with tools for working
 more effectively with children from different cultural backgrounds
 -To provide the KG teachers with strategies and tips for creating an inclusive classroom environment
 and teaching a culturally diverse population of children.
 Good practices will be put on paper and we will develop a Guide for educators with game-based activities (а toolkit for early childhood educators on cultural diversity and responding to prejudice) and Materials for parents with tips for encouraging they child to understand and appreciate the different cultures.
 We and our partners want our kindergartens to be more socially inclusive by respecting the
 differences of all the children, where all the children are feeling valued and their basic needs are met.
 Our main goals are:
 - improving the approach of the children and their families from the marginalized groups in the
 program for early child development
 -improving the ability, opportunity and dignity of the those children who are disadvantage on the
 basis of their identity.
 NUMBER AND PROFILE OF THE PARTICIPANTS
 Children: indirect 80 X 5=400 total: 400
 Teachers: Direct 25 X 5=125 indirect 13 X 5=65 total:190
 Administrative Staff: 2 X 5=10
 Families: 150
 Local Community: 100
 Activities:
 C 1 - Including cultural diversity in our setting’s practices( curriculum)
 C2-C4- Including cultural diversity in our day-to-day practices( classroom management);Developing  a
 Guide for educators with game-based activities
 C 5- Celebrating different cultures( building partnership with diverse families) Developing Materials for parents with tips for encouraging they child to understand and appreciate the different cultures.
 Impact:
 All the partners will use the Multicultural Education lessons uploaded on the online platform during the project and after its completion, which means that the material basis of the kindergarten/school will improve. Teachers can develop new courses for children using the materials produced during the project.
 The project will also involve the development of the human resource training, which is beneficial both in the short and in the long run. Teachers will develop professional relationships with their colleagues from other European countries and they will have the chance to develop future project ideas.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-MT01-KA229-051169.title: School Permaculture Garden
2019-1-MT01-KA229-051169.summary:
All the schools involved in this project have the environment at heart. We promote a healthy lifestyle, inclusion and lifelong learning in our endeavour to provide a holistic education to our pupils who come from multicultural backgrounds (including immigrants).
 
 The main objectives of the partnership for permaculture in schools are the following ones:
 • To develop Care of the Earth, environment and People
 • To develop the key competences, such as ITC skills and linguistic competences	
 • To encourage students to cooperate with European partners since early ages
 • To promote a European dimension amongst all participants, develop internationalization and be open-minded.
 • To improve students’ and teachers’ communication, group working skills, the use of English language.
 • To compare methods of teaching and learning, values of education, school organization and curriculum in order to look for innovative ways of teaching and learning and introduce pedagogical innovations.
 • To find a creative approach to special needs / physically impaired students and people in general.
 
 This project will show that Permaculture is much more than environmental awareness or a gardening technique. It’s an ethical design science that assimilates land, resources, people, and nature in ways that supply human needs as well as benefit the environment.
 
 The role of a European school today is to encourage internationalisation. We need to think of a common Europe, be proud of our own culture but at the same time respect the other ones. This is an interdisciplinary project using the subject of permaculture garden in schools to awaken the knowledge on other countries in Europe. It shares knowledge but not in a stereotypical way, it explains and encourages celebration of the unique identity of partner countries but crucially asks children to evaluate these from another's perspective. By working on this project, as well as improving their knowledge on the environment, pupils will improve their skills in geography, history, the arts, foreign languages and knowledge of other cultures.

2019-1-NL01-KA229-060273.title: Cultural Heritage, from prejudice to awareness
2019-1-NL01-KA229-060273.summary:
Context and objectives: 
 
 This project is designed to improve students' critical thinking and their awareness of being an active European citizen. By taking actively part in the project the students will heighten their self-competence and improve their natural science, technical and digital competences. These goals will be achieved when students deal with different topics around the field "Cultural Heritage". It became clear during the planning of this project that there is a lack of awareness among young people about Cultural Heritage in our countries. Instead, there are a lot of prejudices. By studying those and becoming aware of the similarities between our countries, a basis for European citizenship will be created. From that point on, students can research our Cultural Heritage and explore some similarities in intangible, tangible and natural heritage. Furthermore, our project, Cultural Heritage, from prejudice to awareness, aims at creating and expanding awareness of our European identity by creating a digital platform on which citizens of our countries can learn more about our Cultural Heritage. 
 We also hope to achieve an integral educational approach by including practical work rather than an emphasis on theory. Students will get the chance to experience the efficiency of "do-it-yourself" and "learning by doing". 
 
 The project consists of 4 sub-topics to be worked on by all students together for 6 months each: 
 
 1.	Conceptualizing Cultural Heritage
 - Researching prejudices of the partner countries and creating a common framework for our project 
 - Exploring the features of our common European similarities 
 - Constructing a common framework of Cultural Heritage
 - Creating schedules by using the digital tool GOOGLE SKETCHUP 
 - Transnational meeting in Croatia
 
 2.	Exploring Cultural Heritage 
 - Studying the concept of cultural heritage
 - Learning about digital tools through workshops
 - Teaching fellow students about cultural heritage in different countries 
 - Excursion to national heritage sites / the national organization for cultural heritage
 - Transnational meeting in Poland 
 
 3.	Discovering Cultural Heritage 
 - Analyzing the selection processes of cultural heritage 
 - Exploring different cultural aspects for nomination as cultural heritage
 - Developing suggestions for improvements by using GOOGLE SKETCHUP 
 - Meeting with the municipalities / NGOs
 - Transnational meeting in Finland
 
 4. Creating awareness for Cultural Heritage 
 - Planning and conducting activities to improve awareness of cultural heritage 
 - Creating virtual heritage 
 - Transnational meeting in the Netherlands 
 
 Participants: 
 - OMO Scholengroep Bergen op Zoom e.o. (the Netherlands)
 - Siilinjärvi Upper Secondary School (Finland)
 - Strojarska tehnička škola Fausta Vrančića (Croatia)
 - Zespół Szkół Ogólnokształcących i Technicznych im. Marii Konopnickiej w Milówce (Poland)
 Project leaders: Arnold van der Werff (Netherlands), Marina Kevric (Croatia), Merja Mikkonen (Finland) & Anna Witos (Poland)
 16 teachers (4 from each school) 
 108 students from the participating schools, 30 per school in total
 8 students from every school on transnational learning activities 
 
 Methodology: All of our activities will be implemented by a wide range of innovative teaching methods both in and outside of school, incorporating: critical thinking, digital competence, collaboration and team work, communication skills and personal and social responsibility. Constant evaluation and improvement are self-evident. 
 Intended results: 
 - increased feeling of European Citizenship among young people in society. 
 - Greater awareness for the target groups 
 - use and spread of innovative teaching methods 
 - increased personal technological and digital competences and skills

2019-1-NO01-KA229-060163.title: History and its effects on today's youth (HEY)
2019-1-NO01-KA229-060163.summary:
The project History and its Effects of today’s Youth (HEY) is based on the idea that understanding history is crucial relating to develop the present and the future common Europe. A vision is to create a common understanding of how wars and conflicts, extremist views, immigration and migration have a reciprocal effect on one another, and look at how they challenge the way we teach history to our students. Each country has its own dramatic past that effects how history is thought in classrooms. The partner schools in HEY is selected based on a desire on bringing a broad range of historical events into the project. Experience in former Erasmus+ projects and eTwinning are other wanted qualifications.
 The Croatian partner brings experience in several strategic partnerships and eTwinning to the project. They will arrange a JSE(C1) to develop new teaching methods for the project. Croatia is a country with a dramatic past and they will bring their experiences in teaching their nation’s history into the project. Objectives for C1 is modernization of education. 20 teachers from all five partner schools will participate on C1. Students will take part in preparatory activities and on TwinSpace. 
 The Spanish partner brings experience in several strategic partnerships and eTwinning to the project. The Spanish history of establish democracy after years under General Franco’s govern will be the starting point for the SLE (C4) in Spain. Objectives to be met in C4 is active citizenship, democratic values and fundamental rights.
 The Cypriote partner has some experience in strategic partnership. As Cyprus is a divided island, intercultural dialogue and social inclusion will be the objectives of their SLE (C3). Students and teachers will both practice and experience the value of intercultural dialogue.
 Greek partner brings the present situation of the ongoing refugee crisis into the project. Rhodes is a historically multicultural society and the present situation will be analysed considering this tradition. Non-discrimination, social, civic and intercultural competences are the objectives to be met in the SLE (C5) in Greek. 
 Norway is the coordinator of this project and the less experienced partner in European funded projects. Objectives for the SLE(C2) are critical thinking and media literacy. To meet these objectives students and teachers will use the terror attack on Utøya, right-wing extremism and hatred in social media as basis for developing new understanding and new skills.
 The project has two main target groups. The first, and most important is young people who will be the next generation of decision makers in their local society, in their countries and in Europe. To reach out to a whole generation is of course an unrealistic dream, but as school-based project, we have a great opportunity to challenge young people’s minds to see the benefits of democracy, co- working and multi-ethnic and multi-cultural societies. If we openly discuss our challenges, are critical to easy solutions provided by populist politicians, and are humble to our differences, we will go far. The dissemination will happen continuously through the whole project period and will continue in the hearts and mind of the involved students and schools. 
 
 To reach out to students, teachers have a key role. Therefore, teachers are the other main target of the project. Teachers will participate in all the activities. These teachers will thus have an obligation to share the results and developed methods with their colleagues. The results will be published on the platforms they use on a daily basis.
 For all the SLEs (C2-C5) three students, one teacher and one participating person wil travel. That will make a group of 12 students and 8 adults/teachers to each SLE. This amount of students and teachers will make a manageable group to work with the planned program together with students and teachers from the hosting school. 
 The Cypriote team will administrate the project’s web site and students blog. All digital products from the activities will be shared on the web site and on eTwinning. The Croatian and Spanish team will be responsible for eTwinning activities and support the other partners. Evaluation will be carried out after each JSE and SLE (C1-C5) and at the end of the project period. The Greek team will initiate the evaluation activities. 
 All the products that has been developed during the project will be included in the HEY ebook. This ebook will be shared both locally at the partner schools, nationally in the partner countries and internationally through eTwinning and the project’s web site.

2019-1-PL01-KA229-064825.title: One way ticket
2019-1-PL01-KA229-064825.summary:
Space travels are not a dream anymore. We can do that anytime. But we can get ONLY one way ticket... to another planet. So before we travel we have to collect everything which is valuable for us, living in outer space,  for future generation...Participants of this project will travel light into space - just with their cultural heritage - as it is the  mainspring of humanity.
 The objectives of the project are:
 1. to encourage young people to discover and engage with European's cultural heritage as it has a big role in building the future of Europe and shapes our identities and everyday lives and to reinforce a sense of belonging to a common European space;
 2. to develop digital skills with the focus on the confident, critical and responsible use of digital technologies for collecting information and learning;
 3. to develop literacy skills - with the focus on the use of digital and online media to communicate and to produce, find, and evaluate information to meet educational  demands;
 4. to improve foreign languages skills.
 Results:
 - tangible- .a selection of:   1. Key events in European History (European timeline),  2. European artworks (European Art Museum album),   3. European songs (A European top chart and a recital of European Music-DVD),  4.  places of natural beauty of Europe (European snaps - selection of postcards),  5. European dances (Let's dance European dances-DVD),  6. Forgotten European dishes (European Cookbook of forgotten recipies  ), 7. It happened here - telling local stories, memories, legends (booklet), 8. monuments, buildings  representative of Europe (Replicas of most famous European  buildings-exhibitions, ppt );  project website on eTwinning.
 - intangible- learning, talking to people  about a range of traditional craftmanship, expressions, practices,  dances, cuisine that Europeans value  provide young people with an automatic sort of belonging and unity within a group/country/the EU while allowing for a better understanding of previous generations and a history of where they originated from.
 
 Priorities:
 - Through cherishing  cultural heritage students will discover and start inter-cultural conversation about what they have in common. This project enables its participants to become closer to and more involved with their cultural heritage. It's important because it should be  preserved  and passed on to future generations. It fosters unity and active citizenship. 
 - In this project  relevant basic skills and key competences, which young people will need to succeed in their future life and career, will be developed. Skills such as critical thinking, problem solving, team work, communication and negotiation skills, analytical skills, creativity, and intercultural skills  will be improved in  the project activities.

2019-1-PL01-KA229-064826.title: A school of democracy - we know our rights and duties
2019-1-PL01-KA229-064826.summary: The project started in October 2019 with the email contacts of the teachers involved in the project. In all parter schools the project was announced to the students of the age of 11 -15 and some of them decided to join it. As the formal issues – signing the Grant Agreement, transfering the money – took some time, the teachers decided to postpone the C1 LTT activites and meet in the Croatian partner school in March 2020. Such a change gave the students more time to prepare presentations about the partner schools and about the towns where they live, concentrating on the question: Who rules in your school? In your town? All the students were very well prepared for the C1 LTT activities and they did their best to fulfill the tasks. Making their presentations they broadened their knowledge about the small societies they are part of, understood their role in them and realised what responsible citizenship means. Answering the two questions in their presentations they could see how important in every society democracy is. Moreover the students could observe some events connected with the presidential election in Croatia, which was another lesson of democracy. Unfortunately after the C1 LTT activities we could not continue the project because of the coronavirus pandemic and the lockdown. The project coordinator applied for an additional year to implement the project and to achieve its objectives. The additional year was accepted but the project could not be restarted immediately. The restrictions caused by the pademic did not allow the students to travel to the partner schools. Waiting for better conditions the teachers tried to rebuilt the project potential as the students involved in the C1 LTT activities had left the school. New groups were invited  and introduced to the main objectives and tasks of the project. As the restrictions caused by the pandemic were not lifted, the partner schools decided to continue the project with the virtual C2 LTT activities, organized by the coordinating school in Poland in March 2022. The tasks planned for this part of the project had to be modified and adjusted to new conditions. The teachers chose Teams as a platform useful for the project. The Croatian and Polish students had already experienced activities on Teams while learning online but this platform was new for the Italian and Portuguese groups, so they needed some additional activities to get used to it. The programme of the C2 activities was implemented in such a way that the students worked in their schools for 2-3 hours on such topics as campaign and election in their schools. Then presented their results on Teams, discussed and exchanged ideas. Despite some small technical difficulties at the very beginning the students worked very effectively. Nevertheless they missed the real contacts with students from the partner schools. Soon after the C2 activities the pandemic was over and to the students‘ delight we could continue the project with real meetings. The teachers decided to act very quickly and the C3 LTT activities were organized in the Portuguese school in April 2022. The project work started on 25th April, a very important day in the history of Portugal. On this day the Portuguese people celebrated the 48th anniversary of Revolução dos Cravos, the revolution that brought democracy to Portugal. It was another lesson of history and a picture of the nation fighting for democracy. The main tasks of the C3 LTT activities were designing the area around the school and write a petition  addressed to the local authorities. During the meeting with the Mayor of Braga the petition was handed and the students could take part in the real democratic activity and feel like active citizens. The first day of the C4 LTT activities was 23rd May, a very important date of remembrence and recollection of great personalities of Italian Magistrature: Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino, the two extraordianary men fighting for democracy and legality.  There was another meeting  organized, this time with the Mayor of Bagheria and the students‘ petition was about the school canteen. The main task planned for this phase of the project was a debate. After a very clear preparation the students presented excellent work and the debate taught them how to solve problems in a democratic way. In June 2022 additional LTT activities were organized in the Polish partner school as a complement to the virual C2 LTT activities.  On 28th June the students went to Poznań. It was 66th anniversary of protests against communism and demonstrations in Poznań in 1956. The students could learn about the Polish way to democracy and how the citizens pay tribute and commemorate the victims of those days. The main task of the C5 LTT activities was to sum up and evaluate the whole project. Moreover the students could enjoy the time together – the element of the project that was missing during the virtual C2 LTT activities.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2019-1-PL01-KA229-064897.title: Innovative methods of teaching foreign languages with the use of information and communication technologies
2019-1-PL01-KA229-064897.summary:
The project „Innovative methods of teaching foreign languages with the use of information and communication technologies” was created on the basis of all three schools’ needs that want to participate in a three-side partnership: Poland, Croatia and Italy. The main purpose of the project is exchanging good practices between schools.
The detailed objectives are:
-to improve teachers’ skills in using innovative methods of teaching foreign languages with the use of ICT 
-to develop students’ motivation to learn foreign languages
-to increase efficiency in the process of foreign languages learning with the use of ICT
-to improve skills of using ICT and taking action which will have a positive impact on preparing  students for living in a society.
 250 students, at the age 12-15 years old, will participate in the project. These children want to develop their language skills and they are interested in ICT. There will be 12 students from each country taking part in mobilities. This group will consist of pupils who have good grades at school, disabled children, children having poor living conditions and children with specific learning difficulties. All participants will be supported by teachers from each partnership’s school. 
We have prepared a detailed schedule in order to achieve all the goals. The schedule contains:
-teachers’ meetings in each of 3 countries which are involved in project. During the mobilities teachers will share their knowledge and experience in using ICT in innovation foreign language teaching and learning. Teachers will also have opportunity to take part in open classes which will be based on innovative teaching of English
-students' mobilities when they will have a chance to take part in classes conducted by teachers/ specialists from host country with the use of  innovative methods of teaching foreign languages 
-local activities which will take place between mobilities that aim at good communicating between partners, managing the project and achieving the goals.
Partnership schools will introduce their own methods of teaching foreign languages, which are:
-teaching English with the use of robots coding – POLAND
-teaching English with the use of interactive board - Croatia
-teaching English with the use of digital applications - Italy
During activities related to the project a lot of educational tools will be created. The tools will be used by the teachers from partnership’s schools. These will be: virtual guide, leaflets and brochures with the teaching and learning foreign language methods, classes scripts, photos, multimedia presentations, digital stories, robots, video guides, films from the guide lessons, padlet presenting the whole project, blog with some advice for the teachers. The project's results will be presented on: eTwinning platform, School Education Gateway, Erasmus+ platform. The products will be posted on our schools and local authorities' websites. They will be translated into English, Croatian, Italian and Polish languages .
The effects of the project will be: development of key competences mainly communicating in English, development of concentration, reading and writing, managing in everyday life, development of teachers’ work with new methods, increase students’ achievement connected with ICT. The permanent result of the project will be cultivation of Geography and Culture knowledge, increase students' social skills such as: working in groups, tolerance, creativity, ability to use the knowledge during practical activities. Thanks to digital technologies there will be a progress in students' communization proces. They will be open to European digitalization. All the innovative methods will be used as new solutions not only by our schools, but also by other schools and organisations connected with education.

2019-1-PL01-KA229-064906.title: CLASSIC AGAIN
2019-1-PL01-KA229-064906.summary: Primary School Jana Pawła II in Kleosin together with the partner schools: Ivan Cankar Primary School, I.C. Pacifici Sezze-Bassiano and IES Cantely, have completed a joint 35-month school cooperation project (oryginally the project was planned for 23 months but it was extended because of pandemics). The goals of The CLASSIC AGAIN project have been reached i. e. improving students and teachers' English communication skills, developing reading skills (reading comprehension, the reception of culture texts), creative writing). Project activities have increased  students' motivation to learn and the quality of school work has improved. The mobilities helped to build the attitude of tolerance and openness towards other nations, religions and  understanding cultural diversities. Travelling abroad and hosting people from other countries gave the students a unique opportunity to practise their English skills and to gain knowledge of the history, culture, literature and customs of the partner countries.International project activities  improved students' soft skills and teamwork skills. Sudents' social activity has increased. The partner schools increased implementing innovative activating teaching methods (drama, visual and art techniques, ICT tools). The schools enriched the offer of extracurricular activities, such as creative writing classes, English Language Communication classes, drama classes and ICT classes. During the project the eTwinning platform was used.  The idea behind the project was a creative approach to teaching language,reading competences using the methods of drama and ICT. The participants of the project chose a literary work and through various forms of expression (music, dance, drama) and ICT, they developed a new approach to it. They created modern scenarios, radio recordings, videos and time-lapse photos. During the final project meeting,  the students and teachers from the partner countries, together with the local authorities, parents and teachers from other schools,  had a chance to watch the presentations about the project activities and the final spectacle ( "Some memories from Soplicowo" - "Wspomnienia z Soplicowa", a video recorded with the use of the 'green screen' technology - by Polish students, extracts from 'Don Juan Tenorio' - Spain,'Hlapic' - an audio from Croatia and 'Divine Comedy' - Italy - online).With the use of new technologies, promotional posters, a film, a photo gallery and a blog of the project: CLASSIC AGAIN were created. During mobilities (84 students in total) students  took part in the creative writing workshops in Croatia, online drama workshops - Italy, ICT workshops in Spain and English Language Communication workshops in Poland. The aim of youth exchange was to improve communication skills in English, learn new skills from each other  and get to know the culture of the partner countries. We have proved that schools can learn in an interdisciplinary and creative way. We also learnt about literary works of art from the partner countries which are part of our common European heritage. Communication in mother tongue  (spoken and written), foreign languages ​​and learning skills, cultural awareness and expression are the competences emphasized by the European Council and the European Parliament, necessary for functioning in a knowledge-based society and the participants of the CLASSIC AGAIN project have become aware of that. The project was based on modern and effective methods and forms to develop reading interests. Drama workshops which were held online sensitised students and let them open to emotions but also showed the strength of  teamwork and the possibilities brought by new technologies. The project, developed with partner schools, has enhanced the learners' language and reading competences, has motivated them to learn and contributed to their further self-development. The project was also addressed to those students who had problems with learning or who were in a difficult family situation, and it was them who benefited the most and spread their wings. Taking part in the project has strengthened their self-esteem and motivated them to study.The activities took into account the needs of schools and were planned to improve the quality of education and the development of the students' competences.The finale of the school's cooperation within the framework of the project was the presentation of a work belonging to the classics of the literature of a given nation in a creative  way using modern technology in the national language and in English. The exchange of experience between teachers from partner schools resulted in the change of the existing learning styles and strenghtened the teachers' status.The teachers gained additional skills necessary to work with students in the area of ​​shaping students' key competences and the use of innovative methods and forms of work. As a part of the project, scenarios /lesson plans  using new methods and work tools were developed and have been displayed on the school website and the result dissemination platform.

2019-1-PL01-KA229-064941.title: EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATION - COMMUNICATION SKILLS
2019-1-PL01-KA229-064941.summary:
This project focusing on the subject of "EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATION - COMMUNICATION SKILLS” united 3 European schools from Poland, Romania and Turkey.
 Good communication is at the heart of our social relationships and leads to an increased tendency towards acts of kindness and consideration, making people more inclined to offer their help and support.
 Communication skills are also a prerequisite for the successful inclusion of teenagers of different ages and from different socio-cultural backgrounds. 
 It is becoming increasingly important that students are familiar with how, when and where to express opinions and address people of differing social standings in varying circumstances. 
 A strong grasp of these key skills  proved to be essential in their search for fulfilling employment in a century where human connections are becoming increasingly vital.
 The project team acknowledged the value of providing students with an education that places a high value on the development of good communication skills as a means to vastly improve their employment opportunities. 
 The main aim of this project was to significantly contribute to this process.
 The specific project objectives were: 
 - to raise awareness about communication and its problems among 250 students coming from 3 EU schools over a two and a half year period
 - to observe the communication process among students from 3 EU schools
 - to enhance students communication skills through the exchange of personal and cultural experiences in a variety of key areas. Such as presentation skills, cross-cultural communication, public speaking, and inter-cultural communication
 - to encourage students to use ICT to increase the impact and reach of their communications.
 The project was designed to incorporate the following four sub-stages: 
 - Verbal & Non-verbal Communication
 - Barriers to Communication
 - Visual Communication
 - Digital Communication.
 These sub-stages  helped us produce the following concrete results: 
 - questionnaires
 - Erasmus+ corners
 - logo of the project
 - presentations of the project partners
 - 1 silent theatre play
 - 1 e-booklet
 - 3 Time Capsule Messages Boxes
 - 3 presentations “Communicating for Understanding”
 - 1 common song
 - 1 common calendar
 - 1 exhibition “Create to Communicate”
 - 3 digital stories “My country’s contribution to the European cultural heritage”
 - 1 travel manual
 - 2 webpages for the project
 - promotional materials such as flyers and bookmarks
 - A DVD of the project
 The project was run for two and a half  school years and there was one short-term joint staff training event in the PL, one short-term exchange of groups of pupils in  RO and three online working meetings of groups of pupils organised by TR, RO and PL.
 The project involved students between the ages of 12 and 15 years, teachers, the local community, stakeholders and the local media. 
 A total number of 250 students, 50 students per school, were directly involved in the project, attending activities organised at a local level, from which 120 students (24 students per school)  attended the international meetings (one short-term exchange of groups of pupils in  RO and three online working meetings of groups of pupils organised by TR, RO and PL) along with 40 teachers (8 teachers per school).
 Students  participated in a variety of team building activities such as city games, blindfolded games and problem-solving tasks which helped participants to realize how they currently express themselves and the importance of accuracy and clarity when communicating.
 This direct interaction with fellow EU students along with the production of presentations, group activities, artistic moments (prepared for the official openings), and intercultural activities helped participants to understand more fully how people communicate differently in other EU schools. 
 All students communication skills were enhanced as they were given the opportunity to exchange personal and cultural experiences, develop their presentation skills, become more competent and confident whilst public speaking and develop both cross and inter- cultural communication skills.
 We cannot ignore the long-term benefits of this partnership on the development of our schools. 
 It should be mentioned that the school curricula will be more international for all schools and all generations of students to follow, the quality of the educational process will be enhanced, the schools individual development plans will be advanced and the image of all schools as forward thinking international institutions will be improved at a local, regional and national level.
 Cooperation between three EU countries will contribute to the appreciation of each other’s national values and the educational importance of promoting the EU’s strong cultural heritage.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2019-1-PL01-KA229-064967.title: Sharing the natural and cultural heritage of our region
2019-1-PL01-KA229-064967.summary: Sharing the nature and culture heritage was the project that connected two very interesting countries. Croatia and Poland. During the project students had the opportunity to present their regions in terms of its value and diversity of the natural and geographical environment. In addition, students shared the knowledge concerning culture and areas in which they live. Project tasks were accomplished by performing presentations, quizzes, photo reports, videos, interviews and participation in different trips. The project was carried out in English language using ICT. All activities were shared with partner schools on the eTwinning platform. The platform was also used to maintain constant contact and some live sessions. By implementing the project, students discovered many similarities and differences in the natural environment of their countries. Participation in the project allowed to improve language skills and overcome barriers. It aroused interest not only in science and geography, but also in the culture of European countries. It contributed to increasing the awareness of European values ​​and tolerance. Additionally, participation in the project improved the quality of work at school and contributed to the promotion of the school both in the local community and in Europe. Participating in the project definitely enhanced the education quality, introduced the international component in learning proces, provided greater interest in learning science and geography subjects, gave the opportunity not only to discover different country but also to explore its nature. The students learnt about their immediate environment and compared the results with those of another country, raising awareness of the political and geographical role of their town in the country and the European Union. The students developed their language competences and the staff was motivated to take new actions for the development of their students. The obtained results were made public through the website created on the e-Twinning platform, YouTube and posted on the Erasmus + Results Platform.
