2019-1-RO01-KA229-063004.title: STart-EU-Up!
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063004.summary:
The skills and the competences that young people need in the present time change everyday. They have to be able to adapt to the labor market which is constantly evolving.School has to prepare its students for the labor market, to ensure they gain skills and competences that go beyond the regular competences provided by teaching the regular curriculum.Entrepreneurial skills will contribute to the employability of young people in particular, as well as supporting a new business creation.The main goal of our project is to develop these skills for teachers and students. On the other hand, we intend to raise awareness on the importance of local economy. We want to link the cultural heritage to the world of business and commerce. We intend to do this by emphasizing the ways to promote local products as a way not only to develop local economy, but also to keep the cultural background and traditions alive. We will  find ways to link the past to the present by reinventing six local products and make them suitable for nowadays markets. The students must use their creativity to promote one local product across Europe. The students will work according to a strict timetable and in accordance with the project methodology. There are a few steps we want to take in developing the transnational company:
 - research on the product 
 - find the potential customers
 - carry surveys and studies on the local consumption habits 
 - create the virtual company which markets six products. We will be able to develop this company after having meetings with local businessmen, entrepreneurs, NGOs, Chambers of Commerce and other such entities. These can teach students about the legal and administrative procedures when starting a business, about the whole business principles they have to follow in order to be successful.
 There are educational objectives as well. We aim at promoting equality and inclusion among our students by including students with different difficulties into the carrying out of the activities, promoting European values and citizenship.We also aim at promoting a comprehensive approach to language teaching and learning and ICT use. It will prove that the topic of entrepreneurial education can be taught interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary. Moreover, this project encourages the cooperation between educational institutions and local business environment. We will create a strong connection between our school and the local business environment and the parents.
 We also intend to develop basic skills in an innovative way. We will encourage teamwork, leadership, time management, risk management, project management, self esteem in our students, multiculturalism, respect for diversity, inclusion and equity, project-based learning, creativity, cooperative learning and teaching, oral and written communication in English, cultural awareness, design.
 We will develop a series of final products, both tangible and intangible.We will create reports and surveys, brochures, commercials into the local media, videos posted on youtube, ebook with the steps we take and final products, an eTwinning digital book. We will work on the designing of these products during the six project meetings hosted by the countries involved. During these meetings we will also prepare fairs of the products to introduce it to the local people, do research and presentations about consumerism and work on developing one department in the company at a time.
 On the long term our project aims to bring up students who are well prepared for the entrepreneurial world and for the employment. We are sure that the competences and skills developed by this project will decrease early school drop-out, decrease youth unemployment among our students. As a long term objective, we expect to create young entrepreneurs in the six partner countries. Our schools will incorporate good practices , new methods and new learnings in their curriculum. With these new learnings teachers will be able to educate the students as to become competent entrepreneurs with employability skills.  Our project offers an example of cooperative project -based learning, starting from situations as close to reality as possible, involving students, teachers, parents and the whole local community.
 During the two years of project, links between teachers, students and local business entities will be created. These links will ensure the project sustainability and continuation. There will be local/ regional/national projects which will follow this project.Teaches will continue collaboration with their partners, sharing results and good practices. They will use virtual meetings and the eTwinning platform. Students will maintain the friendships they created via social networks. Schools and local business entities will find new ways to collaborate and develop new projects together.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2019-1-RO01-KA229-063057.title: The Power of Understanding
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063057.summary:
Studying the PISA test results and analyzing the situation in their schools the teachers of 6 partner schools from Romania,Spain,Portugal,Cyprus,Croatia and Lithuania noticed that a large number of students have low learning outcomes and sometimes absenteeism and early school leaving because they don’t understand the literary and non-literary texts and they have not developed critical thinking,they have not the capacity to solve new things,they are not taught to think freely on new issues.More of them learn as simply "robots".
 The project “The Power of Understanding” proposes an exchange of experience through which to identify new methods of teaching and learning in a new form of extracurricular activities of pupils, in clubs. 
 The general objective of partnership is to improve students ‘competences and level of understanding of literary and non- literary texts in order to raise their success rate and avoid early school leaving. 
 In project will be involved about 30 teachers of different subjects and min.300 pupils aged 11 to 15 years old,of which min. 240 students have difficulties in understanding of texts and about 60 students with good learning outcomes,they will act as mentors. In each partner school will be 5 clubs with max.13 students on different domains, “The magic of the word”(mother tongue, foreign languages),“Traveling in time and space”(history/geography),“Ecology club”,“The little journalist”,”We are European citizens”(European culture and civilization).The clubs will work  as extracurricular activities and their activities will be based on interactive methods such storytelling,role play,theatre,comics, etc.The club “The little journalist”will involve the mentors,they will be“the voice”of the pupils from clubs. 
 There will be 5 transnational learning activities and a transnational staff training  activity.Each transnational learning activity for pupils will be focused on the activities from a club.In Romania,the students will participate at“The magic of the word”club where they will learn about national folk tales and traditional holidays of partner countries; in Croatia the learning activities will be carried out within the“Ecology club”where the students will learn about protected animals and plants in each country,in Spain they will learn about national legends within the club“Traveling in time and space”, in Cyprus the students will have the opportunity to come across various cultures and civilizations giving emphasis on their eating habits within the club“We are European citizens “and in Lithuania the students will take interviews,will make exercises of writing of articles for newspapers within the club“The little journalist”.The transnational activity from Portugal "New teaching- learning methods centered on understanding the text and forming critical thinking" will bring together teachers from all partner schools  who will exchange experience on the new methods that have been used in the clubs on different domains, methods that have been successful among the students from the target groups.
 We expect that through activities to develop the understanding competencies of literary & non-literary texts to min. 40 students/partner school,to form the ability of understanding texts in the daily life of min 40 students/partner school,to develop to min. 40 students/partner school new reading and writing comprehension skills, in order to be able to use them in everyday life, to improve the learning outcomes of min. 40 students/ partner school, to raise awareness among at least 300 students from the six partner schools about the importance of understanding reading and developing critical thinking for lifelong learning and the last but not least, to develop for about 300 students' cooperation an collaboration skills, tolerance and initiative, increasing self-esteem and motivation for learning, as well as friendship between pupils from partner schools.During the activities each partner school will edit a magazine“Words” with results of the work from clubs.The pupils from “The little journalist” club will present significant moments of clubs activities on the students’ blog and towards the end of project the teachers will gather all activities plans,methods,tests, analyses,good practice examples in the guide“The Power of Understanding”,guide which will be used in the future activities for other target groups.From beginning we will initiate and develop the project in eTwinning space where we will ensure the visibility of our activities and results from partner school,at international level, were we will initiate international conferences aims to ensure the meetings of students and teachers from partner schools before the transnational learning activities.Through this transnational exchange of experience the schools will achieve the development of all theirs members by promoting personal, academic and professional growth.

2019-1-RO01-KA229-063063.title:
Only the sky is the limit for open hearts! -
SOLIDARITY FOR EQUALITY
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063063.summary:
"One child, one book, one teacher, One pen can change the world" Malala Yousafzai (Speech before the United Nations, July 12, 2013)
 The school should not be focused just on knowledge, but on relationships.The school must be a creative place for new relationships. School is the only place where children can learn what coexistence is.Many situations of inequality, poverty, and injustice are signs of not only the deep lack of fraternity but also the absence of a culture of solidarity.
 Regardless of how much is being discussed or of how many activities are undertaken in schools, it is a fact that the inclusion of students who are the margins of the educational process for various reasons is still the main challenge and problem in all partner schools and in the schools from the  European countries.
 The project is designed to explore the diversity by working on the inclusion of students with disabilities or other vulnerable social groups. Solidarity involves the development of empathy, tolerance, communication, and social skills. According to different conduct researches, in the past decades, the students in our schools have been increasingly drifting away from these values. This contributes to reducing the intellectual and social development of students, which is a great loss to European values. With this project, we want to encourage every student to express himself, and give everyone equal chances. This project is also a good occasion to understand different identities, to be tolerant and to recognize that a wide range of cultures can cohabit. Discovering diversity will enrich everyone’s education and will play an essential part in understanding and accepting each other. The activities aimed by the project will enable students to socialize, learn more about each other, develop empathy, tolerance, communication, social and cultural skills. The planned activities are related to school curriculum (music, art, literature, sport, ICT etc.) The students will have a major role in the implementation of the activities and will enable them to develop their own personal skills and abilities. They will raise their self-esteem and will develop emotional intelligence, empathy, and solidarity.
 One of the main aims is to raise awareness of our own cultural identity, to bring together the common European cultural values as a basis for our coexistence, to feel culture as an enrichment of one's own life and to improve the existing inter cultural teaching.
 The 6 participating schools from Romania, Spain, Poland, Croatia and The Republic of North
 Macedonia, want to involve approximately 1000 participant students (150 direct participants) aged 10-15.
 They will participate in the project approximately 100 teachers (50 direct participants), 10 reprezentants administrative staff, 250 parents, representatives of NGOs and social-cultural organizations, other members of the local community, students and teachers from neighbouring schools. 
 The objectives of the project are:
 1.Increasing emotional maturity, emotional literacy, and empathy of our students.
 2. Developing and emphasizing lifelong values in our students, the value of solidarity (greater sensitivity to the problems of inequality among people and to social marginalization, their commitment to social and educational inclusion).
 3. Encouraging self-esteem in young people - love and respect for oneself is the source of any other kind of love and respect for the other.
 4. Creating a positive school climate where students will take care of each other.
 METHODOLOGY:
 a) Project meetings: demonstrative lectures, presentations, workshops, lectures, round tables, monitoring and evaluation of activities, filling in questionnaires; on-line meetings, 
 b) Student exchanges: learning from experiences, classes, workshops, work in groups or pairs, presentations, lectures, discussions on the topic of meetings, round tables, visits, various art activities, studies, monitoring and evaluation of activities, filling in questionnaires, gamification as an educational method;
 BASIC PRODUCTS  : 
 - e-book, with life stories (attached to a website with free access to the public)
 - project web site - project materials - photos, videos, a detailed description of good practices 
 - as product we will establish Volunteer Clubs at each partner school
 - brochure and leaflets
 -manual for emotional literacy as an additional tool to the program for psycho-social intervention and
 better social inclusion of students.
 LONG -TERM BENEFITS OF PROJECT: 
  - enable students to explore issues of diversity in our society, prejudices, stereotypes about gender, age disability, religion and culture, and promote a sense of tolerance in school and in society
 - make them aware of local and global issues and highlight global responsibility
 -examples of activities for acquiring emotional competences among the students who promote the socio-emotional climate in the classroom and in school, thus promoting and achieving learning.

2019-1-RO01-KA229-063088.title: Tackling Early Leaving - Out of Box Education
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063088.summary:
Bearing in mind the objectives of the Europe 2020 Strategy to reduce early school leaving to less then 10%, the European Priorities in the national context, as announced by the National Agency from Romania and the national statistical data regarding this topic from Romania (18.1%), Spain (18.3%), Italy (14%) and Bulgaria (12.7%) (Eurostat - Statistics explained, 2018), our project decided to tackle early school leaving (ESL),  being mindful of its significant social and economical consequences for students, as well as for the economy and the society as a whole.  
 The objectives of our project are:
 1. To develop 3 skills that prevent students to become early school leavers (decision making, problem solving and effective communication) for 
 1 000 students from 5 partner schools.
 2. To improve 1 000 students' self-esteem and self-efficacy from 5 partner schools.
 3. To raise the awareness of 1000 parents from 5 partner schools regarding early school leaving.
 4. To develop one model of good practice regarding the effective prevention of early school leaving.
 5. To strengthen the capacity of 400 teachers to prevent ESL, whilst promoting participatory approaches, game based learning and ICT - based methodologies.
 The participants who will benefit directly are: 1000 students (with disadvantaged backgrounds and fewer opportunities, who face personal, social, family, economic or school-based problems), 1000 parents from 5 partner schools and 418 teachers from the local community.
 Our project aims to offer an innovative and creative approach to ESL, stimulating the students to engage in more attractive formal and non-formal education, in order to reach the desirable level of knowledge, skills and competence and to increase their commitment to quality, as well as their interest to learn, achieve and become active and responsible members of our society, actively engaged in the labour market. We plan to encourage students to develop personally and socially, with a particular focus on their self-esteem and self-efficacy in order to become more resilient, aiming to address the identified problem by using a structural, school based and person centered strategy that involve: a) to raise students' aspirations and to motivate them to develop personally and socially, b) to encourage a proactive multi-agency approach to ESL, c) to increase parental involvement in motivating and supporting the students and d) to strengthen the teachers' capacity to work with potentially school leavers and to offer a more attractive teaching and learning environment, using participatory approaches, game based learning and gamification  and ICT-based methodology. The project will support the students to increase their commitment to quality, to learn from peers and teachers from European Union, becoming more tolerant and flexible and accepting diversity, to embrace positive role-models, to raise their aspirations and to develop 3 skills that will prevent them to become early school leavers. Furthermore, our project offers a complex and innovative approach to ESL, involving students, parents, teachers, relevant stakeholders and members of the local community, aiming to focus on the students' needs, interests and personality, as well as on the improvement of the teachers, the stakeholders and the parents' knowledge and skills, that will help them to prevent ESL and to respond more effectively to this problem, decreasing on the long term the risk of poverty and social exclusion, whilst promoting inclusive education for all, irrespective of race, color, religion, age, national origin, sex, economical status and disability. 
 The school partners will become known in their communities for their qualitative involvement and commitment to prevent effectively ESL and to work together with other partners from private, public or non-governmental sector in order to offer a proactive multi-agency approach to ESL. The project's results will be disseminated in the local community and the parents and the students' trust in the partner schools will increase significantly as they will prove during the project's implementation that they are committed to qualitative standards in education and they make significant efforts to improve the teaching style and the educational services that they offer. As a result of that, more students will become interested to be enrolled in the partner schools and more teachers will seek to join our professional teams. The project will also help the teachers from the partners schools to gain more experience working in an European environment that is constantly changing, which will help them to gain more knowledge and skills and to become more flexible on the labour market, finding new jobs if needed or contributing more to their school's strategic development. The partner schools will be more willing and prepared to coordinate or to work in partnership with other schools from European Union in order to solve other identified problems.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-RO01-KA229-063187.title: Say NO to violence and discrimination by games
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063187.summary:
In schools,teachers and students cooperate,develop professionally,and all need to feel safe.Unfortunately,discrimination,harassment and aggression are present in schools,although there is legislation to counteract these phenomena and to provide safety and comfort.
 To reduce the number of cases of violence and discrimination,partner schools must work together to find ways and means of eliminating these behaviors.Schools will share experiences,good practices,similarities and differences between prevention plans.The authorities' involvement in addressing these issues will be analyzed.By implementing this project we want to share our experience and acquire new knowledge,by comparing prevention plans in partner schools to help children.We chose the topic as a result of the problems in schools.Our goal is to promote games in close connection with friendly attitude,harmony and continuous tolerance,with the development of communication skills,teamwork and elimination of violence and discrimination,responding to the challenges set by the Europe 2020 Strategy.Since children love games,they are willing to invest more time and effort,so they'll learn better when being involved actively in the game than in  classroom activities.The exchange of experiences and practices allows us to observe good examples and apply them to our schools.We want our students to be aware of the negative effects of violence and discrimination and to help them tolerate, respect and accept each other,to create a friendly atmosphere in our schools.Our project will use traditional, modern and PC games to provide new ways to tackle violence and discrimination,and we want this to be the key to solving the problem.
 The project partners are: Scoala Gimnaziala "Vasile Mitru" Tasca- Romania(coordinator), Osnovno uciliste "Krste Misirkov" Skopje- Macedonia; Szkola Podstawowa Specjalna- Poland, Dalyan Naciye Tinaztepe Ortaokulu- Turkey, Osnovna skola Darda- Croatia,Nauksenu novada vidusskola- Latvia
 The participating groups are: 1981 secondary school students aged 11-15  from partner schools, approximately 3,500 students' parents, except those who work abroad, about 1500 students' grandparents, 240 teachers and representatives of the local community.
 The objectives of the project are:1.To reduce violence and discrimination among 1981 pupils aged 11-15 in Romania, Macedonia, Poland,Turkey, Croatia and Latvia over a 24- month period.
 2.To improve the abilities to deal with violent or discriminated students by developing specific skills of 55 teachers who take part in mobilities and  to exchange best practices.
 3.To develop a strategy to fight violence in schools by games;train 100 students to become conflict mediators in school.
 4. To raise empathy,mutual respect,social and communication skills,communication,emotional and social intelligence and tolerance among 1981 students aged 11-15 from the participant countries.
 5. To increase acceptance and diminish avoidance of disadvantaged students among 1981 pupils aged 11-15  in Romania, Macedonia, Poland,Turkey, Croatia and Latvia.
  6.To improve connections in relationships with others.To develop interpersonal and intercultural communication skills,stimulate positive emotions and well-being, prevent bullying among pupils aged 11-15 in Romania,Macedonia,Poland,Turkey,Croatia and Latvia.
 Activities:C1-Discrimination and violence in schools-common and different aspects;C2-Say NO to stereotypes;C3-Let's be against discrimination and violence;C4- Say YES to empathy;C5-Let's be tolerant through games;C6 - STOP bullying!
 Results:Concrete results- a detailed report on tackling violence and discrimination at school,the project magazine with the most important activities ,a site that will contain all the activities,information about the project and its objectives,students' work during LTTAs, CDs with games,photos,movies and images,a guide of good practices, the friendship perfume,positive message Tshirts,an e-learning platform.
 Planned results-students and teachers will increase their awareness of equality,become more open to engaging with all colleagues,increase respect and tolerance towards others,develop their English communication skills, relationships and skills interpersonal. In addition, participants become more aware of cultural differences, more prepared to cope with aggression and violence.
 Effect: Participating in this project will be a real benefit for our institution.
 We want the number of violent incidents among students to be reduced due to their conscious involvement.
 We will involve as many students as possible to transfer the acquired knowledge to other students.
 In the long run, teachers: they will know how to better address these issues at the institutional level by initiating collaborative projects with local education authorities; they will cooperate and work with their colleagues in partner schools, which will allow them to diversify the methods they will then adopt in their own schools.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2019-1-RO01-KA229-063206.title: Happy schools for happy students
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063206.summary:
All partner schools in this project gathered together in order to resolve common problems such as enhancing students educational results and encouraging them to follow school courses. We are all working with disadvantaged students (migrant/refugees, national minorities, economical and social disadvantages) and some of of our schools are situated in poor regions of our countries. We all asked ourselves "How children become happier in their education life?" We aim to eliminate problems such as familial, environmental, and psychological factors, ensure that children acquire positive personality skills, develop social dialogue skills, raise self-esteem and self-confidence. 
 Long-term impact and results that we expect our students to change and develop on the positive sides are positive emotional development of children towards the school, getting pleasure from the time spent at school, find opportunities to get to know themselves, increase of self-confidence and prevent early school leaving.  
 Teachers will become more professional in dealing with child problems, new teaching-learning approaches will be based on curriculum programes to be created after that. 
 We will involve all students of our schools in local project activities. Each school will involve 6 students accompanied by 2 teachers during each pupils exchanges in partner schools. The selected students and teachers to participate at pupils exchanges are among those who belong the the disadvantaged categories as mentioned in our application form: migrant/refugees, national minorities, economical and social disadvantages.
 As indirect beneficiaries of our project will be students' families and local partners to whom we will disseminate project information and products and which will be actively involved in project activities such as music, dance and drama performances of our students. Students will spread cultural information within their families and local communities as well.
 We will carry educational activities to increase our pupils motivation to follow school courses and making them happier in their every day school life.
 We have determined the implementation and methods of working within our project:
 We have planned the learning-teaching activities monthly. We have set the criteria for the selection of the students and teachers to participate in project activities. We will identify students who are subjected to the threats of school failure and early school leaving, willing to work, idealistic. We will involve teachers with good skills in the field of our project theme, and we will share tasks with each of these participants at every stage of the process. 
 We will include administrative staff, English, ICT teachers and classroom teachers as part of the project team. We will involve the school accountant in managing project budget. With the aim of reaching our project goals, we identified activities as organizing theater-drama activities, having movie time, organizing picnics, music-song contests and visual art exhibitions made up of student works, preparing recycling boxes, organizing sports activities and contests, organizing theater-drama activities. We have decided to co-ordinate all activities of the project partners within the same period under coordinator supervision. We will instantly display our implementation outputs on sharing portals like Etwinning, Facebook, Skype, Twitter and provide the interaction in this way. We will use Twinspace, contact lists (mail group) and WhatsApp for communication.
 We will set criteria to see that our project reaches its goal and we will apply attitude scales and satisfaction surveys to these criteria.
 We will organize seminars at local, regional and national levels to disseminate our project and bring it to other institutions. By inviting local and national mass media, we will be able make our project known to a wider community. We will ultimately influence the policies of education at local and regional level and prepare the ground for the creation of new curriculum programes based on project theme together with innovative and intercultural educational activities thus increasing our pupils interest towards school courses and their educational performances.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-RO01-KA229-063255.title: Let's Share Our Heritage
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063255.summary: Actual society is rapidly changing and we are creating a framework where people is expected to move more frequently from their birthplaces to different locations. To succeed in this new situation it is important to know how to communicate with each other in a multicultural context, with different languages, religions, cultural and socio-economic backgrounds. And the first step in this direction is to know what defines the identity of people, at individual and community level; what defines our own identity. We need to take action and to be aware of the importance of Nature and Cultural heritage. In this project we intend to valorize all those natural and cultural, material and non material resources at local level that, not being milestones of civilization, also help us to explain who we are, our history and our idiosyncrasy. Our objectives are: - To raise interest on natural and cultural heritage, particularly in Europe. - To highlight the importance of environment as an essential element in our lives. - To put into practice new methodological tools based on outdoor activities on local natural and cultural resources with a holistic and multidisciplinary approach. - To promote creativity and entrepreneurship towards the promotion and valuation of environment and material and immaterial cultural heritage. The project partners are six schools from Italy, Turkey, Romania, Croatia, Portugal and Greece, all of them secondary schools. All of them with experience working on transnational projects and with an interesting heritage in their locations. The project is addressed to students 15 to 19 years old. The project activities are planned to investigate about the local natural and cultural heritage, their influence on people’s identity and their potential as a tool to communicate and to work together as well as to promote the development of the local areas where they are located, at both social and economic level. The working scheme is to learn and investigate about the local heritage resources and share that knowledge in transnational meetings; to learn about the entrepreneurial project linked to those heritage resources and to raise appreciation and consideration towards it with the development of promotional material at local and transnational level. Approximately more than 120 mobility (mainly student mobility) is planned for 2 years. It is widely agreed that the prosperity of our world’s future is closely connected to well-educated children. In our project we will make it clear that each student’s voice is heard, because in a milieu of cultural diversity different views act as a catalyst for progress at each level of social life. Student exchanges and other activities in the project will also enhance an understanding toward diverse perspectives on European citizenship and help our students to develop an appreciation of the European cultural diversity and an empathy for different cultures. In the first short-term staff training meeting, in Croatia, teachers will learn about the basic ICT tools and skills needed to successfully deal with the task in the Project and there will be workshop about the creation of a methodology to work on heritage as an educational tool to be made available for everybody via ICT tools under a creative commons licence.The next five short-term  exchange of students, partners and student will devote time to learn about the heritage of the host countries ) reflecting on the influence of heritage on people’s identity , learning about the threats and opportunities of Natural heritage  and the importance of the cultural one , creating promotional material based on their own gathered material (pictures, video clips, graphs, maps, etc.). All the project activity will be based on a project based learning with a multidisciplinary approach organized around outdoor activities and peer-learning sessions in a cooperative transnational working atmosphere. We intend with this project to raise awareness in our students and the educational community towards local heritage and its importance, providing other schools with the guidance and examples needed to replicate the initiative in future projects at local or transnational level with great success
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2019-1-RO01-KA229-063260.title: LifeSteps
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063260.summary: Lifelong learning is a range of well-planned opportunities that contain understanding, knowledge, attitudes, qualities and skills. Together they aim to promote personal, social, and health development and serve to help children master the rules and opportunities that they offer life, take initiatives and responsibilities for their own lives, think critically and creatively, solve conflicts, develop a tolerant and emphatic attitude towards others, easily establish friendship and communicate effectively with others What do I do when I'm lost, when I lose something or it was taken to me, what do I do when I'm out of power and can not communicate electronically, how I report to my colleagues who have a problem ? "Sometimes appear to be absent for the child lacking life skills. It is a responsibility common family, school, community. Every child, regardless of age, needs certain abilities to later lead a balanced life to develop and maintain normal relationships with others in order to achieve their goals and to deal with various difficulties. our generation of very sensitive children and parents who do not meet the challenges of life. This causes us to change the optics of the development of the life skills of preschool children.They come from a super-protective environment that meets the child's natural need for to try alone, to experience and to feed their curiosity. At home, this is not allowed, which leads to the inhibition of the natural and harmonious development of a child. We have concluded with experience with children that the meaning of the term life skills also depends on the meaning given to the word life. we understand quality of life, and when we talk about life skills, we have skills, skills, traits and qualities, attitudes and behaviors that interfere with reaching the level of quality of life that we have in mind and for which we often skip over some important stages. The life skills of a child should be aimed at developing the child's personality, emotional intelligence, social skills and thinking skills. Through this project we have the opportunity to practice and equip preschool children with abilities to help them cope with adversities and continue to grow harmoniously as adapted and competent adults. We want our children to be able to discover their personal resources and qualities, explore the world with curiosity and use intelligence in a smart way, be able to establish relationships of friendship and communicate with others, develop feelings of empathy for those in difficulty, be environmentally responsible, adopt healthy lifestyles, stay permanently anchored at the present but also look with confidence in the future. All these are the premise of a balanced life, are the natural stages of development, the steps of life (LifeSteps) are the stages of life that we want all children to walk.

2019-1-RO01-KA229-063346.title: Guide the Guide!
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063346.summary:
"Guide the guide!" (G2G) is a school exchange partnership developed by five schools from Europe, financially supported by the European Commission through Erasmus+ programme, Key Action 2. It emerged from the need to improve the quality and efficiency of education by using as educational tools the guided tours of museums and cities, which involve students in a creative and innovative way. Therefore, the project aims to increase the use of guided tours of museums and cities as an integrative/complementary educational tool by designing 15 innovative and interactive model guided tours, to increase the correlation between students' theoretical knowledge and the contents presented during guided tours and to create opportunities for learning-by-doing through patrimonial education.
 
 The participants in the project are 150 students, aged 14-18, from schools situated in Romania, Croatia, Italy, Portugal and Spain. All the partner schools are vocational, training students in: tourism and food services (Romanian and Italian schools), health, building trades and agriculture (Croatian school), in Computer science (Spanish school) and in sports, commerce and technology (Portuguese school). 
 
 The project activities are mostly practical ones - taking guided tours of museums and cities in order to identify the existing resources, realizing SWOT analyses, sharing interactive methods and instruments in order to re-design the guided tours, establishing the appropriate content of guided tours and actually implementing the tours with groups of students. In order to carry out the activities in an efficient way, a wide range of methods will be employed, among which we mention: fieldwork, non-formal methods, interactive games, ICT tools, drama techniques, mission-based learning, treasure hunt.
 
 The result we will develop is a pedagogical kit, entitled "Guided tours - Good practice examples", comprising information about the methodology of the 15 interactive guided tours created by the students, with clear examples. The kit will be accompanied by an online virtual multidisciplinary museum with visual materials (photos, presentations, videos) collected during local and international visits.
 
 By getting involved in this project, students will improve their general knowledge in various fields, they will enhance their interest in museology, they will get to know the cultural heritage of Europe, they will develop their key-competences (communication in a foreign language, digital skills, social skills, critical thinking) and, most of all, they will improve their learning skills through peer-to-peer and learning-by-doing methods which, on the long-term, will reflect in students' improved school performance.
 
 The long-term benefits for the participating schools refer to gains generated by planning and developing hands-on activities, implemented within and beyond the project duration, the collaboration with the local authorities and local/regional museums will be enhanced through the project activities because the national cultural heritage will be at the core of all our actions.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2019-1-RO01-KA229-063757.title: Little Friends of Nature
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063757.summary:
The Project proposes the facilitation of the experience exchange and the development of some common methods for improving the institutional ability of the partners to involve pupils and parents in ecological and recycling activities, to form to them pro-ecological behavior, to help parents understand the integral role outdoor time plays in the health and well-being of our kids and our environment and help them find new ways to make children play and learn outdoors. It also aims to raise the level of the education of the teachers taking part in the project through gaining and sharing the experience, learning new methods and techniques and making them use the different approaches in education. We’ll help our children to discover by themselves the importance of recycling and incite them, encourage them to take concrete initiatives in their everyday life. This project can give children a chance to use their imagination to design products that do not harm the environment or increase waste. The education for environmental protection is considered a priority of the European states policies, but it is also an important need of the institutions involved in the project.
 The target group of the project consists of 60 teachers and 500 children enrolled in six partner institutions and their parents. The project’s corporation is made up of the following partners:
 - Gradinita cu Program Prelungit "Floarea Soarelui", Romania – coordinator
 - Create Partnership Trust, UK
 - Kindergarten “Ivanic Grad”, Croatia
 - Istituto Comprensivo Orsino Orsini, Italy
 - Gorukle Aksemsettin ILKOKULU, Turkey
 - Timi Public Kindergarten,Cyprus
 In order to achieve the project's goals we'll organize activities such as  games, exhibitions, artistic and knowledge contests, experiments, trips, meeting with specialists, field researches, sports competitions which will use recycled objects and will be integrated in the school activities, outdoors ecological activities. The activities and the theme of the project will be developed within all the school subjects. The activities will use recyclable materials and will aim to share environmental knowledge, to discover the fact that ecology and environmental protection can be fun and can be integrated in a great number of activities. The pupils will be involved into researches, visits and will draw the conclusions which are essential.The project activities will be divided during the two years of the project as it follows: 
 -in the first year we are going to approach the following themes: environment factors: water, air, soil; energy and household waste recycling; and the living world: forest, animals, vegetation. The children will acquire the necessary knowledge for a better understanding of the secrets of nature, of the way nature works and what we should to protect it.
 -in the second year we are going to plan a series of outdoor ecological activities, trips and sports competition. In order to consolidate the information acquired during the first year and to form lifelong habits, we are going to organize activities to celebrate the main Environmental Events in the Global Eco Calendar. 
 Different training activities for the teachers (webinars, workshops, attending activities carried on by the project partners, training courses) will help them enrich their knowledge, show them a new perspective of modern ways of teaching and improve the strategies they have used until now.
 The achieved results will be:
 -the project website
 -"Erasmus corner" in each school
 -project logo
 -multilingual dictionary for children
 -postcards/decorations on a typical tradition of the country from recyclable materials
 -exhibitions organized in the partner institutions/ public institutions
 -theater performances, sports competitions and contests based on or using recycled objects
 -an eco-calendar displaying aspects of project activities
 -a best-practice manual with outdoor ecological games and successful activities organized for celebrating Environmental Events from the Global Eco Calendar
 -didactic materials from recycled objects
 -Methodological Guide "My Recycling Factory"which will contain the materials, methods and techniques applied in manufacturing toys, crafts and didactic materials necessary for implementing the proposed  activities.
 -6 brochures for parents
 The participation in the project will contribute to the development of the involved schools in all levels: children and parents, teachers, institutional ability, on a long term as we intend to continue implementing the best practice activities gained during the project. The methodological guide and the best practice manual, as didactic auxiliaries, will guide our future activity. We plan to continue taking care of the garden made during the project and to keep improving the playground with recyclable elements.The project's results will remain available on the project website and eTwinning and anyone interested will have free access.

2019-1-RO01-KA229-063789.title: If I were a teacher
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063789.summary:
,, If we were a teacher ,, project  is addressed to teachers and 9-13 years old students from Romania, Turkey, Spain, Italy and Croatia. Our project is created for raising the  awareness about the “co-teaching”  best practice for an effective partnership between teacher and students. The project is written for educators and 9-13 years old students from Romania, Turkey, Spain, Italy and Croatia.  
 Our main intention is to create a meaningful learning for all the  students and to connect the strategies of teaching-learning-evaluation to students' every day life . Children always have many questions, such as  ,,Why do we need to learn? Why do we need homeworks? This is the reason we decided to create our project for our students, in order to make them the real beneficiaries of the learning process. We  realize that our students, no matter what aged are, are eager to feel appreciation form the part of the teachers , and they also need some good answers of their personal problems and experiences.
 As experienced adults, combining experience and theoretical informations, every teacher must think more about what are the requirements of our world in order to ensure an effective learning process for the students. Our students are more and more eager to live in the present, they are always searching an  interactive and animated atmosphere during lessons and in the school activities , so we built our project for  empowering our students responsibility for their personal learning process. They will be recognized as experts and get involved in the educational process as facilitators.
 We intend to use in our project activities a reality-pedagogy approach based on building chances for all  educators and students to work together as a real team in  the process of a  designing part.By building a student-centred approach, all the participants involved in project events will have better understanding of the lesson objectives and will also become more relied to the learning results. We intend  also to pay attention in building a better school atmosphere by changing school spaces, classes or seats in classes. 
 Students involved in all the project implementation will become conscious about their worth and will discover also their big importance  in designing and planning educational events. Students will realize that their work is appreciated at an international level, through the toolkit built especially  for  sharing our knowledge and best practices on how to determine students to be an active part of the planning lessons process. 
 Our project is intended to 50% of the number of students from all 5 schools involved in the specific activities. 
 The main objectives of our project are as following :
 -to create meaningful learning experiences for 125 students and 50 teachers as widely and actively  participants
 -to develop students necessary skills for the hard work of learning
 -to offer teachers  a better insight into students’ knowledge and strategies of critical thinking
 -to improve participants creativity and innovation spirit 
 The project tangible results are questionnaires, Erasmus+ coners, a project website and logo, eTwinning project, leaflets/ flyers, audio visual materials "School presentation";"Interviews: If I were a teacher"; "Bringing real world into classrooms"; "Meaningful learning activities"; "What is Authentic Learning?", puppets theatre, crafts, music concert, mind and cultural games, sport tournament, dictionary, quotes wall, posters, travel guide, e-magazine, photos exhibition, treasure hunt: math game, presentations “What happens if…?”, Erasmus garden, DVD of the project and project toolkit: teaching documents.
 The project events will be proposed to students between 9-13 y.o. and  English will be used as common working language in all mobilities. 
 By using real-life connections from different EU realities in the classroom, we will develop the cultural horizon of our students, develop also social tolerance, respect for diversity and understanding, as well as their engagement in becoming actively involved in the educational process. 
 For creating the project tangible results we will consider behavioral management strategies, paying attention at the collaboration process in the classroom and interaction students-students and students-teachers. Our  project intend to build a safe and affective learning environment at a local and international level as well.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2019-1-RO01-KA229-063851.title: Motivating the learning engine to increase student's school, professional and social success and reduce absenteeism
2019-1-RO01-KA229-063851.summary:
Europe needs strong, educated, involved, active young people in the labor market who truly know their role in society and the benefits of democratic principles. Students are the engine on which the European community is built and the knowledge-based economy is developing. The main reason for this project came from a need of our care school for several years, ie we have a high percentage of unmotivated. students to learn. We are a technological high school
 they are not always students with the lowest grades, but once they enter our system they do not progress, they see high school life as a punishment to stay in classes where it is important to encourage them not to learn. As a result of the previous school year, we had 75% students with an average of 5-5.99; 15% students, 3% dropouts and 7% students with unfinished status, over 45 students / partners with over 40 unmotivated absences and low exam results. So, if we motivate students to learn, we can easily guide them to a career and create generations of active students in the job market.
 
 Specific objectives
 For students
 1. Increase self-esteem in 80% of students participating in learning activities in Croatia by the end of September 2021
 2. Develop a positive attitude towards school education in 80% of students participating in the learning activity in Turkey by the end of November 2021
 3. Developing for 80% of students participating in the learning process in Spain, the ability to be aware of their own learning process based on awareness of the usefulness of the theory in a practical context by the end of March 2020
 4. Development for 80% of the students in the learning activity in Romania, of the career orientation capacity based on the awareness of the importance of the study qualification until the end of December 2021
 5. Development to 80% of the number of students participating in the activities of learning the feeling of equal opportunities in education in the partner countries, by the end of the project.
 For teachers:
 6- developing the skill to integrate in the didactic and extracurricular process the methodologies, the tools used by the partners (learned from each other) according to the project theme, up to 90% of the number of teachers participating in each training activity until the end. from her
 
 Direct target group -120 teachers and students
 The transnational activities dedicated to teacher training involved 40 teachers and 80 students who participated in the transnational activities. The students ranged in age from 11 to 19 years.
 There were 28 participants with economic obstacles, geographical obstacles. We provided 4 short-term exchanges for students and 5 short training courses for teachers. It was necessary to carry out the 9 activities in order to achieve the objectives in which the students and teachers were targeted.
 The objectives were operationalized through student-learning activities and mutual teacher training and the application of their innovative methods in all partner schools. The activities consisted of workshops with exchange of good practices and direct interaction, didactic, cultural, moral, linguistic, scientific, trips to economic agents, participation in classes, online activities.
 Everything was learned in mobility, each participant applied at home, adapted, combined with common online work
 Result intangible
 Motivating students for academic and professional success
 Developing students' team spirit, improving self-confidence
 Teachers have enriched the methodology used in class / extracurricular to motivate students to achieve better school results

Travel to Europe and Asia
Dual Debate Journal Active Participatory Teaching Method
Educational site
Brochure for the educational market-Top 10 professions

 Final results
 Students - Professional polyglot dictionary
 Teacher's Guide - "Transnational Teaching Experiences"
 In the long run, we aim to: had high level teachers and would have a higher prestige being seen by students, for students better school results and school, social, civic involvement

2019-1-RS01-KA229-000845.title: Differently identical
2019-1-RS01-KA229-000845.summary:
The project that we implemented in the previous three years in cooperation with three other schools from Croatia, Turkey and Portugal is the first Erasmus exchange partnership project of our school after two KA1 projects. Our journey began way back in 2019 and here we have come to the end. The project was created as an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of our school and what it is that we would like to change, i.e., improve in the school, among students, parents, employees, in fact, the whole community. Judging by the feedback we received from all participants in the project, both direct and indirect, the results exceeded expectations.
The project was supposed to last only 18 months and contain a number of activities foreseen in the application, however, everything went wrong just a few days before the first trip. Then the new virus COVID19 started spreading around the world and everything was stopped; we didn't even know how and what would be realized, and there were more important things than the project.
In the period from the introduction of the state of emergency until the relaxation of the measures, we did not sit idly by. We implemented a series of activities that we did not plan with the project together, each in accordance with our own and the capabilities of our students and employees, and during online classes, which was something completely new for all of us. Although we did not plan these activities when applying, they served us to get to know each other better (both students and teachers), to develop even friendly relations, to visit each other outside of the official mobilities in the project, and we think that this is the biggest benefit of this project.
Mobilities came with the gradual easing of anti-pandemic measures. Given that the measures were not the same everywhere, the partner schools agreed that, in accordance with the relaxation of the measures, we would make rotations in mobilities, so that the students of all schools, who at that moment had been in the project for a year and a half, could travel and they see their peers whom they have known for a long time, but through monitor screens and phones. So the mobilities came to us very easily and without too much effort, considering that we got to know each other very well in the period before them.
The mobilities were extremely easy to implement. Students and employees in the partner schools knew each other very well, they developed intimate relationships, online activities before the mobility are responsible for that, and thus several items that we planned to improve, but through mobility; so mobilities came to us more as an upgrade of all that knowledge and that's why we believe that the project has far exceeded the basic idea for which it was written.

2019-1-SE01-KA229-060381.title: Teaching Cultural Heritage with Digital Technologies
2019-1-SE01-KA229-060381.summary:
This project is about teaching cultural heritage with the help of digital technology. We are five partners coming from Sweden, Croatia, Poland, Portugal and Spain. Each partner teaches cultural heritage in a different way. Through this project we are going to work together, share and transfer best practices. Moreover, we intend to test, develop and implement new technology-based educational methods, applications and tools. Our products will be an online book with a collection of learning scanarios and lesson plans created throughout the project and a TwinSpace site with the uploaded educational materials developed throughout the project. 
 
 Participants in this project are teachers, students, parents and local stakeholders. However, the main focus is on the teachers and students. They are directly involved in the project and they attend project meetings. Participating teachers come from different subject areas: English, History, Geography, Music, Art and Social Science. The students between 12 and 18 will participate in the TwinSpace project. There will be six students in each mobility and they will be between 13 and 16. Two teachers will accompany each  group of students during mobilities. 
 
 The aims of the project are to explore, develop, introduce and share technology-based educational methods, tools and applications using cultural heritage as the topic. Teachers and students will use English to create material, present it and discuss thus improving linguistic competences. They will improve their knowledge of cultural heritage by learning on-site and through authentic learning. Using ICT to create material, participants will improve their digital skills. They will be involved in creating and updating of TwinSpace project where they will upload educational material. The project will be interdisciplinary involving teachers of different subjects.
 
 By researching and working in teams, students will improve 21st century skills, boost creativity, intrinsic motivation and engagement for their own learning process. They will become independent, autonomous and take control of own learning process. They will develop respect for own culture and empathy for other cultures.  The students  will have opportunity to improve their digital competences, meet in person their peers from other countries. They will discuss the project topics, their experiences, expectations and impressions. They will improve their linguistic competence and public speaking skills by speaking English, creating and delivering presentations that they created to the international  group. They will be able to learn on-site. They will attend group discussions and acquire better understanding of own and partners' cultural heritage and its importance.    
 
 There will be five project meetings during the two-year period. Each meeting will give teachers opportunity to work together, share, transfer best practices and  learn from each other. They will observe other teachers in their work, they will (co)teach  lessons in the international environment and have group discussions. They will reflect on their own teaching practice and eventually improve it. They will create learning scenarios that will  be collected into an eBook to be used in the future. They will master innovative educational tools and applications, raise awarenes of the importance of cultural heritage and the importance of preserving it for future generations. In addition, they will improve linguistic, intercultural and civic competences as well as their 21st century skills. After the project, they will be equipped with innovative, digital-based educational practices (programming, coding, 3D modelling and animation, AR, using Europeana)  and will be  able to disseminate results and outcomes to their professional network.
 
 The overall objective of the project is to examine educational value of European cultural heritage giving it the place it deserves in the education. Our aim is to enable students to acquire skills and competences, primarily digital and cultural, that will make them more competitive and successful workforce ready to enter the modern employment market.

2019-1-SE01-KA229-060522.title: Stay healthy and connected to the offline world
2019-1-SE01-KA229-060522.summary:
Context and background
 News of scientific reports state that overall physiological and mental health is an increasing issue in the world. Part of that problem stems from the sedentary lifestyle that has come to be a normal part of our society, and a contributing factor to that sedentary lifestyle is the increased screen usage (particularly mobile devices).
 
 Methodology
 This project will focus on the positive health benefits of physical activity to combat a sedentary lifestyle. The method of incorporating physical activity both inside and outside of the classroom will break a sedentary lifestyle pattern and develop healthy habits over time. By backing this method with scientific research on the area alongside self evaluation from the students, this project will raise awareness of both the negative health effects of a sedentary lifestyle as well as the positive psychophysiological benefits of an active lifestyle. The results of which will help combat early school leaving as well as improve student grades.
 
 Number and profile of participants
 In total, over the span of 2 years, 160 students aged 12-15 across 5 countries alongside 40 teachers will get the opportunity to participate in the mobility. On top of that during each school visit everyone on the school will be get the chance to take part of the exchange.
 
 Objectives of your project
 The main objective is to create a balance between digital technology and psychophysiological well being among students by helping them stay connected to the offline world. The secondary objective is to raise awareness of the negative health effects of the technological advancement as well as combating a sedentary lifestyle in order to achieve a healthier school while, at the same time, creating a positive learning environment for students.  Furthermore, the goal of this project is to limit the number of students who drop out of school, due to both physical and mental issues, by increasing their psychophysiological health through practising an innovative and open education adapted to the digital era. 
 
 Description of activities
 The planned activities for the different countries will all focus on health and well being, and tackling early school leaving by using open education and innovative practices in the digital era that we currently live in.
 
 The first meeting in Spain will focus on effective stress management during the school timetable.
 The second meeting in Sweden will revolve around how excessive use of mobile phones/screens in general affect the human brain.
 The third meeting in Croatia will be about the positive impacts of physical activity for health and well being.
 The fourth meeting in Turkey will incorporate music as an extension of effective stress management.
 The fifth meeting in Poland will tackle break time activities to exemplify healthier alternatives to staying sedentary with mobile phones or computers.
 
 The purpose of the activities leading up to, between, and after the meetings, will be dynamic over the course of the project. Initially these activities will focus on creating a bond between the schools through the use of video presentations alongside a logotype project to further help tie a bond. The questionnaire at the start will include questions about their perceived screen usage, physical activity, and their overall physical and mental health. This will be followed-up with actual measurements of these categories during each mobility session. Towards the end of the project there will be a research topic where students are to compare their spare time activities with those of their parents and grandparents to help bring forth a nuanced discussion on the topic. At the end of the project the participants will evaluate their progress in relation to the project’s goals through both a questionnaire and a video.
 
 Results and impact envisaged
 Less time spent on social media apps, better sleeping habits, increased physical activity, raised awareness of the signs and impacts of Internet addiction, an increased amount of students participating in physical break activities between lessons rather than remaining sedentary, introduction of some teaching-learning activities that are physically demanding, better understanding on how to use digital technology as a tool, and transnational cooperation to combat the raised issues on a broad front.
 
 Longer term benefits
 Every year the Fridaskolan school in Trollhättan is organising a field study trip by bus for its final year students. The week's study trip is carried out by bus with visits to historically important sites from World War II and also includes an exchange with another European country. We currently have a cooperation with a school in the Netherlands, but we are looking to further expand our network in the future by continuing our cooperation to include the schools in this project as well.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-SE01-KA229-060538.title: Safe Digitalized Schools in the European School Network
2019-1-SE01-KA229-060538.summary:
The internet, which has started to take place in every area of our lives, has led to some new transformations with the opportunities provided by the communication among people. While these transformations are mostly for the benefit of humanity, the internet, which has become a part of our lives, does not always have positive results. Excessive use of internet technologies that make daily life easier presents several problems. Some users can use the internet for a long time, never leaving their places or neglecting their daily life activities. Due to the unhealthy / problematic internet use behavior, these users have become increasingly confronted with more problems and psychological distortions in their lives. When the proper use of the internet cannot be achieved, there is the potential to negatively affect human life and create a dependency. According to the results of the European Online Children's survey (2010), it was revealed that 60% of children are online almost every day and that the age of using the Internet decreases gradually. As a result of our research with our project partners, we observed that many EU countries have the same problems.
 As a result of our meetings with our project partners in accordance with the project partnership structure;
 - students spend an average of 4-5 hours with the internet in their daily life,
 -The negative attitudes towards school among the reasons of indifference are at the top of the list,
 - Teachers in our participating schools need to be renewed in the age of technology;
 -The unscheduled and unplanned use of technology has emerged as academic failure due to the decrease in the motivation of the course.
 
 Project Objectives:
 Increasing teacher competencies in the use of conscious technology;
 Effective use of technology and internet in education,
 Effective use of technology in the courses and the students ' ability to motivate the course,
 Ability to combat technology dependence,
 Safe internet use and cyber bullying skills,
 The ability to plan and implement social and sportive activities which will support development of students through regular children's games will increase.
 
 
 In our project, there are 5 education, training and learning mobilities. These mobilities will take place in Furulundskolan School in Sweden on March 2020, in Hacı Suphiye Bolunmez Imam Hatip Secondary School in Turkey on May 2020, in Ekpedeftırıa Vassılıadı School in Greece on October 2020, in Stejarska Tehnicka Skola Oizijek school in Croatia on March 2021, and in Instituto Di Istruzione Superore, in the Vinci - Giorgio School in Italy on May 2021.Our project partners will participate in all international activities in the Kasımiye Secondary School school and will play an active role in our project at local events.
 In our project, we have agreed to give Europass mobility certificate, Europass CV and participation certificates to the participants.
 -In our project, our participants will create a guide for using web-2 tools,
 -supporting children at risk of technological addiction by contacting them about the use of technology consciously,
 - In order to raise awareness of cyber bullying, educational short films and posters will be prepared with students in all partner country schools,
 -In the case of safe internet use, in all our partner schools, parents will be presented with the participation of local representatives and handbooks will be distributed
 
 
 The traditional game book will be prepared in the time period from the past to the present, which includes traditional games, and the sustainability of our project will be continued after the end of the project.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education
