2020-1-DE03-KA229-077224.title: M-Learning
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077224.summary:
This project aims to convert our current education and training systems into a more efficient, interesting, attractive and better qualified one by means of web 2.0 tools and mobile tool applications. Hence, it contains training of teachers and students on related instruments. Teachers will exchange their experiences about how to use web 2.0 tools like Kahoot, Madmagz, Classdojo, Mentimter, Quizlet, Quizizz, Prezi, Google Classrooms and many more. These tools can help teachers a lot. They don't need to carry bags of books, flascards, experiment items, posters, yearly or daily plans and many more things alike. Once they create their presentations, tests, plans, visual and audio materials on these Web 2.0 tools, the teachers will be able to use them easily no matter where they are as long as they have an internet connection.
 Stundets will be shown and trained about the web 2.0 tools and mobile devices applications which can help their learning process. By means of these instruments students can study, exercise, repeat the subjects or prepare presentations wheverever and whenever they feel like studying or doing exercises.
 Parents will also exploit this project a lot. They will follow their children's studies, exercises and test results, the duration of the completion of the tasks, detailed test results analysis- consicely all the process of learning - which will give an idea about what should be next. In education, parents and teachers must collaborate, this project will let them collaborate more instantly.
 School management team is another beneficiary of this project. There are Smart phone applications that help the managing staff a lot. They can use automatic systems that send instant information and notifications to the parents. They can make all the announcements in a very short time. They will have the chance to store the detailed test results -to be used whenever they need- on certain web sites. By this way, they can observe the development of the school's success.
 The general objective of our project is to icrease the quality of education and training by means of technological facilities - especially web 2.0 tools and mobile apps. Sepecifically;
 We want our teachers
 -to have the digital skills which are prerequisites of our digital era.
 -to benefit from the fruits of the technology.
 -to overcome their fears about the digital  illiteracy.
 -to be able to create enjoyable, attractive, funny and interesting education environments.
 -become more effective and successful in their fields.
 -to able to observe the students' developments with the digital analytics
 -to able to reach instantly any data or information realted with their fields
 As to students, we want to let them:
 -manage their own learning process
 -have more self esteem and self reliance
 -free them from a certain place to learn and do the tasks
 -do exercises, experience other digital materials, and watch different videos on certain topics as much as possible
 -to reduce the time they waste on computers and mobile devices
 -overwhelm their fears about learning the subjects which they think they are not good at.
 We are planning to involve nearly
 -2400 students
 -150 teachers
 -2400 parents all of who will be able to get some further insights about the benefits of technology if used in a good way. Some teachers and students will participate in students and teachers exchanges (numbers are given in LTT section)
 All of our activities are decided accordingly with our objectives. We have  activities which will be done at our schools seperately and we have activities which will be done with all the partners at the same scool. The activities aim to teach, show, practise and use the Web 2.0 tools and mobile apps. Students, teachers and parents will learn how to use and benefit from them. They will have their own accounts and implement those tools in their learning process. 
 The activities also intend to disseminate the resuts and impacts of the project.
 The project will be carried by all the schools simultaneously, and we will be communicating instantly to make sure everything is ok. All schools have a project team and our main leader is Germany, we already made a distribution of tasks each partner has specific responsiblities in addition to common tasks. We have a schedule and all the partners will abide by this. In our international learning and training activities we will have 5 days workshops where we will all exchange experiences and practise web 2.0 tools. at the end of the activities we will be given certificates by the host school.
 We envisage these general results and impacts:
 more motivated teachers and students
 more responsible and successful students
 more attractive learning and education environments
 more interested and concerned parents
 learning anytime free from a certain place
 less wate of paper money and energy
 This project has longer term targets to grow up a new generation equipped with digital competencies and skills that our era requires

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077252.title: European manual for active environmental protection
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077252.summary:
The basic idea of the future Erasmus-Partnership of an intercultural model to create inclusion
 and a special kind of participation in society for children and students with special needs arose
 during the current Erasmus mobility activity and was developed by teachers and students. It
 has a result of the good cooperation between the involved schools.
 The project focused to strengthen the awareness for the environment of our students
 referring to their special needs. The new project  helped the students to defend themselves
 against acts of exclusion, intolerance and xenophobia. The proposals were multi-layered and
 will help the students to develop their own personality, to improve their competences and
 skills, in addition to strengthen their responsibility for nature and the environment. The
 approach to natural resources, ecosystems and the protection against negative circumstances 
 of a natural habitat were now central aspects for our students. Furthermore, the project 
 helped to reduce the amount of early school leavers. The realisation that a good life now and in
 the future corresponds to an entire environment was the base line in every activity. The students
 participated actively in our society and helped to implement the preservation of nature. The
 nature and the landscape are the baseline for our existence. Consequently, they need to be
 protected. In addition, we need to ensure sustainability to realise a balance between the
 current and future life.
 The project was organised interdisciplinary and across forms and  involved the whole
 school.
 In the forefront, local clubs and organisations appeared in the respective schools and presented
 their environmental profile. During the activities multinational thinking and acting as well as
 sympathy and understanding for each other wsd promoted. Every student did a workshop
 including local proposals which imply the resulting and inclusive ideas to document especially
 the social participation. Consequently, we had a selection of a European diversity in all
 partner regions, which gave an insight into the corresponding profiles.
 
 Lesnica (Poland)      protection of forests and recycling
 Rudolstadt                 recycling and renewable energies
 Pula (Croatia)            protection and preservation of the sea – Adria
 Stribro (Czech)          the use of water as a source of energy
 Schweich                   environmental protection, recycling, sustainability ( school in Puck cancelled their participation )
 
 During each mobility every student had to create his or her individual certificate. They were
 able to take photos and made short movies independently. These media skills helped to
 create their individual certificate of attendance including the logo which was the basis and
 the result of the first meeting. The logo was the badge of our project and each student 
 got a T-Shirt with our symbol.
We explored in companionship new ways of learning and learning methods,
 learn about specific and local activities. We also get to know special features of the European
 countries, work practice-oriented and achieve the opportunity of European conferencing.
 Collective practice-oriented working shall generate respect and acceptance for several
 impairments, together with other lifestyle habits accompanied by the national characteristics
 in regard of environmentalism, ecology, diversity of species and territory. Basic features of our
 project for sustainability are aspect of saving water and energy, recycling of material, nutrition
 and of course waiver of plastics and disposable products. These aspects are going to be
 established and developed during the two years of our project.
 Learn basis and learn cause generate the issue of an “European handbook for active
 environmentalism”. The handbook presents country specific core themes. The resulting
 handbook will be used as a basis for future students of each school to draw interest to a certain
 environmental issue.
 The experiences, which the traveling group (6 students/ 3 teachers) gathers in the partner
 school, can be passed on in a full to the other participants directly. A scorecard for active
 environmentalism and sustainability was created corporately and will be used by our
 corresponding firms and institutions in form of a pollution badge which was created by the
 students themselves. That will guarantee an intense cooperation.
 We will use our own homepage, European platforms and E-twinning to present our activities
 and to support the dissemination of our results.
 The participation in that project is an amazing advantage for our students and a chance to get
 to know parts of Europe. For most of them it is the only way to go abroad and get to know
 these activities, countries and traditions. The sustainability is granted throughout the media
 representation. Additionally, the project will be included into the conception of the respective
 schools.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077260.title: Multilingual Learning ::::::::
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077260.summary:
The project „Multilingual learning through digitalised contemporary witness reports on the topic: Awakening and Upheaval – events which have changed the world” deals with the conducting and digitising of contemporary witness reports on selected political current events like climate change, mass tourism, and Brexit or on historical events like the fall of the Berlin Wall, the post-war years after 1945 and fascism. It will result in the creation of a public learning platform consisting of audio-visual contemporary witness reports, additional didactic support material for teachers and learning material in different languages. 

The digitisation in all education sectors currently poses a big challenge to all schools, as the generating of digital teaching materials as well as its handling becomes increasingly important for learners and teachers.

The current level of progress in the process of digitisation in different education sectors in the schools involved in the project varies considerably. Therefore, the schools expect from the project a didactical/methodological exchange on the possibilities, difficulties and dangers of the digitisation in order to advance the promotion of the digital-medial competence and the defining of concrete development steps in the process of the digitisation.

In foreign language teaching and especially in history lessons, definitely the full potential of digitized teaching material has not yet been fully exploited.
Additionally, the availability of education programmes about digitised teaching materials for history lessons is very limited.

The project provides the schools with an innovative didactic approach, as the digitisation of personal stories and memories also means the transition into a cultural or rather into a “digital memory”. This project is supposed to outline and discuss ways, how to deal professionally in class with this change. Furthermore, it should help shaping media-related historical and political learning by using the abundance of digital contemporary witness reports which are available in the internet.  
The aim is to strengthen generic competences for being able to handle information resources and narrations from the internet independently and reflected.

Similar chances can be found for many other subjects and can be implemented by means of the project, so that a promotion of specific subjects and interdisciplinary learning (foreign language skills and media competence) can be achieved through the project. 

Through the collaboration with other schools on a national and international level among cognitive also socio-emotional objectives will be pursued.

During the project, the participants act largely independently and problem-oriented in international groups and learn communication and cooperation structures. Hereby they build an awareness for a productive collaboration which can have a positive effect for the European Community. 

The Otto-Hahn-School has successfully completed an Erasmus project in 2019, which has laid the foundation for this new project. 
The schools, which participated in the last project and which – among others – would like to take part in the new project as well, have already established certain structures (e.g. eTwinning, Twinspace, implementing of international project work in different subjects in the curriculums and guidelines of the schools).  
In the new project we will be able to draw on these existing structures and use them.

The project is designed for 24 months. In the preparation time before the actual start of the project the different schools will deal with content and methodical issues. The project groups, the teacher teams and the individual learning groups (different classes) will establish the framework and specific topics for the project.  Additionally, a pre-structuring, the creation of the needed materials and the search for suitable contemporary witnesses will take place. 

The participants will draw up a guideline which will define guide values and standards for conducting the interviews of the contemporary witnesses. Specific evaluations of the learning process and concrete evaluation sheets for a reflection of the project will be prepared and can be used at the beginning of the project.  A learning platform will be prepared and also an eTwinning platform will be set up.

With the beginning of the project the digitised contemporary witness reports will be produced and used in lessons of different subjects and different school types. Work materials and didactic support materials for teachers will be created and completed and refined during the project meetings (mobilities/activities).

The international teacher team will present these materials to their respective colleagues and all interested people of the school community (parents, pedagogical staff members, students). Also, they will evaluate the materials so that they can be integrated into the existing curriculums.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077314.title: There is no plan(et) B - Can renewable energies fight climate change?
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077314.summary:
In today's world, one of the MOST PRESSING GLOBAL CHALLENGES we face is CLIMATE CHANGE. As the PLANET´S FUTURE STEWARDS, it is crucial for TEENAGERS to be well-informed about this issue. Climate change poses an IMMINENT THREAT to our environment, ecosystems, and the well-being of future generations. By EDUCATING TEENAGERS about climate change, we EMPOWER them to become CATALYSTS for positive change, fostering a sustainable and resilient future for all.
The AIM OF OUR PROJECT was to raise AWARENESS about this topic among our students and that by following the project plan that you can read about above. Due to different circumstances (mainly the ban of students meetings in times of the PANDAMIC) we had to slightly ADJUST OUR PROJECT PLAN. The participants age was planned to be about 14 years. As we had PROLONGED THE PROJECT and some of the students who had started it had already left school we had to find new participants which were of different ages, but luckily that turned out not to be a problem at all. All guests and hosts students were able to develop a friendship during the mobilities.
The 5 subtopics were worked on in the planned order but with breaks during school closings, so that we were not able to stick to the plan to culminate in a mobility in the coordinating country. Thus we had to adjust the dates of the meetings and the coordinating countries which was not easy as the pandemic restrictions and the limited number of possible dates led to some complications. But we managed to realise all mobilities and also working on all planned topics with the students. 
The PARTICIPANTS ACTIVITIES between the meetings took place during the club meetings as well as at home during school closings. The students turned out to be quite eager to find out about background information on the topic and especially filming the vlogs seemed to be much fun. The COOPERATION between the mobilities was different than planned, as building a website with the possibility of discussing things online for all participants was hard to implement so that we decided to use VIDEO CONFERENCES and SOCIAL MEDIA to stay in contact with each other.
As the VLOGS the students made were all worth seeing we decided to upload them all onto our WEBSITE and not only the best of them. So the STUDENTS ARE EVEN MORE PROUD of what they created druing the last years. The videos can also be used in following lessons to start discussions for example about the importance of renewable energies or the problems of fossil fuels. Both topics are topics that for example are worked on in English lessons in year 9 and 10.
The results can be found on our project´s website: https://erasmusael.wixsite.com/thereisnoplanetb
All in all, we can say that our PARTICIPANTS BECAME EXPERTS on the topic of climate change and the chances and limits of renewable energies and can prove themselves as MESSENGERS of living sustainable in the future.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077326.title: Be brave - help us fight the plastic wave: Getting aware of plastics
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077326.summary:
Many young people are concerned about the condition of our planet. Up to now, there has often been a lack of (time) options at school, in which pupils can learn about environmental issues in class and how they can contribute to the environment. Therefore, with the Erasmus + project "Getting aware of plastics" we want to meet this need and address an environmental problem, the use and disposal of plastics, and make it our central project topic. The focus is on pollution from plastic waste. The pupils should deal intensely with the role of plastics in our lives so that, as an informed citizen, they can adopt a responsible attitude towards the environment. The European dimension is derived, on the one hand, from the fact that the sustainable use of plastics cannot be tackled on a national basis, but that plastic waste is a global problem for which the  affluent EUsociety bears particular responsibility and should act together as a community of states. An important European legal basis for this is the one-way plastic directive issued in May 2019. In direct comparison with their European project partners, the pupils can assess the different national implementations and, if possible, use them for their own actions.
 
 This includes acquiring background knowledge about the increasing use of plastic articles in the past two decades and their serious effects on our ecosystem. The students should be clear about the high plastic consumption and consider which plastic items are necessary and in which areas other materials can be used. In addition, the handling of plastic waste will be examined more closely and we should be aware of our direct responsibility for it. The aim of the project is to raise the awareness of the participating students and teachers about the immense problems that plastic represents for our ecosystem and to recognize their own responsibility for this problem and the resulting active commitment to less to zero plastic consumption.
 
 With the exception of the German school in Speyer, the schools participating in the project are all schools which, due to their proximity to the sea, experience directly how harmful plastic waste is to the marine ecosystem. With the Rhine, Speyer lies on a large tributary river, through which a large part of the waste also reaches the sea and from which the effects of plastic waste on the environment can also be seen. All five schools intend to involve pupils aged between 16-18 years in the project. Five pupils and two teachers will travel to the respective project meetings in Germany, Portugal, Croatia, Italy and Greece. The students are accommodated in host families.
 
 The students will carry out a variety of activities related to plastic. There will be workshops to generate knowledge on the economic aspects of plastic use. The pupils will see films or film clips of the pollution of the rivers and seas. They will collect, sort and display plastic waste for the "school family", but also creatively convert it into art objects. They will keep plastic diaries and use the "My little plastic footprint" app to create their own plastic footprint. They will also find out about waste separation and waste disposal on excursions to the waste management yard and visit a manufacturer of plastic bottles made from recycled plastic. There will also be discussions with local / national politicians and young people from the Fridays for Future Organization.
 
 Cooperation with external partners is possible at all five school locations. In this way, the pupils have access to scientific educational institutions that focus on the effects of plastic on our environment and thus also on ourselves. In Speyer there is an opportunity to cooperate with SeaLife, which for us is a particularly attractive location for the results of this project. First and foremost, the presentation of "art objects" made of plastic waste is possible there, but also motivational videos for a more sustainable use of plastic articles can be shown to the visitors.
 
 At all participating schools, the topic can be built into the curriculum of the participating classes and made available to further classes in the form of teaching material. The schools hope to use plastic more sustainably at their own school and beyond.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077338.title: Happy schools 2020
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077338.summary: The Erasmus+ project “Following the footprints of the emperors”, a cooperationbetween nine different schools from nine different European countries, has motivatedthe participants from Portugal, Croatia and Germany to cooperate further in a smaller-scale, joint project. A   fruitful   discussion   about   happiness   and   its   various   forms   made   clear   to   theaforementioned participants that happiness is a topic that is often widely ignored atour   schools,   although   we   were   quickly   able   to   show   a   wide   variety   of   directconnections between happiness, schooling and education. That inspired us to developthe idea of a European project about happiness. In our eyes it is productive to includea Finish school in our cooperation, not only because it would be a means to widen ourcooperation both geographically and culturally, but also because research has shownthat the Finish are the world champions of happiness. Therefore, we installed aneTwinning group in November of 2019 to initiate and establish contact to a Finnishschool.  It is the goal of our project to develop open educational resources (OER) and createmodules focussed on the topic of happiness that can be used by other schools interms of ideas and structure if they want to deal with it. By developing the differentmodules and intensively dealing with fostering and realizing happiness in schoolingand educational contexts at our schools, we wish to make our schools happier placesof learning and developement.   The various modules deal with happiness in general and at schools in particular, stressand countermeasures, the influence of places of education and learning on motivationand success, positive learning, happiness in creative processes and the EuropeanUnion as a project of peace. The participating schools are all experienced in planning and realizing Erasmus+projects.   Whereas   the  Finnish  and  Croatian  schools  are   both   high   schools,   thePortuguese and German schools are vocational colleges. The participating studentsare between 16 and 19 years old. The variety of activities to be carried out ranges from surveys, eTwinning projects,creative tasks (creation of logos, musical and artistic tasks, handicraft), a writingcompetition, the creation of manuals by learners for learners, examples of best-practise and learning materials that should all be integrated into the OERs. Thediversity of projects, methods and perspectives will keep students’ motivation highand addresses their own cultural, social and economic diversity.  Integrating those OERs in class at the participating schools will have a long-termeffect. Both the Finish and German school plan to offer “happiness” as a compulsorysubject choice, the Croatian and Portuguese will use the materials in a wide variety ofsubjects, including social sciences, religious education and ethics, history, art, musicand English. The nature of the OER and their easy dissemination will enable otherschools to both use and develop the materials further and thus even widening theirintercultural and cross-cultural impact. It is therefore that the modules will be bothdeveloped in the languages of the participating countries and English.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077339.title: Sports meet Inclusion
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077339.summary:
Since the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) came into force in Germany in 2009, the term inclusion has been the topic of conversation everywhere. Especially since the CRPD stipulates the changeover to an inclusive education and training system. The German school system, and thus physical education, are now increasingly focused on teaching achievement- and behaviorally heterogeneous students together and thus taking responsibility for a more equitable society. Our project "Sports meet Inclusion" could make an important contribution to this. The content focus of the "Sports meet Inclusion" project is on exercise ideas and examples for the concrete implementation of inclusion and sports. Among other things, inclusive sports such as goalball and sitting volleyball are addressed. Implementation possibilities such as parajudo, wheelchair basketball and parahandball were also learned about by the students involved, to name just a small selection. On a theoretical level, our project "Sports meet Inclusion" addressed general principles of an inclusive exercise and sports program as well as organizational processes. These were worked out together in a guideline called "Sports meet Inclusion" and the results of this work process were recorded in it. The objective of our project, to make the topic of inclusion directly experienceable with the help of sports not only theoretically, but also practically, could be fulfilled in the context of our project work. We were also able to achieve our goal of promoting mutual understanding for the challenges and different realities of life for students with and without special needs. For the participating Erasmus students, this means raising awareness of inclusion through inclusive games and sports (e.g. goalball and sitting volleyball) as well as experiencing the problems of inclusion for themselves in the course of the political simulation game "Model United Nations" in Mannheim's city hall (May 2022) with six other schools in Mannheim. The practical transfer of the project to the schools achieved another goal. Erasmus students taught the game of Goalball to visually impaired children in Romania and introduced the game in physical education classes at IGMH and SPOGI. By teaching basic understanding of inclusion, diversity and common European values, students realized that living diversity in school is an opportunity that benefits all students. In addition to strengthening foreign languages and intercultural competencies, organizational and creative skills were also strengthened among the students and teachers involved. The students jointly and independently developed hoodies for the project and created a new school Erasmus corner at IGMH, which not only informs about the project results, but also acts as a meeting place for meetings and exchange of talks. Our project also aimed to contribute to the knowledge transfer and strengthening of teachers' skills to promote and support diversity and inclusion in the participating schools. The participating teachers were able to use the knowledge gained through the project work to successfully achieve the accreditation of IGMH as an Erasmus school. The focus of the accreditation was on the objective of strengthening inclusion at IGMH. Our project lasted three years and was carried out with a total of 21 students and 9 teachers from IGMH (Mannheim/DE), SPOGI (Zagreb/CR) and Liceul Tehnologic "Dimitrie Leonida" (Constanta/RO). The students are between 9th and 11th grade (15 to 18 years old). The results were bundled and implemented in the form of a guide. The results were achieved by means of group work, independent student activity under the guidance of experts, hands-on experimental learning, knowledge transfer at extracurricular learning sites and through the preparation and follow-up of multimedia presentations. Through the numerous presentations and continuous cooperation with the partner schools, foreign language skills were improved and intensified. All project results were made available on the e-twinning platform. The guide and the teaching modules were also published on the project results platform. Displays, posters, flyers, etc. have found a permanent place in the schools. The project material has been processed and can be used in the schools as a copy template and illustrative material. 
In summary, it is important to emphasize once again that the project activities were worked through in different steps: First the theoretical examination of the topic of inclusion with the simulation game Model United Nations, then the own practical experience through Goalball and Sitting Volleyball. In the next step, these experiences were transformed into a teaching concept with methodical exercise series and tested on students. And as a last and crucial step, it was about the long-term benefit for the school by carrying our concepts into the physical education lessons of our school and these inclusive games are now firmly anchored in our school curriculum. The whole thing is reinforced by our new Erasmus Corner, which is very popular in our school.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077342.title: Tourism and sustainability in european coastal areas
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077342.summary: In light of the increasing negative impacts of tourism on European coastal areas, environment and sustainability have become a matter of considerable importance in modern-day society. Initiatives such as Fridays for future indicate that even the youth among Europe recognizes this a relevant topic. Thus, our project Tourism and Sustainability in European Coastal Areas should draw attention to the significance of creating a new kind of tourism, namely one that suits today’s requirements of environmental and touristic sustainability to counteract the negative consequences of the growing (mass) tourism. Our plan was to raise awareness among our students about the unfavorable repercussions of “traditional” tourism to a country’s local nature, heritage and environment, explaining the causes of it (for example competition in the international hotel industries) and demonstrating possibilities to enhance a sustainable way of tourism (both on a personal and on a more global way). This way our students were required to think about a kind of tourism that creates a positive impact on the inhabitants, environment, culture and economy, while leaving only a minimal footprint on the surrounding ecosystem and respecting local traditions, natural resources and residents. The matter of sustainability was the most crucial aspect of our work. As the topic is quite ambitious and demanding the participating students were supposed to be aged between 16 and 19, interested in European topics and well-grounded in the English language (project language) to be able to plan and put into practice such a sophisticated project. Due to the consequences of the pandemic situation, also younger students or students with a lower level of English had to be integrated. To ensure a wide-ranging overview of the situation in Europe as a whole, our project was realized with groups of about 20 students and 2 teachers from 6 different European countries (Croatia, Germany, Greece, Italy, Portugal and Spain). The schools taking part in the program were all located in a touristic European coastal area, either on an island or peninsula. All of them were affected directly or indirectly by (seasonal) tourism, hence the topic of our project was relevant to all those present at the educational institutions. Our project included six international meetings (one in each country) and some project related activities in the periods in between the on-site presences. Assuming the main issues during the project meetings was tourism and sustainability, divergent priorities and key aspects for each meeting were determined. Starting with an analysis of tourism (Which areas does it affect and to what extent does it work successfully? What are potential beneficial or negative side effects of tourism?) we later on examined various aspects of these areas that may have an effect on the development of tourism, focusing alternately on nature, history, cultural heritage, inhabitants and the touristic behavior of every individual. We tried to contrast the popular form of all-inclusive tourism to an eco-friendlier kind of tourism, also considering cruise tourism. For this purpose, we got in contact to different NGO’s, local politicians, hotel managers, tourists and locals to get access to all different angles. We aimed to investigate the role of all participants in the tourism sector as well as the role of our students themselves regarding the future development of tourism and the questions how to make an indispensable contribution to more sustainability. Through the usage of surveys, interviews, personal diaries, photos and video recordings, we recorded a part of our findings in our final products, namely a book containing a report of each meeting, the analyzed surveys, conclusions of the realized interviews, short films and podcasts on the advantages and disadvantages of tourism in European coastal areas, brochures on ways of achieving a more sustainable tourism, as well as a website containing some basic information about the project meetings, the projects topic was opened to other persons. Due to the project, we did not only promote our student’s key competences (methodological, intercultural, linguistic) and their awareness for the increasing need of sustainability, but also have made a small contribution to reach a wider audience (all people participating in the school communities as well as many inhabitants of the corresponding regions). If our (participating) students and some other residents changed their views on tourism and realized that everyone can contribute to a more sustainable tourism, we mainly have achieved of our aims.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077397.title: Every move counts
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077397.summary:
The project “Every move counts”  was initiated as we see that a majority of our students spend a lot of their free time using electronic recreation and less and less time being physically active. The number of students who practise sport as a regular free time activity is decreasing constantly. It is clear that regular physical activity plays an important role for the foundation of a happy, healthy and longer life whereas inactivity brings dangers such as heart disease, diabetes and obesity. This is, of course, not only our personal impressions but various studies show that a high percentage of students’ physical functional capacity (endurance, speed, strength, mobility, balance, basic motor skills) is far from good.  For example, in Finland 5th and 8th grade students are checked for their physical performance for their national Move! Programme and only one third of students reach level good.
 Apart from that, at all our schools, we have students who aren’t integrated socially for different reasons (language, behavioural, mental problems) and we find that sport is a good way to access  and integrate this group of students. 
 
 School is a really good place to tackle all those problems as it is the only time in a lifespan where everyone can be introduced to physical skills and activities.
 
 Six schools from six countries take part in this project: Croatia, Finland, Germany, Italy, Spain and the UK. Our participants are aged between 13 – 16  and attend different forms of secondary and primary schools and one SEN school. We are going to take about 125 students  on LTTAs but many more people are going to be involved in our project through challenges, European sports week, eTwinning projects and healthy food days at all schools. So the number of students involved will exceed several hundred. 
 Students at our schools come from all sorts of social backgrounds, we have a lot of students with low school performance. Our UK partner is a SEN school with students with various difficulties (physical and mental)
 Our project’s main objective is increasing our students’ participation in sports and other active leisure pursuits, which will bring by many positive effects.  In addition, our students are going to learn how a healthy diet, physical activity and personal well-being are connected and will perceive that physical activity can bring them enjoyment and thus they will continue being active. 
 Besides, students facing exclusion will be integrated through our activities as they will give them opportunities to connect, boost their self-esteem and make them feel accepted. We will adjust our activities so that students with different abilities will be able to take part successfully and feel well. Many activities will focus on our students being active and learning with all senses but we will also activities where students get some theoretical background about the connection of physical activity and health.
 
 Our students are going to be involved in the planning and implementation of our activities and are thus going to learn and improve many competences, particularly the personal, social and learning to learn competence. They will enjoy the physical activities because they are student centred, fun and safe and using different learning methods. Our competitions will be considerate of their needs so that they are motivating and fun. We are going to prioritise the LOVE of sport above LEARNING sport so that they become healthy active adults. 
 
 That is one of the long term results we want to achieve:  healthy active human beings, who know how important it is to live healthily and actively and who are well integrated into society. We want to change their attitudes so that they  understand that regular physical activity is a requisite for their mental, physical, and professional longevity. Apart from changing their attitudes students are going to improve other skills like language and ITC skills. 
 Teachers will improve their methodology and will be inspired and even more motivated by their visits. They will also disseminate their knowledge to colleagues at home.
 The products we are planning are teaching resources, an educational unit and several guides and leaflets, all about physical activity, healthy lifestyle and well-being which will be available online so that European teachers can use them and be inspired by them so that EU money for our project is spent in the most effective and sustainable way. They will also be used at our schools.
 
 But there are more long term benefits of our projects:  we will strengthen our students intrinsic motivation, their self-confidence and independence and their key-competences.  Also the attitudes they develop will outlast the project and make them healthy, active, young Europeans. Taking part in the project will be an invaluable and unique experience which will make a difference in their life and will also influence emotions, attitudes and will make them realize that every move counts.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077401.title: Get together - Bridges connect people in Europe
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077401.summary:
The present project was about a German-French-Italian-Croatian cooperation in the fields of construction technology, architecture and design with a focus on the architecture of bridges. The project aimed at the realization that bridges connect people, both in everyday life and in a figurative sense. the visits aimed at the realization that bridges connect people in Europe, that the history of bridges does not stop at political borders and that architectural styles are witnesses for the continuous mutual influences in Europe over the centuries. The students gained this knowledge by visiting and analyzing notable buildings from the Middle Ages as well as from modern architecture. The architectural tours furthermore served as a basis for the design of architectural signposts, which broadened the students' knowledge about bridges along the centuries and inspired them for their own creations. The findings of the analysis of existing bridges were used to work out one's own design of a bridge and to reproduce it as a scale model in order to grasp and correctly assess the technical features of these structures. Another important aspect of the present project concept was the promotion of intercultural competence, which led to the reduction of any reservations or inhibitions, because in a united Europe it is essential for citizens to approach European partners with an open mind and interest. The students from Germany, Croatia, Italy and France took on the challenge of designing, sketching and building a bridge model, not only using their creative skills but also improving their teamwork and intercultural communication. In each phase of the project, students were divided into mixed groups consisting of members from all four countries. Each group was tasked with developing a bridge model that was not only aesthetically pleasing, but also had to be functional and stable. This required close collaboration and the exchange of ideas across linguistic and cultural boundaries. The students sketched their designs and discussed in detail the materials used. This is where the different cultural perspectives came into play, as each nation brought its own experience and knowledge of construction. The diversity of ideas led to innovative solutions and helped the students strengthen their teamwork. Once the designs were determined, the groups began to implement their models. They worked hard together to build the bridges with care and precision, using materials such as wood, wire, and even recycled items to make their visions a reality. The highlight of the project was the final competition, where the students presented their bridges to an interested audience and a panel of expert judges. This competition not only provided an opportunity for the students to feel proud of their collective work, but also boosted their self-confidence and presentation skills. Overall, the group work between German, Croatian, Italian and French students was an inspiring 
 xperience that not only emphasized the importance of working together across cultural boundaries, but also showed the potential of young people to create amazing things together. It was a project that built bridges not only out of materials, but also between the hearts and minds of the young participants.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077466.title: Traces of our ancestors - European regions in the course of time
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077466.summary:
Traces of our ancestors is a project developed by a group of students from the Quirinus-Gymnasium in 2020. The aim was to bring together young people aged 16-18 to experience historical developments of the second half of the 20th century in their respective cities and regions. Thus, five schools from Portugal, Croatia, Italy, Poland and we as coordinators came together to cooperatively create an EBook to present similarities and differences of each regions historical development. Each nation planned their activities independently presenting the city and region from a  historical perspective. When the application was submitted in 2020, it was not foreseeable to what extent the planned activities could be realized. Thus, some changes are found in the application and current description of the respective activities. The first mobility to Rio Maior, Portugal in February 2021 included visits to historical places (Lisbon, Salinas, Óbidos, Sintra) and a discussion with the former EU Member of Parliament Carlos Coehlo. The second trip to Croatia in March 2021 focused on the development of the cities of Zagreb and Rijeka. In the city of Varazdin we had the chance to travel back in time and get a glimpse of what life was like during the Middle Age in Croatia.
In September, the host schools visited Neuss. Here Roman traces in Neuss & Cologne, as well as Jewish traces were found. Important industrial sites of the Ruhr area (Bochum Mining Museum and Zollverein Coal Mine Industrial Complex) as initiators of the European Coal Community were also visited. In addition, we were given a guided tour of the Düsseldorf state parliament with a member of parliament and gained insight into the various areas of work. Finally, there was a discussion with Dr. Heusgen (Chairman of the Munich Security Conference) about current developments and trends in Europe. The focus was on the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The fourth mobility in Szubin, Poland led among other things to Torún, here the parliament was visited and afterwards the birth house of Kopernikus and a gingerbread workshop were attended. In Bydgoszcz there was a guided EU discussion, which could not be held due to technical malfunction. There was also an interview with contemporary witnesses of the region around Szubin, which was planned and carried out by the students.
During the last mobility in Bernalda, Italy, we visited historical places and met celebrities that shaped the history of Italy in the mid-20th century. Especially the visit to Aliano and Matera were very formative and exciting.
In summary, the project makes clear that all visited cities and regions share different but also common historical developments.Thus Roman & Jewish traces showed up during all mobilities.
The EBook gives an insight into the gained content knowledge of the individual regions in Europe, which represent the traces of our ancestors.In addition, all participants of the project have also been able to gain many intercultural experiences and make new friendships and contacts that will last even after the end of the project.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077506.title: Reconstructing individual fates in World War One
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077506.summary:
The European Union has ensured peace in Central Europe for 70 years. Even in regions where only a few decades ago war, dictatorships and civil war prevailed, it has helped to resolve violent conflicts. Now, however, the unique peace project "EU" has come under threat. Populist politicians are trying to blame the European Union for national problems, playing on the keyboard of nationalist resentment, distorting truths, fomenting intolerance and racism, and raising new border fences. The European idea is forgotten, and happiness is once again sought in the nation-state. But by once again seeking salvation in the nation-state, we separate ourselves from our European neighbors, create national identity by separating ourselves from others, and European partners threaten to become foreign-policy enemies once again.

 A glance at the past is sufficient to show the disastrous consequences of nationalist thinking. The First World War is considered the "primordial catastrophe of the 20th century" (George F. Kennan). Nationalist hubris gave rise to mistrust, even hostility, toward European neighbors, alliances were forged, and a spiral of rearmament emerged. Finally, a spark was enough to trigger the catastrophe. Even then, people did not really believe in a new war, since they maintained intensive trade relations, the upper classes traveled on vacation to neighboring European countries and sent their sons abroad to university, and many workers saw themselves united in "international socialism". Nevertheless, war broke out and claimed over 17 million lives.

In times of resurgent nationalism and growing skepticism towards the EU (especially among young people), the five participating schools from Germany, France, Croatia, Portugal and Romania sensitized their students to the above-mentioned dangers by showing them how the societies of the time, the war participants and their relatives suffered from the First World War, but also how they saw their war opponents and how possibly propagandistic distorted images influenced their perception. The participating schools supported each other in achieving the project goal, as each school has its own potential with regard to the topic, from which the other project partners will benefit (e.g. special knowledge in memorial work, IT and new media, experience with projects, etc.)
The focus was on individual fates from the home towns or regions of the individual countries. The students went on a local/regional search for traces after they had worked out the involvement of their country (or the country to which the place and the region had previously belonged) in history lessons or also in interdisciplinary lessons on history/religion/ etc.. Using pictorial, written and figurative sources, they worked out the "stories" of war participants and their relatives.

 Building on their findings from monuments, archives, museums, etc., the students documented individual fates on film using their smartphones, e.g., by reenacting historical scenes, reading out letters and newspaper reports, recording battlefields and cemeteries, inserting film footage, and so on. But they also learned about World War I from the perspective of the participating countries, from the point of view of certain key issues, and discussed the dangers of nationalism, peacekeeping measures, and the importance of the European Union as a guarantor of a peaceful Europe. Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine, which broke out during the project, gave the topic a frightening topicality.

At the end of the project there are now, on the one hand, cinematic documentaries from different national perspectives, which provide an insight into the thinking, feeling and actions of the soldiers and their relatives and are combined into a series whose transitions contrast the suffering of the people in a Europe shaken by war with the partnership work and friendly meetings of young people today in a common Europe.
Both the cinematic documentaries and other project outcomes, such as local and regional tracking tours, exhibitions on the fates of war participants and relatives, creative works on the First World War on the positive role of the EU after the Second World War and as guarantors of peace, will be made available to the local and regional public in order to convey the project's message outside the school.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077512.title: Yummy and healthy!
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077512.summary:
With our three-year project “yummy & healthy” we worked on an approach to counteract the increasingly unhealthy diet of young people, here: our students. The participants developed an awareness of food and nutrition in general, reconsidered their eating habits and buying behaviour in particular, acquired a broad technical and factual knowledge and learned to make simple and healthy food and drinks themselves. The connection between poor nutrition and health consequences became clear to everyone.
The project's concept and course were related to the topics “health and well-being” and “teaching and learning foreign languages” as defined in the application. In addition to those contents on healthy eating and language lessons, the focus was on overarching goals such as the “development and strengthening of key competences” and “social inclusion”.
All project participants dealt with theoretical knowledge and practical tasks in the areas of: fruits, vegetables, milk, and dairy products as well as cow's milk alternatives, whole meal products and white flour, food and drinks, fast food as opposed to slow food, fat, and sugar as well as sugar substitutes, taste, spices and herbs, nutritional values, vitamins and fiber, calories and calorie consumption, artificial additives, shopping behaviour and eating habits, the food-traffic-light and alternatives, regional products and products from overseas, industrial processing of raw materials as opposed to organic products, cultivation, harvesting and marketing of food. They gained many new insights and learnt a lot. The outputs and outcomes are complex.
In addition, the participants expanded their knowledge of foreign languages and/or German as a second language. Because of our international cooperation, not only during those 4 mobilities, they strengthened their intercultural skills because students from four countries, but with more than 15 different migration background countries, languages, and cultures took part in our project.
IT skills were improved, presentation techniques were learnt, and new programs and platforms were tried out.
The project's content was cross-curricular, repeatedly revised by the teachers and adapted to the needs of the learners. During the regular Zoom conferences, milestones were established for achieving our objectives, outcomes were presented, materials were exchanged, and novel planning steps were executed. There was a very close and successful cooperation between the 4 partner schools from Finland, Croatia, Greece and Germany. The Erasmus+ teams of all participating schools were supported by social and special education teachers, school counsellors and other teaching staff. That allowed students with special needs, refugees and newly arrived immigrants to participate in the project. The school authorities supported the project with the school's own resources, such as exemptions, specialist rooms and the use of the school's infrastructures were made available,
The school community (staff, parents, and students) was continuously informed about the current situation. That led to the content being anchored in everyday school life and some changes have already been achieved (better food in the canteens, some project topics are part of the curricula now,  ...).
The learning successes in the field of key skills are significant: communicative skills have been significantly improved. During the course, the students worked measurably more cooperatively, proactively and in a more goal-orientated manner. In the field of individual skills, the participants developed strategies for self-organization and increasingly gained self-confidence. Being part of the team made them proud and confident. They stayed in contact with students from the partner schools even beyond the project work, and friendships developed. The sense of responsibility for the entire project increased.
We did not achieve all project goals. On the one hand, Corona prevented various planned activities. Homeschooling and the different ways in which the pandemic was handled in the 4 countries made some implementations extremely difficult during the first 1.5 years. The costs also increased because of Corona. On the other hand, the sudden death of our colleague Thomas Bieser tore an unbridgeable gap. We grieved together and through that project, he will be in our hearts forever.

By that project, we lived the European idea and Europe grew together closer. Due to binding structures, a European Day took place at every mobility. All participants were and are aware that we only could carry out our “yummy & healthy” project and mobilities with the help of the European Erasmus+ program. Thank you, EU!
...and: We carry on! The content is too important.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077515.title: We shape our future
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077515.summary:
With our project “We shape our future” we want to actively participate in the positive transformation of our world for its people, nature and prosperity. We want to strengthen universal peace and want to raise awareness that inequality and poverty are the greatest global challenge. We want to work with our students towards the goals of Agenda 2030 because only with collective participation we can shift the world onto a fair and sustainable path. We need to get students to take over responsibility for the world’s future.
 Especially after the coronavirus pandemic, we have to reshape our world and our daily lives and the goals of Agenda 2030 are the best tools to use in order to promote a new awareness. European schools and young people have a central role to play if we want to foster international solidarity and a new concept of citizenship
 
 The project “We shape our future” is accomplished by five schools (GER, BG, IT, SP, HR). In this project we want to empower our students to actively take part in shaping a sustainable future. With our project we want to focus on the values that lie in diversity, equal opportunities, sustainability and well-being.
 We bring our creativity and work force together to create material for activities, so that fellow students and the local community will get involved in our process to shape our future. 
 We will explore the impact of non sustainability on oneself, our own family and friends, our own future plans, the neighbourhood, city and the planet. We ask and answer the questions of how students can contribute in their daily life. We discuss the impact of inequalities in our daily lives (e.g. gender gap, health inequalities) and research on different kind of diversity and inequalities. We create material to raise awareness and share it. We plan activities/events and perform them. We build international contacts.
 
 We have decided to focus on five goals of Agenda 2030: Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages. Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls. Reduce inequality within and among countries. Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable. Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns. Of course, we also have the focus on quality education, peace, justice and strong institutions and a strong and reliable partnership.
 
 In working on an intellectual topic, students build up awareness. In creating material, they take over responsibility. In exchanging experience, they practice communication and in planning and performing activities for others they experience their impact. All these steps will lead them to seeing the chances of participating for a better world.
 
 At the respective schools we prepare (learning) material for activities and events that will first be carried out at the own school. Then we exchange materials and experience so that the partner schools can carry out the same event. In the second year we want to bring our events to the next level and cooperate with out-of-school organisations in school and out of school. We want to collaborate on a local and regional level.
  
 We want to try a new concept for the international meetings. We will meet for three small workshop meetings with 10-18 participants, while we want to organize two big workshop meetings for 80 students. We believe that getting more students together in a meeting can have a synergetic effect on networking, friendships and the involvement back home. The big meetings will not take place at the schools but in a remote group accommodation to give all students much time together and the students of the hosting country the opportunity to stay with the guests. Travelling students will be aged 13-16. Everybody will improve their English language skills. The host will care for arrangements whereas the guests will organize and offer the workshops.
 
 In Italy media experts help us with the concept of later media results. In Spain students get the opportunity of helping in an organization that works towards reducing inequality. In Bulgaria we focus on health living. In Germany we focus on the impact of our consumption on our environment and students learn about the healthy impact of fresh food. In Croatia we will work with a video-making expert so that we finally will have a promotion video for our goals.
 
 On a long-term basis, students of all partner schools improve their language skills, their awareness of healthy lifestyle, the value of equal opportunities, the value of diversity and the conditions of sustainability. In general, this project is a great opportunity to combine digital, physical and intellectual abilities as well as language skills. The overall objective is the development of continuous learning in a European collaborative environment with positive effects on the relation among the community in order to form a strong personality of the teenagers

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077527.title: How Roman are you?
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077527.summary:
The project entitled "How Roman are you?" was initiated by the German school IGS Lüneburg and took place in the period from 2019 to 2023. With the help of the E-Twinning platform, the following partner schools were found: ITT Marconi in Rovereto (Italy), Osnovna skola Bartola Kasica in Vinkovci (Croatia), Colegio de Nuestra Senora de las Mercedes in Granada (Spain), Agrupamento de Escolas Rosa Ramalho in Barcelos (Portugal) and 4th Gymnasium Volos in Volos (Greece). The implementation was made quite difficult by the Corona pandemic. Nevertheless, the project could be carried out because the project period was extended and travelling became possible again. Due to the new scheduling of the individual mobilities, some planned activities could not be carried out during the mobilities. However, all partner schools made an effort to make the programme as appropriate as possible to the theme and exciting. In the first mobility in Italy (end of November 2021), the focus was on history to find out how the respective partner countries came into being and to what extent their origins can be traced back to the Roman Empire. Unfortunately, the German team was not able to take part in this mobility, as at that time all schools in Lower Saxony were banned from travelling by the state ministry due to Corona. 
In May 2022, the mobility took place in Vinkovci, Croatia, under the consideration of Roman culture. The group mainly focused on the way of life of the Romans and made links with today. Teachers conducted workshops and lectures with their groups about life in ancient Rome.
In October 2022, the mobility took place in Granada, Spain. There, the pupils and teachers focused on Roman architecture. Not only Roman buildings in their own country were presented, but also different excavation sites were visited, which showed the structure and construction of Roman houses/villas. In addition, different architectural structures were recreated in miniature with plasticine.
The subsequent mobility in Germany took place at the end of November 2022. The focus topic for this mobility was "language". The pupils mainly studied the Latin language in order to explore the common origin of the languages of all participating countries. They also discovered that many terms are similar in the different languages and that some Latin words are still used.
In March 2023, they went to Barcelos in Portugal, where the theme was "Democracy". For example, the students from each country gave short presentations on the development of democracy in their countries. This was very interesting for the participating students, as some countries are still very young democracies and they thus learned that the form of government "democracy" is not self-evident.
In the last mobility, in May 2023, which took place in Volos/Greece, the topic was "Sport and Games". There, the pupils of all participating countries competed in a competition of running disciplines and basketball. In addition, various games from the respective countries were presented in short presentations based on sports in the Roman Empire.
Between the mobilities, the small groups from the participating countries worked on the content and language of the preparations for the coming exchange, mostly in the form of a working group. In the process, contacts were established in advance and, above all, knowledge of digital tools was trained. Especially in the phase of the corona-related lockdown, additional video conferences took place in order to stay in contact and continue working together. This enabled the students to establish initial contact with each other and a sense of community slowly developed. Due to the extension of time, the project has accompanied the pupils over a period of four years and has thus made up an essential part of their youth. Besides the content-related learning gain, it was above all the cultural exchange with the host families and the host school that left a lasting impression on the students. It was not only their linguistic competence in English that was promoted, but above all the insight into another culture, another family life as well as other school systems. 
Certain commonalities and differences could be clearly identified. Our initial intention to motivate pupils to develop intercultural competences has proved to be an attained goal. In the process, our students have become quite aware of how much the culture of Germany is based on the ancient Roman culture; much to their astonishment.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077534.title: European CNC-Network - Train for EUROPE - Digital Revolution 4.0
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077534.summary:
The school partnership is an initiative of the „European CNC Network“, a consortium of more than 30 vocational schools from Europe that has been in existence since 2004. The most well-known and probably most successful school project within our network was the „Train for EUROPE“, which was awarded the European Youth Charlemagne Prize in 2010.

At that time, the 24 participating partner schools, as part of the school partnership „Train for EUROPE“, collaboratively produced locomotives and individual wagons with characteristic motifs on a model train scale using computer-controlled machine tools. For example, the wagon from Germany displayed a letterpress encased in an open book in honor of Johannes Gutenberg, while the Italian wagon showcased historic inventions by Leonardo da Vinci. At the conclusion of the project, the participants exchanged copies of their own wagons among themselves, ensuring that each of the participating partner schools possessed its own train with at least ten unique wagons. These were displayed in the school foyers in glass cabinets and were used for special events such as „Open House“ days.

The partnership described here directly builds upon the success of the „Train for EUROPE“ with a digital upgrade. The follow-up project focused on interactivity through the digital networking of the existing wagons using modern microprocessor technology, taking into account the current requirements from the „Industry 4.0“ future strategy. The chosen project title is based on the widely embraced industry concept, the „Digital Revolution 4.0“, which, after the invention of the steam engine, mass production on assembly lines, and the introduction of computer technology, is now the fourth stage advancing the intelligent integration of humans and machines in the digital transformation. Our „Train for EUROPE - Digital Revolution 4.0“ precisely adhered to these requirements and, in a sustainable learning environment, also provided an attractive training object for later instructional use.

To achieve this, the existing motif wagons were digitally enhanced in the spirit of STE(A)M by incorporating servomotors, audiovisual effects, and other creative design elements. An interactive user web interface served as a gateway for interactions with visitors. Clicking on the control panel button generated a radio-controlled impulse, activating the audiovisual motion effects of the selected wagon. Simultaneously, the interested user received information about the respective wagon motif and the school that built the wagon. Through web-based networking, it was also possible to control wagons at other school locations. Users could thus operate from a distance across Europe and use an integrated webcam to observe animations at other schools.

The complexity of the project idea posed high demands on the information technology implementation of digital networking, which was embedded in the students' regular curriculum. The students, aged 15 to 20, were supervised by at least two teachers at their school. The expansion of the „Train for EUROPE“ served as a „pedagogical catalyst“, motivating the development of fundamental skills and key competencies. It provided students with a complex action product, the opportunity to work on a challenging technical task alongside other European partners and learn from each other. Through action-oriented peer-to-peer learning, students internalized the subject matter much more intensively, as they independently acquired and deepened their knowledge, sharing and discussing what they learned with other learners.

During the nearly three-year project duration, six project meetings were held. Activities followed the phases of project progress, with early stages being significantly influenced by Covid-19 restrictions. Responsibility for individual project tasks was distributed among the partner schools in working lines and groups. The time between project meetings was utilized to complete agreed-upon tasks and advance the actual project work. Students communicated and discussed their solutions regularly using appropriate web-based groupware platforms.

The collaborative work on a technical challenge intensified the international and intercultural dialogue among the students. By communicating in the working language, English, students simultaneously experienced the development of their language skills. The joint project work fostered a „European Spirit“ that valued and respected both the commonalities and unique differences among the partners.

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077543.title: Sailing the sea of time: European history as OUR (hi)story
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077543.summary:
"Frieden ist nicht selbstverständlich." These words of Jean-Claude Juncker were central for our project which was addressed to students aged 13-17 years from six European countries. In a time of increasing separatism, nationalism and latent racism also in EU countries the motivation of our project was to make our students aware that peace and international cooperation is a treasure which has to be protected actively. Our aim was to promote respect – for both persons and cultures - and responsibility – social and personal - as values for a fair and non-discriminatory society. Our students learned about constructive and destructive moments of European history, found out about cultural connections among our countries and detected values which connect them across times and borders to one cultural unity: Europe. Working on the project collaboratively, the participants themselves practiced constructive and respectful intercultural interaction.  
 
 Objectives of our project were: 
 - increased sense of respect and responsibility
 - strengthening of transversal key competences such as digital, language, learning, social and civic competences
 - improved creative and interdisciplinary thinking, cultural awareness and expression
 - a broader European dimension of learning and teaching.
 
 To reach this we carried out the following activities:
 1. APPROACH (year 1): One starting point of our project was the past: myths and philosophy from Greek antiquity as cradle of European culture. Myths tell us about men's hopes and fears and the struggle for defining one's role in the world, philosophy interprets it. Our students showed their interpretation of antiquity creatively in videos, texts and sketches (and developed it later into board games and on stage) and by comparing ancient fears and hopes to their own. This connection to their present became more intense due to our ice breaking and approaching activities of year 1. Spending most of this time in lockdown they couldn't meet their peers physically, but on TwinSpace and videoconference, compare their momentary situation and dreams for future.
 2. THEATRE YEAR (year 2): In year 2 we moved from cooperation to collaboration. Task for students was to create together a drama with the motto "United in diversity". They invented plot and scenes by collaboratively (TwinSpace, video conference). Local research about persons of cultural importance and historical circumstances  and collaborative writing of linking themes and scenes in international groups (online, finally as part of two physical meetings) alternated. They worked out how to express on stage the importance of cultural expression and variety, common values and, at the same time, to show that spreading these values is a constant process that needs active engagement and responsibilty also beyond European borders, e.g. for times of colonialism. They integrated philosophical thoughts from Greek antiquity, had acting training with local drama teachers or extern actors and, when physical meetings finally were allowed again in all partner regionals, performed their drama together.
 3. BOARD GAME YEAR (year 3): Under the impression of the war at the European borders stressed the motto "Frieden ist nicht selbstverständlich" even more and promoted the chance of cultural connection as statement against war. The kick-off LTTA of this year in East Croatia made us work both on friendship among European artists as on the fact that there had been war in Europe, in many respects similar to the recent one, also three decades ago (the Balkan wars). The students visited memorials and talked to testimonies; they made the topic 'exchange war for peace, confrontation for collaboration, an Iron curtain for reconciliation' prominent in their production of this year - collaborative board games that show European biographies in historical context, each game taking it starting point in one of the countries of our partnership.They developed challenges and questions (historical, cultural, fun ones) for each game together online in international groups; physical meetings marked  the transition to a new step of this main activity: a workshop in 3D printing f.x. allowed local creationof equipment. The final products were played and evaluated together, later made available at every partner school. 
 
Methods we used were: cooperative learning such as collaborative writing online or various workshops on-site; research (library, online, interviews); group work (e.g. jigsaw method); product orientation; blended learning.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-DE03-KA229-077544.title: Cars and Light
2020-1-DE03-KA229-077544.summary:
In the "Cars and Light" project, the students of both schools planned and created a teaching unit with a 1:1 practice-oriented partition on the subject of car lighting systems, identical in construction first at one and then at the other school. This is now being used at both schools. The project therefore resulted in a high-quality, standardized product that will be used in the classroom in the long term and offers transparency and international comparability with regard to the competences to be achieved. This cooperation promoted the key competences of the students to an exceptional degree. Next to the technical competences this were the intercultural competence and the language and communication competence.

Due to Corona, only 11 instead of the planned 14 students took part in the mobilities. The project had to be extended because no travel was possible in the initially planned period. The traveling Croatian team consisted of 6 students and two technical teachers, the German team of 5 students and two teachers.

The work of the students began in advance of the exchange in the local teams with material inspection and project planning. Due to the circumstances, the international digital exchange beforehand was much shorter than planned, but the students got to know each other and reported on the status of preparations at their schools. Before the pupils visited the partner school, preparatory meetings took place, in which the rules of conduct were agreed, first insights into the culture and socio-economic situation of the partner country as well as into the language were given. The Croatian delegation then visited GKS Müllheim from March 28th, 2022 - April 9th, 2022, the delegation from Germany was at the Gospodarska Skola Istituto Professionale Buje from May 30th, 2022 - June 11th, 2022. The language of communication was English.

The joint project work formed the core of the exchange and was carried out daily in mixed teams in a core time of around 3 hours. The work was accompanied by additional modules in theory and practice, which secured the basics and were partly embedded in the regular motor vehicle lessons. In addition, the students took part in the regular classes at the schools, which were also almost exclusively in English. A special timetable was created for the guests, which made it possible for other classes to benefit from this exchange and gave the students an insight into the diverse range of schools. In this way, many contacts were made with students who were not involved in the project.

The school work was framed by company tours and visits to other schools and a cultural program that illustrated the operational world and the cultural characteristics of the respective countries. In particular, the training systems of both countries were compared. In Germany, the Croatian students got to know and appreciate the dual training system. In Croatia, the German students got an insight into school training and into workshops. This knowledge is essential for working in the European environment. It also increases students’ mobility in the European labor market.

Through the visits to companies and other schools in France and Slovenia, new, promising contacts were made, which give reason to hope for multi-national cooperation in the near future. Contacts with companies could also be intensified.
