2020-1-IT02-KA229-079340.title: Sea-Inspired Active Learning of United STEAM
2020-1-IT02-KA229-079340.summary:
This project started from a careful analysis of the needs of students who daily use a lot of new technologies but from which they are distant if not for reasons of play and leisure. The activities carried out made it possible to understand how behind everything that surrounds us in our daily lives there are mathematics, chemistry, physics and science, just like a sea that laps the coasts that surrounds it.  
In our project there have been two fundamental elements: the STEAM disciplines and the sea. For these two reasons we have chosen our partner countries that have been Croatia, Turkey, Greece and Latvia, all countries that live by the sea and whose history has been influenced by it. Moreover, underwater archaeology was another important element that gave our students the opportunity to know the auxiliary sciences of history and how technologies help it. In fact, the construction of an aquatic robot made it possible to observe the seabed, necessary in underwater research. The realization of these activities has been possible thanks to not only of the professionalism of the teachers of the partner countries but also by resorting to internationally renowned authorities such as the Superintendency of the Sea of the Region of Sicily and the Department of Biology of Development of the University of Palermo which gave availability for museum visits carried out. The project had the merit of linking art, history, sustainability and technology and this allowed to involve a large number of female students. It can be said that the basic elements of our project, are confirmed as an essential heritage for our future European citizens. The sea, an element common to partner countries, has been the element that has allowed planning  and realizing the main activities for each of the disciplines involved, consolidating the ability to integrate the different skills, acquired from different knowledge, to implement collaboration and cooperation between the disciplines, between students and among future European citizens. The activities carried out and involved in the development of logical thinking and the application of causality and effect, at the basis of any scientific discipline, has led the young people of the participating countries to rediscover what the element "sea" has represented in the development of European peoples and how much archaeological evidence offers possibility of acquiring awareness of one's own culture, made up of differences but also of elements common to other peoples. The project pursued a main goal: the acquisition of key citizenship skills by exploiting peer learning. 
Therefore, it was necessary to articulate this objective on two levels: to bring young students and female young students in particular closer to the new horizons offered by scientific disciplines, through a naturalistic, historical and artistic path of enhancement and knowledge of their own culture and archaeological heritage, in a European comparison perspective;
to stimulate the thinking of young people to study natural and eco-sustainable resources.
The study of the sea, linked to all the aspects in which it is involved in the course of historical times, has represented for young students an opportunity for reflection not only scientific, for its infinite implications for development, but also cultural, since it is the relationship that peoples have established with the sea that has influenced their development over the centuries. The study of STEM and of the historical, artistic and archaeological heritage, offered to young students who deal with peers of different nationalities, has allowed us to contribute to the construction of a thought that, starting from the acquisition of basic skills of citizenship, develops from a communication substrate of differences to reach awareness of mankind in full agreement with the objectives of Agenda 2030 related to this of the uniqueness of the journey project. Through the performed activities, the project helped to stimulate social and cognitive skills by using a metacognitive teaching that guides students to the awareness of the acquisition of new learning strategies.
The project has achieved five mobilities, 2 of which were for teachers only (in Croatia and Italy) and 3 with students, for 3 teachers and 5 pupils per country (in Greece, Turkey and Latvia) which had have positive long-term effects by cascading around 550 students, more than 100 teachers, 120 families, 50 community local representatives and all the made project materials will remain as resources. The project also allowed to all schools to improve their institutional development plans and the quality of teaching. The teachers  acquired knowledge from the comparison with the educational systems of the European partner countries of the project and updated their teaching styles. The project offered an international dimension to the schools, developing a network of contacts with EU schools and increasing schools' visibility.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-IT02-KA229-079430.title: Help me!
2020-1-IT02-KA229-079430.summary:
Upon receiving communication of our project approval, the partner schools – Italy, Croatia, Romania, Poland and Turkey – started promoting it by spreading the news in the school and local communities through posts on school websites, circular letters, articles on newspapers, presentations to parents, teachers and students in general assemblies. The importance of the issues dealt with – Natural Disasters and Emergency Education - was deeply felt by all of us and the increasing riskiness and frequency of extreme events made it urgent for schools to acquire awareness, knowledge and adequate skills. 
Soon, the project overview, goals and priorities were presented, clear roles, tasks and responsibilities set. Experienced teachers offered their help to the less experienced; we interacted in groups/pairs; online meetings were held regularly. The relationship among partners was friendly and collaborative since the beginning. 
An initial survey was conducted in the partner schools to make the shortcomings to be focused on clearly emerge and to arouse awareness; students aged 15-18 were involved in the logo contest, the “Help me!” Clubs created. During the Covid-19 pandemic and the beginning of the Russian-Ukrainian conflict, which forced us home, we continued to keep the spirit of the project alive by carrying out online meetings, presentations, and workshops. All the partners agreed on the effectiveness of face-to-face meetings.
All the planned LTTAs were carried out:
Step 1: Emergency Education 
Step 2: Emergency kit 
Step 3: Emergency motion plans 
Step 4: Emergency training program 
Step 5: Emergency teams 

OBJECTIVES
The project objectives have been met:
-	we have acquired awareness, knowledge, self-confidence and skills on the project topics and are committed and ready to convey our skills and know-how to our school community and other schools;
-	we are convinced that emergency education should start in schools and have created a Handbook, Digital Games and a Survival Guide on the purpose and started their dissemination on a large scale.

PARTICIPANTS
The partner schools’ community was directly and indirectly involved in the project: 33 teachers in the project management, LTTAs and dissemination; 200 students in all the project stages: research, presentation, dissemination, creation and management of project pages on social media, surveys, posters, banners, digital games, leaflets, vlogs, project outputs. Some acted as team leaders, facilitators, and tourist guides. 1090 students and around 100 teachers were indirectly involved in the project presentation, dissemination and LTTAs; around 505 students from other schools. 
425 Parents, 44 school staff and 250 people from the local communities took part in meetings to discuss the LTTAs management and related safety issues; 102 experts from the Red Cross, Fire Brigades, Civil Protection, local and regional authorities, contributed to make the LTTAs successful.

DESCRIPTION OF ACTIVITIES/METHODOLOGY
The creation of Erasmus project corners and website, school notice boards, “Help me!” clubs, logo contest, surveys, eTwinning, FB, Instagram, Twitter pages were among the first actions made to give maximum visibility to the project, attract the audience attention, create an engaging vibe. 
The action plan was based on international standards and organized in 5 LTTAs, each of them dealing with a sub-topic and consisting of 3 stages: preparation, application and distribution; they were carried out from May 2022 to May 2023. The workshops and drills were essential to their success providing training, skills development, teamwork at local and international level. Cooperation among students was crucial and working in a multicultural environment allowed them to improve their English language competence, communication and public speech skills, teamwork skills. Positive relationships and intercultural exchange were enhanced, cultural awareness and European identity increased.

RESULTS AND IMPACT
All those involved in the project – students, teachers, parents, school staff, local community, Civil Protection, Red Cross, Fire Brigades – have benefited from our projects. The teachers and students have become a resource and have already started taking actions on the matter, the local Institutions and organizations involved have built up strong ties with us and will support us in future projects. 
So far, we have met our goals. By publishing the project outputs on the social media, we expect to reach a much wider audience in the long term, especially the youth on whose support we count for actions for a better planet. Integrating the topic “Climate change and natural disasters” in the current school year curriculum will help increase knowledge and awareness; agreements with Civil Protection and Red Cross are vital for the creation of rescue teams. Dissemination activities are being organized in other schools to promote the results and encourage their use in their current practice.

2020-1-IT02-KA229-079442.title: DON'T CHANGE THE CLIMATE; CHANGE THE SYSTEM!
2020-1-IT02-KA229-079442.summary:
The Motto of the Project “Our goal is to reconcile the economy with our planet, to reconcile the way we produce, the way we consume, with our planet and to make it work for our people”Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission
 Climate Action is the 13th goal of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The Goals are set by the United Nations as part the Development 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Launched in 2015 they have been adopted by 193 countries.As all countries in the world are impacted by the destructive effects of climate change  and we must all take an action.According to the European Environment Agency’s (EEA) latest report,Europe will not achieve its 2030 goals without urgent action during the next 10 years to address the alarming rate of biodiversity loss, increasing impacts of climate change and the overconsumption of natural resources. It’s facing environmental challenges of unprecedented scale and urgency.
 Pupils of today are the adults of tomorrow and most likely to experience the effects of climate change.That is why it is imperative to learn to live sustainably in order to counteract climate change and other environmental challenges.Students will develop their competences in science, technology, and engineering.These will help them to understand the changes caused by human activity and teach them about the responsibility they have as individual citizens.Learning about citizenship competences and the ability to act as responsible citizens and fully participate in civic and social life will also be one of our objectives
 The Objectives of the Project:
 -Gaining greater awareness of sustainable development and making use of concrete tools to implement the real use of good practices in all educational-teaching activities, thereby ensuring the social equality
 - To reduce early school leaving rates (nearly %17) in the communities and make it (% 12 )
 -To promote social inclusion, diversity and non discrimination supporting students with migrant backgrounds
 -To set, critical thinking and creativity, cooperation in science, technology, arts and mathematics (STE(A)M) fields, as well as skills in fields such as climate action
 -To investigate the issue of climate change through discussion, experimentation and observation 
 -To make students more aware and active about a big issue such as the climate change
 The project will last 2 years and involves schools from 2 schools from Italy, Romania,Poland, Crotia, and Turkey.
 Most of pupils who will take part in this project are with fewer opportunities and face problems such as economic obstacles,cultural differences, disabilities ,health problems.
 We will perform the activities with students aged 13 to 16 years old to achieve the objectives of the project.The pupils will work actively on the project, but the whole school community will be involved in it.We will stem from the Traditional Teaching and Learning tecniques and use Innovative tecniques which be inspired from Multiple
 Intelligence Theory Pupils and teachers will collaborate and investigate innovative ways of learning and teaching such as PBL and STEM.Teachers will be promoters of social integration and inclusion of disadvantaged students.They will be able to propose viable strategies for building a better future for students,without segragation and unconfidence,
 Using 3 axes as imperatives of new century: Learning from anywhere and Learning during all life time, Learning for ALL.
 We will also constitute a comissions to eliminate participants in mobilities, to monitor, evaluate the project activities and to disseminate the results and to control the budget.
 The Time Schedule of the Project:
 1st Mobility Turkey February 2021 /5 Pupils 2 teachers from each partner
 2nd Mobility in Crotia May 2021 /5 Pupils 2 teachers from each partner
 3rd Mobility in Poland September 2021 /5 Pupils 2 teachers from each partner
 4th Mobility in Italy  November 2021 / 5 Pupils 2 teachers from each partner
 5th Mobility in Romania February 2022 /5 Pupils 2 teachers from each partner
 6th Mobility in Italy June 2022 / 5 Pupils 2 teachers from each partner
 EXPECTED INTANGIBLE RESULTS
 All participants will be more conscious about innovative teaching and learning tecniques, each partner country's education system ,STEM activities,Enviromental Campaigns.It will contribute better cultural and educational understanding.Students will broaden their linguistic competence ,digital and communication skills and have international friendship.Students at risk of dropout will improve their school marks and participation in classes (in terms of qualifications and number of absence)
 EXPECTED TANGIBLE RESULTS
 12 Leaflets
 1 Guide Book
 2022 Calendar
 6 Lesson Plans
 6 Green Stories
 E-Green Dictionary
 All the project activity will be based on combatting Climate Change with a multidisciplinary approach organized around indoor/outdoor activitiesand peer-learning sessions in a cooperative transnational working atmosphere.

2020-1-IT02-KA229-079446.title: Generation of Sustainability
2020-1-IT02-KA229-079446.summary:
Evaluating the existing situation we saw that due to the industrial revolution, globalization and consumer society influx our planet was going to be affected by a relevant climate change. The issue of climate change had become very important and placed great challenges on societies and thus also on schools.
The young generations were stimulated to run a new path and the impulse of the Swedish student Greta was followed by millions of teenagers. They wanted to show the whole world the importance of facing the problem and the need for younger generations to follow a common route. While “School Strike for Climate” focused on demanding action from the authorities, we strongly believed that personal responsibility had crucial significance too. Unfortunately, it seemed that many of us were still not aware of the fact that our behaviour and attitudes in everyday life were changing our climate and our ecosystem in an irreversible way.
We knew that in the schools' curricula, national focus was not properly set to tackle this relevant problem. The existing strategies of sustainability movement were assessed quite differently in the partner countries, and even a split in Europe was often evoked. 
Our first intent was to inform ourselves about the motivation and consequences of irresponsible attitudes and discuss the relevant Goals set in the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and shape a positive point of view towards sustainable approaches.
With a total of 5 partners from general secondary schools and vocational schools, we created a team of 4 long- term partners and a new one. Through the different perspectives and approaches of each partner, we had several different experiences and faced the project theme in a wide variety of facets.
The project language was English.
Each school granted the mobility of 20 students and 4 teachers, with a staff of other 4 teachers cooperating in the activities.
During each meeting a particular sustainable aspect was approached, such as sustainable energy, sustainable food, sustainable products and waste management, sustainable tourism and transport, sustainable school.
The participants worked project-oriented in multinational teams, which simulated the later professional activity of today's students. They decided, organized and controlled independently and on their own responsibility with regard to the project tasks and the use of the relevant documentation. 
Using digital media, they communicated and cooperated transnationally and realized the effective cognitive interaction in peer groups during the international meetings. 
Participants exchanged and expanded their existing expertise and fact-based knowledge profiting from the international approach. 
They applied scientific analysis and interpretation methods and got so prepared for their university career.
Social interaction with people of different origins, social behaviours and attitudes and different cultural backgrounds leaded to a reduction of reserves and prejudices, of stereotypical thinking and led to a higher sense of responsibility towards this topic as well.
We carried out expert surveys, interviews with local and regional authorities, members of some companies operating in the related sectors and realised workshops to produce our results.
As a final product we also created a Carbon Footprint Calculator to make everyone aware of their personal impact on the environment and how a simple little change by anyone can produce a relevant impact on the planet.
We undertook special work assignments for the participating students in preparation for the meetings which aimed to provide documentation in form of sets of statistical data, presentations, reports and videos, teaching sequences for pair-teaching of the partners in order to have maximum input during the meetings. As products, we elaborated videos and video guides, posters, photo collages, online brochures, a robot powered by solar panel and a carbon footprint calculator which today can be accessed on the project website and the project TwinSpace. 
The created material may be used at schools or youth organizations for educational purposes as well as for personal interest.
As a result, we increased the knowledge of the problem, its causes, culture and social behaviours of the home country, the partner countries and parallels in the development of Europe.
In addition, we improved the competencies of the participants in the critical reception of media contributions in focusing on the real problems and the strategies of the EU for facing the issue. 
We encouraged differentiated thinking, stimulated the students to face and discuss the topics and the use of their language skills (mother tongue and foreign language).
We also promoted the general education of the participants, the development of a common sense of European citizens for a new identity of our own countries and our society respectful of the sustainable choices.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-IT02-KA229-079473.title: Sea Rhapsody in Europe
2020-1-IT02-KA229-079473.summary:
We created our project inspired by the seaside we live close and by the music we like. We asked ourselves: what is a “rhapsody”? According to Oxford Dictionary, it is a “free instrumental composition in one extended movement, typically one that is emotional or exuberant in character”. This definition contained four key-words for our project: free, movement, emotional, exuberant. That’s the way our students are. Following such a vision of our students as a sort of “melody”, our project aimed to make a “creative” connection between our teenagers’ inner universe and the natural environment they live in. 
We strongly believed that one of the most relevant aspects of a teenager's growth, for a full self-knowledge, was the harmonious development of creative and expressive area. Music, dance, body expression, art, sports, these were and always are the favorite activities for many of them, and these can increase their motivation to learn. 
All project activities were therefore organized to allow pupils to create and express themselves around a theme that was common to all partner countries, located in coastal regions: the sea, in its various shapes (cultural, historical, economic, environmental).
The inhabitants of coastal regions always had a special relationship with the sea. Ours are lands of sailors, expert fishermen, hardworking women. The sea represented for us the natural theatre of man and his history: place of exchange, civilization, languages, cultures, arts, ethnic groups, thought. Furthermore, the Goal n.14 of the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals Agenda is about the seas: "Conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources for sustainable development". Taking into account all these aspects, the Project wanted to make pupils aware that the sea represents the greatest message of peace, respect for the environment, disdain for violence and prevarication, rejection of social injustices, love of difference, passion for communication and dialogue, cult of freedom.
Around the project main theme we selected our priorities. Students were leaded to understand the importance of protecting our environment and acquire basic skills and key competences. They learned more about other European countries culture and tradition, mainly about music, songs, plastic arts. 
In each meeting, partners chose a different meaningful aspect of the project topic (environment protection, the sea in our history / traditions/ culture), giving a title to the meeting itself. 
Concrete results of this projects were mainly "art products" and events, linked to music, dance, play, body expression, handcrafts. They were described in details in the webform section devoted to LTTA. Some examples: folk dances and folk songs, songs about the sea in English and national languages, games, plays, amber bracelets, game of tracks and map explorations, excursions, sailing, cup printing/T-shirt printing, pottery. For most of the songs, dances, workshops and activities we made a selection of photos and videos to be collected in the project website and shown at the final meeting in Italy. A final product was produced (using Genially), containing many moments and materials, with the title of the project "Sea Rhapsody in Europe".
All planned activities were closely linked to the priorities and topics of the project. All pupils participating in the mobility had the opportunity to develop a natural respect for the environment they visited, for the cultural specificities of the families that hosted them, and also had the opportunity to express themselves while having fun, in activities that involve fantasy, originality and personal interpretation.
The Portuguese school was an ETwinning school and its contribution was relevant for the creation of a project in support of the Erasmus+ project. During the first months of the project, all teachers and students who intended to take part to the activities registered on the portal, in order to form an eTwinning Group within eTwinning Live. 
The project activities were aimed at achieving the progressive change of our educational institutions and their European dimension. Through the project activities, the participating teachers could acquire new techniques and methodologies to be used with pupils in the didactic approach, both in class and in extracurricular activities, and they could strengthen their know-how for future projects and activities at school. The initiatives envisaged in this project have become part of our Institutes' curriculum and educational offer, therefore benefits on pupils' learning are long term, even after the end of the project.
The project was completed as foreseen in the application phase, but the duration was extended by 12 months. The first year, in fact, due to the Covid-19 pandemic, was carried out with entirely remote activities (meetings on line with countries in pairs, exchange of presentations of our countries and videos containing our typical songs).
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2020-1-IT02-KA229-079580.title: A sustainable table for multiculturalism and inclusion
2020-1-IT02-KA229-079580.summary:
The UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development encourages education system to respond to environmental issues by defining relevant learning objectives and implementing actions that empower students, families and local communities appropriate response. The project “A sustainable table for multiculturalism and inclusion” shares this urge since questionnaires revealed that most students nowadays prefer fast and junk food and rarely adopt green behaviours. Thus, the objectives of this project are: to raise knowledge and awareness of a sustainable food system and its benefits on human life and health in order to persuade youngsters to change their eating habits and preserve our environment; to raise cultural awareness of local, national and European heritage through food choices and eating habits and to develop students’ professional competences in gastronomy as well as their social, civic, entrepreneurship, linguistic and digital competences. It also aims to develop teaching professionalism by increasing teachers’ abilities to develop European networks while working in cross-border projects, sharing ideas and practices and discovering innovative didactic strategies to be used in classroom.
 To achieve these goals, five schools from European countries (Italy, Bulgaria, Croatia, Poland and Romania ) decided to involve students and their families in stimulating activities like practical training, sustainable cooking laboratories in which they experience traditional and innovative recipes, workshops, outdoor activities and comparative studies of European eating habits which, although different, are all united by the same quality “to be sustainable”. Since the best approach to this issue is prevention learned at a young age through healthy eating and active living habits that stand the test of time, we found relevant to target students aged 14-18 (of which 20 students are engaged directly in each mobility) as they will become the next generation aware of the ecological benefits of sustainable consumption. Throughout the activities, by cooperating and combining their own "foods" students create a real sustainable table as a result of their visits at farms and farmers’ market and by using safe and eco-friendly working behaviours. The virtual sustainable table, in the form of an  e-book with traditional and innovative European healthy recipes and safety suggestions for healthy food choices and habits, will be created and spread on the project website and on eTwinning space and presented in the sustainable green day organized in schools with the help of parents and local communities. Students also prepare a diet program based on scientific measurements of body index mass between people who use healthy food and who don't. Tasks and responsibilities are equally divided among partners according to their expertise favouring objective fulfilment and good cooperation is guaranteed by using different communication channels: social networks, e-mail, eTwinning, Skype. 
 The topic for all the activities and the final result- a sustainable table- become the means to get to know and understand cultural diversity and acquire intercultural competences. Multicultural sustainable dishes and practices develop participants’ sense of European citizenship and identity through greater understanding and intercultural responsiveness to environment problems and by training European citizens free from any cultural prejudice, socially committed to the construction of a greener world and more motivated to intervene actively. Project activities also result in increased critical thinking and ability to cooperate effectively and respectfully with other people, increased ability to manage tasks resorting to talents and creativity, developed linguistic, digital and professional skills; a set of good practices regarding healthy eating habits, preservation of the environment and of the national identity by promoting traditional cuisine and local traditions; a set of innovative methodological strategies to be used in classroom and a project blog promoting project activities and outcomes, opinions, useful recommendations for further didactic activities; culinary exhibitions. 
 Through the dissemination activities, whole communities benefit from raised awareness regarding the importance of preserving the environment and the local biodiversity, of encouraging organic sustainable farming and of having a healthy lifestyle based on healthy eating habits which promote a consistent reduction of food waste and consumption of additive free products. Raised awareness of people regarding the importance of changing their unhealthy eating habits benefit their own health as well as the environment and  the whole planet. By adopting a healthy environmentally friendly diet, not only will we increase our life span and the quality of our standard of life, but we will also give our planet the chance to recover and sustain future communities in a balanced eco-system.

2020-1-IT02-KA229-079606.title: STRONGER SCHOOLS WITH 21st CENTURY SKILLS
2020-1-IT02-KA229-079606.summary:
In the EU 2020 Strategy Document; The importance of investing in the development of education and human resources in the 21st century, which is defined as the information age with the scientific and technological advances and revolutionary transformations in information and communication technologies, has been emphasized for economic and social development. In the 21st century that created its own language, when you don't speak this language, lessons for students cannot go beyond being seen as a long and monologue. If we can get students to acquire 21st century skills, our children will be able to perform professions that do not already exist. For the acquisition of 21st century skills our project team has sent the problem areas and solution proposals to the project partners via the School Gateway and e Twinning platforms.When the forms are evaluated, common problems in our schools in our project;
 
 -Monotonous processing of lessons, permanence of learning, difficulty in ensuring continuity
 -Ignoring individual differences in students' interests and abilities,
 -Insufficiency in students' creativity, critical thinking, problem solving skills,
 -Lack of students and teachers on digital literacy-media literacy have been identified as a need.
 
 Good practices for these problems in our project partner schools have been determined with the information forms we sent to our partners;
 
 1- ITALY: Good practices for learning to learn and access information in the information age
 2- LATVIA: Skills to facilitate students' adaptation to the service sector within the scope of Lifelong Learning
 3-TURKEY-MERSİN: Creative problem solving skills and design-oriented thinking practices,
 4-CROATIA:  Systematic programs for teaching life skills
 5-BULGARIA: 21st century Technology Education- Good practices in Robotic Coding
 6-TURKEY-UŞAK: Carries out the project of “Use of Conscious Technology for the Future” and will contribute to the project on Media and Digital Literacy.
 
 These countries will contribute to the project with these practises. Our project is constructed about adapting to the changes with 21st century skills in a rapidly changing and developing world.
 With this project, we aim to increase motivation for attendance to school (attitude scale), to decrease in the number of absentee days (attendance follow up system data), to increase our teachers’ skills by developing  and sharing good practices
 
 Our Project is constructed on the basis of developing 21st skills  of  teachers and gaining these skills to the students. Our project targets:	
 
 *Within the scope of increasing teacher competencies, which is our priority in the project; our teachers’,
 
 -İncrease teacher competencies in ensuring the permanence and continuity of learning and provide students’ participation actively in lessons.
 -Develop students' collaboration and living together skills
 -İncrease teacher competencies to improve students' creativity, critical thinking, acting in harmony with others, problem solving skills
 -Prepare education plans for development of students and teachers on digital literacy-media literacy
 -Qualifications of teachers working in classrooms with students with different interests, abilities and skills will increase according to the European norms and criteria, their status, morale and professionalism 
 
 * To prevent early school dropout, which is among our priorities;
 
 With the activities to be carried out during the project;
 
 -Decrease the absenteeism rate of our students by 5% in the first year and 10% in the second year by increasing the motivation of learning (attendancefollow up system data) with effective learning methods to be carried out at school.
 -Reduce the rate of early school  leaving to 10% with happy teacher-happy students by creating a positive school climate with 21st-century basic skills and equipped teachers with the activities to be done during the project process;
 -In-Class Skills Development Activity Book will be created for our teachers to develop students'
 -Decrease early school leaving rate below 10% with happy teacher-happy students by creating a positive school climate with teachers and students equipped with 21st century basic skills
 -Early school drop-out rates will decrease with improvements on positive attitude towards the students whose psychosocial development is supported by  'Strategy and Mind Games'
 -With EARLY WARNING ALARM Activity : With this forerunner application, students who experience a sudden decrease in course success will be identified and necessary guidance and assistance will be provided for them. By providing individual and group counseling services on issues such as Efficient Studying, Exam Anxiety, etc., students' course success will be increased and early school leaving will be prevented by improving their motivation about the school.
 
 It will provide contribution to smart growth in the EU 2020 strategic targets and reduction of early school leaving to 10%
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2020-1-IT02-KA229-079699.title: Being virtuous in a virtual world
2020-1-IT02-KA229-079699.summary:
The title of our project is "Being virtuous in a virtual world" and the participating schools are six: Croatia, Greece,Italy (the coordinator) Poland, Portugal, Spain.The Italian and the Polish schools in a final project meeting of a previous Erasmus Ka2 talked about a possible and further future cooperation in another KA2 project  finding out a common problem that teachers in any country daily live and face at school, how to deal with the students' ab-use of social networks.In Italy this year  a National Day against bullying and cyberbullying has been established on 8 February 2020 and the school has organized workshops and meetings with psychologists and competent professionals. Other schools were contacted on eTwinning and they all shared the same interest in the topic, since some of them reported repetitive acts of cyberbullying, of sexting and racism in the use of social media. Racism is a great problem expressed in social media in many countries, expecially in countries which receive the largest number of refugees, such as Sicily and Greece.
 The main motivation of this project is to create responsible digital citizens in Europe who use the Internet and social media to share appropriate stories, images, videos and ideas with friends and family, to have a positive digital footprint, to give due credit when sharing an idea, image and video (to respect and be aware of themselves and of the others), to report inappropriate and dangerous online behaviour (cyberbullying, sexting and harassment, hate speech, fake news, acts of racial intolerance).
 The objectives to be achieved are:
 1. To encourage the strengthening of all participants’ linguistic skills;
 2. To promote an understanding and respect of the cultural diversity;
 3.To promote responsibility and respect for the rules of civic society encouraging good practices in the use of the web;
 4.To increase the awareness of being properly social and the expression of one's own creativity without being harmful and insensitive towards other people avoiding predjudices especially to minorities.
 Activities
 First mobility in Poland (8-14 November 2020) only teachers to attend a course and plan the activities of the project.
 7-11 December  2020 digital drawing in inkscape to create projects logo and proposing slogans for the project 
 18-22 January  2021 presenting our school, city and coutry in tools we like the most
 14-20 February 2021 (Croatia) mobility with students
 19-23 April 2021 preparing videos about what will change in ten years, taking in consideration different aspects of life: human body and brain, economy, finance, robotics, transport 
 9-15 May 2021(Portugal) mobility with students
 18-22 October 2021creating a personal avatar and a national avatar to be compared with the other countries' avatars in the next mobility thus  becoming the international Avatar
  7-13 November 2021(Greek) mobility with students 
 17-21 January 2022 creating a national eSafety manual to be compared with the other countries'  in the next mobility, thus becoming the  international manual
 6-12 February 2022(Spain) mobility with students
  8-14 May 2022(Italy) last mobility with students
 All partner institutions are responsible for the cultural programme of the exchange visits to ensure a successful proceeding of the project itself. This means they also look for host families, find resources at school like rooms and technology, organize events, open days at school, meetings with experts.The Italian school assures the good communication (in English) among partners, tackles any problem and is responsible for any decision making. The communication between the project partners is run by means of the social media like Facebook and SKYPE meetings which will be the responsibility of Croatia and eTwinning which will be managed by Portugal. Modern IT based communication is used regularly as needed (emails, WhatsApp, text messages,  phone calls).
 The Spanish school prepares albums, videos, multimedia presentations and all schools regularly  post material to the Facebook page to disseminate our work. The Greek partner will take care of the printing of the e-safety manual and the Polish will collect  and evaluate data (texts and photos/videos) on paper, memory sticks and send it to Croatia to put it on the Facebook site.
 The objectives will be assessed regularly by using questionnaires for students and teachers (multiple choice and open questions to express their opinions and feelings) to find out about the students' improving competences in foreign language skills, tests to check the learning process and the benefits from the project. The monitoring of the response of the local community documents the success of the project (e.g. the number of visitors on the website, articles in mass media).
 To disseminate the results schools will show handouts, reports, videos on each school websites, publish articles on newspapers and news on local TV, create a Twinspace page and organize Erasmus+ events.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-IT02-KA229-079714.title: The Angevins, a European dynasty: testimonies, settlements, relics
2020-1-IT02-KA229-079714.summary:
The project “The Angevins, a European dynasty: testimonies, settlements, relics” was approved by the Italian National Agency for the years 2020-2022 but, due to the pandemic, it was necessary to ask for an extension of its duration in order to implement all the planned activities. Therefore, the official deadline was set at 31 August 2023. 
The project aimed to explore and understand the history and legacy of the Angevin dynasty in some European countries that had experienced that domination in past centuries, through a series of practical activities, group visits to historical sites and by implementing a competence oriented learning for students coming from several parts of Europe, different for language spoken, traditions and lifestyles. The project finally led to the creation of a virtual museum that shows the historical and artistic heritage of the Angevins, which concretely exists and still enriches certain European territories today.
The project was managed by a partnership of 5 schools from 5 European countries: Italy, France, Poland, Hungary and Croatia. Each school involved 25 students, aged 16 - 18, who took part, in turns 5 at a time, in transnational meetings. For each mobility abroad there were two accompanying teachers from each school. The project management also engaged other teachers from the schools, based on the expertise needed, and other students who helped in hosting guest students.
During the mobilities, the participants visited places linked to the Angevin dynasty in France, Hungary, Italy, Croatia and Poland, living an immersive experience in the culture and life habits of foreign countries which allowed them to deepen their historical knowledge about the Angevin dynasty and acquire personal skills valid both at school and in everyday life: greater intercultural awareness, a better understanding of the importance of the artistic and cultural heritage of nations, a clearer comprehension of the idea of active European citizenship, social and civic skills. The constant intercultural dialogue that took place among the students and the teachers involved in the project gave all of them the opportunity to improve their linguistic and communication competences and their interpersonal skills, fostering a more open-minded attitude and greater respect towards any kind of difference and otherness. Moreover, both students and teachers, working on platforms, creating videos, uploading photos and various materials, have also acquired new digital skills that can be used in future projects, activities or jobs.
The methodology adopted during the mobilities combined formal and informal methods and the activities carried out to implement the project range from guided visits to treasure hunts on sites of interest, theoretical reseach, group work to create digital presentations, workshops at school, debates on previous visits and information acquired, quizzes, icebreaking games at the beginning of each transnational meeting. Students discovered a new way to study traditional subjects like history and art in non-formal contexts, outside the classroom, through peer to peer teaching, intercultural cooperative learning and Project based learning; they learnt how to work in international teams and present in English before an audience. All that also strengthened their self-esteem promoting a resposible behaviour both at school and in every context of society. Through the meeting with different scholastic realities, cooperation and exchange between educational teams from different contexts, the teachers involved have developed a greater awareness of their teaching style, enriching it with knowledge of new methodologies that will continue to have positive effects on their teaching practices, thus giving a more European dimension to the school where they work. The schools, hence, have opened up to new forms of relationship and exchange with educational teams from different countries. Indeed, the cooperation inspired the creation of a European network of schools that will continue to interact and cooperate in new projects on other topics.
The concrete product of the project is a virtual museum of the Angevin dynasty, a kind of online museum with pictures and information, providing an overview of the Angevins' history, achievements and relics. It is available to anyone who wants to know about it as it has been put on the public Twinspace of the project and on the partner schools’ websites. The virtual museum ensures that the Angevins' legacy can be accessed and appreciated by a wide audience, regardless of geographical and time boundaries. 
The project results were spread and made visible through various dissemination channels - the schools’ websites, teachers’ meetings, social media pages, eTwinning, local press – to show that participants not only gained valuable insights into the Angevins' history but also acquired essential skills that will benefit in the long term their personal and professional growth.

2020-1-IT02-KA229-079862.title: Discover My City
2020-1-IT02-KA229-079862.summary:
DISCOVER MY CITY was an Erasmus Project, coordinated by Italy whose partners were schools from Turkey, Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece and Germany, in which 118 students between 11 and 17 and 26 teachers had active roles and joined the mobilities.
It has been fully recognized that cultural heritage plays a central role in our society, creating a feeling of togetherness within and across national borders and promoting mutual understanding and shared values. The project mainly aimed at allowing students to become more active and inclusive citizens through activities and tasks that helped them to deepen their knowledge of the historical and cultural background of their own cities and those of the school partners and to investigate the problems these cities are currently facing and their possible consequences in the future. Through the planned activities they also could develop such skills as face-to-face communication, collaboration, working as a team, creativity which are fundamental in their future working life.
After an initial questionnaire to check what they already knew about the natural and cultural values in their cities and if they were aware of the problems there and the big threat for their lives represented by the climate change, we proposed pre-, while- and post-mobility activities to let them know their cities better from a historical and cultural point of view and get more accurate information about the causes and effects of climate change on their daily life, thus strengthening their multilingual, digital, cultural awareness and expression together with their personal and social competences. 
Each mobility dealt with different aspects: the cultural and natural heritage in the partners’ cities, the problems they face in terms of health, transportation, crime, education, the local ancient civilizations and legends, the minorities living in the partners’ cities and their cultural identities (festivals, songs, folk dances), the environmental problems and their causes and effects, important people who are living heritage in the partners’ cities. Before each mobility students had online exams about the topic which were repeated after the mobility. They prepared presentations or reports about the topic to share during mobilities. Furthermore they made a search to find out the connections between their country and the host city according to the topic. During the mobilities each student had an active role through different tasks: the host students acted as tour guides for the guest students while visiting the cities, the participating students carried out various activities working as a team (interviewing people, visiting places and monuments, making searches and presentations, discussing problems and solutions, creating and learning together, comparing). At the end of each mobility they created a final product like a video, a book on local legends, a documentary about people who are living cultural heritage in the partners’ cities. 
Our project was also a chance for the involved teachers to update their professional skills thanks to workshops or seminars they attended during each mobility, especially about eLearning. 
The local activities, which were carried out under our eTwinning project named "My city", aimed at allowing our students to know their cities better according to the following topics: city squares, poems on our cities, city symbols, endemic plants and animals in our cities, legends about our cities. Students working as a team (the groups were created applying some criteria such as motivation, foreign language and technological skills, academic results, involvement in class and school life) created some products (books, photo albums, presentations and videos) using ICT tools, then collected and shared them in the Twinspace of the eTwinning project which was started as soon as this ERASMUS+ project was granted. 
In order to evaluate the students' progress we planned pre and post-mobility exams and 3 checklists to follow the activities. Our main target people were students and teachers at our schools who didn’t join the project mobilities, reached via competitions, project corners, videos, quiz shows, mini congress days. Students with social, economic or family problems were given priority in being involved in the project activities. Younger students and the participating students’ brothers and sisters joined the project too through a creative activity. To reach more people interested in our topic we also had a website , a YouTube channel and we also created pages on social media to share and disseminate results, events, activities. All the partners collaborated with local organizations (municipalities, universities and museums) to share the project and its results as much as possible. During all mobilities local municipalities and people in charge were visited and the local press was invited to all activities.

2020-1-IT02-KA229-079931.title: Life is Art; Art is Life
2020-1-IT02-KA229-079931.summary:
Art is the best way in order to convey many things and one's express himself/herself. Educationalists are of the opinion that art not only supply academical success but also help inclusion of pupils to social environment, so art has a speacial meaning both for teachers and students. Art allows students to learn about themselves, their culture, and their community. Their creativity and imagination can be pushed through the development of art, so they can understand the world and
 their environment better.Being busy with any kinds of art can give the feeling of creating something,group work consciousness, collaboration and so on to our pupils.In this project , there are six partner schools aiming to run a project about art in order to raise students awareness towards art and its benefits in their daily lives.
 The project 's aims are:
 -To include students who are coming from different backgrounds into society and school environment through art.
 -To raise the level of inclusion and collaboration  among students, teachers, parents and community through art
 -To share cultures and arts 
 -To analyse the educational contexts  in the name of art of all partners and base project activities on identified needs
 -To promote the exchange of good and innovative practices and experiences between European schools through cultural heritage
 -To develop pupils' skills researching, literacy, digital skills, and cross-curricular skills: critical thinking, collaboration, initiative, and communication.
 -To update and strengthen the professional competences of teachers regarding methodologies, dynamics and activities regarding art, art history, foreign language, and Ict, developing their knowledge and skills in the design and organization of activities.
 -To share day to day life and find similarities and differences in their culture
 -To increase students' creativity by the activities and workshops held during the project
 -To promote teachers  and students use web 2:00 tools
  In our Project, Life is art; Art is life , we would like to initiate intercultural dialogue among young people14 - 18 aged from European countries and by raising awareness of the role of art,sport, history of art, drama, music, literature and Ict in communication, we aim to promote European perspective both for teachers and students. By this way, the partnership can allow people to broaden their idea of art while allowing art to broaden their idea of people and brings culture into pupils’ s everyday life. In this project, we are also planning to share our cultures through art. Each country is going to choose a national piece of art as a stimulus and send it to a random country in the partnership and then they are going to create a response( music, dance, a play, painting etc.). The students are going to create a piece of art out of their own stimulus and compare the outcomes.
 During mobilities, there are going to be art festivals and the students are going to share their pieces of art in workshops in the festivals. The students are going to divided into groups from different countries to develop a creative project around a specific art form.
 Our main objectives are directing students into arts and make each of them meet new cultures and increase their creativity and Ict skills.In addition, their language skill is going to be developed and group-work dynamics are going to be increased.
  As a concrete visual and tangible result, we will create a photo book comprised of pieces of arts held during mobilities and a film ( a DVD )formed by each mobility's presentations of the students.
  Art-based activities,Presentations, drama technique, reviving, project teaching, observing, games, using technology and workshops, collaborative work, writing diaries, Itinerant exhibition will form the methodology of our project.
 As for the European value, Pupils will benefit from developing friendships with pupils with different nationalities. Participation in the project raises our pupils’ awareness of the life of European children, through exploring and sharing day-to-day experiences, the local community in which they live, their national identity and cultural practices. By comparing the two responses to the same stimulus they will learn from and value their cultural differences that enrich Europe. This project will broaden their idea of belonging to Europe instead of belonging only to their own nation.
 This project will change their idea of art by bringing it into their everyday life and by allowing students to actually create art together with students, teachers and professional artists coming from many different countries and backgrounds.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-LT01-KA229-077849.title: Media Smart Citizens of Future
2020-1-LT01-KA229-077849.summary:
The new communication paradigm, generated by media convergence, has no National borders. For that reason, it is momentous to promote the creation of synergies among different countries and actors and interchange of practices to develop media literacy.Our project aims at promoting media literacy and critical thinking skills which raise awareness of media manipulation and providing the participants with the knowledge and power for efficient and safe use of media outlets.To solve the media literacy problems, the coordinator (Lithuania) decided to collaborate with 5 schools from Portugal,Croatia,Turkey,Spain,Italy, which attach importance to media literacy and conducting studies to tackle with the problem to enable pupils to become more conscious media consumers having the ability of critically thinking. All partner schools have some initiatives at local level but there are few cases where a local activity has been extended to all the nations or outside national borders. By dint of this project, media literacy promoting activities will have European stardom, which will increase their visibility and effectiveness.
 The target audience of the project is students, teachers, parents, local people, neighbouring schools, local authorities, media itself, policy makers. In total 72 teachers who constantly strive for their own professional development and 144 students aged between 14-17 will participate in 6LTTs.
 Each LTT will serve the purposes of attaining the project goals.Thanks to 1st LTT in Lithuania, participants will enhance critical thinking and media literacy to strengthen democracy and counter manipulation, propaganda and disinformation as cited in Erasmus+ program guide and will tell the difference between professional news-gathering and amateur rumour-mongering. The 2nd LTT in Portugal will enable participants to cope with the manipulations by ads and to be judicious consumers. The 3rd LTTA in Italy will enable the participants to access and interpret the right information thanks to their increasing experience in media literacy.That will facilitate the acceptance of cultural difference, diminish racist behavior and develop intercultural skills.The 4th LTT in Croatia will teach them to differentiate different media outlets.In virtue of 5th LTT in Spain, participants will develop skills in media production and subsequently develop their initiatives.Moreover, rather than just being external spectators and information recipients, they will become content makers and learn to reach info through different means. The 6th LTT in Turkey will enable students to become conscious of different forms of online hate speech and their reasons and effects.These objectives will be achieved through outdoor/indoor learning-teaching, scaffolding, problem solving, CLIL, ICT,Inquiry based and Cooperative Learning, Textual and Visual Analyses, Think-pair-share-technique all of which are based on interactive teaching and student-centered methodologies.By the virtues of LTTAs and mentioned techniques and methodologies, we aim at attaining the following concrete results
 -6 issues of e magazines about LTTAs
 -1 e-book covering all LTTs
 -Digital and ceramic version of project logo
 -An action plan about media literacy
 -A podcast named digital footprint to enable students to be safe and conscious on the internet
 -A podcast about offering tips to protect users from cyber bullying and hate speech
 -Brochures about fake news
 -News reports and newspaper about LTTs
 -Slogans, mottos and bookmarks about media literacy
 -Seminars about raising media literacy for pupils, teachers and parents
 -Participants will act independently and replicate what they learnt further in their settings; thus they will be multipliers who can contribute to raising media literacy in their their school, region, country, through Europe
 In the long run, participants’ skills for accessing, analyzing, evaluating and creating media will increase and in virtue of our project, the participants will raise their literacy, life and learning skills which are caterpillars of 21st century education. Since students and teachers will use ICT in some project outputs, their digital skills will improve. In the long run, we will go on organizing a “media literacy” week every year.The concrete results will be available on TwinSpace, YouTube Channel, project's websites, social media platforms for everyone interested in media literacy.The e-book will provide the sustainability of our project as well as being a resource from which all our stakeholders will benefit.Moreover, our project with its results will present implications to curriculum designer to integrate media literacy into their national curriculum.Each partner school will prepare an action plan in which we will organize activities, seminars, meetings, etc.to train students on media literacy.Thus, we will ensure that action plan’s being our organizational culture, which is the hardest evidence of our project’s benefits being long lasting

2020-1-LT01-KA229-077854.summary:
The supplying of rising needs is just possible with using the improving technology. The improving technology have compelled the European societies to the changing promptly in terms of globalization, digitalization, socio-cultural and economic. While every new changing causes a rising of new industries and occupations, the needs having labour force that has more different skills and competence have risen.  The researches reveal that the graduated students who have traditional mathematic education teaching mathematical concepts and connection among them couldn't use these knowledge in real time conditions .
 Therefore, traditional maths education causes learning disability of the students. Also, the learning disability causes the early school leaving.
 Our purpose with the help project is to integrate to the real life situations with to help of technology of the students maths knowledge.

 Our project will take place with 216 people's attendance who are students and teachers. It will consist of boy and girl students whose ages are between 13-15.
 It will be provided equality of opinions-chances among students .It is essential that at least one maths and ICT teacher participate each training and activity of our project. Our project has consist of dividing more lower segments and with piecing together of these lower segments. These segments
 are complete in terms of reporting and evaluation in itself. Every evaluation will provide the effect of new ideas to the project in planning of the activity that will be taken place later. Each of stem activity states the segments. The lower segments that are consisted of piecing together of parts have separated each of others with different data structure, technological approach and algorithm.  These will be published related virtual platforms. Teach-meet activities will be arranged to reach new ideas at teacher trainings.

 We will have provided to be able to evaluate process- driven of the students with becoming widespread in partner schools of alternative measurement and evaluation instruments. It will be given a speech regularly about project training on twitter and followed projects twits with common hashtag.

 It will get easy our participants to suit up to the alternation and improvement process with their life long learning skills. In this context, to get data literacy and to increase digital sufficiencies are the most important competences to keep up in competitive economies of the participants. It will developa common Europeanness aspect with their language improvement and to have intercultural understanding of our participants.
 We aim to reflect the best implementations, to communicate, to create and introduce new ideas with all kinds of real and social media communities that we want to constitute with the participants in the process and following of the project.

2020-1-LT01-KA229-078101.title: ARTHERA
2020-1-LT01-KA229-078101.summary:
Boosting the artistic skills of students with special educational needs by offering them a creative atmosphere is the main aim of this project. While making decisions on our furniture, meal, music, attire, drink, or self-expression ways, actually, the pre-perceptions we have been exposed to until now are affecting these decisions. Improving the quality of life is not only related to budgetary standards but also depends on the natural choices of a person who is nourished by art. Why can't a special person cook and serve a delightful late gourmet feast? Why a minimalist art installation can’t belong to one with down syndrome? How about modern art on sculptures or murals? Or even sarcastic minimalist atonal music? While the arrangement of an artwork is set on the desired form, occasionally certain parts include accidental sections to seek complicity according to particular generic directives, or sometimes this complicity may become the fundamental goal.
 Having a unique name, ARTHERA is creative and also integrative with its artistic approach since art implies creativity, and creativity is the future itself. Youths should be engaged in arts throughout their lives to enrich their emotional and professional growth for art has solid therapeutic efficiency in our system. It can not only adjust breathing and normotension, and also it boosts self-respect, empathy, self-expression, self-exploration, and strength of space and time coordinating skills, as well as neural and intellectual maturity. It is a miraculous path to evolve inclusion and forge social links between students, particularly students with dyslexia, down syndrome, autism, and learning difficulties.
 Furthermore, our project has a PR activity on the school communities, which aims to reach ones who are mostly wasting their real potential by consuming their most valued hours on TV or social media, mini-games, and even drugs. These barriers they are not aware, are enough to push, especially youths to awry ways during the crucial periods of their lives, and this leads people in the market to spend their potentials for nothing rather than becoming skilled labor. Non-attendant teens in arts or sports during their critical periods can not be creative or efficient for skilled labor in the future.

Boosting the hand skills of students with SEN not only strengths their minor&major muscle progress but also forges a marvelous consciousness about intellectual disability via relevant school events. The students are handing out some encouraging knowledge on how to survive healthily such as nutrition, social habits, and the barriers that obstruct real potential for a satisfactory success. Special students inform others about the varied inhibitive of individuals through PR activities in hosting partners’ schoolyards with the disability-based NGOs. They increase awareness on the topics by some leaflets, which are cut as masks with eye holes, to ensure a special look at the world with the perspective of teens with SEN. Instead of highlighting ‘Disability’ as a topic, emphasizing a problem, we name as ‘self-barriers’ (a typical term for this project) for anyone provided tremendous visibility to ARTHERA tag and to its aim, which is also to broaden the rights of disabled. This is a fundamental reformist act for these rights.
 
 Each art thematic mobility includes 5 Days program with 3 students with Special Educational Needs (aged 15 - 21) and 3 teachers for each partner:
 
 Art Thematic Mobilities:
 • Music in Croatia
 • Drama in Spain
 • Dance in Turkey
 • Sculpture in Estonia
 • Paint in Lithuania
 • Design in Italy
 
 ARTHERA also has a unique operation program in advance, thanks to its diversified mobility points including some major centers and some rural areas in Europe. With a perfect leap, super cool teens succeeded in performing artistic and cross-cultural cooperation. The success promoted to heighten the essential synergy to prosper in any field of existence for any member of the community, despite disadvantages.
 
 Like in our schools, special education ought to be centered on self-care and academic skills with social activities such as arts, sports and socialization based on an active citizenship basis. Also as mentioned in the EU Disability Strategy, Education and Training, Accessibility, Equality, Participation, Health, Employment, Social Protection, and External Activity clauses show us that we are still in a distance to disseminate the most effective cure models(!) for the communities to foster the disability rights worldwide and to maintain the fact that disability is a very part of our societies. This is why our project should be operated internationally and not only based on this partnership's demands. Our overall goal is to empower all stakeholders in promoting social rights and recovery in order to sustainably change mentalities and practices and ensure the well-being of people with psychosocial, physical, mental, or cognitive disabilities.

2020-1-LV01-KA229-077425.title: Culture Covers Values
2020-1-LV01-KA229-077425.summary:
The Culture Covers Values project is an international project carried out under the Erasmus + programme. The project partnership consists of 5 partner schools from Latvia, Turkey, Portugal, Croatia, and North Macedonia.
 The aim of the Project was, and continues to be, to build a more understanding society by promoting intercultural cooperation based on mutual understanding, respect and understanding of the diversity of cultures and values. The target group for the project was students of age group 13 to 19.
To achieve the objective of the project, students and teachers initially became familiar with their culture and the values it contained - before each learning activity, students had to conduct a study on a particular group of values - how these values had formed, how they are reflected in cultural elements - poetry, art, architecture, food and cooking traditions, architecture, religion, etc. to achieve the objective of the project.
The results of the studying process were collected and presented during the LTTA, and one joint presentation was created from all the information gathered after each learning activity. Such activities contributed significantly to intercultural understanding, which had a positive impact not only on the intercultural communication skills of each participant, but on the overall attitude towards the processes taking place in the world. 
An integral part of the analysis was an exploration of the country's geography and history. Young people themselves concluded that our lives, traditions and attitudes were influenced by the place where we were born and raised. These were very important conclusions as there is sometimes no need to change anything, but such information helps to understand and accept the differences.
Thanks to carefully developed training programmes and successfully selected training methods, the process of the project was interesting and enjoyable. Motivated and positive teachers were involved in the implementation of the project to assure qualitative process of project implementation.
During the training activities, young people were greeted with interesting “ice breaking” activities, which boosted communication among them since the first activity day. On the first day of mobility there were created WhatsApp groups for smoother and more successful communication between students during the whole LTTA period. During the LTTA students took a lot of photos, made video clips and presentations, wrote essays and overtures, developed logos, digital and printed calendars, posters, participated in contests, used their favourite mobile Apps as Snapchat for Snap word competition and TikTok, and planted friendship trees.
Thoughtfully planned training tours offered an insight into each country's culture. In each LTTA there was an opportunity to get to know the local environment - nature, architecture, infrastructure, etc.
For accompanying people, this was an opportunity to learn new methods and technologies. During the project Wakelet.com was used as well as linktr.ee that previously had not been used in majority of partner’s schools.
The fact that the project was carried out in English contributed to the development of English skills for all the involved in the project.
The project involved children with limited opportunities – orphans, children from very low-income families, immigrants, young people from socially unwell families. For many young people and for some educators this project gave an opportunity to cross the border of their country for first time.  Some participants had their first-flight experience.
Project partners worked very actively on information dissemination activities. The project had its own website, Facebook profile, Instagram account, Wakalet profile, information on eTwinning environment, information on all partner schools’ home pages, publications in newspapers, etc. Nearly 59,000 people were reached through information dissemination activities, but we assume the figure is even higher because two articles were published in Aksaray local newspaper. The number of residents is about 250,000 people.
After the completion of the project, the project partners will continue to maintain the project's website and profiles on social networks.
The project also faced a number of challenges: THE COVID19 pandemic, which led to the extension of the project's implementation time and the restructuring of training activities; Due to the strike at the airport – Latvian participants did not reach their destination – training activity in Portugal, the war in Ukraine and the earthquake in Turkey, which had an emotional impact on all project participants. 
Despite all of the above, thanks to our flexibility and ability to adapt, we were able to overcome all difficulties and fulfil all the tasks we committed to in the project application, which is also confirmed by the results of questionnaires after each learning activity and reflection circles in each partner school.
