We plan a rise in the number of girls in science classes (and maintenance of this state), an increase in the number of students choosing science subjects in the high school exams, an increase in the number of students choosing mathematics, computer science and physics at the extended level during school leaving exams.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2020-1-PL01-KA229-082221.title: SHALL WE PLAY A GAME ?
2020-1-PL01-KA229-082221.summary:
Games play a vital role in education across all age groups. Even for adults, the enjoyment of games persists, regardless of the genre. They represent one of the most effective tools for conveying knowledge. Traditional teaching methods no longer suffice in the classroom. If educators solely rely on conventional approaches, students become disengaged quickly, making it challenging to maintain their attention. Instead of these dull, conventional, and stress-inducing teaching methods, games and outdoor learning activities offer an excellent alternative for students and teachers. Research indicates that students acquire knowledge efficiently and retain it more effectively when actively engaged in the learning process. The usage of games, whether in a traditional classroom setting, outdoor activities, or digital learning environments, becomes evident through the enthusiasm and excitement in students' eyes. This transformation, even in the least enthusiastic students, underscores the pivotal role of games in the learning process.
The anticipated project outcomes involved the incorporation of gamification and 'learning by doing' methods into classroom activities, encompassing the usage of games and fieldwork approaches to enhance students' digital and language competencies. Students and teachers engaged with five primary themes during LTTs:
Let’s Explore
The Game of Reading
Integration via Games
GamEurope
Games Without Frontiers
These activities were complemented by tasks undertaken in eTwinning projects.
We aimed to
-Create an enjoyable and stress-free learning environment that optimizes time usage.
-Implement games and gamification dynamics to solidify learning outcomes.
-Develop a teaching framework incorporating games and effectively integrate project activities into classroom settings, collaborating with local authorities.
-Enhance students' study skills, enabling them to apply these skills across various domains, solve problems, and think practically.
-Boost students' intrinsic motivation, cultivating a genuine interest in course content and a desire to learn, while fostering their self-confidence and sense of control over the learning process.
-Elevate digital competence and technological literacy, incorporating tools like smart boards and web 2.0 technologies into classrooms, thereby expanding teachers' and students' horizons and research capabilities and fostering innovation.
-Strengthen teaching professionals, promoting skill development through training, conferences, and seminars.
-Raise awareness regarding gender equality, democracy, European citizenship, intercultural interaction, and cooperation among students.
-Improve students' English language proficiency, as they will use it for collaboration within international groups and to enhance their cultural awareness.
-Foster creative thinking and problem-solving skills.
The project outcomes are:
Five European Countries Board game “Border – Breakers”  Digital Escape Room, Ebook, Games in Kahoot! & LearningApps and Blooket.
Ebooks & booklets: Integration games, Integrative games, Educational games, Traditional Turkish Games
Collections: Famous scientists and fairy tale writers & Important monuments and sites, Traditional tales from around the world, Differences and similarities in United Traditional Games, Christmas and New Year’s stories with interactive games, Local Food and Agricultural Products & Natural & Historical Beauties of Our Towns, Games for ErasmusDays
Ready to use lessons & Games: Digital Citizenship, Writing project with 4C, St. Patrick’s Day, Easter; Sensory Escape Room; Quartet - card game; Field game “30”
Tutorials on Web 2.0 tools.
Scavenger hunts in Actionbound
Safer Internet Days: Kahoot!  Acrostic poem Be Safe on the Internet – a board game
A virtual board: Cultural puzzles – Jigsawplanet; A picture is worth a thousand words, Summer Games
Penzu journals
Canva presentations for Linguistic and cultural preparation for LTTs.
Teachers became acquainted with a range of digital tools to incorporate into their teaching methods. Students developed the ability to independently create educational materials using digital tools and use them for crafting quizzes and interactive games.
Our schools underwent positive transformations, acquiring new methods like gamification and outdoor learning, in addition to the tools required for implementation within the school environment. Teachers shared their newfound knowledge, exchanged experiences, and boosted their self-confidence.
We disseminated our project results, sharing best practices, accomplishments, methodologies, and new insights with schools locally and internationally. We ran workshops for teachers from our schools and regions, with a focus on gamification methods and tools, as well as outdoor learning methods.
All intangible outcomes are accessible on school websites, the project website, Twinspace, and our Facebook page.

2020-1-PL01-KA229-082232.title: The Mystery of Science
2020-1-PL01-KA229-082232.summary:
The project, in accordance with our assumptions, combined both the knowledge and skills from different fields related to science as well as the social functioning of students (eventually, the age range was from 13 to 17, so slightly broader than assumed). The total number of student participants was 110.
The main goals of the project included: the development of students' knowledge of science subjects and English language skills with the use of modern technologies and ICT, as well as expanding awareness of cultural differences in European countries, with an emphasis especially put on the partner countries. All of the goals - despite the restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic and the war in Ukraine - have been fully implemented.
In addition, the teachers broadened their knowledge and skills. During two short training programs (the first in a remote form, the second as staff mobility), the teachers increased their ICT competencies and broadened their knowledge about CLIL and bilingual teaching.
All five planned mobilities for each of the countries participating in the project were completed. Part of the mobilities, due to the pandemic and the health situation of the students, has been divided into two (Polish, Croatian and Czech). The group from Finland - for the reasons indicated above - made most of its trips at a later date. In the case of mobility to Croatia, both Finnish and Czech students went during the second term. During each trip, as planned, all participants focused on one of the key competencies: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology or geography, and also developed their language skills.
During the first meeting in Poland, the coordinators discussed program differences and the results of the internal evaluation of the project. They focused on how to solve the obstacles they encountered (some of them resulted from the fact that the first year of work was completely remote).
Before each mobility, the students, under the supervision of their teachers, prepared and performed tasks related to the selected scientific field, which were based, if possible, on the plot of the book they selected. The position indicated by them became a fictional base for project design activities; preparation of: materials promoting the book (including quizzes, songs, posters, crosswords) and tasks in the field of science, i.e. during the execution of escape rooms, as well as during games and field tasks (urban game, online and stationary workshops) conducted during various mobilities.
For each country, these were the following novels: for Poland "The Witcher" by Andrzej Sapkowski, Estonia - "Three Jolly Fellows", Czech - "77 Prague Legends", Croatia - "Croatian tales of long ago", Finland - “Moominpappa at Sea”.
Each of the mobilities was preceded - as intended - by time for reading and promoting the book, as well as online activities intended to prepare for individual mobilities, which, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, took place a little later than originally planned. Online activities that were intended to expand students' knowledge before they had the opportunity to meet in person included online lectures, webinars and interactive assignments. In the case of Estonia, these were also tasks that students performed in their own countries, i.e. growing mushrooms based on materials and tips sent by post by Estonian project participants. The culmination of each mobility was an urban game, in which all students participating in a given mobility participated, and during which knowledge in three areas was tested: a selected science subject, knowledge about a given country and city, and knowledge of tropes from a book chosen by a given country. After each mobility, the evaluation surveys determining the effectiveness and form of fulfilling the project assumptions were carried out.
Each session of the project (online work + mobility) resulted in a set of educational materials, such as quizzes, escape rooms, city games, webinars and dictionaries prepared by students and teachers. After each mobility, students also created a short vlog documenting a week spent in a partner country. According to the assumptions, it was supposed to be a photo book, however, the coordinators and participants have decided to change it into a more attractive and interactive form, namely a digital book created by all countries, which documents their experiences and conclusions drawn from each of the mobilities. The book as well as the current reports on the progress of the project are published on school websites and in their social media.
According to the assumptions, the long-term benefits of the project are certainly: increasing the prestige of schools and the local environment and promoting teaching in bilingual departments (of the schools concerned) as well as learning English and developing some positive educational practices among the teachers.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2020-1-PL01-KA229-082320.title: Teen Einsteins
2020-1-PL01-KA229-082320.summary:
The project is a cooperation for innovation and exchange of good practices among five European schools from Poland (the coordinator), Italy, Greece, Croatia and Bulgaria. The project duration is 24 months starting from 1 September 2020. The participants of the project are students aged 13-19 attending comprehensive or vocational schools.The project title is: "Teen Einsteins." The main objective of the project is to increase the level of achievement and interest in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. This will be done through experiential approach towards teaching which proves that only by doing experiments students can understand  science. The project’s mission is to refute the accusation against school that is considered to be irrelevant and far from reality. The real problem of today's education is that science is taught mainly theoretically. The project will teach science practically by letting students discover theory in practice. Students will be observing and deducing. They will be using formulas to produce tangible produce. They will be also exploring jobs which use scientific methods and formulas. 
 The project includes five short exchanges of pupils during which students will be engaged in the activities connected with forensics (Poland), biotechnology (Bulgaria), food processing (Croatia), robotics (Italy) and cosmetology (Greece). The acitivities will be mainly of experiential nature to let students discover the laws of science through action. 
 Before each exchange students will be working on Twinspace carrying out tasks developing their linguistic skills and deepening their knowledge in science, technology, engineering and maths. They will be filming experiments done in class and analysing them. They will also be writing lesson plans including  detaled instructions on how to complete an experiment.  They will be writing quizzes concerning the fields of science they want to master. Quizzes will be solved by students from partner schools to master the language from that field. 
 The project aims to create opportunities for students to develop key competences they will need in their professional life: scientific, social, and linguistic. 
 The expected result of the project is  increased motivation for active participation in  classes of Science and Maths as well as increased interest in engineering and technology. The project is to make lessons more lively and entertaining through introducing more job-related activities into the school curricula to prepare students for the labour market and make them aware of a great variety of the jobs it offers.
 The project will help teachers to take science to the next level.Thanks to the project they will provide their laboratories with essential equipment and resources for regular use to bridge the gap between what a student wants and what a school can offer.The project will grant students a first-class educational experience while teachers will enrich their didactic base for the future.The tangible results will be videos showing scientific experiments, lesson plans for creative teaching of Science/Maths and Robotics as well as dictionaries explaining the language  of professions offered by the partner schools.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2020-1-PL01-KA229-082321.title: UPCYCLING - A PROJECT FROM BOTTOM TO TOP
2020-1-PL01-KA229-082321.summary:
The ideas for this project were developed by a group of teachers connected by a common concern about environmental issues, particularly, about pollution. These teachers have previously collaborated through the eTwinning platform in the project: Waking up to Environmental Destruction, where we did some research which showed that students do not focus on reducing and reusing various materials to a satisfactory level. We evaluated the results and came to the conclusion that the curricula of our schools do not pay enough attention to recycling education or to motivating students toward sustainable living. We concluded that it is worth to encourage students not only to recycle but also to upcycle – using waste materials to create new items of higher value. Additionally, upcycling will help us increase students’ creativity, which is not developed in a satisfactory level within the framework of our curricula and is part of some important key competences, which should be enhanced in our schools. Upcycling provides a creative approach towards recycling. To lead our efforts to results, we would like to create lesson plans which will include ideas created by our project team. Those lesson plans will be permanently included in the curricula of our schools.
 
 The objectives of our project are:
 -Conveying the knowledge about the properties of different materials (glass, plastic, paper, metal, fabrics) and their recycling potential to students.
 -Motivating students to do recycling and upcycling.
 -Introducing lessons about the properties of different materials and their recycling potential as well as lessons concerning upcycling issues into the framework of obligatory classes of technology, design, art and science.
 -Amplifying students’ creativity.
 
 We would like to produce results such as:
 -Increase of students’ knowledge about the properties of various materials and their recycling and upcycling potential, higher level of students’ motivation towards recycling and upcycling and higher level of their creativity.
 -Development of 6 lesson plans based on recycling materials for the subjects of technology and design, science, music and 12 lesson outlines with ideas from various subjects for the art classes.
 -Upcycling workshops during each mobility and as a local activity, creation of musical instruments, shopping bags, masks against coronavirus, sculptures, copies of well known works of art, flower pots, table decorations, participants’ portraits, decorative bottles, recycling bins, bird feeders, planters in a vertical garden, a chandelier, decorative mosaics from plastic caps and other products suggested by students.
 -Creation of an Upcycling Club and a recycling storage area with bins for recycling materials at each school.
 -Production of a leaflet ‘Think green. Use less paper’, a lapbook 'Less waste during shopping’, a comic book about waste, a poster 'Let's recycle better', an interactive poster 'Upcycling fabrics - the trendiest fashion' and an e-photo album with pictures of beautiful natural sites visited during
 mobilities.
 -Exhibition of materials and works created by students during the project.
 
 The main beneficiaries of the project are students from 12 to 16. About 25 students in each school will be partakers involved in all project activities. The indirect participants of the project include students attending the obligatory classes, where the teachers will have lessons using the materials and objects produced in the project. We assume there will be at least 4 groups of students in each partner school (depending on the school's character). The whole school community can attend the exhibition of project products (3300 people in the whole partnership). Each school will have a team of teachers who will collaborate directly in the project. There will also be teachers who will participate in some aspects of the project or provide extra support. Parents and families of core students who are directly involved in the project (about 25 families per school), will inevitably be exposed to our upcycling ideas and will also be involved in hosting foreign students from partner schools during international visits. Last but not least, the local authorities will be present at the meeting organised during the mobilities and will be invited to the final exhibition.
 
 Each mobility will be devoted to a different recycling material, it will be also combined with our project tasks on eTwinning. We will prefer students – centered approach (cooperative learning). Students will work in small groups, both during debates and upcycling workshops.
 Lesson plans will be based on the method of multidisciplinary teaching. Digital technologies will be applied as well. The project will provide a European dimension to our schools and will enable to exchange good practices and expand the horizons of the students and teachers.

2020-1-PT01-KA229-078343.title: Grow Healthy! Let's Create a Well-Being Cocktail!
2020-1-PT01-KA229-078343.summary: The “Grow Healthy! Let's create a wellness cocktail!” project assumes the importance of the internationalization of schools in the sustainability of education, as a differentiating strategy for the development of everyone involved and of all sectors of global society. The four partner schools, Portugal as the coordinating and Croatia, Turkey and Bulgaria as partners, believe that their teachers and students must have the opportunity to improve the quality and competitiveness of their teaching institution and the healthy lifestyle learning. Educational institutions have a duty to help their teachers/staff and students to develop and become physically and balanced people, competent to live and work in the European environment of pluralism, tolerance and receptivity. The project life cycle is 24 months, starting in September (2020) and end in August (2022) and involves the participation of the entire school community. Involves the direct participation in mobility’s of 48 young people (12 from each country), aged between 14 and 19 years old, a significant part being from disadvantaged sociocultural contexts, and 24 teachers (6 each country). The project includes four short-term exchanges of groups of pupils in Portugal/Turkey/Croatia/Bulgaria. During short-term exchanges, participants will work on the topic of physical and emotional well-being, applying technology, theater, games, sport, mindfulness, nutrition, art, biology, geography, languages, among others. The logistics aspects (travel/insurance/CES/accommodation) are ensured. Selection is transparent, disseminating the project, motivating the school community and wider audiences. An interview will be held, with defined and publicized criteria, based on equal opportunities. The students/teachers are asked for the CV/motivation letter. Other project events in each country includes: meetings to delineate content and implementation/evaluation/dissemination/workshops/campaigns/road shows/games. Channels are used to facilitate communication (Twinspace/phone/email/skype).It is intended to produce, among others, the following results, leaflets, posters, videos, CLIL classes, emotional first aid kit, healthy eBook, bulletins, workshops, collaborative learning methods, renewal of instruments and methodologies for assessing projects. This project primarily aims at endowing its participants with the opportunity of international cooperation with the purpose of acquiring and developing basic skills and key competences, fostering innovation when it comes to teaching practices, enhancing ICT use in teaching and promoting life-long learning. The project aims to provide participants with information on human physical and emotional well-being, the creation of new digital tools and materials related to the theme and to integrate them into the existing curricula of the institutions, also contributing to the reduction of obesity, diabetes and sedentary lifestyle and better emotional management. We want have the opportunity to strengthen the sense of European identity in young generations and prepare them to participate in Europe's economic, social and cultural development, as well as offering them opportunities to favor principles, values, individual freedoms and democracy. We intend exchange best practice examples with the partners and a wider community in each participating country and develop Twinspace of the project and a common webpage where schools can communicate and exchange ideas and upload materials. Supporting certificates will be issued and requested the Europass Mobility for students. The involvement of the students/staff in the exploration/dissemination will be encouraged. When the participants return to their schools they will train their peers concerning the knowledge, experience and results they gained during the exchange. All the partners will work together in eTwinning sharing their materials and results, which will also be disseminated via partner school webpages and the project webpage. We believe that the project will result a long-term in a better understanding of human physical and emotional health, increase in healthy diet and active lifestyle in young generations, decrease in obesity, diabetes and emotional issues. Furthermore, we believe that the cooperation among the partners will result in a collection of new, innovative teaching approaches and materials applicable to the curricula of their educational organizations. By making the materials and results of the project publicly available in school webpages, eTwinning, Erasmus + Project Results Platform and the project webpage, other educational institutions and interested individuals and parties will be able to improve their methodologies, beyond the term of the project. Europe's partners promote quality training through cooperation, sharing methodologies, in the current context of globalization, with a solid network of cooperation between all, valuing and giving visibility to the Erasmus + Project.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2020-1-PT01-KA229-078874.title: Play and Learn...In Nature
2020-1-PT01-KA229-078874.summary:
The Play and Learn in Nature project is a project that proves to be innovative in its educational practices by transcending the school walls and contextualizing itself in outdoor environments, in a collaborative action between kindergartens in Portugal, Croatia, Slovenia, Serbia and Poland.
Context: The project originated from the need to provide quality educational practices where the outdoor spaces of schools were valued as learning spaces in contact with nature, caring for and respecting it. In this sense, it was essential to share educational experiences between partner schools, with their differentiated knowledge, which allowed them to complement and enrich the methodological strategies of each educator. Likewise, cooperation with local institutions in promoting activities and projects was recurrent and resulted in high input, both for children and teachers who began to include the activities they learned in their practices and who, by disseminating them , inspired other colleagues. The involvement of families was extraordinarily relevant in the implementation and execution of the project, often providing basic support in carrying out the activities, whether with physical help or with the logistics necessary for success.
The objectives are: to develop children's potential, allowing them to explore and learn in nature; encourage the adoption of healthy lifestyle habits, such as practicing physical activity outdoors; promote respect and care for nature, both in prevention and solution; train staff in alternative educational practices to the detriment of traditional ones; value outdoor spaces as educational learning spaces; encourage collaborative practices between local staff and European project partners; encourage the creation of new projects whose focus is linked to the SDGs; invest, on an ongoing basis, in the digital and linguistic training (command of the English language) of staff and children.
The activities carried out in the project were carefully planned between the partners in order to satisfy the children's interests, help with their difficulties, meet their needs and expand their knowledge. When preparing these plans, the team of coordinators took into account the added value of each school involved to be shared. He also considered the educational offer of his community to enrich the project and the way in which families could be agents that drive and energize the project. This achieved a global involvement of all educational actors responsible for education, in carrying out very functional activities for the motor, cognitive and emotional development of our children. These activities included outdoor games, creation and exploration of the school's organic garden, walks and games in the forest, observation and identification activities of animals and plants, among others.
The results of the project show that the goals established at the beginning were achieved or even surpassed, an excellent indicator of success, which means that the project achieved its main objectives and obtained the desired results in different aspects, namely: with the children, we verified who spend more time playing outdoors, who are more motivated for curricular learning and have a great active participation in protecting and preserving the environment; with the team, it is evident the change in pedagogical practices in which they value playing, the promotion of nature preservation actions, collaborative work, training as teacher training in the areas of the environment, digital and English language skills; with families and the community, there is a high level of participation in school life (in projects and activities), a greater predisposition to learn about alternative and innovative educational practices, greater concern about environmental issues, and a growing curiosity about educational practices from other countries.
The expected long-term benefits are the integral development of children, including their physical and mental health, increased environmental awareness, the formation of healthy lifestyle habits that can last until adulthood, a change in the educational practices of childhood, in order to value playing more as the most serious activity a child can carry out, and greater community involvement in children's education. We consider that this project has and will have a significant impact on education and we hope that the project will contribute to the formation of more conscious and responsible citizens, capable of dealing with the ecological problems of the 21st century.
In conclusion, we believe that this project has created a significant impact on the educational community and we believe it will have a lasting effect on children's lives and teachers' practice.

2020-1-RO01-KA229-079765.title: CULTURAL BRIDGES IN EUROPE
2020-1-RO01-KA229-079765.summary:
The project "Cultural Bridges in Europe" aims to exchange best practices on rediscovering, highlighting the customs and traditions specific to each partner country and cultivating feelings of respect for national and European values that will be promoted within specific activities,will last for 24 months and will run from 01.09.2020 to 31.08.2022.Is based on the common need of the partners involved, to rediscover, conserve and promote their cultural heritage because we have found that there is a tendency to decrease the interest for promoting their own cultural heritage but also a low degree of knowledge of the culture and civilization of countries in the European space.
 Objectives:O.1 The multicultural development and the improvement of the experience in the international cooperation of 88 students and 60 teachers from the 6 schools participating in the project, in the next 2 years.O.2 Promoting the cultural heritage, traditions and customs specific to each participating country through the 6 schools included in the project, in the next 2 years.O.3 Improvement of communication skills in English in 88 pupils between 10-15 and 60 teachers from the 6 schools participating in the project, in the next 2 years.O.4 Improvement of ICT skills for 88 students aged between 10-15 and 60 teachers from the 6 countries involved in the project, in the next 2 years.O.5 Stimulating creativity, critical thinking, educational management and teamwork, for 88 students aged 10-15 and 60 teachers from the 6 partner schools, until the project is completed.
 6 schools are involved in this project:Scoala Gimnaziala Victoria, Romania the projects coordinator; KILIÇASLAN ORTAOKULU, Turkey;32 Primary School of Piraeus, Greece;Osnovna skola Bol, Croatia;CEIP SAN ISIDRO LABRADOR, Spain;ISTITUTO COMPRENSIVO S. BAGOLINO, Italy.
 The age group of the students involved is 10-15 years.Romania and Spain are located in rural areas,in economically and socially disadvantaged communities.The other 4 schools are located in the urban environment but face different social problems:students with disabilities,students of different ethnicities,students with divorced parents,etc.Romania is currently implementing an Erasmus + ka101 project,but has not been involved in Ka229 projects.Spain, Greece and Italy have implemented Ka229 projects and Turkey and Croatia have had Comenius or Erasmus projects in the past.The activities planned in accordance with the objectives of the project are the following:"Who we are?","We discover Turkey","We discover Croatia","We discover Greece","We discover Spain","We discover Italy","We discover Romania".These are activities that will take place within the transnational exchanges,have as purpose the discovery of the cultural heritage of the host country and contain workshops in multinational groups,visiting cultural and historical objectives,traditions, customs,dances and songs,traditional foods,traditional games.The monthly local activities are the following:“Launching the project site” ,"Winter holidays in Europe for friendship" ,"March 8 - International Women's Day",“Sports personalities” ,"To know more, to be better","What is our likeness and what distinguishes us?" ,"Europe gave the world ..." ,"Unique places in Europe" ,"Traditional culinary specialties" ,"Friends forever" .For all these activities we have set the target groups,objectives, expected results,evaluation tools,deadlines and responsible persons.We considered the managerial training of all aspects related to the preparation of participants for exchanges.We carefully planned the follow-up activities,with the purpose of making known the results regarding the improvement of the competences to communicate in English of the students and teachers involved in the project,the improvement of the digital,managerial skills,the increase of the students' motivation,awareness of the cultural values,development of the feeling of European membership and the opportunity offered by the Erasmus + program in establishing transnational contacts for educational purposes.
 Expected results:• Project site• The project journal "Cultural Bridges in Europe"• Encyclopedia of traditions and customs from the countries involved in the project with the title "Encyclopedia of customs and traditions in Europe"• Panels with relevant images from the activities within the transnational mobilities and/or meetings•facebook page and the creation of the eTwinning open group "Cultural Bridges in Europe".The etwinning project "Cultural Bridges in Europe".
  Impact:The validation of this project will set in motion the teaching bodies of the 6 partner schools and the related school and local communities.beneficiaries will understand that united Europe means knowing the other, mutual respect, collaboration, tolerance and acceptance of diversity of all kinds.Schools will gain national and international prestige and will establish transnational ties.

2020-1-RO01-KA229-079801.title: Green Energy Saves the Earth
2020-1-RO01-KA229-079801.summary:
Green Energy Saves the Earth is a 6 countries partnership: in the context of climate change, pollution and other environment issues, the project brings scientific solutions - the use of Green energy that nature provides, with zero pollution and no waste, using the available natural and clean energy resources such as the sunlight, wind, water, waves, geothermal energy, steam and bio-energy to generate power.
 Our preliminary survey in partner schools shows pupils have 80% low knowledge of green energy and need to study it.
 Objectives of the project: 1.  improving students' knowledge, scientific and practical skills related to natural energy and environment 2. making science learning more attractive 3. promoting inclusion by offering equal opportunities of learning to students from different social backgrounds. 
 The project aims to teach young generations about green energy, starting with a target group of 600 pupils from 6 countries, 11-15 years old. Target group can be later expanded to other age groups, increasing the number of direct beneficiaries from partner schools. 
 Target group of indirect beneficiaries starts from 1000 people as random international audience, expanding it to other countries outside the partnership.
 Activities: 
 - Studying production of fuel, hardboard, natural glue from agricultural waste.
 - Making presentations about natural /green energy: sunlight, water, waves, wind, hydroelectric, geothermal and bio-energy as renewable energy sources
 - Studying the use of each energy source in their city. Analysis of natural energy use in the region. Students investigate local situation regarding energy use.
 - Studying pollution in the regions, cities and sources of local pollution.
 - Studying dangers to the environment and eco-system (extinct or endangered species, poisonous fertilizers, chemical pollution in food, plastic waste in nature), how to clean the water of the seas and oceans.
 - Making a blueprint of the ecological home for the green city of the future with green transport and natural energy. What does the future planet look like?
 - Statistics: how much natural energy is used in their community (homes with solar panels, wind generators etc) Comparison between regions/countries. 
 - Creative writings: compositions about the future world using natural energy without pollution.
 - Making posters, drawings about a better future of the world without pollution.
 - Visits of documentation to power plants or hydroelectric companies that use natural energy in the regions 
 - Workshops about carbon footprint, ecological footprint and water footprint. Calculating each footprint.
 - Outdoor activities sanitizing the environment, promoting eco-friendly attitude and responsibility to the environment.
 -Workshop about soil pollution, consequences of chemicals in agriculture. Make a simple natural compost in bottle from wastes of fruit, vegetable, tea.
 - Workshop about causes of water pollution and recycling. Making a simple water filter.
 - Workshop about acid rains and ozone depletion. Causes, consequences, prevention.
 - Workshop about international agreements about the environment and climate change effects.
 - Importance of recycling. Waste battery campaign.
 Methodology: workshops, studies, group activities, practical activities, scientific research, analyses.
 Results / Outputs:
 - Innovative result: Guide for Green Energy, manual for natural, ecological and renewable energy for the future. By this book the project aims to make information available to the world, expanding the target group to as many as possible other beneficiaries and generations.
 The Guide for Natural Energy  contains theoretical information and guidelines for practical lessons and activities about natural resources of energy and how to use them.
 - Project magazine, with scientific articles and studies written by teachers and students, related to the environment issues and solutions.
 - Posters, drawings, essays.
 - Practical engineering results - machines that use natural green energy, power generators built by pupils with the guidance of teachers:
 -a wind generator
 -a sunlight generator
 -a steam turbine(geothermal)
 -a hydropower generator
 -a wave generator
 Outcomes: improved STEM interest and skills, improved knowledge and awareness of environment problems / solutions involving the use of green energy, increased enthusiasm for learning sciences, improved foreign language and ICT skills, better integration of disadvantaged pupils.
 Impact on pupils: improved knowledge and use of green energy, increased interest for science and engineering, improved solidarity in solving environment issues, improved foreign language and ICT skills. Teachers: improved teaching skills. Schools: added European dimension, better quality and management.
  Longterm benefits: better science knowledge for new generations, better mentality, improved responsibility to nature, a cleaner environment, better quality of life, better future for the planet, a better world.

2020-1-RO01-KA229-079850.title: Our Culture Our Future
2020-1-RO01-KA229-079850.summary:
The project consists of six countries Italy, Croatia, Romania, Turkey, Portugal, Macedonia will work together on exploring our European tangible and intangible cultural heritage of each participating country. During the project time, while working on project activities partners will compare their traditions, find differences and similarities, find diversity in European unity. All peoples make their contribution to the culture of the world. That’s why it’s important to respect and safeguard all cultural heritage, through national laws and international treaties. 
 
 Cultural heritage implies a shared link, our belonging to a community. It represents our history and our identity; our link to the past, to our present, and the future. In the case of “cultural heritage,” the heritage doesn’t consist of money or property, but of culture, values and traditions. Heritage” is a property, something that is inherited, passed down from previous generations. So we must protect it and ensure it is passed on to the next generations. This project will motivate us to realize this responsibility and will remind others about the importance of cultural heritage. At this point, a great job falls on educational and public bodies.
 
 The main objective of the project is working on activities related to European cultural heritage. Cultural heritage is our treasure and priceless value for each individual and society and as such, it should be preserved to future generations. Young people and pupils should be familiar with the value of their past. Our aims are to:
 • Reinforce a sense of belonging to Europe 
 • Raise awareness of European common history and values
 • Focus on Engaging students and teachers for an Inclusive and Sustainable Europe project
 • Better protect, safeguard, reuse, enhance, valorize and promote Europe’s cultural heritage
 • Spread the word about the significance of caring for and transmitting our shared heritage
 • Encourage the sharing and appreciation of Europe’s cultural heritage as a common resource
 • Explore the safeguarding challenges of tangible and intangible cultural heritage in the European context. These aims specified in European Framework for Action on Cultural Heritage to get a holistic approach, looking at cultural heritage as a resource for the future and putting people at its heart.
 
 In the light of ET 2020(to promote equity, social cohesion and active citizenship) be the growth of our countries by the need to include our heritage: where the past meets the future, which stressed the role of young people in keeping heritage, tradition and culture alive in educational policies. There are many forms of cultural heritage and in our project, we will handle both tangible and intangible forms.
 
 We plan the concrete results thanks to our project-based activities
 •COOKBOOK
 •Special days list
 •Exhibition of Postcards
 •E-booklet of our Heritages
 •Pdf files of LESSON Plans
 •Cultural Heritage Clubs & UNITs 
 •Brochures& videos of LEGENDS
 •Project Website/Youtube Channel/ FB page
 •Integration of Cultural Heritage in our curriculums
 •4 different eTwinning Projects &2 eTwinning Events
 •Collection of photos/drawings of traditional instruments
 •İmages /videos of buildings, monuments, landscapes, artefacts
 •A PDF file of books, customs, folklore, traditions, Flora&Fauna
 •presentations about famous artists, sportsmen, Nobel and Oscar winners, musicians
 
 All our workshops, peer to peer activities, trips, school clubs and units will provide to explore potential synergies and challenges of the safeguarding of cultural heritage in the European context. The LTT activities will be wit 4 pupils aged 11-15 (1st and 4th LTTs with 5 pupils)and 2 teachers and that will be selected pursuant to the selection rules.10 of the pupils will be with economical/social/geographical obstacles.
 C1 will be on Romanian tangible&intangible heritage
 C2 will be on Macedonian tangible&intangible heritage
 C3 will be on Italian tangible&intangible heritage
 C4 will be on Portuguese  &intangible heritage
 C5 will be on Croatian tangible&intangible heritage
 C6 will be on Turkish tangible&intangible heritage
 
 During LTT activities participants will compare their culture with the others and will get respect to the others. They'll explore monuments, clothing, artwork, heritage sites, artefacts, food, as well as landscapes, languages and oral traditions with project-based learning methods and get awareness on our heritage.
 
 Versatile Contributions of this project aspected in short and long-term for our schools In the long term, for our schools, this project will benefit to
 -increase the usage rate of the cultural heritage at the curriculum
 -Raise awareness of protecting Europe’s cultural heritage
 -increase awareness of European common history and values
 -develop educational aspects for an Inclusive and Sustainable Europe
 -integrate tangible and intangible heritage via teaching historical, sociologic, ecological and environmental subjects into all lectures
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-RO01-KA229-079944.title: Students ENgaged in Sustainability Education(SEnSE)
2020-1-RO01-KA229-079944.summary:
This project was the result of the common needs identified in 4 schools from Croatia, Lithuania, Romania and Spain: the need for inclusion, the need to vary the teaching methods so that they correspond to the characteristics of today's students, the need to carry on with the existing cross-curricular approaches and the need to involve our students in current global issues. 
The project was aimed at strengthening inclusion at our institutions through project-based learning, in response to the growing number of
students who were at risk of exclusion for different reasons. The project involved students aged 6-15 and their teachers, together with local organisations (universities, NGOs, educational stakeholders). It used project-based learning methodology documented by the participating teachers, which helped the students to meet important learning goals, find a solution to a meaningful question to solve a problem, explore phenomena using scientific practices, engage in collaborative activities to find solutions to the driving question, uses learning tools and other scaffolds to support students’ learning and create tangible products that addressed the driving question.
We carried out one short-term training event for our teachers in the fields of PBL and inclusion in order to ensure a balance between the knowledge and skills of the participating staff and the quality of the activities of the project as well.
The participants were involved in  5 modules derived from 5 Sustainable Development Goals, which represented the connection with the real world: "Know disaster, no disaster!" (Climate action), "Slow the flow, save H2O!" (Clean water and sanitation), "Know your trees" (Life on land), "An ocean of plastics" (Life below water) and "Product tales" (Responsible consumption and production). Moreover, the activities of the project focused on creating inclusive classrooms by recognising and valuing diversity, developing positive attitudes towards diversity in our learners, involving
parents, learners and other relevant individuals in creating an inclusive learning environment, assessing individual learners in a variety of ways that allowed them to demonstrate the progress they made and supported the students in identifying, addressing and assessing learning goals based on reasonable adjustment, designing teaching and learning materials which cater for multiple learning styles, using group work which fostered the use of each student's own capacities.
We created 5 booklets which contain the detailed description of the projects made by the students. In terms of intangible results, we obtained an enhanced sense of belonging to the school culture and trust in the students' capacities and potential, enhanced cooperation at EU level, increased professional satisfaction in our teachers, enhanced PBL, ICT and foreign languages competences. 
The most important gains of this project were a developed competence in using project-based learning, the huge progress in using online tools and a complete change in understanding digital learning, not to mention sustainable development. The latter can be expressed in using a variety of ICT instruments in class and online and being able to organise interactive online activities in a multitude of manners.
On the long term, we intend to use the results of the project on a daily basis, in organising elective classes or answering the new national requirements in our countries.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-RO01-KA229-079965.title: SCIENCE IS ALL AROUND US
2020-1-RO01-KA229-079965.summary:
Our technologically advanced society's expanding demands have highlighted the critical need for engineers, scientists, and IT specialists.This is in direct contrast to the current trend among young people, who have demonstrated little interest in pursuing fields connected to Maths and science, both in their academic studies and in their prospective employment choices.Our joint project has brought together five schools from RO,CRO, PO, PL and TR, all of which recognize a common problem that can be effectively addressed through reciprocal learning and the sharing of successful techniques.Our 6th partner, from Latvia, withdrew from the very beginning. 
Our initiative has been methodically aimed at encouraging our pupils' scientific curiosity while also improving their mathematical skills, while additionally improving teaching and evaluation methodologies. 
The main objective of our initiative has been to develop our students' numerical, scientific, and practical abilities through the use of inquiry-based learning methodologies.To achieve our goals, students participated actively in Project clubs, where an integrated, cross-disciplinary approach was used to immerse them in a dynamic process of discovery and learning.New methods were also implemented in regular science and arts classes.
A variety of new techniques, resulted with collaboration with local universities, including inquiry-based learning, hands-on experiences, sports education, virtual online science labs, and STEAM activities, have been implemented. These new methods were meant to help students discover the numerous connections between science and everyday life, sparking their curiosity and nurturing their creativity. Students worked in groups in these environments, conducting scientific investigations and deliberating on solutions proposed by their peers. They played the roles of investigators and analogy builders.
The new teaching-learning methods have given pupils who are passionate about the sciences a thorough comprehension of the subject matter. In addition, it has stimulated the interest of those who had struggled in the past, encouraging them to explore the intriguing nature of the sciences through experiments, outdoor activities, games, thereby preventing early dropout and academic underachievement.
Five LTTAs were part of our initiative, in which 5-7 students and 2-3 teachers from every country, joined together. Participants were encouraged to embrace the qualities of committed citizens who are interested in promoting local and social values by engaging in a variety of activities. Their foreign language ability has significantly improved within the global context of our shared efforts, and their personal and socio-educative growth has also advanced significantly.
Additionally, we have focused  on enhancing students' inventiveness, enhancing their presenting skills, growing their communicative ability, and strengthening their cooperation abilities that are considered to be among the most crucial for success in the 21st-century labor market. These skills will make it easier for them to integrate and adapt to the workforce.
Results :
(O1) 77% of target group students developed numerical and scientific skills
(O2) 81% of students in international meetings improved critical thinking and practical skills
(O3) All participants enhanced knowledge of foreign cultures and inquiry-based learning
(O4) 82% of students improved soft skills and effectiveness in daily life
(O5) Most participants improved communication skills
(O6) All participants enhanced curiosity and creativity by connecting sciences to real life
With its emphasis on highlighting the importance of science, the project has the potential to have a lasting impact. It will continue to offer precious resources and lasting benefits:
Increased Awareness: The project will promote an ongoing interest for science by raising awareness of its importance.
Resourceful Materials: The project's demonstration lessons, innovative materials, and fun STEAM activities will all serve as lasting educational resources.
Academic Reference The "Science for All" guidebook will be a useful resource for educators, providing direction and inspiration for effectively teaching science.
Inspiration from Media: Teachers and students will continue to be motivated and inspired by short films and videos that highlight project activities and student work, kindling a passion for science.
Enriched Teaching:CLIL lesson plans will promote enriched teaching techniques, assuring a more comprehensive education, in subjects like math, physics, biology, geography, and chemistry.
Two magazines that summarize the activities of the international initiative will offer viewpoints and insights to a larger school community, encouraging an exchange of ideas.
Accessibility: The project's dedicated website will make sure that these valuable assets continue to be visible and accessible, helping both teachers and students in the years to come.

2020-1-RO01-KA229-080131.title: Together, beyond differences- Accept me as I am!
2020-1-RO01-KA229-080131.summary:
Every year in all partner schools there are threats such as low motivation, absenteeism, verbal and physical violence, including bullying and cyber-bully, school drop-outs. It has been found that those most affected by these types of behavior are especially students at risk:with a precarious material situation, from single-parent families or with departed parents, of other ethnic groups, students who have learning difficulties. In order to ensure the inclusion of these students from different socio-cultural backgrounds, different ethnicities, with special needs, it is necessary to include them in appropriate educational programs that offer, at the same time, to all students from the partner schools behavioral models that promote tolerance, solidarity, respect beyond any differences, to increase their learning motivation and to help them establish functional relationships based on mutual acceptance and respect.
 The project"Together, beyond differences- Accept me as I am!" is focused on to increase the institutional capacity of the parterer schools to meet pupils’ needs aged between 10 and 15 through programs and educational activities that offer attractive learning alternatives and contexts capable of developing those social competences that ensure the educational and social inclusion of all pupils, programs and activities which promote diversity and intercultural exchange. The project also aims to develop skills for teachers in designing and implementing formal and non-formal learning activities and educational projects adapted to the needs of all categories of students, that ensure equal access to education for all students to combat social exclusion and integrating European values in education and training,thus contributing to increasing the motivation for learning and educating students in the spirit of tolerance and interculturality and limiting negative phenomena affects the school life of the students, contributing to increasing motivation for learning and student education and reducing the risk of school dropout. The objectives were set in accordance with the chosen priorities, related to the development of new competences for both teachers and students involved in the project,by capitalizing the non-formal education valences in activities that will both increase motivation for school success and educational and social inclusion.
 Our project provides 6 international learning opportunities: 4 short-term mobility for 150 students (25 from each school) and 2 short-term mobility for 60 teachers (10 from each school) -valuable sources of examples of good practices and materials that can be used in the long run in the schools involved to promote Europe values,to collect 3 non-formal strategies, 2 methods/techniques, innovative methods of working with pupils with special needs, sharing best practices and developing a Guide to Good Practices of Inclusive Education and a Strategy for combating violence in partner schools and other activities designed to develop to the students attitudes and abilities of social inclusion - acceptance, mutual respect, solidarity.
 The project activities were structured in three directions:
 A. Activities to help students understand and enforce unanimously accepted moral codes of conduct, basic concepts that highlight the nature of interpersonal relationships - gender equality, nondiscrimination, multiculturalism etc., to improve teamwork skills, social skills, to provide them with the opportunity to interact with other educational environments that can be models of harmonious coexistence.On this line is also the Campaign for information and prevention of bullying in schools and eTwinning project "Hate speech...".To ensuring the educational and social inclusion of all students to acquire new skills for students: teamwork skills, improve their social and civic skills- acquire attitudes of acceptance and combat intolerance, appreciate diversity and reduce intolerant behaviors, improved interpersonal and which will help to achieve a comfortable level of functional communication, tolerance, empathy, openness to understand different points of view, manage conflict situations, develop resistance to stress and frustration.
 B. Learning and teaching activities and exchange of best practices for teachers which intended acquiring new non-formal methods and techniques in educational activities - acquire new working skills for teachers through which it is intended acquiring 3 strategies including methods, techniques and non-formal learning tools,2 methods/techniques with pupils with special needs, develop project implementation abilities, work on the eTwininng platform,used to this type of project, build confidence in their ability to develop and implement projects, including Erasmus+ projects. 
 C. Activities aimed at intercultural exchange by promoting the values of the cultural heritage of partner countries and developing the European dimension of partner schools through the strategic partne

2020-1-RO01-KA229-080180.title: Unique National and European Symbols of our Culture and Originality
2020-1-RO01-KA229-080180.summary:
Nowadays, students are required to be culturally aware, they need to learn about it and be able to act as a bridge between cultures and between tradition and modernity and serve as key agents in promoting an intercultural understanding. Adolescents tend to question the customs, traditions, beliefs and attitudes that have been transmitted to them in childhood, while seeking their place in the world and their own identity. Due to the fact that culture and education are not appreciated at their real value, European schools are increasingly having young people with many learning problems, and the lack of culture can prevent them from evolving in a constantly dynamic European market.  The project addresses the need identified in the 6 schools involved to raise the students awareness of UNESCO European heritage, to make the students more sensitive to the meaning of European culture.
 The main goal of this project is to give young people the opportunity to enrich knowledge about European Unesco Heritage by promoting a wider understanding of Unesco heritage as a common European good, through innovative learning, teaching methods and digital ways. 
 The project objectives are: raising young people’s awareness of the importance of Unesco European heritage, its conservation, enhancement and transmission for 500 students by the end of the project; increasing by 20% every 2 months the number of educational activities which can lead to an increase in students’ knowledge about European culture; making 2000 students familiar with their own and other European countries’ Unesco heritage, by promoting local, national and international cultures during 2 years of the project; stimulating the school success of 300 disadvantaged students from partner schools by giving them the chance to improve their knowledge about Unesco cultural heritage participating in outdoor and open education in an intercultural way; improving English language level and the specific vocabulary related to natural and cultural heritage for 500 students directly involved in the project activities, during the project lifetime; developing ICT skills for 2000 students by using the webquests, the online game, the project website, during the project activities.
 This project will involve highschool students, aged 14-19 years. They will participate in the interactive activities, like: Instagram photo competition aimed to encourage students to capture one Europe’s Unesco elements, celebrating the International days observed by UNESCO, creating the original postcard and participating in challenges, participating in lessons using webquests, playing Kahoot games regarding Unesco heritage during classes, creating flyers using QR codes in order to promote Unesco heritage, eTwinning activities. Teachers from each partner school (English, History, Tourism, Geography, ICT) who will bring all the knowledge and will have an active role in project activities.
 The project timeline is divided into 6 topics: natural heritage, cultural heritage, European heritage in danger, representative list of the intangible heritage, intangible elements in need of urgent safeguarding and the tentative list. The specific activities dedicated to each of the 6 topics will be completed with workshops on sustainable tourism, criteria for selection and good safeguarding practices of the sites, and presentations of the most important initiatives that help promote awareness and provide tools for students to engage with heritage: GoUNESCO, Go Heritage Runs, #makeheritagefun.
 Final products and results will be: project website, e-twinning project space, the online app available on Google play which will be addressed to teachers and pupils in secondary schools, a variety of online tools - webquests and Kahoot games created as fun and interactive activities for working in a group and for learning about Unesco European heritage and the international days observed at UNESCO;digital stories and sharing presentations in an interactive way using Microsoft Sway;leaflets with different elements of the European Unesco heritage where QR codes will be introduced.
 Permanent communication (e-mails, WhatsApp, Skype, Messenger, Signal, phone), the agreement signed and assumed by all the partners, the project timeline, the communication and dissemination plan (including DEOR plan), the monitoring plan will be used to avoid some misunderstanding between partners. The project idea is to assure free access of this educational materials to a high number of students and teachers to know more, to understand better and appreciate the Unesco cultural heritage.
 The outcomes have a high potential of leaving a long-lasting effect and will be used for sure by all 6 partner schools many years after the project will end within school curricula. The use of open education and outdoor education in an intercultural way will determine an increase in students' culture, will stimulate the interest for our heritage and the schools success.

2020-1-RO01-KA229-080222.title: There is no difference in being different
2020-1-RO01-KA229-080222.summary:
The 3 project partners were schools who are implementing curricular and extra-curricular activities in the field of European citizen values, of developing their European and international dimensions, of increasing the multicultural knowledge, of combating negative social phenomena (discrimination, segregation and bullying in the learning environment), of enhancing all students social development throughout providing equity and equality of chances to education, social and professional inclusion to all. One of the partner schools (Romania) educates hearing impairment students. After analysing the institutional needs of all 3 schools and notably those of the target groups of pupils, we considered that a strategic partnership was to be capable of satisfying the needs previously reffered to. Therefore, we set the following objectives: 
The general objective was: Promoting equity and inclusion by raising awareness of acceptance and tolerance of the social, linguistic and cultural diversity
 The specific objectives were:
1. Practicing new educational approaches aiming to support better personal and professional development strategies of the hearing impairment students
2. Increasing awareness of the importance of the active citizenship of the hearing students by developing their intercultural knowledge, their feelings of tolerance and acceptance of human diversity, of non-discrimination and non-segregation.  
3. Acquiring foreign languages skills (English and sign language) in order to breakdown the communication barriers and make the most of social and professional inclusion opportunities worldwide, for the target groups (hearing and hearing impairment students)
The target groups were:
 -Romania: 50 deaf students aged 10-19: LTT C2: 8 deaf students aged 12–14; LTT C1: 9 deaf students aged 15–19; 50 deaf students aged 10–19 (including the 17 ones from the international mobilities) as direct local participants
 -Croatia: 30 students aged 15-18: LTT C2: 3 students; LTT C3: 13 students; 30 students (including the 16 ones from the international mobilities) as direct local participants
 -Turkey: 30 students aged 11-17: LTT C1: 8 students aged 13–17; LTT C3: 8 students aged 11–17; 30 students aged 11–17 (including the 16 ones from the international mobilities) as direct local participants
The activities in this project were designed to lead to the achievement of proposed objectives. Therefore we planned combined activities: the physical short-term exchanges of groups of pupils with the virtual activities which took place on eTwinning platform before, during and after the LTT activities. To ensure a quality management of the project, all 3 schools in collaboration, drew up a program: 1 transnational project meeting (the 2nd one originally planned was canceled because of the earthquake in Turkey); selections of the participants; preparation activities of the mobilities; exchanges of groups of pupils; eTwinning activities; dissemination, monitoring and evaluation events. Throughout the LLT activities (icebreaking activities, sports competitions, foreign languages, sign language workshops, art (dance,drama play,role playing games), craft (creation of a banner and of a wall of tolerance), public debate(on human rights), research on the inclusion topic etc.) and the eTwinning activities, the participants developed their empathy, their capacity of tolerance and acceptance of the human diversity, their attitudes towards peers with disabilities and increased their social and language skills.
The project has been designed as a strategic partnership and therefore it aimed at bringing together partners with various competencies, backgrounds and tasks, but the same institutional needs. The schools were selected to cover different population of pupils, to represent diversity in ability, cultural and social field.
The impact on the participating schools was measured in: the openness to implementing new forms of non-formal education beneficial to students with disadvantaged background; practicing new educational approaches; enrichment for the teachers of their pedagogical knowledge through the exchange of good practice during short-term exchanges and presentations of the good practices; strengthened cooperation within the network of institutions involved into the work in the frame of transnational projects; consolidation of a more positive approach to European projects and EU; developing the European and international dimensions of the schools.
We consider that the E+ framework was compatible and supported our efforts of changing mentalities by proposing new and innovative approaches of the young people who are facing discrimination and segregation. Our overall goal was the social and professional inclusion of the deaf young people in order for them to become adults who are viable and independent members of the society, as well as for the hearing young people to embrace diversity and raise their degree of tolerance face to the different

2020-1-RO01-KA229-080276.title: Struggle Against Values Extinction
2020-1-RO01-KA229-080276.summary:
”Struggle Against Values Extinction” (SAVE) is a project aimed to help pupils get to know and value their local identity, traditions, culture and every aspect of their heritage while promoting  the awareness of being part of a larger cultural framework, as well. We expect this project will motivate pupils and teachers to widen their knowledge about the lifestyles of our European neighbours, foreign languages and use of new technologies while encouraging genuine tolerance and friendship.
 
 The overall aim of the project is to develop an individual and collective identity, by promoting the appreciation of cultural heritage through strategies that foster intercultural dialogue between European schools. The objectives pursued are to develop the capacity to identify and preserve cultural heritage, increase the acceptance of cultural diversity, promoting democracy, peace and tolerance, increase the preservation of cultural heritage by bringing ancient crafts and customs back to life, improve geographical, historical and architectural knowledge about European Cities, increase the understanding of linguistic and cultural similarities between partner countries, increase the degree of integration of cultural heritage in education by interdisciplinary activities and implementing new optional courses, improve language, ICT and cross curricular skills, encourage pupils to develop critical thinking, strengthen their independence and increase self-esteem, self-confidence and sense of cooperation, and increase the internationalization of the school by aligning with European policies in the field of education and culture. 
 
 The main beneficiaries of the project are pupils of partner schools, between the ages of 11 and 15 years and teachers from Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Italy, Portugal and Turkey whose experience and expertise in the field of education will prove very valuable in the run-up of this project.
 
 The project activities include: setting up Erasmus Cultural Heritage Clubs, where children will do research projects, work on project material, and organize artistic activities, film viewing, workshops, and online activities with pupils from partner countries; creating a cultural tourism guidebook entitled ”Culture and Heritage Across Europe”, brochures, presentations, UNESCO Cultural Maps, photo albums, recipes, videos and audio recordings; organizing the Folk Heritage Festival; composing an “Etymological Dictionary”; organizing meetings with the elders, parents and cultural authorities to rediscover and revive lost traditions; implementing an optional course entitled  “National Culture and Tradition – Identity Passport in the Big European Family” which will benefit from project acquisitions. The methodology used is designed to engage pupils in project activities and mobilities, to boost their confidence in using languages familiar and interesting to them, to stir their interest in other peoples’ culture, which will result in the acceptance of diversity, increased tolerance among pupils and teachers, preservation of cultural heritage, resurrection of legends, games, recipes, dances and old songs, better knowledge of European Cities, sustainable understanding of content and improvement of school performance, integration in the learning activities of pupils’ critical and analytical thinking.
 
 The impact that the results obtained from carrying out the project activities will have is expected to be strong, producing changes in individuals, institutions, local community and educational factors. Both during and after the project has been completed, all those involved will become more aware of their own cultural heritage and national identity, understanding how their country fits into the European Union as a whole and this will lead to: the consolidation of the European dimension of schools and improvement of school image at local, national and European level; the creation of links between pupils involved in project and mobility activities, permanent relations established between them by carrying out subsequent joint projects; the improvement of teachers’ social and organizational skills needed for their professional development; the continuation of partnerships between schools after completion of this project, taking advantage of the experience gained in developing other educational projects; the development of a positive attitude of parents toward school and toward European values; the promotion of closer ties with local authorities and cultural institutions in the area involved in the project.
 
 Sharing project results in the long run will enable others to benefit from the activities and experience of our project. Dissemination and exploitation of long-term results can serve as an example and contribute to the acquisition of good practices. Therefore, we will ensure that the results of the project will be widely available over a long period of time.
