2019-1-DE02-KA204-006126.title: Multifunctional Agriculture - Rural Education for Action
2019-1-DE02-KA204-006126.summary:
<< Background >>

The future is in the rural structures! These are the insights of the European Commission with regard to the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) after 2020. CAP aims to develop rural communities. MAREA has addressed exactly this goal: strengthening rural areas by making visible and promoting the potentials located there. By combining educational formats and tourism, the project has served several aspects noted in the CAP objective. The developed curriculum in interaction with the established places of learning not only informs about sustainability topics, but also makes them experienceable. The RuralAcademy with the developed curriculum is an excellent tool to create a new sustainable awareness based on local knowledge. The connection to adult education in the field of lifelong learning was essential and the basis for the curriculum, because education contributes to a sustainable change of consciousness. And sustainable change of consciousness is what the project "MAREA" and the RuralAcademy that has been developed and established as a result are all about.

<< Objectives >>

The overall goal of MAREA was to raise awareness of sustainability. The project set-up also strengthened rural areas, addressed a change in awareness of sustainability through the educational formats, and preserved traditional knowledge. All of these secondary goals can be attributed to the overall goal.
In the project itself, a large number of people actively dealt with the topic of sustainable living and were thus encouraged to take action. In addition to the people involved in the built places of learning, people were inspired and enabled with the curriculum to become "Rural Guides" and thus also actively promote sustainable thinking and acting. In the long-term objective, adult education plays a key role. With the project, the project partners have strengthened the active people in rural areas and qualified them to become educators. The places of learning in interaction with the Rural Guides will continue to carry education into the rural areas in the future with assured quality of the teaching formats and reach a large number of people interested in learning, especially adults, through the connection with tourism and other educational formats.

<< Implementation >>

A total of 11 activities were implemented in MAREA. Despite the ongoing Corona pandemic, only two activities could not be implemented in presence due to the flexibility and organizational and communication strength of the partner consortium.

5 international project meetings:
One project meeting was implemented in each partner country, which served for regular coordination and quality assurance of the entire project. In addition, the meetings were used to get to know the networks. The second meeting in Belgium was implemented virtually, all other meetings could take place on site at the project partners as planned.

3 Trainings:
The trainings served the further education and training of the employees and thus the quality assurance and further development of the project. The selection of the organizations was exactly aligned with the objectives. The first training was implemented virtually by the Belgian partner. The other two trainings could be implemented in presence in Croatia and Italy. The (virtual) visit to the places of learning served as a practical example in all three trainings. 

3 Multiplier events:
At the end of the project, one multiplier event each was implemented in presence in Italy, Croatia and Norway.

<< Results >>

In total, three project results were developed: 
In the first project result, a curriculum was created in which the potentials and knowledge of rural areas were integrated in order to make sustainability tangible and experienceable. The knowledge collected and processed there is made interactively accessible to the general public at various places of learning. The places of learning were searched for and mapped as part of the second project result, the so-called database. In the third project result, traditional knowledge of rural areas was prepared in short videos in order to preserve and disseminate this knowledge. Elements of the so-called "Neverending Stories" can be found in part in the curriculum as well as in the description of the individual places of learnings. In addition, a longer video was developed as part of the third project outcome, documenting the project including partner consortium, project results and activities.
Existing structures were used for a sustainable use of the results. The curriculum can be accessed via the online platform "teachable.com". In addition to their description in a booklet, the places of learning were also mapped on the "Mapping for good" platform.

2019-1-DE02-KA204-006527.title: Exchange of good practices and network creation in adult education and e-learning in the field of EU funding
2019-1-DE02-KA204-006527.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was initiated by the lead partner after realizing that no connection between educational institutions in the field of European funding and project management exists across Europe. This connection in form of exchange of good practices, discussions on new methodological approaches, as well as an exchange of information is very important to innovate the training offered by the project partners and organisations reached beyond the partnership. Only through a continuous improvement and innovation of training, the best possible education can be offered to participants. The participants can thus attend more relevant training with an improved learning outcome and have thus, better chances on the local, national and European labor market.

Therefore the exchange of knowledge, the improvement of skills in preparing, developing and implementing training at local, national and European level (through exchange of good practices) and the discussion on methodological approaches (e.g. blended learning), were the needs addressed by the present partnership.

<< Objectives >>

The objective of EU-Learning was to enable the participating organisations and their trainers to exchange best practices in the field of training on European Funding and Project Management (preparation, methodologies, innovative approaches, implementation) and to exchange information on the new funding period, through creating a European network between organisations active in the educational field of EU funding and project management as well as the creation of a handbook with information on the new funding period. 

Through this, it was planned to achieve that the direct target group (training organisations) is enabled to innovate the way they organize and implement their training, particularly in fields that have still a disrupting potential like eLearning, use of ICTs, distance teaching or blended learning. Additionally, the lack of networking and exchange of information was supposed to be reduced through the network creation.

The objective to be achieved for the indirect target group (individuals/adult learners seeking additional qualifications in EU funding) was for them to be able to receive improved and more innovative training. Through this they will have improved skills and accordingly better chances on the labor market.

<< Implementation >>

In order to achieve the project's objectives activities in form of transnational project meetings (TPMs), regular online meetings and a learning, training, teaching activity (LTTA) were implemented.

- TPMs: During the TPMs the fundamental questions for the development of the deliverables were discussed and decisions made. This refers to the handbook as well as the creation of the network. Further, the meetings served to get to know all partner organisations and their training in greater detail. A networking event was also included during the final TPM.

- regular online meetings: On a six-weekly basis online meetings of approx. 2 hours were held. The current status of the development of the deliverables were discussed, as well as challenges and according solutions.

- LTTA: A training of trainers event was conducted during three days. During this LTTA all project partners exchanged and discussed topics, such as the adaptation to different target groups, training needs analysis, partners' training offers, eLearning, challenging situations, business models or the adjustment to the COVID-19 situation.

<< Results >>

TANGIBLE RESULTS/DELIVERABLES
1) HANDBOOK (incl. common declaration): "EU-Funding Opportunities 2021-2027 - A practical Guide" was developed with particularities about the most important funding programmes of the new European funding period 2021-2027. It contains information on the funding instruments, general information on the funding period, the general structure of funding instruments, recommendations on how to create a good project proposal, and a common declaration on the expectations on the new funding period.

2) NETWORK: "PROFUND - Cluster for European Fundraising Training" was founded, consisting of European organizations active in the educational field of EU funding and project management. The Cluster is a foundation for continuous exchange and events.


INTANGIBLE/OTHER RESULTS
1) Creation of a long standing collaboration possibility between the participating organisations 
2) Definition of future common EU projects and trainings at European level
3) Development and increase of know-how for each participating organisation (and its trainers)
4) Possibility for stakeholders to find organisations providing trainings and other services related to EU funding in several European countries

2019-1-DK01-KA204-060174.title: Music, Drama and Storytelling Resources for Competence Building with Marginalised Adults
2019-1-DK01-KA204-060174.summary:
Available statistics show that around one in four adults aged 25-64 in the EU, approximately 70 million people, have not completed any formal education beyond the level of lower secondary education. This figure includes around 20 million people who left the education system with no more than primary education. The OECD Survey of Adult Skills (PIACC) found that on average, in the 17 countries that took part in the first round of this survey, 19.9% and 23.6% of adults respectively have a low level of achievement in literacy and numeracy.

Research also highlights the fact that adults with low level or no qualifications; those in low skilled occupations; the unemployed and economically inactive; older people and the least skilled are less likely to participate in lifelong learning.

There are a wide variety of barriers to education identified in the Adult Education Survey, most notably family responsibilities 21.8%; reconciling education with work schedules 13.6%; financial issues 13.3%; and insufficient ‘prerequisites’ 7.1%. However, perhaps the most important finding is that 80% of adults who do not participate in education and training do not express any interest in becoming involved in organised learning activities.

The strategic framework for European cooperation in education and training adopted in May 2009 set a number of benchmarks to be achieved by 2020. For adult adult participation in learning the objective was that at least 15 % of adults aged 25 to 64 years old should participate in lifelong learning. In the partner countries involved in the ARTSKUL project on Denmark with a participation rate of 26.8% in 2017 has achieved and exceeded the required level. For the other partner countries, the rates in 2017 were, Croatia 2.3%; Cyprus 6.9%; Italy 7.9%; Spain 7.9%; Ireland 8.9% and Portugal 9.8%. It is the opinion of partners that new approaches are needed to try and attract those on the margins of provision back to lifelong learning.

The ARTSKUL project proposes an innovative new service offering that uses performance arts disciplines including music, drama and storytelling to build a suite of embedded learning educational resources to build key transversal skills of low skilled adults. Partners are convinced that the traditional ‘sage-on-the-stage’ model of education is of little initial value in the current context. If educators are to attract adults on the margins of provision a new more holistic approach to teaching is required. In a pedagogic context, the performing arts of storytelling, drama and music have faded into the background and are rarely now considered as appropriate techniques for key competence building. However, in the current context, with the low levels of literacy and numeracy within the marginalised adult target group activities like storytelling, drama and music workshops could be considered as effective techniques to help overcome social and cultural barriers and build key competences among the marginalised adult communities.

It is the intention of the ARTSKUL partners to develop the following intellectual outputs to support the reintegration of adults:
1) A tool-kit of embedded learning resources to build basic skills and competences that are based around the different performing arts disciplines. Research conducted by Eurydice highlights the fact that even the briefest learning experience can be of real value for engaging marginalised adults, therefore, a series of new modular resources that can be broken down into small individual lessons will be developed
2) A digital skills training framework that is based on the most popular digital media platforms to support adults to record the storytelling, drama and music 'performances' that emerge as a result of their engagement during the project life-cycle 
3) An in-service training programme for adult educators to enable them to harness the potential of the different performing arts disciplines for building basic skills and key competences and to develop alternative teaching strategies that allow them to work as facilitators of learning within group settings
4) A bespoke online learning environment to support adult educators engaged in the project and to record the learning experiences of the adults engaged

As there is clear evidence that adult education in its current form is not attractive to the most marginalised adults the ARTSKUL project will place a significant emphasis on the design of the proposed learning resources; the presentation of learning opportunities; the scheduling of different learning activities; to try and address the negative disposition of marginalised adults.

2019-1-EE01-KA204-051675.title: New Education With Success
2019-1-EE01-KA204-051675.summary:
<< Background >>

Lifelong learning has become an essential part of the EU´s response to challenges that derive from globalisation, increased competition and the need for sustainable development and social cohesion. According to SA Kutsekoda (Chamber of Certification), there are only 439 adult educators with existing certificates as the adult educator or andragogue, most of the adult educators are older than 50 years. Therefore, it is of utmost importance to find ways to increase the number of adult educators by motivating young people or those new in the adult education field to become adult educators and train them in topics like media, critical thinking and languages. Supporting the employment of young people and ensuring their social and economic participation are already key issues on the agenda of all EU countries. Also, as most adult educators are elderly people, they are lacking knowledge and skills in innovative teaching methods, especially in the usage of computers and social media. Adult educators, trainers, etc., their knowledge regarding innovative skills is limited. Critical thinking is not included in any syllabus or curriculum. Media and ICT are taught to younger people, but elderly people are left out and their skills perish.

<< Objectives >>

The objective of the project was to give the possibility to educators and trainers for better and more targeted provisions of services through the use of tools which were implemented under the project. To achieve the above aims the project implemented the following objectives:
Identification of the needs of the existing adult trainers and educators;
Development of an on-line e-Learning Toolkit for the general methodology how to include critical thinking into the syllabus of languages, ICT and media with examples;
Development of an on-line manual for training new educators. The use of specific tools would enable the target group to allocate their time to each one of the people who could be in need of their counselling in a more constructive and effective way, via mobilising internet technologies;
Development and implementation of targeted courses, which enable adult educators to support and improve the skills of new adult educators. The practical training courses give a possibility to get more personal communication between adult educators and possibly new adult educators by also upskilling both target groups' knowledge in topics of media, ICT and languages.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities which were implemented under the project’s life cycle were the following:
Development O1 Survey of Needs in the field of Adult Education;
Development O2 Methodology: General methodology and critical thinking in media education, ICT and foreign language education;
Development O3 Manual for training new educators.
In parallel with the project’s research and development activities and throughout the project implementation period, a set of horizontal activities has been done:
Organisation of 5 face-to-face and 10 online TPMs;
Organisation of two LTTA-s in Croatia and Estonia to test the developed IOs;
Organisation of Multiplier Events in each partner country;
Organisation of Pilot workshops in local institutions;
Development of Project Work Plan;
Development Dissemination Plan, design and development dissemination tools;
Development of Quality Assurance Strategy, Evaluation strategy and Risk Management Plan;
Development of Sustainability and Valorisation Plan;
Design of internal and external communication templates;
Disseminate project outputs and activities at local/regional/national and European levels;
Engage the target group and raise awareness of the project and its value.

<< Results >>

The project includes all the necessary results to be coherent and successfully implemented. Complementing the intellectual outputs, the partners have delivered the following results:
A concrete management plan which has the description of all necessary steps and procedures for the implementation of the project;
Minutes following each TPM have been drafted and delivered by the coordinator;
Quality assurance strategy covers the overall course of the project, to make sure all activities had been undertaken in an effective way, leading to the desired results based on the quality standards agreed upon;
The evaluation reports, with an overview of the qualitative and quantitative objectives reached;
A dissemination strategy, with a description of the dissemination tools and activities necessary to reach the target groups and a final dissemination report;
Participants´ lists from all the local national events, in addition the LTTAs  and project partners´ meetings;
The project website and logo;
Printed materials;
Developed newsletters and their dissemination after important project milestones;
Feedback questionnaires from members of the target groups who have been involved in the local events and training sessions.

2019-1-EL01-KA204-062873.title: Preventing Smoking, Alcohol and Internet addictions among children and adolescents: a family oriented training approach for adult learners and educators
2019-1-EL01-KA204-062873.summary:
<< Background >>

Addiction to smoking, alcohol and internet are a common transnational problem, the extent and determinants of which know no boundaries in Europe. Addictive behaviors are high across the EU, especially among children and adolescents in disadvantaged groups contributing to widening health related inequalities regardless of MS or region. Evidence supporting the importance of prevention concerns all MS, as does the importance of family and school as the most crucial protective factors of addictive behaviors among youth. Children and adolescents are particularly vulnerable to smoking, alcohol and internet addiction, a new understudied phenomenon raising concerns and requiring urgent attention. Internet addiction does not have the same social stigma as other addictions. Nevertheless, there are commonalities between tobacco, alcohol and internet abuse: wide availability, common causes such as childhood initiation, social deprivation and exclusion, poor access to education, problematic family and school environments, mental health effects. Although sharing common causes, adult training addressing these three addictions altogether is yet to be developed.

<< Objectives >>

The ADD-freeTraining project objectives are presented as follows:
1. Develop and evaluate an interactive training curriculum on evidence-based methods for alcohol, smoking and internet addiction prevention, reflecting the needs of adult learners, teachers and educators
2. Increase adult learners’, teachers’ and educators’ awareness and skills on relevant addiction prevention emphasizing the need for active parental involvement, skills in social competence and school-based interventions.
3. Enhance partner capabilities to develop and deliver relevant training.
4. Increase awareness of communities, organizations, and other stakeholders on addictions and the new training.
The project promotes a family-centered approach to prevention, simultaneously addressing the school and wider social context and promoting healthy interaction within the family, school, peers and society. The project aims at targeting the ultimate beneficiaries of the training results, i.e. children and adolescents, by protecting them from addiction-related behaviors which are harmful to their health by upgrading the role of adult learners and other adults involved with youth in appropriately preventing and managing these issues.

<< Implementation >>

The project designed and implements innovative training on the prevention of tobacco,alcohol and internet abuse in children/adolescents.Target groups are adult learners,including but not limited to parents from diverse socioeconomic backgrounds,teachers and adult educators including youth workers,parent association representatives and relevant service providers. In order to ensure high quality,training is based on a review of existing training opportunities and participatory research among target groups to determine knowledge gaps and training needs.The resulting evidence-based training package includes diverse training tools aimed to improve relevant knowledge and skills.Common and specialized modules were developed for all target groups.Training focuses on addiction principles, common underlining causes of alcohol, smoking and internet addiction and prevention strategies focusing on family and school based approaches.It was delivered through face-to-face training and the E-Learning platform.The “Training Adaptation Toolkit” provides guidelines for the best use of the training tools.Multiplier transnational/national events enhance knowledge exchange.Dissemination targets all target groups through various dissemination activities.

<< Results >>

The Intellectual Outputs of the project are presented as follows:
1: Addiction Prevention Ecosystem Mapping and Conceptual Framework
2: Methodological framework for the design of the training curriculum
3: Training Package Development for the Prevention of Addictions in Children and adolescents
4: Interactive Web platform, applications and digital learning tools
5: Training Adaptation Toolkit
Upon completion, increased awareness about knowledge gaps and needs of adult learners in relation to smoking, alcohol and internet addictions has already been achieved. The intention of the consortium is to maximize the impact of the project in the future.The newly developed training increases adult learners’, teachers’ and educators’ competences in regards to prevention of alcohol, smoking and internet addiction. Important issues, such as the need for active parental involvement, skills in social competence and relative school based interventions are promoted, while providing ready-to-use related training. By increasing adult learners’, teachers’ and educators’ skills in addiction prevention, the ADD-freeTraining envisions in the long term to promote the health and the well-being of children and adolescents in Europe.

2019-1-FR01-KA204-063017.title: New skills for harbor heritage story telling
2019-1-FR01-KA204-063017.summary:
<< Background >>

Faisant le constat d'une connaissance et d'une mise en valeur fréquemment insuffisantes du patrimoine des villes portuaires, aussi bien dans les ports traditionnels que dans les ports plus récents à vocation industrielle ou marchande, les partenaires du projet, acteurs des ports de Bastia (FR), Catania (IT), Split (HR) et du Pirée (GR), souhaitaient développer des méthodes et contenus de formation pluridisciplinaire pour permettre à un large public d'adultes de se réapproprier ce patrimoine matériel et immatériel et de contribuer à sa mise en valeur touristique. Le patrimoine visé était autant le patrimoine architectural lié à la spécificité des activités portuaires que le patrimoine matériel et immatériel lié aux multiples fonctions et professions qui s'articulent autour de la vie des ports ainsi qu’aux traditions locales.

Dans ce contexte, Harbour Heritage Story Telling vise à développer les méthodes et compétences nécessaires à l’identification du patrimoine et à sa mise en valeur auprès des visiteurs, afin de promouvoir ces villes portuaires auprès des tours opérateurs, professionnels du tourisme, et des touristes eux-mêmes qui les voient surtout comme un lieu de passage ou un élément de décor pittoresque.

<< Objectives >>

HHST propose une approche touristique durable pour la mise en valeur du patrimoine portuaire, en renforçant les compétences des acteurs professionnels et bénévoles qui contribuent à l’activité portuaire : animateurs territoriaux, entrepreneurs, pêcheurs, commerçants, offices du tourisme et guides, associations de valorisation du patrimoine, riverains… Le renforcement de ces compétences vise principalement à leurs permettre :
•	De s’engager dans un processus participatif d’identification et de mise en valeur du patrimoine (via les Ateliers participatifs du Patrimoine)
•	De développer de nouveaux outils pour la création et l’animation de circuits de tourisme culturel durable
•	D’apporter aux visiteurs une nouvelle expérience Culturelle en mettant en valeur l’attractivité du port

L’objectif est aussi de renforcer la coopération entre acteurs de villes portuaires euro-méditerranéennes pour développer l’attractivité de ces quartiers et accroître la durée des séjours des visiteurs. A plus long terme, ce sont l’économie locale, le lien social et l’engagement citoyen, qui devraient bénéficier de ces nouvelles compétences.

<< Implementation >>

Les partenaires ont mené de nombreuses démarches participatives impliquant des adultes de divers secteurs (tourisme, commerce, pêche, animation du territoire, culture) :
-	Phase de recherche et concertation avec les acteurs locaux pour lancer un diagnostic partagé 
-	Ateliers Participatifs du Patrimoine autour de l’identification du patrimoine à valoriser et de la co-construction de Circuits de découverte
-	Visites guidées pilotes sur les circuits de découvertes 

Sur cette base et à partir de leur expertise, ils ont développé un ensemble cohérent d’outils pédagogiques pour le développement de nouvelles compétences. 

Les résultats de la démarche participative ont été synthétisés par les partenaires et consignés dans le Catalogue HHST, illustrant la mise en œuvre de ces compétences. 

Le site internet et la plateforme de formation en ligne conçues par les partenaires, a mis ces produits en accès libre pour l’ensemble des publics cibles, et en 5 langues. 

Une formation transnationale de 20 adultes a permis de former autant de personnes relais du projet sur les ville-portuaires impliquées et au-delà. 

Un travail de dissémination de la démarche HHST, ses productions et ses résultats sur le terrain, a eu lieu tout au long du projet.

<< Results >>

Le projet HHST a permis de développer :
-	Un Guide méthodologique qui pause le cadre de la démarche HHST et introduit les concepts clés
-	Un Cadre de compétences qui identifie les compétences nécessaires pour la mise en place de nouveaux processus d'appropriation du patrimoine des ports et sa mise en valeur touristique et sert de référence pour les formateurs.
-	Un programme de formation, disponible en ligne sur le MOOC du projet, composé d’éléments théoriques, d’activités et d'outils pédagogiques et d'interviews, et proposant 2 cours pour les 2 publics du projet.
-	5 itinéraires de découverte des ports, fondés sur la démarche HHST 
-	Un Catalogue reprenant l’ensemble des démarches développées et les Itinéraires de découvertes des 4 ports
-	La formation de 20 guides et acteurs du tourisme aux outils HHST 
-	L’implication d’environ 900 représentants des secteurs de la formation, culturel, touristique et du développement local des villes portuaires du projets à travers les Ateliers Participatifs du Patrimoine, les visites de terrains, les événements multiplicateurs.

L’ensemble de ces productions sont accessibles à tous via le site internet du projet (http://harbor-heritage.eu/en/home-2/) en anglais et dans les 4 langues du projet.

2019-1-FR01-KA204-063126.title: ECHO-Tourism
2019-1-FR01-KA204-063126.summary:
<< Background >>

The impact of tourism on the environment is significant and its impacts are visible : from the massive overbuilding of the banks, the overconsumption of natural and energy resources, to the overproduction of waste and GHG emissions, the list seems endless. However, and as in many matters, this situation is not inevitable: there are many avenues for improvement, including eco-friendly actions, applicable to tourism.

Responsible tourism approaches are developing in the territories to meet growing demand from tourists. The opening of markets and the attraction provided by these development prospects on sufficiency should make it possible to finance the system at the end of the three years of completion of the project, which is currently the case in France for sobriety actions in other sectors. of activity (particularly in the business world).

This project co-funded by the European Commission as part of the Erasmus + program, has above all an educational scope, as the key of these three years of collaborative work is the creation of a training platform for those who wish to deepen their knowledge in ecological practices : from tourism professionals to the tourists themselves.

<< Objectives >>

The general objective of ECHO-Tourism is to reduce the ecological impact of tourism in an entertaining and engaging way.
The resulting sub-objectives are:
• that tourism professionals and tourists apply eco-gestures in their daily life
• that learning takes place through interaction and constructive exchanges between professionals and tourists
• that tourists bring back home their new “awareness and green behaviour”.
By raising awareness on behaviour change and by involving multiple territories across Europe, ECHO-TOURISM sparkles the initiation of a new way of enjoying the treasures that our planet can offer, and more importantly, brings it to the next level and spread it across many territories through a comprehensive and playful  training program. Completing this program brings new skills to tourism professionals as well as shapes a new dynamic, bringing the opportunity to start new activities, and to enhance their attractivity to the public. This objective is reinforced by the fact that eco-friendly behaviour decreases the energetic bills which allow more funds to be invested in new developments.

<< Implementation >>

The original idea of ​​this project stems from a desire to propagate sobriety practices to limit the ecological footprint linked to tourist activities, by allowing the spin-off in 4 countries, of an adaptable and reproducible model of training that can be easily disseminated and multiplied. To reach its vision the consortium of partners conceived several playful tools, which, combined with its original vision will aim the most efficient training of adults, being tourism professionals or individuals. 
- A website to familiarize yourself with the project and the actions of the actors/partners.
- A platform for monitoring water, food, waste, mobility and electricity consumption that can be used in the professional or domestic context.
- A guide to eco-gestures explaining to participants the daily habits to put into practice to limit their impact on one or all of the topics covered.
- A MOOC (free online course) to train adults in the practice of eco-gestures.
- A methodological guide to enable local actors to implement and reproduce the system independently, in their territories.
- A set of training courses to learn how to use these tools and dissemination events to make them known.

<< Results >>

The ECHO-tourism project aims to ensure that a growing number of tourism stakeholders can appropriate the tools. Concretely, the results and impacts sought are concurrently:
- A global rise of competency (in terms of methodological, technical and contextual analysis) for the participants wishing to engage in the promotion of this type of approach;
- The spin-off of the training process to reduce disparities in access to training in the territories;
- The good coordination of the project and the effectiveness of the dissemination events: the objective is to ensure the quality as well as the sustainability of the actions and tools, after the period of ERASMUS + financing.
Possibilities opened by our productions are the following:
• To be able to learn and put into practice at home and according to your possibilities a whole range of eco gestures, easily adaptable to your structure.
• Be accompanied in the implementation of a responsible approach to sufficiency.
• Communicate with a wider audience on the eco-responsible approach implemented or supported by your structure.
• Integrate a network of local actors promoting exchanges with new partners, or service providers with common values.

2019-1-HR01-KA204-060781.title: Virtual Reality for Language Learning
2019-1-HR01-KA204-060781.summary:
<< Background >>

The demands of the informational age society are growing with the rapid technological advancements and set forth new expectations from lifelong learning programs. There is an increasing
need for changing and innovating teaching methods and for introducing and using ICT in teaching and the entire educational process. At the same time, the amount of new information available to teachers and learners is increasing on a daily basis. This sets forth a new approach to the educational process, both for teachers and staff as well as students, focusing a lot more on independent research, student-centered studies, efficient use of multiple resources and tools. Therefore, the importance of digital literacy emerges as a new key competence to support both learning and teaching models.
We set fort to develop new and innovative language teaching tool which would contribute to:
- increase motivation, focus and cognitive skills, develop critical and creative thinking and communicative competences of learners
- increase teaching and IT skills and competences of language teachers as adult education providers
- internationalization of lifelong learning and promoting cooperation between education providers on EU level

<< Objectives >>

In the most direct terms - we wanted to introduce Virtual Reality as an innovative IT tool into adult education, specifically the language learning sector.
The reasoning for developing VR as an important language learning tool was explained in the original grant proposal. During the project implementation and as a result of transnational collaboration, training and acquisition of new skills and knowledges by project teams, inclusion of associated partners through dissemination, implementation of impact activities and other, we discovered that VR had even greater teaching potential than what we originally proposed. In summary, VR in language learning provides opportunities for:
- learning languages in fully immersive way, providing unique opportunities to all students and thus aiding towards inclusive education
- applying traditional language learning methodologies such as TPR in a new and innovative way
- increasing communicative and problem-solving skills in students, task-based learning
- new teaching tool suited for students with a number of learning difficulties (as demonstrated by an external expert in dyslexia during the project implementation period)
We believe this aim was reached in full.

<< Implementation >>

Development activities:
- developed four Virtual Worlds, plus an additional introductory Virtual World
- developed total of nine Virtual Tasks (eight planned plus one additional, to add an environmental sustainability component to the project)
- developed Teachers' Manual
PMI activities:
- organized six transnational project meetings (one of which was online, due to covid-19 travel restrictions)
- organized two transnational training events (one live, one online)
- organized five multiplier events (one large final conference and three smaller national events)
Supporting activities:
- conducted 274 dissemination activities to promote project and its results to all relevant stakeholders (backed by a detailed dissemination report)
- created project website, Facebook page, logo and six newsletters
- conducted a major piloting event, involving project and associated partners, and a number of other impact assessment activities (backed by a detailed impact report)
- conducted a number of quality management activities
- conducted a number of smaller meetings and training events aimed at introducing different project management tools and procedures, project monitoring and strengthening EU component through transnational collaboration

<< Results >>

1. VIRTUAL WORLDS
We developed four Virtual Worlds as architectural interface where VR learning takes place. They are a technological prerequisite for creating learning content and provide an environment in which students are immersed. The four worlds we created are:
- an international space station
- a deserted tropical island
- ancient Roman town
- a frozen world
Content was chosen based on future consideration to learning content, allowing us to implement tasks that incorporate scientific, cultural, historic and environmental content, but are also interesting and appealing to students. One additional (fifth) smaller world was created to serve as main menu and training environment.
2. VIRTUAL TASKS
These escape-room type tasks are located inside virtual worlds and facilitate task-based learning, problem-solving, creative thinking and communication. We created total of eight distinct tasks (2 per world) plus one additional (ninth) task with a purely creative aspect (to facilitate additional learning styles).
3. TEACHERS' NOTES
A 185-page complete manual for teacher with detailed instructions on how to implement VR4LL in their classrooms, with ready-to-use lesson plans for English (plus some additional in Italian and German).

2019-1-HR01-KA204-060785.title: Financial Literacy for Woman in the NEET system
2019-1-HR01-KA204-060785.summary:
Financial literacy is globally acknowledged as an important element of economic and financial stability and development. There is mounting evidence that those with higher financial literacy can better manage with their money, participate in the stock market and perform better on their portfolio choice, and that they are more likely to choose mutual funds with lower fees. The need for financial education must be addressed to a group of woman that are marginalized, have low-income or are neither in employment nor in education. (NEET) Women who are not financially literate can't be as productive as they could be and are not only harming themselves but also the whole community, so they need a proper education. Partner in this project will develop the curriculum with appropriate, friendly oriented and easy to use digital learning games for NEET women. These resources on the topic of financial literacy will be developed through 4 core competences: money and transactions, planning and managing finances, risk and reward and financial landscape. Each of the selected areas will be developed through 6 mini learning format resources (24 in total). For adult educators, the training programme will be developed to support them in using new resources, to support the delivery of new developed curriculum and also to develop key skills to enable them to work in this new digital environment in the future.  Two adult educators from each partner institution (12 in total) will be participating the teacher training programme to gain and adopt all necessary skills to carry out the piloting of the developed curriculum on the topic of financial literacy to NEET women (75 women engaged in total - 15 from each partner country). An e-learning portal will also be developed to link all developed materials and resources and to support the adult educators during and after completing the training programme; a social networking space where the new trained educators and NEET women can gather and support each other, share advice and offer support.
When all developed financial literacy resources and the e-learning portal will be tested and established and ready to present, the multiplier events will be organized in each partner country where a minimum of 60 persons will  be participating: a minimum of 30 NEET women will attend these events to engage with the resources developed, a minimum of 30 people who are teachers, trainers, and other adult education providers, school managers, representatives of local and regional institutions, stakeholders and government bodies responsible for developing the adult education system, adult educators who complete the training programme will also attend this event to introduce the new resources for the new, modern, dynamic and interactive learning. Main aims of the project for NEET women are to improve understanding of financial concepts and products, build financial skills and competences to be more aware of financial landscapes, to strengthen their confidence and self-esteem in their financial skills to equally participate in modern society.
Main aims of educators are to increase and strengthen self-esteem in carrying out developed curriculum for financial literacy education, to increase digital competence and raise awareness of financial literacy needs.
It is expected that more than 400 people engaged in the project and are familiar with the developed materials and known with the designed new e-learning platform. The expected impact on participating organizations: they will have more efficient and trained teacher staff open to new challenges. The partner organizations will be more prepared for the innovator role and lead innovation in adult education in their town and region. 
All project partners are members of different networks, committees, management groups, representative bodies at regional, national and international levels and enjoy regular contact and interaction with other professionals working in similar circumstances or roles. For the project to have a strong impact at all levels, partners will be the main carriers in presenting and promoting of project concept and outcomes as they emerge.
Project partners will focus the attention of their dissemination efforts at national and international representative bodies like teacher training networks, teacher trade unions, education associations, employment agencies. Building the skills and competences necessary for financial literacy and digital awareness is now a challenge that will remain at the center of education and training for the future. The documents, tools, and resources developed by FLOW project will remain relevant for adult education professionals working with NEET women beyond the project life-cycle and the dynamic media content produced will be appropriate for use for a least another 5 years.

2019-1-HR01-KA204-060794.title: Raising the skills of adults on the margins of lifelong learning
2019-1-HR01-KA204-060794.summary:
As Europe recovers slowly from the effects of the economic crisis there are some key benchmarks that were set as part of the EU2020 strategy that remain outside of the reach for most EU Member States on an individual and throughout the EU on a collective basis. One such target is the 15% adult participation rate in lifelong learning. With current rates of Romania 1.1%; Croatia 2.3%; Poland 3.7%; Cyprus 6.9%; Ireland 8.9%; Portugal 9.8%; none of the countries participating in this project have reached or exceeded the benchmark set.

Engaging marginalised adults in education and training can be a thankless task for educators equipped with no more than the basic pedagogic instruments and approaches. What is needed to attract reluctant learners back to education and training is a comprehensive new approach that ignores the traditional institution based provision focused on subjects and instead pursues a more open and expansive provision based on embedded learning techniques and 'open-house' community learning festivals. Rewarding even the smallest learning achievement is essential to encourage those re-engaged to continue their educational journey.

The ELEVATION project proposes to develop a comprehensive and bespoke new learning framework to attract those furthest from the mainstream back into education and training. The project will develop the following intellectual outputs to help achieve its objectives:
IO1 - A suite of 24 thematic mini-learning format resources for key competence acquisition that embed learning in artistic disciplines; cultural disciplines; digital and social media; sport and hobbies.
IO2 - An in-service training programme and handbook to support adult and community educators to harness the full potential of the bespoke embedded learning resources provided
IO3 - A community learning festival planning handbook that contains all the necessary plans and resources to organise a community learning festival
IO4 - A bespoke e-learning portal to ensure that marginalised adults have access to all learning resources provided on a range of fixed and mobile devices

It is clear from the latest participation figures that current approaches need to be further expanded into non-formal and informal learning areas if the required participation rates are to be achieved. During the lifetime of the ELEVATION project over 600 marginalised adults will be re-engaged in lifelong learning and started back on a learning pathway to inclusion and personal fulfillment.

2019-1-HR01-KA204-060807.title: New Chance for Us
2019-1-HR01-KA204-060807.summary:
<< Background >>

After implementing the Give them a Chance project with our partners from Slovenia and Hungary, we came to the conclusion that it was necessary to further strengthen the capacities of Roma students in adult education as well as competencies and motivation of andragogical workers working with them. We applied the project having in mind that a big problem in the Roma national minority community is the lack of motivation to enroll in adult education programs, early withdrawal from the program, very low level of language, mathematical, and digital competencies among adult students of the Roma national minority. We wanted to achieve greater levels of motivation of lecturers working in partner countries in adult education. Most lecturers working with the adult Roma population in adult education have prejudices against working with the target group because they do not know their customs, culture, language and how it is to live in Roma settlements, which are often ghettoized in all three partner countries. In order to overcome potential obstacles, we formed a partnership between andragogical institutions and Roma associations, and by doing so we connected the needs of members of the Roma national minority and adult education institutions.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we wanted to encourage the inclusion of adult Roma in formal and informal adult programs and reduce the rates of dropping out among members of the Roma national minority. Furthermore, we wanted to motivate them on the importance of education as the key factor in preventing the risk of poverty, and to increase inclusion in adult education programs. We also wanted to motivate andragogical workers to be more ready to work with members of the Roma national minority in the three partner countries. In order to easily identify the causes of dropping out and the lack of interest to be included in educational programs, Roma associations participated, mostly by conducting motivational workshops for students, lecturers and in creating social activation programs, and pointed out the specific problems facing the Roma population encounters in everyday life and the possibility of solving them in order to facilitate the functioning in the society. We encountered many obstacles in the project implementation, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic, where the Roma population did not have access to education due to their poor social status and inability to use IT equipment.

<< Implementation >>

In November of 2019, we organized a kick-off conference where we, together with our partners, presented the project to the local community. We created a Facebook page (https://www.facebook.com/NewChanceforUS) and a web page (https://nec4us.pou-cakovec.hr/) where we regularly informed the public on project activities. Additionally, we promoted the project in the media. We organized multiplicative events in each of three partner countries. We conducted workshops in all three countries for IO1, IO2, and IO3, had two partner meetings face-to-face (Croatia and North Macedonia), two ZOOM meetings, LTT training for lecturers in North Macedonia and a final conference in Croatia.

<< Results >>

Produced outputs:
IO1 – Plan and program of motivational workshops for social activation for lecturers in adult Roma education implemented in all partner countries
IO2 – Plan and program of motivational workshops for social activation for participants and program for social activation created and implemented in all partner countries
IO3 – Plan and program for social activation created and implemented in all partner countries
A web site was created – https://nec4us.pou-cakovec.hr/
A Facebook page was created – https://www.facebook.com/NewChanceforUS
A Facebook platform Murasmus + was created – https://www.facebook.com/murasmus01
as a dissemination platform for all Erasmus + and ESF projects implemented by partner organisations as beneficiaries or partners, and other activities related to adult education, especially related to Roma issues.

2019-1-HR01-KA204-060833.title: Educational theatre as the place of raising inclusion and employability of people with disability - Expander
2019-1-HR01-KA204-060833.summary:
<< Background >>

Educathe+ Expander (E+EX) builds on successful Grundtvig workshop Educathe (2013) and Educathe+ KA2 Strategic Partnership (2015-2017) - and expands on them geographically and in practice. As such, E+EX is a continuation of a long-term commitment to respond to the needs of people with disabilities (PWD), as presented in the "European Disability Strategy 2010-2020: A Renewed Commitment to a Barrier-Free Europe", and to those working with and for PWD. Namely, E+EX contributes by helping remove social and labour market barriers for PWD and those who work with this population by empowering them, producing educational opportunities, raising their employability skills and EU competences (English language, civic and social skills, cultural awareness), and ensuring public recognition of their skills through public performances.

<< Objectives >>

With consideration to the target groups and their needs and with expertise of the partners in mind, we have set three tangible objectives by which to address the needs of all sides.
- PWDs: raising self-esteem and self-awareness through non-formal education
- EDUCATORS: enriching through sharing and networking, while extending their knowledge of working for and with PWDs by combining educational theatre practices
- EMPLOYERS & PUBLIC: raising visibility and raise awareness of the capabilities and employability of PWD

By reaching these objectives, we contribute to some of the main goals of Erasmus+ in adult education (Extending and developing competences of educators), and in horizontal goals of Social inclusion and supporting educators. We believe our work should be public and we reach the public through public performances held at the end of our educational activities with an aim of reaching audience outside of our partnership and sharing with them a message of inclusion and ability of PWD. Stemming from the “Nothing about us without us” motto of all marginalised group, these performances ensure creativity of PWD is acknowledged and put in focus.

<< Implementation >>

E+EX was implemented during an extremely difficult time of COVID-19 lockdown, earthquakes in Croatia, economic crisis, inflation, energy crisis and war in Ukraine. For those reasons, it was extended for a year. Even so, partner managed to organise all planned activities that consisted mostly out of its visible activities:
-	Learning, teaching, and training workshops where partner organisations shared their knowledge of educational theatre
-	Transnational project meetings for project managers
-	Publications of e-Manuals, e-Videos, and public performances – educational and promotional activities
-	Promotional and dissemination activities via all available channels (webpage, social media, EPALE, SALTO-YOUTH, VALOR)
Besides visible activities, partners implemented many “invisible” activities in support of the “visible” activities” – administration, accountancy, advocacy, monitoring, reporting, planning, and continuous communication during a 32 month long implementation.

<< Results >>

E+EX partnership managed to produce: 
-	5 Learning, teaching, and training workshops for educational theatre, each held by a different partner organisation
-	sharing platform for educational theatre knowledge between 5 partner organisations
-	58 international mobilities (1/3 educators, 1/3 assistants, and 1/3 people with disabilities), who were joined by local participants – members of marginalised groups, that make up 86 participants in total who experienced educational theatre and raised their Key competences, and employability skills (soft-skills)
-	5 eManuals
-	5 e-videos
-	5 public performances recorded and published
-	E+EX webpage with basic info, chronology of the project, and all of its outputs
-	Sharing platform where partners share educational and administrative documents
-	5 photo albums sharing the atmosphere from E+EX events
All educational and promotional materials were published on our webpage, social media, EPALE, SALTO-YOUTH, and VALOR and are free and available for everyone interested.

2019-1-HR01-KA204-060923.title: Connecting Circles: The Living Waters of our Rivers
2019-1-HR01-KA204-060923.summary:
<< Background >>

The project addressed social cohesion through preservation of cultural heritage by using it in an innovative way to provide learning, therapeutic assistance and empowerment to a wide array of audiences, including disadvantaged groups. Counselling through storytelling is both an ancient activity and an emerging conceptual model, but oral narrative strategies have rarely been applied in the positive psychology domain. Traditional folk and fairy tales are concerned with concepts that are now scientifically investigated, such as resilience, self-realization, personal growth and meaning in life. This project applied a new narrative approach based on traditional fairy tales, myths and folktales related to rivers for the purpose of promoting psychological well-being and growth. The stories of the rivers and waters can foster the process of transformation, especially for marginalized groups of people who feel disconnected from their communities. Empowerment and healing represents a starting point of their reintegration into society.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to create and promote innovative model of learning and providing assistance, empowerment and therapy to disadvantaged groups through the use of mythology, storytelling, culture and art connected to the rivers.
Specific goals were:
1. To collect and preserve mythological and folk tales, fairy tales and local stories as they relate to rivers and disseminate them widely.
2. To create and disseminate knowledge and innovative tools of using stories and mythology in working with disadvantaged groups to adult learners from the helping professions.
3. To support, participate in and strengthen the European cultural heritage.

<< Implementation >>

Project activities were comprised of project management and implementation (including dissemination activities and channels), development of three intellectual outputs and organisation of six events (two transnational project meetings, one LTTE and three multiplier events). The three intellectual outputs - the collection of traditional folktales from the three project countries; the educational model, frame and curriculum and the Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) were central insofar that organisation of LTTE and multiplier events depended on the timeline of these. Due to COVID-19 pandemic and the epidemiological restrictions, social distancing requirements and travel ban, all events except the kick-off meeting had to be postponed and the project requested and was granted a 12-month extension.

<< Results >>

The project developed three intellectual outputs:
- A Collection of Tales from the Rivers - 15 traditional folktales, five from each country, translated into English and published on the project website at http://connectingcircles.eu/a-collection-of-tales-from-the-rivers/.
- Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) Curriculum and Frame & Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) Content
The course can be accessed at https://www.udemy.com/share/107p1O3@-ZbbUkWzX6OO8cL21ugVacaPPTCpJLZyoOJbn8w89i4s2i9J1qCjekay9KfVMKyKNQ==/ (in English) and https://www.udemy.com/share/107nG43@nWFb4pj7x3MRldy14sva7SaUpjr4gxaWS5ukxnmDeOTzQoJ8rLAN1ClrIn6YHy05HQ==/ in Croatian/Serbian.

The project also organized two transnational project meetings (the kick-off meeting in Croatia and the project partners' meeting in Italy), one LTTE meeting in Serbia and three multiplier events (one in each country).

Dedicated dissemination channels: 
- project web site http://connectingcircles.eu
- project Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/connectingcircles.eu

2019-1-HR01-KA204-060964.title: Education and Support for Positive Parenting
2019-1-HR01-KA204-060964.summary:
<< Background >>

Feedback from participants and users in our previous Erasmus+ project and our regular activities have shown high parents’ interest and needs for an early parenting support system, encouraging us to continue with developed activities in area of pregnancy and childbirth, and to develop support for improving parenting skills and knowledge about responsible, evidence-based, positive and non-violent parenting methods.

This project successfully addressed the needs of parents of the youngest children, creating a framework for training trainers for in-person support and education in all partner countries, training a team of parent-support trainers, but also developed innovative digital tools that are available on-demand and address the needs of parents as their child grows. Reaching parents during pregnancy and in the first three years of their child's life is essential because this is the itme they are forming their parenting style and most open to information. Empowering parents to adopt a positive parenting style and abandon authoritarian, fear-based parenting early on, has an enormous potential to affect these parents but also their children.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of this project were to:

1) Develop innovations in adult education for future and new parents (postpartum and parenting curricula, mobile apps)
2) Disseminate and exploit new and existing innovative information through the education and training of new trainers for volunteers who lead parenting education and support workshops
3) Create a new digital tools(mobile app) for parents and update an existing one
4) Transfer knowledge and practice, joing learning, empowerment and coopeartion, especially in the field of adult education, to the partner organisations.

<< Implementation >>

Activities in Objectve 1
1.1 Create an innovative, evidence-based curriculum on postpartum for training educators on postaprtum support, produced in 6 languages (O1)
1.2 Create an innovative, evidence-based curriculum on parenting challenges for parents of children children 0-3 for training educators on postaprtum support, produced in 6 languages (O2)

Activities in Objective 2
2.1 Train trainers from 4 countires to provide childbirth preparation education to parents in their counties (C1) 
2.2 Train trainers from 4 countries who can train colleagues in their own countries to run postpartum support workshops for parents (O1/C3)
2.3 Train trainers from 4 countries who can train colleagues in their own countries to run parenting support workshops for parents (O2/C5)

Activities in Objective 3
3.1 Create a new mobile app with comprehensive information for parents 0-3, called Growing (O3) translated into 6 languages
3.2 Update the existing mobile app for expectant parents Expecting to include two more languages and technical updates (O4)

Activities in Objective 4
4.1 Experts in each organisation increase their competencies and skills for curriculum development, adult education delivery, project development and implementation

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results of the project are:

O1 - comprehensive curriculum for postpartum workshop leaders (6 languages, adapted for needs of each country as needed), developed and piloted
O2 - comprehensive curriculum for parents of children 0-3 workshop leaders (6 languages, adapted for needs of each country as needed), developed and piloted

in C3 and C5, we piloted O1 and O2 with a cohort of educators who have the skills to deliver trainings for future trainers and run workshops for parents of children 0-3 in the future.

O3 - new mobile app for parents of children 0-3 years old with week by week (later biweekly) information on parenting, child's growth and milestones, family dynamics, nutrition, challenges, available for iOS and Android in 6 languages (GrowingApp - available at www.growingapp.eu)
O4 - updated mobile app for expectant parents, Expecting, with new articles, two new langauges (Hungarian and Spanish), and technical updates needed to keep it running smoothly.

2019-1-HU01-KA204-061083.title: WiseFarmer: Connecting farm generations in the digital age
2019-1-HU01-KA204-061083.summary:
Smallholder and family farms dominate EU' s agriculture, as two-thirds of the 10 million farms are less than 5 ha. This proportion is going to be even higher if we take into account the accessing countries of South-East Europe. Nearly one-third of all active farmers in the EU are over 65, while only 5.6% are under 35 years of age. This phenomenon is described as the “greying of Europe’s farmers”. Smallholders' local knowledge, experience, tradition, attitude, mindset can be tremendous resource and obstacle at the same time.  

The "wise farming" concept is introduced and used by the project, and can be conceived in two dimensions:  1) the value of local experience in farming in general: a personal behavior where “The wise farmer learns from the experience of others” and as opposed to “The smart person who uses his mind and intelligence, the wise uses his experience and experiences of others to solve problems”, and  2) thinking one step further the well-known term of "Smart Farming" (re. digital agriculture) to "Wise Farming", where the introduction of agriculture 4.0 tools are to be put into local context, to match experience, attitude, cultural habits, to validate usefulness not only at the level of business return but also taking care of social, environmental, sustainability and data ownership aspects.

The direct objective of the proposal is to bring together the younger and elder farm generations in a common programme for the exchange of knowledge, access to high quality learning opportunity, facilitation support and sustained collaboration for increased competence, from one side in the use of digital tools, from the other side the crucial farming practices based on local knowledge.

The target group consists of smallholders and family farmers, where personal participation in farming is inevitable, the current level of skills and qualifications are generally low, both on the elder side -  lacking digital skills, and the younger farmers - missing key competencies in the practice of farming.  Elderly farmers have local knowledge that is indispensable in the successful entrepreneurship at the farm level, while younger farmers are more advanced in the use of digital devices, but also lack their specific use in farming, as gaining local (“slow”) knowledge takes a considerable amount of time. 

Peer-to-peer learning - as farmers main and most trusted source of information are other farmers - and knowledge co-creation can give the generations an opportunity to learn in pairs, and circumvent existing obstacles by mentoring each other, therefore the skills of using digital tools can be successfully transferred in the local context as they are connected and matched with local farmer knowledge. 

Besides piloting the learning process itself, the project will develop and execute all supporting materials: 
- Conducting a comprehensive, regional needs analysis and knowledge assessment in every participating country, and developing a matchmaking methodology for the selection process of mentor pairs.
- Creating an online collaboration platform with learning content elements, proven good practices and new digital tools (relevant for the region) and with communication features that enable constant share of ideas and knowledge.

The skills of using digital tools can only be successfully transferred in the local context, at the specific farm level, and it should be matched with local farmer knowledge. Given the importance of the local characteristics, starting from the exploration of needs, developing and conducting the training and continuing with sustained support, the collaborative - mentoring and facilitating - component of the overall process is crucial to glue all the necessary actions together.  Therefore, the project will involve facilitators who are already in the field, working for many years supporting farmers, being trusted, experienced, competent and neutral from business interests. They are primarily professionals accredited and working under the national farm extension services, in accordance with the EU Farm Advisory Service network. In this way, the project will have a positive impact on agricultural knowledge systems as making better use of networks for informal knowledge exchange.

Project results will demonstrate the viability of the approach and methodology, as one of the possible techniques to overcome crucial challenges in the agricultural and rural sectors. The experience can be utilised in a wider strategic context for policymaking, to cope with the abandonment of farming activity especially by young people, the succession of farming, attracting new entrants into agricultural activities, the introduction of digital innovations in a responsible and effective way, suitable for smallholders' and family farmers' needs.

2019-1-HU01-KA204-061167.title: STEMS - Supporting Teachers and Staff in Motivating Adult Learners
2019-1-HU01-KA204-061167.summary:
In order to improve the current insufficient participation of adults in learning in partner countries and across Europe, we need to provide high-quality education opportunities and identify main barriers that hinder participation and persistence of adults in learning. The aim of the project is to address problems and difficulties and respond to the needs of adult education providers and adult learners. 

The project aim is to contribute to:
- increasing adult participation in learning
- adult learners' demands for quality education provision that offers necessary support and takes into account learner needs
- adult education providers' needs for teachers and staff equipped with necessary competences, strategies, and tools for motivating and engaging adult learners as well as maintaining their persistence in learning

The partners are proposing to develop the following intellectual outputs in order to accomplish the set project aims.

IO1 How to Motivate and Engage Adult Learners: A Training Programme for Adult Education Staff and Teachers 
A training programme aimed at increasing motivation competences of teachers and staff in adult education. 

IO2 Open Source Online Platform for Adult Education Staff and Teachers 
An online platform featuring activities and tools in English and partner languages aimed at supporting adult education staff and teachers participating in the training programme. 

IO3 Information Guide for Policy Makers
Guidelines for policy makers responsible for adult education regarding the deployment of professional staff and educators about the importance of their motivation and on how to develop a vision about the importance of adult education in relation to their responsibility for quality assurance and role in the labour market.


The project plans to increase the target groups' quality of interaction with adult learners due to increased communication, and motivation competences, better cooperation, and communication through ICT tools. Thanks to the online platform, the target groups will also improve their access and use of online collections of digital training material and they will need less time to select motivation messages and instruments.

The piloting of the IO1 will be based on practical and interactive training approach and tools in order to ensure that the target group will have the opportunity to apply marketing tools and methods contextualized in their role. The desired result is to have more competent and professional AE staff that can progress beyond their traditional approach to and culture of education.

The project will also have positive results for the participating organisations since project partners will improve their in-person and digital training approaches, strengthen their cooperation with the relevant AE institutions in their regions and countries as well as relevant stakeholders in other countries, contributing to their internationalisation.

2019-1-HU01-KA204-061190.title: Integr-Action Through ETS
2019-1-HU01-KA204-061190.summary:
<< Background >>

The project sets itself to address the educational exclusion of adults with disability in partner countries and in Europe, with its corollary of skills mismatches, exclusion from participation and massive unemployment.
Disabled adults are disproportionally represented among the excluded from education and the labour market, as highlighted by Eurostat data. The findings indicate that adults with disability face lower educational attainment and higher unemployment than their peers not affected by disability, while at the same time participating to a lower degree in formal ad non formal leaning.
Access from education and training, either in both the formal and non-formal sectors, is also more challenging for disabled adults as compared with their peers. Adults with disabilities face higher rates of early leaving from education and lower participation in lifelong learning than the average population, which translates into a mismatch in the acquisition of basic skills, transversal skills and attitudes necessary forfurther education, employability and comcrete participation at all the levels of society.

<< Objectives >>

In their joint work, the project partners aimed to achieve the following three sub-objectives:
1. Social inclusion.
IATETS has used the methodology of education through sport as an opportunity for the full inclusion of adults with disabilities, offering an effective approach to address the social exclusion of people with disabilities from the labour market, education and participation.
2. Improving and expanding the provision of high quality learning opportunities adapted to the needs of people with disabilities was also a key objective of the partners and was pursued.
The IATETS has used the inclusive potential of ETS as an opportunity to improve the skills of adults with disabilities, and re-motivate their participation in the education cycle. 
3. Expand and develop teachers' competences.
In order to help achieve this objective, a specific manual has been produced to provide guidance and methodology to the different actors involved (NGOs, adult education institutions, sports clubs/associations) on how to implement self-training programmes for adults with disabilities through ETS and thus
improving the quality and diversity of their educational offer in this area.

<< Implementation >>

Conducted research, integrated into reports, outlining the educational needs and barriers of people with disabilities, comparing barriers to adult participation in and through sport with existing educational provision.
The research enabled the assessment of existing needs and thus the formulation of policy insights to enhance the participation of adults with disabilities in sport for stakeholders and policy makers at different levels.

2019-1-HU01-KA204-061245.title: CommonPoint - Innovative approaches to training mental health service providers for the quality support of LGBTQI people
2019-1-HU01-KA204-061245.summary:
<< Background >>

Common Point is a strategic partnership project initiated by four NGOs from Europe working with sexual and gender minorities (LGBTQI+ people). Public and private mental health professional services need specific training materials that recognize the realities of LGBTQI people. Throughout formal education, mental health professionals lack opportunities to gain knowledge and skills for supporting LGBTQI+ people effectively. Some dedicated professors might include the topic in specific courses, still, a significant gap remains between the amount of knowledge and practical skills possibly learned at universities and the real needs of LGBTQI+ people seeking support. Nevertheless, practitioners also lack the opportunity to work on their attitudes toward sexuality, and sexual and gender minorities, which is crucial to providing quality support for affected populations. By implementing this project, we aimed to tackle this gap with non-formal educational methods as well as raise awareness of the importance of specific knowledge, skills and attitudes that professionals must acquire to provide quality support for LGBTQI+ people.

<< Objectives >>

We had five particular objectives during the planning, implementation and follow-up of this project. 

1) Improving social inclusion of LGBTQI+ people by increasing the number of mental health service providers tailored to the needs of LGBTQI+ people;
2) increasing knowledge, skills and cultural competencies of mental health professionals in four specific target groups (school counsellors, crisis hotline operators, social workers, clinical psychologists);
3) developing a manual based on best practices and current models for mental health professionals who train students and other professionals;
4) developing innovative online tools and methods for training mental health professionals directly;
5) sharing best practices among LGBTQI+ organizations active in the field of mental health.

<< Implementation >>

To reach our objectives, we implemented three transnational project meetings, two training activities, four multiplying events and several dissemination activities. Transnational project meetings were aimed at planning and evaluating our work together. The kick-off meeting aimed to set common ground together and get to know each other for smooth cooperation. At the mid-term evaluation meeting, we assessed the outcomes reached so far, as well as focused on the cooperation's strengths and weaknesses to exploit our further opportunities. The final evaluation meeting was organized to reflect our work together, finalise our workflows and set sustainability measures. Training activities were carried out to pilot test activities of the intellectual outcomes, as well as to train professionals who are ready to use the Handbook for trainers. Each partner organization organized a multiplying event to involve more and more local professionals and practitioners to disseminate intellectual outputs further.

<< Results >>

Two main intellectual outputs were created through our cooperation. The Common Point Handbook for Trainers guides trainers who would like to implement training for mental health professionals to improve the professionals' attitudes, knowledge and skills related to LGBTQI+ persons. The Common Point E-learning provides a thematic self-education process to mental health professionals. Both of them consist of two main parts. LGBTQI+ 101 part consists of 6 chapters/lessons that provide an introduction to the most important LGBTQI+ topics: Terminology; Transgender, sex-diverse and gender-diverse persons; Coming out; Human rights and the systems of oppression; Mental health risk and minority stress; Personal and professional prejudices. The Field-specific guides for training mental health professionals have 4 main focuses based on the knowledge needs of the specific areas: hotline and chat operators; school counsellors; clinical psychologists; social workers. These parts contain relevant theories, videos, good practices and exercises that help professionals to implement more inclusive practices.
