2019-1-IE01-KA204-051578.title: Arts for Human Rights
2019-1-IE01-KA204-051578.summary:
<< Background >>

Smashing Times International Centre for The Arts and Equality is an organisation developed to promote the use of the Arts and Creative Methods to promote Human Rights and Equality.  We were interested in addressing the gap present for adult educators / Artists and facilitators in curriculum and resources that they can use in their practice to promote human rights and equality in their work.  To provide resources and creative tools which could be used by educators / artists and arts facilitators in the role as educators of adults.

<< Objectives >>

To conduct research with adult educators and learners on the role fo the arts to promote human rights and equality. To develop a range of resources to support the inclusion of Arts education to promote human rights and equality.  To raise awareness of the role of the arts to promote human rights and equality . 

Arts for Human Rights was a European wide three-year, transnational partnership project using creative processes of theatre and film and new digital technologies to promote learning and raising awareness in relation to human rights and gender equality across Europe. The aim was firstly to design a new transnational Arts for Human Rights module that educators, teachers and artists can implement with adult learners using creative processes to promote human rights and gender equality and secondly to design a new, innovative blended learning ‘Train the Trainers’ training curriculum to train educators, teachers and artists in how to implement the Arts for Human Rights module with adult learners.

The educational information to accompany the five lessons consists of five hand-outs; three Ted-Style talks, a short film and an Arts and Human Rights research book.

<< Implementation >>

Project activities included four transnational Partner Exchanges including a kick-off meeting on 22 September 2019, Dublin, Ireland; 24 February 2022, Belgrade, Serbia; 26 April 2022, Vukovar, Croatia and 29 June 2022, Sofia, Bulgaria. There were two online transnational partner exchanges  held on Monday 16 March 2020, attended by 9 from the partnership; and on Tuesday 14 December 2021, attended by 6 from the partnership. A  research process with completed with 173 questionnaires distributed and 77 responses evaluated from five partner countries – Ireland, Spain, Serbia, Croatia and Bulgaria. 

Project assets – an Arts and Human Rights book with stories and articles; an Arts and Human Rights curriculum and train-the-trainer curriculum with five workshop modules on human rights, peace-building, gender equality, LGBTQI+ rights and climate justice; nine hand-outs; one film and three Ted-style talks.
In terms of numbers in attendance, there was a representation of 35 from partner organisations at four on-site and two on-line transnational partner exchanges; 173 questionnaires were distributed and 77 completed; 325 attended 15 multiplier events; and 15,000 were reached via email, and 300,000 reached via communication and dissemination.

<< Results >>

The project resulted in the completion of a range of project assets – an Arts and Human Rights book with stories and articles; an Arts and Human Rights curriculum and train-the-trainer curriculum with five workshop modules on human rights, peace-building, gender equality, LGBTQI+ rights and climate justice; nine hand-outs; one film and three Ted-style talks.
In terms of numbers in attendance, there was a representation of 35 from partner organisations at four on-site and two on-line transnational partner exchanges; 173 questionnaires were distributed and 77 completed; 325 attended 15 multiplier events; and 15,000 were reached via email, and 300,000 reached via communication and dissemination.

2019-1-IS01-KA204-051143.title: Interactive Use of Technology for Adult Education
2019-1-IS01-KA204-051143.summary:
<< Background >>

An amazing selection of technology and methodologies of teaching & learning has already been offered to the partner institutions.
It was difficult for students to decide what is a good choice when trying to boost their learning and self-confidence. When disadvantaged students have gathered the courage starting to study again, they are often disappointed. We wanted to find the best solution for our pedagogical staff and students by sharing best practices and experience between us.
Staying competitive means that educational institutions needed to be innovative and adaptive.
We needed to make use of technology to help students boost their self-confidence. Bad choices can have consequences. The target groups were relevant staff, career- and study counsellors and teachers, but indirect target group were students with no formal education, groups with risk of social exclusion and migrants. The participants got professional development, planning their own technological learning approach and how best to assist their students. The institutions´ students got the opportunity to use technology to make the most of their learning with the use of tried and tested material from the European partners.

<< Objectives >>

Professional development of pedagogical of staff. Emphasis was on interactive study material, user-friendly and rewarding interface
- To share best practices and experience in the use of interactive tutorials-To motivate pedagogical staff and others to learn about interactive use of technology in counselling and teaching
- To help career- and study counsellors learn to design and implement effective strategies for specific adult target groups to enhance basic skills
- To organize workshops on the development and use of exemplary technical projects - To introduce special learning approach when assisting students in connection with the use of ICT
- To nurture the joy of studying
- To improve access of the institutions´ target groups to education, regardless of place and time
- Create the opportunity for learners to assess their own progress in interactive studies
- To make a project website where the project material is published. A link to the website is on the partner institutions´ own websites 
Institutions shared different experiences of using technology for counselling, teaching/learning and different knowledge. Therefore, there was a reason to seek advice and learn best practices from each other.

<< Implementation >>

Participating institutions constantly serve a diverse student population, most of the students have a short formal education. A big number of them are dropouts in the formal school system, for example due to learning difficulties or social situations. The knowledge of our partner institutions, shared with the others, through visits, presentations and workshops helps us better understand teaching & learning processes and implement effective strategies and develop interactive teaching materials which supports our students in a positive and effective way.

<< Results >>

The results are: 
Professional development of teachers, career- and study counsellors and other staff
The study materials that we shared are interactive and the interface user-friendly approach is rewarding
• Increased knowledge in the use of interactive tutorials in teaching and learning by sharing best 
   practices and experience
• Career- and study counsellors, teachers and other pedagogical staff use the
   interactive tools in counselling and teaching/learning
• Career- and study counsellors designed and implement effective strategies for specific adult target
   groups to enhance basic skills in learning
• Increased knowledge of how to design ICT action-plans
• Increased knowledge of the development and use of exemplary technical projects
• Increased knowledge of special learning approaches and how to assist students in connection with   the use of ICT in education
• Increased knowledge of how to nurture the joy of studying and prevent as possible
   disappointment among adult learners
• Improved access of the institutions´ target groups to education, regardless of place and time
• Learners assess their own progress with interactive study-material
• A project website where information and project materials are published

2019-1-IT02-KA204-062493.title: EduStorytelling
2019-1-IT02-KA204-062493.summary:
<< Background >>

“EduStorytelling” (EST) addressed the digital skills and literacy gap affecting European adults coming from disadvantaged backgrounds through the methodology of Digital Storytelling (DST) as a pathway to develop high-quality digital and literacy skills and competencies. It improved attitudes of peer-interaction and cooperative learning, forming part of a comprehensive digital literacy in order to foster personal development, active citizenship and employability perspectives.

Participants involved in the project had a medium or good level of digital and literacy skills and were social workers with previous experience in training adult people. They participated in the project to undertake an upskilling path to improve digital and transversal skills employing the DST methodology. They acquired self-confidence and motivation in order to foster proactive attitudes when working with disadvantaged groups.
EST rationale stemmed from the trend of fast-paced evolution in ICT technologies and digital instruments, triggering a continuous, open-ended re-thinking of established models of social interaction, participation, education, business and employability. The ownership of a set of good literacy and digital skills has become a discriminating factor of employability and of effective exercise citizenship rights.

<< Objectives >>

- To explore the educational potential of DST as an innovative instrument for enhancing digital competences of EU citizens, in continuity with the rationale of the EU Digital Competences Framework for Citizens.
- To develope a cross-border and cross sector synergy with the purpose of creating innovative models of Storytelling education tailored to the needs of Adult learners.
- To Establish a wider community of Storytelling practitioners using MOOC course and interacting with their peers.

<< Implementation >>

-	A total of 3 Transnational Partners' Meetings were implemented.
-	Learning, Teaching, Training Activities - Training Course C1 Short-term joint staff training event

<< Results >>

1. An educational curriculum for adult education trainers.
The partners produced a curriculum for adult education trainers who work with adult learners coming from a disadvantaged background. The curriculum explored the potential of storytelling to improve the digital skills of adult education trainers guiding them through an upskilling path. The materials produced were integrated in the MOOC modules (Result 4).

2. Test of the curriculum in a specific short-term joint staff training event.
The teaching activity envisaged in the project involved adult education trainers. The staff training event tested the curriculum developed in IO1 (Result 1) in order to improve it using the feedback of trainers involved. 

3. A comprehensive “DigiStories” Guide, as a reference for trainers in adult education.
The "DigiStories" Guide is an instrument of professional development and operational guidance usable by adult education institutions and operators working in the planning and execution of educational initiatives aimed at fostering social inclusion, active citizenship and employability of adult targets through Digital Storytelling. 

4. A MOOC online course for direct use by trainers in adult education to be integrated in the educational offer in adult education institutions, complemented by a community section with a Blog storing digital narratives of participants and acting as a hub of a wider DST learning community
The Consortium of partners created an open access MOOC in the languages of all partner countries. It was complemented by a Blog which provided a node of communication and peer- interaction of a wider Digital Storytelling community in partner countries and beyond.

2019-1-IT02-KA204-062808.title: Digital Clil for all
2019-1-IT02-KA204-062808.summary:
Key competences foster the ability to participate in social life, widen job opportunities and improve the socio-occupational conditions of citizens, among these the project "Digital Clil for all" wants to strengthen the digital and multilingual skills of adults. According to what is indicated by the recommendations of the Council of the European Union in 2018, one of the characteristics of key competences is the possibility of being acquired and strengthened during the whole life and the fact that they represent the base to exercise an active citizenship. Despite the importance of soft skills, the latest reports on the topic show a European contest still lagging behind, especially with regard to the adult population: 44% of the population holds basic digital skills and 35.2% knows an extra language compared to the native. Given the importance of strengthening transversal skills throughout the entire life, and finding that the level of digital and multilingual skills for the adult population is still too low, the "Digitalclil 4all" project aims to create a new teaching methodology to be used for adult learning. The Dital Clil method integrates the CLIL approach (Content and Language Integrated Learning), which uses a second language to convey non-linguistic disciplines, with the use of ICT, enhancing the digital dimension in the teaching process. The general objective is therefore to improve and strengthen the digital and linguistic skills of adult learners for a more active participation in the labour market and European society, to this aim the project will support the teaching staff in the ability of improving the level of soft skills of adult learners through the digital clil methodology and will update the teaching methods for adult learning based on the digital and linguistic experience.
The project involves the creation of two Intellectual Outputs:
    • COMPENDIUM OF BEST PRACTICES ON CLIL AND DIGITAL DIDACTIC METHODOLOGY
    • GUIDELINES FOR APPLYING DIDACTIC METHODOLOGY DIGITAL CLIL IN LEARNING FOR ADULTS
All the materials produced by the project will be available in 6 languages (Italian, Romanian, Croatian, Greek, Spanish and English) to ensure maximum usability both in the national contexts where the project will be implemented and in other European countries.
In conclusion, 20 teachers will be directly involved in the research and output definition activities, which will test the digital clil methodology in 10 pilot courses. Precisely, the teachers will participate in a 5-day training event (4 teachers for each partner country) and they will be provided with all the tools necessary to use the "digital Clil" methodology in the classroom. Once back, 10 pilot courses will be launched (2 in Romania, 2 in Cyprus, 2 in Croatia, 2 in Spain and 2 in Italy) in which the methodology will be used in adult classes and for teaching different disciplines chosen by the partner institutions . The results of the pilot courses will be useful to adapt and improve the methodology and deliver a tested product. During the implementation of the project and in order to share the methodology with the stakeholders of the sector, in addition to the 20 teachers, 100 students, 15 experts in innovative teaching methods in the field of linguistic and digital skills, 10 adult training institutes and 200 teachers will be involved. Through the dissemination plan we expect to reach at least 3000 stakeholders (teachers, managers of training institutes and public institutions), 3000 adult citizens.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2019-1-LT01-KA204-060743.title: Development of Cultural and Heritage Tourism Skills within Rural Communities
2019-1-LT01-KA204-060743.summary:
<< Background >>

The project idea came from the nature of the partner organisations, operating in the rural areas and working with the rural communities: farmers, craftspeople, local business people, and other local inhabitants. All of them live their daily rural life which is full of local culture heritage: local crafts, traditions, folkmusic, local food, country life style, nature, local architectre and other simple but interesting things. Some of the partners had members who provided tourism services, such as acommodation, local food products, trainings on food production and crafts, study visits and other which attract the tourists and raise the awareness on the villages and rural culture heritage. The partners raised the need to strentghen the local communities' skills in increasing the visibility of the rural areas in the social media and modern communication channels to promote the rural culture heritage for tourism purposes. As the most effective and popular way of promotion in the social meda are short video clips, the partners identified that their adult members lack of skills in producing the video by smart phones and publication them in the social media, Facebook and Youtube. The project was prepared to fill this gap.

<< Objectives >>

The overall aim of the project was to improve the rural adults' competencies in provision of the cultural and heritage tourism services in the partner countries.

The objectives were threefold:
- development of the training tool-kit for adults training, based on the hands-on learning method; 
- improvement of the adult educators skills in teaching adults on cultural and heritage tourism, 
- improvement and extending of the adult learning opportunities on cultural and heritage tourism. 

There two target groups: 
- adult educators, 
- adult learners. 

The project was aiming to develop the training tookitl for the adults wishing to make videos with the smartphones in promoting the rural cultural heritage. Also, the tool was dedicated for the adult trainers, who would be able to integrate the training toolkit into various training courses related with the local cultural heritage, such as production of local food, farming praciticies, production of crafts, etc.

<< Implementation >>

PARTNERS MEETINGS. 
The in-person and online transnational meetings were organised for project management and partners' communication. The online meetings 
replaced the in-person meetings and were very evffecitve in partners' communication and project management. 

INTELECTUAL OUTPUT
The toolkit was developed according to the mtethodolgy prepared by the partners.The toolkit is composed of the methodology, the description of the best practice cases on rural heritage in partner countries, the videos on the best practice cases produced by the partnerss, the tips the training material for making the videos.

TRAININGS
The in-person and online short-term staff trainings were organised for the both target groups to discuss the project subject (rural heritage through videos) and to pilot the project output (a toolkit on video production). 

DISSEMINATION 
The multiplying events, including the international forum, were organised to disseminate the information on the project and its results and to discuss the project subject (rural heritage for tourism purpose) with the local communities. 
The posts and articles in the social media and web pages were produced to disseminate information on the project.

<< Results >>

PARTNERS MEETINGS
- 2 transnational in-person partner meetings were organised in Norway and Lithuania (2 transnational meetings in Denmark and Iceland were cancelled due to the Covid-19 travel restrictions). 
- 15 online meetings were organised through zoom platform every 2 months. Online meetings replaced the in-person meetings and were very evffecitve in partners' communication and project management. 

INTELECTUAL OUTPUT
- methodology of toolkit development was developed 
- 30 best practice cases (5/partner) on rural heritage were identified (texts) 
- 12 videos (2/partner) on the cultural heritage best practice were produced (videos) + 12 produced as additional results
- 1 training tool-kit was developed, including tips for production of videos (text and video)

TRAININGS
- 2 short-term staff trainings on piloting project output were organised in Croatia and France and 24 (4 per partner) adult educators and learners were trained on cultural and heritage tourism and application tool-kit to the trainings. + 3 participants were trained as additional result
- 2 online workshops were organised and 15 participants were trained as the additional results

DISSEMINATION EVENTS
- 3 multiplying events were organised in Iceland, Norway and Denmark for 40 participants each
- 1 international forum was organised in Lithuania for 40 participants

2019-1-LU01-KA204-050116.title: Move it forward +
2019-1-LU01-KA204-050116.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was inspired by DLI's “Move it forward-Female Digital Starter weekend” concept, with the opportunity to support scaling at the international level and multiply the impact to support female entrepreneurs in new countries.
The main objective was to promote entrepreneurship to more women and support them in their journey. In addition to our respective findings, the following information and reports from the EU commission stated that women’s intellectual and entrepreneurial potential, contribution and creativity are still an under-exploited source of economic growth. In 2019, women still represented only 34.4% of the EU self-employed and 30% of start-up entrepreneurs. Given this data, having more women entrepreneurs would benefit job creation, robust economic growth, and social progress.
For WIDE, the topic of women's economic empowerment is a core value and the project fitted perfectly with its development plan and the needs of the target group in Luxembourg. The project’s idea and target group were very interesting and logical for the consortium and their respective country. With some of the partners being gender equality advocates, WIDE and all the partners adhere to Move It Forward’s objectives enthusiastically.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objectives were to create new learning opportunities and collaborative experiences for women looking to develop entrepreneurial skills and to promote women's entrepreneurship to new social and geographic groups.

The partnership wanted to innovate and support organisations in the field of entrepreneurship support and education, focusing on women, in developing methodologies, activities and resources for collaboration, digital entrepreneurship and mentoring to be able to scale the Move it Forward concept, develop new tools and eventually be able to transfer knowledge to new organisations. From the starting point of the existing concept developed by our Belgian partner DLI, this project was created and implemented to develop relationships with the private sector, enhance practices, enrich collaboration and partner experiences, and finally multiply and sustain the impact on adult education organisations, trainers, mentors, women learners and (future) entrepreneurs, stakeholders and entrepreneurship ecosystem as well as organisations outside the partnership countries.

All the partners were very keen on participating in the development of a new format that had the chance to grow and scale internationally.

<< Implementation >>

All activities were implemented as planned in the project, despite several changes and challenges due to the pandemic situation. All partners contributed to the implementation of the project with the main following activities:
- Project management from September 2019 to May 2022
- Regular dissemination of the project's results
- C1 Training in Brussels with DLI as host and trainer for partners' participants
- 3 Transnational meetings: in Luxembourg, Paris and Brussels and many online coordination meetings
- Development of resources for organising a hackathon (IO1)
- Organisation of pilot Hackathons (IO1, IO3, multiplier events)
- Developing resources for implementing a mentoring process (IO2, IO3)
- Implementing a pilot mentoring programme and follow-up of participants and beneficiaries
- Working on the sustainability of the project (IO3)
- Developing resources to measure the impact and sustainability of the MIF+ hackathon (IO3)
- Final Dissemination Event in Brussels

<< Results >>

Most of our concrete outputs are visible in the 5 languages of the partnership on our MIF+ platform.
The consortium developed resources for organising a hackathon during IO1 by creating a Guide "How to organise a Move it forward+ hackathon", a jury sheet, awards certificates and participant's certificate
During IO2, the consortium produced materials to implement a mentoring process with mentors' and mentees' portfolios. We also have produced a toolkit to develop sustainability via Mentoring together with checklists and a guide regarding Corporate Social Responsibility and Fundraising for a MIF+ event. 
During IO3, the mentoring programme was piloted and partners produced an additional handbook dedicated to project development in a team of women entrepreneurs. In total, 31 women participated in the mentoring pilots.

In 2019 was organised the kick-off meeting of MIF+ was in Luxembourg. Early 2020 was organised the C1 in Brussels hosted by DLI. Then the 2nd and 3rd TN meetings were organised in October 2021 in Paris and in March 2022 in Brussels.

6 hackathons and 1 final event gathering more than 250 women entrepreneurs, mentors, volunteers, and jury members from public and private organisations were organised during the project.

2019-1-MK01-KA204-060319.title: Organic agriculture Innovation platform
2019-1-MK01-KA204-060319.summary:
<< Background >>

The main motivation to apply for this project was to help our country (and the region) reach the potential for organic production, to help the environment and invest in better and healthier future for us and the next generations. We saw great potential in organic agriculture for sustainable and economic development of the country.
One of the biggest obstacles for development of this economic sector is the limited availability of vocational education in organic farming. The greatest constraints faced by farmers on the road to organic agriculture are lack of knowledge, access to markets and the process of conversion and certification. Greater investment in education and capacity-building can help overcoming these constraints. 
With this project we wanted to introduce adult trainers and non-formal education providers with education on organic agricultural, but also introduce them to the rules, laws, regulations, certification, marketing and branding of products, and make education on organic agriculture available to unemployed persons. Another reason to apply for this project was to build a regional network and strategic partnership for promotion of organic agriculture and education. This platform will continue to work in the future.

<< Objectives >>

The overall objective of this project was to increase the knowledge of adult education providers about organic production, marketing and branding of products, thus securing incomes and jobs for farmers and profitability through market driven organic production. 
This objective was achieved by creation of a new and innovative curriculum and enhancing the knowledge about marketing through specially designed trainings and practical handbooks. 
This objective was also accomplished by research and analyses of previous experiences in the project partner’s countries and creation of a baseline study of the current situation.

<< Implementation >>

In this project we:
- Created an educational website (www.opaiplatform.com);
- Created a baseline study;
- Created two handbooks: "Organic Farming Handbook" and "Creation of a Brand Plan";
- Developed new and innovative Curriculum on organic farming and branding;
- Built capacity and exchanged knowledge through two learning, training and teaching activities.
- Promoted the final results of the project at multiplier events in each country that was part of this project. 
- Exchanged and implemented good practices and experience among partners and we established strategic partnership that was strengthen through three transnational project meetings.

<< Results >>

1. We created a website - a place for sharing educational content on organic farming. It’s easy to navigate and easy to read. All of the partners were included in its creation and development.
2. We created a comprehensive baseline study - an analysis of the current situation with current facts and data in each of the countries in the projects, with conclusions and recommendations. The study was disseminated to all stakeholders.
3. We created two practical handbooks: Organic Farming and Creation of a Brand Plan - teaching materials for courses, that provide a solid foundation of knowledge. 
4. We created curriculum with exam questions for organizing a course on organic farming. The course of study will enable the learners to acquire the specific knowledge and skills. The Curriculum will serve as a guide for teachers, and it establishes standards for student performance and teacher accountability.
5. We completed two trainings for capacity building and exchange of knowledge and experience between course providers, experts and our staff with a purpose to increase the skills and knowledge. 
6. The results of the project were promoted at public events.
7. A regional strategic platform and partnership was created and strengthen.

2019-1-NL01-KA204-060276.title: Connectivity
2019-1-NL01-KA204-060276.summary:
<< Background >>

Connectivity was a project focused on developing a method of sustainable inclusion for unemployed adults through educational outdoor activities. We saw the need for such an initiative for multiple reasons. On one hand, there is a shortage when it comes to educational activities and programs designed for adults - there is a growing interest when it comes to working with youth, but offering the same to adults seems to be more difficult. One of the main reasons for this is that these adults are less likely to participate in such events, in most cases the participants are people who already take advantage of many learning opportunities. On the other hand, the organizations that do organize such learning events tend to focus on the activities themselves, without having a method and an approach in mind - this leads to one-time activities with no impact in the long run. 
Through this project initiative, our aim was to offer a solution to this challenge by improving and extending the supply of high-quality learning opportunities tailored to the needs of individual adults facing fewer opportunities so that they can enhance their key competencies and have higher chances to enter the labor market. Inclusion was our response to unemployment.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project, we wanted to involve organizations that are actively working with the target group of unemployed adults (adults facing fewer opportunities) and we wanted to support their work through a series of meetings, training events, and local activities. We wanted to develop a sustainable method of inclusion through which they can approach the members of their target group while offering sustainable and impactful activities in the field of non-formal education. Our aim was to create an impact not only in the case of the adult learners involved but also in the case of the organizations and their local communities. 
By creating an innovative playground and engaging persons with limited formal education not only in the activities of the organizations but also in the work of these organizations, inclusion happened on a much bigger scale and showed us a way to tackle unemployment.
We realized that outdoor activities are less frequently used, even though their significance is indisputable. These activities are engaging and easy to facilitate; additionally, through these activities, people can step out of their comfort zones and learn more about themselves and others. Thus we decided to base our project on outdoor education.

<< Implementation >>

We have facilitated a series of activities in order to create an impact on multiple levels. 
We had four training meetings (we decided to call them meetings since we wanted to create an exchange of experiences and we wanted to involve all our partners and participants; instead of a classical training setup, we created dynamic learning events based on guided practice opportunities), three transnational project meetings in order to evaluate the process with all our project partners, and a variety of multiplier events in each country in order to spread our knowledge and results among other educators and professionals working with people. 
Through all our activities we worked with an emerging design - this means that we had a framework and we adjusted our program plans to the group of participants we had. This helped us through the difficulties caused by the pandemic and it also helped us to create a program that truly represents the learnings and wishes of those who were involved. We worked with the topic of inclusion (inclusion as a response to unemployment) and we put that into practice from the beginning - we involved our partners, participants, associated partners, and stakeholders - based on the impact we wanted to create.

<< Results >>

Through the project timeline we have developed three main outputs: a workbook containing various outdoor activities and some tips and tricks when it comes to the facilitation of these activities, an easy-to-read handbook describing our method of inclusion with case studies and exercises, and an online platform with additional content when it comes to the creation of impact - especially with this specific target group. All these outputs were created based on our first-hand experiences, we tried to make a selection that would support other educators and adult learners in their own professional development. The activities were tested multiple times during the project and the method was used not only in Connectivity but also in other projects happening parallelly. 
Besides these outputs, we created a Facebook page in order to publish the developments of our project and we created various posts and articles through the social media platforms of our partner organizations. 
One of our most significant results is the community of adult learners and educators that we have developed - thanks to this project, there was and is clear communication between these two parties which has led to the creation of more impactful learning events.

2019-1-NL01-KA204-060370.title: Psychological and Psychiatric Comorbidity in Visually Impaired Adults
2019-1-NL01-KA204-060370.summary:
<< Background >>

The complexity of visual impairment with multiple additional disabilities is the reason for often having to choose for a very individualistic approach. A pilot study (Hidden Treasures [Verborgen Schatten], Boessen et al., 2016) showed that there is hardly any literature available on how to work with this target-group. Especially literature about the combination of mental health problems (psychological and psychiatric) problems combined with visual impairment (VI) is lacking. Within the total population of VI people, this group is relatively small. Therefore it is necessary and unavoidable to cooperate with partners abroad to develop more expertise in supporting the target group in their societal participation, mainly by collecting good practices.

<< Objectives >>

During six Transnational Project Meetings (TPM) professionals and members of the target group share their knowledge and experience, leading to the professional development of participants:
- increased knowledge and understanding about complexitiy of practice;
- increased knowledge about possible approaches;
- increased knowledge about instruments and tools to be used;
- increased understanding about contexts and practices in different EU countries.
Leading to the possibility to reflect on own context and practice.

On completion of the project all collected good practices from the six TPM's are brought together in a digital 'Good Practices Book' that will be used for further training of professionals (educators and trainers) in the field of VI adults, aiming to increase societal participation and social inclusion of the target group.

<< Implementation >>

Through six TPM's, organized in five different countries (the Netherlands (2 sessions), Italy, Croatia, Hungary and Germany) participants with various professional backgrounds, e.g. psychologists, occupational therapists, behavioural scientists, vocational rehabilitation specialists, yet all providing care and treatment to persons with a visual impairment and mental health problems could gain new knowledge and insights on how to provide support to this specific group of clients. Each TPM was based on a specific theme being one or more specific psychological or psychiatric disorders. For these training sessions, a format was developed based on core building blocks, i.e.:
•	Interactive sessions with peer-exchanges on concrete cases (intervision).
•	Theoretical input from experts on the themes of each session.
•	Presentation of the national/regional situation in relation to the target group and the themes.
•	Workshops and/or self-experience sessions to further explain tools/instruments or specific support approaches for this group of clients.

<< Results >>

Outputs: 
- gaining new perspectives on the own case by learning through exchange with colleagues during the case-discussions, through the presentations of theoretical background on the different themes and through background information on how the participation in-stitutions organise and offer care and treatment. The material presented during the TPM was assessed as very helpful as well as the discussions on the importance of an effective diagnosis; 
- material related to each of the TPM sessions that can be used for further internal dissemination and use in each participating organisation.

Outcomes/results:
Increased awareness and knowledge about the themes tackled at individual level + learning at level of organisations involved, about the complexity of this group of clients and why an individual approach is needed. Participants were active in sharing the obtained knowledge with colleagues and other staff.

A digital Book of Good Practices containing all information shared during the TPM's. It is expected that through dissemination of this book awareness about the need for tailored interventions for persons with visual impairment and mental health problems will be obtained in organisations and society.

2019-1-PL01-KA204-065092.title: Unnecessary - useful and aesthetic. Creative approach to recycling.
2019-1-PL01-KA204-065092.summary:
<< Background >>

Project "Unnecessary - useful and aesthetic. Creative approach to recycling " is part of the idea of sustainable development, involves socially inclusive activities, promotion of proper behavior in relation to the environment, preservation of natural balance between nature and non-nature. The project is dedicated to the contribution of citizens to environmental protection; environment with its impact on individuals, good health and well-being of members of local communities in the partner countries, as well as promoting creative use of waste in art, art therapy and improvement of ecological awareness of persons at risk of marginalization (disabled, seniors, migrants and refugees). Moreover after conducting an analysis before applying for funding, we came to the conclusion that there are no adequate training materials on the publishing market for teaching staff dealing with the issue of upcycling and the use of recycled materials in applied and artistic art.

<< Objectives >>

The project involves the following objectives:
 - to develop cooperation and exchange of experience of educators for creative activity of persons at risk of marginalization: disabled, elderly people, migrants and refugees,
 - averaging and expanding professional qualifications of people working with groups at risk of marginalization,
- dissemination of art-therapy methods of work among staff working with people from communities at risk of marginalization and people working for these environments, as well as increasing the chances of developing individual educators participating in the project,
 - expanding knowledge and skills in the care of the natural environment and related to the subject of the natural environment of social responsibility as well as expanding cultural competences and developing the creativity of employees and volunteer partners cooperating with partner organizations,
- increasing the awareness of disadvantaged people (disabled, elderly people, migrants and refugees) in the scope of the impact of pro-ecological behavior on the environment, health and well-being.
Methods used in the project: ecological education, art therapy, artistic and theater activities, lectures, workshops, presentations, open work methods.

<< Implementation >>

We have implemented:
- five project meetings with koordinators responsible for project implementation in individual partner organizations. Each partner organized one meeting. Meetings were held approximately every four months. The purpose of the project meetings was to control the proper course of the project. During the first meeting, the planned activities, programs of training meetings, rules of financing and cooperation were discussed. Subsequent meetings were aimed into monitoring.
- a publisation of a manual containing the curriculum "Upcycling of waste electrical and electronic equipment" - the result of intellectual work
- a conference attended by project partners, researchers and educators, instructors, conducting classes in the field of ecology, environmental protection, employees of occupational therapy workshops, artists who use or want to use at work upcycling of used materials.
- five training meetings aimed at deepening knowledge on sustainable development and getting to know the methods of work for environmental protection used by partner organizations.
- numerous local activities related to the acquired knowledge and skills of our instructors.

<< Results >>

As a result of the provided training, conferences, workshop classes and open demonstrations of working methods, the results include: 
- increase of professional skills of educators in the field of working with adults;
- acquiring new educators and improving existing psychological, interpersonal and methodological skills in working with a group, necessary during animating educational classes with the use of art-therapy methods; 
- increasing the chances of individual development and raising the self-esteem of educators participating in the project;
Around 1000 people was involved in the project. In the project we were dealing with sustainable consumption using a separate publication about it - a handbook containing a program of workshops "Upcycle of used electrical and electronic equipment". The aim of the workshop is to raise awareness of the available natural resources in electrical and electronic equipment and the need for proper processing of e-waste. A durable permanent result of the project will be a generally available project website, photos and description methods of work on the websites of partner organizations and the handbook.

2019-1-PL01-KA204-065707.title: BURNOUT AID
2019-1-PL01-KA204-065707.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was addressed to NGO educators working with adults who are facing or might be at risk of facing burnout - specifically those working with adults from disadvantaged target groups (refugees, immigrants, people with disabilities, LGBTQ+, seniors, women) – professionals at risk of burnout that might lead to more severe conditions such as state of tension and preoccupation, depression or even vicarious traumatization. We provided support to leaders, employees and volunteers in NGOs. In a prominently used model (Maslach and Leiter, The Truth about Burnout, 1997), burnout is a crisis in one‘s relationship with work, during which affected people become chronically exhausted, cynical and detached from work, and feel increasingly ineffective on the job. It is not a phenomenon which appears suddenly but develops gradually. Both the employer and the employee can detect burnout among the staff at an early stage and implement strategies in order to intercept the burnout progress.

The three partnering organizations have both: experienced burnout and/or exhaustion in their teams and could observe this syndrome developing among other activists within other NGOs in our three countries. In 2015 Common Zone (from Croatia) conducted a survey on 213 employees from 109 NGOs which showed that an alarming 56% of the respondents experienced burnout once or several times.

Based on our extensive work within the NGO community for years we outlined the needs that we wanted to address. They included: providing healthy working conditions, raising awareness about burnout and its prevention as well as offering tools to combat the burnout phenomenon in the third sector. Burnout in NGOs, and its prevention, had not been a topic well-analyzed and addressed in none of the partnering countries before our project has begun. 

The implementation of the project on an international perspective of 3 countries allowed us to work out results useful for a wide range of educators in European organizations.

The 4 IOs produced in the project are dedicated to satisfying these needs.

<< Objectives >>

Our aim was to research burnout syndrome in an international partnership and create the tools to help prevent and combat it. We wanted to raise awareness about the scale of burnout in NGOs, share our knowledge (as there is a lot of stigma around it), and offer tools to leaders and teams to improve the working environment by learning about the factors specific to the NGO sector that contribute to burnout. When an opportunity arose to dive into the topic of burnout with international colleagues, we saw this as a great way to contribute more directly to helping to diminish this problem in the NGO sector. 


Our goals were:
1) To raise awareness and provide knowledge on the burnout syndrome in NGOs, among
organizations’ managements, decision-makers and society.
2) To prevent the adult-educating staff in the NGOs from developing burnout.
3) To provide help in countervailing burnout among NGO leaders and employees (educators,
regardless of the form of employment, including volunteers) – diagnosis and innovative remedial tools to implement.

Our aim was to cooperate on a transnational level to exchange knowledge and experiences on the topic, compare local conditions, and work on solutions based on different local perspectives in order to create innovative results which will help solve difficulties in the work environment in the EU NGO sector.

<< Implementation >>

Our 4 intellectual outputs included: 

Quantitative research on burnout performed in three countries (including desk research, research conducted in 5 NGOs in each of the three countries, and experts’ interviews) resulted in 3 research reports; 
8 anti-burnout workshops scenarios and their dissemination in the three countries; 
15 video clips produced by each partnering organization tackling the topic of burnout from different angles (i.e. information on the phases of burnout, activists’ testimonies, regenerative working style in NGOs etc.);
Burnout Aid online platform with 2 self-assessment questionnaires (for individuals and organizations) and the recommendations, guidelines, exercises, inspirations regarding burnout prevention. 

We held 7 Transnational Partner Meetings, as well 3 national and 2 international dissemination events by the end of the project. Through communication and inclusion of targeted groups and individuals in the development of the outputs (e.g., interviews, beta testing) we have continuously kept the topic visible within our local annual programs.

<< Results >>

The main result (IO4) was an online platform with an easily accessible set of tools (diagnostic,
prophylactic and remediation/recovery) helping to protect educators in NGOs from job burnout or to deal with it. Web users are able to self-assess burnout risk and get access to research results, recommendations, inspirations, procedures, standards, and best practices. These specific tools are intertwined – the results of the online test (burnout diagnosis) determine the specific tools and materials one gets access to, according to diagnosis (eg. an adequate workshop scenario). The web platform was created in cooperation with all partners and runs in every partner language and in English so the results are available at the local-national level in Poland, Croatia and Slovenia - as well as in Europe and internationally (thanks to the English language version). The physical server was installed in Poland, and the web application is available without restrictions (open access) for an interested public: educators, NGOs, institutions, experts and individuals.

The tools accessible on web application are as follow:
(1a) Diagnostic test for NGOs. 
(1b) Diagnostic test for individuals 
The questionnaire helps to answer the questions: Are you or is your organization at risk of job burnout? What should be improved and how? What decisions are to be made? What are the possible ways to prevent burnout and/or to deal with burnout from the individual and organizational perspective?

Workshop scenarios for NGOs (IO3). We provided 2 types of scenarios – to diagnose and prevent job burnout and to manage the phenomenon of job burnout. We prepared 8
scenarios adaptable to the size of the organization (smaller organization up to 10 people vs. larger organization over 10 people) and to the type of organization’s activity (eg. women, migrants/refugees, older people, LGBTQ+). The goal of the scenarios is strategic rather than informative - the workshop would focus on the questions: What organization/educator is planning to change in the context of burnout? How to prepare and implement a recovery plan?

The scenarios will become a tool for educators working with NGOs, as part of performing their own educational activities in the field of burnout. The scenarios are organized in a way that makes it possible to use them either as a whole or in a modular way (only particular exercises, presentations, and simulations). The scenarios were created in the course of joint work of partner organizations.

Video clips on job burnout (IO2). We prepared a series of 15 video clips about the challenge of burnout, giving voice to both experts dealing with the topic and people who have experienced burnout and have the courage to share their experiences. The script of each film was developed in a way that the film is educational material that can be used during workshops on professional burnout.

Research reports (IO1). We included materials collected during case studies, desk research, qualitative research in NGOs, experts interviews related to the specifics of NGOs in Poland, Croatia and Slovenia. The information (both: general and detailed) was aimed at raising awareness about the problem, preventing burnout and/or helping with burnout – recommendations and expert opinions, statistics and useful sources became the basis for the  online platform content.

The intellectual results have become available on the online platform upon the completion of the project, however, 3 of them were created before the application has been launched: research reports in 3 countries, video clips and workshop scenarios. We have disseminated them through awareness-building campaigns during the project through online and offline promotion/dissemination and on multiplier events - networking educators to share their problems and practice, disseminate the results and build awareness.

2019-1-RO01-KA204-063798.title: Enhancing the social inclusion of low income single parents
2019-1-RO01-KA204-063798.summary:
One of the 5 targets of the Europe 2020 headline indicators is to reduce poverty by lifting at least 20 million people out of the risk of poverty or social exclusion by 2020. In 2016, there were 118.0 million people in the EU-28 who lived in households at risk of poverty or social exclusion (AROPE), equivalent to 23.5% of the entire population.
Everywhere in Europe, single parent families have an increased risk of poverty and social exclusion. In 2016, the highest at-risk-of-poverty rate in the EU-28 was recorded for single persons with dependent children, at more than one third (34%). Bulgaria with 47,4%, Spain with 42,2%, Lithuania with 41,9%, and Romania with 41,4% are among the countries with the highest rates of at-risk-of-poverty single persons with dependent children; Croatia has a rate of 34% and Greece 31,4%. 
According to the 2016 EIGE report “Poverty, gender and lone parents in the EU - Review of the implementation of the Beijing Platform for Action”, almost half (48%) of lone mothers and a third (32%) of lone fathers are at risk of poverty or social exclusion. Women in particular are affected as they make up almost 85% of all one-parent families in the EU. Younger mothers and women with young children are the least-employed parent groups. It is important to note also that single motherhood affects poverty most for low-educated mothers. Although single-mother households are more likely to be poor at all educational levels, the single-mother poverty gap is generally larger the lower the mother’s level of education (Härkönen, J. (2018). Single-mother poverty: how much do educational differences in single motherhood matter?). 
Moreover, having a job is not always enough to guarantee the economic well-being of single parents and keep them out of poverty.
Increasing single parents’ economic independence, with particular attention to single mothers, is key to raising them and their families out of poverty. Work-life balance measures also play a prominent role in supporting the full participation of single parents in society. Access to services such as childcare, long-term care, as well as education and training, and other enabling services can remove barriers to the labour market and contribute to social inclusion.
In order to contribute to the socio-economic empowerment and inclusion of low-income and low-qualified single parents in Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, Lithuania, Romania and Spain, the projects sets the following objectives:
• Support at least 150 socio-economically disadvantaged (low-income, unemployed) single parents who are low-skilled/qualified, in acquiring and developing basic skills and key competences, sense of initiative, entrepreneurial mind-set and skills, in order to foster their employability and socio-educational and personal development, through the running of an online time-bank
• Extend the competences of at least 120 practitioners who support single parents in the teaching of numeracy, entrepreneurial and digital skills, including through the use of digital technologies, so that they can provide high quality learning opportunities tailored to the needs of low-skilled/qualified single parents, such as the running of an (online) time-bank or other similar
• Encourage low-skilled/low-qualified single parents to develop and upgrade their literacy, numeracy, digital, entrepreneurship competences and/or other key competences through peer-to-peer outreach, guidance and motivation 
• Promote access of low-income single parents to childcare and other services (they may be unable to afford) through time-banking (providing services to one another) that can also facilitate/support their entry into the labour market or further training.
The above objective will be achieved by the implementation of the following activities:
1: Training programme for practitioners who support single parents, in the teaching of literacy, numeracy, entrepreneurial and digital skills 
1.1 Development of trainers curriculum 
1.2 Piloting of the trainers curriculum and evaluation
1.3 Development of digital modules
2: Training programme for the building of literacy, numeracy, digital competences, sense of initiative, and entrepreneurial skills of low-skilled single parents
2.1 Development of curriculum for low-skilled single parents
2.2 Implementation of parents’ curriculum and evaluation
2.3 Development of digital modules
3: Elaboration of guide for the development of time-bank business plan & sustainability strategy
3.1 Elaboration of guide for the development of time bank business plan & sustainability strategy
3.2 Workshop with trained single parents 
4: Creation and piloting of single parents’ time bank
4.1 Development of online time bank platform
4.2 Online time bank pilot implementation 
5: Peer-to-peer outreach strategy
5.1 Development of the peer-to-peer outreach strategy
5.2 Implementation of the peer-to-peer outreach strategy

2019-1-RO01-KA204-063802.title: Follow your Vision - FAMILY VOLUNTEERING, a new form of engagement
2019-1-RO01-KA204-063802.summary:
<< Background >>

70 million Europeans struggle with basic reading & writing, calculation, and using digital tools in everyday life. Out of these, many are the marginalized or socially excluded adults we planned to address. Without such skills & other broader abilities needed for a functional professional & personal life, they are at higher risk of unemployment, poverty & social exclusion, as shown in the ET2020/European Agenda for Adult Learning priorities and recommendation on Upskilling Pathways, adopted in 2016.
We believe Family Volunteering to be a valuable non-formal method to drastically improve this situation, but in order for this to happen, we needed to address the capacity-building and resource needs of the adult educators and volunteer-involving organizations and institutions that could run such programs. We decided to dedicate our work to this level, by studying the contexts of our countries, gathering concrete experiences and knowledge, and offering ready-to-use, user-friendly resources to all volunteer-involving organizations, as well as other adult educators and public authorities.

<< Objectives >>

Our project objectives were to:
1. Increase the capacity of adult education structures to design, implement and evaluate quality FV programs in their communities.
2. Develop managerial competencies of at least 60 adult education professionals in 6 partner countries in dealing with specifics of FV projects 
3. Improve the supply, access, and attractiveness for at least 180 adults to new and qualitative educational opportunities.
4. Increase awareness of relevant stakeholders about opportunities FV as an approach can bring to adult learning processes as well as community development.
5. Provide the opportunity and adequate space for awareness and reflection on the effects of FV on the skill development of adult learners.
6. Establish a cohesive European network of organizations committed to and able to enhance FV concept and practice.

<< Implementation >>

We have implemented all the activities we planned in the preparation phase, as stated in the project application. In addition to them, we also delivered Family Volunteering webinars (in each partner country except for Norway) and in Romania, we delivered 3 online 3-hour workshops on developing Family Volunteering Programs for organizations and institutions interested in applying the concept. We also decided among the partners to create the project website - familyvolunteering.eu - in order to better communicate and promote our efforts and results. 

The other activities - the general project management, the development of our IOs, the dissemination, monitoring, and ensuring sustainability - suffered changes in what was initially scheduled, in their timeline, but not in their overall completion. Covid forced us to make significant shifts in our Gantt chart and even to extend the project by another six months, but with an eye on our goals and constant reevaluation of the national and international contexts, we managed to implement all our proposed activities.

<< Results >>

We managed to create 5 quality resources for adult educators interested in FV programs.The research and The Feasibility Kit that bring to light the capacity of the organizations and the needs of the volunteersThe ABC of FV - a handbook that motivates adult educators and inspires through concrete examples.The Step-by-step for a clear path to a successful and rich FV program.The videos promote FV to organizations and practitioners, but they can then become great tools for the same practitioners to gather the support of future volunteers, colleagues and collaborators, and even donors.Finally, our policy recommendations address decision-makers in public institutions as well as volunteer-involving organizations and help them better understand the need for such programs and the support they themselves should provide. 

Through the pilot activities, we developed the competencies of 76 adult educators (we targeted 60) in the 6 partner countries, we involved 314 (target 180) adult volunteers, out of which 59 (target 30) had fewer opportunities. They were involved in 28 activities (target 18) together with their families - 99 families in total.The partners estimate the activities benefited over 3000 other people (we initially targeted 300).

2019-1-RO01-KA204-063947.title: DEVELOPMENT OF A TRAINING PROGRAM FOR THE IMPROVEMENT OF QUALITY OF LIFE OF ELDER PERSONS WITH REDUCED MOBILITY THROUGH THE EXPLOITATION OF ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGIES
2019-1-RO01-KA204-063947.summary:
<< Background >>

The European population is ageing and tends to live longer and independently which requires them to have a good quality of life in their daily environment. This represents one of the socio-political priorities in Europe and worldwide. While Europeans are generally living longer lives, many face multiple health conditions or mobility problems. Relatively high rates of chronic illness, mental health conditions, disability and frailty may be reduced if structural, economic and social drivers of poor health are tackled at an early stage. According to EUROSTAT [1], almost one third of people aged 75 years or more have severe difficulties in walking and almost half report difficulties with at least one personal care or household activity.Thus, it is not surprising that analysts suggest that the aging population will likely exert downward pressure on economic growth due to a significant increase in the old-age dependency ratio. Policy makers respond by converting this challenge into an opportunity by investing in preventative care, rehabilitation, age-friendly environments and assistive technologies (ATs).

[1] https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Disability_statistics_-_elderly_needs_for_help_or_assistance

<< Objectives >>

Reduced Mobility is caused by impairments in movement which affect not only the ability to move from one place to the other but the ability to move the entire body freely and normally. Mobility is an important predictor of Quality of Life (QoL) among and a measure of successful aging. ATs offer products, resources, methods, strategies, practices and services that support Persons with Reduced Mobility in attaining autonomy, independence, QoL and social inclusion. Their development and usage can reduce and even neutralize the barriers caused by the Reduced Mobility. In this context, the ERMAT project was launched with the main objective of increasing the competences (attitudes, knowledge, skills) of Elder Persons with Reduced Mobility (EPRM), Informal Caregivers and Professionals on the application of Assistive Technologies for improving their QoL. Specific objectives: (1) inform about available ATs and their application to the specific needs of EPRM; (2) create awareness and trust for using ATs for improving QoL; (3) promote sense of self care and care supported by ATs; (4) create an e-learning environment to improve digital skills and access for EPRM and supports to properly exploit ATs; (5) adopt a user-centered approach.

<< Implementation >>

ERMAT has started with the development of a co-created METHODOLOGICAL GUIDE (I.O.1) with the direct participation of end-users involved in 2 sessions: 126 participants (co-creation sessions) and 117 participants (validation sessions). The methodological guide was translated in all 6 languages of the consortium.

Training MATERIALS and ACTIVITIES were developed in I.O.2 and I.O.3. The MATERIALS are addressed to ERMAT's end-users to support them in applying ATs to improve their QoL. The Practical Training ACTIVITIES were developed for trainers and include the design of face-to-face and online Sessions, group dynamics and practical activities. All materials were translated in the 6 languages of the consortium. 

The E-TRAINING PLATFORM was created in I.O.4 to incorporate the developed materials. An online available manual was develop to explain the usage of the platform. The platform and the manual were translated in all 6 languages of the consortium. The platform validation was done in all consortium countries with 130 end-users. Multiplier events in 6 countries (142 stakeholders involved); management- and dissemination-actions implemented by all partners. Seven support UNITS were created  to ensure a sustainable exploitation.

<< Results >>

The following outputs and results were obtained: 
- Co-Created Methodological Guide (I.O.1) in 6 languages 
- Training Materials (I.O.2) in 6 languages
- Designed Practical Training Activities (I.O.3) in 6 languages
- Handbook for trainers in 6 languages (I.O.2)
- E-Training Platform (I.O.4) in 6 languages including a manual for the e-training platform usage
- 7 ERMAT SUPPORT UNITS in the members of the Consortium in order to ensure the sustainable exploitation of the project 
- Direct involvement of end-users in 3 sessions (127, 117, 130)
- Implementation of Multiplier Events in 6 countries (142 stakeholders)
- 3 transnational meetings 
- Dissemination plan and dissemination actions: leaflet in 6 languages, project website, advertisement materials (pens with the web address of the project), social media, participation to fairs, conferences, workshops, ERASMUS+ events, press releases, etc
- 1 scientific-technical article accepted for publication in the EDULEARN 2022 proceedings. EDULEARN22, the 14th annual International Conference on Education and New Learning Technologies will be held in Palma de Mallorca (Spain) on the 4th, 5th and 6th of July, 2022.
- Project risk management plan 
- Quality assurance plan

2019-1-RS01-KA204-000793.title: Community Mental Health practices in ex Yugoslavia
2019-1-RS01-KA204-000793.summary:
<< Background >>

Main motive was the need to improve community mental health services in the region of ex- Yugoslavia, provide better quality care and structured educational program that supports it. In this region, mental health problems are rather common, considering the recent history and the traumatic experiences related to years of violence, poverty and isolation. There is a great stigma surrounding mental health and the predominant psychiatric treatment is medical with little or no psycho-social support. After receiving the diagnoses, people are mostly rejected by the society, left completely in the mercy of the psychiatric system. The lack of community services is mostly noticed once these people are being released from the hospital- no adequate support, lack of structured programs, almost no collaboration between the system, CSOs and user led organizations. Partner organizations from the region (the West Balkan Hearing Voices Network) came to the idea to develop structured educational program tailored to fulfill the needs of each organization improving the existing practices in the field. The 5.partner- Met Ggz from the Netherlands had the role of a tutor and supervisor delivering the training, implementing their good practice.

<< Objectives >>

Main objective of this project was to bring the Community Psychiatry practice from the Netherlands to the region of ex-Yugoslavia, strengthen the West Balkan Network through strategic partnership between its representatives, ensuring stable financing for a common exchange program, educational and dissemination activities and regular meetings of the Network by enabling all partners to develop their practice, strengthen collaboration on the regional level, as well as with local Governments, institutions and improve educational programs on a regional level. First specific objective was to empower team members and psychiatric care users (experts by experience) through structured training and regular meetings with peers from other countries, especially considering the fact that the practice in the Netherlands is on a much higher stage of development, with more possibilities for embracing good human rights based European practices. Second specific objective was to improve the quality of service delivery, improving the work of all partners and creating conditions for further development of Community psychiatry in the region. And the last objective was to raise awareness on this subject through dissemination activities and publications.

<< Implementation >>

A- PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION ACTIVITIES
A1 – General project coordination
A2 - Country coordinator meetings
A3 – Monitoring and evaluation
A4 –Preparation of promotional material- leaflets
A5 – Dissemination of promotional material
A6 – Dissemination in AV mass media- video interviews and social media
A7 – Publication and promotion of the book "Our practice- mental health community services"
A8 - Public events
C - LEARNING/TEACHING/TRAINING ACTIVITIES
C1 - Short-term joint staff training event Belgrade, November 2021. (face to face)
C2- Short-term joint staff training event Rijeka, October 2020. (online)
C3- Short-term joint staff training event Ljubljana, February 2020. (face to face)
C4- Short-term joint staff training event Sarajevo, March 2021. (online)
M - TRANSNATIONAL PROJECT MEETINGS

<< Background >>

Prijavili smo se na projekat da bismo ukazali na potrebe prosvetnih radnika/ca da se aktivno uključe u kreiranje inovativnih oblika i kreiranju politika stručnog usavravanja i celoživotnog učenja.   Razmišljanja o ovoj temi nastala su na osnovu iskaza učesnika obuka, koje su organizacije realizovale, a koji se odnose na inovacije u stručnom usavršavanju. Krenuli smo od ispitivanaj potreba, utvrđivanju sličnosti i razlike u dostignutom nivou stručnog usavršavanja u zemljama učesnicama u projektu, predložili koji su to inovativni oblici stručnog usavršavanja koji se mogu realizovati u sve tri zemlje, kao i definisali načine na koji bi donosioci odluka uključivali prosvetne radnike u kreiranju politika stručnog usavršavanja. Usmeravanje ka mogućem rešenju uočenog stanja smo pronašli u javnom zagovaranju I na osnovu rezultata projekta. Pokazatelj opravdanosti izbora teme kojom smo se bavili jesu i pisma podrške sa pozicije zainteresovanih strana koje smo dobili od resornih ministarstava u sve tri zemlje, učešćem njihovih predstavnika na pojedinim aktivnostima (od okruglih stolova, preko radionica do konferencije), značajna medijska zastupljenost u štampanim i elekronskim medijima u sve tri zemlje.
