2020-1-CZ01-KA204-078214.title: Boosting positive narrative on Romani integration through Arts
2020-1-CZ01-KA204-078214.summary:
<< Background >>

Roma is Europe’s largest minority, with an estimated population of 10 -12 million and they have been present since around 1,000 years ago. Thus, they are part and add value to our Cultural European diversity. However, Roma community has been portraited mostly with negative aspects that make it difficult for Society at large to recognize them as part of our EU heritage. This since they have had a small representation by themselves in the framework of the agenda for cultural diversity and intercultural dialogue. The PAL ART project aims to support and  empower Romani community to uptake an active role in their POSITIVE image across EU, examine and moderate different art methods and techniques to support social tolerance practices and inclusive adult education for Romani community in different artistic fields and incorporate Roma artistic expression in the framework of mainstream EU cultural agenda (in national, regional and local cultural activities).The art expression and learning through art are innovative techniques, which were never used to present Romani culture and identity, and this was the main challenge but also innovation of the current initiative.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project PAL ART were linked to supporting Romani in Czech Republic, Bulgaria, Greece, Croatia, Belgium and France to portrait their positive narrative and enhance their EU integration by empowering their creativity in different art fields. This was achieved by completing the specific objectives of the project:
•	To examine and moderate different art methods and techniques to support social tolerance practices and inclusive adult education for Romani community in different artistic fields.
•	To empower Romani community to uptake an active role in their POSITIVE image across EU.
•	To incorporate Roma artistic expression in the framework of mainstream EU cultural agenda (representation in national, regional, and local cultural activities)
•	To enhance the role of the art teachers in the process of social incorporation and involved them in tailor-made approach for intercultural education and upskilling of their communication competencies 
•	To elaborate an innovative training materials and curriculum plans linked to six different art techniques 
•	To pilot the art techniques trainings using the methodology of ‘learning though art’ at local and international level

<< Implementation >>

The project PAL ART had created, piloted, and implemented numerous of activities linked to enhancement of the positive narrative linked to the Romani culture in art in the partners’ countries and among the project partners.  It started with the creation of the Guide for positive narrative on Romani integration through Arts (IO1), aiming to introduce methodologies combining social tolerance practices with Art techniques for achievement of positive narrative for Roma people in Europe. At second stage was elaborated the innovative Facilitator Programme for working in Romani integration through arts (IO2), an art integrated learning curriculum presenting 6 different art techniques and planning the implementation of each one of them using innovative teaching-learning model which is based on the ‘learning through arts' and enhance of the positive narrative in the field of Romani integration and presented in PAL Art MOOC (IO3).  Each partner had created separated curriculums linked to each art techniques and pilot those during the PAL Art Labs (PAL´s) (IO4) and present the final art creations during the PAL´s Exhibitions locally.  Two international training events linked to the official introduction and piloting of IO1 and IO2 was organized.

<< Results >>

•Guide for positive narrative on Romani integration through Arts (IO1),  6 modules and assessed by 122 experts and created as a result of review on 60 articles, 6 countries’ fiches (109 pages), 10 focus groups and 1 digital international event with 51 participants. 
•Facilitator Programme for working in Romani integration through arts (IO2) consisted of training plan and materials of 6 PAL´s pilot International training and PAL Art Labs
•PAL Art MOOC (IO3) and project website assessed internally among 47 experts and had 3851 views from the partners’ countries and currently have been enrolled about 79 experts in the six modules with 40 hours duration each. 
•6 PAL Art Labs (PAL´s) (IO4) linked to 40-hours training of 114 learners supported by 18 trainers-learners and 15 Romani educators, social workers or artist supporting the activities, 70 training lessons and 240 hours of training
•6 PAL´s Exhibitions to disseminate the positive narrative of Romani art works among 220 stakeholders, artists and social workers and to exhibit the art works.
•C1 PAL Art Capacity development (29-30.03.2021) with 51 Trainers and learners and C2 PAL´s pilot International training (09-13.05.2022)  in Zagreb, Croatia with 19 trainers and learners

2020-1-DE02-KA204-007391.title: COMPASS: enhancing motivation of older learners to learn through cultural materials
2020-1-DE02-KA204-007391.summary:
<< Background >>

The project focused on expanding the professional skills of adult educators who teach older learners. The goal was to promote the linguistic skills of older individuals, support their social integration, and strengthen their participation in lifelong learning. The approach was based on the value of European culture as a source of motivation.

Project participants had observed that older adults exhibited some reluctance to engage in lifelong learning and social initiatives. Despite the EU's promotion of multilingualism, specific measures for older people were lacking. The qualification of educators working with older individuals was considered crucial, with cultural narratives intended to enhance motivation.

The project responded to the recommendations of the Council for the promotion of foreign language learning. Offers were designed to cater to their needs, such as being locally accessible and using familiar learning materials.

The overarching goal of the project was to improve the access of older individuals to lifelong learning by complementing traditional methods with online available training materials.

<< Objectives >>

The COMPASS project aimed to motivate older learners to actively participate in lifelong learning, particularly in the field of foreign languages combined with cultural heritage and innovative digital learning methods. To enhance the motivation of older individuals to improve their language skills, educators were to be equipped with targeted techniques, with a focus on engaging older learners who view cultural heritage as a valuable asset. This was to be achieved through the creation of educational materials that improve the teaching skills of adult educators and promote the learning motivation of older individuals. Practical ideas for Content Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) activities, an online course to foster cultural narratives, easily accessible teaching materials for language learning, and a virtual cultural route for older learners were key aspects. Implementation involved the development of a toolbank for adult educators, the execution of an online course, the facilitation of informal study groups of older learners in creating digital books, and the formulation of virtual routes based on the project's outcomes.

<< Implementation >>

A tool bank for adult educators, comprising tools, techniques, and strategies, was developed to work with adults aged 50 and above in the field of foreign language learning with a cultural focus.
    An open educational platform was designed and developed.
    Methodology and teaching materials for a blended course for adult educators, as well as the face-to-face training activity for adult educators, were developed. This course is available in multiple languages. It was tested and further developed during a face-to-face training activity for adult educators in July 2022, with the participation of 18 educators.
    In partner countries, 6 groups of seniors were formed to develop materials for the digital book.
    Virtual cultural routes in each country, targeting older learners, were developed and translated into all project partner languages. The approach was expanded by providing guidelines for educators to create their own routes.
    5 transnational meetings were conducted.
    5 multiplier events involving a total of 193 participants were held.

<< Results >>

As part of the project, four Intellectual Outputs were developed:

IO1: An open platform with a tool bank for adult educators was created: http://www.eucompass.eu/en/

IO2: A blended-learning course titled "Cultural Narratives as a motivational trigger for learning in older learners" for adult educators was developed and tested. The Blended Learning course consists of a total of 6 modules and is available in 7 language versions.

IO3: A digital book titled "COMPASS: Constructing Identity through Cultural memory" was developed with easily accessible teaching/learning material for foreign language learning targeting older learners. It comprises 56 pages and is available in 7 different language versions.

IO4: A virtual Geocaching cultural route with quiz questions was developed, catering to both older learners and educators. The routes can be obtained locally from the contacts and tested in person. Educators also receive detailed instructions on how to create and incorporate their own routes into their teaching.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2020-1-DE02-KA204-007452.title: SUPPORTING PARENTS TO DEAL WITH THE EXCESSIVE ONLINE TIME AND HABITS OF THEIR CHILDREN: A PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION PROGRAMME FOR ALL
2020-1-DE02-KA204-007452.summary:
<< Background >>

The 21st century, also known as the “digital age”, is characterized by increasing internet use. However, criticism of the harmful effects of the Internet has increased. In the meantime, the public discourse is also about the effects of excessive Internet use. The spectrum of problematic behavior in this context is far-reaching. A recent study in 10 EU countries found an overall prevalence of problematic internet use of 4.4% (Durkee et al. 2015). The research suggests that specific family influences, such as the quality and closeness of parent-child relationships, may be a critical set of factors that contribute to a child or adolescent developing patterns of abusive behavior when using the Internet. As a result, many parents and caregivers may feel powerless when faced with the increasing dangers of excessive internet use. Therefore, the STEPin project is about supporting parents and guardians to become role models for their children to use online time constructively and meaningfully while promoting the well-being of their children and families.

<< Objectives >>

The STEPin project has compiled a record of current efforts to deal with internet abuse behavior and implemented a range of measures to counteract this behavior. The aim of these measures was to promote rational, comprehensible and psychologically and socially non-harmful Internet use. In order to promote interpersonal networking, the participants also had the opportunity to meet the local project participants and representatives, such as other parents, educators and local trainers, to interact with them and share their experiences to increase their shared understanding of how to confront or even manage the problem of abusive internet behavior. Motivational activities were organized to encourage parents to first reflect on their habits by reducing their screen time and then to assess and learn how to deal with their children's online behavior.
The transnational nature of the project has produced valuable tools that are transferrable to other EU contexts with minor modifications and additional benefits.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, numerous events were implemented following the work on the material. During these events, the contents of the project were presented and the activities contained therein were carried out. The participants used the contents of the platform and the ToolKit, such as the modules or the assessment tool.
Various measures were taken to disseminate the products and results of the project, including the distribution of newsletters, articles, flyers and posters. The social media presence extended across the platforms Facebook and Instagram to ensure a broad reach for the project.
Multiplier events were also held in five countries to disseminate the information. A total of 10 MEs with a total of around 220 participants took place in the period from March 17th to June 29th, 2023.
18 people took part in the “C1”, including the members of the consortium, parents and adult images as well as other relevant stakeholders. Through this training, the participants of the target group were stimulated to think about their habits in dealing with children's internet behavior.

<< Results >>

A competency framework was developed as part of IO1. This includes a monitoring report, which in turn includes a comparative index, an interactive mapping tool and national reports and a comparative international report.
An important part of IO2 and IO3 is the STEPin platform. It contains all the essential materials that were developed over the course of the project. This also includes the Assessment Tool and the Parental Educational Pack, which provides the most important information on dealing with Internet Abusive Behavior (IAB) within five modules as a Parental Educational Pack. The assessment tool enables users to evaluate internet and screen behavior. The platform also offers the possibility of networking within the target group. In addition, a badge system was developed, which is awarded to participants upon successful completion of the modules. In addition, the upskilling training program was developed as part of IO3 to further advance the project. IO4 included the creation of a ToolKit and a Motivational Strategy as advice on how to deal with internet and screen abuse.

2020-1-DE02-KA204-007552.title: Online Learning Platform against online Hate
2020-1-DE02-KA204-007552.summary:
<< Background >>

Online Hate is a still growing problem in Europe. Education must contribute to fight it, to empower the people targeted by hate. Educators must build competences for hate free communication of users, moderators and owners of net-communities. Civil Courage needs online-skills.
Unfortunately educators in adult education and other pedagoges are overwhelmed too. Existing educational materials and support exist to some extent, but Victims of online hate and/or people interested to fight it have a hard time to find them, as many ressources from short time projects are no longer updated nor optimized for search engines.
Civil Courage to stop online hate cannot be learned cognitively alone, but must be practically trained in realistic and safer training space. Therefore the LOVE-Storm Online Training Room (OTR) will be shared with educators in Italy, Slovakia, Croatia, Germany and all over Europe. The educational concepts for online role plays against online hate will be further developed, documented and disseminated.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted “to tackle hate speech online trough an innovative, open and inclusive Online-Learning Platform (OLP) aimed to train social competences of adult learners to defend free speech and civic participation online”
This Online Learning Platform should allow people who are targeted by online hate and others who want to fight online hate (Learners) to train Civil Courage to defend and stop hate attacks online. This Online Learning platform should fulfill three functions:
1.) The proven and award-winning online training room for civil courage should be improved and released for Europe-wide use to enable educators to run online role games against hatred on the Internet.
2.) Those affected and interested (learners) should find first aid and information in order to be able to react competently to hate online.
3.) Trainers and other “educators” should receive assistance and materials for carrying out online role-playing games and other educational methods against online hate.

<< Implementation >>

A complete project development cycle was carried out to create the online learning platform. The focus was on three multi-day LTTAs: Design Thinking Workshop (virtual 2020), Training for Trainers (HR 2021), Refining (2022, IT). In addition, the partners implemented the development of the learning platform in three main areas (online training room, knowledge platform/multilingual website, scenario editor and sharing mechanism). The software agency devlabor was commissioned with the technical implementation. 
As part of the acquisition, adaptation and further development of the LOVE-storm training approach and the use of online role-playing games against online hate, the partners conducted a total of 28 online and 30 face-to-face workshops with the OTR. 
For further dissemination, the partners in IT, HR, SK presented the online training room and the online learning platform to their national multipliers in three multiplier events each. A multiplyer event for INACH members took place at an international level. In addition, the OLP/OTR were presented to the (professional) public in 37 media reports, numerous social media posts and specialist newsletters as well as 35 conferences/specialist meetings.

<< Results >>

1.) The online training room (OTR) from LOVE-Storm.de has been revised and can now be used throughout Europe to carry out safe and realistic online role games against hatred on the internet. These can be used as webinars as well as in face-to-face settings.
2.) A five-language online learning platform (OLP) was created and optimized for search engines, on which those affected and interested (learners) can find and apply information on how to deal with online hate .
3.) Educators can access a variety of open teaching resources in five languages (English, Slovak, Italian, Croatian & German) - including the training guide and many scenarios - in order to use the online role play space effectively and safely.
3a) A scenario editor allows trainers to adapt scenarios to their needs and create new scenarios. These can be published and used by others.
4.) In SK,HR,IT, 36-48 educators were instructed in the use of the online role play room and over 300 new trainers were registered (950 in total).
5.) The training approach has been scientifically evaluated as generally effective. Preliminary results were published in Cooperazione educativa. Further publications and conference contributions are forthcoming.

2020-1-DE02-KA204-007610.title:
The Art to Dance Community - an African Way of
European Inclusion
2020-1-DE02-KA204-007610.summary:
<< Background >>

Wir wollten vertieft der Frage nachgehen, wie man am besten Tanz unterrichtet, wenn verschiedene Kulturen und Nationalitäten auf dem Tanzparkett aufeinandertreffen: Wie können verschiedene Sprachen zusammen tanzen? Wie schafft man es, dass sich Menschen diverser kultureller Identitäten und sozialer Herkünfte sich durch das gemeinsame Tanzen als Gruppe fühlen und Zusammenhalt entsteht? Um diese Fragen zu erforschen und entsprechende geeignete Formate für den transkulturellen Tanzunterricht zu entwickeln, hat sich das Konsortium mit Partnern aus Deutschland, Portugal, Frankreich und Kroatien bzw. später Nord-Mazedonien gebildet, das Expertisen aus den Bereichen Tanz, Tanzpädagogik, Gestalttherapie und Sozialarbeit vereint. Bereits auf nationaler Ebene sehen sich alle Partner mit Herausforderungen der Transkulturalität konfrontiert und wie sie mit ihren Angebote darauf am besten reagieren und sich weiterentwickeln. Im internationalen Austausch der Projektpartner sollten gemeinsame Probleme, Lösungsansätze und pädagogische Leitlinien behandelt werden, damit Tanz nicht einfach nur (Frontal-)Unterricht ist, sondern eine gelebte "Kunst, Gemeinschaft zu tanzen" mit tatsächlicher gesellschaftlicher Relevanz.

<< Objectives >>

1. Internationaler Erfahrungsaustausch und Förderung von Kollegialität von Kulturschaffenden im Bereich Tanz & Musik (-pädagogik) über Grenzen hinweg
2. Bündelung guter Praxis und Entwicklung geeigneter interaktiver Formate für eine transkulturelle Tanzpädagogik basierend auf afrikanischen Tanzformen und -prinzipien, die für eine Zielgruppe mit diversen kulturellen Identitäten und entsprechenden unterschiedlichen Benachteiligungen zugänglich ist. 
3. Kompetenzerweiterung der teilnehmenden (Tanz-) Pädagog:innen für die eigene künstlerische Praxis und Lehrpraxis, um die innovativen Formate in ihren Organisationen und Ländern langfristig anzubieten und im Praxisalltag weiterzuentwickeln
4. Aufbau einer Netzwerkplattform und langfristiger Austausch zu transkultureller Tanzpädagogik in Europa und darüber hinaus

<< Implementation >>

Im Rahmen des Projekts haben wir 3 Mitarbeiterschulungen und 3 transnationale Projekttreffen (plus ein virtuelles Projekttreffen) durchgeführt. Aufgrund von Corona-Beschränkungen war die erste Mitarbeiterschulung auf den internen Austausch- und Entwicklungsprozess konzentriert. In den beiden darauffolgenden Mitarbeiterschulungen konnten jeweils frei zugängliche transkulturelle Tanzworkshops mit Livemusik mit Lehrenden aller Projektpartner sowie eine im Laufe des Projekts eigens entwickelte interaktive, partizipative Tanzperformance für lokales Publikum angeboten werden. Inhaltlich hat das Konsortium pädagogische Leitlinien und Formate für eine Tanzpädagogik entwickelt, die sich über das Label "Afrikanischer Tanz" hinaus auf Basis der beiden Modelle von Ritual und Gruppenbildung als transkulturelle Methodik auszeichnen. Diese Prinzipien, Gemeinschaft zu tanzen, wurden über die Tanzperformances mit Livemusik und die Tanzworkshop-Formate für Menschen mit diversen kulturellen Identitäten zugänglich und erfahrbar. Begleitend dazu lief der Produktionsprozess der Projektergebnisse des Methodenhandbuchs und der Video-Toolbox, um das Erarbeitete festzuhalten und anderen zugänglich zu machen.

<< Results >>

Als konkrete Projektergebnisse wurde ein praxisorientiertes "The Art to Dance Community" Methodenhandbuch (PDF) sowie eine begleitende Video-Toolbox (auf YouTube) produziert, womit die erarbeiteten pädagogischen Leitlinien und Formate für interessierte Tanzpädagog:innen und andere Interessierte im kulturellen Bildungsbereich in Europa zugänglich gemacht wurden. 

Darüberhinaus wurden zwei Projektvideos der Mitarbeiterschulungen in Portugal und Hamburg produziert, die eindrucksvolle behind the scenes Einblicke in den Projektprozess geben und das Methodenhandbuch und die Video-Toolbox ergänzen und nahbar machen. Beide Videos sind ebenfalls auf YouTube. 

Ein weiteres Projektergebnis ist die partizipative Tanzperformance mit Livemusik als Konzept und erprobtes Kunstwerk, das mit einer eigenen Choreographie, einem tanzpädagogischen Anleitung und eigens komponierter Musik aufwartet und "The Art to Dance Community" lebendig, cool und ansprechend für ein diverses Publikum macht und die normalen Vorstellungen von Tanzunterricht sprengt.

2020-1-DE02-KA204-007671.title: KAUZ - Werkstatt für Klima, Arbeit und Zukunft
2020-1-DE02-KA204-007671.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project to address the urgent need for transformative change in response to the global sustainability and climate crisis. The ecological limits of our planet demand a shift in our mode of living. The COVID-19 pandemic underscored the flaws in our current economic system and the necessity of reevaluating our development model. To achieve a sustainable and democratic future for the EU, active citizen involvement is essential. However, distractions such as performance pressure, stress, and over-consumerism often divert citizens from focusing on solutions, leading to nationalism, extremism, and further ecological destruction. That’s why our project aimed to inform and engage the public, enabling them to make fact-based decisions and embrace the necessary political, societal, and behavioral changes outlined in the European Green Deal. This project identified the need to incite moments of realization that systemic demands are flawed rather than individual capabilities. We sought to promote the concepts of a Just Transition and the Imperial Mode of Living and present alternatives based on the value of solidarity through our educational package.

<< Objectives >>

In this project, we addressed the following five objectives:

Objective 1 was to compile a high-quality blended educational package on the imperial and solidary mode of living and Just Transition to promote active citizenship. The educational package consists of four major outputs: IO1 Workshop programs, IO2 Microlearnings, IO3 Videos, and IO4 Podcasts. 
Objective 2 was to establish a website as a platform for the education package; digital outputs are directly usable online, and the offline materials can be downloaded there. 
Objective 3 was to establish a database of institutions/ organisations/ networks/ dedicated individual multipliers that can be approached to hold workshops and disseminate the educational package. 
Objective 4 was to find a sustainable source of financing to conduct the workshops and produce more microlearnings, videos and podcasts after the project's lifetime to guarantee the sustainability of the project’s outcomes. 
Objective 5 was to attract attention and interest in other countries and establish a plan for involving them in the future.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were implemented in the course of the KAUZ project:

- Conducting nearly 40 test runs of the workshop concepts in all four partner countries, thereby promoting the project and gathering valuable feedback that allowed for continuous improvement.
- Establishment of the KAUZ Youtube Channel as well as the KAUZ Podcast and steadily creating a network of followers to engage with learners in the digital sphere and increase the outreach of the project
- Creation of the KAUZ social media channels to increase the reach of the project and disseminate the project's outputs
- Organizing four multiplier events to attract the interest of multipliers on the final outputs in all partner countries
- organizing two LTTAs for intense feedback on the outputs and dissemination of the material within our organisations
- Conducting six transnational project meetings, with four of them being in-person, two online in addition to several online update project meetings in between
- Various dissemination activities, e.g. presentation to stakeholders, attending networking events, internet-based activities

<< Results >>

The following results were produced in the course of the KAUZ project:

- Establishment of the KAUZ Website as an accessible information and material hub
- Creating four self-explanatory open-source workshop concepts in four languages that can be utilized by multipliers from diverse backgrounds.
- Developing 100 microlearnings, which were published on various social media channels in all four partner countries, primarily on Instagram and Facebook
- Producing four animated explanatory videos and four expert interview videos, which resulted in more than 2,800 related social media interactions.
- Production of 26 podcast episodes ranging from 30 to 90 minutes in length in four languages, which have been downloaded or streamed more than 3,000 times in total.
- Creating a database comprising nearly 200 multipliers from all partner countries.
- Compiling a future plan and activities to ensure the long-term impact of the project, including the submission of an application for a follow-up project.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-DE02-KA204-007675.title: Integrated digital Training in Emergency Management
2020-1-DE02-KA204-007675.summary:
<< Background >>

In large-scale disasters, e.g. if evacuation and temporary shelters are necessary, people who rely on social services in their daily lives will often be left without them.
It is important to train volunteers in working with and better meeting the support needs of such target groups. I_TEM focused children, multicultural groups, persons with disability and elderly people. 
This issue cannot be solved by civil protection organisations alone. Integration of social service providers into the process, and enabling social service experts to become active in emergencies, is necessary for the best possible outcome. This involvement of social services was a gap in earlier attempts to solve this challenge.
In I_TEM, civil protection and social services worked directly together.

The second challenge is that civil protection training methods are usually in presence without making use of digital training opportunities.
Prompted by the Covid-19 pandemic, but also out of a sense that digital elements can improve education and training regardless of the acute urgency at the time, the training concept that was developed in I_TEM uses blended learning - it utilizes e-learning to make the most of the strengths of offline and online instruction.

<< Objectives >>

I_TEM’s objective was to introduce blended learning into civil protection training on a pilot basis – to prove that it is not only possible but can be beneficial to move part of a course into an online space. This does not necessarily mean to replace important lessons only learned in-presence, but can also mean that more valuable classroom time can be used for engaging, interactive teaching methods instead of conveying information that could just as well have been an online self-study task.

The second objective was a contribution to bridging the sectors of civil protection and social services. The joint development and conduction of pilot trainings has the potential to ultimately improve the situation of certain target groups (“vulnerable groups”) in emergencies. The goal is to have trained volunteers that are well prepared to meet the support needs of the target groups focused in the project: Children, multicultural groups, elderly people and people with disabilities. Contrary to earlier attempts and first steps done in this area, we consider it important to develop such a training together with civil protection and social service providers, with the potential of increasing voluntary engagement among social service experts.

<< Implementation >>

The project conducted a series of transnational project meetings that, first of all, reviewed existing material, updated and amended it, and discussed options as to which parts may be suitable for the online part of blended learning and which should clearly remain in-presence. This led up to a first pilot training with participants from both civil protection and social services. This first pilot training focused on only two of the four target groups (children & multicultural groups). With the evaluation results from the pilot training, another preparatory project meeting planned a second pilot training which focused on the remaining two groups (elderly people and people with disabilities). The trainings each were integrated with study visits to relevant stakeholders (a civil protection authority operations centre, and a disabled persons’ organisation)
The second training was also evaluated and, with the collected information and experience from the trainings, I_TEM created a blended learning training concept for civil protection and social service volunteers encompassing all four target groups and making recommendations on how to usefully integrate digital training elements.

<< Results >>

The project produced a blended learning training concept for civil protection and social service volunteers. It contains a model course to teach emergency personnel about specific support needs of the four target groups children, multicultural groups, elderly people and people with disabilities in emergency situations such as an extended stay in an emergency temporary shelter. The concept has considerations for which parts of such a training to provide online and which parts should be an in-presence experience. It also recommends numerous teaching- and training materials and exercises, many of which are provided as open educational resources.
It is a proof of concept of the usefulness of digital elements in emergency volunteer training and is also a case-in-point of the importance and productivity of the collaboration of civil protection and social services personnel in such matters.

2020-1-DE02-KA204-007706.title: Adult Basic Education Digital Literacy
2020-1-DE02-KA204-007706.summary:
<< Background >>

The quick development of digital technologies has dubious impact on the literacy educators and their students offering a great range of digital possibilities. The goal of the ABEDiLi project was to empower adult literacy educators to identify useful digital options and concepts and to incorporate them into their teaching strategies. The aim of the project was to enhance the digital skills of literacy educators, giving them the tools to transfer digital skills and confident to their learners. Literacy students are left behind because of rapid development of technologies. Across Europe 55 mln people aged from 15 to 65 (technical report PIAAC, 2013) struggle with reading and writing and are unable to be a part of Global Village. Operating instructions, product packaging and package manuals - everyday life becomes a permanent challenge without sufficient reading and writing skills. Advancing digital skills of the literacy educators will foster these skills of the people with low literacy levels to involve them into all spheres of life.

<< Objectives >>

The project ABEDiLi – Adult Basic Education Digital Literacy was aiming to enhance the digital skills of the literacy educators. ABEDiLi aimed at enabling literacy teachers and trainers to use digital media in their teaching, giving them the tools to transfer digitalisation conceptually and didactically into their classrooms. The goal of this project was to empower adult basic educators, faced with seemingly endless array of choices offered by digitalisation processes, to identify useful options and concepts and to incorporate them into basic education and media education strategies. The two subject areas, basic skills and media literacy, were linked to facilitate an innovative teaching programme, innovative methods, which will enable adult educators to effectively implement digital media in their literacy classes. Media literacy as well as basic skills content is considered equal and complementary to teaching literacy and numeracy skills within the framework of the project. ABEDiLi strived to empower the adult educators starting from the digital newcomer all the way along to digital pioneers. By enabling teachers to utilise the possibilities offered through digitalisation processes, students ultimately also benefit, as they will be able to increase their level of media literacy in a structured way.

<< Implementation >>

Calls/TMs: Monthly calls, 2 digital TMs and 3 f2f-meetings.  
Reporting: A payment scheme tied to 4 internal reporting points (templates provided by coordinator). 
Dissemination: Partners used their channels: mailing lists, newsletters, social media, etc. offline was scarce due to COVID-19.
Quality assurance under the lead of LUO. 
PM: Coordinator planned and co-ordinated all meetings, kept and updated mailing lists, checked with partners regularly, was available for questions and assistance. Partners voiced their satisfaction at 4 points using online surveys. PM and Dissemination handbooks MS Teams channel helped partners stay on top of tasks. SOOO created the project logo, templates and website. 
IO1: Creation of e-Pool in 7 languages, focus groups, localisation, updated regularly. 
IO2: Curation of VR platforms, choice of VR headsets, conception of 2 Escape Rooms (ER) for teachers and learners, piloting, writing the Guide for ERs and storyboard for the multiplier training, translation.
IO3: Primary research, secondary research, conception of 6 Modules, Guide for implementation of the training programme, powerpoints for each module.
IO4: Development of Handbook, compilation, translation.

<< Results >>

(1)Innovative electronic library of digital tools for literacy educators and students e-Pool in 7 languages. They will be supported by each partner during next two years. Everybody, who is willing to add their or any other useful tool, can fill in the form on the front page and submit it. National hosts will check and dis-approve it. (2) Two Educational Escape Rooms in Virtual Reality were created for literacy educators and students with low literacy levels. They can be played on PCs or in VR headsets. Escape room guide will lead the reader through the Escape rooms, puzzles and their solutions. There are different tips and implementation scenarios. It offers the storyboard for the Multiplier Training for ER as well. (3) Train the Trainer is a ready to use 6 module training programme for online or blended implementation by the trainers of literacy educators. There are also power point presentation for each module Two research reports how to conduct primary and secondary research for the training program for literacy educators.(4)Handbook has compiled all the advantages and challenges during the project. It is written in a plain language. It aims to empower literacy educators on their way to C2 level of digital skills (DigCompEdu).

2020-1-DE02-KA204-007719.title: Digital entrepreneurship education for adults with different abilities
2020-1-DE02-KA204-007719.summary:
<< Background >>

Lately, we are witnessing high unemployment rates, especially for adults with disabilities who have difficulties in getting jobs and gathering relevant experience for their (future) careers. Self-employment and entrepreneurship has turned out to be a valuable option for careers’ building. However, with the development of the IT sector, classic “offline” enterprises do not bring enough clients and profit and, thus, do not survive for long time. We believe that self-employment in digital entrepreneurship can reduce unemployment of adults with disabilities.
With this project, we are answering to the needs defined by institutions, as well as the needs of our educators and beneficiaries. We are promoting digital entrepreneurship of adults with disabilities and quality empowerment of our adult educators to be able to organise quality (digital) entrepreneurship education of our beneficiaries. We are producing intellectual outputs that will serve as a quality knowledge management material for education of current and future adult educators for quality empowerment and mentoring of beneficiaries for digital entrepreneurship, as well as an online (e-learning) course for direct education of adults for digital entrepreneurship start-ups.

<< Objectives >>

- Empower unemployed adults with disabilities for digital entrepreneurship start-up through development of inspiring, innovative and up-to-date handbook, as well as the online course.
- Empower our adult educators and improve knowledge management of our organisations in theory and practice for building competences of educators in digital entrepreneurship for adults with disabilities, through LTTA and innovative curriculum for educators’ training and useful toolkit with workshops for beneficiaries.
- Exchange good practices and further develop quality strategic partnership among partners from 5 European countries with different realities in regards to employment and digital entrepreneurship.

<< Implementation >>

A1 – Project Management
M1 – Kick-off meeting
O1 – Handbook “Exploring Digital Entrepreneurship for adults with different abilities”
M2 – Second meeting
O2 – Curriculum “Empowering adult educators to encourage digital entrepreneurship start-ups among adults with different abilities”
O3 – Toolkit “Mentoring and supporting adults with different abilities for digital entrepreneurship start-up”
M3 – Third meeting
O4 – E-learning course “Digital entrepreneurship start-up course for adults with different abilities”
C1 - LTTA Training of trainers
E1, E2, E3, E4, E5 – Open conferences in SE, HR, RS, IT, DE
M4 – Evaluation meeting

<< Results >>

Outputs:
-	O1 Handbook with relevant topics for start-up of digital enterprises for adults with different abilities. 
-	O2 Curriculum to organise a 7-day long training course on empowering adult educators to further develop organisational culture, mentoring and education for adults with disabilities on digital entrepreneurship start-ups. 
-	O3 Toolkit is a resource material with recommendations and workshops for adult educators to implement in their direct work with beneficiaries on their digital entrepreneurship competences development. 
-	O4 E-learning course is an innovative and up-to-date digital tool / online course for relevant topics and with tools for start-up of digital enterprises for interested individuals, beneficiaries. 

In addition:
-	14 staff / adult educators empowered for delivering trainings for other staff and educators in the topic, and in accordance with the intellectual outputs. 
-	32 multipliers from partner organisations (adult educators, volunteers and management staff) involved in testing the intellectual outputs in work with 113 beneficiaries (in average 16 per partner) 
-	191 local multipliers / adult educators participated the multiplier events in 5 countries

2020-1-DE02-KA204-007742.title: EU Networks for sustainable future
2020-1-DE02-KA204-007742.summary:
<< Background >>

European networks for sustainable future has been a project for exchange of good practice and peer to peer learning between national networks that connect sustainable communities and
community led initiatives from seven European countries. The objective of this partnership was to connect on the regional level and explore possibilities for future regional cooperation.
This connection happened in two separate and fairly diverse European regions. One regional network was created between GEN Netherlands, Oasis France and Samenhuizen from Belgium. Two organisations from Luxembourg joined this project as associate partners. Another regional network was formed between three partners located on the south eastern part of Europe: Permaculture Croatia, Felkelo Nap Hungary and Sunny Hill Slovenia. One Serbian organisation joined as an associate partner. The applicant organisation GEN Europe has 25 years tradition and connects ecovillages all around Europe, that are supported locally by their national networks who act as the link between small projects and the european network. Three partners in this project are members of this umbrella organisation while other three are complementary networks with similar values and vision for the future.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project has been to connect the national networks regionally to foster their member organisations by providing high quality trainings and mentoring programs on socio-economic, environmental and cultural topics of sustainability. Each member organisation has valuable experience and expertise in some area that can inspire others. Exchange of experience, knowledge and good practices that happened during this project mutually inspired partners to be able to offer better and more holistic support to their members.
All partners are promoting alternative lifestyles and support creation of sustainable communities that are ever more interesting models for groups of people who believe that stepping together can bring them better opportunities to conduct satisfactory life in cooperation. Although their scope of work is similar, the historical and socio-economic context of the partner organisations are different. As a consequence, their challenges call for different approaches. The levels of democracy and citizen participation in the two regions are not comparable. This diversity between partners enriched the learning experience for all partners, providing cultural insights and recognition of different realities within Europe.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities of this 2 year long project were:

2 transnational meetings
- A kick off meeting where all partners met together, exchanged experience and explored possibilities for transnational cooperation and transfer of knowledge during the project
- An evaluation meeting where assessment of the cooperation and achievement of objectives was evaluated. The next steps for the time after the project were set.

2 regional meetings, one in each region, where only regional partners and the representative of GEN Europe were present in the mentoring role. These two meetings were dedicated to the formation of the regional networks.

2 trainings for 20 participants each:
- Art of networking and regional cooperation that equipped selected participants sent by partner organisations to set solid foundations for their regional networks.
- CLIPS (Community Lead Incubator Program for Sustainability) intended for the members of the newly formed regional networks that offered tools and guidance to the community-led projects in their initial stages.

Additional activity: 
GEN-WE networking event organised around the Dutch design week in Eindhoven to create possibilities to connect with new possible projects in the WE-region

<< Results >>

The tangible results were: 
- The creation of two web pages: one for each new regional network. https://seeen.eu/ and https://weeen.eu/ 
- a joint database of existing initiatives in both regions was created and linked to the new webpages, to the webpage of GEN Europe, GEN Global and Oasis networks. The database can be seen in the Ecovillage map of both websites: https://weeen.eu/ecovillage-map/ and https://seeen.eu/ecovillage-map/ as well as in the Ecovillage directory https://weeen.eu/ecovillage-directory/ and https://seeen.eu/ecovillage-directory/. This database is linked to GEN's main website: https://ecovillage.org/ and changes in the main website will be automatically replicated in the regional websites. 

The existence of the websites and the joint database will endure beyond the scope of this project, and will serve as a platform where other National and Regional Networks can also publish and keep their Ecovillage information up to date. The outcomes of this project will therefore have a long term impact on all participating partners that will last long beyond the duration of this project, as an inspiration and example for others.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-DK01-KA204-075155.title: Digital Tools and Methods for Safe Transfer Techniques for Caregivers in Today's Health Care Sector
2020-1-DK01-KA204-075155.summary:
<< Background >>

The group of partners applied for funding of the STTech project to reduce work injuries on caregivers caused by transfers of patients with disabilities. A former project in Denmark showed the possibility of reducing work injuries with 36%. The STTech project wanted to build on this experience, go even further and develop new digital tools for teaching safe transfer techniques.

The needs for focus on caregivers work environment was well known in the partner countries. The older population is increasing, which is a global tendency and it will cause a larger number of older adults in need of assistance from a shrinking younger population. 

Analysts and governments agree that our societies will not be able to afford the current care model with the
available funding. As the population structure shifts, most European countries will face, two challenges: 
1) the cost of supporting older people will rise, and 
2) the professional caregivers will be insufficient to support those in need of help. 

This scenario clearly highlights the urgent need for solutions able to reduce costs, to lower the workload of caregivers and to offer effective assistance to older adults.

<< Objectives >>

The overall and long-term goal of the STTech project was to reduce the numbers of work injuries for caregivers related to transfer situations.
The objectives to meet this long-term goal were to:
- extent and develop the competences of educators and others who teach adult caregivers
- increase transferability from training/classroom to everyday work
- focus on the safety and rehabilitative approach for the patient/resident in transfer situations
- develop new digital tools and methods for teaching safe transfer techniques
- develop a Peer Learning model
- implement assisted living technology to reduce work injuries
- create a hosted and maintained website for free access to the developed digital tools, guidelines and interactive handbook in the project.

<< Implementation >>

The activities of the STTech project were:

•	5 planned Transnational Project Meetings, some of them were online due to Covid19 and some face-to-face. 
•	1 extra Transnational Project Meeting in Denmark, that contained a lot of “hands on” workshops using Safe Transfer Techniques.
•	5 Multiplier Events - one in each partner country, some of them were online due to Covid19 and some face-to-face. 
•	Several dissemination activities in the partner countries - workshops, summits, conferences, meetings on local, regional, and national level.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs that the STTech project produced is a co-creation of 4 outputs, which all have been published on the STTech’s website with easy and free access for everyone interested. All outputs have been translated to Croatian, Swedish, Greek, Spanish, Danish and English.

The 4 outputs are:

1.	“GUIDELINES AND TOOLKIT” which consists of recommendations for health professionals/caregivers to reduce the number of transfer related work accidents using safe transfer techniques and a collection of templates of tools, published as word documents on the website to make it easy for teachers/practitioners to adjust the tools to the context they need.

2.	“DIGITAL TOOLS” which consists of 2 digital tools created to improve the way of teaching safe transfer techniques to students/caregivers. The 2 digital tools are Virtual Reality and E-learning programs. 

3.	“INTERACTIVE HANDBOOK” and “WEB VISIT SPOT” which consists of an Interactive Handbook, presenting a Peer Learning Model. The Web Visit Spot, a communication platform for everyone interested. 

4.	“OPEN EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES” which consists of a user-friendly website containing the digital tools of the project: Guidelines, VR, E-learning and Interactive Handbook.

2020-1-EE01-KA204-078012.title: Skilled Instructional Designer in Adult Education.
2020-1-EE01-KA204-078012.summary:
<< Background >>

To highlight the main issues behind the need for the project we saw: educator’s still have problems regarding the use of equipment and ICT tools; difficulties in combining face- to-face learning and online; struggle with technical issues and with IT experts who don't understand educational dimension and learning processes; in some cases overuse of digital tools in unpurposeful ways under the pressure to use ICT which leads to unbalanced learning process. There is a shortage of people who’d support, advise and facilitate educators
with competence in andragogy as well as in using ICT in education. We saw there a great shortage of instructional designers specifically in the field of adult education. The existing curricula and training of the instructional designers focused on formal education and the principles of pedagogy. Therefore, it was important to develop a curriculum to support the competencies of instructional designers in adult education, along with pilot training (recommended e-learning environments, e-learning materials and assessments) that can provide
training for people who work or want to start working as instructional designers in the field of adult education (IDAEs).

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to achieve:
1. Better quality of adult training by using digital tools and environments.
2. Efficient and purposeful use of digital tools in the learning and teaching process in the field of adult education.
3. Digitally competent educators.
4. Cooperation between educators and instructional designers.
5. To create an opportunity for educators to become instructional designers in the field of adult education (IDAE) - a „supportive figure“, a facilitator between an adult educator and a learner.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities implemented during the project:
1. Carrying out the desktop research to profile and describe instructional designer's competencies and training needs in the field of adult education. 
2. Developing the Curriculum of IDAE (IO1)
3. Carrying out the IDAE educators training (based on DigiCompEdu, profile of IDAE, curriculum of IDAE)
4. Creating IDAE Educator’s Handbook (IO3)
5. Developing Instructional resources for IDAE training (IO2) 
6. Carrying out IDAE pilot training in each partner organization (incl. preassessment of participants).

2020-1-EL01-KA204-078922.title: English Lessons with the Use of Songs for People with Mild Cognitive Impairment
2020-1-EL01-KA204-078922.summary:
<< Background >>

Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) is considered to be the preclinical stage of dementia. People suffering from MCI need to improve their cognitive abilities (memory, attention, perception, etc.) in order to avoid the deterioration of their condition. Learning a foreign language is a good way for cognitive enhancement. However, since these people have deficits in their memory and attention abilities, it is not very easy for them to learn a foreign language through a conventional teaching method. For that reason, we should apply other, innovative approaches and methodologies that will help them to remember more easily. The use of songs in foreign language lessons is proved to be a very good technique for more effective acquisition of the language. The educational program we are going to follow uses songs as tools for a better understanding of concepts and rules of the English language and for easier memorization by people with MCI. 
Moreover, apart from cognitive deficits, these people suffer from anxiety, depression symptoms and feeling of loneliness. This program is going to improve their mood and participation in a group can increase their socialization.

<< Objectives >>

With this program, people with MCI learn English which improves their cognitive abilities. The use of songs improves their ability to remember the new language and they also have a psychological impact. We chose to teach songs that convey positive messages and calming music. As they learn the concepts with the positive messages, we expect that people with MCI start to think in a more optimistic way and control their anxiety and stress levels. Through the calming rhythm of the songs their mental health and their mood (depression symptoms) improve. Also, during this program, people with MCI socialize, feel that they belong to a group and participate in activities connected to the lessons, such as singing together, playing games connected with the songs or role playing. The feeling of loneliness in many of them has, replaced by the joy of participating in group activities and their quality of life improved.  Through the implementation of the workshops in other countries and their feedback, this project re-designed and re-developed the existing educational prototype method and it gained a European approach for future users.

<< Implementation >>

This project included 3 different outputs which included the following activities and tasks (T): 
IO1. Development of English song workshops Methodology. T.1.1 Preparation of linguistic material and lessons plan; T.1.2 Partners shared schematic approaches and agree on a complex specification for Workshops and Workshops’ Materials (changes and improvements); T.1.3 Preparation of lesson plan for each unit according to the feedback of participating organisations; T.1.5 Alzheimer Hellas gathered all the units and lesson plans and make a Methodological Guide; 
IO2. Development of Workshops. T.2.1 Train the trainer's workshop; T.2.2 Partners adapted the workshops to their national contexts; T.2.3 Implementation of Workshops; T.2.4 Report of the results of the Workshops; T.2.5 Fine-tune the workshop description and guidelines;
IO3. Co-Created Methodological Guide and Training for trainers via MOOC. T.3.1 Final Methodological Guide; T.3.2 Τechnological infrastructure and guidelines for the e-learning adapted contents; T.3.3 Development of the training contents; T. 3.4 Professionals piloted the MOOC; T. 3.5 Adjustments based on the results of O3-A4 and a final version of MOOC.

<< Results >>

IO1. A Methodological Guide (MG) describing the innovative workshops Methodology is a document that provides trainers with guidelines for teaching languages that focuses on communication in English and the preparation of the lesson plan for each lesson. This MG is accompanied by a Work-Pack for each country which contains teaching material for the learners of each country. There is also a Test-book for each country https://www.songsforcare.eu/documents/. 
IO2. The implementation of the Workshops included 86 people with MCI. They improved their cognitive abilities, psychological symptoms, socialization, and well-being, through the practice of their memory, perception, etc, learning of English vocabulary and grammar, and learning of English songs and elements of British/ American culture. The final result of this IO was the final MG.
IO3. An E-Course was developed which aims to provide participants with the knowledge and materials needed to implement English lessons with the use of songs for people with cognitive deficits. The pilot of the E-course involved 47 professionals and feedback and suggestions were provided, in order to refine the contents of the course, which is available free of charge at: https://www.songsforcare.eu/learning.

2020-1-EL01-KA204-078966.title: RECovery of Adults living with Depression and psychosis in Europe
2020-1-EL01-KA204-078966.summary:
<< Background >>

Mental illness affects around 27% of Europeans annually (European Social Work,2013).European Mental Health Action Plan (2010-2020) provides for inclusion policies at a national level encouraging policymakers to support the transition towards community-based mental health care.Council of Ministers invited the member states and the Commission to set up a cooperation process on Mental Health and Well-being, "managing the evolution of community-based and socially-inclusive approaches to mental health"(2011). Measurements through the REE tool assessed recovery in people with severe mental disorders and it has been widely accepted that the concept of recovery is a way of fulfilling and promising life and receiving increasing attention from practitioners and policy makers on mental health(Penasetal,2020). According to WHO Quality rights (2019),by increasing the protective factors related to the self-esteem of the individual,social skills,responsibility,interpersonal relationships & autonomy, recovery process is strengthened and risk factors are reduced in the course of their lives(Saxena, Jane-Llopis, Hosman, 2006). So that's the need of communities,turn society's attention to the issue of recovery of adults with depression or psychosis.

<< Objectives >>

RECADE expected to promote the empowerment of the target group furthering their social inclusion by adopting the strength-based approach that does not focus on symptoms and which emphasizes resilience and control over life’s challenges, mental health approaches that EuropeanOrganizations promote. Need of communities is to turn attention to the issue of recovery and encourage to raise awareness on recovery on adults with depression or psychosis,caregivers,professionals and services&contribute the protection of human rights as key to mental health and well-being (Keet et al, 2019).While doctors can treat an illness or symptom, only patient is responsible for his own recovery, mobilizing&building capacity for resilience&willingness to pursue wellbeing and happiness.Projects outputs aimed to promote new perceptions and focus on the meaningful autonomous and empowered lives of adults with depression or psychosis. Services,mental health professionals&people experiencing psychosis or depression consent to many scientific studies (Subandi,2023) on the definition and importance of recovery, focusing on benefits that go beyond the symptoms of the disease, thereby promoting autonomous and meaningful life in the community (Williamsetal,2015).

2020-1-EL01-KA204-078972.title: Social Impact Measurement for Civil Society Organizations
2020-1-EL01-KA204-078972.summary:
<< Background >>

The project intended to empower the operation of non-profits within Civil Society. There is a need for knowledge on the measurement of the social value and social impact of the programs, operations & organizations of the Third Sector. Funders and policymakers want to know whether their funds and policies make a difference, and CSOs have been increasingly eager to be in a position to respond to these demands. The third Sector lacks an automatic mechanism to document the benefits it generates, an array of valuation tools and measuring devices has had to be developed to accomplish this task. Systematic pieces of evidence of the impact of the Third Sector at the macro level and in relation to the sector’s supposedly distinctive functions are lacking. But to really measure impact the key is the generation of a counterfactual, or what would have happened to your beneficiaries if your program had not existed when they (hopefully) benefited from it. V This project has created tools that can enhance CSOs position and can assist them not only to become truly effective and efficient but enable them to prove it as well and have provided high-quality learning opportunities tailored to the needs of CSOs.

<< Objectives >>

During the project implementation & upon completion, the project has managed to contribute to the achievement of its objectives. Project partners have managed to create tools & an online platform that provides CSOs with knowledge, skills & competencies to deliver their work and measure their impact and an online environment where CSOs can seek guidance and get trained, building in essence a specialized community of professionals in Europe. People who work in the CSOs can utilize these project outputs in order to elevate their work in terms of measuring their activities’ impact. The created platform is available to be used to improve the learning experience of adult learners by providing high-quality learning opportunities tailored to the needs of CSOs. The project has taken into account different sectors of CSOs activities as well as different local, regional & national environments while formulating the relevant methodology, thus generating a robust tool for measuring impact, not just but primarily, for the Third Sector as it evolves across Europe as a main engine of well-being. Consequently, the project achieved to empower CSOs by enhancing their effectiveness, transparency & governance through social impact measurement methods.

2020-1-ES01-KA204-081956.title: BEING A FEMALE ENTREPRENEUR: Reimagine your Professional-self through Culture
2020-1-ES01-KA204-081956.summary:
<< Background >>

Women continue to face a number of problems, exacerbated by disadvantaged backgrounds (those from rural areas, with economic difficulties, single-parent families, etc.) For women who wish to start their own careers and create their own businesses, it is essential to find new ways to reconcile professional and personal life. The project focused on assistance for the creation and promotion of enterprises, especially enterprises in the CULTURAL and CREATIVE sectors of the European Union due to their power as economic engines. The tools developed and the knowledge acquired by the women entrepreneurs involved facilitate the creation and promotion of these enterprises and the possibility for them to expand and grow economically. All the skills and knowledge acquired through the training and workshops are intended to be recurrent at any time necessary because, for the women who will embark on the adventure of a new enterprise, all the support provided will be well received.

<< Objectives >>

The project's main objective was to provide women from disadvantaged backgrounds (living in rural areas, with economic difficulties, single mothers, etc.), who wish to establish a CULTURAL/CREATIVE ENTERPRISE, as well as aspiring or new entrepreneurs in this field and adults in general, with the appropriate support and guidance. Thus, it was intended to promote personal fulfillment during the initial stages of their entrepreneurial endeavor by improving their skills in the cultural and creative sectors using innovative approaches in training.

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the Project, the following activies were carried out: 
1) Compilation and systematization in a data base of good practice referring cultural  entreprises inside the EU. 2) Create an interactive map of cultural and creative industries in Europe. 3) Design an open educational resource to integrate all the products  4) Elaborating a methodology and a framework for the ICT tool to evaluate the (cultural)  entreprise skills 5) Develop a user guide of the ICT tool 6) Carry a study on social skills, as well as profile of the new and future culture entrepreneurs. 7) Design and development of a self-evaluation tool for social skills 8) Develop a methodology and study plan for an online course targeted to women: aspiring or  new entrepreneurs. 9) Develop contents and learning materials for the online course in English and in the languages  of the partnered countries. 10) Design an ensemble of open badges for non formal and informal validation of  entrepreneurship skills. 11) Perform a pilot test  for each Intellectual Output in the partnered countries with target participants 12) Five trasnational meetings and 6 multiplier events organised (Spain, Cyprus, Greece, Croatia,Romania and Belgium)

<< Results >>

FEMALE Entrepreneur project produced the development of four main intellectual products: 

IO1. Interactive map of cultural and creative industries in Europe: creation of an online educational platform with a database at the legislative level, standards and best practices of cultural entrepreneurship in the EU. 

IO2. ICT tool for the assessment of (cultural) entrepreneurship competencies. 

IO3. Tool for self-assessment of soft skills. 

IO4. Online course for women: aspiring or new cultural entrepreneurs.

2020-1-ES01-KA204-081996.title: BREAKING BARRIERS AND BUILDING BRIDGES (B4). STRENGTHENING ACTIVE CITIZENSHIP COMPETENCES AND CIVIC ENGAGEMENT SKILLS AMONG YOUNG ADULTS WITH INTELLECTUAL DISABILITIES
2020-1-ES01-KA204-081996.summary:
<< Background >>

Young adults with intellectual disabilities (YAID) active contributors for the common good. However, their voices have been historically silenced. This project sought to enable their civic engagement and their full participation in the social reality.
Partner have been working on programs about autonomy, independent life, and incorporation to the workforce of YAID. However, they acknowledged the need to work on global citizenship skills. They admitted the lack of time and resources to provide training and develop tools to enhance such competencies as much as other adults of their age.
The project aimed to prepare staff and YAIS for the effective participation and social commitment.
TRANSNATIONAL need of the project:
- The full social inclusion and active citizenship of adults with intellectual disabilities in Europe cannot be addressed at the national level to achieve significant results.
- The level of complexity of the topics requires skills and experiences that can only be found between excellence and resources from various organizations working together.
- The design and development of IOs to be transferable to other European organizations require incorporating different organizational and pedagogical systems.

<< Objectives >>

In the light of this context the B4 project aimed at:
GENERAL OBJECTIVE
- To raise awareness of young adults with intellectual disabilities (18 to 30) on their rights and common social issues to strengthen their active citizenship and civic engagement.
SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES
- To enable young adults with intellectual disabilities in acquiring and developing key competences and skills to strengthen their global citizenship and civic engagement in the European democratic life.
- To improve isolation of young adults with intellectual disabilities so they can take an active role in society.
- To train trainers and staff members on how to promote active citizenship and civic engagement among young adults with intellectual disabilities.
- To offer training opportunities to the above target groups by using peer group training and mentoring to enhance and support the process of social inclusion.
- To develop a set of tools and activities which will assist young adults with intellectual disability and trainers and staff members.
- To develop an international network with a view to promote lifelong learning and to improve the quality of life and effectiveness of citizenship experiences of young adults with intellectual disabilities.

<< Implementation >>

Activities implemented included: 
FOUR INTELLECTUAL OUTPUTS
IO1. Database on global citizenship and civic engagement among young adults with intellectual disabilities for EU associations/organizations with material, good practices, activities and resources.
IO2. Handbook for staff members and trainers on global citizenship and civic engagement among young adults with intellectual disabilities.
IO3. Moodle platform of the blended training for staff members and trainers: Methodology and Contents.
IO4. Toolkit for young adults with intellectual disabilities on global citizenship and civic engagement among young adults with intellectual disabilities. http://b-action.eu/
TWO LTTA one for staff and another one for young adults with intellectual disabilities:
- A hybrid LTTA aimed at staff to validate IO1 and IO2. The LTTA focused on knowledge, attitudes, skills, and strategies to gain awareness about the topic and skills to support young adult to fully participate. Prague, November 24th to 26th 2020
- A LTTA for young adults with intellectual disabilities. Turin (Italy), May 3rd to 7th 2021
SIX TRANSNATIONAL MEETINGS, three of them were celebrated in person plus three more online TM. 
A MULTIPLIER EVENT (Seville, 29th June 2022)

<< Results >>

TANGIBLE RESULTS: IOs, web, newsletters, logo, videos, and flyers.
INTANGIBLE RESULTS
YOUNG ADULTS WITH INTELLECTUAL DISABILITIES (YAID)
- Knowledge on global citizenship, their rights, and common social issues.
- Awareness of being European citizens and their understanding of their active role in the current challenges of the modern society.
- Development of key competences on civic engagement in the European democratic life.
STAFF
- Acquire pedagogical tools and strategies to promote active citizenship and civic engagement of YAID.
- Leading training sessions in their organization to share with colleagues.
PARTNERS
- Reinforce knowledge on civic engagement through the learning.
- Increase skills for cooperation and identification of new opportunities.
- Share the know-how with other partners and gain from the expertise of other partners.
- Through cooperative, flexible, and personalized learning, partners will experience a variety of methods and procedures at European level, beyond the fragmented knowledge of each of their organizations.
STAKEHOLDERS AND FUTURE USERS
- Access to new tools and skills development paths to support global citizenship and civic engagement of young adults with intellectual disabilities.

2020-1-ES01-KA204-083066.title: TRAINING PROGRAM FOR PROMOTING THE EXERCISE OF DEMOCRATIC RIGHTS OF PERSONS WITH INTELLECTUAL DISABILITIES IN THE DIGITAL SOCIETY
2020-1-ES01-KA204-083066.summary:
<< Background >>

Persons with Intellectual Disabilities (PIDs) encounter significant barriers in their efforts to access their Participation, Representation and Voting Rights;
•	Lack of Critical Thinking and Decision-Making of PID’s
•	Lack of Empowerment and Engagement of PID’s at the levels where they can be involved: Organization/Institution Level, Community Level and Political Level.
•	Lack of awareness and knowledge of Supporters (professionals, relatives) and Stakeholders (community members, Public Administration, Political Parties, polling station staff and others)
•	Lack of specific training and accessible communication methods fields for PID’s and Supporters (relatives, professionals, etc.)
•	In many countries, the Legal Framework restricts PID’S from participating in political life, including voting and candidacy processes 

The use of ICT is challenging for PID’S and a digital divide has gradually formed between them and the connected citizen.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the IDemocracy Project is to increase the competences of Persons with Intellectual Disabilities (PID’S) and their Supporters related to the exercise of democratic rights of PID’s in the Digital Society.

Specific objectives:
•	To aware this target group about their rights and motivate to exercise them.
•	To develop the Critical Thinking and Decision-Making of PID’s regarding collective issues.
•	To increase the exercise of Participation, Representation and Voting Rightsof PID’sat different levels; Organization Level, Community Levell and Political Level: 
•	To train Supporters (professionals, relatives, etc.) in how to enhance the representation, participation and voting of PID’s with full respect of their Rights. 
•	To develop digital skills in the specific framework and trends related to the exercise of democratic rights in the Digital Society, including among others, use of online participation platforms, management of digital identity, contribution to collectives’ debates, etc.
•	To strengthen the cooperation between PID’S, Supporters and other relevant society Stakeholders (Community members, Public Administration, Political Parties, polling station staff and others).

<< Implementation >>

The project started with the development of a “Participatory Design of the Training Scheme” (I.O.1) (not funded) 
•	O1-A1. Procedure for the implementation of the Participatory Design Working Sessions
•	O1-A2& O1-A3. Participatory Design Working Sessions.
•	O1-A4. Development of the Training Scheme 
IDemocracy Training Activities (IO.2) were developed addressed to TRAINERS
•	O2-A1. Design of IDemocracy Training Activities
•	O2-A2. Train the Trainer for IDemocracy Training Activities 
•	O2-A3. Translations of IDemocracy Training Activities
In parallel, the Training Materials (IO.3) were developed for TRAINEES
•	O3-A1. Development of Training Materials 
•	O3-A2. Train the Trainer for Training Materials 
•	O3-A3. Translations of Training Materials
Then, the IDemocracy Training Tool (IO.4) was developed developed
