•	O4-A2. Development of e-Training Tool 
•	O4-A3. Train the Trainer for e-Training Tool 
•	O4-A4. Translations of e-Training Tool
•	O4-A5. Validation of e-Training Tool with users on each country. 
6 NATIONAL MULTIPLIER EVENTS 
Additional Project Activities have been implemented: Project Management, Quality Assurance, Dissemination and development of the Exploitation Strategy.

<< Results >>

A “Participatory Training Scheme” (I.O.1) with the direct participation of Persons with Intellectual Disabilities (PIDs) and their Supporters (not funded).

A set of “IDemocracy Training Activities” (I.O.2) for training PIDs where they put into practice, the exercise of the participation, representation and voting rights at Organization, Community and Political Level, structured in; Digital Skills; Democratic Rights and Intellectual Disability; Engagement at Organization Level; Engagement at Community Level; Engagement at Political Level

A set of “Training Materials” (I.O.3) adapted to the learning difficulties of PIDs, according to the design of the I.O.2; Digital Skills; Democratic Rights and Intellectual Disability; Engagement at Organization Level; Engagement at Community Level; Engagement at Political Level.

A “IDemocracy e-Training Tool” (I.O.4) has been developed for supporting the participatory, experiential and digital training approach. 

IDEMOCRACY has benefited a number of persons
226 PID, Supporters and Stakeholders participated in the Participatory Working Sessions and Pilot Validation Actions 
18.500 PIDs, Supporters and Stakeholders through multiplier events and dissemination actions carried along the project

2020-1-ES01-KA204-083090.title: MEDIA, RELIABLE INFORMATION AND DEAF PEOPLE IN EUROPE 2020
2020-1-ES01-KA204-083090.summary:
<< Background >>

Access to information and communication is a right that has become evident in recent months with the pandemic and global crisis of the coronavirus, a situation in which it is essential to be informed and to know first-hand and in real time the information that They are repeated and they can affect our personal and work life and our health. That is why this project wants to influence access to that information and communication on equal terms for all of society. And this often does not happen with certain groups such as deaf and hearing-impaired people.

Promoting spaces for communication and access to information in real time in their natural language, the sign language, is the objective of this project. In addition, starring this group since what we want is for deaf people to be the protagonists of translating this information live, so it was a space for employability and development for them.

<< Objectives >>

Objectives of the project; General objectives:
a) To support to the access to information and communication for the group of deaf and hearing-impaired people.
b) Implement the figure of the deaf translator in the media.

Specific objectives:
- Analyse the needs and expectations of deaf people to the information and in the media.
- Establish the state of the art in the different states of the EU on access to information and the media.
- Analyse the media and social networks in the member states.
- Identify good practices on issues related to access to information and the media.
- Promote the figure of the deaf translator for live television programs
- Training deaf people in skills that enable them to become deaf translators in the media.
- Carry out transnational meetings with training sessions for the new figure of the deaf translator.
- Spread good practices and the state of the art through social networks, a web platform, with resources and initiatives for everyone.

<< Implementation >>

• Information and communication needs of deaf people; fighting against the fake news and the need of information for deaf people from deaf people; with a best understanding of the needs and points of view.
• Additional training for deaf and hard of hearing people; Red Bee is one (and we can say the only one) with capacity to provide special training for deaf people to be interpreter of official. We are one of the more important provider of E-learning in South Europe and the 3 Federations are 3 of the more innovative European Deaf Associations in Europe, including in training activities.
• Accessibility for deaf people; only United Kingdom has a strong and consolidate system of deaf interpreter of news and official speech for deaf people and hard of hearing people.; Lithuania, Croatia and Spain want to create similar system and try to extend it for all European countries.

<< Results >>

MEDIA ACCESSIBILITY SOLUTIONS FOR DEAF PEOPLE AND TRAINING ACTIONS FOR DEAF PEOPLE: SIGN LANGUAGE INTERPRETER

This product was an analysis of the solutions available for media accessibility in each country from a technical and operational perspective, with special focus on the solution established in the UK by Red Bee Media. It also defined the landscape in terms of sign language training and the availability of suitable candidates in each country. It included a full solution specification, technical diagrams and operational description for the sign language services currently provided by Red Bee Media for live and pre-recorded sign language interpreting and a description of recruitment and training processes. 

WEB PLATFORM AND DISSEMINATION OF THE PROJECT

The web platform was a useful tool for participants and also for other people. This Web Platform contain the audiovisual material and the recordings of the training sessions, allow professionals and other personnel from different countries to have access to the results and products of the project whose intention is to disseminate and exchange best practices. Therefore, these instruments can be useful for acquiring key skills in learning and training.

2020-1-ES01-KA204-083267.title: "FLOW: fun, learning, opportunities, well-being"
2020-1-ES01-KA204-083267.summary:
<< Background >>

This project didn`t intend to give a global answer to adult learners when they are in the learning process but to put a distinct education forward that considers learners' diversity as the fundamental goal. The needs addressed were:
For institutions: A knowledge of how to dynamize and lead groups.
-Avoid school dropout by implementing a high-quality education that creates a sense of classroom belonging.
-An education program that meets the expectations of adult learners.
-Promote employability by identifying market needs.
For adult educators: Training aimed to avoid negative situations in the teaching-learning process.
-Innovative teachers must have enough educational tools to make their classrooms a place where learners can learn and manage their emotions in order to yield effective learning outcomes.
For learners:
-Access to innovative personal and professional development. By acquiring new strategies the learners would not only reach their educational goals but also develop personal growth.
-Overcome fears and difficulties that appear in second language acquisition.
-Help bridge the digital divide so that adult learners can acquire the necessary technological skills they need to be successful in their learning processes.

<< Objectives >>

In the short term, the objectives of this project were to keep emotions under control and empower learners to communicate effectively. 
The strategies carried out were:
-Changing the symptoms: we practiced techniques such as relaxation and role-plays.
-Changing the situation: we promoted collaborative work, group dynamics, and gamification. 
In the midterm, to achieve the main goal of this project, it was necessary to provide an education based on cutting-edge programs that met adult learners´ expectations: 
-A classroom where everyone had fun and felt welcome.
-A classroom where the learner improved and felt appreciated.
-A classroom where the learner made use of ICT thus overcoming the digital divide as this was more perceptible among adult learners.
In the long term, our goal was the creation of a net as a point of reference for European teachers in adult education. The website www.ka204flow.eu is being adapted to provide information about the different trainings, and job shadowing hosted by the eight institutions. 2020-1-FI01-KA204-066636.title: DigiMentor  -  digital promotion and protection skills for Creative and Tradition industries
2020-1-FI01-KA204-066636.summary:
<< Background >>

Partners met during the TCA seminar in Tallinn 2019, and found mutual interest in addressing the needs of their own nearby communities. The main need acknowledged was the digital divide: professionals with background in the Humanities and Arts lack vital digital skills and opportunities to learn them in remote and rural areas of Europe, and in their own languages. GDPR needs to be presented to the target group.  Also, their willingness to seek formal education in digital or technology is poor, due to diverse poor expectations or experiences in the past. Mentoring has been the best way for them to enter digital skills training. Especially the digital promotion skills, to present their skills and competences, are needed in order to support the local organisations and actors also online. Several target groups’ needs were familiar to the partners: museum staff, artists and artisans, sustainable tourism actors and indigenous professionals.  Small and non-governmental cultural organisations lack public funding, and that’s why partners decided to apply.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective was innovation in training for the specified target groups; co-creation of a peer mentoring program suited for cultural professionals in rural areas, and a European network of  Open Badge certified Digimentors. Encouraging creatives to network and offer peer support to enhance more sustainable entrepreneurship, including sustainable tourism, labor market participation, skills acquisition and poverty reduction was also a goal. Partners wanted to improve the level of competences in protecting the creatives' IPR and digital content, including knowledge of GDPR, as key skills of trainers. Partners started by investigating the target groups more closely, to identify their practical needs, and succeeded in creating a bottom-up approach training program. The tailored learning content and local training succeeded in reaching cultural organisations and professionals, and the objective of creating an online peer network was achieved. The partners' European networks expanded, and the relations with local, national and European actors and authorities were strengthened.

<< Implementation >>

Starter inquiry for target groups. Graphic design guidelines, website and social media channels have been created. Online learning materials tailored to cultural actors, in digital skills and mentoring skills, have been finalized in eight languages. All dissemination materials and content in national languages has been shared in social media channels too. The Curricula for a theoretical-practical training course for digital skills and mentoring was created, keeping in mind the starter inquiry. Partners arranged an internal theoretical-practical training course to acquire Open Badge certified DigiMentors for organisations. Each organisation then arranged open training courses for external target groups’ actor-learners, mentored by DigiMentors on site and online. Stakeholder events for communicating the project to local networks were arranged by partners. Multiplier events in Finland were arranged in two parts due to the pandemic: first in 2021 and the second (main) in 2022 at the Finnish Crafts fair which is the biggest crafts fair in Europe. Eleven online progress update meetings were arranged and recorded, two transnational partner meetings arranged on site (Finland and Italy) and three LTTs on site (Norway, Croatia and Latvia).

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs are the website and other media channels, online learning platform in Moodle, printable workbooks, online learning materials and open badge certifications in eight languages (Finnish, Swedish, Norwegian, Russian, Latvian, Italian, Croatian and English), local training and mentoring and the online training activities that have created an European network of 81 certified Digimentors. The network of reliable partners has grown and exceeds the existing partner network of the Digimentor project. The project sparked more project ideas and resulted in a new project targeted for museum professionals (ArtWin). We managed to arrange very successful TM and LTT meetings that increased partner s' networks. The evaluation of there events is in evaluation report (annex).

2020-1-FR01-KA204-080320.title: Network of European Islands for the Development of Sustainable Tourism
2020-1-FR01-KA204-080320.summary:
<< Background >>

Isolation, scarcity of resources, limited space, in other words the insular character, seems to reduce the range of solutions to preserve small islands and their environment. At the same time, this feature is a strength. The islands are laboratories for sustainable development and innovative, environmental, social, legal or technical solutions. Islands share similar challenges and common solutions to ensure the sustainable management of their environment.
One of the key economic sectors on the islands is tourism. Tourism activities, levers of economic development, can, due to a lack of supervision or planning, be sources of pressure on the environment. Sustainably managed tourism can contribute to the sustainable development of islands, and draw global attention to issues of preservation and conservation.
Networking between small islands is essential, in order to reduce the isolation of these territories, enable them to identify and share sustainable solutions, and thus increase their skills and knowledge in the fields of biodiversity and sustainable tourism management. Thanks to this knowledge, managers will in turn be able to train and educate other key players, as well as local communities and visitors.

<< Objectives >>

The general objective was to meet the needs for exchanges and reinforcement of knowledge of the managers of small European islands, to initiate and promote their approaches to the preservation and sustainable management of natural resources, in a logic of strengthening cooperation and solidarity between islands in Europe.
Specific objectives:
1. Strengthen the capacities of small European islands to work in a network: This project has made it possible to create, within the SMILO network, a smaller group of site managers to transfer their know-how.
2. Strengthen technical skills in relation to biodiversity conservation and sustainable tourism.
3. Contribute to the finalise SMILO’s international strategy for the sustainable development of small islands. The project produced a set of recommendations for sustainable tourism, based on shared good practices and concrete advice resulting from the project. These conclusions feed the reflections for the criteria of the strategy.
4. Enrich the SMILO "Best Practices" platform dedicated to promoting and disseminating good practices that can be adapted to island environments and reproducible on other areas.
5. Strengthen the presence of European islands within the SMILO network

<< Implementation >>

Main activities:
Due to covid-19, no face-to-face meeting was possible during the first year of the project. To mobilize partners and train them in the challenges of sustainable tourism, a series of online events were created 
4 inter-island meetings, each three full days on the project islands:
 Day 1 Meeting of the Island Committee of the island, a shared governance body made up of key local players for the island’s sustainable development; Presentation of the project partners of their island; Presentation of the management plan of the host island; visit of the island to experience the territory and its sustainable tourism practices
 Day 2 Training sessions on specific topics related to sustainable tourism; Presentations of good practices from the hosting partner
 Day 3 Continuation of exchanges of good practices; brainstorming to help the hosting partner to find solutions to a chosen issue; drafting of the recommendations
Production of a technical note “Recommendations - Network of European Islands for the development of sustainable tourism”, which shares good practices, practical advice and knowledge discussed during the project, aimed at small European islands and beyond.

<< Results >>

A group of European island managers, within the SMILO network, was created for the long-term. It has already identified activities to continue working together for the sustainable development of their territories.

Thanks to 4 inter-island visits (representing over 20 sessions to exchange good practices, brainstorm sessions to advise local partners on concrete issues, field visits, participation to concrete actions, 6 training sessions led by experts): the technical skills of managers and members of the Island Committee in relation to biodiversity conservation and sustainable tourism have been strengthened

Participation in the project has enabled the islands of Brownsea and Mausund to create an Island Committee, a consultation body bringing together the main stakeholders to agree on a shared vision of the sustainable development of the island in the long term. Participants from each island will pursue their efforts to implement sustainable management activities through these committees

A set of recommendations helps inspire island managers to find sustainable solutions for managing tourism. A podcast “Once Upon an island – green tourism” also shares feedback from the project islands

2020-1-FR01-KA204-080552.title: Exchanging good practices for the social inclusion of people with mental health problems
2020-1-FR01-KA204-080552.summary:
<< Background >>

People with severe and persistent mental problems generally suffer from great isolation, a loss of capacity to undertake, to live in independent housing, to hold a job and to carry out the acts of daily life and often a rupture of family and social links. These effects, combined with stigmatization and, if necessary, prolonged and repeated hospitalizations in psychiatry, which are themselves a factor of social exclusion, frequently lead to the loss of housing, wandering and social exclusion. Given these figures and the proven links (cause or consequence) between mental health problems and social exclusion, it is not surprising that social inclusion is one of the European priorities. This is why the partners of the IncluPsy project decided to address the issue of social inclusion with the following question: What practices are implemented in Europe to promote the social inclusion of people living with mental problems?

<< Objectives >>

1) To develop the knowledge of each partner on practices and devices aiming to promote the recovery and social inclusion of people living with mental problems
2) To raise awareness among the various stakeholders (associations, local authorities, social, medico-social and health institutions) of the issues involved in improving the social inclusion of people living with mental problems
3) To reinforce the consideration, by professionals, volunteers and relatives/caregivers, of the experience, the word and the power to act of people living with mental health problems

2020-1-HR01-KA204-077724.title: Next-generation Assessment Tools
2020-1-HR01-KA204-077724.summary:
<< Background >>

Increasing language competences remains one of the main educational priorities in the EU for a number of reasons: enhanced mobility of individuals across EU; upskilling language competences to increase employability; strengthening European dimension through preservation of language and cultural heritage, etc.
This is why foreign languages became defined as main competences in national qualification frameworks, and language teaching became a part of the official adult education programs in many European countries (including Croatia). Language teaching begins with placement into appropriate courses based on current language competence of learners (particularly important for upskilling). Poor placement often results in low motivation for learning (with courses being too difficult or too easy), early drop-outs from educational programs and withdrawal from further language learning. While Council of Europe created a well-defined framework to define language competences (CEFR), assessment tools to determine the appropriate CEFR level in learners are outdated and often yield poor results. Therefore, we chose to address the need for modern and accurate placement tests for major European languages, to ensure proper placement in courses.

<< Objectives >>

Our main objective was to create a modern, technologically advanced and intuitive placement tests for six European languages: English, French, German, Spanish, Italian and Russian. These tests would provide language teaching institutions and teachers with a tool to quickly and accurately measure existing language competence in potential learners and enroll them into appropriate language courses for further upskilling of language competences. 
To satisfy the needs of 21st century learners (but also modern teaching organizations), tests need to be delivered digitally, available online and across all platforms (PCs, tablets, smart phones, etc). Results provided by these tests need to be aligned with the CEFR, not just the six standard levels (A1 - C2) but all possible sublevels (total 16, including B1+ and B2+, as well as low/high modules) which correspond to most educational programs found in language schools.
Ultimately, we wanted to achieve better placement into language courses, resulting in better acquisition of learning aims and outcomes and long-term upskilling of learners' language competences.

<< Implementation >>

Development activities:
- developed a task builder for creating different types of language questions (Use of Language, reading and listening comprehension) and large database of tasks for all six languages
- developed a modified version of ELO ranking system as a rating algorithm
- developed a test delivery platform
PMI activities:
- organized 5 transnational project meetings (4 live, 1 online)
- organized 1 transnational training event
- organized 4 multiplier events (one large final conference and three smaller national events)
Supporting activities:
- conducted 150+ dissemination activities to promote project and its results to all relevant stakeholders (backed by a detailed dissemination report)
- created project website, Facebook page, logo and four newsletters
- conducted a number of piloting activities and a number of related impact assessment activities (backed by a detailed impact report)
- conducted a number of quality management activities (backed by a detailed quality report)
- conducted a number of smaller meetings and training events aimed at introducing different project management tools and procedures, project monitoring and strengthening EU component through transnational collaboration

<< Results >>

1 - MAINFRAME DATABASE - a language task builder available as an online app (app.nextgenplacement.org). App allows us to create Use of Language questions of following type: multiple choice, single gap, drag and drop, single answer. We built in additional variations to each type allowing us to create 10 different styles of language questions (e.g. drag and drop can be used to create a "Form sentence using words" question or "Put word(s) in correct gap" question). We also created "instruction" interface which allows us to provide customized instructions for each question style in each of the six languages. Finally, we added the "approval" system to questions, to ensure quality management of created content. In addition, we created reading comprehension and listening type questions for evaluating additional language skills, which was not planned in the original proposal.
2 - ALGORITHM SOFTWARE - custom variation of the ELO ranking algorithm to allow determination of test-taker's CEFR level based on statistics - a unique, scientific scoring method, never used in placement tests before.
3 - ONLINE PLATFORM a test-delivery platform allowing any interested party to take the test online and receive instant results.

<< Background >>

Public libraries, adult education institutions and various associations often organise many programmes and activities aimed at sharing knowledge about media literacy, but in recent years we have been faced with a growing number of senior patrons that need help. New technologies are sometimes difficult to accept because of their novelty in general. But new technologies and the digital world can coexist with the analogue one and bring new possibilities - online reading, using new tools and digital resources, better communication and cooperation. In this context, we needed to improve the skills and competencies of the staff as well.

<< Objectives >>

With the project Thir Reading Age, we wanted to:
* increase accessibility to new communication technologies for and develop a reading culture among citizens aged 60+
* develop competencies for AE and library staff working with senior citizens so they can adapt their teaching and services to their local context and learner needs
* develop new educational material and resources aimed at activating senior citizens in the digital space

<< Implementation >>

In order to reach the designed goals, project partners successfully worked on the implementation of the following activities:
*Project management and coordination, which ensured the effective overall technical and financial implementation of the project,
*Design and implementation of the Third Reading Age curriculum aimed at the new ways of learning about online technologies and ways of reading in the digital environment (IO1),
*Design and implementation of the Third Reading Age online platform, enabling senior learners to adopt a new way of learning online (IO2),

*6 piloting activities with 84 seniors that adopted the new curriculum and the project platform as a way of learning about the digital world that surrounds them every day,
*Targeted communication and dissemination activities, through the organization of 5 multiplier events to disseminate the project achievements and to engage as many senior learners

<< Results >>

The project developed 3 Intellectual outputs with specific results:

IO1 Online Reading Curriculum for Older Adults
The Online Reading Curriculum Is aimed at facilitating, encouraging and re-thinking reading for seniors using new technologies. 

IO2 E-reading Community Portal
An open-source online learning portal featuring activities and tools in English and partner languages was created in support of piloting the Curriculum. The activities and tools on the portal are available for self-directed learning for any seniors that were not directly included in the training programme but need to develop competencies in using digital tools, participating in reading clubs, or using national e-reading resources. The portal provides a space for its users to connect at the national level and form their online discussion forums. 

IO3 Training Programme for Adult Educators and Library Staff: Senior Learner Manual
A Training Programme For Adult Educators and Library Staff was created in order to support the delivery of the developed outputs and to ensure a quality training outcome. This training programme placed a significant emphasis on working with non-traditional learning approaches with the full consent of digital media in its use.

2020-1-HR01-KA204-077749.title: „Increasing the language competences of the Roma national minority - "BETTER TOMORROW“
2020-1-HR01-KA204-077749.summary:
<< Background >>

The long-term collaboration of project partners with the Roma community has highlighted the need for the introduction of innovative educational models for Roma. This was further confirmed by a survey conducted with 85 Roma respondents and stakeholders who work with and witness the daily challenges faced by Roma individuals.
As many as 74% of the respondents considered necessary to enable learning through innovative approaches, while 78% believed that there is a need to provide language competence through a web platform that would facilitate their integration into the labor market.The research also revealed insufficient language proficiency among 88% of the respondents when it comes to filling out forms, resumes, and understanding other basic concepts necessary for labor market participation.The analysis identified a lack of multilingual teaching content in organizations that provide education to Roma communities in partner countries. This highlights the need for the development of a curriculum and an innovative web platform that would contribute to enhancing the language skills of Roma individuals.
Based on these findings, the partners have made the decision to embark on this project to address the aforementioned needs.

<< Objectives >>

Due to the inadequate educational structure and prejudices they face, Roma individuals are considered to be among the more challenging groups to employ. We have proven the lack of language competence and the expressed need for modernized language acquisition, with the aim of facilitating easier employment in the country they reside in.An innovative web platform has been developed, featuring multimedia content in three identified Roma languages, four partner languages, and English, with the purpose of enhancing accessibility.By creating this platform, we have achieved the project's goal of providing innovative methods and content for teaching Roma individuals in the area of language competence improvement.We have contributed to education at the EU level, where education is recognized as a key driver of society, innovation, and development, as stated in the EU 2020 Strategy.With developed platform and the application of technology for learning and inclusion, we have ensured new and improved practices that enable Roma to increase their competencies for accessing the labor market.This contributes to their social and economic empowerment as well as to society as a whole, by reducing the unemployment rate and decreasing marginalization.

<< Implementation >>

Main project activities: Questionnaire:defined the most suitable method for conducting the research.
Needs analysis:investigated the content requirements for the innovative web platform and the Roma languages, involving 158 Roma individuals (originally planned for 120). We developed and created:project logo and roll-up banner, partner reports, translated the report into English, including recommendations for web platform content and partner-specific details. Also, curriculum translated into 5 languages and guidelines for the target group using the web platform, educational and multimedia content, translated into Italian, Slovenian, Serbian, Croatian, English, and 3 Roma languages and web platform.
We conducted:Pilot program for 73 participants (originally planned for 50) and analyzed the results through evaluations.User training on the established language learning web platform.Training for experts, enhancing their competencies in working with Roma individuals (10 participants).We organized:4 transnational meetings, event with multiplier effect.We presented the project on national television, at conferences, in schools, through open-door events, through articles on the EPALE platform, and on social media.

<< Results >>

Main results and concrete outcomes produced by the project:
IO1: Needs analysis report and recommendations for the content of the web platform, containing a detailed analysis and the state of each country. The report was translated into partner languages as well as English and made publicly available. Recommendations/guidelines for the development of web platform content.
IO2: Innovative web platform with modules/content for language teaching aimed at Roma employment. The platform includes content in three Roma languages (Romani Chib, Sinti, and Ljimba d'Bajaš), as well as Croatian, Slovenian, Serbian, Italian, and English. It is free and user-friendly, and all PDF content can be freely downloaded. Pilot testing of the web platform was conducted in all partner countries with a sample of 73 participants.
Four transnational meetings were held, and expert training was conducted, resulting in the enhancement of key competencies for professionals involved in working with Roma individuals and current online teaching models. A multiplier event was held, with 115 participants including representatives from non-governmental and governmental organizations, associations working on Roma issues, and stakeholders in the adult education sector.

2020-1-HR01-KA204-077766.title: INACTIVITY IS NOT AN OPTION
2020-1-HR01-KA204-077766.summary:
<< Background >>

In Europe, there is a trend of rapid aging of the population and the problem of their social exclusion. When older people retire, they face many problems. They question whether the society needs them anymore. They are faced with lower incomes, which cause deprivation in material, cultural, social and every other sense. And regardless of the fact that social inclusion is encouraged by various strategies, directives and regulations, i.e. from above, most of them slowly but surely take the path of disinterest and inactivity.
It is precisely this trend of disinterest and inactivity that this project aims to significantly change, emphasizing the need to approach older people in an appropriate way, putting their desires and needs at the centre of activities, that is, to take a bottom-up approach. The wishes and needs of older people are expressed through equality and social cohesion, and active inclusion in social happenings can only be achieved through systematic training and networking.

<< Objectives >>

Project objectives are:
- develop quality innovative tools as an incentive to initiate the creation of programs for senior individuals and groups (guidelines, programs, guides...)
- contribute to a proper understanding of the EU's value system and the possibilities of senior activism
- promote the Erasmus+ program, which enables networking and brings a transnational component and new knowledge and values to people of the third age
- encourage a volunteering system based on the axis senior educator - senior volunteer - user

<< Implementation >>

2. Surveying older people with the purpose of detecting their wishes and needs,
3. Creation of guidelines for the development of intellectual outputs,
4. Development of a system of lifelong education of older people,
5. Pilot project "Close the cycle, use your potential" with the aim of verifying the correctness of the presumptions for the creation and development of the system of lifelong education of older people, of the curriculum and networking methods,

7. Collection of educational materials for teachers, senior educators and volunteers in one place
8. Pilot project "Intergenerational cooperation of professional experts" 
9. Pilot project “Social in-group learning”
10. Pilot project Evaluation of the “ToT curriculum”

12. Activities on the sustainability of project results.

2. GER-APP YouTube channel, 287 subscribers, over 38.500 views, 16 countries on 3 continents.
3. Media support: radio stations Radio FM92 and Radio Laganini Soundset – interviews, event announcements.

2020-1-HR01-KA204-077863.title: Arts of Freedom
2020-1-HR01-KA204-077863.summary:
<< Background >>

Artistic work in prison belongs to a type of work that dictates different rules and possibilities. However, before starting to paint the prison area, the artists - participants in the project are in dire need of education. Through certain forms of education, artists should understand that working in a prison requires a different approach to work than the one they are used to, but also a different approach to the people they will meet while working in that space. We find the reasons for such a belief in the experiences from previous projects. Lack of familiarity with the way of working and behavior often causes stubbornness in artists. This then results in superficiality and inappropriate works. The resistance to learn something or to apply something they are directed to, led us to think about the need to implement a project in which artists would undergo certain forms of education before working in prison. From this, the idea developed to create and publish two educational books (manuals) in which different aspects of artistic work in the prison area will be explained and presented.

<< Objectives >>

In the first book, the content of which is intended for artists who are interested in working in the prison space, we wanted to consolidate educational materials on certain "soft" skills and on ways of behaving and dealing with staff, employees of the prison system and prisoners.
The second book is intended primarily for staff employed in the prison system, but also for the general public, with the aim of raising awareness of the importance of artistic work in atypical spaces (prisons, hospitals, barracks...) and the effects of such and similar projects (therapeutic and aesthetic effects on the observer).
The reason why we felt that the publication of these books is very necessary is the experiences we gained "on the ground" during the implementation of projects in the prison area. Lack of familiarity with the way of working and behavior often causes stubbornness in artists, which then results in superficiality and inappropriate works. The resistance that prison employees know how to provide in the field is sometimes reflected in comments devaluing artistic creations. The majority of the general public also rejects such projects due to misunderstanding and lack of insight (lack of knowledge) into the positive effects of the project.

<< Implementation >>

TPM 1 - organized and implemented by HDLU (November 23, 2020) - virtual
TPM 2 - implemented by the project partner Uniwersytet Jagiellonian, Poland, with the support of the HDLU coordinator (April 6, 2021) - virtual

In addition to the videocall version, a WhatsApp group was also launched to facilitate the flow of information.

<< Results >>

The first result of the project is two books in English and all partner languages ​​(HR, PL, NL, HU)
O1 Educational book for artists:
Intended for artists who are interested in working in the prison space and through which the artists are educated about certain "soft" skills and ways of behaving and treating both the staff and employees of the prison system as well as the prisoners.
O2 Educational book for prison system staff and the general public:
It is intended primarily for staff employed in the prison system, but also for the general public. The goal of this book is to raise awareness about the importance of artistic work in atypical spaces (prisons, hospitals, barracks...) and about the effects of these and similar projects (therapeutic and aesthetic effects on the observer).

Another result of the project is artists trained to work in atypical spaces such as prisons. The education program would precede the departure of the artist to work in the prison area. Only those artists who would react positively to the results of the education will be trained to work in projects and to work in prison institutions.

The third result of the project is focused on the education and awareness of the staff employed in the prison system.

2020-1-HR01-KA204-077868.title: Inclusive education: ensuring participation of persons with disabilities in non-formal adult education
2020-1-HR01-KA204-077868.summary:
<< Background >>

People with disabilities encounter many obstacles when they want to participate in non-formal education. This type of education takes place outside the formal system, so there are no systematic support mechanisms for both participants and providers. Research has shown that only 10% of PWDs are included in adult education at the EU level. What we also know is that non-formal education providers are usually experts in the field they teach, but do not have specific didactic and methodical knowledge. In addition, working with PWDs is even more challenging because people with disabilities are very different and have their own specific requirements in the teaching process.
 With this, we wanted to strengthen the capacity of providers so that they have the knowledge and skills and resources to work with PWDs.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project was to create a model for the inclusion of PWDs in non-formal adult education. We have established a model of collaboration between key stakeholders (experts for PWDs, AT specialists and education providers) and created two informal training programs and a manual that provide key knowledge and skills for working with PWDs. The main purpose of these materials is to ensure that non-formal education providers have in one place easy to understand, clearly structured materials where they can find all important information about people with disabilities, assistive technologies, universal design and ways of working with and for PWDs.

<< Implementation >>

Through the project, we developed a Curriculum on methods and techniques for teaching PWDs, a Curriculum on the implementation of assistive technologies in adult education, and a Manual on the inclusion of PWDs in non-formal adult education. We developed all results through inclusive participatory design. We included PWD experts in the process, and through LTT events and focus groups, we ensured that the results were fully aligned with the needs of the target group, i.e. non-formal education providers.

<< Results >>

Our curricula consist of a curriculum table that describes the training program. There are also ppt presentations for trainers and scripts for participants. But all of this together can be used as self-teaching material, but also as a complete training session for each individual.The manual can be an independent educational tool, but it can serve as a source of information for trainers who want to teach according to our curricula. All materials are made in accordance with the guidelines for digital accessibility, so that they can be used by people with disabilities without difficulty. Also, all materials in eight different languages: in English and partner languages ​​(Greek,Slovenian,Slovak,German,Romanian and Croatian). They are available for download on the IEDA website and partner sites.During the duration of the project, we also created 16 articles on the Epale platform on topics related to the project. Their goal was to sensitize the target group on the importance of accessibility for PWDs.The last article contains links to download intellectual outcomes. In order to model the cooperation of key stakeholders for the inclusion of PWDs in non-formal education, we held 7 final conferences in all cities of partner organizations.

2020-1-HR01-KA204-077872.title: Creativity in Art&Design for Learners and Educators
2020-1-HR01-KA204-077872.summary:
<< Background >>

As an adult education centre that carries out numerous educational programs, we noticed that the number of elderly people participating in educational programs is extremely low. Wanting to find the cause of this, we came to the conclusion that the offer of interesting programs for seniors is very limited, but also that educators who have formal education for teaching do not possess the specific competencies necessary for quality work with seniors, and they need additional education. Accordingly, we decided to develop tools that will eliminate these problems. Through the implementation of the CrADLE project, we encouraged the development and expansion of educators' competencies so that they could provide high-quality education to participants of the creative programes over the age of 54. We enabled seniors who often feel lonely, isolated, unproductive and useless to get involved in the process of lifelong learning. The creative programs that we created with our partners will enable seniors to acquire new skills, have some fun in their free time, and to fulfill their need for learning, creating and socializing. These programs will help seniors in maintaining their psychophysical abilities and strengthening their self-confidence.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the CrADLE project was development and expansion of the competencies of educators/teachers who work with participants of creative workshops over the age of 54, with an emphasis on teaching methods and tools, and the effective use of innovative solutions. Through implementation of this project, 2 intellectual outputs were realized, as was foreseen in the project application.

The first project result - IO1 - 11 curricula for creative workshops for learners over 54 
The second project result - IO2 - manual and accompanying program for educators/teachers who work with learners over 54

Through project implementation, we wanted to strengthen the competences of educators in order to successfully carry out creative workshops intended for seniors, provide them with materials that will be practical, concrete and relevant in working with seniors. At the same time, we wanted to contribute to the quality of life of seniors, and to encourage seniors to learn and spend their free time in socializing and developing their own skills, which is why we created 11 new curricula for creative workshops intended specifically for people over the age of 54. In cooperation with project partners, we successfully achieved all desired goals.

<< Implementation >>

The following project activities were carried out:
1. Project management, administration, monitoring of project implementation
2. Design and development of intellectual outputs - 11 curricula for creative workshops for learners over the age of 54, Train the trainer manual and program for educators
3. Transnational meetings and internal meetings of the project consortium members held via Zoom
4. LTTA - C1 and C2 workshop Train the trainer
5. Dissemination activities - informing the target groups and the public about the project activities and results
6. Research on the needs and challenges of target groups in the process of learning and teaching people over the age of 54, which preceded the creation of the manual and program for educators
7. Carried out piloting of the developed program and manual for educators 
8. Internal and external evaluation of intellectual outputs
9. Evaluation of held transnational meetings, LTTA workshops and pilot program carried out in all partners' organizations
10. Multiplier events by each partner

<< Results >>

The key results we achieved through the project implementation are as follows:
1. 11 curricula for creative expression workshops
2. Manual for educators which explains the specifics and methodology of working with seniors in the field of creative expression, as well as an accompanying program for education of adult educators
3. Educated staff of project partners through LTTA
4. 30 teachers trained to work with seniors in creative expression workshops through carried out piloting
5. Transfer of knowledge and experience among project partners
6. Connecting and expanding the contacts of partner organizations
7. Informed target groups and the general public about the project and developed project results

By using the results, the educators will acquire specific competences for adequate work with seniors, which is why they will be able to better understand the needs of seniors, which is of particular importance for young educators. The educators will share the newly acquired knowledge with their colleagues. By participating in developed creative workshops, seniors will be provided with a better life quality through strengthening awareness of the importance of learning, creative expression and creation in the process of healthy aging.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-HU01-KA204-078736.title: Say no to bullying! Reducing cyber- and offline bullying amongst NEET people
2020-1-HU01-KA204-078736.summary:
<< Background >>

The Konszenzus Foundation aims to integrate and empower disadvantaged social groups. Our aim was to broaden our horizons by participating in international projects and joined the Dlearn network to expand our knowledge and contacts. The application was triggered by our previous experience of researching bullying, including workplace bullying, and the observation that bullying was prevalent in our work with marginalised groups.
The focus on cyberbullying at the beginning of the project stemmed from the realisation that online and offline bullying are interlinked and that both online and offline have an impact on victims. In addition, we recognised the need for specific strategies to address the negative impact of bullying on NEET (Not in Education, Employment, or Training) young people who face particular challenges. These young people are often overlooked by existing initiatives and the pandemic has exacerbated their vulnerability.
Adult education can be an appropriate tool to reach these young people, but specific methods and tools are needed to stop and redirect negative trends. With this, we wanted to help all professionals who have come into contact with NEET young people.

<< Objectives >>

The objective of our project was to reduce the impact and consequences of online and offline bullying at NEET by supporting adult educators, trainers, mentors, social workers and other service providers to prevent bullying, educate, identify and support victims, change bullies' behaviour patterns and activate passive witnesses.
Our goal has not changed during the implementation of the project. We have focused on indirectly supporting NEET young people through professionals because these young people are otherwise not reachable.
However, we have found that the presentation of the NEET problem needs to be given more importance than planned, as the professionals who come into contact with them do not see them as part of a specific group with a complex problem, but only as a target group for their own service.

<< Implementation >>

All the activities planned in the application have been carried out, although there are of course some discrepancies between plans and facts. These are mainly due to the pandemic, which forced us to reduce the number of meetings and participants and to change the timing of the meetings.
Activities carried out:
-	project management
-	2 face-to-face meetings and numerous online TPMs
-	4 IOs: 'Decline the gap' research, Manual for helpers of NEET-people, LME and online curriculum or helpers of NEET-people, and an educational game for NEET people in order to recognise and prevent bullying
-	4 LTTAs
-	dissemination activities according to the communication plan
-	Multiplier events
-	Quality assurance activities

<< Results >>

Our most important achievement is that the project was completed on time, all the planned activities were carried out and the products we had planned were produced. All members of the partnership stayed on board and carried out their tasks.
-	4  Intellectual Outputs ready and available 
-	IO1 final study  on the issue of bullying among or directed at young people avaiable in English, Hungarian, Italian, Croatian and Spanish languages
-	IO2 Manual for helpers avaiable in English, Hungarian, Italian, Croatian and Spanish languages
-	IO3 Learning Management Environment and curriculum for helpers working with neets about how to prevent and handle the bullying,  and how to support the victims
-	IO4 Serious game for NEET people (and helpers) on how to prevent and recognise the bullying and how to use online platforms useful
-	4  Learning / Training / Educational Activities (LTTA) implemented with 36 participants. 
-	13 multiplier events implemented with the participation of 421  persons. Metrics: agenda, attendance Dissemination plan and 2869557 reached people with 272 activities
-	2  project management meetings staged in person with 18 participants, and bimonthly online
-	sheet, summary report
-	93,4 % of the budget used
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2020-1-HU01-KA204-078833.title: Transnational Roadmap for Educators in Digital Soft Skills
2020-1-HU01-KA204-078833.summary:
<< Background >>

The TRENDSS Project was brought to life as a prompt response to the digital shift in educational paradigms generated by the pandemic in order to support educators in their digital transformation challenges, such as:  
-the psychological burden to become digital in an instant - the need for support and community
-navigate through the overwhelming list of new and constantly changing digital tools - the need for comparisons of old and new approaches, see variables and constants, options, critical thinking
-find resources and learn about new pedagogical approaches, soft skills needed for the digital classroom - need for methodological tools and soft skills development. 
The TRENDSS project also addressed the needs of digital learners and developed methodological tools that could create more engaging online lessons and support communication and the processes of motivating, testing, assessing, discussing, reflecting etc. 
The project team consists of experienced actors in adult education (trainers, teachers, coaches, teacher trainers, professors, youth workers and support staff) who experienced the digital challenges firsthand. Therefore, their needs for learning, finding solutions and collaborating transnationally were addressed too.

<< Objectives >>

TRENDSS RECOGNIZED AND ADDRESSED THE FOLLOWING CHALLENGES that put educators in a very vulnerable position:
- They had to digitalize courses, and acquire digital skills suddenly which often resulted in creating lower-quality educational programs,
- Under the pressure of instantaneous changes, the importance of applying pedagogic soft skills appropriate for digital platforms was usually overshadowed by grueling technical challenges and educators often were not aware of the new competencies.
- Unfortunately, inequalities in being digitally equipped or literate caused difficulties for both educators and learners.
BASED ON THE ABOVE, OUR OBJECTIVES were: 
- to support educators by helping develop resilience to cope with the new expectations of the rapid shift to digital instruction
- to raise awareness of soft skills in the digital space
- solutions and methodological tools to create inclusive and engaging digital classrooms,
- to provide information on potential communication styles tailored to virtual platforms, 
- to create new methodological guidelines and practical tools
- to make online education a strategic priority for educators and to establish and elaborate on some potential quality assurance and further training areas.

<< Implementation >>

In chronological order, our project implemented the following main activities:
1. Before the official launch of our project, our partnership started to form and work on our main objectives since the members were already actors in the educational context. We also started to discuss, brainstorm, and define our objectives, roles, responsibilities, and deliverables.
2. After the official launch and online kick-off meeting, the project team started to conduct research and needs analysis that helped us determine the future best outcome of the project deliverables. These activities were conducted online. Primarily, the output leaders were responsible for the research related to their assigned outputs but we helped each other with finding international samples for the research and also with interpreting the findings. 
During this phase, we also managed to agree on our project management, budget, monitoring and dissemination plans.
3. Due to travel restrictions we had to continue the collaboration on the innovation project design online. We had regular project meetings and LTT events for the partner organizations. We started to create our first versions or pilot items of our outputs (chapters, modules, videos, website, etc.) 
4. At the midterm of our project, we finally managed to meet in person for an LTT and TPM in Croatia with the entire project team, which was a perfect opportunity to get to know each other better, enhance motivation and engagement, learn about different cultures, share and exchange knowledge, do teambuilding activities, collaborate and work on output and project questions, evaluate the first output results.
5. We continued working on the outputs intensively and we also had regular online meetings with the project team for output collaboration, monitoring, project management, LTT, TPM, and ME planning purposes and dissemination activities.
6. In 2022 we had chances to arrange several in-person activities: 3 LTTs, 2TPMs, and 4 in-person MEs for over 300 participants. Besides all these, we maintained our regular online meetings and focused more on dissemination and conducted several online events, webinars, published articles, videos, social media posts and blogposts. (Our detailed dissemination log is uploaded to the FTP server.)

<< Results >>

6 OUTPUTS: 

O1 – ROADMAP – E-learning course with 9 asynchronous and interactive e-learning modules with visuals, tests, reflections, and videos to develop soft skills for digital instruction.

O2 – METHODOLOGICAL GUIDELINES – the 13 chapters of the 200-page E-book provide a theoretical framework for digital education, e.g., Course design, Assigning and creating self-study materials, Group dynamics, Motivating techniques, Facilitating online discussions.

O3 – SURVIVAL KIT IN THE DIGITAL ERA - Ebook (100 pages) toolkit for digital educators
50 practical online exercises, tips, and activities for the digital classroom containing energizers, warmers, coolers, fillers, games, 5-minute activities, lead-ins, links 

O4 – SELECTION OF POPULAR SOFTWARE FOR EDUCATORS (40 pages)
6 chapters on 6 pieces of software or apps for Social media, Storage, Process management, Video communication, Quizzes and Graphics. 

O5 – TRENDSS DIGITAL PLATFORM WITH FREE RESOURCES AND BLOGPOSTS (https://trendss.eu/) is the main repository of outputs, resources, contents and serves as a living and growing platform for dissemination, communication and reference purposes.

O6 – VIDEO TUTORIALS
10 educational videos created by a well-known Greek YouTube trainer with practical tips and tutorials on how to create engaging educational video content. (We also published 8 extra videos related to other outputs.)

We also provided online and in-person training open to the public. We organized LTT events (training for the immediate staff of the partner organizations) and 3 main multiplier conferences (in Greece and Hungary) and several online meetups to share our results with the extended target group online which created further resources.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-HU01-KA204-078834.title: Nature-Based Innovations for Urban Forest and Rainwater Management
2020-1-HU01-KA204-078834.summary:
<< Background >>

The Reflex Association and its partners in this call have been working for years on possible solutions to the problem of climate change. Our experience has shown that local communities and municipalities have a lack of knowledge in the field of nature-based solutions. Innovations and solutions related to the territory are much less known than, for example, in the field of energy management. 
The main priority of our application was the innovative settlement of biodiversity solutions, ie the horizontal Environmental and climate goals.
We wanted to create an innovative learning material for adults/stakeholders responsible for the maintenance and development of municipal biodiversity.
The participation of NGOs as partners and target groups in the tender helped with fostering civic engagement.

<< Objectives >>

The overall goal of our project was to help communities of European municipalities to prepare for climate change by sustainably maintaining and developing urban biodiversity and green spaces. 

Specific objectives of our NABI project:

O1 - Exploration and processing of Nature-Based Innovations.
O2 - Forming the key competencies of local community stakeholders. Expanding knowledge related to the field, improving skills and changing attitudes.
O3 - Improving the relationship between the partner organizations and expanding their knowledge related to the field.
O4 - Widespread dissemination of the results to ensure their sustainability.

<< Implementation >>

We worked together with the 6 partners on creating 
- 2 online learning materials with titles: 
-- 1. Inventory of nature-based innovations (in English, Hungarian, Croatian, Italian, Romanian, German languages)
-- 2. Nature-based solutions in Urban development  (in English, Hungarian, Croatian, Italian, Romanian and German languages). In accordance with the original peroposal the second learning manual was not planned in German language, but the German and Austrian partners changed their minds and translated the whole material on their own initiative for free of charge. 
- We organized 10 multiplier events in 6 countries (two-two in Hungary, Romania, Croatia, Italy, one-one in Germany and Austria); 
- attended 3 project management meetings (Pula - Croatia, Florence - Italy and Freiburg - Germany); 
attended a "Learning, Teaching and Training activity" event as capacity-building in Szeged, Hungary. 
- For the activities carried out, active media work and dissemination activities were carried out - 24 website articles, 52 social media articles, 2-2 press releases - 12 press releases (uploaded to FTP under dissemination), 5 presentations on separate (other than NABI multiplier event) events.

<< Results >>

Concrete results are the two online learning materials about Nature-based innovations.
- IO 1 - Inventory of nature-based innovations (in English, Hungarian, Croatian, Italian, Romanian, German languages) Nature Based Innovations case studies from 6 countries. 
- IO 2 -  Nature-based solutions in Urban development  (in English, Hungarian, Croatian, Italian, Romanian and German languages)
consisting of three parts: 
1. Describing the most popular and easily implementable nature-based solutions - 12 topics/methods
+ Glossary - the most commonly used terms are explained briefly in the Glossary part
2. Tools and apps are described helping in implementing certain NABIs - 13-14 tools/apps described
3. Regulation of green space management - different in each country - national regulations in an easily digestible form with concrete reference list - it is only in the national languages: Romanian, Hungarian, Italian, Croatian.

All the learning manuals are available on one bookshelf in each consortium languages (see below link) but pdf versions are also available (attached to FTP and PRP platform in pdf form):

https://fliphtml5.com/bookcase/otrtc/
topics: Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas
Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

2020-1-IE01-KA204-066023.title: Community Climate Coaches
2020-1-IE01-KA204-066023.summary:
<< Background >>

The CCC project was initiated by the Sustainable Ireland Cooperative, and the British Permaculture Association in response to the need for transformative change towards a sustainable, low-carbon future. The project aimed to address the need for innovation, good practice sharing, and training in coaching and facilitating practices for community-led climate action. 

A survey conducted during the application process revealed the specific needs of partner organisations, such as support in implementing climate action at the citizen and community level, fostering collaboration, developing a common language for environmental movements, and enhancing skills and capacity in community-led initiatives. 

The project outputs were designed to directly address these identified needs, ensuring their relevance, impact, and alignment with the target audience's requirements. The survey results provided valuable insights, allowing the project to tailor its outputs and effectively benefit the partners and their networks.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the CCC project, the primary goal was to achieve effective community climate action through the integration of facilitation and coaching thinking. The project aimed to develop a support system, tools, and training specifically tailored for community catalysts. The overarching objective was to shape a new vocation for climate activists, coaches, and facilitators within our networks. The project recognized the importance of good facilitation in driving community engagement and empowering individuals to respond to the biodiversity and climate crises. By equipping community catalysts with the necessary skills and resources, the project sought to enhance their capacity to lead and support climate action initiatives at the local level.

<< Implementation >>

During the CCC project implementation, collaborative working processes created the CCC outputs. Training sessions, workshops, and dissemination events were organised to build community climate coaches' skills and share project outcomes. 

Networking and collaboration were fostered among coaches to facilitate knowledge exchange. The project enhanced coaches' facilitation skills, shaped a new vocation, and provided resources for community-led climate action. 

Dissemination of outputs aimed to inspire and support a wider audience, contributing to the community-based climate action movement. The project's activities aimed to create a supportive ecosystem for coaches, strengthening their collective capacity to engage communities, foster resilience, and address climate challenges. 

By implementing these activities, the CCC project aimed to provide comprehensive resources and training to community climate coaches, enabling them to effectively facilitate and drive community-led climate action in their respective regions and communities.

<< Results >>

The CCC project produced several outputs and results. The Participatory Research and Mapping (IO1) led to the creation of the Regenerative Knowledge Commons, an online tool that curates information on community climate action initiatives. The Community Climate Coaches Toolkit and Resilience Pathway (IO2) provided a comprehensive collection of tools and processes for community-led climate action. The Community Climate Coach Competency Framework and Learning Pathway (IO3) identified core competencies and learning pathways for effective climate action. The Community Climate Action Good Practice Guide (IO4) presented key themes and characteristics of emergent practice. The Curriculum Development for Training for Trainers (IO5) established a blended curriculum and training resources. 

These outputs contributed to the establishment of a scalable support system for community-led climate action and enhanced the competencies of community climate coaches. The project also fostered collaboration, knowledge sharing, and a supportive community of practice among climate action practitioners. The concrete outputs and results of the CCC project provide valuable resources, training, and guidance for community climate action initiatives.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-IE01-KA204-066036.title: Adult Educators supporting Parents from the inside out
2020-1-IE01-KA204-066036.summary:
<< Background >>

Meath Partnership applied for the Inside Out project to develop resources and materials that respond to the needs of parents that we have worked with over the years through our SICAP programme and other health and wellbeing programmes. The parents we worked with highlighted time and time again the various pressures they are increasingly under eg. time pressure, financial pressure, multi-tasking, paying bills etc. and now more commonly, the constant worry that they face in respect to their children spending an increasingly worrying amount of time online. Parents, children, resource workers and educators shared the need for improved and updated resources that focus on improving communication within the more modern family structure. These resources attempted to address topics such as mental wellbeing, communication skills, social media as a social support and stress management – to name but a few. The Inside Out project addressed the need of parents that wished for more quality time with their children through the increased ability to effectively communicate.
In addition, the Inside Out project recognised the need to build the capacity of adult educators who work within the area of parenting support. The Inside Out project developed a new range of innovative training materials which were tailor made to be delivered in various contexts that educators find themselves in. The ‘train the trainer’ so to speak materials, resulted in a unique opportunity for educators to increase their resource pool and provide new, modern courses to their parent groups. 
Finally, the Inside Out project attempted to develop a highly interactive and user-friendly platform for educators and parents to use when they wish and continually engage with in the years to come. 
The Inside Out project delivered numerous trainings across Europe to ensure the materials developed addressed the initial needs of the project and to ensure educators were capable of using the materials long after the project has ended.

<< Objectives >>

The Inside Out project had three clear objectives: 
-	Support parents to invest in quality parent-child communication 
-	Build the capacity of adult educators through the appropriate in-service training and development of new training materials
-	Develop an accessible learning platform (MOOC) to host the educational material developed as part of the project

<< Implementation >>

The Inside Out consortium led by Meath Partnership and comprising of Specktrum Educational Centre Foundation (SEC), COESO, Dante, Right Challenge and ENOROS has developed, piloted and implemented a suite of resources and trainings targeted at families and adult educators. 
The following activities were implemented: 
1.	IO1 – Inside-Out Hybrid Curriculum for Parents: The consortium developed a 12-module curriculum with complementary videos. This curriculum was developed in all partner languages and made available on the website and platform. The modules included: Communication Skills and Styles, Self-care and Well-being, Stress Management, Building Resilience, Managing Challenging Behaviour, Improving the Parent-Child relationship, Social Media as a Social Support, Accessing Supports and Overcoming Isolation, Assessing and Managing Expectations, Communication in the Parent Child Relationship, Reaction vs. Response and finally Dealing with External Influences ie. social media. All these modules were pilot tested in partner countries by a total of 99 parents and guardians. 
2.	IO2 – In-service training for Adult Educators: The consortium developed an in-service training programme that was suitable for adult educators, especially those working in the area of family support. The training programme was developed to ensure that adult educators were fully trained to harness the potential of the Inside Out educational resources. Firstly, Enoros defined the key learning outcomes of the in-service training for adult educators and highlighted what skills, knowledge and competencies should be developed. From there, both Enoros and Dante developed a 50-hour training programme comprised of 21 hours of hands-on workshop learning and 29 hours of online self-directed learning. 
-	21 hours training curriculum: This was comprised of 3-full day workshops that introduced the basic principles of working with parents (Day 1), introduction to the Inside Out curriculum and details on how to deliver (Day 2) and an introduction to the MOOC and how to safely work in online environments (Day 3). 
-	29 hours training curriculum: The 29-hours training curriculum used the 12 lesson plans which were developed in IO1 and support the practitioner in a ‘how-to’ deliver approach.  Each lesson plan had various activities and PPTs to support the practitioner to deliver the training developed in IO1. 
All the materials from IO2 are available through the MOOC and in all partner languages. 
As part of IO2, an LTTA was hosted in Cyprus and attended by 12 adult educators from all partner countries. This was an opportunity for adult educators to learn about the Inside Out curriculum and to prepare the participants for delivery of the pilots upon return home. 
All materials from IO2 was pilot tested with 75 adult educators across Europe.
3.	IO3 – A MOOC was developed by SEC as a one-stop-shop for access to the full suite of resources developed by the project. In addition, IO3 developed a substantial list of 40 OERs per partner that focused on self-care and mental wellbeing, online safety and informed parenting.

<< Results >>

The following results were developed as part of the Inside Out project: 
IO1: 12 parenting modules developed in all partner languages
IO2: 50-hours of blended learning curriculum was developed for adult educators and family practitioners. 
IO3: A high functioning MOOC available in all partner languages and 40 OERs per country gathered.
LTTA: One LTTA was hosted in Cyprus and attended by 12 practitioners.  
Pilots: 99 parents and 75 adult educators attended the pilots hosted by the project across Europe. 
Family Celebration Events: 273 people attended the Multiplier Events and Final Conference hosted by the project partners.
Local Working Groups: 48 adult educators and family support workers participated in the projects local working groups. 
Engagement: The Inside Out project involved a variety of stakeholders that would not have been imagined at the beginning of the project. Partners involved various local government groups, family resource centres and experts working in the field of family support. This will have a long-standing impact on the project and will ensure continued use of the materials.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-IS01-KA204-065831.title: Achieving Sustainability through INTRApreneurship
2020-1-IS01-KA204-065831.summary:
<< Background >>

The whole idea around the SINTRA project was to address the important need for companies and organizations to tackle the issue of sustainable development from within their organisations tapping into the huge resources that they have. Namely their own workforce. Therefore, the focus was on two concepts or ideas. Sustainable development and intrapreneurship. 
The partnership believed that by developing tailor-made training resources and establish an interactive e-Learning Platform and Open Innovation Toolkit, both targeted at sustainability-focused intrapreneurship support of employees, employers and their organisations across Europe they could have impact on advancing towards more sustainable future by training both employers and employees within the organisations. The firm believe by the partnership that the need was there was reaffirmed in the gap analysis done in all partners countries.

<< Objectives >>

The SINTRA consortium set the following objectives:
1. Better understanding of national and sectoral contexts in the field of environmental, social and economic sustainability from an intrapreneurial perspective and identification of existing gaps in the intrapreneurial mindset at organisational level.
2. Elaboration of an innovative training methodology, tools and material, combining the processes of sustainability-focused intrapreneurial training and counselling in a single, integrated approach, in order to enhance the environmental impact of organisations and their social and business sustainability.
3. Address the needs of organisations by delivering pilot sustainability-oriented workshops and counselling services which was enhance intrapreneurial efforts, that might eventually lead to the development/modification of new/existing products and services and the improvement of existing processes.
4. Transfer the project effects to other countries through the set-up of an e-Learning Platform and the creation of an open innovation toolkit (incl. an online app) for sustainability-focused intrapreneurship.

<< Implementation >>
