2020-1-IT02-KA204-079043.title: Competent Inhabitants to Valorise  Inclusive  Communities in EU
2020-1-IT02-KA204-079043.summary:
<< Background >>

Mental health and inclusion processes has changed over the years. EU countries share a common trend to reorganize socio-health services to develop autonomy using community-based approach. Inclusion is hampered by stigma, bad information, inappropriate behavior. In many EU countries psychiatric hospitals were closed/changed according to new needs. Emergency departments were opened within hospitals, territorial services have been organized. There’s a widespread need to think together to valorize housing good practices and Eu values. 

European countries implemented different housing solutions for people with mental health problems. Integrating traditional competencies on de-institutionalization and housing processes into civil society new competencies, is necessary. Finalising effective housing projects, through exchange of good practices between EU countries, means promoting and sharing the EU’s fundamental values of inclusion, protection of human rights and lifelong learning. CIVIC partnership fully agrees with WHO when promote involvemnt of local communities in Mental health issues and highlight the need of a stronger  connection among human rights, community empowerment and mental health.

<< Objectives >>

CIVIC aimed to make Local Communities more competent in Housing projects for people with experience of mental health issues. 

CIVIC’s main goals were:

- Support the diffusion of the training Curriculum on housing and mental health, for local communities.
- Increase networks for non-formal learning in supported Housing 
-  Identify social and civic skill in housing pathways
- Collect and share solutions for housing problems 

Expected results were:
1. wider and easier use of the training Curriculum, in EU.
2. expansion of partner’s cooperation networks 
3. greater participation and awareness of civic and social skills to promote human rights and inclusion
3. greater use of non-formal education in housing with people with mental health problems and / or at risk of social exclusion
4. diffusion of the Curriculum in other group with problems of social exclusion
5. more social-policy makers interested in the development of local communities
6. reduction of stigma
7. more engagement in supported housing and human right within local communities
8. more inclusive local communities

All that is in harmony with the indications for education and inclusion, promoted at National level in Croatia, Greece, Italy, UK and Portugal.

<< Implementation >>

CIVIC promoted exchange of experiences and good practices among partners. The TUTORIAL and the BOOKLET come from that. Housing is intended as “a system of social structures in a network of human relations in a safe neighborhood” CIVIC has taken it a step further in terms of diffusion, quality of use, attention to social skills, civic engagement and participation, connection to human rights.

CIVIC was implemented through:

- 2 TRANSANTIONAL PROJECT MEETINGS:  1. In Rome - Kick off meeting "Together for a more inclusive Housing"; 2. In Athens "EU Values and human rights" focused on the evaluation and the sustainability of CIVIC;
- 2 TRAINING/LEARNING ACTIVITIES milestones for the CIVIC outputs. 1. in Guimaraes PT - focused on the TUTORIAL for a good housing. 2.  in Zagreb HR focused on the BOOKLET. Each partner trained the others starting by their knowhow on supported housing, community-based approach, human rights, non-formal education, social skills;
and 
- ONLINE MEETINGS for Tutorial and Booklet setting up and editing
- INFORMATION AND DISSEMINATION ACTIVITIES, fine-tuning of outputs, papers/documents setting up, meetings, reporting, monitoring activities.

All partners were actively involved in the project implementation.

<< Results >>

Two concrete outputs in 5 languages - (on CIVIC section - www.housing-project.eu)

A. TUTORIAL FOR A GOOD HOUSING: 1-COVER INTRODUCTION 2-THE SURVEY on housing in the pandemic 3-Q&A on the Curriculum 4-THREE INTERVIEWS 5-THE STORYTELLING. 
B. BOOKLET "RECOVERY AND RESPECT HUMAN RIGHTS HOUSING MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES: FROM PROBLEM TO SOLUTION": Introduction. 1. Housing options, funding and satisfaction of the users. 2. Assessment, motivation, and individual recovery plan.3. Rights, decision making and responsibility.4. Rehabilitation, case management and peerwork. 5. Social inclusion and community resources. 6. Flexibility and coordination between the services. 7. Increasing competencies against stigma and discrimination. 8. Evaluation and monitoring of the mental health services. 9. Lifelong learning. 10. From problem to solution. Appendix: helm of recovery; glossary. Bibliography. (about 30.000 words/70 pages). 

Other results, promotion of: 1. Curriculum use, 2. wider partners’ network, 3. human rights and inclusion, 3. non-formal education 4. Curriculum in other groups, 5. communities development, 6. reduction of stigma, 7. supported housing more connected to human rights, 8. inclusive communities.

2020-1-IT02-KA204-079355.title: The chrysalis and the butterfly_  Autobiographical paths of penitentiary pedagogy
2020-1-IT02-KA204-079355.summary:
<< Background >>

The starting point of this project stems from the challenges faced by educational staff (educators, teachers, volunteers, etc.) in carrying out their profession in prison. Education in prison differs from that in schools due to various factors related to the prison environment and its organization, the inmates, rules, and the organization of time, which influence educational activities and make them extremely complex.
The uniqueness of the recipients (awaiting trial or already convicted) conditions their participation in educational activities. The same applies to inmates who work, as work and teaching sessions may overlap.
For these reasons, teachers and volunteers involved in the partnership proposal aim to share their experiences, discuss teaching methodologies and identified challenges, and compare best practices. From these premises, the efforts of participating organizations have focused on exchanging best experiences, mutual availability, and creating tools for sharing produced materials.

<< Objectives >>

The project "The Chrysalis and the Butterfly: Autobiographical Paths in Penitentiary Pedagogy" was born from the hypothesis that a critical pedagogy of art promotes the development of preventive education. In this sense, the word positions itself transversely, helping individuals deprived of freedom to give new meaning to their past. Over these years, we have worked on defining objectives that would transform a project based on oral tradition, literature, reading, writing, and artistic expression into a complement to the educational structure of the penitentiary institution.
1.	Create a space for reflection on specific themes so that individuals deprived of freedom can redefine their lives after the prison experience.
2.	Motivate inmates to describe their experiences and communicate the difficulties of prison life through strategies of oral narration and creative writing.
3.	Provide inmates with tools for self-criticism and communication skills to make their experiences and creations visible inside and outside the penitentiary institution.
4.	Establish connections between the prison community and the educational community.

<< Implementation >>

The project was based on specific paths, "life trajectories," freely used by partners to outline the frames of inmates' lives. At the end of the project, we can summarize the following paths:
1.	The Butterfly's Flight: The inmate narrates or writes, making choices, going back in time, reflecting on the present and the future, composing a meaningful and conscious plot of their existence.
2.	Autobiographical Workshop: Building together "parts of narratives." A workshop is primarily a place for the analysis and construction of the personal identities of the participants. It is intended to "build something together," so the presence of a group is necessary.
3.	Butterfly, Butterflies: The choral nature of experiences, feedback, reflection in the comrade's story has been an opportunity to get to know others in a new way.
4.	The Right to Speak: Autobiography in prison. Many prisoners have never had a real right to speak in their lives. Accepting biography has helped the prisoner/narrator feel welcomed.
5.	Redrawing the Future Workshop: The use of the autobiographical method arises from the need to develop educational opportunities to "go beyond" the bars.

<< Results >>

The most tangible result of the project was the creation of the book "Autobiographical Strategies in Penitentiary Pedagogy," which synthesized the productions and performances carried out by the partners during the partnership into a manual of autobiographical methodology. The book includes monographs of autobiographical literary texts and theatrical representations involving individuals deprived of their freedom.
Printed in 300 copies, the book was distributed by the partners in their territorial and national contexts. A more comprehensive online version is published on the project's website - https://www.candb.si/handbook-autobiographical/ - providing in-depth coverage of all stages of the work and the specific contributions of the operators and inmates.

2020-1-IT02-KA204-079657.title: Empowering Adults with Special nEeds TO BEcame active citizens.
2020-1-IT02-KA204-079657.summary:
<< Background >>

Citizenship is usually defined in terms of the rights and duties people have within their society. People that live in a territory but lack the status of citizen, are deprived of the rights and duties that citizenship involves. Citizenship is more than nationality and a legal status and, over the years, the concept has evolved from a largely passive quality to an active expression of identity and belonging. Identity is the self-understanding and self- consciousness of an individual or a group referring to territory, culture, etc. Identity also deals with social action, with similarities and differences and is expressed in a relational context.
Active citizenship is social, cultural and political responsibility and participation in associational life through areas like formal education, lifelong learning, families, etc. Taking part in lifelong learning activities is itself proof of active citizenship: citizenship as a responsible lifelong learner.
With this project we  focused on strengthening and promoting willingness to participate and to be an active citizen as adult learners with disabilities. It was done through development of  best practices of tools and methodologies for teachers and educators.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the project were:
• Develop guide lines for educators and teachers to enhance the attitude of adult learners with disabilities to become active European citizens;
• Enhance the independence of adult learners with disabilities and make them live experiences of social integration in an international context;
• Improve the autonomy and self-esteem of adult learners with disabilities;
• Support adult learners with disabilities for the acquisition of awareness of their abilities to carry out a life experience in an international context;
• Increase the network of organizations internationally to develop new Erasmus plus projects;
• Reduce the gap between training and what is required to become an active European citizen;
The mobility experience of adult learners with special needs add value to their motivation to learn and is a proactive driving force in their social context.
• Encourage the learning of foreign languages (motivation for learning and teaching foreign languages);
• Enhance teachers’/educators’ motivation to prepare adult learners with special needs to become active European citizens.

<< Implementation >>

1. Project Management & Coordination 
2. Project Management Documents
3. Quality Assurance Plan and quality evaluation of the activities
4. Meetings and evaluation questionnaires which were filled out at different stages of the project to assess the results and provide feedback for improvement.
5. Dissemination Plan and Dissemination Reports - Dissemination and exploitation activities throughout the project, including the visual identity of the project and logo, the dissemination plan, templates design to be used throughout the project uniformly, dissemination sheets for partners to log their activities, 
engagement with key-stakeholders, use of partners’ social media channels for reaching to associate partners and several institutions, networking and partnering, etc 
6. Sustainability and Exploitation Plan, with concrete steps and identified key-stakeholders 
7. Three Transnational Project Meetings (the first was online because of Covid 19)
8. Four Short-term joint staff training events
9. Two Blended mobility of adult learners with disabilities
10. preparation and support of adult learners with disabilities

<< Results >>

Our project sought to develop guide-lines for teachers and educators to enhance skills and competences of adult learners with special needs in active European citizenship by creating an innovative suite of new materials with best practices to supply a critical element of successful.  It was piloted across 4 EU countries and are available in 5 languages (English, German, Croatian, Macedonian and Italian). The materials themselves took the form of new worksheets for teachers and educators involved in adult education with learners with special needs. Instant feedback on process and output was very important to demonstrate the attitudes and behaviour and to make it understood that this is helpful to enhance active citizenship for adults with special needs.
New knowledge and tools on informal learning in this area are widely available to organisations in the partner countries and in other member states.
Taking part in the project adults with disabilities  have used skills which they almost never apply in daily life and through which they  gained competences that will contribute to active citizenship.
The assistants gained knowledge and developed a network for further help with the countries involved.

2020-1-IT02-KA204-079777.title: Adult education to promote RElational Ability
2020-1-IT02-KA204-079777.summary:
<< Background >>

In all European countries there are residential centers care and services that welcome women who are victims of violence with their children, or 'mother-child' shelters that welcome mothers and children who are temporarily in a situation of distress and/or fragility for which they need accompaniment and/or socio-educational support. These services at a European level, albeit with different standards and models, are united by the aim of promoting the well-being of women and minors in order to contain or prevent situations of developmental/relational distress, as well as material distress related to living and working conditions.
Social conditions and the great changes in which our society lives, with the new educational needs of children, require adults to develop new parental and educational skills. To this end, the Re-Ability project has set itself the objective of supporting the parenting skills of mothers who turn to our services and who are faced with an important change, since they are coming out of a difficult history, often made up of violence, but also of emotional deficiency, parental incapacity, and neglect.

<< Objectives >>

The objective of the project is to work on learning and strengthening the skills of the woman/mother to ensure the healthy growth of the child while protecting her rights. Some of the centres for women who are victims of violence or mothers in a vulnerable condition of the partnership organisations work 24 hours a day, they are facilities that welcome the woman and the minor by offering them alternative accommodation; others work more like help desks. In both cases, the time that these centres have in charge of women with their children must be used to promote a real change of perspective on the part of the mother, who must come out of this process stronger than before. Experience in the field teaches us how strong the need is to work with these women both on strengthening existing ties and on the ability to create new ones, a network to which they can refer so as not to feel alone, and this consequently entails the need to strengthen emotional and relational skills.

<< Implementation >>

The ReAbility project foresaw the implementation of 3 Intellectual outputs: The Parenting Education Plan (PEG), the Toolkit of Tools, the Recommendations; 5 TPMs were realised of which the first one online for the Covid emergency, and the others in the partner countries as per the form; we carried out 5 MEs, one in each of the partner countries. We made a software for the construction of the PEG capable of assessing analysing parenting skills, storing the results, collecting information about the subject, giving indications about tools, activities and useful advice. Closely linked the toolkit with suggested activities and finally the mothers took the floor and made recommendations. In addition, we created a project evaluation and monitoring plan, a communication plan for the dissemination of results. We opened a facebook page for the communication of the most important news. We used the home page of the software as a showcase of the project, including the most important info and results.

<< Results >>

The Reability project concretely realised 3 intellectual outputs
IO1: Parenting education plan: a tool for assessing, enhancing and monitoring parenting skills aimed at assessing the parenting skills of the mother taken on by the services for the realisation of an individualised project in which strengths and weaknesses are highlighted, together with the shared definition of the objectives to be achieved
IO2: Promoting and developing the social-relational and emotional competences of mothers: paths, tools, ideas and activities to promote and develop social-relational and emotional competences. Inside, 4 different types of workshops are described. The aim is to strengthen the mother-child relationship. In addition to the workshops, there are a set of activities, tools, recommended film books depending on the objectives to be achieved. 
IO3: New educational needs: recommendations of mothers victims of violence.  These are recommendations developed by frontline mothers. It is a series of indications that are also operational and are intended to be a kind of manifesto for all stakeholders, policy makers, professionals, so as to develop procedures that take into account the needs and wishes of the mothers themselves.

2020-1-IT02-KA204-079809.title: Hi-Ability - Developing social and professional skills through outdoor experiences
2020-1-IT02-KA204-079809.summary:
<< Background >>

The need behind the project was to ensure inclusive education for people with disabilities, to
promote their full participation in social life and their psycho-physical well-being. The implementation of Hi-Ability allowed us to "open the doors to new spaces of education", promoting an education for autonomy, independent and inclusive life, in a context still not very accessible such as hiking and eco-tourism.  In fact, very often, social and cultural interventions aimed at the integration of people with disabilities tend to segregate the beneficiaries, as they are provided within protected, "closed" contexts, taking place in a perspective of “assistance" and isolation. This has negative consequences on the perception of disability towards society and a misreading of the real needs of people with disabilities. By placing the natural environment at the centre of its activities, Hi-Ability has promoted an original methodological approach of a therapeutic-rehabilitation programme based on the socio-educational value of the natural environment.

<< Objectives >>

Through the implementation of the project we wanted to to promote the empowerment and the social inclusion of people with intellectual disability (PWID), by enhancing their abilities in the field of outdoor touring and hiking. Through the implementation of the project we wanted to achieve the following specific objectives (SOs) of the project are 4:

SO1: To improve adult educators’ knowledge, competences and skills on how nature/outdoor experience  can improve the social skills and well-being of PWID
SO2: To promote the acquisition of different skills for adult PWID, with the final aim of providing  them with improved personal and professional abilities, useful for the enhancing of the quality of their lives; 
SO3: To increase the participation in outdoor activities such as hiking and eco-tourism PWID,  promoting accessibility through technological tools. 
OS4: Define a European model for the education of adults with disabilities through the use of outdoor  activities.

The SOs indicated below have been largely achieved.

<< Implementation >>

In order to reach the above-mentioned objectives, the Hi-Ability methodology involved the implementation of four main phases:

1) Training the trainers: development of educational materials and training courses for professionals  working with people with disabilities to improve their skills in outdoor education activities (SO1); 
2) Training people with disabilities as “assistants” to professional guides for outdoor/nature tours: beneficiaries acquired personal and professional skills through a specific training course and were able to test their acquired skills by a pilot experimentation carried out in all involved countries (SO2).  
3) Creation of an app to facilitate the participation of people with DI in outdoor activities (SO3) 
4) Development of policy recommendations and guidelines to facilitate the transferability of the  model to all EU countries (SO4).

The project implementation was also based on the realisation of 4. transnational meetings, 3 LTTAs (functional for the achievement of the set objectives) and 4 final multiplier events.

<< Results >>

Hi-Ability produced the following results (available on the project website in EN,IT,HR,GR):

IO1: Toolkit (OS1)
Toolkit for educators working with PWID. It aims to develop their competences in the field of empowerment and improvement of psychophysical well-being of PWID through outdoor activities.

IO2: App (OS3)
Easy language App addressed to PWID. The App provides information on accessible nature trails and it is available on Google Play and the Apple store.

IO3: Green Guide (OS2)
The Guide is dedicated to PWID and their families/caregivers. It is available in two versions
- an easy-to-read version based on Alternative Augmentative Communication (AAC)
- a full version.

IO4: Policy recommendations and guidelines for transferability (OS4)
Tool for the creation of a European model of social inclusion, for the transfer of results and for the replicability of the Hi-Ability model in other countries.

The project enabled us to create a strong multisectoral network strongly interested both in the methodology tested and in future collaborations focusing on the topic of social inclusion through outdoor learning.

2020-1-IT02-KA204-079836.title: The Mediterranean Caravan: Learning and Sharing Agroecology
2020-1-IT02-KA204-079836.summary:
<< Background >>

In the Mediterranean basin, transitioning towards more sustainable practices and communities is vital. Industrialization has harmed soils, biodiversity, and local seeds, causing land abandonment and widening socio-economic disparities.
Agroecology provides versatile tools to address several environmental, social and economic challenges. 
The Mediterranean Network of Local Solidarity_Based Partnerships for Agroecology (MedNet), revealed that the Principles of Agroecology and their importance for peasant agriculture was one of the top training needs for the network.
The needs were:
-Lack of educational programs on agroecology that respond to the needs of solidarity-based food communities and are specific to the Mediterranean ecosystem.
- Preservation  the traditional knowledge still alive in the Mediterranean countries, with practitioners who are using traditional agricultural knowledge and skills.
The Mediterranean basin is a naturally and culturally interconnected region that extends beyond political boundaries. MedCaravan has operated in Serbia, Croatia, Portugal, Italy, Turkey, France and has had  an impact in the whole Mediterranean basin thanks to the Mednet and Urgenci.

<< Objectives >>

MedCaravan objectives were the following  :
-Support rural communities’ social inclusion through adult learning and the valorisation and empowerment of local knowledge
 	
-Mainstream agroecological practices in small-scale agriculture as a mean to support rural livelihoods while at the same time fostering climate resilience and environmental sustainability
 	
-Build innovation capacities by enhancing technical as well as organizational skills of partners and target groups

The main focus of MedCaravan was to collect, valorise and share local and innovative knowledge about agroecological practices by creating high-quality educational materials, turning community members into its disseminators and offering know-how and expertise to a wide population.The final goal was therefore to strengthen the Mediterranean network of LSPA.

<< Implementation >>

Medcaravan has had several activities:
- IO1 Best Practice Guide for collecting agroecological knowledge 
- IO2 Online Caravan Platform
- IO3 Curriculum on Learning in MedAgroecology
- A set of 3 multiplier events for the 6 partners countries:
  * Knowledge Caravan which aimed to test the methodology for collecting knowledge and train other knowledge collectors (linked to IO1)
  * Caravan for Agroecology, which aimed to  develop a local training on agroecology and identify the trainers for the international event (linked to IO3)
  * Caravan Mediterranean Bazaar which aimed to disseminate the results of the project (linked to IO1/2/3)
- 2 International training events:
  * Training for Knowledge Collectors, which trained staff members on the innovative methodology for collecting knowledge (linked to IO1)
  * Training for Learning and Sharing Agroecology, which trained adults learners from organisations for a common mediterranean agroecology training  program (linked to Io3)
- 1 training of Podcast editing, 35 podcast ,19 webinars (linked to IO2) 
- 4 International Transnational Management meeting

<< Results >>

List of results per outputs/training/ per partner (check indicators file):
* IO1: Best Practice Guide for collecting agroecological knowledge, targeting non-formal and non-academic stakeholders in food communities. 
* IO2: Online Caravan Platform, a centralised hub for educational materials and ensuring the project's sustainability. Platform’s user guide, 19 webinars, 35 podcast.
* IO3: Educational program, Learning on MedAgroecology, with a curriculum and supporting booklet 
* Glossary: a new document with IO1/3 keywords
* Set of 3 multiplier events (E1-18) in all partners countries: Knowledge Caravans, Caravans for Agroecology and Caravan Mediterranean Bazaars, fostering dialogue among food community actors. 440 participants.
* 2 transnational training: Training of Knowledge Collectors (March’22, RS) and Training Learning and Sharing Agroecology (Oct’22, It) 
* 50 participants, contributing to local and MedNet LSPA network knowledge enhancement.
* Dissemination results: 
- Published media content on Urgenci’s and partners’ platforms, including posts, articles, and videos.
- Meetings with associated partners, stakeholders, and decision-makers to inform them about the MedCaravan educational program at national and European levels.

2020-1-IT02-KA204-079967.title: Enhance public library services for visually impaired users through ICT tools and training
2020-1-IT02-KA204-079967.summary:
<< Background >>

The project idea stemmed from a specific need of public libraries’ staff: how to deal with visually impaired users in libraries? This necessity constituted the basis on which the consortium was built and the project developed.
New technologies have opened up new possibilities for reading and for participatory activities targeted to people with disabilities. These days, visually impaired users can access specific computer programmes, digital resources and innovative instruments like screen magnifying monitors, screen readers and speech synthesis, Braille displays.
Even if some of these services are gradually being supplied also in Public & Academic Libraries, there are differences from country to country, with a huge potential for improvement in terms of skills and competencies of libraries’ staff. Even though libraries for blind people are generally well equipped, the request for specialized services for visually impaired in local or national systems is raising constantly.

<< Objectives >>

Through the need analysis emerged 2 main issues:
- library staff is generally poorly aware of the ICT tools for the involvement of visually impaired users and successful experiences and best practices are very little known;
- library staff’s digital competencies are usually not adequate to face this challenge.
 
Starting from these 2 aspects, the project focused on 3 main objectives:
1)Promote the exchange of best practices among the staff of different libraries on ICT tools and services for the involvement of visually impaired readers;
2)Develop library staff’s digital competencies through training activities on ICT tools;
3)Establish a network of libraries for cooperation in the involvement of visually impaired users.
 
Partners wanted TECH.LIBRARY to represent a concrete opportunity for EU libraries to communicate and collaborate, share common needs, improve the skills of their staff, develop innovative approaches in order to improve their services dedicated to visually impaired users.

<< Implementation >>

In order to reach the foreseen goals, the consortium successfully worked to the implementation of the following activities:
1) Project management and coordination, which ensured the effective overall technical and financial implementation of the  project,
2) Exchange of best practices and study visits, from which the partners had the chance to acquire new knowledge on how other libraries work with visually impaired users to foster accessibility and social inclusion, increasing their competencies in the field of ICT tools applied to reading;
3) Design and implementation of the TECH.LIRBARY platform, enabling users to learn about best practices in relation to the project topics, ICT tools for accessible libraries, as well as to get trained, share experiences and networking with other stakeholders, all while sharing and disseminating project activities and initiatives,
4) Short term joint staff training in Rijeka (HR) on latest ICT technologies to offer services to visually impaired users,
5) Targeted communication and dissemination activities, through the organization of 6 conferences to disseminate the project achievements and to engage stakeholders within the TECH.LIBRARY online platform.

<< Results >>

The project allowed to establish a proper network among public libraries of different European countries, sharing common needs, but also ideas, best practices and practical solutions aimed at improving services dedicated to visual impaired people.
As concrete outputs, the project produced:
1) TECH.LIBRARY online platform
2) Training videos in 7 different languages
3) Practical handbook and recommendations of best practices in 7 different languages.


The project activities successfully achieved the initially expected result, producing the following outcomes:
1) Greater awareness on international good practices in the field of visually impaired readers’ involvement through ICT;
2) Wider digital competences for the involvement of visually impaired users;
3) Strengthening of a network of libraries;
4) Production of ad hoc training materials.

2020-1-IT02-KA204-080078.title: Social Inclusion Through Gamification in Education
2020-1-IT02-KA204-080078.summary:
<< Background >>

As the European Union Council Resolution on a renewed European Agenda for Adult Learning highlighted that “much more remains to be done in relation to targeted learning for
Migrants”, the SIGE project was thought to support the social inclusion of low skilled people with a migrant background or belonging to a minority by contributing to the development of a flexible blended gamified learning offer allowing them to
develop the key competences.

The main pre-identified needs of the target, that were analyzed, confirmed and/or changed thanks to the results of the field research and desk research conducted in the first phases of the project, are:
- Improve their comprehension of spoken and written language of their host country that will help them achieve more independence in carrying out everyday activities;
- Strengthen their speaking skills and improve their vocabulary in order enhance their ability, confidence and motivation to interact and build social relations;
- Improve their comprehension of spoken and written english language;
- Learn basic IT skills to enhance the quality of their life and social inclusion;
- Improve their knowledge about the culture of their host country and intercultural awareness and competences;
- Improve their soft skills required from the labor market, like public speaking, communication and teamwork.

<< Objectives >>

The specific objectives of SIGE, implemented and reached by the project, are the following:
O1) Research the needs of the low skilled people with a migrant background or belonging to a minority in relation with key competences and with how flexible, blended and gamified
learning offer could deal with these needs
O2) Explore the educational potential of Gamification and game-based learning as an innovative instrument for enhancing active participation, engagement and inclusion in education and in society
O3) Design an innovative modular blended upskilling learning course tailored for the target that integrates game-based mechanics and game thinking to turn the learning process as a whole into a game as well as practical apps and tools to use games as part of the learning process and that allows for the recognition of prior knowledge
O4) Empower adult educators working with low skilled adult with a migrant background or belonging to a minority to use Gamification and game-based learning to deal with diversified
groups and improve the quality of their teaching practice
O5) Develop a cross-border and cross sector synergy (Sige Network)  with the purpose of creating innovative uses of Gamification tailored to the needs of low skilled people with a migrant background or belonging to a minority

<< Implementation >>

The activities carried out with the support of the PMI budget were the following:

WP0 - Project Management
A1 Project Management
A2 Financial reporting and monitoring
A3 Development of the Dissemination plan

2020-1-IT02-KA204-080081.title: Training in Mediation and Restorative Justice
2020-1-IT02-KA204-080081.summary:
<< Background >>

Restorative Justice is a way of resolving conflicts and repairing harm by involving all the parties affected by wrongdoing. Restorative justice can take different forms, such as mediation, conferencing, circles, or dialogue.
There are different approaches to Restorative Justice (RJ) and mediator training in Europe. Some countries have an established and mature tradition of RJ, while others have experimented with different creative practices despite the absence of clear and shared legislation. 
The MEDIAREJ project aims to take stock of different training methods and implement them through joint staff activities and innovative products, creating a network among trained professionals and organizations. The exchange of experiences is essential to develop shared guidelines on the essential requirements for training mediators and trainers in RJ, taking into account that RJ is primarily a practical science. 
The project also addresses the major challenges concerning justice that have characterized 20th century Europe, such as human trafficking, terrorism and organised crime, and proposes RJ as an alternative to securitarian and punitive approaches that can increase rather than reduce criminal behavior.

<< Objectives >>

MEDIAREJ is a project that aims to develop a shared methodology in training in the field of Restorative Justice (RJ) through the development of original Intellectual Outputs, a Europe-wide training and 6 multiplier events. 
The main objectives of the project are:
to foster RJ competencies in different target groups, 
to develop a standardised competencies framework, a course curriculum for training, original methods and new toolkits, 
to provide training for 28 mediators, trainers and professionals, 
to raise awareness on RJ for other target groups at a local level, to empower staff and strengthen the operational capacity of local RJ centres
to match an adequate quality standard to facilitate the mobility of mediation and RJ experts at the European level.
The project also aims to create and consolidate a network of trainers in mediation working in existing centers; mediators working in restorative practice projects in their territories; mediation experts such as academics and researchers, to facilitate the exchange of practical mediation experiences and to discuss the specific aspects of each context, in order to provide appropriate training for mediators.

<< Implementation >>

Project activities divide among  cross-cutting tasks and specific activities.
Regarding cross-cutting tasks, particularly management, a plan has been developed, partnership agreements and GANTT diagrams have been prepared, and a risk register has been prepared. To ensure smooth project implementation, reporting was divided into several progress reports.The project communication, monitoring and sustainability plans were developed at the beginning of the project and have been ongoing since then. The communication plan has been followed and the website and social media have been regularly updated; a visual identity guide, stakeholder file, newsletters, and event flyers have been produced. To measure the impact of the project, a set of key performance and success indicators were defined and outlined, including ongoing indicators and goal setting for each activity and IO. All partners were actively involved in the enhancement and sustainability efforts from the beginning of the project.
Specific activities implemented throughout the project were:
production of 6 Innovative IO’s 	
5 day LTTA in Croatia 	
6 ME ((Bergamo, Porec, Targu Mures, Valencia, Leuven, Trieste)
1 Online Kick off meeting and 3 blended TPM’s
Over 50 partner meetings

<< Results >>

1.A framework of competences which includes a literature review on the state of the art about training trainers on restorative Justice (RJ), a consultation process, some recommendations and a toolkit for future trainers.
2. A training programme that aims  to produce a series of guidelines and tools (Training Modules) for trainers in RJ programmes, particularly according to the perspective of humanistic mediation. 
3. A toolkit that points out some of the areas where mediation and RJ can be applied and offers a wide range of themes and approaches as conversation starters and material for critical reflection. 
4. This collection aims at analyzing different approaches of RJ in the context of Gender Based Violence which contains a theoretical part and a collection of case studies.
5. Multimedia materials (7 short films and 2 interviews) that can be used by trainers to translate into an interactive visual tool some of the practices related to RJ that highlight critical issues in the approach.
6. A platform is designed in 3 main sections: welcome section with a forum in order to consent visitors to introduce themself, a section related with the resources and materials of the project and a Community of Practice devoted to networking.

2020-1-LT01-KA204-077823.title: We are all together to raise awareness of cultural heritage
2020-1-LT01-KA204-077823.summary:
<< Background >>

The initial project idea was born during the TCA meeting (contact seminar) on 2018 November 14-17 in Santiago de Compostela, Spain. The result of the seminar was achieved and WAAT project partners were united there in Spain. All partners came from diverse backgrounds, but the main idea was to raise awareness of cultural heritage. We wanted to aim to introduce learners to 4 types of heritage because heritage is still thought of as an object (static, immovable, etc.). It was important for us that non-formal adult education had a new opportunity and products and invited people to learn about cultural heritage differently and to be able to recite it in a film format. As a professional working in the field, we felt that people still don't connect with heritage or have limited access to it, and by creating an easy tool we can provide access and raise up the creativity of professionals who works with heritage, because professionals in the field are often immersed in the work of documentary bureaucracy and stop cultivating their creativity.

<< Objectives >>

Together in transnational joint learning activities and meetings, we IMPLEMENTED comprehensive materials on raising awareness for the European heritage sector. Design to strengthen and expand non-formal adult education by offering a new, intriguing, and important cultural heritage theme and new, more modern tools - a newly developed non-formal teaching and learning guide and attractive, and engaging forms of activity (creative ways of representing cultural heritage). Therefore, we develop two intellectual products: a guide for educators/leaners and a digital platform. Basically, help non-formal adult education professionals to clarify and help understand the 4 aspects of cultural heritage.  Also prepared detailed instruction on the creation of films for heritage, teach the practical details of the dissemination of heritage, and have created films accessible for all on the digital platform.

<< Implementation >>

3 TPM (Austria, Lithuania. Italy). 1 set of minutes of each meeting, as well as final reports of the detailed work plan after the meetings. Also 1 sets of attendance sheets for each meeting and evaluation forms after each meeting.  
2 LTTA :  C1 online, C2 live in Croatia.  32 participants in total, 12 Europass were issued after C2 training, and 2 (trial) digital stories. `
2 IO (1. WAAT guide for educators with infographics; 2. WAAT digital platform www.waatproject.eu ). 
13 infographics and all translated into partner language.
Guide translation into each partner language and English.
6 multiplier events.
66 digital stories have been made and are available on the digital platform.
Internal and external evaluation of the project and Intellectual outputs. 
8 local meetings with stakeholders in each partner country (48 meetings in total).
3 online meetings with partners which included agenda, minutes, decisions completed, and internal evaluation. 
10 other online meetings between the coordinator and separate partners by request.
1 Facebook  https://www.facebook.com/WAATproject
1 Twitter  https://twitter.com/WAATproject
Designed Project logo.
Dissemination plan to follow for all partners.
Dissemination activities all the time.

<< Results >>

1. WAAT guide for Educators with infographics. The guide is placed on the digital learning platform and is freely accessible to all in 7 languages. 
Besides a constructivist understanding of heritage, we intend to offer an easy approach to the production of digital video stories. There is no need to have specific knowledge in filmmaking and you do not need special equipment. Based on this WAAT Guide for Educators, the camera of your mobile phone or tablet, as well as basic user knowledge, are enough to produce short digital educational video stories and upload them on the WAAT digital platform. The Guide contains three chapters: 1. Dynamic, constructivist concept of cultural heritage.  2. Production of digital video stories and the WAAT digital platform 3. Application of digital stories in adult education. Also, it has annex. 
2. Digital platform www.waatproject.eu Main purpose of the platform is to function as a tool to upload heritage videos via the WAAT guidelines. It is admirably adapted to mobile devices and has an active virtual map which shows where in Europe the stories were taken.

2020-1-LT01-KA204-077837.title: Supporting Digital Native NEETs Back to Mainstream Education, Training and Employment
2020-1-LT01-KA204-077837.summary:
<< Background >>

With the EU economy in full recovery mode it is important to recognise that certain sub-sets of the population have not as of yet fully benefited from the return to growth. There remains a significant number of younger adults commonly referred to as NEETs - neither in education, employment nor training - on the margins of society and economy in all EU Member States.
NEET gathers a multitude of individuals under its classification. It broadly includes adults between the ages of 20 and 34 years who are on the margins of mainstream society. For most NEETs education has not had the desired impact where essential skills for employment are concerned. They don't have sufficient qualifications for further education and many in their ranks come from disadvantaged backgrounds. For the vast majority of NEETs education and training were not regarded as a priority in their early development years and in many cases their family educational history is one of under-achievement. Despite these educational impairments most of today's NEET population are digital natives and have some level of proficiency in digital and social media. This digital know-how can be the bridge to re-engagement if the right educational intervention is provided.

<< Objectives >>

Erasmus+ project NEET-IDEA focuses on the use of these devices by target group members to produce digital media content which many of them upload and share on a variety of social media platforms. NEET-IDEA partners have built an entire training programme to train the NEET target group to make short films using only their smartphones for producing and editing the content created. The training was focused on building small media production crews/teams of 4 or 5 individuals and assigning different roles in the short-film production, editing and marketing actions required. 
NEET-IDEA is primarily a project about developing specific key transversal skills; building self-confidence; taking responsibility; working in a team environment; being respected and respecting others, all key skills for inclusion. As Woody Allen once said "...everybody wants to be in the movies..." and the NEET-IDEA project gives young digital natives the opportunity to be part of a film crew in a role that fits their personal preferences or personalities. This is the way to achieve the inclusion and up-skilling of NEETs that partners are proposing.

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of Erasmus+ project NEET-IDEA, a number of activities were organised:
(1)	Development of NEET-IDEA materials and methodology for NEETs upskilling and inclusion.
(2)	International Short-term joint staff training event in Ireland provided to support skills acquisition in audiovisual production using available media devices and open source software and also to provide the cascading model of training proposed by supporting the training of further adult educators in their home country.
(3)	Training organized for the trainers to have up to 70 adult educators trained.
(4)	350+ NEETs were involved in film-production activities and 70 short films were created.
(5)	7 NEET-IDEA multiplier events/film festivals were held in each partner country involving 175+ participants.
(6)	Final conference / International film festival was organized as a multiplier event, finalizing event of the project and 50 participants took part in the event.

<< Results >>

As the result of Erasmus+ project NEET-IDEA, 3 intellectual outputs were developed:
(1)	Training programme that uses inquiry-based and embedded-learning methodologies to develop a wide range of skills and attitudes that are essential for personal growth and personal fulfilment.
(2)	Compendium of Inquiry-based and Embedded- learning Resources and NEET-IDEA learner’s guide
(3)	NEET-IDEA MOOC where all results can be easily accessed.

2020-1-LV01-KA204-077548.title: Rural and Regional Libraries as Local Family Entrepreneurship centres
2020-1-LV01-KA204-077548.summary:
<< Background >>

Europe’s economic growth and jobs depend on its ability to support the growth of enterprises. Entrepreneurship creates new companies, opens up new markets, and nurtures new
skills. The most important sources of employment in the EU are Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs). The Commission’s objective is to encourage people to become
entrepreneurs and also make it easier for them to set up and grow their businesses. Only 37% of Europeans would like to be self-employed, compared to 51% of people in
the US and China and thus Europeans should be encouraged more to set up their own business. It is also important to support  rural areas as predominantly rural areas make up half of Europe and represent around 20 % of the population, as nowdays people are migrating from rural areas to urban areas due to lack of job opportunities and rural youth is unable to find any options for their growth. The main idea of the project is to solve above mentioned challenges by promoting (teaching) entrepreneurship in non-urban regions, putting special focus on promotion of family business creation and will use regional and rural libraries as a platform to reach people living regional and rural areas.

<< Objectives >>

The Objectives of the Family Business Library project are:
* Development and implementation of innovative practices of teaching Entrepreneurship to people living in regional and rural areas;
* Increase sense of initiative and entrepreneurship among people living in regional and rural areas;
* Develop a system where libraries serve as a centres for rural entrepreneurship development.

<< Implementation >>

During the project implementation project partners implemented the following activities:
1) Developed content  and developed interactive e-learning course "E-learning module on Entrepreneurship for usage in Libraries" which consists of 6 Modules "Finding the right IDEA and shaping it into an OPPORTUNITY"; "Forms of ENTREPRENEURSHIP", "Realistic PLANING and Business Models", "Basics of MARKETING and BRANDING", "Basics of FINANCIAL PLANNING" and "COMMON MISTAKES and learning from FAILURES".  
2) Developed content for interactive e-learning course "Mentoring methodology and e-learning course module for librarians"
3) Developed Policy Paper "FamilyBusinessLibrary" to better exploit achieved results of the project.

Organised a training activity for librarians participating in the project, so that they better understand the essence of business idea catching and shaping as well as organised 6 Multiplier events in project libraries: 3 were targeted to librarians while 3 to visiting families.

<< Results >>

The project has produced the following results (familybusinesslibrary.art-smart.eu):
1) e-learning course "E-learning module on Entrepreneurship for usage in Libraries" which consists of 6 Modules

3) Policy Paper "FamilyBusinessLibrary" a policy recommendation document.

2020-1-LV01-KA204-077559.title: Network of UNESCO Cultural Spaces
2020-1-LV01-KA204-077559.summary:
<< Background >>

Cultural heritage is a value in itself that builds national self-confidence and a sense of belonging to a region, country and part of the world, but, in addittion, the safeguarding of the ICH contributes to different aspects of sustainable development of different regions in Europe - remote, rural and also urban territories. The eight project partners - representing different cultural values recognised by UNESCO - have created a partnership, supported by many associated partners - to join forces and share experience from several countries in order to provide better understanding of what are the best ways and methods to channel the knowledge to those who need it - people practising UNESCO included traditions. In total the project is addressed to two main target groups: Staff of the partner organisations- adult educators- and practitioners of the ICH elements in partner countries.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project is to promote the education of adult educators working in the field of ICH of seven European countries as well as the education of practitioners of UNESCO-related elements thus safeguarding and promoting these European cultural values. This project was a logical continuation of the Erasmus + programme project "The Network of UNESCO recognised values" where four of this project partners were involved and which focused on musical heritage in partner countries. New project gave the opportunity to expand the existing network, by attracting new partners and to explore other UNESCO-recognised values in all partner countries.

<< Implementation >>

All planned activities were implemented, as well as some additional ones - virtually. In order to exchange methods, approaches and best practices among participating organizations and countries, three virtual and seven in -person Short-term joint staff training events were organised in all partner countries with diverse program to give participants a comprehensive picture of the situation in each country in the field of ICH. 
Nine virtal/ in-person project meetings were organised to discuss administrative issues and ensure the successful implementation of project activities. 
During the course of the project, several educational and informative materials were created to inform target groups about intangible cultural heritage in Europe, different methods and approaches. 
Various dissemination activities were organised, including local seminars in 6 partner countries and conference in Latvia where project results were presented to a broader audience. In addition, social media (Facebook, Instagram, Twitter) and partners’ websites were used to inform all stakeholders about achievements in the project
and to promote the developed materials.

<< Results >>

- seven in-person Short-term joint staff training events organised in order to share experiences, methods and approaches among partner organisations and countries in the field of ICH;
- three virtual training events organised in the first year of the project, when it was not possible to hold face-to-face events due to the pandemic;
 - nine Transnational project meetings organised to discuss project management issues; 
- educational materials created for target groups -practitioners of ICH, staff of partner organisations and other stakeholders, prepared together by all project partners:
1. Eight summaries of methodologies and approaches working with target groups of all partners; 
2. Joint good practise examples booklet (incl. 5 examples of each partner organisation).
Materials are made printable and available online for public free of charge at the project partners’ web sites;
- local seminars in all partner countries, except Latvia (7 in total) within last months of the project where project results were presented to a broader audience;
 - a conference in Latvia at the end of the project (11/08/2023) to present project results to target groups and stakeholders and to to draw public attention to the role and importance of the cultural heritage;
 - other dissemination activities organised (information about project in project partner web sites, Facebook, media etc.); 
- expanded network of European organisations representing UNESCO recognised ICH elements.
As a result of the project staff of the partner organisations - adult educators - gained fresh ideas, different perspectives and exchange classroom techniques/
methodology/ approaches by participating in Short-term joinst staff training events in all partner countries. Impact on partnering organisations as well: opportunity to network at a transnational level, exchange of best practice supporting organisational learning. The education of practitioners of ICH were improved directly through such project activities as created educational materials, conference and seminars, but also indirectly - through capacity building of the partner organisations - adult educators.

2020-1-NL01-KA204-064748.title: Entrepreneurship education for seniors and adults with fewer opportunities
2020-1-NL01-KA204-064748.summary:
<< Background >>

The motivation for this project was to equip seniors and adults with fewer opportunities with a set of skills needed for personal development in the areas of entrepreneurial intelligence and creating (self-)employment opportunities, proactively in today's reality of employment insecurity and the world of extinction of many familiar jobs and occupations now and even more so in the future. This new needed capacity was entrepreneurial intelligence - a competence trained and developed through the acquisition of various skills, knowledge and attitudes through quality non-formal adult education. After analysing the results, we identified the following needs and problems in our communities:
- the difficulty to find quality permanent employment for adults and seniors with fewer opportunities.
- the difficulty to open new businesses as most of the new businesses started in our communities are not innovative and therefore do not generate sufficient profit or even close quite soon.
- not enough opportunities for our beneficiaries to develop their entrepreneurial intelligence and thus their personal, social and cognitive skills, especially those of innovation and creativity in entrepreneurship.
- inadequate and inaccessible educational opportunities, either online or offline, for developing entrepreneurial intelligence and related creativity in entrepreneurship.
- only 7 out of 42 adult educators (17%) have previous experience with enterprises and use this experience and expertise in their non-formal adult education for employability and entrepreneurship of adults (and seniors) with fewer opportunities.
- only 4 out of 42 (9%) adult educators working with beneficiaries in NF adult education have received any kind of training on the intrapersonal aspect of entrepreneurial intelligence and feel confident in organising educational activities on this topic.
With this project, our beneficiaries were able to improve their entrepreneurial intelligence and attitude. We also empowered more adult educators to organise innovative and up-to-date entrepreneurial learning activities within non-formal adult education.

<< Objectives >>

To empower seniors and adults with fewer opportunities in entrepreneurial intelligence and mind-set development (including intrapersonal and interpersonal social-emotional and creativity competences), through development of inspiring, innovative and up-to-date handbook and e-learning courses.
• Empower our adult educators and improve knowledge management of adult education institutions and organisations in theory and practice for building competences of adult educators in entrepreneurial mind-set and creativity in entrepreneurship development of citizens, through training courses, innovative Guidebook with curriculum and e-learning courses for adult educators’ training.
• Exchange good practices and further develop quality strategic partnership among partners from 5 European countries with different realities in regards to citizens’ self-employment and entrepreneurship.
The project proves to be needed/innovative in our communities, also thanks to the transnational contribution of partners from different European countries with their different approaches on motivating target groups. All partners have good practices to showcase and we will learn from each other but also disseminate the learned outcomes to others back home and promote the different practices of entrepreneurship education in adult learning programmes.

<< Implementation >>

M2 Second meeting

O3 E-learning course for educators: Entrepreneurial learning, Intelligence and mind-set development education for seniors and adults with fewer opportunities
O4 E-learning course for beneficiaries: IntRApersonal aspect of Entrepreneurial mind-set development

Project directly impacted organisational capacities to work on providing quality entrepreneurship education to mainly seniors and adults with fewer opportunities. The project positively and long-lasting effects on partner organisations increased their capacity and competences for providing quality adult education activities for entrepreneurial learning based on innovative approach.
With all intellectual outputs, we influenced the change and improvement of existing entrepreneurship adult NFE methodologies and programmes, at first among partner organisations of the project, and later among partner of ours and their wider network of collaborators.

<< Results >>

In this project was developed 5 Intellectual outputs: O1: Handbook on Entrepreneurial learning; O2: Guidebook with Curriculum: “Empowering adult educators for Entrepreneurial learning, Intelligence and mind-set development among seniors and adults with fewer opportunities”; O3: E-learning course for educators: “Entrepreneurial learning, Intelligence and mind-set development education for seniors and adults with fewer opportunities”; O4: E-learning course for seniors, adults / beneficiaries: “IntRApersonal aspect of Entrepreneurial mind-set development”; O5: E-learning course for seniors, adults / beneficiaries: “Leadership, Teamwork and other intERpersonal skills within Entrepreneurial mind-set development”; 4 transnational meetings; we conducted 5 Multiplier events E1,E2,E3,E4,E5; We implemented 1 LTTA (C1) Training of trainers.

2020-1-NO01-KA204-076496.title: Empowering parents and families for active social inclusion and resilience
2020-1-NO01-KA204-076496.summary:
<< Background >>

Background:
The whole world came to a total shutdown following the outbreak of Covid-19, this affected both working and non-working parents and educators, what was considered a normal lifestyle, did not exist anymore as people had no choice but to succumb and adapt to a new digitalized way of life. The only effective way of communicating, working, and schooling, was to resort to the use of online tools. 
Families and educators were forced to delve into the techniques and new online tools. This proved to be a big challenge for many families, especially parents that have challenges communicating with their children, language barriers, digital incompetency, balancing family and work life, and having problems communicating in their children’s school and community. 

Another important factor why we applied for this project was migration processes, which are very different between the respective partner countries. European societies are becoming more exposed to diversity than ever before, and digital communication to enhance and improve social inclusion becomes very relevant. It was observed that many societies are not prepared for these rapid digital processes and changes. It was learned that some countries face the challenges of welcoming refugees even though they are dependent on migrant workers. As societies become culturally mixed, the migration processes can be daunting for some parents and families, They are not only exposed to a new language, but also a culture and tradition that can sometimes be entirely opposite from the one they are used to. Integration requires a great reorganization and readjustment that is accompanied by psychological discomfort and issues related to the sense of identity.  
The “Empowering parents and families for active social inclusion and resilience” project was aimed at creating awareness and empowering parents by providing tools channeled towards improving their parenting knowledge, digital proficiency, courage, creativity, and resilience. This final objective was achieved by the direct involvement of educators and participating organizations that address the needs of parents and families in their everyday work. Therefore the primary target group of this project was adult educators working with parents/families in various contexts such as schools, adult education institutions, or the social care field. They shared significant interests and expertise in practice and engage with participants with similar core values.

The needs addressed in this project are:
Need for better techniques and tools to  support and empower families, who are at risk of being marginalized due to diverse reasons. 
By sharing the best family support practices from each partner country and with better competencies of trainers and student, partners aim to have new tools and methods for preventing families from dropping out from society and thus promoting social inclusion in a diverse way.
This project focuses on developing tools that will improve prior knowledge, skills and attitudes of the professionals and students of family support.
The project will have a cross-generational impact by focusing on supporting active parenting and empowerment of parents who are consciously involved in children’s life and act as role models for active citizenship.
The project also addresses a modern challenge which is a need for cross-cultural skills among experts and today’s citizens of Europe.
More diverse societies require more diverse and culturally sensitive competencies, both from individuals, public service providers and professionals in the parents/family support
sector.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of this project which are in conformity with this Erasmus+KA2 are listed as follows: 
1. To engage educators with a focus on developing and Organizing training for the primary target group, which is the adult educators working with
parents/families tools that will build on the competencies of trainers/educators and students from the social sector, for them to be able to offer better support for families in their everyday lives. 
2. To collaborate and have direct involvement with educators at schools and adult institutions, in creating, self-assessment, and evaluation tools and adapting resources to promote the process of developing self-awareness, being physically and emotionally present, stress management, and effective communication. 
3. To promote and exploit the transformational benefits of ICT, like benchmarking and sharing best practices from the field of family social services and thus learn from each other. 
4. Cooperate and disseminate information about the project via adult education institutions and social care field.
6. Discover and exchange practice activities that will be used to develop new methods and modules for future services.  
5.. To implement the final product within the respective partner countries and development of an open online resource that disseminates the important aspects of the results EN 65

In the EPSIR project, the partners have learned a great deal on the different family situations,challenges, service structures etc. in five different countries. The work that is done toempower parents ́ and children ́s resilience has been analyzed and discussed in versatile,
multidisciplinary ways. It has also been really important to strengthen the competencies in ICT and also ERASMUS+ projects all in all.
For individual participants of this project, the outcome has been significant way to build personal competence and resilience, ict-skills and language skills in order to implement better work with families in the future. The project consortium is very versatile compilation of different kind of organisations which has been both a strength to build different perspectives on the content, but also a challenge when the partners have to build common understanding without getting too deep into the field-specific topics..In this project there were no intellectual outputs, but very practical and useable material was shared during the international trainings. This material is a great help in disseminating the learnings of this project. When evaluating the cooperation of the project partners, the inconsistencies of the application, and the division of tasks and responsibilities. The
communication has been respectful throughout the project even though there has been difficulties to keep up with some of the agreed deadlines.
Some of the partners have planned to continue cooperation in future projects. Also the stakeholders who have took part in dissemination events have shared their interest to take part in future project applications.

<< Implementation >>
