2020-1-NO01-KA204-076547.title: “Democratic Heritage - Memorials and heritage museums engaging migrants in developing resilient democracies”
2020-1-NO01-KA204-076547.summary:
<< Background >>

Migration challenges the attitudes of European governments, populations and individuals in both our current and future generations. Countries all over Europe are engaged in developing strategies in integration and education of migrants, refugees and newcomers, and national and transnational institutions are still only beginning to develop suitable frameworks education in common, democratic values, civic engagement and participation with migrant adult learners. Integrating newcomers into our societies is a challenge which can only be solved on a transnational level.

In our project, partners working with cultural heritage gathered to develop a cross-European forum where we shared and evaluated our best practices in adult migrant learning of common values, civil and democratic competencies: experiences and methods in working with newcomers, refugees and migrants. Using the European Councils democratic competencies together with the expertise from our institutions current learning programs, DH wished to share and develop best practices on how institutions can further develop their innovative participatory methodologies and activities minted on newcomers, refugees and migrant populations in differing European contexts.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of DH was to share and develop the institutions' innovative participatory methodologies, and see how they correspond to the learning requirements detailed in the Council of Europe’s democratic competencies. This was ensured through the committing to a series of transnational best practice workshops and the production of a handbook, serving as intellectual outputs co-produced by all project partners.

A second objective was to collate and collect the data from the activities to help generate more information on the effect that this methodology can have on refugee, migrants and newcomers, relating to the European Council Democratic Competencies. This was planned to be ensured through the development of a survey by the World Value Survey which was to serve as a second intellectual output and was to allow the collection of underrepresented data from migrant, refugee and newcomer populations. This second intellectual output, however, was affected by force majeure.

<< Implementation >>

The project included workshops on best practices across borders, data gathering as well as evaluation of innovative methods and practices. The evaluation was partly conducted based on surveys and questionnaires developed by the project group in addition to best practices, and provided new and useful knowledge which may prove to further advance the knowledge of democratic learning for migrants, refugees and newcomers. Based on the knowledge-sharing on best practices, the partners jointly developed a Handbook.

<< Results >>

The partner organisations jointly produced a Handbook: Democratic Heritage - a handbook for memorials and heritage museums engaging migrants in developing resilient democracies.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
Reception and integration of refugees and migrants
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-PL01-KA204-081598.title: Box of our Memories - Adult education programme caring for memory loss
2020-1-PL01-KA204-081598.summary:
<< Background >>

Contemporary societies are aging, leading to an increase in the number of people affected by dementia and other memory-related conditions. There is an urgent need for effective interventions and tools that will help these individuals maintain their quality of life and preserve their memories.
Moreover, a lack of available suitable resources has been diagnosed. There are limited educational and therapeutic programs available for individuals with dementia, especially those based on reminiscence. The "Box of our Memories" project aimed to address this gap by providing innovative and personalized tools for reminiscence therapy in close collaboration with GLAM sector institutions.
Another premise was to improve the quality of care for older persons. The project sought to enhance the care provided to older adults, particularly those suffering from dementia, by stimulating their memory, cognitive abilities, and emotions through digital memory boxes.
Equally important was the support for informal caregivers. The "Box of our Memories" project aimed not only to help individuals with dementia but also to support their informal caregivers, who often face difficulties and challenges associated with caring for persons with memory disorders.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the Box of our Memories project was to increase the accessibility of reminiscence-based, informal educational interventions for older adults with dementia and other manifestations of cognitive memory loss.
The project's assumption was to develop an innovative informal adult education program dedicated to professionals from the GLAM sector (Galleries, Libraries, Archives, and Museums) and family members caring for individuals with such conditions. The program involved engaging end beneficiaries (individuals with dementia) in the educational process outside the formal training system. It was designed to be short-term and voluntary.
The project's mission was to address the priority of developing the skills of adult educators to support the implementation of Dementia-Friendly Programs. It aimed to provide museum educators and family members with the necessary knowledge and skills to effectively engage and support individuals with dementia and cognitive memory loss. This reinforcement leads to improved caregiving practices and enhances the quality of life for seniors with these conditions.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, the consortium undertook and implemented the following activities:
- Development of four intellectual outputs: Methodological Handbook with Implementation Strategy, Continuous Professional Development Course, Toolkit, and an application for creating digital memory boxes.
- Creation of an online platform containing all project outputs, designed for informal educational interventions for older adults with dementia.
- Conducting six local pilot phases to test the training methodology and project outcomes.
- Organizing four international partner meetings.
- Carrying out one international short-term learning/teaching/training activity.
- Hosting eight dissemination events in each partner country.
- Promoting the expansion of dementia-friendly programs.
- Establishing and fostering effective cooperation with project-associated partners.

<< Results >>

Through the implementation of activities undertaken in the project, the consortium achieved the following results and outcomes:
- Methodological Handbook, containing a guide to the educational process and an implementation strategy for decision-makers. This handbook serves as a valuable toolkit for educators, assisting them in effectively implementing a reminiscence-based approach in their work.
- Innovative Continuous Professional Development (CPD) Course for adult educators.
- Online toolkit for informal adult education, designed for caregivers, family members, and volunteers.
- Platform and application - digital memory boxes. This innovative platform allows seniors and individuals with dementia to record their memories and experiences in digital form, supporting reminiscence therapy.
- 55 educators participating in the pilot phase.
- Creation of 70 digital memory boxes during project activities.
- 13 educators took part in international, short-term learning/teaching/training activities.
- One project website in 7 European languages.
- Developed branding and project layout.
- Approximately 40,000 individuals were direct and indirect recipients of activities promoting the project and its outcomes.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-PL01-KA204-081837.title: BestBonds - extending the competences of adult educators
2020-1-PL01-KA204-081837.summary:
<< Background >>

To compensate for the following shortcomings in the conduct of adult education by our adult educators:
- to understand each other very well in order to make the learning process as effective as possible. The effectiveness is very dependable on educators' preparedness and openness,
- to supply the learners with viable, valid and proper learning methodologies and curricula . Adult learners are much different from youth learners, coming from different, often complicated backgrounds, which often become a fundament for future misunderstandings, unintended results, demotivation and, in a later scope, lack of desired knowledge,
- to presents itself in the form of poor educators' knowledge about not only the learning process itself but, and most of all, motivational strategies, linguistic toolsets, methodologies,
- to be an expert in ICT classroom elements like Social Media and educational policies. Those were crucial in conducting an inclusive and professional teaching-learning process,
- to have online learing space for future work,

<< Objectives >>

For us, the results we have achieved in this project are the ones we pursued. Firstly, ideas and guidelines when working with heterogeneous and diversified classes of adult students, to offer them a personalised and diversified teaching approach to improve the quality of learning. And secondly, sharing good practices according to each partner’s area of specialisation and the creation of a Tool Box - a set of useful tools (online and
offline) for adult teachers, that can be easily used in the classroom with the adults. These can be found on the project’s website.

We would add a third goal, which has been the opportunity of getting to know how each country works with their students, their educational system and the rich cultural heritage of each European region we have visited. Today we know more about Europe and respect each country’s specific traits.

The project made it possible to learn about different educational systems dedicated to adult education. Since there is richness in diversity, it was possible to discuss the different methods and find strengths and weaknesses for each one. The comparison has certainly enriched the participants by providing new ideas, new approaches and new contents to experiment with their learners.

<< Implementation >>

All the proposed activities suggested by the partners float around the idea of action learning. Learning activities provide an important quantity of hands-on lessons in a cooperative learning environment. Peer learning is promoted in these activities. Examples of these can be found both in digital and in traditional face to face format. Highlighting the use of video recording and simple editing through Chromakey and Flipgrid, many traditional tasks were reinterpreted by using gamification.

The application of game-design elements and game principles in the context of adult education provides a scenario where non-formal education is viable and attractive.

.The objective when using these methods is catering for diversity as one of the common traits in our students is the wide range of characters according to the learning styles, needs and motivation.
Thanks to this kind of modern, action-promoting methodology all of the participants had the opportunity to widen their perspective not only as part of the project, but also in other fields of education. Moreover, it was easy to see that gamification enabled the participants to learn even when they were not really aware of it

<< Results >>

Tangible results of the Project are, as follows:
1. An online learning space, for all future learning purposes, for both the educators and learners to use. - www.bestbonds.com.pl
2. A set of guidelines, intellectually and methodologically valid in accordance with the need of educators and learners.
3. An inclusive teacher's profile.
4. A toolbox for all the lesson plans and scenarios.
5. 2 wideos from the trainings in Croatia & Greece.
6. leaflets of the project.

Intangible results of this project are:
1. A good practice network.
2. Exchanging and gaining knowledge through international bonds.
3. Improving the sets of offered services by all partner organizations.
4. Being able to pinpoint all of the strong and weak suits of given national formal education systems.

2020-1-PL01-KA204-082090.title: "On time" competences
2020-1-PL01-KA204-082090.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the implementation of this project due to the existing challenges associated with the transition of partner countries to a market economy, the globalization of world markets, and increased competition for local entities. The project aimed to find new ways to ensure long-term existence and success in the face of these changes. The primary motivation for undertaking this project was the need to strengthen basic skills and develop key competencies of adults, especially those socially excluded. The project sought to address contemporary requirements where a key element of success in competition is also the social inclusion of representatives of disadvantaged groups.
The detailed objectives of the project included identifying the educational needs of adults from disadvantaged groups, activating and motivating the target group to engage in educational activities, introducing effective tools to enhance key competencies, promoting the concept of lifelong learning, strengthening basic skills, developing key competencies of socially excluded individuals, and presenting examples of successfully implemented projects in adult education and social inclusion.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to achieve a series of goals through the implementation of the project, addressing dynamic economic and social changes in partner countries. Our main goal was to confront the challenges arising from economic transformations, global markets' globalization, and increased competition. The project aimed to find new ways to ensure long-term existence and success, especially in the context of intensified competition from domestic entities.
Through the education of adults from disadvantaged groups, the project sought to strengthen basic skills and develop key competencies. Detailed objectives included identifying educational needs, activating and motivating participants to take active educational measures, and promoting the concept of lifelong learning. The project implementation had an interactive character, involving various forms of work. Participants were not only meant to acquire knowledge but also to explore the culture, art, and history of the hosting countries, contributing to an understanding of the national characteristics of the partners, mutual cultural exchange, and dispelling stereotypes.

<< Implementation >>

During the project implementation, we conducted seven adult learner mobilities with diverse thematic scopes in partner countries: Poland, Serbia, Croatia, and Italy, with significant involvement of local communities. Additionally, project meetings were held twice in a traditional format, and multiple online meetings took place with representatives of partner organizations. Furthermore, we produced a project activities film and are currently conducting research on a group of 2000 individuals regarding the effects of the diagnosis and recognition of key competencies developed in the project.

<< Results >>

Participants of the project expanded their knowledge in the field of adult education regarding the strengthening of basic skills and the development of key competencies for socially excluded individuals. As a result of their participation in the project, participants:
Familiarized themselves with methods of identifying educational needs of adults from disadvantaged groups.
Expanded their knowledge in the activation and motivation of the target group to engage in active educational activities.
Learned about effective tools to enhance key competencies of adults.
Broadened their knowledge in promoting the concept of lifelong learning among adults.
Strengthened basic skills of representatives from disadvantaged groups.
Developed key competencies for socially excluded individuals as a key to a better future.
Presented examples of successfully implemented projects in adult education and social inclusion.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-PL01-KA204-082111.title: Volunteering for Heritage – Best Practice Exchange
2020-1-PL01-KA204-082111.summary:
<< Background >>

Both to us and our project partners, engaging volunteers in protecting and popularising cultural heritage is an important aspect of our activities. However, models and good practices in this area differ significantly between countries. The goal of the exchange of good practices was mutual inspiration and discovering various models of operation. The comparison of experiences from Great Britain and Finland was very interesting. Both countries have long traditions of involving people in volunteering, but the volunteers are mainly the elderly and the challenge is to reach youth. In Croatia and in Poland it is mostly students who get involved, whereas retired people are the least active group. Thus, each partner was hoping to get inspirations for working with different age groups. To all partners it was the first best practices exchange in this area, so the project, apart from exploring the experiences of other organisations, invited the organizations to reflect on their own activities in order to accurately present them to the other partners.

<< Objectives >>

The overarching goal of the project was the development of volunteering for heritage and strengthening social awareness concerning this issue. We want to pursue this objective (strengthening social awareness is always a long-term process) by educating the organisations’ staff who work with volunteers as well as through discovering interesting models of operation that can translate into new solutions in our organisations, increasing their attractiveness to potential new volunteers.
Thus, the first objective was to increase the organisations’ staff competences through trainings and exchange of good practices. The next step was to share the new experiences with the staff and volunteers of the organisations. An additional goal was to inspire the volunteers and show them the significance of their work. Thus, the volunteers who had been active in their organisations for a long time were also involved in the project.
Ultimately, we want to create the best possible conditions for getting involved, so that volunteering would be gratifying to the people getting involved, and simultaneously wouldn’t just be a one-sided effort for heritage – we want it to be a developing and educational experience to the participants.

<< Implementation >>

Within the project, 4 study visits were organized – one at each partner’s place of operation – and 2 trainings: one devoted to volunteer management, and the other to the method of “heritage interpretation” applied in work with audiences at heritage sites. The study visits concerned the practices of working with volunteers in the respective countries. In Finland the partners visited local, grassroots museums led by volunteers. In Great Britain they visited churches under the care of Churches Conservation Trust, which are made available to the public thanks to the engagement of volunteers. In Poland and Croatia, the participants observed volunteer projects aimed at youth and
students. 3 representatives of the respective organisations took part in each study visit. In case of the Satakunta Museum they were museum employees, and in case of the other 3 organisations they were employees and representatives of volunteers.

<< Results >>

Above all else, the activities within the project translated into the improvement of the staffs’ competences, who subsequently applied the gained insights and experiences in their work with volunteers. As one of the training participants put it, “Considering that I regularly work and take part in creating volunteers’ tasks, I will be able to directly apply what I learned with immediate effects. It was also very gratifying and inspiring to meet volunteers who take care of the heritage sites we visited.” By equipping practitioners, we can count on them directly applying these insights in their daily work. Beside the activity of the employees, the project also translated into broader activities of
the organisations – e.g. in Finland they started promoting volunteering among younger people; in Poland we recruited new volunteers for cooperation.
As a result of implementing the project:
- 11 people were trained in managing and cooperating with volunteers;
- 11 people were trained in the “heritage interpretation” method and its use by volunteers active at heritage sites;
- 10 networking meetings with other organisations active in the culture and heritage sector took place.

2020-1-PL01-KA204-082125.title: Singing community - exchange of experiences on activation practices for adults and seniors through the choir
2020-1-PL01-KA204-082125.summary:
<< Background >>

Activating seniors and adults, encouraging their active social, cultural and LLL participation, is one of the most important tasks facing all partner institutions involved in this project, especially given demographic trends. Directly related to it is the need to develop conducting skills, especially those related to the ability to work with seniors and intergenerational ensembles, methods of activating them, how to conduct rehearsals, how to communicate and prepare rehearsals, how to select repertoire.
We were told about these challenges by conductors leading such ensembles, and always working in an international project and being able to exchange experiences, knowledge and skills makes it possible to meet these needs.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to exchange experiences between partner institutions and conductors on social, cultural and LLL activation of adults and seniors through singing in choirs. This objective fits perfectly with the horizontal priority: social inclusion. 
Developing a set of methods for working with senior and intergenerational choirs, methods of activating them, as participation in choir rehearsals and concerts is a proven method of social and cultural inclusion for people from different age and social groups, and through these activities - building social capital. It is also a very good method of realising LLL, because during rehearsals, adults, senior citizens learn new songs, they learn singing techniques; they get to know musical pieces or folk songs, which are often part of the European cultural heritage, they get to know their history and cultural context; they practice memory, concentration of attention, and breathing exercises contribute to improving their physical condition, especially for seniors. Through systematic rehearsal meetings, all participants also develop their social competences.
It is mainly these goals that we wanted to achieve through the SingingCom project.

<< Implementation >>

The main project activities, implemented in this project, were:
- 4 transnational partnership meetings in Lodz/Poland, Rijeka/Croatia, Pécs/Hungary and Maribor/Slovenia, the main aim of which was to exchange experiences between conductors, managers and coordinators of amateur choirs, as well as choristers;
- vocal workshops, led by conductors or choir leaders from each partner institution, for adults, seniors or intergenerational choirs; workshops were held once a week, 2h each rehearsal; workshops started in February 2021 and were conducted online until May due to the COVID-19 pandemic;
- a final concert performed by all the amateur choirs involved in the project; each choir prepared a total of 6 pieces in the languages of the partner institutions and L.von Beethoven's "Ode to Joy"; the concerts were recorded, edited and uploaded to the project's YouTube channel;
- The concerts were recorded, edited and posted on the project's YouTube channel; a PDF brochure was produced and published, containing a collection of best practices and methods for working with amateur choirs, activating adults and seniors to participate in this type of cultural activity and counteracting the social exclusion of these groups.

<< Results >>

1. To acquire new skills and develop the professional competence of conductors and choir leaders in the field of activating seniors and adults; voice emission teaching methods; exercises for correct breathing technique; musicalisation and rhythm formation; correct voice impostation habits.
2. Collection and compilation of examples of best practices and methods of work with amateur intergenerational choirs, choirs consisting of seniors and adults (activating seniors and adults; methods of teaching voice emission; exercises developing correct breathing technique; exercises developing habits of correct voice impostation) in the form of a brochure.
3. To produce and record 4 final concerts and upload them to the SingingCom YouTube channel.
4. Experience of working in an international team, especially during the TPM, where the working language was English, using various communication tools such as video conferencing on Zoom, WhatsApp messenger.
5. Development of voice emission skills, social competences, increase of social and cultural activities of the participating choristers.
6. Expansion of the choirs' repertoire.

2020-1-PL01-KA204-082140.title: Portal Project - transition of LARP to the field of adult education
2020-1-PL01-KA204-082140.summary:
<< Background >>

"Portal Project" was our first step on the field of adult education. We responded to need of developing increasingly important social skills, such as: confidence, empathy, negotiation, flexibility, resilience, the ability to shift perspectives, thinks out-of-the-box and step into someone else's shoes. We assumed that inclusion and tolerance are also skills which need training. We assumed that nowadays adults need training even more than youth, which is already raised on games and finds it easier to adopt to everchanging modern environment.

We were linked by the passion to LARP (live action role playing) and belonging to an informal Portal Larp Community, which has organized international Larp Conventions since 2012 in South-Eastern Europe. The twist of the Project was to explore the hidden layers of education, learning and personal development in larp games which do not bear an "EDU" prefix in the title. After two years of meeting and working together, we feel much confident as larp designers to provide adult players with meaningful tools of life-long learning through playing fictional characters in narrative worlds.

<< Objectives >>

1. COOPERATION
A. To strengthen the cooperation between the partner organizations that implement LARP as educational tool.
B. To increase the mobility of Eastern-European larpers and game-designers on the European level.
C. To get Larp games implemented by the local public Institutions which cope with social inclusion on the municipal level.

2. RECOGNITION
A. To create an open-source tool to assess educational outputs of various LARPs within the Erasmus+ framework
B. To share Larp scenarios with a wider audience though Portal Convents and Portal Webpage
C. To establish the Portal Community as an recognized entity connecting larpers and game-designers on European level

3. EDUCATION 
- To engage adult learners from difficult background in LARP games which aim at:
A. Transforming negative attitudes towards migrants, minorities and other socially excluded groups of people
B. Including adults from difficult backgrounds (migrants, convicts, unemployed) into high-quality learning activities
C. Promoting European values of personal freedom, human dignity, solidarity and social responsibility

<< Implementation >>

The innovative (and risky) part of the "Portal Project" was to combine LTT mobilities with open 3-day long international events, namely:

- PoRtaL 9 Larp Convention (Athens, 10-12 September 2021) 
--> https://www.facebook.com/events/745555806354962/

- Portal 10 LARP Conference (Kraków, 24-26 June 2022)
--> https://www.facebook.com/events/826579681380559/

Besides 45 project participants, founded by the grant, there were 255 extra participants from 22 European countries who have joined us in-person and at their own cost to take part in both Conventions.

Both LTT mobilities also comprised of 4-day long internal Workshops of skills and scenarios exchange prepared by the participants themselves.

Three TPM strategic meeting were organized in Budapest, Zagreb and Plovdiv, where we had workshops with local larp communities.

180 adult players have played our local games design for immersive experience towards social inclusion, with extended briefing sessions exploring the educational layers of larping.

The Project was disseminated at international Edu-Larp Conferences and Knutepunkt conventions (Oslo 2021 and Linkoping 2022), thanks to the project budget, Portal Community could enter the European community of larpers and educators.

<< Results >>

The recorded outputs are:

- 31 Videos from the Conventions:

2020-1-PL01-KA204-082210.title: Online Education Now
2020-1-PL01-KA204-082210.summary:
<< Background >>

As a result of the pandemic, the activities of our organizations had to change so far. For this reason, a large part of activities related to the development of education was interrupted for many months. This made it necessary to change the approach and transfer training activities to the Internet. Due to the mismatch between the needs and the real skills of the activists of the partner organizations, a project was created to improve training techniques in a virtual and hybrid form.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to improve the ability to use Internet tools in the work of a trainer in an adult environment. The project facilitated the exchange of good practices between organizations from different backgrounds, strengthened international cooperation, facilitated the transfer of knowledge, involved adults from different backgrounds and with different backgrounds, provided knowledge that will be used in the future, increased the quality of educational activities and gave the opportunity to create new partner networks. An important goal was to match the skills of volunteers involved in the daily work of our organizations with its real needs and challenges, but also with the opportunities that digital development gives us.

<< Implementation >>

The partnership organized a series of five international meetings accompanied by hybrid training on the following topics: digitization and documentation (preparation of digital materials); digital competences in the work of a trainer; trainer's rights and obligations (copyright and press law); trainer's tools; exam system in the digital age and project summary. In addition, a series of training sessions and presentations in the form of online conferences were organized on topics related to the transfer of knowledge as part of non-formal education. As part of local activities, after each international meeting, the partners organized local meetings aimed at sharing good practices developed in the project.

<< Results >>

The project significantly contributed to improving the quality of knowledge transfer in on-line and hybrid form, which the partnership has so far used only in individual cases. Thanks to the project, a large part of educational activities has moved to the Internet. The skills of activists of individual partner organizations in transferring knowledge, especially in the field of digital competences, have significantly improved. The project enabled the exchange of good practices between representatives of organizations with different competences and interests. Incidentally, the project improved the skills of intergenerational and international cooperation thanks to the participation of people of different ages from different European countries. Finally, the project developed knowledge in the use of Internet resources in the work of trainers and increased knowledge of legal regulations in the context of open education.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-1-PL01-KA204-082226.title: Active senior academy
2020-1-PL01-KA204-082226.summary:
<< Background >>

We wanted to implement this project because so far we have not had the opportunity to implement activities under "Adult Education". We believed that due to the implementation of local activities with seniors by all partner organizations of the project, it would be natural to take these activities to the international level. We wanted to enrich older people with a package of competences that they need for everyday functioning. Moreover, we wanted to compare the needs of adults in Poland, Serbia, Croatia, BiH and Ukraine and show common features and differences.
The project responded to the specific needs of older people participating in it, such as: the desire for social and family activity of older people, and at the same time the need to exchange experiences and skills from different countries, in order to show both the common features and the diversity that can contribute to deepening knowledge not only scientific but also cultural and social.
The project also responded to the need to learn how to overcome cultural and social barriers, the need to create socially inclusive environments in each region of the country, whose task is, among other things, to support equality and justice at all ages.

<< Objectives >>

Through the project, we wanted to support the social development of older people, improve their family relationships through active participation in society and at the same time include them in social life, improve the quality of life through educational and mental development. The results we would like to achieve are:
1. Increased language skills among senior listeners and accompanying persons
2. A significant increase in historical and cultural knowledge of individual countries among senior listeners and accompanying persons
3. Increasing the digital competences of project participants among senior listeners and accompanying persons using a computer and the Internet
4. Further joint project and non-project activities,
5. Dissemination European values among senior listeners and accompanying persons
6. Comp increase social among senior listeners and accompanying persons
7. Increased involvement of staff and volunteers in working with older people
8. Increased knowledge about working with older people according to specific thematic issues and listeners - seniors and accompanying persons, staff and volunteers
9. Increased competence in methods of educational work with older people among staff and volunteers.

<< Implementation >>

During the project we completed:
- a short training program for people working with older people
- five combined mobilities for older people and their caregivers
- four international design meetings
- local activities

<< Results >>

PARTNER COOPERATION
1. Increased cooperation between partners and built lasting partnership,
2. Exchange of good practices between older people from Poland, Serbia, Croatia,
3. Exchange of good practices between staff from Poland, Ukraine, Croatia, Serbia and BiH.
CULTURAL
1. Eliminating barriers resulting from general stereotypes,
2. International dialogue,
3. Cultural and cultural exchange,
4. Integration of older people - making new friends,
5. Building bonds between EU citizens and preventing nationalism.
6. Promotion of good neighborly practices
EDUCATIONAL
1. Gaining more knowledge in the field of digital competences,
2. Learning new languages for older people
BUILDING A CONSCIOUS SOCIETY
1. Increased knowledge about other cultures and religions
2. Fight against stereotypes and prejudices of older people towards people from other countries
By implementing the project, partner organizations, students, staff and volunteers will increase their key competences.

2020-1-PT01-KA204-078785.title: Stop epidemic growth through learning
2020-1-PT01-KA204-078785.summary:
<< Background >>

At the time of the application, the COVID-19 pandemic was having a strong impact in everyday life and creating an unprecedented challenge to health and care systems worldwide. Numerous measures to respond to the urgent care needs of those impacted were taken, while also trying to reduce the long-term impact on vulnerable people, in all ways possible. The pandemic brought huge pressures to health and care systems, particularly governments, managers and frontline staff. Since the first cases appeared, countries developed several strategies, adapted services and a wide range of innovations came up, requiring flexibility, especially to address people’s continued care. The emergency state, the use of teleworking, the social distance, all implied uncovering new methods of work, understanding society’s biggest fragilities and brought changes in work and training, tools and routines that came to stay for the years to come. In this process of living “remotely”, by far younger generations had an easier adaptation. Already used to partially live through social media, online sources of knowledge and agile change of methods, the Millennials and Generation Z have used digital technology since a young age and could still be fully connected and maintain their training and work activities with minor deviations. However, this is not the case of the generations born before the 1980's. If, besides age, we address adults with lower qualifications and skills, as it is often the case in the care sector, this was more serious, as they are easily hampered in the search of reliable information due to missing digital skills. Apart from all the innovations that are being developed and new ways of delivering services, there was the need for bottom-up initiatives that build-up the competences of adults through informal/non-formal education, with a special focus on social care professionals, community leaders, informal caregivers and volunteers so that these are prepared to deal with such emergency situations in the future.

<< Objectives >>

The STEP-UP project developed a training tool for adult education where they are introduced to on the impact of behaviours in the spread of a pandemic, through gaming strategies. STEP UP’s educational game aims to train adult learners, being the main target groups community leaders, care professionals, municipality workers and volunteers, especially in their role as educational agents of the broader community, focusing on adults with lower skills and qualifications. 
Our main objectives were to:
•	Develop a meaningful, supportive and innovative training toolkit including the game, training materials and guidance.
•	Ensure wider exploitation and contribute to informal education, especially of those with lower skills and qualifications, by the low access thresholds of a recreational game.
•	Train, empower and support care professionals, community leaders, informal caregivers and volunteers in dealing with emergency situations caused by pandemics.
•	Offer target-group oriented guidelines and insights on early detection, preventive measures, healthcare and social care interventions, policy measures and communication to stakeholders at social and political level.
•	Ensure the outreach and sustainable impacts of the project results.

<< Implementation >>

The STEP-UP partners started by developing a wide desk research on COVID-19 measures, and organized workshops with health and social care professionals, municipality officials, and volunteers to collect information for guidelines development. Each partner was responsible for one theme and performed this together with the target groups, engaging 41 participants in workshops and interviews. The findings were documented in thematic reports that were published in the project website.
These reports were the basis for the Social and Policy interventions Manual, aimed to offer target-group oriented guidelines and insights on 1) early detection, 2) preventive measures, 3) health and social care interventions, 4) policy measures and 5) communication. All partners promoted an extensive review of relevant and accurate materials on COVID19 and other relevant epidemic or pandemic outbreaks, and societal measures to deal with emergency situations were analised and integrated. The work led by AFE included preparing the structure of the manual, a survey that collected feedback from 133 participants, the writing of the manual itself, peer reviews and second opinion check with interviewees, and concluded with the translation and dissemination of the Manual. 
To further exploit all materials collected for the reports and Manual, a Virtual Library, hosted on the STEP-UP website, was developed, with contributions of all partners, led by AFE and SHINE, accompanied by an open call for materials that was not foreseen in the proposal but was an additional engagement and enrichment method.
The STEP_UP game was developed in a collaborative and co-created process with 25 participants in interviews/workshops. The partners started to define the themes and formats of the scripts and locations, scenes and characters involved, also the level of digital literacy and gathered the needs and requirements of learners. A document with the first game breakdown was created by SHINE and each partner developed one character with 5 scenes, the measures to be considered and their expected impacts, in a total of 25 scenes, all peer-reviewed and refined together in the consortium. The stakeholder consultation brought to the partners attention several refinements, as well as measures to prevent/mitigate the pandemic spread that were then included in the game plan. The game was fully developed, and it is available in 6 languages at https://stepupgame.eu/ 
To add to the game and Manual and ensure reach to those less (digitally) literate, STEP_UP developed a Trainers Toolkit and Workshop Methodology that provide adult education facilitators with the tools needed to use the game and other project results in group trainings. The toolkit contains a workshop concept suitable for the game, including options for interactive methods, a video, handouts for different sessions, rewards, certification templates and teaching aids, namely on the use of digital media. It can be used as a single document or downloaded in parts in the Trainer Area, to increase easiness of use.
All project results were presented at 1 (inter)national and 4 national multiplier events with the active participation of the target groups, involving 160 people, to add to 212 participants in the different consultation activities for IOs development.

<< Results >>

The STEP_UP project produced the following results:
STEP_UP Gaming tool (O1): an educational game (also open to recreational usage) to train community leaders, health and social care professionals, municipality workers and volunteers associations on the actual impact of behaviours in the spread of a pandemic / health threatening emergency situation. The game includes preventive measures, impacts and the different levels of measures that individuals, organisations and authorities could take. The game is hosted in an online learning platform in 6 languages that provides an accessible and intuitive entry to all results and will be sustained by SHINE for at least 10 years.
STEP_UP Virtual Library (additional output): developed by SHINE and hosted in the project website, allows all interested people/organisations to filter and search for over 500 COVID19 measures, duly categorised, in all partner languages plus English.
Social and Policy interventions Manual (O2): provides reliable information and guidelines in regard to: introduction on epidemic and pandemic virus outbreaks; early detection; early outbreak of the health emergency; the outbreak is epidemic or pandemic; exit strategy or open-up again; published online in 6 languages. 
Thematic Reports (02): 5 reports available in English on the STEP_UP platform: Early detection (AFE); Preventive measures (SHINE); Health measures (CIPH); Policy measures (ISIS); Communication (WISE).
Survey results (O2): structured overview of opinions on COVID19 measures by 133 participants.
Trainer Toolkit and workshop methodology (O3): offers a user-friendly approach to work with the STEP-UP game thus making use of digital media in adult education. The materials provide access to trainers on background information and methods to discuss contents of the game, as well as the broad range of preventive measures that contribute to a deceleration of infections. It is available in all partner languages and English in a single document and also as a downloadable kit of materials from the STEP_UP platform – Trainers Area.
STEP_UP Briefing paper: with ways to directly address adult educators, political decision-makers and lobby-groups at the local, regional and national level.
STEP_UP Sustainability Plan: an action plan to enhance the sustainability of the game and project results with strategies for dissemination and the plans and concrete actions for further exploitation of STEP_UP.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-PT01-KA204-078846.title:
Developing a strategic European framework for digital
competences for adult education organisations
2020-1-PT01-KA204-078846.summary:
<< Background >>

The EU3Digital consortium identified the need for a more strategic approach to the adoption of IT and the development of associated competencies in a context where many Third Sector Organisations (TSOs) and Social Enterprised (SEs) had adopted different tech packages and applications as a matter of urgency in response to their pressing need to digitise, including the Covid-19 pandemic.  Hence, EU3Digital’s Intellectual Outputs (IOs) aimed at enabling organisations to continue the digitalisation journey in a more strategic way and with greater confidence in their competences and skills.

<< Objectives >>

Through developing the digital skills and competencies of TSOs and SEs, EU3Digital aimed to 1) increase the value and sustainability of  TSOs and SEs; 2)  improve their access to digital tools and dissemination of good practices and resources; 3) increase TSOs and SEs perceived value and effective application of digital competencies in the European third sector; 4) empower, and strengthen the third sector as a whole; and 5)  developing more integrated advocacy for digital inclusion in the Third Sector.
The project did so, by developing a shared understanding of the challenges facing TSOs and SEs in the digitalisation of their organisational processes and systems. Furthermore, the project identified digital competences, which led to the development of a competence framework to meet the unique circumstances of the sector.  The EU3Digital developed practical resources to help TSOs and SEs to develop digital competences and skills to address these challenges. Last but not least, the policy paper aimed at providing a solid basis for advocacy to develop digital competences for the benefit of the European third sector, as well as to inform policymakers at EU level about the needs of the sector to digitalise.

<< Implementation >>

The EU3Digital project involved various activities and meetings to support the development of intellectual outputs and enhance digital skills in third sector organisations and social enterprises. Transnational meetings were organised online and in-person in Spain, and the Netherlands, focusing on project management, planning, knowledge exchange, and addressing implementation issues. The project also conducted three short-term joint staff training events (LTTs) in Portugal, Spain, and Croatia, addressing organisational digital transformation and strategic thinking. Assessment sessions were held after each training activity to gather feedback and improve the training curricula (Curricula Design IO2). A multiplier event was organized by Euclid Network in the Netherlands to disseminate project outputs and promote digital transformation in social enterprises. Consortium and bilateral meetings facilitated collaboration and project progress. Research, including a literature review and interviews, informed the project's approach, while fellows provided valuable input on the competence framework and toolkit.

<< Results >>

EU3Digital was a project dedicated to enhancing digital skills and competences in the third sector and social enterprises. It developed multiple outputs to address the digital needs and challenges of these organisations, such as: 1) The Framework of Digital Competences which identified specific digital skills and competences required by third-sector organizations, serving as a foundation for subsequent outputs. 2) The EU3Digital Curriculum Design which was refined through pilot training activities in different countries, offering practical and effective instruction for acquiring digital skills. 3) The Policy Paper: Titled "Digital Support for Social Impact," which targeted stakeholders involved in sector development, promoting digital inclusion and emphasizing the importance of the digital competences framework. 4) The toolkit on Digital Skills which provided practical guidance, open-access tools, and resources to enable organisations to adapt dynamically to digital advancements. Additionally, the project featured a podcast, "MASTER EU3D," offering insights, practical advice, and discussions on the latest digital trends and innovations in the European Union, further supporting the project's objectives.

Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-RO01-KA204-080000.title: SENSE (of) Community
2020-1-RO01-KA204-080000.summary:
<< Background >>

The project addressed topics such as social inclusion, employability and entrepreneurial initiative of disadvantaged adult learners from rural regions and/or deprived communities. The consortium aimed through the activities developed to exploit the capability of a community-based entrepreneurship model as tool to raise employment, foster social inclusion and lifelong learning participation.
It followed to answer the following needs: 
- the low level of participation in lifelong learning opportunities in the partner communities among low-skilled adults
- the low level of educational attainment highlighted by corresponding research papers
- unemployment & lack of jobs on the local labor market in the partners rural communities, as result an increase in the number of adults from surrounding rural areas they are serving, facing socioeconomic difficulties
- the need to provide new and continuous learning opportunities for supporting social inclusion, employability and entrepreneurial initiative among disadvantaged adult learners
- the need to increase the number of competent and capable educators to provide consistent support to disadvantaged adults.

<< Objectives >>

Specific objectives of the project were:

O1. To develop knowledge, skills and abilities of adult educators from the partner countries in order to create community based entrepreneurship opportunities aimed at
empowering disadvantaged adult learners from rural region and/or deprived communities through promotion of mutual employment of strengths and peer learning activities at international level.

O2. To increase social inclusion, employability and entrepreneurial initiative among disadvantaged adult learners from rural regions and/or deprived communities by delivering of 1 international learning activity on community-based entrepreneurship and practical activities

<< Implementation >>

1. Training Community-based entrepreneurship (Short-term joint staff training events) organized between 18-22.10.2021 in Croatia, Rijeka, targeted to 18 adult educators from the partner organizations involved in the project. It followed to develop participants knowledge and abilities to implement entrepreneurial education opportunities for disadvantaged adult learners.

2. SENSE of Community (Blended mobility of adult learners) organized between 20-24.06.2022, in Portugal, Amadora, targeted to 25 adult learners from the partner communities. It followed to develop participants knowledge and abilities about community-based entrepreneurship, specific steps to open a community-based business, actual planning of business plan models through practical exercises and study visits. 

3. One English course organized by 3 of the partners at local level for 43 adult learners in order to develop their communication skills. 

4. Experiential learning program "SENSE (of) Community" - 3 community-based business plans were elaborated by the participants in C2 in international cooperation.

<< Results >>

Results produced by the project were: 
- 18 adult educators from the partner were trained in the field of community-based entrepreneurship through the development of one Short-term joint staff training events
- 25 disadvantaged adult learners developed knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of community-based entrepreneurship by attending one blended mobility of adult learners
- 1 English course organized in 3 of the partner countries, in total 43 adult learners developed foreign language skills and were empowered to participate in international cooperation with peers
- Practical activity - 3 Community-based entrepreneurship businesses plans were developed the by adult learners involved in the project as result of C2. In Bulgaria the business Swimwithme registered success, as result of the follow up, the municipality of Kardzhali accepted the business idea and agreed to offer funds for the concesion of the premise
- New perspectives for better addressing the needs of our adult learners community, thus increased learning opportunities for disadvantaged adult learners at local levels
- Improvement of the adult education services provided by the organizations
- Developed internationalization of the partner organizations.

2020-1-RO01-KA204-080056.title: Remote Theatre
2020-1-RO01-KA204-080056.summary:
<< Background >>

Foreign languages have a key role among the skills that help people qualify for higher education, then enter or progress in the labor market, and the prominence of foreign language courses in adult education programs organized both by public and private teaching institutions is well established throughout the EU. But the results of these programs are not always in line with expectations. Adult language students are often demotivated by what they perceive to be a lack of progress and an inability to communicate effectively in their target languages. This can translate into high dropout rates which limit the capacity of language teaching institutions to run courses effectively. Language teachers and teacher trainers are constantly reviewing methodologies and techniques in order to improve the efficacy of their work and in recent years, the introduction of new technologies has often been the catalyst for such revision. The main objective of the Remote Theatre project was to provide language teachers and adult language learners with the resources they need to incorporate drama into their language courses on a scale that has never before been attempted, using a range of original resources, developed by experts in the field.

<< Objectives >>

One core part of our project was the introduction of new, innovative teaching methodologies using advance information and communication technologies. With the desire to retain the highest quality service in educational process and in line with the long-term development plans of the partner institutions, the goals of this project were:
- the development of ICT competences and digital literacy of educators for the purpose of modernizing teaching methods and improving the quality of the entire teaching process within the whole institution
- the development of innovative, high-tech educational tools for adult education
- mastering various electronic tools and platforms for developing teaching materials and implementing teaching activities
- the development of creative and critical thinking to facilitate the motivation of teachers and students in selected training courses, as well as other employees within the institution
- promoting and developing digital and virtual literacy among learners for the purpose of ensuring the quality and relevance of education at all levels
- promoting core European value

<< Implementation >>

Project activities included:
1. Development of three separate intellectual outputs, designed to make sure above-listed aims are achieved. To complete this, specific tasks were caried on:
- Researching examples of good practice, gather and analyze various resources arising from partners experience. 
- Writing introductory and methodology chapters
- Writing and editing the plays. 
- Piloting the plays produced in the partners' language schools 
- The development of the training module 
- The development of the CMS, implementation of a security system, the definition of user account roles and access rights, etc.. One lead developer (researcher) from
2. Transnational meetings
3. Short-term joint staff training event
4. Multiplier events as a tool in promoting project results and presenting outputs to large number of interesting parties. 
5. Various dissemination actions, undertaken by all partners at appropriate times, to further contribute to project visibility and sustainability.

<< Results >>

The partners have agreed to produce 3 intellectual outputs (IOs) and they succeeded to deliver:
1. The Remote Theatre Handbook: a manual designed for teachers, teacher trainers, academic managers and content writers. This Handbook is the main training resource for the implementation of Remote Theatre as a language learning methodology in educational institutions. 
2. A collection of RT plays: a publication consisting of 30 plays designed for performing online. All plays are designed to improve language fluency and communication skills in a variety of different contexts. Plays contain all relevant language learning methodologies, focusing predominantly on student-centered learning approach. 
3. Play-it! - an interactive online platform: a complete web-based software solution specifically designed to store, share and enhance all materials related to RT methodology. The platform contains three major components: interactive training module, database of online plays, and a user forum. The link to the platform is https://remotetheatre.amber-it.co/.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2020-1-RO01-KA204-080306.title: INVOLVING PERSONS WITH DOWN SYNDROME IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS THROUGH SERVICE LEARNING
2020-1-RO01-KA204-080306.summary:
<< Background >>

For people with Down syndrome (PDS), life-long learning is not only about learning new skills or vocational training, it´s about being included in society, stating that they have rights to develop a full and effective participation and social inclusion
The 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) call to action. The engagement, inclusion and participation of citizens is pivotal towards realizing the broad goals of sustainable development in such a way that no one is left behind. The success of the 2030 Agenda requires a participatory and inclusive approach in which all stakeholders are engaged and persons with disabilities are equally included as both agents and beneficiaries.
Service Learning is a powerful training methodology for involving PDS and other ID in the implementation of SDGs fostering their social inclusion. 
This approach is not implemented, due to the lack of:
- Awareness on the capacities of PDS as active actors in the implementation of the SDG.
- Knowledge and tools about how to optimize the implementation of the Service-Learning methodology for PDS
- Knowledge and tools of Supports of PDS (mainly professionals and relatives) on how to enhance their involvement in the implementation of SDG through Service Learning.

<< Objectives >>

“SUSTAINABLE-SERVICE-IN-DS” is launched with the main objective of increasing the competences of people with Down syndrome (PDS) and their Supports regarding the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) through Service-Learning, while increasing their social inclusion.
Specific objectives:
•	To make PDS to be active actors in the implementation of SDG and not merely beneficiaries.
•	To increase the engagement of PDS with their local communities, social inclusion and visibility as useful and capable members of the civil society.
•	To transfer knowledge and tools to Supports of PDS in how to be involved in the SDG and to cooperate with PDS.
•	To strengthen the cooperation between Organizations working for PDS and other social stakeholders in order to commonly address problems affecting the local communities

<< Implementation >>

The most important activities implemented in this project are:
Development of a TRAINING SCHEME (IO.1) with the direct participation of PDS and stakeholders in the co-creation workshops. 
Development of a set of 7 LEARNING ACTIVITIES (IO.2) based on the Service-Learning methodology addressed to trainers.  
Development of a set of 7 TRAINING MATERIALS (IO.3) to be used by TRAINEES along the implementation of the SDG-SERVICE-LEARNING FRAMEWORK (I.O.2), adapted to the roles and the different learning needs and individual profiles of the Target Group.
Development of an e-TRAINING PLATFORM (I.O.4) for enhancing the training process. 
Deployment of VALIDATION PILOT ACTIONS in all countries involving PDS, Professionals, Supports and Community Stakeholders where the Experiential Training Methodology was put into practice and tested.
Deployment of a TRANSNATIONAL LEARNING ACTIVITY (blended mobility of adult learners) gathering attendants from participating countries, in Valencia (Spain) in a common learning activity.
Organizing 7 MULTIPLIER EVENTS and introducing the project results to 340 stakeholders.
Dissemination actions reaching 43.828 followers.
Organizing 2 TPM in person, 14 project regular meetings and 6 small staff groups meetings

<< Results >>

The most important concrete outputs and results are:
IO.1  “SUSTAINABLE-SERVICE-IN-DS TRAINING SCHEME”.
-	Procedure Inclusive Working Session 
-	Inclusive Working Sessions 
-	Report on Inclusive Working Sessions 
-	Training Scheme
IO.2 “SUSTAINABLE SERVICE-IN-DS LEARNING ACTIVITIES “.
-	BOOK 1: PHILOSOPHICAL AND THEORETICAL UNDERPINNING. A TRAINING GUIDE FOR ALL
-	BOOK 2: APPROACHES AND CHALLENGES. AN EDUCATIONAL PATH FOR ALL
-	BOOK 3: TRAINING ACTIVITIES FOR PEOPLE WITH DOWN SYNDROME. A GUIDE FOR TRAINERS – set of 7 Learning Activities
IO.3 “TRAINING MATERIALS”.
-	A set of 7 workbooks for trainees, one for each learning activity
-	2 videoclips for understanding SDGs and service learning
IO.4 “SUSTAINABLE SERVICE-DS e-TRAINING PLATFORM”
-	e-Training Platform
-	set of e-games for improving the learning experience
-	User manuals for trainees and trainers 
-	Train the Trainer
Validation Methodology developed for the implementation of Pilot Actions that are detailed in a Validation Report.
Procedure for the implementation of a Transnational Learning Activity, its deployment involving PDS and its Report
Dissemination Plan and Report, Project website and Facebook page together with 7 Multiplier Events complete the quality of the project
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-RS01-KA204-065418.title: Inclusive Digital Education Anti-discrimination AlternativeS
2020-1-RS01-KA204-065418.summary:
<< Background >>

The application for the IDEAS project addressed the needs of women, as well as other socially marginalized vulnerable groups - such as poor, Roma, migrant, non heterosexual, disabled - who are through multiple exclusionary processes denied access to adequate and equal educational opportunities. They are subject to systemic discriminatory practices and in dire need of empowering educational opportunities which would enable them to overcome overwhelming poverty and  allow for social inclusion.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives were to conceptualize a global response to the needs of the women from vulnerable groups, by constructing an educational program which will contribute to
strengthening them, be based on empowering them, and focus on allowing and expanding their full potential.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities of the project were building a dynamic, accessible educational program, the contents of which would clearly address the burning issues of vulnerable, socially marginalized groups (women's rights, sexual harassment, LGBTQ rights, position of Roma women, migrant women, etc.). This educational program transferred onto the podcast format would be free and easily accessible.

<< Results >>

IDEAS project produced - conceptualized, recorded and started broadcasting widely -  36 podcasts as a part of a coherent, dynamic, empowering educational program.

2020-1-SE01-KA204-077803.title: One Block for Educational Credentials
2020-1-SE01-KA204-077803.summary:
<< Background >>

The OBEC Project was developed to address a need that grows steadily as the world becomes increasingly transnational and as people move more and more across national borders: making educational credentials easily verifiable and facilitate recognition by different countries' authorities and employers. That is because “outdated credential systems limit our ability to create new pathways to education, in particular for those who lack access and need it most” (Joint Research Centre; Grech, A. and Camilleri, A. F., 2017), including exchange students, people with non-formal or informal learning backgrounds, and migrants. In fact, more than 40% of the employed highly educated third-country nationals work below their qualification levels in the EU (European Commission, n.d.), which also hinders their ability to fully utilize their skills and realize their economic potential to positively impact the EU economy and societies. In this context, OBEC was build to explore the potential opportunities the innovative Blockchain (BC) technology might offer to address this need by simplifying and facilitating the issuing and validation of learning credentials across European countries in a unified and enforceable manner.

<< Objectives >>

OBEC aimed at introducing the revolutionary possibilities that BC can bring about to inspire important changes within the educational field particularly by promoting the integration and prosperity of all through trusted, transparent, and easily shared and verified credentials in Europe, which could give Europe a global innovation edge in this arena. By developing an in-depth research of the status and knowledge gaps of BC in the education context, OBEC sought to positively impact social inclusion, gender equality, and employability in the EU, particularly benefiting the target groups as well as the involved European communities and economies. OBEC further sought to explore and apply an existing technology to the educational field in order to foster innovative tools for the creation, recognition, validation, and sharing of professional skills and academic qualifications across nations innovative digital tools to foster the notions of inclusivity and diversity. OBEC had the final purpose of contributing to the start of a process in the EU which can revolutionize the world through the creation of a barrier-free education system that can prosper through enriched diversity and increased transnational mobility.

<< Implementation >>

The OBEC project implemented the following activities:
- A research of knowledge gaps and the current state of economic and social integration of the target group and development of a report
- Development of a training curriculum and an associated experimental template for a badge system to utilize BC in EU systems of educational credentials. This was tested with a total of 180 participants.
- Composition of a set of case studies and videos, as well as of guidelines including good practices and mentor’s advice for practitioners
- Implementation of a total of 8 events which disseminated the OBEC project's results (2 in Sweden, 3 in Italy, 2 in Croatia, and 1 in Belgium), during which feedback was collected from participants
- Development of 4 newsletters, 4 press-releases, and 4 articles published on EPALE. Dissemination of results to 573873 people overall
- Explored and introduced certifications based on blockchain technology to educational institutions in Europe, showing the possibilities of moving towards a modern and unified system of learning credentials which can contribute to overall professional integration
- Inspired stakeholders to explore the potential of BC to prompt revolutionary outcomes in the educational field

<< Results >>

As a result, the OBEC consortium achieved the following:
- A comprehensive report which provides an overview of the current challenges, opportunities, and knowledge and perception gaps/issues for the adoption of a Blockchain-based certification system within the educational sector. This included: Interviews and online survey with 45 immigrants, 46 exchange students, 35 people with non-formal/informal learning backgrounds, 26 supporting institutions, 8 private companies, 9 educational institutions; Desk-research of the EU framework, Obstacles/possibilities, and 8 examples of standardized systems.
- The development of a total of 13 upskilling modules in different subjects which were tested in the partner countries with a total of 180 participants throughout 335h of training, having exceeded the target of 120h and 50 participants. The participants were certified through a platform based on Blockchain technology.
- This composition of a text report with 8 chapters and 11 recommendations; a set of 21 case studies that portray the use of Blockchain technology in the EU and internationally, 12 of which are within the educational sector; and 7 videos.
