2019-1-ES01-KA203-065861.title: PromotiNg thE neXus of migrants throUgh active citizenShip
2019-1-ES01-KA203-065861.summary:
<< Background >>

Education enables students to become critically aware and increases their understanding of the European identity. Students from minority backgrounds have a different understanding of what it takes to feel socially included, together with a weaker sense of European identity. Despite a lack of civic knowledge, they have confidence in their ability to engage in civic and citizenship issues. Recently, there has been a focus on the promotion of citizenship education. The NEXUS team believes that attention should be given to students to support their inclusion by enhancing their social and political responsibilities and rights. We believe that attention should be given to democracy as a process of deliberation and consensus-building, and to create a democratic society that values freedom of speech, equality, and making society more just and inclusive. Educational practices that relate to the components of democracy are scarce. It is therefore, necessary to change how civics is approached for students to ensure that members of disadvantaged groups enjoy equality of opportunity to engage in democratic action. As a result, the term “migrant students” was changed to “students with diverse backgrounds” to make the term itself more inclusive.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to empower students to defend their rights, uphold human values, contribute to their society and the global community, and as such, become more active European citizens. NEXUS has aimed at innovating the civic educational process to increase the participation of students in their communities. This aim focuses on the role that HEIs have in promoting the civic and social responsibility of students, with an emphasis on including students with diverse background (including migrants) in such initiatives. Another secondary objective has been to explore how meaningful civic learning is undertaken in online environments using technologies that are familiar and appealing to younger students. NEXUS based its approach to civic education on audiences that favour more personally expressive or self-actualizing politics, often in peer-to-peer networks. Increasingly, young people spend their time in online environments, many of which offer civic engagement opportunities that are more in tune with the appeal of social networking and participatory media creation among peers. NEXUS has aimed to bring together the students’ preference for online activity with the availability of networked citizenship tools.

<< Implementation >>

Firstly, an analysis was undertaken of student needs for the micro-learning units and the MOOC. A curriculum was then designed. This led to the development and piloting of the MOOC. It was then evaluated. A knowledge sharing platform of civics for educators was also designed and piloted. A public population was undertaken of the platform and an exchange of experiences using it was carried out. Secondly, an analysis was undertaken on this area. This gave rise to a classification of service-learning approaches to civics. An in-depth analysis was then undertaken of these in preparation of the best practices guide and policy document for higher education institutions. A final piloting was undertaken of this work with partner universities. Thirdly, a re-wiring of Civics to 4.0: connecting students to institutions in the digital age. This was carried out in three steps: an analysis gave rise to an online inventory of digital tools, a handbook was written on civic education for the digital age. Finally, a Learning, Teaching and Training Activity (LTT activity henceforth), in the form of a face-to-face training was undertaken on the new concept of civics as an illustrative process.

<< Results >>

There are four key results here. Firstly, a series of civic education micro-learning units were produced and fashioned into a MOOC on civic education (“Active citizenship and participation in the digital age”). Secondly, a knowledge-sharing platform (“NEXUS4Civics Community”) was built around open educational resources and practices for civic educators. It focussed on migration and cultural diversity, with guidelines for higher education institutions (HEIs) on student civic engagement. Thirdly, community engagement and service-learning guidelines were developed for HEIs. A policy document was also prepared, which focussed on the implementation of service learning as a pedagogical method for HEIs. The policy document was included as part of an UNESCO initiative. Fourthly, the notion of Civics was re-written to version 4.0. connecting students to institutions in the digital age by combining three elements: an inventory of digital tools for open democracy and digital citizenship education, a handbook for educators on civic education for a digital age, and LTT activity in civics as an illustrative process. Additional results have arisen from publication and dissemination activities and are presented in section 6.2.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

2019-1-FR01-KA203-062936.title: Geothermal Energy European Education Network
2019-1-FR01-KA203-062936.summary:
<< Background >>

The geothermal sector is growing and is on its way to become a pillar of the energetical transition. At present, no dedicated educational programme combining surface installations expertise, management, energy science, regulations and reservoir engineering exists in the field of geothermal engineering. Several stakeholders from the geothermal industry have noticed a lack of qualified engineers in this field which is operating at the frontier of science and engineering. All stakeholders strongly support the innovative Geo3EN initiative.

The Geothermal Energy European Education Network (Geo3En) was created by a highly complementary consortium formed by UniLaSalle (France), Technische Universitat Darmstadt (Germany), University of Zagreb (Croatia) and, originally, the Innovation Centre of Iceland (replaced after its dissolution by Reykjavik University, Iceland).

Geo3En started as an academic spin-off of the H2020 MEET research project on enhanced geothermal systems (https://bit.ly/3deUrNW).

The Geo3En consortium was mandated by 20 associated partners from geothermal energy industry and research in Europe to tackle the lack of qualified junior graduates mastering all elements of the geothermal energy value chain.

<< Objectives >>

Geo3En’s aimed to contribute in making Europe the leader in geothermal energy education and geothermal energy applications by harnessing the quality of existing programmes to create a multi-site European MSc of Excellence in Geothermal Engineering.

Geo3En also aimed to share knowledge and expertise of its consortium partners to provide their students with the required competencies and skill sets in line with the needs of industry and research organization. 

Its final objective was to design an international multi-site MSc of excellence in geothermal energy (taught in English) providing students with skills in geology, materials science, mechanical engineering, energy systems management, modelling, energy economics, but also project management, entrepreneurship and cross-cultural awareness, in order to successfully lead and design complex geothermal energy projects.

Strong links exist between the academic partners involved and industry. These connections permit students to grow their professional network which in turn greatly facilitates their employment perspective.

<< Implementation >>

To achieve its objectives, Geo3En organized 4 European consultations to co-design this 2-year MSc program with its associated partners and stakeholders from the European geothermal sector. This has ensured that the skills acquired during the MSc will be in line with the needs of the industry and research organizations.

The stakeholder consultations were prepared with the help of a competence matrix and quantitative and qualitative tools to ensure fruitful exchanges on the competencies to be integrated based on the mid-term strategies of the stakeholders for the next 10 years.

In addition to these consultations, the consortium members were able to test some of the courses and pedagogical tools developed through IO6, 7 and 8 by organising 8 training activities (4 online and 4 in the field). Geo3En activities and results were also disseminated within their own professional networks and a Geo3En website was created (https://geo3en.eu/).

Finally, in August 2022, the consortium submitted an extended paper on Geo3En results and activities to be presented at the 44th New Zealand (NZ) Geothermal Workshop to be held from 23 to 25/11/2022 in Auckland, NZ.

<< Results >>

The project produced in nine deliverables. With its first work package (WP1), the consortium developed Geo3En’s MSc Curriculum whose results are: the creation of the MSc competence matrix (IO1), its course catalogue (IO3) and Geo3EN Intensive Study Programmes (ISP) Organisations report (IO2). 

Geo3En Stakeholder consultations (WP2) led to the production of Geo3En’s MSc Competencies report based on the competence requirements questionnaire and related stakeholder feedbacks (IO4).

Following the design of the Geo3En curriculum, joint course material and innovative pedagogical tools (WP3) were developed to ensure a smooth transition of the student through the designed curriculum. It led to the production of a report on Site visits and Learning by doing (IO6), a baseline course in geothermal engineering (IO7) and a course module in Entrepreneurship (IO8). 

These tools were partially tested through four onsite training and four online training: the ISP. The test and evaluation of Geo3En’s MSc curriculum (WP4) led to the writing of two reports: the report on innovative pedagogical tool or method (IO9) and the ISP evaluation report (IO10).

2019-1-FR01-KA203-063010.title: Becoming A Digital Global Engineer
2019-1-FR01-KA203-063010.summary:
<< Background >>

The BADGE project takes place in a context of increasing globalisation and teachers of languages and intercultural communication in engineering schools need to prepare their students for global competence, as defined by the OECD (http://www.oecd.org/pisa/pisa-2018-globalcompetence.htm). This project is motivated by a survey carried out by the BADGE partners. It showed that engineers often need foreign languages to speak on the phone or understand information in meetings, to write occasional letters and to read short documents. The analysis of the survey showed that language and communication courses need to incorporate more language for specific purposes (LSP) skills and that engineers often communicate without being aware of intercultural contexts. LC teachers need to integrate these tools into their language courses to familiarise students with them. The survey also showed that only 10% of modern language teachers in engineering schools have a specific engineering qualification, while 79% have no knowledge or experience of the engineering world.

<< Objectives >>

The BADGE partners have developed materials for LSP (language for specific purposes) and intercultural communication competence for use by the modern language teaching community in engineering schools, as they often do not have the competence or time to develop specific resources for engineering students themselves. We have created a multilingual Open Educational Resources (OER) platform containing learning materials and course content, developed jointly by BADGE members, engineering students, professors and industry partners, allowing language teachers to choose course content or learning units that can be adapted to local/national needs, be integrated into existing courses and even lead to new curricula. The platform can be found here: https://www.thebadgeproject.eu/.
Our aim is to train engineers with global digital skills for sustainable internationalisation through improved pedagogical practices.

<< Implementation >>

In our project we developed resources for language teachers in engineering schools. Most of the resources have been tested by the partners who developed them and by other partners in the BADGE project. In OI7, for example, the resources have been jointly tested by more than 200 students.
Each learning unit is published on the OER platform, which is our website: https://www.thebadgeproject.eu/. When students complete one of these courses, implemented by a teacher, they get a digital badge. When they have collected 5 badges, students will get a certificate attesting to their acquired competence. This certificate attests to a wider range of skills than a language certificate alone. The content of the certificate will be indicated in the Europass Diploma Supplement, if the institution implements it.  The impact of innovative teaching material on the development of students' competences will be studied quantitatively and qualitatively, at least in the partner universities, to ensure that the objective of training engineering students to become global digital engineers is achieved.

<< Results >>

As many partners (13) were involved in the project, we divided the work into 8 working groups. Each group, with two or more partners, developed resources in different areas, but all related to LSP for engineering students and intercultural training. Students and industrial partners were always involved in the design of the material. In Intellectual Output 8, comprehensive Moodle courses for EMI (English Medium of Instruction), have been designed to help teachers and staff communicate with international students in engineering schools and teach in English.
The 8 different Intellectual Outputs are:

01 Communication course for future engineers
02 Sustainable writing skills
03 Electronic communication skills
04 Global competence and entrepreneurship
05 Voice of Architecture
06 Soft skills for engineering students
07 Global competence through IT and serious games
08 EMI (English-Medium-Instruction) for teachers and staff
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2019-1-HR01-KA203-060804.title: Teaching mathematics in STEM context for STEM students
2019-1-HR01-KA203-060804.summary:
<< Background >>

This project is addressed to enhance STEM students knowledge and skills in mathematics within the STEM context. Using active and collaborative learning and ICT methodology for learning will lead to enlarge students skills to solve practical problems. Students will be an active part of the educational process using this new methodology. Students gained knowledge and skills in maths can be applied for success in today’s world, such as critical thinking, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration.

<< Objectives >>

A project of this kind is an excellent opportunity for making arguments between minds, criticizing different opinions on some topic, all of it with one goal: achieving excellent skills of maths of students to be used in everyday life.

<< Implementation >>

We had 5 intellectual outputs of the project:
1. Development of the mathSTEM teaching methodology and development of a Guidelines for the mathSTEM methodology.
2. Open Online lessons on mathSTEM methodology
3. Developing e-platform for mathSTEM method
4. Designing a Summer Course
5. Development of training courses for mathSTEM method
We had 2 multiplier events in 1 in our country and 1 in Macedonia in order to get excellent promotion on the achievements of the project; 1 short-term joint staff training events in Croatia and 1 intensive programme for higher education learners in Ohrid, Macedonia and 4 transnational project meetings (2 in our country, 1 in Turkey and 1 online).

<< Results >>

Except for the main results of the project that are already mentioned as intellectual outputs, other results are:
• Students to gain a positive attitude towards mathematics. The motivation for learning mathematics is expected to be increased, and this will gain better achievements of the students not only in mathematics but also in other STEM areas.
• University teachers to gain better competence. They will look at the teaching process from the point of view of the students and have a better understanding of it. This is the way they are going to upgrade their teaching skills.
• All of the participants have gain better linguistic and communication skills.
• Through the work on this project, meeting different people and collaborate with them, they will appreciate the differences and become more open and tolerant of the changes that have to occur in the process of education.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2019-1-HR01-KA203-060959.title: Innovative Solutions based on Emerging Technologies for Improving Social Inclusion of People with Disabilities
2019-1-HR01-KA203-060959.summary:
<< Background >>

The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that more than one billion people are in need of assistive tools. Such tools are becoming increasingly digitized through the use of Information Technology (IT). However, only a small percentage have access to needed technology which has a negative impact not only on their lives but also on their caretakers/families and society as a whole. Because they are perceived as different, they also frequently encounter stigmatization, discrimination, and inequalities, largely by people who are not properly educated on social inclusion. Therefore, without innovative IT solutions based on emerging technologies, people with disabilities (PWDs) are isolated. The INNOSID project builds upon ten years long activities of the “ICT-AAC Competence Network” and broadens its activities geographically (through internationalization) and technologically (through focusing on emerging technologies such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR) and 3D-printing). ICT-AAC's main vision is enhancing
social inclusion of PWDs by designing and developing free IT solutions aimed at enabling communication, supporting education, and raising public awareness about the needs and abilities of people with disabilities.

<< Objectives >>

The INNOSID project was implemented by a consortium consisting of 6 higher education institutions (HEI) and 1 non-governmental organization (NGO) from the domain of people with disabilities, from 5 EU countries (Croatia, Spain, France, Portugal, and Hungary). The project goal was to improve the social inclusion of PWDs by creating innovative IT solutions based on emerging technologies. To reach the project goal, the following three equally important objectives were successfully reached: (i) developing multilingual support for existing IT tools for improving social inclusion of people with disabilities; (ii) designing new innovative IT tools based on emerging technologies for improving social inclusion of people with disabilities; and (iii) improving the higher education system through tackling skill gaps – raising awareness, developing open educational resources and providing training to students and lecturers in the area of innovative IT solutions based on emerging technologies. The target groups are people with disabilities; students from participating HEIs; lecturers (researchers) from participating HEIs; high school students; and IT companies.

<< Implementation >>

The meet the objectives, the project implemented the following activities. The project implemented 8 intellectual output activities aimed at producing materials for improving the social inclusion of people with disabilities. Next, 8 transnational project meetings were successfully organized and used for coordination, management, partner collaboration, and brainstorming, 4 of which were held virtually. To ensure the effective dissemination of project results, 4 multiplier events in Debrecen (Hungary), Valencia (Spain), Zagreb (Croatia), and Santarem (Portugal) were organized for more than 500 participants. This was accompanied by extensive web and social media activities geared toward the dissemination of project results to the target groups. Last, 4 learning/training/teaching (LTT) activities were organized for more than 100 participants (i.e., 63 students and 44 lecturers). The LTT activities were realized as two blended mobility programs with virtual and physical parts. The first blended mobility had a workshop in Dubrovnik during which the students prepared visual prototypes of innovative IT solutions, whereas the second mobility had a hackathon in Valencia during which the students prepared the functional prototypes.

<< Results >>

The results from intellectual outputs can be summarized as follows. First, a study on emerging technologies for improving the social inclusion of people with disabilities was prepared. Second, multilingual support was developed for 5 ICT-AAC applications, namely ICT-AAC Sprays, ICT-AAC What time is it, ICT-AAC Learning colors, ICT-AAC Mathematical carousel, and ICT-AAC Mathematics (support for Croatian, English, Spanish, Hungarian, French, and Portuguese, including multilingual user guides). Third, the Learn To Cook application, including the user guide, was developed as a publicly-available IT tool based on augmented reality for improving the social inclusion of people with disabilities. Fourth, a total of 15 emerging technology studies were prepared. Fifth, 27 slide decks achieved through 2 activities were published as OERs. Sixth, 4 requirements IT tool requirements specifications were achieved. Finally, the Gibalica application, including the user guide, was developed as a publicly-available IT tool based on computer vision for improving the social inclusion of people with disabilities.

The project received the award by AMPEU for the most inclusive project for Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps for the period 2017-2020.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2019-1-HR01-KA203-060969.title: City Monitoring and Integrated Design for Decarbonisation
2019-1-HR01-KA203-060969.summary:
<< Background >>

The CITY MINDED project was developed by the recognition of the capital importance of urban sustainability in contemporary Europe. Nowadays, around 70% of Europeans live in cities and this number will rise. On the other hand, cities generate about 70% of global greenhouse gas emissions. This concentration of population, infrastructure and human activities makes cities particularly vulnerable to the negative impacts of climate change. For these reasons, urban areas are currently the most important test-bed for energy transition and decarbonisation models. However, decarbonisation touches upon a wide variety of topics, ranging from energy to sustainable mobility, urban design, awareness raising, and urban waste management. This calls for a systemic interdisciplinary approach, which, at the time the project was drafted, was not widespread in ordinary academic teaching practices, but was nonetheless deemed necessary by partner organizations to form more employable professional profiles, able to coordinate different disciplinary domains, sources of information, stakeholders and competences.

<< Objectives >>

The overall project objective was to develop and test an innovative, creative, European-scaled learning environment called ‘City decarbonisation itinerant workshops’, where students, specialists and stakeholders can come together to address common onsite challenges and define collaborative urban decarbonisation scenarios through a ‘learning-by-doing’ method. The project-specific objectives were: to bring together and reinforce the linkages among higher education, academic knowledge,
institutions’ experience, and communities’ needs and expectations and to transfer knowledge about the complex issue of city decarbonisation and how to deal with it, by
consolidating and testing innovative training strategies based on an integrated approach and by cocreating knowledge on technologies, legal issues, financial management, social engagement, and monitoring tools in the field of urban sustainability, thus enhancing the students’ capacities to operate in a real-world setting.

<< Implementation >>

The project's main activities included:
- Creation of a team of experts in the fields of urban decarbonisation, sustainable energy and urban design from partner Universities, which have guided the project workshops and the process for the development of decarbonisation scenarios in target areas,
- Definition of a common methodology to guide project implementation,
- Realization of an open web-based platform (IO2) where the developed educational resources have been collected, organized and freely accessed by students and professors for further exploitation,
- Organization of 3 online workshops, touching different target cities (Seville, Siena, Rome), each one involving students from the hosting partner university, together with local stakeholders in the drafting decarbonisation scenarios for target areas,
- Organization of a hybrid 2-week Intensive Course in Malta, where students from partner Universities and teachers/trainers per partner organization have put into practice the final methodology and drafted a sustainable development agenda for a Maltese target area,
- Organization of a Final International Conference in Croatia where all partners presented the project results and proposed guidelines for their transferability.

<< Results >>

The project activities led to the achievement of the following results:
- Development of projects Methodology and guidelines (IO1) aiming to address the implementation of the city decarbonisation itinerant workshops, which are based on the combination of different skills and designed as an innovative teaching and learning experience.
- Realization of an open web-based platform (IO2) where the developed modular online course on urban decarbonisation (IO4) and the educational materials produced during the project are freely accessible to students and professors for further exploitation,
- Collection of decarbonisation scenarios (IO3) developed during four workshops and structured as a repository of data and solutions. The output includes the Carbon footprints produced during the workshops, as well as the analyses and studies of real urban contexts and environmental sustainability conducted in each target area.
- Final Conference Proceedings (IO5) which include abstracts of speeches from the final conference, representing the specific topics focusing on the decarbonisation of urban areas,
- Monographic issue of journal NU3 – le Note di U3 entitled ‘Teaching Decarbonisation. Methodologies and experiences from CITY MINDED’.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2019-1-HR01-KA203-060982.title: Integrated Methodologies to Historical Landscapes Recording: Participatory Approaches
2019-1-HR01-KA203-060982.summary:
<< Background >>

The reason our consortium applied for this project was initial mutual interest in historic landscape research. Many members of our team have, as many others before us, noted some recurring problems in the discipline of landscape studies. Most notable is the lack of coherent and multidisciplinary approach in research on historic landscapes. This is, naturally, a problem that is too wide and too complex to be solved in a uniform way; however, we have decided to contribute to it by tackling a smaller, but nonetheless important, segment in historical landscape studies – teaching on them in a systematic and critical manner. 
Our aim was to create a curriculum for a Master Study that takes into account all of the hidden and not so hidden complexities behind historic/cultural landscape studies – methodological and theoretical basis and approaches from different disciplines, but most importantly the practical applications and the place of landscape studies in competitive job market. Landscapes being one of the most endangered and underappreciated forms of cultural heritage, under constant threat of homogenization and abandonment of rural areas are exactly the reasons why the integrated management model has to be created and implemented.

<< Objectives >>

With implementation of this project we gathered the knowledge and the know-hows of contemporary experts that deal with various segments of landscape studies that have offered their expertise, especially in didactic and methodological aspects. As we have noted during the creation of the Master Study curriculum (our Intellectual Output) we strived to create an inclusive study model that will be applicable in various European (and global) scientific facilities, universities (and other relevant institutions) in order to raise awareness of landscapes and their preservation.
Finally, we wanted to give the possibility of studying a topic that is not taught at university level, as to give at least the initial push for better understanding the constantly disappearing heritage, and initiate its systematic preservation.

<< Implementation >>

The practical part of the work on Intellectual Output was centered around four Intensive Programs (Learning, Teaching and Training Activities) aimed at testing various aspects of methodological and didactic framework behind the curriculum itself. The Intensive Programs – workshops, have included university students on all levels (undergraduate, graduate, doctoral) and of different disciplines (art history, archaeology, history, sociology, anthropology, ethnology and related disciplines.). Furthermore, dissemination activities – conferences and meetings with stakeholders and members of local communities in which we did the practical side of the curriculum work were also an important segment of getting feedback on our main project objective.
In total, four workshops (LTTA) and two dissemination events (Multiplier Events) were the basis for development of the definitive version of our Intellectual Output.

<< Results >>

The most important result is the Intellectual Output of this project – we have created a Master Study curriculum “LANDSCAPE CULTURAL HERITAGE MANAGER”. 
The other results were made clear during our four workshops (LTTA) and two dissemination events (Multiplier Events): the first gave us feedback to improve the final output, the second helped us understand what are the needs of the policy makers, local communities and stakeholders in general. This was important to improve the modes in which we communicate results, concepts and ideas behind the project.
Moreover, throughout the duration of this project, the COVID-19 pandemic provided us with the opportunity to apply and gain a new Erasmus KA02 project (Learning how to Teach, Teaching how to Learn. Facing Challenges of Global Change in Higher Education Using Digital Tools for Reflective, Critical and Inclusive Learning on European Historical Landscapes (EDiToR), that is centered around creation of an online learning platform on historical landscapes as well as training the teachers in new online tools that is relying heavily on the framework created by the HILAR project team and on HILAR’s didactic content.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2019-1-HR01-KA203-060984.title: Applied Data Science Educational Ecosystem
2019-1-HR01-KA203-060984.summary:
<< Background >>

In 2016, 16 million people in Europe worked in data-related jobs and the overall value of the EU data economy reached almost 300 billion EUR – with respective increase expected in both categories according to “high grow” scenario. Therefore, the socio-economic aspect of data and data related industries proved to be crucial for the further development of the EU and its competitiveness capacities in the global economy. 

However, in 2016, a significant gap between total demand and supply of data workers was noticed, with a forecast to face a data skills gap corresponding to 769.000 unfilled positions by 2020. In order to mitigate potential unbalances on the labor market and to support adequate changes in educational approach, we identified the need for reskilling work force developing digital skills in the field of data science.

In order to contribute to this change, we applied for this project to design ready-to-use materials, modules and strategies for HEIs which are often lagging behind in their role of developing and offering educational programmes and materials, providing students with skills which market demands. Especially, we identified that this need is very evident in non-technical sectors where domain-specific data skills are in high demand, but HEIs’ offer in relevant educational programmes and trainings is in many cases inadequate. Finally, ADSEE project was designed in order to deliver useful educational and training modules in data science, especially addressing non-technical HEIs and students.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the ADSEE project was to deliver useful educational and training programme in data science through development of educational modules, adaption of contents and methods according to envisaged needs of the target groups, creation of interactive didactic tools and production of guidelines and recommendations on innovative education approaches in data science. 

By implementing the project, we wanted to create innovative educational modules, specially paying our attention to prepare them in a way to be useful for learning about data-science in non-technical universities. The aim of this approach was to empower non-technical students and experts to apply data science approach and methods in non-technical business, particularly when it comes to data-driven decision making – necessary in many fields. Furthermore, our aim was to implement newly developed materials and modules into the project partners’ learning environments and therefore engage non-technical students with data science in order for them to acquire set of skills important for applying data science in their field of expertise, but also to popularize data science among students. Additionally, our aim was to show lecturers that ADSEE modules can be useful for implementing new teaching strategies and empower them to introduce data science into their teaching. Finally, through gathering important insights and evaluating project activities throughout the whole project lifetime, partners were trying to gather important information for creating guidelines with recommendations for future implementation of activities similar to ones implemented during project. This is how we strived to ensure sustainability, and future and international applicability of successful strategies designed during the project.

<< Implementation >>

As a first project activity, a comprehensive research was conducted. The research set the ground for further project activities – designing and setting up an interactive online repository for hosting learning materials.
Furthermore, partners created four educational modules together with all teaching and learning materials and data repository. Modules are aimed for using in teaching, showing the possibilities of applying data science in different industries and occupations with interdisciplinary examples – retail and marketing, culture and tourism, privacy and job market signaling. Afterwards, partners organized and implemented pilot process in their institutions in order to test newly developed educational modules with students and lecturers, gather important insights and evaluate the modules as well as to popularize data science. Evaluation of the pilot process led to the final activity – designing transferable guidelines for improvements in usage of data science methodologies in education. Partners’ and target group’s insights were gathered and together with important lessons-learned, guidelines were created with a set of recommendations - a model for HEIs, which will help them in adopting efficient and innovative approaches when it comes to teaching about data science.

When it comes to dissemination activities, official project website was established at the beginning of the project – www.adsee.eu. Algebra as project coordinator published results and news on the official project website, as well as on social media account. Project partners shared articles and posts on their accounts in order regularly update public about project and facilitate contact among interested parties. Evidences of project results and dissemination actions were uploaded to Dissemination platform. 

Kick-off meeting was held live in December 2019 in Zagreb (Algebra). From this point on, partners’ meetings were shifted to online environment because of constant Covid-19 restrictions. Nevertheless, Algebra coordinated management activities, organized partners’ meetings regularly. During the project lifetime, after face-to-face kick off meeting in Zagreb, partners met 9 times in the online environment. Meetings were organized in line with the project timeline, having in mind all activities that should been performed, so that meetings were held in order to establish workplan, discuss partners’ progress, brainstorm, deliberate about ideas and tracking project management activities. This is how partnership maintained good and efficient communication which ensured smooth project implementation. Additionally, two dissemination events were held in 2022 (on Algebra University College and Faculty of Information Studies) during which project results were presented to the business and academic community.

<< Results >>

To set the trajectory for implementing project outputs, in the beginning of the project, partners conducted a research which culminated with a comprehensive report. We examined the current academic supply of the study programmes related to data science accessible at HEIs and other education providers in partner countries and, on the other hand, the current market needs in terms of competences and experience required for data scientists and other occupations using data science approach. Research conclusions served partners in the process of deciding about establishment of repository and creating learning modules. 

So, in the next project output, partners were creating an interactive online repository. The repository was first designed and then established as a fully functioning interactive online repository. Partners established it in a way to represent a part of a personalized training mechanism as well as to host the learning materials.

Further results of intellectual outputs are four educational modules showing the possibilities of applying data science in different fields. Partners created these innovative educational modules with lot of interdisciplinary examples. Creation process encompassed designing teaching and learning materials as well as data repository. This way, finalized modules are ready to use and can be used as an improvement of current learning modules, as core part of new learning modules or for the self-study.

Next output was dedicated to the pilot process which was conducted in project partners’ institutions with their lecturers and more that 200 students. Pilot process was thoroughly evaluated before its start, during its implementation and after it finished. This way, partners ensured that evaluation tools and process provide partnership with lecturers’ and students’ opinion on educational modules, implementing data science into their field of expertise as well as about the whole pilot process. The pilot resulted with final evaluation of the pilot efficiency and success-rate of the produced educational modules.
As a culmination of the project, transferable guidelines on data science in different professional environments, with special emphasis on the non-technical ones, were created. In order to create comprehensive guidelines, all previously finalized results of the project were thoroughly examined and the most important lessons-learned were set up in a form of transferable recommendations. Moreover, guidelines actually represent a model for HEIs, which will help them in adopting efficient and innovative approaches when it comes to teaching about data science methods and approach. Partners shaped the guidelines in a way to respond to two necessities: how to efficiently train individuals in data science and how to respond to current challenges and trends represented by data science in business environments. In addition to the guidelines prepared in English, partners prepared guidelines translations to Dutch, German, Slovenian and Croatian.

2019-1-HR01-KA203-060992.title: Inspiring digital entrepreneurship
2019-1-HR01-KA203-060992.summary:
Digital transformation is revolutionising the way Europeans live, study and work. Yet, not all Europeans are ready to fully participate in – ad contribute to – the digital society and economy. According to the European Commission, only 57% of Europeans have the digital skills needed for the digital world we live in. One in six Europeans aged 16-74 has no digital skills at all and one in four only has a low level of digital skills. Furthermore, while 90% of jobs require basic digital competences, 35% of the labour force lacks them. Moreover, 38% of EU companies report that the lack of digital skills negatively affects their performance and competitiveness.

Croatia lags behind: according to the EU Commission “EU Index of Digital Entrepreneurship Systems” Croatia ranks 23 out of the 28 Member States, with particularly low rating in human capital and attitude towards digital entrepreneurship.

To tackle this challenge, the EU launched the “Digital Skills & Jobs Coalition” with the ambition of empowering Europeans to acquire the digital skills they need to thrive in society, remain productive and employable. The Coalition main target is to train 1 million young people for digital jobs through short-term training programmes.

In this context IDEA (Inspiring Digital Entrepreneurship and Awareness in HE) project aims at fulfilling the gaps highlighted in the specific Higher Education priorities - HE: Tackling skills gaps and mismatches of the Erasmus Plus Programme, page 107 by combining training and tools targeted to 2 different set of skills equally needed to boost effectiveness of HE curricula and magnify HE students’ chances of success: Digital Skills and Entrepreneurial skills.  

Through its activities and outputs, IDEA proposes an innovative approach of one important factor influencing entrepreneurial success: the use of digital skills applied to entrepreneurship. One of the first crucial trait of highly successful entrepreneurs is the ability to keep up with the latest trends (social, technological, economical). ”Digital Transformation of European Industry and Enterprises” report shows that the transformative power of digital is enormous and unexploited.  Europe could create up to 1.5 million new jobs in the Internet economy.

The project will be implemented by 9 partners from Croatia, Poland, Belgium, Romania, Italy, Spain, Slovakia from different backgrounds (business/ICT field, HE Institutions and social partners/NGO) over a period of 24 months.

IDEA has the objective of mapping and stock taking of Digital Entrepreneurship dynamics in the countries involved, by identifying common trends, issues, best practices and tools. 
IDEA will boost both digital skills and entrepreneurship by developing and testing a set of innovative materials and resources, which allow HEIs equipping at least 200 HE students of the participating organizations with two crucial entrepreneurial success skills: digital skills applied to entrepreneurship skills by the end of the project. IDEA will also deploy project results throughout Europe via its OER platform destined to become a knowledge hub and an open education focal point.
IDEA will rise awareness among HE Institutions and education authorities concerning the potential of digital skills and entrepreneurship skills and their role as business success factors.
IDEA main aim is to improve professional success chances of HE students with different backgrounds by developing not only their entrepreneurship skills (or knowledge), but also their digital skills.  

Target groups: HE students and recent graduates, HE teachers, trainers/mentors HE schools/institutions, social partners, companies, SMEs.

In order to reach the project’s aim, development of 4 innovative and transferrable intellectual outputs is foreseen: 
O1: IDEA Open Education Resources OER Platform available in 7 languages
IO2: IDEA mapping and stock taking of Digital Entrepreneurship dynamics in the countries involved, identification of common trends, issues, best practices and tools;
IO3: IDEA E-learning training material for Students on Digital Entrepreneurship Training for Entrepreneurial Success;
IO4: Test and validation with 200 students, mainstream and uptake with consequent development of Digital Entrepreneurship Manual and Guidelines for HEIs.
Measures for open access and sustainability are planned, to ensure the usability of the project beyond project’s lifetime. 

The project management and methodology will be tailor-made, involving development of personalized project management, quality assurance and dissemination plans, monitoring/evaluation tools. Thanks to the presence of partners with a high level of experience and multiplication potential, the project will benefit from increased visibility and impact at national and European level. To widen the impact and visibility of the project, a number of 7 multiplier events, totalizing a number of 150 national and international participants is foreseen.

2019-1-HR01-KA203-061000.title: Innovative Approach in Mathematical Education for Maritime Students
2019-1-HR01-KA203-061000.summary:
<< Background >>

Having previous contacts, academic institutions involved in this project have always expressed their dissatisfaction with the ability of students to apply mathematics in maritime subjects. It was due to their poor knowledge they carried from high school, or poor results in mathematics subjects at their higher education institution (HEI). Moreover, all partners knew that the results students achieve at the exams from mathematics were not satisfactory, and even the drop out rates were related to this ''problematic'' subject. On the other hand many maritime subjects, like navigation, ship construction, thermodynamics, etc. needed mathematics knowledge in order to teach students necessary topics from these fields. All HEIs had previous attempts in their efforts to solve this problem, but without considerable success.
The leading institution - Faculty of Maritime Studies of the UNIST suggested the idea to use innovative and effective methods of online learning, already proven to bring results, and that is prof Toni Milun's methodology that he had been applying for years. Therefore, all partners agreed that the need to solve this problem would be effectively addressed by applying this innovative method through common Erasmus project.

<< Objectives >>

The consortium wanted to produce innovative tools and methodology and introduce it into teaching mathematics at maritime institutions. 
Besides this, there are the second level achievements from the project like: widening and strengthening international cooperation, exposing to international peer reviewing, advancements in technological aspects, meeting personal self-affirmation challenges of project team members, internationalization for the institution, team members and students, acquiring external funding for the needs of development, etc.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities implemented in the project were the creation and production of intellectual outputs through the cooperation among institutions; creating lessons; acquiring digital skills for teachers; learning about media and film production; filming lessons and examples; learning process of both teachers and students; cooperation between teachers and students in creating materials; live and virtual meetings; mobility of staff and students; events with the aim of teaching, training and learning for both students and teachers; communication to the public, target groups and wider interested stakeholders; numerous dissemination activities, meetings and events; monitoring and evaluation of the work done with improvements and corrections; publishing results within the HE community and further; managing and administration of the project; solving financial challenges and practical issues especially related to Covid-19 pandemic, etc.

<< Results >>

In general, MareMathics project produced lessons in digital forms, videos and plenty of examples and applications in maritime subjects, all available at:
https://maremathics.pfst.hr/
and specifically:

Intellectual Output 1 at https://maremathics.pfst.hr/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/IO1-Report-All-Partners.pdf

Intellectual Output 3:
videos at https://maremathics.pfst.hr/?cat=14 
worksheets at https://maremathics.pfst.hr/?p=4022
Quizzes at https://maremathics.pfst.hr/?p=4024
GeoGebra tools at https://www.geogebra.org/u/maremathics

2019-1-HR01-KA203-061010.title: Personalized Medicine Inquiry-Based Education
2019-1-HR01-KA203-061010.summary:
<< Background >>

Healthcare in Europe is undergoing fundamental shift towards integration of personalized, participatory, preventive and predictive methods and approaches towards better treatment outcomes and sustainable wellbeing. This, however has not been adequately reflected in the European study programs for future medical and biomedical professionals. In the survey coordinated by European Alliance for Personalized Medicine, it was shown that one of the biggest barriers for the full integration of personalized medicine in Europe is the lack of training and knowledge. This motivated us to create interdisciplinary partnership which could develop much needed training for future professionals in disciplines that are essential to the successful development of P4 medicine.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the PROMISE project is the design of new inquiry-based online teaching modules to familiarize students with P4 Medicine and its principles in order to transform and improve the existing teaching tools and practices in higher education. This educational intervention improved the existing teaching tools and practices in partner institutions. PROMISE teaching modules were designed to give a jump start to students who wish to enter the field of research and train them in the future of practicing research and medicine. Our design allowed rapid translation of cutting –edge science into excellence in higher education training in a format which could be easily transferred to a number of Universities in Europe and beyond.

<< Implementation >>

We had 5 transnational project meetings: Kick-off meeting and four more after that. We were supposed to have another meeting, but we did not hold it because it was during the pandemic.
3 training activities were held for participating staff in the project which is a capacity building for the partners: Intensive training programme in curriculum design, Intensive training programme for the creation of e-learning modules and inquiry-based learning and Media Training. We also had two Blended mobility activities: Learning expedition in Paris and PROMISE summer school in Split. Additionally, a Learning expedition in Zagreb was organized at the end of the project. Considering the pandemic year, we later had two additional activities: PROMISE Summer workshop for students-assistants in Split  and Seminar on P4 medicine in Zagreb.
The project includes 4 intellectual outputs: 1. P4 Medicine curriculum design and P4 certification definition), 2.Four P4 Medicine and Responsible Research and Innovation Modules, 3. Mapping and Analysis of EU P4 Ecosystem and 4. PROMISE Final report and P4 medicine teaching recommendations.  
Two Multiplier Events were also organized: 1st International PROMISE Conference and 2nd Annual PROMISE Conference.

<< Results >>

Our project produced: 1. PROMISE curriculum covering 4 dimensions of learning outcomes for interdisciplinary biomedical students, 2. extensive educational video material consisting of 49 videos, 3. extensive written material, including lessons, quizzes, assignments, scientific articles, etc. (available on the Moodle e-learning platform), 4. PROMISE P4 medicine stakeholders database with different stakeholders, , public and private organizations, and professional bodies in the EU which can influence, impact, or be affected by the areas of development and implementation of P4 approach, 4. two scientific publications: “Tackling Mantle Cell Lymphoma in Europe”, “Accelerating the Development and Validation of Liquid Biopsy for Early Cancer Screening and Treatment Tailoring” and one that is awaiting publication, and is related to impact assessment, 5. video material recorded by PROMISE students (Two videos of impressions of the first generation of our PROMISE students and three of the second), 6. Youth association PROMISE, 7. P4 medicine survey to assess knowledge and gather opinions about P4 medicine current healthcare system among different stakeholder groups which is translated to 5 languages.

2019-1-NL01-KA203-060492.title: European Prescribing License: Preparing future medical doctors in the European Union for safe prescribing
2019-1-NL01-KA203-060492.summary:
<< Background >>

In many European countries, recently graduated doctors write a large proportion of drug prescriptions in hospitals, often with minimal supervision from senior clinicians. In order to prescribe safely and effectively at the start of their professional careers, medical graduates should have acquired appropriate prescribing knowledge and skills. Unfortunately, several studies throughout Europe suggest that medical students have not acquired these necessary competencies by the time they graduate. This is even more worrying since the demands on new prescribers are increasing progressively because of several trends, including a growing number of medicines, increasingly vulnerable patients, and more complicated medication regimens.

Poor education in clinical pharmacology and therapeutics (CPT) during the undergraduate medical curriculum may underlie the lack of prescribing competencies among recent graduates. In most European schools, teaching is currently mainly based on passive learning methods such as listening to lectures and reading study books with little practical training. Modernizing and harmonizing CPT education at a European level might prevent and reduce prescribing errors in the future, thereby improving patient safety.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of this project was to develop, test and implement a standardised assessment on safe prescribing during the undergraduate medical curriculum in Europe. Our ultimate goal is to improve prescribing competence of future European medical doctors, thereby reducing prescribing errors and improving patient safety.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented the following activities:

- Developing a European Prescribing Exam (EuroPE+) including an assessment blueprint and learning outcomes.
- Delivering the EuroPE+ to a total of 2.180 medical students from 9 participating universities. 
- Developing and validating 200 items for the question bank.
- Developing a European essential drug list. 
- Developing an instruction book about the online assessment platform for teachers and medical students. 
- Organizing an online workshop about EuroPE+ for teachers of 9 participating universities about how to use the online assessment tool.
- Organizing an online workshop about EuroPE+ for European clinical pharmacologists during the EACPT Virtual Meeting in 2021. 
- Organizing an online workshop about EuroPE+ for young clinical pharmacologists during the pre-meeting of the EACPT congress in 2022. 
- Organizing a Multiplier Event about EuroPE+ for clinical pharmacologists across Europe.
- Organizing three case-based group discussions with medical students from four European universities. 
- Organizing online lectures about EuroPE+ to medical students of four European universities. 
- Writing seven articles about EuroPE+ and publishing four articles in medical journals.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs of this project are:

- A European Prescribing Exam (EuroPE+) including a definitive assessment blueprint and learning outcomes.
- A European list of 98 essential drugs that form the basis for the question items used in EuroPE+. 
- A question bank including 200 validated items.
- An online assessment platform for medical students and teachers of the participating universities (http://www.prescribingeducation.eu/).
- An instruction book about the online assessment platform for teachers and medical students of participating universities. 
- A student syllabus containing factual knowledge that should be known by medical students in order to meet the predefined outcomes. This syllabus was initially developed for the Dutch National Pharmacotherapy Assessment in collaboration with all medical schools in the Netherlands and has been adapted specifically for this project.
- Four published manuscripts about EuroPE+ in different national and international medical journals and another three manuscripts that will be submitted the beginning of 2023.
- Case-based group discussions that are used to teach medication review skills to medical students.

2019-1-PL01-KA203-065050.title: Economics of Sustainability
2019-1-PL01-KA203-065050.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was meant to address core sustainability issues because of the essential part they play in today’s world. An active approach to solving sustainability problems can have immense potential in contributing to the future existence and development of the world. It is vital to educate young generations, attract their attention to existing problems and create favourable environment and teach how to generate solutions. Such empowerment can stimulate creativity.
The needs addressed were: increased awareness of sustainability issues by introducing the subject into tertiary education curricula, improving creativity and drive to participate in solving common local and global problems.
The plethora of issues, including cultural and social sustainability, sustainability of businesses, environmental and employment relations, marketing, sustainable production and consumption, psychology and communication, sustainable tourism, and hospitality industry, sustainable finance and management, energy use, education, etc. need to be addressed with different intensity in specific regions. However, in the global village era, efforts should be made to draw attention to country/region specific, local issues as well as globally important problems.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective to achieve was to stimulate students' and participating secondary school pupils' awareness of sustainability issues and openness to different cultures, tolerance and responsiveness to different needs, thus strengthening social potential. The project was also aimed at focusing on beneficial actions and support of positive behavioural trends that can contribute to sustainable consumption. Another important objective was to clarify and prove how fun and enjoyment can be combined with socially and environmentally desirable activities in almost every sphere of human life and business activity. It was felt it should be  emphasised that natural human drives and dispositions evolving in time can be efficiently utilised in realising a broad spectrum of different goals. The partners believed that strategies should be shared and ideas developed in the course of the project and later used as inspirations. It was expected that their presentation in an open-access resource in the form of a gamification platform will provide opportunities and tools to address sustainability issues in the process of learner-based teaching, and demonstrate potential  for extention to other spheres and research areas in academia and business.

<< Implementation >>

At the first stage aimed at the development of the joint curriculum for the subject “Economics of Sustainability”, discussions, consultations, and brainstorming sessions were organised to specify areas of particular interest and urgency to form the foundation and background for a coursebook.
Based on the findings of the first phase of the project, a coursebook was written by partners who focused on their areas of expertise and conducted consultations according to specific needs.
The next stage involved workshops, lectures, and project development classes with pupils and students of partner institutions as well as surveys, and discussions with business partners. 
Competitions were also organised to find out students' attitudes to sustainability problems and to identify which areas they thought were the most relevant. These activities led to the creation of content to an open-access platform where ideas for utilising game dynamics in aspects of life and business activity are gathered. Partners invited other teachers to participate in creating out-of-the box ideas within their area of expertise and to demonstrate what sustainability issues they can approach in workshops, competitions, and other activities designed for their classes.

<< Results >>

The first stage involved the development of the joint curriculum for the subject “Economics of Sustainability” (O1) based on research and suggestions of partners.
A coursebook (O2) written by researchers followed their findings of the first phase of the project, which was meant as a support material for the new subject introduced into the curricula of partnering institutions. The additional and far-reaching functions of O2 can be performed by means of the PDF downloadable open-access resource to be used by students and teachers of other institutions worldwide. It is available here : https://www.sbc.org.pl/dlibra/publication/614485/edition/578059/content
Workshops and project development classes with pupils and students of partner institutions were carried out as well as consultations with business partners at the next stage of the project. These led to the creation of an open-access platform (O3) where ideas for utilising game dynamics and mechanics in different aspects can be found, available at : https://econosteam.eu/gamification/

2019-1-PL01-KA203-065831.title: Augmented RealiTy fOr Management SkIlls Development with real-based Cases
2019-1-PL01-KA203-065831.summary:
<< Background >>

Typical classes are based on knowledge transfer in the form of lectures among a large group. Students learn dry facts, even if they are based on case studies, and lack the opportunity to learn by doing and being exposed to real workplaces. The classroom has become a comfort zone, a place where help and assistance are offered, one that is not present in a real environment. Only practicing a variety of real-time interactions allows future graduates to enter the labor market with an adequate skill set. The above-mentioned factors manifest in deficiencies in soft skills and practice of graduates and cause an inability to properly react to the challenges in the future workplace. Responding to the above-mentioned needs, our goal was to enrich the study programs of all partners by implementing an innovative method for teaching and learning soft management skills based on augmented reality (AR).

<< Objectives >>

Working conditions are changing rapidly, workers are being replaced with automation or artificial intelligence, flexible working hours, and different types of employment such as freelancing or telecommuting are utilized commonly. As a result, bringing people together becomes more challenging, and a manager's ability to lead and direct is becoming more critical. The skills required from managers are the facilitation of communication, bringing a diverse workforce together, driving collaboration, and fostering teamwork. Thus, this project aimed to enrich the study programmes of all partners by implementing an innovative method for teaching and learning soft management skills based on augmented reality. The main goal of the AR application is to improve the quality and efficiency of higher education and the qualifications and competencies of students.
We believe that AR applications can support students in acquiring and developing soft skills such as communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. The project was mainly addressed to students and academics of Management and related fields of studies. However, it can be incorporated into and course, as soft skills are more demanded than technical abilities, even among graduates.

<< Implementation >>

The critical activities implemented throughout the project are the following: 
- Activities related to project management (fully described in the Management section).  
- Activities related to the project outputs O1 and O2 led to the project's ultimate goal: to enhance future managers' most critical soft skills (fully described in the Outputs section). 
- M1 - M6 meetings. The meetings facilitated communication and allowed us to bond and build relations between representatives of project partners, which had beneficial effects on cooperation throughout the whole project.
- E1 and E2 meetings enabled discussion of the project progress and adjusted it to the target user needs. Feedback from the business, academics, and students allowed us to ensure the relevance of the proposed form of the exercises and the developed application. 
- C1 and C2 summer school was a crucial activity in evaluating the final output and measuring its impact on the knowledge transfer process.

<< Results >>

The outputs of the project are the following: 
O1 - An interactive AR simulation dedicated to enhancing the training of future managerial staff.
O2 - User manual and laboratory instructions.
In addition to IOs (which will be detailed described in the next sections), we have achieved the following results:  
- academics trained during local staff training, 
- knowledge base materials for staff training, 
- students trained during summer school, 
- knowledge base for summer school, 
 - target groups meeting materials, 
- AR application survey and EEG-supported evaluation, 
- AR based management course preparation report, 
- final report, 
- research papers published in the high-rated journal,
- dedicated website.

2019-1-RO01-KA203-063400.title: Development of innovative approach for training for university professors to work in the modern diverse and intercultural environment
2019-1-RO01-KA203-063400.summary:
Esteban Gonzalez Pons stated in his speech for the 60th anniversary of the Treaties of Roma in front of the European parliament: "Europa is not a market, it is the will to live together. …". However, this will and ability to live together is a process that starts in the schools and last as long as we live. Crucial role in that process is taken by the period of the university education and the academic years. These are times and the places where the young people learn to communicate efficiently and with respect to others opinion based on experience, knowledge, skills and abilities. It is up to the university professors along with students themselves to form specific attitudes not to be intolerant, ignorant or discriminative. Therefore, it is of extreme importance that the university professors & assistants are well prepared and educated to support students to argue and form their points without prejudices and complexes.
Currently, in Romania and all partner countries there is no training or other course for university professors & assistants how to work in an intercultural & cross-cultural (ICC) environment. Although there some courses like ethno-pedagogy, ethno-psychology, intercultural teaching, etc. in the university programmes, it is still a great challenge for the professors themselves to work within an ICC environment given the fact that a good percentage of university students in Romania are from different ethnicity and different cultures. The rationale for the current project are multifold but the major are:
• The university education is a stimulus & preparation for acquiring a profession and specialty in life. Therefore, the way the education is conducted in the university is of utmost importance for the subsequent development of the students.
• Lack of national qualification & qualification programmes for university professors & assistants in ICC training & education in neither of the partners’ countries.
• Unawareness of the university professors & assistants about the main and additional forms of pedagogical interaction in ICC educational environment.
Therefore, the main aim of UniCulture project is to develop an innovative, holistic and interactive approach for training of university professors & teaching staff to conduct educational process in ICC environment.
The specific objectives of the proposal shall be to:
-	Raise the awareness of the university professors & assistants about the need to adopt their teaching styles to the constantly changing and dynamic environment in the universities.
-	Develop the competences of the university professors & assistant in intercultural and cross-cultural communication with the students during and outside the lectures.
-	Stress the importance of proper and adequate intercultural & cross-cultural communication as a mean for better social inclusion of different cultural & vulnerable groups of students.
The main target group of the project shall be the university professors & assistant that work on a daily basis in an environment that is getting more and more diverse, intercultural and demanding.
UniCulture project will develop a holistic & integral approach targeting university professors & assistants. UniCulture training pack will include:
1) Handbook for teaching staff to develop their personal & professional competencies how to work in ICC environment as well as how to overcome the ethnical stereotypes & prejudices in the educational process. It will guide the professors thought the contemporary approaches, methods and tools in ethno-pedagogy, ethno-phycology & intercultural education. 
2) Workbook for teaching staff with practical examples & case studies on how the taught methods & techniques can be applied in everyday life. It will include also interactive tests & exercises that will support the teachers in the learning process.
3) Manual for trainers to facilitate the conduction of UniCulture training course.
4) Guide on intercultural communication & social inclusion that will provide the link between working in such environment & support the inclusion of vulnerable groups. The Guide will develop the needed competences in the professors & assistants to support the social inclusion process in the universities.
UniCulture training pack will be created to support the university professors & assistants `to further develop their social & intercultural competences. It will provide the necessary theoretical and practical knowledge for recognition & application of interactive techniques for various forms of pedagogical interactions in ICC environment. Moreover, UniCulture will enhance the access & active participation of students from vulnerable groups & minorities in the educational & social processes in universities. Thus, it will foster the social inclusion and will fight the discrimination patterns in societies. 
UniCulture proposal shall be developed together by 3 universities, 2 NGOs & 1 associate university in response to all mentioned above topics & aims
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2019-1-RS01-KA203-000901.title: STEM in Heritage Sciences
2019-1-RS01-KA203-000901.summary:
<< Background >>

Over the last decade, the rapid developments in the application of STEM-derived methods and techniques in heritage disciplines, especially in archaeology, has created the need to innovate the HE curricula and to enable students to master novel skills necessary to meet the demands of the best research practices. Since various STEM-related specializations demand highly skilled teachers and adequate infrastructure, it is impossible for a single HE institution to competently cover this vast area of study. The HE institutions gathered in this consortium all specialize in a particular STEM area. The partner institutions have already collaborated on various levels and established good working relations. The project was aimed at creating a synergy, exchanging knowledge, experience, and resources, in order to offer to students of all HEs involved a more comprehensive overview of the most recent developments in the domain of STEM in heritage sciences. Three partners with vast practical experience in implementing STEM-related techniques in archaeological fieldwork are included in order to offer the most efficient hands-on training.

<< Objectives >>

Since a comprehensive coverage of most of the relevant STEM skills and methods in the heritage domain is not possible on the level of an individual HE institution, the main aim of the project HERISTEM has been to create a stable environment for developing a comprehensive coverage of the relevant novel skills and knowledge for students from all partner universities. Each partner was tasked with a particular domain of expertise (remote sensing, geoarchaeology, bioarchaeology, etc.), offering to the students and staff of the partner institutions the possibility to gain insight into the content not habitually offered by the curriculum of the home institution. The teaching material produced during the project implementation and the e-learning platform have been aimed at creating an online public resource for future teaching. Finally, the exchange in the framework of the project was aimed at creating better future conditions for a long-term project of establishing a joint degree on the regional level (Bosnia-Hercegovina, Croatia, Serbia, Slovenia) covering the majority of the relevant STEM-related skills in training of archaeologists and other heritage specialists.

<< Implementation >>

The main LTT activities of the project were workshops for students (geoarchaeology (C4), bioarchaoelogy (C1), remote sensing (C2), data science (C3), museum studies (C5)) and teaching staff (methods of e-learning (C7)), each devoted to a particular field of STEM implementation in archaeology and other heritage disciplines. Each workshop was followed by the production of teaching material (geoarchaeology (IO6), bioarchaoelogy (IO3), remote sensing (IO4), data science (IO5), museum studies (IO7), in order to create the online teaching platform (IO1), as a durable and open access resource for future teaching. 
The planned student and staff study visits (C8, C9, C11, C15), aimed at focused training and exchange of experiences, originally planned for 30 days, had to be of shorter duration (15 instead of 30 days), due to the travel restrictions during the COVID19 pandemic. 
The conference (E4) and the edited and peer-reviewed collection of papers derived from the presentations (IO2), were aimed at the professional public. The museum exhibition (E1) will continue to be shown in various settings after the completion of the project. The general public was approached through the online presentations at the event Researcher’s Night (E5).

<< Results >>

The teaching material from all the course (IO3, IO4, IO5, IO6, IO7, IO8), the recordings of most of the teaching activities, the project recommendations (IO10) and the e-learning platform (IO1), are produced according to the original plan, and will be publicly accessible after the project completion. The intention is to continue developing the contents pertinent to the project aims and to enlarge this online source. 
The final conference Teaching STEM in Heritage (E4) was recorded and resulted in the peer-reviewed collection (IO 2).
The exhibition STEM in Heritage Sciences (E1) offers a comprehensive overview of various topics and case-studies, aimed at the general public. It was conceived as an easily mobile exhibition and, after being shown at all the partner institutions, will continue to be shown in other settings: local museums, schools, etc. This and other activities at public dissemination (e.g. Researcher’s Night E5) aim at the affirmation of archaeology.
Throughout the project period, the partner institutions expanded the collaboration and drafted the plans for future joint efforts, in the direction of developing a regional joint degree specializing in the implementation of STEM in heritage sciences.
