2019-1-SE01-KA203-060500.title: Curating in Context
2019-1-SE01-KA203-060500.summary:
The aim of the Curating in Context project is to develop curatorial training with a strong focus on social impact through the involvement of local, regional and international actors, targeting individuals as well as cultural and civic organisations. The project aims to create educational resources and methods for use within the university and for the further education of cultural workers and citizens through strategies resulting from practices of performing arts and curators. Through methods of cross-pollination of know-how and best practices from the performing arts and civil society, the project also aims to collate the impact of the cultural and civil sectors on society.

The consortium of Curating in Context consists of the NGOs Tanzfabrik Berlin and Lokomotiva, Skopje, as well as the Higher Education Institutions Stockholm University of the Arts and University of Zagreb.
 
New formats of creating, presenting, disseminating and valorising artistic works are needed to match current local and global entanglements. Curating in Context will create knowledge and opportunities for future curators to critically reflect and address different socio-political and economic contexts and develop curatorial methods to rethink the practices of performing arts in relation to the civil sector.

Curating in Context aims to provide key competences and skills through which to:
• navigate between institutions, art organisations, civil society and the free-lance sector,
• enable and support sustainable self-employability,
• innovate fund-raising capabilities,
• manage artist led initiatives,
• create educational material that highlights reflection and engagement with art through context related perspectives such as production conditions, programming, organisation, governance, artistic practice and culture, the economy, the socio-political and cultural environment, and other institutional structures.
 
The Intellectual Outputs addressed in the project are:
1. Curating in Context - Manual /handbook/guidance material
Material that serves as reference for the developed manual/handbook/guidance itself will be available beyond the completion of the project as compendium for curatorial practice. Another, overall outcome of the project is the development of innovative visions and training methods to be implemented in academies and educational offer of NGOs on a long-term basis.
 
2. Curating in Context - Open Education Resource Platform
A Open Education Resource Platform suitable for education and training in HEI and NGO environments available beyond the completion of the project. Its content relates to interdisciplinary, academic and cross- sectorial approaches and methods through curating that allow to interlink specific local contexts with international perspectives. It will be published as a website linked to websites of each partner institution and other key stakeholders.
 
3. Curating in Context - Design and development of course/curriculum
A sustainable course/curriculum "Curating in context" for students and teachers to provide long-term cooperation and continuous dialogue and development. The course/curriculum, consisting in 7.5 ECTS, will be developed and tested by all partners during the project lifetime and will be integrated into their educational offer and individual curricula at all partner organisations.
 
Curating in context is addressing the following target groups:
1. MA students, teachers and alumni of our Higher Education Institutions
2. Mid-career artists
3. Cultural workers
4. Employees in the civic sector
 
On a broader scale, the project aims at strengthening the links between education, training and the professional environment in the civic and cultural sectors, opening of the partnering academic institutions towards the "invisible" knowledge of self-organising, local engagement and transversal learning. Furthermore, it aims at increasing the institutional ability to dialogue and support artists, art organisations and local initiatives in all partner countries as well as increasing mutual understanding of local and international differences and perspectives. Last but not least it will increase the exchange of best practices between northern, western, and south eastern European regions.

2019-1-SI01-KA203-060377.title: Language guidance tool for improving language knowledge
2019-1-SI01-KA203-060377.summary:
<< Background >>

The main aim of the LanGuide project is to support and contribute to the EU language policies of promoting interculturality, multilingualism, digital learning, so as to enhance intercultural understanding and multilingual practices within the internationalisation of tertiary education, within which a growing need for digital learning has been perceived.
In keeping with these objectives, the LanGuide Mobile App provides an open access mobile tool for students, teachers and administrative staff who wish to pursue flexible learning pathways in line with their own needs and learning style in their effort to study new languages or upgrade knowledge of previously acquired languages.  
In order to achieve such a result, the LanGuide project involved experts specialised in language acquisition and software development from 6 partner European universities. Together we developed the LanGuide App, a resource based on common language learning methodology and accessible on a jointly designed language-learning platform. Thus, language learners are offered an innovative tool to acquire language knowledge in some specialist domains, essential for mobility abroad, with ease and at their convenience.

<< Objectives >>

Our main goal was to provide an open access mobile tool, which would support and guide acquisition of language knowledge and communication skills, based on newly developed didactic methodology and usage of newly designed software available on the ubiquitous mobile devices. Such a resource can encourage and facilitate internationalization of higher education mobility programmes.
At the same time, we wished to develop a didactic framework, which can be transferred to learning of any other language beyond the languages of the partnership, namely, Croatian, Italian, Romanian, Slovenian, Spanish, and English, as well as to any other specialist domain beyond Academic language, Secretarial language, language for Mobility and language for IT,  the domains dealt with within the LanGuide project.
Consequently, the aim of the LanGuide project was twofold: a research based didactic framework for mobile language learning and a bank of language exercises for each language based on the new pedagogic insights and exploitable on the new LanGuide App.
Both the pedagogy and the innovative software result from interdisciplinary cooperation and reflect the diversity of the European tertiary institutions.

<< Implementation >>

The international partnership jointly engaged in the following activities:
-	Setting up the LanGuide project website
-	Carrying out a pre-course needs analysis survey
-	Developing of a common teaching/learning methodology for m-learning of foreign languages
-	designing of learning modules and syllabi for 4 specialist domains: Academic language Secretarial language, language for Mobility and language for IT for 3 types of learning personas: students, teachers and administrative staff
-	creating a bank of exercise for basic, intermediate and advanced English for specialisms
-	creating a bank of exercise for basic and intermediate language for 4 specialisms in Croatian, Italian, Romanian, Slovenian, Spanish
-	negotiating and tailoring the software requirements for distributing language-learning materials on the LanGuide Mobile App
-	adapting the language-learning materials for exploitation mobile devices
-	designing the Content Manager
-	designing the mobile app software
-	describing these activities and processed in the LanGuide Monograph
-	implementing internal quality control checks at various stages of the LanGuide project
-	piloting and testing the LanGuide App at all the partner institutions

<< Results >>

There are 3 main final products of our common endeavours:
-	the LanGuide Mobile App, an open-source platform for mobile language learning of English, Croatian, Italian, Romanian, Slovenian and Spanish for 4 specific domains: Academic language Secretarial language, language for Mobility and language for IT and 3 types of learners: students, academics and administrative staff;
-	the LanGuide Monograph: a collection of articles describing the processes and activities that informed work on the LanGuide Mobile App, thus giving insights and advice to teaching practitioners, learners of languages and software developers in terms of creating and using such resources for m-learning;
-	the LanGuide Project Web Site with instructions for downloading the LanGuide App, the Content Manager and further detailed information on the developments and activities of the international partnership, as well as additional learning activities;
As a result of international cooperation common teaching/learning methodology was developed which resulted in multilingual learning modules, which display features of effective intercultural engagement and promote intercultural communicative awareness.

2019-1-SI01-KA203-060575.title: Reformation of education on wood preservation
2019-1-SI01-KA203-060575.summary:
<< Background >>

Re/Forma Viva project incorporated innovative and interdisciplinary approaches to these issues with implementation of intellectual outputs (guidelines for students, 3D model web platform, complimentary database) that give potential to wider application of issues addressed by the project. Incorporating an interdisciplinary approach to the issues of preservation of cultural heritage (in wood) provides additional visibility outside academic and professional circles (tourism, cultural heritage presentation, natural sciences, digital skills and educational tools).

The main purpose of this project was the recognized need for more comprehensive pointers in preservation and documentation with incorporation of 3D methods of outdoor (wooden) sculptures. With the main points being: 
• Use of 3D in conservation documentation
• International documents and guidelines in outdoor wood sculptures preservation
• Outdoor wooden sculptures – conservation and restoration process
• Museum context of outdoor wooden sculptures
• Practical example on Forma Viva Sculpture Park

<< Objectives >>

Main objective of our project proposal was to incorporate ICT and 3D methods in conservation-restoration of cultural heritage (basing our methods partly on experiences from other fields such as archeology, architecture, etc). By providing synergies between partners from various sectors had an impact on all the participating partners. In this way the project proposal was the most successful as we learned to communicate as professionals and students of different fields and by recognizing benefits in this cooperation for all. Partners from conservation-restoration and museum sector strengthened their digital skills and competencies and partners from ICT sector strengthen their cultural skills and awareness on importance of cultural heritage. 

Composing a partnership from cross-sectors and Project leader being an Art Museum provided a good base and case study support for educational purposes. Through project activities participants were faced with practical challenges where they could use theoretical knowledge. Cooperation between two different fields sharing of knowledge and expanding skills was emphasised. Flexibility and open accessibility of created educational tools ensured that participants had access to project outcomes even when in person contact was not possible.

<< Implementation >>

In the project we have prepared:
- Three Intellectual Outputs (Guidelines on preservation of cultural heritage in wood for students, Integrated Web platform of 3D models, Database of documentation approach to preservation of cultural heritage)
-  Six Learning/Teaching/Training Activities (Staff Training Event, Seminar course for students, Summer School and Intensive student programme)
- Seven Multiplier Events (five presentations and two round tables)
- Seven Project Meetings

<< Results >>

Results of the project exceed the expectations from the application stage. As the application was prepared by BO that is not an HE institution the focus in the description was on cultural heritage protection. But throughout the project BO had a role of project management and providing a case study for field work while also implementing theoretical and practical frameworks in IO. During project activities the project workflow already showed the benefits that cooperation in the field of cultural heritage protection and incorporation of digital technologies produces results in education.

In the project we have incorporated:
- three new educational tools in the curriculum
- five new ICT methodologies in currucul of graphic design and new media studies
- three new ICT methodologies in the curriculum of restoration-presservation stuies


Other resoults connected with the project:
- Two exhibitions in galleries and two student exhibitions and presentations at the faculties
- Production of prototype jewellery inspired by 3D model of Forma Viva sculptures
- 3D models of Forma Viva sculptures
- Video on restoration and preservation of sculptures from Forma Viva Sculpture Park

2019-1-SK01-KA203-060778.title: Construction Safety with Education and Training using Immersive Reality
2019-1-SK01-KA203-060778.summary:
<< Background >>

Construction industry represents one of the most dangerous industries in terms of OHS. The construction site is a dynamic and complex environment, which makes it difficult to manage and monitor. Ensuring a safe working environment, i.e. the construction site and the construction process, prevents occupational accidents and even deaths. It is a socially topical topic that persists despite several initiatives. It is also an economic problem that costs about 4% of world GDP. In the XXI. century, it is unacceptable for a worker to be fatally injured during the performance of his work. 
Safety challenges are particularly significant for new and often low-skilled workers due to a lack of training. Injuries and accidents occur because workers are not properly trained in occupational safety. Every construction site is different, so technicians, workers and engineers need to be trained on the unique and potential risks that can arise from each new environment. In order to prevent the emergence of safety risks on construction sites, it is not possible to rely only on traditional, current measures for their prevention.

<< Objectives >>

The CSETIR project (Construction Safety with Education and Training using Immersive Reality) is based on the synergy between higher education institutions and representatives of construction practice. The goal was to introduce the use of intelligent technologies in the proper training process for the elimination of safety risks in the construction industry. The effort is the implementation of digital tools that enable the creation of a virtual environment that simulates construction scenarios and enables teachers, instructors, technicians and engineers to identify and prevent safety risks.
The aim of the project was also to improve the exchange of knowledge between representatives of the three sectors with the aim of innovating approaches to accident prevention through effective cooperation between researchers in the field of virtual reality and construction companies. The CSETIR partnership has developed innovative and interactive VR/AR (virtual and augmented reality) solutions for the prevention of construction site accidents. CSETIR has created a useful tool for teachers, technicians and engineers that can be used in any construction project. The created digital tool with study materials is accessible online on the web site.

<< Implementation >>

The CSETIR project was focused on the creation of a digital education tool for the elimination of safety risks on the construction site. In order to create the tool, it was necessary to analyze the issue of construction safety, the issue of a suitable ICT tool for VR/AR with immersive elements, the possibilities of processing the construction process using building information modeling. 18 safety risk scenarios on the construction site were processed, divided into 6 basic groups, e.g. 4 scenarios related to falling from a height, etc.; and their subsequent description for visualization in a VR environment. The correct use of the created digital tool is supported by the creation of manuals for its use for teachers and students. Of course, the project outputs are available on the project website.
Part of the project solution were activities connected with project management, distribution and management of specific partial project tasks, coordination of their fulfillment, creation of communication channels between the solvers, dissemination activities and project monitoring. The project managers also participated in 7 transnational project meetings (4 face-to-face + 3 online).

<< Results >>

The project outputs were focused on 5 intellectual outputs - IO1- Necessary analyses, IO2 BIM models, IO3 interactive VR/AR solutions, IO4 Teaching manual and IO5 Online platform. The project was not focused on multiplication events or teaching and training activities.
Intellectual output 1 (IO1) was processed in the form of a report in five language versions (in English, Slovak, Portuguese, Croatian and Greek). It contains overviews, analyzes and knowledge of all project solvers related to the field of health and safety in the construction industry, the use of augmented, mixed and virtual reality for possible project solutions, building information modeling (BIM). In IO2, BIM models of construction sites and a library of construction site equipment objects focused mainly on safety are processed. IO3 contains a proposed digital tool for the elimination of safety risks at the construction site in a collaborative virtual environment enabling interaction in the virtual space between multiple participants; and a description of the visualization of security risk scenarios. IO4 provides training manuals for using the developed digital tool. IO5 provides an online platform for accessing project outputs and results in several formats.

2019-1-SK01-KA203-060789.title: Education of Future ICT Experts Based on Smart Society Needs
2019-1-SK01-KA203-060789.summary:
<< Background >>

ICT curricula at HEIs traditionally have STEM content. There are different options in which direction the “new-born” ICT experts can continue in their careers after graduation. They often become new entrepreneurs. Our primary motivation for applying for our project was tackling skills gaps and creating a new innovative course focused on ICT-based entrepreneurship. Another motivation was implementing an intensive interdisciplinary and intercultural study environment and promoting internationalisation. We wanted to contribute to open education and innovative practices in a digital era by creating a vital extension to the education of future ICT experts.
An online survey was conducted in February and March 2019. Two questionnaires were designed - ICT companies and students. Based on the responses of IT companies, it can be noted that when they are recruiting new employees, they attach great importance, in addition to IT skills, to the transfer of skills and business skills. Other factors included digital skills, networking, and language skills. For students, it is crucial to have the possibility to learn Project Management and Planning, Delegation and Time Management, Team Management, Communication and Negotiation skills.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of our project was to enforce ICT student teams to deal with economic, societal, and environmental challenges by introducing entrepreneurial learning that follows and respects the UN's and EU's current strategic documents. We wanted to prepare and develop training courses covering ICT, new technologies and digital competencies that are important when creating new business plans for ICT students' start-ups. 
We wanted to give the project participants chance to collaborate with colleagues from different European universities on an entrepreneurial case related to recognising the needs of society and providing a smart solution by using ICT. We wanted to promote internationalisation. We wanted to achieve and push our project participants to  "go out of the box" of their traditional education (STEM) by giving them some basic knowledge and experience of project-based learning, student teamwork, and blended mobility through developing specific entrepreneurial cases for Smart Society domain.
We wanted to develop educational materials that support additional education in the field of business. These educational materials were prepared for the educational process at HEIs at the ICT-oriented schools and faculties.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented different activities related to project management, development of educational materials, multiplying of project impact, learning, teaching and training of ICT-oriented entrepreneurship.
Our activities related to project management were covered by 8 transnational project meetings (2 online). Our activities related to the development of educational materials were covered by intellectual outputs: IO1 Entrepreneurial cases: "entrepreneurship in ICT" and "entrepreneurship with ICT", IO2 SmartSoc proceedings, IO3 SmartSoc E-learning Platform. Our activities related to multiplying the project impact were covered by 3 multiplier events. Our project activities related to learning, teaching and training activities were organised as blended mobilities. We organised our blended mobilities three times – in 2020, 2021 and 2022. The blended mobility itself was adapted to the duration of one semester. Two phases of blended mobility were planned for the 13-week - virtual and physical. The virtual part lasted 10 weeks and the physical part 2 weeks. There was one spare week to complete the tasks from the virtual part, if a student team needed it, between them. The blended mobility completion was planned for late May by the workshop.

<< Results >>

We developed three independent adaptations of an interdisciplinary and intercultural course focused on the entrepreneurship education of ICT students. Each version is an output of one year of blended mobility that was introduced as a new educational method. Proposals of entrepreneurial cases prepared for student teams and a brief overview of business plans and business model canvases of virtual start-up-s are recorded in the Intellectual output 1 (pdf document published on the project web). Lectures of experts from our workshops (Intellectual Output 2) are recorded, and related presentations are uploaded to the project e-learning portal (Intellectual Output 3). Lectures are our Intellectual output 2. All these outputs are our contribution to open education and innovative practices in a digital era. They are free for everyone interested.
Our project results enable us to bring novelties regarding topics under consideration, i.e., ICT expertise related to smart society needs, with a particular emphasis on entrepreneurship and skills related to evaluation of business perspectives and societal implications of the proposed solution, respecting relevant smart specialisation strategies defined in the EU at different geographical levels.

2019-1-TR01-KA203-076155.title: Enhancing Digital Literacy of University Students (E-DigiLit)
2019-1-TR01-KA203-076155.summary:
<< Background >>

1-Digital divide: Today we know that university students can benefit from the digital age, but older people cannot. The Statistics in EU also indicate similar results. However, the rate of individuals who have carried out learning activities over the internet in the last 3 months has been 15.9% in 2022. As a result, it is clear that Z generation has grown with digital technologies from the moment they were born. However, they need guidance to reach beneficial knowledge on the internet. The solution is to teach digital literacy to them.
2-New digital competencies different from traditional ICT teaching:
 University students spend an increasing part of their lives online. Their aims to be online are generally for entertainment, playing games and socializing. However, they have to learn plagiarism, cyberbullying and problem solving or producing digital content. It is a necessity for the new generation to be trained according to these new competencies in the frame of DIGCOMP.
3-Sustainability:  New trends direct us to take into consideration carbon footprint and protect energy consumption. It is aimed to provide a qualified education opportunity with the flipped education system and synchronous and asynchronous learning tools.

<< Objectives >>

Digital literacy is an umbrella concept for important skill clusters such as ICT literacy, technological literacy and information literacy. This Project was designed to meet the need of university students by improving their ability of surviving in the digital age. For this purpose, four objectives were established to achieve. The objectives were to;

- Improve the digital literacy skills of university students
- Develop a learning environment for digital literacy skills.
- Contribute to the capacity building of universities on digital literacy through training the teaching staff
- Facilitate access to sources related to digital literacy by sharing outputs on the project website

<< Implementation >>

At the beginning of the project, two questionnaires were prepared and applied to the stakeholders and partner institutions and university students to identify the important topics for digital literacy and their needs. We used the result report of the questionnaire to prioritize target group needs and to develop a digital literacy course curriculum and relevant training in each partner country. In order to improve the digital literacy skills of university students, comprehensive training materials based on the curriculum and lesson plan were developed for a new digital literacy course. Also, an online guidebook for teaching staff (Guidebook for Instructor) was developed. After all partners agreed on the teacher training program and students' pilot study, each partner university applied the pilot training for digital literacy courses in their countries by using E-DigiLİt Learning Management System (LMS)(lhttp://lms.edigilit.eu/), developed for this project, or their own e-learning platforms. This LMS includes all education materials including all videos, presentations, lesson plans and gamification elements for the digital literacy course. All education materials were made available to all of Europe.

<< Results >>

Educational Materials of the digital literacy elective course have been prepared to meet the needs of university students with different learning styles. Educational materials (learning materials) were prepared as specified in the curriculum.
Learning materials of the digital literacy elective course were developed according to the target group levels to prepare students for current and future technologies in the digital age.
The Results of the Project are:
1- Tools for providing digital literacy skills are developed
2- Digital literacy skills of university students are improved.
3- Capacity building of universities on providing digital literacy skills are improved
4- Cooperation among partners is strengthened

2019-1-UK01-KA203-061665.title: Child-Centred Competences for Early Childhood Education and Care
2019-1-UK01-KA203-061665.summary:
<< Background >>

As a concept, child-centredness reflects different aspects of  pedagogical approaches to Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC): romantic, democratic and developmental, which are demonstrated in various ways (Campbell-Barr et al., 2018), but far less is known about the role of Higher Education (HE) initial ECEC training for supporting students to work with groups of children, potentially requiring child-centred competences to be enacted in multiple and varying ways. Across Europe, the practice of combining theoretical and practical elements of training for ECEC in HE are well established (Oberhuemer et al., 2010). However, problems remain with the balance between the theoretical and the practical, and how the two might integrated. There is a need to better understand child-centredness to improve recognition of this complex skill, and support students in bridging gaps between theory and practice. The project established a child-centred competences framework to support students in self-evaluation of competences whilst on placement during ECEC initial training. An online e-book and embedded resources will tackle the mismatch between identifying the importance of child-centeredness and how this is realised in initial ECEC training.

<< Objectives >>

The project sought to improve understandings of what it means to be a skilled and competent child-centred ECEC professional in seven countries: Croatia, Denmark, Ireland, Italy, Spain, Romania and UK. The analysis of the training delivered in a previous Strategic Partnership project provided important lessons on how to enhance the previous online courses, whilst informing a new e-book and resources for students and their mentors. The development of a child-centred competences framework, that was cross-referenced against existing ECEC competency profiles and grounded in relevant literature, provides a unique, European wide resource for enhancing the quality of ECEC pedagogical practice and forms the basis of the e-book. Due to the pressures of Covid-19, and recognition of the impact this had on the ECEC community who were at various times providing remote and/or in person ECEC, the original design was altered to focus less on the role of mentors and to provide students with a self-reflection tool. In recognition of this shift, the combining of the competence framework, resources and e-book created a standalone, open access, output that students could access to support their self reflection on their child-centred competences.

<< Implementation >>

Activities consisted of regular meetings, producing outputs and dissemination. 
December 2019 Plymouth, UK -  Meeting to provide overview of the project and IO1 report on evaluation of the online courses led to IO2 and the three online courses being developed and refined.
Timescales for IO2 were adjusted in light of the IO1 report and the early onset of Covid-19, with the courses going live in 
The analysis of competences (IO3) was initiated during the Plymouth meeting and ran concurrently with IO2 and the initial stages of IO5, being completed in March 2020.
The combining of IO4, 5 and 7 began in March 2020 and the child-centred competences framework, e-book and resources were finalised in September 2021. The development of the resources was supported by an online Learning and Teaching Activity in March 2020 (as a replacement to the Romania Transnational Meeting), with subsequent input as needed. Other online meetings took place throughout the course of the project to support the development of the framework, resources and e-book. 
Dissemination activities evolved around the pressure of Covid-19, but were ongoing throughout the project, including the Multiplier Events and other conferences.

<< Results >>

Each of the intellectual outputs produced a concrete report, framework or resource, with outputs four, five and seven being combined to create one discreet output that spoke to each of the areas. This adjustment ensure a more efficient way of working.

O2 Refinement of courses and delivery of courses

O6 Evaluation of courses and resources

2019-1-UK01-KA203-062062.title: Architecture's Afterlife: The Multi-sector impact of an architectural qualification
2019-1-UK01-KA203-062062.summary:
<< Background >>

The Architecture's Afterlife study (AA) sought to identify the cross-sector employment destinations of graduates who did not remain in the architecture sector after graduation. 

Anecdotal evidence based on the mobility of architecture graduates in the UK suggested that up to a third of architecture graduates choose careers other than architecture. Initially, the AA study sought to establish whether this was the case across Europe too. We were also curious as to whether architecture, by virtue of its inherent interdisciplinarity (being informed by social sciences, applied sciences, humanities, natural sciences, etc.), was predisposed to facilitate mobility across sectors. 

Therefore, in surveying architecture graduates who had moved to other sectors, we sought to identify which of the skills acquired during their training had proved most transferable and useful in their current jobs. This research, we reasoned, could provide more general insights not only into which skills are transferable across sectors, but also into which sectors are most receptive to professionals with unrelated degrees, all of which has important implications for sectors facing skills shortages – within and beyond the construction industry.

<< Objectives >>

While the Architecture’s Afterlife study focused on one specific degree type, that of architecture, as its core dataset, it sought to offer a methodology for how other disciplines could assess their own qualification mobility across a range of sectors beyond architecture.

Drawing on both qualitative and quantitative data, the AA study surveyed 2637 respondents living in 65 countries and conducted 49 in depth interviews with architecture graduates working as architects and in other sectors related and unrelated to architecture. 

While it has already been established that the majority of all graduates will work in sectors not directly related to their original degree subject, the research sought to identify which skills are most transferable across sectors – both those that are currently taught and those that aren't but graduates feel are needed. All of this has significant implications for sectors facing skills shortages – including and beyond construction – which assume that such shortages are due to the inability of higher education to produce qualified/skilled candidates, rather than the employers’ inability to recognise the skills candidates actually possess.

<< Implementation >>

WP1: PREPARATORY ANALYSES
WP2:SECTORAL ANALYSES: the data selection of flow A in Project Flow 1: graduates remaining in  architecture. Codified survey responses generated variables that were tested within the qualitative interviews.
WP3: CROSS-SECTORAL STUDY: data flows B + C (Flow 2, 3, 4) to identify relational sectors and actors. The generated data enabled country-specific comparisons.

WP6 DISSEMINATION: WEBSITE, DATABASE, VISUALISATIONS: online platform for all project resources including reports, papers and the survey  As we acquired more and more data, the interactive database collecting survey responses and presenting them in live-generated visualisations grew accordingly and is openly searchable at http://publicdatabase.architectures-afterlife.com/.

2019-1-UK01-KA203-062118.title: Higher Education Curricula Development on the Collaborative Economy in Europe
2019-1-UK01-KA203-062118.summary:
The collaborative economy is an economic model that turns consumers into producers (prosumers). Collaborative economy platforms increasingly cover important sectors of the economy such as peer-to-peer (P2P) accommodation, passenger transport, or collaborative finance. P2P accommodation occurs when individuals offer, in exchange for money, a room or an entire house for short-term accommodation. Companies such as Airbnb or HomeAway have been able to increase the supply of rooms for people to stay in, without the need to create new assets or increase the number of human resources in the company. By enabling regular homeowners to lease unused space, and by providing a marketplace where consumers can easily reach this space, these companies have disrupted the hospitality market and given rise to an informal tourism accommodation sector. These platforms allow citizens to earn revenue from underutilised space and, at the same time, access affordable accommodation when travelling. Conversely, by removing property from the long-term rental market, P2P accommodation platforms contribute to rent price increases, as supply and demand diverge. Neighbourhood dynamics are also disrupted by the arrival of tourists. All these complex implications have attracted scholars’ interest and there are currently plenty of research projects about these topics. Nevertheless, limited attention has so far been given to the production of academic curricula covering the many and varied implications for business and society. 

EU businesses should increase their competitiveness by aligning their skills and operations according to innovative business models. In terms of skills and competences, there is a clear discordance between the research conducted on the topic and academic learning materials within the partner countries. While there are a significant number of researchers working on collaborative economy issues – thus recognising their relevance – these research interest and skills are still not being translated into academic modules/professional training courses. 

The main aim of this project is the creation of modules to fill the knowledge gap about the collaborative economy, particularly in business, economics, management and tourism disciplines. While these disciplines may in some cases address the digitalisation of economic activity, they fail to comprehend the concept of the collaborative economy and all the consequences arising from its steep growth. 

To achieve this, the following objectives have been identified:
● To analyse the workings and characteristics of successful P2P providers (e.g. Airbnb, HomeAway, Booking.com, FairBnb, CouchSurfing, and HomeExchange), and to identify and analyse the role of innovative intermediaries (start-ups) within the market (e.g. UnderTheDoormat, HostMaker). 
● To examine the social, economic and ethical implications that arise from the use of P2P accommodation platforms in different European countries (e.g. impact on traditional accommodation market sector, housing prices, neighbourhoods, consumption patterns, etc.). 
● To design curricula and provide guidance for educators on the use of the learning resources. 
● To disseminate the educational materials in the countries of the involved partners and in the wider EU.

This project will create both academic modules at Masters level and Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) about different aspects of the collaborative economy. The educational materials will support the European agenda for Higher Education Reform by participating in mutually beneficial partnerships between EU higher education institutions and the industry through collaboration with the European Holiday Home Association (EHHA). The project targets HE graduates who want to get involved in the collaborative economy, as well as the general public, since a shorter version of the postgraduate modules will be available open source in MOOC format through the eLearning platform Future Learn. The project will include a collation of scholarship on the collaborative economy, as well as a sector-based analysis of the P2P accommodation by using a mixed-methods approach (e.g. questionnaire survey, interview, case study analysis, etc.). Surveys and interviews with key stakeholders will be used to analyse the workings and impacts of P2P accommodation platforms. Students will be able to critically analyse both business opportunities and the impact the collaborative economy, with a special focus on P2P accommodation. The European Commission (2016) has set an agenda for the collaborative economy to explore these issues to be better informed and finalise the discussion towards shaping a regulatory framework. Therefore, this project will also help to inform policy makers at local and EU level.

Reference
European Commission (2016a), “A European agenda for the collaborative economy”, available at http://europa.eu/rapid/press-release_MEMO-16-2002_en.htm

2020-1-CZ01-KA203-078478.title: Transformation of a traditional language school by means of business model innovation.
2020-1-CZ01-KA203-078478.summary:
<< Background >>

The main motive for the creation of this project was the declining language education market, whether from the point of view of education providers (language schools) or their consumers (clients of language schools). Language schools were struggling with a decrease in clients (drop in demand), falling margins (unattractiveness of the market), high market saturation (a large number of language schools) and an unsustainable business model focused on the classic form and content of education (language without professional context , the teacher as a replicator of teaching, the student as a passive consumer of teaching).
Our goal was to bring teaching closer to current requirements for education and at the same time take into account current trends in business based on the idea of ​​networking, sharing and co-creation. This project reflected the needs of LS clients (to change the form and content of teaching so that the student becomes an active participant in the course and at the same time can focus not only on language, but also personal development) as well as the needs of language school and their lecturers (responding to teaching trends, adapting teaching to clients and using conversation and game-learning techniques).

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project was to create a sustainable business model for language schools. This required: (1) to innovate the existing business model of language schools, (2) to create new products that will better reflect the current requirements of language school clients, (3) to create instructions for trainers so that they become leaders of the teaching process, (4) create tutorials for students to learn more easily, (5) create an online platform that connects course providers with their clients.
Overall, we wanted to achieve the transformation of language schools so that these schools become mediators of education, that is, mediators between trainers (mentors of language education) and clients of language schools. This project was intended to help understand not only how language schools work today (based on the analysis of the business model), but also how the market of language schools works (based on the analysis of the market, competition and customers). The project was to identify the pillars of business sustainability in this sector and to innovate the business model, and by creating new products it was to reflect current market conditions.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented a total of eight activities that led to the achievement of six project outputs. We focused on the three activities that led to the achievement of IO1. This required analyzing the market (activity 1), the business model of language schools (activity 2) and the customers of language schools (activity 3). The market analysis was carried out using methodological sheets that allowed to characterize sub-markets, to analyze competitors in these markets and to analyze external factors. The analysis was focused on the markets of 5 EU countries. The analysis of the business model of language schools was carried out in the form of a questionnaire survey (Q1 and Q2). These three activities also had a connection to the collaboration of new products (activity 4). Activity 5 was based on brainstorming, with the help of which the limits of the current business model were identified and the features of the new business model were proposed in relation to the findings that resulted from activity 1-4. Activities 6 and 7 were implemented as pilot trainings for trainers and clients of language schools. Activity 8 led to the creation of an online Webinar, the content of which consists of partial activities of the project and its outputs.

<< Results >>

As part of this project, we had a total of six outputs. The outputs of the project are: (1) analysis of the market of language schools and analysis of the business model of language schools; (2) creation of four new products (The SMART Mindset Program); (3) Creating a guide for teachers on how to teach in the spirit of the Learn&Lead philosophy; (4) Creating a student tutorial for four new courses; (5) Creating a webinar for online interaction between trainers and students; (6) Proposal of a new business model of language schools.
These outputs contain a total of 8 sub-results for IO1. These are market analysis (R1), customer analysis for all markets (R2), analysis of Slovak customers(R3), questionnaire I (R4), questionnaire II (R5), business model analysis (R6), market analysis of Poland (R7) and market analysis of Croatia (R8). Furthermore, we produced four documents on IO2 (course syllabi), one document on IO3 (guidelines for trainers), four documents on IO4, and one document on IO6 in the form of an innovative business model canvas. The partial outputs of this project consist of a total of 18 documents in the English language. An important output of the project is also a monograph on the transformation of language schools.

2020-1-DE01-KA203-005669.title: Evidence Implementation in Clinical Practice
2020-1-DE01-KA203-005669.summary:
<< Background >>

Within the European Cost Action CA17117 Evidence Based Research (EVBRES) the project coordinator Dr. Robert Prill (RP) met leading actors in the field of Evidence Based Health Care, and discussed several needs for health and society. The Brandenburg Medical School Theodor Fontane (MHB) was founded by several clinics being responsible for health care in the county side. Therefore international partnerships and international knowledge transfer and programs are needed to implement best available evidence into clinical practice. Developing and modifying existing strategies and to teach participants how to best implement knowledge in their clinical setting, combined with projects which really change the clinical practice and also raise awareness on the need for this kind of cooperation and the need for change are of high interest to the MHB. We applied to take the chance to build strategic partnerships with leading actors and organizations in the field across Europe and benefit from their large experience in the field as well as sharing our experience in Evidence Based health care. The Czech partner with their previous Erasmus+ project SPIDER in the field of Evidence Implementation helped finding the direction for this project.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives were to improving skills and qualifications of the partners in Evidence Based Health Care, in particular in critical thinking especially in the implementation and utilization of evidence in health care practice.  Also International cooperation, international relations, development cooperation and to develop and revise new innovative curricula/educational methods/development of training courses for physical therapists, rehabilitation specialists, other allied health professionalizes, medicine and nursing were objectives of the project. We wanted to give one big lack within the medical research process a focus: The implementation of research findings in clinical practice. While only rare activities have been established in Europe, mainly in the few affiliated centers of the Joanna Briggs Institute, it was time to focus this on a university level with a strong connection to clinical institutions. While research finds are published more than ever, their implementation in clinical practice is still lacking. Due to lack of clinical leaders in the field of physiotherapy and allied health professions, there is a strong need for education and for transdisziplinary work.

<< Implementation >>

The most relevant activities have been the learning teaching training (LTT) activities for health care professionals. Within those training courses participants from the medical field and paramedical field were taught on how to become a clinical leader, how to implement change, how to implement best available evidence into clinical practice and how to assess what works in terms of implementation in their field. This included, but was not limited to, preoperative education, reduce of precautions after surgery, oral hygiene in inpatient settings, advanced care planning, diabetes education and many more activities in daily health care practice. LTT also included clinical leader workshops and many hours of discussion and in-person or online mentoring. Implementation strategies and their facilitators and barriers across Europe have been addressed within workshop on a better understanding of differences between health care settings. Apart form LTT we organized two Multiplier Events to present and disseminate the results of the developed 32 Implementation projects, to raise awareness about the implementation approach to further attract people from outside of the participating institutions to deal with implementation in clinical practice.

<< Results >>

The key objective to reduce the gap between research and practice in healthcare and to facilitate international cooperation was reached by training 32 Health Care Professionals in the field of evidence implementation. Four of them were trained to be able to independently train participants in their countries and sending institutions. This project developed two Intellectual Outputs. Addressing this gap was further addressed by implementing 32 Best Practice Implementation Projects to clinical practice settings in the participating countries. This results in unique personal, institutional and European changes

2020-1-DE01-KA203-005671.title: Teaching standard STEM topics with a key competence approach
2020-1-DE01-KA203-005671.summary:
<< Background >>

One element of the European Education Area is to ensure the development of its citizens' key competences. The reason for this is that these key competences were identified as requirement for a healthy and sustainable lifestyle, active and responsible citizenship and personal and professional fulfilment (COM 2019); and thus, naturally, are of utmost importance for each citizen. 

A key competence is defined as a combination of knowledge, skills and attitudes (Council of the European Union, 2018). However, maths and science education at school traditionally delivers fundamental subject knowledge e.g. functions and chemical reactions, but learners’ skills and attitudes to use gained knowledge are not sufficiently nurtured likewise (Maass, Geiger, Romero & Goos 2019). This means, there is a mismatch between what citizens need and what most maths and science classrooms nowadays are prepared to offer.

Thus, we applied with the STEMkey project to provide solutions to develop key-competences in maths, science, technology and engineering (STEM), including digital and technology-based competences. Therewith, STEM classrooms can contribute to the EU's endeveaours to equip its citizens with key competences.

<< Objectives >>

Our objective was to introduce and implement the EU's Key Competence Framework in Higher Education (HE) programmes for future STEM teachers and to find solutions to transfer the framework into STEM education practice. 

Therefore, it was necessary to transform our HE partners' and their students‘ understanding and ability to teach standard STEM topics, such as electricity or chemical elements, in two ways:

1) A transformation from the sole purpose of lessons to deliver isolated subject knowledge to lessons which allow learners to develop skills to use gained knowledge and attitudes to responsibly decide on how to use it in various contexts („global challenges“) ==> key competence-based STEM learning.

2) A transformation from delivering isolated knowledge on one specific topic, to a forward-looking approach which connects knowledge from several subjects and disciplines and also connects to the real-world ==> integrated STEM learning.

One part of the solution is to make HE partners and future teachers understand the relation between knowledge, skills and attitudes, and how they have an effect on peoples' active citizenship. And consequently, emphasize the role STEM education can play for our future.

<< Implementation >>

The STEMkey project implemented the following types of activities:

1) Project Management and Implementation (with the sub-categories planning and monitoring, internal collaboration and communication, risk and quality management, reporting, contact to the Agency and external communication, dissemination and sustainability)

2) Intellectual Outputs (IO; production of the above-mentioned learning materials involving different phases: development and review of the first version of materials, piloting of the materials in partner institutions, revision of the piloted materials and second review and discussion across the Consortium, presenting and discussing during Multiplier Events, piloting and discussion of revised versions during Summer School, production of final versions, translations, implementation at partner institutions)

3) Transnational Project Meetings (TPM, 4 digital and 2 in-person)

4) Multiplier Events (ME, 5 national events and 1 international event, taking place in 6 partner countries) and

5) Learning, Teaching and Training Activities (LTT, Summer School involving all partners and students from 6 partner countries), 
all of which are described in the accordant sections of this report.

<< Results >>

OUTPUTS
(1) 13 modules (IO) for STEM programmes at Higher Education Institutions (HEI)
IO1 introduces the EU Key Competence Framework and introduces approaches to transfer it into STEM classroom practice. 
IO2-IO12 exemplarily cover standard topics from maths, biology, chemistry, physics, engineering and (digital) technology, to explicitly demonstrate how the STEMkey approach is applied.
IO13 provides a toolkit which supports the usage of IO 2-12 and supports users to apply the STEmkey approach to further topics.

(2) STEMkey Partnership Platform
The platform (https://icse.eu/international-projects/stemkey/) is embedded in the website of the International Centre for STEM Education ICSE (icse.eu). There is an interactive space for partners to communicate and exchange files, each institution is featured in a blog and offers the option to start dialogues with experts from these institutions and all materials can be downloaded.

OUTCOMES
(A) Novel ideas on Critical Thinking, Problem-Solving and Creativity in STEM education
(B) HE partners and their students with deep understanding of introduced concepts
(C) Upgraded course programmes at partner HEI
(D) Strong Strategic Partnership, also connected to HEI beyond partnership.

2020-1-DE01-KA203-005687.title: LSP Teacher Education Online Course for Professional Development
2020-1-DE01-KA203-005687.summary:
<< Background >>

Quality teaching has become an issue of importance, but learning to teach in higher education too often is a difficult undertaking. A Communication from the Commission on a Renewed Agenda for Higher Education (2017) mentions the disturbing fact that “too many higher education teachers have received little or no pedagogical training”. This is a matter of particular concern for teachers and learners of Language for Specific Purposes (LSP) in vocational education and training (VET) as well as higher education institutions that do not lead to degrees in languages, where language skills are expected to enhance mobility and employability. Since LSP is in direct relationship with the world of work, it is assumed to play a key role to create multilingual and mobile citizens. The importance of language skills for the labour market is emphasized in different EU documents such as Multilingualism: An Asset for Europe and a Shared Commitment (2008) or The European Strategy for Multilingualism (2008) which promote mobility of the labour force, employability and growth in Europe. Moreover, quality teaching and education are the basis for participation, equal opportunities and the Sustainable Development Goals (UN, 2015).

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to achieve the implementation of solutions and tools to support skills development for existing and future LSP teachers in higher education, both at national level for each of the partners and at a European level. To address the challenges set in the highly specific context of LSP, a transnational and collaborative approach was developed, tested and evaluated. Therefore, existing LSP courses were identified and analysed. Moreover, relevant competences of LSP teachers were defined. Subsequently, needs analyses were carried out and results from previous research projects were taken into account. Based on this, a multilingual learning platform was developed and a self-directed online learning course was designed, implemented, tested and evaluated. It is now available as Open Educational Resource (OER). Therewith, members of the LSP community (especially teachers but also researchers, etc.) may acquire those skills and competencies from now which are necessary to teach languages for a specific professional domain on an advanced level. Moreover, the self-directed online course can be used to refresh and enhance existing skills and competences.

<< Implementation >>

In order to develop a self-directed LSP online course on a transnational collaborative basis, the partners involved carried out the following activities: analysis and synthesis of existing programmes, definition of an online teaching methodology for a LSP teacher education online course, development of the identified course content, implementation of the developed course into a learning management system in all nine languages of the consortium, carry out both a pilot phase and a trialling phase of the developed LSP teacher education online course, analysis of the collected user data and application of learning analytics, evaluation of feedback collected from enrolled users, and quality management of the whole project. In order to carry out and coordinate the activities mentioned before, partners met six times for so-called Transnational Project Meetings and two times for so-called Learning, Teaching and Training Activities on instructional design as well as on learning analytics. Finally, all results were presented to and discussed with the LSP community and other interested parties during the multiplier event, namely the final conference. Furthermore, all results were published and distributed at conferences, social media, etc.

<< Results >>

The main result or product is the developed multilingual LSP online learning course. The course is now available as a massive open online course. It is implemented and ready to use in the project’s learning management system (LMS) but also available as download (Open Educational Resource) which can be implemented in different (universities’) LMS. The course is available in all nine languages of partners of the strategic partnership namely Croatian, English, French, German, Italian, Polish, Slovenian, Spanish and Turkish.

Moreover, piloting and trialling phases were carried out in order to guarantee a smooth and user-friendly course/product. Results were taken into account to revise the course and develop it further but they were also analysed, presented (e.g. at the final conference) and published (e.g. in the project booklet). Results are also available on the project Internet pages as well as in forthcoming publications (special edition in a journal, conference proceedings). Therewith, the results are available for prospective course takers but also contribute to general discussions of teaching LSP, distance education and self-directed learning; findings might be used as blueprints for other instructional designers.

2020-1-DE01-KA203-005700.title: Building the Universities of the Future through Social Innovation Education
2020-1-DE01-KA203-005700.summary:
<< Background >>

To prepare students and universities to thrive in and make a positive contribution to today’s fast pacing world, higher education needs to shift from traditional teaching and learning to more innovative, entrepreneurial, and collaborative practices. Acknowledging the importance of entrepreneurial and socially engaged citizens, the EU emphasises the need to cultivate transversal skills and foster links between higher education and society. 
BUFSIE addresses these needs by promoting Social Innovation Education (SIE) in higher education institutions (HEI), empowering teachers to integrate SIE into their teaching practice, and equipping students with social, entrepreneurial, and civic competences.
BUFSIE scales up the novel educational pedagogy of SIE and transfer it to the higher education level, assisting in this way European HEIs to boost the social, entrepreneurial, and civic competences of their students while at the same time, enhance teachers’ professional development by engaging them into an innovative set of teaching and learning activities. The project emphasizes a value creation approach, leveraging the potential of SIE to empower students across disciplines, foster cooperation, and collectively drive change within HEIs.

<< Objectives >>

BUFSIE intends to be the gateway project for diffusing SIE in European HEIs and embed the change-making skills as part of the modernized curriculum at an EU level has the following objectives: 
Strengthen employability and new professional paths by providing transversal skills and social innovation learning opportunities to students.
Go beyond teaching entrepreneurial competences in the narrow sense of the term and instead, equip and improve the practical skills of students in any field of activity and academic discipline.
Improve teachers’ professional development.
Foster new ways of effective collaboration among university-business-community and build sustainable partnerships towards integrating such collaborations in HEIs.
Enhance education by incorporating and integrating experiential, participatory and student-centered teaching and learning practices whereby the active and practical contribution of students is pivotal.

<< Implementation >>

The BUFSIE project spanned 30 months and comprised several phases. 
The first phase focused on the design of the BUFSIE framework through the research analysis of teachers' and students' perspectives and the assessment of the existence of a Social Innovation (SI) culture and good practices within participating universities and validation of the competence framework.
The second phase focused on the development of educative assets, including the BUFSIE toolbox, which includes an introduction guide to the co-creation process and a handbook and activity repository and serious game, to enhance the implementation of the framework and the SI model. The toolbox was piloted by HEI teachers and students, allowing customization for different educational contexts. 
The third and final phase focused on training HEI teachers through a blended learning approach and testing training materials, followed by the development of a MOOC. This was followed by the piloting, evaluation, and refinement of BUFSIE at the same time, where the Social Innovation Education model, activities, and serious game were tested and refined by educators.

<< Results >>

The main results of BUFSIE are:
BUFSIE framework for embedding Social Innovation Education (SIE) in Higher Education Institutions (HEI) (O1) which combines two most important features of the changemaker of tomorrow, namely entrepreneurial, sustainable, and socially proactive mindset.  
BUFSIE replication toolbox (O2) entailing educational resources and activities to infuse the philosophy of the SIE model, stimulate the development of relevant competences and involve in the co-creation process, establishing a co-creation ecosystem among HEIs local businesses and community members.
BUFSIE Training Program (O3) which stimulates the entrepreneurial and civic orientation of HEI teachers and equips them with the necessary knowledge, skills, and resources to effectively embed the development of entrepreneurial attitudes and civic competences in their learning contexts. Through this programme, provided also as a MOOC, HEI teachers embrace SIE as a methodology and pedagogy that can be used in any discipline.
BUFSIE serious game (O4) for assisting HEIs educators to easily introduce SIE to their students and engage them in co-creation and change-making skills development by using an alternative game-based tool.

2020-1-DE01-KA203-005715.title: Modernising European Legal Education
2020-1-DE01-KA203-005715.summary:
<< Background >>

The main objective of the project is to adapt legal education to the demands of the global labour market. Changes in the legal labour market, including automation, require a re-evaluation of training and teaching methods to prepare graduates for the new challenges. The needs assessment has shown that there is an increasing need to qualify academic staff in new teaching methods and cross-cutting competences, such as teamwork skills, analysis, foreign languages, decision-making skills, etc. So far, universities offer only limited support in this area. In addition, it was found that students have less and less knowledge in the area of scientific work. The practical skills and cross-cutting competences of students are only developed to a limited extent by students in teaching. Therefore, the aim is to improve the quality and relevance of legal education in this context and to ensure that both academic staff and students are well prepared for the evolving demands of the legal profession and the labour market.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the project focused primarily on improving and modernising legal education in order to close the considerable gap between the skills required by future European lawyers and those currently taught in legal education at European academic institutions. Traditional teaching methods, while valuable for imparting legal knowledge, are not sufficient to prepare students for their role in today's dynamic legal profession. The project objectives were overarching and ultimately led to the creation of mechanisms for effective and efficient modernisation of legal education. The focus of the project was on the training of teachers. To this end, teaching methods were imparted that call for key competences and cross-cutting issues. The project aimed to raise awareness of new and innovative topics and their relevance to law studies. It aimed to bring cross-cutting issues such as gender aspects, the Green Deal and digitalisation into legal research and teaching.

<< Implementation >>

The activities carried out contributed to meeting the identified needs and achieving the project objectives. For this purpose, in addition to regular organisational meetings (incl. TPM), various teaching, learning and training activities were carried out. These have dealt in particular with the identification and discussion of new and innovative teaching methods. The comprehensive activity aimed at training teaching staff on innovative legal teaching. Here, participants were taught various methods and best practices were presented. Participants were able to take part in these methods in person. Another activity was the discussion of cross-cutting issues in legal research. In particular, issues of gender equality, climate change, digitalisation and innovative teaching were discussed here. The research projects discussed here were made available to the general public in an open-access publication. The public was also informed about the MELE project and the individual results through dissemination events.

<< Results >>

MELE created a forum and a network for the exchange and improvement of ideas, experiences and best practices for innovative teaching and research on transversal competences, innovative teaching methods and cross-cutting issues. MELE was based on a comprehensive study of higher legal education and the inclusion of the teaching of key competences in the curricula. The project emphasised the importance of a structured approach to the development of teaching staff's didactic skills and provided resources in the form of a methodology toolbox that will support the introduction of innovative teaching methods. MELE developed an online course on Academic Work to be used by undergraduate and postgraduate students to improve their research skills in European and international contexts. The project conducted extensive research on cross-cutting issues with an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary approach, resulting in an open access publication "Innovative Strategies to Address Urgent Cross-Cutting Challenges".
