2020-1-DE01-KA203-005728.title: Coherence in European Teacher Education: Creating transnational communities of practice through virtual scenarios
2020-1-DE01-KA203-005728.summary:
<< Background >>

At its core, the ConnEcTEd project aimed for coherence, profession-orientation, and internationalization through communities of practice in virtual scenarios. The internationalization of TE and the creation of a European Higher Education Area (EHEA) are increasingly important aspects of European TE (European Parliament, 2015; HRK, 2018). The goals of this internationalization lie primarily in the enhancement of TE through an increased perspective of one's professional development, comprehensive cooperations between Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), joint teaching-learning concepts (TLCs), degrees and research, the creation of coherent curricula, and an increase in both student teachers’ and educators’ mobility (European Commission (EC), 2013; EP, 2015) to strengthen professional development and competencies. As physical mobility cannot be realized by all students, universities should also include offers of “internationalization at home” (EC, 2013; van Gaalen & Gielesen, 2016). Physical mobility can thus be supplemented by offers of virtual mobility (ibid.), to give fair and equal access to internationalized TE structures and curricula for all students. Furthermore, internationalization can be achieved through the mobility of faculty members of TE institutions. Needs analyses conducted by the applicant organization (PHFR) in 2018 and 2019 had already pointed to the needs of both student teachers and educators for a stronger orientation towards both internationalization and digitalization in onsite TE.
As the diversity of the various national TE systems and especially between subject cultures (e. g. in Foreign Language Teacher Education, FLTE) are very wide and steps towards internationalization existed mostly only on a small scale and were oftentimes locally limited, efforts towards adding to the EHEA require a lot of personal, conceptual, and structural work as well as knowledge of and transparency between TE systems. 
The ConnEcTEd consortium consists of universities which all have gained expertise in aspects of structural and/or conceptual coherence in TE in the past, and in part already successfully collaborated in TE before the project (for example, integrated French-German TE study programs). Together, they started working on issues of transnational coherence collaboratively to meet the challenges that the diverse TE systems pose on the internationalization of the European TE.
Systematic conceptual analyses based on the notion of coherence in TE initiated the collaboration. A shared conceptual basis was accompanied by a categorization and collection of already existing good examples of coherent TLCs. These samples helped a lot if getting a first understanding of what is meant by coherence in the very different TE systems.
Also, an empirical (quantitative and qualitative) research study on TE actors’, especially student teachers’, perceptions of coherence took place. Moreover, coherent teaching-learning concepts, virtual lecture series, podcasts, among others, were developed and evaluated in transnational project teams. Results of this work can be used as “good practice” for transnational coherence, were disseminated among all participants and beyond the project (in the context of Open Educational Resources, OER) and will be published in scientific journals and volumes. 
This joint conceptualization and development, implementation, and evaluation of coherent TLCs in ConnEcTEd especially helped to gain deeper insights into current paradigms, contexts, and practices of coherence in European TE systems and university sites and broadened the perspective taken on coherence so far. This work is an important, not to say indispensable, component for creating synergies in European TE, and represents an important step towards a strengthened TE within the EHEA.

<< Objectives >>

In the project, we aimed to achieve an internationalization of TE using the conceptual framework of coherence and by means of developing and using virtual scenarios. Both structural and contextual coherence can be created between the central knowledge domains (content knowledge, pedagogical knowledge, pedagogical content knowledge), subjects, phases (university TE, teacher induction, professional development) and between TE actors, and help in reducing a) discontinuities during one’s professionalization and b) the perception of fragmentation and isolated knowledge and skill acquisition. 
The project thus aimed at dealing with challenges to coherence in European TE in a collaborative way, especially to strengthen the transnational cooperations between institutions of TE. This was to be achieved by introducing related and ‘possible-to-be-internationalized’ samples of national curricula, the use of innovative practices in the digital era, and a mutual recognition of qualifications and learning outcomes between these institutions. Considering the rather weak coherence between educational structures and concepts within national TE systems, transnational coherence appeared – and proved – to be especially weak. The large diversity of European TE systems represents a central barrier for the physical and virtual mobility of student teachers and educators. 
A transnational approach to the issue of coherence in TE seemed promising in two ways: A systematic comparison of TE structures (IO1) and concepts (IO3) in the participating institutions was to provide deeper insights into current paradigms of coherence orientation in European TE. Building on this, the joint development and evaluation of teaching concepts and learning opportunities as good practice (e.g., within IO 5 and 6, in IO 7) should have various benefits:  to help the concept initiators to understand, beyond the general contribution of collegial practice, consultation and exchange, whether their teaching concepts have unrecognized curricular prerequisites, that might prohibit a transnational approach towards European TE. An open dissemination of coherence-oriented teaching concepts (see output in showcase/IO 3 and in the IO5 and 6 sections on the project website), in turn, should contribute to establishing a higher degree of transparency and comparability, as well as creating communities of practice in teacher education (TE) (IO8).
The original goal of introducing virtual mobility through this project, was of course influenced by the reality of TE during the COVID-19 pandemic. When we drafted the application in 2019, virtual mobility was only offered by a few institutions of TE, and mostly in FLTE. Suddenly we found ourselves in a situation where virtual mobility was the only way to cooperate, and even the planned Project Meetings of ConnEcTEd had to be carried out in a virtual way for the first 17 months of the project. This has had a strong influence on the project, e.  g., on IO 8, where we had aimed to experience with firsts steps of virtual mobility. But also, all other IO work and cooperation were very much influenced and challenged by the situation starting in 2020. This situation even led to the departure of one of our project partners.
ConnEcTEd managed to established transnational professional learning communities and provided a systematic analysis of five European TE systems to prepare the grounds for deeper international cooperation. Furthermore, the project permitted access to professional training opportunities that are made available to all project partners as well as all TE actors outside the project as materials, recordings, webinars, and many more for later use (e. g., video-tutorials, virtual scenarios, virtual lectures). These activities contributed to the development and use of innovative practices in the digital era as well as to the strengthening of coherence and “internationalization at home.” 
Above all, the possibility of new international cooperation and continuous exchange on the TE educator level, which could not have been achieved without financial and structural support of the European Union, is a main result of the project that should not be underestimated. This cooperation is a central prerequisite for all further efforts towards transnational coherence and was further captured in IO8. The goal here was to realize a digital conceptual toolkit. This required a comprehensive process, involving careful planning, content development, technological infrastructure, testing, and dissemination. By doing so, it empoweres TE institutions across Europe with the resources and tools they need to enhance coherence in internationalization and transnational collaboration, as was done in ConnEcTEd.

<< Implementation >>

Continuous IO work:The activities covering all contextual IO-work (e. g. IO-leader meetings, meetings with the consortium when necessary, working on the IOs in one’s national teams, discussing Io work locally and adapting one’s work) were continuously pursued. All contextual work was followed and supports by activities like the GA- and SB-meetings (in which the IO work was always in the focus), additional (online) meetings (e. g. when challenges as the withdrawal of the Cyprus team appeared; short reconciliations with other partners) and a constant communication via e-mail, Zoom, MS teams (our project management platform) or phone calls. This work finally culminated in the creation of various OER products (e. g. webinars, categorization/analysis frameworks), scientific publications, conference attendances and – difficult to call “product” or “activity” – a strengthened awareness towards working collaboratively on complex educational topic as well as and many useful learning and working experiences regarding transnational collaboration.
During the project, we were able to carry out only one of the originally two planned staff trainings, because we had to shift the original time plan due to the pandemic. 


Learning Teaching Trainings: The workshop was planned by the University of Oslo and the ALU Freiburg to jointly work on the key concepts of the IOs 5 and 6, i. e. "Co-Creating in Foreign Language Teacher Education" and to collaboratively develop them further with members from respective other local teams. The training focused on the collaborative development and discussion of the OERs planned in IO 5 (core practice in foreign language education) and IO 6 (OERs teaching ICC) and was accompanied by webinars before and after. In addition, it included a visit to the partner school network of the University of Oslo and a discussion with relevant stakeholders. A draft agenda of the learning and teaching activity was prepared by the University of Oslo before the kick-off meeting in Freiburg. There, it was discussed in the General Assembly and complemented/adjusted according to the feedback of all partners involved. Each institution was allowed to send a total of three lecturers and researchers from the field of FLTE that worked together in transnational teams to further develop profession- and coherence-oriented concepts — be it in a horizontal sense (concepts, methods, and learning materials that establish links between literature, linguistics, cultural studies, and language practice [CK], foreign language didactics [PCK] and educational sciences [PK]), or concerning vertical coherence between the different phases of teacher education. During the meeting, key results and findings were recorded and uploaded on the project's web portal and the basis was set for the development of joint OERs. The staff training held in Oslo in March 2022 had a focus on Open Educational Resources. This training was also the first physical meeting of the project partners, and it took place 17 months after the project started. This meeting was a turning point in the project, because the mere virtual cooperation until that point was wearing all partners down, and motivation was very low at this point. The face-to-face work in small groups, the external input from Dr. Robert Schuwer, independent consultant and researcher on Open Educational Resources, on OERs (which has also been published as OER on the ConnEcTEd project website) and the subsequent discussions as well as the impulses from the visit to Kuben secondary school and Kuben vocational school in Oslo gave a clear idea of possible and useful end products for IO 5/6. Especially the open working culture in Kuben, based on collegial sharing of teaching concepts, made it possible to learn about reusing and developing teaching materials and the importance of a corresponding institutional policy directly from real practice.


Multiplier Events: In the course of the project, various Multiplier Events were held, targeted a wide and diverse audience, and thus pursued specific and different goals.

Multiplier Event - Helsinki, May 3rd 2022
Helsinki & Turku in May 2022. This multiplier event was organized as a webinar and hosted about 30 participants who were language teacher educators, language teachers and language teacher students. The webinar had four introductions to topics related to digitalization in foreign language education. The participants were activated in breakout rooms to discuss the use and usefulness of the ideas and topics introduced (robots in language education, online teaching, teachers’ digital skills, shared entrance exams to TE in Finland).

Multiplier Event - Turku, October 4th 2022
The EDUTU forum organized by the Faculty of Education of the University of Turku was opening a new kind of cooperation forum between the faculty and the management of the education authorities of Southwest Finland and Satakunta, the headmasters of primary and secondary schools and the directors of day-care centers. The idea is to meet each other and create guidelines for the development of education, to bring together aspects of research and teaching for creating opportunities for developing cooperation with the faculty of education. In this forum, organized for the first time, Professor Mikkilä-Erdmann presented in this event the conceptual background of the coherence research operationalized in the Connected project and empirical findings with the target to inspire the development of educational institutions from day care centers to upper secondary schools in Finland.

Multiplier Event - Nice, May 2nd 2023
This Multiplier Event has taken place at Nice (France) in Université Côte d’Azur. In this case, the relevant actors reached were mainly High School teachers, High School students (specially from Lycée Calmette at Nice) and parents.  The Multiplier Event had as main purpose to present the experience of the CONNECTED project closer through a practical exercise. 
A theatre reading by students has served as a basis for presenting the objectives and main results of the CONNECTED project. Students, accompanied by their teachers have depicted the life of Eva Freud through the reading of her correspondence. After this reading students have been interviewed about the impact of the collaborative project on felt coherence of the teacher education program. Finally, the objectives and results of the CONNECTED project have been presented to the participants on the basis of the practical exercise carried out.

Multiplier Event - Zagreb, June 16th 2023
The multiplier event was organized by the Connected project team from the Faculty of Teacher Education, University of Zagreb with the support of the Department for subject didactics that annually organizes a gathering of teacher educators and mentor teachers with the aim to exchange experiences and new findings in teacher education. Participants of the event were teacher educators, stakeholders of education policy and mentor teachers working in primary schools and kindergartens. In line with project plan and project outcomes, and especially regarding IO1, IO2 and IO4, the emphasis at the multiplier event was set on improvement of teacher education with regards of bridging the gap between theory and practice, and to foster school/kindergarten-university cooperation to enhance coherence in teacher education. The first two speakers, Vinko Filipović, Director of the National Centre for External Evaluation of Education and Maja Zrnčić from Croatian Ministry of culture and media set in their presentations the emphasis on the role of teachers in the education system and the importance of the quality of initial teacher education. They presented new developments in educational system at the national level (introduction of national exams at the end of the primary education, and the national project for literacy development from very early age. Implementation of both presented projects require competent and motivated teachers, and both speakers emphasized the importance to prepare teachers for such projects during their initial education. Vlatka Domović (member of the ConnEcTed team) introduced the project to the participants of the multiplier event. She informed the participants about the project aims, developed IOs and website in which all project results can be accessed. She presented the results obtained by the research conducted within IO4 and stressed that students from the Faculty of Teacher Education don't perceive theory at the faculty and the practice at schools during their initial education to be coherent. In the follow up of the Prof. Domović’s lecture the possibilities for strengthening coherence in the University of Zagreb teacher education program were discussed. Following topics were brought up in the discussion: possibilities of digital transformation in teacher education, internationalization of teacher education and vertical coherence in study program. Vladimir Legac from the Department of English Language Teacher Education at the Faculty of Teacher Education in Zagreb presented in the sense of digitalization, advantages, and disadvantages of Chat-GPT in teacher education. 
In the second part of the Multiplier event, mentor teachers held workshops in which they presented examples of good practice. All presented examples of organized students school practice demonstrated the possibilities of student school practice to draw student’s attention to the relation of the content of the study program with teacher's everyday teaching practice.

Multiplier Event - Freiburg, July 25th 2023
The two-hour multiplier event served a dual purpose: (1) to present selected concepts for coherent teaching in teacher education and for theory-practice connections that were developed within the framework of the ConnEcTeD project, and (2) to describe the research questions, the working approach, the structure, and the various outputs of the ConnEcTeD project, as well as to draw participants' attention to the project's website. A introductory presentation of approximately 30 minutes by Frank Reiser was dedicated to achieving this second objective. For the first objective, three IO5/6 projects (1 x Team Nice, 2 x Team Freiburg/ALU+PH) belonging to the thematic field of cultures of memory were chosen. This area was selected due to its relevance for fostering a deeper understanding of the cultural and symbolic practices of respective language communities, promoting intercultural competence among students, enhancing their critical reflective abilities, and not least, contributing to the overarching goal of democracy education, making it an integral part of educational curricula across various European countries. Therefore, the theme of "Cultures of Memory" represents an important directive for teacher education at universities, where literary, cultural, and didactic insights can be integrated. It is equally pertinent for secondary schools as well as higher education institutions involved in teacher training. The target audience for the event primarily comprised educators in foreign language disciplines at all levels, in the sense of practice networking, however, with a focus on teachers at secondary schools and especially mentors working in the hands-on practical training phase in German teacher education who can act as multipliers. — The following three projects were presented, each of which will also be published as Open Educational Resources (OERs) as part of IO5/6 on the ConnEcTEd project homepage: (1) The collaborative project designed and conducted by Christine Schmider (University of Nice) and Isabelle Sieurin (Lycée Calmette, Nice) involving teacher education students and secondary school students, focused on contemporary history within a local context; (2) the integrated master’s seminar on French autobiography conceived by Melanie Koch-Fröhlich (ALU) and Jakob Willis (PH Freiburg); and (3) the integrated master’s seminar on cultures of memory in Spanish teacher education by Katja Zaki (PH Freiburg) and Frank Reiser (ALU).

Multiplier Event - Oslo, September 22nd 2023
The Norwegian multiplier event was organised by the Oslo team in cooperation with the Norwegian Centre for English and other Foreign Languages in Education at the Østfold University College campus in Halden. Colleagues teaching literature at the college were invited to take part in a mini seminar taking place September 22. The seminar, that was included in a seven-day language festival celebrating the European Day of Languages, was led by Gerard Doetjes, ass. prof. of foreign language didactics (UiO)/head og the Foreign Language Centre and Christian Janss, prof. of German literature (UiO). The seminar started with a short introduction of the ConnEcTEd project, the partners and the IOs. Then, Doetjes and Janss talked about their cooperation within the project. Doetjes shadowed Janss' literature course during a semester and they used his observations as a starting point for discussions about Janss' teaching and the possibility to connect his literature course with Doetjes' didactics course and students' school practice. Colleagues were then invited to share their experiences and to take part in a discussion about teaching literature as a part of language studies, in teacher education and in school.
This Multiplier Event took place on Sept 22nd, 2023, and is outside the project range. The Multiplier Event leader, Gerke Doetjes, stressed that he doesn't want to get any refund for this event. However, we as project team would like to have it mentioned in the Mobility Tool and Final Report for dissemination purposes. Therefore, we artificially dated the Multiplier Event to Aug 31st, 2023, in the Mobility Tool, but correctly dated it in the Final Report.


Dissemination Activities: ConnEcTEd results are disseminated through the project website (see https://www.face-freiburg.de/connected/), a joint scientific publication, conference participation and other local and regional multiplier events. 

Joint publication: Scientific results from the project will be published in a joint publication at Springer in 2023 (autumn): Coherence in European teacher education – theoretical models, empirical studies, instructional approaches. The anthology is edited by four project members (Doetjes, Domovic, Mikkilä-Erdmann & Zaki) and will contain 12 peer-reviewed chapters, introductory remarks and a discussion. By inviting experienced scholars to contribute to the book – two chapters as well as the discussion are written by non-ConnEcTEd members (Heikilä & Hermansen; Toom & Husu; Canrinus)–, we add relevant perspectives and disseminate the project in the field of (foreign language) teacher education. In addition to this joint scientific publication, a systematic review concerning coherence in teacher education is prepared (Mikkilä-Erdmann, Nummi, Erdmann & Laukkanen). 

Conference participation: Project members disseminated results from work carried out in and across ConnEcTEd work packages at 13 scientific conferences in Croatia, Finland, Germany, Greece, Israel, Northern Ireland and Sweden during the course of the project (e. g. conference for education “Kasvatustieteenpäivät” in Oulu 25.11.2022; conferences “EDUFALL” on the 3.11.2022 and “EDUSPRING” on the 7.4.2022 in Turku. Also: TEPE conference Karlstad (May 2023), EARLI conference Thessaloniki (August 2023), DGFF conference Freiburg (September 2023)). Project members’ work in the coming years will be built further upon ConnEcTEd results, and as a consequence of this, dissemination of the project at conferences will continue. 

Multiplier events: In line with the project application, multiplier events were carried out in each country towards the end of the project. The main goal of these events was to reach out to teacher education colleagues from our own and from other universities in order to present our cross-European project and discuss the results, and thus contribute to the further development of teacher education in our countries. Some events were carried out physically at our home universities, some events took place digitally (partly because of Covid restrictions, partly to be able to meet colleagues from other parts of our countries) and some events were hosted by colleagues at other universities. In addition to these multiplier events, project members also took part in several local and regional events where they could disseminate the project, e. g. in schools, research groups and school authorities (see also, section above). Additionally, two summer seminars were held in June 2023 in Turku and one presentation was given in Jyväskylä on the professional development day for Teachers in August 2022. In Freiburg, project results were disseminated via a colloquium of the Department of Education.

<< Results >>

IO work and related outputs
Within the project, all activities mentioned in the application (IO 1 to IO 8) were carried out and almost all products could be developed as planned. 
IO1: So, the partner institutions created an international report on coherence in teacher education for all participating countries. At the beginning of the project, we collected examples of good practice of coherence and published them in a digital showcase on our project website (IO3). For this purpose, a supporting document for the description of examples of good practice was created to provide detailed information on every example in the digital showcase. The website of the project was modified accordingly and the digital showcase of examples of good practice on coherence has been integrated on the website. We jointly published an edited volume on “Coherence in European Teacher Education. - Theoretical Models, Empirical Studies, instructional Approaches” (IO2). Furthermore, we operationalized the conceptual basis due to current research on coherence and created a questionnaire measuring coherence in teacher education. This questionnaire was made available for the participating partner countries. We piloted the questionnaire, collected data, and conducted preliminary analysis (IO4).  Several Open Educational Resources providing contextualized in-depth descriptions of coherence-oriented course concepts in foreign language teacher education were published on the project website; these OERs were initially based on local project ideas, subsequently co-developed in transnational working groups within the project consortium and finally revised by the IO leaders (IO5/6). As a form of ‘coherence creation within the project’, cross-links between the OERs were identified and highlighted. On a meta-level, the cooperative work produced fundamental information about Open Educational Resources and the implementation and challenges of transnational co-creative projects, which have been incorporated into the output of IO 7 and IO 8 and published on the project website. IO7 was about Transnational Virtual Lecture Series: Highlighting comparison and coherence between TE programs. In this IO, we produced introductory videos with an overview of the school system and foreign language teacher education in each partner country or state, recorded webinars of the digital transformation in Foreign Language (Teacher) Education in the partner countries, and podcasts of selected transversal themes and competences in European (Teacher) Education.IO 8 brings coherence- and profession-oriented course materials together, while combining them with internationalized learning environments and collaborative/co-creative methods. A co-creative approach was used to develop a toolkit within IO8, whereby project partners pooled their knowledge and expertise to collaboratively design and create educational resources, curriculum, and instructional materials.

Closer cooperation as “Other outcome”: For almost half of the project time, we couldn’t travel due to Covid 19. The physical meetings that followed March 2022 were thus especially precious to us. One result that is difficult to measure is the strength of relationships that grew between the partner institutions. While some of the consortium members have been long established partners, the links to others were rather weak or non-existent prior to this cooperation.
·	One partnership that has grown particularly is the one between PH Freiburg and the University of Zagreb. Since the start of the project, several colleagues from both universities have been visiting since fall 2021: the Dean and vice-dean of the University of Zagreb have been to Freiburg, and also the head of the international office and the dean’s manager. A faculty member of PH Freiburg’s German Department has visited the German Department at University of Zagreb. All these visits have been carried out through KA 131 STT or STA mobilities. The two institutions will introduce a cooperation for students within a blended format.
·	A member of the Educational Department of PH Freiburg has been to the Université de Côte d’Azur in Nice for several occasions. At the beginning of the project, the cooperation between PH Freiburg and Nice was rather a cooperation between Freiburg’s French and Nice’s German Department. The project thus helped to add another level to the cooperation.
·	The cooperation between the sub-project leaders (affiliated to the University of Oslo, ALU Freiburg and PH Freiburg) of IO5 and IO6, which were organizationally joined very early during the project, as numerous transversal topics (such as co-teaching as an aspect potentially fostering coherence) were recognized as equally relevant for both IOs, was quite steady and intensive. Both the joint organization of the LTTA in Oslo in March 2022 and the supervision and finalization of the OERs were carried out together. After the end of the project, these three participants gave joint presentation at the conference of the German Society for Foreign Language Research (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Fremdsprachenforschung, DGFF) in September 2023. Further joint activities are planned.
·	National/International outreach to other EU-Projects (IPN Kiel) took place. 
·	After presenting the project findings on conferences, new cooperations with partners from other universities were initiated.

2020-1-EE01-KA203-077942.title: Upgrading and Harmonization of Maritime Engineering Master’s Level Courses
2020-1-EE01-KA203-077942.summary:
<< Background >>

The SHIPMARTECH project was carried out by a partnership of 4 universities: Tallinn University of Technology), University of Zagreb, University of Naples Federico II and University of the Aegean. The project aimed at improving and harmonizing MSc courses in Marine Engineering/Naval Architecture across different universities. Initially, the quality of courses varied between universities and they used different levels of electronic support. The project upgraded and harmonized selected courses by bringing them to a similar level of electronic support and structure, making also the quality and content of the courses more consistent between universities. The main motivation behind the project was the need to educate new engineers for the European shipbuilding industry. The industry is dynamic and competitive, with a high-tech future and a positive perspective. But to remain competitive, it needs new talented engineers to rejuvenate the industry and take competencies to a higher level. The SHIPMARTECH project aimed to address this need through cooperation of four universities, developing a set/repository of MSc-level online courses in English to facilitate student mobility and address current and emerging knowledge requirements.

<< Objectives >>

The objective of the SHIPMARTECH project was upgrading and harmonization of Master’s-level courses in Marine Engineering/ Naval Architecture, facilitation of e-learning and internationalisation through cooperation of four universities. To fulfil this objective, a set of online-hosted upgraded courses in English (intellectual output) for Marine Engineering/Naval Architecture 2nd cycle students was developed.

<< Implementation >>

The SHIPMARTECH project created and developed one intellectual output: a set of online-hosted upgraded courses in English for Marine Engineering/Naval Architecture master’s students.
The intellectual output was tested at an Intensive Study Programme (LTT) in Tallinn with an International group of students and teachers. 
Four face-to-face and one virtual LTT staff-training events were organised to advance professional skills of the teachers by providing training in modern engineering pedagogy, online/interactive teaching methods and tools, teaching in multicultural classroom, assessment, etc. 
The results of the project were disseminated through two multiplier events taking place in Piraeus, Greece and at Viinistu, Estonia.
The partnership held five transnational project meetings, three of which were conducted physically and two virtually.

<< Results >>

The SHIPMARTECH project produced one intellectual output: a set of online-hosted upgraded courses in English for Marine Engineering/Naval Architecture master’s students, including: 1) Course upgrading and harmonization needs report of the analysis carried out at the initial stage of the project; 2) 24 upgraded and Marine Engineering/Naval Architecture 2nd-cycle courses in English with harmonized e-support on e-learning platforms of the project partners; 3) Teacher’s guide harmonization and upgrading of Marine Engineering courses; 4) A demo of the courses with sample materials on a physical carrier.

2020-1-EE01-KA203-077990.title: Highly Interactive Guidance Helpful For Leadership In Educationally Relevant Skills
2020-1-EE01-KA203-077990.summary:
<< Background >>

Subjects that relate to science, or STEM, education at school are often seen as irrelevant in the eyes of students. Yet evidence suggests that students take an interest in worldwide science and technology innovations. Consequently, there is a gap between students’ wishes and the manner in which science (STEM) subjects are being taught. This project seeks to address this gap.

The High Fliers project perceives an urgent need to promote a new vision for a STEM teacher career pathway. This is seen, on the one hand, as an attractive and novel approach, contributing towards facilitating life-long learning, while, on the other hand, recognising the need to motivate students to become a STEM teacher. While, there is a lack of science teachers in all associated STEM disciplines, this is even more notable in the school subjects of chemistry and physics within all partner countries (Estonia, Finland, Portugal, Croatia).

<< Objectives >>

1. To design an optional, 4 modular training Programme, attractive for undergraduate and Masters students undertaking studies in STEM faculties. 
2. To pilot High-Fliers Modules to determine the intended impact and how Modules can be strengthened in the future. 
3. Through evidence-based outputs, determine the programme’s impacts on increasing science-related career awareness as components of STEM-related education programmes in:  
(a) introducing novel STEM teacher career pathways, 
(b) enhancing and promoting creativity and innovation skills, and 
(c) stressing the need to raise the importance of communication and other educational elements.

<< Implementation >>

1. Content experts High-Fliers key personnel, responsible for creating of Modules in English and in local languages, guidance materials and an online operational manual, piloting materials in all participating countries, collecting feedback and evaluation.
2. Technical experts supporting adaptation and creation of Modules and 3-minute videos for a Moodle environment, the translation into 4 languages, setting up of online evaluation questionnaires and virtual meetings between partners. 
3. External field experts: an International Advisory team from stakeholder`s organisations in partner countries; 4 members in total, nominated in collaboration with the respective country partner and an International Evaluation Team from each country (12-15 members).  
4. Volunteers, circa 200, who piloted the Modules from the 4 countries, comprising: undergraduate students, teachers, non-formal STEM professionals, university staff, secondary students.  
5. General interest audience targeting project dissemination activities, including 3-minute Module videos, websites social media portals, High-Fliers Multiplier Events, press releases, and presenting High-Fliers programme in science education conferences, locally and at an international level.

<< Results >>

The partnership proposes to increase the STEM teacher professional development through the development of:
1)	4-Modules determined to be: intelligent and resourceful, attractive and enthusiastic, artistic in ways of presenting, good communicator, collaborative, creative and innovative, courageous at heart, curious, aware of personal self-efficacy and self-management skills & ready for receiving coaching, connected to the world and to the needs of others, conceptualising the science, a good organiser.
2)	Support Action (i.e. Coaching)
3)	STEM career education development Programme, offered via Moodle (in English + guidance material in 4 partner country languages) targeting 3 different groups:
•	students (as pre-career support),
•	practicing teachers (as professional development) and non-formal STEM professionals,
•	university science or science-related staff.
4)	An accompanying Online Manual is also proposed (in English + 4 partner country languages).

2020-1-EL01-KA203-079109.title: Smart faRming innOvatiOn Training
2020-1-EL01-KA203-079109.summary:
<< Background >>

Integrated Mixed Farming Systems (MFS), constitute a promising solution to confront the on going food crisis, that can enhance nutrient cycling and increase natural resource usage efficiency. In integrated Mixed Farming environments, ICT, through data collection and analysis, plays a crucial role in farm management decision- making. Nevertheless, current education programs in European Higher Education Institutes (HEIs) do not provide the necessary skills and training tools for students and experts on MFS. In addition, it is essential to promote the engagement of end-users in the shift from conventional farming to MFS supported by ICT,  to ensure the sustainability of MFS. This transition requires highly skilled personnel, multidisciplinary communities of practice, system change methodologies, behavioral decision-making and participatory procedures. The SmartROOT project has addressed the previously mentioned needs and has managed to (a) join together multidisciplinary scientific groups (agronomists, veterinarians, ICT specialists and entrepreneurial networks) and acquire know-how (b) deliver  innovative education tools  (c) design a Joint Master Degree program on MFS and ICT ready to use right after the project’s completion.

<< Objectives >>

Taking into consideration the fact that  the agriculture and farming sectors are among the least digitized in Europe with very low ICT adoption by Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), SmartRoot project focused on five objectives targeting to raise the awareness of related stakeholders (farmers, breeders, entrepreneurs in the food industry, specialists in ICT and students) in MFS techologies. These are:
a.	The development of state-of-the-art technologies and practices in MFS educational approaches. 
b.	The design and development of a Joint Master Degree program that offers academic and technical multidisciplinary knowledge in MFS taking into consideration the challenges that the agriculture domain faces. 
c.	The establishment of an innovative ecosystem between HEIs, SMEs and experts fostering cooperation in a key sector of the European society and economy.
d.	The direct involvement of end users to the preparation and evaluation of the Joint Master Degree program
e.	The creation of a participatory environment for farming stakeholders, SMEs in the ICT domain and experts in related fields, by promoting collaboration with academics and fostering the adoption and utilization of project outputs in their everyday activities.

<< Implementation >>

In order to achieve the objectives mentioned previously SmartRoot project developed tools and Open Access Platforms to promote and acquire knowledge, know- how and best practices from practitioners, academics and organizations related to MFS and ICT sectors in order to support continuous training on MFS. The tools and platforms developed were designed for the socio-professional network and promoted through the multiplier events. Additionally the consortium has trained students and practitioners, through the 3 learning events, to technological solutions for climate smart agriculture  such as robots, UAVs, advanced tracking systems, long-range IoT-enabled sensors. A very important activity implemented was the design and evaluation of an innovative Joint Master’s Degree program on “Information and Communication Technology in Mixed Farming Systems” in order to run in HEIs that are Agronomy /ICT oriented. Finally among the activities implemented in the context of the project is the establishment of a European network between academia, experienced farmers and stakeholders, to engage end-users and allow exchange of knowledge on best practices on various combinations of mixed farming systems.

<< Results >>

SmartROOT produced the following key outputs and results: 
O1: E-book on Mixed Farming Systems (MFS) that highlights a number of best practices in MFS and presents an analytical overview of the technical and soft skills to ensure efficient and sustainable agriculture.
O2: Open Hub for Knowledge Exchange that implements functionalities such as a wiki, a chat, a search tool and a forum for supporting the collaboration between ICT specialists, agronomists, veterinarians.
O3: SmartROOT Virtual Farm Hub, that consists of five interactive tools, an e-class education platform, a farm management tool, a data visualization tool, a geospatial catalogue and an educational game.
O4: Educational Management Platform for MFS, that aims to ease this collaboration process between multiple layers of production, from crop production to food processing. 
O5:  Augmented Reality Learning Environment that uses the ArtTutor to augment with multimedia fields the training and educational material produced by O1. 
O6: SmartROOT Assessment Toolkit and Curriculum Preparation that describes the structure of the Joint Master Degree program in ICT on MFS  and offers an assessment toolkit that includes questionnaires for evaluating the tools and the program.

2020-1-EL01-KA203-079121.title: Innovative education for sustainable development in peripheral rural areas
2020-1-EL01-KA203-079121.summary:
<< Background >>

The EU agricultural sector is facing important challenges. The “Farm to Fork” strategy intends to enable the EU to contribute to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDG). Peripheral rural areas have much to contribute to the achievement of several SDGs. However, such areas suffer from a combination of social, economic, political and environmental pressures. Depopulation, for example, drains them of human capital and forces entrepreneurs to acquire a multitude of different and often novel skills and competences. Producers are often faced with a complex dilemma on how to modernise production while avoiding potential wider social and environmental damage inflicted by the process. Peripheral rural regions by their nature face isolation and often fall under the radar of mainstream education and development. 
 
The partnership therefore aimed to support higher education in peripheral rural areas to enable graduates to improve their (self)employability and capacities to contribute to the wider socio-economic viability and sustainable development. Some of the partners took part in a Horizon2020 networking project HNV-Link, in which such needs were identified as poorly addressed.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to build an improved understanding of the specific skills and competencies required by the labour market to meet the societal needs of peripheral rural areas. Once we had explored the knowledge gaps, we aimed to develop a bespoke E-learning course targeted at improving key skills and competencies in relation to innovation and sustainable development in peripheral rural areas. Through these activities, we wanted to strengthen collaborations between HE and potential regional and cross-regional employers. We aimed to support professional competencies of the HE educators by sharing knowledge between educators in the partner higher education institutes and their education network. We wanted to make a range of the resources available online to contribute to the international pool of open educational resources (OER). Developing and testing the online course, the online virtual learning environment and the summer school with students enabled us to produce an innovative education product merging online learning and place-based education. We wanted this product to be used to equip graduates with skills and competencies relevant to specific labour markets and meet societal needs in peripheral rural areas

<< Implementation >>

RUR’UP project was implemented in full compliance with the Grant Agreement. It developed and implemented a flexible and modular blended course, offering students of partner institutions forward-looking skills appropriate to support sustainable development of peripheral rural areas.
Through focus group consultations and online surveys, partners identified needs and gaps in skills and competences. An online review of HE curricula revealed gaps in addressing the specific issues of HNV areas. (IO1)
Co-elaborating transdisciplinary, OER, and innovative curricula and teaching-training methods was the core of the project. Resulting materials included in the e-learning course (IO2) and the Bank of case studies (IO3)
Digital Platform was created and online training sessions for students were organised (IO4)
Workshops and transnational meetings were organized (Peer-to-peer and collaborative learning process). RUR’UP main face-to-face activity, Summer School, was organised (IO5). The whole process was monitored and assessed through participants and partner debriefing sessions (IO6)
Dissemination activities implemented, Events were organized to share and exchange at regional, national, and international level main project outcomes and impacts

<< Results >>

The project produced a mix of innovative IOs consisting of classical on-site learning tools and blended learning approaches making use of the ICT and resources (detailed in the Outputs section). For future successful strategies of the tertiary EU education system the RUR’UP project produced a state-of-the-art report (IO1). The E-learning course, the second important set of results (IO2), consisting of: a syllabus and educational materials (a set of 6 online lectures, and necessary additional resources). The virtual Bank of Case-Studies (64 materials) on innovative rural development cases in peripheral regions, including those of HNV farming represented the IO3. CPDlearnonline and EPALE ERASMUS+ Space used to create an online platform of digital resources, including the integration of digital badges (IO4). The necessary materials for an on-site Intensive Study Activity (IO5). The education experience summarised and reported in a reflection report that enabled the partnership to critically assess its achievements and process (IO6).
In addition, RUR’UP network was expanded through MEs, and meetings with other projects and networks, and presented the project results to the academia and professional meetings of rural stakeholders.

2020-1-ES01-KA203-082852.title: Integration of transversal skills into health and social care, higher education and the curriculum
2020-1-ES01-KA203-082852.summary:
<< Background >>

This project seeks to prepare health and social care students for the rapidly changing landscape of health and social practice by creating innovative teaching tools and practices. Transversal skills (TS) are crucial to lifelong learning and to promote active and involved European citizenship in civic and social life.
International and national agencies stated the need to shift the focus towards teaching-learning strategies that work on TS throughout the training journey. This is especially relevant in health and social care, where these skills are usually taken for granted. These competencies are also important in tackling gender inequities in health and social care..
The project's context stems from a notable gap in the European Higher Education Area – the inadequate implementation of teaching-learning strategies for transversal skills. Several factors contribute to this gap, including the absence of a comprehensive framework defining the progression of skill development, a lack of standardized teaching-learning methods to facilitate TS acquisition, lecturers' perceptions of limited resources and strategies for fostering TS, and challenges in assessing students' TS development.

<< Objectives >>

Objectives:
The main objective is to design, pilot, implement and evaluate teaching-learning strategies and resources for undergraduate and postgraduate training. The resources will address
learning outcomes related to critical and creative thinking, interpersonal/socio-emotional and citizen-oriented skills and learning to learn.
The two specific objectives are:
1. To promote the development of TS in health and social care students, using innovative strategies such as virtual reality.
2. To enable lecturers to teach, guide and accompany students’ development of TS.

<< Implementation >>

The project included the design (1st year), piloting and training (2nd year), and implementation and evaluation of educational resources (3rd year). The educational resources are the project’s intellectual outputs:
1. Methodological Guide with:
  1.1 Pedagogical framework in which transversal skills are defined and levels of skills development are established 
  1.2. Methodological guide with the most appropriate and innovative teaching-learning strategies to support the development of transversal skills, including an evaluative framework.
3. Toolkit with educational resources to work on TS.
4. Educational resources to improve TS using virtual reality tools.

The project included two intensive programmes for HE learners and two short-term joint staff training events. The activities aimed to train students and lecturers and, at the same time, pilot the educational resources created.

Multiplier events (one per participating country) helped to disseminate the results and project IOs to other HE institutions and were conceived as co-creation workshops which gathered feedback from relevant stakeholders.

<< Results >>

The concrete results produced by the project are :
1. Educational materials and resources to foster students’ development of TS (Methodological Guide and Toolkit), including 3 virtual reality resources and a specific guide about virtual reality.
2. Capacity building of lecturers to implement the educational resources designed in daily teaching.
3. Training and development of students’ TS.
4. Cross-sectoral coordination and participation of all stakeholders in the co-creation process.
5. Internationalization of the participating organizations.

The project impact and long-term benefits included: 
1) improvement in students’ transversal and internationalization skills, 
2) increased likelihood of sustainability in students’ future working life, 
3) greater self-efficiency and increased willingness to work on TS of lecturers, 
4) development of new educational products based on virtual reality, 
5) greater incorporation in the curriculum of teaching and evaluation activities related to TS, 
6) greater openness of HE institutions to society and local networks, 
7) higher level of internationalization and visibility of the participating organizations as well as stronger links between partners.

2020-1-ES01-KA203-083113.title: Inclusive Engagement of Non-Traditional Students in Professional Higher Education
2020-1-ES01-KA203-083113.summary:
<< Background >>

For the past 25 years, the European Higher Education Area  emphasised the importance of the social dimension of HE and its role in promoting equity, social inclusion, and active citizenship. Nevertheless, the Paris Communique (2018) stresses the need for more significant efforts to strengthen the social dimension of HE, underscoring the importance of HEIs to reflect the diversity of populations and calls for improved access and completion for underrepresented groups.While discussions on diversity and inclusion in HE often revolve around making curricula and classrooms more inclusive, they often overlook the broader student experience. Student engagement plays an important role in improving how HEIs are governed, influence the student experience, contribute to a sense of belonging and as a means towards the  acquisition of life skills.Many student engagement systems are tailored to 'traditional' students,- typically young, white, middle-class, full-time.Non-traditional students (NTS) encounter distinct challenges arising from their diverse backgrounds. Consequently, achieving genuinely inclusive student engagement encounters structural impediments, with many HEIs lacking a comprehensive grasp of NTS' requirements and circumstances.

<< Objectives >>

The overall objective of the project has been to enhance student engagement in Professional Higher Education (PHE), with a specific focus on inclusivity for non-traditional students. It sought to create tools and strategies to encourage their participation, improve their overall student experience and contribute to success in their studies and life. Specifically targeting PHE Institutions (PHEIs), InclusiPHE acknowledges their more diverse student body compared to traditional universities. PHEIs also feature unique curriculum characteristics, which are often overlooked in policy discussions. 
The project's goal has thus been to improve policies, mechanisms, and practices for inclusive student engagement of all students regardless of their background and circumstances, encompassing various aspects of the learning journey, quality assurance, institutional decision-making, and student life. More specifically, InclusiPHE aimed to develop resources designed to fill the gaps in knowledge and skills related to student engagement among PHEIs and students’ organisations, empowering them in their role to support the development of an inclusive student engagement culture within their institutions and organisations.

<< Implementation >>

The project activities were broadly divided into 3 phases:

Phase 1 aimed to map the challenges to student engagement faced by non-traditional students in PHE through research and focus group discussions with PHEI leaders, student support staff, student representatives and non-traditional students (NTS). The goal was to identify issues NTS face and areas where engagement processes in PHEIs require improvement. We also identified possible solutions, policy recommendations and provided a collection of existing inclusive student engagement practices.

Phase 2 focused on the creation of a Framework and online tool for self-assessment of inclusive engagement of NTS on the level of the PHEI and the level of students' organisations. Further Guidelines will help to turn the self-assessment into concrete action plans, advancing a commitment to inclusive engagement within PHEIs and students’ organisations

Phase 3 involved designing an online course for student support staff on inclusive student engagement in addition to the development of an online library with resources to support institutional leaders, student support staff and students’ organisations in improving diversity and inclusion of student engagement processes and activities.

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs of InclusiPHE include:
Mapping report on challenges and obstacles of student engagement of non-traditional students in PHE-See: https://inclusiphe.eu/mapping-report/
Collection of good and novel practices of inclusive student engagement across Europe-See: https://inclusiphe.eu/good-practises/
Policy recommendations for inclusive student engagement specifically aimed at local, national and European stakeholder in the PHE sector-See: https://inclusiphe.eu/policy-paper/
Frameworks & action plan guidelines for evaluating and improving inclusive student engagement in PHEIs and students’ organisations-See: https://inclusiphe.eu/sa-tool-guidelines-action-plan
Online self-assessment tools for PHEIs & students’ organisations based on the inclusive student engagement frameworks-see: https://inclusiphe.eu/assesst_fpage/
An online inclusive student engagement Resource Library-See: https://inclusiphe.eu/library/
A step-by-step inclusive student engagement guide for institutional leaders and students’ organisations-See: https://inclusiphe.eu/inclusiphe-guide/
Online self-paced training course for student support staff on inclusive student engagement-See: https://inclusiphe.academy.knowledgeinnovation.eu/courses/inclusiphe/

2020-1-FR01-KA203-079972.title: Beyond academia: broadening the career horizons of doctoral students in marine and maritime sciences in Europe
2020-1-FR01-KA203-079972.summary:
<< Background >>

The SEA-EU-DOC team was created as a result of the desire to work together with several actors in the doctoral sector in the six universities of the SEA-EU Alliance (European University SEA-EU). These include doctoral school directors, doctoral school administrative staff and university international relations staff. The people who initiated the project (University of Brest and University of Cadiz) knew each other from another Erasmus + ScolaMar project (Capacity building , 2016-2019).  The decision to focus the SEA-EU-DOC project on non-academic career opportunities for doctoral graduates was based on a number of observations and hypotheses, confirmed by a large-scale survey of more than 600 doctors working in the 6 partner countries in 2019 financed by a Brittany Regional Council programme to help set up European projects (Boost Europe):
- There was a lack of academic jobs in universities, research institutes, etc.
- More and more doctoral graduates have had to find jobs outside academia.
- Doctoral students are often not prepared for a wide range of career options.
- Non-academic employers are often not aware of the skills of doctorate holders.

<< Objectives >>

SEA-EU-DOC aims to increase the employability of doctorate holders in marine and maritime sciences outside academia.
The objectives were divided into three intellectual outputs:

IO1 : Profiling non-academic employment of marine and maritime sciences doctorate holders
To raise awareness about the variety of career paths in non-academic employment for doctorate holders
To present the added value of a doctorate in the job market and strengthen the recognition of a doctorate in the non-academic sector
To improve the exchange of experiences and good practices in order to adapt doctoral training programmes accordingly

IO2 : “The skill-matching challenge”
To contribute to align the doctoral students’ skills with employers’ expectations in the non-academic sector…
By identifying valuable skills acquired during the doctorate that can be transferred to any work context
By providing insights to increase the quality of doctoral training to better fit the diversity of employment opportunities of doctorate holders

IO3 : Blue doctoral community of tomorrow
To create a community of European marine sciences doctorate holders to facilitate collaboration and further career development

<< Implementation >>

Conducting 72 interviews: 60 written and 12 video interviews
Organization of 4 training events in Brest, Split and Cadiz
Organization of 11 focus groups bringing together PhD students, doctors and companies, public bodies, associations and entrepreneurs.
Organization of 4 transnational meetings and 6 follow-up meetings (visio)
Organization of 6 multiplier events
Organization of a Europe-wide dissemination event (EUA-CDE conference)
Organization of 7 additional dissemination meetings:
- 3 in Brest: 2 meetings with members of the Conseil Doctoral de Bretagne and 1 meeting with members of the Conseil de l'Institut Universitaire Européen de la Mer (IUEM)
- 2 in Cadiz: 1 meeting with the secretary of the doctoral school in marine sciences at the University of Cadiz (EIDEMAR) and 1 meeting with the director of the SEA-EU secretariat in charge of internationalization.
- 1 in Gdansk: presentation to the Forum of Polish Doctoral School Directors (42 directors present)
- 1 in Malta: with the Maltese Minister for Education, Sport, Youth, Research & Innovation
Participation in 4 SEA-EU Governing Board meetings

<< Results >>

A booklet of 60 written interviews and 12 video testimonials (IO1)
A report on surveys of employers and entrepreneurs on the skills of doctoral students (IO2)
A report on focus groups on matching skills to jobs in non-academic sectors (IO2)
A report on alumni networks: 6 national reports and 1 global report "report on alumni networks in European Universities to the Seas. SEA-EU Alliance" (IO3)
A report on the conclusions from the focus groups implementation within project task "building the Blue Doctoral Community of tomorrow (IO3)
A platform to host the alumni network (IO3)
A LinkedIn group to bring together the network of European doctoral students in marine and coastal sciences who have taken part in the training activities.
A website dedicated to the project to disseminate results
A dedicated session and three papers at the annual conference of the European University Association - Council for Doctoral Education network (https://www.eua.eu/events/243-2023-eua-cde-annual-meeting.html#tab2)
A research article submitted for publication in "Higher Education - The International Journal of Higher Education" (in progress) and 2 articles in preparation
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business
Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2020-1-FR01-KA203-080652.title: Students Civic Engagement European project
2020-1-FR01-KA203-080652.summary:
<< Background >>

La Rochelle Université offered to the partner universities of EU-Conexus (a consortium of European universities) to work together on the issue of valuing student civic engagement. The aim was to begin by collectively establishing a definition of student civic engagement, and then to discuss ways of supporting students commited to the process of enhancing the skills acquired through civic engagement: conferences, specific workshops, self-assessment. 

It seemed logical to us to ask the member universities of the EU-CONEXUS European University if they would be willing to support us in this process of reflection and co-construction of solutions for our students. The needs were first, to define what we meant by "student civic engagement", then to develop mechanisms to identify engaged students, raising awareness of the notion of engagement among all students and finally to support engaged students in their projects. All of this while collectively developing means to encourage the recognition and validation of skills acquired through engagement projects.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were:  

The organization of "debathons" co-constructed by the partners, in different partner countries, featuring engaged students selected as part of the project and trained in the exercise (public speaking, argumentation and counter-argumentation...). The themes of the debathons were topical/social issues either chosen by the students or imposed. Debathons were held in public, usually in a public space in the host city.  

The collective drafting of a "white paper" summarizing the procedures implemented as part of the project, with the prospect of spreading it.  

The creation of a digital platform enabling engaged students to self-assess the skills they have acquired as part of their engagement.  

The definition and testing of a "engaged student status", enabling beneficiaries to have flexible working hours, the possibility of substituting work on their engagement project for their compulsory internship, and access to individual support.

<< Implementation >>

Several debathons were organized collectively (involving students and/or staff from the universities involved): La Rochelle, Klaipeda, Valencia; debathons were also organized by partners only with their students, on their campuses, during the project.  

Several transnational meetings were organized, each time a collectively organized debathon was held, but also as part of the project follow-up (in person or, more often, by videoconference).  

Consideration was given to the identification and production of teaching aids for committed students (as part of the general presentation of the engagement, but also to promote the skills acquired); teaching workshops or conferences were therefore organized.  

The drafting of the white paper was spread over a large part of the project's duration.  

The idea of an "engaged student status" was widely discussed, and some partners identified teaching staff who were interested in trying it out.

<< Results >>

The first international debathon was organized in La Rochelle in November 2021. Organizing these events enabled us to draw up procedures for duplicating the event in other territories, train students in debate techniques and discuss possible definitions of engagement. This in turn enabled us to replicate the event at other partner sites. The white paper was written by the University of Valencia, which synthesized the contributions of each partner on their own engagement schemes, bringing in the results of in-depth research on engagement on a European scale.  

Finally, in the last year, we worked on the pooling and creation of teaching aids, notably in preparation for the debathons (conference texts, presentations by local associations, Powerpoints relating to workshops aimed at optimizing public speaking or the valorization of skills acquired through engagement). 

The status of engaged student will be tested at the end of the project (2023-2024) at various partner universities, once the specific features of this status have been defined (as part of the project).

2020-1-HR01-KA203-077777.title: Accelerating the transition towards Edu 4.0 in HEIs
2020-1-HR01-KA203-077777.summary:
<< Background >>

Jobs today are becoming more flexible but more complex and people’s capacities to manage information, think problem-based, use digital resources, communicate effectively, and be resilient are more crucial than ever. This project recognized that without higher education institutions (HEIs) updated and effective education, research and innovation, and inter-relation with the market Europe cannot respond to these challenges. Project activities enabled the environment for learning new skills and teaching approaches in computer science and related disciplines that correspond to the challenges of Industry 4.0, and also Education 4.0. The project contributed to a) resolving skills gaps and mismatches between HEIs, as partners developed a catalog of new teaching skills based on the prior extensive research of the existing knowledge and methods in IO1; b) creating and piloting Joint Creative Classrooms between HEIs based on their experience and expertise in IO3; c) creating new LD models with linking the teaching courses content with newest trends in research and industry 4.0 with LD tool (IO2, IO3). IT companies provided added value with real-case examples in JCCs. All are highly transferable among HEI in Europe and internationally.

<< Objectives >>

The overall objective was to respond to the need for Industry 4.0 with the partnership that developed solutions of how to accelerate the corresponding transition within HEIs in computer science towards Education 4.0, where humans and technologies are aligned with the aim to enable the achievement of skills, competencies, and knowledge necessary. Three specific objectives were: (SO1) to enable continuous improvement of skills of teaching staff to respond to the requirements of Education 4.0; (SO2) to design and develop transferable learning design models that guide implementation of innovative teaching, student performance tracking and learning methods to enable the necessary shifts; (SO3) to promote innovated, effective, internationalized digital age teaching and learning environments. This was achieved with 5 Intellectual Outputs, 8 piloted Joint Creative Classrooms (JCC), 7 multiplier events, and continuous dissemination. Teachers from different educational systems gained valuable skills within an international blended environment. The project increased the attractiveness of STEM since the JCC has been a collaborative practice attended by students from home from different countries and included university-business cooperation.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented activities regarding the creation of Intellectual outputs: monthly coordination online meetings, peer review procedure for assuring the quality of the Intellectual outputs and risks predictions; dissemination activities with project materials and on project channels but also on a local and regional level od partners: https://teach4edu4-project.eu/en/news; creation of a catalog of Joint Creative Classrooms with all details and learning outcomes of JCCs: https://teach4edu4-project.eu/sites/default/files/2022-11/TEACH4EDU4_JCC_Booklet_2022_11_08.pdf; organization of hybrid workshops for teachers to exchange experiences, brainstorm and improve their JCCs; conduction of interviews with teachers and students about JCCs, creating certificates for teachers and students and conducting ECTS procedure for students, working together on publishing academia papers, communicating with the stakeholders and policymakers and other educational systems, monitoring project management quality through questionnaires and communication with partners and impact and sustainability activities (planning of further use and availability of project results).

<< Results >>

5 Intellectual Outputs: IO1: Catalog of new forms of teaching, learning, and assessment in CS in Edu 4.0 and related teachers’ skills and competencies: the main objective of this IO is to identify, collect and organize innovative teaching and learning methods descriptions,  IO2: Learning design models: 3 different LD models (templates) specific for Education 4.0 and Computer Science courses were developed based on the extensive literature review and Joint Creative Classrooms (JCC) pilots, IO3: Collaborative Teaching Methods for Joint Creative Classrooms: The concept of Joint Creative Classrooms, computer science courses held in collaboration with two or more partner universities by using Learning design models and principles, was defined and piloted throughout the project, IO4: The guidebook on the use of learning data to create evidence-based learning design decisions was created to  support teachers and educators in making evidence-based LD decisions and to support them in evaluating the effects of these decisions, IO5: Partnership Manifesto: Transferability of the developed models developed with the main objective to enable the transfer of knowledge, and experience to strengthen and broaden this even beyond the project lifetime as well as to enable the transferability to other partnerships and domains
8 JCCs have been piloted (Information Retrieval and Data Mining, Machine Learning School, Modeling and Computer Simulation, Internet of Things: Embedded Software Development, Robotics: Embedded Software Development, Internet Security and Trustworthiness, Advanced Database Systems, Software Architectures Analysis, and Design), with 26 teachers and more than 260 students (from which 169 successfully completed JCCs and received a certificate of completion and ECTS)
4 newsletters have been created, 1 poster, 1 brochure, and 1 catalog with JCC details, 5 research papers have been published (one paper is accepted for CECIIS 2023 conference in September)
5 TPM have been conducted (Kick-off meeting CRO – online December 2020, hybrid Meet4Edu4 in Croatia September 2021, hybrid Meet4Edu4 in Serbia February 2022, hybrid Meet4Edu4 in Slovakia October 2022, hybrid Meet4Edu4 in Spain March 2023)
7 multiplier events (Ready4Edu4: in Serbia February 2023, in the UK February 2023, in Estonia February 2023, in Spain February 2023, in Italy February 2023, in Slovakia February 2023, and Evolution2Edu4 (final conference) CRO March 2023 have been organized with around 200 participants

2020-1-HR01-KA203-077785.title: Crossing the Gap: Startup education and support for PhD students, researchers and scientists
2020-1-HR01-KA203-077785.summary:
<< Background >>

The implementation of this project sought to "fill the gap" between the academic community and the startup world. Most people in academia do not see startups as something that's meant for them because the media is dominated by overnight success stories. When this project proposal was submitted, there was no related startup education and support program in Croatia specifically designed to facilitate the transition from academia to the startup world. Slovenia and Austria have their own university startup support programs and facilities, but they also have a lot of room for improvement. They lag behind top European universities (Switzerland is the leader with 18.1% of startups that start at university, Austria has 9%, Slovenia 4.7%, and Croatia is not on the list - https://www.statista.com/statistics/878922/startups-founded-from-universities-in-europe/). Both Slovenian and Austrian have been newly emerging during the past few years (http://startupmonitor.eu/EUSM_Country-overviews.pdf), but they alone cannot compete with large ecosystems like the one in Germany (https://yourstory.com/2019/05/germany-funding-exist-startup-oliver-hunke) and in UK (https://www.ft.com/content/8e74ad10-e0be-11e9-b8e0-026e07cbe5b4).

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the COGSTEPS project were positive changes in the perception of startups by the academic and scientific community, the launch of more university startups and spin-off companies, the development of an entrepreneurial mindset and transferable and transversal skills of students, researchers, professors and scientists, the formation of a regional centre for innovation and commercialization of scientific research results between project partners, development of an online platform for startup education and networking, and overcoming the gap between the academic and startup worlds. The goal of this project was to create a clear path, educational materials and support system for every academic startup in the future.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, five dissemination events were organized:
- 3 launch events (https://cogsteps.com/cogsteps-launch-events-organized-in-croatia-austria-and-slovenia/)
- joint presentation of the project as part of PODIM (https://cogsteps.com/podim-2022-program-powered-by-cogsteps/)
- the final conference where the results of the entire project were presented (https://nuqleus.io/2023/07/06/buducnost-hrvatskog-deep-tech-ekosustava-predstastave-je-na-prvom-nuqleus-demo-danu/)

The good practices of leading European universities in their work with academic startups were researched, and based on these results a curriculum was prepared (educational materials created, mentors selected) for four startup education programs. Those four programs were tested through four LTT activities:
- https://cogsteps.com/cogsteps-live-program-has-started-with-startup-101-bootcamp/
- https://cogsteps.com/from-researcher-to-mvp-the-second-cogsteps-live-program-successfully-closed/
- https://cogsteps.com/cogsteps-third-live-program-closes-successfully-from-mvp-to-first-customers/
- https://cogsteps.com/cogsteps-fourth-live-program-closes-successfully-from-customers-to-product/

In addition, many group meetings for planning and networking were held.

<< Results >>

The following results were produced during the project:
- a report on good practices for connecting the academic community with the startup world,
- a web platform for brainstorming and finding startup co-founders among researchers or experts from different fields, which provides educational materials for four different stages of startup development and connects academic startups with supporting institutions for startup development like incubators and venture capital funds, 
- program plan and digital resources (presentations and recordings of lectures) for learning about startup basics for the academic community - topics like startup keywords, lean startup, and design thinking;
- program plan and digital resources (presentations and recordings of lectures) for a transition from academic to the startup world - topics like idea validation, prototyping and storytelling;
- program plan and digital resources (presentations and recordings of lectures) for early-stage academic startups with an MVP - topics like brand, sales and go-to-market strategy;
- program plan and digital resources (presentations and recordings of lectures) for early-stage academic startups with first customers - topics like growth, networking and online marketing.
