2020-1-HR01-KA203-077797.title: Steering Higher Education for Community Engagement
2020-1-HR01-KA203-077797.summary:
<< Background >>

Community engagement in higher education is an increasingly prominent topic both in university practices and in higher education policies. Community engagement refers to partnerships between universities and external communities, encompassing public, business and civil society sectors, to address societal needs. The SHEFCE project aimed to address needs of key stakeholders on how to better structure and support community engagement at the local level (by institutional action-planning at universities, in partnership with communities), at the national level (by providing policy recommendations to remove obstacles to community engagement) and at the European level (by piloting an innovative tool, by developing an online platform and providing recommendations and guidelines for supporting community engagement).

<< Objectives >>

The overall objective of the SHEFCE project was to contribute to increasing community engagement of European universities, in the form of partnerships with local and regional stakeholders to address societal challenges. The specific objective of the SHEFCE project is to build the capacities of universities, policymakers and stakeholders in Europe for mainstreaming community engagement in higher education.

<< Implementation >>

The SHEFCE project methodology thus involved parallel actions at the local level, national level and European level to achieve these objectives. 

•	At the local level, the project applied robust methodologies for self-assessing institutional community engagement at each partner university and for developing high-quality plans to improve their community engagement; 
•	At the national level, the project produced in-depth analyses, organised stakeholder consultations and produced recommendations to support evidence-based policy-making;
•	At the European level, the project conceptualized and developed a valuable online information resource for users on community engagement and piloted an innovative methodology and tool for comparing university performance in community engagement.

<< Results >>

The SHEFCE project produced four key intellectual outputs:

1) University action-plans for community engagement at 5 partner universities
2) Policy recommendations for system-level support for community engagement in higher education in 5 participating countries/regions (Austria, Belgium/Flemish Community; Spain/Autonomous Province of Catalonia; Croatia and Ireland)
3) A European online platform for community engagement in higher education: www.community-engagement.eu 
4) Piloting a European university-community engagement heatmap

Together, these intellectual outputs led to the following outcomes: 

•	Local level outcomes: Improved capacities of 5 universities and their communities for community engagement through institutional self-evaluation and action-planning
•	National level outcomes: Increased awareness of 5 national authorities/stakeholders of the value of community engagement in higher education, of system-level obstacles and of potential policy solutions 
•	European outcomes: (1) Improved accessibility and quality of supportive resources for community engagement in higher education in Europe; (2) Foundation established for comparing European universities’ community engagement in a transnational context
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-HR01-KA203-077806.title: DEVELOPMENT OF EUROPEAN CURRICULUM IN THE FIELD OF SUSTAINABLE CAMPING RESORT MANAGEMENT
2020-1-HR01-KA203-077806.summary:
<< Background >>

Due to the growing importance of the camping industry to the overall European economy and its potential role in meeting the requirements of the green transformation, there is a perceived lack of any formal education specialized in camping management with a focus on sustainability, in Europe. Given the long line of work and research in the camping industry and the fact that the camping industry makes up a large share in the overall European tourism industry, the initiative started at an informal meeting during the camp congress in Croatia. 
Because of the specificity and complexity of campsite services and the future transformation of campsites into green resorts, existing tourism education at the higher education level does not correspond with the actual or future skill needs of the industry. By adopting a participatory approach that facilitates the exchange and co-creation process between different stakeholders,​ the project, i.e. the curriculum and the newly created courses, will, as envisaged, provide the opportunity to bridge the gap between business needs and education in the field of sustainable camping management at the international level.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project CAMPMASTER was to prepare the ground for the launch of the first joint master's degree program in sustainable camping resort management, named Master of Sustainable Outdoor Hospitality Management, under the newly developed curriculum. 
In line with this objective, the project consisted of defining a framework for the competencies, knowledge and skills of a camping resort manager based on close collaboration between camping industry stakeholders, university teaching staff and students, which eventually resulted in the curriculum and organizational structure of the joint master's program. However, the results of the project exceeded expectations and the accreditation process began before the end of the project. So, the joint master's program is accredited by national accreditation agencies from Spain and the Netherlands. Croatia expects to receive confirmation of accreditation in December 2022, which confirms that not only the goal of developing the curriculum has been achieved, but also the start of a new study program, that will begin in September 2023.

<< Implementation >>

All major planned activities were completed on time, such as four intellectual outputs that surveyed students, the camping industry, and stakeholder analysis. The Learning, Teaching and Training activity was realized through the implementation of a learning week in which teachers were trained to teach with new learning methods in the future study. Due to constraints from the COVID -19 pandemic, three of four multiplier events were conducted. Given the unavailability of students, fluctuating numbers of students present and absent, and adaptations to the use of online learning tools, the three planned simultaneous delivery of multiplier events could not be organized as originally planned. Therefore, the partners found a solution through organized congresses of national camping organizations. Nevertheless, all the important information was collected and the project achieved an enviable success through this form of dissemination. Furthermore, for the same reasons as mentioned above, only three out of four transnational meetings could be held. Study modules were developed at all three universities and a high quality Study Handbook was produced, which formed an excellent basis for the preparation of the accreditation process.

<< Results >>

Firstly, the learning outcomes and modules of the future Master study programe on Sustainable camping resort management was defined (IO1). Secondly, the partners developed the complete curriculum with all syllabi, teaching and assessment methods for all courses (IO2), using the manual on how to draft syllabi. Thirdly, these outputs are publicly available alongside other open educational resources (OERs) on the developed Learning platform for the camping industry (IO3) available at: https://camping-master.eu/learning-platform/. And finally, research and analysis of best practices in sustainable camping management resulted in the selection of teaching case studies that are equally open source (IO4) available at: https://camping-master.eu/case-studies/. 
A very important result of the project activities, besides the project results, are the prepared documents for the accreditation of the new joint study program and the successfully submitted application in July 2022, which has been approved so far by the University of Rijeka. Confirmation by the Agency for Science and Higher Education and the final decision on the implementation of the program by the Ministry of Science and Education are expected by the end of the year.

2020-1-IE02-KA203-000758.title: Introducing Intellectual Property Education for Lifelong Learning and the Knowledge Economy
2020-1-IE02-KA203-000758.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project with the aim of introducing education in the field of Intellectual Property (IP), in the curriculum of technical Universities, through training the teaching, support staff and librarians in IP.  The project set out to forecast the needs of today’s and future labour market in the field of IP and to develop relevant learning methodologies, to identify the gap between skills acquired in higher education and the demands of the labour market, to identify and implement best practices and to design methods for the protection of IP. Through the development & implementation of a highly innovative 8 Module IPEDU Curriculum, the project has addressed the core need to improve the current state of education in the field of IP, to facilitate the exchange, flow and co-creation of knowledge in the field of Industrial Property protection. The project has contributed to the professional development of teaching and support staff , in the field of IP Law, through Short-term joint staff training events. The project has addressed the need to provide the teaching and support staff from HEIs with the opportunity to improve and adapt their teaching curricula in the field of Industrial Property to the European level.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the IPEDU project were to improve the current state of education in the field of Intellectual Property, to strengthen the cooperation between universities and the business environment, to facilitate the exchange, flow and co-creation of knowledge in the field of Industrial Property protection. The project also aimed to correlate the curricula in the field of Industrial Property Law with the concrete needs of the labour market and to reduce the significant differences in the curricula of the Industrial Property courses, both at national and European level. The project also endeavoured to introduce education in the field of Industrial Property Law to technical faculties and to contribute to the professional development of teaching staff and support staff , in the field of Industrial Property Law, through Short-term joint staff training events.

<< Implementation >>

Despite a suspension of the project during 2021 due to the impact of Covid 19, the IPEDU project succeeded in implementing all planned activities. 4 Transnational Project Meetings (TPM) were held in the project, in Romania, Germany, Ireland and Slovenia (Final Meeting). Five Multiplier Events (ME’s) were hosted by project partners from RO (MBTT), ES (UPV), HR (UNIZG), SI (UL) and PT (IPP).  While these ME’s were affected by Covid 19, with some events being held online, the events attracted large numbers of delegates as one of the achievements of the project. IPEDU also delivered the 8 Intellectual Outputs (IO's) as envisaged in the original project application. This includes the highly innovative IPEDU Curriculum (8 modules) as well as the Toolkit for the train the trainers theoretical programme. All Short Term Joint Staff Training events were successfully held during the project in HR (hosted by UNIZG-online due to Covid 19), PT (hosted by IPP) and ES (hosted by  UPV). The project also produced a range of analyses, reports, research studies and IP Guides as part of the IO’s of the project as well as the online platform website for the project.

<< Results >>

The IPEDU project produced the “Report on the state of education in the field of intellectual property” (IO1), which reported on the current state of education in the field of IP in the project countries. Intellectual Output 02 produced the report on “Skills and competences needed in the labour market, in the field of industrial property”. The Toolkit for the train – the – trainers theoretical programme (IO3) has given teaching and support staff specific teaching materials and methods in the area of IP Law, a set of resources to guide them in the teaching of IP while a highly innovative 8 module IPEDU Blended Curriculum was produced in IO4.  The Online Platform (IO5) for the project was also created and maintained successfully which has provided up-to-date information on IP Law and education. The project has also produced eLearning modules (IO6), based on the curriculum and teaching materials developed in IO4 as well as a Guide for best practices and policy for industrial property education (IO7). Other results produced included the Research study on the impact of the IP curriculum and training materials (IO8) which assessed the impact of other IO’s produced in the project.

2020-1-IE02-KA203-000759.title: Stakeholder Assembly on Power Relations in Higher Music Education
2020-1-IE02-KA203-000759.summary:
<< Background >>

It has come to light in recent decades that systemic power relations inequalities are embedded in most HMEIs. Media coverage has reported criminal cases involving leadership and faculty in HME, with student and staff surveys reflecting ongoing issues that are complex and nuanced.
Power relations influence the learning and working environment in HMEIs with consequences on how we teach, recruitment, and everyday interactions as well as assessment. With the benefit of expert, impartial and factual advice, a Chairperson plus 50 formed Stakeholder Assemblies to consider topics that are relevant to this issue. Their conclusions formed the basis of reports and recommendations to be submitted to the members of the AEC, an umbrella organisation that is the policy and advocacy voice for over 300 HMEIs. The AEC used its dissemination and training network to share the outcomes of the assemblies with the widest possible reach.

<< Objectives >>

OBJECTIVES
- To create a fair, equitable and safe forum in which a representative group addresses the topic of power relations in the HME sector
- To establish a ‘standard’ of conduct, which AEC members and the wider HME community could adopt
- To enable the adoption of that ‘standard’ through an academic publication, recommendations, policy documents and a training and dissemination plan
- To share our findings with the wider HE community
- To enable cultural change that empowers people and promotes social inclusion

<< Implementation >>

Four Stakeholder Assemblies 
Stakeholder Assembly on Power Relations in Higher Music Education 1: What do we understand power relations to mean in the context of the Higher Music Education Institution?
Stakeholder Assembly on Power Relations in Higher Music Education 2: Gender and Sexual Orientation Stakeholder Assembly on Power Relations in Higher Music Education 2: Gender and Sexual Orientation
 Stakeholder Assembly on Power Relations in Higher Music Education 3: Socioeconomic background and special needs
  Stakeholder Assembly on Power Relations in Higher Music Education 4: Artistic Standards
Multiplier events:        
 Multiplier Event 06-2022 A Case Study in Power Relations: The Symphony Orchestra
 Multiplier Event 11-2022 AEC Congress - Dissemination Workshop on PRIhME
Multiplier Event 02-2023 Power Relations in Pop and Jazz
Multiplier Event 08-2023 Final Conference PRIhME - Lessons for the new academic year
 Transnational Projects Meetings

<< Results >>

The overall PRIhME project consisted of the following components:
 9 project partners engaging with the theme of power relations in higher music education (HME) - all partners remain committed to the project and are fully involved.
4 stakeholder assemblies of 50 people to reflect on issues of power in HME Intellectual Output 1, a publication which brings together the expert papers and research from the assemblies.
Intellectual Output 2 - recommendations for the sector on helping the make HMEIs safe and supportive learning environments with a toolkit and good practises. 
Dissemination of PRIhME information through 4 multiplier events and online presence.
 Multiplier events have taken place in Spain (June 2022), France (November 2022), Italy (2023), as well as online (August 2023). 
The information from PRIhME including reflections, expert papers, videos and more has also been disseminated via a PRIhME webpage.

2020-1-IS01-KA203-065832.title: Teaching Institutional Resilience and Prompt Reaction to Crisis: Good Governance Experiences in Europe
2020-1-IS01-KA203-065832.summary:
<< Background >>

The urgency of finding new ways within the European governance curriculums to teach governance/institutional resilience and prompt reaction in crisis. The project therefore focused on Good Governance Experiences in Europe, in dealing with crises like the COVID-19 situation.

<< Objectives >>

The aim was to educate participants in the optimal ways to build institutional resilience through collaboration of both public and private actors in society. The purpose of the project was to bring a new approach to participation of students as future actors at the national level, European and global business ecosystem. That is aligned with the goals of the Bologna Agenda (BA), to improve quality and relevance of higher education by providing necessary resources and skills.

<< Implementation >>

The activities included: Webinars on Good Governance and Institutional Resilience, Information Sessions on: the Main Results of the project, Curriculum Development in the field of Good Governance, introducing the Collective Volume on Benchmarking Institutional Resilience and Good Governance Across Europe, and online Living Library on Good Governance and Institutional Resilience solutions based on Nordic Experience and Expertise. The learning teaching and training activities delivered included: Short-term joint staff training events and two Intensive programmes for higher education learners. Teachers were invited to these events both from the participant universities and from outside universities.

<< Results >>

The projects concrete outputs include: an In-depth Case Study Analysis on Partner Countries in the Field of Good Governance, a Comparative Curriculum Assessment in the Field of Good
Governance, a collective Volume on Benchmarking Institutional Resilience and Good Governance Across Europe, an In-depth Case Study Analysis on Partner Countries in the Field of
Good Governance, a Course Curriculum on Good Governance in Times of Crisis, a Repository of Open Educational Resources able to enhance educational content and learning on Good Governance, Trust and Institutional Resilience, a TERRAGOV e-learning Platform and, an online simulation game on the effect of crises on the institutional environment in different countries.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2020-1-IT02-KA203-080040.title: Mooc in Enology aimed at Reinforcing competences applying Game-based approach and Olfactive learning for the wine tasting
2020-1-IT02-KA203-080040.summary:
<< Background >>

MERGO project aimed to propose an innovative way to teach enology and viticulture in Higher Educational Institutions. In this sector, the academic lessons in this field are essentially based on theoretical teaching, that are supported by an intense laboratory activity where the “student” could learn in the acquiring the multisensorial skills for the wine recognition (olfactive, gustative and visual). Then, as it is typical in all the training processes, the declaratory learning is consequently supported by lessons and didactical materials with a linguistic approach (commonly are videos, slides or podcasts), while the practical part is made with tangible laboratorial activities. However, differently from other fields where the theoretical aspect is prevalent, in enology and wine tasting it is central to the ability of the “recognition”. On the basis of this background, the MERGO project aimed to face the challenge to produce an innovative pedagogical way to teach enology and viticulture topics combining the distance learning. This is possible because it is emerging mixed reality methods as the Tangible User Interfaces.

<< Objectives >>

MERGO project has the central aim to develop a new way to promote new advanced and innovative solutions based on the ultimate technologies, in order to innovate and promote the excellence in teaching in wine sector.

The project aimed to achieve and propose cutting-edge innovation in the enology sector by:

-        Propose a new model to develop a pedagogical framework for learning mediated through a distance learning course that also improves knowledge of the individual aromas present in wines.

-        Implement an open course aimed at the teaching of enology, viticulture and wine tasting applying an online course able to merge a mobile application aimed at training the olfactory skills of the students.

-        Share the results with the scientific community and the wine sector, by involving the experts in the creation of olfactory exercises.

In the context of wine tasting, TUIs represent a revolution and could place a crucial role in enhancing the basic sensory training of students by incorporating olfactory stimuli recognized by a digital interface. TUIs provide an opportunity for personalized learning, allowing students to progress at their own pace.

<< Implementation >>

MERGO project implemented mainly four macro-tasks aimed at delivering the main four intellectual outputs as proposed in the original proposal.
The actions performed by the Consortium were:

1.      The definition of a methodology and a theoretical framework for the Wine tasting learning (IO1)

2.      The release of a Massive Online Open Course on Wine Tasting in an EU dimension (IO2)

3.      The development of wine tasting mobile app, by designing and implementing a tool based on Tangible User Interfaces paradigm, with learning exercise co-created with the experts in wine sector (IO3)

4.      The dissemination of the results of the project, delivering guidelines with an exploitation strategy that aims to expand across the HEIs involved with a snow-ball effect, promoting change and innovation. (IO4)
During the project, MERGO project involved wine experts, enologists, sommeliers, academic teachers and all kinds of professionals that are involved in the wine sector in order to co-design the activities. European researchers, professors of agriculture and enology, ICT experts in Technology Enhanced Learning, and wine tasters created the exercises of the MERGO APP creating activities and training aligned with the e-learning platform.

<< Results >>

MERGO obtained all the goal set in the proposal by the Partnership. The project delivered:

- A methodology about the application of innovative pedagogies for teaching enology and viticulture in distance education

- A MOOC (https://learn.eduopen.org/eduopenv2/course_details.php?courseid=564)) on sensory assessment and enology principles created by researchers, experts and lecturers of five European countries of the Mediterranean area.

- A free app for smartphones (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=it.smarted.mergo&hl=it&gl=US) that exploits mixed reality methods permits an autonomous training to any student enrolled in the course using its own smartphone The 223 training exercises were co-created by a community of experts in the wine tasting sector and actively involved 103 experts.

- A report on guidelines and recommendations in further application of the MERGO approach.

- 161 participants in multiplier events.

- 2000 people reached by the dissemination activities performed by the Consortium.

The project received a significant enrichment from wine producers and companies, who brought their practical experience and insights into the real-world challenges encountered in the viticulture and oenology fields.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-LI01-KA203-000190.title: Entrepreneurial Self-Leadership Education through Virtual Training
2020-1-LI01-KA203-000190.summary:
<< Background >>

Entrepreneurship skills are becoming increasingly important in today's competitive job market. They not only enable individuals to start a business but also provide a framework for creatively solving problems, leading oneself, and adapting to change.

The project aimed to develop students' self-efficacy, self-confidence, and self-awareness to help them achieve individual and team goals. It involved training in self-leadership, mindfulness, and social skills to promote internationalisation and excellence in teaching.

The training course focused on bringing out the best in students, enriching their abilities, and providing them with a framework for learning, applying, growing, and giving back to society. It was designed to be transnational and adaptable to different contexts, focusing on individual and transpersonal levels.

The comprehensive program fostered interpersonal and intrapersonal skills, cultivated an entrepreneurial mindset, and promoted proactivity and self-reflection. By the end of the program, students had a deeper understanding of themselves and others, acquired new problem-solving skills, and developed an entrepreneurial mindset that would prove valuable in any career path.

<< Objectives >>

The project developed a training program to teach young adults essential skills, such as self-leadership, entrepreneurship, and mindfulness. The program aimed to empower participants to set meaningful goals and learn from their experiences using an adaptive approach. To achieve this goal, the project focused on developing both interpersonal and intrapersonal skills, emphasising mindfulness and self-leadership to foster self-awareness, self-confidence, and a deeper understanding of oneself and one's role in the world. Participants were encouraged to adopt an entrepreneurial mindset and approach challenges with creativity and a can-do attitude.

The project also aimed to have a significant impact on the participants' ability to work effectively in teams and contribute positively to group dynamics. By developing these skills, the project sought to help participants become more effective leaders and collaborators, contributing to the success of their organisations and making a positive impact on society. Ultimately, the project aimed to create a generation of young adults capable of leading from within, making a positive impact on their communities, and leaving a lasting legacy for future generations.

<< Implementation >>

To enhance the entrepreneurial skills of participants, we developed a comprehensive course manual that covers all aspects of entrepreneurship. The manual includes key topics such as identifying business opportunities, developing business plans, conducting market research, and creating funding strategies. To ensure the effectiveness of the curriculum, we implemented it iteratively at multiple partner institutions and conducted ongoing evaluations.

We collaborated with experts and researched best practices in curriculum development to incorporate innovative ideas. We also gathered feedback from participants, enabling us to tailor the curriculum to their needs. Before finalising the project, the partner institutions implemented one more iteration of the course, jointly teaching a class at the Dubrovnik Summer Business Academy, an intensive one-week summer school.

We distilled our observations into teacher's notes, which can be used by other educators who wish to implement the course at their institutions. These notes make it easier for educators to customise the course contents to suit the diverse needs of students. The course is also available for students to take control of their learning and achieve their personal challenges.

<< Results >>

The course manual is a guidebook that covers all aspects of the training program. It explains key concepts, includes case studies and exercises. The program has interactive workshop activities to put the knowledge into practice, which fosters experience-based learning. This training program aims to provide students with foundational knowledge and skills to become successful entrepreneurs and leaders.

Students can access a variety of materials to support their learning in addition to the course manual, including course videos. These videos provide a multisensory experience and guide students through the core concepts covered in the course. Students can watch the videos at their own pace, making it easier to review and revisit content as needed.

Teachers have access to valuable notes to support their teaching. These notes help instructors tailor the course to their specific needs by providing suggestions for different teaching methods, such as group work, interactive lectures, and problem-based learning. By using these notes, instructors can create a more engaging and effective learning experience for their students, adapting the course to different demographic groups.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-MT01-KA203-074246.title: UPgrading the SKIlls of Linguistics and Language Students
2020-1-MT01-KA203-074246.summary:
<< Background >>

Over time, the study of language has taken many different forms, but employment prospects for graduates in language-related disciplines (linguistics, foreign languages, language pedagogy, translation and interpreting) are still rather limited and mostly focused on teaching or translator positions. This stands in stark contrast with their potential employability given the omnipresence of language and communication in society and the number of companies that make language their main business. Technology giants such as Google, Amazon and Facebook all work with language data and the demand for research skills in language-related domains is constantly growing. University curricula, however, are rarely oriented towards skills needed for research and industry, focusing on describing rather than on predicting or explaining linguistic phenomena. The central goal of our project was to identify and tackle these skills gaps and mismatches through the development of a new curriculum component and supporting materials that introduce an integrated research-oriented perspective into language-related programmes with a view to enhancing students’ employability.

<< Objectives >>

UPSKILLS' main aim has been to propose a new profile of graduates in language-related disciplines that fits well in modern working environments — both in industry and academia — and provide university lecturers with the means to support it, thus enhancing their students' job prospects and facilitating their transition to the world of work, all the while creating a better work force for future employers. In doing so, UPSKILLS also sought to sensitise university course designers to the importance of research and technical skills in modern humanities curricula, fostering in this way the modernisation — and hence the attractiveness — of national and European language-related BA curricula. Through the creation of tailored learning materials based on real-world data/problems, we wanted to contribute to improving the effectiveness and relevance of the training of language experts, creating a larger pool of better prepared job candidates for companies recruiting them.

<< Implementation >>

In order to achieve our aims, we engaged in the production of four intellectual outputs (IOs). In the first one, we conducted a detailed needs analysis that provided a new professional profile for language and linguistics experts in the 21st century. In the second, we addressed the goal of integrating research into teaching from an academic, a research infrastructure and an industry-based perspective. For our third IO, we surveyed existing educational resources (e.g. online courses, tutorials) and complemented them with new materials and research projects in an active-learning curriculum component that targets the skills identified in our new professional profile. Finally, our fourth IO was dedicated to the use of existing and creation of new and adaptable educational games that can be used in conjunction with our materials. The delivery of each IO was followed by a multiplier event, where we showcased the project results in a hands-on way, while we also organised two separate train-the-trainers events, one concerning educational games and one concerning learning content creation, as well as a final summer school which enabled select students from our institutions to work on research projects based on our materials.

<< Results >>

1. A detailed professional profile description, entitled "language data and project specialist," for graduates in language-related disciplines. (IO1)

2. A gamified website that familiarises students with this profile. (IO4)

3. Three guides for integrating academic- and industry-based research, as well as research infrastructures into teaching, complemented by a number of reusable resources and a tool for tracking students' research progress. (IO2) 

4. Eleven learning content blocks, ranging from 3-6 ECTS each, complemented by dedicated research projects of extra ECTS value, some of which featured in digital student showcases. (IO3)

5. A searchable list of existing learning content that we surveyed before creating our own materials. (IO3)

6. A dissemination plan providing tips for registering courses in public repositories. (IO3)

7. Three freely available new digital games, accompanied by manuals for their use and adaptation. (IO4)

8. A searchable list of existing educational games that fit the UPSKILLS purposes, alongside guidelines for their use. (IO4)

9. A set of best practice guidelines for game-based learning. (IO4)

10. Reusable training materials for learning content creation and gamification. (IO3/IO4)
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2020-1-NO01-KA203-076512.title: VIRTUAL PRODUCTION STUDIES for the Creative Industries
2020-1-NO01-KA203-076512.summary:
<< Background >>

The partners recognised the need to address and harness disruptions caused by the rapid technological advancements affecting EU Creative Industries and the film/TV, and Games sectors in particular. In tandem, they understood the need for researchers and educators to find ways to mitigate impacts of the climate crisis. VIPROS was an opportunity employ the triangle of research, education and industry to foster innovation and keep education at pace with the changing landscape of creativity, technology and the needs of society.

As vehicle, the partners chose Virtual Production (VP). A concept, which combine digital tools to create realistic sets for film/TV recordings, reducing the need for resources. This innovative approach provides a sustainable alternative to traditional film/TV production that decreases transport, storage and consumption, which fosters eco-friendly practices.

In essence, the intention was to embrace VP, to drive innovation and educational excellence by adapting to rapid technological changes and creating valuable collaborations across domains. This, to ensure the success of students and strengthen the sustained relevance of Europe’s educational practices and its world leading position as incubator of talent.

<< Objectives >>

VIPROS aimed to strengthen innovation across Film, TV, Games, AV-Tech, research, enterprise, and education in response to the Creative Industries' (CI) growing need for innovation and sustainability. The project's strategic objectives can be summarised as:

> Unlocking Creativity: VP provided a platform to realise innovative audiovisual ideas.
> Resource Efficiency: VP introduced cost-effective production methods, enhancing financial and environmental sustainability within the CI.

The project's intended impacts were expected to be:

>> Increased VP research and collaboration between HEI and CI leaders.
>> CI businesses and professionals benefiting from VP/VSS's artistic, practical, financial, and environmental advantages.
>> Reduced skill gaps between STEM and Arts graduates, enhancing CI competitiveness, innovation, and environmentally sustainable practices.
>> VIPROS insights absorbed by CI-focused Funding Bodies and Sector Organisations, contributing to VP's potential in strategies and R&D initiatives

If attained, these intentions brings innovation and sustainability to the CI in general and by bridging STEM and Arts in context of film/TV, benefiting research, businesses, and graduates pertaining to the film/TV, game sectors.

<< Implementation >>

The VIPROS project has implemented following activities:

> 4 Transnational Project meetings (TPM)
> 6 Learning, Teaching, Training Activities (LTTA)
> 4 Multiplier Events (ME)
> Dynamically arranged online meetings in the project’s Joint Project Management Team (JPMT)

As part of the project’s development of Intellectual Outcomes (IO), following activities have also been carried out: 

> 2 Labstudies, performed in dialogue and collaboration between partners / associated partners and distributed over the two phases: Exploration with researchers and students / Exploitation with Professionals and Enterprises.
> 5 Course Trials, distributed among the partners: ADA, NFS and TMX, whereof one was done in collaboration between NFS and TMX, two were done in collaboration between TMX and the National Danish Film School and one done in collaboration between ADA and a VP company.
> Development of seven IO
> Extensive video documentation of all key activities, including preproduction of recordings and postproduction of footage.
> Dynamically arranged online meetings between partners' personnel and meetings with relevant associated partners, professionals, etc. These arranged for exchanges of information during the ongoing IO productions.

<< Results >>

The VIPROS project delivered eight concrete outputs and an essential intangible output, the VIPROS Co-Operation & Dialogue Network, which has added substantial value to the project and contributed to its long-term effects. Tangible outputs involves two additional results. An extra "demonstrator" under IO_2 and a 60+ minute tutorial video for motion tracking equipment installation and calibration. The tutorial supports the project partners’ future collaborations and, by that, facilitates the project sustainability. A key measure, as the partners are already collaborating in new initiatives. 

The main project outputs are the Intellectual Output (IO), presented under an own heading. However, the development of IO also generated valuable sub-results, presented here:

> A shared equipment / knowledge platform, shared between the partners.
> Extensive video documentation of key project activities.
> Successful graduates from the VIPROS Co-Operation & Dialogue Network.
> A substantial network of associated partners.
> New initiatives and projects, e.g., an EMDM project, establishment of Scandinavia's largest research group on VP and a new Erasmus+ project proposal.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-PL01-KA203-081596.title: Enhance Soft Skills to Nurture Competitiveness and Employability
2020-1-PL01-KA203-081596.summary:
<< Background >>

Available research published, among others, by the World Economic Forum indicates that in the modern labour market technical skills alone are not enough, directing attention to a set of 10 soft skills that are crucial for success. At the same time, formal teaching does not focus on their education. The project aimed to increase students' employability by stimulating the development of soft skills and maximising their engagement in the labour market beyond formal curricula. The achieved results of ESSENCE, including in particular a set of tools covering 7 soft skills - allow to fill the gap in this area. The project targeted at (1) students and young university graduates to increase their employment competitiveness and enrich their competences beyond formal teaching; (2) lecturers, higher education institutions, trainers, recruiters, who have been provided with work tools in the form of ready-made courses available under an open license. The essence of the problem was also addressed to the attention of representatives of public institutions, local government officials and parliamentarians (also at the EU level) through the developed Soft Skills Manifesto.

<< Objectives >>

The implementation of the project was to contribute to increasing the employability of university students and their competitiveness on the labour market, through the development of soft skills. Our goal was to enrich the offer of professional development paths going beyond the formal scope of education conducted at universities. The course content developed complies with the CEDEFOP guidelines for learning outcomes and fully aligned with EQF levels 3-5. In addition to the need to fill the existing gap in the area of available training materials for the education of soft skills, the activities undertaken under ESSENCE were to contribute to paying special attention to the need for (1) education in the field of soft skills development among students and young graduates, (2) using the developed tools (module content, case studies, good practices, decision-making games, glossary) to expand the training programmes with practical aspects allowing for the development of soft skills, as well as (3) involvement of policy makers and other stakeholder groups in activities integrating soft skills into educational programs, especially at the level of higher education.

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the project, all partners made every effort to implement the planned activities in accordance with the adopted schedule and action plan. Thanks to the involvement of each of them, all planned activities were successfully undertaken. As part of the project, the OER platform was created, a set of tools was developed based on a preceding process of mapping soft skills with employability. In addition, in order to improve the training materials, a validation process was conducted in the form of pilot trainings addressed to target groups. The wrought soft skills manifesto and operational guidance were provided to representatives of potentially interested institutions at local, regional, national and EU levels operating in both public and private sectors in the fields of higher education, education and politics. In addition, numerous events were organized to promote the results of the project, in which representatives of target groups participated.

<< Results >>

The project results include: (1) a fully accessible online interactive platform (OER) addressed to representatives of all project target groups, which was an e-learning platform and also served as a dissemination tool for other project results, available in 7 languages; (2) a report on mapping soft skills with employability; (3) the ESSENCE toolkit available in 7 languages on 7 soft skills to improve employability, each of which includes animation-enhanced training content, best  practices, case studies, a glossary of key terms, a decision game - available online with the possibility of listening or download as a pdf; (4) soft skills manifesto for universities and operational guidelines. The generated hard results contribute to the increase of competences possessed by young people entering the labour market, the developed set of tools is designed for individual work, and thanks to an open license it can be used for the work of trainers and teachers, which already met with great interest at the stage of validation of materials.

2020-1-PL01-KA203-081809.title: Transnational Quality Education for Organic Food Safety - SAFE-ORGfood
2020-1-PL01-KA203-081809.summary:
<< Background >>

There are numerous food safety aspects that must be taken into consideration by organic food processors. The Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 29 April 2004 on the hygiene of foodstuffs requires all food business operators to implement a system based on HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point) principles. One of the problems faced by the teachers seeking to teach food safety for organic food is that the present teaching programmes and all materials (publications, manuals, guides) are targeted at the production of conventional food. At the same time there is an extremely limited number of educational resources available for organic food safety teaching, that would combine the subject of food safety with the requirements for organic food production. Therefore, the SAFE-ORGfood project consortium aimed to jointly produce comprehensive, innovative educational materials covering various aspects of organic food safety, to be widely used by university teachers in all countries participating in the project and beyond.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed at exchanging knowledge and experience on various aspects of organic food production and food safety, as well as on the teaching methods, among educators and researchers from selected European universities, in order to develop tools and materials that would help university teachers in effective teaching of organic food safety. In each of the SAFE-ORGfood partner countries food safety is considered as a critical issue in the food system, and there is clearly a shortage of educational programmes and materials to teach organic food safety. We planned to produce practical materials useful for the university teachers and other professionals in all participating universities and beyond. The aim was to develop i.e. practical food safety system documentation for selected products, a handbook on organic food safety, ready-to-implement manuals, e-learning materials and finally a set of videos. The aim was to make these all materials freely available, and thus to allow for their wide dissemination and use by students, teachers and various food sector stakeholders. In the longer term, it is expected that the project outcomes will significantly contribute to enhancing the quality of education in the targeted field.

<< Implementation >>

The most important activity was the development of 5 project Intellectual Outputs, such as the Report “Analysis of food safety knowledge among the organic stakeholders” and the scientific publication “Assistance Needed for Increasing Knowledge of HACCP Food Safety Principles for Organic Sector in Selected EU Countries” (O1), “Handbook – theory about food safety in organic production” (O2), “Ready-to-implement manuals with practical solutions on food safety” (O3), “e-learning materials” (O4), and "On-line lectures (videos) on food safety system in organic production" (O5). The joint efforts of the consortium towards the production of these results, were strongly supported by effective communication thanks to the Transnational Project Meetings and videoconferences. On the top of this, the consortium carried out a number of important management and implementation activities, including i.e. development of the project website, various dissemination activities, as well as a number of activities aimed at the project monitoring and evaluation. In the last phase of the project, Multiplier Events were organized by each participating university to widely disseminate the project results.

<< Results >>

The most important outputs of the project are as follows:
1. Report “Analysis of food safety knowledge among the organic stakeholders” and the scientific paper “Assistance Needed for Increasing Knowledge of HACCP Food Safety Principles for Organic Sector in Selected EU Countries” (https://doi.org/10.3390/su15086605) (O1).
2. „Handbook – theory about food safety in organic production” (O2). 
3. „Ready-to-implement manuals with practical solutions on food safety” with practical solutions on food safety for the most typical organic products in each partner country (5 examples of manuals in English + 1 in each partner's language (5 + 5 pieces) and extra work of translation (O3). 
4. „E-learning materials on organic food safety” for master and postgraduate studies (presentations recorded with voice, scripts in 6 language versions) (O4).
5. Seven "On-line lectures (videos) on food safety system in organic production" (O5). 
6. Numerous presentations for the Transnational Project Meetings.
7. Presentations and materials for the SAFE-ORGfood Multiplier Events.
7. Various reports from project monitoring and evaluation activities. 
8. The project website and SAFE-ORGfood Facebook profile.

2020-1-PL01-KA203-081895.title: PROSPER: PROmoting Social entrePreneurship in higher Education for a prospeRous society
2020-1-PL01-KA203-081895.summary:
<< Background >>

PROSPER comes in response to the documented need for infusing Social Economy and Social Entrepreneurship into Higher Education and will particularly focus on countries where the concept of social economy enjoys a moderate level of recognition (Poland, Greece and Bulgaria) and is little known (Austria and Croatia) (CIRIEC,2017). Indicatively, in Poland needs in the field of Social Economy urge for the establishment of permanent links with research community, Croatia, Bulgaria and Greece report some of the lowest rates of employment in the sector (1%, 2,8% and 3,3% respectively) and EC presses for measures that could spread Social Entrepreneurship education in Austria. Additionally, Social Entrepreneurship is currently embedded within Higher Education with a quite narrow approach that has mainly a subject-specific focus and application in business studies. Within this context, it is difficult to leverage its full potential and offer holistic solutions to urgent societal issues. We need to empower and equip people from all educational backgrounds to become social entrepreneurs and develop a sense of purpose that is based upon creating social value through entrepreneurship.

<< Objectives >>

2020-1-PL01-KA203-081964.title: European Road Safety Partnership
2020-1-PL01-KA203-081964.summary:
<< Background >>

Road safety (RS) is a major challenge facing the modern world, with over a million road fatalities each year worldwide. This constitutes the leading cause of death among young people (up to 25 years of age) and an increasing proportion of elderly victims. The situation in Europe indicates that there has been no significant improvement in road safety in recent years.

The Road Infrastructure Safety Management System (RISM) has been developed to improve road safety. The first EU Directive 2008/96/EC stipulated mandatory coverage of only the TEN-T network. The new Directive 2019/1936/EC covers all national roads and all other roads that will be financed or co-financed by the EU. The effectiveness of implementing the Directive relies on preparing dedicated safety management staff. These specialists must be highly competent in both theoretical and practical aspects of road safety.

However, there are significant gaps in technical university curricula in the area of road safety. This suggests that future staff of road authorities will not be fully prepared for the challenges imposed by the Directive. Additionally, staff already engaged in RISM must constantly supplement their knowledge and gain new experience in this field. This will allow for a permanent increase in their competence, which will contribute to the increase of the level of RISM and consequently decrease the number of accidents and victims.

Road safety is an interdisciplinary area that requires adaptation of methods, tools, and actions to improve the safety of road users. Due to the wide variation in the level of road safety in European countries, international cooperation is needed to exchange experiences, standardize the implementation of high safety norms through appropriate methods and tools. The EuroS@P project will raise the level of teaching and training, using innovative didactic materials that will be widely available.

The project was divided into six work packages, resulting in 13 Intellectual Outputs (IO). The new teaching and training materials were developed, including analytical and fieldwork methods and tools dedicated to RS inspections existing roads and the assessment of the safety of pedestrian crossings. The development of an e-learning platform with prepared materials will increase the availability and promotion of the project results.

The main objective of the EuroS@P project was to promote the best educational solutions in the RISM area, with the increase of awareness and knowledge of RS. This includes building an e-learning platform with access to project products, developing teaching and training materials dedicated to conducting classes at universities and training courses for RISM staff, raising competences and skills in RISM by changing curricula at universities and equipping students and staff with didactic materials based on innovative RISM methods and tools, creating the foundations for Road Safety Professional Certification (RSP), and developing a lasting relationship and the continuation of active international cooperation between project partners with the possibility of its extension to other institutions.

The EuroS@P project targets at tudents, researchers, and academic teachers at universities, road authority staff at national, regional, and local levels, experts, specialists, and practitioners involved in RS activities, including staff who conduct training in various RS courses, and all users of road infrastructure.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to promote excellence in teaching and skills development in the field of road safety infrastructure management (RSIM). The project had seek to encourage innovative solutions and develop students and project participants who will become leaders in implementing such solutions in the future. Safety is currently the most important criterion in the design and maintenance of road infrastructure. The EuroS@P project has enabled the creation of innovative educational content through international cooperation, practical implementations, and research projects. The participation of reputable partners in the RS improvement field has allowed the promotion of best practices in RS management. This will prepare the next generation of road authority staff for the challenges imposed by the Directive.

The project's results will help students, RS specialists, and road authority staff improve their competence and knowledge in the area of RSIM. The project will also foster cooperation among various European scientific and research centers in the field of RSIM.

The project emphasizes the importance of extending and developing the competencies of educators and other personnel who support adult learners. To achieve this, the competence of educational staff must be improved continuously, and road authority staff responsible for RISM must keep their knowledge updated and verified. As the field of RS is constantly evolving with new methods, techniques, and tools, it is crucial to raise the knowledge of educational staff.

The EuroS@P project has developed new curricula with innovative teaching methods based on scientific research. The project has prioritized the development of innovative training materials for RISM training. These materials are based on the exchange of knowledge and experience from various scientific and research centres, and they are available on the e-learning platform. 

The project also emphasizes the need for long-term cooperation in raising competencies that will extend beyond the project's time frame and enable the implementation of future projects.

These are the key intellectual outputs of the project:
1. Review of tools and methods for assessing planned road impact on traffic safety on a cooperating road network.
2. Review of tools and methods for identifying high accident rate episodes and ensuring network safety.
3. Review of tools, methods, and programs for conducting road safety on existing roads including inspection of the different types of roads, and specify places like interchanges, intersection, and pedestrian crossing.
4. Review of tools and methods for inspecting road infrastructure safety.
5. Development of a methodology for road safety inspections.
6. Development of a methodology for managing pedestrian crossing safety.

<< Implementation >>

1)	Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities: Gdansk, Poland, Weimar, Germany, Rovinij, Croatia, Catania, Italy. 
2)	Multiplier Events in Gdansk, Poland and Zagreb Croatia;
3)	Project meetings in the traditional way and online of the whole consortium and individual online meetings.
4)	Dissemination of the results of XIV International Road Safety Conference GAMBIT 2023 conferences in Gdansk, Poland, and Road Safety Summer School 2023 in Zagreb, Croatia.
5)	Development of the Intellectual Outputs.
6)	Development of the e-learning platform and webpage.
7)	Implementation of the results within different HE courses and modules.

Studies:
GUT has started implementation of the results of EuroS@P in the academic year 2023/2024 in the subject: Road Infrastructure Safety Management, which has been implemented during the Master's programme in Transport and Civil Engineering (approx. 10-15 students). Selected elements from the project will also be implemented in other subjects. The other partners also plan to implement the results of the project into the training of students in the Transport and Civil Engineering course in the academic year 2024/2025.

Training courses:
GUT, BUW, UZ and UC will use all intellectual outputs to improve the quality of training for the personnel dealing with RISM (Road Safety Audit course). In the RSA course at GUT, the project's materials will be used to improve the quality of training for future RS specialists.

<< Results >>

The first deliverable of the project is the developed three methodologies in the area of RISM: 
•	IO.5 Development of road safety inspection methodology (RSI).
•	IO.10. Development of pedestrian crossing safety management methodology (PCSM).
•	IO.17 Development of roadside safety management methodology (RSSM).

One of the main objectives of the project was to prepare modern teaching and training materials in two subjects: Road Safety Inspection (IO.9 Theoretical and practical teaching materials development related to the road infrastructure safety inspection) and Pedestrian Crossing safety management (IO.13 Theoretical and practical teaching materials development related to the pedestrian crossing safety management). The work included:
According to the syllabuses developed for the classes, the materials include a number of innovative solutions not previously used in the RISM teaching system. Among others: 
•	Dividing lecture classes into parts to allow the student/learner to better focus on the material, 
•	The introduction of quizzes in the lecture sessions to review knowledge before and during the sessions,
•	Interviews with specialists involved in RISM,
•	Increased use of video materials and YouTube materials.
•	Preparing video materials to conduct field activities.
•	Development of dedicated tutorials.
•	Building a knowledge base with publications to support the learning process.
•	
As part of the project implementation, the following type of data was prepared:
•	PowerPoint – presentation, which should be presented by the teacher.
•	PowerPoint-audio – presentation with teacher soundtrack and subtitles if the speaker presented issues in another lounge than English.
•	PowerPoint with YouTube resources.
•	Recorded rural roads, motorways, expressway sections, intersections and interchanges.
•	Shapefile, *.kml, *.pdf with prepared localisation of analysed rural roads, motorways, expressways sections, intersections and interchanges, and pedestrian crossing. 
•	Excel and Adobe Acrobat files with prepared data, sheets.
•	Tutorials presenting issues during students' field activities.
•	Interactive quiz – different quizzes (open questions, multichoice, yes/no). 
•	Webinar, Q&A, PowerPoint - student presentation (Final discussion with the teacher, all groups together).

The EuroS@P project has developed a certification program for road safety professionals (IO.14 Development of Competence Certification Program), called the EuroS@P Road Safety Certification (RSC). The program is designed to assess the core and advanced competencies of road safety professionals and to provide a standardised certification process across Europe. The RSC Certification will have two levels:
•	RSP Level 1: For professionals impacting road safety across various dimensions.
•	RSP Level 2: For those focused on improving road safety performance through infrastructure and road safety management programs.

An important project result is the development of the e-learning platform (IO.15 Development of the e-learning platform). The content of the platform is a result of extensive research on the impact of infrastructure on road safety, combined with established road safety methodologies. The Moodle-based e-learning platform is a comprehensive digital tool that has been developed under the [e-mail removed] project to enhance road safety education. It is available on the Internet, making it accessible to research centres and road authorities across Europe. The platform offers road safety courses that can be integrated into existing university course curricula and provides a one-stop solution for online learning on road safety by offering training on all aspects of the subject at all levels. 

Users of the platform can:
•	Observe EuroS@P Pedestrian Crossing Safety inspection courses for students and experts.
•	Observe EuroS@P Road Safety Inspection courses for students and experts (Student course and Specialist course).
•	Observe the EuroS@P Road Safety Professional certification course.

The platform with EuroS@P courses is accessible at: https://enauczanie.pg.edu.pl/moodle/my/.

Together with the dedicated channel on the YouTube platform, it will complement the course on the e-learning platform. The EuroS@P canal is accessible at youtube.com/@eurosp4658

2020-1-PL01-KA203-081980.title: Teaching Sustainability in Higher Education in the Field of Economics and Management
2020-1-PL01-KA203-081980.summary:
<< Background >>

Our motivation to apply for the SUSTA project resulted from our strong belief that economic universities must deal with environmental issues. As anthropogenic climate change is shaped by human factors, business organizations should reduce their impact on the environment and greener the economies. To this end, teaching sustainability in higher business education is crucial in educating a new generation of sustainability-minded business leaders. However, integrating sustainability issues into higher business education is challenging because higher business education is typically guided by a profit-seeking logic and efficiency paradigm rather than environmental concern. Moreover, the complexity of perspectives related to the interplay of environmental, social and economic pillars is another challenge here needed to be addressed.
To address these challenges, our main goal of the SUSTA project was to create an engaging sustainability teaching concept for business students, aiming to raise awareness and engagement with sustainability issues. Our concept consists of a syllabus, teaching materials (e-book, videos and case studies), tested during the summer school and discussed with stakeholders.

<< Objectives >>

Changing the behaviour of business organizations towards reduction of their impact on the environment is a key issue to mitigate climate change. Teaching sustainability in higher business education is crucial to educating young people as the next generation of sustainability-minded business leaders. During their professional career, they will make key decisions for environmental protection regarding the production and use of products, the type of energy used, waste management, etc.
The main objective of the SUSTA project was to create an engaging concept of teaching sustainability to students of economics and management. However, this main objective included both direct and indirect goals. Our direct objectives were to create an engaging sustainability teaching concept for business students, consisting of an extended syllabus, teaching materials (e-book, videos and case studies), tested during the summer school and discussed with stakeholders. Our indirect goal was to raise awareness of the environmental, social and economic aspects of sustainable development and to engage students and business teachers in sustainable development issues, as well as to share knowledge and experience related to sustainable development.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented all activities in accordance with the original plan. To assess the educational needs of business students in the field of sustainability, we conducted the survey based on questionnaire among students, and desk research on existing sustainability courses. Then, we analysed their results and based on them, we prepared the dictionary of skills and competences in the field of sustainability along with extended syllabus of sustainability course. Then, we developed the primary version of teaching materials. Then, we organized a sustainability summer school for students from partnership to test the initial version of teaching materials. Based on the feedback from students and our own reflection on teaching experience, we prepared the final version of teaching materials in the form of e-book, videos and book of case studies. Throughout the SUSTA project, we organized management activities both scheduled transnational management meetings and ad hoc remote meetings or email exchanges to discuss the current issues related to the project realisation. We also implemented dissemination activities as planned, including multiplier events, social media activities via channels of our universities and the SUSTA channels, etc.

<< Results >>

We produced all outputs exceeding initial expectations. As output IO#1, we produced the report about the educational needs of business students in the field of sustainability. In the report, we showed (1) the sustainability issues observed by students and (2) their educational needs both together for all students, and separately for students from each of six partner countries. We also produced the report about existing courses about sustainability in business-oriented higher education. As output IO#2, we produced the extended syllabus of the course of sustainability dedicated to business students with 5 ECTS points, and dictionary of skills and competences of sustainability. As output IO#3, we produced and published an open access e-book (492 p., 21 co-authors, Bogucki Wydawnictwo Naukowe, ISBN 978-83-7986-488-1, https://doi.org/10.12657/978-83-7986-488-1). As output IO#4, we produced and published an open access collection of case studies together with methodological introduction (319 p. Publisher: University of Zagreb, Faculty of Economics and Business, ISBN 978-953-346-203-5, https://doi.org/10.22598/susta). As output IO#5, we produced movies with lectures and discussions about sustainability (lectures and case study)

2020-1-PL01-KA203-081999.title: Rediscovering „NewEurope” – On-Wheels summer school for Balkan/Central and Eastern Europe trans-border history and politics
2020-1-PL01-KA203-081999.summary:
<< Background >>

The idea for the application for this project appeared during a discussion with colleagues from Sofia University in Bulgaria in 2019, when we agreed that there is a peculiar image of Central-Eastern Europe in the dominant public discourse within the EU that often multiplies prejudices towards and within the region. 
Hence, we defined the project’s needs in three dimensions. Firstly, as the need for educational materials providing for comparative analysis of national experiences in selected topics. This approach allows for a critical bottom up reflection on the levels of distinctiveness and similarities among the countries from the region. Secondly, inherently connected with the first one, is the need for emphasis of the underestimated regional similarities in the political process and their dependence on external factors and path dependence or replication of solutions that bring the region closer to each other than it is usually perceived. Finally, to provide sources of comparison that reveal the patterns of political action in the so-called “New” and “Old” Europe and inspire reflection on the levels of similarity and differences. The production of relevant educational concepts and materials is the cure for these deficiencies.

<< Objectives >>

Providing materials tackling stereotypes and building bridges between the states from the Central-Eastern Europe accenting on the specificities and commonalities of national experiences, as well as within the process of European integration. Project’s main objective was to develop an innovative, holistic and integral approach for training of scholars to conduct educational process in the field of Balkan’s and CEE studies through on-wheels summer school focused on four main fields namely: (i) Minorities and majorities; (ii) Rule of law and European integration; (iii) Identity and nationalism & (iv) Politics and religion. 
Specifically, we aimed at raising the awareness of scholars and educators about the need to organize on-wheels schools in Balkan and CEE history to overcome the existing stereotypes and prejudice in students. Developing the competences of scholars and educators in on-wheels school organisation and conduction with students interested in Balkan & CEE history. Emphasizing the need for deeper understanding of the region in “Old” and “New” Europe states through defining the main principles and approaches for stimulation of the socio-cultural competencies of the higher education teaching staff.

<< Implementation >>

United around the shared understanding of the defined problems, the project partners agreed on the establishment of consortium pursuing the identified goals. We have elaborated a coherent methodological approach that allowed us to produce tangible material results under a shared logic and understanding. The partners brought together renown specialists in Balkan and CEE history and politics in the production of educational materials. These materials, apart from serving their education purpose, raise the awareness on the unfinished process of European integration in CEE and between “New” and “Old” Europe through the dismantling of existing prejudices. They also provide for the better understanding of CEE for outsiders to the region. Once the materials were ready, the project partners engaged in intensive dissemination activities aiming to reach the widest possible audience and to engage as many stakeholders as possible. Piloting of project materials with well established scholars and educators provided us also not only with respected ambassadors of our ideas but also with an excellent feedback and suggestions for further development and improvement.

<< Results >>

As scheduled in the project proposal, our project produced five tangible Intellectual Outputs: Methodological Framework; Training kits; Manual; Guidebook and educational platform with additional resource database. The Training kits constitute the core of this project as they contain selections of educational materials on the topics of Minorities and Majorities, Politics and Religion, Rule of Law and European Integration and National Identity. The Training kits content is based on a shared and consistently followed methodology that allows its further build-up, both horizontally (more topics) and vertically (more educational materials). All the materials are available in all the project participants languages as well as in English in a free of charge and registration requiring Moodle platform. The project has its own website that serves not only as a source of information and promotion of the project, but also as a guiding point for the project idea, aims and access to the project’s products.

2020-1-PL01-KA203-082136.title: Teacher Education About Multilingualism
2020-1-PL01-KA203-082136.summary:
<< Background >>

The project "Teacher Education About Multilingualism" (henceforth TEAM) aims to educate pre-service and in-service teachers in HEI settings about various aspects of multilingualism and bilingualism (the term bilingualism is used to capture both). Basic and up-to-date knowledge about bilingualism is often missing from teacher training curricula in HEIs across Europe, bilingualism often being mentioned in the context of educating students with special educational needs. This situation is unsatisfactory in present-day Europe, where migration both within the EU and from non-EU countries is a major contributor to demographic change. Teachers who have been working in previously homogeneous communities are increasingly more likely to have students with the experience of migration in their classrooms, both migrants and re-emigrants. Against this background, it is vitally important to provide teachers and future teachers, as well as other education professionals, with basic knowledge about bilingualism and multilingualism in the context of education.

<< Objectives >>

Therefore, TEAM aims to: 
1. strengthen the professional training of teachers and other educators in HEIs by preparing them to better deal with linguistic and cultural diversity in the classroom, 2. prepare teachers and other educators to better respond to the needs of students with migration backgrounds by making their teaching more socially relevant and inclusive, 3. improve the quality of academic instruction by creating a new interdisciplinary course curriculum and teaching resources linking teacher training with relevant and up-to-date bilingualism research.

<< Implementation >>

In order to meet these objectives TEAM has developed a comprehensive and interdisciplinary curriculum to educate teachers about various aspects of bilingualism, with a focus on linguistic approaches to bilingualism, neurocognitive processes in bilingualism and second language acquisition, social and cultural aspects of multilingualism, as well as approaches to and strategies implemented in multilingual education. In the next step, audiovisual materials and interactive activities were designed and prepared to teach this curriculum. The produced materials were then implemented by partners in their own teaching at HEIs, either as a separate course, or to complement existing modules and courses, in both traditional classroom and/or blended-learning environments. All the classroom-tested course materials were then put together to form an open education resource and made available to the general public through a dedicated YouTube channel and an open-access Moodle course. The results were evaluated by peer academics and students, and disseminated to the general public through a series of multiplier events carried out by all the partners.

<< Results >>

The intellectual outputs produced by the project include:
- TEAM syllabus for the planned course (IO1),
- TEAM audiovisual materials for the presentation of the course content (IO2), 
- TEAM e-learning course to be taught at partner universities (IO3), and
- TEAM open education resource (IO4).

IO1 has been made available to the end-users on the Moodle platform (IO4) as The Manual. 
IO2 consists of video-recorded interviews, screencasts and testimonials, altogether 88 videos, uploaded to a dedicated YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@TEAMultilingual).
IO3 was meant as a course taught at partner universities, with partners uploading course materials to learning platforms used by their universities. All the materials produced and used in IO3, i.e., interactive activities, were included in IO4. The course materials and activities have been piloted with an estimated 500 students at partner universities during the project lifetime, before being included in the final resource (IO4).
IO4 is an open-access Moodle course: https://teamcourse.bilingualism-matters.org, redirecting to: https://fon.wa.amu.edu.pl/moodle/index.php.
