2020-1-PL01-KA203-082186.title: Social Education on the Move
2020-1-PL01-KA203-082186.summary:
<< Background >>

INCREASING THE ATTRACTIVENESS OF THE EDUCATIONAL OFFER AND IMPROVING THE COMPETENCES OF STAFF/TEACHERS/TRAINERS

NEEDS of STUDENTS
•	To change DOMINATING TRADITIONAL model- at many universities still dominate the traditional, passive model (teacher-sender and the student=recipient). The traditional model is badly assessed and encloses students within the university walls, limits their activity and subjectivity.
•	Adapting education to the changing needs of the labor market .
•	The emphasis on EXPERIENCING and then on the knowledge that can be generated, depending on the needs, either before or after mobile classes.
•	Answering the NEEDS OF STUDENTS who want to acquire new skills and competencies, including communication, organization etc. The mobile model offers definitely greater activity and independence of class participants who act as organizers, experts, guides, players, partners. 
•	Increasing ATTRACTIVENESS OF LEARNING FORMS- active role of students + the participation of external stakeholders (experts, employers, activists, people at risk of marginalization)

STAFF NEEDS
•	Developing didactic skills.
•	Internationalization
•	Learning by doing projects.
•	Developing the network of cooperation
•	Contacts with practitioners

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we wanted to 
•	IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF EDUCATION and increase the level of satisfaction of students and teachers.

•	REFRESH THE DIDACTIC METHODS at partners universities by introduction of the MOBILE SOCIAL EDUCATION MODEL.

•	Making the didactic offer at the universities more flexible and current, filling the needs, attractive for the students.
 
•	Raise students and teachers satisfaction by applying the MODEL OF MOBILE SOCIAL EDUCATION(MmsED) consisting of three modules (1) RESEARCH WALKS; (2) STUDY VISITS; and (3) EDUCATIONAL GAMES ON THE MOVE.

•	Increasing (1) the quality of teaching and (2) strengthening the social competences of students and teachers, and (3) filling the gaps and weaknesses of traditional academic education by making it more practical.

On the other level we also wanted to:
1. DEVELOP A STRONG NETWORK OF INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION - to create new projects together.
2. INCLUDE – innovative themes, forms and tools of social and humanistic education.
3. WRITE PUBLICATIONS WHICH ARE RESULTS OF THE PROJECT
4. INFLUENCE AND EXCHANGE BETWEEN THE PARTNERS INSTITUTIONS by adapting and implementing good practices to the teaching practice.

<< Implementation >>

THE PROJECT's COMPLETED ACTIVITIES

1. Conducting research on mobile methods (initial and middle phase).
2. Exchange of good practices in the field of mobile social education (during the whole project).
3. Conducting pilot/experimental classes evaluated by the participants (mostly in the middle of the project).
4. Preparation of instructional videos (to make a common instructional movie) (O2).
5. Publishing book with articles about mobile methods (O1).
6. Publishing of the student's handbook (O3)
7. Publishing a guide for academic teachers (teacher's toolkit) (O4)
8. Developing the training course MOOC on the Education on the Move (O6)
9. Conducting partner meetings and disseminating the results (7 transnational project meetings, 6 offline/hybrid, 1 online due to COVID).
10. Organizing 11 multiplier events (each partner orgnized and realized one event).
11. Modyfing programmes of selected subjects by adding the mobile methods (O5).
12. Managing colaboration of 11 teams (regular meetings, 4 reports, communication rules/tools, dissemination strategy)
13. Project meetings: total number of teams’ meetings=128 (monthly meetings=30; TPM=7; thematic meetings=69; stakeholders meetings=22) 6 TPM offline/hybrid and 1 only online TPM.

<< Results >>

I. Three books published
• STUDIES ON THE MOBILE MODEL OF SOCIAL EDUCATION (O1) - a collection of jointly created scientific texts (theoretical, methodological, empirical) on the subject of mobile, participatory and inclusive methods and their application. Studies provided a common intellectual basis for using the developed model.
• STUDENT'S HANDBOOK (O3) contains descriptions of good practices in the application of innovative educational tools in the field of social and humanities education. The handbook shows how students can use these methods in future professional practice.
• TEACHER'S TOOLKIT (O4) - contains tips on how to use methods by teachers (walks, study visits, educational field games).

II. Other outputs

• A NEW PROGRAM CONTENT (O5) - adding mobile methods to programms of selected subjects - according to O5 report the changes were done in 128 subjects at 8 universities taking part in the SoMoveED project.
• the MOOC on the Education on the Move (O6) - online course for those who want to know how to conduct activities based on the education on the move.

2020-1-PL01-KA203-082274.title: Rhetoric for Innovative Education
2020-1-PL01-KA203-082274.summary:
<< Background >>

Students starting to learn rhetoric at an academic level have different needs than 10 or even 5 years ago. They have skill gaps, especially in such areas as planning research work, choosing research methods, cooperation, and communicating the results of their projects. On the other hand, they are efficient in using digital tools to find and share information. They are often more sensitive to issues such as avoiding discrimination, climate change, mental health, and well-being.
To tackle these skill gaps and to strengthen their strong points, students needed new, modern-style handbooks and materials, enabling flexible forms of learning as well as activities introducing them to research work in multinational teams.
Academic teachers need to work out new teaching methods. They also need a space to discuss their ideas and share experiences. We concluded that a wide international meeting is needed and that it should be followed by a book, summarizing contemporary perspectives on the didactics of rhetoric.
We also had in mind other groups of stakeholders, such as high school teachers and NGO activists. For them, open-source materials should be available on such topics as debates, critical thinking, and conscious media consumption.

<< Objectives >>

We aimed to work out a new vision of rhetorical studies and to implement new ways of teaching rhetoric at the academic level. We wanted to create a supportive environment and up-to-date resources for teaching and learning rhetoric. To give a frame to our vision, we needed a new program of studies (curricula). Then, we planned a range of teaching materials to be used in rhetoric courses at our universities, but also by other stakeholders: handbooks, an online course, and a website collecting useful online materials. The materials should be “student-friendly”, and therefore made in cooperation with students and reviewed by them.
Since our aim was to engage students in research work, we needed a structure to form international research teams and also various channels for them to cooperate and publish the results of their work.
Our aim was also to create opportunities for academic teachers to discuss ideas and exchange good practices. These could start, but not end, with international meetings and conferences and editing a book  on the didactics of rhetoric. This will serve as a starting point for a rhetorical think tank – an informal net of cooperation between academic teachers of rhetoric from different countries.

<< Implementation >>

Our activities targeted a range of different groups and served various purposes. To engage students in doing research and to develop their skills such as cooperation, communicating and presenting results, we organised workshops (with students in the roles of both participants and leaders), mini-research projects, discussions and debates, we also engaged the students in the process of editing, translating and proofreading the outputs. There were also such activities as a rhetorical board game (as a part of E4, Poland) and improvising speeches (E2, Bulgaria). A bunch of activities was directed at ourselves and our fellow-researchers, to develop our skills, exchange experiences, and also to establish good working conditions. These activities were: a workshop in public speaking (E3, Croatia), a Book Club (E3, Croatia), working meetings, co-editing the outputs, preparing publications for scientific journals, organizing conferences and presenting papers. Activities for a wider audience, promoting common values and civic engagement, encompass: debate workshops for high school students and for teachers, public speaking workshops for teachers, future teachers and other stakeholders, media workshop for academic audience.

<< Results >>

Published  teaching materials include handbooks (O1 – Methods of Rhetorical Criticism. A Handbook) and O3 (Handbook of Debate); an Online Course in Rhetoric (O2) and Teaching Rhetoric Online - a bank of online resources (O5). O1, O2, O5 consist of independent modules, thus enabling flexible learning. They can be easily adjusted for various groups of users
Publishing these materials was accompanied by introducing new teaching practices and assessment methods to our universities. Research-based learning was introduced as a part of output O7 (Students’ Research Teams), and it showed that international cooperation between students may become a standard practice.
Publishing the Curricula (O4) introduced the issue of rhetorical education to a wider audience, not only the academics, but also teachers, lawyers and non-school educational agencies.
Conferences in Zagreb (E3) and in Warsaw (E4) together with publishing the book Rhetorical Research and Didactics (O6) resulted in creating a non-formal network of academic teachers of rhetoric (Rhetorical Think Tank).

2020-1-PT01-KA203-078646.title: Promoting Sustainability as a Fundamental Driver in Software Development Training and Education
2020-1-PT01-KA203-078646.summary:
<< Background >>

Currently, sustainable practices in the context of software engineering are not taught at Computer Science courses. However, the current amount of electricity spent by servers on running programs is far from being trivial. Therefore, software engineers need to take into account more sustainable choices, for instance, a programming language or data structure that will require less energy. The proponents of this project felt the need to educate software engineers to consider sustainability in all aspects of the software engineering process. This project targets university students from computer science courses that could bring these practices to their professional lives in the near future and change the way software companies perceive the impact of running software on the environment.

<< Objectives >>

We aim to provide future software engineers with essential skills to develop software that is not only functionally correct, but also easy to maintain and evolve, that is durable, has a low impact and uses the hardware it is running on in the most energy-efficient way.

<< Implementation >>

Two summer schools and two dissemination events were implemented with the goal of promoting good sustainability practices in the software engineering process.  Two teacher training activities were also implemented with the goal of preparing material for the two summer schools among the teachers and to discuss pedagogical methods and goals.

<< Results >>

Within this project, two teacher training activities, two summer schools and two dissemination activities were organized. Moreover, several scientific publications were released, the proceedings of the teacher training events are publicly available and the proceedings of the two summer schools are being published at LNCS Springer.

2020-1-RO01-KA203-080368.title: Flexibility and Resilience in Digital Transformation and Intelligent Automation - Advanced Skills and Tools for Academia and Entrepreneurs
2020-1-RO01-KA203-080368.summary:
<< Background >>

The FOReSiGHT project was driven by the significant gap in the (trans-disciplinary) discourse and practice of resilience, foresight, risk management, digital transformation, and algorithmic governance, particularly within SMEs and HEI. It was conceived in response to the pressing need for a platform that could facilitate collaboration and bridge the gap in understanding between specialists in various fields, particularly those related to DT and shifts in business models.
The project was motivated by an increasing pace of technological change creating new risks and opportunities for businesses and societies,  a lack of understanding between tech and non-tech professionals about the implications of these changes, and a need for a more transdisciplinary approach to foresight and resilience.
Previous projects highlighted a significant vulnerability in a society transitioning to a digitally-based model, where misunderstanding and miscommunication could lead to significant risks and inefficiencies. As of 2023, with the intensification of the conversation around artificial intelligence, these needs are even more acute, linked with a necessity for proper skills to understand a wave of development unprecedented in Industry x.0.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objective of the FOReSiGHT project was to establish a digital collaboration platform between universities and companies to anticipate and deliver future skills for interfacing between tech and non-tech professionals in intelligent automation (IA), digital transformation (DT), and algorithmic governance (AG).
The project had 3 specific objectives, each corresponding to creating and delivering a kit for foreseeing and integrating skills in IA, DT, and AG. These kits, designed for teachers, trainers, and users, were made available on an existing online platform and delivered through blended learning methods.
The project also aimed to produce specific results related to IOs. These included the development of 37 specific curricula for each of the three areas (IA - 15, DT - 12, AG - 10), creating corresponding study materials, and publishing a whitepaper dedicated to the delivery chain for public policy at national and European levels for each area.
Additionally, the project sought to develop a Foresight Kit for Teachers, Students, and Entrepreneurs, conduct joint staff training sessions, implement blended mobility programs for students, and organize intensive study programs for students and stakeholders.

<< Implementation >>

The project had specific activities, as follows:
A. 3 transnational project meetings - 2 online (the first and last) and one in-person in 2022 in Berlin, Germany.
B. development of Intellectual Outputs - 3 FOReSiGHT Kits for IA, DT, AG containing curricula, study materials, white papers for the respective topics, and a Foresight Kit for Teachers, Students, and Entrepreneurs. 
C. dissemination of Intellectual Outputs through four separate methods:
C1. Multiplier events – 5 events in 2022 and 2023 in 5 countries: Romania, Germany, Italy, Croatia, and Belgium.
C2. Webinars – 21 webinars delivered in 2021, 2022, and 2023 on YouTube and Facebook Live. 
C3. Intensive study programs - 2 5-day events in Berlin, Germany (2022) and Zagreb, Croatia (2023).
C4. Blended mobilities. 7 trips to Berlin, Rome, and Bucharest in 2022 and 2023. 
D. A 3-day joint staff training session in 2021 in Rome, Italy. 
Other than these, the project carried out regular project and financial management activities, with specific tasks to ensure proper deployment and KPI reach.

<< Results >>

The project's main result is creating a digital collaboration platform between universities and companies to foresee and deliver future skills for interfacing between tech and non-tech professionals on IA, DT, AG, and RM. Partners in Romania, Italy, Germany, Croatia, and Belgium delivered it. The result is impactful not just throughout the partners but via the delivery of the Open Education Resources (OER) via the existing online learning platform to the other platform users at European and international levels.
Specific Results: 
A.	3 kits for Foreseeing and Integrating IA, DT, and AG Skills, respectively - curricula, study materials & white paper;
B.	A Foresight Kit for Teachers, Students, and Entrepreneurs;
C.	A joint staff training session–13 participants;
D.	Four programs of 5-day blended mobility programs for students–7 trips overall–55 participants;
E.	Two 5-day intensive study programs for students–80 participating students & 30 trainers;
F.	12000+ trained professionals–492 directly + 11920 indirectly via webinars;
G.	3550 global users of the OER (on BLOCKS platform);
H.	21 webinars-11920 views/participants;
I.	Project website, social media, communication & dissemination plans, promotional materials;
J.	ProjMan results.

2020-1-SI01-KA203-076054.title: Creative Repurposing of Educational Spaces for Innovative Student-centred Environments
2020-1-SI01-KA203-076054.summary:
<< Background >>

Student-centred learning and learner ergonomics are becoming important aspects in all types of educational settings. By recognising the central pedagogical and didactic position of educational institutions in each country, project partners contribute to 'making' citizens through higher education and cultural awareness. The process of educating graduates and citizens is an experimental continuum that enables universities to create conditions for associative activities and play a role as cultural custodians, preserving and reviving the cultural heritage of the political community, but also giving it direction. We found it important to recognise that universities should not carry out such activities alone, but should seek the support of local and regional experts in the field of pedagogy, urban methodology and cultural activities.

Student-centred learning, while somewhat difficult to define in terms of methodology and explicit content, is key to adapting to a more diverse student population and changing needs in terms of how education is delivered.

To achieve these goals, traditional pedagogy, didactics and scholarship have had to be rethought, including how and where learning and teaching take place.

<< Objectives >>

The objective was to develop a MODEL, a MANUAL and POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS based on the activities carried out in the project. The project consortium hoped to achieve a systemic impact on HE through the activities described, both on the institutions involved and on those who would later be interested in using the project results for their own institutional needs. Most educational spaces contain little sensory stimuli and are still too focused on teaching-centred learning methods. Repurposing of learning environments provides students with multiple opportunities to learn and participate in education-related activities with peers, professors and other faculty. Students have the opportunity to work on HE on independent projects that are not necessarily related to their studies and/or courses. This would encourage them to become independent, critical and active members of society. Higher education institutions need to be responsive to the social and economic needs of society, their actions to improve graduate employability, their contribution to national economic growth and local development, and the way they stimulate business creation and innovation in existing enterprises.

<< Implementation >>

The universities involved as partner organisations in this project prepared pilot projects for the repurposing of educational buildings and spaces to begin development and later expand it to a wider range of university environments. They also organised three-day training seminars for potential multipliers of the project results. The aim of the training sessions was to inform the participants about the features of the developed model for repurposing educational buildings and spaces and to show them how to introduce/use the model in their faculties.

All project outcomes have been designed to be easily transferable and implementable in other organisations and educational institutions interested in the reuse of educational buildings and spaces. Through promotional and dissemination activities, we encouraged educators, students, heads of educational institutions and other stakeholders such as decision-makers in municipalities, government structures and also European stakeholders to undertake the repurposing of educational buildings. This enabled the further development of student-centred learning and its use in urban development, as well as the improvement of learner ergonomics in higher education.

<< Results >>

The main outcomes of the project are:
1.	Mapping of existing participatory practises was done to give a clear overview of participatory practises in terms of good practises for repurposing educational buildings and spaces. The lead partner identified, grouped and labelled the mentioned good practises in terms of intellectual output.
2.	The model for repurposing educational buildings and spaces in HE non-formal education institutions and organisations, based on the inventory of existing participatory practises, is the first output of the project, which guides the model and pilot projects as the second output.
3.	The manual for the implementation of the model was prepared in accordance with the results of the mapping of current participatory practises and in collaboration with the model for reuse.
4.	Policy recommendations for public authorities, non-governmental organisations and educational institutions on participatory processes regarding the reuse of public buildings and urban spaces were developed to advocate for greater cooperation between policy makers, civil society and the education sector to improve urban development and participatory processes in cities.

2020-1-SK01-KA203-078263.title: Developing a new curriculum in Global Migration, Diaspora and Border Studies in East-Central Europe
2020-1-SK01-KA203-078263.summary:
<< Background >>

The GlocalEast project was designed to deliver an innovative curriculum in the field of migration, diasporic and border studies, as well as to create a platform for collaboration between actors from academia, the non-governmental sector and state and local government institutions. It responded to the need to improve the quality of educational programs and connect academic education with practical requirements.
The project also resulted in the transfer of expertise among the partner universities. The project consortium included universities that lacked courses on global migration, diaspora and border studies, as well as those that had experiences in these areas. The transfer of know-how was additionally enriched by the jointly shared expertise in the geographically defined area of East and Central Europe (ECE).
Using the digital tools, we also tried to increase the interactivity of teaching activities. Students had the opportunity to comment on the content and methodology of the curriculum. Cooperation with associated partners of the project enabled a better transfer of skills necessary for practice and a connection between universities and actors on the labor market in areas relevant to the curriculum prepared within the project.

<< Objectives >>

GLocalEAst was designed as a project with both short-term (project duration) and long-term goals.
By implementing the GLocalEAst project, it was possible to achieve:
- creation of a functional GLocalEAst cooperation platform in the field of migration, diaspora and border studies, which represents the basis for building further cooperation with the potential of connecting to the network of European university alliances;
- creation of a functional network of interregional cooperation between universities and non-governmental organizations, which could contribute to bridging the academic sector with the labor market;
- strengthening the position of the participating universities on the relevant academic regional scene through the creation of functional partnerships between actors from the academic and non-academic environment;
- improving education by expanding the offer of courses in the field of migration and border studies, which respond to current trends and changing conditions in the region (given migration flows and the need to address them)
- from the point of view of the students participating in the activities within the project, the expected impact was the acquisition of professional knowledge.

<< Implementation >>

The project consisted of the preparation of innovative curriculum in the field of migration, diaspora and border studies with a focus on the region of ECE and of the creation of platform for cooperation between the academic world, institutions of state administration and local self-government and non-governmental organizations in the participating EU (or EU candidate) countries .
Specifically, the following activities were implemented:
1. creation of a platform of experts from the academic community, non-governmental sector and institutions of state administration and local self-government;
2. mapping the current state and shortcomings in academic study programs with a focus on the field of migration, diaspora and border studies;
3. the work of expert groups on designing a new interdisciplinary curriculum in the field of migration, diaspora and border studies, including the preparation of teaching materials;
4. preparation and launch of a course aimed at the general public (especially the non-governmental sector) as long-life learning tool;
5. preparation and launch of an e-learning course for students;
6. use of the knowledge gained through the implementation of the project for the proposal of recommendations.

<< Results >>

O1 - GLocalEAst case studies on actors, processes and practices related to the integration of migrants.
The project partners developed: Overview of university programs in the field of migration, diaspora and border studies (O1/A1), National reports aimed at mapping national, regional and local actors in the field of migration, but also the processes and procedures of migration and integration policies in all partner countries involved in the project (O1/A2). These served as a starting point for the development of the Comparative Final Report within O1.
O2 – GLocalEAst curriculum. The prepared educational units reflect the educational and professional training needs identified during the first stage of project implementation (O1). In addition, the interdisciplinary content of education was prepared within 4 thematic units.
O3 - GLocalEAST Massive Open Online Course (MOOC course) "Migration, borders and diaspora in Eastern and Central Europe" intended mainly for civil society actors and the general public.
O4 – GLocalEAst e-learning course for students prepared within the Moodle platform.
O5 -GLocalEAst Joint Policy Paper Series - recommendations resulting from project implementation addressed to various target groups.

2020-1-SK01-KA203-078379.title: Learning Landscapes
2020-1-SK01-KA203-078379.summary:
<< Background >>

We felt the urgent need to better link higher education actors with local communities and stakeholders, since we understand universities as democratic civic-minded learning communities. We wanted to address this need by offering a new format for collective visioning and by creating an innovative partnership of academia, the public sector and planning professionals with civil society. We built on the idea that the local landscape is the actual forum for democratic community visioning. We felt that academia was missing a vision of how to initiate discourse in society and to create new partnerships, leading to real democratic change for sustainability. We aimed at preparing university staff members for their role as facilitators who are actively shaping the ‘learning landscapes process’ in an inclusive, empowering, and democratic way. We felt the need for skills development in the fields of process design, moderation, communication with civil society, participatory mapping, collective visioning methods and collective strategy building. We also wanted to address students as the future generation of European planners and designers and bring the ‘learning landscapes process’ closer to the civil society.

<< Objectives >>

Through implementing the LeLa project, we were following 5 main objectives: (1) To link universities with their communities in different national and regional contexts that are exemplary for contemporary European challenges; (2) To prepare university staff members for their contemporary and future role as facilitators in shaping the ‘learning landscapes process’ in an inclusive, empowering, and democratic way. To develop the necessary skills in process design, moderation, communication with civil society, participatory mapping, collective visioning, and collective strategy building; (3) To include students in the learning landscape process. To motivate them to share their ideas on local landscapes in discussions, to raise their awareness of Europe and its sustainability challenges and to develop valuable competences such as virtual team work, design for sustainability and intercultural communication; (4) To open up the ‘learning landscapes process’ to civil society by various means such as local design charrettes, open online lecture series, collaborative mapping activities, landscape walks, storytelling events; (5) To create and share knowledge by documenting the learning landscapes methodology as an open educational resource.

<< Implementation >>

In the LeLa project, we implemented a wide range of activities. The main international activities included 5 transnational project meetings in Nitra, Bratislava, Gdańsk, and Zagreb; 4 multiplier events in Gdańsk (2022), Zagreb, Nitra, and Zvolen (2023) in the form of landscape festivals; 2 learning, teaching, and training activities in the form of international and interdisciplinary student and teacher workshops in Gdańsk (2021) and Bratislava (2022); joint elaboration of two main intellectual outputs – Output O1: Handbook of the Learning Landscapes Process and Output O2: The Learning Landscapes Online Laboratory. Within the project management and implementation, all four universities, in cooperation with four NGOs established four local LeLa Living Labs – in Nitra, Bratislava, Zagreb and Gdańsk. These living labs have implemented a wide range of diverse activities, such as design studios, workshops and courses; an international student competition; an international landscape forum; art exhibitions; public discussions and consultations; collaborative mapping and visioning activities, guided landscape walks and cycle tours, hands-on workshops with local communities, prototyping activities, planting trees and many other.

<< Results >>

The project produces two main outputs -  Output O1: Handbook of the Learning Landscapes Process, and Output O2: The Learning Landscapes Online Laboratory. Besides these, there are other tangible project results, such as book publications and book chapters, a thematic special issue and LeLa papers in a peer-reviewed journal, conference papers on LeLa activities with acknowledgements to the Erasmus+ project; invited lectures and panel discussions; e-lecture series; outputs of design studios, workshops, courses, and student competitions; new community parks; many new planted trees, shrubs, and flowers in local landscapes; art installations and exhibitions; articles in local and regional newspapers and interviews in televisions. The most important intangible results consist in testing, and implementing the LeLa process at four universities in three European countries; establishing local Learning Landscapes Living Labs, building strong partnerships and cooperations with municipalities and local governments, different actors and stakeholders, local NGOs, citizen associations, local communities and neighbourhoods; as well as generating new knowledge and developing novel competences and skills for teachers, students and citizens.

2020-1-TR01-KA203-092333.title: Algorithmic Thinking Skills through Play-Based Learning for Future’s Code Literates
2020-1-TR01-KA203-092333.summary:
<< Background >>

In Türkiye, preschool education is quite equipped and there are serious national studies related to permanent learning, especially in the behavioural development of preschool children. The main point focused on the learning of children was to provide them to think freely and analyse situations from different perspectives, developing creative ideas which were the best solutions for the target status. To achieve this, preschool teaching undergraduates needed to learn how to foster children's algorithmic thinking skills in an elective course.
The lecturers involved in the project needed a higher education curriculum for the elective course "Algorithmic Skills in Early Childhood" and also needed teaching materials which were suitable for the flipped learning approach. Therefore, the teaching materials were planned as interactive animated presentations that allow users to pause on some decision stages to take notes, participate in question-answer sections, listen to audio records, watch video footage, do quizzes, etc. The course planned to be prepared would meet the need of the preschool teaching department of Democracy University as well as the same departments of the partner universities.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project practice was to prepare a course programme and teaching materials to teach preschool teaching undergraduates how to reflect the algorithmic thinking skill in all areas of preschool education and integrate them into the teaching of music, art, mathematics, drama, science, behaviour development and language development, which are addressed in early childhood.

With this, the project would also refer to the achievements below.
- Closing skills gaps in ICT-oriented teaching/learning activities for immediate impact on contemporary teaching skills of preschool teaching undergraduates
- Increasing the acquisition of knowledge and skills of preschool teaching undergraduates related to employing algorithmic thinking skills through play-based learning as an innovative teaching approach
- Upskilling the lecturers of the partner universities related to integrating algorithmic thinking skills into all subject areas focused, on preschool education.

<< Implementation >>

1- We prepared a higher education curriculum for the "Algorithmic Thinking Skills in Early Childhood" course. For this, we implemented some subactivities including data collection activities such as workshops and literature reviews for Knowledge Paper preparation and Learning Activity Books as extra outcomes derived from the collected data, especially from the focus group interviews with teachers.

2- Secondly we carried out a series of activities to prepare the interactive animated presentations. Partners firstly worked on the presentation content, and then EDUCLOUD managed the technical works for English versions. Then partners translated the content into national languages. After that, EDUCLOUD placed the translations into the slides and also subtitled/dubbed the animated videos in the presentations. All digital materials (Scorm and zip archive) were uploaded to MOODLE platform: https://lms.algolittle.org/

3- Also, the management and dissemination activities went on including the quality evaluation of project activities and results.

4- Partners' researchers wrote 13 academic papers related to the project topic during project practice. Also, a monograph has currently been prepared and it will be ready in November 2022.

2020-1-TR01-KA203-094242.title:
Energy Usage and Green Public Transportation in Future Smart Cities:
 An Innovative Teaching Program for Students, Stakeholders and Entrepreneurs
2020-1-TR01-KA203-094242.summary:
<< Background >>

The share of transportation in energy usage in the cities is very high. Authorities seek sustainable and green public transportation systems when they plan the future of the cities. Green public transportation is a multidisciplinary subject that focuses on designing the unimodal or intermodal public transportation system in the cities, energy usage in these systems, and information systems to gather information related to possible passengers. So, to support energy consumption solutions, in the scope of the project, we aimed to develop a one-week multidisciplinary training program made up of 7 teaching modules in order to increase the knowledge level and also raise awareness about green public transportation in smart cities for different target groups such as students, potential entrepreneurs, and employees of municipalities.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to increase the awareness and knowledge level of the learners (target groups) about future green public transportation systems in the future smart cities by preparing one-week teaching program. The target groups and objectives were:
Students will face with job opportunities that require multidisciplinary knowledge related to green public transportation in future smart cities that we aim to teach. 
Stakeholders: We planned to increase awareness and capacity building of the stakeholders about green public transportation systems in order to prepare them for future smart cities.
Universities: Each module has the potential to be a single course for the related major and minor programs. Our modules as a whole can be a secondary field program for the related faculties. 
Teaching assistants and academicians in the project may attend conferences and publish articles to increase their visibility. Participant academicians may improve their knowledge about the project subject and have the opportunity to communicate with other related professors and new joint projects may be initiated.
Entrepreneurs: We planned to inform the people who are willing to be entrepreneurs in the near future of smart cities.

<< Implementation >>

We prepared one-week teaching program as the intellectual output. To finalize the intellectual outputs and ensure that our one-week teaching program is applicable, we implemented a draft version in Split and the final version in Ankara. In order to prepare the intellectual outputs, we arranged 12 bimonthly meetings, 2 semi-annual meetings, and 5 transnational meetings.
To ensure the quality of the intellectual outputs, during the project period of two years, we also prepared the templates of all documents such as Syllabi, Lecture notes, Teaching Notes, and rubrics to evaluate syllabi, lecture, and teaching notes documents.

<< Results >>

We prepared a curriculum for one-week teaching program which includes 7 modules. We were faced with the effects of Covid-19 and see that the universities may need variations of teaching programs including online versions. We prepared a document that includes four variations. 
We prepared syllabuses for all modules, Lecture Notes Handbook for the learners as a supplementary document to read before joining the teaching program, and Teaching Manual for the instructors to use if they will teach the same program at their universities. 
We prepared a pre-questionnaire to apply before starting the teaching program and a reflection document to test if the learners benefited from the teaching program. We prepared “Item Bank” document which includes true-false, multiple choice, fill-in-the-blank, and open-ended questions and answers for all modules.   
We prepared a secondary field program entitled “Sustainable Transportation” for the universities. The proposal document includes instructions about the secondary field program and 7 syllabuses of the regular semester courses. We prepared posters, e-newsletters and Q&A videos for all modules available via the project website. In addition to what we promised, we published a scientific book.

2020-1-TR01-KA203-094309.title: STEM in Action; Open Educational Resources for Teachers
2020-1-TR01-KA203-094309.summary:
<< Background >>

Our application for the project was shaped by addressing specific needs in education. Among our main motivations, the innovative potential of the STEM approach in education and its potential to improve students' cognitive skills have an important place. In addition, issues such as unequal access to STEM education and lack of knowledge in this field are also among the key needs that attract attention.
In this application process, the need to increase teachers' knowledge and skills in STEM by targeting their professional development was also among the prioritised objectives. The project also aims to create a common source of knowledge by combining perspectives from different geographies by encouraging international co-operation and sharing of experiences.
Considering these needs during the application process, an approach that reflects the project goals and objectives was adopted and our project application was structured accordingly.

<< Objectives >>

1. Contribution to STEM Education: By emphasising the importance of STEM approach in education, we aimed to improve students' problem solving, critical thinking and innovative design skills. In doing so, we aimed to increase their ability to think solution-oriented to real-world problems.
2. Equality and Access in Education: By providing equal and broad access to STEM education, we aimed to offer opportunities in this field to students and teachers in different geographies. Thus, we aimed to reduce inequalities in education.
3. Teacher Development: By strengthening the knowledge and skills of teachers in the field of STEM, we aimed to support them to provide a more effective and contemporary education to students. In this context, we supported the professional development of teachers in STEM.
4. International Collaboration: By bringing together experiences from different countries, we aimed to create an international co-operation network on STEM education and promote knowledge sharing.
In line with these objectives, we aimed to implement the project and in this way, we planned to contribute to STEM education, increase equality in education, support the development of teachers and strengthen international cooperation.

<< Implementation >>

In the project, various training activities were realised. These activities included transnational meetings, learning visits, knowledge exchange, training material development, seminars and workshops. In addition, two different Learning-Teaching Activities (LTTs) were organised. The first one took place virtually in Ireland and the other face-to-face in Germany. In these activities, trainings on STEM education were provided for teachers and academics.
The partners involved in the project produced various curriculum materials in the field of STEM and created virtual courses and made them available through the project website. In addition, multiplier events such as Science Day Celebration, Pi Day Celebration and face-to-face STEM Courses for local teachers were organised to reach a wider audience.
These activities were considered as important steps towards achieving the project's objectives. Material development for STEM education, training of teachers and academicians, information sharing and dissemination of the results obtained were among the main focal points of the project.

<< Results >>

Our project has achieved several concrete outputs and results:
1. Educational Materials: A rich content was created in the field of STEM. Through the website, 30 video contents and curriculum texts were made available for pre-school, primary school and branch teachers. These materials were designed to provide training opportunities for teachers and students.
2. Academic and Technical Staff Training: More than 30 academics and 5 technical staff were trained on video preparation, STEM approach and STEM curriculum preparation. These trainings were considered as an important step towards achieving the goals of the project.
3. Teacher Outreach and Awareness Raising: At least 70 teachers in 3 countries benefited from the free STEM courses and used these materials for their students. It was also observed that STEM awareness among teachers increased with the dissemination of the project.
4. Project Extension and Dissemination: Although the project was planned for 24 months, it continued for a total of 36 months with an additional 12 months due to COVID-19. Dissemination activities were carried out through Science Day Celebration, Pi Day Celebration and face-to-face STEM Courses for local teachers. These activities contributed to expanding the impact of the project.
These concrete outputs and results were considered as important steps towards achieving the project's goal and producing quality materials for STEM education.

2020-1-UK01-KA203-079064.title: Advanced approacheS and practices for rail training and education  TO inNovate Rail study programmes and Improve rail higher education provision
2020-1-UK01-KA203-079064.summary:
<< Background >>

The ASTONRail project application aimed to address the pressing need for facilitating the development of a skilled rail workforce to enhance efficient rail system operations, promote sustainability and align with UNESCO Sustainable Development goals. With the rail sector's increasing ecological importance, driven by its energy efficiency and environmental benefits, the project sought to bridge an identified skills gap. The rapidly evolving rail industry demanded expertise in new technologies and innovation. The project's transnational approach was essential to secure a skilled and adaptable workforce and facilitate knowledge exchange among universities. Furthermore, it aligned with the European Commission's Fourth Railway Package, emphasising the importance of a skilled rail workforce.
The project's innovation centred on developing specialised rail-related teaching and learning methods that focused on cognitive and transferable skills. This comprehensive approach aimed to attract young professionals, promote sector advancements, and contribute to the rail industry's growth, making it a dynamic and competitive field. The transnational collaboration added value to rail skill development initiatives and the sector's overall progress.

<< Objectives >>

The ASTONRail project pursued distinct objectives in line with its primary aim of establishing a strategic rail higher education partnership. Specifically, these objectives target challenges related to the pressing need for rail workforce development, upskilling and education in the entire sector, namely:
1) Identify Gaps: Analyse industry-education disparities, pinpointing their causes through matching industry expectations with the current rail higher education provision.
2) Develop an Innovative Toolkit: Create diverse teaching methods and approaches to modernise rail education.
3) Test Toolkit: Validate methods in real-world educational settings through the delivery of an intensive programme.
4) Promote Rail Careers: Attract early-career professionals to the sector through intensified engagement and outreach activities.
5) Develop a user-friendly handbook offering easy access to innovative and effective teaching and learning practices for rail skills development and subject-specific knowledge and competencies.
These objectives aimed to foster a skilled, adaptable rail workforce aligned with the rail industry's needs, enhance the rail education provision, and promote an innovative and vibrant rail industry in Europe.

<< Implementation >>

- Partnership Coordination and Management: Aston University coordinated and managed project activities, maintaining a Risk Assessment Management Panel to address potential issues.
- Qualified Global Panel: DICEA established an expert panel to assess rail education programmes worldwide.
- Questionnaire Development and Surveys: UNIZA conducted surveys to gather industry needs data.
- Mapping and Literature Reviews: KTH conducted comprehensive literature reviews to analyse education-industry alignment.
- Toolkit Development: Aston University created a toolkit with innovative teaching materials, methods, and practices for rail higher education.
- Dissemination and Exploitation: EURNEX led various dissemination activities.
- Curriculum and Intensive Study Programme: UNIZG designed a transnational railway engineering curriculum and an intensive study programme.
- Public Awareness and Outreach: UMA raised public awareness about rail careers and made the sector appealing to young professionals.
- Handbook Compilation: TH Wildau compiled a dynamic handbook on modern rail workforce development.
- Technical Specification Development: Aston University drafted a technical specification profile for skilled rail workers.

<< Results >>

- Proactive Strategic Partnership: Established a collaborative network of eight institutions to address rail skills development challenges.
- Industry Impact Awareness: Considered technological trends like digitalization and automation while evaluating education-industry alignment.
- Innovative Teaching and Learning Methods: Designed specialised approaches for various educational levels, emphasising research-based learning, eLearning, and talent management.
- Cognitive and Transferable Skills Enhancement: Focused on developing skills for comprehensive career growth within the rail industry.
- Rail Sector Attractiveness Promotion: Worked to make the rail sector more appealing to young professionals and talents.
- Intensive Study Programme: Implemented a rigorous railway engineering study programme, integrating training events, courses, working experiences, and internships.
- Technical Specification Profile (TSP) Development: Devised and tested a TSP for innovative rail training and higher education provision.
- Living Handbook Compilation: Created a dynamic handbook documenting project outcomes and serving as a guide for educational institutions, contributing to the improvement of rail higher education provision.

2014-1-AT01-KA201-000900.title: Eine österreichisch-kroatische Freundschaft: verbunden durch Natur und Garten
2014-1-AT01-KA201-000900.summary:
The project "Austrian - Croatian Friendship: connected through nature and garden" was supposed to improve relations the pupils had had to the foreign culture, as well as to the culture of their own, and to reinforce the social relations. In that way pupils could broaden their horizons to as many areas as possible. The old and new knowledge were particularly stressed out, focusing especially to the aspects of ecology. Our desire was to sensitize pupils to be aware of the environment with its natural resources. Likewise, our intention was to emphasize Europe as our common homeland and to create the unique European identity.
The project met the standards of the NMS syllabus in the first part of the common educational goals. In the chapter regarding school goals other themes were discussed, such as intercultural learning, language and culture diversity, nature as the foundation of the human life and the importance of nourishment as health prophylaxis, justifying thus the reasons why this project should exist.
Thirty primary school pupils and four teachers from the Croatian primary school in Makarska and thirty primary school pupils and four teachers from the Lower Austrian NMS primary school in Hollabrunn took part in the project. The project coordinator from Austria had already carried out a Commenius – school project and the partner from Croatia had rich knowledge of nourishment and ecology. The project aim was to publish a recipe book of Lower Austria and Dalmatia regions, including plenty of recipes for special regional meals, home and health necessities and biocosmetics. The idea that stood in the focus of the project was the creation of new meals, characterized by the mixture of the typical Austrian and Croatian cuisine. Our plan was to translate the recipe book into all languages the pupils learn, that was into German, Croatian, English, French and Italian, making the recipe book accessible to general public. What we had in mind were Web pages and booklets. Furthermore, the plan was to make a school garden at the NMS school in Hollabrunn, and the awarded garden at the primary school in Makarska needed redecorating. The project participants took care of the school snack-bar once a week supplementing it by bioproducts from the school garden.
The foundation of “Biopoint“, an informative corner designated for the development of consciousness on healthy diet, also served the needs of the project documentation. By means of involving experts, pupils acquired even more exact and more meaningful knowledge and were informed in the field of “Healthy food and healthy way of life” in the best possible way. The cooperation with the following people was planned: a nutritionist, a pharmacist, a health food producer, a garden designer, oil refinery owners…
One very important event for the pupils was a mutual visit to the partner school. Within a one-week stay, the pupils visited together the sights of their partner's region. Staying at the hosts’ families enabled direct intercultural exchange. The project had a positive feedback on all the pupils. 
The pupils gained many new experiences which related to team work, knowledge, and practical exercises. Furthermore, the focal point of our interest was a conscious, intensive engagement in food, the environment and nature. This mutual work was very important for the pupils, because it affected their further life in a more intensive and persevering way. Healthy diet and the choice of organic fruit and vegetables were important aspects, which are preconditions for a long and healthy life. Teachers, parents and involved experts were surrounded by highly motivated pupils, who were whole-heartedly and enthusiastically working on the project.
The representatives of the municipalities, tourist boards, school agencies, counties, journalists were informed of this project, followed its developmental stages and in that way found out how a "Different School" could develop with enthusiasm and a new, innovative approach to learning. The embassies of both countries were the bearers of advertising. By doing so, the results of the project were available and others were able to implement them. The head teachers of the partner schools and the people in charge of the project undertook to keep the school gardens in good condition and to use products further in their teaching. Thus, the book of recipes was much in demand. The whole project was documented on e-Twinning, hence readily and easily accessible to the public for at least 5 years. The album with the photos showing the process of creating and redoing the school gardens of the project partners could be lent to school and public libraries.

2014-1-CZ01-KA201-001715.title: “IT OR NOT IT?” REACHING OUR GOALS EQUIPPED WITH MODERN TOOLS
2014-1-CZ01-KA201-001715.summary:
We are five schools from different parts of Europe (Czech Republic, Poland, Cyprus, Croatia and Spain) drawn together around a common problem that we are experiencing in our schools - low student motivation and lesson participation, their decreasing capability for effective learning and declining responsibility for their lives and studies. Our schools are fairly well equipped with digital technologies, but they are not being used to their full potential and students are bored with conventional and traditional lessons. In view of these facts we have decided to join our experience and work collaboratively to find fresh and innovative solutions to these problems. 

Our aim is to enhance the impact of modern ICT tools on the learning process and develop students´ social skills. We want to transform the learning/ teaching process into something more enticing with the use of multiple and varied digital tools, materials and approaches which will be developed through different activities of the project. We will assist students´ active participation in discovering more effective and enjoyable learning methods through collaborative project work and cooperation. Further, motivate them to participate in the wider society by developing their social skills and encourage them to be more active in achieving their personal goals in life. We as teachers aim to find innovative and effective teaching tools that we will be able to integrate into lessons.  

The name of the project, “IT or not IT?”-  Reaching our goals equipped with modern tools, highlights our main goal: to enhance the impact of modern technologies on students learning and social skills development. All activities of the project are focused around these 5 key goals:
1. Knowing others better - knowing myself better
2. Effective, enjoyable, collaborative learning 
3. Developing our interests using ICT-based tools 
4. “Back to the future” - investigating how ICT has changed our live and how it influences our future.
5. My digital country – My digital Europe 

Student teams will prepare presentations pertaining to each one of the goals using different ICT tools. The usefulness and practicality of ICT tools used will be assessed and evaluated though questionnaires, oral/ written feed-back, blogs, diaries and open discussions. The new software with documentations and evaluation will be added to the “bank of ICT tools” on the project website. Regular evaluation and monitoring of goal achievement and task fulfilment will be done by country coordinators. 

Social skills activities will be developed through local and international student groups that will cooperate and communicate through blogs/ vlogs and social media. During school visits students will participate in different workshops, social and free-time activities incorporating ICT tools. Learning will take place inside and outside the classroom in the wider community. The activities will help students develop language and communication skills, problem/conflict solving, team work, behaviour in diverse situations and awareness of European diversity. 

The results of the project activities are first of all increased ICT, social and language competencies of students and teachers. Each individual participant will reflect on his/her own style of learning, working and communication with others. Development of social skills will help improve student social involvement and cooperation. Participants will become open to new ideas, and gain a better knowledge of other cultures, lifestyle and education of partners.

The project will impact students and teachers enrich their learning/ teaching with new activities, new methods of acquiring knowledge, but also improve their social involvement and cooperation which will contribute to creating a better school environment.  They will gain more confidence in using ICT tools and share their experience and gained knowledge with others through various means.

The physical outcome of the project will be the “bank of ICT tools” presenting practically explored tools, the website presenting all stages of the project, the DVD recordings of the main activities and the samples of the results attained with several ICT tools, devices and applications. The availability of the material for future use and reference will make the effect more enduring and will inspire more schools to put importance on involving the ICT-based methods in social and personal skills development. Results will be disseminated to relevant target groups.

Each partner school will have a project coordinator responsible for management of the project. They will distribute tasks and responsibilities to their school project teams and will monitor the accomplishment of all activities. Our team has all the expertise necessary to carry out this project, linguistic skills, ICT knowledge, good interpersonal skills and a team spirit, our work thus far has been well organised to achieve putting this application together.
topics: Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2014-1-DE03-KA201-001363.title: Plastic-S-kills - Die Plastiktüte zwischen Kult und Katastrophe
2014-1-DE03-KA201-001363.summary:
The project "Plastic(s)kills" is neatly connected to slowenian EU- commissioners Janez Potocnik initiative of incentivating the legal possibilities towards a prohibition of plastic bags in the EU member states. The title of the project refers to the claim of forbidding plastic bags in accordance with its motto "plastic kills", while it also indicates the technical and intellectual "skills" to be developed during the project. These are determined in artistic and creative fields ("plastic arts", exhibitions) in the promotion of media skills (research, internet, web- design, event organization, public relation, etc.)  and in the area of knowledge on the topic of "plastic waste" (research and reading skills) caused by plastic bags. Furthermore the project intends to improve the language skills of the participants (communication with native speakers).
The aim of the project is to promote public awareness and evoke a change of consumers behaviour concerning the use of plastic bags. The target groups are pupils, school communities, primary schools and the local and national societies.
The primary product is an exhibition of 10-15 informative panels dedicated to the desasterous effects on the environment caused by using plastic bags but also on the history, esthetic aspects, production and the significance of plastic bags for industry and commerce. This exhibition will be produced in different languages to be employed in each of the partner countries. The inauguration of the exhibition during the last meeting will be supported by a cultural and informative fringe event. This event contains a round table discussion with participants of the industry, politicians and ecological activists/organizations, a fashion show, an exhibition of plastic bags, fotos, a documentary movie on the project. All other activities of the project, which are realized in four meetings and the time between those meetings, lead to this final event and its primary product.  They are based on two aspects:
First the research on all aspects (industrial, commercial, environmental, artistical) of the plastic bag and the production of informative material and texts and secondly the realization of events and activities to inform and include the target groups concerning a more responsable use of the plastic bag and to support a possible prohibition in the member states.
The project aims to increase the ecological conscience of its participants and their target groups and incentivate in particular the interest and personal engagement of pupils whiche oppose to classical forms of learning.
The practical, actual and realistic topic as well as the teaching methods (pupils as environmental experts, pupils as activists, pupils as event organizers, pupils as PR- managers) promises a high level of personal envolvement. The teachers role also changes to that of an assistant and organizer and sometimes observer. The pupils from Germany, Hungary, Slovenia, Czech Repuplic, Turkey and Croatia share one mission, that of changing the consumers attitude of using too many plastic bags and to support the EU initiative of Janez Potocnik. By doing that they will overcome intercultural differences and strengthen their european identity.
topics: Reaching the policy level/dialogue with decision makers

2014-1-DE03-KA201-001573.title: Preventing Early School Leaving Through Inclusive Strategies
2014-1-DE03-KA201-001573.summary:
In Europe 5.5 million young people quit school before they have completed the upper secondary education. In Romania the rate of early school leaving (ESL) is 18% (2012) and in Turkey it is about 44%, the average rate in the EU is 12.4%. The risk of ESL is especially high for disadvantaged minorities, including Roma. 9% of the Roma in Romania (aged 18-30) complete high school (compared to 41% of other groups). Moreover young people from a migrant background often display a higher than average rate of ESL.
In its conclusions on a strategic framework for European cooperation in education and training (‘ET 2020’) the Council agreed that, by 2020, the share of early leavers from education and training should be less than 10 %. The PEARLS Project – Preventing Early School Leaving Through Inclusive Strategies – contributes to this objective.
An improvement of the situation will be reached by two ways:
1. The project partners will develop a further training for teachers. Teachers will deepen their key competences with regard to handling the diversity among pupils in their classes – in order to commit to the promotion of learning of all students. Units about collaborative teaching, like team teaching will be applied in this context (see Recommendations of the Council, June 2011, 2011/C 191/01).
2. By means of a comprehensive empirical needs analysis at the beginning of the project, it has been explored, which systemic support frameworks need to be implemented in order to reduce the rate of ESL, i.e. mentor programmes, homework clubs, extra-curricular activities to enhance pupil’s self-esteem, parents cafés etc. The objective is, to develop schools into learning environments, viz. external stakeholders (parents, representatives of minorities, enterprises etc.) are being involved into the sphere of school in order to promote the intellectual and emotional development of pupils at risk of ESL. A working group on ESL, which comprised experts nominated by 31 European countries, recommends such measures, since they are considered to be very effective.
The PEARLS further training also entails a module with regard to “school as learning environment”, so that participants can implement basic offers at their schools. They were qualified as multipliers, in this way PEARLS outcomes has a substantial impact in several European regions. Participants successfully took part in the course and they received the EUROPASS certificate (more info on the course: https://www.pearls-erasmus.eu).
The results and activities of the PEARLS project were developed in transnational teams, they were tested, evaluated and some of the modified.

Project partners are:
Elementary schools in Budapest (Hungary), Iasi (Romania) and Edirne (Turkey) and six so called hot spot schools in Berlin, as associative partners. All schools comprise a disproportionate share of pupils who derive from weak socio-economic backgrounds. The Turkish school exclusively has Roma pupils. The Romanian NGO “Gipsy Eye” and the Hungarian Foundation “Artemisszio” have been engaged for years in the field of teacher training, i.e. antidiscriminatory pedagogy.
Applicant is the unit Civic Education of the Leibniz University in Hannover, which educates students to become teachers. It is responsible for the didactic-methodical implementation of the teacher training course. It will be supported by the Humanistic Association Germany. The Teacher Training Agency in Zagreb is responsible for the development of curricula in general education in Croatia, it will ensure, that the PEARLS results will be implemented in national curricula.
The PEARLS project partnership comprises 9 partners from 5 countries. 
Results:
- 1 week teacher training course; EUROPASS certificate
- PEARLS toolkit, OER and handbook in five languages; hands-on approaches, topics: children’s rights, diversity in class as a resource
- PEARLS website in six languages (hu, ru, turk, ger, en, cro) – all products as OER
Impact:
Extensive public relation activities, using diverse channels to reach the end-users: teachers, teacher trainees and pedagogues, educational authorities as well as the interested public. Thus the PEARLS results will be available for 10.000s of European teachers. Moreover it is envisaged, through national conferences with policy makers, to insert the PEARLS approaches into national curricula of teacher (further) trainings. As such structural changes will be initiated, more inclusive schools will be established and in the long run the ESL rate will decrease.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2014-1-DE03-KA201-001618.title: HOBOS Beebox
2014-1-DE03-KA201-001618.summary:
In 2006, HOBOS was founded at the Julius-Maximilians-University of Wurzburg. A single beehive with a great many sensors and a value of several hundred thousand Euros was at the heart of the interactive concept of HOney Bee Online Studies. It was the aim of “HoBeebox” to design a simplified and lower-cost “eHive”, a small number of which were to be produced and installed in schools all over Europe creating an eHive network with access to all data collected. Being quite literally closer them, the object of study becomes easier accessible to the students and triggers more interest in them than a beehive in remote Wurzburg.

The participants of a practical seminar at Deutschhaus Grammar School in Wurzburg constructed the eHive prototype. Thirteen eHives were set up and populated with bee colonies in eight European countries. After finishing school, the team, which were to become BeeBIT e.V., installed more powerful circuit boards and developed the eHive into a commercial product. They have already managed to sell more eHives thus broadening the network. All data collected on the behaviour of bees and the environment are sent to and stored on the BeeBIT servers. The BeeBIT interface on www.beebit.de allows retrieving all or filtered data as spreadsheets or graphs.

This project also developed learning units, presentations and videos that use eHive data. The learning materials are designed for STEM as well as interdisciplinary classes and were tested and evaluated by partner schools in Germany, Austria, Italy, Croatia, Sweden, Poland and Slovenia. On careful consideration of national curricula, selected units were translated into the respective languages. In addition, the German and English versions were used for CLIL. All products of this project are available for free online in BeeBIT’s learning managing system; everyone has access to all learning materials, teaching resources become available to teachers upon registration. Links to BeeBIT on the Science on Stage Europe platform facilitate and enhance international dissemination.

All participants in the project were coordinated by the non-profit organisation “europafels”, which, for more than ten years, has built European-wide networks for educational institutions and provided high-quality teacher training on an international platform. To ensure a long-term effect of the project outputs, an eHive teaching unit is made available through School Education Gateway and also by the “German Department of Education Bozen”. Moreover, an ECTS-Moodle course has become an essential part of the teacher training program at the Ludwig-Maximilians-University of Munich. Other teaching assignments are being discussed. Some project results will be published in a pedagogical journal. The success of the project – even surpassing predefined goals and expectations – was made possible by the high level of commitment, often on a voluntary basis, of all participants.

On BeeBIT’s website, real-life observation and electronic information technology unite to create new forms of smart-object-based teaching potentials that are fully accessible to everyone. The eHive learning materials promote thinking beyond disciplinary boundaries and enhance both students’ independence and intercultural competence: Mirroring the complexity of the data, they are designed to create tasks which transcend simple fauna observation (e.g. mathematical temperature analysis, geographical climate studies) to not only deepen comprehension of ecological correlations within the differentiated living spaces [biotopes] of Europe but also encourage hands-on approaches: from playfully investigating the honeybee in kindergarten to carrying out complex chemical analyses of honey on the secondary level. Using foreign-language materials, learners broaden their understanding of the foreign language. Beehive installation and maintenance increase students’ as well as teachers’ practical, digital and organisational skills and their sense of responsibility. The hands-on design of the teaching resources motivates students with learning disabilities. The project brings scientific thinking and research skills into the school thus reducing, especially for educationally marginalised students, barriers to STEM-based educational and professional fields. It is these academically disadvantaged students that strategies of curriculum development focus on in particular. In a new project, europafels and BeeBIT plan to not only contribute to broadening access to education across all levels of society but also to take the next step in standardising STEM qualifications and mobility across Europe by translating the brand-new Common European Framework of Reference for STEM subjects into practice.

2014-1-EE01-KA201-000453.title: Inspiring studies and future careers
2014-1-EE01-KA201-000453.summary:
The project Inspiring Studies and Future Careers grew out of the recognition that for many pupils the border between school and outside-of-school-life exists very clearly. Youngsters do not understand why they need everything they have to learn. This leads to losing motivation and early school leaving. We believe that motivation is the key factor and it can be achieved through inspiring studies and improving the attainment of young people. Upgrading skills for employability helps to fight poverty and social exclusion. Young people should be entrepreneurial and able to adapt to the changes in the labour market.

With the help of this project we wanted our pupils to think and learn more about how knowledge and skills learned at school can help them in life. Five partner schools worked together: the coordinator Kääpa Kool (Estonia), Vaalan Yhtenäiskoulu (Finland), Friedrich-Spee-Gesamtschule Paderborn (Germany), Osnovna Skola Zaprudje (Croatia) and IES Sabina Mora (Spain). 

The project activities were both international and local including three short-term learning activities, five transnational meetings and tens of local in- and out-of-school events in every country  (web page: ka2inspiringstudies.wixsite.com/erasmus and Padlet: padlet.com/mpuskaric/ErasmusNews)

The project supported an innovative approach to teaching and learning process throughout comparison of educational realities in partner countries. Besides regular lessons non-formal and informal learning are effective instruments for making learning attractive.
Cooperation with different institutions, non-governmental organizations as well as companies has been established in every country. We have prepared lots of special events like Career Days, Science Night, robotics exhibitions and workshops, Code Week, Safer Internet Day, performances in the Technical Museum Nikola Tesla about him as well as about other famous persons from our partner countries. We have organized visits to secondary schools and companies, museums, science centres, universities etc to inform our students of different possibilities on their educational ladder. We had job shadowing days, practical training in companies at home and abroad, STEM workshops and days, fairs (selling self-made goods and products from partner countries), school Olympic Games and other events where pupils got practical entrepreneurial experiences. They helped to organise activities being responsible for the results and taking leadership. School teams worked together to create activities for connecting school subjects with work life. As a result pupils have improved their ability to take initiative, think critically, solve problems and work collaboratively. 

To promote diversity as a cultural wealth of Europe we celebrations - European Day of Languages, school exhibitions - “Strolling Through Europe”, National Costume Design Workshop, creation of digital Christmas cards, lessons guided by pupils about partner countries, celebrations of national holidays with songs and dances from partner countries etc.
The overall impact of the project on partner schools was very positive and it has longer-term benefits. Most objectives were achieved but there is still a lot to do in this field. The project was focused on inspiring young people in their studies and motivate them to think about their future careers.  All partner schools consider the promotion of entrepreneurship and improving the co-operation between education and work life important. We pursue that all our pupils are motivated to finish school and to go on studying to get a job. Teachers have become more confident about using ICT and improved their teaching skills of key competencies. They know more about diversity and inclusion and how to meet the needs of disadvantaged learners but also the gifted ones.

In schools the skills are taught in a wider variety of in-school and outside-of-school settings. Both teachers and pupils have improved their foreign language and cooperation skills as well as understanding of other nations and cultures in Europe. The pupil - centred pedagogical approaches are sustainable and enrich the school life of partner schools after the end of the project. As a result of the project there will be KA1 job shadowing projects e.g. GER will send a teacher to FIN to learn more about the use of tablets and ESP will send a teacher to GER to learn more about technology lessons. Every school has learned something from partners. We go on with career days, job shadowing, STEM days and workshops, secondary schools and company visits. Our intention is to implement successful models we saw in the partner countries into our own school and educational system.
Connections between partner school are strong – our new three-year strategic partnership with the same partners and one more from Hungary is approved by the EU and we are continuing our cooperation. One project can not change the world but long-term partnerships are a way to improvement.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
Preventing early school leaving and failure in education
