2018-1-UK01-KA201-047872.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder – Empowering and Supporting Teachers
2018-1-UK01-KA201-047872.summary:
CONTEXT/BACKGROUND OF PROJECT/OBJECTIVES
 Autism spectrum disorder (autism) affects about 1 in every 100, and impacts all aspects of the individual’s experience, including how they learn. Children and young people with autism share common education needs with all other children, and are entitled to a high quality education. However, they have specific, special needs resulting from the characteristic difficulties in autism regarding communication, social understanding, inflexibility and sensory processing. Education has been identified as the key area of intervention for those with autism, and meaningful access to effective education is crucial. 
 
 Teachers need a range of skills and strategies to meet the needs of these learners, and providing effective education has been identified as challenging throughout Europe, and in Central & Eastern Europe and the Balkans  in particular. Work undertaken by project partners in previous and current strategic partnerships has identified areas of good practice and training/development needs. This partnership focuses on developing appropriate training to support effective teaching, to ensure the inclusion of learners with autism in Croatia, the FYR of Macedonia and Poland.
 
 OBJECTIVES
 - To map current good practice and areas needing development with regard to the educational inclusion of children with autism in Croatia, the FYR of Macedonia and Poland.
 - To develop a model training programme and materials for specialist teachers, providing them with skills to  effectively support the educational inclusion of children and young people with autism in these countries.
 - To use these materials to pilot the programme to specialist teachers from the range of educational settings in Croatia, the FYR of Macedonia and Poland.
 - To evaluate the appropriateness and effectiveness of the materials and the impact of the training using quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis.
 • To share the programme, tools and materials with stakeholders and make recommendations to national policy-makers in these countries, and more broadly across Central/Eastern Europe and the Balkans and Europe as a whole.
 
 NUMBER/PROFILE OF PARTICIPANTS
 A minimum of approximately 3000 persons will benefit from/be the target of the project’s activities during its 2-year lifetime. It is expected that this number will increase greatly in the years following the project as a result of the exploitation of the materials. These will include specialist teachers, individuals with autism and their families, professionals and policymakers.
 
 ACTIVITIES
 a) Initial mapping exercise, including survey of specialist teachers
 b) Development of curriculum/programme
 c) Testing of materials through provision of training
 d) Evaluation
 e) Revision/finalisation of programme
 f) Dissemination
 
 METHODOLOGY
 The project undertaken by this strategic partnership will utilise a collaborative, action-based methodology, and will be evaluated using a mixed-methods, evidence-based programme evaluation approach to data collection and analysis. This methodology has been designed to meaningfully identify impact and to realise practical and practicable ‘real world’ outcomes.
 
 RESULTS ENVISAGED AND BENEFITS
 This project will produce a model training programme designed to meet the needs of specialist educators supporting the educational inclusion of children with autism, locally adapted to meet the needs of three diverse Central/Eastern European/Balkan countries. 
 
 The final programme and materials will be made available via the Erasmus+ dissemination platform, as well as via individual partners’ and the project websites.
 
 Supporting teachers in these countries to understand autism and effective evidence-based approaches and strategies to effectively include children and young people with autism in education will have significant benefits with regard to educational and social inclusion, educational achievement, equality of opportunity and teachers’ professional competence. 
 
 As such, this project will contribute to the development of a more equitable and inclusive Europe in the short, medium and longer terms.

2018-1-UK01-KA201-047940.title: Science Outside the Classroom
2018-1-UK01-KA201-047940.summary:
The Science Outside the Classroom Project engaged 750 learners aged 3-11 years, from the EHPS (140) , WFPS (120) ,Spain (300) , Sweden (80) and Croatia (110) and included children of differing abilities including children with Special Educational Needs and Severe Learning Difficulties. The adults participating included Senior Leaders , Subject Leaders , Teachers at all levels, Outdoor Learning Leads, Teaching Assistants and University Professors .

The project deliberately focused on developing the skills of scientific enquiry outside a typical classroom with regular opportunities to experience teaching and learning in a rich and stimulating outdoor environment which can offer a wide range of benefits to young and older children. Learning Science outside the classroom offered children high quality Science teaching and learning alongside opportunities for physical activity, freedom and movement and promoting a sense of well-being. 

Scientific Enquiry increases children’s capacity to problem-solve and answer questions, work with independence and communicate. Effective thinking and reasoning  would be nurtured alongside qualities such as resilience, determination and confidence. It would focus on the acquisition of skills and key competencies , all useful to society , while addressing underachievement in Science . The outdoor environment is a precious – yet often largely under-valued – resource when nurturing such skills. This was something the project could address.

Our children were highly motivated by the experiential and hands-on opportunities SOtC afforded and the opportunities to adapt science-based lessons were seized by practitioners. . Not only did the children foster a greater appreciation and fondness for the world around them and a sense of responsibility for it too - but outdoor lessons displayed more focused and contextualised teaching and learning which made the learning and understanding the world more relevant.

Training and evaluation tools were provided by the University of Northampton and school to school expertise was shared through three Transnational Meetings and four Learning/Teaching/ Training events. These included training and workshop activities( face to face and virtual ) and visits to our Partner Schools. Transnational meetings , joint training and visits enabled the exchange of good practices between partners with diverse outdoor learning possibilities and experiences and from countries with different curricula expectations and accountability. In this way, we strengthened the profile of the teaching profession , enhanced teachers professional development through collaborative and innovative practices. Intellectual Outputs included resources that can inspire teachers to put aside textbooks in order to deliver high quality learning and teaching in Science outside the confines of the classroom walls.  The  university led training and research added value and weight to both the resources and to the proof of project impact.

The project was Inclusive and purposefully included children with varied levels of SEN in mainstream classes and children with Severe and Significant Learning Difficulties within a Specialist Unit which is part of East Hunsbury Primary School. Its practical nature and careful planning for children allowed us to cater for a range of learning styles and provide opportunities for pupils to actively engage in hands on experiences. Lesson plans were skillfully adapted to meet the diverse learning needs of all children. Levels of engagement and raised attainment was evidenced amongst all participating pupils including the disaffected and those with disabilities and learning difficulties.

The Science Outside the Classroom Project (SOtC) promoted the acquisition of basic and transferable skills and key competences, while addressing under achievement in science through effective and innovative teaching. Through Scientific enquiry, children engaged in a wide range of collaborative investigative tasks, which allowed them to develop important skills to become creative, inventive and hopefully future enterprising adults in a world where the skills and knowledge of the sciences are needed across all sectors of the economy.

The Project Partners communicated regularly ensuring that the project could continue throughout the pandemic . Intellectual outputs were co -created by Project Partners . A Project Website , Teaching Manual , Photobook , Pictionary and Research Paper have all been completed to the very highest standard. Faced with the obstacles of the pandemic, our focus was to ensure our resources were high quality outcomes. The Multiplier Event took place on line due to the Pandemic, but in turn this allowed us to reach 131 participants beyond the four countries involved as participants. The project resources have the potential to transform Science teaching and will be an invaluable support for other practitioners in our schools and beyond.

2018-1-UK01-KA201-048271.title: Expanding the use of the 'Gender Equality Charter Mark for Schools' across Europe
2018-1-UK01-KA201-048271.summary:
Gender inequality is a major concern for early 21st century society. Socially and culturally, we are at a point where gender issues are becoming ever more prominent in social life, both in their potential harm to individuals and society, but also in the need for innovative approaches and solutions. This strategic partnership sees the education sector as a key area regarding gender equality. There is a ‘hidden curriculum’ that is restricting life choices and fuelling sexual harassment. Working to change the school environment will respond to the current need. 
Research shows that Charter Marks used to develop whole-school approaches help to ensure momentum and sustain change, and schools find this approach useful where issues are complex and need support from the whole school community. Members of our strategic partnership have previously created, tried and tested Gender Equality Charter Mark (GECM) tools for secondary schools for three EU countries as part of a previous EU funded project. This GECM is a ‘whole-school approach’ to equip schools to build environments that enable children to critically engage with and make sense of a range of complex issues associated with gender equality. The GECM enables a school to show measurable change and progress in five key areas of school life: leadership, curriculum, physical environment, attitudes and relationships, and the wider community.
The project’s main objective was to expand the use of the GECM tool across Europe. Three ‘expert’ partner organisations within the strategic partnership with expertise in creating the original GECMs supported six ‘new’ partner organisations to adapt the Europe-wide GECM template to create country-specific GECMs and accreditation procedures. Once produced, the GECM tool was introduced to teachers, school leaders and educators in each project country, through training sessions and workshops, building momentum for schools to begin the longer term process of whole-school change regarding gender inequality.
At the conclusion of this project there are country specific Gender Equality Charter Mark tools and accreditation processes fit for purpose, for schools of all ages from 3 – 18 year olds, for Austria, Croatia, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Poland, Slovakia, UK, and a Europe-wide GECM template for other countries to work with. The tools are located here: https://genderequalityinschools.org. There is a country-specific handbook for how to implement the GECM and a handbook of gender equality support materials.
The project has also produced:
Country specific Teacher Professional Development modules (IO5), in total delivered to 438 teachers.
Country specific Initial Teacher Education modules (IO6), in total delivered to 763 trainee students.
Country specific Train the Trainer modules to be used to ensure individual representatives (Trainers) have the knowledge and skills to be able to introduce the GECMs to schools and support a school individually in their journey to achieving the Gender Equality Charter Mark.
Over 1500 schools have been made aware of and interacted with the GECM tools. This will have had some short term and perceived longer term benefits to school pupils in anywhere between one class per school (e.g. 45,000) and whole schools (over 800,000) through changing approaches to school leadership, the curriculum, physical environment, and the attitudes and relationships of both the students, staff and wider community in relation to gender equality issues. 

The Gender Equality in Schools website encourages schools and teachers across Europe to share good practice of how the GECM can be instilled effectively. We are encouraging the formation of a network of GECM schools across international borders that can provide substantial and lasting change due to the way that the GECM is integrated into school policy and ethos. As a result of this we hope to foster and encourage positive change in the approach to gender equality, and develop a culture where children engage their critical thinking skills to understand, question and challenge gender inequality and violence.

2019-1-CY01-KA201-058436.title: Living Opportunities for Our Planet
2019-1-CY01-KA201-058436.summary:
<< Background >>

Following the adoption of the Circular Economy Action Plan in 2015, the EU has promoted measures to stimulate the transition towards a circular economy. The adoption of the circular model may be an effective strategy to break the spiral of inefficiencies that seriously damages the natural, economic and social equilibriums of today’s world. In order to overcome the linear economy model in Europe (and beyond), it is necessary to adopt a re-education strategy in the context of a new economic model, where the axis buy-use-dispose-buy-again is disrupted. The new model needs to be transmitted to children and young people and, most importantly, should be included in European school plans. Therefore, the LOOP project aim was to give students the opportunity to improve their linguistic, technological and scientific knowledge on circular economy, while to teachers it was given the opportunity to dispose of innovative teaching methodologies and key competences on the 4 “Rs” of circular economy (Re-use, Reduce, Recycle, Redesign).

<< Objectives >>

The LOOP project intended to transfer knowledge and competences concerning sustainable development and in particular to current scientific debates around the issues of Circular Economy and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The project aimed to, on the one hand, provide students with scientific knowledge and the skills to understand current global issues related to sustainable development. On the other hand, it intended to also stimulate students in learning, developing and sharing conscious behaviours, while improving their digital skills. The project involved the participation of teachers, students and tutors in the project activities. In particular, the project involved 124 students from 4 schools in 3 EU countries (Cyprus, Croatia and Italy) and 17 teachers. To reach its goals, the project supported and guided students in the development of a number of activities and outputs under the guidance of appropriately trained teachers and tutors and through the project Platform. The activities were based on innovative digital technologies specifically designed to stimulate the inclusion of participants and encourage the learning of the relevant project topics and their basic values.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented the following activities:
IO1 – Online Platform: development of project Platform, core element of the activities;
IO2 – Teachers Training Materials and Web-events: teachers followed a specific training process in order to better support students in the subsequent activities;
IO3 – Elevator Pitch: students had to present themselves (in English) in a 60 seconds video message, which have then been published on the Platform;
IO4 – Students Training and Flipped Classroom: students followed a specific training process in order to consolidate their knowledge on the project topics; then, they had to demonstrate what they have learnt to their classmates through some specific activities in class (Flipped Classroom methodology);
IO5 – Field Research: students worked in national groups and they had to produced digital e-books on a specific topic of the project, through the use of interviews and self-study methods. 
IO6 – Transnational Researches: students worked in transnational groups and had to produced thematic projects (called “microsites”) composed by video teasers, written narrative proposals and interviews.

<< Results >>

The concrete outputs and results achieved by the project are: 
IO1 - Online Platform
IO2 - Teachers Training Material and Web-events: 4 Webinar Masterclasses; 8 Interactive video lessons; 4 written articles; 4 Meeting recordings between partners; “E-Learning guide for the teachers”, an operational guide on the Platform’s features.
IO3 - Elevator Pitch: a 60 seconds video message for each student in which they presented themselves. 
IO4 - Students Training and Flipped Classroom: 4 guidelines (pdf documents); a webinar recording; a list of helpful links for students’ self-study; a Methodological and content report in digital format concerning the main and most relevant results of the performances conducted by students in the classroom; pictures taken during class activities. 
IO5 - Field Research: students created e-books, digital pdf documents in which they investigated the 4 “R’s” of the circular economy. Also, teachers realized a report in which they expressed their view concerning the overall education process.
IO6 - Transnational Researches: transnational groups of students produced thematic projects (or “microsites”) composed of different elements: video teasers, written narrative proposals and interviews.

2019-1-DE03-KA201-059798.title: European values for new generations - Living democracy in schools
2019-1-DE03-KA201-059798.summary:
<< Background >>

The 21st century is marked by an increasingly accelerating transition that affects all areas of social life: living and working together beyond local and national borders. 
These changes unsettle many people and cause social division in many areas: openness and pluralism vs. retreat to cultural identities, respect for otherness vs. discrimination, up to violence and extremism. The technological revolution is changing the world of work in particular: work profile, workplace as well as professions are undergoing massive change.
The partners were aware that all these transformations have and will have an impact on education and especially on education for a democratic culture. 
They see school as an area of living, learning and education that must face these challenges and enable young people to become active, democratic citizens in their society. The partners asked themselves how they could learn from each other's practices and pedagogical approaches to support teachers and schools in this transformative educational process.

<< Objectives >>

The general aim of the project was to share and compare with the partners from Croatia, Finland, Germany, Poland and Spain their pedagogical practices and approaches in the field of pupil participation and representation. Whereby the focus should be on teachers' competences, their students' preparation for their life as active, democratic citizens as well as future actors in the European labour market.
In order to achieve this goal, teachers and trainers should reflect together in workshops on what they have observed, deal intensively with questions of democracy building and tools should be developed for observation in schools and lessons in the partner countries. These were to be made accessible to all stakeholders in Europe via a project homepage.
Another important goal was to identify the need for teacher training on the basis of the analysis of what was observed and to communicate these results in regional round tables in order to achieve a broader understanding of the importance of democracy education. The aim of the project was to compare how schools in the partner countries manage to accompany young people on their way into a society full of new challenges as described above and to give them the opportunity to obtain the necessary knowledge and to develop action skills as well as democratic attitudes and values.

<< Implementation >>

Starting at the end of 2019, the project was overwhelmed by the pandemic and the resulting restrictions on contact and travel during its central observation and production phase. The partners adapted very quickly to the new situation and were able to implement the following activities:
1. development of the planned tools, (see below).
3. workshops: 5 workshops were planned, 1 in each partner country. Of these, only 3 could take place in person, one only online and one in hybrid form. 
4. 13 meetings of the Steering Group: online and presentational, 5 of these in connection with the workshops.
The regional round tables and the grid to be developed could not be held. This was due to the pandemic: the implementation of the online workshops was very time-consuming for all partners, and there were times when the partners were very busy converting both teaching and training to online formats in order to cope with the tasks. 
This overall situation and the burden of school closures or the implementation of online and alternate teaching in Germany made it very difficult for the partner school to answer the interview questions.

<< Results >>

1. a description of the current situation of democracy education in the partner countries
2. an observation sheet for the observation in class 
3. an evaluation matrix of these sheets
4. analysis of the observations in the partner countries
5. analysis of the interviews
6. a collection and documentation of practical examples from the schools
7. "Perspectives" - understanding democracy & listing needs for the teacher-in-service training
6. a project homepage: Information on partners, products
8. a concept for an online student conference with explanatory film
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-DK01-KA201-060288.title: A BETTER LIFE
2019-1-DK01-KA201-060288.summary:
<< Background >>

What we saw in classrooms and what we read in the Eurostats statistics, showed that there was a need to take action towards the risk of poverty, risk of social exclusion and risk of idleness. These elements were of great concern to us, and therefore this project was very important - to enlighten people and hopefully bring A Better Life into the classrooms. We formed the project in compliance with the EU Youth Strategy and the European Pillar of social rights.

It was our belief that we needed to support our young people, teach them their rights, give them the tools and motivate them into believing in themselves, so they would be able to stand stronger once in the labor market in the future.. We wanted to provide effective, sustainable and successful transitions of young people in Europe, to awaken awareness of their own satisfaction in life and to find some motivation for preventing early school leave, in order to get a meaningful life. 
We wanted to focus on social inclusion, to bring awareness to students, that no one should be left behind. And we wanted to give our results to other teachers around Europe - free of use.

The project had 4 important aspects: European citizenship, Inclusion, Health and Friendships across borders.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to build a European Education Area, supporting the implementation of the European strategic cooperation in the field of education and training. This would lead to synergies between schools and organisations from other fields and improve international strategies and management across borders.
Through mobilities we recognized other cultures which gave a greater understanding of social, ethnic, linguistic and cultural diversity in Europe. Also give a greater sense of European identity, so we could gain a positive attitude towards the European project and the EU values and Lifelong Learning.
We expanded participants' horizons and changed their perspective by meeting new people and cultures, by developing tolerance and empathy, and also to understand different minority groups in society.
We helped students interact with their environment and develop their creativity. They met a European dimension in teaching and learning and used ICT in numerous ways.
We gave students a chance to express themselves. We corrected misunderstandings and broke down prejudices. 
We helped students learn to collaborate and cooperate. We listened to and accepted the points of view. 
We created an opportunity to use and improve the English language.

<< Implementation >>

Activities we have implemented can be divided into 2 sections. One section was activities done at the learning/teaching/training events and another section was activities done in between the mobilities. 

Section 1 - at LTT’s:
Get-to-know-each other activities
Sports activities (games, swimming, hiking, biking..)
Give presentations
Workshops on the different topics with experts (some as lectures, some as creative)
Creating exhibitions: Traditional food, traditional medicine, portfolios
Quizzes
Debates
Cultural visits
Interviews, videos
Lectures

Section 2 - between mobilities
Meetings in project teams (preparing project activities at the LTT’s and project monitoring)
Prepare presentations
Writing articles
Creating the magazines
Creating and answering surveys on the topics and gather info on their results
Student talks

<< Results >>

Our main output was an OER website, which contains all of our results and includes tools for teachers in Europe to use. Here are 
- Lessonplans (created at each individual school)
- Articles (written by the students on the different topics, but also on Covid-19, as it has influenced the project a lot)
- Interviews (with teachers and students)
- Results on surveys (on the topics)
- vlogs (short films made by mobile devices)
- Art work 
- Filmmaking and stories

2) Three digital magazines with the relevant topics. The magazines were created mainly at each school, and not in international groups as planned. This was done as the pandemic caused difficulties for the Learning/teaching/training activities, so we decided that it was better to work at each school. But all schools contributed to each magazine.

3) Other results
Teachers found inspiration in each others' teaching tools and methods. 
A network of stakeholders has been built up by each partner
Some students improved their English language which could be measured at their exams
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2019-1-EL01-KA201-062886.title: Early Intervention Services for Families with Children with Vision Impairment and Additional Disabilities
2019-1-EL01-KA201-062886.summary:
<< Background >>

Children with vision impairment and additional disabilities (VIAD) or deafblindness (D/B) have unique needs and require adaptations on intervention strategies. Early intervention services (EISs) are vital for children's health, education and quality of life. It is evident from research and practice, that still this field of early intervention needs empowerment and enrichment regarding material, tools and expertise. 
The ErISFaVIA project concerns the training of professionals regarding EISs for children with VIAD or D/B. Early intervention services are demanding programs and can only be implemented by highly skilled and trained professionals. 
For this, the ErISFAVIA project aimed to respond to this need, by designing integrated early intervention programmes supervised by experts in this field. 
The ErISFAVIA  project aimed to address the needs of a. professionals, and b. children with VIAD and their parents orchestrating intensive on line and face-to-face training and learning events

<< Objectives >>

The ErISFaVIA project aimed to achieve the following objectives: a. to develop a training program for professionals working in early intervention settings, b. to create early intervention opportunities for children with VIAD or D/B, c. to promote the collaboration between universities, schools and associations of children with VIAD or D/B, and d. to point out the best practices and guidelines for the development of effective EISs for children with VIAD or D/B. Ten organizations (e.g. universities, NGOs, schools) were included in the ErISFaVIA project, consisting of researchers and practitioners of common interest and a unique combination of skills and experience both within and outside the academic field on EISs and VIAD or D/B children's education, and shared the knowledge and experience to meet the above objectives.

<< Implementation >>

The activities of the ErISFaVIA project were distributed according to the intellectual outputs and the management and implementation of the project. In particular, the activities are described as follows:
a. designing and creating the program collaboration platform, b. literature review and needs assessment study, c. educational material and training events, d. reflective logs and questionnaires, e. collating case studies and elaborate relevant research data, f. best practices guide, g. dissemination and exploitation and h. policy recommendations and guidelines. The proposed methodology in the ErISFaVIA project was oriented at two levels, namely the local and the overall level. Regarding the item Project management and implementation, each beneficiary was responsible for the local management of its time and resources. The overall strategy of the ErISFaVIA project was based on a synthetic plan of activities to meet its goals. Two Intellectual outputs were translated also in German (i.e. IO5 & IO8) because it was felt that they will empower the exploitation of the project outcomes.

<< Results >>

2019-1-ES01-KA201-064237.title: "ACADAS"-Alliance for inClusive Acknowledgement of eDucational meritS
2019-1-ES01-KA201-064237.summary:
<< Background >>

ASPABER is an entity that provides services to people with intellectual disabilities in the province of A Coruña. Since 2017, it has had 2 educational units through which it has become aware of the barriers that these students have to reach the results in the different educational stages, and as a consequence, that their academic merits are not recognised. The same concern is shared by the other partners, which are, however, in different situations as their educational legislation has been developed differently.

The needs addressed have been:
The special incidence of ESL among people with disabilities (PWD) and the lack of detailed information on this phenomenon at EU level, as definitions of disability and early school leaving vary greatly from country to country.
To carry out an analysis of the dimensions of why education systems in the EU are not adapted to the needs of these groups in order to shift the burden of responsibility for ESL to the actors with competences in education, and to lay the foundations for the involvement of the educational community in measures to prevent ESL.

<< Objectives >>

The general objective of the project was to analyse and exchange good practices in prevention, intervention and monitoring of people with disabilities at particular risk of early school leaving (ESL), defining the main dimensions in which EU education systems are not adapted to the needs of these groups.

The project has three specific objectives: 
1) To analyse the incidence of ESL in PWD; 
2) To identify good practices in prevention (monitoring systems for students with disabilities and accreditation of educational achievements and intervention (appropriate curricular adaptations) that are carried out in the different member countries of the partnership and at all levels that affect the academic success of students with disabilities (policies, schools, family and environment and individual level) and, 
3) To share and compare ideas, practices and measures that are being applied to prevent ESL between partnership countries with a low rate of ESL and partnership countries with a high rate of ESL.

<< Implementation >>

The activities implemented have been grouped into 6 work groups (WT): 
WP1 of COORDINATION AND MANAGEMENT led by ASPABER, involving the rest of the partners in its management.
WP2 COMMUNICATION AND DISSEMINATION OF RESULTS led by EULABTec, who has set the guidelines in the communication carried out by all ACADAS partners.
WP3 EUROPEAN OBSERVATORY ON ESL AMONG STUDENTS WITH DISABILITIES, coordinated by NEU, who led the empirical data collection tasks among the rest of the partnership and was responsible for its interpretation. 
WP4 IMPACT OF POLICIES TO REDUCE esl, CERB has been in charge of leading the work for the elaboration of the catalogue of ESL monitoring and prevention systems with the collaboration of the rest of the partners.
WP5, TRAINING IN EARLY DETECTION AND MONITORING SYSTEMS FOR STUDENTS WITH DISABILITIES AT RISK OF ESL, whose responsibility fell on the School of Special Education St. Ita, which hosted the rest of ACADAS partners, being in charge of organising the transnational training.
WP6, on GOOD PRACTICE IN PREVENTING ESL AMONG STUDENTS WITH DISABILITIES, led by Pro-Mente Croatia with the contribution of the other partners.

<< Results >>

- 3 survey formats to analyse the special risks for PWDs in ESL, targeting different interest groups: families, professionals and students with disabilities; 
- a report on the dimensions and factors affecting the ESL of PWD;
- a catalogue of systems for monitoring and prevention of ESL in PWD at EU level, with special emphasis on the recognition of educational attainment and its accreditation; 
- a set of resources at European level to address intervention in ESL in PWD;
- a catalogue of good practices in monitoring and prevention of ESL in PWD at individual, school and setting level; 
- a roadmap addressed to policy makers with the necessary steps for the standardisation of educational attainment at EU level and the necessary partnerships to achieve it.
Other results obtained not covered in the initial form are:
- analysis of the different education policies of each partner country with special incidence of the LOMLOE as it was published during the project life cycle;
- a compact network of partners that served as a mutual support to share experiences and face the challenges arising from COVID-19 in the daily life of their schools.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-ES01-KA201-064265.title: Crossroads: best practices to empower youngers to continue their post compulsory education from an intersectional perspective
2019-1-ES01-KA201-064265.summary:
In the society of knowledge, life chances of people are increasingly conditioned to educational credentials. Accordingly, the OCDE and the European Commission identify the access and the end of elementary school as a way for social inclusion. However, early school leaving is a common problem in many European countries. Although the vast majority of European countries have implemented strategies to minimize leaving in elementary school, the changes seem not to be enough. Thus, an educational system thought to be inclusive and equative cannot allow the normalisation of today’s percentages of early school leaving.
In this context, the general aim of CROSSROADS project is to develop a Toolkit for teachers gathering innovative methodologies, strategies and good practices aimed at reducing early school leaving caused by the impact of the intersection of different axes of inequality (gender, origin, social class, ethnicity, sexuality…), in the period between Compulsory and Post-Compulsory Secondary Education.
The main activities of the project are: an Internal training (which will allow the partners to test methodologies and to exchange learnings and experiences); Focus Groups with Teachers and Focus Groups with Youth at risk of early school leaving (in which they will discuss the first draft of the Toolkit to guarantee that it takes into account their perspectives); the Exchange of Good Practices Seminar (which will include presentation of good practices, roundtables and field visits); and a Main Dissemination Activity (in Belgium) and National Dissemination Activities.
The main result of the project is the Toolkit for teachers, gathering innovative methodologies, strategies and good practices to prevent early school leaving, from an intersectional perspective and taking into account the voice and experience of youth at risk of early school leaving. The Toolkit will be available in the project and the partners’ websites and it will be published under a Creative Commons licence to promote its use and dissemination.    
CROSSROADS targets three types of participants. The first one is teaching staff committed to prevent early school leaving. They will participate in Focus Groups carried out in the four participating countries (Spain, Poland, Croatia and Belgium), apart from attending the Exchange of Good Practices Seminar and the dissemination activities (100 participants in total). The second target is youth at risk of early school leaving due to their position in the intersection of different axes of inequality (gender, class, origin, sexuality and urban/rural). This target will participate as well in Focus Groups carried out in each participating country and will be invited to participate in the Seminar and the dissemination activities (150 participants). The third target are other stakeholders committed to the prevention of early school leaving, like Public Administrations, NGOs, experts and Media. They will be invited to the Seminar and the dissemination activities (80 participants).
As a result of the project, teaching staff will have a Toolkit with innovative methodologies and best practices based on the experience of organizations working on the field and taking into account the voices of youth from groups at risk of early school leaving. Local and regional education authorities will have training material aimed at preventing early school leaving that they can disseminate to schools and Faculties of Education will be able to use the material in the training of future teaching staff.   
The main objective of the dissemination strategy of the project is to promote the distribution and use of these materials as much as possible, which will also be disseminated in international and national seminars held within the project framework, as well as in the distribution of newsletters and dissemination. Content on various social networks, such as Facebook, Twitter, Linkedin and mobile device applications.
The expected impact of the project in the long term is: to contribute to increase the visibility of the needs of different social groups at risk of early school leaving in the definition of specific methodologies for educational career guidance from an intersectional perspective; to increase the awareness and training of teaching staff regarding inequalities in education; to strengthen the transnational network of entities that are committed to prevent early school leaving; and to improve the knowledge and competences among teaching staff in European countries, through the dissemination of the Toolkit.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-ES01-KA201-064454.title: Arduino SYS-STEM for Schools
2019-1-ES01-KA201-064454.summary:
<< Background >>

The ARDUINO SYS-STEM for SCHOOLS project aims to attract more secondary school students (aged 14-18) into STEM related subjects and future careers by offering attractive, practical learning materials and projects for programming at the right level and wider access to arduino materials and technology. At present, in the EU there is a lack of well trained technical workers and SYS-STEM will help raising the interest in STEM related carees. The project specifically aimes to support teachers and students by creating ready to use attractive didactical materials in arduino including guidelines for establishing an ArdLAB should a school have the means to do so. In either case future users (schools and teachers anywhere) can enjoy the practical possibilities of a well equipped ArdLAB. Many secondary institutions who do not have trained electronics teachers or quality Arduino Labs. Integrating this technology into the curriculum is an opportunity to spread Electronics (STEM) in schools and encourage more young people to become involved in careers in electronics, automation and technology.

<< Objectives >>

-Greater awareness in STEM subjects.
-Improvements in the Quality of secondary education and future professionals. 
-Enhanced employability. 
- provide educators at school level with OPEN ACCESS to the best electronics arduino pedagogy, materials and facilities
- support general education schools and technology teachers establish their own ArdLAB should they have the means to do so
- through use of any of the SYS-STEM outputs, support educators enthuse and inspire general
education school students about electronics and cause them to positively consider STEM
occupations
- prepare young people for the growing opportunities in electronics in the future labour market
-The creation of synergies between different secondary education schools, not only the one created with the partners working in the project, but also with teacher that belong to other schools. 
-Support to STEM teachers. We offer them ready to use didactical material with practical exercices and the possibility to access real Arduino laboratories. With the workshops offered to teachers we have trained and upskilled secondary school teachers.

<< Implementation >>

- O1 - SYS-STEM Methodology
- O2 - SYS-STEM ArdLAB hub
- 3 face to fase Transnational project Meetings and 11 online meetings
- Creation of an internal Moodle platform
- Creation of dissemination and exploitation plan: logo, branding, newletters, facebook page... 
- Creation of the project website and the HUB platform
- Holding of C1 Trainint event in Crete
- Pilot of IO1 and IO2 results
- 20 hour workshops for teachers
- Fine tuning of IO1 and IO2 after the evaluation of the pilots
- Holding of face to face (whenever posible) and online Multiplier Events
- Evaluation of local and global project Impact
- Translation of the project to English, Portuguese, Greek, Spanish, Croatian and Basque
- Quality Assurance activities throughout the project lifetime.

<< Results >>

The Arduino SYS-STEM for Schools Methodology is a package of specific materials and projects for students aged 14-18 in Arduino that includes a structured step-by-step programme in electronics and programming development using Arduino.

Each Module includes all the necessary didactic planning tools and guidelines: learning outcomes that will be achieved, complete sets of materials and examples, simulations, sample exercises in Arduino for students, and solutions.

The SYS-STEM project partners have created 4 remote Arduino Laboratories (ArdLABs) not only for their students but for students from anywhere in the world. These laboratories allow remote access and a variety of STEM experiments without the need of having Arduino equipment available. Schools, Teachers and Students are invited to join-in and use these ArdLABs through the ArdLAB Hub.

For those schools, universities or organisations wishing to develop their own Arduino Labs and make them available to the world (should they wish to share their facilities with other schools and students), SYS-STEM partners have additionally developed an ArdLAB starter Guide to facilitate the process of development and registration of potential additional remote labs to the ArdLAB HUB.

2019-1-ES01-KA201-065362.title: Promoting inclusion to combat early school leaving (PICELS)
2019-1-ES01-KA201-065362.summary:
<< Background >>

Early school leaving (ESL) is a major concern within the European Union. One in seven young Europeans leaves the education system without the necessary skills for a successful transition to active life. In other words, currently, around 6.4 million young people in Europe are defined as early school dropouts. The fact that many young people opt to leave school too early increases the risk of being on unemployment and socially excluded. 
Although national policies and interventions in some countries have led to some decreases, the rates have been incrementally growing with the Covid-19 closing schools, confining families, and maintaining social distance, as well as students not being in school, becoming accustomed to alternative teaching methodologies requiring technological equipment and training will no doubt have placed a strain on already technologically depleted economies. The post-pandemic period has only exacerbated this challenge that affects both the lives of students and teachers, thus, making the need of this project more evident and urgent as teachers feel unprepared and demand practical tools to address this issue.
Despite the multiple variables that impact on ESL, PICESL focuses mainly on in-school factors.

<< Objectives >>

In the light of these figures and context, PICESL aimed to prevent ESL of pupils in situations at risk of social exclusion within European societies, as educational environments become more multicultural and fragmented. 
The SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES of PICESL were:
-	Mapp a selection of effective intercultural/inclusive practices to support vulnerable students and keep them in education until attaining at least an upper secondary education qualification. 
-	Validate a system of indicators to identify effective intercultural/inclusive practices.
-	Design and implement a systematic teacher training program that enables teachers to employ and further develop pedagogies that promote social inclusion and equity of school children at risk of ESL.
-	Disseminate a set of school practices across Europe, as well the system of indicators to help teachers diagnose their own practices.
PICESL is therefore consistent with the European and national contexts (social inclusion and addressing early dropouts from education and disadvantaged situations, strengthening the profiles of the teaching professions). Additionally, the project focus on the expansion and execution of education policies, and the transferability of country-specific good practices.

<< Implementation >>

Activities implemented included: 
Two INTELLECTUAL OUTPUTS:
(IO1) Practical toolkit for teachers on inspiring practices that prevent early school leaving in multicultural educational settings in Europe
(IO2) Course to prevent early school leaving in multicultural educational settings in Europe.
A hybrid LEARNING ACTIVITY (LA) aimed at training teachers and teacher training students in the use of both IOs and validating them for their eventual improvement. The LA focused on knowledge, attitudes, skills, and strategies to support vulnerable and behaviorally disengaged students in prevention of ESL by inspiring students’ interest in learning, boosting their sense of belonginess and building students’ self-esteem.
Two TRANSNATIONAL MEETINGS ™ (the first one and the last) were celebrated in person plus six more online TM.
A MULTIPLIER EVENT (Seville, 2022) where the partnership shared the two IOS to a large audience.

<< Results >>

TANGIBLE RESULTS were the IOs mentioned. 
INTANGIBLE RESULTS were: 
- Teachers updated their knowledge on intercultural/inclusive education and acquired practical tools for the prevention of ESL of disadvantaged students. 
- Teachers were better equipped to integrate an intercultural/inclusive approach into their practices.
- Network between schools, academics, the third sector and public administrations dealing with ESL.
- Awareness raised among political authorities of the need to enhance the professional development of teachers from an intercultural/inclusive perspective as a key element for the prevention of the ESL of disadvantaged students.
Regarding the LONG-TERM IMPACT, PICESL contributed to improving the performance of students at risk of social exclusion, helping to create more inclusive societies, and promoting social cohesion in alignment with the “Agenda 2030” for Sustainable Development of the United Nations: “Guarantee an inclusive, equitable and quality education” (UN, 2015), as well as the Europe 2020 Strategy that has set the objective of reducing the proportion of students leaving education and training prematurely to less than 10%. The Europe 2020 development strategy was at the core of all project activities.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-ES01-KA201-065660.title: ADTRANS - MEDES: ADAPTATION AND TRANSFER OF SCHOOL MEDIATION AS A METHODOLOGICAL TOOL FOR THE PREVENTION OF EARLY SCHOOL DROP OUT
2019-1-ES01-KA201-065660.summary:
<< Background >>

Based on the experience acquired by 6 of the Project partners in the previous project MEDES 2015-1.ES01-KA201-015954, AdTransMEDES has faced the need for community schools to develop and implement tools that are able to prevent conflicts among students. The base of these tools, for our project, has been mediation.
Project partners in France and Croatia identified the need of addressing school conflicts and acknowledge the potential of mediation tools developed with MEDES in this regard.

<< Objectives >>

ADTRANS-MEDES Project has aimed at capitalizing and expanding the applicability range of the intellectual outputs developed by 6 of the project partners within the innovation Project MEDES 2015-1.ES01-KA201-015954, through their adaptation to the social, educational, cultural and administrative specificities of the new partners’ contexts.
Project MEDES developed innovative products to help educational communities to foster mediation as a tool for conflict resolution, Products developed were: 1) Multi-MEDES Toolbox, educational multimedia materials for mediation in schools, 2) School mediation programme “Where do we start from?” and 3) Methodological Guide for the evaluation of educational programmes based on mediation.
Partners will increase the range of applicability of the above mentioned products through the Exchange of experiences and the development of Exchange common activities between experienced entities that took part in MEDES Project (from Spain and Italy) and the entities that have decided to implement these products within the school mediation strategy (from France and Croatia).

<< Implementation >>

The activities carried out have been addressed to build capacities and enable the adaptation and use of the Mediation tools in the new contexts.
In this regard, the 3 MEDES products have been revised, adapted and translated by French and Croatian schools with the support of municipalities and NGOs.
A training activity, addressed to teachers and youth workers from the participating organization was organized. In this activity, the mediation methodology and the guide for its implementation was presented. 14 persons from Spain, Croatia and France were trained.
2 exchange activities among mediator students have been organized. The first took place in Sacile (Italy) with the participation of 48 students and teachers, while the second took place in Vila-real (Spain) with the participation of 41 students and teachers.
Two conferences have been organized (in Sacile and Vila-real) to spread the word

<< Results >>

Despite the outputs of the Project are those from the MEDES previous Project, they have been adapted, simplified (for its use in primary schools) and translated to Croatian and French.
Among other results:
-	17 professionals have been trained in school mediation
-	56 students and teachers have participated in mediation exchanges
-	3 new centres have established mediation programmes or have planned its implementation for the 2022-2023 year.
-        2 conferences have been organized
-	2 new educational centres (IC Sabaudia in Italy and IES Los Palacios in Spain) have known about the project and have planned products implementation.

2019-1-ES01-KA201-065807.title: Prevention of the  early school leaving and school failure in pupils in disadvantaged situation through the implementation of inclusive methodologies and other strategies and the collaboration between parents and teachers.
2019-1-ES01-KA201-065807.summary:
<< Background >>

Murcia has one of the highest figures in early school leaving. In our funcioning as guidances in our schools, we have observed the difficulties that the teachers have in the process of implementation of inclusive methodologies or the lack of collaboration  between teachers and families, especially with those that are in a disadavataged situation.  We had made an analysis of needs of the teachers and families and concluded that we needed to explore new strategies to prevent early school leaving.  
The most important needs we observed were: 1-We, as instutions that participated in the project, needed to observe new good practices in the prevention of early school leaving to help teachers to break fears against the implementation of inclusive methodologies and other strategies to prevent early school leaving; 2- Teachers had to receive new and more efficient training activities that help them to break the barriers in the implementation of inclusive methodologies, and  3- The families could benefit of some training activities -workshops-to help them to participate and to colaborate with teachers in the educational process in a better way.

<< Objectives >>

1- To know new strategies to prevent the school failure and early school leaving, for example, better ways to collaborate with other instutions, how to help to the teachers to break barriers in the implementation of inclusive methodologies.
2- To design and develop training activities for teachers that could help them to overcome the fears to use on a daily basis the methodologies that are considered as innovative and inclusive and that could contribute to improve the teachers competences and skills. 
3- To design and develop some workshops for families to help them to improve some skills, like communication skills, to increase their colaboration with their children´s school, to break some negative actitudes against the school and to favor a more positive point of view about teachers. 
4- To help to teachers and families to reflect on these situation (early school leaving) and to design our materials and training activities thanks to their contributions, ideas, reflections...
5- To help to teachers to develop better teaching-learning processes, to answer to the different type of pupils, taking into account those pupils with some disadvantages and trying to implement the strategies and methodologies that are known as inclusive.

<< Implementation >>

1-Analysis of the situation in school failure and early school leaving at a local, regional, national and european level.
2-Analysis of the teachers and families  needs in the prevention of early school leaving. 
3-Reflection groups (with teachers and families) to reflect on the causes, perceptions, needs, problems... regarding early school leaving. 
4-After these analysis, we have designed and developed courses for teachers (inclusive methodologies, Learning communities, etc) and workshops for parents (communication skills, different ways to participate in the schools, strategies to help to their children in the school...), trying to adapt to the different needs in each country. 
5-With all the conclusions of the previous activities, we have created a Guide of good practices in 7 languages, English and the 6 official languages of the partners and these guides are available in our website. 
6- We have created an European net of institutions with good practices in the prevention of early school leaving, with synergies of colaboration among them.
7-we have made a campaign of donation of digital devices for families with economical problems or another disadvantages.

<< Results >>

-Report of the situation in early school leaving at a local, regional, national and european level.
-Report of the needs of teachers and families regarding the more efficient prevention of the early school leaving.
-Better colaboration among different institutions: educartional, social institutions at a local and regional level in the design and development of strategies to prevent the early school leaving. 
- Seven guides of good practices in the prevention of early school leaving, one in English and others in: Spanish, Croatian, Rumanian, Bulgarian, Portuguese and Greek to help teachers and another guidances to implement inclusive methodologies and another strategies useful in the prevention of early school leaving and availble in a free way in our website.
- The European net of instutions with good practices in the prevention of early school leaving, where more than 80 schools or another educational or social institutions appear and those that are interested in these contents could contact and to stablish future colaborations and mutual enrichment. This net is available in our website: www.changingschoolschanginglives.com
- Materials to support especially to those teachers that want to implement some inclusive methodologies.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-FR01-KA201-062212.title: The Creative School
2019-1-FR01-KA201-062212.summary:
<< Background >>

Selon l'OCDE, dans un monde de plus en plus complexe, les enfants doivent développer des capacités de réflexion de haut niveau afin de trouver des solutions aux problèmes sociaux, émotionnels et économiques, tant sur le plan personnel que dans le contexte du monde au sens large. Afin de relever les défis du XXIe siècle, les élèves doivent faire preuve de créativité, d'innovation, d'esprit d'entreprise et d'adaptabilité, et posséder la motivation, la confiance et les compétences nécessaires pour utiliser la pensée créative et critique de manière ciblée. Le projet Creative School a été conçu pour répondre à ce besoin en proposant des approches éducatives créatives et critiques dans les écoles par le biais d'un engagement avec le secteur culturel, notamment les musées, les galeries et les centres scientifiques.

<< Objectives >>

Creative School a été construit sur la base des résultats de deux précédents projets financés par Erasmus+ : Creative Museum (2014-1-FR01-KA202- 008678) et Making Museum (2017-1-FR01-KA202-037487), en offrant des possibilités de produire et d'évaluer des connaissances, de clarifier des concepts et des idées, de rechercher des opportunités, d'envisager des alternatives et de résoudre des problèmes. Le projet Creative School avait pour objectif d'utiliser les méthodes et outils créatifs et innovants développés tout au long des projets Creative Museum et Making Museum et de les appliquer pour développer des modules d'apprentissage pour les élèves et les enseignants.
Ces modules ont été conçus pour développer l'apprentissage autonome et les capacités de réflexion critique et visuelle en utilisant le contenu du patrimoine culturel mis à disposition par les organisations partenaires.

<< Implementation >>

Le projet a atteint les objectifs prévus de différentes manières : premièrement, par une analyse des besoins en formation et en documentation des enseignants, des éducateurs, des élèves et des parents ; deuxièmement, par la production d'un ensemble de ressources éducatives en libre accès centrées sur le développement des capacités de réflexion par l'engagement dans le patrimoine culturel ; et troisièmement, par la création d'un ensemble de lignes directrices et de recommandations visant à influencer les décideurs politiques et les responsables des programmes scolaires.
Les principaux résultats du projet sont les suivants

Les réalisations principales du projet sont les suivantes : 

La réalisation de l’ "intellectual output" n°01 (IO1) intitulé "Méthodes permettant d'inclure une approche créative et critique dans l'éducation et l'identification des besoins".  
La réalisation de l’ "intellectual output"  n°02 (IO2) intitulé "Développement des ressources éducatives en libre accès du projet Creative School (OER)"
La réalisation de l’ "intellectual output"  n°03 (IO3) intitulé « Lignes directrices et recommandations » :

<< Results >>

Le projet a permis aux enseignants, aux éducateurs et aux élèves d'aborder un large éventail de sujets et de thèmes, notamment l'innovation, les STEAM (sciences, technologies, arts et mathématiques), le développement durable, la revitalisation urbaine, l'innovation sociale et l'entrepreneuriat. 
Les principaux résultats de "Creative School" sont les suivants : 
- une amélioration des capacités des enseignants et éducateurs européens, et une créativité accrue dans la préparation de nouvelles leçons utilisant le large potentiel éducatif présent dans les institutions du patrimoine européen ;
- démonstration de la faisabilité de nouveaux supports de formation adaptés aux objectifs spécifiques des communautés éducatives ciblées, utilisant le patrimoine culturel numérique pour répondre à leur objectif de formation spécifique ;
- la valorisation de l'utilisation des compétences clés, à travers une approche créative et critique ;
- augmentation de la co-création et de la collaboration dans les processus de pensée créative et critique des enseignants/élèves avec les organisations du patrimoine culturel ; 
- une sensibilisation accrue des enseignants européens, ainsi que des décideurs en matière d'éducation et de formation

2019-1-HR01-KA201-060778.title: Schools Innovation Labs
2019-1-HR01-KA201-060778.summary:
<< Background >>

Creativity and innovation have been in the forefront of EU educational policies the last years (ET2020). Nonetheless, conventional ways of teaching related to teacher-centered methods, frontal teaching and chalk and talk still prevail in a good majority of schools in EU27, thus "killing" creativity and innovation in the educational context. This creates a gap between education and employment as studies show that what employers expect most from persons they recruit is creativity and innovation, ability to solve problematic situations, teamwork, information analysis and management, using digital media, efficiency in using information and communication technology tools. As teachers we are aware of that and try to change our approaches to teaching and learning focusing on  development of teachers’ capacity to integrate innovation in daily school practice. 
SiLab project aims at improving the employability of students involved the development of some of the most valued skills in the labour market, namely innovation, creative thinking and digital skills. In project we have focused to achieve though the implementation of the  i-lab to school environment and the creation of i-labs that will integrate innovation in daily school practice.

<< Objectives >>

Four schools from four different countries as well as four institutions have taken part in the project School Innovation Labs (SiLab) with the aim to improve the employability of students involved the development of some of the most valued skills in the labor market, namely innovation, creative thinking and digital skills. 
Prva riječka hrvatska gimnazija (PRHG) acting as the project coordinator, built the project consortium with the following school partners: PSEB-Bulgaria,  AEA-Portugal, PLATON M.E.P.E. and the following institutions IDEC – Greece, VPŠ PAR Rijeka-Croatia, DLEARN  – Italija and TREBAG – Hungary. Each of them carried out different actions to achieve the project‘s goals. 
The specific objectives of the project were:
-To develop the i-lab concept for school education
-To create i-labs at selected schools in the partners countries
-To create an on-line software application for the school i-labs
-To develop a guide for school i-labs, targeting school managers and facilitators

2019-1-HR01-KA201-060815.title: Implementation of Virtual Reality based learning methodology in secondary schools
2019-1-HR01-KA201-060815.summary:
<< Background >>

In present education systems in most of the EU countries, it's becoming very challenging for teachers to motivate students to learn the material presented in the classroom. In the phase of project idea, secondary school partners made surveys  and they provided informations that students easily 'get bored' by the academic content presented in formal education process. Being informed isn't the same as being educated.
Too much information received in a short period of time can easily bored and disengaged them and are not sure why they have to learn about.
VR can change this and motivate them towards academic achievement. By using VR technology, teachers can attract the attention of students to developed VR education material and make studying process exciting and more effective. New school classrooms with VR are technology advanced places of learning that allow significantly increasing of students engagement and learning. The millions of hours of free VR online content suitable for education purpose are available. The present limits can be notified in the lack of necessary IT equipment, as well as lack of teachers skills in ability to customise the material on such way that it can be implemented as a part of the class curriculum.

<< Objectives >>

The main project objectives were: 
-improving quality and attractiveness of education process in regions of Municipalities of Ludbreg-Croatia, Kocani- North Macedonia, Limassol - Cyprus and Pazardzhik - Bulgaria by development and implementation of innovative VR based learning methodology;
- increasing secondary schools teachers and students competences and skills in using of online available VR educational contents in every day classes;
-establishing strategic partnership among different socio-economic types of organisations (local public body, education institutions, NGOs, SME) for increasing of quality level of education with implementing of the best practices and development of innovative education methods.

The specific objectives were:
-developed own innovative ICT-based educational module with utilisation of VR technology;
-improved students achievements in school subjects with help of VR educational technology;
-improved students teamwork skills through the transnational competitive event in the frame of long-term teaching assignment;
-established transnational teachers network by using of eTwinning networking modules;
-created strategic Action plan for transnational cooperation in the field of education.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities that this project implemente were: 
-management and coordination of the project;
-transnational project partners' meetings (4 metings were organized during the project lifetime);
-theoretical and practical short-term joint staff training events (four short term joint staff training events were organized);
-long-term teaching assignments and short term exchange group of pupils (the event was held in Pazardzhik, Bulgaria and students from Bulgaria, North Macedonia and Croatia participated in this event);
-development of the intellectual outputs (Strategic Action plan for transnational partnership in development of educational process in Kochani, Ludbreg, Limassol and Pazardzhik by using of innovative ICT based methods and best practices, Guidelines 'How to implement free online available VR software in everyday classes'  and education module Knowledge as the only way out);
-development and maintenance of the project web site;
-organisation of media publications and press releases for the project activities and results;
- preparation of promotional materials (pens, notebooks, leaflets, brochures, poster);
-preparation of presentations for final dissemination events (4 dissemination event were organized).

<< Results >>

Concrete outputs are:
-Document for long-term strategic transnational partnership among local public bodies, secondary schools, NGOs and entrepreneurs
-Established VR Educational module Knowledge as the only way out
-Prepared Guidelines for secondary school teachers 'How to implement free online available VR software in everyday classes'
-Prepared Strategic Action plan for transnational partnership in development of educational process in Kochani, Ludbreg, Limassol and Pazardzik by using of innovative ICT based methods and best practices

-Prepared Project web site with best practices from project activities and all created materials from the project are at disposal for teachers from other schools (free for downloading) as well as for any other interested stakeholders on local, regional, national and world wide level

2019-1-HR01-KA201-060973.summary:
<< Background >>

We have applied for this project in order to tackle the challenges in the modern educational world - the lack of creativity and the lack of awareness for transversal skills in STEM education. We have applied for the project because we believe that we were able to put up a project team of diverse and experienced partners throughout the European educational community which share the same beliefs and passion. Together, prior to the project proposal, we have commented and thought about the needs of our different schooling systems. We all came to the conclusion that our educational systems are in a dire need of letting the hard-subject based approach go, and welcoming a more soft, individual oriented and more transversal-based approach. Specifically, the needs we have recognized, are fresh, ready-to-use materials and methods which the teachers will not only reproduce, but which will inspire them, and which they will be able to use modularly and in combination with their own teaching practices and methods.

<< Objectives >>

As stated in the project proposal; the overall objective of this project was the improvement of transversal skills in STEM for teachers and trainers and the development of innovative teaching approaches.
The specific objectives of the project were the development of methods, materials & tools for the support of learning and teaching transversal skills, the training of teachers to implement the developed methods, tools and materials in their teaching practice and the evaluation of the applicability and usefulness of developed methods, tools and materials.
We strongly believe we have been able to fulfill these aims; through the developed intellectual outputs, through the wide network of teachers that we contacted, trained with and with whom we disseminated our results, and through the in-partnership exchange of practices which led us to reevaluating ourselves and the results that we produced.
While we do believe that we achieved most of our aims, there were challenges which affected our results and the project in whole. 2019-1-HR01-KA201-060999.title: INDUSTRIAL HERITAGE LAB@ISCED 3 LEVEL
2019-1-HR01-KA201-060999.summary:
<< Background >>

Industrial heritage consists of the remains of industrial culture which are of historical, technological, social, architectural or scientific value. Hence, it is considered to be the important part of the European cultural heritage. This initiative aimed at promoting good practice to transform Europe's industrial, religious and military heritage that have lost their original function for new use(r)s and to turn it into a driver of economic and social development for European cities and regions. Rijeka is the city with very interesting history, especially regarding industrial heritage. Unfortunately, a great majority of this heritage is abandoned and devastated. There are some attempts of local authorities for revalorization of such heritage but in our opinion it is not enough. Therefore, we applied for this project with intention to raise awareness among students and whole local community for this topic.

<< Objectives >>

With the implementation of this project we wanted to achieve several objectives: firstly, to encourage students to research about  local history and to realize the interconnection with historical processes in Europe and the world. In this way students can develop a positive attitude towards local and national history. Secondly, the activities in this project could also motivate students to actively participate in the current issues of local community. Doing so, students are becoming active citizens which one of the main objectives of modern educational systems in Europe and the world.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, students were engaged in many different activities. They analyzed authentic historical materials, made researches about historical personalities, visited many locations of industrial heritage in all countries that were partners in the project. They also critically evaluated the current situation of those sites, noticed that majority of them is in a very bad condition and tried to find an alternative way of reuse of such locations. Furthermore they analyzed the role of local authorities, discussed with their representatives and made interviews with experts in the field. Also visited many museums, archives and institutions which main objective was industrial heritage. Finally, they proposed new ideas and presented solutions for such heritage in a way that can provide a sustainable development of the whole region they live in.

<< Results >>

The project produced three main outcomes: 
O1 - Comparative study: State-of-the-art situation concerning the industrial heritage education. Given the diversity of the industrial heritage-related best practice examples and relevant level of mainstreaming in the countries represented by the project partnership, a comparative analysis was made with a view of relevant policy frameworks and good practice/case studies in the field of valorization and interpretation of industrial heritage.
O2 - Curriculum Framework "INDUSTRIAL HERITAGE. All project partners participated in creation of Curriculum framework which was is set to be implemented in educational systems of all countries members of the project. It is divided in four modules: History, valorization, revitalization and sustainable development and it is suitable for developing modern educational strategies such as problem-based learning and place-based learning.
O3 -   Methodological guide to teach "INDUSTRIAL HERITAGE LAB” at the ISCED 3 level- Following the delivery the Curriculum Framework “INDUSTRIAL HERITAGE LAB”  the project partners developed a comprehensive methodological guide for teaching of industrial heritage-related contents under the
secondary school curriculum.

2019-1-HR01-KA201-061017.title: Teachers' Inquiry on Mathematics Education
2019-1-HR01-KA201-061017.summary:
<< Background >>

One of the main insights from mathematics education research in the past 20 years is that the professional knowledge of mathematics teachers (PKMT) is of crucial importance to implement math teaching that goes beyond rote learning, and which engages students in higher order mathematical activity. Students need to acquire mathematical knowledge which remains relevant to higher education and profess. life in a time where computers take over tasks that formerly had to be done manually. Research has also improved our understanding of the complexity of PKMT, as well as the conditions and constraints for developing it. PKMT consists of delicate combinations of practical and theoretical components, and while deep knowledge of math. contents is needed, so is deep knowledge of how the contents can be taught and learned (didactical knowledge). Moreover, to acquire the appropriate math.and didactical knowledge, suitable course type activities in preservice education are necessary but they do not suffice. One of the most important issues is how to establish learning situations for teachers which involve both observations and experience from the classroom, and explicit and shared knowledge which draws on mathematical and didactical theory.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was to explore how a community of math teachers working together in 1 school can improve their practice through joint exploration, planning and interaction between themselves and with university professors. We explored how such a community can reach a high level of independence and sustainability in creating innovative teaching and learning materials and upgrade their PKMT. The idea was to adapt the well-established format of Lesson study (LS) to conditions in the participating countries. LS is a Japanese model of shared inquiry, performed by small groups of teachers with a specific goal to improve their teaching, and thereby students’ learning - the model is new in Europe and especially at the upper secondary level. In the long term, TIME will transform practice in partnering schools and show how to achieve sustainable teacher innovation. The first part of the project (TIMELESS) was dedicated to establishing LS among partners. The second part (TIME^2) focused on teachers taking the role of designers, as it is the usual practice of independent Lesson study. In particular, teachers learned how to use didactical phenomenology to develop new scenarios with rich and motivating mathematical contexts.
