2019-1-IE01-KA201-051545.title: Engaging Students in the creation of their own STEAM learning
2019-1-IE01-KA201-051545.summary:
<< Background >>

European and national policy statements for the year 2020 and beyond identify a need for increased knowledge and competence in STEAM subjects (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Design, and Mathematics) as  a priority for continued socio-economic development through  fostering  essential innovation and creativity. Related strategies and policies identify a crucially related need to enhance  the engagement and attainment in STEAM subjects of  school students  at  all levels and in all types of educational system in all European countries.  We applied for this project to address these needs through  (1)  identification and analysis of best, innovative  practice in STEAM education at primary and secondary school level in 5 different countries with a contrasting range of socio-economic, demographic, and educational circumstances, and (2) dissemination  of its findings and products  to STEAM teachers and related target groups  across the European area. Hence, "STEAMing" as the title of our project– short for "STEAM: INternational Guidance to best practice. 
"STEAMing" also expresses our innovative, student and project centred style and methods of STEAM education

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to explore the crucial questions of "what works, where, why, and for whom" in STEAM education across Europe   through a  trans-European investigation. We wanted to use  our findings and conclusions to develop and deliver  an innovative range of practical products and resources for the training and support of  STEAM teachers, school leaders, educational advisors, administrators, and policy-makers in any European country. Through the  dissemination of  our outputs to these key target groups and their sustainable exploitation by them, we aimed  to facilitate an enhancement of STEAM teaching and learning that would ultimately make a significant positive impact on the educational engagement and attainment of their pupils and students - the ultimate beneficiaries of our project - across the European area. Towards these general objectives, we aimed to undertake a 3-year programme of research and development in STEAM education and training in  primary and secondary education in 5 different countries: Ireland, Croatia, Norway, Portugal, and Greece. Through this R+D programme we aimed to provide the specific outcomes and outputs outlined  below

<< Implementation >>

(a)	Initial and updated "State of the Art" reports from each partner on key issues of implementing innovative STEAM education in their own countries, regions and institutions; 
(b)	One or more detailed case-studies by each partner, over approximately one school year, of  innovative and demonstrably effective  best practice  in STEAM education in their own organisations and local school networks  
(c)	Detailed  and comprehensive reports from each partner on the aims, methods, findings and conclusions from their  case-studies
(d)	Filmed illustrations of the case-study innovations in practice
(e)	Planning and delivery of: 6 training courses to STEAM staff in the partner organisations; 
(f)   Planning and delivery of 2 international residential 5 day training courses and a 2 day International conference on STEAM education, all  3 of these open to delegates from any European country 
(g)	Producing online and printed versions of 2  substantial handbooks on STEAM education and innovation to accompany our training courses 
(g)	Establishing and maintaining a project website for downloadable access to all its products
(h)	Regular face-to-face and online project management meetings  to plan and deliver all of the above

<< Results >>

As noted above -  6 “State of the Art” reports;6 case-study reports and 6 case-study films, one from each partner; 8 week-long training courses  and an International STEAMing conference supported by  STEAMing handbooks, a resource pack, and a project website;     
  
The 6 training courses for   staff of  all partner organisations  were based on the project’s cumulative work.  They were hosted by each partner in turn in parallel with a project management meeting. Attendance  was funded from the project’s budget.

All training courses  and the STEAMing handbooks are   downloadable for delivery by any school or other organisation in any  country. They can be delivered  in  online and/or face-to-face modes over  flexible periods of time.   2 pilot versions of an international  residential training course open to delegates from any institution in any European country were delivered during the project’s lifetime . These latter were funded by  delegates' fees which themselves were  eligible for ERASMUS+ KA1 funding. 

The project website provides a resource pack for STEAMing implementation. It displays  all  the project's findings and outputs plus a range of presentations and papers from partners and key sources outside the project

2019-1-IT02-KA201-062254.title: GREEN S.E.E.D.S. - Sinergy and Environment to Empower Decentralized Schools
2019-1-IT02-KA201-062254.summary:
<< Background >>

In many regions of Europe, the increasing urbanisation and the consequent population decrease in mountain areas and small islands has severely tested the survival of their schools. Where they survive, they are likely to face deficiencies and organisational problems. 

Prejudices about the quality of teaching and the concern that geographical isolation may result in cultural isolation often lead parents to move, to enrol their children in more central schools, so increasing depopulation. All this is in spite of the commitment of many capable and motivated teachers and of the social and cultural value of these schools, which lies primarily in the relationship with their own community and in the link with the natural habitat, so important to develop a sense of collective belonging and a basis for the protection of local culture and environment. Small schools are a resource, not a limit. Their daily work is a passionate and continuous research and means attention to pupils, inclusion, experimentation and innovation.  

The desire to enhance this identity heritage is at the basis of the European project GREEN S.E.E.D.S.

<< Objectives >>

GENERAL OBJECTIVES 
•	To contribute to breaking the geographical isolation and overcoming the risks of cultural isolation of decentralised schools, enhancing their potential and strengthening awareness in teachers and pupils;
•	To educate the younger generations about the environment and its protection. 

SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES
•	Strengthening teachers' motivation and skills (IO1)
•	Building models for shared teaching at transnational level (IO2)
•	Development of competences in pupils (IO2);
•	Strengthening the environmental awareness of pupils who, in different areas, share the natural environment as a dimension of life (IO2);
•	(Re)reading, by "urban" pupils, of environmental and cultural realities usually known as tourist locations (IO2);
•	Creation of a network for project sustainability (Communication & Dissemination).

<< Implementation >>

The Intellectual Outputs of GREEN S.E.E.D.S. were realised through the following activities:
•	Building of an ad hoc training curriculum designed to meet teachers’ needs  and prepare them for the project methodology: the GREEN S.E.E.D.S. Toolkit (IO1);
•	Teachers’ training on the contents of the GREEN S.E.E.D.S. Toolkit, in two steps
•	Organisation of the groups of classes, from different countries, for the realisation - using the webquest methodology – of the learning units (Seedquest) on: Nature and biodiversity; The forest heritage; The coastal heritage; A sea without plastic: the Seedquest;
•	Realisation of the Seedquests by the participant classes (IO2);
•	Building - for each Seedquest - of a Digital Storytelling;
•	Presentation of the Digital Storytelling to the twinned 'urban' classes.

Breaking the isolation also means networking at European level, in order to turn small schools from a "problem" into a "resource" and promote their survival. Communication and Dissemination promoted the project's philosophy: the signatures collected on the Manifesto (104 signatures) and the adhesions to the Declaration of Intent (21) provide a solid basis for the project's sustainability.

<< Results >>

IO1 - "Toolkit GREEN S.E.D.S.": 5 modules of 3 units each plus the Teaching Guide. The modules and the guide are available in the six project languages (EN, IT, FR, ES, EL, HR).

Teachers’ training: in two phases, it involved 73 teachers:  
•	Training of future trainers at local level: 8 trainers;
•	Training of local teachers at local level: 65 teachers.

IO2 - Seedquests: 20 classes participated in their implementation, for a total of 20 Seedquests implemented and available in the six project languages, for an amount of 120 learning units. 

Twinning with "urban" schools: implemented also through the eTwinning platform, it involved 18 new classes and more than 500 pupils.

IO2 - Digital Storytelling: Seedquests were rewritten in the form of DST, to be presented to the twinned classes. 

GREEN S.E.E.D.S. Manifesto, expressing the principles and values of the project and Declaration of Intent for the establishment of a network of schools for the sustainability of the project (EU-Net-SIMS). A total of 104 people signed the Manifesto and 21 organisations signed the Declaration.

All the indicated outputs are downloadable from the www.greenseeds.eu  platform.

2019-1-IT02-KA201-063073.title: innovative educational ROBOtics strategies for PrImary SChool ExperienceS
2019-1-IT02-KA201-063073.summary:
<< Background >>

Many Europeans do not have adequate digital skills, and there is a shortage of STEM workers. The RoboPisces project (RP), by adopting Educational Robotics (ER) to teach STEAM since primary school,  contributes to developing STEM proficiency. 
Many Europeans are at risk of ESL, and the EU aims to decrease the share of ESL to 9% by 2030. RP sought to positively impact on the ESL risk by showing students that the learning process can be interesting and meaningful and that the teacher can be a cooperation partner. 
Many European teachers still lack the competence to use ICT and use it only to a small extent in classrooms. One of the key aspects of the project was teacher training, which aimed at creating independent and creative teachers that use technology to adapt strategies to the needs of students. 
Despite its many benefits on students’ hard and soft skills development, ER is integrated with school curricula as an optional and seldom activity. Environmental education was identified as an urgent need of our society and one of the main interests of young generations. RP integrated environmental themes, especially the marine environment, to raise students’ interest in Blue careers and to promote ocean literacy.

<< Objectives >>

The RoboPisces project set specific and operational objectives:
1.Improve potential students' achievement and engagement in STEAM by implementing effective and innovative teaching and assessment strategies using robotics kits;
2.Develop transversal skills in pupils using Educational Robotics;
3.Introduce the marine environment using the RoboFish toolkit, thus introducing students to sustainability;
4.Foster digital competence across the curricula tailored to the age groups;
5.Improve student’s interest, participation and motivation to reduce and prevent ESL;
6.Enhance primary school teachers’ skills in the field of robotics and on robotics-based educational methodologies, enabling them to implement a robotic-based curriculum and enriching their professional growth;
7.Create specific assessment tools to evaluate the outcomes of lessons (learning outcomes, attitude to learning, learning motivation etc.).
Aiming to deliver innovative ICT-based educational approaches, the project also intended to increase the level of teachers’ and students’ satisfaction and self-efficacy.
Tangible achievements of these objectives are the 3 intellectual outputs (IOs): RoboFish toolkit (IO2), Educational Curriculum (IO3), Teachers Training Manual (IO4)

<< Implementation >>

The activities implemented during the project:
-Review of existing educational experiences with robotics in STEAM subjects within involved countries
-Identification of the fundamental topics of the curriculum
-Development of the teacher training course about educational robotics, distributed control and marine robotics on the e-learning platform
-Development of the validation strategy for the innovative curriculum of the RoboPisces project
-Create a comprehensive, open source and low-cost toolkit that support the educational activities
-Development of reference materials for teachers (lesson plans and assessment toolkit) that can inspire teachers in the development of a tailored ER activity
-Implementation of the curriculum at school
-Create a MOOC freely accessible from the website of the project
-Create a manual for guiding more teachers through the material of the curriculum
-Create a manual to support teacher training
-Disseminate the project results and outputs during many local, national and international events, on social media and the website of the project and at partners’ websites
-Create the presentation of the toolkit on the project’s website to let teachers explore the technology developed during the project

<< Results >>

The 3 main results of the projects are the RoboFISH toolkit (IO2), the educational curriculum (IO3) and the Teacher training manual (IO4). IO3 (www.robopisces.eu/io3) is an innovative curriculum for teaching educational robotics, IoT and the marine environment at the primary school. It is composed of several modules, each of which focuses on a key topic and includes the respective lesson plans, learning objectives, training materials, practical activities, and assessment methods. The curriculum is divided in two parts: the Basic curriculum, which deal with the fundamental topics of robotics, and the Advanced curriculum, which introduces students to the study of the marine environment and the IoT. The IO2 (www.robopisces.eu/io2) supports the activities of the curriculum providing a set of mechatronic elements for the Basic curriculum and the “advanced kit”, which is a 3D printed robot resembling a fish, for the Advanced curriculum (IO3). IO4 (www.robopisces.eu/io4) builds upon the teachers training activities carried out during the project giving teachers all the information about IO2 and IO3.

2019-1-IT02-KA201-063174.title: EDUCATING COMMUNITY TO REDUCE THE RISK OF CHILDREN’S SOCIAL EXCLUSION
2019-1-IT02-KA201-063174.summary:
<< Background >>

Children were the age group at the highest risk of poverty or social exclusion in the EU in 2017. Children growing up in poverty and social exclusion are less likely to do well in school, enjoy good health and realize their full potential later in life, when they are at a higher risk of becoming unemployed, poor and socially excluded.  It was demonstrated that children from disadvantaged families who are attending schools that offer extracurricular activities as music, volunteering, sport, art, reading groups, has the 127% more chances to be resilient than their peers who attend schools without this kind of offers: extracurricular activities help the children to learn, gain knowledge, socialize, strengthen themselves emotionally. 
Anyway, not always schools have the resources (time, expertise, personnel, funds) to bear the burden of this responsibility alone therefore the birth of synergies among different social actors represents a valid support to reduce the risk of children’s social exclusion.

<< Objectives >>

- promoting reciprocal, multidisciplinary and trans sectoral learning among the staff member involved at different levels in children education (strategies, methods, activities to reduce the risck of social exclusion of disadvantaged children) 
- sharing and collecting and applying validated tools to support the growing path of children at risk of social exclusion aged between 6 and 10 years (children with emotional, economic, social disadvantages) 
- increasing the levels of motivation, academic performance and engaging in acceptable conduct for most of the children involved in the local and transnational activities of the project
- creating a multidisciplinary transnational support network made of professionals, organizations, and schools from the partner countries of the project 
- stimulating the partners to look for new cooperation with other social actors to allow the creation/growing of local educating communities to support their own mission to create culture and better life opportunities for children 
- promoting the cooperation among civil society organizations and educational institutions, leading the creation of educating communities

<< Implementation >>

The exchange of good practices among the partner organizations has been stimulated though the implementation of joint short term staff training events where each partner could share with a heterogeneous group of professionals from the other partner organizations, its knowhow in the promotion of social inclusion of disadvantaged children and eventual good practices in the creation of collaborations with schools/organizations or with the community, more in general, to support their mission.
Each training event has been followed by an experiential phase where the educators will apply the learned competences in their local context, documented and analysed through reports and comparisons in the view of a “transnational” supervision. The transnational and multidisciplinary network support network that has been created during the project, planned and implemented in collaboration a blended mobility for school learners and produced a final publication containing tools and techniques able to promote the cooperation among civil society organizations and educational institutions, starting the creation of educating communities.

<< Results >>

- introduction of new and innovative interventions and activities among the ones usually offered by
the partner organizations 
- creation of a transnational multi-disciplinary support network made of professionals and
organizations and schools 
- creation of concrete validated open resource: a guide available mainly on-line about the building of
educational communities around children with an overview of generalizable good practices from the
project addressing school staff, civil society organizations working with children and teachers,
educators, pedagogues, psychologists, experts in expressive therapies, youth workers, with the purpose to build educating communities able to answer the children’s needs (in particular the ones’ who live in a situation od social or economic disadvantage, with a migration background, with disability, without parental care etc.) 
- creation/enlargement of local educational communities around schools/institutions thanks to the
active role of the partner organizations
- concrete planning of a follow-up plan made of local projects and initiatives by the partners, some applications for Erasmus+ partnership among some of the project partners and new ideas.

2019-1-LV01-KA201-060345.title: Coaching for staff professional development in education
2019-1-LV01-KA201-060345.summary:
<< Background >>

The diversity and complexity of students and classrooms in the 21st century place increasing demands on the teacher to provide effective pedagogy and instruction. To meet these demands teachers have to adopt new professional practices, skills, competences and knowledge. Individual and team coaching is increasingly being seen as the tool through which to address these challenges and support teachers.
Coaching is widely used in business organisations to strengthen individual and team capacity and productivity. In educational settings there are some good examples of how teachers coach teachers, but coaching is not widely used in schools in project partner countries. Our long-term goal outside the scope of this project was to increase schools in which coaching is used as a systematic approach. The goal for CoDe projec was to explore the experience and best practices of partner countries in using coaching as a tool for more effective change management and creation of a supportive and growth oriented environment, and to identify the opportunities that coaching provides for staff development and collaboration.

<< Objectives >>

To reach the above goals we have set the following objectives:
1. To develop a description of current state of coaching in staff development both in business and educational settings.
2. To organize 6 learning visits in partner countries to explore how coaching techniques, both individual and group, have helped to create growth-oriented environments through more effective cooperation and well-being that lead to change in practice, reflection and school-wide collective efficacy that promote student achievement.
3. To create a digital Resource book of individual and group coaching techniques, methods and examples of best practices from different settings in partner countries.
4. To disseminate the best coaching practice and to introduce and try out various coaching techniques and elements in all partner countries.

<< Implementation >>

In project proposal we identified 4 main groups of activities: Transnational Project Meetings; Learning, Teaching, Training Activities; Intellectual Outputs; Multiplier Events, 
Activity implementation started with kick-off/Partners' meeting in Riga and concluded with second partners' meeting in Sheffield. We had 7 online Partners' meetings to discuss ongoing issues as well as development of project outcomes and deliverables.
We organised six learning visits: 4 face - to -face visits: in Sheffield, Zagreb, Brno, and Nicosia and two online learning visits to Latvia and Romania. Each visit was followed by dissemination workshops in all partner institutions.
We developed the desk research methodology, elaborated national country reports and produced common report reflecting the state of coaching in selected institutions in partner countries.
The Digital Resource Book was developed, piloted, peer reviewed by partners, evaluated internally and externally, improved and finalized. 
To disseminate the DRB to wider audience partners organized multiplier events in their countries with participation of educators, school leaders, policy makers, local authorities and business representatives at local, regional and national level

<< Results >>

The partnership has elaborated Desk research "Coaching in schools and companies" with the aim to describe the arrangement, opportunities and limitations of coaching in selected schools and companies and to identify the specifics and challenges/limitations of the implementation of coaching in selected schools. For the research, we opted for qualitative approach, interviews with 27 coaches (mentors, supervisors) working in schools, NGO or business companies and 12 people receiving the support – clients/coachees. We presented the obtained and interpreted data in the framework: main topics of and expectations from coaching, impacts of coaching, how coaching is organized, effective ways to coach, limitations related to coaching, major differences between coaching in schools and companies, and main challenges for the future. 
We have increased professional staff capacity of the partner institutions in terms of coaching by organising learning and exchange of experience visits to all partner countries and the follow-up workshops. 
We have developed the Digital Resource Book for educators and schools to use for building supportive and growth-oriented environments.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
Cooperation between educational institutions and business
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2019-1-MK01-KA201-060287.title: Improving Literacy and learning other languages in elementary school pupils (primary schools) by developing knowledge, skills and attitudes (competences) within extracurricular activities
2019-1-MK01-KA201-060287.summary:
<< Background >>

Teaching and extracurricular activities are an inseparable whole in the educational process in primary education that creates the necessary preconditions for the student to develop into an open, independent, creative and character personality. Within the educational activity in the schools, various extracurricular activities are organized and realized in accordance with the development needs and interests of the students and their active participation, in order for the school to become a place for socialization of students and an attractive learning environment. The choice of extracurricular activities in which the student will be involved independently outside of regular classes, offers him the opportunity to develop interests that regular teaching does not cover or only partially covers. It is especially important that extracurricular activities develop the competencies (knowledge, skills and attitudes) of students in all areas, which are not covered or only partially covered by the curricula, and are in accordance with the National Standards to be achieved by students up to the end of primary education.
Over the past 20 years, reforms in the primary education have been implemented in the Republic of North Macedonia, which mainly focused on formal education, while neglecting the importance of extracurricular activities in schools for the overall development of the child. Thus, there was a discrepancy between regular formal classes  and  extracurricular activities.
Having in mind various domestic and international reports (OECD, PISA) it has been ascertained that the achievements of students are very low and are in decline (especially in the field of Literacy), it was necessary to find ways and strategies for improving the situation in the schools, and in terms of teaching, but also in finding other more creative methods of learning and teaching, motivating pupils to develop the basic competences.
That is why changes are necessary, but not only as the establishment of specific standards of knowledge for each teaching subject (which refers to the study of mother tongue and / or foreign languages), but above all as the development of a flexible and modern system which will encompass the acquisition of knowledge, skills and development of attitudes in each pupil, as well as developing a system based on the competences necessary for the successful involvement of every individual in all processes of contemporary society.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were  to  contribute to building a complementary and coherent system of primary education based on competences that are developed both through regular classes and extracurricular activities through preparation of documents,field research and  recommendations, training and guides for teachers and the exchange of innovative and creative ideas.
This project is an attempt to connect the necessary competences of Language literacy and learning in other languages, interlinking, upgrading and complementing it through learning and learning through "life at school". 
This means developing competencies through extracurricular activities, various forms of association of students, their initiatives and organizations. The project corresponds to the activities envisaged in the Comprehensive Education Strategy 2018-2025 in the area of developing national standards based on key competences for lifelong learning and will contribute through the experience gained in developing curricula, and in particular in the documents relating to extracurricular activities. By implementing project activities we wanted to develop the concept and methodology for realizing  extracurricular activities in the field of Language literacy and using other languages, conduct a field research on this topic and to deliver significant recommendations which could be if interest for national educational institutions in order to maintain better results on this field, train teachers about modern approaches, methods and innovative practices in this field and share good practices from our local context and other countries in region.

<< Implementation >>

The main influence of this project was to contribute to the development of basic competences - Language  literacy and using of  foreign languages, through innovative and creative approaches, through active involvement of students and teachers from primary education throughout  extracurricular activities.

The  activities that we have implemented are:
•	Developed concept and methodology for acquiring competences in  Literacy and the using of other languages through extracurricular activities for primary education
•	Developed appropriate guidelines for the implementation of extracurricular activities in Literacy and studying other languages for teachers 
•	Trained teachers and librarians  to work with students  in the field of extracurricular activities (40 teachers from primary schools and librarians from public libraries)
•	Developed Innovative methods (activities, procedures, guides) for establishing  pupils' clubs in pilot schools to develop appropriate competencies in Literacy and learning other languages
•	Prepared draft curricula - Modules  (as a support materials) for state institutions to change and improve access and work in schools in the field of  extracurricular activities for Literacy and learning other languages
*       Field research with recommendations for relevant national  institutions in the field of education
*       Established  network of teachers from primary schools and public libraries that are trained and  informed about the project results and outputs
*       Created an on line resources that teachers, librarians and other relevant institution could use for further development of this topic.  

 The main impact  from this project activities  is initiating and motivating   teachers  to change their working methods, adapt to the needs of contemporary students and  to establish  new  approaches to extracurricular activities in Literacy and using other languages.

<< Results >>

All planned outputs and other results were produced as planned. 
Intellectual Outputs which present a comprehensive analysis of the current situation related to extracurricular activities in primary education, especially in the fields of Language literacy and the acquisition of foreign languages and gives the schools and teachers practical tools for realizing extracurricular activities in proactive and modern ways. These are:
1. Concept and methodology for realization of extracurricular activities for promotion of Literacy and acquisition of foreign languages
2. Curriculum with  guidelines for teachers to conduct extracurricular activities in the areas of competencies related to Language literacy and acquisition of foreign languages with good practices from pilot schools
3. Modules for training of teachers for realization of extracurricular activities and  presented positive practices from Croatia and Bulgaria
4. Comprehensive field research of actual situation with extracurricular activities  with recommendations for improvement of the situation.
Regarding our piloting,training and dissemination activities  a network of teachers, primary schools and librarians was established and also  on line resources for teachers and other relevant institutions are published and available online.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Teaching and learning of foreign languages
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2019-1-MK01-KA201-060358.title: Social Entrepreneurship Education Development Project
2019-1-MK01-KA201-060358.summary:
<< Background >>

The rationale behind the SEED Project was the success story of the long term partnership we have with the schools and the know-how that was provided by the civil society sector. In this project, lessons learned from an original idea were combined with broader perspectives. Our original idea was that students should have at least one entrepreneurial experience before leaving compulsory education, either in primary or secondary education.
A key goal of the SEED project was to introduce entrepreneurship education even closer to the students while adding an extremely valuable added value - teaching them first-hand the new business model of Social Entrepreneurship as part of the business classes in the 3 schools (Croatia, Lithuania, North Macedonia) and exposing them to business communities.
Developing and promoting entrepreneurship education has been one of the key policy objectives of the EU institutions and Member States for many years. Making profits by doing harm to people and nature disengages young people more than it empowers them. SE by contrast is explicitly about creating value for others: economic, social and environmental value.
SEED project was designed to enable students to become future Social Entrepreneurs.

<< Objectives >>

Through the SEED project young people learned the essential skills for running a business but also learned about philanthropy, creativity, leadership and teamwork. Our belief was that if students were equipped with modern skills and motivation, they could prosper in the modern world. They could find solutions to our most complex problems via using business models. 

Our project has adapted a methodology for developing social entrepreneurs who learn from each other and become a part of the EU mosaic. As well, we provided support to the schools in helping them to build stronger communities and bring power and trust to local people.

By offering a safe space for students to run SE as Virtual Companies, this project upgraded its objectives and empowered students to boost their employability skills through organizing events in real life: mapping SE, organizing "SEED talks" based on TEDx, community events with SE from their region, making decisions about donations, creating school alumni clubs, etc. The name of the project came organically, since we also prepared promotional material prepared by one local social enterprise that produces plantable cards with seeds. The cards are made from recycled paper and can contain seed of Mose rose.

Miliana conveyed all her experiences of the project in the essay with which she applied for a two-year exchange scholarship at the United World Colleges in Southwest Asia (Singapore).She told us that it was the project and volunteering that inspired her to take this step.(https://arno.org.mk/news/from-skopje-to-singapore-social-entrepreneurship-volunteering-and-why-young-people-need-us/)

2019-1-NL01-KA201-060287.title: A Debate And Philosophy Typology
2019-1-NL01-KA201-060287.summary:
<< Background >>

In the days of the Athenian polis, public speaking, debate and philosophy were the cornerstones of democratic life. Philosophy had the form of a dialogue between people with contrasting views, and philosophers taught the art of persuasion to citizens attending the ekklēsia—the principal assembly of the democracy of ancient Athens. In contemporary secondary schools however, debate clubs and philosophy classrooms have become separate worlds that, regrettably, seldom interfere. This state of affairs leads to a waste of knowledge and skills, and lowers the potential impact that debating skills and philosophical thinking could have on strengthening democracy.

<< Objectives >>

With our new philosophical debate methodology, we hope to teach students how to apply philosophical concepts to question the status quo, and to discuss social issues in a respectful way with their peers. As such, we hope that the outputs of the ADAPT project will contribute to the development of high school students into engaged, critical and active citizens, and that teachers will find in it an effective tool to facilitate this process.

<< Implementation >>

We researched the effectivity of using debate as a learning activity in the philosophy classroom. The research by Natascha Kienstra was published in a first paper in the peer-reviewed journal Tydskrif vir Geesteswetenskappe (2021). A second paper was published in Forum Philosophie International, the journal of the Association Internationale des Professeurs de Philosophie (AIPPh), which describes the structure and intent of the project (Kienstra and Velema 2022). A third paper was published in a book from the established Dutch public philosopher Jos Kessels, with the title ‘Hoog spel: Filosoferen in de praktijk’ (Velema 2022).
Based on the research, we designed a set of key concepts that offer philosophy teachers a clear and comprehensive approach to debating. These concepts are visualized with logic symbols, which we have turned into a set of stamps. After downloading our 3D models, these stamps can be materialized with a 3D printer. They can be used in the classroom to analyze and evaluate debates, or used in combination with worksheets that offer practical assignments to become more familiar with our debate methodology.

<< Results >>

The Erasmus+ project with the title A Debate And Philosophy Typology (ADAPT), coordinated by Natascha Kienstra from Tilburg University, aims at overcoming the divide between debate clubs and philosophy classrooms by developing innovative educational materials and researching their effectivity. Our method that combines the argumentative skills of debate education with central concepts in political philosophy can be found at https://debaticons.com.
On this website, we offer an Open Access book with the title ‘Debate / Philosophy: How to start debating in the philosophy classroom’, as well as a set of practical worksheets and a collection of 3D models, which can be turned into a set of stamps with a 3D printer. 
All intellectual outputs of the ADAPT project (book, worksheets, debaticons, website, research papers, and Youtube channel) were developed by a consortium of four secondary schools (Wolfert Bilingual School, Rotterdam; Gimnazija Ledina, Ljubljana; Privatna klasicna gimnazija, Zagreb; ITE Enrico Tosi, Busto Arsizio), two universities (Tilburg University and Erasmus University Rotterdam), and three associations (Za in Proti, Slovenia; Hrvatsko Debatno Drustvo, Croatia; The Noisy Classroom, UK).

2019-1-PL01-KA201-064753.title: Greenopolis – Interactive eBook on Sustainable Development
2019-1-PL01-KA201-064753.summary:
<< Background >>

In the background of Greenopolis project lied the importance of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD). As climate change, overpopulation and inequalities begin to take a toll on our planet and human development, sustainability becomes increasingly important for our future. For the past years, Sustainable Development has been in the EU’s political Agenda. One cannot talk about Sustainable Development without highlighting the role of education. Education is central to the efforts to develop and promote sustainable solutions for the development needs of both people and the planet (UN, 2013). All educational institutions ranging from preschool to tertiary education and including both non-formal and informal education should consider it their responsibility to address sustainable development and to foster the development of key cross-cutting competencies related to sustainability (Issues and Trends in ESD, UN, 2018). In order to address the need to understand ESD as an integral part of quality education and lifelong learning, the partners wanted to develop a project with the goal of contributing to raising conscious European citizens, aware of the sustainability challenges, and ready to contribute to a sustainable European society and to empower teachers and educators to engage in ESD.

<< Objectives >>

The project’s main objective was to develop an innovative and playful pedagogy for Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) of children (from 3 to 6 years old and to raise their interest in STEM, based on an interactive learning eBook, that may be used in formal, non-formal and informal learning settings. 
The objectives were also:
- to raise awareness towards the importance of ESD at various levels, 
- to empower educators in ESD, 
- to raise children’s interest over STEM, as topics like climate change, biodiversity, energy, etc. have a strong STEM background
- to contribute to the development of transversal competences of children (e.g. literacy, citizenship, creativity, communication, storytelling, critical thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, etc.).

<< Implementation >>

The main, undertaken activities led directly to development of the main results. They included the creation of the comprehensive and pedagogically sound storyboards. During their development, a group of teachers and children and in some cases also parents was consulted and asked for input and feedback. Then the stories for beta version of the eBook were developed which implied strong interaction between writing, illustrating and animating. At the same time, the partnership worked on the development of the Facilitator’s Guide, designing activities and exercises that complemented the experience with the eBook. Development relied mostly on desk research and experience of partners, but especially teachers. 26 teachers were trained on how to use the results and then they implemented the pilot. During the pilot the technical aspects, easiness of use and impact in knowledge, skills and attitudes of the children using the eBook were tested. The suggestions collected in the testing phase led to the development of the final version of the eBook and Facilitator’s Guide. Besides those activities partners ensured a set of management, quality and valorisation activities which included 8 contests and 4 Multiplier Events.

<< Results >>

Tangible results:
The main tangible result is the Greenopolis eBook (which consists of 3 chapters), freely available on project’s website 5 languages – EN, HR, GR, PL and PT – with an engaging stories, attractive illustrations and thoughtful interactive features to support the learning and teaching contents related to the Sustainable Development, adequate to the specific age group of pre-school children.
The eBook, as planned, was developed considering the frameworks for ESD education that are currently in use in European countries. Together with the interactive stories, Facilitator’s Guide was developed which is dedicated for teachers and parents, to help them make the most out of the learning opportunity provided by the interactive learning eBook. The results are available at: https://greenopolis.erasmus.site 
Intangible results:
As result of the project, Teachers improved competences in ESD and STEM and are more aware of their importance. They now have access to an innovative and user-friendly tool for ESD that can be used in various settings and are better prepared to support ESD initiatives in the future.
Also children are more aware of the importance of ESD and STEM and have access to an innovative and user-friendly tool for ESD that can be used in various settings, they also gained new competences on ESD and STEM. Moreover, they have a new tool to develop transversal competences like literacy, storytelling, ICT skills, etc.
In addition, also parents have access to an innovative and user-friendly tool for ESD that can share with their children and their own competences in ESD and STEM improved. 
The project caused also increase of awareness about the importance of ESD among stakeholders as well as among participating organisations which during the project development gained many other important competences like communication, language, project management and ICT.

New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2019-1-PL01-KA201-065077.title: Teaching programming in primary school: curriculum, didactic methods, textbooks, online support
2019-1-PL01-KA201-065077.summary:
<< Background >>

At European level there exist noticeable discrepancies in teaching programming in primary schools. In Finland, Croatia and Poland teaching programming at primary school is a basic element of core curriculum for general education, but the most advanced and complex schemes are currently being run in Finland, then in Croatia and recently they have also been introduced in Poland. Whereas in Portugal, programming at primary school is only a topic for debates concerning education.  In the era of digitalization and dynamic technological development, skills related to programming and computational thinking are becoming key competences, unfortunately still inaccessible for students in many European countries. The Erasmus + CodeInnova project was the answer to the great demand for educational solutions supporting digital education at primary school level in an effective and easily accessible way. The creation of a uniform teaching data base to support teachers in many European countries in teaching programming in primary schools became the core activity of the project group.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project to be achieved in the years of the project implementation was the following:
To create a coherent system of teaching programming at primary school together with necessary teaching resources that would be uniform for all project participating countries.
Specific objectives to be achieved in the years of the project implementation:
- to create a coherent core curriculum for teaching programming at primary school,
- to design and test 50 model lesson plans to teach programming at primary school,
- to design, test and share 2 textbooks for teaching programming at grades 1-3 and 4-8 of primary school (modified to grades 1-4 and 5-9, in order to better standardize the materials dedicated to recipients from many European countries )
- to design, test and make available the Internet platform that would support teaching programming at primary school.

<< Implementation >>

All planned project activities were implemented. JYVASKYLAN YLIOPISTO was the Leader of Intellectual Output 1: designing the core curriculum for teaching programming at primary school. Joint and coherent core curriculum for teaching programming constituted the basis for subsequent activities of the project group.  
I Osnovna Szkola Cakovec was the Leader of IO 2: creating 50 tested model lesson plans that would be coherent with the core curriculum. Designing lesson plans was the next logical step in implementing the new core curriculum in practical teaching. 
Skolska knjiga d.d. was the Leader of IO 3. They prepared 2 textbooks for teaching programming at primary school: one for grades 1-4 and the other for grades 4-9, and Intellectual Output 4:  they created the Internet platform that supports teaching programming at primary school. 
Zamojskie Towarzystwo Oświatowe was the Leader of IO 5. They prepared the concept of testing, tested the core curriculum, textbooks, lesson plans and the Internet platform involving over 200 students and 20 teachers. 
Agrupamento de Escolas de Fornos de Algodres was the Leader of Dissemination process. They worked out and implemented strategy for disseminating project results within the EU.

<< Results >>

The following tangible project results have been created under the Erasmus+ CodeInnova project (free materials available in 5 languages):
-	consolidated and coherent core curriculum for teaching programming at primary school (in 4 partner native languages and in English),
-	50 tested model lesson plans to teach programming at primary school consistent with the designed core curriculum (compilation in 4 partner native languages and in English), 
-	2 textbooks for teaching programming at primary school: grades 1-4 and 4-9 (compilation in 4 partner native languages and in English), 
-	the Internet platform that  supports teaching programming at primary school, free access.
Platform:  https://www.skolskiportal.hr/projekt/erasmus-2/
Intangible results:
- project participants gained new knowledge,
- participating teachers got familiar with methods of teaching programming in partner countries,
- there was established a new network of partners,
- interest in teaching programming got increased.

2019-1-PL01-KA201-065079.title: Academy of Special Educational Needs
2019-1-PL01-KA201-065079.summary:
<< Background >>

The project Special Educational Needs Academy was a response to the needs arising from the insufficient knowledge of teachers in terms of diagnosing a student with special educational needs.   TODAY's education requires new solutions aimed at cooperation between different institutions in order to improve the quality of education services. To meet these expectations, it is necessary to supplement the knowledge, competences and working methods offered by many professionals on an ongoing basis. Learning from others, exchanging good practices and good solutions is the best form of further development, strengthening educative quality. The project allowed teachers, specialists and teacher-consultants to expand their knowledge on effective and inclusive teaching methods with creative use of ICT in the process of developing key competences among SEN pupils, with particular emphasis on three project areas: with specific learning difficulties, Asperger syndrome and gifted pupils.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, we wanted to increase the knowledge of teachers/educators/specialists working with a SEN student regarding inclusive education and provide them with modern working tools to achieve better results in day-to-day didactic work. The exchange of experience, good practice in terms of new and varied techniques employed in working with a SEN student will certainly improve the quality of education.
Due to the increasing number of pupils requiring an individual approach, an individualised educational pathway (out of 1,000 pupils - 20% with SEN), the implementation of the project was a very important and valuable experience, which has and will continue to bring long-term benefits in the form of a better prepared staff of specialists. The implementation of the project has also increased awareness among parents of problems related to the needs of their SEN child/pupil and possible forms of support. Learning from each other through exchange of experiences, enrichment of working methods, contributed to strengthening of inter-institutional cooperation and development of best solutions for the diagnosis and support of a SEN pupil.

<< Implementation >>

All project tasks have been completed. Due to the epidemic situation caused by the spread of COVID-19 in Europe the originally planned mobility dates were postponed. 
Completed project tasks:
•	developed project documentation (partnership agreements, contracts with contractors, financial and procurement documentation, certificates, schedules of project tasks, training programmes, national courses);
•	recruited project participants;

2019-1-PT01-KA201-060804.title: Life with values - Character-building and european citizenship
2019-1-PT01-KA201-060804.summary:
<< Background >>

Values can determine how they behave and interact with other individuals and with the environment. These moral values can also be considered social and constitute a set of established rules for a healthy coexistence within a society. 
It was our aim to prepare activities designed to developing some values, recovering the importance that the others should have for us. In a society that is so plural, diverse and rich from a cultural, religious and social point of view, it is fundamental that the new generations recognise in others similarities and differences and know how to accept and live together in this plurality. This is the reason that led us to create this project. With different partners from different parts of Europe, it was possible to live together and promote activities that led the students to reflect on their way of putting up with things, but also to see how others react to the same situations. Through digital tools, which the students master and by which they feel attracted and available to use, we have been giving body to the theme, leading the students to the reflection that we consider was missing, since we are facing increasingly radical groups and that can condition the opinion of each one.

<< Objectives >>

We believed that values were one of the greatest challenges in Europe nowadays. It was our goal to prepare activities designed to develop the concept of some values, using web tools, in order:
- to create a common European culture which develops the awareness of human rights based on the values;
- to  have a good practice exchange through a common network with schools in Europe;
- to provide positive interaction by seeing the good practices on the spot;
- to understand and show empathy, love and respect each other;
- to have a positive approach towards human rights for a peaceful future;
- to be more tolerant to the people not just locally, but internationally, realizing that their opinion cannot be formed from comments, but from conviviality and knowledge;
- to provide the students be aware of each person in the world has equal rights regardless of their nations, wealth, power or weakness;
- to consider the relation between values and personal behavior affecting the achievement of sustainable future;
- to reduce the negative impact of the internet, television and the media;
- to promote English as a subject of study but also a tool to communicate with other people around the world.- to gain competence of using Web tools.

<< Implementation >>

During the realization of our project we implemented many activities, defined jointly by the partners, so that the activities could be worked out in such a way that all the objectives were met. 
During the mobilities students and teachers visited schools and attended lessons in which they got to know different education systems, different teaching methodology and techniques. 
During the mobilities students and teachers attended classes using webtools 2.0. They got to know new tools such as: Kahoot, Padlet, Wordwall, Wordart, Genially, Canva, Padlet, Pixton, Plickers and Tricider (…). Their experience was used to present  their work  during the mobilities.
The participants of the project did sightseeing in the towns of the partner schools. They got to know culture, traditions, customs of the visited places. They took part in meetings with local authorities  which enhanced  the cross-cultural dialogue between them and all partners.
The students and teachers attended art and sport classes which were meant to enhance creativity, integration, fair play competition and the values related to the project.
The students with special needs who participated in the mobilities made others sensitive and aware of the needs of the disabled people.

<< Results >>

The results of the project are visible through the lesson plans prepared so that the students not only perfect the use of digital tools, but also reflect and recognise new ways of acting in situations, promoting and recovering social and moral values. They got to know new tools such as: Kahoot, Padlet, Wordwall, Wordart, Genially, Canva, Padlet, Pixton, Plickers and Tricider… These lesson plans will be used in other classes, by other students and teachers.
We create evaluation surveys which were meant to measure the quality and quantity effectivity of the activities, as well of the project progression and achievements. 
Presentations about Safe Internet. 
Several works, made by students, such as: Violence in the relationship - Storybird, But this is no fair - Pbworks, Human Rights transnational groups presentations, between others. On Padlet they put Popular music values.
Newspaper about each mobility made with a huge contribution from the students.
Online meetings during which participants realized their tasks especially at the time of the pandemic.
The outputs and results were evaluated by the eTwinning Organization and get the National and European Quality Label, due to the collaboration, curricular integration and ICT skills.

2019-1-PT01-KA201-061331.title: Evaluation of competencies in Robotics Learning Scenarios
2019-1-PT01-KA201-061331.summary:
<< Background >>

This project arised from the need of teachers to focus on actions that have a high probability of substantially impacting student learning in the areas of content literacy and confidence in their learning. The team of teachers who allied to design this project considers that together they can walk through practical steps that ensure students have a balance of low, medium and high understanding of content knowledge and skill that they have a command over their own learning. Our schools should have the vision of looking to the development of their students as a whole human being and create environments with meaningful tasks, collaboration and problem solving are present. The project uses Computational Thinking as a fundamental skill used by everyone in the world, like a way of thinking about data and ideas, and using and combining these resources to solve problems. In order to have success in this task, teachers designed Learning Scenarios to develop the curriculum on Programming and Robotics linking to different curriculum subjects. Simultaneous was created the tool to assess student performance. Also we aspired to open up the horizons of the school at European level and  the adaptation of students to the new challenges.

<< Objectives >>

Competencies needed in today’s knowledge-based society require students to develop the ability to use knowledge in ambiguous,social and dynamic situations
Create environments where meaningful tasks collaboration and problem solving are present
Develop computational thinking in problem solving process
Promote active methodologies
Promote effective collaboration projects between different subjects and the effectiveness of methodologies on developing key competences
Develop assessment for learning as an approach to teaching and learning that creates feedback,then used to improve students’ performance
Promote confidence in learning
Reflect about their work, about the options they made to solve the presented problem
Provide tools for students to determine their level proficiency
Identify core computational thinking concepts and skills and provides examples of how they might be rooted in activities across subjects
Design,implement and evaluate Learning Scenarios to develop the curriculum on Programming and Robotics linking to different subjects
Produce an assessment tool to help teachers to make a rigorous student’s learning assessment/self-assessment
The project aims to be a work that can be used in other schools,countries,transnationa

<< Implementation >>

This project intended to develop knowledge that fills the need of powerful engaging strategies to develop student’s competences for the future and track the accomplishments of each student. 
We've organized a curriculum  proposal defined in  levels of knowledge and competences in each level in order to create an assessment tool to help teachers and students evaluate and regulate their learning. 
For that we've built a tool that will be used by teachers to help determine the performance of students that were involved in the development
of learning scenarios. We have develop a capacity building program to teachers (both internationally and afterwards in our own schools), to co-design Learning Scenarios with educational robotics and coding between teachers and students and its experimentation.We've also develop an online
repository with the set of learning scenarios. We´ve shared our findings in multiplier events which would allowed to disseminate our work, achievements and findings and also to share our results.
We have done international events to develop, design and test Learning scenarios, made challenges with the students from the different countries of the partnership, used etwinning platform to work online and transnationally.

The active participation of all and the full support of parents in our activities
The creation of scenarios suitable for the respective ages of the students who participated in the project
The scenarios were applicable to all subjects in the schools
Competitions were held to produce the project’s Logo, to put in practice skills developed
We created a virtual museum with works of students from all countries involved in the project 
A Fairytale competition was held. In Poland the story won 1st prize and was ‘acted out’ by students using robots.
Questionnaires were created 
A curriculum on Code and Robootics and a Teachers Capacity Building Program was developed
A Tool for assessment for learning was develloped (certification)
A Ressource center is online with all Learning Scenarios designed

Social inclusion

Competence of Educators (DigCompEdu)
Knowledge growth in each and betweenpartners

2019-1-RO01-KA201-063036.title: Space Detectives
2019-1-RO01-KA201-063036.summary:
<< Background >>

Teachers needed to challenge students to investigate-as space detectives- future plans for robotic/ human exploration. Participants explored our planet virtually from space, learned about innovative space technology. Coordinators developed the idea that capacity to use space is a vital element for Europe to tackle global challenges. Participants needed to prove, working together, that Europe is a space power that needed students' investigation: they discovered ways for sustainable investment into better, healthier, safer world. Our project aimed education quality, efficiency at European level. Teachers trained students to work for united Space in Europe, using innovative practices. Students saw space as force for digital era, as part of future. Space fascinated, inspired, motivated them to pay attention to lessons, to debate on space achievements. We explored innovative practices of working with space programmes, focusing on teamwork, combining efficiency with knowledge, encouraging open education advantages. We achieved activities addressed to students with tendencies to early school leaving, refugee students(we got Ukrainian students). Being involved in our activities they came to school daily, had tasks to fulfill. Thus, we combated failure in education.

<< Objectives >>

We promoted STEM competences teaching/ learning, skills, scientific methodology, data collection, visualization, analysis. We improved students’ awareness/ knowledge of global issues; we prepared them for future climate challenges. We used space related themes, students’ fascination for space to enhance their literacy/ competence in STEM-related subjects. We highlighted innovative applications from space; raised career prospects awareness for future space explorers, astronauts, researchers. Using space context, we made teaching/ learning of STEM subjects more attractive, accessible; pupils felt more comfortable, familiar with science. Our activities brought STEM subjects within pupils' reach, demolishing misconception that science is for geniuses. Space inspired us, we used/ disseminated ESA/ESERO space-related STEM classroom resources; we developed resources tailored to each partner’s national curricula. We shared best practices, united efforts to foster interest in space, science, technology among European student community, providing educators, students opportunities to participate in space learning activities. We used advantages of taking images from space; students discovered Earth observation satellites exist, their usefulness. Pupils improved ability to analyze images, extract information; understood perspectives, improved ability to work together, share conclusions.

<< Implementation >>

All 6 partners carried out the activities assigned by mutual agreement at partnership level. We had a structured plan for implementing activities: 4 short-term mobilities of 4 pupils groups were achieved: transnational activity C2-Oct 2021-Greece-4 students from each partner school learned for 5 days together with their colleagues from Chalkidona School; transnational activity C4-Nov 2021- Portugal-4 students from each partner school learned together with their colleagues from Povoa Santa Iria School; C5-March 2022-Croatia-4 students from each partner school learned with their colleagues from Zagreb School; C6-May 2022-Italy-4 students from each partner school learned with their colleagues from Messina School. Students worked in pairs/small groups, being responsible for communicating in all physical/online learning activities with students from partner schools. Knowledge acquired as result of participating to activities was disseminated by them to classmates, parents, friends. Students collaborated to gather and create materials, to use them in completing project products. Students learned through games, plays, models, spatial stories created by themselves. They used external knowledge of specific content to understand activities.

<< Results >>

We shared best practices, innovative learning tools; promoted open education across countries(“SPACE Stories& Poems” Ebook, SpaceD Ebook; Space Vlogs; Drama Workshops; magazine articles; rocket launching; researches/ studies on Moon/Planets/ Eclipses; robotics workshop; Space Tourism Film; workshops at Planetarium, Observatories; painting contests; activities with Italian Space Agency; questionnaires, interviews, observations, assessments, feedback surveys were used to measure impact of our activities). Our products assured visibility for our methods worldwide; acquired European dimension (website). Participants improved speaking, writing skills in English. Students developed capacity of taking initiatives, responsibility for activities, self-confidence, learning to understand/ be understood. Workshops assured social inclusion for disadvantaged & refugee students. We improved school curriculum with creative&innovative tools, methods. Our materials supported teaching activities for neighbouring& rural schools. Our strategies helped students learn better, become responsible European citizens. Local communities developed European identity. International dissemination on Etwinning /School Education Gateway led to our external recognition. Other teachers, students applied our activities on space, giving us feedback. We encouraged them to participate in Erasmus+ Programme; we developed new partnerships by taking part to space competitions; we delivered project products to local, regional, national, European decision-makers, media, to spread our techniques to other European schools. To measure impact, we used updates, visits to project website, YouTube channel, Facebook page; meetings with stakeholders; participants involved in workshops, seminars, peer reviews; visibility in social media, website attractiveness; participation to public events. We maintained cooperation with space institutes, transnational partners; we transferred knowhow information on Etwinning/ School Education Gateway.

2019-1-RO01-KA201-063919.summary:
<< Background >>

We live in a digital era! According to research results of the European Commission from 2015, the ICT sector in Europe “is growing rapidly and creating about 120,000 new jobs each year. But due to differences in demands and skills, and despite high unemployment - especially among the young – Europe could face a shortage of up to 900,000 skilled ICT workers by 2020.”
Today's education must prepare citizens for tomorrow's world, which will be a world dominated by technology. That's why we wanted a project that would open the way for teachers and students to this world of the future.
Coding all together was a project which intended to emphasise the importance of coding training in education, both for students and for teachers. 

We had different target groups, each of them with its own educational needs.

Our students (aged between 14-18) need:
-computational and critical thinking
-digital literacy 
-algorithmic reasoning and problem solving
-cross-cultural interaction
-improving English language and social abilities

Our teachers (and trainers) need:
- an innovative way to learn and teach technology
- enhancing awareness of the importance of coding training
- gaining new strategies in teaching

Our organisation's needs:
-exchange good practices
-internationalisation
-expand the knowledge and experiences in the process of the project in the dimensions of regional, national and international
-add new strategies to the coding training in all partners

<< Objectives >>

Our main objective was to open innovative practices in the digital era for our schools and strengthen professional staff in all participating organizations and institutions, raising the quality of innovative education to the exploration of creativity in children.
At the same time, we intended to increase our curriculum quality through our first intellectual output and to protect our school communities from the dangers of the internet, through our second intellectual output. 
The project's aims were to expand the impact of coding knowledge and help students to adapt to the digital age and to shape their future professions.

At the beginning of the project, we proposed to directly involve 800 people, 100 from each partner. During the project we realized that a double number of people were involved, students, teachers, parents, stakeholders, and local authorities. From the beginning, we have prepared numerous dissemination activities and a large multiplication event through which we can make the results of our project known to as many people as possible.

Of course, an important aspect of our initial intentions was to support individuals in acquiring and developing basic skills and key competencies, recognized at the European level. The cooperation of different partner countries in coding training for pupils should improve the tutors' quality of innovative education and competencies. In contrast to the classical education system, students will be active, not passive and they will improve their creative thinking and solving problems. 

Finally, with coding training teachers we have tried to enhance their usage of technological tools and also the students learn how to use technological literacy in the right way.

<< Implementation >>

We are very proud because all planned activities were implemented and many others were done, because of our enthusiastic teams. All involved students loved to be part of any kind of activity because coding is a passion for most of them. That is why our project was an opportunity to learn, practice and create many concrete results, during the three years of the project.

Besides the official activities of our project (Transnational project management meetings, short-term training staff and short-term exchange of students, preparing intellectual outputs and multiplier event), all partners organized a large variety of activities, sometimes together, sometimes in pairs, sometimes at the local level:

<< Results >>

Tangible results:

Two intellectual outputs. 
        O1 - E-curriculum of Coding-Educational computer program based on the Scratch programming language. The main objective was to create an "e-curriculum" for
