2019-1-RS01-KA201-000835.title: It is OK!
2019-1-RS01-KA201-000835.summary:
The prevalence of autism was 1:10,000 twenty years ago. Today, according to the newest data (Autism Speaks), it is 1:59. This information obligates the community to respond by taking into account several perspectives and meeting the needs of autistic children in school.  Autism is a lifelong neurodevelopmental state that affects all spheres of personality and is reflected in the problems of communication, social interaction and the perceptions of the world around them. Social stories proved to be an extremely effective tool for improving all aspects of social communication and interaction with people with autism.
Social stories are brief descriptions of events or activities that contain clear information about what can be expected of some situation and why. They provide people with autism with an idea of how others can react in practical situations and the frameworks of adequate behavior for themselves and others.Our school has years of experience working with children with autism spectrum. Applying different methods and ways of work, experts in defectology  from our school have discovered that the key to working with autistic children is developing strategies for social communication and behavior modification. That is also a precondition for their successful integration into the system of full-time education. For this purpose, social stories are used.
The biggest problem in developing and applying Social stories is the lack of training for teachers in regular schools and absence of Social stories in our language or any other language of our region. In order to form a unique tool base which will be available in three languages we have connected with leading institutions and eminent experts who have great experience working with children as well as in European projects. Therefore, the project aims to build, strengthen and create the skills of teachers working with children with autism spectrum.
 The specific goals are:
• Make Practicum with social stories for teachers
• Train teachers to use the Practicum with social stories
• Train teachers to create individual social stories to overcome confusing and stressful situations in children with autism
Practicum will enable teachers to facilitate children with autism learning and functioning in inclusive education and by directing parents to the appropriate use of social stories will make children adapt to a wider social community.
I-OK includes 4 partners from 3 different countries:
Primary school "Anton Skala" - Belgrade, Serbia - coordinator,Alliance of Association of Serbia for assistance to people with autism – Serbia, Center for Autism–Croatia, CSOP - Bulgaria
The project will begin with research. Focus group surveys in participating countries will be used to determine the need for a specific topic that is an integral part of the Practicum.  The results of this research will be crucial for the development of the next phase of the project.
After analyzing the results of the focus group, the methodological practicum will be developed using the synthesis of the literature used as the starting point for defining the theoretical basis of Practicum.  It will contain a description of what are the specifics of social interaction and communication in people with autism, what are the social stories, who they are intended for, what is benefit of them, the way they are applied, what types exist and how they are developed. 
At the same time partners will work according to given themes on the examination, search and design of appropriate materials for the preparation of the working version of the pilot project.
PRACTICUM DESIGN - The goal is to provide Practicum ultimate look and structure.
PILOT PROJECT – It will serve to assess the quality and applicability of the working version of the practicum. After receiving completed surveys we will analyze responses and make eventual correction of the practicum according to relevant suggestions.
PRACTICUM DEVELOPMENT - Partner organizations will simultaneously work on specific content related to given topics:
The Alliance develops first part of Practicum - methodology of making social stories that will serve as a teachers tutorials
Center for Autism–Health Practicum
CSOP- Daily routine Practicum
"Anton Skala" - School and Behavior
DISSEMINATION AND EVALUATION - All partners will participate in various activities to contribute realization of the project goals. They will join efforts in evaluation and dissemination of the project results.
Final phase of the project will be used to develop a series of analyzing tools that will help implementation of Practicum and tools for sustainability and promotion of the project. The development of the best analyzing tools will be based on interviews with teachers who applied Practicum. Positive results achieved through this project will be distributed so it can refer to as many people as possible.In this respect, in addition to the above activities, the online demining will be carried out.

2019-1-RS01-KA201-000886.title: The Adventures  of Out-of-Classroom  Learning
2019-1-RS01-KA201-000886.summary:
<< Background >>

Contemporary paradigms in the 21st century education propose educational models which perceive the local environment and the natural surroundings as resources for children's learning. In recent years, this idea has been spreading across the region, however, there are no handbooks and other accompanying literature which would assist preschool and school teachers and educators to improve their professional competences. There is an insufficient number of practical examples and literature addressing methodological and pedagogical issues for a program based on outdoor pedagogy to be implemented. Moreover, one cannot imagine modern education without ICT competences, and existing programs of work with children have not offered methods for working with early learners. A need has emerged to enhance and improve the teachers’ competences pertaining to modern work models in the field of outdoor and ICT. Over a period of 34 months, we have been developing innovative methods of working with children by placing them in situations where they would be able to learn in the local community, nature, cultural, sports and educational institutions, while using digital toys along the way.

<< Objectives >>

Our desire was to create a handbook for preschool and school teachers, expert associates, museum educators and other representatives of local communities, which provides innovative ways of working with children, a methodological framework and ideas for using nature and the local environment as a setting where both children and adults would be able to learn. The specific objectives of the program were pertaining to the creation of a program which would include methods and technologies of work based on play, children's exploration activities and the application of digital technologies (digital toys) in kindergarten and school yards, urban areas, nature (forest, field, beach, park ...), cultural and art institutions, schools located in forests… We particularly insisted on implementing the project transnationally due to the diversity of natural and cultural contexts which impact the curricula of the partner organizations where the authors are employed, allowing them to use innovative ideas and create a comprehensive model applicable throughout the region and beyond. With this program, our intention was to include the use of digital technologies for preschool children and those in lower elementary school grades.

<< Implementation >>

The engagement of principals, preschool and school teachers, educators, gallery employees, as well as technical and administrative personnel over a 34-month period has resulted in the creation of a handbook unique in the region. Its creation was preceded by activities which included research of outdoor programs for working with children aged 2 to 10, exchange of examples of good practice in different outdoor environments (urban environments, schools located in forests, stimulating yards, use of digital toys outdoors...), trainings, international meetings of project teams, texts written by experts, technical preparation of the handbook and translation into English language.
In addition to the above, an LTT activity was conducted in October 2020 in Pula, Croatia. Two transnational meetings with the objectives of reflecting on the results, selecting materials for the handbook and conducting technical preparation were held in Dobje elementary school in Slovenia during June 2021 and in kindergarten Maslačak from Pula, Croatia during October 2021. We organized an international conference for 310 participants (20 foreign and 290 local), where we showcased the best examples from practice and presented the handbook.

<< Results >>

The result of the project activities is reflected in innovative models of work  presented in the handbook "The Adventures of Out-of-Classroom Learning ". Its topic is the improvement of the skills of organizing educational work in the local environment, in nature (kindergarten yard, mountains, sea, plains...), urban areas and institutions of culture, education and sports. The handbook also discusses viewpoints and ideas related to the use of digital technologies in the work with preschool children and those in lower elementary school grades. Two versions of the book were published, one in the national languages of the consortium members (Serbian, Croatian and Slovenian), and the other in English language. The former was printed in 250 copies and distributed to all partner organizations, kindergartens and schools which participated in the international conference where the handbook was presented. Both versions of the book exist in electronic form, available to general public on the website of the L.A.P. project, as well as in the Library of Matica srpska. They are primarily intended for employees of kindergartens and elementary schools, parents and institution representatives involved in the education of children.

2019-1-SI01-KA201-060519.title: Eduskills.plus.Media – Photography as a tool for fostering media education in kindergartens
2019-1-SI01-KA201-060519.summary:
<< Background >>

EduSkills+ Media is an education portal that offers didactic materials and information for implementing early media education through photography. Its aim is to offer teachers ideas, tools and information and to motivate them to try out innovative approaches to media education by offering first-hand accounts of experience of the teachers during the project.
The project addressed the need to lay the foundations for digital skills, one of the basic skills for EU citizens, in early childhood. Media education should promote self-determined, reflective and creative use of media. It requires knowledge of media just as much as the reflection on children’s own use of it and, last but not least, the ability to actively and creatively use media as a tool for their own interests. The project aimed at creating opportunities for children to get to know, think and experiment with the medium of photography. Pictures are the basis of media: a form of communication, but also a form of deception. Critically evaluating pictures is becoming a necessity in the digital age, as most pictures are manipulated in one form or another. Visual literacy is therefore called for and the project partnership has developed tools for educators to address this skill.

<< Objectives >>

The main aim of the project was to improve the skills of kindergarten staff in the field of media education. Several studies as well as our own survey among educators show that not enough adequate materials for kindergarten teachers are available and that teachers prefer when the materials are provided online. 

By involving children in the project activities and offering them opportunities to get to know and use medium photography in kindergarten education, the aim was to help them build their media skills. Studies show that 4-6-year-old children are exposed to media for almost 3 hours per day and that one in four 6-year-olds have a smartphone or laptop. However, their use is mostly passive. Through the project activities children had the opportunity to actively, creatively and critically approach photography and experience constructive use of media.

Another important goal of the project was to raise awareness of parents who play the most important role in children’s development. Studies show that most parents are not aware of recommendations concerning age, screen exposure, media content etc. Through the project activities we aimed at contributing to more awareness among parents in our communities as well as the general public.

<< Implementation >>

Development of didactic materials for using photography in kindergartens was the core activity of the project. Over 180 children in partner kindergartens participated and tried out activities developed by the partnership. These activities encompassed many different topics – among others art, language or math. Project activities also included presentations and workshops for kindergarten teachers – both in partner kindergartens as well as in other kindergartens.

To reach and inform parents, information brochures and posters were developed and distributed widely among kindergartens in the countries of the partnership. Online versions were sent to kindergartens as well as other relevant institutions in the field of early childhood education. Downloadable versions of the information materials are available on the EduSkills+ Media portal and can be used by interested kindergartens or parents.

The materials were carefully planned as well as the design of the EduSkills+ Media portal - the final output of our project - in order to make it not only useful but also appealing for users. It appears that this aim was successfully achieved – a staggering 99% of teachers who tested the portal stated that they will visit it again.

<< Results >>

The main output of the project is the education portal EduSkills+ Media, which aims at offering kindergarten teachers different types of materials for introduction of media education through photography in their work. The portal is currently accessible in 6 languages: Croatian, English, Estonian, German, Romanian and Slovene. The information available on the portal includes: 
1. 51 activities for implementation in kindergartens with ready-to-use downloadable materials and didactic methodology for using the materials in kindergartens - a total of more than 300 downloadable fully designed and illustrated pdf files.
2. Introductory information for teachers about the basics of photography and media use in kindergartens which aim at motivating teachers and helping them to introduce photographic activities in their work.
3. Tools for Photography in kindergartens.
4. Videos with experiences of the project partners from the implementation of the activities with children and parents.
5. Materials for parents include a folder "Kids and New Media" as well as a poster and a flyer "How should children use digital devices?"
6. Photo Library with ready to use, free and downloadable photographs to help teachers prepare their own activities.

2019-1-SI01-KA201-060586.title: Transition is our Mission
2019-1-SI01-KA201-060586.summary:
<< Background >>

We are aware of the fact that providing a smooth transition from kindergarten to primary school contributes to better learning outcomes for children. However, in light of recent international studies (e.g. OECD, 2017) and the perceived increase in school drop-outs in recent years, we saw a need to make certain progress in this field. It is clear that kindergarten and primary school teachers are key actors in ensuring successful transitions, but they operate at different levels and, as a result, often do not share a common understanding of soft transitions between different learning environments or are even perceived as professionals on different levels. Therefore, we find it of great importance to more intensively connect professionals from both levels, to organise joint trainings for them and to build professional learning communities. The project aimed to increase awareness, interest and competences of kindergarten and primary school teachers in order to facilitate a smoother transition for children between kindergarten and school environments.

<< Objectives >>

In the first phase of the project, we wanted to analyse the situation in kindergartens and primary schools in Slovenia, Latvia and Croatia in terms of ensuring a smooth transition of children from kindergarten to primary school. Based on these results and preliminary insights into educational practice, we then aimed at designing an innovative multi-day training module on soft transition for teachers in both kindergartens and primary schools. In the final phase of the project, we wanted to bring together the findings of the research, training and intensive work with partner kindergartens and primary schools and develop a handbook which would combine all the results, findings and good practices.

<< Implementation >>

We carried out a survey on a representative sample of kindergartens and primary schools in each country and included kindergarten and school teachers from all 3 countries. A small number of children and their parents also participated in the survey. Based on the results of the survey, past insights into practice and insights from the learning community meetings with partners teachers, we developed a module on soft transition and conducted a 5-day training for kindergarten and school teachers, counsellors and principals. We also carried out 3 study visits to each partner country, which allowed for even better comparison and exchange of our experiences and contributed to the development of the handbook (it includes summaries of the research, examples of inspiring practices from partner kindergartens and schools and key guidelines for further development of soft transition). Several dissemination activities were conducted during the project to promote the project activities and results (conferences, round tables and other relevant events, the Gateway platform). We also set up a project website and a Facebook page, where the results will be available after the end of the project.

<< Results >>

Three results have been developed within the project:
1) National brochures with the results from the survey conducted in Slovenia, Latvia and Croatia. The research examined the current situation in the field of ensuring a smooth transition of children from kindergarten to school - national brochures are available in Slovenian, Latvian and Croatian, whereas the international brochure with comparison of the results from all three countries is in English.
2) A 5-day training module on ensuring a smooth transition of children from kindergarten to school (the module is available in English, Slovenian, Latvian and Croatian).
3) A handbook for practitioners and other interested audience that can help understanding the importance and ensuring pedagogical, professional and developmental continuity in the practice of kindergarten and school teachers in the field of transition of children (in English, Slovenian, Latvian and Croatian).

2019-1-SK01-KA201-060681.title: SHOW ME MY CITY
2019-1-SK01-KA201-060681.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the program  Erasmus+ with the project called „Show Me My City“. Through this project we wanted to continue in international cooperation among pedagogues as well as  municipalities, improve the quality of professional skills and knowledge in the field of early childhood education and care (ECEC).
As the founder of kindergartens in the city of Martin with the teachers we felt the need for more intensive re-processing of regional education as well as creating new ideas in the field of regional education in kindergartens and improving teaching tools and learning resources.
We asked our partner cities for the cooperation a made a great team-work and partnership among:
- The Slovak Republic – The City of Martin, municipality, the founder of kindergartens,
- The Czech Republic – The City of Jičín, municipality, the founder of kindergartens,
- Poland –  The City of Kalisz, municipality, the founder of kindergartens, 
- Croatia – Češki dječji vrtic Ferda Mravence, Daruvar kindergarten.

<< Objectives >>

Together with all involved partners we focused on awareness of the importance of European cultural heritage in pre-school education.
By implementing of the project we enabled the pedagogues to share their experiences in the field of regional education in kindergartens, to improve professional skills and knowledge and to work together on creation of a set of educationl tools that contribute to raising awareness of the importance of European cultural heritage.
The aim was to obtain subjects verified by practice of another European country to improve pre-school education, introduce information about a city, region, its history, traditional food, ancestors, important landmarks and sightseeings in playful way, develop regional and global education and increase the multicultural literacy of children.

<< Implementation >>

The educational activities were always carried out in one given country. The participants of educational activities were personnally present at the educational process in chosen kindergardens in each country. Totally there were four educational activities and one transnational meeting connected with presentation/dissemination of the project results. 
Apart from the educational activities, the participants were given interesting information about the city, region, its history, traditional food, ancestors and significant cultural monuments. The participants of the project presented suggestions and new ideas to improve pre-school education verified in the practice of given country, they led the discussion and compared state and school education programs. All activities as well as the transnational meeting were held face-to-face and the participants were personnally presented. Due to the pandemic situation in Europe and anti-pandemic measures the pedagogues from Croatia were not allowed to travel to one training activity that was held in Czech city Jičín. They took part in educational activity virtually.
The transnational meeting,  that was held in the city of Martin from 19th April to 21st April 2022 and all participants were present personally, focused on testing and introducing new educational tools and results of the project to wide professional and lay public.

<< Results >>

All outputs and results of the project „Show me my cities“ were gradually achieved by pedagogues, participants as well as children of the kindergartens.
1. The teachers compiled propositions for the art competition called „Top Places in My City“. From all artworks there were chosen the most interesting 12 works for each country. The exhibition of chosen drawings and paintings was held during the transnational meeting.
2.  The teachers suggested content and design of the calendar for the year 2023 which consists of chosen artworks.
3. The teachers suggested criteria and shot a video with children who show and present their own city – important landmarks, interesting places and sightseeings.
4.  The teachers put together the board game proposal called „Show Me My City“ as a learning tool used in educational process to enrich regional education of each city involved in the project. The goal of educational games was to introduce the most interesting and important landmarks and sightseeings to players in a playful way.
All done activities were carried out with a goal to preserve cultural heritage of each country. The participants had the opportunity to get to know the cultural heritage of four nations and their local communities.

2019-1-SK01-KA201-060682.title: Self-identification in a multi-ethnic surroundings as a resource of ethnic tolerance
2019-1-SK01-KA201-060682.summary:
<< Background >>

The idea of applying for the project was based on the request of the future final recipients. 
The Methodological Center for Slovaks living abroad has been working at the Matej Bel University in Banská Bystrica for almost 30 years. As one of its activities, Methodological Center organizes educational summer camps for the children of Slovaks living abroad every year. These became the places of the first project ideas - as they are the places where we have been meeting the accompanying teachers from abroad and have been working with children from diverse minority surroundings. Supported by very active cooperation with representatives of Slovak minorities living abroad, we managed to specify the final goals of the project. However, the final project goals have been current for several years and been repeatedly requested by representatives of Slovak minorities. 
It was the minory surrounding as that the basic idea for the form and content of the resulting didactic material worksheets that were created. To support the project impact, the expert who created these didactic materials also emerged from this surroundings.

<< Objectives >>

Based on the long-term cooperation, we identified the lack of high-quality didactic material in the expatriate surroundings that would accept the specific needs in the diasporic conditions of individual countries. Therefore, the goals and results were to create a new specific and innovative form of didactic material including: 
- options for variable addition of specific examples so that it can be used in each of the minority surroundings, even with regard to its specific conditions and needs. In this way, we solve one of the problems of the previous didactic materials, which were created together for all minority environments and did not respect the specificity of the conditions and thus also the educational needs of these surroundings 
- focusing didactic materials on those elements of Slovak culture in a minority surroundings that contribute to the self-identification of its individual members, with an emphasis on positive perception of otherness, which will result in an increased level of mutual tolerance in multi-ethnic surroundings 
- to be free available in e-form.
Beyond the original ideas, we managed to initiate significant interest in the activities of cultural associations in the surroundings of Slovaks in Croatia.

<< Implementation >>

In accordance with the project proposal, we held face-to-face working meetings in each of the project countries - even during the period of pandemic restrictions. In the initial phase of the project, we identified works published which became the starting point for further professional activities. We also implemented all planned training and educational events - in each of the countries according to its priorities: In Romania we gave impetus to intergenerational cooperation, in Serbia to mutual cooperation between school teachers and in Croatia between leaders of cultural associations. We also carried out an online questionnaire survey. We addressed the total of 67 teachers of Slovak schools and heads of cultural centers in minority surroundings of partner countries, who answered three sets of questions. At the end of the project, we organised an educational and training event, the goal of which was the verification and testing of the final form of the resulting didactic material with the aim that this material reflects the conditions and needs of all final recipients. We also implemented the planned multiplication conference, where we presented the project issues to high school students in Slovakia.

<< Results >>

As a result of the project, in accordance with the plan, didactic material became available online. In each of the partner countries, we worked on a specific topic identified in advance:In Romania the Slovak folk song, in Serbia the specificities of the Slovak dialects, which in individual minority surroundings today fulfill the role of the mother tongue, and in Croatia scenic forms of presentation of Slovak cultures that serve as an important motivational factor for self-identification in a multi-ethnic surroundings. Each topic is just an example, we have also created “free worksheets” usable in various surroundings beyond the scope of the project. The resulting material fulfilled the basic goal: it is freely available on the websites of partner organizations and available for use by all surroundings of Slovak minorities not only in partner countries, but also in Europe and overseas, i.e. beyond the scope of the project. When working with this material, we assume its direct impact on the quality of education in the Slovak diaspora, both through the families of educated children and across generations. The benefit will be a qualitative shift in the positive understanding of the differences of Slovak diasporas and ethnic tolerance.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2019-1-TR01-KA201-077586.title: Future Language is Robotic Coding
2019-1-TR01-KA201-077586.summary:
<< Background >>

When we look at the characteristics that qualified individuals should have; They are defined as individuals who can solve problems, question, love to research, have communication skills, are open to cooperation and productive. The process of raising a qualified individual is also related to getting a good education in the digital age, that is, scientific literacy. A literate individual should be able to analyze and evaluate the basic sources and methods related to the quality of scientific data. Developments in science and technology are possible by raising individuals who are interested in this field and will work in this field. Today, individuals' interest in technology at a young age and the most important factor in their efforts to improve themselves in this field are Robots and coding. In terms of innovative approaches, Robotic Coding will be an indispensable part of education all over the world in the coming years. With the rapidly developing technology, Robotic Coding comes first among the subjects preferred by educational institutions both in our country and all over the world. In this context, our project is of great importance for our institution, our partners and our country's education policies.

In our world where technology is developing extremely rapidly, we need well-educated, flexible individuals with good communication skills and computer literacy. Our country and all project partner countries need a well-educated workforce of individuals who have 21st century skills, are talented, and have good interdisciplinary interaction. As Denizli Provincial Directorate of National Education, we have created our project setup, believing that our project will make a great contribution to raising well-trained individuals with high digital skills.
One of the most important issues among the targets and plans of our Denizli Provincial Directorate of National Education is Robotic Coding and STEM education. In this context, the increase in the number of schools with Robotics classrooms in Denizli, and therefore the increase in Robotics courses, is of great importance for the Provincial Directorate of National Education. In addition, from our project partners; Atatürk Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School, which is one of the biggest schools in Denizli, and Nezihe Derya Baltalı Science and Art Center and our project partner schools in Finland, Romania, Portugal, Italy and Croatia are also equipped with LEGO, Arduino and mBot robot kits and have computers. Supported Robotic Coding classes are available. However, due to the rapid progress of technology and the increasing importance of 21st century skills, it has emerged that we need new education models that will provide our children with the power to dominate the information society they live in. We applied to this project in order to meet the necessity of mutual transfer of innovative methods and good practices in the meetings held with our project partners in foreign countries, and the improvement and development of Robotic Coding training of our partners in line with the objectives of our project. In addition, being successful in national and international competitions in all our project partners, increasing academic success, improving the digital competencies of our teachers, improving the knowledge and skills of our students, expanding our corporate culture and international network, creating EU citizenship awareness and creating a culture of multilingualism are among the basic needs of our institution and our partners.

<< Objectives >>

We were aware that in our world where technology is developing extremely fast, we need well-educated, flexible individuals with good communication skills and computer literacy. Our project topic, Robotic Coding, is an extremely popular topic of interest to all students. Thanks to our project, we wanted our students to develop their foreign language and communication skills, improve their problem solving and robotic skills, as well as build lasting friendships. Our aim is to increase the competencies of teachers and to equip our students with information technology skills and to train them as producers, not consumers. In this context, by teaching Robotic Coding to our students who follow technology closely, we aimed to raise a generation that can produce new products and applications as well as using technological products.

With our project, we aimed to open the world of Robotics to students, to contribute to the students' thinking as programmers and problem solvers, and to improve Robotic Coding skills and improve foreign language skills by sharing good practices among our teachers. In addition, with Robotic Coding, we aimed to teach our students to command computers and robots at a young age, so that they can easily use the basic knowledge they have gained in places where computers and machines are available in their business life.
Another aim of our project was to support the education and development policies of our country by raising awareness for a large number of students, who receive coding education in the national and international arena, who think analytically, who are problem-solving, creative, collaborative.

Also we wanted our students and teachers to reach the fairs organized by institutions such as Tübitak and Teknofest in our country, thanks to the information they gained from our project, to design and compete with them, thanks to our project.

Our common goal in our project is to introduce innovative methods and good practices to students in our education regions, to share our experience and knowledge in the field of Robotic Coding throughout Europe, and to increase the number of Robotic Coding classes in our cities with the support of the authorities.
We also want to increase the interest in Robotic Coding by raising awareness in the environment where our project partners are located, and to produce different and new projects in this regard. For this reason, we turned our project achievements and good practices into a module and shared them on our website and social media accounts. ( http://futurelanguage.org/?p=110 ) We also aimed to support our teachers with Robotic-assisted Mathematics (http://futurelanguage.org/?page_id=687), an innovative education method that we discussed in our project.

<< Implementation >>

Our project was implemented within the framework of the following 4 basic skills: Software (Programming), Algorithm, Programming Language, Coding. The activities we implemented during our project were also planned based on these four basic skills.

International activities carried out in our project;

1st Meeting - TPM - Turkey (Denizli Provincial Directorate of National Education) - February 2020 - Project opening and planning meeting.
Activity 2 - LTT - Italy (Istituto Tecnico Settore tecnologico - Liceo Scientifico "E. Mattei” ) - May 2022 - Robotic Coding with LEGO EV3
Activity 3 - LTT - Finland (Vocational College of Ostrobothnia) - April 2022 - Our lessons are easier with LEGO EV3
4th Meeting - TPM - Croatia (Srednja Skola Valpova) - September 2021 - Project Meeting
Activity 5- LTT - Romania (Colegiul Tehnic Gheorghe Cartianu) - December 2021 - mBot Robot Coding with MBlock
Activity 6- LTT - Portugal (Escola Secundária D. Dinis) - September 2021 - Robotic Coding with Arduino
7th Meeting - TPM - Turkey (Atatürk Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School) - May 2022 - Final Meeting

Local activities we carried out in our project;
1 - Design of Project Logo
2 - Creation of the project website
3 - Establishment of project corners in institutions
4 - Organizing the eTwinning "Robotic Coding" event
5 - code.org app
6 - Karaşimşek Led application event
7 - Circle Robot Design with LEGO EV3
8 - LEGO EV3 Robot activity measuring distance between two
9 - Robot activity based on Colors with LEGO EV3
10 - Line Follower Robot Activity with LEGO EV3
11 - LEGO EV3 Three Point Turning Robot event
12 - Scratch Fish Eating Game Event
13 - Race Car Event with LEGO EV3
14 - LEGO EV3 Obstacle Avoidance Robot Event
15 - Arduino Smart Home System Event
16 - Applications to direct mBot robots with MBlock
17 - MBlock LCD application
18 - Arduino Servo Motor Efficiency
19 - Making an obstacle avoiding robot with Arduino
20 - Arduino Line Follower Robot Activity
21 - Robotics Festival

International activities of our project were carried out according to the above calendar, depending on the Pandemic rules of the project partner countries. All local and international activities that we mentioned in the project application form were carried out successfully.

<< Results >>

The main purpose of our project topic Robotic Coding education is to develop students' computational and algorithmic thinking skills and to make the learned soft information concrete.

Concrete results we have produced thanks to our project:
* A process began where the teacher turned into a guide instead of an instructor,
* Professional competence of teachers and competencies of students increased,
* Transfer of good practices, innovative methods and methods between partners was carried out,
* Students have become a part of the education process that actively participates, not passive learners,
* Students learned to reason and be disciplined,
* The achievements, methods and techniques we gained during the project were made into modules and uploaded to our website and shared with the relevant institutions. (http://futurelanguage.org/?page_id=11)
* With the robotic supported Mathematics module (http://futurelanguage.org/?page_id=687), learning was made more enjoyable and easier,
* Students began to use technological resources for problem solving and self-directed learning,
* At the end of the project, teachers' digital literacy skills improved and they learned to transfer these skills to their students,
* Students were able to take responsibility for their own learning,
* With the development of students' individual and teamwork skills, their desire to participate in new projects and competitions has increased,
* Thanks to the awareness created with our project, the number of Robotic coding classes has increased, the existing classes have been revised,
* The lessons were planned according to the students' levels,
* Teachers have been a good guide to prepare students for future needs by developing new learning techniques,
* Teachers started to use their existing knowledge to produce new knowledge, products or processes,
* It became easier for both teachers and students to approach new technology without prejudice and adapt to technological developments,
* Obstacles in using digital media, which teachers and students frequently encounter, have been overcome,
* Teachers have become an active player, directing students to qualified and diverse information sources, rather than being an element that offers ready-made information,
* A process in which each student receives education with his/her own learning speed and the learning speed of the class is not taken as a basis has started.

In addition, our project gave our students the following skills;
* Gained numerical thinking skills that they can use for life,
* They learned that computers model intelligent behavior,
* Improved positive attitudes towards using technology that supports collaboration, learning and productivity,
* They learned how to use new generation smart devices and how to develop these devices,
* They understoodthe engineering design process,
* Them Coding and robot programming skills improved,
* They learned to take personal responsibility for lifelong learning,
* They understood how to think creatively and originally about how design work and problem solving ability are carried out.

One of the most important aims of our project; It was to increase the number of Robotic Coding classes with the support of the authorities in the cities where our partners are located. After the acceptance of our project, a Robotic Coding class was established at Atatürk Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School, one of our local project partners, under the coordination of Denizli Provincial Directorate of National Education. Equipped Robotic coding classes were also created at the Nezihe Derya Baltalı Science and Art Center. Our project partners improved the existing Robotic Coding classes or opened a new Robotic Coding class. Especially Croatia and Romania and Portuguese partners, who have access to LEGO Robotic Coding good practice examples thanks to our project, have enriched their training methods and laboratories in this regard.

2019-1-UK01-KA201-061946.title: Promoting Financial Literacy in Europe
2019-1-UK01-KA201-061946.summary:
<< Background >>

The need for people to be financially capable exists as this ability is fundamental to overall wellbeing. It is also known that financial literacy is generally lower than it should be. Attempts to meet this need have not adequately targeted younger audiences. Both in formal and information education settings, globally, and across Europe specifically, curriculum and learning activities have not adequately provided age-appropriate learning materials and tools for young children. Changes in society (e.g., availability and use of computer/mobile devices) present both opportunities and challenges for learning in general and the acquisition of financial literacy for the target group.

<< Objectives >>

Our intention was to identify age-appropriate learning outcomes for financial literacy, design teaching and learning materials that facilitators of learning can use both in and out of school environments, provide virtual tools to provide challenge and support for independent learning, provide best practice on how to use the materials and tools, and a reflective academic paper on financial literacy for children.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented planned activities such as transnational face-to-face meetings, online-meetings, collaborative development of the intellectual outputs, piloting of the developed outputs, refining of the outputs in response to feedback, dissemination and mainstreaming of the finalised intellectual outputs.

<< Results >>

1.We have documented learning outcomes which place financial literacy among the key outcomes of age-appropriate education.
2.We have provided an extensive range of adaptable teaching and learning resources that teachers and facilitators of learning can use in different learning environments. These have been arranged on the project website to help users in finding relevant activities across topics and age in all the relevant languages.
3.The Financial Literacy App is accessible on computers and smart devices. The games (activities) are best used in addition to the teaching and learning materials. However, they can also be used as a stand-alone resource to initiate or affirm knowledge and skills on financial literacy.
4.The integration toolkit provides best practice on how to teach and learn financial literacy in and out of school environments.
5.The research paper critically reflects on financial literacy pedagogy and shares empirical evidence on the approach we took in designing these learning resources.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-DE03-KA201-077217.title: Environmental Learning based on Values Education from Early Childhood
2020-1-DE03-KA201-077217.summary:
<< Background >>

Everybody should be conscious of the damage we are causing to our planet. Solutions can be found in education, therefore teaching staff is directly responsible. Environmental Education helps students understand how their decisions & actions affect the environment, builds knowledge & skills necessary to address complex environmental issues. The focus was starting from early childhood. Early Childhood Care & Education (ECEC) is the foundation of lifelong learning. ELVE directly contributed to the European horizontal priority of social inclusion & aimed at creating habits in the children that will determine their performance in the future, a transfer of inclusive & environmentally respectful values. A need was seen in fostering development of social, intercultural & critical thinking competences in early childhood related to environmental learning through formal & non-formal learning activities. Another need was seen in developing high quality ECEC systems by supporting initial & continuing professional development of the staff involved in ECEC, creating & testing tools to foster participation of all children in ECEC by developing competencies & raising awareness of both ECEC staff & parents related to environmental & climate goals.

<< Objectives >>

The needs answered in the previous question resulted in the implementation of the following objectives:
ELVE achieved the implementation of a transnational curriculum for ECEC staff reviewing current provision for 3-11 teachers on Environmental Learning; it includes 31 OER materials for teachers to promote innovative learning approaches, a handbook to enhance professional development, and an Innovative Knowledge Hub to download materials and increase awareness on sustainability and social values. Also, a network that was created during the project lifecycle and will continue to exist after the end of the project will increase project outreach and awareness of environmentally and inclusive approaches for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, with ongoing exchange and cooperation.
The project aimed to reach out to at least 60 3-11 teachers etc. to participate directly in the project development; we reached 582; to more than 10.000 EU citizens informed about ELVE; we reached 163.974; to more than 500 organisations & institutions informed about the ELVE; we reached 190. Via individual contacts we were probably able to reach out to the set 500 organisations.

<< Implementation >>

The activities included 4 TPMs, 2 were virtual due to COVID, 2 were held in Bologna, & Zadar, with agendas & minutes recorded. It involved the development of a management, quality, & evaluation plan, which includes an action plan & project schedule, 4 mini evaluation reports, and 2 evaluation reports that include risk analysis. A Communication & dissemination plan was implemented, with a project website available in 6 languages, a cloud system (FAUbox), a logo, social media pages & groups, a leaflet for online & printed distribution, presentation materials, & local dissemination track documents. A mailing list was created, & there were 14 virtual meetings (every 4 to 6 weeks). 2 financial & technical reports have been produced, with 4 progress & financial reports prepared by each partner. These reports were based on a template provided by FAU-ILI & comply with the requirements set out in the signedpartner contracts. An online repository contains copies of all financial & legal documents requested, such as work contracts, progress reports, & copies of invoices for other costs/timesheets. Finally, all contracts between FAU-ILI & partners have been designed & signed, & payments have been implemented as described in the contracts.

<< Results >>

Regarding dissemination & exploitation, project management and evaluation & quality the outputs have been described in the answer under Implementation. 
Further, the project featured five multiplier events in partner countries, with a total number of participants of 301 (anticipated participants in total: 175). There were four Intellectual Outputs (IOs) in which the following concrete outputs have been produced: IO1 involved the creation of a curriculum for pre-& primary school teachers, along with a review of current provisions for 3-11 teachers regarding learning about Environmental Learning based on Values Education, and the design of 31 innovative materials (anticipated: 25) and open educational resources for 3-11 school education teachers and educators. IO2 involved the development of a handbook in six languages that explains the proposed model of Environmental Learning based on socially inclusive values. IO3 involved the creation of a digital platform for informing, exchanging, and downloading OER materials. IO4 involved the implementation of guidelines on Environmental Learning based on Values Education from Early Childhood in all partner countries, as well as the establishment of the ELVE network.

2020-1-DE03-KA201-077376.title: Supporting Inclusion and Diversity in Teaching
2020-1-DE03-KA201-077376.summary:
<< Background >>

While schools in Europe become more diverse and welcome children with different socioeconomic, cultural, religious, language backgrounds, their inclusion in the classroom remains a challenge. In the 2016 Communication “Action Plan on the integration of third country nationals” the European Commission recognised the role of schools in ensuring that migrant children are successfully integrated in society and become engaged citizens, but highlighted that inclusive education should be supported. Building on this, the 2018 Council Recommendation on promoting common values, inclusive education and the European dimension of teaching stressed the importance of ensuring effective and equal access to quality inclusive education with the necessary support for all learners, including those from migrant backgrounds. UNHCR/UNICEF/IOM echoed the calls for additional support to educators in 2019. In response to these developments, a strategic partnership was created in 2020 to set up the Erasmus+ project "Supporting Inclusion and Diversity in Teaching " (SIDiT) that aims to promote the social inclusion of students -including migrants- in the long run by supporting primary school teachers to engage in more inclusive teaching in their classrooms.

<< Objectives >>

The premise of the project is that students' successful inclusion in the classroom is a vital first step for them to acquire the mindset and skills they need to successfully integrate in society. To achieve this, SIDiT proposes an innovative teaching approach, founded on principles of inclusive and intercultural education and inspired by EntreComp and DigComp, which facilitates student-led, project-based work in the classroom on topics of culture, social justice, religion and identity. The project's objectives were: - To develop a teaching methodology focused on ensuring the inclusion of *all* students in classroom activities, while at the same time teaching transversal skills that are equally vital to social inclusion, such as learning to learn, critical thought, media and digital literacy, entrepreneurship or languages; - To improve teachers’ capacity to teach in a fully inclusive manner, regardless of their students’ diverse abilities and background, through the development of a training course which can train primary school teachers to implement the SiDiT methodology; - To encourage the broader adoption and mainstreaming of the SIDiT teaching methodology in primary schools, through the development of Policy Recommendations.

<< Implementation >>

The SIDiT partnership was formed by nine organisations from six different countries; led by Goethe-Institut (DE), it involved primary schools (Toverfluit and Unescoschool, BE), universities (Marino Institute of Education, IE and Par University College, HR), organisations active in the field of education and inclusion (Bantani Education, BE and Materahub, IT), a specialist in educational software (CCS Education, IE) and the University of Athens (EL). 
A set of activities were implemented by the partnership: New and innovative teaching and learning tools were developed, tested and validated in diverse classrooms by students and teachers. A rigorous evaluation process was realised to highlight the project outcomes and impacts. A set of policy recommendations were created for the promotion and further exploitation of the SIDiT methodology as standard practice in primary schools in Europe. Multiple dissemination/multiplier activities - conferences, workshops, meetings- were implemented in all the partner countries, with the aim of raising awareness to relevant stakeholders and enhancing access for teachers to the project results, so that they can engage in more inclusive teaching across Europe.

<< Results >>

Outputs are available on the project's website in all project languages: - A teaching methodology in the form of a handbook with lesson scenarios, predicated on the concepts of inclusion, participation, interaction and communication, while focusing on the acquisition of transversal skills of students; -A self-paced online teacher training course incorporating the basic principles of the SIDiT methodology, designed to train teachers to implement the SIDiT methodology in their classrooms;- Policy Recommendations that support the implementation of the SIDiT methodology as standard practice in primary schools, which include a Case Study and an Inclusive Competences Framework. The outputs received positive attention from headteachers, teachers, education policymakers, academics, student teachers, teacher trainers. Partner organisations benefitted from the implementation of the methodology and became “reference points” to train/advise staff from other universities and schools. According to evaluation results from the piloting of SIDiT, participating students improved their attitudes/ motivation/ interest/ skills after the implementation of SIDiT. Students each year (79%, 78%, 85%) answered they would like to participate again in SIDiT.

2020-1-DK01-KA201-075054.title: The "A" class: integrating and supporting students with autism in the mainstream classroom
2020-1-DK01-KA201-075054.summary:
<< Background >>

Why did you apply for this project? What were the needs you have addressed?
The A-class project was designed & applied to meet a need, triggered by the challenges many teachers face, as integration of children & young people with ASD in mainstream education and classroom, has moved significantly higher up on the political agenda in all EU member states during the recent years.
A study conducted by Aarhus University, Dk in 2018, shows that approximately 2.8% of 16-year-olds can be diagnosed with ASD. Significantly more than the 0.7% who are diagnosed for now in most EU countries.
The significantly higher figure means it is virtually unthinkable for a teacher or other associated pedagogical staff, not minimum once in their career, will be responsible to make this process successful for the student with ASD.

Studies also show that this integration is not very successful. Far too many children/youngsterse with ASD do not thrive. This is primarily because schools & the educational staff lack the knowledge/skills to solve this task, which they are often thrown into at very short notice. We therefore meet a need among teachers:  easily accessible knowledge about integration & tools to deal with students with ASD in the classroom.

<< Objectives >>

The ambition with the A-Class project was:
•to offer teachers, pedagogues & other involved personnel, who at short notice become key players in the integration of children & young people with ASD in regular education and classrooms, a quick access to inspiration, increased knowledge, strengthened skills, so that this integration process proceeds more successfully.
•to design a model, based on the ABA method, to show how many other experiential methods can be processed in an easily accessible way for the educational staff directly involved in the integration of students with ASD in mainstream classes and regular educational programs.

The main objective of the project was to fulfil the above 2 ambitions by developing an easy & freely accessible educational package consisting of a number of products, all collected in; The A-class Educational Package. https://theaclass.eu/
 
Moreover, we want to achieve the benefit of sharing the best knowledge & the best practices in different EU-countries, when it comes to handle the challenges & dilemmas in integrating/supporting students with ASD in mainstream education & classroom.
To raise awareness about the challenges/dilemmas it creates to integrate students with ASD in mainstream education.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, the following activities have been implemented.
-Design of Project Management, dissemination, exploitation & QA plan.
-Development of the project logo, website, fb & continuous updates.
- Writting 6 monthly reports
-Building a stakeholder database involving more than 1000 stakeholders in partner countries
-Establishment sparring groups at all partners.
-Organizing & implementing the work to develop the 6 IO products described in the application. Produce info videos
-Implement 3 F2F & more than 8 partner meetings
-Planning & implementation of Train the Trainers event in Brno (C1) & Train the Teachers event in Nicosia (C2), to present the material, test the course material & e. Learning material to get feedback & be able to qualify the material.
-Launching a wide range of dissemination activities as described in the application - including info video.
-Planning & implementation of a multiplier event in each of the 6 partner countries & an international conference in DK.
-Organize and implement piloting of The A-class educational package involving more than 70 professinals.
-Write Interim & final reporting. 
-Implementing learning & knowledge sharing activities among the partners. Including organising studyvisits.

<< Results >>

The most concrete result of The A-class Educational project:
+F2F curricula and 14 modules for a 5-day course, 30 lessons.
+eLearning curricula and 13 modules for independent online learning
+The A-class Teachers Handbook (104 pages)
+Addendum
+Platform for Further Inspiration
+The A-class Teachers Activity Book
+The A-class Behavioral tool(s)
+Infographic to use teaching students with ASD
+Platform presenting the eLearning program
+Database of minimum 1000 potential recipients of info
+Developing all dissemination material incl. videos incl. https://youtu.be/7UV7htKLFpc
+All translated into 7 language

Another significant result of the project is the information spread to thousands of stakeholders at local, national level and among the partners' European networks, increasing the awareness about this tool for a more successful integration of students with ASD. Perhaps best documented by the markedly high level of interest professionals showed in participating in the final multiplier events. Budgeted to reach out for 190 - reaching 301 (58% higher than budgeted)
 
A last significant result was, that many professionals came to know, how easily they can have access to databases of knowledge in other countries in their own language

2020-1-DK01-KA201-075126.title: School and Home use of Advanced Digital Online Worlds in a Serious Game
2020-1-DK01-KA201-075126.summary:
<< Background >>

Young generations grow up in a world which is vastly different from the world that existed just a few decades ago. However, educational methods are very slow to change and don’t appropriately reflect the way that young people prefer to learn. For instance, many young people don’t read books for entertainment any more, so learning from a book feels “unnatural” for them. In addition we have also seen recent developments, such as the Covid-19 crisis, that has closed many schools across Europe, which highlights the importance of alternative education solutions that are easy for schools to implement.
In recent years serious games have shown an interesting potential to motivate young learners. However, so far very few well-working examples exist that successfully combine high motivation and fun with a solid learning experience. For this reason it is necessary to continue the study of new game approaches that integrate learning content seamlessly into the gameplay.With the SHADOWS project we did just that; in fact, the results are very promising and exciting, hinting at a greater need to explore ways of motivating students to learn and develop initiative when it comes to acquiring knowledge.

<< Objectives >>

The consortium intended to build a serious game as a showcase to integrate learning content and cooperative learning from a school curriculum into a game that is highly motivating. The consortium developed the game for mobile devices and made it available for free so that thousands of learners can benefit from it. It also studied the quality of learning achieved through the game, thus contributing to the further development and advancement of mobile learning and game-based learning.
Cooperative learning plays an important part in this game because learners play together against the computer, and they benefit a lot from helping each other acquire knowledge and skills. The game was designed as a mobile learning tool with the intention of complementing teaching at school and we made a handbook for teachers available which helps educators integrate the game into their classes. We wanted to achieve flexible use by a variety of teachers, so we made the app customizable. Teachers can create their own learning modules that are relevant for their students and share them with their class. This of course requires teachers who are able to embrace mobile learning solutions. In our tests the results look very promising and we believe that the game has already started to contribute to making general education in schools more digital and more modern.

<< Implementation >>

We started out with research activities in which we determined how a game of this kind would need to be built. Our research and experimentation phases ended with the development of a game concept and a pedagogic concept.
We then started the development phase in which we created the game and game content. During this phase we constantly ran test events in which we tested the game and the content. These tests gave us a lot of valuable experience and information. For instance, we tested how much time was needed to answer the questions and we experimented a lot with the type of questions and how to inspire students and motivate them. 
Throughout the project we had project meetings which were essential for getting everyone together, discussing experiences and opinions and adapting our work strategies according to the needs of everyone.
In the end we put a lot of effort into dissemination activities, sharing the game on a local level but also through bigger channels on national levels or even international levels. We also ran multiplier events in all countries in order to let other educators know about the game.

<< Results >>

In the project SHADOWS the consortium developed a serious game that can be played on mobile devices and meets the challenge of helping the player acquire knowledge while at the same time being fun to play. Our idea was to create a game in which the learners play heroes in a fictional kingdom overrun by darkness. Symbolically the darkness represents ignorance, and the learners need to work together to return light (which symbolizes knowledge) to the kingdom. Their heroes can defeat the darkness by vanquishing the forces of ignorance in combat which is powered by successfully answering questions before running out of time and solving little tasks at various difficulty levels. Thus, in order to be successful the learners need to acquire knowledge and skills related to different subjects in school. For instance, the players might have to clear an area in which they need mathematical skills.
In the project we created a game concept and a learning concept and we built the game as an app which we made freely available on Google Play and on the Apple AppStore. 
We also created a handbook for teachers along with instructional videos to make it easier for educators to use the game. These outputs have the role of making it easier for other educators to take advantage of the game and implement it in their class easily. They also give educators more background knowledge and share the experience we gathered and the results of our studies regarding how the game can impact learning.
We created a web platform for adding and editing questions for the game so that teachers can actually customize the game to make it relevant for the content they teach.

2020-1-ES01-KA201-082894.title: Children’s rights, UP! Preventing child sexual abuse through the promotion of key competences and healthy behaviors in young children from all cultures
2020-1-ES01-KA201-082894.summary:
<< Background >>

Child sexual abuse is a phenomenon in Europe, affecting approximately 20% of the population. The consequences of child sexual abuse can be diverse: impact in the psychological, social, and educational spheres, increasing the risk of dropping out. They may also affect the acquisition of key competences. Prevention at an early age is vital and involves the entire community. Before this project, there was no specific prevention programme for child sexual abuse that could be applied in preschool classrooms (4 and 5-year-old boys and girls) adaptable to any context regardless of the culture, religion, or social context; present in the European context and involving the most critical agents in the children's life: the school and the family.
The Children's rights project, UP! responds to all of the above, being able to generate a comprehensive prevention program for child sexual abuse capable of training, raising awareness, and developing tools for the educational community, for families, and children. As a result of this project, five tools (intellectual products) have been created for the different target groups, interconnected.

<< Objectives >>

The project's main objective was to create a programme for preventing child sexual abuse that can be applied in any existing reality regardless of their cultural, religious, or social context in the European environment and capable of involving the educational community, families, and children of 4 and 5 years. The objectives we wanted and we have achieved are the following:
1) Promote the sexual education of boys and girls of 4 and 5 years from health promotion, previously training teachers. 
2) Overcome existing obstacles to developing abuse prevention programmes through awareness-raising instruments. 
3) Offer tools so that teachers can prevent and address situations of child sexual abuse in the classroom through realistic, quality, structured information adapted to every stage. 
4) Offer families tools to prevent child sexual abuse from everyday life through information adapted to their context.

<< Implementation >>

The implementation has been divided into three blocks:

Partners: 3 Transnational Meetings whose objectives were to start the project, agree on a work methodology and distribute tasks, to review and improve the products, to prepare the European conference and establish a dissemination strategy. In addition, 7 bimonthly meetings have been held to evaluate the project's development.

Creation process: Participatory activity of 4 and 5-year-old boys and girls in choosing characters and scenes from the stories (O2). Group of 10 experts from Europe and 4 discussion groups to externally evaluate all the products.

Evaluation and dissemination: Pilot test: the 5 products were tested in 8 different European schools with teachers, boys and girls, and their families. It prioritised its implementation in multicultural contexts, with different family structures and religious or political diversities, also at a socioeconomic level and geographical diversity. National and International Seminars whose objective was to present and disseminate the project and its results. Conference in Brussels (February 6, 2023) the project and its results were presented internationally.

<< Results >>

5 innovative intellectual products have been created which are able to interconnect different social agents: A didactic guide for preschool teachers (O1). This guide gives coherence to the rest of the products. Information on sexual abuse is provided, detailing how to prevent it in the classroom through different activities (using both stories (O2) and different visual products (O5)). The programme also involves the family in prevention stage (O4). In addition, a free and open access online course (O3) was created emphasizing the importance of promoting a healthy sexual education. The products are intended to achieve the following objectives: In the case of teachers and families, it provides knowledge about child sexual abuse, promotes awareness and highlights the tools for its prevention; for children, to work on the complexity of emotions, sexuality and abusive situations adapted to their psychosocial development. After the analysis of the results, they showed an increase in awareness, knowledge of the abuse and tools for its management. Another result showed the impact that the project had on the partners, increasing the knowledge acquired during those two years of work.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2020-1-ES01-KA201-083255.title: Give value to nature: learn how to measure what ecosystem services do for us
2020-1-ES01-KA201-083255.summary:
<< Background >>

The University of Salamanca has been working in recent years on a new paradigm of understanding the relationship between humans and nature, the ecosystem services. Ecosystem services are all the benefits we obtain from nature and aim to emphasise and value the importance that nature and biodiversity have in our lives. The ecosystem services paradigm is on all international environmental agendas, with multiple initiatives such as IPBES (Intergovernmental Platform for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services) under the auspices of the United Nations, the ESP (Ecosystem Services Partnership), the SEEA (System of Environmental Economic Accounting) of UN, or private initiatives such as the Capitals Coalition. It has also quickly found its way onto EU agendas, being at the basis of its Biodiversity Strategy and Climate Change Adaptation Strategy. It is also in all spatial planning policies and other sectoral policies related to energy, fisheries or forestry. There are many research projects funded by the European Union: Esmeralda, Maes, Marfebes, Selina, some of which have already been completed. However, although this paradigm shift is taking place rapidly, it has hardly reached university classrooms, let alone secondary schools.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of ValuingNature Erasmus+ has been to introduce the concept of ecosystem services and nature's contributions to humans in European secondary school classrooms. To do so, we have sought to generate the necessary materials, first, to train the teachers themselves, and second, to generate content and resources that can be used in the classroom, always with a transversal vision of the environment and adapted for different ages. Furthermore, from the very conception of the project, it was intended to be a reflection of European cultural and biogeographical diversity, including partners in the Arctic, Boreal, Alpine, Continental, Atlantic and Mediterranean biogeographical regions. All this in a context of climate change and rapid cultural loss. The aim is that, as early as secondary school, students will reflect on the value of nature in their lives and that this will lead to greater environmental awareness and a better understanding of European environmental and cultural diversity and the links between culture and nature.

<< Implementation >>

Intellectual outputs
O1. Mooc for Teacher Training in Ecosystem Services
O2. APP for Ecosystem Service Environmental and Economic Valuation
O3. Web Platform with Education Resources on Ecosystem Services
O4. E-Book about Intergenerational Dialogues on Ecosystem Services

Multiplier Events
E1. Why introduce ecosystem services into the classroom? A MOOC for teachers (Alcañices, Spain)
E2. Nature pays for us. An educational APP for the economic valuation of ecosystem services (Katerini, Greece)
E3. Intergenerational dialogues about ecosystem services and the relationship between people and nature. An E-Book (Alcañices, Spain)
E4. Ecosystem Services in Baltic Schools. Resources for Teaching from an Erasmus+ Project (Utena, Lithuania)
E5. International Conference: One Europe, Different Relations of European Cultures with Nature. Ecosystem Services under Climate Change. The results of an Erasmus+ Project (Ploce, Croatia)

Transnational Training Activities
C1. Training in Ecosystem Services and Economic Valuation of Natural Capital (Salamanca, Spain)
C2. Training about Different Human-Nature Relationships in Europe under Climate Change (Nuuk, Greenland)
C3. Learning to Work with ValuingNature APP and Web Platform (Katerini, Greece)

<< Results >>

During the project 4 intellectual products were generated that can be consulted and used from the project website https://valuing-nature.eu/moodle/. Specifically, these four IOs were developed to cover the necessary steps to introduce the ecosystem services paradigm in a transversal way in secondary school classrooms. First, it is necessary to train the teachers themselves, for which a MOOC for teacher training (IO1) was created. To have resources with which to work in the classroom from different disciplines and for different age groups, a web platform was generated with proposals for activities to be developed in the classroom (IO2) and with the experiences of teachers who have developed them in culturally and environmentally different countries. In order to work with technologies and provide more resources, the first European APP for the economic valuation of ecosystem services was developed (IO3). Finally, to help students understand how the relationships between humans and nature change over time, which is important in the context of climate change, an E-book on intergenerational dialogues (IO4) was produced.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
