2020-1-FR01-KA201-080130.title: Open up
2020-1-FR01-KA201-080130.summary:
<< Background >>

In line with the European Disability Strategy 2010-2020, European mainstream schools and youth organisations are facing the challenge to include an increasing number of children and teenagers with disabilities. However, educational systems offer only locally bound support to youths with sensory disorders. Special education teachers exist but many ‘regular teachers’ working in mainstream schools are not sufficiently trained for supporting pupils with sensory disorders, nor ready to facilitate their integration. Similarly, youth workers working in mainstream youth organisations face the same challenges.
The partnership consisted of a balanced geographical representation of different types of organisations that cover the complementary expertise needed for this project. It included 4 Health & social care organisations specialised in sensory disorders, 1 VET organisation and 1 SME specialized in web design. Our choice was to focus on visual and hearing impairments, which include many types of impairments. It was motivated by the conviction that this project format allowed us to produce new tools that cover these two fields of disability relatively well, without claiming to provide all the answers.

<< Objectives >>

Our overall objective was to develop the professionals’ capacity to ensure quality inclusive education for children and teenagers with visual and hearing impairments. We specifically targeted formal and non-formal education professionals working in mainstream institutions that are facing the challenge to include an increasing number of children and teenagers with visual and hearing impairments. Our ambition was to pool the six project partners’ good practices in order to co-create, test, and evaluate innovative tools to improve the quality of inclusive education in Europe. In order to achieve this, we have set the following Specific Objectives:
- Co-developing a Guide for professionals detailing the profile of ‘resource person’, knowledge & attitudes that he/she has to have and is able to share 
- Building the capacities of professionals to act as ‘resource persons’ through the co-creation of a new training 
- Boosting the digital skills of professionals through the development of the Open up OERs & training (i.e. e-learning platform)
- Raising awareness of mainstream schools, youth organisations & policy makers on the specific needs for including our end-beneficiairies
- Promoting the transferability of the Open up approach.

<< Implementation >>

Our activities were mainly focused on the co-creation, testing, and evaluation of a set of new tools, that include a guide for professionals, a training curriculum; a OER platform (i.e. e-learning platform) and a joint statement. These activities were referred as ‘Intellectual Outputs’ or ‘IOs’. Each of them was led by one or several project partners and all the partners had to contribute to all IOs by giving their inputs and feedback during their development and testing phases and their translations in their national languages. Alongside this, in order to ensure that the Open up tools were accepted and useful for both formal and non-formal professionals, we have consistently applied a bottom-up approach by organising regular multidisciplinary board meetings where members have been able to share their experiences in order to constantly improve and refine our tools. Their feedback and recommendations enabled us to adapt our IOs to our 4 national contexts and to ensure their transferability.
The other important project activities consisted of ‘project management and implementation’, ‘evaluation & quality assurance’ and ‘dissemination and use of project’s results. All the project partners contributed to these activities as well.

<< Results >>

Our project activities described above enabled us to achieve the objectives previously mentioned. Our IOs can be described as following: 
The Open up Guide for Professional is a handbook divided in two main sections: ‘A - How to support blind or partially sighted youngsters’; ‘B - How to support deaf of hard of hearing youngsters’ in mainstream schools or youth organisations. This handbook also defines the profile of ‘resource person for sensory disorders’;
The Open up Training Curriculum is a roadmap/training tool for the trainers to train the formal and non-formal education professionals to act as the ‘resource person’ defined in the Guide;  
The Open up Educational Resources (OER) platform is a set of e-learning sessions and a self-assessment tools accessible via our website;
The Open up Joint Statement for inclusive education consists of a political and strategic paper aiming at providing policy makers in the field of education, with tailored information and recommendations for improving the quality of inclusive education in Europe.
In total, 404 persons were directly involved in this project and and 6 761 stakeholders of inclusive education have heard about it and potentially use the IOs described above.

2020-1-FR01-KA201-080193.title: Make Europe Great Again
2020-1-FR01-KA201-080193.summary:
<< Background >>

The MEGA project - Make Europe Great Again - began with the observation that, although schools play a fundamental role in education about EU and the creation of a European identity, there are questions about how this knowledge is passed on to pupils.
The EU can only be taught adequately with considerable effort, given the wide range of topics; approaches are often limited, and little is said about Europe in everyday life, the Europe of citizens.
When teachers are asked whether they feel confident teaching about the EU, they say they are sometimes overwhelmed by the complexity of the subject. Confronted with a wide range of documents, websites and resources that they have to research and adapt, most consider getting knowledge about the EU to be a difficult and time-consuming task. 
This lack of initial and ongoing training can be a barrier to education about EU in the classroom.
Yet research shows that an overwhelming majority of young Europeans believe that learning about EU should be part of compulsory school education (2017).
 
That is why MEGA wanted to bring a new way of teaching about Europe, by supporting the work of secondary school teachers and pupils in Croatia, France, Germany, Portugal and Spain.

<< Objectives >>

MEGA aimed to strengthen a sense of belonging to the European project, both among pupils aged 13 to 17, at a time when they are learning to become citizens, and among teachers and education professionals, so that they feel more confident and open to education about EU in the classroom and at school. 
 
To achieve this, the project set itself the following objectives: 
- to propose a new way of teaching about EU - so as to encourage reflection on our role as European citizens; 
- to research and bring together existing high-quality resources for teaching about EU and to save teachers time; 
- enhance teachers' knowledge of the subject by offering them innovative training tools;
- to support quick and easy implementation of education about EU through ready-to-use lesson plans tailored to pupils' knowledge. 
 
As a project in line with the missions of the consortium partners, MEGA wanted to have an impact on several levels:

- the target audiences - by providing them with usable and reusable resources and tools;
- the partner organizations themselves - by giving them greater legitimacy to talk about Europe, train teachers and address school audiences;
- national and European stakeholders - by encouraging them to make changes.

<< Implementation >>

The MEGA project lasted from October 2020 to June 2023. 
During the 1st year, the partners carried out research, data collection and analysis to identify the needs of the target audiences in terms of education about EU: 675 teachers, 1 283 pupils and 80 headmasters were interviewed across all partner countries. The beta version of the project platform was published with the material library (translated and adapted into 6 versions).
After that, the partners concentrated on creating e-learning modules for teachers and lesson plans for pupils. Research activities and creation of content were combined with the development of the platform and a substantial amount of work translating/adapting the resources.
In year 3, a piloting was organized in each country to assess the impact of the productions. Feedback from 86 teachers and 937 pupils was analyzed in the project's final outputs, the 6 policy papers.  
 
To coordinate all this, the consortium held 4 meetings and 15 online meetings. It developed tools to evaluate and ensure the proper management of the project, as well as the real impact on participants and stakeholders. Activities to communicate and disseminate its results were set up throughout the project.

<< Results >>

The MEGA project has succeeded perfectly in its main aim through the production of its intellectual outputs (IO) :
- 6 white papers ‘The challenges of an education about EU’ (5 national versions, 1 executive summary) analyzing how to support teachers and schools. 
- The multilingual platform www.learningeurope.eu. Designed to bring together selected, high-quality teaching materials via 6 material libraries and the other IOs of the project. 
- 5 e-learning modules for teachers; each module translated and adapted into 6 languages. 
- 5 ready-to-use teaching sessions for pupils. For each theme, 1 basic version and 1 advanced version, all translated and adapted. 
- 6 policy papers for a new education about EU (5 national versions, 1 version with a more European perspective). 
 
The piloting of the platform's resources brought out the project's most interesting results: 95% of pilot teachers and pupils were satisfied with the content offered and the way it was implemented, and over 90% of teachers felt more confident about tackling the EU with their pupils. Teachers can use the platform as a generator of ideas. Real refreshment in teaching about EU - it gives them the opportunity to innovate by tackling new themes and perspectives.

2020-1-FR01-KA201-080571.title: TutoDys
2020-1-FR01-KA201-080571.summary:
<< Background >>

This project was initiated to address the lack of specialized educational tools for the 5 to 20% of children in Europe affected by DYS disorders. The aim was to provide practical and effective solutions for teachers, parents, and specialists, who are often ill-equipped to manage these specific cases. With conventional teaching methods often proving inadequate, the dropout rate among these children is estimated to be 30% higher than the average.
Therefore, the need for an online platform offering specialized educational exercises and resources was identified. The project aims to improve access to inclusive education, reduce the risks of school dropout, and equip the adults responsible for the education of these children.

<< Objectives >>

The primary objective of the project was to create a dedicated online platform offering a wide variety of educational exercises tailored for children aged 6 to 12 with DYS disorders. Secondarily, it aimed to enhance the skills of teachers, parents, and specialists in managing these children. Specific goals included improving teachers' professional practices, facilitating individualized support for students, and raising awareness of the unique needs of students with learning disorders. The project also aspired to reduce the school dropout rate and improve the autonomy and self-confidence of the affected children.

<< Implementation >>

The implementation of the project revolved around 6 key activities for the overall success of the project:
A1 - Management and Implementation: Managed the project's administrative tasks, monitored its progress, and assessed its outcomes, all facilitated by digital platforms for communication and resource sharing.
A2 - Process Quality Management: Focused on project management quality and procedures, this activity employed five analytical criteria (Impact, Sustainability, Efficiency, Effectiveness, and Relevance). Multiple surveys were conducted to assess the project's progress and management.
A3 - Quality Management and Qualifications Assessments: This activity evaluated the suitability of the produced content with school curricula and the needs of DYS students.
A4 - Dissemination: A common communication strategy was devised. A strong digital presence was maintained by the partners to promote the project and reach over 82,000 people.
A5 - Digital Presence: Development of a visual identity and a website to facilitate the dissemination of the project.
A6 - Exploitation: Guided external collaborations, ensuring that the project's resources remain available online in the long term.

<< Results >>

The project resulted in the creation of a comprehensive, freely accessible, and free multilingual online learning platform, specifically designed for children aged 6 to 12 with DYS disorders. This tool offers over 6,900 educational exercises and resources in English, French, Croatian, Bulgarian, and Italian, enriched with multimedia elements and reward mechanisms to encourage learner engagement. For educators, parents, and specialists, the platform acts as a reliable tool to supplement and support learning. It also provides a space for tracking and communication between all stakeholders involved in the child's education, including pre-detection tests to better guide educational support and practical guides for using the platform. The TUTODYS project has thus produced concrete results in terms of tools and methods for the inclusion and support of children with DYS disorders in the European educational system.

2020-1-HR01-KA201-077665.title: I will survive!
2020-1-HR01-KA201-077665.summary:
<< Background >>

Working with students with developmental disabilities, as well as regular school students, we have noticed that they do not cope well in extraordinary dangerous situations. In order to prevent unwanted consequences, we wanted to design an optional subject that would be offered to students at school and that would help them prepare for situations they might find themselves in during their lives, which are a potential threat to their life and health. Therefore, we decided to gather partners with relevant knowledge from different fields, write a curriculum, syllabus, manual, create open educational content related to the curriculum, prepare teaching materials to help teachers in implementation, and evaluate the program with students on a short evaluation mobility.

<< Objectives >>

With this project, we wanted to create a new and high-quality curriculum for an optional subject that could be easily implemented in schools, an interactive manual with links to video materials as a means of implementing the program, and teaching materials that will serve as an aid to teachers in preparing lessons. Also, the entire manual and accompanying materials are written and recorded in a simple way, adapted to be understood by students with learning difficulties. The ultimate and most important target group for us are high school students for whom the content created in this project would be useful for the prevention of injuries in situations that are not everyday, for which they are not prepared, and in which they may find themselves and which may be a threat to their life and health . Therefore, we also wanted to conduct a short evaluation with the students to see how much impact we can have on their knowledge with the materials we created in the project.

<< Implementation >>

The activities we implemented through the project were:
1. Learning, teaching, training activities only for teachers during which we learned from partners who are experienced in certain areas and acquired knowledge important for later implementation in partner institutions
2. Writing curricula, manuals and teaching materials and their adaptation for use with students with developmental disabilities
3. Creation of open educational contents, mainly video materials, which are connected with the contents of the manual by qr code
4. Translation of all materials, subtitling, publications
5. Learning, teaching, training activity with students for the purpose of evaluating project results
6. Implementation of dissemination activities for the purpose of spreading news about the project

<< Results >>

The results that we achieved through the project and that can be used for free and found on the Erasmus+ dissemination platform are:
1. Curriculum for the optional course "Survival Skills" translated into 8 languages
2. Syllabus for the optional course "Survival Skills" translated into 8 languages
3. Manual for the optional course "Survival Skills" translated into 8 languages
4. 30 open educational contents translated into 8 languages and published for free use. Each video or presentation is linked by a qr code to the Manual and complements the content of the manual. They are on the project's YT channel on a special playlist.
5. Teaching materials for the optional course "Survival skills" translated into 8 languages
6. Project website translated into 8 languages, where all project results are located

2020-1-HR01-KA201-077710.title: Establishing of STE(A)M classroom concept in pre-school education
2020-1-HR01-KA201-077710.summary:
<< Background >>

STEAM education is a typical sociocultural and constructivist model, which provides children with learning situations and enables them to actively build knowledge and acquire skills through exploration, discovery, cooperation and other channels (Lindeman, K.W. et al., 2014.). And, to this situation was our project dedicated. 
The target groups identified within the project were children and their teachers in kindergartens and their needs were: 
1.Children needed to touch and feel to learn effectively in a way that makes sense to them and in their education process there was a great necessity for introduction of alternative forms of teaching. 
2. Teachers needed an expert support for increasing competences to focus on children and activation of all the children's senses to adopt teaching process - multi-sensory teaching. 
3.The urgent need of more attractive and efficient education approach. Transnational cooperation enabled transfer of experience and good practices among the project partners from different countries. The feedback received from different educational systems was highly important for future improvement of the STE(A)M classroom educational approach.

<< Objectives >>

Main project aim was to promote the synergy among the experience of different socio-economical organisations and Kindergartens, with aim to include best expertise in everyday learning process. 
Main project objectives were:
- to improve quality and attractiveness of early childhood education process;
- to enhance pre-schools teachers’ competences and skills by increasing of their theoretical background and introducing learning by doing method for STEAM related topics;
- to establish strategic partnership among different socio-economic types of organisations for increasing of quality level of education process.

Specific objectives of the project were:
- to develop own and innovative STEAM classroom - based educational approach with large transferability potential;
- to design and implement a special equipment and tools for practical work with kids in the STEAM field that was covered four main topics: Basic Science; Renewable Energies; Energy efficiency, Ecology and Art;
- to improve kids' skills through the alternative forms of teaching especially encouraging experiential learning and team work in the frame of long-term teaching assignment;
- to establish transnational kindergartens' teachers network by using of eTwinning.

<< Implementation >>

With aim to achieve project results PP determined as necessary to have a combination of the following activities: transnational project partner meetings, short-term joint staff training events, short term mobility of groups of pupils, development of Intellectual outputs and multiplier events. The main aim of project meetings were coordination among project partners, on-time preparation of main events as well as monitoring of the realised activities and resolving of the notified challenges that may occur. Intellectual outputs were key project components as the results which have to be achieved: IO1: Handbook for pre-school teachers - How to establish and implement STE(A)M classroom concept in kindergarten classes; IO2: Document for transnational strategic partnership in development of educational process in municipalities of Ludbreg, Kochani, Velingrad, and Kusadasi by using of innovative methods and best practices with included Action Plan for future activities. In the project duration following Learning/teaching and training activities were foreseen - 4 short-term join staff training events. Main aim of those events were to present performed project activities and achieved results in front of the interested stakeholders.

<< Results >>

The results from the project realisation were:
- Developed a new innovative educational approach for implementation of STE(A)M related topics in kindergartens
- Implemented STE(A)M classroom as educational environment as well as attractive and efficient learning methodology in the pre-school teaching process
- Established teacher's network by using of eTwinning module
- Created strategic action plan for transnational cooperation among different socio-economic organisations from regions of Kochani, Velingrad, Kushadasy and Ludbreg, in the field of pre-education with aim to stimulate its development by using of best practices and innovative education methods
- Increased attractiveness of the education process for kids in kindergartens with implementation of learning by doing educational methods
- Increased awareness on regional, national and international level about the importance of STE(A)M classroom and its benefits 
- Increased interest of childrens to STE(A)M.

2020-1-HR01-KA201-077760.title: Empowering girls in STEAM through robotics and coding
2020-1-HR01-KA201-077760.summary:
<< Background >>

According to UNESCO's Institute for Statistics, women are the minority of researchers, publish fewer research papers, are paid less, and do not advance as much in their careers as men. Additionally, gender inequalities at the EU-28 level (and at the level of individual countries) are more noticeable in scientific and engineering occupations (e.g. in 2017, 4.5% were men and 3.1% were women). The reasons why women do not choose STEM are numerous, including stereotypes, gender bias, sociological-cultural complexes, lack of female role models, less experience and lower confidence in their capabilities in the field. At home, boys are more encouraged to take up technology and IT and are more likely to have a tech-savvy father. The RoboGirls project wants to initiate changes, give girls positive examples, increase their confidence and self-esteem towards STEAM motivating them to consider a relevant career in the future, and therefore have a long-term impact on reducing the gender gap. As part of the project, we developed a series of activities for students and teachers in order to achieve this.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the RoboGirls project are to:
1.	Enhance girls’ confidence and self-esteem towards STEAM, motivating them to consider a relevant career in the future
2.	Build the capacity of teachers to implement hands-on STEAM activities using robotics and other technological tools following gender equality approaches
3.	Develop innovative quality learning material, resources and OERs for teachers to promote girls’ empowerment and engagement in digital technologies
4.	To increase and nurture girls’ interest in the digital sector through the development of gender-inclusive teaching activities and open educational resources focused on robotics and coding with a real-world context.
The target groups of the project are teachers, primary and secondary school students, school leaders, school staff, academics, women in the ICT and digital technologies, education policy decision makers and other stakeholders.

<< Implementation >>

In order to achieve the goals of the project, we carried out a series of activities. In developing the Comprehensive guide for educators and the Policy and practice recommendations report, we conducted focus groups with relevant stakeholders from each country to gather opinions and the temporal situation in schools. Conclusions are supported by data from the literature and previous research. We developed an e-learning platform where all developed materials are published. Lessons, workshops, career simulator and thematic school days have been tested with over 1,300 students and more than 70 teachers in five countries. We also developed a Teacher professional development MOOC in the field of gender-inclusive practice for STEAM education in 5 modules, which was tested more than 100 times in the test period. Most of the material is available in English, Croatian, Greek, and Spanish on the website of the project robogirls.eu. Further, one LTTA was held in Athens, attended by 12 teachers and educators. We organized 5 multiplier events, which were attended by more than 250 teachers, students, policy makers and other stakeholders, who learned about the results of the project.

<< Results >>

The obtained outputs of the project are:
1)	Comprehensive guide for educators that consists of (1) an overview of the current situation in Europe and the world, (2) a pedagogical approach to teaching STEAM in a gender-neutral learning environment, and (3) a booklet with 43 activities to work with students. The manual or some parts of it are available in EN, GR, SP and CRO.
2)	An e-learning platform that includes open educational resources: STEAM career simulators for girls, 10 lesson plans, 20 workshops and ideas for 10 thematic school days. All materials are available in EN, GR, SP and CRO.
3)	An online Teacher professional development MOOC that includes 5 modules: (1) Modern pedagogies for gender equality, (2) The basics of the STEAM approach, (3) Use of robotics and coding to teach STEAM, (4) Design a STEAM lesson and (5) STEAM evaluation. Each module requires about 25 hours of work. The course is available in EN language.
4)	Policy and practice recommendations report provides a report on how to reduce the gender gap in the STEAM field. The report is available in EN, and the recommendations in GR, SP and CRO.

2020-1-HR01-KA201-077794.title: GAMe-based learning in MAthematics
2020-1-HR01-KA201-077794.summary:
<< Background >>

Teaching mathematics using innovative methods is a way to reduce the number of students with insufficient skills in mathematics, which was one of the goals of European Cooperation in Education and Training (ET 2020). In addition, it is a way to motivate students to choose a university in the STEM area, which was one of the priorities of Horizon 2020. Making better use of digital technology for teaching and learning and the development of digital competencies and skills were also priorities of the 2018 Digital Education Action Plan of the European Commission. 

Game-Based Learning (GBL) founded on digital technology is a promising method for students to learn mathematical concepts and practice mathematical skills. The use and implementation of this method is an educational challenge in which teachers play a central role and it is crucial to equip teachers with the knowledge and skills they need to excel in this role. 

In these contexts, within the GAMMA project we have developed education materials for mathematics teachers who want to integrate GBL founded on digital technology into their teaching practice. The materials could also be useful for teachers of other subjects who wish to integrate this method into their teaching.

<< Objectives >>

The overall aim of the project was to promote game-based learning founded on digital technology and increase awareness of the importance of using innovative teaching and learning methods. The project specific objectives were:
- to encourage teachers to use and apply digital games in the teaching process;
- to develop teachers’ competencies in game-based learning;
- to motivate and encourage students to actively construct their mathematical knowledge;
- to provide insights into different education systems of European countries;
- to foster partnerships between partner organisations at national and EU levels.

<< Implementation >>

In the first year and a half of project implementation, it was not possible to organise live activities due to the epidemiological situation. During this time we organised the virtual First Transnational Project Meeting (TPM) and virtual parts of the Learning, Teaching and Training Activities (LTTA) in the Netherlands and Greece. After the improvement of the epidemiological situation, we organised a physical part of the LTTA in Greece, a physical LTTA in Croatia, a physical part of the LTTA in the Netherlands, and a physical LTTA in Finland. At the end of the project, we organised the second TPM. The partners developed the intellectual outputs in an iterative process that included phases of work followed by testing or discussion or review by the team members and by their students. The teaching scenarios and games were piloted in the mathematics classes of the partner schools as well as in a few other schools. The feedback on piloting from teachers and students was used for the improvement of the games and the teaching scenarios. After the intellectual outputs were developed, seven Multiplier Events were organised in all partner countries: three in Croatia, two in Greece and one in the Netherlands and Finland each.

<< Results >>

The following intellectual outputs have been developed in the project:
IO1.1. Case Study
IO1.2. GAMMA Handbook for Teachers
IO1.3. Videos about the Handbook chapters
IO1.4. GAMMA Final Project Report
IO2.1. GAMMA Template for the Teaching Scenario
IO2.2. Eight GAMMA teaching scenarios
IO3.1. Manuals for the MaLT2 and ChoiCo authoring systems
IO3.2. Video tutorials for the MaLT2 and ChoiCo authoring systems
IO3.3. Four Focused Authoring Systems (FASs)
IO3.4. Seven GAMMA games

All outputs, except IO1.1., IO.1.3. and IO1.4., are available in English, Croatian, Greek, Dutch and Finnish on the project website http://www.project-gamma.eu/. 
During the project activities, the project-specific objectives were achieved. The project had an impact on changing the research topics of the researchers from the partner universities, as some of them focused their research on GBL. The project participants developed their digital skills and improved their English language skills, increased their job satisfaction, recognised the advantages of teamwork and collaboration, strengthened their social skills, and gained valuable insights into the culture of the partner countries through mobilities.

2020-1-HR01-KA201-077800.title: Artificial Intelligence in Education - challenges and opportunities of the new era: development of a new curriculum, guide for educators and online course for students
2020-1-HR01-KA201-077800.summary:
<< Background >>

In today's hyper-connected world, artificial intelligence (AI) is a vital competency, especially for children and young people. They need to understand what is behind their screen, how social media works, so that they can use advanced ICT safely and responsibly. ICT changes the way people learn, live and work, it changes the necessary skills. The labor market faces a major shortage of experts in the field of advanced ICT and AI. Reports from global ICT leaders as early as 2020 showed a growth in the need for jobs that require data and analytical skills, which increased from 364,000 to 2,720,000 in a year. In 2019 and 2020, when the partnership was established, the partners noticed that the education systems did not have comprehensive educational resources and that only a few enthusiastic teachers were teaching students about AI on their own initiative.
ICT is rapidly developing, rapidly entering all spheres of human activity. Education, which should be the driving force behind changes in society, unfortunately falls short of applying the latest advanced technology. Educational systems around the world do not provide children and young people with opportunities to develop the knowledge and skills needed in the labor market.

<< Objectives >>

General achievements:
- support for high-quality education,
- improving relevance of education systems,
- developing Europeans’ digital skills and making them more visible,
- boosting innovation and digital competences in all education institutions,
- opening up education systems.

Specific achievements:
- the development of a comprehensive curriculum that provide students in primary education with the early acquisition of knowledge and skills to develop future competences,
- the development of methodological manuals, teaching plans, examples of good practice that encourage teachers to teach the latest (rapidly changing) technology,
- creating an international network of collaborating teachers, sharing experiences,
- to share experiences and good practices at local, national and international level with teachers from different schools, local authorities, policy makers,
- provide students with innovative educational content in the field of robotics and artificial intelligence, deepen knowledge and skills, increase interest in jobs of the future.

<< Implementation >>

1. Research of the current situation in educational institutions of partner countries.
2. Development of intellectual results:
a) curriculum for teaching artificial intelligence to students in primary schools, 
b) development of teaching scenarios, video lessons, interactive content, manuals for teachers, 
c) development of online courses and manuals for students).
3. Testing of intellectual results - was carried out in schools that are official partners in the project, schools and associations that are associated members but are not formally part of the consortium.
4. Evaluation of intellectual results - was carried out in schools where intellectual results were tested, at workshops for teachers from different schools of partner countries.
5. Final editing and publication of intellectual results on the project's websites, ESEP and Erasmus+ Dissemination Platform.
6. Dissemination of intellectual results - in partner institutions, in associated partner institutions that are not formally part of the consortium, at professional gatherings and conferences of local, national and international level.

<< Results >>

The project results are gathered around three main results:
1. curriculum for teaching artificial intelligence in primary schools,
2. methodical manuals for teachers, teaching scenarios, video lessons, interactive content and software solutions,
3. online course and student manuals.
All results are free to download, change and adapt to the specific needs and capabilities of each student, class or student.
The project results are available in five languages: Croatian, English, Polish, Portuguese and Dutch, on the project website: https://www.erasmus-artie.eu/index.php,
on ESEP https://school-education.ec.europa.eu/hr/etwinning/projects/artie-artificial-intelligence-education-challenges-and-opportunities-new-era-0-0 and 
on the Erasmus+ Dissemination Platform.

2020-1-HR01-KA201-077816.title: An interdisciplinary approach to mathematical education
2020-1-HR01-KA201-077816.summary:
<< Background >>

After graduation, students often lack math, science, and digital literacy skills, and students' and often teachers' and parents' perceptions of math, its importance, and its role in daily life are misguided. Numerous careers and everyday situations require knowledge, analysis, and interpretation of many mathematical and scientific concepts, an interdisciplinary approach, and also work with digital tools.
Pre-mathematical skills necessary for successful mastery of mathematics and other subjects, especially in STEM, need to be developed at preschool age. Often children have not developed enough in this area in their preschool education, and there is a need to design and implement activities that further develop these skills in the lower grades of elementary school. Interdisciplinary activities are one way to develop such skills.
In addition to the need to find innovative ways to work with students in response to the challenges that modern technology and lifestyles bring to education, there is also a need to train educational staff.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal is to develop students' math, science, and digital literacy. Literacy in the above areas, in addition to educational outcomes, includes awareness of the importance of a particular area for daily life, for the future, and for a responsible civil society that makes rational decisions based on scientific arguments. These are key skills needed in the 21st century.
The aim of the project was to develop activities that, by linking mathematics and other subjects, would foster students' critical and analytical thinking, their creativity and independence, strengthen their digital skills, increase their interest in STEM, but also strengthen the teaching profession.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project, we conducted several activities aimed primarily at students and teachers. We conducted a survey on the attitudes of teachers, students, and parents and analyzed and interpreted the results of this survey. In addition, we designed 55 interdisciplinary scenarios describing the preparation and implementation of activities lasting at least 90 minutes and combining mathematics and other subjects. We conducted each scenario at least twice with students.
We designed a teacher education on Interdisciplinary Approach to Mathematics Education and we implemented that education as an open moodle-based e-course for teacher self-education and teacher professional development in a hybrid format that included 8 hours of live education and self-education via e-course.
In addition, we adapted some of the activities for science outreach and participated in numerous events with them: Science Festival, Researchers' Night, World Science Day for Peace and Development, Pi Day, Evening of Mathematics,...

<< Results >>

The main outcomes of the project are newly developed teaching scenarios that combine mathematics and other subjects in interesting ways to bring mathematics closer to the youngest. The project designed and described in detail more than 52 teaching scenarios, all of which were implemented in primary school classrooms in Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia. In addition, 3 scenarios were designed for special days. The scenarios are available in four languages: English, Croatian, Slovenian and Serbian.
Within the project, the e-course Interdisciplinary Approach to Mathematics Education was developed and implemented exclusively for teacher training, and four teacher training workshops on the same topic were designed and conducted.
A survey was conducted on the attitudes of students, parents and teachers towards mathematics and mathematics education. The basic results of this research were taken into account in the design of the scenarios, but they also resulted in a scientific work in which the results of the conducted test are analyzed in detail.
3 articles were published about the activities developed within the project, and a mathematical exhibition entitled "Taxi Geometry" was designed and set up.

2020-1-HR01-KA201-077826.title: Kids in Clouds
2020-1-HR01-KA201-077826.summary:
<< Background >>

“Kids in Clouds” is a project designed to meet challenges of the modern education system and challenging market needs, by providing an awareness-raising, holistic and flexible education in cloud-computing. The cloud-based services are growing rapidly in the global and European economy. With the rise of 5G technology not only storage but also all data processing and applicative services will move to the cloud environment. This change is anticipated to come in the next 10 years. The move towards cloud-based environment will tremendously impact our work environments, as well as in general the way we use ICT solutions on a daily basis.

If we want to reap the benefits of technology to achieve green and circular economy, one of the most basic preconditions we must satisfy is switching heavily from on-premise to cloud-based environment – and not only for data files storage, but for collaboration, communication, and service providing. We have established that switching from working in on-premise to cloud-based environment creates significant obstacles for users, as it requires them to relate to high-tech solutions in a different way. Therefore, partnership applied for this project with an aim to introduce cloud-based environment to children at the beginning of their primary school learning path. At that point, children do not differentiate on-premise from cloud-based content and services – for them, these are simply the tools to get things done. Sooner they encounter cloud-based services, easier it is for them to learn how to interact with them. We believe it is hugely important to teach children as early as possible to get acquainted and comfortable in the cloud-based eco-system, as this will be the environment they will live and work in already ten years from now.

Why are so many businesses moving to the cloud? It is cost-efficient, secure, fast. Clouds enable us to work from anywhere. If we have learned anything during the current COVID-19 pandemic, it is that sectors of society which are better connected to internet can live through the lockdown much more successfully. Countries where educational systems had a stronger and more robust cloud-infrastructure and cloud-services were able to keep the school year going in a much better way. Additionally, moving to cloud is also environmentally friendly. When you use the cloud, you only use the energy you need: if you use only one application, you do not waste energy for powering an entire computer; therefore, you do not leave oversized carbon footprints.

Finally, together with helping students learn how to use cloud for educational purposes, partnership also addressed the need for empowering teachers for bringing cloud-computing to their lessons on a regular basis and therefore incorporate cloud usage to their teaching process.

<< Objectives >>

“Kids in Clouds” is an interdisciplinary project whose aim was to introduce children with cloud-based services as early as the first grade of the primary school. Its main objective was to deliver well-rounded, useful and transferable educational programme in cloud-computing through development of educational modules for teachers and pupils, adaptation of contents and methods according to envisaged needs of the target groups, creation of didactic tools and production and recommendations on innovative education approaches. 
Overall, these were three primary goals of this project:
1) to make the first step towards overcoming the gap between the need and the current state of understanding of cloud-based technologies
2) to promote cloud-computing as an essential tool for the present and the future
3) to enhance cross-curricular transferability of learning outcomes in different teaching subjects.

Other specific goals objectives of the project:
- support the development of key competences for all individuals from early childhood
- raise digital competences of educators, citizens and organisations
- develop open educational resources
- promote innovative methods and tools for teaching, training and learning
- strengthen the profile of the teaching professions
- increase the level of achievement and interest in STEM.

<< Implementation >>

Partners carried out a wide range of activities in order to implement a high-quality, well-rounded project with the objective to develop educational content in cloud-computing for schools, which were implemented and used by partner organizations. More concretely, project partners worked on activities aimed towards developing online repository of materials for cloud-computing for non-ICT teachers to be used in non-ICT classes. With implementing these activities, partnership contributed to popularization of cloud-computing outside of the ICT field, which is strongly needed for achieving a stronger use of cloud-computing.
This project was carried out transnationally, because if we are to achieve the European digital single market, we must work very hard towards levelling national and regional differences. Since, partners of this project together have knowledge and experience to produce extensive cross-sectoral outputs, partnership has been formed and have jointly worked on the following project activities:
-	project management and coordination
-	conducting dissemination activities
-	preparing and conducting the research as part of Intellectual Output 1; analyzing obtained results and preparing the final output - Gap analysis
-	designing and creating digital educational materials for teachers as part of Intellectual Output 2 
-	creating the online repository of digital educational materials for teachers
-	piloting the newly developed educational materials for teachers as part of Intellectual Output 3; 
-	designing and creating digital educational materials for children as part of Intellectual Output 4 
-	creating the online repository of digital educational materials for children
-	piloting the newly developed educational materials for children as part of Intellectual Output 5; 
-	preparing guidelines and recommendations on how to implement cloud-based computing content as a horizontal element in curricula, including tailoring recommendations so as to fit the demands of the three different national education systems that are partnering in this project (as part of Intellectual Output 3 and Intellectual Output 5)
-	organizing and participating on Transnational Meetings and online partners’ meeting
-	organizing the Multiplier Event.

<< Results >>

The project results are the direct answer to the envisaged target groups’ needs, and they comprise a complete set of resources for popularization and teaching of cloud-computing in schools across EU. Specifically, they are:
- Gap analysis: report on to what extent are cloud-based services in use in schools at the moment. The report was prepared based on 373 questionnaire responses obtained by teachers. Built on that report, partners further determined possibilities and marked the trajectory route on how to deal with the existing situation.
- Online repository of more than 170 digital educational materials for teachers, open-source materials in Bulgarian, Croatian and French. These materials include general knowledge using cloud-based tools, together with didactic strategies on how to teach different subjects with the help of cloud-based tools from the perspective of primary education.
- Online repository of 52 digital educational materials for children as a series of small-scale school projects for different school age groups, which can be used in different classes (language and literature, music, arts, mathematics, science, etc.); materials were designed in a way to be highly usable to a wide section of teachers and children and through this material it is demonstrated how teachers can achieve the required learning outcomes during their lessons by using cloud-based tools. Online open-source materials are available in Bulgarian, Croatian, English and French.
- Piloting of the newly developed educational materials for teachers and children; materials were developed in one and piloted in another country, to ensure that materials are transnationally applicable and can satisfy the needs of very different national education systems. Additionally, the aim was to demonstrate how teachers can achieve the required learning outcomes in their teaching with the help of cloud-computing. In total, 48 teachers and 186 students from Bulgaria, Croatia and France have participated in the pilots.
- Guidelines and recommendations on how to implement cloud-based computing content as a horizontal element in curricula, including tailoring recommendations so as to fit the demands of the three different national education systems that are partnering in this project. 
In addition to these concrete results, the following outcomes can be reported, which were achieved either by direct participation of target groups in project activities or based on dissemination activities:
- increased awareness about the possibilities and importance of cloud-computing in the non-ICT segment of teacher population
- increased partners’ capacities in developing innovative learning materials/tools and encouraged development and adoption of open educational resources in school education
- higher capabilities and stronger skills of teachers (enhanced professional development)
- support for teachers in promoting highly modern and highly needed teaching and learning for the digital era
- strong support for cross-curricular collaboration and innovative learning environments.

2020-1-HU01-KA201-078764.title: REC: Reflection-Education-Care. Strengthening collaborative and reflective teaching practice - Increasing Quality Services in ECEC
2020-1-HU01-KA201-078764.summary:
<< Background >>

Despite the fact that reflection is a key competence for teachers, collaborative reflective methods are not integrative and systemic part of teacher training and teaching practice. In our needs assessment questionnaire of February 2020 was filled in by a total number of 336 ECEC practitioners working with 0-10 year-old children, the majority of the professionals (55-70%) expressed the need to have more group or individual occasions to reflect on their practice. 
Only a minority of teachers have regular formal opportunities to reflect on their work, to talk about fairer workload division, share necessary information about families they work with, to collaborate and seek for solutions for the challenges that the diverse children groups bring in practitioners' everyday lives. Above 40% of answerers operate on a stress level higher that 7 on a 0-10 scale in every country.  Our initiative offered methods for building resilient practitioners' communities from a professional and personal points of view so they can face systemic challenges on a lower level of stress, leading to more successful cooperation among colleagues and they are able to better reflect to the children’s individual needs.

<< Objectives >>

The goals of the REC project were:
- To promote, advocate and support the importance of reflection on practice by a variety of reflective methods that suits the needs of carers/educators working with children from 0-10 years old.
- To help professionalization, self-awareness and transformation of ECEC practice and facilitate collaborative learning within the staffs who work with children from ages 0-10
- To widen the methodological knowledge of institutes involved in teachers' professional development
- To write a guidebook for ECEC services how to start implementing reflective paths tailored to their needs and to how to choose from available methods
- To make a measured impact on reflective practices on quality of teaching practice so we can increase awareness and provide ECEC institutions teacher trainers and policy makers professional support.

On partner meetings, we returned to this set of goals regularly to make sure we keep the focus and align project activities with these goals, keeping also in mind that the wellbeing of children and families is the most important.

<< Implementation >>

1.  The partnership trained each other so all REC partners have the knowledge to hold collaborative reflective sessions with the help of 3 methods: WANDA, Video Coaching, Peer Observation with Reflective Discussion. Before the project, each partner knew 1 or 2 of these methods. 
2. Since the changes brought by collaborative reflective methods are hard to measure quantitatively due to the processes' complex and subjective nature,  partners learned the Most Significant Change qualitative M&E tool to monitor progress and measure change and applied it through the project, making interviews with educators.
3. After community planning, reflective sessions were introduced and strengthened in 11 ECEC institutions, where educators work with children aged 0-10. In 2 countries, facilitators were trained so schools can carry out the reflective sessions after the project ended.
4. A guidebook was written on how to introduce reflective methods in schools.
5. An impact report was written to show the changes with the help of the data collected (interviews, questionnaires, focus groups).
6. Policy recommendations were written and distributed.
7. Conferences were held twice in each country to show the importance of collaborative reflective methods.

<< Results >>

1. A guidebook on how to introduce collaborative reflective methods in schools widely distributed.
2. An impact report showing the changes brought by in the participating institutions and countries.
3. Video coaching handbook in Slovenian.
4. Eight conferences were held altogether in the 4 countries to promote the values of collaborative reflective methods. 
5. REC project was presented at the international teacher training conference (ATEE) in Budapest as a successful model to increase ECEC quality and to keep educators motivated.
6. In each country, a soundboard group was formed (4 in total) from external education related professionals who gathered regularly on a voluntary basis to give feedback and ideas regarding the project.
7. In each country, the methods used in the project were disseminated in teacher training institutes, educational conferences and professional articles.
8. In Belgium, the outcome of this project will also be integrated into the bachelor in Preschool education and the bachelor in Early Childhood Education programmes.

2020-1-IE01-KA201-066061.title: Climate Change studies and research in the European Union
2020-1-IE01-KA201-066061.summary:
<< Background >>

The main objective of this project was to try in some way to tackle the serious matter of climate change, raise awareness of the key issues and develop our students as independent European and global active citizens. We wanted to carry out real world learning for our students on ways to research the effects of climate change locally, regionally and internationally. We also wanted to increase a sense of European identity in our school community by making connections in Europe through worthwhile socially driven projects that develop our students as independent active citizens. We wanted to give them hope in tackling the climate crisis by acting locally but thinking globally. Lastly we wanted to develop key skills of research, communication, presentation, publishing, designing and problem solving, all of which were realized by our students through participation in this project.

We were all introduced to this project idea by a common colleague of all 3 schools. We developed the objectives together to address the following.
needs.
Combating climate action and biodiversity loss in our cities.
Involving socially/financially disadvantaged students in education
Integrating students with special needs into collaborative practice based projects
Developing key skills of research, communication, presenting, designing and problem solving in our students.
Further developing a sense of European identity and connections in our schools.

All of the above and more was achieved through this project.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to help Combat climate action and biodiversity loss in our cities in some way to show our students that they can make a difference in this very serious issue we all face. We wanted to empower our students to become active citizens in realising change at a local, national and international level.
we wanted to Involve socially/financially disadvantaged students in worthwhile engaging education projects.
We wanted to involve students with special needs into collaborative practice based projects that brought real world problems into their learning.
We wanted to Develop key skills of research, communication, presenting, designing and problem solving in our students.
We wanted to Further develop a sense of European identity and create international connections in our schools.
We wanted to build relationships with other organisations in our communities to affect positive change

<< Implementation >>

The project has been very successfully in all three participating countries despite starting with the pandemic
restrictions preventing us from travelling or meeting our respective NGO partners at the schools as planned in year one.
Last year we completed all three LTTA mobilities to our three respect cities with students. All learning outcomes have
been achieved to date and all three Transnational meetings and multiplier events have been held. 
This project has had a greater impact in our school communities, locally and nationally in all three countries receiving a
lot of media attention and also in forming unexpected partnerships with other organisations like ecoed4all, All island
Schools for climate change and the Galway National City Park Initiative..
Coordinators met yearly in transnational meetings to plan the years events and online monthly to keep
each other up to date with activities and events. This was a vital component to keep the momentum we had achieved both with
students research and the corrective actions and awareness we are all generating. 
Students worked with NGO partners in all three countries to research and produce the records aswell as participating in field studies
to fully understand the impacts caused. The students have produced 3 sets of 27 species records for publication. All three
countries have published their 3 sets of records . 
We produced more than three audio visual records per school which have had many views online and we have
all had segments of our projects/interviews aired on National television. We have also had numerous articles in national
newspapers and featured on local radio.
We have had 3 very successful multiplier events in Spain, Ireland and Croatia to disseminate the projects results and
message. 

Unfortunately our wildlife partner EKO in Croatia was not in a position to continue working on the project or supporting our
partner school Susak due to the owners personal difficulties. We met with them to ensure the first years records were
published and met with another agency 20,000 miles of marine explorers during the transnational meeting in August 2022 to
discuss their possible involvement in delivering and supporting the learning outcomes for year 2 and 3. They were happy
to do this which they finished very successfully.
1. Records. All three schools have produced 3 sets of 27 species records as promised in our funded application. All
records have been supervised and stamped by our NGO. and are available online for all partners and public to view.
2. Magazine. The three schools have published 3 sets of records in national magazines as promised in our funded
application.
3. Audiovisual. GCC, Sušak Gymnasium and IES Felix Muriel acquired a drone and have recorded aerial takes of
students forming the species names as promised in our funded application but have all produced additional audio visual
material to spread the projects message.
The lead school Galway Community College has made many connections with other agencies and organisations
through the implementation of the project and working on corrective actions which include. Working with Galway City
Council Parks and environment departments to secure bat owl and swift boxes and native trees for planting on school
grounds, being chosen as a champion school for the Galway National Park City Initiative, becoming a pilot school for
EcoEd4all environmental education and All Island school for climate action in cross border climate action projects. 
, delivering a GMIT Education for Sustainability Module and joining their sustainability team, starting the re-wilding on
GRETB lands on Lough Atalia which is now used as an education nature reserve and an outdoor classroom by all Gretb
centers aswell as GMIT University students. We also formed a Galway school network for climate action and hosted our
first event last year online as part of NUIG SCIFEST which will be held in person on campus again the year on NOV
17th. The project has had a huge positive impact on all students and teachers involved. It has also created awareness
and allowed us to form networks to disseminate our results far wider than we ever could have imagined.
We used Key performance indicators to measure the impact of this project in a number of ways. We recorded
the dissemination of all outputs to include audio visual content and publications in magazines and on social, local and
national media by measuring the viewers, readers and views. We carried out surveys of all participants through
Microsoft forms to record the learning and views of all learners. We also carried out surveys in other schools we
have linked up through collaborations as a result of this project. We have used group presentations, mentee, quizzes,
kahoots to share our learning during the Students mobilities.
We have presented our project results at Climate conferences at University Galway, ATU, Queens University. We have been nominated for a pride of place award this November.

<< Results >>

The project is hosted in all three schools, NGOs and other agencies web sites. As such, it reaches our local and regional communities, students, teachers and families,
alongside more expert public bodies thanks to the involvement in other initiatives and through the collaboration with the NGOs. 
1. Results within the schools have been delivered to targeted public pupils and teachers as planned: they are studying the species, they have done the Records and they
are learning how to innovate environmental studies within curricular subjects and working hours.
2. Some corrective actions are already under way to include the Re-wilding of 20 acres of Gretb lands in Lough Atalia in Galway City which is already being used as an educational Nature reserve and outdoor classroom. Planting of over 1000 trees at a native woodland and erection of bat and bird boxes were carried out as a result of this project.. Also we introduced environmental reviews in all Galway schools as part of our Network to include reduced waste and introducing recycling and composting facilities in our schools.
3. Results of the project have been disseminated widely with all agencies involved and in local and national media.
4. Magazines have been published for all 3 sets of records in all three countries.
5.. Policy Recommendations have been delivered to City-Halls during LTTA's and during Multiplier Events 
6.. Audiovisual content has been produced and shared online, on all websites and on national TV
7.. Magazines and Records have also be uploaded to all partners’ web pages and on social media
All schools have made links with other climate action groups creating sustainable networks for future collaborations.
All 3 schools will continue to deliver sustainable education as part of the schools curricula.
All schools have developed very strong relationships between students and teachers and will continue to work together in the future.
topics: Reaching the policy level/dialogue with decision makers

2020-1-IT02-KA201-079730.title: Digital Reality and Educational Activities in Museums
2020-1-IT02-KA201-079730.summary:
<< Background >>

The DREAM project stems from the partners' desire to systematize and scale the application of the "museater" empirical operating model at a European level to create a stable meeting point between museums and primary schools that allows them to collaborate to meet some of their needs together.

Museums need:
- Diversify their audience.
- Increase the visitor's probability of return in the short term (several visits to the same collection or exhibition) and the medium-long term (lifelong learning services).
- Increase the skills of its staff in digital storytelling and the use of immersive technologies for exhibitions.

Primary school teachers need:
- Learning environments that allow for the dynamic definition of knowledge, skills, and attitudes by students from an early age, but at the same time, that can be inserted with negligible friction in the organizational and regulatory framework of schools.
- Increase skills in digital storytelling and the use of immersive technologies.
- Make a museum visit memorable and desirable for children.

<< Objectives >>

The project's overall objective was to develop an innovative learning environment, which would help teachers of primary schools to strengthen digital key competencies and cultural awareness and expression of students through collaboration with museums and other organizations of the sector. 
For this purpose, the partners defined three operational objectives: 
- Defining a methodology for developing collaborative practices between primary schools and museums aimed at creating "museater representations," which use the museum as a stage and immersive digital environments as scenographies to give children cultural discovery experiences personalized by teachers according to their learning needs. 
- Develop a reference platform for classroom production and museum staging of museater performances. 
- Develop a blended training course aimed at teachers of primary schools for developing collaborative practices with museums and developing and staging museum performances.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities of the project were the following:
- Collection of materials useful for the elaboration of the methodological guide through documentary research, coaching circle, and interviews;
- Drafting of the methodological guide;
- Development of a web repository for the collection and sharing of cultural open educational resources;
- Development of a web app for the design and creation of immersive digital scenographies in a museum environment that can be activated in augmented reality;
- Creation of the training toolkit for the training course for teachers on the staging of museum performances;
- Conducting a pilot edition of the training course;
- Staging at the partnership's museums of the performances created by the local schools;
- Experimentation of an online inter-museum museum performance, streamed from the Tampere Postimuseum.

<< Results >>

The main products of the project are:
- A "Guide to the DREAM methodology," which provides the theoretical foundations of digital cultural heritage, an explanation of the DREAM method for developing a project in the form of a story, a practical example, and support sheets for planning a museum representation.
- A web platform that offers two main functions: the collection and sharing of digital open educational resources that can be used in museum performances; support for creating digital sets for a museum representation. The code is open source and available on GitHub.
- A training course for teachers aimed at creating and staging museum performances. The path is supported by a training toolkit available to museum educators to organize their editions of training activities at their facility.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-IT02-KA201-079803.title: OUTSIDE - Open commUniTies for SustaInable DevelopmEnt
2020-1-IT02-KA201-079803.summary:
<< Background >>

OUTSIDE started from the need to respond to 2 fundamental needs:
1) Promoting the acquisition of key and innovative competences among students
2) Promoting environmental and sustainable development education through the integration of the 17 UN SDGS into the relevant education systems.

We live in a highly complex world, where the role of education and training is crucial.  However, it is necessary for these to adapt to the challenges of the contemporary world and to the transition that involves every sector, school first and foremost.
As confirmed by the preliminary research carried out during the design phase and  the desk and field research activities carried out during the project, the traditional educational methods usually do not meet these needs. The skills needed by modern students involve creativity, problem-solving, entrepreneurship and green skills, which can hardly be developed within classic school contexts.

Therefore, OUTSIDE intends to contribute to rethinking education to address emerging complexity by testing and promoting practical-experiential approaches to promote learning based on solving real problems
related to environmental sustainability.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project, the Consortium wanted to achieve the following objectives: 
- General Objective (GO): to promote the acquisition of innovative skills in students through the creation of entrepreneurial projects based on sustainable development.
- Specific Objectives (SOs):
SO1: Creation of an "open community of learning" involving students, teachers, school staff, institutions, third sector, civil society and business world, based on the development of a multimedia platform;
SO2: To promote the professionalization of teachers in the field of project-based learning, Open Schooling and skills for sustainable development through a specific training course;
SO3: Promoting the protagonism of young people as agents of change, through the collection and promotion of sustainable business projects developed by young people during the project.
SO4: Map the new skills acquired by young students according to an innovative framework developed during the project.

<< Implementation >>

The project structure has been designed in such a way that the activities lead to the achievement of the planned objectives and the delivery of the project results, according to the following framework: 

PHASE 1: Preparation (Research activities) 
PHASE 2: Implementation - Teachers training (Definition/ Design of the modules to be included in the Toolkit IO1; delivery of the blended training course - through the online Resource Center  and C1. 
PHASE  3: Implementation - Development of the Resource Centre IO2 (Technical development; Populating the platform).
PHASE : 4 Implementation - Pilot Action (Establishment of Open Communities of Learning in each piloting country; Experimentation of the OUTSIDE methodology aimed to develop 12 business ideas on environmental/sustainability issues; C2 and C3 to develop IO3 di IO3; Elaboration of IO3).
PHASE  5 Implementation - Framework Development (IO4).
PHASE  6: Dissemination and valorisation  through the production of the transferability guidelines (IO4); organisation of multiplier events; dissemination activities throughout the duration of the project through online channels (social media, website, etc.) and involvement of stakeholders at local and national level.

<< Results >>

OUTSIDE produced 4 IOs, each IO corresponds to the achievement of one SO:
IO1:Training Toolkit for Teachers (OS2): training tool based on the OUTSIDE methodology aimed to develop teachers' knowledge, skills and abilities in environmental and sustainability education through project-based learning and the concept of Open schooling
IO2: Online Resource Centre (OS1): tool for the development of Open Communities of Learning OCLs) and the sustainability of OUTSIDE. IO1 contains resources for the development of green projects, IOs and OERs.
IO3: Collection of business projects (OS3): co-created by the students, contains the 12 green projects created during the project. IO3 is particularly functional to promote the role of students as actors of change. They disseminated their projects online (via IO2 and other online channels) and at final multiplier events (MEs). 
IO4: Competence Framework and Guidelines for Sustainable Local Development (OS4): encourages the experimentation of OUTSIDE in other educational contexts and defines skills/competences that students can develop with the methodology, with the support of local OCLs.

OUTSIDE also carried out: 
- two training activities (1 for teachers, 1 for students)
- 4 MEs in pilot countries.
