2019-1-DE02-KA202-006483.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-DE02-KA202-006483.title: LOG-IN: Logistics VET goes international
2019-1-DE02-KA202-006483.summary:
<< Background >>

Digitalisation and the accompanying technological innovations are changing occupational profiles and increasing the demand for qualified workers. Especially in logistics, as an international interface industry, this digital progress plays a major role and requires a more computer-based, personalised and autonomous approach to logistics teaching. This is needed, for example, for the digital control and monitoring of goods storage and supply chains. Against this background, the LOG-IN project was initiated to support the necessary conversion process of schools and to promote the international exchange of experience among them. LOG-IN focused on new technological advances, i.e. integrating new educational tools such as simulations, virtual reality or just-in-time learning into the classroom and giving learners the opportunity to apply abstract concepts in real-life practice in a risk-free environment.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the "LOG-IN" project was to anchor digital technologies more firmly in vocational education and training, exemplary for the professions in the globally active logistics industry. Logistics processes are becoming more and more digitalised and automated. The use of intelligent technologies is increasing. This has an impact on all work processes and thus on the competence requirements for logistics employees. For example, companies today work with digital merchandise management programmes in order to be able to process operational processes in a targeted and effective manner.
The project objective was to increase the quality of vocational training and to bring it in line with the needs of the labour market. LOG-IN" aimed to significantly strengthen the acquisition of job-related digital competences in training in the logistics sector, to expand the methodological competences of teachers (from knowledge transmitters to facilitators of self-directed learning) in order to prepare young professionals for the requirements of a digital working and living world. The project objective was also to strengthen the capacity development of VET institutions and to promote their internationalisation.

<< Implementation >>

LOG-IN is one of a series of successful BGZ projects in the field of digital transformation of VET and was focused on the logistics sector. 
In the project, activities for the development of transferable learning offers and solutions for the integration of digitalisation in VET exemplary for logistics professions were successfully implemented. 
They included: 
- Conducting a SELFIE survey, the aim of which was to consider the current legal, technical, financial and human resource aspects in all schools and institutions involved in the project.
Development: 
*of a competence matrix for the field of digital logistics. 
*of learning units and a learning unit structure on digital logistics, 
*of a digital training course for teachers  
*of a model of the digital learning environment 
- Testing of the learning units and the course for teachers 
- Establishment of a digital warehouse linked to a digital inventory management system 
- Elaboration of recommendations for educational stakeholders and decision makers
- Conducting national and transnational workshops  
- Networking with stakeholders in the logistics sector  
- Dissemination activities with multiplier events

<< Results >>

LogIn has achieved its central goal of EU-wide transferable and innovative concepts for the integration of digital technologies in logistics professions. In the course of the project, a matrix was developed that provides concrete information on which digital competences are relevant and need to be taught for future training in logistics professions. With the help of newly developed learning units and an associated digital learning platform (simulated company, training camp), analogue processes in logistics can also be taught digitally. At the same time, the teachers' competences were trained in the teaching of this digital learning content and in the use of innovative learning methods (e.g. virtual warehouse). Through the intensive testing and the new learning method and the European dialogue with experts from the logistics sector, LOG-IN was able to formulate recommendations for action on digitalisation in VET for actors in the logistics industry, vocational and higher education as well as for politics and administration. In addition, the cooperation between VET institutions and universities was strengthened. With the EU-wide transferable results, the project strengthens the quality of education in the logistics sector.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2019-1-DE02-KA202-006571.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-DE02-KA202-006571.title: Handle it! - Strategies for addiction treatment in New Psychoactive Substances in Europe
2019-1-DE02-KA202-006571.summary:
<< Background >>

The use of new psychoactive substances (NPS) is an increasing challenge for addiction services worldwide, both in terms of individual health damage potential (cardiovascular arrest, psychoses, long-term brain damage) and in terms of detectability of use, as common rapid drug tests often do not detect NPS. For people with addiction problems who use NPS, access to the addiction support system must be improved or existing access must be reformed and adapted to the new needs with regard to NPS, because so far there are no adequate strategies in prevention and treatment in dealing with NPS.

<< Objectives >>

The aim was for interdisciplinary professionals to learn through international exchange to analyze the care structure of the help system and to acquire the necessary skills to be able to develop new strategies and possible solutions in dealing with NPS consumers. In this way, a transfer of knowledge from the local to the international level was achieved. In this way, the key professional competencies and basic skills of the participants in their field of work were improved, such as their ability to react to the specific needs of the target group, creative conceptual thinking and innovative strategic work in an international context.
The participants were trained by the project and at the same time educated to become multipliers in order to be able to transfer new approaches in dealing with NPS to the partner organizations.

<< Implementation >>

The project originally consisted of four, later of five Learning Teaching Training Activities, as well as several online meetings on project controlling and management. During the project, the participants worked in (online) working groups, especially between the LTTAs, and developed the questionnaires for some case studies, client and staff surveys. And, of course, they realized the surveys in their own organization and their country, analyzed the data and presented the results at the LTTAs. Expert presentations at the LTTAs enabled the participants to expand their knowledge and share their experiences. With the Mobile Reporting a communication platform was created, which documents the results of the project and thus enables an exchange of knowledge on an international level beyond the project participants.

<< Results >>

It's important to say, that we have achieved our goals despite the ongoing corona-pandemic. Project management in these times was a huge challenge. Results to be highlighted
- strengthening of conceptual flexibility in order to be able to react appropriately to the highly volatile needs of the target group
- increasing the ability to cooperate in an international context in order to be able to react to developments in the drug scene
- raising awareness of the topic of NPS, which was carried to the partner organizations by the participants as multipliers
With the help of mobile reporting, the project could be well documented and secured by publishing videos and blog posts on the online platform and made available to a broader target group.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2019-1-EL01-KA202-062479.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-EL01-KA202-062479.title: Promoting employability through Social Solidarity Economy
2019-1-EL01-KA202-062479.summary:
<< Background >>

Successful SSE education within VET training has been the main vision and motive behind this project, and by this, the promotion of the employment of the beneficiaries within the field of SSE. As SSE training has been neglected in most European VET systems, the consortium detected the need to promote comprehensive training and professional development, which integrates alternative socioeconomic models and practices of SSE within the area of VET. 

Specifically, needs detected were: 
•	To describe the general situation concerning SSE training activities in the partner countries and to develop a general framework for quality provision of SSE training within VET. 
•	To develop educational contents regarding SSE in VET. The existing ones were too academic or emperical.
•	To professionalise trainers on SSE by recommending an SSE trainers’ profile with specific knowledge, skills and competences. 
•	To support trainers in SSE by offering specific guidelines that will also address the main principles of VET: For the preparation of curricula, educational material, teaching modules, evaluation of training etc.
•	To promote the visibility of SSE to all direct and indirect target groups of the project, including policymakers and key actors.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to implement & promote the framework of SSE in VET, specifically: 

•	To make SSE visible & familiar to the labour market
•	With regard to social inclusion, employability & sustainability
•	Introducing a competence profile of the SSE VET trainer
•	To provide VET trainers with teaching methods & tools
•	Implementing an alternative pedagogical experience
•	To empower trainers with new approaches, skills & competences coming from SSE
•	To assist trainees in entering the labour market

The implementation of the project offered a high quality educational material to all possible educators, trainers and mentors in order to implement at least 30hours intensive training in SSE that can be applicable in different cultural backgrounds. We aimed to achieve the empowerment of trainers, and from their side they will empower the concept, the meaning and the practices of SSE in order to be more understandable, visible and repeatable.

<< Implementation >>

Within the project, there have been different types of activities implemented:
1. Project management activities
•	Project Management Plan, tools & templates
•	Setting a Steering Committee 
•	Partners Contracts 
•	Online Management Space 
•	Involving members of the Stakeholders’ Committee 

2.	IOs 
IO 1: VET Trainers Guide on SSE, with a Trainers’ Profile (6 languages)
IO 2: Training Modules on SSE Addressed to VET (6 languages)
IO 3: Policy Brief for Introducing SSE in VET System (5 languages)


3.	5 day International Training and Learning Activity held in Prague

4.	3 Transnational meetings (2 with presence and 1 online), 22 extra online partners’ meetings, bilateral online meetings

5.	5 Multiplier events (3 with presence and 2 online) 

6. Dissemination activities 
•	A strategic dissemination plan
•	Target groups & stakeholders’ database per country 
•	Project website and social media account  (FB) 
•	Project presentations through workshops / conferences 
•	Article publications in web / magazines / newspapers 

7.	Evaluation & QA activities 
•	QA & Evaluation Plan 
•	Semester Evaluation by Partners 
•	Meetings’ Evaluation 
•	Multiplier Events’ Evaluation 
•	Training Activity Evaluation

<< Results >>

The Outputs produced were as described in the proposal, yet produced in more languages than initially planned. The project results consist of:
•	a high quality educational material on key SSE topics for trainers in order to implement at least 30hours intensive training that can be applicable in different cultural backgrounds. This material is in 6 languages and indicates aims and intended learning outcomes, content, methods, activities, further reading and a glossary,
•	a trainers’ guide (6 languages) which includes knowledge, skills and competences of the trainers additionally to the methodological guidance on how to design, implement and evaluate a training session or educational programme from scratch. 
•	a policy brief to address the need for changes at official national and European level in order to include the SSE sector in the formal VET system and more specifically in the EQF/NQF. The policy brief has a section Europe and national sections for the participating counties.

The results of the whole project will reinforce visibility for SSE as a vocational area, thus employability for NEETs and for general public, as well as more specialized professionals in the field of vocational education.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2019-1-EL01-KA202-062889.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-EL01-KA202-062889.title: AGRofood sustainable gOalS
2019-1-EL01-KA202-062889.summary:
<< Background >>

EU’s agro-food industry provides 46 million jobs in 15 million businesses, accounting for 6% of the EU’s GDP. In 2017, around 10 million people were directly employed in the EU agricultural sector, representing 5% of EU’s workforce. Working in this sector requires not only sector-specific knowledge and skills but also skills such as entrepreneurship, financial and project management which also should be better addressed in the education and training offer. The shortage of people ready to work in this sector is also linked to other factors such as the ageing workforce or/and the perceived lack of career attractiveness.

In this respect, there is the need for interventions to facilitate innovative processes in favor of productivity and competitiveness, exploring the different international concepts of sustainability and more specifically in the agro-food field as an innovative way to encourage young people to see the food sector as one of the best options for a career choice as well as to up-skill and re-tool the current agro-food workforce to enhance the human development, and ultimately achieve the global goals.

<< Objectives >>

The project's objectives were the following:
-Change the way of thinking of different communities in the partner’s countries, to a more comprehensive approach, establishing the food sector in one of the most attractive areas in EU.
-Establish a new integrated approach to create real impact through a balanced and synergistic relationship between industrial development, academic research and innovation, and coupling private and public end-users requirements.
-Spread the seed, stimulate new and cutting-edge integrated activities and develop actions designed to successfully react to modern challenges.
-Boost the sustainable economic growth of the EU food sector, upgrading the services of the food environment, its resources and the cultural heritage in the most sustainable way.
-Offer new chances to implement professional skills of interest for the Agro-food sector.
-Boost self-employment, through the active empowerment of young people in with actions that support the effective implementation of the Investment Plan for Europe and foster the creation of economic activity with a special focus on them.
-Promotion of business initiatives for the sustainable development of rural areas.
-Enhance the human development, and ultimately achieve the global goals.

<< Implementation >>

For the project AGROS, the following activities were implemented:

Each Leader of Intellectual Output (IO1, IO2, IO3) organized pilot workshops with participants of the target group in their home countries. (Greece, Croatia, Spain) The goal was to discuss the topics of the courses with agri-food experts and create samples of evaluation forms for evaluating them, in order to improve the quality of the material.

Multiplier events in every partner country for the target group and project stakeholders in the framework of the dissemination and exploitation activities in each country.

The C1 joint staff training event had been organized to train the partners’ staff (train the trainers) so as to be able to inform the target group during the multiplier events as regards to the AGROS Training Courses and the use of the AGROS Hub, explain the technical specifications, present ways on how to deliver the material in order to generate more traffic to the Portal.

<< Results >>

Training Course on SDGs and sustainability for Agro-food sector was developed with the goal  to enhance and deepens the knowledge and competences of professionals working in the field of Agro-food sector and VET learners in general.

Training Course on Integrating Innovation processes in Agro-food sector was developed with the goal to highlight the opportunities merged from the innovative alignment with the SDGs, for the professionals working in the field of Agro-food sector and VET learners in general.

Under the IO3, a self-test of Capacity of professionals in this field was created in order to help them become Agro-food Experts, evaluating their knowledge, competences on Agro-food sector related on SDGs but also providing feedback for their development in the field of vocational education.

The aim of IO4 was the creation of an informative Hub (AgrosHUB) for professionals working in the field of Agro-food and any other interested stakeholder who wishes to acquire information on new skills and competences in emerging Agro-food trends related to SDGs, training opportunities, information about the training courses and handbooks, EU funding opportunities for the sector etc.

New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2019-1-ES01-KA202-064075.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-ES01-KA202-064075.title: INCLUSION AND EMPLOYABILITY THROUGH ELECTRIC VEHICLES TECHNOLOGY
2019-1-ES01-KA202-064075.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project due to the lack of specific materials for First level VET students related to the new technology of electric vehicles. Also we have detected the need for updating current workers at workshops who do not have any knowledge about this type of vehicles when dealing with their manipulation and fixing processes.
So we applied for it with the intention to provide quality materials for both aims. To train students who usually are expelled from the system very quickly and to update workers who are forced to learn if they want to avoid being fired because their expertise has become useless with new technologies.
To do this we try to combine ICT technologies to design the ebooks, the online training course and 3D printers opportunities.

<< Objectives >>

Our aim was to favour the development of high quality skills and competences among our teachers and students by developing interactive 3D materials and opening them to society. Likewise, we wanted to focus on some professionals or unemployed people from the automotive sector which need updating by designing an open source spooc training programme.

<< Implementation >>

We have developed the 14 ebooks for VET students focused on different topics of electric vehicles. We have included 3D designs to be printed and used by students whether in the classroom or workshop (in the book you can find both, the programme and the plans for the design to be printed). We have included automatic readers on the book texts to listen to the information instead of reading it to make them inclusive for those students with reading comprehension difficulties. We have designed the autoevaluation of each of the topics and we have translated them all into the seven languages of the partners involved in this project plus English.

At the same time related to our second objective we have developed the electric vehicles spooc training course for current workers or unemployed people. However and due to the  volume of contents and depth of the materials prepared for each unit we did not have time to translate it to the rest of languages and we are presenting  it just in Spanish.

<< Results >>

1. 14 topics on Electric vehicles developed in all languages which provides a total of 112 complete ebooks including students book and teachers guide, together with interactive and inclusive materials and activities, autoevaluation and dictionary of difficult relevant new concepts..
2. Complete SPOOC training course in Spanish for workers and unemployed people updating.

2019-1-ES01-KA202-064294.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-ES01-KA202-064294.title: Coaching Inter-Pairs for employment
2019-1-ES01-KA202-064294.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was requested after carrying out a SWOT analysis which found that 
the use of social networks is widespread among young people, who use them to socialise and communicate.
communicate. However, VET students were not aware of the risks related to the use of social networks when it comes to finding a job, as they are the tool most used by companies when selecting new candidates.
Therefore, it was concluded that it was necessary for VET students to know how to create, maintain and preserve their digital identity for employment by using social networks as a tool to promote their skills, language skills, hobbies etc. and thus become optimal candidates to enter the labour market in a fast and efficient way.
In addition, it was detected that in order to promote the inclusion of VET students it was important to use new learning methodologies and the use of non-formal and informal methods and peer learning was chosen as both encourage collaborative work and promote student motivation. The use of these methodologies has managed to involve students at risk of exclusion.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project has been to promote the employability of VET students through the effective use of social networks by training 6 students in each country who have been the "Digital Coaches".
This general objective has been achieved through the following specific objectives:
-To improve the competences for the effective use of social networks for employment for both learners and VET teachers and trainers. 
-To expand the learning community to facilitate collaboration between VET schools, policy makers and companies to learn first hand how to use social networks to promote employment. 
Using "Coaching" as a non-formal shared learning methodology where coaches have provided
support, advice and information related to social media and ICTs to promote employment.
-Integrating formal, non-formal and informal education, working as digital coaches.

<< Implementation >>

The main activities that have been carried out have been:
-Creation of the learning package
-National trainings, workshops and seminars using the videos, testimonials and real case scenarios (training package)
-Transnational training involving students and teachers from all partners to train the "digital coaches".
Four face-to-face transnational project coordination meetings and more than 15 online meetings, due to the pandemic situation, which allowed to create the training package in a collaborative way (project partners, students, companies) and to manage all the project actions.
-Training activity in Croatia with the participation of 39 students and 20 teachers in which the "digital couches" were trained.
-A mailbox has been created in each participating country (coucher's help desk) in which the digital couches deal with the students' doubts about the creation of their digital identity for employment. 
-The results of the project have been disseminated by different means, which has allowed to extend the learning community at European level.
-Evaluation of the results obtained and the activities carried out has been carried out.
-A sustainability plan of the results has been carried out.

<< Results >>

All the programmed activities have been carried out and the initially proposed objectives have been achieved. Specifically, the results obtained were as follows:
The training package has been created containing:
1.- Videos on how to create a curriculum vitae using Europass, how to use job portals and how to create, maintain and improve your digital identity for employment using social networks.
2.- 14 videos with testimonials and real case scenarios of students from the centres and staff from companies involved in recruitment to learn about their best practices.
recruitment companies to learn about their best practices
The training package can be found at the following address
url:https://erasmusplus.itis.biella.it/cipe/results/training-package/
-The project website has been created and is located at the following URL: https://erasmusplus.itis.biella.it/cipe/
-A facebook page and a youtube channel have been created to share the results of the project.
-An online mailbox has been set up in each participating country where digital coaches supported by teachers answer questions about how to create a digital identity for employment in an efficient way using social media - Coaches helpdesk.
-The transnational learning community has been extended.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2019-1-ES01-KA202-065843.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-ES01-KA202-065843.title: Upgrading Trainers in Dual Vocational Training System
2019-1-ES01-KA202-065843.summary:
<< Background >>

At European level youth unemployment and job precariousness are observed as a reality,being more pronounced in the countries of the Mediterranean area.According to Eurostat in Europe there were 3.36 million unemployed under 25 years old in the EU as a whole,of which 2.39 million were in Euro area.The Euro area unemployment rate was 16.6% for young people at the end of 2018.In fact,several objectives of Europe ET2020 focused on reducing youth unemployment through training and exchange.
Dual VET allows a direct contact of apprentices with the labour market through a real experience from the beginning of their traineeship, they can get to know the job better and significantly, they are more motivated and above all they increase their employability in their chosen professional sector. In this context the role of the company trainer is key. 
NEEDS TO SOLVE
-There is a lack of professionalisation of trainers' competences to help achieve a quality experience.
-Few countries have a system of instructor training, evaluation or communication systems between company, school and student or with the education administration.
- Gaps in the recognition of the work of these educational agents.

<< Objectives >>

Combining the above mentioned priorities with the objectives of the Strategic Partnerships in the field of VET, the GENERAL OBJECTIVE of Upgrading Trainers in Dual VET System (UpT2S) has been to create resources that help the professionalisation and improvement of the competences of the trainers in Dual VET and the employability, labour market insertion and entrepreneurship of the young apprentices. All this from a transnational perspective.

In order to achieve the general objective, the following SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES were defined:

- To give relevance to the work and to improve the professional competences of the trainer in the training process of the young people. To this end, an accessible (online) training course has been created with didactic resources to improve their training function. 

- To develop tools for the evaluation of the trainees' competences and to prepare the trainers to carry out this process.

- To generate a manual of good practices on the role and competences of the trainer. All this, through research, as well as the exchange of experiences and good practices carried out through the project activities.

<< Implementation >>

Despite the problems generated by Covid19 (global containment, national perimeter closures according to epidemiological rate, mobility restriction, school closures, infection of staff or participants, Omicron) which have conditioned the planned schedule and which has been modified according to the evolution of the pandemic, all the intellectual products and activities of the project have been executed satisfactorily, except for the transnational meeting in France held online (Oct-20).
The implementation of the UPT2S Project has followed the following structure: 
1) Initiation - Signing of bilateral agreements, preparation of activities and timetables. 
2) Development of intellectual products of the project: IO1 An online course for company trainers, IO2 An Evaluation Tool, IO3 A good practice guide on the role of the trainer. 
3) Review of intellectual products by external experts (Quality Assurance)
4) Closure-Final evaluation, roadmap for future joint projects 
5) Project management (transversal)-Monitoring reports,virtual and transnational meetings 
6) Dissemination (transversal) - UPT2S website, social networks, meetings addressed to trainers/company, VET teachers and students and educational institutions.

<< Results >>

Among the intellectual outputs produced in UPT2S, there are 
- O1 A 25-hour structured online course for company trainers that can be used by VET centres and educational institutions for this purpose. It has been elaborated by modules (5) and with a wide range of training resources (texts, slides, complementary material, video tutorials (18), tests, practical exercises...).
- O2 ,An evaluation and communication tool that trainers can use to carry out the evaluation and assessment of Dual VET trainees in real time during their internship in the company... 
- O3 A guide of good and successful practices on training and the role of the trainer with an analysis of the existing practice and the role of schools, companies and public institutions in this task.
OTHER RESULTS 
The UpT2S platform (https://upt2sproject.com) has been created and is available to all stakeholders, including the three intellectual outputs generated by the project. It also contains direct access to the project's social networks (Youtube channel, Facebook, Instagram...), news, newsletters, advertising material...
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2019-1-FR01-KA202-062327.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-FR01-KA202-062327.title: VINIMOB
2019-1-FR01-KA202-062327.summary:
<< Background >>

For several years, we have noticed a shortage of manpower in the wine industry due to their growth and the specialization of their activities. The labor needs of cooperatives, producer groups and large companies are also difficult to fill.
The multiplication of tasks has favored the implementation of skills development and recognition mechanisms. 
However, the skills of low-skilled operators acquired through informal learning are generally not recognized.
This need for recognition is all the more significant as new activities, with their demanding level, have appeared and modular training actions have been created to meet the demands of professionals. 

VINIMOB inscribes the European partnership of 6 members, in a process of mutualization of approaches, methodological co-construction and practices that serves as a lever for professional mobility and inclusion of people with special needs.

<< Objectives >>

The VINIMOB project is a logical continuation of the ZERO BARRIER and VITIMOB projects and aims at reinforcing their achievements and amplifying their results. Like them, VINIMOB aims at the inclusion of people with special needs in the wine industry and more particularly in the sectors of production, packaging of wines and their marketing, while promoting geographical mobility. 
The objective is to make on-the-job training and certification in wine-making techniques accessible to all.
The acquisition of skills is facilitated by the implementation of innovative tools whose perspective is equal opportunities for all.

Through VINIMOB, the European partners respond to major challenges such as professional mobility for all with the aim of equal treatment, recognition and capitalization of learning outcomes. 
For this, it was essential to:
- Create common tools, in the fields of didactics and recognition.
- Develop and promote digital tools and platforms in order to ensure the dissemination of good practices and to secure learners' paths.

<< Implementation >>

Two periods of learner mobility were carried out:

- The first took place at the AGAPEI ("AGir avec Amis, Parents et Professionnels pour les Personnes en situation de handicap") in Gaillac and its specialized wine-making establishment (ESAT).
The students, from the four countries of the partnership, were trained for a week in bottling, labeling and order preparation techniques.
- The second week was spent on the Catalan winegrowing estate of OLIVERA where they were trained in packaging, bottle dressing and customer service.

In a rigorous professional environment, marked by a very positive and benevolent spirit, the students had the opportunity to demonstrate their know-how and their level of autonomy. At the end of these intense learning periods, it is with great pride that they were awarded their first "VINIMOB European Mobility Certificate".

The intellectual productions, conceived throughout the project by the partners, were tested and evaluated during the learners' mobility.

<< Results >>

What concrete achievements and other results has your project produced?

To respond to the orientations of the VINIMOB project, intellectual productions have been realized, in an unexpected context of sanitary crisis. 

- A VINIMOB job profile of a multi-purpose cellar assistant, shared and validated at the partnership level.
- An occupational standard developed in compliance with the ECVET system. 
- Digital training modules and innovative didactic tools for the acquisition of skills based on the mastery of professional gestures as well as to offer equality in learning.
- Evaluation tools with a European dimension.

On the other hand, in order to implement and evaluate the relevance of the didactic and pedagogical tools, mentioned above, the partnership has organized two periods of mobilities involving the learners of the member structures.

Finally, in order to highlight and promote the VINIMOB project, the partners have created an institutional website, which was inaugurated during the Erasmus Days, last October, in the presence of Mr. Sébastien THIERRY, deputy director of the French Erasmus+ agency.

2019-1-FR01-KA202-062356.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-FR01-KA202-062356.title: "Stone and wood- two materials of traditional habitat, two materials of artistic expression"
2019-1-FR01-KA202-062356.summary:
<< Background >>

This project gathers seven structures from three countries (France, Poland and Croatia). These three partner territories are anchored on a rich heritage of buildings made of two materials - wood and stone - which have shaped their history and landscape, thus marking the ingenuity and cultural richness of their creators. This heritage is currently an important asset for the economic and social attractiveness of these territories. Our aim is to enable partner organisations to network, to increase their capacity to operate at a transnational level, to share and compare ideas, practices and working methods. The skills required for these trades are based on know-how passed down through the history and traditions of professional wood and stone working techniques. We want to facilitate the acquisition of these traditional skills by offering participants a range of vocational training courses in line with the companies that create jobs in the wood and building trades. This will allow the enrichment of a school training course towards jobs in heritage restoration companies.

<< Objectives >>

Our aim is to enable partner organisations from three territories to network, to increase their capacity to operate transnationally and to share and compare ideas, practices and working methods. 
The project allows the skills and know-how passed on by the history and traditions of the three countries to be confronted and mutually enriched.
The mutual enrichment of these traditional skills offers the participants an increase in their competences and thus a wider access to job-creating companies in the wood and building trades, and particularly to heritage restoration companies, reconciling the pupils with the art and cultural heritage that surrounds them.
The highlighting of this small rural heritage, often forgotten, absent in tourist guides, far from the main paths, is thus the object of a new light with the Erasmus action and the involvement of local schools. Another stated aim is to encourage exchanges between countries on good practices for the protection and enhancement of heritage.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, the joint restoration through two international workcamps of small rural heritage and the collective creation of an artistic work combining three emblematic materials of the three territories: Breton granite and white stone of Brač and wood. The methodology used initiates the adoption of new pedagogical practices allowing the development of transversal skills between the professional disciplines of wood and stone trades and the disciplines of applied art in order to respond to the needs of disadvantaged groups and to take into account the differences in learning achievements linked to geographical and socio-economic disparities. The partners are located at the opposite ends of Europe, East-West and South.

<< Results >>

Le premier résultat est la création d'un guide de bonne pratique concernant la taille de la pierre et les métiers du bois. Ce document regroupe des scénario de cours, taille de Triskèle en bois ou en pierre. Ce document regroupe ce qui a été travaillé par les élèves. Rédigé en anglais, ce document est à l'usages des autre écoles européenne connues dans la taille de la pierre et le travail du bois. 
De façon concrète la réhabilitation de la maison du forgeron en France et le travail sur les éléments décoratifs locaux à Brac, constituent des résultats tangibles que les habitants et les touristes pourront admirer.
Outre la découverte mutuelle des élèves et des enseignants, la découverte et la pratique de la taille de la pierre avec des matériaux différents de ceux utilisés lors de l'enseignement est un point qui a marqué les équipes. Le besoins d'échanger sur les techniques utilisées, la façon d'appréhender les matériaux, a suscité le besoin de poursuivre les découvertes et poursuivre  de façon concrète les évolutions pédagogique initiées. Des projets KA1 sont en cours de rédaction pour poursuive les échanges.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education

2019-1-FR01-KA202-062930.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-FR01-KA202-062930.title: European Wetlands Ambassadors
2019-1-FR01-KA202-062930.summary:
<< Background >>

The "Ambassadors of European Wetlands" (AMHE) project was promoted by the Community of municipalities of South Corsica Communes and a transnational consortium including integration and training organizations, and organizations active in the maintenance of natural wetlands, from 7 countries members (FR, GR, PT, ES, CR, IT). This consortium has worked to meet a dual challenge:
* the growing demand of European citizens for the quality of the environment, the strengthening of the regulatory framework for water quality, the implementation of the Natura 2000 network, the pressures linked to climate change, require maintenance and increased management of the quality of wetlands.
* the increase in long-term unemployment in most European countries, mainly affects the least educated citizens, led to reintegration programs.

The AMHE project jointly responds to:
- the needs of managers of wetlands by providing them with a new profession, allowing more expertise and versatility in their missions, for a better cost/efficiency ratio.
- the needs of people in integration by providing them with better qualifications, more versatility, improving their employability.

<< Objectives >>

The AMHE project aimed to improve the qualification of Europeans engaged in processes of reintegration into employment through economic activity, whether it concerns integration schemes as they are practiced in France or in Italy (contract training-work) or projects of general interest mobilizing the long-term unemployed as they are practiced in Spain or Greece for example.
More specifically, it aimed to improve the training and employability of people in integration mobilized in operations of general interest geared towards the preservation of the environment and in particular towards the enhancement and protection of  European wetlands and waterways.

<< Implementation >>

* definition of the AMHE  job reference through the conduction of documentary research and field research with 37 strategic partners: managers of natural areas and wetlands, support structures for people away from work, administrations in charge of employment and environment policies,….
* development of a vademecum that allows trainers to appropriate the most relevant knowledge, know-how and pedagogical processes
* organization of a transnational training event in the implementation of AMHE content for 17 integration agents and trainers
* conduction of pilot sessions in partner countries with 96 people in a situation of social and professional exclusion or people who have expressed a particular interest in AMHE training
* implementation of a system of validation and recognition of AMHE skills
* development and animation of an online platform, train-the-trainer tool and resource center
* numerous dissemination activities of the project results bringing multiplier effects outside the participating organizations at local/regional/national and European level.

<< Results >>

The AMHE consortium has mobilized a strategic network of associated partners and has developed its activities around the realization of the following intellectual productions:
O1: Framework that outlines the new profession of Wetland Ambassador by bringing new themes such as environmental mediation, knowledge of the environment, ecological engineering and a strengthening of cross-disciplinary skills and capacities for action.
O2: Training framework and training content: includes a matrix of detailed learning outcomes using the EQF level 3 framework and specific guidelines concerning the modes of transmission, the teaching techniques to be implemented and a series of outdoor activities serving as a support for the acquisition of skills.
O3: Skills qualification and validation framework at 3 levels: self-assessment, validation by the field and experience in the work situation, confrontation with external assessment.
O4. Resource center and e-learning tool for training trainers so that they can support the emergence of this new profession.
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market
Equal access and transition to labour market

2019-1-FR01-KA202-063068.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-FR01-KA202-063068.title: Keep innovation in multi partnership cooperation in lifelong career guidance services
2019-1-FR01-KA202-063068.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was born in response to the need formulated by regional, national and European policies to increase cooperation and the search for synergies between stakeholders in the fields of education, training, employment and entrepreneurship, in order to provide better lifelong guidance services.

After the launch of the project, new reports have again shown the importance of increasing cooperation between stakeholders and strengthening the coordination between the actions of these different stakeholders. The CEDEFOP report "A fresh look at guidance practitioner professionalism" (December 2021) also showed the importance of strengthening the competences of guidance practitioners in cooperation.

The Cités des métiers International Network, therefore, applied for this project in order to upskill the function of multi partnership cooperation in lifelong career guidance and ultimately, to strengthen the quality of lifelong guidance services in response to the constantly changing needs of users.

 The project was to be a continuation of the European project COCADE "DEveloping CAreer COunselling services in integrated spaces", during which good practices within lifelong guidance services were shared.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were to upskill the function of multi partnership cooperation in lifelong career guidance and disseminate an innovative ecosystem approach of multi-partnership towards stakeholders. 
Specific objectives were : 
1)adapt services to the needs/expectations of clients in particularly vulnerable people (ex: young people, NEETS, people with digital illiteracy, women, long term unemployed people) 
2)develop competencies in multi-partnership management among professionals working in lifelong career guidance centers 
3)increase the recognition of the work of multi partnership management 
4)promote multi-disciplinary and integrated services in lifelong career guidance to public and private policymakers on the territory in the fields of education, training and employment Contribute to social inclusion and gender equality in the implementation of activities of this project was a cross-cutting objective.

<< Implementation >>

IO1:
- 7 good practices studied and a summary
- 5 stakeholders debates (one in each partner's country)
- A methodological guide for local debates organization
- A vademecum on multi-stakeholder partnership management in lifelong career guidance (ENG/FR)

IO2: 
- Learning materials for a pilot training programme based on the competences framework (IO3)
- Learning materials for a training of trainers
- Different delivery scenarios (face-to-face, fully online, hybrid, self-paced learning, moderated,...)
- Online training space on an existing platform
-2 training of trainers sessions in July 2021 and January 2022. 
- the pilot program has been implemented in the five countries of the consortium.

IO3: 
- Repository of skills 
- Non-formal self assessment tool online based on validation of skills procedure and respository
- Tests of learning outcomes
- Certification process and certificate

IO4: 
- A map of LLCG centers in the EU on KEEP IN PACT website : 81 registered structures
- 2 European surveys and articles with their main conclusions 
- 5 virtual tours of LLCG centers
- a European unformal group of leaders open to external actors

A website, two multiplier events, newsletters and articles published on the website and further

<< Results >>

Outputs produced : 
-Seven cases studies and an overall case studies report about multi-stakeholder cooperation in Lifelong Guidance in Europe
-Database of cooperations at local level between stakeholders involved in the field of employment, VET and lifelong guidance
-Methodological guideline to organise local debate with stakeholders
-Vademecum on multi stakeholder partnerships management in lifelong guidance 
-Training programme for trainers on multi stakeholder cooperation in Lifelong Guidance (with online and face to face activities and learning materials)
-Pilot training programme for professionals in multi-stakeholder cooperation in lifelong guidance
-Online training platform with online module and learning materials for the pilot programme
-Repository of skills of partnership manager in lifelong guidance
-Validation of skills procedure for partnership manager (in line with the training programme)
-Self assesment kit for partnership manager in lifelong guidance 
-Certificate of validation of skills 
-Website of the project
-5 virtual tours of integrated centres in Lifelong Guidance
-Map of Lifelong Guidance centres 

A total of 263 persons not receiving a specific grant benefited from the activities organised by the project

2019-1-FR01-KA202-063096.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-FR01-KA202-063096.title: On the way to the future
2019-1-FR01-KA202-063096.summary:
<< Background >>

The idea for this project, "On the way to the future" for European pupils and schools, came from the statistical data provided by the EC. Early leaving from education and training has been falling steadily in the EU since 2002, for both men and women: the drop from 17.0% in 2002 to 10.6% in 2017 constitutes steady progress in achievement of the Europe 2020 strategy target of 10%.
We would therefore like to participate actively in giving the necessary skills and motivation to young people who have dropped out or who are at risk of dropping out so that they obtain a diploma and their professional integration is facilitated.
"On the way to the future" is a project focused on creating a sense of belonging to the European Union through the knowledge of different cultural, religious and ethnic backgrounds and the promotion and revaluation of traditions and local cultures of different European countries, sometimes very distant. It promotes mobility among students and teachers.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to give the opportunity to students who are failing or dropping out of school to believe in themselves by participating concretely and actively in a European project :  creating a European travel agency in order to have an objective to be achieved under favorable conditions, out of school while giving them the impression of acting freely, despite the school environment. 
The goal was to get them out of their comfort zone and lead them to believe in themselves and in a possible future by opening up to the world and to diversity in order to develop skills, commitment, knowledge, motivation and make them want to stay in school and maybe work in a foreign country one day.
For teachers, it meant learning new, more pragmatic pedagogical practices related to preventing school dropout, increasing self-esteem and developing an entrepreneurial spirit, and creating deep and solid alliances between service providers, learning and training in the European labor market in order to promote employability and to contribute to the creation of new sectoral or cross-sectoral programmes, by developing innovative methods of vocational education.

<< Implementation >>

- creating a virtual travel agency and promote each partner country and region,
- creating logos,
- creating videos ("Who am I?" / "Come to my region..." "How to keep students engaged"),
- making slideshows (jobs, places to visit, food....),
- writing press articles,
- creating Erasmus "corners" in each establishment,
- creating flyers,
- playing the role of a tourist guide,
- visiting and reporting on European places,
- public speaking games,
- making a schedule,
- observing the practices of each partner,
- and sharing experiences.

<< Results >>

With this project young people will gain the capacity to change, to integrate easily into a group, to live a collective experience, to prevent school dropout by encouraging their return to vocational training and their employment in an open and rich European labor market as well as developing their entrepreneurial spirit.  For the teachers, this project allowed them to share teaching experiences and meet new partners for new projects.
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education
Teaching and learning of foreign languages

2019-1-HR01-KA202-060800.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-HR01-KA202-060800.title: Driver Exchange Skill Competition
2019-1-HR01-KA202-060800.summary:
<< Background >>

Through this project we wanted to strengthen the connection between vocational logistics and traffic education and the labor market, as well as ensure quality education in the motor vehicle driver profession through transfer and dissemination of knowledge and skills acquired through good practice and education among European vocational schools.

The aim was to develop sustainable partnership for the establishment and further development of national, regional and sectoral institutions in skills competitions as a way of incresing attractiveness and excellence of vocational education and training in the motor vehicle driver profession. Seeing it as a long-term measure which would contribute to improving and increasing quality in this educational program, we wanted to come up with a system of students experience and knowledge exchange in the form of a competition held once a year. The competition would start by providing knowledge transfer, experience exchange, and promoting excellence and cooperation among all partner schools, which could potentially spread in future to other interested European schools.

<< Objectives >>

Through the project implementation, we wanted to exchange knowledge and ideas on implementing competition in the Motor vehicle driver educational program. Each partner school has transferred their knowledge, experience and expertise to other partners through the good practice examples. We wanted to come up with a skills competitions as a way of increasing attractiveness and excellence of vocational education and training for the motor vehicle driver profession, so the students could present their knowledge and skills in areas covered by educations in partner schools.
Teachers created virtual tasks which were realized and solved by the partner schools' students, and which contained simulated real work tasks related to cargo transport and based on the modern logistics flows of cargo. All the interested can find the materials and tasks available on the webpage.
In  addition to this, we wanted to provide partner schools with the equippment and devices for cargo manipulation, as well as computer program for logistics processes simulation, crucial for teaching and training needs, but also for the competition implementation.

<< Implementation >>

We have implemented the following activities:
-	Transnational Projects Meetings: Kick-off Meeting in Zagreb, Interim Meeting (online), Final Meeting in Kouvoli, Finland. 
-	Short-term joint staff training events: Rides in winter conditions in Finland, Telematics organized online by the Road Traffic School, Security and protection in Serbia, and Forklift management and transport of hazardous substances held in France.
-	Blended mobility of VET learners - Driver Skill Competition held in Croatia. Tasks were created and made available to the public.
-	Mutual cooperation among students and teachers during the project
-	Dissemination activities among teachers of all partner schools, implemented on expert meetings of teachers in the traffic and logistics area in the Republic of Croatia, international expert meeting Interdisciplinarity of traffic and logistics and in every opportunity the schools had to present their activities, including dissemination of DESCO project
-	Project webpage was created
-	Virtual tasks were created and made available to the public on the project webpage

<< Results >>

A skills competitions was created as a form of increasing attractiveness and excellence in vocational education and training for the motor vehicle driver profession. The competition was organized in such a way for students to present their knowledge and skills in areas covered by the Short-term joint staff training events at partner schools. The competition provided knowledge transfer, experience exchange, and promotion of excellence and cooperation of all partner schools. Teachers created virtual tasks which all partner schools' students participated in. Real work tasks related to cargo transport and based on the modern logistics flows of cargo were simulated. Mixed teams which represented their schools participated in the competition (at least one female student in each partner school team).
Teachers' competencies in technological innovations in education as well as using innovative learning methods have been improved, which also means improving competencies of students finishing each of these partner schools. Materials and tasks have been made available for the public.
The Road Traffic School was equipped with a logistics practicum containing all the necessary equipment and devices for cargo manipulation, as well as computer programs and programs for logistics processes simulation, which was used for students' preparation and competition implementation for students in all partner schools.
Partner schools added additional equipment to their logistics practicums where needed.

2019-1-HR01-KA202-060809.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-HR01-KA202-060809.title: Zero waste power in HoReCa
2019-1-HR01-KA202-060809.summary:
<< Background >>

Zero waste power project is a part of a solution to the urgent environmental pollution problem.
Project Zero waste power in the HoReCa sector focuses on the zero waste VET catering education
and at the same time on a business model. It produces tools for enhanced learning about Zero waste
subject and business transformation model. It connects VET catering education with business
experience.
The main focus is implementing standards of zero waste solution in VET education and catering
business through the usage of social media and new digital tools.
During the project, Zero waste practice and standards will be created - digital learning tool,
curriculum, media learning environment, and zero waste evaluation tool.Due to the world climate crisis European environmental strategies are developing and searching for
urgent and concrete actions. One of those actions is creating business zero waste standards in
different parts of human activities. World policy strategies about climate changes are pointing the
need for more action in the business field.
At the moment students around (School Strike 4 Climate) the world is gathering for the same cause -
immediate environmental protection act. This project directly responds to their quest and provides
them tools for action on such an important subject. As students are this project aimed population we
estimate they will continue to use gained knowledge and tools at work field as a chef, managers of
hotels and catering facilities and to establish the zero waste impact on the work field.
For this reason, these project results are benefiting for all society and a sustainable future.

<< Objectives >>

The objective of this project is to strengthen and broaden catering education to meet the needs of
society and the environment. The purpose is to find an answer to the question of what needs to be
done to minimize the waste in the HoReCa sector. The more concrete aim is to develop specific
procedures to meet the needs of HoReCa sector to become Zero waste sector.

The objective of this project is helping VET students by creating an IT Digital Training for sustainable
solutions in the HoReCa sector with the goal of environmental conservation. Also, this tools is meant
for use in the work process in the kitchen and hotels.  We wanted to create  learning tools and new Zero waste
standards in the transformation process to zero waste solution business model.
The achievements exceeding the initial expectations were Zero waste materials adapted for the integration and implementation within the curriculum of SŠGT Celje-the topics and texts from the Zerowaste curriculum and e-book were selected and adapted so that they fit into the curriculum of our school. This means that they were not only implemented during the pilot testing but will remain integrated as an updated part of the school's curriculum. Materials integrated into the subjects cooking and nutrition were translated into Slovenian, too.
The curriculum has been translated and adapted into the Croatian language, so that it can be more easily applied for interested users.
At the Slava Raškaj Center, the zero Waste curriculum is implemented through an extracurricular project activity, which continues to be implemented through the new Zero Waste Catering Lab project for catering students.
Project with its learning/evaluating tools also focuses on students with fewer possibilities in VET
education system by giving support and individualized approach to a specific group of students.
In order for VET education in the HoReCa sector to be more compatible with labor market needs and
community environmental needs, we have focused on creating new tools and content that will
enhance the process of change in the waste management business strategy.

<< Implementation >>

Main activities in project and connection with the project objectives and results:
1. Curriculum design for implementing specific procedures for waste management in HoReCa sector
- the curriculum  contains knowledge and specific instructions on how to organize work in a
catering facility in a way that protects the environment based on zero waste standards. After
acquiring knowledge from the curriculum, students are able to apply the same in their future
professional work.
2. Designing digital learning tools based on curriculum – aim is to support learning through
personalised learning pathways and use of ICT tools - The outcome of this activity is a digital
tool, available for easier learning and learning for both students and for a broader circle of interested
personnel from the HoReCa sector, such as catering facilities and hotels, chefs, confectioners, and
food-related stakeholders. This is an excellent tool also for informal learning and vocational training
and lifelong learning for hospitality professionals who have completed vocational education but still
want to modernize and learn new applicable knowledge.
3. Evaluation tool - creating IT zero waste standard tool, certificating and recognizing competence
according to minimum requirements and minimum zero waste quality standards in HoReCa sector
The purpose of this tool to estimate the Zero Waste standard of catering facilities and to inform the
caterer of the current level of their catering business in relation to the desired Zero Waste standard. It
will also be an incentive for the caterer's activation to start changing their business and to inform his
guests and the local community about it.
He thus becomes a socially responsible entrepreneur who responsibly leads and manages his
catering business. The tool will be able to use for self-assessment, and also it is possible for students
to use this tool and evaluate catering facilities during LTT activities.
In the activities of dissemination and promotion of project results, special emphasis is placed on
all the stakeholders who are actively involved in project activity and who use the Zero Waste
Standard Assessment Tools. With this activities project will have long term impact on a wider range
of stakeholders in environmental protection, as it is a goal of this project.
4. Learning through practice– zero waste professional learning experience for catering students - In
times when young people are increasingly aware that the quality of their life is threatened in the future
due to climate change, their awareness and desire for concrete activities are growing. Therefore, in
our project, we had LTT activities for young VET catering students from three partner
organizations in different EU countries to research the level of Zero Waste standard in various
catering facilities.  Also, they will be able to be disseminators of new knowledge and
skills and initiators of positive changes in the work environment with the long-term goal of rescuing
our planet and creating a healthy future.
5.Social media in education - use of social media (Facebook, Instagram, blogs..) in presenting an
idea and learning subjects of Zero waste -
The students of the VET schools involved in the project were educated to present subjects of zero
waste on social media. With the guidance of their mentors, students are able to apply created
content and to post it on social networks (Instagram, Facebook, blogs). Also, there is a web
page created. It contains all intellectual output material with a direct link to all social media tools in
the project.
This is an excellent model of dissemination since young people are easy to connect through social
networks 
Also, project activities were:
5.ADMINISTRATION
6.QUALITY MANAGEMENT AND EVALUATION
7.DISSEMINATION AND EVALUATION
8.DISSEMINATION

<< Results >>

1. Curriculum design for implementing specific procedures for waste management in HoReCa sector
- the curriculum contains knowledge and specific instructions on how to organize work in a

acquiring knowledge from the curriculum, students will be able to apply the same in their future
professional work.
2. Digital learning tools based on curriculum – aim is to support learning through
personalised learning pathways and use of ICT tools - The outcome of this activity will be a digital
tool, available for easier learning and learning for both students and for a broader circle of interested
personnel from the HoReCa sector, such as catering facilities and hotels, chefs, confectioners, and
food-related stakeholders. This is an excellent tool also for informal learning and vocational training
and lifelong learning for hospitality professionals who have completed vocational education but still
want to modernize and learn new applicable knowledge.
3. Evaluation tool - creating IT zero waste standard tool, certificating and recognizing competence
according to minimum requirements and minimum zero waste quality standards in HoReCa sector
The purpose of this tool to estimate the Zero Waste standard of catering facilities and to inform the
caterer of the current level of their catering business in relation to the desired Zero Waste standard. It
will also be an incentive for the caterer's activation to start changing their business and to inform his
guests and the local community about it.
He thus becomes a socially responsible entrepreneur who responsibly leads and manages his
catering business. The tool will be able to use for self-assessment, and also it is possible for students

2019-1-HR01-KA202-060814.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-HR01-KA202-060814.title: Boosting innovation in welding training
2019-1-HR01-KA202-060814.summary:
<< Background >>

The European Welding Federation has developed an international harmonised system for education, training and qualification in the field of welding technology. It was a pioneer organisation developing the first harmonized system embracing all the European countries for the qualification of personnel for a wide range of levels both in welding, related technologies and inspection. In recent years, EWF and its members have been working on the update of its education system by designing new qualifications and revising existing ones to align them with the learning outcomes approach. This is already an enormous step in the modernisation of the EWF Qualification and Training System, but as it was being done, it was noticed that there is an insufficient awareness among the educational staff of new pedagogical approaches and methodologies that can be used in the system for a better learning, as well as the possibility to embed key competences development in EWF Training System, thus promoting a better prepared workforce. For this reason, this project deals with the development of a curriculum for the training of teachers and trainers and pedagogical guidelines with associated tools in this and STEM field.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of this project are to:
- Promote an uptake of an active learning approach by the EWF Education System and technical training in general
- Promote the use of alternative pedagogical approaches by technical trainers and teachers, e.g. using digital resources, problem-based learning and other innovative approaches
- Challenge educators from the STEM field to embed in their own educational resources the development of key competences in trainees
- Foster an entrepreneurial spirit in European citizens, able to research, select, analyze, organise and present information
- Improve the provision of Higher VET, increasing the attractiveness and relevance of VET
- Promote an assessment framework that will help trainers and teachers deal with the challenge of evaluating the different types of lessons proposed in the WELDONE ToT curriculum.

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the project, all activities were focused on the development of intellectual results and their dissemination. These activities consisted of:
- development of five intellectual outputs
- partner consortium meetings - a total of 21. Of which 2 TPM face-to-face meeting, 2 TPM blended meetings and 17 online meetings.
- 2 trilateral online partner meetings.
- three short-term joint staff training events
- five National outreach seminars in all partner countries and a final conference of the WELDONE project (on two occasions).
- dissemination activities on social networks (Facebook, LinkedIn, You Tube), press releases, 2 Flyers, one poster, 6 newsletters, 4 papers at scientific-professional international conferences, promotion of the WELDONE project on the website and social networks of partner organizations.
- continuous quality checks of all activities and results on the project..

<< Results >>

During the project, the necessary materials were developed that provide access to teaching and learning in the WELDONE way:
1) A ToT curriculum for initial and continuous professional development of trainers and teachers (IO1);
2) A Conceptual Handbook to promote a reflection on the paradigm change that the WELDONE project intends to contribute to (IO2);
3) A set of workshops ready to implement and, in an easy, practical and short time consuming, train educators in using the WELDONE pedagogical approaches and methodologies (IO3);
4) A set of assessment methods to go along the new training and teaching practices - because if you train/teach in a different way, then you need to assess achievement in a different way too (IO4);
5) A pedagogical guideline to approach the EWF Educational and Training System (IO5);
Partner organizations have been trained to work on the development of learning outcomes (C1). Training and testing of workshop models and assessment methods (C2 and C3) were conducted.
Dissemination activities reached more than 65,000 people from the target groups.
The results of the project will be implemented in the EWF education system immediately after the completion of the project and ensure its sustainability.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2019-1-HR01-KA202-060820.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-HR01-KA202-060820.title: Master 4.0: improvement of master craftsman exams
2019-1-HR01-KA202-060820.summary:
<< Background >>

Master craftsman occupations are highly regarded and acknowledged in the EU and project countries. Master craftsman exams enable the career progression, opening craft business and taking apprentices. Also, by becoming the master craftsman one gets the competitive advantage because it emphasizes the excellence and quality of products and services. Croatia and Slovenia have a long tradition of organising master craftsman exams and were facing the challenge of mismatch between exam questions and contemporary trends and technologies. On the other hand, North Macedonia and Montenegro had to develop master craftsman exam programmes and questions, since they had master craftsman exams only for one occupation each.

<< Objectives >>

General aim of Master 4.0 project was to increase the usage of innovative approaches and digital technologies for teaching and learning as well as to promote the lifelong learning.
Specific aim of the project was to improve preparation and organisation of master craftsman exam by improving exam questions and programmes in accordance with labour market needs and contemporary technological trends and introducing ICT for preparation and organisation of master craftsman exams.

<< Implementation >>

In order to ensure standardization of master craftsman exam questions, the methodological framework with guidelines for the development of master craftsman exam questions was designed. Partners designed questions for general parts of the exam – parts for economy, law and pedagogy, as well as questions related to the occupational theoretical part of the exam for specific occupations.
Furthermore, in order to improve the quality of exams and simplify the organisation of exam, the online platform for the preparation and organisation of master craftsman exam was developed. One part of the online platform (https://ispiti.e-majstor.eu/) is open to the public so that everyone has an opportunity to see how master craftsman exam looks like and how to prepare the exam. All partners introduced the online platform in their countries and piloted it during the project.

<< Results >>

The results of the Master 4.0 project are: improved master craftsman exam questions and master craftsman exam programs and developed online platform for preparing and organisation of master craftsman exams. In addition, the methodological framework with guidelines for the development of exam questions for the master craftsman exam that was developed within the project will be used after the project end to improve the exam questions for the master craftsman exam for other professions. The manual for the administrative use of the online platform, as well as a manual for candidates, will continue to be used by the staff in charge of conducting master craftsman exams in project countries, as well as candidates and potential candidates who access the online platform for preparing and organisation of the master craftsman exam.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2019-1-HR01-KA202-060976.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-HR01-KA202-060976.title: International Forclift Training
2019-1-HR01-KA202-060976.summary:
<< Background >>

We wanted to create functional, internationally acceptable and simple training program, which is based on European strategies of vocational education, which will at the same time be a model for bringing closer educational programmes in different countries, and to validate and acknowledge gained knowledge in Europe more easily.

<< Objectives >>

Project International Forklift Training (IFT) is our contribution to the development of European strategies in vocational education. In previous cooperation with partners, we noticed the need to develop mutual learning programmes, which will be based on learning outcomes, learning at work
and where gained knowledge will be equally evaluated and acknowledged no matter where they were acquired. This will contribute to increased quality of education. We will educate our students according to the needs on the labour market and our students will be more competitive and more employable on international level.

<< Implementation >>

We created training module and training program and we're working in schools in accordance with this program. Also, Interactive grosary and Training manual for teachers and mentors are made by the project and we're using it in our schools for the forklift driving training.

<< Results >>

After we have made Forklift training program and forklift manual for teachers and mentors, we trained 12 forklift mentors from all partner institution.  Than we started to train our students for forklift handling. 
More than 100 students in all three partner schools was taking a course of forklift handling, and 24 students from Croatia, France and Slovenia were included in this project international forklift course in Croatia and Slovenia.
