2019-1-HR01-KA202-061006.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-HR01-KA202-061006.title: 3D and Virtual Reality Technologies for VET
2019-1-HR01-KA202-061006.summary:
<< Background >>

The main objective of the project is the dissemination of knowledge to the students, professors and other enthusiasts in the field of new trending technologies of CAD modeling, 3d printing, and Virtual reality. The special focus was on the target audience of medical and technical schools in the area of VET. The main idea of the project was the development, design, and transfer of the innovative specialized skills and tools used in the fields of additive technologies, robotics and virtual reality into the vocational education sector through the developed specialized education modules. Implementing blended learning, in other words coupling online self-paced learning with practical offline training greatly facilitated the acquisition of new knowledge and skills in fast-paced technologies and, is a benefit to teachers, learners, and other interested users. The project users proved rapid acquisition of skills and knowledge, in line with new trends in the industry. Special attention was paid to designing suitable materials for blind and visually impaired people, which had proven the inclusion dimension of the project.

<< Objectives >>

The overall concept underpinning the project comes from observing the current societal situation and demands on the educational sector. In the future education system of Europe, the 4.0 industry or the Internet of things (IoT) has a crucial role. The learning experience and education for digital media are becoming a priority, not only in school education but also in the classroom itself. 3D printing or 3D technologies are disseminated through the project as a significant example to realize that. The practical application of this can be incorporated into a wide variety of school subjects to simplify the often-difficult theoretical concepts for students. One of the main objectives was to introduce new technologies in VET education and promote the importance of it. This technologies will have more important role in the future and will lead to profound economic and social changes through technology, and there is little doubt this will lead to the emergence of new fields of work, and novel jobs. Overall objective was to support schools and teachers who want to integrate 3D and VR in education, since the implementation of it in schools is stagnating due to the lack of knowledge and the project addressed this challenges with the results.

<< Implementation >>

The project produced two intellectual outputs, two multiplier events held in Split and Pula, two physical transnational project meetings (due to COVID-19 pandemic others are held in an online format due to epidemiological restrictions).Online conference on new technologies and AI was held, with respectable participants - rapporteur of European Parliament for the Digital Europe program and European innovator of the year 2017. Team members participated in “Europe in my region” conference.3D models for the blind and visually impaired were presented in the Pula amphitheater. Project results were presented and tested in project partners' schools. At the international exhibition iENA 2021 in (Nurnberg- Germany) project won bronze medal. Silver medal was gained at the international innovation fair ARCA 2021 in Zagreb, Croatia. These awards were exhibited at Medical School Pula exhibition. Project has been presented at two events organized by Croatian Erasmus National Agency - Agency for mobility and EU programs as examples of good practice. At the conference/multiplier event held in Pula, the consortium premiered a 3D walk of Pula's attractions and announced that it will be a gift to the City of Pula for the celebration of the City Day.

<< Results >>

Two intellectual outputs were produced within the project: "Handbook for 3D Recipes" and E-learning course/module – Guidelines for 3D and VR experience. Modules of the handbook for the VET pupils covered 3D printing, virtual reality (VR),  CAD-CAM modeling, robotics, and artificial intelligence (AI). Main activities besides generating educational materials and web page preparation included also the organization and management of the implementation of IO1.Within the IO2 E-learning course/module – Guidelines for 3D and VR experience and e-learning platform and the respective interactive tools were developed. IO2 is placed on the University of Pula Moodle - open-source platform which allows the construction of personalized learning environments. It allows tracking the learning progress and achievements of the pupils. The platform has three sections: Library/warehouse of 3D model, units containing introductory guidelines and a knowledge test which is a base to receive the badge/certificate. It is an open-source library where anyone can upload and download custom 3D objects made with Fusion 360. Additionally, 13 videos were filmed as extra learning material, which was not originally planned in order to add value to the project result.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2019-1-IT01-KA202-007823.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-IT01-KA202-007823.title: Forestry Operators – Reflecting on Equalising Skills and Training
2019-1-IT01-KA202-007823.summary:
<< Background >>

To develop a more inclusive, cohesive and competitive Europe, the recognition of competences and qualifications is essential. Europe is committed to establishing programmes and systems to facilitate the standardisation and mutual recognition of certificates and diplomas in all member states, an important process for both higher education and vocational training.
Regarding the forestry sector, a common training pathway to obtain the qualification 'forestry worker' has not yet been identified, nor a system of mutual recognition of competences. This lack was also highlighted in the European Commission's document 'A new EU Forestry Strategy: For Forests and the Forest Sector (2013)', which states that 'a strategy for forests and the forestry sector is necessary as there is no common EU forestry policy or framework for forest-related issues'.
At the European level, a profound discrepancy can also be seen in relation to the level of skills required to exercise this profession, as well as the social role of forestry workers in individual countries. The latter aspect is usually linked, on the one hand, to the socio-economic system of the country itself and, on the other, to the value attributed to forest heritage and green resources by the reference society.
The example of the Italian context is emblematic. There are no national regulations that precisely frame the profession of forestry operators and forestry workers, so the certification of skills is managed by the individual Region and is only recognised at a local/regional level.
Furthermore, in recent years we have witnessed an increase in environmental crises and natural disasters due to climate change. These natural events cause a great mobilisation of forestry workers and volunteers from different regions and countries. In response to this, the presence of a common skills recognition system is more than necessary, especially in terms of safety at work and proper coordination between countries in the case of cross-border interventions.

<< Objectives >>

Addressing the lack of a common strategy for the forestry sector in Europe, the project promoted the exchange of good practices and techniques between European countries regarding the roles of forestry operators, the skills needed for each role and standards for safety procedures. This approach helps to ensure safe and quality operations throughout Europe and to facilitate cooperation between public authorities responsible for the forestry sector and between operators themselves, for example in the case of cross-border operations. The aim of FOREST was to discuss the possibility of creating a standard level of competence and skills for forestry operators, valid across national borders, and to work together on joint projects to promote innovation and professionalism.
Considering the increased mobility of workers and volunteers in the event of natural disasters, the project focused on mapping, discussing and exchanging know-how regarding forest management, vocational training and safety standards. Collaboration between transnational partners was essential to compare training systems and link vocational training schools in different countries to increase student mobility and facilitate the comparison and alignment of skills.
The overall objective was the development of a sustainable partnership to lay the foundations and further discuss the possibility of creating a common curriculum for forestry workers that is valid and recognised nationally and transnationally.
From an international perspective, the aim was also to disseminate information on the social role of forestry workers and their contribution to forest management.

<< Implementation >>

The realisation of six exchange events at transnational level in the 5 European partner countries (Italy, Austria, Slovenia, Croatia, Romania) was essential to define a common strategy for the harmonisation of training systems and for the mutual recognition of competences, as well as to foster innovation and the introduction of sustainable tools. Through a peer-to-peer methodology, participants were enriched by collaboration and dialogue between colleagues.
Subsequently, a comparative analysis was conducted in the project partner countries (Italy, Austria, Slovenia, Croatia and Romania), with the aim of collecting and assessing the opinion of forest owners on the legislative framework for forestry operations. Fifty operators and forest owners were interviewed by means of a survey. The collection of the surveys was an opportunity to organise local meetings in order to share what has been learnt from the international exchanges with the main stakeholders of their territories, collecting reflections on the strategy to harmonise technical and legislative contents.
The final phase of the project was dedicated to the development of the manual "Towards standardised forestry education at the European level", which brings together the data collected from the interviews and the results of the analyses, some specific reflections on the importance of moving towards a harmonisation of forestry education, and an overview of the best practices that emerged in the project. The document is intended for institutions, education and vocational training practitioners as well as forestry workers.
As far as project management is concerned, 6 project meetings were organised at TPMs, of which 3 were face-to-face and 3 online due to the restrictions caused by the pandemic.

<< Results >>

The implementation of the project laid the foundation for the development of common training for forestry workers (common curriculum, transnationally recognised). The partners were engaged in raising awareness of the importance of forestry's contribution to tackling climate change and improving the social value of forestry workers' jobs.
At the end of the project, the following results were achieved
- 6 international exchange events
- 1 manual containing reflections on the standardisation of forestry training systems
- 5 comparative analyses conducted in Austria, Slovenia, Italy, Romania, Croatia
- 50 forest practitioners and forest owners interviewed
- 175 participants involved and raised awareness
- 1 final conference
topics: Overcoming skills mismatch and addressing the needs of the labour market

2019-1-LT01-KA202-060725.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-LT01-KA202-060725.title: Development of the international conception of police cadets training through cooperative learning
2019-1-LT01-KA202-060725.summary:
<< Background >>

In order to ensure a successful and modern training of police cadets, who have good analytical communication skills and independent global thinking, a need to create innovative training schemes and means, which promote the development of internationally acknowledged competencies and skills and include the police training institutions of other countries into the training process, arises. Consequently, the development of the above-mentioned high-quality skills and competencies through the innovation strategic partnership project directly responds to the needs of the institutions responsible for training police officers in different project partner countries in different sectors of education (higher education and vocational education). For this reason, foreign institutions – Police School in Slupsk (Poland) and Police Academy (Croatia) have been chosen as project partners.
The project focused on finding opportunities to harmonise the training process in the partner countries or to find similarities which would contribute to creating relevant training frameworks to promote quality mobility placements of cadets in police education institutions in other countries including credit transfer implementation (ECVET).

<< Objectives >>

The following objectives were planned to accomplish:
- to create a training programme for police cadets dedicated to international police cadet groups. It enables police cadets from foreign countries to participate in the training process by acknowledging their learning outcomes.
- to organise pilot training in two stages. First stage- pilot training activities were held in each partner institution as a part of the creation of the training programme. Second stage- second international pilot training activities were held in three countries. The events were intended to develop the abilities of communication and international cooperation among police cadets, as well as critical thinking, situation management, command and decision making by means of cooperative learning.
- to develop methodical recommendations for trainers regarding the principles of the organisation of international training events, the application of training methods and the use of training tools through the implementation of the cooperative learning programme.
- to organise transnational meetings with project partners.
- to organise the project closing conference.

<< Implementation >>

The covid-19 constraints influenced an extension of the project's timeframe, the organisation of physical meetings and training. The planned activities were rescheduled, but the project's objectives were achieved and decisions were taken according to the planned programme of activities. During the period of project implementation were completed:
- 4 transnational meetings with project partners.
- pilot training in two stages: in each partner institution and three international pilot training events. The three training sessions were organised at different times in three countries, with a one-week break in between. This approach allowed for adjustments, revisions, changes and improvements to the training programmes.
- creating a training programme for police cadets ("Joint programme for police cadets training through cooperative learning" of 40 academic hours) dedicated to international police cadet groups.
- development of "Methodical recommendations for trainers".
- The project closing conference - as one of the project results' dissemination channels to present intellectual outputs and sharing cadets’ experience to local and international partners.

<< Results >>

During the project, two intellectual outputs were produced:
- a unified training programme for police cadets ("Joint programme for police cadets training through cooperative learning" of 40 academic hours) that enables to implement of international cadet training thus facilitating the development of cadet exchange and the formation of long-term partnerships with foreign police education institutions. The programme has been validated and integrated into training programmes of the partner institutions and enables police cadets from foreign countries to participate in the training process by acknowledging their learning outcomes.
 - the "Methodical recommendations for trainers" defined the basic principles for the organisation of international training events based on cooperative learning, the application of training methods, and the use of training tools and training material. The recommendations are intended for trainers implementing international cooperative learning for police cadets.
The training programme and recommendations are presented in electronic forms and have been officially approved by the partner institutions.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2019-1-MK01-KA202-060350.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-MK01-KA202-060350.title: A Career Counselling Conceptual Model for increasing of ICT entrepreneurship skills of VET secondary schools students
2019-1-MK01-KA202-060350.summary:
<< Background >>

The partnership between the PPs involved in this project was created months before starting to create the project idea.
During the discussions and analysis prior writing the application for this project, the PPs concluded that VET teachers are usually
"bombarded" with requests for opinion about choosing of the faculty /or other future careers/ from the senior students in VET schools in the three countries participating in this project. Unfortunately most of VET teachers lack skills and competences to implement some of the Career Development Activities and assist in students choices with providing a proper advice that will at least reduce their dilemmas.
Schools today have to be more and more concerned with making their students “future-ready.”
That is the main reason why PPs decided to apply for a project for Complete career counseling process, creating business plan and practical inside in ICT entrepreneurship.
With this project we offered and meet the needs for:
- Teachers to get acknowledged with complete carrier guidance process in order to be skilled and help to students in the direction for selecting the future career by newly developed Conceptual Model of career guidance and Counseling process;
- A specially created Career Explorations' program for VET schools' students;
- A work-based competitive activities of students' teams in development of Sustainable Business Model, with included "pitching Investors" approach;
- further professional development for VET schools' staff in support and promotion of potential of youth entrepreneurship

<< Objectives >>

With this project the PPs wanted to:
- Increase the skills and competences of VET teachers and students in better understanding of interconnections between non-formal education, vocational training and labor market respectively;
- Develop new Conceptual module for career counseling which will be implemented in the VET schools with high level of transferability in other schools.
- Promote creative thinking by developing innovative ideas for future ICT based businesses' start-ups among present and future generations of students in project partners VET secondary schools;
- Boost ICT team-entrepreneurship potential among youngsters in municipalities of Kochani, Daruvar and Thira Santorini;
- Integration of “Entrepreneurship & Innovation” as part of the non-formal educational programs at VET schools in Kochani, Daruvar and Thira Santorini;
- Support local e-societies of Kochani, Daruvar and Thira Santorini with qualified ICT SMEs
- Establishing a synergy among VET schools and organizations active in different fields in other socio-economic sectors;
- Further professional development for VET schools' staff in support and promotion of potential of youth entrepreneurship;

<< Implementation >>

For achievement of the project goal and objectives PPs conducted:
- Three transnational PPs meetings;
- Three Shot-term joint staff training events for VET secondary school teachers conducted in accordance with planned Agenda and scope of works;
- 1 Short-term mobility of groups of pupils, for members of best student's teams on national levels, performed in accordance with specially created Career Exploration program;
- about 30 VET schools' teachers trained and have created own eTwinning account, within internal dissemination events in VET schools (min 10 VET school teachers per each school);
- 1 long term teaching assignment
- 3 Multiplier events (one in each country)
- Dissemination of what was learned during the trainings to the teachers in each school.

<< Results >>

1. Created multidisciplinary Career Counseling Conceptual Model consisted of:
-Career Guidance and Counseling module with included Career Test software;
-Process of development of a Business ideas and Basic Business Models including the best "pitching Investors" approach.
- Career Exploration program with Real Work -Based experience for students in ICT company dealing with Augmented reality as well as Virtual reality as “state of the art” software solutions.
2. One Document for transnational strategic partnership among different socio-economical entities for implementation of ICT entrepreneurship potential in non-formal education in VET secondary schools in Kochani, Daruvar and Thira Santorini created;
3. Students’ team work skills are improved;
4. To share the best practice by eTwinning module;
- 32 participants from project partners’ organizations;
- 30 teachers and 87 students from Secondary schools in internal dissemination and long term teaching assignments;
- 120 local stakeholders on 3 national multiplier events.
- Project web page created.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2019-1-MK01-KA202-060468.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-MK01-KA202-060468.title: Think global, entrepreneur local
2019-1-MK01-KA202-060468.summary:
<< Background >>

Social entrepreneurship in schools refers to teach students through learning-by-doing. The teachers guide students through the process of building their own social enterprise ideas that address a local community or school issue. Social enterprise, which is very popular today requires entrepreneurial skills and a community mindset, so it can be competitive at the market. The goal of the project is building the qualities, empowering students who will see themselves as young innovators and change-makers who can make a difference in creative ways and launch their own initiatives. In the realization of this goal the teachers will give their contribution through mutual work with the students, giving directions for work, by using the skills, competences and knowledge gained in the project. The teachers' guide, the curricula and handbook for social entrepreneurship, which are outputs of the project will be used as part of regular school activities on continues base, in every school year in the future.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing this project we want to involve social entrepreneurship in educational process, we want to make training of staff for realization of teaching for social entrepreneurship, to create curricula and Teachers guide by which VET educational process will produce social responsible and creative persons with entrepreneurial spirit for solving social problems, to create handbook based on previous research and analyses of the results.

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the project, various activities were organized in the school. The teachers and students who were a part of the implementation of the project, together with the students, had various activities such as surveys that were conducted in order to collect information that we needed for the production of intellectual outputs. Because the project had an extension due to the Covid situation, many activities were carried out online. So, two LTTA meetings as well as transnational meetings were held online, except for the first one, which was held with physical presence. The last learning, teaching, training activities meeting was realized with physical presence due to calming down of the corona virus situation. In the course of the realization of the project, dissemination as well as multiplier events were realized in Croatia as well as in Macedonia. All three intellectual outputs were presented at individual dissemination activities.

<< Results >>

Social entrepreneurship is explicitly about creating value for others: economic, social and environmental value. With this project we want to gain competences, knowledge and skills for all involved participants, to think, do and act as an entrepreneurs, while solving some social problem. The core values of this project resonate with long-standing key concepts of social entrepreneurship.
Challenge, enjoyment, relevance, depth, development of the whole person with creative ideas and entrepreneurial solutions are at the core of social entrepreneurship. The entrepreneurial environment encourages staff and students to see each other in a different light, building positive relationships and improving self-awareness and understanding of social entrepreneurship. They can be creative and fill useful while finding solutions for real social problems.
Results of the project are:
1. Developing students' competencies - innovation, leadership, visionary, ethics, personal development, sharing experiences that illustrate social entrepreneurship.
2. Getting familiar with the basic concepts of social entrepreneurship and social innovation
3. How to start social enterprise,
4. Legal framework regarding social economy and entrepreneurship,
5. Marketing for social enterprise,
6. How to find investors.
7. Developing a social business plan,
Outputs of the project:
1. Teachers guide for teaching social entrepreneurship with e-books with good practices 
2. Curricula for social entrepreneurship
3. Handbook "Think global, entrepreneur local"
Partnerships between staff in schools, other educational settings and with other organizations will create working relationships that contribute to professional development for teachers and educators and construct clear pathways for integrating social entrepreneurship to teachers guide, curriculum and handbook. Realizing this vision will contribute to the well being of our children and young people and enable them to become resilient, responsible citizens and successful lifelong learners, who contribute effectively to our local and global society. New approach integrated learning, new traditions in partner institutions will be created. The project will produce a comprehensive set of tools for social entrepreneurship: photo album from all project activities, videos promoting social entrepreneurship, teachers guide for social entrepreneurship, curricula and handbook with examples. Everything will be created together with all partners in the project, and the divided equally.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2019-1-PT01-KA202-060782.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-PT01-KA202-060782.title: beeB - Foster for beekeeping bridges through innovative and participative training
2019-1-PT01-KA202-060782.summary:
<< Background >>

Beekeeping is an art which has been practiced for thousands of years and has assumed a growing importance both as a production activity (honey, wax, propolis, royal jelly, etc) and has a critical pillar sustaining biodiversity by providing essential pollination for a wide range of crops and wild plants. In fact the majority of crops grown in the Europe depend on insect pollination and 71% of them on bee pollination.

Honey bees (Apis mellifera) is the most commonly managed bee in the world. In recent years, humankind has witnessed a reduction in the number of bees, not only due to the diseases that afflict them, but also as a result of intensive agriculture and pesticide use, starvation and poor bee nutrition and environmental changes. In addition, the recent invasion of the Asian hornet worsened the situation because of its predatory action on bees. Furthermore, the end of the beekeeping activity as we know it will threaten the survival of the species Apis mellifera because of its total dependence on man beekeeping practices.

There is therefore an urgent need to adopt measures to protect and promote beekeeping and beekeepers. That is one of the European Commission priorities, that has a strategy for tackling the decline in bee numbers across Europe, to protect the health of bees and to support beekeepers (https://ec.europa.eu/food/animals/live_animals/bees/health_en). 

In the European Union (EU), the number of beekeepers is slightly declining, but the number of beehives remains stable. A similar scenario occurs in Portugal, where the number of hives has increased, reflecting the increase in the size of bee farms. In terms of honey production, even though the EU is the world's second largest producer, it does not produce enough honey to meet the domestic demand. At the level of professionalization (number of farms with more than 150 hives) in 2016 in the EU, they were only 3.98% of professional beekeepers, meaning that a majority are small and family beekeepers or family farmers with a marginal beekeeping activity.

Beekeeping is often promoted in the context of rural development because it provides monetary, nutritional, and social benefits to smaller farmers and families, without requiring land ownership or large amounts of capital investment. For similar reasons, beekeeping is also cited as a practice that has the potential to empower rural women and reduce unemployment.  

Given the (1) high importance of non-professionalized beekeepers in the EU, coupled with the (2) different education and training background of people having a beekeeping activity, as well as the (3) lack of specific training in this area, specially focused on modern beekeeping practices (including attention to nutrition, health, and environmental pressures), it seemed important to deliver a b-learning course in modern beekeeping to be built and shared by several countries, thereby fostering cooperation between countries for innovation in the sector, as well as the exchange of good practices. Thus, the beeB project emerged as an opporunity to answer these challenges

<< Objectives >>

The present project aims at overcoming of the negative trends that beekeeping faces, at increasing the economic growth and sustainable development through ecological and good beekeeping practices. This objective will be achieved by delivering a course based on the exchange of best and innovative beekeeping practices, on cross visiting for the promotion and exchange of experiences and implementation of innovation spirals. To this end, we propose to develop a technical training course in a b-learning and participative environment, thus contributing to improve the beekeeper’s level of digital skills. Finally, we propose to carry out activities aimed at beekeepers, technicians and the public in general as a way of disseminating knowledge and fostering the exchange of experiences, addressing the current problems faced by beekeeping, good practices in beekeeping and new ways of promoting bee products.

Public awareness and knowledge is also crucial for the survival and improvement of the bee sector. In that way, it is also intended to involve the general public through information and dissemination actions, such as “Bee Roadmaps” that allow to deliver attention to the importance of pollinators for the sustainability of nature and crop production, based on a participatory approach.

EU countries have different traditions related to beekeeping, as well as different levels of training and technical support, so it makes sense that this project is developed transnationally in order to promote exchange of knowledge and experiences between countries. The project will promote new forms of cooperation at the European level, involving different types of organizations and stakeholders, like official services, education and training institutions, small enterprises, agricultural organizations, farmers associations and others. All intervenient will collaborate in the development, promotion and dissemination of results, at international, national and regional level.

<< Implementation >>

The project created positive and long-lasting effects on the participating organisations and persons directly or indirectly involved in the organised activities, as well as on the beekeeping sector, specially at the nonprofessional, family and women beekeepers’ levels.

During the project, we developed and attractive education and training programmes inline with the expectations and needs of the beekeepers, both at family beekeeping units, women beekeepers and other stakeholders’ levels (professional beekeepers, technicians and beekeepers’ associations may also benefit from the project results and outputs). The process of creation included participatory approaches involving family and women beekeepers and the adoption of ICT-based methodologies (b-learning), aiming to develop a program and materials that fit and benefit local communities in rural territories, and contribute to reduce linked to the geographical and socio-economic disparities increasing competitiveness and employment at regional and local level, where this activity is or might be relevant. The most relevant results were: MOOC Course Curriculum, Collaborative b-Learning HUB for beekeeping with innovation and knowledge, Infographic and pills of knowledge ensemble of organic and good beekeeping practices, 
Bee health field tool, Cross visiting training guide and Bee roadmaps for citizens. Also, the activity Building new ideas for beekeeping using spirals of innovation, a international honey recipes book and the Ba-bee-bee game, for the general public were developed.

The transnational project meetings (and inumerous videoconferences), the training and multiplier events contributed to deepen the partnership, as well as to strengthen the relations with the beekeeping sector, building brigdes for future colaborations, increasing the european coehesion. The development of educational and training pathways that fosters to include family farmers and beekeepers, with an significant focus on the women role, contributed to horizontal priority: Social inclusion (also addressed on the Priorities announced by the Portuguese National Agency), by improving their technical and economic performance, increasing the employment possibilities (new and own business, technical jobs in beekeeping associations, etc etc), contributing to increase the economic and social conditions in rural territories, making the rural territories more appealing, creating new dynamics and jobs, thus reducing discrimination and inequalities between the rural and urban world and between professional and family beekeeping.

The training curriculum and program will also contribute to strengthen synergies and links that will favour the transition between sectors, stakeholders and learners of education and training at national level, with improved use of European reference tools for recognition, validation and transparency of competences and qualifications. The project contributed to enhance the quality and performance of VET systems, improving information and guidance systems and strengthening the European dimension in beekeeping management, consider the profile of the possible applied students and the closeness to them. Since the project will promoted creativity and innovation in the topic it will improve the employment and people’s capacity resulting in rapidly changing management quality in beekeeping, bringing socioeconomic benefits and also preserving the cultural heritage associated with beekeeping and beehive products use. Furthermore, organic and good beekeeping practices offer potential benefits to human health and are extremely important for maintain the food systems, biodiversity and equilibrium of the entire planet. Thus, beekeepers that improve their knowledge in these technologies are improving the welfare of people, promoting human health and protecting the environment. 

The implementation of the proposed partnership between learning institutions and beekeepers and farmers organizations, will allow several learning mobility experiences, promote interdisciplinary co-operation, based on work-based learning and promoting the permeability between the different education and training pathways.Working in the BeeB partnership originated a dynamic, committed and professional environment inside each organisation, fostering the integration of good practices and new methods into daily activities and opening opportunities for new synergies with these and other organisations active in the involved fields and socio-economic sectors.

The project is also to develop user-friendly vocational training tools that can be used at the workplace – b-learning, with a particular attention to the low-skilled beekeepers, and with relevant and innovative learning contents in the field of organic and good beekeeping practices which will be based upon the main principles of EC agriculture policies (contribute to sectoral priority VET: Developing partnerships aimed at promoting work-based learning in all its forms, also addressed on the Priorities announced by the Portuguese National Agency). It will be created a b-learning (blended learning - via electronic and online media and field training visits) platform which support improvements in quality and innovation in vocational education by allowing training at work place, when it’s needed, and allowing in initial and continuing training, with immediate possible application, and providing access to different users and experts from various institutions.

<< Results >>

The most relevant results were: MOOC Course Curriculum (MOOC Course structure, Manual Beekeeping. Reference text for a MOOC course, Analysis of the target groups needs and preferences report, leaflet and scientifc paper), Collaborative b-Learning HUB for beekeeping with innovation and knowledge and Infographic and pills of knowledge ensemble of organic and good beekeeping practices (a set of infographics and videos to allow learners desgin their learning pathway), Bee health field tool (interative tool and a ba-bee-bee game), Cross visiting training guide (guidelines and training itineraries for beekeepers) and Bee roadmaps for citizens (a set of video roads to contribute to increase the awareness in relation to bees and polinators). Also, the activity Building new ideas for beekeeping using spirals of innovation, a international honey recipes book and the Ba-bee-bee game, for the general public were developed. Also, the transnational project meeting, the staff training and multiplier events were particularly relevant to streghten relations and european cohesion among participants, organizations and territories. New projects emerged from beeB partnership, namely related with bee health monitoring, natural beekeeping, drone flour.

2019-1-PT01-KA202-061281.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-PT01-KA202-061281.title: A digital approach to qualifying technicians in Energy Efficiency in Buildings
2019-1-PT01-KA202-061281.summary:
<< Background >>

The partners applied for this project to try to be in line with the objectives of the EU that in 2016, presented the "Clear Energy for all Europeans“ package of proposals aiming to bring EU energy legislation in line to the new 2030 climate and energy targets, aiming at the creation of an integrated energy system at a European level and a European workforce with all the necessary competences to build and manage the energy system of the future.
A study published by CEDEFOP (2018) regarding the training needs in the industry showed that universities are having an active role in education and research in the field of energy efficiency, leading to the conclusion that the existing higher qualifications and skills match with the current needs of the sector, but “the labor market still lacks medium-level and operational manpower, jobs that do require not academic training but solid technical skills”. It was based on this need for specialized manpower, in addition to academic skills, that the partnership identified the need to create a course to train technicians currently working in the area of energy efficiency who want to update or improve their qualifications and also unemployed.

<< Objectives >>

The purpose of the project is to contribute for the 2030 climate and energy targets, through the equipment of EU citizens with a quality harmonized qualification on energy efficiency in buildings, developed to be recognized through all European Union. For this, European tools have been used, such as EQF and ECVET, using Learning Outcomes, oriented vocational curriculum for EQF level 4 and being in line with quality assurance mechanisms (EQAVET).
This qualification on energy efficiency has been built with a view on its potential harmonization among all European Union countries and developed for a b-learning approach.
The target groups for this qualification are workers currently in the energy efficiency field who want to update or upgrade their qualification, workers in need to reskill and unemployed people.

<< Implementation >>

O4-5: Validation and Testing. RPL scheme and tools validation and testing
The RPL validation and testing process was carried out in Croatia and Greece, with 3 participants in each country. 
C1 - EU transfer workshop. 
A successful 3 days transfer workshop was organized by the Project partners 16 participants gathered on the Zoom platform to check out the project results developed so far, and they also got the opportunity to test the WebQuests, which represent a truly innovative qualification assessment tool.
O5-3: Pilot Development
In each country organized a pilot course that aimed to introduce the REACT curriculum and test the teaching materials.
In each national pilot course, 2 competence units were tested.
E1 - Multiplier event in Greece was held 2-4 November and gathered 17 participants. It was used to present the learning tools and experiment with the game linked to learning to VET providers as well as networking with civil engineering and energy efficiency stakeholders from Thessaloniki.
E2 - Multiplier event in Croatia was organized in November 2021. There were in total 20 participants 
E3 - The Final conference was held on 16th of December and had around 45 participants throughout the day.

<< Results >>

The project produced the following outputs:
-1 Dissemination Plan
-1 website and social media (Facebook and Linkedin pages)
-3 teasers
-6 Newsletters (Portuguese, English, Greek and Croatian)
-1 Flyer /poster
-2 National outreach seminars for stakeholder
-1 Final Conference
The results that were developed in 4 languages (Portuguese, English, Greek and Croatian) are:
-Curriculum (IO1) constituted by Professional Profile, Competence Matrix, Training Methodology, Summative Assessment Overview and Alternative Path for obtaining the EEEBT Qualification.
-Training Materials (IO2): Videos, Concept maps, training modules, games, quiz and handbook.  
-Summative assessment Framework (IO3): 20 +5 single choice questions, 2 practical assignments for each CU and 4 webquests
-Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) (IO4) constituted by the documents: Application form, Form of professional and personal motivations, Interview guide (general and technical), portfolio checklist, Self-assessment of competences, Assessment and diplomas.
-Guideline for further exploitation (IO5).

2019-1-RO01-KA202-063965.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-RO01-KA202-063965.title: A Trainers Toolkit To Foster STEM Skills Using Microcontroller Applications
2019-1-RO01-KA202-063965.summary:
<< Background >>

EU priorities of educational systems are to train students in STEM fields and to arrange for hands-on, multidisciplinary, and creative learning opportunities in the classroom. It is imperative that new, dynamic, interdisciplinary, and collaborative methods be developed in order to incentivize progress in the hard sciences, logical disciplines, and cutting-edge equipment. Inventions are built on Future Technologies, and Microcontrollers encouraging real-world, multidisciplinary learning enhancement of one's career and the growth of one's digital VET abilities. The European Union's Commission is always pushing for more widespread use of digital tools in classrooms, applying cutting-edge tools to classroom instruction. The importance of increasing student motivation through 
incorporation of cutting-edge strategies for educational instruction that inspire the use of emerging technology in place of employment is necessary.
Together, engineers, IT experts, and educators in the STEM fields aimed to develop the foundation for building the fundamental and transferable skills necessary to succeed in today's European labor market jobs in the future.
The incorporation of microcontrollers into the modern classroom and the subsequent increase in student interest in STEM subjects provides a realistic perspective on the classroom experience in educational institutions. Also, it entails and makes use of the cutting-edge pedagogical tool of the "flipped classroom," in which educators should encourage their pupils to reverse the traditional learning process by having them begin with the desired outcome.
When you combine the opportunity for outsourcing with this type of learning process, you get people who are more marketable in today's most competitive industries of work.

<< Objectives >>

Microprocessors and microcontrollers have quickly become indispensable in numerous engineering fields. For the "internet of things," "smart cities," "sensor networks," etc. to function, nearly all modern intelligent electronic devices require one or more microprocessor or microcontroller chips.
Partner institute needs assessments highlight the critical importance of preparing VET students and teachers with the skills necessary to thrive in the Information Age of Technology. Based on the findings of the assessments it was clear that there was a demand for realistic classroom situations that take into account two key aspects of the labor market: the development of integrated STEM abilities in students and the need to train and educate future educators. In order to help students develop skills useful in the workplace, educators must have access to open educational resources (OER) and appropriate professional development opportunities. Trainers and educators are interested in collaborating with professionals from various educational systems and the business world to share best practices. Students' demands on trainers stem from their own desires to practice STEM skills on real-world gadgets utilized in the industries of the future (including the ones in which they will find employment after graduation). Future employees need to have their STEM skills honed in a realistic, market-responsive way, and this responsibility falls on both businesses and educational institutions. Companies working on the project have developed a series of questions for use in VET institutions and schools to conduct a needs assessment. Trainers in vocational and educational training (VET) convened focus groups of students and teachers to discuss and prioritize training needs. The necessity of designing, constructing, operating, and programming devices with embedded systems has led to an increase in mechanization, as is obvious to everybody. All of our affiliated organizations provide services related to guidance and mentoring. This project's goal is to pool existing knowledge and experience to develop implementable instruments (IOs) that can be used by other VET providers across Europe to meet this demand. National curriculums emphasize theory and encourage the growth of modular solutions in contrast to the business world, which presents an engineering-based, project-oriented view of employment requirements, the scientific worldview of schools emphasizes the development of skills.
Schools provide the theoretical/methodological framework necessary for integrating these abilities, while businesses provide the empirical/technical framework.
Training for the jobs of the twenty-first century requires a broad range of abilities, from engineering and computer science to creative problem solving, teamwork, and entrepreneurship. To meet the problems of this century, the next generation will need a deeper understanding of mathematical and scientific concepts, as well as the skills to integrate and apply them.
Project objectives: 1. Identifying means to project, program and use embedded systems for educational purposes 
2. Elaborating curricular resources centered on the use of STEM skills to accomplish devices based on microcontrollers
3. Implementing learning activities in STEM school subjects with the view of familiarizing students with the new technologies based on microcontrollers
4. Creating a study curricula for the free access to resources created on the theme of developing applications with microcontrollers.
5. Developing new EU partnerships, with transfer of good practices and innovative curricular resources between the institutions that target the development of STEM skills.

<< Implementation >>

The proposed initiatives, based on the needs assessment and the current plan, were intended to address the pressing methodological issues that have been identified. We hoped to ease students' transition into the jobs of the future by helping them acquire the most in-demand technology skills by bringing together the perspectives of various actors participating in the paradigm from the educational to professional parcours. Therefore, in the first three outputs, we aimed to lay the groundwork for effective student experiments, collect the data and develop a curriculum, establish the methodological guidelines, pilot the curriculum, and compile all feedback into a toolkit that can serve as a valuable resource, be replicated and used by other VET schools, and guarantee the proposal's long-term viability. The toolkit includes pedagogical situations and pre-made computer-assisted lessons for anyone interested in teaching the abilities we believe to be essential in today's high-tech world.
Equal time and responsibility were given to each partner in the project, based on their specific areas of competence. We had five international meetings, one training, and three multiplier events for this project. The actions were time-and goal -bound, and they all contributed to creating the IOs and spreading, multiplying, and capitalizing on the project's findings. Training professionals can improve their skills thanks to the IOs' implementation in schools, and student engagement in STEM education is expected to increase. By using a flipped classroom approach, we can guarantee that students learn both the foundational skills and the transdisciplinary skills identified in the needs assessment. With the help of industry experts, IOs were made even more cutting-edge, enhancing thus the number of opportunities available to Vet school graduates in the job market. The workforce can benefit from workers who have the skills necessary to meet the challenges of Industry 4.0.
Each VET institution provided flipped classroom sessions, students carried out the recommendations made by the business partners. Classes of 30 students  participated in the experiments at schools, with an additional 200 students from the 3 partner schools serving as a trial group for the modules. Together with student project teams, business leaders developed resources that STEM educators may use in their own classroom experiments.

<< Results >>

Involving educational systems from different nations with growth potential and the ability to export technology to other European countries gives the initiative a transnational component. Learning is presented through a student-centered approach through hands-on experience. It is believed that by improving the availability of VET centers to readily available technical resources, the insertion of graduates into the labor market will be improved thanks to a curriculum that is more in line with market demands. Young people want to use cutting-edge tools in realistic workplace settings while learning for free (open source). Vocational and technical education programs should form alliances with prominent businesses using these technologies. Partners in this initiative will advocate for new, system-level approaches that provide sufficient funding for cutting-edge technology.
The project's outcomes include: - improved skills in European project management and application development using microcontrollers among project team members from all partner organizations; - improved skills in application development using microcontrollers among STEM teachers from all partner schools.
From those three schools, 200 students with advanced STEM skills will serve as pilot testers for the curriculum.
The results include 5 intellectual products (three curriculum modules, a library of educational models, a manual, and an online course), four newsletters  detailing the progress of the project, one Multiplier Event held in each VET school partnership country. Also embedded systems/microcontrollers are to be used in the classroom, and chapters O1-O3 of the handbook cover the microcontroller curriculum. The toolkit includes case studies, tutorials, photographs, a library of documents, and a wealth of useful resources. Each VET institution worked with a private sector partner to develop two microcontroller application prototypes.
The higher institution ensured that all scientific data is up to par, with a particular emphasis on the transfer of knowledge from the academic to the business world and the provision of management-level insight to the IOs. The inclusion of STEM and IT themes in the curriculum better prepares students to comprehend the role microcontrollers play in a wide range of devices.
O1: A course on the design and construction of a microcontroller-based system or application (the creation of a plant-watering gadget, a fire alarm, etc.).
O2: Programming Instructions for the Hardware Module
O3: Implementing the tools into educational initiatives with a particular emphasis on bolstering STEM disciplines.
O4: A Methodological Guide for Implementing STEM Teacher Trainers and Piloting Instructional Outcomes 1-3, Complete with Assessment Methodology and Project Work Integration, to Improve Student Motivation and Performance in STEM Courses. VET institutions are able to use the project's curriculum for experimental programs.
O5: A pedagogical toolkit with 25 sets of pedagogical situations developed from piloting module feedback. Some examples of such resources are evaluative tests, project topics, evaluation charts, the project evaluation sheet, and student motivation to study mechatronics and robotics as a result of exposure to STEM disciplines and Computer Studies.

2019-1-SI01-KA202-060553.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-SI01-KA202-060553.title: Modern and Innovative onLine-based Know-how on European Dairy processing
2019-1-SI01-KA202-060553.summary:
<< Background >>

Farming throughout Europe is facing a challenge in how to survive with income only from agricultural activity. In Common Agricultural Policy orientations 2014-2020 it is stressed that it is necessary to
encourage the creation of additional sources of revenue for farms. One of the possible ways to deliver alternative services to broaden and diversify the scope of on-farm activities with other subsidiary activities is processing primary farm products. The 3-year Secondary school programme to gain the qualification for a Dairy Operative has not been carried out in Slovenia in the past ten years while demand for non-formal adult education in the same field has been growing. Farmers who attend these courses, are faced with the issue of course accessibility due to afternoon farm work obligations. With MILK-ed project, we aimed at developing a training programme that is going to equip farmers with the necessary knowledge, skills and competencies for the establishment of an on-farm dairy processing activity. To ensure sustainability of small farms, the backbone of all rural areas, we need to provide farmers with knowledge and skills to diversify their farms to ensure they are not dependent on only one source of income.

<< Objectives >>

Our mission for this project was to provide farmers and dairy production experts with knowledge, skills and competencies for innovative and modern dairy processing online and free of charge. We wanted to achieve our mission by implementing:
- Providing inclusive education and training focused on modern and innovative dairy processing
- Providing a comprehensive online educational platform and promoting the integration of digital technologies in VET
- Promoting access to learning through OER
- Promoting OER in different languages (English, Croatian, Italian, Serbian, Slovenian, and Spanish) and produced in Europe
- Fostering the initial and continuous professional development of formal and non-formal VET providers/trainers in the field of agriculture making them able to train family farmers, students of agricultural programmes, landowners and other rural entrepreneurs for the establishment of an on-farm dairy processing activity.

<< Implementation >>

We implemented project management activities to ensure project's objectives, outputs and reporting were done in foreseen timeline and expected quality. We implemented activities in which we achieved all purposed intellectual outputs. We created case studies for best practice examples from all partners countries (except Lithuania), which were translated in all partners languages and English. We designed and implemented new and innovative training modules on dairy processing which are available free of charge on project's educational platform in English, Slovenian, Serbian, Croatian, Italian and Spanish language. Case studies are also available on the platform in all mentioned languages. We developed  the theoretical and practical curriculum that presents knowledge, skills and competencies for milk processing. During the duration of the project all project partners were implementing dissemination activities to promote the project. We pilot tested the platform and did an evaluation report to optimize the platform and training modules. We organised multiplier events in all partners countries (except Lithuania).

<< Results >>

We created 4 intellectual outputs. We developed case studies for best practices from Slovenia, Serbia. Croatia, Italy and Spain, which included selection of the most relevant successful entrepreneurs from each country. This Case studies were a basic component of a training program.
We created an online-based educational platform where participants can learn all the essentials about dairy processing. The contents for it were developed after we have researched and collected relevant case studies. The training program was focused on modern and innovative dairy processing which  was prepared with the partners cooperation.For educational platform we developed modern and innovative training modules and educational videos in dairy processing which are available free of charge in English, Slovenian, Croatian, Serbian, Italian and Spanish language. We also  included training modules of some local products from different partners countries.
We developed  the theoretical and practical curriculum that presents knowledge, skills and competencies for farmers who would like to diversify their farming activity with dairy processing or dairy processor who would like to increase their knowledge of dairy processing.
topics: Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas
Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas

2019-1-TR01-KA202-074033.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2019-1-TR01-KA202-074033.title: InternPrize : Business Ideas Generation
2019-1-TR01-KA202-074033.summary:
<< Background >>

BIG InternPrize was conceived to:
- establish a new structured and permanent form of relationship and cooperation between VET and enterprise in a Community of Practice,
- introduce the use of bite size learning as a non-formal education that is totally mobile, flexible and easy to take up by a very wide variety of learners and 
- energise young minds to generate business ideas, possibly inspiring startups with sustainability mindsets.

It met the needs of:
young people who
- show promising talent, business orientation and acumen,
- need confidence and help with career orientation,
- may be kept in education with learning environments that are less formal.
- have already started their working life but who can do better given the opportunity to grow and
- could get back into education.

VET trainers needing:
- exposure to the new forms of working with industry and
- new skills and tools for the generation and creative presentation of business ideas, mentoring and leadership of young people.

+ the VET sector always in need of modernisation to maintain relevance in future careers.

+ Industry and the community benefiting from less mismatch between the outcomes of formal education and what employers are looking for in new employees.

<< Objectives >>

BIG InternPrize was established to:
- establish a new structured and permanent form of relationship and cooperation between VET and enterprise in a Community of Practice environment,
- introduce the use of bite size learning as a supplement to formal education, a new form of non-formal education that is totally mobile, flexible and easy to take up by a very wide variety of learners including those who are already starting or thinking of changing their studies or careers, who might be at risk of ESL due to disgruntlement with formal education and those who could possibly see the value to go back into education,
- train VET trainers in mentoring and energising young minds to generate business ideas,
- experiment (and create a concrete example for future emulation and further development) of the use of peer review of the business ideas of students by entrepreneurs who then, in their turn, also serve as role models and
- inspire start ups with thought and due consideration of all economic, ethical, environmental, social responsibility and technical aspects necessary for a successful business rather than with improvisation and trial-and-error.

It was also intended to bring in leadership skills into formal education.

<< Implementation >>

There were horizontal activities related to:
- Management and Implementation,
- Validation and Quality Management and
- Dissemination and Sustainability Strategies.
These activities lasted throughout the project lifetime to sustain the implementation of the project.

The partners implemented three IOs through activities that were in most phases of the project consecutive to each other.

For the IOs the partners implemented
1. RESEARCH ACTIVITIES producing 25 mini research papers on the subject of bite size learning

2. GENERATION AND USE OF VALIDATION TOOLS to be used as part of the strategy of adoption of bite size learning.

3. A JOINT POSITION PAPER on the subject of "VET for the Always Connected, the Disconnected and the Discontented."

4. PRODUCED BITE SIZE LESSONS during training activities C1 and C2 planned in key with 10 skills from the Entrecomp Framework

5. TESTED THE BITE SIZE LESSONS strategy with students

6. PRODUCED TEMPLATES ON THE COP PLATFORM FOR THE GENERATION AND PRESENTATION OF BUSINESS IDEAS and mentored students to use them

6. ORGANISED A PITCHING OF BUSINESS IDEAS CAMP IN MALTA in C3

The partnership published the outputs and results and set the project on a further exploitation plan for sustainability.

<< Results >>

BIG InternPrize brought about
HIGHER QUALITY, WIDER SCOPE AND MORE RELEVANCE OF VET IN LINE WITH PRESENT EMPLOYMENT TRENDS through new skills and tools in the hands of educators to support creativity and a sense of entrepreneurship in the minds and attitudes of young people.

YOUTH LEADERSHIP SKILLS IN FORMAL EDUCATION through trainers taking the lead to learn how to be better trainers presenting in TED TALKS format, in key with the Generation Z mindset that is media oriented, mentoring them through a path towards confidence in themselves and their ideas, instilling in them a critical and analytical mindset during the pitching competition. This widened the scope of education with VET extending itself more into career development, fostering of a sense of entrepreneurship and mentoring.

MORE SUSTAINABLE SUPPORT TO BUDDING CAREERS through the peer review and validation of ideas of economic opportunities for communities during the pitching activities. Students had a forum in which they can obtain objective feedback for their business ideas.

NEW FORM OF ENGAGEMENT OF PLAYERS IN EDUCATION AND ENTERPRISE IN A COP that is not generic networking but more engaging at the level of individual professionals during pitching of business ideas.
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-AT01-KA202-077956.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-AT01-KA202-077956.title: Using Interactive Infographics to Promote Problem Based Learning for the Development of Key Transversal Skills
2020-1-AT01-KA202-077956.summary:
<< Background >>

BFI is a strong believer in Corporate social responsibility and therefore aims to contribute to society by taking part in projects where the Institute’s knowledge and experience can be of use in addressing key social issues such as developing key skills.  As is written in the project application The European Commission has emphasized the need to develop key transversal skills in all sectors of education to sustain the high-value knowledge economy. BFI along with other partners on the project recognized the opportunity to provide all citizens with learning opportunities to develop key transversal skills like digital literacy, entrepreneurship, critical and creative thinking, leadership, innovation, problem-solving, teamwork, and social impact and highlights the importance of learning by doing within VET.  BFI is an organization that makes efforts to help the local community and raise the level of key transversal skills in all sectors of education to sustain the high-value knowledge economy.

<< Objectives >>

In the modern labour market, the challenge faced by employers is that key transversal skills are often hidden and extremely difficult to capture. All employees possess these skills to some extent, but for some, they are more developed than others and it is very important to help those who need to develop or upgrade these skills. Being able to recognise and develop their skills, can bring huge benefits to an organisation and its employees. The overall objective of the SKILL PICS project is to provide all citizens with key transversal skills like digital literacy, entrepreneurship, critical and creative thinking, leadership, innovation, problem-solving, teamwork, and social impact. The acquisition of such skills is not intended just for a specific field of work, but for their usage in a wider range of fields which will increase the value of the citizens in the labour market.

The objectives of this project are to:
•	Promote the acquisition of key transversal skills through the use of alternative pedagogical resources using a problem-based learning approach
•	Support acquisition of key transversal competences in VET
•	Support VET tutors to develop their own problem-based learning resources to include Digital Breakouts and WebQuests in an interdisciplinary way
•	Promote a cross-curricular approach to subjects and, consequently, collaborative work from tutors

<< Implementation >>

The following activities have been implemented during the project lifecycle: 

1.	Learning, Teaching, Training Activities

C1 Short-term joint staff training events - In-service Training
All partners sent a minimum of 2 appropriate and affiliated VET tutors for this event. As the training was e delivered in English all partners ensured that those selected to attend had excellent English language skills. The result of this in-service transnational training event was the establishment of a transnational group of VET tutors who supported each other and further implement the knowledge gained in their partner countries. The in-service training comprised 21 hours of face-to-face workshop instruction and 14 hours of online self-directed learning. Because of the COVID-19 pandemic and partners' inability to travel, the In-service training was held online and was broken into 3 workshops each one with a duration of 7 hours. Each workshop was broken down into a training session and a skills demonstration. 
This 3-day training addressed the following areas:
•	developing interactive and engaging materials using software programs like PowToon, VideoScribe, StoryBoardThat, Google Forms, Canva, KAHOOT, LearningApps etc.
•	building challenge-based learning resources such as digital breakouts or WebQuests
•	integrating media-rich content to develop interactive infographics
Documentation proving the maintenance of the described activity can be found in the Supporting Documentation that was sent via WeTransfer with this Report.

The C2 activity took place on 31 May, 1, 2, and 3 June 2022. It was carried out in a hybrid format, with only the partners from Ireland coming to Madrid (the city hosting the activity), while the rest of the partners connected online. Thus, both JAITEK and FIPL were able to enjoy the training in person, while BFI, CALLIDUS, ALK, RCA, FHB, and INNOVADE did it online. The activity took place on the Zoom videoconferencing platform, since it allowed the creation of smaller rooms apart from the general one, and had a total participation of 22 people. The activities carried out during the C2 were divided progressively during the 4 days of training. In addition, every day there were 30-minute activities that served as icebreakers at the beginning of the connection and 30-minute reflective activities at the end of the meetings.

2.	Implementation of the In-service Training for VET tutors in each partner country
After providing In-service training for adult educators, the next step was to provide In-service training in all partner countries. 112 VET tutors completed the in-service training with different numbers in each partner country. In some partner countries that number was very big (e.g., Spain). During this activity, every partner organisation has organised a local event where embedded learning has been promoted to relevant stakeholders in their countries. 
All the partners submitted evidence of the maintenance of the mentioned activities, and you can find them in the Supporting Documentation that was sent via WeTransfer with this Report.

3.	Multiplier events (workshops)
A minimum of 200 participants attended the SKILL-PICS workshops. During the Multiplier Event, all the resources created in the project were presented. The first one was the IO1: Interactive Infographics which was explained through the use of the 4 materials designed for each infographic and deepening in the 8 Transversal Skills selected by the project. The Multiplier Events were a great success both in terms of maximising project promotion and of developing the key transversal skills of participants. The multiplier events also raised awareness of the need for such skills and how they can help people in finding new jobs or improve their current. There is high potential for exploitation as the VET and adult educators that participated in the Multiplier events stated that they will definitely use the resources for their trainings and share them with other VET educators and all relevant stakeholders.
All the partners submitted evidence of the maintenance of the mentioned activities, and you can find them in the Supporting Documentation that was sent via WeTransfer with this Report.

4.	Final conference of the project where all the project results were shown to the appropriate target groups
62 managers and policymakers from the VET sector and the business development sector attended the Skill-Pics Final Conference which was held in Austria on the 12th of October 2022. At the Final conference, all the pedagogical outputs of the project have been presented. Also, BFI organised a discussion about the relevant topics that this project covers. 
Documentation proving the maintenance of the described activity can be found in the Supporting Documentation that was sent via WeTransfer with this Report.
