2020-1-AT01-KA202-078107.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-AT01-KA202-078107.title: Trainers for Plant Protection in Organic Farming
2020-1-AT01-KA202-078107.summary:
<< Background >>

The TOPPlant project was applied for because of the importance of organic farming and the recognised need for specialised training in this field. The project aims to meet the needs of organic farmers through the development of an innovative methodological curriculum, a comprehensive training manual, crop-specific guidelines and an interactive e-learning tool.

The project addresses the needs of organic farmers by providing appropriate and diverse learning opportunities through different learning techniques. It also supports the development of cooperative agricultural production in different regions by providing intensive extension in organic crop protection, production techniques and quality management. By implementing its innovative methodological curriculum and conducting pilot trainings, TOPPlant meets the need for specialised training in this field and provides the innovative training content through an e-learning tool that can also be accessed via smartphone. Ultimately, TOPPlant contributes to a better and healthier environment by promoting sustainable and clean agriculture.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of this project was to increase institutional capacity for professional training in plant protection in organic agriculture. We wanted to create the program and related materials that can be used for organizing various lifelong learning activities.
Our aim was also to prepare a Handbook for vocational education and training including all aspects of plant protection in organic farming (pest and disease control, weed management) and is applicable as teaching material in courses related to ecological farming at university or in adult educational programmes.
Supported by biohelp, with its 35 years long expertise in organic farming, UNIZG, their teaching as well as practcal expertise in agroculture, together with MATE and their expertise in agroculture and research, and specifically NAKLO Centre who carries out training in the field of agriculture within the scope of formal secondary vocational and technical education and higher education as well as formal and non-formal adult education, finally rounded up by ipcentre as an educational institution with vast experience in teaching - we believe that the objectives and aims have been well met. The project has produced significant outputs and has reached a wide audience.

<< Implementation >>

Naklo lead O1 and prepared special instruction on how to design TOPPlant Curriculum in-line with ECVET and EQF. Naklo prepared Module 1 (IO2), and crop-specific guidelines for onion (IO3) and the assessment/evaluation questionnaire for learning material (IO4).
UNIZG participated in the preparation of the IO1, coordinated the preparation of the IO2, wrote two chapters, and a guideline for grapes (IO3), supported preparation of the guidelines for potatoes, and reviewed rest of IO3. UNIZG was involved in the preparation of e-learning materials. 
MATE completed Module 5 (IO2) of the Handbook (Training Manual for Plant Protection in Organic Farming), prepared a complete Guideline for paprika cultivation  and the weed management section of another Guideline for potato cultivation. Mate involved a research breeder Miklós Pék at Institute of Horticultural Sciences of MATE as an expert in spice paprika production.
biohelp described methods and tools for disease control, guidelines for apple production, and diseases in potato production, and roofread IO2 and IO3. All partners organized a ME. Naklo organized an LTTA, supported by ipcenter. 
ipcenter had a leading role, and supported all IOs and ME events.

<< Results >>

The TOPPlant project produced: 
IO1 - TOPPlant Curriculum in-line with ECVET and EQF
IO2 - Training Manual for Plant Protection in Organic Farming, covering different crops (onion, paprika, potatoes, grape, apple). Training Manual is being used at the Agrocultural University in Zagreb as a supporting material in teaching. Due to the extensive research and efforts that were invested in creation of this Manual, the University Board had externals evaluators have a look at it before it was presented to students. 
IO3 - Guidelines for Plant Protection (each crop was specifically focussed on). An additional Crop was added, 4 were planed and 5 were then focused on, as the consortium agreed that it is doable, and logical given that there are 5 partners in the consortium.
IO4 - E- Learning Tool, available in all respective partner languages and in English.

2020-1-BG01-KA202-079268.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-BG01-KA202-079268.title: More Skilled Hands for Hi-Tech Production
2020-1-BG01-KA202-079268.summary:
<< Background >>

Despite the fact that it employs hundreds of thousands of workers across Europe and generates substantial profits, the composite industry has gone under the radar of the educational system. Although it is one of the few industries still valuing manual labour, the composite industry is characterised by a high added value. However, as with many other industries, the composite manufacturing sector companies suffer from the lack of qualified personnel and the fluctuation of the workforce. To cope with that issue, many companies are providing in-house training for employees.
To address all these challenges, project CompoWin produced a holistic, usable and attractive training system for future composite fabricators. It has been developed to assist SMEs and VET teachers/trainers of general technical knowledge to develop the necessary skills and methodologies to rapidly convert into teaching basic composite techniques. In addition, the newly developed content could be easily adapted and customised for the need for in-house training in composite companies or for reskilling current employees to work with composite materials and techniques.

<< Objectives >>

The CompoWin project focuses on creating a comprehensive, useful and attractive training system for future composite materials manufacturers. It works in several directions:
- Producing a comprehensive analysis of the composite industry development in partner countries, mapping the existing state of development, skills framework, barriers to employment, and current and future technological trends.
- Developing a comprehensive, useful and attractive training system for both employees and training providers to support the development of the composite industry across Europe.
- Addressing the lack of a national vocational standard for composite workers in Europe by initiating the process of transferring the training and vocational standard: Fabricator of plastic composite materials into the VET systems of Bulgaria and Croatia.

<< Implementation >>

The activities of the CompoWin project were grouped into four Intellectual Outputs:
IO1: The Competence and Skills Framework for the composite industry based on comprehensive secondary research in five European countries 
IO2: Training programme and content - Composite fabricator - my future vocation (Industry package) - a comprehensive training programme and content tailored to the specific needs and requirements of the composite industry. 
IO3: System for rapid adoption of a course for the composite industry by educational and commercial organisations (VET package) to serve as a primary reference for an initial go/no-go decision by a relevant manager/training expert of the educational organisation or VET provider whether to adopt the training or not. Following the development and preliminary evaluation of the Training Programme, it was piloted during a Train-the-trainers session (C1)  in Slovenia.
IO4:Transfer and expansion of the training and vocational standard: Fabricator of plastic composite materials - with the support and existing expertise of the partnership, BICC and 3dgrupa initiated procedures to approve and introduce the vocational standard in their national educational systems.

<< Results >>

- Composite Industry - Final Comparative Report delivers more comprehensive background information on the current state of development of the composite industry in participating countries and existing challenges that the sector is facing.
- Catalogue of opportunities and barriers to employment (COBE) and Potential Technologies Focus Catalogue (PTFC) offer an overview of the most common barriers to employment in the composite industry as well as the technological practices (current and future) that are utilised in the sector. 
- CompoHUB.eu e-learning platform and contents - completely updated and expanded with new content and topics. 
- Guidance System for Workers entering the composite industry - this original and innovative system offers a structured approach for planning and monitoring the progress of composite workers' skills development. The system was designed and tested by AFormX, and it was designed to go along with the updated and expanded e-courses on the CompoHub platform. 
- Step-by-Step Guide for Organising Training Sessions and Courses in Composites to enable companies, training providers and vocational schools to adopt the CompoWIN system for their own environment.
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-CZ01-KA202-078132.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-CZ01-KA202-078132.title: From technical drawing to CNC program
2020-1-CZ01-KA202-078132.summary:
<< Background >>

We wanted to expand the knowledge of students and teachers with new knowledge in the creation of technical documentation, programming, and modelling. Partner schools have analogous fields of study that are focused on metal processing using CNC programs and machines. However, the management systems vary from school to school. We wanted to let students and teachers get acquainted with the individual control systems. We agreed on the structure of the project as early as 2019. We also expected internships for students in foreign schools. Therefore, we prepared units of learning outcomes that characterized the individual work procedures. In order for students to prepare for internships, we have prepared a collection of exercises and tasks, which we gradually published in the moodle environment. All educational materials were created in the English language. In order to simplify teaching for students, we have jointly prepared a four-language dictionary of technical terms.
The educational materials that are available on our market are either out of date or do not exist at all. Cooperation between individual partners led to the expansion of portfolios of educational materials for individual schools.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was
- modernize vocational education in partner schools by connecting school and practice
- exchange experiences and bring interconnection of education systems of partner schools
- to carry out the exchange of information, knowledge, and experience between the representatives of different education systems and thus enable their transfer to their own educational programs
- to enable pedagogical staff and students to participate in mobility and get to know another control system for programming CNC machines
- to create conditions for the general availability of educational activities and better orientation in their offer
- proposals for educational innovation
- to increase the quality of training in the field of technical documentation and CNC machining in mechanical engineering and to give it a European dimension
- create common educational materials available online
- deepen cooperation between partner organizations responsible for vocational education and training of graduates for the labour market so that the training meets the requirements of practice
By opening the e-learning after the end of the project at http://moodle.sos-tremosnice.cz/course/view.php?id=147, other users can use the project outputs.

<< Implementation >>

1.)We created all the planned outputs which we placed on the moodle on - http://moodle.sos-tremosnice.cz/course/view.php?id=147 and https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/projects (https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/education_culture/dissemination/share/page/valor-promoter-project-details?nodeRef=workspace://SpacesStore/54ac6d38-8162-4089-8a9f-410e19a49de0&projectNodeRef=workspace://SpacesStore/0ccb5c93-6fb1-442f-99fd-39869fc385f0&mode=edit).
O1:Units of learning outcomes in En. and stored on a moodle.
O2: SolidWorks drawings. The drawings are in En. and placed on the moodle again.
O3: Progr. in the appropriate programming lang. These programs will also be transferred to moodle. Pupils have access to the software from home.
O4: Our school has created an e-learning environment with all outputs. The environment is English.
O5: A dictionary of technical terminology has been created, which enables the translation of basic terminology into four languages (English, Czech, Croatian, and German). Thanks to the Excel alphabet application allows sorting by individual languages.
2.)Five inter. meet. took place. All of them took place in person, one through MS Teams.
3.)We impl. three educ. activities for four students and one teacher from each country.

<< Results >>

In the first phase of the project, each partner created units of learning outcomes after communicating with each other so that the results did not overlap. Based on them, a collection of drawing documentation in SolidWORKS and programs in three control systems (Siemens - Germany, MACH3 - Croatia, Fanuc, Heidenhain - Czech Republic) was created. SolidWORKs is a drawing program that is used not only by schools but also by companies across Europe.
program We created an English environment in moodle at http://moodle.sos-tremosnice.cz/course/view.php?id=147, where individual outputs were gradually placed according to the project schedule. At the same time, an English-Czech-Croatian-German translation professional terminology dictionary was created for easier orientation of students for online study. Where all project outputs were placed. During the mobilities, the pupils processed technical documentation, programmed and modelled. At the end of the mobilities, they always debugged and created a concrete product.
topics: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-CZ01-KA202-078343.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-CZ01-KA202-078343.title: Innovation and Continuing Education in Destination Management
2020-1-CZ01-KA202-078343.summary:
<< Background >>

Before planning the project, the project partners conducted a baseline survey which showed that in their countries evaluation of destinations and their performance is not a part of destination management, tourism and/or public administration educational programmes. In general, it can also be noted that in practically no partner country is specific destination management education a prerequisite for doing this job, either in a managerial or a line position.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the project were:

- To increase the qualification/professionalisation of destination organisations and to teach them to work with effective tools to increase their knowledge and skills;
- to define at European level new professional qualifications for Destination Officer, Destination Manager and Destination Auditor;
- to create a education and methodological tool for the destination management and audit and thus strengthen the education/training offer in this field
- to promote destination audit expertise as part of destination management qualification in partner countries;
- to promote and broaden interest in destination management in order to contribute to increased interest in sustainable and competitive tourism and regional development and related policies;
- Strengthen the network of DM specialists at EU level, allowing a continuous improvement of their professional knowledge and skills through the exchange of professional experience.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were implemented during the project implementation:

- Implementation and evaluation of an international questionnaire survey focused on the identification and ways of assessing the potential of destinations,
- elaboration of a detailed analysis of the tourism management system in each partner country,
- development of a draft set of indicators for valuing and assessing the performance of destinations,
- elaboration of a description of the processes to assess and evaluate key destination elements,
- development of a European model and methodology for destination management and auditing, incorporating the sub-outputs developed,
- development of a educational programme for destination management and destination audit, together with a methodology for its application,
- creation of an explanatory glossary of specific professional terms related to destination management.

<< Results >>

The following main project outputs were created within the project, for the creation of which materials and outputs from all implemented project activities were used. 

1. European Model and Methodology for Destination Management and Audit 
2. Study material for the Destination Management educational course
3. Study material for the educational course Audit of a tourist destination
4. Methodological manual for the training courses
5. Explanatory glossary of specific professional terms related to destination management (DM)

The educational materials developed within the project are gradually implemented in the educational programmes of the partners (if they are educational institutions). In the first possible year of teaching, the compatibility of the proposed courses and supporting materials within the curricula of the partner educational institutions will be practically verified.

New learning and teaching methods and approaches

2020-1-CZ01-KA202-078435.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-CZ01-KA202-078435.title: Tradice regionů očima žáků za podpory odborníků z praxe
2020-1-CZ01-KA202-078435.summary:
<< Background >>

The aim of the project is to increase professional skills of students via exchange experience, comparation of existing knowledge and practical training through professional participation of the business sector in traditional craft. Traditions and traditional crafts, which are very important for every country, are very much forgotten. Crafts were and are very necessary, and young people should know the original crafts of their country and region, and they should appreciate the history of their country. With this project we targeted young people - secondary school students, but also their teachers, for whom this knowledge is a challenge to pass it on to the next young generation.  At the same time, by organising Festivals of Traditions in each country, the public was also introduced to the traditions of the partner countries. At the same time, the project was a motivational tool to attract young people to craft professions.

<< Objectives >>

The intention of the project is to exchange experience, compare existing knowledge and, above all, increase professional skills in the field of traditional crafts with the professional participation of representatives of the business sphere. During five days learning course, which the students will be exposed to the learning environment of a given partner country, get a grasp of how to make a region-specific product under the guidance of a professional, and afterwards present their skills in the form of an exhibition of products that they have made during the implementation of the project that are typical for individual region.  During the training, learning and teaching sessions, students can try out many interesting activities, make their own product in cooperation with students from the host country, practise and improve their language skills and make new friendships.  At the same time, they have the opportunity to gain confidence in communicating abroad, making presentations on stage during the Festival of Traditions, learning a lot of new things about their own traditions and gaining respect for the history of the country. Through this project we wanted to remind traditional values and the importance of selected crafts.

<< Implementation >>

Two main parts of the project were implemented: part 1 is for students (accompanied by teachers), part 2 is for teachers and other staff of partner organisations. Part 1 included 6 study programmes for students of the participating partner organisations, each with 4 students and 2 teachers. Number of programmes: 6 times, each lasting 5 days. 1 meeting was organised in each partner region. These meetings included the organization of the Festival of Traditions, participation in the exhibition of products in the region. Part 2 included business meetings of the main representatives of the partner organizations 3 meetings were held (in Croatia, Slovakia and the Czech Republic), during which various activities were planned, the agenda of the meetings was prepared and consulted and the project outputs were discussed and prepared. The aim of the meetings was to get acquainted with the functioning of the partner entities, their teaching and working methods, to get new information through discussion with entrepreneurs or ways of cooperation with school and company, linking practice and education, discussion on the form of individual outputs, defining activities and objectives of individual meetings, organizational and financial matters,etc.

<< Results >>

Outputs: brochure about the partners, their region, products for the Festival of Traditions in each country. A calendar of each partner's contributions. Organisational manual - a "how to" guide for organising the Festival of Traditions. Posters - each organization 6 posters - 2 about the organization, 2 about the region, 2 about the products of the school students, always in AJ and in their native language. Products to be presented at the Festival of Traditions. Other output - organisation of project meetings (6 +3 in total), involvement of 120 pupils, 58 teachers, 15 representatives of the KHK, 34 participants in business meetings. The implementation of the project included the so-called virtual cooperation. The first one was an online meeting of project partners in December 2020, then the creation of the project logo - each country prepared a logo proposal, which was virtually evaluated by all partners and the proposal from the school from Slovakia was selected. The next assignment was to design a virtual product to be used by the partner organisation. This was a design of an orientation board in the School of Design Kladno. Schools sent their graphic design, the design of a school from Germany was selected.

2020-1-DE02-KA202-007429.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-DE02-KA202-007429.title: Greening the EntreComp Framework to Reconcile Economic Development and Environmental Security
2020-1-DE02-KA202-007429.summary:
<< Background >>

The green economy is an economic system that prioritizes sustainability and low-carbon practices. It aims to ensure that natural resources are used in a way that does not deplete them, and that the environment is protected while promoting economic growth and social equity1. The importance of the green economy lies in its potential to address the challenges of climate change, resource scarcity, and environmental degradation while promoting sustainable development. Therefore it is important to foster start-ups in this field to make support Green change. Here the Green4Future project addresses the needs of people who wants to become an entrepreneur in this field. There was a need to revise the EntreComp framework which was developed by the Joint Research Centre, the European
Commission’s in-house science service in the past. The need for change was obvious with regard to the issues of Green Thinking and Green Economy. That´s where Green4Future stepped in with redesigning the Entre Comp into a new Green EntreComp framework and with supporting modules and eductional offers for the people who want to become Green Entrepreneurs. This fits excellent into the European Green Deal.

<< Objectives >>

Green-4-Future is a strategic partnership in VET which aims to reconcile economic goals with environmental and climate goals. A core idea is to support the ideas of the European Green Deal. Another cruicial idea of the project is to rethink the EntreComp reference framework developed by the JRC. In particular, it is about greening the EntreComp reference framework. In addition to creating a Green EntreComp Framework, i.e. a green version of the EntreComp Reference Framework, the partners of Green-4-Future aim to focus on business modelling for circular economy enterprises, create an in-service training for VET teachers and design a Green-4-Future MOOC. The nine project partners are from Germany, Cyprus, Croatia, Austria, Ireland, Romania, Greece, Bulgaria and Portugal. Coordinator is the University of Paderborn, Germany. The project Green-4-Future comprises 4 universities, 3 research centres/institutes, 2 vocational training institutions, all active in the field of vocational training and green entrepreneurship. The objective to design the results and a MOOC where all courses /materials are availbale and can be used is a great chance to encourage a broad audience to engage in Green Entrepreneurship.

<< Implementation >>

There were four core actions in Green-4-Future: (a)1. Greening the EntreComp Framework, (b) Business Modelling for Circular Economy Businesses, (c) Creating an In-service Training for VET Tutors and (d) design and development of a  Green-4-Future MOOC.
The partners in Green4Future finished all task with regard to these actions promised in the application. They worked on all three 3 interrelated and interconnected competence areas: ‘Ideas and opportunities’, ‘Resources’ and ‘Into
action’ of the EntreComp framework, its 15 competences along an 8-level progression model an the comprehensive list of 442 learning outcomes. The partners revised all competences with regard to Green issues and created an innovative  Green EntreComp framework. Moreover the partners developed a of business modelling training resources that address recognised circular economy business models: The Co-creation of Products/Services Model, The Sustainable Consumption Model and The Collaborative Recycling/Reuse Model. Regarding the In-service Training the patners developed a bespoke training which addresses both the Green EntreComp framework and the circular economy business models. The partners created a MOOC to off the course and all materials to public.

<< Results >>

a) We offered a Green-4-Futre GreenEntreCopm Framework. All action areas, all competences and all outcome descriptors were revised 
b) We offer a curriculum based on Green4Future-Learning Outome Matrices
c) We creted information text and materials for circular economy business models (Green-4-Future Business modelling): The Co-creation of Products/Services Model, The Sustainable Consumption Model and The Collaborative Recycling/Reuse Model. 
d) We developed an innovative Streaming Concept for School Education in Europeec) We created an innovative In-service Training for VET tutos
e) We deveopled an online course on on green entrepreneurship in VET with a modular strcture and we provided interactive learning activities in H5P.
t) We held an international conference in Germany
g) We delivered all Multiplier Events
h) We created the Green-4-Future MOOC with all learning materials and courses in all partner languages to foster implementation.
i) We created the Green-4-Future Website and an additional Green-4-Future project information website to reach different target groups.
j) We developed additional Green-4-Future didactic materials
k) We did Green-4-Future publications in press, newspapers, journals and scientific texts
l) We used and offered a Green-4-Future social media presence
m) Green-4-Future Dissemination material like brochures, leaflets and flyers which can be distributed to the stakeholders and provided a
n) Green-4-Future Newsletter.

2020-1-DE02-KA202-007478.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-DE02-KA202-007478.title: Empowering Digital Teachers in a changing world
2020-1-DE02-KA202-007478.summary:
<< Background >>

With schools and universities closed across most of the EU countries to contain the spread of coronavirus, an unprecedented number of students were out of class for a longer period. This disruption set off a move toward digital teaching. Against this background, it became clear that most schools were not prepared for 100% for the implementation of digital learning. Several key challenges and obstacles were identified. Hence, many teachers continued to use analogue forms of distance learning and reported only limited self-efficacy in implementing digital learning. Teachers who rated themselves as competent in traditional teaching did not automatically feel this way in digital learning. However, self-efficacy and attitudes are significant predictors of subsequent behaviors. Digital learning (from a distance) can only be implemented if the stakeholders involved feel prepared and supported to do so. The lack of preparation for the use of digital learning was evident in almost all European countries. Numerous teachers were not adequately qualified. In this sense, a need for further qualification of teachers in digital learning in different stages of education was identified, which was addressed in this project.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal of the project was to address the rising issue of lacking knowledge and self-efficacy of teachers regarding the implementation of digital learning. Therefore, we developed an innovative training path (guidelines and online course) that can be used for the qualification of teachers to promote their knowledge, self-efficacy and attitudes towards digital learning and teaching. This should support the use of digital learning on a European level. In view of the relevance of inclusive education processes, a focus was placed on content and issues related to inclusive education.

<< Implementation >>

The project implemented the development of two intellectual outputs as well as one learning and teaching activity. 

•	IO1 EDGE guidelines
•	IO2 EDGE Online course

The development of the outputs was accompanied by a mentored piloting with 73 teachers and practitioners across Europe. The mentors were prepared at a Learning and teaching activity.

<< Results >>

The project led to the achievement of the previously identified specific objectives. In the lifetime of the project, the planned intellectual outputs were developed. After completion of the project, the following exploitable and open-licensed results and products are available:

1.	Guidelines: The EDGE guidelines are a digital document available in six languages. Within the guidelines central questions around the topic of digital learning are answered. Guidelines can be downloaded from the project website: https://www.empowering-teachers.org/edge-guidelines.html
 

2.	Online Course: The EDGE Online Course is an asynchronous online course that takes up and extends the questions of the guidelines. It is available in six translations. In addition to the implementation in the learning platform Canvas, a Moodle version of the course is available. The course is available via the project website: https://www.empowering-teachers.org/online-courses.html

3.	A pilot group of 73 teachers have already enrolled in the course during piloting across Europe, as part of the development of the online course. They have been supported by mentors during the online course and were trained in the use and development of digital learning opportunities.

2020-1-DE02-KA202-007605.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-DE02-KA202-007605.title: Empowering Dance - The Soft Skills Teaching and Learning Approach
2020-1-DE02-KA202-007605.summary:
<< Background >>

Empowering Dance - The Soft Skills Teaching and Learning Approach (ED2) was the necessary sequel to Empowering Dance - Developing Soft Skills (2018-1-DE02-KA202-005055), a previous Erasmus+ strategic partnership. That project aimed to empower dance artists/educators to become aware of their implicit knowledge and skills in the field of soft skills teaching to strengthen their self confidence and to develop strategies to transfer their competences to other fields, expanding their job opportunities. ED1 however revealed two gaps that needed to be bridged to support the professional development of dance artists/educators: 1. The need for dance artists/educators to understand the implicit knowledge in their teaching and wider applications of what their embodied knowledge can do. 2. The need to equip dance artists/educators with the necessary skills, competences and language to define and apply soft skills in their practices when working with non-professionals. To address the needs discovered, ED2 developed an IO/Digital Guidebook, that serves as a free online learning and teaching toolkit in two languages (French and English) supporting dance artists/educators in their professional practice.

<< Objectives >>

The main aim was to fill a gap in training, in both form and content, and to develop an accessible and free of charge IO/Digital Guidebook for the skill enhancement and professional development of dance artists/educators. The focus of the IO/Digital Guidebook was to give the target audience a greater understanding of their particular soft skills, and through that awareness, giving them better access to the job market. An additional aim was that the IO/Digital Guidebook would be an ongoing resource for dance artists/educators to use when applying their soft skills in a variety of contexts and when passing on those skills to others. Also important was to generate an IO/Digital Guidebook that could respond to the diverse needs of dance artists/educators with a dynamic and accessible language, allowing them to customise their learning and to regularly return to it as their practice grew and when they encountered various groups in different settings. Additional aims included increasing the visibility and acceptance of the contemporary dance sector, knowledge exchange amongst participants and Partner organisations, the wide dissemination of the newly made IO/Digital Guidebook and the establishing of new partnerships and networks.

<< Implementation >>

There were monthly online jour fixe meetings to coordinate the project amongst the Partners and IO team. There were also 11 TPMs, one virtual and 10 in presence, to monitor project developments and foster exchange amongst the participants.
Initial activities in relation to the IO development included local focus groups with non-professional dancers, led by the local artists/educators, as the basis for developing IO content and twice a month digital meetings with the IO team to collect data and reflect on discoveries. Following that, IO activities included regular online meetings with the University of Zagreb/Academy of Fine Arts students to develop media for the IO, as well as regular Core-IO team sessions for writing, evaluating and designing IO content. Following the first draft, there was a period of testing with the target audience in each Partner location. From those learnings, the Core-IO team met digitally to revise the IO. After the completion of the IO 6 Multiplier Events took place, one in each Partner city, to share the IO and project. Due to a great interest in the IO, several additional workshops and dissemination activities have taken place since autumn 2022. Several more are planned beyond the end of the project.

<< Results >>

The main output is the IO: "Soft Skills in Dance: A Guidebook to Enhance your Practice", launched online at the end of August 2022 in both English and French. It is an unrestricted, free of charge teaching and learning tool empowering a wide range of professionals in the dance sector. There has also been increased awareness by dance artists/educators of their tacit knowledge of soft skills and understanding of how to transfer them to different contexts. Dance artists/educators using the IO/Digital Guidebook are developing new skills, as have all participants in the ED2 project from all 7 partner institutions. The project has increased the visibility and acceptance of the contemporary dance sector by bringing together contemporary dance with the topic of soft skills, which originally comes from the economic sector. The trans-disciplinary sharing of knowledge has informed and enriched the environment of each partner institution; the exchange of knowledge has expanded outwards to dance artists and allied professionals attending Multiplier Events and additional dissemination events. The project participants have formed strong partnerships and gained a deeper understanding of the dance sector in each partner country.

2020-1-DE02-KA202-007665.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-DE02-KA202-007665.title: The use of VR (Virtual Reality) in vocational training
2020-1-DE02-KA202-007665.summary:
<< Background >>

Digitization will fundamentally change the work of the future. Especially in times of corona and social distancing. Accordingly, training and continuing education must also adapt to this circumstance. New technologies must be learned and applied.
The Gewerbliche und Hauswirtschaftliche Schule Horb is currently setting up a "learning factory". Here, students will learn about new technologies and experience Industry 4.0. In order to be able to perform the demanding tasks in a "smart factory," the "skilled workers of tomorrow" must be trained. We want to move part of the training into a "virtual world" before it then moves into the "real working environment". Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality will therefore play an immensely important role in our working lives. For the intended ERASMUS+ project, different work processes were selected as examples. The goal is to create a digital world in which these activities can be practiced before going to the real machine.

<< Objectives >>

All partners are able to transfer real learning and training situations into the virtual world. In addition, concepts for integrating this Virtual Reality into education have been developed. Through the project, transnational strategic partnerships between educational institutions have been created and established. Students and teachers of different European cultural backgrounds experience exchange in terms of everyday life and professional context. Students from all partners are involved in the development of the training opportunities and drive them forward independently.

<< Implementation >>

Documentation and distribution of the project process and results (e.g., via a website) was developed. The project management software used, Microsoft Office 365, was introduced and used across all partners. Cross-country meetings (both face-to-face and online) have been held. Various conferences have been held and documented. All participants participate in the design of learning, teaching and training materials. Best practices have been experienced in various field trips and interpersonal relationships have been strengthened through extracurricular events.

<< Results >>

In each partner institution, special learning situations have been elicited and selected and documented for the project. In the various transnational meetings, software and hardware were considered in a differentiated manner and selected according to formulated criteria. On the basis of these, real training situations could be transferred into a virtual space and the necessary work steps have been documented. Instructions for the implementation of the necessary steps were prepared, so that every organization (also non-participating project partners) is able to use and implement these results. By interweaving the experiences and know-how of the individual partners, all participants experienced an increase in the field of digitalization and VR. Cultural and country-specific experiences and traditions were exchanged and made tangible.  Cross-national partnerships were initiated and established. Friendships were formed. Various plans for further projects are underway. All results (in text, image and video format) are publicly accessible on a specially set up homepage (www.erasmusvr.eu).

2020-1-EL01-KA202-078806.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-EL01-KA202-078806.title: New Skills Development in Precision Agriculture
2020-1-EL01-KA202-078806.summary:
<< Background >>

The Europe 2020 Strategy has been the EU's agenda for growth and jobs over the decade. In 2011, the term Industry 4.0 was coined as part of the growth through digital transformation strategy of EU, conducting roadmaps to promote the digitalization of manufacturing. It concerns a transformation of the production infrastructures such as “connected” farms, new production equipment and “connected” equipment. Precision Agriculture is the core methodology engaged with the definition of digitalization of agriculture. The most essential challenge in the adoption of Precision Agriculture Methodology is the ability of farmers to invest and upgrade their practices of production. The workforce in agriculture is ageing, with over 56%over 55 in Europe. The digital skills of the workforce are thus limited and require additional investment in training to adopt technologies. Taking into consideration the above mentioned, the current project will contribute to the development of an E-learning Platform as a digital tool to meet agricultural stakeholder’s needs on their education and training, with regard to the incorporation of precision agriculture applications in their farms.

<< Objectives >>

The project’s objectives focuses on: 
1.The stimulation of farmers and technical staff working in rural production to cope with the most up-to-date techniques and methodologies concerning the digital farming and more particularly the precision agriculture.  
2.The development of the curriculum (knowledge and skills) of the trainers and the consultants of the agricultural sector on precision agriculture applications 
3.The introduction of innovative methodologies and applications to farmers according to the modern technological progress and the reform of institutional guidelines in European policies and international suggestions 
4.The implementation of a digital E-learning Platform on Precision Agriculture which will be a useful tool for the VET trainers on educating and teaching, incorporating the project outcomes in their sessions. The e-Learning platform and the accompanied handbook will be elaborated to work as means of exploiting by the VET trainers providing them a new teaching methodology during their training process

<< Implementation >>

The VET trainers of every partner were trained on how they will teach farmers and other agricultural stakeholders using the Precision Agriculture Handbook for Beginners (IO1) and the Precision Agriculture VET Curriculum (IO2). The content of the Beginners’ Handbook and the Curriculum was the educational material on precision agriculture which partners developed. Then, they incorporated it in the E-learning platform (IO3) and the VET trainers exploited it to train farmers and relevant stakeholders.

<< Results >>

VET trainers of every partner obtained the knowledge and the skills along with relevant competences to train the members of the targets groups (1.Farmers, 2.Technical staff in rural production, 3.Agricultural consultants/Agriculturalists, 4.VET Trainers specialized in rural development) effectively on the importance of precision agriculture application in succeeding a more qualified workforce for a more sustainable agriculture.

2020-1-ES01-KA202-082219.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-ES01-KA202-082219.title: Breaking Barriers with the insertion of young people with intellectual disabilities in the working world of the 21st century.
2020-1-ES01-KA202-082219.summary:
<< Background >>

We are a Secondary School in Zaragoza which, in addition to the usual teaching (ESO and Baccalaureate), has three Initial Qualification Programmes (Vocational Training Adapted for students with intellectual disabilities), which has been inserting young people into the world of work for 28 years. Although our placement rate in companies is acceptable for the national percentage, we wanted to improve the number of contracts, for this reason we started an exchange of experiences with other countries where we work with the same objectives, in order to implement new ideas that could increase the quality and quantity of our actions and achieve a higher number of contracts of disabled students in companies.
Likewise, our programme needed an update, especially in new technologies, for this reason we have tackled the creation of a new website, the production of quality videos and a banner for the entrance of the centre. In this way, together with the presence in social networks and in the media, we have reached the homes of many more families than in other school years, as well as the personnel management departments of many more companies.

<< Objectives >>

1.- To compare work methodologies between different countries, in order to achieve the comprehensive training of students with special educational needs in the educational stage of Vocational Training.    
2.- To establish comparisons between the different educational systems of the countries involved in the project, in order to see the educational path of these students in the system. 
3.- To exchange good practices of the educational centres that work on the insertion of disabled students in the labour market.
4.- To compare the difficulties encountered in finding jobs in companies in the different countries involved in the project.
5.- To write a document with the conclusions drawn from the meetings, where the proposals to improve the methodology of integral work with disabled pupils between 16/21 years old, especially those referring to the search for jobs and labour insertion, will be collected.  
6.- To implement in each of the vocational training programmes of the different countries the innovative and positive practices that improve the results of integration into the world of work. 
7.- To design a comparative document on the application of the improvement measures in each of the countries involved in the project, which can be reviewed after 3 years of application in the different countries, and to establish a comparison of the number of recruitments. 
8.- Publicise the work carried out among all the project partners through the social networks of the different centres, so that other European entities dedicated to the labour insertion of young people with disabilities can benefit from the good practices.

<< Implementation >>

PREPARATION : Exchange of emails where we decide the date of the face-to-face training days, sharing of the structure of the meetings, elaboration of a summary document, consensual decision making among all the members to modify the project activities (especially the modification of the dates of the face-to-face meetings and sharing of the agendas of the mobilities). Decisions on the previous activities of knowledge of the partners. These pre-acquaintance activities were carried out during the first half of the project, as the covid situation forced us to delay the mobilities. This prior acquaintance between schools made it easier to meet in person afterwards. 
(Code Week, European Vocational Skills Week, making Halloween decorations, sharing different traditions, making Christmas decorations and dishes, drawing competition for the project logo, making drawings for the banner, etc...).
With these activities and the work contribution of each partner, we got to know the type of pupils involved in the project and the teachers of each school who were going to collaborate with us.
   TRAINING ACTIVITIES AND EXCHANGE OF GOOD PRACTICES : 	
5, 6 and 7 October 21. Mobility to Croatia.	
14, 15 and 16 December 21st Exchange in Spain. 
29, 30 and 31 March 22nd Mobility to Italy.
24, 25 and 26 May 22nd. Mobility to Romania.
DOCUMENTATION CARRIED OUT : 
Summary document of each of the countries where the activities to be carried out in the own country are indicated, observed during the mobilities in another of the partner countries, with the aim of improving the labour recruitments. 
Documents accrediting the realisation and participation in the workshops (certificates of attendance, complete mobility programme, minutes of the daily meetings, evaluation of the workshops, videos with photos of the workshops, etc...).
Guide to make companies aware of the characteristics of the person they are going to hire and with recommendations on how to deal with them, in order to facilitate their introduction and well-being in the company.
Documents describing previous knowledge activities, in order to share ways of working or elaboration processes between countries (cooking recipes, elaboration processes of machining or gardening workshop products, etc...).
Some of these documents are attached in annexes, and all of them can be consulted on the results page of our project. 
DISSEMINATION : Essential in all project countries. Both in the media and on social networks. 
IMPLEMENTATION: The collection of new ideas in each of the project countries, and the implementation in all of them.

<< Results >>

Our entry into Europe has meant that our publications on social networks have increased a lot, and the media (local, regional and national) have taken an interest in the project due to the important social impact it has.
The improvement of the centre's website, and the public presence of the project, has meant that many more families have come to the open days to learn about the training cycles, and that local companies are interested in our students at the end of their training, increasing the number of contracts compared to other school years.
In each of the countries, a document has been drawn up indicating which ways of working are interesting to carry out in the other countries, improving innovation in the centres. 
On the other hand, all the teachers participating in the project have learned first-hand what it means to enter Europe, and how interesting it is to learn about other educational systems and other cultures, as well as encouraging the teachers themselves to get out of their comfort zone and improve their skills as teachers.
In all of them, the publicity achieved on social networks has made companies take a more positive view and increased collaborations.

2020-1-ES01-KA202-082752.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-ES01-KA202-082752.title: EU HACKATHON
2020-1-ES01-KA202-082752.summary:
<< Background >>

During the drafting phase of the project, a SWOT analysis was conducted in the participating institutions, through which the following common needs were identified:
The VET institutions needs were:
-Develop key competences in ESTEAME areas and transversal skills using HACHATHONS as a tool to engage VET students in the institute activities.
-Find new resources to motivate students to continue their learning in the ESTEAME area, promoting inclusion and attracting women to these traditionally male-dominated fields, thus promoting gender equality in vocational training institutes.
-Support teachers with effective, structured, and curriculum-relevant teaching solutions regarding equality, science, technology, engineering, arts, mathematics, and ecology (ESTEAME).
-Better understanding and knowledge in innovative solutions for the development of educational content that motivates students and promotes personal development, social inclusion, active citizenship, and employment.
-Internationalize their activities and share best practices on ESTEAME to develop sustainable partnerships.

<< Objectives >>

The GENERAL OBJECTIVE of the EU HACKATHON project has been to allow VET students to approach ESTEAME subjects in a different way and to encourage them to develop cross-cutting skills and key competencies such as digital skills, innovation, critical thinking, problem-solving, etc.

The SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES have been:
-Engage VET students in lifelong learning by developing their key competencies and cross-cutting skills such as digital skills, entrepreneurship, critical thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, flexibility, and learning to learn using HACKATHONS.
-Encourage both male and female VET students equally to continue studying in fields related to ESTEAME.
-Support VET teachers with innovative, effective, structured, and curriculum-relevant teaching solutions for ESTEAME.
-Design, build, and program real-world engineering processes using ESTEAME concepts.
-Participate in HACKATHONS to enhance cross-cutting skills and key competencies using ESTEAME concepts for internationalization.
-Establish a solid framework to internationalize the activities of the participating institutions.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, the following activities have been carried out:
COORDINATION of project activities.
Development of the TEACHER'S GUIDE focused on the use of HACKATHONS as an innovative tool to increase student motivation towards ESTEAME subjects, improve their basic and cross-cutting skills, artistic design, skills for ecological transition, and promote gender equality.
LEARNING COMMUNITY to enhance collaboration between VET institutions and educational authorities with the aim of using HACKATHONS as a tool to foster student inclusion.
Organization of HACKATHONS with the goal of creating engaging challenges that allow students to develop cross-cutting competencies through playful learning experiences applying ESTEAME concepts:
For VET teachers
For national VET students
EU HACKATHON at a transnational level
Project WEBSITE
DISSEMINATION of results.
EVALUATION of results.
SUSTAINABILITY strategy by creating in each participating institution a club for national HACKATHONS and a schedule to conduct online HACKATHONS after the project's funding period.

<< Results >>

The results of the project can be divided into two types: tangible and intangible, as follows:
TANGIBLE Results
-TEACHER'S GUIDE focused on the use of HACKATHONS as an innovative tool to increase student motivation towards the ESTEAME subjects, enhance their basic and cross-cutting skills, artistic design, skills for ecological transition, and promote gender equality.
-Project WEBSITE that contains all materials and activities developed during the project and is located at the following URL.

INTANGIBLE Results
-LEARNING COMMUNITY that involves over 250 teachers, 500 students, 30 VET institutions, 15 companies, 2 universities, 7 public authorities, and 20 civil society organizations..
National and international competitions that contribute to the development of key and cross-cutting competencies in the ESTEAME area using HACKATHONS as a tool to motivate students at risk of exclusion.
-HACKATHON CLUBS that will allow continued work at a transnational level online using HACKATHONS as a methodology, and at a national level in the clubs that have been established alongside the institutions that are part of the learning community.

2020-1-ES01-KA202-083200.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-ES01-KA202-083200.title: Monetising the social value of agri-food cooperatives in rural Europe
2020-1-ES01-KA202-083200.summary:
<< Background >>

AgriCoopValue arises in response to the key needs and challenges of the European cooperative agri-food sector. Contemporary society increasingly demands that organizations not only be economically profitable but also ethical, socially responsible, and environmentally respectful. Despite their strategic importance, many agri-food businesses focus solely on measuring their economic success, overlooking their social and environmental contributions.

The project originates from the lack of specific and effective methodologies to measure the social, environmental, and economic impact in the agri-food sector. AgriCoopValue's primary goal is to develop the SPOLY methodology to monetize the Comprehensive Social Value generated by these organizations at the macroeconomic level, across various subsectors of the agri-food industry, and at the microeconomic level, within each cooperative.

AgriCooValue also addresses the need to raise awareness about the importance of social accounting and enhance the competitiveness of cooperatives in a globalized market.

<< Objectives >>

AgriCoopValue sought to create a conducive framework for the implementation of a unified social accounting system for agri-food cooperatives to monetize their social value and determine their multiplier capacity within EU rural environments.

Specific Objectives:

-Train technicians and trainers from organizations representing agri-food cooperatives in using the SPOLY methodology to monetize the social value of an organization.
-Advance the improvement of the methodology through specific applications in different agri-food subsectors at the European level.
-Train agri-food cooperatives to monetize the social value generated by their own businesses.
-Raise awareness about the importance of social accounting compared to traditional accounting, especially in the social economy sector.
-Consolidate the international acceptance and recognition of the SPOLY methodology and promote the transfer of results internationally.
-Improve the image of European agri-food cooperatives, highlighting their attractiveness and contributing to the enhancement of their competitiveness in a globalized market.

<< Implementation >>

The project was divided into 6 Work Packages (WP) that played a fundamental role in project implementation:

WP1: PROJECT COORDINATION AND MANAGEMENT
WP2: COMMUNICATION AND EXPLOITATION OF PROJECT RESULTS
WP3: TRANSFER OF SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE TO THE COOPERATIVE AGRI-FOOD SECTOR
-Development of mechanisms for academic-private collaboration
-Learning campaign for sector representatives
-Staff training (C1)

WP4: DEVELOPMENT OF NEW APPLICATIONS OF THE CALCULATION METHODOLOGY BY AGRI-FOOD SUBSECTORS OF THE MACROECONOMY
-Creation of transnational working groups
-Development of practical processes, comparative analysis, identification of variables, and standard methodologies for monetizing Social Value by subsectors

WP5: TRAINING FOR MONETIZATION OF SOCIAL VALUE GENERATED AT THE MICROECONOMIC LEVEL
-Creation of a training platform
-Design of a training program for cooperatives
-Implementation of pilot training activities (C2)
-Evaluation of results and corrective measures

WP6: CREATION OF STRATEGIC ALLIANCES FOR THE DISSEMINATION OF THE UNIFIED SOCIAL ACCOUNTING SYSTEM
-Elaboration of strategy and action plans
-Implementation of action plans

<< Results >>

P.I.1 Training Itinerary for Monetizing Social Value in the Agri-Food Sector: provides a valuable guide for training in this area.
P.I.2 Standard Models for Calculating the Social Value of Cooperatives in Each Agri-Food Subsector: facilitates precise and uniform measurement of social value in different areas of the sector.
P.I.3 Online Platform: a central tool for training and disseminating project results. Specific training program, adapted to the specificities of the 5 agri-food subsectors, to train in the monetization of social value.

These results represent substantial achievements in monetizing social value in the European cooperative agri-food sector, providing tools, guides, and a strategic framework to measure and communicate the social, environmental, and economic impact of cooperatives. This strengthens their competitiveness and recognition in a globalized market and promotes greater awareness of the importance of social and corporate social responsibility in the business sphere.

2020-1-FR01-KA202-079846.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-FR01-KA202-079846.title: Cultural animation as a key against elderly social isolation
2020-1-FR01-KA202-079846.summary:
<< Background >>

Following the priorities of the Erasmus+ programme, our project was oriented towards inclusion and diversity. All countries face ageing with social, medical and economic consequences. Studies have reached to the conclusion that "social connections are critical in our daily lives" (https://www.elsevier.com) and the isolation caused by the pandemic has complicated the situation in nursing homes. Every teacher involved shared the same citizenship values but as teachers mainly working in health and social care schools, we were probably aware of the dangerous issues of  a split society. Our students come from rural lower-class families with no easy access to culture or interest in learning foreign languages. EU countries have pledged to reduce the proportion of early school dropouts (10,2% in 2019, https://education.ec.europa.eu/), our project aimed at fighting social obstacles by attractive peer-learning activities providing self-achievement,  developing attractiveness of VET (healthcare workers shortages) and increase future working skills. The lack of language competences remains one "of the main barriers to the participation in europe education, training and youth opportunities" (https://ec.europa.eu). Sharing strategies on an international scale was also a great value for teachers.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed at implementing inclusive workshops for elderly people and trained the pupils expelled from culture or the idea of belonging to the European society. We relied on studies showing loneliness in our societies ("Social participation and social isolation" Eurostat). In 2018, Make.org Foundation and E-Twinning have developed a first programme about twinning between classes from different rural areas and nursing houses (France). Our objectives are inspired by this initiative: to encourage the citizenship of teens to fight against ageism / to promote local approaches  / to facilitate the dissemination of good practices. Although comparisons between countries remain difficult, it is nonetheless certain that the isolation of the elderly is a common problem and that it is essential to share our practices. Artistic education and the discovery of a different culture should serve the objectives of cohesion and thus avoid dropping out of the most vulnerable ones. The partners have thus made the choice to place the cultural dimension as a powerful and playful educational tool in schools and with other organisations. The mobilities also aimed to practice English for students in a different context and to open students' minds by giving them the opportunity of living together and cooperate in the same tolerance project. The "good practices guide" is the result of cooperation, reflection on professional practices, an increase in skills. Its aim was to make students question the tools that work or need to be improved (quality approach) and can be reused by European actors. We also wanted to sustain the cooperation between retirement homes and establishments (training periods).

<< Implementation >>

The activities put in place were many and varied and had to be adapted due to the COVID epidemic but met the objectives.
1) the partnership has proposed activities apart from mobility:- development of common professional techniques (creation of animation sheets) and creation of a skills sheet (ECVET) based on the level to be reached (A-levels). - virtual activity with a retirement home and several videoconferences in English between partners: creation of a cultural quiz. - documentary research around the care of the elderly. - the practice of English in reall was first carried out through correspondence then with the creation of videos for the Europe Day and on social networks before the mobilities.- creation of needs/satisfaction questionnaires for houses retirement (project procedures).
2) Mobilities respected the plan established between the partners : - discovery of the system of care for the elderly in the country. Research or presentation by students. When possible, several visits to retirement homes operating differently were implemented. - Theoretical input inside and outside the establishments in order to create artistic animations. Workshops for the creation of socio-cultural activities between peers around the culture of the country and with the elderly.- immersion and implementation of activities by the students.- evaluation of activities and drafting of the good practice guide. In order to promote the programme, the partners took part in the Erasmus Days.

<< Results >>

Several outputs were realized, in particular intermediate ones, with the writing of magazines and creation of videos in English at the end of each mobility, Powerpoints, quizzes, articles promoting the Erasmus+ program and artistic creations (with the elderly) and exhibitions (dissemination events and during Erasmus Days). However, the  results were mainly the creation of common technical animation sheets that can be used by others and the writing of the "Guide of Good Practices" by means of team working. This guide therefore brings together all the set up workshops, the technical sheets and the project approach. The students also led meetings with partners (national and transnational), built timetables, communicated with partners in English (writing reports). A considerable amount of educational material has been created by students and teachers (Forum/Interactive guide for Paris and London/board games/digital quizzes/professional technical sheets/artistic sheets/promotional videos) and can be reused (sharing of practices). Learning outcomes and activities were automatically assessed (tests/questionnaires) and analyzed (improvement of future activities).
