2020-1-FR01-KA202-079858.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-FR01-KA202-079858.title: Entrepreneurship Training for Innovators
2020-1-FR01-KA202-079858.summary:
<< Background >>

Innovative enterprises play an important role in stimulating economies around the world. However, only a small percentage of new ventures are innovative. Therefore, the objective of the 8 PER CENT project is to support the growth of innovative entrepreneurs in Europe. The project involves 8 partners who are located in France, Portugal, Cyprus, Spain, Croatia, Germany and Netherlands and who have experience in the fields of entrepreneurship, continuing education and education.

The 8% consortium proposed to meet the need of innovative entrepreneurs to train throughout their professional career. This was done through the development of digital training material, which addresses the ten key skills to be developed by innovative entrepreneurs, hosted in an educational platform that is accessible, attractive and adapted to the target group.

Furthermore, the project contributes to the professional development of teachers, trainers and mentors in VET. A continuing education program allows them to maximize the potential of new, dynamic and media-rich educational resources.

<< Objectives >>

The 8 PER CENT consortium has worked to support the growth of innovative entrepreneurs in Europe by developing training materials around the main skills of innovative entrepreneurs and presenting them in an innovative, accessible, attractive and appropriate education ecosystem.

It was a question of proposing a pedagogical approach based on the game and relying on an immersive process using mobile devices (mobile phone or tablet) and social networks. 40 interactive infographics serve as the basis for educational resources (presented as images on social media sites and other specialized sites with direct access by scanning the QR code)
The provision of a continuing education program for VET professionals enables them to develop digital media skills, build confidence to work in e-learning environments and learn more about the skills of innovative entrepreneurs.

<< Implementation >>

- Development of a compendium of 40 interactive infographics on the 10 key skills of innovative entrepreneurs: creative thinking, problem solving, leadership and team management, innovation management, agile management, planning strategy, risk management, business model development, venture capital research, rapid experimentation;
- Development of a continuing education program for VET professionals
- Development of a MOOC platform that guarantees free and continuous access to the educational resources developed.
- Implementation of a transnational training activity, which had the objective of familiarizing VET professionals from partner prganisations with the methods for creating interactive teaching aids.
- Conduction of pilot projects in each country of the consortium in order to better adapt the project results to the target group
- Organization of dissemination activities to obtain multiplier effects outside the participating organizations at local/regional/national or international level.

<< Results >>

As part of the 8 PER CENT project, the partners have developed 3 intellectual products:
IO1 - Compendium of interactive infographics providing innovation and entrepreneurship education aimed at already experienced entrepreneurs
IO2 - Continuing education for VET professionals
IO3 - MOOC 8% offering access to the Compendium of interactive infographics as well as access to innovation entrepreneurship training and the training program
keep on going

With the aim of democratizing access to continuing education, all intellectual productions are available on the project website: https://8percent.eu/

2020-1-FR01-KA202-079967.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-FR01-KA202-079967.title: Support early to make easier the social inclusion
2020-1-FR01-KA202-079967.summary:
<< Background >>

The partnership is working in the support of people with visual impairment, and especially very young children and teenagers. The most important challenge for people with visual impairment is to get the autonomy in their daily lives (empowerment in the daily activities, mobility in movements, body skills, etc.), and especially to be able to get included in the society, at school or in employment. However, most of teenagers, and especially those who have never seen, have big difficulties to live their lives "normally" because of a lack of autonomy, due very often to the environnement who is doing in place of the blind child. The project needs to organise exchange of practices to get knowledge and to feed and to improve professional practices to develop the mobility and the autonomy. The project needs also to provide a guide of recommandations which can advise professionals and parents for the improvement of autonomy and inclusion of children with visual impairment.

<< Objectives >>

The partnership wants to implement the project EARLY to achieve a better knowledge of practices at EU level concerning the early support of young children with visual impairment. The objective is to gather practices, experiences and innovative methodologies, to develop a guide of recommendations for parents, and also the environnement of the children with visual impairment (creches, schools, etc.)

<< Implementation >>

The partnership implemented exchange of practices, with 2 main mobilities (1 in Angers, 1 in Vienna) with presentation of clinical cases, presentations of practices and innovative methodologies, and organisation of workshops to structure the knowledge gathered by each partner. The partnership has also developed a guide of recommendations as a tool for the dissemination of good practices and advices for parents and professionals in the environnement of the child with visual impairment (creches, schools, etc.)

<< Results >>

The project EARLY produced a guide of recommendations in the following languages : French, Italian, German, Croatian, Bulgarian, the languages of the different partners, and a version in English. The guide of recommendations has been structured and defined in accordance with the partners' expectations. The different linguistic versions of the guide of recommendations are available for free at : www.enviter.eu/projects/early

hr.name: Centar za odgoj i obrazovanje Vinko Bek

2020-1-FR01-KA202-080100.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-FR01-KA202-080100.title: Getting Advanced Methods for the Inclusion of everybody in the  New Generation
2020-1-FR01-KA202-080100.summary:
<< Background >>

Our young people often experience failure when they are directed towards the vocational track in the second year of secondary school. Most of them come from low-income social classes or suffer from "DYS" disorders, or even handicaps, and are confronted with their academic failure, which has for years led to a lack of self-confidence.
When they arrive in our schools, our teaching teams do their best  to inculcate life skills, among other things,  in order to contribute to their self-fulfillment and restore their self-esteem.
We thought that approaching this work in a European context was a way of broadening the horizons of our pupils, as well as enriching their learning and allowing our teachers to benefit from the exchange of practices in order to develop their own skills.
Finally, the involvement of the teaching staff in the success of the  young people they are in charge of contributes to the reputation of our schools and makes them more attractive.

<< Objectives >>

.The search for professional and personal fulfillment is the basis of this partnership. The project-based teaching method enables the development of the transversal skills promoted by employers: autonomy, taking initiatives, teamwork, etc. Exchanges in English with European peers can, of course, only be a means of improving their language skills. They also strengthen their sense of belonging to the wide European community and thus help them to appropriate this wide citizenship.
The employability of our young people is also at the heart of the concerns of the project participants. This partnership is a great lift to approach a number of professional skills mobilized in the participation in a project. Digital skills are also highlighted because of the different means  used for the exchanges , among them :  videoconferencing. Developing these skills allows our pupils to grow, to project themselves into the future and to contribute to the ultimate goal of inclusion for all, whether social or professional.

<< Implementation >>

The heart of our partnership is based on monthly video exchanges between the pupils of the schools involved. In order to be able to discover their cultural heritage (1st year) and gastronomy (2nd year) by means of clues, each centre had to do some work beforehand: research, visits and meetings to list and discover their own heritage, writing riddles in English.
All of these actions are aimed at creating a common game.
At the same time, communicating about our partnership is another important part of our project. This promotion was carried out both inside and outside our schools, using various media to reach different targets: posters, press articles, social networks, school websites, meetings with the authorities, the House of Europe during our transnational meetings or dedicated events (Erasmus Days, Europe Day)...
In order to guarantee the success of the project, it is imperative to ensure a regular follow-up within the framework of the activities and the budget, transnational meetings of the pedagogical teams involved complemented by quarterly and even monthly video conferences when the need arises.  Finally, this type of partnership creates links that are strengthened by the difficulties encountered. It is important to maintain these links  over time. The joint production of the final game is a symbol of this. The new involvement of a Bulgarian partner in our project application (LIFT: on the reserve list) is another example of the strong links that can be forged in these partnerships.

<< Results >>

We have created one game per country and one online game accessible from a link. The online game, modeled on "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?", includes questions on the countries and regions of the partnership as well as the two versions of cultural and gastronomic heritage.
All the partners opted for the online game, and one also proposed to concentrate all this work in a book.
The coordinating high school also opted for the production of the board game, which led to work in groups to find the type of game that could group together questions on themes related to cultural or gastronomic heritage. Several quotations were requested for the maps of the regions with playing cards containing the various clues and different levels. Once the quotations were studied, the students and their teachers chose the one that was most feasible. The students of the coordinating high school went to a primary school and a retirement home to present their prototype and test its feasibility: a successful test!
Another concrete result of this partnership is the acquisition of professional and personal skills (self-confidence, autonomy...) but also the development of interpersonal skills and qualities of life in a group: tolerance, inclusion, acceptance of difference, open-mindedness
topics: Cooperation between educational institutions and business

2020-1-FR01-KA202-080248.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-FR01-KA202-080248.title: UnitEd for Global Goals
2020-1-FR01-KA202-080248.summary:
<< Background >>

Tandem plus a postulé pour ce projet en raison de l'importance cruciale de l'Agenda 2030 établi par l'UE. Reconnaissant l'importance de traduire ces objectifs en actions tangibles au sein de nos territoires, le réseau a vu un besoin d'y contribuer concrètement. Le but premier était de promouvoir ces objectifs à travers le réseau Tandem Plus en Europe pour les utilisateurs cibles du réseau: groupes défavorisés avec lesquels les EFP sont souvent en contact, notamment les NEET, les chômeurs, les personnes peu qualifiées, les personnes ayant des difficultés d'apprentissage, les migrants. Ces groupes sont confrontés à des difficultés d'inclusion socio-économique principalement dues à des déficiences en matière de formation, qui sont encore aggravées par divers facteurs sociaux. Par conséquent, ces catégories sont souvent inaccessibles par le biais de campagnes de sensibilisation sociale conventionnelles.
Ce projet t était a permis aux organismes de formation d'impliquer activement ces groupes dans le développement durable local grâce à des méthodologies innovantes partagées au sein du partenariat et du réseau entier et appliquées dans les contextes et services locaux respectifs.

<< Objectives >>

Le projet visait à promouvoir l'inclusion sociale et les ODD en adaptant les programmes de formation aux besoins des groupes vulnérables. 
Parmi ses réalisations :
-La diffusion des objectifs de l'Agenda 2030 en les intégrant dans les activités de formation dispensées par les établissements d'EFP. Cela a permis de sensibiliser les groupes cibles à ces objectifs et de les leur faire comprendre;
-L'intégration des objectifs de développement durable (ODD) dans la formation à l'EFP;
-Renforcement des capacités des établissements d'enseignement et de formation professionnels pour concevoir et mettre en œuvre des programmes éducatifs sur mesure;
-Échange de bonnes pratiques pour faciliter l'apprentissage et l'adaptation d'approches efficaces dans différentes régions;
-Réunions de formation et de débat pour développer et consolider les méthodes et les approches visant à fournir une formation professionnelle et une orientation aux groupes vulnérables. Ces activités ont favorisé la collaboration et le partage des connaissances entre les parties prenantes;
-Équiper les groupes vulnérables avec des connaissance, des compétences et des contacts améliorant leur inclusion socio-économique.

<< Implementation >>

- 5 sessions conjointes de formation/apprentissage pour promouvoir l'intégration des ODD de la durée de 5 jours chacun (tot. 96 participants)
- 5 événements locaux de diffusion (environ 200 participants)
- 6  réunions transnationales (tot.88 participants) de deux jours en présence axées sur l'évaluation et la consolidation des connaissances et du savoir-faire générés lors des sessions d'apprentissage
- 1 formation en ligne (19 participants) sur l'L'ODD 11 - "Villes et communautés durables" relative à la réduction des risques de catastrophe après le tremblement de terre qui a frappé la Croatie (fév 2021) pour partager bonnes pratiques et discuter le rôle des ONG dans la réduction des risques ou dans la récupération après les catastrophes. La formation était enlargi à d'autres pays tels que l’Italie, l'Autriche et Chypre
- 1 événement final en présence qui a retracé le projet et ses résultats
- 2 publications électroniques: 1 recueil général consolidant les résultats du projet et l'expérience partagée (avec matériel en anglais, français, croate, grec, portugais, italien) + 1 annexe avec activités pratiques et ateliers
- Communication de résultats du projet sur le site web de Tandem et résultats ERASMUS + et EPALE comme matériel OER.

<< Results >>

-Le projet a permi d'integrer les principes du développement durable dans les pratiques locales, de promouvoir l'apprentissage par l'expérience et d'encourager la collaboration entre les établissements d'enseignement et de formation professionnels et les ONG locales;
-Le projet a favorisé une collaboration plus étroite entre les organisations participantes et les parties prenantes du secteur de l'enseignement et de la formation professionnels. Cela inclut le renforcement du réseau, le partage des meilleures pratiques et des initiatives conjointes pour promouvoir le développement durable et atteindre les ODD;
-Diffusion et reproduction des bonnes pratiques: le projet a identifié des approches et des pratiques réussies liées aux ODD, qui ont été documentées dans le compendium + annexe (www.tandem-plus.eu/medias/) créé et diffusé parmi les parties prenantes concernées. Ce partage de connaissances et d'expériences encourage la reproduction et l'adaptation de ces pratiques dans d'autres contextes locaux, étendant ainsi l'impact du projet au-delà de ses participants immédiats,
-Capacité accrue des participants et des utilisateurs du compendium à utiliser différentes approches pour atteindre les objectifs sélectionnés de l'Agenda 2030.

2020-1-FR01-KA202-080504.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-FR01-KA202-080504.title: VET changes rural territories toward sustainability
2020-1-FR01-KA202-080504.summary:
<< Background >>

The MFRs and their partners share the observation that everywhere in Europe the needs of the actors of the territory are similar. The aim is to maintain and develop a vocational training offer in rural areas in a dynamic relationship with the development and skills needs of the economy and, more broadly, of the territories. The question of the place of young people was raised from the outset by the partners because they are both the key to development for the future but also a voice that is often little heard.
This is particularly the case for education issues. This issue of vocational training and youth is often not present in regional development plans, even though human capital is created from the work of those involved in education and vocational training in particular. In this project, dialogue between stakeholders and the use of collective intelligence were intended to facilitate the emergence of collective responses and give vocational training the opportunity to express its potential, especially in rural areas.

<< Objectives >>

The partners wanted to give a clearer and more active place to vocational training in rural areas in Europe. One of the shared intentions was to focus on the place of young people in the dialogue around the place of vocational training in rural areas, which was a priority for the partners. By relying on collective intelligence and on the monitoring of changes among the project's stakeholders, the idea was to show the transformative side of this type of practice exchange program and to make it a production that could be used in the field.
Action research and action training were intended to facilitate the reinvestment of each person's learning in their organization and territory. The resulting capitalization was intended to give an additional dimension to the program by going beyond the case study to better understand the importance of the change underway: awareness, capacity building, action and finally social and political commitment.

<< Implementation >>

The activities of VET 4 Change were of 4 different natures mainly: 
- Project follow-up meetings 
- Action-based training sessions 
- Online seminars and workshops 
- Field experiments between sessions 

a major monitoring and evaluation of the change was coordinated by one of the partners (Belgium). The final production that can be used to facilitate a workshop on territorial dialogue around education illustrates the results of this evaluation.

This article summarizes the partners' journey with a 2-minute film to illustrate it:
https://europe.mfr.fr/la-fin-de-v4c-vers-quels-horizons/

<< Results >>

Given the complexity of the context in which this project took place, between health restrictions, the war in Ukraine and all their consequences on the internal organization of the project partners, the concrete results are numerous. Practically, a facilitation tool on rural vocational training issues has been produced and can be found on the VET 4 Change results dissemination page. The project's activities have strengthened stakeholder collectives and larger spaces for dialogue around vocational training in various rural territories in Europe. The vision of rural territories for 2040 is well illustrated by this project, stakeholders emerge stronger (increased power to act), more connected, more resilient and ultimately more prosperous.

On a less tangible but very concrete level, a questioning of the global approach to education has taken its place, close to that of the European institutions and the expression of young people. This gives rise to new projects from a strong collective. Dissemination in the territories and between sectors is developing thanks to the great work of communication and video productions.
topics: Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas
Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas

2020-1-HR01-KA202-077757.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077757.title: Turn off the lights, turn on the stars!
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077757.summary:
<< Background >>

Main objective is raising awareness in teachers and students about the need to protect and preserve the environment, to protect the dark sky areas from light pollution and encourage sustainable environment protection. Specific aims of the project are: encouraging initiative and entrepreneurship in students aiming at environment protection; empowering students to 0take action in order to protect the environment against light pollution by designing and producing solutions and tools for light pollution; empowering students with disabilities to actively participate in project activities; encouraging sustainability of the project activities aiming at protection against light pollution; protecting and preserving natural heritage – natural dark sky; promoting science, astronomy, ecology and entrepreneurship; deepen and broaden students’ knowledge and competencies in science; promoting inclusion and empowering students with disabilities; establishing strong ties with other European schools and sharing best practices with students from other countries; improving language and communication skills; greater intercultural awareness and improving soft social skills as the ability to listen to each other, express opinions, practice tolerance.

<< Objectives >>

The main priority that this project is trying to solve is linked with environmental goals. Through this project we try to create a solution against light pollution. Project is focusing on the increasing of skills and competences of the VET secondary schools’ teachers to perform a complete mentoring process in determination and support of the potential of VET secondary schools’ students and development of their practical skills. In this project, we try to create synergy between environmental education and practical work among students. Students of VET schools are the key players of this project because they use all gathered knowledge to create solution that will prevent light pollution.
The students learn about environmentally-friendly and energy-efficient forms of lighting in the area though field visits and direct experience of beneficial effects that changed lighting has on the  environment. This knowledge and awareness would motivate the students to create potential solutions that could be used for protection against light pollution in the future.

<< Implementation >>

New methods in preventing light pollution in everyday classes. Activities we implement are: Free Writing, Ice Breakers, Think–Pair–Share, Case Studies and Problem-Based Learning, Interactive Demonstrations, Research, Experimentation, Analysis and Statistical Data Processing.

<< Results >>

The results of the project are:
- sharing new knowledge and skills among teachers and students
- cooperation with international partners, establishing strong ties for future cooperation
- brochure on project activities and best practices including multilanguage glossary that can be used by
other schools
- produced solutions against light pollution by students from VET schools
- encouraged surrounding settlements to adapt their public and industrial lighting to minimize light
pollution
- well informed and environmentally conscious teachers and students who can cooperate with local
authorities on management of dark sky parks and environmental issues in general
- gained knowledge and skills among teachers and students about light pollution and the ways to fight it
- glossary of terms in four languages
- adapted lighting around school
-contacted and threatening surrounding settlements to adapt their public and industrial lighting to
minimize light pollution
- creation of a student-made barn door tracker
- a useful tool in astrophotography
- established cooperation and understanding with local authorities
- confident and active student citizens in the field of health and environmental protection issues
- developed intellectual outputs

2020-1-HR01-KA202-077758.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077758.title: Hacking the Code for Women in STEAM
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077758.summary:
<< Background >>

Callidus – Institute for Adult Education is a strong believer in Corporate social responsibility and therefore aims to contribute to society by taking part in project where the Institute’s knowledge and experience can be of use in addressing key social issues such as gender inequality. 
Science, technology, and innovation (STI) affect all aspects of our everyday life. Science and technology are evolving in a rapid pace which, among other things, represents an opportunity for personal growth and better positioning in the labour market on which STI has a direct affect. Thus, STEAM is proving to be a very profitable and stable career choice. Regarding gender equality, this puts women on a crossroad – they have the option to seize this opportunity and increase the number of women in STEAM or continue to fall behind on the labour market. Studies have shown that there are only 28% of women in STEAM even though they make 50% of the labour market and with the further rapid development of STI women are in danger of falling even further behind. It has been recognised that dramatic intervention is needed to balance the scale of women and men in STEAM, and the Steamy Wonders project aims to contribute to that cause.

<< Objectives >>

With the rapid development of STI, a career in STEAM represents the future. Women need to be aware that a career in STEAM is not only a real possible career choice for them, but that it also represents a career choice that will give them stability and better positioning on the labour market. This project aims to empower women of all ages to consider, plan, and achieve a career in STEAM by piloting a multi-faceted educational intervention targeted to women with the goal of balancing the scale between women and man in STEAM. By implementing the Steamy Wonders project the following objectives were achieved: 
•	Promoting scientific, evidence-based reasoning among women with an emphasis on using this approach in career planning, 

•	Providing role model case studies to build the confidence of women for participating in the STEAM field and the rapidly developing scientific and technological world in general, 

•	Developing a custom-made toolkit for women that addresses key competences related to STEAM subjects that include problem-solving, innovation, analytical and critical thinking, and spatial awareness,

•	Providing guidelines for VET tutors for motivating, encouraging and empowering women to stray and build a career in the STEAM sector.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities have been implemented during the project lifecycle: 

1.	Learning, Teaching, and Training Activities
C1 In-service training for VET tutors and career guidance/management experts
All partners sent 2 appropriate and affiliated VET tutors or career guidance/management experts to this event. As the training was e delivered in English all partners ensured that those selected to attend had excellent English language skills. The result of this in-service transnational training event was the establishment of a transnational group of VET tutors and career guidance/management experts who supported each other and further implement the knowledge gained in their partner countries. The in-service training comprised of 21 hours of face-to-face workshop instruction and 14 hours of online self-directed learning. Because of the COVID-19 pandemic and partners' inability to travel, the In-service training was held online and was broken into 3 workshops each one with a duration of 7 hours. Each workshop was broken down into a training session and a skills demonstration. 
This 3-day training addressed the following areas:
•	developing interactive and engaging materials using software programmes like PowToon, VideoScribe, StoryBoardThat, Google Forms, Canva, KAHOOT, LearningApps etc.
•	building challenge-based learning resources such as digital breakouts or WebQuests
•	integrating media-rich content to develop interactive infographics

Documentation proving the maintenance of the described activity can be found in the Supporting Documentation sent via WeTransfer with this Report.

2.	Implementation of the In-service Training for VET tutors in each partner country
After providing In-service training for adult educators, the next step was to provide In-service training in all partner countries. 49 VET tutors completed the in-service training, 7 in each partner country. In some partner countries that number was even bigger (e.g., Austria). During this activity, every partner organisation has organised a local event where embedded learning has been promoted to relevant stakeholders in their countries. 

All the partners submitted evidence of the maintenance of the mentioned activities, and you can find them in the Supporting Documentation that was sent via WeTransfer with this Report.

3.	Multiplier events (workshops)
A minimum of 140 women attended the STEAMY WONDERS Careers workshops. 
During multiplier events in all partner countries, the main attendees were women, but in order to empower women to achieve a career in the STEAM area and with the goal of balancing the scale between women and men in STEAM, it was very important to introduce the unbalance issue also to men which are often not aware of the deficit of women in the STEAM area because sometimes general thinking is that this is not caused by a purely educational reason and also prejudices and they should be introduced to those problems in order to understand how to prevent or encourage women in pursuing a career in the STEAM sector. According to that, partners on the Steamy Wonders project also invited men to attend the Multiplier events as they believe that is the best way to find solutions and raise awareness of the needs for more women in the STEAM area and to enable women to achieve their potential in the STEAM. It’s crucial to raise awareness of both women and men regarding this aim of the project as that is the only way to make long-term improvements. 

All the partners submitted evidence of the maintenance of the mentioned activities, and you can find them in the Supporting Documentation that was sent via WeTransfer with this Report.

4.	Final conference of the project where all the project results were shown to the appropriate target groups
73 senior managers in VET, career guidance and human resource management, and women interested in a career in STEAM attended the Final Conference which was held in Croatia on the 16th of September 2022. At the Final conference, all the pedagogical outputs of the project were presented. Also, Callidus organized a panel discussion about the relevant topics that this project covers. The participants of the panel discussion were a VET tutor in one of the most influential technical schools in the Republic of Croatia, a young woman working in the IT sector, a woman influencer working in the science field, and the main coordinator of the project who led the discussion itself. 
In addition to the participants who took part in the face-to-face form in conference, 25 participants followed the conference via Instagram Live video which was live streaming the panel discussion. 

Documentation proving the maintenance of the described activity can be found in the Supporting Documentation sent via WeTransfer with this Report.

<< Results >>

In the period from 01.09.2020. until 30.09.2022. the following documents, project results and concrete outputs were produced:

2020-1-HR01-KA202-077771.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077771.title: Challenges and practices of teaching economic disciplines in era of digitalization
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077771.summary:
<< Background >>

Digital technologies are an indispensable part of the learning process. Current research and practice show that the education system of future economists needs to be more attentive to the development of teachers' digital competencies and, consequently, the students, especially in the secondary education system. Project partners have recognised the problem of insufficient use of digital technologies in the VET system, influencing passive learning and resulting in a lack of thinking outside the box. In order to modernise the education and training of future economists, it is essential to promote the use of digital technologies for learning in the field of vocational education.

Given the identified needs regarding learning digitalisation in the secondary education system, the project was targeted primarily at teachers from the secondary education system in cooperation with teachers in the field of higher education. Strengthening teachers' competencies for different forms of training has promoted the comprehensiveness of teaching our future economists.

<< Objectives >>

The overall aim of the project was to exchange challenges and practices of teaching economic disciplines in the era of digitalization. Given the set goals, it was expected that partnerships between higher and secondary education institutions would contribute to the development of teaching skills and stimulate creative thinking and further support the entrepreneurial spirit of VET students. 

The main objectives of the project were:
(1) improvement of teaching skills and teaching practices in different economic disciplines with special emphasis on the era of digitization by sharing existing good practices and analyzing the use of new digital teaching and learning technologies in vocational education of economists
(2) encouraging digitalization in participating organizations
(3) increasing students’ satisfaction with acquired knowledge and skills in developing their own entrepreneurial ideas and better inclusion in the labour market.

The involvement of foreign strategic partners from Germany, Poland and Serbia, alongside Croatia, has greatly contributed primarily to the activities of teaching and training teaching staff through the exchange of good practices in the application of new innovative learning tools in teaching economics.

<< Implementation >>

Although the dates and performance type of the planned activities were subject to change due to uncertainty regarding the COVID-19, all activities that were listed in the project application were successfully performed. Main activities included:
a. 2 Transnational Project Meetings: 
- online Kick-off meeting, November 2020, 29 participants, University of Zagreb, Faculty of Economics and Business, Croatia 
- hybrid Final meeting, March 2023, 21 participants, University of Belgrade, Faculty of Economics, Serbia
b. 4 Learning, Teaching and Training Activities: 
- C1 – Accounting, October 2021, 14 participants + hosts, University of Applied Sciences, Germany
- C2 – Trade and international business, February 2022, 12 participants + hosts, Cracow University of Economics, Poland
- C4 – Finance, May 2022, 16 participants + hosts, University of Belgrade, Faculty of Economics, Serbia  
- C5 – Train the Trainers Workshop, November 2022, 26 participants + hosts, University of Zagreb, Faculty of Economics and Business, Croatia.
In addition, some of the other activities included: the preparation of the questionnaire for the primary research, analyzing results, preparing, presenting and publishing scientific papers, and preparing the handbook.

<< Results >>

In line with the objectives of the project, the most important result is the significant improvement of the digital competencies and skills of teachers necessary for teaching economic disciplines in the era of digital transformation. Other important outputs are:
a. conducted empirical research – a survey was conducted in all four partner countries, resulting in 2,897 responses from university and high school students and professors; the research results provided an insight into the level of digital literacy of respondents, their attitudes towards the use of digital and mobile technology in teaching and their opinions regarding the future of e-learning,
b. published and presented scientific papers – a total of 11 scientific papers that were based on the above-mentioned primary research were published in a journal or conference proceedings, which contributed to disseminating our research results to a wider audience,
c. prepared Handbook – we prepared and disseminated a Handbook (110 pages) that contains: a) a descriptive analysis of research results, and b) 12 case studies from different areas of business economics that were created with the help of various digital tools and can be freely used in classes and other forms of education.

2020-1-HR01-KA202-077791.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077791.title: Innovative Training Curricula for Drone Controllers
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077791.summary:
<< Background >>

In line with the major postal operator's efforts, Croatian Post tested smart solutions and alternative ways of delivery with electric vehicles and drones. Drones have already proved their usefulness in crisis situations. Therefore, some industries already use drones in everyday business. Croatian Post successfully completed its first drone delivery from city of Zadar to Preko on island of Ugljan.Trial flight was a part of a pilot project with the Croatian SME company that developed commercial and industrial services using drones. Many postal operators are implementing and testing drone deliveries in their businesses. With advancement of autonomous unmanned flying technology, the use of drones is being considered today even for the commercial deliveries. Drone ecosystem is developing rapidly and is becoming ready to use.

<< Objectives >>

Croatian post realized the benefits of drones in their everyday business, especially possibilities of using drones in delivery of letters and parcels between post offices. But the issue was, aside amateur use for personal purposes, there were no training programs in the market for postal employees to cultivate their drone skills to have broader options in the labour market, pursuing the position of the drone controller. FlyVETUp project addressed exactly this need and opportunity, aiming at the realization of a training materials for using drones on parcel delivery available on open-source e-learning platforms. 
Our project aimed at developing strong partnerships between postal operators, training institutions, ICT companies and VET providers. Consortium worked together, contributing with their specific expertise to provide training materials to postal operator’s staff to help people to gain practical skills. Newly gained skills will provide postal employees to pursue new career and have broader perspective of personal development and new job possibilities.

<< Implementation >>

During the 24 intensive months through a concrete methodology, following activities are implemented: 
b) Training Courses for “UAV controller” preparation,
c) Training programme for Drone Controllers development,
d) Implementation of the curricula to relevant personnel and certification.
At the end of their theoretical and practical training period for UAVs flight, and after they have been passed the exam trainees are certified.

<< Results >>

During the project's life span innovative training program for Drone controller is developed enriched with a specially developed IT technology/on-line training.
In brief the main results are following:
• UTM’s operator and remote pilot’s Occupational profile is developed,
• Syllabus, curricula and training material for Drone controller is designed and developed,
• Innovative training method is available on-line learning platform (MOOC) in three languages (English, Croatian, Greek)

2020-1-HR01-KA202-077801.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077801.title: SCALing up in the creative industries for SMEs and self-employed
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077801.summary:
<< Background >>

Creative and Cultural Industries are considered one of the most promising fields of economic activity in the EU but also a promising sector for significant job creation. Enter wanted to exploit the results of the project “Building creative incubator” and the skills of the new network created locally at the European level, so it started to look for EU partners who already had experience in the CCI field. What was noticed during the creation of the project was that the CCI sector lacked some business skills to make their business more competent and sustainable and expand their business. The partnership was created by 6 partners coming from 5 different countries (Croatia, Italy, Spain, Slovenia and Greece) who wanted to provide the creative and cultural sector with innovative and specific training tools which will support people working in CCI to improve their competencies and skills required to reinforce the competitive advantage of CCI sector. Partners created a transnational training model divided into 5 macro-area, one for each expertise which has been identified as essential to unlock the potential of CCI: Creative and artistic; Technical and engineering; Market and business; Managerial and financial; Process and networking.

<< Objectives >>

By implementing the project partnership wanted to develop specific training tools which will support people working in CCI to improve their competencies and skills required to reinforce the competitive advantage of CC sectors by maintaining a virtuous cycle of creative talent, artistic expression, entrepreneurship and investment. The specific objectives were to develop one transnational training model divided into 5 macro-area, one for each expertise which has been identified as essential to unlock the potential of CCI: Creative and artistic; Technical and engineering; Market and business; Managerial and financial; Process and networking then test the models both on trainers/VET providers and cultural and creative businesses.

<< Implementation >>

Through this project partners set well-defined activities which were implemented by six partners coming from 5 different countries. Partners established 5 working groups with the aim to elaborate detailed training models on 5 identified thematic areas, they developed one international training for internal staff and trainers to transfer the knowledge among partners on training materials related to 5 thematic areas. They developed a handbook to support SMEs and self-employed in CCI to manage their business; developed an online learning platform targeted to entrepreneurs in CCI; implement dissemination activities and five multiplier events to actively involve the participation of stakeholders. Activities were targeted to the businesses operating in the Cultural and Creative sector who benefit from training activities and intellectual outputs, and also at the staff from participating organisations who improved their knowledge and expertise in assisting the companies working in the CCI sector to transform their business models from “project-by-project basis” to “maintainable creative entrepreneurship”.

<< Results >>

There were 2 outputs of the project. An INNOVATIVE TOOLKIT AND HANDBOOK (IO1) consist of five local assessments corresponding to the territorial areas chosen by each project partner, five sets of "Tips and Tools", corresponding to the selected five areas of expertise, five local action plans, for each of the territories represented by the project partners. ONLINE MULTI-LINGUAL TRAINING PLATFORM (IO2) provides marketing and management tools and resources selected specifically for the Cultural and Creative Industries (CCI) field. 
Partners developed a transnational training model for people working in the CCI sector which is divided into 5 macro thematic areas. Increased cooperation among Cultural and Creative Industries and other sectors’ companies to introduce innovative elements in CCIs. Training materials were created and will serve as a basis for further use, development and replication in other contexts. Partners also organized local and International events to properly disseminate the outputs and to concretely involve stakeholders. The local events (Multiplier events) were also the occasion to promote the training models and to stimulate other CCI companies to use them to improve their competencies.

2020-1-HR01-KA202-077805.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077805.title: Training for Agrifood Competences on Blockchain
2020-1-HR01-KA202-077805.summary:
<< Background >>

TRACK project is created in order to the Erasmus Plus 2020 priorities:
Environmental and local objectives, sustainability of the agri-food process, innovativeness.  
Blockchain technologies offer a unique opportunity to further improve efficiency, transparency and traceability in the process of exchanging value and information in the agriculture sector. By leveraging digital records, cryptography and the disintermediation of transaction processing and data storage, blockchain technology can both improve agriculture supply chain and rural development intervention in a number of ways.
TRACK provides knowledge and expertise on how to apply this technology in agri-food sector and opportunity to improve farmers knowledge on a technology that, if correctly adopted, could produce many benefits in agri-food sector. The project created a tool (learning platform) that will enable the workers to learn about this technology and to concretely adopt it while performing their tasks. The learning platform represent a kind of teaching service for those operators that need to find practical examples and material to improve the knowledge and plan the application of blockchain technology within their working environment.

<< Objectives >>

The objective of the project is to improve the knowledge and skills on blockchain technology of people working in agri-food sector by developing and testing a new training module and by providing the agri-food operators with an interactive learning platform to be used for training purposes. These tools are not addressed to ICT experts, who are already skilled about the technology but the training target is agri-food entrepreneurs, managers and technicians, that need to get familiar with the potential benefits raising from distributed ledger technologies. The training is addressed to nontechnical, agri-food business-oriented audiences. It examined blockchains for the enterprise and a set of relevant use cases to fill the gap of knowledge about a new technology that will become more and more strategic in the next years.

<< Implementation >>

In order to achieve the project objectives and deliver the planned results the project has been structured in working components, each coordinated by different project partner and consist of several project activities:
WC – PROJECT COORDINATION – The activities of the project coordination:
WC1.1 – Periodical project meetings
WC1.1 – Interim technical reporting and internal financial reporting
WC1.1 – Monitoring of project activities and indicators.
WC – CO-DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OF TRAINING MODULES – activities represented the starting point of the project and its aim is to produce the first intellectual output. This WC was structured in 2 activities: 
WC2.1 – Toolkit co-designed process
WC2.2 – Development of training modules on blockchain technology
WC – DEVELOPMENT OF TRAINING PLATFORM – production of the second intellectual output; activities:
WC4.1 – Development of functionalities and technical realization
WC4.2 – Research, collection of material and uploading
WC4.3 – Testing phase 
WC4.4 – Fine-tuning 
WC - COMMUNICATION AND DISSEMINATION 
The activities in this WC are:
WC5.1 – Elaboration and implementation of communication strategy
WC5.2 - Multiplier events

<< Results >>

Project generate some very concrete results such as:
-	Improvement of specific skills and competences of farmers and agri-food operators required to adopt the Blochian technologies in their work
-	Improvement of transnational connectivity among organizations working on development of skills in agri-food sector
-	Realization of 2 innovative outputs (Training Modules on Blockchain Technology and Learning platform) that will support the project partners and target groups to further improve their knowledge by organizing additional trainings and providing support to farmers and operators on application of Blockchain technology in agri-food sector.

2020-1-HU01-KA202-078738.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-HU01-KA202-078738.title: Rural Advisory Monitoring and Evaluation System linked to Precision Learning
2020-1-HU01-KA202-078738.summary:
<< Background >>

Small and family farmers provide the bulk of food production in Europe (and the world) and their activities are critical to achieving sustainable rural transformation. However, rural SMEs cannot survive without careful and targeted support and relevant advice, where raising the quality of Rural Advisory Services (RAS) to effectively address modern challenges plays a crucial role. For successful farming practices, the adoption of innovative technologies, and the fulfilment of market-related and administrative challenges, advisory networks have an indispensable role to play. National RAS state accreditation systems' relevance to assess the performance, competence and quality of service provided in the field, at the client’s level, is rather limited and general. Service providers have no means to present evidence to testify the quality and competence of the advisory staff, in lack of their own certified system of monitoring and quality control. Therefore market-based but commercially neutral rural advisory centres need to set up and operate their own system of monitoring, feedback, and evaluation.

<< Objectives >>

The broader objective of our project was to strengthen rural advisory services to improve their standards through a monitoring and evaluation system that can simultaneously support the development of a targeted, personalized, work-based, vocational training programme and the establishment of a quality certification scheme. The main method applied was based on the data generated by the systematic record-keeping related to service provision, to help identify the areas in which the advisors need professional further training. After gathering and analyzing the data, subsequent areas of improvement that need to be focused were highlighted. These areas were grouped into several main categories / knowledge areas and each participant learned only the content that best suited his/her need. This approach we call precision education that allowed us to collect data from the participants, and after analyzing, enabled the participants to learn a customized curriculum in a more effective, focused and time-saving way. The project aimed to model, test and summarize the experiences of this method.

<< Implementation >>

As part of the project management activities, we implemented the followings (brief summary):
• Quality Assurance Plan
• Online Assessment Tool for Project QA
• Process monitoring/control/evaluation according to the QA rules
• Dissemination plan with templates
• Dissemination activities (the list of actions is uploaded to the TPF FTP).
• Progress and evaluation reports, Interim and Final report
• Project website, in English, with general project information in each of the project languages. 
• Organizing the 5 TPMs, 2 of them by a series of online sessions during the COVID period, while 3 of them held physically.
The products of the project were implemented by six intellectual outputs, which are presented in detail in the relevant sections of this final report. They were: 
O1 RAS Dictionary of Competences
O2 Methodologies of RAMONES-PL 
O3 Monitoring and Learning Platform 
O4 Precision Learning Programme 
O5 Certification
O6 RAMONES Guidebook
The Multiplier Events were carried out in two “waves”, firstly in the target (piloting) countries (HU, MK, SK) before the experimental monitoring and learning programme, while secondly, in each project country, presenting the results and providing opportunities for their exploitation.

<< Results >>

During the carrying out of the project activities, the partnership developed six outputs, which were built upon each other. The first product was a Competence Dictionary that identified the main business processes, competences, categories, indicators, and data sources specific to advisory activity. The Methodologies of RAMONES-PL described the process flow and related components of service tracking, monitoring, evaluation, and precision learning. In the third step, we set up the information system of data management. In the next stage, the Learning Programme was implemented in a work-based setting, with the participation of 24 rural advisors and over 700 service clients (as opposed to the planned nearly 300). Parallel we implemented the activities related to certification, which contained the development of a proprietary market-oriented quality assurance scheme according to the project concept, and the preparation for an international standard certification. All results necessary and suitable for effective dissemination in the project countries and EU-wide, were summarized and published in the RAMONES Guidebook.

2020-1-IT01-KA202-008445.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-IT01-KA202-008445.title: Expert on Local Public Transport. Resources development for a transectoral and transnational innovative expertise.
2020-1-IT01-KA202-008445.summary:
<< Background >>

As testified by this Year of Skills, the competence gap is a growing problem in all sectors, and for several reasons it is particularly felt in the local public transport system, called upon to respond to fast changing social, economic and environmental challenges. The project idea was born in 2018 within the collaboration established between Conerobus (LPT company of the Ancona province) and the Polythecnic University of Marche Region, already in place in the framework of the Mobility Academy https://www.mobilityacademy.it/. At that time and during the development of the project idea it was clear the need to strengthen the collaboration between research and the local public transport sector in order to develop integrated solutions supporting the digitalisation and sustainability transition required in the sector and above all to respond to growing needs within a central service provision as the public transport in terms of personalisation, inclusion, efficiency and responsiveness to fast changing conditions. The pandemic has only increased this awareness. The competence gap was recognised as a fundamental aspect to respond in the long term to the above challenges.

<< Objectives >>

The main objectives of the project were: 1. collecting data to define and develop a job profile supporting innovation in the LPT sector and the relative learning outcomes required at European level responding to different context-specific scenarios; 2. provide the LPT sector with training resources able to respond to innovation needs in the LPT in the participating partners and contexts; 3. develop a tool at initial stage with inputs from a transnational perspective to monitor skills mismatch in the LPT sector and update the profile and training resources according to changing conditions; 4. develop a transnational business-research network able to exchange and compare data and practices. These should contribute in supporting up-skillink and re-skilling to contrast skills mismatch and ultimately unemployment in the LPT sector, support innovation and adaptation of a fundamental public service, both to increase sustainability, efficiency and inclusion.

<< Implementation >>

With reference to the planned IOs all activities have been carried out. The project started with the definition of the ELPT framework and vocational profile (Tasks 1.1, 1.2, 1.3). The objective was to identify the skills needed for new professional profile as well as design learning objectives and the training programme. The methodology employed included: analysis of relevant documentation, legislation, national and European occupation bases, previous tenders, job vacancies, initial skills set, interviews (in two rounds).
Then in parallel the Open Educational Resources (Task 1.5), Platform (IO2) and Assessment System (IO3) have been designed and developed. Content development for the OERs have been carried out by all partners under the Task leader, the other two activities have seen the main work from the Task leader but all partners have actively provided guidelines (coordinator), inputs, discussion, observations and several revisions. A Work Based Experience have been ideated according to the OERs and 3 Pilots put in place in Italy, Spain and Croatia. Ultimately the Tool for monitoring of mismatch was developed.

<< Results >>

The project produced the following outputs:
As part of IO1 Expert in Local Public Transport (LPT Expert): design of the vocational profile and Open Educational Resource and IO2 ELP: design and development of the e-learning and resource platform:
- ELPT Skills and competence report with best practices on national and EU level and ELPT Framework
- ELPT VET Profile and Training Methodology (with modules, Units, Topics and Learning Objectives)
- ELPT OERs and platform https://elptransport-elearning.eu/
- Work Based Experience protocol
- Pilot Evaluation Report
IO3. Tools for Assessment, Validation and Recognition of skills 
IO4. Tool aimed at monitoring the skills mismatch and update the profile.
Other results of the project, beyond those linked to its implementation and monitoring, have been the activation of collaborations among LPT companies or local development agencies and academic institutions on the topic of public transport innovation in the three Pilot countries, with exchanges of experiences, debating on local problems and possible solutions, collection of data as well as a practical and valuable experience like the work based experience of Pilots participants.

2020-1-MK01-KA202-077855.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-MK01-KA202-077855.title: Choose a cheese
2020-1-MK01-KA202-077855.summary:
<< Background >>

SOZSU “Gjorce Petrov” in line with the school’s strategic documents wants to introduce a new curriculum and educational programmes, i.e. new profiles and occupations in order to meet needs of local businesses and increase attractiveness of vocational education. In the previous two years school was focused on development of curricula and educational programmes for cheese making as well as relevant training for cheese making.

<< Objectives >>

SOZSU “Gjorce Petrov” implementing this Project wanted to foster small scale cheese production by providing training and product development activities.
Achieving the above aim, it was needed to reach following specific objectives:
1. To Improve animal health and the quality and volume of on-farm forage;
2. To improve hygiene and milk quality;
3. To promote innovation and entrepreneurship in cheese making;
4. To demonstrate how cheese can be defined as tourism product and how to get started cheese tourism

<< Implementation >>

The project aim and objectives were achieved through the implementation of 5 work packages (WP) within 3 phases. The project took place in 3 European states and each WP had an appointed organisation that was responsible for the successful implementation of their designated WP. Activities and expected results were defined for every project phase.
Phase 1 – Preparation phase 
Phase 2- Implementation of concrete training activities to enhance cheese making and strengthening technical skills of the participants in the training and preparation of applicable training material. 
Phase 3 Consolidation of activities, dissemination and creation of awareness for cheese making.

<< Results >>

The results of the project are the following intellectual outputs (IOs):
- Animal Health and Nutrition (O1), 
- Milk Production and Cheese Processing (O2), 
- How to Serve and Cook with Cheese (O3), 
- How to Start up Business with Cheese Tourism (O4).

IOs are available on the web site of SOZSU “Gjorce Petrov”. Apart from that, information and links to the project and its outputs are published on relevant sites for educators as well as in Erasmus+ dissemination platform. This will ensure a long-term transferability of output and sustainability of the project. 

The project has increased the skills and competences of direct participants in the project who were trained in Macedonia, Croatia and Greece in animal health and nutrition, milk production and cheese making thus contributing to improve the situation of local communities.

By means of the output developed the students were educated in such a way that their skills and competences meet the labour market needs. Through the exchange, students has improved their skills on intercultural learning, social relations and even practice foreign language.

In addition, Project has contributed to improvement of the motivation and confidence of students to become successful entrepreneurs.

2020-1-MT01-KA202-074221.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-MT01-KA202-074221.title: Innovative Development Of New Training for Knowledge of Navigating Options of Wealthmanagement
2020-1-MT01-KA202-074221.summary:
<< Background >>

According to PISA 2018 data, 22% of students across OECD countries and economies perform below the baseline level of proficiency in financial literacy, which is necessary to participate in society. Despite the fact that 56% of 15-year-olds in participating OECD countries and economies have bank accounts and 19% have prepaid debit cards, only 31% possess the skills to manage a bank account. This lack of basic financial literacy skills has been observed to be particularly prevalent among lower-income groups, women, and youth. Surveys in Europe indicate that young adults have among the lowest levels of financial literacy, leading to difficulty in choosing the right financial products and a lack of interest in sound financial planning. This often results in overspending, debt-traps, and erosion of wealth.
We strongly believe in the need to improve financial literacy and financial responsibility across all age groups, genders, and levels of education. The project aims to teach financial literacy and management/responsibility starting at a young age, in order to better prepare individuals for their future and to ensure that they are not ill-prepared for the time when they receive their pensions.

<< Objectives >>

The project "I DONT KNOW" implemented several activities in order to achieve its objectives of improving financial literacy among young people in Europe. These activities include:
Internet research to gather information and identify best practices in financial education
Data analysis to understand the specific needs of young EU citizens in financial literacy
Implementation of solutions and tools found through internet research and data analysis
Development and implementation of apps for financial education
Analysis of the results obtained from the implementation of the apps and improvement of the apps based on the results.
The specific activities that were implemented include:
An online digital database of good practices, tools, and resources for financial education
A modular training curriculum for financial education
A digital training platform for learning via APPs for financial education
The "I DONT KNOW" pedagogical handbook
Project management and implementation, including quality control measures to ensure timely implementation and adherence to the allocated budget
Testing of the products with teachers and students
Information activities to disseminate the project deliverables to a wider audience

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation phase of the project, a variety of activities were carried out, including: internet research, data analysis, implementation of solutions identified through research, creation and implementation of apps, and analysis of the results obtained to improve the apps.
The project also included several specific activities such as the development of an online digital database of good practices, tools and resources for financial education, creation of a modular training curriculum, development of a digital training platform for learning via APPs for financial education, and creation of the "I DONT KNOW" pedagogical handbook. 
The Malta Stock Exchange Institute (MSEI) communicated project deliverables during courses organized by the institute and financial literacy events held at the Malta Stock Exchange during the project's duration. A final dissemination and launch conference was also organized at the Exchange, which was attended by over 65 individuals including educators, students, and stakeholders from the financial services sector. The Malta Financial Services Authority (MFSA) also participated in the event and commended the project deliverables in a letter of congratulations.

<< Results >>

The project, I DONT KNOW, aimed to support vocational education teachers and trainers in providing quality financial education to young people through the implementation of an online digital database of good practices, tools, and resources for financial education, a modular training curriculum, a digital training platform for learning via APPs, and a pedagogical handbook.
As a result, the project produced several concrete outputs including an online digital database, a modular training curriculum, a digital training platform, and a pedagogical handbook. Additionally, the project team also engaged in several marketing and dissemination efforts, as well as exploitation and valorization initiatives.
The project also achieved other results such as the improvement of project management, the implementation of quality assurance and project evaluation measures, and the dissemination of project results through online and face-to-face meetings, national and international seminars, and media appearances.
All the above mentioned outputs are available free to use on the website project https://project-idontknow.com/

2020-1-NO01-KA202-076537.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-NO01-KA202-076537.title: Clean, green future through STEM-sport clubs
2020-1-NO01-KA202-076537.summary:
<< Background >>

“Clean, green future through STEM sports clubs” was a European partnership of seven VET schools and educational organizations who developed “STEM clubs” (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) as a new learning and teaching method for STEM based motivation, orientation, preparation and dropout prevention in VET. It was intended as an ongoing leisure activity, as entertaining as sport for young students aged from 10 up to 18 years. All valuable results were available for other European regions who face comparable challenges.

A few of the organizations have collaborated in previous ERASMUS+ project before (2017-1-NO01-KA202-034179), also managed by the applicant Odda Upper Secondary School (Norway). The former collaboration has shown an urgent need for continuing activities for learners in STEM fields to keep motivation for such VET education on a high level and to avoid VET dropouts by better early orientation. The partners have deduced that an ongoing focus on STEM content which was effective for the motivation of young growing people for VET studies in STEM fields. Special STEM competencies were and still are important and relevant for the economy of nearly all European regions. Companies regularly seek specialists on local, regional, national and international level.

<< Objectives >>

The project aimed to make a significant contribution to the development of regional STEM clubs based on the structures of sports clubs. It will show the opportunities for innovative and modern content and attract volunteer educators who are implementing practical training activities and who improve their own competences of methodology, tools, resources and innovative approaches.

STEMclub project OBJECTIVES were:
- To strengthen structures for volunteers in extracurricular STEM activities across the regular schools
- To increase development of STEM clubs in Europe
- To attract young participants in STEM clubs and give them a sustainable basis for their future
- To provide easily accessible tools for volunteers / teachers / trainers = club leaders to exchange good practice, become accessible and get inspired by others
- To increase the quality of education, training and youth work in the regions to which the participating organisations/schools belong to and beyond.

<< Implementation >>

Main activities were implemented:
- 6 Transnational partner meetings within 3-year project duration
- 1 Staff training were organized: for STEM clubs volunteers/leaders (Germany)
- 2 learners’ mobility were organized: focus on empowerment - “We STEAM” (Italy); sustainability “Sustainable Future and Renewable Energy” (Croatia)
- 7 Multiplier events were organized with more than 160 participants (161 local and 7 international and more than 50 partner organization staff/students)
- 2 IOs developed that are accessible on project website: www.stemclubs.eu
- More than 30 STEM clubs / initiatives were established in partner countries

Various dissemination activities (online/offline) that were focused on raising awareness of project outcomes and overall call for collaboration in similar areas and also invitation to visit STEM clubs, join STEMclubs platform, learn from e-learning material.

<< Results >>

IO1 – “STEM club platform”: best practice presented on STEM clubs and volunteers/ teachers/ trainers = club leaders reached out authors of such clubs, exchanged experience, generated collaborative initiatives (even transnational) and showcased their own achievements.
More than 30 STEM clubs / initiatives established.
Research results presented current situation on STEM clubs in partner countries / regions.

O2 – “e-Learning tutorial material for educators in STEM” which ensured quality training of volunteers who wanted to establish STEM clubs and to increase young people long lasting motivation.
Examples of activities for STEM clubs developed.
Research results were presenting best practice of partner organizations.

During the project we made a great visibility and invited many interested parties to connect. Partners who had very little or no experience were super empowered.

Within STEMclub project we have created a strong international network of trainers in STEM - ambassadors of knowledge. They were and are key to empower young people in STEM locally, regionally, nationally and internationally. It became a catalyst for further steps - collaborations with new partners, new initiatives, follow up project proposals development.

Equal access and transition to labour market

2020-1-PL01-KA202-081648.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-PL01-KA202-081648.title: Enhance the nursing sector with skills in clinical Phsycho-Oncology
2020-1-PL01-KA202-081648.summary:
<< Background >>

The incidence of malignant tumours is increasing in Europe, being the second cause of death after cardiovascular disease, especially in Poland. Death from cancer affects one in four men (26.4%) and one in five women (22.8%). Figures for the EU (2022) show that 31% of men and 25% of women will get a cancer diagnosis before the age of 75, with 14% of men and 9% of women dying before this date.

The high incidence highlights the need for a holistic approach to patients, taking into account physical and mental aspects. Medical staff must be equipped with stress management skills and psychological knowledge. In Europe, psycho-oncology, although a relatively young field, is experiencing a shortage of specialists. In some countries, cancer treatment does not include psychological support, highlighting the need to integrate psycho-oncological knowledge into the training of various medical professionals, including nurses.

The project aims to provide psycho-oncology knowledge free of charge and easily accessible. The use of digital tools not only facilitates access to this knowledge, but also integrates basic ICT tools.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the PsychONskills project included:
To provide a renewed set of digital and soft skills that are needed to meet the increased demand for highly skilled nurses caring for oncology patients.
Strengthening the soft and psychological skills of oncology care providers, improving their communication and psychological care of patients.
Develop competency-based professional training for nurses to facilitate the transition from providing unregistered nursing services to formal nursing care.
Dissemination of information on psycho-oncology to the project's target groups: medical staff, patients and their families, medical centres.

<< Implementation >>

The implementation of the Psychonskills project included both content area and administrative activities.
The Psychonskills project started with a comparative study between the partner countries in terms of nurses' competences, education, training opportunities in the field of psycho-oncology and ICT, and in terms of psychological knowledge useful in daily work. The results of this research and the edited comparative report (banchmarking report) within IO1 served as a basis for further project activities. IO 2 produced a training plan and e-course consisting of 4 modules: introduction to psycho-oncology, stress management at work, communication skills in working with patients and ICT skills - working in the cloud and digital environment. IO3 is the testing of the developed course with its evaluation. The IO4 outcome, on the other hand, is an attempt to expand networking by producing information material in the thematic area of the project.
The Psychonskills project also includes administrative tasks in the financial, evaluation and dissemination fields described in the relevant sections of this report. The partnership meetings were held online due to pandemic constraints and the many obligations of the partners to fulfil their duties due to their medical professional profile.

<< Results >>

Benchmarking report IO1
E-learning platform IO2
Pilot test with assessment tool IO3
Information material, extension of the IO4 network and dissemination activities
