2020-1-PL01-KA202-081664.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-PL01-KA202-081664.title: Szkolenia zawodowe dla oświetleniowców i dźwiękowców scenicznych i filmowych
2020-1-PL01-KA202-081664.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was developed on the basis of experience regarding vocational training in the film and music industry, both at the level of high school students and adults. In discussions between various training institutions, such as at a meeting on film education in Munich, it was repeatedly stated that film production needs thorough vocational training in sound and light at the intermediate level of film production. Entrepreneurs involved in the film and stage industry point out that there is a shortage on the labor market of people with the competencies to perform as lighting engineers, sound engineers or those who professionally prepare the stage for a concert or theatrical performance. 
It should be noted that in Poland as well as in the countries of the partner institutions there is a lack of vocational education at the level of a trade school or technical school in professions related to this project. Based on the information gathered, the partner institutions decided to apply for funds to create an international training program, to fill a niche in the market of vocational training services. The composition of the partnership was based on the specifics of each partner and its experience.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to exchange and gather experience in vocational training in the broad aspects of light and sound in film and music production, to hook the idea of vocational training at the secondary level in training institutions and vocational schools.
To develop a pilot program for training in sound and film.

<< Implementation >>

The following project activities were implemented:
- exchange of experience through international meetings, 
- presentations of the professional training process in the workplace at the Film School, music studio, theater, film studio, film sound studio, literature house, Monopolis music stage in Lodz,
- short-term training for trainees and teachers,
- study visits to places of training such as the Film School in Lodz, Art Kombinat, Film Institute in Berlin, TOYA studio, Muszyna Theater in Lodz, Drama Theater in Rijeka, Music Lab music studio and sound laboratory in Turin,
- Establish and develop cooperation with vocational schools, music studios involved in education,
- conducting internal trainings related to the presentation of the training program and the idea of the project.

<< Results >>

The following results were achieved during the project:
- an exchange of experience was realized through meetings of sound and lighting specialists who are certified as teachers or professional instructors, 
- an analysis of the training processes of those involved in film and music production was developed, 
- a professional training program on light on film set, theater and music stage and sound was developed,
-conducted a short form of training of an instructional nature for instructors or vocational teachers, 3 days of training, 24 didactic hours,
-conducted pilot training for the target group conducted by teachers or instructors from partner organizations, 
- educational offer of participating organizations was expanded,
- exchange of experience through study visits to the Film School in Lodz, studio with dolby Atmos, TOYA studio, Musi Lab studio in Turin, Film Institute,- Gaining practice for teachers through exchanges with staff from other institutions,
- conducting internal training with the target group at partner institutions,
- establishing cooperation with other institutions, including the Film School in Lodz, Music Lab in Turin, Film Institute,
- intercultural exchange,
- gaining practice in working in an international team,
The main result of the project is the development of a professional training program with a set of readings, exercises, instructions for instructors, teachers
profession in the field of work of lighting and sound technician on film sets, music scenes.
Provide a description of the training with examples of practice exercises publication will be disseminated and available in pdf form on the websites of the organizations partner organizations.

2020-1-PL01-KA202-082058.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-PL01-KA202-082058.title: Cooperation and education - the key to sustainable development.
2020-1-PL01-KA202-082058.summary:
<< Background >>

Sustainable development, biodiversity and vocational training should serve to educate young people, who are conscious citizens not only of their own country, but also of the wider EU community. Caring for the natural environment, while implementing the idea of sustainable development, is our common task, which required close cooperation between the partners, consisting of the transfer of knowledge, experience and skills related to the education of children, youth and adults. Through the implementation of the project, the coordinator and partners wanted to gain practical and theoretical knowledge in the field of promoting the idea of sustainable development and care for the natural environment as a part of multifunctional forest management in such a way, that it could be passed on to others, and thus raise the level of teaching in the field of education about nature and forestry to the European level. Therefore, it was necessary to support educators in the process of transferring knowledge in this field through mutual exchange of knowledge and experience, and then creating a workshop enabling the transfer of the acquired knowledge to all those interested in the issues of supporting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

<< Objectives >>

Through the implementation of the project, the project coordinator and partners wanted to: achieve tasks giving opportunities to students, society and our partners, get acquainted with the wide possibilities offered by the surrounding natural world, expand cooperation for vocational education in the spirit of respecting the natural environment, with a focus on sustainable development mechanisms, which was to happen through the mutual exchange of practices, experiences and ideas during training visits, raising competences in the field of sustainable multifunctional forest management, increasing competences in the field of industry language in forestry, as well as bringing the level of education to the European level in the field of formal and informal education about nature and forestry. The project was also aimed at engaging the staff of the Forestry Inspectorate, the teaching staff of the Forest School Complex in Ruciane-Nida, foreign partners and school children and youth from Poland and other European countries to cooperate in the field of nature and forest education.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were conducted: 
- culinary workshops were conducted for project partners on the preparation of venison dishes based on traditional hunting cuisine with the use of undergrowth fruits and also for students of FSC based on the gifts of "Forest Orchard"; 
- seedlings were purchased and planted by partners, students of the Forestry School Complex, local government authorities and representatives of the local organization creating "Forest Orchard"; 
- advertising banners for training meetings were bought and financed; 
- classes were conducted for students of various age groups in local schools, transferring the experience gained from foreign partners; 
- partners made training trips in order to help achieving the goals of the project; 
- the partners were acquainted with the touristic aspect of the Great Masurian Lakes region; 
- meetings were organized on examples of good cooperation in the field of education, nature protection, historical and natural knowledge; 
- a conference  for local authorities, institutions and schools was organized to share experiences; 
- a script was created as a tool for exchanging knowledge and experience in the field of natural education for sustainable development.

<< Results >>

We gained knowledge on the possibilities of supporting education in the spirit of sustainable development. We started international cooperation and, as a part of promoting the idea of sustainable development and care for the environment, we jointly completed a task, that gave students, society and our partners a chance to learn about the opportunities offered by the surrounding natural world. We planted "Forest Orchard" - species of trees and shrubs of plants naturally growing in Polish forests and traditional fruit varieties, that became available to the community. There were workshops on the use of the above-mentioned fruit. As part of education supporting the principles of sustainable development and the idea of multifunctional forest management, this place is available to everyone. There were also culinary workshops, practical classes, meetings with students transferring the acquired knowledge, community integration, increased promotion of multifunctional forest management, care for cultural values, familiarization with a wide range of educational methods. At the end of the project, a script was created that gathered the project values in one place. The script developed in four languages can be used by all interested parties.

2020-1-PL01-KA202-082239.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-PL01-KA202-082239.title: Remote working management skills for HR professionals
2020-1-PL01-KA202-082239.summary:
<< Background >>

BACKGROUND
The Covid-19 virus outbreak in late 2019 - early 2020 led to a surge of remote working, where the majority of EU white collar workforce was compelled to work in an out-of-office setting; this comes to a sharp contrast compared to past years, where just 5-10% of EU employees have been working remotely. Nevertheless, such a rise in remote working has not been unprecedented; there has been a steady, yet minimal, increase through the years in the numbers of remote workers (esp. in the ICT sector), with a similar spike during the 2002-2003 SARS outbreak and other similar cases of business interruptions. The difference this time is that the increase in remote working due to Covid-19 virus outbreak has been fuelled
both by more flexible and decentralised management practices, as well as more widely available technologies. Moreover, people are more used to it, be it for work or for personal communication. This led to an immediate and creative adaptation of workplaces to a remote work mode, where in many occasions the entire workforce worked from home.

PAIZ, with a keen interest on the latest advancements in the HR field, identified together with EXELIA (staff of which have worked with PAIZ in the context of work with past employers) a deficit in the current provision of skills and competences regarding the remote management of a workforce and came up with the idea/initiative to address current and future skill needs of HR professions by creating a joint European VET course to address this skill shortage.


NEEDS & CHALLENGES
The most pressing issue and challenge that became obvious is the possibility of a lasting workplace change, where a greater part of the workforce works out of premises in the immediate future. In addition, clear and consistent policies on remote working were missing from many companies, exposing a lack of HR preparations on the topic in many companies (e.g. remote work company-wide policies, management & contingency plans). HR professionals needed to be able to address these new challenges by redesigning processes, and retraining / supporting their colleagues on how to manage an increased remote workforce. From redefining goals and roles of staff, to redesigning personal interactions and normalising the new work environment, HR managers were faced with new tasks that were not part of their portfolios so far, and were rather a small part of the training they had undergone.

<< Objectives >>

OBJECTIVES
The project aimed to document the emerging skills gap for managing a remote workforce, and to develop corresponding Open Educational Resources and a training course for the continuous professional development of HR professionals, trainers, supervisors, consultants and managers of organisations and teams. In particular, partners:
1. Documented the skills required for managing a remote workforce, improving skills intelligence at the EU level
2. Defined learning outcomes for a C-VET course for HR professionals on remote work management
3. Made available a sector-validated online course for HR professionals
4. Provided ready-to-use tools for the workplace to support the role of HR professionals as trainers and mentors.

<< Implementation >>

To document the skills required for managing a remote workforce partners conducted the comprehensive needs analysis to define remote work management skills requirements and mismatches. The labour market & skill needs evidence were collected via a) desk research on existing training offerings, b) a survey on skills requirements & workplace realities, and c) follow-up interviews with employers and HR field experts.
The need analysis was the basis for defining learning outcomes and learning units for a C-VET course for HR professionals on remote work management.
The learning outcomes were clustered into 6 units and transferred into an online course for HR professionals. The partnership developed a modular course available in an online form as a MOOC, aiming to support HR professionals in acquiring and developing remote working skills. The MOOC is available in all the project languages (EN, FR, PL, GR, HR, SI, PT) to ensure wide geographical coverage.
Also a trainer's handbook with VET integration guidelines was developed to support educators and trainers in delivering the REMOWA course, and VET providers to incorporate it in their offerings. 

Partners also developed additional educational materials like: best practice guide, covering technological and organisational examples of remote work, guidelines; remote work protocols and checklists and online assessment tool. All of those open educational resources are downloadable from the project’s website as well as other channels (e.g. the Erasmus+ Project Results Platform, project’s social media).

<< Results >>

OVERVIEW OF PROJECT OUTPUTS
The following list provides an overview of the intellectual outputs and multiplier events of the REMOWA project:
•	Evidence-based, measurable and assessable learning outcomes for VET provision on the knowledge and skills required to be acquired by HR professionals to be able to manage a remote workforce (Output 1).
•	VET learning units on remote working management skills for HR professionals (Output 2).
•	Open Education Resources (OERs) on remote working management (Output 2).
•	REMOWA Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) infrastructures and content in 7 EU languages (EN, PL, FR, GR, PT, HR, SI) -  Output 3.
•	Self-assessment tools for employers and managers to effectively facilitate remote working (Output 4).
•	Best practice guide with remote working case studies and remote working management tools & protocols (Output 4).
•	Six (6) national information days in Poland, Belgium, Greece, Portugal, Croatia, and Slovenia, to share and disseminate REMOWA results.
RESULTS SUPPORTING DISSEMINATION AND SUSTAINABILITY
The partnership developed tools and materials for the dissemination of project activities and outcomes:
1. Project website: One-stop online access to all project outputs and resources, facilitating all target groups and stakeholders in comprehending, assessing, and adopting REMOWA results.
2. Online social media pages (Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter and YouTube channel), videos, and presentations: These tools aimed to extend the reach of dissemination efforts by exploiting the appeal of new media, especially to younger individuals and those not reached by other project dissemination activities.
3. Newsletters & press releases: Addressed to target groups and stakeholders all across EU (through emails), seeking to inform, motivate, and promote involvement in project activities.
4. Printed materials: Brochures/flyers and posters to provide concrete information during project and third-party training, dissemination, and networking events.
5. Six (6) national information days in Poland, Belgium, Greece, Portugal, Croatia, and Slovenia, to share and disseminate REMOWA results.

2020-1-SI01-KA202-075881.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-SI01-KA202-075881.title: Securing Data Privacy in the HealthCare Sector
2020-1-SI01-KA202-075881.summary:
<< Background >>

The health sector, which holds some of the most important and sensitive personal data for patients, is quite vulnerable to cyber-attacks as it was shown after an internal investigation conducted before the proposal was written, mainly due to the limited budget and the fact that cyber-security is not a priority for this sector. The consortium recognized that there was a gap in this field and therefore developed a project, which would fill these gaps. Based on the needs expressed by the partners, the key aim of the project was to incorporate the new digital mentality into companies, employees and young learners, while responding to the fragmented certification system in the field. The consortium addressed needs that focus on the consequences of a potential cyber-attack on the health sector. In particular, on the occasion of the GDPR 2016/679 which requires for healthcare organizations to re-think about their data flows and how they handle and monitor patient data, emerged the need to face the issue of rising skills mismatch between data protection officers/employees across EU countries with different occupational profile on skills and competences and most importantly, different level of legislation/integration on data protection.

<< Objectives >>

- Foster employability of young learners and employees in the health sector, providing them with the new Data Protection (DP) Skills Sets, achieving higher connectivity between the emergence of new job roles and associated skills needs from 2016/679 Directive.
- Enhance transparency, comparability and harmonization of Sectoral skills and qualifications of DP employees, providing a new Occupational Profile that includes new “soft skills” needed in the data privacy area.
- Support setting-up of two new VET Curricula: preparation of a learning-outcome based Training course for DPOs in Health sector & trainers that are going to cover “horizontally” the main areas of skills and competences and share a common learning experience among them at a EU level and an Awareness raising DPO Curriculum accompanied by a strong Peer Mentoring element to enhance the capacities of in-company trainers within the Healthcare sector.
- Develop a new Peer Mentoring Scheme, supported by a Toolbox, that is going to provide the necessary linkage between VET Training and Actual Work and enhance real learning.
- Foster cross-border, transnational / interregional mobility for DPO's in the Health sector that leads to knowledge transfer and new job opportunities.

<< Implementation >>

IO1 Conduction of a current gap analysis and building of a common Occupational Profile for DPOs in Health Sector
A1: Mapping of skills gap and identification of common trends with the use of TNA methodology
A2: In depth analysis of offered VET Curricula in Project’s participating countries (compar. approach) and identification of best practices
A3: Synthesis of a Final Report on data protection guidelines and recommendations for a harmonised Occupational Profile in the Health sector 
IO2 Designing of two VET Curricula and horizontal data protection training for DPOs and employees in health sector
A1: Preparation of a learning-outcome based DPO Curriculum & Training course for DPOs in Health sector & trainers
A2: Designing of assessment standards and adaptation of Curricula in Countries' specific context
A3: Design of an inspiring Peer mentoring toolbox for the support of Health sector peer mentors
IO3 Piloting of Curricula and Peer mentoring Training Scheme in the Health sector
A1: Testing of a digital platform for the support of peer mentoring within the Health Sector
A2: Piloting of two curricula along with accompanied peer mentoring scheme in partners countries
A3: Development of effective feedback loops and satisfaction survey

<< Results >>

Based on the application and the implementation of the activities, the following concrete outputs and results our project produced:
I.O. 1 Conduction of a current gap analysis and building of a common Occupational Profile for DPOs in Health Sector
•	State of the Art Comparative Analysis and new Skills Chart
•	Comparative Analysis of different Data Protection Curricula
•	Final report on guidelines and recommendations for a harmonised DPO Occupational profile in the Health sector

I.O. 2 Designing of two VET Curricula and horizontal data protection training for DPOs and
employees in healthcare sector
•	A Joint DPO VET Curriculum for Healthcare sector
•	An Awareness raising Curriculum on Data Protection accompanied by a strong Peer Mentoring element tailored to Healthcare sector identified needs
•	Assessment standards for the VET curricula
•	Peer Mentoring Toolbox

I.O. 3 Piloting of Curricula and Peer mentoring Training Scheme in the Healthcare sector
•	Fully operational peer mentoring platform accompanied by user manuals
•	Final report on the curricula piloting including policy recommendations for future use
•	Report on trainers/peer mentors and trainees overall satisfaction

2020-1-SI01-KA202-076025.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-SI01-KA202-076025.title: Skilled to be a Fire Expert
2020-1-SI01-KA202-076025.summary:
<< Background >>

This project meet several needs. First, to respond to the need for properly processed and fast flow of information on new fire safety challenges, like increased number of fires (due to modern lifestyles, batteries etc.), growing percentage of population with disabilities, etc., a tool for Lecturers & Trainers of Fire Experts, and for Fire Experts themselves have to be developed. This tool provide state-of-the-art answers in an environment they can rely on and the latest knowledge on fire safety issues. 
On the other hand, there is a need for a faster and connected flow of information between the different engineering sectors involved in fire safety but also between academic/research institutions and professionals to put more emphasis on the effective and supportive development of new fire safety experts skilled to meet the needs of practice. 
In addition, in relatively small countries such as the partner countries, with a shorter tradition of education and training of fire experts than in Northern Europe, connections and knowledge sharing are even more important. Some of the partners are national representatives of EU Fire Protection Associations (CFPA-E), who meet regularly to discuss the latest issues at the European level.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to achieve the exchange of the latest knowledge and information on the emerging challenges of fire protection for fire experts (including lecturers, researchers, scientists, engineers from different field, people from fire safety industry etc.) from participating and other countries, but also to provide the useful education materials in different forms to lecturers, especially for those who lack the latest information in very broad area of fire protection (e.g. recent fires, firefighters interventions, news on the market of products for fire safety, new approaches at planning fire safety in buildings, etc.). Very important was the idea of international sharing of best practice in approaches of education in very specific and complex area as it is fire safety.

<< Implementation >>

Preparation of materials in individual modules, their complementation and accessibility for all (in English and free: https://www.skilledfe.eu/).
Organization of meetings, workshops/seminars to gather various professionals to support dialog in such a multidisciplinary field as fire safety. Very important step in preparing a better future of fire experts in educational approaches was to organize unconventional events where participants could discuss and implement the findings of the modules.
After the events, visits to other related institutions were organized to increase the impact of the project and local-level implementation.
Developing and strengthening external cooperation with organizations from the EU: Fire Safe Europe, CFPA-E, from Turkey: Karabük University, from the UK: UCLAN.
Dissemination of information on the project’s results and increase effectiveness via social media (Twitter, LinkedIn, Researchgate)
Ensuring sustainability and follow-up of the project by establishing a team (individuals from the project team) to take care of the Forum and social media to maintain and promote communication within the community. Preparation of new project proposals based on the feedback on this project.

<< Results >>

The main result of the project is The Platform i.e. website (Skilled to be a Fire Expert (skilledfe.eu)) used for publishing of ongoing work during the project implementation, but, intended to exist as the communication and publishing tool even after the completion of the project, as an open access Online Learning Platform for Fire Expert Trainers. The most important part of the Platform is The Forum (Forum – Skilled to be Fire Expert (skilledfe.eu)), where registered users can debate on different topics, get relevant information and share their.
Eight extensive documents (curriculums) on the state-of-the art of different aspects of fire safety are prepared and published on the Platform (see M1 to M8). 
Brochure of the project was prepared and issued in 500 copies, and also published on Platform.
Beside, during project development seminars/workshops in Zagreb, Ostrava, Prague and two in Ljubljana were organized to discuss particular stage of project development. Many stakeholders participated especially at the last one in Ljubljana, during the international congress Safety and Prevention 2022 in October. 
Presentation of outputs were published in magazine Požar, but also through social media, LinkedIn, Twitter and Researchgate.

2020-1-SK01-KA202-078223.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-SK01-KA202-078223.title: ENDURANCE: Entrepreneurial Capacity-building for Sport
2020-1-SK01-KA202-078223.summary:
<< Background >>

Sports has been the most popular recreational activity for centuries, being an important element of society. The entrepreneurial spirit has also been embedded in societies for ages, helping people to grow socially and economically. The role of entrepreneurship is greater than ever before in the EU due to current socio-economic challenges. Linkages between sports and entrepreneurship are manifold but rarely recognised and capitalised upon. This is valid across many sectors, especially in VET.

In particular, the commonalities between sports and entrepreneurship are found in:
•	MINDSET: in attributes like determination, perseverance, self-confidence, stamina, respect of rules, team play, etc.
•	BEHAVIOURS: opportunity search and evaluation, turning ideas into action, networking, etc.
•	CAREER DIRECTIONS: where athletes and professionals often work on a quasi-entrepreneurial basis.

However, entrepreneurship and sports rarely are found together as effectively connected domains with synergic links in the VET sector. This creates gaps in developing much-needed entrepreneurial competencies due to the low penetration of entrepreneurship education (EE) in sports-oriented disciplines and the lack of tailored entrepreneurship training.

<< Objectives >>

To address these gaps at the EU level, the main ENDURANCE objectives were:
1)	Develop an online interactive and open OER platform to deliver the ENDURANCE training and the other ENDURANCE results.
2)	Map the dynamics of sports and entrepreneurship, common traits and links, and success and failure factors in their linking for sustainable careers for learners in VET and sports systems.
3)	Develop the tailored ENDURANCE entrepreneurship training and toolkit through and for sports for enhanced entrepreneurship, pilot it to a cohort of the target groups’ representatives, and finalise it accordingly.
4)	Sustain project results and promote their uptake in VET and sports ecosystems with the specific ENDURANCE Guidelines for Uptake.
5)	Stimulate the debate, practice and policy options, and sensitise the actors to advance links between sports and entrepreneurship with the ENDURANCE Green Paper.

<< Implementation >>

The activities were organised around the Intellectual Outputs and their tasks:

IO1: ENDURANCE OER Platform available in 7 languages
T1: Develop the structure of the platform
T2: Maintain and operate the OER Platform
Created to share with the target groups the training and other project results. It is completely open and free.

IO2: ENDURANCE Mapping and stock-taking of Sports and Entrepreneurship (S&E) dynamics
T1: Identify common traits and links between S&E
T2: Establish correlations and overlaps between S&E
Comprehensive mapping and stock-taking in partners' countries and beyond.

IO3: ENDURANCE Toolkit: E-learning training material for VET learners linking S&E for Entrepreneurial Success
T1: Develop ENDURANCE Toolkit 
T2: Translate Toolkit in 7 languages
T3: Validation Plan
T4: Deploy ENDURANCE to at least 150 target groups
T5: Fine-Tune ENDURANCE
The key result of the project comprising training contents and tools for enhanced entrepreneurship in and through sports.

IO4: ENDURANCE Guidelines for Uptake & Green Paper
T1: ENDURANCE Guidelines for Uptake
T2: Develop ENDURANCE green paper
The key documents to promote the uptake of the ENDURANCE Toolkit, and to sensitise actors on advancing the linkages between S&E.

<< Results >>

The key outputs and results include mainly:

1) An online interactive and open OER platform at the service of each target group (i.e. learners in VET and sports systems)

2) A comprehensive mapping of the dynamics of S&E, common traits and links between the two, and success and failure factors in linking S&E for sustainable careers for learners in VET and sports systems

3) An ENDURANCE toolkit comprising tailored and custom-made training contents and tools for enhanced entrepreneurship in sports as well as innovative training for enhanced entrepreneurship in sports via supporting the entrepreneurship spirit exploitation through a sports and athlete mindset

4) Guidelines to sustain the project results and promote the uptake of the ENDURANCE toolkit among the education and training and sports ecosystems

5) A Green Paper putting forward elements for debate, practice and policy options to advance the linkages between S&E in wider contexts beyond the partnership

The idea behind ENDURANCE is to trigger entrepreneurial spirit through the characteristics of sport (e.g., precision, respect of rules, determination, failure, team-work, etc.). This is a highly innovative endeavour as there are very few, if any, such resources available.

2020-1-SK01-KA202-078281.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-SK01-KA202-078281.title: Technical innovations in theory and practice
2020-1-SK01-KA202-078281.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was implemented as a partnership of 6 oranizations from 4 countries – Slovakia, the Czech republic, Croatia and Germany. The partners are schools and educational organizations, which operate in industrially strong regions, which are characterized by relatively high growth dynamics. Lack of qualified workforce and lack of connection between vocational education and practice are also the problems related to this. The target group of the project were not only the schools and their students and teachers, but also regional employers, for whom the schools prepare their future employees. The employers and competent employees of the partner identified possible areas in which the project can go and these are industrial 3D printing, robotics and automation of prodution, computer systems and industry 4.0, industrial PC – PLC, hydraulics and pneumatics, logistics and registration, corporate information system.

<< Objectives >>

The main goal was to modernize VET in partner schools by connecting school and practice. The intention was to create outputs in the form of educational outputs and teaching materials which can be used for mobilities, educational innovations or for lifelong education. We also supported introduction of modern systems from the field of robotization and digitization into VET. The significant goal was to analyze the situation in the area of employment and to find out what influence young people most when choosing a new job position. We planned to analyze the needs of employers in the field of competencies of future graduates to adapt the content of education. The intention of the project was to support cooperation between partnerships created by organizations, which are responsible for vocational education and to prepare the graduates for the labor market. This was aimed to improve carier guidance. With this project, we wanted to give the teachers, as well as employees responsible for vocational education, the chance to improve their own professional development by exchanging their experience with their foreign colleagues. This will create new possibilities to extend their future cooperation and to start new multilateral partnership.

<< Implementation >>

The target group were teachers and secondary school students, employers, institutions participating in VET, regional self-government, industry and professional associations. 
The international teams were involved in this project. These teams were preparing, verifying  and implementing the outputs. We carried out surveys of available information as well as through questionaires among the target group. We analyzed the obtained data and we used them in creating the outputs. 
The teachers who were involved produced 4 intellectual outputs. The outputs were then verified in schools but also during four educational activities for students and teachers. We organized professional conference and Job Shadowing for teachers. The students participated in workshops within the Week of professional skills and international competitions.
Apart from educational activities we also organized 4 transnational project meetings and final conference of the project. All the outputs and successes of the project were implemented into the educational programs of particular partners. We informed the public as well as responsible authorities and institutions about the results of the project. All the ouputs were also available to other schools in regions.

<< Results >>

The project created 4 intellectual outputs. In the output 01 „The survey of the needs of regional employers“, we compared trends in the labour market of all participating countries and we worked on surveys to find out what motivate young people when choosing their first job and what are the needs of employers for graduates competencies.
Within the outuput 02 „Proposal of the common curriculum“,we worked on 10 educational programs which can be used in formal education as well as within the international cooperation and lifelong education.
The ouput 03 „Preparation of teaching materials“ included 67 sets of teaching materials in the form of presentations, worksheets, test and exercises in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, ICT and economics.
In the output 04 „Carier guidance and support of technical education in elementary schools“ we focused on preparation of materials to improve technical skills and to increase interest in technical professions.
Through the implementation of the project the partners obtained conditions that are necessary for modernization of education, mainly in the form of know-how, experience and outputs of the project. The ouputs were available to other schools and organizations in local community.

2020-1-UK01-KA202-078917.action_type: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
2020-1-UK01-KA202-078917.title: Oral Potentially Malignant Disorders: Training of Healthcare Professionals
2020-1-UK01-KA202-078917.summary:
<< Background >>

General Medical/Dental Practitioners and many other Healthcare Professionals regularly encounter patients who present with Oral Potentially Malignant Disorders
(OPMDs). OPMDs is a term encompassing multiple disorders which have the ability to transform into cancer.  Although there are multiple modalities of information available to healthcare professions on this topic, most exist in written form (in the English language only) and follow old guidance. Healthcare professionals from different sectors, in particular dentists, general medical practitioners, oral hygienists, dental therapists  have been identified as key professionals on the frontline for the early diagnosis of OPMD and overall management. This e-learning project (WWW.OPMDcare.com) addresses provides a wide practical guidance on the diagnosis of OPMDs and overall management to be used by this particular group of healthcare professionals. It is supported by multiple images , leaflets, e-book articles as well as a variety range of other teaching material. The project addresses the need to educate and inform healthcare professionals on the detection, diagnosis and management of this group of conditions

<< Objectives >>

Through an interactive developmental approach, involving feedback from training delivered, and other stakeholders, we have ensured the project is accessible and relevant to the local educational context and practitioners in partner countries. We wanted to achieve:  
•	the development of an e-learning tool about Oral Medicine for Healthcare Professionals, embracing the recognition, investigation, diagnosis and management of patients presenting with OPMDs. This is accessible to all European Union Healthcare Professionals and translated into several languages (English, French, Portuguese, Croatian and Spanish).  Evidence: www.OPMDcare.com
•	To strengthen the ties among European Union educational and professional health institutions.  This would involve sharing best practices on the topic of OPMD through transitional and online meetings.  Thus far, multiple teaching materials have been created which reflects good interaction and communication between partners. (http://opmdcare.com/downloadable-resources/).
•	To increase professionals’ skills and improve their personal portfolios whilst taking into account the language/content differences between the countries’ education systems. ( >1,700 individuals have participated in e-learning).

<< Implementation >>

Through project management and implementation, the following activities lead to www.OPMDcare.com.  Overall, this supported the following 7 work packages: 
WP1: A Grant Agreement was developed with clearly defined project phases, deadlines and outcomes of each phase through cooperation arrangements, which all partners signed.
WP2: Design of the programme content and tools selection
WP3: Review of literature with content to be used in e-earning 
WP4: Testing of the pilot e-learning modules. Content of e-Book and Posters

2014-1-AT02-KA205-000211.title: Mapping professional open youth work
2014-1-AT02-KA205-000211.summary:
Mapping professional open youth work (in Europe)

The project created a strategic partnership for working on underlying principles and concrete tools for mapping professional open youth work in Europe as of today. It gathered ten partners from nine different countries coming from diverse backgrounds - we managed to have partners from the non-formal and the formal education sector as well as grass root youth work and umbrella organisations. It gave this part of youth work the room for professional debate on the core profile of their work as well as some tools for online discussion and showcasing of professional open youth work. It therefore had two pillars that were closely linked to each other:

1) Debate and Description of „Principles of Professional Open Youth Work in Europe“
The partnership engaged in a very serious discussion about a common defintion and underlying principles of professional open youth work and worked on a document that would respect the various national and background realities and create a clearer profile of this profession in Europe. The result of this process is a "Declaration of Principles" which was published and disseminated in September 2016. Read more about the process and the result here: http://magazine.poywe.org/magazine/logbook-issue-3/mapping-a-profession/

2) Online platform for debate, capacity building and dissemination of knowledge about professional open youth work in Europe consisting of:
The LOGBOOK Platform that was created within this project aims on the one hand to enable exchange of experience and good practice and on the other hand on show casing what Professional Open Youth Work is and what effects it has in Europe today. For achieving this aim it features several things:
a) The LOGBOOK E-Magazine was created and three editions were published during the project duration. It features descriptions of the state of the art of youth work in all participating countries, one hot topic per issue (1. radicalisation of young people and the role of open youth work, 2. professional open youth work and young refugees and 3. youth work as a profession), news and information about training, methods and interviews with young people and youth workers.
b) A video channel with short videos that explain professional open youth work from different angles - currently there is 19 interviews with youth workers and experts from 12 countries.
c) Debate and exchange of experience - to widen the debate we have also created a space for webinars, where we have discussed the final version of our declaration of principles with interested participants.

Apart from this concrete results the project helped to build a stronger network of professional open youth work in Europe that is going to be active and in touch also after the end of this partnership. Several participants of the closing event announced that they will translate the "Declaration of Principiles in their own languages for making it even more accesible for youth workers in their own country. The LOGBOOK Platform will stay and POYWE plans to keep publishing the E-Magazine, continue uploading video interviews that show what professional open youth work is doing and provide webinars for youth workers.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Quality and innovation of youth work

2014-1-HR01-KA205-007210.title: New Eyes & Toys
2014-1-HR01-KA205-007210.summary:
Sometimes children do not appreciate their toys because, being used to see them everyday, they get easily fed up. But, once a new child wants to take their toys, they become jealous and the love for their toys reappears.
Likewise it often happens that people do not appreciate the place where they live and things they have until when another person come and let them understand the real value of their things.
Following this approach the project “New eyes & toys” aimed to let young people find again the love for the place where they live, fostering them to do everything to improve it and be active.
The project involved 30 young people between 20 and 24 so called NEET (Not in Education or Employment or Training) and 6 group leaders (2 for each Country). 
The project idea derived from an analysis which was carried out in Klis by the Municipality together with an informal group of young people created in order to establish a Youth Council. The analysis showed that a majority of young people who do not work or study, and are not enrolled in any training course, are generally reluctant to engage themselves within the local community. Young people between 20 and 24 years old were showed to be the group most affected by unemployment and inactivity.
Furthermore they lack essential knowledge on Europe, what it represents and its promotion towards encouraging social inclusion and cultural diversity. Perhaps due to the crisis or  lack of opportunities, information and stimulation, many Klis youths manifest a certain apathy towards what is not part of their everyday life. 
Following a comparison with the problems encountered by young people in the Municipality of Gavoi (Italy) and Municipalities of Baixo Tâmega (Portugal) we were surprised that they faced similar difficulties. Considering all data, we identified 3 common problems which we aimed to address with the strategic partnership project:
1) youth unemployment (especially due to lack of entrepreneurship and early school leaving);
2) lack of involvement of young people in local decision-making process.;
3) passive citizenship of young people who do not study, do not work and are not enrolled in any training course or initiative. 
Methodologies used in the project were non formal, innovative, interactive and based on "learning by doing". 

Through a series of non formal activities (blended mobilities, forum of discussions, workshops, play roles, focus groups, movie making, etc.)  project implementation resulted into reaching the following specific objectives:

*Increasing entrepreneurship skills of unemployed young citizens in Klis, Gavoi and Baixo Tâmega 
*Reducing the distance between young people and decision makers in Klis, Gavoi and Baixo Tâmega through the creation of a youth council that would help to solve problems of local youth;
*Reducing the number of inactive young citizens (NEETs) in Klis, Gavoi and Baixo Tâmega.
Main outputs will be:
*Completing a guide for youth workers, where trainers, facilitators and people working with young people will find new tools and methodologies to use and replicate;
*Completing a web page for young entrepreneurs, which is different from the web page of the project, collects useful information about procedures to follow in order to open a new activity in Croatia, Portugal and Italy, and includes a space for the interaction of young entrepreneurs and exchange of experiences, ideas and good practices.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Equal access and transition to labour market
Quality and innovation of youth work

2014-1-HR01-KA205-007214.title: Generation 0101
2014-1-HR01-KA205-007214.summary:
With the project Generation 0101 project consortium tackled unemployment as one of the most relevant youth problem in Europe today. Interrelated with this issue, there is a growing need for placing a stronger emphasis on the development and recognition of ICT skills in order for people all over Europe to become better educated and more competitive in the job market. 
Objectives of the project were to increase competitiveness of young people in the job market and thus helping in fighting unemployment in Europe, while emphasizing the importance of ICT for professional development and employability in digital industries, stressing the value of non-formal and informal learning and raising of civic engagement of youth workers and young people in partner countries.
Project consortium consisted of 7 organisations from 6 countries: Centar tehničke kulture Rijeka (Croatia), Asociacija "Langas į ateitį" (Lithuania), Associazione Centro Studi Città di Foligno (Italy), Cyprus Community Media Center (Cyprus), Izmir Universitesi (Turkey), Latvijas Informācijas un komunikācijas tehnoloģijas asociācija (Latvia) and Telecentar (Croatia). Partner organisations had great experience in raising digital skills of young people, while some were also coordinators of National Coalitions for Digital Skills and Jobs. Out of 6 countries involved in project, 3 countries had Digital Agenda consolidated in national documents and 3 countries didn’t recognise importance of integration of objectives of Digital Agenda into existing or newly developed strategies. 
In order to define in detail needs of digital market and youth, research was implemented. Main goal was to analyse educational needs in each country and important challenges which has to be tackled if countries want to respond on needs of digital market. Research revealed that countries with integrated goals of Digital agenda already allocated funds for raising digital skills of youth, but also citizens in general, and already responded on the need of digital market, while other countries are facing bigger gap between skilled workers and market needs. According to the results, seven educational modules were developed and 322 young people educated to be eJournalist, speakers on Community Web Radios, web designers, video editors, coders, mobile apps developers or advanced users of online collaboration tools. Materials developed are adjusted for onsite learning, but also for self-studying and last from 20 to 40 hours. In addition, learning is based on practical skills development and it results with project which can be added to personal portfolio. By the end of education, 142 projects were created from scratch by young people and 19 projects which were directly requested from NGOs, CSOs and other organisations important for community development. Methodology of Hackathon showed its usefulness for testing digital skills of young people while having positive impact on local community.
Long-term impact of the project is sustained with open educational resources developed and available on www.generation0101.eu, their adjustment for integration into formal educational system and by projects (digital solutions) created for national and local organisations.

2014-1-NO02-KA205-000069.title: Borderline boardgames
2014-1-NO02-KA205-000069.summary:
The idea for this project arose first and foremost from the financial difficulties that have permeated much of Europe for several years. The The idea for this project arose first and foremost from the financial difficulties that have permeated much of Europe for several years. The last few years have witnessed a big part of the burden of austerity being heaped onto the shoulders of the continent’s young people. We, the project group, felt there was a need to look into this and see if we, in our professions, could contribute towards something positive.

This project was based on a couple of identified needs that we observed in the various participating countries. First, we saw a need for more effective and innovative instruments to encourage young people to become more aware and educated on how to manage one’s private economy. To become financially literate, to put it differently. This need was in large part based on the financial difficulties much of Europe has been going through over the last several years, and which persists still. Second, we found it to be an ongoing need to have more competence and understanding of conflict management among young people. We see clear links between the macro- and the micro level on this topic. Lastly, we had an idea of combining these two areas to attempt to provide concrete tools, especially to group of young people with fewer opportunities, to deal more constructively with troubling situations of financial difficulty without resorting to conflict.

Communication about the initial ideas started between a few of the partners who knew each other well from a long list of previous collaborations. The project rationale and a couple of concrete ideas were then shared down the network of acquainted trainers, youth workers and organisations. All partners have been involved in this project based on their special competence or experience related to one or both of the concrete tools the project group wanted to develop. The centrepiece of this project has been to develop and produce two educational and interactive board games, to address financial literacy and conflict management - “Real Ideal” and “Mission Z”, respectively.

The project has been undertaken with 10 formal partners, with one external partner that has also been involved throughout the whole project - including holding a crucial role in the actual production of all the game pieces for what has become “Real Ideal” and “Mission Z”. It was an important criterion for us that all the involved organisations, companies and informal groups are involved as directly as possible in field youth work or local community building.

The results include that each partner now is in possession of 1 complete set of “Mission Z” and 4 complete sets of “Real Ideal”, attractively designed and formed in multipurpose materials. All game pieces have been handmade in a village in Portugal, and has thus created some employment during the project period, as well as improved the capacity of the same village and its people to produce more output of a similar sort in the future.

Our testing of the concepts for both games has been rigorous. In total we have tested the two games with 653 participants who have all provided us with written feedback. This has enabled us to modify the games during the project period and adjust for input offered to us by the actual target group for both games, the young people themselves. The feedback from these participants has been overwhelmingly positive, across the board. This is the main thing for us, and gives us a feeling of having contributed well to the field of youth work and non-formal learning methods.

The outputs of this project has also reached other circles, such as banks and universities that are keen on utilising these games in their education of financial literacy and conflict management, respectively. Some concrete partnerships along these lines have already been formalised.

For more, and updated information also after the project’s end, we invite the reader to visit our website: http://bb-games.eu

2014-1-RO01-KA205-002734.summary:

2014-1-SI02-KA205-000257.title: Under the moon
2014-1-SI02-KA205-000257.summary:
The project called UTM shorter for »Under the moon« was held by Slovenian film group MMCT, working and creating in MCT - Mladinski center Trbovlje.
Our goal was to unite people, especially youngsters with different stories and backgrounds from all around the world to create one single story in this extensive and diverse project. The idea was inspired by overall look at people who live their own life in their own way, face different problems in different parts of the world, without knowing that many times their stories are similar and unconsciously deeply connected.
The project is called »Under the moon«, because the moon itself stands as a symbol of connection. We all live under the moon’s light, and if we think about it, together we are unimaginably small against the universe, but at the same time very important. The same is with our stories which are small, but important. 
In this project we included partner organizations from different countries. Each group was made up of 4 participants, aged 16-24 and one leader (together five participants).
Our goal was to connect different stories (with different backgrounds) together in one single film. Each group had to write their own script, and present it to all the participants on the mid-term meeting. Participants filmed the stories in their countries. In the final of the project, all individual films from each group were edited together in one, united creation, which displayed different subjects, such as discrimination, poverty, active citizenship, European citizenship etc. Every month at the time of the project, groups were informed with instructions and informations from the leader of the hosting group, summarized in one minute long videos. Each participating group had to give the feedback to others (with 1min long videos) about what were they doing (regarding the project). 
During the project we had three meetings in different countries. Topic of the first meeting was creating the plan of collaboration between groups during the project, discussion and workshops about media literacy as well as writing the screenplay. At the second meeting, we finished the scripts, evaluated our work and prepared for actualization-filming of the written screenplays. The topic of the last meeting was finishing the film, presentation of the film (premiere in Belgrade) and final evaluation. During our meetings we also organized workshops where the youngsters worked on different fields of media production (depended on the topic during meetings, for example: writing screenplay, filming, editing and post-production, etc.), so through the whole project youngsters learned and acquired competences from media literacy.
With this project we wanted to make an effect on the thinking of majority on the connections of people living on our planet, not knowing about each other, but still being connected no matter in which country they live and their cultural differences. 
Regarding long term effect we would like to point out that this project is just the beginning of strategic partnership between youngsters in different countries. Now, as the project is finished, our connections still live on and while developing, gaining also others, less experienced groups of youngsters with the same thinking and will to learn, so we can share example of good practice with them.

2014-2-DE04-KA205-001398.title: Build your future
2014-2-DE04-KA205-001398.summary:
The Build Your Future Project 2015-2017 was designed to promote the take-up of practical entrepreneurial experiences for young people with fewer opportunities: project’s target group which deserves attention in the context of youth unemployment in Europe. The objectives were to equip young people with skills and attitudes necessary to develop their entrepreneurial mindset; strengthen their employability skills to be better prepared for the employment, self-employment or further education; and to foster cooperation among civil society and policy stakeholders on sustainable support structures and policies for local entrepreneurship.
The project was implemented by the Consortium of 9 Partners from Croatia, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Slovakia, Spain and the UK: experts in youth work and non-formal education. It started with the research of the local context and young people’s needs. Other project activities included the Training of Trainers for youth workers, international blended mobility learning event for young people, online learning and exchange, the Entrepreneurship Labs, the Build Your Future Challenge, partners’ meetings and the Multiplier Events. Main results and impact:
-       The Entrepreneurship Education Course of 5 Modules became an innovative practice-oriented learning tool for young people with fewer opportunities to study entrepreneurship and social entrepreneurship.
-       The Course Material is available in 6 languages: English, German, Croatian, Italian, Slovak and Hungarian.
-       160 young people were selected in Ireland, Italy, Germany, Slovakia, Romania, Croatia and the UK to participate in the project, incl. 75% of young people with fewer opportunities; 113 people graduated.
-      The motivation of young people increased significantly for their current school studies in all countries. Graduates from the Dublin group became the leaders for the Build Your Future-2 in Dublin; 60 project ideas were developed by young people in Croatia.
-       20 youth workers in 7 countries became trainers and mentors to young people.
-      4 international meetings among 134 project participants led to an intensive exchange of experience and learning
-      1.500 EUR were raised for the Build Your Future Challenge to support entrepreneurial ideas of young people. 3 projects out of 7 were awarded the start-up grants
-      401 people attended 10 Multiplier Events in 7 countries.
-      45 Entrepreneurship Labs were organised in 7 countries for 745 participants with over 50 guest speakers and will continue.  
-      The Build Your Future project is set and funded for the 2nd phase in Ireland, UK and Italy.
-      Local municipalities granted their support to the project.
-      11 young people from Italy, Slovakia, Romania and Croatia set up their business.
-      The Evaluation Report with the lessons learnt is available for public use
-      The Course became the working tool to promote participation of young people with fewer opportunities and contributed to youth empowerment on a European scale.

2014-2-FR02-KA205-009192.title: UNEXPRESSED TALENT
2014-2-FR02-KA205-009192.summary:
UNEXPRESSED TALENT (UT)contributes to reduce the phenomenon of social and educational exclusion of young people (14-24 y.o.) by means of their active participation in civil society and increased personal accountability. Literature points out that one of the main indicators of uneasiness, often resulting in school dropout, is linked to an insufficient level of social inclusion and a scarce participation in democratic life as well as a general lack of the so called soft skills allowing young people to make the most proper decisions about their personal and professional life. 
The main problems identified at the beginning of the project, are: 1. Lack of a structured analysis on formal and non-formal education organizations: a scientific-based analysis in order to understand the origins of young people uneasiness and to recognize the alerts of such risks; 2. De-motivation of young people: the high percentage of young NEET is often caused by a lack of coordinated strategies aimed at intercepting, motivating and giving them the confidence and hope in the future; 3. Unexpressed talent: young people in discomfort situation often possess capabilities and a social capital which are not properly exploited by the formal education system or in the environment they live in. 
Such reasoning has led the partners to identify 3 specific objectives: 1. To conduct an analysis in formal and not formal education agencies to determine the phenomenon according to quantitative and qualitative indicators; 2. To motivate young people involving schools, municipalities, associations and project stakeholders to jointly face problems and target common solutions; 3. To connect formal and non-formal education agencies for the purpose of improving both systems. 
In this regard, UT has tackled social uneasiness of young people in difficulty by developing a model of inclusion in active citizenship (CSOs, etc.) by fostering transversal skills and empowering youths by becoming more aware of their unexpressed talents. Such empowerment actions, matched with commitment in civil society dynamics helped better level of integration both at educational and, if relevant employment. 
Led by a European network specialized in training and inclusion of people at risk, TANDEM PLUS (FR), the partnership is made up by diverse but complementary partners, covering 7 different countries (BE, FR, ES, PT, IT, SI, HR) bringing together nine partners whose expertise ranges to different topics as: non-formal education, tools for vulnerable people,  effective transversal skills assessment, scientific research on social issues, compared social analysis, development and test of tools with social impact, services to vulnerable groups as migrants and foreign students, social inclusion. 
Starting with a research phase, the project has provided inputs for development of different strategies for talent appreciation, and has developed a user-friendly assessment tool targeted to teachers, families and youngsters to identify their specific kind of uneasiness or exclusion risk. Following the preliminary research and alert tool, the partner developed a multidimensional model (output4):  expressing talents. In the rationale of the project, this entails a 6-step comprehensive path, made up by a set of methods and tools that aim at creating links between formal and non-formal education stakeholders to support the empowerment of youth, especially for young people between 15 and 25 years of age, to foster autonomy and self-recognition of skills to make talents easily emerge and consequently build strategies to express and promote them with enhances awareness of the wider context in which they live and with the support of a more structured collaboration of territorial organisations. 
The model has been the result of codification and evaluation of tools such as “Unexpressed toolkit- IO 3” and “alert tools – IO 2” that has been tested first with educators and operators of formal and non-formal education during a Joint Staff training week in Madrid and then, after finalization, tested on about 200 youths in each of the 7 countries. The evaluation of the model and its tools (IO 5) has shown that the partners have increased their organizational skills and network at both local level (especially with schools and other local CSOs) and learned and benefited a lot by the transnational cooperation to improve staff skills and methods to be applied to their ordinary work with youth, which will have a positive impact on future work. The evaluation also highlights the overall positive impact on the youths involved in the pilot experimentation of the model, with achievement of the target numbers and increased awareness of talents. The final recommendations, which embed lessons from the experience, provide guidance for further actions for different stakeholders. The recommendations represent a roadmap for further work in the field.

2014-2-HR01-KA205-012522.title: Better Strategies for Youth, Youth for Better Strategies
2014-2-HR01-KA205-012522.summary:
The proposal for this project was derived from MMH’s advocacy practice, as well as from information collected through international cooperation with other national youth councils (NYCs) gathered in the largest European platform of youth organisations - the European Youth Forum (YFJ). Therefore, this project reflected an action that aimed to respond on real needs detected in the youth sector Europe-wide, as it also presented a genuine base for a long-term strategic partnership which have ensured the exchange of practices among youth, research organisations and institutions involved in the project.

The aim of the project was to initiate and develop the advocacy agenda on necessity of developing quality assurance standards of national strategic and programme documents in the field of youth. Youth organisations gathered in this partnership, with the support of the research partners, did tend to advocate together their findings and joint possitions at the EU level, but also in each of their national contexts. With joint advocacy efforts of the Better Strategies project team and the Expert group on Youth Policy (established by the YFJ, for the first time), they have contributed to more effective youth policies at the European and national level, which was an overall idea behind this project. By engaging NYCs from seven (in this project, and within YFJ even more) EU countries in this advocacy process at the EU level - organisations which represent thousands of young people all over the EU - this strategic partnership have directly influenced stimulating the active participation of young people in the EU policy making, as it provides a solid basis for further development. 

Project was implemented through these activities: (1) Mapping of key issues in developing and implementing youth policy strategic documents from perspective of NYCs; (2) NYC capacity building training, which have provided necessary skills and knowledge for project partners; (3) development of advocacy tool which represented recommendations towards more successful youth policy (and was communicated and advocated towards relevant stakeholders), including the inputs provided to the Resolution on youth policy standards (adopted at the Spring COMEM 2016); (4) consultations with national bodies in charge of youth, which were used to collect opinions on the recommendations stated in the advocacy paper and to secure the support of the national bodies in later stages of the process (when concrete recommendations will be implemented, especially concerning developing the next long-term youth strategy); (5) advocacy process towards the YFJ (which started its development during the capacity building training, and was done through presentations, dissemination of the project results, etc.) and which did resulted in including some of the key findings from the project in specific resolutions; (6) Follow-up meeting which served for making a proper systematic evaluation of the project and planning future actions/steps which can be organized to successfully continue efforts towards proper and relevant youth policy. 

Two major results were achieved by implementation of activities specified above: (R1) developed advocacy agenda on quality assurance standards of national strategic and programme documents in the field of youth which was adopted and advocated (and still going on) within a large platform of youth organisations (YFJ); (R2) capacities of national youth councils from the EU partner countries are strengthened and their representatives are now feeling more educated and encouraged in creating and monitoring their concrete national strategic and programme documents in the field of youth, with more active engagement of their respective NYCs. Project results, findings and advocacy efforts were done towards three main target groups: member organisations of the YFJ, representatives of the national bodies in charge of youth policy (inside partner countries), but also  representatives in the EU and Council of Europe bodies in charge of youth.

The project has strengthened and empowered representatives of the project partner organisations, as it generally has raised awareness of other YFJ member organisation on the necessity of youth advocacy within the area of policy development. Project has also raised the awareness of the representatives of bodies in charge of youth policy development on both levels (those on national and those on EU) on the necessity of more effective youth policy (but also monitoring the results). This project's work, together with the advocacy efforts of the YFJ, did surely reactivate the youth policy topic at the European level after long time and it has a potential to provide some positive changes through clear recommendations dealing with youth strategic documents.

2014-2-PT02-KA205-002021.title: Rede de Facilitadores Inclusão Pelo Desporto
2014-2-PT02-KA205-002021.summary:
The Facilitators’ network aims to be a programme that promotes the social and educational function of sport. On this basis, we intend to create the FIT2FIT campaign. This is a transnational project organised by IUNA in partnership with several organisations interested in promoting sport as a means for professional and personal growth and the civic participation of young people by means of training young university students to create social entrepreneurship projects.

The title of the campaign is a pun on the word "Fit" which in English has two meanings "Fit” as in keeping "Fit" and “fitting in”. Within this context it conveys 2 messages: 1) promotion of healthy lifestyle habits and, 2) the need for inclusion within society. It reminds us of the idea that through sport it is possible to “fit in” or include young people in society.

Sport must be seen as much more than just physical activity. As non-formal education it can help young people to develop healthy lifestyles and also teach valuable life skills and help in the process of personal and professional development. This is particularly true for young people from disadvantaged backgrounds.

For these reasons the FIT2FIT campaign will be created. It offers 16 young people aged between 18 and 25 pedagogical training, professional preparation and education in leadership and business skills using the topic of inclusion through sport. At the end of the training, the young people will be integrated into a Group of Facilitators who will facilitate the construction of social and sports entrepreneurship which will be part of the FIT2FIT campaign. The facilitators will act as multipliers at 9 Portuguese, Italian and Croatian higher education institutions. The purpose of the organisation of 8 seminars is to train around 240 young volunteers who are invited to gain organisational and social entrepreneurship competencies which will lead to the implementation of at least 20 new educational and social sport projects aimed at 3000 young people at social risk.

By promoting the multiplication and civic participation of young facilitators and young volunteers using a sustainable business model, we believe we are promoting the employment and inclusion of young people on the job market and at the same time, involving them in the resolution of social and educational issues via the use of the practice of inclusive sport for young people at social risk.

New learning and teaching methods and approaches
