2019-1-PT02-KA205-005995.title: STARTING UP - Accelerators Of Entrepreneurship 4 Inclusion
2019-1-PT02-KA205-005995.summary:
<< Background >>

This project is aimed at young people with intellectual and developmental difficulties (IDD) with a degree of incapacity up to 60%. This target has not had opportunities to continue studies or to enter the labour market.

In 2018, the first HEI course for young people with IDDs (bit.ly/3a3WgZD) started in Portugal (Polytechnic Institute of Santarém), an initiative that has mobilized civil society, the business world and the police makers themselves for this problem, and which needs to be further developed, not only in PT but in all EU.

The PT Government recently approved and published a law (nº4/2019) regarding minimum number of employees with disabilities in companies with more than 75 employees. This actually comes into force in the month of the project submission.

Mainly with non-formal methodologies it was intended to develop tools and competences in youth with IDD for inclusion in labour market, both as employees and as self-employed entrepreneurs with innovation and social concern.

The relevance of the project matches with OECD reports, and the increased value of practitioners and institutions were not yet contributing consistently to innovation and productivity growth within the priority areas of social and labour inclusion.

<< Objectives >>

O1 -  To design a flexible and adapted model of teaching and learning activities using mostly non-formal methodologies with concerns regarding gender and ethics issues. This must have multidisciplinary didactic and educational resources capable of reinforcing or developing soft skills and fostering equity in work contexts.
O2 - To enhance young people with disabilities and their tutors skills according to the priorities set out for youth and in order to answer to the needs of the working contexts of the digital society.
O3 - To develop practices in the context of "real" work that meet the challenges of innovation and respect the basic principles of data protection, open source and security.

2019-2-HR01-KA205-061028.title: Stop child abuse ThrOugh effective training and augmented reality
2019-2-HR01-KA205-061028.summary:
<< Background >>

Sexual abuse of children occurs far more often than previously acknowledged. Children are vulnerable and often ashamed and afraid to report any incidents. As a result, this form of abuse is the hardest to detect, and it has many harmful effects on children and youth. International studies (Barth et al.) reveal that approximately 20% of women and between 5 -10 % of men, report having been victim of sexual violence as children. This phenomenon is not decreasing, and certain forms of sexual violence are becoming a matter of growing concern. Fighting these crimes is very difficult. The Internet makes it easier to “groom” children (solicit children online for sexual purposes) or to produce and distribute child pornography” (EU Commission, Child Sexual Abuse, 2016). The project ‘STOP - STOP Child Abuse Through Effective Training and Augmented Reality’ aimed to provide an innovative answer to the adverse childhood experiences that affect children and youth in Europe.

<< Objectives >>

The project ‘STOP - STOP Child Abuse Through Effective Training and Augmented Reality’aimed to contribute to the prevention and combating of sexual abuse and exploitation of children and youth (9-18 years old), through the creation of an innovative learning methodology, and more specifically the provision of new approaches and tools to youth workers to create innovative training programs on the aforementioned topic. 
When working on the prevention of sexual abuse and protection of children and young people, due to the sensitivity of this topic, youth workers often need additional knowledge, skills and innovative tools to ensure that they will provide protection. Through the STOP project we wanted to provide new approaches and tools to youth workers based on AR game to fight child adverse experience and to empower youth workers to teach children how to respond to suspected abuse and to enhance the youth workers into child `and youth protectors from violence and abuse. 
Also, through the STOP project we wanted to raise awareness about the issue of child sexual abuse and to exchange good practices in this topic among the partner countries.

<< Implementation >>

The project ‘STOP - STOP Child Abuse Through Effective Training and Augmented Reality’ was implemented through the following activities:
-Comparative analysis of the current situation in five European countries, Greece, Cyprus, Italy, Croatia and Spain reviewing legal framework, relevant statistics, key stakeholders and good 
practices dealing with child sexual abuse.
-Focus Group with Youth Workers and Educators to identify their needs 
-Interviews with parents to identify their needs
-An online short-term joint training activity for youth workers and educators focused on project results. 
-An internal and external pilot testing with youth workers, parents, educators and psychologists.
-Online Seminars through the project’s Facebook page on topics related to child sexual abuse.

<< Results >>

The project ‘STOP - STOP Child Abuse Through Effective Training and Augmented Reality’aimed to contribute to the prevention and combating of sexual abuse and exploitation of children and youth. 
To achieve that goal, the following outputs have been developed in the context of the project: A training plan that defines the desired learning outcomes, learning material and an Augmented Reality game with the guidelines for the application of the STOP model.
Outputs:
National Reports consisting of desk research, focus group and interviews results from parents and youth workers. 
Comparative Report with the results from all the partner countries.
STOP Framework – Identifying the topics and learning outcomes – setting the basis for the training material. 
Training Material for Youth Workers
An innovative AR Game for Youth Workers to improve their practices
Guidelines for the application of the STOP Model
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Quality and innovation of youth work

2019-2-HR01-KA205-061076.title: Innovate debate: applied curriculum for debate based youth work
2019-2-HR01-KA205-061076.summary:
<< Background >>

We considered that the rise of populism and political apathy or undermined notions of equality and inclusion, our work has to fill the gap left by formal education and emphasize critical thinking and communication skills while providing a foundation for civic engagement, appreciation of democratic principles, equality and inclusion. Needs analysis of debate practitioners showed that they lack structured, high-quality content that would be freely available and enable a standardised approach to debate-based youth work, running of debate-based youth clubs or implementation of debate methodology in education.

<< Objectives >>

We wanted to create a comprehensive set of tools available to anyone willing to use the debate-based methodology to develop transferable skills for young people. At the same time, we wanted to increase the availability of debate-based youth work, move it into the digital realm and increase its quality., especially the ability to recruit and train new volunteers.
.

<< Implementation >>

We organised work with young people using problem-based learning (PBL) as a student-centred teaching method in which young people learn by actively exploring real-world problems. Using this method we organised 20 youth debate clubs as training, development and testing hubs that worked on this project for 36 months.  This enabled us to work with young people in developing 4 key outputs of the project. Curriculum, online education resource, Elearning platform and an impact study. Development of those outputs was supported by 2 LTT events and a dozen of multiplier activities, online and in real life.

<< Results >>

We created:

Applied debate curriculum - Seventy ready-to-use lesson plans with instructions on how to use them and supporting documentation. Lessons are organised in 4 different curriculum proposals ranging from 3 months to 2 years of activities. (available on resourcebase.idebate.net)

learningbase.idebate.net - E-learning portal with 65 individual lessons arranged in 12 courses
resourcebase.idebate.net - An online educational resource that provides easy access to developed resources, manuals, training plans, quality standards and supporting content 
Including:
Volunteering in debate-based youth work – recruitment, onboarding, training and retention manual
Debate clubs and youth participation manual – connecting debate work with European active citizenship framework and youth goals
Debate clubs in the community – a guide on integrating debate clubs in communities, making them become a place for change
Train the educator's manual and lesson plans

All these materials were developed by participants, volunteers and staff of the IDAC project.

motionbase.idebate.net - An online educational resource that provides educators with a list of topics they could use in their debate-based youth work

We reached over 4000 young people and disseminated project results in more than 20 countries that are adapting and using these outputs.

2019-2-HR01-KA205-061082.title: THOR - The Heart Of Reflection
2019-2-HR01-KA205-061082.summary:
A consortium build by an NGO, a cooperative and a social company from Croatia and Portugal have engaged together in this 16 month project focusing on developing 3 IOs with the focus on ‘reflecting and debriefing’ in all the different spheres the young people are active within: youth work, education, families, peer groups and individual level. The 3 IOs are distinctly focusing on 1) individual reflection set, 2) small groups and peer reflection set and 3) big groups reflection set. Each IO stands on itself, yet they are all interlinked in order to create the opportunity and possibility to easily transfer them to the different realities the young people find themselves in. The different IOs will follow therefore also the same philosophy, a similar structure and a consistent visual (attractive) look.
The development of these IOs is based on a previous internal defined need, a need consecutively confirmed through an international questionnaire.
The different IOs aim to reach on short, medium and long term:
The creation and development of intellectual outputs that will support the facilitation of reflection activities for young people and “youth workers”.
The promotion of a culture of reflection as a key element in learning and to develop tools that support the development of that habit and culture.
The sharing of these youth work experiences into other sectors that also support young people, like teachers, parents and peers.
The creation and implementation of a training activity that will develop competences on reflection methods and use of the tools produced.
Having more efficient tools to create empowerment processes with the young people, first within our own realities, and secondly on a much wider context (regional, national and international)
Besides targeting in the first place young people (with a particular focus towards young people with fewer opportunities), this project intends to have concrete impact in all the different spheres the young people engage within, and consequently therefore also includes the stakeholders within these different spheres (e.g. youth workers, peers, educators, teachers and parents).
Each of the planned IOs consists of 3 dimensions: a reflection tool, a facilitators’ manual and a vídeo tutorial. These 3 dimension complete each IO, but can be used as well separately. The multidimensional aspect serves to increase the user-friendly aspect and aims hereby to increase the future use and impact.
All the outputs will be freely available and possible to download online in different languages. English, Croatian and Portuguese versions at start, with a prediction of future translation to happen still during and after the project.
The project lasts 16 months and contains 3 international Partner Meetings, 1 Training Course (20 participants-future multiplyers) and several Multiplyer Events (reaching minimum 90 stakeholders). The whole project is based upon the principles of non formal education (e.g. self-directed, participative, self-assessment, etc).
The consortium composition is based upon complementary competences: combining game-based learning, design-thinking methodology, digital tools and grass root fieldwork. The different involved partners have build up extensive experience in local, national and international youth work and education, hereby benefitting the mutual strengths. The IOs will be developed progressively, based upon an ongoing process of in depth testing with the variety of stakeholders involved (minimum 300 participants, with minimum 155 young people with fewer opportunities involved).
The expected impact is the creation of a regular accepted habit of reflection and (self) debriefing on individual level, small group and peer level and bigger groups. This not only within the youth work sector, but also in the wider youth field and involving a multiple dimension of involved stakeholders, e.g. youth worker, young people, educators, teachers, family.

2019-2-IT03-KA205-016467.title: Escape from Marginalisation
2019-2-IT03-KA205-016467.summary:
Most of the today approach of youth workers in establishing a contact with youngsters many times is ineffective because the methodologies to attract the youngsters’ attention and interest are outdated. Youth workers struggle in finding contacts and moment of dialogue with youngsters because they use tools that are too far from the daily life of teenagers today, who spend most of the free time online.
Gaming and social networks are some of the most common hobbies for youngsters and can be considered as a passive activity. Or, from other perspective, the youngster in that moment can be described as an active contributor to an activity or a common project in a game platform or as a moderator in a chat.
The forms of establishing and maintaining communication have undergone fundamental changes. ICT-aided solutions are playing an ever-greater role, replacing interpersonal communication. 
Many times, youngsters discover most part of opportunities for their free time online and that’s why they don’t get usually in touch with youth centre and youth workers. Even if youngsters show a big confidence in using online tools they are still not educated in using these tools with full awareness. 

This project responds to the needs of our youngsters (mainstream and marginalised) and youth workers, as well as is in line with the latest findings on European level that there is a need for innovative youth work approach towards youngsters that spend a lot of their time online and do not visit (local) youth centres and youth clubs so much, any more.

With this project, we aim at further empowering our youth workers in innovative usage of digitalisation and gamification methodology in regular work with marginalised youngsters in our communities, in order to increase attractiveness of the youth work activities and make them up-to-date for better impact on inclusion and engagement of both mainstream and marginalised youngsters.

Project objectives:
•	Empower youth workers with knowledge and skills to implement digital tools in their everyday activities, with special focus on inclusion.
•	Empower youth workers and improve knowledge management of youth work organisations in theory and practice for building competences of youth workers in Gamification and adventure/escape room methodology in online and offline youth work for inclusion.
•	Encourage more youth workers for organising creative and innovative digital tools and youth work activities with gamification methodology based on affordable, low-cost and efficient adventure/escape rooms among mainstream and marginalised youngsters in our communities.
•	Attract more youngsters to our youth work activities by multiplying the innovative low-cost and efficient escape rooms against marginalisation in our communities, and thus increase inclusion among youngsters.

We expect following direct participants / beneficiaries of our project: 
-	8 staff / project managers and assistants; 
-	12 teachers/trainers/researchers and technicians working on the intellectual outputs; 
-	20 multipliers youth workers that will test the outputs with at least 80 youngsters (with fewer opportunities) on local level
-	60 participants of the multiplier events’ conferences, with at least 100 youngsters participating at low-cost escape rooms at the multipliers’ events 

Project activities:
A1 – Project Management
M1 – Kick-off meeting
O1 – E-learning course “Digitalisation of youth work for inclusion”
M2 – Second meeting
O2 – Toolkit “Gamification and Escape room methodology in online and offline youth work for inclusion”
M3 – Third meeting
E1, E2, E3, E4 – Open conferences in SE, HR, IT, DE
M4 – Evaluation meeting

Project will directly impact organisational capacities. We expect the positive and long-lasting effects on partner organisations who will increase their capacity and competences for providing quality youth work activities for inclusion based on innovative approach with using digitalisation, gamification and escape rooms methodology in their online and offline youth work with beneficiaries.
With our intellectual outputs, we will influence the change and improvement of existing inclusion youth work / NFE methodologies and programmes, at first among partner organisations of the project, and later among partner of ours and their wider network of collaborators.

Marginalised youth in communities will benefit from the enlarged support tools and mechanisms in their communities from youth workers. There will be more online, as well as offline opportunities of support and direct mentorship of youngsters by now digitalised youth workers.
As a long-term impact, on local and national level, we expect increase of soft skills, critical thinking, active citizenship and inclusion competences of mainstream and fewer opportunities youth. Thus, more youngsters will contribute to building society of inclusive community of active citizens.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Quality and innovation of youth work

2019-2-IT03-KA205-016700.title: Living Land
2019-2-IT03-KA205-016700.summary:
<< Background >>

The lack of prospects for young people in the job market was a serious problem in large parts of the EU; Corona Virus and other emergencies that occurred in our territories in the last two years made it even worst. Before we started to think about the project, we found that the highest unemployment rates were in the south of Europe. In Portugal, Italy and Croatia (three of the countries partners), a little more than one in three people in this age group were out of work. But there wasn’t a unique strategy, not at European neither at local level, and each government and NPO were answering differently to the problem, in order to promote youth inclusion and to reduce the unemployment of young people. That’s why Living Land wanted to create a model based on the comparison between different EU countries, linking PAs and NPOs that were investing on youngsters through traineeships and citizenship activities. We were witnessing the progressive aging of voluntary associations, which were no longer able to attract young people, and a constant disinvestment of young people with respect to participation in community life (parties, trade union organizations).

<< Objectives >>

The goal of the project was to support and enhance skills and competences of youth through both link and cooperation between social and youth workers(in NGOs and PA).The project aimed at promoting quality socio-educational activities,which could help the inclusion of youngsters both in conditions of structural fragility and in a position of temporary disorientation or vulnerability,with respect to their own training, project life and professional aims.This meas offering assistance to those who work directly with them, improving and building their capacities.Therefore, there was a need to extend the knowledge gathered and connect the gap between professional,activist and field work where needed,whether that be lack of cooperation, lack of information or access.Youth operators’ work is primarily important in the development of transversal, social and civil skills in the youngsters.That’s why LL was born with the aim of creating a toolkit that could give operational and methodological support to those workers.This methodological value derives from a common work that included a range of EU countries capable of providing the operator with a fairly complete picture of experiences,good practices and also operational suggestions and tools

<< Implementation >>

-Project Management and implementation: administration and budgeting, dissemination activities (using social networks, emails and newsletters, publishing the infos on our websites),monitoring and evaluation(before it:design of the QEP’s structure and content); recurrent online meetings;monitoring and evaluation
-Research:desktop research and analysis of results, design of questionnaires (semi structured and online), interviews and their analysis; design of an online questionnaire (google form); production of the IO1
-Creation of a visibility package (common logo, layout and a promotional video), of a project web site (IO2), that provides access to updates, information, materials and events related to project’s activities, as well as information about partner. Moreover, each partner organised meetings within our organisations (internal dissemination) and with our networks of entities (external dissemination)
-Transnational project meetings: 1) Poland,oct ’19; 2) Online,oct ’20; 3) Faro,oct ’21; 4) Amsterdam,Jun ’22
-Learning and training activity, hosted by Consorzio Consolida in Lecco, Jun ’22

<< Results >>

As concrete outputs,we realised a document that collects information about NEET situation in EU and some best practice approaches and activities aimed to be used with the young people, especially vulnerable ones,in order to prevent social exclusion and NEET conditions.As a tool for training,it contains concrete example and information about youth employability strategies and also a collection of methodologies that appear to be functional to the engagement, taking charge and development of youth NEET about its treatment and prevention.The GL help to raise awareness about non formal strategies carried out locally to be reinforced and transposed from one country to another.The LL platform(https://livinglandproject.eu)wants to give evidence both to the guidelines’ content and results, as well as to operative toolkits.A range of opportunities existing at local and EU level for youth and youth workers are contained there.The kit aims to develop youth workers’ expertise giving them technical and professional tools, and promotes young participation and citizenship, as well as remotivation and acquisition of transversal skills.It also gives some indications about the quality of the traineeship/apprenticeship offered in the young strategies

2019-2-IT03-KA205-016787.title: Co(YOUTH)working - A model to promote social impact and sustainability among coworking spaces and networks at local level
2019-2-IT03-KA205-016787.summary:
<< Background >>

Quanto gli spazi di coworking contribuiscono davvero allo sviluppo di competenze, all'inclusione sociale e lavorativa dei giovani? Quanto e come riescono a promuovere solidarietà, protagonismo, coinvolgimento e partecipazione giovanile? Quali sono i fattori che potrebbero migliorare l'efficacia dell'azione promossa da questi “nuovi spazi” per i giovani?
In coworking più orientati al business, il gestore spesso relega la funzione sociale ad azione di contorno e/o marketing basato sulla CSR (responsabilità sociale di impresa). Le figure scelte per gestire spazio, iniziative e progetti sono magari molto specializzate sui nuovi trend del mercato del lavoro ma con poca esperienza e capacità di connettersi con il tessuto sociale.
In coworking invece più orientati all’innovazione sociale, il gestore utilizza al contrario elementi business quasi solo per ottenere una sorta di patente di qualità. Le figure scelte per gestire spazio, iniziative e progetti sono esperti dell’azione sociale e, tendenzialmente, più orientati a ricercare fonti di sostegno/finanziamento pubblico che a fare azione imprenditoriale.
Gli esempi e le sperimentazioni di successo dimostrano che l’interazione tra gli abitanti dello “spazio di coworking” non può essere lasciata al caso, ma sono necessari metodi e strumenti per favorire interazioni e sinergie tra che lo vive: l'animazione deve essere indotta.
L'idea progettuale di CoYOUTHworking è nata dalla volontà di permettere agli spazi di coworking di avere un rilevante impatto sociale sul territorio di riferimento, essere un servizio economicamente sostenibile e sostenere lo sviluppo effettivo delle competenze imprenditoriali dei giovani utenti che ospitano. I promotori hanno puntato ad aprire i coworking mettendoli in una relazione di dialogo costante sia con i giovani che li vivono, sia con i soggetti esterni appartenenti alla comunità locale, alimentando un virtuoso processo di partecipazione, cittadinanza attiva e sviluppo del capitale umano e sociale del territorio.

<< Objectives >>

Gli obiettivi di CoYOUTHworking sono stati:
1. delineare il ruolo dello youth worker come figura chiave per la gestione di uno spazio di coworking, individuando le competenze necessarie, valorizzando le azioni e l’approccio animativo per supportare da un lato i giovani imprenditori e le nuove startup, dall'altro lo sviluppo delle comunità locali;
2. proporre una guida utile alle organizzazioni che vogliono aprire uno spazio di coworking (o innovare quello già esistente), che sia la sintesi delle esperienze dei partner: una raccolta di raccomandazioni, strumenti, attività, possibili risorse e rischi (ed eventuali soluzioni);
3. valorizzare il ruolo e il coinvolgimento di enti pubblici e delle reti locali nella gestione degli spazi di coworking, in modo tale da facilitare il dialogo tra gli stakeholder, fornire una visione più ampia della società in cui sono inseriti, monitorare la continuità dei processi, la coerenza e impatto a lungo termine sui territori;
4. elaborare una strategia cross-settoriale di gestione dei coworking che combini l'attenzione al “social impact” e il sostegno allo sviluppo delle startup presenti al loro interno, che coinvolga le realtà per la formazione e lo sviluppo delle competenze.

<< Implementation >>

Le attività principali hanno riguardato:
1. Tre “Project management meeting” (due in Italia, il terzo online) per facilitare il coordinamento del progetto e l’allineamento delle organizzazioni sulle diverse attività.
2. Ricerca e raccolta dati a livello locale, in ogni Paese partner, sulle caratteristiche degli spazi di coworking, oltre che sui bisogni e aspettative dei giovani; i risultati di tali indagini hanno contribuito a delineare i contenuti dei tre output di progetto.
3. Quattro “Work Group meeting” (uno in ogni Paese partner) per l’impostazione dei tre output, la sintesi e condivisione dei risultati del lavoro svolto singolarmente dalle organizzazioni, oltre che per lo svolgimento di study-visit a luoghi di interesse nell’ambito degli spazi di lavoro condiviso; tra un meeting e l’altro, sono state previste sessioni di lavoro online.
4. Eventi di promozione dei risultati in ogni Paese partner.

<< Results >>

Gli output di progetto sono rappresentati da:
1. Un modello strategico-organizzativo per gli spazi di coworking, che permette di combinare partecipazione attiva dei giovani, impatto sociale e promozione dell’imprenditoria giovanile all’interno (e all’esterno) del coworking stesso. 
2. Un modello di competenze per gli operatori degli spazi di coworking, ispirato dal modello ETS - A competence model for youth workers who work internationally e quindi basate sull’approccio proprio dello youth work. Oltre ad elencare le competenze utili che dovrebbero essere acquisite e/o rafforzate, il modello contiene la descrizione di attività animative all’interno delle quali tali competenze possono essere messe in pratica.
3. Un sito internet interattivo, contenente tutti gli output di progetto scaricabili gratuitamente, oltre a un questionario che permette agli operatori e gestori di spazi di coworking di confrontare la propria impostazione con i modelli elaborati dai promotori di CoYOUTHworking.
È stato infine prodotto e pubblicato un video riassuntivo del progetto, con una descrizione delle e suggerimenti e riflessioni principali, oltre a una presentazione dei partner e degli obiettivi del progetto.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2019-2-LU01-KA205-050124.title: Safe from Harm in Scouting
2019-2-LU01-KA205-050124.summary:
<< Background >>

In the recent past, the topic of child safeguarding and prevention has been increasing in importance in several youth organisations and therefore, also in the Scout Movement. Actions happened in the past or even more recent ones have been arising and that led our member organisations and our structures to put an emphasis to ensure that we offer a safe environment to children, young people and adults to live and experience Scouting. We applied for this project with the aim of boosting the work on the area of safeguarding and child and youth protection within the European Scout Region. 

Quickly was identified that national organisations had to put in place policies, procedures and guides to set the frame of the work on safe guarding, as well as train their adults in the application of those policies, in how to identify situations of risk and how to react in face of them. That was the basic need addressed by the project. Some of the partners in the project had nothing in place at the beginning of the project whereas others wanted to update their existing procedures.

The project was seen also as a spotlight for other Scout organisations to start or continue working in the area to make the Scouts a safer space for all our members.

<< Objectives >>

With this project, we wanted to:

- Develop and further implement national Safe from Harm policies and procedures based on the “World Safe from Harm policy” to ensure the “safe passage” of young people throughout their time in the Movement.
- ensuring that such policies and procedures are implemented in all the levels ot the organisation and in the totality of the activities by training the adult Leaders in the practical application of them.
- ensuring the Adult leaders are capable to identity situations of potential harm and be able to react to them.
- ensuring expert tailored support to the project partners and a space for international exchange of best practices
- ensuring a wider advocacy and support of child and youth protection in partnership with internal and external stakeholders


Preventing harmful situations, learning how to respond if a situation comes up and understanding that the federation is always there to support and accompany the scout in question were fundamental thoughts of our approach. By this we wanted to create a structure which gives FNEL the opportunity to be as englobing as possible in order to prevent, act or react in these kinds of situations. Safe from Harm should be present in all workstreams of the federation, events, training sessions and other program-based scout activities should be set up in respect of Safe From Harm guidelines.

<< Implementation >>

During the development of the project we have implemented several activities:

- 2 transnational project meetings, where the partners discussed and evaluated the progress of the project.
- 3 intellectual outputs that was the main weight of the project, with the development of 5 national Safe from harm policies and training materials for each of the national organisations partnering in the project and e-Learning modules to complement the training materials for in person sessions.
- 5 national Trainings on Safe from Harm (Multiplier Events) where the training materials developed were tested and received feedback from the participants.

<< Results >>

The project had the expected tangible outputs as well as some intangible results worth mentioning.

As tangible outputs the result of the development of the three intellectual outputs:

- National Safe from Harm policies and procedures for the 5 partners representing National Scout Associations within the European Scout Region (SLOVENSKY SKAUTING, SAVEZ IZVIDACA HRVATSKE, ZVEZA TABORNIKOV SLOVENIJE, FONDATION AGGL - FNEL, ORGANIZATIA NATIONALA CERCETASII ROMANIEI)
- Set of Safe from Harm training materials for Adult Youth Workers (Scout Leaders) to deliver on in-person training
- Safe from Harm e-Learning modules, to complement the in-person training.

Also, other results that were looked for and that are worth mentioning are the increased awareness in the associations participating in the project about the importance of the topic and the continuous work on the Safe from Harm topic and the already started capacity-building activities and training with Adults to ensure a safer environment for all in Scouting.

2019-2-LV02-KA205-002710.title: Upgrading entrepreneurship skills
2019-2-LV02-KA205-002710.summary:
<< Background >>

When we started to plan the project it was expected by statistics that at least 20% more jobs will require higher level skills. Education needs to drive up both standards and levels of achievement to match this demand, as well as encourage the transversal skills needed to ensure young people are able to be entrepreneurial and adapt to the increasingly inevitable changes in the labour market during their career. Later in 2020 the pandemic started, and it raised the need for quality soft skills training even more. Attention should be particularly focused on the development of entrepreneurial skills, because they not only contribute to new business creation but also to the employability of young people. 
The development of the entrepreneurial capacity of European citizens and organisations is also one of the key policy objectives for the EU and Member States. The main objective of the European Commission is to promote entrepreneurship education and stress its importance at all levels from primary school to university and beyond. As Europe needs more entrepreneurs creating jobs, it is clear it's necessary to support this type of education in all EU countries. Along with the Erasmus+ Program priorities, Project addresses various objectives of European Union: Europe 2020 headline target - Inclusive Growth Employment and Skills (EU flagship initiative "An agenda for new skills and jobs"), promoting entrepreneurship among young people as a key element of the European Youth Pact adopted by the European Council.
Nowadays young people drive the business environment, many start-ups are founded by young people. Entrepreneurship refers to an individual’s ability to turn ideas into action. To be successful at the market there should be a strong combination of soft and hard skills. The OECD has identified three main groups of skills required by entrepreneurs: technical, business management and personal entrepreneurship (for example, self-control and discipline, persistence, leadership). However, it is a wide belief that what you need to start a business is less about technical knowledge and more about having the right attitude.
By 2022 there is still no proper education or training programs for young people, which concentrates not on formal knowledge of the field, but on soft skills. So there is a strong need to teach young people not only how to technically launch entrepreneurship, but how to be an entrepreneur. Personal education and fostering a sense of initiative can be integrated in the school education system and also included in curriculum of universities in different faculties and study programs.

<< Objectives >>

The UPENSKILLS project aim was to identify and define essential soft skills for entrepreneurship and to produce a set of tools to be used as training materials in entrepreneurship related courses and programmes for cultivating entrepreneurial mindset of young people and promotion of youth entrepreneurship education. 
To achieve this aim the Project consisted of two main parts: identification and definition of essential skills for entrepreneurship, and production of a set of “training sheets'' on entrepreneurship skills and competencies to be used as training materials in entrepreneurship related courses and programmes. In order to contribute to the solution of the youth employment problems, the project UPENSKILLS aimed to facilitate the entry of young people to the labour market, encourage youth actively engage in entrepreneurship, through implementation of the following objectives:
- promoting entrepreneurship education in European Union and in partner countries; fostering recognition of entrepreneurship education and reinforcing a discussion about entrepreneurship competence training,
- making entrepreneurship education a basic feature in education systems;
- sharing of ideas, knowledge, experience, and best practices among countries, stakeholders, and practitioners;
- developing innovative instruments of non-formal education to contribute to development of entrepreneurial competences of young people

<< Implementation >>

Main activities and project tasks implemented in the UPENSKILLS project:
- identified and defined key competences and skills to be an entrepreneur;
- created a portrait of the successful entrepreneur;
- identified similarities and differences in the participant countries/regions;
- collected best cases/good practices on entrepreneurship training in non-formal education and produced portfolio of Good Practices;
- produced a flexible and adaptable set of methods (method cards) for entrepreneurship trainers based on previous soft skills demand identification to be added as a part of a course or as a programme itself;
- conducted international training course in Poland for youth workers to equip them with competences to work with the developed toolkit; 
- carried out a pilot testing of new toolkit for young people at national level in partner countries;
- organised two international multiplier events in Spain and Greece and disseminate results.
Main target groups addressed were both youth workers and young people.

<< Results >>

Two intellectual outputs are the most important results of the project.
1. First deliverable is research study "Entrepreneurship skills demand identification". Aim of the research was to identify and define essential entrepreneurial competences in accordance with needs and requirements of the market and feedback of entrepreneurs in order to create the ultimate list of soft skills necessary for young people to become entrepreneurs. The practical aim was to use the results of the research study to produce method cards on those defined skills. 
2. The second project output is Method cards of entrepreneurship skills and competences - a production of a flexible and adaptable set of methods (training sheets) for entrepreneurship trainers. It was made with the purpose of being added as a part of an already existing course or as used as a unified programme itself. One set of tools for entrepreneurship skills training consists of 14 working sheets in a folder with detailed description of an activity to be used both by trainers and trainees. Toolkit was designed in the way that any institution will be able to use it in their entrepreneurial skills raising activities for young people, both formal and non-formal curriculum. It provided added value to the output and made it innovative.
Project also have reached training goals and produced following outcomes and tangible results of the training activities:
1) 28 youth workers equipped with competences and skills - according to feedback by the end of the training course youth workers have developed the key competences (including sense of initiative and entrepreneurship, 8 Key Competences of LifeLong Learning) to a level that equips them to work with young people at professional level and understand the needs of their target group and successful entry to labour market; 
2) gained knowledge of participants on how to use innovative output - method cards, in the youth work and their entrepreneurship educational activities;
3) exchanged experience between participants and shared best practices of partner organisations, intercultural exchange.
In addition the capacity of all participating organisations was strengthened by taking part in the project, and they have increased interest in youth entrepreneurship topics.

2019-2-PT02-KA205-006015.title: Entrepreneurship & Youth Empowerment - Competence Based Development Programme for Social Inclusion and Employment
2019-2-PT02-KA205-006015.summary:
<< Background >>

The problem of social exclusion of young people and disintegration in the labor market arises as a consequence of the absence of key competencies for lifelong learning and entrepreneurial thinking and attitudes, which has severe and limiting effects: 
-Number of young people in social exclusion and disintegration;
-Number of young NEETs;
-Number of unemployed young people.
In a constantly evolving world, the disparities between young people is an ever-increasing reality. The lack of key competences for lifelong learning, entrepreneurial thinking and attitudes and orientation hinders the integration of young Europeans in the labor market and in society.
In order to minimize a number of situations allied to the difficulty of integration in precarious jobs and socially deviant behavior, we implemented this project in order to improve the scenario.
Our action has imposed the need for analysis in view of the difficulties we encounter when dealing with under-represented social groups such as ethnic minorities and migrants who face greater difficulties in social and professional insertion.

<< Objectives >>

1.Promote youth empowerment by developing key competences for lifelong learning and adopting entrepreneurial thoughts and attitudes;
2.Promote youth entrepreneurship, through the transfer of knowledge and methodologies, methods and tools for starting new businesses;
3.Promote the social inclusion of young people, including socially underrepresented groups (such as ethnic minorities and migrants), by creating opportunities and training for integration into the labor market;
4.Promote capacity building of social actors (such as YW, trainers, teachers, etc.) for social inclusion work and youth entrepreneurship;
5.Intensify the potentialities of the NFE methodology in the training and in the personal, social and professional development of young people;
6.To endow the educational institutions with comp. for the incorporation of complementary actions to formal ed. for the personal, social and professional development of young people;
7.Share existing good practices based on the intervention program for the development of key competencies for lifelong learning and adoption of entrepreneurial thoughts and attitudes that is the transition bridge between education and the labor market.

<< Implementation >>

ACTIVITIES AND NO. OF PARTICIPANTS

20 participants.

50 participants.

50 participants.

WB 11/2021.

20 participants.

METHODOLOGY

2019-2-SI02-KA205-015177.title: Youth Worker`s Network
2019-2-SI02-KA205-015177.summary:
<< Background >>

The majority of youth workers are devloped from an active group of young people who participate in various project activities or through the measures of an active employment policy. Both these youth workers and youth workers who have been workin for long time have developed their youth work skills using their own intuition and methodology picked up in various projects and trainings. Youth work in the participating countries does not have a developed educational program that would answer the question: "Why carry out an activity for young people?". Before the project, we did not have a set of literature that would comprehensively address youth work. The entire youth work is based on individual experiences which means that youth workers are only partially qualified to work with young people, and the sector does not have a suitable scientific basis  and consequently less power in political decisions. 

All these challenges were adressed by preparing basic training for youth workers. It enables for youth organizations to conduct training on the basics of youth work and youth workers to specialize professionally. Additionally, by preparing a draft collective agreement, we started the process of professionalizing youth work in Slovenia.

<< Objectives >>

By carrying out the project, we pursued the following project goals:

1. To provide foundations for youth work; theoretical definitions that are based on science and research and are essential basic knowledge of any professional working with young people.
2. Creation of a library of quality literature, which is created within the framework of the development of youth work and based on the needs of youth workers.
3. To offer future and existing youth workers a training program that presented the contents of the first purpose within a set of lectures that provide both basic knowledge and specialized knowledge and the opportunity for further reflection.
4. Develop an additional professional document that the Slovenian youth sector has needed for a long time, a draft collective agreement for the youth sector.

<< Implementation >>

We carried out the following act.: 

1. Regular project management activities. In addition to project meetings, the consortium regularly met and communicated online (regular Zoom meetings, email, Whatsapp).

2. International meetings: 
- Kick-off meeting in Ljubljana. 
- TPM1: project progress review, in Gothenburg.
- TPM2: Review of project progress and adaptations to challenges as a result of the Covid-19 epidemic in the online Zoom environment.
- Evaluation meetings: review of the performance of the implemented activities, final intellectual results and agreement on dissemination activities, in the Zoom online environment.

3. Training: 
- Basics of youth work, in Celje, under the name 'What is and what is not youth work?'.
- Participation and inclusion, in Zadar, under the name 'Participation and inclusion'.
- Informal learning, in Ljubljana, under the name 'To learn or not to learn that is the question'.
- Evaluation and follow-up, in Zagreb, under the name 'Did we make it or didn't we?'

4. Multiplication events:
- Multiplication event in Slovenia.
- Multiplication event in Croatia.
- Sharing content in regular activities in Sweden.

5. Regular communication about the project on the websites and social networks of partners.

<< Results >>

IO1: Guide for youth work, with collected theoretical foundations of YW..
IO2: Training program for youth workers. 
IO3: Draft collective agreement for the youth sector in Slovenia. The draft represents a further step in the field of professionalization of the youth sector in Slovenia.

The comprehensive training guide for professional and quality youth work is a combination of IO1 and IO2, as it combines the contents of both; 
- A library of key quality literature that was created in the context of the development of youth work and the foundations of youth work in the form of theoretical definitions. 
- A training program that combines these contents in a series of lectures that provide both basic and specialized knowledge and an opportunity for further reflection. 

In addition, the content is reinforced with video content, which ensures that the acquisition of the presented knowledge does not require the organization of entire sets of trainings, but that all knowledge is also accessible on an individual level, in one's own time and at the pace of acquiring knowledge. The accessibility of the guide is ensured by translation into all the partnership's languages ​​(Slovenian, Croatian, Swedish) and into English.

2019-2-SK02-KA205-002174.title: Volunteering as an Educational Opportunity
2019-2-SK02-KA205-002174.summary:
<< Background >>

In the project, we mainly responded to the need to connect education with practice, the need to develop key competencies and competencies for life in a democratic society, and the lower level of civic engagement in the countries of Central and Eastern Europe compared to countries with a developed culture of engagement. We have found that many young people could be a valuable source of active citizenship but either has not learned to be active and active proactively or are lost in the information boom they face today. Many organizations and youth workers see volunteering as an educational opportunity but do not take full advantage of its academic potential. Achieving a balance in volunteering between education and personal growth and development of the volunteer on the one hand and fulfilling the community's real needs is not always easy for local and international volunteers. Often there is a strong focus on solidarity service and meeting the needs of beneficiaries without articulated learning. However, the potential of service-learning, which allows responding to the mentioned needs and challenges, is still not sufficiently used in the CEE countries.

<< Objectives >>

The project's general goal was to increase youth's competencies and opportunities to participate in society fully. The project was based on the need to support the international dimension, motivate young people to engage, and, on the other hand, support youth workers in the development of key competencies, a sense of initiative, and civic participation of young people through one of the successful and globally widespread strategies - service learning. The specific goal of the project was:
• improve the quality and relevance of the education offered in the field of service learning strategy implementation in youth work through the development of curricula and related documents and manuals adapted to the context of Central and Eastern European countries;
• to increase the capacities of organizations and youth workers in introducing service learning into practice and its implementation possibilities in cooperation with local and international youth volunteers;
• increase the quality of work with youth, primarily in youth volunteering.

<< Implementation >>

The project's key activities consisted of the creation, testing, and dissemination of innovative outputs, which will be able to be used even after the end of the project. At the beginning of the project, the training of trainers in the service learning strategy and the survey of needs among youth workers were carried out. The evaluation of the project's outputs consisted of implementing service learning training for youth workers and the performance of service learning projects in youth work. Service learning is a strategy that combines service in the community with education, while the whole process is accompanied by deliberate reflection. After the training, male and female workers were selected in each country to be involved in the implementation of service learning projects. During the project, 15 service learning projects were implemented as part of testing, in which 112 young people collaborated with partners in the community. As part of the project, six multinational project meetings were held. The key dissemination activity was a two-day international conference held in Banská Bystrica.

<< Results >>

The main innovative outputs of the project are: IO1 Service learning strategy training for youth workers and a manual for trainers, IO2 Service learning in youth work. Manual for youth workers, IO3 Service learning projects. Manual for youth. IO4 FacilitationBOX for service learning. Outputs are available in English, Slovak, Croatian, Romanian, Polish, and Hungarian. All project outputs are accessible online on www.eduvol.eu. The main results of the project are:
- Development of a service learning strategy in the field of youth work,
- Development of the competencies of youth workers in the field of service learning strategy implementation aimed at strengthening volunteering and civic engagement,
- Development of social, civic, and intercultural competencies and democratic values ​​of young people and increased civic engagement of youth
- Increased awareness of the service learning strategy among various actors
The project had an impact not only on the participating organizations, young people, and youth workers but also on local communities.

2019-3-DE04-KA205-018829.title: Overcoming the limiting realities creatively: Sport methodology in youth work for inclusion
2019-3-DE04-KA205-018829.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for this project because in 2019 sport is an area of life in which people with disabilities arguably had less favourable experiences than their non-disabled peers and competitors. Typical barriers for people with disabilities to participate in sport include lacked of awareness on the part of people without disabilities as to how to involve them in teams adequately; lack of opportunities and programmes for training and competition; too few accessible facilities due to physical barriers.

The unique ability of sports to transcend linguistic, cultural and social barriers makes it an excellent platform for strategies of inclusion and adaptation. Through youth sport work and sports, persons without disabilities interact with persons with disabilities in a positive context forcing them to reshape assumptions about what can and cannot do.

NFE educators and youth workers/leaders working with this target group often had little or no experience in using sport as an educational tool. Many didn't not know how to maximise the potential of sport as a method within their regular youth work, despite of the fact that sport activities can be considered one of the most valuable NFE experiences for children and youngsters.

<< Objectives >>

Our project placed the above-mentioned needs and EU Guidelines/policies into action by developing new curricula and methods for empowering both youth (work) organisations, as well as the sport organisations - to increase their capacity building and human resources for quality envisioning and promoting the physical activity events (youth sport work and sport events) that thus contribute to increasing participation in quality sports by more youngsters, and especially by children and youngsters with disabilities. Objectives:
- Brought positive and long-lasting effects on participating and indirectly on non-participating organisations  by enhancing knowledge management with new innovative youth work and sport resources and training models/curricula in order to provide quality youth sport work programmes for inclusion of youngsters with different abilities in our communities.
- Supported youth workers and sport trainers in acquiring and developing key competences as youth trainers in the field of using sport methodology in youth work 
- Engage into intensive dissemination and exploitation activities of existing and newly produced products and attract more different abilities’ youngsters.

<< Implementation >>

In project we had five project meeting, beside meeting face to face we had online meet innings using Skype, ZOOM, WhatsApp, Slack and emails in general communication. We developed O1, O2 and O3 that are originally wrote in English and in the end translated in Croatian, German, Italian and Serbian by our partner staff as well youth workers. We implemented LTTA in Zagreb Croatia. In the end we had 3 national conferences (IT; HR; RS) and one international conference in Berlin , Germany.

<< Results >>

We developed three outputs and they are available in EN, DE, IT, HR and RS laguages.
O1 – Guidebook “Using NFE and sport methodology for inclusion of youngsters with disabilities”
O2 – Curriculum “Training youth workers and professional sport trainers in using sport methodology for inclusion and interaction of different abilities’ youngsters”
O3 – Toolkit “Sport methods/games – adapted for using in youth / sport work for inclusion and interaction of different abilities’ youngsters”

2019-3-EL02-KA205-005424.title: My Cultural Heritage & My Future
2019-3-EL02-KA205-005424.summary:
<< Background >>

Ο κυριότερος λόγος που αποφασίσαμε να καταθέσουμε το έργο MCMF αποτέλεσαν τα μεγάλα προβλήτα ανεργίας που αντιμετώπιζαν και συνεχίζουν να αντιμετωπίζουν οι νέοι σε όλη την Ευρώπη (ειδικά τα τελευταία έτη με την έξαρση του Covid-19). Aποφασίστηκε να κατατεθεί μια πρόταση για τη προσπάθεια αντιμετώπισης του φαινομένου της ανεργίας μέσω των δυνατοτήτων που προσφέρει η πολιτισμική κληρονομιά και οι εκφάνσεις της. Το έργο στόχευε άμεσα να υπογραμμίσει και να διευρύνει το πλαίσιο που μπορεί να έχει ο πολιτισμικός τομέας, τόσο ως πηγή ευρωπαϊκής ταυτότητας όσο και των καινοτόμων και ποικίλων δραστηριοτήτων που μπορεί να προσφέρει στη δημιουργία θέσεων εργασίας. Ιδιαίτερα σημαντικό ζήτημα επίσης που είχε τεθεί εξαρχής ήτανε η χαρτογράφηση έξι διαφορετικών πολιτισμικών προελεύσεων και ταυτοτήτων για την ανταλλαγή των καλών πρακτικών, μεθόδων και εμπειριών που είχε αναπτύξει ο κάθε οργανισμός ώστε να δημιουργηθεί ένα εκπαιδευτικό εργαλείο (educational toolkit) όπου ο κάθε ενδιαφερόμενος (οργανισμός ή πολίτης) θα μπορούσε εύκολα να χρησιμοποιήσει για να αντιληφθεί τις δυνατότητες που υπάρχουν επάνω στους τομείς της πολιτισμικής κληρονομιάς και στους τρόπους αξιοποίησής της.

<< Objectives >>

Όπως αναφέρθηκε και προηγουμένως κυριότερος στόχος ήτανε να δημιουργηθούν τα κατάλληλα εργαλεία τα οποία με έναν εύκολο και εύχρηστο τρόπο θα μπορούσαν να αξιοποιηθούν από τον οποιοδήποτε για τους τρόπους αναζήτησης εργασίας μέσω των ποικίλων μέσων που προσφέρει ο τομέας του πολιτισμού. Μέσω της χαρτογράφησης διαφορετικών μεθόδων, εργαλείων και εμπειριών του κάθε φορέα εταίρου που είχε αναπτύξει με την πάροδο των ετών που συμμετέχει στο πρόγραμμα, καθώς και την ανάπτυξη ενός ευρωπαϊκού δικτύου οργανισμών και ατόμων το πρόγραμμα:
-προσφέρει ένα εκπαιδευτικό εργαλείο που περιλαμβάνει τόσο τις διαφορετικές πτυχές της πολιτισμικής κληρονομιάς όσο και τρόπους αξιοποίησης των εργαλείων και μεθόδων αυτών για άτομα και οργανισμούς σε τρόπους εύρεσης ή/και δημιουργίας θέσεων εργασίας
-προσφέρει ένα δίκτυο οργανισμών και ατόμων που ασχολούνται ενεργά με την πολιτισμική κληρονομιά 
-προώθησε την έννοια της ευρωπαϊκής πολιτιστικής κληρονομιάς μεταξύ των νέων και φορέων απασχόλησης
-δημιούργησε ένα αρχικό δίκτυο άμεσων 24 καταρτιζόμενων οι οποίοι εκπαίδευσαν και εκπαιδεύτηκαν κατά τη διάρκεια του σχεδίου σε 6 διαφορετικά εργαλεία πολιτισμικής κληρονομιάς τα οποία μεταλαμπαδεύουν στις χώρες τους, είτε σε περιφερειακό είτε σε τοπικό επίπεδο

<< Implementation >>

Το πρόγραμμα ακολούθησε μια λογική δυναμική σειρά για την δημιουργία των παραγόμενων του έργου. Συγκεκριμένα:
-πραγματοποιήθηκαν 3 Διακρατικές Συναντήσεις (Transnational Project Meetings), το πρώτο στην Ελλάδα, το δεύτερο στην Ουγγαρία, το τρίτο στην Ισπανία με τη συμμετοχή συνολικά 38 συμμετεχόντων οι οποίοι αποτελούσαν εργαζόμενους των εταίρων
-πραγματοποιήθηκε μια L/T/T δραστηριότητα συνολικής διάρκειας 5 ημερών το οποίο πραγματοποιήθηκε στην Ευρωπαϊκή πρωτεύουσα πολιτισμού για το 2020, Ριέκα. Συνολικά συμμετείχαν 27 νέοι εκπρόσωποι από κάθε φορέα εταίρο. Κάθε εταίρος μέσω των συμμετεχόντων του εκπαίδευσε τους υπολοίπους στις μεθόδους και εργαλεία που είχε αναπτύξει, ενώ παράλληλα εκπαιδεύτηκε από τους υπολοίπους σε νέους τρόπους και μεθόδους
-συμμετοχή σε δράσεις για τη διάδοση του σχεδίου και των παραδοτέων του
-πραγματοποιήθηκαν συνολικά 20 training sessions διά ζώσης και ηλεκτρονικά με περισσότερους από 250 συμμετέχοντες εντός της κάθε χώρας του εταίρου τόσο για την εσωτερική εκπαίδευση του κάθε οργανισμού όσο και για την διάδοση του σχεδίου στο κοινωνικό ιστό

<< Results >>

Το πρόγραμμα δημιούργησε ως παραδοτέα:
-ένα εκπαιδευτικό εργαλείο (educational toolkit) το οποίο περιλαμβάνει τη χαρτογράφηση πολιτισμικών μεθόδων και εργαλείων που έχει αναπτύξει και χρησιμοποιεί ο κάθε οργανισμός, σύνολο έξι διαφορετικών χωρών, καθώς και τρόπους και μεθόδους χρησιμοποίησης αυτών για την διεύρυνση αναζήτησης εργασίας μέσω της πολιτισμικής κληρονομιάς
-τη δημιουργία ιστοσελίδας για την ευρωπαϊκή δικτύωση σε θέματα πολιτισμού
-τη δημιουργία λογοτύπου
-τη δημιουργία σελίδας μέσων κοινωνικής δικτύωσης
-τη δημιουργία φυλλαδίων καθόλη τη διάρκεια του σχεδίου για τη ενημέρωση τόσο των μελών εθελοντών της κοινοπραξίας όσο και τη διάδοση και ενημέρωση του κοινωνικού ιστού
-τη δημιουργία δελτίων τύπου μετά το πέρας κάθε δραστηριότητας για τη διάδοση του σχεδίου
-τη δημιουργία οπτικοακουστικού υλικού για τη βελτίωση της διάδοσης του σχεδίου
-τη δημιουργία ενός ευρωπαϊκού ερωτηματολόγιου με 446 απαντήσεις (6 national reports, 1 european report)
-τη δημιουργία εγγράφων για τη προστασία των προσωπικών δεδομένων

Ως αποτελέσματα το έργο:
-δημιούργησε σχέδιο υλοποίησης, επικοινωνίας και διαχείρισης
-βρίσκεται στη διαδικασία συγγραφής μιας επιστημονικής εργασίας
-ανάπτυξη γνώσεων και δεξιοτήτων σε 27 συμμετέχοντες πολλαπλασιαστές

2019-3-HR01-KA205-077010.title: EquiTeens: Promotion of gender equality and non-violent relationships for young teenagers
2019-3-HR01-KA205-077010.summary:
EquiTeens aims to tackle the challenges of preventing and eradicating gender-based violence against and among young teenagers by promoting gender equality and by challenging harmful gender stereotypes and norms. Through a joint strategy of partners in 4 countries (AT-BH-HR-NL), EquiTeens will target youth workers, peer educators, social workers, social educators and other professionals and volunteers who work directly with young teenagers aged 13 to 15 in youth work settings, either in youth organizations, clubs, centres or schools. The overall objective of the project is to contribute to the eradication of violence against and among young people. More specifically, the project aims to: 
- create innovative youth work methodology and practices in the field of the prevention of gender-based violence;
- build capacities of youth workers and professionals in related fields for direct work with young teenagers on the topic of the prevention of gender-based violence;
- promote equitable, non-violent and non-toxic expressions of gender relations among young teenagers aged 13-15.
These objectives will be met by:
- developing a comprehensive toolbox for youth workers and other educators working with young teenagers on the topics connected to gender equality and the prevention of gender-based violence, 
- implementing 3 training events to build capacities of youth workers and professionals in related fields for direct work with young teenagers on the topic of the prevention of gender-based violence, 
- hosting 4 multiplying events targeting youth workers and professionals working in related fields for the dissemination of project results
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2019-3-HR01-KA205-077039.title: Migracode 2 - Empowering youth workers in digital schools for refugees, asylum seeking and migrant youth and preventing drop out
2019-3-HR01-KA205-077039.summary:
<< Background >>

Through this project partner organizations wanted to build the capacities of the staff involved in their non-formal educational tech courses for young refugees, asylum seekers and migrants. We aimed to combine and get together youth workers in the digital/tech area working with refugee and migrant populations in order to engage, exchange good practices, connect and empower them and, in the end, promote youth work and establish good practices achieved in the project. More precisely, we wanted to empower and build capacities of youth workers through mobility, sharing knowledge, different trainings and learning methods, and researching and discussing together future best practices. Indirectly, we addressed the needs of refugee youth by fostering equity and inclusion in education, training and youth in order to enable quality learning for all as well as to prevent drop-out of vulnerable groups and promote the participation of disadvantaged groups in society.

<< Objectives >>

The general objective of the project was, on the one hand, to empower youth workers who work with young refugees, asylum seekers and migrants in non-formal digital education and, on the other hand, to strengthen the chance of asylum seekers and refugees on the labor market by empowering them to pursue their education in the digital field by providing the best possible conditions for that and preventing drop out through quality youth work with them. The specific objectives were: getting valuable insight about issues and challenges directly from our target group by conducting a focus group; exchanging best practices for maintaining their motivation and preventing drop-out; exchanging best practices for the recognition of skills learned through non-formal digital education in order to motivate them; exchanging new learning and teaching methods (especially in demanding environments); testing the methods through pilot courses in our digital schools; sharing know-how between partners in order to empower youth worker skills and improve youth work itself; gain visibility by promoting project activities in order for other organizations to start with similar projects.

<< Implementation >>

1. Focus group which was conducted by 3 participating organizations among their previous beneficiaries in order to understand specific needs and challenges refugee youth are facing when it comes to their education in digital schools and to get useful insight for the other activities.
2. Three LTT activities:
- Teaching digital skills to refugee youth and young asylum seekers
- Motivational and environmental factors related to the successful non-formal education in refugee youth
- Validation of non-formal digital education and working in demanding environments
3. Pilot courses in digital schools of each participating organization based on outcomes from previous activities

<< Results >>

- Insight from the target group on educational barriers and challenges they face, reasons behind their drop-outs and struggles in the educational process
- New and improved processes of recognition and validation of competencies gained in non-formal education which other organizations can use also in the future 
- New and improved practices to cater to the needs of disadvantaged groups in terms of their non-formal education - such as onboarding volunteers to become class assistants in a multicultural environment and with a disadvantaged group
- Development of skills of youth workers - different teaching methods and a community of other teacher volunteers among EU
- Greater understanding and responsiveness to social, linguistic and cultural diversity - for all the staff working on these projects but mostly teachers volunteers
- Adjustments and development of curriculums used by youth workers in partner organizations - in order to facilitate the learning process for students and upgrade the teaching methods of youth workers 
-  Best practices in teaching digital skills to refugee youth and young asylum seekers in demanding environments 
- Strategies and methods for education of vulnerable group prone to drop-out
topics: Preventing early school leaving and failure in education
Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

2019-3-IE01-KA205-065721.title: Equality Ambassadors
2019-3-IE01-KA205-065721.summary:
<< Background >>

Europe needs more cohesive and inclusive societies which allow citizens to play an active role in democratic life.  Responding to this need five partner organisations came together and designed a strategic cooperation project that would work with youth workers, youth leaders, teachers, facilitators, artists and young people to promote awareness of common European values and a sense of inclusion in an Equal Europe. The aims were to create a  new Equality Ambassador Peer Leadership Training Curriculum, Equality Ambassadors Resource book and Equality Ambassadors mobile phone digital app –  available online in digital format and access to training  for young people  to become an Equality Ambassador which is a young person who can: 

•	Demonstrate an awareness of and advocate for democracy, equality and human rights
•	Share their own experiences and listen to other’s experiences of inequality
•	Aim to identify changes needed to promote democracy, equality and human rights
•	Aim to identify ways for bringing different communities together 
•	Communicate with others in relation to advocating for democracy, equality and human rights
•	Provide access to an on-line list of resources to promote democracy, equality and human rights

<< Objectives >>

Bring together 10 youth workers and 25 youth from 5 countries across Europe involve them in the development of a new curriculum for an Equality Ambassador Peer Leadership Training Programme, Equality Ambassadors Resource Book, mobile Digital app featuring twenty-five stories of role models related to democracy, equality and human rights in the EU. 
•	Six transnational partner exchanges to be held in Ireland, Serbia, Croatia, Spain, Greece and Ireland, attended by ten youth workers. 
•	As part of curriculum development, each partner holds two focus group sessions and one curriculum development workshop attended by two youth workers and five young people per partner country, totalling 10 youth workers and twenty-five youth. 
•	 Ten Youth Workers trained in how to conduct the Equality Ambassador Curriculum with young people. 
•	The training is rolled out with 200 young people across Europe training them as Equality Ambassadors so they are able to go on to raise awareness of the importance of democracy, equality and human rights and the role of the EU to promote values of equality, tolerance and inclusion. 
•	A Communications and Dissemination strategy conducted, including all  outputs and Final Report and Evaluation are distributed.

<< Implementation >>

Project Management and Implementation. 
Creation of Assets-Intellectual Outputs:
One EA Peer Leadership Training Curriculum; One EA Resource book; EA digital app to accompany training curriculum. 
TPM and Multiplier Events:
Twenty-eight youth workers, staff and volunteers came together and attended five virtual meetings and three transnational partner exchanges. Five virtual meeting dates 16/03/2020; 25/03/2020; 19/10/2020; 9/03/2021; 14/12/2021.Three face-to-face TPM's 17/06/2022 Vukovar, Croatia,  30/08/2022 Kalamata, Greece and 19/10/2022 Dublin, Ireland. Trained personnel then delivered the Peer Leadership training programme with young people through a series of multiplier events. A total of ten multiplier events with a total of 362 in attendance. 
Communication and Dissemination activities reaching 356,736 members of the public and targeted audiences.
Final Report and Evaluations prepared and distributed.
LTTA took place from the 7-9 July 2022 hosted by IFES Coop, Spain with training also conducted by all partners, attended by ten youth workers.
Exceptional Costs

<< Results >>

Eight TPM conducted (5 online, 3 onsite) attended by 28 youth workers, youth leaders and volunteers - eight from Ireland; six from Spain; six from Serbia; four from Croatia and four from Greece. 
30 youth attended 10 focus group sessions and provided input into the development of the three IO's.
Assets:
One Equality Ambassador Peer Leadership Training Curriculum using theatre and new digital technologies to promote democracy, equality and human rights made up of five face-to-face lessons, one on-line lesson plan.
One Equality Ambassadors Resource book with 25 role-model stories related to democracy, equality and human rights – available online –  created to accompany the Equality Ambassadors training curriculum.
One Equality Ambassadors digital app.
10 youth educators and workers were trained in how to implement the Equality Ambassadors curriculum during LTTA  in Valencia, Spain 7-9 July 2022.
10 multiplier events were held across the five partner organisations with a total of 362 in attendance.
Communication and Dissemination activities implemented reaching 356,736 members of the public and targeted audiences..
Equality Ambassadors book and digital Mobile app distributed to 15,000 (3,000 per partner organisation).
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2019-3-PL01-KA205-077890.title: Youth M Power. Breaking the unemployment barrier.
2019-3-PL01-KA205-077890.summary:
<< Background >>

Employment is often seen as one of the cornerstones that helps individuals and communities to overcome disadvantage and achieve their social and economic potential. Conversely, unemployment, underemployment and loss of occupational status are a missed opportunity for individuals, their families and the communities they live in, to realize their potential. This narrative is doubly true for newly arrived migrants and refugees who often see employment as one of the signifiers of success in a new country and a salve for the loss and disruption that inevitably accompanies migration. 

The project was created as the solution for rising social exclusion among youth toward youth with fewer opportunities, migrants, refugees, foreigners, lowering confidence in youth especially those who are excluded, low employment and entrepreneurship initiatives among youth. 
The idea of the project was to develop the tools and methods for empowering the youth with giving them competences, right opportunities, they could build on their strengths, address their challenges, and be part of the contribution.

<< Objectives >>

Through this project we wanted to support the youth including the youth with fewer opportunities in the local communities, to support them integrate in the community and develop their competencies to increase their employability. To achieve this partners organised the trainings for their youth workers where they developed the necessary competences and gain new tools to work with young people. Thus building the competences of youth workers partners develop their capacity and increase the activities offer for young people. Through the trainings youth workers and partners develop their capacity to provide the activities for youth in field of entrepreneurship and social entrepreneurship, youth empowerment especially for the ones with fewer opportunities. The partners develop the local and international activities for youth increasing their competencies and employability, giving them opportunity to learn through international mobilities, getting to know different culture and learn through the NFE tools supporting them in developing their competences and preparing them for employment.

<< Implementation >>

Partners implemented following activities:
-Kick off meeting was organised by Polish organisation in Kraków, Poland
-C1 Short-term joint staff training events about working with disadvantaged youth in the context of empowerment was organised by Polish organisation in Murzasichle, Poland
-local activities in partners communities
-C2 Blended Mobility of young people about Empowerment of youth in the context of introducing oneself as an employee and creating the video resumes. was organised by Spanish organisation in Coma de Ruga, Spain
-local activities in partners communities
-Mid-Evaluation was organised by Spanish organisation in Coma de Ruga, Spain
-C3 Short-term joint staff training events about social enterprise how to work with young people in the context of the growth of their entrepreneurial abilities was organised by Croatian organisation in Susak, Croatia
-local activities in partners communities
-C4 Blended Mobility of young people about creating an outline of social entrepreneurs based on developed tools was organised by Greek organization in Nea Makri, Greece
-local activities in partners communities
-Final evaluation was organised in Wieliczka, Poland

<< Results >>

-32 youth workers directly involved in the Short-term joint staff training events
-64 youth participating in Blended Mobility of young people
-8 local workshops for youth workers after the Short-term joint staff training event
