2019-3-PT02-KA205-006263.title: Learn&Leave no limit
2019-3-PT02-KA205-006263.summary:
<< Background >>

The project Learn & Leave no limit was developed in international partnership with organizations from Portugal, Romania, Croatia and Italy. It addressed social inclusion, employability and entrepreneurial engagement of disadvantaged youngsters coming from rural and geographically disadvantaged regions facing isolation and marginalization and it aimed to exploit the potential of the social enterpreneurship model as one tool for opening new opportunities for them. 
The main needs addressed by the project were related to the issues faced in our youth communities such as: lack of job opportunities, limited profession selection, lower income compared to the urban areas, unsatisfactory educational services, lack of services and infrastructures, leisure opportunities, participation and engagement in the civic life. Thus the partners identified the needs to provide effective strategies to contribute in boosting social inclusion, employability and entrepreneurial engagement, to train and thus enlarge the number of youth workers so to be able to address the large number of young people facing difficulties in our regions, to increase and provide continuously local and international opportunities for personal and professional development of youngsters.

<< Objectives >>

Specific objectives addressed within the project were:  
- To develop knowledge, skills and competencies of youth operators from the partner countries for them to be able to develop Social Innovation Activities aimed at empowering disadvantaged young people from rural and geographically disadvantaged areas. 

- To deliver a training module covering 1 international learning and 4 local experiential programmes on social entrepreneurship targeted to 25 disadvantaged young people living in rural and geographically disadvantaged areas from the partner countries with a view to foster their social inclusion, employability and entrepreneurial engagement.

<< Implementation >>

The following activities were developed: 

C1 organized in Italy, coordinated by MVI between 24-28 February 2022, with attendance of 12 youth workers in presence and 4 youth workers attending virtually, aiming to develop skills and competencies of 16 youth operators from the partner countries to develop Social
Innovation Activities aimed at empowering young people from rural and disadvantaged geographical areas

C2 organized in Croatia by Meraki, between 10-14.04.2022 with the attendance of 2 young people from the partner countries, aiming to develop the knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of social entrepreneurship among disadvantaged young people from the partner countries.

Local experiential program organized in all the partner countries which involved the implementation of 4 fund raising activities with a view to reinforce the knowledge and skills acquired by youngsters during their training abroad and to foster the cooperation between NGOs and business sector.

<< Results >>

1. Training course to develop skills and competencies among 16 youth operators from the partner countries to develop Social Innovation Activities aimed at empowering young people from in rural and geographically disadvantaged areas 
2. A training module covering learning and experiential programmes targeted to disadvantaged young people living rural and geographically disadvantaged areas as following: 
- A blended learning mobility of young people aimed to develop knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of social entrepreneurship among 25 disadvantaged young people from the partner countries living in rural and geographically disadvantaged areas
- 1 Experiential program developed on a period of 2 months with a view to develop knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of social entrepreneurship among 25 disadvantaged young people from the partner countries living in rural and geographically disadvantaged areas. 

1 digital dissemination brochure available in pdf format, in English, capitalising on the partners experience within the project and the educational program created for young people.

2019-3-RS01-KA205-065027.title: Under the Loupe: Rural Youth Work!
2019-3-RS01-KA205-065027.summary:
The project “Under the loupe: Rural Youth Work!” is a 15 months project involving partners from Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia - NAPOR, Prizma, Idrija2020, and two research institutes: Institut drustvenih nauka and Institut drustvenih znanosti “Ivo Pilar” with the aim to explore Rural Youth Work. 
Rural youth are constantly facing one or more challenges related to basic economic and social infrastructures. Their access to quality youth services that are providing possibilities for personal and social development are very limited and often totally inaccessible. Therefore, it is important to create youth work programs where young people are, and based on their needs. Evidence-based research and support in creating new innovative programs and strategies based on good practice examples will make significant step towards rural youth work development and youth engagement.
The partnership aims:
- To ensure social inclusion of rural youth by creating preconditions for their active involvement in community life, through building capacity of youth workers and raising awareness of decision makers, underpinned by relevant policy development. 
- To establish cross-sectoral cooperation among research community and youth workers in order to identify the needs of rural youth and introduce and encourage evidence-based practice.
- To increase visibility and recognition of youth work potential to respond to the needs of rural youth at local, national, regional and EU level.
- To increase quality of rural youth work programs by introducing innovative and inspiring practices from local to EU level.

Main results of the project are: Detailed insight into the current state of rural youth and youth work and identification of trends and needs achieved through cross-sectoral cooperation between research and youth work community. Collected regional and EU innovative rural youth work practices enriched the capacity of rural youth workers and resulted in quality provision of services for rural youth.  Public campaign raised awareness of relevant stakeholders, rural youth, rural youth workers, decision makers and wider public about importance of investing in youth work services in rural areas and its positive implication on rural youth development, as well on community development. Study visit to Slovenia built capacity of youth workers by gaining knowledge and new insights about innovative good practices applicable for creation of new youth work services in rural areas. National meetings gathered all the relevant stakeholders, where majority of parties is committed to investing in rural youth work and developing relevant strategies. Laid foundation for further improvement of policies related to rural youth and youth workers in Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia, through preparation of 3 advocacy documents.
Several activities are planned in order to reach the results: Research in Serbia and Croatia (analysis of the situation of young people in rural areas and needs of rural youth and rural youth workers), Booklet on 20 innovative and inspiring practices in rural youth work in EU and non EU countries,  Public awareness campaign “Let’s go rural!” with 48 created segments and total reach 1.500.000 people for 12 months, three webinars involving 60 rural youth, National discussions in Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia, involving minimum 90 participants from various target groups including decision - makers,  Study visit to Slovenia for 18 rural youth workers from 3 countries to exchange good practices and introduction of innovative methods, approaches and tools used among rural youth workers, Advocacy documents– 3 Final drafts of advocacy documents prepared: Rural Youth Work Strategy (Serbia), Action plan on setting the strategic development framework of municipalities that focuses on rural youth (Slovenia) and Guide for developing supporting program for rural youth organisations, youth and youth workers (Croatia). Careful plan for dissemination and exploitation of results of the project is designed in order to promote the project outputs and outcomes to wide range of organizations and institutions working on national, regional and European level in the field of youth work.
topics: Development of disadvantaged rural and urban areas
Quality and innovation of youth work
Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Tackling geographical remoteness and involving rural areas

2019-3-SI02-KA205-015278.title: Reward system
2019-3-SI02-KA205-015278.summary:
Due to the lack of attractive and encouraging ways of working with young people, in the working area of partner organizations, young people are poorly involved in activities that enable them personal and career growth. The aim of the project, which will involve 57 young people aged between 13 and 29 (including young people with fewer opportunities, with geographical, social and economic barriers), is to develop a new tool and a program that will encourage young people to become active and to benefit from the opportunities offered by the local environment. 
 
The aim of the Slovenian and Croatian partner organizations (Youth Centre Šentjur and the Zagor Association Network) is to:
Develop a special awarding system for collecting points that will attract young people to actively participate in the local environment and prospect in personal and career growth.
Establish a network of youth promoters, young people that work with young people and take care of their animation and inclusion in the established awarding system.
 
For realization of activities and achievement of desired results of the project, the methodology of non-formal education will be used based on the interaction and active participation of all participants (work in small groups, open discussions, debates, various creative techniques for finding ideas, research, testing ...) and learning through experience and active exchange of knowledge and information between participants (cooperative learning). Activities, in which young people will participate, will be based on the learning experience, initiative and entrepreneurship of young people.
topics: Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
Quality and innovation of youth work
Promotion of alternative forms of participation

2019-3-UK01-KA205-077785.title: Digital Entrepreneurship Start-up for Youth
2019-3-UK01-KA205-077785.summary:
<< Background >>

We were witnessing high unemployment rates, especially for young people. Self-employment and entrepreneurship has turned out to be a valuable option for careers’ building. However, with the development of the IT sector, classic “offline” enterprises do not survive for long time. Thus, digital entrepreneurship can reduce youth unemployment.

In order to get into digital entrepreneurship, all interested youngsters need to have respective high(er) level of ICT / digital competences. As most of our unemployed youngsters admit in our short survey that they lack digital business competences, with this project we were contributing to the development of their ICT/digital competences, or in other words – of the relevant and high-quality skills and competences for digital entrepreneurship of theirs. 

With this project, thus, we were answering to the needs defined by institutions, as well as the needs of our own youth workers and youngsters. We are promoting digital entrepreneurship of youngsters and have produced intellectual outputs that serve as a quality knowledge management material for education of current and future youth workers for efficient and effective empowerment and mentoring of youngsters for digital entrepreneurship.

<< Objectives >>

The objectives of the project DigEntY were:
-	Empower unemployed youngsters for digital entrepreneurship start-up through development of inspiring, innovative and up-to-date handbook, as well as the online course.
-	Empower our youth workers and improve knowledge management of youth work organisations in theory and practice for building competences of youth workers in digital entrepreneurship for youngsters, through LTTA and innovative curriculum for youth workers’ training and useful toolkit with workshops for youngsters.
-	Exchange good practices and further develop quality strategic partnership among partners from 5 European countries with different realities in regards to youth employment and digital entrepreneurship

<< Implementation >>

Project activities that we have successfully implemented:
A1 – Project Management
M1 – Kick-off meeting (online)
O1 – Handbook “Digital Entrepreneurship Start-up”
M2 – Second meeting in Zagreb, Croatia
O2 – Curriculum “Empowering youth workers to encourage digital entrepreneurship start-ups among youngsters”
M3 – Third meeting (online)
O3 – Toolkit “Mentoring and supporting youngsters for digital entrepreneurship start-up”
M4 – Fourth meeting (online)
O4 – E-learning course “Digital Entrepreneurship Start-up course for youngsters”
M1-II - face-to-face meeting in Belgrade, Serbia
C1 - LTTA “Training of trainers for digital entrepreneurship start-up for youth”
E1, E2, E3, E4, E5 – Open conferences in Serbia, Croatia, Sweden, Germany and United Kingdom
M5 – Evaluation meeting in London, United Kingdom

<< Results >>

-	O1 Handbook “Digital Entrepreneurship Start-up”, in 5 languages
-	O2 Curriculum “Empowering youth workers to encourage digital entrepreneurship start-ups among youngsters”, in 5 languages
-	O3 Toolkit “Mentoring and supporting youngsters for digital entrepreneurship start-up”, in 5 languages
-	O4 E-learning course “Digital Entrepreneurship Start-up course for youngsters”, in 5 languages
-	Over 25 multipliers (youth workers, volunteers and management staff) using our intellectual outputs in their work with 104 youngsters and testing their effectiveness locally
-	282 participants of 5 multiplier events participated workshops about the importance of youth work in promoting Digital Entrepreneurship Start-up support for youngsters with fewer opportunities
-	434 (young) people visited the different language versions e-learning courses during the implementation phase, using it, testing it and giving feedback about it to the organisers
-	15 youth trainers, participants at the LTTA, have been directly empowered for developing quality youth work programmes promoting Digital Entrepreneurship Start-up. They have further organised small multiplication trainings in their sending organisations, with additional 32 youth workers empowered.

2020-1-DE04-KA205-019427.title: BACK TO THE FUTURE
2020-1-DE04-KA205-019427.summary:
<< Background >>

The project's partners came together while working on numerous KA1s over the past ten years. Informal discussions that took place during projects frequently focused on the follow-up procedure and how, if at all, systematization might be implemented.

This project was an attempt to draw together the approaches of partners (6 youth organisations in five countries, with a considerable history of KA1 cooperation) in the: 
- formalization of a common conception of Follow-Up, based on a research package
- the development of learning materials on specific forms of Follow-Up (e.g. ESK volunteer management, KA1 YE & TCs, local project work, spin-offs, etc.) 
- the presentation of these outputs in a physical and digital format. 

More broadly aim of the strategic partnership was to develop guidelines and capacities for quality follow-up of different youth processes, enabling the transfer of learning from international to local and national environments and offering space for more active engagement of youth leaders within the civil society and youth field. Through this project, we have attempted to contribute to the evergreen topic of follow-up and evaluation within international youth mobilities.

<< Objectives >>

• To strengthen the capacities of youth organizations, towards a better use of the knowledge and experience of the participants in the post-mobility period;
• To develop clear and easily implementable transferable strategies and mechanisms on how to ensure the follow-up and impact in the local community in the post-mobility period;
• To explore the possibilities of measurement of impact from mobilities in the daily lives of the participants in a long-term perspective;
• To offer space for a structured way of knowledge-sharing between different local and international youth organizations and to encourage future collaborations;
• To promote meaningful active participation of youth leaders within civil society organizations and the youth sectors;
• To provide the participants and partner organizations with a set of Online tools that can assist the supporting and managing of the participants during all stages of mobilities (preparation, implementation, and follow-up).

<< Implementation >>

This project sought to develop multiple outputs; as such, we integrated mobilities, local actions, conferences, and Transnational Partner Meetings at key moments to support this development process:
- We hosted a mobility of partners' staff, which played an important role in critiquing our educational modules. This activity was hosted in Nicosia, Cyprus, and engaged directly with the Emhpasys Training Center 
- Several Transnational Partner Meetings were implemented, initially online due to travel restrictions, as well as a final conference in Berlin, Germany. Six multiplier events were hosted across the partnership.
- Throughout the 27 months, the consortium engaged in ongoing cooperation and communication to navigate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, refugee movements, and conflicts on different partners in this cooperation.
- Also, local activities were implemented in order to test one of the project results "Fast forward" card game for youth workers on follow up activities. This was mostly implemented locally as part of several trainings in different countries.
- We have also implemented several online discussion rounds among consortia, in order to update each other on the project progress.

<< Results >>

• Publication: Effective follow-up of International youth mobilities on a local level.
• Online support platform for impact assessment with information and learning modules for other organisations or youth workers.
• Set of recommendations towards youth organizations and institutions on what kind of structural changes they can make to be more inclusive.
• The impact of the project, in the long run, it will contribute towards the development of stronger youth organizations, with a lot of know-how gained from the international level, with developed quality of mentoring and support 
• Engage more young people in different social, cultural, and political processes.

During the research and development process, we also developed a card game for youth workers to better engage with and reflect upon the different themes and topics within the area of follow-up and evaluation. This was an unplanned additional output, but to partners, it seemed a strong way to disseminate our learning within a format that would ensure continuous use of our project-learnings and sustainability of our impact.

2020-1-EE01-KA205-077790.title: Take Action - Together Against Discrimination!
2020-1-EE01-KA205-077790.summary:
<< Background >>

We, as the leading organization, have been working on diversity issues for many years both on a local level and internationally. Within those years we have collaborated with several partners who are facing similar issues. We saw together a need to address diversity issues and inclusion on a strategic level. 

We have seen internationally that the understanding of diversity [by this we mean understanding one's identity, understanding the effects of stereotypes and prejudices in connection to discrimination and violence (including online violence and cyberbullying), understanding of human rights, hate speech, gender issues etc] is quite limited among young people, but also among youth workers and society as a whole. This means that inclusion of various groups is more difficult and there is resistance from different sides. 

Young people are more likely to radicalize, there are more cases of hate speech and this all can lead to violence and exclusion. 

Cultural differences and the lack of information about other ethnic groups backgrounds and habits is another topic that brings disagreements in society. Definitely the problem pops up in rural areas shows our partners experience.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to raise the capacity of partner organizations to work on diversity issues. We wanted to train youth workers through staff trainings to use identity building as tool for fighting against prejudice-based discrimination. Raise capacity of partner organizations to tackle radicalization of young people and to prevent hate speech online and offline via exchange of good practices and jobshadowing. 

One possible solution was that youth organizations should take more active role in promoting diversity and inclusion. Another objective was to train local NGOs in each partner county to be able to work with youngsters on following issues: human rights, gender issues, online safety, hate speech and discrimination. Carry out more than 100  workshops on diversity issues involving directly more than 3000 young people in participating countries. Create at least one new activity plan per partner organization for anti discrimination education, test them and add them to format which allows other organizations to use them in their work. Raise the capacity of partner organizations to use peer to peer methodology for inclusion and promotion of diversity internationally and on local level with youth and youth workers.

<< Implementation >>

In December 2021 we had a kick-off meeting of the project, where we got to know the other partners better and set clear objectives and how to achieve them. 

In February 2022 we organized a training course where we trained youth workers to use identity building as a tool for fighting against prejudice-based discrimination. Through this we raised the capacity of partner organization workers or long-term volunteers to tackle radicalization of young people and to prevent hate speech online and offline and work with human rights related topics in general. Workshops in participants home countries followed after the training course,

May 2022 - January 2023 was an active job shadowing period with 9 mobilities. There were some changes of countries compared to the initial plan.

In September 2022 we organized a midterm meeting to check the job shadowing process. We heard experiences from job shadowers who have finished their mobility as well as well how is the preparation for others going.

The project ended with the final meeting in February 2023 where organizations sent their representatives to sum up the project. Unfortunately the covid and earthquake in Türkiye affected the participation and we had to make some sessions online.

<< Results >>

The result of the project can be measured in numbers but the real impact of the project rolls up in small actions of all participants' lives. As a whole, the project helped to create more solidarity communities across Europe.

As result of project, we have trained 4-8 local organizations in each country (more than 40 in total) involving at least 3 youth workers from each organization (minimum 120 in total) and have carried out locally with local partners via workshops involving young people. Via additional country specific local activities we involved another 225 youngsters per country, so totally in the project more than 2000.
As a result of the project, we have created 12 workshop plans, which have been tested by our youth workers and can be used in work of anti-discrimination. This material and other made during the partnership are uploaded on a common online platform.

On a regular basis we shared on platform our experiences of local and international activities between partners and with other interested stakeholders (for example other NGOs, youth centers). Each partner shared project results to widen the visibility and awareness in their community.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Quality and innovation of youth work

2020-1-EL02-KA205-005631.title: MIGRACODE: Acceleration of refugees' labor insertion & social integration, in Greece
2020-1-EL02-KA205-005631.summary:
<< Background >>

The consortium applied for this project aiming to address two main needs. The first one was the development and expansion of digital skills in the EU labour market, through carrying out specialised technical courses. The second was the need to support the employability and inclusion of refugees, migrants, and asylum seekers, by providing free-of-charge courses, encouraging them to develop skill sets and facilitate their insertion into the workforce.

The collaborating institutions also aimed to exchange knowledge, experience and know hows by collaborating on this project and exchanging best practices.

<< Objectives >>

The general set objectives of the project were:
The exchange of good case practices between the partner NGOs.
The implementation of good case practices in supporting and accelerating labour insertion and social inclusion of the beneficiaries. 
To support and promote the development of youth workers on acquiring skills, knowledge, and experience assisting vulnerable groups 
To improve social inclusion by opening new opportunities for unaccompanied minors, refugees, asylum seekers, unemployed, women, to develop their skills and design their career paths
To better understand the needs of refugees and align IT innovative educational programs with them

The specific objectives set were:
→ To enhance the employability of the students/beneficiaries by :
Αligning digital skills curricula taught with EU IT Certifications Standards to enable graduates to prove their skills and help them secure a job opportunity
Nurture the sense of initiative / entrepreneurial skills
Create a Strategy for Career Days/Networking events with students and tech recruiters
Create an open-source program of employability skills training to be delivered to the beneficiaries
→ To develop and implement non-formal educational practices that can be implemented in the course provided for the beneficiaries to better understand the material taught.
→ To promote/boost gender equality in the IT sector and enable labour insertion for migrant women in tech industry
→ Strengthen the Migracode consortium and the collaboration with stakeholders (companies, foundations, local authorities, etc.) to make the hiring process of the graduates more efficient.

<< Implementation >>

We designed 4 short-term training events, that covered different but important aspects of social integration and IT Industry: 
Gender Equality
Employability & Hiring Processes Standardisation
Increase of Graduation Rate through the coding curricula
Nurture of Entrepreneurial Traits

12 Youth Workers participated in each activity, 2 from each partner (direct beneficiaries) and 800 beneficiaries (refugees/asylum seekers/migrants, aged 18-50 that have work permit in EU) were engaged in these activities in their local communities, by participating in the educational programs.

<< Results >>

The general outputs of the project were:
-The Migracode network is strengthened by adding one new partner: Konexio (France) and Mode Foundation (Poland). Due to the decision of Konexio to terminate their collaboration with the consortium, the partner was replaced by Madrid for refugees.
-The partners gained expertise on how to improve and promote the labour insertion of social vulnerable groups 
-The organisation of 4 Trainings/events based on the needs of the target groups and the expertise of each organisation
- The MIgracode website was updated and serves as a portfolio, where all produced tools/handbooks/Good-case practices are open for anyone interested in using them.

The specific outputs of the project were:
For the participating organisations:
Improvement of the educational programs the organisations offer, support into the labour market and implementation of non-formal educational tools.
Strengthen the community of tech professionals and companies around the organisations.
Increase the students applying and graduating the education programs. 
Explore potential partnerships with other organisations in the EU, exploring different subjects and approaches to support and empower more vulnerable people in their local communities.

For the participants:
Gained different perspectives and mindset from interacting with other youth workers on IT Education and social inclusion from other EU countries.
Developed interpersonal skills and improved their support of vulnerable groups.
Became familiar with digital tools and technologies that are needed in the job market nowadays.
Developed entrepreneurial traits.
For the target groups of the participating organisations: 
The migrants developed skills and competences such as digital, interpersonal, and entrepreneurial, as well as learning agility, working and learning in a team environment,  and communication skills
They became familiar with the concept of non-formal educational practices and the “learning by doing idea”
They had the opportunity to meet new people, build social connections with their peers and felt included in activities happening in their local community
They were empowered to design their career paths, and discover their potential to rebuild their lives in the host societies.
800 refugees/migrants/unemployed participated in the IT educational programs in 6 European Cities, with 60% of them applying for jobs and 40% finding a position.
For the stakeholders:
- Become more open-minded and involved in societal actions in their local community
- Acknowledge the value of synergies between organisations.
- Participation in 12 awareness raising events ( 2 in the city of each partner), to disseminate the project’s results and engage local communities
The project produced 4 deliverables:
Entrepreneurial Guide: a guide developed by the coordinator of the project, exploring entrepreneurship in coding and the best practices to put in place. This guide served as a document to be shared and inspire the consortium.
A report on the 5 top non-formal educational methods in digital schools. A report was compiled using the responses of partners on the non-formal education methods they have tried and found to be the more successful. This document served as a best practices guide for participating organisations.
Enabling labour insertion: How to match the market need with students' skills, through ensuring job placement & internships and through bringing graduates and companies in touch? A report produced that served as a guideline to facilitating insertion of students into the labour market.
‘’How to promote gender equality in the IT workplace and enable labour insertion for migrant women in the tech industry’’. A detailed guide was produced, examining the case study on the ‘’Code woman’’ approach, as well as analysing the steps the organisations need to undertake to provide gender inclusive trainings.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market
Reception and integration of refugees and migrants

2020-1-ES02-KA205-014883.title: Youth heritage
2020-1-ES02-KA205-014883.summary:
<< Background >>

This project has been a way of knowing and looking for the potential of the cultural sector to be both a source of European identity and a setting for the development of innovative activities that promote job creation. Although Europe's cultural heritage is a vital aspect of European identity and a source of creativity that can guide future development in European integration, its cultural potential is still underestimated.
Companies and the employment sector in general require more and more
In this context, we believe that youth services, including youth NGOs, training companies, institutes and employment agencies dealing with youth, should be more active in developing
youth activities to support young people as cultural heritage professionals. For this reason, we identified the need to train youth workers, employment agents and even volunteers to equip them with the necessary tools to initiate and lead activities aimed at young people, such as employment workshops and personalized guidance.

<< Objectives >>

The project has had three main objectives:
-Raise awareness of the jobs that can be created in the cultural sector
-Strengthen the feeling of community in Europe.
-Share and exchange good practices between organizations
To achieve them, we present a project based on four specific objectives:
Specific objective 1: improve the quality of services related to support and advice to young people in professions related to cultural heritage within transnational networks
association, organizing exchanges of good practices and exploring professions related to cultural heritage within the participating countries, sharing experiences and multiplying actions at the local level.
Specific objective 2: Improve the skills in labor areas related to cultural heritage of 24 youth workers, employment agents and volunteers from youth NGOs, youth centers, employment agencies or municipal social services.
Specific objective 3: Promote the concept of European cultural heritage among young workers and employment agents.
Specific objective 4: Implement a support and advice network at European level.

<< Implementation >>

During the project, each partner has carried out local activities to study different jobs in the cultural sector. In addition to the creation of a European web for youth workers, employment agents and volunteers who work daily with young people, as the number of companies and entities dedicated to offering services related to culture is growing. Increasingly, the public sector focuses a large part of its efforts on the preservation and conservation of cultural heritage as a development strategy and local projection. This creates an employment dynamic in the sector and increases the demand for professional experts in cultural management.
The main activity carried out in Rijeka as the European capital of culture produced a great exchange of good practices and impact of the cultural heritage sector on young people. The participants attended presentations by the people who were in charge of carrying out the process of Rijeka being named European Capital of Culture and shared different examples of good practices on jobs related to this sector.

<< Results >>

24 young workers and employment agents will report on good practices in Europe related to employment in cultural heritage.
- 1 training-educational kit for young workers and employment agents that includes innovative tools for employment workshops to be used during the project and in the future
activities.
- Development of computer resources that serve as training tools in non-formal education for employment.
- Development of multimedia tools to promote examples/results of good practices of this project.
- Development of skills for 24 multipliers from 4 countries.
- Sensitization of young workers about the high rate of youth unemployment in Europe and the possibilities that young people have to work in the field related to cultural heritage.
- Creation of a network at European level to support and advise young people on European cultural heritage and job opportunities.
- Campaign to promote European cultural heritage among young workers and employment agencies.
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2020-1-HR01-KA205-077252.title: Dealing with popular myths. Youth work against disinformation and distortion of historical facts
2020-1-HR01-KA205-077252.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was created because the coordinator and the partners wanted to work more on mapping and deconstructing myths and distortions of historical facts among youth and improve their capacities to work on these topics. Besides that, they wanted to create new materials, methods, and tools that would allow them to work on these topics in an innovative and modern way. The partners started from the belief that myths and distortions are carriers of stereotypes but, in many cases, young people accept them as truths and do not question them. They become easy targets for groups spreading myths, which youth are not able to recognize as such. This behavior leads to the growth of prejudices and stereotypes, hate speech, and radicalization. The inability to critically understand information becomes even more worrying in the era of social media because these myths can easily reach young people through social media channels. Besides these reasons for applying the project, the partners identified in the beginning, that one of the motivations to work more on this topic was the Covid-19 pandemic and all myths, distortions, and fake news that were present in the public space, media, and social networks. This convinced the partners that this project is really needed and that youth workers and teachers need new methods and tools to combat these issues. The biggest accent we put on was the development of critical thinking, media literacy, and the prevention of stereotypes and discrimination in young people. The project answered the needs of the organizations to address past, contemporary and debated topics such as myths and distortions and their connection with the growth of populism, discrimination, and radicalization. The partners noticed a growing radicalization among youth, a growing belief in populism, and increasing fake news and hate speech. They felt they were missing the tools to counter these tendencies and felt unable to reach these radicalizing youth.

<< Objectives >>

The main objective of the project was: to deconstruct popular myths and distortions of historical facts, to contribute to giving young people the tools to combat radicalization, prejudices, and stereotypes and to decrease the attraction for populism and authoritarianism among European youth. 
 
Specific objectives of the project were: to increase the capacity of the partners to work with youth on resisting popular myths and distortions of historical facts; combat the spreading of fake news and other forms of online disinformation; counter myths and distortions with narrations based on historical facts; speak against discrimination, segregation and racism; fight manipulation and propaganda; develop critical thinking and media literacy; strengthen democracy and promote European values.

<< Implementation >>

1.)	First transnational partner meeting (kick-off) – online meeting
2.)	First blended mobility (participants age 18-25) – online
3.)	Second blended mobility (participants age 14-18) – online
4.)	Second transnational partner meeting - online
5.)	Creating IO1 – five educational videos
6.)	Creating IO2 – the toolkit
7.)	Seminar for youth workers and teachers – in-person training
8.)	Third transnational partner meeting – in-person meeting
9.)	Local multiplier events
10.)	 Fourth transnational partner meeting
11.)	 Local multiplier events (additional)
12.)	 Creation of IO3 – publication with workshops

<< Results >>

The tangible results we created are the following:
•	IO1 – 5 educational videos (5 in English + 5 in national languages of the partner organizations)
•	IO2 – the toolkit „Dealing with popular myths“
•	IO3 – workshops „Dealing with popular myths“

Intangible results are:
•	increased capacities and competencies in youth work of 5 European organizations, by generating innovative approaches to address the myths and historical distortions shared among youth; 
•	enhanced international cooperation and strengthened networking of the involved organizations; 
•	promoted innovation and development of targeted approaches and methodologies for dealing with the project's topics; 
•	increased ability of the organizations’ staff to deal with the project's topics and issues both in their local community and on the international and European level. 
•	modernized curricula of the partner organizations and improved working methods
•	raised awareness of around 65 young people directly about the myths and distortions 
•	improved competencies of around 65 young people for deconstructing myths and historical distortions, critical thinking, and media literacy
•	improved knowledge and capacities of 25 youth workers and teachers for dealing with the project topics
•	around 300 participants of the multiplier events learned new methodologies on how to work on the project topics and get new tools 
Besides, the project informed directly around 300 young people and other stakeholders about the innovative methodologies of how to work on the topics of myth deconstruction through their participation in the project activities, and around 1000 people were informed indirectly.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Quality and innovation of youth work
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-1-HR01-KA205-077335.title: Better ACT than react
2020-1-HR01-KA205-077335.summary:
<< Background >>

People working with vulnerable groups of youth are struggling on a daily basis with the problem of maintaining work-life balance. Youth with physical disabilities, behavioral problems or intellectual disabilities, youth from alternative care, NEET youth and minorities face difficult problems in their everyday lives that can trigger strong feelings of empathy, sadness, helplessness or anger in youth workers. It can be very hard for youth workers to get proper rest after work and don’t think about distressing problems that young people they work with face. In order to achieve work sustainability, workers should find a balance between work and private life. Considering that we are lacking tools to help youth workers to alleviate the stress and emotions arising from such emotionally demanding work, development of a modern tool that is easily applicable and simple to use is of utmost necessity. Youth workers who learn how to take care of their mental health will be able to teach these skills to young people they work with too. When adopted, these skills make our daily lives more meaningful and enjoyable, even when we are faced with difficult situations and circumstances.

<< Objectives >>

Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) is a form of cognitive-behavioural therapy, an empirically based psychological intervention that uses acceptance and mindfulness strategies with commitment and behavior-change strategies to increase psychological flexibility. Psychological flexibility is the ability to stay in contact with the present moment regardless of unpleasant thoughts, feelings, and bodily sensations, while choosing one's behaviors based on the situation and personal values. 

The objective of this project is to introduce psychological flexibility skills into youth work practices with the aim of empowering professional capacities of youth workers that work with vulnerable groups of young people. As a result, they will be able to cope with stress more successfully, protect themselves from burn-out and transfer those skills to the young people they work with. This objective will be achieved by development of an intellectual output: innovative tool for increasing psychological flexibility that will consist of 2 parts: workshop curriculum that will be used in synergy with the mobile application containing short excercise based on the principles of ACT therapy.

<< Implementation >>

Target group of this project are youth workers from 5 participating countries who took part in producing the described intellectual output, piloting it and disseminating it to the relevant stakeholders. In the beginning of the project, 10 team members took part in joint staff training where they learned the basics of ACT treatment that enabled them to develop the content for the curriculum and the mobile app. The developed materials were tested and revised in the second joint staff training that was organized for additional 15 youth workers who implemented national piloting of the materials afterwards. Through these trainings, youth workers developed their own psychological flexibility and with the help of the developed intellectual output, they were able to transfer these skills in a systematic and easy way to young people they work with. The developed curriculum and mobile app are freely available in the project website and widely disseminated to other youth workers who want to develop better ways of dealing with stress and transfer these skills to youth they work with.

<< Results >>

The Intellectual Output created through this project is Workshop curriculum that is designed to be used in synergy with the mobile app. Some other important results are: 10 team members educated about ACT in 64-hour long education in beginning of the project; 15 associated partners educated on how to use the Intellectual output in the ACT training that prepared them to do the piloting; 10-20 young people from each partner country went through the local testing and piloting of the Intellectual output; at least 30 relevant stakeholders per partner country have been informed about the project results through the Multiplier events that were organized in each partner contry; at least 500 stakeholders have been informed about the project news through the newsletter that was sent through the mailing lists. The impact and long-term effect of this project is raising awareness of the stress that youth workers who work with vulnerable groups of youth deal with in their everyday work, of the importance of adopting healthy ways of dealing with stress and taking care of own mental health for lifelong sustainability, especially in such high-demanding emotional work.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
Quality and innovation of youth work

2020-1-HR01-KA205-077589.title: Youth awareness of the EU system: EU policies and youth participation good practices exchange
2020-1-HR01-KA205-077589.summary:
<< Background >>

The goal was to mitigate the growing trend of youth disinterest in social and political engagement. Also, many active young people do not use all the tools available to them to strengthen their capacities, thanks to which new opportunities would be created for them. The experience of working with young people at the local level shows a lack of information about the possibilities of inclusion in decision-making processes and a lack of trust of young people in institutions. This is precisely why we decided to include cities whose employees sometimes do not have information on how to approach young people and get information about their needs. The project connected youth, civil society organizations, and local self-government into one European concept so that together they could get a broader picture of how to provide a stimulating environment for young people locally. Through the activities of this project proposal, young people acquired social skills necessary for personal development, received information about tools that enable them to turn their ideas into actions, and acquired additional knowledge about existing youth policies.

<< Objectives >>

Through the activities, the young people who were involved in the mobility itself had the opportunity to see how local youth councils function in the two countries and received information about ways to involve young people in decision-making processes at the local level. Based on the comparison, young people could see what information they lacked during the last EU elections, which, in their opinion, could encourage a more significant number of young people to go to the polls. The participants will encourage young people to be more engaged in political processes by improving the aforementioned platform.
During the implementation of the project, civil society organizations connected better with each other, exchanged experiences of working with young people, and cooperation with local authorities.
Also, this was an exceptional opportunity so that the Cities could exchange experiences regarding work with young people and, at the same time, be in direct contact with young people so that they could exchange ideas with each other about ways to involve young people in decision-making processes at the district level.

<< Implementation >>

During the implementation of the entire project, two blended mobility and one training were implemented. During the training of people working with young people, 16 youth workers participated. During five days, the participants had exercises related to emotional intelligence, after which they presented the tools they use in working with young people in their countries. After the exchange of ideas and taking into account the goals of the project itself, the youth workers further perfected the blended mobility implementation plan.Two blended mobilities were reserved for young people, decision-makers, and youth workers.During the five days spent in Cuenca, the participants were introduced to the functioning of EU institutions and the work of young people in different countries. In the end, through the exchange of their own experiences, they came to conclusions on how to intensify the engagement of young people in their countries.During the activity in Šibenik, attended by 33 young people, 14 with fewer opportunities, they learned the basic concepts of democracy through informal learning methods. They worked on designing methods to encourage young people to participate in the upcoming EU parliamentary elections scheduled for 2024year.

<< Results >>

During the implementation of the project, the following results were achieved:
a) Educational/informative materials and advice: online initiatives for exchanging ideas and opinions.
b) Special area on websites and social networks of participating organizations, brochures, leaflets, and dissemination materials (especially online materials)
b) Creation of a network in which organizations, young people, and local self-governments contribute to creating a stimulating environment for young people at the local level.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide
Quality and innovation of youth work

2020-1-IT03-KA205-018135.title: European heritage for youth involvement and entrepreneurship
2020-1-IT03-KA205-018135.summary:
<< Background >>

The project arisen from a needs analysis in the partner countries, which highlighted common needs and issues: youth unemployment; few working opportunities in the small rural centres especially for young people, with a consequent depopulation; degradation of natural and cultural heritage, with a lack of environmental preservation culture and low participation in responsible citizenship; insufficient investments for the development and promotion of cultural objectives; mass tourism encouraged; limited accessibility of some tourist sites; lack of tourist information; lack of public-private partnerships for ecotourism; low involvement of local population for a sustainable tourism promotion.
Addressing these needs, the project aimed to foster exchange and dialogue between young people and youth workers from 7 different EU countries (Italy, Spain, Romania, Greece, Lithuania, Croatia and Portugal) on the issues of safeguarding and promoting natural and cultural heritage and social inclusion, developing entrepreneurial competence in the field of ecological and sustainable tourism and transversal competences for personal and professional development and active participation in society.

<< Objectives >>

The project specific objectives were:
-To raise awareness of the importance of Europe's cultural heritage through informal and non formal education activities, as a tool for social inclusion, youth participation and social entrepreneurship
-To promote the young people environmental education, especially ecotourism education for an active citizenship
-To strengthen the sense of belonging and participation, promoting activities that protect and enhance the common heritage, involving young people and local stakeholders, thus promoting social cohesion
-To improve key competences of youth workers to enhance the quality of their activity
-To foster the inclusion and employability of young people with fewer opportunities (including NEETs) through quality youth work and transnational learning activities
-To ease transition of young people from youth to adulthood, supporting the integration into the labour market developing key competences and promoting creative learning, entrepreneurship, and social entrepreneurship
-To create a European space of reflection for ecological and sustainable tourism as an educational learning experience, fostering personal and professional growth for youngsters.

<< Implementation >>

The main project activities implemented are:
- 3 Project coordination meetings (online, in Croatia and Portugal)
- Creation of the Project multilingual website, integrated with a specific e-learning area with online modules for young people and youth workers
- 2 Short-term joint staff training events in Greece and Spain, to develop competences in youth workers, observing and using non-formal education methods and tools to increase youth participation and involvement, also related to sustainable tourism as an educational tool and as an entrepreneurial drive for local development and youth involvement.
- 1 Blended mobility of young people in Portugal, to develop key competences of young people. They discovered sustainable tourism activities and shared good practices for the environmental protection.
- Dissemination conference
- Local activities: Diagnosis and analysis of situation, identification and collection of good practices in the field of ecological and sustainable tourism and social entrepreneurship; creation of online learning modules for young people and youth workers in the fields of ecological and sustainable tourism and social entrepreneurship; collection of tools developed during the blended mobility, visibility events.

<< Results >>

The project activities led to the achievement of the following results:
OUTPUTS
- Project multilingual website (in English and according to the languages of the partnership), integrated with a specific e-learning area for young people and youth workers in the fields of ecological and sustainable tourism and social entrepreneurship;
- Booklet with diagnosis and analysis of situation, identification and collection of good practices in the field of ecological and sustainable tourism and social entrepreneurship, uploaded in the project website;
- Collection of tools for ecotourism and social entrepreneurship development, developed during the blended mobility for young people.
OUTCOMES
- New competences developed in young people and youth workers;
- Knowledge and experiences connected with project topics shared;
- More awareness about the educational value of European cultural heritage, on the importance of environmental protection and on the concept of ecotourism;
- Creation of a network of 7 European countries for exchanging good practices and working methodologies.

2020-1-LU01-KA205-063213.title: Youth Ambassadors & YInfoPEERs
2020-1-LU01-KA205-063213.summary:
<< Background >>

In the current information landscape, it is increasingly important that young people think critically about the information they access and learn how to advocate for their rights and interests. In fact, they face many challenges regarding information management, such as disinformation, overload of information, and fake news, to name a few. 
Youth information providers strive to ensure that young people access full and reliable information. According to a study published by Åbo Akademi and ERYICA in 2018, there are certain areas of information where young people rely more on their peers than on any other source: the peer-to-peer approach in youth information is essential. 
Every two years since 2012, ERYICA has trained young people to become ambassadors for youth information. At the time when we presented the application of this project, we considered that the programme required a quantum leap. Through the Youth Ambassadors and YinfoPeers project, young people were trained to advocate for the right to information at different levels and become peer educators. 
Another important motivation for applying for this project was the need to permanently involve young people in ERYICA activities and the decision-making process.

<< Objectives >>

When the project application was drafted, the verall objectives were: 
- Co-creating and piloting a training course for peer-to-peer in youth information (Youth InfoPEERS);
- Co-creating and piloting a training course for Youth Ambassadors on the right to information (iNFObassadors);
- Co-creating and piloting a MOOC on how to run a successful online advocacy campaign (iAdvocate online) targeting young people (peer-to-peer) and youth organisations;
- Increasing the outreach of youth information visibility across Europe;
- Developing a structure and support system to ensure the ambassadors' participation during the project, with the active participation and support of the partners;
- Developing a framework that ensures the structured and permanent involvement of young people in the ERYICA network decision-making processes and governance beyond the project; and
- Political awareness-raising at local, national and European levels through multiplier events and targeted communication.

<< Implementation >>

As further explained, the initial project objectives were overall met. We implemented several activities:
- Transnational project meetings with partners and Youth Ambassadors;
- Creation of the infoPEERS training manual;
- Creation of the INFObassadors training manual;
- Creation of the iAdvocate online course;
- Organisation of infoPEERS training course;
- Organisation of INFObassadors training course;
- Organisation of the local-level multiplier events;
- Organisation of the joint-multiplier event in Sibenik, Croatia;
- Development of the Youth Ambassadors framework;
- Development of a Europe-wide campaign;
- Development of an overall youth participation framework for young people;
- Translation of the infoPEERS manual into 8 languages (Catalan, Croatian, French, German, Greek, Slovenian, Spanish, Macedonian).

<< Results >>

A training manual for peer-to-peer in youth information (Youth InfoPEERS IO1) was created, translated into 8 languages and piloted through the infoPEERS training course in Spain. Moreover, A training manual for youth information ambassadors (iNFObassadors IO2) was created and piloted through the online INFObassadors training course, carried out online due to the pandemic. Finally, an online course on how develop online advocacy campaigns (iAdvocate Online IO3) for young people was developed.
A Europe-wide online campaign was co-designed and implemented by the Youth Ambassadors. 
They also piloted part of the iAdvocate online course on advocacy for the right to youth information. 
The consortium organised a multiplier event in Sibenik, where international stakeholders (i.e. the European Commission), local participants, ERYICA GB and other ERYICA members were invited. The event was led by the Youth Ambassadors, who co-organised it, facilitated it and participated as panellists. 
The Youth Ambassadors and project partners also carried out multiplying events at the local level. 
A framework was developed through which Youth Ambassadors can influence the strategic direction of ERYICA and youth information in Europe.
topics: Reaching the policy level/dialogue with decision makers
Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Quality and innovation of youth work

2020-1-NL02-KA205-002910.title: Social entrepreneurship for a sustainable future with less conflict
2020-1-NL02-KA205-002910.summary:
<< Background >>

This project addressed the need for strengthened programs for NEET youth/women in the field of entrepreneurship. In each of the countries involved and throughout Europe in general (and especially among our target groups of immigrants and marginalized groups) girls and young women are less active in business and entrepreneurship, particularly as independent entrepreneurs and business leaders. For that reason, this project aimed to change this situation by equipping youth organizations and youth workers with tools and approaches they can use to support the entrepreneurship of young women in a way that is socially and culturally appropriate. The project gathered organizations that already had experiences in supporting young women to be socially and economically active and allowed them to develop new ways of dealing with the challenges they have identified.

With this project, we answered the needs defined by institutions, as well as the needs of our own youth workers and youth. We were promoting social entrepreneurship (for sustainable development and peacebuilding) of NEET youth, women and quality empowerment of our youth workers to be able to organize quality (social) entrepreneurship education for our beneficiaries

<< Objectives >>

The previously mentioned needs were influenced by the project objectives:

1.) To empower our youth workers and improve knowledge management of youth work organizations in theory and practice for building competencies of youth workers in social entrepreneurship for a sustainable future with less conflict, for NEET youngsters, and young women - through LTTA and innovative curriculum and online course for youth workers’ training.

2.) To empower NEET youngsters, and young women for social entrepreneurship start-up and quality social marketing of theirs, through the development of inspiring, innovative and up-to-date handbooks, toolkits, as well as online courses.

3.) To exchange good practices and further develop quality strategic partnerships among partners from 5 European countries with different realities in regards to youth social entrepreneurship for a sustainable future with less conflict

2020-1-PL01-KA205-078361.title: CRAFT: Co-working in Rural Areas to prepare young people for Future Trends
2020-1-PL01-KA205-078361.summary:
<< Background >>

The project was rooted into evidences from Eurostat, OECD and ILO showing worrying data with respect to youth unemployment rates in Europe and the impact of this in terms of growth and cohesion of EU societies. Considering that young people face specific challenges in the transition from school to work (being new to the labour market, they often meet discriminations and are less likely to find decent jobs) and that geographical barriers represent one of the major factors affecting that transition, pushing youth towards brain-drain and migration to big cities, CRAFT was intended to tackle those challenges boosting self-entrepreneurial skills and the referred mindset. The project took stock of the human and physical capital of rural areas, subverting the perception of challenges from a perspective of opportunity, promoting forward-looking learning activities (digitalised OERs, transnational mobilities, hackathons) around fundamental entrepreneurship competencies referring to 3 strategic areas: personal care and health-related jobs; green economy; STEAM. The need addressed was thus to combat youth unemployment in rural European areas, increasing the labour market participation of the target by facilitating, in particular, coworking startup.

<< Objectives >>

CRAFT intended:
- to promote employment and entrepreneurship in EU rural areas by increasing young people capabilities to reconvert empty spaces so to host collaborative working environments, exploiting the substantial potential offered by trends outlined in the jobs and skills future market;
- to promote youth skills and competencies for the development of co-working spaces focused on the abovementioned 3 specific areas;
- to foster youth ability and autonomy to operate at transnational level for developing joint concrete projects;
- to strengthen a digital mindset among youngsters to effectively tackle the European Skills Deal post-2020;
- to empower youth through the setup of win-win networks involving relevant socio-economic actors as policy change-makers;
- to improve career guidance services through specific recommendations;
- to boost international cooperation (beyond the partner countries) in the Youth field, contributing to the achievement of relevant EU objectives;
- to develop innovative models to shape coworking spaces and setup competitive entrepreneurial ideas;
- to back the standardization of good skills performances among youth in EU rural areas;
- to favour EU-level peer learning between youth and trainers.

<< Implementation >>

Despite the Covid-19 pandemic, the project realised:
- The transversal activities (management, evaluation, communication&dissemination) on a continuous basis (see specific sections)
- A Training programme/IO1 (https://craft-project.eu/craft-training-material/), piloted during the C1, involving 20 young people from Italy, Poland, Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovenia and Norway, as well as 4 trainers
- An Educational 3D virtual world/IO2 (https://craft-project.eu/craft-vw-platform/), internally tested internally in July 2021, piloted during the C1 and validated through Hackathons 
- A training activity (C1) that took place in Sept.2021
- Although lacking ad hoc financial support, partners have setup a "Multi-actor territorial network of policy change-makers"
- 7 Multiplier Events took place in partner countries: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FGdKe53F_xCg3B6eB5FLBFPPbr1jqyJx
- 5 TPMs (4 hybrid, 1 online) + several virtual update meetings: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1dIAUC5Y0GVjXljNP9Grm3A-qwXvpTfwE
- A complete visual identity (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-QSdWtN3Q1ivTm0GVjed9vtPKBwPeIi8) and weekly update of a FB page (https://www.facebook.com/EUprojectCRAFT) counting 1295 followers (Aug.2022)

<< Results >>

The project produced the following outputs and results: 
1 Training programme (IO1), available in English via the project website and YouTube and covering the following learning modules: 1-Managing co-working spaces in rural areas; 2-Career Skills for the Future; 3-Entrepreneurship skills. Its final version is the result of a pilot activity conducted by the partners during the LTTA/C1, involving 17 youngsters from Italy, Poland, Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovenia, Norway, as well as 4 trainers.
1 Educational 3D virtual world (IO2) consisting of 7 missions, applying elements from the escape rooms to help young people test their gained knowledge from the CRAFT modules (IO1). The output is available in EN via the CRAFT website. Its final version is the result of an internal pilot activity conducted by 2 representative/partner, as well as an additional pilot (external) organised during the LTTA held in Croatia.
A training activity (C1) that involved 20 youngsters from 6 partnership countries, who got acquainted on the learning modules' contents and worked on creating and prototyping coworking spaces.
7 Multiplier Events disseminating the project ratio and its results.
Brand identity, including 1 website and 1 FB page, 1 IG page, YouTube
topics: Equal access and transition to labour market

2020-1-PT02-KA205-006692.summary:
<< Background >>

CONTEXT 
The new "adult" generations face difficulties in building their future, especially when it comes to seeking personal and financial independence and exploring new career paths.
In fact, the absence of "simple" key competencies for lifelong learning and of innovative and entrepreneurial thoughts and attitudes, based on a financial education aimed at empowerment and awareness, is the motto for the emergence and/or perpetuity of phenomena of social exclusion, social inequality, unemployment, dependence on social systems, etc.
NEEDS
1. Creation of an economic and financial literacy program, transversal to the development of new key competences, adjusted to the needs, expectations and motivations of young people;
2. To provide young people with new knowledge and experiences that would emphasize their potential in the construction of their life project;
3. To equip youth workers with new knowledge and experiences that would emphasize their potential in working transnationally with young people, especially in solving current problems and needs;
4. Promoting equal access to personal, social and professional development opportunities.

<< Objectives >>

PROJECT GOALS
1. Promote financial literacy and management, through the transfer of knowledge and practices, methodologies, methods and tools to initiate new ways of thinking and acting;
2. To promote youth empowerment by developing key entrepreneurial skills (especially economic and financial literacy) and adopting entrepreneurial thoughts and attitudes;
3. To promote the empowerment of youth workers by transferring new knowledge, practices, methodologies and methods of working with and for young people in the spectrum of financial literacy and the acquisition of key skills;
4. To promote the incorporation of participative and inclusive methodologies in youth work (such as non-formal education) and their potential to complement other methodologies (such as informal and formal education)
5. To promote social inclusion, including under-represented groups, through the creation of empowerment opportunities.

COMMUNICATION AND DISSEMINATION

Competences of the reference framework of the EU Council Recommendations: literary skills; multilingual; mathematical and basic competences in science and technology and engineering; digital; personal, social and learning to learn; citizenship; entrepreneurial and cultural awareness and expression.

2020-1-RO01-KA205-079395.title: InclusiOFF - Let's turn it ON!
2020-1-RO01-KA205-079395.summary:
<< Background >>

One of the main identified needs was to develop strategies to strengthen critical thinking and support all young people when it comes to actively taking part in society, no matter what particular groups they might belong to. Through equipping youth workers to engage young people in non-formal educational activities organised at local level, the project tackled discrimination, racism and segregation, whilst by equipping youth workers with skills to develop and coordinate awareness raising and advocacy actions, the project contributed directly to growing social inclusion at local level, whilst creating sustainable links between youth organisations, public authorities and society at large.

As discrimination and inequalities on different grounds remain realities in everyday life in the EU, the project also addressed the need to empower young people with the necessary skills to develop educational activities to decrease discrimination and exclusion, as well as skills to advocate for policies for social inclusion at local level, in order to transform their communities into inclusive spaces that challenge discrimination of any form.

<< Objectives >>

The primary goal of the project was to empower youth workers and young people to develop competencies to increase social inclusion. 

Specifically, the main objectives of the project were to:
1. Strengthen the capacity of 6 youth organisations to address efficiently and qualitatively social exclusion in their communities.
2. Create a network of 30 youth workers competent in addressing social exclusion through non-formal education and advocacy.
3. Develop competencies of 900 young people (30 young people to each youth worker) to understand and deal with social exclusion in their life and in society.

<< Implementation >>

Over a two-year period, the project consisted of:
- 1 Kick-off Meeting (online)
- 1 training on non-formal educational methods for social inclusion
- 1 practice phase consisting of non-formal educational activities in schools in each local context
- 1 Evaluation Meeting
- 1 training on development and coordination of advocacy campaigns
- 1 practice phase consisting of advocacy campaigns on improvement of social inclusion policies at local level, in each local context
- 1 Final Meeting

<< Results >>

Concrete results of the project
- 30 youth workers trained with greater understanding of social inclusion at societal level and competencies in using non-formal educational methods to foster social inclusion
- 30 youth workers with competencies in advocacy, as well as analysing and monitoring policy, specifically social inclusion policies at local level 
- 6 advocacy campaigns on issues related to the social inclusion of discriminated groups at local level 
- 1 training module for youth workers on social inclusion at individual level and non-formal educational methods
- 1 training module for youth workers on policies for social inclusion and advocacy
- Non-formal educational activities with 916 young people 
- 14 partnerships with schools
- 6 youth organizations with increased expertise in addressing social inclusion in an integrated way
- 20 new local partners (other civil society organizations, students’ organizations, public authorities, schools, youth centres, youth clubs, etc.) attracted in the implementation of the local events /activities
- An integrated toolkit with the methodology and good practices used in the project.
topics: Quality and innovation of youth work
Promotion of alternative forms of participation
