2020-3-IE01-KA205-082901.title: Art Connects Mental Health: A Time to Breathe
2020-3-IE01-KA205-082901.summary:
<< Background >>

Art Connects Mental Health: A Time to Breathe was a two-year European wide transnational partnership project that aimed to provide education, training and awareness-raising at national and European levels using creative processes to promote positive mental health and emotional wellbeing with youth.
Six partner organisations came together to create a blueprint for a Europe-wide Creative Arts for Health and Well Being hub, a new online, interactive, learning resource centre that supports the role of the arts to promote physical and emotional positive mental health and well-being for all. 
We noted that a challenging event like the COVID-19 (coronavirus) pandemic affected everyone’s mental health. While each of us were doing our best to look after ourselves however young people may need extra attention and support.  Building synergies between the arts, youth education, and health and well-being, this project addressed an important need by supporting the role of the arts to promote positive mental health and emotional well-being, to overcome stress and anxiety and to build resilience across Europe, strengthening links across Europe in relation to the arts, education and positive mental health and well-being with and by young people.

<< Objectives >>

The core aim of this project was to bring different partners together and to combine their skills and expertise in order to create a European model for using the arts to promote positive mental health and well-being with youth workers and young people, both face-to-face and online.  We were particularly keen to demonstrate the effectiveness of the arts through innovative processes and actions in its ability to promote physical and emotional health and wellbeing for all.  This is particularly pertinent in a post Covid pandemic society and research has demonstrated the effectiveness of new techniques, including the arts to assist in supporting improved mental health and wellbeing.  We also wanted to showcase how co-operation and working together on a transnational basis can achieve collective benefits with sharing of knowledge and expertise and demonstrating the benefits of a shared approach across Europe.

<< Implementation >>

1. A blueprint for the creation of a European wide Creative Arts for Health and Well-Being Hub (an online interactive platform and learning resource centre) and  resources (curriculum with three online workshops, eight hand-outs and digital app) – all used to manage stress and anxiety and build resilience
2. Sustainable partnership strengthened between six key organisations and links built between arts, education, mental health and new digital technologies with and by young people at national and European levels.
3. Supporting the empowerment of youth workers through the development and uptake of new, innovative and accessible training and resources to promote best practice in teaching and learning for positive mental health and well-being through the arts and digital technologies
4. Training targeted at youth workers either from or working with minority or disadvantaged groups, so as to promote social inclusion and connections for change
5. Building new ways to identify future models for sustainability and skills in networking and policy development that suit the creative and cultural industries in a changed society.

<< Results >>

1. Blueprint for online platform. We developed a blueprint or template for how to establish a Creative Arts for Health and Well-Being hub, an online, interactive, European-wide platform and learning resource using creative processes with young people to promote positive mental health and emotional wellbeing at national and European levels.
2. Creative Arts for Health and Well-Being Curriculum 
3 Creative Art Blogs (handouts) to promote positive mental health and well-being in a time of pandemic.
4. Mobile app A Time to Breath, exploring personal triggers and breathing exercises to overcome stress and anxiety and promote resilience, housed on the Creative Arts for Health and Well-Being hub
5. Four Transnational partner exchanges successfully implemented 
6. Six pilot events conducted
7. Training for Youth Workers implemented
8. Series of multiplier events conducted
9. Communications and Dissemination: Each partner carried out PR and social media campaigns
topics: New learning and teaching methods and approaches
Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses

2020-3-PL01-KA205-095033.title: Młodzi w akcji - wymiana praktyk w celu pobudzenia młodzieży do działania
2020-3-PL01-KA205-095033.summary:
<< Background >>

We applied for the implementation of the project because we wanted to open the foundation to activities in a wider European dimension. We wanted the staff of partner organizations to enrich their knowledge of working with youth through the exchange of practices and experiences. For this purpose, we invited partners who have extensive experience in working with youth and respond to our needs to participate in the project. We wanted our partners to bring experience in promoting non-formal education, volunteering, developing educational programs and animation activities. And also in working with young people with fewer opportunities, of refugee origin. Thanks to the participation of a partner from Austria, we wanted to break negative stereotypes among Polish youth about refugees and youth from countries such as the Middle East. In addition, we really wanted to get acquainted with the culture and customs of other countries. Thanks to the implementation of the project, we wanted to present the Foundation and our ideas to other organizations from EU countries. We also want to pass on our knowledge and skills in the field of work and helping people with disabilities, breaking stereotypes about people with disabilities and their needs. We also wanted our employees and volunteers to strengthen their faith in their own abilities and be more confident in their actions by participating in the project. To improve their skills, they introduced new methods and forms of work.

<< Objectives >>

The aim of the project was to prepare the foundation's staff for activities in a wide European field. Our goals:
1. Increase of skills, exchange of experiences and methods of 17 representatives of non-formal education staff from 5 partner organizations in the field of youth education in the field of social involvement and volunteering through participation in various workshops and trainings during the 20 months of the project.
2. Increase of skills and knowledge of 23 young people in the field of key competences, in particular social and civic competences, through participation in mobility workshops and actions organized during 20 months.
At the same time, the project responded to the specific objectives of the Erasmus+ program in the field of youth, namely:
- supported capacity building of youth workers and practices in the field;
- promote youth work and informal and non-formal learning at European, national, regional and local level;
- promoted entrepreneurship, creative science and social entrepreneurship among young people;
- enabled a group of young people to put ideas into practice, including through social enterprises in their places of residence.

<< Implementation >>

While implementing the project, the following was carried out:
1. 2 international project meetings for the project management staff.
The first coordination meeting was held on June 20-21, 2021 in Poland. A total of 9 people attended the meeting.
The second coordination meeting was held on May 20-21, 2022 in Austria. The meeting took place in Austria at the request and proposal of the Austrian partner. A total of 7 people attended the second coordination meeting.
2. Three short training mobilities for youth education staff were carried out.
The first mobility took place in Poland on October 12-15, 2021. The subject of the training was learning and exchanging experiences in organizing volunteering and working with people with disabilities. In total, 17 people took part in the mobility.
The second mobility takes place in Romania on March 7-11, 2022. During this mobility, A4Action shared its experience with partners in the field of informal education of young people, using theatrical methods, role-playing creativity. In total, 16 people took part in the mobility.
The third mobility took place in Croatia on April 18-22, 2022. The host organization was Delta from Rijeka, supported by InterAktion from Austria. Delta shared with its partners knowledge in the field of working with youth using design thinking, gamification and design thinking. InterAktion, on the other hand, presented methods of working with refugee youth, presenting social inequalities related to origin, skin color, education. In total, 22 people took part in the mobility.
3. Two mixed mobilities of young people were carried out.
The first mixed mobility of young people was carried out in Austria on June 24-30, 2022 in Trofaiach. In total, 28 people took part in the mobility.
The second mixed mobility of young people was carried out in Poland on September 17-21, 2022 in Radocyno. In total, 24 people took part in the mobility.
During the mobility, i.a. knowledge of helping people with disabilities, designing activities and space adapted to the needs of people with disabilities, knowledge of what programs young people can use, such as: European Solidarity Corps, Solidarity Projects, civic budgets, or programs and competitions of other non-governmental organizations.
The program of all mobilities was in line with the assumptions of the project. All planned activities have been completed.

<< Results >>

1. Two international project meetings were held for the project management staff. A total of 16 people attended the two meetings.
2. Three short training mobilities for youth education staff were carried out. In total, 55 people took part in all mobilities.
3. 2 Mixed mobilities of young people were carried out. A total of 52 people attended.
4. 152 hours completed. classes/workshops/educational trainings within all mobilities implemented in the project.
5. There was an exchange of methods and practices of non-formal education and experiences by the educational staff,
6. The level of knowledge and skills of 36 employees of the education staff from partner organizations (Croatia - 4 people, Romania - 9 people, Austria - 6 people, the Homini Association - 8 people, the Wyjdź z Domu Foundation - 9 people) increased in the use of innovative methods of non-formal education of youth through participation in joint workshops and exchange of experiences on, for example, coaching, theater and role-playing, teamwork, design thinking, gamification and design thinking, volunteering, working with people with disabilities.
7. The level of knowledge and skills of 42 youth representatives from partner organizations increased in planning and preparing activities, projects and products through participation in workshops and trainings organized during combined mobilities.
8. The experience of 17 employees of the organization was collected in the field of organization and implementation of youth volunteering and the exchange of volunteering organization practices in the specificity of different countries.
9. The project staff and partner organizations improved their work in an international working group.
10. The level of linguistic and interpersonal competences of the project staff, partner organizations and participating young people has improved.
11. The awareness of the cultural diversity of the Partner countries and the European society has increased.
12. Action plans for local initiatives were developed, which were implemented by young people in each of the partner countries.
13. There was an increase in the knowledge of young people in terms of opportunities that young people have using such programs as the European Solidarity Corps, Solidarity Projects, participatory budgets, or programs and competitions of other non-governmental organizations (24 people).
14. There was an increase in the level of knowledge and skills of 17 people from the staff of partner organizations and 42 young people in the field of helping people with disabilities and designing activities and space adapted to their needs and capabilities.
  15. There was a significant increase in activity among young people who got involved in projects from the European Solidarity Corps for the local community. Currently, 6 projects are being implemented under the European Solidarity Corps through the Leave Home Foundation. In February this year, more projects will be submitted by young people through the Wyjdź z Domu Foundation. These young people come from Gorlice high schools. It is planned to submit another 6 projects.
16. Self-esteem and self-improvement among young people has increased, young people are more willing to implement the new methods they have learned in their projects.
17. The quality of activities carried out for and with the participation of young people has improved.
18. The cooperation between the project partners was strengthened through further exchange of information and knowledge. Partners are preparing to submit further applications under the Erasmus Program and other international competitions.
topics: Promotion of alternative forms of participation
Quality and innovation of youth work
Bridging intercultural, intergenerational and social divide

2020-3-PT02-KA205-007427.title: Building Inclusive Societies: exchanging innovative and good practices to empower local NGO's working with migrants and refugees
2020-3-PT02-KA205-007427.summary:
<< Background >>

Ever since the humanitarian crises that started in 2015, the focus of Agora Aveiro shifted in the direction of human rights. At that time, we started implementing local initiatives to call attention to different issues when it comes to inclusion/discrimination and also, we were partners but also coordinators of numerous project KA1 on this topic. After gaining more experience around the topic, we felt we needed to learn more, and in a more structured and profound way, so a small scale partnership felt like right option for our needs at that time. We carefully organised a consortium in which every partner could learn something practical from each other and therefore improve their work. We applied for this project in 2020, in order to strengthen our organisations, widen our expertise and acquire new competences. As for Agora Aveiro, our main need was to get knowledge and practice on how to approach the topics in a more profound way than what we have been doing so far. Other partners needed to learn how to improve the involvement of local community in their projects, which Agora Aveiro has been doing successfully, but also to become more familiar with Erasmus+ and non-formal education methods in general.

<< Objectives >>

These were the objectives defined in the time of application, and they remained the same till the end:
1- exchanging specific theoretical & practical knowledge among participating organisations. Each organisation shared their knowledge and methodologies they use in their work with migrants and refugees and in the prevention of social exclusion. Our methods are different, but efficient in translatable to other communities facing discrimination and exclusion of different groups. 
2- improving the capacities of partners by improving the skills and competencies of their staff/volunteers. Planned LTTs included participants that are employed or volunteering in participating organisations. Each partner prepared a personalised activity where skills and competencies related to specific methodologies were improved. Participants afterward started using some/all of the learned methodologies in their daily work.
3- raising awareness of the local communities about the difficulties/challenges newcomers face and influencing a broader audience to act towards building a more inclusive society (local communities, stakeholders, youth workers, volunteers in partner organisations)

<< Implementation >>

The project consisted of two transnational meetings, two short term joint staff training activities, two blended mobilities for young people, 12 in-house sharing sessions, and four spin-off activities. 

The main activities were: 
- "Citizen science for inclusive communities" led by Psychosocial Innovation Network
- "Deliberative Workshop methodology for youth workers" led by Social Science Works.
- "Youth leaders of change" led by Mentor 
- "Innovative Tools for Building Inclusive Communities" led by Agora Aveiro

Besides transnational activities, each partner, after each activity organised an in-house session where they shared with their colleagues, volunteers, collaborators the main findings of the mobility activities and discussed the potential of using them in their organisation. After the four activities partners implemented an activity based on what was learned during the project, therefore in Agora Aveiro we used methods from Youth leaders for change to improve our volunteering program, in PIN they organised a Human Library and in Mentor they organised a guerrilla marketing awareness raising activity. In SSW they used the whole experience as an inspiration for a joint project proposal submitted in June 2023 under CERV.

<< Results >>

- 2 transnational meetings (5 pax each);
- 52 mobilities with youth workers, partner NGOs staff, and long-term volunteers took part in 4 project activities, where pax gaining specific theoretical and practical knowledge and improving their skills and competencies as follows: 8 participants were trained in research-based activism, data-driven advocacy, and PFA; 8 pax trainer in Deliberation methodology; 12 junior pax from partner orgs trained in peer education and youth leadership in the context of social inclusion; 16 junior pax trained in using tools for fighting discrimination and building a more inclusive local communities (Human library, guerrilla marketing, Theatre of the oppressed).
- 38 people took part in in-house sharing sessions;
- 13 associated partners joined the project;
- 4 human libraries organised, close to 200 pax;
- 19 migrants/refugees participated in the Human Library events;
- 3 guerrilla marketing activities organised during the project which reached up to 200 people both in the streets of Aveiro and Split;
- Approx 550 pax informed offline about our project and the Erasmus+ programme;
- Approx 30000 pax were reached with the information about the project via social media of 4 partners (approx 1600 per post).

2020-3-RS01-KA205-094490.title: Safebook
2020-3-RS01-KA205-094490.summary:
Project “Safebook” will be implemented in the partnership between Club for Youth Empowerment 018 (KOM 18) from Nis-Serbia, Association Beyond borders from Puglia- Italy, Council for Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency (SPPMD) from Kavadarci – North Macedonia and Impress from Daruvar - Croatia in the period 01.03.2021- 28.02.2022. 
The problems of youth safety are common in 4 countries. What is also common is the role that youth organizations (consortium organizations but also NGOs at the local and national level) have in working on these issues and serving as the bridge between young people and institutions. Having a bigger outreach through non-formal education, the role of youth organizations and youth workers is of a great importance. That is why this project will deal with the safety issues of young people in 4 countries through empowerment of youth workers and educators and development of innovative methods to raise the awareness about important issues. Newly developed tools will focus on 5 segments: peer violence, cyber bullying, abuse of psychoactive substances, discrimination and mental health in time of COVID–19

General objective: 
To contribute to the development of a safety culture of young people 
Specific objectives: 
•	To develop new methods of youth work in the field of youth safety
•	To equip youth workers and educators with set of new educational tools in the field of youth safety 
•	To raise the awareness about safety issues in local communities in 4 countries

Planned activities:
1.Transnational Projects Meeting 1 - Coordination meeting - will be organized in Nis, Serbia in March 2021
2. Development of Intellectual Output – “Safebook” manual - 4 partner organizations and experts and youth workers coming from these 4 organizations will develop “Safebook” manual focusing on 5 segments of youth safety: peer violence, cyber bullying, abuse of psychoactive substances, discrimination and mental health of young people in the period of COVID – 19. In this way the project will result in the increased number of methodologies for youth workers/educators working in the field of youth safety and improved quality of youth work methods in 4 participating countries. Period: April / August 2021
3. Mid - evaluation meeting - will be organized online with the project coordination team in August 2021
4.Testing the new methods - Local workshops – partners’ experts and youth workers who created the “Safebook” manual will test the manual and organize local workshops in Serbia, Croatia, North Macedonia and Italy to test newly adopted methods working with youth workers and young people (20 per country). In this way the quality and applicability of the workshops will be checked while at the same time youth workers and educators will be equipped with set of new educational tools in the field of youth safety. Period: September / November 2021
5. Multiplier events – Every partner organization will organize 1 multiplier event that will include at least 20 youth workers, educators and activities outside the partner organization. This activity will increase the use of the newly developed “Safebook” manual and at the same time raise the awareness about youth safety in local communities of the project. Period: November 2021/January 2022
6.Transnational Projects Meeting 2 - Final evaluation meeting -will be organized in Orta Nova, Italy  in February 2022

Main expected result of the "Safebook" project and its activities is to develop and transfer new and innovative methodology and creative tools and to incorporate them in new and youth friendly manual for youth workers in the field of youth safety and security. Through development of this manual new opportunities for promotion and advancement of the certain areas in non-formal education but also in other sectors such as formal education and sport sectors, like prevention of discrimination, peer violence, cyber bulling and abuse of psychoactive substances as well as protection of mental health of youth during COVID-19 will arise from multiplication and dissemination of the mentioned manual. 
Another very important expected result upon the project completion is to have significant increase in capacity building activities and projects which are aiming at building the capacities of youth workers, peer educators, volunteers and activists in the areas which are the topic of this project. Finally,  one of the expected results is the involvement of other youth NGOs and relevant institutions in the use of the newly developed tools. Project activities will have one final result in the form of well written, youth friendly and innovative manual for youth workers in the field of youth safety. The manual will later be promoted among NGOs, youth workers and peer educators not only from Serbia, North Macedonia, Italy and Croatia, but also from other EU and non-EU countries in order to transfer new and fresh ideas for implementation of projects concerning the potential risks of youth safety
